meta.title: Flora of Hong Kong — searchable text
sources: Species list from HKHerbarium with FOHK extracted 20240321.xlsx

records.text: Herbs, shrubs or climbers, rarely small trees. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate, exstipulate, entire, serrate, rarely pinnatifid, usually covered with cystoliths. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic to nearly actinomorphic, in spikes, racemes, panicles, or heads, rarely solitary or clustered. Bract 1, large or minute. Bracteoles 2, or 4, sometimes absent. Calyx connate at least basally, usually 4–5‑lobed, rarely reduced to an entire ring, cupular or truncate or 10–20‑lobed. Corolla sympetalous, the limb subequally (3‑ or )5‑lobed or (1–)2‑lipped, the lobes imbricate or contorted in bud, usually divided into a distinct narrow tube and a wider throat. Fertile stamens adnate to the base of corolla, 4, didynamous, or 2; filaments free or basally connate into pairs; anthers parallel or superposed, oblong, thecae 1 or 2, spherical, linear, muticous or spurred, longitudinally dehiscent; staminodes 1–3 or absent. Disk annular and nectar‑producing at base of ovary. Ovary superior, 2‑locular; ovules 2–many in each locule; placenta axile; style filiform, simple; stigma entire, or 2‑lobed, with one lobe frequently smaller, or funnel‑shaped. Fruit a loculicidal capsule, 2‑valved, or rarely drupaceous (not ours). Seeds 2–many, usually borne on hook‑like retinacula, or retinacula lacking (Thunbergia, Staurogyne), the testa smooth or roughened, sometimes with mucilaginous trichomes which expand when moistened. About 250 genera and 3500 species in tropical regions of the world; about 50 genera and 320 species in China; 23 genera and 43 species and one variety in Hong Kong. Avicennia , usually placed in Verbenaceae or in its own family Avicenniaceae, is included in this family by the Angiosperm Phylogeny Group on the basis of molecular phylogenetic studies.

Trees, sometimes shrubs. Winter buds imbricate or valvate. Leaves simple, usually palmately lobed, rarely pinnately or palmately compound, opposite, petiolate, usually estipulate. Inflorescence a corymb, umbel, raceme, or panicle, terminal or lateral. Flowers bisexual (but functionally female) or unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals (4–)5, distinct or seldomly connate. Petals (4–)5(–6), rarely 0, imbricate, distinct, like sepals. Stamens usually 8, sometimes 4–6 or 10–12. Disk present or absent. Ovary superior, compressed, usually 2-locular, ovules 2 per locule; style usually bifurcate; stigmas 2. Fruit a winged schizocarp, usually a double samara, usually 1-seeded, endosperm absent. Two genera and ca. 130 species widespread in N temperate and some tropical regions of the world; two genera and about 100 species in China; one genus and four species native to Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with creeping, branched rhizomes and specialized aromatic oil cells. Leaves distichous, ensiform, unifacial, bases overlapping, not differentiated into petiole and blade, with parallel veins. Inflorescence a terminal spadix, bone on leaf-like scape (peduncle), sessile, conoid, cylindrical and finger-like or slender and tail-like, flowering from base to top. Flowers bisexual, 3-merous, densely arranged; tepals 6, free, in 2 whorls; stamens 6, free, in 2 whorls, anthers introrse, thecae globose-ellipsoidal, dehiscing by longitudinal slit; ovary conical, 2–3-locular; ovules many, pendulous from apex of each locule, orthotropous; stigma minute or ± punctate, subsessile. Fruit a several-seeded berry. Seeds oblong to ellipsoidal with fleshy endosperm. One genus and two species distributed in subtropical and temperate Asia, and N America.

Woody vines, trees or shrubs, polygamous or dioecious. Leaves simple, alternate, pinnately veined, exstipulate. Inflorescence usually fascicled, cymose, or paniculate, axillary. Flowers bisexual or unisexual. Sepals 5, rarely fewer, imbricate. Petals 5, sometimes 4 or 6, imbricate or convolute. Stamens 10 –many, distinct or adnate to base of petals; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by apical pores or longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 5–many-locular; ovules 10–many on axile placentation; styles 3–many, distinct or connate, usually persistent. Fruit a berry or capsule. Seeds small, endosperm copious, embryo large, straight. Three genera and ca. 350 species mainly distributed in tropical region of the world; three genera and ca. 60 species in China; two genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, monoecious, dioecious, or polygamodioecious. Stems subterranean or aboveground, woody or not, sometimes branched. Leaves simple, usually aggregated at base of stem or crowded at apex of branches; blade thick and rigid or succulent. Inflorescences terminal or axillary spikes, racemose or paniculate, bracteate, often huge; bracts leaf-like proximally, scale-like distally. Flowers bisexual or functionally unisexual; perianth semisucculent, free or ± connate; tube short to rather long; segments 6, equal to subequal, apex glandular or glandular-pubescent; stamens 6 included or exserted; filaments free; anthers versatile, 2-celled, dehiscence longitudinal. Ovary superior or inferior, 3-locular or occasionally 1-locular, 3-angled, ovoid, or cylindrical, placentation axile; ovules 2–many per locule; style and stigmas various. Fruits a loculicidal capsule or occasionally baccate, or indehiscent and dry or fleshy. Seeds 1–many, globose or somewhat compressed. About 18 genera and 550–600 species distributed worldwide, mainly in tropical and subtropical regions, only two genera and six species native to China; four genera and four species are commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. In addition to the recorded species in this account, Furcraea foetida (L.) Haw.(縫線麻), Polianthes tuberosa L.(晚香玉) and Yucca gloriosa L.(大絲蘭) are occasionally cultivated as garden plants in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Stems erect or prostrate. Leaves opposite or alternate, usually fleshy, often ± terete or triquetrous. Flowers usually bisexual, actinomorphic; calyx tubular or turbinate, with often fleshy, unequal 5– 8 lobes; petals usually many, inserted on calyx-tube, rarely absent; stamens usually many, perigynous, free or united in fascicles at the base; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits; ovary half-inferior or inferior, 1–many-locular, with 1–many ovules on axile or parietal placenta. Fruit a dry capsule, rarely a berry or a nut, usually enclosed in persistent calyx-tube. About 20 genera and 600 species, mainly in S Africa and Mediterranean areas; three genera and three species in China; two genera and two species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees or shrubs. Branches spiny or not, usually terete. Leaves simple, alternate, exstipulate, often oblique at base. Inflorescences axillary, in cymes or umbels, rarely flowers solitary. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, white or pale yellow, fragrant, often bracteate; pedicels jointed. Calyx-lobes 4–10, toothlike or obsolete. Petals as many as calyx lobes, valvate, linear to lorate, sometimes connate at base. Stamens isomerous and alternate with petals or 2–4 times as many as petals, distinct; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk fleshy. Ovary inferior, 1–2-locular; ovule solitary, pendulous; style and stigma simple, or 2–4-lobed. Fruit a drupe, ellipsoidal, ovoid or subglobose. Seeds 1; embryo straight and large; endosperm copious. One genus and ca. 20 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs aquatic or marshy, sometimes laticiferous. Stems corm-like, rhizomatous, or stoloniferous. Leaves basal, emersed or floating, sessile or petiolate; petiole with sheathing base, sheath without auricles; blade linear, lanceolate, ovate or sagittate, margins entire or undulate, with parallel primary veins from base of blade to apex and reticulate secondary veins. Inflorescences scapose, mostly erect, racemose or paniculate; bracts whorled, linear. Flowers actinomorphous, hypogynous, bisexual, unisexual or polygamous. Sepals 3, green, persistent. Petals 3, caducous. Stamens 6-many, free; anthers 2-celled, basifixed or versatile. Gynoecium of 2–many free carpels, carpels in 1 whorl or irregularly spaced, each with 1(–2) anatropous ovules; placentation basal, rarely marginal; styles terminal or lateral, persistent, stigma linear. Fruit a cluster or whorls of laterally compressed achenes, or rarely follicles. Seeds 1–few, oblong or hippocrepiform; endosperm absent. About 11 genera and 75 species, cosmopolitan in distribution, but mainly in N hemisphere; four genera and 20 species in China; two genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, or trees, often succulent, usually with dense rosettes of very fleshy leaves at base (common) or apex (when woody). Stems often very reduced but sometimes well developed. Leaves small to very large, alternate, spiral or distichous, often rosulate, amplexicaul, thick, succulent, sessile. Inflorescence a subterminal, ascending to erect raceme, often branched; peduncle usually well developed; bracts well developed, persistent, scarious. Pedicel usually much shorter than perianth. Perianth segments 6, in 2 whorls, sepaloid and petaloid, or petaloid, usually connate to form a tube, very rarely nearly free. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth tube, usually exserted; anthers dorsifixed, dehiscing by longitudinal slits, introrse. Ovary 3-locular, superior, placentation axile; ovules many per locule. Style apical; stigma singular. Fruit a loculicidal capsule. Seeds endospermic, often winged, endosperm oily. Five genera and about 700 species distributed in Africa, Arabia and Madagascar; one genus and one species widely cultivated in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely subshrubs or climbers. Leaves simple, alternate or opposite, without stipules. Flowers small, bisexual, or rarely unisexual, normally regular, solitary or in axillary dichasial cymes and arranged in spike-like or head-like, usually bracteate inflorescence. Perianth-segments 3– 5, free or sometimes united at the base, usually scarious and colored. Stamens usually as many as perianth-segments and opposite them; filaments free or more often united at the base into a tube, sometimes with petaloid appendixes between the filaments. Ovary superior, comprising 2 or 3 fused carpels, 1-locular, with 1 to many ovules on a basal or free central placenta. Fruit an achene or a small nut, or a 1-seeded circumscissile capsule, rarely a berry, usually enclosed by the persistent perianth. About 71 genera and 800 species, cosmopolitan, but mainly in tropical and warm regions of the world; 15 genera about 40 species in China; six genera with 16 species, including some cultivated ones, in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, rarely woody climbers, hermaphroditic, polygamo-dioecious or dioecious, with vertical resin-ducts in bark. Leaves simple, trifoliate or imparipinnate, alternate, rarely opposite or whorled, exstipulate. Inflorescences thyrsoid, terminal or axillary. Flowers small, actinomorphic, bisexual to unisexual; pedicels often articulate. Sepals distinct or connate at base, imbricate or valvate, caducous or persistent. Petals (0–)3–7, distinct or rarely connate at base, sometimes adnate basally to receptacle, imbricate or valvate, deciduous or persistent. Stamens 5–10, in 1–2 whorls, one, several or all fertile, filaments distinct or rarely connate at base, anthers introrse, dorsi- or basifixed, 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Disk usually distinct, fleshy, complete or lobed. Carpels 1–5, connate, rarely distinct. Ovary superior, 1(–5)-locular, ovule 1 per locule; style 1–5, distinct or connate, stigma slightly enlarged. Fruit usually a drupe with ± resinous mesocarp, 1–5-locular; epicarp thin, mesocarp usually fleshy, fibrous and resinous, endocarp crustaceous to bony. Seeds usually without endosperm, cotyledons fleshy. About 77 genera and 600 species mainly distributed in tropical, subtropical and temperate regions of the world; 16 genera and 50 species in China; four genera and six species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or climbers, evergreen. Young branches glabrous, lepidote or with simple or stellate hairs. Leaves alternate, distichous, papery to leathery, glabrous or pubescent, entire, without stipules. Inflorescences terminal, axillary, leaf-opposed, extra- or supra-axillary, on young growth, ramiflorous or cauliflorous. Flowers solitary or in fascicles, bisexual or unisexual. Pedicels glabrous or pubescent; bracts often present, adnate to base or middle of pedicels. Sepals (2–)3(–4), valvate or imbricate in bud, free or connate at least basally. Petals 3 or 6, rarely more, in 1 or 2 whorls, valvate or imbricate in bud, variable in size and shape, fleshy to papery, free or ± connate. Stamens numerous, apparently spirally arranged; staminodes rarely present; anthers extrorse; connective conspicuous, dilated, liguliform or conical, glabrous or pubescent; filaments short. Carpels 1 to many per flower, free or connate, wholly fused or paracarpous; ovary glabrous or pubescent; ovules 1 to numerous, lateral or basal; style conspicuous or not; stigma capitate or clavate, sometimes 2-cleft and incurved, glabrous or hairy. Fruits apocarpous or syncarpous; monocarps 1 to many, globose, oblong, cylindrical or moniliform, subsessile or stipitate, glabrous or pubescent, indehiscent or rarely dehiscent. Seeds 1 to numerous per monocarp, round, ovoid, discoid, or lenticular; testa smooth or rugose; aril sometimes present; raphes present; endosperm abundant, ruminate. Approximately 128 genera and 2300 species, widespread in tropical and subtropical regions; 24 genera and 103 species in China; six genera and 12 species in Hong Kong. Polyalthia suberosa sensu Benth., non (Roxb.) Thw. was recorded by Dunn & Tutcher (FKH 30. 1912) but this record is doubtful. Key for flowering specimens Key for fruiting specimens

Perennial or annual herbs, rarely shrubs, usually with thick taproots; stems erect or creeping, or acaulescent. Leaves alternate, much dissected to divided or decompound; petioles frequently embracing young inflorescence with a dilated sheath-like base. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, in simple or compound umbels, sometimes capitate. Calyx 5-toothed or obsolete, forming a ring around the top of ovary. Petals 5, yellow, white, pink, purplish or violet, imbricate or valvate in buds. Stamens 5, opposite to petals, filaments filiform, incurved in bud. Ovary inferior, 2-locular, with an anatropous ovule in each locule; styles 2, usually swollen at the base forming a stylopodium which often secretes nectar. Fruit a schizocarp, bilocular, separating into 2 mericarps, these usually suspended from the top of the central column called carpophore, with 5 primary ribs and sometimes 4 intermediate or secondary ones; vittae (oil-tubes) often present in the furrow and on the commissure face, rarely also in the pericarp, sometime obscure; each mericarp 1– seeded, splitting apart at maturity. Seeds face plane, concave to sulcate, with abundant endosperm and a small embryo. About 200 genera and 3000 species widely distributed in the world; 100 genera and about 600 species in China; 16 genera, 18 species and 1 variety in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or vines, rarely subshrubs or herbs, with latex or rarely watery juice. Leaves simple, opposite, rarely whorled or alternate, pinnately‑veined; stipules absent or rarely present. Inflorescences cymose, terminal or axillary, with bracteoles. Flowers bisexual, (4–)5‑merous, actinomorphic. Calyx (4 )5‑partite, quincuncial, basal glands usually present. Corolla (4–)5‑lobed, salverform, funnelform, urceolate, or rarely rotate, lobes overlapping to right or left, rarely valvate. Stamens (4 –)5; filaments short; anthers mostly sagittate, free or connivent into a cone adherent to pistil head, dehiscing longitudinally, base rounded, cordate, sagittate, or prolonged into an empty spur; pollen granular; disk ring‑like or cup‑shaped, 2–5‑lobed, or absent. Ovary superior, rarely half‑inferior, connate or distinct,1‑ or 2‑locular; ovules (1or) 2‑numerous per locule. Style 1; pistil head capitate, conical, or lampshade‑shaped, base stigmatic, apex 2‑cleft and not stigmatic. Fruit a berry, drupe, capsule, or follicle. Seeds with or without coma; endosperm thick and often horny, scanty, sometimes absent; embryo straight or nearly so, cotyledons often large, radicle terete. About 155 genera and 2000 species distributed primarily in the tropics and subtropics, poorly represented in the temperate regions; 44 genera and 145 species in China; 19 genera and 23 species in Hong Kong. A majority of the species in this family is poisonous.

Perennial freshwater herbs with a tuberous-thickened rhizome. Leaves all basal, usually with a long petiole sheathing at base, and a floating blade with a few main parallel veins and many transverse secondary veins, or sometimes leaves wholly submersed and with a scarcely expanded blade. Inflorescences a simple or basally 2–10-forked spike on a long scape projected above water surface, in bud enveloped by a caducous or rarely persistent spathe. Flowers small, hypogynous, perfect or rarely unisexual (the plants then dioecious). Tepals (1–)2(–6), distinct, commonly persistent, often petaloid, or sometimes wanting. Stamens free and distinct, mostly 6 in 2 cycles, or sometimes more (up to 25) in 3–4 cycles; anthers 2-celled, 4-sporangiate and opening by longitudinal slits. Gynoecium of (2–)3–6(–9 or more) carpels, these basally and adaxially coherent for about half or two-thirds of their length, separating at maturity, each carpel narrowed to a short style with a ventral stigmatic groove; ovules 2–12 per ovary, basal or marginal. Fruit a distinct follicle with a mostly, lateral or terminal, often curved beak. Seeds without endosperm. One genus and ca. 45 species, confined to the Old World, predominantly the S hemisphere; one genus and one species in China and Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, evergreen, rarely deciduous. Leaves simple, alternate, minutely stipulate or estipulate. Flowers small, regular, unisexual, rarely bisexual or polygamous, dioecious, in cymes, umbels, racemes, panicles or fascicles, rarely solitary. Calyx 4–6-lobed; lobes imbricate. Petals 4–8, free or connate at base. Stamens as many as and alternate with petals; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, usually 4–8-locular. Fruit a berry or drupe, enclosing 2 or more 1-seeded kernels. About 450 species in four genera, with worldwide distribution; only the genus Ilex in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, sometimes epiphytic or aquatic, rhizomatous or tuberous. Leaves rarely solitary, alternate or clustered, usually petiolate with sheathing bases, blades various (e.g. linear), simple (base often cordate to sagittate), sometimes peltate or variously compound (e.g. pinnate, radiate, pedate); later veins parallel or pinnate or palmate-netted. Inflorescence a spadix, subtended by a spathe; spathe rarely absent, persistent (sometimes only proximally) or deciduous, variously coloured, commonly with tube-like base (margins fused or not) and deciduous limb (blade); spadix cylindrical or ovoid, various parts occasionally naked or with sterile flowers. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, male and female usually on the same plant or functionally on different plants, spadix female below and male above when unisexual; perianth absent or present; stamens 2–12, distinct or connate in synandria; ovary 1, 1–3(–many)-locular, sessile or embedded in spadix; styles 1; stigmas hemispheric, capitate, or discoid (sometimes strongly lobed). Fruits berries, distinct or connate at maturity. Seeds 1– many per berry. About 104 genera and ca. 3300 species distributed worldwide, but chiefly in tropical regions; 35 genera and 200 species in China; 12 genera and 18 indigenous species in Hong Kong. In recent years many Aroids have been introduced to Hong Kong for ornamental use, such as Caladium , Dieffenbachia , Monstera , Philodendron , Zantedeschia , but they are not treated in this flora.

Trees, shrubs, very rarely perennial herbs, sometimes climbers with aerial roots, prickly or not. Leaves alternate, petiolate, simple or compound; stipules present or absent. Inflorescence terminal, usually umbels, heads, spikes or racemes, solitary or racemosely, paniculately or umbellately rearranged. Bracts usually small and deciduous. Flowers regular, mostly small, bisexual, polygamous or dioecious. Calyx-tube adnate to the ovary, lobes small or reduced to a rim, or rarely absent. Petals 5–10, valvate or imbricate, usually free. Stamens 5–10, alternate with and inserted on the petals at the edge of the disk; anthers versatile, 2-celled, introrse, longitudinally dehiscent. Disk epigynous, fleshy, annular. Ovary inferior or half inferior, 1–15-locular, the styles as many as the locules, free or connate; ovules solitary, anatropous. Fruit baccate or drupaceous; seeds solitary in pyrenes, the embryo small, the endosperm uniform or ruminate. About 50 genera and more than 1350 species distributed in the tropic and temperate regions of both hemispheres; 22 genera and about 180 species in China; eight genera and ten species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, with resin in cortex. Branches verticillate; lateral branchlets in 2 series. Leaves spirally arranged or decussate, sessile, decurrent. Cones unisexual, dioecious or rarely monoecious. Pollen cones axillary or terminal on branchlets, solitary or clustered; microsporophylls numerous, spirally arranged, sessile; microsporangia 4 –20, suspended, arranged in 2 rows, filiform; pollen nonsaccate. Seed cones solitary, terminal on branchlets, ellilpsoid or subglobose; bracts numerous, spirally arranged; ovulate scales degenerate or ligulate, connate with bracts on one side, each with 1 ovule at base abaxially; ovules connate with ovulate scales or with bracts. Mature seed cones large, bracts woody or thickly leathery; seeds flattened, connate with bracts or detached. Three genera and 41 species: Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines; Australia, New Zealand, SW Pacific Islands, S America; two genera and four species (all introduced) in China; one genus and two species introduced into Hong Kong.

Evergreen, trees, shrubs or climbers, hermaphroditic, polygamous, monoecious or dioecious, usually with large leaves and inflorescences, armed with spines or unarmed. Stems solitary or clustered, rarely acaulescent, unbranched aerially. Leaves pinnate, palmate or costapalmate, reduplicate or induplicate; pinnae (in pinnate leaves) arranged regularly or in groups, sometimes not on same plane; segments (in palmate leaves) single or multiple-folded, splitting in various degree; rachis sometimes extending into spiny, whiplike climbing organ (cirrus) in climbing species; sheaths open, or closed and sometimes forming crownshafts, with knees and sometimes with flagella in climbing species; petioles short to elongate, with hastula at apex in palmate leaves. Inflorescences borne among or below leaves; peduncle bearing a prophyll and usually 1 or more peduncular bracts; rachis bearing conspicuous or much-reduced rachis bracts; usually multiple-branched; flowers small, bisexual or unisexual, usually 3-merous. Fruits yellow, orange, red, white, purple or black; epicarp smooth, hairy, spiny, or covered in imbricate scales, mesocarp fleshy, fibrous or dry. Seed usually 1, rarely 2–3–10, endosperm homogeneous or ruminate. About 183 genera and 2400 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, America, Africa and the Pacific islands; 18 genera and 70 species in China; 12 genera and 17 species in Hong Kong (including eight cultivated species). Glossary Cirrus (pl. cirri ) – a climbing organ, the apex of leaf rachis elongate to a long, whip-like structure with recurved spines, present in climbing palms, the rattans. Costapalmate – palmate but with a short midrib or costa. Crownshaft – a cylindrical structure formed by the closed, tubular leaf sheaths, wrapping the top of stem. Flagellum (pl. flagella ) – a climbing organ, a modified inflorescence, borne from sheath, elongate, whip-like, armed with recurved spines, present in climbing palms. Hastula – in palmate leaves, a flap of tissue borne at the apex of the petiole, where it joins the blade, usually on the upper surface, rarely on lower or both surface. Induplicate – of a pinna or segment, a fold V-shaped in cross-section. Knee – in climbing palms, a swollen part on leaf sheath, outboard at the base of the petiole. Peduncular bract – the second (and subsequent) bract(s) on an inflorescence main axis after the prophyll, empty. Prophyll – the first bract on an inflorescence main axis. Rachilla (pl. rachillae ) – the last branch of an inflorescence, bearing the flowers. Reduplicate – of a pinna or segment, a fold L-shaped in cross-section.

Lianas, subshrubs, or herbs. Leaves simple, alternate, petiolate; stipules absent. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, cymose, or corymbose, or flowers solitary. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic or actinomorphic. Perianth usually with 1 petaloid whorl (in Saruma with 2 whorls: outer one sepaloid, inner one petaloid), mostly connate into distinct tube, cylindric to campanulate or subglobose; limb rotate, urceolate, cylindric, or ligulate, 1–3-lobed; lobes valvate. Stamens 6–many, in 1 or 2 series; filaments short and thick; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary inferior to superior, 6-locular; carpels connate only at base or fully fused; ovules numerous, usually in 1 or 2 series on parietal placenta. Styles free or connate, column 3- or 6-lobed. Fruit a fleshy or dry capsule. Seeds many; testa somewhat hard or crustaceous; endosperm copious, fleshy; embryo minute. About eight genera and 450–600 species, mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; four genera and 86 species in China; two genera and six species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, climbers or shrubs, rarely treelike, with milky or, less often, clear latex. Leaves simple, opposite or occasionally whorled, very rarely alternate, usually without obvious stipules, margin nearly always entire. Inflorescences terminal, axillary, or extra‑axillary, cymose, often condensed and ± umbel‑like, occasionally raceme‑like. Flowers bisexual, 5‑merous, usually regular. Sepals joined at base only, often with 5 or more basal glands. Corolla sympetalous, reflexed to urn ‑shaped or salverform; lobes valvate or overlapping in bud to right or left. Corona usually present, inserted on corolla, on stamens, or on both. Stamens 5, usually inserted at base of corolla‑tube and adhering to stigma head forming gynostegium; filaments usually connate into a tube enclosing ovaries; anthers 2‑celled, each often with membranous apical appendage; pollen tetrads contained loosely on a spathulate translator with a basal corpusculum (Periplocoideae), or pollen united into waxy pollinia, each attached through a caudicle (stalk) to the retinaculum (gland) between adjacent anthers. Ovaries 2, free, superior; ovules numerous; styles connate; stigma with fleshy head. Fruits of 1 or 2 follicles. Seeds numerous, strongly compressed, with a coma (a prominent basal tuft of silky hairs). About 250 genera and over 2000 species widespread in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in Africa and southern S America, with a moderate representation in N and SE Asia; 44 genera and 271 species in China; 15 genera and 20 species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs, or shrubs, rarely tree, sometimes milky. Leaves alternate or opposite, sometimes rosulate, scattered, or seldom whorled, simple, toothed to pinnately lobed or divided, estipulate. Flowers aggregated into a capitulum, growing on a common receptacle. Receptacle with various shapes, naked, scariously toothed, hairy, or paleaceous, surrounded by an involucre consisting of 1–many series of phyllaries (involucral bracts). Capitula solitary or arranged into racemose, cymose, corymbose, or paniculate clusters. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, rarely neutral; hypanthium adnate to the ovary wall; calyx modified into a pappus of bristles, awns, scales, teeth, or absent; corolla zygomorphic and ligulate with 2–5 teeth at limb apex, or actinomorphic and tubular with 4–5 lobes at apex. Stamens (4–)5; filaments free and inserted on the corolla tube, seldom united; anthers 2‑thecae, coherent and forming a tube surrounding the style, usually bearing apical appendages, base obtuse, acute, sagittate, caudate, or tasselled. Pistil 1; ovary inferior, unilocular, 1‑ovuled; style 2‑branched, the branches separate or connate, with or without appendages. Fruit a cypsela (an achene surrounded by hypanthium), containing a single erect anatropous seed, no endosperm.

A large, cosmopolitan family of flowering plants, with 1000 to 1500 genera and about 25000 to 30000 species in the world; 12 tribes, 76 genera, and about 137 species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial succulent herbs, monoecious or dioecious, parasitic on roots or rhizomes of hosts, without chlorophyll. Rhizome tuberous, single or branched. Leaves alternate, opposite or whorled, scale-like. Inflorescences a spadix, unisexual or androgynous, terminal, often fungoid in appearance, often arising endogenously from the tuber. Flowers unisexual, pedicellate or sessile. Male flowers: larger than female flowers, interspersed among female ones or at the end of spadix, 3(or 4 or more)-merous. Perianth wanting or 3–8-lobed; lobes valvate; stamens 1 or 2 when perianth absent or usually as many as and opposite to perianth-lobes when perianth present; filaments free or connate into a synandrium; anthers 2–4-celled or more, dehiscing by slits or pores. Female flowers: sessile, minute, densely arranged on branches or basally on spadicles and/or shoot axis; perianth absent or reduced, adnate to ovary; ovary inferior, 1–3-locular; ovule solitary in each locule, mostly pendulous, nude or with a single integument; styles 1–2; stigmas discoid. Fruit a 1-seeded achene. Seeds globose, endosperm copious, oily, embryo very small. About 18 genera and 50 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; two genera and 13 species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems watery, translucent or colored. Leaves simple, alternate, opposite or whorled, usually without stipules. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, solitary or in axillary umbelliform cymes, upside down hanging on the pedicels. Sepals usually 3, the 2 lateral small or aborted, the posterior one large, petaloid and often saccate, produced backward into a slender spur-nectary. Petals 5, unequal, the posterior free, flat or saccate, often bifid or emarginate, the 4 lower ones distinct or connate in 2 lateral pairs. Stamens 5, alternate with petals, with short and flat filaments; anthers introrse, ± united to form a cap over the ovary. Ovary superior, 5-locular, with numerous ovules on axile placentas. Fruit a capsule or rarely a berry. Two genera with about 900 species distributed throughout temperate and tropical Eurasia, Africa, C and N America; two genera about 220 species in China; one genus and three species (2 cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous climbing vines, more or less fleshy, often with tuberous rootstocks. Leaves alternate, simple, entire, usually petioled, exstipulate. Flowers bisexual, rarely functionally unisexual, usually small, supported by a pair of bracts, arranged in spikes or racemes in axils of leaves. Perianth-segments 5, united or almost separate. Stamens 5, opposite the perianth-segments and adnate to its base. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with a solitary ovule; styles usually 3, with entire or cleft stigmas. Fruit a drupe, usually enclosed within the persistent fleshy perianth. About four genera and 15 species in tropical and warm areas, especially in tropical America; two genera (introduced) in China, one in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, more or less succulent, often with thick rhizomes or tubers. Stems erect or decumbent, or sometimes acaulescent. Leaves alternate or basal, entire or irregularly toothed or lobed, usually asymmetrical. Stipules 2, usually membranous and deciduous. Inflorescence usually a dichasial cyme, bearing separate male and female flowers. Male flowers: perianth-segments 2–10; stamens many, free or united at the base; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits; female flowers: perianth-segments 2–8; ovary inferior, usually angled or winged, 2–3(4– 6)-locular, with axile placentation and many ovules, rarely 1-locular and with parietal placentation; styles 2–3, rarely 4– 6, free or united at the base; stigmas usually twisted. Fruit a fleshy capsule often winged. Five genera and about more than 1000 species, widely distributed in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world and especially abundant in C and S America; one genus and 160 species (endemic) in China; five species (one introduced) in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or perennial herbs. Leaves alternate or radical, simple, pinnately or ternately compound, with or without stipules. Flowers bisexual, solitary, clustered or arranged in cymose, racemose or paniculate inflorescence; sepals and petals similar, in 2 to many series, imbricate or the outer ones valvate, usually caducous; stamens 6, opposite to petals; anthers 2-celled, usually opening by 2 valves; ovary superior, 1-locular, with a few to many ovules; style very short or none; stigma capitate or dilated and peltate. Fruit a berry or a capsule. About 15 genera and 570 species widespread especially in N temperate regions; 11 genera about 200 species in China; two genera (one cultivated) and two species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or vines, rarely herbs, often with various tendrils and aerial roots. Leaves opposite, alternate, or whorled, simple or pinnately compound, rarely palmately compound, exstipulate, climbers usually with tendrils modified sometimes into hooks or suckers. Inflorescences cymose, paniculate, or racemose, terminal or axillary, rarely flowers borne on old stems. Bracts and bractlets present, sometimes deciduous. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, usually large. Calyx campanulate or tubular, truncate, 2–5‑dentate, or glandular subulate‑dentate. Corolla campanulate or funnelform, usually bilabiate; lobes 5, imbricate or valvate. Stamens 5, usually 2 or 4, rarely all 5 fertile, inserted on corolla‑tube, alternate to lobes, included or exserted; filaments filiform, often slightly enlarged at base, hairy; anthers 2‑celled, splitting by longitudinal slits. Disk fleshy, annular or cupular. Ovary superior, (1–)2(–4)‑locular; placentation axile or parietal; ovules many. Style filiform; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule dehiscing loculicidally or septicidally, rarely fruit fleshy and indehiscent. Seeds many, usually winged or with tufts of hairs at both ends; endosperm absent. About 112 genera and 725 species mostly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 12 genera and 35 species (21 endemic) in China; nine genera and nine species are commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. Indeed, the family is known for spectacular ornamental species. Catalpa speciosa (Warder ex Barney) Engelm. (黃金樹), Clytostoma callistegioides (Cham.) Baill. (連理藤), Macfadyena unguis‑cati (L.) A. H. Gentry (貓爪藤), Pandorea ricasoliana (Tanfani) Baill. ex K. Schum. (非洲凌霄), Radermachera sinica (Hance) Hemsl. (菜豆樹), Tabebuia argentea (Bureau & K. Schum.) Britton (銀鱗金鈴木), Tabebuia heterophylla (DC.) Britton (異葉黃鐘木), Tecoma capensis (Thunb.) Lindl. (硬骨凌霄) were cultivated previously or occasionally in local parks and gardens.

Shrubs or small trees, with red or orange juice. Leaves simple, alternate, entire, long petiolate, palmately veined; stipules small, usually caducous. Inflorescence a terminal thyrse. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic. Sepal 5, distinct, imbricate, contorted. Petals 5, distinct, large and conspicuous, imbricate; Stamens many, distinct or slightly united at base, anthers dehiscing by short slits or pores; Ovary superior, 1-locular; ovules many per parietal placenta; style slender, stigmas bilobed. Capsule spiny, bivalved. Seeds many, obovoid, testa fleshy, red; endosperm copious; embryo large, cotyledon broad, incurved at apex. One genus and one species, native to tropical America, widely cultivated in tropical regions; also cultivated in China including Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees, trunk usually with buttresses at base. Leaves alternate, palmately compound or simple, usually with scales. Stipules caducous. Flowers bisexual, large and showy, actinomorphic, axillary or nearly terminal, solitary or fascicled. Calyx cup-shaped, apex truncate or irregularly 3 – 5-lobed. Petals 5, rarely absent, imbricate, rarely connate with staminal tube at base. Stamens 5 to numerous, staminodes usually present; filaments distinct or connate into a staminal tube, anthers reniform to linear, 1- or 2-celled. Ovary superior, 2–5-locular, each locule with 2 to many anatropous ovules on axile placenta. Style unlobed or 2–5-lobed. Capsule loculicidally dehiscent or indehiscent. Seeds usually enclosed by wooly hairs. About 30 genera and 180 species, widely in tropics especially tropical America; six genera (one native) and eight species (three native) in China; three genera and three species are cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs, or trees, rarely lianas, usually bristly or scabrous‑pubescent. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, exstipulate. Inflorescences often double scorpioid cymes, rarely solitary; bracts present or absent. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic. Calyx usually 5‑parted or lobed, mostly persistent. Corolla tubular, campanulate, rotate, funnelform, or salverform; tube appendages 5, rarely more; limb (4–)5(–8)‑parted; lobes overlapping, rarely twisted in bud. Stamens 5, inserted on corolla tube or rarely at throat, alternate with corolla‑lobe; anthers introrse, 2‑celled, dehiscence longitudinal. Disk present or absent. Ovary superior, 2‑ or 4‑locular; ovules 1 or 2 per locule. Style terminal or gynobasic, branched or not. Fruit 1–4‑seeded drupes or nutlets (mericarps). Seeds vertical or oblique, coat membranous; embryo straight, less often curved; cotyledons flat, fleshy. About 156 genera and 2500 species distributed in temperate and tropical regions; 47 genera and 294 species in China; six genera and seven species in Hong Kong. Borago officinalis L. (玻璃苣) is occasionally cultivated as an ornamental.

Herbs, often with pungent juice. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, usually simple, entire to pinnately dissected, rarely pinnate, estipulate. Inflorescence usually a terminal raceme. Flowers bisexual, usually regular. Sepals 4, decussate, free, not saccate or lateral (inner) pair saccate. Petals 4, imbricate or convolute, usually clawed, free, alternated with sepals, rarely reduced. Stamens 6, tetradynamous, inner 2 short, outer 4 longer, anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, with 2 locules separated by a thin replum connecting 2 partietal placentas, each with one or more ovules in 1–3 rows; nectars rich of hexose. Fruit a silique or silicle, dehiscing into 2 valves or indehiscent. Seeds small, without albumen, embryo much curved, cotyledons either accumbent or incumbent. About 330 genera, 3500 species widely distributed in the world, especially temperate regions; 102 genera and 412 species in China; eight genera, 14 species (one represented by fire varieties) in Hong Kong.

Herbs or rarely shrubs, epiphytic, lithophytic, or terrestrial. Leaves spirally arranged, usually rosulate, sessile, simple, veins parallel, base dilated, sheathing, margin often spinose serrate or sometimes entire. Inflorescences terminal or lateral, scapose or sessile, a panicle, raceme, spike, or head, sometimes reduced to solitary, pseudolateral flowers. Bracts usually brightly coloured and conspicuous. Flowers bisexual or sometimes functionally unisexual, 3-merous. Sepals and petals each 3, distinct, free or basally connate; petals often brightly coloured, basal margin with a pair of scale-like appendages. Stamens 6, in 2 whorls of 3; filaments free, connate, or collectively or individually adnate to petals; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Gynoecium of 3 carpels united to form a compound, 3-locular, superior or very often partly or wholly inferior ovary; ovules few to usually ± many in each locule; placentation axile; styles terminal and often 3-parted; stigmas papillose. Berry or septicidal capsules often or seldom compound and fleshy. Seeds usually winged or plumose; endosperm mealy; embryo small to fairly large. About 50 genera and 2000–2600 species, mainly in tropical America; about ten genera and 30 species introduced in China; five genera, six species and one variety introduced in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, seldom herbs, often lepidote, with stellate, branching or glandular hairs. Leaves simple, opposite or less often whorled, rarely alternate, entire or more often toothed or lobed, interpetiolar stipules commonly represented by a mere line, seldom well developed. Inflorescence a cyme, rearranged in racemes, spikes or panicles. Flowers perfect or often functionally dioecious. Calyx 4(–5)‑lobed, or sometimes very deeply lobed. Corolla 4(–5)‑lobed, lobes imbricate or rarely valvate. Stamens 4(–5), attached to corolla‑tube and alternate with the lobes (posterior one absent or represented by a small staminode). Anthers 2‑celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior or half‑inferior, 2(–4)‑locular; style solitary, with 2‑lobed stigma; ovules numerous, borne on thickened axile placentas. Fruit septicidal capsule, rarely berry. Seeds often winged; endosperm oily. Eight genera, 120 species distributed in tropical and warm regions; one genus, 29 species in China; one genus, two species in Hong Kong.

Small myco- or autotrophic, annual or perennial herbs, often growing from rhizomes or tubers. Leaves simple, exstipulate, usually alternate, lamina entire; autotrophic species with basal rosette of linear or lanceolate green leaves; mycotrophic species with colourless to yellowish or reddish, scale-like leaves. Flowers bisexual, usually actinomorphic, solitary or in terminal cymes or racemes; perianth (3–)6-lobed, corolline, tubular or campanulate; tube occasionally 3-angled or 3-winged; outer perianth parts (sepals) valvate; inner perianth parts (petals) generally smaller, induplicate-valvate, occasionally absent; 3 or all 6 of the perianth-lobes often each with an elongate, slender, terminal appendage; stamens 3 or 6, if 3, then subsessile in the perianth throat, with anther dehiscence by horizontal slits, if 6, then pendent in perianth tube, with anther dehiscence by longitudinal slits; connectives large, often appendiculate; ovary inferior, 1-loculate with parietal placentation, or 3-loculate with axile placentation; ovules many, anatropous, bitegmic; style filiform, shortly cylindrical or conical; stigmas 3, sometimes connate. Fruit capsular, occasionally fleshy, with either persistent perianth tube and style or persistent basal ring of perianth only, dehiscence irregular or by transverse ventral slits. Seeds small, subglobose to linear, many, sometimes with a loose reticulate testa; endosperm present. Approximately 21 genera and 165 species, widespread in tropical and subtropical regions; three genera and 12 species in China; two genera and six species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, bark with prominent resin ducts. Leaves odd-pinnate or trifoliolate, very rarely unifoliolate, alternate, very rarely opposite, exstipulate or rarely stipulate. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate or capitate. Flowers regular, small, hermaphrodite or often polygamous. Calyx usually connate at base, (3–)4–5-lobed; lobes imbricate or valvate. Petals (3–)4–5, rarely 0, distinct, rarely connate, imbricate or valvate. Disk annular or cupular. Stamens as many as or twice as many as petals, inserted at base or margin of disk; filaments free, rarely connate at base; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary superior, rarely perigynous, 1–5-locular, ovules 1–2 per locule; placentation axile; style simple, stigma undivided or 2–5-lobed. Fruit a drupe, indehiscent, rarely a pseudo-capsule and dehiscent. Seeds 1–3, endosperm wanting, embryo straight or curved. About 16 genera and 550 species distributed in tropical regions of the world; three genera and 13 species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs, rarely small trees or herbs. Leaves simple, opposite or alternate, usually leathery, without stipules. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious or rarely dioecious), apetalous, in axillary or terminal racemes or spikes. Male flowers: sepals 4, in 2 series; stamens 4, free, opposite to the sepals; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by valves or longitudinal slits. Female flowers: sepals usually 6, or rarely 4, imbricate; ovary superior, usually 3-locular, rarely 2 – 4-locular, with 1 – 2 ovules on axile placenta in each locule; styles free or connate at the base. Fruit a capsule or a drupe. Four genera about 100 species in temperate, subtropical and tropical regions; three genera about 28 species in China; two genera, four species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Perennial succulent plants. Stems cylindric, globular or flattened, and often constricted or jointed, succulent or woody at base, with areoles (oval or circular areas) bearing spines and glochids (barbed spines or bristles). Leaves usually none or much reduced, and mostly caducous, rarely flat and fleshy. Flowers usually bisexual, regular or irregular, solitary or clustered, arising from areoles; perianthsegments many, sharply or not differentiated into sepals and petals; stamens many, sometimes clustered; ovary 1-locular, inferior, rarely half-inferior or superior, with 2 or more parietal placenta and many ovules. Fruit a berry, often spiny or bristly. About 130 genera and 1650 species mainly in semi-desert regions of N, C and S America; about 65 genera (mostly cultivated) in China; four genera and four species are commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, sometimes vines, rarely herbs, unarmed or armed with sharp prickles. Leaves alternate, pinnate or bipinnate or 1-foliolate, rarely simple; stipules mostly caducous, stipules present or absent. Flowers mostly bisexual, rarely unisexual, zygomorphic, rarely actinomorphic, usually 5-merous. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate, rarely spicate, terminal or rarely leaf-opposed. Bracts small or calyx-like. Sepals 5, or 4 by the union of 2, free or partly united, imbricate or rarely valvate. Petals 5, rarely 4 or absent, the uppermost (adaxial) one covered by the neighbouring 2 petals. Stamens 10, or fewer, rarely many, filaments free to variously connate; anthers 2-celled, usually dehiscing lengthwise, rarely by apical pores. Disk sometimes present. Ovary stipitate or sessile, free or ± adnate to the hypanthium; styles single, undivided; ovules superposed, 1–many. Fruit a legume, 2-valved, or indehiscent. Seeds sometimes arillate, endosperm often wanting; cotyledons fleshy or foliaceous. About 153 genera and 2800 species mostly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, some expanding to temperate regions; 21 genera and about 110 species in China; 11 genera, 31 species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Annual submerged, amphibious, or terrestrial herbs. Stem slender, many‑branched, usually rooted at nodes. Leaves simple, opposite, decussate, exstipulate, blade obovate, linear or spatulate, notched at apex, margin entire or very rarely toothed, somewhat congested towards apex of stems reaching water surface. Plants monoecious, or rarely dioecious. Flowers imperfect, minute, solitary, axillary, unisexual; male in axil of upper part of branches and female in axil of lower part of branches, sometimes in same axil. Bracts 2, membranous, white. Perianth absent. Male flowers: stamen 1, filament slender, anther small, 2‑celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Female flowers: ovary sessile, bicarpellate, 4‑locular; stigmas 2, erect or reflexed, papillate. Fruit schizocarps, separating into 4 nutlets; nutlets dry, winged or not. One genus and ca. 75 species widely distributed worldwide; eight species (one endemic) in China; one species (including two varieties) in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen shrubs, with aromatic bark; buds scaly or naked. Leaves opposite, short-petioled, entire, penninerved, exstipulate. Flowers bisexsual, actinomorphic, solitary, short-stalked, perigynous. Tepals numerous, spirally arranged, not differentiated into sepals and petals. Staments 5 –30, spirally arranged; filaments very short; anthers extrorse, 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Carpels numerous, free, inserted inside of a hollow receptacle with the styles protruding, 1–2-ovuled, developing into one-seeded achenes enclosed by the urn-shaped receptacle. Seeds without endosperm; cotyledons spirally rolled. Two genera with about seven species in E Asia and N America; two genera and six species in China; one genus and one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Mostly perennial herbs, with milky latex. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite or whorled, without stipules. Flowers perfect or rarely imperfect, solitary or clustered, or more often in terminal spike, racemes, or leafy panicles. Calyx‑tube adnate to the ovary; lobes 3–10, usually 5, persistent. Corolla regular or irregular; lobes 3–10, usually 5, valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as the corolla‑lobes and alternate with them, hypogynous and free from the corolla‑tube, or very rarely united to it at the base; anthers opening longitudinally, or united in a ring round the style. Ovary inferior or half‑inferior, 2–5(–6)‑locular, with axile placentation and numerous ovules in each locule; style simple, entire or 2–5(–6)‑lobed. Fruit usually a capsule, opening either in short valves at the top or in lateral pores or slits, rarely an indehiscent berry. About 80 genera and over 2000 species, cosmopolitan but most abundant in the temperate regions of the N hemisphere or of S Africa; 15 genera and about 170 species in China; seven genera and ten species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, dioecious, rarely monoecious. Stipules persistent. Leaves simple, alternate or opposite, entire, palmately lobed or compound. Inflorescence a paniculate (♂) or spicate (♀) cyme, axillary. Male flowers: sepals 5; petals absent; stamens 5; filaments short; anther 2-celled, opening by short slits. Female flowers: calyx appressed to ovary, membranous, entire; petals absent; ovary sessile, 1-locular; style 2-parted, branches filiform; ovules solitary, pendulous, anatropous. Fruit an achene covered by persistent calyx. Seeds with fleshy endosperm and involute or curved embryo. Two genera, four species distributed in N temperate regions; two genera and three species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect, robust, Rhizomes tuberous. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, large, veins pinnate and parallel, base sheathing. Inflorescense a terminal raceme or panicle of showy, 1–2-flowered cincinni. Flowers bisexual, asymmetric, mostly large. Sepals 3, green, free, persistent. Corolla lobes 3, green or coloured, basally connate into a tube and adnate to staminodes. Staminodes and stamen in 2 whorls; outer whorls with (2–)3 conspicuous, petaloid staminodes, usually red or yellow; inner whorl with a reflexed staminode (labellum), narrower than outer staminodes, and a fertile stamen; filaments petaloid; anther 1-celled, adnate to apical margin of filament. Ovary inferior, 3-locular; ovules many per locule; placentation axile. Style petaloid. Capsule 3-valved, usually warty. Seeds many, globose; endosperm copious; embryo straight. One genus and 10–20 species distributed in tropical and subtropical America; several species and hybrids cultivated in China; two species and one hybrid commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs, or climbers, rarely trees. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple or digitately compound; stipules usually none, rarely spiniform or small. Flowers usually in terminal racemes or corymbs, or occasionally solitary and axillary, bisexual or rarely unisexual, regular or often somewhat irregular. Receptacle often prolonged into a gynophone or androgynophore, bearing the gynoecium and androecium. Sepals 4 – 8, free or united below. Petals 4, rarely 8 or wanting, mostly free and alternate with the sepals, with or without a basal claw. Stamens 4 to many; filaments free; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with parietal placentas; style single, often very short or almost none; stigma capitate or bilobed. Fruit a capsule or a berry. About 45 genera more than 1000 species found chiefly within the tropics, a few species stretching northward into temperate regions; five genera and about 42 species in China; three genera and nine species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, less often lianas or herbs. Wood mostly rather soft and often with very broad pith. Stipules absent or small. Leaves opposite, very rarely alternate, simple or imparipinnately divided, rarely ternatisect, sometimes connate at base. Inflorescence a cyme, arranged in corymb or panicle. Flowers bisexual or rarely polygamous, actinomorphic. Calyx 3–5‑lobed, small; lobes imbricate or open in bud, accrescent in fruit; tube adnate to ovary. Corolla gamopetalous, rotate, campanulate, tubiform or infundibular, 4–5‑lobead; lobes imbricate or valvate, sometimes 2‑lipped; tube sometimes saccate at base. Stamens (2 or 4–)5, attached to corolla‑tube, alternate with lobes. Anthers 2‑celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary inferior, (1–)2 – 5(or 8)‑locular, with axile placenta; ovules 1–many in each locule; styles terminal or stigma sessile. Berry, capsule, achene or drupe. Seeds often with bony testa, small straight embryo and oily, fleshy endosperm. About 13 genera, 500 species mainly distributed in N temperate and tropical mountain area, especially NE Asia and N America; 12 genera and more than 200 species in China; four genera and 11 species in Hong Kong.

Soft-stemmed shrubs or small trees, often with an unbranched trunk and a terminal cluster of leaves, lactiferous. Leaves alternate, palmately lobed, long petioled; stipules absent or rarely present and spine-like. Flowers unisexual (monoecious or dioecious) or sometimes bisexual, in cymose, axillary inflorescences, or sometimes solitary in axils of leaves. Male flowers: sessile, in pendulous panicles; calyx 5-lobed; corolla-tube tubular, 5-lobed; stamens 10, in 2 whorls, inserted on corolla-tube, filaments distinct or connate at base, anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent; pistillodes present or absent. Female flowers: solitary or in corymbs; calyx as in male flowers; corolla-tube shorter than male ones, lobes adnate at first and distinct later; ovary superior, 1-locular or 5-locular with septum, ovules many, styles 5, very short or nearly absent, stigmas branched or not. Bisexual flowers: corolla-tube very short or long; stamens 5 –10. Fruit a fleshy berry, large; embryo straight; endosperm fleshy. Four genera and ca. 33 species distributed in tropical America and Africa; one species introduced to China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubby. Stems usually tumid at nodes. Leaves simple, opposite, rarely alternate or verticillate, entire, more or less connate at base. Stipules none, or small and scarious. Flowers actinomorphic, bisexual, rarely unisexual, usually in dichotomous panicles or leafy cymes. Sepals 5, rarely 4, herbaceous or scarious, persistent. Petals as many, contorted in bud, entire or lobed. Stamens free, twice as many as petals and in 2 whorls, rarely fewer. Ovary 1-locular, very rarely divided into imperfect locule; ovules several to many borne on a free central placenta; styles or style-branches 2– 5, stigmatic along their whole length. Fruit a capsule, opening at the top into as many or twice as many teeth or valves as styles. About 75– 80 genera and 2000 species, widespread worldwide, but mostly in temperate regions, especially in the N hemisphere; about 30 genera and 390 species in China; eight genera and nine species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, monoecious or dioecious. Ultimate branchlets jointed, with several short, basal internodes and 1–numerous elongated internodess, slender, ridged, often pubescent at least when young. Leaves small, tooth-like, in whorls of 4 –17; stipules absent. Inflorescences spike-like or head-like, with alternating whorls of tooth-like bracts, in each bract with a single flower and 2 lateral scalelike, persistent (rarely deciduous in male Allocasuarina) bracteoles. Flowers unisexual, without pedicels. Male inflorescences spicate, terminal or lateral, terete, slender. Female inflorescences head-like, globose or ellipsoid, usually terminal on short, lateral branches. Male flowers: tepals 1 or 2, scale-like, deciduous, hooded; stamen 1. Female flowers: perianth absent; carpels 2, fused, only the anterior carpel fertile; ovules 2 (rarely 4). Infructescences woody, cone-like. Samaras flat, winged at apex, initially enclosed by 2 bracteoles. Seed 1; cotyledons large; endosperm absent; embryo straight. Four genera and 97 species, mainly in Australia, extending to SE Asia, Malesia, Pacific Islands; a few species commonly cultivated and occasionally naturalized elsewhere; one genus and three species introduced to China; one genus and two species introduced to Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, erect, scandent or procumbent. Stipules small, usually deciduous or absent. Leaves simple, opposite or alternate, rarely verticillate. Inflorescence a cyme or thyrse, axillary or terminal, or flower fasciculate to solitary. Bracts and bracteoles small. Flowers small, bisexual, unisexual or polygamous (plant monoecious or dioecious), sepals 4–5; petals 4–5, free, rarly medially connate; dark fleshy or membranous, intrastaminal or extrastaminal. Stamens (2–)3–5, rarely numerous, inserted on disk or under disk, staminodes present or absent in female flowers. Anthers (1–)2-celled, basifixed to dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscing. Ovary superior to half-inferior, often partially immersed in disk, 1–5-locular, ovules 1–12(–numerous) per locule; styles terminal, short to 0, stigma simple or lobed. Fruit a capsule, drupe, berry or samara. Seeds usually arillate, rarely exarillate, with or without endosperm. About 98 genera, 1211 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, fewer in temperate regions; 15 genera, 214 species in China; four genera and 14 species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, dioecious; bud scales persistent. Leaves 2-ranked, decussate or more or less opposite, sessile or subsessile, basally somewhat twisted; blade linear, linear-lanceolate, or occasionally lanceolate, margin entire, stomatal bands 2, abaxial, white, as wide as or usually wider than midvein, resin canal abaxial. Pollen cones borne on branches of previous year, aggregated into capitula of 6–8; capitula axillary, solitary, pedunculate or subsessile; peduncle usually with several spirally arranged scales, rarely naked; cones subtended by 1 ovate or triangular-ovate bract; microsporophylls 7–12, each with 2–3 or more pollen sacs; pollen nonsaccate, globose. Seed cones in axils of terminal bud scales, 1–6(–8) per bud, long pedunculate; floral axis with several pairs of decussate bracts each bearing 2 erect, axillary ovules. Seeds ripening in 2nd year, drupelike, completely enclosed by succulent aril, ovoid, ellipsoid, or globose, apex mucronate. Cotyledons 2. Two genera and ca. 12 species, distributed from Himalayas to Japan and Thailand; two genera and seven species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Submerged rootless perennial herbs. Leaves rather stiff, 4–12 in whorls, forked, with linear toothed segments, without stipules. Flowers minute, unixesual (plants monoecious), subsessile, solitary in axils of leaves, but male and female in separarte leaf-whorls. Bracts (explained by some authors as petals) 8–12, linear, with colored hairs at apex. Stamens usually 10 –20 in male flowers; filaments very short; anthers extrorse, opening longitudinally; connectives thickened, usually bilobed. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with a solitary orthotropous ovule. Fruit an achene, ovoid or ellipsoid, with 3 spines. A monotypic family with about seven species widely spread over the world.

Annual or perennial herbs, or shrubs, rarely small trees, monoecious or dioecious. Stem often fleshy or jointed. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, sometimes leafless; usually exstipulate. Inflorescence a spike, panicle or cyme, 1–many-flowered, axillary or terminal. Flower small, actinomorphic, often green, bisexual or unisexual, rarely polygamous; perianth 3 – 5 in a series, free or connate or absent, persistent; Stamens usually as many as and opposite perianth-lobes, filaments free or connate at base, adnate to perianth-lobes or on annular disc. Anthers dehiscent by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 1-locular; ovules 4, basal; styles short; stigmas 2– 5, linear. Utricles often subtended by persistent perianth or bracteoles, indehiscent or rarely circumscissile. Seed 1, embryo annular or spirally twisted or only slightly curved, endosperm much reduced or absent, perisperm abundant or absent. About 100 genera, 400 species distributed in temperate to tropical regions of the world; 42 genera and 190 species in China; six genera, seven species, one subspecies and one variety in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, small trees, or perennial herbs. Leaves simple; stipules small; petioles usually connate at base; leaf blade pinnately veined, margin serrate or crenate. Flowers small, bisexual or unisexual, arranged in spikes, capitula, or panicles; perianth present in female flowers or absent. Bisexual flowers: stamens 1 or 3, on one side of ovary; filaments inconspicuous; connectives developed, if stamens 3, connectives connate at base or free; anthers 1- or 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; ovule 1, pendulous, orthotropous; style short or absent. Unisexual flowers: male flowers many, stamen 1; female flowers few; perianth 3-toothed, calyx-like, connate to ovary. Drupes ovoid or globose; exocarp ± fleshy; endocarp hard. Seeds containing rich endosperm and tiny embryo. Five genera, ca. 70 species, distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; three genera and 15 species occur in China; two genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, lianas or herbs with yellow or otherwise brightly coloured resinous juice. Stipules absent. Leaves simple, usually opposite or whorled, entire, leathery or thick, often with pellucid dots. Cymes terminal, rarely flowers solitary. Bracteoles present. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, regular. Sepals (2–)4 – 5(–6), rarely more, imbricate in pairs. Petals (2–)4– 5(–6) or more, imbricate or convolute. Stamens many, free or grouped into (2–)4–5 bundles. Ovary superior, (1–)3– 5(–20)-locular, placentation axile, rarely parietal on intruded placentas, with 1–many ovules per locule; styles as many as locules, or 1 style with lobed or peltate stigma. Fruit a drupe, berry or capsule. Seeds often arillate, embryo straight or curved, endosperm absent. About 45 genera, 1370 species distributed in tropical and temperate regions of the world; eight genera and 87 species in China; four genera and seven species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, often scandent. Leaves simple, opposite or alternate, rarely whorled, entire, rarely serrate, petiolate, exstipulate, leaf base often with 2 gland-containing flask-shaped cavities. Inflorescence capitate, spicate, racemose or paniculate. Flowers often bisexual, actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic. Calyx lobes 4–5(–8), valvate, persistent or deciduous. Petals 4–5 or absent, imbricate or valvate. Stamens often twice as many as calyx lobes, in 2 whorls, outer whorls sometimes reduced, rarely in pairs or triplets, anthers versatile with longitudinal slits. Disk epigynous. Ovary inferior, 1-locular, with 2–6 anatropous ovules; style 1; stigma capitate or inconspicuous. Fruit 1-seeded, usually indehiscent or drupaceous, often ribbed. Seeds without endosperm, embryo oily with 2 (or 3) folded or spirally twisted cotyledons. About 20 genera and 500 species distributed in tropical and subtropical areas of the world; six genera and 25 species in China; four genera and seven species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, often creeping at the base. Leaves alternate, distichous or spirally arranged, parallel-veined, with sheathing petioles. Inflorescence usually of cincinni in panicles or solitary, sometimes shortened into heads, terminal or issuing from the leaf sheath. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, usually slightly irregular. Sepals 3, free or connate only at base, often boat-shaped or carinate, sometimes galeate at apex. Petals (2–)3, usually blue purple, or white, free, sometimes connate and tubular at middle and free at 2 ends ( Cyanotis ). Stamens 6, free, all or only 2–3 fertile; filaments glabrous or torulose villous; anthers parallel or slightly divergent, longitudinally dehiscent, rarely dehiscent by apical pores. Ovary 3-locular, or reduced to 2-locular, with 1, 2, or more ovules in each locule; style simple, with an entire or 3-lobed stigma. Fruit a capsule, rarely baccate and indehiscent. Seeds peltate or angular, the testa usually wrinkled. About 40 genera and 650 species distributed in tropical, subtropical and temperate regions; 15 genera (two introduced) and 59 species (12 endemic, three introduced) in China; seven genera and 21 species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous small trees, shrubs, or vines. Leaves alternate, estipulate, odd-pinnate, sometimes (1 – )3-foliolate; leaflets subopposite or alternate, margin entire, rarely lobed. Inflorescence a terminal, pseudoterminal, or axillary panicle or raceme. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals (4– )5, distinct or connate at base, imbricate or valvate, persistent. Petals (4 – )5, distinct, rarely connate at middle, imbricate or valvate, rarely circinate. Stamens (8 – )10, in 2 whorls, inner ones usually shorter and abortive; filaments free or connate at base; anthers 2-celled, introrse, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk small or absent. Carpels (3 – )5 or 1, free. Ovary superior, 1-locular; style subulate or filiform; stigma subcapitate, simple or 2-lobed; ovules 2 in each carpel (one smaller or sterile), collateral, erect. Fruit usually a follicle, sessile or stipitate, dehiscing along ventral suture, sometimes along dorsal suture, very rarely circumscissile at base, sometimes indehiscent. Seed 1 (or 2), erect, usually with fleshy aril. About 20 genera and 380 species, mainly distributed in tropical regions of Africa and Asia, some species in the subtropics, only a few species in the New World; six genera and nine species (one endemic) in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs or shrubs, lianas or rarely trees, often lactiferous. Leaves simple, alternate, entire, 3‑lobed or dissected, exstipulate or rarely stipulate. Flowers solitary, axillary or in cymes, racemes, panicles, umbels, bisexual, actinomorphic, usually 5‑merous. Bracts in pair, often small, rarely enlarged after flowering. Sepals distinct, imbricate, often persistent. Corolla sympetalous, funnelform, campanulate, salverform, or urceolate; limb subentire or deeply lobed; lobes valvate. Stamens alternating with corolla lobes, inserted on corolla‑tube; filaments equal or unequal in length; anthers 2‑celled, introrse, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; pollen smooth or spiny. Disk annular or cupular. Ovary superior, 2(–5)‑carpellate, 1–2(–4)‑locular; ovules (1–)2 per locule; placentation basal. Styles 1–2, rarely absent; stigma entire or 2(–3)‑lobed, rarely peltate. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by valves, circumscissile, or irregularly shattering, less often a berry. Seeds usually trigonous, smooth or pubescent. About 58 genera and 1650 species widely distributed in tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions; 20 genera and 129 species in China; 11 genera and 35 species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or rarely herbs. Leaves simple, opposite, rarely alternate, exstipulate. Inflorescence cymose or racemose, paniculate or capitate. Flowers usually bisexual, rarely unisexual (plant monoecious or dioecious) or polygamous, actinomorphic, small. Calyx-tube adnate to ovary, apex 4–5-toothed or truncate. Petals 4–5, rarely absent, often valvate, rarely imbricate. Stamens isomerous and alternate with petals; filaments short; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk present. Ovary inferior, 1–4(–5)-locular, ovule 1 per locule, apical, pendulous; styles 1 or 2–5, distinct. Fruit usually a drupe, rarely a berry. About 15–22 genera and 100 species mainly distributed in temperate and tropical regions; 12 genera and about 60 species in China; three genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial, terrestrial, not aromatic herbs, with ± fleshy rhizomes. Stems usually simple, often long, terete, sometimes spirally contorted, leafy; secondary branches (if present) breaking through leaf sheaths. Leaves spirally arranged, simple, those toward base of stem usually bladeless; leaf sheath tubular, closed; ligule present; petiole short; leaf blade narrowly to broadly elliptic, rolled longitudinally in bud, glabrous to hairy, margin entire. Inflorescence a cone-like spike, terminal on leafy shoots or on separate, short, leafless shoots arising from rhizomes. Bracts imbricate, with linear, nectariferous callus below apex, 1–2-flowered; bracteoles tubular, or folded. Flowers bisexual, epigynous, zygomorphic. Calyx tubular, 2–3-lobed or -toothed. Corolla proximally tubular, distally 3-lobed; lobes unequal, imbricate in bud. Staminodes 5, united into a labellum equaling or much longer than corolla, often ± 3-lobed with crisped margin, never deeply lobed. Fertile stamen 1; filament broad; anther borne below apex of filament or at apex with a connective crest, introrse, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary inferior, 2–3-locular; ovules many per locule; placentation axile. Developed style 1, filiform, usually enclosed between anther locules; stigma with or without abaxial appendage. Stylodes 2, reduced to septal, hollow nectaries at apex of ovary, or absent. Fruit a capsule, 2–3-valved and dehiscing loculicidally, or indehiscent and breaking up irregularly, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds many, black, arillate. Four genera and ca. 120 species of pantropical with centre of diversity in America; one genus and five species (two endemic) in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Stems more or less woody. Leaves succulent, alternate, opposite, or sometimes whorled. Stipule none. Flowers bisexual, or rarely unisexual, in terminal racemes, cymes, or panicles, most commonly 5-merous, seldom 3-, 4-, or 6-merous or even polymerous. Sepals free or occasionally united forming a lobed calyx. Petals free, or sometimes united at the base, rarely forming distinct corolla-tube. Stamens as many as or twice as many as the petals, in 1 or 2 whorls. Ovary superior; carpels as many as the petals, free, or slightly connate at the base, usually each with a small flat scale (nectariferous appendage) at the base; style simple, distinct; ovules numerous, attached to the adaxial suture. Fruit a group of follicles, each with several seeds. About 34 genera with more than 1500 species spreading over the greater parts of the world, but mainly in warm dry regions, particularly abundant in S Africa; 12 genera about 233 species in China; two genera and six species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial climbing or prostrate herbs or woody vines, with spirally coiled tendrils and watery sap, monoecious or dioecious. Stems often angled and sulcate. Leaves often simple, sometimes compound, alternate, exstipulate. Inflorescences, paniculate, racemose or subumbellate, rarely flowers solitary. Flowers unisexual, very rarely bisexual, actinomorphic, bracteate. Male flowers: Calyx 5-lobed; lobes imbricate or spreading; corolla usually sympetalous or apetalous, lobes imbricate, valvate or involute. Stamens often 3, rarely 1–5, distinct or connate in various ways, of which one often 1-celled and the other 2-celled; cells straight to conduplicate, connectives often elongated; pistillodes often present. Female flowers: Calyx-tube adnate to the ovary; staminodes often absent. Ovary inferior or semi-inferior, mostly composed of 3 carpels, 3-locular; ovules usually many per locule; placentas parietal, fleshy; styles 1– 4, usually 1 with 3 stigmas; stigmas thick. Fruit a berry or a pepo, rarely a dry or fleshy capsule, indehiscent or opening in various fashions. Seeds 1-many, large, often compressed and sometimes winged; embryo oily, straight; endosperm wanting or nearly so. About 113 genera and over 800 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, a few in temperate regions; 34 genera and 154 species in China; 14 genera, 21 species and two varieties in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs , monoecious or dioecious. Leaves decussate or in whorls of 3, scalelike and then often dimorphic with flattened facial leaves and keeled lateral leaves, or needlelike particularly in juvenile plants, often with an abaxial resin gland. Pollen cones terminal or axillary, solitary; microsporophylls 6–16, decussate or whorled, each bearing (2 or)3– 6(–9) pollen sacs; pollen wingless. Seed cones usually terminal, solitary, globose, ovoid, or oblong, dehiscent or indehiscent when mature in 1st or 2nd (or 3rd) year; cone scales developing after ovules originate in bract axils; bracts almost completely enveloped by cone scales, free only at apex; ovules 1-numerous per bract axil, erect; cone scales of mature cones 3 –16, flat or peltate, woody, more or less leathery, or succulent, 1–20-seeded. Seeds winged or not; wings derived from seed coat. Cotyledons usually 2, rarely 3– 6. Germination epigeal. 19 genera and ca. 125 species: worldwide; eight genera (one introduced) and 46 species (16 endemic, 13 introduced) in China; six genera and eight species introduced to Hong Kong; here only recorded two genera and two widely cultivated species. Another six species, namely Callitris cupressiformis F. Muell., Callitris robusta R. Br., Chamaecyparis pisifera (Sieb. & Zucc.) Endl. ‘Squarrosa’, Cupressus funebris Endl., Fokienia hodginsii (Dunn) A. Henry & H. H. Thomas and Juniperus chinensis L. ‘Kaizuca’ are not described as there is no recent cultivation or records.

Parasitic herbs without roots. Stems twining, filiform, obtaining nourishment from hosts by haustoria, yellow or reddish, glabrous. Leaves reduced to minute scales. Flowers sessile or short pedicellate, mostly in spicate, racemose, or cymose clusters, 4 – 5‑merous. Bracts minute or absent. Sepals ± connate base. Corolla white, pinkish, or cream coloured, urceolate, tubular, globose or campanulate, inside with fimbriate or crenulate, membranous, infrastaminal scales at base of tube. Stamens as many as corolla lobes, inserted on corolla above scales, alternating with corolla lobes. Pollen smooth. Ovary 2‑loculed; ovules 2 per locule. Styles 1 or 2; stigmas 2, subglobose or elongate, sometimes united. Capsule ovoid or globose, dry or sometimes fleshy, circumscissile or opening irregularly. Seeds 1–4, glabrous; embryo acotyledonous, filiform spiral‑curved. One genus and about 170 species mainly distributed in N & S America, several in Asia and Europe; 11 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, mostly palmlike, dioecious; trunk columnar, sometimes dichotomously branched at apex; bark often thickened and roughened; pith large, xylem and phloem narrow. Leaves borne at apex of trunk, 1(–3)-pinnately compound, spirally arranged; petiole with spines, rarely unarmed, base swollen and hairy; leaflets numerous, alternate to subopposite, dichotomously branched in a few species, midvein present, margin usually entire. Pollen cones borne at apex of trunk, cylindric or fusiform; microsporophylls numerous, scalelike, spirally and tightly arranged along axis of cone, with numerous microsporangia in groups abaxially; pollen tubes producing 2 ciliary motile sperm cells. Megasporophylls several to numerous, flat, arranged in a loose, “conelike” crown surrounding apex of trunk, each with a linear fertile stalk and an apical, pinnatifid or subentire sterile blade; ovules 1 –5 on each side of stalk. Seeds drupelike, seed coat 3-layered (colored sarcotesta, woody sclerotesta, and membranous endotesta), endosperm copious. One genus and ca. 60 species: E Africa (including Madagascar), E and S Asia, N Australia, Pacific Islands; 16 species (eight endemic) in China; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial, rhizomatous to stoloniferous herbs. Culms (stems) simple, solid or hollow, at times septate, usually trigonous, rarely terete or 2-sided, usually nodeless. Leaves usually 3-ranked, rarely distichous or polystichous, usually radical, sometimes cauline, usually sheathing at base; blade usually linear, grass-like, sometimes broader and constricted into a pseudopetiole below; sheath open or closed; ligule often present, sometimes on opposite side to blade. Involucral bracts 1– several, leaf-like or glume-like. Inflorescence unbranched to compoundly or decompoundly branched and umbel-like, or paniculate, comprising 1– many ultimate inflorescence units (spikelets or spicoids). Spikelets comprising 1– many glumes, the glumes membranous to leathery, spirally arranged or 2-ranked, each subtending a single bisexual or unisexual flower or sterile, the spikelet sometimes reduced to a single flower and aggregated into spikes; spicoids (tribe Hypolytreae only) comprising a terminal female flower, 2–12 membranous scale-like floral bracts on a much reduced axis, the lowest 2 bracts opposite and keeled, some of the bracts subtending a male flower, the spicoid subtended and usually hidden by a glumelike spicoid bract, these spirally arranged and aggregated into spikelet-like spikes. Perianth absent or reduced to segments or scale-like segments. Stamens 1–3; anthers basifixed. Stigmas 2–3, rarely styles undivided, the base sometimes persistent and variously shaped in achene. Ovary 2–3-carpellate, unilocular, with a single ovule. Achenes usually hard, 2–3-sided, rarely with a succulent or corky exocarp, surface smooth or variously minutely patterned, sometimes partially or completely enclosed by an enlarged basal prophyll (utricle). About 4000–5000 species in 100–125 genera, worldwide; 36 genera and about 870 species in China; 27 genera, 143 species, one subspecies and one variety in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious; all parts glabrous. Stipules absent. Leaves simple, alternate, leathery, often crowded at branchlet top, entire, often pruinose, penninerved. Racemes axillary. Flowers small. Bracts deciduous. Petals absent. Male flowers: calyx 3–8-lobed, lobes imbricate, persistent or deciduous; stamens 5–12, radiate, filaments short and free; anthers 2-celled, oblong, latrorse, sometimes apiculate; rudimentary ovary absent. Female flowers: calyx 3–8-lobed; staminodes small or absent; ovary imperfectly 2-locular; styles 1–2, very short or absent; stigmas 2; ovules 2 per locule, anatropous, pendulous. Drupes ovoid. Seeds with thin testa, copious oily and proteinaceous endosperm, and minute apical embryo.
