One genus, about ten species distributed in E Asia, Malaysia to tropical Australia; eight species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, lianas, rarely perennial herbs. Leaves spirally arranged, conduplicate, often scabrid, margins toothed, rarely entire; exstipulate, or with long petiolar flanges. Flowers in cymes, panicles, or racemes, sometimes reduced to a single flower, terminal or axillary, horizontally monosymmetrical, bisexual; pedicels articulate; sepals (3 –)4 – 5(–20), imbricare, overlapping, persistent in fruit; petals (2–)3–5(–7), imbricate, often crumpled in bud; stamens numerous, rare 1–10, often asymmetrical, connective often well-developed, anthers basifixed, often dehiscing by pores; carpels 1–20, distinct, or more or less connate at base; with 1–many ovules. Fruits baccate or follicle. Seeds 1–many, arillate or with a rudimentary aril. 12 genera and ca. 300 species in tropical regions; two genera and five species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs usually twining, sometimes woody at the base, with rhizomatous or tuberous rootstock. Stem terete, ridged or winged, sometimes prickly. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, petiolate, simple or palmately compound, with digitate or parallel veins and reticulate veins. Flowers usually unisexual (plants dioecious, rarely monoecious), in axillary spikes or racemes, simple or paniculate. Male flowers: perianth lobes 6, in 2 whorls, basally connate or free; stamens 6, sometimes 3 reduced to staminodes or absent, inserted on perianth or receptacle; ovary rudimentary or absent. Female flowers: similar to male ones; staminodes 3, 6, or absent; ovary inferior, 3-locular; ovules usually 2 per locule, placentation axile; styles 3, free. Fruit a capsule, berry, or samara. Seeds with a membranous wing or not. Nine genera and 650 species widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions, especially in tropical America; one genus and 52 species (21 endemic, two introduced) in China; one genus and nine species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, mostly terrestrial or rarely aquatic, carnivorous; stem with much reduced leaf blades that function as rhizoids below ground, with or without tubers or rhizomes. Leaves basal and rosulate, with sticky, glandular hairs, or with sensitive hairs that trigger closing of blade to trap small animals, juvenile leaf blade circinate in buds; stipulate or exstipulate. Flowers axillary or terminal, often in a coil-like raceme or spike, rarely solitary, bisexual, actinomorphic; sepals usually 5 rarely 4 or 6 – 8, connate at base, imbricate, persistent; petals as many as sepals or more, free, persistent; stamens usually 5, hypogynous, free, alternate with petals, rare 4 – 5-numerous in 2– 4 whorls, filaments free, anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; ovary superior or nearly so, globose or ovoid, 2– 5-carpellate, 1–3-loculed; placentation parietal or basal; styles 2–5, rare 6, simple or branched. Fruit a capsule, dehiscent or indehiscent. Seeds few to numerous; endosperm fleshy; embryo straight. Four genera and more than 100 species distributed in temperate and tropical regions of both hemispheres; two genera and seven species in China; one genus and five species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious or rarely polygamous. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, exstipulate. Flowers actinomorphic, usually unisexual, rarely bisexual, solitary in leaf axils or in cymes. Male flowers usually without pistillodes. Female flowers with or without staminodes. Calyx 3 –7-lobed, persistent and often enlarged when fruiting. Corolla 3 –7-lobed; lobes convolute, rarely imbricate or valvate. Stamens inserted at base of corolla-tube, 2–4 times as many as and opposite to corolla-lobes, rarely as many as and alternate to corolla-lobes; filaments distinct or connate in pairs; anthers basifixed, 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent, rarely dehiscing by apical pores. Ovary superior, 2–16-locular; ovules 1 or 2 per locule. Styles 2– 8, distinct or connate at base; stigma entire or 2-lobed. Fruit a berry, fleshy or leathery. Seeds usually oblong; endosperm copious, sometimes ruminate; embryo straight; hilum small. Three genera and ca. 500 species mainly distributed in tropical regions of the world; one genus and 60 species in China; one genus and six species in Hong Kong.

Erect or scandent shrubs, rarely trees, often covered with peltate or stellate silvery or brown scales. Leaves simple, petiolate, alternate, opposite or in whorls, without stipules. Flowers bisexual or sometimes unisexual (plants dioecious or polygamo-dioecious), regular, mostly 4-merous, apetalous, in axillary clusters or cymes. Perianth-tube in perfect and pistillate flowers tubular, constricted above the ovary, in staminate flowers usually cupulate or almost flat, the upper portion 2- or 4-lobed and deciduous. Stamens equal to and alternate with the perianth-lobes or twice as many, inserted in the tube or at its base. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with a single erect, anatropous ovule; style 1, with simple stigma. Fruit drupe-like or berry-like, consisting of the dry achene enclosed by the thickened lower portion of the persistent perianth-tube. Three genera and about 85 species mainly distributed in N America, Europe and S Asia and Australia; two genera and about 60 species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or semi-evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, sometimes opposite, pinnately veined; stipules persistent or deciduous. Inflorescence racemose, paniculate or cymose, or flowers solitary. Flowers bisexual or rarely unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals 4 – 6, distinct or connate at base, usually valvate or sometimes imbricate. Petals 4 – 6, valvate or rarely imbricate, often laciniate at apex, sometimes wanting. Stamens 8–many, distinct; filaments free and borne on discs; anthers 2-celled, opening by apical pores or longitudinal lateral slits; connective often conspicuously prolonged; disc circular or lobed. Ovary superior, 2–many-locular; styles connate or distinct; ovules 2–many per locule. Fruit a capsule or drupe. Seeds with copious endosperm; embryo flat. About nine genera and 400 – 450 species mainly distributed in tropical to subtropical regions of the world except Africa; two genera and 52 species in China; two genera and eight species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, evergreen or deciduous. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely pseudo-verticillate; margin entire or serrulate; exstipulate. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic or slightly zygomorphic, usually in terminal, racemes or panicles, rarely solitary and axillary. Calyx persistent, (4–)5(–8)-lobed. Corolla sympetalous, campanulate, funnel-shaped or urceolate, usually (4–)5(–10)-lobed; lobes imbricate. Stamens as many as or twice as many as corolla-lobes, inserted at base of a hypogynous disc; filaments free; anthers opening by apical pores or rarely by slits, with appendages in some species. Ovary superior or inferior, (4–)5(–10)-locular; ovules usually numerous; style 1; stigma capitate or discoid. Fruit a capsule, rarely enclosed in an accrescent and fleshy calyx, or a berry. Seeds usually numerous, small, sometimes with a narrow wing, or tails at one or both ends; embryo cylindric; endosperm abundant. Widely distributed in subtropical, temperate, and sub-arctic regions, also at high elevations in the tropics; 15 genera and 757 species in China; five genera, 11 species and 2 varieties in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, growing in wet places or in shallow water. Stem undeveloped, rarely elongate. Leaves alternate, all closely crowded at the base as if in a rosette, narrow and grass-like, parallel-veined, often ± transparent and with transverse minor veins, base sheathing. Inflorescence a dense androgynous head terminating the scape and subtended by an involucre of bracts; scapes thin, twisted and ribbed, base surrounded by a bladeless, tubular sheath. Flowers 2–3-merous, bracteate. Male flowers: sepals 2–3, connate or free; petals 2–3, often inconspicuous; stamens 6. Female flowers: sepals 2–3, free or connate; petals absent to 4, free; ovary (1–)3-locular, with a solitary ovule in each locule; style 1, 1–3-branched. Fruit a capsule, thin, loculicidally dehiscent. Seeds small, contain copious floury endosperm and a small embryo; testa usually reticulate and prickly. Ten genera and ca. 1150 species distributed mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; one genus and 35 species (13 endemic) in China; one genus and seven species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or herbs, rarely woody or herbaceous climbers, sometimes succulent, often with milky juice, very variable in habit. Leaves alternate or opposite, rarely whorled, simple, rarely variously compound, or reduced to scale-like, usually stipulate, sometimes with 1–2 glands at apex or base of petioles. Inflorescences very varied. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), usually small, regular, either without a perianth in one or both sexes, or more frequently with a simple calyx-like perianth, or sometimes also with 4 or 5 petals alternating with the calyx-lobes; staminate flowers usually with intrastaminal disk and with 1 to many stamens; pistillate flowers with hypogynous Disk; ovary consisting of 3 or sometimes 2 or more than 3 united 1-locular or rarely 2-locular carpels, each with 1 or 2 pendulous ovules; styles as many as carpels, free or ± united, entire or divided. Fruit usually capsular, separating into as many elastically 2-valved cocci as carpels, leaving a persistent axis, or rarely succulent and indehiscent, the endocarp consisting of as many as indehiscent nuts or cocci as carpels. Seed laterally attached at or above the middle, with or without an aril. A very large family containing about 317 genera and 5000 species, widespread in the world, primarily in the tropics and subtropics, poorly represented in the temperate regions; about 70 genera and 470 species present in China; 30 genera and 95 species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or herbs, sometimes climbing or decumbent. Stipules mostly present; stipels present or absent. Leaves alternate or rarely opposite, mostly compound, odd- or even-pinnate, trifoliolate, digitate, or 1-foliolate, rarely simple or reduced to scales. Flowers bisexual, very rarely cleistogamous, solitary to forming racemose, paniculate, capitate, or rarely spicate inflorescences. Bracts and bracteoles present. Calyx tubular, regularly (4–)5-toothed or lobed, 2-lipped or spathaceous, lobes or teeth imbricate or valvate. Petals (very rarely absent) 5, papilionaceous, imbricate, free or rarely partially connivent; adaxial petal (vexillum or standard) outermost, the 2 lateral petals (alae or wings) more or less parallel with each other, the lower 2 innermost forming the keel (carina). Stamens often 10, monadelphous or diadelphous, rarely all quite free; often the adaxial (vexillary) filament free or partly united with the others; free part of filaments usually filiform, rarely swollen; anther 2-celled, uniform or very rarely dimorphic and then alternately basifixed and dorsifixed, usually opening by a longitudinal slit; disk rarely present. Ovary of 1 carpel, superior, 1-locular, or sometimes transversely (very rarely longitudinally) septate; ovules 1 –many, inserted on the adaxial suture. Pod dehiscent by one or both sutures, or indehiscent, sometimes winged, sometimes jointed and breaking up into 1-seeded segments. Seeds without or with very scanty endosperm, sometimes strophiolate; radicle sometimes inflexed. About 425 genera, 12000 species distributed worldwide. The more primitive woody genera mostly occur in the S hemisphere and in the tropics whereas the more advanced and herbaceous genera are found in temperate regions, especially rich in Mediterranean countries; 128 genera, 1372 species in China; 53 genera, 130 species, four subspecies and one varieties in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees, rarely shrubs. Leaves alternate or spirally arranged; stipules usually caducous. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious). Male flowers in catkins, spikes, or sometimes panicles; perianth 4 – 6(–9), scale-like, connate or free; filaments filiform; anthers dorsifixed or versatile, opening by longitudinal slits; rudimentary pistil present or not. Female flowers 1–7 subtended by a cupule formed from many fused bracts, forming a separate spike, or sometimes in short clusters at the base of the male inflorescence; perianth 1–7 or more; pistil 1, ovary inferior, 3 – 6(–9)-locular; style and carpels as many as locules. Fruit a nut, solitary or 2–3 partly or entirely enclosed by a cupule or involucre; seeds with large embryo. About seven genera and 1000 species widely distributed in subtropical and temperate regions of both hemispheres; seven genera and 294 species in China; four genera and 36 species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs, sometimes armed. Leaves simple, usually alternate, rarely opposite or whorled, pinnately veined; stipules usually small and caducous, sometimes large, leaf-like and persistent, rarely absent. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemose, spicate, corymbose, or paniculate, sometimes flowers axillary and solitary. Flowers actinomorphic, bisexual or unisexual, sometimes plants dioecious or polygamous. Sepals 3– 8(–15), distinct or connate at base, imbricate, rarely valvate. Petals often present, 3 – 8(–15), distinct, imbricate, alternate with sepals, with or without scales or beard at base. Stamens often many, 1- or many-seriate, or as many as petals and opposite to them; filaments usually distinct, rarely united into a tube; anthers 2-celled, dehiscent longitudinally or rarely opening by apical pores. Ovary superior or rarely inferior, 1-locular with parietal placentas, or imperfectly 2–8-locular; ovules usually 2–many per placenta; styles and stigmas as many as placentas, distinct to completely united. Fruit a berry or a loculicidal capsule or a drupe. Seeds 1–many, often arillate; endosperm usually abundant, oily; embryo straight; cotyledons broad, often cordate. About 93 genera, 1300 species, mostly distributed in tropical regions, rarely in temperate zone; 12 genera, 39 species in China; five genera and eight species in Hong Kong. Dovyalis hebecarpa Warb. and Gynocardia odorata R. Br. are occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs, sometimes climbing, usually with watery sap. Stipules absent. Leaves basal, alternate or rarely subopposite, often dissected. Inflorescence racemose, rarely cymose. Flowers bisexual, usually irregular. Sepals 2, small, caducous. Petals 4, in 2 whorls, imbricate, 1 or both outer with basal spurs or pouch and inner more or less connate. Stamens 4, free or 6 in 2 bundles. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with parietal placentas; ovules 1–many, anatropous to campylotropous; style slender; stigmas 2 or 2–several-lobed. Capsules often with a replum, longitudinally dehiscent or nut-like. Seeds usually arillate, with small embryo and abundant oily endosperm. About 17 genera, 530 species mainly distributed in N temperate, few in tropical Africa; seven genera and 200 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial, or perennial herbs, rarely shrubs or small trees. Stems ascending, erect, or twining. Leaves simple, often opposite, rarely alternate or whorled, base connate, exstipulate. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, simple or complex cymes, sometimes reduced to sessile clusters, often in a thyrse or 1‑flowered. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, usually 4‑ or 5‑merous. Calyx tubular, obconic, campanulate, or rotate. Corolla tubular, funnelform, or rotate; lobes overlapping to right or rarely valvate in bud. Stamens usually as many as and alternate with corolla lobes, inserted on corolla tube; anthers basifixed or dorsifixed, 2‑celled. Disk absent or inconspicuous. Ovary superior, 1( – 2)‑locular, ovules many; placentation usually parietal, rarely free central or axile; stigma entire or 2‑lobed. Fruit a 2‑valved capsule, rarely a berry. Seeds many or rarely few, small; endosperm usually abundant. About 80 genera and 700 species distributed worldwide; 20 genera and 419 species in China; three genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, rarely shrubs, often aromatic. Leaves alternate, sometimes opposite, often lobed, compound or dissected pinnately or palmately, rarely simple and ± entire, stipulate. Flowers in cymes, sometimes solitary, usually bisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic. Sepals 5, usually distinct, imbricate or valvate, sometimes connate at base. Petals 5, rarely 4, 8 or absent, distinct, imbricate, rarely convolute, nectary-glands alternate with petals. Stamens 5–10, in 1–3 whorls, sometimes 1–2 whorls reduced to staminodes; filaments basally connate or distinct; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary superior, 5-carpellate, rarely 2-, 3- or 8-carpellate, plurilocular, placentation axile; ovules 1–2 per locule, pendulous, anatropous. Fruit a schizocarp with 5 one-seeded mericarps separating acropetally from beak and often opening to release seed, or a capsule or mericarps without a beak. Seeds 1–2, endosperm little or wanting; embryo curved. About 14 genera and 730 species widely distributed in temperate, subtropical and tropical regions of the world; two genera and 54 species in China; one genus and one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs, or rarely trees. Leaves opposite or rarely alternate, basal or rarely whorled, usually simple, rarely shallowly to deeply lobed, pinnately or rarely palmately veined; stipules absent. Flowers perfect, usually in axillary cymes or racemes, rarely solitary. Calyx actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic, 4(–5)‑lobed. Corolla gamopetalous, zygomorphic, rarely actinomorphic, usually 2‑lipped. Fertile stamens 2 or 4(–5), epipetalous; anthers free or coherent, thecae 2, parallel, divergent, or divaricate; staminodes 1–3 or absent. Disk ring‑like to cupular, rarely absent. Ovary superior (species of Hong Kong), linear or oblong, rarely ovate, 1‑loculed, with two parietal entire or lobed placentas protruding ± into the cavity but not united in the axis; ovules numerous, anatropous; style simple, with an entire or lobed stigma. Fruit usually a capsule, loculicidal, septicidal, or circumscissile, or rarely a berry, indehiscent. Seeds numerous, with or without albumen; embryo straight, cotyledons equal or unequal after germination. About 133 genera and 3000 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of both hemispheres; 58 genera and 463 species in China; seven genera and seven species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees, dioecious; trunk tall, densely branched. Leaves spirally arranged on long branches and fasciculate on brachyblasts, fan-shaped, long petiolate, base cuneate, apex 2-lobed or notched, margin entire; venation parallel, close, dichotomous. Reproductive structures produced in clusters in axils of scalelike leaves at apex of brachyblast before leaves expanded. Pollen cones pedunculate, catkinlike, microsporophylls numberous, spirally and sparsely arranged; microsporangia 2, ellipsoid; pollen sacs longitudinally dehiscent. Ovules borne on a long, dichotomously branched peduncle sometimes dividing into 3–5 terminal forks; each fork discoid at apex, bearing an erect, sessile ovule; usually only one seed ripening per peduncle. Seed drupelike, long pedunculate, pendulous; sarcotesta fleshy, sclerotesta bony, endotesta membranous; endosperm abundant; cotyledons usually 2, hypogeal. One genus and one species, endemic to China; it is cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen woody vines, rarely erect shrubs or trees, dioecious or sometimes monoecious; stems with swollen nodes. Leaves opposite, petiolate, simple, pinnately veined, margin entire. Flowers unisexual, in spikes. Spikes with many cupular to almost flat, annular, involucral collars, each formed by the fusion of a whorl of bracts. Male spikes solitary or several in terminal or lateral cymes; annular involucral collar densely arranged, each collar with 20– 80 flowers, often also with a whorl of sterile female flowers at apex; male flowers with a cupular, succulent false perianth; stamens 2, rarely 1, filaments fused, exserted from false perianth; anthers with 1 thecae. Female spikes solitary or several in a cymose panicle, often cauliflorous; involucral collars widely separated, each with 4–12 flowers; female flowers with a false perianth tightly enclosing ovule; ovule with 2 integuments, innermost integument elongated into a micropylar tube exserted from false perianth; outer integument with a fleshy, outer layer connate with false perianth and developing into a false seed coat, inner layer bony. Seeds drupelike, enclosed in a red, orange, or yellow, fleshy (rarely corky) false seed coat; endosperm copious, succulent. Cotyledons 2. One genus and about 40 species: mostly tropical and subtropical Asia, Africa and South America; six species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate or radical, rarely opposite, pinnately‑veined; stipules absent. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, usually in cymes, or sometimes in racemes or spikes. Calyx‑tube adnate to the ovary; limb 3–5‑lobed or entire. Corolla 5‑lobed at apex; lobes very thin, induplicate, with membranous margin. Stamens 5, alternate with corolla‑lobes; filaments free, rarely connate to base of corolla‑tube; anthers dorsifixed, introrse, 2‑celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Disk absent. Ovary inferior, half‑inferior or superior, 1–2‑locular, with 1–many ovules in each locule; style entire or 2 – 3‑lobed; stigma surrounded by a cup‑shaped or peltate indusium, usually ciliate on the margin. Fruit a capsule opening in valves, or sometime drupaceous. Seeds 1– many, usually with a fleshy albumen and straight embryo. About 14 genera and 300 species mainly distributed in Australia; two genera and three species in China and in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, sometimes armed. Leaves simple, alternate, margin usually glandular-dentate or serrate, pinnately- or palmately-veined; stipules usually wanting, sometimes present. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, in racemes, panicles or umbels. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual (the plant then sometimes dioecious), actinomorphic. Sepals (3– )5( –9), distinct or sometimes connate at base, imbricate or valvate, sometimes petaloid. Petals as many as and alternate with the sepals, imbricate, valvate or convolute. Stamens usually as many as and opposite to the sepals; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent; staminodes present or absent. Disk usually present. Ovary inferior or superior, 2 – 3( –7)-carpellate, 1– many-locular; placentation axile or parietal; ovules few to many per locule; style distinct or connate at the base; stigma lobed to capitate. Fruit a capsule or a berry. Seeds many, usually arillate; embryo large; endosperm copious or scanty. About 23 genera and ca. 350 species distributed throughout the world; three genera and 75 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, aquatic, amphibious or terrestrial, sometimes with a woody base; cortex commonly with air-cavities. Leaves opposite to alternate or in whorls, very varied in form, usually the submerged leaves pinnately divided into unbranched capillary segments and the aerial leaves normally simple, and toothed or entire; stipules absent. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, regular, usually very small, solitary and axillary or in terminal spikes to panicles. Calyx-tube adnate to the ovary, with 2–4 lobes, or sometimes none. Petals 2–4, free and caducous, or absent. Stamens most commonly 8 in 2 whorls, with the outer set opposite to the sepals, or less often 2–6; anthers basifixed, dehiscing laterally. Ovary inferior, 2–4-locular; styles as many, with feathery or papillose stigmas. Fruit a nut or drupe-like. About nine genera with 145 species widely distributed throughout temperate and subtropical regions, especially in the S hemisphere; two genera and about seven species in China; two genera and four species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs, hermaphroditic, andromonoecious, or monoecious. Leaves usually alternate, petioled, stipules present; leaf blade simple or palmately lobed, pinnately veined or palmately 3–5-veined. Flowers usually arranged in axillary or terminal spikes or heads, rarely in racemes or thyrses or panicles, bisexual or unisexual, actinomorphic or rarely zygomorphic; sepals 4 or 5(–10), sometimes absent, imbricate, usually persistent; petals absent or 4 or 5; stamens 4, 5, or many, free; anthers basifixed, thecae longitudinally or valvately dehiscent. Ovary half-inferior, rarely superior, 2-locular; ovules mostly 1 per carpel, less often many; placentation axile. Styles and stigmas 2. Fruit a capsule, septicidally or septifragally dehiscent; endocarp woody or leathery, usually loose from leathery exocarp. Seeds 1 to many per carpel, sometimes winged. Endosperm thin; embryo straight. About 30 genera and 140 species, mainly distributed in E, W, and SE Asia, rarely in E and S Africa (including Madagascar), NE Australia, America; 18 genera and 74 species in China; nine genera and 12 species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or woody vines. Leaves alternate, simple or palmately compound, with 3(–5) leaflets. Stipules absent. Flowers regular, unisexual or bisexual, arranged in cymose inflorescence; perianth-segments 2–8, united into a tube at base; stamens 3–5(–7), in 1–2 series; filaments usually with a pair of glands or staminodes at base; anthers introrse, 2-celled, opening longitudinally by 2 valves; ovary inferior, 1-locular, with one pendulous ovule; style single, stigma terminal. Fruit a one-seeded achene, sometimes two- or four-winged. About four genera and 68 species mostly in coastal regions of tropics; two genera and 15 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen herbs, shrubs or woody vines. Leaves simple, often opposite, rarely whorled or alternate, estipulate. Inflorescences cymose, corymbose, or in thyrses or panicles. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, rarely dioecious; sterile flowers with enlarged, showy sepals; fertile ones small. Calyx 4 – 12-lobed, lobes imbricate or valvate. Petals 4 – 12, imbricate, valvate, or convolute; basally fused, usually caducous. Stamens 4– many; filaments free or basally united, flat and linear, subulate or filiform; anthers basifixed. Ovary partially to completely inferior, 3 – 6-carpellate; plancentation axile or parietal; ovules 2– many, anatropous; styles as many as carpels, distinct or fused; stigmas capitate or lobed, usually papillate. Fruit a capsule or berry. Seeds many, tiny, winged or not. About 17 genera and ca. 220 species distributed in temperate and subtropical regions of America, Pacific Islands, Asia and Europe; ten genera and about 100 species in China; three genera and four species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, annual or perennial, submerged or floating, aquatic, in fresh or brackish water or marine. Stems short or elongate, sometimes stoloniferous. Leaves radical or cauline, alternate, opposite, subopposite, whorled, or pseudowhorled, sessile or petiolate, usually sheathing at base. Flowers unisexual or bisexual, actinomorphic, enclosed in a bifid spathe or within 2 opposite spathal bracts, or rarely not spatulate; spathes sessile or pedunculate. Stamens 1–many, occasionally some staminodal; anthers 1–4-celled. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; carpels 2–15, fused; ovules few to many, on parietal, sometimes intruding placentas; styles 2–5; stigmas usually bifid. Fruit a fleshy and berry-like capsule dehiscent or opening by decay of pericarp. Seeds many, usually small, without endosperm; embryo straight. About 17 genera with about 80 species: widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; nine genera and about 29 species in China; six genera and nine species in Hong Kong. Some authorities included in this family the genus Najas (Family 333. Najadaceae), which is distinguished by its fruit being an elliptic-oblong achene; the 2-lipped perianth; plant being an annual, submerged in fresh or brackish water; and its sessile leaves.

Trees, shrubs or climbers, sometimes with white sap. Stipules absent. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite. Inflorescences spicate, racemose, paniculate or cymose. Flowers bisexual or unisexual and dioecious, rarely polygamous and dioecious, actinomorphic. Calyx 4–5-lobed; lobes imbricate, rarely valvate. Petals 4–5, free or connate, rarely absent, valvate, rarely imbricate. Stamens as many as and alternate with petals; filaments free; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent; disk present or absent. Ovary superior, 1-locular, rarely 3–5-locular; styles very short or absent, stigma 2–3-lobed, capitate or peltate; ovules 2, anatropous, pendulous. Fruits often a 1-seeded drupe, rarely samaroid. Seeds often with well-developed oily endosperm; coat thin, embryo straight or curved. About 52 genera, 300 species distributed in tropical regions; 13 genera and 25 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, glabrous, aromatic. Leaves simple, alternate, usually fascicled near twig apex, sometimes pseudoverticillate or subopposite, pinnately veined. Flowers bisexual, usually solitary, rarely 2–5 clustered, axillary or inserted above leaf axils; peduncles 1 to several bracteoled; tepals 7–many, distinct, usually glandular, in several whorls, imbricate; stamens many– 4, in several to 1 whorls, erect, filaments tongue-shaped or subterete, anthers 2-celled, basifixed, longitudinally dehiscent, connectives sometimes glandular; carpels usually 7–15, rarely more (21) or fewer (5), distinct, in one whorl, laterally compressed, styles short, subulate, with 1 anatropous ovule. Fruit an aggregate, consisted of several to more than 10 follicles, in one whorl, obliquely on a short torus, in star-shape, dehiscing along ventral sutures. Seeds elliptic or ovate, compressed laterally, endosperm abundant, oily, embryo small. One genus and about 40 species, mainly distributed in E, SE Asia, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, with a few species in SE of N America, West Indies, C & S America; 28 species and two varieties in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual herbs, with rhizomes, bulbs, or corms. Leaves alternate, often 2-ranked, usually sword-shaped to linear, parallel veined, base sheathing. Inflorescence sometimes a spike or reduced to a solitary flower, more often of monochasial, umbellate cymes, each enclosed in 2 opposed bracts; bracts 1–several. Flowers bisexual, showy, actinomorphic or zygomorphic. Perianth segments 6, in 2 whorls, inner and outer ones equal or unequal; tube filiform or trumpet-shaped. Stamens (2–)3; anthers extrorse. Ovary inferior (or superior), 3-locular; ovules few to many; placentation axile. Style with filiform, slender, or petaloid branches, stigmas 3–6. Fruit a loculicidal capsule. Seeds many, with or without aril and wings. About 70–80 genera and 1800–2000 species nearly worldwide, especially S Africa, Asia, and Europe; three genera and 61 species in China; three genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, pinnately-veined, stipulate or exstipulate. Inflorescence cymose, racemose or paniculate. Flowers bisexual, often 5-merous. Sepals imbricate, distinct or connate at base. Petals imbricate or convolute, distinct, persistent. Stamens 5–20, filaments free or connate at base, anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 2–5-loculed, or sometimes plurilocular, placentation axile, with 2 or 1 pendulous ovule per locule; style 1 or 5. Fruit a capsule, septicidal, sometimes loculicidal. Seeds arillate or winged, endosperm little or wanting. Four genera and 21 species distributed in tropical regions of the world; one genus and two species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or rarely shrubs, monoecious or rarely dioecious. Terminal buds subglobose or ovoid to oblong, naked or with scales. Stipules absent. Leaves pinnately compound, sometimes trifoliolate, rarely simple, alternate, rarely opposite; leaflets with glandular, peltate scales. Flowers unisexual, anemophilous, rarely entomophilous. Male flowers arranged in catkin, subtended by an entire or 3-lobed bract; bracteoles 2 or absent; sepals 0–4, adnate to receptacle when present; stamens 3–many, filaments short, free or united at base; anthers glabrous or pubescent, 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Female flowers arranged in capitate or spike-like catkin, with an entire or 3-lobed bracts; bracteoles 2 or 3 (or absent); sepals 0 – 4, adnate to ovary; ovary inferior, 2–3-carpellate, 1-locular; style 1, rarely absent; stigmas 2, plumose or fleshy; ovule 1, orthotropous. Fruit a drupe-like nut or winged nutlet. Seed solitary, without endosperm. Cotyledons 4-lobed, much contorted. Nine genera and about 60 species, mostly distributed in temperate and subtropical regions of the N hemisphere; seven genera and 28 species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, tufted or with erect or creeping rhizome. Stems erect, terete or laterally flattened. Leaves occasionally reduced to a bladeless or nearly bladeless sheath at base of stem; leaf sheath often shortly prolonged on both sides into a pair of auricles at leaf blade junction; leaf blade ususlly linear or filiform, grass-like and flat, or terete, glabrous except for pilose margin on some grasslike blade. Inflorescence a panicle, corymb, or 1-flowered. Flowers bisexual or unisxual (then plants dioecious), regular, usually small, 1–2-bracteolate at base, mostly wind pollinated. Perianth segments (3 or )6, in (1–)2 whorls, free, usually greenish to brownish or blackish, rarely white or yellowish, glume-like. Stamens 3 or 6, if 6, then 3 opposite to outer perianth segments; filaments thin; anthers basifixed, 2-celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; pollen grains in tetrads. Ovary superior, 1-locular, or divided by 3 septa and 3-locular, or incompletely septate; ovules 3 and inserted at base of ovary, or many and biseriate on 3 parietal placentas; stigmas 3, papillose. Capsules 1–3-valved, loculicidal. Seeds globose, ovoid, or fusiform, small, sometimes with caudate appendages; embryo straight, minute, enclosed by fleshy endosperm. About eight genera and 300 species widely distributed in temperate and cold regions of both hemispheres, in tropical regions restricted to high elevations; two genera and 92 species in China; one genus, two species and one subspecies in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, rarely shrubs, usually aromatic. Stems and branches usually 4‑angled. Leaves mostly simple, opposite, rarely whorled or alternate, without stipules. Flowers mostly zygomorphic, axillary, in opposite cymes or rarely solitary, either forming axillary clusters (verticillasters), or in terminal spikes, or racemes, or spike‑like panicles. Calyx persistent, usually 5‑toothed, 2‑lipped or tubular. Corolla with a distinct tube and 4 or 5 lobes, usually forming 2 lips, rarely nearly equal. Stamens epipetalous, 4 or 2, free, rarely filaments connate, sometimes one staminodial; anthers linear, ovoid or rounded, the locules parallel or divaricate, sometimes confluent or rarely dimidiate or disjoined by a slender connectives, usually dehiscing longitudinally; disk persistent. Ovary superior, 2‑locular and each locule 2‑ovuled and style subterminal, or ovary 4‑parted and each lobe 1‑ovuled and style gynobasic (from bases of ovary lobes) with 2‑cleft apex. Fruit usually 4 dry nutlets. Seeds with or without endosperm. About 220 genera and 3500 species of cosmopolitan distribution, but mostly in the Mediterranean region and SW Asia; 96 genera and 807 species in China; 24 genera, 40 species and two varieties in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen shrubs, mostly twining. Leaves alternate, digitately or pinnately compound, exstipulate. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), rare polygamous, regular, in racemes, rarely solitary. Sepals 6 or rarely 3, petaloid. Petals wanting, but nectaries often present. Stamens 6, free or connate, sterile in female flowers; anthers free, extrorse, opening by slits; connectives often produced. Carpels 3 to many, superior, free; stigmas oblique, subsessile; ovules numerous and arranged in longitudinal rows, rarely only one ovule. Fruit a berry or a fleshy follicle, dehiscent or indehiscent. Seeds ovoid or subreniform, with copious endosperm. Nine genera with about 35 species in E Asia and S America; six genera about 45 species in China; one genus and four species in Hong Kong. Notes: Previous reports of species of Akebia in Hong Kong were erroneous.

Evergreen or deciduous, trees or shrubs, rarely parasitic herbaceous vines ( Cassytha ), usually all parts containing aromatic volatile oil. Leaves alternate, opposite, subopposite, or whorled, petiolate, usually leathery, entire, rarely lobed; pinninerved, trinerved or triplinerved, exstipulate. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, regular, usually small, in axillary cymes, clusters, panicles, or racemes. Perianth-tube conical or urceolate, sometimes enlarged in fruit, limb usually 6 or 4 parted and arranged in 2 whorls, or 9 in 3 whorls. Stamens in 3– 4 whorls of 3 each, often partly staminodal; anthers opening by lids. Ovary usually superior, 1-locular; style terminal; stigma simple, discoid or dilated and 2–3-lobed; ovule solitary, pendulous, anatropous. Fruit a drupe or a berry, often cupped or almost enclosed by a persistent, accrescent, fleshy or woody hypanthium. Seed 1, without endosperm; embryo straight. About 45 genera with 2000–2500 species, mainly tropical; 20 genera about 400 species in China; nine genera, 46 species and two varieties in Hong Kong.

Small or minute aquatic herbs, floating or submersed, sometimes forming a green carpet over stagnant, freshwater. Plants not differentiated into stem and leaves; the vegetative structure reduced to small green bodies called fronds, with or without roots. Fronds fleshy or membranous, flat and subrounded to linear, or thickened and nearly globular, with 2 marginal reproductive pouches (or one marginal and the other on adaxial surface). Reproduction almost wholly vegetative; daughter fronds formed from the pouches detaching or remaining attached for many weeks. Flowers unisexual, monoecious, apetalous, emerging from the pouches or from a cavity near median line on adaxial surface, in groups (interpreted as inflorescences by some authors) of 1 pistil (female flower) and 1 or 2 stamens (male flower); anthers 2- or 4-celled; ovary flask-shaped, 1-locular, with 1–7 basal ovules. Fruit a small utricle. Seeds 1–4, smooth or ribbed. Five genera and 38 species distributed worldwide in aquatic ecosystems; four genera and eight species in China; three genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, terrestrial or aquatic. Stems usually modified to rhizoids, stolons or rhizomes, rarely developed, usually with traps (bladders) on stolons or leaves. Leaves alternate or in basal rosette, simple or 1– many times divided, exstipulate. Flowers perfect, zygomorphic, usually in racemes on scapes, rarely solitary. Calyx 2–4(–5)‑lobed, lobes imbricate, persistent. Corolla with short tube, limb 2‑lipped, upper lip entire or 2–3‑lobed, lower lip entire or 2–3(–6)‑lobed; lobes imbricate; spur subulate, cylindric, conical or saccate. Stamens 2, attached to the base of corolla‑tube, included; filaments short, linear; anthers dorsifixed, thecae 2, divaricate, usually confluent. Ovary superior, 1‑locular, with several ovules on a short free central placenta; style short, with 2‑lipped stigma. Fruit usually capsular, loculicidally or circumscissilely dehiscent, rarely indehiscent. Seeds few to numerous, minute, variously shaped and sculptured, without endosperm. Three genera and about 240 species mainly in tropical regions; two genera and 19 species in China; one genus and six species in Hong Kong. Taylor (Kew Bull. Add. Ser., Vol. 14. 1989) provided a worldwide taxonomic study of the genus.

Perennial herbs, with bulbs, corms, rhizomes, or tubers. Leaves basal or alternate, opposite, or whorled on stems, margin entire or spiny, parallel or rarely reticulate-veined. Inflorescence a spike, umbel, raceme, panicle, or flowers solitary. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic; bracts present or absent, sometimes spathaceous; bracteoles present or absent. Perianth segments usually 6, rarely 4, or 8, in 2 whorls, free or connate to form a short tube, with or without corona. Stamens 6, rarely 3, 4, or 8, inserted at perianth throat or at the base of segments and opposite to the segments; filaments free or sometimes connate into a corona; anthers usually 2-locular, basifixed or dorsifixed and versatile, introrse, latrorse, or extrorse, dehiscing usually by vertical slits. Ovary superior, semi-inferior or inferior, (2–)3(–4)-locular, with axile placentae, or rarely 1-locular with a parietal placenta; ovules few to many in each locule; style 1, rarely 3; stigma capitate or 3-lobed. Fruit a capsule or berry. Seeds with endosperm. About 280 genera and 4000 species widespread throughout the world, especially in temperate and subtropical regions; 67 genera and 760 species in China; 24 genera and 33 species (ten cultivated) in Hong Kong.

records.chi: 黃花藺科 (黃花絨葉草科 )
records.sc: 黄花蔺科 (黄花绒叶草科 )
records.text: Herbs, aquatic, perennial, rhizomatous or stoloniferous, caulescent, glabrous, free floating or rooted; sap milky. Leaves basal (or alternate), submersed and floating (rarely emersed), sessile or petiolate, sheathing proximally; blade entire, linear, lanceolate, oblong or obovate, parallel-veined or pinnately veined. Inflorescences scapose umbels, floating (rarely erect), bracteate. Flowers bisexual, hypogynous, pedicellate; sepals 3, persistent; petals 3, deciduous; stamens 3 or 6 or 7–many, distinct; anthers 4-celled, dehiscing longitudinally; pistils (3–)10–20, distinct or coherent proximally, 1-locular; placentation laminar; ovules 12–100. Fruits follicles. Seeds: embryo U-shaped; endosperm absent. Three genera and eight species in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; one genus and one species in China and Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, woody climbers, or herbs, sometimes with axillary spines or tendrils. Stipules usually present, often reduced to lines connecting petiole bases, sometimes reduced to petiolar ocrea or a connate leaf‑sheath. Leaves opposite, occasionally alternate, rarely fasciculate or whorled; margin usually entire; pinnately veined or 3– 7‑veined from base. Flowers in cymes, which often grouped into thyrses or sometimes umbel‑like, scorpioid or reduced to single flowers; bracts usually small. Flowers usually bisexual. Calyx 4‑ or 5‑lobed; lobes free or connate, mostly persistent, imbricate or valvate. Corolla sympetalous; lobes 4 or 5( – 16), valvate, imbricate or contorted in bud. Stamens inserted on corolla, included to exserted, equal in number to corolla lobes and alternating with them or sometimes fewer; filaments free, much shorter to much longer than anthers; anthers basifixed, 2– 4‑locular, dehiscing introrsely or extrorsely by longitudinal slits, base slightly to deeply parted. Disk ring‑shaped or not. Ovary superior or rarely semi‑inferior, (1–)2(–4)‑locular, placentation axile or parietal; ovules 1 – many per locule. Style simple, terminal, persistent or deciduous; stigma usually capitate, entire or shortly 2–4‑cleft. Fruit a capsule, berry, or drupe, 1 – many‑seeded. Seeds sometimes winged; endosperm fleshy or horny; embryo minute, straight; cotyledons small. About 29 genera and about 500 species, mainly in tropical and subtropical regions, absent from Europe; eight genera and 45 species in China; four genera and seven species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen hemiparasitic shrubs. Leaves simple, opposite or alternate, usually pinnately-veined, margin entire, stipules absent. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, spicate, or umbellate; bracts usually inconspicuous. Flowers usually bisexual, rarely unisexual (plants dioecious), 4–6-merous, actinomorphic or zygomorphic, often conspicuous. Calyx adnate to the ovary, entire or shortly toothed, persistent. Petals free or connate, valvate. Disk usually inconspicuous to ± obsolete. Stamens as many as and opposite to petals; filaments slender or absent; anthers 2–4-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary inferior, 1- or 3–4-locular, without true ovules, embryo sacs originating from a central column or at the ovary base, integument absent. Style simple; stigma small. Fruit a berry, rarely a drupe or capsule, with a viscin layer (sticky mucilaginous tissue) outside the vascular bundles. Seed 1; testa absent; endosperm copious; embryo large. About 65 genera and 950 species mainly in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; eight genera and 51 species in China; five genera and five species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs or trees. Stipules much reduced or absent. Leaves opposite, rarely whorled or alternate, simple and commonly entire. Flowers bisexual, solitary or fasciculate in axils or often in terminal spikes, racemes or panicles. Calyx campanulate or tubiform, 3–6(–16)-lobed, with or without appendages between lobes. Petals as many as calyx-lobes or absent, attached at summit of hypanthium. Stamens as many or twice as many as petals, rarely indefinite, inserted in the tube of the calyx, often lower down than the petals; filaments more or less elongate; anthers versatile or seldom basifixed, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 2–6-locular; ovules numerous in each locule, anatropous. Capsules leathery or membranous, dehiscing by valves or by a transverse slit, or seldom indehiscent. Seeds numerous, sometimes winged, without endosperm. About 27 genera and 600 species widespread in tropical countries, with relatively few species in temperate regions; about 11 genera and 47 species in China; six genera and 14 species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen trees or shrubs, usually hairy, rarely glabrous; buds enclosed by hooded stipules. Leaves simple, alternate, sometimes fascicled on apex of twigs and becoming pseudoverticillate, entire, rarely lobed, penninerved, petioled; stipules adnate to petioles or free from petioles, caducous, remaining stipular scars on twigs or petioles. Flowers large, solitary, rarely 2–3 in thyrses, bisexual, rarely unisexual, insect-pollinated; spathose bracts 1 to several below the tepals; tepals 6–9(–45), in 2 to many whorls, 3(–6) in each whorl, usually fleshy, sometimes the outer ones nearly leathery, or reducing to calyx-like; pistils and stamens many, distinct, spirally arranged on elongated torus; androecium usually at the lower part of torus; anthers linear, dehiscing by longitudinal slits, filaments thick and short, sometimes elongated, connectives usually exserted and forming a long or short tip; gynoecium at upper part of torus, sessile or gynophored; carpels folded, usually distinct, sometimes connate at base or rarely connate completely; ovules 2–14 in each carpel, biseriate on ventral sutures. Aggregate apocarpus or sometimes syncarpous; mature follicles woody, bony or leathery, usually dehiscing along dorsal and/or ventral sutures, rarely connate to each other, thick woody or fleshy, irregularly dehiscing; seeds 1–12 in each fruiting carpel, pendulous on a filiform and elastic funiculus, exserted to the follicles; testa fleshy, red, endotesta bony; mature carpels rarely samaroid, seeds connate to endotesta; embryo minute; endosperm copious, oily. 15 genera, ca. 300 species, mainly distributed in SE Asia and SE N America, C America, Antilles Islands, Mexico, Columbia, Venezuela, E Brasil; 11 genera, 107 species and one subspecies in China; four genera and 14 species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, trees or woody vines. Leaves simple, usually opposite, rarely alternate or whorled, entire, usually with two large glands on petiole or abaxial surface; stipules sometime large or united. Inflorescence a raceme or panicle, axillary or terminal. Flowers usually bisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic, 5-merous; pedicels articulated; bracteoles usually 2. Calyx lobes imbricate, rarely valvate, often with a pair of glands at base abaxially. Petals imbricate, base clawed, margin ciliate to fringed. Stamens (1–)2(–3) whorls; filaments usually connate at base; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk obscure. Ovary superior, 3-locular; ovule 1 per locule, pendulous and semianatropous on axile placenta. Style 3, sometimes connate, persistent. Fruits often a schizocarp of winged to nut-like mericarps, rarely a nut or capsule; seed with large straight to curved embryo, endosperm wanting. About 68 genera and 1280 species mainly distributed in tropical and warm regions, especially in America; four genera and 23 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong. In addition to the native species, Malpighia coccigera L., M. glabra L., Thryallis gracilis Kuntze and Tristellateia australasiae A. Rich. are occasionally found in cultivation for ornamental use.

Herbs, shrubs or trees, generally mucilaginous and stellate-pubescent. Leaves simple, alternate, stipulate, usually palmately nerved. Flowers regular, perfect, solitary, or arranged in axillary fascicles or cymes, or in terminal panicles. Sepals (3 –)5, entire, free or connate at base, often subtended by involucral bracteoles (or epicalyx). Petals as many, adnate to the staminal tube at base. Stamens numerous, united into a tube or column around the ovary, free at the top; anthers 1-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary 2–many-carpellate, the carpels in whorls around the columella; style single, with as many or twice as many lobes as carpels, enveloped by the staminal tube, stigmas capitate, clavate; ovules curved. Fruit a schizocarp or a loculicidal capsule. Seeds reniform or ovoid, embryo curved; cotyledons leafy. About 50 genera, 1000 species; some species cultivated for fibre, food or ornamental purposes; 18 genera and 83 species in China; 10 genera, 22 species and 1 variety in Hong Kong.

Perennial, rhizomatous herbs. Aerial stems present or absent. Leaves distichous, differentiated into an open sheath, petiole, and blade; petiole often winged but terete and pulviniform towards apex; blade usually large, sometimes with one straight and one curved side, with many closely parallel veins diverging obliquely from midrib. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, borne on leafy shoots or occasionally on separate, leafless shoots from rhizomes, compound, head-like, spicate, or diffuse and much branched, bracteate. Bracts each subtending a pair of flowers or a cincinnus of paired flowers. Flowers bisexual, asymmetric. Sepals 3, free. Corolla lobes 3, often slightly unequal, basally connate into a tube. Staminodes and stamen in 2 whorls; outer whorl with 1–2 petaloid staminodes, rarely absent; inner whorl with 1 hooded (cucullate) staminode enclosing terminal portion of pistil at anthesis and bearing a lateral appendage (trigger), 1 thicked and fleshy (callose) staminode, and 1 fertile stamen narrowly petaloid laterally; anther 1-celled. Ovary inferior, 1–3-locular, sometimes 2 of locules infertile; ovules 1 per locule. Style cylindrical, adnate to inside of corolla and staminode tube, free portion curved after explosive forward movement (tripping) when released. Capsule loculicidal, rarely indehiscent or berry-like. Seeds 1–3, usually arillate. About 31 genera and ca. 525 species of pantropical but mostly in Americas, absent from Australia; four genera and nine species in China; four genera and seven species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs, or trees, erect or climbing. Branches opposite. Stipules absent. Leaves simple, commonly opposite and verticillate, or decussate with one of a pair slightly smaller than the other. Leaf blade margin entire or serrulate, usually 1–4(–5)-basiveined. Inflorescences cymose, umbellate, corymbose, in paniculate clusters, or cincinnus, rarely flowers solitary. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic but androecium often slightly zygomorphic, usually (3–)4–5(–6)-merous. Bracteoles opposite, usually caducous. Calyx-tube enclosing the ovary and usually cohering with its angles, or sometimes entirely free or adherent; the limb entire, or with as many teeth or lobes as petals. Petals usually 4 or 5, sometimes 3 or 6 or more inserted intermediately below the calyx-teeth, twisted in the bud. Stamens isomorphic or dimorphic, usually as many as or more times than petals and in 2 whorls; filaments often geniculate; anthers typically 2-celled, introrse, basifixed, opening apically by 1 or 2 pores; connective shapes various, usually inflated, decurrent to long stalk or short spur. Ovary usually inferior or half-inferior, rarely superior; locules usually as many as petals, rarely 1-locular; stigma minute, capitate or truncate; placentation axile, free-central, rarely parietal; ovules numerous or few. Fruit a dry or fleshy capsule or a berry, encircled in calyx-tube, longitudinally dehiscent or indehiscent. About 150–160 genera and 4140 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of all continents; 21 genera and 114 species in China; eight genera and 14 species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or sometimes shrublets. Stipules absent. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, usually pinnate. Leaflets opposite or alternate; leaflet somewhat oblique at base, margin usually entire or rarely serrate. Flowers bisexual, dioecious, or polygamo-dioecious, usually in axillary cymose panicles (racemose in Aglaia). Calyx small, 3–6-lobed or with distinct sepals, usually cup-shaped or tubular, imbricate or valvate in buds. Corolla contorted or imbricate (quincuncial in Aglaia). Petals (3–)4–5(–6), rarely more, distinct or connate, sometimes adnate to staminal tube and then valvate. Stamens 5–10(–12), hypogynous, mostly monadelphous by connate filaments (distinct in Toona); anthers usually sessile on stamen tube, erect, included or exserted, 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscing. Disk tubular, annular, obsolete, or absent, free or adnate with ovary. Ovary usually free, 2–5-locular; ovules 1 or 2 or more per locule, collateral or superposed. Style single (or absent in Aglaia); stigma disciform or capitate. Fruit a berry, capsule, or rarely a drupe. Seeds winged or with a fleshy aril wholly or partly covering the seed; endosperm fleshy or absent. About 50 genera and 550 species distributed in tropical, subtropical, and occasionally warm temperate regions of the world; 17 genera and 43 species in China; six genera, seven species and one variety (one genus and one species native) in Hong Kong.

Climbing or twining vines, rarely erect shrubs or small trees. Leaves spirally arranged, often peltate, usually palmately nerved. Stipules absent. Petioles thickened at both ends. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious), usually small, in cymose, racemose or paniculate inflorescence, rarely solitary. Sepals often 6, rarely 1– 4 or 9 –12, usually free, imbricate, in 2– 4 whorls, the inner ones the largest. Petals usually 3– 6, in 1 or 2 whorls, rarely reduced to 4 –2(–1) or absent, free or rarely connate, imbricate or valvate. Male flowers: stamens usually of the same number as the petals, and opposite to them, free or united in a central column, rudimentary pistil very small. Female flowers: carpels 3 – 6, rarely 1–2 or 12, free; style terminal; stigma lobed or divided, rarely entire; ovules 2 per carpel, only 1 developed; staminodes present or absent. Fruit a drupe, with a bony or woody kernel. Seed often curved. About 65 genera and 350 species mostly in tropical and subtropical regions; 19 genera, 78 species in China; seven genera and nine species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, aquatic or nearly so. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple or 3‑foliolate, estipulate. Flowers (4 – )5‑merous, bisexual, rarely polygamous, actinomorphic. Calyx lobes free or united. Corolla rotate or campanulate, lobes united, valvate in bud. Stamens 5, free, alternate with petals, anthers 2‑celled, divaricate, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Pollen grains bilaterally compressed, ± triquetrous, with 3 apertures. Nectaries often present. Ovary superior, 1‑locular, placentation parietal, ovules many; style 1, stigmas 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, dehiscent or indehiscent. Seeds few – many, sometimes winged; endosperm abundant. About five genera and 60 species distributed in temperate and tropical regions worldwide; two genera and seven species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, sometimes lianas, rarely herbs. Leaves alternate, usually bipinnate, rarely once pinnate or become phyllodium; pinnae usually opposite; leaf rachis or petiole usually with glands; petioles with pulvinus; stipules present or absent, sometimes spine-like. Inflorescences spicate or capitate, rarely racemose or paniculate; bracts small, usually deciduous; bracteoles deciduous or absent. Flowers small, bisexual, sometimes unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals united into a single tubular calyx, divided usually into (3–4–)5(–6–7) teeth, rarely entirely distinct. Petals as many as calyx-teeth, valvate in bud, free or united into a tube at the base. Stamens as many as or twice as the number of petals, or sometimes indefinite, free or united below into a tube, free part of filaments usually exserted, anther small, 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits, often with a deciduous gland at the tip; pollen-grains borne in monads or very often in tetrads or polyads. Pistils 1(–15). Ovary superior 1-locular; ovules mostly numerous; style slender; stigma small. Pods dehiscent or indehiscent, sometimes breaking into 1-seeded segment, straight or contorted. Seeds compressed, testa hard, usually with pleurogram. About 56 genera, 2800 species, widespread in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in C and S America, only a few species extend into temperate area; about 17 genera and 66 species in China; nine genera and 17 species in Hong Kong. Desmanthus virgatus (L.) Willd., an introduced species of tropical American origin, was recorded by Dunn & Tutcher (1912), but at present time it is very rare in cultivation, so it is not described here.

Annual or pernnial herbs, rarely shrubby. Leaves simple, opposite, alternate or in false whorls. Flowers bisexual, or rarely unisexual, actinomorphic, in cymose inflorescence or solitary in axils of leaves. Sepals usually 5, free or connate at base, persistent. Petals 5, or more often wanting. Stamens (2–)5 –10; filaments free or more or less connate at base; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Gynoecium usually of 2– 5 carpels united to form a compound, superior ovary with distinct styles and axile placentation. Fruit a capsule, opening loculicidally in valves. About nine genera and 90 species dispersed over tropical and warm regions of both hemispheres; three genera and eight species in China; one genus with two species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, lianas or rarely herbs, with milky juice, armed or unarmed. Stipules 2, usually caducous and leaving an amplexicaul scar. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, entire, serrate, or lobed, palmately or pinnately veined, sometimes with cystoliths. Inflorescence a raceme, panicle, head or spike, axillary, or at trunk or major branches, the axis of inflorescence sometimes thickened to form a head or an invaginated common receptacle. Flowers very small, unisexual (plant monoecious or dioecious). Sepals usually 4, sometimes 1 or up to 8, free or connate, imbricate or valvate, persistent. Petals absent. Stamens as many as and opposite sepals; anthers 1 or 2-celled, opening lengthwise; pistillodes present or absent. Ovary superior or inferior, usually 1-locular, rarely 2-locular; ovules mostly pendulous from apex, rarely basal and erect; styles mostly 2, usually filiform. Fruit a syconium, achene, nut or drupe; often enclosed in enlarged common receptacle to form a fleshy syconium (fig). Seeds with or without endosperm. About 37 genera, 1100 species, widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, less common in temperate regions; nine genera and 144 species in China; seven genera, 36 species, two subspecies and two varieties in Hong Kong.

Perennial or monocarpic herbs, growing from sympodial rhizomes or a massive, sympodial corm. Pseudostems composed of closely packed leaf sheaths. Leaves spirally arranged, petiolate; leaf blade entire, pinnately-veined. Inflorescence terminal or rarely axillary, cymose. Bracts large, spirally arranged, often brilliantly coloured, spathe-like. Flowers bisexual or unisexual by abortion, zygomorphic. Perianth in 2 whorls; 3 outer tepals and 2 inner ones united into a compound tepal; the third inner tepal free. Stamens 5, free; anthers 2-celled. Pistil 1. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, with many anatropous ovules in each locule; placentation axile; styles simple or capitate. Fruit a berry, fleshy or leathery and dry, indehiscent. Seeds hard, not arillate; embryo straight, surrounded by a ± well-developed endosperm and a mealy perisperm. Three genera and ca. 40 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Africa and Asia; three genera and 16 species in China; one genus and four species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Stipules absent. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, entire or toothed, often with glandular or lepidoid hairs. Flowers bisexual, regular or not, axillary, solitary or in cymes. Calyx 5‑lobed. Corolla often 2‑labiate, 5‑lobed, lobes imbricate. Stamens 4, rarely 5 or more, borne on corolla lobes. Anther 2‑celled, longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 2‑locular, (1–)2‑several‑ovuled each locule, or the locule subdivided into 3–10 uniovulate compartments; style simple. Fruit a drupe or separating into 1‑seeded drupe‑like segments. Seeds with ± straight embryo, endosperm scanty or absent. Three genera, 235 species mostly distributed in Australia, Pacific islands, few in tropical America; one genus and one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs, monoecious or dioecious, aromatic. Leaves alternate, simple; stipules absent or rarely present. Flowers in axillary spikes, usually unisexual, anemophilous, without perianth. Male flowers: solitary in axil of each bract, bracteoles absent or 2– 4; stamens often 4 – 8, rarely 2–20, filaments short, free or slightly united at base; anthers 2‑celled, longitudinally dehiscent, sometimes with reduced pistils. Female flowers: solitary or 2– 4 in axil of bract, bracteoles usually 2–4 or absent. Ovary 2-carpellate, 1-locular; ovule solitary, basal, orthotropous; style very short or nearly absent, stigmas 2, slender. Fruit a drupe or nutlet; pericarp fleshy, often with head-like, waxcovered papillae; endocarp hard. Seed 1, endosperm tiny or absent; embryo straight; cotyledons fleshy and thick. Three genera and ca. 50 species, mostly in temperate or subtropical regions of both hemispheres; one genus and four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Mostly evergreen shrubs or small trees, sometimes woody vines or undershrubs, glabrous or with an indumentum of hairs, papillae or scales. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite or subverticillate, usually glandular-punctate or with lineate resin ducts. Stipules none. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, generally in fascicles, racemes, corymbs or umbels, simple or compound and forming panicles. Flowers bisexual or unisexual (plant dioecious or polygamo-dioecious), 4- or 5-merous. Calyx more or less gamosepalous, persistent, often glandular-punctate. Corolla rotate or salverform, the lobes coalescent at base, seldom ( Embelia ) distinct, variously imbricate, convolute or rarely valvate. Stamens adnate to corolla-tube and opposite lobes, rarely almost free; filaments distinct or sometimes fused into a short tube at base; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing introrsely by longitudinal slits or seldom by apical pores. Ovary superior, rarely ( Maesa ) half-inferior, unilocular, with few to many ovules on free-central or basal placenta; style 1, slender, elongate or short, stout or obsolete; stigma punctiform, discoid or styliform and curved. Fruit rounded, seldom ( Aegiceras ) elongate and curved, usually a drupe or berry, slightly fleshy with a thin or thickened endocarp, usually 1-seeded, but several to many seeded in the genus Maesa . About 40 genera and more than 2,000 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of both hemispheres; five genera and 120 species in China; five genera and 25 species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, opposite, sometimes alternate or pseudo-whorled, entire, often with pellucid dots, exstipulate. Inflorescence a spike, cyme, corymb, panicle, or head, axillary or terminal, or rarely flowers solitary. Flowers bisexual, sometimes polygamous, regular, or somewhat irregular. Hypanthium usually adnate to ovary and prolonged above it. Calyx lobes (3–)4–5 or more, distinct or connate into a calyptra. Petals (3–)4 – 5 or more, sometimes absent, distinct or connate into a calyptra. Stamens usually numerous, in 1– several whorls; filaments distinct or connate into 5 bundles opposite petals; anthers 2-celled, dorsifixed or basifixed, dehiscing by longitudinal slits or rarely by apical pores; connectives usually terminating in 1 or more apical glands. Ovary inferior, semi-inferior, or rarely superior, 2– 5(–16)-locular, pseudoseptum sometimes present; ovules 1– several per locule, placentation axile, occasionally parietal. Style simple. Fruit a capsule, berry, drupe, or nut, 1–many-seeded. Seeds without endosperm or endosperm sparse and thin; testa cartilaginous or thinly membranous; embryo straight or curved. About 130 genera and 4500–5000 species distributed in tropical America, Australia and tropical Asia; ten genera and 121 species in China; 12 genera and 26 species in Hong Kong. In addition to species recorded here, Callistemon pinifolius Sweet, Eugenia ventenatii Benth., Leptospermum scoparium Forst. & Forst. f., Lophostemon suaveolens (Soland. ex Gaertn.) Peter G. Wilson & J. T. Waterh., Melaleuca armillaris Sm., M. genistifolia Sm., M. nodosa Sm., M. parviflora Lindl., Psidium cattleianum Sabine var. littorale (Raddi) Mattos, Syncarpia glomulifera (Sm.) Nied., Syzygium cumini (L.) Skeels and S. samarangense (Blume) Merr. & L. M. Perry are occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong.

Small submersed annual herbs, monoecious or rarely dioecious, growing in fresh or brackish water. Stem slender, much branched. Leaves sessile, sub-opposite or apparently whorled, linear or subulate, 1-veined, toothed or entire, somewhat expanded and sheathing at base, and commonly subtending 2 small axillary scales, not ligulate. Flowers unisexual, very small and inconspicuous, hydrophilous, solitary( to few) in axils; male flower mostly subsessile and included in a spathe; perianth 2-lipped at apex; stamen 1, anther sessile, 1–4-celled, opening by longitudinal slits; in female flower perianth absent or this very thin and adhering to carpel; ovary of 1 carpel, 1-locular, stigmas 2–4; ovule solitary, erect from base, anatropous. Fruits usually embraced by leaf-sheath, indehiscent; seeds with a thin testa, straight embryo with large hypocotyl and radicle and no endosperm. One genus and about 40 species widely distributed in the temperate and warm regions of the world; 11 species (one endemic) in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial aquatic herbs, with stout creeping rhizomes. Leaves floating or emersed, peltate, suborbicular, with radiating nerves. Flowers large, bisexual, solitary and terminal on an emersed pedicel; sepals 4–5; petals many and showy, pink, red, yellow or white; stamens many, anthers with clavate appendages at apex; carpels many, free, immersed in the pits of a sponge, obconical receptacle; styles very short, stigmas capitate; ovule 1–2 per carpel, pendulous, anatropous. Fruit a nut, indehicent, embedded in the enlarged receptacle. One genus and two species in Asia, Australia and N America; one species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or herbs, dioecious, carnivorous. Stem erect, prostrate or climbing, simple or branched, cylindric or triangular. Leaves simple, alternate, petiolate or sessile, exstipulate; midvein prolonged into a tendril, apex of tendril usually developing into a pitcher with its lid. Inflorescence a raceme, panicle or cincinnal cyme, terminal. Flowers regular; tepals (3 –)4, in 1 whorl, imbricate, distinct or rarely connate at base, glandular adaxially. Male flowers: filaments united into a column; anthers capitate, (4 –)8 –24 clustered on the apex of column, extrorsely longitudinal dehiscent, 2-celled; pistils inconspicuous. Female flowers: pistils 1, consisting of (3 or) 4 carpels; ovary superior, ovoid-globose or tetragonal-terete, (3 –)4-locular; ovules many, in many rows on axile placentae; style very short to obsolete; stigma disc-like, (3 –)4-lobed. Capsule leathery or woody, loculicidally dehiscing into (3 –)4 valves. Seeds many, filiform; embryo straight; endosperm fleshy. One genus and ca. 85 species distributed in Africa (Madagascar), S & SE Asia, N Australia and Pacific Islands; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs or woody climbers, often with swollen nodes. Leaves simple, petiolate, alternate or opposite, entire, exstipulate. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, solitary or in small terminal cymes, thyrses or umbels, subtended by colored, calyx-like or even corolla-like bracts. Calyx tubular, corolla-like, with a short, 5-lobed limb; ture corolla absent. Stamens 1– 40, usually 3 – 5, free or united at base; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 1-locular, containing a single ovule; style 1, stigma capitate or lobed. Fruit an achene, enclosed by the persistent lower part of perianth-tube. About 30 genera and 290 species, mainly in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in C and S America; six genera (two introduced) and 13 species in China; three genera (two introduced) and four species in Hong Kong.

Aquatic herbs, with horizontal or erect rhizomes. Leaves long-petioled, floating or emersed, ovate to orbicular, with deep sinus. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, solitary and terminal on pedicels; sepals 3–12, usually 4–6, green or petaloid; petals 3–5 or more, free, hypogynous or adherent on the fleshy receptacle; stamens many, often petaloid. Carpels 3 or more, free or united into a many-locular ovary, superior or inferior; stigmas as many as carpels, forking into a radiating and furrowed ring; ovules 1–many, scattered all over the inner walls of the carpels. Fruit a nut or a berry. About six genera and 60 species, cosmopolitan, in fresh water habitat; three genera and eight species in China; one genus and two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, scandent shrubs, trees, or vines, sometimes hemiparasitic, often glabrous. Lateral shoots sometimes with bud scales at base. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, often entire, pinnately- or palmately-veined, rarely 3–5-veined, petiolate, exstipulate. Inflorescences axillary, rarely terminal, cymose, fasciculate, racemose, spicate, or umbellate; bracts small and inconspicuous. Flowers usually bisexual, actinomorphic, 3–7-merous, sometimes heterostylous. Calyx small at anthesis, cupular, discoid, or lobed, sometimes accrescent to partly or wholly covering fruit, sometimes fused to fruit. Petals free or connate at base, valvate. Disk cupular or annular, sometimes accrescent and covering fruit apex. Stamens 3–15; anthers usually 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary usually superior, sometimes inferior, rarely semisuperior, 2–5-locular or 2–5-semilocular; ovules 1 per locule, usually anatropous. Style simple; stigma 2–5-lobed. Fruit a drupe, sometimes with an accrescent calyx. Seed 1; testa thin; endosperm abundant; embryo small; cotyledons 2–4. About 29 genera and 200 species distributed in tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world; five genera and ten species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or erect or scandent shrubs. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate or whorled, simple, trifoliolate, or pinnately compound, margin entire or serrate, without stipules. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, cymose, or paniculate. Flowers actinomorphic, bisexual, rarely unisexual or polygamous (plants monoecious, dioecious or polygamodioecious). Calyx 4(–15)‑lobed, rarely absent. Corolla 4(–12)‑lobed, rarely absent; lobes sometimes united in pairs at base or into a very short corolla‑tube, imbricate or valvate in bud. Stamens 2(–4), inserted at corolla tube or hypogynous; anthers 2‑celled, dehiscent longitudinally. Ovary superior, 2‑loculed; ovules 2 per locule, sometimes 1 or numerous. Style 1 or absent; stigma capitate or 2‑lobed. Fruit a drupe, berry, capsule, or samara. Seeds with or without endosperm, embryo straight; Cotyledons flat; radicle curved upward or downward. About 28 genera, ca. 600 species, mainly distributed in tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions, mostly in Asia; ten genera, 160 species, six subspecies and 25 varieties (95 endemic) in China; six genera and 22 species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, annual or perennial, rarely trees. Leaves simple, alternate or opposite, or occasionally whorled; stipules present and usually caducous, or absent. Flowers often solitary and axillary, or in racemes or spikes, bisexual, rarely unisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic. Calyx 4–5(–6)-lobed; lobes valvate. Petals as many as sepals or rarely absent, imbricate or convolute and occasionally clawed. Stamens as many as sepals in one series or twice as many as sepals in 2 series; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary inferior or rarely semi-inferior, with as many carpels and locules as sepals, septa sometimes thin or absent at maturity; placentation axile or parietal, ovules 1–many per locule; style 1; stigma with as many lobes as sepals. Fruit a loculicidal capsule or indehiscent nut or berry. Seeds many, small, embryo straight, endosperm wanting. About 24 genera and 650 species widely distributed in temperate and subtropical areas of the world; six genera and 64 species in China; two genera and five species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen root-parasitic trees, shrubs or woody vines. Leaves alternate, simple, margin entire, pinnately-veined, exstipulate. Inflorescences axillary or cauliflorous, spicate, racemose, or paniculate or umbellate. Flowers small, actinomorphic, (4–)5-merous, bisexual or unisexual (plants dioecious). Perianth with distinct calyx and corolla, or sepaline; tepals 4–5 (female flowers), or 8, or 10, 1 whorled (female flowers), or 2 whorled, free or partly united, valvate. Stamens as many as and opposite to tepals, free or filaments inserted on tepals; anthers 2-celled, introrse, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk intrastaminal, lobed, annular, or cupular. Ovary superior or semi-inferior, 1-locular; ovule 1, pendulous; style short or absent; stigma entire or shallowly lobed. Fruit a drupe. Seed coat thin; endosperm oily; embryo terete, small, with 3 or 4 linear cotyledons. Ten genera and 33 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; five genera and five species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial, epiphytic, mycotrophic, rarely saprophytic perennial herbs or occasionally woody climbers. Stems erect, cane-like, rhizomatous, tuberous, pseudobulbous or cormous. Leaves basal, cauline or terminal to pseudobulb; convolute, duplicate, conduplicate, reduplicate or plicate; articulate or not. Flowers solitary, spicate, racemose or paniculate; bisexual, rarely unisexual, zygomorphic; perianth colourful, segments 6 in 2 whorls; sepals 3, distinct or connate at base; petals 3, one segment modified into a lip; resupinate or not; nectaries various; stamens 3 with filaments and free, or 2 on side of short stalk, or one with 2 cells erect on column, or one terminal and opercular on column, 1–2-locular; ovary inferior, unilocular with parietal placenta, or axile placenta and 3-locular. Column representing a connate organ of the filament and styles, with a rostrum between the anther and stigma; a foot extending from base of some columns. Pollinia 2–8, very variable, with or without stipe and viscidium. Fruit a capsule. Seed many, without endosperm. About 796 genera and 17500 species distributed worldwide; 193 genera and 1387 species in China; 53 genera and 114 species in Hong Kong. Besides there are some tropical orchids with many horticultural varieties being cultivated in Hong Kong, but they were not treated in this Flora.

Parasitic herbs, without chlorophyll; stems usually simple. Leaves scale‑like, spirally or subimbricately arranged. Inflorescences racemose or spicate, rarely 1‑flowered; bract 1, usually similar to leaves; bracteoles 0–2. Flowers bisexual, subsessile or pedicellate. Calyx tubular, cupular, or campanulate, 4–5‑toothed or lobed. Corolla bilabiate, usually curved, sometimes tubular‑campanulate with 5 subequal lobes; upper lip entire, emarginate or 2‑lobed; lower lip 3‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted at base of corolla tube; filaments slender; anthers often in pairs, 2‑celled, longitudinally dehiscent, sometimes 1 cell fertile and another sterile or reduced to spur. Pistil 2– 3‑carpellate; ovary superior; 1‑locular, usually with 4 parietal placentas; ovules 2–4 or many, anatropous. Style long; stigma inflated, discoid, peltate, or 2–4‑lobed. Capsule usually opening by 2 or 3 valves; seeds minute, 2–4 or many. About 15 genera and 150 species in tropical, subtropical and temperate regions of the world; nine genera and 40 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubs or trees. Leaves basal or alternate, pinnate or digitate, with entire leaflets. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, solitary or in axillary umbels or panicles. Sepals 5, free or united at the base. Petals 5, contorted in the bud, free or slightly connate at the base. Stamens 10, in 2 series, the outer 5 opposite to the petals and shorter than the others, or sometimes very small and without anthers; filaments united at the base; anthers versatile, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 5-angled or 5-lobed nearly to the axis, 5-locular, with 1–many ovules in each locule; styles 5, free or united at the base, with terminal, entire or divided stigma. Fruit a capsule or a berry. About eight genera with about 600 species widely distributed from tropical to temperate regions; three genera and ten species in China; two genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, without milky juice. Stipules small. Leaves simple, alternate, distichous, pinnately-veined; stipules small, unequally inserted. Flowers small, unisexual, in terminal or axillary or cauline racemes or raceme-like inflorescence, or solitary or clustered in the leaf-axils; sepals 5, distinct or connate into a toothed or lobed cup; petals 5, imbricate or valvate, distinct; stamens in one or two sets of 5 each, or 10 or 15 in a single series; anthers opening by longitudinal slits; disk wanting; ovary superior, 2–5-locular, with a single ovule in each locule, lacking obturators; styles free or basally connate, or the stigmas virtually sessile. Fruit drupaceous; endocarp slightly bony or stony, thin to very thick and massive, usually variously tuberculate or muricate or pitted or ridged, sometimes dehiscent by valves; seeds not carunculate.
