Three genera about 26 species in tropical Africa, Asia and New Guinea; one genus and one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, trunk and branches often emitting aerial roots. Leaves in 4 rows or usually spirally arranged and crowded towards top of shoots, linear, leathery, keeled, mostly spinulose on the margins and keel, sheathing at base. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious), very small and many, born in a terminal spadix subtended by (1–)several large spathes, or in several racemosely arranged spadices, or in a terminal panicle. Perianth vestigial or absent. Male flowers: not only closely crowded but often not sharply limited from one another, each with 1– many stamens; filaments free, or often connate into phalanges for most of their length (each such phalange considered to represent a flower); anthers erect, basifixed, 2-celled, the cell sometimes again once divided, opening lengthwise by slits; vestige of ovary absent or very minute. Female flowers: staminodes absent or small and hypogynous or adnate to base of ovary; ovary superior, 1-locular, free or confluent with adjacent ovaries into groups and in fruit forming a syncarp, stigmas separate or united; style very short or absent; ovules anatropous, solitary to many, basal or parietal. Syncarps ellipsoidal to globose; mature carpels woody, drupaceous or baccate, pulpy inside. Seeds minute, with fleshy endosperm and minute embryo. Three genera and 875 species distributed in tropics and subtropics of the Old World especially in oceanic islands; two genera and ten species in China; one genus and five species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely subshrubs or small trees, usually with milky or yellow juice. Leaves often alternate, sometimes subopposite or nearly verticillate, entire, lobed or sinuate, estipulate. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, usually large, solitary and terminal, or arranged in thyrses or umbels, rarely panicles. Sepals 2– 4, distinct or more or less connate, enclosing flower buds, deciduous at anthesis. Petals 4– 6 or 8 –12, in 2 whorls, imbricate, crumpled in bud, rarely apetalous. Stamens usually many, in several whorls, rarely few, filaments distinct, anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; nectaries absent. Pistil composed of 2–many carpels; ovary superior, sessile, or stipitate, 1-locular, with parietal placentation, sometimes 2–many-locular by intrusion of septa; ovules many, rarely 1, styles present or absent, stigmas isomerous with carples, distinct or connate. Capsules dehiscing into valves or by apical pores, rarely indehiscent; seeds usually small, endosperm abundant, fleshy, embryo small. About 23 genera and 200 species, mainly distributed in N temperate regions; twelve genera and 70 species in China. One genera and one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbaceous or woody vines, rarely erect shrubs or trees, with axillary tendrils or not. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple, rarely compound, entire or lobed, glandbearing near base and on petioles; stipules small, deciduous. Flowers in cymes or seldom solitary, bisexual, unisexual or rarely polygamous, regular; calyx-tube tubular, often 5-lobed, rarely 3- or 4-lobes, lobes imbricate, persistent; petals as many as and alternate to sepals, rarely absent, distinct or slightly connate; corona consisting of 1 to several whorls of filaments or scales between corolla and stamens. Stamens 5, rarely 4– 8 or many, filaments distinct or connate into a tube; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Gynoecium with 3 –5 carpels, borne on the apex of androgynophore or gynophore; ovary superior, 1-locular, with parietal placentas; ovules many, anatropous; styles as many as carpels, distinct or connate at base, stigmas capitate or reniform. Fruit a capsule or berry, loculicidally dehiscent or indehiscent. Seeds several to many, with a fleshy red apical aril; endosperm copious, fleshy; embryo large, straight. About 18 genera and 530 species, distributed in tropical and temperate regions, especially in tropical America; two genera and 23 species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubs, Leaves simple, opposite, sometimes alternate on upper part of branches, margin entire or dentate or split, exstipulate. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, axillary, solitary, rarely in cymes. Calyx (4 – )5‑parted. Corolla tubular, bilabiate, ventricose; lobes 5, imbricate. Stamens 4, didynamous, sometime 2; staminodes usually 1; anthers 2‑celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary superior or rarely inferior, 2–(4)‑locular; placentation axile; ovules 2–many, Style acrogenous, filiform; stigma 2‑branched. Fruit a capsule, nut or drupe, with hooks or winged. Seeds 1–many per locule. About four genera and ca. 50 species, mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical oceanic area of the E hemisphere; two genera and two species in China; one genus and one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or trees. Stipules persistent. Leaves simple, alternate. Flowers small, bisexual, actinomorphic, axillary, in pseudospikes or pseudo-racemes. Bracteoles 2, firmly adnate to calyx, ciliate, persistent. Sepals 5, unequal, imbricate, ciliate, persistent. Petals 5, white, imbricate, usually connate with stamens at base. Stamens 5, inflexed in bud, alternate with petals, shorter than petals; anthers small, 2-celled, dehiscing by apical pores. Ovary superior, 5-locular; ovules 2 per locule, collateral, pendulous, style 1, apically 5-lobed, persistent. Capsule ellipsoid, loculicidal. Seeds ellipsoid, flattened, apex winged or not; embryo U-shaped; endosperm very thin. One genus and one species distributed in SE and SW China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Erect, perennial herbs, with rhizome or corm. Leaves alternate, sheathing at base; basal leaves rosulate, equitant; cauline leaves distichous; leaf blade entire, linear to lanceolate, parallel-veined. Inflorescence a simple or compound terminal spike; floral bracts spathe-like. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, sessile. Perianth of 4 tepals, 2-whorled, white or yellow; 2 outer tepals larger, adaxial and abaxial respectively; 2 inner tepals smaller, lateral. Stamen single; filament flattened, free or adnate to tepals; anther dorsifixed, 2-loculate, extrorse to introrse; pollen grains binucleate, shed as monads or tetrads, 1–3-aperturate. Ovary single, superior, 1–3-loculate, with parietal or axile placentation; ovules many per locule, anatropous; style simple; stigma capitate or obscurely 3-lobed. Fruit a dry dehiscent capsule, loculicidal or splitting irregularly. Seeds many; testa spirally-striate; embryo straight; endosperm present. Four genera and five species in Australia, S and SE Asia and W Pacific; one genus and one species in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, shrubs or trees. Leaves simple, alternate, petiolate or sessile, entire, usually exstipulate. Flowers bisexual or rarely unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), in leaf-opposed or axillary racemes or spikes; perianth-segments 4 – 5(–10), free or connate at base; stamens 5 –10(–30), inserted on a fleshy disc; filaments free or connate at base; anthers 2-celled, introse, opening by longitudinal slits; ovary superior, composed of 4–12 carpels; carpels united at least at base, each containing a single ovule; styles very short or none; stigmas as many as the carpels, linear or subulate. Fruit a fleshy berry, dry nut or, rarely a loculicidal capsule. About 18 genera and 65 species, chiefly in tropical and subtropical regions; two genera (one introduced) in China; one genus in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees, rarely shrubs, monoecious. Leaves spirally arranged or in bundles of (1 or)2–5(– 8) when basally subtended by a leaf sheath; leaf blade linear or needlelike, not decurrent. Pollen cones solitary or clustered, with numerous spirally arranged microsporophylls; microsporophyll with 2 microsporangia. Seed cones erect or pendulous, with many spirally arranged ovulate scales and bracts; ovulate scales usually with 2 upright ovules adaxially, free or only basally adnate with bracts. Seed scales appressed, woody or leathery, variable in shape and size, with 2 seeds adaxially, persistent or deciduous after cone maturity. Seeds usually with one membranous wing at apex, rarely not winged. Ten genera, ca. 235 species: N hemisphere; ten genera (two endemic) and 108 species (43 endemic, 24 introduced) in China; two genera and three species (two native, one introduced) in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs or climbers, rarely trees, usually aromatic. Vascular bundles ± scattered in transverse section. Tip of stem sometimes enclosed within a stipule-like sheath, the prophyll, sometimes adnate to petiole (absent in Peperomia). Leaves alternate, often opposite or whorled, simple, base often asymmetric, palmately or pinnately veined. Inflorescence usually a pedunculate spike, rarely grouped into an umbel, leaf-opposed or axillary, rarely terminal. Flowers small, hermaphrodite, polygamous or dioecious, nearly always sessile; bracts small, usually peltate or cup-like, usually without perianth. Stamens 1–10; filaments usually free; anthers 2-celled, distinct or connate, longitudinally dehiscent. Gynoecium 2–5-carpellate, connate; ovary superior, unilocular, ovule 1, orthotropous; stigmas 1–5, sessile or with very short styles. Fruit a small drupe or nutlet; pericarp fleshy, thin or dry, sometimes with sticky papillae or glochidiate spines. Seeds with copious starchy perisperm and a minute embryo embedded in small endosperm. About eight or nine genera, variously estimated to include 2000 –3000 species, distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of America, Asia and Africa; three genera and ca. 70 species occur in China, distributed from Taiwan through SE to SW China; two genera and eight species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, sometimes spiny. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, estipulate, margin entire or serrate. Inflorescences umbellate, corymbose, paniculate, or a solitary flower, bracteate and bracteolate. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic, usually 5-merous. Sepals often distinct or slightly connate. Petals free or connate. Stamens opposite to sepals; filament filiform; anther basifixed or dorsifixed, 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally or by pores. Ovary superior, short stipitate, 2 – 3( –5)-carpellate, usually 1-locular or incompletely 2 – 5-locular; ovules many, anatropous; placentation parietal, axile, or basal; style short, persistent or deciduous. Fruit a capsule or a berry. Seeds many; testa thin; endosperm copious; embryo small. Nine genera and ca. 250 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Africa, Asia, Australia, and Pacific Islands; one genus and 46 species in China; one genus, two species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Herbs, rarely small shrubs, with rhizomes. Stipules absent. Leaves simple, commonly all basal and alternate, seldom cauline and alternate or opposite, often sheathing at base. Inflorescence a bracteate heads or spikes. Flowers small, regular, bisexual, rarely unisexual or polygamous. Sepals 4, imbricate, persistent. Corolla scarious, salverform or tubiform; lobes 4, imbricate. Stamens generally 4, attached to corolla‑tube and alternate with corolla‑lobes; filaments slender; anthers versatile, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 2‑locular; style slender with 2‑lobed stigma; ovules anatropous or hemitropous, 1–40 on axile placenta in each locule, rarely 1‑basal ovule. Fruit a circumscissile capsule or an achene enclosed in persistent calyx. Seeds with usually straight embryo; endosperm copious. Three genera, 75 species distributed all the world; one genus, 20 species in China; one genus, two species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees. Leaves alternate, palmately lobed; petioles with dilated base enclosing the bud. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious), arranged in globose capitula; perianth-segments 4- or 6-merous, arranged in two whorls; stamens 4–6, opposite the outer perianth-segments, filaments very short; ovary superior; carpels 3 – 6, free, each with 1(–2) pendulous ovules. Fruit indehiscent, surrounded at the base by long hairs. One genus with six to seven species in S and E Europe to India and from N America to Mexico; three species introduced to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs and shrubs or climbers, aculescent or with elongated and branched stems. Leaves simple, in basal rosette or alternate on stems, without stipules. Flowers bisexual, regular, in cymose, racemose, spicate or capitulate inflorescence, bracteate. Sepals fused to form a 5-toothed or 5-lobed tube, 5 –10-ribbed; lobes often with scarious margins. Petals 5, united into a tube or connate only at base, persistent; lobes imbricate. Stamens 5, opposite petals, free or inserted on corolla-tube; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with a single basal anatropous ovule; styles 5, free or united. Fruit an achene or a capsule, usually enclosed by persistent sepals. About 22 genera and 440 species, cosmopolitan, but best developed from the Mediterranean region to W and C Asia, especially prefers to dry and saline habitats; seven genera and 46 species in China; two genera and two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, or woody bamboos. Culms often erect, sometimes prostrate or twisted, jointed, internodes hollow or solid. Leaves simple, arranged alternately in 2 ranks, differentiated into sheath, blade, and ligule; leaf sheath surrounding and supporting culminternode, split to base or infrequently tubular with partially or completely fused margins, modified with reduced blade in bamboos (culm sheaths); leaf blades usually long, narrow and flat, veins parallel; ligule membranous or a line of hairs. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, spicate, capitates and paniculate. Spikelets composed of distichous bracts arranged along a slender axis (rachilla); typically 2 lowest bracts (glumes) empty, subtending 1– many florets. Florets composed of 2 opposing bracts enclosing a single small flower, outer bract (lemma) clasping the more delicate, usually 2-keeled inner bract (palea). Flowers bisexual or unisexual, often small; lodicules (small scales representing perianth) 2, rarely 3 or absent, 3– many in bamboos, hyaline or fleshy; stamens (1–)3(–6), or more in some bamboos, filaments capillary, anthers versatile, 2-celled, dehiscing along a longitudinal slit; ovary 1-locular, styles (1–)2(–3), free or united at base, stigmas feathery. Fruit normally a dry indehiscent caryopsis, fleshy in some bamboos; embryo small or large; hilum punctate to linear. About 700 genera and 11000 species widely distributed all over the world; 226 genera and 1795 species in China; 95 genera, 227 species, 11 varieties and 6 cultivars in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, dioecious or rarely monoecious. Leaves spirally arranged, subopposite, or decussate. Pollen cones terminal, solitary or clustered in leaf axils; microsporophylls numerous, spirally arranged, with distinct adaxial and abaxial surfaces; microsporangia 2; pollen 2(or 3)-saccate, rarely nonsaccate. Seed-bearing structures terminal or axillary, solitary, occasionally spikelike, comprising few to several spirally arranged bracts; all or only apical bracts fertile, smooth or warty; basal bracts sometimes fused and succulent (together with peduncle) to form a “receptacle,” or obsolete. Seed drupelike or nutlike, wholly or partly enveloped in a sometimes colored and succulent epimatium. Cotyledons 2. 18 genera and ca. 180 species in tropical, subtropical, and S temperate zones; four genera and 12 species in China; two genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs; roots usually flattened, thalloid or filiform, attached to rocks in flowing water; stems absent or present, small or large, simple or branched. Leaves distichous, scattered, or imbricate, base often sheathed, margin entire or dissected; stipules absent or present. Flowers bisexual, in spike-like inflorescences, cymes, irregularly clusters or solitary, actinomorphic or zygomorphic, enclosed or not by a membranous spathella or spathella lacking. Perianth either present, 3- or 5-lobed, free or united at base or reduced to scale-like petals; tepals 2–many, usually alternating with stamens. Stamens 1–4, or many, in 1–2 whorls or confined to one side of flower, hypogynous; filaments free or connate at base; anthers 2– 4-locular, longitudinally or irregularly dehiscent. Ovary superior, 1–3-locular; ovules numerous, placenta central; styles 1–3. Fruit a capsule, septicidal, with equal or unequal valves; seeds 2–many, minute, without endosperm. About 50 genera and 270 species in tropical and subtropical regions; three genera and six species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, rarely trees, sometimes parasitic ( Salomonia ). Leaves simple, alternate, opposite, or whorled, petiolate or sessile; stipules absent, sometimes a pair of glands or spines. Inflorescence a spike, raceme or panicle, axillary or terminal. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, bracteate and bracteolate. Sepals 5, distinct, rarely connate at base, outer 3 small, inner 2 large, petaloid, or all 5 nearly equal. Petals 3 or 5, often connate at base, central one boat-shaped, often with fimbriate or lamellate or papilionaceous apical appendages. Stamens usually 8 or 10, or 3–7; filaments often united and forming a sheath, rarely distinct; anthers basifixed, 1-celled, usually dehiscing by a single apical pore or longitudinal slits. Disk usually absent or, if present, annular or glandular. Ovary superior, 1–2-locular; ovule 1 per locule, anatropous, pendulous; placentation axile; style 1; stigmas 1 or 2, capitate. Fruit a loculicidal capsule, nut, samara or drupe. Seeds arillate or not, endosperm copious or wanting. About 18 genera and 1000 species distributed worldwide, especially in tropical and subtropical regions; three genera and 54 species in China; three genera and ten species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubs or lianas. Stems often tumid at nodes. Leaves alternate; stipules usually thin and scarious, rarely herbaceous, forming a sheath or ring (the ocrea) round the stem within the petiole. Flowers small, hermaphroditic, occasionally unisexual, clustered in axils of the leaves, or in spikes or racemes forming terminal panicles. Perianth-segments 5– 6, or fewer, regular and equal, or the inner ones enlarged, basally united into a tube. Stamens usually 6–9, in 2 whorls; filaments free or united at the base; anthers 2-celled. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with a single erect ovule; styles or stigmas 2, 3, or rarely more. Fruit an achene or a small nut, usually with angles and enclosed in the persistent perianth. About 51 genera and 1050 species with a worldwide distribution; 13 genera and 238 species in China; three genera (including one cultivated) with 30 species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial aquatic herbs. Rhizomes short and thick or creeping, with fibrous roots. Stem conspicuous or very short. Leaves rosulate or distichous, floating or submersed; petiole mostly distinct, sheathed at base, sometimes inflated; leaf blade broadly ovate, lanceolate, or broadly linear, with many parallel veins. Inflorescences a raceme or spike exserted from sheath of uppermost leaf. Flowers bisexual, mostly actinomorphic, sometimes zygomorphic. Perianth segments 6, in 2 whorls, petaloid, blue or purplish blue, free or basally connate into a tube. Stamens usually 6 in 2 whorls, rarely 3 or 1, inserted on perianth, often unequal or dissimilar; filaments slender, free; anthers 2-celled, introrse, dehiscing by longitudinal slits or rarely by pores. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; placenta parietal or axile; style simple; stigma entire or minutely 3-lobed. Fruit a 3-valved capsule or indehiscent. Six genera and ca. 40 species widely spread over tropical and subtropical regions; two genera (one introduced) and five species in China; two genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubby. Leaves simple, alternate or opposite, often succulent. Stipules scarious or bristle-like, rarely wanting. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, solitary, in clusters or forming racemes, cymes or panicles. Sepals 2, rarely 3– 8, free or partially united at base. Petals 5 or rarely more, sometimes slightly united. Stamens equal in number and opposite to the petals, or more often indefinite. Ovary superior or half-inferior, 1-locular, with several ovules attached to free central or basal placenta; style single, with 2– 8 stigmas or branches. Capsule opening by two or three valves or a lid. About 22 genera and 400 species, with a wide geographical range over the greater part of the world, but especially well represented in S Africa and America; two genera and six species in China; two genera with three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs growing in freshwater, rooted in substrate, with creeping sympodial rhizomes and erect, leafy branches. Leaves alternate or opposite, those immersed thin, those above water often leathery, sheathing at base; sheath free or partially adnate to petiole. Inflorescences a somewhat fleshy spikes, with peduncle surrounded by a sheath at base, elevated a little above water. Flowers small, anemophilous, bisexual, hypogynous, actinomorphic; bracts absent; tepals (2–)4, in one series, distinct, greenish, reddish, or brownish, rounded, flat to convex, shortly clawed. Stamens 4, opposite tepals and basally adnate to the claw, anthers extrorse, 2-celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Gynoecium of 4 distinct carpels; ovules solitary, attached to ventral margin of carpel; styles short; stigmas capitate. Fruiting carpels drupaceous with hard endocarp and soft exocarp or achenial with thin pericarp. Seeds solitary, without endosperm, with coiled embryo. Two genera and about 90 species cosmopolitan; one genus and nine species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Leaves simple, entire to lobed, alternate, opposite or whorled, often all basal and rosulate. Flowers bisexual, usually 5-merous, often dimorphic by heterostyly, solitary or in racemes, panicles, or umbels. Calyx deeply lobed, persistent. Corolla gamopetalous, actinomorphic. Stamens as many as and opposite corolla-lobes; filaments free or united into a tube at base. Ovary superior, rarely semi-inferior, 1-locular, with many ovules on a free-central placenta; style simple, with a inconspicuous capitate stigma. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by valves, rarely circumscissile or indehiscent. About 22 genera with about 1000 species mainly in temperate and mountane regions of the N hemisphere; 12 genera and 517 species in China; two genera and five species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or rarely perennial herbs. Leaves usually alternate, entire or divided, without stipules. Flowers normally bisexual, but sometimes unisexual (plant dioecious), actinomorphic or zygomorphic, usually in racemes, spikes or heads. Perianth-segments 4, petaloid, usually valvate in bud. Stamens as many as, opposite to and inserted in the segments; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 1-locular, sessile or stalked, with 1–several ovules; style simple, often bent inwards and sometimes fleshy or wiry. Fruit a follicle, drupe or nut. About 80 genera and 1700 species in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in Australia and S Africa; four genera (one introduced) and about 25 species in China; two genera (one introduced) and four species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous shrubs or small trees, often spiny. Leaves opposite or subopposite, simple, entire, exstipulate. Flowers terminal and subterminal, solitary or several in clusters, actinomorphic, bisexual. Calyx leathery, tube adnate to ovary; lobes 5–9, valvate, persistent. Petals 5–9, showy, free, crumpled. Stamens numerous, inserted at calyx-tube; filaments free; anthers dorsifixed, 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary inferior, 8–13-locular, locules often in 2 or 3 layers, ovules numerous, axile and parietal; style slender; stigma capitate. Fruit berry-like with leathery rind, subglobose, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds many, embryo straight, endosperm wanting. One genus and two species distributed from SE Europe to the Himalayas; one species introduced to China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, rarely shrubs or woody climbers. Leaves alternate or basal, rarely opposite, simple or compound, palmately veined, rarely pinninerved. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual (plant monoecious or dioecious), actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic, solitary, in cymes or racemes. Sepals 3 or more, usually 5, free, green or petaloid. Petals present or absent, 3 –5 or more, free, or sometimes none, often nectariferous. Stamens many, hypogynous, free, spirally arranged; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits; staminodes sometimes present. Carpels several, usually free, with one or more ovules in each. Fruits indehiscent achenes or berries, or follicular capsules. Seeds small, with abundant endosperm and minute embryo. About 60 genera and 2500 species widely distributed in N temperate regions; 39 genera and 921 species in China; three genera, nine species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, sometimes climbing, often thorny, rarely herbs. Leaves simple, alternate or rarely opposite; stipules minute, caducous or persistent. Flowers small, regular, bisexual or rarely unisexual, in cymes, fascicles or panicles. Calyx campanulate or tubular, 4–5-cleft; lobes valvate. Petals 4–5, often smaller than sepals, unguiculate, adnate to the base of calyx-lobes and alternating with them, or rarely wanting. Stamens as many as the petals and opposite to them; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior or inferior, free or embedded in a well-developed disk, 2–4-locular, with a single erect ovule in each locule; style simple or divided. Fruit mostly fleshy drupes or nuts, but some are dry, indehiscent and winged. About 58 genera with more than 900 species widely spread over most parts of the world, especially in tropical and warm regions; ten genera and about 130 species in China; five genera and eight species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, often with aerial roots. Leaves simple, opposite, petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, sheathing terminal bud, caducous. Inflorescences axillary, cymose or flowers solitary. Flowers usually bisexual, rarely unisexual, 4–5-merous, actinomorphic. Calyx-tube adnate to ovary or free, lobes 4–16, valvate. Petals usually as many as sepals, free, fleshy, usually caducous, margin entire, lacerate, or 2-cleft. Stamens 2–4 times as many as calyx lobes, often in pairs opposite to petals, filaments often connate at base; anther 4–many-celled, dehiscing longitudinally or by a ventral valve. Disk annular or absent. Ovary inferior or semi-inferior, rarely superior, 2–5(–6)-locular; ovules usually 2 per locule, pendulous; style 1; stigma entire, capitate, or lobed. Fruit a drupe or a berry, rarely a capsule. Seeds 1–several, sometimes arillate; embryos sometimes straight, linear, often green (viviparous in mangroves); endosperms copious and oily. About 16 genera and about 130 species distributed in the tropical region of the world, especially in Old World; six genera and 13 species in China; three genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees, shrubs or herbs, spiny or unarmed, sometimes climbing. Leaves usually alternate, sometimes distichous, rarely opposite, simple or compound; stipules usually conspicuous, rarely absent. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, cymose, corymbose, racemose or paniculate, rarely reduced to a single flower. Flowers actinomorphic, 4– 5-numerous, usually bisexual, rarely unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), perigynous, the basal part of sepals, petals and stamens forming a flat to urceolate or sometimes conical receptacle (hypanthium), which is lined or rimmed with a glandular disk. Sepals usually 5, rarely few or more, imbricate; epicalyx segments sometimes also present. Petals as many as sepals, inserted below the margin of the disk, free, imbricate, sometimes absent. Stamens mostly numerous; filaments usually free, rarely connate; anthers small, 2-celled, dehiscing lengthwise. Ovary inferior, semi-inferior or superior; carpels 1–many, free or connate, usually adnate to the hypanthium; ovules often 2 (rarely 1 or several) in each carpel or ovary-locule; styles as many as carpels, free or connate, basal, lateral or subterminal. Fruit a follicle, achene, drupe, hip or pome. Seeds usually without albumen; cotyledons often fleshy with convex back. About 85 genera and ca. 2000 species cosmopolitan, mostly in N temperate zone; 55 genera and 950 species in China; 12 genera, 39 species and two varieties in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, herbs, or rarely climbers. Leaves opposite or whorled, simple and usually entire. Stipules usually interpetiolar, fused at each node or distinct, sometimes leafy or reduced to a stipular line, seldom intrapetiolar and small. Inflorescence various, basically composed of cymes. Flowers bisexual and regular, rarely unisexual or polygamous, often heterostylic. Calyx‑tube fused with ovary, apex 4–5‑lobed, rarely subentire, sometimes one of the lobes enlarged. Corolla tubular, funnel‑shaped, salverform, bell‑shaped or rotate, 4–5‑lobed; lobes valvate, imbricate or contorted in bud. Stamens as many as lobes of corolla, alternating with them and inserted in the tube; anthers 2‑celled, opening by longitudinal slits, or rarely by apical pores. Ovary usually inferior, usually 2‑locular and with axile, apical or basal placentas, rarely 1‑locular with parietal placentas; styles simple, with a simple terminal stigma, or with as many stigmatic lobes as cells of the ovary. Fruit a capsule, berry, drupe or schizocarp; seeds sometimes winged. About 637 genera with 10700 species mainly in tropics and subtropics, and with a few species in temperate and cold regions; 96 genera and about 670 species in China; 35 genera, 78 species and two varieties in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial submersed glabrous herbs, growing in alkaline or brackish water, but sometimes in sea-water. Stems slender. Leaves alternate or opposite, linear or setaceous, 1-veined, sheathing at base. Inflorescence a 2 – several-flowered terminal spike, initially enclosed by the sheathing base of leaves; bract absent. Peduncle elongating at anthesis, elevating inflorescence to or near water surface, or remaining short, occasionally becoming twisted in fruit, then pulling developing fruit below water surface. Flowers bisexual, hypogynous. Perianth absent. Stamens 2, anthers subsessile, extrorse, with two bisporangiate thecae dehiscing by longitudinal slits; connective broad. Gynoecium of 4 or more carpels, stigmas peltate or umbonate; ovule solitary, pendulous from apex of each carpel, campylotropous. Drupelets long-stipitate. Seeds without endosperm. One genus and seven species sub-cosmopolitan; one genus and one species in China and Hong Kong.

Aromatic trees, shrubs or herbs, armed or unarmed. Leaves simple or compound, alternate, rarely opposite, with pellucid gland-dots, exstipulate. Inflorescence in cymes, panicles, racemes or corymbs, rarely flowers solitary and axillary. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic. Sepals (2–)5, sometimes connate at base, often imbricate. Petals twice as many as and alternate with sepals, distinct, rarely connate, imbricate, rarely valvate. Stamens 4–5, or 2(–3–4) times as many as petals, or even up to 60, filaments distinct, rarely connate at base, 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Nectary-disk annular. Gynoecium of (2–)4–5(–many) carpels; carpels distinct or connate; ovary superior, usually (1–)4–5-locular, placentation axile; ovules (1–)2(–many) per locule; styles distinct, coherent or connate; stigmas capitate. Fruit a schizocarp, berry or drupe, etc. Seeds with large, embryo straight or curved, endosperm well developed or wanting. About 160 genera and 1700 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, few in temperate regions; 14 genera and 25 species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or woody climbers. Leaves simple, alternate, or odd-pinnate compound; stipules absent. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, usually in cymes or panicles. Flowers bisexual, or polygamous, actinomorphic or zygomorphic. Sepals 5, rarely 4, free or united at base, imbricate, equal or unequal. Petal 5, rarely 4 or 6, imbricate, equal or the inner 2 much smaller than the outer 3. Stamens 5, rarely 4, opposite to petals, inserted at the base of or on the disc, all fertile or the outer 3 sterile, anthers 2-celled. Disc hypogynous, cup-shaped or annular. Ovary superior, sessile, usually 2, rarely 3-locular, with 2 or 1 half-anatropous ovules in each locule. Fruit 1- seeded, drupaceous. Three genera and about 80 species, distributed in tropical Asia and America, some species widely distributed in temperate E Asia; two genera, about 45 species in China; two genera and six species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, simple, stipulate. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious), in catkins, appearing before or at the same time as the leaves in early spring; each flower subtended by a bract. Perianth wanting. Stamens 2 to many. Ovary superior, 1-locular; stigmas 2– 4, often 2-lobed. Fruit a dehiscent capsule, opening by 2– 4-valves; seeds; many, surrounded by tufts of long silky hairs. Three genera, sub-cosmopolitan, chiefly in N temperate regions; three genera and about 350 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, rarely trees, often parasitic or hemiparasitic. Leaves simple, usually alternate or opposite, sometimes scale-like, rarely absent, entire, usually pinnately-veined, sometimes palmately 3–9-veined, exstipulate. Inflorescences mostly axillary, occasionally terminal, cymose, umbellate, paniculate, racemose, spicate, or clustered, sometimes flowers solitary; bracts scale-like, small, sometimes forming involucre, ± adnate to pedicel; bracteoles sometimes present, paired. Flowers bisexual or unisexual (plants usually dioecious, rarely monoecious), actinomorphic, 3 – 6(–8)-merous, very small; perianth lobes 3– 6(–8), slightly fleshy. Male flowers: perianth lobes valvate or slightly imbricate, sparsely hairy or with tongue-shaped appendage at the insertion of the stamens. Disk epigynous or perigynous, sometimes absent, margin sinuate or lobed, sometimes distinct, glandular or scaly. Stamens as many as and opposite to perianth lobes; anthers 2-celled, parallel or divaricate, usually dehiscing longitudinally. Female and bisexual flowers: perianth tube usually longer than that of male flower. Ovary inferior or half-inferior, 1- or 5 –12-locular; ovules 1 –3(–5); style 1; stigma capitate, small, truncate or lobed. Fruit a drupe or a nut, exocarp usually fleshy, endocarp crustaceous or bony. Seed 1, without a differentiated testa; endosperm copious, usually white and partitioned, fleshy; embryo straight, small, smooth, rugose, or many ridged. About 36 genera and 500 species widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions of the world; seven genera and 33 species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, rarely herbaceous climbers. Leaves pinnately or digitately compound, rarely simple, alternate, usually exstipulate. Inflorescence a terminal or axillary thyrse; bracts and bracteoles small. Flowers unisexual, rarely polygamous or bisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic, usually small. Sepals 4–6, distinct or connate at base, imbricate or valvate. Petals 4–6, sometimes absent, free, imbricate, usually clawed, often with scales or hair-tufted basal appendages. Disk conspicuous, fleshy, entire or interrupted, rarely absent. Stamens 5–10, usually 8, free, rarely connate at base; anthers dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent, introrse; staminodes sometimes present in carpellate flowers, but filaments shorter. Ovary superior, (1–)3(–4)-locular; ovules 1–2, rarely several per locule, placentation axile, rarely parietal; style usually apical; stigma entire or 2–3(–4)-lobed. Fruit a loculicidal capsule, berry, or drupe, or consisting of 2–3 samaras. Seeds 1, rarely 2 or more per locule; testa black or brown, hard, often with a conspicuous fleshy aril or sarcotesta; embryo curved, plicate, or twisted, oily and starchy; endosperm usually wanting. About 135 genera and 1500 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 21 genera and 48 species in China; six genera and six species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, usually lactiferous. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely subopposite, opposite or subverticillate, margin entire, pinnately veined; stipules absent or rarely present. Flowers solitary, several clustered or in cymes, bisexual or unisexual, actinomorphic, bracteolate. Sepals 4 – 8, in 1–2 whorls, imbricate. Corolla-tube short, lobes as many to two times as many as sepals, imbricate, usually entire, rarely with 2 lacerate or lobular appendages. Stamens inserted at corolla base or throat of corolla-tube, as many as corolla lobes, rarely fewer or more, in 2 or 3 whorls, opposite to corolla lobes, rarely alternate to them; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent; staminodes present or absent, alternate with stamens, scale-like to petaloid. Ovary superior, (2–)4 –14(–30)-carpellate and -locular, with axile placentation; ovules 1 per locule. Style 1; stigmas 1, papillate. Fruit a berry or drupe, 1- to many-seeded. Seed coat brown; endosperm usually oily; seed scar lateral and linear to oblong or basal and round. About 55 genera and 800 species distributed in tropical regions of the world; 11 genera and 24 species in China; four genera and four species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous twining vines. Leaves alternate, trifoliate, long-petioled, exstipulate. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious), in drooping racemes from scaly axillary bud. Male flowers: sepals 6, in 2 sets of 3, petaloid; petals 6, very small and scale-like, nectariferous; stamens 6, free, opposite the nectariform petals; filaments short; anthers extrorse, 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits; connectives slightly produced; vestigial carpels linear, usually 4–6. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in staminate flower; staminodes 6; carpels numerous, free, spirally arranged on a globose receptacle, each carpel with a solitary ovule. Fruit a 1-seeded berry, bearing on the enlarged and fleshy receptacle. The family consists only one species distributed in China, Vietnam and Laos.

Perennial herbs, aromatic. Stems erect, ascending, or prostrate, obviously jointed. Leaves simple, alternate; stipules interpetiolar, connate or adnate to base of petiole, forming a sheath. Inflorescence a dense spike or raceme, sometimes resembling a single flower when large involucral petaloid bracts are present at base; bracts evident or inconspicuous. Flowers bisexual. Perianth absent. Stamens usually 3, 6, or 8, free or adnate to ovary base; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Pistils (2- or)3- or 4-carpellate; carpels distinct or connate, if distinct: each carpel with 2–4 ovules, if connate: ovary 1-locular, placentation parietal, each placenta with 6–13 ovules; styles free. Fruit a schizocarp or apically dehiscent capsule; seeds with little endosperm, copious perisperm, minute embryo. Four genera and ca. six species, distributed in E Asia and N America; three genera and four species occur in China; two genera and two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs. Leaves simple or compound, usually spirally arranged, often in basal rosettes, estipulate. Flowers usually in cymes or racemes, rarely solitary, bisexual, actinomorphic, 4- or 5-merous. Sepals sometimes petal-like, imbricate or valvate. Petals usually free, imbricate or valvate, sometimes absent. Stamens 5 – 10; filaments free; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent; staminodes often present. Ovary superior to inferior, 2( –3)-locular with axile placentation; ovules several tomany per locule, in several rows; Styles 2( –3), free. Fruit a capsule, usually septicidal. Seeds many, small; embryo straight; endosperm copious, oily. About 36 genera and 500 species distributed worldwide, especially in temperate and cold regions of N hemisphere; 12 genera and ca. 260 species in China; one genus and one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Woody vines, monoecious or dioecious. Leaves simple, alternate or ± clustered, exstipulate, petiolate. Flowers generally solitary and axillary to leaves on ultimate branches, or in axils of fugacious bracts near base of ultimate shoots, occasionally in pairs or in clusters of up to 8, unisexual, hypogynous, few to numerous parts generally spirally arranged, pedicellate; tepals free, not as distinct sepals and petals, outermost and innermost sometimes reduced; androecium very variable, of 4–80 stamens, sometimes of ± free stamens fused only at base of filaments, sometimes as head of fused stamens or free but tightly compressed stamens; anthers essentially basifixed, thecae dehiscing by longitudinal slits; filaments at least basally fused into modified column of variable shape; gynoecium of 12-300 carpels; carpels developmentally conduplicate; stigmatic crest as unvascularised “pseudostyle”, sometimes modified as peltate “pseudostigma”; ovary unilocular; ovules 2–5(–11), anatropous, ventrally attached or pendulous, bitegmic, crassinucellar. Fruit an aggregate of apocarps; receptacle ellipsoid to elongate; apocarps with carnose pericarp. Seeds 1–5, rarely more, ventrally attached or pendulous, laterally flattened, with copious oily endosperm. Two genera and 39 species, generally distributed in tropical to temperate regions of E and SE Asia, with one species in N America; two genera and 27 species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs, rarely trees. Stipules absent. Leaves opposite, alternate, whorled, or basally opposite and apically alternate, simple or sometimes pinnately dissected. Inflorescences racemose, spicate, or thyrsoid paniculate, or flowers solitary. Flowers bisexual, usually zygomorphic, rarely actinomorphic. Calyx persistent, often (2–)4– 5‑lobed or ‑parted. Corolla sympetalous, limb (3–)4–5‑lobed, often 2‑liped, sometimes basally spurred. Stamens attached to the corolla‑tube, alternate with the lobes, usually 4 or only 4 functional, the adaxial one staminodial or wanting, or sometimes only 2(–3), the abaxial pair reduced or wanting; anthers tetrasporangiate and dithecal, sometimes becoming unithecal during ontogeny, split longitudinally by slits. Disk annulate, cupular, or reduced to a gland. Ovary superior, 2‑loculed, rarely apically 1‑loculed; ovules numerous, rarely 2 per locule, on axile placentas; styles simple; stigma capitate, 2‑lobed. Capsules septicidal, loculicidal or septifragal, sometimes opening by pores or irregularly dehiscent, rarely a berry. Seeds minute or rarely conspicuous, sometimes winged; testa often reticulate; hilum lateral or ventral; endosperm fleshy or absent; embryo straight or curved. About 306 genera and 5850 species, cosmopolitan; 61 genera and 681 species widely distributed in China but with a greater concentration in SW China; 18 genera and 44 species in Hong Kong. Paulownia fortunei (Seem.) Hemsl. (白花泡桐; Photo 250) was also cultivated in Hong Kong previously.

Trees or shrubs; bark, wood and seeds usually bitter. Leaves pinnate to unifoliolate or rarely simple, alternate, sometimes opposite, stipulate or exstipulate. Inflorescence racemose, cymose or thyrsoid, axillary. Flowers small, bisexual or unisexual (plant andromonoecious or dioecious), often with rudiments of opposite sex, actinomorphic. Calyx usually connate at base; lobes 3– 5( – 8), imbricate or valvate. Petals 3– 5( – 8), distinct, imbricate or valvate. Stamens as many as the petals and alternate with them, or twice as many as the petals; filaments distinct, often with basal appendages; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Disk usually present, sometimes a gynophore or androgynophore. Gynoecium often united at base, rarely distinct, usually 2– 5-carpellate. Ovary superior, 2– 5-locular, ovules 1–2 per locule; styles 1 – 5, connate or distinct; stigmas 2 – 5, capitate. Fruit a capsule, samara, rarely a berry or drupe, often a schizocarp of dry or fleshy mericarps; endosperm present or absent; embryo straight or curved. About 22 genera and ca. 95 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; three genera and ten species in China; three genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs and herbs, or lianas, rarely perennial or annual herbs, rhizomatous or tuberous. Stems prickly or not. Leaves simple, evergreen, alternate, rarely opposite, usually leathery, entire; petiolate to subsessile, palmately veined; petioles often sheathed and with tendrils. Leaf sheaths when present, with free margins. Flowers small, unisexual, dioecious, rarely bisexual, often aggregated in umbels, sometimes in spikes, racemes or panicles, rarely solitary. Perianth segments 6; distinct or connate, in 2 whorls, isomerous, petaloid (but usually inconspicuous); stamens usually 6, rarely 3 or more, filaments distinct or connate into a column, anthers 1-celled, basifixed, dehiscing by longitudinal slits, introrse or latrorse. Ovary superior, 3-locular, ovules 1–2 per locule; style absent or very short, stigmas 3. Fruit a berry, usually 3-seeded. Endosperm oily. Embryo well differentiated. Three genera and 320 species distributed in pantropical, extending to temperate regions in both hemisphere; two genera and about 60 species in China; two genera and nine species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs, trees, or vines, with or without spines, glabrous or pubescent with unbranched or branched, often glandular hairs. Leaves alternate or paired and frequently unequal in size, simple to pinnately lobed or compound, petiolate or sessile, without stipules. Inflorescence cymose, branched or unbranched. Flowers usually perfect, (4 – )5‑merous, actinomorphic or zygomorphic; calyx campanulate, sometimes accrescent in fruit, corolla rotate, campanulate, stellate, or urceolate, white, green, yellow, pink, or purple; stamens equal or unequal; filaments generally short and inserted at the corolla base; anthers basifixed, equal or unequal, blunt or tapered toward apex, opening by terminal pores, sometimes expanding into longitudinal slits. Ovary 2‑carpellate; ovules many; style articulate at base or above the base, usually slender; stigma capitate. Fruit a berry, or a capsule, usually many‑seeded; seeds often flattened; embryo embedded in abundant endosperm. About 95 genera with more than 2000 species distributed mainly in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in Americas; 20 genera and 101 species in China; 12 genera and 24 (16 cultivated or naturalized) species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves simple, opposite, entire, leathery and estipulate. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, perigynous, pedicellate, either solitary at terminal or 2–3 in cymes or corymbs. Calyx persistent, 4–8-lobed, leathery, often coloured inside. Petals 4–8 or absent. Stamens many (less often only 12), seriate, inflexed in buds and inserted on the calyx; filaments filiform, long and robust; anthers reniform or ellipsoidal. Ovary superior, sessile, 4 or more locules, enclosed by calyx during anthesis; ovules many; stigma either capitate, peltate or slightly lobed. Fruits on the calyx tube, either valvate capsule or indehiscent globose berry. Seeds many, small and irregular, exalbuminous. Two genera and about 12 species (including three hybrid species), mainly distributed from tropical Asia to tropical Africa; two genera and five species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong, both accidently introduced to mangroves along muddy coast and channels.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves odd-pinnately compound, rarely unifoliolate, opposite, rarely alternate, serrulate, stipulate or exstipulate. Inflorescence paniculate. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, actinomorphic, 5-merous. Sepals distinct or connate, imbricate, often petaloid. Petals imbricate. Stamens inserted outside the disk, alternate with petals; filaments often flat; anthers 2-celled, dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent. Disk annular, ± lobed, sometimes absent. Ovary superior, (2–)3(–4)-locular, ovules 1– several per locule, anatropous; placentation axile. Fruit a head of follicles, a drupe, a berry or a capsule, each locule often with 1 or 2 seeds. Embryo straight, endosperm copious, oily. Six genera and about 60 species distributed in America, Eurasia to Malesia; four genera and 22 species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial erect twining or creeping herbs, rarely subshrubs, with tuberous roots or creeping rhizomes. Leaves whorled, opposite, or alternate, petiolate or sessile, basal veins 3 or more, transverse veinlets many, parallel. Inflorescence racemose or cymose, 1–severalflowered. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic. Perianth segments 4, in 2 whorls, petaloid, distinct. Stamens 4; filaments distinct or slightly connate at base, very short; anthers dorsifixed or basifixed, 2-celled, erect, linear, introrse; connective usually appendaged. Ovary superior or subinferior, 1-locular; ovules 2 or more. Stigma sessile, small. Capsule slightly compressed, 2-valved. Seed appendages on or near funicle, arillate; testa leathery; endosperm copious; embryo hard, small. Three genera and about 35 species distributed in Asia, tropical Australia, one species in E North America; two genera and eight species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, rarely herbs or climbers; indumentum usually stellate. Stipules usually present. Leaves alternate or very rarely opposite, simple of digitately lobed or foliolate. Inflorescence a panicle, raceme, cyme or corymb, axillary or terminal, sometimes 1-flowered. Flowers bisexual or unisexual; sepals 5 –3, valvate, partially connate or rarely free; petals 5, or absent, contorted or imbricate, free or adnate at base to staminal tube, often persistent; stamens free or connate into a narrow tube (androphore), and sometimes with staminodes; anthers 2-celled, opening lengthwise by slits, or rarely by apical pores; ovary 2– 5-locular or rarely reduced to 1 carpel; ovules (1–)2 or more per carpel or locule; styles simple or lobed, rarely free. Capsules or follicles, dehiscent or indehiscent, rarely berries or drupes. Seeds with or without endosperm; cotyledons flat or folded. About 67 genera , 1500 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, few in temperate zone; 19 genera and 84 species in China; ten genera and 11 species in Hong Kong.

Stout perennial herbs, or musa-like trees. Stems formed by the sheathing leaf bases, or with a simple, unbranched trunk. Leaves medium-sized to very large, alternate and in 2 ranks, with a thick midrib and many pinnately paralled veins extending to the margin; petioles long, sheathed at base. Flowers bisexual, irregular, borne in terminal or lateral long-stalked cincinni and enclosed in a large spathe-like and boat-shaped bract; sepals 3, ± equal, free or ± adnate to the petals; petals 3, slightly to more often strongly dissimilar, the lateral ones larger than the median one; stamens usually 5, rarely 6 (in Ravenala), filaments rigid and elongate; anthers linear, opening by longitudinal slits; ovary inferior, 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule on the axile placentas. Fruit a woody capsule dehiscing loculicidally by 3 valves, or a fleshy schizocarp. Seeds many, contain a straight embryo in endosperm, arillate or not. Three genera and seven species in tropical Africa; two genera and three species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs or small shrubs, some members moss‑like, without laticifers. Stipules absent. Leaves alternate, simple, often grass‑like. Inflorescence a raceme, cyme, or lax spike. Flowers perfect or unisexual, zygomorphic. Calyx and corolla 5‑merous. Calyx synsepalous; tube adnate to ovary; limb often 2‑labiate, with 2–5 lobes; lobes imbricate. Corolla synpetalous, often irregular, 5(or6)‑lobed; 4 lobes similar but anterior one (labellum) often different in shape and reflexed. Stamens 2, at lateral sides, adnate with style, forming a gynostemium; anthers extrorse, 2‑celled. Ovary inferior, 2‑locular, incompletely 2‑locular, or even 1‑locular due to reduction of septum; ovules usually numerous, on axile or free‑central placentas, anatropous; stigma entire or 2‑fid, adnate with anthers. Fruit a capsule, usually septicidal. Seeds few to more, often numerous, minute; seed‑coat thin; embryo small, embedded in copious endosperm. Protandrous and entomophilous; gynostemium often irritable, normally bent to labellum side but snapping to an oppositely bent position when touched. Four or five genera and ca. 150 species in Australia, New Zealand, S end of South America, with only Stylidium extending into tropical Asia; one genus and two species in S China and in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, usually stellate pubescent or scaly, rarely glabrous. Leaves usually alternate, simple, petiolate; stipules absent or very minute. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, paniculate, cymose, rarely 1-flowered or several flowers in a fascicle; bracteoles minute or absent. Flowers bisexual, rarely polygamous dioecious, actinomorphic; calyx campanulate, obconical, or cup-shaped, tube completely or partially adnate to ovary, teeth or lobes 4 – 6, sometimes very small or obsolete; corolla gamopetalous, lobes 4 –7, more or less connate at base, imbricate or valvate; stamens twice or sometimes as many as corolla lobes, inserted at base of corolla; filaments mostly flattened, more or less connate into a tube; anthers introrse, 2-celled, cells parallel and opening by longitudinal slits; ovary superior, half inferior, or inferior, 3–5-locular or apically 1-locular and basally 3–5-locular; ovules few or solitary per locule, erect, pendulous, or anatropous, integument 1 or 2, placentation axile or parietal; style linear or subulate; stigma truncate, capitate or 2–5-lobed. Fruit a berry, drupe, or capsule, exocarp fleshy to dry. Seeds wingless or winged, often with a broad hilum; embryo straight or slightly curved; endosperm copious; cotyledons flattened or subterete. 11 genera and ca. 180 species in tropical and temperate America, Asia, and Mediterranean; ten genera and 54 species in China; four genera, five species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, evergreen, rarely deciduous. Leaves spirally or distichously arranged, simple; stipules absent. Inflorescences in spikes, racemes, panicles, or glomerules, rarely flowers solitary. Flowers actinomorphic, bisexual, rarely unisexual, subtended by 1 bract and 2 bracteoles, rarely bractless or with several bracts in leaf axil. Calyx lobes 3–5, valvate or imbricate. Corolla divided to middle or nearly to base, lobes 3–11, imbricate. Stamens many, rarely 4 or 5, adnate to corolla tube, filaments distinct or in fascicles, anthers subglobose, 2-celled. Ovary inferior to semi-inferior, 2–5-locular, but usually 3-locular; ovules 2–4 per locule. Style 1, filiform; stigma small, capitate or 2–5-lobed. Drupes with persistent calyx. Seeds with copious endosperm; embryo straight or curved; cotyledons very short. One genus and ca. 300 species, widely distributed in tropics and subtropics of Asia, Australia, and America; 77 species in China; 14 species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Rhizomes solid, starchy, cylindrical to subcylindrical or tuberous, globose. Leaves all basal, large, entire, pinnatifid, palmately partite or palmatisect blade with pinnately divided segments, long-petiolate, base sheathing, palmately- or pinnately-veined. Inflorescence borne on a radical scape, cymose, umbel-like; involucral bracts (2–)4–6(–12), in 2 whorls, elongate or broad. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic; bracteoles linear, narrower than bracts. Perianth tube adnate to ovary, lobes 6, in 2 whorls, petaloid, darkcoloured. Stamens 6, inserted on perianth lobes; filaments short, apex hooded or spatulate; anthers 2-celled, introrse. Ovary inferior, 6-ribbed, 3-carpellate, unilocular, with ± intruded parietal plancetas; ovules many, anatropous; style short; stigma 3-lobed, usually petaloid. Fruit a berry or rarely a loculicidal capsule. Seeds many; endosperm copious; embryo small. Two genera and about 13 species distributed in pantropical regions of the world; two genera and six species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Small trees, shrubs or subshrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, scalelike, usually sessile, commonly with salt glands; stipule absent. Flower bisexual, actinomorphic, solitary or arranged in spikes, racemes or panicles. Calyx 4 –5-lobed, imbricate, persistent. Petals 4 –5, imbricate, deciduous or persistent. Stamens 4 –5, isomerous and alternate with or twice as many as petals, distinct or connate at lower part. Anthers dorsifixed; 2-celled, dehiscing via longitudinal slits, extrorse, latrorse, or introrse. Disc with 5–10 glands. Pistil 1, composed of 2–5 carpels. Ovary superior, 1-locular; ovules 2–many; styles absent or 3–5, distinct or connate; stigmas 3–5. Capsules loculicidal. Seeds with a bundle of hair or winged. Endosperm present or absent, embryo well differentiated, straight. Four genera, 120 species, widely distributed in temperate and subtropical Eurasia and Africa; three genera and 32 species in China; one genus and one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees, monoecious; trunk straight; main branches more or less whorled. Leaves monomorphic, dimorphic, or trimorphic on same tree, spirally arranged or rarely decussate, lanceolate, subulate, scalelike, or linear. Microsporophylls, bracts and cone scales spirally arranged, rarely decussate. Pollen cones in panicles, or solitary or clustered at branch apices, or axillary, small; microsporangia with 2–9 pollen sacs; pollen nonsaccate. Seed cones terminal or subterminal on previous year's growth; bracts and cone scales semiconnate and free only at apex, or completely united; ovules 2–9 per bract axil, erect or pendulous; cone scales of mature cones flattened or shieldshaped, woody or leathery, 2–9-seeded on abaxial side. Cotyledons 2–9. Nine genera and 12 species, mainly in N temperate; eight genera (one endemic, three introduced) and nine species (one endemic, four introduced) in China; four genera (one native and three introduced) and four species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, pinnately veined, exstipulate. Flowers axillary, rarely terminal, solitary, or sometimes fascicled, bisexual, or rarely unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals mostly 5, rarely 4 or many, imbricate, distinct or very shortly connate at the base. Petals 5, rarely more, distinct or connate at base. Stamens many, in 2–6 series, rarely as few as 5, distinct or connate at base, usually adnate to the base of petals. Ovary superior, rarely half-inferior, 2–10-locular, ovules 2 to many per locule, placentas axile; styles as many as carpels, distinct to connate at base. Fruit a capsule, a berry or a drupe; seeds 1 to many, winged or not, sometimes arillate; embryo large, straight or curved; endosperm present or absent, rarely abundant. About 21 genera and 500 species, mostly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 12 genera and about 270 species in China; ten genera, 32 species and four varieties in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, rarely herbs. Leaves simple, alternate or opposite, entire, exstipulate. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, in heads, umbels, racemes, panicles or spikes, rarely flower solitary. Flowers bisexual or unisexual (plant dioecious). Calyx tubular or campanulate, lobes 4– 5, petaloid, imbricate. Petals wanting or scale-like. Stamens as many as or two times as many as calyx lobes, rarely 2 or 1, in 2 (or 1) whorls, usually inserted at the middle part and throat of calyx; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk annular or cupular, unlobed or divided into 2 – 4 scales. Ovary superior, 1(–2)-locular; ovules 1(–3), anatropous; style 1; stigma capitate or clavate. Fruit a drupe, nut or berry, rarely a capsule. Embryo straight; endosperm present or wanting. About 50 genera and 720 species widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions of the world, especially in Australia and tropical Africa; ten genera and ca. 90 species in China; three genera and six species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or herbs, usually with stellate or peltate scales. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, entire or serrate, sometimes lobed, palmately or pinnately veined. Stipules present, often deciduous, rarely persistent. Inflorescence cymose or cymose-paniculate. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual and dioecious, actinomorphic. Bracts caducous, sometimes large and persistent. Sepals (3 –)5, valvate, distinct, sometimes connate at base. Petals as many as sepals, distinct, imbricate or convolute or valvate, sometimes lacking, usually glandular adaxially. Stamens usually many, distinct or united into 5 –10 bundles at base, anthers 2-celled, dehiscent longitudinally or apically. Ovary superior, 2– 6-locular, sometimes more, ovules 1 to numerous per locule on axile placenta. Style 1, branched or not; stigma capitate or lobed. Fruit a drupe, capsule, sometimes berry-like or samara, 2–10-locular. Seeds usually not arillate, endosperm copious, embryo erect, cotyledons flat. About 52 genera and 500 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical areas; 11 genera and about 77 species in China; four genera and eight species with one additional variety in Hong Kong.

Saprophytic small herbs with simple stem, white, yellow or purplish, not green. Leaves reduced to scales. Inflorescence a terminal bracteate raceme. Flowers very small, actinomorphic, monoecious, or dioecious, rarely polygamous. Perianth segments 3–6(–10), 1-seriate, valvate, sometimes basally connate and with apical appendages, reflexed after flowering. Male flowers with (2–)3 or 6 stamens, sometimes 3 fertile and 3 staminodes, filaments very short or absent, anther sometimes sunk in receptacle, 2- or 4-celled, cells subglobose, at length confluent and opening by a transverse slit; connective sometimes produced into long subulate appendages. Female flowers rarely with staminodes; carpels 10 – many, free, 1-locular; style terminal to almost basal; ovule solitary. Fruiting carpels crowded in a mass, obovoid, opening by a longitudinal slit. Seeds with copious endosperm and small, undifferentiated embryo. Nine genera and 45 species widespread in tropical and subtropical regions, but seldom seen or collected; one genus and four species in China; one genus and two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs. Roots sometimes tuberous. Stems ± succulent, often climbing. Leaves simple, peltate or palmately lobed or divided, alternate, stipulate. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, large, solitary, axillary. Sepals 5, imbricate, adaxial 1(or 3) extended into a nectariferous spur. Petals 5, imbricate, the abaxial 3 often different, clawed. Stamens 8, in 2 whorls, distinct, unequal; anthers 2-celled, dehiscent by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 3-locular, placentation axile; ovule 1 per locule, pendulous from axile apex, anatropous. Style 1; stigma 3-lobed. Fruits separating into 3 one-seeded mericarps, fleshy or dry. Seed without endosperm; embryo straight. Three genera and about 90 species distributed in C and S America; one species cultivated and sometimes naturalized in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, monoecious, with creeping rhizomes, growing in marshes and shallow freshwater. Leaves alternate, radical and cauline, distichous, sheathed at base; leaf blade linear, usually spongy, margin entire. Flowers unisexual, minute, many, densely crowded in a club-shaped spike with the staminate flowers occurring on the upper part and the pistillate flowers on the lower part; bracts deciduous or sometime absent. Perianth consist of many slender threads or elongated spoon-shaped scales mixed with ovaries or stamens; male flower: stamens 1–3, surrounded by hairs, filaments free or fused at base; anthers 2-thecous, basifixed, opening by longitudinal slits; connective thickened, enlarged at apex; pollen grains in monads or tetrads; female flowers: ovary 1-locular, on a long capillary stalk with many fine hairs or bracteoles at base; styles capillary; stigmas broadened or spatulate. Fruit minute, falling off together with pedicel. One genus and about 16 species widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions; one genus and 12 species (two endemic) in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen trees or shrubs. Stipules opposite. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite, base often oblique, margin serrulate, pinnately veined or triveined, caducous. Inflorescence a cyme or flowers solitary. Flowers small, wind-pollinated, unisexual (plant monoecious), bisexual or polygamous. Sepals 3–8, free or connate at base, imbricate or introrse valvate. Petals absent. Stamens as many as sepals and opposite to them, or rarely twice as many or up to 15; filaments straight, free. Anthers 2-celled, dehiscent longitudinally; ovary superior, 1-locular or rarely 2-locular; styles 2; ovules solitary, pendulous. Fruit a samara, drupe or nut. Seeds single, endosperm absent or rather scanty; cotyledons compressed or contorted. About 16 genera, 230 species distributed in tropical and temperate regions, especially in N hemisphere; eight genera and 46 species in China; four genera and nine species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, very rarely trees or lianas, often with cystoliths in epidermal cells of leaves and stems. Leaves simple, alternate or opposite, mostly stipulate. Inflorescence basically cymose, variously modified, often condensed into heads. Flowers small, mostly green, unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious). Perianth biseriate, of 4–5 distinct or connate sepal-like lobes. Male flowers mostly with 4 stamens, opposite to the perianth-lobes, bent inward in the bud; anthers 2-celled; rudimentary pistil often present. Female flowers with a single pistil; ovary superior, free or adnate to perianth, containing a single erect basal ovule; style 1, ending in a brush-like stigma or bearing along its length long collecting hairs; scale-like staminodes often present. Fruit an achene or a drupe often enclosed by persistent perianth. About 47 genera and 1300 species widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions; 25 genera and 341 species in China; seven genera and 17 species with two subspecies and one variety in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, sometimes climbing shrubs, rarely herbs. Indumentum of simple, stellate, and/or other complex hairs. Leaves opposite or rarely whorled, without stipules, simple or 3‑foliolate, less often palmately (or pinnately) compound. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, cymose, spicate, or thyrses. Flowers bisexual or polygamous by abortion, zygomorphic or rarely actinomorphic. Calyx persistent. Corolla 4‑ or 5‑ or more lobed; lobes usually spreading, aestivation overlapping. Fertile stamens inserted on corolla tube, alternate with lobes; filaments free; anthers dorsifixed, 1‑ or 2‑locular, dehiscing by longitudinal slits or sometimes a circular pore. Ovary entire or 4‑grooved, 2–8‑locular; ovules 1 or 2 per locule, erect or pendulous. Style terminal, simple, entire or 2‑cleft. Fruit a drupe or indehiscent capsule, sometimes breaking up into nutlets. Seeds (1 or)2–4, endosperm usually absent, seed coat thin; embryo straight, as long as seed; radicle short, inferior. About 91 genera and ca. 2000 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 20 genera and 182 species in China; 14 genera, 35 species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate or rarely opposite, entire or serrate; stipules small or foliaceous. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, very irregular or nearly regular, solitary or in axillary or terminal spikes, racemes or panicles. Sepals 5, imbricate in the bud, persistent. Petals 5, hypogynous, contorted or imbricate in the bud, the lower one usually larger, saccate or spurred at base. Stamens 5, hypogynous, alternate with the petals; filaments very short; anther erect, introrse, free or connected in a ring round the ovary. Ovary superior, consisting of 3 to 5 fused carpels, 1-locular with 3, rarely 4 or 5, parietal placentas. Fruit a capsule dehiscing into as many valves as placentas, or rarely an indehiscent berry. Seeds small, usually spherical, inserted along the centre of the valves of the capsule, attached by very short funicles. About 22 genera and 900 species, cosmopolitan, but chiefly temperate; four genera in China; only one genus in Hong Kong.

Hemiparasitic shrubs, rarely herbs; nodes articulated, often enlarged. Leaves opposite, often reduced to scales; stipules absent; petiole often indistinct; leaf blade, when present, simple, mostly palmately 3–5-veined, margin entire. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, spicate or cymose, sometimes a solitary flower; bracts inconspicuous. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious or monoecious), (2–)3–4-merous, actinomorphic, minute. Perianth lobes free, valvate. Disk absent. Stamens opposite to perianth lobes, adnate or free; anthers 1–many-celled, sometimes connate into synandria, dehiscing longitudinally or by several pores. Ovary inferior, 1-locular, without true ovules. Style simple or absent; stigma small. Fruit a berry. Seed 1; testa absent; endosperm starchy; embryo rather large. About seven genera and 350 species distributed mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; three genera and 18 species in China; two genera and three species in Hong Kong.

Woody or herbaceous vines, usually with tendrils opposite to leaves, rarely small succulent treelets or herbs, hermaphroditic or polygamo-monoecious to polygamo-dioecious. Stems terete or flattened, ridged or striate; nodes often swollen and articulated. Leaves simple or compound, alternate, stipulate or exstipulate. Inflorescences often leaf-opposite, pseudo-terminal, or axillary, in panicles, thyrses, corymbs, rarely in racemes or spikes. Flowers small, actinomorphic, 4–5(–7)-merous. Calyx small, ± reduced to lobes or a collar. Petals valvate, free or basally connate, or distally connate forming a calyptra. Stamens 4–5(–7), opposite to petals; anthers introrse, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk ring-shaped, cupular, or gland-shaped. Ovary superior, 2-locular; ovules 2 per locule, placentation axile; style simple; stigma discoid or capitate, rarely 4-lobed. Fruit a berry, 1–4-seeded. Seeds endotestal with a deep groove either side of raphe; embryo straight, small; endosperm oily, proteinaceous, copious, ruminate. About 14 genera and 900 species distributed worldwide, but mostly in the tropical or subtropical regions; eight genera and 146 species in China; six genera and 16 species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, exstipulate, petiolate. Inflorescence a raceme or panicle, axillary or terminal. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, axillary or terminal. Bracts and bracteoles present. Sepals 5, imbricate, inner 2 slightly larger. Petals 5, unequal, imbricate, sometimes unguiculate, free, keel without apical appendages. Stamens 8; filaments free or 2–4 adherent at base of ovary, other 4–6 adherent at base of petals; anthers introrse, longitudinally dehiscent. Disk annular, fleshy. Ovary superior; carpels 2, connate, stalked, 1-locular, ovules 2–many per locule, anatropous, placentation parietal; style 1, hairy; stigma capitate. Fruit a drupe, globose, fibrous-fleshy when dry, 1-seeded, seed coat membranous, endosperm absent. One genus and 93 species distributed in Australia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs perennial or sometimes annual. Leaves normally arising in tufts from the top of the rootstock, distichous and equitant, narrow and erect, sheathing at base. Flowers bisexual, in terminal heads or dense spikes; bracts conspicuous, spirally imbricate or decussate, persistent or sometimes caducous. Sepals 3, ± zygomorphic (sometimes the median one much larger, or reduced or absent). Corolla actinomorphic or rarely zygomorphic, usually ephemeral; petals 3, yellow, less often white or blue, free, base clawed or sometimes connate, or forming a long tube. Stamens 3, either all bearing anthers or 2 barren and petal-like; filaments short, adnate and opposite to petals, rarely free; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary superior; style filiform, apex 3-branched or simple. Capsule oblong, 3-valved, loculicidal. About five genera and 300 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; one genus and six species in China; one genus and three species in Hong Kong.

Palm-like plants, dioecious. Stem subterranean to arborescent. Leaves even-pinnately coumpound, clustered at stem apex; pinnae 10 –120, subopposite to opposite, dichotomously veined, with or without a midrib; petiole and lower third of rachis smooth or with small prickles or with reduced spinose pinnae; stipules small or absent. Strobili one to several, usually emerging from center of crown; sporophylls flat to peltate. Pollen cones: microsporophylls many, with sporangia localited on the abaxial surface and rarely on the adaxial surface; microsporangia many, in groups of 2–5 and dehiscent longitudinally; pollen monosulcate, proximal sculpturing psilate to foveolate. Seed cones: ovule-bearing structure many, megasporophylls stalked, each with two ovules. Seed coat consisting of a red or orange/red or white outer fleshy layer and an inner stony layer when mature; megagametophyte farineacous; embryo with two cotyledons and a coiled suspensor. Eight genera and about 180 species in tropical to warm temperate regions of Africa, Australia, the West Indies and N, S, and C America; one genus and one species cultivated in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial, terrestrial, rarely epiphytic, aromatic herbs, with fleshy, tuberous or non-tuberous rhizomes, often with tuber-bearing roots. Stems usually short, replaced by pseudostems formed by leaf sheaths. Leaves distichous, simple, those toward base of plant usually bladeless and reduced to sheaths; leaf sheath open; ligule usually present; petiole present or not, located between leaf blade and sheath, cushion-like in Zingiber; leaf blade suborbicular or lanceolate to narrowly strap-shaped, rolled longitudinally in bud, glabrous or hairy, margin entire; midvein prominent, lateral veins usually many, pinnate, parallel. Inflorescence terminal on pseudostems or on separate short, sheath-covered shoots arising from rhizomes, cylindrical or fusiform, sometimes globose, lax to dense, few- to many-flowered, sometimes with bracteolate cincinni in bract axils and then a thyrse, sometimes a raceme or spike; bracts present, bracteoles present or absent, often conspicuous, coloured. Flowers bisexual, epigynous, zygomorphic. Calyx usually tubular, thin, split on 1 side, sometimes spathe-like, apex 3-toothed or -lobed. Corolla proximally tubular, distally 3-lobed; lobes varying in size and shape. Androecium ancestrally of 6 stamens in 2 cycles of 3, but only median (adaxial) stamen of inner cycle functional, the other 2 stamens of inner cycle sterile and connate to form a petaloid staminode called a labellum, lateral 2 staminodes of outer cycle petaloid, or forming small teeth at base of labellum, or adnate to labellum, or absent, median staminode of outer cycle always reduced; filament of fertile stamen long or short; anther 2-celled, introrse, dehiscing by slits or occasionally pores; connective often extended basally into spurs and/or apically into a crest. Ovary inferior, 3-locular initially, 1- or 3-locular when mature; ovules ± many per locule; placentation parietal, basal, or axile. Style 1, very thin, placed in a furrow of filament and between anther cells; stigma appearing above anther, funnelform, papillose, ± wet, margin often ciliate. Stylodes 2, reduced to nectaries at apex of ovary. Capsules fleshy or dry, dehiscent or indehiscent, sometimes berrylike. Seeds few or many, arillate; aril often lobed or lacerate. About 54 genera and 1300 species; pantropical with centre of diversity in S and SE Asia, some species in America and subtropical and warm-temperate Asia; 20 genera and 216 species in China; four genera and 19 species in Hong Kong.

Submersed marine perennials, with creeping or tuberous rhizomes. Stems flattened, simple or branched, slender. Leaves in 2 rows, linear or filiform, with open or closed sheath often with stipuloid flanges. Flowers monoecious or dioecious, arranged on one side of spadix, initially enclosed in leaf-sheath; bracts absent. Perianth absent or represented by a row of bract-like lobes on each side of axis; male flower reduced to one 1-celled dorsifixed sessile anther opening by a longitudinal slit; pollen thread-like; female flowers consisting of 1 ovary with 2 stigmas, and 1 pendulous orthotropous ovule. Fruits a small drupe or irregularly dehiscing; seeds pendulous, without endosperm. Three genera and 18 species distributed in warm to cool coasts; two genera and seven species in China; one genus and one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs deciduous, rarely evergreen; winter‑buds small, ovoid, with several pairs of outer scales. Leaves opposite, rarely‑whorled, entire or dentate. Inflorescence a panicle or cluster, or flowers single or paired, axillary or terminal. Calyx‑tube narrow, lobes 2 – 6, conspicuous and accrescent, persistent. Corolla tubular to campanulate, 4 – 5‑lobed. Stamens 4, inserted at base of corolla‑tube. Ovary 3‑locular, only 1 locule fertile and 1‑ovuled; style elongate. Achenes leathery, crowned by persistent calyx, 1‑seeded.

About 30 species distributed in E & C Asia and Mexico; nine species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs. Leaves usually palmately lobed. Flowers solitary, axillary; involucral bracts 5 –15, linear filiform, rarely lanceolate, often caducous. Calyx spathaceous, obliquely split on one side, 5-toothed at the apex, caducous. Corolla funnel-form, yellow, 5-lobed. Staminal tubes shorter than the corolla, antheriferous to base. Ovary with 5 carpels, pubescent; style 5, spatulate-discoid, scabrous. Capsules oblong or cylindric, beaked, loculicidally dehiscent, densely hirsute. Seeds numerous, reniform, glandular-papillose, the papillae regularly arranged in longitudinal rows, rarely scabrid.

Approximately 15 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; six species (including cultivated ones) in China; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annuals, or tufted to rhizomatous perennials. Culms scapose. Leaves eligulate, sometimes reduced to a sheath. Inflorescence depauperate anthelate or capitate with few spikelets, or reduced to single spikelet. Primary bracts short, not sheathing. Spikelets with many densely (spiro-)distichous, deciduous glumes, each subtending a flower. Flowers bisexual. Segments absent. Stamens 2–3. Style deeply 3-fid, style base distinct, thickened, deciduous. Achene mostly obovate, stipitate, rounded trigonous, rarely winged, surfaces often tuberulate, rarely smooth.
