About ten species distributed in tropics or subtropics; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs, stems often elongate and climbing. Stipules linear-lanceoate, exstipellate. Leaves deciduous, even-pinnate; leaflets many-paired, without tendril, the petiole ending in a short point. Racemes axillary, terminal or leaf-opposed. Flowers fasciculate at nodes of rachis, small, rose or white. Calyx truncate, teeth very short, upper 2 subconnate. Corolla longer than calyx, purple, pink or white, vexillum ovate, claw short and broad, more or less adherent to the staminal tube; wings narrowly falcate-oblong; keel longer and broader than wings, arcuate. Stamens 9, connate into a sheath split adaxially; vexillary stamen absent; anthers uniform. Ovary subsessile; ovules numerous; styles short, incurved, not bearded, stigma capitate. Pods oblong or linear, plano-compressed, 2-valved, subseptate within between seeds. Seeds 2–many, subglobose or ellipsoidal, shining, sometimes red and black.

About 12 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; four species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Leaves alternate, cordate at base, palmately nerved. Flowers axillary or terminal, solitary or subpaniculate; bracteoles wanting. Pedicels articulate towards the apex. Calyx cupular, patelliform or campanulate, 5-lobed; lobes ovate or lanceolate. Petals 5, connate and adnate to the staminal tube at base. Staminal tube filamentiferous at apex. Ovary 12–15 carpellate; styles as many as carpels; stigmas capitate. Fruits subglobose or turbinate, ripe carpels separating from the cylindric columella. Seeds 2 to 9 in each carpel, reniform, radicle ascending or pointing inward, stellate pilose or glandular papillose.

Over 150 species, in tropical or subtropical regions of both hemispheres; nine species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or woody climbers, very rarely herbs, often very prickly or spiny. Stipules spinescent or fugacious, rarely membranous. Petioles and leaf-rachis glandular. Leaves bipinnate, with many pairs of small leaflets or reduced to a simple phyllodium. Inflorescence cylindric spikes or globose heads, sometimes forming a large panicle; bracts often 2, connate, scale-like, under the head or in the middle or at the base of the peduncle. Flowers small, bisexual or polygamous, usually yellow, rarely white. Calyx campanulate. Petals usually ± united, rarely absent. Stamens numerous, exserted, filaments free or connate at base. Anthers minute, without glands. Ovary sessile or stipitate, with many ovules in 2 rows; style filiform; stigma small, capitate. Pods oblong to linear, straight or curved, flat to terete, membranous to woody, dehiscent into 2 valves or indehiscent. Seeds many, compressed, testa hard and glossy.

About 1200 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 18 species (including cultivated) in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs or treelets. Leaves alternate, dentate or subentire, 3–5-veined from the base or pinnately-veined; stipules lanceolate or subulate, deciduous. Flowers apetalous, in axillary or termianal spikes or racemes of unisexual or androgynous; perianth small and calyx-like. Male flowers: clustered in axils of minute bracts; calyx-lobes 4, valvate in bud; anthers usually 8; filaments free; anther-cells 2, divaricate or pendulous, wavy or tortuous; rudimentary pistil absent. Female flowers: 1–6 subtended by a leafy bract; calyx-lobes 3–5, imbricate in bud; ovary 3- or 2-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 3, finely branched. Capsules small, usually dehiscing into 3 bivalved cocci; pericarp hairy or softly echinate.

About 450 species in world, chiefly in tropical and subtropical regions; 17 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Large fleshy epiphytic herbs with monopodial growth. Roots stout, long, branched. Leaves band-like, 20 × 5 cm. Scape shortly pedunculate. Flowers rather small, in axillary small panicles; sepals and petals similar in colour and size, free, spreading, with transverse bars; lip 3-lobed, attached to the base of the column, slightly saccate at the base, papillose-velvety, fleshy; column short, stout, without wing or foot, with a tooth on each side of the apex; clinandrium truncate; rostellum obtuse; anther semiglobose; pollinia 4 in 2 globose pairs, waxy, on a slender stipe; viscidium ovate; stigma large, suborbicular; ovary cylindrical. Capsules cylindrical, erect, erostrate.

About five species distributed in S and SE Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs with large fleshy purplish brown conical erect pseudobulbs. Stem erect, changing into pseudobulb after anthesis. Cataphylls green at flowering time. New shoot emerging from the base of a mature pseudobulb, consisting of two elements, the flowering branch and the leafy shoot. Leaves 3 or 4, apical to a pseudobulb, chartaceous, arching, plicate-venose. Flowers mediumsized, hardly opening, in a loose raceme axillary to a cataphyll of a developing new shoot; sepals fleshy, coherent and forming an oblique ventricose-urceolate tube, the odd sepal linear, the lateral ones oblique, adnate to the column-foot forming a mentum, reflexed at the apex; petals largely concealed, narrower than the lateral sepals; lip short and broad, attached to the elongate and curved column-foot, movable, 3-lobed, the lateral lobes rectangular, erect, midlobe short, recurved, disk lamellate; column thick, winged, the base produced to an incurved foot; clinandrium short, membranous; rostellum truncate; anthers terminal, incumbent, cucullate; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, each group with a small front pair and a large hind pair, oblong-obovoid, connected by a granular mass at the apex; stigma triangular; ovary cylindrical. Capsules oblong-ellipsoidal, strongly ridged.

About ten species distributed in tropical Asia, New Guinea and Pacific islands; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect shrubs or perennial herbs. Leaves opposite, pinnatifid, spinous‑toothed, rarely entire, without cystoliths. Inflorescence of dense terminal or, less commonly, axillary spikes; bracts, ovate, large, spiny‑margined, growing in size as plant mature; bracteoles 2 in pair, oblong, or absent. Calyx 4‑lobed, with 2 lobes larger and 1 of them often spine‑toothed. Corolla‑tube short, horny, 1‑lipped, upper lip absent, lower lip elongate, obtusely 3‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments included, stout, attached to corolla throat; anther 1‑thecous, densely hairy, linear‑oblong, bearded along one margin. Ovary 2‑locular, ovules 2 per locule; styles slender, stigma 2‑fid. Capsule ellipsoidal, shiny, retinacula present, 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, glabrous, muricate, glandular.

About 50 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World, S Europe; three species and one variety in China; one species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, andro-monoecious, andro-dioecious or dioecious. Leaves often simple and palmately lobed, rarely pinnately or palmately 3–5-foliolate. Inflorescence corymbiform or umbelliform, sometimes racemose or large paniculate. Sepals (4–)5. Petals (4–)5(–6), rarely 0. Stamens (4–)8(–12); filaments distinct. Carpels 2; ovules (1–)2 per locule. Fruit a winged schizocarp, commonly a double samara, usually 1-seeded.

About 130 species widespread in both temperate and tropical regions of Asia, Europe, N and C America, and N Africa; 98 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, rarely subshrubs. Stems decussately branched, with tumid nodes. Leaves opposite, without stipules. Flowers bisexual, in terminal or axillary spikes. Perianth-segments 4–5, slightly unequal, usually glabrous, terminating gradually in a hard sharp point, hardened after flowering, with 1 subulate almost spinous bracteole on each side. Stamens 5; filaments united at the base into a cup, with as many small scale-like staminodes between the filaments; anthers 2-celled. Ovary 1-locular; style simple, with a capitate stigma. Utricles indehiscent, 1-seeded, falling with the persistent perianth and bracteoles.

About six species in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in the Old World; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, pinnately-veined, with oil glands, petiolate. Inflorescence a cyme or thyrse; bracts small, deciduous after flowering. Flowers bisexual, small. Hypanthium obconic or semiglobose. Calyx-lobes 4–5, incurved. Petals 5, distinct or united into a calyptra. Stamens many, distinct, in several whorls; filaments short; anthers minute, 2-celled; cells divergent, dehiscing by an apical pore. Ovary inferior, 2–3-locular; ovules many per locule. Style linear, short. Fruit drupaceous, 1-seeded. Seeds often with a pseudotesta adhering to pericarp; embryo straight, not lobed.

About 11 species distributed in India, Malaysia, Indonesia to Australia; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Two species in China, one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms creeping and often rooting near the base. Leaf blades lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, flat, usually with obscure transverse veins; ligule a narrow membrane. Inflorescence of lax racemes along a central axis, sometimes panicle-like due to irregular secondary branching. Spikelets paired or solitary, obscurely 2-rows, deciduous at maturity below the glumes, florets 2; lower floret staminate or barren, upper floret bisexual; glumes subequal or lower glume shorter, papery, 3–5-veined; upper glume and lower lemma equal, 5-veined, thickened and laterally compressed at apex to form a green crest; upper lemma dorsally compressed, crustaceous, the margins inrolled embraced and enclosed same texture palea, apex glabrous with a little green crest; upper palea with reflexed apex slightly protruding from lemma. Caryopsis elliptic.

About 19 species spread over the tropics; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or trees, unarmed. Leaves opposite, unifoliolate or digitately 3-foliolate; leaflets entire. Inflorescence a thyrse, axillary. Flowers bisexual, 4-merous. Sepals 4. Petals 4, distinct, valvate. Stamens 8, distinct, in 2 whorls; filaments hairy at lower half. Disk small. Carpels connate; ovary 4-locular, ovule 1 per locule; stigmas slightly thicker than styles. Fruit a drupe with 4 drupelets. Seeds solitary or in pairs, endosperm fleshy.

About 44 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Australia and Pacific Islands; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or semi-deciduous woody vines, polygamous or dioecious. Branches glabrous or hairy, often lenticellate. Stipules minute or absent. Leaves papery, membranous or leathery, margin serrate or rarely entire, often long petiolate. Inflorescence cymose, axillary, several- or many-flowered, or flowers solitary. Flowers variable in colour. Sepals 5, sometimes 4 or 6, distinct or connate at base, imbricate, rarely valvate, persistent or not. Petals 5, rarely 4 or 6, imbricate, rarely convolute. Stamens many; filaments slender; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Disc absent. Ovary many-locular; ovules many per locule; styles as many as carpels (15 –30), usually reflexed, persistent. Fruit a berry, globose, ovoid, or ellipsoid, spotted with lenticels or not, glabrous or hairy. Seeds many, small, immersed in pulp; testa reticulate-pitted; endosperm copious; embryo straight, cotyledons short.

About 50 species distributed in SE Asia; 48 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennials. Rhizome creeping. Leaves basal; blades present of leaves reduced to basal sheath; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaflike or subulate. Inflorescence a single capitate cluster of spikelets. Spikelets flattened to subterete. Glumes 2-ranked, lower 2–3 empty and smaller. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 3. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly ovate, trigonous, smooth or verruculose, indistinctly reticulate.

Four to five species in Old World tropics; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Unarmed trees. Stipules small, caducous. Leaves bipinnate, spirally arranged, without glands; leaflets small, alternate, in many pairs. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate, axillary or terminal. Flowers white or yellowish, bisexual or polygamous, shortly stipitate. Calyx campanulate, shortly 5-toothed. Petals 5, lanceolate, coherent below middle or soon free. Stamens 10, free, slightly longer than petals. Anthers ovate, with a deciduous gland at apex. Ovary sessile, many-ovuled; style filiform; Pods strap-shaped, straight, falcate or slightly twisted, leathery, septate between seeds, dehiscent along sutures when ripe. Seeds thick, testa hard, scarlet or two-coloured, mostly enclosed by a thin pulp.

Ten species distributed in tropical Asia and Pacific Islands; one species in mainland China and Hong Kong.

Herbs, erect or creeping, frequently aromatic, blackened when dry, eglandular or glandular villose. Leaves opposite; leaf blade glandular punctate, margin serrate. Flowers in racemes, spikes or heads, sometimes solitary in axils of apical leaves. Bracteoles 2. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; upper lobe usually larger. Corolla tubular; limb 2‑lipped; lower lip spreading, 3(–4)‑lobed; upper lip erect, emarginate or entire. Stamens 4, didynamous, included. Anther 2‑celled; cells separate, short stipitate, 1 or 2 cells of anterior anthers abortive, 2 (or 1) cells of posterior anther fertile; styles apex dilated, entire or 2‑lobed. Capsules ovoid to ellipsoidal, septifragal, 4‑valved, apex ± beaked. Seeds numerous, minute; testa reticulate.

About 15 species distributed in S & SE Asia, Pacific islands; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Anuual herbs, stem erect with opposite leaves trinerved at the base and usually serrate. Capitula homogamous, arranged in terminal corymb or corymbose panicles. Involucres campanulate or hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, 2‑seriate, subequal in length. Receptacle plain, without palea. All florets fertile, corolla white, tubular, lobes 5; anther bases obtuse to subtruncate; stylar branches long and exserted, compressed, apex obtuse. Cypselae 3–5‑costate, apex rounded, glandular or tuberculate. Pappus in clavate form, 3–5, each ending with a gland.

About 20 species distributed in tropical America; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees; terminal buds inconspicuous, loosely surrounded by stipules. Stipules interpetiolar, triangular, bifid, usually persistent. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Flowers bisexual, regular, densely crowded in globular heads on axillary or terminal peduncles, solitary or paniculate. Receptacles hairy. Calyx‑tube short; limb 5‑lobed, persistent. Corolla‑tube slender, lobes 5, valvate in the bud. Stamens 5, inserted in corolla‑tube; filaments short; anthers basifixed, introrse. Ovary 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style exserted, with capitate stigma. Fruit capsular, septicidally dehiscing into 2 valves, many‑seeded; seeds narrow oblong, with a narrow edge or wing.

Three species in E Asia and Indochina; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves distichous, entire or serrulate, petiolate. Flowers axillary, solitary or in pairs, bisexual; pedicels usually recurved, rarely erect; bracteoles 2, attached near apex of pedicel, persistent or deciduous; sepals 5, unequal, imbricate, connate at base, persistent; petals 5, imbricate, connate at base; stamens 15–many, 1– 5-seriate, filaments more or less connate at base, adnate to base of sepals; anthers basifixed, apiculate, base subrounded, hispid; ovary 2– 5-locular; ovules usually many per locule; style simple or 3 – 5-lobed, persistent. Fruit baccate, indehiscent. Seeds many to few.

About 80 species, mostly in tropical Asia, a few in New Guinea and tropical Africa; 21 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial or epiphytic acaulescent herbs, stoloniferous. Leaves rosulate, linear or linear-lanceolate, with a broadened, channelled base, often with marginal spines, frequently scaly. Scape well developed. Inflorescence a spikes or panicle; flowers distichous or polystichous, sessile or stipitate, perfect. Sepals free or connate, usually strongly asymmetric. Petals free, each bearing 2 ± adnate basal scales on the inner side. Stamens included; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary inferior, with few to many ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma contorted or not. Berry dry or fleshy, indehiscent, many-seeded.

More than 180 species, mostly in Mexico and the West Indies to Argentina; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, commonly occuring in mangrove. Leaves alternate, entire, glabrous. Inflorescence consisting of terminal, axillary or leaf-opposed umbels or panicles. Flowers bisexual, 5-merous, pedicellate. Calyx split to base, lobes leathery twisted to the left. Corolla with a short tube, lobes overlapping to right in bud, recurved during aestivation. Stamens with lower part of filaments fused into a tube and inserted on the base of corolla; anthers with transversely septate cells, introrse, dehiscing by longitudinal slit. Ovary fusiform, narrowed into an elongated style; stigma punctiform; ovules many immersed in central globose placenta. Fruit 1-seeded, cylindric, curved, with leathery pericarp; germination of seeds often taking place while still on the plants.

Two species on tropical sea coast of Asia and Australia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Herbs fleshy, with very short and simple stems. Flowers large, solitary or clustered at stem apex, without bracteoles; pedicel more than 5 cm long, erect. Calyx spathe‑like, apex acute or obtuse to rounded. Corolla tubular or campanulate, indistinctly bilabiate; subequally 5‑lobed. Stamens 4, included; anthers adherent, 1 cell fertile, another reduced into a spur. Carpels 2; ovary usually 1‑locular and parietal placentas 2 or 4, occasionally imperfectly 2‑locular and placentas axile. Style slightly curved; stigma fleshy, peltate. Capsule dehiscing by 2 valves. Seeds many.

About four species in tropical and subtropical Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous small trees, armed with sharp spines. Leaves alternate, digitately 3-foliolate. Flowers bisexual, solitary or in few-flowered thyrses, white, fragrant, 5-merous. Sepals connate at base. Petals imbricate. Stamens many, sometimes united into a staminal tube, filaments short, apex subulate; anthers long. Disk small. Styles short, stigmas slightly thicker than styles, finely furrowed. Ovary terete, 8–20-locular, ovules many per locule. Fruit globose or pyriform. Pericarp woody, locular wall thick, fleshy. Seeds many, embedded in fragrant, viscid juice, ellipsoidal and slightly flattened; seed coat woolly hairy.

One species distributed in SE Asia; it is cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or climbers. Leaves opposite, or rarely whorled; leaf blade thin papery or leathery, margin entire; lateral veins indistinct. Inflorescences umbel‑like, axillary or pseudoterminal, 1–10‑flowered cymes; bracts 2, opposite, ovate or lanceolate. Calyx actinomorphic, cylindric or campanulate, 5‑sect from base to 5‑lobed. Corolla red to yellow, rarely greenish or white, zygomorphic; tube narrowly tubular to funnelform‑tubular, often curved, longer than limb; limb indistinctly or distinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes equal or subequal. Stamens 4, adnate to corolla tube near or above middle, usually exserted; anthers basifixed, usually coherent in pairs at apex, thecae parallel, not confluent at apex, dehiscing longitudinally; staminode 1 or absent, adnate to adaxial side of corolla tube. Disk ring‑like. Ovary linear or oblong, 1‑loculed; placentas 2, parietal, projecting inward, 2‑cleft; stigma 1, capitate to depressed‑globose, undivided. Capsule straight, linear, dehiscing loculicidally to base; valves 2 or 4, straight. Seeds with 1(–50) hair‑like appendages, opposite end with 1 hair‑like appendage, seldom 1 linear appendage at each end.

About 140 species in Asia, Pacific islands; 35 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Stems erect or decumbent. Stipules medifixed caducous; stipels absent. Leaves even-pinnate; rhachis ending in a short point; leaflets numerous, closely arranged, sensitive. Racemes axillary, several-flowered. Bracts paired, persistent; bracteoles adnate to calyx. Calyx usually 2-lipped, upper lip 2-lobed, lower lip 3-lobed. Corolla yellow, often lined with purple; petals clawed; vexillum large, orbicular; wings obliquely obovate or oblong, subequal to vexillum; keel slightly incurved, ± beaked. Stamens diadelphous (5+5), or connate at base; anthers uniform. Ovary stipitate, 2–many-ovuled; styles incurved; stigma terminal. Pods linear, stipitate, compressed, 2 –many-segmented; segments flat or convex in middle, indehiscent or rarely dehiscent along dorsal suture. Seed 1.

About 250 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions all over the world; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial stout herbs. Stems very short or indistinct. Leaves in a basal rosette, large, stout, leathery-fleshy or somewhat woody, containing many fibers, apex tipped with a spine, margin usually spiny, rarely entire. Flowering stems branched or simple, tall, stout. Inflorescence terminal, a spike or panicle, mostly very large. Perianth tube short; lobes narrow, subequal. Stamens inserted at throat or in tube of perianth; filament filiform, usually longer than perianth; anther versatile. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, ovules many per locule. Style slender; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit a capsule, oblong, 3-valved, loculicidal. Seeds many, black, thin, flattened.

About 200 species distributed in arid and semiarid regions of the W hemisphere; two species (introduced) in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Additionally, A. angustifolia(狹葉龍舌蘭) is also cultivated as garden plants in Hong Kong but not described in this account.

Annual or perennial, herbs or shrubs. Leaves opposite or with some alternate on upper portion. Capitula homogamous, in terminal corymbose clusters or rarely in loose panicles. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries imbricate in 2–3 series. Receptacles plain or dome‑shaped, naked or some with caducous scales. All florets tubular, corolla regular, 5‑lobed; stamens obtuse and entire at base, with apical appendages; stylar branches clavate, long, apex obtuse. Cypselae 5‑angulate; pappus 1‑seriate, scarious and aristate.

About 30 species in tropical America; two species cultivated, with Ageratum conyzoides naturalized in China and in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, dioecious. Leaves imparipinnate or trifolioliate, rarely simple, alternate, lepidote or stellately pubescent at least on young parts; leaflets entire. Inflorescence an axillary panicle. Male inflorescences large and many-flowered, female ones smaller, few-flowered and sometimes reduced to a short spike. Calyx 3–5-lobed, or with distinct sepals, imbricate. Petals 3–5(–6), distinct or connate at base, imbricate. Staminal-tube usually subglobose, urceolate, campanulate or rarely shortly cylindrical, margin entire, crenate, or shallowly lobed; anthers 5 or 6(–12), inclusive or slightly exserted. Disk absent or inconspicuous. Ovary 1–2(–5)-locular, ovules 1 or 2 per locule. Style short or absent; stigma disciform or clavate. Fruit a berry, nut, or rarely capsule; pericarp leathery, often containing latex. Seeds 1–several, usually surrounded by a fleshy aril; endosperm absent.

About 120 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, tropical Australia, Pacific Islands; eight species in China; one species and one variety often cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect or ascending, rarely branched. Leaves spirally arranged; petiole sheathed, clasping the stem; leaf blade usually oblong-ovate to oblong-lanceolate; midrib strong. Inflorescences subterminal, usually several together; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe erect, ovate-lanceolate or ovate, yellowish green or white inside; spadix cylindrical: female portion at the base fewflowered, about 1/3 – 1/4 the length of male portion; male portion above the female, densely flowered. Male flower: stamens 2, free; anthers sessile, apically dehiscent by a slit or a pore; staminodes between male and female portions of spadix, few, anther-like. Female flower: ovary 1(–2)-locular with 1 ovule in each locule; stigma discoid or funnelform, sessile or nearly so. Berries ovoid or oblongovoid, deep yellow or red, 1-seeded; seed oblong, large.

About 21 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia; two species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with stout creeping rhizomes and erect leafy stems, usually hairy and often glandular. Leaves alternate, interruptedly imparipinnate, the cauline ones with small leaflets interspersed between large leaflets, leaflets several pairs, incised-serrate; stipules large, foliaceous, usually deeply toothed or laciniate, adnate to the base of petioles, persistent. Inflorescence a spike-like raceme, terminal or axillary, often interrupted; pedicels at base, subtended by a laciniate bract, bearing 2 trifid bracteoles near apex. Flowers rather small, 5-merous, bisexual. Hypanthium obconic to turbinate, armed distally with erect or patent, hooked bristles, hardened and 1-grooved at maturity. Epicalyx absent. Sepals 5, imbricate, connivent after anthesis, persistent. Petals 5, yellow, rarely white, larger than the sepals. Disk lining the sepals, margin thickened, annular, glandular. Stamens 5– 15 or more, inserted at the mouth of hypanthium, 1-seriate. Pistils usually 2, free; ovary superior, 1-locular, concealed with the hypanthium; styles terminal, filiform, exserted, stigma dilated, ovules 1 per locule, pendulous. Achenes 1–2, usually only 1 per flower developing, enclosed with the hardened, 10-ribbed hypanthium, distally with hooked prickles; each achene with a single seed; pericarp thin. Seeds pendulous; testa membranous.

About 15 species mostly in N temperate regions and alpine tropical regions; four species in China; one species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, free or united at the base. Flowers in cymes, few‑ or many‑flowered, axillary, leaves opposite, or lateral on aphyllous nodes. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped or bell‑shaped; limb (4–)5‑lobed. Corolla salverform, usually glabrous outside, hairy on the throat; tube cylindric; lobes usually 5, often recurved, contorted in the bud. Stamens usually 5, attached to the throat, alternate with corolla‑lobes; filaments very short; anthers dorsifixed, exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule, immersed in a fleshy axile placenta; style slender; stigma clavate or fusiform, 2‑lobed. Fruit a berry, many‑seeded.

About 50 species in tropical Africa, S & SE Asia to Australia; seven species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or small trees, polygamo-dioecious; branchlets pubescent, with a pith. Leaves imparipinnate or paripinnate, alternate; leaflets opposite or nearly so. Inflorescence a thyrse, axillary or terminal. Flowers small, 5-merous. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes imbricate. Petals 5, valvate. Disk 10-lobed. Stamens 10, inserted at base of disk. Carpels 2–5, free or slightly connate only at base; ovules 1–2 per locule, campylotropous or anatropous; styles 2–5, connate. Fruit a samara, long-elliptic, with a seed surrounded by wing. Seed 1, flat, orbicular, obovate or slightly deltoid; endosperm few or wanting.

About ten species distributed in Asia to N Oceania; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, simple or rarely branched. Leaves rosulate at base or subverticillate at a distance from the rhizomes or on stem middle, margin entire, toothed or lobed, petiolate. Capitula homogamous and discoid, narrow, sessile or shortly pedunculate, often nodding, solitary or few to many arranged as spikes, racemes or panicles, usually 3 florets per head, or sometimes with 4 or 5 florets, rarely single. Involucres narrow‑tubular; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate, rigid, outer ones short ovate, inner ones lanceolate to oblong, gradually longer inward. Receptacle small and glabrous. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, upper limb deeply and obliquely cleft into 5 segments, reflexed; anther bases sagittate with basal appendages filiform, bearing apical appendages; stylar branches short and divergent, adaxial side complanate, apices obtuse rounded to truncate. Cypselae oblanceolate, slightly compressed, usually 5–10‑ribbed and hairy, rarely not. Pappus in 1 row, plumose, equal in length, sometimes absent.

About 80 species distributed in E Asia and India; about 40 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaves simple, opposite, petiolate or sessile, margin dentate to incised. Verticillasters 2 – many‑flowered, axillary or in terminal leafy spike‑like inflorescence; bracts similar to stem leaves or gradually reduced upwards. Flowers subsessile. Calyx ovoid to globose, campanulate to funnelform, usually 10‑veined; teeth 5, subequal. Corolla purple to blue, rarely yellow or white; tube straight to slightly curved, base slightly bent/swollen; throat slightly dilated, villous annulate, rarely glabrous inside; limb 1–2‑lipped; the upper lip usually very short, 2‑fid, the lower lip long and spreading or slightly concave, 3‑lobed, the middle lobe the largest, often notched at apex. Stamens 4, in two pairs ascending, exserted from upper lip, lower 2 longer; filaments straight to slightly curved; anthers 2‑celled, divaricate, often confluent at length apically. Ovary shortly 4‑lobed; style subequally 2‑cleft. Nutlets obovoid, triquetrous, netted on back; scar very large, lateral.

About 50 species spreading throughout the Old World; 18 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Ajuga reptans L. var. purpurea Hort. (紫色匍匐筋骨草) is occasionally cultivated for ornamental purpose.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Trees or shrubs, usually unarmed, rarely scandent and with short spines. Stipules usually small, rarely larger and caducous. Leaves bipinnate, with a gland on the petiole below the pinnae, and others between some or all pinnae and leaflets; leaflets small in numerous pairs or larger in few pairs. Flowers bisexual, in globular heads, forming axillary or terminal panicles. Calyx campanulate or funnel-shaped, 5-toothed. Corolla funnel-shaped, 5-lobed, with a cylindric tube. Stamens many, united at base into a tube, free part of filaments long-exserted. The central flowers of heads with broader calyx and much longer filament-tube. Ovary flattened, style long, slender, stigma minute. Pods broadly linear or oblong, straight, plano-compressed, indehiscent, or dehiscent along both sutures, continuous inside. Seeds ovate or orbicular, compressed, funicle filiform.

About 150 species in tropical to subtropical regions of the world; 17 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, usually glandular at the base, and with two stipels at the insertion of petioles, pinnately- or palmately-veined. Flowers apetalous, unisexual (plant monoecious or dioecious) in spikes, racemes or panicles. Male flowers: several clustered in axil of bract; calyx 2–5-lobed, lobes valvate; stamens 4–8, filaments connate at base, discoid; anthers dorsifixed, 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits, without pistillode. Female flowers: solitary in axil of bract; sepals 4–8, sometimes glandular at base; ovary 2–3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 2–3, free or connate at base, usually linear, entire. Capsules of 2 or bivalved cocci, crustaceous, smooth or tuberculate; seeds subglobose.

About 50 species in the tropics and subtropics; seven species and two varieties in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees; young branches densely stellate-hairy. Leaves simple, alternate, entire or 3–5-lobed, palmately-veined; petioles biglandular at apex. Flowers monoecious in terminal panicles; alabastrum subglobose; calyx-lobes and petals 5, imbricate in the bud; disk-glands 5, alternating with petals. Male flowers: much more than female flowers; calyx 2–3-lobed; petals 5, free; disk-glands 5; stamens 15–20, 3–4-seriate, inserted at elevated receptacles; anthers 2-celled, introrse, connective broader. Female flowers: slightly larger than males; calyx initially entire, closed, afterwards irregularly 2–3-lobed; petals 5, free; disk-glands 5; ovary 2–3-locular, with 1-ovule in each locule; styles 2(–3), deeply 2-lobed. Fruit drupaceous, indehiscent; seeds 1–3, depressed globose.

Two species in tropical Asia and Oceania; one species in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs aquatic or marshy, tuberous, rarely rhizomatous, laticiferous or elaticiferous. Leaves basal, emersed or submersed, leaf blades lanceolate, cordate, or sagittate, with white squamules, 3–7-veined. Inflorescence scapose, emergent, verticillate, paniculate. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 3, herbaceous, persistent. Petals 3, white or pink, membranous, deciduous. Stamens 6, filaments filiform. Carpels many, free, whorled at apex of receptacle; styles terminal or lateral; ovule solitary. Achenes few or many, compressed, forming an echinate head. Seeds dark brown, black-purple or purple-red, hippocrepiform.

About 11 species, mainly distributed in N hemisphere; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs erect or trailing. Leaves whorled, with axillary glands. Flowers large, in terminal or seemingly axillary corymbs. Calyx deeply divided, without basal glands. Corolla yellow, funnelform, narrow part with fringed scales, limb campanulate, lobes overlapping to left. Stamens inserted at narrow part of corolla; filaments very short; anthers narrowly oblong, base rounded, coherent with pistil head; disk cup‑shaped, obscurely 5‑lobed or entire, fleshy, thick. Ovary 1‑locular, with two parietal placentae; ovules numerous; style filiform; pistil head thick, with a membranous, reflexed rim, apex conical, shortly 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule globose, glabrous, sharply spiny, 2‑valved. Seeds numerous, imbricate, compressed, winged or with a membranous margin.

About 14 species distributed in tropical America; two species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, united at the base. Flowers in cymes, terminal on lateral short branches or on nodes of old branches. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped or ovoid; lobes 5, triangular or linear. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric, slightly dilated at apex; lobes usually 5, spreading or reflexed, contorted in the bud. Stamens 5, attached to the throat, alternate with corolla‑lobes; filaments very short; anthers dorsifixed, exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2(–3) ovules in each locule on the septum; style slender; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit a berry, globose, 1–2(–3)‑seeded.

About two species in S China and Vietnam; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, bulbiferous, usually with strong onion or garlick odour. Bulb tunicate, various in shape, ranging from cylindrical to globose. Leaves sessile, usually linear to linear-lanceolate, flat, angled or terete, fistulose or solid, with a closed leaf sheath at base. Scape terminal or lateral. Inflorescence a terminal umbel, enclosed in a spathe-like involucral bract before anthesis; bracteoles present or absent. Perianth segments 6, in 2 whorls, free or united into a tube at base. Stamens 6, in 2 whorls; filaments usually connate at base and adnate to perianth segments, entire or toothed. Ovary superior, often with nectaries at the base, 3-locular, with 1–several ovules in each locule; style simple; stigma entire or 3-cleft. Fruit a loculicidal capsule. Seeds black.

More than 600 species widely distributed in N hemisphere, but mainly in Asia; 133 species in China; four species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms tufted, erect or decumbent. Leaf blades convolute, ovate-oblong to linear, glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs; ligule membranous, ciliate. Inflorescence composed of slender racemes, these digitate or in whorls on a short common axis, rachis triquetrous, spikelets on one side of rachis, sometimes solitary, mostly in pairs, rarely more together, falling as a whole. Spikelets ovate to elliptic, dorsally compressed, florets 2, pedicels unequal; lower glume 1/2 length of spikelet, membranous, 3-veined, acute; upper glume as long as spikelet, herbaceous, 5–7-veined, ciliate along margins; lower floret staminate, lemma herbaceous, glabrous; upper lemma cartilaginous, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea, 5-veined, shortly awned; lodicules 2; stamens 3; styles 2, free, stigmas exserted laterally. Caryopsis ellipsoidal.

Five species distributed in tropical regions of Old World; two species China and in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees, bud scales absent. Leaves alternate, margin serrate; stipules absent. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate; bracteoles small, deciduous; pedicels articulate. Flowers bisexual; calyx tube cup-shaped, 5-toothed; corolla campanulate, lobes 5, imbricate; stamens 10, 5 long and 5 short; filaments flattened, mostly connate into a broad tube and adnate to corolla; ovary superior, 5-locular; ovules 8–10 per locule, in 2 longitudinal rows; style linear, slender, stigma obscurely 5- lobed. Fruit a capsule, loculicidally dehiscent into 5 valves, exocarp slightly fleshy. Seeds with irregularly membranous wings at both ends; embryo straight.

Three species in E and SE Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial evergreen herbs with underground tubers or caulescent stock. Leaves usually large, and sometimes peltate; petiole long, sheathing below; leaf blade usually ovate, cordate at base. Inflorescences solitary or several together; spathe convolute or tubular at base, apex constricted, persistent; limb usually cymbiform, falling off from the tube after anthesis; spadix sessile, shorter than sapthe, cylindrical, erect; female portion short, conical-cylindrical at the base; fertile male portion higher up, cylindrical, sterile male portion in the interval; appendage club-shaped. Flowers unisexual; female flowers: ovary 1-locular, with several ovules; stigma discoid-globose, or stellate; male flowers: stamens 3 – 8, sessile, anthers united into pyramidal synandria. Fruit a berry, usually red when mature.

About 70 species in tropical Asia and Malaysia; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, shrubs, or trees. Leaves rosulate, amplexicaul, thick, succulent, always glabrous, margin mostly hard dentate or spiny, apex sharply pointed. Inflorescence a subterminal, ascending to erect raceme, often branched; bracts persistent, scarious. Perianth usually red, orange, or yellow, rarely greenish or whitish, cylindrical to 3-sided, sometimes slightly curved or with swollen base; segments usually connate to form a tube, very rarely nearly free, usually glabrous, apex spreading. Stamens usually exserted; filaments subulate. Ovary 3-locular; ovules many per locule. Style filiform; stigma small. Fruit a loculicidal capsule. Seeds 3-angled or flattened, often winged.

About 350–400 species distributed in S and tropical Africa (including Madagascar), tropical Arabia; one species commonly cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms solitary or tufted, usually geniculate at base. Leaf blades linear, flat; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a spike-like panicle, cylindrical to capitate, with many, closely packed spikelets; pedicels very short, apices cup-like. Spikelets strongly laterally compressed, 1-flowered, falling entire from pedicel; rachilla extension absent; glumes ± equaling and enclosing floret, broadly lanceolate to oblong, membranous to thinly leathery, prominently 3-veined, strongly keeled, keel usually ciliate, infrequently winged, lower margins almost free or connate for up to half their length, apex obtuse, acute or shortly awned; lemma broadly lanceolate to ovate, usually thinly membranous, keeled, obscurely 5-veined, smooth, glabrous, lower margins often connate, awned from lower back, apex truncate to acute; awn straight when short or geniculate when longer, column smooth, usually twisted at maturity, bristle scabrid; palea absent or very small; lodicules absent. Stigmas pubescent, protogynous; ovary glabrous. Caryopsis obliquely obovate in side view; endosperm sometimes liquid.

About 50 species in temperate and cold regions of the N hemisphere and S America; eight species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Rhizomes creeping, thick. Pseudostems many, well developed, rarely absent. Leaves many, rarely 1–4; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, raceme, or spike, dense or lax, covered by 1–3 spatulate involucral bracts when immature. Bracts (when present) open to base, rarely hooded, each subtending 1 flower or a cincinnus of 2–many flowers; bracteoles open to base or tubular, rarely hooded, sometimes absent. Calyx usually tubular, sometimes split on 1 side. Corolla tube not or slightly longer than calyx, 3-lobed above, dorsal one ± hooded, usually wider than lateral lobes. Lateral staminodes small or absent, subulate or tooth-like, adnate to base of labellum. Labellum often showy, usually larger than corolla lobes, sometimes inconspicuous, margin variously lobed or entire. Filament present or absent; connective crested or not. Ovary usually 3-locular and placentation axile. Stigma usually well expanded, sometimes clavate, rarely geniculate. Stylodes often massive. Capsules usually globose, dry or fleshy, indehiscent or irregularly dehiscent. Seeds many, often angled, arillate.

About 230 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia, and Pacific islands; 51 species in China; ten species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, juice milky. Branches whorled, mostly 4 or 5 together. Leaves whorled, rarely opposite, lateral veins numerous, ending in a marginal vein. Cymes terminal, usually 1 – 5 in terminal thyrses or compound umbels. Flowers white, yellow, or pink. Calyx without glands inside, lobes connate at base. Corolla salverform, tube cylindric, dilated in distal half, pubescent inside; lobes overlapping to right or left. Stamens included, inserted near or above middle of corolla‑tube; anthers ovate, free from pistil head, not caudate; disk absent or of scales. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style or syncarpous; ovules numerous. Follicles 2, free or connate. Seeds oblong or linear, flattened, long‑bearded at both ends.

About 43 species distributed from tropical Africa to C America, and from Himalayas and China to New South Wales, Australia; eight species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems prostrate, ascending or erect. Leaves opposite, entire. Flowers bisexual, in axillary or terminal clusters or head-like spikes. Bracts and bracteoles scarious. Perianth-segments 5, nearly equal, scarious. Stamens 5 or sometimes fewer, very shortly united at base; anthers 1-celled; staminodes entire, toothed or fimbriate. Ovary with a solitary ovule; style very short, with a capitate stigma. Utricle usually flattened, ovate or obcordate, indehiscent.

About 80 species widely spread over the tropical and subtropical regions of the world; six species (five introduced) in China and Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees. Leaves petiolate; stipules usually present, minute, linear, caducous or connate with petiole, leaving small scars; leaf blade leathery, margin usually crenate-serrate, occasionally entire, venation pinnate. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious), petals absent. Male inflorescence a globose to shortly cylindrical many-flowered head, pedunculate and grouped in terminal or subterminal racemes or panicles; bracts 1–4. Female inflorescences capitate, 5–30-flowered, bracts 3–4. Male flowers: stamens many; filaments very short; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Female flowers: ovary inferior, 2-locular; ovules many per locule, axile; styles subulate, divergent, often strongly recurved; stigmas papillose, caducous. Infructescences globose. Capsules woody, without persistent calyx teeth and styles, immersed in rhachis. Seeds many, narrowly winged.

About 11 species, distributed in SE Asia; eight species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or diffuse, branched. Leaves simple, rarely pinnately 3-foliolate; stipellate. Racemes axillary or terminal. Flowers small. Bracts scarious, deciduous. Calyx deeply 5-lobed, lobes hard, sometimes imbricate at base, upper 2 often connate to near apex. Corolla scarcely larger than calyx, shortly clawed; vexillum obovate or suborbicular, oblique oblong; wings adherent on keel; keel slightly curved, obtuse, base with membranous appendage. Stamens diadelphous, alternately long and short. Ovary many-ovuled. Pods compressed or terete, transversely constricted or dividing into 1-seeded segments, dehiscent or indehiscent.

About 30 species distributed in tropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Woody lianas or erect to trailing shrubs, with latex. Leaves in whorls of 3 – 4, rarely opposite. Cymes terminal and/or axillary, sometimes in clusters or short thyrses. Flowers small, 5‑merous. Calyx deeply divided, without basal glands. Corolla white or rarely yellow, salverform, tube cylindric, widened at stamens insertion, lobes overlapping to left; corona scales absent. Stamens included, inserted at or above middle of corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers free from pistil head; disk absent. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style; ovules biseriate, 4 – 6 in each carpel. Style filiform; pistil head capitate, apex shortly 2‑cleft. Fruit a drupe, usually moniliform, with one or more subglobose joints, or not jointed. Seeds ovate or oblong; endosperm horny, ruminate; cotyledons leaflike, erect or curved.

About 70 species distributed in tropical Asia, Australia, Pacific islands; 12 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems erect or decumbent. Leaves alternate, entire, petiolate. Flowers unisexual or polygamous, clustered, in axillary or terminal spikes or panicles; each flower subtended by a bract and 2 bracteoles. Perianth-segments 5, rarely 1–4, scarious. Stamens as many as perianth-segments; filaments free; anthers 2-celled, without staminodes. Ovary 1-locular, with a solitary ovule; style divided to the base into 2 or 3 stigmatic lobes. Utricle opening transversely or indehiscent.

About 50 species widely distributed over the warmer regions of the world; 14 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves cordate or ovate-elliptic, entire or slightly digitate-lobed. Cymes leaf-opposed or subterminal and axillary; calyx 5-parted; petals 5, spathulate, claw concave, broadly glandular at base; anthers 15, 3 in group in sinuses of staminal tube; staminodes 5, ciliate, alternate with anthers. Ovary 5-grooved, 5-locular, locule many-ovuled; styles 5, connivent. Capsules membranous, 5-angled or subwinged, truncate at apex. Seeds many, with endosperm; cotyledons flat, cordate.<br/><br/>Two species distributed in Asia to Australia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, dioecious; branchlets opposite, base without persistent bud scales; winter buds tetragonal-ovate, acute, glossy, scales, decussate, in 3–5 whorles of 4, ridged abaxially. Leaves decussate, but brought into a single plane by twisting of petioles; blade straight or slightly falcate, leathery, linear-lanceolate, lanceolate or elliptic-linear, base decurrent, margin slightly downcurved, adaxial surface with evident midvein, abaxial surface with 2 white, yellowish white or pale brown stomatal bands, resin canal present below sheath of vascular bundle, sclereids present, rarely absent. Pollen cones aggregated into (1 or)2– 6(–10) long, slender, compound racemes or spikes arising from bract axil near apex of branches; individual cones opposite, sessile or subsessile, ellipsoid or subglobose; microsporophylls numerous, ± shield-shaped; pollen sacs 3 – 8. Seed-bearing structures compressed-tetragonal or flattened abaxially, basal part with 6–10 pairs of decussate bracts arranged in 4 rows each of 3 –5 bracts; ovule 1, sessile, erect. Seed ripening in 1st year, long pedunculate, ellipsoid or obovoid-ellipsoid, enclosed except for apex in a saclike aril which is bright red or reddish yellow when ripe; bracts persistent at base.

Five or six species in China and Vietnam; three species (one endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong. It was placed in the Taxaceae in W. C. Cheng's system.

Perennial herbs, rhizomatous; stems erect or creeping at the base. Leaves alternate, petiolate. Flowers in sessile heads, each consisting of several cymes, borne at each node of middle part of stem, penetrating leaf sheaths. Sepals free, carinate, herbaceous. Petals free, purplish, oblong or obovate-orbicular. Stamens 6, all fertile, subequal; filaments torulose villous; anther-cells parallel, ovoid, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary 3-locular; ovules 2 per locule, sometimes 1 in posterior locule. Capsule 3-valved, globose or ovoid, trigonous. Seeds (1–)2 per valve, cylindrical, trigonous, rugose, reticulate.

About 20 species in tropical Africa and Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems erect, slender, many-branched, often 4-angled. Leaves opposite, sessile, without stipules. Flowers small, 4–numerous, actinomorphic, often in axillary cymes or densely fasciculate, rarely solitary. Bracts 2. Calyx campanulate, globular after flowering, 4–6-toothed, with minute appendages between teeth. Petals as many as calyx-lobes, and alternate with it or absent. Stamens 2–8, usually 4. Ovary enclosed within calyx-tube, 2–4-locular, sometimes 1-locular; styles straight; stigma capitate; ovules many on axile placentation. Capsules membranous, lower parts enclosed within calyx-tube, opening whether transversely or irregularly. Seeds numerous, deltoid.

About 30 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mainly in Africa and Asia; four to five species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with fleshy tuberous rhizome. Leaf compound, usually solitary; petiole long, usually smooth, marked with blotches; leaf blade divided into 2 segments, which again once or twice pinnately divided. Peduncle solitary, radical, without bracts under the spathe; spathe funnelform or campanulate at the base, convolute, limb ± spreading; spadix sessile or shortly stipitate, erect; female portion at lower part, continuous with male portion or separated by a sterile portion, the rachis ending in an elongate appendage. Flowers unisexual, without scales or perianth; stamens 1 – 6; ovary 1–4 locular, ovule solitary in each locule. Fruit a berry, subglobose or obovid; seeds 1–4, without endosperm.

About 150 species in the paleotropics, from W Africa, to Australia and Polynesia; 21 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Woody vines, hermaphroditic or polygamo-monoecious. Tendrils 2–3-branched, apex not enlarged nor forming suckers. Leaves simple, 1–2-pinnately or palmately compound, long petiolate. Inflorescence a dichasial cyme, leaf-opposed or pseudoterminal. Flowers small, 5-merous. Calyx saucer-shaped. Petals 5, free. Stamens 5. Disk well developed. Style conspicuous; stigma inconspicuously expanded. Fruit a berry, 1–4-seeded.

About 30 species distributed in Asia, N and C America; 17 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial, or perennial herbs, usually glabrous. Stems erect or decumbent. Leaves opposite or alternate, rarely whorled in three, sessile or short-petiolate. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves, 5-merous. Calyx divided nearly to base. Corolla rotate or funnel-shaped, with a very short tube; lobes contorted in bud. Stamens inserted on base of corolla; filaments usually pubescent; anthers ellipsoid, apex obtuse, dorsifixed. Ovary ovoid; style filiform; stigma obtuse. Capsule globose, circumscissile, many-seeded.

About 20 species spread throughout the temperate zone of both hemisphere; one species in China; it occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Leaves in a dense rosette on the simple, short stem; leaf sheath scarcely enlarged; leaf blade ensiform, margin spinose serrate. Inflorescence terminal, strobiliform, with a tuft of sterile leafy bracts at apex. Flowers bisexual, sessile, in the axils of closely and spirally arranged bracts. Sepals short, imbricate. Petals free, erect, each bearing 2 ligulate scales at base. Stamens 6. Ovaries inferior, coalescing and with bracts and rachis forming a compound, fleshy fruit (syncarp).

Eight species distributed in S America; one species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs with cystoliths. Leaves entire. Inflorescence of terminal or axillary panicle or racemes abbreviated as head‑like. Bracts present; bracteoles small or absent. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed to the base, lobes narrow, equal. Corolla tubular or inflated, limb 2‑lipped, upper lip 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed, imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, exserted or included; filaments linear, or oblate, somewhat pubescent; anther 2‑thecous, thecae equal or unequal, base muticous, sometime hairy. Ovary 2‑locular, 3–many‑ovules per locule; style filiform; stigma 2‑dentate. Capsule linear‑oblong or linear‑elliptic, compressed, retinacula present, 6–many‑seeded. Seeds usually oblong.

About 80 species in tropical regions of Asia extending to Australia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms usually tufted. Leaf blades linear to narrowly linear; ligule scarious or reduced to a line of hairs. Racemes paired or digitate, terminal on the culm or axillary and gathered into a spathate compound panicle; rachis fragile; spikelets paired, 1 sessile, the other pedicellate. Sessile spikelet usually dorsally compressed, usually bisexual; callus short, obtuse, shortly bearded, inserted into internode apex; lower glume lanceolate, membranous to leathery, 2-keeled; upper glume boat-shaped, awned or awnless; lower floret reduced to a hyaline lemma; upper lemma hyaline, 2-lobed, awned from sinus; awn geniculate; stamens 1–3. Pedicellate spikelet male or barren, large or much reduced, awnless.

About 100 species distributed in tropical and warm-temperate regions of both hemispheres; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or biennial glabrous herbs; stem erect, branched. Leaves basal and cauline, 2–3-pinnately dissected, petiolate; ultimate segments filiform or linear. Inflorescence of loose compound umbels, pedunculate; involucral bracts and bracteoles absent; rays numerous, unequal. Calyx-teeth obsolete. Petals yellow, subcordate, apex strongly incurved. Stylopodium conic; styles short, erect when young, spreading or recurved after anthesis. Fruit ellipsoid or ovoid-ellipsoidal, conspicuously flattened dorsally; dorsal ribs filiform, slightly prominent, lateral ribs narrowly winged, tapering at both ends; vittae 1 in each furrow, 2 on commissure. Seed face plane. Carpophore 2-cleft to base.

One species native in Mediterranean region, cultivated and naturalized worldwide; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Biennial or perennial herbs, usually with stout, conic or cylindric taptoot. Leaves basal and cauline petiolate, with conspicuously inflated petiole-sheath; leaf blades 1–4-pinnate or 1–3-ternate-pinnate. Inflorescence of compound umbels, terminal or lateral; involucral bracts many, rarely absent; rays many to several; bracteoles many to a few, entire. Calyx-teeth obsolete or ovate-triangular. Petals white, rarely pink or dark purple, ovate to obovate, apex incurved. Stylopodium short-conic. Fruit ovoid to orbicular, dorsally compressed; dorsal ribs filiform, lateral ribs broad- or narrow-winged, separated when mature; vittae often 1–2 in each furrow, 2–4 on commissure. Seed face plane or slightly concave. Carpophore 2-cleft to base.

Over 90 species in N temperate zone; 45 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs. Roots many and long. Rhizomes slender; pseudobulbs ovoid, above the ground. Leaves solitary, 1 on the apex to each pseudobulb, petiolate. Scape emerging from the base of a mature pseudobulb before the leaf. Flowers medium-sized, in a loose raceme; sepals and petals subequal, spreading; lip 3-lobed, calcarate, attached to the base of the column, lateral lobes erect, obtuse at the apex or triangular-ovate and acute, midlobe ovate or subrotundate, acute; column long, the apical portion winged; clinandrium dentate; rostellum truncate; anther oblong or obovate, convex; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, 2-seriate, the top 2 of each group smaller; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical, striate-sulcate. Capsules cylindrical.

Two species in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs, or sometimes shrubby. Stems and branches softly pubescent or woolly. Leaves simple, dentate. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming dense or interrupted, terminal spikes or panicles. Calyx ovoid or tubular, 10‑veined, apex netted, almost equally 5‑toothed, straight, slightly dilated in fruit. Corolla 2‑lipped; tube as long as calyx, hairy annulate inside; upper lip erect, margin entire, slightly concave; lower lip longer, spreading, 3‑lobed; middle lobe largest, emarginate or 2‑lobulate. Stamens exserted, in 2 pairs, lower 2 usually longer; lower anthers transversely 2‑celled, upper anthers 1‑celled. Style apex 2‑cleft, lobes subulate, subequal. Disk cupulate, crenate. Nutlets black, subglobose, shiny.

About five or six species distributed in SE Asia, Australia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual erect herb. Leaves alternate and dentate. Capitula heterogamous, radiate. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, imbricate. Receptacle slightly convex, paleate, the paleae deciduous. Marginal florets pistillate and fertile, in 1–2 series, corolla ligulate with the ligules spreading and apically 3‑dentate, yellow. Disk florets hermaphrodite and usually fertile, corolla tubular‑campanulate, limb 5‑lobed; anther base sagittate, lobes caudate, apical appendage ovate‑oblong; stylar branches with apex broad and obtuse‑rounded. Cypselae subterete or those of pistillate florets slightly flattened, striate‑costate, glabrous or loosely hairy. Pappus scarious in coroniform and with 4–5 bristles.

About three species native to warm areas of Asia and tropical Africa; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, often crowded towards apex of branchlets, petiolate entire or rarely serrate. Flowers bisexual, axillary, solitary or several in a corymb; bracteoles 2, persistent, close to calyx; sepals 5, imbricate, persistent, connate at base, deeply constricted at middle, enlarged in fruit; petals 5, imbricate, slightly connate at base; stamens 30 – 40, adnate to receptacle, in 1–2 series; filaments free; anthers linear, usually long-cuspidate; ovary half-inferior, 2– 5-locular with 3 to several ovules per locule; ovules suspended from apex of placenta; style 2– 5-lobed. Fruit subglobose, indehiscent, crowned by persistent enlarged calyx; pericarp woody. Seeds arillate; embryo curved.

About four species distributed in S and SE Asia; one species and four varieties in China; one variety in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Young branches with simple or stellate hairs. Leaves leathery, glabrous to pubescent. Inflorescences terminal, leafopposed, or supra-axillary, 1–several-flowered. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 3, valvate in bud, free or connate. Petals 3 or 6, free or connate, in 1 or 2 whorls, fleshy and concave at base inside loosely, with thick edges; outer petals much larger than inner, enclosing reproductive organs; inner petals very small or reduced. Stamens numerous, extrorse; connective with truncate, dilated, or capitate (rarely apiculate or hemispherical) apex, glabrous, hairy or papillose. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary glabrous or hairy, free or fused; ovule 1 per ovary, basal; style conspicuous or not; stigma broadly ovoid, lanceoloid, ellipsoid or cylindrical, glabrous. Fruits syncarpous, many-loculed, ovoid or globose, fleshy, glabrous to hairy; receptacles 2–14(–21) mm in diam.; sepals caducous or persistent. Seeds 1 per monocarp, basal, 1-seriate, ellipsoid to broadly obovoid; raphes generally conspicuous.

Approximately 110 species in tropical America and four species in tropical Africa. Some species cultivated as fruit trees throughout the tropics; five species cultivated in China, and one species in Hong Kong.

Lianas with white latex. Leaves opposite, lateral veins usually wrinkled above. Cymes paniculate, terminal or axillary. Flowers small. Calyx deeply divided, with basal glands inside. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric, slightly dilated at insertion of stamens, throat constricted, faucal scales absent; lobes overlapping and twisted to right. Stamens included, inserted just below middle of corolla‑tube; filaments short; anthers sagittate, connivent, adherent to pistil head, cells spurred at base; disk ring‑like or cup‑shaped, apex truncate or shortly 5‑lobed. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style; ovules numerous in each carpel; style short; pistil head thick, base with a ring‑like membrane. Fruit of paired divaricate follicles, thick, narrowly ovoid, apex acuminate. Seeds compressed, ovate or oblong; beaked, with a long apical coma.

About 16 species distributed in India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Vietnam, China; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs; rhizomes short, hairy on the contact surface, clinging to wet boulders below trees along streams. Leaves basal, petiolate, ovate or elliptic. Flowers small, inconspicuous, in a terminal small raceme; sepals connate, forming a tube above the middle; petals white, very small, mostly concealed; lip adnate to the sides or rarely to the base of the column, unguiculate, the claw with inflexed margin or simple and without folding margin, the apex dilated, often bilobed and fringed or dentate, rarely undivided and entire, the base furnished with 2 calli, rarely without callus; column short, the apex furnished with 2 glossy glands and produced into an elongate appendage on each side; rostellum long and deeply cleft; anther ovate-acuminate, deeply sunk in the clinandrium; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, sectile, with or without slender caudicle; viscidium oblong or obovate, cuneate; stigmas 2, connivent to the lateral glands; ovary ovoid or oblanceolate. Capsules succulent.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Asia and Pacific islands; 20 species and two varieties in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, pinnately-veined, entire; petioles short; stipules 2, small. Flowers small (plant dioecious), in terminal or axillary spikes or racemes, sometimes paniculate, apetalous. Male flowers very small; calyx cup-shaped, 3–8-lobed, lobes imbricate; disk annular or cushion-shaped, entire or lobed; stamens (1–)3–5(–6), filaments free, longer than sepals; anthers 2-celled, connectives short, thickened; rudimentary ovary minute or absent. Female flowers: calyx as in male flowers; ovary 1-locular, with 2 pendulous ovules; styles 2–4, very short and divergent, united at the base. Drupes ovoid, usually somewhat flattened and oblique.

About 200 species distributed primarily in tropics and subtropics, especially in the E hemisphere; 17 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous or woody tendril-climbing vines. Leaves alternate, petiolate, cordate to hastate, entire; ocrea short, caducous or reduced to a fine line. Flowers bisexual, 3– 5 fascicled, forming terminal or axillary racemes, with the rachis elongated into tendrils. Perianthsegments 5, unequal, usually colorful and slightly enlarged in fruit. Stamens 7–8, alternate with the tooth-like nectaries; filaments united at base. Ovary 3-carpellate; style 3; stigma capitate. Achenes 3-angled at least on the upper part, enclosed by the enlarged persistent perianth.

About three species in C America; one species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, leathery. Stipules interpetiolar, deciduous. Cymes few‑flowered on axillary peduncles. Flowers small, bisexual or polygamous. Calyx‑tube ovoid or obovoid, limb truncate or 4–5‑lobed; lobes often unequal, persistent. Corolla funnel‑shaped; tube slender, the throat glabrous or hairy; lobes 4–5, apex obtuse, imbricate in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the throat; filaments short; anthers basifixed. Ovary 2–8‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style filiform; stigma capitate or 2–3‑lobed. Fruit a drupe, with fleshy exocarp and woody or bony endocarp.

About 40 species in Australia, tropical Asia and Madagascar; one species in S China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, somewhat woody at base, rarely dwarf shrubs. Leaves simple, entire, pinnately‑veined, usually opposite below and alternate above. Flowers zygomorphic, in terminal, bracteate racemes, or solitary in leaf‑axils. Calyx deeply and ± equally 5‑lobed. Corolla glandular‑pubescent outside; tube cylindric, produced abaxially at base into a short pouch; limb 2‑lipped, lower lip 3‑lobed, with a prominent palate at base, upper lip 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous, included. Stigma capitate. Capsules with 2 unequal loculi, adaxial longer, narrower above, and opening by an apical pore, abaxial shorter, and with 2 apical pores. Seeds numerous, reticulate‑rugose.

About 20 species distributed in Mediterranean region; one species cultivated in China and in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or subevergreen trees, monoecious or rarely dioecious. Stipules caducous, free. Leaves alternate, serrulate, rarely entire, pinnately veined or distinctly tri-veined; lateral veins ending in margin. Cymes borne at base of annual branchlets. Flowers unisexual. Male flowers: sepals 4–5; petals absent; stamens as many as sepals and opposite to them, rudimentary ovary absent. Female flowers: solitary, axillary, rarely mixed in male inflorescence; sepals 4–5 or 6, without or with few staminodes; ovary unilocular; ovule solitary, anatropous. Fruit a drupe, pericarp slightly fleshy, endocarp cartilaginous.

About four species and one variety distributed in Madagascar, S and SE Asia, E Australia and Mexico; two species and one variety in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, saprophytic or parasitic, aphyllous. Roots fleshy, cord-like. Rhizomes short, horizontal, with membranous black scales, buds inconspicuous, subterminal, axillary to a scale. Cataphylls white, short, sheathing. Stem 30–50 cm tall, terminated by a loose raceme; bracts membranous, reflexed, parallel to the rachis, purple. Flowers small, yellow, in a terminal raceme; sepals subequal, similar, slightly spreading, rather fleshy, oblong, subcymbiform, obtuse at the apex, with a median longitudinal ridge on the back; petals linear-oblong, obtuse, slightly turning outward at the apical end, auriculate at the base, with a median longitudinal ridge; lip 3-lobed, the lateral lobes basal, triangular, acute, erect; the midlobe fleshy, ovate, attached to the glandular and rugose disk elastically, relatively large, concave, the margin wavy and crenate, the apex obtuse; column slender, cylindrical, curved, fleshy, smooth, without wing or any other decoration, the apex truncate; clinandrium truncate, cyathiform; anther fleshy, subglobose-ovate, concave, thecae lateral, parallel; pollinia 4 in 2 ellipsoidal pairs, powdery, often affixed to the rostellum; rostellum narrow, fleshy, hardly distinguishable from the stigma; stigma large and wide, obovate, the upper margin subtrilobed; ovary cylindrical, striate, violate-purple, slightly rugose. Capsules subfusiform, pendulous, strongly rostrate.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Asia and Australia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms erect or subrambling, much branched. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, base gradually narrowed into a short pseudo-petiole; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a solitary short raceme encircled by a small boat-shaped spatheole, terminal; spatheoles many, crowded into a leafy compound panicle; raceme comprising 1 sessile and 2 pedicellate spikelets; pedicels both broad and flattened. Pedicellate spikelets awnless, unequal, 1 well developed, staminate, as large as sessile spikelet, the other rudimentary. Sessile spikelet laterally compressed, glabrous, 2-floret, lower floret staminate, upper floret bisexual or pistillate; lower glume herbaceous or subleathery toward base, abaxially convex, without keels or wings, 2-toothed; upper glume strongly convex, laterally compressed, membranous with hyaline margins, 1-keeled, awnless; lower lemma ovate-lanceolate, palea narrower; upper lemma deeply 2-lobed and awned from sinus, or entire to emarginate and awnless; awn 4–12 mm.

One species distributed in tropics and subtropics of the Old World; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaf sheaths cylindrical, usually covered with tuberculate hairs on adaxial surface, shorter than internode; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, flat, usually covered with tuberculate hairs, terminal leaf usually absent; ligule short, membranous. Inflorescence terminal, composed of (1–)2(–4) erect, closely appressed racemes; spikelets imbricate in one side, pedicellate spikelets completely absent or reduced to stipe-like, rarely a pistillate spikelet with geniculate awn. Sessile spikelet dorsally compressed, usually bisexual, falling off with internode at maturity; florets 2; lower glume broad, flattened, apex broadly truncate or emarginate, 7(–9)-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, midvein keeled; lower floret staminate; upper floret usually pistillate, seldom bisexual, rarely neuter; upper lemma linear-lanceolate, entire or 2-toothed, awnless or with geniculate puberulous awn, palea shorter and broader, membranous; lodicules absent; stamens 2. Caryopsis cylindrical.

About 15 species distributed in tropical Asia; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as the family.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious, rarely monoecious. Leaves simple, alternate, entire or sparsely denticulate, pinnately-veined, petiolate, usually glandular at apex of petioles; stipules 2, caducous. Inflorescence spicate; the male spikes longer than the female ones, densely bracteate, with several flowers in the axil of each bract. Flowers apetalous, without disk. Male flowers: sepals 3–6, imbricate; stamens 2–3, rarely 5 or 8, filaments free, as long as or longer than sepals; anthers small, 2-celled; pistillode very small or absent. Female flowers: sepals 3–6, persistent; ovary usually 2(–4)-locular; ovules 2 per locule; styles usually 2(–4), bilobed, rarely papillate or fringed. Capsules drupaceous, irregularly dehiscent when mature, 1–2-seeded.

About 80 species in S and SE Asia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic caespitose perennial herbs. Stems erect. Leaves many, distichous. Spikes several on the same shoot, axillary, with imbricate scales. Flowers very small, non-resupinate, in axillary spikes; sepals subequal, the odd one ovate, concave, the lateral ones adnate to the column-foot forming a mentum; petals ovate, obtuse; lip fleshy, undivided, attached to the column foot and produced into a conical spur filled with a pendulous appendage, the apex reflexed, disk with an unicorn-like callus; column short, stout, 2-cuspidate at the apex; clinandrium small; rostellum triangular, long acuminate, 2-lobed; anther sessile, acuminate; pollinia 6, in 2 groups of 3, attached to a slender caudicle; viscidium discoid; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical, subsessile. Capsules oblong-ellipsoidal, with persistent perianth at the apex.

About 150 species distributed from tropical Asia to Oceania, but mainly in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or small trees. Leaves alternate, lateral veins slender and dense, nearly parallel to each other. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, in umbels, usually ebracteate. Flowers bisexual, usually 5-merous; calyx tube campanulate, usually hairy, lobes reflexed or erect; petals 10, scale-like, inserted at the throat of calyx-tube, united into a ring at base, usually tomentose; stamens twice as many as the calyx lobes, alternating with petals; filaments very short or absent; anthers ellipsoidal, dorsifixed, pubescent, connective broad. Disk lacking or annular. Ovary subsessile, completely or incompletely 2-locular, pubescent; style very short or inconspicuous; stigma capitate or subulate. Fruit a capsule, loculicidal, compressed laterally, obovoid, included by the persistent calyx at base, pericarp leathery or woody. Seeds 2 or 1, ovoid or ellipsoidal, hanging by a caruncle-like or tail-shaped basal appendage.

About 15 species distributed in SE Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems erect or prostrate. Stipules elongated, partly adnate to petiole; exstipellate. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 2 – 3 pairs. Flowers solitary or several-fasciculate, sessile. Calyx slender, elongated following development, labiate, upper lip whole p4-toothed, lower one linear. Corolla yellow; vexillum suborbicular, clawed; wings oblong, clawed, auriculate; keel incurved, beaked. Stamens monadelphous, one stamen often absent; anther dimorphic, long and short alternately arranged. Ovary subsessile, 2–3(–6)-ovuled, after fertilization the torus elongating greatly and forcing the young fruit underground to ripen. Pods cylindrical, constricted but not septate between the 1– 3(–6) seeds.

About 22 species distributed in tropical America; one species widely cultivated all over the world; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, treelets or perennial herbs, glabrous or pubescent, often prickly. Leaves bipinnate, sometimes tripinnate, with serrate or nearly entire leaflets; stipules adnate to base of petioles. Inflorescence paniculate or umbellately paniculate, consisting of numerous umbels or occasionally heads, terminal or terminal and axillary. Flowers polygamo-monoecious, 5- or occasionally 6-merous. Calyx minutely 5-toothed. Petals 5, imbricate in the bud. Ovary 2–5-locular; styles 2–5, free or connate at base; disk fleshy, small, slightly raised at the margin. Fruit 2–5-celled, subglobose, 3–5-angular; seeds compressed; endosperm uniform.

About 40 species distributed in E to SE Asia and the Americas; 29 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees; branches verticillate, patent or ascending. Leaves spirally arranged, needlelike to broadly ovate or triangular. Pollen cones axillary or terminal on branchlets, cylindric, ovoid, or ellipsoid; microsporophylls densely arranged. Seed cones erect, ellipsoid, or ovoid to subglobose; ovulate scales ligulate; bracts of mature cones large, woody, distal part thickened; seed scales adnate with bracts in basal, detached in apical part. Seeds connate with bracts, not winged or sometimes with 2 lateral wings.

19 species: Papua New Guinea; Australia, New Caledonia, S America; two species (introduced) in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs unarmed. Stipules small. Leaves bipinnate, pinnae in few pairs; petioles with glands; leaflets few to several pairs, rarely 1 pair. Inflorescences globular heads, or the heads arranged in panicles, terminal, axillary or cauliflorous. Flowers white, small; hermaphroditic or polygamous, monomorphic. Calyx campanulate or tubular, 5-toothed. Petals 5, connate to middle. Stamens numerous; filaments exserted, more or less united into a tube. Anthers small, apex eglandular; carpels 1– several, free, sessile, many-ovuled; styles filiform, stigmas terminal, capitellate. Pods strongly curved or spirally twisted, or straight, cylindric, flat or swollen. Seeds ovate or orbiculate, without pleurogram.

About 94 species distributeted in tropical Asia; 11 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, monoecious. Stems solitary, unbranched, leaf scars conspicuous or obscure. Leaves pinnate, reduplicate; sheaths forming a crownshaft on the top of stem, thick and leathery. Inflorescences under the crownshafts, branched 3–4 orders, pendulous; prophylls tubular, deciduous. Flowers in triad of a pair of male flowers with a female one in the middle; male flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 9–24; female flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, staminodes 3–4, ovary triangular ovoid, 1-locular, stigmas 3. Fruits globose to ellipsoidal, red or pink when mature; epicarp smooth, mesocarp thin, fleshy with fibres, endocarp smooth, thin and fragile. Seed usually 1, endosperm ruminate.

Six species native to E Australia, popular as ornamentals in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or treelets, rarely subshrubs, with or without an indumentum. Branches often swollen and flattened-triangular at base. Leaves alternate, rarely subopposite or subverticillate, entire, crenate or serrate, generally with pellucid or coloured glandular dots or stripes. Inflorescence generally racemose, corymbose or subumbellate, simple or compound, terminal or axillary. Flowers bisexual, usually 5- rarely 4-merous. Calyx deeply split, lobes valvate or imbricate, usually glandular dotted. Corolla-tube usually very short, the lobes contorted, overlapping to the right in bud. Stamens attached at base or middle of corolla-tube; filaments very short; anthers opening by slits, very rarely by apical pores. Ovary ovoid or pyramidal; style slender; stigma punctiform; ovules serveral to many arranged in one to several series on the free central placenta. Fruit a 1-seeded drupe, usually globose, red, purple or black when mature; endocarp crustaceous or bony; seeds with hard endosperm and cylindric embryo.

About 400 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, but scarce in Australia; 65 species in China; 14 native species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, monoecious or dioiecious. Stems usually clustered, seldom solitary, pleonanthic or hapaxanthic. Leaves pinnate, induplicate; sheaths covered by various indumentum, with black fibrous auricles; pinnae regular or irregular arranged; linear, elliptic or rhomboid, with ear-like bases, undulate margins and erose apices; green adaxially and whitish grey abaxially. Inflorescences interfoliar or seldom infrafoliar, branched 1–2 orders or seldom unbranched, pendulous or erect; peduncles subtended by several persistent bracts; flowers solitary or in triads; male flowers ovoid, usually sepals 3, petals 3, stamens more than 15, carpel absent; female flowers subglobose, smaller than males, sepals 3, petals 3, staminodes 3 or absent, carpels 2–3. Fruits globose to ellipsoidal, commonly trigonous with the stigma remain, red, yellowish or purplish; epicarp smooth, mesocarp with irritant crystals. Seed 1–3, endosperm homogeneous.

About 20 species distributed from S Asia to N Australia; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.
