Vines or scandent shrubs. Stems herbaceous or woody at base. Leaves petiolate, variable in shape, entire, sometimes silvery sericeous abaxially. Inflorescences several – many‑flowered, axillary, rarely terminal, in loose or compact cymes; bracts small or large, persistent or caducous. Sepals persistent, herbaceous or ± leathery, variable in shape and size, pubescent abaxially, ± enlarged and reflexed in fruit. Corolla purple, red, pink, or white, campanulate, funnelform, or tubular; limb subentire to deeply 5‑lobed, with 5 distinct, mostly pubescent midpetaline bands. Stamens inserted near base of corolla, inclusive or exserted; filaments filiform, dilated at base; pollen grains globose, spiny. Disk annular or cupular, entire or shallowly 5‑lobed. Ovary 2‑ or 4‑locular, 4‑ovuled, pubescent or glabrous. Style 1, filiform, inclusive or exserted; stigma capitate, 2‑lobed or 2‑globular. Berry red or orange, globose or ellipsoidal; pericarp fleshy or leathery. Seeds 4 or fewer, glabrous, rarely pilose at hilum.

About 90 species mainly distributed in tropical Asia, few species in Pacific islands; 22 species in China; three native and one cultivated species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with tuberous or rhizome. Leaves usually appearing with flowers, 1–3; petiole long, ± sheathing and encircling the peduncle; leaf blade trifoliolate, palmately or pedately compound. Peduncle erect, as are the petioles usually marked with spots or blotches. Spathe tube cylindrical, convolute, gradually enlarged toward apex; limb helmet-shaped, apex long acuminate. Flowers unisexual, without perianth, borne at base of spadix. Spadix sessile, included or exserted, terminated by a sterile, usually long and filiform appendage. Male flowers of 2–5, almost sessile 2–4-celled anthers; female flowers with an ovoid 1-locular ovary, containing 1– many ovules, stigma peltate or capitate. Fruit a berry, 1– many-seeded.

About 150 species, mostly in Asia, few in tropical Africa, Middle America and N America; 82 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Perennials or annual herbs. Culms tufted. Leaf blades linear, flat or rolled; ligule a line of hairs. Inflorescence a contracted or open panicle. Spikelets 1-flowered, with long scarious glumes; lemma cylindrical or laterally compressed, indurate, glabrous or scabrid, rarely sparsely hairy, the margins convolute or involute; awn with or without a column, persistent or deciduous, articulate or not; branches glabrous or scabrid, never plumose; floret callus obtuse to pungent or bidentate; palea up to 1/2 length of lemma. Caryopsis terete, or grooved when lemma involute, embryo 1/3 its length.

About 250 species distributed throughout the tropics and subtropics, especially along the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn; 11 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Climbers, sometimes subshrubs, rarely small trees. Roots often tuberous. Leaves entire or 3–5-lobed, pinnately or palmately veined. Flowers axillary, solitary, fasciculate, or arranged in racemes. Perianth uniseriate, zygomorphic, lobes fused; tube often enlarged at or near base to form a utricle, apically cylindric or funnel-shaped, rectilinear or curved; limb ligulate, discoid, or subpeltate; lobes 1–3. Stamens 6 (rarely 4 –10 or many) in 1 series, fully adnate to the style column to form gynostemium; filaments absent; anthers extrorse. Ovary inferior, 4–6-locular; carpels fully connate; gynostemium 3- or 6-lobed. Fruit dry capsules, 6-valved, dehiscing from the apex or from the base or rarely indehiscent. Seeds many, flat, with or without wing, with fleshy funicle, persistent on seed.

About 400 species, widely distributed in tropical, subtropical and temperate regions of the Old World, also in Australia; 45 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches with simple hairs. Leaves leathery, glabrous to pubescent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or extraaxillary, 1( – several)-flowered, borne on thickened, hook-curved peduncles. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 3, valvate in bud, free or basally connate. Petals usually 6, free, in 2 whorls, fleshy; outer and inner petals subequal; inner petals usually connivent, erect. Stamens numerous, extrorse; connective with truncate, dilated or peltate apex, glabrous. Carpels 7 – 15( – 20) per flower; ovary glabrous or hairy, free; ovules (1 –)2 per ovary, basal, 2-seriate; style conspicuous or not; stigma ovoid or obconical, glabrous or hairy. Fruits apocarpous; monocarps 1 –12(–15) per fruit, ovoid or ellipsoid, glabrous to hairy; stipes 0 –10(–15) mm long; receptacles 2 –13(–17) mm in diam.; sepals caducous. Seeds 1– 2 per monocarp, basal, 1 – 2-seriate, ellipsoid to lenticular; raphes generally conspicuous.

Approximately 100 species in tropical Africa and Asia; four species in China, and two species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial plant, herbs, subshrubs or shrubs, aromatic, plant cobwebby, pubescent, glandular, viscid, or glabrescent; stem erect, striated, branched. Leaves alternate, 1–3‑pinnately divided or not, rarely palmately divided, margin usually toothed. Capitula small, usually nodding or pendent at anthesis, heterogamous and disciform, shape globose, hemispherical, ovoid or ellipsoidal, usually with small stipules at base, arranged as spikes, racemes, panicles, or corymbs; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, imbricate, herbaceous with scarious margin, and usually with a green line on midvein, or totally scarious without the green midvein. Receptacle flat, convex or hemispherical, hairy or not. Marginal florets pistillate, in 1–2 rows, corolla narrowly tubular, rarely conical, urceolate or cup‑shaped, 2–3(–4)‑lobed apically; stylar branches exserted, acute at distal ends. Disk florets bisexual, in many rows, fertile or not, corolla tubular, apex 5‑lobed; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular, acute; style divergent, branch apices truncate, usually penicillate and tuberculate; or style not divided, as claviform or funnelform. Cypselae ovoid, obovoid or oblong‑obovoid, faintly striate. Pappus mostly absent.

About 380 species mainly native to temperate regions in N hemisphere, some distributed in C & S America, Africa and Australia. Most with medicinal uses and rich in polyacetylenes, flavonoids, terpenoids and cyanogenic glycosides. Some are used in desert for sand stabilization or used for feeding livestock; about 186 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Clums slender, usually creeping, scrambling or ascending. Leaf blades lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, base cordate, often clasping culm; ligule membranous. Inflorescence of subdigitate, slender, fragile racemes, terminal on culms and branches, not spathate; rachis internodes and pedicels filiform to linear, glabrous or ciliate on angles; spikelets pair dissimilar. Sessile spikelet linear to lanceolate, dorsally or laterally compressed, falling off with internodes; lower glume papery or subleathery, abaxially flat or convex, several-veined, with or without lateral keels, scaberulous to spinulose; upper glume boat-shaped, 2-keeled, apex acute to mucronate, 3-veined; lower floret reduced to an empty hyaline lemma; upper lemma hyaline, entire or shortly 2-toothed, awned from near base; palea small or absent; Stamens 2–3. Caryopsis terete. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or neuter, well developed, reduced, or represented by the pedicel only, sometimes almost completely suppressed.

About 26 species distributed in Old World tropics, mainly in India; introduced in America; 12 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees with milky juice, monoecious. Stipules various. Leaves alternate, entire or pinnately lobed, penninerved. Heads axillary or on brachyblasts, solitary or paired, variable in shape. Flowers unisexual, small, densely crowded on a fleshy rachis, often mixed with peltate bract. Male flowers: perianth 2– 4-lobed, lobes obtuse, concave, valvate or slightly imbricate; stamen 1, erect; pistillode absent. Female flowers: perianth tubular, connate and confluent at lower part with the rachis, mouth minute; ovary enclosed; style central or lateral, stigma entire, rarely 2–3-fid; ovules pendulous. Syncarps fleshy, ellipsoid, cyclindric, globose or lobed, formed by enlarged fleshy connate perianth and carpels, papilary or with hardened spinous, truncate, pyramidal protuberance on surface. Achenes deeply sunk in fleshy rachis of inflorescence, without endosperm.

About 50 species distributed in tropical Asia; 14 species in China; four species and one subspecies in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs. Stems erect, leafy, slightly enlarged at the base. Leaves many, lanceolate, articulate with the sheaths. Inflorescences occasionally branched; bracts small, persistent. Flowers medium-sized, showy, opening one at a time, appearing as if in a terminal raceme; sepals free, subequal, spreading; petals slightly wider than the sepals; lip attached to the base of the column, trumpetshaped, embracing the column, the apex deeply cleft, disk lamellate, with 5 longitudinal keels; column long, slender, slightly curved and enlarged at the apex; clinandrium elevated, rotundate and 2-dentate; rostellum curtain-like, pointed at the middle of the margin; anther terminal, incumbent, concave; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, discoid, laterally compressed, loosely connected by granular material; stigma semi-orbicular, below the rostellum; ovary cylindrical. Capsules cylindrical, strongly rostrate.

One or two species widely distributed in tropical Asia; one species in China and Hong Kong

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms terete, stout or slender. Leaf blades usually linear or linear-lanceolate, ciliate; ligule very short or almost absent and represented by a fringe of ciliate rim. Panicle open or contracted; spikelets paired, rarely solitary; pedicels unequal, slender. Spikelets 2-flowered; rachilla articulate between lower lemma and upper lemma; glume and lower floret persistent or articulate slowly; lower floret male or neuter, upper floret bisexual; glumes subequal or the lower shorter, herbaceous, (2–)3–5(–7)-veined; lower lemma herbaceous, persistent, smooth, 3–7-veined; upper lemma firmer in texture, chartaceous at maturity, scaberulous, awned or awnless; paleae equaling or slightly shorter than lemmas, membranous; lodicules 2; stamens 3; styles 2, free or connate at base.

About 60 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, but mainly in Asia; 20 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Tall rhizomatous perennial herbs. Culms erect, reed-like. Leaves cauline; leaf blades broadly linear, tough, flat, base rounded or cordate; ligule membranous with minutely ciliolate margins. Inflorescence a large terminal panicle, composed of many plumose branches and spikelets. Spikelets wedge-shaped, laterally compressed, 2–5-flowered, disarticulating above glumes and between florets; florets all fertile or the upper reduced; rachilla internodes glabrous; glumes subequal, narrow, as long as spikelet, membranous, 3–5-veined; floret callus short, laterally pilose; lemmas narrow, membranous, rounded on back, 3–9-veined, plumose below middle with spreading silky-white hairs, tapering to an entire or bidentate apex tipped by a straight awnlet in the sinus; palea 1/2–2/3 length of lemma, 2-keeled, densely ciliate on the keels. Stamens 3.

Three species distributed in Mediterranean region eastwards to China; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, acaulescent. Rhizomes and roots often pungently aromatic. Leaves solitary or paired on rhizomes (when paired appearing opposite), usually long-petiolate, often cordate or sagittate. Flowers terminal, solitary (rarely paired). Perianth uniseriate, actinomorphic, campanulate or urceolate, apex 3-lobed, lobes erect, spreading, or reflexed. Stamens 12 in 2 series, free or connate, filaments very short, anthers ovoid, extrorse. Ovary inferior or half-inferior, subglobose, 6-locular; carpels fully connate; styles 6, free or united into column; stigma 2-lobed; ovules many. Capsules subglobse, irregularly dehiscent, often with persistent perianth and stamens. Seeds ellipsoid, flat, plane or grooved ventrally, with fleshy funicle at base; endosperm copious, embryo small.

About 90 species, mainly distributed in SE Asia, a few species in N America, one species endemic to Europe; 39 species in China; one species endemic to Hong Kong.

Herbs, frequently woody at base. Leaves opposite or whorled, short‑petiolate. Cymes terminal and extra‑axillary, erect, umbel‑like, many‑flowered. Calyx deeply 5‑parted, with 5–10 glands inside. Corolla rotate, deeply 5‑parted; lobes reflexed, valvate or rarely overlapping to right. Corona lobes 5, inserted on gynostegium, erect, apex hooded, with an incurved, ligular to horn‑like adaxial appendage. Stamens inserted at base of corolla‑tube; filaments connate into a tube; anther with apical incurved appendages and 1 pollinium in each cell, pendulous. Ovary of 2 separate carpels; stigma flattened at the top. Follicles fusiform, apex acuminate. Seeds flat, with a long coma.

About 120 species distributed in America, some naturalized in Old World; one species cultivated in China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial or subshrubs; roots cord-like, rhizomatous or tuberous. Stems erect or climbing, generally branching, sometimes ± woody. Leaves reduced to dry scales or spiny spurs, the foliage represented by green leaf-like branchlets or cladodes, which borne in clusters, rarely solitary, green, flat, 3-angled, or subterete. Flowers dioecious or hermaphroditic, in axillary clusters, racemes or umbels, rarely flowers solitary; pedicels articulate, subtended by membranous bracteoles. Perianth campanulate; segments free or occasionally connate at base. Stamens 6; filaments adnate to perianth segments; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with 2 or few ovules in each locule. Fruit a berry, 1–few-seeded.

About 130–140 species widely spread in temperate and tropical regions of Africa, Asia, and Europe; 31 species in China; one species native to Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with horizontal rhizome and rather thick fibrous roots. Leaves radical, solitary or 2–4-tufted, long petiolate; leaf blade many-veined. Flowers bisexual, 1(–2) borne on a very short scape, at the surface of ground beneath the foliage, generally embraced by 1–2 bracts at perianth base. Perianth campanulate, urceolate, or cupular, fleshy, apically (4–)6–8(–10)-lobed. Stamens as many as and opposite to perianth segments, usually inserted in proximal part of perianth tube; filaments very short or absent; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary superior, 3–4-locular, with 2–several ovules in each locule; style short, sometimes articulate; stigma usually peltate or mushroom-shaped, large, entire or lobed at margin. Fruit a berry, globose to ovoid-ellipsoidal, usually 1-seeded.

About 55 species distributed in E and SE Asia; 49 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Perennial rarely annual herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Leaves alternate, entire or toothed. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, solitary at terminal or in panicle or corymbose form. Involucres campanulate, hemispherical or obconical; phyllaries 2–many‑seriate with outer shorter, margin scarious, imbricate. Receptacle pitted or alveolate, plane or convex. Ray florets 1–2‑seriate, female and fertile, corolla ligulate, ligules long, obscurely 3‑toothed at apex, white, pink, purple or blue in colour; style filiform. Disk florets tubular, hermaphrodite and all fertile, corolla narrowly tubular or funnelform, deeply 5‑lobed, mostly yellow, or sometimes tinged purple at tips; anther bases obtuse, entire; stylar branches complanate, with lanceolate apical appendages. Cypsela compressed and ribbed, usually pubescent. Pappus setaceous or scarious, white or reddish brown.

A large genus with more than 600 species, cosmopolitan; about 90 species in China; five species and one variety growing naturally in Hong Kong.

Aster novi‑belgii L. (荷蘭菊) was also cultivated previously.

Herbs or subshrubs with cystoliths. Leaves petiolate, margin entire. Flowers in simple or compound spikes or racemes, terminal or axillary, flowers usually secund on rachis. Bracts and bracteoles linear, shorter than calyx. Calyx 5‑lobed, lobes linear to lanceolate, equal. Corolla with ventricose tube, limb 5‑lobed, lobes subequal. Stamens 4, included, didynamous, anther 2‑thecous, thecae oblong, at the same height, base muticous. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles filiform; stigma capitate, 2‑lobed or bidentate. Capsule clavate, with a solid stalk at base, retinacula present, 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, flattened, glabrous, rugose or tuberculate with sinuately incised margin.

About 70 species in tropical regions of the Old World; three species in China; two species cultivated or naturalized in Hong Kong.

Small trees or shrubs, armed with spines or unarmed. Leaves alternate, unifoliolate, entire or crenulate; stipulate scales often present. Flowers axillary, rarely terminal, fasciculate or in short racemose corymbs or panicles, rarely solitary. Calyx 3–5-lobed, lobes imbricate. Petals 3–5, imbricate. Stamens 8 or 10, distinct or connate into several bundles, equal or unequal; anthers ellipsoidal. Ovary 2–5-locular, ovules 1–2 per locule; style as long as ovary, rarely shorter, stigmas capitate or slightly enlarged. Fruit a berry, globose or ellipsoidal, red or bluish black, 1–5-seeded. Seeds ellipsoidal.

About 17 species distributed in tropical Asia and Australia; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, monoecious or dioecious, often with squarrose induments. Leaves alternate, or lower ones opposite, margin entire or toothed. Inflorescence a spike or panicle, or flowers solitary. Flowers unisexual. Male flowers: without bracts and bracteoles; perianth 3 – 5-lobed; stamens 3–5. Female flowers: solitary, subtended by 2-bracteoles; perianth absent or rarely present and then 3 – 5-lobed; ovary globose; stigmas 2. Utricles with membranaceous pericarp, enclosed by enlarged persistent bracteoles.

About 200 species distributed in temperate and subtropical regions of the world; 17 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Small trees or shrubs, dioecious. Leaves simple, opposite, estipulate. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate or racemose-paniculate. Flowers 4-merous, unisexual, actinomorphic, subtended by 1 or 2 bracteoles. Male flowers: calyx small, 4-lobed; petals 4, valvate; stamens 4, filaments short and thick, anthers dorsifixed; pistillode absent. Female flowers: calyx-tube ovoid or subcylindrical, 4-lobed; petals as in males; staminodes absent; disk slightly fleshy; ovary 1-locular, ovule 1 per locule, pendulous; style short and thick, stigma capitate, straight or curving, slightly 2–4-lobed, oblique. Fruit a drupe, fleshy, red when mature, black when dry, crowned with persistent calyx-lobes and style. Seeds with membranous arils.

Ten species distributed in Bhutan, China, N India, Japan, Korea, Myanmar, Sikkim, Vietnam; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Culms erect or geniculate at base, glabrous. Leaf blades linear, flat; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a terminal panicle with large pendulous spikelets. Spikelets more than 10 mm, pendulous, 2–several-flowered, the lower 1–3 florets bisexual, others ± reduced; rachilla pilose or glabrous, disarticulating below each floret or only above glumes, or not disarticulating (cultivated species); glumes lanceolate to elliptic, usually subequal and as long as spikelet, rarely strongly unequal or shorter than spikelet, herbaceous to membranous, 7–11-veined, back rounded, smooth, apex acuminate; floret callus acute to pungent, bearded; lemmas shorter than or equalling the glumes, lanceolate-oblong, rarely exserted, abaxially rounded, 5–9-veined, glabrous to hispid, awned usually from near middle of abaxial side, apex papery, 2-toothed to 2-fid, lobes sometimes extended into fine bristles, awn geniculate with twisted column (or rarely straight), sometimes reduced or absent (cultivated species); palea usually shorter than lemma, 2-keeled, keels ciliate. Stamens 3, stigmas 2. Ovary densely hairy. Caryopsis with long linear hilum.

About 25 species distributed in Mediterranean region, SW Asia, Europe and N Asia, and widely introduced and naturalized in other temperate regions; five species (all introduced) in China; two species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Small trees. Leaves alternate, odd-pinnate, without stipules; leaflets alternate or subopposite, entire. Flowers small, in small axillary panicles, often borne on stems or old branches. Sepals 5, united at the base, imbricate. Petals 5, purple or pink, contorted. Stamens 10, in 2 series, 5 long and 5 short, all antheriferous or the shorter ones without anthers. Ovary superior, 5-locular, with several ovules in each locule. Fruit a berry, with (3–)5(–7) ribs.

Two species native to tropical Asia, also cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees. Branches terete, sometimes 4‑ridged when young, often evidently jointed. Leaves simple, opposite, leathery, entire. Cymes dense, spicate or capitates. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, shorter than calyx, persistent, tomentose abaxially. Calyx cupular, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes overlapping, persistent. Corolla nearly actinomorphic, campanulate, shortly inserted on an inconspicuous disk; lobes 4 or 5, upper lobe often broader than others. Stamens 4, adnate to apical part of corolla tube. Ovary imperfectly 4‑locular; ovule 1 per locule, pendulous. Styles long or short. Stigma 2‑cleft. Capsules subtended by persistent calyx, dehiscent into 2 leathery valves. Seeds erect; cotyledons large, folded.

About 14 species distributed in maritime in tropics and subtropics of both hemispheres; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial or rarely annual herbs, stoloniferous. Culms tufted or decumbent. Leaf sheaths often strongly keeled-compressed and equitant; leaf blades flat or involute, often obtuse; ligule short, membranous-ciliolate. Inflorescence composed of 2–many slender spikelike racemes, mostly subdigitate but sometimes along a short central axis; spikelets single, subsessile, dorsally compressed, alternating or in 2 rows along the narrow triquetrous rachis, floret 1–2, falling off as a whole. Spikelets oblong; lower glume absent; upper glume and lower lemma as long as spikelet, lower palea absent; upper lemma and palea leathery; upper lemma with narrowly inrolled, opaque margins, embracing upper palea to apex; lodicules 2; stamens 3; style 2, free; stigmas plumose, exserted laterally.

About 110 species distributed in tropical and subtropical America, one species in Africa; two species cultivated in China and in Hong Kong.

Herbs, erect or creeping. Leaves opposite, sessile or subsessile. Flowers solitary, axillary or in terminal racemes. Bracteoles 1 or 2, or absent. Sepals 5, entirely free, upper 1 largest, lateral 2 smallest. Corolla‑tube tubular, limb patent, conspicuously or obscurely 2‑lipped; lower lip 3‑lobed; upper lip 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous or equal in length, included. Anther‑cells parallel, free. Ovary ellipsoidal to globose or ovoid, glabrous, stigma dilated, capitate or 2‑lobed. Capsules ovoid or globose, 2‑grooved, 4‑valved. Seeds numerous, minute.

About 60 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mainly in America; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite, linear, sessile, with pellucid dots. Flowers bisexual, axillary, solitary or in cymes, white or red, small, 5-merous, shortly pedicellate or sessile. Bracteoles 2, small, caducous. Hypanthium campanulate or semiglobose, usually adnate to ovary; lobes 5, membranous, persistent. Petals 5, suborbicular. Stamens 5–10(–20), shorter than petals; filaments short; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary inferior or semi-inferior, rarely superior, 2–3-loculed; ovules many per locule; style short; stigma slightly enlarged. Capsule dehiscing into 2 – 3 valves, each valve with 1–3 or more seeds. Seeds reniform, angular; embryo straight; endosperm absent; cotyledons short.

About 70 species distributed in S and SE Asia, Australia; one species in China; also in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, monoecious or dioecious. Rhizome branched or unbranched, smooth or rugose with small scaly warts and/or stellate lenticels. Leaves opposite, alternate and distichous or spiral, or whorled, sessile, fleshy or scale-like. Inflorescences spadix-like, cylindrical, ellipsoidal, ovoid-globose, or globose. Male flowers: pedicellate or sessile, subtended by short, truncate bracts; perianth 3–6-lobed, lobes isomorphic or heteromorphic, valvate, reflexed at anthesis; stamens without filaments, usually as many as perianth-lobes, forming a synandrium; anthers 2-celled, transversely or longitudinally dehiscent. Female flowers: congested on main axis or also on basal stipe of spadicles, perianth wanting; ovary ellipsoidal to fusiform, 1-locular, attenuate toward both ends; ovule solitary, pendulous; style elongated, persistent. Fruit minute, indehiscent; exocarp crustaceous. Seeds globose.

About 19 species mainly distributed in tropical Africa and Australia, temperate to tropical Asia, and the Pacific Islands; 12 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Arborescent bamboos, occasionally shrubby or scrambling, 1–20 m. Rhizomes short necked, pachymorph. Culms unicaespitose, erect to pendulous, rarely subscandent; internodes terete; nodes not raised. Branches several to many, often 1–3 dominant (subequal in Bambusa subg. Lingnania), branchlets of lower branches sometimes forming tough or weak thorns. Culm sheaths deciduous, rarely persistent; auricles usually conspicuous, always with marginal oral setae; blade usually erect. Leaf blade variable in size, transverse veins inconspicuous. Inflorescence iterauctant, fully bracteate, subtended by a broad 2-keeled prophyll; pseudospikelets rarely solitary, usually several- to many-clustered to capitate on flowering branches. Pseudospikelets prophyllate; florets 2–many, terminal floret sterile or imperfect, sessile; fertile glumes preceded by 1 or more gemmiferous, glumaceous, or spathaceous bracts and/or 1–3 empty glumes; rachilla internodes usually distinct and usually disarticulating with florets, falling separately; lemma broad, many-veined; palea 2-keeled, apex acute or shortly bifid; lodicules 3 or 2. Stamens 6; filaments free. Ovary usually stalked, apex thickened and hairy; style solid, usually short; stigmas (1–)3, long, hairy, plumose. Caryopsis terete, apex hairy; pericarp slightly thickened.

More than 100 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide; 80 species (67 endemic) in China, mainly in the south and southwest; 16 species, 3 varieties and 6 cultivars in Hong Kong.

The following species are only cultivated in Tai Po Kau Nature Reserve and not treated here: B. basihirsuta McClure(扁竹), B. cornigera McClure(牛角竹), B. dissimulator McClure var. albinodia McClure(白節坭簕竹), B. insularis L. C. Chia & H. L. Fung(黎庵 高竹), B. malingensis McClure(馬嶺竹), B. mutabilis McClure(黃竹仔) and B. pervariabilis McClure(撐篙竹).

Perennial herbs or shrubs with cystoliths, usually spiny. Leaves opposite, petiolate, margin entire. Inflorescence of mostly axillary cymes, sometimes secund or reduced to dense clusters or flowers solitary; bracts present or absent; bracteoles 2. Calyx deeply 4‑lobed, 2 outer lobes larger, one usually bifid, 2 inner lobes much smaller. Corolla usually large, funnel‑shaped, 5‑lobed; lobes subequal. Fertile stamens 4, didynamous; filaments included; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae oblong at same height, acute or muticous at base; staminodes 1. Ovary 2‑locular, 2 ovules per locule; style filiform, included; stigma bifid or entire. Capsules substipitate, subellipsoidal to ovoid, retinacula present, 2– 4‑seeded. Seed lenticular, pubescent with appressed hygroscopic trichomes.

About 100 species in tropical regions of Asia and Africa; four species in China; one species naturalized in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with tunicate bulbs. Leaves radical, sessile, mostly very narrow, parallel-veined. Scape erect, simple, naked. Inflorescence a terminal raceme, usually many-flowered; bracts small, membranous. Flowers campanulate or wide open, pink or blue; pedicels articulate. Perianth segments 6, nearly equal, free to slightly connate at base. Stamens 6, inserted below the middle or at the base of the segments; filaments slender or slightly dilated toward base; anthers dorsifixed, introrse. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with 1 or 2( or 8–10) ovules in each locule. Style filiform; stigma small. Fruit a capsule, globose to obovoid, loculicidal. Seeds black, sometimes angular.

Two species worldwide, one species in China, Japan, Korea, and Russia, the other in NW Africa and SW Europe; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs. Branchlets usually quadrangular, glabrous or slightly scurfy. Leaves opposite, petiolate, glabrous, margin entire, 5-basiveined. Inflorescences terminal, cymose, usually (1–)3-flowered. Flowers 4-merous. Calyx-tube ovoid or campanulate, 4-ribbed; calyx 4-lobed, without accessory teeth; lobes lanceolate or triangular. Petals 4, pink or white, rarely deep red, broadly obovate, glabrous. Stamens 8, dimorphic, unequal in length, 4 longer and 4 shorter; anthers of longer stamen lanceolate, with 2 bristles at base, apex beaked, connective extended into a short spur at base; anthers of shorter stamen oblong, with 2 bristles at base, apex not beaked, connective slightly inflated, sometimes with inconspicuous spur. Ovary partially adnate to the calyx-tube, pyriform, 4-ribbed, 4-locular, glabrous. Fruit capsular, oblong-globose, obtusely 4-ribbed, apex truncate, dehiscing into 4 valves. Seeds numerous and small.

One species endemic to SE and S China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Twining fleshy vines. Leaves alternate, simple, entire. Spikes axillary or terminal, with deciduous bracteoles. Flowers small, sessile, clustered on elongated and thickened peduncles. Perianthsegmens 5, fleshy, united to middle or upper. Stamens 5; filaments erect in bud, base fused into a tube or disc and adnate to perianthtube. Ovary globose, 1-locular; styles 3. Fruit subglobose, enclosed within persistent fleshy perianth.

About five species in tropical Africa and Asia; one species cultivated in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, rarely subshurbs. Stems often many-branched. Leaves alternate, sessile or subsessile, flat to terete. Inflorescence a spike. Flowers bisexual or pistillate, sessile; perianth subglobose, membranaceous, hairy, 5-lobed; lobes incurved, with winged or not winged appendage on outsides when fruiting. Stamens 5, inserted on perianth-base, exserted. Ovary broad-ovate, sessile; style short; stigma 2(-3). Urticles oblate, pericarp membranaceous, not adnate to seeds. Seeds orbicular or ovate.

About 21 species distributed in tropical to subtropical regions; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

According to the opinion of A. T. Scott (Fedd. Repert. 89: 101–119. 1978) and D. J. Mabberley (The Plant Book, ed. 2, 1997), the genus Kochia Roth was merged into Bassia.

Trees, shrubs, or woody vines; stems often flattened, and sometimes with undivided tendrils at the base of inflorescence. Leaves simple, alternate, entire or 2-lobed or almost 2-foliolate, palmately-veined; stipules small, scale-like, caducous. Inflorescences racemose, paniculate or corymbose; bracts and bracteoles usually linear, caducous; flowers zygomorphic, bisexual, rarely unisexual; calyx-tube short-turbinate, sometimes elongated, limb entire or closed at the apex or shortly 5-toothed; teeth imbricate, variously split during flowering, spathaceous or valvately 5-lobed or partite; petals 5, subequal, usually with a distinct claw; perfect stamens 10, 5 or 3, rarely 1 or 2, filaments free, linear, anthers dorsal, opening lengthwise; staminodes many; ovary usually stipitate, 2 –many-ovuled; styles filiform or short; stigmas terminal, peltate or oblique. Legume oblong or linear, rarely falcate, indehiscent or 2-valved. Seeds many, spherical or ovoid, compressed, with or without endosperm.

About 300 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; about 30 species in China; six species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Perennial succulent herbs, very rarely subshrubs, with rhizomes or tubers. Stems erect or decumbent, or often stemless. Leaves alternate or all basal, simple or rarely palmately compound, base usually oblique asymmetrical, margin often irregularly serrate and divided, occasionally entire; stipules membranous, deciduous. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious), occasionally dioecious, 2–4 to several in dichotomous cymes, rarely numerous and in panicles, with pedicels and bracts; tepals petaloid. Male flower: perianth-segments usually 4, decussate, usually the outer ones longer; stamens numerous; filaments free or connate at base; anthers basifixed, 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Female flower: perianth-segments usually 5 or 4, rarely 2 or 6, free; ovary inferior, 2–3(–4 – 6)-locular; placentas central or parietal; styles as many as locules of ovary, free or united at base; stigma turgid, spirally twisted-tortuous. Fruit a capsule, sometimes berry-like, usually unequally rarely subequally 3-winged, rarely wingless and 3 – 4-horned; seeds minute, very numerous.

About more than 1000 species, widely distributed in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world and; about 160 species in China; five species (one introduced) in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, subopposite or alternate, leathery, entire, pinninerved. Flowers small, bisexual, in panicles or sometimes in axillary fascicles or racemes. Perianth-tube short; lobes 6, equal or subequal. Fertile stamens 9, rarely 6, the 3 inner ones with 2 glands at the base; anthers 2-celled, introrse, those of the inner ones extrorse. Staminodes ovoid, triangular, or cordate, shortly stalked. Fruits drupaceous, ellipsoid, ovoid-ellipsoid or oblong-ellipsoid.

About 200 species mainly distributed in tropical Africa, SE Asia, Australia and America; 35 species in China and two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Rhizome knobby. Aerial stem well developed, erect, solid. Leaves cauline, 2-ranked, sword-shaped, flat. Inflorescence a terminal dichotomously branched panicle of rhipidia. Bracts small, membranous. Perianth tube short; segments nearly similar, outer ones slightly larger than inner ones. Stamens inserted at base of perianth segments. Style 1, slender, 3-lobed at apex. Capsule obovoid or ellipsoidal, dehiscing into 3 valves when mature. Seeds globose, black, glossy.

One species distributed in E and SE Asia.

Annual herbaceous vines, monoecious, all part densely hispid. Leaves palmately 5-lobed, petioles eglandular. Tendrils dichotomous to trichotomous branched. Flowers usually unisexual, large, yellow, solitary. Male flowers: long-pedicellate; calyx-tube broadly campanulate, lobes leaf-like, dentate, reflexed; corolla rotate, 5-partitioned to base, segments obovate, entire; stamens 3, distinct, inserted to the corollatube, filaments short, anthers one 1-celled, two 2-celled, cells sigmoid, connective margined. Female flowers: short-pedicellate; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 3; ovary ovoid; placentas 3; ovules many; style thick; stigmas 3, expanded, 2-lobed. Fruit large, ellipsoid to terete, fleshy, hispid, glaucous, indehiscent. Seeds many, compressed, ovate-oblong, margin tumid.

One species and one variety, cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; commonly cultivated in China, also in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or woody climbers. Leaves alternate, entire, pinnately-veined; stipules subulate. Flowers bisexual, regular, in small fascicles or cymes, usually forming terminal racemes or panicles. Calyx hemispherical or turbinate, apex 5-lobed; lobes triangular. Petals spathulate or cucullate, ± clawed. Stamens 5, equaling or shorter than petals. Ovary superior, half-immersed in the disk, 2-locular; style short, entire or 2-cleft. Fruit an oblong or cylindrical drupe with a 2-celled stone.

About 31 species in E Africa to E Asia and N America; 18 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Bentham (1861, FHK 68) described “Berchemia ? sessiliflora” based only on a single small fruiting specimen from Hong Kong Island collected by C. Wright (K, holotype; US, isotype) and stated that the genus could not be determined with certainty at that time.

Succulent herbs. Leaves alternate, entire or sinuate. Flowers bisexual, solitary or in axillary panicles or spikes. Bracteoles minute or absent. Perianth urceolate, 5-lobed, cohering in fruiting by their enlarged hardened bases. Stamens 5. Ovary compressed, sunk in disc; style short; stigmas 2– 4, subulate. Utricles adnate to perianth-base. Seeds horizontal; testa thin, endosperm floury.

About ten species distributed in Europe, Asia and N Africa; one species in China; one variety cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or creeping, usually tetragonous. Leaves opposite, sometimes alternate in upper portion, simple, toothed or 1–3 times ternate or pinnatisect. Capitula radiate or discoid, solitary or in corymbose panicle. Involucres campanulate or subhemispherical; phyllaries 1–2‑seriate, united at the base, outer layers herbaceous, inner ones scarious. Receptacle paleate; palea narrow and scarious. Margin with or without 1 series of ligulate florets, neutral or rarely pistillate, corolla usually white or yellow. Disk florets tubular, hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla 4–5‑lobed, yellow or brownish orange; anther bases obtuse or sagittate; stylar branches flat with hairy acute or acuminate apical appendages. Cypselae compressed or 3–4‑angled, linear to obovate‑cuneate. Pappus awns 2–4, retrorsely barbed.

More than 200 species distributed in tropical and temperate regions, with richest species in America; ten species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial, saxicolous, and epiphytic herbs. Stemless or with very short stem. Leaves forming broadly funnelform to long-tubular rosettes; leaf blades linear or channel-shaped, margin serrate or serrulate, or rarely entire. Inflorescence a spike, racemes, or panicles; bracts often prominent and coloured. Flowers showy, blue, seldom red or greenish-yellow, actinomorphic or slightly zygomorphic. Sepals free, apex obtuse or rarely mucronate. Petals free, each with 2 ligulate scales at base. Stamens sub-equalling corolla or shorter, free or those opposite petals basally adnate to them; anthers medifixed. Ovary inferior; ovules many; style exceeding the stamens; stigma contorted or not. Fruit a dry berry.

About 62 species, native to tropical America; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees, dioecious, rarely monoecious. Leaves alternate, palmately 3(–5)-foliolate, long-petiolate; stipules small, caducous. Flowers unisexual, apetalous, without disk, in axillary or lateral panicles or racemes. Male flowers: sepals 5, valvate, initially concealing the stamens, afterwards reflexed; stamens 5, free, opposite the sepals; filaments short, anthers large, introrse, longitudinally dehiscent; pistillode short and broad, with short stalk. Female flowers: sepals 5, imbricate; ovary 3–4-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles 3–4, stout, entire, erect or recurved. Fruits small, baccate, globose, indehiscent, epicarps fleshy, endocarps chartaceous; seeds 3–6, oblong, estrophiolate, testa crustaceous, endosperm fleshy, embryo erect, cotyledon broad and flattened.


Two species in India and Sri Lanka to Indonesia, Australia and Polynesia; both in China and cultivated in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaves opposite or the upper part alternate, petiolate, margin serrate. Capitula small, subsessile or pedunclate, terminal or axillary, radiate or subdisciform, yellow; ray floret female, 1–2‑seriate, fertile; ligules small, 2–3‑toothed or absent; disk floret hermaphroditic, fertile, tubular, limb dilated 5‑fid. Involucre broadly ovoid, or subglobose. Phyllaries few, outer ones herbaceous; inner ones passing into the rigidly scarious paleae. Receptacle small, convex. Anther‑bases obtuse, entire. Style‑arms of disk floret narrow, flattened, with acute or subobtuse appendages. Cypselae truncate, of ray floret triquetrous or dorsally compressed, of disk floret 3– 4‑angled or laterally compressed. Pappus of 2–5, unequal bristles, connate at the base.

About ten species widely spread in tropics; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, usually branched. Stems usually terete, glandular pubescent, or rarely pilose. Leaves opposite, petiolate to almost sessile, margin entire or serrulate, 3 – 5(–7)-basiveined, indumentum like that of the branchlets. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, umbellate cymose or cymose paniculate. Bracts absent or small, caducous. Flowers (3–)4(–5)-merous. Calyx-tube campanulate to urceolate, usually 4-ribbed and glandular; calyx-lobes broadly triangular, apex cuspidate. Petals 4, white, rarely pink or purplish, ovate, oblong, or rarely lanceolate. Stamens 4(–5), equal in length; anthers linear, opening by a single pore, connective neither prolonged nor appendaged. Ovary partially or entirely adnate to the calyx-tube, 4-locular, apex with 4 tubercles; ovules numerous. Fruit capsular, ellipsoidal or obovoid, obscurely 4-ribbed, longitudinally dehiscing into 4 valves.

About 12 species distributed in Cambodia, China, E India, Indonesia, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam; nine species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs with irregularly lobed lumpy rhizomes. Stems of the flowering plants short, leafy, with some cataphylls at the base, gradually changing into leaves, the basal section developing into a rhizome after anthesis. Leaves 2 or 4, appearing with the scape, plicate-venose. Flowers purplish red, white-flowered cultivar rare. Flowers medium-sized, showy, in a loose terminal raceme, with deciduous bracts; sepals free, subequal; petals slightly larger, spreading; lip attached to the base of the column, trilobed, lateral lobes erect, slightly embracing the column, midlobe strongly lamellate; column long, without a foot, winged at the apex; clinandrium with broad lateral lobes; rostellum projecting forward forming a roof over the stigma; anther attached to a tooth of the clinandrium, incumbent, ovate; pollinia 8, unequal, in 2 groups of 4 pairs, waxy, oblong and laterally compressed, the base loosely connected by a granular laminiform appendage; viscidium obscure; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical, striate-sulcate. Capsules oblongfusiform, erect, rostrate.

About six species distributed from N Myanmar via China to Japan; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, sometimes subclimbing. Leaves alternate. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, in terminal pyramidal or oblong panicles, sometimes contracted, spike‑like or clustered. Involucres campanulate‑globose; phyllaries 3–5 seriate, imbricate, outer series shortest, pilose abaxially. Receptacles varying from species to species, hairy or glabrous, smooth or scabrous. Florets all tubular, the outer ones very numerous, in several rows, female and filiform, corolla minutely 2–3‑toothed; central florets usually few, hermaphrodite and broader, corollas tubular, with the upper portion slightly widening and shallowly 5‑toothed. Anthers 5, connate, sagittate at base, tails caudate‑acuminate. Stylar branches slender, tips obtuse or slightly pointed. Cypselae small, cylindric or subfusiform, with longitudinal ribs. Pappus of numerous capillary bristles, in a single series.

About 100 species widespread in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 30 species in China; ten species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, submerged freshwater. Stems short or elongate, erect or stoloniferous. Leaves basal or spirally arranged along stem, sessile, lanceolate or linear, with prominent midvein and several lateral veins, sheathed at base, minutely serrulate along margin. Spathe tubular, sessile or pedunculate, bifid at apex, with longitudinal veins, 1-flowered or sometimes several-flowered. Flowers bisexual or unisexual. Sepals 3, persistent, green, linear or lanceolate. Petals 3, white, longer than sepals. Stamens 3–9; filaments slender; anthers 4-celled. Pistils 3; ovary linear, attenuate into a long, filiform beak; styles 3; ovules many. Fruit linear to terete, long, narrow. Seeds many, oblongfusiform, smooth or with spines, sometimes with a filiform projection from each end.

About 11 species in tropical and subtropical regions; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, perennial, rhizomatous, stemless or stemmed. Leaves opposite, sometimes spirally arranged or basal; leaf blade villous to puberulent. Inflorescences lax, axillary, umbel‑like, 1–many‑flowered cymes; bracts 2, opposite. Calyx actinomorphic, 5‑sect from near base. Corolla white, blue, or purple, zygomorphic, tube campanulate to broadly campanulate; limb distinctly or indistinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, shorter than abaxial lip; abaxial lip 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, adnate to abaxial side of corolla tube near base, included; anthers dorsifixed, coherent, thecae divaricate, confluent at apex; staminodes 2 or 3. Disk inconspicuous. Ovary oblong, 1‑loculed; placentas 2, parietal, projecting inward, 2‑cleft, stigma 1, undivided. Capsule straight, narrowly oblong; valves 2, spirally twisted. Seeds unappendaged.

About 20 species in Australia, China, E India, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Polynesia, Vietnam; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs, shrubs, rarely small trees. Leaves alternate or opposite, usually toothed, trinerved. Stipules usually free, deciduous. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), in small dense clusters (glomerules); the clusters in unisexual spikes or panicles. Male flowers: perianth-segments (3–)4(–5), valvate in the bud; stamens as many, inward in bud. Female flowers: perianth tubular, apex constricted, with 2– 4 small teeth, slightly enlarged in fruiting time; ovary enclosed by perianth, 1-locular, with 1 erect ovule; stigma filiform on a short style, persistent. Achene closely enclosed in thin perianth.

About 65 species chiefly tropical and subtropical, a few extended to temperare regions; 25 species in China; three species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs or herbs, perennial, rhizomatous, sometimes stoloniferous, stemmed or stemless. Leaves alternate or basal. Inflorescences axillary, 1 – many‑flowered, umbel‑like cymes; bracts 2, opposite. Calyx actinomorphic, 5‑sect from base; segments equal. Corolla zygomorphic; tube campanulate, slightly shorter than limb; limb slightly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, slightly shorter than to as long as abaxial lip. Stamens 4, adnate to corolla near base, included; anthers basifixed, free, oval, thecae subparallel, confluent at apex, dehiscing longitudinally, poricidally, or transversely; staminode 1. Disk ring‑like or inconspicuous. Ovary ovoid, pubescent or glabrous, 1‑loculed; placentas 2, parietal, projecting inward, 2‑cleft; stigma 1, terminal, capitate, undivided. Capsule straight, linear; valves 2, straight. Seeds unappendaged.

About 12 species in Bhutan, S China, N India, Myanmar, N Vietnam; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or diffuse, often with tumid nodes. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Flowers small, bisexual, in axillary thyrses. Bracts and bracteoles small, caducous. Pedicels articulate at the apex. Calyx united, constricted at middle, lower part tubular, persistent, upper part campanulate or funnel-form, 5-lobed, deciduous after anthesis. Stamens 1–5, exserted. Ovary superior, stalked, 1-locular; style 1; stigma peltate or capitate. Fruit enclosed in persistent calyx, 5 –10 ribbed, often with viscid glands.

About 30 species spread over tropical and subtropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees; Stems usually spiny when young. Leaves palmately compound. Flowers solitary or fascicled, axillary or subterminal; bracts absent; calyx leathery, cup-shaped, truncate or short toothed; petals 5, obovate or obovate-lanceolate; stamens many; filaments connate at base into a tube, in several series, the outermost series aggregated into 5 bundles, alternating with petals; anthers 1-celled, reniform, peltate; ovary 5-locular, ovules many per locule; style slender, longer than stamens; stigma stellately 5-lobed. Capsule loculicidally dehiscing into 5 valves; the valves leathery, with silky wool inside. Seeds small, black, enclosed by woolly hairs.

About 50 species, mainly in tropical America, also in tropical Asia, Africa and Australasia; three species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms solid, tufted. Leaf sheath keeled or rounded on back, with tubercle-based hairs, especially on nodes and often at the mouth; leaf blades linear or lanceolate; ligule short, membranous, margin ciliolate. Inflorescence composed of spike-like racemes, central axis branched, racemes digitately or racemosely arranged, or combined into panicles, more than 8 spikelet pairs; rachis internodes and pedicels slender with a median translucent stripe between thickened margins. Spikelets paired, one sessile, the other pedicellate, dorsally compressed. Sessile spikelet horizontally falling together with adjacent rachis joint and pedicel; callus short, obtuse, bearded; lower glume as long as spikelet, smooth or with 1 or more depressions and/or pits, 7–11-veined, margins inrolled and keeled; upper glume boat-shaped, acute, 3-veined; lower floret reduced to an empty hyaline lemma; upper lemma stipitiform, entire, awned from apex; awn geniculate, glabrous; lodicules 2; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet similar to the sessile or smaller, awnless, staminate or neuter; lower lemma and palea absent.

About 30 species distributed throughout the tropics and subtropics; three species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or biennial herbs, multibranched, hispid and appressed pubescent. Leaves alternate. Racemes bracteates, terminal or axillary. Bracts leaf‑like. Flowers small, pedicellate. Calyx 5‑parted, not enlarged or slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla rotate, blue or white; tube short; throat appendages 5, scale‑like; lobes 5, overlapping in bud, apex obtuse. Stamens 5, inserted in corolla tube, inclusive; filaments extremely short; anthers ovoid, obtuse. Ovary 4‑parted, valves distinct. Style short, not surpassing valves; stigma capitate. Gynobase flat. Nutlets 4, tuberculate, with an oblong, elliptic, or orbicular ring‑like aperture. Seeds usually not curved.

About five species distributed in tropical and NE Asia; all five in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrub, often with spines. Leaves alternate, entire, petiolate. Flowers small, bisexual, in clusters of 3, subtended by large, colored bracts. Pedicels adnate to the midvein of bracts. Calyx-tube usually green, limb 5–6-lobed, red, purple or yellow. Stamens 5–10, included in perianth-tube; filaments unequal. Ovary stalked; stigma laterally. Fruit an achene, 5-ribbed.

About 14 species in C and tropical S America; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs. Stipules minute; stipels absent. Leaves 1-foliolate. Flowers in axillary short racemes. Calyx membranaceous, cup-shaped, truncate and minutely 5-toothed. Corolla white, all petals shortly clawed; vexillum broad, suborbicular; wings falcate-oblong; keels subsimilar to wings or slightly larger, scarcely connate dorsally. Stamens free or connate only at base; anthers oblong. Ovary stipitate, ovules numerous; style subulate, stigma terminal. Pods turgid, ovoid or subglobose, thin-leathery, 2-valved. Seeds 1–2, oblong or subglobose, brown or scarlet, strophiole large.

Four species distributed in W Africa to SE Asia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Based on the species B. callicarpa, the genus Bowringia was named by J. G. Champion in honour of his friend John C. Bowring, Jr. (1821–1893), a local naturalist in the 1850s and the eldest son of Sir John Bowring (1792 – 1872).

Annual or perennial herbs. Clums erect or ascending from the decumbent base. Leaf blades flat, linear to lanceolate, base broad, apex acute, often with cartilaginous margins; ligule very short, long ciliate, or a fringe of hairs. Inflorescence terminal, composed of 2–several racemes along a central axis; spikelets dorsally compressed, sessile or pedicellate, solitary or paired, rarely fascicles, alternating in 2-rows. Spikelets usually elliptic, falling as a whole, florets 1–2, lower floret staminate or neuter, upper floret bisexual; lower glume adaxial, varying in length and veinless to many-veined and subequaling spikelet, base sheathing, sometimes extended downward as a short stipe; upper glume similar and subequal to lower lemma; upper lemma leathery, smooth, striate or rugose, back facing away from rachis, margins inrolled, obtuse to acute, occasionally minutely mucronate; lodicules 2,5–7-veined; styles 2, free from the base, stigmas plumose, exerted laterally.

About 100 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World, especially Africa; nine species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs requiring dormancy in the cool dry season, with fleshy oblong tubers. Stem leafy. Leaves lanceolate, 3–7 cm, sessile. Flowers medium-sized, subtended by foliaceous bracts or solitary in the axils of normal leaves; sepals free, odd one uppermost, ovate, concave, the lateral sepals spreading, oblique; petals small, below the odd sepal and with it forming a hood over the column; lip undivided, fleshy, obcordate, calcarate, the spur stout, short, bilobed at the apex; column short and stout, lateral glands prominent; rostellum yoke-shaped; anther 2-celled, the thecae proximate, parallel; pollinia 2, coarsely tessellate; caudicles short; viscidia large, exposed; stigma 1, large, occupying the front cavity of the column below the rostellum, glossy; ovary sessile, striatesulcate, the ridges papillose. Capsules erect, narrowly oblong.

About 32 species distributed in Africa and tropical Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs. Leaves simple, entire to pinnately dissected. Racemes corymbiform, elongated when fruiting, ebracteate. Sepals 4, base of lateral pair saccate or not. Petals 4, yellow or white, long-clawed. Stamens 6, tetradynamous; nectar glands 4. Ovary 4 –50-ovuled. Siliques linear or oblong, terete, 4-angled or latiseptate, apex rostrate, dehiscing into 2 valves, glabrous, with distinct midrib, septum complete. Seeds usually uniseriate in each locule, globose or ovoid; cotyledons conduplicate.

About 40 species distributed in Eurasia, especially in Mediterranean; 14 species cultivated in China; five species (one represented by five varieties) in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrublets, or shrubs, erect or creeping. Stems usually quadrangular. Leaves petiolate, margin entire or denticulate, with 1–2(–4) pairs of lateral primary veins, tertiary veins parallel. Inflorescences terminal, umbellate, cymose, cymose paniculate, or rarely umbellate cymose; bracts small, often caducous. Flowers (3 or) 4-merous. Calyx-tube funnelform, turbinate, or subcampanulate; calyx-lobes (3 or) 4, apex cuspidate. Petals pink, red or purplish red, ovate, obovate, or broadly ovate, usually oblique. Stamens twice as many as petals, dimorphic, unequal in length; longer stamens usually without tuberculate at the base of anthers; connective decurrent, slightly prolonged. Ovary turbinate, 4-locular; style filiform; stigma apiculate. Capsule turbinate, usually obtusely 4-sided, woody, apex truncate but with crown usually exserted from calyx; calyx lobes usually persistent. Seed numerous, very minute, cuneate, densely granulate.

About 15 species distributed in E and S Asia; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or treelets, monoecious. Leaves simple, alternate, distichous, entire, usually turning black. Flowers apetalous, without disk, solitary or several in axillary clusters. Male flowers: calyx turbinate, funnel-form or hemispherical, fleshy, apex usually shortly 6-lobed; stamens 3, filaments 3, connate into an entirely capitate column; anthers 2-locular, longitudinally dehiscent; pistillode absent. Female flowers: calyx turbinate, hemispherical campanulate, or cap-shaped, 6-dentate to (5–)6-lobed, persistent, accrescent into saucer-shaped or discoid; ovary globose, truncate or depressed, 3-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles 3, bilobed. Capsules usually baccate, globose or depressed-globose, indehiscent, epicarp more or less fleshy, harder when dry, with 3–6 trigonous cocci when mature.


About 26 species in SE to S Asia, Pacific Islands and Australia; five species and one variety in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, rarely woody lianas. Leaves simple, alternate, entire, pinnately-veined, petiolate and stipulate. Flowers small1 unisexual (plant usually monoecious), in axillary clusters. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes valvate in the bud. Petals 5, small. Male flowers: stamens 5; filaments connate at the base, surrounding rudimentary ovary; anthers dorsifixed, introrse, 2-celled; rudimentary ovary terete or obovate, sometimes conical, 2–4-cleft or rarely undivided; disk cup-shaped or discoid. Female flowers: ovary 2-locular, half-enclosed in a cupular disk, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles shortly bifid. Fruit dupaceous, globular or ovoid, enclosing 2 indehiscent cocci.

About 60 species in tropical Africa, Asia and Australia; nine species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs or climbers, with milky juice, monoecious or dioecious. Stipules lateral, free, caducous. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged or distichous, serrulate or 3 –5-lobed; 3-veined at base, secondary veins pinnate. Male catkins solitary, cylindrical. Male flowers: perianth 4-fid, or lobed, valvate; stamens 4, inflexed in bud; pistillode minute. Female heads globose, mixed with persistent bracts. Female flowers: perianth tubular, 3–4-toothed, persistent; ovary enclosed, stipitate; style lateral, 2-partite; ovule pendulous. Syncarps globose; achenes surrounded by bracts and perianth, exserted, fleshy below, crustaceous above.

Four species distributed in E Asia and Pacific Island; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, monoecious or dioecious; root cortex and bark bitter. Leaves imparipinnate, alternate, stipulate or exstipulate; leaflets opposite or nearly so. Inflorescence a thyrse, axillary. Flowers unisexual, rarely bisexual, 4–5-merous. Sepals small, distinct or connate at base, imbricate. Petals small, distinct, valvate. Disk thick, entire or 4–5-lobed. Stamens inserted at base of disk. Carpels 2–5, distinct; ovule 1 per carpel; styles distinct or connate at base; stigmas distinct. Fruit drupaceous, hard, pericarp thin, somewhat fleshy, endocarp bony; seeds without endosperm, hilum broad, testa slightly thick and hard.

About six species mainly distributed in Africa, Asia, and N Oceania; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, often with kneelike pneumatophores. Leaves decussate, entire, glabrous, leathery, petiolate. Inflorescences cymose, 1–5-flowered, pedunculate. Flowers usually nodding; pedicels jointed. Calyx-tube obconical, 8–14(–16)-lobed. Petals as many as calyx lobes, usually 2-lobed and hairy at sinus. Stamens twice as many as petals; anthers introrse, 4-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary inferior, 2–4-locular; ovules 2 per locule. Fruit campanulate, enclosed by persistent calyx-tube. Seed usually solitary, viviparous.

Six species widely distributed in tropical region of the Old World; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, simple, entire. Flowers in terminal or axillary cymes, or occasionally reduced with only 1 flower. Calyx tubular or campanulate, 5‑toothed or 5‑lobed. Corolla salverform or funnelform, white, yellow or purple; tube slender, straight or slightly curved; limb spreading, ± irregular, 5‑lobed; lobes imbricate in bud; stamens 4, in 2 pairs, attached to corolla‑tube, included; filaments thick; anthers monomorphic. Ovary sessile, 2‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style compressed, 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, leathery or fleshy and berry‑like.

About 40 species distributed in tropical America; two species cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Brunfelsia macrophylla Benth. (大葉鴛鴦茉莉) was also cultivated previously.

Herbs hemiparasitic, erect, stiff, usually drying black. Leaves basally opposite, apically alternate; leaf blade margin entire, often coarsely toothed at stem base. Inflorescence spikes or spicate racemes. Bracteoles 2. Calyx tubular, veins 10, sometimes inconspicuous; lobes 5, short. Corolla lobes 5, subequal. Stamens 4, didynamous, included. Anthers 1‑celled, erect, dorsifixed, base obtuse, apex mucronate; styles apically clavate; stigma entire or incised. Capsules loculicidal; valves entire. Seeds numerous, somewhat dorsiventrally compressed.

About 60 species distributed in tropical to subtropical regions; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, rarely trees, or herbs usually with stellate hairs. Branches terete or 4‑angulate. Stipules interpetiolar, with various forms. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate, pinnately‑veined. Inflorescence capitate, racemose, spicate or paniculate. Calyx campanulate, 4‑lobed or 4‑toothed. Corolla infundibular or salverform, 4‑lobed. Stamens 4; anthers almost sessile. Ovary 2‑locular; ovules numerous in each locule. Capsules septicidal. Seeds numerous, small, ± flattened, or obscurely winged.

About 100 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 29 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Buddleja officinalis Maxim. (密蒙花) was also cultivated previously.

Epiphytic perennial herbs. Rhizomes slender, with 3–4 internodes, rooted below the pesudobulb. Pseudobulbs cylindrical, oblong or ovoid, often compressed or slightly flattened on one side near the base. Leaves solitary, apical to a pseudobulb, leathery, oblong, rarely ovate-oblong, rounded or retuse at the apex. Scape filiform, emerging from the base at the flat side of the pseudobulb, with 2–4 basal bracts and some median and supermedian bracts; pedicels filiform. Flowers small, in a subumbelliform raceme, or medium-sized and solitary; sepals subequal, spreading, the odd one free, the lateral ones obliquely dilated at the base and adnate to the column foot forming a mentum; petals smaller than the sepals; lip attached to the column foot, incumbent, mobile, fleshy, tongue-like, recurved, 2-lamellate, often warty; column short, stout, produced into a foot at the base, winged at the apical portion and extended into 2 arms; clinandrium short, 2 dentate; rostellum truncate; anther terminal, incumbent, depressed, hemispherical or obtuse-conical, deciduous; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, unequal, the inner one of each pair smaller, waxy, without caudicles or viscidium; stigma concave, occupying the entire front of the column; ovary obconical. Capsules oblong.

About 1000 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 98 species and three varieties in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials. Culms ± filiform, terete. Leaves basal, or rarely reduced to bladeless sheaths; blades narrowly linear or filiform; sheath with long silky hairs at apex. Involucral bracts leaf-like to glume-like. Inflorescence simple to decompound corymbose or capitate or reduced to a single terminal spikelet. Spikelets ovoid to ellipsoidal, often angular. Glumes many, all fertile, spirally imbricate. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 1–3. Stigmas 3; style base thickened, persistent on achene. Achenes obovoid to orbicular, trigonous to triquetrous, surface variously patterned.

About 100 species in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world; three species in China and Hong Kong.

Achlorophyllous mycoheterotrophic or green autotrophic, annual or perennial herbs; autotrophs with basal rosette of green leaves, and smaller green leaves appressed to stem; mycoheterotrophs with only small bract-like, achlorophyllous, stem leaves. Flowers solitary or in terminal cymes; perianth persistent after anthesis, often 3-winged, occasionally wingless; perianth tube generally 6-lobed, cylindrical to trigonous; outer perianth parts relatively large; inner perianth parts often minute, occasionally lacking; stamens 3, sessile or subsessile on perianth tube; connectives occasionally with (1–)2 apical glandular crests and/or a central, pendent, basal spur; ovary trigonous, 3-loculate, placentation axile; styles fused, branched towards the stigmas; stigmas 3, occasionally sessile, funnel-shaped. Fruit capsular, with persistent perianth, dehiscence generally irregular. Seeds many, oblong or ellipsoidal.

Approximately 57 species in tropical and subtropical regions; ten species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees; branchlets 4-angled. Leaves opposite, leathery, entire and pinnately-veined. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, racemose, spicate or capitate, with a solitary female flower at the apex and several male flowers at the lower part. Male flowers: sepals 4, in 2 series; stamens as many and opposite to the sepals; sterile stamen 1; rudimentary ovary very small. Female flowers: sepals 6, in 2 series; rudimentary stamens very small; ovary consisting of 3 carpels, surmounted by 3 separate styles. Fruit a loculicidal capsule.

About 70 species in C Europe, the Mediterranean region, E Asia and C America; 17 species in China; three species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Trees or climbing shrubs. Leaves polymorphic, usually orbicular or ovate. Cymes terminal or axillary. Flowers small, bisexual; sepals 5, base connate; petals 5, more or less adnate to staminal tube, clawed, hooded at upper portion, apex usually 3-lobed, central lobe long and narrow; stamens united in a short tube, with 5 barren lobes (staminodes) and 5 nearly sessile 2-celled anthers between them; ovary sessile, 5-locular, locule 2-ovulate; style 5-fid at apex or subentire. Capsules globose, echinate, carpels separating when ripe and opening along inner edge, 1-seeded. Seeds without endosperm and with spirally contorted cotyledons.

About 130 species distributed in tropics; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or vines, unarmed or often armed with sharp prickles. Leaves bipinnate. Inflorescence a panicle or raceme, axillary or terminal. Flowers medium-sized or large, yellow or orange. Hypanthium concave. Sepals distinct, imbricate, the lower one larger, cucullate. Petals 5, clawed at base, 4 petals often orbicular, sometimes oblong, the uppermost one smaller, different from the rest 4 by colour, shape and indumentum. Stamens 10, distinct, in 2 whorls; filaments thickened at base, hairy; anthers ovoid or ellipsoidal, dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary 1-locular, ovules 1 – 7; style terete; stigma truncate or concave. Pods ovate, oblong or lanceolate, sometimes falcate, flat or swollen, not winged or narrowly winged, smooth or spiny, leathery or woody, rarely fleshy, dehiscent or indehiscent. Seeds ovoid to globose, endosperm wanting.

About 150 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 17 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, subshrubs, woody or herbaceous twiners. Stipules and stipels small or caducous. Leaves pinnately or sometimes digitately 3-foliolate, alternate, with glandular dots on abaxial surface of leaflets. Racemes axillary or terminal; bracts caducous; bracteoles absent. Calyx campanulate, shortly 5-toothed, the upper 2 teeth united or slightly lobed at apex. Corolla persistent or not; vexillum suborbicular, obovate or obovate-elliptic, stipitate, with incurved auricles on both sides at base; wings narrowly or broadly elliptic, auriculate; keel oblique-orbicular, apex obtuse. Stamens diadelphous (9+1); anthers uniform. Ovary subsessile, 2–many-ovuled. Pods linear-oblong, flattened, with oblique indented lines between the seeds. Seeds reniform or subglobose, shining, marked with blotches of different colour.

About 32 species mainly distributed in tropical Asia, Pacific and Madagascar; seven species and one variety in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Climbers, rarely erect shrubs, dioecious; sheaths, petioles, rachis, cirri and flagella usually armed with various kinds of spines, bristles or hairs. Stems usually clustered, wrapped in sheaths, sometimes bare when old. Leaves pinnate, reduplicate, rarely bifid; pinnae arranged regularly, irregularly or in groups, linear, lanceolate or rhomboid; sheaths variously spiny, often with ocrea, usually with knees in the climbing species; flagellum usually whip-like, borne from sheath, with single or grouped, hook-like or claw-like spines; rachis sometimes terminating in a cirrus armed with single or groups of recurved spines, and mostly present in the species without flagellum. Inflorescences mostly elongate from some flagella, branched to 3 orders, male inflorescences more branched than female ones; prophyll and bracts (overlapped on branches and rachillae) tubular, spiny in climbers. Flower ovoid, small; calyx usually cupshaped, 3-fid; petals 3, longer than sepals; male flowers borne along two opposite side of rachilla; stamens 6; female flower borne together with a sterile flower; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule. Fruits ovoid, subglobose, ellipsoidal or oblong, various coloured, covered with imbricate scales; sepals and petals persistent, flat or stalk-like. Seed usually 1, endosperm homogeneous or ruminate.

About 380 species mostly in tropical and subtropical Asia and Australia; 27 species (15 endemic) in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs, caespitose. Leaves large, plicate-venose, papery. Scape axillary to the second or the fourth leaf of the current year's growth. Flowers medium-sized, in a terminal raceme; sepals equal, free, spreading; petals almost similar as or slightly narrower than the sepals, spreading; lip adnate to the sides of the column, calcarate, 3-lobed, the spur slender, usually longer than the ovary, lateral lobes erect or spreading, midlobe truncate or bilobed, disk with cristate or lobed calli; column short, without foot; clinandrium membranous; rostellum triangular, acuminate, bifid; anther subterminal, incumbent, acuminate; pollinia 8, waxy, lanceolate, attenuate at the apex; viscidium linear or obovate; stigma transversely dumb-bell-shaped, visible from the sides of the rostellum, or U-shaped below the rostellum; ovary subcylindrical. Capsules oblong-ellipsoidal.

About 150 species distributed in tropical Asia, Papua New Guinea, Australia, tropical Africa and C America; 49 species and five varieties in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, cespitose, erect or creeping, rhizomatous. Stem usually unbranched, rarely branched. Leaves all basal, or also cauline, rich in metallic hues, and many of them attractively barred, striped and blotched. Inflorescence mostly capitate or cone-like, subsessile or pedunculate; bracts few to many, imbricate, distichous or spiral. Fower-pairs usually 3 or more in axile of bract; bracteoles usually present; sepals 3, equal or subequal. Corolla 3-parted, tube almost equal to or longer than sepals; staminodes 3, outer staminode 1, rarely 0, usually large, petaloid, cucullate staminode smaller, with lateral lobe; callose staminode often large; fertile stamen 1 with a slightly petaloid appendage; ovary 3-locular. Capsules dehiscent, valves thin-leathery or hard; seeds 1–3, aril 2-lobed.

About 300 species distributed in tropical America; two species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs; stem glandular pubescent. Leaves alternate, entire or undulate. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, solitary to stem and branch terminal. Involucres campanulate or hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, 1–2‑seriate, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate. Receptacle flat or convex, naked. Peripheral florets pistillate and fertile, in 2–3 rows, corolla ligulate, apex 3‑toothed; stylar branches linear. Central florets bisexual but functionally staminate, infertile, corolla tubular with apex 5‑lobed; anther bases sagittate; style undivided or slightly branched, swollen at apex. Cypselae incurved.

About 20 species native to the Mediterranean areas, W Europe and W Asia; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, usually unarmed. Stipules often persistent, or sometimes spinescent, rarely absent. Leaves bipinnate, eglandular, pinnae 1–several pairs; leaflets opposite, small and numerous or larger and from few pairs to one. Flowers in globose axillary heads, or in terminal racemes, 6 – 5-merous, polygamous. Calyx campanulate, toothed. Petals united to middle; the flower in the middle of the heads sometimes heteromorphous, with an elongated tubular corolla. Stamens numerous (up to 100 ), red or white, more or less united into a tube and long-exerted, showy. Anthers mostly glandular-hairy. Ovary sessile, ovules numerous; style filiform. Pods strap-shaped, slightly falcate, flat, rigidly leathery, often narrowed to the base, margins thickened, 2-valved, valves elastically opening from the apex to base, continuous inside. Seeds obovate or orbicular, compressed, testa hard, with pleurogram, without aril.

About 200 species, mainly in tropical and subtropical area of America, W Africa to Pakistan; three species (two cultivated) in China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, erect or rarely scandent. Branchlets terete or tetragonal, covered with stellate, verticillately branched, dendritic, mealy tomentose, or rarely simple and hooked hairs. Leaves simple, opposite or whorled, petiolate or subsessile, margin serrate, rarely entire, usually hairy and glandular. Cymes axillary, sessile or pedunculate. Bracts small, linear, rarely leafy. Flowers small, often actinomorphic. Calyx cupular or campanulate, rarely tubular, truncate or minutely 4‑dentate, persistent in fruit. Corolla purple, red or white, campanulate or tubular, lobes 4. Stamens 4, inserted on the base of corolla tube; filaments slender, often exserted; anthers ovoid or ellipsoidal, dehiscing by longitudinal slits or apical pores. Ovary superior, imperfectly 2‑locular; ovules 1 per locule. Style usually longer than stamens; stigma usually dilated. Fruit a small globose drupe, endocarp bony, mesocarp fleshy, exocarp thin, splitting into 4 pyrenes when mature. Seeds small, ellipsoidal; seed coat membranous; endosperm wanting; cotyledons fleshy.

About 140 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, few in tropical America and Africa, and very few in temperate Asia and N America; 48 species in China; 11 species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, petiolate or sessile. Inflorescence a spike or head, terminal or lateral; bracts deciduous. Flowers bisexual. Hypanthium subglobose or campanulate. Sepals 5, caducous or persistent. Petals 5. Stamens many; filaments distinct or slightly connate at base, red or yellow, usually several times as long as petals; anthers dorsifixed, cells parallel, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary slightly adnate to hypanthium, 3(–4)-locular; ovules many per locule; style linear; stigma not enlarged. Capsule semiglobose to globose, apex truncate, valves included in hypanthium. Seeds linear; testa thin; embryo straight.

About 20 species distributed in Australia; three species introduced to China; two species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual erect herbs. Leaves alternate, coarsely dentate. Capitula large, heterogamous, radiate, solitary. Involucre hemispherical; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate, the outer ones herbaceous or foliaceous, the inner ones membranous‑scarious. Receptacle plain, alveolate. Ray florets 1–2‑seriate, female, corolla ligular, tube short, lip entire or 2‑lobed. Disk florets fertile, corolla tubular, regular, limb shortly 5‑lobed; anther base entire, obtuse, apical appendage very long; style enclosed, stylar branches flat, the apical appendage deltoid. Cypselae compressed, hairy on upper portion, each side with 1 obscure rib; pappus 2‑seriate, the outer setae short.

One species native to N China; it is also cultivated in gardens in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family. Lansdown (2006, Novon 16: 354 – 361) has taxonomically reviewed the genus in Asia recently.

Annual perennial herbs. Leaves simple, alternate, spirally arranged, margin irregularly toothed. Flowers solitary in leaf‑axils, ebracteate. Calyx‑tube adnate to the ovary; limb with 5 small lobes. Corolla open on one side beyond middle; lobes 5, extending forward, margin winged. Stamens 5; filaments free. Ovary inferior, 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style 2 – 3‑branched; the cup‑shaped indusium of stigma slightly 2‑lobed, densely hairy on the margin. Fruit a capsule, opening in 2 valves. Seeds compressed, slightly thickened at margin.

About six species mainly distributed in Australia; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, entire, glabrous, many parallel-veined. Racemes or panicles terminal or axillary. Flowers bisexual or unisexual. Sepals 2–4, imbricate, inner ones often petal like; petals (2–)4 –(8–)12, imbricate; stamens many; filaments free or united into several bundles at base; anthers 2-celled, opening by longitudinal slit; ovary 1-locular, 1-ovuled; style filiform, stigma peltate. Drupes globose or ovoid, pericarp thin, mesocarp fleshy or fibriform. Seeds with thin arils, cotyledons fleshy, oily.

About 187 species mainly distributed in tropical Asia, few in C & S America; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual, prostrate or erect to twining herbs. Leaves subsessile to petiolate, oblong to hastate or sagittate, or rarely pedate. Inflorescences axillary, 1–several‑flowered cymes; bracteoles 2, sepal‑like, inserted immediately below calyx, ovate and sometimes saccate, enclosing calyx, persistent. Sepals subequal, persistent. Corolla campanulate or funnelform, with 5 distinct midpetaline bands, glabrous. Stamens inclusive, equal. Pollen grains globose, pantoporate, not spiny. Ovary 1‑locular or incompletely 2‑locular, 4‑ovuled. Style 1, inclusive; stigmas 2, clavate. Capsule globose, glabrous, indehiscent. Seeds 4, smooth or minutely tuberculate.

About 70 species distributed in temperate and subtropical regions of the world; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, serrate, rarely entire.
