Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or 2–3 clustered, sessile or shortly pedicelled; bracteoles 2–10, spirally arranged, persistent or caducous; sepals 5 to many, distinct or not at all distinguishable from the lower bracteoles; petals 5–12, unequal, slightly connate at the base; stamens many, outer ones with the proximal half connate to the base of petals, inner ones free; anthers more or less basifixed; ovary 3– 5-locular, with 4 – 6 pendulous ovules per locule, styles filiform, connate at base. Capsule woody, globose or oblate, 3– 5-locular, sometimes reduced to 1–2-locular by abortion, opening loculicidally into 3– 5 valves from apex; central axis (columella) persistent, calyx persistent at base of fruit, rarely deciduous. Seeds globose, wingless; semi-globose or polygonal; embryo straight, radicle superior.

About 120 species distributed in E and SE Asia; 98 species in China; 13 species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Deciduous woody vines, without tendrils, climbing by aerial roots. Branchlets terete. Leaves opposite, pinnately or palmately compound; leaflets serrate. Flowers large, red or orange‑red, in terminal thyrses or in clusters. Calyx campanulate, irregularly 5‑lobed. Corolla campanulate‑funnelform, slightly bilabiate; lobes 5, spreading. Stamens 4, didynamous, curved, included. Ovary compressed ellipsoidal, 2‑locular, base surrounded by a large disk, ovules multiseriate per locule. Capsule dehiscing loculicidally, valves woody. Seeds many, compressed, membranous, with semi‑transparent wings.

Two species disjunctly distributed in N America and E Asia; one species in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees, polygamo-monoecious. Leaves simple, alternate, exstipulate, petiolate, pinnately-veined. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, capitate. Bracts 3. Calyx cupular, 5-toothed. Petals 5, caducous, imbricate. Stamens 10, unequal in length, inserted on disk, in 2 whorls; filaments slender, glabrous; anthers 4-celled. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; ovules 1 per locule; style glabrous, 2–3-lobed. Fruit a samara, ellipsoidal, sessile, clustered in globose heads.

Two species endemic to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Rhizome stout, usually ascending, sometimes slightly woody. Stem usually very short or sometimes slightly elongate. Leaves basal or alternate on short stem, usually distichous equitant; leaf blade lorate to ovate-elliptic, basally dilated and amplexicaul. Scape axillary, erect. Inflorescence a terminal spike, densely flowered, bracts lanceolate to ovate, often longer than flowers, sometimes with several sterile bracts apically. Perianth segments 6, proximal 1/2–2/3 connate into a tube, fleshy, sometimes with a ring-like, fleshy appendage in throat; lobes spreading or incurved, sometimes fimbriate at margin. Stamens 6; filaments proximally adnate to perianth tube; anthers positioned as high as or higher than stigma, dorsifixed. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with 2–4 ovules in each locule; style short, 1(–3.5) mm, or absent; stigma small, 3-lobed. Fruit a berry, 1–3-seeded.

About 16 species distributed from India through Himalaya to China; 16 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, rarely shrubs. Leaves alternate, odd-pinnate, rarely unifoliolate, often stipulate, rarely exstipulate; leaflets opposite or subopposite. Inflorescence a thyrse, rarely a raceme or spike, axillary or terminal. Flowers bracteate, hermaphrodite or polygamous, 3-merous. Calyx cupular or campanulate, lobes triangular, valvate. Petals 3, imbricate, usually exceeding calyx, oblong-obovate. Stamens 6, distinct or completely connate; filaments flat; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 2–3-locular; ovules 2 per locule; style terete, or stigma subsessile, capitate, 3-lobed. Drupe ovoid to ellipsoidal, with a 1–3-locular and 1(–3)-seeded stone; cotyledons often partite, contortuplicate.

About 75 species mainly distributed in tropical Africa and Asia; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems twining, prostrate or suberect. Stipules small, wart-like or inconspicuous; stipels present, deciduous. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate. Racemes axillary. Flowers purple-violet, rose, or whitish, solitary or 2– 6-fasciculate on swollen nodes. Bracts and bracteoles minute, deciduous. Calyx campanulate, nodose; 2-lipped; upper lip larger, truncate or 2-lobed, lower lip small or minute, entire or 3-toothed. Corolla longer than calyx; petals shortly clawed; vexillum large, suborbicular, reflexed; wings narrow, falcate or subtwisted, free; keel broader than wings, incurved, obtuse or beaked, beak inflexed or spirally twisted, shorter than vexillum . Stamen monadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary shortly stalked, many-ovuled; styles incurved, beardless. Pods large, loriform or oblong, compressed or slightly turgid, with prominent rib along ventral suture and extra rib parallel and close to it, dehiscing by twisted valves. Seeds 10– 15, elliptic or oblong, hilum linear.

About 50 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; six species in China (including cultivated); three species in Hong Kong.

According to Dunn & Tutcher (1912), Canavalia ensiformis (L.) DC. was cultivated in Hong Kong, but it is uncommon now.
Morphological characters and geographic distribution are the same as those of the family.

Erect or scandent shrubs, sometimes armed. Leaves alternate, shortly petiolate. Inflorescence spicate, axillary; bracts small, persistent. Flowers bisexual, monochlamydeous. Perianth urceolate or campanulate, 4(–5)-lobed, pilose; lobes valvate. Stamens 4–5, opposite to perianth-lobes; filaments filiform, free or connate to disk scales at base; anthers ellipsoidal, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk scales alternate with stamens. Ovary superior, ovoid or cylindric, 1-locular. Style short, hardly exceeding the perianth tube. Drupe ellipsoidal; mesocarp fleshy; endocarp thin. Seed 1; embryo small, with 3 or 4 cotyledons.

Three species distributed in S and SE Asia, Australia, Pacific Islands; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, unarmed or with axillary thorns. Leaves opposite, short‑petiolate, stipules intrapetiolar, triangular, united at the base. Flowers in axillary clusters or cymes. Calyx‑tube short, obconical or hemispherical; limb very short, truncate or 4–5‑toothed. Corolla‑tube short, urn‑shaped, subglobular or funnel‑shaped, usually with a ring of recurved hairs in inner side; lobes 4–5, ovate‑triangular, spreading, valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the corolla throat; filaments short or none; anthers fixed dorsally but near the base. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 pendulous or descending ovule in each locule; style thick; stigma exserted, entire or 2‑lobed. Fruit a drupe, globular or didymous.

About 50 species in tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia and Africa; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms erect or ascending from the decumbent base. Leaf blades linear; ligule membranous, margin ciliate. Inflorescence a terminal open panicle with elongate central axis, rachis internodes and pedicel slender, margins thickened; racemes of 1–5(–8) spikelet pairs, often reduced to triads. Sessile spikelet dorsally compressed; callus very short, obtuse, shortly bearded, falling off with pedicellate spikelet from the joint of rachis; lower glume herbaceous and cartilaginous, apex acute to obtuse, margins narrowly incurved and 2-keeled; upper glume boat-shaped, abaxially keeled; lower floret reduced to a small empty hyaline lemma; upper lemma stipitiform, entire, awned from apex; awn geniculate, glabrous or puberulous; lodicules 2; stamens 3 or absent; styles 2. Pedicellate spikelet similar to the sessile or smaller, herbaceous.

About 14 species distributed in tropics and subtropics in the Old World; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen erect or scandent shrubs, or rarely small trees. Leaves simple, entire, spirally arranged; stipules usually spiny. Flowers in racemes, umbels or panicles, or solitary a little above the axils of the leaves and 2 to many arranged in a vertical row on the flowering branches. Sepals 4, in 2 whorls. Petals 4, imbricate. Stamens 6 to many, free, inserted on the base of gynophore. Ovary usually 1-locular, with (2–)4(– 6) parietal placentae and many ovules. Fruit a fleshy berry, 1–many-seeded.

About 250 species widely distributed from tropical to temperate regions; about 33 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or biennial herbs, glabrous, with simple or furcated hairs. Stems erect. Leaves simple, basal ones pinnately dissected or entire, petiolate, cauline ones toothed or entire, with or without petioles, if epetiolate, then base amplexicaule. Racemes corymbiform. Flowers sparse, white or pink. Sepals 4, oblong; petals 4, spathulate clawed. Stamens 6, tetradynamous; nectar 6. Ovary sessile, ovules many; style short; stigma compressedglobose, lunate. Silicles obcordate to triangular, dehiscing by 2-valves. Seeds brown, 6 –12 per locule, elliptic.

Five species mainly distributed in Mediterranean regions; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, sometimes shrubby. Stems erect, much branched. Leaves simple, alternate. Flowers solitary or in cluster of 2 – 3 in axils of branches. Calyx campanulate or cup‑shaped, apex truncate or minutely 5‑toothed. Corolla rotate, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes valvate in bud. Stamens 5, inserted near base of corolla‑tube; filaments slender; anthers free, opening longitudinally. Ovary 2(–3)‑locular; style slender; stigma clavate, sometimes obscurely 2–3‑lobed. Fruit a pod‑like indehiscent berry, many‑seeded.

About 25 species distributed in S America; one species cultivated in China and in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees. Stems usually with buttresses at base. Leaves decussate, petiolate, margin entire or serrate. Inflorescences axillary, dichasial cymes. Bracteoles 2, distinct or connate at base. Flowers bisexual, small. Calyx 5 – 8-lobed, lobes triangular. Petals as many as calyx lobes, membranous, conspicuously clawed. Stamens twice as many as petals, free; anthers 4-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk annular, fleshy. Ovary inferior, (3–)5–8-locular; ovules 2 per locule; style filiform; stigma discoid, capitate, or obscurely lobed. Fruit a berry, 1–many-seeded. Seeds arillate, not viviparous.

About ten species distributed in tropical regions of the Old World; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual to perennial herbs, with simple hairs or glabrous. Stems erect or prostrate. Leaves simple or pinnately compound. Racemes corymbiform, usually ebracteate. Sepals 4, ovate or oblong, base of lateral pair saccate or not. Petals 4, white, pink or purple, obovate, oblong or spathulate, sometimes clawed; Stamens 6 and tetradynamous, rarely 4; nectar glands confluent and subtending bases of all stamens. Ovary 4–50-ovuled, style distinct or rarely obsolete, stigma capitate, entire. Siliques linear, dehiscent, flat. Seeds uniseriate, oblong or ovate, flat; cotyledons often accumbent.

About 200 species distributed worldwide; 48 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous or woody climbers, rarely shrubs, monoecious or dioecious. Leaves usually biternate or bitrilobate; stipules small, deciduous. Leaflets pinnately lobed or dentate, usually with pellucid glands. Panicles axillary; peduncles rather long, first pair of branches forming tendrils or spines; bracts and bracteoles subulate. Flowers unisexual, zygomorphic; pedicels articulate. Sepals 4–5, imbricate, outer 2 smaller. Petals 4, with a large scale inside, scales of abaxial petals with broadly winged appendage, scales of adaxial petals simple. Disk lobed into 2 large glandular lobes at base of petals. Stamens 8 (male flowers), slightly longer than petals. Ovary (female flowers) ellipsoidal, trigonous, 3-locular; ovules 1 per locule, inserted at middle of middle axis; style short; stigma 3-lobed. Capsules inflated, saclike, 3-locular; pericarp membranous or papery, veined. Seeds 1 per locule, subglobose, hilum cordate or suborbicular.

About 12 species mostly distributed in tropical and subtropical America; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with creeping or stoloniferous rhizome, monoecious, rarely dioecious (not in Hong Kong). Culms densely or loosely tufted, trigonous. Leaves basal or cauline, linear, rarely lanceolate, sheathed at base. Bracts leaf-like to setaceous, rarely scale-like, with or without sheath. Inflorescence racemose, spicate, fasciculate or paniculate with one or more spikes; branches of the inflorescences with or without a sheath-shaped or utriculiform bracteole (cladoprophyll) at base. Spikes with or without peduncle, composed of many unisexual spikelets. Spikelets reduced to a single unisexual naked flower, without perianth, in axil of its single bract (glume). Male flower with (2–)3 stamens, filaments distinct. Female flower with one pistil contained in a connate prophyll (utricle); style slender, sometimes thickened at base, persistent or deciduous, stigmas 3 or 2; reduced spikelet-axis sometimes present in the utricle. Fruit an achene rather tightly or loosely enveloped in the persistent utricle, trigonous, plano-convex or biconvex.

More than 2000 species widely spread over both hemispheres; 502 species (245 endemic) in China; 28 species in Hong Kong.

Carex graciliflora Dunn reported previously (Check List HK Plants 307. 2002; 108. 2004) belongs to another taxon and shall be discussed in a future report.

Majority of the Hong Kong species are forest species, with a few specialized in open habitat. Similar to most genera in Cyperaceae, the Hong Kong Carex species generally do not show any adaptation to animal pollination or seed dispersals, although bees have been seen visiting the male spikes of C. pumila (Shaw, J. C., PhD. Thesis, The University of Hong Kong, 2000) and C. tenebrosa (personal observation), respectively. Utricles of some species may be adapted to animal and water dispersal.

Small trees or shrubs. Stems unbranched, lactiferous. Leaves clustered at stem apex, large, palmately lobed, long petioled; stipules absent. Racemes axillary, long pedunculate. Flowers unisexual or bisexual. Male flowers: calyx minute, 5-lobed; corolla-tube slender, 5-lobed, lobes oblong or linear; stamens 10, inserted at the mouth of corolla-tube; anthers 2-celled, introrse; pistillodes subulate. Female flowers: calyx as in male flowers; petals 5, linear-oblong, caducous; staminodes absent; ovary sessile, 1- or 5-locular, with septum; styles absent or very short; stigmas 5, lobed or not; ovules many, rarely a few, 2–many rows on parietal placentas. Berries fleshy. Seeds many, with fleshy arils.

23 species distributed in tropical America; one species introduced to China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves small, petiolate, alternate on annual twigs, fasciculate on brachyblasts, scabrous, adaxially white spotted, margin coarsely dentate. Inflorescences axillary, usually 2–6‑flowered in sparse glomerules. Calyx 5‑parted; lobes spreading. Corolla white; tube short; throat without appendage; lobes spreading. Stamens exserted. Style terminal on ovary, 2‑cleft nearly to base, nearly as long as corolla, persistent, beaked in fruit; stigmas 2, capitate. Drupes red or yellow, subglobose; endocarp bony, entire at maturity, 4‑seeded.

One species distributed in China, Japan, Indonesia, Australia; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, branches many. Leaves alternate. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, usually pendulous. Involucres campanulate, hemispherical or subglobose; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, outer layers herbaceous or with tips foliaceous, inner ones scarious. Receptacle plain and nude. All florets yellow, fertile; marginal ones female, 1– many‑seriate, corolla tubular with apex 3–5‑lobed. Disk florets many, bisexual, corolla tubular with upper limb dilated, 4–5‑dentate; anther bases sagittate, caudate; stylar branches of disk florets linear, subcomplanate, obtuse to rounded at apex. Cypselae ribbed and grooved, apex narrowed as short glandular beak with a cartilaginous ring. Without pappus.

About 20 species native to C Asia and Europe; 17 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs, or shrubs, erect or climbing. Leaves opposite, simple, entire or dentate, usually with yellow glands. Cymes axillary or terminal, solitary or aggregate into thyrses, rarely flower solitary. Calyx campanulate, limb (4–)5(–6)‑dentate or ‑lobed, lobes often triangular or lanceolate, slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla short‑tubed, slightly 2‑lipped, upper lip 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed, central lobe larger, margin entire or dentate. Stamens 4, unequal or subequal, often strongly exserted, inserted on apical part of corolla tube. Ovary 4‑locular; ovule 1 per locule, pendulous or laterally attached. Stigma 2‑cleft. Fruit dry, globose, usually dividing into four nutlets; nutlet winged or not.

About 16 species distributed in C & E Asia; 14 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, monoecious. Stems solitary or clustered, with a single flowering period, dying after flowering and fruiting. Leaves large, induplicately bipinnate; pinnae triangular, like a fish tail in shape, with irregularly toothed outer margins; sheaths closed, not forming a crownshaft; petioles swollen at base. Inflorescences usually branched 1 order, rarely unbranched; prophyll 1, peduncular bracts several, both tubular and persistent; rachillae usually many, long, pendulous; flowers unisexual, in triads of 1 female with 2 lateral male flower; male flowers: sepals 3, imbricate, petals 3, stamens 6–150, linear, filament short; female flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, staminode 0–6; ovary 3-locular, stigma 3-lobed. Fruits subglobose, orange, red or purple. Seed 1–2, endosperm ruminate except one species homogeneous.

About 13 species distributed in India throughout SE Asia and W Pacific islands; four species in China; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, distichous, usually glandular; stipules small, caducous, rarely persistent. Flowers small, bisexual, axillary, several to many in dense or sparse glomerules, rarely solitary. Pedicels short, articulate, often surrounded by several scale-like bracts. Calyx 4 –5-lobed, lobes imbricate, persistent. Petals absent. Stamens (5 –)8–10(–12); filaments united into a short tube with staminodes at base; staminodes as many as stamens and alternate with them, hairy. Ovary superior, 1-locular; parietal placentas 2– 4, with many ovules per placenta; styles short or absent; stigmas capitate. Capsule fleshy, leathery or hard, dehiscing into 2–3 valves; seeds several to many, ovoid or obovoid, enclosed by a layer of membranous aril.

About 160 species, distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or herbs. Leaves paripinnate, often glandular on petioles and leaf rachis; leaflets opposite, sessile or shortly petiolulate; stipules various. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate, axillary or terminal, rarely flowers solitary or few clustered in leaf axils. Bracts and braceteoles various. Calyx-tube solid, turbinate or slenderly vase-shaped; lobes 5, imbricate, reflexed at anthesis, deciduous. Petals usually 5, obovate or elliptic-oblong, clawed at base or sessile, subequal or lower 2 longer. Stamens 10, usually unequal, in 2 whorls, the outer whorl consisting of 3 long abaxial stamens (filaments sigmoidally bent proximally and incurved distally, often dilated or abruptly nodulose in the outer curve, anthers dorsifixed, dehiscing ventrally above middle by vertical slits and by basal pores) and 2 much shorter, sterile, adaxial stamens, the inner whorl consisting of 2 unequal pairs of stamens (filament straight erect or gently bent forward, anthers dorsifixed, dehiscing by basal pore) and 1 much smaller, sterile stamen. Ovary stipitate, linear incurved, ovules many per locule; styles incurved; stigmas small. Pods pendulous, shortly stipitate, linear or terete or laterally compressed, indehiscent, with septum between seeds; valves woody, stiffly papery or crustaceous. Seeds lying transversely, endosperm present.

About 30 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, few in temperate regions; several species introduced to China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

C. javanica L. and C. javanica var. indochinensis Gagnep. are occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous parasitical twiners. Stems threadlike, ramified, green or greenish brown. Leaves reduced to minute scales. Flowers bisexual, sessile, in axillary spikes, racemes or heads. Perianth ovoid or tubular, lobes 6, in 2 whorls, the outer minute, persistent. Fertile stamens 9, the 3 inner ones with 2 glands at the base; anthers 2- celled, introrse, those of the inner stamens extrorse; staminodes 3, small. Ovary superior, free from the perianth tube at anthesis. Fruit enclosed in the succulent tube of the perianth.

About 17 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mostly in Australia, with a few in Africa; only one species in China; it occurs in Hong Kong.

Tree, rarely shrubby. Branchlets with terminal buds; bud usually compressed ovoid, with many, decussate-imbricate scales. Leaves alternate, usually 2-ranked. Stipules extrapetiolar. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious). Male flowers 3 –7-fascicled, rarely solitary and scattered, forming upright spikes or panicles; perianth 5- or 6-lobed; stamens usually 9 –12; rudimentary pistil very small, densely covered with curved woolly hairs. Female flowers usually 1–3 per cupule, in separate usually short spikes, sometimes at the base of the male spikes; staminodes when present opposite perianth lobes; ovary 3-locular; styles usually 3, terminating in punctiform stigmas. Cupules covered with spine-like or rarely scale-like bracts, solitary and scattered on rachis, completely or partially enclosing nut. Nuts 1–3 per cupule, maturing the second year or rarely in the current year.

About 120 species, mainly in S and E Asia; 58 species in China; ten species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Branches verticillate or pseudoverticillate, slender, hairy when young. Leaves (5 or) 6–17 per whorl. Bracteoles never greatly thickened in infructescence (“cone”), without an abaxial protuberance. Samara body pale yellow-brown or greyish, dull, glabrous.

17 species in Australia, extending to SE Asia, Malesia, Pacific Islands; three species introduced to China; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs erect, perennial and often woody at base, juice watery. Leaves opposite; petioles short, intrapetiolar and interpetiolar glands present; leaf blade herbaceous to somewhat leathery, entire. Flowers terminal and axillary, solitary or rarely in 2‑ or 3‑flowered cymes. Sepals small, narrowly oblong, awl‑shaped, without glands. Corolla purple, red, pink, or white, salverform; tube glabrous or sparsely puberulent, throat constricted, woolly to velvety; lobes spreading, obliquely obovate, overlapping to left, apex apiculate. Stamens inserted at widened portion of corolla‑tube; anthers free, oblong, base obtuse; disk of 2 glands. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style; ovules numerous per carpel. Style filiform, with a collared‑style head. Fruit a paired follicles, many‑seeded.

Eight species distributed in Madagascar, India and Sri Lanka; one species cultivated in China.

Shrubs or small trees, usually armed with opposite axillary thorns. Leaves opposite or crowded on very short lateral branches. Stipules interpetiolar, entire, pointed from the broad base. Flowers solitary or 2 – 3 clustered at apex of short branches or tufts of leaves, usually subsessile. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped or ovoid; limb usually 5‑toothed or 5‑lobed. Corolla bell‑shaped, usually with silky hairs on abaxial surface; tube cylindric, short or long; lobes usually 5, spreading or recurved, contorted in the bud. Stamens usually 5, attached to the throat, alternate with corolla‑lobes; filaments very short; anthers dorsifixed, slightly exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style with 2 thick stigmatic lobes, or nearly entire. Fruit a berry, often crowned by the persistent calyx‑lobes.

About ten species in S, SE Asia and Africa; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Woody or herbaceous vines, hermaphroditic or polygamo-monoecious. Tendrils usually 2- or 3-furcate, rarely racemosely branched. Leaves palmately compound, 3–5(–9)-foliolate; stipules 2, small. Inflorescence a compound dichasium or corymbose polychasium, axillary. Flowers 4-merous. Calyx cupular. Petals 4, spreading at anthesis. Stamens 4, opposite to petals. Disk well developed, membranous, 4-lobed or undulately lobed, connate to ovary. Style short; stigma not lobed. Berry globose or subglobose, 1–4-seeded.

About 60 species distributed in Asia, Oceania and Africa; 17 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees; trunk spiny or not. Leaves spirally arranged, palmately compound, petiolate, leaflets 3–9, glabrous, entire. Flowers solitary or 2–15 fascicled on nodes, pendulous, actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic; calyx campanulate urceolate, irregularly 3 –5-lobed, thick, persistent; petals connate at base, fallen off with stamens and style, reddish or yellowish white; stamen-tube short, adnate to petals; filaments 3 –15, distinct or in 5 bundles, each bundle with 1–3 twisted 1-celled anthers; ovary 5-locular, ovules many per locule; style filiform, obscurely 5-lobed. Capsule woody or leathery, pendulous, ellipsoid or nearly obovoid, loculicidally dehiscing into 5 valves, densely woolly inside. Seeds many, enclosed in woolly hairs, arillate.

About ten species, mainly distributed in tropical America; one species introduced to China, also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs climbing, glabrous, rarely pubescent. Leaves alternate, subentire or serrate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, thyrsoid, cymose, or flowers solitary. Flowers unisexual, rarely bisexual; sepals 5. Petals 5; disk membranous or fleshy, annular to cupulate or 5-lobed, intrastaminal. Stamens 5, inserted on disk margin or under disk; anthers longitudinally dehiscent, introrse. Ovary 3-locular, rarely 1-locular; ovules erect, 1–2 per locule; stigma 3-lobed. Capsules subspheroidal, rarely oblong, leathery, remaining axils after fruit, loculicidally dehiscent. Seeds 1–6, ellipsoidal, albuminous, enveloped by fleshy red arils.

About 31 species distributed in tropical to subtropical regions; 24 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubby. Leaves alternate, petiolate. Flowers bisexual, in terminal spikes, simple, or branched and forming panicles. Bracts and bracteoles chaffy, persistent. Perianth-segments 5, nearly equal, scarious and glabrous. Stamens 5; filaments united at the base into a cup; anthers 2-celled; staminodes absent. Ovary 1-locular, with several ovules; style single, with a capitate or minutely 2-lobed stigma. Utricle opening transversely.

About 50 species dispersed over the World, especially in tropical and warm regions; three species (one endemic) in China; one species and one commonly cultivated variety in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen trees or shrubs. Stipules small, free. Leaves alternate, base slightly oblique, margin entire or serrate, triplinerved. Inflorescence a cyme or fascicle on young shoots, or female flowers solitary. Flowers polygamous. Sepals 4–5, green or purple, imbricate, deciduous when fruiting. Stamens 4 –5. Ovary sessile, borne on hairy torus, 1-locular; style 2-fid, reflexed. Fruit a drupe, exocarp fleshy; endocarp bony. Seed solitary, with membranous seed coats; cotyledons very broad, sometimes crumpled.

About 50 species widely distributed in temperate or tropical regions; 14 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect or ascending, often branched near the base. Leaf blades usually flat; ligule a ciliate rim. Inflorescence a spike-like panicle, composed of spiculate units, arranged on all sides of elongated central axis; units composed of 1–few spikelets inside an involucre, composed of bristles which are connate at lower part, or fixed to a flat disk at base of spikelets, often arranged in 2 heteromorphous rings; units shortly stipitate, each unit with small knob at base, often articulate, falling entire and acting as a bur; central axis protruding beyond uppermost unit. Sessile spikelets lanceolate, acute; glumes unequal, lower usually short or absent, upper usually shorter than spikelet; lower floret staminate or neuter, membranous, lemma thin papery to membranous, palea well developed, stamens 3; upper floret bisexual, lemma indurate at maturity, usually swollen, acuminate, margins thin and flat, palea the same texture; upper lemma firmer, with narrowly involute, firm margins embracing same texture palea; lodicules absent; stamens 3, anthers linear; styles 2, connate at base, exserted apically. Caryopsis elliptic-depressed-globose.

About 23 species distributed in tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial prostrate herbs, glabrous or pubescent, rooting at the nodes. Leaves simple, long petiolate; stipules absent; petioles sheathing at base; blades entire or palmately-veined. Umbels solitary or fasciculate; peduncles axillary, few-flowered, rarely 1-flowered; involucre of 2–3 conspicuous bracts. Calyx-teeth obsolete. Petals white or rose-tinged, valvate in buds, narrow, inflexed at apex. Stylopodium absent. Styles short, equaling filaments. Fruits orbicular or ellipsoidal, reniform, base cordate to truncate, strongly laterally compressed; commissure narrow, constricted; the primary and the secondary ribs prominent, 7–9 per mericarp, filiform. Carpophore entire, very short.

About 20 species mostly in the tropical regions, especially in S Africa; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Small annual herbs; stem decumbent or procumbent, branched. Leaves alternate, oblanceolate‑spatulate, usually toothed. Capitula small, heterogamous and disciform, sessile to subsessile, axillary. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, oblong, herbaceous with hyaline margins. Receptacle hemispherical, naked. Marginal florets female and fertile, in many rows, corolla short and narrowly tubular, inconspicuously 2–3‑lobed at apex. Central florets bisexual and fertile, few, corolla short and broadly tubular, apically 4‑toothed; anther bases obtuse, without apical appendages; stylar branches short, obtuse or truncate at distal ends. Cypselae tetragonous, hairy along the ribs. Pappus none.

About four species native to Australia, S America and Asia; one species as a common weed in China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms tufted, erect. Leaf blades broadly linear to lanceolate, narrowed at base, with distinct cross veins; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, much branched, the primary branches often reduced to racemes. Spikelets lanceolate, laterally compressed or subterete, comprising 1 fertile floret, or 2–3 fertile florets with a barren rachilla extension, or with diminished florets at the apex; glumes shorter than spikelet, unequal, separated by a short internode, 3–5-veined, dorsally keeled, apex acute or acuminate; lower glume 3/4–4/5 length of upper glume; lemmas oblong, dorsally rounded, 5–7-veined, apex acute or apiculate; palea narrower, equal to or shorter than its lemma, keels ciliate or glabrous; lodicules 2. Stamens 2–3.

Three or four species distributed in W Africa, tropical Asia, Australia and Pacific islands; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems prostrate or erect, quadrangular or terete. Leaves cauline, opposite to alternate above, sessile. Flowers axillary, solitary or forming lax spikes or racemes; Bracteoles 2. Calyx spathaceous, split on 1 side, shortly 3–5‑lobed. Corolla funnelform, swelling below throat or distally and gradually expanding, somewhat 2‑lipped; lobes 5, subequal, erect or spreading. Stamens 4, didynamous, included, thecae subequal or one theca smaller and sterile; filaments usually hairy. Ovary ovoid; stigma biflabellate. Capsules loculicidally 2‑valved; valves entire. Seeds numerous; testa spirally striate or reticulate.

About nine species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Australia; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Subepiphytic perennial herbs. Stems bamboo-like, 2 or 3 together, leafy. Leaves all cauline, papery, plicate-venose, disarticulate below the leaf blade. Scapes emerging from the axils of cataphylls or lower leaves, with basal imbricate scale. Flowers medium-sized, showy, in lateral racemes; sepals and petals subsimilar, free, spreading; lip attached to the base of the column, 3-lobed, the lateral lobes erect and the apex recurved, midlobe transversely widened, 2-lobed, crisped; column suberect, short, stout, winged on the sides, slightly enlarged at the base, the apex truncate; clinandrium narrow; rostellum ovate, acute; anther ovoid, incumbent, hanging on the upper margin of the clinandrium; pollinia 8, obovoidacuminate; viscidium small, discoid; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical, striate-sulcate. Capsule oblong, rostrate.

About six species distributed mainly in Japan, China and SE Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3–4, short‑petiolate. Stipules short, intrapetiolar. Flowers bisexual, regular, densely crowded in globular heads, on terminal or axillary peduncles, or sometimes paniculate; bractless or with bracteoles. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped; limb unequally 4–5‑toothed. Corolla tubular‑funnel‑shaped, yellow or white, glabrous at throat, apex 4‑lobed; lobes imbricate. Stamens 4, inserted in throat of corolla; filaments short; anthers dorsifixed, with exserted connectives. Disk inconspicuous. Ovary inferior, 2‑locular, with a solitary pendulous ovule in each locule; style linear, with capitate or clavate stigma. Aggregate fruit globular, composed of numerous leathery nutlets.

About six species in Asia, Africa and N America; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Arborescent or shrubby bamboos. Rhizomes short necked, pachymorph. Culms straight, pendulous, or occasionally clambering; internodes terete, smooth, usually glabrous; wall usually thin; nodal ridge not prominent; sheath scar prominent. Branches many, subequal or occasionally with a dominant branch replacing main culm. Culm sheaths deciduous, thickly papery to leathery, usually rigid, apex truncate or concave; auricles usually conspicuous; oral setae usually developed, often fimbriate; ligule truncate, short, serrulate; blade reflexed, sometimes erect. Leaf sheaths pubescent; auricles usually conspicuous; blade lanceolate or ovate-elliptic, variable in size, transverse veins scarcely visible. Inflorescence fully bracteate, iterauctant, initially densely glomerate with many pseudospikelets, terminal to a leafy shoot, later spicate, lateral to leafless flowering branches, subtended by several large bracts. Spikelets 1-flowered, with a rachilla extension. Glumes 2–3, long mucronate or awned; lemmas similar to glumes, convolute. Palea thin, 2-keeled. Lodicules 3. Stamens 6; filaments free. Ovary stalked; style long, hollow; stigmas 2–3, plumose. Caryopsis nut-like, terete, apex with persistent style base.

About nine species distributed in S and SE Asia; six species in China (Xizang, Yunnan); one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or ascending from a prostrate base, usually pubescent or with glandular hairs. Leaves opposite, usually sessile. Flowers bisexual, in terminal dichotomous cymes. Sepals 5, rarely 4, free. Petals 5, rarely 4, bi-lobed, rarely entire or retuse. Stamens 10, rarely 5; filaments glabrous or hairy. Ovary 1-locular, with many ovules; styles usually 5, rarely 3, opposite with sepals. Capsule cylindrical, crustaceous, opening at the top into twice as many teeth as there are styles.

About 100 species mainly in N temperate regions; 32 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as the family.

Five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees with latex. Branches stout. Leaves alternate. Cymes terminal, long pedunculate. Flowers 5‑merous. Calyx deeply divided, without glands inside. Corolla white, funnelform, throat slightly dilated, ribbed, or with 5 pubescent scales; lobes broad, overlapping to left. Stamens inserted at corolla throat; anthers narrowly oblong, apiculate, free from pistil head, lobes rounded at base; disk absent. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style, glabrous; style filiform, dilated distally; pistil head shortly 2‑cleft. Fruit a drupe, often only one carpel developing, ellipsoidal or globose, with fleshy exocarp, thick, fibrous mesocarp and lignified endocarp. Seeds 1 or 2 per locule, flattened, ellipsoidal, wingless.

Seven species distributed from Madagascar to Australia and Pacific islands; one species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, entire. Flowers in terminal or axillary corymbs or panicles. Calyx campanulate or tubular, apex 5‑lobed or 5‑toothed; lobes valvate in bud. Corolla tubular or salverform, with a long tube ± enlarged or contracted at the throat, apex shallowly 5‑lobed; lobes valvate in bud. Stamens 5, attached to the middle of corolla‑tube; filaments often with hairs or small dentoid appendages at base; anthers opening longitudinally. Ovary 2‑locular, often with a short stipe; ovules 3 – 6 in each locule; style slender; stigma peltate and sometimes obscurely 2‑lobed. Fruit a berry, with a few or only 1 seed.

About 160 species distributed mostly in tropical America; three species cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, or herbs. Leaves paripinnate, often glandular on petioles and leaf rachis; leaflets opposite, sessile or shortly petiolulate; stipules various. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate, axillary or terminal, rarely flowers solitary or few clustered in leaf axils. Braceteoles 2. Calyx-tube short, lobes 5, imbricate. Petals usually 5, subequal or lower 2 longer. Androecium actinomorphic, stamens (4 – )10, in 2 whorls, actinomorphic, the 2 whorls unequal in length, anthers dorsifixed or basifixed, dehiscing by apical pores, thecae ciliolate along the sutures. Ovary slender, sometimes curved, sessile or stipitate, ovules many per locule; styles incurved; stigmas small. Pods elongate, usually compressed, dehiscent. Seeds smooth or pitted, without areoles.

About 330 species in most tropical and subtropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial or epiphytic herbs; rhizomes short, hairy on the contact surface, clinging to wet boulders below trees along streams. Leaves basal, petiolate, ovate or elliptic. Flowers small, inconspicuous, in a terminal small raceme; sepals connate, forming a tube above the middle; petals white, very small, mostly concealed; lip adnate to the sides or rarely to the base of the column, unguiculate, the claw with inflexed margin or simple and without folding margin, the apex dilated, often bilobed and fringed or dentate, rarely undivided and entire, the base furnished with 2 calli, rarely without callus; column short, the apex furnished with 2 glossy glands and produced into an elongate appendage on each side; rostellum long and deeply cleft; anther ovate-acuminate, deeply sunk in the clinandrium; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, sectile, with or without slender caudicle; viscidium oblong or obovate, cuneate; stigmas 2, connivent to the lateral glands; ovary ovoid or oblanceolate. Capsules succulent.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Africa, tropical Asia and Pacific islands; 13 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely subshrubs. Leaves alternate, petiolate, usually nearly pubescent, margin entire, lobed or toothed. Inflorescence a glome rule, rearranged in axillary or terminal spicate or paniculate cymes. Flower bisexual or sometimes pistillate, sessile, without bract and bracteole. Perianth-lobes 5, free or shortly connate at base, persistent. Stamens usually 5. Ovary globose base slightly flattened; stigmas 2– 5. Fruit a utricle with membranaceous pericarp, enclosed by persistent perianth and adnated with seed. Seed 1, horizontal or vertical.

About 100 species distributed worldwide, mainly in temperate regions; 19 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen shrubs; buds with many imbricate scales. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Flowers with very short scaly stalks, solitary from axillary buds on branches of the previous year's growth. Tepals 15 –25, ± waxy, imbricate, yellow; often with purple stripes. Stamens 5 or 6, free; filaments short, dilated at base, usually hairy; anthers 2-celled, extrorse. Carpels 5 –15, free, inserted inside of a hollow receptacle, with 2 ovules in each carpel, usually only one developed. Fruit (enlarged receptacle) constricted at the mouth, puberulous outside.

Three species, all endemic to China.

Shrubby bamboos, rarely subarborescent. Rhizomes leptomorph, with running underground stems. Culms usually diffuse, sometimes tillering (pluricaespitose), erect; internodes terete or 4-angled, often basally grooved above branches; nodes prominent to very prominent, basal nodes often with a ring of sparse or dense root thorns; sheath scars usually with a ring of pubescence or persistent base of culm sheath. Branches 3(–7 on upper culm), subequal, buds ovate-triangular, open at front, prophyll reduced. Culm sheaths deciduous and leathery, or sometimes persistent and papery; auricles minute or absent; blade reduced, to 1 cm, narrow. Leaves (1–)2–5 per ultimate branch; blade lanceolate, base cuneate. Inflorescence fully bracteate, weakly iterauctant, 1–3 single pseudospikelet racemes loosely fasciculate, subtended by gradually enlarged bracts. Spikelets several- to many-flowered, sessile. Rachilla disarticulating. Glumes usually 1–3, frequently 1 subtending a bud; lemma papery or membranous; palea membranous, 2-keeled, obtuse; lodicules 3, membranous. Stamens 3; filaments free. Ovary ellipsoidal; style 1, short; stigmas 2–3, plumose. Fruit a nut-like caryopsis with a hardened pericarp.

About 37 species distributed in E Asia; 34 species (31 endemic) in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious. Leaves simple, opposite, margin entire or serrate, petiolate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal panicles, sometimes cymes or racemes. Flowers bisexual or unisexual. Calyx 4‑parted or 4‑lobed. Corolla white or yellow, 4‑parted; lobes almost free to base or united into a very short tube or joined in pairs at base, valvate in bud. Stamens 2(–4), inserted at base of corolla‑lobes. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 pendulous ovules in each locule; style short; stigma entire or 2‑cleft. Fruit a drupe; endocarp bony. Seed 1; endosperm fleshy or absent; radicle upward.

About 100 species, distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; eight species and one variety in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with short thick rhizome and fibrous roots. Leaves radical, rosulate, petiolate; leaf blade ellipitic to oblong-lanceolate, evergreen, margin entire or minutely undulate. Scape arising from centre of leaf rosette, erect, simple, with 3–30 small, bract-like leaves. Inflorescence a terminal spike, many-flowered; bract absent. Flowers sessile, zygomorphic, small. Perianth segments 6, free; upper 3–4 spatulate-linear to filiform, petal-like; lower 2–3 much shorter or absent. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth segments; anthers basifixed, extrorse, with locules confluent or free. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles 3, stigmatic adaxially. Fruit a capsule, septicidally dehiscent. Seeds fusiform, winged at one end.

Four species distributed in China, Japan, Korea; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs, perennial, often rhizomatous, stemless or with simple or branched stems. Leaves basal or opposite on stems, unequal to equal in a pair. Inflorescences umbel‑like, axillary, 1–many‑flowered cymes; bracts (1 –)2(–3), opposite. Calyx actinomorphic or slightly zygomorphic, 5‑sect from base or (3–)5‑lobed. Corolla purple, blue, white, yellow, pink or purple‑red, zygomorphic; tube funnelform‑tubular to campanulate or cylindric, longer than limb; limb 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, shorter than abaxial lip; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes equal or central lobe longer. Stamens 2, adnate to abaxial side of corolla tube near or above middle, included; anthers dorsifixed, coherent, thecae divaricate, confluent at apex, dehiscing longitudinally; staminodes 1–3 or absent. Disk ring‑like. Ovary linear, 1‑loculed; placentas 2, parietal, rarely 2‑loculed, abaxial locule sterile, or placenta 1, axile, projecting inward, 2‑cleft; stigma 1, abaxial, obtriangular to oblong, 2‑lobed to undivided. Capsule straight, linear to very narrowly ovoid, dehiscing loculicidally to base; valves 2 or 4, straight. Seeds elliptic, glabrous, unappendaged.

About 140 species distributed in tropical regions of Asia; 104 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs or perennial herbs. Leaves opposite or verticillate, serrate; stipules tiny; petioles connected by a transverse ridge on stem. Inflorescences spicate or branched in panicles, terminal or axillary. Flowers small, bisexual; perianth absent. Stamens usually 3, rarely 1, on one side of apical part of ovary if stamens 3, central anther 2-celled or occasionally absent, lateral anthers 1- celled, if stamen 1, anther 2-celled; connectives ovoid, lanceolate, or sometimes linear. Ovary 1-locular; ovule 1, pendulous, orthotropous; style usually absent, rarely present; stigma truncate or parted. Drupes globose, obovoid, or pyriform.

Approximately 17 species distributed in temperate to tropical Asia; ca. 13 species occur in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect or ascending. Leaf blades linear, flat or folded; ligule membranous, short, ciliolate; leaf sheaths rounded or keeled and flabellate. Inflorescence of secund spikes, digitately arranged or occasionally in 2 or more whorls, with biseriate, closely imbricate spikelets. Spikelets sessile, laterally compressed, 2–4(–6)-flowered, lowermost bisexual, second bisexual or sterile, successive florets male or sterile and progressively reduced, disarticulating above glumes; glumes unequal, usually shorter than florets, lanceolate, membranous, 1-veined, acuminate to an awn-point; callus bearded; lemma of fertile floret keeled, lanceolate to obovate, cartilaginous to leathery, usually ciliate on margins and keel, apex entire or emarginate, subapically mucronate or awned; upper lemma and higher lemmas ± reduced or vestigial, awned or awnless, often epaleate and black at maturity; paleae usually of same length as lemma, 2-keeled; lodicules 2, small. Stamens 3. Ovary glabrous; styles 2, short, stigmas laterally exserted. Caryopsis crowned by thickened base of style, ellipsoidal to linear, usually trigonous; pericarp very thin, hyaline, free, embryo rather large; hilum punctiform.

Approximately 50 species distributed in tropical and warm-temperate regions throughout the world; five species (one introduced) in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Besides the three native species, Chloris gayana Kunth is newly introduced as ornamental plants and not treated here.

Perennial herbs. Rhizome short, or sometimes slightly elongate, usually with ± thick or slightly fleshy roots. Leaves basal, subdistichous or fasciculate, sessile or petiolate, usually linear to linear-lanceolate, conduplicate, base sheathing. Scape axillary, slender, branched or not. Inflorescence a terminal raceme or panicle; bracts small. Flowers bisexual, usually white; pedicels articulate. Perianth segments 6, free, 3–7-veined, persistent or marcescent. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth segment; filaments filiform, usually slightly widened near middle; anthers nearly basifixed, introrse. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with 1–several ovules in each locule; style slender; stigma small. Fruit a capsule, acutely 3-angled, loculicidal. Seeds black-coated, flattened.

About 100–150 species distributed mainly in tropical areas, especially in Africa and India; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

records.authority: B. L. Burtt & A. W. Hill
records.text:
Deciduous trees, polygamous or dioecious. Leaves imparipinnate, alternate; leaflets opposite, petiolulate. Flowers 5-merous, unisexual; male flowers arranged in axillary or subterminal thyrsoid panicles; female flowers solitary. Calyx cupular, 5-lobed. Petals 5, distinct, imbricate, revolute at anthesis. Stamens 10, inserted at the base of disk. Disk 10-lobed; lobes alternate to filaments. Ovary superior, 5-locular, ovule 1 per locule; styles 5, distinct; stigmas capitate. Drupe ellipsoidal to obovoid, mesocarp fleshy, endocarp bony, with 5 germination holes at apex; seed without endosperm, cotyledons thick.

Ones species distributed in China, Indochina to NE India and S Japan; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or semi-evergreen trees. Leaves palmately compound, leaflets 5 –7, serrate. Flowers showy, solitary or 2–3 clustered in axils of apical leaves. Calyx cup-shaped, irregularly 2– 5-lobed. Petals 5, linear or oblong, spreading or reflexed. Stamen-tube in 2 whorls, the outer whorl very short, anthers sterile, the inner whorl much longer, with fertile anthers. Capsule loculicidally dehiscing into 5 valves. Seeds numerous, covered with woolly hairs.

About five species in tropical America; one species cultivated in China, also in Hong Kong.

Perennial glabrous herbs; stem creeping with adventitious roots growing at nodes. Leaves alternate, palmatilobed to palmatisect with 3 or 5 segments, long‑petiolate. Capitula homogamous, all florets ligulate and bisexual, axillary, solitary or 2–5 loosely arranged as corymbs. Involucres cylindric; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, outer layers small ovate, inner ones lanceolate. Receptacle plain and nude. Ligulate florets 12–20 per head, corolla yellow, ligule 5‑toothed at apex; anther bases sagittate; stylar branches slender. Cypselae brown, fusiform, slightly compressed, obtusely 10‑ribbed, glabrous, apex attenuate into thick beak. Pappus in 2 rows, white, scaberulous.

One species only, distributed in Russia, Japan, Korea and China; also in Hong Kong.

Erect or decumbent annual herbs or subshrubs. Stipules minute; stipels present. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, or often reduced to remain only a terminal leaflet. Racemes or panicles terminal or axillary. Flowers small. Calyx membranous, campanulate, accrescent in fruiting, 5-lobed; lobes ovate-lanceolate, subequal. Corolla rarely longer than calyx; petals clawed; vexillum broad, base attenuate, clawed; wings adherent to keel; keel obtuse. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary several-ovuled; styles linear, incurved, stigma capitate. Pods 1–several-segmented; segments reticulate, folded on top each other within persistent calyx, indehiscent.

About 13 species distributed in tropical Asia and Atlantic; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Leaves alternate, 1–2‑pinnately divided or margin toothed. Capitulum heterogamous and radiate, pedunculate, solitary or in loose corymbs. Involucres broadly hemispherical; phyllaries 4‑seriate, rigidly herbaceous with margin and apices membranous or scarious. Receptacle convex to hemispherical, nude. Marginal ligulate florets 1‑seriate, or with various series in cultivated form, pistillate and fertile, corolla yellow or white, ligule linear to linear‑oblong. Disk tubular florets bisexual and fertile, corolla yellow, lower part narrow, upper part broad campanulate, apex 5‑lobed; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑elliptic; stylar branches linear, truncate at distal end. Cypselae developed from ray florets 3‑angulate, 2–3‑winged; those developed from disk florets with one side broadly hard‑winged. Both without pappus.

Five species native to Mediterranean region, with wide range of cultivation and hybridization; two to three species cultivated in Hong Kong for ornamental uses or for vegetables, such as Chrysanthemum carinatum Schousb. (蒿子桿), Chrysanthemum coronarium L. (艾菜; Chrysanthemum spatiosum auct. non Bailey; Photo 549) and the one described below.

Shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate; stipules absent. Flowers small, several to many fascicled and axillary, pedicellate or sessile. Sepals 5 (or 6). Corolla campanulate, 5 –11-lobed. Fertile stamens 5 –10 in 1 whorl, inserted at throat and opposite to corolla-lobes; staminodes absent. Ovary 2–10-locular, hairy or not . Style longer to shorter than ovary, glabrous. Fruit a berry, 1– 8-seeded, exocarp thick to very thin. Seed coat papery to crusty; scar narrow to wide, lateral.

About 70 species distributed in Madagascar; tropical and subtropical America, tropical Africa and Asia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms erect or ascending. Leaf blades usually narrow; ligule a short ciliolate rim or a line of hairs. Inflorescence a lax terminal panicle; primary branches whorled, filiform, usually unbranched, each bearing a raceme; racemes usually a triad of 1 sessile bisexual spikelet flanked by 2 pedicellate staminate or barren spikelets, falling off together at maturity, rarely with another pair of spikelets below the triad; rachis internodes and pedicels slender. Sessile spikelet laterally compressed; callus slightly thicken and oblique, 2-floret; lower glume cartilaginous to subleathery, often spinulose; upper glume boat-shaped, usually shortly awned; lower floret reduced to an empty hyaline lemma; upper lemma linear, entire or 2-toothed, awned usually from apex; lodicules 2; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet dorsally compressed, well developed or reduced, staminate or barren. Caryopsis linear.

About 44 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Buds lepidote, hirsute. Leaves usually paripinnate, sometimes imparipinnate, alternate; leaflets usually alternate, entire. Inflorescence a panicle, axillary or terminal. Flowers bisexual, 4–5-merous. Calyx short, 4–5-lobed. Petals 4–5, distinct, convolute. Staminal tube cylindrical, slightly shorter than petals, apex entire or 10-dentate; anthers 10, ellipsoidal, exserted. Disk absent or inconspicuous. Ovary shortly stipitate, 3–5-locular; ovules many per locule, in 2 series. Style thick; stigma capitate. Fruit a septicidal capsule, 3–5-locular. Seeds many per locule, flat, winged; endosperm absent; cotyledons leaf-like, orbicular.

One species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia; one species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, usually all parts aromatic. Leaves alternate or opposite, leathery, usually trinerved or triplinerved. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary or subterminal. Flowers bisexual, rarely polygamous. Perianth-tubes short, cup-shaped or campanulate; lobes 6, subequal. Stamens 9 in 3 whorls, the 3 inner ones with 2 glands at the base; anthers 4-celled, introrse, those of the 3 inner stamens extrorse. Staminodes 3, with capitate or cordate abortive anthers. Fruits fleshy, resting on the enlarged cup-shaped receptacle and base of perianth.

About 250 species distributed in tropical and subtropical E Asia, Australia and Pacific Islands; 49 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic perennial herbs. Rhizomes slender. Pseudobulbs ovoid, slightly flattened on one side. Leaves solitary, terminal to the pseudobulb, fleshy, lasting for 3 years. Scape emerging from the base of the flattened side of a pseudobulb, with basal and submedian scales. Flowers resupinate, of moderate size, graceful and attractive, in a simple umbel arranged in form of a fan; sepals unequal, the odd one free, ovate or ovate-oblong, fornicate, the lateral ones 2–6 times longer than the odd one, adnate to the column foot and forming a mentum at the base, then twisted, with the upper margins meeting before the lip, forming a coherent platform; petals similar to and smaller than the odd sepal, lip tongue-like, fleshy, mobile, contracted at the base and hinged to the end of the column foot, incumbent, recurved; column short, stout, the base produced into an elongate and curved foot, the sides winged, and the wings extended into 2 prominent arms at the apex; clinandrium truncate or dentate; rostellum truncate; anther depressed, hemispherical, deciduous; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, the inner one of each pair smaller, without caudicles or viscidium; stigma strongly concave, with a large glossy sticky gland on the upper margin below the rostellum and two small ones on the opposite margin; ovary obovoid-cylindrical. Capsules oblongellipsoidal, rostrate, ridged.

About 130 species distributed in E Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia and Australia; 25 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs, monoecious, rarely dioecious, plant spiny. Stem branched or not. Leaves alternate, entire, serrate‑dentate to pinnatifid, spiny along margin. Capitula homogamous and discoid, with all florets bisexual or all female, nodding or erect, long‑pedunculate or sessile and spicate. Involucres ovoid, campanulate to globose; phyllaries in many rows, imbricate or inconspicuously imbricate, erect or spreading, cobwebby‑hairy, often sticky, apex spinulose. Receptacle plain or convex, densely long‑hairy. Florets red, purple, rarely yellow or white, corolla tubular, limb equally to obliquely 5‑lobed, sometimes deeply cleft; anther bases sagittate, basal appendages lacerate, filaments free, papillose hairy; stylar branches coherent except the obtuse tips, with a ring of hair below the branches. Cypselae glabrous, compressed or faintly tetragonous, ribbed or smooth, apex truncate or obliquely truncate, rostrate. Pappus unequal in length, plumose, base connate and shed off as a ring.

About 250–300 species distributed in Europe, Asia, N Africa, N & C America; about 50 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Vines, hermaphroditic or polygamo-monoecious. Branches and leaves ± fleshy, pith white. Tendrils unbranched or bifurcate, sometimes racemosely branched. Leaves simple or palmately compound, stipulate. Inflorescence a compound dichasium or an umbel, leaf-opposed. Flowers small, 4-merous. Calyx cupular. Petals spreading at anthesis. Stamens 4. Disk well developed, margin undulate or slightly 4-lobed, connate to the base of ovary. Style 1; stigma undivided or 2-divided. Berry obovoid or ellipsoidal, 1- or 2-seeded.

About 350 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 15 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbaceous vines, monoecious or dioecious. Tendrils dichotomous or trichotomous branched, sometimes unbranched and spine-like. Leaves deeply 3–5-partitioned. Flowers yellow, solitary, rarely fasciculate. Male flowers: calyx-tube broadly campanulate, 5-lobed; corolla rotate or broadly campanulate, deeply 5-partitioned; stamens 3, inserted at the base of calyx-tube, filaments distinct, short; anthers distinct or slightly coherent, one 1-celled, the others 2-celled, cells linear, sigmoid; connective dilated, not protrudent; pistillodes glandular. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 3, setiform or ligulate; ovary ovoid, placentas 3; style short, columnar, stigmas 3, thick, reniform, nearly 2-fid; ovules many, horizontal. Fruit globose or ellipsoid, fleshy, indehiscent, many-seeded. Seeds oblong, compressed, smooth.

Four species distributed in the Mediterranean region, tropical Africa and Asia; one species cultivated in China, also in Hong Kong.

Small trees, armed with spines. Young branches flat and ridged. Leaves alternate, unifoliolate, leathery, margin finely obtuse-dentate, rarely entire, densely pellucid glandular-dotted; petioles often winged. Flowers bisexual, axillary, solitary or in clusters, rarely in cymes. Calyx cupular or urceolate, 3–5-lobed. Petals 4–8, imbricate, often reflexed when full blooming. Stamens 20–60; filaments variously connate, compressed at base; anthers ellipsoidal. Ovary 7–many-locular, ovules 4–8(–many) per locule, in 2 series; styles stout, deciduous; stigma capitate. Fruit a hesperidium, large, ellipsoidal or globose, fleshy; septa membranous. Seeds horizontal or pendulous, seed coat leathery or membranous.

About 20 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, widely cultivated in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 15 species in China; five species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

In addition to the described species, C. aurantiifolia (Christm.) Swingle, C. medica L. var. sarcodactylis (Noot.) Swingle, C. × paradisi Macfad. (Citrus maxima × Citrus sinensis) are occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong.

Large robust perennials with elongate, many-nodose culms, often bearing extra-vaginal shoot at lower nodes. Leaves cauline; blades broadly linear, flat, pseudo-dorsiventral, strongly serrulatescabrous on margins, long sheathing at base. Inflorescence paniculate, consisting of several, terminal and lateral compound anthelas with many elongate anthelas. Spikelets clustered in small heads terminating ultimate anthelalets. Spikelets ovoid, bearing 6–8 glumes on markedly flexuose rhachilla; glumes irregularly spirally disposed, the lower 4–6 empty and smaller than upper 2, both bearing a hermaphrodite flower, only the upper flower producing achene. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 2. Style slender, base not enlarged; stigmas 3. Achene ovoid, subterete or trigonous, the wall thick and corky, stipitate or sessile, smooth.

Four species in tropical and warm-temperate parts of Eurasia, Pacific islands and N & S America; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; roots thalloid, compressed, subcylindrical or ribbon-like, pinnately branched, closely attached to rocks; stems very short, arising laterally from root margins, simple. Leaves on sterile shoots subulate or linear, up to 8 mm; leaves on fertile shoots more or less scale-like, bifid or palmately lobed, with 3 – 9 linear lobes. Flowers shortly stalked, solitary, terminal, zygomorphic, pedicellate, enclosed in spathella before anthesis. Spathella ovoid to globose, apex nipple-shaped. Tepals 2, very small, on both sides of stamen, narrowly triangular to linear, membranous. Stamen 1, simple; filament curved, anther basifixed, 2-locular. Ovary smooth, ovoid, 2-locular; stigmas 2, linear. Capsule smooth, subglobose, opening by 2 valves, the larger one persistent.

Ten species in E and SE Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious, rarely monoecious. Leaves altenate, petiolate, serrate or subentire, pinnately-veined; stipules small, caducous. Flowers in axillary spikes or racemes; perianth calyx-like, without petals. Male flowers: 1– several in axil of bract; calyx 2–4-lobed, lobes valvate; stamens indefinite, mostly 20–30, filaments free, anthers 2-celled, basifixed; anther-cells nearly free, erect, with many small glands between them; rudimentary pistil absent. Female flowers: mostly solitary in axil of bract; calyx-lobes 2 – 4, usually 3, with glands alternating the lobes; ovary 2–3(–4)-locular, with a solitary ovule in each locule; styles short, free or connate at base, Capsules of 2–4 bivalved cocci; seeds subglobose, fleshy.

About 75 species in paleotropical regions; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, unarmed, all parts often with glandular-dots. Branchlets or inflorescence rachis often covered with clustered short hairs. Leaves imparipinnate, leaflets asymmetrical. Inflorescences a panicle, terminal or subterminal. Flower buds globose, rarely ovoid. Flowers bisexual. Calyx 4–5-lobed, connate at base. Petals 4–5, imbricate. Stamens twice as many as petals, in 2 whorls, outer ones opposite to sepals, inner ones opposite to petals. Filaments subulate at apex, geniculate at middle, enlarged at base, rarely filiform. Ovary (1–)4 –5-locular; ovules (1–)2 per locule. Styles short and thick, rarely longer than ovary; stigmas as wide as styles or slightly wider. Fruit a berry, (1–)4-seeded. Seed coat membranous, brown.

About 30 species distributed in Asia, Africa and Australia; ten species in China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious, rarely monoecious. Leaves alternate, usually serrate-dentate, pinnately-veined; stipules small, caducous. Inflorescence spicate or racemose, axillary. Flowers unisexual, without petals and disk with very long, stout at apex pedicels. Male flowers: usually several (rarely solitary) in axil of bract; calyx 3–4-partite, lobes valvate in bud; stamens 35–80; filaments free, anthers dorsifixed, introrse, 4-celled; rudimentary pistil none. Female flowers: solitary or paired in axil of bract; pedicels clavate, thickened after anthesis; calyx 3–5-partite, persistent, lobes imbricate in the bud; staminodes absent; ovary subglobose, longitudinally 4-grooved, 2–3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles elongate, usually connate at base, 2-partite, lobes linear; stigma densely papillose. Capsules of 2–3 bivalved cocci, smooth; seeds subglobose, maculate-striate.

About 25 species in tropical and subtropical regions; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic monopodial herbs. Roots wire-like, branched. Stems slender, terete. Leaves terete, lanceolate, or band-like. Flowers rather small, in an axillary raceme or panicle; sepals subequal, free, spreading, the lateral ones attached to the column foot; petals slightly smaller, spreading; lip 3-lobed, calcarate, attached to the base of the column, spur large, irregular-cylindrical, obtuse, with a callus on the back wall at the entrance and a longitudinal keel on the front wall running down from the base of the midlobe, lateral lobes erect, over the sides of the sac, triangular, acute, midlobe fleshy, straight and triangular, or curved upward and with a callus at its base; column stout, semiterete, with a stout foot; clinandrium truncate, the apex 2-toothed; rostellum concave and U-shaped or subulate; anther terminal, incumbent, the apex truncate or acuminate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy; stipe short, compressed and enlarged to a horse-shoe-shaped base and viscidium, or slender and with a small viscidium; stigma orbicular; ovary obovate-cylindrical. Capsules cylindrical, with persistent column.

About 100 species distributed in tropical Asia and Oceania; 17 species and one varieties in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, petiolate, sparsely pinnately-veined. Inflorescence a thyrse, terminal or axillary; bracts small, caducous. Hypanthium obconic. Calyx-lobes 4–5, connate and forming a calyptra. Petals 4–5, distinct. Stamens many, distinct, in many whorls, anthers 2-celled, cells parallel, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary inferior, 2-locular; ovules several per locule; style linear, shorter than stamens; stigma slightly enlarged. Fruit drupaceous, 1-seeded. Seeds often with a thin pseudotesta; cotyledons thick; embryo straight.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Asia and Australia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous or woody climber. Leaves pinnate, ternate or twice ternate, rarely simple, usually opposite; leaflets entire, dentate, or lobed; petioles sometimes broadened and connate at base. Flowers bisexual, in axillary or terminal panicles or racemes, sometimes solitary. Sepals 4 or 5, valvate in the bud, petaloid and deciduous. Petals none, or small and narrow and passing gradually into the stamens. Stamens numerous, glabrous or pubescent; staminodes sometimes present. Carpels numerous, with a single pendulous ovule in each. Achenes indehiscent, terminating in long feathery persistent style.

About 300 species widely spread throughout the world; 147 species in China; six species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, often with glandular hairs and disagreeably scented. Leaves alternate, digitately compound, with or without stipules; leaflets 3–9, entire or toothed. Flowers in terminal racemes or panicles. Sepals 4, free or connate at the base. Petals 4, alternate with sepals, often with claw. Stamens 6 to many. Ovary usually stipitate, 1-locular, with many ovules; style short or absent. Fruit a capsule, 2-valved, many-seeded.

About 150 species widely dispersed over tropical and subtropical regions; six species and one variety in China; five species (including one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs. Leaves petiolate, dentate. Verticillasters 6 – 10‑flowered, forming terminal racemes; bracts small, ovate, entire, apex cuspidate. Pedicel distinct. Calyx ovoid, hairy and glandular outside, glabrous inside, 2‑lipped, enlarged after anthesis, 10‑veined; upper lip large, orbicular, margin decurrent to the tube; lower lip 4‑toothed, interior 2 teeth longer. Corolla purplish or white, 2‑lipped, hairy outside, not hairy annulate inside; tube narrowly cylindric, much exserted, straight, not oblique at throat; upper lip reflexed, 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger, apex emarginate; lower lip erect, narrow, slightly concave. Stamens 4, declined, much exserted, anterior 2 longer. Style slightly longer than stamens, apex clavate, 2‑cleft. Nutlets ovoid to oblong, wrinkled.

About five species distributed from SE Asia to Australia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, rarely subshrubs or herbs, erect or rarely climbing, deciduous or evergreen. Branchlets usually 4‑angled when young. Leaves simple, opposite or rarely whorled. Inflorescences loosely cymose or capitate, in terminal or rarely axillary paniculate thyrses. Calyx campanulate or cup‑shaped, ca. 5‑dentate or deeply 5‑lobed. Corolla with a slender tube; lobes 5, spreading. Stamens 4, ± exserted. Ovary 4‑locular; ovules pendulous or laterally attached. Style with 2 acute stigmatic lobes. Fruiting calyx ± inflated. Fruit a drupe with four 1‑seeded pyrenes, sometimes separating into two 2‑loculed or four 1‑loculed mericarps.

About 400 species mostly distributed in tropical and subtropical, few in temperate Asia, Africa, and America; 34 species in China; nine species in Hong Kong.

In addition to the described species in this flora, C. macrosiphon Hook. f. (天女散花龍吐珠), C. myricoides (Hochst.) R. Br. ex Volke (楊梅葉大青) and C. speciosissimum Van Geert (爪哇楨桐) were occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves distichous, entire or serrulate; petiolate. Flowers bisexual, axillary, solitary or several clustered; pedicels thickened towards apex; bracteoles 2, small, inserted near apex of pedicel, deciduous; sepals 5, imbricate, slightly connate at base, unequal, outer sepals small, persistent; petals 5, imbricate, connate at base, reflexed at anthesis; stamens about 25, filaments free, glabrous; anthers basifixed, introrse, opening by short slits, apiculate, base cuneate; ovary usually glabrous, 2–3-locular, 5–10 ovules per locule; style 2–3-lobed, persistent. Fruit baccate, ovoid or oblate, many-seeded. Seeds reniform-globose or compressed globose, dark brown and shining, foveolate-pitted.

About ten species in SE Asia and C America; nine species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs with cystoliths. Leaves petiolate, margin entire or serrate. Flowers in terminal, dense cymes. Bracts small, linear or lanceolate; bracteoles small. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed, lobes narrow. Corolla resupinate, tube long, curved, widened upward, limb bilabiate, upper lip forming a prolongation of the corolla‑tube, turned downward, shortly bilobed, innermost in bud, lower lip slightly recurved, much broader than the upper lip, 3‑lobed, middle lobe outermost in bud. Stamens 2, subequal to the upper lip; anther 1‑thecous, base muticous. Staminodes absent. Ovary compressed, 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform, stigma shortly bidentate. Capsule oblong, with a short, solid stalk at base, retinacula present, 4‑seeded.

Two species in tropical Asia; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Leaves petiolate or sessile, dentate or serrate. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming interrupted spikes or panicles; bracteoles setiform, pilose. Calyx tubular, always 13‑veined, straight or slightly curved, ± constricted at middle, ventricose in front at base; throat glabrous or villous; limb 2‑lipped; upper lip 3‑toothed, teeth broad and connate; lower lip longer, 2‑toothed, teeth subulate. Corolla purple‑red, reddish, or white; tube exserted, puberulent abaxially; limb 2‑lipped; upper lip erect, flat; lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger, emarginate or entire. Stamens 4, in 2 pairs, ascending under the upper lip; upper pair always small and imperfect; anther cells 2, divaricate, ± obliquely inserted on dilated connectives. Disk uniform, entire. Ovary glabrous; style unequally 2‑fid. Nutlets ovoid or subglobose, less than 1 mm in diam., glabrous, areolae small, basal.

About 20 species distributed in Asia, Europe; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial twining herbs or subshrubs, rarely trees. Stipules and stipels persistent. Leaves odd-pinnate or 3-foliolate, rarely 1-foliolate; leaflets entire. Flowers in racemes or 1– 2 in axils of leaves, or on old wood. Bracts and bracteoles persistent. Calyx tubular, 5-toothed, teeth triangular or lanceolate, upper 2 subconnate. Corolla exserted from calyx, purplish, blue, white or red; vexillum much larger than petals, erect, emarginate, clawed, not appendaged; wings falcate-oblong, clawed, spreading, adherent in middle to keel; keel shorter than wings, incurved. Stamens diadelphous or monadelphous; anthers alternately dorsifixed and basifixed. Ovary stipitate, many-ovuled; styles elongated, incurved, bearded lengthwise adaxially. Pods stipitate, linear or oblong, compressed, slightly thickened on upper or on both sutures, beaked by persistent style. Seeds subglobose or compressed.

About 60 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions especially America; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial prostrate or climbing herbs, dioecious or rarely monoecious. Roots tuberous. Tendrils usually simple, rarely 2-branched. Leaf blade angled or lobed, sometimes glandular. Male flowers: solitary or arranged in cymes or racemes; calyx-tube short, campanulate or turbinate, lobes 5; corolla campanulate, 5-lobed; stamens 3, inserted at the base of calyx-tube; filaments connate into a column, rarely distinct, anthers connivent or connate, one 1-celled, two 2-celled, cells reflexed, connective not protrudent; pistillodes absent. Female flowers: solitary; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 3, oblong or subulate; ovary ovoid, fusiform, ellipsoid or linear, placentas 3, style filiform, stigma 3-lobed; ovules many, horizontal. Fruit a berry, ovoid or ellipsoid, indehiscent. Seeds many, compressed, ovate, marginate.

About 20 species, mainly distributed in tropical Africa; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Woody vines, rarely half-erect shrubs or small trees. Leaves not peltate, entire or lobed, palmately nerved. Inflorescences cymose or thyrsoid, axillary, elongated, forming panicles or reduced to few flowers. Male flowers: sepals 6 or 9, in 2 or 3 series, the outer ones smaller, the inner ones larger and concave, imbricate; petals 6, smaller than the sepals, cuneate or obovate, often embracing the stamens by auricles at their base; stamens 6 or 9, free, anthers opening by a transverse slit. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; staminodes 6 or absent; carpels 6 or 3; styles cylindrical, stigmas reflexed. Drupes obovate or rotund, laterally compressed, the scar of the style near the base; kernel bony, with a dorsal ridge and lateral ribs.

About eight species in C & N America, Africa, E, SE & S Asia, Malaya, Sumatra, Java, Philippines, Polynesia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs. Leaves 3-foliolate; terminal leaflet large, petiolulate, lateral ones much smaller or obsolete; stipules caducous; stipels scarious. Inflorescences paniculate or racemose, terminal or axillary; bracts ovate, imbricate; bracteole absent. Calyx membranous, broadly campanulate, 5-lobed; upper 2 lobes connate, but distinctly 2-toothed at apex. Corolla much longer than calyx; standard often oblique, suborbicular, ± clawed at base; wings nearly half-deltoid, apex rounded, base auriculate, clawed; keel falcate, longer than wings. Stamens diadelphous. Gynoecia linear, 6–13-ovuled. Pods 5–9-jointed, dehiscing along the undulate dorsal suture, ventral suture straight, lateral surfaces not reticulate veined, with dense minute uncinate and straight hairs. Seeds obliquely transversely elliptic, arillate.

Two species in SE Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or treelets, with clear latex. Leaves alternate, entire, rarely lobed, petiolate, pinnately-veined; stipules small, caducous, sometimes obsolete. Flowers monoecious, rarely dioecious, in axillary racemes. Male flowers: several clustered in axils of bracts; calyx (3–)5(–6)-lobed, lobes imbricate; petals small, 5–6, rarely absent; disk divided into 5–15 free glands; stamens 15–100, without pistillode. Female flowers: solitary in axils of bracts; calyx 5-lobed, petal absent; disk subentire or divided; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 3, unlobed, rarely bifid. Capsules smooth, columella usually persistent; seeds carunculate, cotyledon broad and flattened.

About 15 species distributed from Indonesia and Philippines to New Guinea, tropical Australia, New Caledonia, and Pacific Islands; one species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Small erect herbs with cystoliths. Leaves membranous, margin entire. Inflorescence of loose racemes, or sometimes several forming a terminal panicle, terminal, or terminal and in upper leaf axils; flowers loosely secund in rachis. Bracts and bracteoles minute, subtending pedicels. Calyx 5‑lobed, lobes subequal, short, narrow. Corolla white or purplish white, broadly campanulate, tube short, limb slightly 2‑lipped, upper lip 2‑lobed or subentire, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, included; filaments filiform; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae broadly divergent, parallel at unequal level. Staminodes 2, short. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma capitate. Capsule oblong, with a solid stalk at base, retinacula hooked, 4‑ or few‑seeded. Seeds suborbicular, compressed, smooth, lustrous.

Two species in India, Bhutan, China, Japan and Vietnam; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with milky latex and thick fleshy rootstock. Stems twining or scandent, rarely erect. Leaves alternate, opposite or in clusters. Flowers solitary or in pairs in axils of leaves, or forming few‑flowered cymes terminal on short branches, usually pedicellate. Calyx‑tube adnate to the ovary; limb 5‑lobed.
