Corolla campanulate, attached to the ovary at base; limb 5‑lobed. Stamens 5, attached nearly to the base of corolla‑tube; filaments flattened below middle. Ovary inferior, 3–5‑locular, with numerous ovules on axile placenta; style simple, usually 3‑lobed. Fruit a berry or loculicidal capsule; seeds numerous, sometimes winged.

About 45 species in C, E & S Asia; 44 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms slender, usually ascending from the decumbent base. Leaf blades flat, linear to lanceolate; ligule a line of hairs. Inflorescence a narrow panicle, sometimes contracted and spike-like. Spikelets 2-flowered, florets dissimilar, the lower bisexual, the upper female, separated by a slender rachilla internode; glumes persistent, subequal, shorter than the spikelet, 1–7-veined, broadly obtuse; lemmas both membranous, veinless or obscurely veined, glabrous or pubescent, apex obtuse, the upper a little shorter than the lower; palea similar to lemma. Stamens 2–3. Caryopsis ovate-elliptic.

About 11 species distributed in tropical regions of the Old World; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Epiphytic perennial herbs creeping on the surface of boulders propped and anchored by slender tough roots. Leaves 2, apical to the oblong-ellipsoidal pseudobulb, leathery. Scape between leaves, with several persistent basal scales; flowering bracts deciduous. Flowers medium-sized, opening one at a time, 2 or 3 in a terminal raceme; sepals free, subequal, spreading; petals narrower than or rarely similar to the sepals; lip attached to the base of the column, 3-lobed or undivided, the base concave and slightly saccate, lateral lobes obsolete or erect, partially embracing the column; midlobe expanded and fimbriate or entire and acute, the disk lamellate; column elongate, winged at the apical portion, without foot; clinandrium oblique, membranous, dentate; rostellum membranous, projecting forward and arching over the stigma; anther attached under the margin of the clinandrium, incumbent; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, obovoid, connected at the apex by a granular thin sheet; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical. Capsules ellipsoidal, ridged, rostrate.

About 200 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Oceania; 26 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms usually erect. Leaf blades large, usually broad, flat; ligule short, membranous. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, often many, each subtended by a globose or elongate ivory-like cupule (a modified leaf-sheath within which is a membranous prophyll) and comprising 2 racemes; female raceme enclosed by the cupule and consisting of 1 sessile spikelet accompanied by 2 barren pedicels; male raceme exserted from the mouth of the cupule, short, the spikelets imbricate and borne in pairs or threes, one pedicellate, the other(s) sessile. Female spikelet with glumes orbicular, membranous with a cartilaginous beak, the upper keeled; lower floret represented by an orbicular membranous lemma; upper floret with membranous lemma and palea, stigmas 2, exserted from the cupule. Male spikelet lanceolate to elliptic-oblong; lower glume flat on the back, 2-keeled, the keels winged above; upper glume boatshaped; florets 2, lemma and palea membranous. Caryopsis subglobose to ellipsoidal.

Four species distributed in tropical Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Verticillasters 6–many‑flowered, forming axillary racemes or terminal panicles; bracts early deciduous or absent. Calyx subcampanulate, 5‑toothed, 2‑lipped, accrescent and often declined in fruiting time. Corolla tube exserted long or short, straight or recurved; limb 2‑lipped; upper lip (3‑ or) 4‑lobed, strongly reflexed; lower lip entire, navicular, narrowed at base. Stamens 4, declined, included within lower lip; filaments connate or free, rarely adnate to corolla tube; anther cells apex confluent. Style apex equally 2‑cleft. Nutlets ovoid to globose, smooth, tuberculate or not.

About 90–150 species in tropics of the Old World and in Australia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with underground rhizome or short caudex, sometimes stoloniferous. Leaves basal, simple; petiole long, sheathing at base; blade asymmetrically peltate, base usually cordate; lateral veins many. Inflorescences at or near apex of leafy plant, several together: peduncle erect, shorter than leaves; spathe tube green, ovoid or ellipsoidal, 1/2–1/5 the length of the limb, convolute, persistent; limb orange, oblong or narrowly lanceolate, falling off after anthesis; spadix slender, shorter than spathe, female portion at the base, male portin at apex, with a sterile portion between the female and male portion. Appendage cylindrical, subulate, or none. Flowers unisexual, without perianth; female flower of a single 1-locular ovary, with many ovules; male flower of 2–6 sessile stamens; anthers opening by longitudinal slits. Fruits a berry, green to white or red, many-seeded.

About 13 species in tropical and subtropical Asia; eight species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody vines, rarely scandent shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite, alternate or subverticillate, petiolate, usually with scales, sometimes with a small cavity or a tuft of hairs. Inflorescence paniculate, spicate or racemose, terminal or axillary, densely covered with scales or pubescent. Flowers large, bisexual or polygamous, 4- or 5-merous; bracteoles small, caducous. Calyx-tube tubular, campanulate or infundibuliform, lobes 4 – 5. Petals 4 – 5. Stamens often twice as many as calyx-lobes, in 2 whorls. Disk adnate to calyx-tube, with a ring of hairs. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; ovules 2 – 6. Fruit drupaceous, 4 – 5-winged or -ribbed, indehiscent, 1-seeded.

About 250 species widely distributed in tropical Africa, tropical Asia and America; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, without rhizomes; stems decumbent or erect. Leaves alternate, sheathing at base. Flowers few, irregular, borne on 2 peduncles and enclosed in a folded involucral bracts; involucral bracts spathe-like, usually pedunculate from a split leaf sheath opposite to the blade. Sepals 3, membranous, inner 2 often connate at base. Petals free, blue, spatulate or orbicular, inner (anterior) 2 larger and clawed, the third differently shaped or more sessile than the 2 others. Fertile stamens 3, on 1 side, 1 larger than the others; filaments glabrous; staminodes 3, with deformed anthers. Ovary 2–3-locular, posterior locule with 1 developed or abortive ovule or empty, anterior 2 locules each with 1–2 ovules. Capsule oblong, globose, or ellipsoidal, 3-valved or most frequently 2-valved. Seeds cylindrical or ellipsoidal, reticulate or sub-smooth.

About 170 species mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; eight species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs, rarely shrubs. Leaves alternate, margin entire, dentate or pinnately lobed. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, in form of racemes, corymbs or panicles, rarely solitary. Involucre hemispherical, campanulate to urceolate; phyllaries 2–4‑seriate, ± imbricate, then widely spreading, herbaceous, with scarious margin. Receptacle convex, alveolate or fimbriate, marginal areoles usually smaller in size. Marginal florets female, numerous, corolla filiform, shorter than style and pappus, without ligules or with minute ligules only. Disk florets hermaphrodite or functionally staminate, usually few, tubular, corolla 5‑lobed at the apex; anther bases obtuse and entire; stylar branches of tubular floret puberulent, papillose, with short lanceolate apical appendages. Cypsela compressed, obovate‑oblong, ribbed along the side, mostly pubescent. Pappus hair fine, 1 series or in rarely 2 series with the outer ones very short.

About 80 –100 species distributed mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; ten species and one variety in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Trailing or scandent shrubs. Leaves opposite. Stipules small, interpetiolar, deciduous. Flowers axillary, solitary. Calyx‑tube globular or turbinate; limb 4–5‑lobed, lobes short, persistent. Corolla salverform; tube slender; lobes (4–)5, spreading, imbricate in the bud. Stamens 4–5, attached to the throat; filaments short; anthers linear, basifixed, included in the tube. Ovary 2‑locular, with several ovules in each locule; style entire, club‑shaped at the top, exserted. Fruit a capsule, opening loculicidally in 2 valves. Seeds bordered by a fringed membranous wing.

About 13 species in S and SE Asia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Stipules 2, filiform. Leaves papery, basally 3-veined, usually with linear appendages on both sides at base, margin serrate, petiolate. Flowers bisexual, yellow, solitary or several in cymes. Cymes axillary or extra axillary. Sepals usually 5, rarely 4. Petals as many as sepals. Stamens 10 or more, inserted on androgynophore, distinct. Ovary 2–5-locular, ovules many per locule; style short; stigma peltate or disk-shaped, entire or lobed. Capsule cylindrical or globose, angled or horned, loculicidally dehiscing into 2–5 valves. Seeds many.

About 40 species, mainly distributed in tropical regions of the world; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, usually evidently petiolate, margin entire or serrate, rarely lobed. Cymes mostly corymbose, ebracteate. Flowers bisexual, often heterostylic or ± functionally unisexual. Calyx tubular or campanulate, enlarged after anthesis, persistent. Corolla white, yellow, or orange‑red, campanulate to funnelform, usually (4–)5(–8)‑lobed; lobes antrorse or recurved. Stamens usually well developed; filaments often pubescent at base. Ovary 4‑locular, glabrous; ovule 1 per locule. Style twice 2‑cleft, each branch with a spatulate or capitate stigma. Drupes ovoid, globose, or ellipsoidal, often with watery or sticky fleshy mesocarp and bony endocarp, rarely with corky mesocarp or nut‑like without fleshy mesocarp. Seeds 1–4, endosperm lacking; cotyledons plicate.

About 325 species mostly distributed in tropics of N & S America, poorly represented in Africa and Asia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Arborescent or shrubby plants. Stems simple or few-branched, ± woody, with conspicuous circular leaf scars distally. Leaves crowded at apex of stems, often petiolate; leaf blade elliptic-lanceolate to sword-shaped, parallel veined, midvein conspicuous. Panicles arising from axils of distal leaves, large, many-branched. Flowers bisexual, solitary, usually tubular-campanulate or subcylindrical; pedicel usually short or subsessile. Perianth tube short; lobes 6, in 2 whorls of 3, subequal or the outer ones slightly shorter. Stamens 6, inserted in tube or throat of perianth; anthers versatile. Ovary superior, sessile, 3-locular; ovules 2–many per locule. Style slender; stigma capitate, small. Fruit a capsule, leathery, 1–several-seeded. Seeds black, coated with phytomelanin.

About 20 species distributed in S and SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands, S America; one species (introduced) in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, strongly aromatic, glabrous throughout; taproot slender; stem erect, branched above. Leaves petiolate; blade pinnately dissected; ultimate segments very variable in shape. Inflorescence of compound umbels, terminal or opposite to the leaves; bracts absent, rarely 1; rays several, spreading, unequal; bracteoles several, linear. Calyx-teeth short, acute, often unequal. Petals white or rose-pink, obovate, apex deeply notched, outer petals enlarged (radiant). Stylopodium conic; styles slender, erect. Fruit globose, not readily separating at maturity; pericarp hard; primary and secondary ribs filiform, evident; vittae absent or solitary, obscure in mature fruits. Seed face concave. Carpophore deeply bifid at apex.

One species native to Mediterranean region; cultivated in China, it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Annual to perennial herbs. Stems prostrate or ascending or suberect, glabrous or simply hairy. Leaves simple, basal ones 1–3- pinnatisect, rarely serrate; cauline ones serrate or entire, petiolate or subsessile. Racemes axillary, many flowered. Flowers minute. Sepals 4, ovate or elliptic. Petals 4, white or violet, obovate or spathulate, claw usually absent. Stamens 6, tetradynamous, sometimes reduced to 4 or 2; nectar with 2, 4 or 6 glands. Ovary 2-ovuled. Silicles indehiscent, didymous, reniform or cordate. Seeds 1 per locule, ovoid or oblong, cotyledons incumbent.

Ten species distributed in SW Europe, S America; two species (introduced) in China; one species naturalized in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect, procumbent or climbing, sometimes tuberous. Leaves basal or cauline, ternately bipinnate or palmately divided. Racemes terminal or leaf-opposed. Bracts present. Sepals 2 or absent, scale-like, caducous. Petals 4, 2 whorls, one of the out whorl shortly spurred or shallowly pouched at base, another flat, inner 2 narrower, adherent at tip, dorsal keel-like or winged. Stamens 6, connate into 2 bundles. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with 2 parietal placentas; ovules many. Caspules linear, ellipsoid or ovoid, with persistent style and stigmas at apex, dehiscing into 2 valves, rarely indehiscent; arils sometimes cristate.

About 320 species distributed in N temperate and S Africa, mainly in Asia; 200 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or semievergreen shrubs or small trees; branches usually stellately pubescent; buds perulate. Leaves alternate, petiolate; stipules large, membranous, caducous; leaf blade usually oblique at base, margin serrate, pinnately veined. Inflorescence a raceme, pendulous. Flowers bisexual, usually open before leaves appear; each flower usually with 1 bract and 2 bracteoles. Sepals 5, persistent or deciduous. Petals 5, yellow, orbicular or ovate, rarely oblanceolate. Stamens 5; anther 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent; 5–10 nectar producing disc scales present, alternating with stamens, apex truncate or 2-lobed. Ovary semi-inferior, rarely superior, 2-locular; ovules 3 per locule, 2 of them sterile; styles 2. Capsules woody, dehiscing loculicidally by 4 valves, with persistent styles. Seeds ellipsoid; endosperm fleshy; embryo straight.

About 29 species distributed in E & SE Asia; 20 species in China and one species in Hong Kong.

records.authority: K. D. Hill & L. A. S. Johnson

records.text:
Rhizomes horizontal. Stems sometimes branched, usually spirally twisted, leafy, rarely plants stemless. Leaf blade oblong to lanceolate. Inflorescences terminal or lateral on separate, short, leafless shoots arising from rhizomes, conical, densely many-flowered. Bracts imbricate, 1–2-flowered. Calyx 3-lobed or -toothed at apex. Corolla tube equalling or longer than calyx. Labellum obovate, large, margin incurved. Stamens petaloid; anther cells linear. Ovary 3-locular; ovules many per locule, superposed. Style filiform; stigma funnelform. Stylodes absent. Capsules subglobose or ovoid, woody. Seeds many, black; aril lacerate.

About 90 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; five species (two endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Small annual or perennial herbs, often creeping; stem branched mostly at base. Leaves alternate, or sometimes opposite or rosulate, pinnatifid to pinnatisect. Capitula small, heterogamous and disciform, pedunculate, solitary, axillary, or opposite to leaves. Involucres dish‑like, hemispherical or campanulate; phyllaries in 2–3 series, oblong, herbaceous green with margin scarious. Receptacle flat or convex, naked. Marginal florets female and fertile, 1– many‑seriate, corolla absent with the pistils only. Central florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, yellow, 4– 5‑lobed apically; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages lanceolate; stylar branches obtuse to truncate, or sometimes unbranched. Cypselae oblong or obovate, dorsiventrally compressed, glandular, margin with thicken wings which extended to the apex, base stipitate, especially for the marginal cypselae. Pappus absent.

About 75 species mainly distributed in S hemisphere; two species in China; one species as weed in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, erect or climbing. Leaves alternate, toothed to lyrately pinnatifid. Capitula homogamous and discoid, nodding in flowering stage, solitary or in corymbose arrangement at terminal. Involucres cylindric with base swollen, calyculate; phyllaries uniseriate, linear‑lanceolate, coherent and united into a cylindric tube at anthesis, later splitted and reflexed, herbaceous with margin scarious. Receptacle flat, alveolate with margin of areoles scarious. All florets tubular, corolla tube narrow, gradually and slightly widened at summit, apex 5‑lobed, hermaphrodite and fertile; anther bases entire or shortly auriculate; stylar branches long, linear, papillose hairy. Cypselae cylindric, 8–10‑ribbed, puberulent. Pappus bristles copious, capillary and silky, white in colour, easily shed off.

About 21 species native to tropical Africa, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, evergreen or deciduous. Leaves digitately ternate, alternate; stipules small, caducous. Flowers bisexual or functionally unisexual, in terminal or axillary racemes or corymbs, with caducous bracts. Sepals 4, subequal, much smaller than petals, fused with the raised and lobed disc at the base. Petals 4, clawed. Stamens (8–)12–50, united with gynophore at the base. Gynophore 2– 8 cm, or reduced in male flowers. Ovary 1-locular, with 2 parietal placentae and many ovules; style absent. Fruit a fleshy many-seeded berry.

About 13 species in tropical and subtropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees. Leaves opposite, rarely subopposite, entire, sessile or petiolate. Cymes terminal or axillary, or flowers solitary. Sepals 5, leathery, persistent. Petals 5, red or white, with linear or spotted glands, with or without scales at base. Stamens many, united into 3 – 5 bundles; filaments slender, with fleshy glands alternate to staminal bundles. Ovary 3-locular; styles 3, free, slender, stigma small, ovules 4–many in each locule. Capsules loculicidal. Seeds 4–many, winged on one side.

Six species distributed in SE Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees and shrubs. Leaves simple or digitately compound, alternate or in clusters. Flowers solitary, or in clusters of 2 – 3 on stems. Calyx 2‑ or 5‑divided, often bilabiate. Corolla tubular or campanulate, yellowish brown, with purplish red venations (especially on lobes and adaxial surface of tube), limb 5‑lobed, lobes triangular, apex acuminate. Fertile stamens 4, didynamous, nearly exserted, anthers glabrous, thecae divergent. Disk cupular. Ovary oviod‑ellipsoidal; ovules many in several rows on 4 lateral placentations. Berries subglobose; exocarp dry. Seeds many, not winged.

Six species distributed in tropical America; two species introduced into China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial bulbous herbs. Leaves basal, often large, linear or ensiform. Scape solid. Inflorescences umbellate; involucres 2, large and broad, herbaceous. Flowers sessile or pedicellate. Perianth actinomorphic or slightly zygomorphic, salverform or subsalverform; tube slender, cylindrical; segments 6, lanceolate or linear, spreading or recurved, white or tinged with purple. Stamens inserted at the summit of perianth tube; filament free, filiform; anthers linear, versatile. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule. Style filiform, with an entire or 3-lobed stigma. Fruit a capsule, subglobose, bursting irregularly. Seeds few, nearly globular, often converted into fleshy bulbs.

About 120 species in tropical and subtropical regions of both hemispheres, mainly in Africa; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs, stem branches densely pubescent to tomentose. Leaves alternate, fleshy, narrowly spatulate or oblanceolate, entire or 2–5‑lobed, densely lanate abaxially. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, arranged in leafy racemes or raceme‑panicles. Involucres hemishperical; phyllaries in 3 series, herbaceous, densely tomentose, median and inner layers broadly scarious‑margined. Receptacle hemispherical to conical, alveolate, toothed along margin of areoles. Marginal florets pistillate and fertile, 1‑seriate, corolla tubular, 2–3‑toothed, glandular‑punctate. Disk florets hermaphrodite and fertile, many, corolla tubular, apex 5‑lobed, glandular punctate; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages obtuse oblong; stylar branches truncate at distal ends. Cypselae oblong‑cuneate, 5‑ribbed. Pappus of short coronate and lacerate scales.

A monotypic genus native to China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Stems and branches terete or tetragonal. Stipules small or absent. Leaves simple, pinnately or digitately 3-foliolate. Racemes terminal, axillary, leaf-opposed, or in head-like clusters on apex of branches. Calyx 2-lipped or campanulate. Corolla yellow or deep blue; vexillum orbicular or oblong, often with 2 callosities at the base; wings oblong or obovate, shorter than vexillum; keel incurved and beaked. Stamens all united in a sheath, open on the upper side; anthers dimorphic, alternatively oblong, basifixed and ovoid, dorsifixed. Ovary usually sessile, 2–many-ovuled; styles long, base incurved; stigma small, oblique. Pods oblong, terete or ovoid-globular, rarely tetragonal, turgid. Seeds few to many, estrophiolate.

About 550 species distributed in tropical & subtropical regions; 40 species and three varieties in China; ten species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, rarely subshrubs. Leaves alternate, entire or divided, pinnately-veined or basiveined. Stipules small, linear or subulate, caducous. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or spicate, rarely paniculate, usually androgynous. Male flowers: calyx-lobes mostly 5, imbricate to valvate in the bud; petals 5, convolute in the bud; disk glands usually 5, alternating with the petals; stamens 10–20, free; anthers-celled, adnate; pistillode absent. Female flowers: calyx-lobes 5, persistent; petals rudimentary or none; disk annular or dissected; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 3, 2-cleft or branched. Capsules of 3 bivalved cocci; seeds smooth, carunculate, the testa crustaceous.

About 800 species distributed in the tropics and subtropics of the world; 25 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Stemless or caulescent. Leaves rosulate or evenly polystichous along the stem; blades narrowly triangular, sessile or slightly contracted to subpetiolate at base, spinose-serrate. Inflorescence capitate, sessile, nested in the centre of the rosette or at the apex of the stem, compound. Flowers polygamous in some species at least. Sepals much connate. Petals connate by their claws, naked or with two callosities. Stamens exserted from the throat of the corolla, usually highly adnate to the petal. Ovules usually few, obtuse; placentae apical or median; epigynous tube none or very shallow. Fruits small, rather dry. Seeds small, flat.

About 41 species, xerophytic, saxicolous, or terrestrial, NE Brazil; one species and one variety cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, or shrubs. Leaves alternate, rarely subopposite, usually pinninerved, rarely triplinerved, exstipulate. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary or subterminal. Flowers bisexual. Perianth-tubes turbinate or ovoid, persistent, constricted at the top; lobes 6, subequal, deciduous. Fertile stamens usually 9 in 3 whorls, the 3 innermost ones with 2 glands at the base; anthers 2-celled, introrse, those of the 3 innermost stamens extrorse. Staminodes present, shortly stipitate, eglandular. Ovary enclosed within the perianth-tube. Fruits drupaceous, wholly enclosed in the fleshy or hardened perianth-tubes, smooth or with many longitudinal ridges and grooves.

About 200 –250 species in tropical and subtropical regions, with the distribution centre in Malesia; 19 species in China and three species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or woody lianas, latex white. Leaves opposite, abaxially glaucous. Cymes terminal, apparently axillary ro extra‑axillary, pedunculate. Flower buds cylindric, apex caudate‑acuminate. Calyx with 5 – 10 basal glands. Corolla salverform; tube short‑cylindric or bell‑shaped; lobes 5, linear or ovate, overlapping to right, inserted near middle of corolla‑tube, free from filaments. Filaments broad below, narrow above; anthers connate, adnate to stigma head; pollen tetrads in masses, solitary in each anther cell, pollen carrier spathulate, erect. Stigma head broadly conical. Follicles widely divaricate, narrowly lanceolate in outline; coma white.

About 12 species in SE Asia and tropical Africa; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs, glabrous. Roots thick, spreading, hairy. Rootstocks very short, erect. Leaves 2, petiolate; petioles not sheathing; leaf blade elliptic, chartaceous. Scape simple, with imbricate cataphylls at the base. Flowers non-resupinate; sepals subequal, spreading, involute and acuminate; petals shorter than the sepals; lip erect, undivided, ovate, acute, strongly concave at the base and surrounding the column, velvety-hairy, spotted; column very short, glandularly auriculate; anther erect, acute; pollinia 4, powdery; viscidium large, in direct contact with the stigma, without evident rostellum; stigma discoid, prominent, fleshy, occupying the entire front of the column; ovary cylindrical. Capsules oblong, erect, erostrate.

About 20 species mainly distributed in Oceania and tropical Asia; one species and two varieties in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbaceous vines, monoecious or rarely dioecious. Stems and branches hispid and scabrous. Tendrils not branched. Leaves angled or palmately 3 –7-lobed. Flowers yellow, small. Male flowers: clustered or solitary; calyx-tube campanulate or turbinate, 5-lobed, lobes subulate; corolla rotate or campanulate, 5-lobed; stamens 3, distinct, inserted on the calyx-tube, anthers ellipsoid, one 1-celled, two 2-celled, cells linear, reflexed or curved, connective protrudent, often bifid; pistillodes glandular. Female flower: solitary or rarely clustered; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 3, subulate; ovary globose, ovoid or cylindrical, placentas 3 –5, style short, stigmas 3–5; ovules many, horizontal. Fruits polymorphic, fleshy, indehiscent, smooth or spiny. Seeds many, compressed, ovate or oblong, usually without thickened margin.

About 30 species, distributed in tropical to temperate regions of the world, most species in Africa; three species and three varieties in China; two species and one variety cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial scandent or creeping herbs, monoecious. Stems and branches stout, hispid. tendrils 2– many-branched. Leaves simple, often lobed. Flowers solitary, yellow. Male flowers: calyx-tube campanulate, lobes 5, lanceolate or foliaceous at apex; corolla campanulate, 5-lobed; stamens 3, inserted at base of calyx, filaments distinct, anthers connate, one 1-celled, two 2-celled, cells linear, twisted, connective not protrudent; pistillodes absent. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 3, short, triangular; ovary ellipsoid or globose, placentas 3 –5; style short and thick; stigmas 3, bifid; ovules many, horizontal. Fruit large, fleshy, indehiscent. Seeds many, compressed, smooth, marginate.

About 15 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; three species cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, monoecious; branches verticillate or irregularly so; winter buds ovoid. Leaves spirally arranged, usually in 2-serials because of base twisted on lateral branches, sessile, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, base attenuate, margin serrulate, stomatal bands present on both surfaces but fewer adaxially. Pollen cones terminal, clustered; microsporophylls many, spirally arranged, sessile, scalelike, distal margin serrulate; pollen sacs 3, pendulous. Seed cones 1–3 together, terminal, globose or ellipsoid; bracts and cone scales spirally arranged, sessile, connate at lower part; bracts persistent, broadly ovate or triangular-ovate, flat, large, margin irregularly and finely serrulate, apex long acuminate, hard; ovules 3 per bract axil, sessile; cone scales of mature cones sessile on and fused to proximal middle part of abaxial side of bract, minute, distal part free, 3-lobed, lobes irregularly serrulate at apex. Seeds 3, flat, with 2 narrow, lateral wings. Cotyledons 2.

One species in Cambodia, China, Laos, N Vietnam.

Herbs or shrubs, with mucilaginous and glandular hairs. Leaves opposite or whorled, rarely alternate. Flowers bilateral, solitary or in racemes, borne between petioles, rarely axillary or extra-axillary; bracteoles 2. Calyx-tube angulate, apex 6-lobed and with same appendages, base spurred. Petals 6, unequal, rarely 2 or absent. Stamens 11, rarely 9, 6 or 4, 2 of them shorter than others. Ovary superior, sessile, unequally 2-locular; ovules 3–many in each locule; styles filiform; stigma capitate. Capsules oblong, involved in calyx, laterally dehiscent.

About 300 species native to America and Hawaii Islands; eight species introduced in China; three species cultivated in Hong Kong. Cuphea petiolate (L.) Koehne and C. platycentra Lemarie, both native to America, were once cultivated.

Perennial herbs, usually with terete or tuberous rhizomes. Leaves mostly radical, sessile or petiolate, tufted; leaf blade usually lanceolate, plicate, parallel-veined. Scape emerging from leaf-axils, long or short, erect or apically bent downward. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, in terminal raceme, spike, or head. Perianth often yellow; segments 6, spreading, subequal, sometimes basally connate into a tube. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth segments; anther nearly basifixed or dorsifixed; filament very short, sometimes subequalling anther. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, usually hairy, with 2–many ovules in each locule; style columnar, slender; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit a berry.

About 20 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Rhizomes branched, fleshy, aromatic, often with tuber-bearing roots. Leaves basal; leaf blade broadly lanceolate or oblong, rarely narrowly linear. Inflorescence a terminal spike on pseudostems or on separate shoots arising from rhizomes, sometimes appearing before leaves; peduncle erect. Bracts connate for ca. 1/2 their length and forming pouches, spreading at free ends, each subtending a cincinnus of 2–7 flowers, apical bracts often differently coloured, large, sterile, forming a coma; bracteoles free to base. Calyx usually shortly tubular, split on 1 side, apex 2–3-lobed or -toothed. Corolla funnelform; lobes ovate or oblong, subequal or central lobe longer, apex mucronate. Lateral staminodes petaloid, basally adnate to filament and labellum. Labellum with a thickened, central portion and thinner, lateral lobes overlapping with lateral staminodes. Filament short, broad; anther versatile, base usually spurred; connective appendage absent. Ovary 3-locular. Capsule ellipsoidal, 3-valved, dehiscent.

About 50 species distributed in SE Asia, one species in Australia; 12 species (one introduced) in China; two species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Annual or perennial herbs, creeping or ascending, without rhizomes. Leaves alternate. Flowers regular, in short dense spike-like cincinnus or clusters, either sessile, within the leaf sheath, or pedunculate and surrounded by imbricate falcate bracts. Sepals free or connate only at base. Petals connate and tubular in middle, free at both ends, purple, blue, or white, linear-lanceolate. Stamens 6, all fertile, equal; filaments lanate, rarely glabrous; anther-cells longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary 3-locular, 2 ovules in each locule. Capsule 3-valved. Seeds 1–2 per valve, cylindrical or quadrangular, reticulate or pitted.

About 50 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Africa and Asia to N Australia; five species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Leaves opposite, without stipules. Flowers in clusters, forming terminal racemes or heads; the flower-cluster consisting of 1–3 perfect flowers and on each side a cluster of stiff hooked bristles. Perianth-segments 5, scarious, pilose. Stamens 5; filaments united at the base into a cup, with as many small staminodes between the filaments; anthers 2-celled. Ovary 1-locular; style simple, with a capitate stigma. Utricles indehiscent, 1-seeded.

About 20 species widely distributed in tropical regions of the world; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as the family.

Herbaceous or woody vines. Leaves mostly peltate, palmately nerved. Flowers in axillary panicles. Male flowers: sepals usually 4 or 5, usually united into a campanulate or inflated and globose calyx, rarely free; petals 4 or 5, small, connate or free; stamens united in a central column, anthers horizontal, opening transversely. Female flowers: sepals and petals 1 or 2, opposite to each other, rarely absent; carpel solitary, style short, stigma divided into 3 to many radiating subulate branches. Drupes obovate or subglobose, slightly compressed, the scar of style near the base; the kernel bony, with 2 or 3 rows of tubercles on each side.

About 30 species in S & SE Asia; 12 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Tree, rarely shrubby. Branchlets with terminal buds covered with many imbricate scales. Stipules extrapetiolar. Leaves spirally arranged, entire or dentate. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious). Male flowers in slender pendulous catkins; perianth (4–)6(–7)-lobed; stamens (4–)6(–12), filaments very short; rudimentary pistil very small. Female flowers 1 per cupule, solitary or in 2- to many-flowered spikes; ovary 3-celled; styles 3, stigmas capitate or dilated; staminodes sometimes present. Cupule discoid, cup-shaped or subglobose; bracts scale-like, forming entire concentric rings. Nut usually 1 per cupule, subglobose to ellipsoid or cylindrical, partially enclosed in a cupule.

About 150 species mainly in the temperate regions of N hemisphere, but with some species extended to the tropics at high altitudes; 69 species in China; ten species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, stems ascending or erect, much branched, glabrous. Leaves basal and cauline; petioles sheathing; leaf blade blades 3–4-pinnatisect; cauline leaves usually numerous, reduced upward. Inflorescence of lax terminal or leaf-opposed compound umbels; peduncles usually short or abortive; involucre and involucel lacking; rays rather few, spreading-ascending; umbellules few-flowered, the flowers pedicellate. Caylx-teeth obsolete. Petals white, greenish or pinkish, ovate, acute, apex not narrowed and inflexed, subequal. Stylopodium low conical; styles short to almost obsolete. Fruit ovoid to globose, rounded at both ends or slightly narrowed toward apex, slightly compressed laterally, somewhat constricted at commissure, glabrous, the mericarps subterete in transaction, glabrous, the ribs prominent, somewhat corky; vittae 1 in each furrow, 2 on commissure. Carpophore shortly bifid at apex.

About three species in tropical and temperate America; one species widely naturalized in tropical and temperate region including China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial caespitose herbs, terrestrial or epiphytic. Roots wirelike. Rhizomes short and thick, covered by cataphylls and enlarged into conical pseudobulbs. Leaves 3–5, persistent, petiolate, linear or lanceolate. Scape emerging from the axil of a cataphyll or rarely of a leaf, with imbricate basal scales and cauline sheaths. Flowers moderately large, in a loose raceme; sepals equal, free, spreading; petals similar to or slightly smaller than the sepals, spreading or proximate and over the column; lip attached to the base of the column, 3-lobed, the base fleshy, concave, lateral lobes erect, partially covering the column, midlobe strongly recurved, disk 2-keeled and deeply canaliculate, rarely tubercular; column long, curved, without foot; clinandrium oblique-truncate; anther terminal, incumbent, convex or subglobose; pollinia 2, folded, waxy, in several species separated into 4 readily, on a broad stipe widened to a viscid base; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical, striatesulcate. Capsules fusiform or oblong-ellipsoidal, strongly rostrate.

About 48 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and extends southwards to Papua New Guinea and Australia; 29 species in China; five species in Hong Kong. For it is a very favourite genus for Chinese orchidophiles, many cultivars were cultivated in private gardens of Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual herbs, usually aromatic. Culms erect. Leaf blades filiform to broadly linear; ligule dry membranous, scarious. Inflorescence a dense spathate compound panicle, each ultimate spatheole subtending a pair of short racemes on a short peduncle; spatheoles boat-shaped; lower raceme with one basal pair of homogamous spikelets below the fertile pairs; rachis internodes and pedicels linear, margins white-ciliate. Sessile spikelet dorsally compressed, bisexual or pistillate; callus obtuse, shortly bearded, inserted into internode apex; lower glume papery, flat or concave, sometimes grooved or wrinkled, 2-keeled; keels lateral, with or without wing above middle, with intercarinal veins or not; upper glume boat-shaped, awned or awnless; lower floret reduced to a hyaline lemma; upper lemma narrowly oblong, halfway divided into 2 narrow lobes, with a geniculate awn from sinus, or entire and muticous; lodicules 2, cuneate; stamens 3; styles 2, plumose. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or sterile or absent, narrowly lanceolate, awnless.

About 70 species distributed in tropics and subtropics of Africa, Asia, and Australia, introduced in tropical America; 24 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs or perennial herbs, twining or rarely erect, often rhizomatous. Roots fibrous, woody or fleshy. Leaves opposite, rarely whorled, often petiolate, sometimes with small stipule‑like leaves in axils. Inflorescences extra‑axillary or occasionally terminal, rarely axillary, umbel‑like, corymbose, or raceme‑like. Sepals 5, erect, often with basal glands. Corona rotate or subrotate; tube short; lobes 5, patent or reflexed, overlapping to right or left, rarely subvalvate. Corona inserted at base of gynostegium, membranous or fleshy, cupular, cylindric, or deeply 5‑divided, sometimes with adaxial appendages. Filaments connate into tube; anthers with membranous apical appendage; pollinia 2 per pollinarium, pendulous. Stigma head convex or shortly conical. Follicles fusiform or lanceolate, usually smooth, rarely narrowly winged or setose; coma white.

About 200 species distributed in tropical, subtropical and temperate Eurasia, Africa and America; 57 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, rhizomatous or stoloniferous. Culms usually slender, with alternately long and short internodes. Leaf blades linear or lanceolate, flat; ligule membranous, short, truncate, or only a fringe of hairs; leaf sheath bearded at mouth. Inflorescence 2 – several, slender, digitately arranged spikes. Spikelets sessile, imbricate, biseriate; rachis flat or semiterete. Spikelets sessile, strongly laterally compressed, usually 1-flowered, awnless, imbricate in 2 rows along one side of rachis, disarticulating above glumes; rachilla articulate below lemma, protruding or not, sometimes with a rudimentary floret; glumes subequal, shorter or as long as floret, narrow, herbaceous, 1-veined or upper glume 3-veined, apex acuminate, both or only lower glume persistent; lemma keeled, boat-shaped, cartilaginous, 3-veined, usually pubescent on keel, apex entire, awnless; callus glabrous; lodicules 2, minute. Stamens 3. Ovary glabrous; styles 2, free, stigmas plumose, protruding sideways. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, terete or laterally compressed, pericarp easily separating when soaked, hilum linear.

About ten species distributed in tropical, subtropical and warm-temperate regions; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials, rhizomatous or stoloniferous. Glumes terete to trigonous. Leaves basal, 3-ranked, rarely without blade; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaf-like. Inflorescence terminal, usually simple to decompound, umbel-like with ultimate branches (branches) terminating in 1 or more spikes on finger-like cluster of spikelets, more rarely spikes or spikelet clusters sessile or inflorescence capitate. Spikelets linear to oblong or elliptic, laterally flattened to subterete; axis straight or zigzag, deciduous or persistent. Glumes 2-ranked, deciduous or persistent, sides membranous to papery or leathery, veins none to several, keel acute to rounded. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 1–3. Stigmas (1–)3; style continuous with ovary. Achenes usually trigonous, sometimes triquetrous or dorsiventrally compressed.

About 500 species, cosmopolitan; 36 species in China; 23 species, one variety and one subspecies in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms prostrate and rooting at the lower nodes, upper part erect. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate to lanceolate; ligule membranous. Inflorescence an open or contracted panicle; pedicel usually slender, subequal. Spikelets laterally compressed, deciduous at maturity, florets 2, lower floret sterile, upper floret bisexual; glumes unequal, membranous to herbaceous, 3–5-veined, obtuse or acute; lower glume ovate, smaller; upper glume boat-shaped; lower lemma usually equal to spikelet, 5-veined, obtuse or acute, palea small or absent; upper lemma subleathery to crustaceous, dorsally convex, smooth or minutely pitted, a little greenish crest near the apex, upper palea dorsally slightly convex.

About 11 species distributed in tropical regions of the Old World; two species and one variety in China; one species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect or decumbent, ± compressed, glabrous. Leaf blades linear, flat or loosely folded; ligule membranous, truncate, often ciliolate. Inflorescence digitate, composed of several linear to narrowly oblong secund spikes, spikelets sessile, biseriate, closely imbricate, the uppermost spikelets abortive, terminating in a pointed extension of the flattened rachis. Spikelets elliptic to ovate, laterally compressed, florets several, disarticulating above glumes but not usually between florets; glumes keeled, 1-veined; lower glume smaller, sharply acute; upper glume with a stout oblique awn from just below the broadly rounded emarginate tip; lemmas longer than glumes, membranous, 3-veined, glabrous, strongly keeled, acute to shortly awned and often recurved at the apex; palea subequalling the lemma, the keels sometimes winged; lodicules 2, very small, cuneate. Stamens 3; anthers sometimes small. Ovary glabrous; styles 2, free, rather long, stigmas narrow, subapically exserted. Grain ellipsoidal, terete or compressed, angular, ornamented or smooth, enclosed within a free hyaline pericarp which ruptures at maturity; hilum punctiform, basal.

Approximately ten species, distributed mainly in Africa to India; one species widespread in warm regions of the Old World and introduced in America; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Climbing rattans, sometimes erect, dioecious; leaf sheaths, pinnae, petioles, rachis, cirri and flagellum usually armed with various kinds of spines, bristles or hairs. Stems slender, clustered, rarely solitary. Leaves pinnate; pinnae many, spiny; rachis apex extended to a cirrus in climbers; sheath closed in climbing species, open in erect ones, sparsely to densely covered with various spines, bristles or hairs, ocreas present, obscure; knees present in climbers. Inflorescences branched to 3 orders, male inflorescences more branched than female ones; prophyll boat-like, covering other bracts, persistent, or falling but the basal bract persistent in the species with elongating inflorescences; male flower distichously arranged along rachilla; calyx small, usually 3-fid, cup-like; petals 3; stamens 6; female flowers borne with a sterile flower, ovoid, sepals cup-like, staminodes 6, connate at base forming a ring; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; stigmas 3. Fruits globose, ovoid or ellipsoidal, covered with imbricate scales. Seed usually 1, globose or subglobose, endosperm ruminate.

About 100 species distributed from NE India through Indochina, Philippines, Malaysia, to Indonesia, and New Guinea; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; stems stout and erect. Leaves opposite, 1–3‑pinnate, or some simple. Capitula large, radiate and heterogamous, long‑pedunculate. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries in 2 series; outer ones row foliaceous, reflexed; inner ones scarious, shortly connate at base. Receptacle plain; paleae membranous. Marginal florets neutral or pistillate, 1‑seriate or multi‑seriate in cultivation, corolla ligulate, apex entire or 3‑toothed. Disk florets bisexual and fertile, corolla tubular, apex 5‑lobed; anther bases obtuse; stylar branches hirsute, apical appendages linear‑sublanceolate. Cypselae oblong to lanceolate, subtrigonous with the adaxial surface flat, apex rounded, with 2 inconspicuous teeth.

About 15 species native to S & C America, Mexico, one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or woody climbers. Stipules usually caducous; stipels absent. Leaves alternate, odd-pinnate; leaflets alternate. Flowers small, in terminal or axillary panicles; bracts and bracteoles usually small and caducous. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed, the upper 2 often partly connate. Corolla more or less exserted, white, yellow, purple or violet, often fragrant; vexillum orbicular, ovate to oblong, with well developed claw; wings free, oblong, narrowed or auriculate at base; keel obtuse, more or less connate at tip. Stamens 9 or 10, all united in a sheath open on the upper side, or into two equal bundles or only the vexillary one free. Anthers small, uniform, basifixed, opening at apex. Ovary stipitate, few-ovuled; style short, usually incurved; stigma small. Pods oblong or linear, usually thin, indehiscent, 1–few-seeded. Seeds reniform.

About 100 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 28 species and one variety in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous shrubs or subshrubs. Leaves alternate or subopposite, petiolate. Inflorescences usually terminal (rarely axillary), capitate, racemose or cymose, bracteate or ebracteate. Flowers bisexual or unisexual (plants sometimes dioecious). Calyx tubular or campanulate; lobes 4(–5); petals wanting. Stamens 8 or 10, in 2 whorls, inserted at upper part of calyx-tube; filaments very short or sessile, anthers included or subexserted. Disk annular, often cup-shaped, sometimes absent. Ovary superior, ovoid, 1-locular; ovule 1 per locule, anatropous; style short, stigma capitate. Fruit a drupe, sometimes surrounded by the persistent dry calyx-tube. Testa crustaceous. Embryo fleshy; endosperm scanty or absent.

About 70 species distributed in Asia and Europe; 44 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Herbs, subshrubs or small trees. Leaves simple, alternate, petiolate. Flowers large, usually solitary in branch forks or in axils of leaves; calyx long‑tubular, 5‑toothed or spathe‑like, after anthesis splitting transversely at the very base or above the base and with the left part enlarged as a cup on the fruit; corolla long funnelform or salver‑shaped with spreading plicate limb, shortly and broadly 5‑lobed; stamens 5, inserted below middle of corolla‑tube; anthers opening longitudinally; ovary 2‑locular or falsely 4‑celled; style long filiform, 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, opening by 4‑valves or bursting irregularly, prickly or smooth outside; seeds numerous, reniform or suborbicular, somewhat compressed laterally.

About 16 species distributed mostly in tropical and subtropical regions; three species in China; two species naturalized in Hong Kong.

Datura suaveolens Humb. & Bonpl. ex Willd. (大花曼陀羅) was also cultivated as an ornamental plant.

Biennial herbs, usually pubescent, with thick taproot. Leaves pinnately decompound, the ultimate segments linear to linear-lanceolate; petioles sheathing. Inflorescence of lax compound umbels, terminal and axillary, many-flowered; involucral bracts numerous, pinnately dissected, rarely entire, usually reflexed; bracteoles numerous, toothed or entire. Pedicels unequal. Calyx teeth obsolete to conspicuous. Petals white or yellow, obcordate, with an inflexed apex; flowers at margin of umbellules with enlarged and radiant petals. Stylopodium conic; styles short. Fruit ellipsoidal, dorsally compressed; primary ribs filiform, bristly, secondary ribs winged; wings with glochidiate prickles; vittae 1 in furrows under the secondary ribs, 2 on commissure. Carpophore entire or bifid at apex.

About 20 species distributed in N Africa and SW Asia, Europe, cultivated and naturalized worldwide in temperate regions; one species cultivated in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, often androdioecious. Stipules small, caducous. Leaves opposite, punctate, pinnately-veined, petiolate. Inflorescence a thyrse or panicle, axillary and 1–3-flowered. Flowers bisexual or sometimes staminate, 3–5-merous, often fragrant; bracteoles often small, sometimes caducous. Hypanthium globose, urceolate, or obconiform. Calyx-lobes persistent. Petals pink or white, punctate. Stamens many, in several whorls, distinct; filaments filiform; anthers 2-celled, dorsifixed, dehiscing longitudinally; connectives usually terminating in an apical gland. Ovary inferior, 4–9-locular, placentation axile; ovules 2–many per locule. Style filiform; stigma capitate or peltate. Fruit a berry, globose, vertically ribbed, usually 1–2-seeded per locule. Seeds separated by a vertical false septum, reniform or subglobose; seed coat and pericarp separate; testa bony; embryo horseshoe-shaped; hypocotyl long; cotyledons small.

About 30 species distributed in tropical Asia, Australia and Pacific Islands; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous large trees, unarmed. Leaves large, biparipinnate, stipulate; leaflets small, many. Inflorescences racemose, terminal or axillary. Flowers pedicellate, bisexual, large, showy, white, orange or fresh red. Bracts small, caducous. Calyx-tube short, disciform or turbinate; lobes 5, narrow, subequal, valvate. Petals 5, alternate to calyx-lobes, suborbicular, spreading, long stipitate, margin rugose-wavy. Stamens 10, distinct, downwards curved. Ovary sessile, ovules many; styles filiform; stigmas truncate. Pods linear, flat, pendulous, 2-valved, valves thick and woody. Seeds many, oblong, transversely bearing.

About three species distributed in tropical Africa and tropical Asia; one species cultivated in S China; also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, strongly scented. Leaves alternate, 1–2‑palmately or pinnately divided, serrate, rarely entire. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, solitary or in loose corymbs. Involucres mostly shallow‑dish‑like, rarely campanulate; phyllaries in 3–5 series, margin brownish or blackish scarious, or the outer and middle layers herbaceous with margin pinnatilobed to pinnatifid. Receptacle convex, hemispherical or conical, naked. Marginal florets female and fertile, 1‑seriate, or many‑seriate in some cultivated form, corolla ligulate, colour yellow, white, purple or pink. Disk florets hermaphrodite and fertile, numerous, corolla tubular, apex 5‑lobed, colour yellow, usually glandular; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑lanceolate or elliptic‑oblong; stylar branches linear, apices truncate. Cypselae obovoid‑oblong to subterete, 5–8‑ribbed. Pappus none.

About 30–40 species mainly distributed in Japan, Korea and China; two species commonly growing wild or cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous small trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, leathery, rarely papery, petiolate, pinnately-veined. Inflorescences terminal, cymose, with 4 petaloid bracts. Flowers small, bisexual. Calyx tubular, apex 4-toothed. Petals 4, distinct, rarely connate at base. Stamens 4, filaments slender, anthers 2-celled. Disk annular. Ovary inferior, 2-locular, ovule 1 per locule; style stout; stigma truncate or capitate. Fruit fused into a fleshy syncarpous compound, multiple stoned berry, globose or subglobose; stones asymmetric, seed 1.

Ten species distributed from Himalayas to E Asia; all occurs in China; one species in Hong Kong.

The genus was included in Cornus (sensu lato) in FOC 14: 206 (2005).

Epiphytic and lithophytic herbs; stems erect or rhizomatous, usually without pseudobulbs. Leaves usually many, various, articulate or not. Flowers showy, 1 or several, on leafy or leafless stems, in cymose or racemose clusters; petals generally narrower than sepals; lip entire or trilobed, joined to column foot at base, with a spur or spur-like mentum with lateral sepals. Pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, naked, without caudicles or viscidia.

About 1000 species widely distributed in Old World tropics; 74 species and two varieties in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Arborescent bamboos, large-sized; clumps dense. Rhizomes short necked, pachymorph. Culms unicaespitose, erect, or occasionally scrambling, apex usually pendulous; internodes terete. Branches several to many, none to 3 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous; ligule conspicuous; auricles often absent or small; blade usually recurved, or erect. Leaf blades usually large; ligule conspicuous; auricles usually absent; venation not tessellate. Inflorescence iterauctant, fully bracteate, subtended by a narrow single-keeled prophyll, pseudospikelets clustered in soft or spiky globose mass at nodes of leafless flowering branches. Pseudospikelets prophyllate, (1–)2–8-flowered, with or without rachilla extension and rudiment, sessile, fertile glumes preceded by 1 or more gemmiferous bracts and 0–2 empty glumes. Prophyll narrow, single-keeled. Rachilla internodes usually abbreviated and not disarticulating; florets falling together. Lemma broad, nearly equal to palea, many-veined, sometimes long mucronate; palea of lower florets 2-keeled, but rounded or imperfectly keeled in terminal floret if rachilla extension small or absent, apex acute or shortly bifid; lodicules absent or variably 1–3. Stamens 6; filaments usually free, rarely united into a loose tube. Ovary stalked, apex thickened and hairy; style very short, solid; stigmas 1(–3), long, hairy, plumose. Caryopsis terete, apex hairy; pericarp slightly thickened.

About 40 species distributed in subtropical and tropical Asia; 27 species (15 endemic) in China, mostly in the southwest; three species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Stipules striate, caducous; stipels present. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate or reduced to 1-foliolate; leaflets entire or undulate. Flowers in axillary umbels. Bracts stipule-like. Calyx narrowly turbinate-campanulate, 4–5-lobed, the upper 2 lobes entirely united in appearance of 4-toothed, or partly united and ± 2-lobed, the lower lobes longer. Corolla white or pale yellow; vexillum obovate, elliptic or suborbicular; wings oblong; keel rather straight, long-clawed. Stamens monadelphous. Ovary sessile, 2 – 8-ovuled; style glabrous; stigma capitate. Pods subfalcate, with 1– 8 squared or orbicular-truncate joints, indehiscent.

About 14 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, unarmed, usually glabrous. Leaves simple, entire or sometimes palmately 3–5(–7)-lobed, often with translucent glandular dots; stipules small, scarcely united with the petioles or absent. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, in simple or compound umbels, or in a small racemes of umbels; bracts small or absent; pedicels not articulate. Calyx margin entire or 5-toothed. Petals 5, valvate in the bud. Stamens 5; anthers oval or oblong. Ovary 5-locular; styles distinct or united wholly or partly. Fruit globose or ellipsoidal, distinctly or obscurely 5-ribbed; seeds laterally compressed; endosperm uniform.

About 80 species in tropical American and E to SE Asia; 14 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Parasitic shrubs. Leaves alternate or subopposite on spurs, pinnately-veined. Inflorescences racemose or spicate. Flowers bisexual, 5-merous, actinomorphic or slightly zygomorphic, each flower subtended by a bract. Calyx ovoid or urceolate, limb annular or cupular, persistent. Mature flower bud tubular. Corolla sympetalous, tube inflated, tip clavate, lobes reflexed or twisted with age. Stamens inserted at base of corolla lobes; filaments short, flattened; anthers 4-celled. Ovary 1-locular; placentation basal. Style filiform, 5-angled; stigma capitate. Fruit a berry, exocarp leathery.

About 30 species distributed in Asia, Australia and tropical Africa; one species in China; also in Hong Kong.

Evergreen hemiparasitic woody vines, often on branches of other trees. Stems terete, ridged when young. Leaves alternate, petiolate or sessile, leathery, palmately 3–9(–11)-veined. Flowers bisexual or unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), axillary, solitary, fasciculate, or in cymose or umbellate inflorescences; bracteoles 3–8 subtending each flower. Perianth lobes 5 or 6, triangular, interior with a tuft of hairs or tongue-shaped appendage behind each stamen. Male flowers: stamens as many as and opposite to perianth lobes; filaments short; anthers introrse, cells divaricate, dehiscing obliquely. Disk superior. Female flowers: solitary or in fascicles, usually sessile, perianth tube adnate to ovary, lobes as in males, staminodes present or absent. Ovary inferior; ovules 3; style almost absent; stigmas lobed or capitate. Fruit a drupe, with persistent perianth lobes at apex; endocarp bony, papillate and ridged. Seeds longitudinally furrowed, 8–10 aristate rays on transverse section; embryo straight, short; cotyledons minute.

About ten species distributed from Himalayas and SE Asia to S Australia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody twiners, rarely erect shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, odd-pinnate; leaflets opposite, exstipellate. Racemes or panicles axillary or terminal. Bracts small, caducous; bracteoles sometimes persistent. Calyx campanulate or cup-shaped, truncate or very shortly 4- or 5-toothed. Corolla white, purple or pink, petals clawed; vexillum obovate or orbicular, without appendage, sometimes with a pair of callose thickenings near the base; wings obliquely oblong, slightly adhering to the keel; keel slightly incurved, united at the back; wings and keel auriculate. Stamens 10, monadelphous, vexillary stamen free at base, but connate from the middle with the others in a closed tube, rarely altogether free. Anthers versatile. Ovary sessile or shortly stipitate, with 1 or more ovules; styles filiform, incurved, stigma small, terminal. Pods obliquely orbicular, oblong or elongated, flat, indehiscent, the ventral suture or both sutures margined with a narrow wing. Seeds 1–3, flat, reniform or orbicular.

About 800 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, S America, Oceania and Africa; 25 species and two varieties in China; three species in Hong Kong.

F. C. How (in Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3: 230. 1954) reduced Derris chinensis Benth. (J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 4(Suppl.): 104. 1860; FHK 94. 1861) to a synonym of Millettia taiwaniana Hayata (= M. pachycarpa Benth.).

Perennial herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Stipules persistent or deciduous; stipels subulate or filiform. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate or 1-foliolate. Racemes axillary or terminal, rarely with 1 or 2 axillary flowers. Bracts deciduous or persistent; bracteoles present or absent. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed, the upper 2 more or less connate into a bidentate lip. Corolla white, yellow-white, green-white, pink or purple; petals clawed; vexillum oblong to orbicular; wings more or less adherent to keel. Stamens diadelphous, rarely monadelphous. Ovary sessile; ovules numerous; styles not bearded; stigma terminal. Pods compressed, ± constricted between seeds, indehiscent and breaking up into 1–2-seeded segments.

About 350 species mainly distributed in subtropical and tropical regions; 27 species and five varieties in China; ten species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Small trees, erect or scandent shrubs. Young branches with simple hairs. Leaves papery to leathery, glabrous to pubescent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or supra-axillary, 1(–2)-flowered. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 3, valvate in bud, free. Petals 6, free, in 2 whorls, papery or fleshy; outer petals slightly larger than inner, both whorls concave, enclosing reproductive organs, elongated. Stamens numerous, extrorse; connective with truncate dilated or subglobose apex, glabrous. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary glabrous or hairy, free; ovules 2– 7 per ovary, lateral, 1-seriate; style conspicuous or not; stigma oblong, ovoid or clavate, glabrous. Fruits apocarpous; monocarps (3–)10–40 per fruit, moniliform, glabrous to hairy; stipes 4 – 26 mm long; receptacles 3 – 10 mm in diam.; sepals caducous. Seeds 1– 8 per monocarp, lateral, 1-seriate, globose to ellipsoid; raphes generally conspicuous.

Approximately 30 species in SE Asia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual herbs. Culms compressed. Leaf sheaths keeled, nodes glabrous or hairy; leaf blades linear, flat or inrolled; ligule membranous. Inflorescence of single or subdigitate racemes, terminal or also axillary and sometimes supported by spathes; rachis internodes and pedicels linear, without longitudinal grooved. Spikelets paired, alternate, 1 sessile, the other pedicellate. Sessile spikelet bisexual, dorsally compressed; callus short, obtuse, apex exposed; lower glume papery to cartilaginous, broadly convex to slightly concave, sometimes pitted, rounded on flanks, becoming 2-keeled upward, apex obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, dorsally keeled, awnless; lower floret reduced to an empty hyaline lemma; upper lemma stipitiform, entire or slightly 2-lobed, awned from apex; awn geniculate, glabrous or puberulous; lodicules 2; stamens 2–3. Pedicellate spikelet similar to the sessile spikelet, staminate or barren, awnless.

About 20 species distributed in Africa through India to SE Asia and Australia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Prostrate creeping small herbs. Leaves petiolate; stipules minute; leaf blade reniform to heart‑shaped or orbicular, entire. Flowers solitary, axillary, pedicellate; bracts minute. Sepals joined basally, ± equal, usually spathulate, becoming enlarged in fruit. Corolla campanulate, lobed to middle or below, lobes valvate or imbricate. Stamens inclusive, anthers small; pollen grains not spiny. Ovary deeply 2‑lobed, each lobe with 2 ovules. Styles 2, basal, free, filiform; stigmas capitate. Capsule irregularly 2‑valved or indehiscent, or deeply 2‑lobed. Seeds 1 or 2 per lobe, subglobose, smooth.

About 14 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions all over the world; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Deciduous shrubs. Leaves opposite. Inflorescence terminal, a corymbose cyme or panicle. Flowers bisexual. Calyx 5( –6)-lobed. Petals 5( –6), free, thick and slightly fleshy. Stamens 4 – 10( –20); filaments filiform or subulate; anthers ellipsoidal to ovoid, 2-celled. Ovary semi-inferior to inferior, incompletely 3 – 5-locular; placentation parietal; ovules many; styles 2 – 6, distinct or connate only at base, divergent; stigma ovoid. Fruit a berry, blue. Seeds many, tiny, ovoid, not winged; seed coat membranous, reticulate.

About 12 species mainly in E Asia and adjacent islands; six species (four endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or decumbent. Leaves alternate, lyrately pinnatifid. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, hemispherical or globose, pedunculate, forming racemes or loose panicles, rarely solitary. Involucres small; phyllaries 2‑seriate. Receptacle convex, depressed globose or conical, naked. All florets tubular and fertile, marginal ones many‑seriate, white or yellow, female; central ones funnelform, with 4–5 lobes at apex, green or purple, hermaphrodite. Anthers cuneate and sagittate at base, with apical appendages; stylar branches of bisexual florets short, with lanceolate appendages. Cypselae oblanceolate‑oblong, bilaterally compressed, marginal ribs prominent, glandular at apical and basal portions. Pappus absent or with few short and easily deciduous bristles on the cypselae of bisexual florets.

About five species native to tropical Asia and Africa; three species in China; one species as a common weed in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial diffuse herbs, sometimes shurbs, with cystoliths. Leaves petiolate, usually ovate, margin entire or obscurely undulate. Inflorescence of small cymes in leaf axils, sometimes aggregated into a leafy panicle. Flowers paired but usually one sterile, enclosed within a pairs of slightly unequal bracts which conceal the calyx and corolla tube. Bracts 2, opposite; bracteoles small, linear or linear‑lanceolate. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes equal, narrow, acute. Corolla pink, resupinate by torsion of the tube; tube slender, widened apically; limb bilabiate, upper lip entire or emarginate, lower lip weakly 3‑lobed, lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, long exserted; anthers 2‑thecous, one above the other, base muticous. Staminodes absent. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform, stigma shortly bifid. Capsule ovoid, substipitate or stipitate, the placenta separating elastically and rising from the wall on the dehiscence, 2‑ or 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, glabrous.

About 100 species in tropical and temperate regions of the world; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, annual or perennial. Stems erect, simple or branched. Leaves opposite; leaf blade ovate. Inflorescences lax, axillary, 2 – 10‑flowered cymes; bracts 2, opposite. Calyx actinomorphic, 5‑sect from base; segments narrowly lanceolate. Corolla purplish, zygomorphic; tube slender funnelform, not swollen, longer than limb; limb 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, much shorter than abaxial lip; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal, apex rounded. Stamens 2, adnate to abaxial side of corolla tube middle; anthers basifixed, coherent at apex, thecae parallel, not confluent at apex, dehiscing longitudinally; staminodes 2 or 3. Disk ring‑like. Ovary linear; placentas 2, parietal, slightly projecting inward, 2‑cleft; stigmas 2, equal, undivided. Capsule straight, linear, dehiscing loculicidally to base; valves 2, straight. Seeds ellipsoidal, unappendaged, glabrous.

Two species endemic to China, one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect or ascending from decumbent base. Leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate; ligule membranous, well developed. Inflorescence of digitately arranged racemes, sometimes on a short axis or with secondary branchlets. Spikelets crowded, alternately 2–3-together along keel, unequally pedicellate in a group, sometimes subsessile, deciduous with widened tip of pedicel, dorsally compressed; lower glume absent or very small; upper glume lanceolate, usually pubescent; lower lemma usually ± equal to spikelet, usually pilose or hairiness variable, 3–9-veined; lower palea absent or very small and adnate to base of upper lemma; upper lemma thicken papery or cartilaginous, apex acute, dorsally convex, densely striate and very finely tuberculate, palea the same texture, stamens 3; styles 2, free; lodicules 2. Caryopsis oblong-elliptic.

About 250 species widely spread over tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world; 22 species in China; ten species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect to decumbent, glabrous. Leaf blades linear, flat; ligule short, membranous, truncate. Inflorescence terminal, composed of solitary or subdigitate racemes. Spikelets solitary, usually overlapping in 2 rows; rachis tough, spikelets deciduous from pedicels at maturity; pedicels very short, broad, margin truncate, apex concave. Spikelets lanceolate or narrowly oblong, strongly laterally compressed; callus truncate, shortly bearded; glumes herbaceous or thinly papery, folded with a median keel, keel often winged, lower glume narrower and slightly shorter than upper glume, conduplicate-keeled; lower floret reduced to a narrow hyaline lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline, apex 2-toothed, awned from sinus; upper palea normally absent; lodicules 2; stamens 2. Caryopsis linear, laterally compressed.

About 40 species distributed in Indian Subcontinent, E Asia, Malesia and Australia; six species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, usually monoecious. Leaves paripinnate, alternate, exstipulate; leaflets opposite or subopposite, entire. Thyrses usually large, terminal, or fasciculate, stellate or tomentose; bracts and bracteoles subulate, small. Flowers unisexual, actinomorphic. Calyx cupular; sepals 5, imbricate, stellate-hairy or tomentose. Petals (0–)5, usually spathulate or lanceolate, without scales. Disk acetabuliform. Stamens (male flowers) often 8, exserted; filaments hirsute; anthers ellipsoidal. Ovary (female flowers) obcordiform, 2–3-lobed and 2–3-locular, densely tuberculate, with tufted stellate hairs and tomentose on tubercles; ovules 1 per locule; style between ovary lobes; stigma 2–3-lobed. Fruit deeply lobed into 2 or 3 schizocarps, usually 1–2 developed; fertile schizocarp berry-like, subglobose, pericarp leathery (crustaceous when dry), endocarp papery. Seeds subglobose or ellipsoidal; testa leathery, smooth; hilum elliptic, slightly large; pseudotesta fleshy, embedding all or half of seed.

About seven species distributed in S and SE Asia from Sri Lanka and India to E Malesia and Australia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous or woody vines, with various tubers. Stems twining, often bearing bulbils at axils of leaves. Leaves alternate or opposite, petiolate, simple or palmately compound, basal veins 3–9. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious, rarely monoecious), in axillary spikes, racemes or paniculate. Male flowers: stamens 6, 3 sometimes reduced to staminodes or absent. Female flowers: staminodes 3, 6, or absent. Capsule 3-angled or 3-lobed, opening loculicidally at the angles, often leaving the vein-like edge free. Seeds winged.

More than 600 species widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions; 52 species (21 endemic, two introduced) in China; nine species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious or polygamous. Leaves alternate or rarely subopposite, entire. Male flowers usually arranged in axillary cymes and female ones often solitary and axillary. Calyx 4 –5-lobed, enlarged when fruiting. Corolla 4 –5-lobed, convolute, rarely imbricate. Male flowers: stamens 4 –many, usually 16, distinct or paired; pistillodes present or absent. Female flowers: staminodes 1–16 or absent; ovary (4 –)8(–16)-locular, ovules 1(–2) per locule; styles usually 2– 4, distinct or connate at base, stigma often 2-cleft. Berries fleshy to somewhat leathery, usually with an enlarged persistent calyx. Seeds 1–10, compressed.

About 500 species mainly distributed in tropical regions, and some species extending to temperate regions; 60 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Small or medium-sized annuals, occasionally perennial. Leaves basal and cauline, linear; ligule absent; contraligule absent. Inflorescence comprising of few to many head-like clusters of spikelets borne from the axils of leaf-like bracts, usually almost throughout the length of culm. Spikelets unisexual, the female spikelets with 3–4 glumes and terminated by a female flower; male spikelets large, otherwise minute. Perianth segments absent. Stamen 1. Stigmas 3. Achenes tightly enveloped in 2 subtending glumes and falling off with them, pericarp bony, irregularly rugose, reticulate or smooth. Disk obsolete, adnate to base of the achene.

Six species in the tropics of both hemispheres; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Woody vines. Leaves broadly triangular ovate to broadly triangular orbicular, palmately 3–7-nerved. Cymes supra-axillary, or borne on old stems and forming panicles. Male flowers: sepals 6, in 2 series, usually with black stripes when dry, the inner 3 larger; petals 6, usually rhomboid, base folded inward and embracing the opposite filament; stamens 6, free, anthers transversely dehiscent. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; petals usually 2-lobed at apex; staminodes 6; carpels 3; styles very short; stigmas recurved. Drupes oblong to obovoid, laterally compressed, with style-scar close to base; kernel bony, narrowed at base, with dorsal ridge and many transverse ribs on both faces.

Two species in China and tropical Asia; one species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic monopodial herbs; roots string-like, branched. Leaves leathery, distichous. Scapes several, axillary, short, with basal scales; flowering bracts persistent. Flowers small, in a short axillary spike, opening 1 at a time; sepals subequal, free, spreading; petals slightly narrower than the sepals, spreading; lip 3-lobed, attached to the base of the column, concave, without a foot or spur, lateral lobes erect, obtuse, midlobe narrow, the apex extending into 2 filiform lobes, disk flat, fleshy; column short, oblong, clinandrium truncate; rostellum ovate, obtuse; anther semiglobose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, unequal, the front ones larger, obovoid, attached to a stipe with an ovate viscidium; stigma large covering the entire front of the column; ovary cylindrical. Capsules oblong, the apex crowned with persistent sepals.

Two species distributed in tropical areas of S Asia; one species in S China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, unarmed. Leaves decussately opposite, petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, united at the base, apex acuminate. Flowers bisexual or polygamo‑dioecious, in axillary short cymes or clusters. Calyx‑tube short; limb truncate or with 4–5 teeth. Corolla white, light green or yellowish, bell‑shaped; tube short; lobes 4–5, contorted in the bud. Stamens 4–5, attached to the throat, alternate with corolla‑lobes; filaments short; anthers dorsifixed, exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2–3 ovules in each locule; style short or long, 2‑lobed. Fruit an ovoid or globose berry, seeds solitary or few in each cell.

About 20 species in tropical and subtropical Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, creeping or procumbent, rooting at nodes. Leaves usually entire, with cystoliths. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2 clustered, sessile or subsessile. Bracts absent; bracteoles leaf‑like, stalked, exceeding the calyx. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes equal. Corolla campanulate; tube short; lobes 5, subequal, usually ovate, contorted in bud. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments glabrous; anther incised at base, 2‑thecous; thecae oblong, sometimes with appendage at apex. Ovary 2‑locular, 3–8 ovules per locule; style hispid or subglabrous towards the apex; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal, anterior lobe flattened, posterior one minute. Capsule clavate, retinacula well developed, flat, 6–16‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, pilose, with a narrow, membranous wing.

About 150 species in tropic regions of the Old World from E Africa to SE Asia extending to Australia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs, epiphytic or epilithic. Stems and branches fleshy, usually climbing by adventitious roots, sometimes also twining, or hanging. Leaves opposite or partly in whorls of 3 or 4, fleshy. Inflorescences extra‑axillary, small, rachis short, thick, often branched, eventually raceme‑like, producing a series of often umbel‑like groups of flowers. Flowers mostly very small. Calyx with 5 basal glands. Corolla white, red, or violet, ovoid to urn‑shaped, with a narrow mouth, fleshy; lobes valvate in bud, short, often hairy. Corona‑lobes 5, inserted on gynostegium, slender, erect or ascending, apex entire, notched, 2‑cleft, or with recurved arms. Anthers erect, with apical membrane overlying stigma head; pollinia 1 in each cell, margin translucent, caudicles dilated at apex, erect. Follicles lanceolate or cylindric.

About 80 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Oceania; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Small succulent terrestrial herbs, overwinter in a dormant stage in form of small globose tubers. Stems slender, bearing 3 cataphylls and 2 tiny ovate cauline leaves. Flowers small, 1–2, axillary to leafy bracts, terminal to a tiny stem; sepals spreading, the odd one erect, suborbicular, with the petals forming a shield behind the column, the lateral sepals connate at the base, separated at the middle, bending at an angle of 90º, calcarate; petals erect; column conical, obtuse; rostellum broad triangular, stipitate, with slender long and curved arms; anther 2-celled, the cells divergent; pollinia 2, small, sectile; caudicles elongate, the viscidia exposed; stigmas 2; ovary cylindrical.

About 75 species predominantly African, with a few species in tropical Asia, Australia and Pacific islands; two species in China; one species endemic to Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with creeping rhizomes and fleshy roots. Stem erect, simple or branched in distal part. Leaves alternate, concentrated in distal part of stem (proximal part with only 1–several sheaths), alternate, often shortly petiolate, sometimes sessile; leaf blade linear to suborbicular, 3–7-veined. Inflorescences terminal or pseudolateral (terminal on a short, lateral branchlet opposite to a leaf), umbellate or with flowers paired or solitary; bract absent. Flowers bisexual, often nodding, tubular-campanulate. Perianth segments 6, free, white, greenish, yellow, pink, dark red, or dark purple, often saccate or spurred at base. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth segments; filaments usually ± flat; anthers basifixed to innate, extrorse. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with 2–6 ovules in each locule; style slender, 3-lobed to 3-fid apically with ± recurved lobes. Fruit a berry, dark blue to black, 2(–6)-seeded. Seeds globose or ovoid.

About 20 species distributed in E and SE Asia to Malesia; 14 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees; young branches usually stellately tomentose or with sessile peltate scales. Leaves alternate, shortly petiolate; stipules minute, caducous; leaf blade leathery, margin entire or nearly so, pinnately veined, sometimes with 3 basal veins. Inflorescence a condensed panicle or botryoid, axillary or terminal, few-flowered; bracts 3-lobed. Flowers male or bisexual (plants andromonoecious). Floral cup urceolate to cup-shaped, subtended by sepal-like bracts, often ± ascending on one side. Male flowers sessile, bisexual flowers often pedicellate. Sepals and petals absent. Stamens (1–)5 – 6(15), thecae 2-sporangiate, longitudinally dehiscent; rudimentary carpels present. Ovary superior, enclosed by long floral cup, ovules 1 per locule; stigmas decurrent.
