Capsules woody, ± stalked, arranged in 2 series along axis, densely hispid, dehiscing into 2 valves, persistent calyx-tube shorter than capsules. Seeds ellipsoid.

About six species, distributed in China, Laos, Malaysia, New Guinea; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or trees; branches stellately tomentose or lepidote when young. Leaves alternate, shortly petiolate; stipules lanceolate, caducous; leaf blade leathery, pinnately veined. Inflorescence a condensed panicle or botryoid, flowers axillary, ± sessile; each flower usually subtended by two (simple or 3-lobed) subopposite sepal-like bracteoles, sometimes lacking in male flowers. Flowers male or bisexual (plants andromonoecious). Sepals, petals and floral cup absent. Male flowers: stamens 4 – 8, filaments short, unequal, anthers ellipsoid, thecae 2-sporangiate, longitudinally dehiscent, connective protruded. Bisexual flowers: stamens 5–8, ovary superior, ovules 1 per locule; stigmas decurrent. Capsules ovoid-globose, woody, stellately tomentose, dehiscing above middle by two 2-lobed valves, without persistent calyx tube. Seeds 1 per locule, narrowly ovoid.

About 18 species, distributed in China, NE India (Assam), Indonesia (Java, Sumatra), Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Korea, Malaysia; 12 species (11 endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, sometimes with a glandular resinous exudate on leaves and inflorescences. Leaves simple or pinnate, exstipulate. Flowers bisexual or unisexual (plants dioecious), actinomorphic, solitary and axillary or arranged in terminal and axillary racemes, corymbs or panicles. Sepals (3–)5(–7), valvate or sometimes imbricate. Petals absent. Disk inconspicuous, absent in male flowers. Stamens (male flowers) 5–8; filaments short; anthers ellipsoidal, obtusely 4-gonous, connectives prominent. Ovary (female flowers) ellipsoidal, obcordiform, or transversely ellipsoidal, usually (2–)3(–6)-gonous, (2–)3(–6)-locular; ovules 2 per locule; style apical, much longer than ovary, often twisted; stigma (2–)3(–6)-lobed. Capsules samara-like, (2–)3(–6)-locular, septifragal, boat-like. Seeds 1–2 per locule, arillode present or absent.

About 65 species mainly distributed in Australia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, slender, erect or sometimes decumbent, ± succulent. Leaves opposite, sometimes scale‑like. Flowers axillary, solitary. Bracteoles absent. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes subequal. Corolla‑tube much longer than calyx, distally inflated; limbs 2‑lipped; lower lip 3‑lobed; upper lip 2‑lobed, conspicuously shorter than lower lip. Fertile stamens 2, inserted on posterior side of corolla‑tube; filaments filiform; anther‑cells parallel; staminodes 2, small, inserted on anterior side, styles short, stigma 2‑lamellate, clavate, or capitate. Ovary 2‑loculed; ovules numerous. Capsules loculicidal; valves entire or apex shallowly 2‑lobed. Seeds small, numerous.

About 12 species distributed in tropics of Africa, Asia, Australia; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Arborescent or shrubby plants. Stems simple or branched, ± woody, pithed and with secondary thickening. Leaves often crowded toward apex of stems or spaced along distal part of stems, sessile or petiolate, veins truly parallel from base, lateral veins absent. Inflorescence terminal, racemose or paniculate. Flowers bisexual, clustered, sometimes solitary; pedicel articulate. Perianth cylindrical, campanulate, or funnelform; tube short; lobes 6, similar. Stamens 6, inserted in tube or throat of perianth; anthers versatile. Ovary superior, 3-locular; ovules 1–2 per locule. Style slender; stigma capitate or 3-lobed. Fruit a berry, globose, 1–3-seeded.

About 50 species mainly distributed in tropical regions of Africa and Asia; six species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves imparipinnate, alternate, exstipulate; leaflets opposite or alternate, entire, rarely serrulate. Inflorescence a panicle, axillary or terminal. Flowers small, bisexual, 5-merous. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes imbricate. Petals imbricate, recurved at anthesis. Stamens 10, inserted at base of disk. Disk cupular, shallowly 10-lobed. Ovary 5-locular, ovule 1 per locule; styles 5, joined in upper part. Drupe subglobose, mesocarp fleshy, endocarp pentagonal and slightly compressed. Seed compressed globose, 3-ribbed.

About eight species distributed in tropical Asia; two species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Woody lianas, with white latex. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Inflorescence an umbel‑like cluster of cymules, with long and slender peduncle and pedicels. Sepals 5, overlapping, with 5 basal glands. Corolla rotate to shallowly bowl‑shaped, deeply 5‑divided; lobes overlapping to right. Corona‑lobes 5, ± spreading, thick‑fleshy, adnate to stamens, outer angle obtuse or rectangular, interior angle produced into an acute tooth incumbent to anthers. Anthers with membranous apical appendage; pollinia 2 per pollinarium, oblong, erect. Ovary of 2 separate carpels; ovules many in each carpel; stigma head umbonate or thickly conical. Follicles widely divergent, thick, finely longitudinally ribbed or corrugated. Seeds comose.

About 12 species distributed in S Asia and Africa; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, with a short perennial stock, sometimes lengthening out into leafy stems. Leaves basal and rosulate, or alternate, petiolate, more or less covered with glandular, papillose hairs or bristles; stipulate or exstipulate. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, radical or axillary, terminating in a simple or forked one-sided spike; sepals 5, or rarely 4, 6– 8, free or connate at base, persistent; petals 5, free, closing and contorted after anthesis, persistent; stamens as many as petals; ovary superior, 1-locular, 2–5- carpellate; ovules many; styles 3 – 5, rare 2 or 6, free or connate at base, persistent. Capsule dehiscent, 2– 5-valved. Seeds numerous, ellipsoid or linear, sometimes winged.

About 100 species distributed in tropical to tundra regions, especially concentrated in Australia; six species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems prostrate or ascending, dichotomously branched. Leaves opposite, shortly petiolate, 3 – 5-nerved. Stipules minute, subulate, usually caducous. Flowers solitary or in dichotomous cymes. Sepals 5, herbaceous. Petals absent or 3– 5, deeply 2-lobed. Stamens 5, alternate with sepals; filaments slightly dilated at base. Ovary 1-locular, with several ovules; style single, 3-lobed. Capsule ovoid, opening into 3 valves.

About 44 species, mostly in C America; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, margins entire or serrate, base often asymmetrical, pinnately-veined; petioles short; stipules 2. Flowers dioecious, pedicellate or sessile, apetalous. Male flowers axillary, fasciculate or grouped into glomerules, racemes or panicles; sepals 4–6, distinct, usually unequal, imbricate; stamens 1–25, in 1– several whorls, surrounding the disk or outer ones inserted at margin or sinus of disk, inner ones inserted at the disk, filaments free, anthers 2-celled, usually introrse, rarely extrorse, longitudinally dehiscing; disk flattened or concave, margins shallowly or deeply lobed; rudimentary ovary rather small or absent. Female flowers: solitary, axillary or inserted at lateral older branches; sepals as in male; disk annular; ovary 1–2(–3)-locular; ovules 2 in each cell; styles short, stigmatiform; stigmas 1–2(–3), usually dilating into a peltate or reniform. Drupes or capsules ovoid or subglobose, 1–2(–3)-locular, 1-seeded in each locule; epicarps coriaceous or nearly so; mesocarps fleshy or woody; endocarps woody, papery or crustaceous; seeds without caruncle; endosperm fleshy, cotyledons larger and flattened.

About 200 species in tropical and subtropical Asia, Africa and America; 13 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, stoloniferous. Leaves basal and cauline, 3(–5)-foliolate, with long petioles; leaflets rhombic-ovate, coarsely dentate, short-petiolulate; stipules paired, membranaceous, those of the cauline leaves free, those of basal leaves adnate at the base of petiole, incised, persistent. Flowers solitary, bisexual. Bracteoles usually 3-toothed at apex, alternating with the sepals. Hypanthium cup-shaped, lined inside by a sometimes hairy disk. Sepals 5, persistent, shorter than the bracteoles. Epicalyx 5, sometimes 4, longer than sepals. Petals 5, yellow, cuneate-oblong, truncate or somewhat retuse at apex. Stamens 20 – 30, filaments filiform, anthers subrounded, 2-lobed. Pistils numerous, inserted on a convex receptacle; ovary superior, unilocular, with 1 pendulous ovule; styles lateral, deciduous, stigmas undivided; receptacle pulpy. Collective fruits of many achenes, surrounded by persistent sepals and epicalyx. Achenes minute, compressed ovate, sunk in the surface of the enlarged spongy deciduous receptacle. Seed solitary, reniform, smooth, without endosperm.

Two species distributed in Afghanstan, India, SE and E Asia; and in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual or biennial herbs, or subshrubs; stem usually hairy and glandular. Leaves alternate. Capitula heterogamous, radiate or disciform, usually in corymbs or paniculate corymbose arrangement. Involucres campanulate, hemispherical or obovoid; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate. Receptacle plane or slightly convex, naked. Marginal florets few, pistillate, corolla ligulate or narrowly tubular with 2–3 short teeth apically, yellow or rarely white in colour, stylar branches rounded at apex. Central florets hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, funnelform with limb 5‑lobed, yellow; anther bases sagittate and tailed, apical appendages rounded, obtuse or truncate; stylar branches obtuse or truncate at apex. Cypselae subterete, ribbed, hairy or not. Pappus capillary, in 1–2 series with outer ones shorter.

This genus is technically distinguished from Inula by polarized (vs. radial) endothecial tissue in the anthers, ridged (vs. smooth) receptacles, and truncate to rarely acute (vs. acute) anther appendages, and many species tend to have marginal pistillate florets with tubular corollas with small or very reduced limbs.

About 13 species distributed from Iran to E Africa and E Asia; eight species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Prostrate or twining herbs. Stipules deciduous or absent, stipels minute or absent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets entire, bearing reddish glandular dots especially abaxially. Racemes axillary, rarely flowers solitary. Bracts deciduous or absent; bracteoles absent. Calyx campanulate, upper 2 lobes ± connate into a lip; vexillum suborbicular, erect or spreading, obovate or oblong, base auriculate; wings obliquely obovate or oblong; keel blunt, incurved. Stamens diadelphous, 1 opposite to vexillum free, others connate; anthers uniform. Ovary stipitate or sessile, several-ovuled; styles filiform, incurved, glabrous, stigma capitate. Pods linear or linear-oblong, compressed, straight or curved, septate between seeds, hilum surrounded by rim-like aril.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Asia and Australia; nine species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, spinose or not. Leaves simple, opposite or whorled, margin entire or serrate‑dentate. Racemes axillary or terminal. Bracts small. Calyx 5‑dentate, persistent, enlarged in fruit. Corolla‑tube tubular, straight or curved; limb 2‑lipped, lower lip 3‑lobed and largest, upper lip 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, short, inserted above middle of cylindric corolla tube, obscurely didynamous. Ovary 8‑locular; ovules 1 per locule, pendulous. Style short, inclusive; stigma nearly oblique capitate. Drupes completely enclosed by persistent calyx, mesocarp fleshy, endocarp splitting into 4 pyrenes, pyrene 2‑locular, seed 1 per locule.

About 30 species distributed in tropical America; one species introduced to China and sometimes naturalized; one species widely cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs, monoecious. Stems clustered or solitary, with distinct rings of leaf scars, occasionally branched at base. Leaves pinnate (rarely bifid), reduplicate; pinnae many, regularly or irregularly arranged, linear to lanceolate; sheaths closed and forming a crownshaft, rarely almost open, sometimes fibrous; petioles short to long, or absent. Inflorescences usually interfoliar, rarely borne below the leaf sheaths, branched 1–4 orders; prophyll small; peduncles bracts conspicuous, tubular, caducous; rachillae bracts usually inconspicuous. Flowers sessile, in triads of 1 female with 2 lateral male flowers; male flowers: sepals 3, imbricate, petals 3, ± connate, stamens 3 or 6, pistillode present; female flowers: sepals 3, imbricate, petals 3, imbricate, staminodes 6, very small, stigmas 3. Fruits globose, ellipsoidal or fusiform, with persistent sepals and petals; epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy, endocarp thin, fibrous. Seed ovoid, endosperm homogeneous, embryo subbasal.

About 140 species native to Africa (Madagascar and adjacent islands); one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaves in whorls of 3–10, rarely opposite, sessile or petiolate. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming continuous or rarely interrupted terminal spikes; bracts minute, hairy. Flowers sessile. Calyx campanulate, shortly 5‑toothed, teeth subequal, ciliate, throat glabrous inside. Corolla tubular, straight; tube gradually widened at apex; limb 4‑lobed; lobes subequal, the upper lobe entire or notched. Stamens 4, exserted, subequal and nearly straight; filaments bearded; anthers subglobose, 1‑locular. Disk ring‑like, subentire. Style 2‑fid; lobes subequal, subulate. Nutlets subglobose, smooth.

About 27 species mostly in SE Asia (especially rich in India), only one species extended to Australia; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves pinnate, alternate or rarely opposite. Inflorescence a panicle, axillary. Flowers bisexual, 4–5-merous. Calyx cupular, 4–5-lobed or parted into 4–5 sepals. Petals 4–5, oblong, valvate or apex slightly imbricate, distinct or sometimes adnate to staminal tube at base. Staminal tube cylindrical, slightly shorter than petals, apex usually laciniate or obtusely dentate; anthers 8–10, inclusive. Disk tubular, as long as or longer than ovary, margin entire or obtusely dentate. Ovary (3–)4–5-locular, ovules 1 or 2 per locule. Style as long as staminal tube; stigma disciform. Fruit a capsule, globose or pyriform, dehiscing into (3–)4–5 valves. Seeds arillate or not; hilum broad; cotyledons large.

About 75 species distributed in tropical Asia, tropical Australia, Pacific Islands, New Zealand; 15 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms tufted. Leaf blades linear or broadly linear, flat; ligule absent or a fringe of hairs. Inflorescence a panicle composed of racemes along a central axis; racemes simple or compound, densely spiculate. Spikelets paired or fasciculate, dorsally compressed, broadly elliptic, solitary, sometimes in pairs or 4(–10) together, falling as a whole, sessile or shortly pedicellate, 1–2-floret, lower floret staminate or barren, upper floret bisexual; lower glume triangular, 1/3–1/2(–3/5) spikelet length, acute; upper glume and lower lemma as long as spikelet, lower lemma with short or long awn; upper lemma coriaceous, laterally compressed, smooth, shiny, mucronate, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea; lodicules 2, 5–7-veined; style free from the base.

About 35 species distributed in tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world; eight species in China; four species and two varieties in Hong Kong.

Annual branched herbs, strigose. Leaves opposite. Capitula pedunculate, heterogamous, radiate. Involucres campanulate to hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, in about 2 rows, subequal in size. Receptacle convex, paleate; the paleae linear, bristle‑like, hairy at the distal half. Florets white. Ray florets 2‑seriate, pistillate and fertile, corolla ligulate, limb bifid or entire. Disk florets many, hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, 4‑lobed at apex; anther bases entire or minutely bifid; stylar branches complanate and obtuse, papillose on the abaxial sides. Cypselae laterally compressed or slightly 3–4‑angled, truncate at apex, tuberculate on both sides. Pappus none or shortly toothed.

About four species in tropical regions; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Herbs, perennial, freshwater. Rhizomes and stolons absent. Stems erect, rooted in substrate, branched or unbranched, elongate. Leaves cauline, in whorls of 5 or more, submersed, sessile; blade linear, base sloping to stem, apex obtuse; midvein without rows of lacunae along sides, blade uniform in colour throughout; abaxial surface without prickles or aerenchyma; intravaginal squamules entire. Inflorescences 1-flowered, sessile; spathes not winged. Flowers unisexual, male and female on different plants, projected to surface by slender, elongate floral tube base, pedicellate; petals white. Male flowers: axillary, filaments distinct, anthers linear; pollen in monads. Female flowers: ovary 1-locular; styles 3, not 2-fid. Fruit ovoid, smooth, dehiscing irregularly. Seeds fusiform, mucilaginous.

Three species originated from S America, introduced into N America, Eurasia, Africa, and Australia; one species introduced into China and Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves petiolate, entire or serrate at margin. Inflorescences corymbose or paniculate‑cymose. Calyx 5‑lobed. Corolla white or pale yellow, tubular or tubular‑campanulate, rarely funnelform, 5‑lobed; lobes spreading or reflexed. Filaments slender, usually exserted; anthers ovoid to ellipsoidal. Ovary globose, 2‑locular, ovules 2 per locule. Style terminal, 2‑cleft; stigmas 2, capitate or elongate. Drupes yellow, orange, or pale red, subglobose, glabrous, endocarp divided into two 2‑seeded or four 1‑seeded pyrenes at maturity.

About 50 species mostly distributed in Africa and S Asia, few in N America and the Caribbean; 14 species in China, mainly S of the Changjiang; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial aquatic herbs, floating, with creeping rhizomes, rooting from nodes. Leaves rosulate or alternate; petiole sometimes inflated; leaf blade broadly ovate, cordate or linear-lanceolate. Flowers zygomorphic or subactinomorphic, in terminal spikelike raceme, 2–many-flowered; perianth united below middle into a tube, segments 6, light purplish blue, inner upper one with a yellow blotch in centre. Stamens 6, inserted on proximal part of perianth tube, often 3 longer and 3 shorter; filaments filiform, hairy; anthers dorsifixed, oblong. Ovary sessile, 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule; style filiform, curved; stigma slightly dilated or very shortly 3- or 6-lobed. Capsule ovoid, oblong, or linear-fusiform, included in marcescent perianth tube; pericarp membranous.

Seven species mainly distributed in tropical America, one species in tropical Africa; one species naturalized in China and Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous shrubs, rarely trees, often spiny and covered with silvery or brown stellate scales. Leaves alternate, short-petiolate. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, apetalous, axillary, solitary or clustered. Perianth-tube campanulate or tubular, apex 4-lobed; lobes valvate in bud. Stamens 4; filaments very short, inserted in perianth-tube; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 1-locular; style subulate, recurved, and stigmatic along one side at the top. Fruit berry-like, the ellipsoidal striate stone enclosed by the fleshy perianth-tube.

About 80 species mainly in N temperate and subtropical regions, with a few species extending to tropical areas; 55 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves usually alternate or spirally arranged. Petioles long and usually swollen at both ends; leaf blade usually with black glands abaxially, margin serrate or entire, pinnately veined. Stipules linear or rarely leaf-like, caducous, rarely persistent. Inflorescence racemose, axillary. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, 4- or 5-merous. Sepals 4–6. Petals 4–5, white, free, laciniate at apex, rarely entire or lobed. Stamens numerous, often 10–50; filaments very short; anthers dehiscing by apical pores, with awn or hairs at tip. Disc usually 5–10-lobed, rarely circular. Ovary 2–5-locular; ovules 2–12 per locule; style linear or subulate, not branched. Fruit a drupe, 1–5-locular; endocarp hard, bony, usually lacunose on surface. Seeds usually one per locule; endosperm fleshy; cotyledons thin; embryo straight or curved.

About 360 species distribtuted in tropical regions of the Old World; 38 species and seven varieties in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials; rhizome short or absent; stolons usually present. Culms terete or angular, sometimes transversely septate. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheath; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1–2, glume-like. Inflorescence a single, terminal spikelet. rarely 2-ranked. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments up to 8, bristle-like, sometimes absent. Stamens 1–3. Stigmas 2–3, base of style persistent on achenes. Achenes trigonous or biconvex, mostly obovate, surface smooth, reticulate, pitted, longitudinally grooved or transversely ridged.

About 250 species in tropical and temperate regions of the world; 35 species in China; 11 species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, rigid, hairy throughout. Leaves rosulate at base or alternate above, sessile or shortly petiolate, with pinnate veins. Capitula sessile, aggregated into glomerules surrounded by few foliaceous bracts and subtended by rigid stalk. Involucres oblong to cylindric, slightly compressed; phyllaries in 2 series with 4 involucral bracts in each layer, outer layer shorter and alternate to the inner one, oblong, apex acuminate or with spine. Receptacle small and glabrous. Florets 2 – 5 per capitulum, all tubular, hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla 5‑lobed apically with one side usually more deeply cleft; anther shortly sagittate at base, apical appendages obtuse; style hirsute, branches subulate. Cypselae oblong‑cylindric, 10‑costate, truncate at apex, puberulent. Pappus 5 stiff setaceous scales, dilated at base.

About 30 species mainly found in S America; two species growing as weeds in S China and in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms slightly compressed, usually with one long internode alternating with several short internodes, making the leaves ± in groups on the culm. Leaf blades linear, usually folded; ligule membranous, truncate, usually with a ciliate fringe; leaf sheaths strongly keeled. Inflorescence consisting of secund, subsessile, digitately arranged spikes, seldom a solitary spike. Spikelets several-flowered, ovate to narrowly oblong, laterally compressed, solitary, sessile, biseriate, imbricate; glumes shorter than spikelet, persistent, 1–3(–7)-veined, keeled, awnless; upper glumes at outer side, longer than the lower; lemmas longer than glumes, successively smaller upwards, membranous, 3-veined, glabrous, strongly keeled, keel thickened with 1–3 closely spaced additional veins, obtuse or acute; rachilla glabrous, articulate below lemmas, breaking up maturity or not; palea shorter, 2-veined; lodicules 2, small. Stamens 3; anthers short. Ovary glabrous, styles 2, free, with narrow stigmas. Grain enclosed within a thin, not adnate hyaline pericarp, ellipsoidal to subglobose, trigonous in section, ornamented, embryo basal, nearly circular; hilum basal, punctiform.

About nine species, distributed mostly in E and NE tropical Africa; one species pantropical and one commonly cultivated; two species in China; two species (one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Deciduous shrubs, glabrous or hairy, usually prickly. Leaves digitately compound; stipules wanting or very weakly developed. Inflorescence of many-flowered umbels, solitary, few together, or forming large terminal panicles. Flowers perfect or polygamous; pedicels slightly or not articulate under the flower. Calyx-margin entire or with 5 minute teeth. Petals (4–)5, valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as petals. Ovary 2–5-locular; styles 2–5, distinct or connate at the base. Fruit laterally compressed or subglobose, 2–5-seeded; seeds compressed; endosperm uniform.

About 40 species in E Asian and Himalayan region, one extending to the Philippines, Malay Peninsula; 18 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Leaves opposite, petiolate or sessile, serrate or crenate. Verticillasters forming secund or terete spikes or sometimes in panicles; bracts ovate or flabellate to lanceolate or linear. Calyx campanulate or cylindric, 5‑toothed; teeth subequal or anterior 2 longer. Corolla purplish, white or yellowish, shortly exserted, straight or incurved; limb 4‑ or 5‑lobed, obliquely 2‑lipped; upper lip erect, ± notched; lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed. Stamens 4, usually exserted, lower 2 longer, rarely undeveloped, free; filaments glabrous; anther cells 2, divergent or divaricate, apex confluent. Ovary glabrous. Style usually exserted beyond stamens, apex deeply to shallowly 2‑cleft; lobes subulate, sublinear or clavate, usually equal. Nutlets ovoid to oblong, glabrous or sparsely hairy, tuberculate or smooth.

About 40 species distributed in N temperate and warm parts of the Old World; 33 species in China, one species in Hong Kong.

Straggling shrubs or climbers, rarely erect or arborescent. Leaves alternate and sometimes distichous, petiolate, entire or serrate. Inflorescence terminal or lateral, paniculate, racemose or subumbellate, bracteate at base. Flowers generally unisexual or functionally unisexual (plant dioecious, polygmo-dioecious or monoecious), 4 –5-merous. Calyx deeply split. Corolla lobes almost free or shortly united at base, imbricate or quincuncial. Stamens usually adnate to corolla, rarely free; filaments distinct, slender; anthers opening by longtitudinal slits. Ovary globose or ovoid; style cylindrical; stigma capitate or discoid, sometimes slightly lobed. Fruit a fleshy drupe, 1-seeded, with crustaceous or rarely bony endocarp; endosperm ruminate; embryo terete, transverse.

A pantropical genus with about 140 species; 15 species in China; six species native to Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, usually somewhat glaucous. Leaves alternate, mainly clustered at base, lobed or not, cauline leaves few, entire, toothed to pinnatifid, base amplexicaul. Capitula homogamous and discoid, solitary or several arranged as loose corymbs with long peduncles, head pendulous before flowering stage. Involucres cylindric and swollen at base, without calycules; phyllaries 8–10 in one series, linear‑oblong, coherent but separate later when aged or upon dried, length elongate after anthesis. Receptacle flat and naked, alveolate. Florets many, all bisexual and fertile, corolla filiform‑tubular, gradually and slightly dilated at summit, apex 5‑lobed, colour yellow, pink, purple or red; anther bases obtuse, with narrow apical appendages, stylar branches long, apices truncate and penicillate. Cypselae subterete, truncate at both distal ends, 5‑angulate or ribbed. Pappus capillary and slender, copious, white.

About 100 species native to Asia and tropical Africa primarily, few in America; three species (one cultivated) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, more or less scaly-tomentose. Leaves alternate, entire, pinnately-veined, sometimes peltate; stipules small, caducous; petioles usually biglandular at apex. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious), apetalous. Male flowers almost sessile, in panicles; calyx cupular, shallowly (3–)5-lobed; stamens 5–12, 2–3-whorled, inserted in elevated receptacle, filaments short, free; anthers 2-celled; disk shallowly lobed; pistillode absent. Female flowers in racemes or sometimes shortly branched; calyx cupular, shallowly 3–5-lobed; disk annular; ovary 2–6-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles very short, reduced to a subsessile disk-shaped stigma. Capsules drupaceous, pericarp slightly fleshy, the endocarp of two indehiscent cocci.

About ten species occurring from China through Malaysia, New Guinea to tropical Australia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Trees, monoecious or rarely dioecious. Leaves alternate, usually even-pinnate. Flowers unisexual. Male flowers arranged in pendulous catkin, with a 3-lobed bract; sepals 1– 4, rarely absent; stamens 3 –15, anthers glabrous or pubescent. Female flowers arranged in erect or pendulous spikes, subtended by an enlarged, 3-lobed bract; bract adnate to base of ovary; sepals 4, adnate to ovary; ovary 1-locular; style short or absent; stigmas 2-lobed, with 2 or 4 plumose branches, or short and 4-lobed. Fruit a 3-winged nutlet, (2–)4-chambered at base. Persistent bract enlarged, membranous.

About 12 species distributed in S and SE Asia, N India; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, deciduous or semi-deciduous, with whorled branches. Leaves spirally arranged, crowded towards apex of branches, serrate or subentire. Inflorescence terminal, umbellate or racemose, in precocious umbels or serotinous corymbose-racemes, with nodding flowers. Calyx small, 5-lobed. Corolla campanulate or urceolate, shortly 5-lobed, and marked at base by 5 nectariferous almost pellucid pits. Stamens 10, included; filaments flattened, distinctly dilated towards base; anthers 2-awned at apex, opening by short slits. Ovary superior, 5-locular; style slender; stigma entire. Capsule hard, 5-angled, opening loculicidally in 5-valves.

12 species restricted to E Asia from E Himalaya through China to Japan; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Large woody climbers or scandent shrubs, usually unarmed. Stipules small, setaceous. Leaves bipinnate; petiolar glands absent; terminal pair of pinnae sometimes transformed into tendril; leaflets opposite, 1–many pairs, small and numerous. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, 5-merous, sessile, in slender spikes, solitary or forming raceme-like panicles, axillary or supra-axillary. Calyx campanulate, shortly dentate. Petals free or slightly united at base. Stamens 10, shortly connate at the base and adnate to petals, exserted; anthers with a deciduous gland at apex; filaments filiform. Ovary subsessile; ovules numerous; style filiform; stigma minute. Pods large and long, straight or curved to spirally twisted, plano-compressed, leathery or woody, valves splitting transversely at maturity into 1-seeded segment; segments falling away from the suture, which persists as an empty frame. Seeds large, globular to orbicular, testa thick, brown.

Approximately 30 species mainly in tropical Africa & America; two species and one variety in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual herbs. Culms ± compressed. Leaf blades linear to filiform, apex tapering; ligule short, ciliate. Spikes unilateral, slender, single or 2–several digitately arranged, with biseriate, sessile, imbricate and awned spikelets. Spikelets lanceolate, dorsally compressed, 2(–3)-flowered, lowermost floret fertile, second male or neuter floret sometimes present, uppermost floret reduced to a rudimentary awned lemma at rachilla apex; rachilla articulating above the glumes, protruding and sometimes bearing a reduced floret; glumes shorter or as long as florets, lanceolate to subulate, membranous, 1-veined, apex acute to shortly awned; lemma of fertile floret broadly rounded to almost flat on back, subleathery, raised, scabrous, 3-veined, apex 2-toothed, midvein protruding into a slender awn; callus bearded, blunt; palea equalling the lemma, 2-keeled. Caryopsis narrowly elliptic, dorsally compressed; pericarp free.

About 19 species distributed throughout the tropics; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs erect or prostrate. Leaves alternate, entire or toothed. Capitula disciform, heterogamous. Involucres hemispherical to globose; phyllaries in several series, inner layers longer and narrower, imbricate. Receptacle naked. Marginal florets female and fertile, many‑seriate, corolla tubular with apex 2–3‑lobed; stylar branches exserted. Disk florets bisexual and sterile, fewer in numbers, corolla tubular, apically 4–5‑lobed; style subulate, entire or shortly bifid; stamens 4–5, anther base sagittate, caudate. Cypselae obovoid‑oblong, 5–10‑ribbed, hairy at base. Pappus absent.

About 17 species in Africa, America, Australia and SE Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubby, unarmed succulent plants. Stems upright, often cylindric and woody at the base. Branches flat, 2-edged, with sunken areoles on the edges. Flowers usually large and nocturnal, solitary, arising from areoles; perianth united into a long tube; segments linear lanceolate, white, red or yellow; stamens many, borne on the throat of perianth tube; ovary solitary, style 9 –19-cleft. Fruit a berry, ellipsoid or globose, red or purple, bearing a few bracts.

About 16 species native to tropical and subtropical regions of America; four species (introduced) in China; one cultivated in Hong Kong.

Saprophytic herbs; rhizome coralloid; flowering stems yellow-brown, bracteate. Flowers pink-white, in a terminal raceme, pendant on curved pedicel; sepals and petals similar, distinct, lanceolate, 1.5 × 0.2 cm; lip slightly widened, simple, fleshy, lateral lobes erect, with a conspicuous callus running throughout the middle; spur stout; column short, no foot; anther terminal, grooved on the back; filaments evident; pollinia 2, stipe elongate and curved at the apex, with slender stipe and a viscidium.

Two species widespread in temperate Eurasia, Australia, tropical Africa; both occurring in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Lianas; stems robust, suffrutescent or woody, adhering to trees or rocks by means of aerial roots. Leaves alternate; petiole long, sheathing at base, articulate at apex; leaf blade large, entire, pinnatifid or pinnatisect, with perforations along the midrib or not. Inflorescence axillary, solitary. Peduncle robust. Spathe ovate-cymbiform, apex acute or acuminate, deciduous; spadix sessile, elongate, cylindrical. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, without perianth. Stamens 4(–6); filaments linear, flat; anthers much shorter than filaments; ovary polygonal-cylindrical, apex truncate; 1-locular, with 2–4 ovules. Berries small, not confluent.

About 20 species in tropical Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms usually tufted. Leaf blades narrowly linear; ligule usually reduced to a ciliate rim, rarely membranous. Inflorescence an open, contracted, sometimes spike-like or even head-like panicle. Spikelets laterally compressed, 2–manyflowered, rarely only 1 fertile floret with sterile lemma above it; rachilla zigzag, or straight, tough or gradually breaking up at maturity, in the former case florets deciduous or paleae persistent; in the latter case florets deciduous with adjacent internode of rachilla; glumes mostly subequal, 1(–3)-veined; lemmas membranous to leathery, keeled or rounded, glabrous to asperulous or rarely hairy, 3-veined or the veins sometimes very faint and occasionally suppressed, apex entire, obtuse to acuminate, rarely mucronate; palea equalling lemma or shorter, keels sometimes winged or ciliate, deciduous with lemmas or tardily dropping off; lodicules 2. Stamens 2–3. Ovary glabrous; styles 2, short, stigmas exserted laterally. Fruit enclosed in lemma, globose, ellipsoidal or oblong, usually a caryopsis but sometimes the pericarp free; hilum punctiform, basal.

About 350 species distributed mainly in the tropics and subtropics; 32 species (one introduced) in China; 14 species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or perennial erect herbs. Leaves petiolate, margin entire or crenate, pinnately‑veined. Inflorescences of lax, terminal or rarely axillary spikes, sometimes several forming a panicle. Bracts large, leaf‑like, usually coloured; bracteoles small, narrow. Calyx 5‑lobed, lobes narrow, unequal. Corolla hypocrateriform, tube quite long, slender, limb 5‑lobed, lobes obovate, subequal, imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, inserted below the throat; anther 2‑thecous, thecae parallel. Staminodes 2, clavate or filiform. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform, glabrous or pubescent; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal. Capsule clavate, with a solid stalk at base, retinacula present, 4‑seeded. Seeds compressed, discoid, ringed with hygroscopic hairs.

About 30 species in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia; four species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs; stem stout and erect, branched. Leaves alternate, subentire, toothed or pinnatisect. Capitula heterogamous and disciform, calyculate, arranged as paniculate corymbs at terminal. Involucres cylindric and swollen at base, phyllaries in 1 row, linear or lanceolate, herbaceous with margin scarious. Receptacle flat or slightly concave, naked. All florets fertile. Peripheral florets pistillate, corolla filiform‑tubular, 2‑seriate, apex 2–5‑lobed at apex. Central florets hermaphrodite, narrow and long funnelform‑tubular, 4–5‑toothed; anther bases obtuse; stylar branches elongate with apices truncate or obtuse, pubescent. Cypselae linear‑oblong, pale brown, ribbed. Pappus bristles soft capillary, many‑seriate.

About 15 species mainly distributed in America and Australia; two species naturalized in China; one species in Hong Kong. Erechtites hieracifolius (L.) Raf. ex DC. (梁子菜) was recorded previously.

Perennial herbs. Culms slender, erect or decumbent at base, sometimes stoloniferous. Leaf sheaths ± compressed; leaf blades linear, flat or folded; ligule short, membranous. Inflorescence a solitary terminal raceme; raceme strongly flattened, axis elongate. Pedicellate spikelets reduced to only a pedicel; sessile spikelets dorsally compressed, 2-floret, overlapping along one side of rachis; rachis internodes narrowly clavate; lower glume elliptic-ovate to oblong, papery to leathery, marginally 2-keeled, keels pectinately spiny with comb-like spines; upper glume slightly boat-shaped, 3-veined; lower floret staminate, palea present; stamens 3; upper floret bisexual or female, upper lemma entire, awnless. Caryopsis oblong.

About 11 species distributed in Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia and Australia; five species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic herbs. Roots many and long. Pseudobulbs crowded. Leaves 1–4 to each pseudobulb, coriaceous or chartaceous. Flowers medium-sized or small, non-resupinate, in a terminal raceme, rarely solitary (due to reduction); sepals subequal in length, the odd one symmetrical, concave, the lateral sepals oblique, adnate to the foot of the column forming a mentum; petals similar to or narrower than the sepals; lip 3-lobed, attached to the end of the column foot, recurved, the sides erect, the midlobe lamellate; column short, broad, winged, the base produced into a straight or curved foot; clinandrium truncate or sinuate; rostellum obtuse; anther terminal, incumbent, concave; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, waxy, obovoid, pyriform, the apex coherent slightly by a viscid mass; stigma suborbicular, or the lower margin 3-lobed; ovary subcylindrical or obovoid. Capsules oblong, ridged.

About 370 species distributed in tropical Asia and Oceania; 43 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Perennials. Leaf blade narrow, mostly rolled and needle-like; ligule a fringe of hairs. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, open or contracted, with solitary, pedicellate spikelets. Spikelets all alike, 2-floret, disarticulating below each floret; rachilla very short, without extension; glumes subequal, rounded on the back, 1/2 as long to much exceeding the florets, papery with hyaline or scarious margins; floret callus short, obtuse; lemmas pilose, grooved or smooth, acute or more often awned; paleae usually similar to lemmas in texture and indumentum, entire or bidentate, keels rounded, sometimes excurrent into awns. Stamens (2–)3. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, dorsally compressed.

About 40 species mainly in Australia, with a few species spreading into S and SE Asia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Mostly perennial herbs or subshrubs. Stem erect or prostrate. Leaves alternate, entire, toothed or pinnately lobed. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, solitary or few arranged into racemes, corymbs or panicles. Involucre hemispherical or campanulate; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, lanceolate or linear; receptacle plane or convex, without palea, alveolate. Ray florets 2–many‑seriate, pistillate, fertile, corolla variable, some with short tube and long ligule, others with long tube and short ligule, white, blue, purple or pink in colour, rarely yellow. Disk florets tubular, in form of tube to funnel, perfect, corolla mostly yellow, limb with 5 triangular lobes, lobes sometimes tinged purple; anther bases obtuse or slightly acute, entire, apical appendages ovate‑lanceolate. Cypsela compressed, margin ribbed; pappus bristles either long and uniform or long and short mixed.

About 200 species, cosmopolitan, especially in temperate regions of N America; 35 species in China; one species (naturalized) in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, unarmed. Leaves large, alternate, simple, serrate or dentate, rarely entire, petiolate or nearly subsessile, with conspicuous parallel veins ending in the teeth; stipules free or rarely intrapetiolarly connate, lanceolate. Inflorescence a terminal compound panicle or corymb. Flowers bisexual, 5-merous. Hypanthium obconical, elongated above the ovary, open at the top. Sepals 5, small, acute, erect or spreading, persistent. Petals 5, white, clawed, contorted or imbricate in buds, obovate or orbicular, usually notched, margin sinuate. Stamens 15 – 20( –40), anthers rounded. Ovary inferior, 2 – 5-loculed, with 2 erect ovules in each locule; styles 2–5, usually connate at base, villous; stigmas capitate. Fruit a fleshy pome, crowned by persistent incurved sepals, fleshy or dry, endocarp thin, with 1 or 2 large seeds.

About 26 species in SE and E Asia; 14 species in China; two species (one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Aquatic or marsh herbs, perennial or annual. Leaves linear, all radical or crowded on a short stem. Scapes 3–8-ribbed, with 1 sheathing scale or short leaf at the base and a terminal head. Flowers sessile, in unisexual, in androgynous heads, with imbricate bract 1 under each flower, and a few outer ones empty. Male flowers: sepals 2–3, usually connate into an abaxially split tube, rarely free; petals basally connate and funnelform, apex ± 2–3-lobed, usually with a black gland, margin usually ciliate; stamens 4–6, in 2 whorls; anthers 2-celled. Female flowers: sepals 2–3, free or rarely connate at base; petals 3 or absent, margin ciliate, with or without a black gland at apex; ovary 1–3-locular, style single, with 2 or 3 stigmas. Capsule 2–3-valved, dehiscent loculicidally.

About 400 species distributed mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; 35 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect or decumbent at base. Leaf blades linear, flat or rolled; ligule a fringe of short hairs. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, composed of racemes arranged on all sides along a central axis, spikelets pedicellate, single, paired or clustered on a narrow rachis. Spikelets lanceolate to elliptic, thinly biconvex, subcartilaginous, with acute to aristate apex and bead-like swelling at base, 2-flowered; lower glume vestigial; upper glume equalling spikelet, facing outward, often awn-pointed; lower lemma present or absent, neuter or staminate, with or without palea; upper lemma always shorter than spikelets, crustaceous, papillose, margins inrolled, apex obtuse and often mucronate. Caryopsis free between indurate upper lemma and upper palea, ellipsoidal, dorsally compressed.

About 30 species distributed in tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world, especially tropical Africa and America; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect or suberect herbs or subshrubs, roots often tuberous. Stems simple or little branched. Stipules linear or linear-lanceolate, stipels absent. Leaves pinnately 1 – 3-foliolate. Racemes very short, 1 – 2-flowered, axillary. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed. Corolla extended out of calyx; vexillum obovate, auriculate at base, pubescent on abaxial surface; wings and keel shorter. Stamens diadelphous (9+1); anthers uniform. Ovary sessile, 2-ovuled; styles filiform, glabrous; stigma capitate, small. Pods compressed, rhomboid-elliptic or oblong. Seeds 1 – 2, oblique, funicle attached the end of linear hilum, estrophiolate.

About 130 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mostly in tropical America and E Africa; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody or scandent shrubs. Stems lenticellate, young parts glabrous or reddish tomentose. Leaves petiolate, entire, leathery or papery. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate; bracts caducous, usually minute. Flowers small, fragrant. Sepals free, persistent, subequal, leathery, usually pubescent abaxially. Corolla white or yellow, campanulate, deeply 5‑lobed; tube short, glabrous abaxially; lobes 2‑lobulate apically, midpetaline bands densely appressed pubescent abaxially; lateral lobules glabrous. Stamens inclusive; pollen grains not spiny. Disk inconspicuous. Ovary globose or ellipsoidal, 1‑locular, 4‑ovuled. Styles absent or nearly so. Stigma ± conical, with 5–10 longitudinal, straight or spirally twisted ridges. Fruit a slightly fleshy berry. Seed 1.

About 67 species mainly distributed in S & SE Asia, N Australia; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Biennial or perennial herbs, usually glabrous; stems arising from stout taproots or rootstocks bearing fibrous roots. Leaves simple, entire or pinnately or palmately lobed to divided, often ciliate to spinose; petioles sheathing. Umbels simple, head-like, solitary, or in cymes or racemes. Involucre of one or more series of entire or lobed bracts. Flowers bisexual, sessile, each subtended by a bracteole. Calyx-teeth ovate to lanceolate, acute to obtuse, entire or rarely spinescent. Petals white to purple, ovate to oblong, with variously inflexed and lobed to fimbriate tips. Styles shorter than to extending sepals. Stylopodium and carpophore absent. Fruit globose to obovoid, scarely flattened laterally, variously covered with scales or tubercles; ribs obsolete; commissure broad; vittae mostly 5, inconspicuous. Seed subterete in cross section, the face plane or slightly concave.

About 220 species widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions of both hemispheres; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Stems and branches often armed with thorns. Stipules small; stipels gland-like. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; indumentum sometimes stellate. Racemes axillary and leafless or terminal and leafy at base. Flowers very showy, often appearing before or with few new leaves, mostly scarlet, paired or clustered on the rhachis. Bracts and bracteoles small or absent. Calyx truncate, split or more or less 5-toothed; vexillum large or elongated, erect or spreading, subsessile or long-clawed, not appendaged; wings short, sometimes very small or absent; keel much smaller than vexillum, longer or shorter than wings. Stamens 10; vexillary stamens free or connate only at base, the remainder connate to the middle; anthers uniform. Ovary stalked; ovules numerous; style incurved, not barbate, stigma small, terminal. Pods stalked, linear, falcate, constricted or sinuate between the seeds, 2-valved or follicularly dehiscent by the ventral suture, rarely indehiscent. Seeds ovoid, hilum lateral, oblong, estrophiolate.

About 2000 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of both hemisphere; five species in China; three species in Hong Kong. Erythrina caffra Thunb. (南非刺桐) is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, often containing tanniferous resin. Leaves simple, often polymorphic with different juvenile and mature forms, sometimes with intermediate forms; leaves of juvenile plants opposite, shortly petiolate or sessile, often glandular hairy; leaves of adult plants alternate, petiolate, often with pellucid dots. Inflorescence an umbel or panicle, axillary or terminal. Flowers bisexual, pedicellate or sessile. Hypanthium campanulate, obconic, or semiglobose, apex usually truncate. Sepals rarely distinct. Petals connate, either adnate to sepals into a 1-layered calyptra or not adnate to sepals and then forming a 2-layered calyptra; calyptra deciduous at anthesis. Stamens many, usually distinct, in several whorls; anthers 2-celled, parallel or bifurcate, dehiscing by longitudinal slits or occasionally by apical pores. Ovary adnate to hypanthium, 3–6-locular; ovules many per locule. Style persistent. Capsule completely or partly included in the expanded hypanthium. Seeds many, mostly sterile, developed seeds ovoid or angular; testa rigid, sometimes enlarged into wings.

About 700 species mainly distributed in Australia; about 110 species cultivated in China; six species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, pinnately-veined, petiolate. Flowers bisexual, solitary or clustered at axils of leaves, 4-merous. Hypanthium short. Calyx-lobes 4. Petals 4. Stamens many; anthers parallel, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary 2–3-locular; ovules many per locule. Fruit a berry, with persistent sepals at apex; pericarp thin, separating from testa. Seed usually 1, testa smooth, sometimes bony; embryo straight, fleshy.

About 100 species mostly distributed in tropical America, a few in Africa, S and SE Asia, Australia, New Caledonia, and the Pacific Islands; five species introduced to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual herbs. Culms tufted, usually erect, rarely stoloniferous. Leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate; ligule short, membranous, margin ciliolate. Inflorescence terminal, composed of several to many racemes inserted digitately; racemes elongate with many spikelet pairs, hairy, sessile and pedicellate spikelets of a pair similar, pedicellate spikelets finally falling off entirely from the pedicel, sessile spikelets falling off with adjacent internode, rarely shortly pedicellate and then falling from pedicel; rachis internodes linear, ciliate along angles. Spikelets lanceolate to narrowly oblong, dorsally compressed; callus short, bearded; glumes cartilaginous to leathery; lower glume flat or slightly concave, hairy; upper glume boat-shaped, 1-keeled down midline; upper lemma linear to oblong, shortly 2-toothed or 2-lobed to middle, awned; awn geniculate; palea small or absent.

About 30 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; 14 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial or saprophytic herbs. Rhizomes lumpy, large, with concentric rings. Scapes aphyllous, appearing before the leaves, 50–150 cm tall, with many scales. Flowers large or medium-sized, in terminal loose racemes; sepals equal, spreading, the odd one free, the lateral ones attached to the side of the column foot; petals shorter and broader or narrower than the sepals, spreading; lip 3-lobed, attached to the column, slightly contracted at the base and produced into a spur, lateral lobes erect, midlobe broad, almost entire, disk cristate or lamellate; column rather long, with a foot; clinandrium strongly oblique; rostellum subtruncate; anther terminal, incumbent, semi-globose, produced into an obtuse-conical or bilobed appendage; pollinia 2 pairs, waxy, on a short stipe with viscidium at the base; stigma suborbicular or transversely broad; ovary cylindrical. Capsules oblong, pendulous, ridged.

About 200 species distributed in Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia, America and Australia, but mainly in Africa; 14 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, rarely scandent, glabrous, rarely pubescent. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate or whorled, entire, serrulate, or spinose-denticulate. Cymes axillary, dichotomous or trichotomous. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual and dioecious or gynodioecious, 4–5-merous. Calyx green. Corolla white or yellow-green, rarely purple. Stamens attached on disk; stamens 4–5, introrse or latrorse, longitudinally or obliquely dehiscent. Ovary 4–5-locular, ovules 2(–12) per locule; styles single, short and thick, stigma entire or lobed. Capsules subspheroidal or obovoid, smooth or echinate, angular, deeply lobed, or laterally winged, loculicidally dehiscent. Seeds 1-several, nearly enclosed in scarlet or yellow arils.

About 200 species in N temperate regions, especially in Asia and Australia; 111 species in China; six species in Hong Kong. E. glaber Roxb., E. japonicus var. albomarginatus T. Moort are occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong but not described here.

Annual or perennial herbs, shrubs or subshrubs. Leaves mostly opposite. Capitula homogamous, clustered in a terminal, often loose, panicle or corymb. Involucres oblong, cylindric or campanulate; phyllaries multi‑seriate or in 1–2 series only, imbricate, the outer ones smaller or all with subequal length. Receptacles small, flat or slightly convex, without palea. All florets tubular, corolla usually with apical portion broaden, regularly 5‑lobed, white to pink or purple; stamens 5, anther bases entire and rounded, bearing apical appendages; ovary 5‑angled, stylar branches very long, linear‑subcylindric, sometimes slightly enlarged at the distal end. Cypselae 5‑angulate, truncate at the apex; pappus setae numerous, scabrid, 1‑seriate.

More than 600 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of C & S America; 14 species in China; four species growing wild in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, with milky juice, rarely succulent leafless cactoid shrubs. Stem-leaves alternate, without stipules, the flowering branches, umbellate, dichotomous, with usually opposite leaves; or all the leaves opposite and often stipulate. Flowers unisexual, in cyathia subtended by calyx-like, cup-shaped involucre, within including 10–15 male flowers, and a single female flower in the centre; involucre with 4–5 entire or laciniate lobes, regular or nearly so, with glands between the lobe, sometime bearing petal-like appendages. Male flowers consisting each of a single stamen with an articulated filament; anther-cells 2, globose. Female flowers reduced to a stipitate 3-locular ovary protruding from the involucre, with 1 pendulous ovule in each locule; style 3, free or connate, simple or bifid. Capsules divided into 3 bivalved cocci.

On a broad concept applied here, the genus Euphorbia contains about 2000 species dispersed over nearly the whole world; over 80 species in China; 11 species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, dioecious. Leaves leathery, distichous, usually serrulate, petiolate. Flowers unisexual, small, axillary, solitary or clustered, sessile or shortly pedicellate; bracteoles 2, lying close to sepals; sepals 5, imbricate, persistent; petals 5, white, slightly connate at base; male flowers: stamens 5–35; filaments linear, glabrous, free or adnate to the base of petals; anthers basifixed, 2-celled, connective slightly exserted; vestigial pistil conspicuous; female flowers: ovary superior, 3 – 5-locular, with axile placenta, ovules 3 – 60 per locule; styles 3 – 5, free or connate proximally. Fruit baccate, globose, ovoid or ellipsoid, 2–60 seeds per locule. Seeds globose, black and shining, foveolatepitted; endosperm fleshy, embryo recurved.

About 130 species, E & SE Asia, Indo-malesia, SW Pacific Islands; 81 species in China; eight species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees; young branches and leaves stellate-pubescent. Leaves alternate, petiolate; stipules minute, caducous; leaf blade leathery, pinnately veined. Inflorescence racemose, terminal, pedunculate, subtended by 2 general bracts. Flowers bisexual. Floral cup turbinate, stellate-tomentose. Sepals 5. Petals 5, small, yellow, scale-like. Stamens 5, opposite to sepals, filaments very short; thecae 2-sporangiate, dehiscent into 2 valves; staminodes absent. Ovary inferior, 2-locular; ovules 1 per locule; styles long; stigmas very large, spathulate, verrucose. Capsules ovoid-globose, woody, dehiscing loculicidally. Seeds ovoid.

Three species distributed in China, Vietnam; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, subshrubs, or shrubs. Stems erect, scandent, but never twining. Leaves petiolate or sessile; leaf blade small, entire. Flowers 1 to few, pedicellate or sessile in leaf axils; bracts tiny. Sepals distinct, equal or subequal, not enlarged after flowering. Corolla rotate, funnelform, or salverform; limb ± entire to 5‑lobed, midpetaline bands often pilose abaxially. Stamens inclusive or exserted; pollen grains not spiny. Disk cupular or absent. Ovary glabrous or pilose, (1–)2‑locular; ovules 2 per locule. Styles 2, filiform, distinct or united basally, each 2‑cleft; stigma filiform, terete or slightly clavate. Capsule globose or ovoid, usually 2–4‑valved. Seeds 1–4, smooth or minutely tuberculate, glabrous.

About 100 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions throughout the world, mainly in N & S America; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems erect, branched. Leaves opposite. Cymes axillary or terminal, paniculate. Flowers 4 – 5‑merous. Calyx lobed nearly to base, lobes with keeled ridges abaxially or winged. Corolla rotate, deeply lobed. Stamens inserted at throat of corolla tube just below sinus between corolla lobes; filaments very short; anthers ellipsoidal, 2‑celled, dehiscing by apical pores. Ovary 2‑locular, without glands at base; style linear; stigma small. Capsules 2‑valved, many‑seeded. Seed coat warty.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Africa, Madagascar, tropical and subtropical Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees; branchlets with swollen nodes and annular stipular scars at each node. Leaves alternate, long-petiolate; stipules large, bract-like, coherent, caducous; leaf blade palmately 3 –5-lobed, leathery, palmately veined. Inflorescence capitate, axillary, pedunculate, 7–16-flowered. Flowers bisexual. Floral cup adnate to ovary base. Petals 2–5 or absent, white, linear. Stamens 10 –15; filaments subulate or filiform; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary semi-inferior; ovules 5 or 6 per locule; styles 2. Infructescences globose or subglobose. Capsules dehiscing loculicidally by 4 valves; exocarp usually smooth, sometimes tuberculate. Seeds 5–7 in each locule, upper 4 or 5 sterile and wingless, lower 1 or 2 fertile and narrowly winged.

Four species distributed in Bhutan, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, with milky juice. Leaves alternate or opposite, petiolate, pinnately-veined. Flowers apetalous, unisexual (plant dioecious, rarely monoecious), in axillary or terminal recemes or spikes. Male flowers: 1–2 in axils of bracts; sepals (2–)3, small, imbricate; stamens 3, filaments free, anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent; pistillode absent. Female flowers: calyx 3-lobed or 3-partite; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles slightly connate at base. Capsules subglobose, obtusely 3-angled, divided into 2-valved cocci; column persistent; seeds globose, testa crustaceous; albumen fleshy.


About 40 species in Asia, Africa and Oceania; six species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

records.authority: (I. C. Nielsen) Barneby & J. W. Grimes
records.text:
Unarmed trees. Stipules caducous. Leaves bipinnate, pinnae 6–20 pairs; leaflets numerous, subsessile, opposite. Inflorescence of few-flowered spikes, axillary, solitary or forming efoliate panicles. Flowers homomorphic, sessile. Calyx broadly campanulate or hemispherical, 5(–6)-toothed. Corolla sericeous, lobes as many as calyx-teeth, proximal 1/4 connate into a tube. Stamens numerous, with an intrastaminal disk around the base of ovary. Pods firmly papery, broad-linear, straight, plano-compressed, narrowly winged along ventral suture, late dehiscent through both sutures; testa hard, with pleurogram.

Three species in Moluccas, New Guinea, Solomon Island and Queensland; one species cultivated in China; and also in Hong Kong.

Evergreen perennial herbs; stem scapose. Leaves radical and rosulate, rolling inward as first when in young stage, leaf blade reniform, cordate or fan‑shaped, palmately‑veined, densely hairy when young; petioles long and swollen at base. Cauline leaves absent or appeared as bracts. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, arranged as loose corymbs. Involucres campanulate to turbinate, calyculate at base; phyllaries 1‑seriate, with scarious margin. Receptacle plain, alveolate, shallowly pitted, denticulate along areole margin. Peripheral florets in 1 row, female, corolla ligulate. Disk florets many, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular and 5‑lobed at apex; anther bases sagittate, apical appendages obtuse, oblong; stylar branches rounded or truncate at distal ends, penicillate hairy. Cypselae cylindric, ribbed and hairy. Pappus setae copious, white.

A genus consisting of one species native to E Asia; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Herbs, without latex. Stipules free, caducous. Leaves alternate, distichous, margin toothed. Inflorescences a lax cyme. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious), bracteolate. Male flowers: perianth 4-lobed; stamens 4, filament incurved in buds. Female flowers: perianth 4 – 6-lobed; ovary oblique; style slightly lateral, stigma 2-fid, filiform; ovules pendulous. Achenes small, oblique globose, slightly compressed, enclosed in persistent perianth, pericarpum slightly crustaceous. Seed coat membranaceous, without endosperm.

Two species distributed in E & SE Asia to Australia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or climbers, sometimes epiphytic, with milky juice. Stipules enclosing terminal bud, often caducous and leaving a scar. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, entire or lobed, venation pinnate, sometimes palmately 3–5-veined at base. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious or rarely dioecious), minute, enclosed within fleshy, globose, ellipsoid or obovoid receptacles (called fig or synoecium), solitary or in clusters of 2 or more, axillary or on scaly leafless shoots from trunk or major branches. Figs with a mouth (ostiole) at apex more or less closed by small bracts, sometimes bracts scattered over surface of fig or 2 in a whorl at base or on peduncle. Flowers of three kinds: male, female and gall flowers. Male flowers: usually near the mouth of fig, perianth 3 – 6-lobed, with 1–2 rarely more stamens. Female flowers: usually lining the greater part of cavity, perianth entire, or 2 or more lobes or segments; style usually lateral, with a more or less oblique, variously shaped stigma. Gall flowers: ovary occupied by the pupa of a hymenopterous insect; style short. Achenes enclosed within a common receptacle forming a syconium (fig).

About 1,000 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 99 species in China; 26 species, one subspecies and one variety in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials; rhizome absent or present, stoloniferous. Culms usually tufted, angled, trigonous or flattened. Leaves basal, blade or reduced to bladeless sheaths; blades linear to filiform, often canaliculate, often cellular-reticulate on upper surface, ligule sometimes present, pubescent or membranous. Involucral bracts leaf-like, setaceous or glume-like. Inflorescence simple to decompound, umbel-like or capitate or a single spikelet. Spikelets mostly ovoid or ellipsoidal, terete, angular or ± laterally flattened. Glumes few to many per spikelet, spirally arranged or all 2-ranked. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 1–3. Stigmas 2–3; style base not persistent on achenes. Achenes trigonous or biconvex, surface variously patterned.

Over 200 species mostly in the tropics and subtropics, with highest number in S Asia, Indochina and Malesia; 55 species in China; 27 species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves with long petioles, 3 – 5-lobed or entire, sometimes very large, often cordate, glabrous or covered with stellate hairs. Panicles axillary or terminal. Flowers unisexual or polygamous; calyx tubular, 5-lobed to middle or base, rarely 4-lobed. Petals absent; stamens ususally 10, anthers sessile or on short filaments, 2-celled, opening lengthwise; carpels 5, free; styles short; ovules 2 or more. Mature carpels stipitate, membranous, opening very early and dispersing with seeds adhering to the margins. Seeds globose, wrinkled when dry.

About 12 species distributed in tropical Asia, Africa and Madagascar; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches with simple hairs. Leaves leathery, pubescent or tomentose. Inflorescences terminal, leaf-opposed, or axillary; flowers in cymes or branched panicles. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 3, valvate in bud, basally connate. Petals 6, free, in 2 whorls, fleshy, with thickened ridges; outer and inner petals subequal; inner petals usually connivent, erect. Stamens numerous, extrorse; connective slightly prominent, obtuse, liguliform, pyramidal, or slightly apiculate, glabrous. Carpels few to many per flower; ovary hairy, free; ovules 2 or more per ovary, lateral, 2‑seriate; style not conspicuous; stigma ellipsoid or clavate, usually 2-cleft, glabrous or hairy. Fruits apocarpous; monocarps 1 – 20(–30) per fruit, globose to ellipsoid, glabrous to hairy; stipes 2–48 mm long; receptacles 2 – 13 mm in diam.; sepals caducous. Seeds 1– 12 per monocarp, lateral, 1–2-seriate, ellipsoid to lenticular; raphes conspicuous.

Approximately 60 species in SE Asia and NE Australia; approximately 22 species in China, and three in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious, rarely polygamous; trunk spiny or not; branchlets usually with axillary spines. Leaves alternate, margin usually serrate, rarely entire, pinnately veined, short-petioled; stipules usually absent. Inflorescence a raceme, terminal or axillary. Flowers small, unisexual, rarely bisexual. Sepals 4–7, slightly connate at base, imbricate. Petals absent. Disc fleshy, entire or divided into several glands. Male flower: stamens 15–many; anthers ellipsoid, longitudinally dehiscent; rudimentary ovary absent. Female flowers: incompletely 2–8-locular; ovules 2 per placenta; styles as many as placentas, free or united; stigmas slightly emarginate or 2-lobed. Fruit a berry-like drupe, globose. Seeds 1–2, obovoid.

About 15 to 17 species, distributed in tropical Asia and Africa; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or subshrubs. Stems erect or scandent. Leaves digitately 3-foliolate, rarely 1-foliolate; leaflets covered with small glands particularly on abaxial surface. Flowers in racemes, panicles or globose heads, terminal or axillary. Bracts distichous; bracteoles absent. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes longer than tube, usually glandular. Corolla greenish or yellowish; petals clawed; vexillum oblong or elliptic, auriculate; wings very narrow, usually adherent to incurved keel. Stamens diadelphous (9+1), the one opposite to vexillary free; anthers uniform. Ovary ellipsoidal, 2-ovuled; style filiform, glabrous or slightly hairy at base. Pods ellipsoidal, inflated, not septate, styles oblique and persistent. Seeds 1– 2, globose; hilum oval.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Asia, Africa and Australia, and about five species distributed from NE India to SE Asia; six species and one variety in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with long rhizomes; stems erect or ascending, usually creeping at the base. Leaves alternate. Flowers nearly regular, in terminal panicles; bracts often small. Sepals free, shallowly to strongly boat-shaped, leathery, persistent. Petals free, blue or purple, sometimes white, obovate, clawed. Stamens 6, equal, all fertile; filaments glabrous; anther-cells connate, slightly divergent proximally, ellipsoidal, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary constricted at the base or stalked, 2-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule. Capsule flattened, didymous, 2-valved. Seeds 1 per valve, hemispheric, reticulate or striate.

About 20 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; two species (one endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or treelets, usually unarmed. Leaves simple, alternate, often distichous, pinnately-veined, stipulate. Flowers small, dioecious, rarely monoecious, solitary or in fascicles; bracts obscure, apetalous. Male flowers: pedicels slender; sepals 4 – 7, imbricate, margin entire or serrulate; stamens 4 – 7, inserted at the base of disk and alternate with disk-glands, longer than calyx-lobes; filaments free; anther erect, extrorse, bilocular, longitudinally dehiscing; disk of 4–7 segments, these sometimes connivent or fused; rudimentary ovary small, 2 –3-lobed. Female flowers: pedicels terete or angled; sepals as in male flowers; disk saucer-shaped or patelliform, sometimes thickened, entire or lobed; ovary (2 – )3(– 4)-carpellate; styles free, spreading, bifid or entire; ovules hemitropous, 2 per locule. Capsules globose or triangular, dehiscent into 3 cocci or indehiscent and more or less baccate; columella and sepals persistent; seeds usually triangular, normally 2 per locule.

About 13 species widespread in tropical to temperate regions, especially in Africa, Asia, America and Europe; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, all parts strongly anise-scented; stem erect, grey-green, glabrous. Leaves petiolate, pinnately decompound; ultimate segments filiform or linear. Inflorescence of compound umbels, terminal and lateral; bracts and bracteoles absent; rays numerous, upwards-spreading, unequal. Calyx-teeth obsolete. Petals yellow, obovate, midvein conspicuous, apex narrowly incurved. Stylopodium conic; styles very short, reflexed. Fruit oblong, laterally ± compressed, glabrous; ribs 5, acute or round-obtuse; vittae 1 in each furrow, 2 on commissure. Seed face plane or slightly concave. Carpophore 2-cleft to base.

One species in Mediterranean region, cultivated and naturalized worldwide; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrublets, erect or creeping. Stems quadrangular, sometimes fleshy. Leaves opposite, petiolate to almost sessile, margin usually denticulate or serrulate, (3–)5–7(–9)-basiveined, lateral veins parallel. Inflorescences terminal, umbellate or cymose paniculate, bracteate at the base of peduncle. Flowers 4-merous. Pedicel usually quadrangular, 2-bracteolate. Calyx-tube obconical or funnelform, membranous, 4-sided or 8-veined; calyx-lobes usually triangular, membranous, caducous. Petals pink, red, purple, or rarely white, oblong to obovate, apex oblique; stamens 8, unequal; 4 longer stamens usually pink to purplish red, anthers oblong to oblong-linear, longer than filaments, opening by 1 apical pore, base lengthened and forked, connective sometimes raised at base; 4 shorter stamens pale yellow or white, anthers oblong, 2/3 or 1/2 shorter than filaments, base usually not forked. Ovary inferior, obconical, apex with a membranous 4-lobed crown. Fruit capsular, obconical, apex truncate, opening by 4 apical pores; persistent calyx 8-ribbed.

About eight species distributed in China and Vietnam; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Young branches green, slightly compressed and ridged, spines axillary or without spines. Leaves unifoliolate, rarely simple, with many glandular dots. Flowers solitary or several-fasciculate in leaf axils, bisexual. Calyx 4–5-lobed. Petals 5, imbricate. Stamens 3–4 times as many as petals, filaments connate into 4–5 bundles, with a few distinct. Disk slightly prominent. Ovary globose or ellipsoidal, 3–6(–8)-locular, ovules 1–2 per locule; styles long, stigmas large. Fruit globose, ovoid, ellipsoidal or pyriform; pericarp fleshy, glandular dots slightly prominent or not; pericarp and pulp acid or sweet. Seeds ovoid, base rounded, apex acute, smooth.

About six species distributed in SE Asia; five species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or rarely shrubs, deciduous or rarely evergreen. Winter buds scaly, rarely naked. Leaves odd‑pinnate, opposite; leaflets 3–20, margin usually serrate. Inflorescences paniculate, terminal or axillary towards end of branches, or lateral on branches of previous year; bracts linear to lanceolate, caducous or absent. Flowers small, unisexual, bisexual, or polygamous. Calyx 4‑toothed or irregularly lobed, sometimes absent. Corolla white to yellowish, 4‑lobed to base or absent. Stamens 2, inserted at base of corolla lobes; filaments short, exserted at anthesis. Ovules 2 in each locule, pendulous. Style short; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit a samara with apically elongate wing. Seeds usually 1(–2), ovate‑oblong; endosperm fleshy; radicle erect.

About 65 species mainly distributed in temperate regions and subtropics of N hemisphere, a few spreading to tropics regions; 27 species occur in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials often pubescent. Culms (3–)4–5-angular, nodose. Leaves mostly cauline; blade pubescent or glabrous, 3 – 5-veined; sheaths closed; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaf-like, sheathing at base, equalling or longer than inflorescence. Inflorescence paniculate, with few to many clusters of sessile spikelets at few to several nodes. Spikelets with many glumes. Glumes spirally imbricate, pubescent outside, usually shortly awned, 1–3-veined, the lowest 1–3 empty, Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments 3–6 in 1–2 whorls, each of 3 segments, outer whorl of simple bristles, sometimes absent, inner whorl of bristles, blades or claws. Stamens 2–3. Stigmas 3; style continuous with ovary. Achenes trigonous to triquetrous, apex beaked, base cuneate to stipitate, smooth to trabeculate.

About 30 species in the tropics with the high specific concentration in tropical Africa; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Robust perennials. Rhizome short, woody. Culms central. Leaves basal and cauline; blade linear; ligule present. Involucral bracts leaf-like. Inflorescence paniculate, with several to many partial inflorescence, each bearing many spikelets. Spikelets solitary or clustered, 1–2-flowered. Glumes several, spirally imbricate, upper 2–3 smaller than lower ones, the upper 1–2 bearing flowers. Flowers 1–2, the upper bisexual, the lower (when present) staminate or sterile. Perianth segments usually absent. Stamens (2–)3–6; filaments often elongate and persistent at base of achene. Stigmas (2–)3; style continuous with ovary. Achenes trigonous, 4-angular or terete.

About 30 species, the highest number in E Australia and New Zealand, several species in Malesia and two species in E Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial erect herbs. Leaves alternate and / or basal. Capitula large, long‑pedunculate, heterogamous and radiate, with marginal florets ligulate, neutral or sometimes female and fertile; disk florets tubular, bisexual and usually fertile. Or capitula homogamous with all florets bisexual. Involucres broad; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, imbricate. Receptacle convex to hemispherical, usually setose. Corolla of ray florets, if present, 3‑toothed at distal end, rarely entire; that of disk tubular florets 5‑cleft and bristly at apex; anther bases shortly sagittate, apical appendages acute‑ovate; stylar branches with elongate hirtelleous apical appendages. Cypselae turbinate, 5‑angulate. Pappus consisting of 5–10 aristate scales.

About 20 species native to S to C America; two species cultivated in Hong Kong. One is described below.

Perennial climbing or suberect herbs. Stipules small or deciduous. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, rarely 1–5- or 7-foliolate, stipellate. Racemes axillary; flowers remotely paired or fasciculate, or the lower ones subsolitary in axils of small setaceous bracts, rarely the lower flowers apetalous; bracteoles very small. Calyx deeply 4-lobed; lobes acuminate, the upper one broader, consisting of 2 completely united lobes, lateral ones smaller, lower one often longer. Corolla slightly exserted; vexillum ovate or orbicular, margins slightly inflexed at base or with appendage; wings narrow or obovate, adherent to keel; keel subequal to or longer than wings, not beaked. Stamens free; anthers uniform. Ovary subsessile; ovules numerous; styles filiform, not barbate; stigma small, terminal. Pods linear, compressed, straight or incurved, plano-compressed or rarely concave, 2-valved, thinly filled or subseptate between seeds. Seeds estrophiolate, rarely pods of lower apetalous flowers penetrating soil and ground. Seed 1.

About 140 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of America and Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Leaves opposite. Capitula small, radiate, heterogamous, usually arranged as loose corymbs. Involucres hemispherical or broad campanulate; phyllaries about 5 in 1–2 series, membranous or with the outer series thinly herbaceous. Receptacle conical or elongate, paleate. All florets fertile. Female ones 4–5 in one row, corolla ligulate, spreading, white, entire or 2–3‑lobed. Disk ones numerous bisexual, corolla tubular, yellow, apex 5‑lobed; anther bases sagittate with small auricles. Cypselae ribbed, obovate‑deltoid, pubescent. Pappus scarious, oblong and fimbriate.

About 14 species mainly native to tropical America; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems ± quadrangular, sometimes slightly woody at base. Leaves sessile, in whorls of 4, 6, or 8, of which some are stipules. Flowers small, in axillary or terminal trichotomous cymes or panicles. Calyx‑tube ovoid or globular, completely fused with ovary; limb inconspicuous. Corolla rotate; tube scarcely perceptible, (3–)4‑lobed; lobes valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes; filaments short; anthers exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style short, deeply 2‑cleft; stigma capitate. Fruit small, didymous, dry, indehiscent.

About 400 species spread over all temperate regions of the world; 58 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, usually with yellow resinous juice. Leaves opposite, entire. Cymes terminal or axillary, or flowers solitary. Flower unisexual, bisexual or polygamous; sepals and petals 4 –5, imbricate. Male flowers: stamens many, free or united into 1–5 bundles, surrounding pistillode; pistillodes sometimes absent; anthers dehiscing by longitudinally slits or apical pores. Female flowers: staminodes 8–many, free or united; ovary 2–12-locular; styles short or absent; stigma peltate, entire or divided, ovule 1 in each locule. Berries globose, with leathery pericarp. Seeds with succulent arils.

About 200 species distributed in tropical Asia and S Africa; 21 species in China; two species Hong Kong.

Shrubs, or rarely small trees. Leaves opposite, rarely in whorls of 3. Stipules intrapetiolar, often connate into a sheath, entire. Flowers usually rather large, terminal or axillary, solitary, or rarely clustered or in cymes. Calyx‑tube obconical, ribbed; limb 5–8‑lobed; lobes persistent. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric; lobes 5–12, contorted in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes and alternate with them, attached to the throat of corolla‑tube; anthers nearly sessile.
