Ovary 1‑locular; style stout; stigma clavate or fusiform; ovules numerous on 2 – 6 projecting parietal placentas. Fruit leathery or succulent, indehiscent, usually crowned by the calyx. Seeds numerous, compressed, with thin testa.

About 200 species in tropical and subtropical Asia & Africa; five species in China; one species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, scandent, mostly climbing or creeping, glabrous. Branchlets terete, sometimes with 4 faint ridges. Leaves opposite, entire, petiolate, connected by interpetiolar stipular rims. Flowers axillary, solitary, paired, or in cymes, when in cymes usually few‑flowered but sometimes grouped into a thyrse; bracts small, narrowly triangular. Flowers 4‑ or 5‑merous. Pedicels long. Calyx small, deeply lobed; lobes imbricate, connate, inside with colleters at base. Corolla rotate to nearly campanulate; tube thin, fleshy; lobes thin to thick, fleshy, valvate in bud. Stamens exserted; filaments very short, flat; anthers 2‑ or 4‑celled, connate or free, base 2‑parted, introrse. Ovary small, 2‑locular, with 1 – 4 ovules per locule; style mostly long, slender; stigma capitate or 2‑cleft. Berries red, globose, 1‑seeded or more. Seeds ellipsoidal to orbicular, concave on hilar side but convex on other side, seed coat thin; embryo tiny, almost cylindric; endosperm thick, horny.

Five species in E and SE Asia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual erect herbs. Leaf blades linear to linear-lanceolate, flat or involute, usually tuberculate-pilose; ligule short, membranous. Panicle open or contracted; spikelets 1-flowered, dorsally compressed, usually paired, often with a tuft of short stiff hairs at base; glumes subequal, the lower slightly longer, thinly herbaceous, 3-veined, acute to acuminate, awned or awnless; lemma membranous, 1–3-veined, apex entire or 2-toothed, awned or rarely awnless; palea hyaline membranous, margins ciliate, auriculate at base, 2-veined; lodicules 2, thin; stamens 3, anthers linear; ovary glabrous, styles 2, free, short. Caryopsis free, oblong or linear.

About 30 species widely spread over India and Nepal eastward through SE Asia to Polynesia, Hawaii, and Australia (Queensland); five species and one variety in China; two species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic herbs with monopodial growth. Roots many, thick and long. Stems rather short, covered by roots and remains of degenerated leaves. Leaves rather small, linear-lanceolate, wavy, acute. Scapes short, with 2 – 3 flowers. Flowers rather small, nonresupinate, few on an axillary raceme; sepals and petals subequal, free, spreading in form of a fan; lip undivided, attached to base of the column, broadly saccate, apex transversely dilated and bilobed, the sac smooth inside, without callus or keel; column short, stout, winged; clinandrium truncate; rostellum subulate, bifid; anther terminal, incumbent, convex, acuminate at the apex; pollinia 2, subglobose in appearance from the front, flattened and with a central depression on the back; stipe slender; viscidium bifid; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical. Capsules oblong.

About 47 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia; 28 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stipules membranous, produced below insertion, exstipellate. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 2–several pairs. Racemes axillary, long-pedunculate. Bracts large, membranous, imbricate, obliquely reniform, striate and ciliate, often covering flowers and fruit; bracteoles absent. Calyx membranous, 2-lipped, upper lip entire, lower lip obscurely toothed. Corolla 2–3 times as long as calyx; vexillum suborbicular, clawed; wings incurved, obtuse, smaller than vexillum. Stamens monadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary stipitate; 1–2-ovuled; styles incurved; stigma small, capitate. Pods 1–2-segmented, medium turgid, margin compressed, reticulate, indehiscent. Seeds 1–2, orbicular-reniform, estrophiolate.

About three species distributed in tropical Asia and Africa; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, straggling to twining climbers. Stipules reduced to an interpetiolar line. Leaves opposite, rarely verticillate, margin entire. Thyrses axillary and terminal, many‑flowered or fascicles with few flowers to 1‑flowered. Flowers 5‑merous. Sepals imbricate. Corolla funnelform; lobes imbricate. Stamens inserted at base to middle of corolla tube; filaments strap‑shaped to filiform; anthers narrowly ovate to narrowly oblong, included to exserted, base sagittate, 2‑celled. Ovary 2‑locular, with several ovules per locule. Style filiform; stigma 4‑cleft. Capsules ellipsoidal to narrowly ellipsoidal, septicidal, 4‑valvate, several‑seeded. Seeds winged.

Three species distributed worldwide; two species in N America, one species in E and SE Asia; one species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial, or perennial herbs. Stems ascending to erect, striate or angled. Leaves opposite, rarely whorled or rosette, entire. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, cymose or flowers solitary. Flowers (4–)5(–8)‑merous. Calyx‑tube tubular or campanulate, with 4–5‑keeled ridges abaxially; lobes filiform to ovate, with a prominent midvein. Corolla tubular, funnelform, or campanulate; tube usually much longer than lobes; lobe plicae between lobes overlapping to right or rarely valvate in bud. Stamens as many as and alternate with lobes, inserted on corolla tube; filaments basally ± winged; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 1‑locular, with 5–10 glands at base, sessile or with a long gynophore. Style usually short; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule cylindric to ellipsoidal, wingless or winged, many‑seeded, dehiscing into 2 valves. Seeds small, wingless or winged; seed coat minutely reticulate.

About 360 species distributed in NW Africa (Morocco), America, Asia, E Australia, Europe; about 248 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial orchids. Rhizomes tuberous, ovoid or compressed spherical, with concentric rings. New shoots emerging from the base of the pseudobulb. Leaves 3 or 4, oblong-linear, plicate-venose, deciduous. Scape emerging from a one-year-old rhizome simultaneously with the leafy shoot, the apex bending at anthesis, becoming erect afterward. Flowers rather small, crowded in a nutant raceme; sepals and petals subequal, free, ovate, spreading; lip undivided, attached to the foot of the column, concave, the base ventricosesubsaccate, not spurred, with a thick papillose curved callus above the sac, disk keeled; column short, broad, subterete, with a short foot fused with the lip; clinandrium broadly ovate, apiculate; rostellum truncate, fleshy; anther subglobose, incumbent, with 2 basal flaps; pollinia 2, waxy, globose and profoundly saccate on the back, attached to a slender hyaline stipe with a small viscidium; stigma obovatesuborbicular; ovary oblong. Capsules oblong-ellipsoidal, nutant, strongly rostrate.

About ten species distributed in tropical Asia, Pacific islands and Australia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial creeping herbs. Leaves opposite, reniform, orbicular or ovate‑cordate, usually long‑petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, ovate, entire. Flowers small, solitary or in umbels on axillary or terminal peduncles. Calyx‑tube obovate; limb short, with 4–7 persistent lobes. Corolla tubular‑funnel‑shaped, throat hairy, 4–5‑lobed; lobes valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the upper part of corolla‑tube; anthers dorsifixed, included or slightly exserted. Ovary 2‑celled, with 1 ovule in each cell; style filiform; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit a fleshy drupe, with two 1‑seeded pyrenes.

About 30 species chiefly in tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; stem scapose, erect, with or without scaly leaves in linear or subulate form. Leaves mainly radical, rosulate, entire, toothed or pinnatilobed. Capitula solitary and terminal to scape, heterogamous, radiate or disciform. Involucres disk‑like, campanulate or turbinate; phyllaries 2–many‑seriate, green or sometimes with margin and apex tinged purplish red, glabrous, pubescent or tomentose. Receptacle flat, glabrous, alveolate. All florets fertile. Marginal florets 1–2‑seriate, female, usually with vestigial staminodes, corolla bilabiate, outer lip in long or short ligulate form, apex 2–3‑toothed, inner lip 2‑toothed or deeply divided into 2 filiform segments. Central florets many, hermaphrodite, corolla bilabiate and bilateral symmetrical, outer lip 3–4‑lobed, inner lip 2‑parted; anther bases sagittate, lobes entire or lacerate; stylar branches obtuse apically, adaxial side somewhat compressed. Cypselae cylindric or fusiform, ribbed, sometimes slightly flattened, usually hairy, apex obtuse or narrowed to form beak. Pappus setae capillary or scaberulous.

About 80 species mainly distributed in Africa, also in E & SE Asia; about 20 species in China; two species (one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Arborescent bamboos, large-sized; clumps dense. Rhizomes short necked, pachymorph. Culms unicaespitose, erect, pendulous at apex; internodes green initially, often with yellow stripes, terete. Branches several, 1 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, very broad, densely hairy; ligule conspicuous; auricles absent or small; blade recurved or erect. Leaves usually large, base cuneate; auricles usually absent; ligule conspicuous; blade cuneate at base, venation not tessellate. Inflorescence iterauctant, fully bracteate, subtended by a narrow single-keeled prophyll, pseudospikelets clustered in soft or spiky globose mass at nodes of leafless flowering branches. Pseudospikelets sessile, prophyllate; florets (1–)2–5, with a sterile terminal floret with lemma only, sessile. Fertile glumes preceded by 1 or more gemmiferous bracts and 0–2 empty glumes; rachilla very short, obscure, not disarticulating; lemma broad, many-veined; palea strongly 2-keeled; lodicules absent. Stamens 6; filaments united into a firm tube; anthers apiculate. Ovary stalked, apex thickened and hairy; stigma 1, long, hairy, plumose. Caryopsis terete, apex hairy; pericarp slightly thickened.

About 30 species distributed in tropical Asia; six species (two endemic) in China; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, monoecious or rarely dioecious. Stipules 2, large, connate at base, enclosing terminal buds but deciduous, leaving a circular scar around node. Leaves alternate, entire or rarely serrulate, pinninerved. Cymes axillary, rarely male flowers solitary. Flowers unisexual. Male flowers: sepals 5, imbricate; stamens 5; filaments short, erect, rudimentary ovary pilose. Female flowers: sepals 4– 5, narrower; ovary sessile, 1-locular; ovules 1, pendulous; styles 2, filiform. Drupes ovoid or subglobose, compressed, endocarp cartilaginous. Seeds with or without endosperm.

About six species distributed in Indo-Malesia to Pacific islands; one species in China; it occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with corms. Leaves sword-shaped or linear, in 2 ranks, overlapped each other. Scapes erect, unbranched, usually with several cauline leaves. Flowers sessile, zygomorphic, large and showy, often red, purple, yellow, white, pink and various colours, 5–8 cm in diam.; tube short and curved, perianth segments 6, in 2 whorls, elliptic or ovate, apex obtuse or mucronate; stamens 3, towards one side, filaments inserted on tube. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, placentation axile, ovules many; style slender, apex 3-lobed. Capsule ellipsoidal or obovoid, loculicidal. Seeds flat, winged.

About 250 species mainly distributed in Mediterranean coastal regions, tropical Africa, SW and C Asia; one species often cultivated in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs stoloniferous, gynodioecious or gynomonoecious. Stems ascending to prostrate, rooting at lower nodes. Leaves petiolate, orbicular, cordate or reniform. Verticillasters axillary, 2–6(–many)‑flowered; floral leaf similar to stem leaf; bracts and bracteoles usually subulate. Calyx tubular to campanulate, slightly curved near throat, 15‑veined, indistinctly 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑toothed, lower lip 2‑toothed. Corolla tubular, dilated at apex, 2‑lipped; upper lip straight, emarginate or 2‑lobed; lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed. Stamens 4; filaments glabrous, undeveloped in pistillate flowers; anther cells oblong, parallel or divergent. Ovary glabrous. Style slender, apex subequally 2‑cleft. Nutlets dark brown, oblong‑ovoid, smooth or impressed‑punctate, glabrous.

About eight species spread over Asia and Europe; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees or shrubs, polygamous or dioecious. Stems and branches armed with stout, simple or branched spines. Leaves pinnate or bipinnate, rachis often furrowed; stipules small, caducous; leaflets alternate or subopposite. Inflorescence a raceme or panicle. Hypanthium campanulate, hairy. Calyx lobes 3 – 5, subequal, imbricate. Petals 3 – 5, slightly unequal, as long as calyx lobes or slightly longer, imbricate. Stamens 5–10, exserted or not; filaments distinct, slightly flattened and curved, tomentose at lower half; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary sessile or shortly stipitate; ovules 2–many; style short; stigma large. Pods flattened, indehiscent or tardily dehiscent. Seeds 1 –many, ovoid or ellipsoidal, flat or subcylindrical.

About 14 species distributed in C & SE Asia, E N America and S America; six species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial hairy herbs, with long taproots and short stems. Leaves petiolate, ternate or ternate-pinnate, pinnae usually deeply 3-lobed, margins serrate; petioles sheathing. Inflorescence of compound umbels, terminal or axillary; involucres of a few narrow bracts or wanting; rays many, spreading; bracteoles several, linear-lanceolate. Calyx-teeth minute, conspicuous. Petals white, ovate-lanceolate, apex incurved; stylopodium short-conic; styles very short. Fruit ovoid-oblong, densely pubescent or glabrate, dorsally compressed, lateral and dorsal wings conspicuous, thickened at base. Vittae 1–3 in each furrow, 2–6 on commissure. Seeds flattened dorsally, the face concave.

Two species in E Asia and N America; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, monoecious, rarely dioecious. Stipules thick, mostly persistent. Leaves simple, alternate, distichous or spirally arranged on the branchlets, entire, pinnately-veined, short-petiolate. Flowers apetalous; without disk, in axillary clusters or short-cymules, usually female clusters inserted at the upper part of branchlets, male ones at the lower part. Male flowers: sepals 5 – 6, imbricate; stamens 3 – 8; anthers oblong, sessile on a central column, tipped by their projecting connectivum; pistillode absent. Female flowers: sepals as in male flowers, but slightly thicker; ovary globose, 3 –15-1ocular; with 2 ovules in each locule; styles short, erect and connivent in an oblong or globular mass or in a short ring, or rarely spreading. Capsules globose or depressed-globose, with many longitudinal grooves, loculicidally dehiscent or separating into 2-valved cocci.

About 200 species chiefly in tropical Asia, Pacific Islands, and Malaysia, few in tropical America and Africa; 28 species and two varieties in China; eight species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; stems erect or ascending, branched mainly from base. Leaves mostly crowded at base, radical leaves pinnatisect with the leaf segments linear, long‑petiolate; cauline leaves few and alternate, pinnatisect or linear. Capitula small, heterogamous and radiate, solitary or few formed as loose corymbs. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, connate at base, inner ones longer. Receptacle flat; paleae scarious, linear and flat. All florets fertile. Peripheral florets ligulate, female, 1‑seriate, ligule spreading, entire or 3‑dentate at apex. Central florets tubular, hermaphrodite, corolla 4‑lobed apically; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages short and broadly ovate, stylar branches hairy. Cypselae glabrous, linear, flat, ribbed. Pappus of 2 stiff awns, retrorsely barbed.

About 11 species distributed in N Africa, tropical Asia, Australia and the Pacific islands; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems twining, procumbent or erect. Stipules small, deciduous; stipels persistent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets entire. Racemes axillary, sometimes flowers solitary. Bracts small, attached at base of pedicels; bracteoles 2, adnate to base of calyx. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed, 2-lipped, upper 2 teeth connate up to middle, lower ones lanceolate to subulate. Corolla purple or white; petals clawed; vexillum large, suborbicular or obovate, weakly auriculate; wings narrow, adherent to keel; keel obtuse, shorter than wings. Stamens monadelphous or diadelphous. Ovary subsessile; ovules several; styles slightly incurved, stigma capitate. Pods linear or oblong, weakly septate between seeds, dehiscing by twisted valves. Seeds 1 – 5, ovoid-elliptic, oblate or subglobular.

About nine or ten species in tropics and subtropics of the Old World; six species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, unarmed; young parts often red or brown rusty puberulous. Leaves alternate, unifoliolate or imparipinnate; leaflets entire, alternate. Inflorescence a thyrse, axillary or terminal. Flowers bisexual, small, shortly pedicellate, often hairy. Sepals (4–)5, connate at base. Petals (4–)5, imbricate. Stamens 10, rarely 8 or fewer, equal or unequal, shorter than or as long as petals; filaments subulate, dilated; anthers often with a dorsal or apical gland. Ovary 2–5-locular, ovule solitary and pendulous per locule; style very short, persistent, stigma simple. Fruit a berry, small, dry or fleshy, 1–2(–3)-seeded. Seed coat thinly membranous.

About 50 species distributed in SE Asia and NE Australia; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Semievergreen trees, monoecious; winter buds small; branchlets dimorphic: perennial branchlets remaining green for several years, becoming ridged and grooved with decurrent leaf bases; annual branchlets deciduous, short, never developing scars or buds. Leaves spirally arranged, sessile, base decurrent, trimorphic: leaves on 1–3 year main branches radially spreading, scalelike, relatively thick; leaves on annual branchlets of mature trees in 3 rows, radially spreading, subulate, quadrangular in cross section, deciduous with branchlet as a unit; leaves of annual branchlets of young trees and seedlings often 2-ranked, sessile, linear, flat, thin, deciduous. Pollen cones terminal on scalelike leaves-bearing branchlets, solitary; microsporophylls spirally arranged, sessile; pollen sacs 2–9. Seed cones terminal, shortly pedunculate, erect when mature, ± pyriform; bracts of mature cones nearly completely connate with cone scales (free only at apex), triangular, recurved, borne on central or middle distal part of abaxial side of cone scales; ovules 2 per bract axil; cone scales 20–22, spirally arranged, sessile, woody, basal scales sterile, median scales 2-seeded, with 6–10 triangular, acute teeth at distal margin, distal scales ligulate, multiangular, sterile. Seeds ellipsoid, slightly flattened, small, with a single, terminal, recurved wing. Cotyledons 4 or 5.

One species in China, N Vietnam, extinct in the wild.

Trees or shrubs. Branchlets tomentose, sometimes spiny. Leaves simple, opposite, entire, rarely lobed, usually with large gland patches near base. Inflorescences usually terminal, cymose or paniculate, rarely flowers solitary and axillary; cymules axillary, decussate, several‑flowered, short. Bracts often lanceolate or elliptic, deciduous or persistent. Calyx persistent, campanulate, enlarged in fruit, truncate, 4–5‑dentate or lobed, slightly unequal or oblique, usually with large glands. Corolla zygomorphic, ventricose funnelform, tube narrow at base, throat wide; limb oblique, ca. 2‑lipped, upper lip 2‑lobed or entire, lower lip 3‑lobed with middle lobe larger. Stamens 4, distinctly didynamous, inserted on basal part of corolla tube, usually inclusive, ± exserted; anthers divaricate, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary (2–)4‑locular; ovules 1(–2) per locule. Style slender, stigma often unequally 2‑lobed. Drupes fleshy, endocarp bony, mesocarp fleshy, 1–4‑seeded.

About 35 species distributed in Asia, Australia, and New Guinea; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

G. arborea Roxb. (雲南石梓) and G. hystrix Schult. ex Kurz (刺石梓) are occasionally cultivated.

Annual or rarely perennial herbs. Stem erect or diffusely branched, woolly or villous. Leaves alternate, entire or subentire, sessile or shortly petiolate. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, arranged as terminal or axillary corymbs, spikes or compacted fascicles. Involucres urceolate or campanulate; phyllaries in 2–5 series, imbricate, totally or margin broadly membranous, becoming smaller gradually outward, the outermost lanate. Receptacle flat, convex or concave, pitted or not. All florets fertile, corolla yellow or pale yellow in colour. Peripheral florets numerous, pistillate, corolla filiform with apex minutely 2–4‑dentate. Central florets few, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, limb dilated, apex 5‑lobed; anther acute or obtuse at apex, sagittate at base; stylar branches cylindric, papillose, distal end truncate or capitate. Cypselae oblong, glabrous or rarely loosely hairy and glandular. Pappus in 1 series, united at base or not, deciduous, white or dirty white.

About 200 species distributed worldwide; 19 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, often tomentose or stellately pubescent. Leaves opposite, mostly long‑petiolate. Verticillasters few–many‑flowered, axillary, sometimes basal, rarely terminal, often forming densely sessile or laxly branched cymose inflorescences, rarely seemingly racemose; bracts suborbicular to linear‑lanceolate. Calyx campanulate to tubular, 10‑veined, subequally 5‑toothed. Corolla purple‑red or yellow to white; tube slender, erect or incurved, throat narrow or inflated; limb 2‑lipped; upper lip straight, slightly galeate, entire or emarginate; lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed, middle lobe longest. Stamens 4, lower 2 longest; filaments complanate, hairy on two sides or glabrous; anthers close together in pairs, cells parallel, transverse. Disk subequal or gibbous behind. Style included, apically subequally 2‑cleft. Nutlets drupaceous, glabrous or pubescent, the pericarp usually fleshy and white, with a broad hilum; only 1 or 2, rarely all 4 developed.

About 36 species in SE Asia, from China, Indochina, Malesia to E India; 15 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubby. Leaves opposite, entire. Flowers bisexual, in dense chaffy heads or short spikes. Bracts and bracteoles usually colored, glabrous. Perianth-segments 5, erect, pilose at base or glabrous. Stamens 5; filaments almost entirely united into a long 5-lobed tube; the lobes emarginated or bifid; anthers 1-celled, borne on the lobes or in the sinus of the lobes. Ovary 1-locular; style short, 2 branched. Utricles subglobose or ellipsoid, 1-seeded, indehiscent.

About 100 species mostly in the New World tropics; two species (one cultivated) in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial terrestrial herbs. Stems slender, decumbent or erect, usually with raised lines descending from the base of petioles. Leaves opposite or alternate, rarely in whorls of 3(–5), undivided. Flowers small, bisexual, 3–4-merous; solitary or clustered in the upper leaf-axils, or in terminal racemes or panicles. Calyx-tube adnate to the ovary, terete or angular, the limb 4-lobed, persistent in fruit. Petals 4–8, concave, usually shortly clawed, caducous. Stamens usually twice as many as sepals; filaments short; anthers oblong, 4-celled. Ovary incompletely 3–4-locular, with 1 pendulous ovule in each locule; stigma capitate. Fruits small, nut-like, 1-seeded, pericarp somewhat membranous, 1-locular, septa almost absent.

About 36 species chiefly in Australia and New Zealand; two species in China; also in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs. Leaves entire, opposite, or the uppermost alternate, 3(–5)-nerved. Stipules free, intrapetiolar, often persistent. Flowers in axillary clusters with both male and female flowers or unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious). Male flowers: perianth-segments (3 –)4 – 5, usually free, oblong, valvate and folding inwards at a right angle in the bud, with a transverse ring of hairs on the bending angle; stamens as many as the perianth-segments and opposite to them; rudimentary pistil very small. Female flowers: perianth tubular, constricted and 2– 4-toothed at apex; staminodes absent; ovary included; style very short; stigma filiform, hairy on one side. Achene ovoid, surrounded by accrescent and ribbed perianth.

About three species in tropical and subtropical Asia and Australia; all species occur in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs with creeping or suberect rhizomes, and fibrous roots. Leaves cauline, petiolate, ovate or ovate-elliptic. Flowers small or medium-sized, in a terminal spike; sepals subequal, the odd one ovate, concave, the lateral ones spreading sidewise or backward; petals connivent with the odd sepal and with it forming a hood; lip adnate to the base or basal sides of the column, undivided, concave, ventricose, or subsaccate, fimbriate or villose on the inside, recurved at the apex; column subterrete, short; clinandrium dilated, the margin continued with the rostellum forming a cup; rostellum long, divided into 2 arms; anther ovate, acuminate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, sectile, oblong-acuminate; caudicles slender; viscidium oblong or linear; stigma concave, large; ovary subterete, striate-sulcate. Capsules erect, obovoid or oblong, erostrate, with persistent perianth at the apex.

About 40 species mainly in N temperate regions, but with some species extends southwards to Mexico, SE Asia, Australia and Pacific islands; 29 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems prostrate, sometimes erect. Leaves alternate, oblong‑obovate to spatulate, sinuate‑pinnatifid. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, usually solitary, pedunculate, terminal or axillary. Involucres broadly campanulate; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, herbaceous, margin ciliate. Receptacle convex, hemispherical or conical, naked. Marginal female florets 1–many‑seriate, narrowly tubular, usually 2‑lobed; stylar branches exserted. Disk bisexual florets many, corolla tubular, funnelform, bearing 4–5 lobes at apex; anthers with apical appendages, base lobes rounded; stylar branches stout, with deltoid apical appendages. Cypselae compressed or subcylindric, apex truncate. Pappus short, crown of scale with fimbriate margin.

About ten species native to tropical Asia and Africa; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Lianas, latex white. Leaves opposite, stipulate. Cymes extra‑axillary, short‑pedunculate, raceme‑like, usually simple. Flowers large. Calyx 5 lobed, glands present. Corolla subrotate, thick; lobes 5, longer than tube, overlapping to right. Corona ring‑like, inserted at base of gynostegium, deeply 5‑parted; lobes erect, membranous, revolute, separated by truncate sinus, shorter than anthers. Filaments connate into a tube; anthers somewhat concave at middle, appendages rounded, covering stigma head; pollinia 1 in each anther‑cell, oblong, pendulous. Stigma head elevated. Follicles ovoid‑cylindric, woody. Seeds ovate; coma white.

One species distributed in Vietnam; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, bipinnatifid or undivided, without stipules. Flowers bisexual, in terminal or axillary racemes or panicles. Bracts small, usually caducous. Perianth tubular in flower-bud, usually curved, apex subglobular, usually oblique, opening by 4 linear or linear-spathulate, recurved lobes. Stamens 4; anthers ovate, sessile, inserted in perianth-lobes. Ovary usually stipitate, with 2 lateral ovules; style filiform, with oblique discoid stigma. Follicles leathery or woody, opening along ventral suture, 1– 2-seeded.

About 250 species mostly in Australia; one species cultivated in China; also in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Branchlets usually covered with stellate hairs. Leaves alternate, margin serrate or rarely lobed, basal veins 3 – 5, short-petiolate. Stipules minute, caducous. Flowers bisexual, polygamous, or unisexual and dioecious, usually in 3-flowered cymes, arranged in axillary, terminal or leaf-opposed cymes. Bracts caducous. Peduncles and pedicels usually hairy. Sepals 5, distinct, valvate, hairy abaxially. Petals 5, minute, with scale-like glands at base adaxially. Androgynophore present. Stamens many, distinct; anthers globose, dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary 2– 4-locular, ovules 2– 8 per locule; style 1, usually swollen at apex; stigma swollen, peltate, entire or divided into small lobes, lobes entire, lobed or laciniate. Drupe usually grooved, 2– 4(– 8)-seeded.

About 150 species, distributed in tropics of the Old World; 26 species in China; three species and one variety in Hong Kong. According to Dunn & Tutcher, Grewia asiatica L. occurs in Hong Kong (FKH 51. 1912). It is not recorded here because no specimen of this species has been checked by the author.

Shrubs or lianas, latex white. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Cymes axillary, extra‑axillary or terminal, often shorter than leaves. Flowers subsessile. Calyx with 5 – many basal glands. Corolla salverform, tube long‑cylindric; lobes 5, overlapping to right. Corona‑lobes inserted at throat of corolla‑tube, ± adnate to filaments, ovate. Stamens 5, inserted on throat; filaments short, bases broad, ± connate, upper part narrow, free; anthers adnate to stigma head, apex acuminate, exserted; pollen tetrads in loose masses, 2 in each anther cell and fixed on 1 common retinaculum. Stigma head short conical. Follicles 2, divaricate, linear‑lanceolate in outline. Seeds elliptic.

About four species distributed in S and SE Asia and Australia; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Lianas, with white latex. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Cymes often raceme‑like, sessile or pedunculate, often 2 at a node. Flowers small. Calyx with basal glands. Corolla campanulate; tube with 5 longitudinal ridges inside, sometimes produced into fleshy appendages and /or with lines of hairs along each side; lobes 5, ca. as long as the tube, twisted to right or subvalvate. Corona‑lobes otherwise absent. Stamens 5, inserted at base of corolla‑tube; filaments connate into a tube; anthers erect, apical appendages membranous; pollinia 2 per pollinarium, oblong, erect. Stigma head hemispherical, obtusely conical or clavate and beaked, exceeding anthers. Follicles solitary or paired and widely divergent, ovoid to strongly bearked, often broad at base; seeds comose.

About 25 species distributed in tropical or subtropical Asia, S Africa and Oceania; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous vines, monoecious or dioecious. Tendrils not branched or 2-branched. Leaves entire or 3–5-partitioned, petiolate. Flowers white or yellow. Male flowers: solitary or arranged in racemes; calyx-tube tubular, enlarged at upper part, lobes 5, subulate; corolla rotate, 5-partitioned, lobes oblong or obovate; stamens 3, inserted at the middle of calyx-tube, filaments short, distinct, anthers connate, one 1-celled, two 2-celled, cells conduplicate, connectives not protrudent; pistillodes erect. Female flowers: solitary; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 3, linear; ovary ovoid or ellipsoid, placentas 3; ovules many, horizontal; style filiform; stigmas 3. Fruit a berry. Seeds obovate or oblong, compressed, marginate.

Six species distributed in S Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbaceous vines, dioecious. Tendrils 2-branched or rarely not branched. Leaves palmately compound, 3 –7-foliolate, rarely simple. Inflorescence paniculate, axillary. Peduncles articulate, bracteolate. Male flowers: calyx-tube short, 5-lobed; corolla rotate, 5- partitioned, lobes lanceolate or ovate-oblong; stamens 5, inserted at base of calyx-tube, filaments short, connate at base; anthers 2-celled, cells erect, longitudinally dehiscent, connective narrow, not protrudent; pistillodes absent. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes present; ovary globose, 3 –5-locular; styles 3, rarely 2, distinct, stigmas 2; ovules 2 per locule, pendulous. Berries globose, umbonate, indehiscent, 1–3 seeded. Seeds broadly ovate, compressed, not winged, verrucose or spiny.

About 13 species distributed in tropical Asia to E Asia; 11 species and two varieties in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, sometimes succulent, rarely subshrubs; stem glabrous, pubescent or hispid. Leaves alternate, toothed or pinnatisect, seldom entire. Capitula homogamous and discoid, solitary or in corymbose arrangement. Involucres campanulate or cylindric, calyculate; phyllaries uniseriate, lanceolate, herbaceous with scarious margin. Receptacle plain, pitted or shortly fimbriate. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, with lower part narrow and upper limb abruptly broadened, apex 5‑lobed, yellow or orange‑yellow, rarely purple; anther bases entire or shortly auriculate; stylar branches papillose hairy. Cypselae cylindric, 10‑ribbed, truncate at both ends, glabrous or puberulent. Pappus numerous, capillary, white silky.

About 40 species distributed in Asia, Africa and Australia; ten species in China; one species growing wild in Hong Kong.

Gynura aurantiaca DC. (紫絨草), Gynura bicolor (Roxb. ex Willd.) DC. (風鳳菜), and Gynura japonica (L. f.) Juel [三七草; Gynura segetum (Lour.) Merr.] were recorded previously.

Terrestrial herbs requiring dormancy during the dry cool season; with fleshy subterranean tubers. Stems leafy, herbaceous, deciduous. Leaves convolute, tender, elliptic or lanceolate-elliptic, rarely ovate. Inflorescences racemose, terminal to leafy shoots. Flowers mediumsized or small; sepals subequal, free, the odd one ovate, concave, the lateral sepals spreading sidewise or twisted and curved below the lip; petals usually smaller than the sepals; lip trilobed, calcarate, spur longer than the ovary, the lateral lobes usually wider than the midlobe, spreading; column short, the back erect, the base broad and with a glandular auricle on each side; rostellum large, fleshy, yokeshaped or beak-like, with slender long arms; anther 2-celled, thecae widely separated, broadly attached to the front of the column; pollinia 2, sectile, each on a slender caudicle with viscidium; stigmas 2, slightly curved below the rostellum-arms; ovary cylindrical, slightly narrowed at the apex, striate-sulcate. Capsules fusiform or ellipsoidal, pointed at both ends.

About 600 species widely distributed in tropical, subtropical to temperate regions; 55 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Culms erect, much branched. Leaf blades flat, linear or linear-lanceolate, with long tubercle-based hairs; ligule a short ciliate membrane. Inflorescence of solitary axillary racemes aggregated into a spathate compound panicle; racemes flattened, bearing paired spikelets, fragile, pedicel oblong, adnate to adjacent rachis internode, junction with internode marked by a line. Sessile spikelet hemispherical, bisexual; lower glume leathery, pitted to honeycombed, adaxially semi-globose concave; upper glume thicken papery, shorter and narrower, sunk into cavity of rachis; lower floret barren, without a palea; upper floret with entire awnless lemma. Pedicellate spikelet narrowly ovate, staminate or neuter, lemma thicken papery, stamens 3. Caryopsis broad elliptic.

Two species, one pantropical, the other confined to Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Marine herbs. Rhizomes present; leaf-bearing branches arising from rhizome at each node; stolons absent. Erect stems, if present, rooted in substrate, unbranched, short; scales 2, midway or higher on stem. Leaves 2–8, terminal pairs or pseudowhorls (rarely distichous), submersed, sessile or petiolate; blade linear to ovate, base tapering to stem, apex obtuse, midvein without lacunae along side(s), blade uniform in colour throughout, abaxially without prickles, intravaginal squamules entire. Inflorescences 1-flowered or cymose, sessile; spathes not winged. Flowers unisexual, male and female on same plants or on different plants, submersed, sessile, nearly sessile (female), or pedicellate (male); petals absent. Male flowers: filaments distinct; anthers linear to fusiform; pollen in moniliform chains. Female flowers: ovary 1-locular; styles 3–5, not 2-fid. Fruits ovoid to spherical, smooth or ridged, not echinate, dehiscing by decay of pericarp. Seeds spherical or nearly so, echinate to reticulate.

About 13 species in tropical and warm temperate seas; four species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Yip and Lai (Acta Phytotaxonomica Sinica 44(4): 457 – 463. 2006) recently provided a treatment of this genus based on field and herbarium specimens from Hong Kong.

Shrubs or herbs. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 or 4, petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, multifid or bristle‑like, usually caducous. Cymes terminal, dichotomous or trichotomous, with flowers often arranged on one side of the branches. Calyx‑tube ovoid or turbinate; lobes 4–6, usually short and erect, persistent. Corolla tubular or bell‑shaped; tube 4– 6‑ribbed, constricted at the base, villose on the throat; lobes 4–6, imbricate in the bud. Stamens 4–6, attached to the base of corolla‑tube; anthers with appendages on the apex of connectives, basifixed, included or slightly exserted. Ovary 5‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style filiform, with club‑shaped stigma. Fruit a berry, many‑seeded.

About 14 species in C & S America; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen scandent shrubs, climbing by aerial roots. Leaves simple, alternate, petiolate, coarsely dentate or lobed, but entire on flowering shoots; stipules absent. Inflorescence a compact raceme of umbellules, or occasionally umbellules solitary. Flowers bisexual. Pedicels not articulate under the calyx. Calyx margin subentire or 5-toothed. Petals 5, valvate in the bud. Stamens 5; anthers ovate. Ovary 5-locular; styles united into a short column. Fruit a drupe, globose. Seeds ovoid; endosperm ruminate.

About 15 species, N Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia, Europe; two species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial or epiphytic herbs, with tuberous rhizomes. Pseudostems erect, leafy. Ligule conspicuous; leaf blade usually oblong or lanceolate. Inflorescence a terminal spike, densely many flowered; bracts imbricate or lax, 1- or more flowered; bracteoles tubular. Calyx tubular, usually split on 1 side, apex truncate or 3-toothed. Corolla tube long, slender; lobes reflexed at anthesis, linear. Lateral staminodes petaloid, larger than corolla lobes. Labellum suborbicular, large, apex usually 2-cleft; claw long or short. Filament usually long, rarely absent; anther dorsifixed, base divaricate; connective appendage absent. Ovary 3-locular; placentation axile. Capsule globose, 3-valved. Seeds many; aril lacerate.

About 50 species in tropical and subtropical Asia, Africa (Madagascar); 28 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Stems erect or half‑scandent, terete or quadrangular. Leaves opposite, or rarely whorled. Stipules free or united with the petioles in a short sheath, entire or fringed with bristle‑like subulate lobes. Flowers in axillary clusters or terminal panicles, or rarely in axillary pedunculate cymes. Calyx‑tube usually turbinate or obconical, limb distinct or inconspicuous, usually 4–5‑lobed; lobes persistent. Corolla‑tube usually short, limb 4– 5‑lobed; lobes spreading, valvate in bud, and usually hairy adaxially at base. Stamens as many as and alternate with the corolla‑lobes; anthers basifixed, exserted from corolla‑tube. Ovary 2(–3)‑locular, with several ovules in each locule; style linear; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, subglobular to ovoid or ellipsoidal, dehiscent or indehiscent.

A large genus, with more than 400 species widely distributed over tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 59 species in China; 19 species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial large herbs, scabrous to hirsute. Leaves opposite, or those on upper portion alternate, sometimes all alternate, 3‑nerved, petiolate. Capitula large, heterogamous and radiate, solitary or in corymbs. Involucres dish‑form or broadly hemispherical; phyllaries 2–many‑seriate, herbaceous or foliaceous. Receptacle flat or slightly convex; paleae enfolding the florets. Marginal florets neutral, in 1 series, corolla ligulate and spreading, yellow. Central florets bisexual and fertile, numerous, corolla tubular, 5‑lobed, yellow, purple or brown. Cypselae oblong or obovate, slightly compressed or 4‑angulate. Pappus 2 scales, sometimes together with 2 or more small intermediate scales, deciduous.

About 100 species native to America; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Helianthus tuberosus L. (菊芋、菊藷) was also cultivated previously.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, entire or toothed. Flowers bisexual, regular, in axillary racemes. Bracts usually triangular, sometimes leafy, persistent or caducous. Pedicels usually in pairs and often united to the middle. Perianth tubular, apex 4-lobed; lobes linear, recurved. Stamens 4; anthers subsessile, inserted in the perianth-lobes. Ovary sessile or subsessile, with 2 ovules; style slender, club-shaped at the top. Fruit an indehiscent nut.

About 97 species mainly in SE Asia and Australia; 20 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, more or less stellate-tomentose. Leaves simple, entire or serrate. Flowers axillary, rarely terminal, solitary or in cymes; bracteoles small or remote from calyx; calyx tubular, shortly 5-lobed; petals 5, regular or sub-bilabiate; claws elongated, all or the lower often with ear-like appendages; stamens 10, at top of elongated staminal column; staminodes 5; ovary stalked, 5-lobed, 5-locular, with several ovules in each locule; styles united, linear, slightly thickened and stigmatose at apex. Carpels separating when ripen, dehiscing along ventral suture, straight or often at length spirally twisted, often stellate-tomentose or setose. Seeds verruculose with scanty endosperm.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Asia and America; nine species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely subshrubs, pubescent or strigose, rarely scabrous. Leaves alternate, less often opposite, sessile or petiolate. Cymes terminal, rarely axillary, unilateral, scorpioid, bracteate or not. Calyx 5‑parted. Corolla white or light bluish purple, less often yellow, cylindric or funnelform, strigose outside, glabrous and rarely appressed pubescent inside; throat frequently pubescent; limb 5‑parted. Filaments extremely short; anthers inclusive. Ovary completely or incompletely divided into 4 lobes; ovules 4. Style terminal; stigma conical or ring‑like. Fruit nutlet‑like dry drupes, without evident mesocarp at maturity, endocarp bony, dividing into four 1‑seeded or two 2‑seeded mericarps. Seeds straight or curved, endosperm thin or absent.

About 250 species distributed in tropical and temperate regions; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs. Leaves opposite or alternate, pinnately-veined. Inflorescences axillary, rarely terminal, racemose or spicate. Flowers bisexual, 4–6-merous, actinomorphic, each flower subtended by 1 bract. Calyx ovoid or urceolate, limb 4–6-denticulate, persistent. Mature flower bud straight, lower portion usually slightly inflated and angled, upper portion subclavate. Petals free, straight, spreading. Stamens usually inserted at petals. Filaments short; anthers 2–4-celled, sometimes multilocellate, ellipsoidal. Ovary 1-loculed. Style subcylindrical; stigma capitate or truncate. Fruit a berry, ovoid or ellipsoidal, exocarp leathery, smooth or pubescent.

About 50 species distributed tropical and subtropical Africa and Asia; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms erect or creeping and rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades linear, flat; ligule narrow, membranous, margin ciliate. Inflorescence a spike-like raceme, solitary or in groups in upper leaf axils. Spikelet paired, one sessile, the other pedicellate, pairs alternating along rachis. Sessile spikelet appressed to hollow in rachis; lower glume narrowly elliptic, rigidly herbaceous to leathery, abaxial flat, margin 2-keeled, indistinctly winged on adaxial surface, obtuse to caudate or rarely 2-lobed; upper glume sometimes adnate to internode, mucronate or awned; lower floret barren, without palea; upper floret bisexual, lemma membranous, entire, awnless; stamens 3. Caryopsis ovate or oblong. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile, but base truncate and lacking callus.

About 14 species spread over tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

records.authority: Bunge ex Fisch. & C. A. Mey.
records.text:
Annual or biennial herbs; stem erect, branched apically. Leaves lyrately pinnatisect, upper surfaces green and glabrous, lower surfaces greyish white and densely tomentose. Capitula homogamous, pedunculate, loosely corymbose at stem and branch terminal, rarely solitary. Involucres ovoid; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate, outer few series with purplish red cristate appendages on abaxial sides near apices. Receptacle flat or slightly convex, densely fimbriate. All florets bisexual and fertile, corolla tubular, red or purple in colour, upper limb short, deeply 5‑cleft, lower tube long filiform; anther bases caudate and basal appendages lacerate; filaments separate and glabrous; stylar branches separate, apices truncate. Cypselae oblong‑cuneate, ribbed, glabrous, apex obliquely truncate. Pappus 2‑seriate, inner layer long plumose, base connate and deciduous as a ring; outer layer scarious and short.

One species distributed in Asia and Australia.

Trees with well-developed buttresses, monoecious. Leaves alternate, simple or digitate, usually lepidote abaxially, pinnately veined. Panicles axillary; pedicels jointed. Flowers unisexual, small; calyx campanulate or urceolate, shortly 4–6-lobed; petals absent. Male flower: stamens 4–15, filaments united into a column; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing lengthwise, in a ring on apex of column, staminodes present; pistillode minute or completely reduced. Female flower: similar to male flowers, but with sterile anthers; carpels 4–6, loosely connivent, with one erect ovule in each carpel; style very short with minute stigmas. Ripe carpels free, woody or leathery, with carina or wings, indehiscent. Seeds lacking endosperm.

About 30 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia to Australia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs with creeping rhizomes. Leaves cauline, ovate, petiolate. Flowers non-resupinate, small, hardly opening, in a terminal raceme; sepals free, subequal, ovate; petals largely concealed; lip uppermost, adnate to the sides of the column, fleshy, undivided, strongly concave, the base furnished with papillose calli, the apex short and inflexed; column short, with 2 lateral glands, the apex with fleshy appendages and adnate to the lip; rostellum erect, elongate and bilobed; anther erect, ovate, acute; pollinia 2 or 4 in 2 pairs, sectile, obovoid and acuminate; caudicles slender; viscidium oblong, affixed between the lobes of the rostellum; stigma transversely 2-lobed, below the erect rostellum; ovary oblong-cylindrical, erect, striate-sulcate. Capsules oblong-ovoid, erect.

About 20 species mainly in tropical Asia; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or treelets, unarmed, Leaves 2–5-pinnately compound; stipules connate to petioles; leaflets entire. Flowers polygamous, in terminal panicle of umbels, with bisexual flowers and male flowers in separate umbels; bracts and bracteoles persistent. Pedicels not articulate. Calyx-margin minutely dentate. Petals 5, valvate in the bud. Stamens 5. Ovary 2-locular; styles 2, free or united to middle. Fruit a drupe, laterally compressed. Seed compressed, endosperm ruminate.

About 5 species in S and SE Asia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms usually stout, tufted. Leaf sheaths usually keeled; leaf blades linear, flat; ligule membranous, sometimes with ciliate fringe. Inflorescence of solitary racemes, terminal or axillary and loosely aggregated into a spathate panicle. Racemes linear, dense, spikelets paired, one sessile and the other pedicellate, imbricate, 1 – several pairs of homogamous spikelets (staminate or neuter) at base of raceme below fertile pairs, upper heterogamous. Homogamous spikelets herbaceous, flat, lanceolateoblong. Sessile spikelet subterete; callus long, pungent, bearded, its apex exposed; lower glume leathery, base subrounded, margins inrolled embraced upper glume; upper glume awnless; lower floret reduced to a hyaline lemma; upper lemma stipe-like, with an awn arising from the apex; awn geniculate, with hairy column. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, lanceolate-oblong, larger than sessile spikelet, similar to homogamous spikelets, awnless.

Six species distributed throughout the tropics and subtropics; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Climbing vines, woody or somewhat herbaceous. Stem and branches not prickly. Leaves alternate, in 2 ranks, usually ovate or oblong-lanceolate, main veins 5–9; petioles with one pair of tendrils near base. Inflorescence a solitary, many-flowered umbel, borne in axil of leaf or scale-like bract; peduncle usually compressed. Flowers small; tepals connate into a tube with opening only at toothed apex. Male flowers: stamens 3, 6, or 9–12; filaments ± connate, forming a column; anthers distinct, introrse. Female flowers: ovary 3-locular; ovules 1–2 per locule; stigmas 3, usually recurved; staminodes 3–6. Fruit a berry, black, globose, 1–6-seeded.

About 12 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia; nine species (five endemic) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Twining or prostrate herbs. Leaves petiolate, base usually cordate, margin entire or lobed. Cymes axillary, 1–several‑flowered; bracts 2, leaflike, persistent. Sepals 5; outer 3 larger, ovate, slightly enlarged in fruit; inner 2 much smaller. Corolla campanulate or funnelform; limb shallowly 5‑lobed. Stamens inclusive; filaments dilated at base; pollen grains not spiny. Disk annular. Pistil inclusive; ovary hairy, 1‑locular or imperfectly 2‑locular apically, 4‑ovuled. Style 1, filiform; stigmas 2, ovate‑oblong, complanate. Capsule globose, 4‑valved, pilose. Seeds 1–4, smooth.

One species distributed in tropical Africa and Asia; it also occurs in China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs, small trees or herbs, usually pubescent with stellate hairs. Leaves alternate, toothed or palmately lobed, stipulate. Flowers bisexual, 5-merous, solitary, axillary; bracteoles 5 –12. Calyx campanulate, rarely cup-shaped or tubular, 5-toothed, persistent. Corolla showy, yellow, scarlet or white. Staminal-tube truncate or 5-toothed at apex; anthers reniform. Ovary 5-locular, 3 to many ovules per locule; style branches 5, stigmas capitate or spathulate. Fruit a dehiscent capsule. Seeds reniform, pubescent or glandularly papillose.

Over 200 species majority confined to the Old World, most numerous in tropical Africa; 24 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Hibiscus trionum L. was recorded in Hong Kong by Dunn & Tutcher (1912), but no recent record is available, so it is not described here.

Perennial herbs, bulbiferous. Leaves basal, linear or strap-shaped. Scape hollow. Inflorescences umbellate; involucres 2, spreading or recurved. Flowers pedicellate. Perianth funnel-shaped, horizontal or declinate; tube usually short, with minute scales in the throat; segments 6, equal or the inner ones narrower, red or whitish and sometimes white-striped. Stamens 6, inserted in the throat, ± declinate; filament free, filiform; anthers versatile. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule. Style erect or slightly declinate, with an entire or 3-lobed stigma. Fruit a capsule, subglobose, loculicidally 3-valved. Seeds usually flattened.

About 76 species in tropical America; two species cultivated in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody vines or scandent shrubs. Leaves opposite, leathery or subleathery, entire, without glands or with a serial sparse glands near margin on abaxial surface; stipules absent or minute. Racemes axillary or terminal. Flower bisexual, zygomorphic, white, sometimes pinkish, fragrant; pedicels articulated above middle; bracteoles 2. Calyx 5-lobed, with a large gland at base or without glands. Petals 5, clawed at base, unequal, silky hairy. Stamen 10, all fertile, unequal, one of them larger, filament free or connate at lower part. Ovary shallowly 3-lobed; lobes with 3–5 appendages on abaxial surface; style single, rarely 2, apex curved. Fruit a schizocarp, each carpel developed into a samara, each samara with 3 wings, the middle wing longest, lateral wings shorter. Seed polygonal-globose.

About 25 species distributed in SE Asia, Fiji and Mauritius; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs; branchlets hairy. Leaves simple, opposite, entire or serrate, petiolate. Cymes axillary or crowded at apex. Calyx membranous, salverform, colourful, subentire. Corolla‑tube curved, apex shallowly 5‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted at the base of corolla‑tube, exserted; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary slightly compressed, ovules 4. Style slender; stigma 2‑cleft. Fruit nearly 4‑valved to base.

About three species distributed in India, Madagascar and tropical Africa; one species introduced to China; it is commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite or verticillate, margin glandular-dentate, rarely entire, petioled; stipules small, caducous or absent. Flowers bisexual, small, usually in terminal or axillary racemes or panicles. Pedicels articulate. Bracts small, caducous or persistent. Calyx tube turbinate, connate to base of ovary. Calyx-lobes persistent, (4–)5–8(–12). Petals usually as many as and similar to sepals, inserted at throat of calyx. Stamens as many as and opposite to petals, or many; filaments filiform; anthers subglobose, small, dorsifixed; glands of disc as many as sepals and opposite to them. Ovary perigynous, 1-locular; parietal placentas 2–5, ovules (1–)3–7 per placenta; styles 2–5(–7), filiform, distinct or slightly united at base; stigmas 1, small, capitate. Capsule 2–5 mm in diam., leathery, dehiscing apically into 2–8 valves, with persistent calyx-lobes and petals. Seeds 1 to several. Cotyledons leaf-like.

About 180 –200 species, distributed in tropical regions of the world; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, erect or ascending, rhizomatous. Stems longitudinally ridged and sulcate. Leaves entire; stipules membranous; petioles shorter than leaf blades. Inflorescence a terminal or leaf-opposed spike, with 4 (rarely 6 or 8), white petal-like involucral bracts at base. Flowers white when mature, small. Stamens 3(–4), longer than styles; filaments ca. 3 times as long as anthers, basal part connate to ovary; anthers oblong. Pistils 3, 3-carpellate; carpels partly connate; ovary semi-inferior (flowers perigynous), 1-locular; placentae 3, each with 6 –9 ovules; styles 3, recurved. Capsules subglobose, dehiscent at apex.

One species occurs in E and SE Asia; it occurs in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs or lianas, epiphytic or epilithic, often twining or climbing by adventitious roots. Leaves opposite, fleshy, papery, or membranous. Inflorescences extra‑axillary or, less often, terminal; umbel‑like, perennial, producing a succession of globose or flat‑topped clusters, usually many, the old rachis thick with ± contiguous pedicel‑scars. Calyx small, with basal glands. Corolla fleshy; rotate or bell‑shaped, lobes valvate, interior often densely hairy or scurfy. Corona‑lobes 5, depressed‑patent or ± adnate vertically to gynostegium, fleshy, glossy when dried, inner angle a tooth incumbent on anthers, outer angle rounded or acute, margin revolute, longitudinally grooved basally. Stamens short‑connate, apical membrane of anthers appressed against stigma head; pollinia 1 in each cell, oblong, erect, with raised, translucent margin. Stigma head discoid, rounded or subapiculate. Follicles often solitary, cylindric‑fusiform.

At least 100 species in SE Asia to Oceania; 30 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, twining. Stems rough with retrorse spines. Stipules persistent for sometimes. Leaves opposite, palmately 3–7- lobed, or undivided, serrate. Male inflorescence laxly paniculate. Male flowers: sepals 5, imbricate; stamens 5; anthers oblong. Female inflorescence cone-like spicate. Female flowers: calyx thinly membranous, closely appressed to ovary, margin entire; ovary sessile; style 2-branched; ovules pendulous. Achenes broadly ovoid, enclosed within persistent, often glandular calyx. Pericarp crustaceous. Seeds with white fleshy endosperm, and spirally involute embryo.

Three species distributed in N temperate regions; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, evergreen or deciduous; bud-scales absent. Leaves alternate, margin entire or serrate; stipules absent. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate or sub-corymbose; bracts and bracteoles small, early deciduous; flowers small, bisexual; pedicels not articulate; calyx 5-toothed; petals 5, bases free, slightly coherent, imbricate or valvate, revolute after anthesis; stamens 8–10, exserted; filaments slightly adnate to petals; anthers oblong, connective 2–3-toothed at the apex; ovary half inferior, 3 – 4-locular; ovules many per locule, irregularly arranged; styles 3 –5, partly connate, stigma capitellate. Fruit a capsule, ovoid, 1/3–2/3 surrounded by calyx, 3 –4-locular, loculicidally dehiscent. Seeds numerous, flattened; seed-coat thin, reticulate, fringed on both sides; embryo straight.

Four species in China, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam; one variety in Hong Hong.

Deciduous or evergreen subshrubs or shrubs, rarely small trees. Bark usually exfoliating in sheets. Branchlets with white or yellow large piths. Leaves opposite, rarely verticillate. Inflorescence terminal, sometimes axillary, a corymbose or umbellate cyme, or thyrse. Flowers fertile or sterile. Sterile flowers few, sometimes absent, borne at margin of inflorescence, with 2 or 5 enlarged petaloid sepals. Fertile flowers usually many, borne at middle of inflorescence, bisexual, small. Calyx tube adnate to ovary, 4 – 5-lobed. Petals 4 – 5, free, valvate, rarely connate and forming a calyptra. Stamens usually 10. Ovary inferior to semi-inferior, imperfectly or perfectly 2 – 5-locular; ovules many; styles 2 – 5, free or connate at base. Fruit a capsule, hemispheric to turbinate, small, dehiscing apically. Seeds many, small, winged or wingless.

About 70 species distributed in Asia, N & S America; 33 species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs, submerged. Stems elongate, branched. Leaves verticillate or lowermost opposite, sessile, linear to narrowly elliptic, margin serrate with 2 small, fringed nodal scales. Plants dioecious or monoecious; flowers unisexual, axillary. Male spathe subsessile, membranous, subglobose, with apical knob and corona of setae, 1-flowered; male flowers shortly pedicellate, free from spathe on water surface at anthesis; sepals 3, ovate or obovate, convex; petals 3, narrower than sepals; stamens 3. Female spathe tubular, sessile, bifid at apex, 1-flowered; sepals and petals similar to male ones; ovary cylindrical, attenuate into a filiform beak; styles (2–)3; ovules few. Fruit cylindrical or linear.

One species and one variety distributed in temperate to tropical; one species and one variety in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, stems prostrate or creeping, usually rooting at the nodes. Leaves simple, base cordate, margin crenate to deeply lobed; stipules small, membranous; petioles not sheathing. Flowers bisexual, white, greenish or yellow, in simple, small heads or umbels, opposite to the leaves or axillary. Calyx-teeth minute or obsolete. Petals entire, ovate, valvate the bud. Stylopodium conic to depressed. Fruits orbicular or broader than long, laterally compressed, base cordate, dorsal surface rounded; dorsal and lateral ribs usually conspicuous; vittae inconspicuous. Seed face plane to concave; endocarp woody. Carpophore usually absent.

About 75–100 species widely distributed in tropical, subtropical and temperate regions, more numerous in the S hemisphere; 14 species in China; two species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Aquatic perennial herbs, sometimes with axillary spines. Leaves sessile or short‑petiolate, margin entire or slightly undulate. Flowers sessile, several in axillary whorls. Bracts elliptic or lanceolate; bracteoles small or none. Calyx tubular, 5‑lobed; lobes linear to lanceolate. Corolla tubular, ventricose, 2‑lipped, upper lip shallowly 2‑toothed, lower lip 3‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous, posterior pair similar to others or smaller; anthers incised at base, 2‑thecous, thecae at same height. Ovary oblong, 4–many ovules per locule; stigma entire or bidentate. Capsule linear to narrowly oblong, terete, retinacula hardened and curved, acute, many‑seeded. Seeds with long mucilaginous hair.

About 100 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; seven species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Climbing succulent plants. Stems elongated, 3-angled or 3-winged, adhering to walls or trees by means of aerial roots; areoles borne on the ridges of angles, felted, short-spinose or spineless. Flowers usually large and white, rarely red, nocturnal. Perianth-segments many, united into a long tube, with large green or purplish scales outside; limb very broad. Stamens many, in 2 whorls, attached on the perianth-tube or on the throat. Ovary spineless; stigma with many simple or branched lobes. Fruit a fleshy berry, with scales outside.

About 18 species in tropical America; one species is commonly cultivated or naturalized in S China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, usually 0.3 – 1.5 m tall; rootstock more or less woody, often subtuberous or tuberous. Stems erect or often ascending, terete. Stipules scarious or thinly papery, striate, nearly glabrous or variously hairy; stipels scarious, filiform. Leaves 3-foliolate or (3–)5 – 7-foliolate, entire or undulate. Inflorescences terminal or terminal and axillary, sometimes a fertile shoot separately arising from basal part of main stems, pseudoracemose or lax-paniculate, lax-flowered, with 2 – 5 flowers at each node; primary bracts subtending secondary bracts; pedicels usually uncinate-hairy; bracteoles absent. Calyx broadly or very broadly campanulate, 4-lobed; upper lobe entire or minutely 2-toothed at apex; petals clawed. Stamens monadelphous. Ovary stipitate. Pods distinctly stipitate, 2 – 5-jointed, densely uncinate-hairy on lateral surfaces, nearly glabrous or entirely glabrescent on both sutures, dorsal suture distinctly thickened and straight or shallowly undulate, ventral suture very deeply incised. Seeds flat, obliquely depressed obovate, without rim-aril around hilum.

About 14 species distributed in Asia, few species in America; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial hydrophilous herbs. Culms spongy, creeping and rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades linear or broadly linear, acute; ligule membranous. Inflorescence usually a cylindrical spike-like panicle. Spikelets lanceolate, deciduous with pedicels, dorsally compressed, fasciculate, pedicels very short, florets 2, lower floret staminate or neuter, upper floret bisexual; lower glume much shorter than spikelet; upper glume and lower lemma shorter than or subequalling spikelet, 3–5-veined, apex acute to shortly awned; lower palea absent; upper lemma membranous, margins thin and embracing upper palea except at apex; stamens 3; ovary glabrous, styles 2, free, stigma plumose, exserted laterally from upper part of spikelets.

Five species distributed in the tropics and warm regions of both hemisphere; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, bulbiferous. Leaves basal, ensiform or linear. Scape solid. Inflorescences umbellate, rarely flower solitary; involucres ovate-lanceolate, membranous. Flowers white, fragrant. Perianth actinomorphic salverform; tube slender, very long; segments 6, oblong, lanceolate, or linear. Stamens 6, inserted at throat of perianth tube; filament basally united by a petaloid staminal cup, free part erect, filiform; anther versatile, linear. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule. Style slightly declinate, slender; stigma capitate, small. Fruit a capsule.

About 30–40 species in Mesoamerica and tropical America; one species introduced to China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual. Culms erect or geniculate at base, usually tufted. Leaf blades linear, midvein distinct, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, truncate or rounded. Inflorescence a compound spathate panicle, each ultimate spatheole subtending a peduncle bearing a pair of short racemes; raceme pairs 2–many-awned, often reflexed at maturity. Racemes with 0–2 pairs of homogamous spikelets below the fertile pairs, these similar to pedicellate spikelets; pedicels and internodes slender. Sessile spikelet dorsally compressed or subterete; callus obtuse to pungent, bearded, its apex exposed; lower glume lanceolate to linear, incurving, convexly rounded without keels; upper glume boat-shaped, keeled, margins membranous hyaline, ciliate, 3-veined, awnless; lower floret reduced to a hyaline lemma; upper lemma stipiform, 2-toothed, awned between the teeth; awn geniculate with hairy column; palea small; lodicules 2, small; stamens 3; style free, stigma penicillate. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, narrowly lanceolate, slightly longer than the sessile.

About 64 species distributed mainly in Africa, a few species extending to other tropical regions; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs. Leaves opposite, rarely whorled, often with glandular spots. Cymes terminal or axillary, rarely flower solitary. Sepals 5, often persistent. Petals 5, yellow, rarely pink or purplish, oblique. Stamens many, free or united into 3–5-bundles, opposite to petals, filaments slender; anther dorsifixed, connective glandular. Ovary 3–5-locular, ovules many in each locule, rarely few; styles (2–)3–5, free or connate; stigma small. Capsules septicidal. Seeds small, without aril.

About 400 species distributed in temperate to subtropical regions of the world; 40 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Spreading to erect perennial herbs or shrubs with cystoliths. Leaves opposite, petiolate, margin entire or dentate. Flowers in clustered spikes, capitellate, or rarely solitary. Bract leaf‑like, petiolate; bracteoles 2 or 4, free or connate forming an obconic or cylindric involucres, enclosing 1–4 flowers, all of which but one are usually reduced or obsolete. Calyx very small, usually obscured by bracteoles, scarious or membranous, deeply 5‑lobed, lobes equal to subequal in length, linear‑lanceolate. Corolla rose‑pink or whitish or blue, resupinate by torsion of tube, tube subcylindric to expanded distally into a narrow throat, limb bilabiate, upper lip subentire or shallowly 2‑lobed, lower lip turned upward, shallowly 3‑lobed, lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, inserted near apex of corolla tube, exserted; anthers 1‑thecous, theca muticous. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform, exserted, stigma 2‑lobed, lobes equal or unequal. Capsule ellipsoidal, stalked, retinacula subulate, 2‑ or 4‑seeded. Seeds, ovoid, compressed, smooth or pustular‑tuberculate, with a narrow, membranous wing.

About 40 species in tropical regions of the Old World; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Moderately robust to robust, stoloniferous or rhizomatous perennials; roots coarse. Culms central or lateral, the latter with cataphylls at base. Leaves 3-ranked, basal or cauline; blade leathery, glabrous, pseudopetiole present or 0; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaf-like, basal bract usually longest. Inflorescence usually an open compound panicle, more rarely capitate with 1– many spikes. Spikes comprising many spirally imbricate glume-like bracts (spicoid bracts) each subtending a partial inflorescence (spicoid) with a much reduced axis. Spicoids comprising a naked, terminal female flower and 2(–3) scale-like floral bracts, all subtending a male flower comprising 1 stamen, the lowest 2 floral bracts opposite, keeled. Stigmas 2–3. Achenes sculptured, often with spongy conical apex.

About 60 species distributed in pantropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Rhizomes subglobose or tuberous. Leaves basal, linear, less than 1 cm broad, sessile. Flowering stems shorter than leaves, slender, usually pilose. Inflorescences terminal, umbellate or racemose, few-flowered or flower solitary. Perianth segments 6, free, persistent. Stamens inserted at base of perianth segments; filament short; anther nearly basifixed. Ovary inferior, 3-locular; style short; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit a capsule.

About 100 species widely distributed in tropical regions; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Woody vine. Leaves undivided, palmately 3– (rarely 5–7)-nerved. Inflorescences axillary, cymose or paniculate. Male flowers: sepals 7–12, spirally arranged, the outer ones smaller, the inner ones larger, imbricate, with membranous margins; petals 4 –9, fleshy, usually obovate or spathulate, sometimes absent; stamens 6 to many, free or connate; filaments thickened at apex; anthers opening longitudinally. Female flowers: sepals and petals similar to that in males; staminodes present or absent; carpels 2 or 3, sometimes 6 or 1; style short; stigma entire or 3-lobed. Drupe compressed obovoid to subglobose, with style-scar near base; kernel bony, with radiating ribs.

About six species in S & SE Asia to Polynesia and Australia; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, often aromatic. Leaves opposite, serrate. Flowers in dense capitula, compact spikes, or in few‑flowered clusters, often seund; bracts subulate to setaceous. Calyx tubular, straight to oblique, 10‑veined; teeth 5, subequal, acute or awned, erect, ± dilated in fruit. Corolla tube cylindric to swollen on one side; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip 2‑lobed, lobes erect, spreading or reflexed; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe abruptly reflexed with thickened margins, sometimes saccate at the base. Stamens 4, lower 2 longer, declined; filaments free, without basal appendages; anther cells 2, apically confluent. Disk entire. Style apex 2‑cleft or subentire. Nutlets ovoid to oblong, smooth or rugose.

More than 350 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the New World; four species naturalized in China; two species naturalized in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms prostrate and branched at base. Leaf blades flat, usually broad. Inflorescence a panicle or the primary branches simple and raceme-like. Spikelets lanceolate, slightly laterally compressed, florets 2, solitary or paired at base; pedicels unequal; glumes herbaceous, 3–7-veined, subequal or lower glume slightly short, lower floret staminate or barren; lower glume and upper glume similar, palea membranous, narrow and small; upper floret bisexual; lemma leathery, with a semicircular to oblong callus, this laterally expanded into 2 membranous wings adnate to the lemma base, these often represented in dried material by scars, smooth and shiny, margins flat or inrolled palea; lodicules 2; style free from the base.

About 30 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the New World; one pantropical species occurs in China and Hong Kong.

Scramblers or woody lianas, with latex. Leaves opposite. Inflorescences cymose, terminal and/or axillary. Flowers small. Calyx with basal glands inside, lobes free. Corolla white, yellowish or red, salverform; tube widened near base, throat hairy; lobes oblong, falcate, overlapping to right in bud, with inflexed distal halves. Stamens included, inserted at or below middle of corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers sagittate, adherent to pistil head, cells spurred at base; disk entire, 5‑crenate or 5‑dentate, or deeply divided into 5 erect segments. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style, adnate basally to disk, pubescent; ovules numerous; pistil head ovoid or cup‑shaped. Fruit of paired follicles, spreading or divaricate. Seeds numerous, linear, compressed, unbeaked, with an apical coma.

Eight species distributed in SE Asia, N Australia, Pacific islands; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, deciduous or evergreen. Leaves altenate, rarely opposite, margin entire, crenate, serrate or spinose; stipules minute, callose, usually persistent. Inflorescences cymose, (simple or much branched), umbels or solitary and axillary on the current year's growth, or fasciculate and axillary on the second year's or older growth. Flowers small, white, pink, or red; regular, unisexual (plant dioecious). Male flowers: calyx patelliform, 4–6-lobed; corolla rotate, petals 4–8, slightly connate at base; stamens epipetalous; anthers oblong-ovate, with rounded base; rudimentary ovary subglobose. Female flowers: 4–8-merous; calyx persistent; petals connate and spreading; staminodes with sagittate sterile anthers; ovary ovoid, 4–7-loculate, style rarely developed, stigma discoid, capitate or columnar. Fruit a bacco-drupe, globose, mature red or black, with a membranous or chartaceous exocarp, a fleshy mesocarp, and distinct coriaceous, woody or stony endocarps. Pyrenes 4–7, smooth, striate, striate-sulcate or rugose and pitted, 1-seeded.

Over 400 species distributed in the tropical, subtropical, and warm temperate zones of both hemispheres; about 200 species in China; 17 species and one variety in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Scandent shrubs or lianas. Leaves alternate, 3-foliolate; petioles often twisted at middle; leaflets petiolulate, entire, pinnately veined. Flowers bisexual, in axillary cymose inflorescence; perianth-segments 10, in 2 series, the outer 5 united into a short tube at base, the inner 5 petaloid, valvate in buds; stamens 5, alternating with inner perianthsegments; filaments filiform, with glands or petaloid staminodes at the slightly dilated base; ovary inferior, 1-locular, ovule solitary, pendulous. Fruit an indehiscent achene, 2–4-winged.

About 18 species in tropical regions of the Old World; about 14 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Characters of the family except the lower 4 petals united into 2 lateral pairs; fruit a capsule, bursting elastically in 5 valves.

About 900 species chiefly in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World, with a few species in N America; more than 200 species in China; three species (included one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with long rhizomes. Culms erect, unbranched. Leaf blades lanceolate or linear, flat; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a contracted panicle, terminal, spike-like; spikelets paired, pedicellate, subequal, deciduous at maturity within a plumose involucre of hairs; rachis internodes and pedicels persistent, densely silky hairy; callus very small, pilose with long hairs usually exceeding out of the spikelet; glumes papery, subequal, lanceolate, abaxially long-pilose, apex and margins membranous; lower floret reduced to an empty hyaline veinless lemma, shorter than spikelet; upper lemma similar to the lower, hyaline membranous, veinless, awnless; palea short, broad; lodicules absent; stamens 1–2; styles 2, connate at base. Caryopsis elliptic.

About ten species distributed throughout the tropics and subtropics; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or herbs, rarely small trees, adpressed pubescent, with sparse medifixed (“T”-form) hairs, sometimes glandular hairy or with glands. Stipules deciduous or persistent; stipels present or absent. Leaves odd-pinnate, rarely digitately 3-foliolate or simple; leaflets usually opposite, rarely alternate, entire. Flowers in axillary racemes or clusters, sometimes in spikes or panicles. Bracts caducous. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed, subequal or lower one longer. Corolla purple or pink, rarely white or yellow, caducous; vexillum broadly elliptic, ovate or suborbicular, apex obtuse, emarginate or mucronate, shortly clawed, often persisting for a time; wings oblong or obovate, narrower, auriculate, slightly cohering with keel; keel lanceolate or oblanceolate, straight or curved, gibbous on each side and often spurred. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform with glandular tips. Ovary sessile; ovules 1–numerous; styles glabrous; stigma capitate, often penicillate. Pods linear or oblong, straight or curved, terete, 3–4-sided, or plano-compressed transversely between seeds. Seeds estrophiolate.

More than 700 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mostly in Africa; 81 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Indigofera decora Lindl. was recorded by Bentham (FHK 77. 1861), based on Col. Eyre's drawings, but no specimen has been found, so it is not described here.

Shrubby bamboos. Rhizomes leptomorph, with running underground stems. Culms pluricaespitose, nodding; internodes usually terete, usually with a dense, persistent, apical, yellow-brown tomentose to setaceous ring below nodes, rarely apically glabrous; wall thick; nodes usually flat, sometimes prominent. Branches usually solitary, nearly as thick as culms. Culm sheaths persistent, usually shorter than internodes, papery or nearly leathery; auricles usually developed; blade usually recurved, lanceolate. Leaf sheaths cylindrical, very thick, smooth. Leaves usually large relative to culm size, transverse veins distinct. Inflorescence largely ebracteate, terminal, a raceme or open panicle; branches usually subtended by tiny bracts. Spikelets several- to many-flowered, pedicellate. Rachilla articulate. Glumes 2–3, ovate or lanceolate; lemma oblong or lanceolate, nearly leathery; palea 2-keeled, shorter than lemma; lodicules 3. Stamens 3, long exserted; anthers yellow. Ovary ovoid; style 1, short; stigmas usually 2, plumose. Caryopsis dark brown at maturity.

At least 23 species distributed in mainly China, one species in Japan; 22 species (all endemic) in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, often twining, sometimes prostrate, erect, or floating. Leaves petiolate, entire, lobed, or divided. Inflorescences mostly axillary, cymose, 1–many‑flowered, rarely paniculate. Bracts various. Flowers small to large. Sepals persistent, equal to unequal, ± enlarged in fruit. Corolla variously coloured, rarely yellow, funnelform, campanulate, or salverform; limb 5‑lobed to entire, midpetaline bands well defined.
