Stamens inclusive or exserted; filaments filiform, usually unequal, dilated and pubescent at base; anthers ovate or linear, longitudinally dehiscent, not twisted; pollen grains globular, finely spiny. Disk annular. Ovary 2–4‑locular, 4‑ or 6‑ovuled. Style 1, filiform, inclusive or exserted; stigma capitate, or 2‑ or 3‑globular. Capsule globose or ovoid, 4‑ or 6‑valved. Seeds 4(–6) or fewer, glabrous or pubescent.

About 500 species widely distributed in tropical to warm temperate regions, especially of N & S America; 29 species in China; 17 species in Hong Kong.

In addition to the species described, Ipomoea horsfalliae Hook. (王子薯) and I. coccinea L. (橙紅蔦蘿) are occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, usually with short or long rhizomes (or bulbs), sometimes with swollen storage roots. Leaves mostly basal, 2-ranked, sword-shaped to linear. Aerial stem developed, much shorter than or longer than leaves. Inflorescence of rhipidia arranged in racemes, panicles, or solitary. Flowers white, yellow, blue, violet, or purple, relatively large, often fragrant. Perianth tube usually trumpet-shaped, sometimes very narrowly so, very short to long; outer 3 perianth segments (falls) ornamented or not, with a crested, bearded, or beardless claw (haft), and an expanded, usually reflexed limb (blade), the beard or crest (when present) extending along midvein of proximal part of limb adaxially; inner 3 perianth segments (standards) smaller, never ornamented, erect or spreading. Stamens opposed to style branches and appressed to them; filaments free, flattened. Style with 3 coloured, expanded, petaloid branches, arching over stamens, apex of branches extended as 2 lobes (crests) projecting beyond flap-like, abaxial stigma. Capsule globose, ellipsoidal, or cylindrical, apex beaked or not. Seeds pyriform, flattened and D-shaped, or irregularly angled, sometimes arillate.

About 225 species in temperate regions of the N hemisphere; 58 species (21 endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs; columns erect or procumbent. Leaf blades narrowly lanceolate to ovate, often with tubercle-based hairs; ligule a fringe of stiff hairs or obsolete. Inflorescence an open or contracted panicle, branches on all sides. Spikelets ovate or ovateglobose, always muticous, 2-flowered; the upper flower female or rarely hermaphrodite, the lower male or sometimes hermaphrodite, and both articulate on the rhachis; glumes subequal, herbaceous, falling soon after florets, 5–9-veined; lower lemma variable, similar to the upper or of different size and texture; upper lemma papery to leathery, glabrous or pubescent with short curved hairs, 5–7-veined; lodicules 2, small; stamens 3; styles 2, penicillate. Caryopsis ellipsoidal or subglobose.

About 90 species distributed in the tropics, but mainly in Asia; 18 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect or geniculate at base, often much branched. Leaf blades linear to lanceolate, sometimes with a pseudo-petiole; ligule membranous. Inflorescence of paired racemes as a solitary cylindrical raceme, or occasionally subdigitate, terminal and axillary, exserted or sometimes supported by a spatheole; spikelets paired, similar or not; rachis internodes and pedicels stoutly linear to thickly clavate, U-shaped or triquetrous in cross section, usually triquetrous or slightly compressed, fragile at maturity. Sessile spikelet dorsally compressed; callus truncate or obtuse, inserted into hollow internode apex; lower glume oblong or lanceolate, papery to leathery, often rugose, apex usually flat; upper glume boat-shaped, awnless or with straight awn from apex; lower floret staminate or neuter, palea developed; upper floret bisexual, lemma usually deeply 2-lobed, awned from sinus, rarely awnless; awn geniculate, glabrous; lodicules 2, obcuneate. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile or much smaller, upper lemma sometimes geniculately awned.

About 70 species spread throughout the tropics but mainly in Asia, especially in India; 12 species in China; five species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, shrubs or subshrubs, with thick, woody rhizomes. Leaves opposite, usually petiolate and toothed. Cymes axillary and terminal, (1–)3–many‑flowered, arranged in lax thyrses or panicles, rarely in dense spikes. Flowers pedicellate. Calyx campanulate to tubular‑campanulate, straight or declined, often accrescent; limb equally or subequally 5‑toothed or 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑toothed, lower lip 2‑toothed. Corolla tube exserted, declined or abruptly deflexed, sometimes straight, ± saccate to spurred abaxially near base, 2‑lipped; upper lip 4‑cleft, recurved or reflexed; lower lip entire, concave, navicular. Stamens 4, declined; filaments free, edentate; anther 2‑celled apex usually confluent. Style apex short 2‑cleft. Nutlets subcircular or occasionally oblong to ovoid, glabrous or hairy, smooth, granular or dotted.

About 100 species mainly in tropical and subtropical Asia, only a few species in Africa; 77 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, petiolate, pinnately-veined, margin usually glandular-dentate or serrate, rarely entire; stipules small, usually deciduous. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate, many-flowered. Flowers bisexual, small. Calyx tube adnate to base of ovary, obconical, cupular or hemispherical; lobes 5, persistent. Petals 5, valvate, erect or reflexed at anthesis. Stamens 5, alternate with petals; filaments subulate; anthers ovoid to ellipsoidal. Ovary superior to semi-inferior, 2 – 3-locular, long ellipsoidal; ovules many, 2-seriate on axile placentation; style simple, striate, sometimes divided into middle; stigma capitate. Capsules conical to long ellipsoidal, apex cleft, with persistent calyx lobes and petals. Seeds many, flattened oblong.


About 27 species mainly distributed in SE Asia, one species in N America; 15 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; stem mostly erect, sometimes stoloniferous, branched. Leaves pinnately divided or simple, basal ones persistent at flowering stage. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and bisexual, corymbose at terminal. Involucres cylindric; phyllaries 2–4‑seriate. Ligulate florets (5–)7–27 per head, corolla yellow, rarely white or purplish red; stylar branches slender; anther bases sagittate. Cypselae brown, rarely black, obtusely 8–10‑ribbed, hirtelleous along ribs particularly in upper portion, apex acute and forming filiform beak. Pappus white or brownish, scaberulous.

About 20–25 species, distributed in E to SE Asia; about 13 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial lactiferous herbs, usually glaucous. Radical leaves persistent at anthesis, long‑petiolate; cauline ones alternate. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, corymbose at terminal. Involucres cylindric or campanulate at flowering stage, sometimes becoming ovoid when fruiting; phyllaries in 2–3 series, herbaceous, glabrous. Receptacle plain, naked. Ligulate florets 10–30 per head, corolla yellow, white or purple, ligule 5‑toothed at apex; anther bases sagittate, stylar branches slender. Cypselae compressed, brown, fusiform or elliptic, acutely and sharply 10‑ribbed as wings, glabrous, apex attenuate into filiform beak, shorter than the cypsela body. Pappus 2‑seriate, white, unequal in length, scaberulous.

About 20 species distributed in E to S Asia; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves entrie; stipules small or wanting. Inflorescence a dichasium, axillary. Flowers small. Sepals 5, connate at base. Petals 5, convolute, persistent. Stamens 5–20, inserted outside and against disk. Disk bowl-shaped, entire or slightly lobed, free from ovary. Ovary 5-loculed, with 2 pendulous ovules per locule. Style 1; stigma capitate or mushroom-shaped. Capsule ellipsoidal or conical, leathery or woody, septicidal, sometimes with a false septum at middle of each carpel. Seeds winged or crowned with a calyptriform aril; endosperm fleshy; embryo straight.

Three species distributed in tropical Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite, rarely in whorls of 3, petiolate or sessile. Stipules interpetiolar, usually united at the base into a sheath, apex pointed. Flowers in terminal, dense trichotomous or corymbiform cymes. Calyx‑tube usually ovoid; limb with 4(–5) persistent teeth. Corolla salverform; tube slender; lobes 4(–5), imbricate or contorted in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the throat; filaments short or wanting; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style filiform, with 2 stigmatic lobes. Fruit a drupe, globular or slightly depressed, with leathery or fleshy exocarp.

About 400 species in the tropics, but mainly in the Old World; 19 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Ornamental species such as Ixora coccinea L. (紅仙丹花、橙紅龍船花) and Ixora coccinea f. lutea (Hutch.) F. R. Fosberg & H. H. Sachet (黃龍船花、黃花龍船花) are also cultivated locally.

Trees, sometimes shrubs; stems glabrous or hairy. Leaves opposite, (1–)2‑pinnately compound, rarely simple, leaflets many, small. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate. Calyx small, campanulate to tubular, truncate or 5‑dentate. Corolla blue or bluish purple, tubular to campanulate, limb slightly bilabiate, 5‑lobed, finely pubescent abaxially. Stamens 4, included; anthers glabrous, thecae unequal or 1‑celled. Staminodes elongate, glandular, longer than fertile stamens. Disk annular. Ovary compressed conical, hairy; ovules in 8 rows per locule. Capsules woody, elliptic or oblong, tardily dehiscent. Seeds flat, transparent or brown winged.

About 50 species distributed in tropical America; two species introduced to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs or woody vines, rarely erect, hairy, rarely glabrous. Leaves petiolate, base often cordate, margin entire, rarely dentate or lobed. Inflorescences axillary, often umbelliform or capitate cymes, or solitary flowers; bracts linear, subulate, or leaflike. Sepals equal or unequal. Corolla funnelform or campanulate, with 5 distinct midpetaline bands; limb 5‑toothed or subentire. Stamens inclusive; pollen grains globose, not spiny. Disk small or absent. Pistil inclusive; ovary 2‑locular; ovules 2 per locule. Style 1, filiform; stigmas 2, elliptic or oblong, flat. Capsule globose, 4‑ or 8‑valved. Seeds 4 or fewer, smooth or minutely papillate, glabrous or velutinous, abaxial edges often with a narrow wing.

About 120 species mainly distributed in N & S America, a few species also in Africa and Asia; one species and one variety in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody lianas, with white latex. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Cymes extra‑axillary, umbel‑like, simple or dichotomous. Calyx deeply 5‑parted, usually eglandular, segments erect and connate at base. Corolla salverform or urn‑shaped; tube elongate, base broad, throat constricted or slightly dilated, with 5 pairs of longitudinal lines of hairs inside; lobes 5, twisted to right, usually longer than tube, acuminate in bud. Corona‑lobes 5, adnate to back of stamens, erect, apex free, dorsally compressed, with board‑shaped processes on back, conspicuous, rarely minute or obsolete. Filaments connate into a short tube; anthers with apical membranous appendage, erect or inflexed on stigma head; pollinia 1 in each anther‑cell, erect. Stigma head conical or capitate, included in apical anther membrane. Follicles lanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, apex acuminate. Seeds comose.

About five species distributed in China and Thailand; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Scandent or erect shrubs, deciduous or evergreen. Branchlets terete or quadrangular. Leaves opposite or alternate, simple, 3‑foliolate, or odd‑pinnate, margin entire; petiole articulate. Inflorescences dichasial, thyrsoid, sometimes racemose, paniculate, umbelliform or capitate, rarely flowers solitary; bracts subulate or linear, sometimes leafy. Flowers bisexual, usually fragrant. Calyx campanulate, cupular, or funnelform, 4–12‑lobed. Corolla white or yellow, rarely red or purple, salverform or funnelform; tube long; lobes 4–12, imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, included, inserted about middle of corolla tube; filaments short; anthers introrse. Ovary 2‑locular, usually 2 ovules in each locule. Style filiform; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit a berry, didymous or one half aborted. Seed 1 in each carpel, with little or without endosperm; radicle downward.

About 300 species, mainly in temperate and tropical zones, one species in the Mediterranean region; 43 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or tall herbs with milky or watery juice. Leaves alternate, unlobed or palmately lobed; petioles usually biglandular at apex; stipules small, setiform or modified into a series of stipitate glands. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious, rarely dioecious), in terminal or axillary cymes or panicles. Male flowers: sepals 5, imbricate, slightly connate at the base; petals 5, imbricate, free or sometimes connate at the base; disk-glands 5, free or connate into annular; stamens 8–12, sometimes more, in 2–6 series, filaments ± connate, anthers 2-celled; pistillode filamentous or absent. Female flowers: sepals 5–6, free, imbricate, usually persistent; disk annular, lobed or dissected, sometimes with staminodes; ovary 2–5-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles unlobed or bifid, sometimes dilated. Fruits capsular; seeds carunculate; testa crustaceous; albumen fleshy.

About 175 species in tropics and subtropics of America; five species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs, annual or perennial, with or without a rhizome, stoloniferous or only with fibrous roots. Culms tufted or scattered, usually compressed triquetrous. Leaves usually basal; leaf blade slightly short, with slightly long to short sheaths. Bracts few, leaf-shaped. Anthela simple or compound, laxly spreading to congested into capitulum; anthelas elongate or abbreviated, rarely nearly absent. Spikelets few to many, arranged into spikes or fascicles; rachilla not articulate at base, persistent, narrowly winged or wingless; scales distichous, gradually deciduous from base to apex of rachilla at maturity, basalmost 1–2 usually without a flower but remaining ones each with a bisexual flower. Flowers without hypogynous segments or scale-like perianth parts. Stamens (1–)3; connective prominent above anther or not. Style base not swollen; stigmas 2(–3), deciduous at maturity. Achene biconvex, plano-convex, 1 side facing rachilla, surface prominently puncticulate, reticulately striate, or rarely smooth.

About ten species distributed in Africa, America, Asia, Australia and C Europe; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Rhizome shortly or long creeping. Stems often tufted. Leaves either all basal or also cauline; leaf sheath open on 1 side, apex often auriculate; leaf blade grass-like, terete, or scale-like. Inflorescence terminal, or pseudolateral when basal involucral bract seemingly a continuation of stem, usually many-flowered; ultimate divisions into dense heads, lax cymes, or 1-flowered. Bracteoles present or absent. Perianth segments 6, in 2 whorls, papery to hyaline. Stamens 6 or 3, attached to base of perianth segments; filaments filiform, anthers oblong or linear. Ovary 1–2-locular; placentae 3, parietal, sometimes inconspicuously prominent but more frequently protruding and sometimes connate at middle; ovules many per locule; style 1; stigmas twisted. Capsule 3-valved; valves usually bearing placentae at middle. Seeds ovoid or oblong, minute, sometimes appendaged.

About 240 species widely distributed in both hemispheres, most abundant in temperate and cold regions, rarely tropical; 76 species in China; two species and one subspecies in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, monoecious or dioecious; branchlets not arranged in a plane, terete or 3-, 4-, or 6-angled in cross section. Leaves scalelike or needlelike, scalelike leaves opposite or decussate, rarely in whorls of 3, needlelike leaves usually opposite or in whorls of 3, base not jointed; juvenile leaves always needlelike; adult leaves scalelike or needlelike, usually not dimorphic along branchlets but sometimes different on juvenile and adult branchlets, with 1 or 2 pale stomatal bands adaxially, or in addition a few stomata near base abaxially. Pollen cones solitary, axillary or terminal, yellow, ovoid or globose; microsporophylls 6–16, each with 2– 8 pollen sacs. Seed cones terminal or axillary, berrylike or drupelike, globose or ovoid, indehiscent or slightly dehiscent when mature in (1st or) 2nd (or 3rd) year; cone scales connate or fused, succulent; each fertile scale bearing 1–3 seeds; free bract apex a small point. Seeds 1–6 per cone, wingless, usually with resin pits. Cotyledons 2–6.

About 60 species, widely distributed in temperate to subtropical areas of N hemisphere; 23 species (ten endemic, two introduced) in China; one species widely cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, subshrubs or shrubs with cystoliths. Leaves sessile or petiolate, margin entire or sinuate. Inflorescence of terminal and/or axillary spikes or dichasia, sometimes compound, paniculate. Bracts very variable in shape, sometimes prominent and/or brightly coloured, margin entire; bracteoles usually 2, narrow, or absent. Calyx deeply 4–5‑lobed, lobes equal or subequal, linear. Corolla tubular or funnel‑shaped, with a distinct tube, strongly bilabiate, upper lip erect, apex acuminate, entire or 2‑lobed, lower lip patent, obovate, 3‑lobed, lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, filaments usually dilated, anthers 2‑thecous, thecae oblong or spherical, at same height or superposed, one or both spurred or not at the base. Staminodes absent. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma slightly bilobed. Capsule sessile or with a solid stalk, usually clavate, retinacula present, 2 – 4‑seeded. Seeds compressed, tuberculate.

About 600 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 70 species in China; nine species in Hong Kong.

Woody vines, glabrous (except K. induta A. C. Sm.); dioecious or monoecious. Leaves alternate, exstipulate; blade papery to leathery, elliptic to ovate, apex acute or acuminate, base cuneate (especially when young), obtuse, truncate or subcordate, margins denticulate to entire. Flowers unisexual, generally solitary in axils of leaves or fugacious bracts, occasionally with secondary flower growing in axils of bract, or in clusters of 2–4 forming glomerules, occasionally cauliflorous; tepals 7–24. Staminate flowers with androecium of numerous (13–80) stamens; stamens sometimes ± free but adnate at base of filaments and occasionally with several subulate appendages attached to distal apex of receptacle, stamens sometimes aggregated into subglobose head with connectives either broader than thick with thecae of adjacent stamens contiguous, or else with connective as broad as thick with thecae of adjacent stamens not contiguous; pollen hexacolpate, distally syncolpate. Pistillate flowers with gynoecium of numerous (17–ca. 300) free carpels; stigmatic crest forming subulate or laterally flattened “pseudostyle”, or modified as subpeltate or irregular “pseudostigma”; ovary with 1–5(–11) pendulous or ventrally attached ovules. Fruit an aggregate of apocarps attached to ellipsoid or clavate receptacle; apocarps subglobose to obovoid or elongate-obovoid, ripening red or yellow. Seeds 1–5(–11), smooth.

Sixteen species in tropical to temperate regions of E and SE Asia; eight species in China and two species in Hong Kong.

Succulent herbs, subshrubs or shrubs, usually with erect stems. Leaves opposite or in whorls, sometimes alternate on the upper part of stems, simple, lobed or pinnately compound. Flowers 4-merous, usually colored and showy, in terminal paniculate cymes. Sepals free or united, often inflated at base, apex 4-lobed. Petals united, tubular or salverform, apex 4-lobed. Stamens twice as many as corollalobes, in two whorls, attached to corolla-tube; scales (nectariferous appendages) 4, linear or suborbicular. Ovary superior; carpels 4, free, apically narrowed into styles. Fruit a group of follicles, many-seeded.

About 145 species in S Africa, Madagascar and S America, but with a few species naturalized elsewhere; about seven species (three introduced) in China; five species (cultivated or naturalized) in Hong Kong.

Perennial rhizomatous herbs. Leaves alternate, entire or serrate, sessile or petiolate. Capitula solitary or in loose corymb form, heterogamous, radiate. Involucre hemispherical; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, imbricate, herbaceous, membranous along the margin. Receptacle convex, alveolate. Ray florets uniseriate, female, corolla ligular, pilose, white, pink or purple. Disk florets perfect, tubular, trumpet‑shaped, the limb 5‑lobed, yellow changing to red or purple; stamens exserted, anthers rounded and entire at base; stylar branches flattened, with subulate or ovate, acute appendages. Cypselae of ray florets trigonous, 3‑ribbed; those of the disk florets compressed, 2‑ribbed; pappus coronate, scarious.

About 20 species distributed in E & S Asia; seven species in China; one species native to Hong Kong.

This genus is very similar to Aster, with the only difference that the former one has pappus less developed, appearing as a scarious crown or scale‑like bristles no longer than 1 mm.

Trees. Branches terete. Leaves leathery, entire. Inflorescences axillary, cymes, 4–9-flowered, pedunculate. Calyx deeply 5-lobed, subtended by connate, cup-like bracteoles. Petals 5, with long setae in sinus between petals, 2-lobed; lobes apically fimbriate. Stamens numerous, or rarely indefinite; anthers 4-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary inferior, 1-loculed; ovules 6 per locule. Style filiform; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit with persistent calyx, attached to plant until falling with viviparous seedling. Seed 1, germinating on plant. Hypocotyl cylindrical, spindle-shaped or clavate, apex pointed.

Two species distributed in E and SE Asia; one species in China; also in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees; crown broad; bark grey, fissured; branches whorled, spreading. Leaves spirally and usually ± pectinately arranged, linear to linear-lanceolate, flattened, midvein raised on both sides, stomatal lines present or absent adaxially, usually 2 bands separated by midvein abaxially, vascular bundle 1, resin canals 2, sublateral, marginal; petiole short, slightly enlarged at base. Pollen cones lateral or terminal, 4–8 in umbellate clusters; pollen 2-saccate. Seed cones terminal, solitary, erect, maturing in the current year. Seed scales woody, persistent. Bracts ligulate-spatulate, shorter than seed scales, persistent, not exserted, apex 3-lobed. Seeds large, triangular-oblong, covered on 1 side by wing, together as long as seed scales. Cotyledons 2–4.

Five species: China, Laos, Vietnam; five species (three endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves paripinnate; leaflets entire. Panicles axillary or subterminal. Flowers bisexual, 4–5-merous. Calyx parted nearly to base; lobes imbricate. Petals distinct, imbricate, much longer than calyx when in bud. Staminal tube urceolate; anthers 8–10, inserted on inside apical part of the tube. Disk cup-shaped. Ovary 4–5-locular; ovules 12–16(–18) per locule, amphitropous. Stigma disciform, with 4 grooves on apex. Capsule globose or nearly so, woody, apically 4- or 5-valvate when mature. Seeds broad, oblong to suborbicular, margin with round membranous wing.

Seven species in tropical Africa, Madagascar; one species cultivated in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Leaves opposite. Stipules united into a short sheath, entire or fringed with bristle‑like teeth. Flowers in terminal cymes or corymbs; the branches often lengthened into one‑sided spikes. Calyx‑tube ovoid; limb with 4 minute persistent teeth. Corolla salverform; tube slender, hairy in throat; lobes 4, valvate in the bud. Stamens 4, attached to the throat of corolla; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 pendulous ovule in each locule; style filiform; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit small and dry; separating into 2 valves from the base upward or falling off together, leaving a persistent filiform axis.

About seven to nine species distributed in tropical Asia and Africa; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, deciduous, polygamo-monoecious or polygamo-dioecious. Leaves imparipinnate or bipinnate, exstipulate; leaflets alternate or opposite, usually serrate or parted, rarely entire. Thyrses terminal, rarely axillary, large; branches many, spreading. Flowers zygomorphic. Sepals (4–)5, valvate, outer 2 smaller. Petals 4(–5), slightly unequal in length, adaxially with 2-lobed scales at base, clawed. Disk thick, apex often crenate. Stamens often 8, sometimes fewer, inserted on disk; filaments distinct, often villous. Ovary 3-locular; ovules 2 per locule, on upper half of middle axis; style short or slightly longer; stigma 3-lobed or entire. Capsules swollen, ovoid, ellipsoidal, or subglobose, trigonous, loculicidal into 3 schizocarps; carpels membranous, reticulate. Seeds 1 per locule, globose, arillodes absent.

Three species distributed in Japan, China and Fiji; three species in China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shurbs with white latex. Leaves opposite. Cymes terminal, 3 – many‑flowered, bracteate; peduncle long or short; bracteoles small or large. Flowers white or rose, 5‑merous. Calyx small, deeply divided, without glands. Corolla salverform; tube 2.3 – 5 cm, narrow, dilated at or below apex; throat without scales, pilose inside; lobes overlapping to right. Stamens inserted above middle of corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers narrowly oblong or ovate, included, free from pistil head, base rounded; disk scales alternate with ovaries. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style; ovules 2 per locule; style filiform; pistil head thickened, with short basal collar and apiculate apex. Fruit a drupe, solitary or paired, ellipsoidal, often with a large appendage. Seeds oblong or ovoid, flattened, not comose.

About 20 species distributed from China and Myanmar to N Australia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Parasitic shrubs or subshrubs, monoecious. Branches opposite or dichotomous; stem usually flattened, successive internodes in the same plane. Leaves scale-like, in 2 ranks, usually fused into a ring. Inflorescence axillary, cymose, 1-flowered at first, later the flowers in each group developing successively to form a dense cluster; peduncle and pedicel nearly absent; bracts absent, but flowers subtended by hairs. Male flower globose in mature bud; perianth lobes 3; anthers sessile, 2-celled, introrse, connate into a synandrium, dehiscing longitudinally. Female flower ovoid in mature bud; placentation free, central; style absent; stigma nipple-shaped. Fruit a berry, ellipsoidal or pyriform, crowned by persistent perianth.

About 25 species distributed in tropical and temperate regions of the Old World (except Europe); one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Annual prostrate or decumbent herbs. Stems many-branched, pubescent. Stipules 2, large, persistent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate. Flowers 1–2, axillary, often reduced and without petals. Bract 1; bracteoles 4, persistent. Calyx 5-toothed, teeth equal; vexillum subequal to wings, shorter than keel. Corolla and stamen-tube of flowers deciduous in fruiting, abortive or cleistogamous flowers persistent. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary 1-ovuled. Pods compressed, indehiscent, 1-seeded.

Two species distributed in E Asia; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennials. Rhizome short or horizontally creeping, sometimes knotty. Leaves basal, 3-ranked, the blades elongate or reduced; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaf-like. Inflorescence capitate. Spikes 1–few, sessile, cylindrical, ellipsoidal or globose; axis short. Spikelets many, falling entire, crowded, bilaterally flattened. Glumes several, 2-ranked, strongly laterally flattened, sides membranous to hyaline, veins 0– several, keel strongly acute, sometimes winged, smooth, spinulose or serrulate. Flowers 1–5 per spikelet, bisexual or male in upper glumes. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 2–3. Stigmas 2. Achenes 1–2 per spikelet, laterally biconvex with one margins facing the axis.

About 75 species in temperate, subtropical and tropical regions of both hemispheres; seven species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial twining or suberect herbs. Stipules reflexed, persistent; stipels lanceolate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate. Racemes axillary, nodes of rhachis swollen. Calyx campanulate, 2-lipped, upper lip entire or emarginate, lower lip 3-lobed. Corolla purple or white; vexillum orbicular, reflexed, auriculate at base, with 2 callosities on adaxial surface; wings oblong; keel incurved at a right angle. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform; styles abruptly upturned, laterally compressed, bearded in upper part, stigma terminal. Pods obliquely oblong-falcate, compressed, sinuous with minute warts along both sutures, shallowly septate between seeds within. Seeds slightly compressed, dark brown, hilum linear with white aril.

One species and three subspecies native of Africa, now widely cultivated throughout the tropics; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial lactiferous herbs. Leaves simple or divided. Capitula homogamous will all florets ligulate, arranged as corymbs or panicles at stem and branch terminals. Involucres ovoid; phyllaries 3–5‑seriate, imbricate. Receptacle plain, naked. Ligulate florets about 7–25 per head, yellow, ligule truncate and 5‑lobed at apex, bisexual and fertile; anther bases sagittate; stylar branches slender. Cypselae brown, obovate, oblanceolate or elongate‑elliptic, compressed, slightly (1 or )3–10‑ribbed on each side, apex acute and forming filiform beak usually 2–4 times longer than the cypsela, or sometimes as long as or shorter than the cypsela. Pappus bristles white, in 2 rows, scaberulous or capillary.

About 75 species mainly distributed in N America, Europe, C & W Asia, Mediterranean regions; seven species in China; one species with many cultivars in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, glabrous. Branches terete. Leaves decussate, leathery, often with a gland or a small hole near tip of midvein on abaxial surface. Flowers showy, axillary, solitary or in racemes or panicles. Bracts leaf-like; bracteoles 2, caducous. Flowers 8–16(–many). Calyx campanulate or oblate, leathery, 10–12-toothed, teeth long-deltoid, membranous, without appendage. Petals 8–12, inserted on throat of calyx-tube, clawed and crisped. Stamens 16–32, inserted at middle of calyx-tube, whorled, long and erect, filaments filiform; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 1-locular or imperfectly 2-locular; ovules numerous; styles very long; stigma capitate. Capsules hard, imperfectly loculicidal dehiscing into 2 – 4 valves, or irregularly dehiscing at apex.

Ten species distributed in tropical America; one species introduced into China and Hong Kong.

Annual climbing vines, monoecious, softly pubescent. Tendrils bifid. Petioles with 2 glands at apex. Flowers large, white, solitary. Male flowers: pedicels long; calyx-tube narrowly campanulate or infundibuliform, lobes 5; corolla lobes 5, free, spreading; stamens 3, filaments distinct, anthers inclusive, slightly coalescent or distinct, ellipsoid, one 1-celled, two 2-celled, cells sigmoid, connective not protrudent; pistillode glandular. Female flowers: pedicels short; calyx-tube cupular, calyx lobes and corolla as in male flowers; ovary ovoid or cylindrical, placentas 3, styles short, stigmas 3, 2-lobed; ovules many, horizontal. Fruits polymorphic, indehiscent, fleshy. Pericarp woody when mature. Seeds many, obovate, compressed, marginate.

Six species, mainly distributed in tropical African region; one species cultivated in China, also in Hong Kong.

Small perennial rhizomatous or stoloniferous herbs; stem scapiform. Leaves radical and rosulate. Capitula solitary, heterogamous, radiate. Involucre hemispherical; phyllaries 2–4‑seriate. Receptacle convex, without palea, areole with a central projection. Marginal ray florets in 1–several series, fertile. Disk tubular florets few, corolla 4–5‑lobed, bisexual or functionally staminate, bearing no fruits; anther bases obtuse, entire; stylar branches flattened with lanceolate or triangular papillose apical appendages. Cypselae compressed with thick margins, obovate to oblanceolate, glabrous, shortly beaked, no pappus.

About five species distributed from Japan to SE Asia, Australia and New Zealand, also in C & S America; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Stipules minute, deciduous. Leaves opposite, subopposite or fasciculate on upper parts of branchlets, entire. Panicles terminal or axillary; pedicels articulate. Flowers showy, actinomorphic. Calyx oblate or turbinate, leathery, angled or winged, 5–9-lobed. Petals 6, or as many as calyx-lobes, base clawed, margin crisped. Stamens 6– numerous, inserted near base of calyx-tube, filament slender, not equal in length. Ovary 3–6-locular; ovules numerous in each locule; styles filiform, with a capitate stigma. Capsules woody, base surrounded by persistent calyx and adherent with it, loculicidally opening in 3 – 6 valves. Seeds numerous, terminating in a wing.

About 55 species distributed in Asia and Atlantic; 16 species in China; four species (three cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, or with basal part woody. Stem erect, tomentose, pubescent or glabrous. Leaves alternate, sessile, margin entire or toothed, base often decurrent and forming wings on the stem. Capitula many, heterogamous, disciform, in racemes on axillary branches. Involucres campanulate or subhemispherical; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate, outer layers shorter and herbaceous, often recurved, inner ones longer and scarious. Receptacle plain, nude. Florets yellow to purple. Marginal ones many, female and fertile, corolla filiform‑tubular, usually 4‑lobed, or sometimes 3‑ or 5‑lobed; stylar branches obtuse. Disk florets few, hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, apex with 5 lobes; anther base sagittate or shortly 2‑cleft, lobes obtuse or acute, often unequal in length; stylar branches linear‑subulate, papillose. Cypselae elliptic‑oblong, 10‑ribbed, glabrous or hairy. Pappus bristles 1‑seriate, white, deciduous.

About 20 species, native to tropical Africa and SE Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect or scandent shrubs, aromatic, pubescent or glabrous. Branches tetragonal, sometimes prickly. Leaves simple, opposite, crenate, often rugose. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, capitate, pedunculate. Bracts large, wider at base; bracteoles tiny. Calyx small, membranous, limb truncate or sinuate dentate. Corolla with different colours in the same capitula, nearly actinomorphic or slightly 2‑lipped, tube slender; lobes 4 or 5, spreading. Stamens 4, didynamous, inclusive, anthers ovoid, thecae parallel. Ovary 2‑locular. Style inclusive; stigma obliquely subcapitate. Drupes baccate, with two 1‑seeded pyrenes.

About 150 species distributed in tropical and subtropical America, one species naturalized in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

L. montevidensis (Spreng.) Briq. (小葉馬纓丹; Photo 155) and L. trifolia L. (三葉臭金鳳) are cultivated as ornamentals.

Perennial, evergreen, marsh or aquatic herbs. Stem erect or ascending, robust. Leaves several crowded at stem-apex; petiole long, prickly, sheathed at base; blade of juvenile leaves sagittate-hastate, that of adult leaves bipinnatifid-pedate, abaxially prickly on midrib and lateral veins. Peduncle long, prickly; spathe widened at base, apex elongate and twisted, opened by a slit when mature; spadix sessile, cylindrical, densely flowered. Flowers bisexual; tepals 4( or 6), free; stamens 4 – 6; ovary 1-locular, 1-ovuled; style very short; stigma suborbicular. Fruit a berry. Seed large, compressed, subcuneate.

Two species distributed in tropical Asia; one species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, often with disagreeable odour when bruised. Branches terete but compressed at the nodes. Leaves opposite, distichous, often with distinct transverse veins. Stipules interpetiolar, pointed, with a broad base. Flowers small, in axillary clusters, cymes or heads. Calyx‑tube short; limb short or long, 3–6‑toothed. Corolla funnel‑shaped or salverform; tube usually dilated at the top, the throat villose; lobes 4–6, valvate in the bud. Stamens 4–6, attached to the corolla‑throat; filaments short; anthers often apiculate, dorsifixed, included in the tube or shortly exserted. Ovary 4–9‑locular, with 1 erect ovule in each locule; style divided at the top into 4–9 stigmatic linear lobes. Fruit a drupe, with four to nine 1‑seeded pyrenes.

About 180 species in tropical Asia, Australia and W Africa; 33 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Biennial or perennial herbs or subshrubs. Leaves undivided or pinnatilobed to pinnatifid, margin usually toothed. Capitula homogamous, all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, racemose, corymbose, paniculate or fasciculate at stem terminal, or solitary. Involucres cylindric; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, outer layers short, inner layers much longer. Receptacle plain, naked. Ligulate florets yellow or reddish purple, ligule truncate and 5‑toothed at apex; stylar branches slender; anther bases sagittate. Cypselae 3–6‑ribbed, apex truncate and beakless. Pappus capillary, white, persistent or deciduous as a whole ring.

About 50 species distributed in Africa, Europe and Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, with milky latex. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, rarely radical and forming rosette. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves or in terminal racemes. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes unequal or subequal. Corolla salverform, slightly zygomorphic; limb 5‑lobed, subequal. Stamens 5, partly or all adnate to corolla‑tube; anthers coherent, sometimes bearded at apex. Ovary inferior, 2‑locular, with numerous ovules; style slender; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, opening by 2 valves.

About 25 species in W North America, Australia, Mediterranean region and S Africa; one species naturalized in S China and in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, often armed. Leaves decussate, entire, shortly petiolate. Flowers 4-merous, in large panicles. Calyx-tube very short, lobes 4, without appendages. Petals 4, crisped and clawed. Stamens 8, sometimes 4 – 12, in pairs inserted at the base of calyx-tube, exserted from corolla. Ovary 2–4-locular, style long. Capsules imperfectly enveloped by calyx, irregularly dehiscent or indehiscent. Seeds numerous, exalate.

Only one species, widely cultivated in tropical regions.

Perennial, aquatic or marsh herbs. Culms slender, with swollen, hairy nodes, erect or ascending from the creeping or floating base. Leaf blades mainly cauline, linear-lanceolate; ligule papery. Inflorescence a lax panicle, branches often simple and raceme-like, pedicels short. Spikelets 1-flowered, elliptic to narrowly oblong, strongly laterally compressed, not stipitate, disarticulating from pedicel; glumes absent; lemma boat-shaped, keeled, papery to leathery, prominently 5-veined, marginal veins interlocking with marginal veins of palea, keel scabrid to pectinate ciliate, apex acute or beaked, awnless or awned; palea resembling lemma but narrower, 3-veined, keel ciliate. Stamens 1, 2, 3, or 6. Caryopsis oblong; hilum linear.

Approximately 20 species in tropical and warm temperate regions of the world; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Small aquatic herbs, free floating or submersed. Fronds flat, 1– many cohering together, each with a single long root on abaxial surface, green, or sometimes reddish abaxially, margin entire, with (1–)2 lateral pouches at base, reproducing daughter fronds and flower (rarely in most species); veins 1–5(–7), leaving from node towards apex. Daughter fronds connected to mother frond by a thin white stipe or a green stalk. Flowers minute, petalless, male and female separate but surrounded by same small membranous spathe: stamens 2, anthers 4-celled; pistil 1, 1–7-ovuled. Seeds longitudinally ribbed.

About 13 species distributed nearly worldwide; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect herbs. Leaves opposite, often lobed or dissected. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming terminal spikes; bracteoles subulate or spinescent. Calyx obconical or tubular‑campanulate, 5‑veined and 5‑toothed; teeth subulate or prickly, subequal. Corolla white, reddish, to purplish, 2‑lipped; tube exserted; upper lip entire, erect, villous or glabrous; lower lip ± spreading, spotted, 3‑lobed, the middle lobe deeply notched or obcordate, larger than lateral lobes. Stamens 4, in 2 pairs, ascending under the upper lip; the lower pair slightly longer; anther 2‑celled, with parallel transverse cells. Disk uniform. Style equally 2‑fid, lobes subulate. Nutlets smooth, triquetrous, truncate at apex.

About 20 species distributed in Africa, Asia, Europe, N & S America; 12 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs with cystoliths. Leaves petiolate, margin entire or crenate‑serrate. Inflorescence of axillary and terminal densely bracteate spikes, usually one‑sided. Bract usually scarious, larger than calyx‑lobes; bracteoles similar but smaller. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed, lobes unequal, anterior two fused at base or free, posterior one larger than others, lateral lobes smallest. Corolla tubular, suddenly ventricose in middle, limb bilabiate, upper lip shallowly 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted near middle of corolla tube, exserted from mouth of corolla; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae at same level, muticous. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules per locule; style filiform; stigma capitellate, minutely bifid or entire. Capsule oblong or conical, usually 4‑angled, retinacula present, 4‑ or 2‑seeded. Seeds ovate‑oblong or orbicular, flattened, pubescent with hygroscopic hairs.

About 100 species in tropical regions of the Old World and few in America; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs, sometimes subshrubs or climbers, usually with simple or glandular hairs. Leaves basal and cauline, entire or pinnately dissected, petiolate or sessile. Racemes terminal and axillary. Sepals 4, ovate or oblong, base not saccate; petals 4, white, pink or yellowish, linear to spathulate, sometimes rudimentary or absent. Stamens 6, 2 or 4, base with minute glands. Ovary 2-ovuled, stigma capitate, entire or rarely 2-lobed. Silicles ovate, elliptic to orbiculate. Seeds oblong or ovate, 1 per locule, winged or not, cotyledons incumbent, rarely accumbent or diplecolobal.

About 180 species distributed in all continents except Antarctic; 16 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with short, woody rhizome, often stoloniferous. Stems tufted, usually nodeless, terete, compressed, or 3–4-angular. Leaves basal, equitant, similar to the stems. Inflorescence paniculate. Bracts shorter than the inflorescence, the lowest with a short pungent blade, the upper ones smaller and shorter. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate. Flowers usually 2–4, the upper one bisexual, the lower one(s) sterile, or male by reduction. Rachilla short, straight. Glumes 4–7, spirally arranged, imbricate, scaberulous at the top. Perianth segments 3 or 6 biseriate, white hypogynous scales, which are narrow, hyaline (therefore easily overlooked in young flowers), under the fruit broadened and incrassate, spongiose, ovate to lanceolate, shorter than the achene. Stamens 3, anthers linear, connective distinctly produced. Style continuous with the ovary, stigmas 3; style base persistent, at the first bulbous to dome-shaped, ultimately depressedhemispherical. Achene oblong or oblong-elliptic, obtusely trigonous, crusty, often smooth and shining when ripe.

About 100 species in tropical Asia to Australia, New Zealand and New Caledonia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Robust, rhizomatous perennial. Culms terete, transversely septate. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths. Inflorescence bract 1, erect, continuous with the culm. Inflorescence psedudolateral capitate or a single spike. Spikes comprising many spirally imbricate glume-like bracts (spicoid bracts), each subtending a partial inflorescence (spicoid) with a much reduced axis. Spicoids comprising a single naked female flower, and many scale-like floral bracts, the 3–4 immediately below the female flower empty, the remainder subtending a male flower comprising 1 stamen, the lowest 2 opposite and keeled. Preianth bristle absent. Stigmas 2. Achenes dorsiventrally flattened, ± smooth to longitudinally ribbed.

One species from Madagascar, India, Sri Lanka, SE & E Asia to Australia and Pacific islands; also in China and Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennial herbs, tufted or rhizomatous. Culms erect or ascending, often rooting at base. Leaf blades linear or lanceolate, usually flat, margins involute; ligule short, membranous, sometimes with a ciliate fringe. Inflorescence open, composed of several to many slender secund racemes scattered along a central axis. Spikelets biseriate, usually crowded on abaxial side of rachis, sessile to shortly pedicellate, laterally compressed, one broad side appressed to rachis, usually overlapping, florets 1–several; rachilla disarticulating above glumes and between florets; glumes 1-veined, membranous, keeled, usually shorter than the lemmas, subequal to unequal, persistent; lemmas membranous, 3-veined, generally hairy along the veins, keeled or rounded, obtuse or 2-dentate, sometimes mucronate to short-awned; palea equal to or slightly shorter than lemma, 2-veined; lodicules 2, minute. Stamens (1–)3. Styles 2, short; stigmas plumose, laterally exserted. Caryopsis laterally or dorsally compressed.

About 30 species distributed in tropical and warm temperate regions; three species in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Stipules small, subulate or linear, persistent or deciduous; stipels absent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets entire, apex rounded and bristle-tipped, net-veined. Flowers in axillary racemes, often contracted into dense fascicles; the lower fascicles in many species often mixed with small apetalous cleistogamous flowers, producing nevertheless perfect pods. Bracts small, persistent. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed or -lobed or the 2 upper teeth united into one. Petals clawed; vexillum obovate or oblong; wings oblong, adherent to keel or free; keel obtuse, incurved. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary sessile or stipitate, with a single ovule; style incurved, stigma small, terminal. Pods ovate, obovate or elliptic, plano-compressed, reticulate, indehiscent. Seed 1, suborbicular, estrophiolate.

More than 60 species distributed in N America, E Asia to NE Australia; 26 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, unarmed. Stipules setaceous, small, deciduous. Petioles often glandular; leaves bipinnate; leaflets numerous and small or few and larger, oblique. Flowers sessile, usually bisexual, in globose heads. Peduncles solitary or fasciculate, axillary. Bracts usually 2. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed. Petals 5, free or nearly so. Stamens 10, free, exserted; anthers without gland at apex. Ovary stipitate, ovules numerous; style filiform. Pods stipitate, broadly linear, plano-compressed, leathery, 2-valved, without septa. Seeds many, transverse, ovate, flat.

About 40 species, all in America, one species introduced and naturalized in the Old World; it occurs in mainland China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Leaves alternate. Capitula radiate and heterogamous, solitary or occasionally in loose corymbose form, pedunculate. Involucres shallow dish‑like; phyllaries 3–4 rows, margin scarious or membranous. Receptacle convex, sometimes conical, naked. Marginal florets one‑seriate, female and fertile, corolla ligulate, colour white, pink or rarely yellow. Disk florets many, bisexual and fertile, corolla tubular, 5‑lobed at apex, tube swollen basally, colour yellow; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑lanceolate; stylar branches linear, truncate at apices. Cypselae usually 10‑ribbed. Pappus none, or of a short crown or auricle.

About 30 species mainly in C & S Europe; two to three species cultivated in Hong Kong for ornamental uses. One described below.

Herbs or subshrubs. Stems erect or diffuse. Leaves entire or dentate. Verticillasters few–many‑flowered, widely spaced, sometimes forming terminal, capitulate clusters. Calyx tubular to obconical, rarely dilated, 8–10‑veined, straight or curved, truncate or oblique at throat; teeth 8–10, usually unequal, the posterior one the largest. Corolla usually white, rarely yellow, purple, brownish, or red, 2‑lipped; tube slender, often not exserted; upper lip straight, concave, densely villous outside; lower lip longer, 3‑lobed, spreading, middle lobe largest. Stamens in 2 pairs, the upper pair shorter; all ascending under upper lip; anther cells 2, ovoid, divaricate, apex confluent, often orange. Disk entire or lobed, uniform or enlarged anteriorly. Style unequally 2‑cleft at apex, posterior lobe short or obsolete. Nutlets ovoid, triquetrous, subtruncate at apex.

About 100 species in Africa, Asia, Australia, Pacific islands; eight species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

The voucher specimen for a previous report of Leucas zeylanica (L.) R. Br. (皺面草) (FKH 212. 1912) is wanted. Dunn's treatment of the Labiatae in China (Not. Roy. Bot. Gard. Edin. No. 28: 127 – 208. 1915) did not list any record of this species from Hong Kong.

Evergreen small to moderate shrubs, hermaphroditic, occasionally dioecious. Stems solitary or clustered, with node rings. Leaves palmate, rounded, subrounded or fan-shaped in outline, deeply divided almost to hastula into 1-fold or multiplefold, wedge-shaped segments or undivided, segments regularly dentate at apex; sheath open, with fibrous margin, ocrea conspicuous; petioles usually spiny bilaterally, spines sometimes small, few, or absent; hastula present. Inflorescences axillary, branched 1–2 orders or unbranched; prophyll tubular, persistent; bracts small, inconspicuous; flower bisexual or unisexual, calyx 3-lobed, petals 3, stamens 6; carpels 3 free or nearly so in bisexual flower. Fruits globose, ovoid or ellipsoidal, small, epicarp thin and smooth, mesocarp flesh, slightly fibrous, endocarp thin, crustaceous. Seed 1, globose, endosperm homogeneous.

About 147 species distributed from Bhutan and NE India via S and SE Asia to Pacific islands (Vanuatu); three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, usually solitary. Leaves mostly radical and rosulate, or concentrated in the lower stem portion, rolling backward when in young stage, leaf blade cordate, reniform, sagittate or ovate‑oblong, palmately‑ or pinnately‑veined; petioles long with the base broaden as sheath. Cauline leaves few, alternate, smaller in size when growing upward, base sheathed or not. Uppermost leaves appeared as bracts. Capitula nodding or deflexed, arranged as corymbs, compound corymbs, racemes, panicle‑racemes, or solitary, base subtended with bracteoles or not; pedunculate. Involucres broadly campanulate, hemispherical or turbinate; phyllaries in 1 row, margin scarious. Marginal florets pistillate, corolla ligulate, rarely absent or as tubular form, colour yellow. Disk florets bisexual, corolla tubular, apex 5‑lobed; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages ovate or deltoid, acute; stylar branches obtuse or rounded at distal ends. Cypselae cylindric, ribbed, glabrous. Pappus copious, long or short, rarely absent.

About 140 species mainly distributed in Asia and Europe; 111 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen shrubs, or small trees. Leaves simple, opposite, entire. Inflorescences terminal, rarely axillary, panicles of cymes. Flowers bisexual; calyx campanulate or cupular, 4‑toothed or truncate; corolla white, funnelform, 4‑lobed, lobes shorter than or as long as corolla tube, valvate in bud, spreading in flower. Stamens 2, inserted on corolla tube, included or exserted; anthers oblong or ellipsoidal, sometimes suborbicular; ovary spheroidal, 2‑locular, with 2 pendulous or anatropous ovules in each locule; style cylindric; stigma slightly 2‑cleft. Fruit a drupe, 1–4‑seeded; endosperm fleshy; radicle upward.

About 45 species mainly in warm area of Asia, few spread to Europe, Malaysia, Australia; 27 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with underground scaly bulbs and erect simple leafy stem. Leaves alternate, rarely whorled, sessile or subsessile, usually linear to linear-lanceolate. Inflorescence terminal, a raceme or solitary flower, very rarely an umbel or corymb; bracts leaf-like. Flowers usually large, funnel-shaped. Perianth segments 6, free, narrowed and erect at the base, spreading or recurved at the top, white, yellow, greenish, or reddish to purplish, each bearing a nectar-groove or -furrow at base. Stamens 6, inserted at the base of perianth segments; filaments subulate or filiform, sometimes pubescent; anthers dorsifixed, versatile. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule. Style elongate, slender; stigma 3-angled or 3-lobed. Fruit a capsule, loculicidally 3-valved. Seeds many, flat, narrowly winged, horizontally piled up in each valve.

About 115 species in temperate and alpine regions of N hemisphere, especially in E Asia; 54 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, aquatic, with aerial leaves. Leaves petiolate, ovate to orbicular. Scapes erect; umbels terminal; bracts forming an involucre; pedicels thick. Sepals persistent, green. Petals yellowish, thin. Stamens many, with sterile staminodes in outermost whorl; filaments flattened. Carpels many, free, crowded into a head, laterally compressed; stigmas sessile. Seeds many, strongly curved; embryo U-shaped.

Two species in tropical to subtropical regions of N & S America and naturalized in tropical Asia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

This genus is included in the Alismataceae by some authorities.

Annual herbs or perennial, in marshy areas or aquatic, often aromatic when bruised, with transparent dots. Stems erect, prostrate, or creeping, simple or many‑branched. Submerged leaves in aquatic species whorled, pinnately parted to capillary‑multiparted, glabrous. Aerial leaves opposite to whorled, sesssile or petiolate, blade lanceolate or pinnately divided, glandular punctate, margin entire or serrate, if leaf undivided, then veins pinnate or parallel. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves, or in axillary or terminal spikes or racemes. Bracteoles 2 or absent. Calyx tubular, lobes subequal or the upper lobe larger than others. Corolla tubular or funnelform, 2‑lipped; lower lip 3‑lobed; upper one entire or 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, included, didynamous. Anther locules stipitate. Ovary glabrous; stigma 2‑lamellate. Capsules included in calyx, septicidal. Seeds minute, numerous.

About 40 species distributed in tropical to subtropical Africa, Asia, Australia, and Pacific islands; ten species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs. Leaves basal or alternate on the aerial stems in the shrubby species, entire or pinnately lobed. Flowers 2 to many in spikes, subtended by scale-like bracts and arranged into branched cymes or panicles. Sepals tubular, 5–10-ribbed, scarious, often colored, apex 5-lobed. Petals 5, free or connate at base. Stamens 5 inserted at base of petals. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with a single pendulous ovule; styles 5, free. Fruit a capsule, 5-ribbed, dehiscent or indehiscent.

About 150 species, cosmopolitan, but especially in maritime and arid regions on N hemisphere; 22 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous shrubs or small trees, aromatic. Leaves alternate, entire or tri-lobed, pinnately veined, triveined or tripliveined. Inflorescences umbellate; umbels solitary or 2–many inserted on axillary spurs, each umbel subtended by 2 pairs of decussate bracts. Flowers unisexual, (plant dioecious); involucral bracts 4, decussate. Perianth-lobes 6, sometimes 7–9, subequal or the outer 3 slightly larger than the inner 3, deciduous. Male flowers with usually 9 fertile stamens in 3 whorls; filaments of the innear 3 stamens with 2 glands at the base; anthers 2-celled, all introrse; pistillodes small. Female flowers with 9 staminodes; ovary ovoid; style short; stigma peltate. Fruits drupaceous, globose or ellipsoid, 1-seeded, on enlarged perianth-tube.

About 100 species distribute Asia, tropical region of N America; 40 species in China. Five species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Herbs erect, prostrate, or creeping. Leaves opposite; petiolate or sessile; leaf blade often toothed or rarely entire; veins pinnate or palmate. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, sometimes pseudo‑umbellate, rarely paniculate, or flowers solitary. Flowers opposite or alternate, often pedicellate. Bracteoles absent. Calyx lobes 5, equal or subequal, parted or split on 1 side. Corolla 2‑lipped; lower lip larger than upper ones, extended, upper lip erect. Stamens 4, all fertile or anterior reduced and filaments with appendages. Anthers coherent or apex of anterior cells pointed or spurred. Styles mostly 2‑laminate, apex often enlarged. Seeds small, numerous.

About 70 species widely distributed throughout warm regions of the world; 29 species in China; ten species in Hong Kong.

In addition, a cultivar under the name Lindernia rotundifolia ‘Aurea’ (迷你虎耳草; Photos 275–276) has also been recorded in various localities in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic or terrestrial perennial herbs. Stems short, changing to compressed ovoid or cylindrical fleshy pseudobulbs. Leaves 1–4, persistent to the second year, ensiform or plicate-venose. Flowers small, many, in terminal racemes; sepals free, spreading, the odd one linear, erect, the lateral ones oblique-ovate, often recurved; petals linear or filiform, ± curved; lip undivided, cuneate at the base, with 2 tuberculate calli, gradually widened and bent at the middle, tongue-like, truncate or dentate, the apex emarginate; column semiterete, elongate, arcuate, the apical portion winged; rostellum truncate; anther terminal, incumbent, subglobose, acute, retuse or acuminate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, obovoid, without obvious viscidium; stigma 1, concave; ovary obconical. Capsules oblong-obovoid.

About 250 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, with a few species occur in N temperate zone; 52 species in China; eight species in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials. Clums erect, ± cylindrical, smooth. Leaves basal, linear, flat to ± canaliculate; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaf-like. Inflorescence capitate, terminal or pseudolateral. Spikes 1–8, ovoid, comprising many, densely imbricate spikelets each subtended by a spikelet bract. Spikelet bracts glume-like, conspicuous, hiding spikelet, apex short to elongate and sometimes strongly recurved. Spikelets comprising 2 glumes, both similar, the lower one empty, the upper one subtending a flower, sometimes 1 or both reduced or 0. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 1–3. Stigmas 2–3; style continuous with ovary. Achenes obovate, ellipsoidal to narrowly cylindrical.

About 35 species distributed in temperate and subtropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees. Leaves alternate, petiolate; stipules linear, usually adnate to base of petioles, caducous; leaf blade palmately 3 –7-lobed, margin serrate, palmately veined. Male inflorescence capitate or spicate, several to many together racemosely arranged. Female inflorescence capitate, with 1 bract. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious). Sepals and petals absent. Male flowers: stamens many; filaments as long as anthers; anthers ovoid, 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Female flowers: ovary semi-inferior, 2- locular; ovules many, inserted on septum, only lowest ones fertile; stigmas decurrent. Infructescences globose. Capsules woody, dehiscing into 2 valves; pericarp thin; styles persistent. Seeds many, narrowly winged.

Five species distributed in E and SW Asia, C and N America; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with short thick rhizome, often stoloniferous. Roots sometimes with fleshy, fusiform tuberous. Leaves radical, tufted, sessile, linear, parallel-veined. Inflorescence a raceme or a reduced panicle terminating on a leafless scape. Flowers bisexual, often in clusters of 2–4, sometimes solitary, small, subtended by a bract and a few bracteoles; pedicels articulate. Perianth segments 6, free, in 2 series, white or purplish. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth segments; filaments narrowly linear; anthers basifixed. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style columnar, slightly 3-angled; stigma small. Fruit bursting irregularly at an early stage and exposing young seeds. Seeds berry-like, globose or ellipsoidal, deep blue to purple at maturity.

Eight species distributed in E, and SE Asia; six species (three endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, monoecious. Leaves paripinnate, alternate, exstipulate. Thyrses terminal, golden tomentose; bracts and bracteoles small. Flowers unisexual, actinomorphic. Calyx cupular, 4–5-lobed, valvate. Petals absent. Disk acetabuliform, entire. Stamens (male flowers) 6–8, exserted; filaments filiform, pilose. Ovary (female flowers) shortly stalked, obcordiform, 2–3-lobed, 2–3-locular; ovules 1 per locule; style inserted between ovary lobes; stigma 2–3-lobed. Fruit deeply lobed into 2–3 schizocarps, usually only 1–2 developed, ovoid or subglobose; pericarp leathery (crustaceous when dry), abaxially with tortoise-shell-like fissure, with scattered conical prominents, sometimes nearly smooth. Seeds nearly same shape as schizocarps; testa brown, shining, leathery; arillode fleshy, wrapping all or lower half of seed.

One species distributed in SE China and Malesia, widely cultivated in subtropical regions; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees. Branchlets with terminal buds covered by spirally imbricate scales. Stipules extrapetiolar. Leaves spirally arranged, entire or dentate. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious). Male flowers in upright simple or branched spikes with rudimentary ovary; perianth 4–6-lobed; stamens usually 10 –12, much longer than the perianth. Female flowers 1 per cupule, solitary or 2–(3 –5) clustered at the base of male spikes, or in separate spikes; ovary usually 3-localar; style 3; stigma punctiform. Cupules corky, woody or crustaceous, enclosing completely or partly the nut; bracts variously shaped. Nut always solitary; pericarp woody or bony, scar convex or concave.

About 300 species, mostly in tropical and subtropical areas of Asia; 123 species in China; 14 species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, evergreen or deciduous. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite or verticillate, pinnately veined. Inflorescences cymoseumbellate, the cymes or umbels solitary or clustered in axils of leaves; involucral bracts 4–6, decussate, persistent at anthesis. Flowers unisexual, dioecious; perianth with a long or short tube; lobes usually 6 in 2 whorls, equal or unequal, rarely wanting or 8. Staminate flowers: fertile stamens 9 or 12, rarely more, in 3–4 whorls of 3 each; filaments of the 3rd and 4th whorl (if present) stamens usually bearing 2 glands at the base; anthers 4-celled, all introrse; rudimentary pistil present or absent. Pistillate flowers: staminodes as many as the stamens of the staminate flowers; ovary superior, style prominent. Fruits a drupe, sometimes succulent, resting on the cup-shaped, enlarged perianth-tube.

About 200 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia, N America to subtropical S America; about 72 species in China; eight species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Evergreen large trees, generally hermaphroditic. Stems solitary, bare or covered with petiole bases, rings of leaf scars obvious or not. Leaves palmate, rarely costapalmate, induplicate, dead leaves usually marcescent or deciduous below crown; blades divided to about 1/2 or more depth into single fold, rarely multifold, linear-lanceolate segments; segments 2-lobed, or the lobes split once again and sometimes pendulous; sheath open, with brown fibres; petioles well developed, unarmed or armed with strong or weak spines on bilateral margins; hastula present. Inflorescences axillary, branched to 5 orders; prophyll and peduncular bracts tubular. Flower small, bisexual, rarely dioecious; calyx and corolla 3-lobed; stamens 6; carpels 3, free, but share the same style. Fruits globose, ovoid or ellipsoidal, blue-black, purple-black, black or dark brown, developing from 1 carpel, with 2 sterile carpel-remains at base. Seed 1, globose, ovoid or ellipsoidal, endosperm homogeneous.

About 33 species in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Australia; three species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs or rarely subshrubs, usually with milky latex. Leaves alternate, distichous or spirally arranged, sometimes rosulate. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, solitary and axillary, or in terminal racemes or panicles. Bracts present or absent. Calyx‑tube short or ovoid; limb 5‑lobed, persistent. Corolla synpetalous, zygomorphic, slit open on the upper side to the base, ± bilabiate; lobes 5, the 2 upper lobes usually shorter and erect, forming an upper lip; the 3 lower lobes spreading and forming a lower lip, sometimes all the lobes spreading horizontally. Stamens 5, attached to the corolla‑tube and alternate with the corolla‑lobes; filaments free; anthers united into a ring round the style; stigma 2‑lobed. Ovary inferior or half‑inferior, 2 locular, with numerous ovules on axile placenta. Fruit a capsule opening at the top in 2 loculicidal valves.

About 350 species mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; 17 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Woody climbers, rarely erect shrubs, puberulent or glabrescent. Leaves petiolate, opposite, entire or crenulate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, cymose. Flowers bisexual; sepals and petals 5, disk fleshy, pulvinate or cupular, extrastaminal. Stamens 3; anthers 1-celled, basifixed, extrorse, transversely dehiscent. Ovary partially immersed in disk, 3-locular; ovules 4–15(–22) per locule; styles terete. Capsules transversely flattened, lobed to base, leathery, loculicidally dehiscent. Seeds numerous, with membranous basal wing, exalbuminous.

About 20 species distributed in tropical regions of Africa, Asia and Australia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

This genus was put in Hippocrateaceae by Cronquest (1988), but recently authors recognized that to combine it with Celastraceae is more reasonable.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaf blades linear, flat or rolled, often auriculate at base; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a single, stiff, 2-sided raceme, spikelets arranged in 2 opposite rows, their inner edges sunk in hollows of the tough rachis. Spikelets laterally compressed, 3–12(–22)-flowered, uppermost floret reduced; glumes leathery, lower glume absent (except terminal spikelet); upper glume abaxial, narrow, persistent, shorter than lemmas to as long as spikelet; lemmas membranous to leathery, rounded on back, 5–9-veined, with or without a subterminal awn; palea usually equal to lemma. Caryopsis tightly enclosed by hardened lemma and palea; hilum linear.

About eight species in temperate N Africa, Asia and Europe, especially the Mediterranean region; six species (four introduced) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Climbers (species in Hong Kong); winter‑buds with scales. Stipules absent or rarely intrapetiolar. Leaves opposite, entire or rarely lobed. Flowers in axillary, pedunculate pairs, or in sessile whorls, each pair with 2 bracts and 2 bracteoles, the latter often connate, rarely absent. Calyx 5‑toothed. Corolla with slender or short, often gibbous tube; limb obliquely 2‑lipped, upper lip 4‑lobed, lower lip entire, or nearly equally 5‑lobed. Stamens 5; anthers versatile. Ovary 2–3(–5)‑locular, with several ovules in each locule; styles filiform; stigma capitate. Berry with 1 or a few seeds.

About 200 species distributed in temperate to subtropical regions of N hemisphere; 98 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs; roots many, with small, spindle-shaped tubers. Culms unbranched. Leaves all cauline, narrowly lanceolate, manyveined and distinctly with cross veinlets, base contracted and petiole-like. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, composed of unilateral racemes. Spikelets falling entire, 1-flowered, rachilla extension bearing a bunch of up to 9 smaller sterile lemmas; cross veinlets evident on glumes and lemmas; glumes unequal, 5–7-veined, apex obtuse; fertile lemma 7-veined, all lemmas with a retrorsely scaberulous awn, those of the sterile lemmas developing into a fan of recurved hooks at maturity. Stamens 2 or 3.

Two species in warm temperate and tropical Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate or clustered at apex of branches, rarely opposite. Inflorescence an axillary cyme; bracts caducous or absent. Flowers bisexual, 5-merous. Hypanthium ovoid or obconic, pubescent. Sepals imbricate, persistent. Petals white or yellow, pubescent. Stamens many; filaments usually connate into 5 bundles opposite to petals; anthers dorsifixed, cells parallel, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary inferior or semi-inferior, 3-locular; ovules many. Style shorter than stamens; stigma slightly enlarged. Capsule semiglobose or cup-shaped, apex truncate, dehiscing into 3 valves, valves included in hypanthium. Seeds several, linear, sometimes winged.

Four species distributed in Australia and S New Guinea; one species introduced to China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or semievergreen shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, unequal, pinnately veined, short-petioled. Inflorescence capitate, shortly spicate, or racemose, axillary or terminal. Flowers bisexual, usually 4 or 5-merous. Floral cup obconical, stellatepubescent. Sepals ovate, pubescent, deciduous. Petals strap-like. Stamens 4 or 5, perigynous, anther 2-celled, each dehiscing into 2 valves, connective protrudent; disc scales present. Ovary semi-inferior, 2-locular; ovules 1 per locule. Capsules dehiscing into two 2-lobed valves. Seeds 1 per carpel, long-ovoid, hilum white.

Three species distributed in China, E and N India, Japan; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs; rhizome creeping, rooted on nodes; stem erect. Leaves alternate, ovate, dark purple with golden veins. Flowers white, in a terminal raceme, resupinate; sepals subequal, lateral ones spreading backward; petals connivent with the dorsal sepal; lip twisted, saccate, widened, divergently bilobed; column twisted, apex enlarged; rostellum bilobed; anther ovate, acuminate, pollinia 2, sectile; viscidium oblong; stigma 1, on plain side of the column; ovary hairy.

About four species distributed in India, Myanmar, Indochina to Indonesia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs; stems branched or not, erect to prostrate and rooting at nodes Leaves alternate or opposite, usually entire; stipules present. Flowers solitary in leaf axils, rarely in clusters or arranged in terminal spikes or racemes, sessile or shortly pedicellate, bisexual, actinomorphic. Bracteoles 2. Calyx tube not prolonged beyond ovary; lobes (3–)4 – 5, green, persistent after anthesis. Petals as many as sepals or absent, yellow or white, caducous. Stamens as many as or twice as many as sepals. Ovary with as many locules as sepals, rarely more; ovules many per locule, in 2–many series; style 1; stigma capitate. Capsules linear to cylindrical, dehiscing irregularly or by a terminal pore. Seeds many, obovoid, glabrous, free or embedded in powdery or woody endocarp, raphe small or conspicuous.

About 75 species widely distributed throughout the world; nine species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbaceous vines, monoecious, glabrous or puberulous. Tendrils bi- or multi-fid, pilose. Leaves usually 5–7-lobed. Flowers yellow. Male flowers: arranged in racemes; calyx-tube campanulate or turbinate, lobes 5; corolla rotate, lobes 5, free, spreading; stamens 3, rarely 5, distinct, anthers one 1-celled, two 2-celled when stamens 3, or all 1-celled when stamens 5, cells linear, sigmoid, connective usually dilated; pistillodes glandular or absent. Female flowers: solitary; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 3, or rarely 4–5; ovary cylindrical, placentas 3; styles columnar, stigmas 3, bifid; ovules many, horizontal. Fruits cylindric or terete, ribbed or not, fleshy when young, dried when old, fibrous inside, dehiscent by apical opercula. Seeds many, oblong, compressed.

Eight species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; two species cultivated in China, also in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, ± fleshy. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, racemose or spicate. Flowers short pedicellate or subsessile. Calyx-tube long tubular, with 2 bracteoles at base, the limb 5-lobed. Petals 5. Stamens 10, in 2 (or 1) whorls, or 5(–7); filaments slender; anthers opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary 1-locular; ovules 2, rarely 5; style subulate or clavate. Fruit drupaceous, woody, ribbed or striate. Seed 1.

Two species distributed in coastal areas of E hemisphere; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, subshrubs or sometimes creeping herbs. Leaves simple, alternate, solitary or unequal‑paired. Flowers 1–several fascicled in axils of leaves; peduncles obsolete or absent. Calyx cup‑shaped, (5–)10‑toothed; the teeth subulate or linear, unequal. Corolla rotate or stellate, white or purplish blue, 5‑lobed to middle. Stamens 5, inserted near apex of corolla‑tube; filaments short, glabrous; anthers opening by apical pores. Ovary ovoid, 2‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style slender; stigma obtuse. Fruit a berry, globose, red or purple‑red when mature.

About 180 species distributed mostly in C and S America; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, often thorny. Leaves alternate or clustered, entire. Flowers usually pedicellate, solitary or several clustered in axils of the leaves or at the old nodes. Calyx campanulate, 5‑toothed or 5‑lobed, persistent. Corolla tubular or funnelform, limb (4–)5‑lobed, the lobes imbricate in the bud. Stamens 5, attached to middle or below middle of corolla‑tube; anthers opening longitudinally. Ovary 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style slender; stigma shallowly 2‑lobed. Fruit a berry, globular or ovoid; seeds numerous.

About 80 species distributed in warm and temperate regions, especially in S America; seven species and three varieties in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, or subshrubs. Leaves alternate, pinnate or pinnatifid. Flowers in cymes or panicles, extra‑axillary. Calyx rotate, deeply 5–6‑lobed; lobed linear‑lanceolate. Corolla rotate, yellow; tube short; limb 5–6‑lobed; lobes lanceolate. Stamens 5–6, inserted in corolla‑tube; filaments short; anthers coherent, opening longitudinally. Ovary 2–5‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style slender; stigma capitate. Fruit a berry, depressed globose or globose, many‑seeded.

About nine species distributed in S and N America; one species cultivated in China and in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, rarely trees, deciduous or evergreen. Branchlets terete or angled. Leaves alternate, short-petioled, entire or obscurely serrulate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemose or paniculate. Pedicels with 1 bract and 2 bracteoles at base. Calyx divided beyond middle; lobes (4–)5(–8), persistent. Corolla urceolate or campanulate, white, rarely red, shortly 4–5-lobed. Stamens 10, rarely 8–16; filaments flattened, with a pair of appendages near apex or without; anthers obtuse, without appendages, opening by apical pores. Ovary superior, (4–)5-locular, with many ovules in each locule; stigma truncate. Capsule subglobose or ovoid, (4–)5-angled, loculicidal, with thickened sutures. Seeds oblong-ovoid or spindle-shaped to shortly linear, minute, ends often truncated.

35 species in E Asia and N America; five species in China; one variety in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees. Leaves paripinnate; leaflets 3–5 pairs, opposite, asymmetrical; stipules small, subulate or sharply triangular, caducous or tardily deciduous. Inflorescence a panicle, terminal or axillary; peduncles subtended by red or white bracts; bracteoles small, paired on or near pedicel apex. Flowers purplish red or pink. Calyx tubular, apex 4-lobed, lobes imbricate, reflexed after flowering. Petals 5, upper 3 larger, obovate, long stipitate, lower 2 very small, scale-like or subulate. Fertile stamens 2, distinct or slightly connate at base; filaments exserted, reflexed in bud; anthers ellipsoidal, dehiscing longitudinally; staminodes 3–8, unequal, subulate, without anthers or with small globose anthers. Ovary oblong, flat, stipitate, ovules 6 – 14; styles slender; stigmas small, capitate. Pods oblong or obovate-oblong, flat, thickly leathery or woody, 2-valved, valves flat or slightly twisted or coiled. Seeds flat, oblique broad-elliptic or suborbicular, glossy, margin thickened or not. Cotyledons flat, embryo small.

Two species distributed in S to SE China and Vietnam; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Erect or procumbent perennial herbs, rarely suffruticose. Leaves alternate, opposite or whorled, usually entire, often with pellucid or colored glands. Flowers usually 5-merous, solitary, or in racemes, panicles, umbels or head-like clusters. Calyx deeply divided. Corolla white, yellow or rarely pink, subrotate or campanulate; tube very short; lobes contorted in bud. Stamens as many as and opposite corolla lobes; filaments free or connate into a tube at the base and ± adnate to corolla tube; anthers basifixed or versatile, opening by apical pores or lateral slits. Capsule globose, usually opening by valves.

About 180 species mainly in temperate and subtropical regions of the N hemisphere; 138 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees or shrubs; buds axillary, free from petioles. Leaves alternate, odd-pinnate; leaflets mostly opposite, estipellate. Racemes or panicles terminal. Bracts deciduous. Flowers numerous and dense, bracteolate. Calyx campanulate, 4–5-toothed. Corolla white; vexillum recurved, thickened at base; wings obliquely oblong, base hastate; keel semi-sagittate, subcoherent dorsally. Stamens 10, very shortly connate at base; anthers versatile. Ovary subsessile, densely hairy, few-ovuled; style subulate, stigma minute, terminal. Pods subsessile, winged along the ventral suture or not, plano-compressed, scarcely dehiscent, hirsute. Seeds 1–5, oblong, compressed, testa thin, brown, astrophiolate.

About nine species distributed in E Asia; eight species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, young branches and leaves usually pubescent or tomentose.
