Leaves alternate, often peltate, entire or lobed, pinnately- or palmately-veined, with 2 depressed glands at the base on the adaxial surface; stipules, free or connate, caducous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious, rarely monoecious), without petals and disk, in axillay racemes or panicles. Male flowers many in clusters; calyx 2–4-lobed, lobes valvate; stamens 1–3 or 5–15, rarely 20–30, filaments free or connate at base, anthers 3–4-celled; pistillode absent. Female bracts 1 or few in a large or small often toothed bract; calyx urceolate or cup-shaped, lobed or shortly dentate; ovary 1–6-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles short or slender, entire, free or rarely connate at base. Capsules of 1–5 bivalved cocci, naked or spiny, usually glandular or warty; seeds subglobose, testa crustaceous.

About 500 species in Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia; 16 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Perennials; rhizome short or horizontally decumbent, occasionally emitting stolons. Culms laxly tufted or solitary and disposed along the rhizome, ancipitous, biconvex or terete, at times transversely septate, usually 1 – 2-nodose. Leaves 2-ranked, basal few cataphylloid; blades ancipitous or terete, sometimes much reduced, rarely transversely septate, spongiose inside; sheaths elongate, ligule none. Inflorescences paniculate bearing 1 – several partial panicles; branches often fasciculate; branchlets flexuous and zigzag; bracts sheathing, often spathaceous. Spikelets frequently clustered, ovoid to subturbinate with fruit, subtended by 1 – 2 bracteoles, bearing several glumes, on ± straight persistent rhachilla, 1 – several-flowered, but only the lowest or lowest 2 flowers hermaphrodite and fruitbearing, the upper flowers reduced. Glumes 2-ranked, keeled, the lower 1 – 4 empty and smaller than the fruit-bearing one(s), the fruitbearing one(s) the largest, the remaining upper glumes gradually smaller, bearing male flowers or empty. Flowers hermaphrodite or staminate; perianth segments often none, rarely up to 6, filiform, scabrous. Stamens (1 – )3. Stigmas 3. Achenes mostly ovoidal or ellipsoidal, triquetrous to subterete, sessile or stipitate, the surfaces smooth to wrinkled, the apex crowned with a pyramidal, often pubescent, persistent style base, which is adnate to the achene body.

About 45 species distributed in tropical and temperate regions but mostly in Australia and New Zealand; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, entire, pinnately veined. Flowers bisexual, in panicles, terminal or becoming lateral by the elongation of the shoot; involucral bracts deciduous after anthesis. Perianth-tubes short; lobes 6 in 2 whorls, equal, subequal, or occasionally the outer 3 smaller than the inner ones, persistent. Stamens 9 in 3 whorls, the 3 inner ones with stipitate glands; anthers 4- celled, introrse, those of the 3 inner stamens extrorse or lateral. Staminodes present, shortly stalked, sagittate. Ovary sessile. Fruits fleshy, globose, rarely ellipsoid, subtended by persistent and reflexed perianth-lobes; pedicels not enlarged or slightly enlarged in fruit.

About 100 species in tropical and subtropical SE and S Asia; ca. 85 species in China and 12 species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or scandent shrubs, with milky juice. Branches usually spinose. Stipules 2. Leaves alternate, entire; lateral veins pinnate. Inflorescences axillary, racemose, spicate or capitate, with many sterile bracts at base. Flowers dioecious; Bracts 2–4 in each flower, adnated to perianth-lobes; perianth-lobes usually 4, rarely 3 or 5, free or basally connate, each lobe with 2–7 embedded yellow glands. Male flowers: stamens 4, straight in buds; pistillodes subulate or absent. Female flowers: sessile, perianth-lobes fleshy, peltate, free or basally connate, apex thick; ovary free or immersed in receptacle; style short, 2-fid or undivided. Syncarps formed by laterally fused flowers and bracts, fleshy, globose; achenes many, small, ovoid, pericarp crustaceous, enclosed in fleshy persistent perianth lobes.

About 12 species distributed in Africa, Asia, Australia and America; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, all parts glabrous. Leaves opposite. Inflorescences axillary, racemose or spicate, rarely umbellate; each flower with 1 bract and 2 bracteoles at base; bract small, shorter than the calyx; bracteoles often connate, rarely free. Flowers bisexual, 6-merous, actinomorphic or sometimes zygomorphic. Calyx ovoid to ellipsoidal, limb annular or cupular, persistent. Corolla sympetalous, tube dilated at lower part, usually 6-keeled in middle portion, then constricted abruptly to a neck and expanded to a clavate tip; lobes 6, reflexed. Filaments short; anthers 4-celled, sometimes multilocellate. Ovary at first 3-loculed, then 1-loculed; placentation free, central. Style filiform, base usually articulated. Stigma capitate. Berry ovoid or ellipsoidal.

About 40 species distributed in tropical S and SE Asia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect or straggling shrubs, rarely arborescent. Leaves alternate, frequently with glandular nervilliform lines (secretory canals). Inflorescence axillary or terminal, racemose or paniculate. Flowers 5- rarely 4-merous, bisexual or unisexual, subtended by a pair of bracteoles on pedicels or at base of calyx. Calyx-tube adnate halfway to ovary; lobes valvate, persistent. Corolla white or light yellow, campanulate or rarely urceolate, connate at base or sometimes beyond middle; lobes imbricate or quincuncial, glandular-lined. Stamens adnate to corolla-tube, included; anthers ovate or reniform, about equaling the filaments, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary half inferior, with ovules immersed in a globose central placenta; style cylindrical; stigma capitate or shortly 3 –5-lobed. Fruit subglobose, dry to thinly fleshy, seeds several to many.

About 200 species distributed in palaeotropical regions; 29 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, usually deciduous, rarely evergreen; twigs with annular stipular scars. Leaves alternate, sometimes fascicled at apex of short branches and becoming pseudoverticillate, entire, rarely bilobed; stipules membranous, adnate to petioles, and remaining stipular scars on petioles; young leaves erect, folded in buds. Flowers bisexual, usually fragrant, large, solitary, rarely 2–3 terminal on normal branches, usually appearing before or at the same time as leaves, pistils mature prior to stamens; tepals white, pink or purplish red, rarely yellow, 9 –21(– 45), 3 –5 in each whorl, subequal, sometimes the outer ones smaller, greenish or yellowish brown, calyx-like; stamens caducous, filaments flat, connectives elongated and forming a short or long tip, rarely not exserted, thecae dehiscing introrsely or laterally; gynoecium linked to androecium, without gynophore. Carpels distinct, many or few, styles curved outwards, stigmas papillate and located in the adaxial side, each carpel 2-ovuled (rarely lower ones 3 – 4-ovuled). Aggregate usually cylindrical, ovoid-cylindrical or cylindrical-ovoid when mature, usually curved because of carpels partly undeveloped. Mature follicles leathery or woody, free from each other, rarely connate, dehiscing along dorsal sutures, apex long or short beaked. Seeds 1–2, testa orange-red or fresh red, fleshy,oily, endotesta rigid, hilum connected to placentation by filiform funicle.

About 90 species, distributed in SE Asia, SE N America, C America, Antilles Islands; 31 species occurred in China, distributed in SW, NE China, Area S of Qinling to E China; three species (two cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs. Stems little branched, without spines. Leaves pinnately compound; leaflets leathery, usually spinose dentate. Flowers in terminal racemes; perianth-segments usually 9, the 3 outermost (sometimes interpreted as bracteoles) small and sepaloid, the 6 inner bright yellow, petaloid; stamens 6, opening by 2 valves; ovary 1-locular, with a few ovules. Fruit a 2-seeded berry, dark blue, usually glaucous.

About 100 species in E & S Asia, C & N America; about 30 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Climbing shrubs with latex. Stipules lateral, deciduous. Leaves alternate, entire or obscurely dentate, pinnately veined. Flower dioecious. Male inflorescence a spike, axillary, simple or branched. Male flowers: perianth 3– 4-lobed, lobes valvate; stamens 3– 4, filaments incurved in bud, pistillodes minute. Female inflorescence a small head, axillary, globose, solitary or clustered, with many bracts at base. Female flowers: mostly sterile, usually 1 or 2(–5) fertile, perianth urceolate; ovary included; style central, deeply 2-fid, stigma filiform; ovules pendulous. Infructescence accrescent; achenes enclosed by thin and fleshy perianth, pericarp thin.

Only one species distributed in S, E Asia to Australia; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

This genus is sometimes placed within the genus Trophis P. Brown. Here the author followed the treatment of Flora of China and kept it as a distinct genus.

Terrestrial perennial herbs dormant during the cool dry season. Stems leafy, changing into elongate subconical or cylindrical pseudobulbs. Leaves large, plicate-venose, papery. Flowers very small and many, non-resupinate, in a terminal raceme; sepals free, spreading and often curved; petals filiform, curved forward; lip sessile, erect, spreading or the sides erect, auriculate at the base, with a depression near the column, the apex acute or bilobed; column very short, sunk in the sinus of the depression of the lip, terete, truncate at the apex; rostellum truncate; anther suborbicular, sessile, erect; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, oblong-obovoid, without caudicle; viscidium a narrow mass lining the truncate rostellum; stigma concave; ovary obconical, striate-sulcate. Capsules ellipsoidal, the apex truncate, with the column surrounded by persistent remains of the sepals and petals.

About 300 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, only a few species occur in N temperate zone; 21 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious or monoecious, usually with stellate hairs. Leaves alternate or opposite, entire, toothed or sometimes lobulate, sometimes peltate, often glandular abaxially and with 2 to several granular glands near base. Flowers small or minute, in axillary or terminal panicles, spikes or racemes, apetalous, without disk; males clustered, female solitary in the bracts. Disk often absent. Males flowers: clustered in bract; calyx globose or ovoid, 3–5-partite; stamens numerous; filaments free, anthers 2-celled, dorsifixed or nearly basifixed, longitudinally dehiscent, connectives truncate; pistillode absent or very minute. Female flowers: solitary in bract; calyx spathaceous or 3–5-lobed; ovary 2–4-locular, with a solitary in each locule; styles free or connate at base, spreading or recurved, entire, plumose or papillose. Capsule of 2–3(–4) bivalved cocci, smooth, tuberculate or echinate; seeds ovoid-oblong or globose, testa crustaceous.

About 150 species chiefly in tropical and subtropical Asia and Australia, few in Africa and Madagascar; 27 species and 12 varieties in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaves alternate, angled or palmately lobed. Flowers axillary, solitary or fasciculate; involucral bracts 3, distinct, linear. Sepals cupular, 5-lobed; lobes deltoid, acute. Petals obcordate, cuneate, with deeper colored veins converging towards the claw. Staminal tube with free filaments at apical portion. Ovary 9- to 15-carpellate; ovules 1 in each locule; styles as many as carpels, oblique clavate; stigmas decurrent on adaxial surface. Fruit discoid, at maturity separating into round-reniform indehiscent carpels.

About 30 species, all native to the Old World; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Leaves ovate, dentate or palmately lobed. Flowers axillary, solitary or in terminal racemes. Bracteoles usually 3, rarely 1 or absent, linear or subulate, not connate. Calyx cup-shaped, 5-lobed, foliaceous in fruit. Petals 5, yellow. Staminal tube antheriferous only at the apical end; filaments slender. Ovary (5 –)10 –15-carpellate; ovule 1 in each carpel; stylar branches as many as carpels. Fruit discoid; carpels compressed, reniform, setose and strigose, indehiscent, at maturity separating from the columella.

About 80 species mainly in tropical America; two species naturalized as pantropic weeds; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs; branchlets slightly pubescent. Leaves palmately lobed or not; stipules caducous. Flowers solitary, axillary. Bracteoles 5 –10, lanceolate-spathulate, slightly connate at base. Calyx bell-shaped, apical 1/4 lobed; lobes 5, deltoid-lanceolate. Corolla red, tubular, petals 5, imbricate, rolling into a hanging cylinder at anthesis. Staminal tube exceeding corolla, apex 5-toothed, the apical one-tenth staminiferous. Ovary 5-carpellate; styles 10, exserted; stigmas discoid. Fruit berry-like. Seeds sticky, with red fleshy coat.

Three species, native to Central and South America; one variety cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, andro-monoecious. Leaves simple, alternate, entire, petiolate. Inflorescence a terminal panicle. Flowers small, 4–5-merous. Calyx 4–5-lobed; lobes connate at base, imbricate. Petals 4–5(–6), distinct, sometimes adnate to disk, imbricate. Disk usually lobed. Stamens 5, rarely 8–12, distinct or united with disk at base, usually 1 or 2 well-developed and bigger. Ovary glabrous, 1-locular, style 1, terminal. Fruit a drupe, mesocarp fleshy or fibrous, endocarp thick and bony, compressed. Seed flat, testa thinly papery.


About 35 species distributed in tropical Asia; five species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees. Stipules enclosing young buds, lower part adnate to petioles, caducous, leaving long or short scars on petioles. Leaves leathery, entire, folded in buds. Flowers bisexual, terminal and solitary; tepals usually 9–13, 3 in each whorl, subequal, the outer 3 usually thinner, subleathery, greenish or red; filaments short and inconspicuous, anthers linear, dehiscing introrsely, connectives exserted and mucronate; gynoecium sessile; carpels numerous, spirally arranged, distinct, adaxially completely connate to receptacle, abaxially usually with 1 or several furrows at base, each carpel 4- or more ovuled. Aggregates dense, globose, ovoid, terete or ellipsoidovoid; mature follicles subwoody, or thicky woody, persistent, dehiscent along dorsal suture or sometimes also along ventral suture, usually beaked at apex, with 4 or more seeds.

About 30 species, distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia. 23 species in China, distributed in the areas south of Changjiang River valley. One species native to Hong Kong.

Shrubs or treelets, rarely herbs, with milky juice. Leaves alternate, mostly palmately lobed or dissected; petioles glandular or stipellate at apex; stipules small, usually caducous. Inflorescences mostly racemose-paniculate, terminal or axillary on upper branchlets, usually with a few female flowers at the base and many male flowers on the upper part. Flowers unisexual, apetalous; calyx usually campanulate; lobes 5, imbricate, free or connate at base. Male flowers: disk intrastaminal, usually 10-lobed; stamens 8–15, in 2 series, filaments free, slender, anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent, connectives hairy at apex; pistillode small, or absent. Female flowers: disk annular, sometimes with staminodia; ovary 3-locular, rarely 5-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles short, free, mostly multifid or lacerate, rarely bifid, stigmas broad. Capsule dividing into 3 valved cocci; columella often persistent; seeds carunculate, testa dry, crustaceous; albumen fleshy, cotyledon broad and flat.

About 60 species in tropic of America, mostly native to Brazil; five species cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, lactiferous. Leaves alternate, leathery to almost leathery, lateral veins dense; stipules caducous. Flowers solitary or several clustered in leaf axils. Sepals 6, in 2 whorls. Corolla 6-lobed, outer lobes with 2 petaloid appendages. Stamens 6; staminodes 6, alternate to corolla lobes, lobed or not. Ovary 6–14-locular, ovules 1 per locule. Fruit a berry, 1– 6-seeded. Seeds compressed, scar lateral.

About 70 species distributed tropical regions of the world; two species (one native) in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Robust, stonoliferous or rhizomatous perennials; rhizomes woody, roots coarse. Culms central or lateral (arising from lower leaf axils or below the leaves), the latter with cataphylls at base. Leaves 3-ranked, basal or cauline; blade linear to oblong, leathery; pseudopetiole present or absent; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaf-like in capitate and centrally culmed species, otherwise glumelike. Inflorescence paniculate, capitate with few to many spikes or a single spike only. Spikes comprising few to many spirally imbricate glume-like bracts (spicoid bracts), each subtending a partial inflorescence with a much reduced axis (spicoid). Spicoid comprising a naked, terminal female flower and 6 scale-like floral bracts, the lowest 2 opposite, keeled, the lowest 3 subtending a male flower comprising 1 stamen, the remainder empty. Perianth segments absent. Stigmas 3 (or rarely 2). Achenes with a hard or succulent exocarp, smooth or sculptured, lateral costae or furrows 0 or 2–3.

About 80 species in the tropics; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody climbers, sometimes with tendrils. Leaves leathery, opposite or subopposite, entire, petiolate, pinnately-veined. Inflorescences axillary, rarely terminal or super-axillary, usually cymose, female inflorescence usually more strong and few-flowered than male ones. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious). Male flowers: calyx small, cupular, 5-dentate; corolla funnel-form, fleshy, 5-lobed, lobes valvate, hairy; stamens 5, free, shorter than corolla, filaments slightly thinner at base, upward ampliate; anther dorsifixed, introrse, pistillode present. Female flowers: calyx as in male flowers, persistent and enlarged in fruiting; corolla 5-lobed, base slightly connate, apex incurved; ovary 1-locular, ovules 2, stigma disciform, 5-lobed, staminodes present. Drupe elliptic, 1-seeded.

Two species in tropical Asia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Caulescent, erect or prostrate herbs, sometimes much branched, occasionally with tuberous, swollen rhizomes. Leaves both basal and cauline or all cauline; petiole sheathing at base. Inflorescences 2–several per leafy shoot, each a dichotomous panicle or raceme. Bracts green, few, distichous, each subtending 2–6 pedicellate flower pairs, herbaceous, late deciduous or persistent. Sepals green, herbaceous. Corolla white; tube 4–14 mm, base often inflated; lobes subequal. Staminodes white, occasionally tinged or marked with purple; tube usually short; outer staminodes 2, petaloid, obovate, exceeding corolla lobes; cucullate staminode with median or subterminal appendage; callose staminode obovate, apex petaloid. Ovary 1-locular by abortion. Style thick. Capsules obovoid to ellipsoidal, dehiscent. Seed 1.

About 32 species distributed in tropical America; two species (introduced) in China and Hong Kong.

Perennials or annuals. Spikelets with few to many glumes distichously disposed on a continuous simple axis (rachilla), subterete, subtetragonous, or laterally flattened; rachilla jointed at base, usually above prophyll or above lowest glume, hence spikelets falling entire. Glumes all nearly alike, often only 1– several of these flower-bearing, rarely all flower-bearing. Flower bisexual with 1–3 stamens and trigonous pistil. Achenes trigonous, linear-oblong or elliptic, one of sides facing rachilla; style not jointed at base, 3-lobed at apex forming 3 stigmas.

About 200 species distributed in temperate, subtropical and tropical regions of the world; ten species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees. Leaves opposite, pinnately compound, exstipulate. Inflorescences terminal, raceomose or thyrsoid, ± hirsute. Bracts inconspicuous. Flowers night‑flowering. Calyx enclosed in buds, splitting to base at one side and spathaceous when flowering, greyish brown woolly abaxially, tuberculate. Corolla campanulate, tube short, swollen at one side, apex 5‑lobed; lobes subequal, orbicular, thick and shrunk. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments hairy at base; thecae divergent. Disk annular. Ovary ellipsoidal, woolly. Capsule long cylindric, flat, greyish brown tomentose and floccose, septum woody, flat. Seeds long elliptic, in 2 rows, membranous, with white transparent wings at both ends.

About 13 species distributed in Africa and tropical Asia; one species and one variety in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody lianas, with white latex. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Inflorescences terminal or extra‑axillary, umbel‑like, paniculate, or raceme‑like, pedunculate. Sepals 5, quincuncial, basal glands or scales often present. Corolla urceolate or campanulate, throat often hairy; lobes 5, twisted to right. Corona‑lobes 5, erect, acuminate, fleshy, attached to gynostegium. Stamens 5, filaments connate into a tube; anthers erect, appendages inflexed; pollinia 2 per pollinarium, often oblong, erect. Stigma head flat, convex, or beaked. Follicles mostly thick, acuminate, smooth or longitudinally winged; coma white.

About 100 species distributed in Asia, America, tropical Africa; 25 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, relatively small. Stems erect or procumbent and rooting from lower nodes. Leaves in a rosette or opposite, often upper leaves alternate; petioles winged. Racemes ± secund. Bracts small; bracteoles present or absent. Flowers small, pedicellate. Calyx infundibular or campanulate, 5‑lobed. Corolla blue to violet, tubular, strongly 2‑lipped; palate with 2 longitudinal plaits; lower lip 3‑lobed; upper lip 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted on corolla tube, included. Anther‑cells divergent, apically connivent. Ovary hairy or glabrous, styles glabrous, stigma 2‑lamellate. Capsule ± compressed, included in cupular persistent calyx, loculicidal. Seeds small, numerous, ellipsoidal, testa reticulate.

About 30 species distributed in Asia to Australia; 25 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, rarely shrubs. Stipules partly adnate to petiole. Leaves alternate, pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets usually dentate, lateral veins running out into teeth. Racemes axillary, sometimes flowers in heads or solitary. Bracts smaller or absent; bracteoles absent. Flowers small. Calyx campanulate, equally 5-toothed. Corolla yellow (hybrids often purple, violet or brown); vexillum obovate or oblong, base narrowly reflexed; wings oblong, one side toothed; keel obtuse, shorter than wings. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform; styles short, stigma terminal. Ovary linear; ovules numerous, rarely 1. Pods spirally falcate or often shell-like, longer than calyx, angulate or prickly on sutures. Seeds 1–many, small, estrophiolate.

More than 70 species distributed in W and S Europe, C to W Asia, N and S Africa, everywhere in tropical regions; 13 species introduced to China; four species cultivated or naturalized in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, petiolate or sessile. Inflorescence a spike or head, terminal or lateral; bracts deciduous. Flowers bisexual. Hypanthium subglobose or campanulate. Sepals 5, caducous or persistent. Petals 5. Stamens many; filaments basally connate into 5 bundles opposite to petals; anthers dorsifixed, cells parallel, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary slightly adnate to hypanthium, 3-locular; ovules many per locule; style linear; stigma ± enlarged. Capsule semiglobose to globose, valves included in hypanthium. Seeds cylindrical to subtriangular; testa thin; embryo straight.

About 150 species mainly distributed in Australia; several species cultivated in China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or subshrubs. Leaves opposite, petiolate, usually hairy, entire, 5–7-basiveined, rarely 9-basiveined. Flowers terminal, solitary or in panicles, usually large and showy. Calyx-tube urceolate-globose, usually covered with bristles or scales; the limb of 5(–6) deciduous lobes or teeth, and often with as many accessory ones. Petals as many, obcordate or obovate. Stamens twice as many, unequal in length, 5 longer alternating with 5 shorter ones, longer stamens purplish, anthers lanceolate, curved, without tubercles at base, connective extended at base, stalked, curved, the end 2-lobed; shorter stamens with yellow anthers, connective not extended. Ovary half-inferior, ovoid, 5-locular, apex usually densely covered with hairs; ovules numerous, placentation axile, sometimes fleshy in fruiting. Fruit capsular, more or less succulent, opening irregularly. Seeds small, cochleate.

About 22 species distributed in SE Asia, N Australia, Pacific Islands; five species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees or shrubs. Branchlets with obvious leaf scars and lenticels, hairy. Leaves bipinnate to tripinnate, alternate; leaflet usually serrate or sometimes entire. Panicles axillary, multi-branched. Flowers bisexual. Calyx 5–6-parted; lobes imbricate. Petals 5–6, white or purple, distinct, imbricate. Staminal tube cylindrical, with 10–12 stripes, mouth expanding; anthers 10–12, inserted between staminal tube lobes, inclusive or partly exserted. Disk annular. Ovary subglobose, 3–6(–8)-locular, ovules 2 per locule, superposed. Style slender; stigma capitate, 3–6-lobed. Fruit a drupe, nearly fleshy; stone bony. Seed 1, pendulous; testa hard crustaceous; endosperm fleshy, thin, or absent.

Three species distributed in S tropical Africa, tropical to temperate Asia; one species in China, it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed. Leaves opposite or whorled, digitately 3-foliolate or 1-foliolate. Inflorescence a thyrse, axillary or on branches, rarely terminal or cauliflorous. Flowers small, bisexual or functionally unisexual. Sepals 4. Petals 4, distinct, valvate or imbricate. Stamens 4 or 8, distinct. Gynoecium 4-carpellate; carpels connate at base or completely united; ovules 2 or sometimes 1 per carpel; styles adnate to each other, stigmas capitate. Fruit 1–4 follicles; follicles connate at base, dehiscing along dorsal and ventral sutures, apex with or without beaked awn, 1–2-seeded.

About 240 species distributed SE Asia, Malesia, Australia, New Zealand and Pacific Islands; eight species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms tufted, often creeping and rooting at the base. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, usually loose; leaf blades linear, flat; ligule a ciliate rim. Inflorescence a panicle, branched; pedicels slender, glabrous or with a few long hairs at the tip. Spikelets elliptic or oblong, ± laterally compressed, disarticulating below the glumes, hairy or glabrous; lower glume small or absent, veinless; upper glume as long as lower lemma, membranous to papery, 5 – 9-veined, emarginate or 2-lobed, awned or awnless, sometimes gibbous on the back and tapering to a beak; lower lemma resembling the upper glume, usually with a slender awn from sinus; upper lemma shorter, membranous, obscurely veined, awnless; palea as long as upper lemma; lodicules 2; stamens 3; styles 2; stigma plumose.

About 22 species distributed mainly in tropical regions and S Africa; two species in China and Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Buds naked, brownish tomentose. Leaves simple or pinnate, alternate; petioles usually thickened at the base. Flowers small, hermaphroditic, in terminal or axillary panicles. Sepals 5, sometimes 4, imbricate, usually with bracteoles underneath. Petals 5, imbricate, unequal, 3 outer ones larger, usually suborbicular or reniform, 2 inner ones much smaller, bifid or entire. Stamens 5, 2 fertile ones opposite to the 2 inner petals, filaments short and flattened, incurved, expanded at the top into a cup, bearing two globose 2-celled anthers; the other 3 stamens degenerated, opposite to the outer petals. Disc cup-shaped. Ovary sessile, 2–(rarely 3)-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule. Fruit a drupe, with fleshy mesocarp; endocarp stony or crustaceous. Seed more or less globose, usually somewhat concave ventrally, without endosperm.

About 50 species mainly in SE Asia with a few in S America; 29 species and seven varieties in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or herbs, slightly stellate-pubescent, Leaves ovate or broadly cordate, serrate. Inflorescence a cyme or glome. Flower small, bisexual. Calyx campanulate, 5-fid; petals 5, spathulate or oblong, marcescent; stamens 5, opposite to petals, connate from base to middle; anthers 2-celled; staminodes absent or minute; ovary 5-locular, 1–2-ovuled each locule; styles 5, free or united at base, stigma slightly thickened. Capsules dehiscent, 5-valved, locule 1-seeded. Seeds obovate, with thinly endosperm, cotyledons flat.

About 54 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in America; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Woody lianas or sometimes low shrubs, latex present. Leaves opposite. Cymes terminal or axillary. Flowers white. Calyx without glands. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric, dilated at staminal insertion; lobes usually oblique‑falcate, overlapping to left; corona scales 5 or 10, erect. Stamens inserted at or below middle of corolla‑tube, included; filaments very short; anthers free from pistil head, base rounded; disk absent. Ovary syncarpous, 2‑loculed; ovules numerous. Style short; pistil head apex dilated, 2‑cleft. Fruit a berry. Seeds numerous; coma absent.

About 50 species in tropical or subtropical Asia and Australia; 12 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, often glabrous. Branches terete or quadrangular, much branched. Leaves petiolate or sessile, usually leathery, pinnately-veined, margin entire. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, cymose or umbellate. Flowers 4-merous, small. Calyx-tube hemispherical or campanulate; the limb entire or obtusely 4(–5)-lobed. Petals 4(–5), ovate or orbicular. Stamens twice as many as petals, all similar; anthers shorter than filaments, with a thick connective, forming a conical spur at the base. Ovary inferior, entirely adnate to the calyx, 1-locular, apex truncate, with 8 radiated sulci, margin of sulci raised or forming narrow wings; ovules 6–12, attached to a central placenta. Fruit a baccate drupe, often globular, apex with annular persistent calyx, exocarp usually succulent. Seeds solitary or rarely 2 or 3, bony, with convolute cotyledons.

About 300 species distributed in tropical regions of Africa, Asia, Australia, Madagascar, and Pacific Islands; 11 species (six endemic) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, strongly scented, often with creeping rhizomes. Leaves opposite, often dotted with glands. Verticillasters (2–6)–many‑flowered, forming terminal heads or spikes; bracts lanceolate to linear, ± distinct. Calyx tubular or campanulate, 10‑veined, throat glabrous or hairy, nearly regular, 5‑toothed; teeth subequal. Corolla funnel‑shaped, ± regular or slightly irregular; tube generally included, throat slightly dilated or saccate in front, limb 4‑lobed; lobes equal, entire, the uppermost lobe slightly broader than other 3, emarginate. Stamens 4, subequal and erect; filaments glabrous; anther cells 2, parallel. Disk entire, uniform. Style shortly 2‑branched, branches subequal. Nutlets ovoid, smooth or reticulate.

About 30 species mainly distributed in N temperate regions, a few in the S hemisphere; six native and six cultivated species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs. Stems often twining, sometimes prostrate or erect. Leaves large or small, usually petiolate, rarely sessile, margin entire, 3‑lobed or palmately lobed. Flowers axillary, solitary or in several – many‑flowered cymes; bracts usually small. Sepals variable in shape, subequal or outer 2 smaller, persistent, often enlarged in fruit. Corolla often yellow or white, funnelform or campanulate, midpetaline bands 5‑veined; limb entire or ± 5‑angled. Stamens inclusive, often unequal; filaments dilated basally, filiform distally; anthers often spirally twisted; pollen grains globose, not spiny. Disc annular. Pistil inclusive; ovary 2 – 4‑locular, 4‑ovuled. Style 1, filiform; stigmas 2‑globular. Capsule 1 – 4‑locular, usually 4‑valved or ± irregularly dehiscing. Seeds 1 – 4, glabrous or hairy.

About 80 species distributed in tropical regions of Africa, Asia, Australia, N & S America; 19 species in China; six species in Hong Kong (one introduced).

Annual herbs. Stems erect or procumbent. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Verticillasters forming terminal racemes; bracts sessile, often caducous. Calyx campanulate in flower, 8–10‑veined, tubular or urceolate‑tubular and transversely pitted in fruit, 2‑lipped; upper lip 3‑toothed, middle tooth very large; lower lip entire, occasionally emarginate. Corolla white or reddish; tube short, throat inflated, not hairy annulate inside; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip truncate or 4‑toothed; lower lip longer, oblong, concave, margin entire. Stamens 4, in 2 pairs, exserted; the upper pair filaments with a tooth or appendages at the base; anthers 1‑locellate. Style longer than stamens, apex unequally 2‑cleft, lobes subulate. Nutlets oblong or ovoid, smooth or inconspicuously tuberculate.

About eight to ten species in tropical Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees, monoecious; main branches irregularly whorled; branchlets opposite or subopposite; winter buds ovoid or ellipsoid, bud scales 6–8 pairs, decussate. Leaves deciduous together with lateral branchlet as a unit, linear, soft, decussate, 2-ranked, stomatal bands 4–8, on abaxial surface only, or on both surfaces on seedling leaves, base twisted. Pollen cones borne in spikes or panicles, shortly pedunculate; microsporophylls 15–20, decussate, each with 3 pollen sacs, except apical and basal with 2. Seed cones terminal or subterminal on previous year's growth, solitary, shortly pedunculate at pollination, becoming long pedunculate and pendulous, subglobose, slightly cubic, or occasionally oblong-globose, ripening in 1st year; peduncle clothed with decussate, linear leaves; cone scales 16–24, persistent, decussate, shieldlike, woody, grooved, 5–9-seeded (when fertile), base cuneate, distal part transversely rhombic. Seeds 5–9, compressed-obovoid, winged all round, apex emarginate. Cotyledons 2.

One species in central China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves leathery, simple, alternate, entire; stipules membranous, hooded, 2-valved, adnate or distinct to petioles, caducous, remaining an annular scar on twigs or, if adnate to petioles, a linear scar on petioles. Young leaves erect, folded in buds. Flowers bisexual, usually fragrant, solitary and axillary, subtended by 2– 4 deciduous spathose bracts. Tepals 6 –21, in whorls of 3 or 6, subequal, or rarely the inner ones much smaller than the outer ones; stamens numerous, connectives elongated, dehiscing laterally or nearly laterally, filaments short or long, connectives exserted and forming a long or short tip, rarely not exserted; gynoecium stipitate, carpels numerous or few, adaxial base inserted on rachis, upper part free, usually partly undeveloped; ovules 2 to several in each carpel. Aggregate a syncarp, usually spike-like; mature follicles leathery or woody, completely persistent on fruiting axis, sessile or short-stalked, dehiscing into 2 valves along dorsal sutures or along both dorsal and ventral sutures. Seeds 2 to several, red or brown.

About 50 species, distributed in tropical, subtropical Asia and temperate China, S Japan; 41 species in China, mainly in SW to E China; six species (two cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, very small, cushion‑like. Stems slender, prostrate, many‑branched. Leaves opposite, small, sessile. Flowers axillary., solitary, ebracteolate. Calyx campanulate, 5‑ribbed, 5‑fid, nearly to a third of its length; lobes deltate‑ovoid, ciliate. Corolla tube short, straight; limb 2‑lipped, lower lip patent, 3‑lobed, upper lip entire, short, erect. Stamens 2, included; filaments filiform; anthers connivent, 1‑celled. Ovary ovoid to globose; stigma inflexed, ligular. Capsules slightly flattened, 2‑grooved, loculicidally 2‑valved; valves entire. Seeds few, ovoid‑fusiform, ± smooth.

One species distributed in E Asia, Pacific island; also in China and in Hong Kong.

Low-growing perennial or annual herbs. Culms tufted, slender. Leaves mostly basal; leaf blades linear, inrolled; ligule short, ciliate from a membranous base. Inflorescence a single spike; spike unilateral, very slender, ± falcate; spikelets sessile, biseriate, closely imbricate; rachis crescentic in section. Spikelets small, lightly dorsally compressed, narrowly subterete, floret 1 without prolonged rachilla or sterile florets, disarticulating above glumes; glumes subequal, as long as spikelet and enclosing floret, firmly membranous, 1-veined, margins infolding, apex acute, both or only upper deciduous; lower glume keeled; upper glume rounded; lemma shorter than glumes, ovate, keeled, thinly membranous, 3-veined, ciliate on veins, apex acute or minutely emarginate and mucronulate; palea subequal to lemma, keels ciliate. Caryopsis ellipsoidal.

Six species spread throughout the tropics; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, leathery, margin entire or slightly lobed, basal veins 3, shortly petiolate. Inflorescence cymose or paniculate, terminal or axillary. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 5, distinct. Petals 5, or rarely wanting, with glands at base adaxially. Stamens many, free, inserted on androgynophore. Ovary superior, hairy or glabrous, usually 3-locular; ovules 4–7 per locule. Style 1; stigma thin or lobed. Drupe globose or pyriform, not sulcate.

About 60 species, mainly distributed in Africa and SE Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or treelets. Leaves simple, alternate, pinnately-veined, short-petiolate; stipules small. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious), usually in axillary fascicles, or sometimes female flowers solitary. Male flowers: sepals 5, imbricate; petals 5, longer than the sepals; stamens 10 or 5, in 2 or 1 series, inserted at the fleshy receptacle, the outer ones alternating to the petals, the inner ones sometimes absent or reduced and scale-formed; filaments free; anthers longitudinally dehiscent. Female flowers: sepals and petals as male flowers, but slightly larger; ovary fleshy, 2(–3)-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles short, 2-parted, lobes divaricate. Drupes usually globose, epicarp scabrous, endocarps bony; seeds with fleshy endosperm.

About ten species in tropical Asia and Africa; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Slender subshrubs or tall herbs. Leaves alternate, petiolate, ovate to lanceolate, entire or lightly toothed along margin. Capitula heterogamous, minute, radiate, densely clustered in corymb or panicle. Involucre campanulate, phyllaries imbricate, many‑seriate, with various shapes from ovate, lanceolate to linear. Receptacle naked or rarely scarious, flat or slightly convex. Marginal florets many‑seriate, pistillate, corolla ligulate, filiform, ligule linear, white; style long and slender. Disk florets few, bisexual or functionally staminate, corolla tubular, 3–5‑lobed at the apex; anther base obtuse and entire, apex acute. Cypsela cylindric or ovate‑oblong, angulate. Pappus setae copious, scabrid.

About ten species native to tropical Asia and Africa; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms slender, creeping or rambling, usually much branched. Leaf blades broadly linear to lanceolate; ligule membranous, truncate. Inflorescence terminal, composed of 1–many subdigitate racemes on a short axis; racemes usually fragile, with sessile and pedicellate spikelets in a pair, rarely both spikelets unequally pedicellate. Sessile spikelet lanceolate, dorsally compressed, falling off with adjacent rachis-joint; callus shortly bearded; glumes herbaceous to cartilaginous; lower glume flat or deeply grooved on back or with a broad median channel, 2-keeled at least toward apex, ciliate or scabrous on the keel, margins inflexed; upper glume boatshaped, midvein keeled, 1–3-veined, acute to shortly awned; lower floret almost sterile, reduced to a single scale or absent; upper floret bisexual, lemma linear to cordate, deeply 2-lobed, shortly 2-toothed, or rarely entire, usually awned; awn slender and straight or geniculate; stamens 2–3. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet similar to the sessile but slightly narrower and less concave, occasionally slightly smaller and staminate, finally falling off from pedicel.

About 20 species distributed in Indian Subcontinent and SE Asia, a few species in Africa; 13 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, evergreen or deciduous. Branchlet more or less 4-angulate, glabrous, estipulate. Leaves opposite, entire. Inflorescence axillary, fasciculate or cymose. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual dioecious, (4–)5-merous; sepals connate at base, imbricate, margin irregularly serrulate or ciliate, persistent. Corolla white or yellow-white; lobes imbricate; disk annular or absent, (4–)5-angled, intrastaminal. Anthers longitudinally dehiscent, introrse, rarely extrorse. Ovary 2–3-locular; ovules erect, 2 per locule; styles short; stigma shallowly 2–4-lobed or entire. Capsules ellipsoidal or oblong, leathery, 1-locular, laterally split along one side. Seeds 1, ovoid, sarcotestal, without aril.

About 66 species distriburted in SE Asia, Macronesia; 24 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or climbing herbs. Leaves opposite or verticillate. Capitula homogamous, discoid, 4‑flowered, with variable arrangement. Involucres oblong‑campanulate or cylindric; phyllaries 4, united at base. Receptacle small, no palea. Florets tubular, bisexual and fertile, corolla funnel‑shaped, 5‑lobed at apex; stamens 5, anther bases rounded and entire, with apical appendages; stylar branches elongate, appendages linear, papillose or finely hirsute, apex acute. Cypselae glabrous, oblong‑cylindric, 4–10‑ribbed, sometimes glandular or setose. Pappus of scabrid bristles, in 1–2 series.

About 430 species in tropical America; one species is becoming troublesome weed in China and in Hong Kong.

Woody climbers or trees. Stipules caducous or persistent; stipels present or absent. Leaves odd-pinnate, usually evergreen; leaflets 2–many pairs, usually opposite, entire. Panicles terminal or axillary; calyx campanulate, 5-toothed, the upper 2 sometimes subconnate. Corolla purple, rose or white; vexillum large, spreading or reflexed; wings oblong, free from keel, auriculate or clawed at base; keel incurved, obtuse, clawed at base. Stamens 10, monadelphous, vexillary stamens free at base. Anthers uniform. Ovary with or without disk around the base. Pods linear, oblong to globular, flat or thick, leathery or woody, 2-valved or tardily dehiscent. Seeds 1–few, orbicular or reniform.

About 250 species distributed in Africa, Asia and Atlantic; 35 species in China; nine species in Hong Kong.

A worldwide revision of the genus was conducted by Dunn (J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 41: 123 – 243. 1912) where all species recognized here have been treated.

Shrubs or herbs, mostly armed, rarely trees or climbers. Stipules small; stipels usually 2 to each pinna. Leaves bipinnate, often sensitive. Flowers small, bisexual or polygamous, sessile, usually 4-merous, in globose heads or cylindrical spikes. Peduncles axillary, solitary or fasciculate in the upper axils, the upper ones sometimes racemosely branched. Calyx campanulate with teeth. Petals 4, connate at base. Stamens 4 or 8, free, exserted; anthers without glands at apex. Ovary many-ovuled; style filiform. Pods oblong or linear, usually plano-compressed, membranous or leathery, consisting of 3 – 6 one-seeded joints, separating from the persistent margins. Seeds ovate or orbicular, flat.


About 480 species mostly in tropical America; three species and one variety introduced to China; two species naturalized in Hong Kong. Mimosa diplotricha C. Wright ex Sauvalle (巴西含羞草) and Mimosa diplotricha var. inermis (Adelb.) Veldk. (無刺含羞草) have also been recorded previously.

Perennial herbs. Leaves opposite. Flowers bisexual, in axillary cymes, each flower surrounded by a calyx-like involucre. Calyx infundibuliform, corolla-like, with a long tube, constricted above the ovary, and a spreading, plicate, slightly 5-lobed limb. Stamens 3 – 5, as long as perianth-tube or sometimes exserted; filaments unequal, united at base. Ovary superior, 1-locular; style filiform; stigma capitate. Fruit an achene, exocarp leathery and ribbed.

About 45 species in tropical and warm regions of America; one species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, tufted or rhizomatous. Culms erect, solid. Leaves basal or cauline; leaf blades linear, flat; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a panicle, often large and plumose, composed of racemes arranged on a long or short axis; raceme axis tough, internodes slender, spikelets paired, pedicellate; pedicels slender, flattened, slightly clavate. Spikelets similar, lanceolate, dorsally compressed; callus bearded with hairs shorter than, as long as or longer than the spikelet; glumes papery or membranous; lower floret usually represented by a hyaline sterile lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline, awned or awnless; stamens 2–3. Caryopsis oblong or ellipsoidal.

About 14 species mostly distributed in SE Asia and Pacific islands; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs with the leaves remaining on the fifth year's growth. Rhizomes short and stout, the internodes thicker than long. Leaves ovate-cordate, produced 1 annually, petiolate, articulation near the cordate base of the leaf blade. Scapes emerging from one-year-old pseudobulbs, with 3 basal and a submedian sheaths. Flowers medium-sized, few in a short terminal raceme; sepals and petals subequal, the lateral sepals oblique, connate at the base and adnate to the column-foot forming a mentum; lip fleshy, undivided, subrhomboid, the sides erect, the apex triangular-acute, disk with 3 prominent keels; column long, erect, fleshy, slightly incurved, winged on both sides; rostellum deltoid; anther terminal, ovate, concave, bicornute; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, each group agglutinated at the base by a sticky mass; stigma transversely concave; ovary subcylindrical, striate.

About eight species distributed in S China, SE Asia and Pacific islands; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Erect or creeping herbs. Stems quadrangular, woody at the base. Leaves opposite. Stipules interpetiolar, persistent. Flowers in axillary or terminal heads. Calyx‑tube turbinate, obovoid or subglobular; limb 4 – 5‑lobed; lobes unequal, persistent. Corolla salverform or funnel‑shaped; tube usually with a ring of long hairs inside, glabrous or pubescent on the throat; lobes 4, valvate in the bud. Stamens 4, attached to the throat of corolla; anthers included or exserted. Ovary 2(3)‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style with 2 linear lobes at apex. Fruit a capsule, opening transversely at or a little below middle.

About 30 species mainly in tropical America, also in Africa and Australia; one species (introduced) in S China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial delicate herbs. Leaves opposite along stem and/or in a whorl at base, subsessile; stipules absent. Flowers axillary and/or terminal, solitary or in pedunculate umbel‑like cymes, which sometimes branched to form irregular compound umbels, 4‑merous, white or yellow, rarely pale blue. Calyx campanulate, 2 – 4‑lobed, lobes valvate. Corolla campanulate (salverform or urceolate), often bearded at mouth, tube short to long, lobes exduplicate‑valvate in bud. Stamens inserted on lower half of corolla tube; filaments much longer than anthers; anthers introrse, extrorse, or rarely latrorse, included to slightly exerted, 2‑celled. Pistil glabrous. Ovary superior to slightly inferior, with many ovules per locule. Style one, base usually parted, rarely 2 separate styles; stigma capitate or 2‑cleft. Capsules globose to subglobose, opening by apical loculicidal slits, 2‑horned, each terminated by a style which may be split or remain partly connate, many‑seeded. Seeds minute, cylindric‑ellipsoidal to angular; seed coat thin reticulate to verrucose or almost very minutely papillate; endosperm fleshy.

About 40 species, mainly Australia, but extending to E, S and SE Asia and Pacific islands; two species in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual herbs. Culms erect, tufted. Leaf blades linear, flat; ligule short, membranous. Racemes terminal, cylindrical or flattened; rachis internode clavate to pyriform, fragile, base truncate with central peg, spikelets paired, one sessile, the other pedicellate or occasionally in triplets of 2 sessile and 1 pedicellate. Sessile spikelet closely appressed or sunk in hollow in rachis, usually longer than adjacent internode; lower glume papery to leathery, ± flat, smooth or sculptured, marginally 2-keeled, keels winged at least at apex; upper glume boat-shaped, membranous; lower floret barren, with or without a small palea; upper floret bisexual with entire awnless lemma; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet varying from well developed to rudimentary or absent; pedicel oblong, clavate or leaf-like, free or partially or fully adnate to rachis internode.

About 30 species distributed throughout the tropics; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems much branched, glabrous. Leaves subopposite or more often in false whorls, and in rosettes at base. Flowers small, in axillary umbellate-clusters, or in terminal or leaf-opposite cymes. Sepals 5, free, with scarious white margins. Petals none. Stamens usually 3, sometimes 4 or 5, rarely 6–7, alternating with the sepals. Carpels 3(–5), united, forming a superior ovary, with many ovules; styles 3, very short. Capsule opening by 3– 5 valves.

About 20 species, mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbaceous vines, monoecious or dioecious. Tendrils unbranched or 2-branched. Leaves simple, often palmately 3 –7-lobed, rarely undivided, sometimes palmately compound. Male flowers: solitary or in racemes; pedicels often with a large bract; calyx-tube 5-lobed; corolla yellow or white, 5-lobed; stamens 3, sometimes 5 or 2, filaments distinct, anthers coherent, one 1-celled, the other 2-celled, cells reflexed, straight or curved, connective not protrudent; pistillodes glandular or absent. Female flowers: perianth as in male flowers; staminodes 3 or absent; ovary ellipsoid or fusiform, placentas 3; style slender, stigmas 3, undivided or 2-lobed; ovules many, horizontal. Fruits medium-sized, ellipsoid or fusiform, indehiscent or dehiscing into 3-valved when mature, usually verrucose or spiny. Seeds several to many, ovate or oblong, smooth or reticulate.

About 40 species mainly distributed in tropical Africa, some cultivated in the tropical regions; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, aquatic or paludose with short or creeping rhizomes. Leaves radical or alternate on vegetative stems, usually solitary on flowering stem. Inflorescences a terminal raceme, enveloped in broad leaf sheaths when young; peduncle with a large bract at base. Flowers subsessile or shortly pedicellate; perianth segments free nearly to base, spreading during anthesis and afterward spirally contorted, inner segments wider than outer. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth, dimorphic: one with long filament and a lateral, oblique tooth, anther basifixed, blue, large; the others subequal, anthers basifixed, yellow, small. Ovary 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma subentire or minutely 3-lobed. Capsule loculicidal, 3-valved.

Eight species distributed in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia, and Australia; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Erect or climbing shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite, rarely in whorls of 3. Stipules usually membranous and united at the base in a sheath within the petioles. Flowers in axillary or terminal single, umbellate or paniculate heads. Calyx‑tube urceolate or hemispherical, ± united by cohesion; limb short, scarcely toothed. Corolla‑tube cylindric or slightly dilated at the top, usually short; lobes (4–)5(–7), valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to throat of corolla‑tube; anthers included in the tube or rarely exserted. Ovary 2‑ to imperfect 4‑locular with 1 erect or ascending ovule in each locule. Style exserted, with 2 stigmatic lobes. Fruits of each flower‑head usually united in one compound berry, with many 1‑seeded pyrenes.

About 100 species widely distributed in tropical regions, but chiefly in tropical Asia and Africa; 27 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees or shrubs, monoecious or dioecious. Winter buds with 3 – 6 imbricate scales. Stipules caducous. Leaves alternate, simple, entire, serrate to variously lobed, with 3–5 veins at base. Spikes catkin-like, pendulous, ebracteate. Male flowers: perianth 4-lobed, lobes imbricate; stamens 4, incurved in bud, later elongating and exserted; pistillodes turbinate. Female flower: perianth 4-lobed, lobes imbricate, fleshy in fruit; ovary 1-locular, sessile; style 2-parted, ovules pendulous. Syncarps black berrylike, consisting of many achenes enclosed in enlarging succulent perianths (sorosis). Seeds subglobose, testa membranaceous, endosperm abundant.

About 16 species distributed in temperate and warm regions of the world; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, aromatic. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Verticillasters 2‑flowered, forming terminal racemes; bracts small or lower ones large and leafy. Flowers pedicellate. Calyx campanulate, 10‑veined, often gibbous at the base, throat pubescent, limb subequally 5‑toothed and 2‑lipped; upper lip 3‑toothed, teeth acute to obtuse; lower lip 2‑toothed, generally slightly longer, teeth lanceolate. Corolla white or rose to purple‑red, tube glabrous or hairy annulate inside; limb nearly 2‑lipped, upper lip emarginate; lower lip 3‑lobed, margin crenate; lateral lobes smaller than middle lobe. Stamens 4, in 2 pairs, only the upper pair fertile, anther cells 2, divaricate, the lower pair reduced, with indistinct anther cells. Disk glandular, produced in the front. Style apex subequally to equally 2‑cleft. Nutlets subglobose to globose, sparsely netted or pitted with small depressions.

About 22 species distributed in SE Asia and E Asia; 12 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous or woody twiners. Stipules deciduous. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, often stipellate. Inflorescence racemose, rarely paniculate, axillary or borne on old leafless stems and branches. Bracts small or caducous. Calyx campanulate, 2-lipped, upper lip entire or 2-lobed, lower lip 3-lobed, longer than others. Corolla showy, purple, red, yellowish green or white, vexillum rounded, clawed and auriculate at base, usually smaller than other petals; wings oblong or ovate, incurved, often adherent to keel; keel linear-oblong, incurved, acute and hardened at tip, as long as or longer than wings; vexillary stamen free, remainder connate; anthers dimorphous, the longer ones sub-basifixed, the shorter ones versatile, often barbate. Ovary sessile, villous, few-ovuled; style filiform, not barbate, stigma small, terminal. Pods thick, ovate, oblong or linear, often clothed with irritant bristles, 2-valved, septate between seeds or filled, valves leathery, variously ribbed or nude. Seeds rounded or oblong, hilum short or linear, discoid, arillate or exarillate.

About 100 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 15 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Herbs perennial, rarely annual. Roots fibrous or fusiform thickened. Stems creeping or ascending, sometimes main stem abortive. Leaves alternate and cauline or in a basal rosette. Cincinni solitary or several, forming panicles, shortened into heads, or sometimes reduced to solitary flowers. Flowers regular. Sepals free, shallowly to strongly boat-shaped. Petals free, purple, blue, pink, yellow, or nearly white, orbicular or obovate. Fertile stamens 3 or 2, opposite to sepals; filaments glabrous or hairy; anther cells opening by longitudinal slits; staminodes 3(–4), or absent, opposite to petals; antherodes sagittate or 3-sect. Ovary 3-locular, with 1–7 ovules in each locule. Capsule 3-valved, ovoid, ellipsoidal or globose. Seeds 1–2 per valve, uniseriate, quadrangular, reticulate, pitted, rugose, or verrucose.

About 50 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mainly in Asia; 20 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, unarmed. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate, rarely unifoliolate; leaflets alternate. Inflorescence a corymbose thyrse, terminal and axillary. Calyx 5-lobed. Petals 5, distinct, imbricate. Stamens 10; filaments linear-subulate; anthers small. Ovary 2–5-locular, ovules (1–)2 per locule; style slender, often longer than ovary; stigma capitate. Fruit a berry, (1–)2-seeded. Seed coat smooth or woolly.

About 12 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, NE Australia; nine species in China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, tufted, rhizomatous and stoloniferous. Pseudostems composed of closely packed leaf sheaths, more than 60 cm, base slightly swollen. Leaves large; petiole long, base enlarged into a sheath; leaf blade oblong, entire. Inflorescence terminal, erect or pendulous. Bracts green, brown, dull purple, or rarely yellow, flat or furrowed, convolute or imbricate in bud, usually deciduous. Flowers in 1 or 2 rows per bract; flowers in proximal bracts always female (with reduced stamens) or bisexual; flowers in distal bracts usually male (with reduced gynoecium); sometimes (in cultivated or semicultivated forms) all flowers functionally sterile. Compound tepal tubular, soon splitting to base on 1 side, apex 5-toothed; free tepal inserted within compound tepal and opposite to it. Stamens 5; filaments short; anther linear, 2-celled. Berries elongate, fleshy, with many seeds (except in parthenocarpic forms). Seeds irregularly globose to lenticular.

About 30 species, mainly in SE Asia; 14 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Erect or scandent shrubs, rarely small trees. Stipules interpetiolar, 2‑lobed or sometimes divided into 2 separate segments, usually deciduous. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3, petiolate. Flowers bisexual, in terminal corymbs. Calyx‑tube ellipsoidal or turbinate, the limb 5‑lobed, one of the lobes in a few of the outer flowers of each corymb often enlarged into a stalked, bract‑like, coloured leaf. Corolla funnel‑shaped, tube usually elongate, hairy at the throat; lobes 5, valvate in bud. Stamens 5, inserted in upper part of the tube; filaments very short; anthers basifixed, included in the tube or nearly so. Ovary 2‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule. Fruit a berry, indehiscent; seeds numerous, small.

About 120 species in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Pacific islands and Africa; 31 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Mussaenda erythophylla Schum. & Thonn. (紅葉金花; Photo 368) was also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, entire or toothed, with scattered glands. Flowers solitary or in cymes, axillary. Calyx 5‑lobed, persistent. Corolla white or pink with purple maculae, campanulate or funnelform, 5(– 7)‑lobed. Stamens 4(–7). Ovary 2‑locular, 1–2‑ovuled in each locule or the locule subdivided into 3–10 uniovulate compartments. Drupe small, slightly fleshy or dry. Seeds 1–2 in each locule.

About 28 species distributed in Australia and tropical Asia; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Biennial or perennial herbs. Stems prostrate or erect. Leaves opposite, ovate-cordate. Flowers bisexual, in terminal dichotomous cymes. Sepals 5. Petals 5, white, shorter than sepals, deeply 2-lobed to near base. Stamens 10; filaments slightly dilated at base. Ovary 1-locular; styles 5. Capsule ovoid, opening to middle into 5 valves; the valves 2-toothed at apex. Seeds reniform, with tubercles on ridges.

Only one species widely spread over temperate and subtropical regions in Europe, Asia and Africa, also in Hong Kong.

Aquatic perennial herbs. Leaves alternate or whorled, sessile or subsessile, linear to ovate, entire, serrate, or more often pectinate-divided. Flowers very small, usually unisexual, monoecious, sessile, solitary in axil of leaves, or rarely in spikes. Bracts 2, entire or lobed. Male flowers: calyx-tube short, apex 2–4-lobed or entire; petals 2–4, caducous; stamens 2 –8, free, anthers basifixed, opening by longitudinal slits; rudimentary pistils present or absent. Female flowers: calyx-tube adnate to ovary, 4-grooved, apex 4-lobed or entire; petals small and caducous, or wanting; staminodes present or absent; ovary inferior, 4-locular, or rarely 2-locular, with a solitary anatropous ovule in each locule; style (2–)4; stigmas feathery. Fruit separating into (2–)4 one-seeded mericarps.

About 36 species, cosmopolitan, but mainly in Australia; 11 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate or spirally arranged, frequently punctate. Inflorescence umbellate or fascicled, axillary or borne on very short scaly branchlets or spurs. Flowers bisexual or unisexual (plant mostly dioecious), 4–5-merous. Calyx small, deeply split or united to 1/2 length; lobes imbricate or valvate, persistent. Corolla-lobes almost free, rarely fused to middle, usually ciliate and punctate. Stamens inserted on the lower part of corolla; filaments free or at base connate into a tube and proximally fused with corolla-tube; anthers ovate or reniform, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary glabrous; ovules few, in 1 series. Fruit a dry or fleshy drupe, 1-seeded, with crusty or leathery endocarp.

About 300 species, distributed in Africa and Asia; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, dioecious or rarely monoecious. Leaves opposite or subopposite; petiole twisted through 90°; blade broadly ovateelliptic to oblong-lanceolate, without obvious midvein but with many, slender, parallel, longitudinal veins, stomatal lines abaxial or rarely on all surfaces. Pollen cones axillary, solitary or clustered in small, spikelike groups of 3–6, borne on naked peduncles, ovoidcylindric, with basal sterile scales; pollen 2-saccate. Seed-bearing structures terminal on short, scaly, axillary branchlets, solitary or occasionally paired; bracts usually obsolete, scarcely thicker than peduncle, rarely succulent and thicker than peduncle; ovule inverted. Epimatium wholly enveloping seed, leathery, with bluish black bloom when ripe. Seed drupelike, globose.

Five to seven species in Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Japan (including Ryukyu Islands), Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam; three species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as the family.

Evergreen shrubs. Leaves alternate, twice or thrice pinnately compound; rhachis articulate; leaflets entire. Flowers small, white, in terminal panicles; sepals many, spirally arranged, gradually increasing in size from out towards inside; petals 6, slightly larger than the inner sepals; nectaries none; stamens 6, opposite to the petals; anthers subsessile, opening with longitudinal slit; ovary 1-locular, with 1–2 ovules. Fruit a berry, globular, scarlet when mature.

A monotypic genus, the only one species distributed in S China and Japan; it is cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, bulbiferous. Bulbs ovoid-globose, coated with tunic. Leaves basal, linear and flat or narrow and terete, appearing with the flowers. Scape erect, solid. Inflorescence a several-flowered umbel, rarely flowers solitary; involucres spathe-like, membranous, basally tubular. Flowers white or yellow, mostly declined or nodding, rarely erect. Perianth salverform, with a short cylindrical or funnelform tube; segments 6, erect or recurved, subequal; corona narrowly tubular, corolla-like or shallowly cupular. Stamens inserted in perianth tube; anther basifixed. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule. Style filiform; stigma 3-lobed, small. Fruit a loculicidal capsule.

About 60 species distributed mainly in C Europe and the Mediterranean region; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, aquatic or terrestrial, glabrous or strigose. Stems prostrate or decumbent. Leaves all cauline, pinnately compound or simple, entire or pectinately pinnatisect. Racemes terminal, many flowered, elongated when fruiting. Sepals 4, ovate or oblong, base of lateral pair subsaccate or not. Petals 4, white or purplish, obovate or spathulate. Stamens 6, tetradynamous; medium glands absent, lateral glands 2, annular or semiannular. Siliques dehiscent, smooth or slightly torulose, subcylindric, septum complete. Seeds 1–2, seriate, oblong or ovoid, plump; cotyledons accumbent.

Five species distributed in Africa, Asia, Europe and N America; one species introduced to China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or sometimes shrubby. Terminal vegetative bud strongly compressed, rarely conical. Stipules large, interpetiolar, elliptic or obovate, caducous. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Flowers 4–5‑merous, bisexual, regular, densely crowded into a terminal globular head. Peduncles axillary or terminal, unbranched with a node bearing reduced leaves and stipules. Receptacles glabrous. Calyx‑tubes coalescent, the limb 4–5‑lobed; lobes persistent. Corolla funnel‑shaped, usually 5‑lobed; lobes imbricate. Stamens as many, inserted in the upper part of the tube; filaments short, glabrous; anthers basifixed, introrse. Ovary 2‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style exserted, with spindle‑shaped stigma. Fruit a fleshy, globular syncarp, composed of numerous indehiscent drupelets; seeds ovoid or ellipsoidal, sometimes bilaterally compressed.

About ten species in tropical Asia, Australia and Africa; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Nauclea orientalis L. (東方烏檀) was also cultivated in Hong Kong Botanical Garden previously (Sunyatsenia 6: 235. 1946).

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or decumbent. Leaves opposite, ovate to lanceolate. Stipules interpetiolar, united at the base, apex fringed with bristles. Flowers small, 4‑merous, in axillary or terminal cymes or heads. Calyx‑tube usually short; calyx‑teeth erect or recurved, usually with wide sinus. Corolla funnel‑shaped or tubular; lobes valvate in bud, usually shorter than the tube. Stamens attached to apex of corolla‑tube; anthers basifixed, linear‑oblong, included or exserted. Disk inconspicuous. Ovary 2(–4)‑locular; style linear; stigma 2–4‑lobed. Capsules in pairs, compressed, leathery or membranous, crowned by the calyx‑lobes.

About 30 species mainly in tropical Asia and Australia; eight species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family

Two species in E and S Asia, N Australia, C and N America; one cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees and shrubs. Leaves alternate, clustered or whorled, rarely subopposite, triplinerved, rarely pinninerved. Flowers unisexual, dioecious, in umbels; the umbels solitary or clustered, bracteate at base; bracts decussate, deciduous. Perianth-lobes 4 in 2 whorls. Staminate flowers: fertile stamens 6 in 3 whorls; filaments of the inner 3 stamens with 2 glands at the base; anthers 4-celled, all introrse. Pistillate flowers: staminodes 6, linear or clavate. Ovary superior; style short; stigma peltate. Fruits globose, with resin on the slightly dilated perianth tube.

About 85 species distributed in Indo-Malaysia to E Asia; 45 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Terrestrial perennial herbs, with leaves remaining on the third year's growth. Roots few. Rhizomes fleshy, the internodes longer than thick. Leaves ovate, fleshy, produced 1 annually, disarticulation near the truncate base. Scapes emerging from the base of the last internode, with 1 basal and 1 submedian sheaths. Flowers few, non-resupinate, in a loose terminal raceme; sepals and petals subequal, spreading like a fan; lip uppermost, undivided, long and narrow, calcarate, the spur enlarged at the end, the lateral lobes obsolete, midlobe spreading, 2-lobed, erect, disk cristate-lamellate and papillose to the base; column long and stout, winged, the apex erose; clinandrium broad; rostellum fleshy, truncate, recurved; anther terminal, rectangular and 2-cornute; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, waxy, laterally compressed, 2-seriate, the upper ones smaller, loosely associated by granular basal membrane; stigma discoid; ovary subcylindrical-ovoid. Capsules oblong, reflexed, ridged.

About 18 species distributed in tropical Himalaya via S China to SE Asia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, juice watery. Leaves in whorls of 3, with glands in the axils, lateral veins numerous, parallel. Inflorescences thyrsoid, terminal or axillary. Sepals with colleters adaxially. Corolla funnelform, cylindric near base, throat open wide, lobes overlapping to right; corona segments 5, petal‑like, large, fringed. Stamens inserted at apex of corolla‑tube; anthers sagittate, with a bristly, filiform apical appendage, pilose, connivent, adherent to pistil head; disk absent. Ovary syncarpous, 2‑locular; ovules numerous in each locule. Fruit a follicle, narrowly oblong, glabrous. Seeds numerous, densely pilose, with apical coma.

A monotypic genus distributed in S Europe, N Africa and SW Asia.

Terrestrial orchids requiring dormancy annually; rhizome slender, the end enlarged into a subglobose corm; erect stems short, subterranean, branched, each branch bearing a solitary, cordate leaf, lying flat over the ground. Scape delicate, aphyllous, bearing few scales and 2 flowers. Flowers appearing before the leaves; sepals and petals similar, subequal, free, parallel to the column and slightly divergent at the apex; lip undivided, ecalcarate, the basal portion embracing the column, the apical portion subrotundate, slightly cleft, the disk inverted-carinate, and the base gibbous; column slender and long, clavate, thin and curved above the base; rostellum fleshy and truncate; anther terminal, subglobose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, finely granular, without caudicle or viscidium; stigma suborbicular; ovary short, campanulate, deeply sulcate, bent at the juncture with the pedicel.

About 50 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Oceania and Africa; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs. Rhizome usually retrorse, with several stout aerial roots. Stem erect, often woody at base, not branched. Leaves several to many, plicate, basally contracted into a clasping, petiole-like stalk. Inflorescence erect, terminal, racemose, not branched; peduncle with several foliaceous sterile bracts; floral bracts relatively large, green. Flowers resupinate, almost actinomorphic, not opening widely. Sepals and petals often connivent. Sepals similar or lateral ones slightly oblique, fleshy. Petals similar; lip usually slightly different in shape and larger than petals. Column straight, often short, with 3 fertile stamens; central stamen often shorter than lateral ones; lateral stamens often with locules unequal in length; anthers free but filaments connate at base and adnate to style for much of their length; ovary 3-locular, distinct from pedicel; style narrowly cylindrical, apex with slightly dilated stigma. Fruit either a berry or a dry capsule dehiscent at maturity.

About ten species distributed from SE Asia through New Guinea to the SW Pacific islands; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Tall reed-like perennial herbs. Leaf cauline, blades linear, flat or rolled; ligule a line of hairs. Inflorescence a large plumose panicle, primary branches in clusters or solitary on central axis. Spikelets laterally compressed, 2–7-flowered; florets all bisexual with the upper reduced, or sometimes the lowest sterile and without a palea; glumes lanceolate, subequal or unequal, scariousmembranous, 1–3-veined, obtuse to acuminate or aristulate; lemmas longer than glumes, ovate-lanceolate, scariousmembranous, 3-veined, lateral veins long-ciliate with spreading hairs as long as lemma, apex setaceously bidentate with a short, often recurved awn from the sinus; palea almost as long as the lemma, hyaline, keels very shortly ciliate; callus obtuse, bearded. Caryopsis linear, subterete.

About five species distributed in the Old World tropics; four species (two endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Leaves alternate, petiolate; leaf blade simple, irregularly toothed or lobed. Flowers solitary, axillary or in branch forks, pedicellate, actinomorphic. Calyx campanulate, deeply 5‑parted. Corolla campanulate, shallowly lobed; lobes ovate. Stamens included, attached to corolla tube; filaments slender; anthers elliptic, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary 3‑5‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma subcapitate, 3‑5‑lobed. Fruiting calyx conspicuously enlarged, persistent, enclosing fruit, lobes cordate‑sagittate, each with 2 basal auriculate lobes. Berry globose, dry. Seeds reniform‑discoid, compressed, pitted.

One species native to S America, but widely cultivated or naturalized elsewhere, also in China and in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, shrubs or small trees, often viscid‑pubescent. Leaves simple, alternate, entire, or rarely sinuate, petiolate or sessile. Inflorescences paniculate, racemose or reduced to solitary flower. Calyx tubular or tubular‑campanulate, regular or irregular, 5‑lobed, persistent and enlarged in fruiting time. Corolla tubular, funnelform or salverform, regular or slightly irregular; tube elongate; limb 5‑lobed or subentire. Stamens 5, inserted half way in corolla‑tube; filaments slender; anthers opening longitudinal. Ovary 2‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by apical valves.

About 95 species distributed in Africa, Americas, Australia and Oceania; three species cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial aquatic herbs, with thick rhizomes. Leaves floating, orbicular or ovate, with deep sinus at base. Flowers large, bisexual, solitary on a long pedicel; sepals 4, almost free; petals many, in many series, white, red, blue or yellow, sometimes the inner ones gradually passing into stamens; stamens many, anthers with or without appendages; carpels many, in 1 series, sunk in the fleshy disc forming a many-locular ovary crowned by the connate radiating furrowed stigmas. Fruit a sponge berry, dehiscent irregularly.

About 50 species widely spread in tropical and temperate regions; five species in China; two species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, aquatic. Leaves alternate, rarely apparently opposite; leaf blade floating, ovate or suborbicular, base cordate, veins palmate. Flowers often clustered at nodes, rarely solitary. Calyx lobed to near base. Corolla often campanulate or rotate, deeply lobed, throat with 5 bundles of long fimbriae. Stamens inserted on corolla tube, alternate to corolla‑lobes; filaments short or absent. Nectaries 5, often opposite to corolla‑lobes. Style linear, attached at ovary base. Capsules ovoid or ellipsoidal, indehiscent, few seeded. Seeds compressed or globose, smooth or ornamented.

About 40 species distributed in temperate and tropical regions of the world; six species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, strongly scented. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Verticillasters 6(–10)‑flowered, forming terminal, racemes or panicles; pedicels recurved under the calyx; bracts small, caducous. Calyx ovoid to campanulate, declined in fruit, limb 2‑lipped; upper lip 3‑toothed, middle tooth large, suborbicular to obovate, margin winged, decurrent, strongly reflexed in fruit, lateral teeth shorter; lower lip 2 toothed, teeth narrower, apex acuminate to spinescent, sometimes approximate. Corolla tube slightly shorter than calyx or rarely exserted, not hairy annulate inside, dilated, obliquely campanulate at throat; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip truncate, subequally (3‑ or) 4‑lobed; lower lip somewhat elongate or not, declined, margin entire, flat or slightly concave. Stamens 4, exserted, declined on lower corolla lip, lower 2 longer; filaments free or lower 2 connate at base; anthers ovoid‑reniform, 1‑locellate. Style longer than stamens, 2‑cleft at apex; lobes subequal, subulate or flat. Nutlets ovoid or subglobose, smooth or glandular foveolate, viscid when moist, with a white basal areola.

About 100–150 species spread throughout the temperate and tropical regions worldwide, especially in Africa and S America; five species in China; two species cultivated or naturalized in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or shrubs with cystoliths. Leaves sessile to petiolate, margin entire to crenate. Inflorescences mostly terminal dichasial racemes, spikes or thyrses, sometimes branched basally and forming a panicle. Flowers heterostylic, usually pedicellate, 1–many alternate, opposite or whorled on each node. Bracts subopposite, opposite, or whorled, green or coloured, margin entire; bracteoles small. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed, lobes equal, subulate. Corolla white, red or yellow, tube long, limb 5‑lobed or bilabiate, the upper lip 2‑lobed, the lower lip 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, usually included in pin flower, stamens exserted in thrum flower; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae parallel, muticous at base. Staminodes 2. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style of thrum flower included in corolla throat, style of pin flower exserted from mouth of corolla; stigma funnelform or 2‑lobed, lobes equal or unequal. Capsules clavate, stipitate, retinacula hooked, 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, glabrous.

About 30 species in tropical and subtropical regions of America; one species cultivated in S China and Hong Kong.

Perennial or biennial herbs, glabrous, with fibrous or tuberous roots; stems slender, decumbent and ascending or erect, rooting at basal nodes. Leaves 1–4-pinnate; ultimate segments ovate to linear, margin serrate to pinnatifid or sometimes reduced to fistulose phyllodes; petioles sheathing. Inflorescence of compound umbels; peduncles terminal or lateral; involucre wanting or of a few narrow bracts; rays many, spreading; bracteoles numerous, shorter than flowers. Flowers white. Calyx-teeth small, lanceolate, persistent. Petals obovate with a narrow inflexed apex; styles erect, elongate; stylopodium conic. Fruit glabrous, oblong or globose, nearly terete, very slightly compressed laterally, ribs low and obtuse. Vittae usually solitary in each furrow, 2 on the commissure. Carpophores wanting. Seeds subterete, the face plane.
