About 30 species in N hemisphere, S Africa and Australia; 11 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs, caulescent or acaulescent. Leaves alternate or rosette, exstipulate. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, solitary, axillary, sometimes in terminal leafy spikes, racemes, or corymbs. Calyx-tube prolonged, often well beyond ovary; lobes 4, green or yellowish, often tinged or striped red or purple, reflexed, deciduous soon after anthesis. Petals 4, yellow, purple, pink, or white. Stamens 8. Ovary inferior, 4-locular; ovules many; stigma unlobed or 4-lobed. Fruit a capsule, straight or curved, terete to 4-angled or winged, dehiscent loculicidally. Seeds many, in 1 or 2(or 3) rows or in clusters, angled or not.

About 80 species distributed in temperate to subtropical areas of N, C, and S America, naturalized elsewhere; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, simple, margin entire or serrate, petiolate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal panicles, sometimes racemes or umbels. Flowers small, bisexual, unisexual or polygamous. Calyx campanulate, small, 4‑lobed to subtruncate. Corolla with a short tube, 4‑lobed or 4‑parted, or lobes absent; lobes usually shorter than tube, rarely equal or longer than tube, cucullately valvate in bud. Stamens 2, inserted at base of corolla tube, included; filaments short; anthers ovate, elliptic, or subrounded. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 pendulous ovules in each locule; style short; stigma capitate or slightly 2‑cleft. Fruit a drupe, elliptic, oblong, ovate or subglobose, exocarp thin and fleshy, endocarp thick and hard. Seed 1; endosperm fleshy; radicle short, upward.

More than 40 species, mainly distributed in S and SE Asia, Pacific islands, tropical Africa, S Europe; 14 species (one cultivated) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

records.authority: Z. P. Wang & G. H. Ye

records.text:
Twining herbs; stems, peduncles, and petioles often winged. Leaves petiolate, base often cordate. Cymes axillary, 1 – several‑flowered; bracts large, caducous. Sepals often enlarged in fruit, margin becoming irregularly lacerate. Corolla funnelform or campanulate, glabrous or midpetaline bands pubescent abaxially. Stamens inclusive; filaments filiform; anthers often spirally twisted at dehiscence; pollen not spiny. Disk annular. Ovary glabrous, 2‑locular, 2 ovules per locule. Style filiform, inclusive; stigma 2‑globose. Capsules compressed globose, circumscissile in or above middle, ± fleshy, separating from papery endocarp; pericarp split irregularly. Seeds 2 – 4, dull black, trigonous or globular, glabrous or angles pilose.

About 15 species distributed worldwide in the tropics; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, often stoloniferous, with short and thick rhizomes; roots sometimes with fleshy, tuberous part near tip. Stem suberect or prostrate, short or elongate, usually enclosed by leaf sheath. Leaves radical, tufted or scattered, sessile or petiolate; leaf blade linear to oblong, usually whitish streaked abaxially, parallel veined. Scape arising from a leaf axil. Inflorescence a raceme or reduced panicle terminal on a leafless scape; bracts small, membranous. Flowers small, bisexual, solitary or several-clustered in axil of bracts, usually nodding; pedicel articulate. Perianth segments 6, free, in 2 whorls, adnate near top of ovary. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth segments; filaments usually very short; anthers basifixed, sometimes connate. Ovary semi-inferior, 3-locular, with 2(–6) ovules in each locule; style 1, columnar; stigma capitate, small. Fruit bursting irregularly at an early stage and exposing young seeds. Seeds berry-like, usually blue at maturity.

About 65 species in warm-temperate, subtropical, and tropical Asia; 47 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, rarely shrubby. Leaves opposite, entire; stipules interpetiolar, persistent or caducous, entire or deeply 2‑lobed, often with colleters in the axils. Flowers usually heterostylic, or sometimes homostylic, sessile or short‑pedicellate along the branches of terminal or rarely axillary pedunculate cymes. Calyx usually small, turbinate or obconical, with 5 or 10 longitudinal ribs; limb 5(–6)‑lobed. Corolla‑tube slender; lobes 5( – 6), valvate in bud. Stamens 5(–6); anthers included or slightly exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with several ovules in each locule, attached to a placenta ascending from near the base. Capsule much flattened and very broad, almost 2‑lobed at the top, opening loculicidally in 2 valves. Seeds several, angular.

About 150 species widely distributed in tropical Asia and Pacific islands; about 70 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms trailing, or ascending from the creeping base. Leaf blades ovate, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, often with cross veins; ligule a ciliate membrane. Inflorescence composed of several racemes spaced along a central axis; spikelets usually paired or fascicles, sometimes solitary. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate to ovate, weakly laterally compressed, florets 2; glumes subequal, often pilose, the lower or both tipped by a viscid awn; lower floret barren, lemma as long as spikelet, acute to shortly awned, palea absent or much reduced; upper floret bisexual, lemma papery or subcoriaceous, smooth and shiny, with opaque inrolled margins embraced upper palea, acute; lodicules 2, thin membranous; styles free from the base.

About nine species spread over the tropics and subtropics; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Small or large succulent plants, very variable in size and habit, ranging from shrubs to small trees. Stem and branch-joints cylindric, globular or flat, with axillary areoles bearing woolly hairs and barbed spines or bristles. Leaves usually small, cylindric or subulate, caducous. Flowers actinomorphic, solitary, arising from areoles near apex of branch-joints. Perianth-segments many, outer ones green or colored, inner ones petaloid, green, red or yellow. Stamens many, much shorter than the inner perianth-segments. Ovary inferior; style single; stigma shortly lobed. Fruit a berry, globose, ovoid or ellipsoid, spiny or naked.

About 300 species native to America; about 50 species (introduced) in China; one naturalized in Hong Kong.

Herbs, perennial, rhizomatous, stemless. Leaves basal; leaf blade obelliptic or ovate, margin serrate or entire. Inflorescences lax or dense, axillary cymes; bracts 2, opposite, rarely apparently absent. Calyx actinomorphic, 5‑sect from base; segments lanceolate. Corolla zygomorphic; tube campanulate‑cylindric to broadly tubular, sometimes ampliate basally, throat sometimes constricted, longer than limb; limb slightly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, lobes lanceolate or ovate; abaxial lip 3‑lobed to 3‑sect, lobes equal or subequal, apex rounded to acute. Stamens 4, adnate to corolla tube near base to near middle, included, rarely exserted; anthers basifixed, rarely dorsifixed, free, thecae parallel, not confluent at apex, seldom horseshoe‑shaped, transverse; staminode 1, rarely absent. Disk ring‑like, margin entire. Pistil glabrous or pubescent; ovary oblong; placentas 2, parietal, projecting inward, 2‑cleft; style shorter than ovary; stigma 1, terminal, oblate to capitate, undivided, or 2, equal, oblate, undivided or rarely 2‑lobed. Capsule straight, oblanceolate‑oblong to oblong; valves 2, straight. Seeds ovoid, no appendage.

About 28 species in China, Thailand, Vietnam; 27 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, 3-nerved or pinninerved; cystoliths punctiform. Stipules scarious, free, lateral. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious), in head-like clusters; the clusters forming axillary twice to thrice branched dichotomous cymes, rarely solitary on short peduncles. Male flowers: perianth-segments 3 – 4, valvate in the bud; stamens 3– 4, filaments inflexed in bud; rudimentary pistil small, ± wooly. Female flowers: perianth tubular, slightly fleshy, adnate to the ovary, apex constricted, inconspicuously 3 –4 toothed; stigma sessile, discoid or peltate, with long ciliate hairs on the margin; staminodes absent. Achene drupaceous, the base or almost wholly enclosed by the accrescent, discoid or cupular fleshy receptacle.

About 18 species in tropical and subtropical regions of E Asia and in New Guinea; ten species in China; one species (including one subspecies) in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees. Stipules small; stipels absent. Leaves odd-pinnate, rarely simple; leaflets opposite, leathery, entire. Racemes or panicles terminal or axillary, bracteolate. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed, the upper 2 teeth more or less connate. Corolla white or purple. Petals clawed; vexillum orbicular; wings and keel oblique, obovate-oblong; keel free. Stamens 10, free, all fertile or 5 abortive; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary subsessile; style filiform, stigma lateral. Pods ellipsoidal or oblong, 2-valved, rarely indehiscent. Seeds 1–few, scarlet or 2-coloured.

About 100 species distributed in tropical America, SE Asia and NW Australia; 35 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Trees, few‑branched. Leaves opposite, large, 2–3‑pinnately compound; leaflets ovate, entire. Inflorescences racemose, terminal, erect and long. Calyx large, purple, leathery, broadly campanulate, fleshy, apex subtruncate or inconspicuously dentate. Corolla large, purple‑red, campanulate; limb slightly bilabiate; lobes 5, spreading, apex rounded, margin sinuous. Stamens 5, subequal, all fertile; filaments slender, long, compressed; anthers ellipsoidal, 2‑celled, glabrous; thecae parallel. Style filiform; stigma lingulate, compressed. Capsule dehiscing septicidally, long lanceolate, woody, compressed, to 1 m; septum woody, flat. Seeds in several rows, very thin, compressed, orbicular, surrounded by a transparent broad wing.

One species distributed Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial. Culms tufted, erect or ascending. Leaf blades mainly cauline, broadly linear, herbaceous, flat, with smooth or scabrid margins; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a panicle, often nodding, with raceme-like primary branches; pedicels short. Spikelets with 1 fertile floret above 2 sterile lemmas, strongly laterally compressed, disarticulating below sterile lemmas, persistent in cultivated species; glumes vestigial, remaining after disarticulation as a shallow lobed frill at pedicel apex; fertile lemma boat-shaped, strongly keeled, leathery, closely papillose, sometimes spinulose, infrequently smooth, prominently 5-veined, apex awnless to long awned; palea resembling lemma but narrower, 3-veined, apex beaked. Stamens 6. Caryopsis variable in shape, hilum linear.

Approximately 25 species in warm parts of Africa, Asia, Australia and C & S America; five species (two introduced) in China; one species (cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Erect herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Leaves opposite or sometimes in whorls of 3, petiolate or sessile, 3–7-basiveined. Inflorescences terminal, capitate or paniculate. Flowers 4–5-merous, usually bracteate. Calyx-tube urceolate or flask-shaped; the limb of 4–5 lobes or teeth, often with bristle-like appendages or stalked tuft of hairs between them. Petals as many, obovate to broadly ovate. Stamens twice as many, equal or subequal; anthers opening in a single pore, connectives without appendage at base. Ovary half-inferior, 4–5-locular, apex with a ring of bristles. Fruit capsular, ovoid or oblong ovoid, middle part often contracted, usually ribbed, longitudinally dehiscing by 4–5 apical pores. Seeds numerous, curved (cochleate), densely granulate.

About 50 species distributed in tropical W Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs to small trees, dioecious or androdioecious. Leaves opposite, simple, petiolate; leaf blade entire or serrate, usually glandular dotted, ± leathery. Inflorescences cymose, fasciculate in leaf axils or in very short and axillary or terminal panicles; bracts 2, united at base, usually ciliate. Flowers bisexual, usually functional unisexual. Calyx cupular, 4‑lobed. Corolla usually white or yellowish, campanulate, cylindric, or urceolate, lobed, parted, or divided almost to base; lobes 4, imbricate in bud. Stamens 2(–4), mostly attached to upper half of corolla tube; filament short; anther extrorsely dehiscent, connectives mucronate. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 pendulous ovules in each locule; stigma capitate or 2‑cleft; abortive pistil subulate or conical. Fruit a drupe, elliptic or obovate; endocarp hard or bony; endosperm fleshy; radicle erect.

About 30 species, mainly distributed in E and SE Asia, a few in America; 26 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with stout taproots; stems erect and tall, usually hollow, glabrous or hairy. Leaves basal and cauline; petiole sheaths inflated; leaf blade 2–3-ternate-pinnate or pinnately compound; pinnae serrate to lobed. Inflorescence of loose compound umbels; rays few to many; involucral bracts few, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate; bracteoles several, linear to linear-lanceolate. Calyx-teeth triangular-ovate, conspicuous. Petals white, pink, purplish or violet, ovate to obovate, with a narrowly inflexed apex. Fruit oblong-ovoid, strongly flattened dorsally, pubescent or glabrous, the lateral ribs broadly thin or corky-winged, the dorsal ribs also prominent but not winged; carpophore 2-cleft to the base. Vittae 1 or 2 in each furrow, 2–many on the commissure. Seed strongly compressed dorsally, the inner face plane to concave.<br/><br/>About ten species in E Asia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, of freshwater. Stems usually corm-like. Leaves all basal, petiolate, usually sheathing at base; blades submerged or sometimes floating, linear to broadly ovate, 3–11-veined. Spathes elliptic or ovate, usually 2–6-winged, apex bifid or trifid, with 1 – many flowers. Flowers bisexual or unisexual and plants dioecious. Male flowers with longer pedicel. Bisexual and female flowers shortly pedicellate or without pedicel. Sepals 3, greenish, linear, oblong, or ovate. Petals 3, coloured, orbicular to broadly obovate, much longer and wider than sepals. Stamens 3–15; filaments linear, flattened; anthers laterally dehiscent; staminodes (absent or 1–)3, often present in female flowers. Ovary of 3, 6 or 9 (or more) carpels; ovules many; stigmas 2 per style, linear. Fruit cylindrical, fusiform, or conical. Seeds many, small, often hairy.

About 21 species distributed in tropical to temperate areas; about five species in China (two endemic); one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms slender, decumbent and rooting at the lower nodes. Leaf sheath shorter than internode, margins ciliate; leaf blade lanceolate, open and flat; ligule truncate, ± ciliolate. Inflorescence an open panicle, primary branches spaced along the central axis, spikelets borne on short secondary branches, singly or in appressed secondary racemelets, falling off from pedicel, pedicel very short. Spikelets elliptic, dorsally compressed, 2-floret; glumes similar, 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, herbaceous, 3–5(–7)-veined; lower floret sterile or staminate, lemma as long as the spikelet, membranous, 7–9-veined; upper floret bisexual, lemma leathery to cartilaginous, 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, glabrous, 3–5-veined, margins narrow, hyaline, incurved upward embraced same texture palea, acute; lodicules thin, 5-veined; style free from the base.

Three species distributed in Old World tropics; one species and one variety in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, acaulescent or caulescent, often with underground tuberous or bulbous stem. Leaves basal or alternate, digitate; leaflets usually 3, sometimes 5 or more, entire; stipules very small or wanting. Flowers 1–several terminating axillary peduncles, forming simple or irregularly compound umbels or cymes. Sepals 5, free or slightly connate at the base. Petals 5, yellow, white, pink or red. Stamens 10, in 2 series, 5 long and 5 short, all bearing anthers. Ovary 5-locular; styles 5, free. Fruit a capsule, opening at the angles in valves.

About 500 species, cosmopolitan, but mainly in S America; seven species (3 introduced) in China; two species (introduced) in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, sometimes straggling. Branches stout, armed with opposite axillary thorns. Leaves opposite or crowded on very short lateral branches. Stipules interpetiolar, free or united at the base. Flowers pedicellate, in few‑ to many‑flowered clusters or cymes, axillary or at apex of short branches or tufts of leaves. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped or bell‑shaped; limb usually 5‑toothed. Corolla salverform, usually glabrous abaxially; tube cylindric, usually pubescent at throat or on the upper parts of the tube; lobes usually 5, recurved in anthesis, contorted in the bud. Stamens 5, attached to the throat, alternate with corolla‑lobes; filaments very short; anthers dorsifixed, exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with several to many ovules in each locule; style slender, with 2 divaricate or coherent stigmatic lobes. Fruit a berry, few‑ to many‑seeded.

About 20 species in S & SE Asia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial twining or erect herbs, with fleshy tubers. Stipules and stipels present. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets large, ovate or rhomboid, entire or sinuately lobed. Racemes or panicles axillary; rhachis often nodose. Bracts caducous; bracteoles small, subpersistent or minute and caducous. Calyx 2-lipped, upper lip emarginate, lower lip 3-toothed. Corolla violet or white, exserted from calyx; vexillum broadly obovate, with 2 inflexed auricles at base; wings oblong or falcate, often adherent to middle of keel; keel subequal to wings. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary many-ovuled; styles filiform, inflexed distally. Pods loriform, 2-valved, constricted between seeds. Seeds compressed, suborbicular or transversely oblong.

Six species distributed in tropical America; one species cultivated in China, also in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Leaves large, petiolate. Inflorescence of a showy terminal spikes, 4‑sided, flowers 1 – many in cluster. Bracts conspicuous, overlapping. Bracteoles small or absent. Calyx 5‑lobed, lobes equal or uppermost narrower. Corolla tubular, ringent, slenderly obconic, curved, 2‑lipped, upper lip narrow, 2‑lobed apically, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal. Stamens 2, subequal to the corolla, attached near the base of tube; anthers deeply sagittate, 2‑thecous, thecae parallel, muticous at base. Staminodes absent. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma obtuse. Capsule 4‑seeded.

About 12 species in neotropics; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs, dormant in winter. Rhizomes flesh, cylindrical or yoke-shaped, with 2 buds developing into a leafless scape and a vegetative shoot separately. Leaves linear, papery, plicate-venose. Scape aphyllous, with many brownish cataphylls. Flowers medium-sized, resupinate, hairy, in a terminal raceme; sepals subequal, the odd one free, the lateral ones oblique at the base, adnate to the short column-foot forming a mentum; petals slightly narrower than the sepals; lip attached to the column-foot, subgibbous at the base, 3-lobed, lateral lobes erect, rounded, midlobe slightly recurved, retuse, disk fleshy, papillose; column long, arcuate, semiterete and plane in front, enlarged at the apex, forming 2 lateral pouches; clinandrium membranous; rostellum obtuse; anther terminal, pilose, 2-lobed; pollinia 8, waxy, obovoid-cuneate, subcoherent at the apex of the slender caudicles; ovary cylindrical, hairy. Capsules oblong, ridged and rostrate.

About five species distributed in tropical Asia, Papua New Guinea and Pacific islands; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Twining herbs or shrubs. Branches terete, twisted. Leaves opposite, rarely in whorls of 3 or 4, petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, usually triangular, deciduous. Flowers in axillary or terminal cymes, often paniculate. Calyx‑tube turbinate or ovoid; limb 4–5‑lobed, persistent. Corolla tubular or funnel‑shaped, pubescent outside, glabrous or hairy at throat; limb 4 – 5‑lobed, lobes valvate and folded in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the top of corolla‑tube; anthers dorsifixed or basifixed, included. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style deeply 2‑parted, twisted. Fruit dry, the exocarp fragile, consisting of 2 compressed nutlets.

About 20 species mainly in tropical and subtropical Asia and America; 11 species in China; two species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, usually spiny. Leaves alternate, 3-veined at base, entire or serrate; stipules usually converted into spines. Flowers small, bisexual, in axillary or sometimes terminal cymes. Calyx 5-lobed. Petals 5, spathulate or fan-shaped, laterally involute. Stamens 5, alternate with petals and slightly longer than them. Ovary half-immersed in the disk, 3-locular, with 3 oblong stigmas. Fruit dry, hemispherical, 2–3-celled, surrounded by a broad corky wing.

About six species distributed from S Europe to E Asia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, with or without prop roots, rarely epiphytes. Stems erect or prostrate, simple or forked. Leaves spirally arranged, stiff, long-linear, keeled, often prickly on midrib and along margins, base sheathing. Inflorescence terminal, pendent, capitate or spicate; spathes usually coloured. Flowers unisexual, dioecious, without perianth. Male flowers generally distinct, with stamens very variable in numbers, free or aggregated into phalanges of various forms. Female flowers densely crowded in a head or oblong spike, staminodes absent; ovaries becoming woody or drupaceous, and sometimes united, forming a globose or ellipsoidal syncarp. Seeds minute, testa striated, albumen hard fleshy.

About 700 species, distributed in tropical zones from Africa to Asia and various archipelagos in the Pacific; six species in China; five species (one introduced) in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect, ascending or prostrate. Leaf blades filiform or linear to ovate-lanceolate, usually flat. Inflorescence usually a terminal open panicle, branches spreading. Spikelets dorsally compressed, deciduous below the glumes, 2-floret, the lower floret staminate or barren; glumes herbaceous to membranous, occasionally equal, usually unequal; lower usually shorter than the spikelet; upper as long as spikelet, or slightly shorter; lower lemma similar to upper glume, with or without a palea; upper floret bisexual, lemma leathery or cartilaginous, the margins inrolled embraced palea; lodicules 2; stamens 3; styles 2, free, stigma penicillate.

About 500 species distributed in tropical and warmer temperate regions of the world; 21 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs, rarely subshrubs; plant usually hispid, with milky juice, usually with pungent odour. Stem single or branched, sometimes very short. Leaves varied in shape, unlobed or pinnately to bipinnately lobed, margin sinuate, basal ones petiolate, cauline ones sessile. Flowers solitary on long pedicels, rarely arranged in racemes; flower buds pendulous, ovoid or subglobose; sepals 2, rarely 3, deciduous before flowering; petals 4, rarely 5 – 6, in 2 whorls, red, white, yellow or pale purple; stamens many, filaments filiform, coloured. Pistil 2–18-carpelled, ovary 1-locular, style absent, stigmas flat or plateform, with 4 –18-radiate lobes; parietal placentation 4 –18, ovules many. Capsules cylindrical or subglobose, dehiscing by apical pores; seeds small, reniform, with striate or netted ornamentation.

About 50 species, mainly distributed in Europe and temperate Asia, few in America, Australia and Africa; six species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial or epiphytic herbs with sympodial growth. New shoots arising from the base of an old one. Leaves oblong-linear, or band-like, distichous, uniformly green or tessellated with darker and paler green. Scape terminal to a leafy shoot. Flowers rather large and showy, solitary or in a loose raceme; odd sepal uppermost, large, colourful, lateral sepals connate forming a synsepalum generally hidden behind the lip; petals narrower than the odd sepal, spreading out horizontally; lip slipper-shaped, the margin of the basal half incurved, the base of the pouch raised slightly into an auricle on each side; column short, terete, terminated by a foliaceous staminode; fertile anthers 2, on the sides of the column, sessile, subglobose, locules 2, parallel; pollen grains dusty and in a sticky mass, not consolidated into pollinium; stigma discoid, on a short stalk; ovary cylindrical. Capsules fusiform.

About 66 species distributed in tropical Asia to Pacific islands; 18 species in China; one species native to Hong Kong.

Annual or biennial herbs; leaves alternate, simple or pinnatipartite; radical ones withered at anthesis, rarely persistent. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate, arranged as corymbs or corymbose panicles at terminal. Involucres cylindric; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, with or without spongy thickening along midvein. Receptacle plain, naked. Ligulate florets 5–19 per head, corolla yellow or orange‑yellow; stylar branches slender; anther bases sagittate. Cypselae mostly black or blackish brown, fusiform, elliptic or elliptic‑oblong, 10–12‑ribbed, minutely hirtellous along ribs especially on upper portion, apex attenuate, forming thick rostrum. Pappus in one series, white, finely scaberulous, deciduous.

About eight to ten species distributed in E to SE Asia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, rhizomatous. Leaves simple, alternate, margin dentate. Verticillasters axillary, many‑flowered, often forming globose clusters; bracteoles numerous, filiform, deciduous. Calyx tubular to obconical, 5 – 10‑veined, ± 5‑toothed; the teeth deciduous or persistent; tube slightly incurved. Corolla 2‑lipped; tube hairy annulate inside, gradually dilated at apex; upper lip erect or galeate, densely hairy abaxially; lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed, the middle lobe larger. Stamens 4, ascending under upper lip, the lower pair longer; filaments glabrous, without basal appendages; anther cells 2, parallel or divergent. Disk uniform, entire. Ovary apex truncate, glabrous or hairy. Style apex subequally 2‑cleft, lobes subulate. Nutlets obovoid or triquetrous oblong, glabrous or hairy.

About 24 species spread over China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam; 23 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with thick or slender, horizontal, jointed and scarred rhizome. Stem erect, simple. Leaves 4 – many in a terminal whorl, petiolate or sessile; blade lanceolate to ovate, usually with 3 main veins and netted veinlets. Flowers bisexual, solitary, terminal, pedunculate. Perianth segments (6–)8–14, free, in 2 whorls; outer ones leafy, green, rarely ± white, ovate to lanceolate; inner ones linear or occasionally absent. Stamens usually as many as perianth segments; filaments narrow, flat; anthers basifixed, often with convex connective apically. Ovary superior, 1-locular with parietal placentation or 4–10-locular with axile placentation; style short; stigma 4–10-lobed. Fruit a berry or a berry-like capsule, several- to many-seeded.

About 24 species distributed in tropical to temperate regions of Asia and Europe; 22 species in China, one species in Hong Kong.

Woody vines, hermaphroditic. Bark lenticellate, pith white. Tendrils racemosely 4–12-branched, apex expanded when young, later turning into suckers. Leaves simple, or palmately compound, long petiolate. Inflorescence in panicles or corymbose polychasium, leaf-opposed or pseudoterminal. Flowers 5-merous. Calyx small, cupular. Petals free. Stamens 5, opposite to petals. Disk inconspicuous. Style short. Berry small, 1–4-seeded.

About 15 species distributed in Asia and N America; nine species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

According to FKH (65. 1912), Vitis himalayana Brandis [=Parthenocissus semicordata (Wall.) Planch.] was also cultivated previously.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms tufted, erect, or with creeping rhizomes. Leaf blades linear or narrowly lanceolate, flat with involute margins; ligule short, membranous. Inflorescence composed of solitary, digitate or scattered racemes; rachis flat, often winged; spikelets solitary or paired, alternating in 2–4-rows on one side of axis, deciduous with pedicels. Spikelets elliptic or subelliptic or subrounded, 2-floret, dorsally compressed; lower glume absent or rarely present as a small scale; upper glume and lower lemma as long as spikelet or rarely upper glume shorter, membranous to subpapery, 3–7-veined; lower floret neuter, lower palea absent; upper floret bisexual, upper lemma usually coriaceous to crustaceous, rarely softer, margins inrolled embracing upper palea, upper palea similar to upper lemma, apex obtuse to apiculate; lodicules 2; stamens 3; style penicillate.

About 330 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 16 species in China; seven species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbaceous vines, with axillary tendrils. Leaves simple, entire or lobed, gland-bearing near base or on petioles; stipules linear or leaf-like, rarely absent. Cymes axillary; peduncles articulate. Flowers bisexual; sepals 5, often petaloid, sometimes with a hornlike appendage abaxially; petals 5, sometimes absent, as long as sepals; corona often consisting of filaments and scales; androgynophore present, surrounded by a membranous cupular appendage at base; stamens 5(– 8); ovary 1-locular; ovules many; styles 3. Fruit a berry, indehiscent; seeds arillate.

About 350 species mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical America, rarely in Asia and Australia; 19 species in China; two species in Hong Kong. Passiflora edulis Sims and P. suberosa L. are occasionally planted as ornamentals in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite, rarely in whorls. Stipules intrapetiolar, usually united into a sheath. Flowers in corymbiform cymes. Calyx‑tube turbinate or bell‑shaped; limb 4( – 5)‑lobed, lobes deciduous or persistent. Corolla salverform; tube slender; lobes 4, contorted in the bud. Stamens 4( – 5), attached to the throat; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style slender, usually exserted; stigma fusiform or clavate, entire or 2‑lobed, the lobes not spreading. Fruit a globular berry, 2‑celled.

About 400 species in S Africa, tropical Asia and N Australia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs, requiring dormancy in the cool and dry winter season. Leaves cauline, ovate-elliptic, up to 11 × 4.5 cm, entire. Flowers large, showy, in a terminal raceme; sepals ovate, spreading, all pointing upward, the lateral one connivent with the odd sepal; petals small, linear; lip 3-lobed, calcarate, the spur twice or more times longer than the ovary and pedicels together, the lateral lobes spreading, fringed, the midlobe linear, entire, obtuse; column broad, shield-like, retuse at the apex; rostellum fleshy, flat, broadly triangular, upright, rounded and notched at the apex, with long arms; anther cells divergent; pollinia 2, finely tessellate; caudicles slender, elongate; viscidia concealed; stigmas 2, below the rostellum, free from the auricles, grooved down the middle.

Seven species distributed in tropical and subtropical area of Asia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs or shrubs, aromatic. Stems slightly fleshy. Leaves simple, opposite or alternate, stipulate; blades unlobed or palmately lobed, margin undulate, serrate. Inflorescence a umbel, cyme, axillary and leaf-opposed, rarely flowers solitary. Flowers bracteate, zygomorphic, 5-merous. Sepals 5, imbricate, connate at base, the adaxial one elongated and forming a spur and connate to pedicel. Petals 5, imbricate, upper 2 larger and isomorphic, lower 3 isomorphic. Nectary-glands absent. Stamens 10, some or all without anthers, filaments usually connate. Ovary 5-carpellate, 5-locular, ovules 2 per locule, styles 5. Fruit a capsule, beaked, dehiscing into 5 valves; mature valves curved upward. Seed 1 per locule, endosperm wanting.

About 300 species distributed in tropical montane regions of the world; five species introduced to China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial or occasionally paludose herbs, with a few fleshy roots. Leaves caespitose, all basal, shortly petiolate; leaf blades elliptic. Flowers small, in a terminal few-flowered raceme; sepals lanceolate, hiding the petals; lip fleshy, undivided; column short; anthers oblong-ovoid; pollinia 2, granular, viscidium terminal; stigmas 2.

About 67 species mainly distributed in tropical America and tropical Asia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with short rhizomes and thick roots. Stem usually short, rarely elongate and procumbent. Leaves basal or congested on stems, petiolate; leaf blade linear to elliptic-ovate, margin entire or serrulate, subplicate-veined, with conspicuous, transverse veins between main, parallel veins, glabrous. Inflorescence usually a raceme terminating on scape. Flowers solitary or in clusters of 2–5, subtended by a bract; pedicel articulate near apex; bracteole absent or 1. Perianth segments 6, basally united into a tube, free part spreading. Stamens 6; filaments dilated and connate into a fleshy ring, rarely free; anthers subsessile. Ovary semi-inferior, 3-locular, with 2–4(–5) ovules in each locule; style shortly conical to columnar; stigma capitate to 3-lobed, small. Fruit bursting at an early stage and exposing young seeds. Seeds berry-like, ellipsoidal to globose, blue at maturity.

About 16 species distributed in topical and subtropical regions of Asia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, leaves distichous, alternate, usually very oblique. Stipules in opposite pairs. Flowers in axillary cymes or clusters (plants monoecious or dioecious). Male flowers: perianthsegments 4 – 5, elliptic, united at the base, imbricate in the bud; stamens as many and opposite to the segments; rudimentary pistil small, obconical. Female flowers: perianth-segments free, narrowly oblong, usually unequal; staminodes squamiform; ovary 1-locular, with 1 erect ovule; stigma sessile, small, shortly penicillate. Achene small, ovoid or ellipsoid, slightly compressed, surrounded by persistent perianth.

About 60 species chiefly in tropical Asia; 20 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees, unarmed. Leaves bipinnate; pinnae opposite; leaflets many, opposite, sessile. Inflorescence an axillary or terminal panicle or raceme. Bracts small, deciduous or persistent; bracteole absent. Flowers bisexual, yellow, large and showy. Calyx-tube rather short; lobes 5, subequal, imbricate. Petals 5, spreading, imbricate. Stamens 10, free, filaments slightly exserted, densely hirsute at base, anthers ellipsoidal, dorsifixed. Ovary sessile, 3– 8-ovuled; style long; stigma large, peltate, capitate or disciform. Pods long elliptic, flat, thin and hard, indehiscent, winged along both sutures. Seeds 2– 8, flat; endosperm wanting.

About 12 species distributed in S & SE Asia and tropical Australia; two species (one introduced) in China; also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms stout and solid, erect or ascending. Leaf blades linear, flat conduplicate or inrolled, margins scabrid; ligule short, glabrous or ciliate. Inflorescence a spike-like panicle, cylindrical to subglobose; branches many, contracted into short clusters of 1 or more spikelets subtended by an involucre of bristles; involucres deciduous with the spikelets at maturity leaving peduncle stumps or scars on the main axis; bristles slender, scabrous, sometimes plumose. Spikelets solitary or 2–3-fasciculate, sessile or pedicellate, usually lanceolate, florets 2, falling off as a whole; glumes unequal, lower glume thin and small, 0–3-veined, upper glume longer than lower glume, 1–3-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, lower lemma slightly shorter than spikelet, or sometimes as long, with broadly incurved margins, 3–8-veined; upper lemma bisexual, as long as spikelet or shorter, herbaceous or indurated thickened papery or coriaceous; lodicules 2; stamens 3; style base ± connate.

About 80 species spread throughout the tropics; 11 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.
The morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Herbs or subshrubs, erect or prostrate, usually hispid or tomentose. Leaves opposite; stipules interpetiolar, multi‑fid or bristly, united at the base. Flowers usually in corymbs. Calyx‑lobes 4 – 6, unequal. Corolla tubular, pilose abaxially; tube dilated and villous in the throat, apex 4 – 6‑lobed; lobes valvate in bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, inserted in the upper part of the corolla‑tube. Disk often produced into a cone after anthesis. Ovary 2‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style exserted. Fruit a membranous or leathery capsule, opening loculicidally; seeds small, numerous.

About 34 species in Africa to Arabia and Madagascar; one species cultivated in China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Leaves opposite, narrow. Cymes raceme‑like or umbel‑like. Pedicels threadlike. Calyx with basal glands. Corolla rotate or nearly bell‑shaped; tube short; lobes narrow, longer than tube, twisted to right. Corona‑lobes 5, inserted on corolla‑tube, apical appendages denticulate or lobed. Filaments connate into a short tube; anthers erect, apex membranous and inflexed on base of stigma; pollinia 1 in each cell, erect, ovoid, apex with a small translucent beak. Stigma head conical or flat, apex 2‑cleft. Follicles cylindric‑lanceolate, smooth.

Four species distributed in SE Asia; one species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, annual or, usually perennial, rooting from lower nodes and with erect or ascending flowering shoots. Stems usually dwarf, fleshy; vascular bundles free, scattered. Prophylls absent. Leaves alternate, opposite, or whorled, main lateral veins all basal, reticulate veins inconspicuous. Flowers bisexual, very small, often within depressions in rachis, sessile. Inflorescence a spike, usually erect, terminal, axillary, or rarely leafopposed, solitary, paired or clustered, rachis as thick or slightly thicker than peduncle; bracts ± orbicular, peltate, sometimes oblong. Stamens 2, filaments short, anther cells ± globose, ellipsoid, or cylindric. Ovary 1-locular; ovule 1; stigma 1, rarely 2-cleft, globose, apex obtuse or acute, beaked or brush-like, lateral or terminal. Fruit a very small, sticky nutlet, often partly enclosed in pit in rachis, sometimes distinctly curved.

About 1000 species, widely distributed in tropical and subtropical areas; seven species and two varieties occur from SE to SW China; two species in Hong Kong.

In addition, Peperomia obtusifolia A. Dietr. and Peperomia sandersii C. DC. are occasionally cultivated as ornamentals in Hong Kong.

Woody vines. Leaves palmately nerved. Cymes axillary, solitary or 2–3 fascicled. Male flowers: sepals 9, in 3 whorls, the outmost 3 minute, bracteal, the inner 6 larger and concave, imbricate; petals 6, cuneate or rhomboid-obovate, lateral margins involute and clasping opposite stamen; stamens 6, free or ± connate, anthers dehiscing longitudinally. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; staminodes 6, clavellate; carpels 3; style short; stigma 2-parted, or the lobes bifid again. Drupes compressed globose with style-scar near base; kernel bony, broadly obovate-globose, dorsally covered with conical or short spiny processes on both faces; seeds horseshoe-shaped.

About two or three species in SE Asia; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Annual aromatic herbs. Leaves simple, opposite. Verticillasters 2‑flowered, forming terminal and axillary secund racemes; bracts broadly ovate to subrounded. Flowers pedicellate. Calyx campanulate, 10‑veined, straight in flower, enlarged, spreading or pendulous, swollen on one side in fruit, throat pilose annulate, limb 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑toothed, the middle tooth smallest, lower lip 2‑toothed, teeth lanceolate. Corolla white to purple‑red, with a short tube, throat oblique; limb shortly 5‑cleft, nearly 2‑lipped; upper lip emarginate; lower lip 3‑lobed, lateral lobes smaller than middle lobe, similar to upper lip. Stamens 4, subequal, nearly straight, not exserted; anther cells 2, parallel, becoming divergent or divaricate. Style included, apex 2‑cleft; lobes subequal, subulate. Nutlets subglobose, reticulate.

A monotypic genus distributed in E Asia; one species and two varieties in China and Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs, with small oblong tubers on slender stalks, passing the dry cool winter in dormancy. Leaves 2 or 3, close together, usually at the ground level, 2–12 cm. Flowers small, spirally arranged in a terminal spike; sepals subequal, free, erect, connivent; petals small, below the odd sepal and with it forming a hood; lip trilobed and calcarate, the spur shorter than the ovary, the disk fleshy, recurved, often with a mound-like callus, the lateral lobes entire, filiform or rarely ovate, the midlobe ovate, obtuse; column short, conical, auricles prominent, the apex entire, rotundate; rostellum yoke-shaped; anther 2-celled, the thecae parallel; pollinia 2, obovoid, sectile, the fragments relatively large, the caudicles short, equal or shorter than the pollinia; viscidia oblong or linear, relatively long; stigmas 2, convex, entirely adnate to the base of the lip and to the auricles of the column; ovary sessile. Capsules small, not much longer than the ovary, ellipsoidal, with persistent perianth.

About 60 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Pacific islands; 21 species in China; five species native to Hong Kong, growing along paths in forested areas or on exposed slopes.

Annual or sometimes perennial herbs. Culms ascending from the decumbent base. Leaf blades short, broad, base slightly cordate, margins often pectinate-ciliate; ligule a membranous rim. Inflorescence a cylindrical, spike-like raceme. Spikelets all alike, 1-flowered, bisexual, borne directly on all sides of main axis, single or often ± in groups, falling entirely from a very short pedicel; glumes subequal, as long as spikelet and enclosing floret, papery, 1-veined, rounded, strongly convex, scabrous, apex with a long slender awn far exceeding glume body, lower glume tightly embraced by upper glume, its awn usually longer than upper glume awn; lemmas lanceolate, shorter than glumes, hyaline, 1-veined, glabrous, apex acute; palea hyaline, slightly shorter than lemma, flattened; lodicules 2. Stamens 3; anthers small. Styles very short, stigmas poorly developed. Caryopsis linear-lanceolate, terete or flattened, apex acute, almost as long as the glumes at maturity.

About ten species distributed in the Old World tropics; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees, rarely shrubs. Terminal vegetative bud conical. Stipules narrowly triangular, sometimes bifid at apex, deciduous. Leaves opposite. Inflorescences globular capitate; peduncles usually axillary, unbranched or branched like a simple dichasium or trichasium. Flowers bisexual, regular, 4–5‑merous, subsessile, densely crowded on the hairy receptacle; interfloral bracteoles spathulate to filiform‑spathulate. Hypanthia mutually free. Calyx‑tube short, lobes deltoid to elliptic‑oblong, apex obtuse, persistent. Corolla hypocrateriform to narrowly infundibular; lobes valvate in the bud but subimbricate at the apex. Stamens inserted in the upper part of corolla‑tube; filaments short, glabrous; anthers basifixed, introrse, protruding from the throat. Ovary 2‑locular, with up to 10 pendulous ovules in each locule; style exserted, stigma globose to obovoid. Infructescence a globular head, composed of numerous fruitlets with a hard endocarp splitting septicidally and loculicidally into 4 valves from base to apex.

Four species in E Asia to Malesia regions; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Leaves alternate, or tufted on spur branches petiolate, lanceolate, oblong, or ovate, entire, dentate, or denticulate. Capitula discoid, homogamous, subsessile or pedunculate, solitary and terminal, or arranged in corymbose or paniculate inflorescence. Involucre campanulate or cylindric; phyllaries few‑ to multi‑seriate, imbricate, herbaceous or leathery; receptacle flat, alveolate or not, glabrous or villous around alveola, without paleae. Florets few, hermaphrodite, fertile, tubular, corollas deeply 5‑lobed, regularly or slightly irregularly, rarely obviously irregularly, lobes linear, revolute. Anther bases long tailed, apex appendaged. Styles shallowly divided at apex, style arms very short, abaxially with short hairs or papillae, apices obtuse. Cypselae terete, obovoid or obconic, ribbed. Pappus of scabrid bristles, numerous.

About 25 species distributed from Afghanistan to Japan; 18 species (17 endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Biennial or rarely annual glabrous herbs; stems erect, branching above. Leaves 2–3-pinnate; ultimate segments ovate to linear, toothed or lobed. Inflorescence of compound umbels, terminal and axillary; involucral bracts few or absent; bracteoles several. Calyx-teeth obsolete. Petals yellow or yellowish-green, obovate, apex emarginate, narrow, inflexed. Stylopodium low-conic; styles short, spreading. Fruit ovoid-oblong, slightly flattened laterally, mericarps subrounded in cross section, commissure constricted, glabrous, shiny; ribs 5, filiform, prominent; vittae 1 in each furrow, 2 on commissure. Seed face plane. Carpophore 2-cleft to base or to middle.

Two species native in S and W Europe, cultivated worldwide; one species (introduced) in China; also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, usually with glandular hairs. Leaves simple, entire, alternate or sometimes opposite on the upper part of stem. Flowers solitary, terminal and axillary. Calyx 5‑lobed to near base; lobes oblong to linear. Corolla funnelform or salverform; limb usually 5‑lobed regular or obscurely 2‑lipped; lobes broad and short, imbricate in the bud. Stamens 5, inserted at or below middle in corolla‑tube, 4 in pairs, the fifth much smaller or rudimentary. Ovary 2‑locular; stigma 2‑lobed; ovules numerous in each locule. Fruit a capsule, many‑seeded.

About three species distributed in S America; one species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with thick rootstock surrounded by fibrous of remnant leaf-sheath; stems striate, branched above. Leaves ternately or pinnately compound, petiole sheaths inflated. Inflorescence of compound umbels; involucral bracts wanting or few; rays few to many; bracteoles few to numerous or wanting. Calyx-teeth prominent to obsolete. Petals ovate to obovate with narrower inflexed apex, white or reddish, rarely yellow. Stylopodium low-conic. Fruit ellipsoidal, oblong to suborbicular, the dorsal ribs filiform, not winged, the lateral ribs usually winged; vittae solitary to several in each furrow, 2–several on the commissure. Seeds dorsally compressed, slightly concave to plane.

About 100–200 species in Europe, Asia and Africa; 40 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs requiring dormancy in the dry cool season. Young shoot emerging from the base of a one-year-old pseudobulb and changing into a pseudobulb after anthesis. Leaves 5 or 6, plicate-venose. Scape axillary to the second leaf from the bottom. Flowers large, showy, in a terminal raceme; sepals and petals similar in size and colour, free, spreading; lip undivided, trumpet-shaped, embracing the column, calcarate, the spur short and pointed, the apical margin wavy; column long, slightly enlarged and winged at the apical portion, without foot; clinandrium short, oblique, sinuate at the margin; rostellum subtruncate; anther attached to the margin of the clinandrium, incumbent, convex; pollinia 8, waxy, unequal, obovoid, slightly compressed laterally; connected at the apex by granular mass; stigma suborbicular; ovary obovoid-cylindrical. Capsules ellipsoidal, pendulous, rostrate, ridged.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia and Oceania; eight species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms usually tufted, sometimes the lowest internode swollen into a corm. Leaf blades flat, linear; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a contracted or spike-like panicle. Spikelets strongly laterally compressed, ovate, 3-flowered, the lower 2 floret usually reduced to sterile lemmas and uppermost floret bisexual, disarticulating above glumes at maturity, rachilla not or very rarely extended beyond uppermost floret; glumes subequal, boat-shaped, as long as spikelet and enclosing florets, herbaceous, prominently 3-veined, strongly keeled and often winged along midvein; sterile lemmas usually subulate and up to 1/2 length of fertile lemma, rarely chaffy or as little fleshy scales, sometimes reduced to an obscure knob; fertile lemma laterally compressed, leathery often becoming cartilaginous and shiny, rounded on back, obscurely 5﹣veined, awnless; palea resembling lemma, 2﹣veined. Stamens 3. Caryopsis tightly enclosed by lemma and palea; embryo small; hilum linear.

About 15 species distributed mainly in the Mediterranean region and warm-temperate parts of the New World; five species (four introduced) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Twining or erect herbs, often with hooked hairs. Stipules basifixed, base not elongated, persistent; stipels present. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate. Racemes axillary. Bracts and bracteoles persistent or deciduous. Flowers borne on swollen nodes. Calyx 2-lipped, upper lip 2-toothed connate, lower lip 3-toothed. Corolla yellow, white, red, or purple. Petals clawed; vexillum orbicular, reflexed, base with appendage or not; wings obovate or oblong, adherent to keel; keel linear, beak long, spirally coiled through 1–2 twins. Stamens diadelphous; styles spiral with keel over 360˚; stigma oblique. Pods linear or oblong, subterete or compressed, 2-valved. Seeds 2–many, oblong or reniform, hilum shortly linear, estrophiolate.

About 50 species distributed in warm regions, especially tropical America; three species cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs with short rhizome. Inflorescence scape 1 m or longer, with few cauline leaves gradually replaced by alternate bracts. Flowers perianth yellow. Stamens adnate with base of inner and adaxial tepals; anthers spirally twisted, extrorse; pollen grains shed as tetrads. Staminodes cuneate, acute, shorter than fertile stamens. Ovary 3-loculate, with parietal placentation. Fruit capsule loculicidal, triangularoblong.

Monotypic, in Australia, S and SE Asia, W Pacific, China and Hong Kong.

Evergreen large to dwarf shrubs, dioecious. Stems solitary or clustered, often with spirally arranged petiole bases or rough leaf scars. Leaves pinnate, induplicate; pinnae regularly arranged or grouped, linear to linear-lanceolate; the lower ones sometimes modified as stout spines (acanthophylls); sheaths open, fibrous. Inflorescences axillary, branched, erect or pendulous when fruiting; peduncle bearing a prophyll, other bracts inconspicuous; rachillae clustered or spirally arranged along rachis. Flowers small, unisexual; male flower with calyx 3-lobed, petals 3, stamens 6, rarely 3 or 9, pistillode absent; female flower subglobose, with sepals 3-lobed, petals 3, staminodes 6; carpels 3, free. Fruits obovoid, oblong, usually developed from 1 carpel, variously coloured, epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy, endocarp thin and membranous. Seed 1, elongate, deeply grooved, endosperm homogeneous, rarely ruminate.

About 14 species in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Africa; three species in China (one introduced); two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic perennial herbs growing on damp rocks or rarely on trunks of trees along streams. Rhizomes covered by imbricate scales. New shoots emerging from the base of the pseudobulbs, each bearing a terminal raceme, after anthesis a joint behind the inflorescence changing into a pseudobulb with 2 leaves. Leaves terminal to pseudobulb, evergreen, elliptic or lanceolate. Flowering shoots horizontal, bearing green cataphylls and 2 underdeveloped leaves at anthesis, becoming erect and with the leaves and pseudobulbs developed after flowering. Flowers rather small, non-resupinate, in a terminal raceme; sepals subequal, ovate, spreading, slightly concave; petals slightly narrower than the sepals; lip strongly concave, subsaccate at the base, the lateral lobes small and erect, midlobe straight or recurved; column stout, the apex broadly winged; rostellum truncate, projected forward covering the stigmatic cavity; anther incumbent, subglobose; pollinia 4, waxy, ovoid, and acuminate; viscidium apical; stigma discoid; ovary cylindrical, striate. Capsules elliptic-obovoid, strongly ridged and grooved.

About 30 species distributed in tropical Asia, Australia and Pacific islands; 14 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, unarmed. Leaves alternate, simple, petiolate, entire or serrate, pinnately-veined; stipules free, small, caducous. Inflorescence a terminal, panicle- or corymb-shaped compound raceme. Hypanthium campanulate or turbinate, adhering to the ovary. Sepals 5, short, persistent. Petals 5, white to pinkish, more or less clawed at base. Stamens 20, rarely more, inserted in the throat of the hypanthium. Ovary more or less inferior, 2–5-loculed, with 2 erect ovules in each locule; styles 2–5, connate at base. Fruit a small, 1–4-seeded pome, crowned by an annular remains of the calyx-teeth; testa firm, endosperm thin or absent, cotyledons plano-convex.

About 25 species in S and E Asia; 18 species in China; three species (one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Perennial reeds, rhizomatous. Culms tall, erect. Leaves all cauline; leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, flat; ligule membranous with ciliate margin. Inflorescence a large terminal panicle, composed of many branches and silky-hairy spikelets. Spikelets laterally compressed, with 3–11 loosely arranged florets, lowest floret masculine or empty, resembling glumes but longer, persistent, succeeding florets bisexual, the uppermost ± reduced; rachilla bearded above with long silky hairs, disarticulating between bisexual florets; glumes 3–5-veined, unequal, papery, much shorter than lowest lemma; floret callus linear, silky-plumose with long spreading hairs; lowest lemma 3–7-veined, ± persistent; fertile lemmas narrow, 1–3-veined, entire, acuminate, glabrous, rounded or slightly keeled on back; palea short, hyaline, ca. 2/3 length of lemma. Stamens 3, or 2 in the lowest floret.

A cosmopolitan genus of four or five species; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Stems unbranched. Rhizomes creeping. Basal leaves 1 or more; cauline leaf 1 or absent; leaf sheath and petiole long. Inflorescences on leafy shoots, subtended by a cauline leaf or often in a very compact, congested group of few to many small spikes. Bracts spirally arranged, often shredding into fibers after anthesis, at least at apex. Flower pairs 2–many per bracts. Sepals usually longer than corolla tube, membranous. Corolla tube proximally ± solid, distally hollow; lobes 3, oblong, subequal. Outer staminodes 2, petaloid, obovate, staminode tube longer than corolla tube; callose staminode wholly callose, not petaloid at apex. Style curved after tripping; stigma enlarged, blunted. Fruit globose to ellipsoidal, dehiscent, often late dehiscent; pericarp hard. Seeds 1–3; aril membranous.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Asia; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Prostrate herbs. Stems herbaceous, usually acutely 4‑angled, sometimes woody at base, often spiny, hirsute, glandular, rooting at node. Leaves simple, opposite. Inflorescences terminal, spicate or capitate, ± elongate in fruit. Bracts obovate. Flowers small, sessile or subsessile. Calyx small, membranous, ± 2‑lipped, 4‑lobed. Corolla sometimes 2‑lipped; upper lip smaller, entire or 2‑lobed, lower lip larger, 3‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted on distal part of corolla tube, inclusive. Ovary 2‑locular; ovule 1 per locule. Style short; stigma capitate. Fruit small, dry, splitting into two 1‑seeded nutlets.

About ten species distributed in Africa, America, and Asia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs or herbs, without laticiferous juice. Leaves alternate, entire, usually distichous, giving the smaller branches the appearance of pinnate leaves; stipules small, usually persistent. Flowers usually small, unisexual (plant monoecious or rarely dioecious), apetalous in axillary clusters or solitary. Male flowers: sepals (2–)3–6, in 1 or 2 series, free, imbricate, in the buds; disk prominent, entire or 3–6-lobed; stamens 2–6, filaments united in a central column or free; anthers 2-celled, extrorse; pistillode absent. Female flowers: sepals as in male flowers; ovary usually 3(–4–12)-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles 3–12, free or united at the base, more or less 2-lobed. Fruit usually a capsule, separating into 2-valved cocci or loculicidally dehiscent; seeds trigonous.

About 750–800 species distributed primarily in the tropics and subtropics, poorly represented in the temperate regions; 33 species, one subspecies and four varieties in China; 12 species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or subshrubs. Stipules striate; stipels present. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets entire or repand. Panicles racemiform, composed of umbels enclosed in opposite, orbicular, persistent leafy bracts. Calyx campanulate, 5-lobed, the upper 2 usually united into one, the lower 3 longer than the upper ones. Corolla white or yellowish, rarely purple; vexillum obovate or broad-obovate, base clawed or attenuate; wings narrowly elliptic, smaller than keel, auriculate and clawed; keel incurved, auriculate, long-clawed. Stamens monadelphous, or the vexillary stamen more or less free. Ovary longer than stamen. Disk present. Pods 2–7-jointed; joints orbicular-truncate, flat. Seeds arillate.

Six species distributed in S Asia and N Australia; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Arborescent or shrubby bamboos. Rhizomes leptomorph, with running underground stems. Culms diffuse; internodes profoundly flattened or grooved on one side above branches; nodes 2-ridged. Branches 2, subequal, rarely with a much smaller, central or lateral 3rd branch. Culm sheaths deciduous, papery to subleathery; ligule usually conspicuous; usually auricled with long bristles; blade usually recurved or reflexed. Leaf blade with distinct transverse veins, usually abaxially pilose proximally. Inflorescence bracteate, partially iterauctant, composed of 1–7-spikeleted racemes gathered into fascicles or globose mass subtended by a tiny, membranous, 2-keeled prophyll, 0–1 gemmiferous bract, 2–6, gradually enlarged scaly bracts, and 2–7 spathiform bracts. Spikelets with 2–7 florets, terminal one sterile. Glumes absent to 1(–3). Rachilla extending beyond uppermost floret, disarticulating just below fertile florets. Lemma variable in size and texture; palea 2-keeled, apex bifid; lodicules 3, ciliate. Stamens 3. Style long; stigmas (1–)3, plumose. Caryopsis elliptical to linear-lanceolate, dorsally grooved.

At least 51 species distributed in China, India, Japan, Myanmar; introduced to many other countries; 51 species (49 endemic) in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Phyllostachys sulphurea (Carrière) Rivière & C. Rivière ‘Houzeau’(綠皮黃筋竹), P. vivax McClure(烏哺雞竹) and P. glauca McClure f. yunzhu J. L. Lu(筠竹) are only cultivated in Lung Chai, Lantau Island and not treated here.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaves simple, alternate or sometimes paired, entire or irregularly sinuate‑toothed, rarely pinnately lobed. Flowers solitary, axillary or extra‑axillary. Calyx campanulate, 5‑lobed; lobes valvate in bud, inflated after flowering. Corolla broadly campanulate or nearly rotate, white or yellow, shallowly 5‑lobed or only 5‑angled, folded in bud. Stamens 5, inserted at base of corolla‑tube; filaments dilated at base; anthers short, opening longitudinally. Ovary 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style slender; stigma obscurely 2‑lobed. Fruit a berry, globose, enclosed in the inflated calyx, many‑seeded.

About 75 species distributed mostly in Americas; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or scandent herbs, shrubs or rarely trees. Leaves simple, alternate, exstipulate. Inflorescence a many-flowered, terminal or leaf-opposed raceme. Flowers bisexual or functionally unisexual; perianth-segments 4–5, small, ± petaloid; stamens 5 –10(–30), inserted on margin of disc, in 2 series, rudimentary in functionally female flowers. Carpels 5–10(–15), free or fused; styles as many as carpels, free. Fruit fleshy, syncarpous, compressed globose, 5 –10-grooved.

About 25 species in tropical and warm regions; four species (one introduced) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees, all parts bitter; branches glabrous. Leaves imparipinnate, alternate, stipulate, base of petioles and petiolules often enlarged; leaflets opposite or nearly so, entire or serrate. Inflorescence a thyrse, axillary. Flowers unisexual, 4–5-merous. Pedicels articulate at lower half. Sepals small, distinct or connate at base, persistent. Petals valvate or nearly so, apex with an incurved acumen, longer than sepals and persistent in females. Stamens inserted at base of disk. Disk slightly thickened, entire or shallowly 4–5-lobed, sometimes enlarged in fruit. Carpels 2–5, distinct, ovule 1 per carpel; styles connate at base; stigmas distinct. Fruit comprising one or more drupaceous monocarps, exocarp thin, fleshy, rugose when dry; endocarp bony. Seeds with a broad hilum, without endosperm; testa membranous.

About nine species distributed in tropical and subtropical America and Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems creeping or diffuse. Leaves opposite, petiolate, margin crenate. Flowers in terminal or axillary racemes. Bracts small; bracteoles absent. Sepals 4, spreading; lower and upper ones large and further enlarged in fruit, base cordate; lateral lobes narrow. Corolla limb strongly 2‑lipped; lower lip longer than upper lip, spreading, 3‑lobed; upper lip base wide, apex emarginate. Stamens 4, included, anterior pair reduced to staminodes; posterior pair fertile. Anthers coherent, cells distinct, divaricate. Stigma 2‑lamellate. Capsules included in calyx, septicidal, valves separating from wide placental axis. Seeds numerous; testa rugose and scrobiculate‑reticulate.

One species distributed in S and SE Asia; it also occurs in China and in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees. Leaves spirally arranged, pseudoverticillate, or in whorls of three, petiolate, serrate to crenulate, rarely entire. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate or racemose. Pedicels short, often curved downwards, with 1–2 bracts and bracteoles at base or near apex. Calyx deeply 5-lobed. Corolla ovoid-urceolate, white, rarely reddish, shortly 5-lobed. Stamens 10, included; filaments free or connate with corolla-tube at base; anthers dorsifixed, with a pair of reflexed awns on back, opening by terminal pores. Ovary 5-locular, with many ovules in each locule. Capsule opening loculicidally by 5 valves.

Seven species in E Asia and E North America; three species in China; only one species recorded in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, rarely shrubs. Leaves opposite, subequal or very unequal in pairs, symmetrical or sometimes oblique, margin toothed or rarely entire, trinerved, or rarely pinninerved; cystoliths usually linear. Stipules membranous and squamiform, or herbaceous and leafy, intrapetiolar, or rarely interpetiolar. Inflorescence axillary, solitary or in pairs, cymose, forming spikes, panicles or clusters. Flowers unisexual, rarely polygamous (plants monoecious or dioecious). Male flowers 4- or 5-merous; perianth united at base or up to middle; segments valvate, or rarely imbricate in the bud; stamens as many as perianth-segments and opposite to them; rudimentary pistil small. Female flowers usually 3-merous, sometimes 2-, 5- or 4-merous; perianth free or slightly united, usually unequal, enlarged in fruiting time; sterile stamens bending inwards, squamiform; ovary erect, apex slightly oblique; stigma sessile, shortly penicillate. Achene ovoid or subglobose, more or less compressed, smooth or tuberculate.

About 400 species spread worldwide, but mainly in tropical and subtropical regions; 80 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen woody vines, with aerial rootlets. Leaves opposite, petiolate, leathery, margin entire or dentate. Inflorescence terminal, a corymbose panicle. Flowers bisexual, small, white. Calyx tube adnate to ovary, conical; lobes 4 – 5, imbricate. Petals 4 – 5, valvate, connate at upper part and forming a calyptra, caducous. Stamens 8 – 10, inserted at margin of disk; filaments slender; anthers subglobose, 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary inferior, 4 – 5-locular; ovules many; style 1, short, robust; stigma 4 – 6-lobed. Fruit a capsule, turbinate, 4 – 5-valved, dehiscing irregularly along ribs. Seeds many, oblong, with membranous wings at both ends.

Three species distributed in SE Asia; two species in China; both of them occur in Hong Kong.

Perennial, biennial or annual herbs; stems erect, caulescent, branching, glabrous or pubescent. Basal leaves petiolate, sheathing at base; blades simple, ternate or pinnately compound; cauline leaves often heteromorphic. Umbels terminal and lateral; involucral bracts and bracteoles present or absent, usually entire. Calyx-teeth obsolete, sometimes conspicuous, lanceolate, minute. Petals white, rarely purple, with narrow inflexed apex, glabrous to hirsute. Stylopodium conical. Fruit ovoid or ellipsoidal, narrow at apex, rounded or cordate at base, slightly laterally compressed, glabrous to pubescent, the ribs filiform, prominent; carpophores 2-cleft to the middle or to the base; vittae 2–3 in each furrow, 2–4 on the commissure. Seeds subterete in cross section, the face concave to nearly plane.


About 150 species in the N hemisphere, a few in S Africa and S America; 44 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with tuberous rhizome. Leaves 1–5, usually with bulbils on the petiole; leaf blade entire, tripartite, trilobate or pedate. Peduncle solitary, equaling or exceeding petiole. Spathe persistent, tube convolute, constricted at apex, limb oblongcymbiform, 2 times as long as tube; spadix monoecious: female portion adnate to spathe-tube from base to the constricted apex by one side, bearing ovaries at other side; male portion free from spatheblade, exserted from the tube; appendages often elongate filiform. Flowers without scales or perianth: male flower consisting of 2 stamens fused into synandria, filament short; female flower of a 1-locular ovary, with 1 basal ovule. Berries oblong-ovoid, 1-seeded.

About six species in E Asia; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees, rarely shrubs; branches verticillate; branchlets strongly dimorphic: long branchlets bearing scalelike leaves and spreading leaf bundles; short branchlets bearing leaves in bundles of 2–5(–7); winter buds large, with numerous scales. Leaves dimorphic, needlelike, slender or stout, straight or twisted, triangular, flabellate-triangular, or semiorbicular in cross section, stomatal lines several, on 1, 2, or all surfaces, vascular bundles 1 or 2, resin canals 2–10 or more, marginal or median, rarely internal, base enclosed by persistent or deciduous, membranous sheath. Pollen cones usually borne in spikelike clusters at base of 1st-year branchlets, sessile, cylindric or ovoid; pollen 2-saccate. Seed cones pedunculate or subsessile, erect or pendulous, cylindric or ovoid, maturing in 2nd or 3rd year. Seed scales spirally arranged, woody, exposed apex thickened and ridged (the apophysis), with a prominent protuberance (umbo), usually terminating in a spine or prickle, persistent. Bracts minute. Seeds variable in color, shape, and size, winged or not; wing adnate or articulated to seed. Cotyledons 3–18.

About 110 species: N Africa, Asia, Europe, N America; 39 species (seven endemic, 16 introduced) in China; two species (one endemic, one introduced) in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or climbers, rarely herbs or small trees, aromatic. Stems thickened at nodes; outer vascular bundles in a ring, inner bundles scattered in 1 or 2 series. Prophylls present, often ± connate to petiole, caducous, forming a prominent ring-like stipular scar at each node. Leaves alternate, entire, main lateral veins all basal or partly pinnate. Flowers mostly unisexual (plant dioecious, less often monoecious) or bisexual, sessile. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or rarely terminal, spicate rarely the spikes grouped into an apparently axillary umbel. Bracts small, sometimes adnate to rachis, often peltate. Stamens 2– 6, usually on rachis, rarely at base of ovary, anthers 2-locular, 2– 4-lobed. Ovary distinct or sometimes immersed in rachis; ovule 1; stigmas (2–)3 –5. Fruit a drupe, sessile or stalked, often red or yellow, ovoid, globose, or obovoid to cuneate-obovoid and laterally compressed, rarely ellipsoidal, usually glabrous.

1000–2000 species, distributed mainly in tropical regions; at least 59 species occur in China, from Taiwan through SE to SW China; six species (one introduced) in Hong Kong.

Floating aquatic herbs, acaulescent or the stem strongly abbreviated. Leaves spirally arranged, rosulate; petiole very short, almost absent, with very small ligulate sheath; leaf blade obovate, obovate-cuneate or obcordate, densely hairy; primary veins parallel, rib-like, secondary veins reticulate. Inflorescences small, on a very short peduncle hidden in leaf-bases. Spathe very small, white, leaflike, glabrous internally, hairy externally, lower margins connate to middle and with ovary wall forming a tube, limb ovate, expanded, apex acute-acuminate. Spadix shorter than spathe, dorsal 2/3 adnate to spathe; female portion with single gynoecium at base; male portion subtended by a thin, annular flap, composed of a basally naked spadix axis supporting a single whorl of a few flowers. Flowers unisexual, without scales or perianth. Male flower a synandrium composed of 2 connate stamens; thecae dehiscing by single apical slit. Female flower of a single pistil obliquely adnate to spadix axis; ovary ovoid, 1-locular with many ovules. Fruit a small ellipsoidal berry.

A monotypic genus widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of both hemispheres.

Annual or pereninal, spreading or climbing herbs by tendrils. Stems glabrous. Stipules leaf-like, semi-cordate or semi-sagittate; rachis of pinnate leaves ending in a branched tendril. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 1–3 pairs, ovate or elliptic, entire or serrate. Racemes axillary, with long peduncles or flowers solitary. Bracts caducous; bracteoles absent. Calyx campanulate, base oblique or gibbous, lobes subequal or upper 2 broader. Petals shortly clawed; vexillum obovate; wings falcate-oblong, adherent to keel; keel shorter than wings, incurved. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary subsessile; styles compressed and inflexed, longitudinaly bearded on one side. Pods oblong, 2-valved. Seeds 4 – 8, globose, hilum oblong, covered by thin aril.

About six species distributed in Europe and Asia; one species cultivated in China; also in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate or pseudoverticillate, usually clustered at branchlet apex, margin entire, undulate-dentate, or rugose. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, umbellate, corymbose, paniculate, or a solitary flower. Flowers bisexual, rarely polygamous. Sepals free, usually short and small. Petals free or connate at base. Stamens shorter than petals; filament glabrous; anther dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary shortly stipitate, 2 – or 3( –5)- carpellate, 1-locular or incompletely 2 – 5-locular; ovules many, sometimes 1 – 4; placentas parietal or basal; style usually persistent. Capsule ellipsoid or globose, sometimes compressed, dehiscing by 2 – 5 valves; pericarp woody or leathery, usually with horizontal striae adaxially. Seeds usually covered by viscid pulp.

About 150 species distributed in tropical Asia, tropical and S Africa, Atlantic Islands, Australia, Indian Ocean Islands and Pacific Islands; 46 species in China; two species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Herbs annual or perennial. Leaves usually basal, rosulate, generally long‑petiolate; blade broad‑ovate, oblong to linear, entire or serrate, rarely pinnately or palmately divided. Inflorescences a terete spike or head, terminal on scapes. Bracts and sepals with thickened or winged midvein. Flowers bisexual, rarely polygamous or unisexual. Sepals 4, persistent. Corolla salverform; lobes 4. Stamens 4, attached to corolla‑tube, usually exserted. Ovary 2‑or pseudo‑4‑locular; ovules 2–40, on axile placentas. Capsules circumscissile; pericarp membranous. Seeds 2–many, subglobular or depressed.

About 270 species, cosmopolitan; 20 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs, requiring dormancy in the winter dry and cool season, with fusiform tubers each bearing a subterminal bud. Stem solitary, leafy. Leaves 1 at the ground level and 1 or 2 cauline, bract-like. Flowers small, in a terminal spike; sepals free, the odd one uppermost, ovate, concave, the lateral sepals reflexed; petals oblique ovate, the base of the lower side subcordate, apex acute or obtuse; lip undivided, tongue-like, hanging, calcarate; column short and stout, deeply retuse at the apex, the glands prominent; rostellum horizontal, collar-like, fleshy; anther 2-celled, the thecae divergent, widely separated; pollinia 2, finely tessellate, on slender caudicles; viscidia discoid; stigma situated above the lip below the rostellum, discoid, deeply depressed in the middle; ovary bending and slightly narrowed at the apex, the ridges winged. Capsules ellipsoidal.

About 150 species mainly in N temperate regions, with a few species extends southwards to S America, tropical Africa and Asia; 41 species and three subspecies in China; two species in Hong Kong.

According to FRPS (17: 307–308) and FOC (25: 104), Platanthera tipuloides (L. f.) Lindl.(筒距舌唇蘭) is also distributed in Hong Kong, but the present author did not see any specimen collected from Hong Kong.

Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

One species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, aromatic, monoecious; bark thin, reddish brown, flaking in long strips; branchlets arranged in a plane, spreading or ascending, flattened. Leaves dimorphic, decussate, 4-ranked, scalelike, base decurrent, with an abaxial resin gland. Pollen cones ovoid, with 8–12 microsporophylls, each with 3–6 pollen sacs. Seed cones terminal, solitary, subglobose, dehiscent when mature in 1st year; cone scales 6 or 8, decussate, flat, thick, woody, only the middle 2 pairs fertile; free bract apex a long, recurved cusp. Seeds wingless, rarely with a very narrow wing, often ridged. Cotyledons 2.

One species in China, Korea, E Russia; it is cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with milky latex. Leaves whorled, or sometimes opposite or alternate. Flowers solitary and terminal, or 2 or 3 in a loose raceme. Calyx‑tube turbinate or hemispheric, adnate to the ovary; limb 5‑lobed. Corolla broadly campanulate, deep blue, 5‑lobed. Stamens 5, free; filaments flattened at base. Ovary inferior, 5‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style simple, stigma 5‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, opening at the top loculicidally in 5 valves.

A single species in E Asia.

Shrubs, subshrubs or perennial herbs. Stems erect or decumbent‑ascending. Leaves alternate, dentate. Capitula solitary or arranged as corymbs, heterogamous, disciform. Involucres ovoid, broadly campanulate or subhemispherical; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate, outer ones usually broadly ovate, inner ones narrower and longer. Receptacles plain, naked or fimbriate. Outer florets many‑seriate, female and fertile, corolla white, yellow or pale purple, filiform‑tubular, apex shallowly 3‑lobed, minutely denticulate or truncate; cypselae 4–5‑angulate, grooved. Central florets few, hermaphrodite but functionally staminate, sterile, corolla tubular, throat dilated, limb 5‑lobed; anther base tailed, acuminate, apical appendages obtuse; style unbranched or sometimes bifid, papillose; hypanthium often indistinct and vestigial. Pappus setose, in 1 series, free or connate at base, persistent.

About 80 species distributed in Asia, N & S America, Africa and Australia; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, sometimes climbing. Leaves alternate, entire; petioles often dilated at the base and amplexicaul. Flowers in terminal spikes. Bracts and bracteoles shorter than calyx. Calyx tubular, glandular, 5-ribbed, parts between the ribs scarious, apex 5-lobed. Corolla salverform, with slender tube and 5 spreading lobes. Stamens 5, free; filaments filiform, dilated at the base. Ovary 1-locular, with a single ovule; styles slender, 5 branched. Capsule enclosed in the persistent calyx, opening transversely near the base.

About ten species in temperate and subtropical regions; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees with copious latex. Branchlets 2 – 3 cm thick, nearly fleshy. Leaves alternate, long petiolate. Cymes terminal, 2‑ or 3‑branched, pedunculate; bracts usually large, deciduous before anthesis. Flowers fragrant, waxy. Calyx small, without glands. Corolla white, yellowish, pink‑red, or rose‑purple, funnelform, tube narrow, hairy inside, faucal scales absent, lobes overlapping to left. Stamens inserted at or near base of corolla‑tube; anthers free from pistil head, oblong, rounded at base; disk absent. Ovary of 2 separate carpels; ovules numerous; style short; pistil head obtusely 2‑cleft. Fruit of paired follicles; seeds many, flat proximally, with a membranous wing.

Seven species distributed in tropical America; two species cultivated in China; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, tufted, sometimes stoloniferous. Culms with or without bulbous bases. Leaf blades flat, folded or involute, abaxially keeled, adaxially with 1 groove on either side of the midvein. Inflorescence an open or contracted panicle; branches 1–9 per node.
