Spikelets laterally compressed, 2–several-flowered, rachilla disarticulating above glumes and between florets, uppermost floret vestigial; glumes unequal, or subequal, lower glume 1- or 3-veined, upper glume 3 (or 5)-veined; lemmas laterally compressed, membranous but often with hyaline margins which tend to inflex at maturity, usually distinctly keeled, 5(–7)-veined, distal margins and apex membranous, apex awnless, rarely minutely mucronate; floret callus short, truncate, blunt, glabrous or with a web of woolly hairs; palea subequal or infrequently to 2/3 length as lemma, keels scaberulous to stiffly ciliolate. Stamens (1 or) 3. Anthers sometimes vestigial. Ovary glabrous. Caryopsis oblong to fusiform, triangular to oval in cross section, sometimes grooved, free or adhering to the palea; hilum basal and punctiform, rounded to oval.

About 500 species distributed in temperate regions throughout the world; 81 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, dioecious. Leaves spirally arranged, rarely subopposite, with single, obvious, often raised midvein on 1 or both surfaces. Pollen cones axillary, rarely terminal, solitary or in clusters; microsporophylls numerous, spirally arranged; microsporangia 2; pollen 2-saccate. Seed-bearing structures usually borne in leaf or bract axils, solitary; apical bracts fertile; basal bracts often fused to form a receptacle; ovule 1 (rarely few), inverted. Epimatium wholly enveloping seed, sometimes colored and succulent. Seed ripening in first year, drupelike, dry, or leathery.

About 100 species in E Asia, tropical and subtropical regions of S hemisphere; seven species in China; one species and one varieties in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms slender, densely tufted. Leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate; ligule a membranous ciliate rim. Inflorescence of spike-like racemes, terminating the culm branches; sessile and pedicellate spikelets of a pair similar, both fertile; rachis internodes and pedicels shorter than spikelets; pedicel broad and flat, densely long pilose. Sessile spikelet oblong, laterally compressed; callus obtuse, bearded with long silky hairs; glumes subequal, membranous or thinly cartilaginous; lower glume strongly convex, dorsally compressed, 3–5-veined, apex truncate, ciliate; upper glume boat-shaped, slightly longer than lower glume, strongly compressed-keeled, apex 2-toothed, with an long and flexuose awn from sinus; upper lemma hyaline, 2-lobed for 1/3–1/2 of its length, awned; awn long, very slender, geniculate near base; stamens 1–2. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet often smaller, 1-floret, bisexual or female.

Four species distributed from India to SE Asia, NE Australia, and Polynesia; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Leaves opposite, petiolate or subsessile, ± hairy or tomentose. Verticillasters regular or secund, forming continuous or interrupted spikes or panicles; bracts and bracteoles linear to ovate. Calyx tubular or campanulate, equally or subequally 5‑toothed. Corolla with a short tube; limb nearly 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑lobed, the middle lobe usually longer and narrower than the lateral ones; lower lip entire, as long as to slightly longer than upper lip. Stamens 4, exserted, usually straight, the lower pair often slightly shorter than the upper; filaments bearded at middle; anthers terminal, 1‑celled. Disk subentire. Style shortly 2‑fid, lobes subulate, subequal. Nutlets ovoid to globose, slightly flattened, smooth.

About 40 species distributed in E India to Malesia and S China to Japan, and a few species in Africa; 16 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with horizontal rhizomes; stems erect or creeping at the base. Leaves large, alternate. Flowers actinomorphic, in terminal panicles; involucral bracts nearly leaf-like, borne on peduncles; bracts small. Sepals free, shallowly boat-shaped, often enlarging and persistent in fruits. Petals free, white, blue, purple, or greenish yellow, sometimes spotted, ovate-elliptic, ovate-orbicular, or obovate, sometimes clawed. Stamens 6, all fertile, equal or 3 smaller, or only anterior 3 fertile; filaments glabrous; anther-cells oblong, longitudinally dehiscent; antherodes deltoid-lanceolate or sagittate. Ovary 3-locular; ovules (1–)5–10 per locule. Fruits baccate, globose, 3-valved, indehiscent. Seeds (1–)5–8 per valve, purplish grey, polygonal, slightly flattened.

About 17 species in tropical, subtropical, and warm-temperate regions of the E hemisphere; eight species (one endemic) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or spreading. Leaves opposite or in false whorls. Stipules white, scarious. Flowers in terminal or axillary dichotomous cymes, densely flowered. Sepals 5, scarious and translucent. Petals 5, small, entire or 2-toothed. Stamens 5. Ovary 1-locular, with many ovules; style single, 3-cleft or nearly entire. Capsule opening into 3 valves.

About 50 species in tropical and subtropical regions; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or diffuse, dichotomously branched. Leaves opposite or sometimes false verticillate, sessile or indistinctly petiolate; stipules 2– 4, triangular, scarious. Flowers small, in axillary or terminal cymose cluster. Sepals 5, free, centrally rigid abxially, hyaline at margin. Petals 5 or often fewer, less than half the length of sepals, hyaline, entire or toothed. Stamens 3– 5; filaments united at base. Ovary 1-locular, with numerous ovules; style short, 3-lobed. Capsule shorter than calyx, opening by 3 valves.

About six species in tropical and subtropical regions; one species in China; it occurs in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite or whorled, margin entire, petiolate, exstipulate. Inflorescence a raceme or panicle, terminal, axillary or extra-axillary. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic; bracts 1–3, persistent or caducous; bracteoles present. Sepals 5, unequal, persistent or caducous, outer 3 small, inner 2 petaloid, large. Petals 3, lower 1/2 connate, keel boat-shaped, cucullate, or helmet-shaped, apex often with appendage, lateral petals smaller. Stamens 8; filaments united at least at base and forming a sheath, opening on upper side, adnate with petals; anthers basifixed, 1–2-celled, dehiscing by apical pore. Disk present or absent. Ovary 2-locular, compressed; style 1, erect or curved; stigmas 1 or 2. Fruit a loculicidal capsule, compressed, often winged. Seeds 2, usually black, ovoid, pubescent or glabrous, arillate; endosperm present or absent.

About 500 species distributed worldwide; 45 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect, prostrate or climbing. Leaves alternate, entire or lobed; stipules united into a sheath (ocrea). Flowers small, green or red, clustered or rarely solitary in axils of the upper leaves, or in little cluster surrounded by a sheathing bract, and forming terminal spikes, heads or panicles. Perianth-segments 5, or rarely fewer, united into a tube at the base. Stamens 5 – 8, sometimes variable in the same species. Ovary compressed or triangular; styles 3 or 2, united at the base or almost free; stigma entire. Fruit an achene or small nut, triangular or flattened, enclosed in or surrounded by the persistent perianth.

About 230 species, widely distributed over most parts or the world, but especially in N temperate regions; 113 species in China; 25 species and one variety in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Leaf blades flat, linear; ligule membranous. Panicle contracted to spike-like, often bristly with many small deciduous spikelets. Spikelets with 1-flowered, laterally compressed, narrowly oblong to oblong, falling entire together with pedicel or upper part of it; rachilla not prolonged; glumes longer than floret, subequal, papery, scabrid, 1-veined, apex entire to 2-lobed, often with slender awn from apex; lemma ca. 1/2 as long as glumes, truncate, hyaline, obscurely 5-veined, veins usually shortly excurrent from truncate apex, awnless or with fine subapical awnlet or geniculate dorsal awn; palea 1/2 as long to equalling lemma. Stamens 1–3.

About 25 species distributed in warm-temperate regions of the world and on tropical mountains; six species (at least four introduced) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, hermaphroditic, andro-monoecious or dioecious, unarmed, usually glabrous. Leaves 1–5-pinnately compound; stipules sometimes intrapetiolar and adnate to petiole or absent. Inflorescence of umbels or heads, sometimes in spikes, arranged in panicles or otherwise. Flowers (4–)5(–8)– merous; pedicels articulate. Calyx-margin truncate or minutely toothed. Petals valvate in the bud, free or coherent at apex. Stamens as many as petals. Ovary 5–8-locular; styles free or rarely connate at base. Disk flat or subconical. Fruit subglobose, ribbed when dry. Seeds compressed, endosperm smooth.

About 150 species in tropical regions of Indian and Pacific Oceans; five species cultivated in S China; one species widely cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, petiolate, entire or serrate. Flowers axillary, usually solitary, white; pedicels short; bracteoles 3–7, caducous; sepals 5, imbricate, unequal; petals 5, unequal, distinct or connate at base, persistent; stamens many, 1–5-seriate, connate at base and adhering to the petals; anthers inserted dorsally in basal incision; ovary 3–5(–6)-locular, ovules 4–8 per locule, pendulous, style slender, 3–6-lobed at the tip. Capsule woody, oblong-cylindric, 5-locular, loculicidally dehiscing, with a solid persistent central axis (columella). Seeds many, compressed or angled, obliquely winged above; endosperm abscent.

About 20 species distributed in tropical or subtropical Asia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, stoloniferous. Leaf blades broadly linear; ligule short, truncate, ciliolate. Inflorescence a solitary terminal raceme, fragile, with golden yellow or rusty hairy; rachis internodes broadly linear, densely ciliate on margins, shorter than spikelets, fragile at spikelet maturity; spikelets borne in threes, 2 sessile and 1 pedicellate at each node; sessile and pedicellate spikelets similar, both fertile or pedicellate spikelet male or barren, occasionally lowermost spikelets paired. Spikelets oblong; callus bearded; lower glume flat, villous, flanks keeled, apex truncate, ciliate; upper glume slightly longer than the lower, 1–3-veined, keeled along midvein; lower floret absent; upper lemma cordate, bidentate or subentire, awned; awn geniculate; palea very small or absent; stamens 3.

One species distributed in SE Asia, including China and Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves odd-pinnate; leaflets opposite, exstipellate. Racemes axillary. Flowers whitish. Bracts caducous; bracteoles minute or absent. Calyx truncate, with obsolete teeth; vexillum thinly silky abaxially, suborbicular, with inflexed auricles at base; wings obliquely oblong, slightly adherent to keel; keel obtuse. Petals coherent at apex. Vexillary stamen free at base, but connate from middle into a closed tube; anthers versatile. Ovary subsessile, 2-ovuled; style filiform, incurved, stigma small, terminal. Pods obliquely oblong, flat, thickly leathery, subfleshy or almost woody, indehiscent, 1-seeded, beaked. Seeds reniform, rather thick, with a small hilum.

One species distributed in S to SE Asia and N Australia, S & SE China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Small trees or erect shrubs. Young branches with simple hairs. Leaves leathery, glabrous, pubescent or tomentose. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or supra-axillary, 1–several-flowered. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 3, valvate in bud, free or connate. Petals 6, free or connate, in 2 whorls, fleshy, edges cohering at first, becoming free; outer petals slightly smaller than inner, both whorls basally concave, enclosing reproductive organs, erect. Stamens few, extrorse; connective with truncate dilated apex, glabrous. Carpels 5–8 per flower; ovary glabrous or hairy, free; ovules 1 or 2 per ovary, basal or lateral, 1-seriate; style not conspicuous; stigma subcapitate, discoid to flat and lobed, glabrous. Fruits apocarpous; monocarps 1– 9(–14) per fruit, globose or ovoid, glabrous to hairy; stipes 0–10 mm long; receptacles 1– 5 mm in diam.; sepals persistent. Seeds 1–4 per monocarp, basal or lateral, 1-seriate, globose to ellipsoid or lenticular; raphes (in)conspicuous.

Approximately 30 species in tropical E Asia and Australia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs or shrubs. Leaves simple, opposite or alternate, usually glabrous, with conspicuous oil glands growing along margin. Capitula homogamous‑discoid. Involucres cylindric to campanulate; phyllaries 5–9 in one series, free or united. Receptacle small and alveolate. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, yellow or purplish, corolla tube slender and much longer than the upper funnelform throat; anther bases obtuse; stylar branches long and exserted, hairy, bearing subulate apical appendages. Cypselae cylindric and attenuate. Pappus of bristle hair.

About 30 species native to N & S America; one species newly found in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, more or less succulent. Leaves alternate or sub-opposite, or crowded towards apex of stems in false whorls, terete or flat. Stipules scarious, or modified into tufts of hairs, rarely wanting. Flowers solitary, or in terminal clusters, usually surrounded by 4 or more leafy bracts. Sepals 2, connate at base, the free part caducous. Petals 4– 5, free or united at base. Stamens 4 to many. Ovary half-inferior, 1-locular, with many ovules; styles 2 to many. Capsule opening transversely.

About 40 species, widely spread over tropical and warm regions of the world; five species (two endemic) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

The genus differs from the other genus (Groenlandia) of the family by the alternate leaves and drupaceous fruit with hard endocarp and soft exocarp.

About 90 species cosmopolitan; nine species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic shrubs or subshrubs; stems usually creeping or climbing, adhering to rocks or trees by means of aerial roots. Leaves alternate, usually articulate on the ± dilated petioles; petioles winged or foliaceous; leaf blade linear-lanceolate, lanceolate, elliptic or ovate-oblong, leathery, entire. Inflorescence terminal or axillary; peduncles axillary, often bracteate below the spathe; spathe ovate, reflexed; spadix sessile or stipitate, globular or cylindrical. Flowers many, bisexual; tepal of 6 small concave scales or segments; stamens 6, opposite to the perianth-scales; filaments flat; anthers 2-celled; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; stigma sessile. Berries 1–2-seeded.

About 80 species in tropical Asia, Australia, Madagascar, Polynesia; eight species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Lianas woody, latex white. Leaves opposite. Cymes racemose or paniculate, 3–5‑branched, terminal or axillary. Flowers usually small, 5‑merous. Calyx deeply divided, with many basal glands inside. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric, throat narrowed, without scales; lobes overlapping to right. Stamens inserted at apex of corolla‑tube; filaments short; anthers exserted, sagittate, connivent at middle, adherent to pistil head, cells spurred at base; disk 5‑parted. Ovary of 2 separate carpels, shorter than disk; ovules numerous in each carpel. Style thickened at middle or near base; pistil head ovoid or fusiform, apex short conical. Fruit of paired linear follicles. Seeds linear, with an apical coma.

About four species in SE Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, subshrubs or perennial herbs. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, usually entire, 3-nerved or triplinerved; stipules usually free, persistent. Flowers usually in axillary clusters (glomerules), rarely in naked spikes; the glomerules bisexual or rarely unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious). Male flowers: perianth usually united to middle; segments (3 –)4 – 5, elliptic, convex on the back, valvate in the bud; stamens as many and opposite to the perianth-segments; rudimentary pistil obovate or clavate. Female flowers: perianth tubular, apex constricted, with 2– 4 small teeth, more or less enlarged at fruiting time; ovary included; stigma filiform, villose along one side, articulate on the ovary, deciduous. Achene ovoid, enclosed in the persistent and occasionally 2-winged perianth.

About 37 species in tropical and subtropical regions; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems usually prostrate, rooting at the nodes. Leaves alternate. Flowers solitary, axillary, rarely in racemes. Calyx adnate to the ovary; lobes 5, subequal, entire or toothed, persistent. Corolla zygomorphic, slit open on the upper side nearly to the base; limb 5‑lobed, ± bilabiate, the 2 upper lobes linear, the 3 lower lobes lanceolate or oblong. Stamens 5, free from the corolla; anthers purplish blue or straw‑yellow, united into a ring round the style, the 2 lower ones hairy at the top; stigma slightly 2‑lobed. Ovary inferior, 2‑locular, with numerous ovules. Fruit a berry or dry and indehiscent.

About 30–40 species in tropical and subtropical regions; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, characterized with pungent smell. Leaves opposite, petiolate, serrate. Capitula homogamous, discoid, in terminal cymose form. Involucre campanulate; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, non‑persistent. Receptacle highly conical, without palea. Florets all tubular, corolla regular, apex 5‑lobed; stamens slightly exserted, anther bases slightly acute, apical appendages long; ovary angular, stylar branches cylindric, long. Cypsela ribbed; pappus capillary.

About 15 species native to S America; one species appeared in Guangdong and in Hong Kong after 1990.

Shrubs or trees, erect or rarely scandent. Branches usually terete, often with orbicular or elliptic yellowish white glandular lenticels. Leaves simple, opposite, margin entire or serrate, exstipulate. Inflorescences terminal, in panicles, leaf opposed cymes, clusters, paniculate corymbs, or spike‑like thyrses. Bracts linear or lanceolate, minute, rarely leaf‑like. Flowers small. Calyx cupular or campanulate, truncate, sinuately dentate, or rarely long dentate, teeth equal or clearly 2‑lipped, persistent and slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla‑tube short, throat with a ring of white hairs; limb 2‑lipped and 4‑lobed, upper lip with 1 lobe, lower lip 3‑lobed. Stamens 4, often didynamous, shorter than corolla or sometimes slightly exserted; anthers globose, dorsifixed, thecae parallel or divergent at base. Ovary (2–)4‑locular; ovules 1(–2) per locule, pendulous or laterally attached. Style filiform; stigma 2‑cleft. Drupes globose, obovoid or ellipsoidal, usually with a 4‑locular pyrene. Seeds ellipsoidal, testa thin; endosperm wanting.

About 200 species distributed in the tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; 46 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, usually glabrous. Leaves alternate, distichous, ± asymmetrical, entire or toothed, pinninerved; cystoliths linear, very small. Stipules intrapetiolar, small, entire. Flowers unisexual, in glomerules (plants monoecious or dioecious). Male glomerules in loose cymes or crowded on a small receptacle; female glomerules compact, head-like, subsessile on a fleshy globose or clavate receptacle. Male flowers: perianth deeply 5-lobed; lobes obovate, fleshy; stamens 5; rudimentary pistil globose or obovoid. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 3– 4, obovate-navicular, free or united at the base, ± fleshy; staminodes absent; ovary ovoid; stigma sessile, penicillate. Achene ovoid or ellipsoid, surrounded by flesy perianth.

About 20 species in tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, unarmed, rarely with thorns. Leaves simple, alternate, pinnately-veined, entire or serrate, with small glands in the margin and/or at the base, or on the petioles; stipules small, caducous. Inflorescences umbellate, corymbose, racemose, fasciculate, or flowers solitary. Sepals 5, imbricate, usually caducous. Petals 5, usually white or pink. Stamens 15–many, perigynous, inserted on the mouth of hypanthium. Ovary of a single carpel, superior, with 2 pendulous ovules; style elongated; stigma capitate. Fruit a drupe, usually 1-seeded.

About 280 species mainly distributed in N temperate regions, some species extending to tropical and subtropical regions; about 100 species in China; six (three cultivated) species in Hong Kong.

Perennial erect herbs, rigid. Leaves alternate, basal ones in rosulate form, subsessile, pinnately‑veined. Capitula sessile, homogamous, 1–6 forming axillary aggregates without stalks; involucres consisting of 2 sets of 4 oblong phyllaries, outer series shorter. Receptacle small and naked. Florets 4 per capitulum, all bisexual and fertile, corolla tubular and 5‑lobed, usually with one side more deeply cleft; anther bases shortly sagittate, obtuse; stylar branches hairy, acute. Cypselae linear‑oblong, 10‑ribbed, hairy. Pappus bristles few, 5–15, persistent, unequal in length, slender, usually with several apically folded as sigmoid.

Two species native to tropical America and Africa; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs with cystoliths. Leaves sessile to petiolate, margin entire or dentate. Inflorescence of simple or compound racemes or spikes, axillary or terminal, flowers 1–many on each node, sessile or pedunculate. Bracts and bracteoles linear, much shorter than calyx, margin entire. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes linear, equal. Corolla hypocrateriform; tube slender, not or scarcely enlarged upward, limb 5‑lobed or 2‑lipped; lobes equal or two slightly smaller, imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, inserted in throat of corolla, included in corolla tube or exserted from mouth of corolla; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae equal to subequal, parallel, at the same height, muticous. Staminodes 2 or absent. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style included or exserted; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes equal. Capsule clavate with long solid stalk, retinacula present, 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, flattened, pitted or smooth, glabrous.

About 60 species in the tropics worldwide; six species in China; one cultivar cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Culms usually erect, slender, glabrous. Leaf blades narrowly linear, often inrolled; ligule a narrow membranous rim, margin densely ciliate. Inflorescence terminal, composed of several to many subdigitate racemes in a dense brush-like cluster; racemes tough or fragile, spikelets of a pair similar, usually both pedicellate on unequal pedicels, both fertile; rachis internodes and pedicels linear, hairy along angles. Spikelets lanceolate or lanceolate-oblong; callus obtuse to acuminate, shortly bearded; glumes membranous or papery; lower glume slightly convex, flanks rounded, 2-keeled upward, abaxial side usually hairy, keels ciliate toward apex, apex truncate or bidentate; upper glume boat-shaped, apex mucronate or awned; lower floret reduced to an oblong hyaline lemma or absent; upper floret bisexual; upper lemma usually extremely narrow, even reduced to base of awn, stipe-like, entire or 2-toothed, awned; awn well developed, geniculate; palea usually absent; stamens 1–3.

Three to five species distributed in NE India and Myanmar through SE Asia to the Philippines, Australia, Pacific islands; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Bark grey, smooth. Young branchlets hairy. Leaves opposite, pinnately-veined, petiolate. Flowers axillary, large, usually 1–3 per axil, 4–5-merous. Bracts 2. Hypanthium campanulate or urceolate. Calyx-lobes unequal. Petals white. Stamens many, distinct, in many whorls; anthers ellipsoidal, basifixed, cells parallel, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary inferior, connate to hypanthium, 4–5-locular or more; ovules many per locule; style linear; stigma expanded. Berry globose to pyriform, many-seeded, apex with persistent calyx-lobes; placenta well developed, fleshy. Seed coat hard; embryo curved; hypocotyl long; cotyledons short.

About 150 species distributed in tropical America; two species introduced to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, generally erect, rarely climbing. Leaves opposite, rarely in whorls of 3 or 4. Stipules intrapetiolar, usually united into a sheath, entire or 2‑lobed, deciduous or persistent. Flowers small, bisexual, rarely polygamo‑dioecious, in corymbiform or paniculate cymes, terminal or very rarely axillary. Calyx‑tube very short; limb with (4–)5(–6) lobes or teeth, deciduous or persistent. Corolla funnel‑shaped, tubular or ± bell‑shaped; tube straight, short or elongate, glabrous or hairy on throat; lobes usually (4–)5(–6), spreading, valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the apex of corolla‑tube; anthers linear to oblong, dorsifixed, included or shortly exserted. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 erect ovule in each locule; style with 2 short stigmatic lobes. Fruit a drupe, with 2 kernels, flat on the inner face and usually furrowed on the back.

About 1400 species spreading over the tropical and subtropical regions; 18 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Stipules deciduous; stipels absent. Leaves odd-pinnate; pedicels articulate; leaflets alternate. Racemes or panicles axillary or terminal. Bracts and bracteoles small, caducous. Corolla yellow, rarely whitish mixed with violet, usually showy. Calyx campanulate, slightly curved, with short teeth, the upper 2 teeth more or less connate. Petals long-clawed; vexillum orbicular or broadly ovate; wings obliquely obovate or oblong; keel as long as or shorter than wings. Stamens monadelphous or diadelphous (5+5) or (9+1); anthers dorsifixed. Ovary sessile or stipitate, generally 2-ovuled; styles filiform, incurved, not barbate; stigma small, terminal. Pods orbicular or ovate, rarely oval-oblong, more or less oblique or falcate, compressed, indehiscent, 1–2-seeded, surrounded by a more or less thickened horizontal wing.

About 50 species distributed in tropical regions; one species cultivated in China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs. Leaves entire, or variously lobed to pinnatisect. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and bisexual, at terminal arranged as corymbs, panicles or racemose panicles. Involucres ovoid; phyllaries green and thick, 4–5‑seriate, gradually longer inward, imbricate. Receptacle plain and naked. Ligulate florets 9–25 per head, corolla yellow, rarely white, ligule truncate and 5‑toothed at apex, white pubescent near the summit of lower tube; anther bases sagittate; stylar branches slender. Cypselae obovate, elliptic or oblong, colour black, blackish brown to reddish brown, dorsiventrally compressed, surface glabrous, 1‑ or 3‑striate on each side, margin thinly or thickly winged, apex with stout or filiform beak. Pappus in 2 series, white.

About 11 species distributed in E & SE Asia; mostly in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, lepidote or stellate-tomentose. Leaves simple, leathery, oblique, entire or serrate, lobed or not, pinnately veined or 3 –7-veined, often cordate, rarely peltate at base. Flowers bisexual, solitary or several in cymes, axillary; calyx tubular, 5-lobed or -parted; petals 5, deciduous; stamens 15, in 5 groups of each 3, united into a column at base, with 5 long barren filaments and 15 shorter fertile ones, each bearing a linear 2-celled anther; cells parallel, connectives apiculate; ovary 5-locular, with several ovules in each locule; style entire, stigma clavate, 5-grooved. Capsule woody or leathery, terete or angular, loculicidally 5-valved. Seeds winged at upper end; endosperm thin or absent.

About 25 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia; nine species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Twining vines; roots sometimes bearing tubers. Stipules dorsifixed or basifixed; stipels present. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets large, ovate or rhomboid, entire or sinuately lobed. Racemes or panicles axillary, sometimes several racemes clustered at branch apex. Bracts caducous; bracteoles present. Flowers often aggregated on swollen nodes. Calyx campanulate, upper 2 teeth ± connate. Corolla blue or purple; petals clawed; vexillum suborbicular or obovate, with appendage and 2 auricles at base; wings narrow, auriculate and adherent to keel; keel equal to wings, apex slightly curved. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary sessile or subsessile, many-ovuled. Pods linear, compressed or terete, 2-valved, continuous within or septate between seeds. Seeds, suborbicular or oblong, compressed.

About 35 species distributed from India to Malaysia; eight species in China; two species and two varieties in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, petiolate, pinnately-veined. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious), apetalous; disk absent. Male flowers in axillary racemes or spikes; calyx 4–6-parted, lobes imbricate; stamens 2 – 4; pistillode absent. Female flowers solitary, axillary; calyx 5-parted, lobes narrow, imbricate; ovary ovoid or oblong-ovoid, 2-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles dilated, petaloid, 2 – 5-branched at the upper portion, papillose. Drupes indehiscent, long-pedicellate, 1-locular, 1-seeded; mesocarp fleshy; pyrene stone-hard; testa membranous or crustaceous; endosperm fleshy.

About four species distributed from India, Sri Lanka to Ryukyu Islands; two species (one cultivated) in China (Guangdong, Taiwan, Hong Kong).

Subshrubs. Stipules free; stipels present. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, sometimes 1-foliolate; leaflets entire. Racemes terminal. Bracts scarious, caducous; bracteoles absent. Flowers small, often paired on rhachis. Calyx campanulate, deeply lobed, upper 2 lobes connate high up. Corolla quite exserted; petals subequal; vexillum suborbicular, base attenuate; wings obliquely oblong, adherent to keel; keel obtuse, slightly incurved with a narrow lateral appendage on each side. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary sessile, with several ovules; styles filiform, incurved, stigma capitate. Pods oblong, turgid, transversely venose, 2-valved, continuous within. Seeds 6 –10, small, subreniform.

Only one species, distributed in tropical Africa, Asia to E Australia; also in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials, rhizomatous or stoloniferous. Culms terete to trigonous. Leaves basal, 3-ranked, rarely without blade; ligule 0. Involucral bract several, leaf-like. Inflorescence terminal, usually umbel-like, with primary, secondary and sometimes tertiary branches terminating in 1 or more spikes or finger-like cluster of spikelets, more rarely capitate. Spikelets linear to oblong or elliptic, laterally flattened; axis persistent. Glumes few to many, 2-ranked, persistent, sides membranous to leathery, veins 0– several, keel acute obtuse. Flowers bisexual. Perianth biconvex, with one margin facing the spikelets axis.

About 70 species in temperate, subtropical and tropical regions of the world, with high concentration of species in Africa; 11 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, entire, rarely serrate, blades usually with an impressed gland on each side at the base; stipules small, deciduous or rarely persistent. Inflorescence racemose, axillary and lateral, solitary or fasciculate. Flowers usually 5-merous and bisexual, sometimes polygamo-dioecious. Hypanthium obconical or cyathiform, with a persistent annular base, usually partly or entirely caducous after anthesis. Sepals 5 – 10( – 2), small. Petals as many as and usually resembling the sepals, very rarely absent. Stamens 10–30 or more, 1–many-seriate; anthers didymous. Ovary of a single carpel, superior, with 2 pendulous ovules, enclosed in the hypanthium; style terminal, glabrous or hairy; stigma capitate. Fruit a drupe, dry, leathery, usually as broad as or broader than long, with a smooth stone, containing a single seed.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Africa, S and SE Asia, NE Australia, New Guinea, Pacific Islands; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, usually with thorny branches. Leaves alternate or fasciculate, simple, crenate, entire or serrulate, shortly petiolate or sessile; stipules minute, caducous, but on long shoots persistent longer and sometimes leafy. Inflorescence a terminal corymb-shaped thyrse. Hypanthium obconical. Sepals 5, persistent and incurved after anthesis. Petals 5, suborbicular, spreading, base shortly clawed. Stamens ca. 20; filaments subulate. Carpels (2–)5, apically free, the basal half adnate to the hypanthium; ovary 5-locular, semi-inferior; ovules 2 per locule, anatropous, collateral; styles (2–4– )5, free, stigmas dilated. Fruit a pome, red or orange, without sclereids, with a persistent calyx at the apex; pyrenes 5. Seeds with testa.

Ten species in SE Europe to E Asia; seven species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves spirally arranged, leathery, serrate. Flowers axillary, solitary, pedicellate or subsessile; bracteoles 2 or rarely more, caducous or persistent; sepals 5, imbricate, persistent or caducous, unequal; petals 5 or rarely more, slightly connate at base; stamens many, more or less connate at the base, and adnate to the base of petals; anthers dorsally inserted on basal incision; ovary superior, 3 – 6-locular with 2–5 ovules per locule; styles 3– 6, free or connate at base. Fruit a drupe, indehiscent, or a capsule, loculicidally dehiscing from the base, central axis robust, persistent. Seeds 2– 5 per locule, ellipsoid, compressed, wingless.

About 25 species distributed in E India, Malay Peninsula to S China; 13 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen woody vines. Leaves opposite, palmately compound, 2–3‑foliolate, terminal leaflet often modified into a 3‑branched tendril. Inflorescences terminal, thyrsoid, racomose or paniculate. Calyx campanulate or ± tubular, truncate or 5‑dentate. Corolla funnelform, tube slightly curved, lobes 5, valvate, reflexed at anthesis. Fertile stamens 4, didynamous, exserted. Disk annular or cupular. Ovary superior, linear, 2‑locular, ovules many in (1 – )2( – 3)‑series on each placentation; style 1, stigma 2‑lobed. Capsules long linear, septicidally dehiscing, valve flat, leathery, smooth and striate. Seeds elliptic, winged, imbricate.

Three to four species distributed in tropical S America; one species introduced to S China; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Deciduous rarely half-evergreen trees, rarely shrubs, sometimes thorny. Leaves alternate, simple, serrate or entire, rarely lobed, petiolate; stipules small, caducous. Inflorescences an umbel-like raceme, few-flowered; bracts subulate, deciduous. Flowers with or before the leaves. Hypanthium urceolate, adnate to the ovary. Sepals 5, reflexed or spreading, persistent or deciduous. Petals 5, white or rarely pinkish, shortly clawed. Stamens 15 – 30, shorter than the petals, anthers usually red. Ovary inferior, 2 – 5-locular, separate or connate at base, ovules 2 (rarely many) in each locule; styles 2 – 5, free but closely constricted basally by the staminal disk, stigmas truncate to 2-patite. Fruit a pome, pyriform to globose, brown to yellow, sometimes lenticellate; mesocarp fleshy and with copious stones or grit-cells. Seeds ovoid, black or nearly black.

About 25 species in Europe, N Africa and E Asia; seven species in China; two species (one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or Tree, rarely shrubs. Branchlets with terminal bud covered with many imbricate scales. Leaves short-petiolate, penninerved, lobed or entire. Male flowers in slender, pendulous catkins; perianth 4 –7-lobed; stamens 4–12, usually 6. Female flowers 1 per cupule, solitary or in 2- to many-flowered spikes; ovary 3- or rarely 4 – 5-locular; style elongated, dilated above and stigmatose on the inner surface. Fruit a nut, subglobose to oblong or cylindric, surrounded at base or sometimes entirely enclosed by a cup-like cupule or involucre covered with imbricate scales.

About 100 species in the temperate regions of the northern hemisphnere and into the tropics at high altitudes; 33 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Woody vines or scandent shrubs. Leaves opposite or subopposite, entire. Inflorescence spicate. Flowers large, bisexual, white or red. Calyx-tube long and slender, prolonged well beyond ovary, lobes 5, small, deciduous. Petals 5, imbricate, enlarged after anthesis. Stamens 10, in 2 whorls. Disk present or absent. Ovary 1-locular, ovules 2–4; style filiform. Fruit drupaceous or capsular, with 5 ribs or narrow wings. Seed 1.

About 17 species distributed in S Asia and tropical Africa; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs, terrestrial or partly aquatic. Stems erect, ascending, or prostrate. Leaves basal and alternate on stems, simple or ternately compound, entire, serrate, or trilobed; petioles elongate, base broadened into sheath. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, solitary or in cymes. Sepals 5, green, caducous. Petals 5, sometimes 6 –10, yellow, clawed and with a nectary at base. Stamens numerous, centripetal. Carpels 5 to many, free, 1-ovuled, ripening into small hard achenes clustered on the receptacle to form a little head. Achenes ovoid or bilaterally compressed, dorsal suture ribbed or winged.

About 550 species widespread in N temperate regions; 125 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs, usually simply hairy, sometimes with fleshy roots. Leaves simple, lyrate, pinnately lobate or pinnatipartite. Racemes corymbiform, ebracteate. Flowers large. Sepals 4, oblong or linear, base of lateral pair saccate. Petals 4, yellow, white, pink or purple, usually with dark veins, obovate or suborbicular, long clawed. Stamens 6, tetradynamous, filaments not dilated at base; nectar 4-glanded. Ovary 2–22-ovuled; stigma capitate, entire or slightly 2-lobed. Siliques indehiscent, thick, more or less constricted between seeds. Seeds uniseriate, brown, plump, ovoid or globose, cotyledons conduplicate.

Three species distributed in Mediterranean regions; two species introduced to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs with latex. Leaves whorled, rarely opposite, with glands in axils. Cymes pedunculate, terminal or axillary. Calyx deeply divided, without glands. Corolla salverform or campanulate, white, yellow, green, or pink, rarely with a red tube; tube cylindric, ± inflated at or above middle, usually pubescent inside, lobes overlapping to left. Stamens inserted in the inflated part of corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers ovate, free from pistil head, base rounded; disk ring‑like or cup‑shaped, entire or lobed at apex. Ovary of 2 carpels connate at base or of 2 free carpels, in each case united into a common style with a collared style head; pistil head drum ‑shaped, with a pendulous ring, apex shortly 2‑cleft. Drupes 2, distinct or connate. Seed 1, without coma.

About 60 species distributed pantropically; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Tree-like plants. Leaves large, in 2 ranks toward top of stem; petioles long, with many air-canals, ± sheathing at base. Inflorescences axillary, much shorter than the leaves, with several stiff and boat-shaped, distichously and racemosely arranged bracts, each enveloping a compact, few-flowered helicoid cyme; sepals 3, free, subequal; petals 3, the lateral 2 like the sepals, the middle one slightly shorter and narrower; stamens 6, free; ovary 3-locular, each with many ovules on the axile placentas; style slender, stigma clavate. Fruit a 3-celled woody capsule, with many seeds.

A monotypic genus native to Madagascar.

Trees. Leaves simple, entire, leathery. Panicles terminal, corymbose. Flowers white; calyx campanulate, or funnel-shaped, irregularly 3 – 5-fid; petals 5, clawed; staminal column elongated, adnate to gynophore, forming an androgynophore, shortly 5-lobed at top, each lobe bearing 3 sessile anthers outside and all irregularly crowded in a globose head, anther cells divaricate; ovary enclosed in staminal column, 5-grooved, 5-locular, 2-ovuled in each locule; stigma sessile, 5-lobed. Capsules woody, loculicidally 5-valved. Seeds superposed, oblong, compressed, winged at lower end; endosperm fleshy.

About 18 species distributed mainly in China and Himalaya regions; 14 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees, bud scales present. Leaves alternate, serrate or serrulate; stipules absent. Inflorescences axillary or at nodes of previous year branchlets, racemose or paniculate, 3 –10-flowered; pedicels articulated; calyx tube obconical and completely adnate to ovary, 5 –10-ribbed, 5-toothed; corolla campanulate, lobes 5, imbricate, shortly connate at the base; stamens 10, 5 long and 5 short; filaments flattened, basally connate and adnate to corolla; anthers ovate to oblong; ovary inferior, 3– 4-locular; ovules 4 per locule; style elongate, slender; stigma obscurely 4–5-lobed. Fruit woody, indehiscent, broadly cylindrical, apex with persistent style forming a short rostrum; exocarp thin, hard, 5 –10-ribbed; mesocarp indistinct from endocarp with many radiate lacunae. Seeds 1–3, narrowly cylindrical; seed-coat almost leathery; embryo fleshy.

Five species distributed in China, Myanmar, Vietnam; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennials. Rhizomes long-creeping, branching. Culms 1 or few, trigonous, smooth. Leaves many, crowded along and often obscuring lower part of culm, leathery; ligule absent. Involucral bract leaf-like. Inflorescence capitate. Spikes 3–8, often exceeded by upper leaves and involucral bracts. Spikelets falling off entire when mature, comprising 1 fertile glumes above and 1–2 sterile glumes below (excluding basal prophyll); rachilla corky-thickened. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 3. Stigmas 3. Achenes oblong to ellipsoidal, trigonous.

One species in pantropical regions; also distributed in China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, often with spinescent branches. Leaves alternate or subopposite, pinnately-veined; stipules small, caducous. Flowers small, bisexual, polygamous or unisexual (plants dioecious), in axillary clusters, umbels or racemes. Calyx 4–5-lobed; lobes keeled adaxially. Petals 4–5, adnate to the top of the cup-shaped or hemispherical calyx-tube, or sometimes wanting. Stamens 4–5, opposite to the petals; filaments very short. Disk adnate to calyx-tube. Ovary free, usually shorter than the calyx-tube, 2–4-locular; style 2–4-cleft. Fruit a berry-like drupe, with 2–4 one-seeded kernels.

About 300 species mainly in the temperate regions of the N hemisphere; 57 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Large lianas, stems thick, procumbent or climbing. Leaves distichous; petioles articulate, ± sheathed; leaf blades entire, pinnatifid or pinnatisect; lateral veins sub-parallel. Inflorescence terminal, solitary or sometimes 2–3 cymosely arranged. Spathe sessile, deciduous, convolute or concave; spadix cylindrical, shorter than spathe. Flowers bisexual or sometimes with a few male at the base of spadix, without scales or perianth; stamens 4, filaments flat; anther terminal, 2-celled; ovary 1-locular or incompletely 2-locular, 2– many-ovuled; stigma sessile on the truncate top of ovary. Berries red when mature, 2– many-seeded.

About 100 species distributed in tropical Africa, Asia and Australia; nine species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs, unarmed. Leaves simple, alternate, shortly petiolate, leathery, serrate or entire, pinnately-veined; stipules deciduous. Inflorescences racemose, paniculate or corymbose; bracts subulate or lanceolate, deciduous. Hypanthium campanulate to tubular. Sepals 5, subulate or triangular, erect or reflexed, falling off together with the upper rim of the hypanthium after anthesis. Petals 5, white to pinkish, oblong or obovate, clawed at base. Stamens 15–20, inserted on the mouth of the hypanthium. Carpels 2, completely connate with each other and adnate to the hypanthium. Ovary inferior, 2( –3)-locular; styles 2( –3), elongate, connate at base; stigmas truncate; ovules basal, erect, 2 per locule. Fruit a pome, subglobose, mostly 1-seeded, crowned by an annular remains of the calyx-teeth, often black or purplish-black. Seeds globose or turgid, testa thin but firm, endosperm absent.

About 15 species in SE and E Asia; seven species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Small to moderate shrubs, dioecious or polygamous. Stems clustered, slender, green, with distinct rings of leaf scar, covered with fibrous interwoven leaf sheaths on upper part. Leaves palmate, induplicate, split to 3/4 or more depth into several-ribbed segments, segment 2– many, minutely teethed on margins; sheaths with black or greyish black, interwoven fibres; petioles long and slender, elliptic in cross-section, unarmed; hastula small, triangular. Inflorescences axillary, branched 2–3 orders; peduncles short; prophyll closely or loosely tubular, splitting along the abaxial midline; flowers solitary or spirally arranged; male flowers: calyx cup-shaped, 3-lobed, corolla 3-lobed, stamens 6, in 2 whorls; female flower: sepals and petals similar to male flower, carpels 3, free, staminodes 6. Fruits usually developed from 1 carpel, globose or ovoid, sometimes borne on short stalks; epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy, slightly fibrous, endocarp thin, crustaceous, fragile. Seed 1, globose or subglobose, endosperm homogeneous.

About 11 species in China, Laos, Sumatra, Thailand and Vietnam; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or perennial erect herbs with cystoliths, laxly branched, sometimes subscandent. Leaves petiolate or sessile, margin entire or undulate. Flowers 1 – few in fascicles or in lax axillary or terminal cymes combined into paniculate thyrses. Bracts and bracteoles small, linear‑lanceolate. Calyx 5‑lobed, lobes narrow, apex acuminate. Corolla tubular; tube elongated, slender; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip linear, erect, lower lip broadly 3‑lobed, lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, inserted on the throat of corolla; anther 2‑thecous, thecae superposed or parallel, muticous. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform, stigma entire or obscurely 2‑lobed. Capsule clavate with a long solid stalk at base, retinacula present, 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, compressed.

About 15 species in the tropical regions of the Old World; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Shrubs, rarely trees, evergreen or deciduous. Leaves alternate, rarely pseudoverticillate, petiolate, margin entire, very rarely ciliateserrulate. Flowers usually in terminal umbel-like racemes, rarely solitary and axillary. Calyx 5-lobed, rarely 6–10-lobed; lobes often very small, irregular, persistent. Corolla campanulate, funnel-shaped, tubular or hypocrateriform, regular or slightly zygomorphic, usually 5-lobed; lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 5–10, usually 10, rarely more; filaments slender, glabrous or hairy; anthers dorsifixed, without appendage, opening by apical or oblique pores. Disc usually thick, 5–10(–14)-lobed. Ovary usually 5(–20)-locular, with many ovules in each locule; style slender; stigma capitate-discoid, crenate to lobed. Capsule oblong, to ovoid, rarely falcate, septicidal. Seeds minute, vary numerous.

About 960 species, mainly found in E and SE Asia, also some species in America and Europe and one species in Australia; 542 species in China; six indigenous species in Hong Kong. A number of species, varieties and cultivars were widely cultivated in Hong Kong and two commonly-cultivated species are included here.

The ecology, genetic variation and structure of local native species have been studied recently (Ng & Corlett, Canadian Journal of Botany 78: 221–229. 2000; Molecular Ecology 9: 959–969. 2000; Plant Ecology 164: 225–233. 2002).

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, leathery, pinnately veined, petiolate; stipules absent. Inflorescence capitate, axillary, pedunculate, 5 – 8-flowered; involucral bracts 5-many, imbricate. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic. Floral cup very short, enclosing base of ovary. Sepals absent or rudimentary. Petals 2–6, red, spathulate or oblanceolate, well developed only on abaxial side of flower, making the head as whole like a rayed flower. Stamens 4–11; filaments linear; anther 2-celled, each dehiscent into 2 valves. Ovary semi-inferior, 2-locular or imperfectly so; ovules 12–18 per locule; styles 2, long, very slender, nearly equal to stamens. Capsules loculicidally dehiscing above middle by 4 valves; pericarp thin. Seeds flattened, mostly sterile and wingless, fertile seeds laterally narrowly winged.

About ten species distributed in China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees. Leaves opposite, tripliveined, petiolate. Inflorescence a cyme, 1 – 3-flowered, axillary. Hypanthium ovoid to subglobose. Calyx-lobes 4 – 5, leathery, persistent. Petals 4 – 5, larger than calyx-lobes. Stamens many, distinct, in many whorls, usually shorter than petals; anthers dorsifixed to nearly basifixed, versatile, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary inferior, adnate to hypanthium, 3(–4)-locular, sometimes with false transverse septa; ovules arranged in 2 lines per locule. Style linear; stigma capitate or peltate. Berry urceolate or globose. Seeds many, flat, reniform; testa hard; embryo curved or spiral.

About 18 species distributed in tropical Asia, Australia, SW Pacific Islands; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Deciduous shrubs or trees, polygamous or dioecious. Leaves imparipinnately compound, rarely trifoliolate or simple; leaf rachis sometimes winged; leaflets petiolate or sessile, serrate or entire. Inflorescence paniculate or thyrsoid, axillary or terminal. Flowers functionally unisexual or bisexual, usually 5-merous. Calyx (4–)5(–6)-lobed; lobes imbricate. Petals (4–)5(–6), imbricate. Stamens (4–)5(–6), or rarely 10, distinct, inserted at the base of disk. Disk annular. Ovary 1-locular, styles 3, often united basally; stigma capitate. Drupe globose, dry, slightly compressed, smooth or hairy, stone leathery or bony. Seed 1, cotyledons flat.

About 200 species distributed in subtropical and warm temperate regions of the world; 14 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Shrublets or herbs, climbing, prostrate, or rarely erect. Stipules ovate or lanceolate. Leaves pinnately, rarely subdigitately 3-foliolate, exstipellate or minutely stipellate; leaflets with scattered, resinous dots abaxially. Racemes axillary, rarely flowers solitary. Flowers yellow, vexillum often lined, rarely purple. Bracts caducous; bracteoles absent. Calyx 5-lobed, upper 2 lobes more or less connate. Corolla inclusive or exserted; vexillum obovate or orbicular, spreading or reflexed, auriculate at base; wings narrow; keel incurved at apex. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary subsessile, (1–)2-ovuled; styles incurved adaxially, filiform or thickened; stigma small, terminal. Pods compressed, obliquely orbicular, oblong or falcate, dehiscing by 2 valves, continuous within or rarely septate. Seeds (1–)2, compressed globose or subreniform, hilum lateral, funicle central or scarcely oblique, strophiole thick, small or absent.

About 200 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mainly in Asia; 13 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials. Culms central. Leaves basal and/or cauline; blade linear to lanceolate; sheaths closed; ligule absent. Inflorescence of terminal and lateral umbel-like partial inflorescence, or paniculate or capitate. Spikelets lanceolate, ovate to elliptic, flattened to terete. Glumes 5–9 (rarely more), distichous or spirally imbricate, membranous to papery, 1-veined, the basal 2–3 glumes empty and small, the remainder glumes gradually larger with a single flower, the uppermost glume often empty. Flowers either all bisexual, the upper ones not maturing achene, or lower 1– few bisexual and upper ones staminate, or unisexual with the lowest pistillate and upper ones staminate. Perianth segments 0–6, rarely more, bristle-like, upwardly or retrorsely scabrous, rarely smooth. Stamens (1–)2–3. Stigmas 2 or style undivided. Achenes biconvex, smooth, cancellate, rugose or sometimes spinose; style base persistent, variously shaped.

About 350 species distributed worldwide; seven species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs, densely villose when young. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate; leaf blade oblong or elliptic, surfaces sericeous to hirsute or woolly, glabrescent. Inflorescences axillary, many‑flowered cymes; bracts 2, opposite. Calyx actinomorphic, 5‑sect from base. Corolla white to reddish or purple, zygomorphic; tube campanulate tubular, not swollen, shorter than limb; limb indistinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, abaxial lip 3‑lobed. Stamens 4, adnate to corolla tube near base, included; anthers basifixed, free, thecae parallel, confluent at apex, dehiscing longitudinally; staminode absent or 1, adnate to adaxial side of corolla tube. Disk ring‑like or absent. Ovary ovoid, 1‑loculed; placentas 2, parietal, projecting inward, 2‑cleft. Stigma 1, terminal, depressed globose, undivided. Berry ovoid to spherical, indehiscent. Seeds spherical, glabrous, unappendaged.

About 13 species in SE Asia and Pacific islands; four to five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect or creeping herbs. Leaves opposite, sessile or petiolate. Stipules united at the base into a sheath, fringed with filiform or subulate lobes. Flowers small, bisexual or sometimes polygamo‑dioecious, in terminal head‑like clusters. Calyx‑tube turbinate or globular; limb 4–8‑lobed; lobes lanceolate or subulate, persistent. Corolla funnel‑shaped; throat glabrous; limb 3–6‑lobed; lobes ovate or lanceolate, valvate in the bud. Stamens 3–6, attached to the throat; filaments slender; anthers dorsifixed, linear or oblong, exserted. Ovary 3–4‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style with 3–4 linear or spathulate lobes. Fruit a capsule.

About 15 species in C & S America; one species naturalized in S China and in Hong Kong.

Tall herbs or subshrubs. Leaves alternate, peltate, palmately divided; stipules connate, deciduous. Flowers monoecious, without petals, in terminal raceme-like panicles; the upper ones female, the lower male. Male flowers: calyx 3 – 5-partite, lobes valvate in bud; stamens numerous, up to 100, anthers crowded on branched filaments; anther 2-celled, globular, distinct; rudimentary pistil absent. Female flowers: calyx-lobes 5, valvate in bud, caducous; staminodes none; ovary globose, 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 3, deeply 2-cleft and plumose. Capsules mostly echinate, dividing into 3 bivalved cocci.

A monotypic genus native to NE Africa, now widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.

Epiphytic herbs with monopodial growth. Roots long, strong and branched. Stems slender. Leaves distichous, oblong, erose at the apex. Peduncles as long as the leaves, with basal and median sterile bracts. Flowers rather small, in an axillary panicle; sepals free, spreading, the odd one concave; petals slightly smaller than the sepals; lip 3-lobed, calcarate, attached to the base of the column; spur enlarged and rotundate at the apex, with a horizontal flap in the back wall near the entrance and a keel on the front wall, lateral lobes erect and truncate, midlobe fleshy, ovate; column short and broad, produced into 2 arms at the apex; clinandrium elongate; rostellum produced below the tip of the anther; anther terminal, ovate, the apex beaked; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, on a short stipe attached to a slender caudicle enlarged, curved, and grooved at the pollinian end and with a small viscidium at the rostellum end; stigma suborbicular; ovary cylindrical. Capsules fusiform.

About 40 species distributed in SE Asia, Pacific islands and Australia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual to perennial herbs, glabrous or simply hairy. Stems erect or prostrate. Leaves simple, entire to pinnatipartite. Racemes terminal, elongated with fruiting. Sepals 4, oblong or ovate. Petals 4, yellow, obovate or spathulate, shortly clawed or not. Stamens 6, tetradynamous, rarely 4 and equal in length; nectar glands confluent. Siliques or silicles, dehiscent, linear to oblong or globose, terete or slightly latiseptate. Seeds biseriate or rarely uniseriate; cotyledons accumbent.

About 75 species distributed worldwide; nine species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Erect, scrambling, or climbing shrubs, mostly prickly or bristly. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate, rarely simple; stipules leafy, partly adnate to the petioles. Flowers showy, solitary or in small corymbs or panicles, terminal on the branchlets, usually 5-mrerous. Hypanthium usually globular to urceolate, enclosing the ovary, contracted towards the top. Sepals 5, often unequal, sometimes lobed, caducous or persistent. Petals 5, white, yellow or pink to red, imbricate. Stamens numerous, several-seriate, inserted on the disk at the edge of the hypanthium. Carpels numerous, rarely few, free, enclosed in the hypanthium, with 1 suspended ovule in each; styles terminal or subterminal, free or united. Fruit a hip, formed from fleshy hypanthium, enclosing several or many bony achenes.

About 200 species mostly distributed in N temperate regions; 95 species in China; eight species (four cultivated) and one variety in Hong Kong.

Annual, rarely perennial herbs, glabrous or subglabrous. Leaves decussate or verticillate, rarely alternate, sessile or subsessile. Flowers small, 3 – 6-merous, actinomorphic, solitary in axil of leaves, or in spikes or racemes, axillary or terminal; bracteoles 2. Calyx-tube cylindric, subglobular or pot-like, scarious, rarely leathery, 3 – 6-toothed, without appendages between lobes, or with setiform appendages. Petals 3 – 6, minute or absent, persistent or caducous. Stamens 1 – 6. Ovary 2 – 5-locular; styles short or long; stigma disciform. Capsule not wholly involved by calyx-tube, septicidal, 2–5-valved; fruit wall transversely striate (seen under magnifier). Seeds minute.

About 50 species mainly distributed in tropical regions of Asia and Africa, few in Australia, Europe and America; six species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms erect or geniculate at base. Leaf blades linear, flat, glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs; ligule short, truncate. Inflorescence of single axillary racemes; racemes cylindrical, fragile, transversely articulate. Pedicellate spikelet tightly erect, as long as or shorter than sessile spikelet, herbaceous; pedicel broad, partly or wholly adnate to adjacent rachis internode; sessile spikelets sunken within a cavity formed by rachis and adjacent pedicel, 1–2-floret; lower glume ovate-oblong, leathery, shallowly convex, marginally 2-keeled, narrowly winged along keel, apex obtuse or acute; upper glume boat-shaped; lower floret staminate, palea present; upper floret with entire awnless lemma; stamens 3; lodicules 2, cuneate; styles 2, free; stigmas plumose. Caryopsis ovate or oblong.

Five species distributed in Old World tropics; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Vines or shrubs, rarely small trees. Leaves odd-pinnate, rarely 1-foliolate; leaflets subopposite or alternate. Inflorescences an axillary or pseudoterminal panicle; bracts ovate-lanceolate; bracteoles lanceolate. Flowers 5-merous, small. Sepals imbricate, persistent, enlarged after anthesis, closely clasping the base of follicle. Petals longer than sepals, glabrous. Stamens 10, those opposite sepals longer than those opposite petals; filaments connate at base, glabrous. Carpels 5, free, usually only 1 developed, hairy or glabrous; style slender; stigma capitate, inconspicuously 2-lobed. Follicle solitary, sessile, glabrous, smooth or longitudinally fine sulcate, dehiscing along ventral suture, rarely dehiscing irregularly at base. Seed 1, flattened; testa glossy, glabrous, with a cupular, fleshy aril adnate at base; endosperm absent.

About 90 species distributed in tropical regions of the world; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Large trees, monoecious. Stems solitary, robust, generally grey-white or grey-brown, rings of leaf scars conspicuous when young. Leaves pinnate, reduplicate; pinnae many, elongate lanceolate; sheaths closed, forming a prominent crownshaft; petioles short, channeled adaxially, rounded abaxially. Inflorescences borne under crwonshafts, branched 3–4 orders; peduncles short; prophylls tubular, 2-keeled laterally, leathery; peduncular bracts long, splitting longitudinally; rachillae straight or zigzagged; rachilla bracts small. Flowers usually in triads of 1 central female and 2 lateral males, paired or solitary male flowers distally; male flowers: sepals 3, triangular, short, petals 3, much longer than sepals, stamens 6–12, pistillodes small, subglobose; female flowers: ovoid, sepals 3, petals 3, connate at lower part, staminodes 6, connate in 6-lobed cupule, adnate to petal-base; ovary subglobose, 1-locular; stigmas 3, recurved. Fruits obovoid, oblong-ellipsoidal or subglobose, epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy and slightly fibrous, endocarp thin, fragile. Seed 1, ellipsoidal, endosperm homogeneous.

Ten species in Caribbean region; one species commonly cultivated in S China and Hong Kong.

Perennial, or rarely annual herbs, with quadrangular stems and branches, scabrous, hispid or with prickles. Leaves in whorls of 4 or 6, of which 2 are real leaves and the remainder are stipules. Flowers small, in axillary or terminal cymes. Pedicels articulate at apex. Calyx‑tube ovoid or subglobular; limb truncate or with minute teeth. Corolla rotate, shortly bell‑shaped or funnel‑shaped, usually 5‑lobed; lobes valvate in bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the tube; filaments very short. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 but deeply 2‑lobed style or 2 separate styles; ovule 1 in each locule. Fruit fleshy, globular didymous or through abortion, only 1 carpel developed.

About 70 species distributed in Europe, Asia, S Africa and America; 36 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect, scrambling or creeping shrubs or subshrubs, usually prickly. Leaves simple, 3 – 5-foliolate, or imparipinnate; stipules free or adnate to the base of petioles, rarely absent. Inflorescences terminal or axillary panicles or racemes, rarely strongly reduced and flowers solitary. Flowers usually 5-merous, mostly bisexual, rarely unisexual and the plant dioecious. Hypanthium campanulate or urceolate. Epicalyx absent. Sepals (4– )5(–6–8), imbricate, persistent. Petals mostly 5, white or pink, orbicular, mostly unguiculate. Stamens numerous, indefinite, mostly 2-seriate, inserted on mouth of hypanthium, filaments filiform, anthers didymous. Disk absent. Carpels numerous, with a single ovule in each, inserted on a receptacle; styles (sub)terminal, filiform, stigmas capitate or bifid. Aggregate fruit berry-like, formed by the union of the succulent carpels, round the conical or shortly oblong, dry receptacle. Seeds pendulous, testa membranous, cotyledons plano-convex.

About 700 species distributed worldwide, especially abundant in the N hemisphere; 208 species in China; eight species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, sometimes with long and thin tuberous roots. Leaves sessile to petiolate, margin entire to sinuate or dentate. Inflorescences of reduced or expanded dichasia in leaf axils, sometimes forming dichasial spikes, thyrses or panicles, rarely reduced to solitary flower; flowers sessile or pedunculate. Bracts opposite, usually narrow, green, margin entire; bracteoles 2, minute or absent. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed, lobes equal or subequal, linear‑lanceolate. Corolla infundibular, tube inflated above from a narrow basal cylindric portion, limbs 5‑lobed, lobes contorted in bud, ovate to rounded. Stamens 4, didynamous, included, filaments sometimes united in pairs at base, anther 2‑thecous, thecae equal, parallel to subsagittate, muticous at base. Staminodes 1 or absent. Ovary with 3–10 ovules per locule; style included or slightly exserted; stigma subulate, 2‑lobed, lobes equal or unequal. Capsule substipitate or stipitate, retinacula hooked, 4–20‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, pubescent with hygroscopic trichomes.

About 250 species in tropical regions of the world; one species widely cultivated and naturalized in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely shrubby. Stems erect, usually sulcate. Leaves basal and cauline; cauline leaves alternate; ocrea scarious, usually caducous. Flowers bisexual, rarey unisexual and plant dioecious, in whorl-like clusters, forming terminal simple or paniculate racemes. Perianth-segments 6, the inner 3 enlarged after flowering, and closing over the fruit. Stamens 6, in 2 whorls. Ovary 1-locular; styles 3, very short, with fringed stigmas. Achenes 3-angled, usually enclosed by the persistent inner perianth-segments.

About 200 species widely distributed over most parts of the world, but mainly in temperate regions; 27 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Decumbent to erect herbs. Leaves petiolate, margin entire. Spikes axillary or terminal, secund or not. Bracts 2‑ranked, or 4‑ranked, just 2 ranks fertile. Bracts (fertile or sterile) unimorphic or dimorphic, margin usually scarious; bracteoles similar to bracts or narrower. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑lanceolate, equal or unequal. Corolla small, basal tube cylindric, limb bilabiate, upper lip erect, entire to emarginate, lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed, lobes imbricate in bud. Stamens 2, inserted in throat of corolla; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae subequal in size, subequal or superposed, lower thecae white‑spurred at base. Ovary 2‑locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma entire or slightly bifid. Capsule ovate or oblong, shortly stalked, the placenta rising from base as fruit ripens, scattering the seeds, retinacula hooked, 4‑seeded. Seeds compressed, orbicular, glabrous, verrucose.

About 50 species in tropical regions; 17 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as the family.

Perennial suffrutescent herbs or dwarf shrubs, glabrous except for inflorescence. Stems erect or often recurved or pendent, quadrangular or terete. Leaves cauline, opposite or verticillate, sessile or petiolate, linear‑lanceolate to ovoid, acuminate, with entire or dentate margin, sometimes reduced to small scales. Flowers usually distinctly pedicellate. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed. Corolla bright red, cylindric, limb 2‑lipped, lobes rounded, tube cylindric. Stamens 4, included. Ovary ovoid to globose, with long hyaline inner hairs. Seeds numerous, ovoid, testa exalate.

About 52 species distributed in tropical America; one species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, strongly scented, all parts glandular-punctate. Stems woody at base. Leaves alternate, pinnately compound. Inflorescence a thyrse or corymb. Flowers yellow, 4–5-merous. Calyx 4–5-lobed, persistent. Petals imbricate, margin lacerate. Stamens 8–10, unequal, the alternate one shorter. Gynoecium composed of 4–5 carpels; carpels distinct at upper part and coherent at lower part, 4–5-locular, ovules 2 or more per locule. Fruit 4–5 follicles. Seeds ridged. Seed coat tuberculate.

About seven species distributed in Canary Islands, Mediterranean regions to SW Asia; two species introduced to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Woody climbers or scandent shrubs. Branchlets with persistent bud-scales at base. Leaves simple, alternate, mostly entire. Flowers usually hermaphroditic, axillary, solitary or in cymes or panicles. Sepals 5 or 4, imbricate, united at the base, persistent. Petals usually 5, rarely 6 or 4, opposite to the sepals. Stamens as many as and opposite to the petals, all fertile; filaments more or less flattened, inserted at the base of disc; anthers introrse or extrorse. Ovary 1- or 2-locular, with 2 superposed ovules in each locule; styles 2, coherent. Fruit a drupe, containing a single reniform seed.

About 30 species in S and SE of Asia; 16 species, four subspecies and two varities in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial stout herbs, rhizomatous. Culms erect, solid, usually unbranched. Leaves cauline, blades narrowly to broadly linear, margin scabrous, midrib broad and white; ligule membranous, margin ciliolate. Inflorescence terminal, a large plumose panicle with elongate central axis, its branches bearing many hairy racemes; racemes fragile, sessile and pedicellate spikelet of a pair similar, both fertile; rachis internodes and pedicels filiform with cupular apex, pedicels resembling internode but often shorter. Spikelets usually small, lanceolate, with hairs much longer than spikelets; lower glume flat to broadly convex, 2-keeled; upper glume boat-shaped, 1-keeled; lower floret reduced to an empty hyaline lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma membranous hyaline, with or without a short straight awn; stamens 2–3.

Between 35 and 40 species distributed throughout the tropics and subtropics, but mainly in Asia; 12 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culm erect or geniculate at the base. Leaf blades linear to convolute; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a dense and narrow cylindrical, spike-like panicle. Spikelets asymmetrical, lanceolate-oblong to ovate, usually laterally or rarely dorsally compressed, florets 2, lower floret staminate or barren, upper floret bisexual, deciduous from the swollen apex of pedicel; glumes unequal, lower glume slightly small, margins membranous; upper glume triangular-ovate, deeply concave and gibbous on the back, 7–11-veined; lower lemma similar to upper glume but less gibbous; palea often much reduced, hyaline; upper lemma oblong, dorsally compressed, often much shorter than spikelet, thinly leathery to cartilaginous, smooth, shiny, margins inrolled embraced palea. Lodicules 2; styles 2, free from the base.

About 30 species distributed in the tropics, but mainly in Africa; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or evergreen shrubs, often ± scandent, with spinescent side-branches. Leaves alternate or subopposite, pinnately-veined; stipules small, caducous. Flowers bisexual, sessile, in clusters along the branches, forming terminal or axillary spikes and often paniculate. Calyx hemispherical or campanulate, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, midvein raised adaxially. Petals 5, cucullate. Stamens 5, opposite to petals. Ovary surrounded by a thick, 5-lobed disk, 2–3-locular; style short, with a slightly 3-lobed stigma. Fruit a drupe, with fleshy or leathery exocarp and 2–3 indehiscent nutlets.

About 35 species distributed over E and S Asia and in N America; 19 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems usually tufted. Leaves linear or linear-subulate, connate at base. Stipules wanting. Flowers bisexual, solitary in axils of leaves or forming terminal 2–3- flowered cymes. Sepals 4 – 5. Petals 4 – 5, sometimes wanting, usually shorter than sepals, apex entire or retuse. Stamens 4– 5, sometimes 8 or 10. Ovary 1-locular, with many ovules; styles 4 – 5, alternate with sepals. Capsule ovoid, opening to the middle into 4 – 5 valves.

About 30 species, widely spread over N temperate regions; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or rarely annual herbs, aquatic. Stems often with rhizomes. Emersed leaves sagittate, floating leaves mostly cordate, submersed phyllodes linear. Flowers in whorls of 2 or 3, forming a raceme or a narrow panicle, with female flowers proximally, male ones distally. Sepals 3, herbaceous. Petals 3, delicate, white or rarely pink. Stamens 6–many; filaments filiform. Carpels many, crowded on a large globose or oblong receptacle, laterally flattened; styles ventral or apical. Achenes laterally compressed, beaked, winged. Seeds hippocrepiform.

About 25 species mainly in temperate and tropical America; nine species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous shrubs or trees; winter-buds covered with a single scale. Leaves alternate, rarely subopposite, mostly lanceolate, dentate or entire; stipules often developed, chiefly on vigorous branches. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious), usually in upright catkins, solitary on bracteate or leafy peduncles or branches, each flower subtended by a scale-like bract, with 1 or 2 glands or rarely a small lobed disc at the base. Male flowers: stamens usually 2, rarely 1–12; filaments slender, free or sometimes connate, exceeding the bract; female flowers: ovary 2-carpellate, sessile or stipitate; style very short or almost obsolete; stigmas 2, entire or bifid. Capsules 2-valved; seeds surrounded by tufts of long silky hairs.

About 300 species widely distributed in cold and temperate regions; 275 species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, sometimes parasitic. Leaves simple, alternate, petiolate or sessile, margin entire. Inflorescence a spike, terminal, bracts with a scarious margin, bracteoles absent. Flowers very small, zygomorphic. Sepals 5, persistent, nearly equal; inner 2 often slightly larger. Petals 3, usually pink-purple, keel cucullate, or arched, longer than lateral petals, without appendages. Stamens 4–5, filaments united and forming a sheath, adnate to the petal base; anthers connate, dehiscing by an apical pore. Disk absent. Ovary compressed, 2-locular; style curved, thickened toward apex; stigma capitate. Fruit a capsule, laterally compressed, loculicidal, margin denticulate. Seeds ovoid, glabrous, endosperm present, not arillate.

About 14 species distributed in tropical Asia and tropical Australia; three species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs, or shrubs. Leaves opposite, simple or pinnately compound. Verticillasters 2–many‑flowered, forming terminal and axillary racemes or panicles; bracts small or large, sometimes brilliantly coloured in cultivated forms. Calyx tubular to campanulate, 2‑lipped; upper lip entire, 2‑toothed, or 3‑mucronate; lower lip notched or 2‑toothed. Corolla 2‑lipped; tube with or without hairy annulus inside; upper lip straight or falcate, entire or emarginate; lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed; the central lobe usually wider than the lateral ones, entire or emarginate. Fertile stamens 2, representing the lower pair; filaments short, articulating with a slender connective, and sometimes produced beyond the joint; connectives linear, transverse, with an upper ascending arm which bears a linear fertile anther‑cell or empty; staminodes 2, small or absent. Disk usually enlarged anteriorly. Style shortly 2‑cleft, lobes subulate, linear or circular, equal or the lower larger, sometimes flattened. Nutlets ovoid, often triquetrous, glabrous, smooth.

About 900–1100 species widely distributed in temperate and subtropical regions of the world; 84 species in China; five species (three native) in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, rarely perennial herbs. Branches full of pith. Stipules present or becoming a gland. Leaves opposite, imparipinnate, leaflets serrulate. Inflorescence an umbel‑like corymb. Flowers small, bisexual, regular, bracteolate. Calyx (3–)5‑lobed or toothed. Corolla rotate or rotate‑campanulate, (3–)5‑parted. Stamens 5, inserted at base of corolla. Anthers extrorse. Disk convex or absent. Ovary (3–)5‑locular; styles 3‑parted; ovules solitary in each locule. Drupe berry‑like, containing 3–5 pyrenes.

More than 20 species distributed in N hemisphere and subtropical area; four to five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect to scandent perennial herbs or shrubs, with cystoliths. Leaves opposite, subsessile to petiolate, margin entire to crenuate, coloured on the veins. Flowers usually large and conspicuous, solitary or more often fasciculate, forming terminal heads, spikes or racemes. Bracts large or small, free, rarely partly connate; bracteoles 2. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes subequal to unequal in size. Corolla yellow, orange, red or purple; tube cylindric or ± expanded distally, limb subactinomorphic, 5‑lobed; lobes small, often recoiled, contorted in bud. Stamens 2, usually exserted; anthers 2‑thecous; thecae equal in size, parallel, longitudinally ciliate, mucronate at base, dehiscing towards lower lip; staminodes 2. Ovary 2‑locular, 3–4 ovules per locule; style usullay exserted; stigma 2‑lobed; lobes unequal. Capsule estipitate, linear‑ellipsoidal, retinacula present, 6–8‑seeded. Seeds lenticular.

About 60 species native to tropical America; two species cultivated in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Biennial or perennial herbs, with rootstocks, tubers or fasciculate fibrous roots. Stems erect or ascending, or scapose, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves with sheathing petioles or subsessile; leaf blade orbicular, round-cordate or cordate-pentagonal, palmately 3–5-lobed, the segments toothed, lobed or dissected. Umbels simple or irregularly compound; involucres foliaceous; bracteoles longer or shorter than the rays. Flowers polygamous; bisexual flowers sessile or subsessile, in the center of the umbel; staminate flowers usually stalked, peripheral. Calyx-teeth prominent. Petals spathulate to ovate, with narrow inflexed apices. Styles filiform, shorter or longer than the calyx-lobes, spreading to recurved. Stylopodium lacking or flattened and disk-like. Fruit globose or oblong-ovoid, somewhat compressed laterally, densely covered with prickles, spines or tubercles; ribs obscure; carpophore wanting; carpels subterete. Vittae 5 or more, usually obscure. Seed-face plane or sulcate.


About 40 species, widely distributed throughout the world, except in Australia and New Zealand; 15 species and one variety in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, rhizomatous. Leaves 1–6, basal or on very short stem, thick, rigid, often fleshy, flat or subterete, often with transverse green stripes. Inflorescence spicate, racemose or paniculate. Flowers bisexual, solitary or clustered; pedicels articulate; perianth tube tubular, lobes 6, reflexed or spreading; stamens 6, inserted on the throat of perianth tube, exserted, filaments filiform, anthers dorsifixed, dehiscent introrsely. Ovary superior, 3-locular, ovule 1 per locule; style slender, stigma small. Fruit a berry, 1–3-seeded.

About 50 species distributed in Africa and Asia.

Trees, rarely shrubs, monoecious. Leaves paripinnate, rarely simple, alternate, exstipulate; leaflets entire, opposite or alternate. Thyrses large, many-branched, terminal or fasciculate at apex of branchlets; bracts and bracteoles subulate, small. Flowers unisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic. Sepals 4–5, imbricate, outer 2 smaller. Petals 4–5, clawed or not, with (1–)2 scales at base adaxially. Disk fleshy, acetabuliform or semilunar, sometimes lobed. Stamens (male flowers) 8, rarely more or fewer, exserted; filaments ± hairy. Ovary (female flowers) obovoid or turbinate, usually 3-lobed, 3-locular; ovules 1 per locule, ascending; style terminal.
