Fruit dehiscent into 3 schizocarps, usually 1–2 developed, developed schizocarps subglobose or obovoid, abaxially slightly flat; pericarp fleshy, containing abundant saponin. Seeds black or pale brown, ellipsoidal or subglobose, testa bony, hilum linear.

About 13 species distributed in warm regions of N & S America, Asia, and Australia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, with milky juice. Leaves alternate, entire or serrate, pinnately-veined; petioles apically biglandular; stipules caducous. Flowers apetalous, unisexual (plant monoecious or sometimes dioecious), in terminal or axillary spikes, racemes or spicate panicles; bracts bearing 2 large glands at base on abaxial surfaces. Male flowers small, yellow, several fascicled in axil of bracts, without pistillode; calyx membranous, cupular-shaped, shallowly 2–3-lobed or 2 – 3-toothed; stamens 2–3, filaments free; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent. Female flowers larger than male ones, solitary in axil of bracts; calyx cup-shaped, 3-partite, or cylindric and 3-dentate; ovary 2–3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles usually 3, free or connate at base; stigma revolute, entire. Capsules globose, pyriform or 3-valved, rarely baccate, usually 3-locular, loculicidally dehiscent or indehiscent; seeds subglobose, sometimes covered with waxy aril, central column persistent, exocarp hard; albumen fleshy, cotyledon broad flattened.

About 120 species, all in the tropical regions, especially in S America; nine species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves paripinnate; petioles short and stout; stipules 2, often connate into a conical sheath, caducous. Corymbose panicles axillary or terminal. Involucral bracts caducous. Bract 1, hairy or glabrous, deciduous or persistent; bracteoles 2, subopposite, often persistent and colourful. Flowers pedicellate, yellow to deeply red, bisexual or unisexual, apetalous. Calyx-tube elongated, upper part slightly enlarged, apex with a disk; lobes 4(–6), petaloid, ovate or oblong, slightly unequal, imbricate. Stamens 4 – 10, all developed or 1–2 reduced, inserted at the disk on calyx throat; filaments exserted, distinct, reflexed in bud, anthers ellipsoidal or subglobose, dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary compressed oblong, hairy or glabrous, shortly stipitate; ovules several to more than 10, stipe adnate to calyx-tube; style linear, stigmas capitate. Pods compressed oblong, slightly curved, leathery to subwoody, 2-valved. Seeds 1 – 8, elliptic or ovate, bilaterally compressed; seed-coat rigid; radicle small, erect.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Asia; two species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs, glabrous; wood without vessels. Leaves opposite, stipules small; petioles short, base connate; leaf blade elliptic, ovateelliptic, or elliptic-lanceolate, margin serrate, with glandular-tipped teeth. Spikes terminal, usually branched, ± in panicles; flowers bisexual, perianth and pedicel absent; bract 1, triangular, persistent. Stamen 1, fleshy, clavate to compressed; anther 2(–3)-celled, cells lateral to introrse. Ovary globose or ovoid; style absent; stigma subcapitate or minutely spotted. Drupes globose or ovoid.

Three species distributed in SE Asia to India; one species in S China, also in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs. Leaves alternate, entire, pinnately-veined or 3-veined. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, head-like or racemose. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious), usually androgynous, with female flowers at the lower part and male flowers on the upper part, or sometimes males and females borne on separate inflorescences. Male flowers: bracteoles 2; sepals 4, in 2 series; stamens as many as and opposite to sepals, exserted; rudimentary pistil oblong, 4-angled, concave at apex. Female flowers: bracteoles numerous, imbricate; sepals 4–6, decussate or in 2 series; ovary 2–3-locular; style 2–3, initially coalescent at apex, separate and recurved after pollination. Fruit drupe-like, ovoid or globose, exocarp fleshy or dry, endocarp crustaceous, 1–2-seeded.

About 20 species in SE and S Asia; nine species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees. Leaves opposite, subopposite, or rarely alternate, leathery; stipules small, caducous and leaving conspicuous scars on petioles. Flowers small, solitary or in axillary racemes or panicles. Bracts small, triangular. Sepals 5, imbricate. Corolla broadly campanulate; lobes 5, ovate, imbricate. Stamens 5, inserted at corolla-tube and opposite to lobes, filaments short, anthers 2- celled; staminodes 5, subulate to triangular, inserted at throat and alternate to corolla-lobes. Ovary 1- or 2-locular, glabrous; ovules 1 per locule. Style short; stigma capitate or 2-lobed. Fruit a drupe, ellipsoid, 1- or 2-seeded. Seed scar small, rounded.

About nine species distributed in tropical Asia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as the family.

Trees or shrubs. Branchlets usually with more or less stiff appressed hairs or subulate scales. Stipules absent. Leaves serrate or serrulate at margin; veins with scales or stiff hairs, lateral veins many, parallel. Flowers bisexual, in axillary thyrsoid or paniculate cymes, rarely solitary. Bracts small, linear. Sepals 5, imbricate. Petals 5, imbricate, usually connate at base. Stamens many, inserted at base of petals; anthers obtrigonal, dorsifixed, dehiscing by longitudinal slits or by apical pores. Ovary superior, 3–5-locular, with many ovules per locule; styles 3–5, connate at lower half, rarely distinct, stigma simple to discoid. Berry globose or depressed-globose, usually ridged, white to pale green, rarely red. Seeds many, small, brown, buried in pulp, areolate.

About 300 species distributed in tropical regions of Asia and America; 13 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, rarely herbs or climbers, monoecious or dioecious. Leaves simple, alternate, entire, pinnately-veined or rarely 3-veined. Stipules paired, inserted bilaterally at the base of petiole. Flowers smaller, apetalous. Male flowers clustered or solitary, rarely forming racemes or short cymes, axillary or borne on stems; pedicels usually bracteolate at base; calyx discoid, cup-shaped or turbinate, entire or 6-lobed; lobes imbricate, erect or spreading; disk 6–12-lobed, segments unequal, opposite to sepals, rarely without disk; stamens 3, filaments usually connate into a short column, anthers free, longitudinally dehiscent; pistillode absent. Female flowers: 1–2 or mixed with male flowers in axil of leaves, rarely inserted at the base of male inflorescences; calyx usually 6-parted; lobes biseriate, imbricate, sometimes thickened in fruiting times; disk absent; ovary ovoid or depressed globose, 3-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles 3, free or connate at base, 2-branched at apex, arms recurved. Capsules depressed or ovoid, separating into 3 bivalved cocci when mature.

About 56 species in Madagascar, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia and Australia; 14 species and two varieties species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, erect or ascending, rhizomatous. Stems longitudinally ridged and sulcate. Leaves entire; stipules membranous. Inflorescence a leaf-opposed or terminal raceme. Flowers white when mature, small. Stamens usually 6, sometimes 8, rarely 3, longer than styles; filaments ca. as long as or slightly longer than anthers; anthers oblong. Pistils 4, 3- or 4-carpellate, with carpels distinct or connate at base; ovary superior; each carpel with 2–4 ovules; styles 4, recurved. Fruit a schizocarp with 3 or 4 1-seeded mericarps.

Two species distributed disjunctly in E Asia and N America; one species occurs in China; it occurs in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs, sometimes subshrubs; stem glabrous, pubescent to tomentose, or plant without stem. Leaves alternate, margin entire, toothed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect. Capitula homogamous and discoid, sessile or pedunculate, in corymbose, paniculate or racemose form, sometimes aggregated on stem terminal, rarely solitary. Involucres cylindric, campanulate, ovoid or globose; phyllaries in many rows, appressed, imbricate, growing longer and narrower inward, sometimes with reddish scarious apical appendages or herbaceous green appendages. Receptacle flat or convex, densely setaceous or not. All florets bisexual and fertile, corolla tubular, lower tube filiform, upper limb broaden and deeply cleft into 5 lobes, colour purple or purple‑red, rarely white; anther bases sagittate, basal appendages lacerate, filaments separate and glabrous; style branches divided, linear, obtuse or subobtuse apically. Cypselae obtusely 4‑angulate or many‑ribbed, sometimes transversely rugose, apex truncate, shortly coronate or not. Pappus (1–)2‑seriate; outer ones shorter in length, capillary or slightly plumose, deciduous individually; inner ones longer, plumose, base connate, deciduous as a ring or persistent.

About 400 species distributed in Asia, Europe, N America and Australia; about 260 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial, rarely annual or biennial herbs. Stem caespitose or simple. Leaves both basal and cauline, petiolate; cauline ones alternate, rarely opposite, margin dentate or lobate. Inflorescence a few- to many-flowered cyme or flower solitary, bracteate. Flowers usually bisexual, sometimes unisexual, actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic. Sepals (4– )5, sometimes adnate to ovary at base. Petals (4– )5, yellow, orange, white, or red to purple, distinctly veined, margin usually entire. Stamens (8– )10; filaments subulate or clavate. Ovary superior to inferior, usually 2-locular; placentation usually axile; ovules many; disk sometimes well developed, annular or semi-annular. Fruit a 2-valved capsule. Seeds many, small.

About 450 species distributed in temperate and cold regions of the world, mainly in N hemisphere; 216 species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, erect or scandent. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, entire or toothed. Flowers usually 5‑merous, forming cymes or sometimes solitary. Calyx‑tube adnate to the ovary; limb short, ring‑ to cup‑shaped or toothed. Corolla open on the upper side to the base, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes subequal or the upper 2 slightly shorter, usually spreading digitately at full blooming. Anthers free. Ovary inferior, rarely half‑inferior, 1–4‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; stigma surrounded by a cup‑shaped indusium and ciliate on the margin. Fruit drupaceous, indehiscent, 1–4‑seeded.

About 80 species mainly in Australasia, with two species widely spread in tropical regions; two species in China and in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or trees, sometimes subscandent, hermaphroditic or andro-monoecious, unarmed; branchlets glabrous or stellate-tomentose. Leaves digitately compound; stipules connate within petiole. Flowers in umbels, racemes, spikes or globose heads, rearranged in panicles or compound racemes, bracts hairy, deciduous or persistent, pedicels not articulate. Calyx-margin entire or minutely 5-toothed. Petals 5–7, valvate in the bud. Stamens as many as petals. Ovary 5–7-locular, rarely less or more; styles partly or completely united into a column or stigmas sessile. Fruit a drupe, globose or ovoid, 5–7-seeded, angled or not; seeds laterally compressed; endosperm uniform or slightly ruminate.

About 1100 species widely distributed in the tropical and subtropical regions of both hemispheres; 35 species in China; one species native to Hong Kong. Some ornamental species are cultivated in gardens.

Evergreeen trees. Leaves spirally arranged, petiolate, margin entire or serrate. Flowers bisexual, axillary or subterminal, solitary or subracemosely arranged; bracteoles 2–7, caducous. Sepals 5, imbricate, persistent, slightly connate at base; petals 5, subequal, outermost one enveloping the others, shortly connate at base; stamens many, adnate to base of petals, anthers versatile; ovary 5-locular with 2–6 ovules per locule; style simple, shortly lobed at the top. Capsule globose or depressed globose, woody, dehiscing into 5 valves; central axis stout, persistent. Seeds small, reniform, flat, surrounded by a membranous wing.

About 20 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia to New Guinea; 13 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms slender, branched, erect or prostrate at base. Leaf blades linear or oblong-linear; ligule membranous. Inflorescence a solitary slender fragile raceme, terminal or axillary, supported by a spatheole; rachis internodes and pedicels filiform to clavate, glabrous to ciliate or villous, apex cupular with scarious lobed rim; spikelets of a dissimilar pair. Sessile spikelet dorsally compressed or squeezed between internode and pedicel; callus obconical, obtuse, shortly bearded, inserted into internode apex; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, papery to subleathery, abaxially convex, flanks inflexed, often 2-keeled, usually wingless; upper glume boatshaped; lower floret reduced to a hyaline lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline, deeply 2-lobed, awned from sinus; awn geniculate, column glabrous. Caryopsis linear. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, usually smaller than sessile spikelet, sometimes much reduced to a lemma, awned.

About 60 species spread throughout tropics and subtropics; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Rhizomes subcylindrical, short, thick. Leaf blade entire, pinnately-veined, base elongate. Inflorescence with 4 involucral bracts. Perianth campanulate, 6-lobed; lobes variable in size, caducous. Fruit a capsule. Seeds oblong, irregularly oblong, ovoid, or semilunar.

Two species distributed in China, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam; one species in Hong Kong.

Arborescent bamboos, sometimes shrubby or scrambling. Rhizomes short necked, pachymorph. Culms erect, pendulous, or clambering, straight or slightly flexuose; internodes terete, distally often white powdery; wall usually thin; nodal ridge not prominent; sheath scar prominent. Branches many, subequal. Culm sheaths deciduous, leathery to thickly papery, usually rigid, white powdery, apex truncate or concave, sometimes with subcircular projection at base of one margin; auricles usually inconspicuous; oral setae usually developed; ligule short, truncate, margin serrulate or fimbriate; blade usually reflexed, adaxially densely hispid, apex usually involute. Leaf sheaths usually grooved; auricles usually inconspicuous; blade large, transverse veins partially visible abaxially. Inflorescence fully bracteate, iterauctant; with several to many sessile pseudospikelets in loose, spicate clusters on leafy or leafless flowering branches. Pseudospikelet prophyll triangular to linear-lanceolate; gemmiferous bracts 1–several; fertile florets 1–2, or florets 3–4 with only terminal or subterminal floret fertile; rachilla usually disarticulating, extending beyond fertile floret, glumes usually absent; lemma convolute; palea similar to lemma, but longer, not keeled; lodicules usually absent, sometimes 1–3. Stamens 6. Ovary stalked; style 1; stigmas 3, plumose. Caryopsis fusiform, apex with persistent style base.

About 50 species distributed in SE Asia; nine species (five endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Succulent plants. Stems much branched and short-jointed; joints usually flat, or becoming ± cylindric in age; areoles borne on the margins and the truncate end of joints, with a few bristles. Flowers ± zygomorphic, arising from the areoles, solitary; perianth-segments many, united into a tube below; stamens many; ovary inferior, spineless. Fruit a berry, globose or obconical, red or purplish.

About five to six species, all native to Brazil; two species (introduced) in China, one commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials, sometimes with decumbent creeping rhizomes. Culms trigonous or terete, not nodose above base, naked, clothed at base with a few to several bladeless leaf sheaths. Leaves mostly reduced to bladeless sheaths, rarely leaf blade present; ligule absent. Involucral bracts culm-like, lowest bract erect, remainder usually indistinct. Inflorescences varying from open anthela to contracted head, frequently becoming pseudolateral with its lowest bract erect and continuous with culm, small, secondary inflorescence sometimes present within lowermost leaf sheath at culm base. Spikelets mostly ovoid or ellipsoidal, rarely flattened, with many glumes on a continuous axis. Glumes spirally imbricate, rarely 2-ranked, usually membranous, all bearing a bisexual flower in axil. Flowers with 3 – 6 perianth segments, needle-like, spinulose-scabrous, rarely broader and fimbriate, or sometimes reduced to none. Stamens 3. Stigmas 3 or less commonly digynous; style continuous with ovary. Achenes biconvex or trigonous, smooth to transversely wrinkled, maturing brown or black.

About 100 species distributed worldwide with highest species diversity in E and S Asia and temperate N America; 22 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Annuals or perennials. Rhizome sometimes creeping or woody. Culms erect or with ascending base rooting at nodes. Leaves basal and cauline, rarely reduced to bladeless sheaths; ligule absent. Involucral bracts leaf-like or glume-like. Inflorescence panicle-like, rarely capitate or reduced to a single spikelet. Spikelets usually lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, flattened, several-glumed, few-flowered. Glumes distichous, caducous, 1-veined, keel acute, lower several glumes empty. Flowers usually bisexual, the uppermost one often not producing mature achenes or male. Perianth segments 0–6. Stamens (1–)3(–6). Stigmas 2(–3); style continuous ovary. Achenes trigonous.

About 120 species, mostly in Oceania and SE Asia, only with a few species in Europe and Americas; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Branchlets unarmed, often caducous. Leaf blade pinnately-veined. Inflorescences racemose or spicate; peduncle sometimes with persistent bud scales at base; rachis slightly zigzagged. Flowers sometimes ± opposite, fragrant, often heterostylous. Bracts and bracteoles persistent. Calyx adherent to ovary, truncate or 4–5(–6)-denticulate, accrescent. Corolla tubular, campanulate, or urceolate; lobes 4–6, with a tuft of hairs behind each filament. Stamens 4–5(–6), epipetalous, opposite to petal-lobes; filaments short; anther 2-celled. Disk annular, fleshy. Ovary semisuperior, basally 3-loculed, apically 1-loculed; placenta central, free; ovules 3; style slender, shorter than or as long as corolla tube; stigma 3-lobed. Drupe united with calyx and apparently inferior, tipped with disk and calyx teeth, often ± longitudinally striate when dried, 1-seeded; endosperm copious.

About 30 species distributed in tropical and subtropical America and Asia; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Small, delicate, achlorophyllous, mycotrophic herbs, rhizomatous. Stem erect, simple or rarely branched, with scale-like leaves, whitish, pinkish, or reddish. Inflorescence a terminal raceme, sometimes branched from base. Flowers unisexual or hermaphrodite. Perianth segments 4–10, usually 6, equal or unequal, inner side papillate, apex sometimes with tufts of hairs, or ending in a globose knob or short point. Male flowers with 2, 3 or 6 stamens, opposed perianth segments; anthers 1–4-celled, sessile or on short filaments, often connate at base forming a small and flat circular androphore in centre of flower. Female flowers with 10–80 free carpels; style laterally or basally, apex papillate to penicillate or glabrous. Bisexual flowers with 3–6 persistent stamens; anthers 1-celled. Carpels 10–80 as in female flower, style club-shaped. Follicle with 1 seed, dehiscent.

About 30 species, pantropical but mainly in Indo-Malesia; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Tufted or rhizomatous perennials. Culms few- or many-noded, terete to triquetrous. Leaves basal and cauline, ligulate; blades linear; basal sheaths open, cauline sheaths tubular. Involucral bracts leaf-like, spreading. Inflorescence terminal, paniculate, simple to decompound. Spikelets generally small, ovoid or ellipsoidal, terete. Glumes spirally arranged, mostly membranous, deciduous, each subtending a flower. Flowers bisexual. Perianth segments (0–)3–6, filiform, as long as to much longer than the fruit (and then often extremely contorted), ± scabrid, deciduous with the fruit. Stamens 1–3. Style base not distinct, not thickened, persistent; stigmas 2–3. Achene obovate to elliptic, (compressed) trigonous or biconvex, beaked, smooth.

About 35 species mostly in the temperate regions of N hemisphere; 12 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennials. Rhizome usually woody, knotted. Culms solitary or tufted, usually erect, sometimes climbing or scrambling. Leaves cauline or basal and cauline, the latter sometimes apparently in whole; blade mostly linear; sheath closed, often 3-winged or terete; ligule absent; contraligule usually present. Inflorescence usually paniculate, bearing a terminal and 1– several (rarely none) lateral partial inflorescences, occasionally reduced and spike-like or capitate. Spikelets unisexual or bisexual; bisexual spikelets with terminal female flower and 1– several lateral male ones; female spikelets with a single female flower and 1– several lateral glumes (reduced male flowers); male spikelets with several to many glumes. Glumes spirally arranged or 2-ranked. Flowers unisexual. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 1–3 per male flower. Stigmas 3; style continuous with the ovary, caducous. Achenes terete or subtrigonous, mostly globose, ovoid or subpyramidal, with bony pericarp and a stipe-like, 3-lobed or cup-like, rarely indistinct disk attached at the base.

About 200 species in tropical and subtropical regions of both hemispheres, with the highest number of species in tropical America; 24 species in China; nine species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, often spinose on trunk and branches. Leaves alternate, leathery, entire or serrate or crenate, pinnately veined or 3-veined, sometimes with 2 glands at apex of petioles or at base of leaf blades; stipules small, caducous. Racemes terminal or axillary, sometimes flowers clustered or solitary. Flowers small, bisexual. Sepals 4 – 6, imbricate, slightly united at base. Petals as many as and similar to sepals. Stamens many, inserted on thick torus; filaments longer than petals; anthers ellipsoid, dorsifixed, connectives prolonged to appendages; disc entire or 8 –10-lobed, sometimes absent; ovary sessile, 1-locular, with 2– 4 parietal placentas; ovules several; styles linear; stigmas entire or 2– 4-lobed. Berry fleshy, with persistent sepals, petals, and stamens; seeds 2– 4.

About 40 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, many‑branched. Leaves opposite or whorled, generally glandular punctate, margin entire or toothed. Flowers 1–2 in axils of leaves. Pedicels slender. Calyx 4–5‑lobed; lobes imbricate, ovate to lanceolate. Corolla nearly regular; tube inconspicuous, limb subrotate, densely hairy at throat; lobes 4, imbricate. Stamens 4, subequal; anther‑cells distinct, parallel or divergent. Ovary globose; ovules numerous, styles apically ± enlarged. Capsules ovoid to globose, septicidal and secondarily loculicidal; valves thin, margin involute. Seeds many, small, foveolate.

About 20 species, mostly from tropical America; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Parasitic shrubs; young branches and leaves hairy. Leaves opposite or subopposite, pinnately-veined. Inflorescences axillary or borne on leafless nodes, racemose or sometimes umbellate. Flowers bisexual, 4-merous, zygomorphic, each flower subtended by 1 scale-like bract. Calyx pyriform or turbinate, base attenuate, limb annular, persistent. Mature flower bud tubular. Corolla sympetalous, curved, basal portion ± inflated, split along 1 side at anthesis, tip ellipsoidal or ovoid, lobes all reflexed toward the side away from the split. Stamens inserted at base of corolla lobes; filaments short; anthers 4-celled, sometimes with septum. Ovary 1-locular; placentation basal. Style filiform, 4-angled; stigma only slightly enlarged and capitate. Fruit a berry, turbinate, clavate, or pyriform, 1-seeded, base narrow or often attenuate into a stipe, exocarp leathery, pubescent or glabrous.

About 50 species distributed in S and SE Asia; ten species (two endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, not aromatic. Leaves opposite, petiolate, rarely sessile. Flowers in terminal or axillary racemes or spikes; bracts minute or conspicuous and foliaceous. Calyx short campanulate, 2‑lipped; lips entire, the upper one with a large deciduous shield‑ or pouch‑like appendage (scutellum) on its back; in fruit, at first the lips closed together, then the upper lip falling away together with the appendage. Corolla 2‑lipped; tube rather long, usually sharply recurved from the base and erect upwards, not hairy annulate inside; upper lip often boat‑shaped, entire or notched; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe broad, flattened, entire, lateral lobes ± joined to upper lip and sometimes spreading. Stamens 4, lower pair longer, underlying upper lip; anthers close together in pairs, bearded on cell aperture; upper pair conspicuously 2‑celled, ± apically acute, lower pair 1‑celled by abortion. Disk tubular, elongate. Style subulate, apically unequally 2‑cleft. Nutlets raised on a short, oblique, or curved stalk (gynophore).

About 350 species distributed nearly throughout the world, but only a few in tropical Africa; 98 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, rarely herbs. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, petiolate, pinnately-veined; stipules small. Flowers apetalous, unisexual (plant usually monoecious), in terminal, axillary, leaf-opposed or extra-axillary racemes or spikes; bracts small, with 2 glands at base. Male flowers: 1–3 in axils of bracts; pedicels slender; sepals often 3, free or connate at base; stamens 2–3(–4), filaments free or connate at base; anthers 2-celled, longitudinally dehiscent, pistillode absent. Female flowers: solitary in axils of bracts; pedicels short; sepals 3; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 3, free or connate at base. Capsules subglobose, smooth or echinate, divided into 3 bivalved cocci; seeds globose or oblong, carunculate, albumen fleshy.


About 100 species mainly distributed in tropical regions of the New World, but with outliers in temperate N America, Asia, and Australasia; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbaceous vines, monoecious, hispidulous. Roots tuberous. Tendrils 3 –5-branched. Leaves polygonal or lobed. Male flowers: arranged in axillary racemes; calyx-tube plateform, lobes 5; corolla rotate, 5-lobed, lobes ovate-lanceolate; stamens 3, inserted at the base of calyx-tube, filaments connate, anthers free, one 1-celled, two 2-celled, cells flexuous; pistillode absent. Female flowers: solitary or in pairs, usually in the same axil with the male ones; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary fusiform, 1-locular, setose, style short, stigma 5-lobed; ovule 1, pendulous. Fruit fleshy, obovoid, sulcate at apex. Seed 1, ovate, compressed. Testa woody, smooth.

About five species distributed in Mexico and C America; one species cultivated in China, also in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs. Leaves alternate, stipulate or exstipulate. Inflorescence a raceme or panicle, terminal or axillary, bracteate. Flowers zygomorphic, small. Sepals 5, caducous, unequal; outer 3 small, inner 2 petaloid, large. Petals 3, lateral petals and keel connate or free, keel helmet-shaped, with cockscomb-shaped appendage at apex. Stamens 8, filaments united in lower part and forming a sheath, adnate to petals; anthers 2-celled, introrse, dehiscing by oblique pores. Disk reniform. Ovary 1-locular, with one pendulous ovule; style falcate; stigma short, lobed or not. Fruit usually a samara, 1-seeded. Seed subglobose, endosperm wanting, not arillate, seed coat membranous.

About 80 species mainly distributed in tropical America, a few distributed in the tropics of Asia and tropical Africa; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial succulent herbs, usually glabrous. Stems erect or diffuse, rarely woody at base. Leaves fleshy, mostly alternate, but in many species opposite or whorled, entire or toothed. Cymes terminal, often with second branches. Flowers normally bisexual and (4– )5( –9)-merous. Sepals free or connate at the base. Petals usually distinct or ± connate at the base. Stamens normally twice as many as the petals and in two whorls, the inner ones attached to the base of petals. Carpels usually distinct, sometimes slightly connate at the base. Scales (nectariferous appendages) attached to the base of carpels, entire or emarginate. Fruit a group of follicles, many-seeded.

More than 300 species widely distributed in N temperate regions and tropical mountains; about 125 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, subshrubs or shrubs; stem erect, stoloniferous, decumbent or scandent. Basal leaves usually petiolate, without auricles, shape triangular, lyrate or pinnately parted. Cauline leaves usually sessile, but sometimes petiolate, auriculate at base, lyrately or pinnately lobed, margin toothed, with pinnate venations. Capitula erect or nodding, pedunculate, mostly in corymbose or thyrsoid arrangement at terminal, rarely solitary and axillary, heterogamous with both ligulate and tubular florets, or homogamous with tubular florets only. Involucres hemispherical, bell‑shaped or cylindric; phyllaries in 1 series, free or coherent at base, herbaceous or coriaceous, margin scarious, base calyculate. Receptacle plain, naked. Marginal ligulate florets 1‑seriate, female and fertile, corolla yellow in colour, 2–3‑lobed apically; or ray florets absent. Disk tubular florets many, bisexual and fertile, corolla yellow, funnelform or cylindric, apex 4–5‑lobed; anther bases shortly obtuse‑auriculate, apical appendages ovate, acute or obtuse, filament dilated at distal end; stylar branches recurved, truncate at apex, papillose hairy. Cypselae terete, ribbed, glabrous or pubescent. Pappus capillary, uniform or sometimes dimorphous, colour white, pale brown or tinged red, sometimes absent from ligulate florets or rarely absent from all florets.

A cosmopolitan genus with about 1000 species in the world; about 63 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees, shrubs, subshrubs or herbs. Leaves paripinnate, often glandular on petioles and leaf rachis; leaflets opposite, sessile or shortly petiolulate; stipules various, stipels lacking. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate, axillary or terminal, rarely flowers solitary or few clustered in leaf axils. Bracteoles absent. Calyx-tube short, lobes 5, imbricate. Petals usually 5, subequal or lower 2 longer. Androecium zygomorphic, stamens (4–)10, ± graduated in length from adaxial to abaxial side of flower, the 3 adaxial stamens staminodal, the (6–)7 fertile anthers basifixed, usually modified into heteromorphic sets of 4 medium and (2–)3 abaxial, all beakless or variably beaked or appendaged at apex, dehiscing by pores or short slits, the thecae either glabrous or pubescent but not ciliolate along the lateral sutures. Ovary slender, sometimes curved, sessile or stipitate, ovules many per locule; styles incurved; stigmas small. Pods either indehiscent, or breaking inelastically through one or both sutures; if through both, then the valves not coiling. Seed-coat often with a closed areole on each face or margin.

About 300 species in tropical and subtropical regions; 18 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

In addition, S. bicapsularis (L.) Roxb., S. floribunda (Cav.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby, S. hirsuta (L.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby, S. spectabilis (DC.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby, S. multijuga (Rich.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby and S. polyphylla (Jacq.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby are occasionally cultivated in Hong Kong.

Small shrubs, many‑branched, fetid when rubbed. Leaves rather small, opposite or crowded on short branchlets, short‑petiolate or subsessile; stipules united into a short sheath, apex with 3–8 bristles. Flowers small, terminal or axillary, solitary or in small clusters, sessile. Calyx‑tube obconical, very short; limb 4–6 lobed; lobes triangular or triangular‑lanceolate, acute, persistent. Corolla funnel‑shaped; tube slender, dilated near apex, hairy inside; limb 4 – 6‑lobed; lobes equal to the tube, valvate in the bud. Stamens 4 – 6, attached to the tube. Ovary 2‑locular, with a solitary ovule in each locule; style filiform; stigma bifid. Fruit a drupe, with 2 pyrenes.

Two species in China, Japan and Vietnam; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Erect or creeping herbs, usually pubescent. Leaves opposite or alternate, margin entire, dentate or parted. Flowers solitary, axillary, rarely in cymes. Pedicel short. Calyx small, 5‑lobed. Corolla white or pale purple, tubular, obscurely bilabiate, 5‑lobed. Stamens 4, didynamous. Ovary 2‑locular, divided by a false septum. Ovules many per locule, uniseriate. Fruit a capsule, ellipsoidal, longitudinally dehiscent. Seeds many, obovoid, compressed, winged, smooth or rugose.

About 30 species, mainly distributed in Africa and Asia; one species cultivated in China; it also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs, rarely trees. Stipules small, basifixed, often caducous, stipels minute or absent. Leaves even-pinnate, rachis ending in a short stipules point; leaflets numerous, narrow, entire, often glaucous. Racemes axillary. Bracts and bracteoles setaceous, usually caducous. Pedicels slender. Calyx campanulate, shortly 5-toothed. Corolla yellow or spotted, rarely white, red or purple-black (sometimes very large, e.g. S. grandiflora Pers.). Petals all clawed; vexillum suborbicular, spreading or reflexed, with two ascending spurs at top of claw; wings falcate-oblong, longer than upcurved keel. Stamens 10, diadelphous; anthers uniform, dorsifixed. Ovary often stipitate; ovules numerous, style incurved, stigma capitate. Pods linear, terete, constricted and septate between seeds. Seeds numerous, cylidrincal or subquadrate, without strophiole.

About 50 species distributed in tropical and subtropical areas of the world; five species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Succulent herbs or subshrubs. Stems prostrate or erect. Leaves opposite, fleshy, exstipulate; petioles often dilated and sheathing at the base. Flowers axillary, solitary, clustered or in cymes; calyx deeply 5-lobed, lobes often colored adaxially; petals absent; stamens 5, alternate with calyx-lobes, or many and inserted near apex of calyx-tube; filaments filiform, free or united at the base; ovary superior, 3 – 5-locular, with many ovules in each loucular; styles 3– 5, filiform. Capsules membranous, opening transversely at middle; seeds reniform, smooth.

About 17 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms usually tufted, erect geniculate at base, sometimes stoloniferous. Leaf blades linear to lanceolate, with a broad or attenuate base and acute tip; ligule divided into hair-like slips or ciliate. Inflorescence a panicle, dense and spike-like or open with the spikelets contracted around the primary branches; spikelets (or some of them) subtended by 1–several bristles which persist on the branches after the spikelets fall. Spikelets elliptic, awnless, florets 2; glumes and lower lemma membranous to herbaceous; lower glume ovate or triangular, 3–5-veined or veinless; upper glume 5–7-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, palea present, reduced or absent; upper lemma coriaceous, strongly convex, rugose, punctate or smooth, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea; lodicules 2; stamens 3; styles 2. Caryopsis elliptic-globose or ovate-globose.

About 130 species distributed from tropical to warm-temperate regions of the world; 14 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Undershrubs or herbs, stellate-pubescent throughout. Leaves alternate, serrate or weekly lobed. Flowers solitary, subfasciculate, or in panicles or corymbs, axillary or terminal. Pedicels articulate. Epicalyx wanting. Calyx cup-shaped or subcampanulate, 5-lobed; lobes deltoid, acuminate. Corolla subrotate, 5-lobed, connate at base and adnate to the staminal tube. Staminal tube with free filaments at apex. Ovary with 5 to 10 carpels; styles as many as carpels, reflexed; stigmas capitate; ovule 1 in each carpel, pendulous. Fruits subdiscoid or subglobose, carpels birostrate or muticous, at maturity separating from the columella, apical end clefted, the back and sides striatesulcate or smooth. Seed remaining in the pericarp, smooth, glabrous, black, sometimes pilose around the hilum.

About 200 species, majority belonging to the New World; 13 species in the warmer regions of China; six species in Hong Kong.

Annual branched erect herbs, glandular and hairy. Leaves opposite, toothed. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, in loose panicle form. Involucres campanulate or hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous bearing stipitate glands, 2‑seriate; outer ones usually 5, linear‑spatulate, spreading; inner ones enclosing the hypanthia of ray florets. Receptacle small, paleate; palea membranous, enveloping the cypselae. Marginal florets pistillate, 1–2‑seriate, corolla ligulate with apex 2–3‑lobed. Disk florets bisexual, corolla tubular and 5‑cleft at apex, all florets fertile or with some central florets sterile; stylar branches short, slightly flattened, acute or obtuse; anther bases entire. Cypselae obovate to oblong, oblique‑tetragonous, truncate apically, blackish brown, glabrous. Pappus none.

About four species widely distributed in warm areas of the world; three species in China; one species growing as weed in Hong Kong.

Arborescent or shrubby bamboos. Rhizomes leptomorph, with running underground stems. Culms diffuse, sometimes also clustering, erect to nodding; internodes substantially grooved above branches, initially usually pubescent; nodes prominent, sheath rings corky. Branches 3, rarely 5–7 at higher nodes, subequal, buds initially closed at front. Culm sheaths deciduous, setose; ligule serrate or entire; blade lanceolate. Leaves 3–9 per ultimate branch; blade lanceolate. Inflorescence fully bracteate, partially iterauctant, lateral, racemose, prophyllate. Spikelets 1–3, subtended by a prophyll and 2–more gradually enlarged bracts or glumes, apical 1–2 bracts usually with axillary buds, forming secondary pseudospikelets, lateral spikelets sessile, terminal spikelet variably pedicellate. Spikelets with several to many (up to 50) florets. Rachilla disarticulating between florets. Lemma leathery, apex acute; palea about as long as lemma or slightly shorter, 2-keeled, rounded at apex, ciliolate; lodicules 3, membranous, many-veined. Stamens 3, sometimes 2 or 4; filaments free. Ovary ellipsoidal; style 1, sometimes absent, usually long; stigmas 2–3, plumose. Fruit a caryopsis.

About ten species distributed in S and SW China, N Vietnam; introduced to Japan during the Tang Dynasty; ten species (nine endemic) in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Trees, rarely shrubs. Leaves alternate, exstipulate. Flowers small, usually clustered in leaf axils. Sepals 5 (or 6), imbricate. Corolla campanulate, tube short, lobes 5 (or 6), imbricate. Stamens 5 (or 6), inserted at throat and opposite to corolla-lobes; filaments reflexed at apex; anthers extrorsely or slightly latrorsely dehiscent; staminodes as many as corolla lobes and alternate to them, scale-like or petaloid. Ovary glabrous or villous, 5-locular, rarely 2– 4-locular; ovules 1 per locule. Fruit a berry, ovoid to globose; pericarp usually thick, sometimes fleshy; 1–(2–5)-seeded. Seed scar basal, sometimes lateral.

Four species distributed in S & SW China and N Vietnam; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Stems erect, basally woody, apical many‑branched. Leaves opposite, sessile or short petiolate; leaf blade pinnately parted or dissected. Racemes terminal; bracts foliaceous, parted to entire. Flowers opposite, sparse. Pedicel short. Bracteoles 2, linear. Calyx tube campanulate, 4–8 times longer than wide, membranous, 10‑veined; lobes 5, subequal, sublanceolate. Corolla tube slender, straight, as long as or slightly longer than calyx tube; limb 2‑lipped; lower lip as long as upper, 3‑lobed; lobes ovate‑triangular, subequal, apex acute, with two petaloid plaits; upper lip galeate, bowed. Stamens didynamous, slightly exserted. Ovary 2‑loculed. Style slightly exserted. Capsules black to black‑brown, enclosed by persistent calyx. Seeds numerous, oblong‑ovoid; seed coat reticulate, wing thick, fleshy, hyaline.

Four species distributed in Asia; two species in China and in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, unarmed. Bark thick and smooth. Leaves alternate, simple, entire, densely glandular-dotted. Inflorescence a terminal panicle. Flowers unisexual or polygamous, white or yellow. Calyx 4–5-lobed, margin ciliolate. Petals 4–5, imbricate, glandular-dotted, 2–4 times as long as sepals, reflexed at anthesis. Stamens 4–5, filaments distinct. Ovary 2–5-locular, ovule 1 per locule; style short; stigma capitate. Fruit a drupe, ovoid or subglobose, with 2–5 one-seeded stones. Seeds small, compressed ovoid, endosperm fleshy, embryo straight.

About 14 species distributed in SE Asia and neighbouring islands; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves simple, alternate, long petiolate, margin entire or serrate, pinnately veined; stipules caducous. Flowers usually bisexual, solitary or in clusters, axillary, long stalked. Sepals 4 –5, valvate or imbricate, slightly connate at base. Petals 4 –5, rarely absent, obovate, margin entire or laciniate at apex. Stamens many, inserted on disc; filaments short; anthers opening by apical pores or vertical slits, connective usually elongated and forming a beak. Disc broad, thick. Ovary 2–7-locular, pubescent; style free or connate; ovules several per locule. Capsule globose or ovoid, prickly, septicidally dehiscing into 3 –7 valves; exocarp woody, thick; endocarp thin, leathery. Seed(s) 1 to several, pendulous, usually arillate; endosperm fleshy, copious. Cotyledons flat.

About 120 species, mainly distributed in tropics and subtropics; 14 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Climbing woody vines or shrubs, rarely herbs, usually with short, thick rhizomes. Stems and branches usually prickly. Leaves alternate, in 2 ranks; petiole usually with an abscission zone, narrowly winged on both sides; tendrils often present; leaf blade usually ovate to lanceolate, main veins 3–7. Inflorescence axillary, an umbel or a panicle, raceme, or spike of umbels; peduncle sometimes with a scale like prophyll at base. Flowers small; tepals 6, often distinct. Male flowers: stamens 6, rarely more, inserted at base of tepals, filaments distinct, anthers basifixed, introrse. Female flowers: ovary 3-locular; ovules 1 or 2 per locule; style very short; stigmas 3; staminodes 0–6. Berries red to black, globose, usually 1–3-seeded.

About 300 species distributed in tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions of both hemispheres; 79 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs or subshrubs. Stipules scarious, long-ovate, medifixed, persistent; stipels absent. Leaves even-pinnate, rachis ending in a bristle, sensitive; leaflets 5–9 pairs, entire. Racemes or cymes axillary or terminal, more or less helicoids, sometimes flower solitary and axillary. Bracts small, caducous; bracteoles paired, sheathing at base of calyx, persistent. Calyx 2-lipped, lips subentire. Corolla exserted from calyx, yellow, blue or purple. Petals clawed; vexillum orbicular or oblong; wings and keels equal to vexillum; keel incurved, apex obtuse. Stamens diadelphous (5+5); anthers uniform. Ovary linear, 2–9-ovuled, styles incurved, stigma small, terminal. Pods compressed or turgid, consisting of several segments folded within persistent, accrescent calyx; segments suborbicular, indehiscent. Seeds reniform, smooth.

About 35 species distributed in tropical Africa and Asia; five species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs, climbers or soft‑wooded small trees, sometimes prickly. Leaves entire or irregularly toothed, lobed, or divided, rarely pinnately compound, alternate, solitary or in pairs, with a smaller one developed in the axil of the larger one. Flowers bisexual or andromonoecious, solitary, or more often in short racemes or cymes on lateral or leaf opposed peduncles, sometimes paniculate. Calyx 4–5‑lobed, persistent, sometimes enlarged in fruit. Corolla rotate or slightly cup‑shaped, 5‑angled or 5‑lobed; lobes folded in the bud. Stamens 4–5, attached to throat of corolla; filaments very short; anthers oblong or linear, erect and connivent in a cone round the style, opening at the top in 1 or 2 pores, without any prominent connective between the cells. Ovary 2(–5)‑locular, with numerous ovules on axile placenta; style simple, with small, obtuse stigma. Fruit a berry.

About 1200 species distributed mostly in tropical and subtropical regions; 41 species (about 20 introduced) in China; 12 species in Hong Kong (mostly cultivated or naturalized)

Perennial herbaceous vines, dioecious or monoecious; roots tuberous. Tendrils unbranched, glabrous. Leaves polymorphic, petiolate. Male flowers: arranged in umbels or corymbs; peduncles short; calyx tube campanulate, lobes 5, subulate; corolla yellow or yellowish white, 5-lobed, lobes triangular; stamens 3, filaments short, anthers globose, two 2-celled, one 1-celled, cells conduplicate or curved, connectives enlarged; pistillodes 3. Female flowers: solitary; calyx and corolla same as in male flowers; ovary ellipsoid, hairy; ovules several, horizontal; staminodes 3. Berries ellipsoid or ovoid, indehiscent. Seeds several, globose.

Two species distributed in Cambodia, India, Myanmar, Vietnam and China; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with rhizomes. Leaves alternate. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, arranged in racemes, panicles, corymbs or clustered as glomerules. Involucres subcampanulate; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, imbricate. Receptacle small, flat, alveolate. Marginal florets female, 1‑seriate, corolla ligulate, yellow in colour, rarely white. Disk florets bisexual, corolla tubular, trumpet‑shaped, the limb with 5 lobes; anther bases obtuse or subsagittate; stylar branches complanate, apical appendages lanceolate. All florets fertile; cypselae cylindric, distinctly 8–many‑ribbed; pappus setae slender, in 1 or 2 series.

Over 100 species native to temperate N hemisphere; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Small annual herbs. Leaves alternate, pinnatisect. Capitula heterogamous, disciform, sessile and axillary. Involucres dish‑like to hemispherical; phyllaries 2‑seriate, margin scarious. Receptacle convex or conical, naked. Outer florets in many series, female and fertile, corolla absent with the pistils only; style shortly branched. Central florets bisexual but usually infertile, corolla tubular, 3–4‑lobed at apex; anther bases obtuse; style usually capitate at tip. Cypselae of pistillate florets dorsiventrally compressed, margins with wings which extended to the apex, style persistent. Pappus absent.

Eight species native to America and Australia; one species naturalized in China; it also occurs as a weed in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial herbs. Radical leaves rosulate. Cauline leaves alternate, base usually auriculate and amplexicaul, margin entire, toothed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, often bearing callose hair or spines. Capitula homogamous, arranged as corymbs, corymbose panicles or pseudo‑umbels, usually pendulous after flowering stage. Involucres ovoid, campanulate, urceolate, cylindric or disciform; phyllaries 3–5‑seriate, imbricate, herbaceous or membranous, glabrous or glandular‑hairy, margin usually scarious. Receptacle plain, naked. Florets many, more than 80, all bisexual and fertile, corolla ligulate, yellow, ligule truncate and 3‑ or 5‑toothed apically; anther bases sagittate; stylar branches slender. Cypselae ovoid or ellipsoidal, rarely obconic, ribbed, horizontally rugose or smooth, apex without beaks. Pappus copious, many‑seriate, white, capillary and soft, entangled with each other.

About 50 species distributed in Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia and N America; eight species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, erect or creeping and rhizomatous. Branches usually quadrangular, winged or not. Leaves opposite or appearing verticillate due to the abbreviated internodes, petiolate or sessile, with 1–4 pairs of lateral primary veins or pinnately-veined. Inflorescences terminal or sometimes axillary, scorpioid cymose or subumbellate, pedunculate; bracts small, caducous. Flowers 3 (or 6)-merous. Calyx-tube tubular-campanulate, 3-ribbed, with trichomes. Calyx-lobes broadly triangular, small, very short. Petals pink, red, or purplish red, oblong-elliptic. Stamens 3 or 6, equal or unequal; filaments filiform; anthers opening by 1 or 2 pores, connective not inflated and usually without appendage. Ovary 3-locular, often crowned by membranous 3 – 6-lobed scales. Fruit capsular, obconical to cylindrical-obconical, more or less 3-edged.

About 150 species distributed in tropical regions of Asia; six species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs; bark flaky; trunk not buttressed, densely surrounded by thick, cone-shaped and upright pneumatophores; root subsurface at slight depth and radiating. Flowers solitary or 2 – 3 at the end of the branchlet. Calyx leathery, 4 – 8-lobed, often coloured inside. Petals narrow, vestigial or absent, caducous. Stigma capitate or peltate; style folded in bud. Stamens numerous and caducous; anthers reniform and small. Ovary superior. Fruits berry, globular. Seeds numerous, embedded in pulp.

About nine species in the genus (including 3 hybrid species), ranging from E Africa through Indo-Malay to tropical Australia and into Micronesia and Melanesia including the Hainan Island and Fujian Province of China; two native and one introduced species in China; two species in Hong Kong, both introduced. Kwok et al. (Hong Kong Biodiversity, Issue No. 10: 9–12. 2005) provided a report of the Sonneratia species and their situation in Hong Kong SAR.

Trees, shrubs, or rarely perennial herbs. Leaves odd-pinnate; leaflets numerous and small or few and larger; stipels setaceous or often absent. Flowers in terminal racemes or leafy panicles. Bracts linear, minute or absent; bracteoles often absent. Calyx-teeth short. Corolla white, yellow, or rarely blue-violet; vexillum broadly obovate or orbicular, erect or spreading, usually shorter (rarely longer) than keel; wings oblong, oblique; keel oblong, almost straight, overlapping or connate dorsally. Stamens 10, free, or rarely connate at base; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary shortly stipitate; ovules numerous; style incurved, stigma minute, terminal. Pods moniliform, terete or slightly compressed, fleshy to woody, indehiscent or opening very tardily by 2-valves. Seeds obovoid or globose, not strophiolate; cotyledons thick.

More than 70 species distributed in tropical to temperate regions; 21 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs or perennial, or subshrubs. Stems erect to ascending; branches opposite, rarely 3 in a whorl apically. Leaves opposite below, alternate above, or verticillate, narrow, often pinnatisect with linear or filiform segments. Flowers solitary and axillary, or in terminal racemes, shortly pedicellate; pedicels 2‑bracteolate. Calyx campanulate, or tubular, 5‑toothed or shortly 5‑lobed. Corolla pink, rose‑violet to white, cream or yellow, subrotate, with 5 subequal, usually entire lobes; tube short. Stamens 4, didynamous, not completely included; filaments short, curved; anthers at least one pair, connivent, 2‑celled, one cell fertile, poricidal, the others smaller, stipitate, empty. Ovary ovoid to globose. Stigma tongue‑shaped. Capsule ovoid or oblong, loculicidally 2‑valved; valves entire or 2‑fid. Seeds numerous, oblong or obovoid, testa reticulate.

About 40 species from Himalayas to Indochina, Indo‑Malaysia, New Guinea and Australia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms usually stout, erect. Leaf blades linear to linear-lanceolate; ligule a ciliate membrane. Inflorescence a large terminal panicle with elongate central axis; primary branches simple or branched, bearing short dense racemes of paired spikelets (one sessile, other short pedicellate, the uppermost pair forming a triad with a terminal spikelet, one sessile, two pedicellate); rachis internodes and pedicels linear, slender, ciliate. Sessile spikelet dorsally compressed; callus obtuse, bearded, inserted into internode apex; lower glume usually leathery, abaxial flat or convex, 2-keeled and winged upward; upper glume boat-shaped, keeled upward; lower floret reduced to an empty hyaline lemma; upper lemma oblong or oblong-lanceolate, entire and muticous or 2-lobed, awned from sinus or infrequently awnless; awn bigeniculate, glabrous; lodicules ciliate. Pedicellate spikelet well developed or reduced to a glume, usually much narrower than sessile spikelet, awnless.

About 30 species distributed worldwide in tropics and subtropics, temperate zones; five species in China and Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees. Leaves opposite, odd‑pinnately compound. Inflorescences terminal, dense, paniculate or racemose. Calyx large, spathaceous. Corolla broadly campanulate, orange‑red to bright red, tube shrunk at base, swollen at one side in middle; limb 5‑lobed, lobes unequal, corrugated. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted on corolla‑tube; filaments glabrous; anthers divergent. Disk annular. Ovary narrowly ovoid, 2‑locular, ovules many; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes lingulate. Capsules slender, flat, loculicidally dehiscing; valves subwoody. Seeds many, membranous winged.

One species distributed in tropical Africa; it is widely cultivated in S China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial perennial herbs, dormant in winter. Rhizomes compressed globose. Leaves linear, plicate-venose, appearing before the flowers. Scape emerging from a lateral bud of the rhizome, with basal scales; flowers bright yellow or purple; variations evident with the lip and column. Flowers medium-sized, in a loose terminal raceme; sepals and petals subequal, free, spreading; lip 3-lobed, attached to the base of the column, slightly saccate at the base, lateral lobes erect, rotundate at the apex, midlobe panduriform, with or without a tooth on each side at the base, the disk with 2 tuberculate-ridged calli near the sinus and a keel running from the calli toward the apex; column long, arcuate, winged near the apex and with or without horn-like appendages; clinandrium short, incurved; rostellum truncate; anthers terminal, incumbent, convex; pollinia 8, subequal, in 2 groups of 4 pairs, waxy, obovoid; viscidium triangular; ovary pubescent. Capsules oblong, with persistent perianth, prominently ridged.

About 46 species distributed in tropical Asia, Pacific islands and Australia; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Tall climbing shrubs, often tomentose. Stipules small, stipellate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate. Flowers small, numerous, in axillary or terminal panicles; bracts and bracteoles small, narrow. Calyx campanulate or tubular, 5-toothed, 2-lipped, the 2 upper teeth connate, apex entire or emarginate. Corolla rose, purple or white; vexillum ovate or suborbicular, obtuse, without appendages; wings obliquely oblong, free; keel almost straight, obtuse, shorter than wings; vexillary stamens free, remainder connate; anthers uniform. Ovary sessile or stipitate; ovules 2; style subulate or compressed, incurved, not barbate, stigma small, terminal. Pods subsessile or stipitate, broadly linear, often falcate, ± thickened and dehiscent at top, 1-seeded. Seeds flat, obovate, estrophiolate.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Asia; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or procumbent, ± swollen at nodes. Leaves decussate; stipules scarious, connate at base. Flowers bisexual, in racemose cymes. Sepals 5, free, green, with scarious margin. Petals 5, white or pink, entire. Stamens 2–5 or 10. Ovary 1-locular, with numerous ovules; styles 3. Capsules ovoid, opening by 3 valves.

About 25 species in N temperate regions; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, rarely subshrubs. Branches usually quadrangular. Leaves opposite, sessile or short-petiolate; stipules shortly sheathing, bordered with bristle‑like teeth. Flowers small, clustered in the axils of leaves or sometimes in terminal heads or cymes. Calyx‑tube obovate or obconical; limb 2–4(–5)‑lobed, often with small teeth between the lobes. Corolla funnel‑shaped or salverform; limb 4‑lobed; lobes spreading, valvate in the bud. Stamens 4, attached to the throat; anthers basifixed. Ovary 2‑locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; style slender; stigma capitate or 2‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, leathery or crustaceous, separating in 2 valves or only splitting near apex.

About 150 species widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; five species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs. Culms creeping and rooting at nodes. Leaf sheaths hairy, shorter than internode; leaf blades ovate, base amplexicaul, apex acute; ligule a line of hairs. Inflorescence terminal, an ovoid outlined small panicle. Spikelets ovate, 1-flowered; floret bisexual, easily falling from the joint of the pedicel; glumes hyaline membranous, glabrous; lower glume shorter, veinless, upper glume as long as spikelet or slightly shorter than spikelet, 1-veined; lemma and palea thinly membranous, lemma broad ovate, dorsally pubescent, 1-veined; palea equal to lemma; stamens 3; style penicillate. Caryopsis ovate.

One species distributed from India to S China and Malay Peninsula; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, without milky latex. Leaves alternate, entire. Flowers bisexual, sessile, in terminal and compact spikes, each flower subtended by a bract and 2 bracteoles. Calyx synsepalous, persistent; lobes 5, imbricate, connivent over the top of the ovary. Corolla regular, urceolate‑campanulate; lobes 5, imbricate. Stamens 5, attached to the base of corolla‑tube, alternate with the corolla‑lobes; filaments short; anthers 2‑celled, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary inferior or half‑inferior, bilocular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style very short; stigma capitate or indistinctly 2‑lobed. Fruit a membranous, circumscissile capsule; seeds numerous.

A small genus with only two species, one pantropical, one in W Africa; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs; stems erect or ascending. Leaves opposite, sometimes with the basal ones rosulate. Capitula heterogamous‑radiate or homogamous‑discoid, solitary, terminal to stem and branches, or axillary to upper leaves, bearing long peduncles. Involucres shallow‑dish‑like; phyllaries in 1–2 series. Receptacle cylindric‑conical; paleae cymbiform, enclosing the ovaries of disk florets. All florets fertile. Ray florets, when present, pistillate, 1‑seriate, corolla ligulate with apex 2–3‑lobed. Central florets hermaphrodite, many, corolla tubular and 4–5‑cleft apically; anther base obtuse, apex acute; stylar branches short and truncate. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, the marginal ones 3‑angled, the disk ones laterally compressed. Pappus none or with 1–2(–3) short awns.

About 60 species mainly native to tropical areas of America; two species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or biennial herbs. Leaves alternate, petiolate, usually triangular-ovate or hastate. Flowers unisexual, dioecious; male ones in terminal leafless spikes or panicles; female ones in axillary clusters. Male flowers: perianth deeply 4 – 5-lobed; stamens as many as perianth-lobes, exserted, without disc and rudimentary ovary. Female flowers: without perianth; ovary subglobose, within 2 connated bracteoles; stigmas 4–5, filiform. Utricles compressedglobose, enclosed within hardened bracteoles, unarmed or with 2–3 dorsal spines; pericarp membranaceous, adnated with seed testa. Seeds erect, albumen floury.

About three species; one species cultivated in China; it also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, dioecious or sometimes androdioecious. Culms tufted, stout, solid, with creeping and rooting stolons. Leaf blades hard, linear to subulate-involute, ± rigid; ligule a line of hairs. Inflorescence terminal, composed of many solitary racemes subtended by prophylls and spathate sheaths and condensed into a compact fascicle; male inflorescence with exserted racemes bearing several spikelets and ending in a short point; female or bisexual inflorescence stellately globose, falling entire, composed of many racemes reduced to a solitary basal spikelet hidden among subtending spathes, its rachis prolonged into a long needle-like spine. Spikelets ovateoblong, dorsally compressed; male spikelet herbaceous, few, alternate and dorsal in shallow cavities of rachis, deciduous with short pedicel, 2-floret, with shorter glumes; female spikelet papery, tardily deciduous as a whole at maturity, with glumes as long as spikelet or slightly shorter; lower lemma as long as spikelet, acute; upper lemma thicken papery, inrolled embraced same texture palea.

Four species distributed from India to SE Asia and Australia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Deciduous shrubs, unarmed. Leaves simple, alternate, usually shortly petiolate, serrate or incised-serrate, sometimes lobed, veins pinnate, rarely 3 – 5 from the base; stipules absent. Flowers arranged in umbels, umbel-like racemes, or contracted corymbs or panicles at apex of the new shoots, bisexual, rarely unisexual and polygamous, white or rose. Hypanthium campanulate or shortly turbinate. Sepals 5, valvate or slightly imbricate, usually shorter than hypanthium. Petals 5, white, rarely yellow or red, imbricate or contorted, usually longer than sepals. Stamens 15 to numerous, borne between disk and petals; anthers didymous. Disk annular, at the rim of the hypanthium, collar-shaped or lobed. Carpels (3– )5( –8), antepetalous, free; ovules 2– several per carpel, pendulous; styles terminal or subterminal; stigmas capitellate or disciform. Follicles bony, often dehiscent along the adaxial suture and at length splitting abaxially at the top. Seeds linear or oblong, testa membranous; endosperm thin or absent.

About 80 to 120 species in N temperate regions; 70 species in China; four species (three cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial caespitose herbs, lacking pseudobulbs. Leaves in a basal rosette. Inflorescence a spiral spike terminal to a stipe. Flowers compact; sepals free; petals narrow, hidden by dorsal sepal; lip sessile or clawed, concave, adnate to column; column terete, footless; clinandrium continued into rostellum, anther dorsal sessile; pollinia 2, with or without viscidium; stigma large, entire.

About 50 species distributed mainly in N America, only a few species found in S America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia; two species in China and Hong Kong.

Small aquatic herbs, free floating. Fronds flat or sometimes convex (gibbous) on abaxial surface, 1–10 cohering together, each with 5–21 roots, green and shining adaxially, often red abaxially, margin entire, with 2 lateral pouches at base, reproducing daughter fronds and flower; veins (5–)7–21, leaving from node towards apex, sometimes visible on upper surface. Daughter fronds connected to mother frond by thin white stipe. Flowers minute, male and female separate but within same small membranous spathe: stamens 2, anthers 4-celled; ovary 1-locular, 2-ovuled. Fruit globular, winged.

Two to four species distributed nearly worldwide; one species in China and Hong Kong

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms slender, tufted. Leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, often rigidly ciliate; ligule a line of hairs. Inflorescence a contracted or divaricate panicle, rarely spiciform. Spikelets with 1 bisexual floret, subterete or ± compressed, awnless, glabrous; rachilla disarticulating above glumes; glumes usually shorter than lemma, unequal, membranous, deciduous or persistent, 1-veined or veinless, apex obtuse, acute or acuminate; lemma elliptic to narrowly ovate, thinly membranous, 1–3-veined, glabrous, rounded on back; palea resembling lemma, with 2 close veins, often split deeply between the veins as grain grows. Stamens 2–3. Ovary glabrous; styles 2, free, short, stigmas plumose, exserted laterally. Grain globose to ellipsoidal, rounded or truncate, pericarp free, commonly swelling when wet and expelling the grain, which often adheres to spikelet apex.

Approximately 150 species distributed in the tropics and subtropics, extending into warm-temperate regions; eight species (one introduced) in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, rarely subshrubs, sometimes rhizomatous. Leaves simple, opposite, crenate or serrate. Verticillasters 2 – many‑flowered, forming terminal spikes. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 5‑ or 10‑veined; teeth 5, unequal, acute to bristle‑like, or spinescent. Corolla red, purple, yellow, or white, 2‑lipped; tube cylindric, usually villous annulate inside; upper lip ascending, concave; lower lip spreading, 3‑lobed, the middle lobe the largest, entire or emarginate. Stamens 4, subequal, ascending; anther cells 2, divaricate; filaments glabrous. Style 2‑fid, the lobes subequal. Nutlets ovoid to oblong, smooth or tuberculate, apex obtuse to rounded.

About 300 species widely distributed in Africa, Asia, Europe, N & S America; 18 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or shrubs. Stems and branches tetragonal, often pilose or glabrous. Branches usually forked. Leaves simple, opposite, rarely alternate, petiolate; leaf blade dentate or crenate, often rugose. Spikes terminal, usually long, lax; rachis often angular, excavated. Flowers ± immersed in excavated rachis when young. Calyx tubular, membranous, 4–5‑dentate. Corolla white, blue, pale red, slender, cylindric; tube often curved, ± villous in throat; lobes 5, equal or slightly unequal, spreading. Stamens 2, fertile, inserted on distal part of corolla tube, inclusive; thecae divaricate. Ovary supported by a short ring‑like disk, 2‑locular; ovules 1 per locule. Style exserted. Stigma capitate. Capsules enclosed by persistent calyx, splitting into two 1‑seeded nutlets.

About 65 species distributed in tropical America, a few species introduced into the Old World; one species as naturalized weed in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Evergreen twining shrubs, glabrous. Leaves digitate, long-petioled; leaflets 3 –7(–9), entire, stalked. Flowers functionally unisexual (plants monoeious), in few-flowered axillary racemes. Sepals 6, petaloid, outer 3 often ovate or lanceolate, apex acuminate, inner 3 smaller. Petals lacking, or rarely represented by nectaries. Male flower: stamens 6; filaments connate into a tube; vestigial carpels small. Female flower: staminodes 6, small; carpels 3, free, conduplicate; with many ovules on parietal placenta; stigmas sessile, capitate. Fruit an indehiscent pod-like berry. Seeds numerous, black, in several rows.

About 13 species distributed from Myanmar through Indochina and China to Korea and Japan; 12 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or small undershrubs. Leaves opposite, petiolate or sessile, entire or nearly so. Flowers usually arranged in racemes or spikes, terminal or axillary. Bracts spirally arranged, leaf‑like or spathulate; bracteoles spathulate or linear, slightly smaller than bracts. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate or lanceolate‑linear, equal or unequal, persistent. Corolla with short cylindric basal tube, campanulate, 5‑lobed; lobes subequal, patent. Stamens 4, didynamous, included or anterior pair slightly exserted; filaments usually hairy, rarely glabrous; anthers 2‑thecous; thecae parallel, equal, or rarely unequal; staminodes small or absent. Ovary oblong or spherical, glabrous or nearly so, ovules several per locule, arranged in 2 or 4 rows; style glabrous, filiform; stigma 2‑lobed, sometimes repeatedly 2‑lobed. Capsule oblong, retinacula absent. Seeds many, small, subspherical or cuboidal.

About 80 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the world; 14 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or prostrate. Leaves broad and flat, rarely subulate. Flowers bisexual, in terminal dichotomous cymes, rarely solitary in axils of leaves. Sepals 5, rarely 4. Petals 5, rarely 4, white, or rarely green, bifid, rarely retuse or with more lobes. Stamens 10, sometimes fewer (8, or 2–5). Ovary 1-locular, rarely 3-locular when young; ovules many, but only 1–2 developed; styles 3, rarely 2. Capsule globose or ovoid, opening at the top into twice as many teeth as there are styles.

About 120 species widely spread over temperate and cold regions; 64 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial twining or creeping herbs, rarely subshrubs. Roots tufted, tuberous, fusiform, fleshy. Leaves whorled, opposite, or alternate, petiolate. Inflorescence axillary, racemose or 1–3 in clusters, sometimes borne on petiole or leaf midvein. Bracts subulate or lanceolate. Perianth segments subequal, lanceolate. Stamens erect, inserted at base of perianth segments; filaments distinct or ± connate at base; anthers basifixed, apex often adaxially appendaged; connective extended into a perianth-like, linearlanceolate, long appendage. Ovary superior; ovules basally attached to placenta, style absent. Capsule ovoid to ellipsoidal. Seeds erect, ellipsoidal, longitudinally ribbed; funicle bearded.

About 27 species distributed in Asia, Australia; seven species (five endemic) in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennials, stoloniferous. Leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, obtuse or acute; ligule ciliate. Inflorescence of very short racemes bearing a few sessile spikelets; racemes arranged singly and sunk in pockets on one or both sides of a foliaceous or corky axis, raceme rachis ending in a point. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, sessile or short pedicellate, alternating; glumes unequal, membranous, lower lemma small; upper lemma subequal to spikelet; lower floret staminate or neuter, lemma as long as the spikelet, usually coriaceous, rarely papery, smooth, acute; palea membranous, stamen present or not; upper lemma slightly shorter than lower lemma, indurate, smooth, inrolled embraced same texture palea.

Seven species distributed in tropical and subtropical coastal regions from the Indian Ocean to SE Asia and the Pacific Ocean; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbaceous or woody vines, often with tuberous roots. Leaves mostly peltate, long-petioled and palmately nerved. Flowers in axillary umbels or condensed to discoid heads. Male flowers: sepals (4–)6–8, in 2 series, free or occasionally connate at base; petals 3–4, in 1 series, shorter than the sepals; stamens 2–6, united in a central column, bearing a flat disc with the anthers on the margin. Female flowers: sepals (1–)3–4, in 1 series; petals as many; carpel solitary, style very short, lobed or fimbriate. Drupes flattened, the scar of the style near the base; kernel horseshoe-shaped, dorsally tuberculous.

About 40 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; about 30 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves undivided and pinnately veined, or palmately lobed or digitate. Inflorescence paniculate or racemose, axillary. Flowers unisexual, monoecious or polygamous, the terminal mostly female and more precocious; calyx (4–)5-fid or -parted, often more or less petaloid; petals absent; staminal column with 15–10-anthers at apex. Carpels 5, partly free, 2–many-ovuled; style peltate or lobed at apex. Ripe carpels free, stellately spreading, follicules dehiscent soon. Seeds with endosperm.

About 150 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in tropical Asia; 23 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, evergreen or deciduous. Winter buds laterally compressed; bud scales 1 to several, imbricate. Leaves alternate, shortpetioled, serrate. Flowers axillary, solitary or several arranged in a short raceme, pedicellate; bracteoles 2, persistent or rarely caducous; sepals 5, persistent, imbricate, basally connate; petals 5, imbricate, slightly connate at base; stamens many, basally connate into a short tube and adnate to petals; anthers dorsifixed; ovary superior, 5-locular with 2– 4(–7) ovules per locule; styles connate or free. Capsule ovoid and wraped by persistent sepals, 5-ribbed, 5-locular with (1–)2– 4 seeds per locule, loculicidally dehiscent into 5 valves, central axis abortive, apex rostrate. Seeds compressed, usually narrowly winged.

About 20 species disjunctly distributed in E Asia and N America; 15 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, or with a woody trunk. Leaves in two ranks, basal or crowded towards apex of stem, long petiolate; leaf blade oblong, entire. Inflorescences axillary, with 1–2 spathe-bracts, each enveloping a few-flowered helicoid cyme. Flowers bisexual, very irregular; sepals 3, white or yellow, narrow-lanceolate and long-pointed, much projecting; petals 3, white or blue, the middle one small, the other 2 connivent to form an arrow-shaped organ and enveloping the stamens in a groove; stamens 5, filaments slender; anthers linear, opening by longitudinal slits; ovary 3-locular, style 3-branched; ovules many. Capsule 3-angled, loculicidal.

Four species native to S Africa; two species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Herbs, parasitic on roots. Leaves opposite below, alternate above, narrow, sometimes reduced to scales. Flowers axillary, solitary or in spikes, usually with a pair of bracteoles. Calyx tubular, conspicuously 5–15‑ribbed, limb 5‑lobed. Corolla salverform; tube curved; limb patent, weakly 2‑lipped; lower lip 3‑lobed; upper lip shorter than lower lip, usually emarginate or 2‑fid. Stamens 4, didynamous. Anthers 1‑celled, apex pointed, stigma clavate. Capsules loculicidally 2‑valved. Seeds numerous, ovoid to oblong; testa reticulate.

About 20 species distributed in Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia, Oceania; four species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs, shrubs or small trees, some species gregarious and monocarpic. Stems usually quadrangular, becoming woody and hollow in age. Leaves in opposite pairs, often unequal in size, petiolate or sessile, serrate, serrulate, or entire, usually with prominent cystoliths on adaxial surface. Flowers in axillary and terminal spike (sometimes distantly one‑sided), bracteate heads, head‑like clustered, or less commonly in pedicellate opened panicle. Bracts usually distant from the leaves, persistent or deciduous as flowers open, very varied in size and shape, sometimes of two types in species with a capitate inflorescence (with barren outer bracts differing from inner flower‑bearing ones); bracteoles usually linear, sometimes absent. Calyx 5‑lobed to the base; the lobes nearly equal, or with the middle lobe distantly longer than others, or fused into bipartite or tripartite, valvate. Corolla tubular or funnel‑shaped, blue, white, yellow or pink, the tube either gradually widened from the base or narrowly cylindric and abruptly widened, campanulate or gibbous; limb 5‑lobed, lobes equal or subequal, usually ovate, spreading, valvate in buds. Stamens 4, didynamous and basally monadelphous, included or exserted, two filaments distantly longer than other two, or sometimes 2(–5); anthers 2‑celled, the cells oblong, parallel, muticous, glabrous or bearded at one end; pollen spherical and echinulate or ellipsoidal and variously ribbed; staminodes 1, or 2, or absent. Ovary oblong‑globular, 2‑locular with 2–8 ovules in each; styles long, filiform, slender, simple, sometimes persistent after the corolla falls; stigma with one obsolete lobe. Capsule oblong or elliptic, 2–16‑seeded, apically pubescent or glabrous; retinacula strong, curved. Seeds flattened, usually elliptic, glabrous or appressed hairy, sometimes with a distant areola.

About 400 species distributed in tropical Asia; about 100 species in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with rhizomes. Stems erect or absent. Leaves distichous, long-petiolate. Inflorescence a raceme or panicle, rachis often zigzag; bracts often brightly coloured and caducous; bracteoles absent or scale-like. Sepals 3, free. Corolla tube short; outer staminodes 2 or absent, cucullate staminode with auricle, callose staminode broader, apex slightly emarginate; fertile stamen with appendage. Ovary 1-locular, smooth or warty. Fruit a capsule; seeds arillate.

Ten to 15 species spreading over the humid American tropics, but concentrated in C America and SE Brazil; one species introduced in China and Hong Kong.

Lianas or erect or stolon‑bearing shrubs, rarely trees, with latex. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3. Cymes mostly dichasial, terminal, pedunculate or sessile. Flowers large. Sepals free or connate at base, imbricate or quincuncial, basal glands 5 – many. Corolla funnelform, usually turning darker and dark streaked at anthesis; tube short, throat wide; lobes overlapping and mostly twisted to right, distal portions mostly forming filiform, involute long tails; corona 10‑lobed, inserted at base of corolla‑lobes. Stamens inserted at apex of corolla‑tube; filaments short; anthers sagittate, connivent, adherent to pistil head, spurred at base; disk absent. Ovary of 2 separate carpels, often partly connate at base; ovules numerous in each carpel. Style filiform. Fruit of 2 divaricate follicles, connate at the base. Seeds numerous, with beaked apical coma.

About 38 species distributed in tropical Africa, Asia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs, trees, or woody lianas, armed or unarmed; lianas with axillary simple or double curled tendrils, sometimes with axillary thorns. Stipules often reduced to a straight ciliate ridge connecting petiole bases. Leaves petiolate to sometimes subsessile; leaf blade margin entire, basal veins 3–7, secondary veins 1–3 distinct pairs from or near base curved along margin in species represented. Inflorescences terminal and/or axillary, thyrsoid; bracts scale‑like to sepal‑like. Flowers pedicellate or sessile, 4‑ or 5‑merous. Corolla rotate to salverform; lobes valvate in bud, spreading to reflexed when open. Stamens inserted at corolla throat to middle of corolla tube, exserted to included; filaments long to short, mostly filiform; anthers orbicular to narrowly oblong, base mostly slightly 2‑cleft, introrse, 2‑celled and separate. Ovary (1–)2‑locular, with few to many ovules per locule. Style cylindric; stigma capitate of faintly 2‑cleft. Berries orange or red when ripe in species represented, usually globose to ellipsoidal, thin to thick walled, outside smooth to minutely warty, glabrous; pulp fleshy, usually orange; 1 –15‑seeded.
