Seeds ± flattened to saucer‑shaped, circular to elliptic in outline; seed coat sericeous, felty, or scabrous and glabrous; embryo spatulate; endosperm horny; cotyledon leaflike.

About 190 species in tropics and subtropics; 11 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, annual or perennial, often covered with glandular hairs. Leaves alternate, simple, cauline or in a basal rosette. Inflorescences a cyme, raceme, or lax spike, terminal. Flowers perfect, zygomorphic. Calyx with anterior 2 lobes often connate into a shallowly 2‑lobed segment. Corolla irregular, lobes distinct or 2 or 4 connate, anterior one small and reflexed; corona often present, formed by glandular appendix at throat. Stamens at lateral sides, completely adnate with style, forming a long gynostemium usually exserted from corolla, bent and irritable, base movable; anthers sessile, just below stigma. Ovary 2‑locular or partially 1‑locular; ovules numerous.

About 120 species in Australia (where most species occur) and tropical Asia (eight species, four endemic to Asia); two species in S China and in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, stellate pubescent or scaly, rarely glabrous; bud-scales absent. Leaves usually alternate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemose, paniculate, or cymose, sometimes 1-flowered or several-flowered in a fascicle; bracteoles small, caducous. Flowers bisexual; pedicels not articulate; calyx cup-shaped, 5-toothed, rarely 2– 6-lobed or truncate; corolla campanulate, lobes 5 –7, imbricate or valvate; stamens 10, rare 8 –9 or 11–13, attached high on corolla tube; filaments flattened; anthers oblong; ovary superior, 3-locular when young, becoming 1-locular; ovules 1–many per locule, placentation parietal; style subulate or filiform; stigma capitate or 3-lobed. Fruit a drupe, indehiscent or dehiscing by 3 valves, exocarp fleshy to dry. Seeds 1–3; seed-coat thick, with a large basal hilum; endosperm fleshy or almost bony; embryo straight.

About 130 species disjunctly distributed in E Asia and America, Mediterranean; 31 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Annual herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Leaves sessile, usually terete or semi-terete, fleshy, entire. Inflorescences axillary, clustered or flowers solitary. Flower bisexual or pistillate, subtended by 3 bracteoles; perianth subglobose, lobes 5, free or connate to middle, often with winged, or horn-like projection when fruiting. Stamens 5, filaments short. Ovary globose, stigmas 2–5. Utricles enclosed by or sometimes adnate to perianth; pericarp membranaceous, free to seed. Seed 1, horizontal or vertical, seed coat crustaceous or membranaceous.

About 100 species distributed worldwide; 20 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Small to large trees, monoecious, unarmed or armed. Stems solitary or clustered, tall or short, sometimes subterranean, with rough rings of leaf scars. Leaves pinnate, reduplicate, recurved; pinnae few to many, regularly or irregularly arranged, in 1 or several planes, linear, single-fold; sheaths open, fibrous. Inflorescences interfoliar, branched 1 order, rarely spicate, much shorter than leaves; prophyll tubular, 2-keeled; peduncular bracts much longer than prophyll, enclosing the inflorescences until flowering, often spindle-shaped before split; peduncles usually longer than rachis, glabrous or hairy, rachillae few or many, usually zigzagged. Flowers unisexual, in triads of 2 male with 1 central female, paired or solitary male flowers distally; male flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 6, anthers elongate, pistillodes minute; female flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, staminodes membranous, ringed, 6-teethed, ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule. Fruits globose, ovoid or ellipsoidal; green, brown, yellow or reddish; epicarp smooth, longitudinally striate, mesocarp fleshy or dry, fibrous, endocarp thick, woody, with 3 germinating pores near base. Seed 1(–2), endosperm homogeneous or ruminate.

About 31 species in S America, from Venezuela southwards to Argentina; one species cultivated for ornamental in S China and Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Annual erect herbs; stem pubescent to pilose, branches and leaves both opposite. Leaves toothed and with winged petiole. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, sessile or shortly pedunculate, usually with several heads aggregated on axils and branch terminals. Involucres ovoid‑oblong; phyllaries few, outer ones foliaceous, inner ones scarious and narrower, subtending the ray florets. Receptacle small; paleae scarious, subtending the disk florets. All florets fertile. Marginal florets female, corolla ligulate, limb short and apically 2–3‑toothed. Disk florets bisexual, corolla tubular, apices shallowly 4‑lobed; anthers 4, apex rounded, base entire or shortly bifid, truncate or shortly sagittate; stylar branches slender, hairy and acute. Cypselae of ray florets dorsiventrally compressed, margin with broad lacerate hard wings; pappus two sharp and stiff spines at apex. Cypselae of disk florets narrower, oblong‑cuneate, flat or subtrigonous, not winged, usually tuberculate; pappus 2–4 stiff spines at summit.

About 50 species native to America and Africa, one species commonly distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.

Trees or shrubs. Branchlets sometimes 2–4-angulate, usually glabrous. Leaves opposite or sometimes whorled, rarely alternate, petiolate to subsessile, pinnately-veined, with conspicuous glands. Inflorescence a thyrse, composed of 3–many-flowered cymes, terminal or axillary; bracts small, deciduous after flowering. Flowers stipitate or not. Hypanthium obconic or sometimes clavate. Calyx lobes 4–5 or rarely more, usually short, caducous or persistent. Petals 4 – 5 or rarely more, distinct or united into a calyptra. Stamens many, distinct, rarely slightly connate at base; anthers minute, versatile, 2-celled; cells parallel, dehiscing longitudinally; connectives usually terminating in an apical gland. Ovary inferior, 2–3-locular; ovules many per locule. Style linear. Fruit drupaceous, 1(or 2)-seeded. Seeds often with a pseudotesta ± adhering to pericarp; embryo straight; cotyledons thick, adhering in a mass.

About 500 species mainly distributed in tropical Asia, with a few in Australia and Africa; 77 species in China; nine species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs to large trees. Leaves palmate or simple; leaflets 3 – 9, entire or toothed. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, sometimes reduced to a few‑flowered raceme or single flower. Calyx cup‑shaped, campanulate or tubular, truncate or 2‑lipped to slightly 5‑lobed. Corolla tubular to funnel‑shaped or campanulate, hairless or hairy on outside of tube. Stamens sometimes projecting. Fruit a linear to oblong capsule, dehiscing perpendicular to the septum.

About 100 species distributed from Mexico to N Argentina; three species introduced into China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, latex white. Stems repeatedly dichotomously branched. Leaves opposite; adaxial surface of petiole often with a basal semicircular or semiamplexicaul ocrea. Cymes corymbose or umbellate, at branch forks, (1‑ or) many‑flowered. Calyx divided to middle or deeper, mostly with few to many basal glands inside. Corolla salverform, widened at or near middle; lobes sharply overlapping to left (or right). Stamens inserted at widened part of corolla‑tube; filaments short or almost none; anthers oblong or narrowly triangular, free from pistil head, base sagittate or deeply cordate and not spurred; disk none. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a commom style; ovules numerous; style filiform; pistil head of a subglobose or lampshade‑shaped basal part and stigmoid, 2‑cleft apical part. Fruit of paired, divaricate follicles. Seeds with a red or orange fleshy aril; coma absent.

About 99 species distributed in Africa, Asia, N America, Pacific islands, S America; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Subshrubs or shrubs. Stipules free or connate. Leaves 1-foliolate, stipulate; petioles winged. Racemes terminal and axillary, usually 2–3-flowered at a node. Bracts dimorphic; bracteoles present or absent. Calyx campanulate, 5-lobed; upper 2 lobes minutely 2-toothed or sometimes entire at apex. Petals with well developed veins; vexillum orbicular to transversely broadly elliptic or obovate; wings elliptic oblong, longer than keel, rounded at apex, conspicuously auriculate like an appendage at base of lamina, claw broad; keel acute or obtuse at apex. Stamens 10, diadelphous. Ovary sessile, with distinct disk around base, pubescent, 5–8-ovuled; styles glabrous; stigma capitate. Pods exserted, straight or slightly incurved, compressed, narrowly oblong, usually 5–8-segmented, ventral sutures nearly straight or slightly undulate, dorsal sutures shallowly to deeply constricted. Seeds transversely broadly to transversely elliptic, rim-arillate, concave at hilum.

Six species distributed in tropical Asia, Pacific Islands, New Caledonia and N Australia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual aromatic herbs. Stem erect and branched, glabrous. Leaves opposite or alternate, mostly pinnate or pinnatifid, glandular‑dotted. Capitula solitary or arranged as corymbs, heterogamous and radiate, pedunculate. Involucres with 3–10 phyllaries in 1 series and united into a cylindric‑campanulate tube with triangular teeth free on top, glandular‑dotted. Receptacle flat, glabrous. Florets yellow, orange to red, all fertile. Marginal ligulate florets in 1 row, or several‑seriate in some cultivated form, female. Disk tubular florets bisexual, corolla 5‑lobed; stylar branches hairy near the apices. Cypselae linear to linear‑oblong, angulate or compressed. Pappus several unequal scales, some awned.

About 30 species native to C and S America; two to three species cultivated commonly in China and in Hong Kong.

Tagetes tenuifolia Cav. (細葉萬壽菊) was also cultivated previously.

Terrestrial perennial herbs with slender erect pseudobulbs. Rhizomes short and stout, the internodes thicker than long. Leaves solitary, 1 terminal to each pseudobulb, petiolate, linear-lanceolate. Scape emerging from the side of a pseudobulb, aphyllous, slender and long, with several sheaths at the base. Flowers medium-sized, resupinate, in a well-spaced raceme; sepals subequal, spreading, the odd one free, the lateral ones adnate to the short foot of the column forming a mentum; petals narrower than the sepals; lip attached to the apex of the column foot, slightly gibbous at the base, 3-lobed, the lateral lobes erect, parallel to the column, the apex obtuse, the midlobe suborbicular, entire, disk lamellate; column slender, slightly oblique, dentate; rostellum truncate; anther terminal incumbent, convex, bicornute; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, 2-seriate, waxy, laterally compressed; stigma suborbicular, concave; ovary oblong-obovoid, striate-sulcate. Capsules ellipsoidal, rostrate.

About 13 species distributed from E Himalaya, China, Japan, Indochina and adjacent islands; 11 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs or subshrubs, more or less succulent. Stems erect, glabrous. Leaves alternate or sub-opposite, flat, entire. Stipules none. Flowers small, in terminal panicles, racemes or cymes, rarely solitary and axillary. Sepals 2, free or connate at base, usually caducous. Petals 5, rarely more (8–10), red, often caducous. Stamens 5 to many (10–30), usually adherent to base of petals. Ovary superior, 1-locular; ovules many on a free central placenta; style usually 3- lobed. Capsule globose or ovoid, opening by 2–3 valves.

About 50 species mainly in N and C America; one species naturalized in S China and Hong Kong.

Trees. Leaves paripinnate, alternate. Stipules small, caducous. Inflorescenes terminal, racemose or narrowly paniculate. Bracts and bracteoles ovate-oblong, colourful, usually caducous. Calyx-tube narrowly turbinate, 4-lobed; lobes imbricate. Petals only posterior 3 developed, subequal, anterior 2 small, scale-like, included in the base of staminal tube. Fertile stamens 3, connate into an upcurved tube or sheath at the lower half; filaments short, anthers dorsifixed; staminodes spinose-hairy, inserted at apex of staminal tube. Ovary stipitate, stipe adnate to calyx-tube, ovules many; styles elongated, stigmas capitate. Pods long cylindrical, indehiscent, exocarp thin, rigid, mesocarp thick and fleshy, endocarp thinly membranous, with septum between seeds. Seeds oblique rectangular or oblique ovate, compressed. Cotyledons thick, fleshy; embryo basal, erect.

One species native to Africa, cultivated in tropical regions of the world; it is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

Deciduous small trees or shrubs, multi-branched; branches terete, slender. Leaves minute, scalelike, alternate, sessile, amplexicaul or sheathing at base, with salt glands; stipules absent. Flowers small, bisexual, white or pale red, short pedicelled or sessile, arranged in spikes or panicles. Calyx non-fleshy or fleshy, 4 –5-lobed, persistent. Petals isomerous with calyx lobes, deciduous or persistent. Stamens 4–5, opposite to petals, anthers extrorse, apex apiculate. Pistil 1, composed of 3 – 4 carpels; ovary superior, surrounded by more or less lobed disc, 1-locular, ovules many; styles 3 – 4; stigmas short, capitate. Capsule conical, dehiscing into 3 –5 valves; seeds many, minute, apex with a bundle of hair.

About 90 species, distributed in Asia, N Africa, S Africa and Europe; 18 species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial lactiferous and acaulescent herbs, scapes erect and hollow. Leaves all radical, rosulate at base, shape spatulate, oblanceolate to lanceolate, pinnatilobed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, rarely entire. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate, hermaphrodite and fertile, solitary and terminal to scape. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries herbaceous, abaxial side sometimes with thickened or horn‑like structure near the apex, outer layers short, in 2–3 rows, reflexed or adpressed at anthesis; inner layers longer, in single row, erect. Receptacle flat, naked, seldom with paleae. Ligulate florets many, corolla yellow, rarely white, red or purple‑red, apex truncate and 5‑toothed; anther bases sagittate, bearing apical appendages; style branches slender, linear and obtuse. Cypselae fusiform or obovate‑oblong, 5–10‑ribbed, acutely to obtusely tuberculate, apex attenuate to form filiform beak. Pappus copious, growing on the beak‑like a parachute, capillary, length unequal, persistent. Upon fruiting stage, the whole involucre reflexed and the seeds arranged as globular head exposing to the wind.

About 2000 species native to temperate and subtropical regions, mainly distributed in the N hemisphere; about 70 species in China; one species naturalized in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite, petiolate. Stipules interpetiolar, entire, pointed with a broad base, deciduous. Flowers usually numerous, in terminal broad or corymbiform cymes. Calyx‑tube various; limb short, 5‑toothed. Corolla funnel‑shaped or salverform; tube cylindric; lobes (4–)5, spreading or recurved, contorted in the bud. Stamens as many as corolla‑lobes, attached to the throat; filaments very short or absent; anthers dorsifixed. Ovary 2‑locular, usually with numerous, or seldom (1–)2 ovules in each locule; style long, slightly thickened at the top, undivided. Fruit a globular berry, leathery or fleshy, 1 – many‑seeded.

About 370 species in tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia and tropical Africa; 17 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Tarenna brevicymigera W. C. Chen (Acta Bot. Austro Sinica, 3: 26. 1986; type locality: Vietnam) was once reported from Lamma Island (F. W. Xing 8623).

Parasitic shrubs; young branchlets and leaves usually tomentose. Leaves opposite or alternate, pinnately-veined. Inflorescences axillary, umbellate or rarely racemose, 2–5-flowered; each flower usually subtended by one scale-like bract. Flowers bisexual, 4–5-merous, zygomorphic. Calyx ellipsoidal or ovoid, rarely subglobose, base rounded, limb annular, entire or denticulate, persistent. Mature flower bud tubular, tip ellipsoidal or ovoid. Corolla sympetalous, slightly curved, basal portion ± inflated, split along one side at anthesis, lobes all reflexed toward the side away from the split. Stamens inserted at base of corolla lobes; filaments short; anthers 4-celled, sometimes with septum. Ovary 1-locular; placentation basal. Style filiform, 4–5-angled; stigma usually capitate. Fruit a berry, ellipsoidal or ovoid, rarely globose, exocarp leathery, verrucose or granular, rarely smooth, pubescent or glabrous, base rounded. Seed 1.

About 25 species distributed in S and SE Asia; 18 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous or semievergreen trees, monoecious; main branches persistent; lateral branches alternate and deciduous in winter; winter buds globose, small. Leaves spirally arranged, base decurrent,dimorphic: subulate leaves on main branches persistent; linear leaves on lateral branchlets deciduous together with branchlet as a unit, 2-ranked. Pollen cones terminal, in long, pendulous, catkinlike racemes or panicles; microsporophylls 6–many, spirally arranged; pollen sacs 4–9. Seed cones solitary, attached laterally by minute peduncle to apex of previous year's growth, globose or ellipsoid but faceted; bracts scales almost completely connate with its cone scale but with free, protruding, triangular, acute apex; ovules 2 per bract axil; cone scales shield-shaped, woody at maturity, apex irregularly quadrangular. Seeds 2 per cone scale, irregularly triquetrous, large, strongly keeled, wingless. Cotyledons 4–9.

Two species in Guatemala, Mexico, United States; both introduced in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, erect or scandent. Stems often hairy. Leaves opposite, usually simple, 3‑foliolate or odd‑pinnately compound; leaflets serrate at margin. Inflorescences terminal, paniculate or racemose. Calyx campanulate, 5‑lobed. Corolla tubular or funnelform, slightly curved, bilabiate. Fertile stamens 4, exserted, thecae pendulous, divergent. Ovary 2‑locular; ovules many per locule. Disk cupular. Capsule linear, compressed, loculicidal. Seeds winged.

About 14 species distributed in tropical Africa and tropical America; two species introduced to China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Deciduous tall trees. Branchlets stellate hairy. Leaves simple, large, opposite or whorled, entire, petiolate. Panicles terminal, with many dichotomous cymes. Bracts small, narrow, caducous. Calyx campanulate, tube short, lobes spreading, limb 5–6‑lobed, enlarged in fruit. Corolla‑tube short, limb 5–6‑lobed, lobes revolute. Stamens 5 or 6, inserted on apical part of tube, exserted; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary 4‑locular; ovule 1 per locule. Stigma 2‑cleft. Fruit enclosed in enlarged persistent calyx, endocarp bony, exocarp thin. Seeds ellipsoidal.

About three species distributed in India, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Philippines; one species introduced and sometimes naturalized in tropical and subtropical China; it is cultivated in Hong Kong.

Lianas, with white latex. Leaves opposite, long‑petiolate. Cymes extra‑axillary, pendulous, rachis laxly branched. Calyx with 5 glands at base. Corolla‑tube cylindric with enlarged base, throat sometimes constricted; lobes 5, patent, twisted to right. Corona‑lobes 5, adnate to base of staminal tube, margin and apex free, erect, oblong, obtuse, with ligulate inner lobes adnate to near apex, or corona‑lobes notched. Stamens 5, attached to the base of corolla; filaments connate into a tube; membranous anther appendages incurved; pollinia 1 in each cell, oblong, erect. Ovary of 2 separate carpels; style short; stigma head convex or conical. Follicles thick, acuminate, smooth. Seeds comose.

About ten species distributed in Asia, Oceania and tropical Africa; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrublets, or shrubs. Stipules present; stipels absent. Leaves odd-pinnate; leaflets opposite, entire, often silky hairy abaxially. Racemes terminal, leaf-opposed, or axillary. Bracts present; bracteoles absent. Flowers paired or clustered at nodes of rachis. Calyx campanulate, 5-toothed, teeth or lobes subequal or the upper 2 more connate. Corolla red, purple or white; petals clawed; vexillum suborbicular, hairy abaxially; wings obliquely obovate or oblong, slightly adherent to keel; keel incurved. Stamens diadelphous. Anthers uniform. Ovary sessile, with many ovules; styles upcurved; stigma capitate. Pods linear or oblong, compressed, 2-valved, not septate between seeds, tip beaked. Seeds oblong, sometimes with a small strophiole.

About 400 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, mostly in Africa; 11 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees with buttress, rarely shrubs. Leaves often alternate, usually pseudoverticillate on branch apex, rarely opposite or subopposite, usually with 2 or more glands at the base of leaf blade. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, spicate or racemose, sometimes paniculate. Flowers small, (4–)5-merous, bisexual or polygamous; bracts deciduous. Calyx-tube cupular, prolonged beyond ovary, lobes 4 or 5, valvate; petals absent; stamens 8 or 10, in 2 whorls, anthers dorsifixed. Disk bearded or villous, rarely glabrous or subglabrous. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; ovules 2(–4); style 1. Fruit drupaceous, with 2–5 ribs or leathery wings. Seed 1; endosperm lacking, cotyledons convolute.

About 200 species distributed in tropical regions of the world; eight species in China; four species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, often crowded towards apex of branchlets, entire, rarely serrate, petiolate. Flowers usually hermaphrodite, or polygamo-dioecious, borne below expanded leaves, solitary or frequently in a cluster, pedicellate; bracteoles 2, deciduous or persistent, alternate or nearly opposite; sepals 5, persistent or rarely deciduous, imbricate, margin glandular dentate, more or less connate at the base; petals 5, imbricate, slightly connate at the base; stamens 30 – 50, 2(–many) seriate; filaments adnate to base of petals; anthers basifixed, glabrous. Ovary superior, 1–3-locular, or 4 – 6-locular with false septae, 1–20 ovules per locule; style simple, stigma 2–3-lobed. Fruit baccate, indehiscent or irregularly dehiscent. Seeds reniform, slightly compressed, red arillate; endosperm abundent.

About 90 species in tropical and subtropical Asia, Central and S America, and Africa; 13 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen shrubs or lianas. Leaves simple, entire or serrate, often scabrid on one or both sides; petioles short, furrowed. Panicles axillary or terminal, few to many-flowered. Flowers actinomorphic, hermaphrodite; sepals 4– 5, persistent, often reflexed in fruit; petals 3 – 5, with emarginated apex, whitish or slightly reddish; stamens numerous, dilated at distal end, with long filament and short thecae along rhomboid receptacle; carpels 1– 4, free, with 4 –20 ovules, style short, simple. Follicles leathery, opening with 1–2 longitudinal silts, ovoid to globular with style persisting as a short beak. Seeds reniform to ovoid or globular, glabrous, glossy dark brown to black; aril fleshy, cup-shaped, reddish or purplish, with fimbriate or laciniate margin.

A pantropical genus of ca. 45 species; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed, dioecious. Leaves opposite, imparipinnate. Inflorescence a thyrse, terminal or subterminal. Flowers small, functionally unisexual, 4–5-merous. Calyx 4–5-lobed. Petals distinct, imbricate. Stamens 4–5, distinct. Disk pulvinate to conical. Gynoecium 4–5-carpellate; carpels distinct or connate at base, ovules 1–2 per carpel; style apical; stigma peltate. Fruit 1–5 distinct or basally connate follicles.

Nine species distributed in E, S, and SE Asia; seven species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Succulent herbs or subshrubs, often with white small tubercles. Stems erect, prostrate or scandent. Leaves alternate, flat, entire, exstipulate. Flowers solitary or clustered in axil of leaves, pedicellate or sessile. Calyx-tube adnate to ovary, often angled; lobes 3 – 5, short and often unequal. Petals absent. Stamens few to many, inserted on calyx-tube and alternate with calyx-lobes. Ovary inferior, 2–9‑locular, each locule with a pendulous ovule; styles as many as ovary locules. Fruit a bony nutlet, indehiscent, often angled.

About 60 species in SE & S Asia, Africa and Australia; one species in China, also in Hong Kong.

Unarmed shrubs or treelets, stoloniferous. Leaves simple, long-petiolate, palmately lobed; stipules 2, subulate, adnate to the base of petioles. Flowers bisexual, in umbels and forming large terminal panicles; pedicels not articulate. Calyx-margin entire or obscurely toothed. Petals 4–5, ovate, acute, valvate in the bud. Stamens 4–5. Ovary 2-locular; styles 2, erect, recurved at apices. Fruit baccate, drupaceous.

One species endemic to China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Climbers, woody, rarely herbaceous, usually polygamo-dioecious. Stems and branches terete or flattened. Tendrils unbranched or bifurcate, sometimes palmately branched. Leaves usually palmately compound, 3–7-foliolate, rarely simple. Inflorescence a polychasium, an umbel, or a compound cyme, axillary. Flowers 4-merous. Calyx saucer-shaped, apex truncate or 4-dentate, Petals spreading, free, usually hooded or galeate, sometimes corniculate. Stamens short. Disk well developed in male flowers, inconspicuous in female flowers. Style short or inconspicuous. Stigma usually 4-divided, rarely irregularly divided. Berry globose, ellipsoidal, or obovoid, 1–4-seeded.

About 100 species distributed in Asia to Oceania; 44 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs, with rhizomes or stolons. Leaves simple, opposite, serrate. Verticillasters 2 – 3‑flowered, forming terminal and axillary spike‑like inflorescence. Calyx 10‑veined, ± 2‑lipped; tube tubular to campanulate, swollen in front at base; limb 5‑toothed. Corolla 1‑lipped; tube included or exserted, not hairy annulate inside; limb 5‑lobed, with middle lobe circular or spathulate, occasionally 2‑lobulate; lateral lobes 4, small. Stamens 4, lower 2 slightly longer, all exserted from posterior sinus of corolla; anthers reniform, with 2 divaricate cells. Disk symmetrical. Ovary globose. Style equally or subequally 2‑fid. Nutlets obovoid, glabrous, rugose or reticulate; surface of contact large, oblique or lateral.

About 260 species distributed worldwide, but abundant in the Mediterranean region; 18 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with fibrous roots, often glabrous. Stems terete, usually branched. Leaves basal and cauline, 1–4-ternately or pinnately compound, rarely simple; leaflets usually palmately lobed, rarely entire; petioles broadened forming a sheath at base; stipules present or absent. Inflorescences usually monochasial cymes, sometimes paniculate, 1–200-flowered. Flowers usually bisexual, rarely unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals 4–5, elliptic or narrowly ovate, yellowish green, white, pink or purplish, petal-like, often caducous. Petals absent. Stamens usually numerous; connectives obtuse or apiculate; filaments linear or oblanceolate. Carpels 2 to many, 1-ovulate; style short or long, more or less with stigmatic tissue on the ventral surface. Achenes, sessile or stalked, ellipsoid, narrow ovate or fusiformis, usually longitudinally ribbed.

About 200 species widespread over temperate regions of Asia, Europe, Africa, N & S America; 67 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic small perennial herbs. Stems short, changing into globose pseudobulbs with 1 or 2 leaves. Scapes aphyllous, with sheathing bracts at the base. Flowers small, hardly opening, closely arranged in a spike; sepals equal, connivent; petals smaller than the odd sepal; lip undivided, attached to the base of the column, concave; column very short, conical, without wings or foot; rostellum terminal, acuminate; anther subsessile, ovate-acuminate; pollinia 8, in 2 groups of 4, obovoid-globose, attached to an elongate stipe with widened apex and an elliptic viscidium; stigma large, ovate; ovary obconical, very short. Capsules small, oblong.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Asia, especially in SE Asia; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual herbs. Culms erect tufted, glabrous. Leaf sheaths keeled, margins membranous, the upper usually shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, margins rough; ligule short, membranous or papery. Inflorescence a leafy compound panicle composed of short racemes; each raceme on a short peduncle subtended by a sheathing spatheole, loosely arranged or gathered into fan-shaped spathate fascicles. The lowest two pairs of raceme forming a kind of involucre, staminate or empty, muticous, sessile, all or partly persistent, the upper part of raceme 1–3-jointed, the upper joint with triad of one sessile bisexual and two pedicellate staminate or empty spikelets, occasionally lower joints except involucre, each with 1 sessile bisexual and 1 pedicellate staminate or empty spikelet. Sessile spikelet subterete or dorsally compressed; callus mostly acute to pungent, sometimes obtuse, bearded; lower glume usually leathery, margins membranous; upper glume abaxially carinate, laterally deeply grooved; lower floret reduced to a hyaline lemma; upper lemma stipitiform, entire, passing into a geniculate awn with pubescent column, occasionally awnless; lodicules 2, cuneate; stamens 0–3; style free from the base. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet mostly larger than sessile spikelet, staminate or neuter.

About 27 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World, mainly in Asia; 13 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs, covered with scales or stellate hairs throughout. Leaves alternate, entire or palmately lobed. Flowers solitary or in small axillary cymes; bracteoles 3 or 5, sometimes caducous. Calyx cup-shaped, apex truncate or minutely 5-toothed. Corolla campanulate; petals 5, yellow. Staminal tube cylindric, apex toothed; filaments paired; anthers horseshoe-shaped. Ovary 5-loculate; style clavate, 5-sulcate; stigmas scabrous. Capsules globose or pyriform, woody or leathery. Seeds ovoid, pubescent, glabrous or scabrous papillose.

About 15 species in tropical Asia and Africa; three species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Evergreen trees or many‑branched shrubs, with white latex. Leaves alternate, rather densely together on slender branchlets. Cymes terminal and leaf‑opposed. Calyx deeply divided, with many basal glands inside. Corolla yellow, funnelform, lobes overlapping to left, with 5 narrow, long‑hairy scales on the throat. Stamens inserted on distal narrow part of corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers narrowly oblong, attached to each other apically across top of pistil head but not adnate to it; disk small than ovary, fleshy. Ovary of 2 carpels connate in lower half, than free and uniting again into a common style, several ovules per carpel; style filiform, head with wide bluntly‑lobed frill. Fruit a drupe, triangular‑globose, laterally compressed; with fleshy exocarp and stony mesocarp; endocarps free from each other. Seed 1 per locule, wingless, not comose.

Eight species in tropical America; two species cultivated in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Achlorophyllous mycoheterotrophic herbs; tuberous. Stems simple or branched. Leaves cauline, bract-like, small. Flowers solitary, terminal. Perianth tube actinomorphic to zygomorphic, cylindrical, urceolate, or sometimes campanulate, with prominent annulus at mouth, lateral wings absent; tepals 6, apically distinct; outer tepals as long or shorter than inner tepals; inner tepals sometimes apically connivent or connate into an erect mitre. Stamens 6, generally laterally connate, pendent from annulus, occasionally distinct; connectives with 0–2 apical and 0–2 basal appendages. Ovary obconical or obovoid, 1-locular, with 3 parietal placentas; stigmas 3, simple or bilabiate. Fruit fleshy with persistent perianth base; dehiscence by abscission of apex.

About 43 species, pantropical; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Epiphytic herbs. Aerial roots long and branched. Leaves oblong-elliptic, distichous. Scapes short, subsessile, many on a shoot, with imbricate persistent scales. Flowers showy, ephemeral, in a short axillary raceme; sepals equal, free, spreading; petals slightly smaller; lip 3-lobed, saccate, adnate to the base of the column, spur conical, lateral lobes erect, obtuse, midlobe triangularovate, obtuse, disk with a callus; column short, semiterete, with fleshy arms; clinandrium oblique; rostellum fleshy, horse-shoeshaped; anther terminal, incumbent, convex; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, unequal, the front one of each pair smaller, obovoid-oblong, on a white viscidium with a recurved ovate membrane resting over the horse-shoe-shaped rostellum; stigma suborbicular; ovary obovoidcylindrical. Capsules oblong.

About 120 species distributed from tropical Asia to Oceania; 12 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms solid, creeping, branching into many erect flowering culms. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, stiff; ligule ciliate. Inflorescence monoecious, composed of a solitary deciduous raceme with spathe; rachis bearing 1–2 persistent bisexual or female spikelets at the base and several deciduous male spikelets above, spikelets secund in one row; male portion of the rachis shedding the spikelets after fertilization and folding onto the fertile spikelets, thus enclosing them in a capsule-like fruit-case. Lower glume small or absent; upper glume equal to spikelet, 5-veined; lower floret barren or male, lemma as long as spikelet, palea well developed, stamen or not; upper floret fertile, thinly papery, lemma with flat margins and hairy apex, inrolled embraced same texture palea. Male spikelets similar but both florets staminate, smooth, with broadly inflexed margins.

Two species distributed from Madagascar to Polynesia; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Climbing herbs or shrubs, lacking cystoliths. Leaves petiolate, entire or sinuate lobed. Flowers pedicellate, solitary or paired in leaf axis or in terminal raceme. Bracts leaf‑like; bracteoles paired, prominent, enclosing calyx and corolla tube, persistent. Calyx cupular with 10–20 subulate lobes or reduced to an entire ring. Corolla large, funnel‑shaped, tube with short cylindric base then widened, equally 5‑lobed, lobes contorted in bud. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted near the base of corolla tube; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae oblong or ovoid, parallel, spurred or not at base, sometimes bearded. Disk shortly annular or pulvinate. Ovary fleshy, 2‑locular, with 2 collateral ovules per locule; style long, stout; stigma bifid, entire or fringed. Capsule globose with conspicuous, woody beak in upper part, loculicidally dehiscent, hook‑like retinacula absent. Seeds 4, compressed to spherical, glabrous.

About 200 species in tropical regions of the Old World; ten species in China; five species cultivated or naturalized in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Culms tufted, reed-like. Leaf blades flat, reticulately veined; ligule scarious. Inflorescence a large open panicle. Spikelets tiny, laterally compressed, 2-flowered, disarticulating above the glumes and between the florets; glumes ca. 1/2 length as the lemmas, hyaline, usually obtuse; lower floret barren and reduced to an acuminate membranous lemma, palea absent; upper floret bisexual, lemma ovate, acute or mucronate, ciliate on margins; a third, upmost floret exist or not, male or rudimentary, palea short, truncate. Stamens 2–3. Caryopsis subglobose; hilum punctiform.

A monotypic genus in SE Asia.

Perennial herbs, with a short rhizome and fibrous or tuberous roots. Leaves radical or nearly so, grass-like, usually narrow-linear or subulate. Scape axillary. Inflorescence usually a terminal raceme or panicle, sometimes constricted into an umbel; bracts small. Flowers bisexual; pedicels articulate proximally. Perianth segments 6, free, 3-veined in the centre; outer 3 with thin entire edges, inner 3 very delicate and rolled inwards in the bud or ciliate on the edge. Stamens 6, inserted at the base of perianth segments, inner ones sometimes reduced; filaments slender; anthers basifixed, inner ones usually longer. Ovary superior, 3-locular , with 2 ovules in each locule; style filiform; stigma small. Fruit a loculicidal capsule.

About 50 species mainly distributed in Australia, only a few species extending to tropical Asia; one species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Vines. Leaves palmately nerved, base cordate, sometimes sagittate or hastate. Inflorescences axillary or borne on old stems, racemose, cymose or paniculate, solitary or fascicled. Male flowers: sepals usually 6, sometimes more or fewer, the outer 3 usually smaller, membranous, imbricate; petals 6, rarely 3, base unguiculate; stamens 6, filaments usually free, anthers nearly extrorse, opening by longitudinal and ± oblique slits. Female flowers: sepals and petals similar to that in males, except petals often smaller; staminodes 6, shorter than petals; carpels 3; style short and thick; stigmas ligulate-peltate, margin undulate or fimbriate. Drupes 1–3, short-stalked; style-scar subterminal; kernel bony, dorsally convex and sometimes verrucose or tuberculate, ventrally more or less flat, with a central aperture.

More than 30 species in tropical and subtropical E hemisphere; six species and two varieties in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Large annual or perennial erect herbs or shrubs. Leaves alternate in upper stem, opposite near base, simple or 3– 5‑lobed, trinerved. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, usually solitary; peduncle inflated apically. Involucres hemispherical or broadly campanulate; phyllaries in 2–4 series, bearing many longitudinal lines, hardened below, herbaceous or membranous above. Receptacle convex, paleate; the paleae acuminate to aristate‑acuminate, flat or slightly enclosing the achenes. Marginal florets in 1 row, female or neutral, corolla ligulate and spreading, entire or 2– 3‑lobed at apex. Disk florets many, bisexual and usually fertile, corolla tubular, 5‑cleft at apex; anther tube exserted, base sagittate and obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑oblong, obtuse; stylar branches terminated by acute‑lanceolate hairy appendages. Cypselae oblong or obovate, compressed, 4‑ribbed, pubescent. Pappus coronate scales, sometimes together with 1–2 awns.

About ten species native to C America and Mexico; one species cultivated in China and in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs. Stems and branches armed with many hooked spines. Leaves alternate, digitately 3-foliolate, densely glandular-dotted. Inflorescence a corymbose thyrse or panicle, axillary or terminal. Flowers unisexual, small, 4– 5-merous. Calyx 4–5-lobed. Petals 4–5, imbricate or valvate. Male flower: stamens 4–5, pistillode clavate. Female flower: staminodes short and small, half as long as pistil, without anthers; ovary 4–5-carpellate, 4–5-locular, ovules 2 per locule; style very short; stigma capitate. Fruit a drupe, subglobose, with 4–8 stones. Seeds reniform; seed coat rigid and bony; endosperm fleshy; embryo curved.

One species distributed in E & SE Asia, E & SW Africa; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Trees; bark coarse, exfoliated. Buds subglobose, with several outer scales. Leaves pinnate, alternate; leaflets petiolulate, opposite or alternate. Inflorescence a terminal or axillary panicle. Flowers bisexual, small, (4–)5-merous. Calyx tubular, short, (4–)5-lobed or with (4–)5 distinct sepals. Petals (4–)5, alternate with sepals, distinct, imbricate or contorted in buds. Stamens (4–)5, distinct, alternate with petals; staminodes 5 or absent. Disk thick and fleshy, forming a 5-ridged short column. Ovary 5-locular; ovules 8–15 per locule; style simple; stigma disciform. Fruit a 5-locular capsule, leathery or woody, septifragal. Seeds many per locule, compressed laterally, winged at both ends or at the lower end; endosperm thin.

About five species distributed in Asia, Australia; three species in China; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs glabrous or villous, rarely hispidulous. Leaves opposite, usually petiolate. Inflorescences racemose or in axillary umbellate fascicles, rarely dichotomous and terminal flowers reduced, or 1‑flowered. Flowers pedicellate. Calyx ribbed or winged, usually 5‑lobed. Corolla 2‑lipped; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal; upper lip erect, apex entire, emarginate, or 2‑lobed. Stamens 4; anterior filaments with appendages, or less often without appendages; posterior stamens included. Anthers connivent in pairs, cells often apically confluent. Ovary usually with short coarse hairs at apex; styles apically 2‑lamellate. Capsules oblong, included in persistent calyx, opening by pores. Seeds numerous, scrobiculate.

About 50 species distributed in tropical Africa and Asia; ten species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs, rarely trees. Leaves alternate, petiolate, entire. Cymes terminal or axillary, corymbose, ebracteate. Calyx 4–5‑parted; lobes linear, lanceolate or lanceolate‑ovate, imbricate. Corolla white or pale green, usually funnelform; tube usually exceeding calyx, pubescent abaxially; throat without appendage; lobes 4 or 5, overlapping or valvate in bud. Stamens 4 or 5, inclusive; filaments short, inserted on corolla tube; anthers ovoid to ellipsoidal, mucronate or obtuse at apex. Disk slightly convex or sometimes nearly cupular. Ovary 4‑locular; ovules 1 per locule, pendulous. Style terminal; stigma entire or slightly 2‑cleft, base fleshy, ring‑like, inflated. Drupes with watery, sticky, or corky mesocarp, endocarp divided into two 2‑seeded or four 1‑seeded mericarps at maturity. Seeds pendulous or oblique, straight or incurved; endosperm fleshy, copious or thin; cotyledons ovate or elliptic.

About 150 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or woody lianas, villous or rusty tomentose, rarely glabrous. Leaves opposite. Cymes axillary, umbel‑like. Sepals 5, small, sometimes with minute basal glands. Corolla rotate or rarely bell‑shaped; tube very short; lobes 5, patent‑reflexed, overlapping to left, rarely to right. Corona lobes 5, inserted at back of gynostegium, dorsally compressed, slightly exceeding stamens. Anthers small, retuse, sometimes with minute apical appendage appressed to stigma head; pollinia 2 in each anther cell, erect or horizontal. Style short; stigma head exserted beyond anthers, beaked or swollen. Follicles divaricate, terete, usually villous. Seeds flat, beaked; coma white.

About 40 species distributed in tropical Asia, Africa and Pacific islands; 11 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Lianas woody, latex white. Leaves opposite. Cymes lax, terminal or axillary. Flowers white or purplish, 5‑merous. Calyx small, deeply divided, basal glands 5 – 10, apex usually denticulate. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric, 5‑angled, dilated at insertion of stamens, throat constricted; lobes sharply overlapping to right. Stamens inserted at or above middle of corolla‑tube; anthers sagittate, connivent, adherent to pistil head, anther included or the acuminate tips exserted, cells spurred at base; disk scales 5, free. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style, usually longer than disk; ovules numerous in each carpel. Style short; pistil head conical. Fruit of paired follicles, linear or fusiform, divergent or parallel. Seeds linear‑oblong, unbeaked, coma silky white.

About 15 species distributed worldwide, one species in N America, 14 species in Asia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, without rhizomes; stems usually ascending from the decumbent base, rarely erect. Leaves alternate or spirally arranged, sheathing at nodes. Flowers regular, in pseudoterminal or lateral clusters, rarely solitary; flower-clusters sessile, or forming a panicle; involucral bracts mostly spathe-like; bracts filiform. Sepals 3, free or connate at base, boat-shaped. Petals 3, free or with claws fused at base. Stamens 6, all fertile, subequal or antepetalous 3 shorter; filaments glabrous or bearded; anther-cells ellipsoidal or oblong, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary 3-locular; with 2 ovules in each locule. Fruit an ovoid capsule, 3-valved. Seeds (1–)2 per valve.

About 70 species mainly distributed in tropical America; three species commonly cultivated in Hong Kong.

Another species Tradescantia fluminensis Vell. was cultivated previously.

Small trees or large shrubs, monoecious or dioecious. Stipules free, deciduous. Leaves alternate, ovate to narrowly lanceolate, margin denticulate, 3-veined, rarely 5-veined or pinninerved. Flowers unisexual or polygamous, densely arranged in cymes, paired and axillary. Male flowers: sepals 4(–5), valvate or slightly imbricate; stamens as many as sepals; filaments straight; rudimentary ovary present. Female flowers: calyx 4 –5-lobed; ovary sessile, base with villose cycles; style short; stigmas 2, linear, ovules solitary, pendulous. Drupes small, erect, ovoid or subglobose, with persistent sepals and stigmas, exocarp fleshy, endocarp bony. Seeds with fleshy endosperm.

About 15 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; six species and one variety in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbaceous vines, dioecious, rarely monoecious. Tendrils usually 2– 6-branched, rarely unbranched. Leaves simple, unlobed or palmately 3 –9-lobed, rarely compound, 3 –5-foliolate. Flowers usually white, rarely pink or red. Male flowers: usually in racemes, rarely solitary; calyx-tube tubular, frequently dilated at the apex, 5-lobed, lobes entire or serrate or laciniate; corolla 5-partitioned, lobes usually long fimbriate; stamens 3; filaments very short, distinct; anthers connate, two 2-celled, one 1-celled, the cells conduplicate. Female flowers: solitary, very rarely in racemes. Calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes absent; ovary inferior, ovoid or fusiform, 1-locular, with 3 parietal placentas; ovules usually many, often horizontal; style slender; stigmas 3, entire or 3 – 6-lobed. Fruit fleshy, globose, ovoid or fusiform, many-seeded, indehiscent. Seeds many, 1- or 3-locular.

About 80 species distributed in Asia and N Australia; 33 species and six varieties in China; five species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Leaves opposite, incised‑toothed or pinnatisect. Capitula few, heterogamous and radiate, solitary or in cymose form, long‑pedunculate. Involucres ovoid or campanulate; phyllaries 2–5‑seriate, outer 1–2 layers herbaceous, innermost scarious, longer and narrower. Receptacle flat or convex; paleae scarious. All florets fertile. Marginal florets in 1 row, female, corolla white, yellow or purplish, ligulate, or 2‑lipped with the outer lip larger, 3‑cleft, and the inner tiny lip 2‑lobed or unlobed. Central florets many, bisexual, corolla tubular, 5‑dentate apically, yellow or green; anther bases sagittate, apical appendages oblong‑ovate; stylar branches rough hairy, subulate at apex. Cypselae oblong‑cuneate or subcylindric, hairy. Pappus plumose.

About 26 species native to tropical America; one species in China and in Hong Kong as a common weed.

Herbs. Stipules adnate to petioles. Leaves digitately 3- or rarely 5–7-foliolate, rarely pinnately 3–5-foliolate; leaflets mostly denticulate. Flowers mostly purple, red or white, rarely yellow, in spicate, capitate, umbellate inflorescence, or rarely solitary. Bracts small or absent, sometimes membranous, persisent or deciduous, sometimes outer ones connate into a dentate or lobed involucre; bracteoles absent. Calyx-teeth or lobes subequal or the lower longer, the upper 2 sometimes more or less connate. Petals marcescent, all clawed, or the lower 4 more or less adnate to staminal sheath; vexillum oblong or ovate; wings narrow; keel shorter than wings, obtuse. Vexillary stamen free or rarely connate at middle with others; alternate filaments or all of them dilated at apex, or scarcely dilated; anthers uniform. Ovary with few ovules, styles filiform, incurved distally, stigma capitate or hooked. Pods oblong and subterete or obovate-compressed, enclosed by marcescent calyx and petals, mostly membranous, indehiscent. Seeds 1–2(–8), estrophiolate.

About 250 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; 13 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, rarely opposite to nearly whorled, unlobed, pinnately-veined; with a pair of glands at apex of petiole; stipules small, persistent or deciduous. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or thyrsoid. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious). Male flowers: sepals 5, free, imbricate; petals 5, exceeding the calyx; disk cupular or annular, sometimes divided into 5 glands; stamens 3–5, filaments connate into a column or the upper half free; anther 2-celled, extrorse, connectives enlarged. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in male flowers; disk annular or cupular, usually unlobed; ovary 3-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 3, free or connate at base, bifid at apex. Capsules 3-valved; smooth or ± tuberculate.

About 50 species in tropical Asia, extending from India and Sri Lanka to New Guinea; ten species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial twining herbs. Leaves opposite. Inflorescences axillary and terminal, 1‑flowered or in cymes. Flowers 5‑merous. Calyx tube campanulate, usually with 5‑keeled ridges. Corolla tubular or broadly tubular, plicae present. Stamens inserted at basal part of corolla tube, unequal, apically recurved. Disk present, annular. Ovary 1‑locular; ovules many. Style slender, slightly recurved; stigma linear, recurved at anthesis. Fruit a 2‑valved capsule or berry, many‑seeded. Seeds triquetrous to compressed, winged or wingless.

About 25 species distributed in E and S Asia; 19 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Erect or procumbent herbs or subshrubs, stellate hairy or pubescent. Leaves simple, alternate, not lobed or palmately 3– 5-lobed, palmately veined, margin serrate. Flowers bisexual, solitary or arranged in axillary or extra-axillary cymes. Sepals 5, distinct, valvate, usually with hooked appendages at apex. Petals 5, distinct, with thickened glands at base adaxially. Stamens many to 5, distinct, inserted on fleshy, segmented androgynophore; anthers dorsifixed, subglobose, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary 2–5-locular, ovules 2 per locule; style 1; stigma 2–5-lobed. Capsule subglobose, dehiscing into 3– 6 valves, or indehiscent, spiny or strigose, spines pointed, erect or hooked.

About 60 species, mainly distributed in tropical and subtropical areas; six species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Roots sometimes tuberous. Stems slightly succulent. Leaves peltate, entire or sometimes lobed. Flowers yellow, orange or purple. Sepals 5, adaxial 1 extended into a spur. Petals 5, imbricate, the abaxial 3 often different, clawed. Stamens 8, in 2 whorls, distinct, unequal; anthers 2-celled, dehiscent by longitudinal slits. Ovary superior, 3-locular, placentation axile; ovule 1 per locule, pendulous from axile apex, anatropous. Style 1; stigma 3-lobed. Fruits separating into 3 one-seeded mericarps, fleshy or dry. Seed without endosperm; embryo straight.

Terrestrial herbs; rhizome ascending, stout; roots wiry, fibrous. Stem erect, rigid, branched or unbranched, noded, with sheaths at nodes. Leaves 2–many, plicate, ovate to narrowly lanceolate, base contracted into amplexicaul sheaths. Inflorescence a short raceme or panicle, terminal or arising from leaf axils near apex of stem, several- or many-flowered. Flowers usually in 2 alternate rows, rarely clustered; sepals narrow, subequal, the lateral ones broader than the odd one, connate at the base and enclosing the lip; petals subsimilar to the odd sepal; lip undivided, equal to the sepals in length, canaliculate, embracing the column, shortly calcarate, acuminate at the apex; column short, bearing the anther on the back; anther erect, ovate-acuminate; pollinia 2, caudicles subulate, viscidium peltate; rostellum elongate, the sides dilated and membranous partially covering the anther, the apex subulate, bifid; ovary oblong. Capsules ovoid-oblong.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Asia and Pacific islands; four species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, bulbiferous. Stem usually simple, scape-like but leaf-bearing. Leaves basal and alternate on stem, linear to narrowly ovate, sessile and clasping at base. Flowers usually large, solitary and terminal; bracts absent or sometimes present. Perianth segments 6, free, often coloured, outer and inner ones different in shape. Stamens 6, equal or 3 longer; filaments sometimes hairy; anthers basifixed. Ovary superior, 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule. Style columnar or very short; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit a capsule, loculicidally 3-valved. Seeds flat, usually subdeltoid.

About 150 species in temperate regions of Asia, Europe and N Africa, mainly in C Asia and the Mediterranean region; 13 species in China; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Small trees or shrubs. Leaves odd-pinnately compound, sometimes unifoliolate, opposite, stipulate; leaflets opposite, subleathery, petiolulate. Flowers small, 5-merous, bisexual, rarely unisexual. Stamens inserted outside the disk. Disk crenate or lobed. Ovary 3-locular, composed of 3 completely connate carpels, ovules several per locule; styles 3, connate or distinct; stigmas subcapitate. Fruit a berry, subglobose, indehiscent, pericarp fleshy or leathery. Seeds angular, testa bony or crustaceous; aril wanting.

About 40 species distributed in tropical regions of Asia and America; 13 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Perennial lianas, herbaceous or woody. Inflorescences extra‑axillary, rarely terminal, mostly with several cymules born along a simple or branched, often zigzag rachis, less often umbel‑like; cymules raceme‑like or sometimes umbel‑like. Calyx with basal glands. Corolla rotate or subrotate, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes narrowly overlapping to right to subvalvate, often distinctly veined. Corona lobes 5, usually erect, turgid, adnate to and not exceeding gynostegium; anthers short, appendages arching over stigma head; pollinia 2 per pollinarium, horizontal, suberect, rarely erect, caudicles ascending or suberect, retinaculum small. Stigma head depressed, flattened or concave, rarely longer than anthers. Follicles oblong‑lanceolate or fusiform. Seeds comose.

About 60 species distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia, Africa and Australia; 31 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as the family.

One species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, with tuberous rhizome. Leaves 2–5, radical; leaf blade sagittate-hastate, 3–5-lobed, or pedatisect, venation reticulate, often with 2–3-submarginal veins. Peduncle radical, without bracts under the spathe. Spathe convolute or tubular at the base, persistent, throat ± constricted, limb ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, usually reddish purple, rarely white, apex acuminate; spadix androgynous: female flowers at the base, male flowers higher up, with neutral flowers either between the female and male flowers, or both; the rachis ending in a club-shaped or pointed appendage. Female flowers 1-locular, with 1 or more ovules. Male flowers with 1–3 stamens; anthers 2-celled, sessile or on short filament, opening by slits or pores, the connective sometimes prolonged. Berries ovoid, red or purple, 1(–2)-seeded.

About 40 species in India to Malaysia, Australia; 13 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Woody climber; stems and branches usually with hooked spines. Leaves opposite, usually with domatia in the axils of lateral veins. Stipules interpetiolar, entire or bifid. Flowers bisexual, regular, densely crowded in globular heads, on axillary or terminal peduncles, usually solitary, rarely paniculate. Calyx‑tube spindle‑shaped, limb bell‑shaped or tubular, 5‑lobed. Corolla salverform or funelform, limb 5‑lobed; lobes valvate. Stamens 5, inserted in the throat of corolla; filaments short; anthers basifixed, exserted. Ovary inferior, 2‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; style exserted, with capitate or clavate stigma. Fruit an elongate capsule, many‑seeded, dehiscing septicidally into 2 valves; seed winged.

About 34 species mainly in tropical Asia and Australia, a few in tropical America and Africa; 11 species in China, three species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, subshrubs or shrubs. Stipules and stipels present. Leaves simple, pinnately 3-foliolate or odd-pinnate; leaflets often large, reticulate-venose. Inflorescences racemose, terminal or axillary, rarely paniculate. Bracts imbricate, persistent or deciduous; bracteoles absent. Flowers paired in each bract; pedicels hooked-inflexed at apex after flowering. Calyx 5-lobed, the upper 2 lobes shorter, sometimes more or less connate, lower ones longer, bristle-like. Petals shortly clawed; vexillum orbicular or obovate; wings narrow, adhering to keel, auriculate; keel obtuse, slightly upcurved. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary subsessile, 2 –10-ovuled; styles filiform, incurved; stigma capitate. Pods compressed, divided transversely into rounded segments, each folded over the other or segments ± triangular and becoming coiled into a flat circle.

About 20 species distributed in tropical Africa, Asia and Australia; nine species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Lianas woody, latex white. Leaves opposite. Cymes paniculate, terminal or axillary, 3‑branched. Flowers small. Calyx deeply divided, with basal glands inside. Corolla nearly urceolate, throat without scales; lobes short, overlapping to right. Stamens included, inserted at base of corolla‑tube; filaments short; anthers narrowly oblong, sagittate, connivent, adherent to pistil head, cells spurred at base; disk ring‑like, entire or 5‑lobed. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style, villous at apex; ovules numerous in each carpel. Style short; pistil head ovoid, conical or oblong, apex 2‑cleft. Fruit of paired follicles, stipitate or not, cylindric or narrowly ellipsoidal, spreading. Seeds numerous, oblong or linear, compressed, pubescent, with a terminal white coma.

About 15 species distributed in SE Asia; eight species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or small shrubs, stellate pubescent. Leaves alternate, palmately lobed or sinuate, palmately 3- to 7-nerved, the middle one with a conspicuous gland near the base. Flowers axillary, solitary, subfasciculate, or crowded at the end of branchlets. Bracteoles campanulate, 5-lobed; lobes lanceolate, acute, striate towards the base. Calyx cup-shaped, deeply 5-parted; lobes ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 1-nerved, keeled. Corolla purplish-red; petals 5, stellate-pilose abaxially. Staminal tube dilated and united with the petals at base; anthers subsessile. Ovary depressed-globose, hirtellous, 5-locular, each with 1 ovule; styles 10, reflexed; stigmas discoid, end fimbriate. Fruit subglobose, mature carpels separating from the axis, triangular obovoid, leathery, indehiscent; dorsally convex, stellately hirsute and with glochidiate spines; laterally plane, striate. Seeds obovoid-trigonous or reniform, glabrous.

About six species in the warmer regions of both hemispheres; three species in China; two species growing naturally in Hong Kong.

Perennial or annual, marsh or aquatic herbs, without true roots. Stems modified to rhizoids and stolons, rarely developed. Leaves alternate or in basal rosette, simple or 1–many times divided, 1–3‑veined, rarely with dichotomously branched or pinnate veins. Traps small bladder‑like, borne on stolons or leaves. Flowers irregular, in terminal racemes on scapes, rarely solitary. Calyx deeply 2‑lobed; lobes usually unequal. Corolla spurred, bilabiate, upper lip entire or 2–3‑lobed, lower lip larger, entire or 2–3(–6)‑lobed, with a variously raised palate in throat. Capsule globose, ovoid or ellipsoidal, opening by longitudinal slits or circumscissile, rarely indehiscent. Seeds few to many, with various prominences or appendages.

About 200 species cosmopolitan but mainly in tropics; 17 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches usually with stellate hairs. Leaves leathery, glabrous or stellate-pubescent. Inflorescences terminal, leaf-opposed or supra-axillary, 1–4-flowered. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 3, valvate in bud, free or basally connate. Petals 6, free or connate, in 2 whorls, fleshy, papery or membranous; outer petals slightly larger than inner, both whorls generally spreading. Stamens numerous, extrorse; connective with a truncate, liguliform and enlarged apex, glabrous, rarely hairy. Carpels few to numerous per flower; ovary hairy, free, oblong or cylindrical; ovules 3–30 per ovary, lateral, 1- or 2-seriate; style not conspicuous; stigma obconical to cylindrical, usually 2-cleft and incurved, glabrous or hairy. Fruits apocarpous; monocarps 1–70 per fruit, ellipsoid to cylindrical, constricted, sparsely to densely hairy, sometimes spiny; stipes 0– 140 mm long; receptacles 3– 24 mm in diam.; sepals caducous. Seeds 1–30 per monocarp, lateral,1–2-seriate, ellipsoid to lenticular or ovoid; raphes conspicuous, ribbed.

Approximately 110 species in tropical Africa, Asia and Australia; nine species in China, and four species in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or rarely small trees, evergreen or deciduous. Leaves alternate, short-petiolate, margin entire or toothed. Flowers in axillary or terminal racemes, rarely solitary or in pairs. Calyx-tube adnate to the ovary, apex 4–5-lobed or toothed. Corolla urceolate, campanulate, or tubular, 4–5-lobed or toothed; lobes erect or recurved, mostly shorter than the tube. Stamens 10 or 8 usually included; anther cell (theca) prolonged into terminal tubule, opening in oblique pores at the top of the tubule. Ovary inferior, (4–)5-locular, sometimes almost divided into 10 cells by false dissepiments; ovules many in each locule. Fruit a several-seeded berry, usually globose, crowned by the persistent calyx-lobes.

About 450 species distributed throughout the N hemisphere, and also in the tropical mountainous regions of C and S America, Asia and Malesia, a few in Africa and Madagascar; 92 species in China (51 endemic); only one species and one variety are known from Hong Kong.

Herbs, submerged, stoloniferous, without erect stems. Leaves basal, sessile, linear or strap-shaped, veins 3–9, parallel, slightly sheathed at base, margin minutely serrulate or entire. Plants dioecious; flowers unisexual. Male flowers many, minute, shortly pedicellate, clustered together on a central column enclosed by a common spathe, each flower finally breaking free and floating on water surface; spathe ovate or broadly lanceolate, shortly pedunculate; sepals 3, convex, 2 larger than the third; petals 3 or 2, minute; stamens 1–3; female spathe tubular, bifid at apex, pedunculate; peduncles long, coiled after anthesis. Female flowers solitary in spathe; sepals 3; petals 3, minute. Ovary narrowly cylindrical or narrowly triangular-cylindrical; ovules many; styles 3, bifid. Fruit cylindrical or triangularcylindrical. Seeds many, oblong or fusiform.

About eight species distributed in tropical and subtropical; three species in China (one endemic); one species in Hong Kong.

Recent studies of the genus have resolved taxonomic problems of certain species in the tropics, based on living materials (e.g. Lowden, Aquatic Botany 13: 269–298. 1982; Jacobs & Frank, Telopea 7: 111–118. 1997).

Tall woody climbers. Leaves alternate, 2-ranked, pinnately-veined, elegantly marked with transverse veinlets between the pinnate veins. Flowers bisexual, regular, in small axillary cymes or terminal panicles. Calyx obconic, 5-lobed; lobes divaricate. Petals 5, subtriangular or cucullate. Stamens 5, adnate to the base of petals. Ovary immersed in the 5-lobed disk, 2-locular, ending in a short conical style or stigmas. Fruit a 1-seeded nut, base surrounded by the persistent calyx, apex with a long oblong flat wing.

About 35 species in tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs. Rhizomes thick and short, with many ± fleshy roots. Stems erect, terete, leafy, usually enclosed by fibers disintegrated leaf sheaths at base. Leaves alternate, sheathed and clasping, strongly plicate-veined, usually gradually reduced in size upward and replaced by bracts. Inflorescence usually a terminal panicle, many-flowered. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, shortly pedicellate or subsessile; perianth segments 6, free, rarely connate at base, white, yellowish, green, or dark purple-brown, persistent in fruit. Stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth segments; anthers reniform to cordate-orbicular, with locules confluent and dehiscent by an apical valve. Ovary superior, 3-locular, slightly 3-lobed apically, usually with many ovules in each locule; styles 3, short, persistent, stigmatic adaxially. Fruit a septicidal capsule. Seeds several per valve, flattened, narrowly winged.

About 40 species distributed mainly in temperate regions of the N hemisphere; 13 species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Herbs or subshrubs. Stems erect or prostrate, glabrous or hairy. Leaves opposite, rarely whorled or alternate, sessile, dentate, lobed, or pinnatifid, rarely entire. Spikes usually terminal, simple or branched, rachis not excavated. Bracts small. Flowers alternate, nearly zygomorphic. Calyx membranous, tubular, 5‑dentate. Corolla‑tube erect or curved; lobes 5, unequal, spreading, oblong, apex obtuse, rounded or slightly emarginate, imbricate in buds. Stamens 4, fertile, didynamous, inserted at middle of corolla tube, inclusive; anthers ovoid, thecae parallel or slightly divergent. Ovary 4‑locular; ovules erect, 1 per locule. Fruit dry, enclosed in persistent calyx, dehiscing into four 1‑seeded pyrenes. Seeds without endosperm.

About 250 species mainly distributed in tropical America; one species in China; it also occurs in Hong Kong.

Additional species (V. × hybrida Voss 鋪地馬鞭草, V. rigida Spreng. 顯脈馬鞭草 and V. tenuisecta Briq.) are occasionally cultivated as ornamentals. Native to S America, the pantropical weed V. bonariensis L. (南美馬鞭草) was also recorded.

Deciduous trees; young branches pubescent. Leaves alternate, entire or lobed; palmately-veined; petioles biglandular at the apex; stipules small, caducous. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious or dioecious), in terminal or axillary corymbiform panicles. Male flowers: calyx initially entirely closed, afterwards spreading and spathe-like, split or irregularly 2–5-fid, caducous; petals 5, imbricate or contorted in bud, unguiculate at base; disk-glands 5, alternating with petals; stamens 7–12, in 2 series, outer filaments free, inner ones ± connate; anther introrse, 2-celled, connectives broad. Female flowers: calyx, petals and disk-glands as in male flowers; ovary 3–8-locular, with 1 ovule in each locule; styles 3–4, 2-lobed. Drupes large, subglobose, rostrate at apex, indehiscent or slightly dehiscent at base; pericarp crustaceous; seeds large, 3–8, testa woody, albumen thick, oily.

About three species in E Asia; two species in China and cultivated in Hong Kong.

Herbs, shrubs or subshrubs, erect, ascending or scandent. Capitula discoid, in corymbose, paniculate or racemose form. Involucres subcylindric, campanulate or subglobose; phyllaries in many series, imbricate, length shorter outside, apex obtuse, acute to acuminate, some with awn‑tip. Receptacle alveolate and toothed at anthesis, some fimbriate. All florets tubular, bisexual and fertile, corolla usually pink or purple in colour, lower portion slender, upper part broaden as funnel‑shape or campanulate, apex regularly 5‑cleft; anther bases sagittate or obtuse, apical appendages acute; stylar branches linear, subacute, hairy. Cypselae cylindric, ribbed or angulate, apex truncate, callose at base, glabrous or puberulous, sometimes glandular. Pappus in 1 or 2 series with outer ones shorter.

About 1000 species distributed in both hemispheres; 27 species in China; eight species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, annual, or sometimes suffrutescent. Stems erect, procumbent, or creeping. Leaves mostly opposite, rarely whorled or upper ones alternate, entire or variously pinnatifid to pinnatisect. Inflorescences terminal or lateral. Calyx 4 – 5‑lobed, divided to base, if 5‑lobed, upper lobe much smaller or absent. Corolla 4‑sect or 4‑lobed, rarely slightly 2‑lipped; tube short, rarely conspicuous; limb subrotate; lobes unequal. Stamens 2, exserted; anther‑cells apically confluent. Ovary ovoid, often laterally compressed; styles persistent; stigma capitate. Capsules diverse in shape, slightly or strongly compressed laterally, 1‑grooved, loculicidal. Seeds 2–50 per capsule, flattened and convex on both sides, navicular or cupular.

About 250 species cosmopolitan, mainly in Asia and Europe; 53 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Small shrubs or trees. Buds mostly nude. Stipules small, or obsolete, rarely large. Leaves simple, opposite, rarely in whorls of 3, margin entire to dentate, sometimes with stellate hairs. Corymbs or panicles axillary or terminal, bracteate. Flowers bisexual or the inflorescence with marginal sterile flowers. Calyx 5‑toothed, persistent. Corolla white or rose, rotate, campanulate or tubular, 5‑lobed; lobes imbricate. Stamens 5, inserted on corolla‑tube. Anthers exserted. Disk absent. Ovary 1–3‑locular; style 3‑lobed; ovule solitary, pendulous. Drupes dry or fleshy, sometimes compressed, 1‑seeded. Seeds oblong, compressed, grooved or with inflexed margins; endosperm rarely ruminate; embryo minute.

About 150 species distributed in temperate to subtropical regions, especially in Asia and N America; 74 species in China; four species in Hong Kong.

Herbs. Stems climbing or prostrate, rarely erect, slender, angulate, many-branched. Stipules absent. Leaves even-pinnate, ending in a simple or branched tendril or bristle; leaflets (1–)2 – 12 pairs. Racemes axillary, rarely flowers solitary or 2– 20 in axillary clusters. Bracts small, deciduous; bracteoles absent. Calyx subcampanulate, 5-toothed, often oblique at base, teeth subequal or upper shorter than lower. Corolla pale blue, blue-black or purple, rarely yellow or white; petals clawed; wings obliquely oblong, adherent to middle of keel; keel shorter than wings. Stamens diadelphous or monadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary subsessile; ovules 2 – 7; styles pubescent at apex. Pods compressed, (except V. faba) non-septate, 2-valved. Seeds subglobose or compressed.

About 200 species distributed in N temperate zone with extensions to S America; 43 species in China; three species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Twining or erect herbs, rarely subshrubs. Stipules basifixed or dorsifixed. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate. Racemes axillary or terminal, node of rachis often thickened and glandular. Bracts and bracteoles deciduous. Calyx 5-toothed, 2-lipped. Corolla white, yellow, blue or purple; vexillum orbicular, with appendage at base; wings shorter than vexillum; keel subequal to wings, incurved, not beaked or produced into an incurved somewhat spiral beak (but at angle over 360˚). Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary sessile, styles filiform, upper part thickened, bearded or hirsute lengthwise inside; stigma oblique. Pods linear or linear-oblong, terete or flat, 2-valved. Seeds reniform or subquadrate, hilum short, with or without arils.

About 150 species distributed in tropical regions; 16 species in China; six species and two subspecies in Hong Kong.

Herbs, mostly perennial, stemless or leafy-stemmed. Leaves simple, basal or alternate on stem, petiolate; stipules persistent, often leafy. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic. Peduncles axillary, 1- or rarely 2-flowered; flowers dimorphic, those in spring with showy petals and those in summer cleistogamous, apetalous, and bearing abundant seeds. Petaliferous flowers: sepals 5, nearly equal, produced at the base below their insertion; petals 5, unequal, the abaxial one largest, and produced into a spur or pouch at the base, the other 4 in 2 unlike pairs. Stamens 5, connected in a ring round the gynoecium; filaments very short; anther 2-celled, the 2 lower with nectar-bearing appendages projecting backward into the spur. Ovary 1-locular, consisting of 3 carpels, with numerous ovules on 3-parietal placentas; styles straight or geniculate at base, often lobed or more or less dilated at apex. Capsules elastically dehiscing into 3 valves.

More than 500 species, widely distributed in temperate regions throughout the world; about 114 species in China; five species (one cultivated) in Hong Kong.

Parasitic shrubs or subshrubs, monoecious or dioecious. Stems and branches opposite, dichotomous, or verticillate; internodes terete or flattened, successive internodes at right angles to each other. Leaves well developed or scale-like. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, cymose, 1–7-flowered; peduncle short to nearly absent; involucre navicular, composed of 2 bracts. Pedicel absent; bracts 0–2. Male flower ovoid or ellipsoidal in mature bud; perianth lobes usually 4; filaments absent; anthers adnate to perianth lobes, rarely connate into synandrium, ovoid or ellipsoidal, multicelled, dehiscing by numerous pores. Female flower ovoid to ellipsoidal in mature bud; perianth lobes (3–)4, usually deciduous; placentation basal. Style short or absent; stigma nipple-shaped or cushion-shaped. Berry subglobose, ovoid, or ellipsoidal, often with persistent style; exocarp smooth or verrucose. Seed 1, endosperm fleshy, embryos 1–3.

About 70 species distributed in temperate and tropical regions of the Old World; 12 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs. Leaves opposite, palmately (1–)3–7‑foliolate; leaflets petiolulate, margin entire, dentate, serrate or incised. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, in cymes, thyrses, or panicles. Bracts usually small, often caducous. Calyx campanulate, rarely tubular or funnelform, sometimes 2‑lipped, usually truncate or shortly 5‑dentate, persistent and slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla longer than calyx, 2‑lipped, lower lip 3‑lobed with middle lobe evidently larger, upper lip usually 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, subequal or didynamous, inclusive or exserted. Ovary 2‑ or 4‑locular; ovules 1 or 2 per locule. Style filiform; stigma 2‑cleft. Drupes subtended by persistent calyx, globose, ovoid, or obovoid, endocarp a bony pyrene, mesocarp usually fleshy. Seeds obovoid or oblong, endosperm wanting; cotyledons usually fleshy.

About 250 species distributed in tropical and temperate regions of the world; 14 species in China; four species and one variety in Hong Kong.

In addition to the species described here, V. agnus‑castus L. (紫花牡荊, including V. agnus‑castus ‘Alba’ 白牡荊) and V. tripinnata (Lour.) Merr. (越南牡荊; Photo 178) are occasionally cultivated as ornamentals in Hong Kong.

Woody vines, usually polygamo-dioecious, rarely hermaphroditic. Tendrils leaf-opposed, usually simple or bifurcate. Leaves usually simple, often lobed, sometimes palmately or pinnately compound; stipules usually caducous. Inflorescence a thyrse, leaf-opposite. Flowers 5-merous, small. Calyx saucer-shaped; sepals minute. Petals united at apex and shed as a cap (calyptra) at anthesis. Stamens opposite to petals, undeveloped and abortive in female flowers. Disk conspicuous, 5-lobed or ring-shaped, hypogynous. Ovary connate to disk at base; style short, slender; stigma slightly expanded. Berry globose, 2–4-seeded.

About 60 species mainly distributed in temperate regions extending to the subtropical regions; 37 species in China; seven species in Hong Kong.

Perennial acaulescent herbs, mostly epiphytic. Leaves in dense rosettes, rather broad, scurfy or becoming glabrous adaxially, not spinose, sometimes spotted, barred or striped. Scape usually conspicuous. Inflorescence usually of distichous-flowered spikes, in mostly flattened spikes with highly coloured large bracts. Flowers perfect. Sepals erect, free, coloured. Petals free, erect, often with recurved tops, exceeding the calyx, bearing 2 basal scales on inner side. Stamens included or exserted. Ovary nearly or quite superior; stigma conduplicate-spiral, simple-erect, or of the convolute-blade type; ovules many. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing septicidally from the base. Seeds fusiform with a long straight basal coma.

About 193 species distributed from Mexico and the West Indies to Argentina and Uruguay; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, leafy. Leaves ovate-elliptic, at the ground level, forming a rosette. Scapes with foliaceous bracts. Flowers small, non-resupinate, hardly open, in a terminal spike; sepals subequal, free, the odd one ovate, concave, the lateral ones obliquely auriculate at the base; petals smaller than the sepals and concealed by them; lip erect, undivided, spurred, fleshy, concave, the spur oblong-conical, with two hanging stipitate calli; column very short, stout; rostellum long, bifurcate; anther erect, ovate; pollinia 2, sectile, obovoid and acuminate; caudicles short; viscidium obovoid, between the arms of the rostellum; stigmas 2, below the rostellum; ovary oblong, striate-sulcate. Capsules oblong, erect, erostrate.

About 40 species distributed in S to SE Asia and Pacific islands; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, with milky latex. Stems erect or ascendent. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, rarely opposite. Flowers solitary, terminal or in the upper axils of leaves, or forming loose terminal dichotomous leafy panicles. Calyx‑tube adnate to the ovary; limb 3–5‑lobed, persistent. Corolla regular, campanulate, 5‑lobed. Stamens 5, free, alternate to the corolla‑lobes; filaments usually flattened at base, ciliate. Ovary inferior, 2–3(– 5)‑locular, with numerous ovules in each locule; stigma 2–3(–5)‑lobed. Fruit a capsule, opening at the top loculicidally in as many valves as locule.

About 200 species subcosmopolitan, especially in S temperate regions; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Herbs, subshrubs, rarely trees, with stellate and simple hairs mixed. Stipules narrow. Leaves simple, serrate. Cymes or glomes terminal or axillary. Flowers minute, bisexual; calyx 5-fid; petals 5, spathulate, marcescent; stamens 5, connate at base, opposite to petals; anthers 2-celled; staminodes absent; ovary sessile, 1-locular, 2-ovuled; styles excentric clavate or fimbriate on upper part. Capsules dehiscent, 2-valved, 1-seeded. Seeds with endosperm and flat cotyledons.

About 50 species mainly distributed in tropical America; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs; stems erect, creeping or scandent. Leaves opposite, margin toothed, rarely entire. Capitula heterogamous, radiate. Involucres campanulate or hemispherical; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, imbricate; outer layer foliaceous, green, strigose; inner one subcoriaceous at base, narrower, subtending the ray florets. Receptacle flat or convex, paleate; the paleae curved and enveloping the disk florets. All florets fertile.
