Marginal florets female, corolla ligulate, spreading, apex 2–3‑lobed, tube short, yellow, in one series. Disk florets bisexual, corolla tubular, apex shallowly 5‑cleft, yellow, numerous; anther bases sagittate, apical appendages ovate, acute or obtuse; stylar branches papillose‑hairy. Cypselae obovate or oblong‑cuneate, those developed from ligulate florets trigonous, those formed from tubular florets laterally compressed. Pappus none or of 1–3 bristles or appeared as scarious crown.

About 60 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; six species in China; five species in Hong Kong (three native species growing wild, one introduced species commonly cultivated and naturalized).

Evergreen or deciduous shrubs or small trees. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate. Inflorescence usually terminal and subterminal, rarely axillary, fasciculate or solitary, spicate, racemose, capitate, or paniculate; involucre absent or present; peduncle long or short. Flowers bisexual, 4- or 5-merous. Calyx-tube cylindric or tubular, sometimes slightly funnel-shaped, often deciduous after anthesis; lobes 4 or 5, spreading. Petaloid appendages absent. Stamens twice as many as calyx-lobes, in 2 series; filaments very short; anthers oblong. Disk hypogynous, membranous, 2–4-lobed, scale-like. Ovary superior, sessile, rarely shortly stipitate, 1-locular, 1-ovuled; style 1, short, distinct or obscure; stigma large, capitate, globose, or disciform. Fruit a succulent berry or rather dry. Endosperm scanty or absent; cotyledons fleshy.

About 70 species distributed in E Asia, Malaysia, Australia, and Pacific islands; 48 species in China (41 endemic); three species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous twining shrubs. Stipules caducous. Leaves alternate, odd-pinnate; leaflets entire, pinnately-veined. Flowers in pendulous racemes. Bracts caducous; bracteoles absent. Calyx cup-shaped, 5-toothed, the upper 2 teeth short and ± connate, the lower teeth often longer. Corolla blue to purplish, rarely white; vexillum orbicular, usually with 2 callosities at base; wings oblong-falcate, auriculate, free from the keel, sometimes coherent at apex; keel incurved, obtuse. Stamens 10, diadelphous, vexillary stamen free or connate at middle with the others; filaments not dilated; anthers uniform. Ovary stipitate; style inflexed, glabrous, stigma small, terminal; ovules numerous. Pods stipitate, elongated, flattened, with several seeds, usually slightly constricted between the seeds, tardily dehiscing by 2-valves. Seeds reniform, without strophiole.

About ten species distributed in E Asia, N America and Atlantic; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Minute aquatic herbs; plants rootless, free floating on or below the water surface. Fronds 1 or 2 cohering in groups, symmetrical, globular, ovoid or boat-shaped, green adaxially, green to transparent abaxially, never reddish, with 1 basal pouch reproducing daughter fronds and flower; veins absent. Daughter fronds connected to mother frond by a very short stipe (not visible). Flowers minute, petalless, male and female separate but within same reproductive pouch but without spathe. Stamen 1, sessile, anther 2-celled. Ovary 1-locular, with 1 ovule. Seed 1, nearly smooth.

About 11 species distributed nearly worldwide; one species in China and Hong Kong.

Trees or shrubs with latex. Leaves opposite, petiolate with axillary glands. Cymes terminal or subterminal, dichasial, few‑ to many‑flowered. Sepals quincuncial, with 5–10 basal, scale‑like glands inside. Corolla salverform, funnelform, subrotate, or rotate; tube cylindric to campanulate, lobes overlapping to left; corona ligulate, fringed, or cup‑shaped, entire or subentire at apex, shallowly or deeply divided, sometimes absent. Stamens inserted at corolla mouth or in corolla‑tube; anthers sagittate, connivent and adherent to pistil head, exserted, spurred at base; disk absent. Ovary of 2 separate carpels united into a common style or of two connate carpels; ovules numerous in each carpel. Style filiform; pistil head ovoid, usually dilated at base. Fruit of 2 follicles, connate or divaricate. Seeds narrowly fusiform, with an apical coma directed toward fruit base, beakless.

About 23 species in tropical Africa, Asia, Australia; six species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Coarse annual erect herbs; stem branched, sometimes spiny. Leaves alternate, petiolate, toothed or lobed. Capitula unisexual and monoecious, the male ones at the apical portion of the branch, and the female ones axillary to leaves. Staminate heads globose; involucres broadly hemispherical; phyllaries in 1–3 series, separate, oblong‑lanceolate; receptacle cylindric, with paleae enclosing the tubular male florets; corolla tubular and apically 5‑lobed; anthers free, apex curved inward, obtuse at base, filaments united into a tube and enclosing the rudimentary style; style undivided with the apical end broadened and pilose. Pistillate heads sessile or with a short stipe, ovoid‑oblong; outer phyllaries small, linear; inner phyllaries coriaceous, appeared as an ovoid, hooked and 2‑beaked bur in which 2 florets are enclosed; receptacle microscopic, corolla none with only the pistil; stylar branches long and exposed outside the bur. Cypselae 2 per capitulum, ellipsoidal, enclosed in the prickly bur; pappus absent.

About 25 species originally from America, now distributed in most tropical and temperate regions; three species and one variety in China; one species in Hong Kong.
Morphological characters and geographical distribution are the same as those of the family.

Perennial prostrate herbs. Leaves petiolate, linear, oblong‑linear, lanceolate‑elliptic, or oblanceolate to spatulate, base ± hastate; basal lobes ± amplexicaul, dentate or entire, apex acute to emarginate, mucronate, or tridentate. Cymes axillary, 1(–3)‑flowered. Sepals oblong or oblong‑ovate, ± equal to unequal, acute or obtuse, enlarged in fruit; inner 3 narrower. Corolla pale yellowish or whitish, often with a purplish center, broadly funnelform or campanulate. Anthers not twisted at dehiscence; pollen grains globose, not spiny. Pistil inclusive; ovary 2‑locular, 4‑ovuled. Style 1, filiform; stigmas 2‑globular. Capsule 4‑valved, glabrous or pubescent apically. Seeds 1–4, brownish to black, ovoid‑trigonous.

Two species distributed in tropical regions of Asia, Africa, and Australia; one species in China and in Hong Kong.

Shrubs or small trees, dioecious or rarely polygamous, trunk and branches usually spiny. Leaves alternate, thinly leathery, margin glandular-serrate or -crenate, rarely entire, pinnately veined, shortly petiolate; stipules absent. Inflorescence racemose or paniculate, axillary. Flowers unisexual, rarely bisexual, small. Bracts small, caducous. Pedicles articulate. Sepals 4–6(–8), small, imbricate, slightly united at base. Petals absent. Male flower: disc usually 4–8-lobed, rarely entire; stamens many; filaments filiform; anthers basifixed, without appendages; pistillodes absent. Female flower: Disc circular. Ovary 1-locular; parietal placentas 2, rarely 3–6, ovules 2 to many per placenta; styles short or absent; stigmas capitate or 2–6-lobed. Berry black; pericarp thinly leathery. Seeds several, subobovoid, arillate.

About 100 species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; three species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Rush-like herbs, perennial or rarely annual. Leaves equitant, radical or nearly so, sheathing at base; leaf blade linear to ensiform, smooth, papillose, rugose, or scaberulose. Flowers yellow, in terminal heads; peduncle scape-like, terete to compressed, sometimes winged or ribbed; bracts leathery, imbricate, basal ones usually smaller and sterile, median ones larger and each enveloping a flower, apex emarginate, rounded, or acute, margin scarious, entire, ciliate, fimbriate, or lacerate. Sepals 3, lateral 2-keeled and compressed, entire, dentate, or ciliate, wings membranous; the median one broader and more petal-like, enveloping corolla or sometimes ± reduced or obsolete. Petals 3, free, limb obovate, narrowly clawed. Stamens usually 3, fertile; filaments flattened; anthers basifixed, extrorse, dehiscing by vertical slits. Staminodia 3 or rarely absent, alternate with petals, often clawed, 2-cleft or 2-brachiate and branches with penicillate hairs. Ovary usually sessile, 1 or 3-locular or imperfectly 3-locular. Style filiform, apex 3-branched; stigmas usually U-shaped. Seeds obovoid to ellipsoidal, longitudinally striate, apex usually apiculate.

About 280 species mainly in tropical and subtropical America, some species in Africa, Asia, and Australia; six species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Annual, biennial or perennial lactiferous herbs; stem usually branched. Leaves mostly basal, sometimes alternate on stem, usually pinnately divided. Capitula small, homogamous with all florets ligulate and bisexual, pedunculate and arranged as panicles, corymbs or paniculate corymbs. Involucres cylindric to campanulate; mainly with a principal series of linear phyllaries and 1–2 rows of much reduced ovate ones at bottom, abaxial side with or without cristate appendages near the apex. Receptacle plain, alveolate, usually naked. Ligulate florets 5–25, corolla yellow, ligule truncate and 5‑lobed at apex; style branches slender; anther bases sagittate. Cypselae fusiform, 10–20‑ribbed, apex shortly beaked or without beaks. Pappus 1–2‑seriate, white or rarely grey, capillary or scaberulous, deciduous or persistent.

About 40 species distributed in C, E and tropical Asia, especially in Himalayas; about 37 species in China; two species in Hong Kong.

Deciduous trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, entire or rarely bilobed; stipules membranaceous, adante to petioles, caducous, leaving a scar on petiole; young leaves erect and folded in buds. Flowers solitary, terminal, bisexual, blooming before leaves or at the same time as leaves; tepals 9–21(–45), in whorls of 3–5, subequal, sometimes the outer ones smaller; stamens caducous, anthers dehiscing laterally or introrse-laterally; gynophore absent; carpels free, styles curved outward, 2 ovuled. Fruit an aggregate, usually cylindrical and distorted because of sterile carpels; follicles leathery or ± woody, free, rarely connate, dehiscent along dorsal suture, persistent on receptacles.

About 18 species, distributed in temperate and subtropical SE Asia and N America; 15 species in China; two species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Stem with or without persistent leaf bases. Cataphylls alternating with leaf flushes, sheathing at first, with a pair of inconspicuous stipules. Leaves 2–15, even-pinnate; stipules present; petioles smooth or armed with scattered prickles; rhachis smooth or armed with scattered prickles in lower one-third to two-thirds, ending in a terminal acute spine; leaflets linear to oblong to broadly ovate, sessile to petiolulate, with or without a collar-shaped gland, apex rounded to long-acuminate, margin entire or more commonly serrate in upper leaf. Pollen cones: pedunculate, cream colored to tan to dark to reddish brown, 1–30, emerging from center of leaf crown, cylindrical but gradually tapering toward acute apex, densely pubescent; microsporophylls obscurely peltate, 8– 64 abaxial microsporangia in 2– 4 clusters; pollen exine foveolate. Seed cones: pedunculate, tomentose, green to dark reddish brown, usually solitary but often to 3, cylindrical to slightly ovoid with blunt or slightly acute apex, densely pubescent or glabrous; megasporophylls arranged in 5–21 vertical orthostichies, the exposed tips thick, truncate, hexagonal, with six lateral facets surrounding a central prominent, often depressed facet, each bearing two lateral ovules. Seed with red to orang-red or white sarcotesta and a stony endotesta, ovoid.

A genus about 55 species represented sporadically throughout the Neotropics; one species cultivated in Hong Kong.

Evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs, dioecious or polygamous. Stems and branches usually armed with prickles. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate, rarely unifoliolate or 3-foliolate; leaflets alternate or opposite, with pellucid dots. Inflorescence a panicle or corymbose thyrse, terminal or axillary. Flowers unisexual. Perianth 1–2 whorls. Sepals 4–8. Petals 4–5 or wanting. Male flower: stamens 4–10, anthers often with a apical gland; pistillode pulvinate; style (0–)2–4-lobed. Female flower: staminodes wanting or scalelike; gynoecium 2–5-carpellate; carpels distinct, ovules 2 per carpel; style coherent or distinct; stigma capitate. Fruit 1–5 follicles; pericarp red, glandular-dotted. Follicle 1(–2)-seeded. Seed black, shiny; endosperm fleshy; embryo straight or curved.

About 250 species distributed in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world; about 40 species in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs. Culms stout, erect, many-noded. Leaf blades broad linear, flat. Spikelets unisexual, separated into male and female inflorescences, spikelets of a pair alike. Male inflorescence terminal, consisting of 1 – many spike-like racemes; racemes racemosely arranged on all sides of the main axis and forming a large open panicle. Female inflorescence axillary, enclosed in enveloping foliaceous sheaths, consisting of stout, almost woody axis, which bears the spikelets in densely arranged even vertical rows; glumes broad, truncate or emarginate at apex; lemma hyaline, membranous; palea usually similar to lemma, but small or absent.

Five species distributed in C America, one cultivated (Z. mays) – an important food for mankind and livestock, widely cultivated elsewhere; one species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbaceous vines, monoecious or dioecious. Stems climbing or prostrate. Tendrils unbranched or rarely 2-branched. Leaves petiolate, simple, entire or 3 –5-lobed or -partitioned. Male flowers in racemes or cymes; calyx campanulate or infundibular, 5-lobed; corolla campanulate, 5-lobed; stamens 3, inserted at base of corolla tube; anthers all 2-celled or two 2-celled and one 1-celled, cells straight or slightly curved, connectives thickened; pistillodes present. Female flowers solitary or a few in a cyme; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes present; ovary ovoid or fusiform, 3-locular; ovules many, horizontal; style columnar; stigmas 3. Berries globose or fusiform, indehiscent, small, glabrous. Seeds many, small, elliptic, compressed, smooth or tuberculate, often with thickened margin.

Seven species distributed in Africa and tropical and subtropical Asia; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs, bulbiferous. Bulbs ovoid-globose, coated with tunic. Leaves basal, few to several, linear, appearing with the flowers. Flower solitary, terminal to a slender, hollow scape. Involucre 1, basally tubular, splitting on one side beyond middle. Perianth funnelshaped; tube short or long, often with minute scales near the throat; segments 6, subequal. Stamens 6, 3 long alternating with 3 short, inserted at throat or in tube of perianth; filaments erect to slightly declinate; anther linear, dorsifixed. Ovary inferior, 3-locular, with many ovules in each locule. Stigma 3-lobed or 3-notched. Fruit a capsule, subglobose, loculicidally 3-valved. Seeds black, slightly flattened.

About 40 species in warmer regions of W hemisphere; two species cultivated in China and Hong Kong.

Terrestrial herbs; rhizomes usually elongate, stem-like, creeping, rooting at nodes. Stems erect, terete, foliate. Leaves cauline. Flowers small, inconspicuous, hardly opening, in a terminal spike; sepals subequal, the odd one concave and gibbous at the base; the lateral sepals oblique-ovate; petals small, forming a hood with the odd sepal; lip fleshy, adnate to the sides of the column, parallel to the sepals and petals, fleshy, saccate at the base, bilobed or entire at the apex, the sac containing 2 calli, the apex transversely widened, often bilobed, connected to the saccate base by an elongate fleshy claw with inflexed margin; column short, stout, with 2 apical glands; rostellum large, deeply divided; clinandrium membranous, dilated, cupular; anther ovate-oblong, acute; pollinia 2, sectile, attached to a spathulate or linear-oblanceolate stipe; viscidium subdiscoid; stigmas 2, below the rostellum; ovary cylindrical or ellipsoidal, striatesulcate. Capsules ellipsoidal, striate-sulcate.

About 50 species distributed from tropical Africa to tropical and subtropical Asia; 13 species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Rhizomes branched, tuberous, aromatic. Pseudostems erect, leafy. Leaves distichous, held in plane parallel to rhizome; petiole swollen, cushion-like; leaf blade oblong, lanceolate or linear. Inflorescences conical, arising from rhizomes on peduncle clothed with scale-like sheaths, rarely breaking through leaf sheaths without peduncle; bracts closely imbricate, green or other colour, 1-flowered, persistent; bracteoles not tubular. Calyx tubular, split on 1 side, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube slender; central lobe white or cream, usually wider than lateral lobes. Lateral staminodes adnate to labellum, forming a 3-lobed labellum; central lobe retuse or cleft at apex. Filament short; connective with elongate appendage wrapped around style. Ovary 3-locular; ovules many per locule; placentation axile. Style slender, extending beyond anther locules; stigma not expanded. Capsule dehiscent loculicidally or irregularly. Seeds black, covered by aril; aril white, margin irregularly lacerate.

Between 100 and 150 species in tropical to warm-temperate Asia; 42 species (one introduced) in China; six species in Hong Kong.

Annual or perennial herbs, or subshrubs. Leaves opposite, entire, sessile. Capitula radiate and heterogamous, solitary and terminal on branches. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries in 3 or more series, imbricate, broad and scarious along margin. Receptacle conical or cylindric, chaffy with the palea enclosing the disk florets. Florets all fertile. Marginal ray florets 1‑seriate, or many‑seriate in cultivated form, female, corolla tubes short, ligules spreading. Central tubular florets many, hermaphrodite, corolla 5‑lobed. Stylar branches acute or truncate at apex; anther base entire. Cypselae flattened, subtruncate or obtuse, angulate, with the corolla persistent upon fruiting stage. Pappus none or of 1–3 awns.

About 17 species concentrated in Mexico; one species introduced in Hong Kong for ornamental purposes.

Annual or perennial herbs. Stipules foliaceous, base produced below insertion, peltate, exstipellate. Leaves digitately 2–4-foliolate; leaflets often pellucid-punctate. Racemes or spikes terminal or axillary, interrupted. Bracts paired, enclosing flowers; bracteoles absent. Calyx 2-lipped, upper 2 lobes connate nearly to apex. Flowers usually yellow. Petals subequal, exserted from calyx; vexillum suborbicular, clawed; wings obliquely obovate or oblong; keel incurved, subrostrate. Stamens monadelphous in a closed tube, with long, sub-basifixed and short, dorsifixed anthers alternately arranged. Ovary sessile; ovules numerous; styles filiform; stigma small, terminal. Pods compressed, ventral suture straight, dorsal suture sinuate; segments several, suborbicular, compressed, spinose or glabrous. Seeds orbicular-reniform, estrophiolate.

About 80 species, distributed in tropical and subtropical regions; two species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Submersed perennial herbs. Stems compressed, usually branched. Leaves distichous, linear, flat, ribbon-like, sheathing at base. Flowers monoecious, male and female flowers alternate in 2 rows forming a unilateral spike; perianth absent; male flowers consisting of a single, sessile, 1-celled anther; female flowers with 2 fused carpels; styles slender; stigma 2, filiform. Fruits ovoid, rounded at base, irregularly dehiscent, beaked. Seed solitary, longitudinally ribbed.

About 12 species widely distributed in temperate and warm regions; five species in China; one species in Hong Kong.

Perennial herbs with creeping rhizomes or partly stoloniferous. Culms arising from nodes along stolons, often densely branched at ground level. Leaf blades conspicuously distichous, stiff, flat or involute; ligule short, ciliolate. Inflorescence a cylindrical, dense, spikelike raceme, with spikelets arranged on all sides and appressed to axis, falling off entirely from pedicel. Spikelets laterally compressed, 1-flowered, bisexual; lower glume usually absent, or small, thinly membranous and veinless; upper glume as long as spikelet, enclosing floret, laterally compressed, leathery, apex acute or midvein excurrent into mucro; lemma smaller and hidden inside of the upper glume, membranous, 1 – 3-veined, apex acute or emarginate; palea reduced or absent; lodicules absent. Stamens 3. Styles 2, long, connate at base, stigmas apically exserted. Caryopsis oblong, free; hilum punctiform.

About ten species distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Japan, China, India, New Guinea, and Australasia, several species widely cultivated elsewhere as tropical lawn grasses; five species in China; three species in Hong Kong.

Abelia chinensis R. Br. 糯米條（茶條樹）
Narr. Journey China 376. 1818; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 117. 1988; FGD 4: 292, fig. 174. 2000.

Deciduous shrubs, 0.6–1 m tall. Young branchlets red‑brown, pubescent. Leaves opposite, rarely 3‑whorled, ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 2–5 × 1–3.5 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely crenate, veins densely white villose abaxially. Cymes on upper branchlets, axillary, paniculate. Flowers fragrant. Bracteoles 6, ca. 2 mm. Calyx‑tube cylindric, ca. 6 mm, pubescent; lobes 5, orbicular‑ovate. Stamens inserted at base of corolla‑tube. Achenes cylindric, 3–4 mm, crowned by persistent calyx.

Locality: Stanley, Lantau Island. HK sheet 13287, 24848, 40562.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench 咖啡黃葵（金寶菜）
Methodus 617. 1794; FRPS 49(2): 56, pl. 13: 3. 1984; FGD 2: 187. 1991.
Hibiscus esculentus L., Sp. Pl. 696. 1753; Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 87. 1886.

Tall annual herb, up to 1.5 m tall, strigose-hirsute throughout. Petioles 7–15 cm; stipules linear, 7–8 mm; leaf blade broadly elliptic to orbicular in outline, 10 –30 cm in diam., wider than long, base cordate, palmately 5- or 7-lobed; lobes triangular, the central one 2–6 × 3 – 4.5 cm at the base, margin dentate. Flowers solitary; pedicels 1–2 cm. Corolla yellow with maroon eye, 5–7 cm across. Capsules 8 –10 cm or longer, cylindric, beaked, strigose-hirsute. Seeds glandularly striate.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 6988, 32923; S. Y. Hu 11054 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in Hebei, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Hunan, Hubei, Yunnan, Guangdong; native to India.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (A common food plant of the Mediterranean area, introduced to Hong Kong in some vegetable gardens).
records.uses: Food (A common food plant of the Mediterranean area, introduced to Hong Kong in some vegetable gardens).

records.text:
Abelmoschus moschatus (L.) Medik. 黃葵
Malvenfam. 46. 1787; FRPS 49(2): 58, pl. 15: 1–3. 1984; FGD 2: 188, fig. 116. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 737, pl. 371. 1993.
Hibiscus abelmoschus L., Sp. Pl. 696. 1753; FHK 34. 1861; FKH 48. 1912.

Tall annual or perennial herb, up to 2 m tall, long-hirsute throughout. Petioles 9–15 cm; stipules lanceolate, 6–7 mm; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, 6–15 cm in diam., palmately 5–7-lobed, lobes of the lower ones ovate-triangular, those of the upper ones elliptic or linear, the central lobe 6–12 × 1.5–3 cm. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels 3– 8 cm; bracteoles 7–10, linear, caducous. Corolla 10 cm in diam., yellow, dark purple at base. Staminal tube 2.5 cm. Capsules ovate-ellipsoid, 4 – 6 cm, 2 cm in diam., shortly beaked, long-strigose. Seeds longitudinally and glandularly striate.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Au Mun, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Yuen Tun Ha, Luk Keng, Nam Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool, Wong Wan Chau. Y. S. Lau 770; S. Y. Hu 5618, 12417 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated or naturalized in Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, India; native to the Old World tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal, essential oil, fibre.

Abildgaardia ovata (Burm. f.) Kral 獨穗柄果莎
Sida 4(2): 72. 1971. Carex ovata Burm. f., Fl. Indica 194. 1768.
Fimbristylis ovata (Burm. f.) Kern, Blumea 15(1): 126. 1967; FHN 4: 298. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 274. 2000; FYN 15: 615. 2003; FGD 8: 310. 2007; FOC 23: 217. 2010; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 111. 2004.
Cyperus monostachyus L., Mant. Pl. 2: 180. 1771.
Abildgaardia monostachya (L.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 296. 1805; FHK 389. 1861.
Fimbristylis monostachya (L.) Hassk., Pl. Jav. Rar. 61. 1848; FKH 298. 1912; FRPS 11: 229. 1961.

Perennial; rhizomes short. Culms tufted, 6–40 cm tall, 0.3–0.8 mm thick, trigonous, smooth below, spinulose-scabrous above. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, up to 30 cm × 0.5–1.2 mm, flattish with weakly incurved margins or weakly inrolled; sheath 1–6 cm, dorsally pale green to pale brown, ventrally whitish-hyaline; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3, glume-like or with setaceous blade 0.5–1 cm. Inflorescence reduced to 1 terminal spikelet, with a 1–2 cm long peduncle. Spikelets ovate, ovate-lanceolate, somewhat flattened, 8–15 × 3–7 mm, 10–20-flowered. Glumes 8–20 per spikelet, 2-ranked below, ± spirally arranged above, ovate to broadly ovate, 3–6 × 2–4 mm, apex acute, slightly incurved, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obvoid, trigonous, 2–2.5 × 1.3–1.5 mm, stiple ca. 0.5 mm, white or cream, ± densely verruculose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 604; Y. W. Lam 258, 953.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Abrus cantoniensis Hance 廣州相思子（廣東相思子）
J. Bot. 6: 112. 1868; FKH 82. 1912; FRPS 40: 126. 1994; FGD 229, fig. 127. 2003.

Woody climber, 1–2 m tall. Stems densely yellow-brown hirsute when young, glabrescent in age. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 7–12 pairs; membranous or thin papery, oblong or obovate-oblong, 5 – 12 × 3 – 5 mm, base slightly cordate, apex truncate, apiculate, sparsely pubescent adaxially, strigose abaxially, veins elevated on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, short. Calyx cup-shaped, 3 mm, rarely 4–5-toothed. Corolla purplish; vexillum ovate-elliptic, 8 mm, emarginate; wings and keel equal in length with vexillum. Stamens 9. Ovary subsessile. Pods oblong, 2.2 – 3 × 0.7–0.8 cm, compressed, beaked, sparsely yellowish pubescent, 4 – 7-seeded. Seeds oblong, 5– 6 mm, dark brown or yellow brown.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Hung Fa Ling, Po Sam Pai, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3267; HK sheet 7702, 36000.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan; Thailand.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Aug. – Sep.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Abrus mollis Hance 毛相思子
J. Bot. 9(101): 130. 1871; FKH 82. 1912; FRPS 40: 125. 1994; FGD 5: 228. 2003.

Climbing shrub. Branches, leaf-rachis and petioles yellow-villose. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 10 – 16 pairs, membranous, oblong or the uppermost one obovate, 1 – 2.5 × 0.5–1 cm, base rounded, apex truncate, apiculate, villose on both surfaces, but the hairs more dense and white abaxially. Racemes axillary, 3–7 cm. Flowers 4 – 6-fasciculate at nodes of rachis. Calyx campanulate, grey-villose. Corolla pink or purplish. Pods oblong, compressed, 3.5–5 × 0.8–1 cm, densely villose, dehiscent, 4–9-seeded. Seeds ovate, 5 × 3.5 cm, compressed, dark brown or black, brilliant.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 220; Y. S. Lau 768, 1366.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Indochina.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul. –Aug.; fruiting: Sep. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), materials (beads), seeds very poisonous.

Abrus precatorius L. 相思子
Syst. Nat. (ed. 12), 2: 472. 1767; FHK 92. 1861; FKH 82. 1912; FRPS 40: 123. 1994; FGD 5: 228. 2003.

Climbing shrub, much branched, minutely white strigose. Leaves even-pinnate, 10–15 cm; leaflets 8–15 pairs, membranous, oblong or several distal pairs oblanceolate-oblong, 10 – 22 × 4–6 mm, base rounded, apex truncate, apiculate. Racemes axillary, 3–6 cm, many-flowered, crowded in a head-shaped cluster. Calyx campanulate, shallowly 4-lobed, whitely strigose. Corolla purplish, petals nearly equal in length; vexillum broadly ovate, with deltoid claw; wings and keel very narrow. Stamens 9. Ovary hairy. Pods oblong, 2.5 – 3 × 1 – 1.5 cm, slightly turgid, densely strigose, dehiscent, valves leathery, 5-seeded. Seeds elliptic, 5 – 6 mm, bright scarlet, with a black spot on one side.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 393; P. S. Choi 363; HK sheet 39272.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical regions.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Sep.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.

Abutilon indicum (L.) Sweet 磨盤草
Hort. Brit. 54. 1826; FHK 33. 1861; FKH 47. 1912; FHN 2: 94. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 37. 1984; FTW ed. 2, 3: 739, pl. 372. 1993.
Sida indica L., Cent. Pl. 2: 26. 1756; FRPS 49(2): 37. 1984; FGD 2: 198, fig. 126. 1991; FTW ed 2, 3: 739. 1993.

Annual or perennial herb, 0.5 –1 m tall, much branched, greyish stellate puberulent throughout. Petioles 2–4 cm; stipules subulate, 1–2 mm; leaf blade ovate or suborbicular, 1.5–7(–9) × 2.5–7 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin coarsely dentate. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels slender, 4– 5(–7) cm, articulate towards apex. Calyx patelliform, 6 –10 mm across; lobes 5, broadly ovate, mucronate. Corolla yellow, 2–2.5 cm across. Staminal tube stellate-hirsute. Fruit depressed globose, 1.5 cm in diam., top flat; carpels 15 –20, very short-awned. Seeds reniform, stellate-pilose.

Locality: Deep Bay, Yung Shue O, Tai Po, Shatin, Yuen Tun Ha, Plover Cove, Sam A Tsuen, Stonecutters Island, Lantau Island, Leung Shuen Wan Chau (Tall Island). Y. S. Lau 1275; HK sheet 11174; S. Y. Hu 5769, 12617 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wastelands, thickets near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

Abutilon pictum (Gillies ex Hook. & Arn.) Walp. 金鈴花
Repert. Bot. Syst. 1: 324. 1842.
Abutilon striatum Dicks. ex Lindl., Edwards's Bot. Reg. 39. 1839; FRPS 49(2): 33, pl. 8: 2–3. 1984.
Sida picta Gillies ex Hook., Bot. Misc. 3: 154. 1833.

Shrub, to 2 m tall; branchlets glabrous. Leaves 5 –7 cm in diam., palmately (3 –)5–7-lobed, basal portion reniform, large lobes caudate at apex, glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent abaxially. Flowers golden-orange with red veins, solitary, axillary; peduncles slender, 10 –17 cm, bending at anthesis. Calyx cup-shaped, deeply cleft; lobes deltoid lanceolate, 1.3 –1.8 cm. Corolla lantern-like, hanging; petals imbricate, clawed, 4 cm, 1.6 cm across middle, branches of red veins reticulate. Staminal column exceeding petals, basal threefourth sterile, styles 10 –12, exceeding petals, distinct; stigmas discoid. Fruit not known.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2658; HK sheet 32799; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22038 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in China; native of Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Oct.

Abutilon theophrasti Medik. 苘麻
Malvenfam. 28. 1787; FRPS 49(2): 36. 1984; FGD 2: 199. 1991.
Sida abutilon L., Sp. Pl. 685. 1753.
Abutilon avicennae Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 251, t. 135, fig. 1. 1791.

Annual herb or subshrub, 1–2 m tall, much branched. Branches, petioles and pedicels stellate puberulous. Petioles 3–12 cm; leaf blade suborbiculate, 3.5 –15 cm in diam., base cordate, apex long-acuminate, margin slightly crenulate, stellate hirsute adaxially, tomentose abaxially. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 1–3 cm, articulate towards apex. Calyx cup-shaped, densely tomentellate; lobes 5, orbicular, oblong in fruit, mucronate. Corolla yellow; lobes obovate, ca. 1cm. Staminal tube glabrous, filamentiferous at apex. Fruits black, depressed globose, 2 cm across, top flat; carpels 12 to 16, strongly birostrate, awns 5 mm. Seeds reniform, stellate-pilose.

Locality: Yuen Long, Mo Fan Heung, Jubilee Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1498; HK sheet 36223; S. Y. Hu 10742 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cosmopolitan in the temperate region of the N hemisphere.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Materials (fibre).

Acacia auriculiformis Cunn. ex Benth. 耳果相思（耳葉相思）
London J. Bot. 1: 377. 1842.

Evergreen trees, to 20 m tall. Bark gray-white, smooth. Branches pendulous; branchlets angular, glabrous, with conspicuous lenticels. Phyllodium falcate-oblong, 10–20 × 1.5 –4(–6) cm, conspicuous main veins 3 or 4, both ends attenuate. Spikes 1 to several, fasciculate, axillary or terminal, 3.5–8 cm. Flowers orange-yellow. Calyx 0.5–1 mm, shallowly dentate. Petals oblong, 1.5–2 mm. Filaments 2.5–4 mm. Ovary densely puberulous Pods contorted when mature, 5–8 × 0.8 – 1.2 cm, valves ligneous. Seeds ca. 12, black, ca. 5–3.5 mm, encircled by a 2-folded, yellow, orange to red aril.

Locality: Widely cultivated in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3321, 3322.
Dist.: Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi (cultivated); native to N Australia and New Guinea.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep. –Nov.; fruiting: Oct.–Apr.
Uses: Afforestation, environmental.

Acacia concinna (Willd.) DC. 藤金合歡
Prodr. 2: 464. 1825; FHK 91. 1861; FKH 91. 1912; I. C. Nielsen, Fl. Camb, Laos, Vietn. 19: 58. 1981; FGD 5: 154. 2003.
Mimosa concinna Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 1039. 1806.
Acacia sinuata (Lour.) Merr., Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc., n.s., 24(2): 186. 1935; FRPS 39: 34. 1988.
Mimosa sinuata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 653. 1790.

Climber; branchlets and leaf-rachises grey-tomentose, with numerous hooked prickles on branches and petioles. Stipules ovate-cordate, deciduous. Leaves bipinnate, 10 – 20 cm; pinnae 6 –18 pairs, 8 –12 cm, with a gland near the base of petiole and between the uppermost pinnae; leaflets 15–25 pairs, linear-oblong, 8–12 × 2–3 mm, greenish adaxially, glaucous abaxially, hirsute or glabrescent on both surfaces, margin ciliate; midvein near upper margin. Flowers white or yellowish, fragrant, in globular heads of 9 –12 mm in diam., forming in a panicle; peduncle and branches tomentose. Calyx funnel-shaped, 2 mm. Corolla slightly exserted. Pods brown, strap-shaped, 8 – 15 × 2 – 3 cm, margin straight or slightly sinuate. Seeds 6–10.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Wong Chuk Hang, Shek O, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1521, 1587; K. Y. Tam 110.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Yunnan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul.– Dec.
Uses: Material (tannin), medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Acacia sinuata (Lour.) Merr. is based on Mimosa sinuata Lour., but E. D. Merrill did not mention any type specimen of the species and the name is therefore regarded as dubious (cf. Nielson 1980).
records.uses:
Material (tannin), medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Acacia sinuata (Lour.) Merr. is based on Mimosa sinuata Lour., but E. D. Merrill did not mention any type specimen of the species and the name is therefore regarded as dubious (cf. Nielson 1980).

records.text:
Acacia confusa Merr. 台灣相思
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 5(1): 27. 1910; FRPS 39: 24. 1988; FGD 5: 151. 2003.
Acacia richii auct. non A. Grey: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 91. 1912.

Evergreen tree, 6–15 m tall, glabrous. Branches grey or brown, unarmed; branchlets slender. Leaves reduced to simple phyllodia, alternate, leathery, lanceolate, 6–10 × 0.5 – 1.3 cm, straight or slightly falcate, narrowed to both ends, apex slightly obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces, conspicuously 3 – 5(–8)-parallel-veined. Flowers numerous, in globose heads of 6– 10 mm in diam., solitary or 2–3-fasciculate in axil of phyllodia. Peduncles slender, 8–10 mm. Flowers golden-yellow, fragrant. Calyx half as long as corolla. Petals greenish, 2 mm. Stamens numerous, exserted. Ovary tawny villose; style 4 mm. Pods flat, 4– 9(–12) × 0.7 – 1 cm, black brown.

Locality: Widely cultivated in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1807; Y. S. Lau 2138; L. T. Lo 140.
Distribution: Mostly cultivated in Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan, Jiangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; Philippines, Indonesia, Fiji.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Oct.; fruiting: Aug. – Dec.
Uses: Afforestation, environmental.

Acacia farnesiana (L.) Willd. 金合歡
Sp. Pl. 4: 1083. 1806; FHK 101. 1861; FKH 91. 1912; FRPS 39: 28. 1988; FGD 5: 152. 2003.
Mimosa farnesiana L., Sp. Pl. 521. 1753.

Shrub or small tree, 2–4 m tall, many-branched; bark rough, brown; branchlets zigzag, with small lenticels. Stipules spine-like, 1–2 cm, but shorter in short branchlets. Leaves bipinnate, 2–7 cm, leaf-rachis villose, glandular; pinnae 4 –8 pairs, 1.5–3.5 cm, axillary; leaflets 10–20 pairs, linear-oblong, 2 – 6 × 1 – 1.5 mm, glabrous. Flowers yellow, fragrant, in axillary heads of 1 – 3, 1 – 1.5 cm in diam. Peduncles hairy, 1–3 cm; bracts borne on apex of peduncle or nearly so. Calyx 1.5 mm, 5-toothed. Petals 2.5 mm, connate into a tube, 5-toothed. Stamens twice as long as corolla. Ovary cylindric, puberulent. Pods turgid, subcylindric, 3 – 7 × 8 – 15 mm, brown, glabrous, straight or curved, scarcely dehiscent, filled with a pith which separates seeds from each other. Seeds several, brown, ovate, 6 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Yuen Long, Cheung Chau (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1141; HK sheet 1585, 8754.
Distribution: Cultivated in Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; native to tropical America, widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep. –Nov.
Uses: Environmental (ornamental, honey, soil improver).

Acacia mangium Willd. 大葉相思（馬占相思）
Sp. Pl., ed. 4, 4(2): 1053 – 1054. 1806.

Evergreen tree to 30 m tall, trunk usually straight and may exceed half tree height. Branchlets stout, very acutely angled, glabrous. Phyllodium falcate, normally 11 – 25 × 3.3 – 9 cm wide, glabrous, with 3 or 4 prominent longitudinal veins that are clearly confluent at the base but which remain separate from the lower margin, minor veins strongly anastomosing to form a prominent reticulum. Spikes cylindrical, 8–11 cm long, white to cream; peduncles 6 – 10 mm long. Pods tightly coiled and twisted, sometimes tightly spirally coiled, 3–5 mm wide, leathery to subwoody. Seeds with a bright orange aril.

Locality: Widely cultivated in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3323
Distribution: Guangdong (cultivated); native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug. – Oct.; fruiting: Oct.– Jun.
Uses: Afforestation, environmental.

Acacia pennata (L.) Willd. 羽葉金合歡

Sp. Pl. 4(2): 1090. 1806; FRPS 39: 36. 1988; FGD 5: 154. 2003.

Acacia hainanensis Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 3: 86. 1913.

Acacia pennata subsp. hainanensis I. C. Nielsen, Adansonia ser. 2, 19(3): 352. 1980.


Climber with copious scattered prickles. Branchlets and leaf-rachises rusty pubescent, with plate-shaped glands at the base of petioles and between upper pinnae. Pinnae 8–22 pairs; leaflets 30–54 pairs, linear, 5–10 × 0.5–1.5 mm, densely crowded, base truncate, apex slightly obtuse, margin ciliate, midvein more close to upper margin. Flowers in globular heads of 1 cm in diam., forming axillary or terminal panicle. Peduncles 1–2 cm, solitary or 2–3-fasciculate, dark brown pubescent. Calyx subcampanulate, 1.5 mm, 5-toothed. Corolla 2 mm. Ovary puberulent. Pods strap-shaped, 9–20 × 2–3.5 cm, glabrous or puberulous when young, margin slightly sinuate. Seeds 8–12, oblong, flat.


Locality: Sha Tau Kok. F. W. Xing 8891.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Yunnan; tropical Asia and Africa.

Ecology: Thin forests, usually climbing on shrubs or small trees. Flowering: Mar. – Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Apr.

Acalypha australis L. 鐵莧菜（朴草）
Sp. Pl. 1004. 1753; FKH 239. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 100, pl. 24: 1 – 6. 1996; FGD 5: 96, fig. 57. 2003.
Acalypha chinensis Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 880. 1826.

Annual herb, 20–50 cm tall; branchlets slender, appressedly pubescent to pilose. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–6 cm, pubescent; stipules lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, pubescent; leaf blade narrowly ovate, subrhomboid or broadly lanceolate, 3–9 × 1–5 cm, base cuneate, rarely obtuse, apex short-acuminate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent on midvein abaxially, margin crenulate-serrate; basal veins 3. Spikes axillary, rarely terminal, 1.5–5 cm, with female flowers at base and male flowers on the upper part; female bracts ovate-cordate, 1.4–2.5 × 1–2 cm in fruiting time, margin with triangular serratures, pilose on the palmate veins; male bracts ovate, ca. 0.5 mm. Male flowers: 5–7 clustered in axil of bract; calyx-lobes 4, ovate, ca. 0.5 mm; stamens 7 – 8. Female flowers: 1 – 3 in axil of bract, sessile; calyx-lobes 3, narrowly ovate, 0.5–1 mm, pilose; ovary pilose; styles 3, ca. 2 mm; stigma lacerate. Capsules of 3 bivalved cocci, globose, 4 mm in diam., pilose, the hairs thickened at base.

Locality: Bowen Rd., Victoria Peak, Kowloon Railway Terminus, Fanling, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 1913, 2809; HK sheet 36072; S. Y. Hu 10698 (CUHK).
Distribution:Widely spread almost over all provinces of China; Russia, India, Japan, Korea, Laos, Vietnam, Philippines and N Australia.
Ecology:Wastelands, roadsides and cultivated fields. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. –Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Acalypha hispida Burm. f. 紅穗鐵莧菜（狗尾紅）
Fl. Indica 303, pl. 61: 1. 1768; FRPS 44(2): 110. 1996; FGD 5: 99. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 26. 2005.

Shrub, 1 – 3 m tall; branchlets initially grey-tomentellous, glabrous in age. Leaves papery; petioles 4 – 8 cm, pubescent; stipules narrowly triangular, 0.6 – 1 cm, pilose; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate, 8–20 × 5–14 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded or slightly cordate, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrate, subglabrous adaxially, pilose on veins abaxially, basal veins 3–5. Female spikes axillary, 15 – 30 cm, pendulous, rachis pubescent; bracts of female flowers ovate-rhomboid, ca. 1 mm, entire, pubescent abaxially. Female flowers: 3 – 7 clustered in axil of bracts; calyx-lobes 3 – 4, subovate, ca. 0.8 mm, apex acute, pubescent; ovary subglobose, densely yellowish hirsute; styles 3, 6 – 7 mm, crimson, lacerate. Male flowers and fruits unknown.

Locality: Cultivated in Gardens. Y. S. Lau 1976; HK sheet 6121; S. Y. Hu 5335 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to the Pacific Islands, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb. –Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Acalypha indica L. 熱帶鐵莧菜（山朴草）
Sp. Pl. 1003. 1753; FHK 303. 1861; FKH 239. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 102. 1996; FGD 5: 97. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 26. 2005.

Annual erect herb, 0.5–1 m tall; young branches slightly pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 1.5–3.5 cm, pubescent; stipules narrowly triangular, ca. 1 mm; leaf blade rhomboid-ovate or ovate, 2–3.5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin serrulate on distal half, pubescent along veins on both surfaces; basal veins 5. Spikes axillary, rarely terminal, 2–7 cm, interrupted, with 1–8 distant orbicular leafy bracts, of 4–5 mm in diam., each containing 1–2 sessile female flowers, and ending in a small slender male catkin, with ovate-triangular or broadly triangular bracts of 0.5 mm, each subtending 5–7 male flowers. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 0.5 mm; calyx-lobes 4, narrowly ovate, 0.4 mm; stamens 8. Female flowers: sepals 3, narrowly triangular, ca. 0.5 mm, sparsely ciliate; ovary hairy, styles 3, 2.5–3 mm; lacerate. Capsules of 3 bivalved cocci, ca. 2 mm in diam., pubescent.

Locality: Shau KeiWan. HK sheet 6117.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Cambodia,Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, tropical regions of Africa and C America.
Ecology:Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar. – Oct.
Notes: A common weed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa.

Acalypha lanceolata Willd. 麻葉鐵莧菜
Sp. Pl. 4: 524. 1805; FRPS 44(2): 103, pl. 24: 7 – 9. 1996; FGD 5: 97. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 29. 2005.
Acalypha fallax Müll. Arg., Linnaea 34: 43. 1865; FKH 239. 1912.

Annual erect herb, 40–70 cm tall; young branches densely tawny pubescent and sparsely hirsute. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–5.5 cm, densely pubescent; stipules linear-lanceolate, ca. 4 – 10 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade rhomboid-ovate or oblong-ovate, 4 – 8 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate, sparsely hairy on both surfaces; basal veins 5 – 7. Spikes axillary, 1– 2.5 cm, with female flowers at base and male flowers on the distal part, sometimes with 1 – 3 abnormal female flowers at apex of rachis; bracts of female flowers 3 – 9, half orbicular, 2.5 – 4 × 5 – 6 mm, with short acute teeth, tomentose abaxially; bracts of male flowers lanceolate, ca. 0.5 mm. Male flowers: 5 – 7 clustered in axil of bracts; pedicels 0.5 mm; calyx-lobes 4; stamens 8. Female flowers: solitary in axil of bracts; calyx-lobes 3, narrowly triangular, ca. 0.5 mm; ovary pubescent; styles 3, ca. 2 mm, lacerate; ovary oblate-obovoid, 1-locular; style 1, inserted at base of ovary, lacerate. Capsules of 3 bivalved cocci, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., pubescent; seeds ovoid, ca. 1.8 mm, smooth.

Locality: Tsing Yi Island. M. F. Lui, K. M. To, C. P. Jung s.n. (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan; S to SE Asia and Pacific Islands.
Ecology:Wastelands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Mar. – Oct.

Acalypha suirenbiensis Yamam. 花蓮鐵莧菜
J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 5: 178. 1935; FRPS 44(2): 111. 1996.

Shrub; young branches densely pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 8 – 20 cm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate, 10 – 20 × 8 – 15 cm, base obtuse, subtruncate or shallowly cordate, apex caudate-acuminate, margin subentire or crenate-serrate, with tufts of hairs in axil of veins; basal veins 5. Flowers dioecious; female spikes axillary, 10 – 25 cm; peduncles 2 – 5 cm; bracts ovate, ca. 1 mm, hairy. Female flowers: solitary in axil of bracts; calyx-lobes 3, ovate, ca. 1 mm; ovary pubescent; styles 3, 2.5 – 5 mm, lacerate. Male flower not seen. Capsules of 3 bivalved cocci, globose, ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 23035 (CUHK).
Distribution: Taiwan (Lanyu).
Ecology: Flowering: Jul. –Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Acalypha wilkesiana Müll. Arg. 紅桑

Prodr. 15(2): 817. 1866; FRPS 44(2): 112. 1996; FGD 5: 99. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 32. 2005.


Shrub, 1–4 m tall; young branches pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 2–3 cm, pilose; stipules narrowly triangular, ca. 8 × 2–3 mm, pubescent, leaf blade broadly ovate, 10 – 18 × 6 – 12 cm, rounded or shortly acute at base, apex acuminate, margin crenate-dentate, glabrous except on the veins, bronzy-green variously mottled with shades of red and purple; basal veins 3 – 5. Spikes slender, axillary, the male 10 – 20 cm, with ovate bracts, the female 5 – 10 cm with broader and larger bracts. Male flowers: 9 – 17 clustered in axil of bracts; pedicels ca. 1 mm; calyx-lobes 4, narrowly ovate, ca. 0.7 mm; stamens 8. Female flowers: 1–2 in axil of bracts, sessile; calyx-lobes 3–4, narrowly ovate or triangular-ovate, 0.5 – 1 mm, ciliate; ovary densely hairy; styles 3, 6 – 7 mm, lacerate. Capsules of 3 bivalved cocci, ca. 4 mm in diam., sparsely villose.


Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1964; HK sheet 24845; S. Y. Hu 6166 (CUHK).

Distribution: Native of Polynesia and Fiji, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.

Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.

Uses: Ornamental.

Notes: There are two cultivars commonly cultivated in Hong Kong, Acalypha wilkesiana ‘Marginata’ [金邊紅桑(金紅桑)] with red leaf margin and A. wilkesiana ‘Java White’ (白邊紅桑) with white leaf margin.
records.uses:
Ornamental.

Notes: There are two cultivars commonly cultivated in Hong Kong, Acalypha wilkesiana ‘Marginata’ [金邊紅桑(金紅桑)] with red leaf margin and A. wilkesiana ‘Java White’ (白邊紅桑) with white leaf margin.

records.text:
Acampe rigida (Buch.-Ham. ex Sm.) P. F. Hunt 多花脆蘭
Kew Bull. 24: 98. 1970; FRPS 19: 286, pl. 43: 1–2. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 735, pl. 310. 2000; FGD 7: 496, fig. 256. 2006; FOC 25: 449. 2009.
Aerides rigida Buch.-Ham. ex Sm., Rees Cyclopedia 39. 1819.
Acampe multiflora (Lindl.) Lindl., Fol. Orch. Acampe 1. 1853; FHK 358. 1861; FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1–2): 41. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 112. 1977.

Roots thick and strong, many, branching profusely, up to 50 cm long, 3–10 mm in diam.; stem upright, monopodial, leafy, stout, covered by overlapping leaf sheaths. Leaves distichous, dull green, thick coriaceous, linear, 20–35 × 4–4.5 cm, base folded, apex obtuse or obliqueretuse, midrib inconspicuous above, elevated beneath. Inflorescence an axillary panicle; flowers non-resupinate, very fleshy, creamy white, turning yellow when old, speckled with bright reddish purple on the outside and streaked horizontally on the inside; sepals all alike in size, shape and colour, oblong, slightly incurved, apex rounded or obtuse, 11 × 6–7 mm; petals narrower than the sepals, spathulate, 12 × 4.5 mm, apex rounded; lip very fleshy, non-movable, midlobe tongue-like, ovate, creamy yellow tinged lavender with irregular red specks above and below, margin erose, apex curved downwards, lateral lobes wall-like, velvety inside; disk with a yellow median ridge; column fleshy, very short, 2 mm high, bright purplish red; anther yellow, apical to the column; pollinia fixed at the end of a narrow caudicle; ovary smooth, with inconspicuous lines.

Locality: Shek O, Kowloon Peak, Fo Tan Valley, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. K. Y. Chan 1374 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 7352 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2024, 2364.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; S and SE Asia.
Ecology: Damp rocks under trees along streams. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Acanthephippium striatum Lindl. 錐囊罎花蘭（中華罎花蘭）
Edwards's Bot. Reg. 24(Misc.): 41. 1838; FOC 25: 310. 2009.
Acanthephippium sinense Rolfe, Kew Bull. 142. 1913; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25: 11. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 90, fig. 50. 1977; FRPS 18: 323. 1999; FGD 7: 404, fig. 206. 2006; Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 129. 2004.

Terrestrial perennial herb; pseudobulb ovoid-cylindrical, covered with several membranous sheaths. Leaves papery, obovateelliptic, 20–25 cm, base attenuating into a petiole, apex acute or acuminate. Flowers medium-sized, the odd sepal elliptic-oblong, 1.8–2 × 0.8–1 cm, apex obtuse; lateral ones oblique ovate, slightly wider than the odd sepal, with a 1.3 cm long conical mentum at base; petals ovate-oblong, 2 × 0.7 cm, apex acuminate; lip 3-lobed, lateral lobes erect, apex rounded, curved forward; midlobe rhombic-triangular, 10 × 8 mm, lamellate, apex acute, disk becoming thick near the two lateral lobes, with 3 ridges; column 1.3 cm, with a 8–10 mm long column-foot; pollinia 8 in 2 groups; ovary cylindrical.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 10166, 13699 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.

Acanthus ilicifolius L. 老鼠簕
Sp. Pl. 639. 1753; FHK 263. 1861; FKH 199. 1912; FHN 3: 553. 1974; FRPS 70: 45. 2002.
Dilivaria ilicifolia (L.) Juss., Gen. Pl. 103. 1789.

Erect shrubs, up to 2 m tall; stems rarely branched, stout, glabrous. Petioles thick, 3–6 mm, glabrous, with 2 stipule‑like spines at base; leaf blades oblong to oblong‑lanceolate, 6–14 × 2–5 cm, pinnatifid, base acute, apex truncate, margin with few large spines, glabrous, lateral veins 5–7 pairs, reaching to the teeth. Spikes terminal, to 16.5 cm; bracts broad ovate, 7–8 mm, innocuous, caducous; bracteoles ovate, about 5 mm, leathery. Calyx‑lobes 4, 2 outer ones larger, 10–13 mm, apex emarginate, scarious at margins, sometimes crispate, 2 inner ovate, about 10 mm, entire. Corolla pale, 3–4 cm; tubes 6 mm, upper lips reduced, lower lip obovate, about 3 mm, thin‑leathery, apex trifid, soft hairy on outer side, with a stripe of 3–4 mm broad on both sides of upper parts. Stamens 4, equal, anther‑theca 1, longitudinal scissile, with a line of hairs on both sides of suture; filaments 1.5 cm; anther‑theca longitudinally scissile; style 2.2 cm, longitudinal lineated; stigma 2‑fid. Capsule elliptic, 2.5–3 cm; seeds 4, ellipsoidal, complanate, light yellow.

Locality: Shek O, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Nam Sang Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2279, 2290; Y. S. Lau 225, 2216.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; SE Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Mangrove swamps. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Acanthus ilicifolius L. var. xiamenensis (R. T. Zhang) Y. F. Deng, N. H. Xia & H. B. Chen 廈門老鼠簕
J. Trop. Subtrop. Bot. 14: 530. 2006.
Acanthus xiamenensis R. T. Zhang, Wuyi Sci. J. 5: 237. 1985.
Acanthus ebracteatus Vahl. var. xiamenensis (R. T. Zhang) C. Y. Wu & C. C. Hu, FRPS 70: 47. 2002.

Differs from var. ilicifolius in its leaf margin serrate or subentire, lateral veins not reaching to the teeth, and netted near the margin.

Locality: Mai Po, Tai Po. S. Y. Hu 11542 (CAS); S. Y. Hu 13544 (IBSC, PE).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Mangrove swamps. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Acer buergerianum Miq. 三角槭
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavi 2: 88. 1865; FRPS 46: 183, pl. 55: 1. 1981; FFJ 3: 306, fig. 207. 1987; FGD 3: 274. 1995.
Acer trifidum f. buergerianum (Miq.) Schwer., Gartenflora 42: 258. 1893.

Deciduous tree, 4–10(–20) m tall, andro-monoecious. Bark rough, brown. Young branchlets purplish green, old branchlets waxy. Leaves simple; petioles slender, 2.5–5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade membranous, ovate, obovate or elliptic, (3–)6–10 × 4–6 cm, base rounded or cuneate, usually 3-lobed; middle lobe triangular-ovate, apex acute or shortly acuminate; lateral lobes short, margin usually entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glaucous; primary veins 3(–5), conspicuous abaxially. Inflorescence terminal, corymbose, ca. 3 cm wide. Peduncles 1.5–2 cm. Sepals 5, ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous. Petals 5, yellowish white, narrowly lanceolate or spathulate-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 8, nearly as long as sepals or shorter. Ovary densely yellowish villous. Fruit yellowish brown; nutlets strongly convex, 6–7 mm in diam.; wing broad at middle, contracted at base, wings spreading at acute angle.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 373.
Distribution: S, E, C & SW China; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Aug.

Acer reticulatum Champ. 網脈槭（長葉槭）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 312. 1851; FHK 47. 1861; FRPS 46: 216. 1981; FGD 3: 277. 1995.
Acer laevigatum var. reticulatum (Champ.) Rehder, Trees & Shrubs 1(4): 180. 1905.
Acer laevigatum subsp. reticulatum (Champ.) A.E. Murray, Kalmia 8: 6. 1977.

Evergreen tree, 5 m tall, andromonoecious. Bark deep grey. Branchlets slender, glabrous, green when young, yellowish green when old. Leaves simple; petioles 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, sulcate adaxially; leaf blade leathery, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 10–15 × 4–5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, margin entire, light green on both surfaces, abaxially with tufts of hairs at vein axils when young; 3-veined at base, lateral veins 7 or 8 pairs, reticulate veins slightly prominent abaxially. Inflorescence terminal, corymbose paniculate, 2 × 3 cm; peduncles 2–3 cm, glabrous. Sepals 5, pale purple or pale green, ovate or ovate-oblong, ca. 2 mm. Petals 5, white, spathulate, longer than sepals, slightly retuse. Stamens 8, filaments ca. 6 mm, glabrous. Ovary slightly pubescent. Fruit purplish at first, later becoming yellow; nutlets strongly convex, ellipsoidal or ellipsoidal-oblong, ca. 6–8 mm in diam., wings spreading at obtuse angle.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Shek O, Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Fo Tan, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 877; P. S. Choi 386; Y. W. Lam 154.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Winter; fruiting: Spring.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Gough and Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Acer sino-oblongum F. P. Metcalf 濱海槭（華南飛蛾樹）
Lingnan Sci. J. 11: 202. 1932; FRPS 46: 205, pl. 58: 3. 1981; FGD 3: 276. 1995.
Acer oblongum Benth., FHK 47. 1861, non Wall. ex DC. (1824).

Evergreen tree, 5–7 m tall, andro-monoecious. Bark brownish grey, rough. Branchlets glabrous, purple to brownish purple, lenticels ovate or rounded. Leaves simple; petioles 1–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, elliptical or elliptical-oblong, 6–9 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate, margin entire, glaucous abaxially; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, slightly prominent abaxially. Inflorescence terminal, corymbose; peduncle ca. 1 cm. Flowers greenish yellow. Sepals 5, obovate-oblong, ca. 4 mm. Petals 5, oblanceolate, as long as sepals. Stamens 8. Ovary glabrous. Fruiting pedicels 5–10 mm, villous. Nutlets pale yellowish brown, strongly convex; wings spreading at acute angle.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Tam, Repulse Bay, Aberdeen, Mount Nicholson, Pat Sin Leng, Bride's Pool, Tsing Yi. Y. S. Lau 1008, 1259, 2670.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1854 and 1855.

Acer tutcheri Duthie 嶺南槭
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1: 16. 1908; FKH 67. 1912; FRPS 46: 175, pl. 51: 2. 1981; FFJ 3: 303. 1987; FGD 3: 274, pl. 184. 1995.
Acer oliverianum var. tutcheri (Duthie) Metc. ex Kussm., Handb. Laubgeh. 1: 104. 1959.

Deciduous tree, 5–10(–15) m tall, andro-monoecious. Bark brown or dark brown. Branchlets slender, glabrous, green or purplish green when young. Leaves simple; petioles 2–3 cm, slender, glabrous; leaf blade membranous, broadly ovate, 6–7 × 8–11 cm, base rounded or subtruncate, usually 3(–5)-lobed; lobes triangular-ovate, rarely ovate-oblong, apex acuminate, rarely caudate-acuminate, margin sparsely serrulate, sometimes entire near base, glabrous on both surfaces or hairy at vein axils abaxially; basal veins 3. Inflorescence terminal, 6–7 cm. Peduncles ca. 3 cm. Sepals 4, ovate-oblong, yellowish green. Petals 4, obovate, pale yellowish white, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens 8, filaments glabrous. Ovary densely white pilose. Fruit yellowish; nutlets convex, ca. 6 mm in diam.; wings spreading obtusely or almost horizontally.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 3248; Y. W. Lam 1360; K. Y. Tam 104.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Sep.
Note: The type specimen (W. J. Tutcher s.n., K) was collected by W. J. Tutcher from Lantau Island in 1894. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Achyranthes aspera L. 土牛膝
Sp. Pl. 204. 1753; FHK 285. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 407. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 227. 1979; FGD 4: 108. 2000; FOC 5: 424. 2003.

Perennial herb, 50–120 cm tall, greyish pubescent throughout. Stems quadrangular, woody at the base. Leaves papery; petioles 5 –15 mm; leaf blade ovate, obovate or oblong-elliptic, 4 –10 × 1.5 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire. Spikes terminal or axillary, 10 –30 cm. Flowers green, reflexed after anthesis. Bracteoles subulate and spiny, 2.5 –3.5 mm, base ovate, membranous, not lobed. Perianth-segments 5, lanceolate, 4.5 – 5 mm, with a hard and sharp point. Stamens 5; filaments united at the base; staminodes apex fimbriate. Utricle ellipsoid, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. Gibbs 10192; Y. S. Lau 1505; HK sheet 36017.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SW to SE Asia; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Wastelands and grassy places near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Achyranthes bidentata Blume 牛膝
Bijdr. 545. 1825; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 408, fig. 218. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 228. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 391. 1996; FGD 4: 108, fig, 68. 2000; FOC 5: 425. 2003.

Perennial herb, 25–120 cm tall. Stems angled or quadrangular; branches initially pubescent, glabrous in age. Leaves papery; petioles 5–30 mm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate, elliptic or ellipticlanceolate, rarely oblanceolate, 4.5–13 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, pubescent on both surfaces. Spikes terminal or axillary, 3 – 5 cm; rachis densely pubescent. Flowers green, spreading or reflexed after anthesis. Bracteoles subulate and spiny, 2.5 –3 mm, with 2 minute basal auricles. Perianth-segments 5, lanceolate, 3 –5 mm, with a hard and sharp point. Stamens 5; filaments united at the base; staminodes apex truncate. Utricle ellipsoid, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. HK sheet 31567.
Distribution: Most provinces of China; E Asia, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, W tropical Africa, S W Pacific.
Ecology: Wastelands, bushes and woodlands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Traditional Chinese medicine.

Acmena acuminatissima (Blume) Merr. & L. M. Perry 肖蒲桃
J. Arnold Arbor. pl. 1019: 205. 1938; FHN 2: 11, fig. 295. 1965; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 995, fig. 3720. 1972; FRPS 53(1): 60, pl. 10: 1 –6. 1984; FGX 1: 914. 1991; FGD 3: 180, fig. 128. 1995.
Eugenia acuminatissima (Blume) Kurz, Prelim. Rep. Forest Pegu App. A 63, App. B 51. 1875; FKH 105. 1912.
Syzygium acuminatissimum (Blume) DC., Prodr. 3: 261. 1828; FOC 13: 343. 2007.
Myrtus acuminatissima Blume, Bijdr. 1088. 1826.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Branchlets terete or obtusely angulate. Petioles 5–8 mm; leaf blade leathery, ovate-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 5 – 12 × 1 – 3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate-acuminate and with a ca. 2 cm acumen, with numerous oil glands adaxially; lateral veins many. Inflorescence a thyrse composed of 3-flowered cymes, terminal, 3–6 cm; rachis ridged. Flower-buds obovoid, 3 – 4 mm. Pedicels short. Hypanthium obconic, upper margin incurved. Calyx lobes inconspicuous. Petals white, distinct, ca. 1 mm. Stamens ca. 1 mm. Fruit blackish purple when mature, globose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak. Y. S. Lau 3270.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.– Oct.

Acorus gramineus Soland. ex Aiton 金錢蒲
Hort. Kew. 1: 474. 1789; FKH 289. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 8. 1979; FFJ 6: 411. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 665. 2000; FGD 9: 176. 2009.
Acorus calamus auct. non L: FHK 345. 1861.
Acorus tatarinowii Schott, Oster. Bot. Zeitschr. 9: 101. 1859.

Perennial aromatic herb, 15–55 cm tall, with short, creeping rhizomes and many fleshy roots. Leaves distichous, ensiform, (15–)20–45(–55) × 0.3–1.4 cm, apex acuminate, dark green, venation parallel, midrib lacking. Peduncle 9–25 cm, compressed triangular. Spathe green, leaf-like, ± equaling the peduncle. Spadix narrowly cylindrical to subcylindrical, nearly erect, 3–14 cm, 3–14 cm, densely flowered, yellow; tepals 6, in 2 whorls, ± oblong, 1.5–2 × 0.7–1 mm, membranous, apex rounded or acute; anthers yellow, 0.4–0.5 mm in diam. Infructescence yellowish at maturity. Berry obovoid-globose, several-seeded. Seed ellipsoidal, 2–3 × 0.8–1.2 mm, hairy at base.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ha Hang, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1728; Y. W. Lam 642; HK sheet 35813.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Xinjiang, Qinghai, Ningxia, Gansu, Shanxi, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Philippines, SE Asia.
Ecology: Wet places and rocks near water. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses. Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Acroceras tonkinense (Balansa) C. E. Hubbard ex Bor 山雞穀草
Indian Forest Rec., Bot. 1(3): 78. 1938; FHN 4: 414. 1977; FOC 22: 515. 2006; FGD 9: 412. 2009.
Panicum tonkinense Balansa, J. Bot. (Morot) 4: 140. 1890.
Neohusnotia tonkinensis (Balansa) A. Camus, Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 26(7): 664. 1921; FRPS 10(1): 236. 1990.

Perennial. Culms 65(–100) cm tall, nodes densely pubescent with soft white hairs. Leaf sheaths glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs, one margin tuberculate-ciliate; leaf blades lanceolate, 10–20 × 1–3 cm, glabrous or abaxial surface pilose, margins thickened, pectinate-ciliate at base, scabrous, midvein prominent abaxially, apex narrowly acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, obtuse. Panicle open, 15–25 × 5–10 cm, axis and branches stiff, scabrous; racemes ascending, with secondary branching; spikelets widely spaced, paired or single in upper part. Spikelets 5–5.5 mm; lower glume broadly elliptic, 3/4 spikelet length, 5-veined; upper glume and lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5-veined, apex slightly thickened; lower palea hyaline, narrow; upper lemma smooth, shining, slightly shorter than spikelet, apex thickened and protruding.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 9931.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests under shade. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.
Notes: This species is more robust in habit than Acroceras munroanum (鳳頭黍), with larger leaves and harshly scabrous leaf margins and inflorescence. The species was reported as Acroceras munroanum (Balansa) Henrard previously (Check List HK Plants 321. 2002; 113. 2004).

Acronychia pedunculata (L.) Miq. 山油柑（降真香）
Fl. Ind. Bat. Suppl. 532. 1861; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 553, fig. 2835. 1972; FHN 3: 38. 1974; FTW 3: 508, fig. 705. 1977; FGD 2: 249, fig. 164: 4 –6. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 106, pl. 26: 1 – 6. 1997.
Acronychia laurifolia Blume, Cat. Gew. Buitenz. 27. 63. 1823; FKH 56. 1912.
Cyminosma pedunculata DC., Prodr. 1: 722. 1824; FHK 60. 1861.
Gela lanceolata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 232. 1790.
Jambolifera pedunculata L., Sp. Pl. 349. 1753.

Tree, 5–15 m tall. Bark greyish white to greyish yellow, smooth. Juvenile branches fragrant, often hollow. Leaves unifoliolate; leaflets elliptic to oblong, sometime obovate-elliptic, 7–18 × 3.5–7 cm. Flowers yellowish white, 1.2–1.5 cm in diam. Petals narrowly elliptic, margin and apex slightly incurved at first, apex reflexed and slightly pendulous when full blooming, hairy adaxially. Ovary hairy, rarely glabrous. Infructescence pendulous. Fruit pale yellow, translucent, subglobose and slightly angled, 1–1.5 cm in diam., apex flat, slightly concave and with 4 shallow furrows in middle. Each drupelet 1-seeded. Seed obovoid, 4–5 × 2–3 mm; seed coat brownish black, bony.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 991; L. T. Lo 82; K. L. Yip 4400.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), timber.

Actinidia callosa Lindl. var. discolor C. F. Liang 異色獼猴桃
FRPS 49(2): 315, pl. 64: 6 –7. 1984; FFJ 3: 455, fig. 317. 1988; FGD 4: 144. 2000.
Actinidia fanjingshanensis S. D. Shi & Q. B. Wang, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 16(4): 345. 1994.

Deciduous woody vine. Branches glabrous, greyish yellow when dried. Pith solid, pale brown, lamellate. Petioles reddish, 2–4 cm, glabrous; leaf blade obovate or elliptic, 5 –12 × 3–6 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, slightly oblique, apex acute to acuminate, margin serrate to nearly entire, dark brown adaxially and greyish brown abaxially when dried, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Cymes 1–3-flowered; peduncles 0.5 –1.2 cm; pedicels 0.5 –1.5 cm. Flowers white. Sepals 5, ovate, 4 – 5 mm, glabrous. Petals 5, obovate-oblong, 8 –10 mm. Filaments 3 – 5 mm; anthers yellow, ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm, sagittate at base. Ovary subglobose, densely white-tomentose; styles slightly longer than ovary. Fruit subglobose to ellipsoid, 1.5 –2 cm, glabrous when mature, greenish brown, with conspicuous spots outside and with reflexed persistent sepals at base.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. K. Y. Tam 101; Y. W. Lam 1638.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Anhui, Shanxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Actinidia latifolia (Gardn. & Champ.) Merr. 闊葉獼猴桃
J. Straits Branch Roy. Asiat. Soc. 86: 330. 1922; FRPS 49(2): 255, pl. 72: 1. 1984; FFJ 3: 458. 1988; FGD 4: 148, fig. 95. 2000.
Heptaca latifolia Gardn. & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 243. 1849.
Actinidia championii Benth., FHK 26. 1861; FKH 44. 1912.

Deciduous woody vine. Branchlets subglabrous, whitish lenticellate; pith white, lamellate, solid or hollow. Petioles 3–7 cm, glabrous to puberulous; leaf blade broadly ovate, 8–13 × 5–8.5 cm, base rounded, shallowly cordate or broadly cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin remotely callose-serrulate, glabrous adaxially, densely greyish to yellowish brown-tomentose, with appressed stellate hairs on abaxial surface; lateral veins 6–7 pairs. Cymes 3- or 4-branched, many-flowered; peduncles 2.5– 8.5 cm, densely brownish tomentose; pedicels 0.5 –1.5 cm, densely brownish tomentose; bracts linear, 1–2 mm. Flowers white, fragrant, 1.4 –1.6 cm in diam. Sepals 5, spathulate-ovate, 4–5 mm, reflexed after anthesis, yellowish tomentose on both surfaces. Petals 5–8, oblong to obovate-oblong, 6–8 mm, reflexed after anthesis. Filaments 2– 4 mm, slender; anthers sagittate-ovoid, ca. 1 mm, pubescent. Ovary globose, ca. 2 mm, densely pilose; styles 2–3 mm. Fruit brown, subglobose to ovoid, 3 –3.5 × 2–2.5 cm, spotted, glabrous when mature. Seeds 2–2.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 946; Y. S. Lau 2514, 3019.
Distribtution: SW, S to E China; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Actinoschoenus chinensis (Benth.) Benth. 中華星穗莎
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 14: 33, 1881; Gen. Pl. 3: 1058. 1883.
Arthrostylis chinensis Benth., FHK 397. 1861.
Fimbristylis chinensis (Benth.) Tang & Wang, FRPS 11: 106. 1961; FHN 4: 296. 1977.
Fimbristylis actinoschoenus auct. non C. B. Clarke: FKH 298. 1912.
Fimbristylis thouarsii auct. non (Kunth) Merr.: FGD 8: 309. 2007; FOC 23: 253. 2010; Check List HK Plants 315. 2002; 111. 2004.

Perennial. Culms tufted, 15–40 cm tall, triquetrous, slender, with 2 sheaths at base. Leaves basal, reduced to bladeless sheath. Sheath brown, with prominent ribes, margin membranous and darker. Involucral bracts subulate, shorter than inflorescence, soon reflexed and hidden by inflorescence. Inflorescence capitate. Spikelets 1–2(–6), lanceolate, 6–8 × 0.5–2 mm, few-flowered. Glumes 5–7, lower ones distichous, lowest 3 without flowers, uppermost one with sterile flower, variable in shape and size, smaller upward, semiorbicular, broadly ovate or oblong-ovate, 0.25–2 mm, membranous, brown, glabrous, 3-veined, apex mucronate. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style slender, base enlarged; stigmas 3. Achenes cream-coloured to light brownish, obovoid, 1–1.2 mm, trigonous, smooth to verruculose and indistinctly reticulate.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Deep Water Bay Rd., Lower Shing Mun Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1641; HK sheet 41766, 41767.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Sandy farmlands, forests, rocks.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Wright s.n.) Benth. was collected from Hong Kong in 1850s. The species was considered conspecific with Actinoschoenus thouarsii (Kunth) Benth. (= Fimbristylis thouarsii Kunth) by many authors, but A. chinensis is easily distinguished from the latter by its spikelets being 1–2(–6) and glumes much broader.

Adenanthera microsperma Teijsm. & Binn. 海紅豆

Natuurk. Tijdschr. Nederl. Ind. 27: 58. 1864.

Adenanthera pavonina var. microsperma (Teijsm. & Binn.) I. C. Nielsen, Adansonia n.s. 2, 19(3): 341. 1980; FRPS 39: 5, pl. 1. 1988.

Adenanthera pavonina auct. non L.: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 90. 1912.


Deciduous tree, 5–20 m tall. Branchlets puberulent. Leaves bipinnate. Petioles and leaf-rachis puberulent, eglandular; pinnae 3–5 pairs; leaflets 4 –7 pairs, alternate, oblong or ovate, 2.5–3.5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, broadly obtuse at both ends, puberulent on both surfaces, with short petiolules. Racemes axillary, simple or forming terminal panicle on branchlets, puberulent. Flowers small, white or yellow, fragrant, shortly pedicellate. Calyx less then 1 mm, as well as pedicels golden yellow puberulous. Petals lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, glabrous, slightly connate at base. Stamens 10, as long as corolla or longer. Ovary villose, nearly sessile; style filiform; stigma small. Pods narrowly oblong, 10–20 × 1.2–1.4 cm, valves contorted after dehiscence. Seeds red, bright, subglobose to ellipsoidal, 5–8 × 4.5–7 mm.


Locality: Chai Wan, Happy Valley, Ting Kok, Lam Tsuen, Hang Ha Po, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1323; H. C. Tang 2286; Y. W. Lam 93.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan; Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam.

Ecology: Forests near villages or cultivated in gardens. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul. –Oct.

Uses: Ornamental.

Adenosma glutinosum (L.) Druce 毛麝香
Bot. Exch. Club Soc. Brit. Isles 3: 413. 1914; FHN 3: 500. 1974; FGD 4: 368. 2000; FRPS 18: 25. 1998.
Gerardia glutinosa L., Sp. Pl. 2: 611. 1753.
Digitalis sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 378. 1790.
Pterostigma grandiflorum Benth., Prodr. 10: 380. 1846; FHK 247. 1861.
Adenosma grandiflorum (Benth.) Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 185. 1912.

Herbs, 30–100 cm tall. Stems erect, purplish, terete or upper part slightly 4‑angulate, densely villous with eglandular and glandular hairs. Leaves opposite or upper ones alternate; petioles 3–20 mm; leaf blade lanceolate‑ovate to broadly ovate, 2–10 × 1–5 cm, base cuneate, truncate or subcordate, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate and sometimes double serrate. Flowers axillary and solitary or in leafy racemes apically on stems and branches. Bracts small. Pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm, elongating to 2 cm in fruit. Calyx 0.7–1.3 cm; lobes narrowly lanceolate. Corolla purple‑red to violet, 0.9–2.8 cm; lower lip 3(–4)‑lobed; upper lip ovate‑orbicular, apex truncate to emarginate. Anterior anthers with 1 fertile cell; posterior anthers with 2 fertile cells; styles gradually widened and narrowly winged. Capsules ovoid, 5–9 × 3–6 mm, 2‑grooved, apex beaked. Seeds brown to dark brown.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 561, 2026; Y. S. Lau 32.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Oceania.
Ecology: Thickets, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Adenosma indianum (Lour.) Merr. 球花毛麝香
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. n.s. 24(2): 351. 1935; FHN 3: 501. 1974; FGD 4: 369. 2000; FOC 18: 25. 1998.
Manulea indiana Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 386. 1790.
Pterostigma capitatum Benth., Scroph. Ind. 21. 1835; FHK 248. 1861.
Adenosma capicatum Benth. ex Hance, J. Bot. Linn. Soc. Bot. 13: 114. 1872; FKH 186. 1912.

Annual herbs, 20–60(–100) cm tall, wholly glandular hairy. Stems erect, branched. Petiole 2–6 mm; leaf blade ovate to narrowly elliptic, 1.5–4.5 × 0.5–1.2 cm, base broad‑cuneate or acute, apex obtuse, margin serrate. Inflorescences globose to cylindric spicate, 0.7–2 cm. Bracts narrowly ovate, forming an involucre at the base of spikes. Flowers sessile. Calyx 4–5 mm; lobes narrowly ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 2–3 mm. Corolla pale purple to dark blue, ca. 6 mm, throat hairy; lower lip lobes equal, suborbicular, ca. 1 mm. Anterior anthers with 1 fertile cell; posterior anthers with 2 fertile cells. Ovary narrowly ovoid. Capsules ovoid, ca. 3 mm, 2‑grooved. Seeds yellow.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8396, 11236; HK sheet 20396.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Yunnan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Adenostemma lavenia (L.) Kuntze 下田菊
Rev. Gen. Pl. 304. 1891; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 92. 1965; FRPS 74: 50. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 816. 1998; FGD 8: 217, fig. 129. 2007.
Adenostemma viscosum Forst., Char. Gen. Pl. 45, t. 45. 1775; FHK 171. 1861; FKH 139. 1912.
Verbesina lavenia L., Sp. Pl. 902. 1753.

Annual herbs, 40–100 cm tall. Stems erect, branched on upper portion, lower part nearly glabrous, puberulent upward. Basal leaves withered or remained at anthesis, smaller in size; middle leaves ovate, 4–9 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, forming petiole 0.5–4 cm long with narrow wing, apex obtuse or acute, leaf margin crenate‑serrate, subglabrous on both surfaces, sparsely puberulent along the midvein; upper leaves smaller in size, 0.5–2 cm. Capitula in loose terminal corymbs; peduncles 1–4 cm, densely pubescent, hair multicellular. Involucres hemispherical, 5–8 mm across, or up to 10 mm at fruiting stage; phyllaries 2‑seriate, 4–5 × 1 mm, oblong, apex rounded, greenish, outer series connate at base. Florets all tubular, pinkish to maroon, 2–2.5 mm, broader at upper region, with 5 deltoid lobes at apex, glandular pilose especially at lower region; style white, branches clavate, prominently exserted; anther included, base obtuse, without apical appendages. Cypselae chestnut brown, 3–4 × 1 mm, oblanceolate, truncate distal end, glandular. Pappus 3–4 clavate projections, end up with sticky glands, base connate into a ring.

Locality: Aberdeen, Clear Water Bay, Nam Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun Reservoir, Ta Tit Yan. C. P. Lau 032 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 21201A (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 781.
Distribution: S to C China; SE Asia, Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Australia.
Ecology: Banks of paddy fields and wastelands. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Adina pilulifera (Lam.) Franch. ex Drake 水團花
J. Bot. (Morot) 9: 207. 1895; Hand.‑Mazz., Symb. Sin. 8: 1018. 1936; FHN 3: 288, fig. 727. 1974; Ridsdale, Blumea 24(2): 357, fig. 1(d), 3(h). 1978; FRPS 71(1): 274, pl. 73: 1 – 2. 1999; FYN 15: 132, pl. 25: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 6: 162. 2005.
Adina globiflora Salisb., Parad. Lond. pl. 115. 1807; FHK 146. 1861; FKH 124. 1912.
Cephalanthus pilulifera Lam., Encycl. 1: 678. 1785.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, to 5 m tall, many‑branched. Stipules bifid, caducous. Leaves opposite, thickly papery; petioles 2–6 mm; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic‑lanceolate, or sometimes obovate‑oblong or obovate‑oblanceolate, 4–12 × 1.5–3 cm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, tip blunt, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glabrous or puberulent, with hairy domatia in axils of lateral veins; lateral veins 6–12 on each side of midvein. Flowering head globular, 8–12 mm in diam. across corollas. Peduncles axillary, 2–5 cm, unbranched, rarely 3 together at the ends of the branches, each bearing a flowering head. Calyx‑tube 1.2–2 mm, pubescent at the base; lobes clavate to spathulate, 1–1.8 mm, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs. Corolla white, 3–5 mm, tube 2–3 mm, glabrous; lobes deltoid, ca. 0.5 mm. Stamens 5, inserted in the throat of corolla; filaments short; anthers 0.5–1 mm. Ovary 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style exserted, with small, globose or obovoid stigma. Fruiting head globose, 8–10 mm in diam.; fruitlets 2–4 mm, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24058, 24084; HK Sheet 39081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets by streams and in ravines. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
