Adinandra glischroloma Hand.-Mazz. var. jubata (H. L. Li) Kobuski 長毛楊桐
J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 21. 1947.
Adinandra jubata Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25: 422. 1944; FGD 2: 158. 1991.

Shrub or small tree, branchlets and terminal buds densely villose, with spreading tawny or rusty hairs. Leaves leathery; petioles 8–10 mm, densely hirsute; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 8–13 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, dark green and glabrous adaxially, yellowish green and rusty-hirsute abaxially. Flowers white, axillary, 2–3 clustered, rarely solitary. Pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm, often recurved, densely hirsute; bracteoles 2, caducous. Sepals broadly ovate, 5–14 mm, apex acute, densely rusty hirtellous abaxially. Petals oblong or ovate-oblong, 8–15 × 4–6 mm, apex rounded, hirtellous abaxially. Stamens ca. 25, 5–9 mm; filaments glabrous; anthers linear, 2–4.5 mm, hispid, connective prolonged. Ovary ovoid, densely hirsute, 3-locular, many ovules per locule; style l, ca. 8 mm, densely hirsute. Fruit globose, black when mature, 0.8–1.3 cm in diam., densely hirsute.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Sze Tau Leng. Y. W. Lam 243; F. W. Xing 8009; S. C. Ng 4486; K. L. Yip 4083.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Guangxi, S Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

Adinandra millettii (Hook. & Arn.) Benth. & Hook. f. ex Hance 黃瑞木
J. Bot. 16: 9. 1878; FKH 43. 1912; FGD 2: 158. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 48. 1998.
Cleyera millettii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 171, t. 33. 1841.

Shrub or small tree, 2–10 m tall; branchlets greyish brown, pubescent when young; terminal buds appressed pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 3 – 5 mm, sparsely pubescent, glabrescent ; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 4 –9 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or sparsely serrate towards apex, glabrous and shining adaxially, paler, appressed pubescent or glabrescent abaxially. Flowers white, solitary, axillary. Pedicels slender, ca. 2 cm, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent; bracteoles linear-lanceolate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, caducous. Sepals ovate-lanceolate or ovate-triangular, 7– 8 × 4 – 5 mm, apex acute, margin ciliolate and glandular, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent abaxially. Petals ovate-oblong to oblong, ca. 9 × 4–5 mm, apex acute, glabrous. Stamens ca. 25, 6–7 mm; filaments ca. 3 mm, glabrous or white pubescent proximally; anthers linear-oblong, ca. 2 mm, hispid, connective prolonged. Ovary globose, pubescent, 3-locular, many ovules per locule. Style simple, 7–8 mm, glabrous. Fruit globose, pubescent, ca. 1 cm in diam., black when mature, many seeded.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Mong Tsai, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 109; Y. S. Lau 1409; K. L. Yip 4076.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.

Aechmea fasciata (Lindl.) Baker 蜻蜓鳳梨
J. Bot. 17: 231. 1879.
Billbergia fasciata Lindl., Bot. Reg. 13: t. 1130. 1828.

Perennial herb. Leaves rosulate; leaf sheath broad, usually brownish-red, leaf blade ligulate, outer ones apex acute, inner ones apex rounded, with a minutely cuspidate tip, green, glaucous, with very manifest transverse, white bars (consisting of white scales), margin with robust, brownish black spines. Inflorescence a panicle, terminal on a robust, white-woolly peduncle; flowers of a same branch arranged to 3 or more directions; floral bracts well-developed, lanceolate, outer ones to 10 cm, narrower and shorter inwards, margin serrulate, pink to crimson. Sepals keeled, basally connate, with a rounded, minutely apiculate tip, white hairy. Petals violet or red, rounded, 2–3 cm.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to Brazil.
Uses: Ornamental.

Aegiceras corniculatum (L.) Blanco 蠟燭果
Fl. Filip. 79. 1837; Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 55, fig. 8. 1902; B. C. Stone, Tree Fl. Malaya 4: 266. 1989; K. Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand, 6(2): 176. 1996; FOC 15: 9. 1996.
Rhizophora corniculata L., Amoen. Acad. 4: 123. 1759.
Aegiceras majus J. Gaertner, Deucr. & Sem. 1: 216, pl. 46, fig. 1. 1788; FHK 208. 1861; FKH 160. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, 1.5– 4 m tall, much branched; branchlets terete, glabrous, brownish black when dry. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade obovate or elliptic, 3–10 x 2–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex rounded or emarginate, margin entire and slightly recurved, leathery, glabrous, with many minute pores on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–11 pairs, slender and slightly raised on both surfaces, ascending and anastomosing near the edge; veinlets obscure. Umbels terminal, axillary or leaf-opposed, sessile or very shortly peduncled, usually many flowered. Pedicels ca. 1 cm. Flowers white, without bracteole. Calyx split to base; lobes leathery, oblique-oblong, ca. 6 × 3 mm, gibbous and thickened at base. Corolla-tube ca. 3.5 mm, villous adaxially; lobes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, ca. 6.5 × 3 mm, apex acute, reflexed. Stamens shorter than corolla; filaments 6 –7 mm, base fused into a tube, densely villous, free part slightly longer than the tube, glabrous; anthers 2.5 –3 mm, dorsifixed. Ovary ovoid; style 6 –8 mm, subulate, with black glandular dots. Fruit cylindric, curved, falcate or crescent-shaped, 5 – 8 cm, acuminate at apex.

Locality: Tytam Took (Tai Tam Tuk), Sai Wan, Shek O, Shatin, Ma Wan Island, Mai Po, Sai Kung, Yung Shue Au, Ho Chung. Y. S. Lau 1377, 2707; P. S. Choi 131, 207, 208; H. C. Tang 1291, 1902.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Guangxi; India, Malaysia, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Sea coasts, mangroves, muddy flats. Flowering: Dec.–Feb; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Aeginetia indica L. 野菰
Sp. Pl. 2: 632. 1753; FHK 257. 1861; FKH 191. 1912; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 4: 320. 1884; FRPS 69: 77, pl. 21: 1 – 8. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 713, pl. 327. 1998; FOC 18: 240. 1998; FGD 4: 399, fig. 242. 2000.

Plant 20–35 cm tall. Root slightly fleshy. Stems very short, unbranched or branched from near base. Scales deltoid, 5–10 mm, apex acuminate, glabrous. Flowers usually solitary, 3–5 cm. Pedicels usually erect, 15–24 cm, glabrous. Calyx 2–3.5 cm, apex acute or acuminate. Corolla pinkish purple, indistinctly bilabiate, tubular‑campanulate, 2–4.5 cm; tube slightly curved; lobes subentire. Filaments purple, 7–9 mm, glabrous; anthers yellow. Ovary 1‑locular; parietal placentas 4; style 1–1.5 cm; stigma pale yellow. Capsule conical, or long ovoid‑globose, 2–3 cm; seeds yellow, ellipsoidal.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1004, 1270; HK sheet 41662.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Aegle marmelos (L.) Corrêa 木橘（肖木蘋果）
Trans. Linn. Soc. 5: 223. 1800; FRPS 43(2): 210, pl. 51. 1997.
Crataeva marmelos L., Sp. Pl. 1: 444. 1753.

Tree to 10 m tall. Bark grey. Spines many, thick and hard, straight, to 3 cm. Long branches with 1 normal leaf and 1 or 2 spines on each node. Short branches with 1 leaf and no spines on each node. Leaves various in size. Leaves of seedling simple, opposite or subopposite. Leaves on lower part of stems unifoliolate, on upper part of stems digitately 3-foliolate, sometimes 2-foliolate. Leaflets broadly ovate or long elliptic, 4–12 × 2–5 cm, central one larger and with 2 cm petiolule, lateral ones sessile, margin shallowly obtuse-dentate. Flowers solitary or few in axils, pedicellate. Sepals 4–5, finely hairy. Petals 4–5, white, slightly fleshy, with pellucid glandular dots, ca. 1 cm. Stamens up to 50, ± connate into many bundles, filaments very short, anthers linear and long. Fruiting pedicels 4–6 cm, as thick as the branches bearing fruit. Fruit 10–12 × 6–8 cm; pericarp pale greenish yellow, smooth, woody when dry, 3–4 mm thick, 10–15-locular. Seeds many, compressed ovoid, apex sharp.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1597; L. T. Lo 257.
Distribution: Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Aeschynanthus acuminatus Wall. ex A. DC. 芒毛苣苔
Prodr. 9: 263. 1845; FKH 193. 1912; FRPS 69: 502. 1990; FOC 18: 377. 1998; FGD 6: 284, pl. 156. 2005.
Aeschynanthus chinensis Gardner & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 328. 1849.
Aeschynanthus acuminatus var. chinensis (Gardner & Champ.) C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 5: 31. 1883.

Climber, stems 25–100 cm, branched, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 2–5 mm; leaf blade thin leathery, oblanceolate to oblong, 4.5–9 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or mucronate, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins indistinct. Cymes axillary or pseudoterminal, 2–5‑flowered; peduncle 1–3 cm, glabrous; bracts 2, opposite, suborbicular, 3–9 × 5–10 mm, apex obtuse or rotund, glabrous; pedicel ca. 1 cm, glabrous. Calyx 5‑sect from base; lobes narrowly ovate to ovate‑oblong, 3–7 × 2–3 mm, apex obtuse, outside glabrous. Corolla red or greenish, 1.5–2.5 cm, outside glabrous, inside puberulent or purple spot at base of abaxial lip, without tufts of hairs, mouth strongly oblique; tube 0.8–1.6 cm long, ca. 5 mm in diam.; limb distinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, lobes erect, 4–6 mm long; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes reflexed, 5–7 mm long, lobes narrowly ovate. Stamens 4, didynamous, exserted, adnate to corolla tube near middle; filaments purple, 1–2 cm; anthers coherent in pairs at apex, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; staminode 1, ca. 2 mm. Disk ring‑like. Pistil glabrous; ovary 1–1.5 cm; style ca. 5 mm; stigma 1, disk‑shaped. Capsule 6.5–10 cm, glabrous. Seeds narrowly oblong, with 1 hair‑like appendage at each end.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1726; Y. S. Lau 917, 2447.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Taiwan; Bhutan, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Trailing on trees and rocks by streams or in forests. Flowering: Dec.–Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Feb.–May.
Notes: The type specimen of Aeschynanthus chinensis was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong between 1847 and 1850.

Aeschynomene indica L. 合萌（田皂角）
Sp. Pl. 2: 713. 1753; FHK 79. 1861; FKH 77. 1912; FRPS 41: 351. 1995; FGD 5: 347, fig. 192. 2003.

Annual herb or subshrub. Stems erect, 0.3 – 1 m tall, multibranched, glabrous. Leaves even-pinnate, rhachis slender near base; leaflets 20–30 pairs, linear or oblong, 5–10 × 2–2.5 mm, base oblique, entire, apex obtuse or emarginate, mucronate, densely glandular adaxially, ± glaucous abaxially. Recemes axillary, 1.5 – 2 cm, 1 – 4-flowered. Calyx 4 – 6 mm, 2-lipped, glabrous. Corolla yellowish, lined with purple, 8 – 9 mm; vexillum suborbicular, 7 – 8 mm broad, shortly clawed; wings oblong, long-clawed; keel shorter than wings. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary linear. Pods linear, 3–4 × 0.3 cm, ventral suture straight, dorsal suture sinuate; segments 4–8(–10), smooth or finally papillose on face, indehiscent. Seeds black brown, reniform, 3 – 3.5 × 2.5 –3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1989; Y. S. Lau 911, 1996.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; pantropics.
Ecology: Wet and open places. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Uses: Green manure, medicinal (folklore), seeds poisonous.

Agave americana L. 龍舌蘭
Sp. Pl. 1: 323. 1753; FHN 4: 157. 1977; FTW 5: 87. 1978; FRPS 16(1): 31. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 5: 75. 2000; FOC 24: 271. 2000; FGD 9: 219. 2009.

Stems indistinct. Leaves usually 30–40 or more, in a basal rosette, oblanceolate, 1–2 m × 15–20 cm, fleshy, apex recurved and tipped with a dark brown spine 1.5–2.5 cm, margin sparsely spiny, glaucous adaxially. Panicle large, many-branched, 6–12 m. Perianth greenish yellow, segments sometimes with 1 green stripe; tube ca. 1.2 cm; lobes 2.5–3 cm. Stamens ca. twice as long as perianth. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28381.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S and SW China, naturalized in some regions of S China; native to tropical America.
Uses: Material (fibre), ornamental.

Ageratum conyzoides L. 藿香薊
Sp. Pl. 839. 1753; FHK 171. 1861; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1–2): 93. 1965; FRPS 74: 53. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 820. 1998; FGD 8: 217, fig. 128. 2007.

Erect aromatic herbs 8–80 cm tall, with or without branches, pubescent throughout the vegetative organs, with multicellular straight trichomes. Leaves opposite, ovate or elliptic, base usually cuneate or sometimes rounded, apex acute, margin crenulate‑dentate, trinerved or some inconspicuously 5‑veined, usually with yellow glands on abaxial surface; middle leaves 2–8 cm × 1–6 cm, with petiole 0.5–4 cm; upper and lower leaves smaller in size. Capitula in dense terminal corymbs. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 2‑seriate, subequal, 3–4 mm, broad, oblong or lanceolate‑oblong, glabrous or occasionally with few hair, apex acute or acuminate, shallowly serrulate, not entire. Receptacle dome‑shaped, smoothed and pitted, with persistent phyllaries after fruit dispersal. Florets tubular, white, blue or violet, corolla 1.5–2.5 mm, 5‑lobed, slightly pilose on upper portion; stylar branches 1.5–2 mm, apical part glistering densely papillose. Cypselae brownish black, linear‑oblong, 1.5–1.8 mm, 5‑angulate, pilose. Pappus 5, scarious and awned, 2–2.5 mm, equal or longer than the corolla.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1935, 2196; S. Y. Hu 5296 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to C & S America, widely cultivated and naturalized.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ageratum houstonianum Mill. 熊耳草
Gard. Dict. ed. 8. 1768; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 94. 1965; FRPS 74: 51. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 820. 1998; FGD 8: 216. 2007.

Erect annual herbs 30–100 cm tall, with or without branches, pubescent throughout the vegetative organ. Leaves opposite, deltoid‑cordate, base cordate or sometimes truncate, apex acute or rounded, margin crenate‑dentate, pilose on both sides, trinervous or inconspicuously 5‑veined; mid‑cauline ones 2–6 × 1.5–3 cm, with petiole 0.7– 3 cm; upper and lower ones smaller. Capitula in corymbose form; peduncles densely villose. Involucres campanulate to hemispherical, 5–6 mm across; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, narrowly lanceolate, 4–5 mm, densely hairy and glandular, apex long‑acuminate, entire. Receptacle dome‑shaped, with persistent phyllaries after fruit dispersal. Florets tubular, corolla 2–3.2 mm, shortly 5‑lobed, white to light‑violet, apex hairy; stylar branches violet, 1.5–2 mm. Cypselae black, 1.5–2 mm, 5‑angulate. Pappus 5, scarious and awned, 1.2–1.5 mm, shorter than corolla.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1937; H. C. Tang 1233; L. T. Lo 89.
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Nature trail, farmlands and wastelands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.

Aglaia odorata Lour. 米仔蘭
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 173. 1790; FKH 58. 1912; FGZ 440. 1956; FHN 3: 65. 1974; FYN 1: 239, pl. 57: 9. 1977; FFJ 2: 386, fig. 285. 1985; FGD 2: 289, fig. 184. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 70, pl. 17: 1 – 5. 1997.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, to 8 m. Young branches stellately lepidote at apex. Leaves alternate; petioles and leaf-rachis narrowly winged; leaflets 3–5, opposite; blades thickly papery, obovate to oblong, 2–7(–11) × 0.8–3.5(–5) cm, apical one largest, base cuneate, apex obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 8 on each side, very slender, prominent on both surfaces. Panicles 5–10 cm, glabrous. Flowers fragrant, ca. 2 mm in diam. Pedicels 1–3 mm, slender. Calyx 5-lobed, lobes orbicular. Petals 5, yellow, oblong to suborbicular, 1.5–2 mm, apex rounded to truncate. Staminal tube slightly shorter than petals, obovoid to nearly campanulate, glabrous abaxially, apex entire or crenate. Anthers 5, ovoid, inclusive. Ovary ovoid, densely yellow hirsute. Berry ovoid to subglobose, 1–1.2 cm, stellately lepidote at first. Seeds with a fleshy aril.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1619, 3187; HK sheet 36074.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, flower used for fumigating tea.
records.uses: Ornamental, flower used for fumigating tea.

records.text:
Aglaia odorata var. microphyllina C. DC. 小葉米仔蘭
Monogr. Phan. 1: 602. 1878; FGD 2: 290. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 70. 1997.

It differs from var. odorata by leaflets 5–7(–9), narrowly elliptic or narrowly oblanceolate-elliptic, shorter than 4 cm, 0.8–1.5 cm wide.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 276.
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Aglaonema modestum Schott ex Engl. 廣東萬年青
Monogr. Phan. 2: 442. 1897; FHN 4: 134, fig. 1039. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 43. 1979; FYN 2: 760. 1979; FFJ 6: 418, fig. 378. 1995; FGD 9: 187, fig. 103. 2009; FOC 23: 23. 2010.

Perennial evergreen herb. Stems erect, green and smooth, 40–70 cm tall; internodes 1–2 cm. Leaves mostly crowded towards stemapex; petiole 5–20 cm, green, the lower half sheathed and clasping stem at base; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 15–25 × 6–13 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate-acuminate, margin entire, dark green above, paler beneath; lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Peduncle slender, 5–10 cm. Spathe yellow-green, oblong-lanceolate, 5.5–7 × 1.5 cm, apex long-acuminate. Spadix cylindrical, about 2/3 the length of spathe; female portion 5–7.5 mm; male portion elongate, 2–3 cm. Flowers unisexual, without scales or perianth. Berries oblong-ovoid, ca. 2 cm, orange-red when mature, oblong.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. HK sheet 28245, 29749.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Agrimonia pilosa Ledeb. 龍牙草
Ind. Sem. Hort. Dorpat. Suppl. 1. 1823; FFJ 2: 282. 1985; FRPS 37: 457. 1985; FGD 4: 227. 2000; FOC 9: 382. 2003.
Agrimonia eupatoria auct. non L.: FKH 95. 1912.

Perennial herb, 30 – 120 cm tall, with short rhizomes; stems erect, sparsely pilose, rarely rigid hirsute in lower part. Leaves imparipinnate; petioles pilose; stipules large, leaf-like, obovate-oblong, entire or dentate; leaflets sessile or subsessile, usually (2–)3–4 pairs, reduced to 3 leaflets on upper ones, obovate, obovate-elliptic or obovate-lanceolate, 1.5–5 × 1 – 2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, rarely acuminate, margin coarsely serrate, pilose on both surfaces, abaxially glandular-punctate. Raceme slender, terminal, branched or unbranched, 10 – 15 cm or longer; peduncles pilose; bracts usually deeply 3-lobed, segments linear; bracteoles opposite, ovate, entire or lobed; pedicels 1 – 5 mm, pilose. Flowers 6 – 9 mm in diam.; hypanthium obconic, sparsely pilose abaxially; sepals 5, triangular-ovate, apex acuminate; petals 5, yellow, oblong; stamens 5 –15; styles 2, filiform, stigmas capitate. Achenes conical, 10-ribbed, sparsely pilose, with a multiseriate crown of prickles, 7–8 × 3–4 mm including prickles, prickles erect when young, connivent at maturity.

Locality: Tai Wai. Y. S. Lau 3303.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; C Europe, Russia, Mongolia, Korea, Japan, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Grassy lands, thickets and streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Agrimonia pilosa Ledeb. var. nepalensis (D. Don) Nakai 黃龍尾
FFJ 2: 283. 1985; FRPS 37: 458. 1985; FGD 4: 227. 2000; FOC 9: 383. 2003.
Agrimonia nepalensis D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 229. 1825.

It differs from var. pilosa in stems being densely and rigidly hirsute in lower part; leaflets abaxially densely pubescent or tomentose-pubescent between veins, and sparsely glandular punctate, adaxially hirsute or hirtellous on veins.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 1638.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Henan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hebei, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Gansu; Japan, Nepal, Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grassy lands, thickets and streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: May– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Agrimonia eupatoria L. previously (Check List HK Plants 29. 1993).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Agrimonia eupatoria L. previously (Check List HK Plants 29. 1993).

records.text:
Aidia canthioides (Champ. ex Benth.) Masam. 香楠（山黃皮）
Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 28: 118 1938; FRPS 71(1): 351, pl. 92: 1 – 7. 1999; FYN 15: 177. 2003; FGD 6: 181. 2005.
Randia canthioides Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 194. 1852; FHK 155. 1861; FKH 131. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 318. 1998.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed, 1–12 m tall. Branches glabrous. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 5–18 mm; stipules broadly triangular, 3–8 mm, apex acute or acuminate, deciduous, leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, oblong‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 4–18 × 2–8 cm, base broadly cuneate or sometimes subrounded, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, sometimes acute, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 3–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes umbel‑like, axillary, 3–5 cm in diam. Peduncle very short or none. Pedicels slender, 5–16 mm, glabrous. Calyx covered with appressed rusty hairs abaxially; tube turbinate, 4–6 mm; lobes 5, triangular, 1–2 mm, apex acute. Corolla salverform, white or yellow; tube 8–10 mm, glabrous abaxially, villose on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, 4–7 mm, apex acute, recurved. Anthers linear‑oblong, ca. 3.5 mm, exserted. Style ca. 10 mm; stigma fusiform, 2‑lobes. Berry globose, 5–8 mm in diam., rusty pubescent or glabrescent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Ma On Shan, Fa Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 421; Y. W. Lam 480; K. L. Yip 4536.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan;  Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Aidia cochinchinensis Lour. 茜樹（越南香楠）
Fl. Cochinch. 143. 1790; Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 28: 118. 1938; FRPS 71(1): 354, pl. 93: 1 – 6. 1999; FYN 15: 178. 2003; FGD 6: 181, fig. 94. 2005.
Randia cochinchinensis (Lour.) Merr., Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. n.s., 24(2): 365. 1935; FTW ed. 2, 4: 319, pl. 144, photo 193. 1998.
Randia densiflora (Wall.) Benth., FHK 155. 1861; FKH 131. 1912, p.p.
Webera densiflora Wall., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 2: 536. 1824.
Randia henryi E. Pritz., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29(5): 581. 1901.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed, 2–15 m tall. Branchlets petioles and stipules glabrous. Leaves leathery or papery; petioles 4–10(–18) mm; stipules lanceolate, 4–8(–10) mm, glabrous, deciduous; leaf blade elliptic‑oblong, oblong‑lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 6 – 21 × 1.5 – 8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, glabrous, but often with tufts of short hairs in axils of veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins slender, 5–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes leaf‑opposed, or lateral on aphyllous nodes. Peduncles 5 – 10 mm. Pedicels 1 – 2 mm, together with peduncles pubescent. Calyx glabrous; tube cup‑shaped, 3.5 – 4 mm; lobes 4( – 5), triangular, 1 – 1.5 mm. Corolla yellow or white; tube 3 – 4 mm, glabrous abaxially, densely yellowish villose on the throat; lobes 4( – 5), oblong, 6 – 10 mm, apex acute, spreading or reflexed, pubescent with minute appressed hairs on abaxial surface. Anthers linear‑lanceolate, 4 – 8 mm, exserted. Style ca. 7 mm; stigma fusiform, 2‑lobes. Berry globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 648; HK sheet 39493, 40772.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; spreading over tropical Asia & Australia.
Ecology: Ravines under forests or in thickets. Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: May–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: This species was recorded previously as Randia acutidens Hemsl. & Wils. var. laxiflora Dunn. (FKH 131. 1912).

Aidia pycnantha (Drake) Tirveng. 多毛茜草樹
Nord. Journ. Bot. 3(4): 455. 1983; FRPS 71(1): 349. 1999; FYN 15: 177. 2003; FGD 6. 182. 2005.
Randia pycnantha Drake in Morot, Journ. de Bot. 9: 218. 1895.
Randia acuminatissima Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 15(3): 259 – 260. 1919[1920].
Aidia acuminatissima (Merr.) Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 29: 238. 1939.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed, 2–10 m tall. Young branches ferruginous soft hairy. Petioles 5–15 mm long, softy hairy; leaf blade oblong, oblong‑lanceolate or oblong‑oblanceolate, 10–20 × 3–8 cm, leathery or papery, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, acuminate portion to 2.5 cm long, straight or curved, base cuneate, sometimes unaequilateral, when dry reddish brown, adaxially glabrous, slightly shiny, abaxially ferruginous soft hairy; lateral veins 10–14 pairs, together with reticulate veins prominent abaxially; stipules lanceolate, to 1 cm long, apex long pointed, pubescent. Inflorescence a cyme, leaf opposed, many‑flowered, 4–6, × 5–12 cm, ferruginous soft hairy; bracts and bractlets linear‑lanceolate, 2–4 mm long. Pedicels 1.5 – 4 mm long. Calyx and hypanthium 4 – 5 mm long, ferruginous soft hairy; tube cupulate, 3 mm long, limb slightly expanded, apically 5‑lobed; lobes triangular, apex pointed, 1–2 mm long. Corolla white or pale yellow, salverform, glabrous abaxially; tube ca. 4 mm long, densely villose in throat; lobes 5, oblong‑oblanceolate, 7–9 mm, reflexed at anthesis. Anthers linear‑lanceolate, exserted, ca. 7 mm long; filaments ca. 2.5 mm long. Ovary 2‑celled; style and stigma 7–8 mm long, glabrous; stigma fusiform, with shallow sulcate striate. Fruit a berry, globose, 6 – 8 mm in diam., sparsely ferruginous hairy or subglabrous, black when dry, apex with annular remnants of calyx limb.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2966; P. S. Choi 293; Y. W. Lam 1702.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thicket or lowland forest. Flowering: Feb.–Nov.; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Notes: This species was recorded previously as Randia densiflora (Wall.) Benth. (FKH 131. 1912, p.p.).

Ailanthus fordii Noot. 常綠臭椿（福氏臭椿）

Fl. Malesiana, Ser. 1, Spermatoph. 6: 220. 1962; FYN 1: 181, pl. 43: 1– 2. 1977; FFJ 2: 378, fig. 280. 1985; FGD 1: 230. 1987; FRPS 43(3): 3. 1997.

Ailanthus malabarica auct. non DC.: FKH 57. 1912.


Evergreen small tree, 3–5 m tall; branchlets greyish brown, densely puberulous. Leaves crowded at apex of branches, 40–60 cm; rachis puberulous; petioles 7–13 cm; leaflets 6–13 pairs, opposite or nearly so, blade papery to leathery, oblong-ovate, 7–13 × 4–6 cm, base obtuse, oblique, apex short acuminate or obtuse, margin entire, with scattered small and flat glands abaxially. Thyrses terminal, 20–40 × 20 cm, branch base articulate. Flowers unisexual or polygamous, 1–3-clustered; pedicels 1–2 mm; bracts small, triangular. Calyx cupular, puberulous, ca. 0.5 mm, 5-lobed. Petals 5, glabrous, 2–3 × 1 mm. Stamens curved and folded, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.8 mm. Carpels 5, densely puberulous; styles connate, 0.5–1 mm, ± puberulous, stigma 5, distinct or base slightly connate. Samara 3–5 × 1–1.8 cm.


Locality: Cape D' Aguilar, Mount Gough, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Lamma Island. Also cultivated at gardens and roadsides. Y. S. Lau 1438, 1472; K. L. Yip 4538.

Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Yunnan.

Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.

Uses: Roadside tree.

Note: The type specimen was collected by C. Ford from Hong Kong Island between 1884 and 1886. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Roadside tree.

Note: The type specimen was collected by C. Ford from Hong Kong Island between 1884 and 1886. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Ainsliaea fragrans Champ. 杏葉兔兒風
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 236. 1852; FHK 192. 1861; FKH 149. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 95. 1965; FRPS 79: 31. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 822. 1998; FGD 8: 241. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, scapose and simple, 15–40 cm tall, brownish pubescent to pilose. Leaves 4–6 crowded at base or in the lower part of stem in subverticillate form, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 2–11 × 1.5–6 cm, base conspicuously cordate, apex obtuse to rounded and usually mucronulate, margin curved‑mucronulate, upper surfaces green, glabrous or loosely hairy, lower surfaces pale green or somewhat purple‑red, pilose, hair denser along veins and margins; petiole 2–7 cm, not winged, densely pilose. Capitula with 3 florets each, sessile or with short peduncle 1–2(–9) mm, arranged as spike or raceme; inflorescence axis brownish pubescent to pilose, bearing few subulate bracteoles 1–2 mm. Involucres narrow cylindric‑tubular, 8–10 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries about 5–7‑seriate, glabrous, sometimes tinged purplish red, apex acute; outer layers ovate, 1.2–2.2 × 0.5–1.3 mm; median layers ovate‑elliptic, 3–5 × 1.5–2 mm; inner ones linear‑oblong, 5.5–9 × 2–2.5 mm, margin scarious. Receptacle small, naked. All florets bisexual and fertile, colour white, aromatic, corolla tubular, 7 – 9 mm, upper limb deeply and obliquely cleft into 5 linear segments of 3–5 mm; anther bases sagittate and caudate, apical appendages oblong‑truncate; stylar branches short, 0.5 mm, obtuse apically. Cypselae brown, oblanceolate‑oblong, slightly compressed, 4–5 × 0.8–1 mm, ribbed, villous especially on the apical portion. Pappus pale brown, equal, plumose, 8–10 mm, base connate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1573; C. P. Lau 083 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 9118 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: Thickets, grasslands. Flowering: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ainsliaea macroclinidioides Hayata 燈臺兔兒風
J. Coll. Sci. Tokyo 25(19): 141, pl. 22. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 97. 1965; FRPS 79: 59. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 824. 1998; FGD 8: 244. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect or sometimes decumbent, simple, 25–40 cm tall, densely pilose or glabrescent later. Leaves crowded at the stem middle part or above, in rosette or verticillate form, sometimes with few leaves scattered below, ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2–6 × 1.5–4 cm, base truncate or faintly cordate, apex obtuse or acute, and usually mucronulate, margin entire and curved‑mucronulate, adaxial surface green, glabrous or villous, abaxial surface pale green, loosely or densely villous, much hair growing along veins and margins; petioles 1–6.5 cm, pilose. Capitula with 3 florets each, sessile or shortly pedunculate, arranged as spike or raceme, sometimes with few clustered at apical portion; inflorescence axis glabrous or loosely hairy, bearing few bracteoles. Involucres narrow cylindric‑tubular, 3–4 mm across; phyllaries 6–7‑seriate, purplish green, longitudinally veined abaxially, glabrous or slightly hairy near apices of those in the inner series; outer phyllaries ovate, 1.2–3 × 0.8–2 mm, obtuse; middle ones ovate‑oblong, 4–6 × 2–2.2 mm, obtuse; inner ones lanceolate‑oblong, 8 – 10 × 1.5 mm, acute. Receptacle plain, naked. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla white, tubular, 10 – 13 mm, upper limb deeply and obliquely 5‑cleft, lobes linear, 4–6 mm; anther bases sagittate and caudate, apical appendages oblong‑truncate; stylar branches divergent, less than 1 mm, rather flat, obtuse at apices. Cypselae brown, subcylindric, base narrowed, about 2–3 mm, ribbed, hairy. Pappus in 1 row, 6–7 mm, pale brown, plumose, base connate.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 11275 (CUHK); C. P. Lau 060 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 327.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.

Ainsliaea walkeri Hook. f. 華南兔兒風
Bot. Mag. 102: t. 6225. 1876; FKH 149. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1–2): 102. 1965; FRPS 79: 66. 1996; FGD 8: 245. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, simple, 15–40 cm high, loosely pubescent on apical part. Leaves crowded on middle portion of stem, sometimes with few scattered below, leaf blade oblong to linear, 3–8 × 0.3–0.7 cm, base gradually narrowed down, apex abruptly acute, margin of leaf apical half with 1–3 mucro growing along each side, upper surfaces green, lower surfaces pale green, glabrous above and below, midvein prominent on both sides; petioles 0.3–2 cm long, glabrous, base slightly broaden. Capitula with 3 florets each, bearing short peduncles of 2–11 mm, arranged as raceme to narrow panicle at terminal; inflorescence axis with few subulate bracteoles. Involucres narrow cylindric‑tubular, 9–11 × 2.5–3 mm; phyllaries 5‑seriate, glabrous or subglabrous, tinged purple‑red at apex and along margin; outer phyllaries ovate, 1–2.5 × 0.5–1 mm, shortly acuminate; median ones ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.2–1.8 mm, acuminate or acute, margin thinly scarious; inner ones lanceolate to lanceolate‑oblong, 8–11 × 1.5–2 mm, acute, margin broadly scarious. Receptacle small, naked. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla white, ca. 1 cm, upper limb deeply and obliquely cleft into 5 linear segments; anther bases sagittate and caudate, apical appendages obtuse‑rounded to truncate; stylar branches divergent, short, less than 0.5 mm, flat, apices obtuse‑rounded. Cypselae brown, oblanceolate‑oblong, 4–6 × 0.6–1 mm, compressed, ribbed, densely villous. Pappus plumose, 6–6.5 mm, base connate.

Locality: Tai Tam, Bride's Pool, Luk Keng. P. S. Choi 229; Y. S. Lau 2636; S. Y. Hu 6565 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was derived from cultivated plants raised from seed collected by Captain Walker from Hong Kong Island before 1873.

Ajuga nipponensis Makino 紫背金盤
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 23(267): 67 – 68. 1909; FRPS 65(2): 76. 1977; FOC 17: 68. 1994; FGD 3: 392. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 438, pl. 186. 1998.
Ajuga genevensis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 561. 1753; FKH 212. 1912.
Ajuga decumbens auct. non Thunb.: FKH 212. 1912.

Annual or biennial herbs, 10–20 cm or taller; stems usually erect, branched from base, villous or pilose. Leaves opposite, petiolate; leaf blade broadly elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, 2–4.5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex obtuse, margin irregularly undulate‑crenate, ciliate, sparsely hirsute or pubescent on both surfaces. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming terminal spike‑like inflorescence; lower bracts similar to stem leaf, gradually reduced upward, ovate to broadly lanceolate, 0.8–1.5 cm, green or sometimes tinged with purple, ciliate; pedicels short or almost absent. Calyx campanulate, 3–5 mm, villous on upper half, the teeth triangular, subequal, about half the length of the calyx. Corolla bluish or blue‑purple, rarely white or greenish, with dark lines, 7–11 mm, base slightly swollen, sparsely pubescent adaxially, villous annulate at throat abaxially; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe flabellate, truncate or emarginate at apex, lateral lobes narrowly oblong. Nutlets obovoid rugose‑reticulate dorsally.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ping Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2683; P. S. Choi 531; Y. W. Lam 1307.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Wet places, old walls. Flowering: Dec.–Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Alangium chinense (Lour.) Harms 八角楓
Ber. Deutsch. Bot. Ges. 15: 24. 1897; Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 637, fig. 252. 1963; FHN 3: 119. 1974; FRPS 52(2): 166. 1983; FGD 3: 288. 1995.
Stylidium chinense Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 221. 1790.
Alangium lamarckii auct. non Thwaites: FKH 120. 1912.
Marlea begoniaefolia Roxb., [Hort. Bengal. 28. 1814]; Pl. Corom. 3: 80, t. 283. 1819; FHK 138. 1861; FKH 120. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, 3–5(–15) m tall. Branchlets pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petioles reddish, 2.5–3.5 cm, puberulous, glabrescent; leaf blade suborbicular, elliptic or ovate, 13–19 × 3–7 cm, papery, base usually oblique, one side rounded and the other side cuneate, apex acuminate, entire or 3–7-lobed, adaxially glabrous, abaxially tufted pubescent at axils of veins; basal veins 3–5(–7). Inflorescences cymose, many-flowered. Flowers ca. 2 cm; pedicels 0.5–1.5 mm; bracteoles linear or lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Calyx-lobes 6–8, toothlike, 0.5–1 × 2.5–3 mm. Petals 6–8, white at first, turning yellow later, linear, 1–1.5 cm. Stamens isomerous and as long as petals; filaments slightly flat, 2–3 mm, pubescent; anthers 6–8 mm, connectives glabrous. Style glabrous, stigma capitate, 2–4-lobed. Drupe ovoid, 5–7 × 5–8 mm, black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2392; Y. S. Lau 2502; HK sheet 2178.
Distribution: S, E, C & SW China; SE Asia, E Africa.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: May – Jul., Sep. – Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Albizia chinensis (Osbeck) Merr. 楹樹
Amer. J. Bot. 3(10): 575. 1916; FRPS 39: 67. 1988; FGD 5: 148. 2003.
Mimosa chinensis Osbeck, Dagbok Ostind. Resa 233. 1757.
Acacia stipulata DC., Prodr. 2: 469. 1825.
Albizia stipulata (DC.) Boiv., Encycl. 19(2): 33. 1838; FHK 102. 1861; FKH 91. 1912.

Deciduous tree, up to 30 m tall; branchlets yellow pubescent. Stipules large, membranous, cordate, apex apiculate, deciduous. Leaves bipinnate, pinnae 6 – 12 pairs, with glands near base of petioles and on leaf-rachis; leaflets 20– 35(–40) pairs, sessile, oblong-linear, falcate, 6 – 10 × 2 – 3 mm, base subtruncate, apex acuminate, margin ciliate, villose abaxially; midvein close to upper edge. Heads consisting of 10 – 20 flowers, forming a terminal panicle. Peduncles long or short, densely villose. Flowers greenish white or lightly yellow, densely yellow brown tomentose. Calyx funnel-shaped, 3 mm, shortly 5-toothed. Corolla twice as long as calyx, lobes ovate-deltoid. Stamens 25 mm. Ovary yellow brown villose. Pods plano-compressed, 10 – 15 × 2 cm, initially ± pubescent, glabrous when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lautau Island. C. P. Lau 61; Y. S. Lau 1160; HK sheet 37913.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Hunan, Yunnan, Xizang; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, open fields. Flowering: Mar. –May; fruiting: Jun.– Dec.
Uses: Timber.

Albizia corniculata (Lour.) Druce 天香藤
Rept. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 4: 603. 1917; FRPS 39: 57. 1988; FGD 5: 146. 2003.
Mimosa corniculata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 651. 1790.
Albizia millettii Benth., London J. Bot. 3: 89. 1844; FHK 102. 1861; FKH 91. 1912.

Scandent shrub or vine, 5–20 m or longer. Branchlets often with a curved prickle under petiole. Stipules small, deciduous. Petioles with a complanate gland near the base. Leaves bipinnate, pinnae 2 – 6 pairs; leaflets 4 – 10 pairs, oblong or obovate-oblong, 12 – 25 × 7–15 mm, base oblique, apex obtuse or emarginate or ± mucronate, glabrous adaxially, puberulous abaxially. Heads consisting usually of 6 – 12 sessile flowers, forming a terminal or axillary panicle; peduncle slender, sparsely pubescent, 5 – 10 mm. Calyx shorter than 1 mm, puberulent. Corolla white, puberulent; tube 4 mm, lobes 2 mm; filaments 1 cm. Pods strap-shaped, 10–20 × 3–4 cm, flat, glabrous. Seeds 7–11, oblong, brown.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1770; Y. S. Lau 129, 1986.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Philippines, Kalimantan.
Ecology: Open fields or forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. –Nov.

Albizia julibrissin Durazz. 合歡
Mag. Tosc. 3(4): 11. 1772; FRPS 39: 65. 1988; FGD 5: 148, fig. 86. 2003.

Deciduous tree, up to 16 m tall. Branchlets angular, together with leaf-rachis, inflorescences tomentose or pubescent. Stipules linear-lanceolate, much smaller than leaflet, deciduous. Leaves bipinnate, pinnae 4–12 pairs, sometimes to 20 pairs in cultivation, with glands near base of petioles and on leaf-rachis of uppermost pinnae; leaflets 10–30 pairs, obliquely linear to oblong, 6–12 × 1–4 mm, apex apiculate, midvein close to upper edge, base truncate, margin ciliate; panicles terminal. Flowers pink. Calyx tubular, 3 mm. Corolla 8 mm, lobes triangular, 1.5 mm. Calyx and corolla pubescent; filaments 2.5 cm. Pods strap-shaped, flat, 9–15 × 1.5–2.5 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1117.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; temperate region of Aisa, widely cultivated and naturalized.
Ecology: Flowering: May – Jul.
Uses: Environmental.

Albizia lebbeck (L.) Benth. 大葉合歡
London J. Bot. 3: 87. 1844; FRPS 39: 62. 1988; FGD 5: 148. 2003.
Mimosa lebbeck L., Sp. Pl. 516. 1753.

Deciduous tree, 8–12 m tall. Branchlets minutely pubescent, glabrous in age. Stipules small, caducous. Leaves bipinnate; with disk-like glands near the base of petioles and at the insertion of pinnae on rachis, pubescent or glabrous; pinnae 2 – 4 pairs, 6 – 15 cm; leaflets 4–8 pairs, long elliptic or slightly oblique-oblong, 2 – 4.5 × (0.9–)1.3 – 2 cm, apex obtuse or retuse, glabrous on both surfaces or sparsely and finely pubescent abaxially, midvein slightly close to upper edge. Heads up to 4 cm in diam. Peduncles 1 – 4 together axillary. Pedicels 3 – 4 mm, puberulous. Flowers fragrant. Calyx tubular, 4 mm, puberulous, with short teeth. Corolla greenish yellow, infundibuliform, 7 – 8 mm, lobes deltoid-ovate. Stamens white or light yellowish green. Pods straw yellow, strap-shaped, 15 – 28 × 2.5–4.5 cm, flat, remain on trees very long after ripen. Seeds brown, 4 – 12, elliptic, 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 7; Y. S. Lau 1951, 2608.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; native to tropical Africa, widely cultivated throughout tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Roadsides and gardens. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Oct. –May of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Althaea rosea (L.) Cav. 蜀葵
Diss. 2: 91, t. 28, fig 1. 1786; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 9, pl. 3. 1955; FRPS 49(2): 11, pl. 3: 1–3. 1984; FGD 2: 196, fig. 123. 1991.
Alcea rosea L., Sp. Pl. 687. 1753.

Biennial herb, 1–2 m tall at anthesis; densely bristly throughout. Leaves alternate; stipules ovate, 8 mm; petioles 5–15 cm; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, 6–16 cm in diam., palmately and shallowly 5–7-lobed; lobes triangular or subrotundate, sparsely stellate pubescent on adaxial surface, stellate bristly or tomentose and bristly on abaxial surface. Flowers solitary or subfasciculate, axillary, often raceme-like due to subtending leaves gradually diminishing into leaf-like bracts; pedicels 2– 5 mm, lengthening to 15 mm in fruit, densely lanate and bristly; involucral bracts 6- or 7-lobed, ovate-lanceolate. Calyx longer than bracts, densely bristly, striate and sulcate. Corolla 6 – 8 cm across, color various, usually red. Fruit 2 cm in diam., pubescent; carpels suborbicular, back 1 mm wide, longitudinally sulcate, sides 4 mm in diam., striate-sulcate, reticulate, rugose, black.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7275, 7275A, 13018 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely cultivated, origin unknown.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Aug.

Alchornea trewioides (Benth.) Müll. Arg. 紅背山麻桿

Linnaea 34: 168. 1865; FKH 239. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 70, pl. 16: 1–3. 1996; FGD 5: 86. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 47. 2005.

Stipellaria trewioides Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 3. 1854; FHK 305. 1861.


Shrub, 1–2 m tall; branchlets initially grey-puberulous. Leaves thinly papery; stipules lanceolate, 2–3.5 mm; stipels subulate, 3–5 mm, hairy, deciduous; petioles 7–12 cm; leaf blade broad-ovate, 8–15 × 7–13 cm, base shallowly cordate or subtruncate, with 4 macular glands, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely glandular-serrulate, glabrous adaxially, reddish and puberulous along veins abaxially; basal veins 3. Male inflorescences spicate axillary, 7–15 cm, puberulous; bracts triangular, ca. 1 mm. Female inflorescences racemose, terminal, 5–6 cm, 5–12-flowered, puberulous; bracts narrowly triangular, ca. 4 mm, with 2 glands at base; bracteoles lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Male flowers: 3–11 clustered in axil of bract; pedicels ca. 2 mm, glabrous, jointed at middle; sepals 4, oblong, glabrous; stamens 7–8. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 1 mm; sepals 5–6, lanceolate, 3–4 mm, pubescent, one of them with a gland at base; ovary globose, tomentellous; styles 3, linear, 12–15 mm, connate at base. Capsules globose, 8–10 mm in diam., 3-sulcate smooth, tomentellous.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 973; K. Y. Tam 116, 126; S. Y. Hu 7256 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Thailand.

Ecology: Thin forests and shrublands. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Aleurites moluccana (L.)Willd. 石栗
Sp. Pl. 4: 590. 1805; FRPS 44(2): 140, pl. 33: 1 – 4. 1996; FGD 5: 107. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 49. 2005.
Jatropha moluccana L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1006. 1753.
Aleurites triloba J. R. Forst. & G. Forst., Char. Gen. Pl. (ed. 2) 111, pl. 56. 1776.

Evergreen tree to 18 m tall; bark deep-grey; young parts stellate-hairy. Leaves papery; petioles 6–12 cm, densely stellate-puberulous, biglandular at apex; leaf blade ovate, ovate-oblong, ovate-lanceolate or ovate-triangular, 14–20 × 7–17 cm, entire or shallowly 1–5-lobed, base broad-cuneate or rounded, rarely shallowly cordate, apex acute to acuminate; basal veins 3–5. Panicles corymbiform, 15–20 cm. Male flowers: calyx 2–3 mm, deeply 2-lobed, densely puberulous; petals oblong or lanceolate, 6–10 mm, white, adaxially hairy at base; stamens 15–20, in 3–4 series. Female flowers: calyx ca. 6 mm, usually 3-lobed; petals slightly longer than calyx; ovary densely stellate-puberulous, 2-locular; styles 2, ca. 2 mm, 2-parted. Drupes subglobose or laterally compressed, ca. 5 × 5–6 cm, 2-seeded; seeds laterally flat; testa hard and tuberculate-ribbed.

Locality:Widely cultivated in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 489; Y. S. Lau 3112; HK sheet 32812; S. Y. Hu 5361, 10627 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, material (lipids).

Alisma plantago-aquatica L. 澤瀉
Sp. Pl. 342. 1753; Dandy in Tutin et al., Fl. Europ. 5: 2. 1980; FRPS 8: 141. 1992; R. Haynes, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 352. 2001; FGD 9: 159. 2009; FOC 23: 87. 2010.

Perennial herb, growing in tufts at the bottom of the water. Tuber fleshy, 1–3.5 cm in diam., or more. Submersed leaves linear or lanceolate; emersed leaves petiolate; petioles of 1.5–30 cm, base sheathed, upper part terete, spongy; leaf blades broadlanceolate, elliptic to ovate, 2–11 × 1.3–7 cm, base broad-cunneate to shallowly cordate, apex acuminate, rarely acute; veins 5. Scapes 78 – 100 cm tall or more. Inflorescences paniculate, with 4–9 whorls, each whorl with 3–5 flowers or branches. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 2.5–3.5 × 2–3 mm, 7-veined. Petals white, pink or purplish, suborbiculate, 3.5–6.5 × 3.6 mm. Stamens in 1 series, filaments filiform. Carpels 17–23 in a single whorl; styles ventral. Achenes elliptic or suboblong, 2.5 × 1.5 mm, compressed, dorsally with 1–2 shallow sulci. Seeds purple-brown.

Locality: Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2575.
Distribution: NE to NW China, Yunnan; widespread throughout most regions of Europe and Asia.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Allamanda cathartica L. 軟枝黃蟬
Mant. Pl. 2: 214. 1771; FHK 217. 1861; FRPS 63: 76, pl. 25. 1977; FGD 1: 428, fig. 473. 1987; FOC 16: 166. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 70, fig. 23. 1999.
Allemanda cathartia L. var. hendersonii (Bull. ex Dombrain) L. H. Bailey & Raffill, Stand. Cycl. Hort. 1: 247. 1914; FRPS 63: 76. 1977.

Shrubs trailing, to 4 m, with white latex. Stems glabrous. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 – 5; petioles ca. 5 mm; leaf blade obovate, narrowly obovate, or oblong, 6 – 15 × 4 – 5 cm, glabrous or villous along veins on abaxial surface, lateral veins flattened. Peduncle short. Corolla yellow; tube 4 – 8 cm, amply funnelform, cylindric in proximal half, campanulate in distal half, limb 9 – 14 cm in diam.; lobes obovate‑truncate to orbicular. Capsules subglobose, 3 – 7 × 3 – 5 cm, white spines to 1 cm. Seeds compressed, winged or with a membranous margin.

Locality: Commonly cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1621; HK sheet 18570, 18574.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan (cultivated); native to Guiana.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. – Dec.
Usese: Ornamental.

Allamanda schottii Pohl 黃蟬
Pl. Bras. Icon. Descr. 1: 73, pl. 58. 1827; FOC 16: 165. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 72. 1999.
Allemanda neriifolia Hook., Bot. Mag. 77, pl. 4594. 1851; FRPS 63: 75. 1977; FGD 1: 427, fig. 472. 1987.

Shrubs erect, to 2 m tall, with clear sap. Leaves in whorls of 3 – 5, subsessile; leaf blade elliptic or narrowly obovate, 5–14 × 2–4 cm, minutely hispid along veins, lateral veins elevated on abaxial surface. Flowers 4–6 cm. Corolla tube rather narrowly funnelform, ca. 3 cm, distinctly inflated at base, limb ca. 4 cm in diam.; lobes pale yellow, ovate or orbicular, ca. 2 cm, obtuse. Capsules globose, ca. 3 cm in diam., long spiny. Seeds ca. 2 × 1.5 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated. Y. S. Lau 486, 1434; HK sheet 18579.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan (cultivated).
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Oct.; fruiting: Jan. – Mar.
Uses: Ornamental.

Alleizettella leucocarpa (Champ. ex Benth.) Tirveng. 白果香楠（白果山黃皮）
Nordic J. Bot. 3(4): 455. 1983; FRPS 71(1): 358, pl. 92: 8 – 11. 1999; FGD 6: 183, fig. 96. 2005.
Randia leucocarpa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 194. 1852; FHK 154. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall, unarmed. Branchlets and petioles rusty strigose, glabrescent in age. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 2.5–5(–10) mm; stipules broadly triangular, ca. 5 mm, apex acuminate, hairy; leaf blade oblong‑obovate, oblong, narrowly elliptic or lanceolate, 4.5–11(–17) × 1.5 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, rusty strigose along midvein and lateral veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins slender, 4–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes few‑flowered, terminal on lateral short branches and on nodes of old branches, strigose. Peduncles to 2 mm or almost none. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx strigose; tube bell‑shaped, 2–2.5 mm, strigose; lobes 5, triangular, ca. 1 mm, apex acute. Corolla white, salverform; tube ca. 3 mm, strigose on the upper part of abaxial surface, villose on the throat; lobes 5, subovate, 2.5–3 mm, apex acute, spreading. Berry globose, 0.8 – 1.3 cm in diam., pale yellowish white when mature, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, 2–4‑seeded.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 422, 507; Y. W. Lam 1389.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Apr. –Jun.; fruiting: Apr.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Allium chinense G. Don 蕎頭
Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 6: 83. 1827; FRPS 14: 259, pl. 84. 1980; FOC 24: 196. 2000; FGD 5: 448. 2003.

Perennial herb. Bulbs clustered, narrowly ovoid, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; coated with white or reddish tunic. Leaves radical, 2–5, semiterete, fistulose, 25–45 cm × 1–3 mm, obscurely 3–5-angled. Scape lateral, subequalling leaves, terete, covered with leaf sheaths only at base. Involucral bract 2-valved, persistent. Umbel nearly hemispheric, laxly flowered; pedicels subequal, 2–4 times longer than perianth, bracteolate. Perianth pale purple to dull purple; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones slightly shorter than inner ones, broadly elliptic to suborbicular, 4–6 × 3–4 mm. Stamens 6; filaments equal, about one and a half the length of perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments; outer ones subulate; inner ones broadened at base, 1-toothed on each side. Ovary obovoid-globose, with concave nectaries covered by hood-like projections at base; style exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 11871.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical China, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indochina, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Allium fistulosum L. 蔥
Sp. Pl. 1: 301. 1753; FRPS 14: 256, pl. 80. 1980; FOC 24: 193. 2000; FGD 5: 449. 2003.

Perennial herb. Bulb cylindrical, solitary or clustered, coated with white or red-brown tunic. Leaves cylindrical, fistulose, 25–50 × 0.5–1 cm, gradually narrowed toward the pointed apex. Scape erect, terete, fistulose, slightly longer than leaves, covered with leaf sheaths for ca. 1/3 its length. Involucral bract 2-valved, persistent. Umbel globose, many-flowered; pedicels subequal, slender, 2–3 times longer than perianth; bracteoles absent. Perianth white; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones slightly shorter than inner ones, ovate, 4–7 × 2–3 mm, apex acuminate, with a reflexed point. Stamens 6; filaments equal, about 1.5–2 times longer than perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments. Ovary obovoid, with inconspicuous nectaries at base; style exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2679; K. S. Pang 8.
Distribution: Possibly native to W China, but no wild plants have been collected; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), food (vegetable).

Allium sativum L. 蒜頭
Sp. Pl. 1: 296. 1753; FRPS 14: 268, pl. 96. 1980; FOC 24: 200. 2000; FGD 5: 449. 2003.

Perennial herb. Bulb solitary, globose to applanate-globose, usually consisting of 6–10 bulbils enclosed in a common tunic; tunic white to purplish, membranous, entire. Leaves broadly linear to linear-lanceolate, flat or keeled abaxially, shorter than scape, to 2.5 cm wide, apex acuminate. Scape 25–60 cm, terete, covered with leaf sheaths for ca. 1/2 its length. Involucral bract united into a tube enclosing the umbel, upward gradually narrowed into a beak of 7–20 cm, deciduous. Umbel with many bulblets and few flowers; pedicels slender, longer than perianth; bracteoles ovate, rather large, membranous, apex acute. Perianth usually pale red; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones ovate-lanceolate, ca. 4 × 1.4 mm; inner ones ovate, ca. 3 × 1.4 mm. Stamens 6; filaments shorter than perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments; outer ones subulate; inner ones broadened at base, 1-toothed on each side, teeth with apex filiform and longer than perianth segments. Ovary globose; style not exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 9.
Distribution: Only cultivated, possibly of W Asia origin.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Allium tuberosum Rottler ex Spreng. 韭
Syst. Veg. 2: 38. 1825; FRPS 14: 221, pl. 47. 1980; FOC 24: 179. 2000; FGD 5: 450. 2003.
Allium odorum auct. non L.: FKH 280. 1912.

Perennial herb. Bulbs cylindrical, clustered, coated with yellowish brown tunic. Leaves radical, linear, flat and solid, 15–30 cm × 1.5–8 mm, margin smooth. Scape terete, 20–50 cm, ± 2-angled, covered with leaf sheaths only at base. Involucral bract 2–3-valved, persistent. Umbel hemispheric to subglobose, laxly many-flowered; pedicels subequal, 2–4 times longer than perianth, bracteolate. Perianth white; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones oblong-ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 4–7 × 1.8–3 mm, inner ones oblong-ovate, 4–7 × 2–3.5 mm. Stamens 6; filaments equal, about 4/5 the length of perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments. Ovary obconical-globose, without concave nectaries at base.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2594.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China and elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), food (vegetable).

Alloteropsis cimicina (L.) Stapf 臭蟲草
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 487. 1919; FHN 4: 430. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 303, pl. 93: 7–11. 1990; FOC 22: 519. 2006; FGD 9: 432. 2009.
Milium cimicinum L., Mant. Pl. 184. 1771.
Axonopus cimicinus (L.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 12, 154. 1812; FKH 313. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, ascending, up to 60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, cordate, 3–10 × 1–2 cm, glabrous, abaxial surface pectinate-setose along margins and veins, adaxial surface glabrous; ligule ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 4–6, 10–15 cm, narrowly ascending, rachis glabrous, bare of spikelets in the lower part, spikelets paired or solitary. Lower glume ovate-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, 3-veined, acuminate; upper glume as long as spikelet, papery, margins stiff ciliate, apex acute; lower lemma similar to upper glume but thicker and glabrous, palea small, stamens 3; upper lemma ovate-elliptic, tuberculate, awn 2–3 mm; upper palea papillose with swollen lacrimiform hairs.

Locality: Kowloon. HK sheet 38086.
Distribution: Hainan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Pacific islands, Cambodia, New Guinea, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Weedy places, thin forests. Flowering: Sep.

Alloteropsis semialata (R. Br.) Hitchc. 毛穎草
Contr. U. S. Natl. Herb. 12: 210. 1909; FHN 4: 429. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 301, pl. 93: 1–4. 1990; FFJ 6: 227, fig. 193. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 454, pl. 188. 2000; FOC 22: 519. 2006; FGD 9: 432, fig. 223. 2009.
Panicum semialatum R. Br., Prodr. 192. 1810.
Axonopus semialatus (R. Br.) Hook. f., Fl. of Brit. Ind. 7(21): 64. 1897[1896]; FKH 313. 1912.

Perennial herb with a short rhizome. Culms erect, tufted, 30–70 cm, ± pubescent below inflorescence and bearded at nodes. Leaf sheaths persistent, densely and conspicuously silky hairy, upper glabrous or margins and mouth pilose; leaf blades linear, flat or convolute, stiff, 10–50 × 0.1–1 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, tuberculate-pilose, adaxial surface sparsely to densely hairy; ligule membranous, ca. 1 mm. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–4, 3–13 cm, rachis slender, triangled, pilose. Spikelets lanceolate, 5–6 mm, usually paired on one side; lower glume ovate, ca. 1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined, mucronate or awn-tipped; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined, margins ciliate, occasionally winged, awntipped; lower lemma as long as upper glume, awnless, often sparsely ciliate along margins, embraced a short hyaline, clefted, small palea; upper lemma ovate-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, smooth, with a rigid 2–3 mm awn-point. Anthers orange, ca. 3 mm; style exserted apically.

Locality: Aberdeen, Kadoorie Farm, Tuen Mun. S. C. Ng 2169; HK sheet 8231, 32244.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Pacific islands, Africa.
Ecology: Hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Feb. – Aug.

Alniphyllum fortunei (Hemsl.)Makino 赤楊葉
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 20: 93. 1906; FGD 1: 383. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 122. 1987; FOC 15: 264. 1996.
Halesia fortunei Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 75. 1889.
Alniphyllum pterospermum auct. non Matsum.: FKH 164. 1912.

Tree to 20 m tall; bark greyish brown; branchlets, leaves, inflorescence brownish stellate-pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 8 –18 × 4 – 8 cm, apex acute to acuminate, base broadly cuneate to cuneate, margin remotely serrate, sparsely to densely brownish stellate pubescent to tomentose, sometimes glabrescent abaxially, lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate, 10 –20-flowered, 8 –15 cm; flowers 1.5 –2 cm, reddish white; pedicels 4 – 8 mm; calyx cup-shaped, 4 –5 mm, densely grey stellate pubescent, with ovate-lanceolate teeth; corolla lobes elliptic, 10 –15 × 5 –7 mm; stamens 10, filament-tube ca. 8 mm, anthers 3 mm; style 1.5 –1.8 cm, villose. Fruit oblong to ellipsoid, 1–2.5 cm, black, sparsely white stellate pubescent or glabrous. Seeds many, oblong, 5–7 mm, winged at both ends.

Locality: Happy Valley, Mount Nicholson, Kwun Yam Shan, New Territories, Lantau Island. HK sheet 18179, 35066; W. J. Tutcher 8484.
Distribution: Hainan, Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; India, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests on hill slopes. Flowering: Apr.– Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Alocasia cucullata (Lour.) Schott 尖尾芋
Melet. Bot. 18. 1832; FKH 289. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 75, pl. 14: 1. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 5: 667. 2000; FGD 9: 202. 2009.
Arum cucullatum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 536. 1790.
Alocasia cucullata (Lour.) G. Don, Hort. Brit. ed. 3, 631. 1839; FFJ 6: 434. 1995; FOC 23: 78. 2010; Check List HK Plants 105. 2004.

Herb evergreen, caulescent stock erect, 3–6 cm thick, branched, stoloniferous. Leaves peltate; petiole green, 25–80 cm, sheathed below medium; blade broadly ovate to ovate-cordate, 10–16 (–40) × 7–18(–28) cm, base shallowly cordate, apex acute, margin entire; lateral veins 4–8 on each side, the lowest one basal. Inflorescences usually solitary, axillary. Peduncle terete, 20–30 cm. Spathe green, tube oblong-ovoid, 4–8 cm; limb cymbiform, 5–15 cm, margin convolute. Spadix shorter than spathe, ca. 10 cm; female portion cylindrical, 1.5–2.5 cm; sterile male portion 2–3 cm; fertile male portion subfusiform, 3.5 cm; appendage pale green, yellowish green, narrowly conical, ca. 3.5 cm. Berry subglobose, 6–8 mm in diam., 1-seeded.

Locality: Happy Valley, Victoria Peak, Sha Tin, Tai Mong Tsai, Sai Keng, Nam Chung, Luk Keng. HK sheet 33004, 33063.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides, wet places. Flowering: May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Alocasia macrorrhizos (L.) G. Don 海芋
Hort. Brit. ed. 3, 631. 1839; FFJ 6: 435, fig. 394. 1995.
Arum macrorrhizum L., Sp. Pl. ed. 1: 965. 1753.
Arum indicum Lour., Fl. Cochich. 2: 536. 1790.
Caladium odorum Lindl., Bot. Reg. 8: t. 641. 1822.
Colocasia odora (Lindl.) Bornyn., Nouv. Ann. Mus. Hist. Nat. 3: 145, t. 7. 1834; FHK 343. 1861.
Alocasia odora (Roxb.) K. Koch, Index Seminum Hort. Berol. 1854(App.): 5. 1854; FOC 23: 77. 2010; Check List HK Plants 105. 2004.
Colocasia indica (Lour.) Kunth., Enum. Pl. 3: 39. 1841; FHK 343. 1861.
Alocasia macrorrhiza (L.) Schott, Osterr. Bot. Wochenbl. 4: 409. 1854; FKH 289. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 76. 1979; FGD 9: 203, fig. 117. 2009; Check List HK Plants 298. 2002, nom. illeg. prior.

Large evergreen perennial herb, to 2(–3) m tall; caulescent stock stout, to 15 cm thick, unbranched. Leaves spirally arranged, crowded toward apex of the stock, ± peltate; petiole green, 0.5–2(–3) m, sheathing at base; leaf blade broadly ovate, 50–100 × 40–100 cm, base sagittate, apex acute, margin entire; lateral veins 9–12 pairs. Peduncle 2–3 together, terete, green, 12–60 cm. Spathe tube inrolled, green, narrowly ellipsoidal, 5–9 cm, convolute and constricted at apex; limb yellowish green or pale green, lanceolate and concave, 10–20 × 4–5 cm. Spadix rather short: female portion green, 2–4 cm; sterile male portion white or pale green, 2.5–6 cm; fertile male portion 3–7 cm; appendage yellowish, conical, 3–5.5 cm. Berries ovoid, 8–10 mm, red when mature, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 7732, 29735.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Bangaladesh, India, Malay Peninsula, Indochina, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests and shaded places. Flowering: All year round in tropics.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Some authors consider Alocasia odora a distinct species which differs from A. macrorrhizos in having shortly peltate leaves, whereas leaves of A. macrorrhizos are deeply cordate at the base with the lateral costae partially naked in the sinus.

records.text:
Aloe vera (L.) Burm. f. 蘆薈
Fl. Indica 83. 1768; FOC 24: 160. 2000; FGD 6: 355, fig. 210. 2005.
Aloe perfoliata L. var. vera L., Sp. Pl. 1: 320. 1753.
Aloe barbadensis Mill. var. chinensis Haw., Supp. Pl. Succ. 45. 1819.
Aloe chinensis (Haw.) Baker, Bot. Mag. pl. 6301. 1877.
Aloe vera (L.) Burm. f. var. chinensis (Haw.) A. Berger, Pflanzenr. 33(IV, 38, 3): 230. 1908; FRPS 14: 62, fig. 8. 1980; Check List HK Plants 365. 2002; 127. 2004.

A succulent herb. Stems short, suckering freely to form dense clumps. Leaves nearly basal, pale green, sometimes with pale spots in very young plants, linear-lanceolate, 15–35(–50) × 4–5(–7) cm, apex 2–3-dentate-pointed, margin sparsely spiny-dentate. Inflorescence erect, 60–90 cm; peduncle to 2 cm thick; raceme 30–40 cm, sometimes with 1–2 branches, many-flowered; bracts whitish, broadly lanceolate, ca. 1 cm, veins 5–7, apex acute. Flowers reflexed; pedicel nearly half as long as bract. Perianth pale yellow mottled with red, slightly ventricose, 2.5(–3) cm, outer lobes slightly recurved at apex. Style conspicuously exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28788, 28789.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S and SW China; probably originated in Mediterranean region, widely cultivated and occasionally naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Alopecurus aequalis Sobol. 看麥娘
Fl. Petrop. 16. 1799; FKH 325. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 264, pl. 64: 8 – 9. 1987; FFJ 6: 113, fig. 85. 1995; FOC 22: 366. 2006; FGD 9: 396, fig. 203. 2009.
Alopecurus amurensis Kom., Izv. Imp. Bot. Sada Petra Velikago 16: 151. 1961.
Alopecurus aequalis Sobol. var. amurensis (Kom.) Ohwi, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 55: 360. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 5: 343. 2000.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, 10–45 cm tall. Culms loosely tufted, ascending from geniculate base. Leaf blades soft, 2–10 cm × 2–6 mm, abaxial surface smooth, glabrous, adaxial surface closely ribbed, scaberulous; ligule 2–5 mm, obtuse; leaf sheaths smooth, slightly inflated. Panicle narrowly cylindrical, 2–7 × 3–6 mm, pale grey-green. Spikelets elliptic or oblong, 1.5–3 mm; glumes membranous, smooth, keels ciliate-hispid, lateral veins hispid on lower part, margins connate at base, ± parallel at the tips, apices obtuse; lemma equalling or slightly longer than glumes, margins connate below middle, awned from lower 1/4–1/3, apex obtuse; awn included within spikelet or exserted up to 1.2 mm, straight. Anthers orange, 0.5–0.8 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 836, 1539; S. P. Lau 106.
Distribution: Spread over most provinces of China; widely distributed in Europe, temperate Asia and N America.
Ecology: Banks of ditches, rice fields, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–May.

Alopecurus japonicus Steud. 日本看麥娘
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 149. 1854; FKH 325. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 262, pl. 64: 6–7. 1987; FFJ 6: 114. 1995; FOC 22: 366. 2006; FGD 9: 396. 2009.

Annual herb, 25–50 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, often forming large clump. Leaf blades soft, glaucous, 3–12 × 0.3–0.7 cm, abaxial surface smooth, adaxial surface scaberulous; ligule 2–5 mm. Panicle cylindrical, 3–10 cm, yellowgreen; leaf sheaths lax, smooth, glabrous, upper sheaths inflated. Spikelets ovate-oblong, 4.8–7 mm; glumes herbaceous, smooth, keels wingless, stiffly ciliate, lateral veins pubescent near base or glabrous, margins connate only at extreme base, apices subacute; lemma slightly longer than glumes, herbaceous, margins connate in lower 2/5, awned from near base, apex subacute; awn exserted 5 – 8 mm from spikelet, weakly geniculate, column not twisted. Anthers white, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. HK sheet 30736.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Banks of rice fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–May.

Alpinia calcarata Roscoe 距花山薑
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8: 347. 1807; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 97. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 84. 1981; FOC 24: 336. 2000.

Pseudostems to 1.3 m. Leaves sessile; ligule 8 – 15 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse; leaf blade linear-lanceolate, 20–32 × 2–3.5 cm or narrower, base attenuate, apex acuminate and caudate-mucronate, margin with well-spaced, short bristles, glabrous. Panicles less than 10 cm; rachis slightly velvety; proximal branches 3–4-flowered. Bracteoles oblong, to 1.7 cm, membranous, apex obtuse. Pedicel ca. 3 mm. Calyx to 1.2 cm, split on 1 side, pubescent, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube white, ca. 9 mm; lobes oblong, ca. 2.2 cm. Lateral staminodes red, subulate, ca. 3 mm, adnate to base of labellum. Labellum white with rose red and purple streaks, obovate, 2.7–3.5 × 1.5–2 cm, apex emarginate. Filaments ca. 1.3 cm; anther 5–7 mm. Ovary 3–4 mm in diam., sericeous. Capsules red, globose.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Tai Au Mun, Tin Ha Village. Y. S. Lau 2998; HK sheet 34821.
Distribution: Guangdong; Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Alpinia formosana K. Schum. 美山薑
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 27(3): 283. 1899; FRPS 16(2): 86. 1981; FOC 24: 336. 2000.

Pseudostems to 1(–3.5) m. Ligule to 1 cm, abaxially villous, apex obtuse; petiole absent or to 1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or oblonglanceolate, 50–70 × 8–12 cm, both ends acuminate. Panicles narrow, 15–20 cm; rachis glabrous or sparsely villous; branches 2–3-flowered; bracteoles elliptic, ca. 1.5 cm, apex mucronate. Pedicel ca. 3 mm. Calyx 1.3–1.7 cm, split on 1 side, apex 3-toothed, ciliate. Corolla tube ca. 1 cm, glabrous; lobes oblong, ca. 1.5 cm, apex ciliate. Lateral staminodes subulate, less than 2 mm. Labellum white tinged with yellow, marked with red stripes at centre, broadly ovate, ca. 3 cm, apex shortly 2-cleft, crisped. Stamen ca. 2 cm, with a knee-like bend. Ovary subglobose, white sericeous. Capsule vermilion, ellipsoidal, wrinkled.

Locality: Hong Kong Wai, Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 5526 (CUHK).
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Alpinia galanga (L.) Willd. 紅豆蔻
Sp. Pl. 1(1): 12. 1797; FHK 348. 1861; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 97. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 71. 1981; FGD 2: 411. 1991; FOC 24: 343. 2000.

Rhizomes tuberous. Pseudostems ca. 2 m. Ligule suborbicular, ca. 5 mm; petiole ca. 6 mm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 25–35 × 6–10 cm, base attenuate, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous or abaxially pubescent. Panicles ca. 20 × 30 cm; rachis glabrous or pubescent; branches many, 2–4 cm, 3–6-flowered. Bracts and bracteoles persistent; bracteoles lanceolate, 5–8 mm. Flowers greenwhite, fragrant. Calyx tubular, 6–10 mm, persistent. Corolla tube 6–10 mm; lobes oblong, 1.6–1.8 cm. Lateral staminodes purple, subulate or linear, 2–10 mm. Labellum white with red lines, obovate-spatulate, ca. 2 cm, apex deeply 2-cleft. Filaments ca. 1 cm; anther ca. 7 mm. Capsules brown or red when dry, oblong, slightly contracted at middle, 1–1.5 cm × ca. 7 mm, thin, glabrous. Seeds 3–6.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Ma Nam Wat, Tsung Tsai Yuen, Sha Lo Tung, Chung Mei, Nam Chung. H. C. Tang 226; Y. S. Lau 2732; L. T. Lo 497.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Alpinia hainanensis K. Schum. 草豆蔻
Pflanzenr. 46(20): 335. 1904; FHN 4: 99. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 83. 1981; FGD 2: 414. 1991; FOC 24: 339. 2000.
Alpinia katsumada Hayata, Icon. Plan. Formosan. 5: 224. 1915; FPRS 16(2): 91. 1981; FGD 2: 416. 1991.
Alpinia henryi K. Schum., Pflanzenr. 20(IV.46): 335. 1904; FPRS 16(2): 92. 1981; FGD 2: 417. 1991.
Alpinia kainanntensis Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 33: 28. 1943.

Pseudostems to 3 m. Ligule (3–)5–10 mm, abaxially hirsute; petiole absent to 2 cm; leaf blade linear-lanceolate, 20–65 × 2–12 cm, base obliquely attenuate, margin hairy, apex acuminate, with spirally caudate mucro, glabrous or rarely abaxially sparsely hirsute. Racemes erect, 10–30 cm, yellow hirsute; bracts 4–4.5 cm, glabrous; bracteoles milky white, broadly elliptic, 2–3.5 cm, hirsute at base and gradually becoming glabrous toward mucronate apex. Pedicel 2–3 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 cm, split on 1 side, abaxially hairy, apex 2-toothed. Corolla tube 8–10 mm; lobes lanceolate, 2.5–3 cm, margin ciliate. Lateral staminodes subulate, ca. 3 mm. Labellum marked with radiate, purple stripes from centre to margin, triangular-ovate, 3.5–4.5 cm, apex shallowly 2-cleft. Filament ca. 1.5 cm; anther 1.2–1.5 cm. Ovary hirsute, ca. 5 mm in diam. Capsule globose, 2–3 cm in diam., yellow hirsute.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 173; L. T. Lo 24; HK sheet 28026.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore)

Alpinia japonica (Thunb.) Miq. 山薑
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 3: 140. 1867; FRPS 16(2): 102. 1981; FGD 2: 419. 1991; FOC 24: 341. 2000.
Globba japonica Thunb. in Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 73. 1784.

Pseudostems 35–70 cm. Ligule 2-cleft, ca. 2 mm, pubescent; petiole to 2 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, oblanceolate, or narrowly long elliptic, 25–40 × 4–7 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, mucronate, pubescent especially abaxially. Racemes 15–30 cm; rachis densely tomentose; involucral bracts lanceolate, ca. 9 cm, deciduous at anthesis; bracteoles very small, early deciduous. Flowers usually paired on rachis, often also with degenerate flowers; pedicel ca. 2 mm. Calyx clavate, 1–1.2 cm, pubescent, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube ca. 1 cm, sparsely puberulent; lobes oblong, ca. 1 cm, abaxially tomentose, central one hood-like. Lateral staminodes linear, ca. 5 mm. Labellum white marked with red stripes, ovate, ca. 6 mm wide, margin irregularly notched, apex 2-cleft. Stamen 1.2–1.4 cm. Ovary densely tomentose. Capsule salmon red, globose or ellipsoidal, 1–1.5 cm in diam., pubescent, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds ca. 5 × 3 mm, many-angled, with camphor-like odour.

Locality: Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 7093; HK sheet 36003.
Distribution: SE to SW China; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Alpinia oblongifolia Hayata 華山薑
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 215. 1915; FOC 24: 342. 2000.
Alpinia chinensis auct. non (Retz.) Rosc.: FHK 349. 1861; FKH 273. 1912; FHN 4: 96. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 77. 1981.
Alpinia suishaensis Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 9: 123. 1920; R. M. Sm, Edinb. J. Bot. 47(1): 59. 1990.

Pseudostems ca. 1 m. Ligule 4–10 mm, membranous, margin ciliate; petiole ca. 5 mm; leaf blade oblong, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 20–30 × 3–10 cm, glabrous, base rounded or attenuate, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate. Panicles narrow, 15–30 × 2–2.5 cm; branches 3–10 mm, 1–4-flowered; bracteoles 1–3 mm, deciduous. Pedicel to 1 mm. Calyx tubular, 5–7 mm, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube slightly longer than calyx; lobes oblong, 6–7 mm. Lateral staminodes subulate, 1–2 mm. Labellum white with 2 red stripes from base to middle, ovate, 6–8 mm, apex 2-lobed. Filament ca. 5 mm; anther ca. 3 mm. Ovary globose. Capsule red, globose, 5–8 mm in diam. Seeds 5–8.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Chuk Kok. Y. W. Lam 2263; HK sheet 34246, 35852.
Distribution: SW to SE China.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Alpinia officinarum Hance 高良薑
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 6. 1873; FHN 4: 98. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 100. 1981; FGD 2: 418. 1991; FOC 24: 340. 2000.

Rhizomes elongate, terete. Pseudostems 40–110 cm. Leaves sessile; ligule lanceolate, entire, 2–3(–5) cm, membranous; leaf blade linear, 20–30 × 1.2–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex caudate, glabrous. Racemes erect, 6–10 cm; rachis tomentose; bracteoles very small, less than 1 cm. Pedicel 1–2 mm. Calyx 8–10 cm, puberulent, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube slightly shorter than calyx; lobes oblong, ca. 1.5 cm, central one hood-like. Labellum white with red streaks, ovate, ca. 2 cm. Filament ca. 1 cm; anther ca. 6 mm. Ovary tomentose. Capsules red, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Au Mun, Clear Water Bay, Tung Lung Chau. Y. S. Lau 2834; Y. W. Lam 1788; S. C. Ng 2816.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Alpinia sichuanensis Z. Y. Zhu 四川山薑（箭稈風）
Bull. Sichuan School Chin. Mat. Med. 8: 15. 1986; FOC 24: 342. 2000; Z. L. Zhao, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 41(6): 575. 2003.
Alpinia jianganfeng T. L. Wu, Novon 7: 441. 1997; FOC 24: 342. 2000.

Pseudostems to 1 m. Ligule 2-cleft, ca. 2 mm, margin ciliate; petiole absent to 4 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 20–30 × 2–4 (–6) cm, base attenuate, apex narrowly caudate, glabrous except hispid at subapical margin. Spikes erect, 10–20 cm; rachis tomentose; bracteoles very small. Flowers in clusters of 3 on rachis. Calyx cylindrical, abaxially pubescent, apex 3-cleft. Corolla tube subequaling or slightly longer than calyx; lobes oblong, 8–10 mm, abaxially villous. Lateral staminodes linear, ca. 2 mm. Labellum obovate, 0.7–1.3 cm, margin crisped, apex 2-cleft. Stamen longer than labellum; anther ca. 4 mm. Ovary globose, pubescent. Capsule globose, 7–8 mm in diam., pubescent, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds 5–6.

Locality: Sunset Peak. HK sheet 34721, 34722, 36147.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Alpinia stachyodes Hance 密苞山薑
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 126. 1873; FKH 272. 1912; FOC 24: 345. 2000.
Alpinia densibracteata T. L. Wu & Senjen, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(3): 32. 1978; FRPS 16(2): 80. 1981; FGD 2: 413. 1991.

Pseudostems 1–1.5 m. Leaf sheath tomentose; ligule orbicular, 2-cleft, ca. 1 cm, tomentose, margin ciliate; petiole 0.5–2 cm, tomentose; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 20–40 × 4–7 cm, leathery, base attenuate, apex acuminate, with caudate tip ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous except tomentose at margin and apex, or abaxially tomentose especially on median veins. Spikes erect, subsessile, cylindrical, 10–16 cm; involucral bract linear, 8–9 cm × 8–10 mm; bracts ovate or lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 cm, densely imbricate tomentose, 3-flowered, persistent; bracteoles lanceolate, 5–10 mm, tomentose, persistent. Flowers fragrant, tomentose. Calyx tubular, 1–1.5 cm, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube ca. 1.2 cm; lobes oblong, ca. 6 mm, concave. Lateral staminodes linear, ca. 2 mm. Labellum striped at centre, rhomboidal-ovate, obscurely 3-lobed, ca. 7 × 3 mm, margin undulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 94, 451, 667.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forlklore).

Alpinia zerumbet (Pers.) B. L. Burtt & R. M. Sm. 豔山薑
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 31(2): 204. 1972; FHN 4: 96. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 86. 1981; FGD 2: 415. 1991; FOC 24: 336. 2000.
Costus zerumbet Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 3. 1805.
Alpinia speciosa (Wendl.) K. Schum., Pflanzenr. (IV.46): 339. 1904, non Dietr.(1839).
Alpinia nutans auct. non (L.) Rosc.: FHK 348. 1861; FKH 272. 1912.

Pseudostems 2–3 m. Ligule 5–10 mm, abaxially hairy; petiole 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, 30–60 × 5–10 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate with a spiral mucro, glabrous except pubescent at margin.
