Panicles drooping, to 30 cm, enclosed by 2 long sheaths when young; rachis purple-red, velvety; branches very short, 1–2(–3)-flowered; bracteoles enclose flower buds, white with pink apex, elliptic, 3–3.5 cm, glabrous. Pedicel 1–2 cm. Calyx white, subcampanulate, ca. 2 cm, split on 1 side, apex toothed. Corolla tube shorter than calyx; lobes milky white with pink apex, oblong, ca. 3 mm; central lobe larger than lateral ones. Lateral staminodes subulate, ca. 2 mm. Labellum yellow with purple-red stripes, broadly ovate-spatulate, 4–6 cm, crisped. Stamen ca. 2.5 mm. Ovary golden yellow hirsute. Capsule vermilion, globose, ca. 2 cm in diam., ribbed, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds angled.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42838.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: A cultivar (Alpinia zerumbet ‘Variegata’ 花葉豔山薑) is cultivated in Hong Kong for ornamental use. It is characterized by its leaves variegated in feather design with stripes and bands of creamy yellow.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: A cultivar (Alpinia zerumbet ‘Variegata’ 花葉豔山薑) is cultivated in Hong Kong for ornamental use. It is characterized by its leaves variegated in feather design with stripes and bands of creamy yellow.

records.text:
Alstonia scholaris (L. ) R. Br. 糖膠樹（黑板樹）
Asclepiadeae 65. 1810; FRPS 63: 90, pl. 30. 1977; FGD 1: 448, fig. 501. 1987; FOC 16: 155. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 45. 1999.
Echites scholaris L., Mant. Pl. 1: 53. 1767.

Trees to 40 m tall, glabrous with crown pagoda‑like initially, later shallow, flattish and dense. Bark grey; branchlets copiously lenticellate. Leaves in whorls of 3–10; petioles 1–3 cm; leaf blade narrowly obovate to very narrowly spatulate, 7–28 × 2–11cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex usually rounded; lateral veins 25–50 on each side of midvein, at an angle 80–90° to midvein. Cymes dense, pubescent; peduncle 4–7 cm. Pedicels ca. 1 cm. Sepals ovate, 1–1.9 × 1.5–2.3 mm, apex acute to rounded, pubescent. Corolla white; tube 6–10 mm; lobes broadly ovate or broadly obovate, 2–4.5 mm, overlapping to left. Ovary of 2 separate carpels, pubescent. Fruit a pair of follicles, linear, 20–57 cm × 2–5 mm. Seeds oblong, margin ciliate, with tufts of hairs on both ends.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 404; Y. W. Lam 114.
Distribution: SW Guangxi, S Yunnan, cultivated in Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Hunan, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, New Guinea, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug. – Nov.; fruiting: Dec. – Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Alternanthera bettzickiana (Regel) G. Nicholson 錦繡莧（紅草）
Ill. Gard. Dict. 1: 59. 1884; FRPS 25(2): 237. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 395. 1996; FGD 4: 111. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Telanthera bettzickiana Regel, Ind. Sem. Hort. Petrop. 28. 1862, et Gartenflora 11: 178. 1862.

Perennial herb, 20 – 50 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate at base, much branched, young shoots pubescent. Leaves papery; petiole 1– 4 cm; leaf blade rhombic, elliptic to narrowly spatulate, 1– 8 × 0.5 –2.5 cm, apex obtuse or acute, gradually tapering to the base, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces when young, later glabrescent, purplish or green, with white-yellow to red blotches. Flowers in terminal and axillary, sessile heads. Bracts and bracteoles ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm. Perianth-segments 5, unequal, the outer 3 longer, pubescent. Stamens 5; anthers linear oblong. Ovary glabrous, with a short style and capitate stigma.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1557, 2176.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropics; possibly originated from Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Alternanthera dentata (Moench) Stuchl. ex R. E. Fr. f. rubiginosa Suess. 紅龍莧
Repert. Spec. Nov. 35: 299. 1934.
Alternanthera dentata (Moench) Stuchl. ex R. F. Fr. cv. Rubiginosa

Short-lived perennial herb, 30–160 cm tall, all parts dark purple except inflorescence. Stems obtusely quadrangular, ± swollen at nodes, sparsely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 5 –20 mm; leaf blade ovate elliptic to elliptic lanceolate, 3–6 × 1.5–3 cm, base attenuate, apex short-acuminate or acute, margin entire, sparsely strigillose on adaxial surface and on veins of abaxial surface. Flowers in axillary and terminal subglobose heads of 6 –9 mm in diam.; peduncles 3–15 mm; bracts and perianth scarious, white to greenish; stamens usually 5, equaling to the perianth.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens.
Distribution: West Indies to Brazil. Widely cultivated in tropic and subtropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornanmental.

Alternanthera paronychioides A. St.-Hil. 星星蝦鉗菜
Voy. Distr. Diam. 2: 439. 1833; FTW ed. 2, 2: 395. 1996; FGD 4: 112. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.

Annual or perennial herb. Stems tufted, prostrate, 30 –50 cm or longer, young shoots white-pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.5 –1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, ovate or obovate, 1–3 × 0.4 –1 cm, apex obtuse or acute, gradually narrowed to the base, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, sparsely pubescent on abaxial surface. Flowers in axillary, sessile clusters; flower-clusters globose, ovoid, ca. 1 cm in diam. Bracteoles ovate-oblong, ca. 2 mm, white and scarious 1–1.5 mm. Perianth -segments 5, nearly equal, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, scarious, apex acute and mucronate, 3-nerved and sparsely pubescent on the lower part. Stamens 5, very short, with intervening teeth or appendages (staminodes). Utricle obcordate, laterally compressed, ca. 1.5 mm long.

Locality: Mai Po, Tai Shan Wai. Exotic. P. S. Choi 526; Y. W. Lam 736.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong (naturalized). Native to tropical America, widely dispersed over most tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.

Alternanthera philoxeroides (Mart.) Griseb. 空心莧（空心蓮子草）
Abh. Konigl. Ges. Wiss. Gottingen 24: 36. 1879; FRPS 25(2): 236. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 395. 1996; FGD 4: 112. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Bucholzia philoxeroides Mart., Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 13(1): 107. 1825.

Perennial herb. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, 50 –120 cm or longer, obscurely quadrangular, with a line of short hairs in the groove on both sides. Leaves papery; petiole 3 – 5 mm; leaf blade oblong-oblanceolate, to narrowly obovate, 2.5 – 5 × 1–2 cm, apex acute or obtuse, gradually narrowed to the base, margin entire, glabrous or with appressed hairs on adaxial surfaces. Flowers in axillary, peduncled clusters of 1–1.5 cm in diam. Peduncles 1–2(–3) cm, sparsely pubescent. Bracts ovate; bracteoles lanceolate, both about 2 mm, white and scarious. Perianthsegments 5, oblong, 4–5(–6) mm, apex acute, white, scarious and shining. Stamens usually 5, alternating with linear-oblong staminodes. Ovary pyriform.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2719; L. T. Lo 506.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian (naturalized). Native to S
America; naturalized in N America, tropical Asia, and Australia.
Ecology: Wet places on roadsides and cultivated fields or wastelands. Flowering: May– Oct.

Alternanthera pungens Kunth 刺花蓮子草
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 2: 206. 1817; FRPS 25(2): 234. 1979; K. Larsen, Fl. Thailand, 5(4): 403. 1992; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Alternanthera repens (L.) Link, Enum. Hort. Berol. Alt. 1: 154. 1821.
Achyranthes repens L., Sp. Pl. 205. 1753.

Annual herb. Stems prostrate, 20–30 cm or longer, densely white-strigose. Leaves papery; petiole 3 – 5 mm, glabrous or hairy; leaf blade ovate, obovate or oblong-obovate, 1–2.5 × 0.5 –1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex rounded, margin entire, glabrous or sparsely pubescent with appressed hairs on both surfaces. Flowers in axillary, sessile clusters; flower-clusters globose to oblong-ovoid, 0.5–1 cm. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, strongly spinescent. Bracteoles lanceolate, 3– 4 mm, apex acuminate or acute. Perianth-segments 5, the outer 2 navicular, ca. 5 mm, apex pungent, with tuft of hairs near base, middle one oblong-elliptic, 3 –3.5 mm, acute, inner 2 smaller, embracing ovary, with dorsal hair-tuft, scarious. Stamens 5, with intervening teeth (staminodes). Ovary compressed globose; style very short. Utricle compressed ovoid, 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: The New Territories. Exotic. Y. S. Lau 3315.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian (naturalized). Native to Brazil; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May– Oct.

Alternanthera sessilis (L.) DC. 蝦鉗菜（蓮子草）
Cat. Pl. Horti Monsp. 77. 1813; FHK 286. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 409. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 234. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 396, pl. 184, Photo 154. 1996; FGD 4: 111. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Gomphrena sesselis L., Sp. Pl. 225. 1753.
Alternanthera nodiflora R. Brown, Prodr. 1: 417. 1810; FKH 214. 1912; FGD 4: 111. 2000.

Perennial herb. Stems prostrate, 15 – 50 cm or longer, with a line of short hairs on one side. Leaves subsessile; leaf blade variable in shape and size, linear lanceolate, oblong-elliptic to oblong obovate, 1–8 × 0.2–2 cm, apex rounded, obtuse or acute, gradually narrowed to the base, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers in axillary, sessile clusters, surrounded by a few short woolly hairs; flowerclusters initially globose, afterwards elongate and cylindric, to 1–1.5 cm. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, white and scarious 1–1.5 mm. Perianth-segments 5, oblong-lanceolate, 1.5 –2 mm, scarious, apex acute, but not pungent. Stamens 3, very short. Utricle obcordate, laterally compressed, falling with the perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 4547; Y. S. Lau 399; H. C. Tang 2017.
Distribution: A common weed widely distributed throughout tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands and cultivated fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), animal food.

Altingia chinensis (Champ. ex Benth.) Oliv. ex Hance 蕈樹（阿丁楓、山荔枝）
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 103. 1873; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 64,pl. 14. 1979; FGD 1: 158, fig. 174. 1987; FOC 9: 21. 2003.
Liquidambar chinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 164. 1852; FHK 132. 1861.

Tree up to 20 m tall, glabrous except the inflorescences. Stipules caducous; petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade obovate-oblong, 7–13 × 3 – 4.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acute, margin serrate; lateral veins prominent on both surfaces. Male inflorescences ca. 1 cm, usually many arranged in panicles; peduncle pubescent. Female inflorescence solitary or many in panicles, 15–26-flowered; peduncle 2– 4 cm. Male flowers: stamens subsessile; anthers obovoid. Female flowers: calyx connate with ovary, styles 3 –4 mm, pubescent, apex recurved. Infructescences subglobose, 1.7–2.8 cm wide, base truncate, without persistent styles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 206; HK sheet 34771.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung Valley woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung Valley woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Altingia gracilipes Hemsl. 細柄蕈樹
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2837. 1907; FRPS 35(2): 66. 1979; FGD1: 159. 1987; FOC 9: 20. 2003.
Altingia gracilipes var. serrulata Tutch., Rep. Bot. & For. Dept. Hongk. 1914: 31. 1915; FRPS 35(2): 67. 1979; FGD 1: 159. 1979; Check List HK Plants 56. 2002; 25. 2004.
Altingia gracilipes f. uniflora H. T. Chang, Sunyatsenia 7: 74. 1948.

Tree 12–20 m tall; young branches hairy. Stipules absent; petiole slender, 1.3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate, 4.7 × 1.5 –2.5 cm, leathery, base obtuse or narrowly rounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin usually entire or sometimes serrate, abaxially glabrous; lateral veins 5 or 6 pairs. Male inflorescences globose, 0.5– 0.6 cm in diam., usually several arranged in a panicle. Female inflorescences solitary or arranged in raceme, 5 – 6-flowered; peduncle 2–3 cm, pubescent. Male flowers: stamens sessile; anthers red, obovoid, ca. 1.5 mm. Female flowers: styles ca. 2.5 mm, apex recurved. Infructescences obconical, 1.5 –2 cm wide, base cuneate.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung. Y. S. Lau 2634; L. T. Lo 629.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Materials (resin).

Alysicarpus bupleurifolius (L.) DC. 柴胡葉鏈莢豆
Prodr. 2: 352. 1825; FHK 81. 1861; FKH 80. 1912; FRPS 41: 88. 1995; FGD 5: 286. 2003.
Hedysarum bupleurifolium L., Sp. Pl. 745. 1753.

Perennial herb. Stems erect or diffuse, 25 –120 cm tall, many-branched, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves simple, linear to linear-lanceolate, 4–7 × 4 – 5 mm, lower ones shorter, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute, glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent along veins abaxially; lateral veins 10 –13 pairs. Racemes terminal, 3 –18 cm. Flowers 10–20-coupled at nodes of rhachis, lax. Calyx 6 –8 mm, 5-lobed, lobes lanceolate, dry and hard. Corolla slightly shorter than calyx, yellowish or yellow green. Pods 6 – 15 × 1.8 mm, exserted from calyx, segments 3–6, brown, glabrous; persistent calyx much longer than the first segment of pods.

Locality: Tai Hang, Kwai Chung. Y. S. Lau 4, 2019; Y. W. Lam 856.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Polynesia, Mauritius.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Sep. –Nov.

Alysicarpus vaginalis (L.) DC. 鏈莢豆
Prodr. 2: 353. 1825; FHK 80. 1861; FKH 80. 1912; FRPS 41: 85. 1955; FGD 5: 286, fig. 154. 2003.
Alysicarpus vaginalis var. diversifolius Chun, FGZ 334. 1956.

Perennial herb, caespitose or many-branched at base. Stems erect, upper portion prostrate, 30 – 90 cm tall, glabrous or slightly pubescent. Leaves simple, varied in form, upper ones ovate-oblong, oblong-lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 3–6.5 × 1 – 2 cm, lower ones cordate, suborbicular or ovate, 1–3 × 1 cm, glabrous adaxially, slightly pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 4 –5(–9) pairs. Racemes axillary or terminal, 1.5–7 cm, 3 – 6-coupled at nodes of rachis. Calyx 5–6 mm, 5-lobed, lobes longer than calyx-tubes. Corolla violet, slightly exserted from calyx; vexillum broad, obovate. Ovary pubescent. Pods terete, 1.5–2.5 × 0.2–0.25 cm, pubescent; faintly reticulate, segments 4–7, 2.5–3 mm, dehiscent; persistent calyx slightly longer than first segment.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1666; S. P. Lau 183; Y. W. Lam 1264.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Taiwan; tropics of the old world.
Ecology: Gassy and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Green manure.

Alyxia sinensis Champ. ex Benth. 鏈珠藤
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 334. 1852; FHK 219. 1861; FKH 168. 1912; FRPS 63: 65, pl. 22. 1977; FGD 1: 443, fig. 494. 1987; FOC 16: 161. 1995.

Lianas woody, to 3 m, glabrous except for inflorescences. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3; petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade orbicular, elliptic, ovate, or obovate, 1.5–3.5 × 0.8–2 cm, leathery, margin revolute, apex rounded or retuse, lateral veins inconspicuous. Cymes axillary or subterminal, less than 2 cm. Flowers densely crowded, 5–6 cm. Sepals ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, obtuse, pubescent. Corolla reddish to white, constricted at apex, tube 2–3 mm; lobes ovate, ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary villous. Fruit moniliform, stipitate, with 2 or 3 ellipsoidal joints of ca. 10 × 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1976, 2131; HK sheet 40801.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, forest margins; 200 – 500 m. Flowering: Jul. – Oct.; fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Amaranthus blitum L. 凹頭莧
Sp. Pl. 990. 1753; FKH 214. 1912; FOC 5: 421. 2003.
Amaranthus lividus L., Sp. Pl. 990. 1753; FRPS 25(2): 217. 1979; FGD 4: 101. 2000.

Annual herb, 10 –30 cm tall. Stems decumbent or ascending, green or purplish, branched from the base. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate to rhombic-ovate, 1.5– 4.5 × 1–3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex retuse, with a mucro in the sinus, margin entire or obscurely undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers many, greenish, in dense axillary clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal spikes or panicles. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, less than 1 mm. Perianth-segments 3, oblong, 1–1.5 mm; stigmas 2 or 3. Utricles ovoid, 1.5–3 mm, distinctly longer than perianth, smooth or slightly wrinkled.

Locality: Ping Shan. Y. W. Lam 372, 1349.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China, except NW dry regions. A pantropical weed, adventive to warm temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Amaranthus spinosus L. 刺莧
Sp. Pl. 991. 1753; FHK 284. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 404. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 210. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 398, pl. 185, photo 155. 1996; FGD 4: 99. 2000; FOC 5: 419. 2003.

Annual herb, 30 –100 cm tall. Stems erect, green or purplish. Leaves alternate, armed with 1 or 2 straight spines in each axil; petioles 1– 8 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3 –12 × 1– 5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, aristate, margin entire, glabrous or sparsely puberulent on veins when young. Flowers many, greenish, in dense axillary clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal spikes, either simple or paniculately branched. Female flowers always on the lower part of the spikes. Bracts and bracteoles ovate triangular, ca. 5 mm. Perianth-segments 5, oblong, ca. 1.5 mm. Stigmas 2–3. Utricles oblong, 1–1.2 mm, opening transversely.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. L. Gibbs 7752; Y. S. Lau 2166, 3084.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian. A common weed of the tropics, subtropics and warm temperate regions; probably originated from neotropics.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides and cultivated fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Amaranthus tricolor L. 莧菜
Sp. Pl. 989. 1753; FHN 1: 404. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 212. 1979; FGD 4: 100. 2000; FOC 5: 420. 2003.

Annual herb, 30–150 cm tall. Stems erect, green or purplish, glabrous or puberulous when young. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate to rhombic-ovate or ovate-triangular, 4 –10 × 2–7 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate with mucro at the tip, margin entire or obscurely undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers many, greenish, in dense axillary clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal spikes or panicles. Male and female flowers mixed on the rachis. Bracts and bracteoles ovate-lanceolate, 2.5 –3 mm, aristate. Perianth-segments 3, oblong, 3– 5 mm. Stigmas 3. Utricles oblong-ovoid, 2–2.5 mm, opening transversely.

Locality: Cultivated. S. T. Dunn 9313; Y. S. Lau 3128.
Distribution: Widely cultivated and naturalized in tropics, probably originated from tropical Asia.
Ecology: Sometimes escaped from cultivation, in wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable), ornamental.

Amaranthus viridis L. 綠莧（野莧）
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1405. 1763; FHK 284. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 405, fig. 216. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 216, pl. 47: 5 – 8. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 400, pl. 186. 1996; FGD 4: 100. 2000; FOC 5: 420. 2003.

Annual herb, 20–60 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, green or purplish, branched on the upper part. Leaves alternate; petioles 3– 6 cm; leaf blade ovate to rhombic-ovate, 3 –9 × 2.5 – 6 cm, base broadly cuneate or subtruncate, apex obtuse or emarginate, margin entire or obscurely undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers many, greenish, in dense clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal panicles. Bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, less than 1 mm. Perianth-segments 3(– 4), oblong, ca. 1.5 mm. Stigmas 3. Utricles subglobose, 1–1.5 mm, not or slightly longer than perianth, strongly wrinkled, indehiscent or bursts irregularly.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2148; Y. W. Lam 951.
Distribution: A pantropical weed, adventive to warm temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Abroma augusta (L.) L. f. 昂天蓮
Suppl. Pl. 341, 1781; FHN 2: 85. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 181. 1984; FGD 1: 148. 1987.
Theobroma angusta L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 12) 233. 1767.
Abroma fastuosa Jacq., Hort. Vind. 3: 3, t. 1. 1776; FKH 50. 1912.

Shrub, 1– 4 m tall. Branchlets densely stellate-tomentose. Petioles 1–10 cm; leaves cordate or ovate-cordate, occasionally slightly 3– 5-lobed, 10 –22 × 9 –18 cm, base cordate or obliquely cordate, apex acute or acuminate, sparsely stellate pubescent adaxially, densely tomentose abaxially. Cymes 1– 5-flowered. Flowers purple; sepals lanceolate, 15 –18 mm; petals 2– 5 cm; ovary oblong, ca. 1–5 mm. Capsules membranous, obconic, 3–6 in diam., apex truncate, stellate-hairy, 5-winged, margin long tomentose. Seeds black, ellipsoid, ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Cultivated, though not common nowadays. HK sheet 543, 544, 3732.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou; India, Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring to summer.

Amentotaxus argotaenia (Hance) Pilg. 穗花杉
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 54: 41. 1916; FRPS 7: 455, pl. 104: 4–7. 1978; FFrev. ed. 1: 321, fig. 298. 1991; FOC 4: 92. 1999; FGD 4: 42. 2000.
Podocarpus argotaenia Hance, Journ. Bot. 21: 357. 1883;FKH 256. 1913.

Shrub or small tree to 7 m; bark greyish brown or pale reddish brown. Leafy branchlets ascending or suberect. Leaves subsessile or with a petiole up to 3 mm, dark green adaxially, linear or linearlanceolate, falcate or straight, 2–11 cm × 5–11 mm, leathery, base cuneate to attenuate, asymmetric, margin flat or very narrowly revolute, apex dark, callose, rounded to sharply triangular, abaxial surface with two 1–2 mm wide stomatal bands. Pollen-cone racemes borne (1 or)2– 4(–10) together, 1.5–6.5 cm; cones in ca. 12 pairs, ovoid, ca. 3.5 × 2.5 –3.2 mm; bracts ca. 6 at base of otherwise naked peduncle, distal bract ca. 2.5 × 2 mm, keeled; microsporophylls 6–8, peltate, each with (2 or)3(–5) pollen sacs. Seed-bearing structures with peduncle to ca. 2/3 length of subtending leaf. Aril bright red when ripe. Seed finally red, narrowly obovoid-ellipsoid, 1.9 –2.6 × 1–1.3 cm, with small, mucronulate apex; peduncle 1.1–1.4 cm, compressed-quadrangular, dilated below bracts, naked.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 165, 206.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Xizang, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu;Vietnam.
Ecology: In forests. Pollinating: Apr.; seed maturing: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Note: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Note: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Amischotolype hispida (Less. & A. Rich.) D. Y. Hong 穿鞘花
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 461. 1974; FHN 4: 80, fig. 997. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 71, pl. 19: 1–3. 1997; FOC 24: 23. 2000; FGD 6: 314, fig. 178. 2005.
Forrestia hispida Less. & A. Rich., Voy. Astrolabe 2: t. 1. 1834.
Forrestia chinensis N. E. Br., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 158. 1903; FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb, up to 1 m tall; stems erect, creeping at the base, glabrous. Leaves borne on the upper part of stem; leaf sheaths to 4 cm, densely brownish yellow hirsute; leaf blade elliptic, 15–50 × 5–10.5 cm, base long-attenuate into a winged petiole, apex acuminate, brownish yellow hirsute near margin on both surfaces and below middle of abaxial major veins. Heads 2–3 cm in diam., with 20 or more flowers. Sepals green, obovate, 5–13 mm, abaxially densely brown hirsute along midvein, rarely subglabrous, elsewhere glabrous or very sparsely hairy. Petals white, lanceolate, 4–10 mm, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens 6, ca. 12 mm; filaments bearded. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, ca. 7 mm, much shorter than persistent sepals, sparsely hirsutulous near obtuse apex. Seeds ca. 3 × 2 mm, rugose.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Kap Lung, Mau Ping. Y. S. Lau 3023; Y. W. Lam 979.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Streamsides, forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Ammannia arenaria Kunth 耳基水莧
Nov. Gen. Sp. (4th ed.) 6: 190. 1824; FRPS 52 (2): 70. 1983.
Ammannia senegalensis auct. non Lam.: DC., Prodr. 3: 77. 1828; FKH 109. 1912, p.p.

Erect herb, 15–55 cm tall. Stems 4-angled, few-branched. Leaves opposite, membranous, narrowly lanceolate or narrowly oblong, 2–7 × 0.3–1.5 cm, base cordate-auriculate, apex acuminate, semiamplexicaul. Cymes axillary. Peduncles 2–5 mm. Bracts 1.5 mm; bracteoles scale-like. Calyx campanulate, angled, teeth 4, broadly deltoid. Petals 4, red, suborbicular, slightly longer than calyx-tooth, caducous or absent. Stamens 4. Capsules purple-red, oblate, 2.5–3 mm in diam., irregularly circumscissile. Seeds subdeltoid, 0.5 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin Tau Tsuen, Peng Shan Ha Chuen, Peng Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2380; Y. W. Lam 1000, 1350; K. Y. Tam s. n. (HK sheet 39334).
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shaanxi, Gansu, Yunnan; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Wet places and paddy field. Flowering: Dec.–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.

Ammannia baccifera L. 水莧菜（細葉水莧）
Sp. Pl. 120. 1753; FRPS 52(2): 69. 1983; FKH 109. 1912; FGD 3: 75, fig. 51. 1995.

Annual herb, 10 – 15 cm tall. Stems erect, many-branched, slightly 4-angled and narrowly winged. Leaves opposite on lower part of stem, ± alternate on upper part of stem, subsessile; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 6–15 × 3–5 mm on lateral branchlet, up to 7 cm on upper part of stem, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse. Cymes or flower fascicles axillary; pedicles 1.5 mm. Flowers minute, 1 mm, green or purplish. Calyx 4-toothed, teeth deltoid, appendages folded or dentate. Petals absent. Stamens 4. Capsules purple, globular, 1.2 – 1.5 mm in diam., upper part irregularly circumscissile. Seeds black, minute, subdeltoid.

Locality: Lamma Island. E. M. Gibbs 5155.
Distribution: E, C, S & SW China; Vietnam, India, Philippines, Malaysia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Paddy field or wet places. Flowering: Aug. – Oct.; fruiting: Sep.– Dec.

Ammannia multiflora Roxb. 多花水莧
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 447. 1820; FRPS 52(2): 69. 1983; FGD 3: 76. 1995.
Ammannia senegalensis auct. non Lam.: DC., Prodr. 3: 77. 1828; FKH 109. 1912, p.p.

Erect herbs, 8–40 cm tall. Stems many-branched, 4-angled. Leaves opposite, subsessile; leaf blade linear or narrowly lanceolate, 8–25 × 2–8 mm, base cuneate (leaves on lower part of stem), or auriculate to subrounded (leaves on upper part of stem), apex acuminate. Flowers minute, in lax, dichotomous cymes. Peduncles 2–3 mm; bracteoles 2; pedicels 1–1.5 mm. Calyx-tube angulate, teeth 4, shorter than tube. Petals 4, obovate, caducous. Stamens 4, rarely 6–8. Capsules deeply red, oblate, 1.5–2 mm in diam., upper half exserted from calyx. Seeds black brown, minute, triangular.

Locality: So Kon Po. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 1922).
Distribution: Widely distributed in S China; Asia, Europe, Africa, Australia
Ecology: Swamp. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Sep.

Amorphophallus dunnii Tutcher 南蛇棒（鄧氏蒟蒻）
Journ. Bot. 49: 273. 1911; FKH 288. 1912; FHN 4: 138, fig. 1044. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 92, pl. 16: 5 – 9. 1979; FYN 2: 790. 1979; W. Hett. & Vander Ham, Blumea 46: 281. 2001; FGD 9: 196. 2009; FOC 23: 26. 2010.
Amorphophallus odoratus W. Hett. & H. Li, Blumea 39: 265. 1994.

Perennial herb; tuber subglobose or depressed-globose. Leaf solitary; petiole 30–90 cm, 1 cm in diam., with many, elongate, confluent, pale green or brownish green spots; leaf blade green, dissected; leaflets lanceolate or oblanceolate, 7–14 × 8 cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate. Inflorescence solitary. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle 20–60 cm; spathe broadly ovate to elliptic, 12–26 × 14 cm, strongly concave, top acute, overarching the spadix, base shortly convolute, externally bright pale green, basally with rounded white spots; spadix slightly shorter than spathe, stipitate or subsessile, 8–20 cm; female portion cylindrical, yellowish, 1.5–3 cm, base narrow; male portion 1.5–4.5 cm, appendage conical, ovate, greenish white, 4.5–14 cm, narrowing above middle, apex obtuse. Ovary obovate, 1–2.5 mm. Berries blue, cylindrical; seed solitary, black.

Locality: Mount Parker, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. HK sheet 7729, 29714.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by S. T. Dunn and W. J. Tutcher from Lantau Island and Mount Parker in between 1909 and 1911 respectively. The type specimen of A. odoratus was collected by Simmons from Tai Mo Shan in 1994.

Amorphophallus kiusianus (Makino) Makino 東亞魔芋
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 27: 244. 1913; Hett. & Peng, Bot. Acad. Sin. 36. 105, f. 4. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 671. 2000; FGD 9: 195. 2009; FOC 23: 29. 2010.
Amorphophallus konjac K. Koch ex Matsum. & Hayata var. kiusiana Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 25: 16. 1911.
Amorphophallus variabilis auct. non Blume: FHK. 343. 1861; FKH 288. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 95. 1979; Check List HK Plants 298. 2002; 105. 2004.

Perennial herb; tuber depressed-globose. Leaves trisected, lobes lanceolate or oblong-elliptic, 6–20 × 3–4.5 cm; petiole glabrous, 80 cm, with grey or pale green spots. Peduncle 120 cm; spathe triangular, 9–25 × 4–13 cm, base and blade constricted, blade margins inrolled or wavy, pink-green or purple-brown externally, with small white spots; spadix sessile or subsessile, 9–22 cm, female portion conical, 1–4 cm, male portion cylindrical or slightly obconical, 2.5–4.5 cm, appendage fusiform-conical or long cylindrical, 4–16 cm, abruptly acute or obtuse. Ovary obovoid. Berries rounded or ovoid.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 29717, 29718.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Jul.

Ampelopsis cantoniensis (Hook. & Arn.) Planch. 廣東蛇葡萄
Monogr. Phan. 5: 460. 1887; FGZ 422. 1956; FRPS 48(2): 49. 1998.
Cissus cantoniensis Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 175. 1833, p. p.
Ampelopsis cantoniensis K. Koch var. lecoides (Maxim.) F. Y. Lu, FTW 3: 667. 1977.
Ampelopsis leeoides (Maxim.) Planch., Monogr. Phan. 5: 462. 1887.
Vitis cantoniensis auct. non Seem.: FHK 54. 1861; FKH 65. 1912.

Branchlets terete, with longitudinal ridges, ± pubescent when young; tendrils bifurcate, to 12 cm. Leaves bipinnate, or pinnate on upper branches, basal pinnae of bipinnate leaves usually trifoliolate; petiole 2–8 cm, central petiolule 1–3 cm, lateral petiolules 0–2.5 cm, sparsely pubescent when young, glabrescent; leaflets ovate, ovate-elliptic, or oblong, 3–11 × 1.5–6 cm, base truncate, apex acute, acuminate, or cuspidate, abaxially glaucous, sparsely pubescent on veins, glabrescent. Inflorescence corymbose, terminal or leaf-opposed; rachis pubescent; peduncle 2–4 cm, ± sparsely pubescent. Pedicels 1–3 mm, nearly glabrous. Calyx glabrous. Petals ovate-elliptic, 1.7–2.7 mm, glabrous. Anthers ovoid-elliptic. Ovary at the lower part adnate to disk. Berry globose, 6–8 mm in diam., 2–4-seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1286; HK sheet 39082, 40120.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Laos, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests of valleys and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Notes: According to FRPS, the type specimen was collected from Hong Kong. But in the protologue, the authors didn’t mention any specimen from Hong Kong.

Ampelopsis heterophylla (Thunb.) Siebold & Zucc. var. kulingensis (Rehd.) C. L. Li 牯嶺蛇葡萄
Chin. J. Appl. Envirn. Biol. 2(1): 48. 1996; FRPS 48(2): 38. 1998.
Ampelopsis brevipedunculata (Maxim.) Trautv. var. kulingensis Rehd., Gent. Herb. 1: 36. 1920; FFJ 4: 379. 1987.
Vitis heterophylla auct. non Thunb.: Benth., FHK 53. 1861.

Plant pubescent to nearly glabrous. Branchlets terete, with longitudinal ridges; tendrils 2- or 3-branched. Leaves simple; petiole 2–10 cm; leaf blade papery, conspicuously 5-angled, 5–16 × 4–16 cm, base cordate, rarely truncate, notches nearly obtuse, rarely rounded, 3-lobed at upper part; lobes caudate at apex, margin with acute teeth, abaxially pale green. Peduncle 2.5–3 cm. Pedicels 1–3 mm. Petals ovate-elliptic, 0.8–1.8 mm. Anthers narrowly elliptic. Ovary at the lower part adnate to disk; style slightly enlarged at base. Berry 5–8 mm in diam., reddish blue, 2–4-seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 947, 1008, 1084.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Ampelopsis brevipedunculata Koehne previously (Check List HK Plants 51. 1993).

Anagallis arvensis L. 琉璃繁縷
Sp. Pl. 148. 1753; FKH 157. 1912; FRPS 59(1): 136, pl. 36: 1– 4. 1989; FOC 15: 79. 1996.

Annual or biennial glabrous herb, 10 –30 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, erect or ascendent from the decumbent base. Leaves decussate, sessile; leaf blade ovate to narrowly ovate, 7–18(–25) × 3–12(–15) mm, base subrounded, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves. Pedicels slender, 2–3 cm, recurved in fruiting. Calyx 3.5–6 mm, divided nearly to the base; lobes linear lanceolate, margin membranous. Corolla rotate, reddish, divided nearly to base; lobes obovate, 4–6 × 2.7–3 mm. Stamens included; filaments puberulous. Capsule globose, ca. 3.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 4335.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; temperate Asia, Indian Subcontinent, Europe, N Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated areas, wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

Ananas comosus (L.) Merr. 鳳梨
Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 133. 1917; FHN 4: 86. 1977; FOC 24: 18. 2000.
Bromelia comosa L., Stickm. Herb. Amb. 21, 1754.

Perennial herb, with a simple, short stem, usually with suckers arising from the the base. Leaves closely and spirally arranged in a rosette, leaf blade sword-shaped, margin coarsely and laxly spinose-serrate. Inflorescence strobiliform, many-flowered, with a tuft of sterile leafy bracts at apex; floral bracts inconspicuous, margin serrulate or entire. Flowers many. Sepals free, slightly asymmetric, apex obtuse. Petals violet or reddish, free but connivent and tube-like. Stamens included. Syncarp globose, ovoid, or elongate, 15 cm or longer at maturity, becoming fleshy and fragrant. Seeds absent or very rare.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions; native to tropical America.
Uses: Fruit.

Andrographis paniculata (Burm. f.) Nees 穿心蓮
Pl. As. Rar. 3: 116. 1832; FHN 3: 556. 1974; FRPS. 70: 207. 2002.
Justicia paniculata Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 9. 1768.

Annual herbs up to 30–50 cm tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, glabrous. Petioles 0.3–1 cm; leaf blades papery, ovate‑lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 1.5–7 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, adaxially green, abaxially pale green, lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Panicle axillary or terminal, 5–9 cm; rachis subglabrous. Pedicels 2–8 mm long, sparsely pubescent. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm; bracteoles linear, 2–2.5 mm. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear, 2.5–3 mm, abaxially glabrous or glandular‑pilose. Corolla white, ca. 1.5 cm, outside pilose; tube‑base cylindric ca. 0.8 cm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip ca. 0.6 cm, reflexed, 2‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 1 × 1 mm, lower lips with purple dots, ca. 0.7 cm, erect, 3‑lobed, lobes lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments pubescent; anther 2‑thecous; anther‑thecae 2, unequal, the larger one hairy at base. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; style 6–9 mm, sparsely pilose towards base. Capsule narrowly cylindric, ca. 1.5 cm, glabous or sparsely glandular‑pubescent, many‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 × 1.5 mm, glabrous, rugose.

Locality: Hung Mui Kuk, Castle Peak, Man Uk Pin, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 399, 2044; Y. S. Lau 816, 2569.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; SE Asia.
Ecology: Cultivated and naturalized, roadsides, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Feb. Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Andropogon chinensis (Nees) Merr. 華鬚芒草
Philipp. J. Sci. 12: 101. 1917; FHN 4: 478, fig. 1264. 1977; FFJ 6: 274, fig. 248. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 185, pl. 45: 1–15. 1997; FOC 22: 623. 2006; FGD 9: 497, fig. 263. 2009.
Homoeatherum chinense Nees, Nat. Syst. Bot., 448. 1836.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 40–100 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear, flat or involute when dry, 8–25 × 0.2–0.3 cm; ligule 1–2.5 mm, membranous, obtuse. Racemes paired, 1.5–3(–5) cm, exserted from spatheole; spatheoles boat-shaped or linear; peduncle puberulous; rachis internodes subequal to pedicels, cuneate, the lower with 1–3 mm hairs, tips cupular, obliquely toothed. Sessile spikelet linear, ca. 5 mm, callus acute and pungent; lower glume deeply concave between dorsal keels, glabrous, shortly awned, mucronate or 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, 2-lobed, with an awn from the sinus; awn 6–10 mm; lower lemma linear-oblong, hyaline membranous; upper lemma 2-lobed, an awn from the sinus; awn 2–3 cm; palea 1/2 length of lower glume, margins ciliate; lodicules 2; stamens 3; style free, glumose. Pedicellate spikelet oblong-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, 2-awned; awn of lower glume 4–10 mm, awn of upper glume much shorter.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak. S. C. Ng 1521.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Africa, SW Asia (Yemen).
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Anethum graveolens L. 蒔蘿

Sp. Pl. 1: 263. 1753; FRPS 55(2): 215, pl. 87: 1 – 4. 1985; FGD 2: 342, fig. 231. 1991; FOC 14: 134. 2005.

Peucedanum graveolens (L.) Hiern, Botany [Fortieth Parallel] 5: 129. 1871.

Ferula marathrophylla Walp., Nov. Act. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 347. 1843; FKH 117. 1912.


Annual herb, 30–75(–100) cm tall, glabrous, strongly aromatic. Petioles 5–6 cm, sheathing at base and scarious-margined; leaf blade broadly ovate in outline, 3–4-pinnately divided; ultimate segments filiform, 4–20 × ca. 0.5 mm; upper stem leaves smaller and less divided. Umbels terminal, 5–15 cm across; peduncle 3–14 cm; rays 10–25, 3–5 cm; umbellules 15–25-flowered; pedicels 6–10 mm. Fruit brown, 3–5 × 2–2.5 mm; lateral ribs grey-white, narrowly winged.


Locality: New Territories (cultivated).

Distribution: Native to the Mediterranean region, widely cultivated and adventive worldwide.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore), spice.

Angelica decursiva (Miq.) Franch. & Sav. 紫花前胡
Enum. Pl. Jap. 1: 187. 1875; FRPS 55(3): 28. 1992; FOC 14: 164. 2005.
Porphyroscias decursiva Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavi 3: 62. 1867.
Peucedanum decursivum (Miq.) Maxim., Mel. Biol. 12: 472. 1886; FKH 118. 1912; FGD 2: 344, fig. 233. 1991.

Perennial herb, 1–2 m high. Taproot conic, 1–2 cm thick, strongly aromatic. Stems often purplish, ribbed, glabrous. Petioles 10–35 cm, sheaths purple, elliptic. Leaf blades triangular to ovate in outline, 10–25 cm, 1–2-ternate-pinnate; rachis winged; pinnae 3–5, again 3–5-lobed; ultimate lobes ovate or oblong-lanceolate, 5–12.5 × 2.5–6 cm, apex acute, margin cuspidate-serrate, midveins often purple-green, hispidulous along veins adaxially; upper stem leaf reduced into an inflated petiole-sheath. Peduncles 2–8 cm, pubescent; involucral bracts 1–3, purplish, ovate, sheath-like, reflexed; rays 7–14(–22), 2–4 cm, pubescent; bracteoles 3–8, linear to lanceolate, green or purple; pedicels pubescent. Calyx-teeth triangular-subulate. Petals dark purple, obovate or ellipsoidal-lanceolate, apex incurved but not notched. Fruit oblong to ovoid-orbicular, 4–7 × 3–5 mm; dorsal ribs filiform, acute, lateral ribs thicky narrow-winged; vittae 1–3 in each furrow, 4–6 on commissure.

Locality: Hong Kong Botanical Gardens. HK sheet 12630, 12631.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Taiwan, Liaoning; Japan, Korea, Russia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ania hongkongensis (Rolfe) T. Tang & F. T. Wang 香港安蘭（香港帶唇蘭）
Acta Phytotax. 1: 46. 88. 1951; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25: 48. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 68, fig. 34. 1977.
Tainia hongkongensis Rolfe, Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 195. 1896; FKH 264. 1912; FRPS 18: 240. 1999; FGD 7: 406. 2006; FOC 25: 282. 2009; Check List HK Plants 383. 2002; 133. 2004.
Ania angustifolia auct. non Lindl.: FHK 356. 1861.

Terrestrial herb, pseudobulbs ovoid, sheathing when young, bearing a terminal leaf. Leaves petiolate; petioles slender, 13–16 × 0.2–0.3 cm, base covered with a 6 cm tube-like sheath; leaf blades oblong-elliptic, 26 × 3–4 cm, base attenuate into petioles, apex acuminate. Flowers yellowish green with purplish brown spots or veins; sepals subequal, oblong-lanceolate, 20 × 2.2–3.5 mm, apex acuminate; lateral sepals connate to the column base; petals obovate-lanceolate, similar size with sepals, apex acuminate, base attenuate; lip white with yellowish green veins, obovate, apiculate at apex, base spurred, the two sides near base ± covering the column, disk with 3 narrow ridges; column white with light purple, slightly enlarged at apex; anther obovoid, truncate at the base; pollinia 8 in 2 groups.

Locality: Stubb Rd., Repulse Bay, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Wong Lung Hang. S. Y. Hu 9853, 13219 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2129.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Among loose rocks or under trees from hillsides. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wilford from Mount Parker in 1858.

Ania ruybarrettoi S. Y. Hu & Barretto 南方安蘭（南方帶唇蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 25 fig. 12. 1976.
Tainia ruybarrettoi (S. Y. Hu & Barretto) Aver., Opred. Orkhid. V’etnama. 403. 1994; FOC 25: 283. 2009.
Tainia ruybarrettoi (S. Y. Hu & Barretto) Z. H. Tsi, FRPS 18: 243. 1999; FGD 7: 406. 2006; Check List HK Plants 383. 2002; 133. 2004.

Terrestrial herb; rhizome horizontal, the terminal internode enlarging into a pseudobulb; pseudobulbs crowded together or very closely spaced, ovoid and smooth when young, grooved and winkled when old, dull green or purple in colour at anthesis bearing 2 cataphylls and a terminal leaf. Leaves solitary, dark green, slightly grooved at apex, petiolate; petioles 15 – 25 cm, oriented at the apex of the pseudobulb; leaf blades lanceolate, 30–45 × 4.5–5.3 cm, conspicuously veined with 9 longitudinal veins, prominently elevated beneath. Flowers 5 – 28, well-spaced; sepals and petals similar in size and colour, palmately arranged in one plane, 2.7–3.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, purplish yellow with 3– 5 purple longitudinal veins running from the base to apex, margin yellow; odd sepal dorsal, linear-lanceolate, lateral ones slightly falcate; petals oblique-oblanceolate; lip 3-lobed, spurred, bent, crescent-shaped, the sides erect, covering almost the entire column, extending forward into a distinct rounded lobe at the apex, streaked and dotted bright purple, the inner surface marked with lines of bright purple hairs, the midlobe ovate, slightly curved downwards, margin wavy, apex acute, pale lavender flushed yellow, darker purple beneath, disk longitudinally 5-ridged, becoming 5-crested at the throat; spur orange-yellow, rounded and smooth at apex; column back white, the front streaked purple, truncate, slightly arcuate; anther hanging, ovoid, creamy yellow; pollina 8 in 4 pairs.

Locality: Sai Kung, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok. S. Y. Hu 13098 (CUHK); HK sheet 30331, 30431.
Distribution: Guangxi.
Ecology: Bamboo forests. Flowering: Mar.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13098A, K, holotype; PE, isotype) was collected by Ruy Barretto from Pat Sin Leng in 1968. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Anisomeles indica (L.) Kuntze 廣防風
Rev. Gen. Pl. 512. 1891; H. Keng, Garden's Bull. Sing. 24: 34. 1969; FOC 17: 188. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 445, pl. 189. 1998.
Anisomeles ovata R. Br., Hort. Kew. ed. 2, 3: 364. 1811; FHK 278. 1861; FKH 211. 1912.
Epimeredi indica (L.) Rothm., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. Beih., 53: 12. 1944; FRPS 66: 42, pl. 6. 1977; FGD 3: 429. 1995.

Robust herbs, or sometimes shrubby, 0.5–2 m tall; stems erect, 4‑angled, sparingly hairy to densely pubescent. Leaves simple; petioles 1.5–4 cm, tomentose; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 4–9 × 2.5–6.5 cm, base rounded to truncate, subcordate, less often shortly cuneate, entire, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate‑dentate, hirsute or woolly on both surfaces. Verticillasters forming interrupted or dense spikes; bracts linear, 3–4 mm, pilose. Calyx campanulate, 5–7 mm, lengthening to 10 mm in fruit, shortly pedicellate, hirsute and pilose; teeth triangular‑lanceolate, subequal, ciliate. Corolla purplish, ca. 1.3 mm, glabrous abaxially. Filaments hirsute. Nutlets broadly ovoid, 1.8–2 × 1.4–1.5 mm, ± compressed.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kau Wa Keng, Tai Po, Tin Fu Tsai, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3126; S. P. Choi 160; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. Butt 24037.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages, margins of forests. Flowering: Jun. – Nov.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Anisopappus chinensis (L.) Hook. & Arn. 山黃菊
Bot. Beech. Voy. 196. 1836; FHK 180. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 116. 1965; FRPS 75: 317. 1979; FGD 8: 151, fig. 84. 2007.
Verbesina chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 901. 1753.

Annual herbs; stem erect, 25–110 cm tall, striate, glandular, pubescent with hair multicellular, lower portion less hairy or subglabrous, base woody. Leaves on lower part withered at anthesis; those on middle part lanceolate to lanceolate‑oblong, 3–5 × 0.7–2 cm, both surfaces pubescent and glandular, denser beneath, base broadly cuneate or truncate, apex obtuse‑rounded, margin irregularly dentate with the teeth obtuse, trinerved or triplinerved, with reticulate veinlets, prominent on lower leaf surfaces; petiole 0.5–2.5 cm. Upper leaves smaller in size and shorter‑petiolate. Capitula terminal to main stem or branches, several arranged as loose corymbs; peduncle 4–7 cm, densely pubescent. Involucres hemispherical, 6–9 mm; phyllaries 3‑seriate, lanceolate to linear‑oblong, 3–6 mm with outer ones shorter, densely pubescent and glandular on abaxial surfaces. Receptacle slightly convex, the center of areoles elevated; palea carinate, about 5 mm, enveloped the cypselae of disk florets, deciduous. Marginal ligulate florets female, corolla yellow, 6 mm, apex truncate and 3‑toothed, glandular. Disk tubular florets bisexual, corolla tubular‑campanulate, 3–3.5 mm, apex 5 ovate and glandular lobes. Cypselae subcylindric, loosely puberulent, truncate apically, narrowed at base; those of ligulate florets 2 mm, about 10‑striate‑costate; the disk ones 2.5 mm, 4–5‑angulate. Pappus scarious, coroniform and 2–3 mm together with 4–5 bristles of 0.5–1 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 383; S. Y. Hu 12405 (CUHK); N. H. Li 245 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.

Anneslea fragrans Wall. var. hainanensis Kobuski 海南茶梨
J. Arnold Arbor. 33: 86. 1952; FHN 1: 503. 1964; FGD 2: 176. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 180. 1998.
Anneslea hainanensis (Kobuski) Hu, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 265. 1963.

Evergreen tree, up to 15 m tall. Leaves leathery; petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blade oblong to elliptic, 7–15 × 3–7 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or rarely rounded, margin entire or sparsely serrate towards apex. Flowers in axillary clusters; pedicels 1–2 cm; bracteoles 2, broadly ovate to triangular-ovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm, margin sparsely glandular; sepals reddish, broadly ovate, 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, base slightly connate, apex rounded to obtuse, margin glandular; petals red or white, broadly ovate, 6 – 8 mm, connate at base; stamens ca. 40, ca. 1.5 mm; filaments connate at base; anthers linear, glabrous, connective prolonged; ovary half-inferior, 3-locular, glabrous; styles ca. 1.5 mm, 3-lobed. Fruit ovoid, 2–2.5 cm, 2–3-locular with 2–3 seeds per locule, indehiscent, wrapped by persistent enlarged sepals; carpopodium 2–4 cm. Seeds long obovate, 7–10 × 5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 218; F. W. Xing 6893; P. S. So 4.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.
Uses: Materials (timber).

Annona squamosa L. 番荔枝
Sp. Pl. 1: 537. 1753; FGZ 84, fig. 24. 1956; FHN 1: 258. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 171, pl. 79. 1979; FGD 2: 39. 1991; FYN 5:61, fig. 18: 1 –8. 1991.

Small trees, to 4 m. Young branches pubescent. Petioles 9– 15 × ca. 1.5 mm. Leaf blades 9– 13.5 × 4 – 5 cm, oblong or ellipticoblong, glabrous or slightly pubescent both sides, base cuneate, apex obtuse or subacute; midvein impressed adaxially; secondary veins 6 – 8 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or terminal, 1–2(–4)-flowered. Flowers greenish (to yellow); pedicel 17.5–20.5 × ca. 0.8 mm, glabrous; bracts adnate to base or middle of pedicel. Sepals broadly ovate. Outer petals ca. 18 × 5 mm, narrowly oblong, reddish towards base adaxially; inner petals rudimentary, ca. 2 × 2.3 mm, triangular. Stamens numerous, ca. 1 mm long; connective capitate. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary glabrous; stigma glabrous. Fruits 8–10 cm in diam. when mature, ovate or globose, tuberculate, glaucous, pulp creamy-yellow, soft. Seeds blackish, shiny.

Locality: Hong Kong Zoological & Botanical Gardens, The University of Hong Kong Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Kei Ling Ha Hoi, Sai Kung (cultivated). C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/06 (HKU); HK sheet 1027.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated). Widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Anodendron affine (Hook. & Arn.) Druce 鱔藤
Rep. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 4(Suppl. 2): 605. 1917; FRPS 63: 175, pl. 59. 1977; FGD 1: 464, fig. 519. 1987; FOC 16: 182. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 128. 1999.
Holarrhena affinis Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 198. 1837.
Aganosma laevis Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 335. 1853; FHK 221. 1861.
Anodendron laeve (Champ.) Maxim. ex Franch. & Sav., Enum. Pl. Jap. 1(2): 315. 1875; Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 169. 1912.
Anodendron fangchengense Tsiang & P. T. Li, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 11: 378, pl. 48. 1973; FRPS 63: 176. 1977.
Anodendron salicifolium Tsiang & P. T. Li, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 11: 379. 1973; FRPS 63: 177, pl. 60. 1977.

Lianas to 10 m or longer, glabrous except for corolla. Branches pale grey. Petioles 0.5–2 cm; leaf blade narrowly oblong to narrowly ovate, 3–14 × 1.2–5 cm, papery or somewhat leathery, deep green adaxially, lighter abaxially; lateral veins 6–12 on each side of midvein, usually wrinkled in dry state. Cymes paniculate, terminal or axiallary, 3–26 × 3–13 cm, long‑pedunculate. Sepals ovate, 2–3 mm. Corolla white or yellowish green, pilose inside, tube 3 – 4.5 mm; lobes falcate, narrowly oblong, as long as or shorter than the tube. Stamens inserted at base of corolla‑tube; disk cup‑shaped, shallowly 5‑lobed or entire, attached to ovaries. Follicles narrowly ellipsoidal, dilated at base, 8–13 × 1.6–3 cm. Seed tawny, beaked, ca. 2 cm × 6 m, coma ca. 6 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2104; P. S. Choi 428; Y. W. Lam 623.
Distribution: S, SW & E China; Vietnam, Japan, India. Ecology: Thickets or thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.; fruiting: Jun.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Aganosma laevis was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Aganosma laevis was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Anoectochilus yungianus S. Y. Hu 香港金線蘭（容氏開唇蘭）
Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 24(3–4): 257, fig. 1a, 2a–e. 1971; 25(1–2): 50. 1972; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 45, fig. 17. 1977; FRPS 17: 221. 1999; FGD 7: 364. 2006; FOC 25: 79. 2009, pro syn. sub A. roxburghii.

Terrestrial herb, 10–20 cm tall, the basal 3–5 internodes lying on the forest floor having the appearance of rhizome, the distal upright portion consisting of 4 or 5 internodes, short and bearing a rosette of leaves. Leaves petiolate, leaf blades ovate, 1.5–5 × 1–3 cm, base subtruncate, apex acute, velvety green above, purple beneath, with 5 coral-red veins and distinct reticulation of veinlets. Flowers white, 4–5, in a terminal raceme; pedicels 2–3 mm; sepal distinct, villose, the dorsal one ovate, strongly recurved at the apex, gibbous at base; the lateral two spreading, 6–7 mm; petals white, falcate, oblique, 6–7 mm, flush with the margin of the odd sepal and lining its inside; lip white, with a conical spur, attached to column, bending at an angle of 90º, fringed on the sides, prolonged into 2 terminal lobes (epichile); column short, with 2 front wings; anther ovoid, apex long, pointed; pollinia 2, sectile; ovary 13–16 mm, villose, hairs glandular.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. C. P. Lau 173 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3230; Y. W. Lam 1171.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests, alt. 400 m. Flowering: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by S. Y. Hu from Tai Mo Shan in 1971.

Antidesma bunius (L.) Spreng. 五月茶（五味子）

Syst. Veg. 1: 826. 1825; FHK 318. 1861; FKH 237. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 63, pl. 16: 4– 7. 1994; FGD 5: 39. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 61. 2005.

Stilago bunius L., Mant. 122. 1767.


Tree up to 10 m tall, branchlets glabrous except the buds. Leaves papery or leathery; stipules linear, caducous; petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, obovate or oblong-obovate, 8–16(–23) × 3–10 cm, base broadly cuneate or cuneate, apex acute to rounded, mucronate, dark-green and shining adaxially, glabrous or slightly pubescent on midven abaxially; lateral veins 7–11 pairs. Male spikes 6–17 cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Male flowers: calyx cup-shaped, 3–4-lobed, lobes ovate-triangular; stamens 3– 4, ca. 2.5 mm; disk cup-shaped, entire or irregularly lobed; rudimentary ovary clavate. Female racemes 5–12(–18) cm. Female flowers: calyx and disk as in male flowers; pistils slightly longer than the sepals; ovary broad-ovoid, glabrous; styles terminal; stigma short and broad, retuse at the apex. Drupes subglobose, compressed-ovoid or ellipsoidal, 8–10 × 8 mm, red to black when mature; fruiting pedicels ca. 4 mm.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 172, 1017, 1275, 1867; Y. S. Lau 306; P. S. Choi 124.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Xizang, Jiangxi, Fujian; India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, New Guinea, Queensland, Sri Lanka, Vietnam.

Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Uses: Food (fruit), material (wood).

Antidesma fordii Hemsl. 黃毛五月茶（早禾樹）
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 430. 1894; FKH 237. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 54, pl. 14: 1 – 5. 1994; FGD 5: 38, fig. 23. 2003.

Small tree up to 7 m tall; branchlets, petioles, stipules and rachis of inflorescence yellow-tomentose; stipules ovate-lanceolate, to 1 cm; petioles 1–3 mm; leaf blade papery, oblong, elliptic or obovate, 7–25 × 3–10.5 cm, base rotund or obtuse, apex short- or caudate-acuminate, adaxially glabrous when full grown, densely pubescent on abaxial surface; lateral veins 7–11 pairs, elevated abaxially. Inflorescences spicate (male) or racemose (female), terminal or axillary, 8–13 cm; bracts linear, ca. 1 mm. Male flowers: calyx 5-lobed, lobes broadly ovate, ca. 1 × 1mm; disk 5-lobed; stamens 5, inserted at inner side of disk. Female flowers: pedicels 1–3 mm; calyx as in male; disk cup-shaped, glabrous; ovary ellipsoidal, 3 mm; styles 3, terminal; stigma bipartite. Drupes fusiform, ca. 7 × 4 mm.

Locality: Lai ChiWo, Sha Tau Kok, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Sha Lo Tung, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 2516; HK sheet 24623; Hu & But 20637 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi,Yunnan, Fujian; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Montane forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Antidesma ghaesembilla Gaertn. 方葉五月茶

Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 89, pl. 39. 1788; FKH. 10: 237. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 56, pl. 15: 1– 5. 1994; FGD 5: 28. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 65. 2005.

Antidesma paniculatum Roxb. ex Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 764. 1806; FHK 318. 1861.


Tree up to 20 m tall; branchlets densely yellow-pubescent. Leaves papery; stipules linear, caducous. Petioles 5–20 mm, pubescent; leaf blade oblong, ovate, obovate or rotund, 3–9.5 × 2–5 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, apex rounded, obtuse or acute, sometimes mucronate or retuse, margin slightly revolute, pubescent on veins abaxially; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Inflorescence spicate (male) or racemose (female), 3–8 cm, yellow-pubescent. Male flowers: calyx usually 5-lobed, lobes obovate; stamens 4–5(–7), 2–2.5 mm, filaments free; disk 4- to 6-lobed; rudimentary ovary obconical, 0.7 mm. Female flowers: pedicels very short; calyx as in male flowers; disk annular; ovary ovoid, ca. 1 mm in diam.; styles 3, terminal. Drupes depressed globose, ca. 4.5 mm in diam.


Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Davis, Pok Fu Lam Rd., Hok Tau, Sai Kung, So Kwun Wat, Tai Po Tsai, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Mong Tsai, Central Island, Clear Water Bay, Ko Lau Wan, Chuen Lung, Lautau Island. L. T. Lo 94; P. S. Choi 232; K. Y. Tam 133.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Australia, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Vietnam.

Ecology: Open shrublands, mixed dry forests. Flowering: Mar.– Sep.; fruiting: Jun. – Dec.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (potential as fruit).

Antidesma japonicum Siebold & Zucc. 日本五月茶（五味子木）

Abh. Bayr. Akad. Munch. 4: 212. 1846; FHK 318. 1861; FKH 237. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 65, pl. 18: 7 – 11. 1994; FGD 5: 39, fig. 24. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 66. 2005.


Shrub or small tree, 2–4 m tall, glabrous or the young parts very slightly pubescent. Leaves papery to sub-leathery; stipules linear, caducous; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, rarely obovate, 3.5–13 × 1.5–5 cm, base cuneate, obtuse or rounded, apex usually caudate-acuminate, mucronulate, glabrous or pubescent on veins abaxially; lateral veins 5–10 pairs. Racemes terminal, to 10 cm, laxly flowered; rachis slender, sparsely pubescent. Male flowers: pedicels 1–1.5 mm, base with lanceolate bracteoles; calyx campanulate, ca. 0.7 mm, 3–5-lobed, lobes ovate-triangular, sparsely pubescent to glabrous abaxially; stamens 2–5, exserted; disk cushion-shaped. Female flowers: pedicels much shorter, calyx and disk as in male flowers, but smaller; staminodes 1–2; ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 mm, glabrous, styles terminal, stigma 2–3-fid. Drupes ellipsoidal, ca. 5–6 mm in diam.


Locality: Bowen Rd., Deep Water Bay, Harlech Rd., Hatton Rd., Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 18; P. S. Choi 447; Y. W. Lam 95.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Qinghai, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam.

Ecology: Thin forests on mountain slopes or in ravines. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Sep.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Antidesma montanum Blume 山地五月茶

Bijdr. 1124. 1825; FRPS 44(1): 60, pl. 17. 1994; FGD 5: 41. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 70. 2005.


Small tree or shrub, 2–8(–15) m tall, branchlets pubescent when young, glabrescent in age. Leaves papery; stipules linear, 4–10 mm, persistant; petioles to 1 cm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic, oblong, obovate-oblong, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 7–25 × 2–10 cm, base acute or obtuse, apex long- or short-caudate, glabrous or sparsely pubescent on veins abaxially; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Racemes terminal or axillary, 5–16 cm, simple or with 1–2 branches; rachis pubescent or puberulous. Male flowers: pedicels 0.5–1 mm; calyx deeply 3–5-lobed, lobes broadly ovate, apex obtuse, puberulous, margin with irregular teeth; stamens 3–5; disk fleshy, 3–5-lobed; rudimentary ovary obconical to subglobose, apex obtuse, sometimes obscurely lobed. Female flowers: calyx cup-shaped, 3–5-lobed, lobes oblong-triangular, puberulous; disk small, lobed; ovary ovoid, glabrous, styles terminal. Drupes ovoid, 5–8 mm; fruiting pedicels 3–4 mm.


Locality: Ha Wo Hang. P. T. Li 2423, 2424, 2425 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia.

Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul. –Nov.

Antidesma pseudomicrophyllum Croizat 柳葉五月茶

J. Arnold Arb. 21: 496. 1940; FRPS 44(1): 58, pl. 16: 1 – 3. 1994.

Antidesma neriifolium Pax & Hoffm. var. pseudomicrophyllum (Croizat) H. S. Kiu, FGD 5: 42. 2003.


Tree up to 12 m tall; young branches, petioles, rachis of inflorescences and pedicels pubescent or puberulous. Leaves papery; petioles 2–4 mm; leaf blade linear or linear-lanceolate, 4–12 × 0.8–1 cm, base obtuse to rotund, apex acuminate, mucronulate; lateral veins 6–12, delicate, nearly parallel. Racemes axillary and terminal, 1–3 cm, rachis densely puberulous. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 0.8 mm; calyx-lobes 4, broad-ovate, ca. 1 mm; disk discoid; stamens 3, exceeding the calyx. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 0.5 mm; calyx cup-shaped, 4–6-lobed, lobes 0.5 mm; disk discoid; ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 1 mm, styles terminal, 2–3-fid. Drupes ellipsoidal, ca. 5× 3–4 mm, red when mature.


Locality: Aberdeen Rd. H. C. Tang 1325 (CUHK); P. T. Li 2407, 2408, 2409 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan.

Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Oct.

Antidesma venosum E. Mey. ex Tul. 小葉五月茶

Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 3, 15: 232. 1851; FRPS 44(1): 63, pl. 16: 4 – 7. 1994.

Antidesma microphyllum Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 432. 1894; FKH 237. 1912; FGD 5: 41. 2003.

Antidesma montanum P. Hoffm. var. microphyllum (Hemsl.) P. Hoffm., Kew Bull. 54: 357. 1999; P. Hoffm., Fl. Thailand 8(1): 72. 2005, p.p. excl. syn. A. pseudomicrophyllum Croizat.

Antidesma neriifolium Pax & Hoffm., Pflanzenr. 81(IV. 147. XV): 130. 1921; FGD 41.2003.


Shrub, 1–3 m tall; branchlets densely yellow-pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves sub-leathery; stipules linear-lanceolate, 5–10 mm, puberulous; petioles 3–5 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate or narrowly oblong-elliptic, 3–10 × 0.4 –2.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse or acuminate, glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent abaxially; midvein and lateral veins elevated abaxially, pubescent on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Racemes solitary or 2–3-clustered, pubescent; bracts ovate, 1 mm, puberulous. Male flowers: pedicels very short; calyx 4–5-lobed, lobes broadly ovate or rounded, ca. 2–3 mm in diam., apex usually glandular; disk annular; stamens 4–5, inserted at sinus of disk, anthers 0.5 mm wide; rudimentary ovary clavate, as high as the disk. Female flowers: pedicels 1–1.5 mm; calyx and disk as in male flowers; ovary ovoid, glabrous, styles 3–4, terminal. Drupes ovoid, ca. 5 × 3 mm, red to purple when mature; apex with a persistent style; fruiting pedicels 1.5–2 mm.


Locality: Aberdeen, Shek O, Mount Gough, Happy Valley, Hatton Rd., Pok Fu Lam, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1325, 1806; Y. S. Lau 137; L. T. Lo 606.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; E Africa, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.

Ecology: Forests on montane slopes or in ravines. Flowering: May – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Nov.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Antigonon leptopus Hook. & Arn. 珊瑚藤
Bot. Beech. Voy. 308. 1841; FHN 1: 385, fig. 203. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 294; 1996; FGD 4: 80, fig. 53. 2000.

Perennial tendril-climbing vines, to 10 m or longer, with thick tuberous root. Stems angular, woody at base, covered with short hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 0.8–2 cm; leaf blade ovate-triangular, 6–15 × 4– 8 cm, base cordate to sagittate, apex acuminate, tip blunt, margin crenate-undulate, covered with soft short hairs on both surfaces; veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Flowers in terminal panicles and axillary racemes, 5 –10 cm, densely flowered, with the rachis terminating in forked tendrils; pedicels slender, 0.5 –1 cm, pubescent. Perianth-segments 5, pink or white, the outer 3 elliptic, 1–1.5 × 0.6 –1.2 cm, apex rounded, base cordate, inner 2 oblong, 1–1.2 × 0.4 –0.6 cm, apex obtuse, narrowed to the base. Stamens 8; filaments united at base, the free parts covered with rusty glandular hairs. Achenes 1–1.5 cm, 3-angled, enclosed in the enlarged, persistent perianth.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. H. C. Tang 176; L. T. Lo 561.
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely cultivated or naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Antirhea chinensis (Champ. ex Benth.) F. B. Forbes & Hemsl. 毛茶
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23(156): 384. 1888; FHN 3: 339, fig. 756. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 16, pl. 6. 1999; FGD 6: 196, fig. 106. 2005.
Guettardella chinensis Champ. & Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 197. 1852; FHK 158. 1861.

Evergreen shrubs, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets covered when young with appressed hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 4–10 mm, densely sericeous; stipules triangular, ca. 4 mm, apex acuminate, sericeous; leaf blade oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 3–7(–9) × 1–2.5(–3) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, slightly incurved, sprinkled with a few hairs or glabrous on adaxial surface, densely sericeous on abaxial surface. Cymes axillary, sericeous. Peduncles 1 – 3 cm. Calyx scarcely 2 mm, covered with appressed hairs; tube very short; limb enlarged, 4–5‑lobed; lobes linear or lanceolate, 0.5–1.5 mm, unequal. Corolla yellow, densely covered with greyish silky hair abaxially; lobes 4(–5), ovate, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Drupe ellipsoidal, 5–7 mm, obtusely angled, pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. Y. Tam 145; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24062; HK sheet 39142.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Gough and Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Antirrhinum majus L. 金魚草
Sp. Pl. 617. 1753; D. A. Webb in T. G. Tutin & V. H. Heywood, Fl. Europ. 3: 223. 1972.

Perennial herbs. Stems up to 150 cm, erect or straggling, glabrous. Leaves linear to ovate, 10–70 × 1–25 mm, base distinctly cuneate. Inflorescence glabrous or glandular‑pubescent. Pedicels 2–10 mm. Bracts ovate, 2–10 mm. Calyx‑lobes ovate‑oblong to suborbicular, 6–8 mm. Corolla usually pink or purple, 3–4.5 cm. Capsules oblong, 10 – 14 mm, glandular‑pubescent or glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Y. Chan 1428 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 9646 (CUHK); H. T. Shun 28 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mediterranean region, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental (aquarium).

Aphananthe aspera (Thunb.) Planch. 糙葉樹
Prodr. 17: 208. 1873; FGD 2: 224. 1991; FOC 5: 12. 2003.
Prunus aspera Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 463. 1784.

Tree, 7–20 m tall or more, monoecious. Branchlets slender, scabrous hairy when young. Stipules linear-lanceolate, nearly 1 cm. Petioles 7–15 cm; leaves papery, ovate, narrowly ovate, or rarely subelliptic, 5 –13 × 3 – 6 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex attenuate to cuspidate, margin regularly and sharply serrulate except base, sparsely scabrous hairy on both surfaces, denser abaxially, 3-veined and pinninerved; lateral veins 6 –8 pairs, obliquely ascending to teeth. Male cymes fasciculated at base of young branchlets, axillary. Sepals 5, rarely 4, persistent; stamens as many as sepals; ovary hairy. Drupes black when dry, ovoid-globose, 8 –9 mm in diam., scabrous hairy.

Locality: Sha Tau Kok. Y. W. Lam 360.
Distribution: S, E & SW China, Hubei, Shanxi; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Aphananthe cuspidata (Blume) Planch. 滇糙葉樹（坡命工）
Prodr. 17: 209. 1873; FGD 2: 226. 1991; FOC 5: 12. 2003.
Cyclostemon cuspidatum Blume, Bijdr. 599. 1825.
Gironniera nitida Benth., FHK 325. 1861; FKH 243. 1912.
Gironniera cuspidata (Blume) Kurz, For. Fl. Brit. Burma 2: 479. 1877; FHN 2: 370. 1965.

Tree, 10 –18 m tall, dioecious. Branchlets slender, glabrous. Stipules lanceolate , 6–10 mm. Petioles 7–10 mm; leaves leathery, nitid, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 6–13 × 2–5 cm, base obtuse, apex long acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, pinninerved; lateral veins 6 –10 pairs, anastomosing before reaching margin, or inconspicuously serrate, reticulate veins dense, conspicuous on both surfaces. Male inflorescences short, many-flowered. Male flowers: sepals 4–5, oblanceolate, ca. 2 mm; staminodes becoming a fascicle of yellow hairs. Female inflorescences ca. 1 cm, branched, sometimes 1–2-flowered, axillary; sepals oblong, ca. 12 mm, adnated to ovary. Drupes ovoid, 8 –10 mm in diam., glabrous, beak 3 – 4 mm at tip. Stalk up to 1 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 589; Y. S. Lau 2682.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May, Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep., Nov.–Dec.

Aphyllorchis montana Rchb. f. 無葉蘭
Linnaea 41: 57. 1877; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 54, fig. 24. 1977; FRPS 17: 84, pl. 10: 6–7. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 749. 2000; FGD 7: 339, fig. 168. 2006; FOC 25: 178. 2009.

Saprophytic herb, 40 70 cm tall at flowering time; the lower portion of the stem marked by sheaths of 0.5–2 cm, the middle portion by scales of 1–1.3 cm, the apical portion being the raceme of 10–20 cm. Flowers pale yellow, subtended by linear-lanceolate bracts of 6–14 mm; dorsal sepal oblong-obovate, 9–11 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals slightly shorter; petals oblong; lip trilobed, 7–9 mm, the lateral lobes deltoid, the apical lobe ovate, 5–7 mm, obtuse; column 7–10 mm, enlarged at the distal end.

Locality: Sha Tin (Hu 1977), Tsuen Wan (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; widespread species occurring in N India to Sri Lanka thence eastward, through warm areas in China to Indonesia, Philippines, northward to Japan.
Ecology: Shade of large trees. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: This species was first recorded in 1975. Recent studies (e.g. M. Roy et al., BMC Biology 7: 51. 2009) show that the species is associated with a board spectrum of ectomycorrhizal fungi.

Apluda mutica L. 水蔗草
Sp. Pl. 1: 82. 1753; FHK 422. 1861; FKH 325. 1912; FHN 4: 462, fig. 1249. 1977; FFJ 6: 254, fig. 223. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 167, pl. 39: 1 – 10. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 522, pl. 220. 2000; FOC 22: 614. 2006; FGD 9: 478, fig. 250. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or ascending from decumbent base, up to 3 m tall. Leaf sheaths ciliate or not; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 10–35× 0.3–2 cm, base petiolate, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Spathate panicle up to 50 cm, branches very slender with spaced spathes subtending small clusters of spatheoles. Sessile spikelet 4–6 mm, bisexual; lower glume long ovate, rounded, margins slightly inrolled, obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, 5–7-veined; lower lemma subequal to lower glume; upper lemma boatshaped, deeply 2-lobed with 4–12 mm awn, or entire to emarginate and awnless. Pedicellate spikelet reduced to lemma; normal pedicellate spikelet 2-floret, lower glume long ovate, papery to thin-leathery, apex acute or slightly 2-toothed, upper glume as long as or slightly shorter than lower glume; lower floret staminate; upper floret staminate or seldom bisexual and fertile.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1029, 1044; HK sheet 35847.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SW Asia, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Pacific islands, Australia (Queensland), Indian Ocean islands (Mascarenes), Madagascar.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets, sometimes forming large colonies. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Apocopis intermedius (A. Camus) Chai-Anan 異穗楔穎草
Thai Forest Bull. Bot. 6: 46. 1972; FOC 22: 599. 2006; FGD 9: 472. 2009.
Lophopogon intermedium A. Camus, Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 25: 285. 1919.
Apocopis heterogamus Keng & S. L. Chen, FRPS 10(2): 112, pl. 26: 1–3. 1997; FYN 9: 644. 2003.
Apocopis wrightii Munro var. macranthus S. L. Chen, FRPS 10(2): 112. 1997; Check List HK Plants 322. 2002; 113. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, ca. 40–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous to hirsute; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 6–15 × 0.3–0.5 cm, tuberculate-pilose when young, or sometimes densely hispid; ligule ca. 1.5 mm. Racemes 2, 2–4 cm, lowermost spikelets barren, awnless; rachis internodes 2.5–3 mm, loosely ciliate with yellowish brown soft hairs. Sessile spikelet 6–9 mm; callus hairs yellowish brown; lower glume oblong, firmly herbaceous, glabrous or hispid, greenish yellow with a scarious brown or red band across apex, veins green, straight, connected there by transverse veinlets, terminating below apex, truncate or ciliate; upper glume oblong, as long as lower glume or slightly longer, submembranous, dark red on the upper, emarginate and short ciliate, 3-veined; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, as long as lower glume or slightly shorter, hyaline membranous, apex ciliate; upper floret staminate or barren, lemma linear-lanceolate, apex entire or 2-toothed, awned or awnless; awn geniculate, 2–3 cm. Pedicellate spikelet developed, ca. 5 mm, awned.

Locality: Sai Wan, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 2000; HK sheet 15247.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Yunnan, Zhejiang; Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

Apocopis wrightii Munro 瑞氏楔穎草
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts. 4: 363. 1860; FHK 421. 1861; FKH 320. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 111. 1997; FOC 22: 599. 2006; FGD 9: 471. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 30–60 cm tall, branching above base, 6–7-noded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear, 8–12 × 0.2–0.6 cm, tuberculate-pilose, rarely glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm. Racemes 2–5 cm, lowermost spikelets barren, awnless; rachis internodes 1.5–2 mm, yellowish brown ciliate; pedicel yellowish brown bearded. Sessile spikelet 3.5–6 mm; callus yellowish brown bearded; lower glume obovate-oblong, firmly herbaceous, glabrous or thinly hispid, greenish yellow with a scarious red-brown band across apex, veins green, straight, terminating below apex, connected there by transverse veinlets, apex truncate, ciliate; lower florets exserted from the apex, lemma oblong-lanceolate; upper floret bisexual, lemma apex 2-denticulate or subentire, awned; awn geniculate, 2–3 cm. Pedicellate spikelet absent or rudimentary.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, High Island, Wang Shan Keuk. S. Y. Hu 7769, 8501, 10881 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Thailand.
Ecology: Open grassy hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Aponogeton lakhonensis A. Camus 水蕹
Notul. Syst.(Paris) 1: 273. 1910; FRPS 8: 34. 1992; FGD 6: 303. 2005; FOC 23: 104. 2010.
Aponogeton natans auct. non (L.) Engl. & Krause: FHN 4: 64. 1977.
Aponogeton monostachyon auct. non L. f.: FKH 291. 1912.

Aquatic herb; rhizomes ovoid-globular or oblong, toward 2 cm. Leaves basal, submersed or floating, narrow ovate to lanceolate, 4–6 × 0.7–2 cm, base cordate or rounded, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire, midvein 1, parallel veins 3–4 on each sides of midvein; petioles of submersed leaves 9–15 cm, of floating leaves 40–60 cm. Scapes ca. 20 cm, exserted from the water when flowering; spikes cylindrical, ca. 5 cm; spathes caducous. Flowers bisexual, tepals 2, yellow, free, spathulate-obovate, 2×0.7 mm, midrib obvious. Stamens 6, slightly longer than tepals, free, 2-cycled. Carpels 3–6, free or connate at base, ovary 4–6-ovuled. Follicle ovoid, apex attenuate into a short and obtuse beak.

Locality: Tsuen Wan. W. J. Tutcher 11576; HK sheet 29894.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; India, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Ponds, ditches or paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Aporusa dioica (Roxb.) Müll. Arg. 銀柴（大沙葉）
Prodr. 15(2): 472. 1866; FRPS 44(1): 126, pl. 37. 1994; FGD 5: 54, fig. 31. 2003.
Alnus dioica Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 3: 580. 1832.
Aporosa chinensis (Champ. & Benth.) Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 13: 34. 1934.
Aporosa frutescens auct. non Blume: FHK 317. 1861.
Aporosa leptostachya Benth., FHK 317. 1861; FKH 236. 1912.
Scepa chinensis Champ. & Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 72. 1854.

Tree to 9 m tall, but usually shrubby in secondary forests and thickets, ca. 2 m tall, young parts rusty-pubescent. Leaves sub-leathery; stipules obliquely ovate-lanceolate, 4–6 mm; petioles 5–12 mm, with 2 glands at apex; leaf blade elliptic, narrowly ovate, oblong-elliptic, obovate or oblanceolate, 6–12 × 3.5–6 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex rounded to acute, entire or sparsely and shallowly dentate, glabrous and shining adaxially, sparsely pubescent along veins abaxially. Male spikes ca. 2.5 cm, the flowers densely clustered; bracts ovate-triangular, ca. 1 mm, pubescent outside; sepals usually 4, oblong-ovate; stamens 2–4, longer than sepals. Capsules ellipsoidal, 1–1.3 cm, pubescent, 2-seeded; seeds subovate, ca. 9 × 5.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 32231, 38729, 40117.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi,Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Appendicula cornuta Blume 牛齒蘭
Bijdr. 6: fig. 12, et 7: 302. 1825; FRPS 19: 58, pl. 9: 7–9. 1999; FGD 7: 445, fig. 224. 2006; FOC 25: 364. 2009.
Apendicula bifaria Lindl. ex Benth., Hook. J. Bot. Kew Misc. 7: 35. 1855; FHK 358. 1861; FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 57, fig. 26. 1977.

Epiphytic caespitose perennial herb; stems erect or hanging, subcylindrical. Leaves distichous, ovate-elliptic or oblong, 2–4 × 0.5–1.2 cm, base sheathing, apex obtuse, notched, apiculate. Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; S to SE Asia.
