Aquilaria sinensis (Lour.) Spreng. 土沉香（牙香樹、白木香）
Syst. Veg. 2: 356. 1825; FHN 1: 434, fig. 238. 1964; FFJ 4: 37, fig. 31. 1989; FGX 1: 616, pl. 255: 8– 12. 1991; FGD 3: 84, fig. 58. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 290, pl. 45: 5 – 8. 1999.
Ophiospermum sinense Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 281. 1790.
Aquilaria grandiflora Benth., FHK 297. 1861; FKH 227. 1912.
Aquilaria sinensis (Lour.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 15(3): 248. 1919 [1920].

Evergreen tree, 5–15 m tall; bark dark grey; branchlets terete, puberulous, glabrescent. Petiole 5 mm, pubescent. Leaves subovate, obovate to elliptic, 5–10 × 2–5 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex short acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 15 – 20 on each side of midvein, veins and veinlets slender, subparallel, obscure. Flowers yellowish green; pedicel 5–10 mm; calyx tube shallowly campanulate, ca. 6 mm, densely pubescent on both surfaces, lobes 5, ovate, 3 – 5 mm long, pubescent on both surfaces; petals 10, scale-like, inserted at the throat of calyx-tube, hairy; stamens 10 in 1 whorl, filaments ca. 1 mm; ovary ovoid, hairy. Capsules obovoid, 2–3 × 2 cm, apex apiculate, base tapering, densely yellowish brown pubescent. Seeds dark brown, ovoid, base with a ca. 2 cm tail-shaped appendage.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3319; K. L. Yip 4540; S. K. Chan 1.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan.
Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), incense, resin.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), incense, resin.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Arachis hypogaea L. 落花生
Sp. Pl. 741. 1753; FKH 78. 1912; FRPS 41: 361. 1995; FGD 5: 354. 2003.

Annual herb. Roots richly nodulose. Stems erect or prostrate, 30– 80 cm, yellow-villose at first. Stipules lanceolate, 2– 4 cm, united with petiole in lower leaf. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 2 pairs, ovate-oblong or obovate, 2.4 × 0.5–2 cm, base subrounded, apex obtuse, sometimes emarginate, hairy on both surfaces, margin ciliate, lateral veins ca. 10 on each side of midvein. Calyx-tube slender, 4 – 6 mm. Corolla yellow; vexillum 1.7 cm in diam., apex emarginate; wings free of keel, oblong or oblique-ovate; keel long ovoid, shorter than wings, incurved, beaked. Stamens monadelphous. Ovary ripens underground into a reticulate pod containing 1 – 3(–6) seeds. Seeds 1 –4, ellipsoidal-ovoid, 10 – 15 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1141; HK sheet 7194, 40153.
Distribution: Native to S America, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Oil, food.

Aralia chinensis L. 楤木
Sp. Pl. 273. 1753; FHK 135. 1861; J. Wen, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 38: 1. 2000.
Aralia planchoniana Hance, J. Bot. 4: 172. 1866.
Aralia decaisneana auct. non Hance: Li, Sargentia 2: 111. 1942, p.p.; FRPS 54: 157. 1978; FGD 1. 293. 1987.
Aralia spinosa auct. non L.: FKH 118. 1912.

Prickly and tawny-tomentose shrub, ca. 3 m tall; prickles slender, short, straight, base slightly expanded. Leaves usually bipinnate, ca. 1.2 m, with a pair of leaflets at each division of the rachis, pinnae 7–11-foliolate; leaflets leathery, subsessile to short-petiolulate, ovate to oblong-ovate, 8–11 × 4–8 cm, base rounded or subcordate, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, tawny-tomentose on both surfaces, especially along the veins abaxially; lateral veins 6– 8 pairs on each side of midvein, the tertiary veins obscure; petiolules 0– 5 mm. Inflorescence consisting of numerous, 30–50-flowered umbels of 2.5 cm in diam., forming a large terminal panicle, 30–60 cm, branches up to 50 cm, villose-tomentose. Pedicels about 1 cm, tomentose; bracteoles 3 mm, persistent. Calyx 2 mm, glabrous, distinctly 5-dentate. Petals 5, triangular-ovate, 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens 5, filaments 2.5 mm long. Ovary 5-locular; styles 5, united at base. Fruit globose, 4 mm in diam., prominently 5-ridged when dry.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. Gibbs 7551; H. C. Tang 2159; HK sheet 12754.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Sunny hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Nov.
Notes: This plant was misidentified by most Chinese authors as Aralia decaisneana Hance, which is endemic to Taiwan. The species was reported as Aralia decaisneana Hance previously (Check List HK Plants 204. 2002; 72. 2004).

Aralia finlaysoniana (Wall. ex G. Don) Seem. 虎刺楤木
J. Bot. 6: 134. 1868; J. Wen, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 38: 2. 2000.
Aralia armata auct. non Seem.: FRPS 54: 154. 1978; FGD 1. 292. 1987.
Aralia dasyphylla auct. non Miq.: FKH 118. 1912.

Prickly shrub, 4 m tall; prickles conical, short, less than 4 mm, often recurved, the base broadened. Leaves usually tripinnate, with a pair of leaflets at each division of the rachis, the ultimate pinnules 5–9-foliolate, the rachis and partial rachises and petioles prickly; leaflets blade papery, subsessile, ovate-oblong, 4–11 × 2–5 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex acuminate, margin serrate, pilose on both surfaces especially along the veins; lateral veins 4–6 pairs on each side of midvein, the tertiary veins inconspicuous. Inflorescence a large, terminal panicle up to 50 cm, consisting of numerous, many-flowered umbels of 2–2.5 cm in diam. Pedicels 1–1.5 cm, pubescent. Calyx 2 mm, glabrous, distinctly 5-dendate. Petals 5, triangular-ovate, 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens 5. Ovary 5-locular, styles 5, distinct, erect. Fruit globose, 4 mm in diam., prominently 5-ridged when dry.

Locality: Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1694.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: Aug. – Sep.; fruiting: Nov.
Notes: A common species in S China, but it was misidentified as A. armata Seem. by most authors. A. armata Seem. is distributed in SW China (Yunnan Province), India, NW Myanmar and Thailand. The species was reported as Aralia armata (Wall.) Seem. previously (Check List HK Plants 72. 2004).

Araucaria cunninghamii Aiton ex D. Don 南洋杉
Lambert, Descr. Pinus, ed. 2, 3: t. 79. 1837; FRPS 7: 28. 1978; FOC 4: 9. 1999; FGD 4: 8. 2000.

Tree to 30 m tall (up to 70 m in original habitats); bark grey-brown or dark grey, rough, transversely split; crown tower-shaped; lateral branchlets dense, drooping. Leaves dimorphic: leaves of young trees and lateral branchlets loosely arranged, needlelike, falcate, subulate, or triangular, ca. 0.7–1.7 cm × 2.5 mm wide at base, stomatal lines numerous adaxially and weakly evident abaxially; leaves on mature trees and cone-bearing branchlets densely arranged, overlapping, stretching upward, ovate to triangular, 0.6–1 cm, ca. 4 mm wide at base, ridged or not, midvein obvious or not, with many white stomatal lines adaxially, only with irregular stomatal lines at lower half abaxially. Pollen cones terminal, solitary, ovoid or ellipsoid. Seed cones ovoid or ellipsoid, 6–10 × 4.5–7.5 cm; bracts narrowly obovate, sharply ridged, with thin, lateral wing, apex caudate, thickened, acute, obviously reflexed; seed scales thin at apex. Seeds ellipsoid, with a membranous, lateral wing.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 433; L. T. Lo 476.
Distribution: Cultivated in S & SW China. Native to Papua New Guinea; NE Australia.
Uses: Ornamental.

Araucaria heterophylla (Salisb.) Franco 異葉南洋杉
Anais Inst. Super. Agron. 19: 11. 1952; FRPS 7: 30. 1978; FOC 4: 10. 1999; FGD 4: 9. 2000.
Eutassa heterophylla Salisb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8:316. 1807.

Tree to 30 m (up to 70 m in original habitats); bark dark grey, flaking; crown tower-shaped; branchlets spreading horizontally or drooping; lateral branchlets usually pinnately arranged, drooping. Leaves dimorphic: those of young trees and lateral branchlets loosely arranged, spreading openly, bright green, glaucous abaxially, subulate, usually laterally depressed, upcurved, 6–12 mm, 3- or 4- ridged; those of mature trees and cone-bearing branchlets densely arranged, slightly openly spreading, broadly ovate or triangularovate, 5 –9 mm, widest at base, midvein obviously raised or not, apex obtuse. Pollen cones terminal, solitary. Seed cones subglobose, 8 –12 × 7–11 cm, sometimes wider than long; apex of bracts triangular, flattened, acute, upcurved. Seeds ellipsoid, slightly flattened, with a lateral wing.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 432; HK sheet40551.
Distribution: Cultivated in SE & SW China; native to Australia(Norfolk Island).
Uses: Ornamental.

Archidendron clypearia (Jack) I. C. Nielsen 猴耳環
Adansonia n.s. 19(1): 15. 1979 & in Aubrev., Fl. Camb. Laos Vietn. 19: 115. 1981; FGD 5: 144. 2003.
Inga clyperia Jack, Malayan Misc. 2(7): 78. 1822.
Pithecellobium clypearia (Jack) Benth., London J. Bot. 3: 209. 1844; FHK 103. 1861; FKH 92. 1912; FRPS 39: 53. 1988.

Tree, up to 10 m tall. Branchlets acutely angulate, densely yellow-tomentose. Petioles quadrangular. Leaves bipinnate, with glands on leaf-rachis and at the base of petioles; pinnae (3–)4 – 5(–8) pairs, densely yellow tomentose, the lowermost pinna with 3 – 6 pairs of leaflets, the uppermost one with 10–12 pairs of leaflets; leaflets leathery, oblique, rhombic, 1– 7 × 0.7– 3 cm, the upper one largest, downwards smaller, shining adaxially, slightly brown pubescent on both surfaces, base very unequal-sided; subsessile. Heads of several flowers forming terminal or axillary panicle. Calyx campanulate, 2 mm, 5-toothed, as well as corolla densely brown-villose. Corolla white or yellowish, 4–5 mm, connate below middle; lobes lanceolate. Stamens twice as long as corolla, connate below middle. Ovary stalked, hairy. Pods twisted, 1– 1.5 cm wide, forming 2 or 3 coils, indented between the seeds on the outer edge. Seeds 4–10, elliptic or broadly elliptic, 1 cm, black, testa wrinkled.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2479; Y. S. Lau 297; HK sheet 8852.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb. – Jun.; fruiting: Apr. –Aug.
Uses: Environmental, materials (tannin).

Archidendron lucidum (Benth.) I. C. Nielsen 亮葉猴耳環

Adansonia n.s. 19(1): 19. 1979, & in Aubrev., Fl. Camb. Laos Vietn. 19: 120. 1981; FGD 5: 143, fig. 84. 2003.

Pithecellobium lucidum Benth., London J. Bot. 3: 207. 1844; FHK 102. 1861; FKH 92. 1912; FRPS 39: 52. 1988.


Tree, 2 – 10 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and inflorescence shortly brown-tomentose. Pinnae 1– 2 pairs, base of petioles, and leaf rachis with round sunken glands, leaflets 2–3 pairs in lower pinnae, 4 – 5 pairs in upper pinnae, obliquely ovate or oblong, 5–9(–11) × 2–4.5 cm, the terminal pair larger, opposite, the others alternate and smaller, base oblique, apex acuminate mucronate, glabrous on both surfaces or puberulous on veins, shining and deep green adaxially. Heads globular, with 10 –20 flowers, on a peduncle less than 1.5 cm, and forming a long terminal panicle. Calyx under 2 mm, together with corolla shortly brown tomentose. Petals white, 4–5 mm, connate up to middle. Ovary shortly stipitate, glabrous. Pods twisted into a ring, 2 – 3 cm wide, the outer edge indented between the seeds. Seeds black, 1.5 × 1 cm.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 209; Y. S. Lau 2992; HK sheet 40061.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand.

Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul. –Dec.

Archidendron utile (Chun & F. C. How) I. C. Nielsen 薄葉猴耳環
Adansonia n.s., 19: 20. 1979, & in Aubrev., Fl. Camb. Laos Vietn. 19: 122. 1981; FGD 5: 144. 2003.
Pithecellobium utile Chun & F. C. How, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 7(1): 17 –19, pl. 5: 2. 1958; FRPS 39: 53. 1988.

Shrub, 1 – 2 m tall, rarely small trees. Branchlets terete, brown-pubescent. Pinnae 2 – 3 pairs, 10–18 cm, with glands on petioles and at the insertion of the apical 1 – 2 leaflets; leaflets membranous, 4 – 7 pairs, opposite, oblong-rhombic, 2– 9 × 1.5 – 4 cm, the terminal pair larger, the others smaller, base obtuse or acute, apex obtuse, mucronate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially; petiolules short. Heads 1 cm in diam. (not including filaments), forming a terminal panicle, ca. 30 cm. Flowers sessile, white, fragrant. Calyx campanulate, 1.5–2 mm, teeth and corolla pubescent. Corolla 6 – 7 mm, lobes ovate or oblong, less than 2 mm; filaments 12 – 15 mm. Ovary shortly stipitate, glabrous. Pods red brown, falcate, 6– 10 × 1 – 1.3 cm. Seeds suborbicular, 10 mm, black and shining.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung, Wu Kau Tang. F. W. Xing 7162, 8416; Y. W. Lam 2045.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar. –Aug.; fruiting: Apr. – Dec.

Archontophoenix alexandrae (F. Muell.) H. Wendl. & Drude 假檳榔
Linnaea 39: 212. 1875; FHN 4: 170, fig. 1072. 1977; FGD 2: 460, fig. 323. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 130. 1991.

Evergreen tree, to 20 m tall, monoecious. Stems solitary, with leaf scar rings. Leaves pinnate, up to 2.5 m; pinnae arranged regularly, about 80 on each side of rachis, long lanceolate, up to 80 × 5 cm, green adaxially, whitish abaxially; petioles 20–40 cm; sheaths closed and forming a crownshaft on top of stem, green, thick and leathery. Inflorescences under the crownshafts, up to 70 cm, branched 3–4 orders, pendulous; prophylls tubular, deciduous. Flowers white, in triad of a pair of male flowers with a female one in the middle; male flowers: 5–6 mm, sepals usually 3, petals 3, stamens 9–16; female flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, staminodes 3–4. Fruits globose, 0.8–1 cm in diam., red when mature; epicarp smooth, mesocarp thin, fleshy, with fibres, endocarp smooth, thin and fragile. Seed usually 1, endosperm ruminate.

Locality: Commonly cultivated. HK sheet 29451, 29452, 29453.
Distribution: Australia; widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ardisia crenata Sims 朱砂根
Bot. Mag. 45: pl. 1950. 1817; FRPS 58: 68. 1979; FOC 15: 19. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. A. kusukusensis Hayata.
Ardisia crispa A. DC., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 17: 124. 1834, & Prodr. 8: 134. 1844, nom. confus., non Bladhia crispa Thunb. 1784; FHK 206. 1861; FKH 160. 1912.
Ardisia linangensis C. M. Hu, Bot. J. South China 1: 5. 1992.

Shrub, 1–2 m rarely to 3 m tall. Branchlets slender, terete or slightly angular, glabrous, generally bearing 2–5 leaves on upper half. Leaves alternate; petioles 4–10 mm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, ± leathery elliptic to oblong-lanceolate or oblanceolate, (4.5–)6–15(–20) × 1.2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, crisp- or undulate-crenate, margin ± recurved, with large marginal glands, glabrous, minutely rusty lepidote on abaxial surface; glandular dots many, scattered, black or sometimes colorless, slightly convex when dry; lateral veins 12–18 pairs, ± raised abaxially, meeting in an irregular intramarginal vein near edge; veins usually obscure. Inflorescence subumbellate or corymbose, simple or compound, terminal on branchlets, glabrous or puberulous; primary rays 2–4 cm. Pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx split almost to base; lobes ovate to oblong-ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, acute or obtuse, punctate. Corolla white or pinkish, 4–5.5 mm, deeply lobed; lobes ovate, acute, ca. 3 mm wide, with scattered glandular dots. Anthers triangular-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, usually punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style 3–4.5 mm; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, 6–8 mm in diam., bright red, with black glandular dots.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 17735, 34491; H. C. Tang 14, 2143.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, Hubei, Hunan, Yunan, SW Xizang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Cambodia, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Forest , hillsides, valleys and stream banks. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ardisia cymosa Blume 小紫金牛
Bijdr. 689. 1826; C. M. Hu, Blumea 44: 393. 1999.
Ardisia chinensis Benth., FHK 207. 1861; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 90. 1979; FOC 15: 26. 1996.
Ardisia triflora Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 67. 1889.
Ardisia argenticaulis Yang & Dwyer, Taiwania 34: 287. 1989; FOC 15: 27. 1996, syn. nov.

Small shrub, up to 45 cm tall. Stem ascending-erect, longitudinal ridged by shrinking when dry, often creeping and rooted at base, young parts densely rusty scaly. Leaves alternate; petioles 3 – 8 mm, brown scaly; leaf blade papery, obovate to elliptic, 2.7–9(–12) × 1.2– 4 cm, base cuneate-attenuate, apex acuminate or acute, margin ± revolute, subentire or more often obtusely dentate above middle, glabrous adaxially, ± brown scaly abaxially, epunctate; lateral veins 12–28 pairs, with many shorter intercalated pairs and ramified copiously, marginal vein present or imperfect. Inflorescence subumbellate, 3 –7-flowered, in axils of leaves near apex of stem, brown scaly. Peduncle 1–3 cm. Pedicels 5 – 8 mm. Flowers white or tinged pink, 3 –3.5 mm. Calyx ca. 1.2 mm, split nearly to base; lobes ovate-triangular, ca. 1 mm, acute, ciliate, punctate or not. Corolla deeply lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2 mm, ± acuminate, not punctate. Anthers ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apiculate, not punctate. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 3 mm; ovules 5 – 6, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., from purple to black when mature.

Locality: Mount Parker, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. HK sheet 3009, 17726; L. T. Lo 430.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Sichuan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Thin forests, valleys, stream banks. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Ardisia elliptica Thunb. 東方紫金牛
Nov. Gen. Pl. 8: 119. 1798; Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 11: 54. 1932; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand, 6 (2): 128. 1996; FOC 15: 14. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. A. squamulosa Presl., A. kotoensis Hayata.
Ardisia litoralis Andr., Bot. Rep. T. 630. 1811; King & Gamble, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 74(2): 135. 1906.
Ardisia humilis auct. non Vahl (s. str.): Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 127, fig. 20: A–E. 1902.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3 m or occasionally up to 10 m tall, glabrous throughout; branchlets terete or slightly angular, greyish brown. Leaves alternate; petioles 10–15 mm; leaf blade subleathery, elliptic to obovate-oblong, 6 –12 × 2.5 –5 cm, base cuneate, apex bluntly acute to rounded, entire; glandular dots many, scattered, evident only with illumination or sometimes blackish and visible on both surfaces; lateral veins 13–18 pairs, with shorter and thinner intercalated pairs, invisible in fresh plants, ± prominent in dry state, usually not forming an uniform intramarginal vein. Inflorescence corymbose-racemose or subumbellate, (2–)4 – 8-flowered, in axils of normal leaves on upper part of branches, 3 – 8 cm including the peduncle. Pedicels 8 –15 mm. Flowers pink. Calyx ca. 3 mm, split to 2/3 of its length; lobes broadly ovate or orbicular, obtuse, thickly dotted with brown or black glands, margin ± scarious, distinctly ciliate. Corolla deeply lobed; lobes lanceolate, apex acuminate, with scattered purple glandular lines. Anthers lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, locellate, apiculate, punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 6 mm; ovules many, in 3 series on placenta. Fruit slightly compressed globose, grey, with dark purple dots, 6 – 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated in Fairview Park, Mai Po. HK sheet 36156, 36197.
Distribution: Macau; India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Along coasts behind mangroves. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Ardisia faberi Hemsl. 月月紅
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 64. 1889; FRPS 58: 88. 1979.

Small shrub with creeping rhizomes. Stem ascending, up to 30 cm tall, densely rusty crisped villous when young. Leaves subverticillate or subopposite on the lower part of the stem; petioles 3– 8 mm, densely crisped villous; leaf blade papery, ovate- to lanceolate-elliptic or oblanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin coarsely serrate, not glandular, crisped villous on both surfaces; lateral nerves 5 –9 pairs; marginal veins absent. Inflorescence in axils of reduced leaves or normal leaves, subumbellate, few flowered. Peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm, densely pilose. Pedicels 6–12 mm, crisped villous. Calyx split nearly to base, lobes linear-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, densely villous. Corolla white to pink, deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, 4 –5 mm, ± glandular, glabrous, apex acute or obtuse. Anthers ovate, apiculate, not glandular on back. Ovary glabrous; ovules 5 – 6, in 1 series. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., glabrous or puberulous, turning red when mature.

Locality: Tsing Yi. HK sheet 35864, 36113; Xing 8825 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Evergreen forests, valleys and stream banks. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan.

Ardisia fordii Hemsl. 灰色紫金牛
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 64. 1889; FRPS 58: 56. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 89. 1996; FOC 15: 27. 1996.
Embelia fordii Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236 (Heft 9): 326. 1902.

Small shrub, 30 – 60 cm tall; branches slender, terete, densely covered with rusty scales. Leaves alternate; petioles ca. 3 mm, rusty scaly; leaf blade papery, lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 2.5 –5 × 1–1.6 cm, apex acute or subacuminate, tip blunt, cuneately tapering to the obtuse or rounded base, entire, abaxial surface with scattered rusty peltate scales; lateral veins many and fine, parallel, meeting in an intramarginal vein near edge. Inflorescence umbellate, with (1–)2 flowers, axillary on the upper part of branches or subterminal, glabrous or nearly so. Peduncle 2–5 mm. Pedicels 5–7 mm, flowers pink, ca. 4 mm. Calyx split almost to base; lobes ovate, ca. 1.5 mm long, acute or subobtuse, dotted with black glands, ciliolate. Corolla deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, acute, sparsely punctate. Anthers ovate apiculate, not punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style equaling corolla-lobes; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., deep red with black glandular dots.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok. P. S. Choi 390, 514; Y. S. Lau 2813.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Thailand.
Ecology: Evergreen forest , stream banks, valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as Ardisia affinis Hemsl. previously (Check List HK Plants 51. 1993).

Ardisia hanceana Mez 郎傘樹（大羅傘樹）
Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 149. 1902; FKH 160. 1912; C. M. Hu, Bot. J. South China 1992: 6. 1992; FOC 15: 21. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. A. impressa H. R. Fletcher
Ardisia elegantissima H. Leveille, Feddes Repert. Sp. Nov. 10: 373. 1912.
Ardisia elegans auct. non Andr.: Walker, Philipp. J. Sci. 73: 110. 1940; FRPS 58: 66. 1979.

Shrub 1–3 m tall, glabrous except for inflorescence. Branches 20–50 cm, terete or slightly angulate on the upper part. Leaves alternate, ± evenly distributed on the upper 2/3 of branches; petioles channelled and marginate, 6–15 mm; leaf blade rigidly papery, oblong-lanceolate or sometimes elliptic-obovate, 7–12(–15) × 2– 4(–5) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin coarsely crenate, with 4 – 8(–10) marginal glands on each side, abaxial surface ± minutely lepidote, often with very small pores, not punctate; lateral veins 12–15 pairs, slender, at an angle about 60˚ with the midvein, curved-ascending at a distance (ca. 4– 8 mm) from the edge, usually not forming an uniform intramarginal vein; veins invisible. Inflorescence compound-corymbose, glabrescent or minutely puberulous, terminal on branches. Peduncle 0.5 –2(–4) cm; primary rays 2.5 –5.5 cm, each bearing 5 –10 flowers. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Calyx 2–2.5 mm, split nearly to base; lobes ovate to oblong-ovate, acute or obtuse, usually broadest at base, scarcely punctate or with a few light brown glandular dots. Corolla pink, rarely white, 6 –7(– 8) mm, deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, ± acuminate, scarcely punctate or with a few orange glandular dots. Anthers ovate-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, apiculate. Ovary glabrous; style 6–7 mm; ovules 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, dark red or black when mature, 8 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Little Hong Kong, Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Nicholson, Wong Chuk Yeung, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 3042, 17764, 31587; Y. S. Lau 1541; Y. W. Lam 505, 650.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, valleys, stream banks. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Dec.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island around 1850.

Ardisia lindleyana D. Dietr. 山血丹
Syn. Pl. 1: 617. 1839, excl. syn. Ardisia macrocarpa Wall.; C. M. Hu, Bot. J. South China 1992: 7. 1992; FOC 15: 19. 1996.
Ardisia punctata Lindl., Bot. Reg. 10: pl. 827. Sep. 1824, non Jack ex Wall. Mar–Jun. 1824; FHK 206. 1861; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 72. 1979.

Shrub, 0.5 –2 m tall, young parts and branchlets rusty puberulous. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–1.5 cm, densely rusty puberulous; leaf blade, ± leathery or rigidly papery, oblong to elliptic-lanceolate, rarely lanceolate, 7–18 × (1.2–)1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin narrowly recurved, subentire or ± undulate due to the projecting marginal glands, adaxially glabrous, abaxially minutely tawny-puberulous, especially on the midvein, punctate, with bigger and denser glands along the margins; lateral veins 6–12 pairs, at an angle about 60˚ with the midvein, meeting in a conspicuous intramarginal vein 4– 8 mm apart from the edge; veins obscure. Inflorescence subumbellate, usually simple, 6–16-flowered, terminal on special flowering branches, subtended by 1–2(–3) reduced leaves or leaflike bracts. Pedicels 6 –12 mm, lengthening to 2.5 cm in fruit, rusty puberulous. Calyx 2–2.5 mm, split to base; lobes oblong-ovate, acute, puberulous or glabrescent sparsely punctate. Corolla white, deeply lobed; lobes oblong-elliptic, ca. 4.5 × 2.5mm, apex obtuse, with thick black-glands. Anthers lanceolate, ca. 3.8 mm, acute, black-punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 3.5 mm; ovules 4 –5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., dark red when mature, black punctate.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. HK sheet 3011, 34244; Y. S. Lau 2742; Y. W. Lam 1356.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and shrubby areas, mountain slopes. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Ardisia maclurei Merr. 心葉紫金牛
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 21: 351. 1922; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 714. 1963; FTW 3: 53. 1978; FRPS 58: 89. 1979; FOC 15: 25. 1996.
Ardisia sciophila Suzuki-tokio, J. Jap. Bot. 13: 507, fig. 1, 2. 1937.

Small shrub, 4 –15 cm tall. Stem erect or ascending from creeping rhizomes, densely rusty crisped villous when young. Leaves alternate, rarely almost whorled; petioles 0.5 –2.5 cm, rusty pilose; leaf blade papery, ovate- or oblong-elliptic, 4 – 6 × 2.5 –4 cm, base cordate, apex acute to obtuse, margin irregularly serrate, pilose on both surfaces, especially on the midvein; lateral veins ca. 6 pairs, prominent, ending in teeth. Inflorescence axillary from reduced leaves or normal leaves, subumbellate, rarely racemose, rusty-villous, 4 – 6-flowered. Peduncle 1– 4 cm. Bracts linear to narrowly lanceolate, 3–5 mm, pilose. Pedicels slender, 3–7 mm. Calyx split nearly to base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 3.5 mm, pilose on midvein or almost glabrous, margin ciliate, apex acuminate. Corolla white or pink , ca. 4 mm, deeply lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 2 mm broad, glabrous, sparsely punctate, apex acuminate. Anthers ovate, not punctate dorsally, apex acute. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 2.5 mm; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., glabrous, dark reddish when mature.

Locality: Tai Po Kau Nature Reserve. F. W. Xing 8875 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests of hillsides and valleys. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Dec.–May.

Ardisia mamillata Hance 虎舌紅
J. Bot. 22: 290. 1884; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 84, pl. 13: 3– 4. 1979; FOC 15: 26. 1996.

Small shrub. Stem erect or ascending-erect from a creeping rhizome, 5–15 cm , rarely up to 25 cm, densely rusty pilose on young parts. Leaves alternate, often crowded towards apex of stem; petioles 5 –15(–18) mm, densely pilose; leaf blade papery, elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 7–14 × 3 –5 cm, base cuneate to obtuse or narrowly rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin obscurely undulate-crenate, marginal glands inconspicuous, densely covered with rusty appressed hairs and black glandular dots on both surfaces; the hairs on adaxial surface rising from tuberculate processes, to 3 mm long; lateral veins 6 –9 pairs, slender, departing at an angle about 60˚ from the midvein; veins very fine. Inflorescence simple, subumbellate, 10–15-flowered, terminal on special flowering branches of 3– 8 cm long, with 1–2(–3) small leaves near apex. Pedicels 5–12 mm, densely rusty pilose. Calyx split to near base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, sparsely pilose and punctate. Corolla pink or whitish, deeply lobed; lobes ovate-lanceolate, ca. 6 mm, apex acute, black-punctate. Anthers ovate-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apiculate. Ovary glabrous or nearly so; ovules many, in 3 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., ± punctate, bright red when mature.

Locality: Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung. Ford s.n. (GH); P. S. Choi 230; Y. W. Lam 1998.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Hunan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen forest, valleys, shady damp places. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ardisia primulifolia Gardn. & Champ. 蓮座紫金牛
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 324. 1849; FHK 207. 1861;FKH 159. 1912; FRPS 58: 86, pl. 13: 5. 1979; FOC 15: 25.1996.

Small subshrub. Stem almost absent or rarely up to 6 cm high. Leaves aggregate at apex of stem forming a rosette; petioles 2–5 mm, ± rusty pilose; leaf blade papery, elliptic to ellipticobovate, 7–17 × 3 –10 cm, base obtuse, apex rounded or rarely broadly acute, margin obscurely undulate-crenate, densely covered with rusty appressed long (3– 4 mm) hairs on adaxial surface and mainly on midvein and veins of abaxial surface, minutely punctate on both surfaces; lateral veins about 6 pairs, at an angle about 80˚ with the midvein, ramifying and curved-ascending at half way from the margin, with branches ending in marginal glands near the edge. Inflorescence terminal on a 3 –9(–15) cm long scape-like peduncle, arising from the leaf rosette, subumbellate, simple or compound, secondary rays (if present) 6 –10(–20) mm, each bearing 3 –5 flowers. Pedicels 5–9 mm, rusty pilose. Calyx split to near base; lobes lanceolate, 3.5 – 4 mm, rusty pilose at base and near margins, sparsely black-punctate. Corolla pink, deeply lobed; lobes  vate lanceolate, 4.5–5 × 2–3 mm, apex acute, black-punctate towards apex. Anthers ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, apiculate, punctate on back; style slender ca. 3 mm. Ovary glabrous; ovules 3 –5 in one series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., bright red when mature.

Locality: Mount Parker, Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Champion s.n. (K); E. D. Merrill
11094; H. C. Tang 430; Y. S. Lau 2584.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Nov.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

records.text:
Ardisia pusilla A. DC. 九節龍
Trans. Linn. Soc., London 17: 126. 1834; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 88. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand, 6(2): 146.1996; FOC 15: 24. 1996.
Ardisia reptans Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 5: 220. 1910.
Ardisia villosa Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236 (Heft 9): 152. 1902, non Roxb. (1824).

Small shrub, stem creeping at base, upper part ascendent, to 30 cm tall, densely covered with light brown crisped long hairs when young. Leaves opposite or subverticillate; petioles ca. 5 mm, villous; leaf blade papery, elliptic-ovate or obovate, 1.5 – 6.5 × 1–3.5 cm, base acute or rounded, apex broadly acute or obtuse, serrate or denticulate, adaxial surface sparsely strigose at least when young, abaxial surface strigose or mixed with long crisped hairs, with scattered minute orange glandular dots, especially along the margin; lateral veins 4–6(–8) pairs, prominent abaxially, ending in callose teeth; reticulation of veinlets conspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescence umbellate, (1–)2– 4-flowered, pubescent or hirsute, in axils of reduced leaves. Peduncle slender, 1– 4 cm. Pedicels 4–10 mm. Calyx split nearly to base; lobes lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, acuminate, pilose or glabrescent, indistinctly punctate. Corolla white or pink, 3– 4 mm, deeply lobed; lobes ovate or broadly ovate, acute, sparsely punctate. Anthers ovate, generally punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style equaling corolla-lobes; ovules 6 –7, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., red when mature, dotted with small dark glands.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. HK sheet 3060, 17829, 36155.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Sichuan; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Thailand.
Ecology: Evergreen forests, hillsides, stream banks. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Ardisia quinquegona Blume 羅傘樹
Bijdr. 689. 1826; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 54, pl. 8: 1–2. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 91. 1996; FOC 15: 14. 1996.
Ardisia pauciflora Heyne ex Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 2: 279. 1824; FHK 206. 1861.

Shrub 1–2 m tall. Branchlets slender, ± dilated at insertion, weakly angulate and ± rusty scaly when young, becoming terete and smooth in age. Leaves papery; petioles channelled, 5–10 mm, initially lepidote; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, rarely oblanceolate 5 –16 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, entire, adaxial surface dull green and glabrous, abaxial surface covered with appressed rusty scales; glandular dots many, pellucid, evident under transillumination; lateral veins many, very fine, nearly at right angle with the midvein, meeting in an intramarginal vein near edge; veinlets obscure. Inflorescence axillary or lateral, ± brown scaly, subumbellate, usually simple, rarely with 1–2 branches, often appearing a terminal lax panicle due to falling or lack of subtending leaves on lateral branches. Peduncle 1–3.5 cm; branches (if present) 4–8 mm, each bearing 3–8 subumbellate flowers. Pedicels 3–8 mm. Flowers white or pink, ca. 3 mm. Calyx ca. 1 mm, split nearly to base; lobes triangular-ovate, acute, glabrous, sparsely punctate and minutely ciliate. Corolla 2–2.5 mm, deeply lobed; lobes broadly elliptic-ovate, 1.25 –1.8 mm wide, acute, distinctly punctate with reddish or dark small glandular dots. Anthers ovate, ca. 1 mm, apiculate, scarcely punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 2.5 mm; ovules many, in 2 series on placenta. Fruit typically compressed globose, 5 –7 m in diam., ± 5-angled, sometimes globose and without angles.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1149, 1754, 2179.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Sichuan; Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests, hillsides and in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb.

Ardisia sieboldii Miq. 多枝紫金牛
Cat. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 3: 190. 1867; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 709, fig. 291. 1963; FRPS 58: 50, pl. 6: 12–13. 1979; FOC 15: 14. 1996.

Shrub or small tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets terete, finely wrinkled when dry, sparsely brownish lepidote near apex. Leaves alternate; petioles marginate, 5–10 mm; leaf blade subleathery, obovate to elliptic, 5 –8(–14) × 2.3–4(–5) cm, base cuneate, apex broadly to narrowly acute, tip blunt, margin entire, glabrous or sometimes minutely brown scaly on abaxial surface; lateral veins 12–18 pairs, slender, at an angle about 60˚ to the midvein, forming an intramarginal vein near edge. Inflorescences compound, subumbellate or cymose, axillary near end of branches. Peduncle 2–4(–7) cm, secondary branches 5–15 mm, each bearing 4– 6 subumbellate flowers. Pedicels ca. 5 mm, brown scaly. Flowers white, ca. 3 mm. Calyx united for 1/3 their length, lobes ca. 1.5 mm, ovate-triangular, acute, sparsely punctate. Corolla white, ca. 3 mm, deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, apex acute, inconspicuously punctate. Anthers ovate, apiculate, punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style exserted before anthesis; ovules many, multiseriate. Fruit subglobose, red to blackish, 6–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Yeung Chau Island. HK sheet 3047.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thin forests near seashore. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jan.–Apr.
Notes: The species was reported as Ardisia obtusa Mez previously (Check List HK Plants 51. 1993).

Ardisia villosa Roxb. 雪下紅
Fl. Ind. 2: 274. 1824; FRPS 58: 83, pl. 13: 1. 1979; FOC 15: 25. 1996.
Ardisia dumetosa Tutch., Rep. Bot. & For. Dep. Hongkong 1914: 33. 1915.

Small shrub, 30 –100 cm tall. Stem erect, densely rusty villose-tomentose when young. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 mm, rusty villose; leaf blade papery, elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, rarely oblanceolate, (4 –)7–15 × 2.5 –5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin narrowly recurved, subentire or slightly notched at the marginal glands, adaxial surface glabrous except for the puberulous midvein, abaxial surface rusty villose especially on the midvein, black-punctate on both surfaces; lateral veins 12–16 pairs, at an angle about 60˚ with the midvein, ending in marginal glands and forming an irregular intramarginal vein near the edge; veins very fine, conspicuous on abaxial surface. Inflorescence subumbellate, simple or compound, 6–12-flowered, densely rusty villose, terminal on leafy or leafless specialized branches or rarely lateral on main stem. Peduncle 5 –20(– 40) mm; secondary rays (if present) 4 – 8 mm, each bearing 3 –5 flowers. Pedicels 5 –10 mm. Calyx split to near base; lobes oblong lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apex ± obtuse, villose on both surfaces. Corolla pink or white, deeply lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 4 mm, acute, black-punctate. Anthers ovate-lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, ± punctate on back. Ovary ovoid; style ca. 4.5 mm, ± puberulous at base; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, 5–7 mm in diam., dark red or blackish when mature.

Locality: Fanling, Sheung Shui. HK sheet 17752, 17860.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Mynamar, Thailand, West Malaysia , Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets, on mountain slopes and valleys. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Feb.–Jul.

Arenga pinnata (Wurmb.) Merr. 砂糖椰子（桄榔）
Interpr. Herb. Amboin.: 119. 1917; FOC 23: 151. 2010.

Evergreen tree; stems solitary, up to 20 m tall and 30–60 in diam., with long internodes. Leaves pinnate, up to 7 × 1.6 m; pinnae about 110 pairs pointed to different directions, 40–120 × 5 cm, linear, with ear-like bases, undulate margins and erose apices, green adaxially and whitish abaxially; petioles to 1.5 m; sheaths persistent, with black needle-like fibres. Inflorescences interfoliar or seldom infrafoliar, up to 3.5 m, branched 1 order, pendulous; flowers solitary, large; male flowers purplish, ovoid, about 2 cm, sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 60–120; female flowers subglobse, 5–6 cm in diam., sepals 3, petals 3, carpels 3. Fruits subglobose, 7 cm in diam., trigonous, with stigma remains, yellowish or orangish. Seed 1–3, ovoid, black, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, New Guinea.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Lasting 1–2 years after flowering.
Uses: Ornamental, additive (flavouring), food (sugar, starch).
Notes: Arenga westerhoutii Griff., a plant native to Hainan, Guangxi and Yunnan, was previously misidentified as A. pinnata (cf. FHN 4: 167, fig. 1068. 1977; FGD 2: 452. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 110. 1991) but differs in pinnae arrangement, with pinnae of A. westerhoutii being regularly arranged and spaced in same plane except for basal few pinnae.

records.text:
Argyreia acuta Lour. 白鶴藤
Fl. Cochinch. 135. 1790; FGZ 588. 1956; FHN 3: 494, fig. 878. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 135. 1979; FOC 16: 320. 1995; FGD 4: 342, fig. 203. 2000.
Lettsomia chalmersii Hance, J. Bot. 16(188): 230. 1878.

Twining vine. Stems terete, densely silvery sericeous when young, later yellowish or glabrescent. Petiole 3–4(–6) cm; leaf blade elliptic, ovate or suborbicular, 5–12 × 3–8(–11) cm, base rounded, slightly cordate, or truncate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially firmly appressed silvery sericeous. Cymes many‑flowered, axillary or terminal; peduncle 3.5–7 cm, silvery sericeous; bracts elliptic or obovate, 0.8–2.2 cm, silvery sericeous abaxially, deciduous. Pedicel ca. 5 mm. Sepals ovate‑oblong, unequal; outer ones 9–12 mm; inner ones 6–7 mm, silvery apex obtuse, sericeous abaxially. Corolla white, funnelform, ca. 2.8 cm, silvery sericeous abaxially; limb deeply 5‑lobed; lobes oblong, 1.5 mm, apex emarginate, midpetaline bands slivery sericeous. Stamens exserted; filaments hairy at base. Pistil exserted; ovary glabrous, 2‑locular. Berry enclosed by enlarged calyx, red, globose, ca. 8 mm in diam. Fruiting sepals leathery, red inside. Seeds 2–4, brown, ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak. HK sheet 33906.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; India, Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Argyreia capitiformis (Poir.) Ooststr. 頭花銀背藤
Fl. Malesiana, ser. 1. 6(6): 941. 1972; FOC 16: 317. 1995.
Convolvulus capitiformis Poir., Encycl. Suppl. 3: 469. 1814.
Convolvulus capitatus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 28. 1794
Argyreia capitata (Vahl) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 423. 1833; FHN 3: 494. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 129. 1979; FGD 4: 342. 2000; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.
Argyreia verrucosohispida Y. Y. Qian, Guihaia 11(3): 211, fig. 2. 1991.
Ipomoea capitata (Vahl) Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 4: 238. 1819
Lettsomia capitata (Vahl) Benth. & Hook. f., Gen. Pl. 2(2): 870. 1876.
Lettsomia capitiformis (Poir.) Kerr, Fl. Siam. 3(2): 30. 1954.
Lettsomia strigosa Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 1: 491. 1832; FKH 178. 1912.

Scandent shrub, 10–15 m tall. Stems spreading brown hirsute. Petiole 3–10 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate to suborbicular, rarely oblong, 7–18 × 4–13 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, dull yellow hirsute on both surfaces. Cymes capitate, dense, many‑flowered; peduncle 6 – 15 cm, spreading hirsute; bracts persistent, elliptic to lanceolate, 1.5–4 cm, both ends acute, hirsute abaxially. Pedicel short or absent. Sepals long‑ovate to broadly lanceolate, apex acuminate, densely hirsute abaxially, outer 3 sepals ca. 1.5 cm, inner 2 sepals 1–1.2 cm. Corolla pink to reddish purple, funnelform, 4–5 cm, hirsute abaxially; limb shallowly lobed or subentire. Stamens and pistil inclusive; filaments ca. 1.5 cm, glandular pilose basally. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, 2‑locular. Berries orange‑red, globose, ca. 8 mm in diam. Seeds 4 or fewer, ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Castle Peak, Shek Kong, Lam Tsuen. L. Gibbs 7651; Y. S. Lau 2409, 3076.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, to Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.; fruiting: Feb.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Argyreia mollis (Burm. f.) Choisy 銀背藤
Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève. 6: 421. 1833; FOC 16: 315. 1995.
Convolvulus mollis Burm. f., Fl. Indica 44, t. 17. 1768.
Argyreia championii Benth., FHK 236. 1861.
Argyreia obtecta (Choisy) C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 4(10): 186. 1883.
Lettsomia championii (Benth.) Benth. & Hook. f., Gen. Pl. 2: 879. 1876; FKH 178. 1912.
Argyreia obtusifolia auct. non Lour.: FHN 3: 494. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 120. 1979; FGD 4: 341. 2000; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.

Large twining vine, to 10 m tall. Stems densely pubescent when young. Petiole 1.5–4 cm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic to oblong, 7–11 × 2.5–7 cm, base broadly cuneate or rotund, apex shortly acuminate, acute or obtuse, adaxially sparsely strigose or glabrous, abaxially densely pale yellow pubescent. Cymes (1–)5–7‑flowered. Peduncle 2.5–3.5 cm, densely pale yellow pubescent; bracts caducous, ovate, ca. 5 mm. Pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm. Sepals unequal, densely firmly appressed pubescent abaxially, enlarged in fruit; outer 2 broadly elliptic, 8–10 mm; inner 3 oblong, slightly shorter. Corolla pale red or pale purple, broadly campanulate, 4–5 cm, midpetaline bands appressed pubescent abaxially; limb ± entire or slightly lobed. Stamens and pistil inclusive; filaments pilose at base. Ovary glabrous, 4‑locular. Berry red or orange‑red, subglobose, 0.8–1 cm in diam. Seeds 4 or fewer, black, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Glenealy, Victoria Peak, Castle Peak, Plover Cove, Lantau Island. S. T. Dunn 5147; H. C. Tang 2158; Y. S. Lau 1310.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Dense forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep. – Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Convolvulus sericeus L. (Mant. Pl. 43. 1767) was included in the synonymy of this species. If Convolvulus sericeus L. is conspecific with this species, a new combination should be made.

records.text:
Argyreia nervosa (Burm. f.) Bojer 美麗銀背藤
Hortus Maurit. 224. 1837; FRPS 64(1): 123, pl. 29: 2–3. 1979; FGD 4: 341. 2000.
Convolvulus nervosus Burm. f., Fl. Indica 48, pl. 20, fig. 1. 1768.
Argyreia speciosa (L. f.) Sweet, Hort. Brit. 289. 1827; FKH 178. 1912.
Lettsomia nervosa (Burm. f.) Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 78. 1824.
Rivea nervosa (Burm. f.) Hallier f., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 381. 1897.

Vine. Stems densely white pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole shorter than or as long as leaves, tomentose; leaf blade ovate to orbicular, 10–30 × 8–25 cm, base cordate, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous adaxially, white or greyish white pubescent abaxially. Cymes many‑flowered. Peduncle to 20 cm or longer, tomentose. Bracts large, ovate to elliptic, caducous. Pedicels short, angular. Sepals subequal, ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–2 cm, apex obtuse or acute, tomentose abaxially. Corolla pink, tubular‑funnelform, ca. 6 cm; limb shallowly lobed, midpetaline bands pubescent. Stamens and pistil inclusive; filaments pilose at base. Ovary glabrous, 4‑locular. Berries subglobose, 1–1.5 cm.

Locality: Green Island (probably cultivated). Y. W. Lam 1211; F. W. Xing 9491.
Distribution: Guangdong; India, Bengaladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Arisaema cordatum N. E. Br. 心檐南星
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 177. 1903; FKH 288. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 163, pl. 31: 4 – 5. 1979; FGD 9: 206. 2009; FOC 23: 61. 2010.
Arisaema brevistipitatum Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 13(1): 19. 1934.

Perennial slender herb; tuberous rhizome globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam. Leaves solitary, bipinnatifid-pedate; petiole slender, 10–30 cm; leaflets (5–)7, sessile, oblong, 7–10 × 1.5–3 cm, broadly cuneate at base, apex acute to abruptly acuminate. Peduncle slender, 2–4.5 cm. Spathe violet when dried, tube funnelform, 3–3.5 cm, throat margins broadly auriculate; limb triangular-ovate, apex acuminate. Spadix unisexual: male portion shortly stipitate, synandria composed of 2 anthers, anthers globose, dehiscing by apical pores; appendage 15–27 cm, lower portion fusiform, exceeding from throat then narrowed into filiform and hanging.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. HK sheet 33108, 35025.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forest and thickets. Flowering: Apr.
Notes: The holotype specimen (A. B. Westland 92, K) was collected by A. B. Westland from Tai Mo Shan in 1887.

Arisaema erubescens (Wall.) Schott 一把傘南星
Melet. Bot. 17. 1832; FRPS 13(2): 189, pl. 37: 1 – 8. 1979; FYN 2: 830, fig. 220: 1–8. 1979; FFJ 6: 425, fig. 386. 1995; FGD 9: 207. 2009; FOC 23: 67. 2010.
Arum erubescens Wall., Pl. Asia. Rar. 2: 30, t. 135. 1831.
Arisaema consanguineum Schott, Bonplandia (Hanover) 7: 27. 1859; FKH 288. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 673. 2000.

Perennial herb; tuberous rhizome depressed globose. Leaf 1–2, radiately 9–15(–20)-foliolate; petiole, 40–80(–120) cm, basal 1/3–1/2 sheathing; leaflets lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate to elliptic, usually 1 upward, the others radiately spreading. Peduncle shorter than petiole, erect. Spathe green to dark purple, with stripes or not, slightly recurved at mouth; tube cylindrical, 4–8 cm, auriculate at mouth limb oblong-ovate, acuminate with a filiform tail to 12–14 cm. Plants dioecious: male spadix 2–2.5cm, flowers dense; female spadix ca. 2 cm; appendage clavate, erect, 2–4.5 cm. Berries red when mature, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. HK sheet 29667, 33667.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China (except Nei Mongol, Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning, Xinjiang); India, Nepal, Sikkim, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May – Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Arisaema heterophyllum Blume 異葉天南星
Rumphia 1: 110. 1835; FRPS 13(2): 157, pl. 30: 1–3. 1979; FYN 2: 822, fig. 218: 1 – 3. 1979; FFJ 6: 428, fig. 389. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 675. 2000; FGD 9: 205, fig. 118. 2009; FOC 23: 60. 2010.
Arisaema kwangtungensis Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 15(3): 228 – 229. 1919[1920].

Perennial herb; tuberous rhizome depressed globose, 2–4 cm in diam. Leaf usually 1–2, pedately compound; petiole glaucous, 30–60 cm, basal 3/4 sheathing; leaflets 11–19(–21), oblanceolate, oblong or linear-oblong, cuneate at base, apex acuminate; terminal one shorter than the others. Peduncle usually longer than petiole. Spathe tube cylindrical, 3–8 cm, glaucous externally, whitish green internally, throat slightly recurved; limb ovate to ovatelanceolate, 5–11 × 3–5 cm, apex acuminate, dark green to pale green. Bisexual spadix: female portion 1–2.2 cm, at the base; male portion 1.5–3.2 cm, higher up, ending in appendage. Unisexual spadix: male portion 3–5 cm; appendage elongate, filiform. Ovaries globose, style distinct, stigma punctate, ovules 3–4. Synandria stalked, anthers 2–3, dehiscing by apical slits. Berries yellowish red or red, cylindrical, usually with a single clavate seed.

Locality: Sunset Peak. HK sheet 32931, 34879.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW region and Xizang; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Arisaema penicillatum N. E. Br. 畫筆南星
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 18: 248, t. 5. 1880; FKH 288. 1912; FHN 4: 140. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 123, pl. 23: 11 – 13. 1979; FYN 2: 804, fig. 216: 11 – 13. 1979; FGD 9: 204. 2009; FOC 23: 48. 2010.
Arisaema laminatum auct. non Blume: FHK 342. 1861.

Perennial herb; tuberous rhizome subglobose. Leaves 2; petioles 25–30 cm, basal 1/2 sheathing; leaf blade 3-partite; lobes ovatelanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 8–14 cm, oblique at the base, apex acuminate and aristate, the central one petiolulate, lateral ones almost sessile. Peduncle usually shorter than petiole; spathe tube pale green, 4 cm, convolute; limb pale green to white, broadly ovate and ending in a fine and long (12–25 mm) point. Spadix unisexual or bisexual: female portion pyramidal, green, ca. 1 cm; male portion long conical, sparsely bearing male flowers; appendage filiform, 3–5 cm, covered with filiform or subulate neuter flowers at apex. Synandria of 3 stamens; anthers ovate, opening by longitudinal apical slits. Ovaries ovoid, apex constructed into a short style, stigma capitate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak. HK sheet 7727, 34081.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jun.
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected by Harland, Hance, Urquhart, Lamont and C. Ford between 1840s and 1880. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Aristida chinensis Munro 華三芒草
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts. 4: 363. 1860; FHK 427. 1861; FKH 325. 1912; FHN 4: 371, fig. 1182. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 115. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 366. 2000; FOC 22: 454. 2006; FGD 9: 343, fig. 163. 2009.
Aristida formosana Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 41: 379. 1927.

Perennial herb, 30–60 cm tall. Culms densely tufted, erect, glabrous, unbranched. Leaf blades involute, filiform, curling when dry, 10–20 cm × 1–1.5 mm, abaxial surface smooth, adaxial surface pubescent; ligule a fringe of hairs, ca. 0.2–0.5 mm. Panicle ovate in outline, open, loose, 1/3 to 1/2 length of plant; branches 3–15 cm, divaricate, solitary or in small widely spaced groups along central axis, bearded in axils, strongly scabrid, lower part naked. Spikelets ca. 8 mm, 1-flowered, grey-green to purple; glumes linear-lanceolate, subleathery, 1–3-veined, acuminate-mucronate, unequal, lower one 8–14 mm, scabrid on vein, the upper one shorter and smooth; callus ca. 0.5 mm; lemma 5–8 mm, terete, smooth, margin slightly inrolled; awn branches arising directly from lemma apex, central branch 1–1.5 cm, laterals slightly shorter or subequal to central branch; palea minute, linear-lanceolate, papery, 2–keeled, ca. 1.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. P. H. But 157; HK sheet 8619, 30744.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Aristida cumingiana Trin. & Rupr. 黃草毛（黃毛草）
Sp. Gram. Stipac. 141. 1842; FKH 325. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 119, pl. 37: 1–2. 1990; FOC 22: 453. 2006; FGD 9: 343. 2009.

Annual herb, 6–20 cm tall. Culms slender, erect from geniculate base, branched. Leaf blades linear, involute, 2.5–10 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface hairy; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, inconspicuous. Panicle oblong to ovate in outline, loose, open, 5–10 cm; branches slender, ascending, in pairs or 3 together along main axis; pedicel long. Spikelets 3–3.5 mm, green or purple; glumes unequal, 1-veined, scabrid on vein, apex acuminate-mucronate, lower glume lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, upper glume narrowly lanceolate-oblong, 2.8–3.5 mm; callus small, broadly obtuse; lemma 1.7–2 mm, upper part scabrid; awn arising directly from lemma apex, stiffly spreading, central branch 5–8 mm, laterals about half as long.

Locality: Aberdeen (fide FKH 325. 1912).
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal, Indonesia, Philippines, New Guinea, N Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Hillslopes, dry grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Aristolochia championii Merr. & Chun 長葉馬兜鈴
Sunyatsenia 5: 47. 1940; FGD 1: 55, fig. 54. 1987; FRPS 24: 219, pl. 51: 7–9. 1988; FOC 5: 264. 2004.
Aristolochia longifolia Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 116. 1854, non A. longlifolia Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 490. 1832; FHK 333. 1861; FKH 219. 1912.
Aristolochia compressicaulis Z. L. Yang in J. Wuhan Bot. Res., 6(1): 32. 1988, nom. inval.

Woody vine; tubers fusiform, 3–5 cm in diam. Stems terete, densely pubescent with rusty soft hairs. Petiole 1–2.5 cm, densely villous; leaf blade leathery, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 15–25 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base rounded or shallowly cordate, apex narrowly acuminate, entire, subglabrous adaxially, densely brown villous abaxially, veins pinnate, 5–10 pairs. Flowers solitary or in 2–5-flowered racemes. Pedicel 3–4 cm, pendulous, brown villous; bracts small, lanceolate. Perianth yellow, with reddish brown veins; tube geniculately curved, abaxially villous; limb discoid, 4–6 cm in diam., 3-lobed, adaxially papillate; lobes broadly rounded, slightly unequal. Anthers ellipsoid, ca. 3 mm. Gynostemium 3-lobed. Capsule ellipsoid, ca. 6 × 3 cm, dehiscing basipetally. Seeds ovoid, ca. 5 × 3 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, High West, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1631; HK Sheet 34401.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion in 1848 to 1849. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

records.text:
Aristolochia fordiana Hemsl. 福氏馬兜鈴（通城虎）
J. Bot. 23: 286. 1885; FKH 219. 1912; FGD 1: 48, fig. 46. 1987; FRPS 24: 231, pl. 55: 5– 8. 1988; FOC 5: 266. 2004.

Herbaceous vine; tubers terete, slender. Stems 6-angled, glabrous. Petiole 2–4 cm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery or thinly leathery, ovatecordate or ovate-triangular, 10–12 × 5–8 cm, base cordate, apex long-acuminate, glabrous adaxially, densely puberulous abaxially, veins palmate, 5–7 from base, reticulation of veins conspicuous. Racemes 3- or 4-flowered, 3–5 cm, or flowers solitary. Pedicel ca. 0.8 cm; bracts subulate to lanceolate-ovate. Perianth yellowish green; tube rectilinear or slightly curved, abaxially glabrous; utricle globose, ca. 3.5 mm in diam., sessile; tube ca. 15 × 2 mm; limb unilateral, ligulate, ovate-oblong, 1–1.5 ×0.5 cm. Anthers ellipsoid, ca. 0.3 mm. Ovary ellipsoid, ca. 5 mm. Gynostemium 6-lobed. Capsule ellipsoid or obovoid, 1.5–2 cm in diam., dehiscing acropetally. Seeds ovoid, ca. 5 × 5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. HK Sheet 10460, 34033.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest, thickets, crevices of rocks. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by A. B. Westland from Tai Mo Shan.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by A. B. Westland from Tai Mo Shan.

records.text:
Aristolochia tagala Chamisso 印度馬兜鈴（耳葉馬兜鈴）
Linnaea 7: 207, pl. 5, fig. 3. 1832; FKH 219. 1912; FGD 1: 50, fig. 47. 1987; FRPS 24: 243, pl. 60: 1–5. 1988; FOC 5: 269. 2003.
Aristolochia roxburghiana Klotzsch, Monatsber. Konigl. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin 1859: 596. 1859.

Herbaceous vine; tubers terete, more than 1 m, 3 –5 cm in diam. Stems terete, slightly furrowed, glabrous. Petiole 2–5.4 cm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, ovate-cordate or oblong-ovate, 8–12(–24) × 4–14(–20) cm, base deeply cordate, apex short-acuminate, both surfaces glabrous, veins palmate, 5 from base. Racemes 2- or 3-flowered, 2– 6 cm. Pedicels ca. 1 cm; bracts ovate-lanceolate. Perianth pale yellowish or greenish; tube rectilinear or slightly curved; utricle globose, 5– 8 mm in diam.; limb ligulate, oblong, 2–3 × 0.6 cm. Anthers ovoid, ca. 1 mm. Gynostemium 6-lobed. Capsule obovoid-globose to ovoid-cylindric, 3–5.5 × 2–3.5 cm, dehiscing acropetally. Seeds subcordiform, ca. 8 × 8 mm.

Locality: Tai Po, Fanling, Ho Chung. Also cultivated. P. S. Choi 399; HK Sheet 33864.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Aristolochia thwaitesii Hook. f. 海邊馬兜鈴（田氏馬兜鈴）
Bot. Mag. 82: t. 4918. 1856; FKH 220. 1912; FGD 1:57, fig. 57. 1987; FRPS 24: 225. 1988; FOC 5: 265. 2003 .

Erect subshrub; tubers ellipsoid or terete, up to 10 cm or longer, ca. 7 cm in diam. Stems up to 70 cm, terete, villous. Petioles ca. 1 cm, villous; leaf blade leathery, spathulate, narrowly oblanceolate, or oblong-oblanceolate, 10–15 × 2.5–3 cm, base attenuate to subcuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, subglabrous adaxially, densely brown-villous abaxially, veins pinnate, 12–16 pairs. Racemes arising from the base of plant, 3–7-flowered, up to 8 cm. Pedicel ca. 3 cm, recurved, villous; bracts lanceolate, villous. Perianth yellow-green; tube geniculately curved, densely brown villous abaxially; basal portion of tube 1.5–2.5 × 0.5–1.0 cm; limb subcylindric to conic, symmetric, 1.5–3 cm in diam., 5– or 6– dentate. Anthers ellipsoid, ca. 2 mm. Gynostemium 3-lobed. Capsule ovoid-globose, 3.5 × 2–2.5 cm, dehiscing basipetally. Seeds ovoid, ca. 4 × 3 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Wong Nai Chung Gap, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 8273; Y. W. Lam 1633.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thickets, bamboo forests and crevices of rocks. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

records.text:
Aristolochia westlandii Hemsl. 香港馬兜鈴（威氏馬兜鈴）
J. Bot. 23: 286. 1885; FKH 219. 1912; FGD 1: 54, fig. 53. 1987;FRPS 24: 217, pl. 51: 1–3. 1988; FOC 5: 263. 2003.

Woody vine; tubers fusiform, 3 –5 cm in diam., usually moniliform. Stems terete, densely villous. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, slightly hairy; leaf blade leathery or papery, narrowly lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 12–20 × 2–5 cm, base narrowly auriculate, apex acute, glabrous adaxially, sparsely villous abaxially, glaucous, veins pinnate, 8–12 pairs. Flowers solitary, axillary, on leafy shoots or on old woody stems. Pedicels pendulous, 7–12 cm, villous. Perianth yellow with purple veins and blotches, 10–15 cm; tube geniculately curved, villous abaxially; basal portion of tube 5–6 × 1.5–2 cm; limb discoid, 8–13 cm in diam., shallowly 3-lobed or emarginate; lobes broadly rounded, slightly unequal. Anthers ellipsoid, 4.5– 5 mm. Gynostemium 3-lobed. Capsule ovoid, hexagonous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1639; HK Sheet 23776.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by A. B. Westland from Tai Mo Shan around 1880. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

Cleome viscosa L. 黃花草臭屎菜）
Sp. Pl. 672. 1753; FHN 1: 344. 1964; FGD 1: 81, fig. 86. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 2: 739, pl. 348, photo 329. 1996; FRPS 32: 537, pl. 135. 1999.
Polanisia viscosa DC., Prodr. 1: 242. 1824; FHK 17. 1861; FKH 35. 1912.

Annual herb, 30 –100 cm tall, covered with short glandular hairs and disagreeably scented. Leaves digitately compound; petioles (1–)2– 4 (– 6) cm; leaflets 3 –5(–7), subsessile, blade obovate to obovate-oblong, the middle one larger, 1–5 × 0.5 – 1.5 cm, margin entire, ciliate. Flowers solitary in axils of gradually reduced upper leaves, in appearance of a terminal raceme. Bract leafy, 3-lobed. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm. Sepals narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate-elliptic, 6 –7 ×1–3 mm. Petals yellow, narrowly obovate or spathulate, 7–12 × 3 –5 mm, without claw. Stamens 10–22(–30), inserted on disc. Gynophore none. Ovary cylindrical, ca. 8 mm, with viscid glandular hairs; style very short. Capsule cylindrical, 4 –10 cm.

Locality: Wan Chai, Wong Chuk Hang, Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 118; Y. W. Lam 1548; HK sheet 189.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Waste places. Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artabotrys hexapetalus (L. f.) Bhandari 鷹爪花
Baileya 12: 149. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 122, pl. 55. 1979; FGD 2: 31. 1991; FYN 5: 44. 1991.
Annona hexapetala L. f., Suppl. Pl. 270. 1782.
Artabotrys uncinatus (Lam.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci., C. 7: 234. 1912; FHN 1: 238, fig. 115. 1964.
Artabotrys odoratissimus R. Br. in Edward, Bot. Reg. 5: fig. 423. 1819; FHK 10. 1861; FKH 30. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches glabrous. Leaves subleathery; petioles 4 – 6 × 1.2 – 1.9 mm, without transverse ribs; leaf blades ca. 9– 16 × 3 – 6 cm, oblong, lanceolate or narrowly elliptical, glabrous, base cuneate, apex short acuminate; midvein impressed or flush adaxially; secondary veins 9– 12( – 14) pairs. Inflorescences ± leaf-opposed, 1 – 2-flowered. Flowers pale green or yellow; pedicels ca. 12 × 2 – 4 mm. Sepals 4.5– 7 × 3.5 – 5 mm, triangular, basally connate, puberulous abaxially. Petals oblong or ovate-lanceolate, pubescent; outer petals ca. 22– 28 × 7 mm; inner petals 22–24 × 4– 6 mm. Stamens numerous, ca. 1.5 mm long; connective peltate and prominent. Carpels 11–20 per flower; stigma ovoid. Monocarps 3 – 5( – 7) per fruit, 2.5 – 4 × 2.5 cm, ovoid, apiculate, glabrous; pedicel ca. 2 cm long; stipes ca. 1 – 3.5 mm long. Seeds 1– 2 per monocarp, blackish-grey.

Locality: Cultivated. L. Chau s.n. (HKU); L. T. Lo 235; Y. S. Lau 3250.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan. Widely distributed in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Lowland areas. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb.
Uses: Flowers used for perfumes in India, roots used medicinally.
records.uses: Flowers used for perfumes in India, roots used medicinally.

records.text:
Artabotrys hongkongensis Hance 香港鷹爪花
J. Bot. 8: 71. 1870; FKH 30. 1912; FHN 1: 239. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 125, fig. 56: 1–9. 1979; FGD 2: 31, fig. 25: 5–8. 1991; FYN 5: 45. 1991.
Artabotrys blumei Hook. f. & Thomson, Fl. Ind. 1: 128. 1855, p.p.; FHK 10. 1861.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches sparsely pubescent. Leaves sub-leathery; petioles 1.5–3(–4.5) × 1–1.4 mm, with transverse ribs; leaf blades ca. 6.5– 10 × 3 cm, oblong or obovate, glabrous, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acuminate; midvein flush or prominent adaxially; secondary veins 5– 7 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 1-flowered. Flowers whitish to yellow; pedicels (6.5–)8 –13.5 × 0.5–0.8 mm. Sepals 3.5–5 × 3.5–4 mm, triangular, basally connate, pubescent abaxially. Petals oblong, pubescent abaxially; outer petals 6.5– 11(–13.5) × 2–6.5 mm; inner petals 8–12 × 2.5–6 mm, with strongly concave claw. Stamens numerous, ca. 1.7 mm long; connective peltate and prominent. Carpels 7–10 per flower; stigma clavate. Monocarps (1–)2 – 3(– 5) per fruit, 2–3.5 × 1.5–3 cm, ovoid, apiculate, glabrous; pedicel ca. 2 cm long; stipes ca. 3–3.5 mm long. Seeds 1–2 per monocarp, black.

Locality: Tai Tam, Nam Fung Road, Lantau Peak. C. L. Law et al. 00/12 (HKU); L. T. Lo 341; Y. S. Lau 2802.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from “Buddhist Temple, East Point” (now Causeway Bay) by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Artemisia annua L. 黃花蒿
Sp. Pl. 1: 847. 1753; FHK 187. 1861; FKH 147. 1912; FRPS 76(2): 62. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 834, pl. 386. 1998; FGD 8: 204, fig. 122. 2007.

Annual herbs, strongly aromatic; stem 70–150(–200) cm tall, branched above, initially puberulous, glabrescent. Lowermost cauline leaves ovate to triangular‑ovate in outline, 3–7 × 2–6 cm, 3(–4)‑pinnately parted, segments 5–8(–10) pairs, ultimate lobes deeply serrate, teeth triangular, 1–2 × 0.5 mm, Median cauline leaves 2(– 3)‑pinnately and pectinately parted; petiole 1–2 cm. Upper leaves 1(–2)‑pinnately parted. Capitula globose, numerous, 1.5–2.5 mm in diam., shortly pedunculate and with leafy bracts, arranged as pyramid‑shaped paniculate inflorescences. Involucres with 3–4 series of phyllaries, with green midvein, margin broadly scarious; outer layer oblong‑ovate to narrowly elliptic; middle and inner layers broadly ovate to ovate. Receptacle small, convex. Marginal pistillate florets 10–18, corolla filiform‑tubular, apex minutely 2–3‑lobed, glandular abaxially; style much longer than the corolla tube and conspicuously exserted, bifid. Disk bisexual florets 10–30, corolla tubular; anther linear, apical appendages elongate‑triangular; style slightly longer than the corolla. Cypselae small, ellipsoidal‑ovoid, slightly compressed. Pappus none.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 2668.
Distribution: Widely spread over Eurasia, from E Europe to Caucasus, Asia Minor, E Siberia and China, and widely naturalized.
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia capillaris Thunb. 茵陳蒿
Fl. Jap. 309. 1784; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 126. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 216. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 837. 1998; FGD 8: 209. 2007.
Artemisia scoparia auct. non Waldst.: Check List HK Plants 68. 1993.

Annual or biennial herbs or subshrubs, aromatic; stem 30–150 cm tall, reddish brown or brown, faintly striate, base woody, branched above, silky pubescent or glabrescent. Basal and lower leaves ovate or elliptic, 2–5 × 1.5–3 cm, 2(–3)‑pinnatisect, with 2–3 pairs of primary lateral segments, ultimate lobules straightly linear or linear‑lanceolate, 5–10 × 0.5–2 mm, both surfaces densely silky pubescent, usually withered at anthesis. Median leaves ovate or elliptic, 2–4 × 1.5–3 cm, (1–)2‑pinnatisect, leaf lobes straightly linear‑filiform, 5–15 × 0.3–1 mm, base subsessile, apex acute, subglabrous. Upper leaves 3‑ or 5‑sect. Capitula many, ovoid to ellipsoidal, 2 – 3 × 1.3–2 mm, shortly pedunculate, with small linear bracts at base, arranged as racemose panicles. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, pale yellow with a green line at midvein, glabrous, margin scarious; outer ones small ovate, 1–1.3 mm; middle and inner layers ovate‑oblong, 1.5–2 mm. Peripheral florets 6–10, female and fertile, corolla conical‑tubular, 0.6 – 0.7 mm long, apically 2–3‑lobed, glandular on abaxial side; style divided, branches long and exserted, acute. Central florets 3–7, bisexual but infertile, corolla ellipsoidal‑tubular, 1.5–1.8 mm, 5‑lobed at apex, abaxially glandular; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular; style short, clavate form, apex swollen, slightly bifid or not, ovary vestigial. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, length 0.8 – 1 mm, without pappus.

Locality: Sai Kung, Port Island, Tai A Chau, Ping Chau. P. S. Choi 469; Y. W. Lam 288; S. Y. Hu 8733 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Liaoning, Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Philippines, Cochinchina via Malaysia to Indonesia.
Ecology: Coastal grasslands. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia indica Willd. 五月艾
Sp. Pl. 3: 1846. 1800; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 136. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 117. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 839. 1998; FGD 8: 206, fig. 123. 2007.
Artemisia vulgaris auct. non L.: FHK 187. 1861; FKH 147. 1912.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, strongly aromatic; stem 30–120 cm tall, branched above, reddish brown, striate, base glabrescent, upper part arachnoid. Basal leaves withered at anthesis, ovate to ovate‑oblong in outline, (1–)2‑pinnatisect, primary lobes elliptic, terminal one largest, lateral ones 3–4 pairs, midvein winged. Median cauline leaves similar, ovate, ovate‑oblong or elliptic, 4–9 × 2–5.5 cm, 1–2‑pinnatisect, lobes elliptic lanceolate, linear‑lanceolate to linear, base falsely stipulate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire, coarsely serrate or lobed, terminal segment largest, 1.5–4 cm long, lateral ones 3–4 pairs, 1–2.5 cm. Upper leaves pinnately parted, with lateral lobes 1–3 pairs, or undivided and appeared as linear‑lanceolate in shape. Leaf upper surfaces loosely cobwebby or glabrescent, lower surfaces densely covered with greyish arachnoid woolly hair. Capitula ovoid to oblong‑ovoid, numerous, 2.5–4 × 2–2.5 mm, shortly pedunculate and with leafy bracts, arranged as leafy spike‑like to racemose panicles. Involucres with 3–4 series of phyllaries, woolly hairy, with green midvein, margin broadly scarious; outer layer ovate and obtuse, 1.5 mm; middle and inner layers elliptic oblong to oblong, apex rounded, 2–3 mm. Receptacle small, convex. Marginal pistillate florets 4–8, corolla filiform‑tubular, about 1–1.2 mm, apex minutely 2–3‑lobed, glandular abaxially; style much longer than the corolla tube and conspicuously exserted, bifid, apex acute. Disk bisexual florets 8–12, corolla tubular, about 2 mm, upper half funnelform to campanulate, lower half narrowed, abaxial side glandular; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular and long‑acuminate; style slightly longer than the corolla, branched, truncate and penicillate at distal ends. Cypselae oblong, about 0.8–1 mm, truncate at both ends, faintly striate. Pappus absent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, High Island, Ping Chau, Lantau Island. H. Y. Yeung 84 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 7658 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 154.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; C & S Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands and wastelands. Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia japonica Thunb. 牡蒿
Fl. Jap. 308. 1784; FHK 186. 1861; FKH 147. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 233. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 241. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 839. 1998; FGD 8: 210. 2007.

Perennial aromatic herbs; stem 40–130 cm tall, striate, purplish brown or brown, branched at upper portion, puberulous and later glabrescent. Leaves subsessile or sessile, loosely puberulous or glabrous on both sides. Basal and lower leaves obovate or spatulate, 4–5.5 × 1.5–2 cm, apex rounded and irregularly toothed, usually withered at flowering stage. Median leaves spatulate‑cuneate, 2–5.5 × 0.4–1.5 cm, apical 1/3 incisely lobed and toothed, and / or obliquely pinnatifid from apex to centre, usually with small linear false stipules at base. Upper leaves smaller in size. Capitula numerous, arranged as leafy racemose panicles, shape ovoid‑ellipsoidal, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, heterogamous and disciform, sessile or with tiny peduncles. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, imbricate, abaxially glabrous, with green line along midvein, margin scarious; outer ones ovate, 1–1.2 mm, apex obtuse; middle ones ovate‑oblong, 1.5–1.8 mm, apex rounded; inner ones oblong, length about 2 mm, apex rounded, broadly scarious. Marginal pistillate florets 3–8, fertile, corolla conical‑tubular, apex 2–3‑lobed; style branched, long and exserted, acute. Central florets 5–10, bisexual but infertile, corolla ellipsoidal‑tubular; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular and long‑acuminate; style short and claviform, apex swollen, slightly divided or not, vestigial ovary inconspicuous. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, faintly striate, about 1 mm. Pappus absent.

Locality: Shing Mun, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Castle Peak, Ping Chau. L. T. Lo 185; Y. W. Lam 1134; S. Y. Hu 11290 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Liaoning, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India to Afghanistan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia lactiflora Wall. ex DC. 白苞蒿（甜菜子）
Prodr. 6: 115. 1837; FKH 147. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 238. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 174. 1991; FGD 8: 209. 2007.

Perennial aromatic herbs 50–100 cm tall; stem striate, loosely cobwebby pubescent, glabrescent later. Basal leaves withered at flowering stage. Middle cauline leaves ovate or ovate‑elliptic, 5–9 × 4–9 cm, upper part pinnatilobed into 3 ovate to ovate‑oblong lobes, lower part pinnatisect with 1–2 pairs of lateral lobes, ovate or ovate‑oblong, the basal one smallest in size, apex usually obtuse, sometimes acute, margin serrate, both surfaces sparsely pubescent or glabrescent; petiole 1.5–5 cm. Capitula sessile, without leafy bracts at base, heterogamous and disciform, oblong to subglobose, 4–5 × 3–4.5 mm, arranged as spikes. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, semi‑membranous, glabrous abaxially; outer ones ovate, about 1.5 mm; middle and inner ones oblong, length 2.5–3 mm. Receptacle conical. All florets fertile. Marginal female florets 3 – 6, corolla narrowly tubular, about 1 mm, glandular outside, apex 2‑lobed; style long and exserted, twice the length of corolla, divided. Disk bisexual florets 4–10, corolla funnelform‑tubular, 1.8–2 mm, glandular, apex 5‑lobed; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular, long‑acuminate; style subequal in length with the corolla, shortly branched, truncate and penicillate at distal ends. Cypselae oblong, faintly striate, 0.8–1 mm. Pappus none.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po. H. Y. Yeung 526 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2635, 3033.
Distribution: Area S of Qinling Range; E & SE Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia lavandulaefolia DC. 野艾蒿
Prodr. 6: 110. 1837; FRPS 76(2): 92, pl. 12: 1 – 8. 1991; FFJ 5: 380, fig. 351. 1993; FGD 8: 205. 2007.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, 50 – 120 cm tall; stems erect, striate, densely arachnoid‑pubescent. Leaves densely tomentose abaxially, white glandular punctate and sparsely arachnoid‑pubescent adaxially. Basal and lowermost leaves long petiolate; leaf blade ovate to suborbicular, 8 – 13 × 7 – 8 cm, 2‑pinnatisect. Petiole of middle cauline leaves 1 – 2( – 3) cm; leaf blade ovate, ovate‑elliptic, or suborbicular, 6 – 8 × 5 – 7 cm, (1 or) 2‑pinnatisect; segments 2 or 3 pairs, 30 50( – 70) × 5 – 7( – 9) mm; lobules 2 or 3 pairs, lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, serrate. Uppermost leaves and leafy bracts pinnatisect or 3‑lobed or entire. Capitula numerous, ellipsoidal or oblong, 2 – 2.5 mm in diam., pedicellate or subsessile, arranged in panicles; phyllaries densely arachnoid‑tomentose. Marginal female florets 4 – 9. Disk bisexual florets 10 – 20; corolla limb purple. Cypselae oblong or obovoid.

Locality: Tsing Yi. L. T. Lo 182.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Nei Mongol, Heilongjiang, Liaoning, Jilin, Shandong, Jiangsu; Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia (Far East).
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia princeps Pamp. 魁蒿
Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital., n. s. 36(4): 444. 1930; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 153. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 120. 1991; FGD 8: 207. 2007.

Perennial herbs, 40–150 cm tall; stem purplish brown or brown, striate, branched above, cobwebby tomentose or later glabrescent. Basal leaves withered at anthesis. Middle leaves petiolate, petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, leaf blade ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 6–10 × 4–6 cm, pinnatipartite to pinnatisect, usually with 2 pairs of lateral lobes, elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, apex obtuse, margin coarsely serrate or lobed, upper surfaces loosely arachnoid to glabrous, lower surfaces densely white cobwebby tomentose. Upper leaves smaller in size, 3‑parted or undivided. Capitula heterogamous and disciform, elliptic‑ovoid, 2.5–3.5 × 1.5–2.5 mm, sessile or subsessile, with small leafy bracts at base, arranged as spikes which form panicles. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, with green line on midvein, cobwebby hairy, scarious along margin, outer ones small ovate, middle ones oblong, inner ones obovate‑oblong, semi‑membranous. Marginal female florets 5–7, corolla narrowly tubular, 2‑lobed at apex; style long and exserted, branched. Central bisexual florets 4–9, corolla tubular, 5‑lobed at apex, glandular outside; anther bases short‑acute, apical appendages elongate‑triangular; style with length subequal to corolla, divided, apex truncate and penicillate. Cypselae oblong, 1.5 mm, without pappus.

Locality: Mount Gough. Y. S. Lau 1962.
Distribution: S, SW, C & N China, Shaanxi, Gansu, Nei Mongol, Liaoning; also in Korea and Japan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Arthraxon hispidus (Thunb.) Makino 藎草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo). 26: 214. 1912; FFJ 6: 260, fig. 231. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 218, pl. 54: 1–7. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 524, pl. 221. 2000; FOC 22: 619. 2006; FGD 9: 487, fig. 257. 2009.
Phalaris hispida Thunb., Fl. Jap. 44. 1784.
Arthraxon pauciflorus Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 39: 276. 1925; FTW ed. 2, 5: 526. 2000.
Arthraxon ciliaris P. Beauv, Ess. Agrostogr. 111, pl. 11, fig. 6. 1812; FKH 321. 1912.
Arthraxon hispidus (Thunb.) Makino var. cryptatherus (Hackel) Honda, FHN 4: 474. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 221. 1997.
