Annual herb. Culms slender, glabrous, sprawling, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, 30–60 cm tall, many-branched. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous or tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades ovate-lanceolate, 2–5 0.6–1.5 cm, glabrous, pubescent or tuberculate-pilose, base amplexicaul, margins pectinate-setose at least around base; ligule membranous, margins ciliate. Racemes slender, 2–10 or more, digitate or fascicles, terminal. Sessile spikelet greyish green or purplish, ovate-lanceolate, laterally compressed; lower glume lanceolate, herbaceous, abaxially rounded, margins membranous, 6–9-veined, veins scabridhispidulous to spinulose; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as lower glume, 3-veined; lower lemma oblong, 2/3 lower glume length, hyaline membranous, acute; upper lemma as long as lower palea, hyaline membranous, with a geniculate awn near the base; awn up to 12 mm, well developed and exserted from glumes, or sometimes reduced and included. Pedicellate spikelet usually absent; pedicel reduced to a minute stump, sometimes up to 2 mm or more.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42047.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; tropical to temperate regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Shade and moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam. 菠蘿蜜
Encyl. 3: 209. 1789; FHN 2: 381. 1964; FGD 1: 182. 1987; FOC 5: 31. 2003.
Artocarpus intergrifolia auct. non L. f.: FKH 247. 1912.
Artocarpus macrocarpon Dancer, Cat. Bot. Gard. Jamaica: 1. 1792; Check List HK Plants 59. 2002, “macrocarpus”.

Tree, 10 –20 m tall; old trees buttressed. Petioles 1–3 cm; leaves spirally arranged, elliptic or obovate, 7–15 × 3 –7 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin entire (young trees or germinate shoots often divided), glabrous adaxially, slightly coarse abaxially; lateral veins 6–8 pairs. Heads on trunk or on brachyblasts. Male heads cylindric or clavate-elliptic, 2–7 cm; peduncles 1–5 cm. Syncarps yellow-brown, ellipsoid to globose, or with irregular form, 30 –100 × 25 –50 cm, with stiff hexagonal tubercles and thick hairs.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 6569, 25816.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian (cultivated); native to India, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring to summer; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit), timber, medicinal (folklore).

Artocarpus hypargyreus Hance ex Benth. 白桂木
FHK 325. 1861, “hypargyrea”; FKH 248. 1912; FHN 2: 383. 1965; FGD 1: 185. 1987; FOC 5: 33. 2003.
Ficus laceratifolia auct. non Lévl. & Van.: FKH 246. 1912.

Large tree, 10–25 m tall; bark dark purple. Young branches white pubescent. Petioles 1.5–2 cm, hairy; leaves leathery, oblong, elliptic to obovate, 8–15 × 4–7 cm, base cuneate, apex narrowacuminate, margin entire or slightly sinuate-toothed (leaves of young trees often pinnately divided), glabrous and shining adaxially, rough with powdery white tomentum abaxially; lateral veins 6–7 pairs, reticulate veins raised and pubescent. Head solitary, axillary. Male heads obovoid to ellipsoid, 1.5–2 × 1–1.5 cm; peduncles 2–4.5 cm, hairy. Male flowers: perianth 4-lobed, lobes spathulate plumosehairy, adnated to clavate or subpeltate bracts; stamen 1, anther ellipsoid. Female heads rather smaller. Female flowers: perianth densely hairy; style shortly protruding. Syncarps subglobose, 3–4 cm in diam., yellowish to orange, brown pubescent, slightly papillary on surfaces; stalk 3–5 cm; pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 587; Y. S. Lau 1958.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by H. F. Hance around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Timber, food (fruit).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by H. F. Hance around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Artocarpus nitidus Trécul subsp. lingnanensis (Merr.) F. M. Jarrett 桂木（紅桂木）
J. Arnold Arbor. 41: 124. 1960; FHN 2: 382. 1965; FGD 1: 182. 1987; FOC 5: 33. 2003.
Artocarpus lingnanensis Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 302. 1929.

Tree to 17 m tall. Bark black to brown, longitudinally fissured. Branchlets wrinkled, appressed puberulent, rapidly glabrescent. Stipules lanceolate, caducous. Petiole 0.5 –1.5 cm; leaves distichous, thinly leathery, oblong-elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 7–15 × 3 –7 cm, base cuneate to ± rounded, apex mucronate to caudate, margin entire or irregularly shallowly toothed, glabrous on both surfaces; secondary veins 6 –10 on each side of midvein, adaxially prominent. Male inflorescences capitate, obovoid, or oblong, 2.5 –12 × 2.7–7 mm. Peduncle of female inflorescences 1.5 –5 mm. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 2– 4, basally connate for 0.5 – 0.5 mm. Syncarps red when mature, ± globose, with coarse pubescence.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).

Artocarpus styracifolius Pierre 二色菠蘿蜜
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 2: 492. 1905,“styracifolia”; FHN 2: 382. 1965; FGD 1: 183. 1987; FOC 5: 32. 2003.

Tree, up to 20 m tall; young branchlets densely white pubescent. Petioles 8 –14 mm, hairy; leaves distichous, oblong or obovatelanceolate, sometimes elliptic, 4– 8 × 2.5 –3 cm, base cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex caudate, margin entire (young leaves often lobed), white powdery hairy abaxially; lateral veins 4 –7 pairs. Head axillary, solitary. Male heads elliptic, obovate or cyclindric, 6–12 × 4 –7 mm, densely white pubescent. Female heads yellow, red-brown when dry, globose, 6 –10 mm in diam. Syncarps globose, 4 cm in diam., villose, with many cylindric protuberances on surfaces; achenes globose.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang. Y. W. Lam 889; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 38342).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).

Artocarpus tonkinensis A. Chev. ex Gagnep. 胭脂樹
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 73: 90. 1926; FHN 2: 383. 1965; FGD 1: 184. 1987; FOC 5: 34. 2003.

Tree, 14 –16 m tall. Branchlets reddish-brown, adpressedly pubescent. Petioles 4–10 mm, puberulent; leaves elliptic, obovate or oblong, 8–20 × 4–10 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute, margin entire or shallowly serrate, densely puberulent abaxially; lateral veins 6 –9 pairs, midvein purple-red when dry. Heads axillary, solitary. Male heads obovoid or ellipsoid, 0.8–1.5 cm wide; peduncles shorter than head. Bracts peltate. Male flowers: perianth 2–3-lobed, ciliate; stamen 1. Female heads globose. Female flowers: perianth perfectly confluent. Syncarps yellow, subglobose, 6.5 cm in diam.; stalk 3–4 cm. Achenes ellipsoid, 12–15 × 9–12 mm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Lai Chi Wo. L. T. Lo 261.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring to summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).

Arundina graminifolia (D. Don) Hochr. 竹葉蘭
Bull. New York Bot. Gard. 6: 270. 1910; FRPS 18: 334, pl. 56: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 755, pl. 321. 2000; FGD 7: 395, fig. 201. 2006; FOC 25: 315. 2009.
Bletia graminifolia D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 29. 1825.
Arundina chinensis Blume, Bijdr. 8: 402. 1825; FHK 355. 1861; FKH 265. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 62, fig. 29. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; stems erect, grass-like and stiff, leafy, the basal portion swelling into a small ovoid pseudobulb covered by imbricate brown tough scales, the aerial portion cylindrical, covered by fresh or persistent sheaths. Leaves linear-lanceolate, thinly leathery or papery, 5–20 × 0.6 cm, base slightly narrowed and bearing cylindrical sheaths, apex acute; sheaths amplexicaul and overlapping, 2–4 cm, articulate at the apical end. Inflorescences terminal, racemose or paniculate; flowers resupinate, colourful and showy; sepals elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 2.5–4 × 0.7–0.9 cm, apex acute, pale rose-mauve; petals elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 2.5 –3.5 × 1.3–1.8 cm, rose-mauve with darker median veins; lip trumpet-shaped, 3–4 cm, embracing the column, wavy at the margin, deeply cleft at the apex, pale magenta and deepening into bright rose-purple towards the margin and apex; column slender, curved and slightly winged at the apical end; anther terminal, 2-celled; pollinia 8, discoid; ovary slender, glabrous, striate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9432, 12294A (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3135; HK sheet 34780.
Distribution: C, E, S & SW China; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy slopes or along the banks of streams in exposed areas. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Arundinella nepalensis Trin. 石芒草（石珍芒）
Gram. Panic. 62. 1826; FHK 416. 1861; FKH 318. 1912; FHN 4: 445. 1977; FFJ 6: 188, fig. 156. 1995; FRPS 10(1): 147, fig. 45: 1–3. 1990; FOC 22: 568. 2006; FGD 9: 398. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, stout, 0.6–2(–3) m tall, simple or branched, internodes usually glabrous, nodes appressed silky pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internodes except 1–2 nodes at base, glabrous or pubescent; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 10–50 × 0.5–2 cm, glabrous or thinly to densely tuberculate-pilose, base rounded, apex long acuminate; ligule dry membranous, very short. Panicle open or loosely contracted; central axis ribbed, smooth; branches slender, alternate, fasciculate or subverticillate; pedicels unequal, glabrous. Glumes usually glabrous; lower glume ovate-lanceolate, 2–4 mm, 3–5-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 4.5–5.5 mm, 5-veined; lower floret staminate or barren; upper floret bisexual, lemma awned; awn geniculate with brown twisted column.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 583; Y. W. Lam 939; HK sheet 14993.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Hubei, Fujian; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Mountain grasslands, hill thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Arundinella setosa Trin. 刺芒野古草
Gram. Panic. 63. 1826; FHK 416. 1861; FKH 318. 1912; FHN 4: 445, fig. 1236. 1977; FFJ 6: 187, fig. 155. 1995; FRPS 10(1): 163, pl. 51: 1–3. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 444, pl. 183. 2000; FOC 22: 565. 2006; FGD 9: 399. 2009.
Arundinella sinensis Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 342. 1904; FKH 318. 1912.

Perennial stout herb. Culms erect, tufted or solitary, (35–)60–190 cm tall, nodes glabrous or pubescent. Leaf sheaths glabrous or tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades linear, flat or margins slightly inrolled, 10 – 30(–70) × 0.3–1 cm, glabrous or tuberculatehispid; ligule dry membranous, ca. 0.5 mm, ciliate. Panicle open or somewhat contracted, 10–45 cm; central axis and branches scabrid; branches spreading or ascending, usually solitary; pedicels scabrid, unequal, apex usually with several white long stiff hairs. Spikelets 5–7 mm; glumes ovate-lanceolate, apex acuminate and awn-pointed, glabrous or scaberulous along veins; lower glume 4–6 mm, 3–5-veined; upper glume 5–7 mm, 5-veined; lower floret male or barren; upper floret bisexual, awned, flanked by 2 slender erect bristles; bristles mostly 1–3 mm; awn geniculate with brown twisted column, 6–10 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shatin Pass Rd., Ma Liu Shui, Ninepin Group, Lantau Island, Po Toi Islands. Y. W. Lam 1059; HK sheet 41946, 42042.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over India, Indochina through Malay Peninsula to Indonesia, Philippines, New Guinea and Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Arundo donax L. 蘆竹
Sp. Pl. 1: 81. 1753; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 367. 1977; FFJ 6: 130, fig. 101. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 326, pl. 123. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 20. 2002; FOC 22: 448. 2006; FGD 9: 339. 2009.

Perennial, reed-like herb, 2–6 m tall. Culms stout, erect, 1–3 cm in diam., often with slender branches from upper nodes. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, flat, 30–60 × 2–5 cm, base rounded or cordate, amplexicaul, margins scabrous; ligule ca. 2 mm, fimbriate on upper margin, siliceous on dorsal side; leaf sheaths longer than internodes, usually glabrous except hairy at mouth. Panicle 30–70 × 5–8(10) cm, usually purplish, densely branched; branches 10–25 cm, ascending, axes strigose at nodes. Spikelets terete, 10–15 mm, 2–5-flowered; glumes subequal, (8–)10–13 mm, lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, papery, siliceous, 3–5-veined, apex acute or with short awn; lower glume covered with a few silky hairs abaxially; lemma linear-lanceolate, (6–)8–13 mm, 3–7-veined, midvein prolonged into ca. 3 mm awn, 2 lateral veins also shortly extended, basal part densely covered with long silky hairs which are nearly as long as lemma; palea ca. 1/2 length of lemma, 2-keeled, margins ciliate, apex truncate; lodicules 2, truncate, veined. Stamens 3, anthers ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Siu Lek Yuen, Chuen Lung, Peng Chau. Y. S. Lau 2538; L. Y. Lo 363; HK sheet 41736.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); Asia-Temperate, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, N Africa, cultivated and naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: River banks and other damp places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, fuel (potential biomass for energy generation).
records.uses: Ornamental, fuel (potential biomass for energy generation).

records.text:
Asarum hongkongense S. M. Hwang & T. P. Wong Siu 香港細辛
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 28: 406. 1990; FOC 5: 252. 2003.

Perennial herb. Rhizomes horizontal, ca. 3 mm in diam. Leaves solitary; petiole 12–30 cm, glabrous; leaf blade nearly leathery, ovate-cordate to ovate, 6 –11 × 5 – 8 cm, base deeply cordate, basal lobes semi-orbicular, apex acute or apiculate, margin entire, shining adaxially, both surfaces glabrous; basal veins 7, impressed adaxially and elevated abaxially. Peduncle ascending, 1.5–4 cm. Perianth purple-green, campanulate-urceolate, ca. 2 × 2.5 cm; perianth-lobes connate beyond attachment to ovary, glabrous abaxially; tube broadly ovoid to subglobose, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 cm, slightly constricted at throat, adaxially longitudinally papillate-rugose, orifice ring inconspicuous; lobes broadly ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1.2 cm, base with purple papillate-corrugate area; lateral lobes erect or spreading. Stamens 12; filaments much shorter than anthers; connectives slightly extended beyond anthers, obtuse. Ovary subsuperior; styles connate, apex with 6, erect, slightly 2-cleft arms; stigmas subterminal.

Locality: Sunset Peak. P. Chow s.n. (HK sheet 34402).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by P. Chow from Lantau Island in 1983. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by P. Chow from Lantau Island in 1983. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Asclepias curassavica L. 馬利筋（蓮生桂子花）
Sp. Pl. 1: 215. 1753; FHK 225. 1861; FKH 170. 1912; FRPS 63. 388, pl. 141. 1977; FGD 1: 511, fig. 582. 1987; FOC 16: 203. 1995.

Perennial herbs to 1 m tall. Stems pale grey, puberulent to glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles to 1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, 6–15 × 1–4 cm, base decurrent to petiole, apex acuminate or acute, glabrous or abaxially puberulent along veins. Cymes up to as long as leaves, 10–20‑flowered; peduncle 3.5 – 6 cm, pubescent. Pedicels 1.2–1.5 cm, pubescent. Sepals lanceolate, 3 × 1 mm, pubescent. Corolla purple or red, 7 – 9 mm; lobes oblong, 5–8 × 3 mm, reflexed. Corona lobes yellow or orange, 3.5 – 4 mm; gynostegium 2.5 – 3 mm. Follicles fusiform, 5–10 × 1–1.5 cm. Seeds ovate, 6–7 × 3 mm; coma 2 – 4 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. C. P. Lau 59; H. C. Tang 398; Y. S. Lau 235.
Distribution: Native to tropical America, widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Asparagus cochinchinensis (Lour.) Merr. 天門冬
Fl. Indo-Chine 6: 780. 1908, et Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 230. 1919; FRPS 15: 106, pl. 33: 6 – 7. 1978; FOC 24: 211. 2000; FGD 6: 341, fig. 196. 2005.
Asparagus lucidus Lindl., Edwards's Bot. Reg. 7: 29. 1844; FHK 371. 1861; FKH 278. 1912.
Asparagus sinicus (Miq.) C. H. Wright, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(250): 103. 1903; FKH 278. 1912.
Asparagopsis sinica Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 90. 1861.
Melanthium cochinchinense Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 216. 1790.

Perennial herb. Roots cord-like, often swollen or with tuberous part at end. Stems straggling or half-climbing, 1–2 m, often woody at base, much branched, with short frequently reflexed prickles under most of the branches. Cladodes usually in fascicles of 3, subfalcate, 0.5–8 cm × 1–2 mm, flat or slightly 3-angled. Flowers small, dioecious, 1–2(–8) in axillary cluster; pedicels 2–6 mm, articulate at middle. Male flowers: perianth segments 6, free, green or greenish white, obovate-oblanceoate, 2–3 mm; stamens 6, adnate to the base of perianth segments, included, anthers ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm; pistillode very small. Female flowers with staminode, ovary ca. 2 mm; style very short. Berry green, 6–7 mm in diam., 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 145; HK sheet 35876.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Margins of forests, roadsides in ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Aspidistra fimbriata F. T. Wang & K. Y. Lang 流蘇蜘蛛抱蛋
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(1): 76. 1978; FRPS 15: 22, pl. 7: 1–3. 1978; FOC 24: 245. 2000; FGD 6: 366. 2005.
Aspidistra lurida auct. non Ker Gawl.: FKH 279. 1912.

Perennial herb. Rhizome horizontal, subterete, 5–6 mm thick. Leaves solitary, 3–4 cm spaced; petiole 25–35 cm, stiff; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 30–45 × 3.5–6 cm, basally gradually narrowed, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes minutely serrulate. Scape 3–10 mm; bracts 4–5. Flower solitary. Perianth campanulate, tube 7–9 mm, 1–1.5 cm in diam., 8–10-lobed apically; lobes ovate-deltoid slightly spreading, 6–8 × 3.5–5 mm, purple speckled abaxially, pink and with 4 fleshy, fimbriate keels adaxially. Stamens 8–10, inserted proximally in perianth tube, subsessile; anthers broadly ovate, ca. 1.8 mm. Pistil ca. 4 mm; stigma purple, peltate, large, ca. 7 mm in diam., 4-lobed at margin, lobes emarginate at apex.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker. HK sheet 7600.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests along ravines. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Aspidistra lurida Ker Gawl. 九龍盤
Bot. Reg. 8: pl. 628. 1822; FKH 279. 1912; FRPS 15: 19. 1978; FOC 24: 246. 2000; FGD 6: 366. 2005.
Aspidistra elatior auct. non Blume: FKH 279. 1912; Check List HK Plants 125. 2004.
Aspidistra punctata auct. non Lindl.: FKH 279. 1912.

Perennial herb. Rhizome horizontal, terete, to 8 mm thick. Leaves solitary, 1–2 cm spaced; petioles 10–30 cm, stiff; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 15–40 × 3–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire. Scape 1–3 cm, arching; bracts 3–4, broadly ovate, 7–8 mm, dark reddish, membranous. Flower solitary, nodding. Perianth campanulate, 10 – 15 mm, apex 6 – 8-lobed, purplish red abaxially, dark purple adaxially; tube 5–8 mm, 6–10 mm in diam.; lobes ovate-deltoid, spreading, 5–7 mm, with 2–4 papillose keels near the base adaxially. Stamens 6(–8), inserted proximally in perianth tube, subsessile. Pistil equalling perianth tube; ovary speckled with purple; stigma peltate, orbicular, 5–8 mm in diam., strongly convex, inconspicuously 4-lobed at margin, lobes entire at apex.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap. HK sheet 7603, 7604, 24985.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.

Aspidistra minutiflora Stapf 小花蜘蛛抱蛋


J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 113. 1903; FKH 279. 1912; FRPS 15: 22, pl. 8: 5 – 6. 1978; FOC 24: 250. 2000; FGD 6: 365, fig. 218. 2005. Perennial herb. Rhizome horizontal, subterete, 5–6 mm thick. Leaves 2–3-tufted, borne on nodes of rhizome; leaf blade linear, rarely lorate to lorate-oblanceolate, 26–65 × 1–2.5 cm, basally gradually narrowed into inconspicuous petiole, apex acuminate, parallel-veined, midvein distinct, margin entire or distally serrulate. Scape solitary, slender, 1–2.5 cm; bracts 2–4, broadly ovate. Flower solitary, terminal. Perianth urceolate, green, tinged and speckled with purple, 4.5–5 × 4–6 mm, ± fleshy; apex shallowly 4–6-lobed; lobes erect, deltoid, 1–2 × 1–1.5 mm. Stamens (4–)6, inserted at base of perianth tube, subsessile; anthers nearly broadly ovate, ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary 3-locular; style short; stigma orbicular, 1.5–2.5 mm in diam., margin (4–)6-crenate. Berry subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam.


Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 388; HK sheet 30763.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan.

Ecology: Moist places on hillsides, cliffs. Flowering: Oct.

Uses: Ornamental.

Aspidistra punctata Lindl. 紫點蜘蛛抱蛋
Bot. Reg. 12. pl. 799. 1826; FOC 24: 243. 2000; FGD 6: 366. 2005.

Perennial herb. Rhizome terete. Leaves solitary; petioles 7.5–50 cm, stiff; leaf blade lanceolate, 25–30 × 4.5–5.5 cm. Scape rather short; bracts ca. 5, dotted with purplish brown spots. Flower solitary, nodding. Perianth campanulate, pale green, dotted with purplish brown spots abaxially, fleshy, 8-lobed apically; lobes ovate, adaxially yellowish green and with 2 fleshy keels; keels dark purple, densely and minutely papillose. Stamens 8, inserted at middle of perianth tube, subsessile, lower than stigma in position; anthers oblong. Ovary with deeply coloured speckles, ovoid, angled; stigma white, orbicular, large, ca. 9 mm in diam., apically with 4 radial, fork-tipped ridges from centre to margin.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. C. P. Lau 97, 100 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.

Aster ageratoides Turcz. 三脈紫菀
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 17: 154. 1837; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 270. 1965; FRPS 74: 159. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 849. 1998; FGD 8: 174. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 40–100 cm tall, ribbed, glabrous on lower portion, sparsely puberulent upward. Basal leaves ovate, 4–6 × 2.5–3.5 cm, attenuate to form 4–8 cm of petiole, usually withered at anthesis; middle leaves elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate, 6–8.5 × 3–5 cm, base attenuate‑cuneate to form broadly‑winged petiole 3–9 cm, apex acuminate, margin with 4–7 pairs of serrate teeth; upper leaves smaller in size, subentire or shallowly toothed, subsessile or shortly petiolate. All leaves thin, triplinerved, scabrous adaxially, pubescent and sometimes glandular abaxially. Capitula corymbose or panicle‑corymbose. Involucres obconic or hemispherical; phyllaries 3‑seriate, imbricate, thickly scarious or leathery, oblong, pubescent, ciliate along margin, apex obtuse to rounded, apical region green or sometimes tinged purple, outer ones 2 mm, middle 3 mm, innermost 4 mm. Receptacle flat, alveolate, with edges of areoles shallowly chaffy. Ray florets 10–15, corolla tube 2 mm, ligules white or rarely purple, linear‑oblong, 5–8 × 0.8–1.2 mm. Disk tubular florets yellow, 5 mm, lower half of corolla tube narrower, upper half broader, bearing 5 lobes, 1.5–2 mm. Cypselae brown, densely pubescent, obovate‑oblong, 2–2.5 mm, slightly compressed, laterally ribbed, with midrib on one or both surfaces. Pappus reddish, about 4 mm.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. P. S. Choi 527; Y. S. Lau 3028; S. Y. Hu & & P. P. H. But 22966 (CUHK).
Distribution: SE to NE China; E Asia, Siberia, Mongolia, S Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: May–Dec.

Aster ageratoides var. scaberulus (Miq.) Ling. 微糙三脈紫菀
FRPS 74: 162. 1985; FGD 8: 174. 2007; Check List HK Plants 275. 2002.
Aster scaberulus Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 100. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 299. 1965.
Aster trinervius auct. non Roxb. ex D. Don: Benth., FHK 174. 1861; FKH 141. 1912.

Stem, lower surfaces of leaves and phyllaries more densely hairy, scaberulous and glandular. Leaves relatively thicker.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1317; P. S. Choi 105; HK sheet 38777.
Distribution: S to SW, and C to E China; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: May–Dec.

Aster baccharoides (Benth.) Steetz 白舌紫菀
Bot. Voy. Herald 385. 1857; FHK 175. 1861; FKH 141 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 276. 1965; FRPS 74: 195. 1985; FGD 8: 175, fig. 96. 2007.
Aster brevipes Benth., FHK 175. 1861; FKH 141. 1912.
Diplopappus baccharoides Benth., Lond. J. Bot. 1: 487. 1842.

Subshrubs or herbs with lower portion woody; stem erect, 50–100 cm tall, covered with short curved hair. Lower leaves spatulate‑oblong, usually withered at anthesis; middle leaves elliptic, 2–6 × 0.6–1.5 cm, sessile or with very short petiole, apex acute, margin entire or loosely serrulate at apical half; upper leaves smaller in size, subentire. All leaves scabrid on adaxial surfaces, pubescent and glandular on abaxial surfaces, midvein protrude on abaxial side. Capitula arranged in panicle‑corymb. Involucres turbinate with 5–7 × 2–3 mm; phyllaries in 4–7 series, imbricate, puberulent, margin scarious and ciliate; outermost ones ovate, 1.5 mm, apex nearly acute; those in middle layers obovate‑oblong, apex obtuse, length increasing inward; innermost ones oblanceolate‑oblong, 5 – 6 mm, apex rounded. Receptacle alveolate, with flat top, turbinate shape can be observed when phyllaries removed. Ray florets 10–15, corolla tube 3 mm, ligules white, 4.5–5 × 1.5–2 mm. Disk florets tubular, yellow, corolla tube 3 mm, 5‑lobed, lobes 2–3 mm, reflexed and rolling back; anthers exposed. Cypselae narrowly oblong, 2–2.5 mm, slightly compressed, sometimes ribbed, densely pubescent. Pappus white, 3.5–4.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1290, 2048; L. T. Lo 565.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.

Aster panduratus Nees ex Walp. 琴葉紫菀
Nov. Act. Cur. 19, Suppl. 1: 258. 1843; FKH 141. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 296. 1965; FRPS 74: 145. 1985; FGD 8: 173. 2007.

Perennial erect herb, 30–150 cm tall, branched on upper part, ribbed, strigose villose and glandular throughout. Lower leaves usually withered at anthesis, pandurate or spatulate‑oblong, 5–8 × 1.5–2.5 cm; middle leaves pandurate to oblong, 3–6 × 1–1.5 cm, base cordate or auriculate, sessile and subamplexicaul, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire; those on the flowering branches smaller, ovate‑oblong, base cordate and amplexicaul, margin entire. All leaves hispid or pilose along veins and margin, glandular. Capitula 1.2–1.8 cm across, terminal to shoots, solitary or forming loose corymbose clusters; peduncles 0.5–6 cm, densely pubescent or pilose, with linear‑lanceolate or ovate bract subtending the head. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 3‑seriate, oblong‑lanceolate; outermost herbaceous, 3 mm, apex acute, pubescent; middle and inner ones 4 mm and 5 mm respectively, apex and midvein herbaceous, margin scarious. Receptacle chaffy. Marginal ligulate florets about 18–30, pale purple to white, corolla tube 1.5 mm, limb 5–8 mm. Disk tubular florets greenish yellow or yellow, 3 mm including lobe of 1 mm, hairy. Cypselae brown, obovate, 1.5–2 mm, ribbed along sides, puberulous. Pappus 3 mm, white to reddish.

Locality: Chai Wan, Shatin Pass Rd., Kowloon Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 869, 2526; L. T. Lo 567.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.

Aster striatus Champ. ex Benth. 香港紫菀
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 233. 1852; FHK 174. 1861; FKH 141. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 300. 1965.

Perennial erect herb, 12–30 cm tall; stem striate, strigose throughout. Radical leaves persist at anthesis, arranged in rosette form, spatulate, 3–7 × 1–1.5 cm, apex rounded to obtuse, scabrous on both surfaces, hair denser along margin and midvein on abaxial surface; cauline ones few, pandurate‑oblong, 1–4 × 0.5–0.8 cm, base usually auriculate, amplexicaul, apex acute. Capitula hemispherical. Phyllaries in 2–3 series, lanceolate‑oblong, apex acute or acuminate, herbaceous at the middle and apical region, margin scarious, slightly fimbriate at edges, outermost 4 mm, inner ones 5 mm. Ray florets about 30, corolla tube 1.5 mm, limb 5 mm. Central tubular ones 3 mm, funnelform, hairy on the tube. Cypselae obovate, 3 mm, puberulent. Pappus white to pale red, equal in length, 3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, South Ninepin Island, Beaufort Island. S. L. Thrower 1518 (CUHK); W. J. Tutcher 4820; S. P. Lau 177.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Aster subulatus Michx. 鑽形紫菀
Fl. Bor.‑Amer. 2: 111. 1803; FTW ed. 2, 4: 861. 1998.

Annual or rarely biennial herbs; stem erect, 30–120 cm tall, branched on upper portion, glabrous, terete. Leaves linear to lanceolate, less than 1.5 cm wide, margin subentire or occasionally shallowly toothed, sessile and subamplexicaul, glabrous and smooth; those on branches smaller in size, bract‑like. Capitula arranged in loose panicle or corymb. Involucres subcylindric; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, linear‑lanceolate to subulate, apex acute or acuminate, greenish, some tinged purple at the tip, margin scarious, outermost ones 2 mm, length gradually increased inward, innermost 5 mm. Marginal ligulate florets white or pale pink in colour, limb 1.5–5 mm, slightly exserted at anthesis, always recurved and rolling back when dried. Central tubular florets yellow, 3 mm, lower half of corolla tube narrower, upper half broader, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae pale brown, cylindric, 0.8–2 mm, pubescent. Pappus 4–5 mm, longer than tubular florets, white or reddish, easily shed off as a whole ring.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. W. Lam 365, 733, 985.
Distribution: Native to N America, introduced and distributed throughout temperate N hemisphere.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: May–Dec.
Notes: As a weed.

Asystasia gangetica (L.) T. Anderson 寬葉十萬錯
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 235. 1860; FRPS 70: 217. 2002.
Justicia gangetica L., Cent. II Pl. 3. 1756.
Asystasia coromandelica Wight ex Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 89. 1832.

Perennial ascending herbs, up to 0.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, pilose. Petioles 3–5 mm, pubescent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 3–12 × 1–5 cm, base truncate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire or slightly crenulate, glabrous or sparsely pilose, especially on the veins, adaxially covered with numerous cystoliths. Racemes axillary or terminal, up to 16 cm. Pedicels 2–3 mm, pilose. Bracts triangular, ca. 5 mm, pilose; bracteoles linear‑lanceolate, 1–2.5 mm, pilose. Calyx ca. 7 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 5–7 × 1–1.2 mm, abaxially pubescent, with glandular‑tipped pilose, margin ciliate. Corolla yellow or white, 3 – 3.5 cm, funnel‑shaped, outside glandular‑pilose, inside glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 8 cm, ventricose and gradually widened to ca. 1 cm wide at mouth; lobes obovate or semiorbicular, ca. 0.7–1.2 × 0.8–1 cm, middle lobe with a violet blotch. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anther‑thecae 3 × 1 mm, muticous. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm; style ca. 1.8 cm, velutinous; stigma capitellate, 2‑lobed. Capsule oblong, ca. 1.3 cm, pubescent 2–4‑seeded. Seeds irregularly obovate, flat, 3–5 mm, tuberculate‑rugose, margin with dense mucilaginous hairs.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. HK sheet 21382, 40596.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan; pantropical weeds.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Jan.–Mar.

Asystasia micrantha (Nees) Y. F. Deng & N. H. Xia, stat. nov. 小花十萬錯
Asystasia coromandeliana α micrantha Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 89. 1832.
Asystasia gangetica (L.) T. Anderson subsp. micrantha (Nees) Ensermu Kelbessa in J. H. Seyani & A. C. Chikuni (eds.), Proc. XIII Plenary Meet. AETFAT, Zomba, Malawi, 1991, 1: 343. 1994.

Perennial ascending herbs, ca. 0.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, pilose along sulci and on the nodes. Petioles 1–4 cm, slightly winged, pubescent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 5–11 × 2–5 cm, base truncate, rounded, decurrent onto the petioles, apex shortly acuminate or acute, margin entire or slightly crenulate, glabrous except for pilose on the veins, adaxially covered with numerous cystoliths, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Racemes axillary or terminal, 3–8 cm. Pedicels 1–3 mm, pilose. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, ca. 2.5 × 1 mm, pubescent; bracteoles triangular‑lanceolate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, glabrescent except for the ciliate margin. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 4–5 × 1–1.2 mm, apex acuminate, abaxially sparsely pubescent, margin ciliate. Corolla white, pale violet, spotted on the center lobe of the lower lip, 1.2–1.5 cm, campanulate, outside pilose, inside glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 3 cm, gradually widened to ca. 5 mm wide at mouth; lobes ovate or semiorbicular, ca. 3 × 2 mm, middle lobe with a violet blotch. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 6 mm, the shorter pair ca. 4 mm; anther‑thecae 2 × 1 mm, muticous. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm, comose; style 0.8–1 cm, velutinous towards the base; stigma capitellate, 2‑lobed. Capsule oblong, 1.8–2 cm, ca. 2 mm wide, pubescent, base solid‑stalked, 2 – 4‑seeded. Seeds irregularly obovate, flat, 3–5 mm, margin angled, glabrous, tuberculate‑rugose.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. W. Lam 2119; S. C. Ng 4128; F. W. Xing 8996 (IBSC).
Distribution: Taiwan; pantropical weeds.
Ecology: Margins of forests, gardens or roadsides. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Jan.–Mar.

Atalantia buxifolia (Poir.) Oliv. 酒餅簕

J. Proc. Linn. Soc., Bot. 5(Suppl. 2): 26. 1861; FHK 51. 1861; FKH 56. 1912; FHN 3: 47, fig. 557. 1974; FGD 2: 261, fig. 173: 5 –6. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 156, pl. 41. 1997.

Citrus buxifolia Poir., Encycl. 4: 580. 1797.

Limonia monophylla Lour., Fl. Cochchin. 1: 271. 1790, non L. (1767), nom. illeg.

Severinia buxifolia (Poir.) Ten., Index Sem. (Napoli) 3. 1840; FTW 3: 525. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 3: 529, pl. 273. 1993.

Dumula sinensis Lour. ex B. A. Gomes, Mem. Acad. Sci. Lisb. Cl. Sci. Pol. Mor. Bel.-Let, n.s. 4(1): 29. 1868.

Severinia monophylla Tanaka, J. Bot. (Morot) 68: 232. 1930.


Shrub, to 2.5 m tall, multibranched. Branchlets green when young, greyish brown when old, internodes slightly flat, spines many, straight, to 4 cm, rarely nearly unarmed. Leaves hard leathery, fragrant; petiole 1–7 mm, robust; leaflet blade ovate, obovate, elliptic or suborbicular, 2–6(–10) × 1–5 cm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex rounded or obtuse, emarginate; midvein slightly prominent adaxially, lateral veins dense, subparallel. Flowers several-fasciculate in axils, rarely solitary, subsessile. Sepals 5. Petals 5, white, 3–4 mm, glandular-dotted. Stamens 10, filaments white, distinct, sometimes few connate at base. Styles as long as ovary, green. Fruit globose, compressed globose or subellipsoidal, 0.8–1.2 cm in diam.; pericarp smooth, with slightly raised glands, bluish black when mature, with persistent calyx; pulp translucent, (1–)2-seeded. Seed coat thinly membranous.


Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1294, 1849, 2268.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.

Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May – Dec.; fruiting: Sep. – Dec.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The species was reported as Severinia buxifolia (Poir.) Ten. previously (Check List HK Plants 201. 2002; 71. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The species was reported as Severinia buxifolia (Poir.) Ten. previously (Check List HK Plants 201. 2002; 71. 2004).

records.text:
Atriplex maximowicziana Makino 海濱藜
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 10: 2. 1896; FOC 5: 365. 2003.

Perennial herb, monoecious. Stem 30 –100 cm tall, densely farinose, many branched; branches ascending. Leaves alternate or lower ones subopposite, rhomboid-ovate or ovate-oblong, 2–3 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse and mucronate, margin slightly 3-lobed, densely farinose on both surfaces. Male flowers in ca. 1 cm long, terminal, densely packed spikes; perianth-lobes 5, obovate; stamens 5. Female flowers smaller, clustered into panicles. Utricles compressed-globose or biconvex, persistent bracteoles rhomboid-ovate, 6–9 mm, margin triangular-toothed, connate only at base. Seeds reddish brown, 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai O, Sha Chau. HK sheet 36803; S. P. Lau 128.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong; Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as A. nummularia Lindl. previously (Check List HK Plants 64. 1993).

Aucuba chinensis Benth. 桃葉珊瑚
FHK 138. 1861; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. 23: 346. 1886; FKH 120. 1912; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 675, fig. 282. 1963; FHN 3: 117. 1974, p.p., excl. fl. descr.; FFJ 4: 205. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 3: 979, pl. 488. 1993; FOC 14: 223. 2005.

Tree or shrub, 3–6(–12) m tall; branches dichotomous, stout. Petiole 2–4 cm; leaf blade elliptic to broadly elliptic, 10–20 × 3.5–8 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate or cuneate, slightly oblique, apex acute or obtusely acuminate, margin slightly revolute, often serrate or glandular dentate; midvein raised abaxially, lateral veins 6–8(–10) on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal, paniculate. Male inflorescences 5–13 cm; peduncles ca. 3 mm, pubescent; bracteole 1. Male flowers purplish red; calyx 4-dentate, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; petals 4, oblong or ovate, 3–4 × 2– 2.5 mm, apex cuspidate, pilose or glabrous abaxially; stamens 4, ca. 3 mm, anthers yellow, 2-celled. Female inflorescences 4 – 5 cm; bractoles 2. Female flowers yellow green or yellowish; calyx and petals as in male flowers; ovary cylindrical; style stout; stigma capitate, slightly oblique. Drupes bright red or dark red, cylindrical or ovoid, 1.4–1.8 cm, 8–10(–12) mm in diam., apex with persistent calyx teeth and styles.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 49, 666; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 34839).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Myanmar, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jan.– Feb.; fruiting: Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen (Harland s.n.) was collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Avena fatua L. 野燕麥
Sp. Pl. 1: 80. 1753; FHK 430. 1861; FKH 326. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 172, pl. 44: 4–6. 1987; FFJ 6: 126, fig. 97. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 351. 2000; FOC 22: 324. 2006; FGD 9: 389. 2009.
Avena fatua L. subsp. meridionalis Malzev, Trudy Prikl. Bot. 20: 140. 1929.
Avena meridionalis (Malzev) Roshev., Fl. Turkm. 1: 105. 1932; FRPS 9(3): 170. 1987.

Annual herb, 60 – 120 cm tall. Culms erect or geniculate at base, glabrous, 2–4-noded. Leaf blades linear, 10–30 × 0.4–1.5 cm, scabrid or adaxial surface and margins pilose; ligule tongue-shaped, 1–5 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous or basal sheaths puberulous. Panicle narrowly to broadly pyramidal, 10–40 cm, branches scabrid. Spikelets pendulous, 1.8–2.5 cm, 2–3-flowered; rachilla articulate beneath each floret, easily disarticulating at maturity, internodes hirsute or glabrous, callus densely bearded with hairs up to 4 mm; glumes lanceolate, subequal, herbaceous, 9–11-veined, apex finely acute; lemmas 1.5–2.5 cm, leathery, densely hispid in lower half, green and scaberulous above, awned from near middle, apex unequally and shortly 2–4-toothed; awn 2–4 cm, geniculate, column twisted, blackish brown; palea flattened, 2-keeled, margins ciliate. Caryopsis hairy; hilum linear.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Lung Farm. HK sheet 30756.
Distribution: Widely spread over all provinces of China; native to Europe and W Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands, margins of fields, and abandoned lands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Avena fatua L. var. glabrata Peterm. 光稃野燕麥
Fl. Bienitz 13. 1841; FRPS 9(3): 173, pl. 44: 7. 1987; FFJ 6: 127. 1995; FOC 22: 325. 2006; FGD 9: 389. 2009.

It differs from the type variety by its lemmas being glabrous, and turning yellowish at maturity.

Locality: Fanling. Y. S. Lau 3113.
Distribution: The same as for the species.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes, roadsides, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Avena sativa L. 燕麥
Sp. Pl. 1: 79. 1753; FRPS 9(3): 173, pl. 44: 9 – 11. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 5: 351. 2000; FOC 22: 324. 2006; FGD 9: 389. 2009.

Annual herb, 40–80 cm tall. Leaf blades linear, 8–30 × 0.4–1.5 cm, glabrous, margins sometimes scaberulous; ligule papery, tongue-shaped, 2–6 mm; leaf sheaths usually glabrous. Panicle (10–)20–40 cm, nodding; branches spreading or contracted. Spikelets nodding, 2–3 cm, 1–2-flowered; rachilla ± glabrous, straight, not disarticulating or fracturing irregularly at maturity, florets lacking a basal bearded callus; glumes lanceolate, subequal, as long as spikelet, 7–9-veined; lemmas 1.2–2.5 cm, leathery in lower half, herbaceous and distinctly veined above, apex minutely and irregularly 2–4-denticulate; awn 2.5 –3.5 cm, weakly geniculate or rudimentary or absent; palea shorter than the lemma, minutely hairy on the two keels. Caryopsis hairy, adherent to lemma and palea at maturity, hilum linear.

Locality: So Kon Po, Castle Peak. Y. S. Lau 3285; HK sheet 8637, 8638.
Distribution: Cultivated throughout China.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Food (cereal), animal food (fodder).

Averrhoa carambola L. 楊桃
Sp. Pl. 428. 1753; FHK 56. 1861; FKH 54. 1912; FHN 1: 415, fig. 224. 1964; FGD 2: 100, fig. 68. 1991.

Evergreen small tree, usually 5–8 m tall. Branchlets dark brown, puberulent. Leaves alternate, 8–18 cm, with 5–11 leaflets; petioles and rachis puberulent; leaflets alternate or subopposite; petiolules ca. 2 mm; blade ovate to elliptic, 3– 8 × 2 – 3.5 cm, apex shortly acuminate, base subrounded, very oblique, glabrous on both surfaces. Panicles axillary, sessile, 2.5–5 cm, pubescent. Sepals united and cup-shaped, 2.5–5 mm. Petals spathulate, 8–10 × 3–4 mm, initially dark red, becoming pink or whitish when in full blooming. Stamens 10, the 5 smaller ones usually very minute and without anthers. Fruit ellipsoidal or ovoid, succulent, with (3–)5(–8) ribs, transverse section stellate.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 59; Y. S. Lau 3002; HK sheet 612.
Distribution: Native to Malesia, now cultivated throughout tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Avicennia marina (Forssk.) Vierh. 海欖雌（白骨壤）
Denkschr. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.‑Naturwiss. Kl. 71: 435. 1907; FHN 4: 6. 1977; FTW 4: 410. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 5. 1982; FFJ 4: 517, fig. 410. 1989; FOC 17: 49. 1994; FGD 3: 340, fig. 223. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 404, pl. 175, photo 238 – 239. 1998.
Sceura marina Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.‑Arab. 37. 1775.
Avicennia officinalis auct. non L.: FKH 205. 1912.

Shrub 1.5–6 m tall. Branchlets ridged when young. Leaves subsessile; leaf blade elliptic to ovate, 2–7 × 1–3.5 cm, base acuminate, apex obtuse, adaxially glabrous and shiny, abaxially pubescent; midvein conspicuous, lateral veins 4–6 pairs. Cymes dense, capitates. Peduncle 1–2.5 cm. Bracts 5, ca. 2.5 × 3 mm, in 2 whorls, outer ones densely tomentose, inner ones smooth, blackish brown. Flowers ca. 5 mm in diam. Calyx‑lobe ca. 3 × 2–3 mm, tomentose abaxially. Corolla yellow, tube short, limb 4‑lobed, lobes ca. 2 mm, tomentose abaxially. Stamens slightly exserted. Ovary densely tomentose distally. Fruit subglobose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., hairy.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Tai Po, Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Mai Po, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Kei Ling Ha, Yung Shue O, Chek Keng, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1496, 2793; Y. W. Lam 795.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, E Africa, N Australia.
Ecology: Mangrove. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Axonopus compressus (Sw.) P. Beauv. 地毯草
Ess. Agrostogr. 12. 1812; FHN 4: 424, fig. 1223. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 278, pl. 84. 1990; FFJ 6: 224. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 456, pl. 189. 2000; FOC 22: 531. 2006; FGD 9: 426, fig. 220. 2009.
Milium compressum Sw., Prodr. 24. 1788.

Perennial herb, with creeping, long stolons. Culms 8–60 cm tall, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths loose, strongly compressed, keeled, basal sheaths imbricate; leaf blades broadly linear to lanceolate, flat or folded, 5–20 × 0.6–1.2 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose, apex rounded, margins sparsely ciliate at the base; ligule ca. 0.5 mm. Racemes 2–5, digitate or subdigitate, 4–10 cm; rachis triangular, glabrous; spikelets in 2-rows along one-side. Spikelets solitary, oblong-lanceolate, 2–3 mm, pilose or glabrous; lower lemma absent; upper glume as long as or longer than lower lemma, 2–4-veined, midvein absent; upper lemma oblong-elliptic, shorter than spikelet, leathery, margins slightly thicken and inrolled embraced same texture palea, obtuse with an apical tuft of hairs, mucronate and pubescent at apex; stigmas plumose, pale.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong (naturalised). Y. S. Lau 1799, 2253; S. P. Lau 49.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; originated from tropical America, widely introduced elsewhere.
Ecology: Roadsides, weedy places on moist ground. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Environment (erosion control), animal food (forage).

Axonopus fissifolius (Raddi) Kuhlm. 類地毯草
Comm. Linh. Telegr., Bot. 67(Bot. 11): 87. 1922; FOC 22: 531. 2006; FGD 9: 426. 2009.
Paspalum fissifolium Raddi, Agrostogr. Bras. 26. 1823.
Axonopus affinis Chase, J. Wash. Acad. Sci 28: 180. fig. 1, 2. 1938; FRPS 10(1): 280. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 456. 2000; Check List HK Plants 324. 2002; 114. 2004.

Perennial herb; stolons creeping. Culms compressed, 15–50 cm tall, nodes glabrous. Leaf sheaths compressed; leaf blades broadly linear, folded, 5–20 × 0.3–0.6 cm, obtuse; ligule ciliate. Racemes 2–4, 2-paired, any others spaced slightly below, 3–8 cm, only slightly diverging; rachis glabrous. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, pilose near margins and apex or subglabrous; upper glume and lower lemma 2–4-veined, margins with silky hairs; upper floret bisexual, lemma pale, ovate, leathery, obtuse; stigmas purple. Caryopsis elliptic-oblong.

Locality: Tai Lung Farm (cultivated). S. P. Lau 191; HK sheet 35848.
Distribution: Taiwan, Xizang (cultivated or naturalised); native to tropical America, naturalized in paleotropics.
Ecology: Moist muddy or sandy meadows. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Environment (erosion control), animal food (forage).

Bacopa monnieri (L.) Pennell 假馬齒莧
Proc. Acad. Nat. Sci. Philadelphia 98: 94. 1946; FOC 18: 21. 1998.
Lysimachia monnieri L., Cent. Pl. II, 2: 9. 1756.
Bacopa monnieri (L.) Wettst., Nat. Pflanzenfam. IV(3b): 77. 1891, nom. illeg.; FHN 3: 498. 1974; FRPS 67(2): 87. 1979; FGD 4: 383. 2000; Check List HK Plants 244. 2002; 84. 2004.
Herpestis monnieri Kunth, Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 2: 366. 1818; FHK 249. 1861; FKH 187. 1912.

Herbs creeping; stems ± succulent, glabrous. Leaves sessile, oblong‑oblanceolate, 0.8–2 cm × 3–6 mm, apex rounded, margin entire or rarely dentate. Flowers axillary; pedicels 0.5–3.5 cm. Bracteoles 2, linear. Sepals 5, ca. 5 mm, unequal. Corolla blue, purple, or white, 8–10 mm, obscurely 2‑lipped. Stamens didynamous. Stigma capitate. Capsules narrowly ovoid, enveloped in persistent calyx. Seeds yellow‑brown, ellipsoidal, truncate at one end, longitudinally striate.

Locality: Tai Long Wan, Sha Tin, Plover Cove, Lai Chi Wo, Luk Keng, Kat O. Y. S. Lau 1994, 2150, 3118.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Bacopa repens (Sw.) Wettst. 田玄參
Nat. Pflanzenfam. IV(3b):76. 1895; FOC 18: 22. 1998.
Gratiola repens Sw., Prodr. 14. 1788.
Sinobacopa aquatica D. Y. Hong, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 25(5): 395. 1987.

Herbs creeping. Stems succulent, rooting at nodes. Leaves sessile, obovate to obovate‑lanceolate, 1.2–2.5 × 0.7– 1.3 cm, margin entire. Flowers axillary, pendulous; pedicels 1–2 cm. Bracteoles absent. Sepals 4 or 5, 3 – 4 mm, unequal, margin ciliate. Corolla white, almost as long as sepals; lobes obovate; upper lip lobed to middle, lobes narrowly obovate. Stamens equal in length, ca. 1.2 mm, inserted at throat; filaments as long as anthers. Anthers ± sagittate. Stigma 2‑parted. Capsules globose, ca. 1.7 mm in diam. Seeds columnar‑oblong, ca. 0.5 mm; testa reticulate.

Locality: Tai Mong Tsai, Sai Keng, Tsiu Hang, Peng Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1443; Y. W. Lam 982, 2227.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; N & S America.
Ecology: Wet places, watersides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

Baeckea frutescens L. 崗松
Sp. Pl. 1: 358. 1753; FHK 118. 1861; FKH 104. 1912; FGZ 207. 1956; FHN 2: 2, fig. 286. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 57, pl. 9: 4 – 8. 1984; FFJ 4: 79, fig. 62. 1989; FGX 1: 873. 1991; FGD 3: 162, fig. 116. 1995; FOC 13: 330. 2007.
Baeckea chinensis Gaertn., Fruct. 1: 157, t. 31. 1788.
Baeckea frutescens var. brachyphylla Merr. & L. M. Perry, J. Arnold Arb. 20: 102. 1939.

Shrub or sometimes small tree; branches slender. Petioles 0.5–0.6 mm; leaf blade linear, 5–10 × ca. 1 mm, apex sharp pointed, grooved adaxially, with pellucid oil glands abaxially; midvein 1, lateral veins absent. Flowers solitary, small. Pedicels 1 –1.5 mm. Hypanthium campanulate, ca. 1.5 mm. Calyx-lobes 5, triangular, small, apex acute. Petals white, distinct, orbicular, ca. 1.5 mm, base clawed. Stamens 10 or less, in pairs opposite to calyx lobes. Ovary inferior, 2–3-locular. Style persistent. Capsule ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 332, 1289; L. T. Lo 444.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; tropical Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Thickets, sunny hillslopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), essential oil.

Balanophora harlandii Hook. f. 紅苳蛇菰
Trans. Linn. Soc. London, Bot. 22: 426. 1859; FHK 140. 1861; Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 410. 1894; FKH 230. 1912; FTW 2: 255, pl. 288. 1976; FRPS 24: 265. 1988; FFJ rev. ed. 1: 510, fig. 460. 1991; FOC 5: 276. 2003.
Balanophora harlandii var. mutinoides (Hayata) F. W. Xing, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 12(4): 381. 1992.
Balanophora lancangensis Y. Y. Qian, J. Trop. & Subtrop. Bot. 4(2): 12, fig. 1. 1996.
Balanophora minor Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(177): 410, pl. 9, fig. 1. 1894.
Balanophora mutinoides Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 3: 168, pl. 31. 1913; FRPS 24: 267, pl. 65: 6 – 8. 1988.

Herb, dioecious, 8–15 cm tall. Rhizome robust, yellowish to brownish, often branched, surface with scaly warts. Scapes dark red to yellow, 2–5.5 cm. Leaves 6–12, yellow to reddish, usually clustered on base of scape, decussate, subopposite, or spiral, scale-like, oblong-ovate, 1.5–4.5 × 1.5–2.5 cm. Male inflorescences subspheroidal, 1.8–2.5 × 1.5–2 cm. Male flowers: pedicellate, 3-merous, 1.5–3 mm in diam., perianth-lobes broadly triangular; synandria subdiscoid; anthers 3, transversely dehiscent. Female inflorescence ovoid to ellipsoidal. Female flowers: ovary ovoid to long-ovoid; style filiform. Fruit long-ovoid, pale yellow, lustrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lamma Island, Kat O, Tung Lung Chau. H. C. Tang 1884; Y. S. Lau 1220; P. S. Choi 231.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina and Thailand.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected from Mount Gough by W. A. Harland in 1858.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected from Mount Gough by W. A. Harland in 1858.

records.text:
Balanophora hongkongensis K. M. Lau, N. H. Li & S. Y. Hu 香港蛇菰
Harvard Pap. Bot. 7(2): 437. 2003; FOC 5: 275. 2003, pro syn. sub B. laxiflora Hemsl.

Herb, dioecious, 3–10 cm tall. Rhizomes branched; branches subspherical, 3–10 cm in diam., surface irregularly warty, yellowish brown. Scapes orange-red, 2–11 cm in diam. Leaves 8–14, alternate, ovate-lanceolate, 1.2–4 × 0.8–1 cm, apex acute. Male inflorescences cylindrical, 2–10 × 0.5–1.6 cm. Male flowers: subsessile; perianth-lobes 4–6, suborbicular to ovate, 2–3 mm, apex acute to obtuse; synandria sessile, discoid, 3–4 mm in diam.; anthers 10 –30 or more, dehiscing by slits. Female inflorescences ovoid-spheroidal to oblong-ellipsoidal, 1.5–8 × 1–3 cm. Female flowers: ovaries stipitate, fusiform, 0.5 mm.

Locality: Castle Peak. N. H. Li & K. M. Lau 310; HK sheet 38569, 38571.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Dense forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Castle Peak by N. H. Li and K. M. Lau on 9 Dec. 2000.

Bambusa beecheyana Munro 吊絲球竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 108. 1868; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 27. 1985; FOC 22: 36. 2006; FGD 9: 265, fig. 133. 2009.
Arundarbor beecheyana (Munro) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 761. 1891.
Dendrocalamopsis beecheyana (Munro) Keng f., J. Bamboo Res. 2(1): 12. 1983; FRPS 9(1): 143. 1996.
Neosinocalamus beecheyanus (Munro) Keng f. & T. H. Wen, J. Bamboo Res. 4(2): 18. 1985.
Sinocalamus beecheyanus (Munro) McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 67. 1940.

Culms to 16 m, 9–10 cm in diam., apically long pendulous; internodes 34–41 cm, initially thickly white powdery, sparsely pubescent, without a brown pubescent ring below nodes; wall 1.5–2 cm thick; nodes flat, basal ones without branches. Branches several, 1–3 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, leathery, initially with uneven, dark brown, spinous hairs; auricles small at lower nodes, larger at distal nodes; oral setae present or absent; ligule 2–4 mm, ciliate; blade recurved, triangular, base 1/2–4/5 as wide as sheath apex, adaxially hirtellous. Leaf sheaths initially hirtellous; ligule truncate, 0.5–1 mm; auricles absent or minute; oral setae scarce or absent; blade oblong-lanceolate, 11–28 × 1.5–3.5 cm. Pseudospikelets 1.5–2 × 0.5–0.8 cm; florets 6–8; rachilla not disarticulating, internodes ca. 2 mm. Glumes 2, cordate, 4–5 mm, ciliate; lemma ca. 0.9 × 0.9 cm; palea 4–8 mm, abaxially hirtellous, apex acuminate or obtuse; lodicules 3, ciliate. Anthers ca. 5 mm. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm; styles 3–4 mm; stigmas 2–4, ca. 6 mm. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Kowloon, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1127; Y. S. Lau 2671; L. T. Lo 637.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan.
Ecology: New shoots: Jun.–Jul.; flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Vegetable.

Bambusa chungii McClure 粉簞竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 15: 639. 1936; HKB 28. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 120, pl. 29. 1996; FOC 22: 33. 2006; FGD 9: 258, fig. 132. 2009.
Lingnania chungii (McClure) McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 35. 1940.
Lingnania chungii (McClure) McClure var. petilla T. H. Wen, J. Bamboo. Res. 1(1): 34. 1982.

Culms 5–10(–18) m, 3–5(–7) cm in diam.; internodes 30–45(–100) cm, initially white powdery, glabrous; wall 3–5 mm thick; nodes flat; sheath scars corky, initially with a ring of dense, brown hairs; branching from distal nodes only. Branches many, subequal. Culm sheaths deciduous, thinly leathery, initially white powdery, silky hairy, apex later glabrous, concave; auricles narrowly oblong, glossy; ligule ca. 1.5 mm, serrulate or long fimbriate; blade deciduous, strongly reflexed, base 1/5–1/3 as wide as sheath apex, adaxially hispidulous. Leaf sheaths glabrous; auricles usually developed; oral setae straight; blade lanceolate, 10–16(–20) × 1–2(–3.5) cm. Pseudospikelets ca. 2 cm; gemmiferous bracts 1–2; florets 4–5. Glumes 1–2; lemma 9–12 mm; palea about as long as lemma. Styles 1–2 mm; stigmas 3 or 2. Caryopsis triangular, 8 – 9 mm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1125; Nan-Zhu 1125.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Hunan, SE Yunnan.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa chunii L. C. Chia & H. L. Fung 煥鏞簕竹
Kew Bull. 37: 593. 1983; HKB 29. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 58, pl. 13: 12. 1996; FOC 22: 13. 2006; FGD 9: 230. 2009.

Culms 10–12 m, 4.5–6.5 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically drooping; internodes slightly curved, 25–30 cm, very thinly white powdery, very sparsely stiffly hairy, with a ring of grey hairs below each node; wall thick; branching to base. Branches at lower nodes usually solitary, with tough, sharp thorns, at upper nodes 3–several with central 3 longer and thicker. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, with several marginal white stripes on each side, leathery, glabrous, apex obliquely truncate with unequal, triangular protuberance on each shoulder; auricles unequal, linear-lanceolate, small, usually wrinkled, abaxially hispidulous; oral setae well developed, 5–10 mm, undulate, hispidulous at base; ligule 5–7 mm, margin irregular, dentate, laciniate; blade erect, broadly lanceolate, abaxially glabrous, base nearly 1/2 width of sheath apex. Leaf blade lanceolate, 9.5–19 × 1.5–2 cm, abaxially pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospiklets linear, compressed, ca. 4.5 cm long, clustered at nodes of flowering branches; gemmiferous bracts 1–2, ovate, apex minutely obtuse or acute; fertile florets 5–14, and 1–2 sterile floret at apex; rachilla segments ca. 2 mm long, ciliate; lemma 9–10 × 4–4.5 mm, glossy and glabrous, veins in 9–11, apex acute; palea shorter than lemma, 8–9 × 3.5–4 mm, oblong, 2-keeled, glabrous, minutely ciliate on margins at its base, apex obtuse or sometimes emarginate; lodicules 3 subequal, ovate or obovate, 2 × 1 mm, 3-veined, the veins faint, ﬁmbriate along margins; stamens 6, anthers 3 × 0.3 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary narrow obovoid, apex thickened and scabrous, ciliate; style short; stigmas 3, long, plumose; Fruit ovoid, deep furrow lined, 6–7 × 2–2.5 cm.

Locality: Yuen Long. HK sheet 35339, 35340.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong
Ecology: Cultivated around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Notes: The type specimen (Nan-Zhu (南竹隊) 2802, IBSC) was collected from Ko Po Tsuen, Yuen Long, New Territories in 1980. The species epithet is respectfully dedicated to Professor Woon-Young Chun, the founder and former Director of South China Botanical Garden. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Bambusa eutuldoides McClure 大眼竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 8. 1940; HKB 33. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 82, pl. 17: 1–12. 1996; FOC 22: 22. 2006; FGD 9: 241. 2009.

Culms 6–12 m, 4–6 cm in diam., basally straight, apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–40 cm, fistulose, initially thinly white powdery, sometimes sparsely deciduously stiffly hairy below nodes; wall ca. 5 mm thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal several with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from 2nd or 3rd node up. Branches several or many, clustered, central 3 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, triangular to narrowly triangular, leathery, glabrous or sometimes very sparsely stiffly strigose, apex long slanted along one side, extremely asymmetric, arched; auricles extremely asymmetric, of various shapes, rigid, wrinkled; larger auricle extremely decurrent, oblanceolate to narrowly oblong, 5–6.5 × ca. 1.5 cm; smaller auricle suborbicular or oblong, ca. 1 cm in diam., or sometimes thoroughly joined to blade base; oral setae undulate; ligule 3–5 mm, irregularly dentate or laciniate, shortly fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect, asymmetric, triangular to narrowly triangular, base slightly narrowed and then extending outward to join auricles, nearly 3/5 width of sheath apex, abaxially sparsely stiffly deciduous-hairy. Leaf blade abaxially green, lanceolate to broadly lanceolate, usually 12–25 × 1.4–2.5 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets sessile, clustered at each node of flowering branches and branchlets, linear, 2.5–5.5 cm, with several bud-bearing bracts at base; florets 5–6; rachilla segments flat, 3–4 mm, apex inflated and ciliolate. Glume 1, with very small purple spots, oblong, 9–10 mm, 11-veined, glabrous, apex acute, apiculate; lemma similar to glumes, oblong, 1.2–1.3 cm, 13–15-veined; palea lanceolate, ca. 1.1 cm, keels ciliolate toward tip, 4-veined between and 2-veined on either side of keels; lodicules 3, unequal, anterior 2 narrow, ca. 2 mm, apex long ciliate, posterior 1 larger, broadly ovate or suborbicular, ca. 2 mm. Anthers ca. 5 mm, apex bifid. Ovary subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., apex hispidulous; style very short, hispidulous; stigmas 3. Caryopsis initially nearly obovoid, ca. 5 mm, apex hispidulous with persistent style base.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2771; H. C. Tang 1100.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Environmental, ornamental.

Bambusa flexuosa Munro 小簕竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 101. 1868; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 34. 1985; FOC 22: 12. 2006; FGD 9: 228. 2009.
Arundarbor flexuosa (Munro) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 760. 1891.
Bambusa scabriculma W. T. Lin, J. S. China Agric. Univ. 14(1): 46. 1993.

Culms 6–7 m, 3.5–6 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically nodding; internodes 20–30 cm, sparsely stiffly brown strigose, with a ring of silky brown hairs below each node; wall thick. Branches to base, solitary at lower nodes, flexuose, densely interwoven, branchlets specialized into tough thorns, higher nodes with 3–several branches. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, leathery, prominently ribbed-striate when dry, sparsely stiffly dark brown strigose, apex concave with a triangular protuberance on each shoulder; auricles narrowly filiform or absent; ligule 4–5 mm, dentate or laciniate, fimbriate; blade erect or recurved, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, base ca. 1/2 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to lanceolate, 7–11 × 1.2–1.6 cm, both surfaces glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or clustered, slightly compressed, 2–3 cm, gemmiferous bracts ca. 4; florets 8–12 with middle florets perfect; rachilla flexuose, internodes flat, 2–2.5 mm, hispid. Glumes usually absent; lemma oblong-lanceolate, 8–10 mm, apex acute; palea usually shorter than lemma, keels ciliate; lodicules 3, subequal, margins long ciliate, apex obtuse. Filaments enlarged at base; anther obtuse at apex. Style short; stigmas 3.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling, Lantau Island (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1121; Y. S. Lau 2470; Nan-Zhu 2757.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan.
Ecology: Hills, river banks. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Hedges. Notes: It has been named incorrectly by some authors as Bambusa bambos (L.) Voss.
records.uses: Hedges. Notes: It has been named incorrectly by some authors as Bambusa bambos (L.) Voss.

records.text:
Bambusa gibba McClure 坭竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 10. 1940; FHN 4: 354. 1977; HKB 35. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 68, pl. 14: 1–10. 1996; FOC 22: 16. 2006; FGD 9: 235. 2009.

Culms 7–10 m, 3.5–6 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically suberect; internodes 30–40 cm, inflated near base, initially white powdery, basal internodes initially sparsely stiffly grey-white or brown strigose; wall 3–5 mm thick; nodes glabrous; branching to base. Branches usually 3 at lower nodes with branchlets sometimes specialized into weak thorns; several on middle and upper nodes, 3 central branches dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, glabrous, apex obliquely truncate, with a triangular protuberance on higher shoulder; auricles obviously unequal, sometimes weak; larger auricle ovate-lanceolate or narrowly oblong, 5–6 mm; smaller auricle ovate or elliptic, 2–3 mm; oral setae slender, undulate; ligule arched, 2–3 mm, finely dentate and fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect, narrowly triangular, base not narrowed, nearly 2/3 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 8.5–14.5 × 0.8–1.3 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets linear, 2–3 cm; prophylls ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, keels ciliate, apex obtuse; gemmiferous bracts 4, ovate, 1.5–3.5 mm, apex obtuse and mucronate; florets 4–8; rachilla segments flat, ca. 3.5 mm, slightly hairy, apex inflated and ciliolate. Glume 1, ovate-elliptic, 6–6.5 mm, 15-veined, apex acute, mucronate; lemma ovate-oblong, ca. 1.1 cm, 17-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea nearly as long as lemma or shorter, keels glabrous, 3-veined between and on either side of keels, apex obtuse with a cluster of white hairs; lodicules 3, subequal, ca. 1.5 mm, margins long ciliate toward apex, base thickened, anterior 2 broadly elliptic, posterior ovate. Anther obtuse at apex. Ovary ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm, base stalked, apex hairy; style ca. 0.5 mm; stigmas 3. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, New Territories, Lantau Island (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2770.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Low hills, around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Hedges, timber.

Bambusa gibboides W. T. Lin 魚肚腩竹
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(1): 70. 1978; HKB 36. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 98, pl. 18: 1 – 10. 1996; FOC 22: 26. 2006; FGD 9: 247. 2009.

Culms 10–12 m, 5–7 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically drooping; internodes slightly curved, basally slightly swollen, 40–47 cm, initially thinly white powdery, stiffly brown strigose; wall slightly thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal 2 usually with rings of greywhite silky hairs; branching from basal or 2nd node up. Branches solitary on basal nodes, several to many at mid-culm and distal nodes, central obviously dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, with appressed, dull brown hairs near base, apex subtruncate; auricles unequal, horizontal along both sides of sheath apex, larger ones oblong to narrowly oblong, ca. 2 × 0.5–0.6 cm, smaller auricle elliptic, ca. 1/2 size of larger one; oral setae undulate; ligule 2–3 mm, dentate, shortly fringed; blade erect, narrowly ovate to ovatetriangular, ca. 1/2 as long as sheath, base slightly rounded and joined to auricles for ca. 3 mm, ca. 2/3 width of sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 10–20 × 1.3–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets several, clustered at nodes of flowering branches, linear-lanceolate, slightly flat, 3–4 cm; prophylls ovate, keels ciliolate toward apex, apex obtuse; gemmiferous bracts usually 2, ovate; florets 5–7, apical 1–2 usually sterile; rachilla segments flat, 3–4 mm, apex inflated and hairy. Glume 1, ovate, 6–8 mm, many-veined, apex mucronate; lemma ovate-elliptic, 1–1.4 cm, glabrous, many-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea slightly longer than lemma, sparsely very shortly ciliolate near apex or sometimes subglabrous, 6–7-veined between and 3–4-veined on either side of keels, apex obtuse; lodicules 3, unequal, posterior 1 slightly larger, obovate, base thickened, margin finely ciliate. Filaments short; anthers yellow, apex obtuse. Ovary ovoid, apex hispidulous; style very short; stigmas 3. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3299; Nan-Zhu 2775.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Vegetable.

Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. 孝順竹（蓬來竹）
Syst. Veg. 7(2): 1350. 1830; FGZ 771. 1956; FHN 4: 355. 1977; FRPS 9(1): 108, pl. 26: 1–15. 1996; FOC 22: 30. 2006; FGD 9: 251. 2009.
Arundo multiplex Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 58. 1790.
Arundinaria glaucescens (Willd.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 144, 152. 1812.
Bambusa glaucescens (Willd.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 7(4): 230. 1912; HKB 37. 1985.
Bambusa nana Roxb., Fl. Ind. (ed. 1832) 2: 199. 1832.
Ludolfia glaucescens Willd., Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 2: 320. 1808.

Culms suberect or apically slightly drooping, 4–7 m, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam.; internodes 30–50 cm, thinly white powdery, distally stiffly deciduously brown or dull brown hairy, especially densely so below nodes; wall usually rather thin; nodes slightly prominent, glabrous; branching from 2nd or 3rd node up. Branches several to many, clustered, subequal or central slightly dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, trapezoid, initially thinly white powdery, glabrous, asymmetrically arched, slanted along outer side, apex asymmetrically arched, convex; auricles very small to inconspicuous, oral setae few; ligule 1–1.5 mm, irregularly dentate; blade deciduous, erect, narrowly triangular, base nearly as wide as sheath apex, abaxially with scattered, stiff, dull brown hairs, adaxially scabrous, apex acuminate. Leaves 5–12 per ultimate branch; leaf blade abaxially pale glaucous, adaxially bright green, linear, 5–16 × 0.7–1.6 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or several clustered at nodes of flowering branches, linear to linear-lanceolate, 3–6 cm; prophylls ca. 3.5 mm, 2-keeled, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts usually 1 or 2, ovate to narrowly ovate, 4–7.5 mm, glabrous, 9–13-veined, apex obtuse or acute; florets (3–)5–13, middle ones fertile; rachilla segments flat, 4–4.5 mm, glabrous. Glumes absent; lemma asymmetrical, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 1.8 cm, glabrous, 19–21-veined, apex acute; palea linear, 1.4–1.6 cm, keels ciliolate, 6-veined between and 4-veined on one side and 3-veined on other side of keels, apex subtruncate, ciliolate, with a fine hairy tip on each side; lodicules 3, anterior 2 subovate, 2.5–3 mm, posterior narrowly lanceolate, 3–5 mm, margins glabrous. Filaments 0.8–1 cm; anthers purple, ca. 6 mm, apex penicillate. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1 mm, base with stalk ca. 1 mm, apex thickened and hispidulous; stigmas 3 or variable in number, ca. 5 mm, directly exserted from ovary apex. Mature caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui (cultivated). Y. S. Lau 3047; L. T. Lo 637; S. C. Lau 747. Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Wild and cultivated, fields, mountains, low hills, riversides. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental, hedges.

Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. 'Alphonse Karr' 小琴絲竹
R. A. Young, Agr. Handb. 193: 40. 1961; FRPS 9(1): 112. 1996.

It differs from B. multiplex var. multiplex by culm internodes yellow with green stripes.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. 'Fernleaf' 鳳尾竹
R. A. Young, Agric. Handb. 193: 40. 1961; FTW 5: 755. 1978; FRPS 9(1): 113. 1996.
Bambusa glaucescens (Willd.) Siebold ex Munro ‘Fernleaf’, Phytologia 52(4): 258. 1982; HKB 38. 1985.
Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. var. fernleaf R. A. Young, Natl. Hort. Mag. 25: 261. 1946.
Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. f. fernleaf (R. A. Young) T. P. Yi, J. Sichuan For. Sci. & Techn. 28(3): 17. 2007.

It differs from B. multiplex var. riviereorum by plants 3–6 m tall, culm internodes hollow, branchlets slightly curved downwards, with 9–13 leaves, leaf blade 3.3–6.5 × 0.4–0.7 cm.

Locality: Ma Liu Shui, Sheung Shui (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1116.
Distribution: S, E & SW China.
Ecology: Wild and cultivated, fields, mountains, low hills, riversides. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. 'Silverstripe' 銀絲竹
R. A. Young, Agric. Handb. 193: 41. 1961; FRPS 9(1): 112. 1996.
Bambusa glaucescens (Willd.) Siebold ex Munro ‘Silvrstripe’ L.C. Chia & But; Phytologia 52(4): 259. 1982; HKB 39. 1985.

It differs from B. multiplex var. multiplex by lower internodes of culm, culm sheath and few foliage, leaves green with white stripes.

Locality: Tai Po Kau (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2774.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. 'Stripestem Fernleaf' 小葉琴絲竹
R. A. Young, Agr. Handb. 193: 41. 1961; FRPS 9(1): 112. 1996.

It differs from B. multiplex ‘Fernleaf’ by plant shorter, 1–3 m, culms pale red first, turning yellow later, with green stripes, ultimate branches with 12–20 leaves, leaf blade 1.6–3.8 cm.

Locality: Sai Kung (cultivated). HK sheet 37609.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan, Sichuan (cultivated).
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. var. riviereorum Maire 觀音竹
Fl. Afrique N. 1: 355. 1952; FRPS 9(1): 111. 1996; FOC 22: 31. 2006.
Bambusa glaucescens (Willd.) Siebold ex Munro var. riviereorum (Maire) L. C. Chia & H. L. Fung, Phytologyia 52(4): 257. 1982; HKB 39. 1985.
Bambusa multiplex (Lour) Raeusch ex Schult. & Schult. f. var. nana auct. non (Roxb.) Keng f.: FGZ 771. 1956.

It differs from B. multiplex var. multiplex by culms 1–3 m, 3–5 mm in diam., internodes solid, branches usually bent downward, bow-shaped, culm sheath slanted along one side, apex asymmetrically arched-convex, ultimate branches with 13–23 leaves, blades small, 1.6–3.2 × 0.3–0.7 cm.

Locality: Lantau Island (cultivated). N. K. Chan 2795.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa lapidea McClure 油簕竹（油刺竹）
Lingnan Sci. J. 19: 531. 1940; FGZ 774. 1956; HKB 41. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 63, pl. 15: 13. 1996; FOC 22: 15. 2006; FGD 9: 233. 2009.
Bambusa miyiensis T. P. Yi, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 2(4): 99. 1982.

Culms 7  7 m, 4–7 cm in diam., basally straight, apically slightly drooping; internodes 20–35 cm, obviously shorter and slightly swollen near base and sometimes inconspicuously pale green striped and purple streaked, glabrous; wall 1–2 cm thick; nodes with a ring of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar, several basal nodes usually with short aerial roots, lower ones with a ring of silky hairs above sheath scar; branching from basal 3rd or 4th node up. Branches usually several to many, clustered at mid-culm and basal nodes, central 3 codominant; branchlets usually specialized into weak or tough thorns. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, leathery, glossy when fresh, ribbed-striate when dry, glabrous or stiffly hairy at basal margins only, apex subtruncate or slightly asymmetrical, arched; auricles undulate, wrinkled, inflated outward, densely hispidulous or subglabrous abaxially, unequal; larger auricle slightly decurrent, orbicular or ovate, 3.5–4 × 1–1.5 cm; small ones oblong or ovate, ca. 3 × 1–1.5 cm; ligule 4–5 mm, margin nearly entire and densely fimbriate; blade persistent, erect, inflated outward, ovate to oval, base slightly narrowed and then extended toward both sides and joined to auricles, apex abruptly acuminate, sharply tipped. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, usually 8–23 × 1–2 cm, both surfaces glabrous. Pseudospikelets linear, compressed, more than 2 cm; gemmiferous bracts 2–4; fertile florets 5–6, then 2 sterile florets; rachilla segments usually fistulose, ca. 2.5 cm, apex ciliolate. Glumes absent; lemma to 8.5 mm, abaxially glossy and glabrous, many-veined, margins glabrous, apex obtuse or acute and finely tipped; palea slightly shorter than lemma, keels ciliate near apex, 2-veined between and scabrous on either side of keels, apex obtuse or sometimes emarginate; lodicules 3, subequal, ovate or obovate, ca. 1.5 mm, margins ciliate, apex obtuse. Anthers ca. 4 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary narrowly obovoid, apex thickened and scabrous; style very short, scabrous; stigmas 3.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui, Kam Tin (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1104, 1132; N. K. Chan 2759.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Plains, hills, riversides, around villages. New shoots: Summer; flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Scaffolding, construction.

Bambusa pachinensis Hayata var. hirsutissima (Odash.) W. C. Lin 長毛米篩竹
Bull. Taiwan Forest. Res. Inst. 98: 21. 1964; FRPS 9(1): 105, pl. 25: 15 – 16. 1996; FOC 22: 28. 2006; FGD 9: 249. 2009.
Leleba beisitiku Odash. var. hirsutissima Odash., J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 8: 58. 1936.
Bambusa textilis McClure var. fusca McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 16. 1940; HKB 48. 1985.
Leleba pachinensis (Hayata) Nakai var. hir-sutissima (Odash.) W. C. Lin, Bull. Taiwan Forest. Res. Inst. 69: 61, fig. 28–29. 1961.

Culms 3–8 m, 1–4.5 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–70 cm, initially thinly white powdery, sparsely stiffly pale or dark brown strigose; wall thin; nodes flat, basal 5 nodes usually with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from 8th to 10th node up. Branches several to many, clustered, 3 central dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, leathery, rigid, broadly arched, uniformly stiffly dull brown strigose, apex slanted on outer side, asymmetrical; auricles unequal, slightly wrinkled, larger ones oblong or lanceolate, 1–1.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, ends subrounded and slanted downward, smaller auricle subovate, ca. 1/3 size of larger one, ends slightly ascending; oral setae fine, curved, long; ligule ca. 1 mm, long fimbriate, fimbriae 5–10 mm; blade erect, slightly asymmetrically ovate to ovate-triangular, 1/3–1/2 length of sheath, base slightly cordate, narrowed and joined with auricles for 2–3 mm, abaxially very sparsely brown hairy, adaxially scabrous, apex acuminate, apiculate. Leaf blade linear to lanceolate, 8–18 × 1–2 cm, abaxially densely villous, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 2–3.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm; prophylls ca. 2.5 mm, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts 2–3, ovate, to 7 mm, glabrous, 15–17-veined, apex obtuse and mucronate. Lemma ovate-elliptic, ca. 1.2 cm, glabrous, 17–19-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea lanceolate, ca. 1.1 cm, slightly shorter than lemma, keels not ciliate, 5–6-veined between and 3–4-veined on either side of keels, margin irregularly dentate, apex 3-fid and with a cluster of white long hairs; lodicules 3, unequal, anterior 2 spatulate, ca. 3 mm, margins long ciliate, posterior 1 nearly obovate-elliptic, ca. 1.6 mm. Filaments slender; anthers ca. 4 mm. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm, base stalked, apex thickened and hispid; style ca. 0.5 mm, hispid; stigmas 3, ca. 5 mm. Mature caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sha Tin, Lantau Island. Nan-Zhu 2776, 2785; HK sheet 0883.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Usually cultivated, low hills, around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Weaving.

Bambusa rutila McClure 木竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 19: 533. 1940; HKB 45. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 63, pl. 14: 11. 1996; FOC 22: 14. 2006; FGD 9: 232. 2009.
Bambusa shuangliuensis T. P. Yi, Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(4): 100, fig. 2. 1982.

Culms 8–12 m, 4–6 cm in diam., basally slightly flexuose, apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–35 cm; wall thick; lower internodes usually initially densely stiffly dark brown strigose, basal internodes sometimes with several inconspicuous pale yellow stripes; nodes with a ring of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar and a ring of stiff, brown hairs on sheath scar, several basal nodes usually with short aerial roots; branching from 3rd or 4th node up. Branches usually 3–12 on mid-culm and basal nodes; central 3 dominant, reflexed; those on lower nodes usually with branchlets specialized into weak or tough thorns.
