Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, glabrous or with stiff, dark brown hairs near margins and base, apex slightly oblique and truncate; auricles extremely unequal, abaxially densely hispidulous; larger auricle ovate-oblong, oblong, or narrowly reniform, inflated outward, undulate, wrinkled, ca. 1.5 cm wide; smaller auricle subovate or elliptic, ca. 1 cm wide, undulate, wrinkled; ligule 4–5 mm, dentate, fimbriate; blade persistent, erect, subtriangular or ovate, base nearly 2/5 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, usually 10–18 × 1–1.7 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets linear-lanceolate, compressed, to 3 cm; prophylls obtuse at apex, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts 3–8, ovate, 1–4 mm, margins ciliolate or subglabrous near apex, apex obtuse and finely tipped; florets ca. 9, apical 1–2 florets sterile; rachilla segments 2–3 mm, apex ciliolate. Glumes absent; lemma ovate-lanceolate, to 8 mm, abaxially glabrous, many-veined, margins ciliolate near apex, finely tipped, apex obtuse or acute and scabrous; palea longer or shorter than lemma, keels ciliate or scabrous at apex, 2–3-veined between keels, apex penicillate; lodicules 3, subequal, ovate or obovate, margins ciliate. Anther obtuse at apex. Ovary obovoid, apex thickened and hairy; style very short; stigmas 3, scabrid.

Locality: Fanling, Chung Mei (cultivated). N. K. Chan 2755; HK sheet 16466.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan.
Ecology: Open fields, around villages. New shoots: Summer; flowering: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Materials (construction).

Bambusa sinospinosa McClure 車筒竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 19: 411. 1940; HKB 46. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 56, pl. 13: 1–11. 1996; FOC 22: 12. 2006; FGD 9: 229. 2009.

Culms 15–24 m, 8–14 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes 20–26 cm, mainly glabrous but with a ring of grey silky hairs below basal 1 or 2 nodes; wall 10–30 mm thick; branching to base. Branches usually solitary at lower nodes, with tough thorns; branchlets interwoven; branches 3–several above lower nodes. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, leathery, densely stiffly dark brown hairy toward base, apex truncate; auricles usually reflexed, oblong to obovate, subequal, rugose, adaxially densely strigose, margin with undulate or erect setae; ligule 3–5 mm, dentate, fimbriate; blade erect or recurved, base ca. 1/2 width of sheath apex. Leaf blade linearlanceolate, 7–17 × 1.2–1.6 cm, both surfaces glabrous or abaxially proximally pilose. Pseudospikelets solitary or several clustered at each node of flowering branch, linear to linear-lanceolate, slightly compressed, to 4 cm, prophylls obtuse, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts 3–5, narrowly triangular or subovate, glabrous, obtuse; fertile florets 6–12; rachilla internodes 2–4 mm. Glumes usually absent; lemma ovate-oblong, 5–9.5 mm, many-veined, apex obtusely acute or acute with fine tip; palea usually slightly longer than lemma, keels ciliolate, 3–5-veined between keels; lodicules 3, unequal, obovate, ca. 1.4 mm, obtuse, margins ciliate. Filaments distinct; anther obtuse at apex. Ovary narrow, apex thickened and hispidulous; style slender, hispidulous; stigmas 3.

Locality: New Territiories (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2772.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Riversides, near villages. New shoots: May–Jun.; flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Materials (construction), environmental.
Notes: Bambusa arundo sensu Benth. (FHK 435. 1861) perhaps belongs to this species.

Bambusa textilis McClure 青皮竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 14. 1940; FGZ 772. 1956; HKB 47. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 122, pl. 30: 1–12. 1996; FOC 22: 29. 2006; FGD 9: 250. 2009.

Culms 8–10 m, 3–5 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes green, 40–70 cm, initially thinly white powdery, ± stiffly pale brown hairy; wall 2–5 mm thick; nodes flat, glabrous; branching from 7th to 11th node upward. Culm sheaths deciduous, leathery, rigid, slightly glossy, basally stiffly dull brown strigose, apex slightly slanted and asymmetric, broadly arched; auricles unequal, ends not decurrent, larger one narrowly oblong to lanceolate, slightly slanted, ca. 1.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, smaller one oblong, not slanted, ca. 1/2 size of larger; oral setae slender, undulate; ligule ca. 2 mm, dentate or sometimes laciniate, ciliolate; blade deciduous, erect, narrowly ovatetriangular, ca. 2/3 as long as sheath, abaxially sometimes stiffly hairy between veins, basally sparsely dull brown hairy, adaxially scabrid, base slightly cordate, narrowed, nearly 2/3 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 9–17 × 1–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or several to many, clustered at each node of flowering branches, dull purple when fresh, bronze-coloured when dry, linear-lanceolate, slightly curved, 3–4.5 × 0.5–0.8 cm; prophylls ovate, ca. 3 mm, keels glabrous; gemmiferous bracts 2–3, ovate, 3–4.5 mm, glabrous, apex acute, mucronate; florets 5–8, apical one sterile; rachilla segments subterete or flat, ca. 4 mm, apex enlarged. Glume 1, ovate, ca. 6 mm, ca. 20-veined, glabrous, apex acute, mucronate; lemma elliptic, 1.1–1.4 cm, glabrous, ca. 25-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea lanceolate, 1.2–1.4 cm, slightly longer than lemma, keels glabrous, ca. 10-veined between and 4-veined on either side of keels; lodicules unequal; anterior 2 subspatulate, ca. 3 mm, margins long ciliate; posterior obovate-elliptic, ca. 2 mm. Filaments slender; anthers yellow, ca. 5 mm. Ovary broadly ovoid, ca. 2 mm in diam., base stalked, apex thickened and hispidulous; style ca. 0.7 mm, hispidulous; stigmas 3, 6–7 mm. Mature caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Kwun Yam Shan, Sheung Shui (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1109; Nan-Zhu 2768; S. C. Lau 753.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi. E
cology: Usually cultivated, along rivers, around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Weaving, ornamental.

Bambusa textilis McClure var. glabra McClure 光稈青皮竹（黃竹）
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 16. 1940; HKB 49. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 125. 1996; FOC 22: 30. 2006; FGD 9: 251. 2009.

Culms 3–5 cm in diam.; internodes and sheaths glabrous. Culm sheath blade nearly 1/2 as long as sheath proper, base slightly rounded; ligule 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: Tai Po, Chung Mei (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2753.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa textilis McClure var. gracilis McClure 崖州竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 16. 1940; HKB 50. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 126. 1996; FOC 22: 30. 2006; FGD 9: 251. 2009.

Culms slender, less than 3 cm in diam. Culm sheath with sparse, stiff, dull brown hairs near both sides and base, blade to 1/2 as long as sheath proper, base slightly rounded; ligule ca. 1 mm.

Locality: New Territories (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2764.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa tuldoides Munro 青稈竹（花眉竹）
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 93. 1868; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 51. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 87, pl. 20: 1–10. 1996; FOC 22: 23. 2006; FGD 9: 243, fig. 131. 2009.
Bambusa angulata Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 94. 1868.
Bambusa breviflora Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 96. 1868.
Bambusa fauriei Hack., Bull. Herb. Boissier, sér. 2, 4(6): 529. 1904.
Bambusa flavonoda W. T. Lin, J. Bamboo Res. 1986(2): 23. 1986.
Bambusa longiflora W. T. Lin, Bull. Bot. Lab. N.-E. Forest. Inst., Harbin 1980(6): 85, fig. 1. 1980.
Bambusa parvifolia W. T. Lin, Bamboo Res. 1986(2): 22. 1986.
Chimonobambusa angulata (Munro) Nakai, Sci. Educ. (Tokyo) 15(16): 67. 1932.
Tetragonocalamus angulatus (Munro) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 9(2): 86, 88, pl. 10. 1933.
Bambusa tulda auct. non Roxb.: FHK 434. 1861.

Culms 6–10 m, 3–5 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–36 cm, initially thinly white powdery; wall thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal 1 or 2 with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from base up. Branches several to many, clustered, central 3 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, convex and slanted along outer margin for 1/10–1/8 of length of sheath, with 1–3 pale yellow stripes toward outer margin, glabrous, apex asymmetrically arched; auricles unequal, outer one larger, ovate to ovate-elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 1–1.4 cm, slightly wrinkled; inner one smaller, ovate to elliptic, ascending, ca. 1/2 size of larger; oral setae slender, undulate; ligule 3–4 mm, laciniate, dznsely fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect, asymmetrically ovate-triangular to narrowly triangular, sparsely deciduously stiffly brown or pale brown strigose, base slightly rounded and then extending outward to join auricles for 5–7 mm, nearly 2/3–3/4 width of sheath apex, margin slightly wrinkled near base and fringed, apex subulate, acuminate. Leaf blade lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 10–18 × 1.5–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose near base. Pseudospikelets several at each node of flowering branches, pale green, linear-lanceolate, slightly flat, 2–3 × 0.3–0.4 cm; prophylls 2-keeled, keels ciliate, subtended by sheath-like bracts; gemmiferous bracts 2, glabrous, apex obtuse; florets 6 – 7, proximally and distally sterile; rachilla segments flat, 3–4 mm, apex inflated and cupular, hairy. Glume 1, ovateoblong, ca. 8.5 mm, glabrous, apex acute; lemma ovate-oblong, 1.1–1.4 cm, ca. 19-veined, glabrous, apex obtuse, mucronate; palea about as long as or slightly shorter than lemma, 4-veined between and 4-veined on either side of keels, penicillate; lodicules 3, anterior 2 obovate, oblique, short, ca. 2.5 mm, broad, margins long ciliate; posterior 1 long, ca. 3 mm, narrow. Anthers ca. 3 mm, apex emarginate. Ovary obovoid, ca. 1.2 mm, stalked, apex thickened and hispid; style ca. 0.7 mm, hispid; stigmas 3, ca. 5.5 mm. Caryopsis terete, slightly curved, ca. 8 mm, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., apex obtuse and thickened, hispid, with remains of style.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1108; Y. S. Lau 849, 2686.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Low hills, river banks, commonly cultivated around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Timber, weaving.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance 3657, K) was collected from Hong Kong in 1862.

Bambusa ventricosa McClure 佛肚竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 17: 57. 1938; FGZ 770. 1956; FHN 4: 354. 1977; FTW 5: 764, pl. 1511. 1978; HKB 52. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 70, pl. 15: 1–12. 1996; FOC 22: 17. 2006; FGD 9: 236. 2009.
Leleba ventricosa (McClure) W. C. Lin, Bull. Taiwan Forest Res. Inst. 150: 1305, fig. 1. 1963.

Culms dimorphic; normal culms 8–10 m, 3–5 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–35 cm, basally slightly swollen, not white powdery, initially glabrous; lower nodes with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from 3rd or 4th node up, basal 1 or 2 nodes also with short aerial roots; branches 1–3 on lower nodes; branchlets of these sometimes condensed into weak thorns; branches several to many at mid-culm and upper nodes, with central 3 slightly longer and thicker. Abnormal culms (usual in potted plants) 25–50 cm, 1–2 cm in diam., internodes shortened and swollen at base, branch internodes also shortened and swollen; branches only on upper nodes, usually solitary, without thorns. Culm sheaths deciduous, obviously ribbedstriate, glabrous, apex nearly symmetrical, broadly arched or subtruncate; auricles unequal; larger auricle narrowly ovate to ovatelanceolate, 5–6 mm; smaller auricle ovate, 3–5 mm; oral setae curved; ligule 0.5–1 mm, very shortly finely fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect or recurved, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, base slightly arched, narrowed, slightly narrower than sheath apex. Leaf sheath glabrous; ligule subtruncate, very short; auricles ovate or falcate; oral setae several, curved; blade linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, 9–18 × 1–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or many clustered on each node, linear-lanceolate, slightly compressed, 3–4 cm; prophylls oval, 2.5–3 mm, 2-keeled, apex obtuse; gemmiferous bracts 1–2, narrowly ovate, 4–5 mm, 13–15-veined, apex acute; florets 6–8, basal 1–2 and apical 2–3 usually sterile; rachilla segments flat, 2–3 mm, apex inflated and cupular. Glumes absent or 1, ovate-elliptic, 6.5–8 mm, 15–17-veined, apex acute; lemma ovate-elliptic, 9–11 mm, glabrous, 19–21-veined, apex acute; palea nearly as long as lemma, ciliolate near apex, 4-veined between and on either side of keels, apex acuminate with a cluster of white hairs; lodicules 3, ca. 2 mm, margins long ciliate, anterior 2 slightly asymmetrical, posterior broadly elliptic. Filaments slender; anthers yellow, ca. 6 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary broadly ovoid, 1–1.2 mm, stalked, apex thickened and hairy; style very short, hairy; stigmas 3, ca. 6 mm. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Po and gardens (cultivated). S. C. Lau 793.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Late summer to autumn.
Uses: Hedges, ornamental.
Notes: Widely cultivated in S China as an ornamental potted plant, this bamboo is sometimes considered to be a cultivar of Bambusa tuldoides, but the flowering material on which that decision was based, collected in the United States, may not represent this species. Moreover, in China the culm sheath of B. ventricosa is substantially different from that of B. tuldoides.

Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. 龍頭竹（銀竹、泰山竹）
Coll. Pl. 2: 26. 1810; FTW 5: 765, pl. 1512. 1978; HKB 53. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 96, pl. 24: 1–3. 1996; FOC 22: 25. 2006; FGD 9: 254. 2009.

Clumps rather open. Culms 8–15 m, 5–9 cm in diam., basally straight or flexuose, apically drooping; internodes deep green, 20–30 cm, initially thinly white powdery, stiffly pale brown strigose; wall slightly thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal several with aerial roots and rings of greyish white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; usually branching from lower nodes. Branches several to many, clustered, central dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, densely stiffly deciduously dark brown hairy, apex arched below blade, concave below auricles; auricles conspicuous, ascending, nearly equal in shape and size, oblong or reniform, 8–10 mm; oral setae curved, fine; ligule 3–4 mm, serrate, very shortly white ciliolate; blade deciduous, erect or deflexed, broadly triangular to triangular, base slightly rounded, ca. 1/2 width of sheath apex, abaxially sparsely stiffly dull brown hairy, adaxially densely stiffly dull brown hairy between veins, apex involute, sharply apiculate. Leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, 10–30 × 1.3–2.5 cm, both surfaces glabrous. Pseudospikelets several, clustered at nodes, narrowly lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, slightly flattened, 2–3.5 × 0.4–0.5 mm, apparently bifid; gemmiferous bracts several; florets 5–10; rachilla segments 1.5–3 mm. Glumes 1–2, abaxially shortly hairy near apex, apex apiculate; lemma 8–10 mm, abaxially shortly hairy near apex, apex apiculate; palea slightly shorter than lemma, keels ciliolate; lodicules 3, 2–2.5 mm, margins long ciliate. Anthers ca. 6 mm, apex penicillate. Style 3–7 mm, slender; stigmas 3, short.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui, Shing Mun Arboretum and gardens (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1103; N. K. Chan 2763.
Distribution: Yunnan; SE Asia; cultivated in the tropical and subtropical regions all over the world.
Ecology: Riversides, open forests. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. 'Vittata' 黃金間碧竹
Fieldiana, Bot., n.s. 24(2): 60. 1955; FRPS 9(1): 97. 1996; FGD 9: 254. 2009.
Bambusa striata Lodd. ex Lindl., Penny Cyclop. 3: 357. 1835.
Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. var. striata (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Gamble, Ann. Roy. Bot. Gard. (Calcutta) 7: 44. 1896; FGZ 771. 1956; FHN 4: 354. 1977; FTW 5: 766. 1978.
Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. var. vittata Rivière & C. Rivière, Bull. Soc. Natl. Acclim. France , ser. 3, 5: 640. 1878; HKB 54. 1985.

It differs from B. vulgaris by culm internodes yellow with green stripes.

Locality: Widely cultivated in Hong Kong. K. S. Pang 13.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. 'Wamin' 大佛肚竹
McClure, Bamb. 162, f. 72(5–6). 1966; FTW 5: 766. 1978; HKB 55. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 97. 1996; FGD 9: 255. 2009.
Bambusa ? wamin Brandis ex E. G. Camus, Bambus. 135. 1913.
Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. f. waminii T. H. Wen, J. Bamboo Res. 4(2): 16. 1985.

It differs from B. vulgaris by culm internodes shortened and basally swollen.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 273.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Barleria cristata L. 假杜鵑
Sp. Pl. 636. 1753; FHK 262. 1861; FKH 199. 1912; FHN 3: 553. 1974; FRPS 70: 63. 2002.

Under shrub, to 2 m tall; stems terete, branched, covered with soft hairs. Petioles (0–)0.3–1 cm; leaf blades papery, elliptic, oblong or ovate, 2–4 × 1.3–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute, sometimes acuminate, margin entire, villous on both surfaces, especially along the veins, lateral veins 4–7 pairs. Flowers subsessile, in dense axillary clusters becoming capitate at branch ends. Bracts absent; bracteoles very variable, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1.0–2.2 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin usually spiny‑margined but sometimes bristly pilose‑margined, spinescent with age, 3–7‑veined. Outer calyx‑lobes narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, 1.2–2.5 × 0.5–1.3 cm, apex mucronate, margin spiny, pilose, reticulate, inner calyx‑lobes linear or lanceolate, 6–12 mm, scarious‑margined, 1‑veined. Corolla purplish‑blue, 5 – 6.5 cm; tube pilose, narrowly cylindric in the lower half, then gradually widened; lobes equal, oblong‑elliptic, ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous. Fertile stamens 4, didynamous; filaments pilose, especially towards the base; staminodes 1, filament sparsely pilose. Ovary oblong‑ellipsoidal, glabrous; styles linear, ca. 2.5 cm long, glabrous; stigma slightly inflated. Capsules oblong, 1.4–1.8 cm, black, acute at both ends, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds suborbicular or ovate, ca. 5 × 4 mm, flattened, densely adpressed pubescent.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. Y. S. Lau 182; H. C. Tang 1478; Y. W. Lam 1209.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides, hillslopes. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.
Uses. Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Barnardia japonica (Thunb.) Schult. & Schult. f. 綿棗兒
Syst. Veg. 7: 555. 1829; FOC 24: 203. 2000; FGD 6: 337, fig. 192. 2005.
Scilla chinensis Benth., FHK 373. 1861, nom. illeg. (included B. scilloides Lindl.).
Scilla scilloides (Lindl.) Druce, Rep. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles. 4: 646. 1917; FRPS 14: 166, fig. 22. 1980; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.
Barnardia scilloides Lindl., Sketch Veg. Swan R. pl. 1029. 1826.
Ornithogalum japonicum Thunb. Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 328. 1784.

Perennial herb. Bulbs ovoid, 1–3 cm across, covered with blackish brown tunic. Leaves narrow-linear, 15–30 cm × 2–8 mm. Scape erect, longer than leaves. Raceme 5–20 cm, densely flowered; bracts narrowly lanceolate, membranous; pedicels 6–12 mm. Perianth segments rose purple, pink, or white, obovate, elliptic, or narrowly elliptic, 2.5–4 × 1–2 mm, slightly connate and discoid at base. Stamens 2–3.5 mm; filaments sublanceolate, papillose-puberulent or glabrous. Ovary 1.5–2 mm, papillosepuberulent; style 1–1.3 mm. Capsule subobovoid, 3–6 × 2–4 mm. Seeds 1–3, 2.5–5 mm, black.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Violet, Tai Tam Tuk, Victoria Peak. P. S. Choi 51; Y. S. Lau 2335.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shanxi, Henan, Hebei, Nei Mongol, Jilin, Liaoning, Heilongjiang, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, E Russia.
Ecology: Hillsides, amongst grass. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Barthea barthei (Hance ex Benth.) Krasser 棱果花（芭茜）

Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(7): 175, fig. 768. 1893; FRPS 53(1): 179. 1984.

Dissochaeta barthei Hance ex Benth., FHK 115. 1861.

Barthea chinensis Hook. f., Gen. Pl. 1: 751. 1867, nom. illeg. superfl.; FKH 107. 1912.


Shrub, 0.7 – 1.5(–3) m tall. Branchlets ± quadrangular, puberulous and glandular scurfy when young. Leaves opposite; petiole 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade firmly papery to subleathery, elliptic, subrotund, ovate, or ovate-lanceolate, (3.5–)6–11(–15) × (1.8–)2.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly obtuse, apex acuminate, margin entire or serrulate, glabrous, scurfy abaxially, 5-basiveined, lateral veins inconspicuous. Inflorescences terminal, cymose, (1–)3-flowered but usually only 1 fertile; pedicels ca. 7 mm, 4-ribbed, scurfy. Calyx-tube ca. 0.6 or 1.4 cm, 4-ribbed, with narrow wings on ribs, densely scurfy; calyx-lobes triangular or linear-lanceolate, apex cuspidate, ca. 3 mm, margin membranous. Petals white, tinged with pink abaxially, oblong-elliptic to obovate, 1.1 – 1.8 × 1 – 1.6 cm, apically oblique. Anthers with 2 bristles at the base, the 4 longer stamens ca. 1 cm, with an oblong dorsal appendage or spur, the 4 others ca. 3 mm, without the dorsal appendage. Ovary 4-ribbed, glabrous, crowned by an irregularly lobed ring, with short glandular bristles. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca.1 × 0.6 cm, opening in 4 valves.


Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1286, 1382; HK sheet 1791; N. K. Chun 40219, 40153 (IBSC); Y. Tsiang 41 (IBSC).

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan.

Ecology: Mixed forests, forested mountain slopes, open thickets, wooded ravines, along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Oct. – Dec. or May.

Notes: The syntype specimens were collected from Victoria Peak by Hance, Barthe and Wilford around 1850s. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Basella alba L. 落葵（潺菜）
Sp. Pl. 272. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 2: 340. 1996; FRPS 26: 44. 1996; FGD 4: 115, fig. 72. 2000; FOC 5: 445. 2003.
Basella rubra L., Sp. Pl. 272. 1753; FGZ 149, fig. 60. 1956; FHN 1: 411, fig. 221. 1964.

Perennial twining vine. Stems fleshy, glabrous, green or purplish. Leaves fleshy; petioles 1–3 cm; leaf blade ovate or suborbicular, 3–12 × 3–10 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire. Spikes axillary, 4–20 cm. Flowers small, sessile, in small clusters. Perianth fleshy, lower part white, apex purple, with 5 obtuse lobes. Stamens 5, included; filaments erect in bud. Ovary globose; styles 3. Fruit subglobse, 5 –7 mm in diam., enclosed within fleshy persistent perianth, dark purple when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 495; Y. S. Lau 2846.
Distribution: Pantropical. Widely cultivated in China, sometimes escaped from cultivation.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Food (vegetable), ornamental.

Bassia scoparia (L.) A. J. Scott 地膚
Fedd. Repert. 89: 108. 1978.
Kochia scoparia (L.) Schrad. in Neues Journ. 3: 85. 1809; FGD 3: 63. 1995; FOC 5: 385. 2003.
Chenopodium scoparium L., Sp. Pl. 221. 1753.

Annual herb, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems terete, slightly pubescent or glabrous on lower parts. Leaves sessile, lanceolate or linear lanceolate, 0.7– 5 × 1–7 mm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous or slightly hairy, 3-veined. Spikes 1–3-flowered, axillary. Flowers bisexual or pistillate; perianth subglobose, green-yellowish; lobes 5, subtriangular, winged on outside. Stamens 5, exserted, inserted at base of perianth. Anthers yellowish, ovoid. Ovary oblate; style very short; stigmas 2–3, filiform. Utricles oblate, subtended by persistent perianth, pericarps membranaceous. Seeds black-brown, ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Lam Tsuen (Kadoorie Farm).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Europe, Asia.
Ecology: Farmland, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Bauhinia championii (Benth.) Benth. 缺葉藤（龍鬚藤）
FHK 99. 1861; FKH 90. 1912; FHN 2: 221. 1965; FRPS 39: 172. 1988; FGD 5: 194. 2003; FGX 2: 479, pl. 202: 1 – 9. 2005.
Phanera championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 78. 1852.

Woody tendrilled vine; branches rusty pubescent; tendrils simple or in pairs. Petioles 0.8–4 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades papery, ovate to ovate-lanceolate or cordate, 5.5–10 × 2–11 cm, base truncate or cordate, apex acuminate, rounded, obtuse or bilobed, usually acuminate at apex of lobes, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent, gradually glabrescent, glaucous when dry, 5–9-veined. Racemes axillary, sometimes opposite to leaves or several in panicle, 5–25 cm, grey pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles small, subulate, ca. 1 mm. Flower-buds ellipsoidal, 2.5–4 mm, grey pubescent. Pedicels slender, 0.7–1.5 cm. Hypanthium funnel-shaped, ca. 2 mm; sepals lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Petals white, spathulate, ca. 4.5 mm, clawed. Fertile stamens 3, filaments ca. 5.5 mm, glabrous; staminodes 2. Ovary short stipitate, pubescent, style short, stigma small. Pods obovate-oblong or narrowly oblong, 5–13 × 1.5–3.5 cm, leathery, flat, glabrous. Seeds 2–5, orbicular, flat, 0.8–1.3 cm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1872, 2038; Y. S. Lau 1272.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thin forest and thickets. Flowering: Jun. – Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Bauhinia corymbosa Roxb. ex DC. 首冠藤（深裂葉羊蹄甲）
Mem. Legum. 13: 487. 1825; FKH 90. 1912; FRPS 39: 196. 1988; FGD 5: 196. 2003.
Phanera corymbosa (Roxb. ex DC) Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 264. 1852.

Woody tendrilled vine; young branches tendrils, petioles and inflorescence reddish pubescent; tendrils simple or paired. Petioles 0.7– 2 cm; stipules linear, slightly falcate, pointed, ca. 2 mm; leaf blades papery, suborbicular, 1.5– 4 × 2– 4 cm, 2-lobed to 2/3– 3/4 of the length, base truncate or slightly cordate, apex of lobes rounded, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glabrous or reddish brown pubescent at base and along the veins, 7-veined. Inflorescences terminal or leaf opposite, pyramidal or conical corymbs. Peduncles short. Pedicels slender, ca. 1 cm. Bracts and bracteoles subulate, ca. 3 mm. Flower-buds ovoid, apex acute, reddish brown pubescent. Hypanthium 1.8 – 2.5 cm. Sepals ca. 6 mm, abaxially pubescent, reflexed when anthesis. Petals white, pinkish striated, broadly spathulate or suborbicular, 7 – 12 × 6 – 10 mm, abaxially velutinous, margin revolute, claw short. Fertile stamens 3, filaments reddish, 0.8–1 cm; staminodes 2–5. Ovary stipitate, glabrous; stigma peltate. Pods narrowly oblong, 10–25 × 1.5– 2.8 cm, thick leathery, flat, straight or slightly falcate, glabrous, glossy. Seed many, oblong, ca. 8 mm in diam., brown.

Locality: Yim Tin Tsai, Lantau Island. Gibbson 5616; F. W. Xing 9675.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Forest and thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bauhinia glauca (Wall. ex Benth.) Benth. 粉葉羊蹄甲（羊蹄甲藤）
FHK 99. 1861; FKH 90. 1912; FRPS 39: 194. 1998; FGD 5: 196. 2003; FGX 2: 486, pl. 206: 1 – 9. 2005.
Phanera glauca Wall. ex Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 265. 1852.

Woody tendrilled vines; young branches reddish pubescent, soon glabrescent. Petioles 2–4 cm, sparsely pubescent; stipules linear, ca. 4 mm; leaf blades papery, suborbicular, 4–9 × 4–10 cm, 2-lobed to 1/3–1/2 of the length, with rather narrow sinus and ovate, obtuse lobes, base broadly cordate or truncate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sometimes sparsely pubescent, 9 –11-veined. Inflorescences of short, compact corymbs, lateral. Peduncles 2.5–6 cm, rusty pubescent, gradually glabrescent. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Flower-buds ovoid, rusty pubescent. Bracts subulate, ca. 5 mm; bracteoles similar but smaller, 4–5 mm, inserted in the lower half of the pedicel. Hypanthium 1.2–1.5 cm, sparsely pubescent. Sepals ovate, ca. 6 mm, acute, abaxially rusty pubescent. Petals white, obovate, subequal, margin undulate, 1–1.2 cm, claw ca. 8 mm. Fertile stamens 3, filaments pink, longer than petals; staminodes 5–7. Ovary glabrous stipitate; styles ca. 4 mm, stigma oblique, peltate. Pods narrowly oblong, straight or falcate, 12–32 × 2–6 cm, thin, glabrous, indehiscent. Seeds 10–20, ovate, flat, ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1975; HK sheet 40113, 40600.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi; India, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul. – Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bauhinia purpurea L. 紅花羊蹄甲
Sp. Pl. 1: 375. 1753; FHN 2: 216. 1965; FRPS 39: 156. 1988; FGD 5: 190. 2003; FGX 2: 475. 2005.
Phanera purpurea (L.) Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 262. 1852.

Evergreen tree, 5–10 m tall; bark greyish, smooth; branches glabrescent. Petioles 2.5–4.5 cm; stipules minute, 1–2 mm; leaf blades thick-papery, suborbicular in outline, 10–15 × 9–14 cm, abaxially sparsely pubescent, adaxially glabrous, 2-lobed to 1/3–1/2 of the length, base rounded to cordate, apex of lobes rounded, palmately 9–13-veined. Racemes lateral or terminal, 6–10-flowered, sometimes compound, brown sericeous. Bracts ovate-acute, 1–2 mm; bracteoles similar, inserted at about the middle of the pedicel. Buds clavate, velvety, 4–5-angled mainly toward the twisted apex, 3–5 mm. Peduncles 7–12 mm. Hypanthium turbinate, 7–12 mm. Sepals splitting on one side into 2 reflexed lobes, 2–2.5 cm. Petals 5, reddish, narrowly lanceolate, the posterior oblanceolate, 3–5 cm, claw 5–10 mm, pink or dark purple. Fertile stamens 3(–4); filaments shortly connate at base, 3–4 cm; anthers 5–7 mm; staminodes 5 or 6, filiform, 6–10 mm. Ovary velvety, 1 cm, stipitate; stipe 1 cm, yellowish brown sericeous; styles short; stigma peltate, oblique, flat. Pods linear, compressed, 12–25 × 2–2.5 cm, glabrous, irregularly veined, dehiscent. Seeds ca. 10, suborbicular, flat, 1.2–1.5 cm in diam., dark brown.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 637, 1352; HK sheet 8645.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; tropical Asia, cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bauhinia variegata L. 宮粉羊蹄甲
Sp. Pl. 1: 375. 1753; FKH 90. 1912; FHN 2: 218. 1965; FRPS 39: 159. 1988; FGD 5: 190. 2003; FGX 2: 475. 2005.
Phanera variegata (L.) Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 262. 1852.
Bauhinia variegata var. chinensis DC., Prodr. 2: 514. 1825.

Tree, up to 15 m tall; branches greyish pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 2.5–3.5 cm, puberulous to glabrous; stipules minute, 1–2 mm, caducous; leaf blades broadly ovate to orbicular in outline, 5–9 × 7–11 cm, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glaucous and sparsely greyish pubescent, 2-lobed to 1/3 of the length, base cordate, sometimes truncate, apex of lobes rounded, palmately 11–13-veined. Racemes lateral or terminal, subcorymbose, few-flowered; axis tomentose. Peduncles stout and short. Pedicels short, 3–5 mm. Bracts triangular, very small, caducous; bracteoles similar, inserted below the middle of pedicel. Flower-buds fusiform, 3 –4 cm, finely hairy. Hypanthium infundibuliform, ca. 15 cm long. Sepals 2–3 cm, splitting on one side; lobes 2–3 cm. Petals subequal, violet, obovate or oblanceolate, 4–5 cm, with a short claw, margin often crisped. Fertile stamens 5, unequal; filaments 2–4 mm, glabrous; anthers 6–7 mm, elliptic; staminodes 5, capillary, 0.5– 1 cm. Ovary pubescent particularly along the sultures, ca. 2 cm, stipitate; stipe pubescent, 1.5 cm; style short; stigma small, capitate. Pod strap-shaped, obliquely striate, 15–25 × 1.5–2 cm, dehiscent. Seeds 10–15, flat, orbicular, 1.0–1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 8420; H. C. Tang 92; HK sheet 41000.
Distribution: S China; Malaysia, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, India.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bauhinia variegata var. candida (Aiton) Buch.-Ham. 白花洋紫荊

Trans. Linn. Soc. London 13(2): 497. 1822; FRPS 39: 159. 1988; FGD 5: 190. 2003.

Bauhinia candida Aiton, Hort. Kew. 2: 49. 1789.

Bauhinia variegata var. alboflava de Wit, Reinwardtia 3: 412. 1956. 


Petals white. Staminodes absent.


Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 17; HK sheet 41004, 41005.

Distribution: S China; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, India.

Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.

Uses: Ornamental.

Bauhinia × blakeana Dunn 洋紫荊
J. Bot. 46(10): 325. 1908; FRPS 39: 156. 1988; FGD 5: 191. 2003; FGX 2: 475, pl. 199: 1 – 2. 2005.

Tree, 8 –10 m; branchlets pubescent. Petioles 3.5 – 4 cm, brown pubescent; leaf blades sub-leathery, suborbicular or broadly cordate in outline, 8.5– 13 × 9– 14 cm, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely pubescent, 2-lobed to 1/4– 1/3 of the length, base cordate or sometimes truncate, apex of lobes obtuse, 9 – 13-veined. Racemes terminal or axillary, sometimes paniculate. Bracts and bracteoles triangular, acute at apex, 2 –3.5 mm. Flower-buds fusiform, ca. 2.5 cm. Hypanthium turbinate. Petals red, subequal, oblanceolate, clawed, 5 – 8 × 2.5 – 3 cm. Fertile stamens 5; staminodes 2 – 5. Ovary pubescent, long stipitate. Pods usually not produced.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2651; P. S. Choi 22; HK sheet 40999.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was originally discovered near the seashore in Pok Fu Lam by the fathers of the Mission Etrangérès in Hong Kong, who produced cuttings. The type specimen was collected from a tree raised from such cuttings and cultivated in the Hong Kong Botanical Gardens in 1905. The specific epithet commemorated Sir Henry and Lady Blake for their support to the Gardens. The species was adopted as the city flower of Hong Kong in 1965 and became the floral emblem of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in 1997. Local researchers, based on molecular evidence, confirmed that this species was a hybrid between B. purpurea L. and B. variegata L. (Amer. J. Bot. 92: 525 –533. 2005; J. Integr. Plant Biol. 50: 111– 118. 2008).
records.uses:
Ornamental.

Begonia cucullata Willd. var. hookeri (Sweet)）L. S. Sm. & Schub. 四季秋海棠
Darwiniana 5: 104. 1941; C. M. Hu in FGD 3: 146. 1995.
Begonia hookeri Sweet, Hort. Brit. (ed. 2) 437. 1850.
Begonia semperflorens auct. non Link & Otto: FGZ 190. 1956; FHN 1: 489. 1964.

Perennial herbs, 15 – 45 cm tall. Stems succulent, green or reddish. Leaves alternate, ± fleshy; petioles 0.5 –2 (–3) cm; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 5 –10 × 3.5 –7.5 cm, apex rounded or obtuse, base broadly rounded or slightly cordate and oblique, margin serrulate, ciliate, shining adaxially. Cymes axillary. Peduncle 1.5 – 4 cm. Flowers rosy, pink or white; male flowers: 1–2 cm in diam., perianth-segments 4, outer 2 suborbicular, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., inner 2 obovate-oblong, 8–10 × 4–5 mm; female flowers: smaller, perianth segments 5; ovary 3-locular. Capsule 10–12 mm long, with 3 slightly unequal wings.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 12255.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Begonia fimbristipula Hance 紫背天葵
J. Bot. 21: 202. 1883; FKH 113. 1912; FHN 1: 490. 1964; FGD 3: 146. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 190. 1999.

Perennial small herb, with tuberous root. Stem very short, less than 1.5 cm, usually with only one leaf. Petioles shorter or longer than leaf blade, with coarse hairs or glabrescent. Stipules small 2–3 mm, ovate-lanceolate, margin fimbriate. Leaf blade orbicular- or ovatecordate, 4 –15 × 3 –12 cm, apex acuminate, base cordate, basal lobes more or less overlapped, sparsely or densely covered with small coarse hairs on adaxial surface, usually purplish and strigose along veins on abaxial surface, margin irregularly double-serrate. Cymes twice or thrice branched. Peduncles slender, 3 –15 cm, red, glabrous. Flowers pink, slightly scented; male flowers: perianth segments 4, outer 2 ovate, 6 –12 mm, inner 2 obovate-oblong; female flowers: smaller, perianth-segments 3, two larger, half-orbicular, ca. 3 mm, another one smaller and narrower, oblong; ovary 3-locular. Capsule triangular, glabrous, with 3 unequal wings.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1402; L. T. Lo 47.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Clefts of stones by streams or shaded and wet places. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, beverage.

Begonia hongkongensis F. W. Xing 香港秋海棠
Ann. Bot. Fennici 42: 151, fig. 1–2. 2005.

Perennial herbs, with creeping rhizome. Stems 10 –21 cm, glabrous. Petioles of basal leaves 5 –10 cm, sparsely covered with short hairs near apex. Stipules membranous, lanceolate, 1–2 × 2–2.5 mm. Leaf blade oblong-ovate to rhombic-ovate, 7–14 × 2.3 – 4.5 cm, apex acuminate, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, slightly oblique, margin irregularly and remotely serrate and shallowly 1–4-lobed, glabrous adaxially, sparsely covered with brown short hairs along veins on abaxial surface; cauline leaves 2–3, similar to basal leaves, 4.5–9 × 1.7–5.3 cm. Cymes dichotomous. Peduncles ca. 5 cm in fruiting time, glabrous. Flowers white. Male flowers: pedicels 7–14 mm; perianth-segments 4, outer 2 broadly ovate or oblong, 10 × 9 mm, inner 2 smaller, ovate. Female flowers: pedicels 2–2.5 cm; perianth 5, 7–12 × 6 –12 mm; ovary 2-locular. Capsule oblong, subglabrous, with 3 unequal wings.

Locality: Kau Keng Shan, Shum Tseng. Xing et al. 9972, 15248 (IBSC).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Kau Keng Shan by F. W. Xing in 1997.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Kau Keng Shan by F. W. Xing in 1997.

records.text:
Begonia crassirostris Irmsch. 粗喙秋海棠
Mitt. Inst. Allg. Bot. Hamburg 10: 513. 1939; FHN 1: 488, fig. 267. 1964; FGD 3: 147. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 150. 1999.

Perennial herb, 90–150 cm tall. Stems erect, glabrous, usually unbranched. Leaves alternate; petioles slender, the lower ones up to 10 cm; leaf blade obliquely oblong, 11–27 × 3.5 –10 cm, apex acuminate, base cordate and strongly oblique, the outer basal lobe 1.5 –6 × 2.5–6 cm, the inner one orbicular, margin ± irregularly denticulate. Cymes axillary. Peduncles 9–11 mm. Pedicels ca. 10 mm. Flowers white; male flowers: perianth-segments 3, outer 2 broadly obovate or suborbicular, 9 –10 × 8 –9 mm, inner 2 slightly smaller, broadly orbicular; female flowers: perianth-segments 6, obovate, outer ones 14–16 × 8–9 mm, inner ones ca. 13 × 7 mm; ovary subglobose, 3-locular. Capsule subglobose, to 14 mm long, without wings.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Tsz Mun Tin. HK sheet 34613; F. W. Xing 7242; Y. W. Lam 1699.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests by streams and wet places. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Begonia palmata D. Don 裂葉秋海棠
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 223. 1825; Hara, Fl. E. Himal. 215. 1966; FGD 3: 149, fig. 107. 1995.
Begonia laciniata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 2, 3: 649. 1832; FHK 126. 1861; FKH 114. 1912.
Begonia palmata D. Don. var. bowringiana (Champ. ex Benth.) J. Golding & C. Kareg., Phytologia 54: 494. 1984; FRPS 52(1): 234. 1999.
Begonia bowringiana Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 120. 1852.

Perennial herb, 15 – 60 cm tall, with horizontal rhizomes. Stems erect or decumbent at base, ± tawny tomentose. Leaves alternate; petioles usually shorter than leaf-blade, tawny tomentose; leaf blade obliquely ovate, 12–20 × 10 –15 cm, apex acuminate, base obliquely cordate, margin irregularly and shallowly 5 –7- lobed or coarsely toothed, adaxially strigose or with remaining small tubercles when the hairs falling off, abaxially pale green, tawny tomentose on veins. Cymes axillary or terminal. Peduncles 3 –12 mm, densely tawny tomentose. Flowers pink or white; male flowers: perianth-segments 4, outer 2 ovate-elliptic to oblong, 10 –25 × 7–11 mm, inner 2 smaller, elliptic to oblong; female flowers: perianth segments 5, oblong, subequal, 9–15 mm long; ovary 2-locular, puberulous. Capsule 10 –15 mm long, with 3 unequal wings.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 918; HK sheet 12233; H. C. Tang 1827.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Jiangxi; also in India, Nepal, Myanmar and Vietnam.
Ecology: Streamsides, margins of forests and other wet places. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Begonia bowringiana was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850; Begonia circumlobata Hance reported from Lantau Island (FKH 114. 1912) was a misidentification of B. palmata.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Begonia bowringiana was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850; Begonia circumlobata Hance reported from Lantau Island (FKH 114. 1912) was a misidentification of B. palmata.

records.text:
Beilschmiedia fordii Dunn 廣東瓊楠
J. Bot. 45: 404. 1907; FKH 222. 1912; FRPS 31: 142, pl. 37: 1. 1982.

Tree, 6–18 m tall. Terminal buds ovate-lanceolate, glabrous. Branchlets angular, glabrous. Leaves leathery, alternate or opposite; petioles glabrous, 1–2 cm, leaf blade lanceolate, oblong-elliptic to broadly elliptic, 7–13 × 2.5–4.6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate or obtuse, glabrous, adaxially dark green, abaxially paler, turning brown when dry; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins slender, 6–9 on each side of midvein. Cymose panicles usually axillary, 1–3 cm, densely flowered. Pedicels 3–5 mm. Perianth-lobes yellowish green, ovate to oblong, 1.5–2 mm, glabrous. Fruit ellipsoid, 1.4–1.8 cm, rounded on both ends, usually warty.

Locality: Happy Valley. HK sheet 4746, 4754.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.–Jun. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in August 1881.

Beilschmiedia glandulosa N. H. Xia, F. N. Wei & Y. F. Deng 腺葉瓊楠
J. Trop. & Subtrop. Bot. 14(1): 78, fig. 1. 2006.
Beilschmiedia fagifolia auct. non Nees: Dunn & Tutch., FKH 222. 1912.

Tree; branchlets greyish brown, pubescent, glabrescent, terminal buds pubescent. Leaves subopposite, leathery, elliptic, narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, 4.5 – 8.5 × 1.5 –3.5 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire, glabrous, brownish abaxially when dry, densely glandular spotted adaxially; main veins elevated on both surfaces, lateral veins 5 –7 pairs, together with tertiary veins prominent on both surfaces. Petioles 5–8 mm. Inflorescences axillary, racemose or thyrsoid, 1–3 clustered, 1.5 –3 cm, shortly pedunculate. Bracteoles ovate, ca. 1 × 0.6 mm, pilose. Pedicels 2– 4 mm. Flowers ca. 4 × 4 mm, perianth-tube short. Perianthlobes 6, rarely 7– 8, ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, pilose inside, sparsely villose outside. Fertile stamens 9 in 3 whorls, 6 of outer two whorls opposite to perianth-lobes, filaments 1 mm, densely pilose, anthers ca. 0.8 mm, 2-celled, cells introrse, each of the third whorl stamens with a pair of short-stalked orbicular-reniform glands near the base of filaments, filaments ca. 0.5 mm, densely villose, anthers ca. 0.5 mm, 2-celled, cells extrorse. Staminodes 3 of the innermost whorl, ca. 0.8 mm, ovoid. Ovary cylindrical, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely villose, style ca. 1 mm, stigma capitate. Fruit ellipsoid, apiculate, bluish black when maturing, 1.5–2.2 x 1–1.5 cm, smooth, wrinkled when dry. Seeds 1.3 –2 x 0.8 –1.2 cm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Mount Cameron, Bowen Road, Mount Parker, Tai Tam, Severn Road, Deep Water Bay Road, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. HK sheet 34208; Y.S. Lau 440; K. L. Yip 4197.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as B. tsangii Merr. previously (Check List HK Plants 42. 2002). The type specimen (F. Yip s.n., HK sheet 34327) was collected from Tai Tam, Hong Kong Island in August 1982.

Belamcanda chinensis (L.) DC. 射干
Liliac. 3: t. 121. 1805; FHK 365. 1861; FKH 274. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 131, pl. 42: 1–5. 1985; FOC 24: 312. 2000; FGD 6: 381, fig. 226. 2005.
Ixia chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 36. 1753.
Belamcanda chinensis (L.) DC. var. taiwanensis S. S. Ying, Coloured Illustr. Pl. Taiwan 1: 273. 1980.
Belamcanda pampaninii H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 8(160–162): 59–60. 1910.
Belamcanda punctata Moench, Methodus 529. 1794.
Pardanthus chinensis (L.) Ker Gawl., Ann. Bot. (König & Sims) 1: 246. 1805.

Rhizome yellow or pale brown. Stems 11.5 m. Leaves 20–60 × 2–4 cm, apex acuminate, midvein obscure. Flowers reddish orange with dark spots, 3–4 cm in diam.; pedicel slender, ca. 1.5 cm. Bracts lanceolate or ovate, membranous; outer perianth segments obovate or elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 1 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate; inner ones slightly narrower and shorter. Stamens 1.8–2 cm, filaments subterete, slightly broader at base, anthers linear, extrorse. Style 3-lobed at apex, lobes spreading. Capsule 2.5–3 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex not beaked. Seeds ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 7409, 28298.
Distribution: All over China except NW part; SE Asia and Russia.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Benincasa hispida (Thunb.) Cogn. 冬瓜
Mor. Phan. 3: 513. 1881; FRPS 73(1): 198. 1986; FFJ 5: 253, fig. 237. 1993; FGD 3: 128. 1995.
Cucurbita hispida Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 868. 1784; Fl. Jap. 322. 1784.

Annual large herbaceous vine. Stems and branches yellow-brown-hispid and villous, sulcate and angled. Tendrils short and slender. Petioles stout, 5 –20 cm, yellow-brown-hispid and villous; leaf blade reniform-suborbicular, 19 –24 × 10 –30 cm, base deeply cordate, apex acute, margin dentate, 5 –7-lobed, lobes broadly triangular or ovate, pilose to subglabrous adaxially, scabrous and hispid abaxially. Pedicels hispid, 5 –15 cm in male flowers, shorter than 5 cm in female flowers. Bracts pubescent, 6 –10 mm. Calyx-tube villous, lobes lanceolate, dentate, 8 –12 mm. Corolla-lobes 3 –6 × 2.5–4 cm, pubescent on both surfaces, densely hispid at margin near base; filaments 2–3 mm, expanded at base, hispid; anthers 5 mm. Ovary ovoid or cylindric, densely hispid, 2– 4 cm long; styles 2–3 mm, stigmas 3, 12–15 mm wide, 2-lobed. Fruit ellipsoid or terete, 25 –70 × 10 –25 cm, glaucous, hairy. Seeds many, flattened, ovate, 10 –11 × 5 –7 mm, with or without thickened margin.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 12036.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia, E Australia, Madagascar.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Food (fruit), Medicine (folklore).

Benincasa hispida (Thunb.) Cogn. var. chieh-qua How 節瓜
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3(1): 76. 1954; FRPS 73(1): 200. 1986; FFJ 5: 253. 1993; FGD 3: 129. 1995.

It differs from var. hispida by its yellow-hispid ovary and the fruit being terete, 15 –20 × 4 –11 cm, densely white hispid, not glaucous or slightly glaucous.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 515.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Spring and summer.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Berchemia floribunda (Wall.) Brongn. 多花勾兒茶
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot. 10: 357, pl. 13: 1. 1826; FRPS 48(1): 125, pl. 33: 3 – 4. 1982; FGD 4: 260, fig. 154. 2000.
Berchemia racemosa Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(2): 147. 1845; FHK 67. 1861; FKH 63. 1912.
Berchemia giraldiana C. K. Schneid., Ill. Handb. Laubholzk. 2: 263, fig. 182: m– n, 183: k. 1909; FGZ 418. 1956.

Woody climber, 1–4 m tall; branchlets yellowish to brown, glabrous. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-elliptic, 5–8 × 3–5 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute, glabrous; lateral veins 9–11 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Flowers 2–3 clustered and racemosely arranged, usually forming large (to 15 cm) terminal panicle; rachis glabrous or puberulent; pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx broadly campanulate, 2–3 mm, 5-lobed to middle, lobes triangular. Petals obovate, ca. 1.5 mm, laterally involute, embracing the stamens. Stamens equaling petals or slightly exserted. Ovary half-immersed in the disk; style short, undivided. Drupe oblong or cylindric, 7–10 × 4–5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Tai Long Sai Wan, Chek Keng, Kiu Tsui, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1161, 2324; Y. S. Lau 2114.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina to Nepal and India.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.; fruiting: Feb.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Berchemia lineata (L.) DC. 鐵包金（老鼠耳）
Prodr. 2: 23. 1825; FHK 67. 1861; FKH 63. 1912; FRPS 48(1): 111, pl. 28: 5 –6. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 3: 682, pl. 352. 1993; FGD 4: 260. 2000.
Rhamnus lineata L., Cent. Pl. 2: 11. 1756.

Diffuse or half-climbing shrub, to 2 m tall. Young shoots puberulent, glabrescent. Leaves papery, 2-ranked; petioles 1–2 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong, 1–2 × 0.4–1.5 cm, base rounded, apex rounded or obtuse, glabrous; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flowers 2–4 clustered in axils of the leaves or a few clusters aggregated at the ends of the branches above the leaves; pedicels 3–6 mm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 4 mm, 5-lobed to the base; lobes narrowly lanceolate or linear. Petals spathulate, ca. 4 mm. Stamens slightly exserted. Ovary half-immersed in the disk; style clavate. Drupe ovate to ovate-oblong, 3–4 × 2–2.5 mm, black when mature.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sheung Shui, Tai Long Sai Wan, Ma Wan, Ping Chau. W. J. Tutcher 8401; Y. S. Lau 762.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jul. – Oct.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Beta vulgaris L. var. cicla L. 莙薘菜
Sp. Pl. 222. 1753; FHN 1: 398. 1964; FGD 3: 67. 1995; FOC 5: 354. 2003.

Annual or biennial succulent herbs, 0.3–1 m tall; roots fleshy, branched, not tuberous. Petioles rough, long; basal leaves ovate or oblong-ovate, 20–30 × 10–15 cm, base cuneate or cordate, decurrent, margin sinuate, apex obtuse, midvein elevated abaxially; cauline leaves smaller, rhombic-ovate to lanceolate. Flowers sessile, small, green, solitary or 2–3 clustered in paniculate spikes. Bracts linear. Perianth-lobes oblong, thickened at base when fruiting. Utricles with lower part enclosed in hardened perianth, upper part slightly fleshy. Seeds reddish brown, 2–3 mm in diam., shiny.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Europe, Asia & N Africa.
Ecology: Farmland, roadside. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Vegetable.

Bidens alba (L.) DC. 白花鬼針草
Prodr. 5: 605. 1836; F. R. Fosberg & M. H. Sachet, Smithsonian Contr. Bot. 46: 22. 1980.
Coreopsis alba L., Sp. Pl. 2: 908. 1753.
Bidens pilosa var. radiata Sch.‑Bip. in Webb & Berthel., Hist. Nat. Îles Canaries 3(2): 242. 1844; FTW ed. 2, 4: 870, pl. 404. 1998.

Annual erect herbs, 0.3–1.5 m tall; stems striate, subtetragonous, glabrous or somewhat puberulent. Leaves opposite, ternate to pinnatisect, median ones 3.5–11.5 cm long, margin serrate‑mucronate, glabrous on both surfaces except the margin with curved hair, leaf lobes ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, base usually cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, sometimes truncate or rounded, petiole 1–4.5 cm, narrowly winged, loosely hairy along the margin. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, 1.5–3 cm across, corymbose paniculate at terminal of main stem and lateral branches. Peduncle subglabrous or loosely pubescent, 1.8–8 cm. Involucres bowl‑shaped, 4–6 mm across, hairy near base; phyllaries 2‑seriate; outer ones herbaceous, spatulate with apex dilated, rounded and reflexed, 3–4 × 1–1.5 mm, ciliate along margin; inner rows scarious, linear‑lanceolate, 5–5.5 × 1.2–1.3 mm, ciliate near the apex. Marginal ligulate florets prominent and exposing outside the involucres, 5–8 per capitulum, neutral, corolla white, tube 1–2 mm, ligule 8–14 mm, apex with 3 rounded‑obtuse lobes. Disk tubular florets many, perfect, corolla yellow, 5 mm, the upper 2/3 broadly campanulate, the lower 1/3 narrowed, apically 5‑cleft, puberulent on abaxial side of the lobes. Cypselae linear, 7–9.5 × 0.8–0.9 mm, slightly compressed, striate, blackish brown, bearing pale brown hooks and tubercles near two distal ends. Pappus 2(–3) stiff awns of 2 mm long, retrorsely barbed, pale brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3191; Y. W. Lam 21.; S. Y. Hu & Y. C. Kong 050 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to tropical America, widely naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: May–Dec.
Notes: Often regarded as a variety of Bidens pilosa.

Bidens bipinnata L. 婆婆針
Sp. Pl. 2: 832. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 315. 1965; FRPS 75: 380, pl. 64: 3 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 136. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 868, photo 422. 1998.

Annual erect herbs, 20–100 cm tall, subtetragonous, glabrous or sparsely puberulent on upper part. Petiole 1.5–5 cm. Leaves 3–14 cm long, bipinnate or bipinnatipartite, terminal leaflets rhomboid‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, lateral segments ovate and acute, both surfaces pubescent, especially along margin and veins, margin irregularly and loosely toothed or lobed. Capitula 6–10 mm across. Peduncle 1.5–10 cm, longer in fruiting stage. Involucres bowl‑shaped, base hairy; outer phyllaries herbaceous green, linear‑lanceolate, 4–5 mm, apex obtuse, hairy along margin and on abaxial side; inner phyllaries scarious brown, lanceolate‑oblong, 4–6 mm, pubescent, margin membranous and yellow, apex densely hairy. Paleae lanceolate and narrower. Marginal ligulate florets neutral, corolla 6–7 mm, yellow, ligule elliptic or obovate, apex entire or 2 – 3‑lobed. Central tubular florets hermaphrodite, corolla 4–4.5 mm, yellow, upper 2/3 campanulate, lower 1/3 narrowed, apex 5‑cleft. Cypselae blackish brown, linear, 3–4‑angulate, slightly compressed, 7–10 × 0.8–1 mm, tuberculate and shortly hooked at upper part. Pappus of (2–)3–4, stiff and retrorsely barbed awns, pale brown, 3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2297; Y. W. Lam 758; S. Y. Hu 6960 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to N and NE, E to SW China; America, Europe, Asia, E Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Bidens biternata (Lour.) Merr. & Sherff 金盞銀盤
Bot. Gaz. 88(3): 293. 1929; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 315. 1965; FRPS 75: 378, pl. 65: 1 – 4. 1979; FGD 8: 136, fig. 71. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 869. 1998.
Coreopsis biternata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 508. 1790.

Annual erect herbs; stem 30–150 cm tall, subtetragonous, glabrous or sparsely puberulent. Leaves 1‑pinnatisect to pinnatipartite, 3–10 cm long, terminal segment ovate‑lanceolate, 2.5–7.5 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, lateral segments 1–2 pairs, ovate, smaller than the terminal ones, 1.5–5 × 0.7–2 cm, apex acute or obtuse; both regularly and densely serrate‑mucronate, pubescent on both surfaces. Capitula 6–9 mm across. Peduncles 1.5–7.5 cm, in fruiting stage appeared longer. Involucres bowl‑shaped, hairy below; outer phyllaries herbaceous green, linear, 2–3 mm when flowering, 3–4 mm when fruiting, width 0.5–0.8 mm, apex acute to obtuse, hairy along margin and on abaxial side; inner phyllaries scarious brown, lanceolate‑oblong, 5–6 mm, hairy outside, margin membranous and yellow, apex acuminate and densely hairy. Palea oblong, narrower. Ligulate florets 3–5, or sometimes absent, neutral, corolla pale yellow, oblong, 4–5.5 × 2.5–3 mm. Tubular florets bisexual, 4–4.5 mm, 5‑dentate, yellow. Cypselae blackish brown, linear, tetragonous, narrowed at two distal ends, 8–12 × 0.8–1 mm, finely hispid on the upper part. Pappus 3–4 stiff awns, about 3 mm, pale brown, retrorsely barbed.

Locality: Peng Chau, Ping Chau, Tai Po. HK sheet 2660; S. Y. Hu 7895 (CUHK); Y. Wong 008 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to N and E to SE China; Asia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Bidens pilosa L. 鬼針草
Sp. Pl. 2: 832. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 318. 1965; FRPS 75: 377. 1979; FGD 8: 135. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 869. 1998.

Annual erect herbs; stems 20–100 cm tall, subtetragonous, glabrous or with upper portion sparsely puberulent. Leaves mostly ternate, the median ones 3–7 cm long, with petiole 1–3.3 cm and narrowly winged, leaf segments ovate, the terminal lobes larger, apically acuminate and basally rounded or narrowed to the petiole, lateral lobes smaller, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute, both surfaces glabrous or loosely pubescent, margin serrate‑mucronate; upper leaves sometimes non‑divided, lanceolate in shape. Capitula 0.8–1 cm across, discoid with all florets tubular or heterogamous with several small rays. Peduncle 1.5–7.5 cm, those in fruiting stage longer. Involucres hairy near the base; outer phyllaries herbaceous green, spatulate, 3–4 mm at anthesis, up to 5 mm at fruiting stage, margin ciliate, apex obtuse‑rounded; inner phyllaries scarious, brown, lanceolate‑oblong, 4–5 mm when flowering, 5–6 mm when fruiting, margin yellowish membranous, apex densely hairy. Palea narrower, linear‑lanceolate. Ligulate florets, if present, 4–5 mm, nearly enclosed in the involucres and thus inconspicuous, neutral, white in colour. Tubular florets 3 mm, 5‑toothed, yellow, fertile. Cypselae blackish brown, linear, 5–9 × 0.7–1 mm, somewhat laterally compressed, slightly 4‑angulate, finely hispid in upper part. Pappus 2–3 stiff awns, pale brown, 2–2.5 mm, retrorsely barbed.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2357; Y. S. Lau 85; S. Y. Hu 5293 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to C, E to SW China; widely distributed in Asia and tropical America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Usually the plants bearing ray florets are regarded as B. pilosa var. minor, while the ones bearing discoid heads are known as B. pilosa var. pilosa.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Usually the plants bearing ray florets are regarded as B. pilosa var. minor, while the ones bearing discoid heads are known as B. pilosa var. pilosa.

records.text:
Billbergia pyramidalis (Sims) Lindl. 水塔花
Bot. Reg. 13: sub pl. 1068. 1827; FRPS 13(3): 67. 1997.
Bromelia pyramidalis Sims, Bot. Reg. 42: pl. 1732. 1815.

Stem very short. Leaves 6–15, forming a rosette; leaf blade lorate, 25–40 × 2–4 cm, apex acute or acuminate, with closely set, small marginal spines, abaxially usually with many white transverse bands, adaxially and basally pale or dark coloured. Spikes erect; bracts pink, lanceolate, 5–7 cm. Sepals 3, obtuse, pale red. Petals 3, bright red, ca. 4 cm, tipped with violet, during anthesis erect, with recurved, slightly broadened and rounded tips. Filaments equalling the corolla or slightly shorter; stigmas contorted, violet. Fruit a berry.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28122, 28133.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong (cultivated); native to tropical America, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bischofia javanica Blume 秋楓
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 17: 1168. 1825; FKH 236. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 185, pl. 56: 2 –4. 1994; FGD 5: 67, fig. 37. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 124. 2005.
Andrachne trifoliata Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 3: 728. 1832.
Bischofia trifoliata (Roxb.) Hook., Hooker's Icon. 9: pl. 844. 1851.

Evergreen tree, up to 40 m tall; branchlets glabrous. Leaves papery, palmately 3(–5)-foliolate; stipules membranous, lanceolate, ca. 8 mm, caducous; petioles 8 – 20 cm; leaflets ovate, elliptic, obovate or elliptic-ovate, 7–15 × 4–8 cm, base broadly cuneate to obtuse, apex acute or caudate-acuminate, margin denticulate, with 2–3 denticles in each cm, sparsely pubescent on veins when young, glabrous in age. Flowers in axillary panicles, the male 8–13 cm, the female 15–27 cm, pendent. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 1 mm; sepals 5, membranous, semiorbicular, puberulous abaxially; filaments short; pistillode small, peltate, pubescent. Female flowers: pedicels 2–3 mm; sepals 5, oblong-ovate, puberulous abaxially, margin membranous; ovary smooth, glabrous, 3–4-locular; styles 3–4, linear, entire. Fruits globose or subglobose, 6–13 mm in diam., brownish; seeds oblong, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 790, 1238; Y. S. Lau 512, 1419; S. Y. Hu 6491, 11590 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in SE Asia, Malesia and Australia
Ecology: Lowland forests, streamsides, often cultivated in gardens or as roadside tree. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Bischofia polycarpa (H. Lév.) Airy Shaw 重陽木

Kew Bull. 27(2): 271. 1972; FRPS 44(1): 187, pl. 56 : 1. 1994; FGD 5: 67. 2003.

Celtis polycarpa H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 11(286 – 290): 296. 1912.

Bischofia racemosa Cheng & C. D. Chu, Sci. Silv. Sin. 8(1): 13. 1963.


Deciduous tree, up to 15 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves 3-foliolate; stipules small, caducous; petioles 9 – 13.5 cm; leaflets papery, ovate or elliptic-ovate, sometimes oblong-ovate, 5–9(–14) × 3–6(–9) cm, the terminal usually larger than the lateral ones, base rounded or shallowly cordate, apex acute or short-acuminate, margin denticulate, with 4 – 5 denticles in each cm. Flowers in pendent racemes on branches of previous year, the male 8–13 cm, the female 3–12 cm. Male flowers: sepals 5, semiorbicular, membranous, spreading; filaments short, pistillode prominent. Female flowers: sepals as in male flower, with white-membranous margin; ovary 3 – 4-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles 2 – 3, entire. Fruits globose, 5 – 7 mm in diam., brownish red when mature.


Locality: Cultivated in Sheung Shui,Yuen Long, Tai Po. Y. W. Lam 267, 268; HK sheet 39527.

Distribution: N Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.

Ecology: Flowering: Apr. –May; fruiting: Oct. –Nov.

Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Bixa orellana L. 紅木
Sp. Pl. 512. 1753; FGZ 176, fig. 80. 1956; FRPS 50(2): 180. 1990; FGD 4: 132. 2000.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 2–10 m tall; bark greyish brown or brown, smooth; young branchlets and inflorescence densely covered with red-brown glandular hairs. Petioles 2.5– 7.5 cm, glabrous. Leaves ovate, 8 –20 × 5 –13 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, dotted with resin-like glands; palmately 5-veins arising from the base. Thyrses 5 –10 cm. Flowers large, pink, 4 –5 cm in diam. Sepals obovate, ca. 2 cm, densely red-brown lepidote, with glands at base. Petals obovate, 1–2 cm. Anthers ellipsoid, yellow, 2-celled. Ovary 1-locular, style 1, stigmas bilobed. Capsule subglobose or ovoid, 2.5 – 4 cm, 2-valved, densely spiny; spines purplish brown, 1–2 cm. Seeds obovoid, dark red.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 216, 430, 1236.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (dye).

Blainvillea acumella (L.) Philip. 百能葳
Blumea 6: 350. 1950; FHN 3: 405, fig. 808. 1974; FRPS 75: 348, pl. 59: 3 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 122, fig. 61. 2007.
Spilanthes acmella (L.) Murray, Syst. Veg. ed. 13, 610. 1774.
Blainvillea latifolia (L. f.) DC. ex Wright, Contr. Bot. Ind. 17. 1834.
Eclipta latifolia L. f., Suppl. P. 378. 1781.
Verbesina acmella L., Fl. Zeyl. 309. 1748.

Annual herbs, 40 – 60 cm tall; stem erect, many‑branched, pubescent. Lower leaves opposite; petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3 – 6 × 2 – 3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely serrate, strigose or pilose on both surfaces; upper leaves smaller, usually alternate, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 2 – 3 × 1.3 – 1.5 cm, base usually rounded. Capitula axillary or terminal, ca. 1 cm in diam., peduncles slender, 1.5 – 4 cm. Phyllaries in two series; outer ones herbaceous, green, ovate‑oblong, ca. 6 mm long, apex shortly acute or obtuse, dorsally covered with harsh hairs; inner ones ovate to oblong‑linear, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, lower part scarious, sparsely pubescent. Paleae oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, apex aristiform, dorsally pubescent. Ray florets one series, ligules yellow or yellowish white, ca. 3 mm, apex 2 – 4‑toothed. Disk florets campanulate, limbs 5‑toothed. Cypselae of ray florets cuneiform triquetrous, curved, ca. 4 mm, those of disk florets compressed, ca. 5 mm. Pappus of 2 – 5, unequal bristles, connate at the base.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41860, 41861.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Africa, America, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides.

Blastus cochinchinensis Lour. 柏拉木
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 526. 1790; FKH 107. 1912; FHN 2: 30, t. 303. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 182. 1984.
Anplectrum parviflorum Benth., FHK 116. 1861
Blastus parviflorus (Benth.) Triana, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 28(1): 116. 1871 [1872].

Shrub, 0.6 – 3 m tall. Stems terete; young branches, leaves, petioles and inflorescences with minute, yellow glands. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2(–3) cm; leaf blade lanceolate, narrowly elliptic, or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–12(–18) × 2– 4(–5) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or obscurely denticulate. Inflorescences axillary, umbellate cymose; peduncle ca. 2 mm to almost absent; pedicels ca. 3 mm, densely glandular. Calyx-tube campanulate, ca. 4 mm, obtusely 4-sided, densely glandular; calyx-lobes 4(–5), broadly ovate, ca. 1 mm. Petals 4(–5), white or pink, ovate, ca. 4 mm, apex acuminate to subacute. Stamens 4(–5), equal; filaments ca. 4 mm; anthers pink, lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, geniculate; connective slightly inflated, decurrent at base of anther. Ovary urceolate, 4-locular, slightly glandular, apex 4-bulged. Fruit ca. 3 × 2–3 mm, quadrangular, encircled by persistent calyx which is equal to fruit.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ng Tung Chai, Lai Chi Wo, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2747; Y. W. Lam 526, 1897; N. K. Chun 41882 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests, stony soil. Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.

Blastus pauciflorus (Benth.) Guillaumin 少花柏拉木
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 60: 90. 1913; FRPS 53(1): 187. 1984.
Allomorphia pauciflora Benth., Lond. J. Bot. 1: 485. 1842; FKH 107. 1912.
Oxyspora pauciflora Benth., FHK 116. 1861.

Shrub, ca. 0.7 m tall. Stems terete, much branched; branchlets and petioles and inflorescence puberulous and sparsely glandular when young. Leaves opposite; petiole 0.4 –1.5(–2.8) cm; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate to ovate, (5–)10–12(–25) × (2–)3–7.3(–10) cm, base obtuse to rounded, sometimes slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate, margin nearly entire to minutely denticulate, 3–5-basiveined, puberulous but densely so and with minute, yellow glands on abaxial surface. Inflorescences terminal, paniculate cymose, 7.5 – 13 × 3 – 7 cm; bracts inconspicuous. Pedicels 1– 3 mm. Calyx-tube funnelform, 3.8– 6(–8) mm, 4-sided, densely glandular; calyx-lobes shortly triangular or spathulate, less than 1 mm. Petals (3–)4, pink to reddish lavender, ovate, 2.5– 4(–5) mm, inclined to one side, glandular, apex acute. Stamens (3–)4, equal; filaments 5 – 7(–10) mm, sparsely puberulous; anthers linear, (4.8–)6.2 – 7.4(–8) mm, slightly curved, with 2 tubercules or sagittate at base; connective not or only slightly inflated, extended to base. Ovary ovoid, (3–)4-locular, more or less glandular, apex (3–)4-bulged. Fruit ellipsoidal, 3.8 – 4.5 × 2.5 – 3 mm, encircled by persistent calyx, 4-sided, ca. 3 × 2 mm, dehiscing longitudinally.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7476, 9825; HK sheet 1794.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Mixed forests, mountain slopes, low hills, valleys, stream banks, moist places, roadsides. Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Bletilla striata (Thunb. ex Murray) Rchb. f. 白芨
Bot. Zeit. 36: 75. 1878; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 74, fig. 37. 1977; FRPS 18: 50, pl. 6: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 340, fig. 169. 2006; FOC 25: 210. 2009.
Limodorum striatum Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 816. 1784.
Bletia hyacinthina (Sm.) R. Br., Hort. Kew ed. 2, 5: 206. 1813; FKH 263. 1912.
Cymbidium hyacinthinum Sm., Exot. Bot. 1: 117, t. 60. 1804.

Terrestrial perennial herb; rhizomes compressed, ginger-like. Leaves petiolate, petioles sheathing with conspicuous joint; leaf blades elliptic or lanceolate, 10–15(–30) × 2–4 cm. Flowers resupinate, bright purple, wide open; sepals and petals similar in length and width, 2.5–3 × 0.5–0.7 cm; dorsal sepal linear-oblong, obtuse at apex; lateral ones oblique-falcate; petals almost horizontal, oblong-oblanceolate-oblique, slightly twisted; lip horizontal, tubular and covering the column, slightly enlarged towards the apex, 3-lobed, 2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, light purple, darker towards apex and margin, lateral lobes erect, midlobe tongue-like, with 5 longitudinal wavy crests running all the way, 2 additional ridges near to the base, the margin ruffled and wavy; column long, slender, slightly arcuate; anther oblong, white; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, ovary slender, slightly curved.

Locality: Cultivated in Hong Kong; Y. K. Leung 26 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11699 (CUHK); HK sheet 35812.
Distribution: Shaanxi, Gansu, areas S of Changjiang; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Blumea balsamifera (L.) DC. 艾納香
Prodr. 5: 447. 1836; Randeria, Blumea 10: 237. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 321. 1965; FRPS 75: 19. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 875, pl. 407, photo 424. 1998.
Conyza balsamifera L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 1280. 1763.

Erect perennial herb or subshrub, 0.5–3 m tall, usually unbranched, whole plant tomentose with brownish white hairs, thinning out on older parts. Leaves oblong, thick papery when fresh, much thinner when old or dried, lower ones 25 × 7 cm, decreasing to ca. 11 × 4 cm towards the top; margins with sharp, forward‑pointing teeth. Petioles varying between 5–30 mm, bearing narrow auricles on both sides; auricles occurring opposite or sub‑opposite to one another on the petiole, 3–5 pairs on the lower petioles, 2–3 pairs on the upper ones. Capitula pedunculate, 5–8 mm across, forming a large, woolly panicle. Phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, the innermost longest, successively decreasing in length outward. Receptacles 2–3 mm across, glabrous; outer pistillate florets 6 mm, 2–4‑lobed; hermaphrodite ones in the centre, 6–7 mm in length, 5‑lobed, much less in number than the pistillate ones. Cypselae cylindric, 1 mm, densely hirsute; pappus reddish brown, 4–6 mm.

Locality: Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23124 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3218; E. M. Gibbs 5162.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Pakistan, India, Thailand, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Blumea clarkei Hook. f. 七里明
Fl. Brit. India 3(8): 267. 1881; Randeria, Blumea 10: 252. 1960; Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 23: 66. 1968; FRPS 75: 29, pl. 5: 1–6. 1979; FGD 8: 156. 2007.
Blumea hongkongensis H. Lév. & Vaniot, Bull. Acad. Int. Geogr. Bot. 12(158): 22. 1903; FKH 143. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall; stems unbranched, young parts velutinous. Leaves subsessile or with a petiole up to 5 mm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate to linear‑oblong, 8–14 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margins distantly serrate or dentate with mucronate teeth, glabrous or sometimes velutinous with prominent‑based hairs on adaxial surface, tomentellous abaxially; upper leaves sessile, oblong, 3–5 × 1–2 cm, margin denticulate, rarely subentire. Capitula numerous, 8–12 in diam., usually 3–5 clustered, sessile or shortly pedunculate, forming narrow, terminal, compact panicles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, ca. 12 mm; phyllaries 4‑seriate, apex purplish red, outer ones lanceolate, 3–5 mm, apex acute or acuminate, densely pubescent abaxially, ciliate, middle and inner ones lanceolate or linear, ca. 11 mm, margin scarious, sparsely pubescent abaxially. Receptacles slightly convex, alveolate, sparsely pubescent. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets slender tubular, 6–7 mm, limb 3–5‑toothed; central hermaphrodite florets tubular, about the same length of the pistillate florets, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae cylindric, ca. 1.2 mm, ribbed. Pappus white, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 8589; Y. S. Lau 1369; S. C. Ng 3218.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Indochina, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.

Blumea hieracifolia (D. Don) DC. 毛氈草
Contr. Bot. India 15. 1834; FHK 178. 1861 (incl. varieties); FKH 143. 1912; Randeria, Blumea 10: 246. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 324. 1965; FRPS 75: 24, pl. 4: 1–7. 1979; FGD 8: 157. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 878, pl. 410, photo 427. 1998.
Erigeron hieracifolium D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 172. 1825.

Perennial erect herbs, to 1 m tall, whole plant covered with short, fine, viscid, glandular hairs. Leaves papery, subsessile; leaf blade obovate or oblanceolate, 7–13 × 2–4 cm, base attenuate, decurrent, apex acute or mucronate, margins serrate with mucronate teeth. Inflorescence terminal and axillary, length relatively short, the whole appearing fasciculate. Capitula ca. 5–8 mm across, 2–7 clustered, forming spicate‑panicles. Involucre cylindric or campanulate; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, upper part purplish, outer ones linear‑lanceolate, 2–3 mm, apex acuminate, abaxially white‑tomentose, middle ones linear‑oblong, 4–6 mm, apex acute, margin scarious, sparsely pubescent abaxially or only on the upper part, inner ones filiform, scarious, glabrous, ca. 6 mm. Receptacles convex, glabrous. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous, slender tubular, limb 3‑toothed; central bisexual florets tubular, about as long as the pistillate flowers, limb 5(–6)‑toothed. Cypselae cylindric, 1–1.2 mm; pappus white, 5–6 mm long. On flowering the basal leaves wither, turning dark brown to black, but stay on the plant.

Locality: Sai Kung, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9160; Y. S. Lau 2663; S. Y. Hu 23231 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan; Pakistan, India, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of cultivated fields and grassy banks. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.

Blumea lacera (Burm. f.) DC. 見霜黃
Contr. Bot. India 14. 1834; FHK 178. 1861; FKH 142. 1912; Randeria, Blumea 10: 264. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 325. 1965; FRPS 75: 33. 1979; FGD 8: 158, fig. 86. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 878, pl. 411, photo 428. 1998.
Conyza lacera Burm. f., Fl. Indica 180. 1768.

Perennial herbs, to 60 cm tall; stems simple or branched on the upper part, striate, tomentose to densely velutinous with silky whitish hairs. Lower leaves usually petiolate; petioles 1–3 cm; leaf blade elliptic‑oblong to obovate‑oblong, 7–15 × 4–5 cm, base cuneate or long attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin irregularly and coarsely toothed, sometimes lyrately lobed on the lower half, tomentose to velutinous adaxially, tomentose to woolly abaxially; upper leaves sessile or very shortly petiolate, leaf blade obovate to oblong‑elliptic, 2.5–4 × 1.5– 2 cm, base attenuate, apex rounded or apiculate, irregularly toothed on upper half, sometimes entire, sericeous tomentose on both surfaces. Capitula 5–6.5 mm in diam., arranged in axillary and terminal, dense to lax panicles; peduncles 0–10 mm. Phyllaries ca. 4‑seriate, herbaceous, linear, apex long‑acuminate, entirely reflexed at maturity, outer ones white‑pilose abaxially, densely ciliate. Receptacles convex, alveolate, glabrous, yellow; outer pistillate florets tubular, ca. 4 mm, limb 3‑toothed; central hermaphrodite florets tubular, ca. 5 mm, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae 1–2 mm, sparsely hirsute, ribbed; pappus 4 mm, white.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Po, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Castle Peak, Ping Chau. K. M. Lau 546 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 10099 (CUHK); W. J. Tutcher 8591.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, SE Africa, N Australia.
Ecology: Margins of cultivated fields and grassy banks. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.

Blumea laciniata (Roxb.) DC. 六耳鈴
Prodr. 5: 436. 1836; Randeria, Blumea 10: 258. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 325. 1965; Kitam, Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 23: 68. 1968; FRPS 75: 38, pl. 6: 7–12. 1979; FGD 8: 159. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 882, pl. 412. 1998.
Conyza laciniata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 427. 1832.
Blumea glandulosa auct. non DC.: Benth., FHK 177. 1861.

Perennial herbs, to 1.8 m tall. Stems hairy, with fine, slightly raised ribs. Leaves obovate, papery, lower ones 12– 30 × 6–15 cm, base attenuate into narrowly winged petioles, apex obtuse, margins often runcinate‑lyrate and distantly dentate, possessing sharp, irregular teeth; upper leaves decreasing to 3 × 1 cm, petioles also decreasing to almost sessile. Capitula forming panicles which in turn forming a spreading inflorescence reaching 40 cm. Peduncles pubescent; involucres campanulate with bracts spreading and reflexed at maturity. Receptacles 2.5– 3.5 mm in diam., convex, areas surrounding the attachment points of the cypselae covered sparsely with short, coarse hairs. Corolla yellow; pistillate florets slender tubular, 4.5 mm, with 2–3 glabrous teeth on the limb; hermaphrodite florets tubular, 4.5 mm, limb opening wider towards apex, with 5 pubescent teeth. Cypselae cylindric to subfusiform, 0.7–1 mm, ribbed. Pappus white, 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. M. Lau 547 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 25; S. Y. Hu 13700 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Pakistan, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of cultivated fields, grassy banks. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Notes: Blumea species do not have ligulate (or ray florets) but they have two types of disk florets (Photo 504, × 30). Those on the outside rims of the receptacle (Photos 506, 508, 515) are slender and all female (pistillate) and possess no anthers inside their corolla. Those in the centre are broader, possess both male and female parts (hermaphrodite or bisexual, Photo 505, × 25), and are less numerous. In Photo 505, both the outside corolla tube (light yellow) and the anther tube (bright yellow) are slit open and the central pistil is separated out. The anthers can just be seen attached to the base of the corolla by 5 column‑like appendages.

Blumea lanceolaria (Roxb.) Druce 千頭艾納香
Rep. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 4: 609. 1917; Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 4: 155. 1935; Randeria, Blumea 10: 218. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 326. 1965; FRPS 75: 17. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 884, pl. 413. 1998.
Conyza lanceolaria Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 432. 1832.
Blumea myriocephala DC., Prodr. 5: 445. 1836; FKH 142. 1912.

Erect perennial herbs, 1–2 m tall. Stems striate, woody at base.
