Leaves subleathery; petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blade narrow obovate to oblanceolate, 15–23 × 4–5 cm, base attenuate, decurrent, sometimes with auricular appendages, apex acuminate, margins with coarse teeth; dark green adaxially, lighter abaxially; glabrous or sometimes slightly hairy on abaxial surface. Capitula many, 3 mm in diam., usually 3–4 clustered, subsessile or with a short peduncle (5–10 mm), forming a terminal pyramidal panicle. Involucre cylindric or subcampanulate, 6– 8 mm; phyllaries 5–6‑seriate, green or purplish, outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse or ± acute, pubescent abaxially, middle ones narrowly lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, 3–4 mm, apex acute, margin scarious, inner ones linear, ca. 8 mm, apex acute, sparsely pubescent. Receptacle flat, foveolate, densely white pubescent. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous, slender tubular, ca. 7 mm, limb 3‑lobed, glabrous; central bisexual florets tubular, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae ca. 1.5 mm, 5‑ribbed; pappus yellowish.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fung Yuen, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 3093; W. J. Tutcher 11416.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Taiwan; India, Pakistan, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.

Blumea megacephala (Randeria) C. C. Chang & Y. Q. Tseng 東風草（大頭艾納香）
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12(3): 310. 1974; FRPS 75: 11, pl. 2: 1 – 7. 1979; FGD 8: 153, fig. 85. 2007.
Blumea riparia DC. var. megacephala Randeria, Blumea 10(1): 215. 1960; FTW ed. 2, 4: 888, pl. 417, photo 430. 1998.
Blumea chinensis auct. non DC.: Benth., FHK 177. 1861.

Scandent perennial herb, branches elongate and scandent. Stems cylindric, striate, growing to 1–3 m or longer. Leaves ovate to oblong, 7–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, margins mucronulate or mucronulate‑denticulate, both surfaces sparsely hairy, becoming glabrous later; petioles 2–5 mm. Capitula relatively large, 10–15 mm in diam., arranged in axillary panicles or subcorymbose inflorescences. Peduncles 1– 3 cm. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 5–6 seriate, the outermost series shortest. Receptacle flat, with long white hairs. Outer pistillate florets many, corolla slender tubular, 2–4‑lobed, puberulent; the central bisexual florets tubular, corollas 5‑lobed, with white multi‑cellular hairs. Cypselae cylindric, ribbed, 0.7 mm long. Pappus white, 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1458; Y. W. Lam 1147; S. Y. Hu 9200 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.

Blumea mollis (D. Don) Merr. 柔毛艾納香
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 5(5): 395. 1910; Randeria, Blumea 10: 261. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 328. 1965; FRPS 75: 32. 1979; FGD 8: 158. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 884, pl. 415, photo 429. 1998.
Erigeron molle D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 172. 1825.
Blumea wightiana DC., Contr. Bot. India 14. 1834; Benth., FHK 178. 1861.

Annual erect herbs, to 60 cm tall. Stems slender, with soft, glandular, somewhat viscid hairs. Lower leaves obovate, 7–9 × 3–4 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex broadly obtuse, margin irregularly serrulate, sericeous pilose with glandular hair on both surfaces; petioles 1–2 cm. Upper leaves subsessile, gradually decreasing, 1–2 × 0.3– 0.8 cm. Capitula numerous, sessile or on a very short peduncle, 3–5 mm in diam., usually 3 – 5 clustered, forming a narrow and short panicle. Involucres campanulate, ca. 5 mm; phyllaries in 4 series, purplish, outer ones linear, ca. 3 mm, apex acuminate, densely soft‑villous and with multicellular hairs and glands abaxially, innear ones linear, 5– 6 mm, margin scarious, ciliate. Receptacles convex, glabrous. Outer pistillate florets filiform, 4–5 mm, limbs 3‑toothed; central bisexual florets about 10; corolla tubular, purplish, 4–5 mm, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae fusiform, ribbed, pubescent, ca. 0.7 mm. Pappus ca. 3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Fanling. K. M. Lau 545 (CUHK); H. C. Tang 1199; Y. S. Lau 2623.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; S Asia, Indonesia to N Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes, preferring sunny locations. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.

Blumea oblongifolia Kitam. 長圓葉艾納香
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 2(1): 37. 1933; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 328. 1965; FRPS 75: 30, pl. 5: 7–12. 1979; FGD 8: 156. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 888, pl. 416. 1998.

Perennial herbs; stems erect, to 1.5 m tall, striate, velutinous particularly on young parts. Leaves subsessile or short petiolate, oblong to narrowly elliptic‑oblong, 9–14 × 3.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin distantly serrate with mucronate teeth, pubescent adaxially, ± villous abaxially. Capitula numerous, 8–12 mm in diam., forming terminal and axillary panicles; peduncles up to 2 cm, densely villous. Involucres globose‑campanulate; phyllaries 4‑seriate, green, outer ones lanceolate, 4–5 mm, apex caudate‑acuminate, densely villous abaxially, middle and inner ones linear or linear‑lanceolate, 7–7.5 mm, apex caudate, margin scarious, pubescent abaxially. Receptacle slightly convex, alveolate, hairy. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous, slender tubular, 5–5.5 mm, limb 3–4‑toothed; central hermaphrodite florets less numerous, tubular, 6 mm, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae cylindric, ca. 1 mm, ribbed, sparsely hirsute. Pappus white, 5–6 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2278, 2425; S. Y. Hu 22816A (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Moist places in ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Notes: At first glance, and without the help of flowers, this species can be confused with B. lacera. Their leaf shapes are similar, and in some locations they grow close to each other. However, the leaves of this species are more oblong, with a firmer papery texture, both in the fresh and in the dried state. The present species does not usually branch, and can be over 1 m tall; B. lacera often branches, never reaches 1 m tall even at maturity.

Blumea sessiliflora Decne. 無梗艾納香
Nouv. Ann. Mus. Hist. Nat. 3: 140. 1834; Randeria, Blumea 10: 257. 1960; FRPS 75: 35. 1979.

Annual herbs, to 1.3 m tall; stems erect, usually unbranched, with slightly raised longitudinal ribs, covered sparsely with short, coarse hairs. Lower leaves sessile, oblanceolate to obovate‑oblong, 10–16 × 4–6 cm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex acute, margins runcinate‑lyrate, with irregular teeth, pilose on both surfaces; upper leaves decreasing gradually, sessile, oblanceolate to oblong, 3–6 × 0.5–1.5 cm; the uppermost leaves linear, bract‑like, entire or with a few sharp teeth. Capitula 3–4 mm across, 3 or more clustered, sessile or on a very short peduncle (2 mm), forming axillary panicles varying from 9 cm at the very bottom axils to 22 cm on mid‑stem, and gradually decreasing to 4–5 cm at apex. Involucre cylindric or subcampanulate, 4–6 mm; phyllaries 4– 5‑seriate, straw‑coloured or green, outer and middle ones lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, 2–4 mm, apex acuminate, margin scarious, densely pubescent abaxially, inner ones linear, 4–6 mm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent abaxially. Receptacle slightly convex, foveolate, glabrous, scabrous, about 2 mm across. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous; corolla slender tubular, 3.5–4 mm, limb 3‑lobed; bisexual florets fewer, corolla tubular, 4–5 mm, slightly enlarged at the 5‑lobed limb. Cypselae cylindric or subfusiform, 0.5 mm, ribbed. Pappus white, 3 mm.

Locality: The Peak, Kowloon Peak, Sha Tin, Tai Lam Chung, Lamma Island. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22903 (CUHK); S. L. Thrower 1487 (CUHK); N. H. Li & K. M. Lau 544 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Indonesia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, prefering sheltered, damp locations. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.
Notes: Despite its production of numerous fruits, it is not common in Hong Kong.

Blyxa aubertii Rich. 無尾水篩
Mem. Cl. Sci. Math. Phys. Inst. France 12(2): 19. 1812; Fl. Males. 5(4): 390. 1957; FHN 4: 61. 1977 [“auberti”]; FRPS 8: 174, pl. 68: 1–2. 1992; FFJ 6: 28. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 11. 2000; FGD 6: 298. 2005; FOC 23: 99. 2010.
Blyxa ecaudata Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan 5: 208, pl. 77c – f. 1915.
Blyxa roxburghii auct. non Rich.: FHK 347. 1861; FKH 257. 1912.

Submerged herb. Stems shortened. Leaves all in basal rosette, linear, 5–17(–60) cm × 3(–12) mm, veins 5–9, apex acuminate. Spathes green, 3–5 cm × ca. 2 mm, with peduncle 2.7–8 cm. Flowers bisexual. Sepals greenish purple, linear-lanceolate, 5–7 × ca. 1 mm. Petals 9–17 × ca. 0.5 mm. Stamens 3; filaments 3–6 mm; anthers 1–1.8 mm. Ovary narrowly cylindrical, 2.5–4 cm; styles ca. 7 mm. Fruit (2–)4–6(–8) cm. Seeds 30–70, oblong-ovoid, 1.2–1.8 × ca. 0.6 mm, ca. 6–12-ribbed; ribs obscurely tuberculate or ridged; rounded at both ends, without tails.

Locality: Happy Valley, Chai Wan, Sai Keng, Tai O. HK sheet 7051, 27111, 27112.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E & S Asia, Africa, Australia, also introduced into N America.
Ecology: Paddy fields and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Blyxa octandra (Roxb.) Planch ex Thwaites previously (Check List HK Plants 77. 1993).

Blyxa japonica (Miq.) Maxim. ex Asch. & Gürke 水篩
Engler & Prantl, Pflanzenfam. 2(1): 253. 1889; FGZ 649, fig. 343. 1956; FRPS 8: 171, pl. 67: 1 – 2. 1992; FFJ 6: 29. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 13, pl. 6. 2000; FGD 6: 297, fig. 166. 2005; FOC 23: 98. 2010.
Hydrilla japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavi 2: 271. 1866.
Blyxa laevissima Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 208 – 209, fig. 77a – b. 1915.
Ottelia japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 271. 1866.
Lagarosiphon roxburghii auct. non Benth.: FKH 257. 1912.

Submerged herb. Stems elongate, 10–20 cm tall, branched. Leaves cauline, lanceolate, 3–6 cm × 1–3 mm, veins 3, apex acuminate. Spathes sessile, green, 1–3 cm × 1–3 mm. Flowers bisexual. Sepals green with purple midvein, linear-lanceolate, 2–4 × 0.5–1 mm. Petals 6–10 × 0.5–1 mm. Stamens 3; filaments 1–3 mm, smooth; anthers 1.8–2.5 mm. Ovary conical; styles 3–4 mm. Fruit 1–2.5 cm. Seeds 30 – 60, narrowly elliptic, smooth, obtuse at both ends.

Locality: Pat Heung. HK sheet 27094.
Distribution: NE, E, C & S China to Sichuan; Japan, Korea, Indochina to S Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Paddy fields, marshy pools and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Boea hygrometrica (Bunge) R. Br. 旋蒴苣苔
Pl. Jav. Rar. 120. 1840 [On Cyrtandreae 120. 1839]; FRPS 69: 474. 1990; FOC 18: 368. 1998; FGD 6: 283. 2005.
Dorcoceras hygrometrica Bunge, Enum. Pl. China Bor. 54. 1833.

Herbs, perennial, stemless. Leaves basal and rosulate; petiole to 0.5 cm; leaf blade suborbicular to ovate, 1.5–4 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate to truncate, apex rounded, margin dentate to crenulate, adaxially white villous, abaxially densely white to brownish woolly; venation palmate, nearly parallel; veins 3–9. Cymes umbel‑like, 2–5‑flowered; peduncle 5–18 cm, puberulent to pubescent; bracts linear to lanceolate, 1–3 mm long; pedicels 1–3cm, pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 5‑sect from near base; segments narrowly lanceolate, 2–3 mm, apex obtuse, margin entire, abaxially puberulent, adaxially glandular puberulent. Corolla blue‑purple, 1–1.5 cm, abaxially sparsely pubescent; tube ca. 5 mm, 6–10 mm in diam.; limb distinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip lobes ca. 4 mm; abaxial lip lobes equal, obovate or ovate, 5–6 mm. Stamens 2, adnate to corolla tube near middle; filaments ca. 1 mm, glabrous; anthers coherent in pairs at apex, anther thecae obovate, ca. 2 mm; staminodes 3. Pistil pubescent; ovary oblong, ca. 5 mm; style ca. 4 mm, glabrous; stigma 1, terminal. Capsule oblong, 3–3.5 cm, pubescent, twisted. Seeds ovate.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang. W. J. Tutcher 10926.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, SW Liaoning, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Rocks in ravines and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.

Boehmeria densiflora Hook. & Arn. 密花苧麻
Bot. Beechey Voy. 271. 1838; FKH 250. 1912; FOC 5: 174. 2003.
Boehmeria penduliflora Wedd. ex Long var. loochooensis (Wedd.) W. T. Wang, FRPS 23(2): 355. 1995; FGD 6: 103. 2005.
Boehmeria platyphylla D. Don. var. loochooensis Wedd., Prodr. 16(1): 213. 1869.

Shrub to 2 m tall. Branchlets densely covered with appressed short hairs. Leaves opposite, rarely subopposite; stipules subulate, to 1.5 cm; petioles 1–2 cm, hispid; leaf blade lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 5 –19 × 1.2–3.5 cm, base obtuse or subrounded, apex acuminate, margin obtusely denticulate above the base, adaxial surface scabrous, sparsely pubescent, glabrescent, bullate due to impressed reticulation of veins, abaxial surface covered with appressed short hairs on raised veins; lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein. Female spikes axillary, 4–12 cm; male spikes shorter, borne on separate plants, or on the same plant but below the females. Male flower clusters 1–2 mm in diam.; female flower cluster 2.5 – 6 mm in diam. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, elliptic, ca. 1.2 mm, puberulent abaxially; stamens 4, ca. 1.8 mm; rudimentary pistil elliptic, ca. 0.5 mm. Female flowers rhomboid or oblanceolate, 1–1.5 mm; stigma 0.7–1 mm. Achene compressed elongate-ellipsoid to fusiform, ca. 0.5 mm, margin more or less flattened.

Locality: Stubbs Road, Lugard Road, Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 31319.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Roadsides, hillslopes, stream banks. Flowering: Apr.–May.

Boehmeria macrophylla Hornem. 水苧麻
Hort. Bot. Hafn. 2: 890. 1815; Grierson & Long, Fl. Bhutan 1(1): 126. 1983; FRPS 23(2): 336, pl. 75: 1–2. 1995; FOC 5: 169. 2003; FGD 6: 105. 2005.
Boehmeria platyphylla D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 60. 1825; FKH 250. 1912.

Subshrub, 1–2(–3.5) m tall. Stems covered with appressed short hairs on upper part. Leaves opposite or nearly so; petioles 0.8– 8 cm, unequal in the same pair; leaf blade ovate to elliptic-ovate, 6.5 –14 × 3.2–7.5 cm, base rounded or shallowly cordate, ± oblique, apex longcuspidate or acuminate, margin denticulate above the base, adaxial surface slightly scabrous, covered with appressed short hairs, abaxial surface sparsely covered with appressed short hairs; lateral veins 2–3 on each side of midvein. Flower-clusters (glomerules) 1–2.5 mm in diam., forming axillary, solitary spikes of 7–15 cm, or the rachis with a few branches, usually the males below the females. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, navicular or elliptic, ca. 1 mm, sparsely puberulent abaxially; stamens 4, ca. 1.5 mm; rudimentary pistil narrowly obovoid, ca. 0.4 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments rhomboid or elliptic, ca. 1 mm, apex with 2 small teeth, puberulent abaxially; style 1–1.6 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak. H. C. Tang 1417; W. J. Tutcher 11209.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, SE Xizang; Vietnam, Myanmar, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests or by streams.
Uses: Material (fibre).

Boehmeria nivea (L.) Gaudich. 苧麻
Voy. Uranie, Bot. 12: 499. 1830; FHK 331. 1861; FKH 250. 1912; FHN 2: 414. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 327, pl. 73: 1– 4. 1995; FOC 5: 166. 2003; FGD 6: 101, fig. 43. 2005.
Urtica nivea L., Syst. 985. 1753.

Subshrub, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems and petioles covered with spreading long hairs and appressed short hairs. Leaves alternate; stipules free, subulate-lanceolate, 7–11 mm, hairy abaxially; petioles 2.5–9.5 cm; leaf blade orbicular-ovate or broadly ovate, 6–15 × 4–11 cm, base subtruncate or broadly cuneate, apex cuspidate, margin dentate, adaxial surface slightly scabrous, sparsely strigose, abaxial surface densely white-tomentose; lateral veins 3 on each side of midvein. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), in glomerules. Female glomerules globular, 0.5–2 mm in diam., numerous, in axillary panicles. Male glomerules 1–3 mm in diam., in panicles, usually below the females. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, narrowly elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, united to middle, apex acute, sparsely pubescent abaxially; stamens 4, ca. 2 mm; rudimentary pistil narrowly obovoid, ca. 0.7 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments elliptic, 0.6–1 mm, apex minutely 2–3-toothed, puberulent abaxially; style filiform, 0.5 –0.6 mm. Achene subglobular, ca. 0.6 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong, either wild or in cultivation. HK sheet 25985, 25989, 40468.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Waste places near villages. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Material (fibre).

Boehmeria nivea var. tenacissima (Gaudich.) Miq. 青葉苧麻
Fl. Ind. Bat. 1(2): 253. 1859; FOC 5: 167. 2003; FGD 6: 102. 2005.
Boehmeria nivea (L.) Gaudich. var. nippononivea (Koidz.) W. T. Wang, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 3(3): 320. 1981; FRPS 23(2): 330, pl. 73: 5. 1995; FOC 5: 166. 2003.
Boehmeria nipononivea Koidz., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 10: 223. 1941.
Boehmeria tenacissima Gaudich., Voy. Uranie, Bot. 500. 1830.

It differs from var. nivea mainly by the following characters: Stems and petioles only covered with appressed short hairs, without spreading hairs; leaf blade generally ovate, rarely orbicular-ovate, base abruptly narrowed, cuneate; stipules united at the base.

Locality: Tseng Lan Shue. Y. S. Lau 2716; HK sheet 25986.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Waste places near villages.
Uses: Material (fibre).

Boeica guileana B. L. Burtt 紫花短筒苣苔
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 35: 371. 1977; FRPS 69: 256. 1990; FOC 18: 288. 1998; FGD 6: 259. 2005.

Herbs, stemless. Leaves basal, rosulate; petioles 1–3 cm, densely villous; leaf blade elliptic, 2–5 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acute to rounded, margin serrate to double serrate, white villous and puberulent; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Cymes 1‑flowered; peduncle 2–7 cm, purple villous; bracts 2, linear, ca. 3 mm, purple villose, margin entire; pedicels 1–2 cm, purple villose. Calyx zygomorphic, 5‑sect from base; segments lanceolate to linear, outside villous, margin entire. Corolla blue purple, ca. 1 cm, outside puberulent; tube ca. 2 mm; limb distinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed from middle, lobes obovate, ca. 6 × 5 mm, apex obtuse; abaxial lip 3‑lobed from base, lobes obovate, ca. 10 × 6 mm. Stamens 4, free, adnate to corolla tube near base; filaments ca. 4 mm, sparsely puberulent; anthers obovate, ca. 2 mm, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk ring‑like. Pistil pubescent; ovary conical, ca. 3 mm long; style ca. 7 mm long; stigma 1, terminal. Capsule oblong, 1–1.5 cm, densely pubescent, much longer than persistent calyx. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Luk Keng. P. S. Choi 542; S. C. Ng 2217; F. W. Xing 7345.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Damp rocks in forests, in steep ravines or on cliffs. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by D. P. M. Guile from Ma On Shan in July 1971. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Boerhavia diffusa L. 黃細心
Sp. Pl. 3. 1753; FGZ 172. 1956; FGD 2: 108, fig. 75. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 320, pl. 149, photo 135. 1996; FRPS 26: 11, pl. 2: 5 –7. 1996; FOC 5: 434. 2003.
Boerhavia repens L., Sp. Pl. 3. 1753; FKH 213. 1912.

Perennial herb, 1–2 m tall. Stems diffuse, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-oblong, 0.5 – 5 × 0.5 –3 cm, base obtuse, cuneate or cordate, apex obtuse, acuminate or acute, margin slightly undulate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, often glaucous and glandular on abaxial surface. Thyrses axillary, 0.5 –7 cm; pedicels 0.3 –2 mm; bracteoles 1–3, lanceolate. Calyx ca. 4 mm, constricted at middle, upper part campanulate, 1–2 mm, white, red or purple, 5-lobed, lower part tubular, 1–1.2 mm, 5-ribed. Stamens 1–3(–5), slightly exserted. Ovary obovate or obovate-oblong. Fruit clavate, 2.5–3.3 mm, 5-ribbed, covered with glands and hairs.

Locality: Hung Hom, Lantau Island, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 2478, 3125; HK Sheet 22959.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Boerhavia erecta L. 直立黃細心
Sp. Pl. 3. 1753; FGD 2: 108. 1991; FRPS 26: 12, pl. 2: 8. 1996; FOC 5: 433. 2003.

Perennial herb, 20– 80 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent at base, initially puberulous, glabrescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1.5 – 4 cm; leaf blade ovate or lanceolate, 1.5 – 5 × 1– 4 cm, base rounded or truncate, apex acute, rarely obtuse, margin entire, adaxially scabrous, abaxially white, puberulous or glandular. Thyrses axillary, 2–3 cm; pedicels 0.5 – 5 mm; bracteoles 1–2, lanceolate, 0.8 –1 mm. Calyx 1.7–2.5 cm, constricted at middle, upper part campanulate, 1.5–2 mm, white, red or purple, 5-lobed, lower part tubular, 1–1.2 mm, 5-ribbed. Stamens 2–3, slightly exserted. Fruit obconical, 3 –3.5 mm, 5-ribbed, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 1269.
Distribution: Guangdong, Xisha Islands; Malesia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Bombax ceiba L. 木棉
Sp. Pl. 511. 1753.
Gossampinus malabarica (DC.) Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 126. 1927; FGZ 243. 1956; FHN 2: 87, fig. 337. 1965.
Bombax malabaricum DC., Prodr. 1: 479. 1824; FRPS 49(2): 106, pl. 29: 5 –9. 1984; FGD 3: 215, fig. 146. 1995.

Tree, up to 25 m tall; bark greyish white, trunk of young trees and branches of older trees usually very spiny. Stipules small. Petioles 10 –20 cm; petiolules 1.5– 4 cm; leaflets 5–7, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 10 –20 × 3.5 –7 cm, base broad cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins 15 –17 pairs. Flowers usually red, sometimes orange-red, ca. 10 cm in diam.; calyx 2– 4.5 cm, glabrous abaxially, densely yellowish sericeous adaxially, 3 – 5-lobed, lobes semiorbicular, 1.5 × 2.3 cm; petals fleshy, obovate-oblong, 8 –10 × 3 – 4 cm, stellate-puberulous on both surfaces; stamen-tubes short, filaments thick; style longer than stamens. Capsule ellipsoid, obtuse, 10 –15 × 4.5 – 5 cm, densely greyish-white-villous and stellate-puberulous. Seeds many, obovate, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1104, 2454; HK sheet 3573.
Distribution: S & SW China; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Bothriochloa bladhii (Retz.) S. T. Blake 臭根子草
Proc. Roy. Soc. Queensland. 80: 62. 1969; FRPS 10(2): 148. 1997; FYN 9: 663, pl. 110: 4–6. 2003; FOC 22: 607. 2006; FGD 9: 494. 2009.

Andropogon bladhii Retz., Observ. Bot. 2: 27. 1761.
Andropogon intermedius R. Br., Prodr. 1: 202. 1810; FKH 323. 1912.
Andropogon vachellii Nees, Bot. Beechey Voy. 243. 1838; FHK 423. 1861.
Bothriochloa intermedia (R. Br.) A. Camus, Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 76(1930): 164. 1931; FFJ 6: 267, fig. 239. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 527. 2000.
Bothriochloa glabra (Roxb.) A. Camus, Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 76: 164. 1931; FHN 4: 476, fig. 1262. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 149. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 527, pl. 222. 2000.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or decumbent at base, 60–90(–150) cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, the upper shorter and the lower longer than internodes; leaf blades linear, 10–30 × 0.2–1 cm, glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs on both surfaces; ligule membranous, 0.5–2 mm, truncate. Inflorescence composed of many racemes borne in loose whorls along an elongate central axis; rachis internodes and pedicels thinly ciliate. Sessile spikelet bisexual, oblong-lanceolate, callus white bearded; lower glume narrowly oblong-lanceolate, dorsally compressed, glabrous or pubescent below middle, abaxially slightly concave, margins inrolled to 2-keeled, ciliate on keel, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, margins membranous and the upper ciliate, acute; lower lemma ovate or oblong-lanceolate, seldom margins and apex sparsely ciliate, acute; upper lemma absent, linear, a geniculate awn arising from the apex, awn 10–16 mm. Pedicellate spikelet barren or rarely staminate, narrower than sessile spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 120, 589; Y. S. Lau 2250.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Xinjiang, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, SW Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Bothriochloa ischaemum (L.) Keng 白羊草
Contr. Biol. Lab. Chin. Assoc. Advancem. Sci., Sect. Bot. 10: 201. 1936; FHN 4: 476. 1977; FFJ 6: 266, fig. 238. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 144. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 527, pl. 223. 2000; FOC 22: 608. 2006; FGD 9: 493. 2009.
Andropogon ischaemum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1047. 1753; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculately ascending, 30–70 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, congested at plant base; leaf blades linear, 3–18 × 0.2–0.3 cm, usually sparingly hairy with tubercle-based hairs, the lower glabrous, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, obtuse or rounded, ciliate. Inflorescence composed of 4–15 racemes, subdigitate; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate with long white or pinkish silky hairs. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate, callus bearded; lower glume usually cartilaginous, sometimes herbaceous, silky-pilose below 1/3 length, apex obtuse and membranous, margins inrolled, 5–7-veined; upper glume boatshaped, keel scabrous, ciliate above the middle, margins submembranous; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, apex acute, upper margins sparsely ciliate; upper lemma reduced to linear, with a geniculate awn arising from the apex; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, subequal to sessile spikelet, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. C. Ng 2023.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Ningxia, Nei Mongol, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Shandong, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; C and SW Asia, Europe, N Africa, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides, disturbed places. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Animal food (forage), environmental (erosion control).

Bothriochloa pertusa (L.) A. Camus 孔穎草
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, N. S. 76: 164. 1931 [“1930”]; H. B. Gill. et al, Fl. Malaya 3: 281. 1971; FRPS 10(2): 145, pl. 35: 1–6, 77: 2. 1997; FYN 9: 666, pl. 110: 9–10. 2003; FOC 22: 608. 2006; FGD 9: 493, fig. 260. 2009.
Holcus pertusus L., Mant. Pl. 2: 301. 1771.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, up to 100 cm tall, 5- or more-noded, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous, keeled; leaf blades linear, 5–20 × 0.1 – 0.4 cm, tuberclebased hairs on both surfaces or abaxial surface glabrous, apex acute, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–2 mm, dry membranous. Inflorescence composed of 3–8(–13) racemes, subdigitate; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate with long silky hairs. Sessile spikelet lanceolate, callus bearded; lower glume papery, a circular pit in the upper 1/3, glabrous sparsely hirtellous to silky-pilose below middle, margins incurved and 2-keeled, scabrous on the keel, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, acute; lower lemma oblong, glabrous; upper lemma linear, a geniculate awn arising from the apex, awn 1–2 cm long. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, purplish, subequal to sessile spikelet, glabrous.

Locality: Quarry Bay. HK sheet 15532.
Distribution: Guangdong, Sichuan, Yunnan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, naturalized elsewhere in tropics. Ecology: Grassy hills, disturbed grounds, alt. 1200–1500 m. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (forage), environmental (erosion control).

Bothriospermum zeylanicum (J. Jacq.) Druce 柔弱斑種草
Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles. 4: 610. 1917; FOC 16: 420. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 388. 1998.
Anchusa zeylanica J. Jacq., Ecl. Pl. Rar. 1: 47, t. 29. 1812.
Anchusa tenella Hornem., Hort. Bot. Hafn. 1: 176. 1815.
Bothriospermum tenellum (Hornem.) Fisch. & C. A. Mey., Index Sem. (St. Petersburg) 1: 24. 1835; FHK 235. 1861; FKH 177. 1912; FGZ 569, fig. 304. 1956; FTW 4: 393. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 218. 1990; FFJ 4: 514, fig. 408. 1989; Check List HK Plants 227. 2002; 79. 2004.

Annual herb, 15–30 cm tall. Stems slender, crowded, erect or prostrate, multibranched, appressed hispid. Leaf blade elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 1–2.5 cm × 5–10 mm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse, mucronulate, sparsely short appressed bristly or strigose. Racemes numerous, to 12 cm; lower bracts several, lanceolate, 1.5– 5 mm, apex acute; upper ones very small. Pedicel 1–2 mm, not elongate or somewhat elongate in fruit. Calyx 1 – 1.5 mm, to 3 mm in fruit, with short ascending white bristles. Corolla blue or pale blue, 1.5 – 1.8 mm, base ca. 1 mm wide, slightly longer than calyx; throat appendages ca. 0.2 mm; limb 2.5–3 mm wide; lobes orbicular, ca. 1 mm. Style terete, ca. 0.5 mm. Nutlets grey, reniform, 1–1.2 mm.

Locality: South Bay Rd., Fanling, Sheung Shui, Lam Tsuen, Peng Shan. Y. S. Lau 2673, 3059; Y. W. Lam 2267.
Distribution: S, SW, E, N & NE China; Korea, Japan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Pakistan, India, Vietnam, Indonesia (Java, naturalized).
Ecology: Grasslands along roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Oct.

Bougainvillea spectabilis Willd. 葉子花（毛寶巾、簕杜鵑）
Sp. Pl. 2: 348. 1799; FGZ 170. 1956; FGD 2: 107. 1991; FRPS 26: 6. 1996; FOC 5: 432. 2003.

Scandent shrub. Stems to 10 m or longer, puberulous; branches often with spines. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, 4 –9 × 2– 4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded or subtruncate, often slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate, puberulent on both surfaces or glabrescent abaxially. Flowers in cluster of 3, subtended by 3 large bracts and forming large, terminal panicles. Pedicels adnate to the midvein of bracts. Bracts leafy, broadly ovate to subrounded, 3 –3.8 × 2.5 –2.8 cm, red, purple or orange. Calyx-tube ca. 1.4 mm, 5-ribed, puberulent abaxially; limb ca. 7 mm in diam., 5-lobed, white or pink. Stamens usually 8, unequal, included; filaments united at the base. Ovary elongate; stigma feathery, on one side of the style.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens or as a pot plant. Y. S. Lau 1087, 1091, 3064.
Distribution: Cultivated in S China; native to Brazil.
Ecology: The plant thrives in sunny places, flowering almost all the year round, but never set fruit in Hong Kong and S China.
Notes: Bougainvillea glabra Choisy is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It is very similar to this species, but can be distinguished by its glabrescent calyx-tube, young shoots and leaves.

Bowringia callicarpa Champ. ex Benth. 藤槐
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 75. 1852; FHK 95. 1861; FKH 87. 1912; FRPS 40: 97. 1994; FGD 5: 220, fig. 123. 2003.

Scandent shrub. Leaves simple; petioles 1 – 3 cm, slightly turgid on both ends; stipules small, ovate-deltoid; leaf blade sub-leathery, oblong or ovate-oblong, 6 – 13 × 2 – 6 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 5 –6 on each side of midvein. Racemes axillary, 2 – 5-flowered; pedicels 10 – 13 cm. Calyx cup-shaped, teeth minute. Corolla white; vexillum suborbicular or oblong, 6–8 mm, apex emarginate or obcordate; claw 1 –2 mm; wings falcate-oblong, slightly longer than vexillum; keel oblong, 5– 7 mm. Stamens 10, unequal, free. Pods ovoid, 2.5 – 3 × 1.5 cm, apex rostrate, with distinct reticulate veins on both surfaces. Seeds l – 2, dark brown or black, elliptic, 12 × 8 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 475; Y. S. Lau 1168; K. L. Yip 4103.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Dec.– Jan.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by John C. Bowring, Jr. around 1850.

Brachiaria brizantha (Hochst. ex A. Rich) Stapf 柵狀臂形草（信號草）
Fl. trop. Afr. 9: 531. 1919.
Panicum brizanthum Hochst. ex A. Rich., Tent. Fl. Abyss. 2: 363. 1851.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, or geniculately ascending, to 100–200(–300) cm tall. Leaf blades linear, or lanceolate; ligule a fringe of hairs. Inflorescence composed of racemes; racemes (1–)2–16; borne along a central axis; rhachis narrowly winged, margins ciliate. Spikelet single, packing adaxial, 1-rowed. Spikelets elliptic, 4–6 mm, falling entire, dorsally compressed, subacute or acute; glumes dissimilar; lower glume ovate, clasping, 1/3 length of spikelet, membranous, no keels, 7–11-veined, obtuse or acute; upper glume oblong, as long as spikelet, cartilaginous, no keels, 7–9-veined, glabrous or pubescent, obtuse or acute; lower florets staminate, with palea; lower lemma similar to upper glume; upper lemma elliptic, 3.5–5.5 mm.

Locality: Ta Kwu Ling. Y. W. Lam 859; HK sheet 35005.
Distribution: Africa; naturalized elsewhere in tropics.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Spring to autumn.

Brachiaria mutica (Forssk.) Stapf 巴拉草
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 526. 1919; FRPS 10(1): 269. 1990; FFJ 6: 218. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 458, pl. 190. 2000; FOC 22: 520. 2006; FGD 9: 423. 2009.
Panicum muticum Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.-Arab. 20. 1775.
Urochloa mutica (Forssk.) T. Q. Nguyen, Novosti Sist. Vysa. Rast. 1966: 13. 1966.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, to 3 m tall, nodes densely villous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or villous at mouth, longer than internode; leaf blades broadly linear, 10–30 × 1–2 cm, thinly pilose or subglabrous; ligule membranous, ca. 1 mm. Inflorescence racemose; racemes 10–20 cm, solitary, paired or grouped; spikelets paired or solitary in upper part of raceme, in untidy rows or sometimes on short secondary branchlets in lower part of raceme. Spikelets green or purplish, elliptic, 2.5–3.5 mm; lower glume triangular, 1/4–1/3 length of spikelet, 1-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined; lower floret staminate, lower lemma 5-veined, rugulose, palea subequal to lemma; upper lemma ca. 3 mm, crustaceous, margins narrowly incurved.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sha Tin, Yuen Long, Nam Sang Wai, San Tin, Mai Po, Plover Cove, Tsing Yi. Y. S. Lau 2533; L. T. Lo 552; HK sheet 39681.
Distribution: Cultivated in Fujian and Taiwan, probably originated from tropical Africa, now widely introduced and naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Streamsides, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Brachiaria subquadripara (Trin.) Hitchc. 四生臂形草
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 214. 1931 [“1929”]; FHN 4: 420. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 266, pl. 80: 1–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 217, fig. 184. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 460. 2000; FOC 22: 522. 2006; FGD 9: 422, fig. 217. 2009.
Panicum subquadriparum Trin., Gram. Panic. 145. 1826.
Urochloa subquadripara (Trin.) R. D. Webster, Austral. Paniceae 252. 1987.

Annual herb. Culms slender, straggling, rooting at lower nodes, 20–60 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths loose, usually glabrous, rarely with tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 4–15 × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous or pubescent, base subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margins thicker and scabrous. Inflorescence axis 3–10 cm; racemes 3–6, 2–4 cm, divergent to reflexed; rachis, narrowly winged, nearly glabrous; spikelets single, in 2 rows; pedicels glabrous. Spikelets elliptic, 3.5–4 mm, glabrous, acute; lower glume broadly ovate, 1/3–1/2 spikelet length, 5–7-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined; upper lemma finely rugose, margins slightly inrolled embraced same texture palea, subacute; stamens 3; style base free.

Locality: Aberdeen, Kowloon Peak, To Fung Shan, Plover Cove, Peng Chau. Y. W. Lam 778, 989, 1610.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Australia, widely naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Grassy places of hillslopes, open fields and thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Brachycorythis galeandra (Rchb. f.) Summerh. 短距苞葉蘭（頭盔蘭）
Kew Bull. 10: 241. 1955; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 30, fig. 7. 1977; FRPS 17: 284, pl. 41: 4–6. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 760. 2000; FGD 7: 765, fig. 186. 2006; FOC 25: 101. 2009.
Platanthera galeandra Rchb. f., Linnaea 25: 226. 1852.
Habenaria galeandra (Rchb. f.) Benth., FHK 363. 1861.
Platanthera obcordata auct. non Rchb. f.: FKH 269. 1912.

Terrestrial herb up to 25 cm tall, needing a resting period during winter dry season; underground tuber ellipsoidal, 1.5 2 cm thick. Leaves 9–15, all cauline, internodes 1.5–2 cm; petiolate; leaf blade lanceolate-elliptic, 3–4.5 × 1–1.5 cm. Flowers white with rose-lilac lines; lip spurred; column white; anthers with parallel thecae; pollinia 2; ovary cylindrical, 1.2 cm, papillose.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Kowloon Peak, Ma On Shan, Shing Mun. K. K. Mark 25(2844) (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 10521 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2495.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Short grasses on windy peaks of high mountains in Hong Kong. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.

Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. 芥菜
Conspect. Fl. Chark 8. 1859; FGD 3: 30. 1995; FOC 8: 20. 2001.
Brassica juncea var. crispifolia L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb.1:：91. 1891; FGD 3: 30. 1995.
Brassica juncea var. foliosa L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb. 2: 263. 1930; FGD 3: 30. 1995.

Annual herbs, 30–150 cm tall, glaucous, with pungent smell. Basal leaves broad-ovate to obovate, 15–20 cm, lyrate, lateral lobes 2–3 pairs, margin incised or dentate. Petioles 3–9 cm, with small lobes; cauline leaves smaller, not amplexicaul. Racemes terminal. Flowers yellow, 7–10 mm in diam.; pedicles 4–10 mm. Sepals oblong-elliptic, 4–5 mm. Petals obovate, 8–10 mm, claw 4–5 mm. Siliques linear, 3 –5.5 cm, beak 6–12 mm, slightly constricted between seeds; stalk 15–25 mm. Seeds purple-brown, globose, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 183.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Uses: Vegetable, spice, medicinal (seed).

Brassica oleracea L. 葉甘藍
Sp. Pl. 2: 667. 1753; FOC 8: 17. 2001.

Biennial or perennial herb, rarely annual, 0.6–1.5 m tall, glabrous, glaucous. Stems erect or decumbent, branched at or above middle, sometimes fleshy at base. Basal and lowermost cauline leaves long petiolate, sometimes strongly overlapping and forming a head; petiole to 30 cm; leaf blade ovate, oblong or lanceolate, to 40 × 15 cm, margin entire, repand or dentate, sometimes pinnatifid or pinnatisect and with a large terminal lobe and smaller, 1–13, oblong or ovate, lateral lobes on each side of midvein; upper cauline leaves sessile or subsessile, oblanceolate, ovate or oblong, to 10 × 4 cm, base amplexicaul, auriculate or rarely cuneate, margin entire, repand, or rarely dentate. Racemes sometimes fleshy and condensed into a head. Sepals oblong, 0.8 –1.5 cm, erect. Petals creamy yellow or rarely white, ovate or elliptic, 1.8 –2.5 cm, claw 0.7–1.5 cm. Siliques linear, 3–9 × 3–5 mm, terete, 10–20-seeded per locule, valves with a prominent midrib. Seeds dark brown or blackish, globose, 1.5 –2.5 mm in diam., minutely reticulate.

Wild populations of var. oleracea are known only from the coastal cliffs of W Europe; five varieties are cultivated in Hong Kong for vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. albiflora Kuntze 芥蘭
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 19. 1891; FOC 8: 18. 2001.
Brassica alboglabra L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb. 1: 79. 1922; FGD 3: 27. 1995.

Stems 30–40 cm tall, not fleshy, narrowly cylindric. Basal and lower cauline leaves green, few to several, widely spaced, not grouped into a head, ovate, 6–10 cm, base auriculate, decurrent, margin sinuate or irregularly serrulate. Inflorescence lax, not fleshy. Flowers white or rarely creamy white.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. botrytis L. 椰菜花
Sp. Pl. 667. 1753; FGD 3: 26. 1995; FOC 8: 18. 2001.

Stems 60–90 cm tall, glaucous, base elongated, not fleshy. Basal and lower cauline leaves green, few to several, widely spaced, not group into a head. Inflorescence fleshy, forming a compact globose head. Flower buds, pedicels, rachis and peduncles white.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. capitata L. 椰菜（甘藍）
Sp. Pl. 667. 1753; FGD 3: 26. 1995; FOC 8: 18. 2001.

Stems highly shortened, not fleshy, conical. Basal and lower cauline leaves green, many, oblong-obovate to orbicular, overlapped layer upon layer forming a globose or compressed-globose head, 20 – 40 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. gongylodes L. 芥蘭頭
Sp. Pl. 667. 1753; FOC 8: 18. 2001.
Brassica caulorapa (DC.) Pasq., Catal. Ort. Bot. Nap. 17. 1867; FGD 3: 27. 1995.

Stems 30– 60 cm tall, base highly shortened, fleshy, globose. Basal leaves not overlapping into a head, broad-ovate to oblong, 13 –20 cm, margin irregularly dentate; cauline leaves oblong to linear-oblong, margin sinuate. Inflorescences neither fleshy nor condensed into a head.

Locality: Cultivated. Leung & Wong s.n. (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. italica Plenck 西蘭花
Icon. Pl. Medic. 6: 29. 1794; FOC 8: 18. 2001.

Different from the above variety by: inflorescence somewhat loose, usually obconical; flower buds, pedicels, rachis and peduncles green.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica chinensis L. 白菜（青菜）
Gent. Pl. 1: 19. 1755; FKH 34. 1912; FHN 1: 355. 1964; FGD 3: 29. 1995.
Brassica rapa var. chinensis (L.) Kitamura, Mem. Coll. Sci. Univ. Kyoto, ser. B, 19: 79. 1950; FOC 8: 20. 2001, p.p.

Annual or biennial herb, 25–70 cm tall, glabrous. Basal leaves obovate, oblong or broad-ovate, 20 –30 cm, spreading, blades glabrous, entire or repand. Petioles green or white, 3 –5 cm, fleshy or thickened, wingless, base amplexicaul or not. Racemes terminal. Flowers yellowish, ca. 9 mm. Sepals oblong, 3 – 4 mm. Petals oblong, ca. 5 mm, base broad-clawed, apex obtuse. Siliques linear, 2–6 cm, beak 8–12 mm; stalk up to 3 cm. Seeds purple-brown, globose, 1–1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 9121; S. T. Dunn 1078.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; native to Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica pekinensis (Lour.) Rupr. 大白菜（黃牙白）
Fl. Ingr. 96. 1860; L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb. 1: 97, fig. 43. 1922; FHN 1: 355. 1964; FGD 3: 29. 1995.
Brassica rapa var. glabra Regel, Gartenflora 9: 9. 1860; FOC 8: 20. 2001.

Biennial herb, 40 – 60 cm tall. Basal leaves many and large, thin, obovate-oblong or broad-ovate, margin sinuate. Petioles complanate, 5 –10 × 8 cm, margin crisped, thin, wing-like; cauline leaves amplexicaul, entire or serrate. Flowers light yellow, 1.2–1.5 cm in diam.; pedicles 4 – 6 mm. Sepals oblong or ovatelanceolate, 4 –5 mm. Petals obovate, 7– 8 mm, base clawed. Siliques 3 – 6 cm × 3 mm, compressed, beak 4 –10 mm. Seeds brown, globose, 1–1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated; native to N China.
Ecology: Flowering: May.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica parachinensis L. H. Bailey 菜心
Gentes Herb. 1: 102. 1922; FGD 3: 29. 1995.
Brassica rapa var. chinensis auct. non (L.) Kitamura: FOC 8: 20. 2001, p.p.

The differences between the above species and this species are the base of basal leaves of this species not amplexicaul and petioles slender and sulcate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3074.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Uses: Vegetable.

Bredia fordii (Hance) Diels 葉底紅
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 65(2 – 3): 110. 1933; Hansen, Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 14: 424. 1992.
Phyllagathis fordii (Hance) C. Chen, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin, 4(3): 50. 1984; FRPS 53(1): 224. 1984.
Otanthera fordii Hance, J. Bot. 19(218): 47. 1881.

Shrublet, or shrubby herb, 20 – 50(–100) cm tall; young branches, petiole and inflorescences densely pilose and glandular pubescent. Leaves firmly papery; petiole 2.5– 6.5 cm; leaf blade cordate, elliptic-cordate to ovate-cordate, 4–10(–13.5) × 2–5.5(–10) cm, apex shortly acuminate to obtusely acute, margin double denticulate, ciliate, sparsely pilose and pubescent on both surfaces, especially on veins of abaxial surface. Inflorescences terminal, umbellate, cymose, or cymose paniculate; peduncle 1–5.5 cm; pedicels 0.8–2 cm. Calyx-tube 5–7 mm, campanulate-funnelform; calyx-lobes linear-lanceolate to narrowly triangular, 3–5 mm. Petals purple to purplish red, 7–14 × 6–8 mm, ovate to broadly ovate, apex acuminate, sometimes glandular pubescent, slightly oblique, ciliate. Stamens ± unequal, 1.6–1.8 cm; anthers lanceolate, 7–11 mm, geniculate or slightly curved; connective decurrent, slightly inflated at base. Ovary ovoid, apex with a membranous crown. Capsule, cup-shaped, bristly, 6–10 × 8–12 mm, top truncate.

Locality: No precise locality. HK sheet 11612.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, hillsides, margins of woodlands, shaded damp places, valleys, streamsides, roadsides. Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Phyllagathis fordii (Hance) C. Chen previously (Check List HK Plants 167. 2002; 61. 2004). The type specimen of Phyllagathis fordii was collected from Happy Valley by C. Ford between 1879 and 1880.

Breynia fruticosa (L.) Hook f. 黑面神（鬼畫符）

Fl. Brit. Ind. 5(14): 331, in obs. 1887; FKH 255. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 181, pl. 55: 1 – 6. 1994; FGD 5: 65. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 136. 2005.

Andrachne fruticosa L., Sp. Pl. 1014. 1753.


Shrub, 1 – 3 m tall, glabrous throughout; branches purple, compressed at upper part; branchlets green. Leaves leathery; stipules triangular-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm; petioles 3 – 4 mm; leaf blade ovate, broadly ovate, or rhombic-ovate, 3 – 7 × 1.8 – 3.5 cm, obtuse or acute on both ends, dark-green adaxially, glaucous abaxially, turning black when dry; lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Flowers small, solitary or 2–4 in axillary clusters, usually the male flowers in lower axils, female flowers in upper axils, sometimes male and female flowers borne on different branchlets. Male flowers: pedicels 2–3 mm; calyx turbinate, ca. 2 mm, 6-dentate; stamens 3, connate into a column. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 2 mm; calyx campanulate, shallowly 6-lobed, ca. 4 mm in diam., lobes subequal, subtruncate and apiculate, much enlarged in fruit, radiate spreading; ovary ovoid, styles 3, bilobed, lobes recurved. Fruits globose, 6 –7 mm in diam., crowned with persistent calyx.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2037, 2227; S. P. Lau 147, 179.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos.

Ecology: Shrublands or sunny magins of forests. Flowering: Apr.– Sep.; fruiting: May– Dec.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Bridelia insulana Hance 禾串樹（大葉逼迫仔）
J. Bot. 15: 337. 1877; FRPS 44(1): 47, pl. 12: 4 – 7. 1994; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 146. 2005.
Bridelia balansae Tutcher, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 37: 66. 1905; FKH 233. 1912; FGD 5: 33. 2003.

Tree up to 17 m tall, monoecious; stems scatteringly spinose; branchlets glabrous. Leaves thin-leathery or papery; stipules linear-lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, caducous; petioles 3 – 10 mm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, 5 – 25 × 1.5 – 7.5 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate, glabrous or only puberulous abaxially, margin slightly revolute; lateral veins 5 – 11 on each side of midvein. Flowers clustered in axil of leaves or bracts; bracts triangular ca. 1 mm, pubescent. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 2 mm, pubescent; calyx ca. 2 mm, lobes triangular, puberulous abaxially; petals spatulate, ca. 1 mm; filaments connate to middle; disk shallowly cup-shaped; rudimentary ovary ovoid-conical. Female flowers 4 – 5 mm in diam.; pedicels ca. 1 mm; calyx as in male flowers; petals obovate, ca. 1 mm; disk urceolate, enclosing the lower part of ovary; ovary ovoid, styles 2, free, ca. 1.5 mm, bifid at the apex, lobes linear. Drupes oblong-ovoid or ovoid, 9 – 11 × 7 – 8 mm, purple-black when mature, 1-celled, the stalk very stout, 3 – 5 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Bowen Rd., Tai Mo Shan, Lady Clementi's Ride, Fanling,Wong Nai Chung. H. C. Tang 2032, 2429; HK sheet 5368; W. J. Tutcher 7090, 9973; S. Y. Hu 12582 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Montane forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Bridelia balansae (Hongkong Bot. Gard. no. 974) was collected from Hong Kong Island.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Bridelia balansae (Hongkong Bot. Gard. no. 974) was collected from Hong Kong Island.

records.text:
Bridelia tomentosa Blume 土蜜樹（逼迫仔）

Bijdr. 597. 1825; FHK 309. 1861; FKH 233. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 30, pl. 8: 1 – 4. 1994; FGD 5: 32, fig. 21. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 151. 2005.

Bridelia tomentosa Blume β chinensis Müll.Arg., Prodr. 15(2): 501. 1866.

Bridelia monoica Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 13: 142. 1918.


Shrub or treelet, monoecious or dioecious, 2 – 5 m tall; branchlets slender, tawny pubescent when young. Stipules linear-lanceolate, ca. 7 mm, usually caducous, pubescent. Petioles 3–5 mm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, oblong, oblong-elliptic or obovate-oblong, 3–9 × 1.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute or obtuse, scabrous adaxially, greenish and pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 9–12 on each side of midvein, elevated abaxially. Flowers very small, in globular sessile, axillary clusters. Male flowers: calyx-lobes 5, triangular, ca. 1.2 × 1 mm; petals obovate, membranous, ca. 1 mm, apex 3–5-toothed; stamens 5, filaments connate at proximal half; rudimentary ovary conical; disk shallowly cup-shaped. Female flowers: calyx as in male flowers; petals obovate or spatulate, entire or denticulate, shorter than sepals; disk urceolate, enclosing the ovary; ovary ovoid, styles 2, bipartite, lobes linear. Drupes subglobose, 4 – 7 × 5 mm, 2-locular; seeds brown-red, oblong-ovate, 3.5 – 4 × 3 mm, ventral surface compressed with longitudinal groove, dorsal surface slightly elevated, with longitudinal stripes.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 45, 294, 630, 1363, 1459; HK Sheet 5374, 5376.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Indonesia, Malaysia to Australia.

Ecology: Montane sparse forests or thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Broussonetia kaempferi Sieb. var. australis Suzuki 藤構（葡蟠）
Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 24: 433. 1934; FOC 5: 27. 2003.
Broussonetia kaempferi auct. non Sieb.: FKH 244. 1912

Climber, with milky juice, dioecious. Branches and branchlets elongate, brown pubescent when young. Leaves alternate, ovate-elliptic, 3.5–8 × 2–3 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrulate, scabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially. Male spikes 1.5–2.5 cm. Male flowers: perianth 4–3-parted; segments hairy abaxially; stamens 4–3, pistillode minute. Female heads globose. Female flowers: perianth hairy; style filiform, reddish violet. Syncarps red, globose, 1 cm in diam., with persistent exserted styles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Ho Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. D. P. M. Guile s.n. (HK sheet 30347); P. S. Choi 350.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Fibre, medicinal (folklore).

Broussonetia papyrifera (L.) L'Hérit. ex Vent. 構樹
Tabl. Regn. Veg. 3: 458. 1799; FHN 2: 378. 1965; FGD 1: 178. 1987; FOC 5: 26. 2003.
Morus papyrifera L., Sp. Pl. 986. 1753.

Tree, 10 –20 m tall, dioecious. Branchlets densely pubescent. Stipules ovate, 1.5–2 × 0.8–1 cm. Petioles 2.5–8 cm; leaves thick papery, broad-ovate or oblong-ovate, 6–18 × 5–9 cm, base cordate, unequal, apex acuminute, margin serrulate or 3 –5-lobed, scabrous and sparsely hirsute adaxially, densely tomentose abaxially, basal veins 3; lateral veins 6 –7 pairs. Male catkin cylindrical, 4 – 8 cm. Male flowers: perianth 4-lobed, hairy; stamens 4. Female heads globose, bracts clavate. Female flowers: perianth tubular, apex adnated with style; ovary ovoid. Syncarps red, globose, 1.5–3 cm in diam., fleshy; bracts and perianth persistent, clustered together; achenes red, pericarp crustaceous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2350.
Distribution: Areas S of Shanxi Province; Japan, India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wasteland, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Fibre.

Brucea javanica (L.) Merr. 鴉膽子（苦參子）

J. Arnold Arb. 9: 3. 1928; FGZ 437, fig. 232. 1956; FHN 3: 55, fig. 561. 1974; FYN 1: 186, pl. 44: 1–3. 1977; FTW 3: 540. 1977; FFJ 2: 379, fig. 281. 1985; FGD 1: 232. 1987; FRPS 43(3): 10. 1997.

Rhus javanica L., Sp. Pl. 265. 1753.

Brucea sumatrana Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 12. 1814; FHK 60. 1861; FKH 57. 1912.


Deciduous shrub to tree, to 10 m or taller; young branches, petioles and inflorescence yellow pubescent. Leaves 20–40 cm; leaflets 3–15; petiolules 4–8 mm; blade ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 5–20(–13) × 2.5–5(–6.5) cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, ± oblique, apex acuminate, margin coarsely serrate, pubescent on both surfaces, especially abaxially. Male inflorescences 15–25(–40) cm, female ones half as long as males. Flowers small, dark purple, 1.5–2 mm in diam. Male flowers: pedicels slender, ca. 3 mm; sepals puberulous, 0.5–1 mm; petals sparsely puberulous or subglabrous, 1–2 mm; filaments subulate, ca. 0.6 mm, the anthers ca. 0.4 mm. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 2.5 mm; sepals and petals as in males, stamens rudimentary. Drupes 1–4, distinct, long-ovoid, 6–8 × 4–6 mm, greyish black when mature; exocarp reticulate, wrinkled when dry; endocarp hard bony. Seeds yellow-white, ovoid.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 26; L. T. Lo 131; S. P. Lau 146.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia to Australia.

Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Bruguiera gymnorhiza (L.) Savigny 木欖
Encycl. 4(2): 696. 1798; FKH 103. 1912; FHN 2: 443. 1965; FRPS 52(2): 136. 1983; FGD 1: 109. 1987.
Rhizophora gymnorhiza L., Sp. Pl. 1: 443. 1753.

Tree 6– 20 m tall; bark grey, coarsely fissured. Stipules often reddish, ca. 4 cm. Petiole 2–4.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic-oblong, 7–15 × 3 – 5.5 cm, base cuneate, or rarely obtuse, apex acute, thickly leathery, glabrous. Pedicel 1–2.5 cm. Flowers solitary, red or pinkish red, ca. 3–3.5 cm when full blooming. Calyx-tube dark yellowish red, smooth; lobes 11–13, linear, 1.5–2 cm, glabrous. Petals 1.1–1.5 cm, villous at lower half, 2-cleft, with 3 or 4 bristles at sinus. Stamens slightly shorter than petals; filaments filiform; anthers linear to lanceolate, 4–5 mm. Disk cup-shaped. Ovary 3-locular; style filiform, ca. 1.5 cm; stigma 3–4-lobed. Hypocotyls 15–25 cm, smooth.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung, Kiu Tsui, Yung Shue Au, Tai Po, Plover Cove, Mai Po, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 228; L. T. Lo 446; P. S. Choi 206.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam, E Africa, N Australia, Indian Ocean Islands, Madagascar, New Guinea, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Mangrove forests. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Notes: The species is sometimes cited as “Bruguiera gymnorrhiza (L.) Lam., Tabl. Encyl., pl. 397. 1793”, but no epithet occurs there whereas the plate description (with full name) occurs on 2: 517 in 1819; therefore this name was validly published as at 1819 and thus not of priority.

Brunfelsia calycina Benth. 大鴛鴦茉莉
Prodr. 10: 199. 1847; FGZ 579. 1956; FFJ 5: 5. 1993.

Evergreen shrubs, 1–1.5 m tall, much branched, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves alternate; petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blade oblong to elliptic‑oblong, 5.5–8.5(–10) × 1.5–3(–3.5) cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire. Flowers solitary or in few‑flowered cymes; pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx tubular, 12–16 mm, 5‑toothed. Corolla salverform; tube slender, 1.5–2 cm; limb spreading, 2.5–3.5 cm in diam., initially violet but change to white later. Stamens and style included. Fruit subglobse, berry‑like, pale yellow when mature, 5–7 mm in diam., indehiscent.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34809.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring and autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Buchnera cruciata Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don 黑草（鬼羽箭）
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 91. 1825; FHK 253. 1861; FKH 190. 1912; FOC 18: 88. 1998; FGD 4: 392. 2000.

Herbs 8–50 cm tall, with curved hairs. Stems simple or apically somewhat branched. Basal leaves rosulate; petioles inconspicuous; leaf blade obovate, 2–2.5 × 1–1.5 cm, base tapering. Stem leaves sessile, linear to linear‑oblong, 1.5–4.5 × 0.3–0.5(–1.2) cm, margin often with 2–few obtuse teeth. Spikes terminal, cylindric to subquadrangular, 1–4.5 cm, lengthening to 6.5 cm in fruit. Bracts ovate, ca. 4.8 × 2.5 mm, densely villous; bracteoles linear, 2–3 mm, villous. Calyx 4–4.5 mm, villous; tube slightly curved; lobes triangular, subequal. Corolla blue‑purple, narrowly tubular, somewhat curved, 6–7 mm, somewhat ribbed, villous on portion exserted from calyx, throat constricted; lobes obovate to oblanceolate, 1.5–2 × ca. 1 mm. Anthers ca. 1 mm. Ovary ovoid, 2–2.5 mm. Capsules oblong, ca. 5 mm. Seeds ± spirally striate.

Locality: Ta Kwu Ling, Kong Nga Po. L. T. Lo 256; P. S. Choi 78; Y. W. Lam 2011.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian; S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Buddleja asiatica Lour. 白背楓（駁骨丹）
Fl. Cochinch. 72. 1790; FHK 231. 1861; FKH 174. 1912; FRPS 61: 276. 1992.

Shrubs or subshrubs evergreen, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets, inflorescence and abaxial surface of leaves densely grey to yellow tomentose or villose. Leaves opposite, petioles 4–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate, 7–18 × 1.5–4.5 cm, margin serrulate. Flowers 1–3 in cymes, rearranged in terminal and axillary panicles of 7–25 cm; pedicel 1 mm. Calyx campanulate or tubiform, 1.5–4 mm. Corolla white, sometimes greenish, tube cylindric, straight, 3–6 mm, sparsely pubescent abaxially; lobes very short. Stamens attached to upper part of corolla‑tube. Ovary glabrous; style short; stigma capitate. Capsules elliptic, 3–5 × 1.5–3 mm. Seeds grey‑brown, elliptic, 0.8–1 mm, shortly winged on both ends.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap, Barker Rd., Bowen Rd., Mount Davis Rd., Fei Ngo Shan, Kadoorie Farm, Cheung Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 972, 2014; Y. W. Lam 639.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shanxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Buddleja lindleyana Fortune 醉魚草（百寶花）
Edwards's Bot. Reg. 25. 1844; FHK 231. 1861; FKH 174. 1912; FRPS 61. 308. 1992.

Shrubs deciduous, up to 2 m tall. Branches 4‑angulate, slightly winged; branchlets, abaxial surface of young leaves and inflorescence brown stellate hairy. Leaves opposite, ovate, ovate‑lanceolate or elliptic, 5–10 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or sparsely sinuate‑toothed. Cymes rearranged in terminal racemes, slightly pendulous, 10–45 cm, tomentose; flowers turning to one side, densely glandular lepidote; pedicels ca. 1.5 mm. Calyx campanulate, 4 mm. Corolla purple; tube 1–1.5 cm, slightly curved; lobes broad‑ovate or suborbicular, 3.5 × 3 mm. Stamens attached to lower part of corolla‑tube. Ovary ovoid, 1.5–2.2 mm, glabrous. Capsules oblong or elliptic, 5–6 mm, lepidote. Seeds brownish, small, without wing.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap. HK sheet 3933.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental, poisonous.

Bulbophyllum affine Lindl. 赤唇石豆蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 48. 1830; FRPS 19: 173, pl. 25: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 763. 2000; FGD 7: 424, fig. 215. 2006; FOC 25: 410. 2009.

Rhizomes stout and thick, 4–5 mm in diam., with imbricate scale-like sheaths. Pseudobulb erect, subcylindrical, 3–4 cm long, 5–8 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves thickly coriaceous or fleshy, upright, oblong, 5–25 × 1–5 cm, apex obtuse and notched, midrib impressed above, elevated beneath. Flowers light yellow with purple veins, thick; odd sepal lanceolate, 1.5–2 × 0.4–0.5 cm, apex acute; lateral sepals falcate-lanceolate, same length with the odd one, apex acute, base oblique and slightly wider, adnate to the column foot forming a mentum; petals lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, apex acute, margin entire; lip fleshy, lanceolate, shorter than the petals, apex acuminate, slightly curved downward, grooved at base, lateral margins dark purple; column short and thick, 5 mm.

Locality: Lantau Island.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, India, Japan.
Ecology: Rocks along streams in forests. Flowering: May–Jul.

Bulbophyllum ambrosia (Hance) Schltr. 芳香石豆蘭（馥石蘭）
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. Beih. 4: 247. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 86. 1977; FRPS 19: 174, pl. 25: 7. 1999; FGD 7: 425. 2006; FOC 25: 407. 2009.
Eria ambrosia Hance, J. Bot. 21(8): 232. 1883.
Bulbophyllum watsonianum Rchb. f., Flora 71: 155. 1888; FKH 262. 1912.

Rhizomes 2–4 mm in diam., with imbricate scale-like sheaths. Pseudobulbs erect or slightly curved upward, cylindrical, 2–5 cm long, 3–6 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves leathery, oblong, 3.5–12 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate into a petiole 3–6 mm, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers light purplish yellow; odd sepal broad-ovate or oblong, 1 × 0.5 cm, apex acute, glabrous, margin entire; lateral sepals oblique ovate-triangular, same length with the odd one but slightly wider, the upper portion oblique and twisted to become beak-like, apex obtuse, base adnate to the column foot forming a mentum; petals triangular, 5–6 × 0.3 cm, margin entire; lip subovate, thicker at apex, winged in the middle, grooved at base, margin slightly wavy, strongly recurved; column short and thick.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lantau Island. K. K. Mark 5(2144) (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1763; HK sheet 7064.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 22156, BM) was collected by C. Ford from Victoria Peak in Mar. 1875.

Bulbophyllum kwangtungense Schltr. 廣東石豆蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. 19: 381. 1924; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1–2): 62. 1972; FRPS 19: 196, pl. 28: 7. 1999; FGD 7: 427, fig. 217. 2006; FOC 25: 414. 2009.
Bulbophyllum radiatum auct. non Lindl.: Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 13. 1903; FHK 353. 1861; FKH 262. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 86. 1977.

Rhizomes 2 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs erect, cylindrical, 1–2.5 cm long, 2–5 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves coriaceous, oblong, 2.5–3 × 0.5–1.5 cm, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers light yellow; sepals separate, lanceolate, 8–10 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acuminate, margin from the middle to apex curved inward; lateral sepals slightly longer than the odd one, adnate to the column foot at base, mentum not obvious; petals ovate-lanceolate, 4–5 × 0.5 mm, apex acuminate, margin entire; lip fleshy, lanceolate, curved outward, 1.5 × 0.5 mm, apex obtuse, grooved below the middle, with 2–3 small keels becoming a thick one from the middle to apex; column 0.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. K. K. Mark 1, 4 (CUHK); HK sheet 27295, 34409.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Rocks in forests and ravines. Flowering: May–Aug.

Bulbophyllum levinei Schltr. 齒瓣石豆蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. 19: 389. 1924; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1 – 2): 62. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 87, fig. 47. 1977; FRPS 19: 191, pl. 29: 7–9. 1999; FGD 7: 425. 2006; FOC 25: 417. 2009.

Rhizomes slender, prostrate; pseudobulbs aggregated at rhizomes, subcylindrical, 5–10 mm long, 2–4 mm in diam. Leaves thinly coriaceous, oblong or obovate-lanceolate, 3–4 × 0.5–0.7 cm, base attenuate into a petiole 4–10 mm, apex acute, margin slightly wavy, midrib usually impressed above. Flowers membraneous, purplish white; odd sepal ovate-lanceolate, notched, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm, upper portion narrower and thicker, apex acute, margin denticulate; lateral sepals oblique ovate-lanceolate, 5–6 mm, same width with the odd one, upper portion thicker, base adnate to the column forming a mentum, margin entire; petals ovate-lanceolate, 3.5 × 1.5 mm, margin denticulate, apex acute; lip fleshy, grooved below the middle, curved outside and downwards, apex acute, base truncate; column 1.2 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. N. H. Li 96 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 406.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Trunks along streams in forests. Flowering: May–Aug.

Bulbophyllum odoratissimum (Sm.) Lindl. 密花石豆蘭（香石豆蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 55. 1830; FKH 262. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1–2): 62. 1972; FRPS 19: 195, pl. 28: 8–9. 1999; FGD 7: 426, fig. 206. 2006; FOC 25: 414. 2009.
Stelis odoratissima Sm., Ress Cyclop. 34: 12. 1814.

Rizomes 2–4 mm in diam., branched; pseudobulbs subcylindrical, erect, 2.5–5 cm long, 3–6 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves coriaceous, oblong, 4–13.5 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse and notched. Flowers fragrant, white at the beginning and turning orange-yellow in the upper portion of both sepals and petals; sepals separate, lanceolate, apex obtuse or acute, margin curved inward, appearing like a narrow tube; odd sepal notched, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.5 mm, lateral sepals 4–14 × 2 mm; petals thinner than sepals, subovate or elliptic, 1–2 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse; lip orange-red, fleshy, tongue-shaped, slightly curved outward and downward, with 2 papillose keels, apex obtuse, adnate to the column foot at base, margin with tiny papillae or white hairs; column short and thick, 1 mm; column foot orangered, 1 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Nai Chung. S. Y. Hu 7321A (CUHK); HK sheet 27291, 32981.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang; Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Bare rocks or rocks in shade in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.

Bulbophyllum stenobulbon Parish & Rchb. f. 短足石豆蘭
Trans. Linn. Soc. 30: 153. 1874; FRPS 19: 194. 1999; FOC 25: 413. 2009.
Bulbophyllum youngsayeanum S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 29. 1976.

Rhizomes 1–1.5 mm in diam., branched, bearing a pseudobulb between 1.5–3 cm. Roots growing at the node bearing the pseudobulb. Pseudobulb erect, ovoid-cylindrical or cylindrical, 1–1.5 cm long, changeable in sizes, 3–6 mm across middle, bearing 1 leaf at the apex. Leaves leathery, oblong, 1.5–3.3 × 1 cm; base narrowed into petioles 2–3 mm; apex round-obtuse and emarginate; midrib depressed above. Scapes 1 or 2, emerged from base of pseudobulb, slender as hairs, longer than pseudobulb; racemes shortened into umbel-form, bearing 2–4 flowers; peduncle bearing 3–4 membranous-tubular sheaths; bracts 2–3 mm, ovate-lanceolate, emarginate, longer or shorter than the pedicel and ovary together, apex acute; sepals and petals pale yellow; sepals distinct, thin; the dorsal one lanceolate, 4.5–5 × 1.3–1.5 mm, ± uncurved above middle, acuminate at apex with 3 veins; petals thin, ovate, 2–2.4 × 0.8–1 mm across middle, apex obtuse, entire with 3 veins, only the middle one reaching the apex; lip orange, fleshy, tongue-like or ovate-lanceolate, flat, 2 × 0.5–0.7 mm, rounded or truncate at apex, slightly recurved, grooved at base, densely fine papillose on the back, often with 3 vertical ribs above, the sides thickened and swell up; column 1 mm, the apical teeth same height with anther, awl-like, 0.5 mm; foot very short, turning upward slightly, 1–1.3 mm, the free portion 0.3 mm; anther hemispherical, short in front.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 10136, 12052 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1749.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan; Sikkim, Bhutan, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Jun.
Notes: The holotype specimen of B. youngsayeanum (S. Y. Hu 12052, K) was collected from Tai Mo Shan in 1969.

Bulbostylis barbata (Rottb.) Kunth 球柱草
Enum. Pl. 2: 208. 1837; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 71. 1961; FHN 4: 285. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 193. 2000; FYN 15: 597. 2003; FGD 8: 293. 2007; FOC 23: 219. 2010.
Scirpus barbatus Rottb., Progr. 27. 1772.
Isolepis barbata (Rottb.) R. Br., Prodr., Fl. Nov. Holl. 222. 1810; FHK 393. 1861.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 5–30 cm tall, 0.2–0.4 mm thick, ± terete, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal; blade filiform, 4–10 cm × 0.2–0.5 mm, acute, glabrous to sparsely pilose above; sheath 0.5–2 cm, brownish. Involucral bracts 1–3, setaceous, the longest 0.3–2.5 cm. Inflorescence capitate, 5–15 mm wide. Spikelets 2–20, lanceolate to ovoid-conical, angular, 3–8 × 1–1.8 mm. Glumes 715 per spikelet, ovate, 1.5–2.3 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute, recurvedmucronate, sides membranous, yellowish green to rusty or chestnut brown, ciliolate to puberulent, margins hyaline, keel acute. Stamen 1(–2); anther oblong, 0.2–0.3 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes whitish, obovoid-orbicular, trigonous, 0.6–0.8 × 0.4–0.6 mm, ± smooth to finely papillose.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Lung, Wu Shek Kok, Tung Chung, Yi O. Y. W. Lam 799, 826; Y. S. Lau 2626.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW regions; pantropics.
Ecology: Open-dry sandy places, frequent on dunes and sandy ground near sea. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Bulbostylis densa (Wall.) Hand.-Mazz. 絲葉球柱草
Vegetationsbilder 20(7): 16. 1930; FRPS 11: 70. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 194. 2000; FYN 15: 597. 2003; FGD 8: 292. 2007; FOC 23: 218. 2010.
Scirpus densus Wall., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 231. 1820.
Bulbostylis cappillarus auct. non (L.) Kunth: FKH 300. 1912.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms tufted, filiform, 5–40 cm tall, 0.2–0.5 mm thick, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal; blade filiform, 2–10 cm × 0.4–0.5 mm, apex acute, glabrous to sparsely pilose; sheath pale brown. Involucral bracts setaceous to ± glume-like, the longest up to 0.7 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, sometimes condensed and appearing ± capitate; primary branches 1–5, 2–5 cm. Spikelets (1–)2–8, solitary or clustered, cylindrical-ovoid to ovoid, somewhat angular, 3–6 × 1.5 mm. Glumes 5–18 per spikelet, ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–2 × 1 mm, light chestnut brown, glabrous, apex subacute, sides membranous, margins hyaline, keel acute, pale brown. Stamens 2; anthers oblong, 0.2–0.3 mm long. Style ca. 1 mm, stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid-orbicular, trigonous, 0.7–0.9 × 0.5–0.8 mm, maturing greyish, indistinctly transversely wrinkled, minutely papillose.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2740; HK sheet 42189.
Distribution: Areas S of Huanghe; widespread in the Old World tropics.
Ecology: Open, wet, grassy places or on wet rock outcrops. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Bulbostylis puberula (Poir.) Kunth 毛鱗球柱草
Enum. Pl. 2: 213. 1837; FRPS 11: 70. 1961; FHN 4: 285. 1977; FGD 8: 293. 2007; FOC 23: 218. 2010.
Scirpus puberulus Poir. in Lamk., Enc. 6: 767. 1804.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 7–40 cm tall, 0.3–0.8 mm thick, scabrid, glabrous to puberulent. Leaves basal; blade filiform, 2–9 cm × 0.3–0.6 mm, glabrous to puberulent; sheath 0.8–3 cm long, pubescent, pale brown. Involucral bracts 2–4, leaf-like, the longest up to 4 cm. Inflorescence simple, often condensed and appearing ± capitate, 1–1.5 × 1.5 cm. Spikelets (1–)5–20, solitary, ovoid to cylindrical-ovoid, angular, 4–8 × 1.4–1.6 mm. Glumes 5–14 per spikelet, broadly ovate, 1.7–2.2 × 1.5–2 mm, densely pubescent, apex acute, recurved-mucronate, side membranous, pale greenish to light brown, margins hyaline, keel acute. Stamen 1; anther 0.5–0.7 mm long. Style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, triquetrous, 0.8–1 × 0.5–0.8 mm, whitish to pale yellowish, transversely wrinkled, obscurely reticulate with longitudinally oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 13499.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; widespread in tropical Africa and Asia.
Ecology: Sandy places near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Burmannia championii Thwaites 頭花水玉簪
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 325. 1864; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 666. 1890; Ridl., Mat. Fl. Mal. Penins. 2: 72. 1908; Ridl., Fl. Mal. Penins. 4: 306. 1924; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 138. 1938; Jonker, Fl. Males., ser. I, 4(1): 17–18. 1948; Ohwi, Fl. Jap., 336. 1953; FRPS 16(2): 173. 1981; FGD 2: 480. 1991; FOC 23: 123. 2010.
Burmannia dazielii Rendle, J. Bot. 40: 311. 1902.
Burmannia hunanensis K. M. Liu & C. L. Long, Ann. Bot. Fennici 38: 211. 2001.

Achlorophyllous, holomycotrophic herb, flowering at 3–22 cm. Stem white, slender. Basal rosette leaves absent. Cauline leaves ovate-triangular, 1.5–6 × 1–3 mm. Bracts ovate-triangular, 1.5–6 mm. Inflorescences with 3–13 flowers. Flowers pedicellate or sessile, white with yellow tepals, 5–11 mm long. Perianth tube 3–5 mm long; wings reduced to ribs or absent; outer tepals narrowly triangular, 1.5–3 mm long, with single margin; inner tepals spathulate, 0.8–1.4 mm long, with single margin. Stamens sessile or with short filament, basally adnate to perianth; connectives sometimes with 2 small apical crests but lacking a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal or obovoid, 2.5–3.5 mm long. Capsule subglobose. Seeds subglobose.

Locality: Mount Violet, Tai Mo Shan. R. Barretto & K. Barretto s.n.; S. C. Ng s.n. (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hunan, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Guinea, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Wet areas in forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Burmannia chinensis Gand. 香港水玉簪
Bull. Soc. Bot. Fr. 66: 290. 1919; D. X. Zhang & R. M. K. Saunders, Nord. J. Bot. 20: 391 – 392. 2000; FOC 23: 122. 2010.
Burmannia pusilla (Wall. ex Miers) Thwaites var. hongkongensis Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 131–132. 1938; FRPS 16(2): 171. 1981; FGD 2: 479. 1991; Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 128. 2004.

Chlorophyllous, semi-mycotrophic herb, flowering at 4.5–20 cm. Stems green, slender. Basal rosette leaves few, lanceolate, 0.3–1.2 cm × 1–3 mm. Cauline leaves linear, 5–18 × ca. 2 mm. Bracts lanceolate, 5–6 mm. Inflorescences with 1–3(–4) flowers. Flowers pedicellate or subsessile, purple or yellow, 3–8 mm long. Perianth tube 4–6.5 mm long; wings conspicuous, 1–3 mm wide; outer tepals broadly ovate, 1–3 mm long, with single or shallow double margin; inner tepals spathulate, 0.5–1.2 mm long, with single margin. Stamens sessile; connectives with 2 apical crests and sometimes a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal or obovoid, 2.5–7 mm long. Capsule obovoid. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam Reservoir, HKU Campus, Tai Tam Tuk, Ho Pui, Crescent Island. E. Bodinier 924 (HK, LY, P); E. Bodinier 924 bis (E, HK, P); HK sheet 7053.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang; India, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Generally wet grasslands. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.

Burmannia coelestis D. Don 三品一枝花（雛錫杖）
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 44. 1825; Schultes, Syst. Veg. 7(2): 75. 1830; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 665. 1888; Ridl., J. Str. Br. Roy. As. Soc. 22: 333. 1890; Ridl., Mat. Fl. Mal. Penins. 2: 71. 1908; Ridl., Fl. Mal. Penins. 4: 304. 1924; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 120. 1938; Jonker, Fl. Males., ser. I, 4(1): 17. 1948; FRPS 16(2): 171. 1981; FGD 2: 479. 1991; D. X. Zhang & R. M. K. Saunders, Nord. J. Bot. 20: 388–391. 2000; FOC 23: 122. 2010.

Chlorophyllous, semi-mycotrophic herb, flowering at 10–40 cm. Stems green, slender. Basal rosette leaves few, linear-lanceolate, 0.5–2 cm × ca. 3 mm. Cauline leaves linear, 5–30 × ca. 2.5 mm. Bracts lanceolate, 3–6 mm. Inflorescences with (1–)2–6(–8) flowers. Flowers pedicellate or subsessile, blue-purple with yellow tepals, 10–15 mm long. Perianth tube 4.5–13 mm long; wings conspicuous, 1.5–3 mm wide; outer tepals ovate-triangular, 1–2 mm long, with prominent double margin; inner tepals triangular, 0.5–1 mm long, with double margin. Stamens sessile; connectives with 2 apical crests and a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal or obovoid, 3–7 mm long. Capsule obovoid. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Sheung Shui. W. J. Tutcher 8152.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan; Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, New Guinea, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Generally wet grasslands. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.

Burmannia itoana Makino 纖草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 27: 1. 1913; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 153. 1938; Ohwi, Fl. Jap., 337. 1953; T. L. Wu & S. Chen, FRPS 16(2): 173. 1981; FGD 2: 480. 1991; FOC 23: 123. 2010.
Burmannia takeoi Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 212. 1915.
Burmannia pingbienensis H. Li, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 21(2): 127. 1983.

Achlorophyllous, holomycotrophic herb, flowering at 5–15 cm. Stem light blue, slender. Basal rosette leaves absent. Cauline leaves ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 × 1.5–2.5 mm. Bracts ovate-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm. Inflorescences with 1–3 flowers. Flowers pedicellate, blue-purple, 8–11 mm long. Perianth tube 3.5–5.5 mm long; wings conspicuous, 1–2 mm wide; outer tepals ovate-triangular, 1.5–2 mm long, with single margin; inner tepals orbiculate, very small, with single margin. Stamens sessile; connectives with 1 apical crest and a pendent basal spur. Ovary subglobose, 2–3.5 mm long. Capsule subglobose. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. G. Siu & K. Chu s.n. (HKU); R. T. Corlett s.n. (HKU); D. X. Zhang 98001 (HKU); Y. W. Lam 1787.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Japan.
Ecology: Wet, evergreen forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Burmannia wallichii (Miers) Hook. f. 亭立（華氏水玉簪）
Fl. Brit. India 5: 666. 1888; Ridl., Mat. Fl. Mal. Penins. 2: 71. 1908; Gagnep. in Lecomte & Humbert, Fl. Gén. Indo-Chine 6: 21. 1908; Ridl., Fl. Mal. Penins. 4: 305. 1924; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 145. 1938; FRPS 16(2): 173. 1981; FGD 2: 480. 1991; R. M. K. Saunders, Blumea 41: 336. 1996; FOC 23: 123. 2010.
Gonyanthes wallichii Miers, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 18: 537. 1841.

Achlorophyllous, holomycotrophic herb, flowering at 4–11.5 cm. Stem purple, slender. Basal rosette leaves absent. Cauline leaves triangular-subulate, 1.5–3.5 × 1–1.5 mm. Bracts triangular-lanceolate, 2–3.5 mm. Inflorescences with 1–3 flowers. Flowers sessile, blue-purple, 5–10 mm long. Perianth tube 2.5–5.5 mm long; wings narrow or reduced to ribs, 0.2–0.8 mm wide; outer tepals ovatetriangular, ca. 1 mm long, with single margin; inner tepals orbiculate, very small, with single margin.
