Stamens sessile; connectives lacking apical crests, sometimes with a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal to subglobose, 1.5–3 mm long. Capsule subglobose. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Tam Tuk, Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang. S. Y. Hu 5921 (A, US), 13913 (A); H.C. Tang 2513; Y. S. Lau 2057; D. X. Zhang 95001 (HKU).
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Yunnan; Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Peninsular Malaysia.
Ecology: Wet areas in dense forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Buxus bodinieri H. Lév. 雀舌黃楊
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 11(304 – 308): 549. 1913; M. Cheng, FRPS 45(1): 36, pl. 9: 15 – 21. 1980; FGD 3: 231. 1995.

Evergreen shrub, 2–4 m tall. Young shoots 4-angled, puberulous, subterete and glabrous in age. Leaves subleathery; petioles 1–2 mm; leaf blade spathulate, rarely obovate, 2 – 4 × 0.8 – 1.8 cm, base or narrowly cuneate, or sometimes acute, apex obtuse or rounded, usually emarginate, adaxial surface green and shining, sometimes puberulous on midvein, abaxial surface paler, ± glaucescent; midvein raised on both surfaces; lateral veins numerous, conspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, head-like, with 8–10 male flowers and 1 terminal female flower; rachis ca. 2.5 mm. Bracts ovate, glabrous or puberulous abaxially. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 0.4 mm; sepals 4, ovate-orbicular, ca. 2.5 mm, glabrous; stamens ca. 6 mm; rudimentary pistil as long as sepals or slightly longer. Female flower: sepals 2 –2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, ca. 2 mm in diam.; styles ca. 1.5 mm. Capsule ovoid, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Nam Chung, Shek Pan Tam, Luk Keng. P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 34758); Y. S. Lau 1823.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thickets by streams or in ravines. Flowering: Feb. –Mar.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Buxus harlandii Hance 匙葉黃楊
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 13: 123 – 124. 1873 (‘Harlandi’); FHN 2: 339. 1965; FRPS 45(1): 33, pl. 9: 9 – 14. 1980; FGD 3: 233. 1995.
Buxus sempervirens auct. non L.: FHK 315. 1861; FKH 233. 1912.

Evergreen shrub, ca. 1 m tall, much branched. Young shoots 4-angled, glabrescent; old branches subterete, glabrous. Leaves leathery, subsessile or with a very short petiole; leaf blade spathulate or sometimes narrowly oblong, 2–4 × 0.5–0.9 cm, apex rounded or obtuse, usually emarginate, gradually narrowed to the base, adaxial surface green and shining, sometimes puberulous on midvein; midvein raised on both surface, lateral veins conspicuous adaxially, obscure abaxially. Inflorescence head-like, axillary and terminal, with 8–10 male flowers and 1 terminal female flower; rachis 3–4 mm. Bracts ovate, acute. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 1 mm; sepals broadly ovate to broadly elliptic, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; stamens ca. 4 mm; rudimentary pistil ca. 1 mm, half as long as sepals. Female flower: sepals broadly ovate, ca. 2 mm; ovary ovoid, glabrous; styles dilated at the base, as long as ovary. Capsule subglobose, ca. 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Nam Chung, Wu Kau Tang. H. C. Tang 1499; W. J. Tutcher 11180; HK sheet 39398.
Distribution: Hainan and E Guangdong.
Ecology: Rocky banks of streams and in thin forests. Flowering: May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by A. W. Harland and H. F. Hance from Tai Tam Tuk, Hong Kong Island in 1858. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by A. W. Harland and H. F. Hance from Tai Tam Tuk, Hong Kong Island in 1858. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Buxus sinica (Rehder & E. H. Wilson) M. Cheng 黃楊
FRPS 45(1): 37. 1980; FGD 3: 234. 1995.
Buxus microphylla Siebold & Zucc. var. sinica Rehder & E. H. Wilson, Pl. Wils. 2: 165. 1914.

Evergreen shrub or rarely small trees. Young shoots puberulous; old branches subterete, greyish white. Leaves leathery to thick-leathery; petioles very short, usually puberulous; leaf blade broadly elliptic, broadly obovate, ovate-elliptic or oblong, 1.5–3.5 × 0.8–2 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex rounded or obtuse, usually emarginate, adaxial surface dark green and shining, with raised midvein and conspicuous lateral veins, abaxial surface paler, midvein plane, lateral veins obscure. Inflorescence axillary, head-like, with 8 – 10 male flowers and 1 terminal female flower; rachis 3 – 4 mm, puberulous. Bracts broadly ovate, 2 – 2.5 mm, ± puberulous. Male flowers sessile; sepals 4, outer 2 ovate-elliptic, inner 2 suborbicular, 2.5–3 mm, glabrous; stamens ca. 4 mm; rudimentary pistil 2/3 or sometimes 1/2 the length of sepals. Female flower: sepals ca. 3 mm; ovary slightly longer than styles. Capsule subglobose, 6–8(–10) mm in diam.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Po Toi Islands. Y. S. Lau 919, 1265, 2374.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thickets by streams and in ravines.
Uses: Ornamental.

Buxus sinica subsp. aemulans (Rehder & E. H. Wilson) M. Cheng 尖葉黃楊

FRPS 45(1): 40. 1980; FGD 3: 234. 1995.

Buxus microphylla var. aemulans Rehder & E. H. Wilson, Pl. Wils. 2: 169. 1914.


This subspecies is characterized by the leaves being elliptic-lanceolate to lanceolate 2 – 3.5 × 1 – 1.3 cm, shortly acuminate to both ends, and render it easily identifiable.


Locality: Ping Fung Shan, Wong Lung Hang, Lantau Peak. C. Ford s.n. (HK sheet 6357); L. T. Lo 566; Y. S. Lau 1737.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.

Ecology: Thickets by streams.

Uses: Ornamental.

Byttneria aspera Colebr. 刺果藤
Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 2: 283. 1824; FRPS 49(2): 186. 1984; FGD 1: 149. 1987.
Buettneria aspera Colebr. in Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 2: 283. 1824; FHK 39. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 86. 1965;.

Large woody climber, slightly tomentose on young parts. Petioles 2–8 cm, hairy; leaves broad-ovate, cordate or suborbicular, 7–23 × 5.5 –16 cm, base cordate, apex obtuse or acute, nearly glabrous adaxially, white stellate-pubescent abaxially, 5-veined. Panicles shorter than leaves. Flowers small, yellowish and slightly pink adaxially; sepals ovate, 2 mm, pubescent; petals shortly bifid at top, with linear appendage longer or equal to sepals; staminal tube short; anther alternate with staminodes. Capsules globose, 3 – 4 cm in diam., covered with short stout prickles, pubescent. Seeds black, oblong, ca. 12 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 503, 2218; H. C. Tang 2159.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Margin of forests or valleys. Flowering: Spring to summer.
Uses: Fibre, medicinal.

Caesalpinia bonduc (L.) Roxb. 刺蘇木
Fl. Ind. (ed. 2) 2: 362. 1832; FRPS 39: 98, pl. 32: 1 – 8. 1988; FGD 5: 172. 2003; FGX 2: 451, pl. 186: 11 – 19. 2005.
Guilandia bonduc L., Sp. Pl. 381. 1753.
Caesalpinia crista auct. non L.: FHN 2: 225, fig. 418. 1965.

Spiny vine, all parts yellow pubescent; spines straight or curved. Leaves 30– 45 cm; rachis with hooked spines; pinnae 6– 9 pairs, opposite; stalk of pinnae very short, with a spine at base; stipules large, leafy, usually lobed, deciduous; leaflets 6 –12 pairs, membranous, oblong, 1.5 – 4 × 1.2 – 2 cm, base oblique, apex obtuse and with an acumen, yellow pubescent on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, long pedunculate, densely flowered at upper part and sparsely flowered at lower part. Pedicels 3 – 5 mm; bracts subulate, 6 – 8 mm, hairy, reflexed, deciduous at anthesis. Hypanthium concave. Sepals 5, 8 mm, rusty hairy on both surfaces. Petals yellow, uppermost one with red dots, oblanceolate, clawed. Filaments short, woolly hairy at base. Ovary hairy. Pods leathery, oblong, 5 – 7 × 4 – 5 cm, apex beaked and swollen, finely long spiny abaxially. Seeds 2 – 3, subglobose, grey, glossy.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 748, 1101; S. P. Lau 182.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug. – Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Mar.

Caesalpinia crista L. 華南雲實（假老虎簕）
Sp. Pl. 380. 1753; FTW 3: 185. 1977; FRPS 39: 102. 1988; FGD 5: 172. 2003; FGX 2: 453. 2005.
Guilandina nuga L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 1: 546. 1762.
Caesalpinia kwangtungensis Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 8(1): 7. 1927.
Caesalpinia nuga (L.) W. T. Aiton, Hort. Kew. (ed. 2) 3: 32. 1811.

Woody vine, all parts rusty tomentose. Leaves bipinnate; rachis 25–35 cm, spiny, pubescent; pinnae 8–16 pairs, 5–8 cm; leaflets 6–10 pairs, opposite, leathery, ovate-lanceolate, ovate or elliptic, 12–25 × 6–12 mm, base rounded, apex acute, glabrous, deep green and glossy adaxially, glaucous and sparsely rusty hairy abaxially. Racemes 10–20 cm, forming loose and large panicles. Flowers fragrant. Pedicels slender, 5–15 mm. Sepals lanceolate, ca. 6 mm, glabrous. Petals 5, unequal, 4 petals yellow, ovate, glabrous, shortly clawed, uppermost one with red spots, hairy at middle adaxially. Stamens slightly exserted; filaments enlarged at base, hairy. Ovary hairy, ovules 2. Pods broadly ovate, leathery, 3– 4 × 2 – 3 cm, swollen, with reticulate veins, beaked at apex. Seed 1, flat.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 955, 2527; HK sheet 40140.
Distribution: SW China; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Dec.

Caesalpinia decapetala (Roth) Alston 雲實
Handb. Fl. Ceylon suppl. 6: 89. 1931; FRPS 39: 107, pl. 35: 1– 4. 1988; FGD 5: 174. 2003; FGX 2: 455, pl. 189: 4 – 8. 2005.
Reichardia decapetala Roth, Nov. Pl. Sp. 212. 1821.
Caesalpinia sepiaria Roxb., Fl. Ind. (ed. 2) 2: 360. 1832; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 351, fig. 2431. 1972.
Caesalpinia japonica Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(2): 117. 1845; FKH 89. 1912.

Spiny vine; bark dark red. Branches, leaf rachis and inflorescences pubescent, with hooked spines. Leaves bipinnate, 20–30 cm; pinnae 3–10 pairs, opposite, stipitate, with 1 pair of spines at base; leaflets 8 – 12 pairs, membranous, oblong, 12 – 25 × 6–12 mm, nearly obtuse at both ends, pubescent on both surfaces, later glabrescent. Stipules small, oblique ovate, apex acuminate, caducous. Racemes terminal, erect, 15 – 30 cm, hairy. Peduncles rather spiny. Pedicels 3 – 4 cm, hairy, articulate below calyx. Calyx-lobes oblong, pubescent. Petals 5, yellow, membranous, orbicular or obovate, 10–12 mm, revolute at anthesis, base shortly stipitate. Stamens nearly as long as petals; filaments flat at base, woolly hairy at lower part. Ovary glabrous. Pods oblong-tongue-shaped, 6 – 12 × 2.5–3 cm, rigid, leathery, chestnut-brown, glabrous and glossy, swollen along ventral suture and forming a narrow wing, dehiscing along ventral suture when mature, apex beaked. Seeds 6 – 9, brown, 11 × 6 mm.

Locality: Castle Peak. HK sheet 8462.
Distribution: Area S of Yellow River; subtropical and temperate regions of the old world.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Mar. Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Caesalpinia minax Hance 喙莢雲實（南蛇簕）
J. Bot. 22(12): 365. 1884; FKH 88. 1912; FRPS 39: 98, pl. 32: 9 – 17. 1988; FGD 5: 173. 2003; FGX 2: 451, pl. 186: 1 – 10. 2005.
Caesalpinia morsei Dunn, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 35(247): 492. 1903.

Spiny vine, all parts hairy. Stipules subulate and hard. Leaves bipinnate, to 45 cm; pinnae 5 – 8 pairs; leaflets 6 – 12 pairs, elliptic or oblong, 2–4 × 1.1 – 1.7 cm, base rounded, slightly oblique, apex rounded or acute, pubescent along midveins on both surfaces. Racemes or panicles terminal. Bracts ovate-lanceolate, apex shortly acuminate. Calyx-lobes ca. 13 mm, densely yellow tomentose. Petals white, with purple spots, obovate, ca. 18 × 12 mm, apex rounded, hairy abaxially and on margins. Stamens 10, slightly shorter than petals, filaments densely villous at lower part. Ovary densely covered with fine spines, styles slightly longer than stamens, glabrous. Pods densely covered with needle-like spines, oblong, 7.5–13 × 4 – 4.5 cm, apex obtuse and beaked. Seeds 4 – 8, elliptic, 18 × 10 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 639, 2983; HK sheet 23829.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets of valleys. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Caesalpinia pulcherrima (L.) Sw. 洋金鳳（金鳳花）
Observ. Bot. 166. 1791; FGZ 317, fig. 172. 1956; FHN 2: 225. 1965; FRPS 39: 107, pl. 35: 5 – 7. 1988; FGD 5: 171. 2003; FGX 2: 455, pl. 189: 1– 3. 2005.

Shrub or small tree; branchlets smooth, green or glaucous green, sparsely spiny. Leaves bipinnate, 12 – 26 cm; pinnae 4 – 8 pairs, opposite, 6–12 cm; leaflets 7– 11, oblong or obovate, 1– 2 cm × 0.4– 0.8 cm, base oblique, apex emarginate, sometimes with a mucro. Racemes terminal or axillary, 25 cm; pedicels 4.5– 7 cm. Hypanthium concave, turbinate, glabrous. Sepals glabrous, lowest one 14 mm, the rest ca. 10 mm. Petals orange-red or yellow, orbicular, 2 – 2.5 cm, margin wrinkled wavy, clawed. Filaments red, long exserted, 5 – 6 cm, base thick, hairy. Ovary glabrous; style long, orange-yellow. Pods narrow and thin, oblanceolate-oblong, 6 –10 × 1.5–2 cm, glabrous, not winged, apex long beaked, black when mature. Seeds 6– 9.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 225; Y. S. Lau 993, 2376.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan (cultivated); native to W Indies, widely cultivated in tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: All year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Caesalpinia sappan L. 蘇木
Sp. Pl. 381. 1753; FKH 89. 1912; FHN 2: 227. 1965; FRPS 39: 105, pl. 34: 8 – 11. 1988; FGD 5: 170, fig. 101. 2003; FGX 2: 455, pl. 188: 1 –4. 2005.

Small tree, to 6 m tall, sparsely armed, ± finely pubescent except old branches, adaxial surface of leaves and pods. Branches densely and conspicuously lenticellate. Leaves 30–45 cm; pinnae opposite, 7–13 pairs, 8–12 cm; leaflets 10–17 pairs, papery, sessile, long elliptic to oblong-rhomboid, 1–2 × 0.5–0.7 cm, base oblique, apex emarginate. Panicles terminal or axillary, nearly as long as leaves. Bracts large, lanceolate, caducous. Pedicels 1.5 cm, finely pubescent. Receptacle shallowly campanulate. Petals yellow, broadly obovate, ca. 9 mm, the uppermost one pinkish at base, stipitate. Stamens slightly exserted, filaments densely pubescent at lower part. Ovary greyish tomentose, stipitate; style slender, hairy; stigma truncate. Pods indehiscent, reddish brown, woody, slightly compressed, suboblong to oblong-obovate, 7 × 3.5–4 cm, base slightly narrowed, apex oblique truncate, beaked. Seeds 3–4, oblong, slightly compressed, pale brown.

Locality: Kowloon (fide FKH 89. 1912).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May– Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Mar.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), raw material (dye).

Caesalpinia vernalis Champ. 春雲實
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 77. 1852; FHK 97. 1861; FKH 88. 1912; FRPS 39: 103. 1988; FGD 5: 173. 2003.

Spiny vine, all parts rusty tomentose. Leaves bipinnate, rachis 25–35 cm, spiny and pubescent; pinnae 8–16 pairs, 5–8 cm; petiolules 1.5 –2 mm; leaflets 6 – 10 pairs, opposite, leathery, ovate-lanceolate, ovate or elliptic, 12 – 25 × 6– 12 mm, base rounded, apex acute, glabrous and green adaxially, glaucous and sparsely rusty tomentose abaxially. Panicles axillary or terminal, many-flowered. Pedicels 7– 9 mm. Calyx-lobes obovate-oblong, ciliate, lower one larger, 1 cm. Petals yellow, uppermost one smaller, revolute, with red spots. Stamens declined at apex; filaments pubescent at lower part. Ovary tomentose, ovules 2; styles thick, stigma oblique truncate. Pods oblique oblong, 4 –6 × 2.5 – 3.5 cm, woody, blackish purple, without reticulate veins, rugose, apex beaked. Seeds 2, axe-shaped, slightly concave at one end, glossy, 1.7 × 2 cm, hilum truncate at one end.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 388, 2226; Y. S. Lau 502.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests by streams. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Aberdeen by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Cajanus cajan (L.) Millsp. 木豆
Publ. Field Columbian Mus., Bot. Ser. 2(1): 53. 1900; FRPS 41: 301. 1995; FGD 5: 334, fig. 184. 2003.
Cytisus cajan L., Sp. Pl. 739. 1753.
Cajanus indicus Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 248. 1826; FHK 89. 1861; FKH 84. 1912.

Erect shrub, 1 – 3 m tall, much branched; branchlets angulate, covered with short silky hairs. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; petioles 1.5– 5 cm; leaflets elliptic to lanceolate, 5 – 10 × 1.5 – 2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, greyish pubescent especially on abaxial surface, glandular dots yellow, inconspicuous. Racemes 10 –20-flowered, 5 –15 cm, forming leafy panicles. Calyx campanulate, 7 mm, pubescent on the teeth. Corolla yellow or orange, brownish on back, varying into other color combinations; vexillum suborbicular, 1.3 cm, base clawed and auriculate; wings obovate, 15 mm, shortly auriculate; keel lunate, 12 × 5 mm. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary hairy. Pods linear-oblong, 4 – 7 × 0.6 – 1.1 cm, obliquely grooved between seeds. Seeds 3 – 6, subglobose, 6 – 7 mm, obscurely red, sometimes with brown spots.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2069; P. S. Choi 500; Y. W. Lam 194.
Distribution: SW to SE China (cultivated); native to India, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: All year around.
Uses: Food, green manure, forage.

Cajanus scarabaeoides (L.) Thouars 蔓草蟲豆
Dict. Sc. Nat. 6: 167. 1817; FGD 5: 335. 2003.
Dolichos scarabaeoides L., Sp. Pl. 720. 1753.
Atylosia scarabaeoides (Baill.) Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 242. 1852; FHK 90. 1861; FKH 85. 1912; FRPS 41: 306. 1995.

Herbaceous twiner. Stems slender, striate, brown-pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, terminal leaflets elliptic, obovate to oblong, 1.5 – 4 × 0.8– 2(–3) cm, apex obtuse or rounded, lateral ones smaller, pale brown-pubescent especially abaxially. Racemes axillary, 1 – 5-flowered. Calyx campanulate, 7 – 10 mm, with narrowly triangular teeth. Corolla yellow. Petals clawed and auriculate, deciduous after anthesis; vexillum dark purple, striate, obovate, 8 × 7 mm; wings oblong, 7 mm, slightly incurved; keel lunate, 7 mm. Stamens diadelphous; anthers uniform. Ovary silky villose. Pods oblong, 1.5 – 2.5 × 6 mm, densely and softly pubescent, grooved almost at right angles to sutures. Seeds 5 – 6, oblong, ca. 4 mm, dark brown.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ap Lei Chau, Stonecutters Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Lam Chung, Tuen Mun, Pak Nai, Sha Po. H. C. Tang 2070; L. T. Lo 36; P. S. Choi 67.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Asia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Open fields and thickets. Flowering: Jan.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Calamus ?egregius Burret 短葉省藤
Notizbl. Bot. Gart. Berlin-Dahlem 13: 599. 1937; FHN 4: 173. 1977; FGD 2: 469. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 105. 1991; FOC 23: 139. 2010.
Calamus latifolius auct. non Roxb.: FKH 286. 1912.

Climbing rattan. Stems clustered, to 30 m or longer. Leaves pinnate, pinnae 2–3-clustered in alternate groups, lanceolate, 10–23 × 2–3 cm, margins bristly; rachis 0.85–1.5 m long, with single recurved spines abaxially, apex of leaf rachis elongate to a whip-like cirri with clawed spines; sheath whitish green with flattened, 1–2 cm long spines and brown hairs, ocreas 1.5–5 cm, split, knees present, flagella absent. Inflorescences branched to 2 orders, 0.25–1 m long, not flagellate; prophylls tubular, 2-ridged laterally, with scattered, short spines, rachillae 2–4 cm long.

Locality: Happy Valley, S of Wan Chai Gap. W. J. Tutcher 4678, 8473; HK sheet 7683.
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Forests or thickets.
Usage: Materials (handcrafts).
Notes: According to Dunn and Tutcher (1912), Calamus latifolius is present in Hong Kong, but the voucher specimens (W. J. Tutcher 4678, 8473), rather poor and without fruits, are here temporarily determined as Calamus egregius, and further material is necessary before its status can be settled. The species was reported as Calamus palustris Griff. previously (Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004).

Calamus tetradactylus Hance 白藤
J. Bot. 13: 289. 1875; FKH 286. 1912; FHN 4: 174, fig. 1075. 1977; FGD 2: 471. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 87. 1991; FOC 23: 140. 2010.
Calamus bonianus Becc., Webbia 3: 231. 1910; FRPS 13(1): 87. 1991.
Calamus tetradactylus Hance var. bonianus (Becc.) Conrard, Fl. Gén. Indo-Chine 6: 1047. 1937.

Climbing rattan. Stems clustered, to 6 m or longer, slender, 6–15 cm in diam. Leaves pinnate, 45–55 cm; pinnae 2–4-clustered, 4–5 at apex, lanceolate, 10–26 × 2–5.5 cm; rachis with few single hook-like spines; cirrus absent; sheath green, glabrous, with few triangular spines or not; knees present; flagellum slender, to 1 m, with hook-like single spines; petioles short. Inflorescences borne from flagella, prophyll tubular, male inflorescences branched 2–3 orders, ca. 50 cm, the lower branches ca. 8 cm; rachillae 10–13 mm, with 4–6 flowers per side; male flowers small, ca. 3 mm; female inflorescences branched 2 orders, branches 3–4, 8–15 cm, the lower rachillae 2.5–5 cm, with 5–6 flowers per side; female flowers small, 3–4 mm. Fruits globose, 8–9 mm in diam., whitish yellow, scales in 21–23 vertical rows, with a groove in the middle, persistent sepals and petals stalk-like. Seeds 1, 6 mm in diam., endosperm homogeneous or slightly ruminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1748, 2654; HK sheet 39265.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Materials (furniture, handcrafts).
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18979, BM) was collected by G. Dods from Wong Nai Chung around 1870s.

Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18979, BM) was collected by G. Dods from Wong Nai Chung around 1870s.

Calamus thysanolepis Hance 毛鱗省藤
J. Bot. 12: 265. 1874; FKH 286. 1912; FGD 2: 474. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 68. 1991; FOC 23: 137. 2010.
Calamus hoplites Dunn, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 38: 369. 1908; FRPS 13(1): 69. 1991.
Calamus thysanolepis Hance var. polylepis Wei, Guihaia 6: 24. 1986; FRPS 13(1): 69. 1991.

Erect shrubs. Stems clustered, to 5 m tall. Leaves pinnate, to 1.6 m, pinnae 2–6 in groups, point at different directions, not in the same plane, linear or elongate lanceolate, middle pinnae 30–38 × 1.5–2 cm, adaxial veins and margins bristly, abaxial rachis with short, single, hook-like spine; sheath open, without knee and flagellum, greenish brown; spines black and dense, to 2 cm; ocreas to 30 cm; petioles sparsely armed with straight, black-tipped spines. Inflorescences to 1 m, erect; male inflorescence branched 2–3 orders, female one branched 2 order; prophyll split to fibre-like, sometimes longer than the branch; male rachilla 3–4 cm, bearing 12–15 flowers each side; female rachilla 7.5 cm. Fruits ovoid, 15 × 10 mm, scales in 18–21 vertical rows, reddish brown, without groove in the middle, with cilia on the margins; persistent sepals and petals stalk-like. Seed 1, ellipsoidal, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 408, 451; K. L. Yip 4213.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun. – Jul.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Materials.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18373, BM) was collected by G. Dods from Tai Tam Tuk in Nov. 1873.

Calamus walkeri Hance 多果省藤
J. Bot. 12: 266. 1874; FKH 286. 1912; FGD 2: 470. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 75. 1991; FOC 23: 141. 2010.
Calamus faberi Becc., Ann. Roy. Bot. Gard. Calc. 11(1): 274, t. 99. 1908; FHN 4: 175. 1977; FGD 2: 470. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 75. 1991 [“faberii”]; Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004.
Calamus faberi Becc. var. brevispicatus (Wei) S. J. Pei & S. Y. Chen, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 27: 133. 1989; FRPS 13(1): 76. 1991.
Calamus tonkinensis Becc., Ann. Roy. Bot. Gard. Calc. 11(1): 275. 1908.
Calamus tonkinensis Becc. var. brevispicatus Wei, Guihaia 9: 31. 1986.

Climbing rattan. Stems clustered, to 30 m or longer, about 3 cm in diam. Leaves pinnate, 1–3 m; pinnae arranged regularly on the same plane, linear-lanceolate, 30–45 × 1.5–2.5 cm, bristly on midveins and margins; rachis with single, black-tipped, claw-like spines; cirri absent; sheath green hairy and spiny; spines flattened to 2.5 cm; ocreas dense bristly; flagellum whip-like, to 5 m, with strong, claw-like spines. Inflorescences borne from flagella; female inflorescences branched 2 orders, branches 12–20 cm, with 10–20 rachillae on each side; prophyll tubular, flattened, with short sparse spines; lower rachillae 5–7 cm, with 12–16 flowers on each side; flowers small, ca. 3 mm. Fruits oblong-ovoid, 1–1.2 × 1 cm, yellowish brown when mature, scales in 15–18 vertical rows, with brown narrow margin; endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Happy Valley, Mount Parker. Y. W. Lam 578; HK sheet 7709, 29556.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.; fruiting: Sep.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Materials (furniture, handcrafts).
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18225, BM) was collected by A. L. Walker from Hong Kong Island in Aug. 1873.

Calanthe graciliflora Hayata 鈎距蝦脊蘭
J. Coll. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 30: 329. 1911, et Icon. Pl. Formos. 4: 68, t. 31. 1914; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 202. 1972; FRPS 18: 316. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 786. 2000; FGD 7: 418. 2006; FOC 25: 307. 2009.
Calanthe striata auct. non (Sw.) R. Br.: S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, rhizomes inconspicuous; pseudobulbs short, subovoid, covered by cataphylls and leaf sheaths. Leaves basal, elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 15–23(–33) × 6–8 cm, conspicuously plicate, base gradually attenuating into sheathing petioles, apex acuminate, glabrous at two sides. Flowers resupinate, fragrant, pale lemon-yellow, deeper towards the margin, with sepals and petals washed brownish outside; sepal similar in shape and colour, equally spaced, elliptic, 10–15 ×, 5–6 mm, apex acute; petals obovate or obovatelanceolate, 10–13 × 3–4 mm, apex acute; lip 3-lobed, white with purplish marks on lateral and midlobes; lateral lobes obovate-triangular, 3–4 mm; midlobe obovate, straight, truncate and apiculate at the middle, column 4 mm, glabrous, rounded at the apex, broadly winged on each side; anther white, ovate; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 11552A (CUHK); HK sheet 32508, 34043.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.

Calanthe speciosa (Blume) Lindl. 二列葉蝦脊蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. 250. 1833; Su, Quart. J. Expt. Forest. Natl. Taiwan Univ. 4(3): 87, pl. 3. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 789. 2000; FOC 25: 296. 2009.
Amblyglottis speciosa Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 371. 1925.
Calanthe formosana Rolfe, Ann. Bot. 9: 157. 1895; FRPS 18: 278, pl. 48: 5. 1999; FGD 7: 415. 2006; Check List HK Plants 372. 2002; 129. 2004.
Calanthe curculigoides auct. non Lindl.: FKH 264. 1912.
Calanthe patsinensis S. Y. Hu, Chung Chi Journal 11: 13, fig. 1. 1972, et Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 202. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, up to 120 cm tall, completely glabrous; pseudobulbs cylindrical, sheathing. Leaves distichous, oblong-elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 20–60(–95) × 4–6 cm, base attenuating into a long petiole, apex acuminate; petiole stout, 6–10(–20) cm, base enlarging into sheaths. Flowers yellow or yellow-orange, in a terminal raceme; sepals subequal, elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 10–15 × 4–5 mm, apex acuminate; petals ovate-elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 10–13 × 5–6 mm, apex acute; lip adnate to the sides of the column, 3-lobed; lateral lobes ovate-triangular, 5 mm apart from each other; apical lobe fan-shaped, 5 × 5 mm, truncate, apiculate at the apex, gradually narrowed towards the base; column 3–5 mm, winged at the apex; anther elongate-conical; pollinia 8, strongly attenuate; ovary subcylindrical, subtrigonous, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok. K. K. Mark 2 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 570; Y. W. Lam 179.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of C. patsinensis (S. Y. Hu 10013, A, holotype) was collected from Pat Sin Leng in 1970.

Calanthe sylvatica (Thouars) Lindl. 長距蝦脊蘭（粉紅蝦脊蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 250. 1833; FRPS 18: 301. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 789. 2000; FGD 7: 416. 2006; FOC 25: 300. 2009.
Centrosis sylvatica Thouars, Hist. Orchid. pl. 35 & 36. 1822.
Bletia masuca D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal 30. 1825.
Calanthe masuca (D. Don) Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 249. 1833; FKH 265. 1912.
Calanthe masuca Lindl. var. sinensis Rendle, J. Bot. Brit. For. 40: 310. 1902; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93, fig. 52. 1977.

Terrestrial herb up to 80 cm, rhizomes inconspicuous; pseudobulbs narrow conical, 1–2 cm long, 1 cm across at base. Leaves all basal, elliptic to ovate, 15–40 × 7–11 cm, base attenuate into petioles, apex acute or acuminate, margin wavy. Flowers rather large, sepals all alike in colour, delightfully bright lavender, darker on the outside; odd sepal elliptic, 18–20 × 6–10 mm, apex acute; lateral sepals oblique-elliptic or oblong, apex acute; petals obovate or oblong, lavender shading to white inside along the centre, 1.5–2.5 × 1–1.3 cm, apex obtuse or acute; lip adnate to the sides of the column, 3-lobed; lateral lobes deep purple, oblique, falcate-lanceolate, 3–5 × 1.5–2 mm; midlobe light purple, fan-shaped, 1–1.5 × 1.5–1.8 cm, the apex bilobed with an acute recurved point between the lobes; column white, waxy; anther white, ovate; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, all white; ovary hairy, with pink ridges and green depressions.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12676 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1639; HK sheet 34679.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Taiwan; Nepal, India, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Japan.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forest. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Calanthe triplicata (Willemet) Ames 三褶蝦脊蘭（白花蝦脊蘭）
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 2(4): 326. 1907; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 207. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93. 1977; FRPS 18: 308, pl. 53: 3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 791. 2000; FGD 7: 417. 2006; FOC 25: 302. 2009.
Orchis triplicata Willemet, Usteri Ann. Bot. 18: 52. 1796.
Calanthe veratrifolia R. Br., Bot. Reg. 9: ad t. 720. 1823; FKH 265. 1912.

Perennial herb, bearing no leaf at anthesis; stems short, fleshy, consisting of 1–3 green fleshy stems; stems with 2 or 3 oblong joints, each joint 1.3–4 cm long, 1.2–3.5 cm in diam., slightly compressed, partially covered by remnants of sheaths. Leaves emerging after anthesis. Flowers white, 2–few, in a terminal raceme; stipe 35–40 cm, bracts 3 or 4, greenish, the upper ones 1.5 cm; pedicels 2–3 cm, hairy; flowers 4 cm across; dorsal sepal ovate-lanceolate, 25 × 6 mm, acute, lateral sepals similar in size and shape, turning upwards against the dorsal one; petals elliptic-oblong, 2.5 cm, apex obtuse; lip conspicuous, the lateral lobes connate to the column forming a funnel; the front lobe turning 90° upward, enlarged into a trilobed suborbicular epichile, biparted at apex.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Sha Tin, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 10701, 13822 (CUHK); HK sheet 7097, 27424.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia, Madagascar.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Calathea ornata (Lindl.) Körn. 肖竹芋
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 35(1): 127. 1862; FRPS 16(2): 165. 1981.

Strong virgorous plant, 30 – 90 cm tall. Leaves oblonglanceolate, 30–90 cm, young leaves often marked with pink and white lines along lateral veins; adult foliage rich green adaxially and dull purple-red abaxially, ± cordate at base, apex acute; petiole becoming 60 cm or more long with age. Spike ovoid, ca. 8 cm; peduncles to 35 cm; petals violet; staminode yellowish.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Taiwan (cultivated); native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Calathea zebrina (Sims) Lindl. 絨葉肖竹芋（斑葉肖竹芋）
Bot. Reg. sub pl. 1210. 1829; FRPS 16(2): 165. 1981; FGD 2: 439. 1991.
Maranta zebrina Sims, Curt's Bot. Mag. t. 1926. 1817.

Plant 50–100 cm tall. Leaves cauline; petioles to 45 cm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 30–60 cm long and nearly or quite half as broad, base unequilateral, apex obtuse or very short-acute, velvety green and with alternating bars of pale yellow-green and olive-green extending outward from midrib adaxially, purplish-red abaxially in adult. Head solitary on scape, nearly globular or ovoid; bracts imbricate, dilate-ovate, ca. 5 cm wide, purple inside; sepals oblong, to 2.5 cm; corolla blue-purple or white, lobes oblonglanceolate, 1.5 cm; staminode pale lilac, 1.7 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3219, 3288; HK sheet 28072.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan (cultivated); native to Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Calendula officinalis L. 金盞花
Sp. Pl. 921. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1 – 2): 10. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 327. 1999; FGD 8: 232, fig. 142. 2007.

Annual herbs 20–70 cm tall; stem branched, covered with glandular pubescent hair. Basal leaves spatulate to oblanceolate, 4.5–16.5 × 1–4 cm, apex obtuse‑rounded, margin entire. Middle cauline leaves oblanceolate‑oblong, sessile and amplexicaul, 4–10 × 1–3.5 cm, apex obtuse, margin undulate, loosely and minutely toothed, both surfaces puberulous to pubescent, hair denser along margin and midvein. Upper leaves smaller in size, lanceolate‑oblong. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, solitary to stem and branch terminals, 4–8 cm across. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, 2‑seriate, lanceolate‑oblong, outer layer slightly longer than the inner ones, 10–13 × 1.5–2 mm, apex long acuminate‑caudate, abaxially hirsute, hair multicellular. Marginal ligulate florets in 2–3 series, colour yellow or orange‑yellow, ligule linear oblong, 1.5 – 3 × 0.4–0.8 cm, tube short and hairy, female and fertile. Disk tubular florets about 5 mm, apex with 5 lanceolate lobes, functionally staminate and infertile. Cypselae pale yellow or pale brown, incurved, abaxial side densely tuberculate and wrinkled, glandular hairy, adaxial side longitudinally striate. Pappus absent.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 15995; S. Y. Hu 9311A (CUHK); H. Y. Yeung 182 (CUHK).
Distribution: S Europe and N Africa, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Calliandra haematocephala Hassk. 朱纓花（紅絨球）
Retzia 1: 216. 1855; FRPS 39: 38. 1988; FGD 5: 142, fig. 83. 2003.

Deciduous shrub, 1–3 m tall. Branchlet terete, brown, rough. Stipules ovate-lanceolate, persistent. Leaves bipinnate; petioles 1 – 2.5 cm; pinnae one pair, 8 – 13 cm; leaflets 7 – 9 pairs, oblique-lanceolate, 2–4 cm × 7–15 mm, base oblique, apex obtuse, mucronate, margin sparsely pilose, midvein close to upper; petiolules 1 mm. Heads axillary, 3 cm in diam. (including filaments); peduncle 1–3.5 cm. Calyx campanulate, 2 mm. Corolla tube 3.5–5 mm, purplish, 5-lobed; lobes reflexed, 3 mm, glabrous. Stamens numerous, exserted, very brilliant, filament-tube 6 cm, white, with a subulate appendix inside the mouth, free part of filament 2 cm, deep red. Pods linear-oblanceolate, 6–11 × 0.5–1.3 cm, dull brown, valves elastically open from apex to base along sutures when ripen, reflexed. Seeds 5–6, oblong, 7–10 × 4 mm, brown.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 270; Y. S. Lau 1080, 1733.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to S America.
Ecology: Cultivated in gardens. Flowering: Aug. – Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Another species, Calliandra riparia Pittier (C. surinamensis auct. non Benth.: Check List HK Plants 31. 1993), native to S America, was once cultivated in Hong Kong but became uncommon in recent times.

Notes: Another species, Calliandra riparia Pittier (C. surinamensis auct. non Benth.: Check List HK Plants 31. 1993), native to S America, was once cultivated in Hong Kong but became uncommon in recent times.

Callicarpa brevipes (Benth.) Hance 短柄紫珠（短序紫珠）
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., ser. 5, 5(5): 233. 1886; FKH 203. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 69. 1982; FFJ 4: 533. 1989; FOC 17: 14. 1994; FGD 3: 359. 1995.
Callicarpa longifolia Lam. var. brevipes Benth., FHK 270. 1861.
Callicarpa longifolia auct. non Lam.: FKH 202. 1912, p.p.

Shrub 1–2.5 m tall. Branchlets obscurely tetragonal, yellow‑brown stellate pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole ca. 5 mm; leaf blade papery, narrowly lanceolate to lanceolate, 9–24 × 1.5–4 cm, base obtuse, rarely cuneate or slightly cordate, apex acuminate, margin subentire to sparsely serrulate along apical part, adaxially glabrous, abaxially stellate pubescent on veins and yellow glandular; lateral veins 9–12 pairs. Cymes ca. 1.5 cm across. Peduncle slender, subequal to slightly longer than petioles. Calyx cup‑shaped, yellow glandular, subglabrous, subtruncate to minutely 4‑dentate. Corolla white, ca. 3.5 mm, glabrous. Filaments nearly as long as corolla; anthers ellipsoidal, densely yellow glandular, dehiscing by apical pores. Ovary glabrous, glandular. Style slightly longer than stamens. Fruit subglobose, red to purple, 3–4 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3134; HK sheet 39931, 40464.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Hunan, S Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The syntypes (Champion s.n., Wright s.n. and Wilford s.n.) were collected from Hong Kong in 1850. The species was reported as Callicarpa longifolia Lam. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

Callicarpa cathayana H. T. Chang 華紫珠
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 1(3 – 4): 305. 1951; FYN 1: 412, pl. 98: 16 – 18. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 65, fig. 30. 1982; FFJ 4: 533. 1989; FOC 17: 13. 1994; FGD 3: 357. 1995.

Shrub, 1.5–3 m tall. Branchlets slender, slightly stellate tomentose when young, glabrescent. Petiole less than 1 mm; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic‑ovate or ovate, 4–8 × 1.5–3 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, subglabrous and red glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces. Cymes slender, 1–1.5 cm across, sparsely stellate tomentose. Peduncle and pedicels slenlder, ± stellate hairy and red glandular. Bracts small. Calyx cupular, truncate to minutely 4‑dentate, teeth obtusely triangular, stellate tomentose, red glandular. Corolla purple, sparsely stellate tomentose and red glandular abaxially. Filaments equal or slightly longer than corolla. Ovary glabrous. Style slightly longer than stamens. Fruit globose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po, Fanling, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 732; L. T. Lo 126; HK sheet 40823.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Mixed forests on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Callicarpa dichotoma (Lour.) K. Koch 白棠子樹
Dendrologie 2: 336. 1872; FGZ 631. 1956; FRPS 65(1): 54, fig. 23. 1982; FFJ 4: 531, fig. 421. 1989; FOC 17: 11. 1994; FGD 3: 355. 1995.
Porphyra dichotoma Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 70. 1790.
Callicarpa purpurea auct. non Juss.: FKH 202. 1912.

Shrub 1–1.5(–3) m tall, multibranched. Branchlets slender, with stellate hairs when young. Leaves sessile or subsessile; leaf blade papery, lanceolate to obovate, 2–6(–10) × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, apex usually very short acuminate with an obtuse tip, margin coarsely dentate along apical part, adaxially glabrous and subscabrous, abaxially densely yellow‑glandular and with glandular stellate hairs; veins 4–6 pairs. Cymes 1–2.5 cm across. Peduncle and pedicels slender, stellate hairy at first, glabrescent in fruit. Bracts linear. Calyx cupular, less than 1 mm, subtruncate or obscurely dentate, glabrous, ± glandular abaxially. Corolla purple, tube twice as long as calyx tube, glabrous. Stamens exserted; filaments twice as long as corolla tube, glabrous. Ovary glabrous, sparsely yellow glandular. Fruit subglobose, 1–2 mm in diam., ± glandular.

Locality: New Territories. W. J. Tutcher 8141.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Henan, Hebei; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Callicarpa formosana Rolfe 杜虹花
J. Bot. 20(240): 358. 1882; FKH 203. 1912; FHN 4: 11. 1977; FYN 1: 406, pl. 97: 5 – 7. 1977; FTW 4: 413. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 43. 1982; FFJ 4: 529, fig. 419. 1989; FOC 17: 8. 1994; FGD 3: 353. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 406, pl. 176. 1998.
Callicarpa aspera Hand.‑Mazz., Sitzungsber. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.‑Naturwiss. Cl., Abt. 1 59: 110. 1877.
Callicarpa integerrima Champ. var. serrulata H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25(4): 425. 1944.
Callicarpa ningpoensis Mats., Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 27: 273. 1913.
Callicarpa rubella Lindl. f. robusta C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 39. 1932.

Shrub 1–3 m tall. Branchlets, petioles, cymes and calyx densely greyish yellow stellate tomentose. Petiole robust, 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade thin leathery, elliptic to ovate‑elliptic, 6–15 × 3–8 cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex acuminate or nearly acute, margin serrate, adaxially slightly rough, minutely hispid, abaxially greyish yellow stellate tomentose and yellow glandular; lateral veins 8–12 pairs. Cymes dense, subglobose, 3–4 cm across. Peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm. Bracts small. Calyx cupular, greyish yellow stellate tomentose; teeth 4, triangular. Corolla purple to purplish, ca. 2.5 mm, glabrous, lobes ca. 1 mm, apex rounded. Stamens ca. 5 mm, 2 times as long as corolla or slightly longer. Ovary glabrous. Fruit subglobose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 605, 1319; Y. W. Lam 1617.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Callicarpa pedunculata R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

Callicarpa integerrima Champ. 全緣葉紫珠
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 135. 1853; FHK 270. 1861; FKH 202. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 34, fig. 9. 1982; FFJ 4: 525. 1989; FOC 17: 6. 1994; FGD 3: 350. 1995.
Callicarpa integrifolia Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 253. 1890.

Scandent shrub. Branchlets terete, brown; young branchlets, petioles, and inflorescences densely yellowish brown tomentose, hairs branched to densely dendritic. Petiole ca. 2 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, ovate or elliptic, 7–17 × 4–9 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire, adaxially yellow‑brown stellate tomentose, abaxially densely greyish yellow tomentose; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Cymes large, 6–11 cm across. Peduncle 2–5 cm. Pedicel and calyx densely stellate tomentose. Calyx‑limb subtruncate. Corolla purple, ca. 2–2.5 mm, glabrous. Stamens 2 times as long as corolla; anthers longitudinally dehiscing. Ovary stellate tomentose. Fruit subglobose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam., stellate tomentose when young, glabrescent.

Locality: Bowen Rd., Cheung Sheung, Luk Keng, Nam Chung, Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 2210; Y. S. Lau 2072; HK sheet 4319.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Callicarpa kochiana Makino 枇杷葉紫珠
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 28(331): 181–182. 1914; FRPS 65(1): 30. 1982; FFJ 4: 524, fig. 415. 1989; FOC 17: 6. 1994; FGD 3: 349, fig. 229. 1995.
Callicarpa longiloba Merr., Philipp. J. Sc. 13(3): 156. 1918.
Callicarpa loureiri Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 205. 1837; FGZ 629. 1956.
Callicarpa tomentosa auct. non Willd.: FHK 269. 1861.

Shrub 1–4 m tall. Branchlets, petioles, and inflorescences densely yellowish brown branched stellate tomentose. Petiole 1–3 cm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, elliptic, or ovate‑elliptic, 12–22 × 4–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrate, adaxially glabrous or slightly pilose especially on veins, abaxially densely yellowish brown stellate tomentose, obscurely yellow glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 10–18 pairs, prominent abaxially. Cymes 3–6 cm across. Peduncle 1–2 cm. Flowers subsessile. Calyx tubular, 2–2.5 mm, tube tomentose, teeth acute. Corolla pink to purple, lobes densely tomentose. Stamens exserted; filaments ca. 3.5 mm; anthers ovoid, ca. 1 mm. Style longer than stamens. Stigmas enlarged. Fruit globose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., nearly completely enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 575, 1038; L. T. Lo 142.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Henan, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest edges, forests in valleys. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Callicarpa longibracteata H. T. Chang 長苞紫珠
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 1(3 – 4): 277. 1951; FRPS 65(1): 37, fig. 11. 1982; FOC 17: 7. 1994; FGD 3: 350. 1995.

Shrub to 3 m tall. Young branches yellow stellate tomentose. Petiole ca. 2 cm, yellow stellate tomentose; leaf blade oblong‑elliptic to elliptic‑lanceolate, 15–20 × 5–8 cm, base obtuse to rounded and oblique, margin entire or serrulate above to middle, adaxially glabrous but stellate tomentose along midvein when young, abaxially densely yellow‑grey stellate tomentose; lateral veins 14 pairs, prominent abaxially. Cymes 6–9 cm across. Peduncle 3–5 cm. Bracts lanceolate, 3–4 × 1 cm. Calyx campanulate, stellate tomentose; teeth linear, ca. 1 mm. Corolla pink, ca. 2 mm, puberulent. Filaments ca. 5 mm; anthers ca. 0.6 mm, longitudinally dehiscing. Ovary glabrous. Style 6–7 mm. Fruit globose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Luk Keng, Lantau Island. S. C. Ng 2858; Y. W. Lam 1705.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.
Notes: The type specimen (W. Y. Chun 5121, IBSC) was collected from mixed forests of altitude 100 – 300 m in Hong Kong in Aug. 1926.

Callicarpa longissima (Hemsl.) Merr 尖尾楓
Philipp. J. Sci. 12(2): 108. 1917; FGZ 631. 1956; FTW 4: 416. 1978, excl. syn. C. taiwaniana; FRPS 65(1): 52. 1982; FFJ 4: 531. 1989; FOC 17: 10. 1994; FGD 3: 354. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 411. 1998.
Callicarpa longifolia Lam. var. longissima Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 253. 1890.
Callicarpa longifolia auct. non Lam.: FKH 202. 1912, p.p.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3.5(–7) m tall. Branchlets purplish brown, tetragonal, with a ring of hair at node, stellate hairy when young. Petiole 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade papery, lanceolate to oblong‑lanceolate, 13–25 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin subentire to obscurely serrulate, adaxially subglabrous except long villous pubescence mainly along veins, abaxially glabrous, yellow glandular when fresh; veins 12–20 pairs, elevated on both surfaces. Cymes hairy, 3–6 cm across. Peduncle 1.5–3 cm. Calyx subtruncate to obscurely dentate, glabrous, glandular, limb inconspicuously 4‑dentate or truncate. Corolla pale purple, ca. 2.5 mm, glabrous. Stamens ca. twice as long as corolla tube. Ovary glabrous. Fruit oblique globose, 1–1.5 mm in diam., glabrous, glandular.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Nam Hang, Fung Yuen, Ha Hang, Luk Keng, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2275, Y. S. Lau 1314, 2960.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes and open fields. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: It was reported as Callicarpa longifolia var. lanceolaria (Roxb.) C. B. Clarke previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

Callicarpa macrophylla Vahl 大葉紫珠
Symb. Bot. 3: 13, pl. 53. 1794; FHK 270. 1861; FKH 202. 1912; FGZ 630, fig. 336. 1956; FYN 1: 403, pl. 96: 9–12. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 38. 1982; FOC 17: 7. 1994; FGD 3: 351. 1995.
Callicarpa dunniana H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222 – 226): 456. 1911.
Callicarpa macrophylla var. kouytchensis H. Lév., Fl. Kouy‑Tchéou 440. 1915.

Shrub or small tree, 3–5 m. Branchlets nearly tetragonal, densely greyish mealy branched tomentose. Petiole robust, 1–3 cm, densely grey unevenly stellate tomentose; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, narrowly elliptic, or ovate‑elliptic, 10–23 × 5–11 cm, base cuneate to broadly obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin serrulate, adaxially pubescent especially on veins, abaxially densely unevenly grey stellate tomentose and glandular; lateral veins 8–11 pairs; veinlets slightly impressed adaxially. Cymes 4–8 cm across, densely unevenly grey stellate tomentose. Peduncle robust, 2–3 cm. Bracts linear. Calyx cupular, ca. 1 mm, subtruncate, grey stellate tomentose, yellow glandular. Corolla purple, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely stellate tomentose; filaments ca. 5 mm; anthers yellow glandular. Ovary puberulent. Fruit globose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., puberulent, glandular.

Locality: Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Kau Yi Chau, Tai A Chau. S. P. Lau 151; HK sheet 34818, 34907.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Callicarpa nudiflora Hook. & Arn. 裸花紫珠
Bot. Beechey Voy. 206, pl. 46. 1837; FGZ 630. 1956; FRPS 65(1): 37. 1982; FFJ 4: 526. 1989; FOC 17: 7. 1994; FGD 3: 351. 1995.
Callicarpa acuminata Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 408. 1820, nom. illeg.
Callicarpa acuminata var. angustifolia F. P. Metcalf, Lingnan Sci. J. 11(3): 407. 1932.
Callicarpa macrophylla Vahl var. sinensis C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 4(12): 568. 1885.
Callicarpa reevesii Wall. ex Schauer, Prodr. 11: 641. 1847; FHK 270. 1861; FKH 202. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, 3–4(–7) m. Old branches glabrous, evidently lenticellate. Young branchlets, petioles, abaxial leaf surfaces, and inflorescences unevenly greyish brown stellate tomentose. Petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic to lanceolate, 12–22 × 4–7 cm, base obtuse to subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate, slightly undulate, or subentire, adaxially dark green and subglabrous except for stellate tomentose veins, abaxially densely greyish brown unevenly stellate tomentose; lateral veins 14–18 pairs. Cymes 8–13 cm across. Peduncle 3– 8 cm. Bracts linear‑lanceolate. Pedicel ca. 1 mm. Calyx cupular, usually glabrous, truncate to obscurely 4‑dentate. Corolla purple to pink, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens 2–3 times as long as corolla; anthers ellipsoidal, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary glabrous. Fruit subglobose, ca. 2 mm in diam., red, turning black when dry.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1138, 1896; Y. S. Lau 365.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan; Bangladesh, India, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Callicarpa rubella Lindl. 紅紫珠
Bot. Reg. 11: pl. 883. 1825; FHK 271. 1861; FKH 203. 1912; FYN 1: 410, pl. 98: 6 – 10. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 63. 1982; FFJ 4: 526, fig. 417. 1989; FOC 17: 13. 1994; FGD 3: 357. 1995.
Callicarpa dielsii (H. Lév.) C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 37. 1932.
Callicarpa panduriformis H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222 – 226): 455. 1911.
Callicarpa rubella var. dielsii (H. Lév.) H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25(4): 425. 1944.
Callicarpa rubella var. hemsleyana Diels, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29(3 – 4): 547 – 548. 1900.
Callicarpa tenuiflora Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 135. 1853.
Viburnum dielsii H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222 – 226): 443. 1911.

Shrub, 1.5–2 m tall. Branchlets robust, with brown stellate and glandular hairs. Petiole very short to subsessile; leaf blade papery, obovate or obovate‑elliptic, 10–15 × 4–8 cm, base cordate and sometimes oblique, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrulate, irregularly serrate, or serrate, adaxially with glandular hairs, abaxially with stellate, simple, and glandular hairs and yellow glandular; lateral veins 6–10 pairs, midvein, lateral veins, and reticulate veins elevated on both surfaces. Cymes 2–4 cm across, covered with brown stellate and glandular hairs. Peduncle to 3 cm. Bracts small. Calyx subtruncate to slightly dentate with obtusely triangular teeth, with stellate hairs, glandular hairs, and yellow glands. Corolla purple, sometimes greenish, or white, ca. 3 mm, puberulent, yellow glandular. Stamens twice as long as corolla. Fruit subglobose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tsim Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. U. A. On 5605; Y. S. Lau 1253; P. S. Choi 210.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of Callicarpa tenuiflora was collected by J. G. Champion from “Saywan” (Chai Wan) between 1847 and 1850.

Callistemon rigidus R. Br. 紅千層
Bot. Reg. 5: t. 393. 1819; DC., Prodr. 3: 223. 1828; FGZ 208, fig. 100. 1956; FHN 2: 4, fig. 288. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 53, pl. 9: 1 – 3. 1984; FFJ 4: 92, fig. 77. 1989; FGX 1: 900. 1991; FGD 3: 171, fig. 120. 1995; FYN 7: 106. 1997.

Small tree. Bark dark grey; young branchlets angulate, covered with long silky hairs at first, glabrescent. Petioles very short; leaf blade leathery, linear 5–9 × 0.3–0.6 cm, apex acute, with conspicuous oil glands, silky hairy at first, glabrescent; midvein prominent on both surfaces. Spikes terminal, ca. 10 cm; rachis growing into normal branches after flowering. Hypanthium slightly hairy. Sepals semiorbicular, membranous. Petals green, ovate, ca. 6 × 4.5 mm, with oil glands. Stamens 2.5 cm, brightly red; anthers dark purple, ellipsoidal. Styles slightly longer than stamens, red with green apex. Capsule semiglobose, 5 × 7 mm, apex truncate, dehiscing into 3 valves. Seeds linear, 1 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 508, 861; Y. S. Lau 599.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi (cultivated); native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Environmental, ornamental.

Callistemon viminalis G. Don 串錢柳

Hort. Brit. 197. 1830.


Small tree, 2– 5 m. Bark thick, longitudinally-cracked ; branchlets lax and flexible, usually drooping. Petioles absent; leaf blade linear, 8–9 × 0.7–0.8 cm, apex acute, with numerous conspicuous oil glands; midvein more prominent on abaxial surface; margin entire, not swollen. Spikes terminal, ca. 15 cm, usually hanging down. Hypanthium hairy. Sepals 5, surmounting the floral tube. Petals greenish, ca. 8 mm. Stamens numerous, 2.5 cm, red, united at base. Ovary inferior, 3-locular each with numerous ovules; styles slender, red. Capsule 5–8 mm.


Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 727; L. T. Lo 13.

Distribution: Guangdong (cultivated); native to Australia.

Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Aug.

Uses: Ornamental, environmental.

Callistephus chinensis (L.) Nees 翠菊
Gen. Sp. Aster. 222. 1832; FRPS 74: 109. 1985; FGD 8: 177, fig. 98. 2007.
Aster chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 877. 1753.

Erect annual herbs, 30–100 cm tall, hirsute throughout. Leaves in the middle portion of stem ovate or spatulate, 3–6 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, serrate on margin; petiole winged, 2–4 cm; leaves changed to smaller size in upper portion, oblanceolate, long‑oblong or linear, entire or slightly serrate at distal end. Capitula terminal to branches, 4 – 8 cm across. Involucres hemispherical, 2–4 cm across; phyllaries 3‑seriate, nearly equal in length; outer ones foliaceous, oblong‑lanceolate or spatulate, 10–20 × 2–4 mm, apex rounded, coarsely ciliate on margin; those in middle layer spatulate, membranous, tinged purple; inner ones long‑oblong, apex obtuse, membranous, semi‑transparent. Ligulate florets in 1–several series, 10–30 × 2–5 mm; cultivated form with various colours, white, red, pink, purple or blue. Achenes oblong‑oblanceolate, slightly compressed, 3 mm, pilose on upper portion. Pappus 2‑seriate, outer ones short; inner ones plumose, caducous.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 113 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22444 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 12979 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to SW and N China; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Callitriche palustris var. elegans (Petrov) Y. L. Chang 東北水馬齒
Fl. Pl. Herb. Chin. Bor.‑Orient. 6: 53. 1977; FRPS 45(1): 12, pl. 4: 6 – 7. 1980; FOC 11: 320. 2008.
Callitriche bengalensis Petrov, Izv. Glavn. Bot. Sada S.S.S.R. 27: 358. 1928.
Callitriche stagnalis auct. non Scop.: FKH 102. 1912.

Flowers generally with a carpellate and staminate flower in one of a pair of axils opposed by a single carpellate flower in other axil, very occasionally 2 carpellate flowers and 1 staminate flower in a single axil; bracts persistent, 0.8 – 1.2 mm, falcate; styles erect to slightly spreading, shorter than 1.5 mm; filaments ± straight, fugacious, rarely visible in axils below rosettes, shorter than 2.2 mm; anthers ca. 0.4 × 0.3 mm. Fruit black when mature, 1 – 1.4 × 0.7 – 1.1 mm, sessile, higher than wide, widest above middle, slightly strumose, mericarps sharply reticulate, reticulations appearing ± clearly in vertical rows; wing all around, mainly toward apex, less than 0.3 mm wide.

Locality: Lam Tsuen. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 21976 (K); K. Y. Chan 1414 (IBSC, HK).
Distribution: N Heilongjiang, Jiangxi, E Jilin, Liaoning, E Nei Mongol; Japan, E Russia.
Ecology: Along ditches, in marshes. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Notes: The species was reported as C. stagnalis Scop. previously in various local literature (Hu, Enum. Vasc. Pl. Hongk. & N.T. 39. 1972; Corlett et al., Mem. Hongk. Nat. Hist. Soc. 23: 39. 2000; Check List HK Plants 240. 2002; 83. 2004), based on a specimen from Lam Tsuen (K. Y. Chan 1414); the duplicate at K was cited as C. palustris var. palustris by Lansdown (Novon 16: 358. 2006).

Callitriche palustris var. oryzetorum (Petrov) Lansdown 廣東水馬齒
Novon 16: 359. 2006; FOC 11: 320. 2008.
Callitriche oryzetorum Petrov, Izv. Glavn. Bot. Sada S.S.S.R. 27: 358. 1928; FRPS 45(1): 14. 1980; FGD 4: 130. 2000.

Flowers with a carpellate and staminate flower in each axil, very occasionally 2 carpellate flowers and 1 staminate flower in a single axil; bracts persistent, broadly ovoid, 0.58–0.9(–1) mm; styles erect to spreading, shorter than 1.7 mm; filaments straight; 1.6–2.7 mm; anthers 0.4–0.5 × 0.3–0.4 mm. Fruit brown when mature, 0.7–1 × 0.6–0.8 mm, widest near middle, smooth; wing lacking or up to 0.1 mm, only at apex.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11356 (PE).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Running water in ditches.

Calogyne pilosa R. Br. subsp. chinensis (Benth.) H. S. Kiu 火花離根香
Guihaia 9(3): 194. 1989.
Calogyne chinensis Benth., J. Linn. Soc. 5: 78. 1861; FGD 2: 361. 1991.
Calogyne pilosa auct. non R. Br.: FRPS 73(2): 179. 1983.

Perennial herbs, 5–15 cm tall, aromatic when dry; Stems erect, sparsely pubescent; branches slender, diffuse or procumbent after anthesis. Leaves fasciculate at the base of stem, subsessile; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to linear, 10–25 × 1–3 mm, base attenuate, apex acute, sparsely hirsute on both surfaces, margin remotely undulate‑dentate, ciliate; upper stem leaves alternate and smaller, sometimes with ear‑like lobes at the base. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels slender, 5–10(–20) mm. Calyx‑tube ovoid, less than 2 mm, covered with white short hairs; lobes 5, lanceolate, 4–5 × 1–1.5 mm. Corolla yellow, 6–7 mm, hairy abaxially. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 2.5 mm. Capsule ovoid, 4 – 4.5 × 3–3.5 mm, 7–12‑seeded.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 10484.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Moist places, grassy hillslopes, pine forests. Flowering: May–Dec.

Calophyllum membranaceum Gardn. & Champ. 胡桐
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 309. 1849; FHK 25. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 83. 1990; FHN 2: 56. 1965; FGD 3: 211. 1995

Shrub or small tree, 1–5 m tall. Branchlets narrowly 4-winged, glabrous. Petioles 0.4–1 cm; leaves thinly leathery, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, 4 –13 × 1.5 – 4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, acute or caudate-acuminate, margin entire, often slightly sinuaterevolute, shining on both surfaces, midvein elevated on both surfaces; lateral veins many, slender, parallel. Cymes axillary, 1–3 cm, (1–)3–9-flowered. Flowers white, reddish. Sepals 4, outer 2 suborbicular, ca. 4 mm; inner 2 petal-like, obovate, ca. 8 mm. Petals 4, obovate, ca. 8 mm. Stamens many; filaments united into 4 bundles at base. Ovary ovoid; style 4.5–5.5 mm. Drupes yellow, ovoid-oblong, 16 –20 × 10 –12 mm, apex mucronate. Seeds ca. 15 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 393; K. L. Yip 4099.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi; India, Sri Lanka, Indochina, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Polynesia, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Calystegia hederacea Wall. 打碗花（旋花）
Fl. Ind. 2: 94. 1824; FRPS 64(1): 47. 1979; FFJ 4: 484. 1989; FOC 16: 287. 1995; FGD 4: 339, fig. 201. 2000.
Calystegia hederacea Wall. var. elongata Liou & Ling, Fl. Ill. Nord Chine 1: 25, pl. 8, fig. 2. 1931.
Volvulus hederaceus (Wall.) Kuntze, Rev. Gén. Bot. 447. 1891.

Annual herb, glabrous. Stems erect when young, later shoots prostrate or twining, finely striate. Petiole 1–5 cm; basal leaf blade oblong, 2–3(–5.5) × 1–2.5 cm, base hastate, apex rounded, distal leaf blade 3‑lobed, middle lobe oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, lateral lobes subtriangular, entire or 2–3‑lobed. Lower peduncles exceeding leaves, upper peduncles shorter; bracteoles ± ovate, 0.7–1.4(–1.8) cm × (4–)6–10(–12) mm, flat, apex acute to ± obtuse. Corolla pale pink or occasionally whitish or purplish, 2–3.5 cm. Stamens 1.1–1.6(–1.9) cm; anthers 3–4 mm.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 3022.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Afghanistan, India, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, NE Africa, rarely introduced in N America.
Ecology: Wastelands and farmlands. Flowering: Mar. – Sep.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Calystegia sepium (L.) R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 222. 2002; 77. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Calystegia sepium (L.) R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 222. 2002; 77. 2004).

Camellia caudata Wall. 長尾毛蕊茶
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 36. 1832; FKH 46. 1912; FRPS 49(3): 192. 1998.
Thea caudata (Wall.) Seem., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 22: 348. 1859.
Theopsis caudata (Wall.) Hu, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 266. 1963; FHN 1: 497. 1964.
Camellia assimilis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 309. 1851; FHK 30. 1861; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 144. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 193. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, branchlets pubescent. Leaves membranaceous; petioles 3–7 mm, pubescent; leaf blade oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 4–12 × 1–3.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex long-caudate to caudate, margin serrulate, glabrous adaxially except for the hirsute midvein, slightly hirsute to nearly glabrous abaxially; Flowers axillary, solitary or 2–3 clustered; pedicels 3 –6 mm, pubescent; bracteoles 3 –6, semiorbicular to broadly ovate, 1– 6 mm, abaxially pubescent, margin ciliolate; sepals 5, 2– 4 mm, broadly ovate to suborbicular, silky-hairy abaxially, margin ciliolate; petals 5–7, white, 1–3 cm, connate at base, silky-hairy abaxially; stamens many, in 2 whorls, 1–2.5 cm, connate to middle, filaments densely silky-pilose; ovary globose, 2 mm in diam., densely tomentellous; styles 1–2.5 cm, tomentellous, 3-lobed at apex. Capsule ellipsoid-globose, 2 cm in diam., l-locular and l-seeded. Seeds brown, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1680; P. S. Choi 516.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Xizang, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: Oct.–Jan.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen of Camellia assimilis was collected from Mount Gough and Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G.Campion around 1850.

Camellia crapnelliana Tutch. 紅皮糙果茶
J. Linn. Soc. London 37: 63. 1904; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 129. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 18. 1998.
Thea crapnelliana (Tutch.) Rehd., J. Arnold Arbor. 5: 238. 1924.

Tree or shrub, branches and branchlets reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 6–12 mm, glabrous; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 7–19 × 3–6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex bluntly cuspidate, margin denticulate, glabrous; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, obscure adaxially, raised abaxially. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or paired, 6–10 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 7–13, persistent, suborbicular, 0.3–2 cm, tawny tomentellous abaxially; petals 6–8, white, obovate to obovate-oblong, 3.5–6.5 × 2–4 cm, connate at base, apex rounded to emarginate; stamens many, ca. 1.5 –1.7 cm; filaments glabrous, basal ca. 5 mm connated; ovary ca. 2 mm in diam., 3–5-locular, densely tomentose; styles 3–5, free, ca. 1.5 cm, proximal part pubescent to tomentose. Capsule greyish brown, subglobose, 5–10 cm in diam., 3–5-locular with 3–5 seeds per locule, furfuraceous, dehiscing into 3–5 valves; central axis thick, persistent; pericarp woody, (6–)10–15 mm thick. Seeds brown, semiglobose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Mau Ping. W. J. Tutcher 967; Y. S. Lau 1328.
Distribution: Guangdong, E Guangxi, E Jiangxi, Fujian, S Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Parker, Hong Kong Island in 1903. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Camellia euryoides Lindl. 柃葉茶
Bot. Reg. 1: 983. 1826; FGD 2: 140. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 162. 1998.
Thea euryoides (Lindl.) Booth, Trans. Hort. Soc. London 7560. 1830.

Shrub or small tree, young branches densely greyish yellow-pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 1–3 mm, pubescent; leaf blades thinly leathery, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, 2– 4 × 0.7–1.4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex bluntly acuminate, margin serrulate, hirtellous along midvein adaxially, sparsely appressed villose or glabrescent abaxially; lateral veins obscure on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 5–9 mm, slender, glabrous; bracteoles 4 or 5, triangular to broadly ovate, 1–1.5 mm, abaxially puberulous near apex, margin ciliolate; sepals 5, ca. 2.5 mm, connate at base, abaxially puberulous near apex, adaxially sericeous, margin ciliolate; petals 5, white, obovate to broadly obovate, ca. 2 cm, connate at base, abaxially glabrous, apex emarginate to truncate; stamens many, in 2 whorls, 0.9 –1.5 cm, glabrous; proximal 2/3 of filaments connate into a cup; ovary ovoid, 1.5–2 mm, glabrous; styles ca. 1.8 mm, glabrous, 3-lobed at apex. Capsules subglobose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., 1-locular with l seed; pericarp green to brown, thinly woody; central axis abortive. Seeds brown, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Mount Parker, Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 8066; HK sheet 35553.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Camellia furfuracea (Merr.) Cohen-Stuart 糙果茶
Bull. Jard. Bot. Buitenzorg, ser. 3, 1: 240. 1919; FGD 2: 130. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 19. 1998.
Thea furfuracea Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 13(3): 149. 1918.
Theopsis furfuracea (Merr.) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 16(12): 706. 1940.

Small tree or shrub, branches and branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves papery, narrowly to broadly elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 8–15 × 2.5 – 5.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, margin mucronulate-denticulate, glabrous; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, slightly impressed above, elevated below; petioles 4 –9 mm, glabrous. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or paired, 2–3.5 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 7–8, persistent, semiorbicular to suborbicular, smaller ones 2.5 –4 mm long, larger ones 8 –13 mm long, pubescent or yellow-tomentose abaxially; petals 6 –8, white, obovate, 1.5 –2 × 0.9–1.2 cm, connate at base for about 4 mm; stamens many, ca. 1.3–1.5 cm; filaments glabrous, connate at base, filament tube 5–6 mm; ovary ca. 1.5 mm in diam., 3-locular, densely tomentose, ovules 2– 4 per locule; styles 3, free, ca. 1.8 cm, pubescent almost to apex. Capsule subglobose, greyish brown, furfuraceous, 2–4 cm in diam., dehiscing into 3 valves; central axis thick, persistent; pericarp woody, 2–4 mm thick. Seeds brown, semiglobose, 1.5 –2 × 0.8 –1.7 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Au Pui Wan. K. L. Yip 4166; P. S. So 11.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Camellia granthamiana Sealy 大苞山茶
J. Roy. Hort. Soc. 81: 182. 1956; FGD 2: 127. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 6. 1998.

Shrub or tree, up to 8 m tall. Petioles 8–12 mm; leaf blades leathery, oblong-elliptic or elliptic, 7–11 × 3– 5 cm, base rounded to obtuse, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous, lateral veins 6–7 on each side of midvein, rugose adaxially when dry. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary, 10–14 cm in diam., subsessile; bracts and sepals 12, persistent, crustaceous, leathery, orbicular, 3– 4 cm, grey silky-hairy abaxially; petals 8 –10, white, broadly obovate, 5 –7 × 3.8 – 5 cm, basal 1.5 cm united, glabrous; stamens many, ca. 2.5 cm, basal 5– 6 mm united, glabrous. Ovary globose, 4 – 5 mm in diam., 5-locular, densely white-tomentose; styles 2 cm, 5-lobed at apex, densely white-tomentose. Capsule subglobose, ca. 6 cm in diam., furfuraceous, surrounded by persistent sepals, dehiscing into 5 valves; pericarp 5 mm thick. Seeds dark brown, spherical, 1–1.5 cm long.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 2056; P. S. Choi 246.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in a ravine of Tai Mo Shan by Hong Kong Herbarium staff in 1955. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental, materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in a ravine of Tai Mo Shan by Hong Kong Herbarium staff in 1955. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
