Camellia hongkongensis Seem. 香港茶
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 22: 342, t. 60. 1859; FHK 30. 1861; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 134. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 71. 1998.
Thea hongkongensis (Seem.) Pierre, Fl. For. Cochinch. 2: t. 117. 1887.

Shrub or small tree, up to 10 m tall, young branches reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles ca. 1 cm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong, 7–13 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex acuminate, margin entire or obscurely undulate-denticulate, light green adaxially, dark green and glabrous abaxially; midvein impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially, lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers subterminal, solitary, subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 9–11, 3 –20 mm, silky hairy, deciduous or persistent in fruit; petals 6–7, broadly obovate, 3.5–4 cm, connate at base; stamens many, ca. 3 cm, glabrous, connate at base; ovary globose, ca. 2 mm in diam., 3-locular, densely tomentose; styles 3 – 4, free, 2.8 –3.3 cm, glabrous. Capsule brown, globose to oblate, ca. 3 cm in diam., 3– 4-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule. Seeds brown, subglobose to globose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson, Mount Parker. W. Y. Chun 9172; C. Wang 30303; N. K. Chun 40030, 40280, 40286; H. T. Chang 6558, 6559.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Aug.– Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in a ravine of Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in 1849. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental, materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in a ravine of Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in 1849. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Camellia japonica L. 山茶
Sp. Pl. 2: 698. 1753; FGD 2: 134. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 87. 1998.
Thea japonica (L.) Baill., Hist. Pl. 4: 229. 1873.

Shrub or small tree, branches and branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 8 –15 mm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong or obovate-oblong, 5 –12 × 3 – 6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate or acute, margin serrulate, glabrous, lateral veins 7– 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or in pairs, 5 – 8 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 10, suborbicular to orbicular, 0.5 –2 cm in diam., pubescent; petals 6 –7, 2.5 –3.5 cm, rose or white, connate at base, silky-pubescent abaxially; stamens many, filaments connate about half way into a tube and united at base with petals, glabrous, 2.5 –3.5 cm, anthers oblong, 2 mm; ovary ovoid, 2.5 mm in diam., glabrous, 3-locular; styles ca. 2.8 cm, 3-lobed at the apex, glabrous. Capsule globose, 2.5 – 4.5 cm in diam., 3-locular with 1 or 2 seeds per locule; pericarp woody, 5 – 8 mm thick when dry. Seeds brown, semiglobose to globose, 1–2 cm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32805; C. H. Tsou 1824.
Distribution: Shandong, Zhejiang; S Japan, S Korea. Widely cultivated in gardens.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Camellia kissii Wall. 落瓣油茶
Asiat. Res. 13: 429. 1820; FHN 1: 500. 1964; FGD 2: 131. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 24. 1998.
Thea sasanqua var. kissi (Wall.) Pierre, Fl. For. Cochinch. 2: sub. t. 115 – 6. 1887.

Shrub or small tree; branchlets greyish brown, pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 4 –7 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blade oblong, or oblong-elliptic, 5 –7 × 1.5 –3 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrulate; hirtellous along midvein adaxially, villose or glabrescent abaxially, lateral veins 6– 8 on each side of midvein, slightly impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, or slightly raised on both surfaces. Flowers axillary, solitary or in pair, 2–3 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 9–10, 2–7 mm, pubescent, caducous; petals 5– 8, white, nearly free, obovate to ovate, 1.2–1.5 cm, pubescent abaxially; stamens 6–9 mm, glabrous, filaments basal 1–3 mm connate; ovary 3-locular, white-tomentose; styles 3, 3–7 mm, connate at base, glabrous or tomentose proximally. Capsule subglobose to globose-pyriform, 1.4 –2.5 × 1.5 –2 cm, usually l locule developed with 1 seed per locule, dehiscing into 2–3 valves; pericarp thickly, ca. 1.5 mm thick. Seed brown, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Kwun Yam Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Bride's Pool. Y. S. Lau 2811; HK sheet 33868.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan and Yunnan; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Sikkim, Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen forests and thickets. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Camellia oleifera Abel 油茶
Narr. Journey China 174, 363. 1818; FHN 1: 500. 1964; FGD 2: 128. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 13. 1998.
Camellia drupifera Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 411. 1790; FKH 46. 1912, non. rej. prop.
Thea oleifera (Abel) Rehd. & Wils., Pl. Wilson. 2: 393. 1915.

Shrub or small tree, young branchlets reddish brown, pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 5–10 mm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 6–10 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate to serrulate, sparsely pilose along midvein or glabrous adaxially, hirtellous along midvein abaxially, lateral veins 5– 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or in pairs, 4 – 6 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 8–11, broadly ovate, 3 –12 mm, yellow-tomentose abaxially, margin membranous and ciliolate, caducous; petals 5–7, white, nearly free, obovate, oblong-obovate, or oblanceolate, 2.5– 4 × 1.5 –2.5 cm, 2-lobed at apex; stamens 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, filaments connate at base into a tube; ovary globose, 2–3 mm in diam., 3-locular, white-tomentose; styles 0.8–1.2 cm, glabrous or tomentose at base, 3-lobed. Capsule globose to ellipsoid, 2– 4 cm in diam., 1–3-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule, dehiscing into 2–3 valves; pericarp 3 – 6 mm thick, villose. Seeds brown to reddish brown, globose to semiglobose, 1.5 –2 cm in diam.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. L. T. Lo 652; Y. S. Lau 3275; Y. W. Lam 134.
Distribution: Area S of Changjiang River; N Laos, N Myanmar, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: Dec.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Materials (lipids).

Camellia reticulata Lindl. 滇山茶
Bot. Reg. t. 1078. 1827; FRPS 49(3): 68. 1998.
Desmitus reticulata (Lindl.) Rafin., Sylva Tellur 39. 1838.
Thea reticulata (Lindl.) Kochs, Bot. Jahbr. Syst. 27: 595. 1900.

Shrub or tree, branches and branchlets greyish brown, pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 6–13 mm, pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blade oblong to oblong-elliptic, 5 –12 × 3 – 5.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin serrulate, sparsely appressed pubescent or glabrescent adaxially, glabrous abaxially; lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein and raised on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or 2–3 clustered, 7–10 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 9 –11, deciduous after anthesis; petals 5–7 but often more for some cultivars, rose to pink, rarely white, obovate to broadly obovate, 4–6 × 3 – 4.5 cm, apex emarginate, connate at base; stamens many, 3 – 4 cm, glabrous, filaments connate at base; ovary globose, 3 – 4 mm in diam., 3 – 5-locular, tomentose; styles 2.5 –3.5 cm, glabrous or hairy proximally, 3– 5-lobed at apex. Capsule globose to oblate, 3.5– 4 × 4 – 5 cm, 3 – 5-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule; pericarp firmly fleshy, ca. l cm thick or 5– 6 mm when dry. Seeds brown, semiglobose to globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 33869, 33870.
Distribution: Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Camellia salicifolia Champ. ex Benth. 柳葉茶
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 309. 1851; FHK 30. 1861; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 142. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 194. 1998.
Thea salicifolia (Champ.) Seem., Trans. L. Soc. 22: 349. 1859.
Camelliastrum salicifolia (Champ.) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 16: 701. 1940.

Shrub or small tree, young branchlets densely pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 1–3 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blades membranaceous, lanceolate, 6 –10 × 1.5 –2.5 cm, base rounded, apex long-acuminate to caudate, margin serrulate, glabrous adaxially except for the pubescent midvein, densely pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Flowers axillary, solitary; pedicels 4– 5 mm, densely villose; bracteoles 4– 5, lanceolate, 4 –10 mm, pubescent, persistent; sepals 5, lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, silky-hairy abaxially; petals 5 – 6, white, subequal, obovate to obovate-elliptic, 1.5 –2 × 0.8 –1.5 cm, silky-hairy abaxially, connate at base; stamens many, in 2 whorls, filaments ca. 1–1.5 cm, connate to 3/4 of its length, free portion hairy, anthers pubescent; ovary densely tomentellous; styles ca. 1 cm, densely tomentellous, 3-lobed. Capsule globose, 1.5 –2.5 cm in diam., llocular with l seed, apex shortly conical; pericarp ca. 1 mm thick. Seed brown, subglobose.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 1487; N. H. Li 3.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian,Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion around 1850.

Camellia sasanqua Thunb. 茶梅
Fl.: Jap. 273, t. 30. 1784; FKH 46. 1912; FHN 1: 500. 1964; FRPS 49(3): 12. 1998.

Small tree; young branchlets pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 4 – 6 mm, glabrescent; leaf blade elliptic, 3 – 6 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, or sometimes rounded, apex acute, margin serrulate; lateral veins 5 –6 on each side of midvein, obscure on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or terminal, 4 –7 cm in diam.; bracteoles and sepals 6 –7, pubescent; petals 6–7, red, nearly free, unequal, broadly obovate, the largest one 5 × 6 cm; stamens many, free, 1.5 –2 cm; ovary pilose, styles 1–1.3 cm, free or 3-lobed at apex. Capsules globose, 1.5 –2 cm across, 1–3-locular. Seeds brown, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 274; Y. S. Lau 3021.
Distribution: Native to Japan. Widely cultivated.
Uses: Ornamental.

Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze 茶
Trudy Imp. S.-Peterburgsk. Bot. Sada 10: 195. 1887; FGD 2: 137. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 130. 1998.
Thea sinensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 515. 1753; FHN 1: 496. 1964.
Camellia thea Link., Enum. Hort. Berol. Alt. 2: 73. 1822; FKH 45. 1912.

Shrub or small tree; young branches pubescent, glabrescent; terminal buds silvery grey sericeous. Petioles 3 – 8 mm, glabrous; leaf blades leathery, elliptic to oblong, 4 –12 × 2– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin serrate to serrulate, glabrous adaxially, glabrous or pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2–3 clustered, 2–3 cm in diam.; pedicels 4– 6 mm, recurved, pubescent or glabrous; bracteoles 2, caducous, ovate, ca. 2 mm; sepals 5, persistent, leathery, broadly ovate to suborbicular, 3–4 mm, glabrous or white-pubescent abaxially, white-sericeous adaxially, margin ciliolate; petals 6 –8, white, outer 1–3 sepaloid, inner ones obovate to broadly obovate, 1–1.6 × 1.2–2 cm, connate at base, apex rounded, glabrous or pubescent; stamens many, 0.8 –1.3 cm, glabrous, in 3– 4 whorls, connate at base; ovary globose, 3-locular, pubescent; styles ca. 1 cm, glabrous or pubescent at base, 3-lobed at apex. Capsule oblate, rarely globose, 1–1.5 × 1.5–3 cm, 1–2-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule; pericarp ca. l mm thick; central axis persistent. Seeds brown, subglobose, 1–1.4 cm in diam.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1390; HK sheet 32921.
Distribution: Area S of Changjiang River; Japan, Korea, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical parts of the world.
Ecology: Forests and thickets, or cultivated. Flowering: Oct.–Feb.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Food (beverage base), medicinal (source of caffeine & theophylline).
records.uses: Food (beverage base), medicinal (source of caffeine & theophylline).

records.text:
Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze var. waldenae (S. Y. Hu) H. T. Chang 香花茶
Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 20(1): 98. 1981; FGD 2: 137. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 131. 1998.
Camellia waldenae S. Y. Hu, Wild Flowers of Hong Kong. 61. 1977.

Differs from var. sinensis by its narrowly oblanceolate leaves and sweet-smelling flowers.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang. S. Y. Hu 12573 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 428.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forest.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Tai Mo Shan by S. Y. Hu.

Campsis grandiflora (Thunb.) Schum. 凌霄
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(3b): 230. 1894; FHN 3: 530, fig. 907. 1974; FRPS 69: 33, pl. 1: 1 – 3. 1990; FFJ 5: 82, fig. 90. 1993; FOC 18: 220. 1998.
Bignonia grandiflora Thunb., Fl. Jap. 253. 1784.
Bignonia chinensis Lam., Encycl. 1: 423. 1785.
Tecoma chinensis K. Koch, Dendr. 2: 307. 1872.
Campsis chinensis (Lam.) Voss., Vilm. Blumengart. ed. 3, 801. 1895.

Stems woody. Leaf rachis 4–13 cm; leaflets 7–9; petiolules 1–5(–10) mm, with a cluster of hairs between petiolules; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3–6(–9) × 1.5–3(–5) cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate‑acuminate, both surfaces glabrous, densely glandular abaxially; lateral veins 6–7 pairs. Thyrses large, lax. Peduncle to 20 cm. Flowers 4–6.5 cm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 3 cm, divided halfway; lobes triangular, ca. 1.5 cm, acuminate. Corolla red adaxially, orange‑red abaxially, ca. 5 cm in diam.; lobes semi‑orbicular, flat and erect. Stamens inserted at base of corolla tube; filaments linear, 2–2.5 cm; anthers divergent, yellow. Style linear, ca. 3 cm; stigma compressed, 2‑lobed. Capsule apex obtuse.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2384.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang, Henan, Shandong, Hebei, Shaanxi (cultivated or wild); Japan, India, Pakistan and Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: May –Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Camptotheca acuminata Decne. 喜樹
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 20: 157. 1873; FRPS 52(2): 145, pl. 41. 1983; FGD 4: 285. 2000.

Tree to 20 m tall; bark grey, deeply fissured and furrowed; young branchlets purplish green, puberulous, old branchlets glabrous. Petiole 1.5–3 cm, puberulous; leaf blade papery, elliptic to ovate-oblong, 8–28 × 6–12 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex acute, margin entire, dense greyish pubescent along veins abaxially, lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein. Heads, 1.5–2 cm in diam., often 2–9 heads rearranged in panicles; peduncle 3–6 cm, puberulous; bracts 3, triangular, 2.5–3 mm, both surfaces pubescent. Calyx cupular, shallowly 5-lobed; lobes triangular. Petals 5, ovate-oblong, pale green, ca. 2 mm, densely pubescent abaxially. Disk conspicuous. Stamens 10, outer 5 longer than petals, glabrous, inner 5 shorter, filaments slender. Style ca. 4 mm, glabrous, 2–3-lobed, lobes recurved. Samaras ellipsoidal, narrowly winged, grey-brown, 2.5–3.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 187; Y. W. Lam 18, 2204.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental (roadside tree).

Campylandra wattii C. B. Clarke 彎蕊開口箭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 25: 78. 1889; FOC 24: 236. 2000; FGD 6: 346, fig. 201. 2005.
Campylandra cauliflora Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 213–215. 1934.
Tupistra wattii (C. B. Clarke) Hook. f., Fl. Brit. India 6(18): 325. 1892; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.

Perennial herb. Rhizome elongate, stem-like, ± curved, to 1.2 cm thick. Stem elongate. Leaves spirally arranged on stem, subdistichous; petioles 3–9 cm, basally dilated and amplexicaul; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to narrowly elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 8–20 × 3–7 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate. Spikes 3–6, densely flowered, with several sterile bracts apically; peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm; fertile bracts linear-lanceolate, 1.2–1.8(–5) cm. Perianth tube 3–5 mm; segments red-brown or yellowish green, broadly ovate, 3.5–4 × 2–4 mm, fleshy. Stamens 6; filaments proximally widened and adnate to perianth tube, free part incurved, 1.5–2 mm. Ovary globose; style inconspicuous; stigma 3-lobed. Berry red at maturity, globose, 0.9–1.1 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 166, 433.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Shaded and moist places in forests. Flowering: Feb.–May.

Canarium album (Lour.) Raeusch. 橄欖（白欖）
Nomencl. Bot. 287. 1797; FKH 57. 1912; FGZ 438. 1956; FHN 3: 57, fig. 562. 1974; FYN 1: 197, pl. 46: 1– 10. 1977; FFJ 2: 381, fig. 282. 1985; FGD 3: 267, fig. 181. 1995; FRPS 43(3): 25, pl. 7: 1–10. 1997.
Pimela alba Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 408. 1790.

Tree, 10–25 m tall. Branchlets yellowish brown tomentose when young, glabrescent. Leaves odd-pinnate; stipules linear, yellowish brown tomentose, caducous; leaflets 7–11(–17), shortly petiolulate; blade papery to leathery, oblong-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 6–20 × 2–5.5 cm, base rounded or cuneate, oblique, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, scabrous abaxially; lateral veins 12–16 pairs, conspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, slightly tomentose or glabrescent, shorter than leaves. Calyx cupular, shallowly 3-lobed, 2.5–3 mm. Petals white, twice as long as calyx. Stamens glabrous; filaments connate at lower half. Ovary densely pubescent. Drupe ovoid or spindle-shaped, suborbicular in cross section, 2.5–3.5 cm, yellow green, glabrous; exocarp thick, wrinkled when dry, stone acuminate at both ends.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 645; HK sheet 40740.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Fruit, roadside tree, timber.

Canarium tramdenum C. D. Dai & Yakovlev 烏欖
Bot. Zhurn. (Moscow & Leningrad) 70(6): 784. 1985; FGD 3: 267. 1995.
Canarium pimela K. D. König, Ann. Bot. (Konig & Sims) 1: 361, t. 7: 1. 1805, nom. illeg.; FGZ 439. 1956; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 463, fig. 2856. 1972.
Canarium pimela Leenh., Blumea 9(2): 406, fig. 25. 1959, isonym; FHN 2: 57. 1974; FYN 1: 198, pl. 46: 14–16. 1977; FRPS 43(3): 27, pl. 7: 14 –16. 1997.
Canarium pimeloides Govaerts, World Checklist Seed Plants 3(1): 12. 1999.

Tree, up to 20 m tall. Leaves odd-pinnate, exstipulate; leaflets 7–13(–17), blade papery to leathery, broadly elliptic, ovate, oblong, ovate-lanceolate or obovate, 3–20 × 2–8 cm, base cuneate to subrounded, oblique, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, smooth abaxially; lateral veins 8–15 pairs, reticulate veins conspicuous. Inflorescence a cymose panicle, glabrous. Calyx cupular, ca. 2 mm, shallowly-lobed. Petals 3 times as long as calyx. Stamens glabrous; filaments connate at lower half. Ovary glabrous. Infructescence 8–35 cm long, 1–4-fruited. Drupe purple black when mature, narrowly ovoid, 3–4 × 1.7–2 cm, orbicular to inconspicuously triangular in cross section.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 2476; Y. S. Lau 1164; K. L. Yip 4101.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan (cultivated); Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Timber, fruit used for making preserved fruit.
Notes: Canarium pimela K. D. König was proposed to be conserved by Y. F. Deng & G. H. Zhu (Taxon 54(2): 550. 2005) and approved by Nomenclature Committee for Vascular Plants (Taxon 56(2): 592. 2007). If the proposal is approved by Nomenclature Section of the next International Botanical Congress, the correct name of this species will be Canarium pimela K. D. König.

records.text:
Canavalia gladiata (Jacq.) DC. 刀豆
Prodr. 2: 404. 1825; FHK 88. 1861; Sauer, Brittonia 16: 149. 1964; FRPS 41: 208. 1995; FGD 5: 305, fig. 162. 2003.
Dolichos gladiatus Jacq., Collectanea 2: 276. 1788.

Climbing herb to several metres long. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets ovate, 8–15 × 8–12 cm, base rounded or oblique (lateral ones), apex acuminate, acute, sparsely whitish pubescent on both surfaces at first. Racemes axillary, 10 – 20-flowered. Peduncles 20 – 25 cm. Flowers 2 – 3-fasciculate on node. Calyx 15– 16 mm, slightly pubescent, upper lip with 2 broadly orbicular lobes, lower lip with 2(–3) small teeth. Corolla white or pink, 3–3.5 cm; petals clawed and auriculate; vexillum broadly elliptic, 3.5– 4 × 2.5 cm, emarginate; wings and keel oblong, incurved, smaller than vexillum. Ovary linear, hairy. Pods loriform, thickly leathery, 20 – 35 × 3.5– 5 cm, slightly curved, with extra rib. Seeds reddish-brown, elliptic-oblong, 3.5 × 2 cm; hilum ca. 1.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 7903.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China; plant originally cultivated in Far East, now widely cultivated in tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.– Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Green manure, forage.

Canavalia lineata (Thunb.) DC. 狹刀豆
Prodr. 2: 404. 1825; FRPS 41: 210. 1995; Sauer, Brittonia 16: 162. 1964; FGD 5: 306. 2003.
Dolichos lineatus Thunb., Fl. Jap. 280. 1784.

Perennial twining herb. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets hardly leathery, ovate or obovate, 6– 14 × 4– 10 cm, base truncate or cuneate, apex rounded or cuspidate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Racemes axillary. Calyx 12 mm, pubescent, upper lip large, broadly 2-lobed, lower lip 3-toothed; teeth small, subtruncate. Corolla purplish-red; vexillum broadly ovate, 2.5 cm, emarginate, auriculate and with 2 callosities at base; wings linear-oblong, slightly falcate; keel obovate-oblong. Pods oblong, compressed, 6 –10 × 2.5–3 cm, with extra rib ca. 3 mm from sutural rib. Seeds 2 –3, brown, ovate, 1.7 × 7 mm, blotched.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Kei Ling Ha, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3254; Y. W. Lam 900; HK sheet 39828.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Philippines, Vietnam to Indonesia.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. – Oct.

Canavalia maritima Thouars 海刀豆
J. Bot. Agric. 1: 80. 1813; FGD 5: 306. 2003.
Dolichos maritimus Aubl., Hist. Pl. Guiane 765. 1775.
Canavalia obtusifolia (Lam.) DC., Prodr. 2: 402. 1825; FKH 84. 1912.

Perennial herbaceous twiner. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets obovate, ovate, elliptic or suborbicular, 5–8 × 4.5–6.5 cm, base cuneate or subrounded, apex rounded, truncate, emarginate or apiculate, lateral ones often oblique, villose on both surfaces, lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Racemes axillary, 30 cm including peduncles. Flowers 1 –3-fasciculate on each node. Calyx campanulate, 1 – 1.2 cm, pubescent, upper lobes semiorbicular, lower ones smaller. Corolla purple-red; vexillum orbicular, ca. 2.5 cm, emarginate; wings falcate, auriculate; keel oblong, curved, auriculate. Ovary tomentose. Pods linear-oblong, 8 – 12 × 2 – 2.5 cm, adpressed pubescent at first, beaked at tip, with extra rib 0.3 mm form sutural rib. Seeds brown, elliptic, 13– 15 × 10 mm; hilum ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma Shi Chau, Ma Wan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1378; HK sheet 34216, 40708.
Distribution: SE to S China; tropical coastal areas. One of the commonest and most characteristic sea-coast plants.
Ecology: Sandy beaches.

Canna glauca L. 粉美人蕉
Sp. Pl. 1: 1. 1753; FRPS 16(2): 155. 1981; FGD 2: 434. 1991.

Rhizomes elongate; stem 1.5–2 m, green. Leaves green, glaucous, lanceolate, to 50 × 10–15 cm, base attenuate, apex long-acuminate, margin hyaline. Racemes simple or sparingly branched, with a green, pruinose rachis; bracts round, brown; flowers in pairs, rarely in threes; light yellow, not dotted; sepals green, ovate, 1.2 cm; corolla tube 1–2 cm, lobes linear-lanceolate, 2.5–5 × 5 cm, erect; outer cycle staminodes 3, obovate-oblong, 6–7.5 × 2–3 cm, entire; labellum yellowish, much narrower, linear-lanceolate, bifid at apex, twisty at medium; stamens obovatesubfalcate, apex acute, revolute; style narrow-lanceolate. Capsules oblong, 3.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32948.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions, native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Canna indica L. 美人蕉
Sp. Pl. 1: 1. 1753; FHK 349. 1861; FKH 273. 1912; FHN 4: 103. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 157. 1981; FGD 2: 435. 1991; FOC 24: 378. 2000.
Canna edulis Ker, Bot. Reg. 9: t. 775. 1823; FHN 4: 104. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 157. 1981; FGD 2: 435. 1991.

Rhizome developed, much branched. Stems stout, to 2.5 m. Leaf sheath green or purple; petiole short; leaf blade ovate-oblong to oblong, 30–60 × 10–20 cm, adaxially green, abaxially and at margin green or purple. Inflorescence a raceme of cincinni. Bracts light purple, ovate, ca. 8 mm. Flowers 1–2 per cincinnus. Sepals pale purplish green, lanceolate, ca. 1.5 cm. Corolla tube apricot yellow, ca. 1.5 cm; lobes erect, red to apricot yellow with purplish apex, lanceolate, ca. 4 cm. Staminodes 2(–3), erect, red with apricot yellow base, oblanceolate, 4–5.5 cm × 7–10 mm, 1 with apex emarginate; labellum red, sometimes with yellow spots, lanceolate, ca. 4.5 cm, margin revolute, apex emarginate; fertile stamen with filament reddish apricot yellow, lanceolate, ca. 4.2 cm. Anther ca. 9 mm. Ovary green, globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., warty. Style red to apricot yellow, narrow, ca. 6 cm, base adnate to staminode column. Capsule broadly ovoid, 1.2–1.8 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2428, 3075; HK sheet 7351.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to India.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (forklore), food (tuberous rhizome).

Canna × generalis L. H. Bailey & E. Z. Bailey 大花美人蕉
Hortus 118. 1930, et Man. Cult. Pl. 291. 1949; FRPS 16(2): 155. 1981; FGD 2: 434. 1991.
Canna orchioides Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 291. 1949.

Plant ca. 1.5 m tall; stems, leaves and inflorescences glaucous. Leaves elliptic, to 40 × 20 cm, sheath and margins purple. Racemes terminal, 15–30 cm; flower large dense, 1–2 each bract; sepals lanceolate, 1.5–3 cm; corolla tube 5–10 mm, lobes lanceolate, 4.5–6.5 cm; outer cycle staminodes 3, obovate-spathulate, 5–10 × 2–5 cm, various coloured, red, orange, white, etc.; labellum obovatespathulate, ca. 4.5 × 1.2–4 cm; stamen lanceolate, ca. 4 × 2.5 cm; style loriform.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2715.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: There are many cultivars in this species, common ones are ‘President’, ‘Striates’, ‘Scarlet Beauty’ and ‘King Humbert’.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: There are many cultivars in this species, common ones are ‘President’, ‘Striates’, ‘Scarlet Beauty’ and ‘King Humbert’.

Cansjera rheedii J. F. Gmel. 山柑藤（山柑）
Syst. Nat. 2: 280. 1791; FHN 2: 458, fig. 522. 1965; FGD 4: 249, fig. 149. 2000; FRPS 24: 47, pl. 12: 1– 5. 1988; FOC 5: 205. 2003.

Scandent shrub, 2–6 m. Branchlets sometimes armed; branchlets and inflorescences yellowish tomentose. Petioles 2–4 mm, tomentulose; leaf blade thinly leathery, ovate to elliptic, 4–13 × 2.5–6 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, sometimes asymmetrical, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrescent; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences fasciculate, 1–3 cm; bracts triangular, ca. 1 mm. Perianth urceolate, yellow, ca. 3 mm in diam., tomentulose abaxially; lobes 4, ovate-triangular, ca. 0.5 mm, recurved. Filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers broadly ovoid. Disk scales 4, ovate, apex acute. Ovary cylindric; style ca. 1 mm, persistent; stigma capitate, 4-lobed. Drupe ellipsoidal, 1.2–1.5 × 0.7–1 cm, orange-red when mature, glabrous, apex mucronate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Deep Water Bay, New Territories, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2453, 3062; HK sheet 38774.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; S & SE Asia, Australia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Oct. – Dec.; fruiting: Jan.–Apr.

Canthium dicoccum (Gaertn.) Merr. 魚骨木（鐵矢米）
Philipp. J. Sci. 35(1): 8. 1928.
Canthium dicoccum (Gaertn.) Teysm. & Binn., Cat. Hort. Bog. 1866, nom. invalid.
Canthium didymum C. F. Gaertn., Suppl. Carp. 94, t. 196. 1806; FHK 159. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.
Psydrax dicoccos Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 125, t. 26, fig. 2. 1788

Shrubs or small trees, to 15 m tall, spineless. Branchlets dark brown, glabrous. Leaves opposite, leathery; petioles 8–15 mm; stipules 3–5 mm, with a broad base, apex acute or acuminate; leaf blade ovate or elliptic or ovate‑lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, obtuse or acute, glabrous, shining on both surfaces when dry; lateral veins slender, 3–5 on each side of midvein. Cymes axillary, loose and often many‑flowered, short‑pedunculate, shorter than the subtending leaves. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1–1.2 mm, apex truncate or inconspicuously 5‑toothed. Corolla greenish white or yellowish; tube ca. 3 mm, tomentose on the throat; lobes 4 or 5, oblong, slightly shorter than the tube. Drupes obovate or obovate‑ellipsoidal, 6 – 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 319, 1415; HK sheet 39115.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang; Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent, Australia.
Ecology: Ravines, forests and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.

Canthium horridum Blume 豬肚木（小葉鐵矢米）
Catalogus 45. 1823; Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 16: 966. 1926; FHK 159. 1861; FYN 15: 199, pl. 40: 13 – 15. 2003; FGD 6: 195. 2005.
Canthium parvifolium auct. non Roxb.: FKH 132. 1912.

Shrubs, 2–3 m tall, armed with straight axillary thorns. Young shoots ± pubescent. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 2– 3 mm, ± pubescent; stipules 2–3 mm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, ± pubescent abaxially, at least when young; lateral veins slender, 2 – 3 on each side of midvein. Flowers small, sessile or short‑pedicellate, solitary or clustered in axils of leaves. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1 – 1.5 mm, apex with minute, undulate teeth. Corolla white; tube short, ca. 2 mm, glabrous outside, with retrorse beard on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, ca. 3 mm, apex acute. Drupes globular or didymous, 1–2 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1152.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, Malesia and Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Capillipedium assimile (Steud.) A. Camus 硬稈子草（竹枝細柄草）
Fl. Indo-Chine. 7: 314. 1922; FFJ 6: 268, fig. 240. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 152, pl. 36: 1–6, 77: 1. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 530. 2000; FOC 22: 606. 2006; FGD 9: 495. 2009.
Andropogon montanus Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 271. 1820; FHK 423. 1861.
Andropogon assimilis Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 397. 1854; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms hard, 1.5–3.5 m tall, geniculate at base. Leaf sheaths glabrous, bearded at mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–15 × 0.2–0.6 cm, glabrous or hispidulous, base tapering, apex setaceously acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm, dry membranous, truncate or obtuse. Panicle open, branches fascicles; branches pilose in axils; rachis internodes and pedicels long-ciliate, fragile. Sessile spikelet oblong, dorsally compressed, callus bearded; lower glume obtuse, scabrous or hispidulous, 2-keeled, ciliatehispid on keel, 2–5-veined; upper glume as long as lower glume, 3-veined; lower lemma oblong, 2/3 upper lemma length, obtuse; upper lemma linear, an awn of 0.6–1.5 cm long arising from the apex. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, linear-lanceolate, up to twice length of sessile spikelet.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 2283; HK sheet 41992.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Capillipedium parviflorum (R. Br.) Stapf 細柄草（吊絲草）
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 169. 1917; FHN 4: 475, fig. 1261. 1977; FFJ 6: 269, fig. 241. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 151, pl. 36: 7–11, 76: 4. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 531, pl. 225. 2000; FOC 22: 606. 2006; FGD 9: 495, fig. 261. 2009.
Holcus parviflorus R. Br., Prodr. 199. 1810.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or slightly decumbent at base, 30–150 cm tall; nodes shortly bearded. Leaf sheaths shorter or longer than internode, glabrous or pilose, ciliate at mouth; leaf blades linear, 10–30 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous or hispid, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule dry membranous, 0.5–1.5 mm. Panicle oblong; branches fasciculate, pilose in axils; racemes usually composed of triads, occasionally with 1–2 additional spikelet pairs; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2 the length of sessile spikelet, shortly ciliate at base. Sessile spikelet bisexual, oblong, 3–4 mm; lower glume shallowly concave between veins, 4-veined, margins keeled, hispidulous above middle keel, apex narrowly obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as lower glume, slightly scabrous on keel, acute, 3-veined, upper margins ciliate; lower lemma 1/4–1/3 glume length, obtuse or dentate; upper lemma linear, tipped with an awn of 1–1.5 cm. Pedicellate spikelet equal to the sessile spikelet and often staminate, or smaller and barren.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1866; P. S. Choi 107; Y. W. Lam 2171.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujain, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Grassy field on hillslopes, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Capparis acutifolia Sweet 獨行千里（尖葉槌果藤）
Hort. Brit. (ed. 2) 585. 1830; FGD 1: 89, fig. 100. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 2: 735. photo 322. 1996; FRPS 32: 498. 1999.
Capparis membranacea Gardn. & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 241. 1849; FHK 18. 1831; FKH 35. 1912.

Scandent shrub, glabrous, or sometimes with caducous yellowish short hairs on young shoots and petioles, with or without spines. Leaves membranous or slightly leathery; petioles 5–7 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, very variable in size, 4 –15(–19.5) × (0.8 –)1– 4(– 6.3) cm, base acute or cuneate, sometimes rounded, apex acuminate, glabrous, yellowish green when dry. Flowers white, solitary, borne a little above axils of leaves, often 2–4 together in a vertical row on flowering branches. Pedicels 1–1.5 cm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 5 –7 × 3 – 4 mm, outer ones glabrous, inner ones with caducous yellowish hairs when young. Petals oblong, ca. 1 × 0.3 cm. Stamens 20 –30. Gynophore 1.5 –2.5 cm, glabrous. Ovary ovoid or conical, glabrous. Fruit subglobose, 1–2.5 × 1–1.5 cm, usually with a short beak at apex.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. HK sheet 208, 212, 10395, 38797.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Capparis membranacea was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Capparis membranacea was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Capparis cantoniensis Lour. 廣州槌果藤
Fl. Cochinch. 331. 1790; FGZ 107. 1956; Jacobs, Fl. Mal. 1. 6: 76. 1960; FHN 1: 349. 1964; FGD 1: 88, fig. 97. 1987; FRPS 32: 526. 1999.
Capparis pumila Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 260. 1852; FHK 18. 1861; FKH 36. 1912.

Scandent shrub. Branches slender, with small recurved spines, glabrous or slightly pubescent on the upper part. Leaves subleathery; petiole 4– 6(–10) mm, pubescent; leaf blade oblongovate to oblong-lanceolate, 5 –10(–12) × 1.5– 4 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex usually acuminate, glabrous. Panicles consisting of few-flowered umbels, terminal or axillary. Pedicels 4–10 mm, puberulent. Flowers white, ca. 1 cm in diam. Sepals 4–5 × 2.5 –3 mm, with white membranous margins. Petals obovate or oblong, 4–6 × 1.5–2.5 mm. Stamens 20–45; filaments 8–15 mm. Gynophore 6–8(–12) mm. Ovary ovoid or conical, glabrous. Fruit globose, 6 –10(–15) mm in diam., apex rounded, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau, Po Toi. K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 38775, 40219).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.; fruiting: Jun.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Capparis pumila was collected from “the Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in January 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Capparis pumila was collected from “the Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in January 1850.

records.text:
Capsella bursa-pastoris (L.) Medik. 薺菜
Pfl.-Gatt. 85. 1792; FHK 16. 1861; FKH 35. 1912; FGD 3: 34. 1995; FOC 8: 43. 2001.
Thlaspi bursa-pastoris L., Sp. Pl. 2: 647. 1753.

Annual or biennial herb, 10–15 cm tall, glabrous or with simple or furcate hairs. Stems erect, simple or branched. Basal leaves rosulate, lyrate, up to 12 cm, terminal lobes ovate to oblong, lateral lobes 3–8 pairs. Petioles 5–40 mm; cauline leaves narrowly lanceolate or lanceolate up to 6 cm, base auriculate, amplexicaul. Racemes terminal and axillary, up to 20 cm; pedicel 3 – 8 mm. Flowers white, 2.5 mm. Sepals oblong, 1.5–2 mm. Petals ovate, 2–3 mm, shortly clawed. Silicles obtriangular or obcordate-triangular, 5 – 8 mm, flat, apex emarginate, stalk 5–15 mm. Seeds 2-ranked, brownish, oblong, 1 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Ng Tung Chai, Wun Yiu. P. S. Choi 115; Y. S. Lau 81, 1752.
Distribution: Widely distributed in temperate regions.
Ecology: Farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Mar.
Uses: Vegetable, medicinal.

Capsicum annuum L. 辣椒
Sp. Pl. 188. 1753; FHN 3: 469, fig. 861. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 62. 1978; FGD 2: 368. 1991; FOC 17: 313. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 550. 1998.

Annual or perennial herbs, 50–80 cm tall. Stems much branched, woody at base. Leaves alternate or the upper paired or clustered; petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire or obscurely sinuate, sparsely pubescent along midvein on adaxial surface, with tufts of hairs in axils of veins on abaxial surface. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves or branches. Calyx cup‑shaped, obscurely 5‑toothed. Corolla white, 5‑lobed. Stamens 5; anthers blue‑purple. Berry usually red, orange‑yellow, variously shaped.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 21.
Distribution: Native to Mexico and S America; widely cultivated worldwide and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (vegetable), additive (colouring, flavouring).
Notes: Three varieties of this species, C. annuum var. conoides (Mill.) Irish (朝天椒; Photo 103), C. annuum var. fasciculatum (Sturtev.) Irish (簇生椒) and C. annuum var. grossum (L.) Sendtn. (菜椒; Photo 104), are also cultivated.

Notes: Three varieties of this species, C. annuum var. conoides (Mill.) Irish (朝天椒; Photo 103), C. annuum var. fasciculatum (Sturtev.) Irish (簇生椒) and C. annuum var. grossum (L.) Sendtn. (菜椒; Photo 104), are also cultivated.

records.text:
Carallia brachiata (Lour.) Merr. 竹節樹
Philipp. J. Sci. 15(3): 249. 1919 [1920]; FHN 2: 48. 1965; FRPS 52(2): 139. 1983; FGD 1: 112. 1987.
Diatoma brachiata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 296. 1790.
Carallia integerrima DC., Prodr. 3: 33. 1828; FHK 111. 1861; FKH 103. 1912.

Tree, 7–10 m tall, with buttresses at base. Branches greyish brown. Stipules 1–2.5 cm. Petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blade elliptic, obovate or oblong, 5–8 × 3–4.5 cm, thinly leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, with sparse, conspicuous purplish red spots abaxially. Inflorescences 1–6 cm; peduncle 0.8–1.2 cm. Flowers shortly pedicellate or sessile; bracteoles 2 or 3, partially connate into a cup. Calyx-lobes 6 or 7, triangular, 3 – 4 mm. Petals white, suborbicular, ca. 1.8 – 2 × 1.5–1.8 mm, apically lacerate. Stamens ca. 2 mm. Ovary globose, ca. 2 mm; style ca. 2 mm; stigma discoid, 4–8-lobed. Fruit subglobose, ca. 4–6 mm in diam., glossy, apex with persistent calyx-lobes. Seeds reniform or oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1375, 2023; C. H. Tsou 1876.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; SE Asia, N Australia, Madagascar, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Winter to spring; fruiting: Spring to summer.

Cardamine flexuosa With. 彎曲碎米薺
Arr. Brit. Pl. (ed. 3) 3: 578. 1796; FGD 3: 38. 1995; FOC 8: 105. 2001.
Cardamine hirsuta auct. non L.: FHK 16. 1861; FKH 34. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, ca. 30 cm tall, sparsely pubescent. Stems erect, ascending or decumbent branched from base, usually flexuous. Leaves pinnately compound; basal leaves not rosulate; leaflets 3 –7 pairs, ovate, obovate or oblong, 2–5 mm, petiolulate; cauline ones 3–5 pairs, ovate or linear, entire or 1–3-lobed. Racemes terminal; rachis flexuous; pedicles 2–4 mm. Sepals oblong, 1.5– 2.5 mm. Petals white, spathulate, ca. 3.5 mm. Stamens 6, rarely 4. Ovary 18–40-ovuled. Siliques linear, 1.2–2 cm, flat. Seeds brown, oblong, 1 mm, flat, apex narrowly margined or not.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 532; S. P. Lau 26; Y. S. Lau 2095.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian (cultivated); Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal.

Cardiospermum halicacabum L. 倒地鈴（包草）
Sp. Pl. 1: 366. 1753; FHK 46. 1861; FKH 66. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 4, fig. 1. 1985; FFJ 3: 316, fig. 213. 1987; FGD 1: 237, fig. 261. 1987; FTW ed, 2. 3: 601. 1993.
Cardiospermum halicacabum var. microcarpum (Kunth) Blume, Rumphia 3: 185. 1847; FHN 3: 77, fig. 576. 1974.
Cardiospermum microcarpum Kunth, Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 5: 104. 1821.

Herbaceous climber, 1–1.5 m or longer. Stems and branches green, slender, 5–6-sulcate, glabrous or sparsely hairy. Leaves biternate, triangular in outline; petioles 3–4 cm; leaflets subsessile, thinly papery, terminal one obliquely lanceolate or subrhombic, 3–8 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex acuminate; lateral ones slightly smaller, ovate or narrowly elliptic, margin sparsely serrate or pinnately parted, adaxially sparsely villous on midvein and lateral veins, adaxially subglabrous or sparsely pilosulose. Panicles few-flowered, nearly as long as or slightly longer than leaves; peduncles straight, 4–8 cm, tendrils spiral. Petals 4, ciliate, outer 2 ovate, 8–10 mm, inner 2 narrowly elliptic, ca. 2 times as long as outer ones. Petals milky-white, obovate. Stamens (male flowers) nearly as long as or slightly longer than petals; filaments sparsely long villous. Ovary (female flowers) obovoid or sometimes subglobose, pubescent. Capsules brown, pearlike, turbinate-obtriangular or sometimes nearly ellipsoidal, 1.5–3 × 2–4 cm, pubescent. Seeds black, shiny, ca. 5 mm in diam.; hilum green when fresh, white when dry, cordate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Yin Kong, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 237; Y. W. Lam 1793; HK sheet 40714.
Distribution: E, S, SW & N China; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Farmlands and wastelands. Flowering: Summer to autumn; fruiting: Autumn to early winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Carex arisanensis Hayata 阿里山薹草
J. Coll. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 30: 378. 1911 et Icon. Pl. Form. 6: 130, pl. 18. 1916; FTW 5: 349. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 200. 2000; FRPS 12: 348–349. 2000; FGD 8: 388. 2007; FOC 23: 400. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms lateral and borne in axils of leaves, 10–40 cm tall, slender and flaccid, trigonous, smooth, base of culms with short leafy-sheaths. Leaves shorter or longer than the culm, linear, 4–8 mm wide, flat, soft herbaceous. Upper bracts spathe-like, upper part glumaceous to rarely with short lanceolate leaf blade 5–10 mm, sheath less than 2 mm to not exist; lower bracts have longer leaf blade, 1–4 cm, and longer sheaths 2–4 mm. Spikes (2–)3–4, terminal spike staminate, lanceolate-oblong, 5–8 mm, peduncle short, < 2 mm to sessile, very close to the adjacent pistillate spike; lateral spikes all pistillate, oblong to elliptic, 8–10 cm, spikelets very few, 2–3(–4), densely clustered; peduncles of upper spikes short to almost absent, lower spikes with slender and rather flaccid peduncles up to 3 cm long-exserted beyond the bract sheath. Male glumes oblong to elliptic, 3–4 × ca. 1.5 mm, apex broad-acute or obtuse, midrib green, margin broad hyaline. Female glumes ovate-oblong, 3.5–5 × 1.2 mm, apex acute, pale, margin broad hyaline, midrib green. Utricles longer than glumes, ovate-fusiform, trigonous, 6.5–7 mm, glabrous, brown-green, membranous, many-veined, base cuneate, upper part attenuate to a long beak; orifice hyaline, emarginate, 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, obovate-elliptic, trigonous, ca. 3 mm, pale brown; style base not thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1392, 2269; H. G. Ye. et al. 1163, 1168.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Montane hillside forests, usually in wet seepages or streamsides, alt. 600–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.

Carex baccans Nees 漿果薹草
Wight, Contr. Bot. India 122. 1834; S. T. Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 325. 1910; FKH 305. 1912; FHN 4: 337. 1977; FTW 5: 310, pl. 1347. 1978; Flora Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 137, fig. 119: 15, 127, 131i. 1979; FFJ 6: 350. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 200. 2000; FRPS 12: 62, pl. 13: 1–4. 2000; FYN 15: 702, fig. 163: 1–4. 2003; FGD 8: 367. 2007; FOC 23: 288. 2010.

Rhizome woody. Culms central to borne in leave axils, erect and robust, 80–150 cm tall, 0.5–0.6 cm thick, trigonous, glabrous, leafy below middle-part. Leaves both cauline and basal, flat, 8–12 mm wide, glabrous abaxially, scabrid adaxially, papery, basal persistent leaf sheaths red-brown, reticulate. Bracts leafy, longer than inflorescence, long-sheathed; panicle compound, ovate, 10–35 cm; inflorescence branches 3–8, single, oblong to ovate, 5–6 × 3–4 cm, lower 1–3 branches more widely-spaced, axis bluntly triquetrous, nearly glabrous; bractlets glumaceous, lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, leathery, only the basal one with short sheath, others sheathless, awned; peduncles of inflorescence branches rigid, the basal one 12–14 cm, upper ones gradually shorter, usually enclosed in bractlet-sheath; spikes producing from utriculiform cladoprophylls, numerous, cylindrical, 3–6 cm, bisexual and androgynous; male part of spike tenuous, with only few spikelets, 1/2 or 1/3 length of female part; female part with dense and numerous spikelets; male glumes broadly ovate, 3–4.5 × 2–2.5 mm, awned, membranous, chestnut-brown; female glumes broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 2–2.5 mm, awned, papery, purplish brown or chestnutbrown, with 1 green midvein, margins hyaline; utricles obovate-globose or nearly globose, inflated, 3.5–4.5 mm, nearly leathery, red to purplish red when mature, shining, with many vertical veins, upper margins hairy, shortly stipulate at base, shortly beaked at apex, beak mouth minutely bidentate. Achene elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, brown when mature, shortly stipulate at base, apex apiculate; style base not thickened, stigmas 3.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. Y. W. Lam 1310, 1740; HK sheet 13913.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Montane hillside grasslands, alt. 700–900 m. Fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The utricle is berry-like and brightly coloured when ripe. It may be adapted for seed dispersals by birds and mammals.

Carex bodinieri Franch. 濱海薹草
Bull. Soc. Philom. Paris, ser. 8, 7: 85. 1895 et in Nouv. Arch. Mus. Paris 3, ser. 8: 243, 1896; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot, 36: 295. 1903, pro syn. sub C. longipes D. Don; FFJ 6: 349, fig. 311. 1995; FRPS 12: 445, pl. 91: 5 – 7. 2000; FGD 8: 392. 2007; FOC 23: 436. 2010.
Carex brunnea auct. non Thunb.: Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 325. 1910; FKH 306. 1912.
Carex longipes auct. non D. Don: FKH 306. 1912.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms tufted or loosely tufted, rather slender, 35–60 cm tall, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, shorter than culm, 1.7–2.8 mm wide, flat, rather stiff, scabrous on both surfaces and margins; sheaths short, usually splitting to base into fibers. Bracts sheathed, sheaths 1.0–3.0 cm, the lower bracts leafy, upper blades reduced to bristle-like. Inflorescence a diffuse and loose compound raceme, lower bracts bear 2(–3) branches, among them usually 1 is compound, with several 2 or more spikes; middle and upper bracts each with 1(–2) spikes, very rarely more; bracts and branches loosely distributed, the lower branches can be up to 10 cm apart, the upper branches closer to each other. Spikes many, androgynous, cylindrical to narrow-lanceolate, 1–2.5 cm, male part range from less than 1/4 of the length for lower spike to nearly 1/2 for the upper spikes, female spikelets 9–12, rather loosely distributed on spikes, peduncle slender and extend out of the sheath by up to 4 cm. Male glume narrowly ovate, 3–6 mm, apex acute, yellowbrown, hyaline, with brown short lines, midrib green 1-veined. Female glumes broad-ovate, 2.8–3 mm, apex acute, muticous or rarely with short awn, membranous, yellow-brown to brown, middle with brown short lines, midrib green 3-veined. Utricle suberect, slightly longer than glume, broad-elliptic, compressed plano-convex, 3.9–4.5 mm, membranous, pale brown to reddishbrown, dorsal side with up to 9 thin veins, glabrous or with sparse hairs towards the margins, upper margins loosely hispid, upper part abruptly contracted into a medium length beak ca. 1.3 mm, base gradually contracted to a short stipe; orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, ovate to broad-elliptic, compressed plano-convex, 2–2.3 × 1.3–1.6 mm, yellowish to dark brown; style base slightly thickened; stigmas 2, usually shorter than to occasionally equal to utricle.

Locality: High West, Nam Fung Rd., Magazine Gap, Wan Chai Gap, Pik Uk. S. T. Dunn Ex Herb. Hongk. 7187 (K), S. C. Ng 1552, 2810; HK sheet 42115, 42117.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui; Japan. Ecology: Montane hillside open forests; alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen (Bodinier 1334 (P)) was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island in 1895.

Specimens of this species were reported as Carex brunnea Thunb. previously (S. T. Dunn l.c.; Check List HK Plants 306. 2002; 108. 2004; Corlett et al., Mem. Hong Kong. Nat. Hist. Soc. 23: 113).

Clarke (1903) identified Bodinier 334 from Happy Valley of Hong Kong as C. longipes, which he considered as conspecific with C. bodinieri. Without citing any specimen, FGD 8: 393 also mentioned C. longipes distributed in Hong Kong and “recorded from coastal region of Guangdong”, but this is not mentioned by FRPS and FOC. In this study, I follow the FRPS treatment of considering C. longipes and C. bodinieri different species. I have not noted any specimen of C. longipes in Hong Kong. Bodinier 334 was not examined by me, but it is unlikely to be C. longipes, as the inclusion of Hong Kong into its distribution range results in disjunct distribution for this species. It happens that the specimen cited by Clarke (1903) is very similar to the type specimen of C. bodinieri (Bodinier 1334) in collection number and locality. A possibility is that Bodinier 334 may be a typo mistake of Bodinier 1334.

Carex breviculmis R. Br. 青綠薹草
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 242. 1810; FTW 5: 335. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 150. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 5: 205. 2000; FRPS 12: 161, pl. 33: 1 – 4. 2000; FYN 15: 727. 2003; FGD 8: 376. 2007; FOC 23: 326. 2010.
Carex leucochlora Bunge, Enum. Pl. Chin. Bor. 68. 1833, FFJ 6: 360, fig. 325. 1995.

Rhizome short. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, erect to oblique, ca. 20 cm tall, trigonous, slender. Basal sheaths pale-brown and split into fibers. Leaves longer or shorter than the culm, blades 2–3 mm wide, flat, margins scabrid, papery. Lowest bract leafy, longer than the subtended spikes, sheath ca. 9.2 mm; upper bracts bristle-like, nearly sheathless. Spikes 2–5, upper spikes contiguous, lower spikes more remotely spaced. Terminal spike staminate, oblong, 1–1.2 cm × 2–3 mm, nearly sessile, close to the next lateral spike. Lateral spikes androgynous, but the uppermost lateral spikes is occasionally a short mainly male spike, other lateral spikes are mainly pistillate, oblong-ovate, 8–15 × 3–4 mm wide, spikelets 30 – 50, densely distributed on spikes; peduncles up to 3.5 cm for the lowest spike, to almost absent for the upper spikes. Male glumes obovate-oblong, apex acuminate and shortly mucronate, membranous, pale-yellow. Female glumes oblong, 1.7–2 mm (excluding awn) × ca. 0.8 mm, apex truncate or rounded, midrib 3-veined, excurrent into an awn 0.7–1 mm, membranous, pale greenish to pale yellowish. Utricles nearly equal the glume, obovate, obtusely trigonous, 2.3–2.4 mm, membranous, pale yellowish green, many-veined, upper part densely puberulent, suddenly contracted to a conical beak, orifice emarginate, base attenuate into a short stipe. Achene tightly enveloped, ovate, 1.8 mm, dark brown, apex discoid-annulate; stylebase conically thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Cheung Sheung. S. C. Ng 1081.
Distribution: Widespread from NE through C to S and SW China; India, Myanmar, Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Hillside grasslands, alt. 400 m. Fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Carex canina Dunn 長柄薹草（果柄薹草）
J. Bot. 47: 325. 1910; FKH 305. 1912; FGD 8: 385. 2007.
Carex hastata Kük., Fedde Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 27: 110. 1929, syn. nov.; FRPS 12: 325, pl. 70: 9 – 11. 2000; FOC 23: 394. 2010.
Carex lianchengensis S. Y. Liang et Y. Z. Huang, FFJ 6: 690. 1995, syn. nov.; FRPS 12: 334. 2000 [“lienchengensis”]; FOC 23: 396. 2010.

Rhizome short, woody, covered with fibers of dark brown disintegrating leaf sheath. Culms lateral to tufted and borne in axils of leaves, 25–40 cm tall, slender, trigonous, upper part scabrid, basal sheaths bladeless or having short leaf blade less than 8 cm. Leaves longer than or equal to the culms, linear, 4–6 mm wide, flat, stiff papery, margins scabrid. Bracts short leafy; sheath short, 3–4 mm. Spikes 2–3, cluster towards the top of culms, uppermost lateral spikes almost at the same height as the terminal spike; terminal spike staminate, linear, ca. 1 cm, peduncle short, 3–9 mm; pistillate spikes lateral, oblong-ovate to ovate, 10–15 × 7–10 mm, spikelets very few, only 2–7, but densely distributed on spikes, peduncle short 7–13 mm. Male glumes lanceolate, ca. 3.8 × 1.5 mm, apex obtuse, pale green, midrib green. Female glumes ovate, 5–7 × 2–2.5 mm, apex acute, pale green, 3-veined, green. Utricles longer than the glume, obliquely patent, rhomboid, 7.5–9.2 mm, membranous, yellow-green, glabrous, finely many-veined, base cuneate, upper part abruptly contracted above to a beak 1.5 × 2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, elliptic, trigonous, up to 4.3–5 mm, yellow-brown to black, middle of achene constricted to excavated, base attenuate into a short erect stipe 0.5–1 mm, upper part attenuate into an erect and robust cylindrical beak ca. 1 mm, apex of beak annulate; style-base thickened, stigmas 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 2930, 3054, 3056; Y. W. Lam 1372.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (S. T. Dunn 7154, HK) was collected from Lantau Island in 1909. The author has examined the types of C. canina and C. hastata (Y. L. Keng 2353, PE), and found them similar in their inflorescence, glumes, utricles and achenes, as well as their leaves and growth form. Carex lianchengensis (H. B. Chen, s.n. [Chinese National Herbarium 28928], PE, isotype), is also similar to C. canina in all aspects apart from the culm and leaf length, which are not enough to separate two species, as size varies greatly among specimens of C. canina from Hong Kong. The author has noted small size plants of C. canina in the field comparable to the size of the isotype of C. lianchengensis.

FRPS mentioned that C. lianchengensis differs from C. canina in culm position. However, culm position is not a reliable character for separation of species in the section Rhomboidales Kükenthal to which all these species belong. Species in this section vary within species with respect to the lateral culms position, which may be borne in axils of middle or lateral leaves, as demonstrated in C. manca and C. harlandii.

Carex chinensis Retz. 中華薹草
Retz. Observ. Bot. 3: 42. 1783; FHK 402. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 280. 1903–04; FKH 305. 1912; FFJ 6: 371, fig. 338. 1995; FRPS 12: 314. 2000; FGD 8: 383. 2007; FOC 23: 386. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody, obliquely ascending, covered with brown fibers formed from old disintegrating leaf sheaths. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, oblique to erect, slender, 20–55 cm tall, obtusely trigonous, basal sheaths brown and tinging reddish. Leaves longer than the culm, 3.5–5.5 mm wide, margins scabrid, papery. Bracts with short leaf blade, 8–12 cm, sheath long, 1–3 cm. Spikes 4–5, distant; male spike terminal, narrow-lanceolate to linear, 2.5–3 × 2.5–5.2 mm; peduncle 2–3 cm; lateral, spikes almost completely pistillate 2–3.5 cm × 6–6.5 mm, female spikelets 26 – 75, rather densely distributed on spikes; peduncles erect, slender, 2.5–4.5 cm. Male glumes 4.5–6.5 mm, oblanceolate to oblong, apex with awn, light brown. Female glumes oblong, apex truncate or sometimes emarginate or acuminate, 4.5–5.7 × 0.6–0.9 mm, pale, the midrib extend into a scabrid long awn, 1–2 mm. Utricles slightly shorter than the glume, obliquely patent, rhomboid-elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, membranous, yellow-green, sparsely puberulent, many-veined, upper part abruptly contract into a medium beak, orifice 2-toothed, base attenuate into a stipe. Achenes tightly enveloped, rhomboid, trigonous, 1.7–2.2 × ca. 1 mm wide, upper part broadly acute, beak short, apex annulate or rarely not so; style thickened at base; stigmas 3.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1232, 2351; Y. S. Lau 2703; S. P. Lau 86.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Fairly common in montane hillside open forests, alt. 100–800 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Apr.

Carex cruciata Wahlenb. 十字薹草
Kongl. Vetensk. Acad. Nya Handl. 24: 149. 1803; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 281. 1903-04; FKH 305. 1912; FHN 4: 338. 1977; FTW 5: 310, pl. 1347. 1978; Fl. Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 118, fig. 118: 3a; 124a – d. 1979; FFJ 6: 350 – 51, fig. 313. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 209, pl. 80. 2000; FRPS 12: 72, pl. 14: 9 – 11. 2000; FYN 15: 707, fig. 165: 6 – 8. 2003; FGD 8: 368. 2007; FOC 23: 291. 2010.
Carex benghalensis Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 572. 1832; FHK 401. 1861.

Rhizome thick, woody, with stolons. Culms central to borne in leave axils, erect, 40–90 cm tall, shorter than or ± equal to leaves, 2–4 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves mainly basal, a few cauline, flat, 4–8 mm wide, scabrid abaxially and adaxially along midrib, veins and margins, papery, persistent sheaths dark brown, fibriform. Bracts leafy, longer than inflorescence branches, long-sheathed towards base; panicle compound; inflorescence branches ovate-triangular, 4–10 × 3–6 cm wide, usually single; peduncles of inflorescence branches rigid, smooth, trigonous to flattened, lowest one 10–18 cm, upper ones gradually shorter; inflorescence axis trigonous to slightly flattened, covered in dense short hairs; bractlets glumaceous and awned, 0.7–3.0 mm, hairy abaxially; cladoprophylls utriculiform, without flower, several-veined and hairy abaxially; spikes many, all producing from cladoprophylls, patent horizontally, 4–17 mm, bisexual, androgynous; male part of spike about one-third to as long as female part; male glumes lanceolate, 2.5–3.0 mm, acuminate, mucronate, membranous, pale brownish white, with dense brown spots and short lines; female glumes ovate, ca. 2 mm, membranous, apex obtuse to acute, shortly awned ca. 0.4 mm, 3-veined. Utricles longer than glumes, elliptic, inflated trigonous, 3–3.2 mm, pale brownish white, with brown spots and short lines, smooth or upper part loosely hairy, with several raised veins, nearly sessile, apex attenuate into medium beak about 1/3 length of utricle, hairy or glabrous laterally, beak opening obliquely truncate. Achenes ovateelliptic, trigonous, 1.5–1.8 mm, dark brown when mature; base of style slightly thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2127; S. C. Ng 2229; L. T. Lo 161.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, India, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Madagascar.
Ecology: Hillside grasslands, roadsides, alt. 50–900 m. Fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The ripe utricle is fleshy and white. It may be adapted for dispersals by birds.

Carex cryptostachys Brongn. 隱穗薹草
Duperrey, Voy. Monde, Phanerog. 152. 1832; FHK 403. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 281. 1903 – 04; FKH 306. 1912; FHN 4: 340. 1977; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 148, fig. 120: 26. 1979; FFJ 6: 358, fig. 322. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 209, pl. 81. 2000; FRPS 12: 141, pl. 29: 1–5. 2000; FYN 15: 723, fig. 169: 1–5. 2003; FGD 8: 372. 2007; FOC 23: 317. 2010.

Rhizome oblique, woody, covered with dark brown fibrous remains of basal sheaths. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, slightly pendent to oblique, slender, 10–25 cm tall, slender and weak, flattened trigonous. Leaves longer than or as long as the culms, blades 3–16 mm wide, flat, smooth on both surfaces, slightly scabrid along margins, stiff papery. Bracts bristle-like, sheath 4–8 mm and spathe-like. Spikes 6–10, all androgynous, oblong to cylindrical, 8–25 mm, spikelets rather loose; male part short, 2–4 mm; peduncle 4–8 mm, only slightly longer than sheath, slender. Female glumes ovate-oblong to ovate, 2–2.3 mm, pale-brown to yellow-green, the midrib green, apex acute, mucronate to acuminate. Utricles distinctly longer than the glume, 3-ribbed longitudinally, elliptic to oblongfusiform, obscurely trigonous or slightly flattened, 3–3.8 mm, membranous, yellow-green to pale yellow, puberulent above, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe 0.5–1 mm, attenuate above into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achene 2.2–2.5 mm; shape is either trigonous rhombic or trigonous but flattened dorsiventually into elliptic-fusiform shape; faces excavated both at upper and lower parts, and angles excavated at middle; yellowish to dark brown; style-base curved and persistent; stigmas 3.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1206; Y. S. Lau, 3037; S. C. Ng 1268, 2917; Y. W. Lam 1367; HK sheet 13995.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Common in almost all forest habitats in Hong Kong, occasionally also found in rock crevices along streamsides of steep ravine, alt. 50–800 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Notes: Two extreme forms with some intermediates were observed among Hong Kong specimen. The trigonous form characterised by trigonous rhombic urtricle and achene, with excavation at the middle of achene angles and on all faces is close to the description of FRPS and FTW (e.g. HK sheet 13995; H. C. Tang 1206). It is usually found in forest habitat with relatively thick soil. The flattened form is characterized by dorsiventrally flattened utricle and secondarily flattened trigonous achene, excavation is shallow or even absent (e.g. Y. S. Lau 3037; S. C. Ng 1268, 2917). It generally has narrower and shorter leaves, and usually found in rock crevices along streamsides of steep ravine. Intermediates with less obvious dorsiventrally flattened utricle and achene and intermediate constriction at the achene angle had been observed in both Hong Kong (Y. W. Lam 1367) and Hainan (S.K. Lau 606 (PE) and Y. Zhong 4198 (PE)) specimens.

Carex filicina Nees 蕨狀薹草
Wight, Contrib. Bot. India, 123. 1834; FHN 4: 339. 1977; Fl. Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 122, fig. 118: 4. 1979; FFJ 6: 351, fig. 314. 1995; FRPS 12: 75, pl. 15: 6 – 9. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 212. 2000; FYN 15: 704, fig. 164: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 8: 369. 2007; FOC 23: 292. 2010.

Rhizome thick, woody. Culms borne in leave axils, loosely tufted, oblique to erect, 40–90 cm tall, shorter than leaves or rarely longer, 2–2.5 mm thick, trigonous, glabrous. Leaves flat, 4–10 mm wide, glabrous on both sides, papery; sheaths persistent, purplish red or purplish brown, split into fibers towards base. Bracts leafy, longer than inflorescence branches, long-sheathed; panicle compound, 20–50 cm; inflorescence branches 4–8, triangular-ovate, 4–8 cm wide, 3–5 cm, single, rarely binate; peduncles of inflorescence branches tenuous, trigonous, lowest one 10–20 cm, upper ones gradually shorter, sparsely hairy on ridges; rachis sharply trigonous to slightly flattened, short hairy; bractlets glumaceous, 1–1.5 mm, apex with or without awn; cladoprophylls utriculiform, without flower; spikes all producing from cladoprophylls, numerous, patent or slightly patent, oblong or oblong-cylindrical, 5–15 mm, bisexual, androgynous, male part of spike shorter than female part, with 3–7 spikelets; female part with 2–16 spikelets. Male glumes lanceolate, 2–3 mm, acuminate, membranous, brown or reddish brown; female glumes ovate or lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, membranous, acuminate or acute, brown, reddish brown or pale brown with reddish brown spots and short lines, glabrous, with 1 midvein. Utricles membranous, brown or reddish brown, or wholly pale brown with reddish brown spots and short lines, elliptic or narrowly elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.4 mm, glabrous, with 2 lateral veins and several fine veins abaxially, nearly sessile, apex contracted into long excurved beak about 1/2 or more the length of utricle, beak opening obliquely truncate. Achenes narrow elliptic to rounded-rhomboid, trigonous, ca. 1.6 mm, yellowish brown to dark brown when mature; base of style not thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Nei Lak Shan, Shek Pik. Y. W. Lam 1395; S. C. Ng 1593; J. C. Shaw 105.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Margins of hillside forests and grasslands, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Carex funhuangshanica F. T. Wang & Tang ex P. C. Li 鳳凰山薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 37(2): 168, fig. 7. 1999; FRPS 12: 179, pl. 35; 9 – 11. 2000 [“fenghuangshanica”]; FOC 23: 332. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms borne in leave axils, oblique, slender and rather flaccid, 15–25 cm tall, 0.8 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves longer than the culm, flat, 1.5–4 mm wide, stiff papery, margins smooth to slightly scabrid, persistent sheaths brown and spilt into fibers. Bracts leafy and longer than the inflorescence, up to 12 cm, lowest bract not different with sterile leaves; sheath 2–7 mm. Spikes (1–)2, lowest spike may be borne near the base of culm, androgynous, oblong, 1–2 cm × 4 – 5 mm, peduncle slender, ca. 1 cm; male part 1/4–1/2 the length spike, male spikelets 8 – 13, rather densely distributed on the male part. Male glumes ovate, 2.2–2.6 mm, apex obtuse, papery, yellowish green to yellowish brown, abaxial side with 1 green midrib and several weak veins. Female glumes ovate or broad-ovate, 2.5–3 mm, apex obtuse, leathery, abaxial side with 1 green midrib and several weak vein, yellowish green on both sides, margins white hyaline. Utricles ovate to broad-elliptic, trigonous, 4.3–4.9 mm, greenish to yellowish brown, leathery, glabrous, each side with several robust veins, margins narrowly winged and ciliate, upper part attenuate into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed, base cuneate and nearly sessile. Achene ovate to broad-elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, brownish, base attenuate into a short stipe, apex without beak; style-base thickened conically, stigmas 3.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Castle Peak, Mui Wo, Yi O, San Tau. S. C. Ng 1333; Y. W. Lam 1495; HK sheet 14008.
Distribution: Guangxi.
Ecology: Lowland sparse forests, alt. 10–200 m. Fruiting: May – Jun.
Notes: The species was reported as Carex speciosa Kunth previously (Check List HK Plants 308. 2002; 109. 2004).

Carex harlandii Boott 長囊薹草
Ill. Gen. Carex 2: 87, pl. 255. 1860; FHK 403. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 289. 1903–04; FKH 306. 1912; FFJ 6: 371, fig. 339. 1995; FRPS 12: 323, pl. 65: 1–4. 2000; FGD 8: 384. 2007; FOC 23: 393. 2010.
Carex anomocarya Nelmes, Kew Bull. 1950: 202. 1951; FHN 4: 344. 1977; Fl. Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 144, fig. 120: 22, fig. 128. 1979.

Rhizome thick and woody, covered with fibers of disintegrating leaf sheath. Culms lateral or borne in axils of leaves, oblique to erect, 30–90 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, basal leaves 2–5, ranging from short and sheath-like to long leaf-like equal to culms. Leaves of sterile ramets longer than the culm, broad-linear, 10–25 cm wide, flat, base plicate, upper margins slightly scabrous, papery, apex acuminate. Bracts leafy, with sheath, lower bracts longer than the subtended spikelets, becoming shorter for upper bracts. Spikes (2–)3–4 at the upper part of culm, upper spikes close, more distally spaced down the culm. Male spike terminal, linear-cylindrical, 4.5–7 cm, peduncle short to almost absent. Lateral spikes androgynous, pistillate on the lower four-fifths or more, cylindrical, 5–8 cm × 8–10 mm wide, spikelets 28–70, rather densely distributed on spikes, peduncles 5 cm or less. Female glumes ovate-oblong or oblong, ca. 6 mm (including awn), pale-green, 3-veined, midrib excurrent into a scabrous awn ca. 1.8 mm. Utricles longer than the glumes, 8–9 mm (including beak), obliquely patent, elliptic-rhomboid, papery, brown, yellow-green or green, glabrous, many-veined, lower part attenuate toward base, upper part attenuate into a long beak 3.3–3.8 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, rhomboid-elliptic, trigonous, 5–5.7 mm, yellow-brown to dark brown, middle of the achene constricted on angles, base attenuate into a curve stipe, upper part attenuate to a robust and erect cylindrical beak, apex of beak annulate; style base thickened conical, stigmas 3.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Shek O, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Soko Islands. Y. W. Lam 1393, 2085; J. C. Shaw 365.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Fujian, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hubei; Myanmar, Thailand, N Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Common in hillside and lowland forests, alt. 10–700 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Harland from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Carex ligata Boott ex Benth. 香港薹草（顯柱薹草）
FHK 402. 1861; Boott, Ill. Gen. Carex 4: 211. 1867; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 294. 1903–04; Kük., Pflanzenr. 38(IV, 20): 473, fig. 75G–K. 1909; FKH 306. 1912; FRPS 12: 146. 2000 pro parte, excluding C. nexa Boott ex Benth.; FGD 8: 374. 2007; FOC 23: 319. 2010 pro parte, excluding C. nexa Boott ex Benth.
Carex hongkongensis Franch., Nouv. Arch. Mus. Paris III 10: 93. 1898.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms borne in leave axils, erect, 25–40 cm tall, slender, obtusely trigonous, smooth, basal sheaths dark brown and split into fibers. Leaves longer than the culm, 3–5 mm wide, flat, abaxial surface slightly scabrid, margins scabrid, papery. Bracts leafy, 2–3 cm, shorter than the subtended spikes; sheath brownish to greenish, 0.5–1 cm. Spikes 3–4, remote and ± regularly spaced on the stem; male spike terminal, narrowly cylindrical, 3–4 cm, ca. 1 – 1.3 mm thick, peduncle 3–4 cm; pistillate spikes lateral, cylindrical, 1–2 cm × 3.5–4 mm, spikelets 10–40, rather densely distributed on spikes, peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm, slender. Male glumes oblong, apex rounded, 2.4–2.9 × 1–1.3 mm, lower margins clasping the spike rachis to almost amplexicaul, pale greenish with broad hyaline margin and green midrib. Female glumes obovate-oblong, apex acute to obtuse, 2.2–2.8 mm, greenish with broad hyaline margin and 1–3 green midribs. Utricles longer than the glumes, rhombic, trigonous, 3–3.3 mm, membranous, puberulent above, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe, upper part cuspidate into a beak 0.3–0.4 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, rhombic, trigonous, 2.1–2.4 mm; upper part of the achene form into a ivory-coloured stout, cylindrical crown 0.3–0.4 mm, shallowly concave at top; faces slightly depressed to excavated at both the upper and lower part, middle of achene raised into angle longitudinally, base attenuate into a stipe ca. 0.2 mm; style base thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 1233, 2916; HK sheet 42104.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Hillside and ravine forests, alt. 300–700 m. Fruiting: Mar.–May.
Notes: The syntype specimens (Harland 790 ex parte; C. Wright 8, 78, 79, & 602; Wilford 263, all deposited at K) were collected from Hong Kong. FRPS also mentioned this species distributed in Anhui province. The author had examined the Anhui specimen at PE (S. W. Su 87033), and found it very different from the above type specimens with respect to its achene and male spikelet.

Carex maculata Boott 斑點果薹草
Trans. Linn. Soc. 20: 128. 1846; Hayata, Icon. Plant Formos. 10: 60. 1921; FTW 5: 359, pl. 1360. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 157, fig. 121: 39. 1979; FFJ 6: 354, fig. 317. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 220, pl. 84. 2000; FRPS 12: 140, pl. 28: 1–4. 2000; FGD 8: 372. 2007; FOC 23: 317. 2010.

Rhizome slender and woody. Culms borne in leave axils, oblique to erect, 40–50 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, with a few brown leafless sheath at the base. Leaves equal to or shorter than culm, sheathed, blades 3–6 mm wide, flat, smooth but slightly scabrid along leaf margins and toward apex, herbaceous. Bracts sheathed and leafy, longer than inflorescences, sheath up to 4 cm for the lowest spikes, getting shorter towards the terminal of the inflorescence. Spikes 3–4, the lowest spike remote, the others congregated towards top of culm; terminal spike staminate, linear-cylindrical, 1.2–2.5 cm, peduncle short (3 mm) to almost obsolete; lateral spikes pistillate, oblong-cylindrical to cylindrical, 1.5–2.5 cm, spikelets dense, the lower spikes has rather long peduncle up to 5 cm, peduncle becoming shorter (to 3 mm) for higher spikes. Male glumes oblong-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, obtuse, sometimes mucronate, membranous, with 3 longitudinal green veins. Female glumes oblong-ovate to ovate, 1.5–1.7 mm, acute to obtuse, membranous, yellowish brown with brown short lines. Utricles borne obliquely, longer than glume, broad-obovate to broad-elliptic, trigonous but slightly flattened dorsiventrally, 2.1–2.5 mm, membranous, brown, reddish brown to dark-purple, densely papillate, 3–5-veined on each side, base attenuate to cuneate, apex abruptly contracted into a short beak, orifice subtruncate to slightly emarginate. Achene tightly enveloped in utricle, broad-obovate to broad-elliptical, trigonous, 1.5–1.7 mm, yellowish brown to pale yellow or pale brown, base abruptly contracted to a short stipe, apex with a short curved style base, style base not thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Shing Mun Arboretum, Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 13584 (K); S. C. Ng 1309; HK sheet 42078.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, open hillside forests, alt. 300–900 m. Fruiting: Mar.–May
Notes: A distinctive species characterised by reddish brown female spikelets. The leaves, although erect, are rather soft in texture and resemble that of wetland grasses.

Carex manca Boott ex Benth. 彎柄薹草（紅苞薹草）
FHK 402. 1861; Boott, Ill. Gen. Carex 4: 131, t. 425. 1867; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 297. 1903–04; FKH 306. 1912; FFJ 6: 372. 1995; FRPS 12: 319. 2000; X. F. Jing et al., J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 22(1): 50. 2004; FGD 8: 384. 2007; FOC 23: 391. 2010.

Rhizome thick and short, woody, covered with brown disintegrating leaf sheath. Culms lateral or borne in axils of leaves at the outside, oblique, slender, 30–70 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, base of culms with leafless sheathes. Basal leaves shorter than the culms (7–10 cm) or absent; leaves of sterile ramets longer than the culms, 6–8.5 mm wide, flat, leaf base plicate, papery, upper margins scabrid, adaxial side pale green. Bracts with short leaf blade, 1 cm or less, sheath loose, 1–2.5 cm. Spikes 2–3; male spike terminal, linear-cylindrical, 3.5–4.5 cm, borne on long peduncle 5.5–7.5 cm; lateral spikes androgynous, female for the lower half to two-thirds, oblong-cylindrical, 2–3 cm, female spikelets 12–18, rather loosely distributed on spikes, peduncles less than 7 cm. Male glumes oblanceolate-oblong, ca. 7 mm × 2–2.4 mm, apex acute, pale to yellow-brown, hyaline, midrib 3-veined green. Female glumes oblonglanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, ca. 5.5 mm, apex acute to rounded, or rarely truncate or emarginate, pale to yellowish, 3-veined, green; midrib extend into a short mucronate point or rarely with an awn to 1.2 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, rhomboid-elliptic, trigonous, 6–6.5 mm, membranous, many-veined, yellow-green, upper part sparsely puberulent and abruptly contracted above to a smooth long beak ca. 2 mm, orifice 2-toothed, base cuneate into a short beak. Achenes tightly enveloped, yellow-brown to dark brown, ovate to broad-elliptic, 3–4 mm (including beak), trigonous, angles constricted at the middle, upper part abruptly contracted into a cylindrical beak which is often curved, base abruptly end in a curved stipe; stigmas 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. S. C. Ng 1344; HK sheet 42076, 42077.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hubei.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 200–500 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Harland 790 ex parte (K)) was collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Carex nemostachys Steud. 條穗薹草（線穗薹草）
Flora 29: 23. 1846 et Synops. Cyper. 218. 1855; FHN 4: 341. 1977; FTW 5: 351. 1978; FFJ 6: 367, fig. 334. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 223. 2000; FRPS 12: 285, pl. 58: 1 – 3. 2000; FGD 8: 380, fig. 210. 2007; FOC 23: 374. 2010.

Rhizomes thick, sometimes stoloniferous. Culms 40–90 cm tall, erect, robust and stiff, trigonous, upper part scabrid, basal sheaths disintegrating into yellow-brown fibers. Leaves slightly longer than the culms, 4–7 mm wide, stiff, thick papery to leathery, lower part plicate, becoming flat towards upper part, veins and margins scabrid. Bracts sheathless, lower bracts leafy and longer than subtended spikes, 10–17 cm, upper bracts reduced to bristle shorter than spikes. Spikes 5–8, contiguous towards the top of culm, becoming more spaced towards middle of culm; male spike terminal, cylindrical-linear, 6–8 cm, peduncle short to almost obsolete; female spikes lateral, cylindrical, 5–8 cm × 2.5–3 mm, female spikelets very abundant, more than 100, and rather densely distributed on the long spikes, peduncle short for the lower spikes, almost absent for upper spikes. Male glumes ca. 5 mm, linear to narrow-lanceolate, margins scabrid and with rough hairs, 1–3-veined yellowish. Female glumes 3.5–4.5 × ca. 0.4 mm, narrow-lanceolate, apex with awn, margins of awn scabrid, membranous, pale-greyish, 1–3-veined. Utricles patent, curved outward away from rachis, slightly shorter than glume (including awn), ovate or broad-ovate, obtusely trigonous, 3–3.6 mm, membranous, brown, few-veined, hispidulous, base cuneate, upper part abruptly contracted to a slender, recurved beak, orifice obliquely truncate to minutely 2-toothed. Achene loosely enveloped, broad-obovate to broad-elliptical, trigonous, 1.8–2.0 mm, brownish yellow to brown; style base not thickened, stigmas 3.
