Locality: Sha Lo Tung, Fo Tan. H. C. Tang 2297; Y. S. Lau 3080; HK sheet 36026.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Bengladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Japan.
Ecology: Streamsides, wet places under forests, open grassy abandoned farmlands, alt. ca. 200 m. Fruiting: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.

Carex nexa Boott ex Benth. 聯結薹草
FHK 402. 1861; Boott, Ill. Gen. Carex 4: 194. 1867; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 300. 1903–04; FKH 306. 1912; FRPS 12: 211. 2000 pro syn. sub C. ligata Boott ex Benth.; FGD 8: 374. 2007; FOC 23: 319. 2010 pro syn. sub C. ligata Boott ex Benth.
Carex ligata Boott ex Benth. var. nexa (Boott ex Benth.) Kük., Pflanzenr. 38(IV, 20): 474. 1909.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms borne in leave axils, 30–50 cm tall, oblique to erect, slender, obtusely trigonous to flattened trigonous, smooth, basal sheaths dark brown and split into fibers. Leaves longer than or equal to the culm, 3–4.5 mm wide, flat, smooth dorsally and slightly scabrid along margins, papery. Bracts leafy, ca. 5 cm and longer than subtended spikes for lower bracts, becoming shorter and bristle-like towards top of culms; sheath greenish, 5–25 mm, getting shorter towards top of culms. Spikes 3–5, rather remote, regularly spaced; terminal spike staminate, linear, 5–6 cm × 1.8–2.2 mm, peduncle 2–3 cm; lateral spikes pistillate or androgynous, cylindrical, 2–3.5 cm × 3.5–3.9 mm, spikelets 18–35, and fairly densely distributed on spikes, peduncle slender 6–40 cm, getting shorter towards top of culm. Male glumes oblanceolate to oblong-obovate, apex acute, 6.7–7.5 × 1.3–1.4 mm, yellowish to brownish, hyaline, 1–3-veined at the middle, midrib brown. Female glumes oblong, 3.1–3.6 × 0.9–1.1 mm, apex acute, acuminate to shortly awned, pale yellowish green to brownish, midrib brown. Utricles longer than the glume, slightly curved outward from the rachis, ellipticfusiform, trigonous, 3.2–3.7 × 0.9–1 mm, membranous, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe, gradually attenuate above to a beak ca. 0.5 mm, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, elliptic-fusiform, trigonous, 2.1–2.3 mm; upper part of the achene form into an ivory-coloured, cylindrical crown 0.1–0.2 mm, shallowly concave to flat at top; faces slightly depressed at both the upper and lower part, middle of achene ridges excavated, base attenuate into a stipe ca. 0.2 mm; style base thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, D’Aguilar Peak, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Tung Lung Chau, Shek Pik, Ngong Ping (Lantau Island). S. C. Ng 1169; HK sheet 8219, 14015, 42197.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimens (C. Harland 790 ex parte (K); C. Wright 100, 607 (K)) were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s. This species was treated as a variety of C. ligata by Kükenthal (1909) FRPS and FOC have considered it a synonym of C. ligata. I have examined the type specimens of these two species at K, and found their differences are significant enough to be considered as different species. The achene of C. ligata is rhombic and without excavation at the middle of the achene. The male spikelet of C. ligata is narrowcylindrical, and the male glumes are greenish in colour and much shorter than that of C. nexa.

Carex phacota Spreng. 鏡子薹草
Syst. Veg. 3: 826. 1826; FKH 306. 1912; FHN 4: 341. 1977; FTW 5: 365. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 170, fig. 122: 52, 132: c. 1979; FFJ 6: 346, fig. 307. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 225. 2000; FRPS 12: 431. 2000; FYN 15: 782. 2003; FGD 8: 391, fig. 212. 2007; FOC 23: 431. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms central, with basal leaves, 50–70 cm tall, acute-trigonous, base with yellow green to yellowishbrown sheaths, which splitting into reticulate fibers. Leaves longer or shorter than the culm, 2–5 mm wide, flat, margins slightly revolute, base plicate. Lower bracts leaf-like, longer than spikes, sheath absent to very short, ca. 2 mm, upper bracts bristle-like. Spikes 3–5, close to each other, pendent to somewhat extent; male spike terminal, linear-cylindrical, 3–6 cm × 2–2.5 mm wide, peduncle 2–2.5 cm; lateral spikes pistillate, often pendent, long-cylindrical, 2.5–6.5 cm × 3–4.5 mm, spikelets 100–120 and very densely distributed. Male glumes oblong to lanceolate, ca. 2.5 (awn excluded) × 0.5 mm, apex emarginate to obtuse, with an awn ca. 0.5 mm. Female glumes oblong, 2–2.9 mm, (awn excluded), apex truncate or emarginate, pale and hyaline with rusty dots and short lines, midrib green 3-veined, extend into a scabrous awn 0.9–1.2 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, broad-ovate or elliptic, 2–2.5 × 1.7–1.8 mm, biconvex, densely papillose, greenish brown to dark brown, upper part abruptly contracted above to a short beak ca. 0.2 mm, the orifice entire to slightly emarginate. Achenes rather loosely enveloped, rounded or broadly ovate, ca. 1.8 mm, biconvex, brown, densely papillose; style long, base not thickened; stigmas 2.

Locality: Beacon Hill, Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen, Sha Lo Tung, Sunset Peak. S.Y. Hu 9829 (K); HK sheet 41813, 42081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, N Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, open wetlands and abandoned farmlands, alt. 200–800 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Mar.

Carex pruinosa Boott 粉被薹草
Proc. Linn. Soc. 1: 255. 1858 et Ill. Gen. Carex 1: 65, t. 174. 1858; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 306. 1903 – 04; FKH 306. 1912; FFJ 6: 346, fig. 306. 1995; FRPS 12: 428. 2000; FYN 15: 782. 2003; FGD 8: 390, fig. 211. 2007; FOC 23: 430. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms tufted, 30–80 cm tall, rather stiff, smooth, with red-brown sheaths at base. Leaves equal to or shorter than the culm, 3–5 mm wide, flat, margins revolute. Bracts leafy, longer than spikes. Spikes 3–5, well-spaced at the upper part of culm, peduncle slender 1.5–4 cm; male spike terminal, occasionally with several male spikelets at apex, narrow-cylindrical, 2–3 mm; lateral spikes male, pendent, sometimes with male flowers at apex, cylindrical, 15–35 × 4–7 mm, male spikelets 50–80 and very densely distributed. Female glumes ovate to oblong, ca. 3.3 × 1.4 mm, apex acuminate with short mucronate tip < 0.5 mm, midrib 3-veined green, hyaline on the two sides, with dense ferruginous dots and short lines. Utricles equal to or slightly longer than the glume, oblongovate, 2.5–3 × 2–2.3 mm, densely papillose and red-brown glandular, base broad-cuneate, abruptly contracted above into a short beak, orifice emarginate. Achenes rather loosely enveloped, broad-ovate, biconvex, ca. 2 × 1.5 mm, yellow-brown; stigmas 2.

Locality: Mount Kellet.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuen, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Bhutan, N Thailand, Indonesia.
Ecology: Ravines, streamsides, grasslands, alt. 50–2500 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Jun.
Notes: Record of this species in Hong Kong was mentioned in C. B. Clarke (1903) and FKH (1912), but no specimen of this species had been deposited in the Hong Kong Herbarium. Although Clarke (1903) had cited a specimen from Mount Kellet (Bodinier 1431), but it was not seen in K. The above description and information are based on FRPS and a Guangdong specimen deposited in HK (HK sheet 14101).

Carex pseudolaticeps Tang & F. T. Wang ex S. Y. Liang 彌勒山薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 36: 536, fig. 3: 1 – 5. 1998; FRPS 12: 326, pl. 67: 1 – 5. 2000 [“pseudo-laticeps”]; FGD 8: 385. 2007; FOC 23: 394. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody with brown fibers of disintegrated leaf sheath. Plant pubescent throughout. Culms lateral or borne in axils of outer leaves, lateral culms with or without basal leaves, 7 – 35 cm tall, trigonous, base of culm with leafless sheath. Leaves longer than the culms, 6 – 12 mm wide, flat, base plicate, soft papery. Bracts short leafy to bristle-like, sheath up to 2.5 cm. Spikes 3 – 4, fairly close towards the top of culms; male spike terminal, narrowly cylindrical, ca. 3.5 cm, peduncle less than 3 cm; lateral spikes 3, androgynous, male part short at the top one-fifth to one-eighth, cylindrical, 1 – 4 cm, spikelets 13 – 48, rather densely distributed on spikes, peduncles 0.5 – 3 cm. Male glumes ovate, ca. 3.5 × 1.4 mm, apex rounded to broad-acute, hyaline, midrib green and keeled. Female glumes lanceolate, ca. 4.5 mm, pale greenish; midrib green, 3-veined and excurrent into a mucronate tip ca. 1.5 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, obliquely patent, ovate-elliptic, 7 – 7.5 mm, papery, green-brown, densely pubescent, many-veined, base attenuate, upper part attenuate to a long beak 2.8 – 3.2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, rhomboid-ovate to broad-elliptic, 4.2 – 4.5 mm, trigonous, middle of achenes constricted on the angles, black, base with a short curved stipe, upper part attenuate into an erect cylindrical beak 1.4 – 1.8 mm, apex of beak annulate; style base thickened at base; stigmas 3.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Nei Lak Shan. S. C. Ng 2920, 3048.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Montane hillside forests, alt. 600 – 800 m. Fruiting: Mar. – Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (C. L. Tso 20216, PE, holotype) was collected from Nei Lak Shan, Lantau Island in 1929.

Carex pumila Thunb. 矮生薹草
Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 846. 1784; FHK 402. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 307. 1903 – 04; FKH 305. 1912; FTW 5: 357, pl. 1359. 1978; FFJ 6: 356, fig. 320. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 227, pl. 88. 2000; FRPS 12: 373, pl. 78: 1 – 4. 2000; Y. L. Zheng & Y. F. Deng, Guihaia 23(6): 542. 2003; FGD 8: 388. 2007; FOC 23: 408. 2010.

Rhizome slender, stoloniferous. Culms central, 10–20 cm tall, trigonous, middle and basal part completely enclosed by sheath of basal leaves, lowest sheaths bladeless and reddish brown. Leaves longer than or equalling culm, blades 2–3.5 mm wide, flat, leathery, upper part of the leaves scabrous along veins and margins, with long sheath. Lower bracts leafy, longer than or shorter than culms, 5–10 cm, sheath short ca. 6 mm; upper bracts become smaller, reducing to bristle or glume for the terminal spike. Spikes 3–6, the top 1–2 staminate, clavate or narrowly cylindrical, 1.5–2.5 cm, peduncle short, < 0.7 mm; the other spikes pistillate, oblong or oblongcylindrical, 1.5–2 cm, ca. 8 mm wide, spikelets quite many, 13–19, rather loosely distributed, peduncle short, < 8 mm. Male glumes oblong, ca. 5.8 × 2 mm, apex acute and with or without short mucronate tip, yellowish brown and with magenta dots and short lines towards the base and middle of glume, midrib leathery, margins hyaline. Female glumes broad-ovate, 4.5–5.5 mm, apex acute and mucronate, membranous, brownish with rusty or magenta short lines, midrib 3-veined green, margin white and hyaline. Utricles longer than glumes, obliquely patent, ovate, inflated-trigonous, 6.2–6.6 × ca. 2.1 mm, corky, yellowish or yellowish brown, glabrous, distinctly several-veined, abruptly contracted to a broadly cuneate base and a thick stipe < 1 mm, upper part gradually narrowed to a rather broad and short beak ca. 2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes rather tightly enveloped, broad-obovate to elliptic, trigonous, 3.5 × 1.7 mm, base with short-stipe, style-base not thickened, stigmas 3.

Locality: Sai Kung (Tai Long Wan), Pak Shek Kok. J. C. Shaw 393; S. C. Ng 1392; Y. W. Lam 1767.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Liaoning, Hebei, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Coastal sandy beaches. Grow in mobile sand at the seaward margin of sand dune vegetation, alt. 0–2 m. Fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Carex scaposa C. B. Clarke 花葶薹草
Bot. Mag. 113, pl. 6940. 1887; FKH 305. 1912; FHN 4: 337. 1977; FFJ 6: 352, fig. 315. 1995; FRPS 12: 82, pl. 16: 1–4. 2000; FYN 15: 710, fig. 166: 1–4. 2003; FGD 8: 369. 2007; FOC 23: 294. 2010.

Rhizome woody. Culms central, oblique to erect, 35–70 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, blunty trigonous, sparsely pubescent, with or without leafless glabrous papery pale brown spathe-like sheath at the base or on the culm towards the base. Leaves basal, tufted, longer or shorter than culms; petiole 20–30 cm, glabrous, papery, sometimes leaf base extending downwards forming narrow wings; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic-linear, to elliptic-oblanceolate, 20–35 × 2.5–4.5 cm wide, with 3 longitudinal veins, base attenuate to acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces or scabrid abaxially. Bracts spathe-like, shorter than inflorescence branches; inflorescence compound, 3  several-branched; inflorescence branches paniculate, triangular-ovate, 2–3.5 × 2–3 cm wide, single or binate; peduncles rigid, trigonous, 4–8 cm, densely pubescent; axis of inflorescence branches sharply trigonous to flattened, densely pubescent; bractlets glumaceous, broad lanceolate, 2–5 mm, brown to pale brown; cladoprophylls utriculiform, without flower. Spikes about 20, all producing from cladoprophylls, patent, bisexual, androgynous, oblong-cylindrical, 7–15 mm. Male part of spike linear-lanceolate, shorter than female part, and fewer spikelets; male glumes ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, membranous, pale brown. Female part with 5–7 spikelets; female glumes ovate, 2.5–2.7 mm, membranous, acuminate, brown with spots and 3 longitudinal veins, margins ciliate when young. Utricles elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, papery, pale brown with dense brown spots, with 2 lateral veins abaxially, glabrous, nearly sessile, apex contracted gradually into medium beak up to 1/2 of the utricle length, beak opening emarginate. Achenes broad elliptic, trigonous, 2–2.5 mm, brown when mature; base of style not thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 435; HK sheet 39599, 41605.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Montane hillside forests, alt. 600–900 m. Fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Notes: A distinctive species characterised by broad lanceolate leaves with rather long petiole. The local specimens are rather consistent in leaf shape and petiole length, but FRPS (12: 82 – 84) has reported considerable variation among specimens within China.

Carex teinogyna Boott 長柱頭薹草（細梗薹草）
Ill. Gen. Carex 1: 60, pl. 158. 1858; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 175, fig. 123: 59. 1979; FFJ 6: 347, fig. 308. 1995; FRPS 12: 436, pl. 89. 2000; FYN 15: 788, fig. 185: 1–4. 2003; FGD 8: 392. 2007; FOC 23: 433. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms densely tufted, 25–60(–90) cm tall, rather slender, trigonous to flattened, scabrid. Leaves shorter than or equalling the culms, 2.5–3 mm wide, lower part conduplicate, midrib canaliculate, becoming flat towards upper part, veins and margins scabrous, basal sheaths usually splitting into fibers. Bracts shorter than or equal to branches of inflorescence, the lower bracts leaf-like, < 12 cm, upper bracts reducing to bristle-like; sheaths 5–25 mm. Inflorescence compound, spikes rather dense on inflorescences, lower bracts with (2–)3 branches of inflorescence, among them at least one branched further into 2 or more spikes; middle and upper bracts bear (1–)2–3 spikes. Spikes linear, 1–5 cm, androgynous, male part only ca. 1/4 of the spikes, remaining part of spikes male, male spikelets 7–25 and rather loosely distributed, peduncle slender but short, ca. 4–5 mm, usually only slightly longer than subtending bract-sheath. Male glumes similar to male glumes. Female glumes oblong-ovate, 3.5–4 mm, apex acute with a short scabrid mucronate point or awn, hyaline, brown to reddish brown, midrib green 3-veined. Utricles equal to or shorter than glume, oblong or narrow-elliptic, plano-convex, 3.2–4.7 × 1.1–1.3 mm, membranous, dark-brown to brown, hispidulous but a little bit less so at the middle, severalveined, base abruptly contracted to a short stipe, abruptly narrowed above to a rather long beak 1–1.4 mm, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, elliptic, 1.8–2.3 × 1.1–1.3 mm, yellowish to dark-brown or black, sessile; style base slightly thickened, stigmas 2, slender and longer than utricle (including beak), persistent.

Locality: Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Bride's Pool, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2807; L. T. Lo 420; Y. W. Lam 1443.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Common in hillside forests and streamsides, alt. 100–700 m. Fruiting: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: Its long persistent styles may help dispersal by attaching to passing-by mammals and birds or by assisting floatation on water surface.

Carex tenebrosa Boott 芒尖鱗薹草（薄葉薹草）
Ill. Gen. Carex 2: 88, t. 256. 1860; FHK 402. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 313. 1903 – 04; FKH 306. 1912; FRPS 12: 331–332. 2000; FGD 8: 386. 2007; FOC 23: 395. 2010.

Rhizome stout and woody, with dark brown fibers of disintegrating leaf sheath. Dried specimen dark olive-green. Culms central or lateral with basal leaves, 80–100 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, leathery. Leaves longer than the culms, 5–8 mm wide, flat to moderately revolute, margins scabrid, leathery. Lower bracts leaf-like, ca. 8 cm, reducing to setaceous for upper bracts, scabrous, sheath less than 5 cm. Spikes 3–4; male spike terminal, broad-linear with tapering ends, 4–9 cm, peduncle long, < 10 cm; lateral spikes 2–3, androgynous, male part about two- to three-fifths of the spike, cylindrical, 6–9.5 cm, spikelets 80–100 and very densely distributed on spikes, peduncle long for lower spikes, become shorter for upper spikes, 3–20 cm. Male glume oblong, 5–6 × 1.4–2.5 mm, apex emarginate to truncate with a hispid awn ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, pale brown. Female glumes oblong, 6.5–7.5 × 2.2–2.8 mm, apex truncate to emarginate, brown-green, the midrib project extend into a scabrous awn 3–4 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, rhomboid, 7–8.5 mm, stiff papery, dark olive-green, many-veined, base cunneate, sparsely hispid on margins, upper part attenuate into a long beak 3–4 mm, margin of beak scabrous along margins, orifice deeply 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, 4.7–5 × ca. 2 mm, rhomboid, trigonous, middle of achenes constricted, upper part contracted to an erect or slightly oblique cylindrical beak 1.5–2 mm, apex of beak slightly inflated; style-base slightly thickened; stigmas 3, rather long.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Pai Ngak Shan, Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 1226, 2152; HK sheet 42079.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The species was reported as Carex thibetica Franch. previously (Check List HK Plants 308. 2002; 109. 2004).

Carex tenuispicula Tang ex S. Y. Liang 纖穗薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 34: 92, fig. 1. 1996; FRPS 12: 149, pl. 30: 9 – 12. 2000; FGD 8: 375. 2007; FOC 23: 320. 2010.
Carex tenuispicula Y. C. Tang, FFJ 6: 359. 1995. ined.

Rhizome short. Culms borne in the leave axil, trigonous, 10–30 cm tall, oblique, very slender and rather flaccid, pale brownish to pale greenish. Basal sheaths split into dark brown fibers. Leaves shorter than or longer than culms, 7–40 cm × 2–4 mm, flat, scabrid along margins, papery. Bracts leafy and longer than spikes for lower bracts, 5–12 cm, becoming shorter and bristle-like towards top of culms; sheath ca. 2 mm for lower and middle bracts, or absent for upper bracts. Spikes 4 – 6, pale brownish to pale yellowish, remote especially for lower spikes, lowerest spikes are often from near base of culms; male spike terminal, linear, 3–4 cm × 0.5–0.7 mm, peduncle 3–4 mm. Lateral spikes androgynous, mainly pistillate, narrowly cylindrical, 1–4 cm × 1.5–1.7 mm, female spikelets 9–28, rather loosely distributed, peduncle long and slender, 4–10 cm, lower spikes often pendent with longer peduncle. Male glumes broad ovate, apex rounded, 1.5–1.6 cm, margin ciliate, very pale brownish. Pistillate glumes broad ovate, apex obtuse to rounded, 1.3–1.5 mm, membranous, pale-brown, margin hyaline and ciliate. Utricles longer than the glume, fusiform, trigonous, 2.2–3 × ca. 1 mm, membranous, very pale brownish, many-veined, upper part gradually attenuate forming a short beak, orifice slightly 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, pale brownish to brown, rhombic or fusiform, trigonous, 1.9–2.1 × ca. 0.9 mm, faces slightly depressed at upper and lower part, upper part of the achene form into a short cylindrical neck ca. 0.2 × 0.2 mm, pale yellowish to pale brownish, apex flat; base attenuate into a stipe; style-base slightly thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan, Nei Lak Shan, Keung Shan, Sunset Peak. HK sheet 41935, 41936, 41939.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 300–500 m. Fruiting: Jan.–Mar.

Carex tristachya Thunb. 三穗薹草
Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 845. 1784; FKH 306. 1912; FHN 4: 342. 1977; FFJ 6: 361, fig. 326. 1995; FRPS 12: 158, pl. 32: 1–4. 2000; FGD 8: 375. 2007; FOC 23: 324. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, erect to oblique, 12–40 cm tall, slender, obtusely trigonous, smooth. Basal sheath dark brown and split into fibers. Leaves shorter or equal to the culm, 2–3 mm wide, flat, papery, margins scabrid. Bracts leafy for the lowest spikes, longer than the subtended spikes, 2–4 cm, upper bracts reduce to sheath similar to glumes in colour, texture and size; lower sheath up to 2 cm. Spikes 4–6, upper ones closer to contiguous, more remotely spaced for lower spikes; terminal spike staminate, narrowly linear-cylindrical, 18–23 × ca. 1.5 mm, peduncle very short to obsolete; lateral spikes pistillate, cylindrical, 1–1.5 cm × 2–2.5 mm, spikelets 12–17, rather densely distributed on spikes; peduncles of lowest spikes extend far beyond sheath, up to 10 cm, those of upper spikes getting shorter, the peduncle of the uppermost spike is short and only slightly extend out of sheath. Male glumes broad ovate, ca. 2.4 × 1.3 mm, base of margin free or slightly connate to below the middle; filament of stamen thread-like or flat. Female glumes elliptic to oblong, 1.8–1.9 × 1.0–1.1 mm, apex mucronate, obtuse to truncate, pale yellow, midrib green. Utricles longer than the glumes, erect, ovate-fusiform, trigonous, 2.8–3.0 mm × ca. 1 mm, membranous, green, many-veined, puberulent, upper part attenuate into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed, base attenuate into a short stipe. Achene tightly enveloped, ovate, ca. 2.1 mm, brown to dark brown, apex discoid-annulate; style base thickened conically; stigmas 3.

Locality: San Tau, Tung Lung Chau. S. C. Ng 2153; HK sheet 41933, 41934.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Hillside open forests and shrublands, alt. 10–100 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Apr.

Carex truncatigluma C. B. Clarke 截鱗薹草
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 315. 1904; FFJ 6: 359, fig. 323. 1995; FRPS 12: 144, pl. 30: 1 – 4. 2000; FYN 15: 725, fig. 169: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 8: 373. 2007; FOC 23: 318. 2010.
Carex gracilispica Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form 10: 62, fig. 39. 1921; FTW 5: 331, pl. 1355. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 149. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 5: 213, pl. 82. 2000.

Rhizome woody, obliquely ascending, covered with greyish brown fibrous remains of leaf sheath. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils to lateral, oblique to erect, slender, 15–35 cm tall, trigonous. Leaves longer than or equal to the culms, 5–8 mm wide, flat, slightly scabrid to smooth on both surfaces, stiff papery. Bracts bristle-like to short-leafy, with sheath 6–8 mm. Spikes 3–6, male spike terminal, linear cylindrical, 3.5–5 × 0.1 cm, peduncle almost obsolete or very short, ca. 0.5 cm. Lateral spikes female, cylindrical, 3.5–5 × 0.2–0.3 cm thick, spikelets rather loose; the highest pistillate spike surpass or equal the staminate spike in length, with peduncle equal to or slightly longer than the enclosing bract sheath; the lower pistillate spikes remote and with longer peduncles up to 2–4 cm, extending beyond the sheath. Male glumes oblong, apex rounded, 3–3.5 mm, pale yellowish brown. Female glumes broad-obovate, apex truncate or rounded to minutely murconate, yellowish, margins broadly hyaline, midrib green. Utricles longer than the glume, rhombic-fusiform, trigonous, 3.4–4.2 × 1–1.1 mm, pale greenish brown, membranous, puberulent, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe, upper part cuspidate into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, rhombic-fusiform, trigonous, 2.5–3 × 1–1.1 mm, pale brown to dark brown; upper part of the achene form into a ivory-coloured stout, cylindrical crown, ca. 0.5 mm, apex truncate to shallowly concave; faces of achene excavated at the lower part, but only slightly so at the upper part; base attenuate into a stipe ca. 0.5 mm; style base slightly thickened and persistent; stigmas 3.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung, Sha Lo Tung, Lantau Peak, Cheung Chau. J. C. Shaw 410; S. C. Ng 1208; HK sheet 36834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Malay Peninsula, Philippines.
Ecology: Fairly common in hillside forests, alt. 50–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.

Carex tsiangii F. T. Wang & Tang 三念薹草
Contrib. Inst. Bot. Nat. Acad. Peiping 6(2): 59. 1949; FRPS 12: 92. 2000; FGD 8: 371. 2007; FOC 23: 298. 2010.

Rhizome woody, with stolons. Culms lateral, erect to oblique, 45–55 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, trigonous to flattened, glabrous, with leafless brown sheaths at culm base and towards lower part of the culm. Leaves longer than culms, basal, several leaves and basal leafless brown sheaths forming a high shoot, leaf blades linear, flat, 5–7 mm wide, glabrous to slightly scabrous on both sides, margins entire or scabrid, soft papery. Bracts spathe-like and leafless, shorter than inflorescence branches; panicle compound, 10–30 cm, 3–10-branched; inflorescence branches broadly ovate, ca. 2 × 2 cm, single or binate, each with 3–10 spikes, peduncles tenuous, 2–7 cm, pubescent; inflorescence axis sharply trigonous, densely hirsutus when young; bractlets glumaceous, lanceolate, 3–9 mm, pale brown with brown dots, loosely pubescent; spikes horizontally patent, bisexual, androgynous, 8–12 mm, cylindrical, male part equal to female part, female part with 3–15 spikelets; male glumes lanceolate, 3–3.5 mm, acute, brown with brown spots and short lines, with 1 midvein; female glumes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, acute, membranous, pale brown with brown spots and short lines, with 1 midvein, loosely pubescent, margins ciliate. Utricles broad-elliptic, obtusely trigonous, 3–4.2 mm wide, papery, brown, glabrous, with several fine veins, apex contracted into long beak about 50% of the whole length of utricle, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achenes elliptic or broad-elliptic, trigonous, ca. 2 mm; style base thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. S. C. Ng 1531, 2651.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Margins of montane hillside open forests and hillside forests with grasslands, alt. 700–900 m. Fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Carex zunyiensis Tang & F. T. Wang 遵義薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 24: 241. 1986; FRPS 12: 336, pl. 70: 1–4. 2000; FYN 15: 772. 2003; Y. L. Zheng & Y. F. Deng, Guihaia 23(6): 542. 2003; X. F. Jing et al., J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 22(1): 51. 2004; FGD 8: 387. 2007; FOC 23: 397. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms lateral or in axils of outer leaves, 4–12 cm tall, much shorter than leaves, basal leaves sheath-like with leaf blade, 5–9 cm, or without leaf blade. Sterile leaves 25–60 × 0.8–1 cm, flat, base plicate, blade smooth on both sides, margins slightly revolute and scabrid, basal sheaths split into dark brown fibers. Bracts short leafy, longer than subtending spikelets but less than 8 cm for lower spikelets, pale yellowish to pale greenish. Spikes 2–3, close together towards top of culm; male spike terminal, linearcylindrical, 3–3.5 cm × ca. 2 mm; female spikes lateral, oblong-cylindrical, 2.5–3 × ca. 1 cm, spikelets many and dense on the spikes, peduncle short 0.8–1 cm. Male glumes narrow-oblong to lanceolate, ca. 3.4 × 0.8 mm, apex acuminate, yellowish, midrib 3-veined. Female glumes lanceolate, 4.5–5.8 mm, apex acute, greenish yellow to pale yellow, margins scabrous, midrib raised. Utricles longer than the glume, obliquely patent, elliptic, 4–5 × 2.1–2.4 mm, thin papery, pale yellow to green, many-veined, base cuneate, upper part contracted into an erect cylindrical beak ca. 2.2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes 4.3–4.9 × 2.4–2.6 mm, tightly enveloped, pale yellow to yellowish brown, ovate-elliptic, trigonous, middle of achene excavated on the angles, base cuneate into a short and slightly curved stipe, upper part contract into a short curved beak ca. 1 mm, apex of beak annulate; stigmas 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 2161, 3055.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Anhui, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Jan.–Apr.
Notes: A distinctive species characterised by its short inflorescence borne near or half-buried in the ground.

Carica papaya L. 番木瓜
Sp. Pl. 1036. 1753; FHN 1: 492, fig. 268. 1964; FRPS 52(1): 122. 1999; FGD 5: 23, fig. 17. 2003.
Papaya carica Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 191, fig. 122. 1791.

Small tree, to 8 m tall, usually unbranched, sometimes branched due to injury, containing white latex in all parts, dioecious or polygamous. Petioles hollowed, to 1 m; leaf blades suborbicular, 25 –75 cm in diam., palmately and deeply 7–11- lobed, glabrous, lobes deeply and broadly toothed. Male flowers sessile, in pendulous panicles, up to 1 m; calyx small, connate at base, 5-lobed; corolla light yellow, tube 2.5 cm, lobes ca. 1.8 cm; stamens 10, in 2 whorls, alternate to corolla lobes. Female flowers solitary or in several-flowered cymes, short pedicelled or sessile; corolla-tube very short, lobes 5, oblong to lanceolate, fleshy, ca. 5 × 2 cm; ovary ovoid, 2–3 cm long, 1 locular, ovules many; styles short, 5, stigmas 5, fan-shaped, sessile, deeply 5-cleft. Bisexual flowers: stamens 5 or 10, inserted on long or very short corollatubes. Berries ellipsoid or obovoid, 15 –30 cm, orange-yellow when mature. Seeds many, black, globose, testa fleshy, endotesta woody, rugose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2144.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Carmona microphylla (Lam.) G. Don 基及樹（福建茶）
Gen. Hist. 4: 391. 1837; FHN 3: 453. 1974; FRPS 64(2): 21. 1990; FOC 16: 337. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 388. 1998.
Ehretia microphylla Lam., Encycl. Meth. 1: 425. 1783; FTW 4: 400. 1978; FFJ 4: 506, fig. 403. 1989.
Carmona heterophylla Cav., Icon. 5: 22, pl. 23. 1799.
Ehretia buxifolia Roxb., Pl. Coromandel 1: 42, pl. 57. 1795.
Ehretia dentata Courchet, Fl. Indo‑Chine 4: 206. 1914.

Shrub, 1–4 m tall, multibranched; bark brown; branches slender, sparsely hirtellous when young. Petiole 1–5 mm; leaf blade leathery, obovate to spatulate, 0.8–4 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate, apex rounded to acute, margin coarsely crenate, adaxially hirtellous or spotted, abaxially subglabrous. Glomerules spreading, 0.5–1.5 cm wide. Peduncle slender, 1–1.5 cm, pubescent. Pedicel 1–1.5 mm, or ± obsolete. Calyx 4–6 mm, parted nearly to base; lobes linear or linear‑oblanceolate, 0.5–0.8 mm, spreading hirtellous, densely appressed pubescent inside. Corolla white or slightly reddish, campanulate, 4–6 mm; lobes spreading, oblong, longer than tube. Filaments 2.5–4 mm, inserted near base of corolla; anthers ellipsoidal, 1.5–1.8 mm. Style 4–6 mm, glabrous. Drupes 3–4 mm in diam.; endocarp globose, reticulate‑wrinkled, 2–3 mm in diam., apex short beaked.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2312.
Distribution: Hainan, S Guangdong, Taiwan, widely cultivated in S China; S & E Asia, New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Carpesium abrotanoides L. 天名精
Sp. Pl. 860. 1753; FKH 144. 1912; FRPS 75: 313. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 893. 1998; FGD 8: 149, fig. 82. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem 50–100 cm tall, striate, branches many, lower portion woody and subglabrous, upper part pubescent. Basal leaves withered at anthesis, median and upper ones 4–11.5 × 0.8–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin irregularly dentate, adaxial surface puberulent, abaxial surface pubescent and glandular, petiole 5–15 mm; leaves on upper portion smaller in size, apex acute to acuminate, petioles much shorter or almost absent. Capitula axillary, subsessile or shortly pedunculate, arranged as spicate form, sometimes subtended by several elliptic or lanceolate leaves of 4–15 mm. Involucres depressed‑globose, 6–10 mm across; phyllaries 3‑seriate; outer ones ovate and shortest, about 3.5 mm, apex obtuse, basally scarious and apically foliaceous, margin of upper half ciliate, abaxial side pubescent; middle phyllaries lanceolate‑oblong, 4.5–5 mm; while inner ones oblong, 5–6 mm, both scarious, with rounded apex, margin ciliate and shallowly serrulate near the tip, not entire. Receptacle plane, nude, the centre of areoles elevated. Florets yellow, glandular near the limb apex, marginal ones female, corolla narrowly tubular, 1–1.5 mm, apex 5‑lobed; central florets hermaphrodite, corolla similar in shape but larger, 2–2.5 mm; anther sagittate at base with caudate and split lobes, the apical appendages oblong and truncate at tip; stylar branches subcomplanate, apex rounded. Cypselae oblong‑cylindric, 3–3.5 mm, striate‑costate, narrowed at base, apex rostrate and with an annular cartilaginous crown, glandular at the base and on the rostrum. Pappus absent.

Locality: Sha Tin, Wu Kai Sha. W. J. Tutcher 11229; HK sheet 32940; N. H. Li 12 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Japan, Korea, Myanmar, Sikkim.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Caryopteris incana (Thunb. ex Houtt.) Miq. 蘭香草
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno‑Batavum 2: 97. 1866; FGZ 634. 1956; FTW 4: 418. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 198. 1982; FFJ 4: 551, fig. 431. 1989; FOC 17: 45. 1994; FGD 3: 384. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 414, photo. 178. 1998.
Nepeta incana Thunb. ex Houtt., Nat. Hist. 2(9): 307. 1778.
Barbula sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochchin. 367. 1790.
Caryopteris mastacantnus Schauer, Prodr. 11: 625. 1847; FHK 268. 1861; FKH 205. 1912.
Caryopteris ovata Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 144. 1861.
Caryopteris sinensis (Lour.) Dippel, Handb. Laubholzkunde 1: 59, fig. 24. 1889.

Perennial herb, 20–60 cm or taller, aromatic, with woody base. Branchlets terete, often slightly purple, greyish white pubescent, glabrescent. Petiole 0.3–1.7 mm; leaf blade thickly papery, oblong, ovate or lanceolate, 1.5–7(–9) × 0.4–4 cm, base cuneate, subrounded, or truncate, apex obtuse to acute, margin coarsely serrate to rarely subentire, greyish white pubescent and yellow glandular on both surfaces. Inflorescences dense corymbose cymes. Bracts and bracteoles absent. Calyx cupular, ca. 2 mm, pubescent and glandular abaxially, 5‑lobed, lobes oblong‑lanceolate, longer than tube. Corolla purplish to bluish, tube ca. 6 mm, throat with a ring of hairs, lower lobe fringed, pubescent and glandular on both surfaces. Stamens and style exserted. Ovary pubescent. Fruiting calyx 4– 5 mm. Fruit ca. 2.5 mm in diam., hirsute, nutlets with winged edges.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lamma Island, Tai A Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1296; P. S. Choi 517; Y. W. Lam 1181.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangsu; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Caryota maxima Blume 魚尾葵
Mart., Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 195. 1838; FOC 23: 150. 2010.
Caryota ochlandra Hance, J. Bot. 17: 174. 1879; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 163, fig. 1064. 1977; FGD 2: 454, fig. 318. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 115. 1991; Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004.

Large tree. Stems solitary, to 25 m tall, to 50 cm in diam., nodes well spaced. Leaves bipinnate, to 4 m, borne along upper half of stems; pinnae 12–28 per side of secondary rachis, drooping, the top pinna being the biggest, triangular, other pinnae smaller downwards, rhombic, the outer margin straight, upper 1/4 to 1/2 of inner margin irregularly toothed; sheaths with black fibres on the margin. Inflorescences to 3.5 m, branched 1 order, rachillae many, 1.5–2.5 m; male flowers ovoid, 15–20 mm, yellowish, stamens 50–110, anthers linear; female flowers 5–6 mm in diam., staminodes 3. Fruits globose, 2–2.5 cm in diam., reddish or orange when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 10561.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, food (starch).

Caryota mitis Lour. 短穗魚尾葵（小魚尾葵）
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 569. 1790; FHN 4: 164. 1977; FGD 2: 453. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 115. 1991; FOC 23: 150. 2010.

Large shrub. Stems clustered, 5–8 m tall, 8–15 cm in diam., light green, with well spaced leaf nodes. Leaves bipinnate, to 3 m or longer; pinnae 10–20 on each side of secondary rachis, basal pinnae smaller than the upper ones, triangular, the outer margin straight, upper 1/2 of inner margin erose; sheaths margin with black fibres. Inflorescences 30–60 cm, branched 1 order, rachillae 20–60, 25–55 cm; male flowers elongate ovoid, 8–10 × 2.5–3 mm, stamens 12–25; female flowers 4–5 mm in diam., staminodes 3. Fruits globose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Casearia glomerata Roxb. 嘉賜樹
Fl. Ind., ed. 2, 2: 419. 1832; FHK 122. 1861; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 311. 1904; FKH 110. 1912; FHN 1: 463. 1964; FFJ 4: 16, fig. 15. 1989; FGD 2: 111. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 76, pl. 18: 1. 1999.
Casearia glomerata Roxb. f. pubinervis How & Ko, Acta Bot. Sin. 8(1): 31. 1959; FGX 1: 667. 1991.

Shrub or small tree, 2–10 m tall. Young branches puberulous; old branches terete and glabrous. Petioles 0.6–1.4 cm, subglabrous; leaf blade oblong to oblong-elliptic, 9 –12 × 3 – 5 cm, thinly leathery, base obtuse or rounded, slightly oblique, apex acuminate, margin repand or obtusely dentate, sparsely puberulous when young, glabrescent; lateral veins 7– 8 pairs. Pedicels 0.7–1 cm, densely yellowish brown-puberulous; bracts broadly triangular, ca. 1 mm. Flowers in glomerules, 10 –30-flowered. Calyx lobes 5, oblong, 2–3 mm, densely yellowish puberulous. Stamens 8 –10; filaments puberulous; anthers suborbicular; staminodes elliptic, apex with a bundle of hair. Ovary glabrous, ovoid-conical, ca. 1.5 mm; styles short; stigmas capitate. Capsule ovoid, leathery, 1.2 cm, yellow to orange-red, densely tuberculate when dry; seeds many, ovoid, ca. 4 mm, with red arils.

Locality: Mount Parker, Shatin, Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1459; K. Y. Tam 1459; L. T. Lo 442.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Xizang; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.; fruiting: Oct. to spring of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Casearia velutina Bl. 毛嘉賜樹
Mus. Bot. 1: 253. 1850; FFJ 4: 15. 1989; FRPS 52(1): 73, pl. 17: 6. 1999.
Casearia balansae Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 3: 234. 1914; FRPS 52(1): 71. 1999.
Casearia balansae Gagnep. var. cuneifolia Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 2: 244. 1914.
Casearia villilimba Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 23: 254. 1923; FHN 1: 463. 1964; FGD 2: 110, fig. 76. 1991.
Casearia petelotii Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 56. 1938.

Small tree, to 10 m tall; branchlets zigzag, densely rusty pubescent. Petioles 0.5–1 cm, stout, densely brown-pubescent; leaf blade black when dry, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 7–20 × 4 – 8 cm, thickly papery, base rounded, unequilateral, apex acuminate, margin serrate, sparsely pilose initially, glabrescent or only pubescent along midveins adaxially, densely yellowish brown villose abaxially; lateral veins 6–12 pairs. Flowers several to many in glomerules. Pedicels 2– 4 mm, pilose. Calyx lobes 5, oblong-elliptic, 2–3 mm, pilose on both surfaces. Stamens 8; filaments puberulous; anthers ellipsoid. Staminodes hairy, apex with a bundle of hair. Ovary ellipsoid, pilose; styles short, ca. 1.5 mm; stigmas discoid. Capsule ellipsoid, 1–1.2 cm, glabrous, fleshy, yellow when mature, black when dried; stipe slightly pubescent. Seeds many, ovoid, pale yellow.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang. H. C. Tang 2508; Y. S. Lau 1367; Y. W. Lam 221.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Guizhou, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The species was reported as C. grewiaefolia Vent. previously (Check List HK Plants 40. 1993).

Cassia fistula L. 臘腸樹（豬腸豆）
Sp. Pl. 1: 377. 1753; FHN 2: 230. 1965; FRPS 39: 110, pl. 43: 3 – 4. 1988; FGD 5: 182. 2003; FGX 2: 466. 2005.

Deciduous small to medium-sized tree, to 15 m tall. Branches slender. Bark smooth, grey when young, rough and dark brown when old. Petioles short; leaves 30 – 40 cm; rachis and petioles not winged, eglanduar; leaflets 3 – 4 pairs, thinly leathery, broadly ovate, ovate or oblong, 8 – 13 × 3.5 – 7 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate and obtuse, margin entire, puberulous on both surfaces when young, glabrescent; lateral veins slender, conspicuous on both surfaces. Racemes to 30 cm or longer, lax, pendulous. Flowers blooming at the same time as leaves appearing, ca. 4 cm in diam. Pedicels slender, 2–5 cm, ebracteate. Sepals long ovate, thin, 1–1.5 cm, reflexed after flowering. Petals yellow, obovate, subequal, 2 – 2.5 cm, conspicuously veined. Stamens 10, 3 of them with long and curved filaments, exserted, 4 of them short and straight, with broad and large anthers, the rest 3 very small, sterile; anthers longitudinally dehiscent. Pods terete, 30–60 × 2 – 2.5 cm, dark brown, indehiscent, 3-furrowed. Seeds 40 – 100, separated by septum.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 25; Y. S. Lau 1906; HK sheet 8523.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, timber.

Cassytha filiformis L. 無根藤
Sp. Pl. 1: 35. 1753; FHK 294. 1861; FHN 1: 301, fig. 147. 1964; FRPS 31: 463, pl. 124. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 437, pl. 203. 1996.

Stems filiform or wiry, pale green to yellow-green, glabrous or slightly pubescent when young, twining round and attaching to other plants by means of small suckers. Leaves reduced to tiny scales, alternate, ca. 1 mm. Inflorescences spicate, 2–5 cm, rarely reduced to single flower, densely rusty pubescent; bract and bracteoles broad ovate, small, ca. 1 mm, brown, ciliate. Flowers white, less than 2 mm, sessile; perianth-lobes 6 in 2 whorls, the outer 3 much smaller than the inner ones. Stamens 9; filaments of the outer stamens broad and petal-like, of the other 6 filiform; anthers all fertile. Fruit drupaceous, ovoid, enclosed in the succulent tube of the perianth and crowned by the persistent connivent perianth-lobes, to 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 172; Y. S. Lau 2307.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa, and Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets on slopes. Flowering and fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Castanopsis carlesii (Hemsl.) Hayata 米櫧（小紅栲）
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6 (suppl.): 72. 1917; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 88. 1963; FFJ 1: 384, fig. 335. 1982; FRPS 22: 66, pl. 18: 5– 8. 1998; FOC 4: 330. 1999.
Quercus carlesii Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 26: t. 2591. 1899.
Castanopsis cuspidata (Thunb. ex Murray) Schott. var. carlesii (Hemsl.) Yamazaki, J. Jap. Bot. 62(11): 333. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 2: 55, pl. 20, photo 19. 1996.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots and rachis of inflorescences sparsely reddish brown scurfy. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles to 1 cm, base thickened; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate-laceolate, 4 –12 × 1– 4.5 cm, base cuneate, ± oblique, apex acuminate to narrowly caudate, margin entire or with a few shallow teeth above middle, abaxial surface initially reddish brown scurfy, greyish brown to silvery when full grown; lateral veins 8 –11 on each side of midvein. Male spikes simple or branched, 5 –7 cm; rachis glabrous or glabrescent. Female spikes 3– 4 cm, lengthening to 7–8.5 cm in fruiting time, glabrous; flower 1 per cupule. Cupule subglobose to ovoid, 0.8 –1.2 cm in diam., usually entirely enclosing nut, wall 0.5–1 mm thick, yellowish brown to reddish brown tomentose abaxially; bracts spine-like or reduced to tubercles, arranged into 6–7 continuous or interrupted rings. Nut subglobose to broadly conical, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., apex shortly pointed; scar ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9119; Y. S. Lau 1722; L. T. Lo 379.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).

Castanopsis concinna (Champ. ex Benth.) A. DC. 華南錐（毛葉栲栗）
J. Bot. 1: 182. 1863; FRPS 22: 30, pl. 5: 5 –7. 1998; FOC 4: 322. 1999.
Castanea concinna Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 115. 1854; FHK 319. 1861.

Tree, 10–15 m tall. Branches of the current year growth and rachis of inflorescences softly tomentose. Leaves firmly leathery; petioles 4–12 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.5–3.5(–5) cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, slightly revolute, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose on midvein when young, abaxially reddish brown scurfy; lateral veins 12–16 on each side of midvein. Male spikes 5–10 cm, solitary in the axils of the young leaves and forming a terminal leafy panicle. Female spikes solitary, 4–8 cm in fruiting time. Cupule globose, 5–6 cm in diam., splitting into 4 regular segments, wall 2–4 mm thick, densely crowded with stout clustered branching spines. Nut 1 per cupule, compressed globular, ca. 1 × 1.4 cm, densely pubescent; scar covering 1/3–1/2 of nut.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Wong Nai Chung, Happy Valley, Sai Kung, Tai Wai, Tai Mo Shan. W. J. Tutcher 8410; Y. S. Lau 199; H. C. Tang 1469.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.– Oct. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Castanopsis eyrei (Champ. ex Benth.) Tutch. 甜櫧（埃氏栲）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 37: 68. 1905; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 390. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 57, pl. 22. 1996; FRPS 22: 53, pl. 13: 5 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 327. 1999.
Quercus eyrei Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 114. 1854; FHK 320. 1861.

Tree, 8 –15 m tall. Bark greyish brown, longitudinally fissured. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles to 0.7–1(–1.5) cm, base thickened; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, rarely ovate-elliptic, 5–7(–13) × 1.5 –2.5(– 5) cm, base cuneate, ± oblique, apex caudate-acuminate, margin entire or with a few coarse serratures towards apex, green, glabrous and shining on both surfaces; lateral veins 8 –10 on each side of midvein, very slender but evident. Male spikes 3.5– 5 cm, in a terminal panicle; rachis glabrous. Females spikes simple and shorter; flowers 1 per cupule. Cupule subglobose to broad ovoid, 1.5–3 cm in diam., splitting irregularly when mature, wall ca. 1 mm thick, greyish to yellowish grey puberulent outside; bracts spine-like, 4 – 8 mm, usually entirely covering cupule. Nut 1 per cupule, broadly conical, 1–1.4 cm in diam., glabrous; scar basal, 8 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen, Middle Gap, Wong Nai Chung. W. J. Tutcher 2031, 4675; Y. S. Lau 2953.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Qinghai, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in Wong Nai Chung by Eyre between 1849 and 1851.

Castanopsis fabri Hance 羅浮錐（白櫞）
J. Bot. 22: 230. 1884; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 386. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 57, pl. 23, photo 21. 1996; FRPS 22: 71, pl. 20: 6–13. 1998; FOC 4: 331. 1999.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots glabrescent or sparsely pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles (0.5–)1–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, 6–10(–15) × 2.5– 4.5(– 5) cm, base subrounded to cuneate, rarely broadly cuneate, ± oblique, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrate on the upper 1/3, rarely entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially reddish brown to yellowish brown scurfy when young; lateral veins 10–12 on each side of midvein. Male spikes simple or branched and forming panicles, rachis sparsely pubescent. Female spikes 8 –17 cm in fruiting time; flowers 2 or 3 per cupule. Cupule globose, broadly ellipsoid or ovoid, 2–3 cm in diam., entirely enclosing nut, splitting irregularly when mature, wall ca.1 mm thick; bracts spine-like, 4– 6(–10) mm, brown to yellowish brown when dry, sparsely pubescent to glabrescent, base connate into bundles and 4 – 5 interrupted rings, apex branched. Nut (1–)2(–3) per cupule, conical, 1–1.4 × 1–1.2 cm, glabrous; scar 8 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Tam Tuk, Victoria Peak, Wan Chai Gap, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 4609; Y. S. Lau 455; H. C. Tang 792.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).

Castanopsis fargesii Franch. 栲
J. Bot. (Morot) 13: 195. 1899; FFJ 1: 388, fig. 341. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 61, pl. 24. 1996; FRPS 22: 55, pl. 15: 1–9. 1998; FOC 4: 328. 1999.

Tree, 10 –20 m tall. Branchlets rusty scurfy when young, glabrous in age. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5(–2) cm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic-lanceolate rarely ovate, 6.5 – 8(–15) × 1.8 –2.5(– 5) cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, sometimes oblique, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or with 1–3 pairs of shallow teeth towards apex, densely reddish brown scurfy on abaxial surface; lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein. Male spikes solitary or forming panicles; flowers solitary, but crowded on the rachis. Female spikes solitary, glabrous, to 30 cm; flowers 1 per cupule and scattered on rachis. Cupule globose to broadly ovoid, 1.5 –2.5 × 9 –30 cm in diam., splitting irregularly, wall ca. 1 mm thick, whitish grey to brownish puberulent abaxially; bracts spine-like, 6 –10 mm, base connate into 4 –6 zoned bundles. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.8 –1.4 cm, glabrous; scar 8–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan (Ng Tung Chai). F. W. Xing 6932, 8971.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).

Castanopsis fissa (Champ. ex Benth.) Rehd. & Wils. 黧蒴錐（裂斗錐栗）
Pl. Wilson. 3: 204. 1916; FFJ 1: 386, fig. 338. 1982; FRPS 22: 21, pl. 3: 5 –14. 1998; FOC 4: 320. 1999.
Quercus fissa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 114. 1854; FHK 320. 1861; FKH 252. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Bud-scales and apex of young leaves reddish purple or yellowish brown puberulent. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong to obovate-elliptic, very variable in size, usually 11–23(–30) × 5 –9 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate to rounded, margin undulate and crenate on the lower half, adaxially glabrous, abaxially yellowish brown puberulent when young; lateral veins 15 –20(–28) on each side of midvein. Spikes erect, 8 –15 cm, forming a terminal panicle; the males usually many, with 1 terminal female or sometimes 1–2 androgynous spikes just below the female one; rachis glabrous. Infructescence 8–18 cm. Cupule ovoid to ellipsoid, 1–1.5 cm in diam., entirely enclosing the nut when young, afterwards splitting into 2–3(– 4) irregular segments, wall 0.5 –1 mm thick, slightly tomentose outside; bracts scale-like, triangular and imbricate when young, irregularly zoned with age. Nut 1 per cupule, globose to elliptic, 1.3 –1.8 × 1.1–1.6 cm, apex tawny tomentose; scar 4 –7 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely planted. H. C. Tang 858, 2091, 2386.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Afforestation.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from the Happy Valley Woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Castanopsis fordii Hance 毛錐
J. Bot. 22: 230. 1884; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 387, fig. 340. 1982; FRPS 22: 33, pl. 5: 8 –10. 1998; FOC 4: 323. 1999.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Bark rough, dark grey, finely fissured. Branchlets and rachis of inflorescence densely tawny tomentose. Leaves leathery; petioles short and stout, 1–3(–5) mm; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate or oblanceolate-oblong, 9–14(–21) × 3–7 cm, base slightly cordate, rarely rounded, apex acute, or rarely rounded, margin entire and revolute, densely reddish brown tomentose on abaxial surface; lateral veins (12–)14 –18 on each side of midvein. Male spikes usually forming panicle, densely flowered. Female spikes 6–12 cm in fruiting time; flowers 1 per cupule. Cupule globose, 4.5 – 6 cm in diam. including spines, splitting into 4 – 5 regular segments when mature, wall 0.5 –1 mm thick; bracts spine-like entirely covering cupule; spines 10 –15(–20) mm, connate into bundles, pubescent. Nut 1 per cupule, compressed conical, 1.2–1.5 × 1.5 –2 cm, with appressed hairs; scar basal, 4–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tiu Shau Ngam. Y. W. Lam 220; F. W. Xing 8787.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Fuelwood.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Ford from Lo Fau Shan, Guangdong Province in Sept. 1888.

Castanopsis kawakamii Hayata 吊皮錐
J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 30(1): 300. 1911; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 86. 1963; FFJ 1: 389, fig. 342. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 64, pl. 27, photo 24. 1996; FRPS 22: 26, pl. 5: 1–4. 1998; FOC 4: 321. 1999.
Castanopsis greenii Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 150. 1928.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Bark fissured, exfoliating in long stripes hanging on the trunk. Branchlets reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5(–2.5) cm; leaf blade ovate, ovate‑lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–12 × 2–5 cm, rarely broader, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, ± oblique, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire or rarely with 1–3 minute teeth towards apex, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins conspicuous abaxially. Male spikes usually forming panicles; rachis sparsely pubescent. Female spikes 5–10 cm, glabrous; flowers 1 per cupule. Cupule globose, 5 –8(–10) cm in diam. including the spines, splitting into 4, rarely 5 segments; bracts spine-like, 20–30 mm, connate to middle into radial branched bundles. Nut 1 per cupule, compressed globose, 1.2–1.5 × 1.7–2 cm, densely tawny tomentose; scar covering 1/3 of nut.

Locality: Sha Tin, Wu Kau Tang. W. Y. Chun 4966.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen of Castanopsis greenii Chun (W. Y. Chun 4966, HK sheet 26578) was collected in Shatin by W. Y. Chun on 24 March 1927. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Castanopsis lamontii Hance 鹿角錐（鐵錐樹）
J. Bot. 13: 368. 1875; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 387. 1982; FRPS 22: 74, pl. 21: 1– 5. 1998; FOC 4: 332. 1999.
Castanopsis tribuloides auct. non A. DC.: FKH 254. 1912.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Bark greyish brown, longitudinally fissured, inner bark dark reddish brown. Branchlets dark brown, glabrous. Leaves thick-papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm, base dark brown when dry; leaf blade elliptic, ovate or oblong, (6 –)12–23(–30) × (2–)3 –5(–8) cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, ± oblique, apex acuminate to long-acuminate, margin entire, or sometimes with a few obtuse serratures near apex, glabrous, abaxially glaucous when full grown; lateral veins 10 –12(–15) on each side of midvein. Male spikes axillary, 8–9 cm, usually forming leafy panicle. Female spike axillary, above the male ones, 10–20 cm in fruiting time, flowers 3 per cupule; rachis very thick. Cupule globose to subglobose, 4– 6 cm in diam. including spines, wall ca. 1 mm thick; bracts spine-like, stout, 0.5 –1(–1.5) cm, connate into 4 – 6 spine-zones. Nut 2–3 per cupule, broadly conical, 1.5 –2.5 cm high, densely pubescent; scar covering 2/5 –1/2 of nut.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Kellet, Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Po Kau, Ta Tit Yan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 7011, 25062, 25671.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by J. Lamont (in Herb. Hance No. 18992, K, BM) in 1874.
records.uses:
Material (wood), environmental.
