records.text:
Castanopsis sclerophylla (Lindl.) Schott. 苦櫧
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 638. 1912; FFJ 1: 385, fig. 337. 1982; FRPS 22: 25, pl. 4: 8 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 321. 1999.
Quercus sclerophylla Lindl. in Lindl. & Paxton, Fl. Gard. 1: 59. 1850; FKH 252. 1912.

Tree, 5–10 m tall. Bark shallowly fissured, exfoliating in flakes. Branchlets of the current year reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.2–1.6(–2.5) cm; leaf blade oblong to ovateelliptic, sometimes obovate-elliptic, 6–12(–17) × 2–5(–7) cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, ± oblique, apex acuminate or abruptly and shortly caudate, margin serrulate from middle to apex, glabrous, abaxially silver-grey when full grown; lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein, slender but evident. Male spikes usually solitary, axillary, 5 –15 cm. Female spikes to 15 cm; rachis glabrous. Cupule globose to subglobose 1.4 –1.5 cm in diam., enclosing completely (when young) or 3/5 – 4/5 (when mature) of nut, wall ca. 1 mm thick, yellowish brown puberulent outside; bracts scale-like, mostly reduced and base united in 6–7 zoned ribs. Nut 1 per cupule, subglobose , 1–1.4 cm in diam., top puberulous; scar to 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Happy Valley, Garden Road. C. P. Lau 40.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, E Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Materials (wood), food (nut).

Casuarina cunninghamiana Miq. 細枝木麻黃（肯氏木麻黃）
Rev. Crit. Casuar. 56. 1848; FRPS 20(1): 3, pl. 1: 1–10. 1982; FOC 4: 107. 1999; FGD 5: 380. 2003.

Tree dioecious, to 25(–35) m tall, often with suckers from roots. Bark finely fissured and scaly, grey, inner layer pale red. Ultimate branchlets spreading to slightly pendulous, dark green, greyish green, or glaucous-green when dry, 15 –38 cm × 0.5 –0.7 mm; internodes 4 – 5 mm. Leaves erect, 8(–10) per whorl, narrowly lanceolate. Male spikes 1.2–2(– 4) cm. Cones ellipsoid or subglobose, 7–12 mm, truncate at both ends; apex of bracteoles acute. Samaras 3– 5 mm including wing.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3324.
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, agroforestry.

Casuarina equisetifolia L. 木麻黃
Amoen. Acad. 4: 143. 1759; FRPS 20(1): 2. 1982; FOC 4: 106. 1999; FGD 5: 379. 2003.

Tree monoecious, to 35 m tall, without suckers from roots. Bark scaly, inner layer red-brown on old trees. Ultimate branchlets usually pendulous, greyish green, 10 –27 cm × 0.8 – 0.9 mm; internodes (2.5 –)4 –9 mm. Leaves erect and appressed to branchlets, 6 – 8 per whorl, lanceolate or triangular, 1–3 mm. Male inflorescences 1– 4 cm. Cones ellipsoid, 1.2–2.5 cm, greyish green or yellowish brown tomentose when young, glabrous at maturity, base and apex truncate to obtuse; apex of bracteoles slightly obtuse or acute. Samaras 5 – 8 mm including wing.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 35816, 34685.
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian. Native to Australia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Planted as wind breaks and for soil stabilizations.
records.uses: Planted as wind breaks and for soil stabilizations.

records.text:
Catharanthus roseus (L.) G. Don 長春花
Gen. Hist. 4: 95. 1837; FRPS 63: 83, pl. 28. 1977; FGD 1: 447, fig. 500. 1987; FOC 16: 157. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 48, fig. 16, 1999.
Vinca rosea L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 10), 2: 944. 1759; FHK 220. 1861; FKH 168. 1912.
Catharanthus roseus (L.) G. Don var. albus G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 95. 1837.

Subshrubs or perennial herbs, erect or decumbent, 30–50(–100) cm tall. Young stems puberulent. Leaves obovate or elliptic, 2.5–9 × 1–3.5 cm, herbaceous, apex minutely apiculate, lateral veins 7–11 on each side of midvein. Corolla pink or white with a purple, pink or less often yellow eye; tube 2.5–3 cm, pilose inside, throat villous; lobes broadly obovate, 1.2–2 cm. Stamens attached to the top of corolla‑tube. Ovary 1.9–3 mm, puberulent; style including pistil head 1.9–2.1 cm. Follicles narrowly oblong, longitudinally grooved, apex acute, sparsely puberulent, 15–30 × 3 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2709; HK sheet 9065, 18647.
Distribution: S, SW & C China (cultivated); native to E Africa; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Oct.; fruiting: Oct. – Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Catunaregam spinosa (Thunb.) Tirveng. 山石榴（山蒲桃）
Bull. Mus. Hist. Nat. (Paris) 35: 13. 1978; Taxon 27(5 – 6): 515. 1979; Verdc., Kew Bull. 36(3): 505. 1981; FRPS 71(1): 338, pl. 89. 1999; FYN 15: 170, pl. 34: 3 – 5. 2003; FGD 6: 177, fig. 91. 2005.
Randia dumetorum (Retz.) Lam., Tabl. Encycl. 2: 227. 1794; FHK 154. 1861; FKH 131. 1912.
Randia spinosa (Thunb.) Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 981. 1826; FHN 3: 321. 1974.
Gardenia spinosa Thunb., Diss. Gard. 7: 16. 1780.

Shrubs or small trees, 1–10 m tall, many‑branched, armed with axillary stout thorns. Leaves papary or subleathery; petioles 2–8 mm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; stipules membranous, ovate, 3–4.5 mm, apex acute, deciduous, leaf blade obovate or oblong‑obovate, 2–8(–11) × 2–4.5(–5.7) cm, base cuneate, apex acute, or obtuse, sparsely and minutely strigose on adaxial surface and along midvein and lateral veins when young, soon glabrescent; lateral veins slender, 4–7 on each side of midvein. Flowers solitary or 2 – 3 clustered at apex of lateral short branches or tufts of leaves. Pedicels 2–5 mm, together with calyx covered with tawny long hairs. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped or ovoid, 4–6 mm; lobes 5, broadly elliptic, 5–6 × 4–4.5 mm, apex broadly acute, green, 3 – 5‑veined. Corolla bell‑shaped, initially white, later turning pale yellow; tube 5 – 6 mm, densely sericeous near apex outside, with a ring of long hairs on upper part inside; lobes 5, broadly elliptic to subrounded, 8 – 11 × 8 – 9 mm, apex rounded, spreading. Anthers linear‑oblong, ca. 3 mm, exserted. Style 4–6 mm; stigma globular, with 2 coherent lobes. Berry globose, 2–4 cm in diam., crowned by persistent calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap, Mount Nicholson, Tai Po, Lai Chi Wo, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 696; Y. S. Lau 1895; HK sheet 40206.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: May–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental (hedges), medicinal (folklore).

Cayratia corniculata (Benth.) Gagnep. 角花烏蘞莓
Notul. Syst. (Paris) 1: 347. 1911; FHN 3: 27. 1947; FFJ 3: 387, fig. 273. 1987; FRPS 48(2): 84. 1998.
Vitis corniculata Benth., FHK 54. 1861; FKH 65. 1912.
Vitis angustifolia Wall. ex Benth., FHK 54. 1861.
Columella corniculata (Benth.) Merr., Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 11: 133. 1916.

Herbaceous vine, glabrous except petals. Branchlets terete, with longitudinal ridges; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves 5-foliolate, membranous; petiole 2–4.5 cm. Central leaflet broadly lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 4–9 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin with 5 or 6 teeth on each side; petiolules to 3 cm. Lateral leaflets smaller, ovate-elliptic, 2–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base usually oblique, cuneate or rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin sparsely denticulate; petiolules 0.4–1.5 cm. Peduncle 3–3.5 cm. Pedicels 1.5–2.5 mm. Calyx shallowly cupular, margin membranous, apex truncate. Petals ovate-elliptic, 1.5–2.5 mm, sparsely papillose-hairy, corniculate at apex. Anthers ovoid. Berry globose, 8–10 mm in diam., black when matured, 2–4-seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 330, 2245; HK sheet 40004.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Malaysia, Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island.

Cayratia japonica (Thunb. ex Murray) Gagnep. 烏蘞莓
Notul. Syst. (Paris) 1: 349. 1911; FGZ 424. 1956; FHN 3: 28. 1974; FFJ 3: 387. 1987; FRPS 48(2): 78. 1998.
Cayratia trifolia (L.) Domin var. quinquefolia W. T. Wang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 17(3): 8. 92. 1979.
Vitis japonica Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14: 244. 1784; FKH 65. 1912.

Herbaceous vine, stems, young leaves and petioles reddish. Branchlets terete, with longitudinal ridges, pubescent when young, glabrescent; tendrils 2–3-furcate. Leaves 5-foliolate, or sometimes trifoliolate, membranous; petioles 1.5–10 cm; central leaflet elliptic, oblong to narrowly ovate, 2.5–9(–14.5) × 1.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely serrate, pubescent along veins on both surfaces or subglabrous, petiolule 0.5–2.5 cm; lateral leaflets smaller. Peduncle 1–13 cm. Pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx cupular, papillose or nearly glabrous, margin entire or undulate. Petals triangular-ovate, 1–1.5 mm, not corniculate at apex. Anthers ovoid. Berry globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., 2–4-seeded.

Locality: Tsiu Hang, Tai Po, Shan Liu. Y. W. Lam 325, 903; HK sheet 36084.
Distribution: E, C, S & SW China; India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Ceiba pentandra (L.) Gaertn. 吉貝（美洲木棉）
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 244. 1791; FGD 3: 216. 1995.
Bombax pentandrum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 511. 1753.

Tree, up to 30 m tall; branches verticillate, spiny when young. Petioles 7–14 cm; petiolules 3– 4 mm; leaflets 5–9, thin-leathery, oblong-lanceolate, 5 –16 × 1.5– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or remotely and minutely toothed toward the apex, glabrous, glaucous abaxially. Flowers fascicled in leaf axils on upper part of twigs, sometimes solitary, reddish or yellowish white. Pedicels 2.5 – 5 cm. Calyx 1.25 –2 cm, glabrous adaxially. Petals obovate-oblong, 2.5 – 4 cm, densely white-villous abaxially. Filaments in 5 bundles, each bundle with 1 anther; anthers reniform. Ovary glabrous; styles 2.5–3.5 cm, stigma clavate, 5-lobed. Capsule ellipsoid, 7.5 –15 × 3– 5 cm, stipe 7–25 cm, dehiscing into 5 valves, densely covered with silky wool abaxially. Seeds globose, endocarp leathery, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2277; HK sheet 35803.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental, timber.

Celastrus aculeatus Merr. 過山楓

Lingnan Sci. J. 13(1): 37. 1934; FRPS 45(3): 123. 1999.


Deciduous climbing shrub. Branches glabrous, densely lenticellate; young shoots initially tawny pubescent. Petioles 8–18 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic or broadly elliptic, 5–10 × 2.4–5 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex shortly acuminate to subrounded with a short, abrupt point, margin sparsely serrate, glabrous; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein, veinlets obscure. Cymes 3-flowered, axillary and lateral; peduncles 2–5 mm; pedicels 2–3 mm, articulate just below calyx, together with peduncle tawny pubescent when young. Male flowers: sepals triangular, ca. 2.5 mm; petals oblong-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm; disk entire, ± fleshy; stamens 3–4 mm; filaments papillose. Capsules subglobose, 7–8 mm in diam. Seeds black crescent-shaped.


Locality: Wan Chai Gap, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Lam Chung. Y. S. Lam 106; H. C. Tang 2087; Y. S. Lau 1010.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.

Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering: Feb. –Apr.; fruiting: Jul. –Sep.

Notes: The species was reported as Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. (Check List HK Plants 50. 1993) and C. kusanoi Hayata (Check List HK Plants 171. 2002; 62. 2004) previously.

Celastrus hindsii Benth. 青江藤
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 334. 1851; FKH 62. 1912; FRPS 45(3): 125. 1999.
Celastrus monospermus auct. non Roxb.: FHK 63. 1861.

Evergreen shrub, trailing or climbing, glabrous; branchlets purplish. Petioles 6–7 mm; leaf blade oblong to elliptic-oblanceolate, 7–14 × 3–6 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate or acute, margin sparsely serrate, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, veinlets closely spaced and parallel, conspicuous. Cymose-panicles terminal or axillary, 5–14 cm. Pedicels 4–5 mm, articulate just above middle. Male flowers: calyx lobes nearly semi-orbicular, 1 mm; petals oblong, 2.5 mm, greenish, ciliate; disk cupular, shallowly lobed; stamens seated on margin of disk. Female flowers: ovary subglobose; staminodes ca. 1 mm. Capsules subglobose, 7–9 × 6.5–8.5 mm, opening in 3 valves. Seeds subglobose, 5–8 mm, enclosed in orange pulpy aril.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 131; N. H. Li 58; F. W. Xing 6780.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen (R. B. Hinds s. n., K) was collected from Hong Kong Island in 1841.

Celastrus monospermus Roxb. 獨子藤（單子南蛇藤）
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 394. 1824; FRPS 45(3): 126. 1999.
Celastrus benthamii Rehd. & Wild., Pl. Wilson., 2: 358. 1915.
Celastrus championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc., 3: 334. 1851; FHK 64. 1861; FKH 61. 1912.

Evergreen climbing shrub, glabrous; branchlets minutely striate. Petioles ca. 15 mm; leaf blade subleathery, oblong to narrowly elliptic, 5–17 × 3–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrulate, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein. Cymose-panicles, dichotomous, 5–14 cm; peduncles 1–2.5 cm; pedicels 1–4 mm, articulate at the base. Male flowers: calyx-lobes deltoid-semiorbicular, ca. 1 mm; petals oblong, ca. 2.5 mm, reflexed; disk fleshy, shallowly 5-lobed; stamens 5, inserted under disk, 2.5–3 mm. Female flowers: pistils bottle-shaped, stigma 3-lobed; staminodes 1 mm. Capsules broadly ellipsoidal, rarely globose, 10–18 × 9–14 mm, opening in 3 valves, 1-seeded. Seeds elliptic, 10–15 × 6–9 mm, glabrous, arils purple-brown.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 408; N. H. Li 57; Y. W. Lam 579.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; India, Vietnam, Myanmar, Pakistan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Sep.
Notes: The type specimen of Celastrus championii Benth. (J. G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island.

Celastrus stylosus Wall. 顯柱南蛇藤
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 401– 402. 1824; FRPS 45(3): 119. 1999.

Deciduous climbing shrub; branchlets usually glabrous, lenticellate. Petioles 1.3–2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic, rarely oblong-obovate, 6.5–12.5 × 3–7 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex shortly to abruptly acuminate, margin sparsely serrate, glabrous; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, veinlets distinct. Cymes 3–7-flowered, axillary and lateral; peduncles 8–20 mm; pedicels 5–7 mm, articulate below middle. Male flowers: sepals ovate to elliptic, 1–2 mm; petals oblong-obovate, 3.5–4 mm, margin slightly erose; disk thin, slightly lobed; stamens slightly longer than petals, smooth or papillose. Capsules, subglobose, 6.5–8 mm in diam. Seeds slightly curved.

Locality: Kam Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. W. J. Tutcher 9151; P. S. Choi 392; N. H. Li 57.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering: Feb. –Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Sep.

Celosia argentea L. 青葙（野雞冠）
Sp. Pl. 205. 1753; FHK 284. 1861; FKH 213. 1912; FHN 1: 402. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 400, pl. 187. 1996; FRPS 25(2): 200, pl. 44: 1– 4. 1996; FGD 4: 102. 2000; FOC 5: 416. 2003.

Annual herb, 30–100 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, angled, young shoots purplish. Leaves alternate; petioles 2– 15 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 5 –8 × 1–3 cm, gradually narrowed to both ends, margin entire or very minutely serrulate. Spikes terminal, 3 –10 cm, densely flowered; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, 3–5 mm, white, scarious. Perianth-segments oblong-lanceolate, 6–8 mm, pink, with white and scarious margins. Stamens 5; filaments and anthers pink or purplish; style 3– 5 mm, minutely 2-lobed. Utricles ovoid, 3 –3.5 mm, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Kowloon, Sha Tin, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 11720; Y. S. Lau 1157, 2192.
Distribution: A pantropical weed, dispersed over most parts of China.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal, animal food.

Celosia argentea L. var. cristata (L.) Kuntze 雞冠花
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 541. 1891; FHN 1: 403. 1964; FGD 4: 103. 2000.
Celosia cristata L., Sp. Pl. 205. 1753; FHN 1: 403. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 403. 1996; FRPS 25(2): 201. 1979; FOC 5: 416. 2003.

This variety is a tetraploid cultigen derived from Celosia argentea. Leaves ovate, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 6–15 × 1.5– 6 cm. Spikes terminal, the main axis strongly flattened or much branched, cristate or feathered, or with plumy slender spikes and panicles; bracts, bracteoles and perianth variously colored, ranging from white to orange, red to purple.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 23009, 23010.
Distribution: Cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Cultivated in flowering beds or as a pot plant. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Celtis biondii Pamp. 紫彈朴
Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital., n.s., 17: 252, fig. 3. 1910; FGD 2: 220. 1991; FOC 5: 17. 2003.

Deciduous tree, 4–18 m tall; young shoots densely red-brown pubescent, glabrescent when old. Petioles 4 –7 mm; leaves leathery, abaxially, often becoming black when dry, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 4 –9 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, obtuse, oblique, apex acuminate, margin serrate on upper half, often densely strigose abaxially, shorter and sparser adaxially, 3-veined. Sepals 4, elliptic. Stamens 4. Drupes often 2, axillary, subglobose, 6 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent when young. Fruits stalk 12–15 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Peng Chau. Y. W. Lam 22271; F. W. Xing 9125.
Distribution: S, E, & C China, Gansu, Shaanxi; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.

Celtis sinensis Pers. 朴樹
Syn. Pl. 1: 292. 1805; FHK 324. 1861; FKH 243. 1912, p.p.; FHN 2: 368. 1965; FGD 2: 220. 1965; FOC 5: 18. 2003.

Deciduous tree, about 10 m tall; bark grey. Young shoots pubescent, glabrescent when old. Petioles 5–10 mm; leaves ovate or ovate-oblong, 5 –10 × 2.5 –5 cm, base rounded and slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate, margin serrate on upper half, pubescent on both surfaces when young, glabrescent when old, prominently 3-veined. Male cymes at lower part of annual branchlets. Female flowers: axillary at upper branchlets; sepals 4; stamens 4, opposite to sepals; filaments hairy at base; ovary ovate, grown on densely white tomentose torus; style 2, reflexed. Drupes red-brown, subglobose, 5–7 mm in diam., fruit stalk equal or slightly longer than petioles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong and widely planted. H. C. Tang 519; Y. W. Lam 897.
Distribution: S, E, C & SW China.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Timber, fibre.

Celtis timorensis Span. 假玉桂
Linnaea 15: 343. 1841; FOC 5: 16. 2003.
Celtis cinnamomea Lindl. ex Planch., Ann. Sci. Nat. ser. 3, Bot. 10: 303. 1848; FGD 2: 221, fig. 142. 1991.
Celtis philippensis auct. non Blanco: FHK 324. 1861; FKH 243. 1912; FHN 2: 368. 1965; FGD 2: 221. 1991.

Tree, 5–8 m tall. Branchlets slender, adpressedly red-brown pubescent when young. Petioles ca. 1 cm; leaves subleathery, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 5 –15 × 2.5 – 6 cm, base oblique, obtuse or cuneate, apex acuminate, often cuspidate, entire or obscurely serrulate upper most, 3-veined. Cymes 2–3-branched, 15 –25 mm, elongated to 3.5–4 cm when fruiting, adpressed red-brown pubescent. Sepals 4, oblong, ciliate; styles 2. Drupes ellipsoid, 8 × 5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Shing Mun, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 841, 2970.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Fibre, timber.

Cenchrus echinatus L. 蒺藜草
Sp. Pl. 2: 1050. 1753; FRPS 10(1): 375, pl. 114: 14–22. 1990; FFJ 6: 191. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 462, pl. 192. 2000; FOC 22: 553. 2006; FGD 9: 445, fig. 228. 2009.
Cenchrus calyculatus auct. non Gavan: FHN 4: 440, pl. 1231. 1977.

Annual herb. Culms geniculate, usually rooting at basal nodes, ca. 50 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, compressed, keeled, glabrous or upper margins ciliate, overlapping at base; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 5–20(–40) × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous to pubescent; ligule ca. 1 mm, a ring of hairs. Inflorescence a solitary raceme, 3–10 × ca. 1 cm; axis scabrous; burs globose, 0.4–1 cm, truncate, stipe pubescent, all spines and bristles whorled and retrorsely barbed, inner spines connate for 1/3–1/2 their length forming a globose cupule, dorsally fuzz, margins white ciliate, outer spines in 2 divergent whorls, a median whorl of stout rigid spines equaling the inner teeth, and an outermost whorl of relatively few short, slender bristles. Spikelets 2–4(–6) in bur, elliptic-lanceolate, 2-floret; lower glume triangular-lanceolate, 1/3–1/2 spikelet length, acute, 1-veined; upper glume 2/3 – 3/4 spikelet length, 5-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5-veined, palea 2/3 length of lower lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma 5-veined, inrolled embraced same texture palea; lodicules absent; style penicillate. Caryopsis depressed-globose.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Hang, Kau Wa Keng, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 1560, 1972; Y. W. Lam 5.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; a widespread weed of the tropics and subtropics, native to America.
Ecology: Sandy grasslands near seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Summer.

Centella asiatica (L.) Urb. 積雪草（崩大碗）

Fl. Bras. 11: 287, pl. 78, fig. 1. 1879; FRPS 55(1): 31, pl. 10. 1979; FGD 2: 329, fig. 217. 1991; FOC 14: 18. 2005.

Hydrocotyle asiatica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 234. 1753; FHK 134. 1861; FKH 116. 1912.

Hydrocotyle lurida Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. (Walpers) 2: 690. 1852.


Perennial herb; stems long-creeping, glabrous or sparsely hairy, rooting at nodes. Leaves alternate or 2–3 congested at nodes; petioles 1.5–15 cm; leaf blade orbicular-reniform, entire, crenate or lobulate, 2.5–5 cm in diam., glabrous or nearly so. Umbels axillary 3–5-flowered; peduncles 2–8 mm; pedicels very short or obsolete; involucral bracts 2, ovate, membranous, persistent. Fruit ca. 3 × 3–4 mm, flattened, depressed, ovate-globose, loosely pubescent when young, soon glabrescent.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2390, 2666; S. P. Lau 178.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread throughout tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.

Ecology: Shady and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.

Notes: The type specimen of Hydrocotyle lurida was collected from Hong Kong.

Centipeda minima (L.) A. Br. & Aschers. 石胡荽
Index Sem. (Berlin) 1867: App. 6. 1867; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1 – 2): 21. 1966; FRPS 76(1): 132. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 898. 1998; FGD 8: 201, fig. 121. 2007.
Myriogyne minuta (G. Forst) Less., Linnaea 6: 219. 1831; FHK 186. 1861; FKH 146. 1912.
Cotula minuta G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 57. 1786.
Artemisia minima L., Sp. Pl. 849. 1753.

Small annual herbs, branches many; stem decumbent, 4–20 cm or longer, glabrous or covered with cobwebby hair. Leaves alternate, sessile, oblanceolate to spatulate, 5–18 × 1–7 mm, base cuneate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or with 1–2 pairs of teeth in upper half, glabrous or cobwebby hairy on both surfaces, abaxially glandular‑punctate. Capitula small, depressed globose, 3–4 mm in diam., solitary and axillary, sessile or subsessile. Involucres depressed hemispherical; phyllaries in 2–3 series, outer 1–2 layers oblong and larger in size, inner layers obovate‑oblong, all herbaceous green, with hyaline and lacerate margins and apices, glabrous or loosely cobwebby on abaxial side. Marginal florets pistillate, many‑seriate, corolla narrowly tubular, 0.2 mm, shorter than the ovary, pale greenish yellow in colour, minutely 2–3‑toothed at apex. Central florets bisexual, corolla tubular, 0.5 mm, apex 4‑lobed, colour pale purple. All florets fertile. Cypselae narrowly and obliquely oblong, 1–1.2 mm in length, 4‑angulate, base cuneate, brown in colour, ribs pale brown and hairy. Pappus wanting.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2187; S. L. Thrower 1350 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11889 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, India, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of farmlands. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Centotheca lappacea (L.) Desv. 假淡竹葉
Nouv. Bull. Sci. Soc. Philm. Paris 2: 189. 1810; FKH 329. 1912; FFJ 6: 132, fig. 104. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 332. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 34, pl. 3: 4. 2002; FOC 22: 445. 2006; FGD 9: 384, fig. 192. 2009.
Cenchrus lappaceus L., Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 2: 1488. 1763.

Perennial herb, 40–100 cm tall. Culms loosely tufted, erect, smooth, 4–7-noded, clothed at base with few cataphylls. Leaf blades lanceolate-elliptic, 4–15 × 1–3 cm, base petiole-like, abaxial surface glabrous with cross veins, adaxial surface glabrous or loosely hispidulous, apex long attenuate; ligule 1–1.5 mm, apex rounded; leaf sheaths smooth or ciliate along one margin. Panicle large, open, 12–25 cm, primary branches up to 15 cm; pedicels 2.5–3 mm, slender, pubescent. Spikelets 4–8 mm, florets 2–3; glumes subleathery, elliptic, apex acute, (3–)5-veined; lower glume 2–2.5 mm, upper glume 3–3.5 mm; lowest lemma ca. 4 mm, subleathery, 7-veined, glabrous, apex acute; upper lemmas slightly smaller than the lowest, coarsely setose with tuberclebased, reflexing bristles near upper margins, the hairs retrorsely hispid when mature; paleae ca. 3 mm, firm, 2-keeled, ciliolate along keels, apex acute, hispid on the upper part of keel. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, 1–1.2 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu & S. Liu 155; S. Y. Hu 8595 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, W tropical Africa, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, shady roadsides and other moist shady ground. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Centranthera cochinchinensis (Lour.) Merr. 胡麻草
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. 24(2): 353. 1935; FHN 3: 512. 1974; FOC 18: 85. 1998; FGD 4: 395. 2000.
Digitalis cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 378. 1790.
Centranthera hispida auct. non. R. Br.: FHK 254. 1861; FKH 190. 1912.
Centranthera brunoniana auct. non Wall.: FKH 190. 1912; FGZ 592. 1956.

Herbs, (13–)30–60 cm tall. Stems erect, simple or few‑branched, hispid. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate, sessile, linear‑lanceolate, 2–3 cm × 3–4 mm, margin entire and subrevolute, hispid on both surfaces. Bracts shorter than or rarely as long as corolla. Flowers borne above middle of stem. Calyx spathaceous, 7–10 mm, densely hispid, apex shallowly 3‑lobed. Corolla reddish white with yellow stripes, 3.5–4 cm; lower lip 3‑lobed, orbicular, upper lip orbicular, 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, filaments woolly. Ovary glabrous. Capsules ovoid, 4–8 mm, apex mucronate. Seeds yellow, small, spirally striate.

Locality: Wan Chai, Mount Violet, Ma On Shan, Yung Shue O. Y. S. Lau 2787, 3260; Y. W. Lam 423.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Centranthera tranquebarica (Spreng.) Merr. ex Merr. & Chun 矮胡麻草
Sunyatsenia 5: 182. 1940; FOC 18: 85. 1998; FGD 4: 395, fig. 239. 2000.
Razumovia tranquebarica Spreng., Mant. Prim. Fl. Hal. 45. 1807.
Centranthera tonkinensis Bonati, Not. Syst. Lecomte 1: 337. 1911; FGD 4: 395. 2000.
Centranthera humifusa Wall., Scroph. Ind. 50. 1835; Rep. Bot. & Forest. Dep. Hongk. (1916) 22. 1917.

Herbs, 5–30 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate, slender, branched from base. Leaves linear‑lanceolate, 8–25 × 2– 3 mm, glabrous on both surfaces or abaxially short hairy. Bracts longer than corolla. Calyx ovate, ca. 3 mm at anthesis, hispidulous. Corolla yellow, brown striate, 9–13 mm; throat densely black punctate; lower lip lobes suboblong, ca. 3 mm; upper lip lobes suborbicular, 3 × 2 mm. Stamens 2–5 mm; filaments white lanose‑villous. Ovary oblong, 3 × 2.5 mm, glabrous. Capsules subglobose, 4–5 × ca. 4 mm, as long as persistent calyx. Seeds yellow, cylindric‑conical, ca. 1 mm; testa reticulate.

Locality: Shau Kei Wan, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 11444; HK sheet 39461.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Cephalantheropsis obcordata (Lindl.) Ormerod 黃蘭（嶺南黃蘭）
Orchid Digest. 62: 157. 1998; FOC 25: 289. 2009.
Bletia obcordata Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 123. 1831.
Calanthe gracilis Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 251. 1833; FKH 254. 1912.
Cephalantheropsis gracilis (Lindl.) S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 213. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 56, fig. 25. 1977; FRPS 18: 255, pl. 45: 7. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 795. 2000; Check List HK Plants 372. 2002; 129. 2004.
Limatodes gracilis (Lindl.) Lindl., Fol. Orchid. Limatodis 1. 1855; FHK 359. 1861.

Perennial herb. Stems cane-like growing close together on a short creeping rhizome, to 1 m tall; internodes many, 5–10 cm. Leaves 5–8, papery, oblong-lanceolate, 30 × 5–8 cm; scapes 60 cm, rachis 5–20 cm; bracts membraneous. Flowers yellow; segments oblong, 9–11 × 4 mm, hairy outside; lip trilobed, lateral lobes erect; epichile 2-lobed, crisped; column fleshy; anther terminal; pollinia 8.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Pat Sin Leng, Sheung Tsat Muk Kiu. S. Y. Hu 10013, 10014 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 502.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Clinging to wet rocks in shade along streams. Flowering: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.

Cephalanthus tetrandrus (Roxb.) Ridsdale & Bakh. f. 風箱樹
Blumea 23(1): 182. 1976; FRPS 71(1): 279, pl. 75. 1999; FGD 6: 163, fig. 82. 2005.
Cephalanthus occidentalis auct. non L.: Dunn & Tutch., FKH 124. 1912.
Nauclea tetrandra Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 2: 125. 1824.

Deciduous shrubs or small trees, 1–5 m tall. Branchlets pubescent when young, brown and glabrous in age. Stipules broadly ovate, 3–5 mm, usually with a black gland at the cuspidate apex. Leaves opposite or in whorls, subleathery; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 10–15 × 3–5 cm, base obtuse or subcordate, apex acute, adaxially glabrous or sparsely puberulent, abaxially glabrous or densely pubescent, especially in the axils of veins; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein. Flowers heads globular, across calyces 8–12 cm in diam., terminal or axillary; peduncle 2.5–6 cm, simple or branched, pubescent. Calyx‑tube 2–3 mm, sparsely puberulent; lobes 4, apex obtuse, densely puberulent, usually with a black gland at the sinus of the lobes. Corolla white, tube 7–12 mm, glabrous abaxially, puberulent adaxially; lobes 4, oblong, with a black gland at the sinus of the lobes. Ovary inferior; style long exserted. Aggregate fruit globose, 10–20 mm in diam.; nutlets 4–6 mm, with persistent calyx at apex.

Locality: San Wai, Ta Kwu Ling. W. J. Tutcher 8153; HK sheet 40705.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina to India and Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets by streams. Flowering: Late spring to autumn; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cephalostachyum pergracile Munro 香糯竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 141. 1868; HKB 56. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 29, pl. 6: 1–10. 1996; FOC 22: 55. 2006; FGD 9: 279. 2009.
Schizostachyum pergracile (Munro) R. B. Majumdar, Fl. Ind. Enumerat.-Monocot. 282. 1989.

Culms erect, 9–12 m, 5–7.5 cm in diam., apically drooping; internodes 30–45 cm, initially densely appressed setose; wall thin. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, brown, shorter than culms, 10–15 × 15–20 cm, thickly leathery, smooth, densely glossy black-brown setose; auricles rounded, undulate, hirsute near margins; ligule inconspicuous; blade reflexed, ovate-acuminate, ca. 5 cm, articulate with sheath, adaxially densely hairy. Leaf sheath margins ciliate; ligule ciliate; blade narrowly lanceolate, 15–35 × 2.5–3.8(–6) cm, base rounded. Inflorescences capitate, at nodes of leafless branch, 1.5–3 cm in diam., subtended by bracts. Pseudospikelet 1.2–2 × ca. 0.2 cm, densely yellow hirtellous, rachilla extended, 5–6 mm. Glumes 2–3, 0.6–1.1 cm; lemma 1.3–1.8 cm, densely hairy, apex long mucronate or awned; palea about as long as or longer than lemma, apex bifid; lodicules lanceolate, narrow, membranous, apex acute. Anthers purple. Stigmas 3. Caryopsis 6–8 × 2–3 mm, glabrous, apex with persistent style base.

Locality: Tai Po Kau (cultivated).
Distribution: S Yunnan; Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Cultivated. New Shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cerastium fontanum Baumg. subsp. trivale (Link) Jalas 簇生卷耳

Arch. Soc. Zool. Bot. Fenn. “Vanamo” 18: 63. 1963; FRPS 26: 86, pl. 20: 1– 6. 1996.

Cerastium fontanum Baumg. subsp. vulgare (Hartm.) Greuter, Willdenowia 12: 37. 1982; FOC 6: 35. 2001.

Cerastium triviale Link, Enum. Pl. Hort. Berol. 1: 433. 1821, nom. illeg. superfl.

Cerastium vulgare Hartm., Handb. Skand. Fl. 182. 1820.


Perennial or annual herb, 15 –30 cm tall. Stems single or tufted, erect, white-puberulent or glandular hairy. Leaves subsessile, basal ones spathulate or obovate-oblanceolate; cauline ones ovate, narrowly ovate-oblong to lanceolate, 1–3(–4) × 0.3–1(–1.2) cm, apex acute or obtuse, puberulent on both surfaces. Cymes terminal. Pedicels slender, 5–25 mm, densely glandular-hairy, turned down after flowering. Sepals 5, oblong-lanceolate, 5.5– 6.5 mm, densely glandular hairy outside. Petals 5, white, obovate-oblong, equaling or slightly shorter than sepals, apex shallowly 2-lobed, glabrous. Stamens shorter than petals; filaments glabrous. Ovary oblong‑ellipsoid; styles 5, linear. Capsule cylindrical, 8–10 mm, opening at the top into 10 teeth.


Locality: Sheung Shui, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 2821, 3054; HK sheet 2521.

Distribution: Dispersed over most parts of China; Mongolia, Korea, Japan, Indochina, India, Iran.

Ecology: Grassy slopes, forest margins. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Ceratophyllum demersum L. 金魚藻
Sp. Pl. 992. 1753; FRPS 27: 16, fig. 6. 1979.

Submerged perennial herb. Stems 40–50 cm, branched. Leaves 4 –12 in whorls, once or twice forked, segments filiform or linear, 15–20 × 0.1–0.5 mm, finely toothed on one side, apex with whitish cartilaginous tip. Bracts 9 –12, linear, 1.5 –2 mm, pale green, translucent, 3-toothed and with purplish hairs at apex. Stamens 10–16, ± congested. Ovary ovoid; style subulate. Achenes broadly ellipsoid, 4 –5 × 1.5 –2 mm, with 3 spines.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 26750, 26752.
Distribution: Cosmopolitan.
Ecology: Ponds and streams, in still or slow fresh water; also cultivated in aquarium as an ornamental plant.

Cerbera manghas L. 海杧果
Sp. Pl. 1: 208. 1753; FRPS 63: 33, pl. 11. 1977; FGD 1: 432, fig. 478. 1987; FOC 16: 165. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 67. 1999.
Cerbera odollam auct. non Gaertn.: FHK 219. 1861; FKH 168. 1912.

Trees to 8 m tall. Bark grey‑brown; branches whorled, marked with leaf scars. Petioles 2.5 – 6 cm; leaf blade elliptic to obovate, 6 – 37 × 2.3 – 7.8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate; lateral veins 20 – 30 on each side of midvein, diverging almost at right angle to midvein. Inflorescence few‑ to many‑flowered, lax, 7 – 30 cm. Pedicels terete, 1 – 2 cm. Flowers 4 – 7 cm in diam. Corolla white, with a pink eye; tube 2.5 – 4 cm, villous inside; lobes ovate, falcate, 1.5 – 2.5 cm. Drupes 5.8 × 4 – 6 cm, smooth. Seeds usually single.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 278; L. T. Lo 127, 485.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Hillslopes near seashore and beaches above the high‑tide mark. Flowering: Apr. – Nov.; fruiting: Jul. – Dec.

Cestrum nocturnum L. 夜香樹
Sp. Pl. 191. 1753; FGZ 577. 1956; FRPS 67(1): 149, pl. 40: 6 – 10. 1978; FGD 2: 387, fig. 266: 1–3. 1991; FFJ 5: 6, fig. 4. 1993; FOC 17: 331. 1994.

Shrubs 2–3 m tall, with slender reclining branches, glabrous throughout. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.5–1 cm; leaf blade oblong‑ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 5–15 × 2–4.5 cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, ± oblique, margin entire. Flowers in terminal and axillary cymes, 5–10 cm, very fragrant at night. Pedicels ca. 0.5 mm. Calyx narrowly campanulate, 2.5–3 mm, apex 5‑toothed. Corolla salverform, pale green to cream‑coloured; tube slender, ca. 2 cm, slightly contracted at throat; apex 5‑lobed; lobes triangular, ca. 4 mm, erect or spreading. Stamens 5, attached to the upper part of corolla‑tube; filaments with a pair of dentoid appendages at the base; anthers reaching the throat. Ovary ovoid, with a short stipe; style equaling corolla‑tube; stigma capitate. Berry oblong, 6–7 mm, 1‑seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 664, 2959; L. T. Lo 596.
Distribution: Native to S America; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Chamaecrista leschenaultiana (DC.) Degener 短葉決明
Fl. Hawaiiensis Fam. 169b. 1934.
Cassia leschenaultiana DC., Mem. Soc. Phys. Geneve 2: 132. 1824; FRPS 39: 128. 1988; FGD 5: 181. 2003; FGX 2: 466, pl. 194: 5 –8. 2005.
Cassia mimosoides var. wallichiana (DC.) Baker, Fl. Brit. India 2(5): 266. 1878; FHN 2: 234. 1965.
Cassia mimosoides subsp. leschenaultiana (DC.) Ohashi, J. Jap. Bot. 50: 308. 1975; FTW 3: 201. 1977.
Cassia wallichiana DC., Mem. Soc. Phys. Geneve 2: 132. 1824.
Chamaecrista nictitans var. glabrata (Vogel) H. S. Irwin & Barneby, Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 35: 822. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 3: 180. 1993.

Annual or perennial shrubby herb, 0.3 – 0.8(–1) m tall. Stems erect, branched; young branches densely yellow pubescent. Stipules linear-subulate, 7 – 9 mm, persistent. Inflorescences axillary, 1– several-flowered. Bracteoles ca. 5 mm. Sepals linear, ca. 1 cm, sparsely yellow pubescent abaxially. Petals orange-yellow, slightly longer than or as long as sepals. Stamens 10, sometimes 1–3 reduced. Ovary densely white pubescent. Pods flat, 2.5 – 5 × 0.5 cm, 8 –16-seeded.

Locality: Po Toi Islands, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1046; F. W. Xing 9629.
Distribution: SW to SE China; India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia leschenaultiana DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 135. 2002; 51. 2004).

Chamaecrista mimosoides (L.) Greene 含羞草決明（山扁豆）
Pittonia 4(20D): 27. 1899; FTW ed. 2, 3: 180. 1993.
Cassia mimosoides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 379. 1753; FHK 98. 1861; FKH 89. 1912; FHN 2: 234. 1965; FRPS 39: 126, pl. 42: 1 – 4. 1988; FGD 5: 181. 2003; FGX 2: 464, pl. 194: 1 – 4. 2005.

Annual or perennial shrubby herb, 30–60 cm tall, many-branched. Branches slender, puberulous. Stipules linear-subulate, 4–7 mm, obviously striped, persistent. Leaves 4–8 cm, with a disciform gland at the distal end of petiole or below the lowest pair of leaflets; leaflets 20–50 pairs, reddish brown when dry, linear-falcate, 3–4 × 1 mm, apex shortly acute, asymmetrical; midveins near the upper margin. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2–several in short racemes. Bracteoles ca. 3 mm. Sepals 6–8 mm, apex acute, sparsely pubescent abaxially. Petals yellow, slightly longer than sepals, unequal, shortly stipitate. Stamens 10, 5 longer and 5 shorter. Pods falcate, flat, 2.5–5 × 0.4 cm, fruiting pedicels 1.5–2 cm. Seeds 10–16.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 182, 384; Y. W. Lam 1024.
Distribution: SW to SE China; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Thickets, slopes and open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Uses: Green manure, medicinal (folklore).

Cheirostylis chinensis Rolfe 中華叉柱蘭（甌蘭）
Ann. Bot. 9: 158. 1895, et J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 43. 1903; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 44, fig. 16. 1977; FRPS 17: 166, pl. 21: 12–15. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 796, pl. 335. 2000; FGD 7: 355. 2006; FOC 25: 62. 2009.

Perennial saxicolous small herb; rhizomes succulent, 4.5 cm long, 1.2 cm thick; stem erect. Leaves ovate-cordate, 2.5–4 × 2–3 cm, acute. Flowers white, resupinate, 4–5 in a terminal raceme; scape 15–20 cm, villose glandular; pedicels 2–3 mm; calyx urceolate, 6–7 mm, tube 4 mm, 3-lobed, the odd lobe dorsal; petals oblique lanceolate, 5 mm; lip bilobed, base gibbous, bilobed at the apex, fringed; column 2 mm; anthers orange; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, granular; ovary glandular-villose.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 205; HK sheet 33354.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Philippines.
Ecology: Damp moss-covered rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

Cheirostylis clibborndyeri S. Y. Hu & Barreto 叉柱蘭（太魯閣叉柱蘭）
Chung Chi Journal. 13(2): 15, fig. 8. 1976; FOC 25: 60. 2009.
Cheirostylis hungyehensis T. P. Lin, Native Orch. Taiwan 2: 73(f.) 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 798, pl. 336. 2000.
Cheirostylis tatewakii auct. non Masam.: Masam. ex S. S. Ying, Col. Illust. Fl. Taiwan 4: 802. 1992; FRPS 17: 164. 1999; FGD 7: 355. 2006; Check List HK Plants 373. 2002; 130. 2004.

Small succulent perennial herb, 12–15 cm tall at flowering time; rhizome worm-like, 4–6 cm, fleshy, consisting of 4 to 6 internodes, those on the ends thinner. Leaves 3 or 4, terminal to the apical end; leaf blades ovate, 1–2 × 0.7–1.2 cm, green and variegated with lighter green bands, apex acute. Flowers white or greenish white, 5 or 6 in a raceme terminal to a scape of 12–15 cm; pedicels 2 or 3 mm; calyx tubular, 5 mm including the 2 mm free portions; petals white, 5 mm, oblanceolate-spathulate; lip white, unguiculate, entire, 2–5 mm, apex tongue-like, 2 mm; column 1 mm, with 2 arms at the apex, each with a gland; anther sagittate, orange; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, granular; ovary ellipsoidal, 5 cm, glabrous. Fruit ovoid-ellipsoidal, 7 mm, with tubercles on ridges.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9900, 13055 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 289; Y. W. Lam 216.
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Wet rocks in shade of forest-ravines and hillslopes. Flowering: Jan–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13055, K, holotype; A, CUHK, HK, PE, isotypes) was collected by R. Clibborn-Dyer from Victoria Peak on 6 Mar. 1973.

Cheirostylis jamesleungii S. Y. Hu & Barreto 粉紅叉柱蘭（毛甌蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 13, fig. 6. 1976; FRPS 17: 166. 1999; FGD 7: 355. 2006; FOC 25: 62. 2009.

Small succulent perennial herb, before flowering, the plant consisting of a worm-like rhizome, 4–5 cm long, 2–6 mm in diam., with 6 – 7 internodes. At flowering time, a slender scape 10 cm high emerged from the apical end. Leaves 3 terminal to rhizome, petiolate; leaf blade cordate, 3–8 mm long and wide, acute, papillose. Flowers 2–3, subsessile; calyx 4 mm, oblique tubular; petals oblique-lanceolate; lip white, 2-lobed, 5 mm, 3 mm across apex, each lobe with 5–6 coarse teeth; anther dorsal; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary villose, 5 mm, pink.

Locality: Lantau Island S. Y. Hu 9720A (K).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Moist places, alt. 600 m. Flowering: Mar.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 9720A, K) was collected by J. Leung from Lantau Island on 22 Mar. 1970.

Cheirostylis liukiuensis Masam. 琉球叉柱蘭
J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 2: 36. 1930; FTW ed. 2, 5: 800. 2000; FOC 25: 60. 2009.

Perennial herb, 5–9 cm tall; rhizome moniliform, 8–10 mm in diam., sometimes branching, fleshy; roots hair-like. Leaves 3–4, scattered along stem; leaf blades ovate to ovate-orbicular, 2–3 × 1–2 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute, abaxially reddish purple, adaxially dark greyish green; petiole-like base and sheath 0.7–1 cm. Flowers white or greenish white, 5 or 7 in a terminal raceme. Peduncle hairy, initially ca. 5 cm, gradually elongate to 10 – 20 cm after anthesis; pedicels 2–3 mm; calyx tubular, pubescent, 4.5–5 mm including the 2.5 mm free portions; petals white, 4.5 mm, oblong-oblanceolate; lip white, 6 mm, tripartite; column erect, 2.2–2.4 mm, with 2 arms at the apex; anther broadly ovoid; pollinia ca. 1.2 mm; ovary ellipsoidal, pubescent.

Locality: Sha Tin (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyus).
Ecology: Shade of forest-ravines. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.

Cheirostylis monteiroi S. Y. Hu & Barreto 箭藥叉柱蘭（大花甌蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 15, fig. 7. 1976; FRPS 17: 169. 1999; FGD 7: 356. 2006; FOC 25: 61. 2009.
Cheirostylis flabellata auct. non Wight: Icon. Pl. Ind. Orient. 5: 16, pl. 1727. 1852; FKH 267. 1912.

Perennial succulent saxicolous herb; rhizomes fleshy, with 4–6 internodes. Leaves 2–3, ovate, 1.2–1.6 × 0.8 –1 cm, acute or acuminate. Flowers white, 2–8 terminal to a scape of 7–9 cm; calyx tubular, without distinct sepals, glabrous, tube 3 mm; lobes 2 mm; petals white, oblique-lanceolate, 5 × 1.5 mm; lip bilobed, 4.5 mm, adnate to column, apical lobes suborbicular, 7 mm in diam., white with green centre, fringed; column 1 mm, with an anterior arm of 1.5 mm on each side; anther yellow, sagittate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary cylindrical, 5–6 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Violet Hill. S. Y. Hu 13056 (CUHK); U. A. On s.n. (HK sheet 7133).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Rocks in ravine of forests, alt. 300 m. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13056, K, holotype; A, CUHK, HK, PE, isotypes) was collected by R. Clibborn-Dyer from Violet Hill on 6 Mar. 1973. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Chenopodium acuminatum Willd. subsp. virgatum (Thunb.) Kitam. 狹葉尖頭葉藜
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 20: 206. 1962; FGD 3: 65. 1995; FOC 5: 380. 2003.
Chenopodium virgatum Thunb., Nov. Act. Reg. Soc. Upsal. 143. 1815.
Chenopodium vachelii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 269. 1838.
Chenopodium acuminatum auct. non Willd.: FHK 28. 1861; FKH 215. 1912; FHN 1: 397. 1964.

Annual herb, up to 80 cm tall. Stems erect, angulate, much branched; branches ascending, farinose. Petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm; leaves narrowly ovate, oblong or lanceolate, 1– 4 × 0.5 –2.5 cm, base cuneate, rounded or truncate, apex acute or acuminate, mucronate, margin entire, translucent, greenish and glabrous adaxially, grey-white and farinose abaxially. Inflorescence a terminal leafy panicle. Flowers bisexual; perianth-lobes 5, broadly ovate, margin membranaceous, ridged near central. Stamens 5. Utricles compressed-globose, smooth. Seeds black, 1 mm in diam., shiny.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung, Tsing Lung Tau, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Pui O, Tung Chung. HK sheet 36802, 36805.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Hebei, Liaoning; Japan.
Ecology: Wastelands near seashore and on lakes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Chenopodium album L. 藜
Sp. Pl. 219. 1753; FHK 282. 1861; FKH 215. 1912; FRPS 25(2): 98. 1979; FGD 3: 67. 1995; FOC 5: 383. 2003.

Annual herb, 30 –150 cm tall. Stems rough, erect, angulate, with green or purple striae. Leaves petiolate, rhomboid-ovate to broad-lanceolate, 3– 6 × 2.5– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, lower ones more or less sinuately toothed or angular, upper ones usually narrow and entire. Clusters of flowers in short axillary spikes, either dense or interrupted, upper ones forming a long panicle, leafy at base. Flowers bisexual; perianth-lobes 5, broad-ovate to elliptic, keeled abaxially, mealy-white, apex emarginated. Stamens 5, exserted; stigmas 2. Utricles compressedglobose, smooth; entirely enclosed in perianth. Seeds horizontal, black, 1.2–1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Lung. Y. S. Lau 960, 2156.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; temperate and tropical regions.
Ecology: Farmland and roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal, noxious weed.

Chenopodium ficifolium Sm. 小藜
Fl. Brit. 1: 276. 1800; FKH 215. 1912; FOC 5: 383. 2003.
Chenopodium serotinum auct. non L.: FHN 1: 396. 1964; FGD 3: 66. 1995.

Annual herb, 20 – 50 cm tall. Stems erect, much branched; branches ascending, farinose when young. Leaves petiolate, ovateoblong, 2.5 – 5 × 1–3.5 cm, often shallowly 3-lobed, central lobe oblong, margin sinuate-toothed, farinose abaxially. Inflorescence a terminal leafy panicle, 4–12 cm; perianth subglobose, deeply 5- lobed; lobes broadly ovate, keeled and farinose abaxially. Stamens 5, exserted; stigmas 2, filiform. Utricles compressed-globose, smooth. Seeds horizontal, black, 1 mm in diam., shiny.

Locality: Ha Hang. K. Wong s.n. (HK sheet 23122, 23158).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; temperate and tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Farmlands, wastelands and roadsides. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Notes: The name Chenopodium serotinum L. has often been misapplied to this species but in fact refers to a species of Atriplex (FOC 5: 383. 2003).

Chimonanthus praecox (L.) Link. 臘梅
Enum. Pl. Hort. Berol. 2: 66. 1822; FRPS 30(2): 7. 1979; P.T. Li & Z. Q. Li, Higher Pl. China 3: 204. 2000.
Calycanthus praecox L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 718. 1762.

Shrub to 3 m tall, almost evergreen in Hong Kong; buds with imbricate scales. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 5 mm; leaf blade papery to sub-leathery, elliptic-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 5 –25 × 2– 8 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous except the puberulent veins on abaxial surface. Flowers solitary on branches of the previous year's growth, fragrant, 2– 4 cm in diam., the outer tepals yellow, elliptic to oblong; the inner ones shorter, base clawed and striped purple brown. Fruit (enlarged receptacle) urn-shaped, 2–5 × 1–2.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens.
Distribution: Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Anhui, Henan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov. to Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species is deciduous in N China, flowering before the leaves appear, but in Hong Kong it is almost evergreen.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species is deciduous in N China, flowering before the leaves appear, but in Hong Kong it is almost evergreen.

records.text:
Chimonobambusa quadrangularis (Franceschi) Makino 方竹（四方竹）
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 28: 153. 1914; HKB 57. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 340, pl. 93: 1 – 6. 1996; FOC 22: 158. 2006; FGD 9: 314, fig. 148. 2009.
Bambusa quadrangularis Franceschi, Bull. Soc. Tosc. Ortic. 5: 401. 1880.
Arundinaria quadrangularis (Franceschi) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 9: 71. 1895.
Phyllostachys quadrangularis (Franceschi) Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. 36: 443. 1904.

Culms erect, 3–8 m tall, to 2.5 cm in diam.; internodes obtusely 4-angled, 8–22 cm, sparsely coarsely scabrid, apically more densely so; nodes prominent, supra-nodal ridge raised at branching nodes, level at branchless nodes, lower nodes each with a ring of short, declined root thorns; sheath scar corky, initially with a fulvous, tomentose, minutely setose ring. Culm sheaths deciduous, shorter than internodes, papery, veins prominent, transverse veinlets purple-brown, margins ciliate; auricles, oral setae, and ligule absent; blade deciduous, subulate, 3–5 mm, articulate. Leaves 2–5 per ultimate branch; sheaths leathery, glabrous, margins apically ciliate; oral setae deciduous, erect, glabrate; ligule truncate, short, ciliate, with minute setae; pseudopetiole ca. 1.8 mm; blade elliptical to lanceolate, 8–29 × 1–2.7 cm, papery, abaxially initially pubescent, adaxially glabrous, secondary veins 4–7-paired, tertiary veins 5–7, apex acuminate. Inflorescence racemose or paniculate, terminal ones slender, glabrous, subtended by persistent, gradually enlarged bracts. Spikelets (1–)2–4, 2–3 cm, slender; florets 2–5, basal absent to 2 rudimentary. Glumes 1–3, lanceolate, 4–5 mm; lemma green, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, subequal to palea, papery, 5–7-veined; lodicules narrowly ovate. Anthers 3.5–4 mm. Stigmas 2.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 16457, 16459.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang; Japan, cultivated in Europe and N America.
Ecology: New shoots: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Chionanthus ramiflorus Roxb. 枝花李欖
Fl. Ind. ed. 1, 106–107. 1820; FOC 15: 294. 1996; FGD 5: 421. 2003.
Linociera ramiflora (Roxb.) Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 52. 1837; FHN 3: 216, fig. 668. 1974; FRPS 61: 114, pl. 32: 1 – 3. 1992; Check List HK Plants 243. 2002; 84. 2004.
Linociera ramiflora f. pubisepala L. C. Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3(3): 352. 1955.

Trees, 6–15(–25) m tall, branchlets terete, usually compressed at nodes, lenticellate. Petiole 2–5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade elliptic, oblong‑elliptic, or ovate‑elliptic, rarely obovate‑oblong, (5–)8–20(–30) × (2–)4–7(–12) cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, or blunt, subleathery, glabrous, densely dotted with raised pimples adaxially; lateral veins 7–15 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces or obscure adaxially. Panicles usually axillary, loose, 2.5–12 cm; pedicel 1–5 mm. Calyx ca. 1 mm; lobes ovate, ca. 0.5 mm, acute or blunt. Corolla white or yellow, 2.5 – 5.5; lobes oblong, 2–2.5 mm, slightly united at base. Anthers elliptic. Ovary elliptic; style very short or absent. Drupe blue‑black, pruinose, elliptic or long‑elliptic, 1–3 × 0.5–1.5 cm.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Ma On Shan, Ngau Ngak Shan, Wu Kau Tang. F. W. Xing 8116, 8627; Y. W. Lam 643.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Nepal, India, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets in ravines. Flowering: Dec.–Jun. of the following year; fruiting: May–Mar. of the following year.

Chionanthus retusus Lindl. & Paxton 流蘇樹
Paxt. Fl. Gard. 3: 85, fig. 273. 1852; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 375, fig. 306. 1989; FRPS 61: 119, pl. 33: 1 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 293. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 129, pl. 48. 1998; FGD 5: 419, fig. 221. 2003.
Chionanthus serrulatus Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 3: 150–151, fig. 28. 1913.

Deciduous trees or shrubs to 20 m tall. Branchlets terete, glabrous, or pubescent when young. Petioles 0.5–2 cm, densely covered with curly hairs; leaf blade oblong, elliptic, or orbicular, sometimes ovate or obovate, 3–10 × 2– 4.5 cm, base rounded to cuneate, rarely subcordate, apex blunt, sometimes retuse or acute, ± leathery, abaxially villous along midvein, adaxially villous or glabrescent except on veins; lateral veins 3 or 4 on each side of midvein, slightly raised on both surfaces. Cymose panicles terminal on lateral shoots, 3–12 cm; pedicels 0.8–1 cm, glabrous. Calyx cup‑shaped, 4‑parted; lobes deltoid, 1–2 mm. Corolla white, 4‑parted; tube 2–4 mm; lobes linear‑spatulate, 1.5–2.5 cm. Anthers long ovate, 1.5–2 mm; connectives elongate. Drupe 1–1.5 cm × 6–10 mm, blue‑black or black, pruinose, ovoid.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 18463.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Chionographis chinensis K. Krause 白絲草（中國白絲草）
Notizbl. Bot. Gart. Berlin-Dahlem 10: 807. 1929; FRPS 14: 14. 1980; FOC 24: 88. 2000; FGD 6: 344, fig. 198. 2005.

Perennial herb, with short thick rhizome. Leaves radical, rosulate; petioles 1–6 cm; leaf blade ellipitic to ovate-oblong, (1–)3–7 × 1–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin slightly undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Scape 14–40 cm, with 4–5 alternate, small, bract-like leaves. Flowers fragrant, in a dense flowered terminal spike. Perianth segments 6, white to pale yellow; upper 3–4 narrowly spatulate, 3–8 × 0.2–0.5 mm; lower 2–3 much smaller, sometimes absent. Stamens 6, unequal, 1–1.5 mm, 3 longer than others; anthers subcordate-ovate, with locules confluent. Capsule ellipsoidal to ± obovoid, ca. 4 × 2 mm, ± 3-angled, dehiscent distally.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 217; HK sheet 30333.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, other shady and damp places. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Chionographis japonica Maxim. previously (Check List HK Plants 80. 1993).

Chirita sinensis Lindl. 唇柱苣苔
Edward's Bot. Reg. 30: pl. 59. 1844; FHK 259. 1861; FKH 194. 1912; FRPS 69: 382. 1990; FOC 18: 334. 1998; FGD 6: 273. 2005.
Didymocarpus sinensis (Lindl.) H. Lév., Compt. Rend. Hebd. Seances Acad. Sci. 34: 427. 1906.
Chirita sinensis Lindl. var. angustifolia Dunn, J. Bot. 45(539): 403. 1907; FGD 6: 274. 2005.

Herbs, perennial, stemless. Leaves basal; petiole 4–8 × 1 cm, villose; leaf blade papery, ovate to oblong, (4–)5–10 × (2–)3.5–8 cm, base attenuate to cordate, apex obtuse or rounded, margin repand to crenate, appressed pubescent and pilose, glandular; lateral veins 3 – 5 pairs, inconspicuous. Cymes axillary, 2–6‑flowered; peduncle 8 – 14 cm, villose; bracts 2, ovate, 1–3 × 0.5–2 cm, apex obtuse, margin entire or crenulate, villous; pedicel 1 – 1.5 cm, densely pilose. Calyx 5‑sect from base; segments equal, ovate, 4–5 mm, outside puberulent to pilose, inside glabrous, margin entire, apex obtuse or rounded. Corolla purple or white, 3.5–4 cm, inside tinged purple with 2 yellow longitudinal lines adaxially of tube, outside sparsely pubescent to pilose, inside puberulent only on purple spot of adaxial lip; tube tubular to broadly funnelform, often gibbous abaxially, 2–2.5 cm long, ca. 1 cm in diam.; limb 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 5 mm long; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes 0.7–1.5 cm long, ovate, apex obtuse. Stamens 2, adnate to abaxial side of corolla tube near middle, include; filaments ca. 1.5 cm, puberulent; anthers ca. 3 mm, glabrous to pubescent; staminodes 2, ca. 6 mm. Disk ring‑like, entire. Pistil puberulent; ovary linear, ca. 2 cm; style 5 mm; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule ca. 4 cm, puberulent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2235; Y. S. Lau 417, 2761.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Wet shady places by streams or rocks in valleys. Flowering: May–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.

Chloranthus serratus (Thunb.) Roem. & Schult. 及己（四葉對）
Syst. Veg. 3: 461. 1818; FRPS 20(1): 91. 1982; FGD 3: 21, fig. 15. 1995; FOC 4: 136. 1999.
Nigrina serrata Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 7: 142, pl. 5, fig. 1. 1815.

Perennial herb, 15–50 cm tall. Rhizomes procumbent, short, ca. 3 mm in diam., with many yellowish brown fibrous roots. Stems erect, glabrous, with distinct swollen nodes. Leaves opposite, 4–6 on the upper part of stem; petiole 0.8–2.5 cm; leaf blade papery, elliptic, obovate, ovate-lanceolate, suborbicular, or broadly elliptic, sometimes ovate-elliptic or oblong, 7–15 × 3–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrulate, with glandular-tipped teeth, glabrous or pubescent on veins abaxially; lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midvein. Spikes terminal, sometimes axillary, 1 or 2- or 3- branched; peduncles 1–3.5 cm; bracts triangular or nearly semiorbicular, usually several toothed at apex. Flowers white. Stamens 3, on outside of apical part of ovary; connectives oblong, connate at basal part, central anther with 2 locules; lateral ones each with 1 locule;. Ovary ovoid; style absent; stigma thick, short. Drupes green, globose or pyriform.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Kap Lung. HK Sheet 34863, 34448.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Anhui, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Japan.
Ecology: Wet places in forests, swamps, streamsides, ravines. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal.

Chloranthus spicatus (Thunb.) Makino 金粟蘭（珍珠蘭）
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 180. 1902; FRPS 20(1): 83, pl. 26: 1–5. 1982; FGD 3: 20. 1995; FOC 4: 134. 1999.
Nigrina spicata Thunb., Nov. Gen. Pl. 59. 1783.
Chloranthus inconspicuous Swartz, Philos. Trans. 78: 359, t. 15. 1787; FHK 334. 1861; FKH 221. 1912.

Subshrub, erect or slightly prostrate at base, 30–60 cm. Stems terete, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.8–1.8 cm, leaf blade thick papery, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 5–11 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin crenate-serrate, with glandular-tipped teeth, abaxially pale yellowish green, adaxially deep green and shiny; lateral veins 6–8 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces. Spikes arranged, in panicles, usually terminal, rarely axillary; bracts triangular. Flowers yellowish green, small, very fragrant. Stamens 3; connectives connate at base; central anther sometimes apex shallowly 3-lobed, with one 2 loucles; lateral anthers smaller, each with one locule. Ovary obovoid.

Locality: Cultivated. HK Sheet 23950.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal.

Chloris barbata Sw. 孟仁草
Fl. Ind. Occid. 1: 200. 1797; FHK 429. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 75, pl. 23: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 162. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 403. 2000; FOC 22: 490. 2006; FGD 9: 374. 2009.
Andropogon barbatus L., Mant. Pl. Altera 302. 1771, non Linnaeus (1759).
Chloris inflata Link, Enum. Hort. Berol. 1: 105. 1821.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb. Culms ascending from the decumbent base, 0.2–1 m tall, usually rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades usually folded, 10–40 × 0.3–0.8 cm, glabrous, apex acute; ligule ciliate, ca. 0.3 mm; leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous. Inflorescence of 5–9 digitately arranged spikes; spikes erect or ascending, 3–8 cm, ± flexuous and purplish; rachis scabrous. Spikelets with 3- or 4-flowered, 3(–4)-awned; glumes membranous, conspicuously 1-veined; the lower deltoid-lanceolate, 1.2–1.5 mm, apex acute; the upper narrowly lanceolate, 1.7–2.5 mm, apex shortly mucronate; lower floret fertile, lemmas elliptic in side view, 1.7–2.5 mm, pilose on keel, ciliate on upper margins with 1–1.5 mm hairs, awn 4.5–7 mm; palea ca. 2.2 mm; upper florets sterile, lemmas empty, inflated, overlapping to form a knob at side of fertile floret; second lemma turbinate, truncate, 1–1.5 mm, glabrous or sparsely appressed-pilose on back, awn 2.5–7 mm. Stamens 3, anthers ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.6 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 851, 882; HK sheet 42064.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical to warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Beaches, wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.

Chloris formosana (Honda) Keng 台灣虎尾草
FHN 4: 385, fig. 1193. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 403. 2000; FGD 9: 375. 2009;
Chloris barbata Sw. var. formosana Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 40: 437. 1926.

Annual herb. Culms erect from the decumbent base, 20–70 cm tall, usually rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades usually folded, 4–40 × 0.2–0.3 cm, glabrous, sometimes scabrous on adaxial surface and margins; ligule 0.5–1 mm, ciliate; leaf sheaths laterally compressed, keeled, glabrous, apex acute. Inflorescence of 4–9 digitately arranged spikes; spikes 3–8 cm, erect or somewhat lax, pallid or purplish; rachis puberulous. Spikelets 3-flowered, 3-awned, ca. 2.5 mm (excluding the awn), sessile; glumes membranous, 1-veined; lower glume 1–2 mm, lanceolate, apex acute; upper glume 2–3 mm, with a sinus at the apex, midrib prolong into an awn; lemma of fertile floret ovate, 2.3–3 mm, with a lateral groove, glabrous on keel, densely ciliate on upper margins with ca. 1 mm hairs; awn (2–)4–6 mm; palea as long as the lemma, rounded at the apex, 2-keeled; upper florets sterile, lemmas empty, flattened or only slightly inflated, overlapping to form a knob at side of fertile floret; second lemma oblanceolate, truncate, 1.6–2 mm, glabrous, awn 2.5–5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.6 mm, ellipsoidal.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau. HK sheet 34207, 34660, 41957.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy or gravelly soils near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Chloris virgata Sw. 虎尾草
Fl. Ind. Occid. 1: 203. 1797; FKH 327. 1912; FTW 5: 464. 1978; FRPS 10(1): 79. pl. 22: 1–4. 1990; FOC 22: 489. 2006; FGD 9: 374. 2009.
Chloris caudata Trin. ex Bunge, Enum. Pl. Chin. Bor. 70. 1833.

Annual. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, 12–75 cm tall. Basal leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat or folded, 5–30 cm, 2–7 mm wide; ligule 0.5–1 mm. Racemes digitate, 5–12, erect or slightly slanting, 2–10 cm; rachis scabrous or hispid. Spikelets with 2 or 3 florets, 2-awned; lower glume 1.8–2.2 mm; upper glume 3–4 mm, acuminate; lemma of fertile floret obovatelanceolate in side view, 2.8–3.5 mm, keel gibbous, conspicuously bearded on upper margins with a spreading tuft of 2.5–3.5 mm silky hairs, margins, keel and flanks silky-ciliate or glabrous; awn 5–15 mm; second floret sterile, oblong, glabrous, awn 4–10 mm; third floret occasionally present, reduced to a small clavate scale, awnless.

Locality: High Island Reservoir. HK Sheet 34207.
Distribution: Common in China; Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan; Africa, America, SW Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Common on stony slopes, steppes, sandy riversides, roadsides, fields, plantations, frequent on walls and roofs, alt. 3700 m. Flowering and fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Chlorophytum laxum R. Br. 小花吊蘭
Prodr. 277. 1810; FKH 279. 1912; FRPS 14: 45, pl. 10: 4–5. 1980; FOC 24: 206. 2000; FGD 6: 364, fig. 217. 2005.
Anthericum parviflorum (Wight) Benth., FHK 373. 1861.
Phalangium parviflorum Wight, Icon. Pl. Ind. Orient., pl. 2039. 1840.

Perennial herb. Rhizome inconspicuous, with many ± fleshy roots. Leaves sessile, subdistichous, linear, grass-like, 10–20 cm × 3–5 mm, glabrous, 11–15-veined. Scape slender, erect or arching, 10–30 cm, simple or sometimes with 1–2 branches. Raceme laxly flowered; bracts narrowly deltoid to lanceolate, very small; pedicels 2–4 mm, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit, articulate proximally. Perianth segments 6, white to greenish white, lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, closely 3-veined. Stamens shorter than perianth segments; anthers subglobose, ca. 0.4 mm. Capsule broadly globose to broadly obcordate, ca. 3 × 5(–7.5) mm; seeds usually 1 per valve.

Locality: Chai Wan, Tai Tam Tuk, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2590; Y. W. Lam 907.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Thailand, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Chlorophytum comosum (Thunb.) Jacques, native to S Africa, is cultivated in Hong Kong as an ornamental. It can be easily recognized by its rosulate (not subdistichous) leaves and larger flowers (perianth segments to 1 cm long).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: Chlorophytum comosum (Thunb.) Jacques, native to S Africa, is cultivated in Hong Kong as an ornamental. It can be easily recognized by its rosulate (not subdistichous) leaves and larger flowers (perianth segments to 1 cm long).

records.text:
Choerospondias axillaris (Roxb.) B. L. Burtt & A. W. Hill 南酸棗（酸棗）
Ann. Bot. (Oxford), n.s. 1: 254. 1937; FHN 3: 106, fig. 602. 1974; FRPS 45(1): 86, pl. 26: 7– 11. 1980; FFJ 3: 252, fig. 172. 1987; FGD 2: 312, fig. 204. 1991.
Spondias axillaris Roxb., Fl. Ind. (ed. 1832) 2: 453. 1832.
Poupartia fordii Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 26(3): t. 2557. 1898; FKH 12. 1912.

Deciduous tree, 7–20 m tall; branchlets ± robust, dark purplish brown, glabrous, lenticellate. Leaves 20–25 cm including the petiole; rachis puberulous; petioles inflated at base, puberulous; leaflets 7–15, opposite or alternate; petiolules 0.5–1.2 cm, glabrous to puberulous; blade papery, ovate to lanceolate, 4–12 × 2–4.5 cm, base ± oblique, broadly cuneate to rounded, apex long-acuminate, entire or serrate at the base, puberulous or subglabrous on both surfaces, or with tufts of hair in the axils of veins abaxially; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein, prominent on both surfaces. Male inflorescences 4–10 cm, minutely pubescent to glabrous. Calyx minutely pubescent to glabrous; lobes triangular, ca. 1 mm. Petals purple, oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm. Stamens exserted. Female flower solitary in axils of distal leaves, larger than male flowers. Ovary ca. 1.5 mm, 5-locular. Drupe ellipsoidal or ovoid, yellow at maturity, 2.5–3 × 2 cm, rounded at both ends.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also planted. H. C. Tang 2327; L. T. Lo 18, 495.
Distribution: S & SW China; S Japan, NE India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos and Thailand.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Early summer; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Roadside tree, timber.

Chorisia speciosa A. St.-Hil. 絲木棉（美人樹）
Pl. Usuel. Bras. 63. 1828.

Deciduous trees, 8–15 m tall, trunk with short spines. Leaves spirally arranged on the current years’ branches; petioles 4 –12 cm, petiolules 6–15 mm, glabrous; leaflets 6–7, firmly papery, narrowly oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, the center one larger, 5.5–12 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex ± acuminate, margin serrate above the base, glabrous, adaxially bright green, abaxially pale green. Flowers solitary or 2–3 clustered in axils of apical leaves, sometimes appearing a cymose-panicle due to the subtending leaves falling off. Pedicels 1.5 –2.5 cm. Caylx cup-shaped, 2–2.5 cm, apex shallowly 4–6-lobed; lobes unequal, apex obtuse or sub-rounded. Petals 5, distinct, oblanceolate, 9.5 –10.5 cm, broadest at middle (ca. 3.5 cm), dark red, pink, white with dark strips on the proximal half of adaxial surface. Outer stamen-tube ca. 1.8 cm; anthers 10, sterile, dark purplish red, covered with crisped hairs; inner stamen-tube 8.5 cm, with 5 fertile anthers. Style slightly longer than inner stamen-tube; stigma capitate, hairy.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 39817, 39818.
Distribution: Brazil, S to SW America; cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Chorisis repens (L.) DC. 苦蕒菜
Prodr. 7: 178. 1838; FRPS 80(1): 260. 1997.
Prenanthes repens L., Sp. Pl. 798. 1753.
Ixeris repens (L.) A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. n.s. 6: 397. 1858; FHK 194. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 6. 1967; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1001. 1998; FGD 8: 269. 2007; Check List HK Plants 284. 2002; 97. 2004.
Lactuca repens (L.) Benth. ex Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19: 532. 1874; FKH 150. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem creeping, up to 2 m or longer, glabrous, forming adventitious roots and long‑petiolate leaves at nodes. Leaves thick, broad‑ovate, 2.5–3 × 1.5–5 cm, palmatilobed to palmatisect, segments usually 3 or occasionally 5, elliptic, regularly or irregularly orbicular, apex rounded or broadly obtuse, margin mucronulate, shallowly sinuate or sometimes with an obtuse tooth or a small elliptic lobe on one side, both surfaces glabrous; petioles 1.5–6.5 cm, base clasping. Flowering branch axillary, 3–5.5 cm, bearing ovate‑oblong bracteoles, with 2–6 capitula arranged as loose corymbs. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite; peduncles 0.8–1.5 cm. Involucres cylindric, 10–12 mm; phyllaries glabrous abaxially, slightly ciliate and sometimes tinged purple near apex, 2–3‑seriate; outer two layers ovate or elliptic, 3–6 × 1.2–1.8 mm, apex acute or acuminate; inner layer lanceolate‑oblong, 10–12 × 2–2.5 mm, acute. Ligulate florets 12 – 20 per head, corolla yellow, about 10–11 mm, lower tube 4 mm, ligule 6–7 mm, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae fusiform, brown, slightly compressed, 4 × 1 mm, glabrous, obtusely 10‑ribbed, apex attenuate into a thick beak about 0.5 – 1 × 0.2–0.3 mm. Pappus growing on the beak, white in colour, 5 mm, minutely scaberulous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 465; HK sheet 16359; S. Y. Hu 12472 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in S, E, N & NE China; also in Japan, Korea, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.

Christia obcordata (Poir.) Bakh. f. 鋪地蝙蝠草
Reinwardtia 6(1): 91. 1961; FRPS 41: 83. 1995; FGD 5: 285. 2003.
Hedysarum obcordatum Poir., Encycl. 6(2): 425– 426. 1805.
Lourea obcordata (Poir.) Desv., J. Bot. Agric. 1: 122. 1813; FHK 82. 1861; FKH 80. 1912.

Perennial prostrate herb, 15 – 60 cm tall. Stems slender, grey pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, rarely 1-foliolate; leaflets membranous, terminal one reniform, obcordate or orbicular-deltoid, 5–15 × 10–20 mm, apex truncate, emarginate, lateral ones smaller, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 3 – 5 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 3 – 18 cm. Calyx campanulate, hairy, 2 mm, 5-toothed, distinctly reticulate. Corolla violet or roseate, slightly longer than calyx. Pods enclosed by persistent calyx; segments 4–5, orbicular, 2.5 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 1917; L. T. Lo 491; Y. W. Lam 1133.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; S & SE Asia to N Australia.
Ecology: Open field. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: May– Sep.

Chrysanthemum segetum L. 茼蒿
Sp. Pl. 889. 1753; FKH 146. 1912; FRPS 76(1): 22. 1983; FGD 8: 199, fig. 118. 2007.
Chrysanthemum coronarium var. spatiosum Bailey, Gentes Herb. 1: 47. 1920; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(12): 27. 1966.

Annual herbs; stems erect, 20–80 cm tall, fleshy, glabrous or subglabrous. Leaves elliptic, obovate‑elliptic to oblanceolate, margin coarsely and irregularly serrate or dentate, sometimes shallowly pinnatifid, 4–12 × 3–4 cm, base cuneate, sessile, apex rounded, both surfaces glabrous; leaves in upper stem smaller in size. Capitulum solitary at stem terminal or few at branches; peduncle about 5 cm. Involucres broad hemispherical, 1–2 cm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, imbricate, ovate, rigidly herbaceous with margin and apices hyaline, the membranous apices of the innermost layer broaden as appendages. Marginal ligulate florets 1.5 cm, ligule linear‑oblong, yellow. Central tubular florets yellow or orange‑yellow, lower portion narrow and glandular, upper portion campanulate, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae of ray florets trigonous and narrowly 2‑winged on both lateral sides; those of disk florets oblong, inconspicuously ribbed, with one side broadly hard‑winged. Pappus absent.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 9409A, 11875 (CUHK); HK sheet 2665.
Distribution: Cultivated all over China; native to Mediterranean region.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Chrysophyllum lanceolatum (Blume) A. DC. var. stellatocarpon P. Royen 金葉樹
Blumea. 9: 32. 1958; FHN 3: 161, fig. 642. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 60, pl. 11: 3 – 4. 1987; FGD 2: 350. 1991; FOC 15: 208. 1996.
Chrysophyllum roxburghii auct. non G. Don: FKH 160. 1912.

Trees, 10 –20 m or taller. Branchlets yellow pubescent when young. Petioles shorter than 1 cm, glabrous or pubescent; leaf blade thinly leathery, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, slightly asymmetrical, 7–12 × 1.8–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate-cuspidate, glabrous on both surfaces, yellowish brown when dry; lateral veins many, closely spaced and slender. Flowers fascicled. Pedicels slender, 5 mm, rusty pubescent. Sepals 5, slightly pubescent abaxially, margin fimbriate. Corolla white, broadly campanulate, 1.8–3 mm, glabrous, 5-lobed; lobes as long as sepals, margin fimbriate. Stamens 5, filaments short. Ovary ca. 0.6 mm, 5-locular, 5-ridged, rusty tomentose. Style ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous. Berry subglobose, brown to purplish black, 5-ridged, 1.5 –2 cm in diam., rusty tomentose when young. Seeds often 5, obovoid, compressed laterally, 11–13 mm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung, Lai Chi Wo. HK sheet 3092; K. Y. Tam 121; Y. W. Lam 1898.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Indochina to Singapore.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (root & leaves), food (fruit).

Chrysopogon aciculatus (Retz.) Trin. 竹節草
Fund. Agrost. 188. 1820; FHK 424. 1861; FKH 324. 1912; FHN 4: 472, fig. 1259. 1977; FFJ 6: 265, fig. 236. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 135, pl. 32: 1–7. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 534, pl. 226. 2000; FOC 22: 604. 2006; FGD 9: 491, fig. 259. 2009.
Andropogon aciculatus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 22. 1789.

Perennial rhizomatous and stoloniferous herb. Culms erect or prostrate at the base, 20–50 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous or ciliate at mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose near base, apex obtuse, margins serrate; ligule short, 0.1–0.3 mm. Panicle terminal, purplish brown, oblong or linear-oblong; branches erect when dry, slender, usually whorled, each bearing one sessile and perfect, two pedicellate and sterile spikelet. Sessile spikelet cylindrical-lanceolate; callus acicular, 4–6 mm, bearded with golden hairs, obliquely attached to branch apex; glumes leathery; lower glume lanceolate, 2-keeled upward, keels hispidulous, apex acute to 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, setulose on back and upper keel, acuminate or mucronate, mucro 1–2 mm; lower lemma linear-oblong, slightly shorter than glume; upper lemma entire, awned; awn straight, 4–7 mm. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, 3/4 length of sessile spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1854; S. P. Lau 4; HK sheet 40715.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.Oct.

Chukrasia tabularis A. Juss. 麻楝
Mem. Mus. Hist. Nat. 19: 251, pl. 22. 1830; FHN 3: 70, fig. 572. 1974; FYN 1: 211, pl. 49: 1 – 4. 1977; FFJ 2: 389. 1985; FGD 2: 297, fig. 192. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 47, pl. 11: 1 – 6. 1997.

Tree, to 25 m tall. Bark longitudinally fissured. Young shoots, petioles and leaf rachis tawny puberulent. Leaves usually paripinnate, 30–50 cm; petioles 4.5–7 cm; leaflets alternate, 10–16; petiolules 2–4 mm, puberulent; blades papery, ovate to oblong-lanceolate, (5–)7–12 × 3–5 cm, base oblique, broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, puberulent along veins on both surfaces; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein, prominent abaxially. Panicles terminal, lax, about half as long as leaves; peduncle short. Flowers 1.2–1.5 cm, fragrant. Pedicels short, articulate. Calyx ca. 2 mm, puberulous abaxially, teeth short, obtuse. Petals yellow or slightly purplish, oblong, 1.2–1.5 cm. Staminal tube cylindrical, glabrous, apex truncate; anthers 10, ellipsoidal. Ovary stipitate, slightly hispidulous. Style cylindrical, short and thick, hairy. Capsule greyish yellow to brown, subglobose to ellipsoidal, ca. 4.5 × 3.5–4 cm, usually 3-valved, woody, surface coarse and verrucose. Seeds flat, elliptic, ca. 3 × 0.5 mm, wing membranous.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 44; Y. W. Lam 266, 334.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Zhejiang, Fujian; Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Indochina, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jul.– Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Timber.

Cinnamomum appelianum Schewe 毛桂
Sitzungsber. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.-Naturwiss. Cl., Abt. 1. 61: 20. 1925; FRPS 31: 222, pl. 60: 1–5. 1982.
Cinnamomum taimoshanicum Chun ex H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1959(1): 21. 1959.
Cinnamomum villosulum S. Lee & F. N. Wei, Guihaia 8(4): 301, fig. 1. 1988.

Small tree, 4–6 m tall; branchlets subopposite, densely tawny hirsute-tomentose when young. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles thick, 4–5(–9) cm, tawny hirsute-tomentose; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, elliptic-lanceolate, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 4.5 –11.5 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate to subrounded, apex abruptly and shortly acuminate, adaxially tawny pubescent on veins, glabrous in age, abaxially densely tawny pubescent, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Panicles or cymes 4 – 6.5 cm, densely tawny pubescent, usually shorter than the substanding leaves, (3 –)5 –7(–11)-flowered. Peduncles slender, 1–1.5(–3.5) cm. Pedicels 2–3 mm.
