Flowers white, 3 –5 mm; perianth tube obconical, 1–1.5 mm; lobes broadly obovate to oblong-ovate, 3 –3.5 × 2 mm, acute, silky puberulent on both surfaces. Stamens 9; filaments pilose. Immature fruit ellipsoid.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. HK sheet 36068; Y. W. Lam 89.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Woods in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of C. taimoshanicum Chun ex H. T. Chang was collected from Tai Mo Shan by N. K. Chun.

Cinnamomum burmannii (C. G. & T. Nees) Blume 陰香
Bijdr. 569. 1826; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 264. 1964; FRPS 31: 202, pl. 52: 1– 6. 1982.
Laurus burmannii C. G. & T. Nees, Disput. Cinn. 57, t. 4. 1823.
Cinnamomum dulce Nees in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 75. 1831; FHK 290. 1861.

Tree, up to 14 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles slender, 0.5–1.2 cm, subglabrous; leaf blade leathery, ovate, oblong to lanceolate, 5.5–10.5 × 2–5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, green and shining adaxially, ± glaucous abaxially, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins plane adaxially, raised abaxially. Panicles or cymes axillary or subterminal, 2–6 cm, ± greyish puberulent. Pedicels slender, 4–6 mm. Flowers greenish white, ca. 5 mm; perianth densely greyish puberulent on both surfaces; tube very short; lobes oblong-ovate. Stamens 9, filaments puberulent. Fruit ovoid, 8 × 5 mm, purplish black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated. L. T. Lo 9; Y. S. Lau 2102.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Indonesia and Philippines.
Ecology: Mixed forests on hillslope or by streams. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Additive (flavouring).

Cinnamomum camphora (L.) J. Presl 樟
Prir. Rostlin 2: 36 et 47–56, t. 8. 1825; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 262. 1964; FRPS 31: 182, pl. 43: 1–3. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 440, 1996.
Laurus camphora L., Sp. Pl. 369. 1753.

Tree, up to 30 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves alternate; petioles slender, 2–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ovateelliptic, 6 –12 × 2.5 –5.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute, margin entire, subleathery, glabrous or sparsely puberulent abaxially when young, triplinerved, with domatia in axils of secondary and tertiary veins. Panicles or cymes axillary, 3.5–7 cm; peduncles 2.5 – 4.5 cm, glabrous or puberulent, especially on the nodes. Pedicels 1–2 mm, glabrous. Flowers yellowish white, ca. 3 mm; perianthtube obconical, ca. 1 mm; lobes elliptic, white or yellowish, ca. 2 mm. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Fruit ovoid or subglobose, 6 – 8 mm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely cultivated. H. C. Tang 2354; Y. S. Lau 92.
Distribution: Widely distributed in South to Southwest China; Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: In woods near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Materials (essential oils, wood), medicinal (source of camphor), ornamental.
records.uses: Materials (essential oils, wood), medicinal (source of camphor), ornamental.

records.text:
Cinnamomum aromaticum Nees 肉桂
Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 74. 1831.
Cinnamomum cassia Presl, Prir. Rostlin 2: 36 & 44 – 45, fig. 6 (sinister). 1825; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 263. 1964; FRPS 31: 223, pl. 59: 1–5. 1982.

Tree, all parts strongly camphor-scented; branchlets dark brown, ± tetragonous, puberulent. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles thick, 1.2–2 cm, greyish yellow puberulent; leaf blade thick-leathery, oblong-elliptic to sublanceolate, 8 –16(–34) × 4 –5.5(–9.5) cm, base acute, apex slightly acute, tip blunt, margin cartilaginous, slightly involute, glabrous, green and shining adaxially, pale and sparsely yellowish puberulent abaxially when young, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins prominently impresed on adaxial surface, strongly raised on abaxial surface. Panicles axillary, 8 –16 cm, many-flowered, densely tawny tomentulose. Pedicels 3 – 6 mm, glabrous. Flowers white; perianth densely tawny tomentulose on both surfaces; tube obconical, ca. 2 mm; lobes ovate-oblong, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Fruit ellipsoid, 10 × 7–9 mm, purplish black when mature.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. P. S. Choi 411; L. T. Lo 616.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan. Also cultivated in India, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Additive (flavouring), material (essential oils), medicinal (folklore).

Cinnamomum jensenianum Hand.-Mazz. 野黃桂
Sitzungsber. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.-Naturwiss. Cl., Abt. 1. 58: 63. 1921; FRPS 31: 194, pl. 49: 8 –14. 1982.
Cinnamomum pauciflorum H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1959(1): 21. 1959.
Cinnamomum pedunculatum auct. non Nees: Dunn & Tutch. FKH 223. 1912.

Small tree, to 6 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves subopposite, thick-leathery; petioles slender, 2–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 5 –10(–20) × 1.5 –3(–6) cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin thickened and entire, together with main veins yellowish, adaxial surface glabrous, green and shining, abaxial surface pulverulent when young, glabrous when aged; triplinerved, main veins and lateral veins raise on both surfaces. Cymes 2–5-flowered. Peduncles slender, usually 1.5 –2.5 cm, subglabrous. Pedicels 5–10(–20) mm, erect, gradually thickened upwards. Flowers yellowish or white; perianth tube short, ca. 1.5 mm; lobes obovate, subequal, 2–5(– 6) × 1.75(–2.2) mm, acute, abaxially glabrous, adaxially sericeous. Stamens 9, filaments pilose. Fruit ovoid, up to 1(–1.2) × 0.6(–0.7) mm, apiculate, glabrous.

Locality: Wong Lung Hang. Y. W. Lam 616.
Distribution: Guangdong, W Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests in valleys. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Cinnamomum parthenoxylon (Jack) Meisn. 黃樟
Prodr. 15(1): 26. 1864; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 261. 196; FRPS 31: 186, pl. 46: 1–6. 1982, pro syn. sub C. porrectum (Roxb.) Kosterm.
Laurus parthenoxylon Jack, Malayan Miscellanies 1: 28. 1820.
Camphora parthenoxylon Nees in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 72. 1831; FHK 290. 1861.

Tree, 10–20 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves alternate; petioles 1.5–3.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade elliptic-ovate or long elliptic-ovate, leathery, 6–12 × 3–6 cm, much smaller on the flowering branchlets, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex usually acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire, dark green and shining adaxially, pale green or glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces, pinnately veined; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein; domatia in axils of lateral veins inconspicuous. Panicles or cymes axillary on the upper part of twigs or subterminal, 4.5–8 cm, 5–10-flowered, glabrous. Peduncles 3–5.5 cm. Pedicels slender, up to 4 mm. Perianth-tube obconical, ca. 1 mm; lobes narrowly elliptic, ca. 2 × 1.2 mm, greenish yellow, puberulous adaxially. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Fruit globose, 6–8 mm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 699; S. T. Dunn s.n. (HK sheet 4791).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Pakistan, India, Indochina, Malaysia to Indonesia.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Mar.– May; fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Materials (essential oils).

Cinnamomum validinerve Hance 粗脈桂
J. Bot. 20: 80. 1822; FKH 223. 1912; FRPS 31: 198. 1982.

Small tree, all parts strongly camphor-scented; branchlets angular, glabrous or minutely tomentulose near apex. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.8 –1.3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thick-leathery, elliptic, 4–9.5 × 2–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly and shortly acuminate, tip blunt, dark green and shining adaxially, paler and reddish abaxially, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins slightly impressed adaxially and strongly raised abaxially, transversal veins inconspicuous. Panicles about the length of the substanding leaves, cymosely branching, the utmost branch 3-flowered. Pedicels very short, greyish white sericeous. Perianth-lobes ovate, apex obtuse. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Mount Parker, Jardine's Lookout, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 118; HK sheet 4804.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thin forest. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen (Herb. Hance No. 21045, BM) was collected in the valley of Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in June 1879.

Cirrhopetalum bicolor (Lindl.) Rolfe 二色卷瓣蘭（二色石豆蘭）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(249): 14. 1903; FKH 262. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 86. 1977.
Bulbophyllum bicolor Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 49. 1830; FRPS 19: 227. 1999; FGD 7: 430. 2006; FOC 25: 428. 2009; Check List HK Plants 370. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizome stout, 3–4 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs ovoid-spherical, 1.5–2 cm long, 8–13 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves leathery, oblong, 10–15 × 2–2.5 cm, base attenuate into a petiole 1.5 cm, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers light yellow, inside base with purple dots, purplish red at tips of both sepals and petals; odd sepal oblong, 15 × 10 mm, apex acuminate, margin with thick red cilia; lateral sepals oblique ovate-lanceolate, 20 × 7.5 mm, apex obtuse, twisted above the base; petals oblong, 10 × 6 mm, apex apiculate, margin entire; lip olive green, turning orange-red in later time, ovate, curved downwards, adnate to the column foot, apex obtuse.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 10162 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1805; HK sheet 30760.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Cirrhopetalum delitescens (Hance) Rolfe 直唇卷瓣蘭
Gard. Chron. n. s. 18: 461. 1882; FKH 262. 1912.
Bulbophyllum delitescens Hance, J. Bot. 14(2): 44. 1876; FRPS 19: 209, pl. 32: 1. 1999; FGD 7: 429. 2006; FOC 25: 423. 2009; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizomes stout, prostrate, 4 mm in diam.; pseudobulb ovoid or subglobose, 1.7–3.5 cm long, 5–10 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves thin-leathery, oblong or elliptic, sometimes obovate-oblong, 16–25 × 3.5–6 cm, base cuneat, apex obtuse or acute. Flowers purple, odd sepal ovate, depressed to become boat-shaped, 1 × 3 mm, apex truncate and notched, with an awn to 7 mm in the middle of the notch, margin entire; lateral sepals narrowly lanceolate, 6 × 0.2 cm, apex acuminate, adnate to the column foot, twisted above the base, upper and lower margins connate; petals falcate-lanceolate, 5–7 × 1.5–2 mm, apex truncate and notched, with an awn in the middle of the notch, margin entire; lip fleshy, tongue-like, recurved, 5 mm, apex obtuse, base grooved and adnate to the column foot, glabrous; column 3 mm, winged.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 7065, 27305, 34047.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trunks and rocks in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by J. Lamont and C. Ford from Victoria Peak before 1876.

Cirrhopetalum miniatum Rolfe 斑唇卷瓣蘭
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1913(1): 28. 1913; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 186. 1977.
Bulbophyllum pecten-veneris (Gagnep.) Seidenf., Dansk Bot. Ark. 29(1): 37. 1973, et Opera Bot. 114: 278, fig. 182. 1992; FRPS 19: 233. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 771. 2000; FGD 7: 430. 2006; FOC 25: 433. 2009; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizomes 1–2 mm in diam., prostrate; pseudobulbs ovoid-spherical, 5–12 mm long, 5–10 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves thickly leathery, elliptic, oblong-lanceolate or ovate, 1–6 × 0.7–1.8 cm, apex obtuse or sometimes slightly retuse. Flowers yellowish green or yellow with some brown colour; odd sepal ovate, notched, 5 × 2.5 mm, apex acute, margin above base with fimbriate hairs; lateral sepals narrowly lanceolate, 3.5–5 × 0.25 cm, apex long and caudate, base adnate to the column foot, twisted above the base, upper and lower margins connate to each other, margins curved inwards, attenuate to apex forming a long tail-like tube; petals oblique ovate, 2.5–3 × 1.5 mm, apex acute, margins above middle with fimbriate hairs; lip fleshy, tongue-like, curved outwards and downwards, 2.5 mm, apex acute, glabrous; column 2 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Hubei, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Trunks and rocks in forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.

Cirrhopetalum tigridum (Hance) Rolfe 虎斑卷瓣蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36(249): 15. 1903; FKH 262. 1912.
Bulbophyllum tigridum Hance, J. Bot. 21(8): 232. 1883; FGD 7: 428. 2006; FOC 25: 427. 2009.
Bulbophyllum retusiusculum Rchb. f. var. tigridum (Hance) Z. H. Tsi, Guihaia 15(2): 108. 1995; FRPS 19: 222. 1999; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizomes prostrate, 2 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs ovoid-conical, 5–25 mm long, 4–13 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves leathery, oblong or ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–8 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate into a short petiole, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers small, dull red with purplish red veins; odd sepal oblong-ovate or subrectangular, apex subtruncate; lateral sepals lanceolate or linear, 5–7 mm, apex acuminate, adnate to the column foot at base; petals subequal to the odd sepal, apex obtuse, adnate to the column foot at base; lip fleshy, tongue-like, curved outwards and downwards, apex obtuse, grooved near base; column winged, wider near base; column foot curved upwards.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. G. Barretto 137; HK sheet 27310.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Rocks or trunks in forests. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.

Cirrhopetalum tseanum S. Y. Hu & Barretto 香港卷瓣蘭
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 30, fig. 14. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 84. 1977.
Bulbophyllum tseanum (S. Y. Hu & Barretto) Z. H. Tsi, FRPS 19: 239. 1999; FGD 7: 432. 2006; FOC 25: 434. 2009; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Saxicolous orchid; root fibrous, many; rhizomes creeping, 3 mm in diam., covered by straw-like scales; pseudobulbs oblique-ovoid, 1–1.5 cm long, 6 – 8 mm across the base. Leaves solitary, petiolate, petioles 3–7 mm, folded, articulate at base; leaf blades thick, leathery, oblong, 4–7 × 1.7–2.5 cm, base obtuse, apex rotundate and retuse, midrib impressed above, hardly visible beneath. Flowers 4 or 5 in a subumbelliform raceme terminal to the scape, bracts subulate, 3 mm, acuminate and apiculate; odd sepal cucullate, 5 × 4 mm, light yellow and uniformly crimson-lake along the margin, ciliate, hairs dark red, apex extending forward to a caudate filiform process, 4 mm; lateral sepals oblique, twisted, turning upwards with the upper margins meeting in front of the lip, to form a tongue-like elliptic blade, 1.8–2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, densely mottled dull purplish red and light yellow, margin yellow, recurved, apex retuse; petals obliqueovate, 4 × 2.5 mm, light yellow, dark red along the margin, ciliate and acuminate, apex filiform, 4 mm; lip attached to the apex of the long mentum, movable, glossy orange, fleshy, tongue-like, recurved, with a median longitudinal ridge and a groove along each side; column 3 mm, stout and winged on each side; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary obconical, 2 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sha Tau Kok (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Rocks in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 13586, K) was collected by S. C. Tse from Pat Sin Leng in 1974.

Cirsium hupehense Pamp. 湖北薊（馬刺薊）
Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital. n.s. 18(1): 86. 1911; FRPS 78(1): 121. 1987; FGD 8; 250. 2007.

Perennial herbs, 50–200 cm tall; stem erect, striate, branched or not, loosely greyish white tomentose especially on the upper portion. Leaves thick, upper surfaces green, subglabrous or scabrous, lower surfaces greyish white, densely woolly hairy, distinctly one‑veined. Median cauline leaves oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 7–13 × 0.8–2.5 cm, sessile, apex acute, margin entire or sometimes basally dentate or dentate‑serrate, but never pinnatilobed or cleft, spinules alternatively long and short growing along margin, the longer ones 3–5 mm, the short ones 1–2 mm. Upper leaves smaller in size, oblong, lanceolate to linear. Capitula arranged as loose corymbs at branch terminal, seldom solitary. Involucres ovoid‑globose, 1.2–2.5 cm across; phyllaries 6‑seriate, imbricate, abaxial side viscid and arachnoid hairy; outer two layers ovate‑lanceolate, 4–5 × 1 mm, apical spinule about 1 mm; middle layers lanceolate, 6–7 × 2 mm, spinule 1–2 mm, sometimes scarious near the base of spine; inner two layers lanceolate‑oblong to oblong, 10–15 × 1–1.5 mm, apex dilated and scarious, forming appendages about 1–3 mm, purplish red. Florets purple, pink to red, corolla lower tube filiform, 9–11 mm, upper limb broaden, 9–10 mm, apex obliquely and deeply cleft as 5 linear lobes 5–6 mm. Cypselae cuneate‑obovate, about 2–4 mm, apex obliquely truncate and rostrate. Pappus plumose, unequal in length, varied from 1–1.6 cm, white to pale brown, base connate and deciduous as a ring.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 186, 1332; P. S. Choi 456.
Didtribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Oct.–May of the following year.

Cirsium japonicum Fisch. ex DC. 薊
Prodr. 6: 642. 1837; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1–2): 55. 1966; FRPS 78(1): 103. 1987; FGD 8: 249, fig. 151. 2007;.
Cnicus japonicus (Fisch. ex DC.) Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19(5): 503. 1874; FKH 149. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 30–150 cm tall, striate, branched or not, loosely to densely multicellular‑hairy and tomentose, especially near the head. Leaves green and multicellular scabrous above and beneath. Leaves oblanceolate or oblong in outline, 6–30 × 2–10 cm, pinnatilobed to pinnatisect, lateral segments 6 – 12 pairs, triangular, hemispherical or oblong, width varied from 0.5–4 cm, those in the middle larger in size, margin coarsely and irregularly dentate, spines unequal in length, 1–6 mm, leaf base attenuate as short or long winged petiole, the petiole wing also toothed and spiny, apical segment ovate or triangular. Upper stem leaves gradually smaller in size, sessile, base dilated and semi‑amplexicaul. Capitula erect, seldom nodding, solitary or few at stem terminal. Involucres broadly campanulate, 2.5 – 3 cm across; phyllaries 6‑seriate, imbricate, abaxial side cobwebby hairy and with viscid glands along midvein, margin ciliate; outer layers lanceolate, 5–7 × 2 mm, apical spinules long and hard, 2.5–5 mm; middle layers oblong‑lanceolate, 10–13 × 1.5–2 mm, spinules short and soft, 1–3 mm; inner layers linear‑lanceolate with length 15–20 mm, width 1–1.2 mm, apex acuminate without spinules. Florets red or purple, 2–2.2 cm, lower filiform tube 0.9–1.1 cm, upper limb 1.1–1.2 mm and unequally cleft into 5 linear lobes 5–6 mm. Cypselae compressed, obliquely cuneate‑oblanceolate, 3.5 mm, apex obliquely truncate and with rostrum less than 1 mm. Pappus pale brown, feathery, length unequal, 1–1.6 cm, base connate and shed off as a ring.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Clear Water Bay, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. T. K. Leung & T. K. Wang 2515; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23833 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cirsium lineare (Thunb.) Sch. Bip. 絲葉薊
Linnaea 19: 335. 1874; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1 – 2): 58. 1966; FTW ed. 2, 4: 909, pl. 428. 1998; FRPS 78(1): 120. 1987; FGD 8: 250. 2007; Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 41: 179. 1991.
Carduus linearis Thunb., Fl. Jap. 305. 1784.
Cirsium chinense Gardner & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 323. 1849; FHK 168. 1861.
Cnicus chinensis Benth. ex Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19(5): 503 – 504. 1874; FKH 149. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 50–150 cm tall, striate, branched in upper portion, glabrous, subglabrous or sparsely cobwebby hairy or multicellular hairy. Middle leaves oblong, lanceolate to oblanceolate, 6–12 × 2–2.5 cm, gradually smaller in size when growing upward, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, base attenuate, apex acute, obtuse or caudate‑acuminate, sessile or shortly petiolate, adaxial surfaces green, scabrous, abaxial surfaces pale green or whitish, loosely cobwebby hairy or subglabrous, margin entire, sometimes basally dentate, but not pinnatilobed, finely and closely curved‑spinulose. Capitula arranged as loose corymbs at branch terminal. Involucres ovoid; phyllaries 6‑seriate, imbricate; outer and median layers triangular to triangular‑lanceolate, 5–8 × 2–5 mm, apex spinules 2 mm; inner layers lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, apex dilated, reddish scarious. Florets purplish red, corolla 2 cm, lower tube as long as upper limb, apex obliquely and deeply cleft into 5 linear lobes. Cypselae cuneate‑obovoid, 2.5–4 × 1.5–1.8 mm, smooth and glabrous, with many blackish brown lines, apex obliquely truncate and with small rostrum 0.5–1 mm. Pappus pale brown to greyish white, plumose, 1.3–1.5 cm, base connate and shed off as a ring.

Locality: Mount Gough, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. S. L. Thrower 1431, 1422 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11148 (CUHK); C. P. Lau 178 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Liaoning, Nei Mongol, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen of Cirsium chinense was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1849.

Cissus pteroclada Hayata 翼莖白粉藤
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 2: 107. 1912; FTW 3: 671. 1977; FRPS 48(2): 62. 1998.
Vitis pteroclada (Hayata) Hayata, Gen. Ind. Fl. Form. 15. 1916.
Cissus hastata auct. non (Miq.) Planch.: FHN 3: 17. 1974; FFJ 3: 372. 1987.

Herbaceous vine. Branchlets with 4 wings and longitudinal ridges, glabrous; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves simple; petiole 2–7 cm, glabrous; leaf blade oval or narrowly oval, 5–12 × 4–9 cm, glabrous, base cordate or subtruncate, notch obtuse and angular, apex cuspidate or acute, margin with 6–9 fine teeth on each side. Inflorescence a thyrse, arranged in umbelliform, terminal or leaf-opposed; peduncle 1–2 cm, pubescent. Pedicel 2–4 mm, glabrous. Calyx entire. Petals 4. Anthers oval. Lower part of ovary adnate to disk; style conical, short; stigma slightly expanded. Berry 1–1.5 × 0.8–1.4 cm, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Tsz Mun Tin, Shui Long Wo. Y. W. Lam 159; S. C. Ng 2521.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Cissus repens Lam. 白粉藤
Encycl. 1: 31. 1783; FGZ 423. 1956; FHN 3: 18. 1974; FTW 3: 671. 1977; FFJ 3: 373. 1988; FRPS 48(2): 49. 1998.
Cissus cordata Roxb., Fl. Ind. (ed. 2) 1: 407. 1832.
Vitis cordata [Wall., Cat. n. 6001] Voigt, Hort. Suburb. Calc. 28. 1845; FHK 54. 1861.
Vitis repens (Lam.) Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 125. 1834; FKH 65. 1912.

Herbaceous vine. Branchlets terete, with longitudinal ridges, usually glaucous, glabrous; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves simple; petioles 2.5–7 cm, glabrous; leaf blade cordate-oval, 5–13 × 4–9 cm, glabrous, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin with 9–12 sharp teeth on each side. Inflorescence a thyrse, arranged in umbelliform, terminal or leaf-opposed; peduncle 1–3 cm, glabrous. Pedicels 2–4 mm, nearly glabrous. Calyx entire or undulate. Petals triangular-ovate, ca. 3 mm, glabrous. Anthers ovoid-elliptic. Lower part of ovary adnate to disk; style conical; stigma slightly expanded. Berry 0.8–1.2 cm × 4–8 mm, 1-seeded.

Locality: Repulse Bay, Sai Kung, Tai Wai , Fanling, Sheung Shui, Tung Chung. L. T. Lo 143, 514; HK sheet 39785.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Nov.–May of the following year.

Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai 西瓜
Cat. Sem. Spor. Hort. Bot. Univ. Imp. Tokyo 30: n 854. 1916; FRPS 73(1): 200. 1986; FFJ 5: 254, fig. 238. 1993; FGD 3: 125. 1995.
Momordica lanata Thunb., Prodr. Pl. Cap. 13. 1800.
Citrullus vulgaris Schrad. ex Kckl. & Zeyh., Enum. Pl. Afr. Austr. 2: 279. 1836; FHK 125. 1861; FGZ 188. 1956; FHN 1: 475. 1964.

Annual herb. Stems and branches stout, sulcate-angular, villous. Tendrils puberulous, 2-branched. Petioles 3 –12 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade triangular-ovate, 8 –20 × 5 –15 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin denticulate, hispid on both surfaces, 3-partitioned, middle lobe longer; lobes pinnately partitioned. Flowers solitary. Male flowers: pedicels 3 – 4 cm, villous; calyx-tube villous, lobes narrowly lanceolate, as long as tubes; corolla pale yellow, 2.5–3 cm in diam., greenish and villous abaxially, lobes ovate-oblong, 1–1.5 × 0.5 –0.8 cm. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary densely villous, 5 – 8 mm; styles 4 –5 mm; stigmas 3, reniform. Fruits globose or ellipsoid. Smooth, with pale green or bluish stripes and patches; pulp red, white or pale yellow, juicy. Seeds many, flattened, ovate, black or white, striped or patched, 1–1.5 × 0.5 –0.8 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 530, 244; HK sheet 2012.
Distribution: Cultivated in China; native to Africa.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Citrus limonia Osb. 黎檬
Reise Ost. China 250. 1765; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 558, fig. 2845. 1972; FHN 3: 51, fig. 559. 1974; FGD 2: 273, fig. 178: 1. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 200, pl. 49: 4– 6. 1997.

Small tree, with many spines. Young leaves and flower buds often dark purplish red. Spines long, sharp, ascending. Leaves unifoliolate; petioles winged; wings linear or very narrow; leaf blade broadly elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 6–12 × 3–5 cm, apex rounded or obtuse, margin obtusely dentate, bright yellow abaxially when dry. Flowers solitary or fasciculate in axils of leaves, sometimes in 3–5-flowered racemes. Petals 1–1.5 cm, pale purplish abaxially. Stamens 25–30, 4 or 5 in bundles. Ovary ovoid, styles 4 times as long as ovary. Fruit compressed globose or globose; pericarp rather thin, smooth, pale yellow or orange-red, slightly difficult to peel off; segments 9–11; pulp pale yellow or orange-red, acid. Seeds many or few, long ovoid, apex sharp or slightly obtuse, small, smooth and not ridged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1593, 2073; HK sheet 4692.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), edible.

Citrus maxima (Burm. ex Rumph.) Merr. 柚
Bur. Sci. Publ. Manil. Amboin. 46: 296. 1917; FRPS 43(2): 187, pl. 50: 1–3, 13 – 17. 1997.
Aurantium maximum Burm., Herb. Amboin. Auct. Index Univ. Sign. Z. 1, Verso. 1755.
Citrus aurantium var. grandis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 783. 1753.
Citrus grandis (L.) Osbeck, Dagbok Ost. Resa 98. 1757; FGZ 430, fig. 228. 1956; FHN 3: 52. 1974; FGD 2: 271. 1991.

Tree to 10 m tall, spiny or not. Young branches flat and ridged, together with abaxial surfaces of leaves, calyx and ovary densely pubescent. Leaves rather thick, dark green, broadly ovate or elliptic, 9–16 cm long including wings, 4–8 cm wide, base rounded, apex obtuse or rounded; wings 2–4 × 0.5–3 cm. Inflorescences a raceme, rarely flowers solitary. Flower buds pale purplish red, rarely milky white. Calyx irregularly 3–5-lobed. Petals 1.5–2 cm. Stamens 25–35, sometime partly sterile. Styles thick and long; stigma slightly larger than ovary. Fruit globose, compressed globose, pyriform or broadly conical, over 10 cm arcoss, pale yellow or yellowish green; pericarp thick, spongy; the segments 10–15(–19), pulp white, pink or fresh red, rarely milky yellow. Seeds 0–200, often sub-rectangular, obviously ridged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2460.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River (cultivated); widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Fruit, medicinal (folklore).

Citrus medica L. 香櫞（枸櫞）
Sp. Pl. 1: 782. 1753; FHN 3: 50. 1974; FGD 2: 270. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 184. 1997.

Shrub or small tree. Young branches and leaves usually dark purplish red. Stems armed with many thick spines; spines to 4 cm. Leaves simple, rarely unifoliolate. Petiole short, not winged; leaf blade elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 6–12 × 3–6 cm, apex rounded or obtuse, rarely acute, margin shallowly obtuse-dentate. Racemes 3 –11-flowered, rarely flower solitary. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual. Petals 5, 1.5–2 cm. Stamens 30–60. Ovary terete, style thick and long. Fruit ellipsoidal, subglobose or fusiform, to 2 kg; pericarp pale yellow, rough, thick or thin, difficult to peel off, endocarp white or slightly pale yellow, soft, segments 10–15, pulp transparent or pale milky yellow, acid or slightly sweet, fragrant. Seeds small, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 4689.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan (cultivated); Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, India.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Citrus reticulata Blanco 柑橘
Fl. Filip. 610. 1837; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 561, fig. mal. 1972; FHN 3: 54. 1974; FGD 2: 278, fig. 179. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 201. 1997.
Citrus nobilis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 466. 1790.

Small tree, multibranched. Branches spreading and pendulous, with few spines. Leaves unifoliolate; petioles winged, wings usually narrow or rudimentary; leaf blade lanceolate, elliptic or broadly ovate, varied in size, apex often emarginate, margin at least dentate at upper half, rarely entire. Flowers solitary or 2–3-fasciculate. Calyx irregularly 3– 5-lobed. Petals often 1.5 cm, reflexed when full blooming. Stamens 20–25. Styles slender; stigmas capitate. Fruit various in shape, often compressed globose to subglobose; pericarp thin and smooth, or thick and rough, pale yellow to red, easy to peel off; segments 7–14, rarely more; pulp sweet or acid, pale yellow to orange-red. Seeds many or few, often ovoid, base rounded, apex acute.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1777, 2009, 2462.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range (cultivated).
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Fruit, medicinal (folklore).

Citrus sinensis (L.) Osb. 甜橙（橙）
Reise Ost. China 250. 1765; FHN 3: 53. 1974; FTW 3: 5. 1977; FGD 2: 275. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 196. 1997.
Citrus aurantium var. sinensis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 782. 1753.
Aurantium sinense Mill., Gard. Dict. (ed. 8). 1768.

Tree. Branches with a few spines or nearly unarmed. Leaves unifoliolate; petioles winged, wings narrow and long, conspicuous or rudimentary; leaf blade ovate or ovate-elliptic, rarely lanceolate, 6–10 × 3–5 cm. Flowers in few-flowered racemes or solitary. Calyx 3–5-lobed. Petals white, rarely pale purplish red abaxially, 1.2–1.5 cm. Stamens 20–25. Styles thick and strong; stigma capitate, enlarged. Fruit globose, compressed globose or ellipsoidal, orange-yellow to orange-red; pericarp difficult to peel off; segments 9–12; pulp pale yellow, orange-red or purplish red, sweet or slightly acid. Seeds few or wanting, slightly ribbed.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2426.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range (cultivated).
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Fruit.

Cladium chinense Nees ex Hook. & Arn. 華克拉莎
Bot. Beech. Voy. 227. 1838; FRPS 11: 118. 1961.
Cladium jamaicence Crantz subsp. chinense (Nees) T. Koyama in H. Hara, Stearn & L. H. J. Williams, Enum. Fl. Pl. Nepal 1: 105. 1978; FOC 23: 258. 2010.
Cladium mariscus (L.) Pohl subsp. chinense (Nees) Govaerts, World Checkl. Seed Pl. 3(1): 15. 1999.
Mariscus chinensis (Nees) Fernald, Rhodora 25: 51. 1923.
Cladium mariscus (L.) Pohl subsp. jamaicense auct. non (Crantz) Kük.: FGD 8: 318. 2007; Check List HK Plants 309. 2002; 109. 2004.
Cladium jamaicense auct. non Crantz: FKH 302. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 237. 2000.
Cladium mariscus auct. non R. Br.: FHK 397. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome thick, horizontal. Culm solitary, 1–3 m tall, terete, many-nodose, often bearing extra-vaginal shoot at lower nodes. Leaves cauline; blades elongate, broadly linear, flat, 60–90 × 0.8–1.5 cm, thickly leathery, gradually tapering above to 3-sided caudate apex, strongly serrulate-scabrous on margins; sheaths shorter than the internode. Inflorescence 30–90 cm, with terminal and lateral 5–9 anthelas, those rather contiguous or the lower ones spaced; bracts leafy, sheathing at base, the lower bract-blades much surpassing their subtending anthelas; anthelas 4–8 cm long and as broad, the peduncle and anthelas flattened. Spikelets congested in globose heads of 4–12, 4–9 mm in diam., the spikelets ovateelliptic to broadly so, 3 × 2 mm, rusty brown. Glumes 6–8, broadly ovate to ovate, 1–2.5 mm, abruptly contracted above to obtuse or subacute apex, the lower 46 empty, each of the apical 2 bearing a bisexual flower, the upper flower only producing achene. Stamens 2; anthers oblong, ca. 2 mm. Style slender; stigmas 3, pilose. Achene ovoid, ca. 2.5 mm, brown, rounded at base, apiculate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 2168; S. P. Lau 48; HK sheet 33347.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests, streams and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jun.

Cladopus austrosinensis M. Kato & Y. Kita 飛瀑草
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 54: 92. 2003.
Cladopus nymanii auct. non H. Möller: W. Y. Chun & Y. Tsiang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 261. 1963; FHN 1: 373. 1964; FGD 2: 68. 1991.

Roots creeping, adhering to rock surface, subcylindrical, compressed, branched, 0.5–1(–1.3) mm wide. Leaves on fertile shoots simple or palmately lobed; lobes linear, flat, apex obtuse, to 6 mm; leaves in fertile shoots 8–10, in two rows, digitate; lobes 3 – 9, oblong or linear, to 0.7 × 0.3 mm, rough, with silica on surface, linear lobes to 5 mm. Flower buds covered by spathella; spathella globose, apex mucronate, mucros simple or sometimes forked, ca. 0.4 mm, irregularly rupturing near apex at anthesis; tepals 2, on both sides of stamen, linear, 1 – 1.5 mm; stamen 1, to 1.5 mm, ca. 1 mm thick, 2-celled, with 2 nearly vertical grooves. Stigmas 2, forked near base, ca. 0.6 mm, equal, linear to subulate, entire, procumbent; ovules borne over septa surface, 25–34 per locule; septae convex in center, margin thin. Stalk of capsule to 1.7 mm long. Capsule globose, 1.5 mm, smooth, 2 valved.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: On rocks in streams. Flowering & fruiting: May.
Notes: According to M. Kato & Y. Kita (2003), this species was recorded from Tai Mo Shan (Iwatsuki 63, TI). No specimen collected from Hong Kong was seen by the authors. The species was reported as Cladopus nymanii H. Möller previously (Check List HK Plants 157. 2002; 58. 2004).

Claoxylon indicum (Reinw. ex Blume) Hassk. 白桐樹（丟了棒）

Cat. Hort. Bot. Bogor. 235. 1844; FKH 238. 1912; FRPS. 44(2): 79, pl. 18: 1 – 4. 1996; FGD 5: 89, fig. 49. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 160. 2005.

Claoxylon parviflorum Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beech. Voy. 212. 1841, non A. Juss. 1824; FHK 305. 1861.

Erytrochilus indicus Reinw. ex Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 615. 1825.


Shrub or tree, 3–12 m tall, softly tomentose in the young parts; branchlets stout, grey-white, sparsely lenticellate. Leaves papery; petioles 5–15 cm, with 2 glands at apex; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade usually ovate or broadly ovate, 10–22 × 6–13 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, slightly oblique, apex obtuse or acute, margin irregularly serrate, sparsely pilose on both surfaces. Racemes spicate, tomentose, the male slender, 10–23 cm, the female 5–20 cm. Male flowers: 3–7 clustered in axil of bract; pedicels ca. 4 mm; calyx-lobes 3–4, 3 mm, hairy; stamens 15–25, filaments ca. 2 mm, with narrowly ovate glands alternating the filaments. Female flowers: solitary in axil of bract; pedicels very short; sepals 3, sub-triangular, 1.5 mm, tomentose; disk 3-lobed or shallowly undulate; ovary ovoid, tomentose; styles 3, ca. 3 mm. Capsules 8 mm in diam., softly tomentose, often reddish.


Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Causeway Bay, Shek O Gap, Lam Tsuen, Tai Long Wan, Tai Po, Yuen Long, Castle Peak, Green Island, Ta Mon Island. K. Wong 1150; H. C. Tang 1946; Y. S. Lau 575.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.

Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Mar. – Dec.

Clausena lansium (Lour.) Skeels 黃皮
U. S. Depart. Agr. Bur. Pl. Ind. Bull. 176: 29. 1909; FHN 3: 42, fig. 553. 1974; FGD 2: 257, fig. 170. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 132, pl. 33: 5– 9. 1997.
Quinaria lansium Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 272. 1790.
Clausena wampi (Blanco) Oliv., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 5(suppl. 2): 34. 1861.
Clausena wampi (Blanco) Oliv. ex Benth., FHK 51. 1861; FKH 56. 1912.
Cookia wampi Blanco, Fl. Filip. 358. 1837.

Evergreen small trees, to 12 m tall. Branchlets, leaf rachis, inflorescence rachis and veins of leaves on abaxial surface hirsute, with scattered and raised fine glandular dots. Leaves 5–11-foliolate; petiolules 4–8 mm; leaflets ovate or ovate-elliptic, asymmetrical, 6–14 × 3– 6 cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, margin wavy or coarsely crenate; midveins finely pubescent on both surfaces. Panicles terminal, many-flowered. Flower-buds globose, 5-ribbed. Calyx-lobes broadly ovate, ca. 1 mm, pubescent abaxially. Petals oblong, ca. 5 mm, pubescent on both surfaces or glabrous adaxially. Stamens 10, unequal, the 5 longer ones as long as petals; filaments filiform, slightly dilated at lower half, not geniculate. Ovary densely hirsute, shortly stipitate. Fruit globose, ellipsoidal or broadly ovoid, 1.5–3 × 1–2 cm, pale yellow to dark yellow, finely hairy; pulp milky white, translucent, 1–4-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1555, 1808, 2865.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Guizhou (cultivated), native to S China.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Fruit.

Cleidion brevipetiolatum Pax & K. Hoffm. 棒柄花
Pflanzenr. IV 63 (IV. 147. VII): 292. 1914; FRPS 44(2): 75, pl. 17: 1 –5. 1996; FGD 5: 88, fig. 48. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 166. 2005.
Cleidion javanicum auct. non Blume: Tutcher, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 37: 67. 1905; FKH 240. 1912.

Tree up to 12 m tall, monoecious; branchlets glabrous. Leaves alternate or subopposite, thin-leathery, usually 3–5 crowded near apex of branchlets; petioles 0.3–3 cm; stipules lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, caducous; leaf blade obovate, obovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 7–21 × 2.5–8 cm, base narrowed, obtuse, with several glands, apex shortly acuminate or obtuse, sparsely serrulate on the distal half; abaxially bearded in axil of veins and sprinkled with glands; lateral veins 5–9. Male inflorescences racemose, axillary, 5–20 cm, rachis puberulous. Male flowers: 3–7 clustered in axil of bract; pedicels 1–1.5 mm, articulate, pubescent; bracts broad-triangular, 1.5 mm; bracteoles triangular, 0.5 mm; sepals 3, elliptic, 2–2.5 mm, sparsely pubescent at base; stamens 40–65, filaments ca. 1 mm, anthers 4-celled, connectives produced, subulate. Female flowers solitary, axillary; sepals 5, unequal, lanceolate or triangular, 2–20 × 0.5–6 mm, enlarged to 9–30 × 4–10 mm in fruit; ovary globose, densely pubescent; styles 5, ca. 1 cm, connate at base, 2-partite to near base, lobes linear. Capsules of 3 bivalved cocci, oblate, 1.2–1.5 cm in diam.; seeds subglobose, 6–7 mm in diam., brown-maculate.

Locality: Hok Tsui, Shek O Gap, Ng Tung Chai, Castle Peak. P. S. Choi 547; Y. W. Lam 269, 274.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.

Cleisostoma paniculatum (Ker Gawl.) Garay 大序隔距蘭
Bot. Mus. Leafl. Harvard Univ. 23(4): 173. 1972; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 115. 1977; FRPS 19: 323, pl. 47: 11–14. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 808, pl. 341. 2000; FGD 7: 493, fig. 254. 2006; FOC 25: 461. 2009.
Aerides paniculata Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 3: t. 220. 1817.
Sarcanthus cerinus (Hance) Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 36. 1903; FKH 266. 1912.
Cleisostoma cerinum Hance, J. Bot. 20: 359. 1882.

Monopodial herb; stems erect, compressed cylindrical, 18–25 cm tall. Leaves band-like, apex retuse or bilobed, the longest 14 cm. Inflorescence a panicle with many small flowers; flowers yellow, with 2 fairly broad bands of lilac-mauve on sepals and petals; odd sepal dorsal, oblong, 6 × 3.5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral ones oblique-oblong, 4.5 × 3 mm, apex acute, pointing upwards; petals linearoblong, 4 × 1.7 mm, apex obtuse; lip 5 mm, with a unicorn-like callus at the entrance and continued downwards to the spur, as a membrane-like partition; column 3 mm; anther cap 2-lobed; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, attached to a horse-shoe-like viscid disk by a wide stipe; stigma pear-shaped, situated beneath the rostellum; ovary and pedicel 6 mm.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 27571, 34211.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Thailand, Vietnam, NE India.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Sep.

Cleisostoma rostratum (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Garay 尖喙隔距蘭（福氏隔距蘭）
Bot. Mus. Leafl. 23: 174. 1972; FOC 25: 460. 2009.
Sarcanthus rostratus Lodd. ex Lindl., Coll. Bot. ad pl. 39B. 1826.
Cleisostoma fordii Hance, J. Bot. Brit. For. 14: 45. 1875; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 115, fig. 69. 1977; Check List HK Plants 373. 2002; 130. 2004.
Cleisostoma rostratum (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Seidef. ex Averyanov, Vasc. Pl. Syn. Vietnam. Fl. 1: 53. 1990, et Iden. Guide Vietnam. Orch. 376. 1994; FRPS 19: 319. 1999; FGD 7: 492. 2006, nom. illeg. prior.
Sarcanthus fordii (Hance) Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 37. 1903; FKH 266. 1912.

Epiphytic or saxicolous; roots wire-like, light grey, greyish green when mature, slightly compressed; stems subterete, dark green, longitudinally striate below the insertion of the leaf blades and horizontally wrinkled elsewhere. Leaves distichous, dark green, rather fleshy, stiff, linear-lanceolate, 8–14 × 1–1.6 cm, midrib narrowly compressed above, distinctly elevated below, base cuneate and distinctly articulate, apex suddenly constricted and long acuminate. Flowers resupinate, erect; sepals and petals similar in colour and design, apex acute, yellowish green with 2 carminered bands on each side; odd sepal dorsal, elliptic, 7 × 3 mm, concave and arcuate; lateral ones rather low, in line with the lip, oblique obovate-elliptic, 6 × 3 mm, reflexed; petals laterally partitioned, pointing slightly forward, oblong, 6 × 2.5 mm; lip calcarate, 3-lobed, lilac-mauve, white at base, lateral lobes erect, cuspidate at apex, midlobe folded along the sides and curved upwards forming a beak-like structure, with a fleshy tongue-like callus; column white, fleshy, apex truncate, slightly narrowed at the centre; anther cordate and beak-like at apex; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary very small, 2–3 mm.

Locality: Fo Tan Valley, Tai Mo Shan, Nam Chung, Yi O. K. Y. Chan 1373 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1765; Y. W. Lam 944.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trunks and rocks in forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

Cleisostoma simondii (Gagnep.) Seidenf. var. guangdongense Z. H. Tsi 廣東隔距蘭（柱葉隔距蘭）
Bull. Bot. Res. 3(4): 84, fig. 1. 1983; FRPS 19: 330. 1999; FGD 7: 492. 2006; FOC 25: 463. 2009.
Sarcanthus teretifolius auct. non (Lindl.) Lindl.: FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 28 (1, 2): 156. 1975.

Epiphytic herb, to 50 cm tall; stems 4 mm in diam., branched. Leaves terete, 7–11 cm, 3 mm in diam., apex obtuse. Flowers having the size and shape of a bee, in axillary racemes; dorsal sepal rounded; lateral sepals and petals oblong, all greenish marked with red longitudinal lines, apex rounded; lip saccate, lateral lobes erect, midlobe oblong; apex triangular-acute, white with pink veins. Column 3 mm. Capsules cylindrical, 3.5 × 0.6 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9754, 12294B (CUHK); K. L. Yip 4518.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Trunks in forests. Flowering: May–Nov.

Cleisostoma williamsonii (Rchb. f.) Garay 紅花隔距蘭
Bot. Mus. Leafl. 23: 176. 1972; FRPS 19: 324. 1999; FGD 7: 491. 2006; FOC 25: 462. 2009.
Sarcanthus williamsonii Rchb. f., Gard. Chron. 674. 1865.
Cleisostoma hongkongense (Rolfe) Garay, Bot. Mus. Leafl. 23(4): 172. 1972.
Sarcanthus hongkongensis Rolfe, Kew Bull. 1898: 198. 1898; J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 37. 1903; FKH 266. 1912; FHN 4: 262. 1977.

Epiphytic herb, to 70 cm tall; stems 3–4 mm in diam., branched or unbranched, internodes 1–2.5 cm. Leaves terete, 6–10 cm × 2–3 mm, apex obtuse. Racemes or panicles lateral; bracts ovate-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm. Flowers pale lilac, opening widely, dorsal sepal ovate-elliptic, cymbiform, ca. 2.2 × 1.5 mm, rounded; lateral sepals ovate-elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 1.5 mm, apex obtuse. Petals oblong, ca. 2.2 × 1 mm; lip saccate, lateral lobes erect, ligulate-oblong; midlobe narrowly ovate-triangular, fleshy, adaxially with a ridge raised and triangular near spur entrance; spur globose, ca. 2 mm in diam. Column ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan. C. Ford s.n. (K); HK sheet 34049.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; NE India to Indochina and Indonesia.
Ecology: Trunks in forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen of Sarcanthus hongkongensis (C. Ford. s.n.) was collected from Hong Kong before 1893. Rolfe (1903) noted that “the flowers are pale lilac, with the column, the side-lobes of the lip, and the base of the front lobes bright purple”.

Cleistocalyx nervosum (DC.) Kosterm. 水翁
Bull. Bot. Surv. India 29(1-4): 17. 1987 [1989].
Cleistocalyx operculatus (Roxb.) Merr. & L. M. Perry, J. Arnold Arbor. 18(4): 337. 1937; FGZ 206. 1965; FHN 2: 22. 1965; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 996, fig. 3721. 1972; FRPS 53(1): 118. 1984; FGX 1: 901, pl. 356: 3. 1991; FGD 3: 196, fig. 135. 1995; FYN 7: 128. 1997.
Eugenia operculata Roxb., [Hort. Bengal. 37. 1814] Fl. Ind. ed. 2, 2: 486. 1832; FKH 105. 1912.
Syzygium nervosum DC., Prodr. 3: 260. 1828; FOC 13: 344. 2007.

Tree, to 15 m tall, multibranched. Bark thick, greyish brown. Young branchlets flattened, furrowed. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, oblong to elliptic, 11–17 × 4.5–7 cm, base broadly cuneate to slightly rounded, apex acute to acuminate, glandular punctate on both surfaces; lateral veins 9 – 13 on each side of midvein, reticulate veins conspicuous. Thyrses lateral on leafless branches, 6–12 cm. Flowers 2–3 in clusters, sessile. Flower-buds oval, ca. 5 × 3.5 mm. Hypanthium semiglobose, ca. 3 mm. Calyptra 2 –3 mm, apex beaked. Petals obsolete. Stamens 5– 8 mm. Style 3 – 5 mm. Fruit purplish black when mature, broadly ovoid, 1 –1.2 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1871; HK sheet 30218.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, N Australia.
Ecology: Places near water. Flowering: May– Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), essential oil.
Notes: The species was reported as Cleistocalyx operculatus (Roxb.) Merr. & L. M. Perry previously (Check List HK Plants 161. 2002; 59. 2004).

Medicinal (folklore), essential oil.
Notes: The species was reported as Cleistocalyx operculatus (Roxb.) Merr. & L. M. Perry previously (Check List HK Plants 161. 2002; 59. 2004).

records.text:
Clematis chinensis Osbeck 威靈仙
Dagb. Ostind. Resa 205, 242. 1757; FRPS 28: 161. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 581, pl. 240. 1996; FOC 6: 356. 2001; FGD 5: 15. 2003.
Clematis sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 345. 1790.

Woody climber, turning black in drying. Stems and branches almost glabrous or sparsely puberulous. Leaves pinnate; petioles 3.5 –6 cm; leaflets 3–7, usually 5, papery, ovate to lanceolate, 2.5 –5 × 1–1.8 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded or shallowly cordate, apex acute to acuminate, rarely emarginate, margin entire, subglabrous. Panicles axillary or terminal, many-flowered. Flowers 1–2 cm in diam. Sepals 4(–5), white, spreading, oblong to oblong-obovate, 8 –10 × 2–3 mm, apex apiculate, densely white-pubescent at margin on abaxil surface. Stamens glabrous; anthers 2 times longer than filaments. Achenes compressed, 3–7, ovoid to broadly ellipsoid, persistent styles 2–5 cm, feathery.

Locality: Tai Hang, Tai Po, Luk Keng. H. C. Tang 2033; Ross s.n. (HK sheet 29).
Distribution: SE, C to SW China; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and grassy slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Clematis crassifolia Benth. 厚葉鐵線蓮
FHK 7. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FHN 1: 307. 1964; FRPS 28: 178, pl. 53. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 518, pl. 241. 1996; FOC 6: 353. 2001; FGD 5: 14. 2003.

Woody climber, glabrous with exception of the flowers. Leaves ternately compound; leaflets leathery, oblong elliptic or ovate, 7–10 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, 3-nerved. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary or terminal, many-flowered. Flowers 2.4–5 cm in diam. Sepals 4, spreading, white or tinged with red, lanceolate to oblanceolate, 1.2–2 × 0.2– 0.5 cm, densely pubescent at margin and on adaxial surface. Stamens glabrous, anthers ellipsoid, ca. 2 mm; filaments 3 –5 times longer than the anthers. Achenes narrowly ovoid, puberulent; persistent style 1.2–2 cm feathery.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2127; Y. S. Lau 817; HK sheet 40220.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests in ravine. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Feb.–Mar.
Notes: The type specimens was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford around 1858.

Clematis loureiroana DC. 絲鐵線蓮（甘木通、長毛鐵線蓮）
Syst. Nat. 1: 144. 1817; FOC 6: 369. 2001.
Clematis filamentosa Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 197. 1909; FKH 26. 1912; FRPS 28: 233, pl. 78: 1– 6. 1980; FGD 5: 12. 2003.

Woody climber, glabrous with exception of the inflorescence. Leaves ternate; petioles 4 –10 cm; leaflets thinly leathery, ovate to lanceolate, 7–11 × 4– 8 cm, base rounded to subcordate, apex obtusely rotund, margin entire, 5-palmately veined; petiolules 2–5 cm. Racemes axillary, usually 5–7-flowered; pedicels 3 – 4 cm, initially brown pubescent near apex, glabrescent; bracts linear lanceolate; sepals 4, white, narrowly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 13 –20 × 4–6 mm, spreading, rusty pubescent abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Stamens glabrous; connectives prolonged, 1–2 times longer than the anthers; staminodes broadly linear, glabrous. Achenes narrowly ovoid, brown, 10 × 2 mm, pubescent; persistent style 3–5 cm, filiform, villose.

Locality: Ha Hang, Fanling, Fung Yuen, Lin Ma Hang. Y. S. Lau 2827, 2848; HK sheet 76.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets by streams and in valleys. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jan.–Feb.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Ha Hang near Tai Po by S. T. Dunn in January in 1904.

Clematis meyeniana Walp. 毛柱鐵線蓮（甘草藤）
Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 19 (suppl.1): 297. 1843; FHK 6. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FHN 1: 306. 1964; FRPS 28: 171, pl. 22. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 532, pl. 249. 1996; FOC 6: 354. 2001; FGD 5: 14. 2003.
Clematis oreophila Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 3. 1851.

Woody climber. Leaves ternate; leaflets subleathery, ovate to oblong-ovate, sometimes broad-ovate, 4.5 –11.5 × 1.5– 6 cm, base rounded, broadly cuneate or sometimes cordate, apex acute, acuminate, or obtusely acute, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, 3 –5-nerved. Panicles axillary or terminal, loose and many-flowered. Flowers white, 1.5 –2 cm in diam. Sepal 4, spreading, oblong to lanceolate, 7–12 × 3–4 mm, pubescent only on the margin of abaxil surface. Stamens glabrous; anthers slightly longer than the filaments. Achenes narrowly falcate-ovoid, or narrowly obovoid, pubscent; persistent style up to 2.5 cm, feathery.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 341; N. H. Li 131; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24064.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Thicket in ravines. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen of this species was collected near Kap Shui Mun by F. J. F. Meyen in 1831.

Clematis meyeniana Walp. var. granulata Finet & Gagnep. 沙葉鐵線蓮
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 50: 530. 1903; FHN 1: 307. 1964; FRPS 28: 173. 1980; FOC 6: 355. 2001.

Differs from C. meyeniana var. meyeniana by the leaflets being finely tuberculate on abaxial surface.
Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 547, 1804.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Clematis parviloba Gardner & Champ. 裂葉鐵線蓮（小裂鐵線蓮）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 241. 1849; FHK 6. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FRPS 28: 180, pl. 54. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 532, pl. 251. 1996; FOC 6: 351. 2001 ; FGD 5: 16. 2003.
Clematis pierotii Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 3: 1. 1867.

Subshrubby climber, stem and branches loosely clothed with short silky hairs. Leaves mostly twice ternate; leaflets papery, ovatelanceolate or oblong-ovate, 1.5 – 6 × 0.8 –2.3 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, entire or coarsely serrate, appressed pubescent on both surfaces, 3-nerved. Panicles few flowered and leafy, axillary or terminal; pedicels 1–2.5 cm. Flowers 1.5–3.5 cm in diam. Sepals 4, white, sublanceolate to narrow obovate, 8 –20 × 3 –7 cm, densely covered with silky hairs abaxially. Stamens glabrous, anthers ca. 2 mm, much shorter than filaments. Achenes ovoid, ca. 4 × 3 mm, pubescent, persistent styles ca. 4 cm, feathery.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. H. C. Tang 1542, 1764; C. P. Lau 115.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: May– Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from West Point, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Clematis uncinata Champ. 柱果鐵線蓮（鉤葉鐵線蓮）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 255. 1851; FHK 6. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FRPS 28: 165. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 544, pl. 257: 1–9. 1996; FOC 6: 359. 2001; FGD 5: 15. 2003.
Clematis uncinata var. floribunda Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 30: 18. 1911, & Icon. Pl. Formosan. 7: 20. 1911.
Clematis uncinata var. biternata W. T. Wang in L. K. Fu et al, Higher Plants of China 3: 374. 2000.

Subshrubby climber, turning black in drying. Leaves pinnate; leaflets 5 –15, thin leathery, broad-ovate, ovate to lanceolate, 5–11 × 1.5 –5 cm, base broadly cuneate, sometimes cordate or truncate, apex acuminate to acute, with a short hooked point, margin entire and ± thickened, glabrous, shining adaxially, 3-nerved at the base. Panicles axillary or terminal, many-flowered. Sepals 4, white, linear lanceolate to oblanceolate, 10 –17 × 2–3 mm, white-pubescent on the margin. Stamens glabrous; anthers linear, much longer than filaments. Achenes cylindric, terminating in awn-shaped feathery persistent style.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun. L. T. Lo 146; W. J. Tutcher 4676; Y. S. Lau 998.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests in ravine. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Parker, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in 1848.

Cleome burmannii Wight & Arn. 印度白花菜
Prodr. 1: 22. 1834; Hook. f. & Thoms., Fl. Brit. Ind. 1: 170. 1875.

Annual herb, 30 –65 cm tall. Stems, branches and pedicels glabrous, but sparsely pubescent when young. Leaves alternate, 3-foliate; petioles 1.5–3 cm; leaflets rhomboid-ovate, the middle one larger, 1.8 –3 × 0.7–1.4 cm, narrowed to both ends, tip blunt, lateral leaflets smaller, 1–2 × 0.5 –1 cm glabrescent or sparsely pubescent on abaxial veins, margin entire, ciliate. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels slender, ca. 2.5 cm. Sepals 4, lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm. Petals 4, purplish red, oblanceolate, ca. 5 mm. Capsule 4– 6 cm, terete, tapering at both ends, glabrous.

Locality: Chuen Lung, Sheung Pak Nai. Naturalized. L. T. Lo 346; Y. W. Lam 376.
Distribution: India.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Cleome rutidosperma DC. 皺子白花菜
Prodr. 1: 241. 1824; FTW ed. 2, 2: 739, pl. 347. 1996; FRPS 32: 539. 1999.

Annual herb, to 90 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, covered with viscid glandular hairs, but sometimes glabrescent. Leaves digitate-trifoliolate; petioles 2–20 mm, glandular hairy; leaflets subsessile; leaf blade elliptic lanceolate, the middle one larger, 1–2.5 × 0.5 –1.2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, acuminate, obtuse or rounded, glandular hairy on veins abaxially. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves, forming interrupted leafy racemes. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm, lengthening to 3 cm in fruit. Sepals 4, green, lanceolate, ca. 4 mm. Petals 4, oblanceolate-elliptic, ca. 6 × 2 mm, base narrowed into a short claw. Stamens 6; filaments 5 –7 mm. Gynophore 1.5 –2 mm. Ovary cylindrical, glabrous; style very short; stigma capitate. Capsule cylindrical, 3.5– 6 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22192, 22155 (CUHK).
Distribution: Yunnan, Taiwan; native to tropical Africa, naturalized elsewhere in tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands, farmlands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Clerodendranthus spicatus (Thunb.) C. Y. Wu ex H. W. Li 腎茶
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 233. 1974; FRPS 66: 574, pl. 123. 1977; FOC 17: 299. 1994; FGD 3: 477, fig. 298. 1995.
Clerodendrum spicatum Thunb., Fl. Jav. 22. 1825.
Clerodendranthus stamineus (Benth.) Kudô, Mem. Fac. Sci. Taihoku Imp. Univ. 2: 117. 1929.
Orthosiphon stamineus Benth., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 15. 1830.
Ocimum aristatum Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14: 833 – 834. 1826.
Orthosiphon aristatus (Blume) Miq., Fl. Ned. Ind. 2: 943. 1858; FTW ed. 2, 4: 500. 1998.

Perennial herbs, 1–1.5 m tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, retrorse pubescent. Leaves opposite; petiole (3–)5–15 mm; leaf blade ovate, rhombic‑ovate to ovate‑oblong, (1.2–)2–5.5 × (0.8–)1.3–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to truncate‑cuneate, apex acute, margin coarsely mucronate, dentate to remotely mucronate‑crenate, pubescent and sparsely impressed glandular on both surfaces. Verticillasters 6‑flowered, forming loose terminal racemes of 8–12 cm; rachis densely pubescent; bracts orbicular‑ovate, ca. 3.5 mm, entire, apex cuspidate, longitudinally parallel veined. Pedicel to 5 mm, densely pubescent. Calyx 5–6 mm, puberulous and rusty glandular outside; upper lip orbicular, ca. 2.5 mm in diam.; teeth of lower lip triangular, awned, margin ciliolate, interior 2 teeth ca. 2 times as long as lateral teeth; fruiting calyx to 1.1 cm, reticulate veins distinct; upper lip conspicuously reflexed. Corolla purplish or white, puberulous and sparsely rusty glandular on upper lip; tube 0.9–1.9 cm; upper lip reflexed, ca. 6 mm in diam., 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger, apex emarginate; lower lip oblong, ca. 5 mm; filaments 2–4 cm exserted from corolla‑tube. Nutlets dark brown, ovoid, ca. 2 × 1.6 mm, wrinkled.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 190; HK sheet 32793.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); SE Asia and N Australia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum canescens Wall. ex Walp. 灰毛大青（獅子球）
Repert. Bot. Syst. 4: 105. 1845; FHK 272. 1861; FKH 205. 1912; FYN 1: 473, pl. 113: 7 – 8. 1977; FTW 4: 421. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 171. 1982; FFJ 4: 547. 1989; FOC 17: 39. 1994; FGD 3: 379, fig. 245. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 416. 1998.
Clerodendrum haematocalyx Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 238. 1852.
Clerodendrum viscosum auct. non Vent.: FHN 4: 25. 1977; Check List HK Plants 59. 1993.

Shrub, 1–3.5 m tall. Petioles and peduncles densely yellowish to brownish tomentose to nearly villous. Branchlets tetragonal. Petiole 1.5–12 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate or cordate, rarely ovate, 6–18 × 4–15 cm, base cordate to subtruncate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sparsely mucronate‑dentate, villous especially on veins. Inflorescences terminal, subconical. Peduncle robust, 1.5–11 cm. Bracts leaf‑like, elliptic to ovate, 0.5–2.4 cm. Calyx green when young, ca. 1.3 cm, membranous, deeply 5‑lobed, lobes ovate to broadly ovate. Corolla white or pinkish, outside puberulent; tube slender, ca. 2 cm; lobes obovate‑oblong, 5–6 mm, reflexed. Stamens and style exserted. Fruiting calyx red. Drupes green when young, dark blue to black at maturity, subglobose, ca. 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 540; Y. S. Lau 1281; P. S. Choi 379.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Clerodendrum chinense (Osbeck) Mabb. 重瓣臭茉莉
Pl.‑Book (corr. repr. 1989) 707. 1989; FOC 17: 39. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 416. 1998.
Cryptanthus chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 215. 1757.
Clerodendrum philippinum Schauer, Prodr. 11: 666. 1847; FTW 4: 423. 1978; FYN 1: 470, pl. 112: 3 – 6. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 173, fig. 91. 1982.
Clerodendrum fragrans auct. non Vent.: FKH 205. 1912, p.p.

Shrub, 0.5–1.2 m tall. Branchlets nearly tetragonal to terete, pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole 3–17 cm, pubescent to tomentose; leaf blade broadly ovate to nearly heart‑shaped, 9–22 × 8–21 cm, base truncate, broadly truncate, or subcordate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely irregularly dentate, adaxially strigose, abaxially pubescent especially on veins and with several large glands near base. Cymes terminal, dense corymbose. Peduncle tomentose. Bracts lanceolate, 1.5–3 cm; pubescent, with several large glands. Flowers double, fragrant. Calyx campanulate, 1.5–1.7 cm, deeply 5‑lobed, pubescent, with several large glands; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 0.7– 1 cm. Corolla white, pinkish, or red, tube short, lobes ovate.

Locality: Sai Kung, Wun Yiu, Fung Kat Heung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 103, 2211; HK sheet 21897.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum fragrans (Vent.) Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993, p.p.).
records.uses:
Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum fragrans (Vent.) Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993, p.p.).

records.text:
Clerodendrum cyrtophyllum Turcz. 大青
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 36(3): 222. 1863; FKH 205. 1912; FHN 4: 24, fig. 955. 1977; FYN 1: 460, pl. 110: 1 – 3. 1977; FTW 4: 421. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 164. 1982; FFJ 4: 549, fig. 429. 1989; FOC 17: 38. 1994; FGD 3: 378. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 417, photo 247. 1998.
Clerodendrum amplius Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 5, 5: 233. 1866.
Clerodendrum formosanum Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 31: 85. 1886, ‘Clerodendron’.
Cordia venosa Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(174): 143. 1890.

Shrub or small tree, 1–10 m tall. Branchlets yellowish brown, pubescent. Petiole 1–8 cm; leaf blade papery, elliptic, ovate‑elliptic, oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 6–20 × 3–9 cm, base rounded to cuneate, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire, glabrous or sparsely pubescent along veins, abaxially glandular; lateral veins 6–10 pairs. Cymes corymbose, terminal or subterminal, 10–16 × 20–25 cm. Bracts linear, 3–7 mm. Flowers small, fragrant. Calyx cupular, 3–4 mm, minutely tomentose and glandular abaxially, glabrous adaxially; lobes triangular‑ovate, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, sparsely puberulent, glandular; tube slender, ca. 1 cm; lobes ovate, ca. 5 mm. Stamens and style exserted. Ovary glabrous. Stigma 2‑lobed. Fruiting calyx red. Drupes blue‑purple, obovoid to globose, 5–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 886, 1979; P. S. Choi 380.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum fortunatum L. 白花燈籠（鬼燈籠）
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 889. 1763; FKH 205. 1912; FGZ 633, fig. 338. 1956; FHN 4: 23. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 156, fig. 79. 1982; FFJ 4: 544. 1989; FOC 17: 37. 1994; FGD 3: 377, fig. 243. 1995.
Clerodendrum castaneifolium Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 205. 1837, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum lividum Lindl., Bot. Reg. 11: pl. 945. 1825, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum oxysepalum Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 114. 1861, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum pentagonum Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 238. 1852, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum pumilum (Lour.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 2: 759. 1825, ‘Clerodendron’.
Volkameria pumila Lour., Fl. Cochin. 388. 1790.

Shrub to 2.5 m tall. Branchlets densely yellowish brown pubescent when young. Petiole 0.5–3 cm, densely yellowish brown pubescent; leaf blade papery, long elliptic, obovate‑lanceolate, or rarely ovate‑elliptic, 5–17.5 × 1.5–5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or undulate, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially pubescent along veins and densely small yellow glandular. Cymes axillary, shorter than leaves, 3– 9‑flowered. Peduncle 1–4 cm, densely brown pubescent. Bracts linear, densely brown pubescent. Calyx reddish purple, 5‑veined, like lantern in shape, 1–1.3 cm, deeply 5‑lobed, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially; lobes broadly ovate. Corolla white or pinkish, salverform; tube straight, ± funnelform, slightly longer than calyx; limb oblique; lobes oblong, ca. 6 mm, reflexed. Stamens longer than corolla. Style filiform, shorter than stamens. Stigma 2‑lobed. Fruiting calyx inflated. Drupes dark blue‑green, subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam., enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1767, 2124; K. L. Yip 4485.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangxi; Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wastelands and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum inerme (L.) Gaertn. 苦郎樹（假茉莉）
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 271, pl. 75. 1788; FHK 271. 1861; FKH 204. 1912; FGZ 632. 1956; FHN 4: 22. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 154, fig. 77. 1982; FFJ 4: 543, fig. 426. 1989; FOC 17: 42. 1994; FGD 3: 377. 1995.
Volkameria inermis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 637. 1753.

Scandent shrub, to 2 m. Stems erect or creeping. Branchlets tetragonal, yellowish grey, pubescent. Petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, ovate, elliptic or elliptic‑lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base obtuse, apex obtuse, margin entire, slightly revolute, adaxially dark green, subglabrous, abaxially pale green, glabrous or sparsely pubescent along veins, small glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–7 pairs. Cymes axillary, usually 3‑flowered, pubescent. Peduncle 2–4 mm. Bracts linear, ca. 2 cm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx campanulate, finely pubescent abaxially, sparsely glandular, apex subtruncate, with minute rudimentary teeth. Corolla white; tube 2–3 cm, ca. 2 mm in diam. at throat, densely silky pubescent adaxially, subglabrous and inconspicuously glandular abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes elliptic, ca. 7 mm. Stamens 4(–6), filaments purple, slender, exserted. Ovary glabrous. Style glabrous, exserted. Stigma 2‑lobed. Drupes greyish yellow, obovoid to subglobose, 6–11 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 712, 2152; Y. W. Lam 25.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum japonicum (Thunb.) Sweet 赬桐
Hort. Brit. 1: 322. 1826; FHN 4: 23. 1977; FYN 1: 478, pl. 114: 5. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 187, fig. 99. 1982; FFJ 4: 544, fig. 427. 1989; FOC 17: 36. 1994; FGD 3: 381. 1995.
Volkameria japonica Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 203. 1780.
Clerodendrum kaempferi (Jacq.) Siebold, Verh. Batav. Genootsch. Kunsten 3: 207. 1789; FGZ 634. 1956; FTW ed. 2, 4: 419, photo 249. 1998.
Volkameria kaempferi Jacq., Collectanea 3: 207. 1789.

Shrub, 1–4 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal, pubescent to subglabrous, nodes sometimes villous. Petiole 0.5–15 cm, densely yellowish brown pubescent; leaf blade nearly heart‑shaped, 8–35 × 6–27 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate to acute, margin sparsely serrulate to dentate, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely covered with many peltate glands and yellowish brown pubescent. Thyrses terminal, 15–34 × 13–35 cm. Bracts broadly ovate, ovate‑lanceolate, linear‑lanceolate, reddish; bracteoles usually reddish. Calyx red, 1–1.5 cm, abaxially pubescent and peltate glandular, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate to ovate, 0.7–1.3 cm. Corolla red, rarely white; tube 1.7–2.2 cm, puberulous abaxially; lobes oblong, 1–1.5 cm. Stamens and style 3 times as long as corolla‑tube or longer. Ovary glabrous, 4‑locular. Stigma 2‑cleft. Fruiting calyx much longer than fruit, enlarged, enclosing fruit at first, reflexed at maturity. Drupes subglobose, bluish black at maturity, 7–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 174; Y. S. Lau 985, 1901.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Clerodendrum lindleyi Decne ex Planch. 尖齒臭茉莉
Fl. Serres Jard. Eur. 9: 17. 1853; FYN 1: 471, pl. 112: 8. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 174, fig. 92. 1982; FFJ 4: 548. 1989; FOC 17: 39. 1994; FGD 3: 380. 1995.
Clerodendrum fragrans auct. non Vent.: FKH 205. 1912, p.p.

Shrub, 0.5–3 m tall. Branchlets pubescent, nearly tetragonal when young, becoming subterete, pubescent. Petiole 2–11 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, broadly ovate to heart‑shaped, 6.5–12.5(–22) × 5.5–10(–20) cm, base truncate to cordate, apex acuminate, margin irregularly serrate or undulate, pubescent especially abaxially, with several peltate glands at base. Cymes terminal, dense, corymbose. Peduncle pubescent. Bracts many, lanceolate, 2.5–4 cm, puberulent, with several peltate glands. Calyx 1–1.5 cm, deeply 5‑lobed, densely puberulent, with several peltate glands; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 4–10 mm. Corolla purplish red or pale red, tube 2–3 cm; lobes obovate, 5– 7 mm. Stamens exserted. Style exceeding stamens. Drupes enclosed in purple, inflated, persistent calyx, bluish black, subglobose, 5–6 mm in diam.

Locality: New Territories. S. T. Dunn 1194.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum fragrans (Vent.) Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993, p.p.).

Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum thomsonae Balf. 龍吐珠
Edinburgh New Philos. J. 15(2): 233, t. 2. 1862; FGZ 632. 1956; FHN 4: 22. 1977; FYN 1:458, pl. 109: 3 – 4. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 156. 1982; FFJ 4: 543. 1989; FGD 3: 377. 1995.

Scandent shrub, 2–5 m. Young branchlets tetragonal, yellowish brown tomentose, glabrescent. Petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade papery, narrowly ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base subrotund, apex acuminate, entire, adaxially slightly rough, hispidulous, abaxially subglabrous; basal veins 3. Cymes axillary or pseudoterminal, dichotomous, 7– 15 × 10–17 cm. Bracts narrowly lanceolate, 0.5–1 cm. Calyx white, connate at base, enlarged at middle, apex deeply 5‑lobed, finely pubescent abaxially; lobes elliptic, ca. 9 mm. Corolla‑tube as long as calyx. Stamens 4, exserted. Style exserted; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruiting calyx not enlarged, reddish purple. Drupes subglobose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., pyrenes 2–4.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1498, 1892; HK sheet 21984.
Distribution: Native to tropical W Africa, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Clerodendrum wallichii Merr. 垂茉莉（黑葉龍吐珠）
J. Arnold Arbor. 33(3): 220. 1952; FYN 1: 461, pl. 110: 8 – 9. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 158, fig. 80. 1982; FOC 17: 36. 1994.
Clerodendrum nutans Wall. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 103. 1825, nom. illeg.

Shrub or small tree, 2–4 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal, ± winged, glabrous. Petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade subleathery, oblong to oblong‑lanceolate, 11–18 × 2.5–4 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins 7–8 pairs, adaxially slightly prominent. Thyrses terminal, 20–33 cm, pendulous, glabrous, axis and peduncle tetragonal or winged; cymes opposite or decussate, several‑flowered. Bracts small, linear or subulate. Calyx red to purple, ca. 1 cm, tube very short; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, 7–8 mm, enlarged in fruit. Corolla white, tube ca. 1.1 cm; lobes obovate, 1.1–1.5 cm. Stamens and style exserted. Fruiting calyx red to purple, inflated, thickened. Drupes yellowish green when young, black and shiny at maturity, globose, 1–1.3 cm in diam., often 2‑sulcate.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 184.
Distribution: Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang; Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum nutans Wall. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum nutans Wall. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).
