Cleyera japonica Thunb. 紅淡比
Nov. Gen. 3: 69. 1783, p. p.; FGD 2: 159. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 56, 1998

Shrub or small tree, branches and branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 5–10 mm, glabrous, canaliculate; leaf blade oblong to elliptic-oblong, 5–9 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous. Flowers axillary, or 2– 5 clustered; pedicels ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous; bracteoles 2, alternate, deciduous; sepals 5, subrounded, ca. 3.5 × 3.5 mm, imbricate, apex rounded, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, margin ciliate; petals 5, white, obovate-oblong, ca. 1 × 0.5 cm, reflexed at anthesis; stamens about 25, in 2 series, unequal, 5 –7 mm; filaments slender, glabrous; anthers elliptic, hispid; ovary glabrous, 2-locular; style 6–10 mm, 2- lobed. Fruit baccate, globose, purplish black when mature, 6–9 mm in diam. Seeds many, compressed, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Chek Keng, Tung Lung Chau. F. W. Xing 9393; S. C. Ng 2171.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; India, Japan.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests. Flowering: Apr.–May.

Cleyera parvifolia (Kobuski) Hu ex L. K. Ling. 小葉紅淡比
Iconogr. Cormophytorum Sinicorum Suppl. 2: 481. 1983; FRPS 50(1): 61. 1998.
Cleyera japonica Thunb. var. parvifolia Kobuski, J. Arnold Arbor. 18(2): 125. 1937; FTW 2: 604. 1976; FGD 2: 160. 1991.

Small tree or shrub, branches reddish brown, branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery, elliptic, 3–5.5 × 1.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, slightly revolute, glabrous, midvein prominent on both surfaces, lateral veins 5 –6 pairs; petioles 3 – 5 mm, glabrous, sulcate above. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2–3 in cluster; pedicels 5 – 8 mm, glabrous; bracteoles 2, deciduous; sepals 5, triangular, ca. 3.5 × 2 mm, imbricate, apex acute, margin ciliate, persistent in fruit; petals 5, white, oblong or obovate-oblong, 5 – 6 × 2.5 –3 cm; stamens about 25, 2-seriate, unequal, ca. 5 mm long; filaments filiform, glabrous; anthers ovoid, hispid, 2-celled, longitudinally opening, ca. 2 mm; ovary spherical, glabrous, 2-locular; style ca. 4 mm, apex 2-fid. Fruit baccate, globose, black, 5 mm in diam. Seeds many, compressed, dark brown, shiny, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung. S. C. Ng 2176; Y. W. Lam 1427; K. L. Yip 4085.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: May; fruiting: Sep.

Clinacanthus nutans (Burm. f.) Lindau 鱷嘴花
Engler & Prantl, Pflanzenfam. 4(3b): 340. 1895; FHN 3: 566. 1974; FRPS 70: 252. 2002.
Justicia nutans Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 10: t. 5, fig. 1. 1768.
Clinacanthus burmanni Nees, Prodr. 11: 511. 1847

Herbs, up to 1 m tall. Stems terete, striped, glabrescent. Petioles 3–8 mm, sulcate, bifariously pubescent; leaf blades papery, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, 7–11 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex caudate, margin subentire or dentate, pubescent when young on both surfaces, then glabrescent except for the pilose veins abaxially, lateral veins 4–6 pairs, elevated abaxially. Spikes terminal, subsecund, usually 3 – several forming a large, lax panicle to ca. 1.5 cm. Rachis glandular‑pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles linear, ca. 8 × 2 mm, apex acute, abaxially glandular‑pilose. Calyx 9–13 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes linear, apex acute, abaxially glandular‑pilose. Corolla dull red with a green base, 3–3.5 cm, outside pilose, inside glabrous except for a circled hairs ca. 5 mm above the base; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm long and ca. 3 mm, gradually widened to ca. 6 mm at mouth, 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, triangular, 1.5–2 × 0.5 cm, apex emarginate, lower lip nutant, 1.6–2 × 1 cm, with yellow streaks, 3‑lobed; lobes ovate, 3 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 1.5 cm; anthers ovate‑linear, ca. 4 × 1 mm, muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, glabrous; styles ca. 3 cm, few hairs at base. Capsules oblong, ca. 2 cm, pilose. Seeds orbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated or introduced. HK sheet 38978, 39670; P. H. Liang 8978 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clinopodium gracile (Benth.) Matsum. 細風輪菜
Index Pl. Jap. 2: 538. 1912; FRPS 66: 235, pl. 54: 1 – 6. 1977; FOC 17: 230. 1994; FGD 3: 440. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 452, pl. 193. 1998.
Calamintha gracilis Benth., Prodr. 12: 232. 1848; FKH 210. 1912.

Perennial herbs. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, puberulous, rooting on the lower nodes. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5–1 cm, puberulous; leaf blade broadly ovate or subrounded 1–2 × 0.8–1.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute, margin crenate‑serrate, glabrous on both surfaces except on the veins. Verticillasters many‑flowered in axils of upper leaves, sometimes aggregated in racemose or subcapitate terminal inflorescence; bracts subulate, puberulous. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 2–3 mm, lengthening to 4–4.5 in fruit, sparsely hirsute; tube slightly inflated below; upper teeth recurved, highly connate, slightly shorter than the lower ones; lower teeth subulate, ciliate, slightly incurved. Corolla straight, 3–4 mm, barely exserted. Anther‑cells parallel, connivent. Nutlets rounded, compressed, 0.5–0.6 mm across, pale brown, finely reticulate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 2209; P. S. Choi 128; Y. W. Lam 1559.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Open fields, wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Clitoria hanceana Hemsl. 廣東蝶豆（韓氏蝶豆）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23(154): 187. 1887; FKH 82. 1912; FRPS 41: 263. 1993; FGD 5: 323. 2003.

Subshrub with fleshy spindle-shaped roots. Stems terete, grey pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets subequal or lateral ones smaller, oblong, 6.5 – 14 × 2.8 – 5.5 cm, base obtuse or sometimes subcuneate, apex acute or rounded, often apiculate, glabrous adaxially, adpressed pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 9–12 on each side of midvein. Flowers 2 –3 or 1 in axils of leaves. Calyx 2 cm, 5-toothed, striate-venose, lobes about equal to tube, hairy. Corolla white or yellowish, ca. 3 cm; vexillum striate-venose, tomentose abaxially; wings and keel smaller, clawed. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary pubescent. Pods linear-oblong, 3.5 – 6 × 0.6 cm, long-beaked. Seeds 2 – 7, black, elliptic, 4 × 3 mm.

Locality: Kowloon. W. J. Tutcher 5357, 5609.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clitoria ternatea L. 蝶豆
Sp. Pl. 753. 1753; FKH 82. 1912; FRPS 41: 262. 1995; FGD 5: 322, fig. 176. 2003.

Herbaceous climber. Stems and branchlets slender, adpressed pubescent. Leaves odd-pinnate; leaflets 5 –7(–9), elliptic or subovate, 2.5– 5 × 1.5 – 3.5 cm, base obtuse, apex obtuse, emarginate, mucronate, sparsely adpressed pubescent or sometimes glabrous. Flowers large, solitary, axillary. Bracteoles suborbicular, 5– 8 mm in diam. Calyx 1.5– 2 cm, 5-toothed, teeth lanceolate. Corolla blue, pink, white, up to 5.5 cm; vexillum obovate, 3 cm in diam., white or with orange mark at center; wings and keel smaller than vexillum. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary pubescent. Pods linear, 5 – 11 × 1 cm, flat, beaked. Seeds 6 – 10, black, oblong, 6 × 4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 403; Y. S. Lau 2322; K. Y. Chan 169.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to India.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun. –Nov.
Uses: Green manure, ornamental, seed poisonous.

Coccinia grandis (L.) Voigt 紅瓜
Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 59. 1845; FRPS 73(1): 263. 1986; FGD 3: 140, fig. 101. 1995.
Bryonia grandis L., Mant. 1: 126. 1767.
Coccinia indica Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Penins. Ind. Or. 1: 347. 1834; FKH 112. 1912.

Herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems angulate and sulcate, glabrous or with scattered pubescence. Tendrils not branched. Petioles 1–5 cm; leaf blade broadly heart-shaped, 4–10 × 4–10 cm, usually pentagonal or 5-lobed, base deeply cordate, with several glands, apex obtuse, with raised spots on both surfaces. Flowers white or yellowish, solitary. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 2– 4 cm, glabrous; calyx-tube broadly campanulate, lobes linearlanceolate, 3 – 4 mm; corolla 2.5 –3.5 cm, lobes ovate, glabrous abaxially, pubescent adaxially; stamens 3, filaments and anthers connate, filaments 2–3 mm, anthers subglobose, 6 –7 mm long. Female flowers: pedicels 2.5–6 cm; staminodes 3, subulate; ovary fusiform, 1.2–1.5 cm, styles 6–7 mm, stigmas 3, 5–6 mm. Berries ellipsoid, 5 × 2.5 cm, red when mature, glabrous. Seeds yellow, oblong, 6 –7 × 2.5 – 4 mm, densely tuberculate.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Tsuen Wan, Shan Liu, Ping Shan. Y. W. Lam 369, 371, 834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Africa, SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Cocculus orbiculatus (L.) DC. 木防己
Syst. Nat. 1: 523. 1817; Forman, Kew Bull. 22: 372–374. 1968; FGD 1: 37, fig. 38. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 32, pl. 7: 1– 8. 1996.
Menispermum orbiculatus L., Sp. Pl. 341. 1753.
Menispermum trilobus Thunb., Fl. Jap. 194. 1784.
Cocculus trilobus (Thunb.) DC., Syst. 1: 522. 1817; FHN 1: 321. 1964.
Cocculus thunbergii DC., Syst. Nat. 1: 524. 1818; FKH 31. 1912.
Cocculus ovalifolius DC., Syst. Nat. 1: 526. 1818; FHK 13. 1861.

Woody vine. Young shoots densely pubescent, glabrescent in age. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles (0.5–)1–3 cm, puberulous; leaf blade variable in shape and size, usually ovate or elliptic, sometimes obovate or obcordate, or occasionally suborbicular or oblong, 3–8(–10) × 0.5–2.5(–5) cm, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, sometimes slightly emarginate, margin entire or obtusely 3-lobed; glabrous or pubescent especially on abaxial surface, palmately 3–5-nerved. Cymes axillary, few-flowered, or many-flowered and racemosely arranged, up to 10 cm or longer, puberulous. Male flowers: sepals 6, broadly elliptic, 6–15 mm, glabrous; petals 6, lanceolate, 1–2 mm, apex divided into 2 acuminate or acute lobes; stamens 6, shorter than petals. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; staminodes 6, very small; carpels 6, glabrous. Drupes subglobose, red to reddish purple, usually 7–8 mm in diam.; kernel bony, 5–6 mm in diam., dorsally ornamented with branched ridges.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1285; Y. S. Lau 338, 900; HK sheet 1102.
Distribution: Most parts of China except NW China and Xizang; widely distributed in SE & E Asia and extending to Hawaii.
Ecology: Thickets near villages. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Codariocalyx gyroides (Roxb. ex Link) Hassk. 圓葉舞草
Flora 25(2. Beibl. 4): 49. 1842; FRPS 41: 60, pl. 10: 11. 1995; FGD 5: 277, fig. 147. 2003.
Hedysarum gyroides Roxb. [Hort. Beng. 57. 1814, nom. nud.] ex Link, Enum. Alt. 2: 247. 1822.
Desmodium gyroides (Roxb. ex Link) DC., Prodr. 2: 236. 1826; FHN 2: 274. 1965.

Erect shrub, 1–3 m tall; stem terete, villose when young, later glabrescent. Leaves 3-foliolate; stipules narrowly triangular, 12 – 15 mm, white silky hairy at first, later glabrescent, margin white silky hairy; petioles 2 –2.5 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaflets papery; terminal leaflet blade obovate or elliptic, 3.5 – 6 × 2.5 – 3.5 cm, base obtuse, apex rotund or emarginate, appressed pubescent on both surfaces; lateral leaflets much smaller than terminal one, 1.5 – 2 × 0.8 – 1 cm, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely pubescent. Panicles or racemes terminal or axillary, 8 –10 cm, densely flowered a upper half; bracts broadly ovate, 6–9.5 × 4–5.5 mm, white pilose abaxially, striate, margin ciliate. Pedicels 4–9 mm, densely yellow pubescent. Calyx broadly campanulate, 2 – 2.5 mm; tube 1.2 – 1.7 mm; upper lobe deeply 2-toothed at apex, ca. 1 mm, lower lobes ca. 0.8 mm. Corolla purple; standard 9– 11 × 9–11 mm; wings 7– 9 × 4–6 mm, base auriculate; keel 9– 12 mm, long clawed. Stamens 9 – 11 mm. Gynoecia 1.2 – 1.4 cm; ovary linear, hairy. Pods falcate, 2.5 – 5 × 0.4– 0.6 cm, dehiscing along dorsal suture when mature, densely yellow short-hooked hairy and villose.

Locality: Tai Po. P. Chow s.n. (HK sheet 38949); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24070 (CUHK, HK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Mountain slopes. Flowering: Sep. – Oct.; fruiting: Jan.

Codiaeum variegatum (L.) A. Juss. 變葉木（灑金榕）
Euphorb. Gen. 80, 111, pl. 9, fig. 30. 1824; FRPS 44(2): 149, pl. 36: 1– 4. 1996; FGD 5: 112, fig. 65. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 188. 2005.
Croton variegatum L., Sp. Pl. ed. 3, 1424. 1764.

Shrub up to 3 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves thinly leathery, very variable in shape and size, linear, linear-lanceolate, oblong, elliptic, lanceolate, ovate, spathulate, fiddle-shaped to obovate, entire or lobed, 5–30 × 0.3–8 cm, base cuneate, acute to obtuse, apex acute, acuminate to rounded, usually marked with white, yellow or red. Flowers in axillary racemes of 8–30 cm. Male flowers: pedicels slender; calyx-lobes 5, ca. 3 mm; petals 5, white, smaller than calyx-lobes; disk-glands 5; stamens 20–30. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 1 mm; calyx-lobes ca. 1 mm, yellowish; petals absent; disk annular; ovary 3-locular; styles recurved. Capsules subglobose, slightly flattened, glabrous, ca. 9 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7058 (CUHK); Hu & But 28 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Malay Peninsula to Pacific; widely cultivated in tropic regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep.–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Codonacanthus pauciflorus (Nees) Nees 鐘花草
Prodr. 11: 103. 1847; FHK 267. 1861; FKH 199. 1912; FHN 3: 557. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 651. 1998; FRPS 70: 228. 2002.
Asystasia pauciflora Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 90. 1832.
Codonacanthus acuminatus Nees, Prodr. 11: 103. 1847.

Perennial erect herbs, 20–60 cm tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, bifariously pubescent. Petioles 3–13 mm, puberulent or glabrous; leaf blades thin papery, elliptic, ovate or lanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base rounded, cuneate, or attenuate and decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or slightly undulate, adaxially green, glabrous or with few large‑celled hairs, with numerous cystoliths, abaxially pale green, glabrous except for loose puberulent on the midveins, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Racemes simple or usually few forming a terminal panicle, 3–10 cm, flowers usually only one fertile on each node, distant. Peduncles 1–3 cm, puberulent. Rachis puberulent. Pedicels 1–3 mm, puberulent. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, apex acute, puberulent; bracteoles ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm, apex acute, puberulent. Calyx ca. 2.5 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, puberulent. Corolla white, campanulate, 8–10 mm, glabrous; tube cylindric, ca. 2 mm, abruptly dilated and widened to 8–10 mm at mouth, upper lip 2‑lobed, rarely subentire, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 4 × 4 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 2, included, filaments ca. 2.5 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae oblong, ca. 1.2 mm, parallel at unequal level. Ovary glabrous; styles filiform, ca. 6 mm; stigma shortly 2‑lobed. Capsule oblanceolate, ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous, (2 or )4‑seeded at upper half. Seeds orbicular, ca. 2 mm, glabrous, ridged on the margin.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 158; L. T. Lo 318; K. L. Yip 4460.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Bhutan.
Ecology: Forests, wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

Codonopsis javanica (Blume) Hook. f. 金錢豹
Ill. Himal. Pl. 116, t. 16B. 1855.
Campanumoea javanica Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 13: 727. 1825; FRPS 73(2): 70. 1983; FGD 3: 320. 1995.
Campanumoea pilosula auct. non Franch.: FKH 153. 1912.

Perennial twining herbs, glabrous throughout. Tap root thick and fleshy, cylindric or obconical, 5–10 cm, to 5 cm in diam. Leaves opposite, very rarely alternate; petioles 2–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 2–7 × 1.5–6 cm, base cordate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire or crenulate. Flowers solitary and axillary. Calyx not attached to ovary; 5‑lobed nearly to the base; lobes oblong or ovate‑lanceolate, 1–2 cm, persistent. Corolla campanulate, 1–1.3 cm, white or light green, with purple stripes inside; 5‑lobed to middle; lobes ovate. Stamens 5; filaments filiform, 3 – 9 mm; anthers 2–6 mm. Ovary 4–5‑locular, with numerous ovules. Fruit a berry, depressed globose, 10–12(–15) mm in diam.; purplish red when mature.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung, Castle Peak. W. J. Tutcher 10550; P. S. Choi 134; HK sheet 31588.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Sikkim, Bhutan to Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places in thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Codonopsis lanceolata (Siebold & Zucc.) Trautv. 羊乳
Trudy Imp. S.‑Peterburgsk. Bot. Sada 6: 46. 1879; Hemsl., J. Soc. Bot. 26: 5. 1889; FKH 153. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 37. 1983; FGD 3:321, fig. 208. 1995.
Campanumoea lanceolata Siebold & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 1: 174, t. 91. 1835.

Perennial twining herbs, usually glabrous throughout. Tap root thick and fleshy, fusiform, to 20 cm long and 6 cm in diam., with milky latex. Leaves alternate on stems (usually small), 2–4 opposite or in false whorls at apex of branches; petioles short, 1–5 mm; leaf blade rhombic‑ovate or elliptic, 3–7(–10) × 1.5–3(–4.5) cm, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or undulate‑serrate. Flowers solitary or in pairs terminal on branches. Calyx‑tube attached to the middle of the ovary; lobes 5, ovate‑lanceolate, 12–15 × 5–7 mm, persistent and slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla broadly campanulate, 2 – 3 cm; lobes 5, triangular, 0.5 – 1 cm, creamy white outside, purple inside. Ovary half‑inferior; stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule hemispheric, 2–2.5 cm in diam.; seeds winged.

Locality: Ma On Shan. P. Chow 138; F. W. Xing 7340; HK sheet 40895.
Distribution: SE to NE China; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Thin forests and grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Coelachne simpliciuscula (Wight & Arn. ex Steud.) Munro ex Benth. 小麗草
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 19: 93. 1881; FFJ 6: 165, fig. 135. 1995; FOC 22: 560. 2006; FGD 9: 367, fig. 179. 2009.
Panicum simpliciusculum Wight & Arn. ex Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 96. 1854.
Coelachne pulchella auct. non R. Br.: FHK 428. 1861; FKH 326. 1912.

Annual herb, 10–20 cm tall. Culms slender, ascending from the decumbent base, rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades soft, lanceolate, 1–3 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or hirtellous along veins; ligule a line of short hairs; leaf sheaths loose, glabrous or upper margins ciliolate. Panicle linear, loosely spiciform, 3–8 × 0.5–1 cm. Spikelets green or often purplish, 2–3 mm, borne on short erect branches; rachilla internode 0.6–0.8 mm; glumes broadly ovate, herbaceous with membranous margins, lower glume 0.9–1.2 mm, 1–3(–5)-veined, upper glume ca. 1.5 mm, 5–7-veined; lemmas lanceolate, lower lemma 2–2.3 mm, glabrous or puberulous, lower palea equal to lemma; upper lemma 1.6–1.7 mm, pubescent below middle on centre back and margins. Anthers 2–3, ca. 0.3 mm. Caryopsis brown at maturity, ca. 1.2 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Wai. C. Wilford 253 (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Marshy places and streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Coelogyne fimbriata Lindl. 流蘇貝母蘭
Bot. Reg. 11: t. 868. 1825; FHK 354. 1861; FKH 264. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 83, fig. 45. 1977; FRPS 18: 344, pl. 57: 3–4. 1999; FGD 7: 463, fig. 232. 2006; FOC 25: 318. 2009.

Creeping terrestrial herb; rhizomes 2–3 mm thick consisting of 8–10 internodes; annual growth consisting of a rhizome ending with an oblong or ellipsoidal pseudobulb of 3–4 × 1–2 cm, terminated with 2 leaves. Leaves petiolate, petioles 5–6 mm; leaf blades oblong-elliptic, 4.5–10 × 1.5–2 cm, apex acute. Flowers lemon-yellow, 2 (sometimes 1 or 3) terminal to a short scape of 2–3 cm; sepals alike, oriented in an equal triangle, ovate, 2 × 0.8–0.9 cm, apex acute; petals linear, 2 × 0.2 cm; lip with fimbriate apical lobe, yellow and marked with cinnamon-brown lines and patches on the side; column 12–13 mm, winged; anther conical; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary 4 × 2 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 6176, 11094 (CUHK); G. Barretto 316.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Jiangxi; Sikkim, India, Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia.
Ecology: Tree trunks or large rocks in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.

Coelogyne leungiana S. Y. Hu 單唇貝母蘭
Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25: 223, fig. 9a–e. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 84. 1977; FRPS 18: 341. 1999; FGD 7: 463. 2006; FOC 25: 318. 2009.

Epiphytic herb, rhizomes elongate, 1 mm thick, branched; pseudobulbs oblong-ellipsoidal, 2–4 × 0.8–1.5 cm, the base subtended by scales of 1–2 cm. Leaves petiolate, petioles 6–8 mm; leaf blades oblong-elliptic, 5–8 × 1.3–2.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers yellow, 1 or 2 apical to a scape of 2.5–3.5 cm; pedicels 3–4 mm; sepals and petals similar, ovate-lanceolate, 2 cm; lip entire, ovate-lanceolate, 2 × 0.7 cm across middle; column narrowly winged, 1.4 cm; anther ovoid, 3 mm across middle; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary subturbinate, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng. S. Y. Hu 11004, 12454 (CUHK).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Exposed rocks. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. Leung from New Territories in 1969.

Coix lacryma-jobi L. 薏苡
Sp. Pl. 2: 972. 1753; FKH 317. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 293, pl. 73: 1–2. 1997; FFJ 6: 277, fig. 252. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 536. 2000; FOC 22: 648. 2006; FGD 9: 510, fig. 272. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect, robust, 1–2 m tall, glabrous, branched. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous; leaf blades linearlanceolate, flat and open, 10–40 × 1.5–7 cm, usually glabrous, midvein stout, base subrounded or cordate, apex acuminate or long acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule ca.1 mm, dry membranous, ciliate. Male raceme 1–5 cm, spikelets in pairs with terminal triad. Male spikelets oblong-ovate; glumes many-veined, lower glume winged on keels, wing margin ciliolate; anthers 4–5 mm. Female spikelet usually 3, one fertile, and 2 sterile at base; lower glume acuminate and beak-like; stamen usually absent; style thin and long, exserted apically from apex of involucre. Caryopsis ovoid or subglobose, ca. 5–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 912, 1018, 2299.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, widely naturalized in tropics, cultivated in paleotropics.
Ecology: Wet places by streams, ditches and open fields, often cultivated. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Food (beverage base), medicinal (folklore).

Coleus scutellarioides (L.) Benth. 五彩蘇（洋紫蘇）
Edward's Bot. Reg. 15: t. 1300. 1830; FRPS 66: 542. 1977; FOC 17: 293. 1994; FGD 3: 468. 1995.
Coleus blumei Benth., Labiat. Gen. Sp. 56. 1832.
Solenostemon scutellarioides (L.) Codd, Bothalia 11(4): 439 – 440. 1975.
Ocimum scutellarioides L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 834. 1763.

Annual herbs, erect or ascending, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems and branches finely pubescent or glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–5(–8) cm; leaf blade variable in size, shape and colour, generally ovate in outline, 3–7(–15) × (1–)3–5(–10) cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin crenate, serrate or sometimes laciniate, variously coloured with yellow, dull red and purplish or green, puberulent on midvein and secondary veins; verticillasters many‑flowered, forming panicles of 5–10(–25) cm, puberulent. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, lengthening to 7 mm in fruit, 10‑veined, minutely hispid, glandular; middle lobe of upper lip broadly ovate, as long as or longer than lobes of lower lip, reflexed in fruit; lateral lobes ovate, about half the length of middle lobe; lower lip rhombic, longer than upper lip, lobes narrowly triangular. Corolla purple to blue, 0.8 – 1.3 cm, puberulent, tube abruptly recurved, throat to 2.5 mm wide, upper lip erect. Nutlets brown, broadly ovoid to globose, 1–1.2 mm, shiny.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 90; HK sheet 4437.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Dec.–Jul. of the following years; fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was also reported as Coleus pumilus Blanco or Coleus scutellarioides var. crispipilus (Merr.) H. Keng previously (Check List HK Plants 76. 1993; 81. 2004). Other Coleus species were also cultivated for ornamental purpose, including such occasional examples as Coleus aromaticus Benth. (芳香鞘蕊花), Coleus carnosifolius (Hemsl.) Dunn (肉葉鞘蕊花) and others.
records.uses:
Ornamental.

Other Coleus species were also cultivated for ornamental purpose, including such occasional examples as Coleus aromaticus Benth. (芳香鞘蕊花), Coleus carnosifolius (Hemsl.) Dunn (肉葉鞘蕊花) and others.

records.text:
Colocasia esculenta (L.) Schott 芋
Melet. Bot. 18. 1832; FYN 2: 778. 1979; FFJ 6: 432, fig. 393. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 678. 2000; FGD 9: 201, fig. 116. 2009; FOC 23: 74. 2010.
Arum esculentum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 965. 1753.
Colocasia antiquorum Schott, Melet. Bot. 18. 1832; FKH 288. 1912.

Perennial herb; tuber ovoid to ellipsoidal. Leaves 2–3 or more, peltate; petiole 20–90 cm, green or purplish, sheathing at base; leaf blade ovate to oblong-ovate in outline, 20–50 × 10–35 cm, base deeply cordate, apex acute or shortly acuminate; lateral veins 4 pairs. Peduncle usually solitary, shorter than petiole. Spathe various in length, usually 20 cm, tube green, ovoid, ca. 4 cm; limb pale yellow to greenish, lanceolate or elliptic, acuminate, ca. 17 cm, margins inrolled; spadix ca. 10 cm, female portion conical, 3–3.5 cm, at the base; sterile portion slender, cylindrical, 3–3.3 cm; male portion cylindrical, 4–4.5 cm; appendage subulate ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Cultivated or wild. HK sheet 32847, 36157.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; widely cultivated in the tropics. E
cology: Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Food.

Combretum alfredii Hance 風車子
J. Bot. 9(101): 131. 1871; FYN 1: 95, pl. 24: 9 – 12. 1977; FRPS 53(1): 27, pl. 5: 9 –12. 1984, excl. syn. Combretum extensum Roxb. ex G. Don; FGD 3: 202, fig. 139: 7 – 9. 1995.
Combretum kwangsiense H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 24(4): 450. 1943.

Woody vine or scandent shrub, 15 – 20 m or longer; bark greyish brown, striate; branchlets, petioles, inflorescences and calyx densely rusty or white villous. Petiole very short; leaf blade ovate, long elliptic, ovate-oblong or oblong, 6–18 × (3–)5–8 cm, base rounded, truncate or shallowly cordate, apex acuminate or acute, adaxially pubescent at first, later puberulous along midvein; lateral veins 5 – 8(–10) on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, elevated abaxially, reticulate veins conspicuous. Spikes densely flowered, rearranged in terminal panicles. Calyx-tube infundibuliform, lobes 5. Petals 5, pale red or scarlet, hairy abaxially. Ovary 5-ribbed, hairy; ovules 2. Fruit ellipsoidal or obovoid, 2.5 – 3.5 cm, 2 – 2.5 cm in diam. including the wings, pubescent and sparsely red scaly, with 5 membranous wings.

Locality: Shui Long Wo, Kei Ling Ha, Yung Shue O, Kai Kung Leng. S. C. Ng 2522; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24073; HK sheet 39418.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Mar.; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.

Commelina auriculata Blume 耳苞鴨跖草
Enum. Pl. Javae 1: 2. 1827; FKH 283. 1912; FFJ 6: 455. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 132. 1997; FOC 24: 38. 2000; FGD 6: 321, fig. 183. 2005.

Perennial herb, stems ascending to 1.4 m, glabrous except sparsely hairy in a line distally. Leaf sheaths 0.6–1.8 cm, hairy, fringed with long hairs at mouth; leaf blade elliptic-lanceolate to lanceolate, 2–4(–8) × 1–2 cm, base ± oblique and narrowed into a short (ca. 3 mm) petiole, apex acuminate, adaxially sparsely scabrid, abaxially sometimes pubescent, or glabrous on both surfaces. Involucral bracts opposite to upper leaves, solitary or 2–3 aggregated at apex of branches, with ca. 5 mm long stalk, funnelform, ca. 1 cm, glabrous or slightly white hispid, proximal margins connate, apex acute. Peduncle simple (one branch reduced), with 2 – 5 small, bisexual flowers. Sepals 3, pale green, lanceolate or obovate, 3–4 mm, apex obtuse, posterior 2 ± connate. Petals 3, blue or with a white one, 2 longer ones ca. 7 mm, the other shorter, ca. 3 mm. Capsule globose, trigonous, ca. 4 mm, 2–3-valved with posterior valve indehiscent. Seeds 1 per valve, grey-brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm, smooth, flat on one surface.

Locality: Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 748.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Indonesia, W Oceania.
Ecology: Ravines, shaded and humid places. Flowering: Jun.

Commelina benghalensis L. 飯包草
Sp. Pl. 1: 41. 1753; FHK 376. 1861; FKH 284. 1912; FFJ 6: 455, fig. 409. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 128, pl. 31: 3 – 4. 1997; FOC 24: 37. 2000; FGD 6: 321. 2005.

Perennial herb; stems much branched, creeping at the base, ascending distally to 70 cm or more, sparsely pubescent. Leaves petiolate; leaf sheaths 0.5–1.5 cm, sparsely hirsute-ciliate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic-ovate, 3–7 × 1.5–4 cm, base rounded and narrowed into a broad petiole, apex obtuse or acute, subglabrous, ciliate on leaf sheath and petiole. Involucral bracts opposite to the upper leaves, solitary, or 2–3 aggregated at apex of branches, sessile or very shortly stalked, funnelform and ± compressed, 1–1.4 cm, sparsely hairy, margins connate, open at the apex only. Peduncle 2-branched; the proximal branch longer than the bract, with 1 male flowers, the distal branch shorter, with 2–3 included, fertile flowers. Sepals 3, green unequal, lanceolate or obovate, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Petals 3, blue, ovate, 3–5 mm, posterior 2 ± connate, stalked. Capsule ellipsoidal, 4–6 mm, 3-valved. Seeds black, cylindrical or semi-cylindrical, ca. 2 mm, rugose, irregularly reticulate, truncate at one end.

Locality: Tai Wai, Ting Kau, Yuen Long, Nam Sang Wai. Y. W. Lam 747, 766; HK sheet 39783.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical Africa and Asia.
Ecology: Lowland wet places. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Commelina communis L. 鴨跖草
Sp. Pl. 1: 40. 1753; FHK 376. 1861; FKH 284. 1912; FFJ 6: 454, fig. 408. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 127, pl. 29: 6–7. 1997; FOC 24: 36. 2000; FGD 6: 321. 2005.

Annual herb; stems much branched, creeping or ascending to 50 cm or more, rooting at nodes, glabrous or puberulent on the upper portion. Leaves sessile or nearly so; leaf sheaths 0.7–1 cm, glabrous, scarcely ciliate; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–7(–9) × 1–2 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate, glabrous. Involucral bracts cordate, folded, 1.2–2.5 cm, apex acute, base with 1.5–4 cm long stalk, often hirsute-ciliate. Peduncle 2-branched; one branch ca. 8 mm, with 1–2 male flowers, the other branch shorter, with 3–4 bisexual flowers, nearly included in the bract; pedicels ca. 3 mm at anthesis, curved and less than 6 mm in fruit. Sepals 3, green, membranous, the posterior 2 ovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm. Petals 3, the anterior 2 dark blue, ovate, ca. 9 × 8 mm, the posterior one white, ca. 5 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, 5–7 mm, 2-valved. Seeds 2 per valve, brown-yellow, irregularly pitted, truncate at one end.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2763; Y. W. Lam 414; HK sheet 41587.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except for Qinghai, Xinjiang, and Xizang; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Indochina, Thailand.
Ecology: Shaded and humid places. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Commelina diffusa Burm. f. 節節草
Fl. Indica 18, pl. 7, fig. 2. 1768; FFJ 6: 453. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 126. 1997; FOC 24: 36. 2000; FGD 6: 320. 2005.
Commelina salicifolia auct. non Roxb.: FHK 376. 1861.
Commelina nudiflora auct. non L.: FKH 284. 1912.

Annual herb; stems creeping at the base, branching and ascending to 40 cm or more. Leaves subsessile; leaf sheath 0.6–3 cm, with red spots when dry, hispidulous throughout or in a line, ciliate on the edge; leaf blade lanceolate or proximal ones oblong, 3–12 × 0.8–3 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate or acute, margin scabrous. Involucral bracts ovate-lanceolate, folded, 1–4 cm, glabrous or hispidulous abaxially, base cordate or rounded, apex acuminate or shortly so. Peduncle 2 branched; 1 branch 1.5–2 cm, with 1–4 long-exserted male flowers; the other much shorter, with 3–5 included bisexual flowers; pedicels thick and curved, ca. 3 mm, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit. Sepals 3, unequal, the anterior one lanceolate, ca. 3 × 2 mm, the posterior 2 obovate, ca. 5 × 3 mm, ± connate at the base. Petals blue, 2 longer ones broadly ovate, ca. 4.5 × 6 mm, clawed; the third smaller, ovate, ca. 4 × 4 mm, scarcely clawed. Fertile stamens 3; filaments 5–7 mm. Capsule oblong, trigonous, ca. 5 mm, 3-valved. Seeds black, ovoid-globose, ca. 2 mm, reticulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2313; L. T. Lo 525; HK sheet 41520.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; worldwide in Tropics and Subtropics.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Commelina paludosa Blume 大苞鴨跖草
Enum. Pl. Javae 1: 2. 1827; FFJ 6: 456, fig. 410. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 129, pl. 31: 1 – 2. 1997; FOC 24: 37. 2000; FGD 6: 322. 2005.
Commelina obliqua Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 45. 1825; FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb; stems often erect from the geniculate base to 1 m, simple or sometimes branched distally, glabrous or sparsely hispidulous. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath 2–3.5 cm, hispid in a line on one side, fringed with long hairs at mouth, sometimes either glabrous with only a few hairs at mouth or hirsute throughout; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 6–18 × 2–4.5(–7) cm, base attenuate, apex long acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces or adaxially granular hairy and abaxially hirsute. Involucral bracts often 4–10 aggregated at apex of branches, sessile, funnelform, ca. 2 × 1.5–2 cm, proximal margins connate, apex acute or shortly so, glabrescent. Peduncle unbranched, ca. 1.2 cm, with (1–)3–7 flowers nearly included in involucral bracts; pedicels ca. 7 mm, twisted. Sepals 3, pale green, lanceolate, 3–6 mm. Petals 3, blue or sometimes the posterior one white, obovate to spathulate, 5–8 mm. Fertile stamens 3, unequal; filaments glabrous. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, ca. 4 mm, 3-valved. Seeds 1 per valve, dark brown, ellipsoidal, slightly flattened, finely reticulate.

Locality: Fanling, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 250; K. L. Yip 4089; HK sheet 29280.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Malaysia.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Conyza bonariensis (L.) Cronq. 香絲草
Bull. Torrey Bot. Club. 70: 632. 1943; FRPS 74: 350. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 914. 1998; FGD 8: 186. 2007.
Erigeron bonariensis L., Sp. Pl. 863. 1753.
Erigeron linifolius Willd., Sp. Pl. 3(3): 1955. 1803; FHK 176. 1861.

Annual or biennial herb; stem erect, 25–60 cm tall; lateral branches usually grow over the main axis, pubescent throughout, sparsely hirsute. Leaves densely pubescent on both surfaces; basal leaves usually withered at flowering period, oblanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, coarsely toothed or shallowly pinnatifid along margin, 3–10 × 0.2– 0.8 cm; middle leaves linear‑lanceolate to linear, entire or slightly toothed, 3–10 × 0.1–0.5 cm; upper leaves linear, entire, 1.5–6 × 0.1–0.2 cm or much smaller. Capitula 4 – 6 × 8 – 10 mm, arranged in terminal racemes or racemose‑panicles. Involucres urceolate, then widely spreading; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, herbaceous, margin scarious, densely covered with greyish white hair, inner layers 3–4 mm, outermost 2–3 mm. Receptacle flat. Marginal female florets numerous, white, corolla tube filiform, 3 mm, with or without minute ligules, 2–4‑cleft. Central bisexual florets tubular, yellow, 3 mm, upper part cylindric, lower part filiform, 5 lobes at apex. Cypselae oblong, 1.5 mm, compressed, pilose, straw‑coloured. Pappus bristles in 1 series, 3 mm, reddish brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. S. L. Thrower 1401 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2012, 2196.
Distribution: Origin from S America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Conyza canadensis (L.) Cronq. 小蓬草
Bull. Torrey Bot. Club. 70: 632. 1943; FRPS 74: 348. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 916. 1998; FGD 8: 185, fig. 104. 2007.
Erigeron canadensis L., Sp. Pl. 863. 1753.

Annual herbs, 30–120 cm tall; stems erect, densely or loosely hirsute or glabrous, branched on upper portion. Basal leaves usually withered at flowering stage; middle cauline leaves linear‑lanceolate, 3.5–10 cm × 2–6 mm, leaf surfaces nearly glabrous, bearing loose and distinct, curved and stiff hair along margin; upper leaves much reduced to about 1 cm long, linear. Capitula 3–4 × 2–3.5 mm, numerous, forming large pyramidal panicle. Involucres subcylindric, then widely spreading; phyllaries in 3–4 series, linear to linear‑lanceolate; outer ones about or less than 1 mm, glabrous or loosely ciliate, herbaceous; inner ones ca. 3 mm, glabrous, scarious along margin. Receptacle flat. Marginal female florets white, ligulate, corolla tube 2 mm, filiform, ciliate near the throat, ligule 0.5 mm. Central bisexual florets yellow, tubular, 2.5 mm, upper part cylindric, lower part filiform, 4–5‑lobed and ciliate at apex. Cypselae linear‑oblong, ca. 1 mm, compressed, minutely pubescent, pale brown. Pappus bristles in 1 series, ca. 2 mm, white to yellowish brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2383; Y. W. Lam 1007;S. L. Thrower 1538 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to N America, distributed worldwide.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Conyza japonica (Thunb.) Less. 白酒草
Syn. Compos. 204. 1832; FKH 142. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1–2): 70. 1966; FRPS 74: 342. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 918. 1998; FGD 8: 185. 2007.
Erigeron japonicum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 312. 1784.
Conyza veronicaefolia Wall. ex DC., Prodr. 5: 382. 1836; FHK 176. 1861.

Annual or biennial herbs, 15–50 cm tall. Stems erect, branched in upper portion, striate, villose. Leaves amplexicaul, villous on both surfaces; radical leaves in rosettes, obovate to spatulate, 4–11 × 1.5–4 cm, base attenuate to form wing with petiole, apex rounded, crenate or dentate; middle leaves oblanceolate to oblong, sessile, 4–5 × 0.5–1.5 cm; upper leaves much reduced in size, linear‑lanceolate. Capitula globose, 7 – 10 mm across, numerous, in tight corymbs or clustered as glomerules in terminal. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 2 – 3‑seriate, imbricate, pubescent, green in the middle, scarious and purple along margin, apex acute or acuminate; outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, 2 mm; inner ones linear‑lanceolate, 4 mm. Receptacle hemispherical, areole of hermaphrodite florets larger than those of marginal female florets, fimbriate. Florets all fertile, yellow. Ray florets numerous, pistillate, corolla filiform, 1.8–2 mm, half the length of style, ciliate at tip; style 3 mm, reddish purple. Disk florets 15, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, 4 mm, swollen in upper part, with 5 ovate lobes, each lobe bearing 2 or 3 hairs. Cypsela obovate, flattened, minutely puberulous, yellow; pappus bristles greyish white, 1‑seriate, 4 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 2015; Y. W. Lam 582; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22842 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to C and E to SW China; Japan, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Conyza sumatrensis (Retz.) Walker 蘇門白酒草
J. Jap. Bot. 46: 72. 1971; FRPS 74: 350. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 919. 1998; FGD 8: 186. 2007.
Erigeron sumatrensis Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 28. 1789.
Erigeron floribundus auct. non (H. B. K.) Sch.‑Bip.

Annual or biennial herbs, 50–100 cm tall. Stems erect, hirsute‑pubescent throughout. Basal leaves withered at flowering period; leaves in lower part oblanceolate or lanceolate, 5–15 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin coarsely toothed or subentire; middle and upper leaves gradually smaller upward, lanceolate to linear, subentire or shallowly toothed. All leaves pubescent on both surfaces. Capitula 3–5 × 5–8 mm, arranged in large panicle. Involucres urceolate, then widely spreading; phyllaries 3‑seriate, linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, greyish green, hirsute, outer ones 2–3 mm, innermost 4 mm, scarious along margin. Receptacle flat. Ray florets numerous, pistillate, corolla tube filiform, 4 mm, bearing minute ligule, pale yellow. Disk florets 5–10, hermaphrodite, pale yellow, narrowly tubular with 5 lobes at apex, 4 mm, upper part minutely ciliate. Cypselae oblong‑oblanceolate, 0.7–1.5 mm, compressed, slightly pubescent, pale brown. Pappus capillary, 4 mm, in 1 series, white to yellowish brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1900; Y. W. Lam 994; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23103 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to S America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Feb.–Aug.

Coptosapelta diffusa (Champ. ex Benth.) Steenis 流蘇子
Amer. J. Bot. 56: 806. 1969; FTW ed. 2, 4: 248, pl. 109, photo 167. 1998; FYN 15: 112, pl. 21: 1 – 5. 2003; FGD 6: 154, fig. 73. 2005.
Thysanospermum diffusum Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 168. 1852; FHK 146. 1861; FKH 125. 1912.

Evergreen trailing shrubs, to 5 m or longer, many‑branched. Branches slender, covered with appressed tawny hairs when young, glabrescent in age. Leaves firmly papery to leathery; petioles 2–5 mm, sparsely hairy; stipules lanceolate, 3–7 mm, deciduous; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2–7 × 1–2.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially with appressed hairs on the midvein and edges. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels 3–18 mm, usually bearing 2 bracteoles above the middle. Calyx‑tube globose; lobes ovate, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white or yellowish; tube 1.2–2 cm, pubescent outside and on the upper part inside; lobes 5, oblong, 4–6 × 1.4–1.6 mm, pubescent on adaxial surface. Capsule globose but slightly compressed, 5–7 mm in diam., with 2 furrows. Seeds suborbicular, very thin, fringed with fimbriate wing.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan, Sham Tseng, Tai O, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1284; HK sheet 40021, 40754.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Ravines, hillsides, trailing upon trees or rocks. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Corchorus aestuans L. 甜麻（假黃麻）
Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 1079. 1774; FTW 3: 695. 1977; FFJ 3: 396, fig. 279. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 80, pl. 20: 4 –7. 1989; FGD 4: 163. fig. 105. 2000.
Corchorus acutangulus Lam., Encycl. 2: 104. 1786; FHK 40. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 64. 1965.

Annual herbs, up to ca. 1 m tall; stem red brown, slightly yellowish puberulous. Stipules subulate, 4mm. Petioles ca. 0.5–2 cm, pale yellow-hispid; leaf blade ovate, 2–6.5 × 1– 4 cm, base rounded, apex short acuminate or acute, margin serrate, one pair of teeth near base usually elongating into caudate appendages, sparsely hispid on both surfaces; basal veins 3, lateral veins 3– 6 pairs. Peduncle and pedicels very short or almost obsolete. Sepals 5, narrowly oblong, ca. 5 mm, boat-shaped at distal half, horned at apex, purple red abaxially. Petals nearly as long as sepals, obovate, yellow. Stamens many, ca. 3 mm, yellow. Ovary long cylindric, pubescent. Style clavate; stigma 5-toothed. Capsule cylindrical, angular cylindric, ca. 1.5–3 cm, 6-ribbed, 3–4 of the ribs expaned into narrow wings, terminating in 3 entire or bifid points or horns, dehiscing into 3–4 valves when mature. Seeds many.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Long Sai Wan, Tsing Yi, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 899, 2382.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; tropical Asia, C America, Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides and near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Corchorus capsularis L. 黃麻
Sp. Pl. 529. 1753; FHK 40. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 63. 1965; FRPS 49(1): 78. 1989; FGD 4: 163. 2000.

Annual erect woody herbs, 1–2.5 m tall, glabrous; stems erect woody. Stipules filiform, deciduous. Petioles 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade ovate lanceolate or lanceolate, 5–12 × 2–5 cm, papery, base round, apex acuminate, margin rough coarsely serrate, one pair of teeth near base subulate and curved downward; 3 basal veins ascending but not exceeding middle of leaf blade, lateral veins 6–7 pairs. Peduncle and pedicels short. Sepals 5, pale purple, 3 –4 mm. Petals yellow, narrowly obovate, as long as sepals. Stamens 8–22, inserted on short androgynophore. Ovary globose, 5-locular; stigma lobed. Capsule globose, 1 cm in diam., without horns at apex, ribbed and verrucose on the surface, dehiscing into 5 valves when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Fanling, Luk Keng, Sha Po, Pui O (cultivated or naturalized). Y. S. Lau 1313, 1991; Y. W. Lam 1234.
Distribution: Commonly cultivated in regions S of Changjiang River; native to tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Late autumn.

Cordia dichotoma G. Forst. 破布木
Fl. Ins. Austr. 18. 1786; FGZ 566. 1956; FHN 3: 452, fig. 852. 1974; FTW 4: 395. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 9, pl. 1: 8 – 12. 1990; FFJ 4: 505, fig. 402. 1989; FOC 16: 333. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 390, photo 226. 1998.
Varronia sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 138. 1790.
Cordia myxa auct. non L.: FKH 176. 1912.

Tree, 3–8 m tall. Branches sparsely pilose when young, glabrescent. Petiole 2–5 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, ovate to broadly ovate or elliptic, 6–13 × 4–9 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex obtuse to mucronate, margin usually subundulate to undulate dentate, rarely entire, sparsely pubescent or glabrous. Inflorescences terminating leafy lateral branches, dichotomously branched into corymbose cymes, widely spaced, 5–8 cm wide. Flowers dimorphic, sessile. Calyx campanulate, 5–6 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes unequal, triangular. Corolla white, nearly as long as calyx; lobes shorter than tube. Filaments of male flowers ca. 3.5 mm, filaments of bisexual flowers 1–2 mm. Rudimentary pistil globose. Style united portion 1–1.5 mm, first branches ca. 1 mm, second branches 2–3 mm; stigma spatulate. Drupes yellow or reddish, subglobose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., with sticky mesocarp, surrounded by persistent calyx.

Locality: Stanley, Garden Rd., Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung (Tai Long), Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 878, 1390; P. S. Choi 344.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Kashmir, Myanmar, Pakistan, N India, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, NE Australia, Pacific islands
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Oil, medicinal (folklore), timber.

Cordyline fruticosa (L.) A. Chev. 朱蕉
Cat. Pl. Jard. Bot. Saigon. 66. 1919; FRPS 14: 273, pl. 51: 2. 1980; FOC 24: 204. 2000; FGD 9: 212, fig. 121. 2009.
Convallaria fruticosa L., Herb. Amb. 16. 1754.
Asparagus terminalis L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 1: 450. 1762, nom. illeg. superfl.(included Convallaria fruticosa L. 1754).
Dracaena terminalis L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 12) 12: 246. 1767.
Cordyline terminalis (L.) Kunth, Abh. Königl. Akad. Wiss. Berlin 30. 1820; FTW ed. 2, 5: 76. 2000.
Aletris chinensis Lam., Encycl. 1: 79. 1873.

Erect shrubby plant, 1–3 m. Stems simple or sometimes branched. Leaves petiolate; petiole 10–30 cm, sulcate adaxially; leaf blade green or variously coloured, oblong-lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 25 – 50 × 5–10 cm, midvein distinct and raised abaxially, base amplexicaul, apex aristate. Panicle 30–60 cm; branches many, spreading, 6–13 cm, many-flowered. Flowers subsessile or shortly pedicellate; bracteoles 3, ovate, 2–3 mm, apex cuspidate, margin broadly membranous. Perianth reddish, yellowish, or bluish purple; tube 5–6 mm; lobes erect or recurved, nearly as long as tube. Stamens inserted in throat of perianth, slightly shorter than perianth. Fruit reddish, several-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan; probably native to Pacific islands but cultivated pantropically.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Coriandrum sativum L. 芫荽
Sp. Pl. 1: 256. 1753; FHK 135. 1861; FKH 118. 1912; FRPS 55(1): 89, pl. 40. 1979; FGD 2: 337, fig. 225. 1991; FOC 14: 30. 2005.

Annual herb, to 60 cm tall. Basal and lower leaves pinnate to 2-pinnatisect; petioles to 13 cm, shortly sheathing at base; blades ovate in outline, to 14 × 8 cm; pinnae broadly ovate or flabelliform, 1–2 × 1–1.5 cm, variously toothed or incised; ultimate segments broad. Mid and upper cauline leaves ternate-2–3-pinnatisect, reducing upwards; ultimate segments linear to filiform, 2–15 × 0.5–1.5 mm, obtuse, entire. Peduncles 2–10 cm; rays 2–8, 1–2.5 cm; bracteoles 2–5, linear, entire; umbellules 3–9-flowered. Pedicels 2–5 mm. Calyx-teeth ovate-deltoid or ovate-lanceolate, unequal. Fruit 1.5–5 mm wide.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2698; HK sheet 12663.
Distribution: Native to Mediterranean region; cultivated in China.
Uses: Vegetable.

Coronopus didymus (L.) J. E. Smith 臭薺
Fl. Brit. 2: 691. 1804; FGD 3: 33. 1995; FOC 8: 34. 2001.
Lepidium didymus L. , Syst. Nat. (ed. 12) 2: 433. 1767.
Senebiera pinnatifida DC., Mem. Soc. Hist. Nat. Paris 7: 144, pl. 9. 1799; FKH 35. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, with foul smell, 10–50 cm tall. Stems usually prostrate, several tufted, branched above. Petioles 5–8 mm; leaves pinnatisect or bipinnatisect, lateral lobes 2–7 on each side or rachis, variable in size, linear or narrow-oblong, 4 – 8 mm, glabrous on both surfaces; cauline leaves similar to basal ones, progressively smaller and less divided upward. Racemes terminal or lateral and leaf-opposed. Flowers 1 mm in diam. Sepals ovate, 0.5–0.7 mm. Petals white, elliptic to linear, 0.4–0.5 mm. Stamens often 2, rarely 4, filaments white, dilated at base, anthers ovoid. Silicles 1.5 × 2–2.5 mm, didymous, compressed, emarginate at both ends; valves semiorbicular, prominately reticulate or rugose. Seeds red-brown, reniform, ca. 1 mm, finely reticulate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Hang, Shatin. Y. S. Lau 2100, 1785; W. J. Tutcher 6763.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Taiwan, Shandong, Hubei, Sichuan, Yunnan; Europe, N America, Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides, valleys. Flowering: Mar; fruiting: Apr.

Corydalis balansae Prain 台灣黃堇
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 65: 25. 1879; FRPS 32: 440. 1999; FGD 4: 64. 2000.
Corydalis tashiroi Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 33: 65. 1909.

Annual or biennial herb, ca. 50 cm tall, without tubers. Stems glabrous, many-branched, angulate. Petiole 7–16 cm; cauline leaves bipinnate, outline broadly ovate, 10 –20 × 10 –15 cm; leaflets pinnately parted to divided, segments obovate or ovate, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin incised. Racemes leaf-opposed, ca. 12 cm. Bracts oblong-lanceolate or ovate. Flowers yellow, 1.2–2 cm. Petals often shallowly cristate, outer one shortly spurred. Stigma 2-fid. Capsules linear, 3–4.5 × 0.3 cm. Seeds black, many, densely small pitted, carunculate.

Locality: Lantau Island (Tung Chung). Y. W. Lam 33.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Jul.

Corylopsis multiflora Hance 瑞木（大果臘瓣花）
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., sér. 4, 15: 224. 1861; FHN 2: 335. 1965; FRPS 35(2): 82, pl. 18. 1979; FFJ 2: 254, fig. 213. 1985; FGD 1: 162, fig. 178. 1987; FOC 9: 37. 2003.
Corylopsis wilsonii Hemsl., Icon. Pl. 29: pl. 2819. 1919.

Shrub or small tree; young branches tomentose; older branches grey-brown, glabrescent; buds grey-white tomentose. Stipules oblong, 1.8–2 cm, hairy; petiole 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade leathery, ovate, obovate or obovate-elliptic, 7–15 × 4 – 8 cm, base almost symmetrical, cordate, apex acute, margin serrate, teeth mucronate, abaxially glaucous, stellately pubescent at least along veins; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Inflorescence 2–4 cm, with 1–5 leaves at base, peduncle pubescent; general bracts ovate, 1.5–2 cm, abaxially hairy. Calyx tube glabrous. Petals oblanceolate, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm. Stamens 6–7 mm, exserted. Ovary glabrous, styles slightly shorter than stamens. Capsules hard woody, glabrous, 1.2–2 × 0.8 –1.4 cm. Seeds 8–10 mm, black.

Locality: Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 2117; F. W. Xing 9194.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Taiwan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Eucalyptus citriodora Hook. 檸檬桉
J. Exped. Trop. Australia 235. 1848; FHN 2: 2, fig. 287. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 37. 1984; FFJ 4: 81, fig. 63. 1989; FGX 1: 877, pl. 342: 1 – 3. 1991; FGD 3: 165. 1995; FYN 7: 99. 1997; FOC 13: 324. 2007.
Eucalyptus maculata Hook. var. citriodora (Hook.) L. H. Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 540. 1924; FGZ 213. 1956.
Corymbia citriodora (Hook.) K. D. Hill & L. A. S. Johnson, Telopea 6(2– 3): 388. 1995.

Tree, to 28 m tall, strongly lemon scented. Bark smooth, greyish white, exfoliating. Leaves of juvenile plants: peltate, petiolate; leaf blade lanceolate, base rounded, glandular hairy, with black glands on both surfaces. Leaves of adult plant: petioles 1.5–2 cm; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, 10 – 25 × ca. 1 – 4 cm, slightly twisted, with black glands on both surfaces. Inflorescences paniculate, terminal or axillary, umbels 1–3-flowered; peduncle 3–4 mm, 2-ridged. Flower buds long obovoid, 6–7 mm. Pedicels 3–4 mm, ridged. Hypanthium ca. 5 × 4 mm; calyptra ca. 1.5 mm, slightly wider than hypanthium, apex rounded, apiculate. Stamens 6– 7 mm, in 2 whorls. Capsule urceolate, 1–1.2 × 0.8–1 cm; valves 3 or 4, inclusive in hypanthium.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1527; L. T. Lo 322.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Dec.
Uses: Environmental, timber, essential oil, ornamental.

Eucalyptus torelliana F. Muell. 毛葉桉
Fragm. 10: 106. 1877. FRPS 53(1): 37. 1984; FFJ 4: 81, fig. 64. 1989; FGX 1: 882, pl. 344: 5– 8. 1991; FGD 3: 165. 1995; FYN 7: 98. 1997; FOC 13: 323. 2007.
Corymbia torelliana (F. Muell.) K. D. Hill & L. A. S. Johnson, Telopea 6(2– 3): 385. 1995.

Tree; bark greyish green, smooth, exfoliating but persistent at trunk base. Branchlets terete, hirsute. Leaves of juvenile plants: peltate, shortly petiolate; leaf blade ovate, 7 – 15 × 4 – 9 cm, abaxially pubescent. Leaves of adult plants: petioles 1 – 2 cm, hirsute; leaf blade thinly leathery, ovate, 10–14 × 1–7 cm, base rounded, apex acute, grey and pubescent abaxially. Inflorescences paniculate, terminal or axillary, 8 – 11 cm, umbels 3 – 7-flowered; peduncle pubescent. Flower buds obovoid, ca. 10 × 6 – 7 mm. Pedicels 1–3 mm, glabrous. Hypanthium semiglobose, ca. 6 mm; calyptra 4 – 4.5 mm, apex rounded. Stamens 8 – 10 mm. Style 5–7 mm. Capsule globose, 1–1.3 cm in diam., constricted distally; valves 3, included in hypanthium.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 11247, 34515.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan (cultivated); native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Environmental.

Costus speciosus (J. König) Sm. 閉鞘薑
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 1: 249. 1791; FHN 4: 91. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 149. 1981; FGD 2: 432. 1991; FOC 24: 321. 2000.
Banksea speciosa J. König, Observ. Bot. 3: 75. 1783.

Stems 1–3 m, base slightly woody, apex branched and spirally twisted when old. Petiole 5–7 mm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 15–20 × 6–10 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate or caudateacuminate, abaxially densely sericeous. Inflorescences terminal, ellipsoidal or ovoid, 5–15 cm. Bracts bright red, ovate, ca. 2 cm, leathery, pubescent, apex sharply pointed; bracteoles pale red, 1.2–1.5 cm. Calyx red, 1.8–2 cm, leathery, apex 3-lobed; lobes reddish black, rigid, and densely sericeous at apex. Corolla tube ca. 1 cm; lobes oblong-elliptic, ca. 5 cm, apex white or red. Labellum white, trumpet-shaped, 6.5–9 cm, apex toothed and crisped, with edges overlapping. Stamens petaloid, white with orange-yellow base, urceolate, ca. 4.5–1.3 cm, pubescent. Capsules red, globose, ca. 1.5 cm, slightly woody. Seeds black, glossy, ca. 3 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Tai Hang Rd., Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 605; Y. S. Lau 2123; HK sheet 39872.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Cotula anthemoides L. 芫荽菊
Sp. Pl. 891. 1753; FHK 185. 1861; FKH 146. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 204. 1966; FRPS 76(1): 134. 1983; FGD 8: 200, fig. 119. 2007.

Small annual herbs; stem procumbent or decumbent, 4–15 cm or longer, branched and diffuse, glabrous or brownish villose. Leaves alternate, subglabrous or loosely villose on both surfaces, bipinnatisect, primary lateral lobes elliptic‑oblong, about 5 pairs, terminal lobes triangular to lanceolate, shortly acute; basal leaves oblanceolate‑oblong, 3–5 × 1–2 cm; median cauline leaves oblong or elliptic, 1.5–2.5 × 0.7–1.6 cm, base semi‑amplexicaul. Capitula heterogamous and disciform, 4–7 mm across, solitary on branch terminals, axillary, or opposite to leaves; peduncle 5–10 mm. Involucres dish‑like; phyllaries 2‑seriate, oblong, green with a red line on midvein, margin scarious, apex obtuse to rounded; outer layer larger in size, about 2–3 mm; inner layer smaller, 1–1.5 mm. Receptacle flat, naked. Marginal florets pistillate, in many rows, corolla none with the pistils only. Disk florets hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, yellow, 4‑lobed at apex. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, dorsiventrally compressed, 1–1.2 × 0.8 mm, smooth, glandular, margin broadly and thickly winged, base with stalks derived from the receptacle, especially appeared on the outer cypselae. Pappus absent.

Locality: Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Sha Tin, High Island, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 243; W. J. Tutcher 9163; S. Y. Hu 12909 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, India, Pakistan, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places near streams, paddy fields. Flowering: Jul.–Apr. of the following year.

Crassocephalum crepidioides (Benth.) S. Moore 野茼蒿
J. Bot. 50: 211. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 205. 1966; FTW ed. 2, 4: 922, pl. 434. 1998; FRPS 77(1): 304, pl. 67: 1–2. 1999; FGD 8: 228, fig. 139. 2007.
Gynura crepidioides Benth., Niger Fl. 438. 1849.

Annual erect herbs; stem 30–100 cm tall, striate, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves elliptic or elliptic‑oblong, 7–13 × 3–5 cm, petiole 1–2(–5.5) cm long, base narrowed to petiole, apex acute or acuminate, margin irregularly serrate or double‑serrate, some lyrately pinnatifid with terminal lobe large ovate‑elliptic, and 1–3 pairs of lateral lobes near base, smaller and elliptic‑oblong, both surfaces glabrous or subglabrous. Capitula homogamous and discoid, several arranged as corymbs at terminal. Involucres cylindric with base swollen, about 9–11 mm long, 5 mm across middle, 6–8 mm across base, calyculate with several linear bracteoles 2 3 mm; phyllaries linear‑lanceolate, 9–11 × 0.7–1.5 mm, abaxial side puberulous, margin scarious, apex acute and with tuft of minute hair. Receptacle flat, alveolate with margin of areoles shortly scarious, areoles elevated at centre. All florets tubular, bisexual and fertile, corolla yellow with limb purplish or reddish brown, or appeared as orange‑red, 8 – 11 mm long, tube filiform and slender, gradually and slightly dilated at summit, apex 5‑lobed; anthers included, base shortly sagittate, apical appendages elongate‑lanceolate; stylar branches exserted, acute apically, papillose hairy. Cypselae cylindric, 2–2.5 mm long, reddish brown to brown, ribbed, puberulent. Pappus bristles copious, capillary and silky, white in colour, 9–10 mm long, easily shed off.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1549; S. Y. Pang & S. L. Wong 302 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 5453 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; India, Indochina, Africa.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Crateva trifoliata (Roxb.) B. S. Sun 鈍葉魚木
FRPS 32: 489. 1999.
Capparis trifoliata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey 2: 571. 1832.
Crateva adansonii subsp. trifoliata (Roxb.) Jacobs, Blumea 12(2): 199. 1964.
Crateva erythrocarpa Gagn., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 55: 322. 1908; FHN 1: 345. 1964.

Deciduous tree or shrub, 1.5 –30 m tall. Branches greyish brown, with leaf-scars. Leaves digitately ternate; petioles 4.5 – 12 cm, canaliculated. Leaflets papery; petiolules 3–10 mm; blade ovate, elliptic or ovate-lanceolae, 7–12 × 3 –5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, rarely obtuse, lateral ones inaequilateral, glabrous; lateral veins usually 5 –7 on each side of midvein. Corymbs lateral or terminal. Pedicels 4– 6 cm. Sepals 3–5 × 2–3 mm, orange red when dry. Petals initially white, later turning pale yellow, ovate or oblong, 1–2 × 1–1.3 cm; claw 4 – 8 mm. Stamens 15–26, purple, unequal. Gynophore 1.5 – 4.5 cm. Ovary ellipsoid; stigma sessile. Fruit globose, ca. 4 cm in diam., smooth, red when mature.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Ng Tung Chai, also cultivated. L. T. Lo 281; F. W. Xing 8162; HK sheet 40177.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India, Malaysia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was reported as Crateva religiosa G. Forst. previously (Check List HK Plants 41. 1993).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: This species was reported as Crateva religiosa G. Forst. previously (Check List HK Plants 41. 1993).

records.text:
Crateva unilocularis Buch.-Ham. 樹頭菜
Trans. Linn. Soc. 15: 121. 1827; FGD 1: 83, fig. 90. 1987; FRPS 32: 486, pl. 123. 1999.
Crateva religiosa auct. non Forst. f.: FKH 36. 1912; FGZ 108, fig. 40. 1956; FHN 1: 346, fig. 175. 1964.

Deciduous tree, 4–6(–15) m tall. Leaves digitately ternate; petioles 4–12 cm, with glands at apex. Leaflets thinly leathery; petiolules 5 –10 mm; blade ovate or elliptic, (4–)7–18 × (2.5–)3–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, lateral ones inaequilateral, glabrous, adaxially ± shining, abaxially greyish; lateral veins usually 8 –11 on each side of midvein. Corymbs terminal. Pedicels 3 –7 cm. Sepals lanceolate, 3 –7 × 2–3 mm. Petals white or pale yellow; petal-blade ovate or oblong, 1–3.5 × 0.5 –2.5 cm; claw 0.7–1 cm. Stamens 13 –30. Gynophore 4 – 7 cm. Ovary ovoid, 3 – 4 mm; stigma capitate, subsessile. Fruit subglobose, 2.5– 4 cm in diam., initially smooth, with yellow or cream tubercles when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 486; H. C. Tang 131.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; tropical Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cratoxylum cochinchinense (Lour.) Blume 黃牛木
Mus. Bot. Lugd. Bat. 2: l7. 1852; FRPS 50(2): 76.1990; FHN 2: 53. 1965; FGD 3: 204. 1995.
Hypericum cochinchinense Lour. Fl. Cochinch. 472. 1790.
Cratoxylum polyanthum Korth. Verh. Nat. Gesch. Bot. 175, t. 36. 1842; FHK 24. 1861; FKH 42. 1912.

Shrubs or trees, 1–10 m tall, bark yellowish-white, glabrous. Petioles 2– 5 mm; leaves elliptic, narrow-elliptic, ovate-oblong or rarely subovate, 3 –11 × 1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acute, shortly acuminate or slightly obtuse; lateral veins slightly obvious on both surfaces. Cymes axillary or extra-axillary, 1– 5-flowered. Flowers red, ca. 1 cm in diam. Sepals elliptic, 5 –7 mm. Petals obovate, ca. 10 –14 mm, base cuneate, without scale, with linear-glands. Stamens usually united into 3 bundles, 4–8 mm, glands 3, alternate with staminal bundles, conic, 2–3 mm. Capsules elliptic, 8–12 mm, with persistent calyx. Seeds 6 mm, winged on one side.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 110, 2270; Y. S. Lau 2180.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets or secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Crescentia alata H. B. & K. 十架樹
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 3: 158. 1818 [1819]; FRPS 69: 58, pl. 16. 1990; FFJ 5: 86, fig. 94. 1993.

Small tree, 5–12 m tall, to 25 cm in d.b.h. Branches glabrous, terete, fissured. Leaves leathery, clustered on brachyblasts, usually simple leaves and digitately 3( – 5)‑foliolate compound leaves on the same brachyblast. Simple leaves subsessile, linear to elliptic‑linear, 1.9–3.2 × 0.3–1 cm, similar to leaflets or petiole of compound leaves. Compound leaves: petiole winged, 2.7–11.5 × 0.3–1.5 cm, oblanceolate, lepidote; leaflets subsessile, oblanceolate, 1–4.5 × 0.3–1.2 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex rotund or emarginate, margin entire, lepidote and glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers solitary or in clusters of 2 on stems. Pedicels lepidote, 5–8 mm. Calyx divided to base, lobes 2, ovate, 1.5–2 cm, subequal, glabrous, slightly lepidote at base, often with impressed plateform glands. Corolla yellowish brown, with purplish red patches and stripes, campanulate, swollen at one side, tube 2.8–5.5 cm; limb 5‑lobed, lobes broadly triangular, 1–1.5 cm, apex mucronate, glandular‑lepidote abaxially. Fertile stamens 4, slightly exserted, thecae partly divergent. Ovary conical, glabrous and lepidote, 5–6 mm; ovules in many rows on 4 lateral placentations. Style filiform, exserted. Berries subglobose, 7 –10 cm. Seeds small, thin, 6–7 × 7–9 mm, not winged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1224; HK sheet 32500, 39028.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to Mexico to Costa Rica, widely cultivated in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Crinum asiaticum L. var. sinicum (Roxb. ex Herb.) Baker 文殊蘭
Handb. Amaryll. 75. 1888; FHN 4: 145, fig. 1050. 1977; FRPS 16(1): 8, pl. 2: 1–2. 1985; FGD 5: 446, fig. 240. 2003.
Crinum sinicum Roxb. ex Herb., Bot. Mag. 47: 7, sub pl. 2121. 1820.
Crinum asiaticum auct. non L.: FHK 388. 1861.

Stout perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs narrowly cylindrical, up to 30 cm long and 10–15 cm in diam. Leaves basal, linear-lanceolate, 50–120 × 6–10(–15) cm, apex shortly acuminate, sharply pointed, margin entire, dark green; midvein impressed adaxially, keeled abaxially. Scape solid, 0.6–1 m. Umbel 10–20-flowered; involucres 2, broadly lanceolate, 7–12.5 × 3.5–4.5 cm, green, herbaceous; bracts linear, 7–11 cm × 3–5 mm, membranous. Flowers white, fragrant; pedicels 0.5–2 cm. Perianth salverform; tube greenish white, straight, 6–9 cm; segments linear-lanceolate, 6 –8 cm × 6–10 mm, apex acuminate. Stamens 6, subequal; filament ca. 4 cm, purplish apically; anther linear, 1.5–2 cm. Style filiform, slightly shorter than stamens, declinate. Capsule subglobose, 3–5 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Long Sai Wan, Ham Tin, Tai Wan, Long Ke, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 508; Y. S. Lau 2317.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Sandy places near seaside and river banks. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Crinum latifolium L. is cultivated for ornamental purpose in Hong Kong. It can be easily recognized by its rosepurple and larger flower.
records.uses:
Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Crinum latifolium L. is cultivated for ornamental purpose in Hong Kong. It can be easily recognized by its rosepurple and larger flower.

records.text:
Crossostephium chinense (L.) Makino 芙蓉菊
Bot. Mag. Tokyo 20: 33. 1906; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 231. 1966; FRPS 76(1): 131. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 927. 1998; FGD 8: 194, fig. 114. 2007.
Artemisia chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 849. 1753.

Perennial aromatic herbs to subshrubs, 10–40 cm tall, branched in upper portion, branches ascending, densely greyish tomentose, with leaves crowded at shoot apices, the vegetative shoots having very short internodes, the flowering shoots with longer internodes. Leaves fleshy, narrowly spatulate to oblanceolate, 1.5–4 × 0.4–1.2 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, sessile, entire or 3–5‑lobed near the tip, apex obtuse‑rounded, both surfaces densely covered with greyish lanate and stellate hair. Capitula heterogamous and disciform, subglobose, 7 mm across, in leafy racemose or racemose‑panicle form; peduncle short, 6–15 mm. Involucres hemispherical, 3 × 7 mm, densely lanate; phyllaries in 3 series, herbaceous; outer ones ovate‑deltoid, 1.5–2 mm, obtuse or acute; middle layers elliptic, 2–2.2 mm, scarious margined; inner layers oblong, 2.5–3 mm, with wider scarious margin. Receptacle hemispherical‑conical, areoles irregularly toothed, without palea. Peripherical florets female and fertile, in one row, corolla tubular, 1.5 mm, 2–3‑dentate at apex, glandular‑punctate. Central florets bisexual and fertile, many, corolla tubular, 1.5 mm, 5‑dentate apically, glandular punctate. Cypselae oblong, 0.8–1.5 mm, 5‑costate, glandular. Pappus of scarious crown about 0.2–0.5 mm, toothed along rims.

Locality: Cape Collinson, Basalt Island. Also cultivated as pot plants. Y. S. Lau 1773; F. W. Xing 9234.
Distribution: Distributed in coastal regions of SE China; Indochina, Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Crevices of rocks near seashore. Flowering: Jul.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Crotalaria albida Heyne ex Roth 響鈴豆
Nov. Pl. Sp. 333. 1821; FHK 74. 1861; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 369. 1998; FGD 5: 371. 2003.

Perennial herb, 20–70 cm tall, often woody at base. Branches slender, numerous, decumbent or ascending, adpressed pubescent. Leaves simple, oblanceolate, 15 – 40 × 0.3 – 1.7 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or rounded, mucronate, subglabrous adaxially, slightly pubescent abaxially. Racemes terminal or axillary, up to 20 cm, 6 – 20-flowered. Calyx 2-lipped, 6 – 8 mm, finely appressed pubescent. Corolla yellowish; vexillum obovate-elliptic, 6 – 8 mm, base callose, apex fasciculate, pilose; wings obovate, 6 – 8 mm; keel curved almost at an right angle, narrowed above middle and forming a long beak. Ovary sessile. Pods terete, 7– 10 mm, glabrous. Seeds 6– 12.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kwai Chung, Tsuen Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. P. S. Choi 59; Y. W. Lam 1113; K. Y. Tam 135.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian; S to SE Asia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Hillslopes and thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: May – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Crotalaria calycina Schrank 長萼豬屎豆
Pl. Rar. Hort. Monac., pl. 12. 1819; FHK 74. 1861; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 364. 1998; FGD 5: 368. 2003.

Perennial erect herb, 30–80 cm tall. Stems terete, densely brown hirsute. Leaves simple, sessile, oblong-linear or linear-lanceolate, 3–12 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, hairy along midvein adaxially, densely brown pilose abaxially. Racemes terminal, rarely axillary, 3–12-flowered. Calyx 2-lipped, 2–3 cm, deeply divided nearly to base, teeth lanceolate, densely brown pilose abaxially. Corolla golden yellow, shorter than calyx; vexillum obovoid or orbicular, 1.5 – 2.5 cm, base 2-callose; wings oblong; keel nearly straight, long beaked. Ovary sessile. Pods elliptic-terete, ca. 1.5 cm, black when mature. Seeds 20–30.

Locality: Shek O, Po Toi Islands, Cheung Chau. Y. S. Lau 1199; Y. W. Lam 1644; HK sheet 6600.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. – Dec.

Crotalaria chinensis L. 中國豬屎豆
Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 2: 1158. 1759; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 369. 1998; FGD 5: 367. 2003.

Herb, 15–60 cm tall. Stems terete, often woody at base, many-branched, densely brown-yellow pilose. Leaves simple, variable in shape, usually lanceolate, linear-lanceolate, linear or oblong-linear, sometimes oblong or ovoid, 2 – 3.5 × 0.4 – 1 cm, acuminate at both ends, subglabrous or very sparsely pubescent adaxially, densely hirsute abaxially, especially on veins and margins. Racemes terminal, 1–5-flowered. Calyx 2-lipped, 8–10 mm, deeply divided nearly to base. Corolla yellowish, as long as calyx; vexillum ovate or orbicular, 7– 9 mm in diam., with callosities at base; wings oblong, 7– 9 mm; keel nearly straight, narrowed into a beak above middle. Ovary sessile. Pods short terete, 8– 12 mm, glabrous. Seeds 15 – 20, horseshoe-shaped, ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Fanling, Lantau Island, Ninepin group. W. J. Tutcher 10543; S. P. Lau 138; HK sheet 6604.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; S Asia, Indochina.
Ecology: Abandoned lands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.– Dec.

Crotalaria ferruginea Graham ex Benth. 假地藍
Lond. J. Bot. 2: 476. 1843; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 362. 1998; FGD 5: 366. 2003.

Herb, 60–120 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, often woody at base, many-branched, brown pubescent with spreading hairs. Leaves simple, oblong, 2–6 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acuminate, pubescent on both surfaces, but hairs denser on veins abaxially. Racemes terminal or axillary, 2– 6-flowered. Calyx 2-lipped, 10–12 mm, deeply divided nearly to base, teeth lanceolate. Corolla yellow; vexillum oblong, 8 – 10 mm; wings oblong, 8 mm; keel equal to wings, narrowed into a long beak above middle. Ovary sessile. Pods oblong, 2 – 3 × 1 cm, glabrous, black when mature. Seeds 20–30.

Locality: Beacon Hill. W. J. Tutcher 10583.
Distribution: SW to SE China; S to SE Asia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), green manure, forage.

Crotalaria linifolia L. f. 線葉豬屎豆
Suppl. Pl. 332. 1781; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 375. 1998; FGD 5: 371. 2003.

Annual or biennial erect herb, 30 – 60 cm tall, often woody at base. Stems terete, densely pubescent. Leaves simple, oblanceolate or oblong, 2–5 × 0.6–1 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse or emarginate, apiculate, silky hairy on both surfaces. Racemes terminal or axillary, many-flowered, 10–20 cm. Calyx 2-lipped, 8–9 mm, upper 2 connate, lower ones lanceolate, densely rusty-pubescent. Corolla yellow; vexillum orbicular, base callose, apex rounded or emarginate, 6 – 8 mm in diam.; wings obovate, 8 – 9 mm; keel 9 – 10 mm, suberect, narrowed into a beak above middle. Ovary sessile. Pods short terete, 4–6 mm, glabrous. Seeds 6 – 10.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 6622.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Lowland hills, roadsides. Flowering: May – Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Crotalaria pallida Aiton var. obovata (G. Don) Polhill 豬屎豆
Kew Bull. 22: 262. 1968; J. B. Gillett et al, Fl. Trop. E Afr. No. 61 (Legum. Part 4 ): 906. 1971; FTW 3: 112. 1977.
Crotalaria pallida Aiton, Hort. Kew 3: 20. 1789; FRPS 42(2): 349. 1998; FGD 5: 365, fig. 202. 2003.

Perennial herb or subshrub. Stems and branches terete, marked with slender longitudinal grooves, closely adpressed puberulent. Leaves digitately 3-foliolate; leaflets oblong or elliptic, 3 – 6 × 1.5– 3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate and shortly mucronate, glabrous adaxially, slightly silky pubescent abaxially. Racemes terminal, ca. 25 cm, 10 – 40-flowered. Calyx subcampanulate, 4 – 6 mm, 5-toothed, densely pubescent. Corolla yellow; vexillum orbicular or elliptic, 10 mm in diam., with 2 callosities at base; wings oblong, 8 mm; keel 13 mm, incurved nearly at a right angle, long-beaked. Ovary sessile. Pods oblong, 3 – 4 × 0.5 – 0.8 cm, valves contorted after split. Seeds 20 – 30, reniform, ca. 3 mm.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1997, 2041; HK sheet 40830.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Sep. – Dec.
Uses: Green manure.
Notes: The species was reported as Crotalaria pallida Aiton previously (Check List HK Plants 141. 2002; 53. 2004).
records.uses:
Green manure.
Notes: The species was reported as Crotalaria pallida Aiton previously (Check List HK Plants 141. 2002; 53. 2004).

records.text:
Crotalaria retusa L. 吊裙草
Sp. Pl. 715. 1873; FHK 74. 1861; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 358. 1998; FGD 5: 370. 2003.

Erect herb, 60–120 cm tall. Branches terete, striate, pubescent. Leaves simple, oblong or oblanceolate, 3 – 8 × 1 – 3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex emarginate, glabrous adaxially, slightly pubescent abaxially, veins distinct. Racemes terminal, ca. 5 cm, 10 – 20-flowered. Calyx 2-lipped, 10 – 12 mm, teeth lanceolate, sparsely pubescent. Corolla yellow; vexillum orbicular or elliptic, 1–1.5 cm, with 2 callosities at base; wings oblong 1 –1.5 cm; keel equal in length with wings, gradually narrowed into a long beak above middle. Pods oblong, 3– 4 cm, glabrous, turgid; neck ca. 2 mm. Seeds 10 – 20, brown, elliptic, 2 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Beacon Hill, Chuen Lung, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Tuen Mun, Long Ke, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. P. S. Choi 40, 509; K. Y. Tam 136.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan (cultivated); Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Vietnam, India, tropical and subtropical regions of America, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands and grasslands, sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore)

Crotalaria sessiliflora L. 野百合
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1004. 1763; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 366. 1998; FGD 5: 369. 2003.
Crotalaria brevipes Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 44. 1852; FHK 74. 1861.

Erect herb, 30–100 cm tall, often woody at base. Stems simple or branched on upper parts, adpressed strigose. Leaves simple, variable in shape, usually linear or linear-lanceolate, 3 – 8 × 0.5–1 cm, acuminate at both ends, subglabrous adaxially, densely silky pubescent abaxially, subsessile. Racemes terminal or axillary, 2–20-flowered, sometimes head-like on apex of branches. Calyx 2-lipped, 10–15 mm, densely brown hirsute. Corolla blue or violet, as long as calyx; vexillum oblong, 7 – 10 × 4 – 7 mm, with 2 callosities at base, apex obtuse or emarginate; wings oblong or lanceolate-oblong, equal to vexillum; keel narrowed into a long beak above middle. Ovary sessile. Pods short terete, 1 × 0.5 cm, pendulous, glabrous, black when mature. Seeds 10–15.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1564; P. S. Choi 61, 237.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E Asia to SE Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides and hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: May– Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Crotalaria uncinella Lam. 毬果豬屎豆（鈎狀豬屎豆）
Encycl. 2(1): 200–201. 1786; FRPS 42(2): 379. 1998; FGD 5: 363. 2003.
