Crotalaria elliptica Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 279. 1832; FHK 75. 1861; FKH 74. 1912.

Herb or subshrub, up to 1 m tall. Branches terete, pubescent at first. Leaves digitately 3-foliolate; leaflets elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 2.5–3 × 1–1.5 cm, terminal one larger, base slightly cuneate, apex obtuse, mucronate or sometimes emarginate, glabrous adaxially, slightly pubescent abaxially. Racemes terminal, axillary or leaf-opposed, 10 – 30-flowered. Calyx subcampanulate, 3–4 mm, 5-toothed. Corolla yellow; vexillum orbicular or elliptic, 5 mm; wings oblong; keel longer than vexillum, incurved, with contorted long beak. Ovary sessile. Pods ovoid-globular, 5 mm, pubescent. Seeds 2.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Sai Kung, Po Toi Islands. L. T. Lo 509; Y. W. Lam 492, 1049.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Africa, tropical and subtropical Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Dec.

Crotalaria zanzibarica Benth. 光萼豬屎豆
Lond. J. Bot. 2: 584. 1843; FRPS 42(2): 350. 1998; FGD 5: 364. 2003.

Herb or subshrub, 1.5–2 m tall. Branches terete, pubescent, with longitudinal grooves. Leaves digitately 3-foliolate; leaflets oblong, 6 – 10 × 2 – 3 cm, acuminate on both ends, mucronate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially. Racemes terminal, up to 20 cm, 10 – 20-flowered. Calyx subcampanulate, 4 – 5 mm, 5-toothed, glabrous. Corolla yellow; vexillum orbicular, 12 mm in diam., apex aristulate, with 2 callosities at base; wings oblong, equaling vexillum in length; keel 15 mm, narrowed above middle. Ovary sessile. Pods oblong, 3–4 cm, pericarps black, with persistent filaments and calyx at base. Seeds 20–30, reniform, scarlet.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3307.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Open wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. – Dec.
Uses: Green manure.

Croton crassifolius Geiseler 雞骨香（金棉楓）
Croton Monogr. 19. 1807; FRPS 44(2): 130. 1996; FGD 5: 101. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 202. 2005.
Croton chinense Benth., FHK 309. 1861; FKH 238. 1912.

Shrub 20–50 cm tall; branches of the current year, leaves and inflorescences rather densely stellate-tomentose. Leaves papery, biglandular at the base or at the apex of petiole; stipules subulate, 2–3 mm, caducous; petioles 2–4 cm long; leaf blade ovate, ovate-elliptic to oblong, 4–10 × 2–6 cm, base rotund to slightly cordate, apex obtuse to short-acuminate, margin obscurely serrate or nearly entire, with small stipitate glands at the serratures, adaxially usually wrinkled and becoming glabrous; basal veins 3–5. Racemes terminal, 5–10 cm; bracts 2–4 mm, divided into subulate lobes, often tipped with a gland. Male flowers: calyx-lobes stellate-tomentose abaxially; petals oblong, about as long as calyx-lobes; disk glands very minute or none; stamens 14–20, intermixed with hairs. Female flowers: usually several at the base of the raceme; calyx as in male flowers; petals none; ovary densely yellow-tomentose; styles 4-parted, lobes linear. Capsule, subglobose, ca. 1 cm in diam., densely tawny tomentose.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Black's Link, Pok Fu Lam, Fanling,Yuen Long, LoWu, Tai LongWan. Y. S. Lau 285, 523; H. C. Tang 2475; S. Y. Hu 13123 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. Flowering: Nov.–Jun. of the following year; fruiting: Feb.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens of C. chinense Benth. were collected from Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens of C. chinense Benth. were collected from Hong Kong.

records.text:
Croton hancei Benth. 香港巴豆
FHK 308. 1861; FKH 238. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 136. 1996; FGD 5: 105. 2003.

Shrub or treelet, 1–5 m tall, glabrous, except a minute stellate-lepidote on the young branches and inflorescences. Leaves papery, usually biglandular at the base; petioles 2–5 mm, puberulous; stipules subulate, 3–4 mm;leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 8–18 × 2–5 cm, narrowed below the middle, but obtuse at the base, apex acuminate, margin entire or minutely serrate. Racemes terminal, ca. 3 cm; bracts small, ovate. Male flowers: several clustered in axil of bracts; pedicels very short; alabastrum globose, ca. 2 mm in diam.; calyx-lobes ovate; petals narrow and small; stamens 16, intermixed with a few hairs. Female flowers: usually solitary at the base; calyx-lobes 5, oblong, 4–5 mm; ovary globular, hairy; styles shortly columnar, with 3 short bifid lobes.

Locality: TsingYi Island. K. Y. Tam 128; Y. W. Lam 144.
Distribution: Hong Kong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (H. F. Hance Herb. No. 10163, BM) was collected by H. F. Hance around 1850 in Hong Kong Island. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Croton lachnocarpus Benth. 毛果巴豆

Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 5. 1854; FHK 308. 1861, ‘lachnocarpum’; FKH 238. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 131, pl. 31: 1 – 5. 1996; FGD 5: 101. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 213. 2005.


Shrub, 1–3 m tall; branches of the current year, leaves and inflorescences more or less pubescent with stellate hairs. Leaves papery, biglandular at the base or at apex of petioles; petioles 1–6 cm, densely stellate-pubescent; stipules linear, 3–5 mm hairy; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to elliptic-ovate, rarely oblong-lanceolate, 4–13 × 1.5–5 cm, base rotund to slightly cordate, apex obtuse, acute to acuminate, margin obscurely serrulate, with small stipitate glands at the serratures; basal veins 3. Racemes terminal, 6–15 cm; bracts subulate, ca. 1 mm. Male flowers: pedicels 2–3 mm; calyx-lobes ovate-triangular, ca. 2 mm, stellate-pubescent; petals oblong, ca. 2 mm; stamens 10–12. Female flowers: calyx-lobes lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, stellate-pubescent; petals minute, subulate; ovary villose; styles 3, subulate, bifid. Capsules subglobose, 6–12 mm in diam., hairy; seeds ellipsoidal, dark-brown, smooth.


Locality: Cape Collinson Rd., Tai Tam Tuk Reservoir, Tai Tam, Kam Shan Country Park, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Tolo Harbour. Y. S. Lau 335, 1407; L. T. Lo 338; S. Y. Hu 13807 (CUHK).

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi.

Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Croton moonii Thwaites 月光巴豆
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 276. 1864.

Treelet to 5 m tall; branches, petioles, inflorescences and abaxial surface of leaves stellate-lepidote. Leaves biglandular at the base; petioles 1.5–2 cm; leaf blade oblong, ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, 7–15 × 3–5 cm, base rounded or unequally cordate, apex acute to acuminate, margin obscurely serrulate; adaxially glabrous, olive-green, becoming greyish or glaucous when dry; lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, tomentose and stellate-lepidote; calyx-lobes as many as and equaling the petals, ovate, obtuse, stellate-tomentose; disk of male obscure, of female small, annular; stamens 10–16; filaments pilose; ovary stellate-hispid; styles 3, biparted. Capsules depressed-globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., scurfy and tuberculate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 898, 2532; L. T. Lo 632.
Distribution: Native to Sri Lanka; cultivated in S Guangdong.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Croton tiglium L. 巴豆
Sp. Pl. 1004. 1753; FKH 238. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 133. 1996; FGD 5: 102. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 222. 2005.

Treelet, 3–7 m tall; young branches sparsely stellate-hairy, glabrous in age. Leaves papery, biglandular at the base; stipules subulate, 1.5–4 mm, caducous; petioles 2.5–6 cm, subglabrous; leaf blade ovate, ovate-elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 5–15 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate to rotund, rarely slightly cordate, apex acute or acuminate, sometimes long-acuminate, margin serrulate or subentire, glabrous or glabrescent, yellowish to brownish when dry; basal veins 3–5. Racemes terminal, 8–20 cm; bracts subulate, ca. 2 mm. Male flowers: 1– several in axil of bract; pedicels slender, 5 – 9 mm; alabastrum subglobose, sparsely stellate-hairy or glabrescent; calyx-lobes ovate-triangular, 2–3 mm; petals oblong, slightly longer than calyx-lobes; stamens 16–17. Female flowers: 5–20, borne on the proximal part of the raceme; pedicels 3–4 mm; calyx-lobes oblong-lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, glabrescent; ovary densely stellate-hairy; styles biparted, lobes linear. Capsules ellipsoidal, oblong-ovoid or subglobose, 1–2 × 1–2 cm, sparsely stellate-hairy or glabrescent; seeds elliptic or oblong-ovate, 8–12 × 6–7 mm, grey-brown.

Locality: Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Kam Shan, Sha Tau Kok, Shing Mun, Tin Fu Tsai, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 613; N. H. Li 104; K. Y. Tam 142; S. Y. Hu 10468 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Thin forests, stream banks. Flowering: Jan.– Jul.; fruiting: May– Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), pesticide, poison (fish, mammals).

Cryptanthus bromelioides Otto & A. Dietr. 銀背姬鳳梨
Allg. Gartenzeitung 4: 297. 1836; L. H. Bailey, Hortus Third 339. 1976.

Leaves all alike, not petioled, green adaxially, silvery abaxially, to 17 × 3.5 cm, spiny-margined. Inflorescences on a scape of 15 cm. Flowers many, in clusters of 4–6 in axils of keeled bracts, milky-white, ca. 4 cm, tube of calyx longer than lobes.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cryptanthus bromelioides Otto & A. Dietr. var. tricolor M. B. Foster 三色鳳梨
Bull. Bromeliad Soc. 3: 30. 1953; L. H. Bailey, Hortus Third 339. 1976.

It differs from var. bromelioides by leaves striped with ivory-white and green, overlaid with carmine-rose.

Locality: Cultivated. Distribution: Native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cryptanthus bromelioides Otto & A. Dietr. cv. Tricolor previously (Check List HK Plants 350. 2002; 122. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cryptanthus bromelioides Otto & A. Dietr. cv. Tricolor previously (Check List HK Plants 350. 2002; 122. 2004).

records.text:
Cryptocarya chinensis (Hance) Hemsl. 厚殼桂
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 370. 1891; FKH 222. 1912; FHN 1: 282. 1964; FRPS 31: 443, pl. 116: 9–10. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 449, pl. 207. 1996.
Beilschmiedia chinensis Hance, J. Bot. 20: 79. 1882.

Tree, up to 20 m tall. Branchlets terete, finely and longitudinally striated, initially tawny tomentose, glabrescent. Leaves leathery, alternate or opposite; petioles 1 cm long. Leaf blade long elliptic, 7–11 × 3.5 –5.5 cm, base broad cuneate, apex acuminate, adaxially green and shining, abaxially glaucous, initially tawny tomentose on both surfaces, glabrescent, triplinerved; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein. Panicles axillary or terminal, 1.5 – 4 cm, tawny tomentellate. Flowers yellowish, ca. 3 mm long. Pedicels less than 0.5 mm. Perianth-tubes turbinate, 1–1.5 mm; lobes yellowish subobovate, ca. 2 mm, apex acute. Stamens 9; filaments pubescent. Staminodes sagittate, pubescent. Ovary clavate, ca. 2 mm. Fruit globose or compressed globose, 7.5–9 × 9–12 mm, longitudinally furrowed, purplish-black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 158; Y. W. Lam 1424.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Ford s.n. in Herb. Hance No. 21705, BM) was collected in the valley of “Su-kun-pu” (now So Kong Po), Hong Kong Island in May 1881.

Cryptocarya concinna Hance 黃果厚殼桂（黃果桂）
J. Bot. 20: 79. 1882; FKH 222. 1912; FHN 1: 282. 1964; FRPS 31: 455, pl. 122: 1– 6. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 449, photo 183. 1996.
Cryptocarya konishii Hayata ex Kawakami, List Pl. Form. 1910.

Tree, up to 18 m tall; bark brownish. Young branches slender, angular, yellowish brown tomentellate. Leaves alternate, subleathery; petioles 0.4 –1 cm, yellowish-brown puberulous; leaf blade oblong elliptic or oblong, 5 –10 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate, often unequal, apex obtuse, subacute to shortly acuminate, adaxially shining, glabrous, abaxially ± glaucous, slightly puberulous when young, glabrescent, pinninerved; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 4 –7 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary or terminal, (2–)4– 8 cm, puberulous. Pedicels 1–2 mm, puberulous. Perianth-tubes campanulate, ca. 1 mm; lobes oblong, ca. 2.5 mm, apex obtuse, puberulous on both surfaces. Stamens 9; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm; filaments pubescent at the base. Ovary enclosed in perianth tubes after anthesis. Fruit long ellipsoid, 1.5 –2 × 8 mm, with 12 longitudinal grooves, black to bluish-black when mature.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar Peak (Hok Tsui Shan), Stubbs Road. Y. S. Lau 2341; HK sheet 24825.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Taiwan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on slopes. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Cryptocarya densiflora Bl. 叢花厚殼桂
Bijdr. 556. 1826; FHN 1: 281. 1964; FRPS 31: 441, pl. 116: 1– 8. 1982.
Cryptocarya laevigata Elmer, Leafl. Philipp. Bot. 8: 2720. 1915.

Tree, 7–20 m tall. Branchlets angular, rusty tomentose. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2 cm, rusty tomentose or glabrescent; leaf blade long elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 10–15 × 5–8.5 cm, base cuneate, broadly cuneate to rounded, apex shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially glaucous, initially rusty pubescent, glabrescent, triplinerved; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 2–3 on each side of midvein. Panicles axillary or terminal, 2.5–8 cm, densely flowered. Pedicels less than 1 mm, densely tawny puberulous. Perianth white, ca. 4 mm, divided to middle, puberulous; tubes turbinate; lobes ovate, apex acute. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Staminodes sagittate, stalked. Ovary clavate, ca. 2 mm. Fruit subglobose, 1.2–1.8 × 1.5–2.5 cm, smooth, obscurely grooved, black when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan. S. C. Ng 2864; Y. W. Lam 236.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests in valley. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Cryptolepis sinensis (Lour.) Merr. 白葉藤
Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 254. 1919; FRPS 63: 263, pl. 90. 1977; FGD 1: 538, fig. 618. 1987; FOC 16: 193. 1995.
Pergularia sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 167. 1790.
Cryptolepis elegans Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 162. 1837; FKH 170. 1912.

Lianas to 3 m; glabrous throughout. Branchlets red‑brown, exfoliating. Petioles 5–7 mm; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate, 1.5–6 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex rounded, apiculate; lateral veins 5–9 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal or axillary, lax, longer than leaves. Pedicels 1–3.5 cm. Sepals ovate, ca. 1 mm; basal glands 10. Corolla yellowish; tube ca. 5 mm; lobes oblong‑lanceolate or linear, 1–1.5 cm. Corona lobes club‑shaped. Anthers glabrous. Follicles cylindric, to 12.5 cm × 6.8 mm. Seeds brown, oblong, ca. 1 cm × 2 mm; coma ca. 2.5 cm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 267; HK sheet 1844.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Sep.; fruiting: Jun. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cryptostylis arachnites (Blume) Hassk. 隱柱蘭
Cat. Bog. 8. 1844; FKH 268. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 39, fig. 13. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 102. 2002; FRPS 17: 237. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 819. 2000; FGD 7: 346, fig. 147. 2006.
Zosterostylis arachnites Blume, Bijdr. 419. 1825.
Cryptostylis arachnites (Blume) Blume, Coll. Orchid. 133. 1859; FOC 25: 89. 2009.

Terrestrial herb, 25–30 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves petiolate; petioles 4–12 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 8–11 × 3.5–5.5 cm, apex acuminate and apiculate, with many lateral veins running to the apex, purple-green beneath. Flowers very unusual; sepals 3, widely separate, linear, acuminate, light green, 1.2–1.3 × 0.2 cm at base, margin in-rolled, the lateral ones 2.5 cm between apices, the odd one shorter; petals shorter than sepals, lanceolate, aculeate, pale green, 7–8 mm, margin in-rolled; lip ovate, erect, reflexed, base concave and slightly saccate, apex acute, 1.2–1.3 × 0.6–0.8 cm, completely covered with velvet red-brown hairs, lemon-yellow, with 5 brown veins running palmately from base to margin and apex, with some red-brown patches; column 0.5 mm, with a glandular auricle on each side; anther erect, 2 mm, cap yellow and papillose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, viscidium violet; stigma large, discoid, covering the entire front of the column; ovary glabrous, 8 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Violet Hill, Sai Kung. HK sheet 7134.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; SE & S Asia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

Cucumis melo L. 甜瓜
Sp. Pl. 1011. 1753; FRPS 73(1): 202. 1986; FFJ 5: 255, fig. 239. 1993; FGD 3: 126. 1995.
Cucumis bisexualis A. M. Lu & G. C. Wang ex Lu & Z. Y. Zhang, Bull. Bot. Res. North-east Inst. 4(2): 126. 1984.

Annual creeping or climbing herb. Stems angled, hispidulous. Petioles 7–12 cm, setose; leaf blade suborbicular or reniform in outline, pentagonal or 3–7-lobed, 7–15 × 7–15 cm, base cordate, margin dentate, pubescent on both surfaces, hispid along veins abaxially. Male flowers: solitary or clustered; pedicels filiform, 0.5 –4 cm; calyx-tube villous, 6 –8 mm, lobes subulate, shorter than tubes; corolla yellow, 2 cm long; tube 1–2 mm, lobes ovate-oblong; stamens 3; anther cells flexuous, 3– 4 mm; pistillodes 1 mm. Female flowers: solitary; pedicel 1–2 cm; ovary ellipsoid or fusiform, densely white-lanate, villous or puberulous; style 1–2 mm; stigmas 3, connivent, 2–2.5 mm. Fruit polymorphic, usually globose or ellipsoid, often grooved or patched, not spiny, pubescent or glabrous. Seeds many, yellow-white, oblong, 10 –12 × 5 –7 mm, margin not thickened.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: F1owering and fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Cucumis melo L. var. conomon (Thunb.) Makino 白瓜（越瓜）
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 16. 1902; FGZ 190. 1956; FHN 1: 476. 1964; FFJ 5: 256. 1993; FGD 3: 126. 1995.

It differs from var. melo by its fruit being terete, obtuse or slightly truncate at both ends, up to 60 cm long, 5 – 6 cm in diam., smooth, striped, pulp white or pale green.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 12131 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer.
Uses: Food (fruit)

Cucumis sativus L. 黃瓜（青瓜）
Sp. Pl. 1012. 1753; FRPS 73(1): 205. 1986; FFJ 5: 256, fig. 240. 1993; FGD 3: 127, fig. 89. 1995

Annual climbing or creeping herb, monoecious. Stem angled, hispid. Tendrils slender, not branched. Petioles 2.5–23 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate-cordate, membranous, 7–20 x 7–20 cm, margin 3 –5-angular or -lobed, lobes triangular-ovate, usually pentagonal, base deeply cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin dentate, hispidulous on both surfaces. Flowers yellow. Male flowers: often clustered; pedicel filiform, 5 –15 mm, puberulous; calyx-tube tubular, lobes linear-lanceolate or subulate, 1.2 cm; corolla lobes oblong-lanceolate, 2.5 × 1.6 cm; stamens 3, filaments subglabrous, anthers 3 – 4 mm, connective 1 mm. Female flowers: solitary or clustered, pedicels 1–3 cm, pubescent; ovary fusiform, muricate. Fruit cylindrical, 10 –30 cm, 3.5 –5 cm in diam., green or yellow-green, muricate, usually verrucose. Seeds small, oblong, white, 5–10 mm, without thickened margin.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 12078, 34060.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Cucurbita moschata Duchesne 南瓜
Essai Hist. Nat. Courges 7, 15-16. 1786; FHN 1: 483. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 262. 1986; FFJ 5: 257, fig. 241. 1993; FGD 3: 139, fig. 100. 1995.
Cucurbita pepo L. var. moschata Duch. ex Lam., Encycl. 2: 152. 1786.

Annual prostrate or climbing herb. Stems terete or slightly 5-ridged, densely white-setose. Tendrils 3– 4-branched, hispid and tomentose. Petioles stout, to 25 cm, setose; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate-orbicular in outline, pentagonal or 5-lobed, 15– 40 × 20 – 40 cm, margin serrulate, setose and white patched on both surfaces. Male flowers: pedicels to 33 cm, setose; calyx setose, tube short, 5 – 6 mm, lobes linear, 1–1.5 cm, pubescent, enlarged or leaf-like at apex; corolla tubular, 8 cm long, 6 cm in diam., hairy, lobes spreading, rugose, 5 × 6 cm, with 3 longitudinal veins; stamens 3, filaments glandular, 5– 8 mm, enlarged at base, anthers connivent. Female flowers: ovary 1-locular, style short, stigma enlarged, 2-lobed. Fruiting pedicel stout, angled and sulcate, 5–7 cm, enlarged at apex. Fruits varied in shape, size and color, usually sub-pyriform, compressed globose, ovoid. Pericarp sulcate and verrucose. Seeds many, ovate or oblong, grey-white, margin thickened, 1–1.5 × 0.7–1 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2757; L. T. Lo 175; HK sheet 2013.
Distribution: Widely cultivated worldwide; native to Mexico and C America.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Cunninghamia lanceolata (Lamb.) Hook. 杉木
Bot. Mag. 54: t. 2743. 1827; FRPS 7: 285, pl. 66: 1–13. 1978; FOC 4: 55. 1999; FGD 4: 19, fig. 10. 2000.
Cunninghamia sinensis auct. non R. Br. ex Rich: FHK 337.1861; FKH 256. 1912.

Tree up to 50 m tall; trunk to 3 m d.b.h.; bark dark grey to dark brown, or reddish brown, longitudinally fissured, inner bark pale red. Leaves narrowly linear-lanceolate, straight or slightly falcate, 2– 6 cm × 3 –5 mm, base decurrent, apex usually symmetric and spinescent, margin denticulate, adaxial surface glossy deep green,with 2 narrow stomatal bands, bands white powdery or not, abaxial surface pale green, with 1 stomatal band along midvein each side, band white powdery. Pollen cone conical, 0.5–1.5 cm long, with a short peduncle, usually 40 clustered at apex. Seed cones terminal, 1–4 together, ovoid or subglobose; bracts glaucous or rather glossy, broadly ovate or triangular-ovate, base with short claw 1. Seeds dark brown, oblong or narrowly ovate, 5–6 × ca. 4 mm, narrowly winged laterally.

Locality: Widely planted in countryside. Y. S. Hsu s.n.; C. C. Luo 1281.
Distribution: Exact native distribution uncertain owing to widespread planting. Widely cultivated in areas S of Qinling Range; Cambodia, Laos, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Pollinating: Jan.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Afforestation, timber.

Cuphea hyssopifolia Kunth 細葉萼距花
Nov. Gen. Sp. (4th ed.) 6: 199. 1823 [1824].

Little shrub, 30–60 cm tall, much branched. Branches sparsely hirsute, internodes very short, 4–6 mm. Leaves opposite; petioles 1 – 1.5 mm; leaf blade elliptic to narrowly ellitptic, 0.8 – 2.5 × 0.4 – 1 cm, base obtuse, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous adaxially, sparsely hirsute on veins abaxially, lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flowers solitary axillary, 7–8 mm in diam. Pedicels slender, 2 – 3 mm, sparsely hirsute. Calyx 4 – 5 mm, sparsely hairy on the ribs, slightly gibbous at base limb, 6-toothed. Petals 6, obovate-elliptic, 2 – 2.5 × 1.2 – 2 mm, nearly equal, purplish red to pink, apex acute, base ± clawed. Stamens included. Capsules ellipsoidal.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 134; Y. S. Lau 2511.
Distribution: Native to Mexico.
Ecology: Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Curculigo capitulata (Lour.) Kuntze 大葉仙茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 703. 1891; FKH 275. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 34. 1985; FOC 24: 271. 2000; FGD 4: 412, fig. 250. 2000.
Curculigo recurvata W. T. Aiton, FKH 275. 1912.
Leucojum capitulatum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 199. 1790.

Perennial stout herb, 0.8–1 m tall. Rhizomes tuberous, thick, with creeping, slender stolons. Leaves radical; petioles 30–50(–80) cm, base dilated and clasping the root stock, densely brown pubescent; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate to suboblong, 30–90 × 4–16 cm, apex acuminate, margin entire, veins conspicuous, plicate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent especially on veins. Scape 6–15(–20) cm, ± compressed, brown villous. Racemes densely flowered, condensed to a head, 2.5–5.5 cm in diam.; bracts lanceolate, 2–6 cm, brown villous on veins and margin; pedicels 8–10 mm, brown villous. Perianth ca. 2 cm, brown villous abaxially; tube ca. 1 cm; segments yellow, elliptic-lanceolate, 8–10 × 3.5–5 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 6; filament slender, 2–3 mm; anther linear, 4–5 mm. Ovary subglobose to oblong, hairy; style longer than stamens, slender; stigma subcapitate. Berry white, subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam., beakless.

Locality: Mount Parker, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1696; L. T. Lo 477.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Bhutan, Sikkim, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Forests, moist places in ravines. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Curculigo orchioides Gaertn. 仙茅
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 63. 1788; FKH 275. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 37. 1985; FOC 24: 272. 2000; FGD 4: 413. 2000.
Curculigo orchioides Gaertn. var. minor Benth., FHK 366. 1861.

Perennial herb, 10–20(–40) cm tall. Rhizomes vertical, subterete, ca. 10 × 1 cm, similar to taproot. Leaves radical, grass-like, sessile or shortly petiolate; leaf blade lanceolate to linear, usually 10–20(–40) × 0.5–2.5 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex narrowly acuminate, laxly pilose or glabrous; veins inconspicuous. Scape short, 6–7 cm, nearly enclosed in base of sheathing petiole, pilose; bracts lanceolate, 2.5–5 cm, margin ciliate. Racemes umbel-like, 4–6-flowered; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Perianth yellow; tube filiform, ca. 18 mm; segments oblong-lanceolate, 8–12 × 2.5–3 mm, outer ones sometimes abaxially laxly pilose. Stamens 6, about half the length of perianth segments; filament 1.5–2.5 mm; anther 2–4 mm. Ovary narrowly oblong, to 7.5 mm, pilose. Stigma lobes longer than style. Berry ± fusiform, ca. 1.5 cm, beaked at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 28455, 32791.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Pakistan, India, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes, thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Curcuma aromatica Salisb. 郁金（鬱金）
Parad. Lond. 1: pl. 96. 1807; FHN 4: 95. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 60. 1981; FGD 2: 407. 1991; FOC 24: 362. 2000.

Plants ca. 1 m tall. Rhizomes yellow inside, elliptic or narrowly so, fleshy, aromatic; roots with fusiform tubers. Petiole equaling leaf blade; leaf blade oblong, 30–60 × 10–20 cm, base attenuate, apex narrowly caudate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent. Inflorescences on separate shoots arising from rhizomes, usually appearing before leaves; spike cylindrical, ca. 15 × 8 cm; fertile bracts pale green, ovate, 4–5 cm; coma bracts white, tinged with red.

Locality: Shing Mun, Mau Ping, Tai Po. Aubrey 11548; L. T. Lo 474; HK sheet 27957.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin Forests.

Curcuma longa L. 薑黃
Sp. Pl. 1: 2. 1753; FRPS 16(2): 62. 1981; FGD 2: 408. 1991; FOC 24: 361. 2000.
Curcuma domestica Valeton, Bull. Jard. Bot. Buitenz. 2 ser. 27: 31. 1918; FHN 4: 94. 1977.

Plants ca. 1 m tall. Rhizomes many-branched, orange inside, cylindrical, aromatic; roots tuberous at tip. Petiole 20–45 cm, leaf blade green, oblong or elliptic, 30–45(–90) × 15–18 cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, glabrous. Inflorescences terminal on pseudostems. Peduncle 12–20 cm; spike cylindrical, 12–18 × 4–9 cm; fertile bracts pale green, ovate or oblong, 3–5 cm, apex obtuse; coma bracts spreading, white and green, sometimes tinged reddish purple, apex acute. Calyx white, 0.8–1.2 cm, puberulent, apex unequally 3-toothed. Corolla pale yellow; tube to 3 cm; lobes deltoid, 1–1.5 cm, central one larger, apex mucronate. Lateral staminodes shorter than labellum. Labellum yellowish with central, yellow band, obovate, 1.2–2 cm. Anther spurred at base. Ovary sparsely hairy.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 27960.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore), spice.

Cuscuta australis R. Br. 南方菟絲子
Prodr. 491. 1810; FTW 4: 351, pl. 1034. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 144, pl. 32: 1 – 3. 1979; FFJ 4: 474, fig. 379. 1989; FOC 16: 322. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 344, pl. 154, photo 202. 1998; FGD 4: 330. 2000.
Cuscuta hygrophilae H. Pearson, Icon. Pl. 28, pl. 2704. 1901.
Cuscuta kawakamii Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 125. 1915.
Cuscuta millettii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 201. 1837.
Cuscuta obtusiflora Kunth var. australis (R. Br.) Engelm., Trans. Acad. Sci. St. Louis 1: 492. 1859.
Cuscuta chinensis auct. non Lam.: FGZ 581. 1956.

Annual herb. Stems golden, thin, ca. 1 mm in diam. Inflorescences lateral, compact cymose glomerules, several – many‑flowered, subsessile. Bracts scale‑like. Pedicel 1–2.5 mm. Calyx nearly as long as corolla tube; sepals (3–)4–5, often unequal, oblong or orbicular, ca. 1.5 mm. Corolla white or creamy white, cupular, ca. 3 mm; lobes persistent, erect, ovate or oblong, as long as tube. Stamens inserted at sinus, shorter than lobes; scales shorter than tube, deeply 2‑cleft, fimbrillate. Ovary compressed globose. Styles 2, ca. 1 mm; stigmas capitate. Capsule enclosed by persistent corolla at lower half, subglobose, 3–4 mm in diam., irregularly opening, not circumscissile. Seeds 4, brownish, ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm, scabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 774, 1052; HK sheet 19970.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Parasitic on plants of Leguminosae, Compositae or Verbenaceae. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cuscuta campestris Yunck. 田野菟絲子
Mem. Torrey Bot. Club. 18: 138. 1932; FOC 16: 323. 1995.
Cuscuta arvensis Beyr. ex Engelm., Manual ed. 2, 336. 1856.

Annual herb. Stems yellowish green to yellow or orange, 0.5–0.8 mm in diam., smooth. Inflorescences lateral, usually compact globular clusters, 4–18‑flowered, subsessile. Pedicel ca. 1 mm. Calyx enclosing corolla tube, ca. 1.5 mm; sepals 5, oval or orbicular, sometimes wider than long. Corolla white, short campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm, 4‑ or 5‑lobed; lobes broadly triangular, apex acute or obtuse, often reflexed. Stamens shorter to longer than corolla lobes; anthers ovate, shorter than filaments; scales distinct, ovate, ca. as long as corolla tube, fimbrillate. Ovary globose. Styles 2; stigma capitate. Capsule compressed globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., ca. 2 mm high, with persistent corolla at base, irregularly opening. Seeds 1–4, often 3 or 4, dull yellow, ovoid.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 37677, 41647, 41859.
Distribution: Fujian, Xinjiang, Guangdong (cultivated for biocontrol of Mikania micrantha Kunth); Africa, Asia, Australia, Europe, N & S America, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Roadsides, fields, margins of beaches, parasitic on Mikania micrantha, Spinifex littoreus, Urena lobata, etc. Flowering & fruiting: Dec.–Jul. of the following year.

Cuscuta chinensis Lam. 菟絲子
Encycl. 2: 229. 1786; FKH 182. 1912; FRPS 64(1): 145, pl. 31: 4 – 7. 1979; FFJ 4: 473, fig. 378. 1989; FOC 16: 323. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 347. 1998; FGD 4: 330. 2000.

Annual herb. Stems yellow, thin, ca. 1 mm in diam. Inflorescences lateral, compact cymose glomerules, several–many‑flowered, subsessile. Bracts and bracteoles scale‑like. Pedicel ca. 1 mm. Sepals 5, triangular, ca. 1.5 mm, apex obtuse, connate at lower half. Corolla white, urceolate, ca. 3 mm; lobes persistent triangular‑ovate, apex acute or obtuse, reflexed. Stamens inserted at throat; scales oblong, long fimbriate. Ovary subglobose. Styles 2, ca. 1 mm; stigma capitate. Capsule nearly completely enclosed by persistent corolla, subglobose, ca. 3 mm in diam., circumscissile. Seeds 2–4, pale brown, ovoid, ca. 1 mm, scabrous.

Locality: Sha Tin. L. T. Lo 12, 364.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; W, E & S Asia, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Fields, open mountain slopes, thickets, sandy beaches, parasitic often on plants of Leguminosae and Compositae. Flowering & fruiting: Jul. – Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cuscuta japonica Choisy 金燈藤
Syst. Verz. 2: 130. 1854; FHK 241. 1861; FKH 182. 1912; FRPS 64(1): 147, pl. 31: 8 – 11. 1979; FFJ 4: 475. 1989; FGD 4: 331. 2000; FOC 16: 323. 1995.
Cuscuta reflexa Roxb. var. densiflora Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 57. 1853; Check List HK Plants 226. 2002; 79. 2004.

Annual herb. Stems yellow or often with purplish spots, slightly stout, 1–2 mm in diam., multibranched. Inflorescences spicate or paniculate, 1–3 cm. Bracts and bracteoles scale‑like, broadly ovate, ca. 2 mm. Flowers subsessile. Sepals 5, ca. 2 mm, semi‑orbicular, purplish tuberculate abaxially. Corolla pink or greenish white, campanulate to tubular, 3–5 mm, shallowly 5‑lobed; lobes erect or reflexed, ovate‑triangular, much shorter than tube, apex obtuse. Stamens inserted at throat; filaments very short or absent; scales oblong, fimbriate. Ovary globose, smooth. Style 1, longer than or as long as ovary; stigma elongate, 2‑lobed, lobes tongue‑shaped. Capsule ovoid, ca. 5 mm, circumscissile near base. Seeds 1–3, brown, 2–2.5 mm, smooth.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, High West, Shek O, Po Toi Island. P. S. Choi 336; HK sheet 39388, 40810.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, Russia, Vietnam.
Ecology: On herbs or shrubs. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Cuscuta reflexa var. densiflora (J.G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Cuscuta reflexa var. densiflora (J.G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Hong Kong.

records.text:
Cyanotis arachnoidea C. B. Clarke 蛛絲毛藍耳草
Monogr. Phan. 3: 250. 1881; FRSP 13(3): 122, pl. 30: 10. 1997; FOC 24: 22. 2000; FGD 6: 318. 2005.

Perennial herb, with fibrous roots; main stem strongly abbreviated and amply branched; branches diffuse, 20–80 cm. Leaves on the main stem rosulate, linear, 8–20(–30) × 0.5–1.5 cm; leaves on fertile branches much shorter, 5–7 cm, abaxially rather densely arachnoid. Flowers in terminal and axillary heads, sessile or on peduncle to 4 cm; bracts 7–8 mm. Sepals connate at base, linear-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, abaxially arachnoid. Petals blue-purple, blue, or white, ca. 6 mm. Filaments blue arachnoid. Capsule broadly oblong, trigonous, ca. 2.5 mm, densely hirsutulous at apex. Seeds grey-brown, pitted.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 254; Y. W. Lam 924.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Ravines, humid rocks. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cyanotis axillaris (L.) D. Don ex Sweet 鞘苞花
Hort. Brit. 430. 1826; FHK 378. 1861; FKH 284. 1912; FOC 24: 23. 2000.
Commelina axillaris L., Sp. Pl. 1: 42. 1753.
Amischophacelus axillaris (L.) R. S. Rao & Kammathy, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 59: 379. 1966; FRPS 13(3): 120, pl. 30: 6 – 9. 1997; FGD 6: 323. 2005; Check List HK Plants 302. 2002; 107. 2004.

Annual herb, 30–40 cm tall, with roots fibrous; stems with long creeping branches. Leaves all cauline, linear or linearlanceolate, (2–)5–10 cm × 5–8 mm, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Flowers 2–3 together, nearly sessile within the short loose leaf sheath. Sepals linear-spatulate, 6–9 mm, divided nearly to the base, hirsute on abaxial surface. Petals ovate, deep blue, ca. 12 mm. Filaments thickened above a dense tuft of articulate hairs. Capsule oblong, trigonous, 4–5 mm, hispid at apex, with 6 horned projections. Seeds grey-black or grey-brown, pitted.

Locality: Tai Au Mun. Y. S. Lau 2597.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Moist sandy lowlands. Flowering: Spring and autumn.

Cyanotis vaga (Lour.) Schultes & J. H. Schultes 藍耳草
Syst. Veg. 7: 1153. 1830; FRPS 13(3): 122, pl. 30: 1 – 2. 1997; FOC 24: 22. 2000; FGD 6: 319. 2005.
Tradescantia vaga Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 193. 1790.
Cyanotis barbata D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 45. 1825; FKH 284. 1912.
Cyanotis fasciculata auct. non Roem. & Schult.: FHK 378. 1861.
Cyanotis kewensis auct. non C. B. Clarke: FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb, with globose bulbs, ± white woolly or glabrescent; stems ascending, 10–60 cm tall. Leaves all cauline, linear to lanceolate, 5–15 cm × 3–15 mm. Flowers in small clusters, 2–3 together, unequally pedunculate or nearly sessile, terminal or in the upper axils, and each cluster surrounded by 8–10 lanceolate much calcite imbricate bracts; proximal bracts 8–12 mm. Sepals connate at base, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, abaxially white hirsute. Petals purple or blue-purple, 6–8 mm. Filaments woolly below the anthers. Capsule obovoid, trigonous, ca. 2.5 mm, hirsutulous at apex. Seeds grey-brown, striate and finely reticulate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1987; Y. W. Lam 924.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.

Cyathula prostrata (L.) Blume 杯莧
Bijdr. 549. 1825; FHK 285. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 405. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 403, pl. 188. 1996; FRPS 25(2): 218. 1979; FGD 4: 104, fig, 65. 2000; FOC 5: 421. 2003.
Achyranthes prostrata L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 296. 1762.

Perennial herb, pubescent throughout. Stems prostrate, usually purplish, rooting at nodes; flowering branches ascending or erect, 15–50 cm tall. Leaves opposite; petioles 2–3 mm; leaf blade obovate to obovate-elliptic, 1–6(– 8) × 0.5 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or abruptly acute, margin entire. Racemes terminal, 5 –20 cm; flower-clusters reflexed, 3 – 8 mm spaced on rachis, consisting of 2–3 perfect flowers and 2–3 cluster of purplish hooked bristles. Perianth segments 5, oblong, ca. 5 mm, densely white pubescent outside. Stamens 5; staminodes apex truncate or slightly 2-toothed. Utricles globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., indehiscent.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen. Y. S. Lau 1343; Y. W. Lam 2187; HK sheet 4539.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian subcontinent, tropical Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages, also in bushes in valleys or by streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cycas revoluta Thunb. 蘇鐵
Verh. Holl. Maatsch. Weetensch. Haarlem. 20(2): 424, 426 – 427.1782; FKH 256. 1912; FRPS 7: 7, pl. 1: 1– 6. 1978; FFJ rev. ed.1: 268, fig. 252. 1991; FOC 4: 4. 1999; FGD 4: 3, fig. 1. 2000.

Trunk to 2–8 m; bark grey-black, scaly. Leaves fascicled at apex of stem, 1-pinnate; petiole subtetragonal in cross section, 10–20 cm, with 6–18 spines along each side; leaflets in 60–150 pairs, straight to subfalcate, 10–20 cm × 4–7 mm, leathery, sparsely pubescent abaxially, base decurrent, margin strongly recurved, apex acuminate, pungent. Pollen cones pale yellow, ovoid-cylindric, 30–60 × 8–15 cm; microsporophylls narrowly cuneate, 3.5–6 × 1.7–2.5 cm, apex rounded-truncate, cuspidate. Megasporophylls yellow to pale brown, 14–22 cm, densely tomentose; stalk 7–12 cm; sterile blade ovate to narrowly so, 6–11 × 4–7 cm, deeply laciniate, with 21–35 lobes 1–3 cm; ovules 2 or 3 on each side of stalk, densely pale brown tomentose. Seeds 2(–5), orange to red, obovoid or ellipsoid, somewhat compressed, (3–)4–5 × 2.5–3.5 cm, sparsely hairy; sclerotesta not grooved on sides.

Locality: Widely cultivated in gardens and parks. HK sheet27073; Y. S. Lau 1896.
Ecology: Pollinating: May–Jul.; seed maturity: Sep.– Oct.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan. Widely cultivatedin China.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cycas taiwaniana Carruth. 廣東蘇鐵（台灣蘇鐵）
J. Bot. 31: 2. 1893; FKH 256. 1912; FRPS 7: 9, pl. 2: 1–4. 1978; FFJ rev. ed. 1: 268, fig. 253. 1991; FOC 4: 5. 1999; FGD 4: 4, fig. 2. 2000.
Cycas fairylakea D. Y. Wang, Cycads in China (eds. F.X. Wang & H.B. Liang): 54. 1996; FGD 4: 4. 2000.
Cycas revoluta Thunb. var. taiwaniana (Carruth.) J. Schust., Pflanzenr. 99, 4(1): 84. 1932.
Cycas siamensis auct. non Miq.: Check List HK Plants 26. 1993.

Trunk cylindric, to 3.5 m; bark dark brown or grey-brown, scaly. Leaves fascicled at apex of stem, 1-pinnate; petiole obovate in cross section, 40 –120 cm, with 30 –60 spines along each side of basal part, glabrous; leaflets in 70 –150 pairs, often falcate, 18 –35 cm × 11–14 mm, leathery, glabrous abaxially, midvein raised on both surfaces only when fresh, slightly raised or flat abaxially when dry, base decurrent, margin flat, apex attenuate, pungent. Pollen cones ovoid or ellipsoid-cylindric, 30–45 × 8–10 cm; microsporophylls narrowly cuneate, 2–3 cm × 5– 8 mm; apex obtuse-rounded, with very short, upcurved mucro. Megasporophylls more than 30, tightly grouped, 15 –22 cm, pale brown tomentose; stalk 8 –12 cm; sterile blade rhombic-ovate, 7–12 × 6 –7 cm, margin glabresent and pectinate, with (11–)23 – 47 lobes 2–3.5 cm, terminal lobe ± flattened, 2–3.5 cm × 5–10 mm, margin usually irregularly serrulate, apex acute; ovules 2 or 3 on each side of distal part of stalk, glabrous. Seeds 2(–4), pale yellowish, globose, or broadly obovoid, slightly compressed, 2.8–3.3 × 2.5 –3 cm; sclerotesta finely verrucose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 690; HK sheet 27079.
Distribution: Guangdong, E Guangxi, SW Hunan, SE Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cyclea hypoglauca (Schauer) Diels 粉葉輪環藤
Pflanzenr. IV. 94: 319. 1910; FHN 1: 325. 1964; FGD 1: 45. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 75. 1996.
Cissampelos hypoglauca Schauer, Nov. Act. Acad. Leop. Carol. 11 (Suppl. 1): 479. 1843.
Cyclea deltoidea Miers, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 258. 1851; FHK 14. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.

Herbaceous or ± woody vine. Branchlets slender, glabrous. Leaves peltate, papery; petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to triangular ovate, 2.5–7 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base truncate to rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, adaxially shining, abaxially glaucous, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, palmately 5–7- nerved. Panicles narrow, almost reduced to racemes. Male flowers: sepals 4 or 5, free, obovate or obovate-cuneate, 1–1.2 mm; petals 4 or 5, usually connate and saucer-shaped, scarcely lobed, 0.5–1 mm; stamens united in a central column, 1–1.2 mm, slightly exserted. Female flowers: sepals 2, suborbicular, ca. 0.8 in diam.; petals 2, unequal; ovary glabrous. Drupes red, glabrous; the kernel ca. 3.5 mm, dorsally with 3 rows of tuberculous ribs on each side.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Tsing Yi. Y. W. Lam 149, 999; H. C. Tang 994.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest edges and bushes on hillsides. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Cyclobalanopsis bella (Chun & Tsiang) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen 檳榔青岡
J. Beijing Forest Univ. 15(4): 45. 1993; FRPS 22: 302, pl. 95: 1– 4. 1998; FOC 4: 393. 1999.
Quercus bella Chun & Tsiang, J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 326. 1947.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Branchlets angular, initially pubescent, glabrescent with age. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 8 –15 × 2–3.5 cm, base cuneate, slightly oblique, apex acuminate, margin serrate above middle, adaxially glabrous, abaxially covered with short appressed hairs when young, glabrous and glaucous in age; lateral veins 12–14 on each side of midvein. Male spikes unknown. Female spikes 1–2 cm, usually with 2–3 cupules. Cupule discoid, ca. 5 mm high, 2.5–3 cm in diam., greyish yellow-puberulent outside, surrounding the base of nut; bracts in 6 –8 concentric rings. Nut compressed globose, 1.5 –2 cm high, 1.5 –2 cm in diam., pubescent when young; scar slightly concave, 1–1.4 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po, Yin Ngam. Y. W. Lam 215.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis blakei (Skan) Schott. 櫟子青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 649. 1912; FRPS 22: 304, pl. 95: 5 –10. 1998; FOC 4: 393. 1999.
Quercus blakei Skan, Hooker's Icon. Pl. 27: t. 2662. 1901; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 35 m tall. Bark greyish black, smooth. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles slender, 1.5–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade narrowly ovate-elliptic to obovate-oblanceolate, variable in size, 7–12 × 1.5 –2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate on the upper 1/3, reddish-tomentose on both surfaces when young, soon glabrescent; lateral veins 8–14 on each side of midvein. Male spike ca. 4 cm, tawny tomentose. Female spikes 1–2 cm, with 1–2 cupules. Cupule solitary or in pairs, discoid, 5–10 mm high, 2–3 cm in diam., dark-brown-tomentose outside, surrounding the base of nut; bracts in 6 –7 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoidal or ovoid, 2.5 –3.5 cm high, 1.5 –3 cm in diam., scar 7–11 mm in diam.

Locality: Ta Tit Yan, Tai Po, She Shan Tsuen. W. J. Tutcher 7288, 11293; S. C. Ng 3525.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from “Tatitin”, New Territories by C. Ford.

records.text:
Cyclobalanopsis championii (Benth.) Oerst. 嶺南青岡
Vidensk. Meddel. Dansk Naturhist. Foren. Kjobenhavn 1866: 79. 1876; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 100. 1963; FFJ 1: 405, fig. 361. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 69, pl. 29, photo 25. 1996; FRPS 22: 281, pl. 103: 3 –7. 1998; FOC 4: 388. 1999.
Quercus championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 113. 1854; FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots, petioles and inflorescence tawny tomentose. Leaves thickly leathery; petioles 0.8–1.5 cm; leaf blade obovate to oblong, 3.5 –10(–13) × 2–3.5(– 6) cm, base cuneate to acute, apex broadly obtuse or rounded, with a blunt tip, rarely retuse, margin revolute, entire or sometimes slightly crenulate near apex, adaxially glabrous and shining when full-grown, abaxially densely brownish stellate-tomentose; lateral veins 6 –10 on each side of midvein, as is the midvein impressed adaxially, conspicuously raised abaxially. Male spike 4– 8 cm. Female spikes erect, ca. 4 cm, with 3–10 cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 7–10 mm high, 1.4 –1.7 cm in diam., brownish-tomentose abaxially, enclosing 1/3–1/4 of nut; bracts in 4–7 concentric rings. Nut broadly ovoid or compressed globose, 1.5 –2 cm high, 1.2–1.5(–1.8) cm in diam., rounded on both ends, pubescent when young; scar 4 – 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lautau Island. H. C. Tang 621; C. P. Lau 60; HK sheet 6718
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Dec. to Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Cyclobalanopsis chungii (Metc.) Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen ex Q. F. Zheng 福建青岡
FFJ 1: 405, fig. 362. 1982; FRPS 22: 282, pl. 103: 8 –10. 1998; FOC 4: 388. 1999.
Quercus chungii Metc., Lingnan Sci. J. 10: 481. 1931.

Tree, to 15 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and inflorescence densely brown stellate tomentose. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1–2.2 cm; leaf blade obovate, obovate-elliptic to elliptic, 5–12 × 1.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex short-caudate, rarely acute, margin obscurely serrulate or crenulate towards apex, rarely entire, adaxially glabrous and shining when full-grown, abaxially densely greyish brown stellate-tomentose; lateral veins 9–15 on each side of midvein. Male spike unknown; Female spikes erect, 1.5–2 cm, with 2–6 cupules. Cupule discoid, 6–8 mm high, 1.2–1.8 cm in diam., brown-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/4–1/3 of nut; bracts in 5–7 concentric rings. Nut compressed globose or ovoid, 1.5–2.1 cm high, 1.4–1.8 cm in diam., top flat-rounded, minutely tomentose; scar 1–1.2 cm in diam.

Locality: Castle Peak, So Kwun Wat. P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 38401); F. W. Xing 9333, 10205.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis edithiae (Skan) Schott. 華南青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 650. 1912; FRPS 22: 306, pl. 86: 5–7. 1998; FOC 4: 393. 1999.
Quercus edithiae Skan, Hooker's Icon. Pl. 27: t. 2661. 1901; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Branchlets slightly angular, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 2–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong to obovateoblong, 5–16 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate, apex broadly acute, margin shallowly serrulate on the upper 1/3, adaxially dark green, glabrous, abaxially greyish brown-tomentose when young, glabrous in age; lateral veins 9 –12 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Male spike 2–3 cm, densely yellow-tomentose. Female spikes 1–2 cm in fruiting time, with 3– 4 cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 12–15 mm high, 1.8 –2.5 cm in diam., wall 2–3 mm thick, dark-yellow-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/4 –1/3 of nut; bracts in 6 – 8 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoid to cylindrical-ellipsoid, 3– 4.5 cm high, 2–3 cm in diam.; scar slightly convex, ca. 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Sai Kung, Tai Wai, Ta Tit Yan. W. J. Tutcher 8049, 9486; L. T. Lo 371.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The leaves of this species are somewhat similar to C. blakei, but can be easily distinguished by its bowl-shaped and yellow-tomentose cupule. The type specimen was collected from “Tatitin”, New Territories, by C. Ford.
