Cyclobalanopsis glauca (Thunb.) Oerst. 青岡
Vidensk. Meddel. Dansk Naturhist. Foren. Kjobenhavn 1866: 78. 1867; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 101. 1963; FFJ 1: 408, fig. 365. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 72, pl. 31. 1996; FRPS 22: 315, pl. 98: 1. 1998; FOC 4: 396. 1999.
Quercus glauca Thunb., Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 858. 1784; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade obovate-elliptic or elliptic, 6–15(–18) × 2.5 – 5(– 8) cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, margin remotely serrate on the upper half, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially glaucous, with appressed hairs and scurfy lepidote; lateral veins 9 –10 on each side of midvein. Male spike (2–)5 – 6 cm, rachis brown-tomentose. Female spikes 1.5 –3 cm in fruiting time, with 1–3 cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 6 –7 mm high, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., sparsely pubescent outside, enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts in 5–7 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoid-ovoid or ellipsoid, 1–1.5 cm high, 0.9 –1.2 cm in diam., scar flat or slightly convex, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Shek O, Cape D'Aguilar, Pok Fu Lam, Ma On Shan. X. Y. Zhuang 1931; Y. S. Lau 1514, 3009.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, N India, Bhutan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis hui (Chun) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen 雷公青岡
J. Beijing Forest. Univ. 15(4): 45. 1993; FRPS 22: 282, pl. 85: 1–3. 1998; FOC 4: 388. 1999.
Quercus hui Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 126. 1928.

Tree, 10–15 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and inflorescences densely tawny-tomentose when young, glabrescent with age. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1–1.4 cm; leaf blade oblong, oblanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 7–13 × 1.5 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate, often slightly oblique, apex obtuse, rarely acuminate, margin recurved, entire or obscurely serrulate towards apex, adaxially glabrous and shining when full-grown, abaxially tawny-tomentose when young, gradually glabrate; lateral veins 6 –10 on each side of midvein. Male spike 5–9 cm, 2–4 clustered. Female spikes 1–2 cm, with 2–5 cupules crowded at apex of rachis. Cupule shallow bowl-shaped, 6–10 mm high, 1.5 –3 cm in diam., brown-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/2 of nut; bracts in 4 – 6 concentric rings. Nut compressed globose, 1.5–2 cm high, 1.5 –2.5 cm in diam., densely tawny-tomentose when young, but glabrescent later; scar concave, 7–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng. Y. W. Lam 500, 501.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis litseoides (Dunn) Schott. 木薑葉青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 658. 1912; FRPS 22: 277, pl. 85: 6– 8. 1998; FOC 4: 387. 1999.
Quercus litseoides Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 377. 1909; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets slender, initially tomentose, gradually glabrate. Leaves subsessile, blade obovate-oblanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 2.5–7 × 0.8–3 cm, apex broadly obtuse to rounded, base cuneate, margin entire, adaxially dark green, abaxially greyish green, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein. Male spike 3–5 cm; rachis and perianth brown‑tomentose. Female spikes ca. 1 cm, with 2 apical cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 5–6 mm high, 1–1.5 cm in diam., sparsely greyish-brown-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts in 5–7 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoidal, 1.5–1.8 cm high, ca. 1 cm in diam., puberulent at apex; scar flat 5–6 mm in diam.

Locality: Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 6597; H. C. Tang 2149; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35584).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Jan.; fruiting: Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis myrsinifolia (Blume) Oerst. 小葉青岡
Skr. Vidensk.-Selsk. Christiana, Math.-Naturvidensk. Kl. 9(6): 387. 1871; FFJ 1: 407. 1982; FRPS 22: 325, pl. 98: 3. 1998; FTW ed. 2, 2: 78, pl. 36. 1996; FOC 4: 398. 1999.
Quercus myrsinifolia Blume, Mus. Bot. 1: 305. 1850.

Tree, 10 –15 m tall. Branchlets glabrous, with raised light brown lenticels. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate or broadly ovate-oblong, 5–12 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate or sub-rounded, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, margin serrulate above middle, adaxially green, abaxially glaucous, becoming dark grey when dry, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 10–14 on each side of midvein. Male spike 4 – 6(–9) cm, rachis slender, ± tawny tomentose. Female spikes 1.5–3 cm, with 2–3 cupules. Cupule cup-shaped, 5 –7 mm high, 0.7–1 cm in diam., whitish pubescent outside, enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts in 6 –9 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoid, 1.3 –2 cm high, 0.8 –1.1 cm in diam., glabrous, apex rounded; scar flat, ca. 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3164; H. C. Tang 11651; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6801).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Woods by streams or ravines. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis neglecta Schott. 竹葉青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 650. 1912; FOC 4: 387. 1999.
Cyclobalanopsis bambusifolia (Hance) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen, J. Forest. Univ. 15(4): 44. 1993; FRPS 22: 280, pl. 85: 4 –5. 1998.
Quercus bambusifolia Hance in Seem. Bot. Voy. Herald, t. 91. 1875, non Fortune (1860).
Quercus salicina auct. non Blume: FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots silky-hairy, glabrous in age. Leaves thinly leathery, crowded towards apex of branchlets; petioles 2– 5 mm, glabrous; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to ellipticlanceolate, 3–11 × 0.6–1.8 cm, narrowed to both ends, apex blunt, margin entire, adaxially dark green, glabrous, abaxially ± glaucous, glabrous or with some long hairs at base; lateral veins 7–14 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Male catkins axillary, very slender, 2.5–5 cm, rachis rusty-tomentose. Female spikes short and erect, 0.5–1 cm, with 2 flowers; styles 3 or 4. Infructescences 5–10 mm, usually with only one fruit. Cupule discoid or cup-shaped, 5–10 mm high, 1.3–1.8 cm in diam., enclosing ca. 1/2 of nut, greyish brown tomentose outside; bracts in 4–6 concentric rings. Nut obovoid or ellipsoid, 1.5–2.5 cm high, 1–1.6 cm in diam., slightly tomentose; scar convex, 5–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Mount Gough, Mount Nicholson, Tai Tam, Wan Chai Gap. Y. S. Lau 1703; H. C. Tang 1137; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6819).
Distribution: Hainan. Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Woodlands. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Oct.

Cyclospermum leptophyllum (Pers.) Sprague ex Britton & P. Wilson 細葉旱芹
Bot. Porto Rico. 6: 52. 1925; FOC 14: 115. 2005.
Pimpinella leptophylla Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 324. 1805.
Apium leptophyllum (Pers.) F. Muell. ex Benth., Fl. Austral. 3: 372. 1866; FKH 116. 1912; FRPS 55(2): 6. 1985; FGD 2: 341. 1991.

Annual herb, 30–130 cm tall. Basal leaves elliptic-ovate in outline, 2–10 × 2–8 cm, 3–4-pinnatisect; the ultimate segments linear to filiform, 1.5–7 × 0.5–1 mm; petioles 10–20 cm. Cauline leaves ternate-pinnately decompound, ultimate segments filiform. Inflorescence of compound umbels, terminal and axillary; peduncles 3–8 cm; involucre of a few inconspicuous, entire bracts or wanting; rays 10–20, subequal to unequal, 1–5 cm; involucre of 5 or 6 linear, acute, entire bracteoles shorter than the flowers; pedicels 2–5 mm. Fruit globose, 2–4 × 1.5–3 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shek O Rd. U. A. On 8492; Y. S. Lau 1588.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; America, Australia, Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Grassy fields along ditches and other damp places. Flowering: May.
Notes: The species was reported as Apium leptophyllum (Pers.) F. Muell. ex Benth. previously (Check List HK Plants 205. 2002; 72. 2004).

Cymbidium ensifolium (L.) Sw. 建蘭
Nov. Acta Soc. Sci. Upsal. 6: 77. 1799; FHK 357. 1861; FKH 265. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 98, fig. 55. 1977; FFJ 6: 616. 1995; FRPS 18: 213. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 823. 2000; FGD 7: 395, fig. 195. 2006; FOC 25: 274. 2009.
Epidendrum ensifolium L., Sp. Pl. 2: 954. 1753.
Cymbidium xiphiifolium Lindl., Bot. Reg. 7: t. 529. 1821; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 96. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs very small, ovoid, subterranean. Leaves grass-like, tufted, linear, 50–70 cm. Flowers fragrant, 3–5 cm across, racemose, on scapes as long as leaves; sepals spreading, white tinged green, occasionally lined red near base; petals white, shorter and wider than sepals, forming a roof over the column; lip pale yellow or white with irregular red blotches, the midlobe papillose, recurved. Column short, hidden by the petals.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Fo Tan Valley, High Island Reservoir, Tung Chung. K. K. Mark 13(2404) (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 8212 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 126.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; widely distributed in SE and S Asia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cymbidium kanran Makino 寒蘭
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 10. 1902; FRPS 18: 217. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 828. 2000; FGD 7: 386. 2006; FOC 25: 275. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs narrowly ovoid, ± compressed. Leaves usually 4–5 on pseudobulb, linear, 40–70 × 0.9–1.7 cm, dark green, thinly leathery. Scape arising from base of pseudobulb, 25–60–(80) cm. Racemes 10- or more-flowered; bracts linear-lanceolate, 2.5–3 × 0.3–0.4 cm; pedicel and ovary 20–25(–30) mm. Flowers fragrant, 3–5 cm across, variable in colour; sepals and petals pale yellowish green with purplish red striations; lip yellowish, mottled purplish red; petals narrowly ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 20–30 × 5–10 mm; lip obovate obscurely 3-lobed. Column whitish, 10–17 mm, with reddish spots on ventral side.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1189.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cymbidium lancifolium Hook. 兔耳蘭
Exot. Bot. 1: t. 51. 1823; FRPS 18: 225, pl. 36: 3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 829. 2000; FGD 7: 384, fig. 194. 2006; FOC 25: 278. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs ellipsoidal, slightly compressed, 4–5 cm long, 10 cm across one way, 6 cm across the other. Leaves petiolate, 2–4 terminal to pseudobulbs; petioles slender, folded, faintly articulate; leaf blades dark green, elliptic, 10–19 × 3.5–4.5 cm, base gradually attenuate to the folded petiole, apex shortly acuminate or acute, midrib impressed above and elevated beneath, lateral veins obscure above, evident beneath. Inflorescences racemose, light green; flowers pale green, creamy white, with red and purple blotches and streaks; sepals uniformly pale green with a satin sheen, linear-lanceolate, 3.5 × 0.5 cm, slightly recurved; petals oblique-lanceolate, 2.5 × 0.7 cm, inner margin slightly overlapping, creamy white with a conspicuous purplish red longitudinal median line within; lip fleshy, delicately creamy white; lateral lobes erect, brilliant purplish red suffused with creamy white on inner sides; midlobe oblong-ovate, apex obtuse and strongly recurved, irregularly and sparsely marked with red patches; column arching, creamy white, inconspicuously diffused pink at the back, with red lines and streaks at the front; anther subglobose, yellowish, papillose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 34239, 35993.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cymbidium maclehoseae S. Y. Hu 冬月蘭
Chung Chi Journal 11: 15, fig. 2. 1972; FRPS 18: 225. 1999; FGD 7: 384, fig. 194. 2006; FOC 25: 278. 2009, pro syn. sub C. lancifolium.

Large terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs elongate-ellipsoidal, 8–10 cm long, 1.5–1.7 cm in diam. Leaves petiolate, petioles equitant, lower portion sheathing, upper part subcylindrical-canaliculate; leaf blades elliptic, 13–21 × 3.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, midrib impressed above and elevated beneath. Inflorescences racemose, lateral to the pseudobulb; flowers greenish cream-white; sepals lanceolate, 2.5 × 0.4 cm, basal one-third recurved; petals lanceolate, 2.2 × 0.45 cm, slightly oblique and falcate at base, basal one-fourth faintly purple-lined on the inside; lip irregularly purple maculate; lateral lobes erect, narrow, fleshy; midlobe tongue-like, recurved and rolling backward, trough deeply grooved along the median longitudinal line, fleshy; column slightly arcuate, cream-white, maculate purple on the flat front surface; anther subglobose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 9369 (A).
Distribution: Known only from Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec. (fide Hu, 1972)
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 9369, A) was collected by S. Y. Hu from New Territories in 1969. The species has been synonymised under Cymbidium lancifolium Hook. s.l. by some authors (e.g. FOC 25: 278. 2009).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 9369, A) was collected by S. Y. Hu from New Territories in 1969. The species has been synonymised under Cymbidium lancifolium Hook. s.l. by some authors (e.g. FOC 25: 278. 2009).

records.text:
Cymbidium sinense (Jacks. ex Andrews) Willd. 墨蘭（報歲蘭）
Sp. Pl. ed. 4. 111. 1805; FHN 4: 246. 1977; FRPS 18: 215. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 831. 2000; FGD 7: 386. 2006; FOC 25: 274. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs ovoid, 3 cm long, 2 cm in diam. Leaves narrow-linear, shorter than the scape. Flowers 5 cm in diam., in racemes above the foliage, on greenish-brown rachis; sepals and petals lanceolate, pale-yellow, faintly red-lined, red toward base; lip red, narrowly yellow along the margin, yellow patched with white-centre at base, without distinct lateral lobes; column short, white.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 9492, 11504 (CUHK); HK sheet 34337.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Burma, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cymbopogon goeringii (Steud.) A. Camus 橘草
Rev. Bot. Appl. Agric. Colon. 1: 286. 1921; FRPS 10(2): 204, pl. 51: 8–14. 1997; FYN 9: 686, pl. 112: 14–17. 2003; FOC 22: 629. 2006; FGD 9: 499. 2009.
Andropogon goeringii Steud., Flora 29: 22. 1846.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 50–110 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, the upper shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, 15–40 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous, margins scabrous, apex finely acuminate; ligule 0.5–4.5 mm, obtuse and rounded. Spathate compound panicle narrow, loose, 15–35 cm, 1–2 tiers of branching; spatheoles 1.5–2 cm, purple; racemes often purplish, paired; rachis internodes and pedicels apex cupular, margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate, 4.5– 6 mm, callus ca. 0.5 mm, pubescent and subglabrous; lower glume flat or slightly concave toward base, sharply 2-keeled throughout; keels winged above middle; upper glume boat-shaped, margins narrow membranous and ciliate, narrow wing on the keel, acute; lower lemma about 3/4 length of glume, narrow and acuminate, 2-keeled, ciliate; upper lemma very narrow, ca. 3 mm, with a geniculate awn from sinus; upper lemma 2-lobed; awn 1–2 cm; palea absent; style brown, penicillate, exerted laterally. Pedicellate spikelet 4–6 mm, pedicel white long pilose.

Locality: Mount Parker, Cape D'Aguilar, Lantau Island. HK sheet 38089, 41940, 42036.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, S Korea.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Cymbopogon martini (Roxb.) W. Watson 魯沙香茅
Himalayan Districts N.W. Prov. India. 392. 1882; FRPS 10(2): 192. 1997 [“martinii”]; FOC 22: 626. 2006.
Andropogon martini Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 280. 1820; FHK 424. 1861.
Cymbopogon schoenanthus Spreng., Pl. Min. Cogn. Pug. 2: 15. 1815; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb, with a short woody rootstock. Culms tufted, up to 3 m tall, lower nodes often swollen, mealy. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades usually glaucous at abaxial surface, dark green at adaxial surface, lanceolate, up to 50 × 2–3 cm, glabrous, base cordate, often amplexicaul, apex filiform; ligule 2–4 mm. Spathate panicle narrow, dense, erect, 20–30 cm; spatheoles green becoming reddish, 2–4 cm; racemes 1.5–2 cm; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate on margins; pedicel of homogamous pair swollen, barrel-shaped, shiny, fused to internode at base. Sessile spikelet oblong, 3.5–4.5 mm; lower glume deeply grooved below middle, appearing as a line or keel on inside; keels winged above middle, veinless or 2-veined between keels; upper lemma 2-lobed; awn 1.4–1.8 cm. Pedicellate spikelet 3.5–4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. L. Thrower s.n. (CUHK).
Distribution: Sichuan, Yunnan; Indian Subcontinent, widely cultivated in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Material (essential oil).

Cymbopogon mekongensis A. Camus 青香茅
Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 26: 563. 1920; FOC 22: 626. 2006.
Cymbopogon caesius auct. non Stapf: FHN 4: 480. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 196, pl. 46: 8–14. 1997; FGD 9: 498. 2009; Check List HK Plants 329. 2002; 116. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculate, tufted, 30–80 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, the upper shorter than internodes; leaf blades linear, glabrous, 10–25 × 0.2–0.6 cm, apex filiform; ligule 0.7–3 mm. Spathate compound panicle narrow, 10–30 cm, spathes densely clustered, racemes paired; rachis internodes and pedicels ca. 1.5 mm. Sessile spikelet oblanceolate; lower glume ovatelanceolate, deeply grooved below middle; keels broadly winged above middle, veinless or obscurely 2-veined between keels; upper glume boat-shaped, narrow wing on the keel, margins membranous and ciliate, acute; upper lemma deeply 2-lobed; awn 1–1.5 cm, from the sinus, geniculate; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet 3–4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 5126; S. P. Lau 133; HK sheet 15738.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang; Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Roadsides, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Cymbopogon nardus (L.) Rendle 亞香茅
Cat. Afr. Pl. 2: 155. 1899; FKH 323. 1912; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 296. 1971; FHN 4: 479, fig. 1265. 1977; FFJ 6: 276. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 199. 1997; FOC 22: 628. 2006; FGD 9: 499. 2009.
Andropogon nardus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1046. 1753.

Perennial herb. Culms densely tufted. Leaf sheaths reddish purple at base, smooth, glabrous, the upper shorter than internode, most crowded at base of culm; leaf blades dark green or dark brown when dry, linear, flat, 30–50 × 0.5–2 cm, glabrous, adaxial surface smooth, abaxial surface scabrid, base narrow, apex attenuate to needle, margins scabrous; ligule 2–3 mm, membranous, glabrous. Spathate panicle large, narrow, congested, 60–90 cm; spatheoles reddish brown, 1–2.5 cm; racemes 1–2 cm; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate on margins, back glabrous or pubescent. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate; lower glume reddish brown or purplish upward, papery, flat or slightly concave, sharply 2-keeled; keels narrowly winged, veinless or obscurely veined between keels; upper glume boat-shaped, membranous, ciliate; lower lemma oblong, ciliate, veinless; upper lemma linear, entire or slightly 2-lobed, mucronate or very shortly awned; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or seldom neuter, 3.5–7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 31542, 33469.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); Indian Subcontinent, widely cultivated in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), material (essential oil).

Cymbopogon tortilis (J. Presl) A. Camus 扭鞘香茅
Rev. Bot. Appl. Agric. Colon. 5: 206. 1925; FHN 4: 481. 1977; FFJ 6: 275, fig. 249. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 536. 2000; FOC 22: 628. 2006.
Anthistiria tortilis J. Presl in C. Presl, Reliq. Haenk. 1: 347. 1830.
Cymbopogon hamatulus (Hook. & Arn.) A. Camus, Bot. Beechey Voy. 244. 1838; FRPS 10(2): 207, pl. 51: 1–7. 1997; FGD 9: 500. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, slender, 50–150 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous, shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, glabrous or tomentose near the base of adaxial surface, 25–60 × 0.2–0.7 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex finely acuminate; ligule 2–3 mm, dry membranous. Spathate compound panicle narrow, 20–35 cm, 2–3 tiers of branching; spatheoles reddish brown, 1.2–1.5 cm; racemes 1–1.5 cm, paired; rachis internodes and pedicels obliquely cupular, margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblonglanceolate, 3.5–4.5 mm, callus very short; lower glume flat, sharply 2-keeled throughout; keels narrowly winged above middle, 2–5-veined between keels; upper glume boat-shaped, narrow wing on the keel, acute; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, 2-keeled, ciliate; upper lemma very narrow, 2-lobed; awn 0.7–1 cm; palea absent. Pedicellate spikelet 3–3.5 mm, awnless.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 53; Y. S. Lau 2534; Y. W. Lam 6.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Cymbopogon hamatulus (Nees ex Hook. & Arn.) A. Camus previously (Check List HK Plants 330. 2002; 116. 2004).

Cynanchum corymbosum Wight 刺瓜
Contrib. Bot. Ind. 56. 1834; FRPS 63: 379, pl. 138. 1977; FGD 1: 504, fig. 571. 1987; FOC 16: 212. 1995.

Perennial herbs, with thick tubers. Stems twining, to 2 m, pale grey, pubescent along 2 lines. Petioles 2.5–4.5 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4.5–12(–20) × 3.5–8(–10) cm, thinly papery, base deeply cordate, basal lobes rounded, apex apiculate or acuminate, glabrous except for veins, abaxially glaucous, adaxially darkening on drying, basal veins 5, lateral veins 3 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences raceme‑like, 2.5–7 cm, laxly branched and less often to 13 cm; cymules 2‑flowered; peduncle 1–5 cm, puberulent; pedicels 2–18 mm, pubescent. Sepals ovate, 1.5–2 × 1 mm, glabrous or pubescent; basal glands 5, minute. Corolla greenish white drying dark, subrotate; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 5 × 1.5 mm, glabrous. Corona ± tubular, pure white, 3–4 mm high, plicate and with ± free adaxial appendages between acute teeth, marginal teeth 10, alternately rounded and acute, ca. 0.5–0.7 mm. Anther with oval appendages; pollinia oblong. Stigma head 2‑fid, included within anthers. Follicles fusiform, 9–12 × 2–3 cm, conspicuously echinate; spines curved at tip. Seeds brown, 7–10 × 5 mm, conspicuously dentate at end opposite coma; coma 3–4 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tin Fu Tsai. L. T. Lo 635; HK sheet 34041.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian; Cambodia, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, open woods, riversides, valleys. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cynanchum insulanum (Hance) Hemsl. 海南杯冠藤
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26(173): 107. 1889; FRPS 63: 383. 1977; FGD 1: 507, fig. 575. 1987; FOC 16: 213. 1995.
Cynoctonum insulanum Hance, J. Bot. 6(71): 330. 1868.

Twining herbs, to 60 cm, glabrous except for pubescent nodes, petioles and leaf margins. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–15 mm; leaf blade oblong‑hastate, ovate‑triangular to linear‑lanceolate, 2–3.5 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base rounded to subcordate‑hastate, apex acute or short apiculate, lateral veins 5 or 6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences umbel‑like, much shorter than leaves, 4‑ or 5‑flowered. Sepal oblong, ca. 1 × 0.5 mm, acute; basal glands 5. Corolla greenish white, subrotate; tube ca. 0.5 mm; lobes ovate‑oblong, ca. 2 × 1 mm, acute. Corona‑tube cupular, thinly membranous, ca. 2 mm, longer than gynostegium, longitudinally plicate; anthers nearly square, appendages ovate; pollinia oblong. Stigma head capitate, included within anthers. Follicles lanceolate, 4.5 – 5 × 0.7–0.8 cm, with 2 inconspicuous longitudinal ridges, glabrous. Seeds oblong, 3 mm; coma 2 cm.

Locality: Sai Kung (Tai Wan). Y. W. Lam 466, 1219; HK sheet 39286.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Cynanchum paniculatum (Bunge) Kitag. 徐長卿
J. Jap. Bot. 16: 20. 1940; FRPS 63: 351, pl. 125. 1977; FGD 1: 509, fig. 578. 1987; FOC 16: 218. 1995.
Asclepias paniculata Bunge, Enum. Pl. China Bor. 43. 1833.

Perennial herbs. Roots numerous fibrous, fragrant. Stems slender, erect, to 1 m, glabrous or hispid on lower part, unbranched or with few branches from upper parts. Leaves opposite; petioles 3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to linear, 5–13 × 0.5–1.5 cm, stiffly papery, both ends acute, glabrous or adaxially puberulent, ciliate, lateral veins obscure. Inflorescences terminal and from upper nodes, laxly branched, to 7 cm; peduncle 2.5–4 cm; pedicels 5–10 mm. Sepals lanceolate, 1–1.5 × 0.5 mm; with or without glands. Corolla yellow‑green, subrotate, globrous; tube short; lobes ovate, 4–5.5 × 1.5–3 mm. Corona deeply 5‑lobed, lobes ovate‑oblong, fleshy, slightly laterally compressed, apex obtuse, as long as anthers, adaxially keeled up to middle and adnate to anthers. Anther with semiorbicular appendages, slightly shorter than stigma head; pollinia oblong. Stigma head slightly umbonate. Follicles lanceolate in outline, 4–8 × 0.3–0.8 cm. Seeds oblong, 5 × 3 mm; coma 1.5–3 cm.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Ko Lau Wan. Y. S. Lau 3114; HK sheet 32938.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, Mongolia.
Ecology: Sunny grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cynodon dactylon (L.) Pers. 狗牙根
Syn. Pl. 1: 85. 1805; FHK 428. 1861; FKH 326. 1912; FHN 4: 387, fig. 1195. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 84, pl. 25: 1–6. 1990; FFJ 6: 163, fig. 133. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 406. 2000; FOC 22: 493. 2006; FGD 9: 376, fig. 185. 2009.
Panicum dactylon L., Sp. Pl. 1: 85. 1753.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms slender, erect or ascending from the creeping stolons, 10–40 cm tall. Leaf blades linear, 1–12 × 0.1–0.4 cm, usually glabrous, scaberulous, apex subacute; auricles and orifices bearded; ligule a short ciliolate rim; leaf sheaths bearded at mouth, otherwise glabrous or thinly pilose. Spikes (2–)3–6, digitately arranged, 2–7 cm, spreading. Spikelets usually 1-flowered, sessile, imbricate in 2 rows on one side of axis, 2–2.7(–3) mm, purplish or green, breaking up above the glumes at maturity; glumes linear-lanceolate, membranous, often purplish, equal or slightly unequal, 1.5–2 mm, 1-veined, keel scabrous, thickened; lemma as long as spikelet, silky villous along keel, hairs straight, otherwise glabrous or lateral veins thinly villous, apex subacute; palea glabrous, keels scaberulous. Anthers 3, more than 1 mm. Caryopsis subterete, tightly enclosed between the hardened lemma and palea, usually turgid or scarcely laterally compressed.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 15; Y. S. Lau 2251; HK sheet 39699.
Distribution: Widely distributed in regions S of Huanghe; tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, margins of fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control, ornamental), animal food (fodder, forage).
records.uses: Environmental (erosion control, ornamental), animal food (fodder, forage).

records.text:
Cyperus compressus L. 扁穗莎草
Sp. Pl. 1: 46. 1753; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 147. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 239. 2000; FGD 8: 330. 2007; FOC 23: 237. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent, roots fibrous. Culms tufted, 8–35(–50) cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, 3–20 cm × 1–4 mm, acute, flat to channelled; sheath 1–7 cm, pale brown to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 2–5 cm, the longest up to 30 cm. Inflorescence simple to ± capitate, open to congested, 1.5–10 × 2–10 cm; primary branches (when present) 2–5, 0.8–15 cm; spikes solitary. Spikes ovate, 1.2–1.3 × 1.5–4 cm; axis 0.1– 0.5 cm. Spikelets 3–10 per spike, patent to spreading, often appearing finger-like, linear to oblong-lanceolate, 10–25 × 2.5–4 mm, flattened; axis zigzag. Glumes ovate, 3–4 × 2–2.7 mm, apex acute, mucronate, sides herbaceous or papery, 3-veined, pale green to pale golden brown, keel sharply acute, green. Stamens 3; anthers 0.7–1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 0.7–1 mm, dark brown, shiny, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw & G Reels 75; Y. W. Lam 763; HK sheet 37111.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Xizang, Gansu, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Shanxi, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Cyperus cuspidatus Kunth 長尖莎草
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 1: 204–205. 1815[1816]; FRPS 11: 155. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 240. 2000; FYN 15: 642. 2003; FGD 8: 331. 2007; FOC 23: 227. 2010.
Cyperus uncinatus auct. non Poir.: FKH 295. 1912.

Annual. Roots fibrous. Culms tufted, 3–15 cm tall, flaccid, trigonous, smooth, base with few leaves. Leaves shorter than culm; leaf blade 1–2 mm wide, usually folded. Involucral bracts 2–3, linear, longer than inflorescence. Inflorescences simple to capitate, 1.5 – 4 × 2.5 – 6 cm; primary branches 2–6, mostly to 2 cm. Spikelets 5– many, digitately arranged at a primary branches, linear, 5–15 × 2–3 mm, strongly flattened; axis straight, wingless. Glumes narrowly elliptic, 1–1.5 × 0.6–1 mm, emarginate, strongly recurvedmucronate, awn 0.5–1 mm, sides thinly papery, rusty brown to chestnut-brown, keel acute, 3-veined, greenish sometimes purplishlineolate. Stamens 2–3; anthers 0.2–0.3 mm. Style 0.3–0.6 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid to cylindrical-obovoid, trigonous, 0.5–0.6 × 0.3–0.4 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Beacon Hill, Tai Mo Shan. S. P. Lau 24; HK sheet 7841, 13237.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Shandong, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Open grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Cyperus difformis L. 異型莎草
Cent. Pl. II 6. 1756; FHK 385. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 152. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 240. 2000; FYN 15: 642. 2003; FGD 8: 332. 2007; FOC 23: 226. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent; roots fibrous. Culms tufted, (10–)25–60 cm tall, 2–5 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, sides concave. Leaves slightly shorter than culm; blade linear, 2–22 × 2–6 mm, acute, folded, sheath 2–10 mm, pale or yellowish brown to pinkish. Involucral bracts 2–3, unequal, the longest up to 25 cm. Inflorescence simple, open, occasionally congested; primary branches 3–9, 1–4 cm. Spikelets many, in congested globose clusters, 2–6 × 2–6 mm, linear to linear-oblong, 2–8 × 1–1.3 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes ± orbicular, 0.5–0.8 × 0.4–0.8 mm, apex rounded or shallowly emarginate, sides membranous, faintly 3-veined, deep green tinged with brownish purple, margins white hyaline, keel yellowish. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.1 mm. Style short, stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal-obovoid, trigonous, 0.5–0.7 × 0.3 mm, maturing yellowish.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 155; Y. S. Lau 2489; Y. W. Lam 1585.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Wet grasslands and along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Cyperus diffusus Vahl 多脈莎草（綠穗莎草）
Enum. Pl. 2: 321. 1805; FHK 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 148. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000.
Cyperus laxus Lam.: FGD 8: 331. 2007.

Perennial. Rhizomatous short. Culms ± tufted, 30–80 cm tall, 3–5 mm thick, trigonous to subtriquetrous, smooth. Leaf blades linear, 8–48 × 0.3–2 cm, abruptly acute, flattish, sheath 4–10 cm, pale green to rusty or purplish brown. Involucral bracts 4–12, unequal, the longest up to 50 cm. Inflorescence simple to decompound, open to rather dense, 6 20 × 7–30 cm; primary branches 10 – 20 or more, 2.5 – 20 cm; secondary and tertiary branches 0.5–4 cm. Spikelets in open finger-like clusters of (1–)2–9, oblong, subterete, 3–10 × 1.5–3 mm; axis straight. Glumes 6–20 per spikelet, ovate-orbicular, 1.5–2 × 1.5–2 mm, obtuse, recurved-mucronate, awn 0.2–0.5 mm, sides thinly herbaceous, indistinctly to prominently 7–11-veined, greenish tinged with pale or reddish brown, keel acute to subobtuse, greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes elliptic, trigonous, 1.2–1.5 × 0.7–0.8 mm, blackish brown, indistinctly minutely punctate.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po. Y. W. Lam 1309, 1311, 2086.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Xizang, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia, Indian Ocean islands, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests of valleys and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Cyperus distans L. f. 疏穗莎草
Suppl. Pl. 103. 1781; FHK 387. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 138. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 242. 2000; FYN 15: 631. 2003; FGD 8: 329. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody. Culms 1–few, 20–100 cm tall, 2–5 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth, thicked at base. Leaves basal, shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 100 cm × 4–10 mm, acuminate, weakly folded; sheath 5–20 cm, light brown to purple brown. Involucral bracts 4–6, the longest 20–60 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, open, 9–28 × 9–27 cm; primary branches 5–12, 3–17 cm; secondary branches 0.5–3 cm. Spikes broadly ovoid-pyramidal, 4–6 × 3–5 cm; axis 0.2–0.3 cm. Spikelets 8–20 per spike, mostly spreading, rather distant, linear, 8–40 × 0.8–1 mm, subterete; axis zigzag, winged, visible between glumes. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, rather distant, elliptic or oblong-ovate, 1.8–2 × 1–1.2 mm, apex obtuse to rounded-obtuse, sides membranous, 3–5-veined below keel, light to dark reddish brown, margins narrowly hyaline around apex, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical to cylindrical-ellipsoidal, trigonous, 1.5–1.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2256; Y. W. Lam 328, 761.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Vietnam, Africa, Australia, America.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Cyperus eleusinoides Kunth 穇穗莎草
Enum. Pl. 2: 39. 1837; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 139. 1961; FYN 15: 631. 2003; FGD 8: 325. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.
Cyperus nutans Vahl subsp. eleusinoides (Kunth) T. Koyama, Gard. Bull. Singapore 30: 136. 1977.
Cyperus nutans Vahl var. eleusinoides (Kunth) R.W. Haines, Bot. Bihar Orissa 5: 898. 1924.

Perennial; rhizome short, surculose. Culms stout, to 1 m tall, trigonous, smooth, base swollen, tuber-shaped, with leaves at basal part. Leaves shorter than culm; leaf blade 6–12 mm wide, flat, margin scabrous; sheath long, brown. Bracts 5–6, basal 2–3 longer than inflorescence. Anthelas compound or decompound, 6–12, to 18 cm, each with 3–6 anthelalets; anthelalets mostly to 4 cm, unequal in length. Spikes oblong to cylindrical, 1–3 cm × 4–10 mm, with very many spikelets, suberect. Spikelets polystichous, densely arranged, linear-oblong, 4–8 × ca. 2 mm, 6  2-flowered; rachilla winged, wings white hyaline, early deciduous. Glumes lax, ovate-elliptic, ca. 2 mm, pale and brown striate or brown, apex mucronate, membranous, apical margin white hyaline, veins 5–7, keel green. Stamens 3; anthers linear; connective prominent above anther. Style short; stigmas 3. Achene obovoid, trigonous, ca. 2/3 as long as scale, dark brown, surface densely and slightly prominently punctate.

Locality: Stonecutters Island, Port Shelter, New Territories. S. L. Thrower 1289 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Cyperus exaltatus Retz. 高稈莎草
Observ. Bot. 5: 11. 1789; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 130. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 242. 2000; FGD 8: 324. 2007; FOC 23: 230. 2010.

Rhizomatous perennial. Culms tufted, 60–180 cm tall, 6–10 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, up to 170 cm × 6–15 mm, acuminate, flattish-plicate; sheath purplebrown. Involucral bracts 4–6, the longest up to 70 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 15–27 × 17–30 cm; primary branches 5–9, 3–18 cm; secondary branches 0.5–5 cm, or spikes ± sessile clusters. Spikes erect-patent to patent, narrowly to broadly cylindrical, 2 – 5 × 0.7–1.5 cm; axis 1.5–4.8 cm. Spikelets 20–40, crowded, erect-patent to patent ± 2-ranked, oblong-lanceolate to linear, 4–10 × 1–2 mm, flattened; axis straight, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–2 × 1.2–1.5 mm, acute, mucronate, sides membranous, 3–5-veined, greenish to yellowish brown, keel pale to mid-brown. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm, connective minute. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to ellipsoidal-obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–0.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, yellowish brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Castle Peak, Hong Kong Wetland Park. Y. S. Lau 2275; S. C. Ng 986; HK sheet 40461.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Cyperus haspan L. 畦畔莎草
Sp. Pl. 1: 45. 1753; FHK 386. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 153. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 244. 2000; FYN 15: 639. 2003; FGD 8: 332. 2007; FOC 23: 227. 2010.

Annual or short-lived perennial; rhizome short to slightly long. Culms tufted or solitary, 10–40 cm tall, 0.5–2.2 mm thick, rather weak, sharply triquetrous, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, 2–20 cm × 2–5 mm, acute, flattish-plicate; sheath up to 6 cm, reddish purple to purplish. Involucral bracts 2–3, unequal, the longest up to 10 cm. Inflorescence simple to decompound, open to somewhat congested, 3–15 × 3–15 cm; primary branches 10–22, 1.2–10(–20) cm × 0.2–0.7 mm; secondary and tertiary branches 1–2.5 cm or 0. Spikelets 1 or in finger-like clusters of 3–6(–10), linear-oblong or linear-lanceolate, 5–10 × 1–2 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes ± oblong to elliptic-lanceolate or ovate, (1–)1.1–1.5 × 0.5–0.7 mm, at apex obtuse or mucronulate, straight to slightly recurved, sides membranous, pale brownish and often tinged with rusty brown or purplish brown, keel greenish or pale brown, 3-veined. Stamens 1–3; anthers narrowly oblong, ca. 0.5 mm, connective hispidulous. Style short, stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, sides ± flat, 0.4–0.5 × 0.4–0.5 mm, creamy yellow, verruculose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 159; HK sheet 38161, 42177.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Henan, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Cyperus imbricatus Retz. 疊穗莎草
Observ. Bot. 5: 12. 1788; FRPS 11: 131. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 244. 2000; FGD 8: 325. 2007; FOC 23: 231. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms 37–130 cm tall, 2–8 mm thick, indistinctly to distinctly trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, up to 60 × 5–15 cm, acuminate, flattish; sheath dark brown or reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest up to 60 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, 8–22 × 10–25 cm; primary branches 5–8, up to 15 cm; secondary branches 1–2 cm, spikes more usually in ± sessile clusters. Spikes erect-patent to patent, narrowly cylindrical, 1.5–4 × 0.3–0.9 cm, pale yellowish brown, axis 1.5–5 cm, winged, usually obscured by spikelets. Spikelets 50–70 or more, densely imbricate, suberect, lanceolate to linear-oblong, 3–6 × 1–2 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes 9 or more, in longest spikelets, ovate to ovate-oval, 1.2–1.8 × 1 mm, obtuse, recurved mucronate, sides membranous, 3-veined, yellowish brown, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.3 mm, connective minute. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to ± ovoid, trigonous, 0.6–0.8 × 0.4 mm, slightly obcompressed, yellowish.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2215; HK sheet 37122; 39386.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, India, Nepal, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Madagascar, Africa, America, SW Asia, Indian Ocean islands.
Ecology: Wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Cyperus involucratus Rottb. 風車草
Descr. Pl. Rar. 22. 1772; FGD 8: 330. 2007.
Cyperus alternifolius L. subsp. flabelliformis (Rottb.) Kük., Pflnanzenr. 4 (20, heft 101): 193. 1936; FRPS 11: 148. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 239. 2000; FYN 15: 637. 2003.

Perennial. Rhizome white, short, thick. Culms tufted, 0.5–1.8 cm tall, 3–10 mm thick, trigonous to ± terete at base, scabrous below inflorescence. Leaves bladeless, reduced to sheaths; sheaths 10–20 cm, pale greenish to yellow brown, apex obliquely truncate. Involucral bracts 15 or more, ± equal, 20–50 × 0.5–1.5 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 9–12 × 15–30 cm; primary branches many, ± equal, 7–10 cm, patent; secondary branches 1–1.5 cm. Spikelets in clusters of 3–10, oblonglanceolate to elliptic, flattened, 3–8 × 1.5–3 mm, densely 8–36-flowered, light green to rusty brown, the midrib green, axis straight. Glumes ovate, 1.8–2 × 1.2–1.5 mm, acute, sides membranous, 3–5-veined, pale green sometimes tinged with rusty brown, keel acute, greenish to pale brown. Stamens 3, anther linear, yellow, ca. 1 mm. Ovary trigonous, 0.5 mm; style ca. 1 mm, stigmas 3, ca. 1 mm. Achenes trigonous, broadly elliptic, ca. 0.5 mm wide, brown, reticulate-tuberculate, cell margin wavy; wave raised.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. H. C. Tang 2346; J. C. Shaw 895; HK sheet 32811.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong, Hunan, Taiwan; native to Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated in gardens. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cyperus flabelliformis Rottb. previously (Check List HK Plants 309. 2002; 109. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cyperus flabelliformis Rottb. previously (Check List HK Plants 309. 2002; 109. 2004).

records.text:
Cyperus iria L. 碎米莎草
Sp. Pl. 1: 45. 1753; FHK 386. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 143. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 245. 2000; FYN 15: 635. 2003; FGD 8: 329. 2007; FOC 23: 235. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent, roots fibrous. Culms 1–several, 8–60 cm tall, 2–3(–5) mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves 2–3 per culm; blade linear, 4–18 cm × 2–6 mm, flattish to weakly channelled; sheath 2–10 mm, reddish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest up to 40 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open, 5–20 × 3–15 cm; primary branches 3–7, 2–12(–15) cm; secondary branches very short or 0, the spikes in clusters of 35. Spikes broadly ovoid to oblong-ovate or linear-oblong, 1–5 × 0.2–0.7 cm; axis 1–2.5 cm. Spikelets spicately arranged, erectpatent, oblong-elliptic to linear-oblong, 9–13 × 1.6–2 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes obovate-orbicular, 0.7–1.3 × 1–1.5 mm, rounded to shallowly emarginate, mucronulate, sides thinly herbaceous, 3–5-veined, greenish to yellowish or midbrown, margins whitish-hyaline above, keel acute, green. Stamens 2–3; anthers 0.2–0.3 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 0.5–0.8 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1965; J. C. Shaw 507; K. L. Yip 4196.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia, Korea, Japan, Vietnam, India, Iran, N Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Cyperus malaccensis Lam. 茳芏
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 146. 1791; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 141. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 245. 2000; FGD 8: 327. 2007; FOC 23: 234. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome long-creeping. Culms 1–few, 60–180 cm tall, 7–12(–15) mm thick, smooth, sharply triquetrous. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths except for upper 1–3 leaves; blade linear, linear-lanceolate, 5–25 cm × 3–16 mm, acute or shortly acuminate, ± flattened; sheath 8–20 cm, greenish to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–4, the longest up to 30 cm × 8–15 mm. Inflorescence simple to compound, somewhat congested, subglobose, 2–10 × 4–15 cm; primary branches 3–8, unequal, 3–10 cm; secondary branches 0.3–1.6 cm. Spikes ovoid, 1–2.5 cm; axis 0.2–1 cm, smooth, glabrous. Spikelets 2–15 per spike, linear, 10–13 × 1.2–1.8 mm, subterete; axis straight. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, elliptic to ovate, 2–2.2 × 1–1.5 mm, obtuse, sides papery, indistinctly 5–7-veined around keel, glaucous and tinged or flecked with brown or dark reddish, the margins widely pale-membranous, keel rounded, brownish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical, trigonous, 1.7–2 × 0.5 mm, blackish brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Yuen Long, Castle Peak, Sha Po Tsuen, Lung Kwu Tan, Silver Mine Bay. Y. W. Lam 1590; HK sheet 39092, 39650.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Japan, Australia.
Ecology: Ditches or muddy places near estuary. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Weaving.

Cyperus malaccensis Lam. var. brevifolius Boeck. 短葉茳芏（鹹水草）
Linnaea 35: 604. 1867; FRPS 11: 141. 1961.
Cyperus malaccensis Lam. subsp. monophyllus (Vahl) T. Koyama, FTW ed. 2, 5: 246. 2000; FOC 23: 234. 2010.
Cyperus monophyllus Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 352. 1806.
Cyperus tegetiformis auct. non Roxb.: FKH 296. 1912.

Leaves blade short to very short, sometimes basalmost sheath bladeless. Involucral bracts shorter than inflorescence. Glumes not incurved.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Sha Tin, Castle Peak, Mai Po, Sai Kung, Nai Chung, Sam A Tsuen, Yung Shue O, Silver Mine Bay. J. C. Shaw 672; Y. S. Lau 1995; Y. W. Lam 682.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places near streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Ties, strings (clums).

Cyperus nutans Vahl 垂穗莎草
Enum. Pl. 2: 363. 1805; FRPS 11: 138. 1961; FYN 15: 631. 2003; FGD 8: 325. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1–few, 70–120(–150) cm tall, 4–10 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, 20–40 cm × 6–15 mm, acute, flattish-plicate, whitish below; sheath 10–30 cm, greenish to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 4–6, the longest 50–75 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, lax, 15–30 × 8–20 cm; primary branches 6–12, erect-patent, up to 30 cm; secondary branches 0.3 – 3.5 cm. Spikes subsessile, 6 × 1 cm, radically spreading. Spikelets 1.5–2 mm wide. Glumes up to 2.2 mm, more conspicuously mucronate, tinged with glaucous green. Stamens 3; anthers linear-oblong. Style very short; stigmas 3. Achenes obovate to broadly elliptic, 1–1.2 × 0.5–0.7 mm, rather abruptly narrowed to apiculate apex.

Locality: Tai Shui Hang. HK sheet 13120, 13122.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Cyperus nutans Vahl var. eleusinoides (Kunth) Haines previously (Check List HK Plants 88. 1993).

Cyperus orthostachyus Franch. & Sav. 三輪草
Enum. Pl. Jap. 218. 1879; FRPS 11: 145. 1961; FOC 23: 236. 2010.
Cyperus truncatus Turcz. ex Ledeb. var. orthostachyus (Franch. & Sav.) C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 218. 1903.

Annual, rhizome absent, with only fibrous roots. Culms slender, 8–65 cm tall, compressed triquetrous, smooth, with few leaves at basal part. Leaves shorter than or equalling culm; sheath brownish; leaf blade 3–6 mm wide, flat, margin scabrous. Bracts 3–4, leaf-shaped, very much longer than inflorescence or basalmost 1–2 longer than inflorescence, margin scabrous. Anthela simple, rarely compound; anthelas 5–11, mostly to 15(–20) cm, unequal in length, each with 1(–5) spike. Spikes ovate-oblong, broadly ovate, or oblong cylindrical in outline, 1–3.5 × 1–3 cm, with 5–32 or many spikelets. Spikelets slightly laxly or densely arranged, lanceolate to linear, 0.3–2.5 cm × 1–2 mm, obliquely spreading or suberect, sometimes level spreading after anthesis, 6–46-flowered; rachilla wings white, narrow, hyaline; glumes greyish brown, broadly ovate to elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, keel abaxially green, veins 5–7 and obscure, margin apically white hyaline, apex rounded to retuse and muticous. Stamens 3; anthers ellipsoidal, short; connective prominent above anther. Style short; stigmas 3, slightly short. Achene brown, obovoid, nearly as long as scale, trigonous, surface puncticulate, apex mucronate.

Locality: Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 1341.
Distribution: Chongqing, Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Shaanxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang; Japan, Korea, Russia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Cultivated. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cyperus papyrus L. 紙莎草
Sp. Pl. 47. 1753.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody. Culms 1–5 m tall, 2–4 cm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths. Involucral bracts up to 12, the longest 5–10 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 20–35 cm in diam.; primary branches many (up to 200 or more), ± equal, 10–30 cm; secondary branches up to 2 cm, spikes more usually in sessile clusters. Spikes cylindrical, 1–3 × 0.6–1 cm; axis 1.5–3 cm. Spikelets spreading, linear, 6–12 × 1 mm, subterete; axis straight, winged. Glumes 5–17 per spikelet, elliptic to ovateelliptic, 2–2.5 mm, obtuse, sides membranous, 3-veined below keel, light brownish, keel green. Stamens 3. Stigmas 3. Achenes ovoid, trigonous, 0.9–11 × 0.4–0.5 mm, greyish, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 42173.
Distribution: Native to tropical Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated in ponds or wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, paper making.

Cyperus pilosus Vahl 毛軸莎草
Enum. Pl. 2: 354. 1805; FHK 387. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 141. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000; FYN 15: 633. 2003; FGD 8: 326. 2007; FOC 23: 234. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome with long stolons. Culms 1–few, 25–28(–120) cm tall, 5–8 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth or scabrid on angles below inflorescence. Leaves few to several per culm; blade broadly linear, 13–47 cm × 6–13 mm, acute, flattish to plicate; sheath 3–10 cm, pale greenish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest up to 50 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to rather congested; primary branches 4–7(–10), 12–14(–20) cm; secondary branches 0.5–2 cm or spikes in ± sessile clusters. Spikes ± oblong, 2–3 × 1–2 cm; axis 1.5–3 cm, densely shortly hispid. Spikelets 5–25 per spike, rather distant, spreading, linearlanceolate to elliptic-oblong, 4–15 × 1–2 mm, flattened to subterete; axis straight. Glumes 5–9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate to broadly deltoid-ovate, 1.8–2.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, acute, often mucronulate, sides thinly papery to membranous, 5–7-veined, pale brown tinged with reddish brown, margins whitish-hyaline, keel obtuse, green, smooth. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–0.8 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly ellipsoidal to obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 0.5–0.8 mm, maturing dark brown, ± smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Castle Peak, Sheung Miu Tin, Tung Chung, Shui Hau. Y. W. Lam 2231; J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 163; HK sheet 39642.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Chongqing, Hunan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Xizang, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, C Asia, tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Cyperus platystylis R. Br. 盤柱莎草
Prodr. 214. 1810; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000; FOC 23: 224. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms 1–3, 30–90(–120) cm tall, 3–8 mm thick, triquetrous, scabrid on angles. Leaves ± equalling culm; blade linear, up to 90 cm × 5–12(–20) mm, long-acuminate, flattish-plicate, sheath light brown to purplish brown, Involucral bracts 4–12, unequal, the longest 30 – 80 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 7–20(–30) × 4–10 cm; primary branches 10–17, unequal, 2–10 cm; secondary branches up to 4 cm, arising along a short axis. Spikelets in finger-like clusters of 2–8, oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, 5–20 × 2.5–3 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes ovate to broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, subobtuse, mucronate, sides thickly membranous to herbaceous, greenish to brown. Stamens 3; anthers 1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical-ellipsoidal or cylindrical-ovoid, trigonous, laterally compressed, adaxial side concave, 1.7–2 × 0.8–1 mm, mid-brown with broad pale brown thickening on angles and apex, shiny, ± smooth.

Locality: Hong Kong. (fide H. G. Ye & S. L. Peng (eds.), Plant Div. Inventory of Guangdong 583. 2006)
Distribution: Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.

Cyperus procerus Rottb. 闊穗莎草
Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 29, t. 5, fig. 3. 1773; FKH 296. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000; FGD 8: 326. 2007; FOC 23: 235. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome with long stolons. Culms 1–few, 50–100(–150) cm tall, 4–7(–10) mm thick, smooth, triquetrous. Leaves surpassing culm; blade linear, up to 60–150 cm × 7–10(–15) mm, long-acute, often subtriquetrous toward apex, canaliculate; sheath 8–28 cm, pale greenish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 3 – 4, the longest 20 – 70 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, rather open, 10–15 cm × 8–12 cm; primary branches 3–7, 6–15(–20) cm; secondary branches up to 2 cm or spikes sometimes solitary. Spikes broadly ovoid, 2–4 cm; axis 2–3 cm, scabrid. Spikelets 4–8 per spike, rather distant, patent to spreading, oblong to linearlanceolate, 5–18 × 2.5–3.5 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, oval or ovate, 2.5–3 × 2–2.2 mm, sides membranous, 5–7-veined, pale brown to reddish brown, margins broadly white-hyaline near apex, keel obtuse, reddish brown, smooth. Stamens 3; anthers 1.2–1.8 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal, trigonous, 1.3–1.5 × 0.6–0.8 mm, maturing dark brown, ± smooth.

Locality: Yung Shue Au. S. C. Ng 4488.
Distribution: S & SW China; India, Vietnam, Malaysia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places near water. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.

Cyperus pygmaeus Rottb. 矮莎草
Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 20, pl. 14, fig. 4 – 5. 1773; FRPS 11: 157. 1961; FGD 8: 334. 2007; FOC 23: 228. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent, with fibrous roots. Culms tufted, 12–18 cm tall, compressed triquetrous, slightly concave on 3 sides, few leaved basally. Leaves shorter than culm; sheath reddish brown, short; leaf blade 2–2.5 mm wide, flat, apical margin and abaxially midvein spinulose. Involucral bracts 4–7, leaf-like, longer than inflorescence, ± horizontal to sometimes downwards reflexed. Inflorescences capitate, with many spikelets. Spikelets densely aggregated, narrowly oblong-ovoid to suboblong, 4–5 × ca. 1.5 mm, 10–15-flowered. Glumes distichous, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, yellowish white but medially rust brown and shortly striate, 3-veined, midvein green and apically forming a slight keel, apex acute and excurved mucronate. Stamen usually 1; anther short, linear; connective slightly prominent beyond anthers. Style short; stigmas 2(–3), longer than style. Achene oblong, 1–1.2 mm, 2/3–3/4 as long as subtending glume, lenticular with one flat and one convex side, minutely papillose.

Locality: Chek Keng. HK sheet 42208.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Mediterranean and E Africa through W Asia and India to SE Asia, Malesia and Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, wet places in sand.

Cyperus rotundus L. 香附子
Sp. Pl. 1: 45. 1753; FHK 387. 1861; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 134. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 250. 2000; FYN 15: 627. 2003; FGD 8: 328. 2007; FOC 23: 232. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome with stolons, terminated by a globose-ovoid tuber. Culms tuberous at base, 10–60 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves few, shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 60 cm × 2–5 mm, acuminate, flattish; sheath pale brown. Involucral bracts 2–3(–5), the longest usually equalling or shorter than inflorescence, 2–35 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, 3–8(–15) × 2–5(–10) cm; primary branches 2–10, 1–8(–12) cm; secondary branches (when present), 0.7–2 cm, spikes usually solitary. Spikes obovoid, 1.5–5 cm; axis 0.2–0.8 cm. Spikelets 3–10 per spike, suberect to patent, narrowly oblong to linear, 10–30 × 1.5–3 mm, flattened; axis ± straight, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 3–3.5 × 2 mm, obtuse, mucronate, ± recurved, sides membranous, 5–7-veined, reddish or slightly purplish brown with pale narrow hyaline margins, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical to obovoid-cylindrical, trigonous, 1.3–1.5 × 0.5–0.7 mm, brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2229; J. C. Shaw 432; HK sheet 37085.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cyperus stoloniferus Retz. 粗根莖莎草
Observ. Bot. 4: 10. 1786; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 134. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 251. 2000; FGD 8: 328. 2007; FOC 23: 231. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome long, thick, woody, base of shoot with ellipsoidal to ovoid tubers. Culms 1–2, 8–40 cm tall, 0.7–3 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, base swollen. Leaves usually shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 50 cm × 2–4 mm, acuminate, flattish to canaliculate; sheath pale brown, becoming fibrous. Involucral bracts 2–3, the longest 10–30 cm. Inflorescence simple, often congested, up to 6 × 6 cm; primary branches 2–5, 0.5–6 cm, spikes solitary. Spikes obovoid, 1.5–2.5 cm; axis 0.3 – 0.5 cm. Spikelets 3 – 8 per spike, suberect to patent, linear oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 6–15 × 1.5–2 mm, often weakly curved; axis slightly zigzag, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, broadly ovate, 2.2–2.7 × 2–2.3 mm, obtuse, mucronate, sides thickly membranous, 5–7-veined, pale brown to dark reddish brown, keel pale green. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 1 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Sai Kung, Castle Peak, Lamma Island, Lautau Island. J. C. Shaw 537; HK sheet 39434, 40719.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Pakistan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Madagascar, Indian Ocean islands, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and mudflats. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Cyperus tenuiculmis Bóeck. 四棱穗莎草（棱穗莎草）
Linnaea 30: 286. 1870; FTW ed. 2, 5: 251. 2000; FYN 15: 629. 2003; FGD 8: 328. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.
Cyperus zollingeri auct. non Steud.: FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 137. 1961; Check List HK Plants 311. 2002; 110. 2004.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1–few, 35–70(–90) cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaf blades narrowly linear, 9–28 × 0.2–0.6 cm, sharply acute, folded; sheath 2–16 cm, light brown. Involucral 2–7, the longest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence simple, lax, occasionally congested, up to 15 cm; primary branches 2–8, 1–16 cm; spikes solitary. Spikes ovoid, up to 5 cm; axis 0.5–1.3 cm. Spikelets 7–14 per spike, suberect to patent, often appearing ± finger-like, linear to linear-lanceolate, 10–30 × 1.5–2 mm, slightly flattened; axis zigzag, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate-elliptic to elliptic, 3.5–4 × 2–2.5 mm, apex obtuse to ± acute, sides papery, 7–9-veined, yellow brown to mid-brown, keel similar. Stamens 3; anthers 1–1.5 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes elliptic or obovate, triquetrous with concave sides, 1.7–2 × 0.8–1 mm, maturing blackish, minutely punctate.

Locality: Hong Kong.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Vietnam, Africa, Australia, America.
Ecology: Hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Notes: C. zollingeri Steud. is closely related and occurs in Peninsula Malaysia.

Cyperus tenuispica Steud. 窄穗莎草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 11. 1854; FRPS 11: 153. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 253. 2000; FGD 8: 332. 2007; FOC 23: 227. 2010. Cyperus flavidus C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 20: 287. 1883.

Annual or rarely short-lived perennial. Culms tufted, (3–)5–35 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 20 cm × 2–4 mm, acute, flat, soft; sheath up to 5 cm long, reddish brown to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 1–3, unequal, the longest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to rather congested, 3–10 × 3–10 cm; primary branches 5–10, 3–10 cm × 0.4–0.7 mm; secondary branches 0 or 0.4–2 cm. Spikelets 1 or in finger-like clusters of 2–9, linear-oblong, 3–12 × 1–1.5 mm, flattened; axis slightly zigzag. Glumes ovate to oblong-ovate, 0.8–1 × 0.5–0.8 mm, apex truncate or obtuse, shortly recurved-mucronate, straight to slightly recurved, sides membranous, veins inconspicuous, reddish brown or purplish brown, keel yellow green. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.2–0.4 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid-orbicular or ovoid, broadly trigonous, sides rounded, 0.3–0.5 × 0.2–0.3 mm, maturing white or creamy yellow, usually minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun. HK sheet 7831, 13127.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Taiwan; widely distributed in temperate and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Open grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Cyrtococcum patens (L.) A. Camus 弓果黍
Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 27: 118. 1921; FHN 4: 412. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 195, pl. 59: 10. 1990; FFJ 6: 200, fig. 167. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 465. 2000; FOC 22: 514. 2006; FGD 9: 409. 2009.
Panicum patens L., Sp. Pl. 1: 18. 1753; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms slender, smooth and glabrous, basal nodes branching and rooting, 15–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, glabrous or loosely pilose with tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–8 × 0.3–1 cm, pubescent on both surfaces or subglabrous, basal margins with a few long, stiff, tubercle-based hairs, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 0.5–1 mm, rounded. Panicle 5–15 cm, often diffuse, branches loosely ascending to widely spreading, very slender, glabrous; pedicels filiform, longer than spikelets. Spikelets purplish at maturity, 1–2 mm, varying from glabrous to appressed-pubescent or shortly hispid with stiff, conspicuously tubercle-based hairs; glumes 3-veined, the lower ovate, ca. 1/2 length of spikelet, the upper boat-shaped, 2/3 length of spikelet; lower lemma subequal to spikelet, 5-veined, margins ciliate, obtuse; upper lemma ca. 1.5 mm, gibbous convex, with a scar at apex; upper palea oblong, included in upper lemma.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1627; HK sheet 42007.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical Asia and Pacific islands (Polynesia).
Ecology: Moist places in forests and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.

Cyrtococcum patens (L.) A. Camus var. latifolium (Honda) Ohwi 散穗弓果黍
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11: 47. 1942; FRPS 10(1): 196, pl. 59: 9. 1990; FOC 22: 514. 2006; FGD 9: 410. 2009.
Panicum patens f. latifolium Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 37: 25. 1923.
Cyrtococcum accrescens (Trin.) Stapf, Hooker's Icon. Pl. 31(4): 2, t. 3096. 1922; FHN 4: 412. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 462, pl. 193. 2000; Check List HK Plants 330. 2002; 116. 2004.

It differs from var. patens by its culms up to 60 cm tall, leaf blades 7–15 × 1.2–2 cm; ligule 1–2 mm, panicle larger, 16–30 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1030, 1664; P. S. Choi 281.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Taiwan; India, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Malay Peninsula, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Moist places in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn to winter.

Dactyloctenium aegyptium (L.) Willd. 龍爪茅
Enum. Pl. 2: 1029. 1809; FHK 429. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 384. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 66, pl. 19. 1990; FFJ 6: 144, fig. 118. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 410. 2000; FOC 22: 481. 2006; FGD 9: 358, fig. 171. 2009.
Cynosurus aegyptius L., Sp. Pl. 1: 72. 1753.

Annual herb. Culms erect or ascending from the decumbent base, 15–70 cm tall. Leaf blades flat, 3–25 × 0.2–0.7 cm, tuberculatepilose on both surfaces, especially along the margins, apex acute or acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm, margin ciliate; leaf sheaths with ciliate margin. Inflorescence of 2–7(–9) stout digitate spikes. Spikelets broadly ovate, 3–4.5 mm, 3–4-flowered; glumes subequal, 1.5–2.2 mm; lower glume narrowly lanceolate, keel thick, hispidulous; upper glume elliptic to narrowly obovate, keel smooth, extended into a stout scabrid awn 1/2–2 times length of glume body; lemmas ovate, 2.6–4 mm, keel gibbous, hispidulous above middle, often extended into a stout cusp or mucro up to 1 mm; palea equal to lemma, tip 2-toothed. Anthers 3, 0.25–0.8 mm. Grain ca. 1 mm, broadly obtriangular, transversely rugose.

Locality: Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Fanling, Tai A Chau. HK sheet 39143, 41735, 42000.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions throughout the world.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, wastelands, roadsides and other weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Dactyloctenium aegyptium (L.) P. Beauv. previously (Check List HK Plants 330. 2002; 116. 2004).

Daemonorops jenkinsiana (Griff.) Mart. 黃藤
Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 327. 1853; FOC 23: 142. 2010.
Calamus jenkinsianus Griff., Calcutta J. Nat. Hist. 5: 81. 1845.
Calamus margaritae Hance, J. Bot. 12: 266. 1874; FKH 286. 1912.
Daemonorops margaritae (Hance) Becc., Rec. Bot. Surv. India 2: 220. 1902; FHN 4: 172, fig. 1074. 1977; FGD 2: 476, fig. 335. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 59. 1991; Check List HK Plants 295. 2002; 104. 2004.

Climbing rattan, or sometimes shrubby. Stems clustered, to 20 m or longer, 4–6 cm in diam., covered by spiny leaf sheaths. Leaves pinnate, 1.5–3 m; pinnae many, regularly arranged, linear or linearlanceolate, middle one 30–45 × 1.5–2 cm, adaxially bristly on veins; rachis apex elongate into a cirrus to 2 m, which armed with strong claw-like spines; sheath densely covered with brown to black hairs, spiny; spines sparsely distributed or in rows, black, flattened or needle-like; ocreas obscure; knees conspicuous. Inflorescences erect, spindly before blooming, 25–30 cm; prophyll boat-like, with flat and straight spines outside, branched 2–3 orders; bracts with few spines or not; male rachillla ca. 3 cm; male flowers oblongovoid, ca. 5 mm; calyx cup-like, slightly 3-fid; petals 3; female rachilla 2–4 cm, 4–7 flowers per side. Fruits globose, 1.7–2 cm in diam., brownish yellow, scales in 18–20 vertical rows, distinctly grooved in the middle, margins slightly dark; persistent sepals and petals flattened. Seed 1, subglobose, endosperm ruminate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Po, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1135; K. L. Yip 4190; HK sheet 7687.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Nepal, Bhutan, India, Bangladesh.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Materials (furniture, thatching).
Notes: The type specimen of Calamus margaritae (Hance Herb. No. 18407, BM) was collected by M. Dods from Wong Nai Chung Valley in Apr. 1874.

Notes: The type specimen of Calamus margaritae (Hance Herb. No. 18407, BM) was collected by M. Dods from Wong Nai Chung Valley in Apr. 1874.

Dahlia pinnata Cav. 大麗花（洋芍藥）
Icon. 1: 57. 1791; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 232. 1966; FRPS 75: 367. 1979; FGD 8: 129, fig. 65. 2007.

Perennial herbs with large tuberous fleshy roots; stem erect and stout, branched, 0.5–1.5(–2) m tall. Leaves 1– 3‑pinnate, some upper leaves simple; leaflets ovate or ovate‑oblong, both surfaces glabrous. Capitula large, 6–12 cm across, long pedunculate, usually nodding. Involucres hemispherical; outer phyllaries foliaceous, ovate‑elliptic; inner ones scarious, elliptic‑lanceolate. Marginal ligulate florets 1‑seriate or multi‑seriate in some cultivation, neutral, colour various, white, red or purple, ligule ovate, apex entire or minutely 3‑toothed. Central tubular florets many, bisexual and fertile, yellow in colour, apical half of corolla campanulate; some cultivars with all florets ligulate. Cypselae oblong, 9 – 12 × 3–4 mm, black, adaxial side flattened, abaxial side convex, apex rounded, 2 inconspicuous teeth at summit.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. H. Y. Yeung 172 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Dalbergia assamica Benth. 南嶺黄檀
Pl. Jungh. 2: 256. 1852; C. Niyomdham, Thai Fores. Bull (Bot.) 30: 126. 2002.
Dalbergia balansae Prain, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 70: 54. 1901; FRPS 40: 120. 1994; FGD 5: 226. 2003.

Tree, 6–15 m tall; bark greyish black, rough, longitudinally fissured. Leaves odd-pinnate, 10 – 15 cm; rachis and petioles pubescent; leaflets 13–15, papery, oblong or obovate-oblong, 2–4 × 2 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex rounded or nearly truncate, often emarginate, yellow brown pubescent when young, glabrescent at maturity. Panicles axillary, 5 – 10 cm. Calyx campanulate, 4 – 5 mm, sparsely net-veined, the upper 2 teeth subconnate, the lowest one longest, lanceolate. Corolla white, 6–7 mm, all petals clawed; vexillum orbicular, emarginate, with 2 appendages at base; wings obovate; keel sublunate. Stamens 10, diadelphous (5+5). Ovary hairy; ovules 3 – 4. Pods oblong, 5 – 6 × 2– 2.5 cm, 1– 2(–4)-seeded. Seeds reniform, 3.5 × 5 mm, flat.

Locality: Mount Parker, Stubbs Rd., Tsiu Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Kwu Tung, also cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1618, 2034; Y. W. Lam 1480.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam and Thailand.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: May – Oct.; fruiting: Sep.– Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Dalbergia balansae Prain previously (Check List HK Plants 142. 2002; 53. 2004).
