Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The type specimen of Adamia chinensis was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

records.text:
Dichrocephala integrifolia (L. f.) Kuntze 魚眼草
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 333. 1891; FTW ed. 2, 4: 933. 1998; FGD 8: 192, fig. 111. 2007.
Hippia integrifolia L. f., Suppl. Pl. 389. 1781.
Dichrocephala latifolia DC., Contr. Bot. India 2. 1834; Prodr. 5: 372. 1836; FHK 173. 1861; FKH 140. 1912.
Dichrocephala bicolor (Roth) Schltdl., Linnaea 25: 209. 1852; Li, FTW 4: 847. 1975.
Dichrocephala auriculata (Thunb.) Druce, Rep. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 4: 619. 1917; FRPS 74: 77, pl. 25: 1 – 3. 1985.

Annual herbs, 12–40 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, usually branched from the basal part, loosely pilose. Leaves ovate to elliptic, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, those in middle part 2–11 × 1–4.5 cm, lyrately lobed with the terminal lobe largest, up to 4.5 cm across, ovate, 1–2 pairs of lateral lobes, oblong to obovate, base attenuate to form winged petiole of 1–3 cm, apex acute to obtuse, leaf margin irregularly crenate‑serrate; leaves in lower and upper parts smaller in size, but similar in shape, with the lower ones less lobed. Capitula small, 2–3.5 mm across, globose, forming panicles terminal or axillary to the stem. Phyllaries in 1–2 series, ovate‑oblong, apex acute, margin slightly scarious and fimbriate, central part and midvein green in colour, outer phyllaries 1 mm, the inner ones slightly shorter. Receptacle globose with flattened top. Marginal florets in many series, corolla tubular, usually 2‑lobed, 0.3–0.5 mm, white. Disk florets few, corolla tubular, funnelform to campanulate, tetramerous, 1 mm, green. Cypselae obovate‑oblanceolate, compressed, thickened on both sides, glandular at apical region. Pappus lacking, or bearing 1–2 short bristles on cypselae of central florets.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 7620, 9617 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 517.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Abandoned cultivated fields, banks of paddy fields. Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dicliptera chinensis (L.) Juss. 狗肝菜
Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 9: 268. 1807; FHK 266. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FHN 3: 563. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 654. 1998; FRPS 70: 236. 2002.
Justicia chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 16. 1753.

Annual or biannual herbs, 30–80 cm tall. Stems diffuse at base, erect above, quadrangular, ridged, glabrous except for pubescent on young branches and nodes. Petioles to 0.5–3 cm, puberulent; leaf blades ovate‑elliptic, 2–8 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate or attenuate and decurrent onto the petiole, apex short acuminate or acute, margin entire or slightly undulate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely puberulent along the veins, lateral veins 4 – 5 pairs, slightly prominent abaxially. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, a dichasial 3‑flowered cyme, or sometimes several forming a short panicle, 1–4 cm. Peduncles 2–5 mm; pedicels 0.5–3 mm, puberulent. Bracts 2, large, unequal, elliptic or narrowly obovate, 8–13 × 3–5 mm, apex acute, mucronate, margin ciliate, abaxially puberulent, 3‑veined; bracteoles linear, ca. 5 mm, apex acuminate, abaxially hirsute. Calyx ca. 5 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes equal, linear, apex acuminate, margin hirsute. Corolla pale purple, 1–1.2 cm, outside puberulent; tube slender, ca. 6 mm; limb bilabiate, upper lip ovate, ca. 5 × 3 mm, apex entire, lower lip oblong, ca. 4 × 1.5 mm, shallowly 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, exserted, adnate near apex of corolla tube; filaments ca. 4 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae spherical, ca. 1.2 mm in diam., parallel, one above the other. Ovary pilose at the tip; style filiform, ca. 1.4 cm; stigma unequally 2‑lobed. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, apiculate, ca. 6 mm, puberulent, 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam., pubescent, verrucose.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Sha Tin, Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 2017; Y. S. Lau 2845.
Ecology: Roadsides, thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Didymostigma obtusum (C. B. Clarke) W. T. Wang 雙片苣苔
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 22: 189. 1984; FRPS 69: 273. 1990; FOC 18: 292. 1998; FGD 6: 261, pl. 144. 2005.
Chirita obtusa C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 5: 114. 1883.
Roettlera obtusa (C. B. Clarke) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 476. 1891.

Herbs, perennial. Stems erect, simple or branched, 10–30 cm tall, pubescent to densely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–4 cm, villose; leaf blade ovate, 2–12 × 1.5–7 cm, base sometimes slightly oblique, broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute to obtuse, margin crenate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially sparsely pubescent often with purple tinged spotted; lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Cymes axillary, 2–10‑flowered; peduncle 2–4 cm, pubescent; bracts 2, lanceolate‑linear, 3–6 mm, pubescent; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Calyx 5‑sect from base; segments linear, 7 – 10 mm, villose. Corolla white or purple‑blue, 3.5–5 cm, abaxially pubescent; tube slightly funnelform‑tubular, 3 – 3.5 cm, ca. 1 cm in diam.; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, lobes 5–7 mm; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes 0.9 – 1.2 cm, rounded. Stamens 2, glabrous, adnate to abaxial side of corolla tube near base, included; filaments slightly tortuous, ca. 1 cm; anther ca. 2 mm; staminodes 2, ca. 5 mm. Disk ring‑like, entire. Pistil sparsely pubescent; ovary linear, ca. 2 cm; style ca. 1 cm; stigma 2. Capsule 4–8 cm. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po Kau, Ho Pui. L. T. Lo 416; Y. W. Lam 1149; HK sheet 35341.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, shaded streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Digitaria ciliaris (Retz.) Koeler 纖毛馬唐（升馬唐）
Descr. Gram. 27. 1802; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 196, fig. 40. 1971; FRPS 10(1): 326, pl. 102: 1–3. 1990; FFJ 6: 234, fig. 201. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 466. 2000; FOC 22: 543. 2006; FGD 9: 438. 2009.
Panicum ciliare Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 16. 1786.

Annual herb. Culms ascending from decumbent base, branching and rooting at lower nodes, 20–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, ± tubercle-based pilose; leaf blades linear to lanceolate, 3–25 × 0.2–1 2 cm, adaxial surface usually pilose, margins thickened and scabrous; ligule membranous, 13 mm. Inflorescence digitate or subdigitate, axis short; racemes 3–12, 5–17 cm; spikelets paired; rachis winged, ca. 1 mm wide, margins scabrous (serrate). Spikelets lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 mm, suppressed on one side of rachis; pedicels unequal, triangular, serrate; lower glume very small, triangular; upper glume lanceolate, 1/2–4/5 length of spikelet, narrow, margins ciliate, 3-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined, veins evenly spaced or a broader glabrous interspace flanking the midvein, lateral interveins appressed pubescent to ciliate or villous; upper lemma elliptic, as long as spikelet, coriaceous, apex acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1693, 2252; Y. W. Lam 1064.
Distribution: Widely spread over almost all provinces of China; and throughout the tropics and subtropics, but rare in Africa.
Ecology: Roadsides, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Digitaria cruciata (Nees ex Steudel) A. Camus 十字馬唐
Lecomte, Fl. Indo-Chine. 7: 399. 1922; FRPS 10(1): 329. 1990; FYN 9: 553. 2003; FOC 22: 543. 2006.
Panicum cruciatum Nees ex Steudel, Syn. Pl. Glum. 1: 39. 1853.

Annual herb. Culms decumbent at base, branching and rooting at lower nodes, 30–100 cm tall, nodes thinly hispid. Leaf sheaths glabrous or hispid, usually shorter than internode; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.3–1 cm, papillose-hispid on both surfaces or adaxial surface glabrous, margins thickened, undulate, scabrous; ligule 1–2.5 mm. Inflorescence subdigitate, axis 1–5 cm; racemes 5–8, 3–15 cm; spikelets paired, imbricate; rachis winged, ca. 1 mm broad, midrib triquetrous, margins slightly scabrous. Spikelets plumply elliptic-oblong, 2.5–3 mm, ca. 1.2 mm broad; lower glume minute, veinless; upper glume broadly ovate, 1/3 as long as spikelet, 3-veined, subglabrous, margins membranous, apex broadly obtuse; lower lemma slightly shorter than upper lemma, 7-veined with intervein spaces nearly equidistant, glabrous or margins pilose; upper lemma pale purplish grey at maturity, apex abruptly apiculate, exserted from spikelet.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 627.
Distribution: Hubei, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; India, Sikkim, Nepal.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Digitaria fibrosa (Hack.) Stapf 纖維馬唐
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1912: 428. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 312. 1990; FFJ 6: 230, fig. 196. 1995; FOC 22: 541. 2006; FGD 9: 434. 2009.
Panicum fibrosum Hack., Oesterr. Bot. Z. 51: 330. 1901
Digitaria setifolia auct. non Stapf: FKH 314. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 20–50 cm tall, girthed at base by fibrous remains of old leaf sheaths. Leaf sheaths pilose at lower part and mouth; leaf blades linear, flat or involute, 3  0 × 0.25–0.4 cm, pilose or subglabrous, apex acuminate, terminal blade short and small; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, membranous, truncate. Inflorescence subdigitate, axis usually glabrous; racemes 2–5, alternating; spikelets paired or ternate or solitary in the upper, loosely arranged; rachis slenderly triquetrous, smooth, glabrous, not winged; pedicels tips slightly swollen. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, 3–3.5 mm; lower glume very small, subrounded or broad triangular; upper glume ca. 4/5 length of spikelet but narrow, pallid yellow-brown, 3-veined, pilose between veins and margins; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined, hairiness variable, usually glabrous on either side of midvein, 2nd intervein space and margins usually pilose, acuminate; upper lemma slightly shorter than or equal to spikelets.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 20646.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; Laos, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Digitaria henryi Rendle 亨利馬唐
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 323. 1904; FRPS 10(1): 325. 1990; FFJ 6: 233. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 467, pl. 194. 2000; FOC 22: 543. 2006; FGD 9: 437. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, slender, creeping and often rooting at base, 20–50 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 3–8 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or sparingly hispid near base; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence subdigitate, axis short; racemes 3–10, 3–8 cm; spikelets lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, paired; rachis flat, winged, ca. 0.5 mm broad. Spikelets lanceolate, 2–3 mm, acuminate; lower glume ca. 0.2 mm; upper glume lanceolate, 1/2 as long as spikelet, 3 – 5-veined, margins pubescent; lower lemma slightly longer than upper lemma, 7-veined with broader intervein spaces flanking the midvein, pilose along lateral intervein spaces and margins; upper lemma subleathery, acuminate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41963, 42009.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, naturalized in Hawaii.
Ecology: Grassy fields, sandy seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Digitaria heterantha (Hook. f.) Merr. 二型馬唐
Enum. Philipp. Fl. Pl. 1: 54. 1923; FHN 4: 433. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 332, pl. 104. 1990; FFJ 6: 231, fig. 198. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 467. 2000; FOC 22: 541. 2006; FGD 9: 435, fig. 224. 2009.
Paspalum heteranthum Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 7: 16. 1896[1897], based on Panicum heteranthum Nees & Meyen (1841) not Link (1827).
Panicum barbatum auct non (Willd) Kunth: FHK 410. 1861.
Digitaria barbata auct. non Willd.: FKH 314. 1912.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms branching and rooting at lower nodes, 50–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, subcompressed, glabrous to papillose-pilose, densely pilose at the base; leaf blades broadly linear, 5–15 × 0.3–0.6 cm, glabrous to papillose-pilose on both surfaces; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–4, 5–25 cm, the lower ± bare; rachis triquetrous, thick, rigid, winged. Spikelets paired, ca. 4 mm, pedicellate one villous, sessile one glabrous, rather far apart on rachis, lanceolate; lower glume very small, veinless; upper glume lanceolate, more than 1/2 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined, margins glabrous or ciliate above 1/3–1/2 in sessile spikelet, appressed pubescent in pedicellate spikelet; lower lemma glabrous in sessile spikelet and with spreading hairs in pedicellate spikelet, 5–9-veined, veins equally distant, thick, prominent, interspaces slit-like, acuminate; upper lemma lanceolate, pale and ± leathery, acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42048, 42049.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Digitaria longiflora (Retz.) Pers. 長花馬唐
Syn. Pl. 1: 85. 1805; FKH 314. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 308, pl. 95: 6–10. 1990; FFJ 6: 229. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 469. 2000; FOC 22: 546. 2006; FGD 9: 433. 2009.
Paspalum longiflorum Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 15. 1786.
Paspalum brevifolium Fluegge, Gram. Monogr. Paspalum 150. 1810; FHK 408. 1861.

Perennial herb, usually with slender stolons. Culms slender, glabrous, 10–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, pubescent or glabrous; leaf blades broadly linear to lanceolate, 1–5 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or papillose-pilose at base; ligule membranous, 1–1.5 mm, ± truncate. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–4, 2–8 cm, usually curving outward; rachis ribbon-like, winged, 0.5–0.8 mm wide, winged; pedicels cylindrical, smooth, with discoid tips. Spikelets elliptic, 1.2–1.5 mm, minutely pubescent near margins, acuminate; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as spikelet, 3–5-veined, back and margins densely appressed-pubescent; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, glabrous between middle and lateral veins, otherwise pubescent; upper lemma yellowish brown, apex acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 628, 2249; HK sheet 41978.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Old World tropics, America.
Ecology: Grassy fields, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Digitaria radicosa (J. Presl) Miq. 紅尾翎
Fl. Ned. Ind. 3: 437. 1857; FRPS 10(1): 325. 1990; FFJ 6: 233. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 470. 2000; FOC 22: 542. 2006; FGD 9: 437. 2009.
Panicum radicosum J. Presl, Reliq. Haenk. 1: 297. 1830.
Digitaria tenuispica Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(253): 326–327. 1904; FKH 314. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms slender, prostrate at base, branching, 20–50 cm tall, glabrous, lower nodes rooted. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, usually glabrous or pubescent; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 2–8 × 0.2–0.7 cm, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface scabrous, pubescent or papillose-pilose at base; ligule membranous, truncate, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–3(–4), slender, 4–10 cm; rachis triquetrous, narrowly winged, margins smooth or almost so or slightly scabrous; spikelets narrowly lanceolate, 2.8–3 mm, acute or acuminate, paired, one pedicellate and other very shortly pedicellate or subsessile; lower glume triangular, 0.2–0.3 mm; upper glume lanceolate, 1/3–2/3 length of spikelet, villous, 1–3-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, a broad intervein space on either side of midvein, lateral veins very close together near margin, lateral veins and margins pilose; upper lemma yellowish at maturity, narrowly lanceolate, thicken papery. Anthers 0.5–1 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. HK sheet 40844, 41962, 42030.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Malesia, Australia, Indian Ocean islands, Madagascar.
Ecology: Moist weedy places, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Digitaria sanguinalis (L.) Scop. 馬唐
Fl. Carniol. ed. 2, 1: 52. 1771; FKH 314. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 329, pl. 103: 7–9. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 470. 2000; FOC 22: 542. 2006; FGD 9: 436, fig. 225. 2009.
Panicum sanguinale L., Sp. Pl. 1: 57. 1753; FHK 410. 1861.
Panicum commutatum auct. non (Schult. f.) Nees: FHK 410. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms erect or ascending from decumbent base, 10–100 cm tall, glabrous or hairy at nodes. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, glabrous or sparsely papillose-pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.3–1.2 cm, glabrous or pilose, base rounded, margins thickened, scabrous; ligule 1–3 mm, membranous, obtuse. Inflorescence digitate or subdigitate, axis 1–2 cm; racemes 4–12, stiff, 5–18 cm, upper alternating or digitate, the base subverticillate; rachis winged, margins scabrous. Spikelets usually paired, one pedicellate and other sessile or shortly pedicellate, elliptic-lanceolate, 3–3.5 mm, acute; lower glume small, triangular, veinless; upper glume lanceolate, 1/3–3/4 spikelet length, 3-veined, pubescent, margins ciliate; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, veins evenly spaced or a broader interspace flanking the midvein, midvein smooth, lateral veins setiform-scabrous especially toward the apex, appressed-pubescent on lateral intervein spaces and margins; upper lemma greenish grey, as long as spikelet, subcoriaceous, lanceolate, apex acuminate.

Locality: Tuen Mun. HK sheet 14537, 34217.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; warm-temperate subtropical regions throughout the world.
Ecology: Roadsides, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Digitaria setigera Roth ex Roem. & Schult. 海南馬唐
Syst. Veg. 2: 474. 1817; FRPS 10(1): 324, pl. 101: 6 – 9. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 471, pl. 195. 2000; FOC 22: 542. 2006; FGD 9: 436. 2009.
Digitaria microbachne Henrard, Mede. Rijks-Herb. 61: 13. 1930; Check List HK Plants 332. 2002; 116. 2004.

Annual or perennial herb. Culms tufted, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, 30–100 cm tall, many noded, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or papillose-pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.3–1.2 cm, glabrous on both surfaces, papillose-pilose at base, base subrounded, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence digitate or subdigitate, axis 1–4 cm; racemes 5–12, stiff, 5–15 cm; spikelets paired; rachis triquetrous, narrowly winged, margins scabrous. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate-oblong, 2–3 mm, acute; lower glume absent or a minute rim; upper glume up to 1/3 length of spikelet, 1–3-veined or veinless, margins ciliate; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, veins evenly spaced or with a wider interspace flanking the midvein, lateral intervein spaces and margins appressed pubescent to villous, rarely ciliate or setose; upper lemma yellowish to grey, subequalling lower lemma, acuminate.

Locality: Happy Valley. HK sheet 33912, 41964, 42031.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Digitaria violascens Link 紫馬唐
Hort. Berol. 1: 229. 1827; FRPS 10(1): 308, pl. 95: 1–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 229, fig. 194. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 471, pl. 196. 2000; FOC 22: 547. 2006; FGD 9: 434. 2009.
Digitaria violascens Link var. villosa Keng, Sunyatsenia 3: 19. 1935.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, 20–50(–70) cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths mostly shorter than internode, glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–15 × 0.2–0.7 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose at base and mouth, margins scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous. Inflorescence subdigitate; racemes (2–)4–7(–10), ascending, 3–14 cm; rachis slightly scabrous; pedicels scabrous, with discoid tips. Spikelets elliptic, 2 or 3 per node, 1–2.5 mm; lower glume absent; upper glume lanceolate, slightly shorter than spikelet, 3-veined, intervein spaces and margins appressed-pubescent; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, intervein spaces and margins pubescent, but usually glabrous flanking the middle vein; upper lemma dark brown or blackish purple at maturity, as long as spikelet, coriaceous, apex acute.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 8293, 30738, 31899.
Distribution: Widely spread over C to S and E to W China; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Australia, S America.
Ecology: Grassy hillsides, roadsides, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Dimeria falcata Hack. 鐮形觿茅
Monogr. Phan. 6: 85. 1889; FKH 320. 1912; FFJ 6: 236, fig. 203. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 177, pl. 42: 1–9. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 538, pl. 227. 2000; FOC 22: 615. 2006; FGD 9: 453. 2009.
Dimeria falcata Hack. var. tenuior Keng & Y. L. Yang, J. Nanjing Univ., Nat. Sci. ed. 1980(4): 106. 1980.
Dimeria fuscescens auct. non Trin.: FHK 419. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms erect, tufted, 20–70 cm tall. Leaf sheaths hirsute with short tubercle-based hairs or glabrous at base, the lower longer than internode and the upper shorter than internode; leaf blades dark green or reddish, linear, 4–20 × 0.2–0.3 mm, hirsute, apex finely acuminate; ligule 0.4–0.5 mm. Racemes 2–3, digitate, slightly curved; rachis flattened, margin scabrid or white-ciliate. Spikelets solitary, alternating, reddish brown or nearly purplish, linear-oblong, laterally compressed, base bearded; glumes papery, lower glume ca. 2.8 mm, chartaceous, dorsally keeled and ciliate, 1-veined; upper glume keeled, white-pilose near margins and on keel, margins broadly scabrous, apex acute; lower lemma oblanceolate, membranous, hyaline, 1-veined, upper margins ciliate; upper lemma shorter than upper glume, oblonglanceolate, hyaline membranous, 2-lobed, a slender awn exserted from the sinus; awn 7–10 mm, geniculate; upper palea absent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lower Shing Mun, Wang Shan Keuk. HK sheet 41943, 41947, 42005.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Moist grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

Dimeria ornithopoda Trin. 觿茅
Fund. Agrost. 167. 1820; FFJ 6: 235, fig. 202. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 171, pl. 42: 20. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 540. 2000; FOC 22: 615. 2006; FGD 9: 452, fig. 234. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect or geniculate at base, glabrous, 3–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths keeled, with scattered tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear, soft, 1.5–5 × 0.1–0.3 cm, hispid with scattered tubercle-based hairs or glabrescent, acuminate; ligule 0.5–1 mm, ciliate at the apex. Racemes 2–3, subdigitate, ascending at first, then divergent; rachis triquetrous, flexuose or straight linear, scabrid on angles; pedicels glabrous, alternate in one side of rachis. Spikelets linear-oblong or narrow elliptic, strongly laterally compressed, usually purple or reddish brown; glumes herbaceous with broad scarious margins, sometimes with a few long stiff hairs near apex of keel, or stiffly pilose throughout, keel usually wingless, occasionally upper glume narrowly winged, with rounded midline or sharply keeled apex; lower lemma shorter than spikelet, extremely compressed, dorsally scabrid, stiffly pilose throughout, margins thin, acute; upper lemma as long as spikelet; laterally compressed, margin hyaline membranous, acute, 2-lobed, an slender awn from the sinus; awn geniculate; upper palea absent; stamens 2; styles 2. Caryopsis linear-oblong.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. W. Lam 470, 1320; HK sheet 41993.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, India, Malaysia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Streamsides and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Dimeria sinensis Rendle 華觿茅
Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 359. 1904; FKH 320. 1912; FFJ 6: 236. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 181, pl. 44: 1–9. 1997; FOC 22: 616. 2006; FGD 9: 453. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect, 12–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths hispid with tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear, 1.5–9 × 0.2–0.4 cm, setose with tubercle-based bristles; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, dry membranous. Raceme solitary, slightly flexuous, margins densely short ciliate; rachis flat, margins narrowly winged, densely ciliate with white silky hairs, white bearded on outer margin. Spikelets reddish brown or purplish brown, oblong, callus short and truncate, bearded; lower glume slightly shorter than spikelet, keel densely bearded, margins and flank densely or sparsely white-ciliate, below the apex with sparsely hispid hairy near margins, acute; upper glume as long as spikelet, glabrous or sparsely ciliate, sharply keeled, margins hyaline membranous, silky-white villous near margin, apex acute keel with broadly wings; lower lemma lanceolate, hyaline membranous, margins sparsely ciliate, veinless; upper lemma hyaline membranous, 2-lobed, with an awn from the sinus, upper palea absent; awn geniculate in the middle, column twisted, yellowish brown; stamen 2; anthers ca. 1 mm; style base short, connate. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. F. W. Xing 9600; HK sheet 39423, 41952.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Thailand.
Ecology: Moist places on hillsides, roadsides and grassy fields.

Dimocarpus longan Lour. 龍眼
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 233. 1790; FYN 1: 266, pl. 63: 1– 2. 1977; FRPS 47(1): 28, pl. 9. 1985; FFJ 3: 317, fig. 215. 1987; FGD 1: 245, fig. 270. 1987.
Euphoria longan (Lour.) Steud., Nomencl. Bot. 1: 328. 1821; FHN 3: 83. 1974.
Euphoria longana Lam., Encycl. 3(1): 574. 1792; FTW ed. 2, 3: 602. 1993.
Nephelium longana Cambess., Mem. Mus. Hist. Nat. 18: 30. 1829; FKH 66. 1912.

Tree, usually ca. 10 m tall. Branches strong, puberulous, with scattered glaucous lenticels. Leaves 15–30 cm or longer including the petiole; leaflets (3–)4–5(–6) pairs; petiolules less than 5 mm; blades thinly leathery, oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 6–15 × 2.5–5 cm, base extremely asymmetrical, apex acute, sometimes slightly obtuse, abaxially powdery green, adaxially deep green and shiny, both surfaces glabrous; lateral veins 12–15 pairs, prominent abaxially. Inflorescences terminal or axillary near apex, large, many-branched, densely stellate hairy. Pedicels short. Sepals triangular-ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, subleathery, both surfaces brownish yellow tomentose with tufts of stellate hairs. Petals milky-white, lanceolate, nearly as long as sepals, only pilosulose abaxially. Filaments hirsute. Fruit usually yellowish brown or sometimes greyish yellow, subglobose, 1.2–2.5 cm in diam., abaxially slightly rugose, or with few slightly prominent tubercles. Seeds brown, shining, with fleshy arillode.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 146; HK sheet 6012, 10710.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring and summer; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Fruit, timber.

Dioscorea alata L. 參薯
Sp. Pl. 2: 1033. 1753; FHN 4: 152. 1977; FRPS 16(1): 117, pl. 37: 1–6. 1985; FFJ 6: 550. 1995; FOC 24: 296. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 88. 2000; FGD 6: 395, fig. 236. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 11, fig. 1, 2. 2009.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers variable, globose, conical or cylindrical, usually branched. Stem twining to right, glabrous, with 4 narrow ridges or membranous wings, sometimes prickly at base, usually bearing bulblets in leaf axils. Leaves alternate, but opposite distally on stem, simple; petiole green or purplish red, 3–10(–15) cm; leaf blade papery, ovate to triangular-ovate, 6–15(–20) × 3–13 cm, base sagittate to deeply cordate, apex shortly acuminate or caudate, glabrous on both surfaces, green or purplish red; basal veins 5–7. Male spikes solitary or a few together, 1.5–4 cm, sometimes forming a panicle to 20 – 30 cm; rachis ± zigzagged; male flowers light green, outer perianth lobes broadly ovate, 1.5–2 mm; stamens 6. Female spikes solitary or 2–3 together in leaf axils. Female flowers with 6 staminodes; ovary glabrous. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate, sometimes obcordate lobes, 1.5–2.5 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 10.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical area.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Food.

Dioscorea benthamii Prain & Burkill 大青薯（邊氏薯蕷）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 4: 448. 1908; FRPS 16(1): 108, pl. 33: 17–19. 1985; FFJ 6: 549. 1995; FOC 24: 294. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 89. 2000; FGD 6: 397. 2005.
Dioscorea oppositifolia auct. non L.: FHK 367. 1861.

Herbaceous twining vines, glabrous throughout, with tuberous rootstock. Stem twining to right, slender, to 20 m. Leaves papery, usually opposite, simple; petiole 0.5–2 cm; leaf blade obovate-oblong or oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 2–7(–9) × 0.7–4 cm, base rounded, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, abaxially whitish; basal veins 3or5(or7). Male spikes solitary or 2–3 together in leaf axils, 2–3 cm, or forming short panicles; rachis obviously zigzagged; male flowers sessile; bracts and perianth lobes purplish brown dotted; stamens 6. Female spikes usually solitary or paired, 3–10 cm; female flowers subsessile, bracts ovate, apex acuminate; outer perianth lobes broadly ovate; staminodes 6. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate lobes, ca. 1.5 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak. Y. W. Lam 284, 751; HK sheet 41994.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected from Little Hong Kong, Happy Valley and Tai Tam between 1878 and 1879.

Dioscorea bulbifera L. 黃獨
Sp. Pl. 2: 1033. 1753; FKH 276. 1912; FHN 4: 151. 1977; FRPS 16(1): 88, pl. 26: 1–5. 1985; FFJ 6: 545. 1995; FOC 24: 287. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 89. 2000; FGD 6: 395. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 25, fig. 9, 10. 2009.
Dioscorea sativa auct. non L.: FHK 368. 1861; FKH 276. 1912.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers usually solitary, globular to pyriform, 4–10 cm thick, with black cork and many fibrous roots. Stem twining to left, glabrous, smooth, bearing bulblets in axils of leaves. Leaves alternate, simple; petiole 2.5–12 cm; leaf blade broadly cordate, 5–15(–26) × 4–14(–26) cm, apex caudate-acuminate, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous. Male spikes usually clustered in leaf axils, drooping, sometimes forming panicles, 3–10 cm or longer; male flowers solitary, ± contiguous along rachis; perianth purple; stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth, filaments nearly as long as anthers. Female spikes often 2 or more together, similar to male ones, 20–50 cm; female flowers sessile, erect; staminodes 6. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblong-orbicular lobes, 1.5–3 cm, straw-coloured, densely purplish dotted, glabrous, base and apex rounded. Seeds inserted near apex of capsule, dark brown, winged toward base.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Sham Tseng, Ta Kwu Ling. P. S. Choi 522; F. W. Xing 7396; HK sheet 40753.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Bhutan, Africa, Oceania.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets, ravines, river banks. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dioscorea cirrhosa Lour. 薯莨
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 625. 1790; FRPS 16(1): 108, pl. 34: 1–4. 1985; FFJ 6: 551, fig. 484. 1995; FOC 24: 294. 2000; FGD 6: 396. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 29, fig. 11, 12. 2009.
Dioscorea rhipogonoides Oliv., Hooker's Icon. Pl. t. 1868; FKH 276. 1912.
Dioscorea matsudae Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 96. 1896; FTW ed. 2, 5: 96. 2000.

Twining vines, glabrous throughout; tubers variable in shape, globose, ovoid, oblong or gourd-shaped, very hard; cork dark brown; transverse section light brown or red, purplish black when dry. Stem twining to right, to 18 m or longer, almost woody, prickly at base. Leaves alternate on the lower part of stem, opposite on the upper part of stem, simple; petiole 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate to linear, 5–20 × 0.6–14 cm, leathery, base rounded, sometimes triangular lobed, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire, adaxially dark green, abaxially whitish, basal veins 3 or 5, reticulate veins prominent. Male spikes axillary, forming panicles of 2–14 cm or longer; rachis straight; male flowers with 6 stamens. Female spike solitary, to 10 cm. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate lobes, 2–3.5 cm, base emarginate, attenuate into pedicel ca. 7 mm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2472; Y. W. Lam 14; K. L. Yip 4098.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets on mountain slopes, and in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Material (tannin, dye), medicinal (folklore).

Dioscorea fordii Prain & Burkill 山薯
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 4: 450. 1908; FKH 276. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 114, pl. 36: 5 – 10. 1985; FFJ 6: 554, fig. 488. 1995; FOC 24: 295. 2000; FGD 6: 398. 2005.
Dioscorea batatas auct. non Decne: FHK 368. 1861; FKH 276. 1912.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers vertical, cylindrical; cork brown. Stem twining to right, glabrous, prickly at base. Leaves papery, simple, alternate on lower part of stem, opposite on upper part of stem; petioles 3–6 cm; leaf blade broadly lanceolate, oblong-ovate to elliptic-ovate, 5–12 × 2.5–8.5 cm, base sagittate or hastate to deeply cordate or rounded, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; basal veins 5 or 7, outermost ones near margin. Male spikes axillary, solitary or 2–4 together, 1.5–3 cm, or forming panicles to 40 cm; rachis zigzagged; male flowers sessile; outer perianth lobes broadly ovate, 1.5–2 mm, inner ones obovate, narrower but thicker than outer; stamens 6. Female spike often solitary, to 25 cm in fruit. Capsule of 3 flat, wing-like oblate lobes, 1.5–3 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 766; L. T. Lo 314; HK sheet 40826.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The syntype specimens (C. Ford 6, K. Wong 659, Lamont 758, K) were collected from Hong Kong Island and Lantau Island between 1851 and 1890s.

Dioscorea futschauensis Uline ex R. Knuth 福州薯蕷
Pflanzenr. 87(IV. 43): 264. 1924; FRPS 16(1): 73, pl. 20: 1–4. 1985; FFJ 6: 548, fig. 481. 1995; FOC 24: 282. 2000; FGD 6: 393, fig. 235. 2005.

Herbaceous twining vines; rhizomes horizontal, irregularly cylindrical, hard, cork yellowish brown. Stem twining to left, glabrous. Leaves alternate, simple, ± leathery; petiole 4–5 cm; leaf blade ovate-triangular in outline, to 10 × 11 cm, base deeply cordate, apex acuminate, uniformly hispidulous, densely so abaxially, reticulate veins prominent; leaves on lower part of stem palmately 7-lobed; lobes variable in size, those on upper part of stem margin entire or slightly undulate. Male spikes axillary, usually forming panicles; male flowers solitary or occasionally paired; pedicel 1–1.5 mm; perianth orange, 4–5 mm, 6-lobed; lobes oblong-ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex rounded; stamens 6, sometimes only 3 developed. Female spikes to 7 cm, few-flowered; female flowers with staminodes; ovary oblong-ellipsoidal. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like broadly obovoid lobes, 1.5–1.8 × 1–1.2 cm, base rounded, apex slightly emarginate to truncate, dark brown, not shiny. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, 4–5 mm in diam. (excluding wing), winged all round.

Locality: Ping Chau. F. W. Xing 9098; Y. W. Lam 275.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests, mountain slopes, ravines. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dioscorea hamiltonii Hook. f. 褐苞薯蕷
Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 295. 1892; Prain & Burkill, J. Proc. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 10: 39. 1914; R. Knuth, Pflanzenr. 4, 43: 266. 1924; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1.): 63, fig. 33, 34. 2009.
Dioscorea persimilis Prain & Burkill, J. Proc. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 4: 454. 1908; FKH 276. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 114, pl. 37: 7–12. 1985; FFJ 6: 552, fig. 486. 1995; FOC 24: 295. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 96. 2000; FGD 6: 398. 2005; Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 128. 2004.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers cylindrical, cork yellowish brown. Stem twining to right, glabrous, often 4–8-ridged. Leaves papery, simple, alternate on lower part of stem, opposite on upper part of stem; leaf blade orbicular, ovate, or triangular to elliptic-ovate, 3–13 × 1.5–8 cm, base sagittate or hastate or deeply or broadly cordate, apex acute, acuminate, or caudate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, reddish brown when dry; basal veins 7 or 9, reticulate veins prominent. Male spikes axillary, solitary or 2–4 together, 1–4 cm, usually forming panicles to 40 cm; rachis obviously zigzagged; male flowers sessile; bracts and outer perianth lobes brown spotted; stamens 6. Female spikes solitary or paired, to 20 cm in fruiting time; female flowers subsessile; staminodes small. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate lobes, 1.5–2.5 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Sai Kung, Man Kam To, Tai A Chau. S. P. Lau 160; P. S. Choi 288; HK sheet 40256.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed forests, thickets, on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.; fruiting: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dioscorea hispida Dennst. 白薯莨
Schlussel Hortortus Malab. 15, 33. 1818; FRPS 16(1): 99, pl. 31: 1–5. 1985; FFJ 6: 543, fig. 477. 1995; FOC 24: 290. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 93. 2000; FGD 6: 392. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 67, fig. 35, 36. 2009.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers ovoid or irregularly shaped and variable in size. Stem terete, twining to left, to 25 m or longer, prickly, initially pubescent. Leaves alternate, palmately 3-foliolate; petiole to 30 cm, hairy; central leaflet ± ovate to elliptic, 6–12(–17.5) × 4–12 cm, base obtuse to truncate, apex acuminate, adaxially sparsely hispid, glabrescent, abaxially hispid, palmately-veined; lateral leaflets ovateelliptic or nearly broadly oblong, oblique, smaller than middle leaflet, margin entire; petiolules terete, 0.5–1 cm. Male spikes in axillary panicles, 15–50 cm, densely tomentose; male flowers sessile, in dense clusters; stamens 6. Female spikes simple, to 40 cm. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like ellipsoidal lobes, 4–6 × 2.5–3 cm, leathery, densely pubescent. Seeds inserted near apex of capsule, winged toward base.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Fung Yuen, Lin O. W. J. Tutcher 10953, 11772; Y. S. Lau 2493.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, E Xizang; Bhutan, India, Sikkim, Thailand to Malesia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dioscorea pentaphylla L. 五葉薯蕷
Sp. Pl. 2: 1032. 1753; FRPS 16(1): 95, pl. 28: 7–10. 1985; FFJ 6: 544. 1995; FOC 24: 289. 2000; FGD 6: 393, fig. 234. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 95, fig. 52, 53. 2009.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers variously shaped, usually long ovoid, with many fibrous roots. Stem terete, twining to left, prickly and sparsely puberulent when young, usually bearing bulblets in leaf axils. Leaves alternate, palmately 3–7-foliolate; petiole 3–13 cm, densely reddish brown pubescent; leaflets obovate-elliptic, oblong to elliptic (the outermost 2 lateral ones obliquely ovate-elliptic), 6.5–24 × 1.5–9 cm, base attenuate into a ± tomentose petiolule, apex acute, margin entire, adaxially appressed pubescent or subglabrous, abaxially sparsely pubescent, pinnately-veined. Male spikes in axillary panicles to 50 cm, with brown short pubescence on axis; male flowers sessile or subsessile, with bract and reniform bracteole forming an involucel around perianth, sparsely hairy; stamens 3. Female spikes simple or branched, to 25 cm, brown puberulent; female flowers subsessile; bracts, perianth, and ovary hairy. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like ellipsoidal lobes, 2–2.5 × 1–1.3 cm, thinly leathery, sparsely hairy, black at maturity. Seeds inserted near apex of capsule, winged toward base.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Lam. HK sheet 7524, 39080.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Yunnan, Xizang; Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Myanmar, Laos, Nepal, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea, Africa, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.; fruiting: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Diospyros eriantha Champ. ex Benth. 烏柿（烏材）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew. Gard. Misc. 4: 302. 1852; FHK 210. 1861; FKH 161. 1912; FHN 3: 151. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 133, pl. 31: 3 –5. 1987; FFJ 4: 318, fig. 251. 1989; FGD 3: 304. 1995; FOC 15: 231. 1996.

Evergreen tree or shrub, to 13 m tall; young branches, young leaves and inflorescense rusty strigose, old branches glabrescent. Leaves distichous. Petioles 5 – 6 mm, densely brown-strigose; leaf blade papery, oblong-lanceolate, 5 –15 × 1.8 – 4 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate, glabrous and shining adaxially, rusty-strigose along midvein and lateral veins abaxially; lateral veins 4 –8 pairs. Male flowers 1–3 clustered in leaf axils, subsessile, with several imbricate ovate bracts; calyx 4-lobed, lobes lanceolate, 4 –5 mm, strigose; corolla white, salverform, strigose abaxially; tubes 7– 8 mm; lobes 4, lanceolate, 4 –5 mm; stamens 14 –16; pistillodes small. Female flowers solitary and axillary, subsessile; perianth as in male flowers; ovary densely strigose, 2-locular; staminodes 8. Fruit ellipsoid, 1.5 × 1 cm, hairy initially, later only hairy at apex. Seeds 1–2; persistent calyx lobes ovate, ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. N. H. Li 103; Y. S. Lau 1923; C. P. Lau 1.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian; Japan, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Lowland thin forests and streamsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Diospyros kaki Thunb. 柿
Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 208. 1780; FKH 161. 1912; FGZ 467. 1956; FHN 3: 150. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 141, pl. 34: 1. 1987; FFJ 4: 322, fig. 256. 1989; FGD 3: 302. 1995; FOC 15: 225. 1996.

Deciduous tree, 5–12 m tall, polygamous. Young branchlets densely brown-pubescent, glabrascent. Petioles 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade papery or leathery, ovate-elliptic, broadly ovate or obovate, 7–17 × 5–10 cm, base attenuate or subrounded, pubescent on both surfaces when young, pubescent abaxially when mature; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs. Male flowers small, 3–5 in cymes; pedicels 0.6–1 cm, pubescent. Calyx nearly as long as corolla, hairy on both surfaces, lobes 4; corolla urn-shaped, tubes ca. 1 cm, glabrous, 4-lobed; lobes broadly ovate, ca. 4 mm, reflexed. Stamens 16 –24. Female flowers solitary; staminodes 8(–16); ovary glabrous or pubescent, 8-locular, styles distinct, pubescent. Berries ovoid or depressed globose, 3.5– 8.5 cm in diam. Pericarp thin, orange or pale red, persistent calyx lobes 3 – 4 cm in diam., fruiting stipes ca. 1 cm, pubescent.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 920; L. T. Lo 571; Y. S. Lau 1111.
Distribution: Native to China, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Diospyros morrisiana Hance 羅浮柿
Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 14. 1852; FHK 210. 1861; FKH 161. 1912; FGZ 468. 1956; FHN 3: 154. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 119, pl. 21: 2–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 319, fig. 253. 1989; FGD 3: 297, fig. 193. 1995; FOC 15: 223. 1996.

Deciduous shrub or tree, to 20 m tall. Young branches very sparsely puberulous, glabrescent. Petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, elliptic, oblong or ovoid, 5–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to obtuse, margin sometimes slightly undulate and recurved, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–8 pairs, inconspicuous. Male flowers: 2–3 in cymes; pedicels ca. 2 mm; calyx campanulate, 4-lobed; lobes triangular, tomentose, ca. 5 mm; corolla white, urn-shaped, ca. 7 mm, glabrous, 4-lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm; stamens 16–20, conspicuously hairy. Female flowers solitary; calyx-lobes 4, divided to about middle, tomentose; corolla nearly urn-shaped, ca. 7 mm; corolla lobes 4, ca. 3 × 3 mm, glabrous abaxially, densely brown-tomentose adaxially; staminodes 6; ovary globose, glabrous, styles 4, tomentose, connate at lower half. Berries yellow, subglobose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., 4-locular, glabrous, apex sometimes apiculate. Seeds castaneous, oblong, 10–14 × 5–7 mm, persistent calyx nearly square, subglabrous; fruiting pedicels very short.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1762; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24065; H. C. Tang 1402.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes or by streams. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Diospyros tsangii Merr. 油杯子（延平柿）
Lingnan Sci. J. 13: 43. 1934; FRPS 60(1): 126, pl. 29: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 318, fig. 252. 1989; FGD 3: 300, fig. 194. 1995; FOC 15: 225. 1996.

Shrub or small tree, 3–10 m tall; young branchlets slender, rusty pubescent, old branches glabrous. Petioles 3–6 mm, rusty pubescent; leaf blade papery, oblong or oblong-elliptic, 4–9 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, sparsely rusty pubescent along midvein and lateral veins adaxially, sparsely rusty pubescent along midvein and lateral veins or subglabrous abaxially; lateral veins 3 –5 pairs. Male flowers 1–3 in cymes, peduncles ca. 3 mm, white-pubescent; pedicels ca. 2 mm, white-pubescent; calyx densely pubescent abaxially, lobes 4, lanceolate, ca. 10 × 2.5 mm; corolla urn-shaped, white, glabrous, 4-lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 3 mm, white-pubescent on both surfaces; stamens 16, in pairs. Female flowers solitary, larger than male flowers; staminodes 8; ovary hairy. Berries globose or ellipsoid, 1–3.5 cm in diam., orange when mature, pilose; persistent calyx-lobes to 1.5 cm, pubescent.

Locality: Tai Tam, Sai Kung. F. W. Xing 8764.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Feb.–May; fruiting: Aug.

Diospyros tutcheri Dunn 嶺南柿
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1913: 354. 1913; FOC 15: 230. 1996.
Diospyros taamii Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 26(2): 166, fig. 3. 1945.

Small tree 6 m tall. Young branchlets yellowish brown, glabrous. Petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, elliptic or oblong, 6 –14 × 2.5 –5 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 or 6 pairs. Male flowers in cymes; pedicels 5 – 6 mm, articulate near apex; calyx 4-lobed, 1–2 mm, lobes triangular; corolla urn-shaped, 7– 8 mm, sericeous abaxially, 4-lobed, lobes broadly ovate, reflexed; stamens 16, in pairs; filaments pubescent; pistillodes small, hispid. Female flowers solitary, pendulous; pedicels 1.3 –1.5 cm, sericeous; calyx-lobes 4, ovate, 8 mm; corolla urn-shaped, ca. 5 mm, constricted at mouth, lobes 4, shorter than tubes, tomentose on both surfaces; staminodes 4; ovary depressed globose, 3 mm, 8-locular. Berries globose, ca. 3 cm in diam., glabrous; persistent calyx lobes long ovate, 1–2 cm fruiting pedicels 1–3 cm, slender.

Locality: Mount Gough, Findlay Road, Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng. H. C. Tang 1871; S. C. Ng 3515; F. W. Xing 7084.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Thin forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Gough by W. J. Tutcher in 1911.

Diospyros vaccinioides Lindl. 小果柿
Exot. Fl. 2: 139. 1825; FKH 161. 1912; FRPS 60(1): 99. 1987; FGD 3: 296. 1995; FOC 15: 221. 1996.
Rospidios vaccinioides A. DC., Prodr. 8: 220. 1844; FHK 210. 1861.
Diospyros vaccinioides var. oblongata Merr. & Chun, Sunyatsenia 5: 162. 1940; FHN 3: 150. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 100. 1987.

Evergreen shrub 1–3 m tall, much branched. Young branchlets firmly rusty villous. Petioles 1–2 mm, rusty pubescent, glabrescent; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, oblong to ovate, 1–3.5 × 1–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute and mucronate, glabrous except pilose along midveins abaxially; lateral veins 5– 6 pairs. Male flowers solitary or in cymes, small, pendulous, subsessile; calyx divided nearly to base, lobes 4, narrowly lanceolate, pubescent; corolla ca. 4.5 mm, lobes 4; stamens 16. Female flowers solitary; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 4– 8, linear; ovary glabrous. Berries globose or ellipsoid, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., subsessile; seeds 1–3, testa dark brown; persistent calyx lobes lanceolate, 5– 8 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1402; C. H. Tsou 1867; Y. S. Lau 562.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets in ravines or on hillslopes. Flowering: May; fruiting: Autumn and winter.

Diplacrum caricinum R. Br. 裂穎茅
Prodr. 241. 1810; FKH 304. 1912; FGZ 766. 1956; FRPS 11: 217. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 254. 2000; FGD 8: 362. 2007; FOC 23: 269. 2010.
Scleria caricina (R. Br.) Benth., Fl. Austr. 7: 426. 1878.

Small, diffuse, slender annual. Culms loosely tufted, 10–30 cm tall, ca. 1 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal and cauline, linear, 1–4 × 0.2–0.5 cm, apex shortly acute, margin minutely scabrous toward apex; sheaths slightly dilated upwards, wingless. Inflorescence consisting of axillary clusters of spikelets almost throughout the length of the culm; spikelets unisexual, 1–2 mm long; peduncles short, scarcely exserted from the leaf sheath. Primary bracts leaf-like. Male spikelets ca. 1.5 mm long, few-flowered. Stamen 1; filament up to 1.5 mm long; anther oblong, ca. 0.4 mm long. Female spikelet ca. 2 mm long. Glumes paired, ca. 2 mm long, broadly oblong, apex 3-lobed, side thinly membranous, 5–8-veined, pale greenish. Stigmas 3. Achenes tightly enveloped by 2 subtending glumes and falling off with them, globose, 0.7–1 mm in diam., umbonulate at apex, with 3 prominent, longitudinal ribs, irregularly ribbed, slightly hispidulous at apex, whitish. Disk adnate to base of the achene, obtusely triangular in outline.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Kwun Tong, Sai Kung, Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 1399; Y. S. Lau 3184; Y. W. Lam 1626.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Japan, Micronesia, Australia.
Ecology: Farmlands and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Diploclisia glaucescens (Blume) Diels 蒼白秤鈎風
Pflanzenr. IV. 94: 225. 1910; FHN 1: 320, fig. 159. 1964; Forman, Kew Bull. 22: 363. 1968; FGD 1: 35, fig. 36. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 31, pl. 6: 6. 1996.
Cocculus glaucescens Blume, Bijdr. 25. 1825
Diploclisia macrocarpa (Wright) Miers, Ann. Mag. Nat. Hist., ser. 2, 7: 42. 1851.
Cocculus macrocarpus Wright, Illstr. 1: 22, t. 7. 42. 1840; FHK 12. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.

Large woody vine, glabrous throughout. Stems up to 20 m or longer; branchlets light brown, striate. Leaves thinly leathery, sometimes peltate; petioles 3–7 cm; leaf blade triangular orbicular, sometimes broadly ovate-triangular, 3 –6 × 3–7 cm, base truncate, subrounded or slightly cordate, apex abruptly acute to rounded and apiculate, glaucescent on abaxial surface, usually palmately 5-nerved. Cymes forming panicles, 10 –30 cm, usually fascicled and borne on leafless old stems. Flowers light yellow, slightly fragrant. Male flowers: sepals ovate-oblong, 1.5 –2.5 mm; petals obovate or rhomboid, ca. 1.5 mm; stamens ca. 2 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males, except petals 2-lobed at apex. Drupes yellowish red, glaucous, narrowly oblong-obovate, 1.3 –2 × 0.7– 0.9 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Cape D'Aguilar, Wan Chai, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 552, 2217; HK sheet 152.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Ceylon, Myanmar, Thailand, Malesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Diploprora championii (Lindl.) Hook. f. 蛇舌蘭
Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 26. 1890, et Hook., Icon. Pl. 2: t. 2120. 1892; FHK 357. 1861; FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3–4): 375. 1973, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 108, fig. 62. 1977; FRPS 19: 282, pl. 43: 3–4. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 854, pl. 362. 2000; FGD 7: 489, fig. 252. 2006; FOC 25: 448. 2009.
Cottonia championii Lindl., J. Bot. Kew (Misc.) 7: 35. 1855; FHK 357. 1861.

Monopodial herb; roots cord-like, grooved, 15 cm or longer, 2 mm in diam.; stem leafy, green, slightly compressed and zig-zag. Leaves sessile, fleshy, evergreen, distichous, oblong or oblonglanceolate, 4–8 × 1.2–2.2 cm, base oblique or slightly twisted, apex acute, slightly recurved, midrib impressed above, elevated beneath. Inflorescence a hanging raceme; flowers 3–8 on a rachis; sepals and petals pale cream to yellow, deepening with age, wide spread, apex obtuse; odd sepal dorsal, plane, oblong-ovate, 9–10 × 5 mm, truncate at base; lateral sepals ovate-elliptic, 8 × 5 mm, apex tinged pink; petals oblique-oblong, 8 × 3.5 mm; lip suborbicular, with the margin raised forming a shallow saucer, base uneven with a flat floor, elevated in middle with lower lateral and apical sides depressed, delicately lavender-pink with bright yellow patches within, the front extending into a filiform process, triangular at base, forked at apex; column lilac, short, thick and smooth, rounded at the back and apex; anther globose, lavender, apex pointed; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, globose, waxy.

Locality: Violet Hill, The Peak, Wong Nai Chung, Mount Kellett, Pok Fu Lam Country Park. S. Y. Hu 9349, 11663A (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1766; P. S. Choi 222.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trees or rocks in shade areas in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Aug.; fruiting: Mar.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Diplospora dubia (Lindl.) Masam. 狗骨柴（三萼木）
Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 29: 269. 1939; Ali & Robbrecht, Blumea 35(2): 297. 1991; FRPS 71(1): 364, pl. 96: 1 – 8. 1999; FYN 15: 185, pl. 37: 6 – 10. 2003; FGD 6: 186, fig. 98. 2005.
Diplospora viridiflora DC., Prodr. 4: 477. 1830; FHK 157. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.
Tricalysia dubia (Lindl.) Ohwi, Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 102(2): 137. 1941; FHN 3: 328, fig. 750. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 334, pl. 150, photo 196. 1998.
Canthium dubium Lindl., Bot. Reg. 12: pl. 1026. 1826.

Shrubs or trees, 1–12 m tall, unarmed, branches and leaves glabrous. Leaves leathery, or rarely thickly papery; petioles 4–10(–15) mm; stipules 5–8 mm, with a broad base, apex subulate, white pubescent at base adaxially; leaf blade ovate‑oblong, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, 5–13(–19) × 1.5–5.5(–8) cm, base cuneate or acute, sometimes slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate, abruptly acuminate or acute, tip often blunt, margin entire, often slightly revolute, yellowish green and ± shining in drying; lateral veins slender 5–11 on each side of midvein. Flowers clustered in short dense axillary cymes, 7.5–11 mm in diam. Peduncles 2–6 mm. Pedicels 1–4 mm, together with peduncle and calyx puberulent. Calyx‑tube ca. 1 mm; limb slightly dilated, 4‑toothed. Corolla white or yellow; tube ca. 3 mm; lobes 4, oblong, about the length of the tube, recurved. Berry subglobose, 4–6 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent or glabrous, orange‑red, turning black when dry, 4 – 8‑seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 35352, 35598, 39958.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Jan.–May; fruiting: May–Feb. of the following year.

Dipteracanthus repens (L.) Hassk. 楠草（蘆莉草）
Hoev. & De Vriense, Tidschr. Nat. Gesch. 10: 129. 1843; FHN 3: 549. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 656, pl. 300, photo 338. 1998; FRPS 70: 50. 2002.
Ruellia repens L., Mant. 89. 1767; FHK 261. 1861; FKH 198. 1912; Check List HK Plants 51. 1974; 70. 1978.
Dipteracanthus lanceolatus Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 82. 1832.

Perennial creeping herb, 15–50 cm tall. Stems subquadrangular, finely pubescent or glabrescent. Petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blades thin papery, ovate to linear‑lanceolate, 1.4–4 × 0.8–2 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate or acute, margin subentire, sparsely strigose on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Flowers axillary, solitary; pedicels ca. 1 mm. Bracteoles leaf‑like, ovate or ovate‑oblong, 0.8–1 cm. Calyx‑lobes ca. 5 mm, lanceolate, scarcely ciliate. Corolla white, ca. 2 cm, pilose outside, campanulate; tube‑base ca. 5 mm, ventricose and gradually widened to ca. 5 mm at mouth; lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 3 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 4, included, didynamous, filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, the shorter pair ca. 2 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm. Ovary comose; style ca. 1 cm, hirsute; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal. Capsule spindle‑like, ca. 1.2 cm, brownish yellow, slightly pilose; 12–16‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, flat, ca. 3 mm in diam., appressed pilose, with a conspicuous entire white membranous wing.

Locality: Hong Kong Wai. C. Wright s.n. (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands, roadsides. Flowering: Early spring.

Dischidia chinensis Champ. ex Benth. 眼樹蓮（瓜子金）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 55. 1853; FHK 228. 1861; FKH 173. 1912; FRPS 63: 504, pl. 188. 1977; FGD 1: 489, fig. 551. 1987; FOC 16: 237. 1995.

Herbs, glabrous throughout; stems green, clinging, twining, or hanging from trees or rocks, to 2 m. Petioles 2 – 3 mm; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic, 1.5 – 3 × 1 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute to rounded, lateral veins 4 or 5 on each side of midvein. Umbels to 9‑flowered; peduncle ca. 2 mm; pedicels 1 mm. Sepals ovate, ciliate. Corolla yellowish white, throat thickened, villous; lobes ovate‑triangular, 1 × 1 mm. Corona‑lobes anchor‑shaped, stalked, apex linear, 2‑cleft, spreading and recurved at both ends, with a small rounded papilla in sinus of divaricate arms. Pollinia oblong, caudicles enlarged at apex; apical membrane of anther acute. Ovaries glabrous; stigma head slightly apiculate. Follicles lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, 5 – 8 × 0.4 cm, smooth. Seeds ovate‑oblong; coma 2.5 cm.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang, Castle Peak, Fo Tan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 10223; Y. S. Lau 1215; HK sheet 39857.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed woods, often climbing on trees. Flowering: May – Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental. Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental. Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Disperis lantauensis S. Y. Hu 香港雙袋蘭（象鼻蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 11(1): 17, fig. 3(a–c). 1972; Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3–4): 376. 1973; Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 36, fig. 11. 1977; FRPS 17: 494. 1999 [“D. nantauensis”]; Kurzweil, Blumea 50: 145. 2005 & FOC 25: 165. 2009, pro syn. sub Disperis neilgherrensis Wight (1851).

Perennial terrestrial herb, 5 cm tall at flowering time, with an underground corm 4 mm in diam. Leaves cauline, sessile, ovate, 4 mm long and wide, entire, acute. Flowers solitary or two, terminal to stem; dorsal sepal erect, orbicular, 4 mm in diam.; petals oblique elliptic, 2 mm, base oblique cuneate, apex acute, forming a shield with the dorsal sepal, lateral sepals connate at base, 5 mm between apex, each with an obtuse spur; ovary and pedicel forming a cylinder of 6 mm.

Locality: Kowloon Peak, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. G. Barretto 295.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes. Flowering: Jul.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 10812, A) was collected by S. Y. Hu from Sunset Peak, Lantau Island on 30 Jul. 1970. Some authors (e.g. Seidenfaden, Bot. Tidsskr. 65: 103. 1969; Kurzweil, 2005) adopted a broad species concept which included all Asian species under the synonymy of Disperis neilgherrensis, sensu lato, which is known for the high variability in characters used previously to delimit such taxa.

Disporum uniflorum Baker ex S. Moore 少花萬壽竹
J. Bot. 13: 230. 1875; FOC 24: 157. 2000.
Disporum sessile auct. non D. Don: FKH 281. 1912; FRPS 15: 45, pl. 16: 4. 1978; Check List HK Plants 125. 2004.

Perennial herb, 20–80 cm tall. Rhizome fleshy, shortly creeping, often with stolons. Stems erect, smooth, simple or bifurcately branched on distal part. Leaves alternate; petioles 5 – 10 mm; leaf blade broadly elliptic, oblong-ovate to lanceolate, 4–9 × 1–6.5 cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate to acute, glabrous, papillose on margin and veins. Flowers yellow, 1–3(–5) terminal on branches; pedicels 3–5 mm. Perianth segments 6, spatulate-oblanceolate to obovate, 2–3 cm × 5–10 mm, base gibbous-spurred; spurs 1–2 mm. Stamens 6, included; filaments 1.5–2 cm, minutely papillose proximally; anthers 4–8 mm. Ovary 4–5 mm; style 1.5 – 2.3 cm; stigma 3-lobed. Berries blue-black, subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. P. S. Choi 196; Y. S. Lau 1529.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning; Korea.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Disporum cantoniense (Lour.) Merr., distributed in SW to SE China, is also cultivated in Hong Kong as an ornamental. It can be recognized by its creeping rhizome without stolon and slightly opening flowers and purplish tepals.

records.text:
Distyliopsis dunnii (Hemsl.) P. K. Endress 尖葉假蚊母樹
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 90: 30. 1970; FFJ 2: 260. 1985; FOC 9: 31. 2003.
Sycopsis dunnii Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2836. 1907; FRPS 35(2): 114, pl. 24. 1979; FGD 1: 166, fig. 181. 1987.

Shrub or small tree; young branches with sessile, peltate scales. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, densely lepidote; leaf blade oblong or ovateoblong, occasionally oblong-lanceolate, 6 –9 × 2.5 –4.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire, both surfaces glabrescent. Flowers arranged in axillary short spike or racemes. Bracts oblong. Male flowers: borne on lower part, sessile, calyx 5 – 6- teethed. Stamens 5–9, filaments 2–5 mm, without rudimentary ovary. Bisexual flowers: borne on the upper part, shortly pedicellate; floral cup 2–3 mm; stamens 4 –11. Ovary villous; styles 4 –5 mm, glabrous, recurved. Capsules 1– 4, stalked, 1–1.3 cm, grey-brown villous, persistent floral cup 3– 4 mm, with dense sessile scales.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 432; Y. W. Lam 1403.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Laos.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Distyliopsis tutcheri (Hemsl.) P. K. Endress 鈍葉假蚊母樹
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 90: 30. 1970; FFJ 2: 261. 1985; FOC 9: 32. 2003.
Sycopsis tutcheri Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2834. 1907; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 115. 1979; FGD 1: 167. 1987.
Sycopsis oblanceolata H. T. Chang, Sunyatsenia 7: 72. 1948.

Shrub or small tree; young branches with sessile, peltate scales. Petioles 3– 6 mm, densely lepidote; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 3 – 6 × 2–3 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or subrounded, margin entire. Male flowers not seen. Female (or bisexual) flowers arranged in 1–2 cm long racemes. Peduncle and rachis lepidote; pedicels 3 – 4 mm; bracts oblong, lepidote; ovary villous, style 3–5 mm, recurved. Capsules 1–5, 1–1.3 cm, yellowbrown- villous, persistent floral cup 4 –5 mm, with sessile scales.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lantau Island. HK sheet 10909, 10910.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from east of Mountain Lodge, Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by W. J. Tutcher on 6 January 1904.

Distylium racemosum Sieb. & Zucc. 蚊母樹
Fl. Jap. 1: 178. 1835; FHK 133. 1861; FRPS 35(2): 102. 1979; FGD 1: 163. 1987; FOC 9: 29. 2003.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous except ovary; young branches stellate-lepidote; buds lepidote. Petioles 0.5 –1 cm, sparsely stellate-lepidote; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 3 –6 × 1.5 –3.5 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex slightly obtuse, margin entire; lateral veins 5 or 6 pairs, reticulation of veins inconspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescences 1.8 –2 cm, male and female flowers on the same inflorescence, with female ones on the top. Floral bracts lanceolate, 2–3 mm. Male flower: stamens 5 – 6, filaments 1.5–2 mm; anthers red, 2.5–3.5 mm. Female flower: ovary stellatetomentose; styles 6 –7 mm. Capsules ovoid, 1–1.3 cm, stellatepubescent with brown hairs. Seeds ovoid, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Tung Chung, Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 285, 2081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Korea, Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Dodonaea viscosa (L.) Jacq. 車桑子（坡柳）
Enum. Pl. Carib. 19. 1760; FKH 67. 1912; FYN 1: 282, pl. 66: 7 – 8. 1977; FTW 3: 584. 1977; FRPS 47(1): 59, fig. 20. 1985; FFJ 3: 319, fig. 217. 1987; FGD 1: 253, fig. 281. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 3: 602. 1993.
Ptelea viscosa L., Sp. Pl. 1: 118. 1753.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3 m or taller. Branches flat, narrowly winged or ridged, with sticky juice. Leaves simple, short-petiolate or subsessile; leaf blade papery, variable in shape and size, linear, linear-spooniform, linear-lanceolate, or oblong, 5–12 × 0.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, margin entire or inconspicuously shallowly wavy, both surfaces with sticky juice, glabrous, shining when dry, lateral veins many. Inflorescences terminal or axillary near apices, shorter than leaves, densely flowered, rachis and branches ridged. Pedicels 2–5(–10) mm, slender. Sepals 4, lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, ca. 3 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 7–8; filaments less than 1 mm; anthers incurved, ca. 2.5 mm, glandular. Ovary ellipsoidal, abaxially with sticky juice, 2–3-locular; styles ca. 6 mm, apex 2–3-lobed. Capsules obcordiform or compressed-globose, 2–3-winged, 1.5–2.2 cm tall, with wing 1.8–2.5 cm wide, testa membranous or papery, veined. Seeds 1–2 per locule, black, lens-like.

Locality: Ting Kok Rd., Sai Kung, Tai Lam Chung, Pak Nai, Tung Chung, Yi Long. Y. S. Lau 3058; P. S. Choi 157, 280.
Distribution: E, S & SW China; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and wastelands. Flowering: Autumn; fruiting: Late winter to early spring.

Dopatrium junceum (Roxb.) Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth. 虻眼
Scroph. Ind. 31. 1835; FHK 249. 1861; FKH 187. 1912; FHN 3: 499. 1974; FOC 18: 23. 1998; FGD 4: 397. 2000.

Annual herbs, to 50 cm tall. Stems succulent, erect, many‑branched from base. Branches slender, longitudinally striate, glabrous. Leaves sometimes scale‑like, gradually decreasing in size upward, sessile, lanceolate to subspatulate‑lanceolate, to 2 cm, base amplexicaul and generally narrowly attenuate, apex acute to ± obtuse, margin entire. Flowers solitary and axillary. Pedicels slender, to 1 cm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, 5‑lobed. Corolla white, rose, or pale purple, ca. 5 mm; lower lip spreading flat; upper lip erect, short. Fertile stamens 2, staminodes 2. Capsules globose, ca. 2 mm in diam. Seeds ovoid‑oblong; testa reticulate.

Locality: East Point. W. J. Tutcher 1341.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Shaanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Japan, India, SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Marshy grounds. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.

Dracaena fragrans (L.) Ker Gawl. 巴西鐵樹
Bot. Mag. 27: pl. 1081. 1808; FTW ed. 2, 5: 77. 2000; FGD 9: 213. 2009.
Aletris fragrans L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 456. 1762.

Arborescent or shrubby plant, to 6 m. Stem erect, simple or rarely branched at apex, greyish brown, smooth, with circular leaf scars when young. Leaves crowded at apex of stem and branches, oblong-lanceolate, 30–90 × 6–9 cm, apex acute, margin ± wavy, green or with white or yellow stripes, midveins raised on both surfaces. Panicles erect, 30–60 cm. Bracts acute, scarious; pedicels 7–21 cm. Flowers small, pale yellow, fragrant. Perianth campanulate, 1–2 cm, lobes ± reflexed. Ovary sessile. Berries globose, red.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions, native to Africa.
Uses: Ornamental.

Dracontomelon duperreanum Pierre 人面子
Fl. Forest. Cochinch. 5: t. 374. 1898; FYN 2: 375. 1979; FRPS 45(1): 83, pl. 26: 1 – 4. 1980; FFJ 3: 251, fig. 171. 1987; FGD 2: 310, fig. 202. 1991.
Dracontomelon sinense Stapf, Hooker's Icon. Pl. 27(2): t. 2641. 1900.
Dracontomelon mangiferum auct. non Blume: Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. 23: 149. 1886; FKH 69. 1912.
Dracontomelon dao auct. non (Blanco) Merr. & Rolfe: FGZ 449, fig. 212. 1956; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 637, fig. 3004. 1972; FHN 3: 104, fig. 600. 1974.

Evergreen tree, 20–25(–40) m tall; branchlets minutely grey tomentose. Leaves 30–45 cm including the petiole; rachis and petioles ribbed, tomentulose; leaflets 11–17; petiolules 2–5 mm; blade subleathery, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 6–12 × 2.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, oblique, apex acuminate, margin entire, minutely pubescent along midvein on both surfaces, covered with white tufts of hair in vein axils abaxially; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, reticulate venation prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal, shorter than leaves, densely pubescent; pedicels 2–3 mm, hirsute. Calyx lobes ovate, 4–6 mm, apex obtuse, tomentulose on both surfaces. Petals white, lanceolate or narrowly oblong, ca. 7–8 mm, glabrous. Filaments ca. 3.5 mm; anthers ca. 1.5 mm. Disk lobed, undulate. Ovary glabrous, 2.5–3 mm. Drupe ca. 2 × 2.5 cm, yellow at maturity, endocarp compressed, 1.7–1.9 cm in diam., with 4–5 pores at apex.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 1643.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Fruit, timber.

Dregea volubilis (L. f.) Benth. ex Hook. f. 南山藤
Fl. Brit. India 4: 46. 1883; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 493, pl. 183. 1977; FGD 1: 525, fig. 600. 1987; FOC 16: 250. 1995.
Asclepias volubilis L. f. Suppl. 170. 1781.

Lianas to 12 m. Branches pale grey, lenticellate; branchlets green, smooth. Petioles 2.5–6 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate or suborbicular, 7–18 × 4–17 cm, base shallowly cordate, apex acute or short‑acuminate, glabrous or ± softly pubescent, lateral veins 4 pairs. Inflorescences pendulous, many‑flowered; peduncle 2–6 cm, slender, puberulent. Pedicels 2–2.5 cm; flowers green or yellowish green, fragrant. Sepals ovate‑oblong, 2.5–3 mm, pubescent, ciliate. Corolla glabrous, lobes broadly ovate, 6–12 × 5–12 mm, obtuse, ciliate. Corona yellowish green, 4–4.5 mm in diam. Anther appendage white; pollinia oblong. Ovaries pilose. Follicles narrowly ovoid, 10–15 × 3–4 cm, longitudinally wrinkled‑striate or irregularly ribbed. Seeds ovate, 12 × 6 mm, flattened, marginate; coma 4.5 cm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Ping Kong, Kei Ling Ha. S. C. Ng 2520; HK sheet 34046, 40152.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Nepal, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Drosera burmannii Vahl 錦地羅
Symb. Bot. 3: 50. 1794; FKH 100. 1912; FHK 129. 1861; FHN 1: 371. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 18. 1984; FGD 2: 64. 1991; FOC 8: 199. 2001.

Annual or biennial herb, with few fibrous roots; stem unbranched, extremely short, without tuber below ground. Leaves basal, forming a flat rosette, yellowish green or red to reddish violet, spathulate to obovate-spathulate, 6–15 × 5–7 mm, base attenuate, apex fimbriate, glandular hairy or glabrous; petioles short or absent; stipule 3–7 mm, connate with petiole at base, 5–7-fid, lobes laciniate. Inflorescence scapiform; racemes 1–3, 2–19-flowered, 6 –22 cm, subglabrous or with white or red to reddish violet glands; bracts hastate, 3- or 5-lobed, 1–3 mm; pedicels erect, 1–7 mm, glandular hairy or glabrous; sepals 5, united at base, light green, red, or reddish violet, narrowly oblong, 2–3 mm, striate, tuberculate, glandular hairs and white glands abaxially; petals 5, obovate, white to light red to reddish violet, ca. 4 × 2–3 mm; stamens 5, ca. 3 mm; ovary subglobose, glabrous; placentas 5, rare 6; styles 5, rare 6, filiform, 2–3 mm, incurved; stigma tooth-like. Capsule 5- (or rarely 6-) valved. Seeds many, dark-brown to black, veined.

Locality: Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson. H. C. Tang 2314; HK sheet 36058.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Sandy places. Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Drosera indica L. 長葉茅膏菜
Sp. Pl. 1: 282. 1753; FKH 100. 1912; FHN 1: 372. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 18. 1984; FGD 2: 65. 1991; FOC 8: 200. 2001.

Annual herb, with fibrous roots; stem unbranched, erect or procumbent, 2– 40 cm, not forming tubers below ground, pubescent with short, glandular hairs. Leaves cauline, alternate, light green or red, narrowly linear, 2–12 × 0.1–0.3 cm, white or reddish glandular pubescent, or glabrous, apex acute; stipule absent or reduced and hair-like; petioles 5–10 mm, glandular hairy or glabrous. Inflorescence axillary or leaf opposed, 6–30 cm, 1–30-flowered, glandular pubescent; peduncles to 12 cm; bracts linear, 2–8 mm; pedicels 0.6–1.5 cm, glandular pubescent; sepals 5, united near the base, lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 3 – 5 × 1–2 mm, margin entire or serrate, glandular pubescent abaxially; petals 5, white, light red, orange, or reddish violet, obovate to oblanceolate, ca. 6 mm; stamens 5, 3–5 mm, papillose, filaments flattened; ovary obovoid or subglobose, 1–2 mm; placentas 3; styles 3, deeply 2-lobed nearly to base, usually incurved; stigma simple, 2–3 mm. Capsule globose-obovoid, 3-valved, 4– 6 mm. Seeds black, small; venation thick and scrobiculate.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tung Chung. Y. M. Wan 6; Y. W. Lam 1265; S. P. Lau 58.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Wet places, soggy soils. Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Drosera oblanceolata Y. Z. Ruan 長柱茅膏菜
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 19: 340. 1981; FRPS 34(1): 21. 1984; FGD 2: 65. 1991; FOC 8: 200. 2001.

Perennial herb, with fibrous roots. Stems unbranched, short, without tuber below ground. Leaves basal, dense, petiolate, circinately 2-folded towards stipule when young; stipules light red, 1.5 –4.6 cm, scarious, deeply 3-parted, middle lobe 2- or 3-fid; petioles 3 –7 mm; leaf blade orbicular to oblanceolate, elliptic, or linear, 1.5 – 4.6 cm × (1–)2– 4 mm, pilose with glandular hairs, ciliate. Inflorescences 1 or 2, scapiform, 5–9 cm; peduncle glabrous; cincinnus corymbose, 8–10-flowered; bracts linear, ca. 2 mm; pedicels 3– 5 mm. Sepals 5, united at base, green, narrowly obovate to oblong, ca. 4 mm, glabrous, persistent. Petals pink, obovate to cuneate. Stamens 5. Ovary ellipsoid-globose to globose, ca. 2 mm; placentas 3; styles 3, 2–3 mm, each style deeply 2-lobed, sometimes again 2-lobed; stigma multi-fid. Capsule 3-valved. Seeds black, ellipsoid-globose, ca. 0.3 mm; venation scrobiculate.

Locality: Sunset Peak. H. G. Ye et al. 1176; Y. S. Lau 2599.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Sunny meadows and bogs. Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Drosera peltata Smith ex Willd. 光萼茅膏菜（茅膏菜）
Sp. Pl. 1: 1546. 1797; FKH 100. 1912; FOC 8: 201. 2001
Drosera peltata Smith ex Willd. var. glabrata Y. Z. Ruan, FRPS 34(1): 27. 1984; FGD 2: 66. 1991.

Perennial herb; stems erect or climbing, branched distally, 9 – 45 cm, with a tuber below ground, glabrous or with black, papillose glands. Basal leaves densely whorled, or absent in some populations, peltate, orbicular to suborbicular, 2– 4 × 6 – 8 mm, some leaves reduced, linear, ca. 2 mm, yellowish green to green; exstipulate; petioles 2–8 mm. Cauline leaves remote, peltate or lunate to semiorbicular, 2–3 × 4– 5 mm, margin glandular hairy, yellowish green; petioles 0.8 –1.3 cm; exstipulate. Inflorescence terminal; cincinnus 2–6 cm, 3 –22-flowered; bracts cuneate to oblanceolate or subulate; pedicels 0.6–2 cm; sepals 5–7, united near base, yellowish green, lanceolate to ovate, 2– 4 mm × ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous to glandular hairy, apex 5 –7-fid; petals usually white, rarely pink or red, oblong-cuneate, 4 – 6 × 2–3 mm; stamens 5, 2–4 mm; ovary subglobose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam.; styles 3– 5, sometimes 2 or 6, ca. 0.8 mm, each style deeply bi-lobed, again 2–5-lobed; stigma 2–3-fid. Capsule subglobose, (2–)3– 5(– 6)-valved. Seeds many, ellipsoid, ovoid to globose, ca. 0.4 mm; venation scrobiculate.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Ping Fung Shan. K. Y. Tam 132; Y. W. Lam 26, 241.
Distribution: Anhui, Gansu, Guangdong, Guangxi, W Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy fields, thickets and thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Drosera spathulata Labill. 寬苞茅膏菜
Nov. Holl. Pl. 1: 79. 1804; FRPS 34(1): 20. 1984; FOC 8: 200. 2001
Drosera loureirii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 31: 167. 1833; FHK 130. 1861; FKH 100. 1912.
Drosera spathulata Labill. var. loureirii (Hook. & Arn.) Y. Z. Ruan, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 19: 341. 1981; FGD 2: 64. 1991.

Perennial herb, with 1 or 2 black, fibrous roots; stem short, without tuber below ground. Leaves forming a dense, flat rosette, circinately 1-folded toward stipule when young, obovate or spathulate, or cuneate, 0.9–2.8 × 0.2–0.5 mm, glandular hairy; stipules light red, narrow, 4 – 8 mm, scarious, apex fimbriate, setaceous; petioles flattened, gradually dilated distally, 8–10 mm, glandular hairy. Inflorescences 1– 6, scapiform, sometimes branched, 4 –25 cm; peduncle densely glandular hairy; racemes 1-sided, 10 –20-flowered; bracts linear to oblanceolate, ca. 2 mm or more, 3-lobed; pedicels 1–3 mm, densely glandular hairy; sepals 5, united at base, lanceolate or narrowly ovate, 1.5 – 4 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, margin entire or l-toothed, densely glandular hairy outside; petals white or pink to reddish violet, obovate, 2–6 mm; stamens 5, 2.5– 6 mm; filaments flat, ca. 5 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1.5 mm; ovary ellipsoid; placentas 3– 4; styles 3– 4, ca. 2.5 mm, each style deeply 2-lobed to base, sometimes again lobed distally; stigma simple, persistent. Capsule 3 – 4-valved, ca. 1.5 mm; valves obdeltoid, incurved. Seeds small, black, ovoid or ellipsoid; venation thick and scrobiculate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ho Pui, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 662; Y. S. Lau 2172; H. C. Tang 2251.
