Distribution: Guangdong, S Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Grassy fields and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

Drymaria cordata (L.) Schult. 荷蓮豆
Syst. Veg. 5: 406. 1819; FHK 22. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; Hand.-Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 202. 1929; FHN 1: 377, fig. 196. 1964; FGD 2: 80, fig. 55. 1991; FOC 6: 6. 2001.
Drymaria diandra Bl., Bijdr. 62. 1825; FRPS 26: 61, pl. 10: 8 –12. 1996; S. S. Ying, FTW ed. 2, 2: 360, pl. 167. 1996.

Annual herb. Stems prostrate, rooting at nodes, glabrous. Leaves opposite, short petiolate; leaf blade ovate-cordate or orbicular, about 1–1.5 cm long and broad, 3 – 5-nerved. Flowers in axillary or terminal cymes. Pedicels 1.5–3 mm, with glandular hairs. Sepals narrowly ovate, 2–3.5 mm, herbaceous, with scarious margin, 3-nerved, glandular-hairy. Petals white, obovate-cuneate, ca. 2.5 mm, deeply 2-lobed. Stamens slightly shorter than sepals; filaments slightly dilated at base. Ovary ovoid; styles 3, united at base. Capsule ovoid, 3-valved.

Locality: Tsiu Hang, Mui Tsz Lam, Mau Ping, Chung Mei, TaiM Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Lin Fa Shan. W. J. Tutcher 11146; Y. S. Lau 1342, 1627.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia,
Indian subcontinent, Malesia, Australia, N Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides and other damp shaded places. Flowering: Apr.– Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Drypetes arcuatinervia Merr. & Chun 拱網核果木（拱弧脈核果木）
Sunyatsenia 5: 95. 1940; FRPS 44(1): 47, pl. 12: 1 –2. 1994; FGD 5: 36. 2003.
Drypetes arcuatinervia Merr. & Chun var. elongata Merr. & Chun, Sunyataenia 5: 96. 1940.

Shrub, 1–5 m tall; branches densely lenticellate; branchlets glabrous. Leaves papery or thin-leathery; stipules small, triangular, caducous; petioles 2–5 mm; leaf blade oblong, oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, rarely elliptic, 6–15 × 2–6 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate, margin sparsely serrulate; lateral veins 7–8 on each side of midvein. Flowers in axillary clusters or borne on leafless spurs. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 2 mm; sepals 4–5(–6), elliptic or rotund, margin erose-lacerate; disk 4–6-fid; stamens 4–6, inserted at sinus of disk, filaments short and slightly flattened; anthers rotund. Female flowers: sepals and disk as in male flowers; ovary ovoid, 1-locular. Drupes ovoid, ca. 1 cm in diam., apex acute, sometimes rostrate, 1-seeded.

Locality: Po Toi Island.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Shrublands. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Apr. of the following year.

Duchesnea indica (Andrews) Focke 蛇莓
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(3): 33. 1888; FFJ 2: 314. 1985; FRPS 37: 358. 1985; FGD 4: 221. 2000; FOC 9: 338. 2003.
Fragaria indica Andrews, Bot. Repos. 7: pl. 479. 1807; FKH 95. 1912.

Perennial herb, with short rhizomes; stolons many, slender, 30 – 100 cm, pilose. Leaves palmately 3(– 5)-foliolate, many at each node; petioles 1 – 5 cm, pilose; leaflets obovate or rhombic-oblong, 1.5 – 5 × 1 – 3 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin obtusely serrate, pilose on both surfaces or adaxially glabrous. Flowers solitary, axillary, 1.2–2.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 2–8 cm, slender, pilose; hypanthium cup-shaped, 2–3.5 mm in diam., abaxially sparsely pilose; sepals ovate or lanceolate, 4 – 6 × 2–3 mm, apex acute, abaxially sparsely pilose; epicalyx obovate, 5 – 8 mm, apex usually 3 – 5-dentate, abaxially sparsely pilose; petals yellow, obovate, 5 – 10 mm, apex obtuse; stamens 20 – 30, filaments up to 2.5 mm, anthers ca. 0.5 mm; pistils 20 – 30, free; receptacle enlarged in fruits, globose or ellipsoidal, fleshy, ca. 1.5 × 1.3 cm, scarlet red when ripe, abaxially long hairy; achenes many, ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm, smooth or inconspicuously papillate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai. H. C. Tang 799; L. T. Lo 238; Y. S. Lau 2949.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; temperate and tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Wastelands and roadsides near villages.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Duhaldea cappa (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) Pruski & Anderb 羊耳菊（白牛膽）
Comp. Newsl. 40: 44. 2003.
Inula cappa (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) DC., Prodr. 5: 469, 1836; FHK 180. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 296. 1966; FRPS 75: 271. 1979; FGD 8: 146. 2007; Check List HK Plants 283. 2002; 97. 2004.
Conyza cappa Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 176. 1825.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs; stem erect, 50–100(–200) cm high, densely covered with brownish sericeous hair throughout. Lower leaves withered at anthesis, remaining the axillary buds; middle and upper leaves elliptic‑oblong, 3–11 cm long, 1.5–4 cm wide, with upper ones smaller in size, base rounded to subcuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin with small curved teeth, scabrous above, with dense and thick layer of greyish white silky hair beneath, pinnately veined with those on lower surfaces prominent, subsessile or shortly petiolate, not longer than 5 mm. Capitula in terminal corymbose panicle. Involucres 5–7(–8) mm long, 4–5 mm across, campanulate; phyllaries 5‑seriate, apex acute, outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm long, herbaceous, densely brownish hairy throughout the abaxial side; changing gradually inward in shape, sizes, texture with the innermost being linear‑lanceolate, 5–6 mm long, scarious, hairy only at base and along the midvein. Florets yellow, marginal ones female, corolla narrowly tubular, 3–4 mm long, apex 3–4‑lobed and glandular. Disk florets hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, 4.5 –6 mm long, apex 5 triangular lobes and glandular. Cypselae cylindric, 1.5–1.8 mm long, silky hairy and about 10‑ribbed. Pappus 4–5 mm long, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1815; H. Y. Yueng 150 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 12406 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in E to S & SW China; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malaysia.
Ecology: Wastelands and thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dunbaria crinita (Dunn) Maesen 簇毛野扁豆
Wagening. Agr. Univ. Pap. 98-1: 26. 1998.
Atylosia crinita Dunn, J. Bot. 47(6): 198. 1909.
Dunbaria flavescens Nguyen van Thuan, Adansonia, ser. 2, 16 - 4: 512. 1977; Thuan, Fl. Cambodge, Laos, Vietnam 17: 124. 1979.

Perennial twining herb. Branches striate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; terminal leaflet ovate to ovate-elliptic, 5 – 8 × 3 – 4 cm, base rounded, apex acute, lateral ones smaller, obliquely ovate or ovate-elliptic, densely velvety with short hairs adaxially, and with many reddish vesicular glands on both surfaces. Racemes up to 7 cm, 10–20-flowered or more. Calyx glandular, tube ca. 4 mm, teeth triangular. Vexillum orbicular, 15 – 18 × 15 mm, base clawed, biauriculate, apex emarginate; wings obovate, equal to keel in length; keel rostrate. Ovary linear, grey silky-hairy, glandular. Stamens diadelphous. Pods linear, 4 – 5 × 0.6 – 0.7 cm, hairy. Seeds 6 – 8, brown to brown with black mosaic, orbicular, 4 × 4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 10901 (CUHK); Y. W. Taam 1615 (A, G, NY, US); J. P. W. Woo 369 (P).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Weedy place. Flowering: Aug. – Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Notes: Previously cultivated in Hong Kong Botanical Gardens, grown from seeds from Hainan.

Dunbaria fusca (Wall.) Kurz 黃毛野扁豆
Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 43(2): 186. 1874; FKH 85. 1912; FRPS 41: 308. 1995; FGD 5: 336. 2003.
Phaseolus fuscus Wall., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 1: 6, pl. 6. 1830.

Perennial twining herb. Stems to 3 m or longer, striate, densely grey pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets subequal, terminal one ovate, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 5 –9.5 × 2.5 –4 cm, base rounded or subcuneate, apex acute to acuminate, mucronate, glabrous or thinly pubescent adaxially, densely grey to grey-brown pubescent and red gland-dotted abaxially, trinerved. Racemes axillary, 4 – 15 cm, 10 – 15-flowered. Calyx campanulate, 4 – 7 mm, teeth triangular. Corolla purple-red, ca. 1.3 cm; vexillum orbicular, 12 × 10 mm, base clawed and biauriculate; wings oblong; keel incurved, circinate-rostrate. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary sessile, densely golden hirsute, squarish ovoid, 4 × 4 mm, estrophiole rather conspicuous.

Locality: Tsuen Wan, Shing Mun, Bride's Pool. Y. S. Lau 1002, 1969; P. S. Choi 50.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Anhui; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Climbing in thickets, low herbage, evergreen jungles and deciduous forests, hillslopes or grasslands. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.

Dunbaria podocarpa Kurz 長柄野扁豆
Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 43(2): 185. 1874; FKH 85. 1912; FRPS 41: 312. 1995; FGD 5: 338. 2003.

Perennial twining herb. Stems 1–4 m, densely grey pubescent, striate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; terminal leaflet rhombic, 3–4 × 3–4 cm, base obtuse, apex acute, rounded or subtruncate, lateral ones smaller, obliquely ovate, grey pubescent on both surfaces, with red glandular dots abaxially; trinerved. Racemes short, 1–2(–4)-flowered. Calyx campanulate, teeth ovate-lanceolate, pubescent and orange glandular-dotted. Corolla yellow, 1.5–2 cm; vexillum transversely elliptic, base 2-auriculate; wings narrowly elliptic, base with incurved auricle at one side; keel strongly curved, long beaked. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary linear, densely silky villose and dotted with orange glands. Pods linear-oblong, 5–8 × 0.9–1.1 cm, densely silky villose and dotted with orange glands, apex long beaked. Seeds 7–11, black, suborbicular, ca. 4 mm in diam., flat.

Locality: Mount Gough, Tai Po, Shek Kong, Fanling. Y. S. Lau 802, 892; Y. W. Lam 1680.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. –Nov.

Dunbaria punctata (Wight & Arn.) Benth. 圓葉野扁豆
Pl. Jungh. 2: 242. 1852; FGD 5: 337, fig. 185. 2003.
Dolichos punctatus Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 247. 1834.
Dunbaria rotundifolia (Lour.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 15(3): 242. 1919 [1920]; FRPS 41: 310. 1995.
Indigofera rotundifolia Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 458. 1790; ibid., ed. 2: 559. 1793.
Dunbaria conspersa Benth., Pl. Jungh. 1: 241. 1852; FHK 89. 1861; FKH 85. 1912.

Perennial twining herb. Stems slender, slightly pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets papery, terminal one orbicular-rhomboid, 1.5–2.7 × 3 cm, base rounded, apex obtuse or rounded, slightly and very shortly pubescent on both surfaces or subglabrous, black-brown gland-dotted, especially denser on abaxial surface, trinerved. Flowers 1– 2, axillary. Calyx campanulate; lobes lanceolate-falcate, the upper and lower ones longer than the tube, densely red gland-dotted and pubescent. Corolla yellow, 1 –1.5 cm; vexillum obovate-orbicular, 6– 8 mm, base 2-auriculate, apex emarginate; wings obovate, ca. 6 mm; keel falcate, obtusely beaked. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary sessile. Pods linear-oblong, 3 – 5 × 0.8 cm, flat, slightly curved, puberulent or glabrous, tip pin-like beaked. Seeds 6 – 8, black-brown, suborbicular, 3 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen, Kwai Chung, Sha Tin, Fanling, Shek Kong. L. T. Lo 527; Y. W. Lam 1116; HK sheet 35641.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Dunbaria rotundifolia (Lour.) Merr. previously (Check List HK Plants 145. 2002; 54. 2004).

Dunbaria villosa (Thunb. ex Murray) Makino 野扁豆
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16(180): 35. 1902; FRPS 41: 311. 1995; Maesen, Wageningen Agr. Univ. Pap. 98-1: 93. 1998.
Glycine villosa Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg. ed. 14: 659. 1784.
Atylosia subrhombea Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 3: 51. 1867.
Dunbaria subrhombea (Miq.) Hemsl., J. Bot. 14(163): 207. 1876; Thuan, Fl. Cambodge, Laos, Vietnam 17: 116. 1979.

Perennial twining herb. Branches delicate, sparsely whitish pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets 3-lobed, rather unequal, terminal one rhomboid to deltoid, 1.5–3(–5) × 2–4(–5) cm, base rounded to broad-cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, mucronate, lateral ones obliquely rhomboid, 1– 2.5 × 1– 2.5 cm. Racemes 2– 8-flowered. Calyx 4– 13 mm, densely pubescent abaxially. Corolla yellow; vexillum obovate, 16 × 12 mm, base clawed, apex emarginate, auriculate; wings elongate-obovate, 12 × 3– 5 mm; keel curved, tip circinate-rostrate. Stamens diadelphous; anthers basifixed. Pods brown, linear-falcate, 3.5– 4.5 × 0.7 – 0.8 cm. Seeds 6 – 7, black to brown, with or without mosaic, quadrate-ovoid, 4 × 4 mm, estrophiole divided.

Locality: Fanling, Tai Po. W. J. Tutcher 10549; S. Y. Hu 5718 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Liaoning; Myanmar, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grassy fields, thickets, roadsides. Flowering: Aug. – Oct.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Duranta erecta L. 假連翹
Sp. Pl. 2: 637. 1753; FOC 17: 2. 1994.
Duranta repens L., Sp. Pl. 2: 637. 1753; FGZ 626. 1956; FHN 4: 5, fig. 947. 1977; FYN 1: 399, pl. 95: 3 – 4. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 22, fig. 7. 1982; FFJ 4: 522, fig. 414. 1989; FGD 3: 347, fig. 228. 1995.

Shrub, often scandent, 1.5–3 m. Branches spiny, pubescent when young. Leaves opposite, sometimes whorled. Petiole ca. 1 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2–6.5 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin entire to crenate distally, pubescent. Calyx‑tube tubular, ca. 5 mm, 5‑veined, pubescent on both surfaces. Corolla often bluish purple, ca. 8 mm, slightly irregular 5‑lobed. Stamens inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Styles shorter than corolla‑tube. Drupes globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., shorter than calyx, shiny, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 48, 183; L. T. Lo 572.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang; native to America.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental (hedges).

Dypsis lutescens (H. Wendl.) Beentje & J. Dransf. 散尾葵
Palms Madagascar. 212. 1995. Chrysalidocarpus lutescens H. Wendl., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 36(8): 117–118. 1878; FGD 462, fig. 325. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 125. 1991; Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004.

Shrub, 2–6 m tall, unarmed, monoecious. Stems clustered, yellowish green, crownshaft greenish grey, node rings conspicuous. Leaves pinnate, recurved, 1.5–2.5 m; pinnae 40–60 pairs, regularly arranged, linear or linear-lanceolate, 30–40 × 1–2 cm, shorter upwards, shallowly bifid at apex; sheaths closed and forming a crownshaft. Inflorescences borne below the sheaths, 50–70 cm, branched 2–3 orders; branches 20–30 cm; rachillae 8–10, 12–18 cm. Flower small, ovoid, golden yellow; male flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 6; female flower: sepals 3, petals 3, style short. Fruits obovoid or ovoid, 1.5–2 × 0.8–1 cm, yellow to purple. Seed slightly obovoid, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1846.
Distribution: Madagascar; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Dysophylla stellata (Lour.) Benth. 水虎尾
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 1: 30. 1830; FRPS 66: 382. 1977; FOC 17: 262. 1994; FGD 3: 456, fig. 285. 1995.
Dysophylla verticillata Benth., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 1: 30. 1830; FKH 208. 1912.
Dysophylla stellatus (Lour.) Kuntze, Gen. Pl. 2: 429. 1891; FTW ed. 2, 4: 511, pl. 228. 1998.
Mentha stellata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 361. 1790.

Annual herbs, 15–50 cm tall. Stems erect, verticillately branched above middle, glabrous or very sparsely hirsute, nodes sometimes grey villous. Leaves in whorls of 4–10, sessile or very shortly petiolate; leaf blade linear to lanceolate, 2–7 cm × 0.2–0.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin remotely serrulate or entire, revolute or flat, glabrous, abaxially grey. Spikes cylindric, 0.5–7(–9) cm × 4–6.5(–8) mm, continuous, densely flowered; bracts lanceolate, conspicuously longer than calyx. Calyx campanulate, 1–1.2 mm, lengthening to 1.8 mm in fruit, densely grey tomentose abaxially. Corolla purple‑red, 1.8–2 mm, lobes subequal. Nutlets brown, obovoid.

Locality: Sha Tau Kok. S. B. C. Ross 11449.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, wet areas along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Dysoxylum hongkongense (Tutcher) Merr. 香港樫木
Lingnan Sci. J. 13(1): 33. 1934; FHN 3: 63. 1974; FGD 2: 287. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 558. 1993; FRPS 43(3): 89, pl. 21: 4– 5. 1997.
Chisocheton hongkongensis Tutcher, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 37: 64. 1905; FKH 58. 1912.

Tree, to 25 m tall. Young branches yellow pubescent to subglabrous. Leaves imparipinnate or paripinnate, 20–40 cm or longer; leaflets 9–16, opposite, subopposite, or alternate; petiolules 0.5–1.5 cm; blades subleathery, long-elliptic, 5–27 × 3–7 cm, base oblique, apex obtuse to shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein slightly impressed adaxially and prominent abaxially, lateral veins 8–15 on each side of midvein. Panicles axillary near apex of branch, 12–25 cm, pubescent, with tawny appressed hairs. Pedicels stout, 2–4 mm. Calyx shallowly cupular, 5-lobed, pubescent abaxially. Petals 5, white, long-elliptic, 5–6 × ca. 2 mm, tawny pubescent abaxially. Staminal tube ca. 4 mm, hairy abaxially, apex truncate to undulate-crenulate; anthers 8, ellipsoidal, inclusive. Disk tubular, obtusely dentate, apex brightly yellow ciliate. Ovary 3-locular, densely covered with yellow silky hairs. Style ca. 2 mm, flat, glabrous; stigma flat, disciform, glabrous. Capsule pyriform to ellipsoidal, ca. 4 cm in diam. Seeds brown, long ellipsoidal, to 2.5 cm, arillate.

Locality: Mount Parker, Cape D'Aguilar, Ng Tung Chai. W. J. Tutcher 1056; Y. S. Lau 2745; HK sheet 40374.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Apr.
Uses. Timber.
Notes: The type specimen (Hong Kong Herb. No. 969) was collected from Mount Parker, Hong Kong Island by W. J. Tutcher in 1903. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Chenopodium ambrosioides L. 土荊芥
Sp. Pl. 219. 1753; FKH 215. 1912; FRPS 25(2): 82. 1979; FHN 1: 396. 1964; FGD 3: 65. 1995.
Dysphania ambrosioides (L.) Mosyakin & Clemants, Ukrayins’k. Bot. Zurn. 59: 382. 2002; FOC 5: 377. 2003.

Annual or perennial herb, 50–80 cm tall, with strong smell. Stems erect much branched, with whitish or yellowish glandular hairs (not farinose) or subglabrous. Leaves oblong or lanceolate, 2–10 × 0.5 –2 cm, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin sinuate, dentate to parted, glabrous adaxially, sparsely oil-spotted abaxially. Inflorescence a terminal leafy panicle or spike, 2–10 cm. Flowers bisexual and pistillate. Perianth-lobes 5, rarely 3. Stamens 5; stigmas 3, rarely 4, filiform, exserted. Utricles compressed-globose. Seeds horizontal or oblique, black or dark red, 0.7 mm in diam., smooth and shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. HK sheet 36804; Y. S. Lau 3206.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Hunan, Sichuan; native to tropical America, widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Near villages, roadsides and riversides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal.
Note: This species was transferred to Dysphania R. Br. by Mosyakin & Clements (2002) and accepted in Flora of China. But there are no distinct characters to separate Dysphania from Chenopodium, except the glandular hairs of Dysphania.
records.uses:
Medicinal.
Note: This species was transferred to Dysphania R. Br. by Mosyakin & Clements (2002) and accepted in Flora of China. But there are no distinct characters to separate Dysphania from Chenopodium, except the glandular hairs of Dysphania.

records.text:
Echinochloa colona (L.) Link 光頭稗
Hort. Berol. 2: 209. 1833; FHN 4: 418. 1977 [“colonum”]; FRPS 10(1): 252, pl. 77: 1–3. 1990 [“colonum”]; FFJ 6: 213, fig. 180. 1995 [“colonum”]; FTW ed. 2, 5: 474. 2000; FOC 22: 517. 2006; FGD 9: 418. 2009.
Panicum colonum L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 2: 870. 1759; FHK 411. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms erect, 10–60 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths compressed and keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat, 3–30 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous, base rounded, apex acuminate, margins slightly scabrous; ligule absent. Panicle narrow, 5–10 cm; central axis slender, triquetrous, glabrous; racemes 1–2 cm, erect or sometimes stiffly diverging, simple, separated or overlapping by up to half their length or more, spikelets tightly congested in 4 neat rows. Spikelets ovate-oblong, 2–3 mm, hirtellous; lower glume triangular, 1/3 to 1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume similar to lower lemma, mucronate to awn-pointed, 5–7-veined; lower floret usually neuter, palea membranous, slightly shorter than lemma, obtuse, 2-keeled, with short ciliate on the keel; upper lemma elliptic, smooth and shiny, margins inrolled embraced a hyaline palea of equal length.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1342; HK sheet 40835, 41984.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Xinjiang, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; warm regions throughout the world.
Ecology: A weed of farmlands and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. 稗
Ess. Agrostogr. 53. 1812; FHN 4: 419. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 252, pl. 77: 4–7. 1990; FFJ 6: 214, fig. 181. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 474, pl. 197. 2000; FOC 22: 517. 2006; FGD 9: 418, fig. 216. 2009.
Panicum crusgalli L., Sp. Pl. 1: 56. 1753; FHK 411. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms erect, glabrous, 20–160 cm tall. Leaf sheath loose, glabrous, the lower longer and the upper shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, 5–40 × 0.2–2 cm, usually glabrous, smooth except for scabrous margins, base rounded, apex acute or acuminate; ligule absent. Panicle erect, lanceolate to ovate or pyramidal, 6–26 cm; central axis ribbed, rib scabrous or usually with tubercle-based setae; racemes 2–10 cm, usually ascending or slightly close to central axis, simple or the longest with inconspicuous branchlets near the base, rachis scabrous or usually with tubercle-based setae, spikelets loosely to densely crowded. Spikelets green or purplish, ovate, 3–4 mm, spinulose along veins; lower glume triangular, ca. 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined, tuberculate-pilose on veins, base embraced spikelet, acute; floret neuter, lemmas herbaceous, 7-veined, tuberculate-pilose on veins, tipped with an robust awn arising from the apex, palea thin membranous, narrow, 2-keeled; upper lemma elliptic, smooth, shiny, mucronate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 35647, 42202, 42203.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; throughout subtropical and warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Paddy fields, marshes, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. var. austrojaponensis Ohwi 小旱稗（小果稗）
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11: 38. 1942 [“austro-japonensis”]; FRPS 10(1): 253. 1990; FYN 9: 514. 2003; FOC 22: 518. 2006; FGD 9: 419. 2009.

Culms 20–40 cm tall. Leaf blades often involute, 0.2–0.5 cm broad. Inflorescence narrow and slender; racemes short, erect, appressed to axis, simple. Spikelets purplish, 2.5–3 mm, hispid along veins, lower lemma awnless or with a short awn.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 1610; L. T. Lo 581; HK sheet 39688.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Philippines.
Ecology: Marshes, ditches, damp grasslands.

Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. var. breviseta (Döll) Podp. 短芒稗
Prace Morav.-Slez. Akad. Ved. Prir. 2(sign. 20): 745. 1925; FHN 4: 419. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 253. 1990; FOC 22: 518. 2006; FGD 9: 419. 2009.
Panicum crusgalli L. var. brevisetum Döll, Fl. Bad. 1: 232. 1857.

Culms 30–75 cm tall. Leaf blades 8–15 × 0.4–0.6 cm. Inflorescence narrow, 8–10 cm; racemes simple. Spikelets green, ovateelliptic, ca. 3 mm, hispid along veins, mucronate or with a short awn less than 5 mm.

Locality: Fanling, Peng Shan, Mai Po. Y. W. Lam 1344; HK sheet 14443, 41966.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Weedy places.

Echinochloa cruspavonis (Kunth) Schult. 孔雀稗
Mant. 2: 269. 1824; FRPS 10(1): 256, pl. 78: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 215. 1995; FOC 22: 517. 2006; FGD 9: 420. 2009.
Oplismenus cruspavonis Kunth, Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 1: 108. 1815 [“1816”].

Annual or perennial herb. Culms robust, straggling and rooting at base, 1.2–1.8 m tall. Leaf sheaths loose, smooth and glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat, 10–40 × 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, margins harshly scabrous; ligule absent. Inflorescence nodding, large, loose, 15–25 cm; branches mostly compound, spikelets many, crowded on secondary branchlets. Spikelets purple-tinged, ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 mm, hispid on veins, the hairs not tubercle-based; lower glume triangular, 1/3–2/5 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, rostrate, 5-veined, stiff hairs on the veins; lower lemma sterile, herbaceous, 5–7-veined, with a stout awn, 1–1.5 cm; upper lemma leathery, smooth and shiny, mucronate.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap. H. C. Tang 1969.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Anhui, Fujian; widely spread over tropical regions.
Ecology: Marshes and other damp places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Echinochloa glabrescens Munro ex Hook. f. 硬稃稗
Fl. Brit. Ind. 7(21): 31. 1897; FRPS 10(1): 258, pl. 78: 1–4. 1990; FYN 9: 515. 2003; FGD 9: 420. 2009.
Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. var. formosensis Ohwi, Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11(1): 38. 1942 [“Crus-galli”]; FHN 4: 419. 1977; FTW 5: 554. 1978.
Echinochloa glabrescens Kossenko, Bot. Mater. Gerb. Bot. Inst. Komarova Akad. Nauk SSSR. 11: 40. 1949; FOC 22: 517. 2006.

Annual herb. Culms erect or slightly decumbent at base, 30–120 cm tall. Leaf sheaths smooth and glabrous; leaf blades linearlanceolate or linear, flat, 10–38 × 0.6–1.5 cm, glabrous, margins thickened, acuminate; ligule absent. Inflorescence narrow panicle, 5–25 × 1–2(–4) cm; racemes 1–4 cm, simple or the middle subverticillate. Spikelets light green, 3.5–5 mm, glabrous or tuberculatepilose; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined, acute; upper glume equal to spikelet, 5-veined, inconspicuously scabrous to shortly hispid along veins; lower floret neuter; lemmas coriaceous, hard and shiny, especially down the centre, tuberculate-pilose on the veins, the lower cuspidate to awned. Caryopsis broad elliptic.

Locality: Kowloon, Castle Peak, Yuen Long, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 742, 2201; HK sheet 14441.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang; Bhutan, NE India, Japan, Korea, Nepal, Africa.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Eclipta prostrata (L.) L. 鱧腸
Mant. Pl. 2: 286. 1771; FHK 181, 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 241. 1966; FRPS 75: 344, pl. 58: 1–5. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 935. 1998.
Verbesina prostrata L., Sp. Pl. 2: 902. 1753.
Eclipta alba (L.) Haask., Pl. Jav. Rar. 528. 1848; FHK 181. 1861; FKH 145. 1912.
Verbesina alba L., Sp. Pl. 2: 902. 1753.

Annual herbs; stems erect, ascending or prostrate, 8–70 cm tall, branched mainly at the bottom, covered with adpressed strigose hair throughout. Leaves opposite, subsessile or shortly petiolate, lanceolate or elliptic, 2–6.5 × 0.3–1.8 cm, base narrowed, apex acute‑acuminate, margin serrulate or sometimes slightly undulate, strigose on both surfaces. Capitula 6–8 mm across when flowering, enlarged to 10 mm in fruiting stage. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries green, herbaceous, in 2 series, lanceolate‑oblong, 3–4 × 1.5–2 mm, outer ones slightly longer, apex acute, abaxial surfaces strigose. Receptacle convex, paleate; paleae 1.8–2.2 mm, linear, hairy at distal half. Marginal ligulate florets 2‑seriate, corolla white, tube 0.8–1 mm, ligule 1.6–1.8 mm, bifid or entire. Disk tubular florets many, corolla white, 1.3–1.5 mm, 4‑cleft at apex; anther bases sagittate and acute, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches flattened, apex obtuse, outer surfaces papillose. Cypselae brown, oblong, 2.5–2.8 × 1.3–1.5 mm, laterally compressed with those developed from female florets showing slightly 3‑angled in cross‑section, those from bisexual florets slightly 4‑angled, apex truncate, tuberculate on two surfaces, ribbed on lateral margins, glabrous, Pappus none or of few short teeth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1984; S. Y. Hu 5289 (CUHK); S. L. Thrower 473 (CUHK).
Distribution: Spread over most provinces of China; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Streamsides, banks of paddy fields, roadsides and other wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Egeria densa Planch. 水蘊草
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., sér. 3, 11: 80. 1849; FOC 23: 102. 2010.

Submerged herb. Stems 1–3 mm in diam. Leaves whorled, recurved, 10–40 × 1.5–4.5 mm, margin minutely serrate. Male spathes 2–4-flowered, 7.5–12 mm; pedicel to 8 cm. Sepals 3; petals 3, ovate, white; stamens 9, anthers yellow.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 42833.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Ditches in cultivation areas. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: This species is known to spread and become invasive in mild climate.

Ehretia acuminata R. Br. 厚殼樹
Prodr. 147. 1810; FKH 177. 1912; FOC 16: 334. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 393, photo 228. 1998.
Cordia thyrsiflora Siebold & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 2: 26. 1846. (Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math. Phys. Cl. 4(3): 150, pl. 3. 1846.)
Ehretia acuminata var. obovata (Lindl.) I. M. Johnst., J. Arnold Arbor. 32(1): 21. 1951; FHN 3: 454. 1974.
Ehretia taiwaniana Nakai, J. Arnold Arbor. 5(1): 38. 1924; FGZ 567. 1956.
Ehretia thyrsiflora (Siebold & Zucc.) Nakai, Trees & Shrubs Japan Proper, ed. 1, 327. 1922; FRPS 64(2): 12. 1990; FFJ 4: 507. 1989.

Tree to 15 m tall, glabrous except young parts; bark black‑grey, laciniate; branchlets brown, conspicuously lenticellate. Petiole 1.5–3.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic to obovate or oblong‑obovate, 5–15 × 4–6 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acute or apiculate, margin serrulate with teeth curved upward, glabrous or sparsely puberulent. Inflorescences paniculate, terminal, 8–15 cm. Flowers small, crowded, fragrant. Calyx 1.5–2 mm; lobes ovate, ciliate. Corolla white, campanulate, 3–4 mm; lobes spreading, oblong, longer than tube. Filaments 2–3 mm, inserted on 0.5–1 mm from the base of tube; anthers ovoid, ca. 1 mm. Style 1.5–2.5 mm. Drupes yellow or orange, 3–4 mm in diam.; endocarp wrinkled, divided into two 2‑seeded pyrenes at maturity.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Wai, Sha Tin, Kam Tin, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 531; P. S. Choi 214; HK sheet 39744.
Distribution: S, SW, C & E China; Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Japan, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore), dye, ornamental.

Ehretia longiflora Champ. ex Benth. 長花厚殼樹
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 58. 1853; FHK 234. 1861; FKH 176. 1912; FTW 4: 400. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 18. 1990; FFJ 4: 507. 1989; FOC 16: 336. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 395, photo 230. 1998.
Ehretia glaucescens Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 3: 153. 1913.

Deciduous tree, 5–15 m tall; bark dark grey to dark brown, scaly; branchlets glabrous. Petiole 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, elliptic to oblong or oblong‑oblanceolate, 8–15 × 4–8 cm, base broadly cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins 4–7 pairs. Cymes corymbose, terminating lateral branches, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, ebracteate. Flowers sessile or short pedicellate. Calyx 1.5–2 mm, glabrous; lobes semiorbicular, inconspicuously ciliate. Corolla white, tubular‑campanulate, 0.7–1 cm, glabrous; throat 4–5 mm wide; lobes slightly recurved, ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 2–3 mm, shorter than tube. Filaments 0.8–1 cm; anthers ca. 1 mm. Ovary glabrous. Style 0.7–1.5 cm. Drupes pale yellow or red, globose, 0.8–1.5 cm in diam.; endocarp ribbed, divided into four 1‑seeded pyrenes at maturity.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Bride's Pool, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 140, 2393; HK sheet 40351.
Distribution: Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley woods between 1847 and 1850.

Eichhornia crassipes (Mart.) Solms 鳳眼藍
A. DC & C. DC, Monogr. Phan. 4: 527. 1883; FHN 4: 122, fig. 1029. 1977; FFJ 6: 464, fig. 417. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 139, pl. 33. 1997; FOC 24: 41. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 133. 2000; FGD 8: 275, fig. 169. 2007.
Pontederia crassipes Mart., Nov. Gen. Sp. Pl. 1: 9. 1823.
Eichhornia speciosa Kunth, Enum. Pl. 5(4): 131. 1843; FKH 281. 1912.

Aquatic herb, floating, 25–60 cm tall, with long stolons and many black fibrous roots. Stems very short. Leaves radical, rosulate; leaf blade orbicular, broadly ovate, or rhomboidal, 4.5–14.5 × 5–14 cm, leathery, glabrous, densely veined, base shallowly cordate, rounded, or broadly cuneate; petiole 10–40 cm, spongy, usually very much swollen at or below middle. Racemes 7–15-flowered; peduncle 35–45 cm. Perianth segments 6, purplish blue, petaloid, ovate to elliptic, upper one larger, with yellow blotch at centre adaxially, the others subequal but lower one narrower. Stamens 6, 3 long and 3 short; filaments curved, glandular hairy. Pistil heterostylic; stigma glandular hairy. Capsule ovoid.

Locality: Naturalised in Hong Kong. HK sheet 29199.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (naturalized); native to Brazil, now widely introduced and naturalized in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Ponds, ditches, streams, paddy fields. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (forage), noxious weed.

Elaeagnus loureirii Champ. ex Benth. 雞柏紫藤（羅氏胡頹子）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 196. 1853, ‘Loureiri’. FHK 298. 1861; FKH 228. 1912; FRPS 52(2): 9. 1983; FGD 4: 272. 2000.

Evergreen scandent shrub, without thorns; young shoots, abaxial surface of leaves and flowers densely covered with rusty-brown scurfy scales. Leaves alternate, papery; petioles 8 – 12 mm; leaf blade elliptic, ovate-elliptic to ovate-oblong, 4 – 13.5 × 2 – 3.5 cm, base subrounded or cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire, adaxial surface glabrous, greyish green when dry. Flowers usually 2 or 3 together, in lateral clusters or short racemes. Pedicels 8–11 mm. Perianth tubular, lower portion enclosing the ovary, upper portion campanulate, 10–13 mm, apex 4-lobed; lobes triangular, ca. 6 mm. Stamens 4, inserted in perianth-tube. Fruit ellipsoidal, 15 – 20 × 8 – 12 mm, covered with brown scales, orange-red when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mong Tsai, Lantau Island. C. Ford s.n. (HK sheet 5132); S. T. Dunn s.n. (HK sheet 24902); H. C. Tang 2340.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Oct. – Dec.; fruiting: Apr.–May of the following year.
Uses: Food (fruit edible).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Parker by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Food (fruit edible).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Parker by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Elaeagnus tutcheri Dunn 香港胡頹子（塔氏胡頹子）
J. Bot. 45: 404. 1907; FKH 228. 1912; FRPS 52(2): 37, pl. 10: 4 – 6. 1983; FGD 4: 274. 2000.

Evergreen scandent shrub, without thorns; young shoots and flowers densely covered with rusty-brown scurfy scales. Leaves alternate, leathery; petioles 8–11 mm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or obovate, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, base rounded, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or slightly undulate, adaxial surface initially covered with brown scurfy scales, glabrous and shining when full grown, abaxial surface densely covered with silvery and brown scales. Flowers usually 2 or 4 together, in lateral clusters or short racemes. Pedicels 2–3 mm. Perianth tubular, lower portion enclosing the ovary, upper portion campanulate, 4–5 mm, apex 4-lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 3 mm, sparsely stellate-hairy adaxially. Stamens 4, inserted in perianth-tube. Fruit ellipsoidal, 8 – 9 × 5.5 – 6.5 mm, covered with brown scales, orange-red when mature.

Locality: Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai O, Mirs Bay (Ping Chau). C. Ford 553; Y. S. Lau 456, 2833; HK sheet 40174.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Hunan.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Nov. – Dec.; fruiting: Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Food (fruit edible).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Cape D'Aguilar by W. J. Tutcher.
records.uses:
Food (fruit edible).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Cape D'Aguilar by W. J. Tutcher.

records.text:
Elaeocarpus chinensis (Gardn. & Champ.) Hook. f. ex Benth. 中華杜英（野杜英）
FHK 43. 1861; FGD 1:118. 1987; FRPS 49 (1): 22, pl. 4:1– 6. 1989.
Friesia chinensis Gardn. & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 243. 1849; l. c. 3: 264. 1851.
Elaeocarpus integripetalus Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 11: 6. 1943

Small tree, 3 –7 m tall. Branchlets puberulous at first, glabrescent. Petioles 1.5 –2 cm; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 5 –8 × 2–3 cm, thin leathery, base rounded, rarely broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin minutely crenate, abaxially pubescent at first, later glabrescent, black glandular-punctate; lateral veins 4– 6 pairs. Racemes in axils of fallen leaves, 3– 4 cm; rachis and peduncles puberulous. Pedicels ca. 3 mm. Flowers polygamous. Bisexual flowers: sepals lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, puberulous on both surfaces. Petals oblong, ca. 3 mm, margin nearly entire, sparse-puberulous adaxially, glabrous abaxially. Stamens 8 –10, ca. 2 mm; filaments very short; anthers without hairs at apex. Ovary 2-locular. Male flowers: sepals and petals as in bisexual flowers; stamens 8 –10, without pistillodes. Drupe ellipsoid, 7– 8 mm, endocarp with 2 ventral sutures.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. C. Ng 3145; Y. W. Lam 645; P. S. Choi 30.
Distribution: Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley Woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley Woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

records.text:
Elaeocarpus decipiens Hemsl. 杜英
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 94. 1886; FGD 1: 117, fig. 123: 1A–1D. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 33, pl. 6: 10 –14. 1989.
Elaeocarpus lanceaefolius auct. non Roxb.: FHK 42. 1861; Forbes & Hemsley, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 95. 1885.

Small tree, 5 –15 m tall. Branchlets puberulous at first, glabrescent. Petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate, 7–12 × 2– 4 cm, leathery, base attenuate, apex acuminate, tip blunt, margin serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Racemes 5 –10 cm, puberulous; peduncles slender; pedicels 4 – 5 mm. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 5, lanceolate, ca. 5 – 6 mm. Petals 5, white, obovate, as long as sepals, puberulous near base adaxially, glabrous abaxially, laciniate on distal half; segments 10 –16. Stamens 25 –30, anthers without appendage at apex. Disc 5‑lobed, pubescent. Ovary 3-locular, tomentose; ovules 2 per locule. Drupe ellipsoid, 1-locular, 2–3 cm; exocarp glabrous; endocarp bony, with many ventral sutures; seed 1, ca. 1.5 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Long Sai Wan, Long Ke. H. C. Tang 2392; Y. S. Lau 166; Y. W. Lam 1335.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Elaeocarpus dubius A. DC. 顯脈杜英（山模果）
Bull. Herb. Boiss. Ser. 2, 3: 366. 1903; FHN 2: 70. 1965; FGD 1: 121, fig. 126: 1A-1E. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 16, pl. 3: 1– 5. 1989.

Tree to 25 m tall. Branchlets slender, silver-grey-pubescent at first, glabrescent. Petioles slender, 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 5–7(–10) × 2–2.5(–4) cm, thin leathery, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, margin crenate, glabrous; lateral veins 8–10 pairs, reticulation of veins conspicuous when dry. Racemes axillary, 3–5 cm; peduncles silvery grey-white pubescent, 4 –7-flowered. Pedicels 7–9 mm. Sepals 5, narrowly lanceolate, conspicuously keeled, 7–8 mm, puberulous on abaxial surface. Petals 5, as long as sepals, oblong, 7–8 × ca. 2.5 mm, grey-white-pubescent on both surfaces, distal 1/3 laciniate; segments 9–11. Stamens 20 –23; anthers ca. 3.5 mm, with awns (ca. 1.5 mm) at apex. Disc 10-lobed, pubescent. Ovary 3-locular, pubescent; style ca. 5 mm. Drupe ellipsoid, 1–1.3 cm, glabrous; endocarp bony, with 3 ventral sutures.

Locality: Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang. W. J. Tutcher 10219; Y. S. Lau 1516.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was misidentified as E. griffithii Mast. by Tutcher (Rep. Bot. For. Hongk. 1914: 30. 1915).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was misidentified as E. griffithii Mast. by Tutcher (Rep. Bot. For. Hongk. 1914: 30. 1915).

records.text:
Elaeocarpus hainanensis Oliv. 水石榕
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 25: t. 2462. 1896; FHN 2: 67. 1965; FGD 1: 116, fig. 122: 1A–1E. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 8. 1989.

Small tree, to 5 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves clustered at twig apices; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, or oblanceolate, 7–15 × 1.5–3 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin denticulate, glabrous; lateral veins 14–16 pairs. Racemes axillary, 5–8 cm, 2–6-flowered. Flowers 3–4 cm in diam. Bracts persistent, leaf-like, sessile, ovate or elliptic, 1–1.6 cm, base rounded or auriculate, margin dentate. Pedicels 4 cm. Sepals 5, lanceolate, 1.2–2 cm. Petals 5, white, as long as sepals, obovate, hairy, apex laciniate; segments 30–46, 4–6 mm. Stamens many; connective prolonged and awn-like. Disc many-lobed, tomentose. Ovary 2-locular, glabrous; ovules 2 per locule. Style ca. 1 cm. Drupe fusiform, 4–5 cm, ca. 1–1.2 cm in diam.; endocarp hard, with 2 ventral sutures. Seeds ca. 2 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1492; P. S. Choi 359.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, SW Guangxi, SE Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Elaeocarpus japonicus Sieb. & Zucc. 日本杜英
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: pt. 2. 165. 1845; FGD 1: 119. fig. 125: 2A–2D. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 20. 1989.
Elaeocarpus yunnanensis Brandis ex Tutch., Rep. Bot. For. Dept. Hongk. 1914: 30. 1915.
Elaeocarpus japonicus var. euplebius Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 123. 1928; FHN 2: 68. 1965.

Tree, to 25 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Buds sericeous. Petioles 2– 6 cm; leaf blade varied in shape and size, often ovate, sometimes elliptic, obovate, or lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 6–12(–17) × 3–6 cm, leathery, base rounded or obtuse, acute, or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin sparsely dentate, both surfaces densely silvery-grey-sericeous at first, glabrescent, black glandular-punctate abaxially; lateral veins 5– 8 pairs. Racemes axillary, 3– 6 cm. Flowers polygamous. Pedicels 3– 4 mm, puberulous. Bisexual flowers: sepals oblong, ca. 4 mm, pubescent on both surfaces. Petals oblong, as long as sepals, entire or incised, pubescent on both surfaces or only on abaxial surface. Stamens 15; anthers ca. 2 mm, without awns at apex, puberulous. Disc 5- or 10-lobed. Ovary pubescent, 3‑locular; style ca. 3 mm, pubescent. Male flowers: stamens 9 –12; pistillodes present or not. Drupe ellipsoid, 1–1.3 × ca. 0.8 cm, shiny, with 3 ventral sutures; seed 1, ca. 8 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 2159; Y. S. Lau 298; N. K. Chun 40646.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr. –May; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Elaeocarpus nitentifolius Merr. & Chun 絹毛杜英
Sunyatsenia 2: 279. 1935; FHN 2: 68. 1965; FGD 1: 119, fig. 125: 1A–1E. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 19, pl. 5: 1– 5. 1989.

Tree to 20 m tall. Branchlets and petioles silvery-white-sericeous. Petioles 2–4 cm; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, 8–15 × 3.5–7.5 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex long acuminate or nearly caudate, margin densely serrulate, adaxially glabrescent, sericeous along veins, abaxially silvery-white-sericeous, not black-punctate; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Racemes axillary, 2–4.5 cm; rachis hairy; bracts caducous, lanceolate. Flowers polygamous, usually pendulous. Pedicels 4 – 5 mm. Sepals 4 – 5, lanceolate, 4 mm, gray-puberulous abaxially. Petals 4– 5, oblong, ca. 4 mm, glabrous, incised, with 5 or 6 segements. Stamens 12–15; anthers without awns at apex. Disc inconspicuously lobed. Ovary 2-locular, sparsely sericeous; style ca. 2.5 mm, pubescent, 2- or 3-lobed at apex. Drupe ellipsoid, small, shining, 1.5 –2 × 1 cm.

Locality: Pok Fa Lam, Wu Kau Tang, Sheung Wo Hang. W. J. Tutcher 11152; Y. W. Lam 1278; K. L. Yip 4464.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Elaeocarpus sylvestris (Lour.) Poir. 山杜英（膽八樹）
Encycl. Suppl. 11: 704. 1811; FGD 1: 121, fig. 121: 1A–1F. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 24, pl. 1: 1– 6. 1989.
Adenodus sylvestris Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 294. 1790.
Elaeocarpus henryi Hance, J. Bot. 23: 322. 1885.
Elaeocarpus kwangtungensis Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 5: 229. 1924.

Trees to 15 m tall. Branchlets slender, glabrous or sparsely pilose. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade narrowly obovate, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, papery, base narrowly cuneate, apex ± rounded, margin crenate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins usually 5 –6 pairs. Racemes axillary, 4–6 cm, glabrous. Flowers bisexual. Pedicels 3–5 mm, slender, glabrous. Sepals 5, lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, sparsely pubescent. Petals 5, obovate, laciniate on distal half; segments 10–12, pubescent at base abaxially. Stamens ca. 15, 3 mm; anthers without awns at apex. Disc 5-lobed, white-pubescent. Ovary pubescent, 2–3-locular; style ca. 2 mm. Drupe ellipsoid, 1–1.2 cm; endocarp thinly bony, with 3 ventral sutures.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1126; P. S. Choi 140; K. L. Yip 4495.
Distribution: Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Eleocharis acicularis (L.) R. Br. 牛毛氈
Prodr. 1: 224. 1810; Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 2: 154. 1817; FKH 297. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 254. 2000; FGD 8: 291. 2007.
Scirpus acicularis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 48. 1753.
Eleocharis yokoscensis (Franch. & Sav.) Tang & F. T. Wang, FRPS 11: 54, pl. 20: 10–13. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 567. 1988; FYN 15: 590. 2003; FOC 23: 193. 2010.

Perennial, with capillary stolons, usually forming dense mats. Culms erect, capillary, angular-sulcate (usually 4-angled), smooth, 3–10(–30) cm tall, 0.1  .3(–0.5) mm thick, often much elongate in deep or running water. Sheaths thinly membranous, loose, oblique at the mouth, often reddish at the base, the apex scarious and often somewhat inflated. Spikelet ovate to lanceolate, ± flattened, acute, (3–)5–8( –15)-flowered, 2–4(–7) × 1–1.5 mm. Glumes thinly membranous, suberect, oblong-ovate, 1.5–2 × 1–1.5 mm, apex ± obtuse, pale green with scarious margins and often reddish brown sides, the lower ones subdistichous, 1-veined. Perianth segments 1–4, very slender, equalling or exceeding the achenes, often reduced or absent. Stamens 2–3; anthers linear, 0.6–1 mm; connective shortly produced. Sigmas 3. Achenes whitish to light brown, obovate-oblong, 0.7–1 × 0.4–0.5 mm, almost terete or trigonous, on each face with 2 – 4 distinct longitudinal ribs connected by many transverse cross-ridges; epidermal cells transversely linear; style bases minute, depressed pyramidal, 1/3–1/2 as wide as the achene.

Locality: Sha Tin, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling. Y. S. Lau 1501, 2173; S. T. Chan 199.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; N America, Europe, E Russia, Korea, Japan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.

Eleocharis acutangula (Roxb.) Schult. 銳棱荸薺
Mant, 2: 91. 1824; FHN 4: 282. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 255. 2000; FGD 8: 289. 2007; FOC 23. 192. 2010.
Scirpus acutangulus Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 216. 1820.
Eleocharis fistulosa Link, Jahrb. Gewächsk. 3: 78. 1820; FRPS 11: 51. 1961.

Stoloniferous perennial; stolons often terminated by a small tuber. Culms tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 2.5–4 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth. Sheaths up to 10 cm, triangular-acute, pale green to brownish. Spikelets cylindrical, 2–4 cm × 3–4 mm. Glumes ovate to ovate-elliptic, 4–5 mm, rounded, herbaceous, green, margins hyaline. Perianth segments 6, longer than achenes, usually barbellate. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1.5–1.7 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovate, compressed-trigonous, 1.5–2 × 1.4 mm, apex constricted into a short neck, style base subulate-deltoid, surface yellowish brown, indistinctly shallowly pitted transversely oblong epidermal cell.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 1722, 2169, 2225.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Marshes and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Eleocharis atropurpurea (Retz.) J. Presl & C. Presl 紫果藺
Reliq. Haenk. 1(3): 196. 1828; FRPS 11: 62. 1961; FHN 4: 284. 1977; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 571. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 255. 2000; FYN 15: 595. 2003; FGD 8: 290. 2007; FOC 23: 197. 2010.
Scirpus atropurpureus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 14. 1789.

Dwarf annual; rhizome absent. Stems tufted, erect or curved, capillary, angular-sulcate, smooth, 4–15 cm tall, 0.3–0.7 mm thick. Sheaths appressed, purplish or brownish at the base, apex of the uppermost oblique, often attenuate. Spikelets oblong-ovoid, ± obtuse, somewhat angular, densely many-flowered, 2–4 (finally lengthening to 8) mm, 1.5–2 mm across. Glumes elliptic, 0.9–1.3 × 0.5–0.7 mm, apex obtuse, membranous, keeled, 1-veined, with green keel and pale or ± purplish sides. Perianth segments 3–6, slender, minutely retrorsely scabrous to almost smooth, shorter than to about as long as the achene, whitish, translucent, not rarely vestigial or absent. Stamens 1–2; anthers linear or oblong-linear, minutely apiculate, 0.3–0.7 mm. Stigmas 2. Achene black, obovate, biconvex, 0.5–0.7 × 0.3–0.4 mm, smooth, shining; epidermal cells very inconspicuous. Style base minute, flattened, strongly depressed, disciform or depressed-conical, 1/4–1/3 as wide as the achene.

Locality: Castle Peak, Tung Lung Chau. HK sheet 13341, 37014.
Distribution: Anhui, Shandong, Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangsu; widely spread over tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Paddy fields and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Eleocharis dulcis (Burm. f.) Trin. ex Hensch. 荸薺（馬蹄）
Vita Rumphii 186. 1833; FRPS 11: 49. 1961; FHN 4: 280. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 257. 2000; FYN 15: 588. 2003; FGD 8: 288. 2007; FOC 23: 191. 2010.
Andropogon dulcis Burm. f., Fl. Indica 219. 1768.
Eleocharis tuberosa Schult., Mant. 2: 86. 1824; FKH 297. 1912.
Eleocharis plantaginea R. Br., Prodr. 1: 224. 1810; FKH 297. 1912.

Perennial. Stolons elongate, terminated by a small tuber. Tubers 5–7 mm across. Culms tufted, 40–90 cm tall, 3–7 mm thick, terete, transversely sepatate, spongiose, easily flattened when dry. Sheaths 3–20 cm, apex truncate, reddish brown. Spikelet cylindrical, 2–5 × 0.4–0.6 cm. Glumes many per spikelet, ellipticoblong to oblong-obovate, 5–6.5 × 1.7–3.2 mm, apex obtuse to rounded-truncate, sides herbaceous or papery, whitish, margins narrow, hyaline, midrib greenish. Perianth segments 6–8, longer than achenes, flattened below, barbellate above. Stamens 3; anthers 2.5–3 mm long. Stigmas 2. Achenes brown, obovate, biconvex, 1.7–2.2 × 1.5–1.8 mm, apex indistinctly annulate, style base triangular-conical, surface shiny yellowish or greyish brown, indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 536; Y. W. Lam 1775; HK sheet 39700.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Madagascar, W Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Ponds, marshes and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Food (tuber).

Eleocharis equisetina J. Presl & C. Presl 木賊狀荸薺
Reliq. Haenk. 1(3): 195. 1828; FRPS 11: 48. 1961; FHN 4: 280. 1977; FGD 8: 287. 2007.
Eleocharis kuroguwai Ohwi, J. Jap. Bot. 12(9): 654. 1936.
Eleocharis dulcis auct. non (Burm. f.) Trin. ex Hensch.: FOC 23: 191. 2010, p.p.

Perennial. Stolons elongate, terminated by a small tuber. Culms tufted, 30–50 cm tall, 2–3 mm thick, terete, transversely septate, spongiose, easily flattened when dry. Sheaths 5–15 cm, apex truncate, reddish brown, glabrous. Spikelet cylindrical, 2–4 × 0.2–0.3 cm. Glumes oblong-obovate, 3–8 × 4 mm, apex obtuse, subleathery, greenish or brownish, margin hyaline. Perianth 7–8, ca. 1.5 times of achenes. Stamens 3, anthers linear. Stigmas 3. Achenes ca. 2 × 1.2 mm, obovoid or ellipsoidal, biconvex, yellow, apex indistinctly annulate, style base triangular-conical, surface shiny yellowish or greyish brown, indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Yuen Long, Mai Po, Kuk Po, Lai Chi Wo, Tai Mo Shan, Ma Wan. Y. W. Lam 1208, 1848; J. C. Shaw 114.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Japan, SE Asia, India.
Ecology: Marshes and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Eleocharis geniculata (L.) Roem. & Schult. 黑籽荸薺
Syst. Veg. 2: 150. 1817; FHN 4: 284. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 259. 2000; FGD 8: 290. 2007; FOC 23: 197. 2010.
Scirpus geniculatus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 48. 1753.
Eleocharis capitata R. Br., Prodr. 1: 225. 1810; FKH 297. 1912.
Scirpus capitatus Willd., Sp. Pl. 1: 294. 1798. non L. 1753; FHK 394. 1861.
Eleocharis caribaea (Rottb.) S. F. Blake, Rhodora 20: 24. 1918; FRPS 11: 61. 1961.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 7–40 cm tall, 0.2–0.4(–0.7) mm thick. Sheaths 0.5–3 cm, apex obliquely truncate, pale green, to reddish or purple brown below. Spikelets ovoid-globose to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 3–7 × 3–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, closely imbricate, broadly elliptic to ovate, 1.8–2 × 1.2 mm, apex obtuse, sides membranous, pale brown, midrib green. Perianth segments 6–8, slightly longer than achenes, sparsely barbellate. Stamens 2–3; anthers linear, ca. 0.5 mm long. Stigmas 2. Achenes black, broadly obovate, biconvex, 0.9–1 × 0.7– 0.8 mm, rounded, maturing shinny black, ± smooth; style base depressed-conical.

Locality: Sai Wan, Shap Sze Heung, Yung Shue O, San Tau. Y. W. Lam 1640, 2168; Y. S. Lau 669.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Marshes, wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Jul.

Eleocharis ochrostachys Steud. 假馬蹄（假荸薺）
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 80. 1855; FRPS 11: 51. 1961; FHN 4: 282. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 259. 2000; FGD 8: 289. 2007; FOC 23: 192. 2010.
Eleocharis variegata auct. non Kunth: FKH 297. 1912; Check List HK Plants 89. 1993.

Perennial. Stolons elongate, 1.5–2.5 mm thick. Culms tufted, 40–80 cm tall, 2–3 mm thick, terete to weakly angular, without transverse septa, longitudinally canaliculate on surface when dry. Sheaths 6–15 cm, apex mucronulate, pale brown to reddish brown. Spikelets cylindrical to ovoid, 1–2.5 cm × 3–4 m. Glumes several to many per spikelet, ovate to ovate-oblong, 4–5 × 2–2.2 mm, apex obtuse, sides herbaceous, pale green, finely striate, margins broadly membranous. Perianth segments 6–7, much exceeding achenes, barbellate. Stamens 3; anthers 0.7–0.8 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovate, compressed-trigonous, 1.5–2 × 1.3–1.6 mm, apex annulate, surface yellowish brown, shiny, with longitudinal rows of transversely linear-oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Aberdeen, Kwun Tong, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 916, 1302; HK sheet 13364.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Japan, Micronesia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and lakes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Eleocharis pellucida var. japonica (Miq.) Tang & F. T. Wang 稻田荸薺
FRPS 11: 58. 1961; FHN 4: 283. 1977; FYN 15: 593. 2003; FOC 23: 195. 2010.
Eleocharis congesta auct. non D. Don: FGD 8: 292. 2007; Check List HK Plants 312. 2002; 110. 2004.
Eleocharis japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 142. 1865.
Eleocharis congesta D. Don subsp. japonica (Miq.) T. Koyama, FTW 5: 220. 1978, ed. 2, 5: 257. 2000.
Scirpus japonicus (Miq.) Franch. & Sav., Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 109. 1877.
Eleocharis afflata Steud., Zoll. Verz. Ind. Archip. 84. 1851; FKH 297. 1912.
Scirpus afflatus (Steud.) Benth., FHK 394. 1861.

Stoloniferous perennial; stolons often terminated by a small tuber. Culms tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 2.5–4 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth. Sheaths 4–10 cm, triangular-acute, pale green to brownish. Spikelets cylindrical, 2 – 4 cm × 3–4 mm. Glumes ovate to ovateelliptic, ca. 2.2 × 1 mm, rounded, herbaceous, green, margins hyaline. Perianth segments 6, longer than achenes, usually barbellate. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1.5–1.7 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes yellowish brown, broadly obovate, 1.5–2 × 1.4 mm, compressed-trigonous, apex constricted into a short neck, style base subulate-deltoid, surface indistinctly shallowly pitted transversely oblong epidermal cell.

Locality: Sai Kung, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 3089; Y. W. Lam 1703; HK sheet 39235.
Distribution: S, SE & SW China; Russia, Korea, Japan, India, Myanmar, Indochina, Indonesia, Philippines, Europe, N America. Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May – Aug.

Eleocharis retroflexa (Poir.) Urb. 貝殼葉荸薺
Symb. Antill. 2: 165. 1900; FHN 4: 283. 1977; FGD 8: 290. 2007; FOC 23: 193. 2010.
Scirpus retroflexus Poir., Encycl. 6(2): 753. 1805.
Eleocharis chaetaria Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 2: 154. 1817; FRPS 11: 54. 1961.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms tufted, often recurved, 4–14 cm tall, 0.2–0.3 mm thick, angular. Sheaths 0.3–0.5 cm long, apex lanceolate, acute, pale brown to reddish brown below. Spikelets broadly ovate, 3–4 × 1.7–2.5 mm, laterally ± flattened. Glumes 3–8 per spikelet, ± 2-ranked, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 2.5–3 × 1.5–2 mm, pale brown to reddish, sides membranous, apex subacute, margins broad-hyaline, the glumes keeled, keel ± acute. Perianth segments 6, flattened, equalling to slightly longer than achenes, sparsely scabrid above. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–1 × 0.6–0.7 mm, apex rounded, style base depressed-conical, decurrent with apex, surface trabeculate with 7–9 rows of deeply pitted epidermal cells, pale yellow.

Locality: Sai Kung, Lai Chi Wo, Ham Tin, Pui O. Y. W. Lam 1718; S. C. Ng 1080; HK sheet 39295.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia, tropical America.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Eleocharis spiralis (Rottb.) Roem. & Schult. 螺旋鱗荸薺
Syst. Veg. 2: 155. 1817; FRPS 11: 50, pl. 19: 1 – 3. 1961; FHN 4: 281. 1977; FGD 8: 289. 2007.
Scirpus spiralis Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 45, t. 15, fig. 1. 1773.

Stoloniferous perennial. Stolons ca. 3 mm thick. Culms tufted, 30–60 cm tall, 2–4 mm thick, usually triquetrous, rarely subterete, smooth. Sheaths 3–17 cm, light green to purplish, apex often with setaceous blade 1–4 mm. Spikelets cylindrical, yellowish, 1.5–3 cm × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, densely imbricate, broadly obovate, 3.2–4 × 2–2.5 mm, very broadly obtuse to truncate, sides subleathery, yellowish brown. Perianth segments 5–6, slender, shorter than or equalling achenes, rarely longer, pale brownish, sparsely patent-spinulose. Stamens 3; anthers linear, 2–2.3 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes black, obovoid to ovoid, biconvex, 1.5–1.7 × 1.2–1.4 mm, apex rounded or indistinctly annulate, style base conical, surface maturing dark brown, indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Wu Kai Sha, Yuen Long, Yung Shue O, Mai Po, Plover Cove, Tai Ho. J. C. Shaw 671; Y. W. Lam 746, 1142.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; Africa, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Weaving.

Eleocharis tetraquetra Nees 龍師草
Contr. Bot. India 113. 1834; FRPS 11: 55. 1961; FHN 4: 283. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 259. 2000; FGD 8: 291. 2007; FOC 23: 194. 2010.

Stoloniferous perennial; stolons slender. Culms tufted, 30–90 cm tall, 1–2.5 mm thick, acutely 4(–5)-angled. Sheaths 6–15 cm, apex obtuse, mucronulate, pale brown to reddish or purple brown. Spikelet somewhat oblique, oblong or lanceolate, 8–10 × 3–5 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, oblong to ovate, 3–4 × 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse, sides papery, rusty brown above, margins narrowly hyaline, midrib greenish. Perianth segments 6(–8), slightly longer to twice as long as achenes body, retrorsely barbellate, spinules rather long. Stigmas 3. Achenes obovate, flattened trigonous, 1.5–2 × 1–1.2 mm, apex rounded, style base deltoid, surface smooth, maturing greenish brown, ± smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Penny's Bay. J. C. Shaw & R. Corlett 115; Y. W. Law 1593; HK sheet 38291.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Fujian, Jiangxi, Heilongjiang, Liaoning, Sichuan, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Japan, Russia, Afghanistan, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Elephantopus scaber L. 地膽草
Sp. Pl. 814. 1753; FHK 170. 1861; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 242. 1966; FRPS 74: 43. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 938. 1998; FGD 8: 237, fig. 145. 2007.

Erect perennial herbs 15–50 cm tall; stem terete, branched dichotomously at upper portion, strigose and glandular throughout. Radical leaves remained at anthesis, rosulate in arrangement, oblanceolate to spatulate in shape, 5.5– 20 × 1.5–3 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, with a mucro, margin shallowly and irregularly crenate‑serrulate, strigose on both surfaces, and glandular abaxially, lateral pinnate veins 16–17 on each side of the midvein; cauline leaves few, scattered, oblanceolate to oblong, smaller in size, about 1–10 × 0.4–1.2 cm, sessile, strigose on both surfaces, glandular abaxially. Glomerules all stalked, the stalks 2–10 mm; each surrounded by 3 broadly ovate bracts, foliaceous, 6–10 × 10–12 mm, acute and mucronate at apex, shallowly serrulate along margin, densely hairy, glandular, strongly reticulate. Involucres cylindric‑oblong, phyllaries coriaceous, basal white, apical green or tinged purple, hairy and glandular, 2‑seriate; outer 4 involucral bracts lanceolate‑oblong, 4–5 mm, apex long‑acuminate; inner 4 elliptic‑oblong, 8–9 mm, twice longer than the outer ones, apex spinulose. Florets 4 per capitulum, 7 mm; corolla lobes purple, about 2 mm. Cypselae brown, 4 mm, apex truncate, basal portion gradually narrowed, strongly 10‑ribbed and grooved, puberulent and glandular. Pappus setae 5(6 – 8), stiff, purple, 4–5 mm, dilated and scaly at base, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. Y. Chan 1218 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11033 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 555.
Distribution: S, SW & E China; Asia, America and tropical regions of Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Elephantopus tomentosus L. 白花地膽草
Sp. Pl. 814. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 242. 1966; FRPS 74: 45. 1985; FGD 8: 238. 2007.
Elephantopus mollis Kunth, Nov. Gen. Sp. 4: 26. 1820; FTW ed. 2, 4: 938. 1998.

Perennial erect herbs 70–100 cm tall; stems striate; branches many on upper portion, strigose to hirsute, glandular. Basal leaves rosulate, deteriorate before anthesis; lower and middle cauline leaves numerous, obovate‑oblong, 5–17 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base attenuate to form winged petiole, subamplexicaul, apex acute, margin crenate‑serrate, lateral pinnate veins 10–12, pilose and glandular on both surfaces; upper cauline leaves elliptic‑oblong, 3–6 × 1–2 cm, or much smaller upward, subsessile, acute at apex. Capitula sessile and clustered into glomerules, each glomerule subtended with stalk 1–7 cm; and surrounded by 3 broadly ovate‑cordate foliaceous bracts, 8–18 × 8–12 mm, acute and awned at apex, strongly reticulate, serrulate, hairy and glandular. Involucres cylindric‑oblong; phyllaries scarious, hairy and glandular at distal half, in 2 series, each layer with 4 involucral bracts; outer series shorter, 3–4 mm, lanceolate‑oblong, apex long‑acuminate, green near the tip, 1‑veined at the middle; inner ones oblong, twice longer than the outer ones, 6–7 mm, upper half green, awned‑tip. Florets 4 per capitulum, corolla white, 3–4 mm, funnelform, tube slender, glabrous. Cypselae brown, linear‑oblong, 2.5–3 mm, 10‑ribbed, apex truncate, base gradually narrowed, puberulent. Pappus 5 stiff setae, 4 mm, dilated and scaly at base, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2224; S. L. Thrower 472 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11726 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Eleusine coracana (L.) Gaertn. 穇
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 8, t. 1, fig. 11. 1788; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 384. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 66, pl. 18: 10–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 144. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 412. 2000; FOC 22: 482. 2006; FGD 9: 357, fig. 170. 2009.
Cynosurus coracanus L., Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 875. 1759.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, robust, erect or ascending, usually branched, 50–120 cm tall. Leaf blades flat, 30–60 × 0.6–1.2 cm, pilose or glabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous, overlapping. Inflorescence of subdigitate one-sided spikes; the spikes 5–10 cm × 8–10 mm, often incurved at maturity. Spikelets very closely imbricate, ovate, 5–9 mm, 6–9-flowered, not disarticulating at maturity; glumes lanceolate-oblong, scabrid along the winged keel; lower glume 3-veined, 1.5–3 mm; upper glume with additional veins in keel, 1.8–5 mm; lemmas triangular-ovate, 2.2–4.7 mm, keel 3-veined, scabrid and narrowly winged, subacute; palea as long as the lemma, narrowly ovate, keels scabrid, winged. Grain an utricle, ca. 1 mm, yellowish brown, globose, finely striatepunctuate.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 16002.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Ningxia, Henan, Hubei, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in Old World tropics. Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (cereal), animal food (fodder).

Eleusine indica (L.) Gaertn. 牛筋草
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 8. 1789; FHK 429. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 383. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 64, pl. 18: 1–9. 1990; FFJ 6: 143, fig. 117. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 412. 2000; FOC 22: 482. 2006; FGD 9: 356. 2009.
Cynosurus indicus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 72. 1753.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 10–90 cm tall. Leaf blades flat or folded, 10–15 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose on adaxial surface; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, at most sparsely ciliolate. Leaf sheaths laterally compressed and keeled, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose. Inflorescence of 2–7 digitate spikes; the spikes ascending, 3–10 cm × 3–5 mm. Spikelets elliptic, 4.5–8 mm, 3–9-flowered; glumes lanceolate, scabrid along keel; lower glume 1-veined, 1.5–2 mm, lowest floret ca. 3 mm; upper glume with small additional veins in the thickened keel, 2–3 mm; lemmas ovate, 2–4 mm, keeled along small additional veins, keel acute; palea membranous, 2-keeled, shorter than the lemma. Anthers 3, ca. 0.6 mm. Grain ca. 1.5 mm, blackish, oblong or ovate, ventrally grooved, obliquely striate with fine close lines running vertically between the striae.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1025, 2233; S. P. Lau 17.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Eleutherococcus trifoliatus (L.) S. Y. Hu 白簕
J. Arnold. Arb. 61: 110. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 3: 994. 1993.
Zanthoxylum trifoliatum L., Sp. Pl. 270. 1753.
Acanthopanax trifoliatus (L.) Voss, Vilm. Blumengaert. (ed. 3) 1: 406. 1894; FRPS 54: 112, pl. 14: 9 – 11. 1978.
Panax aculeatus Aiton, Hort. Kew. ed. 1, 3: 448. 1789.
Acanthopanax aculeatus (Aiton) H. Witte, Ann. Hort. Bot. Pays.-Bas. 4: 89. 1860; FKH 119. 1912.

Scandent shrub or climber, 2–7 m tall. Branchlets and petioles prickly; prickles short, sharp-pointed, recurved at the tips, broadened and elongated at base. Leaves usually 3-foliolate, rarely 4–5-foliolate, long or short-petiolate; petioles glabrous, slightly prickly or not, 2–6 cm; petiolules 2–8 mm; leaflets papery, elliptic-ovate to elliptic-oblong, 4–8 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate, lateral ones sometimes slightly oblique, apex acuminate, margin generally serrulate, glabrous, sometimes very slightly setose along the midvein and veins adaxially, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces, tertiary veins inconspicuous. Umbels few–many-flowered, forming terminal racemes or compound umbels; peduncles glabrous, 2–7 cm; pedicels slender, glabrous, ca. 1 cm. Calyx glabrous, 1.5 mm, slightly 5-toothed. Petals 5, triangular, 2 mm, glabrous on both surfaces. Stamens 5, filaments 3 mm. Ovary 2-locular; styles 2, connate to middle. Fruit rounded, laterally compressed, 3–4 cm, style-column 1.5 mm, bifid to middle.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1085, 2192; Y. S. Lau 1282.
Distribution: Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Ravines, forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Elsholtzia argyi H. Lév. 紫花香薷
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 8: 425. 1910; FRPS 66: 343. 1977; FOC 17: 254. 1994; FGD 3: 449. 1995.

Herbs 50–100 cm tall. Stems often purplish, grooved, with white hairs in grooves. Leaves opposite; petiole 0.8– 2.5 cm, narrowly winged, white pubescent; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 2–6 × 1–3 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, decurrent, apex shortly acuminate, margin crenate or crenate‑serrate, adaxially sparsely pilose, abaxially impressed glandular, white pubescent on veins. Verticillasters 8‑flowered, forming secund spikes of 2–7 cm; bracts rounded, ca. 5 mm, apex abruptly spinescent, spines to 2 mm, abaxially white villous, yellow glandular, purplish, adaxially glabrous, margin ciliate. Pedicel ca. 1 mm, white pilose. Calyx tubular, ca. 2.5 mm, white villous abaxially; teeth subulate, subequal, apex spinescent, margin ciliate. Corolla rose‑purple, ca. 6 mm, white villous abaxially, glandular at apex; upper lip notched, margin villous; lower lip slightly spreading, middle lobe oblong, apex usually mucronate; lateral lobes arcuate. Anthers dark purple. Nutlets dark brown, oblong, ca. 1 mm, minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan. S. B. C. Ross 11450; Y. S. Lau 2077, 3025.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Elsholtzia ciliata (Thunb.) Hyl. previously (Check List HK Plants 76. 1993).

Embelia laeta (L.) Mez 酸藤子
Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 326. 1902; FRPS 58: 120, pl. 19: 4. 1979; FOC 15: 31. 1996.
Samara laeta L., Mant. Pl. (ed. 2) 199. 1771.
Samara obovata Benth., FHK 205. 1861.
Embelia obovata (Benth.) Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 62. 1889; FKH 159. 1912.

Scandent shrub or climber, 1–3 m or longer. Branches glabrous, ± wrinkled when dry, lenticellate. Leaves alternate; petioles 5 – 10 mm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, obovate to oblong-obovate, 2.5 –5(–7) × 0.8 –2(–2.8) cm, base cuneate, apex subrounded to obtuse, sometimes emarginate, margin entire, glabrous, deep green adaxially, greyish green abaxially, not punctate; lateral nerves 6 –10(–12) pairs, at an angle about 50˚ with midrib, obliquely ascending, anastomosing near edge; veins very fine but conspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescence lateral or axillary, racemose, 3– 8 mm, 3 – 8-flowered, ± glandular puberulous. Bracts ovate, ca. 1 mm, ciliolate. Pedicels 1.5 –2 mm. Flowers white, 4-merous, functionally unisexual, but bear vestigial organs of the opposite sex. Calyx 0.6 –0.8 mm, split to 2/3 of its length; lobes ovate, acute. Corolla-lobes almost free, ovate to oblong-ovate, 1.8 –2 mm, obtuse, glabrous outside, densely papillose adaxially, obscurely punctate. In male flowers, stamens comparatively larger, inserted on base of corolla-lobes, with filaments ca. equaling corolla-lobes; ovary much reduced, without ovules. In female flowers, ovary glabrous, pyriform, with well developed ovules; stamens much reduced. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., obscurely punctate.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. HK sheet 17698; H. C. Tang 115, 785.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margin of forest, shrubby mountain slopes, roadsides. Flowering: Dec.–Mar.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Embelia parviflora Wall. ex A. DC 當歸藤
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 17: 130. 1834; FRPS 58: 113, pl. 17: 5 –7. 1979; FOC 15: 31. 1996.
Embelia myrtifolia Hemsl. & Mez, Notizbl. Bot. Gart. Berlin 3: 107. 1901; FKH 159. 1912.

Scandent shrub or climber, up to 3 m or longer. Branches light brown, with scattered elongate lenticelles; branchlets slender, usually distichous, densely rusty villose, with ± glandular or stellate-tipped hairs. Leaves distichous; petioles 0.5–1 mm, villose; leaf blade papery, ovate to oblong-ovate, ovate, 1–2 × 0.6 –1 cm, base rounded or subtruncate, apex obtuse to broadly obtuse, entire, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface ± puberulous, especially on the raised midvein; glandular dots many, visible on both surfaces when dry; lateral veins fine and very obscure. Inflorescence axillary, subumbellate or cymose, 2–4-flowered, rusty puberulous. Peduncle 1–1.5 mm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Flowers white, 5-merous. Calyx 0.5 –0.8 mm, split to near base; lobes ovate-triangular, acute, minutely ciliate. Corolla slightly united at base; lobes oblong or oblong-elliptic, 1.5 –2 × 1 mm, obtuse, densely papillose on margins and inside. Stamens in male flowers inserted on the lower 1/3 of the corolla-lobes; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers ovoid. In female flowers ovary ovoid, glabrous; style twice as long as the ovary, ± pubescent at base; stigma flattened or disc-shaped. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., dark reddish, ± punctate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 17670.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Dec.–May; fruiting: Jan.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Embelia ribes N. L. Burman 白花酸藤子
Fl. Ind. 62, pl. 23. 1768; FHK 204. 1861; FKH 159. 1912; FRPS 58: 104, pl. 16: 4 – 6. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 154. 1996; FOC 15: 32. 1996.

Scandent shrub or climber, usually 3 – 6 m or longer. Branchlets slender, new growth under the inflorescence minutely puberulous, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles 5 –10 mm; leaf blade obovate-elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 4 – 8(–10) × 1.2–3 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex shortly acuminate, tip blunt, margin entire, slightly recurved, glabrous; glandular dots many, scattered, black or colorless, ± convex when dry; lateral veins many; reticulation of veins distinct on abaxial surfaces when dry. Panicle terminal, 10 –20 cm, with a spread of 10 –18 cm cm at base, densely puberulous, 2–3-branched; secondary branches slender, each bearing many racemosely arranged flowers. Pedicels 1–2 mm. Flowers greenish or whitish, 5- rarely 4-merous, functionally unisexual, but bear vestigial organs of the opposite sex. Calyx ca. 0.5 mm, split about to middle; lobes triangular, acute or obtuse, densely puberulous. Corolla-lobes almost free, elliptic, ca. 1.5 –2 mm, with a few glandular dots, densely papillose outside. In male flowers, stamens adnate ± to middle of corolla-lobes and slightly shorter than them; anthers ovoid or oblong, punctate on back; ovary highly reduced and lack ovules. In female flowers, pistil fully developed, slightly shorter than corolla-lobes, with ovoid glabrous ovary and capitate stigma on a short style; stamens much reduced. Fruit globose, 3– 4 mm in diam., reddish or black, wrinkled when dry.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong; H. C. Tang 11, 2321; Y. S. Lau 924, 1353.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; widely distributed in India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, southwards through Malay Peninsula to Indonesia and New Guinea.
Ecology: Open thickets and disturbed evergreen forest. Flowering: Jan.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Dec.

Embelia rudis Hand.-Mazz. 網脈酸藤子
Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl., Anz. 59: 108. 1922; H. L. Li, Woody Fl Taiwan 717. 1963; FRPS 58: 108. 1979; FOC 15: 33. 1996, pro syn. sub E. vestita Roxb.

Scandent shrub, to 10 m or longer. Branchlets glabrous, copiously lenticellate. Leaves alternate, subleathery; petioles 6–8 mm, marginate, ± puberulous; leaf blade oblong-ovate to ovate, rarely broadly lanceolate, 5–10 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or obtuse, rarely cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin finely or coarsely serrate, glabrous, sparsely and indistinctly punctate; lateral veins many, ending to the teeth; reticulation of veins prominent, raised on both surfaces. Inflorescence racemose, axillary, 1–2(–3) cm, puberulous. Pedicels 2–3(–5) mm; bracteoles subulate, ca. 1 mm, papillose. Flowers greenish or white, 5-merous, 1–2 mm. Calyx united at base; lobes ovate, ca. 0.7 mm, ciliate. Corollalobes almost free, ovate-oblong or elliptic, 1–2 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, ciliate, puberulous or papillose in middle and especially near the base adaxially. Stamens in male flowers ca. equaling corolla-lobes; anthers oblong or ovate, punctate on back. In female flowers ovary pear-shaped or globose, glabrous; style ca. 0.5 mm, curved. Fruit globose, 4–5 mm in diam., blue black or reddish when mature.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau. Y. W. Lam 1397; P. S. Choi 343, 492; H. C. Tang 2231; F. W. Xing 7092, 8192 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.

Embelia undulata (Wall.) Mez 平葉酸藤子
Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 327. 1902; FOC 15: 33. 1996.
Myrsine undulata Wall., Fl. Ind. 2: 299. 1824.
Samara longifolia Benth., FHK 205. 1861.
Embelia longifolia (Benth.) Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 62. 1889; FKH 159. 1912; Anonymous, Check List HK Plants 51. 1993.

Scandent shrub, rarely arborescent, 2– 4 m tall. Branchlets terete, glabrous, ± lenticellate-warty.
