Leaves alternate; petioles 1–1.5(– 2) cm, deeply channelled, black punctate; leaf blade papery to subleathery, elliptic to oblong, or rarely obovate, (4 –)7.5 –11.5(–18) × (1.8 –)3 –5(– 8) cm, base acute or cuneate, decurrent on petiole, apex acute or acuminate, rarely rounded, margin entire, glabrous, with many minute black glandular dots or lines on abaxial surface; lateral veins many, prominent. Inflorescence racemose, 1–2(– 6) cm, usually rising from axils of leaf scars on branches of previous year's growth, puberulent. Flowers yellowish or greenish, 4-merous. Pedicels 1.5 –3 mm. Calyx less than 1 mm, deeply split; lobes triangular or ovate, black punctate. Corolla-lobes almost free, elliptic to ovate, apex obtuse or acute, red punctate abaxially. Stamens inserted at base of corolla-lobes and exserted up to 1 mm, staminodes ca. 2/3 petal length; anthers narrowly oblong, ca. 1 mm. Ovary globose, glabrous; style straight, epunctate; stigma capitate. Fruit globose, (8 –)10 –15 mm in diam., longitudinally ribbed, black punctate.

Locality: Little Hong Kong, Mount Nicholson, Sheung Wo Hang, Lantau Island. HK sheet 2970, 17667; Y. W. Lam 1281.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; India, Nepal.
Ecology: Evergreen forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan.

Embelia vestita Roxb. 密齒酸藤子
Fl. Ind. 2: 288. 1824; FOC 15: 33. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. E. rudis Hand.-Mazz.
Embelia oblongifolia Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 62. 1882; FKH 159. 1912; FRPS 58: 110, pl. 17: 1–3. 1979.

Scandent shrub or climber, to 10 m or longer. Branchlets glabrous or puberulous; old branches copiously lenticellate. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 m, with narrow crisped wings on distal part; leaf blade papery, oblong-elliptic to oblong-ovate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–10 × 2–3.5 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute, margin usually remotely serrate on upper half or near apex, rarely entire, glabrous and glossy, not punctate or with minute glands near apex on abaxial surface; lateral veins 10–18 pairs, with shorter intermediates, at an angle about 70˚ with the midvein, curved-ascending, anastomosing near the edge; reticulation of veins prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, racemose, 1–3 cm, rusty puberulous. Pedicels 3–4 mm, patent, usually at right angle to the rachis. Flowers 5-merous, greenish or white, 2.5–3 mm. Calyx deeply split; lobes broadly ovate, 0.5–0.7 mm, ciliate, sparsely and minutely punctate, glabrous or nearly so. Corolla-lobes almost free, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, ca. 1 mm wide, broadly obtuse or slightly emarginate, glabrous abaxially, densely papillose adaxially, dotted with brown glands. Stamens in male flowers adnate to base of corolla-lobes; anthers ovate, punctate on back. In female flowers ovary pyriforms, glabrous, with a short, curved style. Fruit globose, 6–8 mm in diam., red when mature, ± punctate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 17686, 25195, 30556; Y. S. Lau 1746.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margin of forests, shrubby mountain slopes. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Oct.–Jul.

Emilia prenanthoidea DC. 小一點紅
Prodr. 6: 302. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 243. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 325. 1999.

Annual herbs; stem erect or ascending, 20–80 cm tall, somewhat glaucous, glabrous or loosely pubescent. Basal leaves small, obovate or obovate‑oblong, 3–8 × 1–3 cm, base attenuate into long winged petiole, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or loosely toothed. Middle cauline leaves oblong to linear‑oblong, 2.5–8 × 0.5–1.2 cm, sessile and amplexicaul, base sagittate or auriculate, apex obtuse or acute, margin slightly sinuate toothed, adaxial surface green, abaxial surface purplish, both glabrous or sparsely crisped hairy. Upper leaves linear‑lanceolate, smaller in size. Capitula homogamous and discoid, 1–1.5 cm across, loosely corymbose; peduncles (0.5–)2– 10.5 cm. Involucres cylindric or narrowly campanulate, shorter than florets, which only enclosing lower 1/2 to 2/3 of the florets, base without calyculus; phyllaries about 10 in 1 row, linear‑oblong, 6–8 × 1–2 mm, apex acute or obtuse, margin scarious, abaxial side glabrous. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, 8–11 mm, lower half filiform, upper half gradually widen, apex with 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 2 mm in length, colour red, pink or purple‑pink. Cypselae brown, cylindric, 3 × 0.5 mm, ribbed, glabrous. Pappus copious, capillary and slender, white, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Ma On Shan, Sha Tau Kok, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1251; S. Y. Hu 11808 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22134 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indochina to India.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

Emilia sonchifolia (L.) DC. 一點紅
Contr. Bot. India 24. 1834; Prodr. 6: 302. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 244. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 324, pl. 68: 1–2. 1999; FGD 8: 230, fig. 140. 2007.
Senecio sonchifolia (L.) Moench., Suppl. Meth. 231. 1802; FHK 189. 1861.
Cacalia sonchifolia L., Sp. Pl. 2: 835. 1753.

Annual herbs; stem erect or ascending, 15–40 cm tall, branched near base, glaucous, glabrous or loosely pilose. Leaves mainly clustered at base and lower stem portion, adaxial surfaces green, abaxial surfaces purplish, both subglabrous or sparsely crisped hairy. Basal and lower leaves lyrately pinnati‑lobed, 4.5–11 × 2–6 cm, terminal lobes large, broadly ovate‑deltoid to ovate‑cordate, base semi‑ or totally amplexicaul, for the leaves growing near the middle stem portion having base hastately amplexicaul, apex broadly obtuse or nearly rounded, margin irregularly dentate, midvein below thinly to broadly winged, lateral lobes usually in 1 pair, small triangular, oblong to lanceolate‑oblong, obtuse or acute, sometimes the lateral lobes inconspicuous and even absent in the lowermost leaves, resembling as long winged petiole. Uppermost leaves linear‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 3.5–6 cm, base sessile and amplexicaul, apex acute, margin subentire to irregularly toothed. Capitula homogamous and discoid, 3 – 5 mm across, pendulous before flowering, erect later, non‑calyculate, usually with 2–5 heads arranged as loose corymbs, pedunculate with length of peduncles 2–14 cm. Involucres cylindric with base swollen, 10 – 13 × 3 – 3.5 mm, length subequal to florets or enclosing 5/6 of the florets; phyllaries about 8 in 1 series, linear, apex acute, herbaceous green, margin narrowly scarious, glabrous abaxially. Florets pink or pale purple, 8–11 mm, corolla filiform‑tubular with limb gradually and slightly widen, apex 5 linear‑oblong lobes about 2 mm. Cypselae brown, subterete, 3–3.5 × 0.5 mm, 5‑angulate, puberulent along ribs. Pappus copious, white, capillary and slender, 7–8 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2253; Y. Wong 011 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22274 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Endospermum chinense Benth. 黃桐
FHK 304. 1861; FKH 240. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 183, pl. 48: 1 – 6. 1996; FGD 5: 123, fig. 75. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 256. 2005.

Tree up to 5 m tall; young branches, petioles, inflorescences and fruits covered with minute scaly tomentum. Leaves usually crowded towards apex of branchlets, thinly leathery; stipules triangular-ovate, 3–4 mm, hairy; petioles 4–9 cm; leaf blade elliptic, ovate, broadly ovate or subrotund, 8–20 × 4–14 cm, base broad-cuneate, truncate to shallowly cordate, with 2 large convex glands near the insertion of petiole, apex acute to obtuse, subglabrous or sparsely stellate-hairy abaxially, margins entire; lateral veins 5 – 7. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary, male 10–20 cm, female 6–10 cm, bracts ovate, 1–2 mm. Male flowers: calyx cupular, with 4–5 shallow crenulation; stamens 5–12, in 2–3 series, filaments ca. 1 mm. Female flowers: calyx cupular, ca. 2 mm, undulately 3–5-lobed, hairy, persistent; disk annular, 2–4-lobed; ovary subglobose, tomentulose, 2–3-locular. Fruits subglobose, ca. 1 cm in diam., pericarp slightly fleshy, tomentose.

Locality: Aberdeen, Stubbs Rd., Shing Mun, Tai Po, Ho Chung, Tolo Harbour. C. P. Lau 96; H. C. Tang 2490; HK sheet 24847.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Environmental, Material (timber), medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected by J. G. Champion and H. F. Hance from Aberdeen, Hong Kong Island around 1850.

Environmental, Material (timber), medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected by J. G. Champion and H. F. Hance from Aberdeen, Hong Kong Island around 1850.

Engelhardia fenzelii Merr. 白皮黃杞
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 300. 1929; FRPS 21: 13, pl. 3: 2. 1979; FGD 2: 322. 1991.
Engelhardtia roxburgiana auct. non. Wall.: FOC 4: 278. 1999, p.p. (quoad syn. Engelhardtia fenzelii Merr.)

Tree, 5–15 m; bark greyish yellow; branchlets greyish white, lenticellate. Bud, young branches, leaf axis, inflorescence and fruit with golden or brownish yellow peltate scales. Petioles 1.5–3 cm. Leaves 8 –18 cm; leaflets usually 2 pairs, sometimes 1 pair, subopposite, leathery, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 6 –9 × 2.5 – 5 cm, asymmetrical, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, olive or pale brown and glossy when dried; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, inconspicuous; petiolules 3– 6 mm. Inflorescence terminal, slightly pendulous, ca. 10 × 4 cm; peduncle 2– 4 cm, with peltate scales. Nutlet glabrous, 3– 4 mm. Persistent bract membranous, 3-lobed, densely covered with brownish yellow peltate scales; lobes glabrous, central lobe 2.5 × 0.8 cm, lateral lobes 1.5 × 0.6 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 887; C. P. Lau 115.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Engelhardia roxburghiana Lindl. ex. Wall. 黃杞
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 85. 1831; FRPS 21: 12, pl. 3: 1. 1979; FGD 2: 322, fig. 212. 1991; FOC 4: 278. 1999, excl. syn. E. fenzelii Merr. & E. unijuga Chun ex P. Y. Chen.
Engelhardtia chrysolepis Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Ser. 4, 15: 227. 1861.
Engelhardtia formosana Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6: 61. 1916.
Engelhardtia wallichiana auct. non Lindl.: FKH 251. 1912.

Tree to 30 m tall; bark dark brown. Branchlets purplish or dark brown. Buds, young branches, abaxial surfaces of leaves and inflorescence covered with brown peltate scales. Petioles 3 –8 cm. Leaves 12–25 cm; leaflets 3 – 5 pairs, oblong, oblong‑elliptic or ovate, 5 –12 × 2– 4 cm, asymmetrical, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, lateral veins 10 –13 pairs; petiolules 0.6 –1.5 cm. Inflorescence terminal, pendulous. Infructescence 15 –25 cm. Nutlet globose, densely covered with peltate scales, 4 mm in diam. Persistent bract membranous, 3‑lobed, densely covered with peltate scales, lobes glabrous, central lobe 3 –5 × 0.8 –1.2 cm, lateral lobes 1.5 –2 × 0.5 –0.8 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po Kau, Tseng Lan Shue. Y. S. Lau 1437, 2718.
Distribution: S & SW China; Indochina, Indonesia, Myanmar, E Pakistan, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Enkianthus quinqueflorus Lour. 吊鐘花
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 277, 1790; FHK 200. 1861; FKH 154. 1912; FRPS 57(3): 12, pl. 4: 1–2. 1991; FOC 14: 245. 2005.

Deciduous or semi-deciduous shrub or trees, 1–3(–10) m tall, glabrous throughout, with whorled branches. Leaves crowded at ends of branches; petiole 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade obovate-lanceolate to elliptic, rarely lanceolate, 5–12.5 × 1.8–4 cm, base cuneate to attenuate, apex acuminate or shortly to abruptly acuminate, margin entire, thick papery to leathery, shining adaxially, reticulation of veins raised and prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence single and terminal, umbellate, 6–8(–16)-flowered, enclosed in imbricate, reddish scales in buds; scales ovate to pyriformis, glabrous, margins ciliated, apex obtuse with a blunt point, up to 9–16 × 6–8 mm. Pedicels 1–2 cm, usually curved and pointing downward. Calyx 5-lobed, reddish; lobes triangular ovate to triangular, 2–3 × 1.5–2 mm. Corolla broadly campanulate, ca. 1.2 cm in diam., depth ± equals to diam., pink, red, or white, shortly 5- lobed; tube broad; limb 0.8–1.2 cm in diam.; lobes triangular ovate, obtuse, about 1/3 length of corolla-tube, more or less recurved. Stamens 10, included; filaments puberulent; anther-cells tipped with awn-like appendages. Ovary glabrous or densely pubescent; style ca. 4 mm. Capsule ovoid, 5-angled, ca. 1.2 × 1.0 cm; stalk erect; seeds several to many.

Locality: Harlic Road, Wong Nai Chung, Beacon Hill, Kadoorie Farm & Botanic Garden, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Sunset Peak. H. C. Tang 1860; Y. S. Lau 1754; S. Y. Hu 13593 (IBSC); F. W. Xing 6879 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Common in Hong Kong, occasionally abundant in open hillside shrublands, alt. 50–700 m. Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Majority of individuals in Hong Kong are deciduous; emergence of young leaves occur after the older leaves fall, and the leafless period often coincides with flowering. However, a significant proportion of plants produce young leaves and even flowers before old leaves fall.

Entada phaseoloides (L.) Merr. 榼藤

Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 9: 86. 1914; FRPS 39: 13. 1988; FGD 5: 158, fig. 92. 2003.

Lens phaseoloides L. Herb. Amb. 18. 1754.


Evergreen, large, woody climber. Stems spirally twisted. Branches glabrous. Petioles short; leaves 10 – 25 cm; pinnae usually 2 pairs; leaflets 1 – 2(–4) pairs, opposite, apical pair of pinnae transformed into tendril; leaflets leathery, elliptic or long-obovate, 3 – 9 × 1.5 – 4.5 cm, base slightly oblique, apex obtuse, emarginate. Spikes 15 – 25 cm, densely flowered, solitary or forming a panicle, villose. Flowers small, white, slightly fragrant. Bracts pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 2 mm, 5-toothed. Petals 5, oblong, 4 mm, glabrous, apex acute, slightly united at base. Stamens slightly longer than corolla. Ovary glabrous, style filiform. Pods up to 100 × 8 – 12 cm, curved, flat, with a parchment-like endocarp. Seeds dark brown, orbicular, 4–6 cm in diam., flat, testa woody, brilliant.


Locality: Tai Po Kau, Mau Ping, Hoi Ha, Kei Ling Ha Lo Wai. Y. S. Lau 2571; Y. W. Lam 574; K. Y. Tam 120.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan.

Ecology: Forests. Fruiting: Apr.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Enteropogon dolichostachyus (Lag.) Keng ex Lazarides 腸鬚草
Austral. J. Bot., Suppl. Ser. 5: 31. 1972; FOC 22: 490. 2006.
Chloris dolichostachya Lag., Gen. Sp. Pl. 5. 1816; FHN 4: 386, fig. 1194. 1977.
Enteropogon dolichostachyus (Lag.) Keng, Claves Gen. Sp. Gram. Prim. Sinic. 197. 1957 (nom. inval.); FTW ed. 2, 5: 406, pl. 165. 2000; FGD 9: 375, fig. 184. 2009; Check List HK Plants 334. 2002; 117. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, (0.5–)1–1.5(–2) m tall. Leaf blades linear, flat or rolled, 15–45 × 0.4–1.5 cm, midrib white, conspicuous, surface scabrous, loosely glandular hairy, often tuberculate-hispid near ligule, apex setaceous; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, fimbriate; leaf sheaths glabrous or tuberculate-hispid, especially on margin, pilose at mouth. Spikes 10–20 cm, 3–5(–10) digitately arranged, ascending at first, later divaricate or drooping; rachis triquetrous, scabrous. Spikelets 5–7 mm, 2-flowered; glumes papery, deltoid-lanceolate, apex acute and aristate, conspicuously 1-veined; lower glume linearlanceolate, 2–3 mm; upper glume lanceolate, 3–5 mm, awnpointed; lemma of fertile floret purplish, oblong-lanceolate, 3.5–5 mm, glabrous, scabrous along either side of midvein and toward apex; awn 8–16 mm; palea linear-lanceolate, upper margin siliceous, with the same texture and length as the lemma, keels scabrous; upper floret reduced to an oblong 0.8 – 1.8 mm sterile lemma with 2–5 mm awn, appressed to fertile floret. Caryopsis reddish brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm.

Locality: Ping Chau. S. C. Ng 2031.
Distribution: Hainan, S Yunnan, Taiwan; Afghanistan through India to SE Asia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Epaltes australis Less. 球菊（鵝不食草）
Linnaea 5: 148. 1831; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 245. 1966; FRPS 75: 56. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 942. 1998; FGD 8: 166, fig. 92. 2007.
Sphaeromorphaea australis (Less.) Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 6(2): 80. 1937.

Annual herbs; stem 7–30 cm, prostrate, branched at base, shallowly striate, loosely pilose. Leaves sessile, obovate to oblanceolate, 1–4 × 0.3–1.5 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin irregularly dentate, both surfaces sparsely pilose and pitted. Capitula many, growing laterally, subsessile or shortly pedunculate, globose first and then become broader. Involucres hemispherical, 4–5 mm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, green, scarious; outer 2 layers ovate to obovate, 1–2 mm, apex rounded; inner 2 layers obovate‑oblong, 2–2.5 mm, obtuse. Receptacle slightly convex, glabrous. Outer pistillate florets numerous, fertile, corolla tubular, 1 mm, distally narrowed and with apex minutely 3‑lobed, bottom inflated, loosely glandular; stylar branches blunt and exserted. Central bisexual florets fewer, functionally staminate, corolla tubular, campanulate, 1.2 mm, apex 4 triangular and obtuse lobes, pale purple to pink in colour, slightly glandular; stamens 4. Cypselae of outer female florets obovoid‑oblong, 1 mm, 10‑ribbed, apex truncate, base narrowed and hairy, glandular. Those of disk florets similar but empty. Pappus absent.

Locality: Fanling, Sha Tin, Tsim Bei Tsui, Pak Shek Kok, Ho Pui, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 670; S. Y. Hu 11888, 12521 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Moist places of abandoned lands. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.

Epiphyllum oxypetalum (DC.) Haw. 曇花
Phil. Mag. 6: 109. 1829; FHN 1: 494. 1964; FGX 1: 738. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 284. 1999; FGD 4: 138. 2000.

Shrubby succulent plant, 2.5–3 m tall. Branch-joints flat, green, 15–40 × 5–6 cm, thickened in the middle, margin undulate, with areoles, unarmed. Flowers solitary, arising from areoles, white, nocturnal. Perianth-tube 15–20 cm; limb 10–12 cm in diam.; segments many, outer ones scale-like, 2.5–3 mm, inner ones lanceolate, 5–6 cm; stamens many; anthers light yellow. Ovary ovoid, slightly angled; style 16–18-cleft.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 2053.
Distribution: Mexico, Mesoamerica; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: In Hong Kong usually cultivated as a pot plant. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Epipogium roseum (D. Don) Lindl. 虎舌蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 1: 177. 1857; Barretto, Mem. Hong Kong Nat. Hist. Soc. 18: 47, fig. 1. 1988; FRPS 18: 43. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 863. 2000; FGD 7: 334, fig. 163. 2006; FOC 25: 208. 2009.
Limodorum roseum D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 30. 1825.

Saprophytic herb, pink-white, lacking chlorophyll, 30–40 cm tall at flowering time; rhizome fusiform, 2–3 ×1–1.5 cm; upright stems, 20–30 cm tall, bearing scale-like bracts and terminal racemes. Flowers white to pink, pedicellate, resupinate, nutant after anthesis, about 10 in a raceme; bracts longer than ovary; pedicels 2 mm, bending; sepals and petals alike, ovate-lanceolate, 8–12 × 2–4 mm; lip white with irregular patches of rose-mauve, ovate, 8–10 mm, trowel-shaped, spur clavate, 5.5 mm; column 3.5–4 mm, apex auriculate; anther fleshy; pollinia 2, glandular. Capsule oblong, 7 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak. HK sheet 34554.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Xizang, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, India, Thailand, E Himalayan regions, then eastward to the Philippines and Australia.
Ecology: Shade places in forests. Flowering: May.

Epipremnum pinnatum (L.) Engl. 麒麟葉
Pflanzenr. 37(4, 23B): 60. 1908; FGZ 694. 1956; FRPS 13(2): 28, pl. 4: 1 – 7. 1979; FYN 2: 749, fig. 203: 1 – 7. 1979; FFJ 6: 414, fig. 375. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 681, pl. 293, photo 72. 2000; FGD 9: 183, fig. 100. 2009; FOC 23: 15. 2010.
Pothos pinnata L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2: 1374. 1763.
Epipremnum mirabile Schott, Gen. Aroid. t. 79. 1858; FKH 289. 1912.
Rhaphidophora pinnata Schott, Bonplandia 5: 45. 1857; FHN 4: 133, fig. 1037. 1977.

Robust liana; stem terete, 2.5–4 cm thick at base, adhering to trees or rocks by means of aerial roots. Leaves large; petiole 25–40 cm, articulate at apex. Leaf blade of juvenile plants lanceolate to lanceolate-oblong, base shallowly cordate, that of adult plants oblong to broadly oblong, 40–60 × 30 – 40 cm, base broadly subcordate, apex acute, regularly pinnatifid and often small perforations along both sides of midrib; lateral lobes 12–13 on each side, narrowly lanceolate to somewhat falcate. Peduncle terete, 10–14 cm; spathe 10–12 cm, apex acuminate; spadix cylindrical, ca. 10 cm, sessile; ovary hexagonal, apex truncate. Berries ellipsoidal, several-seeded.

Locality: New Territories. W. J. Tutcher 9122.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula, Philippines, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests, climbing on trees and rocks. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Eragrostis atrovirens (Desf.) Trin. ex Steud. 鼠婦草
Nom. Bot., ed. 2, 1: 562. 1840; FHN 4: 376. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 16, pl. 4: 1–2. 1990; FFJ 6: 150. 1995; FOC 22: 474. 2006; FGD 9: 349. 2009.
Poa atrovirens Desf., Fl. Atlant. 1: 73, pl. 17. 1798.
Eragrostis elegantula (Kunth) Nees ex Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 266. 1854; FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect from the geniculate base, 50–120 cm tall, 4–6(–8)-noded. Leaf blades flat or inrolled, 4–17 × 0.2–0.3 cm, adaxial surface scabrous, near base pilose, abaxial surface glabrous; ligules a ciliolate membrane, 0.2–0.3 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous but pilose along summit. Panicle open, 5–20(–25) × 2–15 cm; branches 1–several per node. Spikelets plumbeous and purplish, narrowly oblong, 5–15(–25) × 1.5–2.5 mm, 8–50-flowered, pedicels 0.5–5(–15) mm; breaking up from the base, rachilla persistent, glabrous in axils; glumes subequal, ovate-elliptic, 1-veined; lower glume ovate, 1–1.3 mm, apex acute; upper glume narrowly ovate, 1.3–2.3 mm, apex acuminate; lemmas broadly ovate and acute to subacute when flattened, 1.8–2.2 mm, apex acute; palea loosely ciliate along keel, 1.6–1.8 mm. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–1 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. W. Lam 809, 1323; HK sheet 42029.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Roadsides, stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Eragrostis autumnalis Keng 秋畫眉草
Contr. Biol. Lab. Chin. Assoc. Advancem. Sci. Sect. Bot. 10: 178. 1936; FRPS 10(1): 24, pl. 6: 4. 1990; FFJ 6: 149. 1995; FOC 22: 476. 2006; FGD 9: 348. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect from the geniculate base, 15–45 cm tall, 3–4-noded, often branched at the lower nodes. Leaf blades usually inrolled or plicate, 6–12 × 0.2–0.3 cm; ligules a line of hairs; leaf sheaths compressed, glabrous, along summit with long deciduous hairs. Panicle 6–15 × 3–5 cm; branches usually clustered, glabrous in axils. Spikelets grey-green, 3–5 × ca. 2 mm, 3–10-flowered, with pedicels 1–5 mm; glumes 1-veined, lower glume ca. 1.5 mm, upper glume ca. 2 mm; lemma broadly ovate, apex acute, lower lemma ca. 2 mm; palea ca. 1.5 mm, 2-keeled, along keels ciliate, persistent or tardily deciduous. Stamens 3; anthers ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis red-brown, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Chuen Lung. Y. S. Lau 2223; Y. W. Lam 938.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Grasslands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Eragrostis perennans Keng previously (Check List HK Plants 92. 1993).

Eragrostis brownii (Kunth) Nees 長畫眉草
Cat. Indian Pl. 105. 1834; FOC 22: 473. 2006; FGD 9: 351. 2009.
Eragrostis zeylanica Nees & Meyen, Nov. Act. Acad. Caes Leop-Carol, 19(Suppl.): 204. 1843; FHK 433. 1861; FHN 4: 378. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 13, pl. 3: 1–2. 1990; Check List HK Plants 335. 2002; 117. 2004.
Eragrostis elongata auct. non Jacq.: FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 15–60 cm tall, 2–5-noded, branched at lower nodes. Leaf blades flat or inrolled, 3–10 cm × 1–3 mm; ligules membranous, ca. 0.2 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous and smooth, pilose along summit. Panicle 3–18 cm; branches solitary with spikelets at base. Spikelets livid green, purplish or dark brown, oblong-elliptic, 4–20 × 1.5–2.5 mm, 7–manyflowered, subsessile or with very short pedicel, apex acute; glumes ovate-lanceolate, 1–2 mm; lower glume 1-veined, ca. 1.2 mm; upper glume 1–3-veined, the laterals usually faint, ca. 1.8 mm; lower lemmas 2–2.5 mm; palea slightly shorter than lemma, 1.5–2 mm, ciliolate along keels, apex emarginate. Stamens 3; anthers 0.3–1.3 mm. Caryopsis dark brown, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. HK sheet 8666, 16144, 42043.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; widely spread over Japan, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Open fields, mountain slopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Spring.

Eragrostis cumingii Steud. 珠芽畫眉草（扭枝畫眉草）
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 266. 1854; FOC 22: 475. 2006; FGD 9: 348. 2009.
Eragrostis reflexa Hack., Philip. J. Sci. 3: 168. 1948; FRPS 10(1): 13, pl. 3: 3–5, 120: 2. 1990; Check List HK Plants 335. 2002; 117. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms erect, ca. 25 cm tall, glabrous, usually with scaly buds at base. Leaf blades linear, inrolled, 5  9 × 0.1–0.2 cm, glabrous on both surfaces, except with long pilose at base of adaxial surface; ligule 0.1–0.3 mm, fimbriate; leaf sheaths compressed at base, glabrous, but long pilose along summit. Panicle open, 8–30 × 4–8 cm; branches solitary, naked at lower part, glabrous in axils. Spikelets yellowish green or grey-green, narrowly oblong, 5–20 × 2–2.5 mm, 8–40-flowered, pedicels without glands; glumes papery, deltoid-oblong, easily falling off when mature, lower glume 1-veined, ca. 1 mm, upper glume 1–3-veined, ca. 1.3 mm; lemmas broadly ovate, lateral veins nearly parallel, lower lemma ca. 2 mm; palea papery, oblanceolate, persistent or tardily deciduous, strongly 2-keeled, along keels ciliolate. Anthers ca. 0.2 mm. Caryopsis elliptic, terete to laterally flattened, 0.8–1 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2262; HK sheet 8665, 16143.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hubei Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang; Japan, SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Open fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Eragrostis curvula (Schrad.) Nees 彎葉畫眉草
Fl. Afr. Austral. Ill. 397. 1841; FRPS 10(1): 18, pl. 120: 9, 124: 1. 1990; FFJ 6: 152. 1995; FOC 22: 474. 2006. Poa curvula Schrad., Gött. Gel. Anz. 3: 2073. 1821.

Perennial herb. Culms densely tufted, erect, 80–120 cm tall, slightly compressed at the base. Leaf blades linear to filiform, (5–)10–40 cm × 1–2.5(–3) mm, attenuate to a fine point, arcuate spreading, scabrous; leaf sheaths scabrous with retrorse hairs at lower part, glabrous upward, shorter than internodes, long pilose along the summit. Panicles open, 12–35 × 6–9 cm; branches solitary or in pairs, ascending, naked at base, at least the lower densely pilose in axils. Spikelets grey-green, (4–)6–11 × 1.5–2 mm, 5–16-flowered, breaking up from the base, rachilla persistent below but fragile above; glumes lanceolate, apex acuminate, 1-veined, lower glume lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm, upper glume narrowly ovate, 1.8–2.5 mm; lemmas broadly oblong, apex acute or obtuse, veins prominent, 1.8–2.6 mm, appressed to the rachilla; palea subequal to lemma, 2-keeled, smooth or minutely scaberulous on the keels, persistent or tardily deciduous. Stamens 3; anthers 0.8–1.2 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal to obovoid, dorsally compressed, adaxial surface with a shallow, broad groove or ungrooved, smooth, mostly translucent, light brown, 1–1.7 mm.

Locality: Mai Po, Shing Mun (introduced). Y. S. Lau 3039; HK sheet 34228.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangxi, Yunnan, Xinjiang, Hubei, Jiangsu, Fujian; native to Africa.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Animal food (fodder), ornamental.

Eragrostis cylindrica (Roxb.) Nees ex Hook. & Arn. 短穗畫眉草
Bot. Beechey Voy. 251. 1838; FFJ 6: 150, fig. 123. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 418. 2000; FOC 22: 473. 2006; FGD 9: 350. 2009.
Poa cylindrica Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 335. 1820.
Eragrostis geniculata Nees & Meyen, Gramineae 71–72. 1841; FHK 433. 1861; FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, ascending from the geniculate base, 20–70 cm tall, glabrous, 3–4-noded. Leaf linear, usually inrolled, 3–15 cm × 2–5 mm, pilose; ligules reduced into a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths shorter than internodes, pilose, especially near the summit. Panicle constricted and spike-like, 2 –8 × 1–2.5 cm, lower branches 0.5–1.5 cm, erect-ascending, pilose in axils. Spikelets yellowish brown or tinged with purple, sessile or nearly so, ca. 7 cm × 22.5–3 mm, 4–17-flowered; glume 1-veined, lanceolate, apex acute, lower glume ca. 1.5 mm, upper glume ca. 2 mm; lemma papery, ovate-oblong, apex mucronate, lowest lemma ca. 2 mm; palea persistent, elliptic, papery, ca. 1.8 mm, apex acute, along keels and margins ciliate. Stamens 3. Caryopsis yellow, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lantau Island. HK sheet 42012, 42014.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Eragrostis fauriei Ohwi 佛歐里畫眉草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo). 55: 278. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 5: 420. 2000; FOC 22: 474. 2006.
Eragrostis stenophylla auct. non Hack.: FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms densely tufted, erect, glabrous, 30–60 cm tall. Leaf blades leathery, 10 × 2–5 mm, margins inrolled; ligule long ciliate; leaf sheaths shorter than the internode. Panicle 10–15 cm, loose, branches ascending, scabrous, axils glabrous. Spikelets lanceolate, slightly compressed, 5–10 × 2.5 mm, 6–15-flowered, ascending or slightly appressed, distinctly pedicellate, greyish or slightly tinged with purple; glumes broadly lanceolate, acuminate, 1-veined; lower glume 1–1.5 mm; upper glume 1.5–1.7 mm; lemmas ca. 2 mm, ovate, apex acute; minutely punctate, keels distinctly scabrous, lateral veins distinct, subparallel, ca. 2/3 length of lemma; palea persistent, keels arc-shaped, ciliate-scabrous; rachilla persistent, slightly compressed; stamens 3, anthers oblong, blackish purple, ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis elliptic, slightly compressed, obscurely striolate, ca. 0.7 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung. L. T. Lo 553; HK sheet 8688.
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Eragrostis ferruginea P. Beauv. 知風草
Ess. Agrostogr. 71. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 22, pl. 122: 8. 1990; FFJ 6: 151. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 420. 2000; FOC 22: 475. 2006; FGD 9: 350. 2009.
Poa ferruginea Thunb., Syst. Veg., ed. 14 (J. A. Murray). 114. 1784.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 30–110 cm tall. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, (4–)20–40 × 2–6 mm, glabrous or sparingly covered with silky hairs on basal part of adaxial surface; ligules a line of hairs, ca. 1 mm; leaf sheaths laterally compressed, densely pilose along margins and summit, sometimes glandular along main vein. Panicle large and open, 15–40 × 4–15 cm, 1–3-branched at each node, glabrous in axils; branchlet and pedicel usually glandular at middle or above middle. Spikelets oblong, blackish purple, grey-green, rarely yellowish green, 5–10 × 2–2.5 mm, (4–)7–12-flowered; glumes subleathery, lanceolate, open, 1-veined, apex acuminate, lower glume linear-lanceolate, 1–2 mm, upper glume lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm; lemmas subleathery, ovatelanceolate to oblong, 2.4–3 mm, 3-veined, apex obtuse, lower lemma ca. 3 mm; palea persistent, papery, elliptic, ca. 2 mm, 2-keeled, ciliolate along keels. Anthers ca. 1 mm. Caryopsis rectangular-prismatic with a shallow, narrow adaxial groove, laterally compressed, faintly striate, reddish brown, 0.7–1.5 mm.

Locality: Clear Water Bay. Y. S. Lau 3099, 3190.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shaanxi, Anhui, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Laos, Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Eragrostis japonica (Thunb.) Trin. 亂草
Mém. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Pétersb., Sér. 6. 1: 405. 1831; FRPS 10(1): 30, pl. 123: 4. 1990; FFJ 6: 147. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 420. 2000; FOC 22: 479. 2006; FGD 9: 347. 2009.
Poa japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 51. 1784.
Eragrostis tenella auct. non P. Beauv.: FHK 431. 1861.
Eragrostis interrupta auct. non P. Beauv.: FKH 328. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, 30–100 cm tall, 3–4-noded. Leaf blades flat, 3–25 × 0.3–0.5 cm, smooth and glabrous; ligule scarious, ca. 0.5 mm, truncate, ciliate at apex; leaf sheaths usually loose, longer than internodes, glabrous. Panicle elongate, 6–40 × 1.5–6 cm, branches 3–14 cm, slender, clustered or verticillate, glabrous in axils. Spikelets usually purplish at maturity, ovate, 1–2(–3) mm, 4–8-flowered; rachilla fragile, distarticulating between florets from top downward at maturity; glumes papery, ovate-lanceolate, subequal, 0.6–0.8 mm, 1-veined, apex acute to obtuse; lemmas papery, broadly elliptic, distinctly 3-veined, basal part inrolled, apex obtuse, lower lemma ca. 1 mm; palea subequal to lemma, 2-keeled, scabrous along keels. Stamens 2; anthers ca. 0.2 mm. Caryopsis red-brown, ovoid, circular in cross-section, 0.3–0.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. HK sheet 8675.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines.
Ecology: Open fields, roadsides, stream banks and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Eragrostis pilosa (L.) P. Beauv. var. imberbis Franch. 無毛畫眉草
Nouv. Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat. Paris 11, 7: 145, 1884; Fl. Ill. Pl. Prim. Sin. Gram. 315. 1959; FRPS 10(1): 23, pl. 121: 1. 1990; FFJ 6: 150. 1995.
Eragrostis pilosa auct. non (L.) P. Beauv, Check List HK Plants 92. 1993.

Annual herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 15–30 cm tall, 4-noded, smooth. Leaf blades flat or inrolled, 6–20 × 0.2–0.4 cm, glabrous; ligule ca. 0.4 mm, upper half turned into a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous at mouth, compressed, margin submembranous. Panicle elliptic to ovate, 10–25 × 3.5–14 cm; branches solitary to verticillate, glabrous in axils, usually ascending, pedicels as long or longer than spikelets. Spikelets linear, 3–10 × 1–1.5 mm, purplish-green, 4–14-flowered, florets ± appressed to the rachilla, breaking up from the base, the rachilla persistent; glumes membranous, lanceolate, apex acuminate, lower glume without vein, 0.4–0.7 mm, upper glume indistinctly 1-veined, 0.7–1.3 mm; lemmas papery, ovate, apex acute, lower lemma ca. 1.8 mm; palea papery, oblanceolate, apex obtuse, ca. 1.5 mm, along keels persistent or tardily deciduous ciliate. Stamens 3; anthers 0.1–0.3 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal with one side straight, 0.6–1 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Wong Nai Chung. H. C. Tang 1916; HK sheet 8677.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China (except Xinjiang, Gansu); very widely distributed in tropical and warm regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Farmlands and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting : Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Eragrostis pilosissima Link 多毛知風草
Hort. Berol. 1: 189. 1827; FHK 432. 1861; FKH 329. 1912; FHN 4: 377. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 18, pl. 122: 1. 1990; FFJ 6: 154. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 423. 2000; FOC 22: 474. 2006; FGD 9: 352. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect, slender and rigid, 30–40 cm tall. Leaf blades usually inrolled, 5–10 × 0.1–0.2 cm, densely pilose on both surfaces; ligule a fringe of hairs, ca. 0.3 mm; leaf sheaths densely pilose, usually shorter than internodes but longer than internodes at base. Panicle lax, 4–10 × 2–5 cm; branch usually solitary, slender, glabrous in axils. Spikelets yellow, oblong, 3–7 × ca. 2 mm, 7–14-flowered; rachilla zigzag-shaped; glumes papery, 1-veined, lanceolate; lower glume emarginate or obtuse at the apex, ca. 0.8 mm; upper glume obtuse at the apex, ca. 1.2 mm; lemmas ovate-oblong, papery, margins membranous, ca. 1.8 mm, 3-veined, lateral veins faint, mucronate, deciduous; palea slightly shorter than lemma, slightly arc-shaped, 2-keeled, ca. 1.6 mm, minutely ciliate along keels, persistent or tardily deciduous. Stamens 3; anthers ca. 0.8 mm. Caryopsis ovate, bluntly triangular in section, ca. 0.8 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 159; Y. W. Lam 1066, 1034.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Dry hillslopes, open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.

Eragrostis spartinoides Steud. 呂宋畫眉草
Syn. Pl. Glum. 1: 265. 1854; Check List HK Plants 335. 2002.
Poa polymorpha var. α R. Br., Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 180. 1810.
Eragrostis elongata (Willd.) J. Jacq. var. brachyclados Domin, Biblioth. Bot. 20(85): 400. 1915, p.p.
Eragrostis elongata (Willd.) J. Jacq. var. festucoides Domin, Biblioth. Bot. 20(85): 400. 1915.
Eragrostis cumingii Steud. var. novaguineensis Jansen, Reinwardtia 2: 271. 1953.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 20–80 cm tall. Leaf sheaths pilose or ciliolate on the outer or both margins; leaf blades usually involute (rarely flat), 1–3 mm wide, filiform or linear, sometimes with scattered hairs; ligules a fringe of hairs, 0.2–0.3 mm. Panicle open, linear or lanceolate, 5–60 × 3–6 cm; branches spreading to divaricate, sparsely divided, entirely spikelet-bearing or naked near axil. Spikelets linear, laterally compressed, 5–28 × 1.5–2.5 mm; rachilla zig-zagged, thick, wider at internode apex; fertile florets 8–57, pedicels 0.5–1.5 mm; breaking up at maturity, rachilla persistent; glumes subequal, ovate, 1-veined, apex acute; lower glume ca. 1.5 mm, upper glume 0.9–2.8 mm; lemmas lanceolate to ovate, 1.5 –2.3 mm, apex acute, deciduous; palea ± as long as lemma, persistent and tardily deciduous. Stamens (2–)3; anthers 0.3–0.7 mm. Caryopsis strongly laterally compressed, oblong-ellipsoidal, ca. 0.6 mm; pericarp tardily free on moistening.

Locality: New Territories, CUHK campus. HK sheet 35875.
Distribution: Tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Creek banks, sandy clay. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.

Eragrostis tenella (L.) P. Beauv. ex Roem. & Schult. 鯽魚草
Syst. Veg. 2: 576. 1817; FKH 329. 1912; FHN 4: 374. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 28, pl. 123: 2. 1990; FFJ 6: 146, fig. 119. 1995; FOC 22: 478. 2006; FGD 9: 346. 2009.
Poa tenella L., Sp. Pl. 1: 69. 1753.
Eragrostis plumosa auct. non Link: FHK 431. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms slender, 10–60 cm tall, glabrous, striate. Leaf blades flat, 3–10 × 0.2–0.5 cm, adaxial surface scabrous, abaxial surface glabrous and smooth; ligule a line of short hairs; leaf sheaths shorter than internodes, pilose along margin and summit. Panicle open, 5–16 cm; branches spreading and with long hairs at axils, branchlets and pedicels with oblong yellowish glands. Spikelets ovate or oblong-ovate, 2–2.5 mm, 4–10-flowered; rachilla fragile, disarticulate between florets from above downward at maturity; glumes membranous, 1-veined, subequal, 0.5–1 mm, falling off when mature; lemmas broadly ovate, apex obtuse, smooth or scaberulous, ca. 1 mm; palea persistent or tardily deciduous, ciliate along keels, hairs ca. 0.3 mm, rigidly spreading at maturity. Stamens 3; anthers ca. 0.3 mm. Caryopsis red, ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1686, 2800; S. P. Lau 7.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Open fields, moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Eragrostis unioloides (Retz.) Nees ex Steud. 牛虱草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 264. 1854; FHK 432. 1861; FHN 4: 375. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 27, pl. 121: 6 .1990; FFJ 6: 147, fig. 120. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 425. 2000; FOC 22: 477. 2006; FGD 9: 347, fig. 165. 2009.
Poa unioloides Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 19. 1788.
Poa amabilis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 68. 1753.
Eragrostis amabilis (L.) Wight & Arn., Cat. Indian Pl. 1834: no. 1777. 1834; FKH 329. 1912.
Eragrostis formosana Hayata, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 21: 53. 1907.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb. Culms erect from the geniculate base, 20–80 cm tall, 3–5-noded. Leaf blades linear, flat or inrolled, 2–20 × 0.2–0.4 cm, subamplexicaul at the base, adaxial surface long pilose, abaxial surface smooth; ligule membranous, ca. 0.8 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous and smooth, long pilose along the summit. Panicle open, 5–20 × 3–5 cm; branches slender, glabrous in axils. Spikelets purplish red at maturity, oblong, 5–10 × 2–4 mm, 10–20-flowered, closely imbricate, pedicel 0.2–1 cm, distarticulating between florets from base upwards at maturity; rachilla persistent; glumes narrowly lanceolate in side-view, 1-veined, the lower 1.5–2 mm, the upper 2–2.5 mm, apex subacute; lemmas broadly ovate to suborbicular when flattened, puncticulate, veins prominent, ca. 2 mm, mucronulate; palea slightly shorter than the lemma, 2-keeled, very narrowly winged and ciliolate, falling off together with its lemma at maturity. Stamens 2; anthers purple, 0.2–0.5 mm. Caryopsis orange-brown, laterally compressed, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.8 mm.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1638; L. T. Lo 113; HK sheet 16203.
Distribution: Fujian, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan, S China.
Ecology: Mountain slopes, grasslands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Eranthemum pulchellum Andrews 可愛花
Bot. Repos. 2: pl. 88. 1800; FRPS 70: 59. 2002.
Justicia pulchellum (Andrews) Roxb., Pl. Chrom. 2: 41, t. 177. 1805.
Pseuderanthemum pulchellum (Andrews) Merr., Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 7: 248. 1912.
Justicia nervosum Vahl, Enum. Pl. 1: 164. 1804.
Eranthemum nervosum (Vahl) R. Br. ex Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 1: 174. 1817; FHN 3: 551. 1974; Check List HK Plants 252. 2002; 87. 2004.
Daedalacanthus nervosus (Vahl) T. Anderson, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 9: 487. 1867.

Shrubs, 0.7–1.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, greyish green, glabrous or subglabrous. Petioles (0.3–)2– 3.5 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, (3–)9–20 × (1–)4–9 cm, base attenuate and decurrent onto the petioles, apex acuminate, margin entire or crenate, glabrous, lateral veins 8–10 pairs, prominent on both surfaces, reticulate veins prominent abaxially, densely covered with cystoliths especially adaxially. Spikes terminal or axillary, 1.5–6 cm. Peduncle 0.5–3 cm, glabrous, densely covered with white cystoliths. Bracts leaf‑like, obovate, 1–1.5 × 0.6–0.9 cm, apex acute, reticulate veined, green along veins, otherwise white, sparsely puberulent; bracteoles linear lanceolate, greyish white, ca. 5 mm, abaxially sparsely pilose. Calyx 6–8 mm, whitish, sparsely puberulent, 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, ca. 4–5 mm, apex acuminate. Corolla blue, ca. 3 cm, curved, outside puberulent, inside bifariously pubescent; tube‑base narrowly cylindric, ca. 2 mm, abruptly widened to ca. 1.8 cm at mouth; lobes obovate, ca. 6–8 × 5–6 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 6 mm; anther oblong, ca. 3 mm. Staminodes 2, ca. 2 mm. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous; stigma 2‑lobed, larger one linear‑lanceolate, sparsely pilose. Capsule stipitate, 1–1.3 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 415; Y. S. Lau 1009, 1506.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); India, Bhutan, Sikkim, Nepal, naturalized in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Erechtites valerianifolius (Link ex Spreng.) DC. 裂葉芹菊（菊芹）
Prodr. 6: 295. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 247. 1966; FTW ed. 2, 4: 944, photo 447. 1998; FRPS 77(1): 307. 1999; FGD 8: 231. 2007.
Senecio valerianifolius Link ex Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 565. 1826.

Annual herbs; stem stout and erect, 50–150 cm tall, striate, branched in upper portion or not branched, glabrous. Leaves oblong or elliptic, 3.5–13 × 1.5–10 cm, base narrowed down to form winged petiole 1.5–9 cm, pinnately lobed, the terminal portion pinnatifid with lobes large, ovate‑elliptic, lower portion pinnatisect with 5–8 pairs of lanceolate‑oblong lateral lobes, smaller and narrower than the terminal ones, apex acuminate, margin double serrate or irregularly lobed; leaves pinnately‑veined, glabrous above and beneath. Upper leaves similar but smaller in size. Capitula erect or nodding, arranged as paniculate corymbs at stem terminal. Involucres cylindric‑campanulate with base swollen, 7–8 mm high, 3–4 mm across middle, 4–5 mm across base, calyculate; phyllaries 12–14 in one series, linear, 7–8 × 0.8–1 mm, acute or acuminate, herbaceous with margin scarious, abaxial side glabrous or loosely puberulent. Receptacle flat or slightly concave, alveolate with areoles elevated at centre. Florets many, pale yellowish purple in colour. Marginal ones 1–2 rows, female and fertile, corolla filiform‑tubular, 7–9 mm, apex 5‑toothed. Disk florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla narrow and long tubular, 9 mm, with distal 1–1.5 mm as funnelform, apex 5‑lobed and papillose. Cypselae cylindric, 3–4 mm, 10– 12‑ribbed, grooves brown and puberulent, ribs pale brown. Pappus bristles copious, fine and slender, white at base and tinged purplish red on upper part, subequal in length with the florets.

Locality: Naturalized. H. Y. Yeung 550 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 559; P. S. Choi 479.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely distributed in the tropics.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: May–Jun.
Notes: The species was reported as Erechtites valerianaefolia (Wolf) DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 96. 2004).

Eremochloa ciliaris (L.) Merr. 蜈蚣草
Philipp. J. Sci. 1(Suppl. 5): 331. 1906; FHN 4: 464. 1977; FFJ 6: 256, fig. 226. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 271, pl. 68: 4. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 542. 2000; FOC 22: 646. 2006; FGD 9: 485. 2009.
Nardus ciliaris L., Sp. Pl. 1: 53. 1753.
Ischaemum leersioides Munro, Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 363. 1860; FHK 425. 1861.
Eremochloa leersioides Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 264. 1889; FKH 321. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, erect, tufted, 20–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths crowded at base of culm, overlapping, the upper shorter than internodes, mouth ciliate; leaf blades 3–15 × 0.1–0.4 cm, glabrous or pubescent, acute; ligule membranous, 0.5–1 mm. Raceme solitary, falcately curved; rachis internodes rib-like, puberulous to thinly hirsute. Sessile spikelet ovate, imbricate in one side of rachis; lower glume oblong-ovate, firmly papery, pubescent on back or subglabrous, marginal spines longer than glume width, longest 1.5–5 mm, 6–7-veined; upper glume as long as lower glume, thicken membranous, narrow wing on the lower part of keel, 3-veined; lower floret staminate, lemma slightly shorter than glume, ovate-oblong, apex obtuse; palea narrow; upper floret bisexual or pistillate, lemma oblong, slightly shorter than lower lemma, apex obtuse, palea narrow; style free, yellowish brown, penicillate. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet absent; pedicel narrowly ellipsoidal, ending in short point.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 39389, 39390, 41990.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Open places on hills. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Eremochloa ophiuroides (Munro) Hack. 假儉草
Monogr. Phan. 6: 261. 1889; FKH 321. 1912; FHN 4: 463, fig. 1250. 1977; FFJ 6: 255, fig. 225. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 271, pl. 68: 1–2, 79: 1. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 544, pl. 229. 2000; FOC 22: 645. 2006; FGD 9: 484, fig. 255. 2009.
Ischaemum ophiuroides Munro, Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 363. 1860; FHK 425. 1861.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms decumbent, 10–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths compressed, overlapping at base, hairy at mouth; leaf blades flat, (1–)3–10 × 0.2–0.4 cm, usually glabrous, apex obtuse, terminal absent; ligule 0.2–5 mm, margin ciliate. Raceme terminal, compressed, erect or slightly curved; rachis internodes narrowly oblong-clavate. Sessile spikelet oblong, imbricate in axis along one side; lower glume oblong, ± leathery, glabrous, marginal spines short along incurving lower keels or reduced to knobs, apex acute but appearing broadly truncate because of flanking membranous wings, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, thicken membranous, 3-veined; lower floret staminate, lemma membranous, subequal to glume; upper floret bisexual, lemma apex obtuse; style reddish brown. Pedicellate spikelet vestigial or absent; pedicel ± leaf-like, ellipsoidal-subulate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. S. P. Lau 50; HK sheet 40710, 41956.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Moist grassy fields, hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Eremochloa zeylanica (Hack. ex Trimen) Hack. 馬陸草
Monogr. Phan. 6: 263. 1889; FRPS 10(2): 273, pl. 68: 3. 1997; FYN 9: 732. 2003; FOC 22: 646. 2006.
Ischaemum zeylanicum Hack. ex Trimen, Cat. Ceyl. Pl. 107. 1885.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, slender, tufted, 20–60 cm tall. Leaves mostly basal; leaf sheaths mostly imbricate at the base, glabrous; leaf blades linear, (1–)3–15 × 0.1–0.5 cm, glabrous or sparsely pilose, apex rounded, cuspidate; ligule ca. 0.5–1 mm, membranous. Raceme solitary, terminal, flexuous, erect or curved; rachis internodes clavate, with a ring of pilose at the base. Sessile spikelet elliptic, overlapping in one side; lower glume elliptic-ovate, hard papery, glabrous, marginal spines terete, equalling or much longer than glume width flanked by narrow wings, apex acute; upper glume boat-shaped, membranous, 2-keeled, the lower keel with narrow wings; lower floret staminate, lemma oblong, hyaline membranous, acute, 3-veined; palea as long as lemma and narrower; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline membranous, truncate. Pedicellate spikelet a very small rudiment; pedicel subulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1333; HK sheet 42004, 42060.
Distribution: W Guangxi, Sichuan, SE Yunnan; Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Open grassy fields.

Eria corneri Rchb. f. 半柱毛蘭
Gard. Chron. n. s. 2: 106. 1878; FKH 263. 1912; FRPS 19: 15. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 864, photo 109. 2000; FGD 7: 400. 2006; FOC 25: 345. 2009.

Roots wire-like, young portion densely hairy, older ones branched; stems very short, obscured by the aggregated pseudobulbs; pseudobulbs subtetragonous, compressed-ovoid. Leaves 2, persistent on 2-year-old pseudobulb; petioles 1.5–2 × 0.8 cm, slightly folded; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 15–25 × 2.7–5.5 cm, attenuate at both ends, apex acuminate, cuspidate at the tip; midrib plane above, elevated beneath, with 2 major veins parallel on each side. Inflorescence a scape, 10–15 cm, furnished with 3 imbricate scales at the base, a sterile bract at the middle and a terminal raceme of 6–50 flowers; bracts caducous; flowers cream-white, tinged yellow at the apices of the sepals, petals and the mentum; odd sepal dorsal, linear-lanceolate, 13–14 × 2.5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral sepals obliqueovate, united with the column foot forming the mentum, the lower margin shorter and strongly curved; petals linear-falcate, 10–11 × 2 mm, apex round; lip movable, 3-lobed, cream-white, speckled reddish purple, curved, the lateral lobes erect, short and broad, midlobe ovate-subrotundate, lamellate, margin erose; column subcylindrical, 3 × 1.5 mm, the foot 5 mm; anther oblong, 1.5 mm; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs; ovary obconical-subcylindrical, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. S. Y. Hu 9748, 12758 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1757.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Shade and wet rocks along bank of streams. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Eria gagnepainii A. D. Hawkes & A. H. Heller 香港毛蘭
Lloydia 20: 130. 1957 [“gagnepaini”]; FRPS 19: 17, pl. 3: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 400. 2006; FOC 25: 345. 2009.
Eria coronaria auct. non Rchb. f.: Herklots, Hongkong Naturalist 6: 24, fig. 3. 1935.
Eria herklotsii P. J. Cribb, Orch. Rev. 84: 130, fig. 76, 77. 1976.

Epiphytic herb, glabrous throughout; rhizome creeping, 4–5 mm in diam., with funnel-shaped sheaths 0.7–1.5 cm. Pseudobulb cylindrical, 5–20 cm × 3–6 mm with a long, lacerate sheath at base. Leaves 2, subterminal, sessile, narrowly elliptic, obovate-elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 10–25 × 2.5–6 cm, apex acuminate, with 5–9 main veins. Flowers 5–12, bracts ovate-lanceolate to linear, 6–11 × 1.5–2 mm; pedicel including ovary 1–1.5 mm; dorsal sepals narrowly elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 14–16 × 3 – 5 mm, apex acute or obtuse; lateral sepals falcate-lanceolate, 12–16 × 5–8 mm, obtuse or acuminate, connate and forming a mentum (ca. 5 mm) at base; petals initially white, gradually turning cream-yellow, oblong-oblanceolate, 11–13 × 1.5–3 mm, acute or obtuse; lip ca. 9 × 8 mm, 3-lobed, lateral lobes parallel to midlobe, suboblong to ovate-triangular, obtuse; midlobe subtriangular or ovate-triangular, 2–3 × 2 mm. Column light green, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, SE Xizang.
Ecology: Rocks in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen of E. herklotsii was collected by G. A. C. Herklots from Tai Mo Shan before 1935.

Eria lasiopetala (Willd.) Ormerod 白綿毛蘭
Opera Bot. 124: 22. 1995; FRPS 19: 26. 1999; FGD 7: 402. 2006.
Aerides lasiopetala Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 130. 1805.
Eria flava Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 65. 1830; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 89. 1977.
Dendrolirium lasiopetalum (Willd.) S. C. Chen & J. J. Wood, FOC 25: 351. 2009.

Epiphytic herb; roots brownish, purplish red when young; rhizome slender, creeping, consisting of 3–5 internodes and terminated by an erect oblong-ovoid pseudobulb bearing leaves at apex. Leaves 3–4, petioles 1.5–2.5 cm, folded; leaf blades thick, leathery, lanceolate-linear, 9–18 × 1.2–3 cm, attenuate at both ends, apex acute. Flowers 2–5, bracts lanceolate, caducous; sepals yellowish green, densely woolly outside, lime-green and tinged yellow inside; the odd one dorsal, oblong-ovate, 16 × 5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 2.5–3 cm between apices, connate and forming a mentum at base, 2 cm from apex of mentum to the acute tip; petals lime-green, oblong-oblanceolate, 12 × 2 mm, apex obtuse; lip greenish yellow, movable, 3-lobed, lateral lobe erect, triangular, obtuse, 2–3 mm long; midlobe spathulate-obcordate, 11–12 × 7 mm, slightly recurved, margin slightly wavy, dull violet, middle thickened and slightly crested; column light green, apex shortly produced, rounded; anther yellow, oblong-subglobose; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4, each group with 2 larger ones and 2 smaller ones; ovary obconical, woolly.

Locality: Fo Tan Valley, Tai Po. S. Y. Hu 13146 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3071, 3268.
Distribution: Hainan; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.

Eria rosea Lindl. 玫瑰毛蘭
Bot. Reg. 12: t. 978. 1826; FHK 353. 1861; FKH 263. 1912; FRPS 19: 13, pl. 2: 1–4. 1999; FGD 7: 399. 2006.
Cryptochilus roseus (Lindl.) S. C. Chen & J. J. Wood, FOC 25: 362. 2009.

Rizome horizontal, with short internodes; pseudobulbs large, slightly compressed, ovoid, 2–3 cm long, 2–3.5 cm across, growing close to each other. Leaf solitary; new growth with scale leaves 1–8 cm, sheath-like, green and rather fleshy at anthesis, apex mucronate, turning brown and parchment-like and completely disintegrating by the second year; foliaceous leaf leathery, fleshy and firm, base elongate into a cylindrical petiole after anthesis; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 5–23 × 1.5–4.5 cm, about 2–3 mm thick, base cuneate and gradually attenuate into the petiole, apex obtuse and apiculate. Inflorescence a scape, bearing 3 or 4 flowers; flowers incompletely resupinate, projecting the column and the lip in a horizontal position; sepals greenish white; the odd one ovate, slightly arcuate, 12–13 × 6 mm; lateral sepals tinged pink at base, triangular-ovate, obliquely ridged along the middle, base connate and adnate to the foot forming a double-headed sac; petals white with pink lines at base, ovate, 11–12 × 8–9 mm; lip 3-lobed, pink marked with purplish red veins especially on lateral lobes, distinctly golden on the ridges of the front lobe, base saccate and adnate to the foot, front lobe slightly recurved; column slightly enlarged at apex and extending into 2 foliaceous lateral lobes; anther red, subglobose; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs; ovary subsessile, striate-sulcate.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 11457 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1761; S. P. Lau 87.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Shade and damp rocks in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–May.

Eria sinica (Lindl.) Lindl. 小毛蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 3: 48. 1859; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 88, fig. 48. 1977; FRPS. 19: 12, pl. 1: 6–8. 1999; FGD 7: 398. 2006.
Conchidium sinicum Lindl., J. Bot. Kew (Misc.) 7: 34. 1855.
Eria pusilla (Griff.) Lindl., J. Linn. Soc. 3: 48. 1859; FHK 353. 1861; FRPS 19: 11. 1999; FGD 7: 398. 2006.
Conchidium pusillum Griff., Pl. Asiat. 3: 321, pl. 310. 1851; FOC 25: 347. 2009.

Rhizomes thread-like, originating from the lower side of a pseudobulb, scales inconspicuous; pseudobulbs dorsiventrally compressed-globose, often formed in pairs, generally crowded together in colonies, 3–6 mm in diam. Leaves entire, ovate, lanceolate, obovate or oblanceolate, 7–10 × 2–4 mm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex acute and apiculate, the midrib evident. Inflorescence a scape, slender, 3–4 mm, the flower bract terminal, 1–5 mm, sheathing below and cymbiform above. Flower solitary, greenish-yellow, pedicel and ovary together 1.5 mm; perianth (4–)5 mm, segments lanceolate, 1–2 mm at the base; lateral sepals fusing at their lower portion forming a prominent, swollen irregularly shaped sac; lip tongue-like, movable, shorter than the lateral sepals and the petals, the margin minutely denticulate; column minute, 0.5 mm long and wide; anther cap rugose; pollinia partially exposed, the base viscid, 8 in 4 pairs.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tung Chung, Lantau Peak. S. Y. Hu 9104, 9207, 12874 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Growing with mosses and ferns over surface of exposed rocks, on top of mountain. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.

Eriachne pallescens R. Br. 鷓鴣草
Prodr. 184. 1810; FKH 326. 1912; FHN 4: 371, fig. 1181. 1977; FRPS 9(3): 123, fig. 30: 4–6. 1987; FOC 22: 561. 2006; FGD 9: 341. 2009.

Perennial herb, 20–60 cm tall, with many wiry roots. Culms tufted, erect, sometimes branched from the base, glabrous. Leaf blade 2–10 cm, stiff, usually rolled and needle-like, usually papillose-pilose; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, ciliate; leaf sheaths usually shorter than internodes, ciliate along margins and mouth. Panicle open, 5–10 cm; branches very slender, smooth and glabrous. Spikelets purplish, 4–5.5 mm; glumes ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm, glabrous, 9–10-veined; lemmas 3–3.5 mm, densely hispid, apex constricted, bidentate, awned from sinus; awn erect, subequal to lemma body; palea equal to its lemma, dorsally hispid. Anthers 2, 2–2.5 mm. Caryopsis oblong, ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 562; HK sheet 41944, 41954.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.

Erigeron karvinskianus DC. 加勒比飛蓬
Prodr. 5: 285. 1836; C. M. Hu, Check List HK Plants 281. 2002.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs 30–50 cm tall; stems slender, many‑branched, growth of branches terminated by two capitula. Leaves dimorphous, sparsely pilose; those on vegetative shoots trilobed, ovate‑rhombic in outline, 1.5–3.5 cm × 5–15 mm, base cuneate, lobes ovate, entire, acute; upper cauline leaves narrowly elliptic, 1–2 cm × 2 – 5 mm, both ends acute. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, solitary or in a loose panicle. Involucre campanulate, 5 mm across; phyllaries 3‑seriate, herbaceous, lanceolate, 2–4 mm, the outer ones shorter. Receptacles flat, smooth, areoles inconspicuous, the attachments of ovaries each marked by a conic elevation and a fibrous remains of vascular tissue. Marginal ligulate florets white, turning purplish pink after anthesis, slightly over 40, 2‑seriate, neuter, ligules 5.5 × 1 mm, 3‑lobed, tube 1.5 mm, stylar branches exserted. Central tubular florets yellow, numerous, hermaphrodite, corolla 5‑lobed; stamens 5, anther bases obtuse, apical appendages ovate, acute; style appendages rounded or obtuse. Achenes brown, compressed‑oblong, 1.4 mm, sparsely pilose, base with a white spongy ring, each side with a stout rib, apex truncate, apiculate at center. Pappus 2‑seriate, with short scarious ones alternate with capillary bristles.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1239; S. Y. Hu 7197, 13245 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong; native to Mexico and Panama.
Ecology: Cultivated or naturalized, usually found in wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Eriobotrya fragrans Champ. ex Benth. 香花枇杷（山枇杷）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 80. 1852; FHK 108. 1861; FKH 97. 1912; FRPS 36: 267. 1974; FGD 4: 180. 2000; FOC 9: 139. 2003.

Evergreen small tree or shrub, up to 10 m, branchlets and petioles initially densely tomentose, later glabrescent. Petioles 1.5–3 cm; leaf blade leathery, oblong-elliptic, 7 – 15 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin remotely and conspicuously dentate above the middle, initially densely tomentose, glabrescent in age, midveins prominent on both surfaces, lateral veins 9–11 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 7–9 cm, many-flowered; peduncles and pedicels densely brown tomentose; pedicels 2–5 mm. Flowers fragrant, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.; hypanthium obconical, 4 –7 mm, abaxially densely brown tomentose; sepals triangular-ovate, 3– 4 mm, abaxially densely brown tomentose, persistent; petals white, elliptic, ca. 5 × 3 mm, basally brown tomentose; stamens 20, shorter than petals; ovary tomentose, 4–5-locular; styles 4–5, white tomentose below the middle. Pome brown, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., granular-punctate, tomentose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island (Victoria Peak, Happy Valley, Mount Nicholson), Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island (Sunset Peak). U. A. On 5248; H. C. Tang 2110; Y. S. Lau 932.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Hunan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Oct.– Dec.; fruiting: May–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen was collected in a ravine on Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Eriobotrya japonica (Thunb.) Lindl. 枇杷
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 13(1): 102. 1822; FRPS 36: 262. 1974; FGD 4: 180. 2000; FOC 9: 138. 2003.
Mespilus japonica Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 199, 208. 1780.

Evergreen tree, up to 10 m tall; branchlets rather stout, densely rusty tomentose. Leaves more or less crowded at apex of branchlet; petioles 0.6–1.0 cm, rusty tomentose; leaf blade thick leathery, elliptic-oblong to broadly oblong-lanceolate, 12 – 30 × 3 – 9 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin remotely dentate above middle, adaxially tomentose when young, soon glabrescent, lustrous, abaxially densely rusty tomentose, lateral veins 11 – 21 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, many-flowered, 7 – 20 cm, densely rusty tomentose; pedicels 2–8 mm. Flowers fragrant, 1.2– 2.0 cm in diam.; hypanthium obconical, 4–5 mm; sepals triangular-ovate, 2–3 mm, apex obtuse, persistent; petals white, oblong or ovate, 5 – 9 × 4 – 6 mm, apex emarginate or obtuse; stamens 20, shorter than petals; ovary densely rusty tomentose apically, 5-locular; styles 5, free. Pome globose or ovoid, 2–5 cm in diam., yellow or orange. Seeds 1–5, globose to ovoid, 1 – 1.5 cm in diam., lustrous, with firm, brown testa.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1093; HK sheet 10184.
Distribution: S of Qinling Range, widely cultivated; Japan, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.– Dec.; fruiting: May– Jun.
Uses: Fruit, medicinal (folklore), timber.
Notes: This species was known in cultivation for its fruit in Hong Kong Island as early as 1850s. (Bentham, 1861; Herklots, Food & Flowers, No. 1: 57—58. 1948.)
records.uses:
Fruit, medicinal (folklore), timber.
Notes: This species was known in cultivation for its fruit in Hong Kong Island as early as 1850s. (Bentham, 1861; Herklots, Food & Flowers, No. 1: 57—58. 1948.)

records.text:
Eriocaulon australe R. Br. 毛穀精草
Prodr. 254. 1810; FHK 382. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 83. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 31, pl. 8: 1–11. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 154. 1999; FOC 24: 10. 2000; FGD 9: 162. 2009.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves linear, usually 10–30 cm × 1.5–3(–5) mm, sometimes up to 50 cm long and 5–8 mm broad, sparsely villous, veins 10–15. Scapes 15–60 cm, 5–7-ribbed. Flower-heads subglobose, 6–8 mm in diam., glaucous, base truncate; receptacle villous; involucral bracts broadly obovate, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., in 2–3 series, much shorter than flower-head, leathery, apex obtuse or acute, abaxially sparsely villous; floral bracts obovate, abaxially densely white clavate hairy toward acute apex. Male flowers: sepals 3, slightly connate at base, 2 larger, boat-like, dorsally winged, abaxially hairy toward apex, another one smaller, oblanceolate-oblong glabrous; petals 3, linear, connate at base into a tube, white clavate hairy at apex, gland black, ovate; anthers black. Female flowers: sepals 3, similar to that in males, 2–2.3 mm; petals 3, linear, white clavate hairy at apex, with black glands at centre; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Shek O, Quarry Bay, Sha Tin, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 171, 2545; Y. W. Lam 1260.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Indochina, Thailand, Malaysia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Marshlands and boggy grounds. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Eriocaulon cinereum R. Br. 白藥穀精草
Prodr. 254. 1810; FKH 292. 1912; FRPS 13(3): 49, pl. 14: 1–11. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 189. 1999; FOC 24: 13. 2000; FGD 9: 166. 2009.
Eriocaulon heteranthum Benth., FHK 382. 1861; FHN 4: 85, fig. 1000. 1977.
Eriocaulon sieboldianum Siebold & Zucc. ex Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 272. 1855.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves all radical, narrowly linear, 1–5(–7) cm × 0.8–1.5 mm, ending in fine points, glabrous. Scapes many and slender, 3–12(–18) cm, 4–6-ribbed. Flower-heads light yellow to dark green, at first hemispherical, broadly ovoid when full grown, 2–4 mm in diam.; receptacle villous, occasionally glabrous; involucral bracts pale green-yellow to blackish, oblong to obovate-oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, about half the length of the head, membranous, glabrous; floral bracts oblong to oblanceolate, glabrous or occasionally abaxially villous. Male flowers: sepals united at base into a tube, upper part flat, spathe-like, apex irregularly 3-toothed, glabrous or abaxially hairy toward apex; petals united into a tube at base, limb 3-lobed, lobes ovate to oblong, anterior one slightly larger than others, shortly hairy at apex, gland black or brown; anthers white to dusky. Female flowers: sepals 2(–3), blackish, free, linear, glabrous or sparsely villous abaxially and at margin; petals absent; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 5299; HK sheet 7794, 7797.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Indonesia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other moist situations. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. – Oct.

Eriocaulon nantoense Hayata 南投穀精草
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 10: 51. 1921; FRPS 13(3): 26, pl. 6: 1 – 11. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 99. 1999; FOC 24: 9. 2000; FGD 9: 162. 2009.
Eriocaulon luzulifolium auct. non Mart.: FKH 292. 1912.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves all radical, linear to linear-lanceolate, 2–5 cm × 1.5–3 mm, apex pointed. Scapes slender, 5–20(–26) cm, 4 – 5-ribbed. Flower-heads blackish when dry, subglobose, 3.5–5(–6) mm in diam.; receptacle sparsely pubescent, or densely white villous; involucral bracts straw-coloured, obovate-cuneate, slightly shorter than the head, apex rounded or nearly so, rigid, glabrescent; floral bracts obovate to oblanceolate, apex shortly acuminate, abaxially white clavate hairy toward apex. Male flowers: sepals 3, connate into a spathe, split on abaxial side, or only united at base and with 3 free lobes, blackish, with white short hairs at the top; petals united into a tube, upper part 3-lobed, lobes equal or the anterior one slightly larger than others, white clavate hairy toward apex, gland brownish, grey, black, inconspicuous, or absent; anthers black. Female flowers: sepals 3, dusky, free, boatlike, dorsally keeled, with white clavate hairy toward apex; petals 3, oblanceolate-linear, membranous, hairy, gland present or absent; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1175; HK sheet 29957.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Marshlands and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Eriocaulon setaceum L. 絲葉穀精草
Sp. Pl. 1: 87. 1753; FHK 383. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 84. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 37, pl. 10: 16 – 26. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 68. 1999; FOC 24: 11. 2000; FGD 9: 164. 2009.

Annual herb. Stem 1–5(–25) cm; roots many fibrous, tufted. Leaves radical, filiform, 3–5 cm × 0.1–0.2 mm, slightly enlarged at the base, glabrous, transparent, pale yellowish green, with transverse minor veins between parallel-veins under lens. Scapes very slender, 5–11 cm, 6-ribbed, glabrous. Flower-heads dusky, ovoid-globose, ca. 3 mm in diam.; receptacle subglabrous or villous; involucral bracts reflexed, straw-coloured, ovate, ca. 1 mm, membranous, glabrous; floral bracts orbicular to oblanceolate, abaxially white clavate hairy toward apex or glabrous. Male flowers: sepals spathe-like, apex 3-lobed, shortly hairy abaxially; petals 3, elliptic to subulate, small, anterior one slightly larger than others, white clavate hairy adaxially and toward apex abaxially, gland black, sometimes absent; anthers black. Female flowers: sepals 3, free, boat-like to obovate, abaxially white clavate hairy toward margin; petals 3, free, oblanceolatelinear, unequal, membranous, gland black, sometimes absent; ovary 3-locular; style deeply 3-cleft.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 7210, 11577.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Japan, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, N Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, ponds, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Eriocaulon sexangulare L. 華南穀精草
Sp. Pl. 1: 87. 1753; FRPS 13(3): 35, pl. 8: 12 – 22. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 189. 1999; FOC 24: 11. 2000; FGD 9: 163, fig. 87. 2009.
Eriocaulon wallichianum Mart., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 26 – 27, pl. 249. 1832; FHK 381. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 84. 1977.
Eriocaulon cantoniensis Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beech. Voy. 219. 1837.
Eriocaulon sinicum Miq., J. Bot. Néerl. 1: 87. 1861; FKH 292. 1912.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves linearlanceolate, 5–25 cm × 3–15 mm, apex very pointed, glabrous. Scapes 10–25(–35) cm, scarcely angular. Flower-heads subglobose, 5–7 mm in diam., glaucous, base truncate; receptacle glabrous; involucral bracts straw-coloured, subrounded, in 1 series, about 1/3 the length of the head, leathery, abaxially white clavate hairy; floral bracts obovate, 2–2.5 mm, leathery, very closely imbricate, apex obtuse or with a very short inflected point, and slightly mealy at the tip, abaxially hairy toward apex. Male flowers: sepals 3, ± connate at the base, of which 2 boat-shaped, with a winged keel, another one oblong-lanceolate, much smaller, flat, irregularly and minutely toothed at apex; petals (2–)3, linear, base united into a tube, apex pubescent, gland indistinct or absent; anthers (4–)6, black. Female flowers: sepals (2–)3, ovate, of which 2 larger, similar to that in males, another one smaller, lanceolate, sometimes reduced or absent; petals (2–)3, linear, unequal, membranous, occasionally villous at centre, apex white clavate hairy; ovary (2–)3-locular; style (2–)3-cleft.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1941; Y. S. Lau 346, 2336.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Africa.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other moist situations. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Mar. of the following year.

Eriocaulon tonkinense Ruhland 越南穀精草
Pflanzenr. IV 30 (Heft 13): 72. 1903; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 194. 1999; FOC 24: 12. 2000; FGD 9: 164. 2009.
Eriocaulon cristatum Mart. var. brevicalyx C. H. Wright, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(251): 199. 1903.
Eriocaulon yaoshanense Ruhland var. brevicalyx (C. H. Wright) W. L. Ma, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 29(4): 301. 1991; FRPS 13(3): 42. 1997; Check List HK Plants 305. 2002; 108. 2004.
Eriocaulon cristatum auct. non Mart.: Benth., FHK 382. 1861; FKH 292. 1912.

Herb caulescent. Rhizomes elongate, 2–3 cm. Leaves all radical, narrow-linear to almost subulate, 7–25 cm × 0.6–0.8 mm. Scapes 15–25(–30) cm, stiff, 5–7-ribbed. Flower-heads subglobose, 3–8 mm in diam., brown or black at base and grey at apex; receptacle glabrous; involucral bracts broadly obovate, straw-coloured, blackish at apex; floral bracts obovate to cuneate, dark at the top and fringed with short white hairs. Male flowers: sepals connate into a spathe, apex 3-lobed, lobes nearly equal, posterior one flat, lateral ones boatlike, all fringed with short white hairs at top; petals 3, obovate to elliptic, with one larger than others, adaxially white clavate hairy toward apex, gland black; stamens 6, anthers milky white to brownish. Female flowers: sepals 3, similar that in males; petals 3, free, oblanceolatelinear, white clavate hairy adaxially and at apex, gland black; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Lan Nai Wan, Shek O. W. J. Tutcher 7245; Y. S. Lau 1488; HK sheet 35728.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Marshlands. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

Eriocaulon truncatum Buch.-Ham. ex Mart. 菲律賓穀精草
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 29. 1832; FHK 382. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 85. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 62. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 179. 1999; FOC 24: 13. 2000; FGD 9: 165. 2009.
Eriocaulon merrillii Ruhland ex Perkins, Fragm. Fl. Philipp. 1: 136. 1904; FRPS 13(3): 47. 1997; Check List HK Plants 305. 2002; 108. 2004.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves all radical, linear-lanceolate, 2–6 cm × 2–5(–6) mm. Scapes 2–13 cm. Flowerheads straw-coloured, at first hemispherical, nearly globular when full grown, 4–5 mm in diam.; receptacle glabrous or subglabrous to villous; involucral bracts straw-coloured, various in shape, ovate-elliptic, oblong to obovate-oblong, almost as long as the head, membranous, apex obtuse, glabrous; floral bracts obovate to oblanceolate, hyaline, glabrous or sparsely hairy. Male flowers: sepals 2, connate into a spathe, 1–1.8 mm, blackish, glabrous or sparsely hairy at margin, apex 2–3-lobed; petals united into a tube at base, apex 3-lobed, lobes puberulous, each with a black gland or gland absent; anthers (5–)6, black. Female flowers: sepals 2, linear, blackish, free, usually glabrous; petals 3(–4), villous adaxially and at margin, apex white clavate hairy; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sham Tseng, Ho Pui, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 934, 1780, 2172.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Thailand, Indonesia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Eriochloa procera (Retz.) C. E. Hubb. 高野黍
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1930: 256. 1930; FHN 4: 423, fig. 1222. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 277, pl. 83: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 219. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 476. 2000; FOC 22: 525. 2006; FGD 9: 425. 2009.
Agrostis procera Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 19. 1786.
Eriochloa annulata (Flüggé) Kunth, Révis. Gramin 1: 30. 1829; FHK 409. 1861.
Eriochloa ramosa (Retz.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FKH 313. 1912.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, 30–150 cm tall. Culms erect or ascending from the geniculate base, usually pubescent at nodes. Leaf blades linear, 8–20 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule a fringe of white hairs of ca. 0.6 mm; leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous. Panicle 10–20 cm, composed of several racemes; racemes 3–7 cm, loosely ascending, bare of spikelets proximally, which mostly paired, single toward raceme apex; axis and rachis very slender, puberulous, pedicels usually without setae, those of a pair often partially connate. Spikelets lanceolate, 3–4 mm, herbaceous, sharply acute, basal swelling ca. 0.3 mm and often purplish; lower glume minute; upper glume and lower lemma 5-veined, pilose with appressed silky hairs, lower palea absent; upper lemma rugulose-punctulate, mucro 0.3 – 0.5 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung, Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 735; HK sheet 39648, 41619.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent. Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Eriosema chinense Vogel 雞頭薯
Nova Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 31. 1843; FHK 91. 1861; FKH 85. 1912; FRPS 41: 341. 1995; FGD 5: 343, fig. 188. 2003.

Perennial herb. Stems 20–50 cm, generally unbranched, densely brown pilose and mixed with shorter hairs. Roots fusiform, fleshy. Leaves 1-foliolate, lanceolate, 3–7 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base rounded or sometimes slightly cordate, apex obtuse or acute, brown-pilose adaxially, grey tomentose abaxially, but brown pilose on midvein. Racemes very short, 1–2-flowered, axillary. Calyx campanulate, 3 mm, 3-toothed, brown silky pubescent. Corolla yellow, ca. 9 mm; vexillum obovate, base auriculate; wings obovate-oblong, auriculate at one side; keel shorter than wings. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary densely white hirsute. Pods rhomboid-elliptic, 8–10 × 6 mm, brown hirsute. Seeds 2, reniform, black, hilum linear.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Reservoirs, Fanling, Ho Pui, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 635; H. C. Tang 956, 1813.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Erycibe obtusifolia Benth. 丁公藤
FHK 236. 1861; FHN 3: 477. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 20, pl. 4: 5 – 6. 1979; FOC 16: 279. 1995; FGD 4: 333, fig. 196. 2000.
Erycibe versatilihirta C. Y. Ma, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 7(1): 91, pl. 1. 1985.

Woody vine, glabrous except for inflorescences. Stems to 5 cm in diam.; branchlets distinctly striate‑angular, yellowish brown when dry.
