Petiole 0.8–1.2 cm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic or obovate, 6–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute; lateral veins 4–6 pairs, prominent abaxially. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate or racemose, 4–15 cm. Pedicels 4–6 mm. Sepals suborbicular, ca. 3 mm in diam., ± dull yellow pubescent abaxially. Corolla yellowish white, 8–10 mm; lobules broadly elliptic, undulate, entire. Stamens unequal, apex acuminate; filaments ca. as long as anthers. Ovary ellipsoidal, glabrous. Stigma conical, adnate to ovary, spirally ridged. Fruit red to yellow, ellipsoidal, 1.2–1.4 × 0.7–0.8 cm.

Locality: Stanley, Cape Collinson, Cape D'Aguilar, Lung Fu Shan, Lantau Island, Tung Lung Chau, Lamma Island. Y. W. Lam 1448; S. C. Ng 2172; HK sheet 38756.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Eryngium foetidum L. 刺芹（假芫荽）
Sp. Pl. 232. 1753; FRPS 55(1): 64, pl. 28. 1979; FGD 2: 326, fig. 215. 1991; FOC 14: 24. 2005.

Biennial herb, glabrous, 5–60 cm tall. Basal leaves several forming a rosette; petioles short, broadly sheathing up to 3 cm; leaf blade subleathery, lanceolate or oblanceolate, 2–27 × 1–5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin crenate to finely spinulose-serrate; the upper cauline leaves much reduced, sessile and usually opposite, deeply spinulose-serrate to parted. Inflorescence divaricately trifurcate, the lateral branches often continuing, to form a monochasium, heads numerous, small, short-pedunculate, flowers numerous; heads cylindric, 7–11 mm; involucre 5–6, foliaceous, spreading and reflexed, lanceolate, 1–4 × 0.2–1 cm, margin 1–3-spinulose serrate; bracteoles linear or lanceolate, 2–3 mm, scarious-margined. Calyx-teeth lanceolate to ovate, ca. 0.5 mm, acute, weakly mucronate. Petals white or pale yellow, oblanceolate to ovate, 0.5 mm. Styles short, slightly extending the sepals. Fruit globose or slightly broader than long, about 1.5 mm, densely papillose with globose, tawny processes.

Locality: Yuen Tun Ha, Luk Keng, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 54; HK sheet 27015.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; widely distributed and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, S America and Africa.
Ecology: Shady and wet places in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), flavoring.

Erythrina corallodendron L. 龍牙花
Sp. Pl. 706. 1753; FRPS 41: 164. 1995; FGD 5: 295, fig. 158. 2003.

Shrub or small tree, 3–5 m tall. Stems and branches prickly. Leaflets rhombic-ovate, 5–10 × 3.5 – 7 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, caudate, glabrous, sometimes with prickles on petioles and midvein of leaflet on abaxial surface. Racemes axillary, over to 30 cm. Flowers 2– 3 in clusters. Calyx campanulate, ca. 9 mm, apex subtruncate, only with one small projection abaxially, glabrous. Corolla deeply red; vexillum oblong, ca. 4.2 cm, apex emarginate; wings ca. 1.4 cm, keel ca. 2.2 cm, both clawed. Stamens 10, diadelphous, filaments unequal. Ovary stalked, white pubescent. Pods ca. 10 cm, glabrous, stipitate, apex beaked, slightly constricted between seeds. Seeds deep red, often with one black spot.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1624, 1829; HK sheet 23393.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan (cultivated); native to W Indies, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May – Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Erythrina crista-galli L. 雞冠刺桐

Mantissa Plantarum 1: 99-100. 1767; FRPS 41: 166. 1995; FGD 5: 295. 2003.


Deciduous shrub or small tree, stems and petioles with few prickles. Leaflets ovate or lanceolate-elleptic, 4–10 × 2.5– 6 cm, base round or cuneate, glabrous on both sides. Flowers appearing at same time with leaves. Flowers solitary or 2 – 3 together, forming leafy, loose, terminal racemes. Calyx campanulate, 10 – 12 mm, apex bifid. Corolla deep red, vexillum reflexed, nearly pipa-formed, 4.5 – 5 cm, wings very small, lanceolate 1 mm, keel curved, slightly shorter than vexillum. Stamens 10, monadelphous. Ovary thinly tomentose, stipitate. Pods 15 × 1.3 cm, constricted between seeds. Seeds blackish with brownish markings.


Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 7795; Y. S. Lau 1667.

Distribution: Yunnan and Taiwan (cultivated); Native to Brazil.

Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Apr. – Jul.

Uses: Ornamental.

Erythrina variegata L. 刺桐
Herb. Amb. 10. 1754; FRPS 41: 167. 1995; FGD 5: 296. 2003.

Large tree, up to 20 m tall. Branches with conic brown or blackish spines. Leaves usually crowded towards apex of branchlets; leaflets membranous, broadly ovate or rhombic-ovate, 15– 30 × 15 –30 cm, base broadly cuncate or truncate, apex acuminate or obtuse, triveined. Calyx spathiform, 2 – 3 cm, laterally splitted. Corolla red, 6 – 7 cm; vexillum elliptic, 5 – 6 × 2.5 cm, apex rounded, shortly clawed; wings and keel subequal, ca. 1.5 cm. Stamens 10, monadelphous. Ovary puberulous. Pods black, 15–30 × 2 –3 cm, slightly curved and constricted between seeds. Seeds 1 –8, reniform, 1.5 × 1 cm, deep red.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1837, 3078; HK sheet 7796.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Australia, Pacific Islands, E Africa, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Eucalyptus camaldulensis Dehnh. 赤桉
Cat. Pl. Hort. Camald., ed. 2, 20. 1832; FGZ 217. 1956; FRPS 53(1): 44. 1984; FFJ 4: 84, fig. 68: 1– 2. 1989; FGX 1: 879. 1991; FZJ 4: 284, fig. 359. 1993; FGD 3: 165, fig. 118: 1 – 3. 1995; FYN 7: 100, fig. 30: 3. 1997; FOC 13: 326. 2007.
Eucalyptus rostrata Schlecht., Linnea 2: 655. 1847.

Tree, to 25 m tall. Bark smooth, dark grey, exfoliating but persistent at trunk base. Branches terete, youngest parts angulate. Leaves of juvenile plants: petiolate; leaf blade broadly lanceolate, 6 – 9 × 2.5 – 4 cm. Leaves of adult plants: petiole slender, 1.5 – 2.5 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, narrowly lanceolate, 6 – 30 × 1 – 2 cm, slightly twisted, with small black glands on both surfaces. Inflorescence an umbel, axillary, 5 – 11-flowered; peduncle 1 – 1.5 cm, slender, terete. Flower buds ovoid, 5 – 8 mm. Pedicels 5 – 7 mm. Hypanthium semiglobose, ca. 3 mm; calyptra semiglobose at base, 5– 7 mm, abruptly constricted above middle, apex acute and beaked. Stamens 5–7 mm. Capsule subglobose, 5 –6 mm in diam.; valves (3 or) 4 (or 5), exserted from hypanthium.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1433; HK sheet 34746.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Dec.–Aug.
Uses: Environmental, timber, essential oil.

Eucalyptus exserta F. Muell. 窿緣桉
J. Proc. Linn. Soc., Bot. 3: 85. 1859; FGZ 217. 1956; FHN 2: 3. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 46. 1984; FFJ 4: 90, fig. 75. 1989; FGX 1: 898, pl. 348: 3 –6. 1991; FGD 3: 169. 1995; FYN 7: 104. 1997; FOC 13: 326. 2007.

Tree, 15 – 18 m tall. Bark persistent, greyish brown, rough, and fissured. Young branchlets obtusely angulate, slender, usually pendulous. Leaves of juvenile plants: shortly petiolate; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, less than 1 cm wide. Leaves of adult plants: petioles slender, ca. 1.5 cm; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, 8 – 15 × 1 – 1.5 cm, slightly twisted, with many minute black glands on both surfaces. Inflorescence an umbel, axillary, 3 – 8-flowered; peduncle 4 – 20 mm, terete. Flower buds long ovoid, 8 – 10 mm. Pedicels 3–4 mm. Hypanthium semiglobose, 2.5–3 × ca. 4 mm; calyptra long conic, 5–7 mm, apex acuminate. Stamens 6– 7 mm. Capsule subglobose, 6–7 mm in diam.; valves 4, strongly exserted from hypanthium.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34326, 34672, 35810.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Sep.
Uses: Environmental, timber, essential oil.

Eucalyptus robusta Sm. 大葉桉
Spec. Bot. New Holland 39, t. 13. 1793; FGZ 216. 1956; FHN 2: 3. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 40, pl. 7: 1– 3. 1984; FFJ 4: 88, fig. 73. 1989; FGX 1: 890, pl. 347: 8 – 10. 1991; FGD 3: 169. 1995; FYN 7: 104, fig. 31: 3 – 4. 1997; FOC 13: 325. 2007.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Bark persistent, dark brown, rough and fissured. Young branchlets angulate. Leaves of juvenile plants: petiolate; leaf blade thickly leathery, ovate, ca. 11 × 7 cm. Leaves of adult plants: petioles 1.5–2.5 cm; leaf blade thickly leathery, ovate-lanceolate, 8– 17 × 3 –7 cm, base oblique, with glands on both surfaces. Inflorescence an umbel, axillary, 4 – 8-flowered; peduncle less than 2.5 cm, compressed. Flower buds 1.4 – 2 × 0.7 – 1 cm. Pedicels short and thick. Hypanthium semiglobose to obconic, 7 – 9 × 6 – 8 mm; calyptra nearly as long as hypanthium, apex constricted into a beak. Stamens 1 –1.2 cm. Capsule kettle-shaped, sometimes somewhat constricted in middle, 1–1.5 cm; disk broad; valves 3 or 4, included in hypanthium.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1421; HK sheet 11250, 11253.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to E Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost year-round.
Uses: Timber, essential oil, medicinal (folklore), environmental.

Eucalyptus tereticornis Sm. 細葉桉

Spec. Bot. New Holcland 1: 41. 1795; FGZ 218. 1956; FRPS 53(1): 43, pl. 7: 4– 6. 1984; FFJ 4: 83, fig. 66. 1989; FGX 1: 881, pl. 343: 7 – 10. 1991; FGD 3: 165. 1995; FYN 7: 100. 1997; FOC 13: 325. 2007.

Eucalyptus umbellata (Gaertn.) Domin, Biblioth. Bot. 89: 467. 1928, nom. illeg., non Eucalyptus umbellata Desf. (1814).

Leptospermum umbellatum Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 174, pl. 35. 1788.


Tree, to 25 m tall. Bark greyish white, smooth, exfoliating in long strips, sometimes persistent at trunk base. Branchlets terete, slender, pendulous. Leaves of juvenile plants: ovate to broadly lanceolate, to 10 cm wide. Leaves of adult plants: petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, 10–25 × 1.5–2 cm, slightly twisted, with small glands on both surfaces. Inflorescence an umbel, axillary, 5 –8-flowered; peduncle 1– 1.5 cm, stout, terete. Flowers buds long ovoid, 8– 12 mm. Pedicels 3– 6 mm. Hypanthium hemispheric, 2.5–3 × 4–5 mm; calyptra conic, 7–10 mm, apex acuminate. Stamens 6–9 mm. Capsule subglobose to ovoid, 6–8 mm in diam.; valves 4 or 5, exserted from hypanthium.


Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34749.

Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to Australia.

Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.

Uses: Timber, essential oil, environmental.

Eugenia uniflora L. 紅果仔
Sp. Pl. 1: 470. 1753; FGZ 207. 1956; FRPS 53(1): 58. 1984; FFJ 4: 95, fig. 81. 1989; FYN 7: 108. 1997; FOC 13: 331. 2007.

Shrubs or trees, to 5 m tall, glabrous. Petioles ca. 1.5 mm; leaf blade papery, ovate to elliptic, 3.2–4.2 × 2.3–3 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acuminate, mucronate, or obtuse, dark green and glossy adaxially, pale green abaxially, and with many pellucid glands on both surfaces; lateral veins ca. 5 on each side of midvein, slightly conspicuous. Flowers white, slightly fragrant. Calyx-lobes long elliptic, reflexed. Berries dark red when mature, globose, 1–2 cm in diam., 8-ridged, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1551; P. S. Choi 152; HK sheet 11311.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Ornamental, edible (fruit).

Eulalia phaeothrix (Hack.) Kuntze 棕茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FHN 4: 454. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 85. 1997; FYN 9: 624. 2003; FOC 22: 587. 2006; FGD 9: 466. 2009.
Pollinia phaeothrix Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 168. 1889.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, 0.3–0.8(–1) m tall, white-villous below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths longer or the upper slightly shorter than internode, pilose or glabrescent, basal sheaths woolly with dark reddish brown hairs, finally fibrous; leaf blades narrowly linear, 15–45 × 0.1–0.6 cm, glabrous or pilose, apex acute; ligule 0.5–1 mm, truncate, ciliate. Racemes (1–)2–8, digitate, golden brown or yellowish brown; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, densely ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate, dark brown; callus hairs 1/8 spikelet length; lower glume papery, oblong-lanceolate, abaxial flat or slightly concave; upper glume boatshaped, apex slightly obtuse, tri-denticulate, pilose along upper margins and keel; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, slightly shorter than glumes, narrower to the apex, the upper margins ciliate; lower palea absent; upper lemma narrow, 2-lobed nearly to the middle, an awn arising from the sinus; awn 1–2 cm, indistinct 2-geniculate; upper palea absent; stamen 3; anthers 2.5–3 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet.

Locality: Kwun Tong. HK sheet 15177.
Distribution: Hainan, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, S India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Grassy hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Eulalia quadrinervis (Hack.) Kuntze 四脈金茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FFJ 6: 245, fig. 214. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 89, pl. 19: 1 – 8. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 546. 2000; FOC 22: 587. 2006; FGD 9: 464. 2009.
Pollinia quadrinervis Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 158. 1889.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 80 – 120 cm tall, glabrous or puberulous at nodes. Leaf sheaths glabrous, rarely thinly appressed pilose between veins, the lower longer and the upper shorter than internodes; leaf blades linear, 10–40 × 0.4–0.6 cm, glabrous to tuberculate-villous, abaxial surface glaucous, apex acuminatefiliform, terminal usually absent; ligule 1–1.5 mm, truncate. Racemes 2–7, subdigitate, brown yellow; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, silky villous. Sessile spikelet golden brown, oblong-lanceolate; callus hairs 1/6–1/3 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly elliptic, back slightly concave and villous below middle, 2–4 green veins between keels, connected by veinlets below apex and between lateral veins, upper keels shortly pectinate-ciliate, apex membranous, subacute; upper glume boatshaped, membranous, glabrous, scabrous along keel, apex acute; lower floret usually 1 lemma, oblong-lanceolate, as long as or shorter than glume; upper lemma ovate-oblong, 2-lobed in upper 1/3, with an geniculate awn arising from the sinus; awn 1.2–2 cm; palea oblong-lanceolate; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet, pedicel as long as or slightly shorter than rachis internode.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 311, 564; Y. S. Lau 3011.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, N India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Korea, Philippines.
Ecology: Hillslopes, open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Eulalia speciosa (Debeaux) Kuntze 金茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FHN 4: 453. 1977; FFJ 6: 245. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 83, pl. 19: 9 – 12. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 6: 548. 2000; FOC 22: 586. 2006; FGD 9: 465. 2009.
Erianthus speciosus Debeaux, Acta Soc. Linn. Bordeaux 32: 53. 1878.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, to 1 m tall. Basal leaf sheaths with golden brown hairs, finally fibrous; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 25–50 × 0.4–0.7 cm, adaxially farinose, white pilose at base, otherwise glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, truncate and ciliate. Racemes 4–7(–13) on a 3–4 cm axis, digitate, 10–25 cm, hairs whitish, yellowish or golden brown; rachis internodes and pedicels 2/3 as long to subequaling spikelet, ciliate. Sessile 4.6–5.7 mm, dark brown; callus hairs 1/6-1/3 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly lanceolate-oblong, back concave, villous below middle, veinless between keels, upper keels stiffly ciliate, apex subobtuse; upper lemma narrow, margin pilose, 2-toothed in upper 1/3; awn 1.5–2 cm. Anthers 2.5–3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsing Yi, Lai Chi Chong. S. Y. Hu 8330, 8472, 11193 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, SE Asia, Philippines.
Ecology: Hillslopes, grassy fields.

Eulophia flava (Lindl.) Hook. f. 黃花美冠蘭
Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 7. 1890; FKH 265. 1912; FRPS 18: 177. 1999; FGD 7: 389. 2006; FOC 25: 256. 2009.
Cyrtopera flava Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 189. 1833; FHK 357. 1861.

Terrestrial herb; roots wire-like, 4–5 mm in diam.; rhizomes tuber-like, white, irregularly ovoid, 6–8 cm long, 3–5 cm in diam., with distinct oblique, black concentric joints. Leaves 2–4, pedicellate, the pedicels sheathing, 25 cm or longer, covered by cataphylls 12–30 cm; leaf blades plicate, oblong-elliptic, (25–)45–50 × (4.5–)10 cm. Inflorescence a raceme; flowers bright canary-yellow and creamy yellow; dorsal sepal elliptic, 3 × 1 cm, apex acuminate, with 7 longitudinal veins slightly elevated above; lateral sepals wide-spreading, subfalcate-oblong, with 1 median longitudinal ridge, 2.5–3 × 0.8–1 cm, base oblique, truncate, apex acuminate and slightly keeled; petals situated below the dorsal sepal, broadelliptic, 2.6 × 1.5 cm, with the inner edge overlapping above the column; lip 3-lobed, subconical, saccate at base; lateral lobes creamy yellow, slightly reflexed; front lobe yellow, rounded, margin wavy and curved upwards; column arching, white or very light yellow, tinged greenish at apex, apex enlarged, apiculate at the back; anther conical, honey-yellow; pollinia 2, orange, roundish and compressed; ovary smooth, shallowly grooved.

Locality: Tai Tam, Cape D'Aguilar, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. S. Y. Hu 10164 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2637; HK sheet 33096.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Crevices of rocks along streams, open grassy slopes. Flowering: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Eulophia graminea Lindl. 美冠蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 182. 1833; FRPS 18: 182, pl. 32: 4–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 874. 2000; FGD 7: 388, fig. 196. 2006; FOC 25: 255. 2009.
Eulophia sinensis Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 91. 1861; FKH 265. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72, fig. 36. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; roots many, 2 mm in diam.; at anthesis rhizomes partially exposed, globular-conical, green at the basal half, covered by fibrous, stiff, dead leaf scales. Leaves 7–8 developed at post-anthesis, equitant, bluish green, 4–12(–35) × (0.7–)1–1.5 cm, deeply furrowed along the midrib, apex acuminate and acute. Flowers 9–20, rather small; sepals similar in colour and size, the dorsal one oblong, 12 × 2 mm, apex acute, slightly recurved; lateral sepals widespread, olive-green with a satin-like sheen, faintly tinged with purplish red stripes; petals oblong, slightly shorter than the sepals, 8–9 × 2 mm, apex acute, recurved with a rather broad, faint purplish red mid-longitudinal vein and 2 narrower ones; lip distinctly spurred and trilobed, midlobe obovate, margins crisped, apex acute, white, lateral lobes running upward and forward, greenish outside with 4–5 palmate, oblique, purplish red ridges inside; column 3.5 mm, smooth, green tinged pink, apex produced into a sharp point and enlarged into a scalloped crest; anther yellow, with 2 rounded, apical, ear-like papillose lobes; pollinia 2, subglobose; ovary 4–5 mm, glossy greenish maroon.

Locality: Ho Chung, Sha Tin, Lam Tsuen, Pillar Point. K. Y. Chan 1472 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 13781A (CUHK); K. L. Yip 4064; HK sheet 40320.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Anhui, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy slopes, open fields. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Recent studies of reproductive biology and genetics show that this species is a self-compatible but pollinator-dependent outcrossing colonizer (Sun, Am. J. Bot. 84: 224–232. 1997; Sun & Wong, Am. J. Bot. 88: 2180–2188. 2001).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: Recent studies of reproductive biology and genetics show that this species is a self-compatible but pollinator-dependent outcrossing colonizer (Sun, Am. J. Bot. 84: 224–232. 1997; Sun & Wong, Am. J. Bot. 88: 2180–2188. 2001).

records.text:
Eulophia zollingeri (Rchb. f.) J. J. Sm. 無葉美冠蘭
Fl. Buitenz. 6: 228. 1905; FFJ 6: 600, fig. 521. 1995; FRPS 18: 185. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 878, pl. 373. 2000; FOC 25: 254. 2009.
Cyrtopera zollingeri Rchb. f., Bonplandia 5: 38. 1857.
Eulophia yushuiana S. Y. Hu, Chung Chi Journal 11: 19, fig. 3(d–h). 1972.

Terrestrial herb appearing as scapes bearing brownish yellow-red flowers; roots many, fleshy, brittle; rhizomes irregularly cylindrical, ginger-like, those of the flowering plants 6–13 cm long, 2.3 cm in diam. Scape 30–50 cm long, 4–8 mm in diam., with 3–5 brownishgreen cataphylls at the base, the internodes 6–7 cm, olive-green, the flowering axis 10–20 cm, with 15 – 30 flowers well spaced; pedicels 7 mm. Flowers brownish red-green, the odd sepal ovate-oblong, 20 × 8 mm, base truncate, apex acuminate; lateral sepals spreading, oblique ovate-elliptic, 25 × 8–9 mm; petals obovate, shiny brownish red, 1.7 cm; lip shortly spurred, saccate at the base, 3-lobed, 2-ridged at the throat, purplish beige outside, purplish red and sparsely hairy inside, the front lobe ovate, slightly recurved, 7 × 5 mm, hairy, margin purplish red, centre yellow; column 10 mm, light green; anther yellow-red and trimmed with maroon at the basal end; pollinia 2; rostellum fleshy; ovary beige-brown, 13 mm long, 2.5 mm in diam., striate-sulcate.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, New Territories. S. Y. Hu 10274 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 406, 453.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Ryukyu.
Ecology: Margins of swamps. Flowering: May–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen of Eulophia yushuiana (S. Y. Hu 10274, A, holotype; CUHK, isotype) was collected from Clear Water Bay on 29 May 1970.

Euonymus actinocarpa Loes. 紫刺衛矛
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 30: 459. 1902; J. S. Ma, Thaiszia 11: 48. 2001.
Euonymus angustatus Sprague, Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1908: 35. 1908; FKH 60. 1912; FRPS 45(3): 25. 1999.

Large climbing shrub. Branchlets 4-angular or sometimes weakly winged. Petioles 6–9 mm; leaf blade subleathery, oblong-ovate, 7–10 × 2–5 cm, base subrounded or borad-cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate on distal part. Inflorescence terminal or lateral, with a spread of 7–8 cm at base, 4–5-branched. Peduncle and branches narrowly winged. Flowers 7–10 mm in diam. Sepals 4, flat orbiculate. Petals 4, white-greenish, suborbiculate, 4–5 mm; disk annular, shallowly 4-lobed. Stamens 4, nearly inserted on disk margin. Ovary deltoid-ovoid. Capsules purple-red, subglobular, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam. including spines; spines flat and broad, 6–9 mm. Seeds purple-brown, 1 or 2 in each cell, oblong, 7– 8 × 3 – 4 mm, arils yellowish.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Kowloon Reservior, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Mau Ping, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 598; P. S. Choi 352, 402.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan.
Ecology: Ravines in woods. Flowering: Feb. –Apr.; fruiting: Jul. –Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of Euonymus angustatus (Herb. Hongk. no. 639, K, IBSC) was collected from Tai Mo Shan by U. On in 1898.

Euonymus hederaceus Champ. ex Benth. 常春衛矛
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 333. 1851; FHK 63. 1861; FKH 60. 1912; FRPS 45(3): 10. 1999.

Climbing shrub, 1–2 m tall; rooting readily. Young branches angular. Petioles 6–12 mm; leaf leathery or thinly leathery, ovate or elliptic, 3–7 × 2–4.5 cm, base subrounded or broad cuneate, apex obtuse or acuminate, lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein, thin and conspicuous. Cymes much shorter than leaves, few-flowered, once or twice branched. Peduncles 1–2 cm. Flowers white-greenish, 8–10 mm in diam. Sepals and petals 4. Disk subsquare. Stamens 4, attached on disk margin, filaments ca. 2 mm. Ovary slightly compressed. Capsules purple-red, globular, 8–10 cm in diam., 4-locular, slightly 4-furrowed, but otherwise entire. Seeds enveloped in a scarlet aril.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1287; K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 39671, 40808).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Aug.
Notes: The lectotype specimen (J. G. Champion s.n., K) designated by Cao & Ma (Taxon 55: 227. 2006) was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Euonymus gibber Hance 流蘇衛矛
J. Bot. 20(231): 77. 1882; FKH 61. 1912; FRPS 45(3): 51. 1999.

Erect shrub. Petioles 5–7 mm; leaf blade leathery to thick-leathery, opposite or in whorled of three, narrowly elliptic or long obovate, 5–10 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse-acute, margin nearly entire, often revolute, lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midvein, obscure. Cymes large, open, twice to thrice branched. Peduncles 3–5 cm. Flowers (4–)5-merous. Sepals margin erose. Petals suborbicular, base shortly clawed, apex fimbriate. Disk slightly 5-lobed. Stamens attached on protuberance of disk; filaments complanate. Ovary most part connate with disk; styles short. Capsules obovate, upper 5-lobed. Seeds with shallowly cupular arils.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 11281; HK sheet 917, 5163.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Nov.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. no. 21780) was collected before 1882 by C. Ford from individuals cultivated in Hong Kong Botanical Gardens, which were originated from hills of Hong Kong Island.

Euonymus laxiflorus Champ. ex Benth. 疏花衛矛
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 333. 1851; FHK 63. 1861; FKH 61. 1912; FRPS 45(3): 60. 1999.

Erect shrub. Branches terete. Petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blade papery or subleathery, ovate-elliptic, oblong or elliptic, 5–12 × 2–6 cm, base broad-cuneate or subrounded, apex obtusely acuminate, margin entire or obscurely crenate, lateral veins obscure. Cymes loose, 5–9-flowered, rather shorter than leaves. Peduncles ca. 1 cm. Flowers ca. 8 mm in diam. Sepals 5, margin shortly purple-ciliate. Petals 5, purplish, margin crenate and wavy, base attenuate; disk shallowly 5-lobed. Stamens 5, sessile. Ovary without style. Capsules purple, obconic, 7–9 × 9 mm, top flat. Seeds oblong, 5–9 × 3–5 mm, enveloped in shallowly cupular, orange arils.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2701, 3051; K. L. Yip 4244.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley Woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley Woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Euonymus nitidus Benth. 中華衛矛
London J. Bot. 1: 483. 1842; FHK 62. 1861; FRPS 45(3): 56. 1999.
Euonymus chinensis Lindl., Trans. Hort. Soc. London 6: 74. 1826; FKH 61. 1912, non Lour. (1790).

Erect shrub or small tree 1–5 m tall. Petioles 6–10 mm; leaf blade leathery, shining, obovate-lanceolate, 4–13 × 2–5.5 cm, apex acuminate, margin entire. Cymes shorter than leaves, once to thrice branched, 1–15-flowered. Flowers 5–8 mm in diam. Sepals 4. Petals 4, white or yellow-green, base shortly clawed; disk small, shallowly 4-lobed. Stamens 4, filament inconspicuous. Capsules reddish, deltoid-ovoid, 8–14 cm, 4-locular, lobes scarcely prominent, rounded at top. Seeds brown-red, broadly elliptic, 6–8 mm, enveloped in a orange aril.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 358; Y. W. Lam 1435; S. C. Ng 2023.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Oct.
Notes: The holotype specimen (R. B. Hinds s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island in 1841.

Euonymus tsoi Merr. 長葉衛矛
Sunyatsenia 1(4): 198. 1934; J. S. Ma, Thaiszia 11: 220. 2001.
Euonymus longifolius Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 332. 1851, non Medic. (1782); FHK 62. 1861; FKH 61. 1912.
Euonymus kwangtungensis C. Y. Cheng, Icon. Corm. Sin. Suppl. 2: 226. 1983; FRPS 45(3): 60. 1999.

Erect small shrub. Petioles 5–8 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 8–14 × 1.5–3 cm, apex acuminate, smooth and shining, margin entire or sparsely serrate, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, obscure. Cymes 1–2, axillary, slightly longer than petioles, 3– few-flowered. Peduncles 2–12 mm. Flowers ca. 7 mm in diam. Sepals 5. Petals 5, suborbicular, ca. 3 mm, slightly crenate or waved on edge; disk shallowly 5-lobed. Stamens 5, sessile. Ovary without style; stigma slightly 5-lobed. Capsules reddish, obdeltoid, flat at top, shallowly 5-lobed.

Locality: Happy Valley, Morrison Hill, Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 514; HK sheet 38549, 40188.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb. – Jun.; fruiting: Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen of E. longifolius was collected from Happy Valley woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Eupatorium chinense L. 華澤蘭
Sp. Pl. 837: 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 255. 1966; FRPS 74: 63, pl. 21: 4–6. 1985; FGD 8: 213. 2007.
Eupatorium reevesii Wall. ex DC., Prodr. 5: 179. 1836; FHK 171. 1861; FKH 140. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 70–100 cm tall; stem herbaceous or woody at base, striate, many‑branched, pubescent to tomentose. Leaves sessile or with short petiole (2–4 mm), ovate, base rounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin regularly crenate‑serrate, pinnately‑veined, scabrid and sparsely glandular adaxially, densely yellow glandular‑punctate abaxially; lower leaves usually withered at flowering stage, those on upper portion 3.5–5.5 × 2–3 cm. Capitula arranged in a loose corymb, with 1–2 ovate prophylls. Involucres cylindric‑oblong, 4.5–5 mm; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, imbricate, apex obtuse or rounded; outer shorter ones ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 1–2 mm, hairy and glandular; middle and inner longer ones lanceolate‑oblong or oblong, length increases inward, 5–6 mm, loosely hairy and glandular, apex and margin white and scarious. Receptacle small. Florets 5 per capitulum, corolla white, pink or red, 3–4 mm, apical half slightly broadened, 5 deltoid lobes, glandular; anther apical appendages triangular, acute; stylar branches 2.5–3 mm, slender, papillose. Cypselae cylindric‑oblong, pentagonous, 2 mm, base acute, blackish brown, slightly hairy, glandular. Pappus 3–4 mm, nearly equal to length of corolla.

Locality: San Wai, Tai Mo Shan, Lai Chi Wo, Shing Mun Reservoir, Lantau Island. K. Y. Chan 1260 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 12435 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1321.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy banks. Flowering: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Eupatorium japonicum Thunb. 白頭婆
Fl. Jap. 307. 1784; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 257. 1966; FRPS 74: 60. 1985; FGD 8: 213, fig. 125. 2007.
Eupatorium wallichii DC., Prodr. 5: 179. 1836; FHK 172. 1861.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 60–200 cm tall. Stem erect, few‑branched, pubescent, hair multicellular and kinky, those on peduncles much denser, but appearing looser or glabrescent on lower portion of stem. Petioles 0.5–2 cm, densely pubescent. Middle leaf blade long‑elliptic to lanceolate, 6–14 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, with 6–7 pairs of pinnate veins, both surfaces yellow punctate, pubescent or pilose, hair denser on midveins, veins and along margins, sharply serrate or double serrate; upper and lower leaves smaller in size, basal leaves withered at anthesis. Capitula arranged in tight corymb. Involucres cylindric‑oblong, 5–6 mm; phyllaries 3‑seriate, green or tinged red, apex obtuse or rounded; outer ones 2 mm, ovate; middle and inner layers 4–6 mm, long‑elliptic to oblong. Florets 5 per capitulum, corolla white, pink or purple, 4.5–5 mm, shallowly 5‑lobed, lobes about 0.5 mm; stylar branches 3–4 mm. Cypselae pale blackish brown, elliptic‑oblong, 3–4 mm, 5‑ribbed, glabrous, glandular. Pappus white, 4–5 mm, shorter than corolla.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 427; Y. S. Lau 1291.
Distribution: Area S of Huanghe; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Eupatorium lindleyanum DC. 林澤蘭
Prodr. 5: 180. 1836; FHK 172. 1861; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 259. 1966; FRPS 74: 59. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 960. 1998; FGD 8: 212. 2007.

Perennial erect herbs 50–150 cm tall, annual flowering stem solitary, emerging from the caudex, the leafy portion 1.5–4 mm across, striate, densely pubescent or pilose, hair multicellular. Lower leaves withered at anthesis; middle ones sessile or with very short petiole (3–5 mm), trinerved, linear‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–9 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin serrate or coarsely serrate, scabrid or pilose on both surfaces, densely glandular punctate abaxially; upper leaves smaller and narrower. Capitula form tight corymb at terminal, with 1–3 ovate prophylls at the distal end. Involucres 4–6 mm, cylindric‑campanulate; phyllaries about 10, arranged in 2– 3 series, imbricate, green at basal portion, straw‑coloured at apex and along margin, glandular, apex acute or acuminate; outermost ovate, 1–2 mm; median and inner ones oblong‑lanceolate to oblong, length increases inward, 5–6 mm. Receptacle small. Florets white, pink or purplish‑red, 5 per capitulum, corolla 3.5–4.5 mm, glandular, apical half broadened, bearing 5 deltoid lobes; anther apical appendages triangular, acute or obtuse; stylar branches 2 mm long, papillose. Cypselae cylindric oblong, pentagonous, 2.5 mm, brownish black, glandular; pappus 4 mm, white, persistent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Kau To Hang, Ping Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2614; P. S. Choi 455; S. Y. Hu 11024 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Xinjiang.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, margins of forests or in thickets. Flowering: May–Dec.

Eupatorium odoratum L. 飛機草
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1205. 1759; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 260. 1966; FRPS 74: 56. 1985; FGD 8: 211. 2007.
Chromolaena odorata (L.) R. M. King & H. Rob., Phytologia 20(3): 204. 1970.

Perennial herbs, 1–3 m tall, with sprawling rhizomes; stem erect, densely pubescent or tomentose, branches opposite, growing horizontally and perpendicular to the main axis. Leaves ovate or ovate‑deltoid, 4–10 × 1.5–5 cm, base broadly cuneate or truncate, apex acuminate, densely pilose on both surfaces, glandular abaxially, prominently trinerved, margin sparsely dentate, subentire towards apex; petioles 1–2 cm. Capitula in loose corymbs. Involucres cylindric, 7–10 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, imbricate, straw‑coloured with 3 conspicuous parallel green veines and scarious margin; outer ones ovate, 1.8–2 mm, puberulent, apex obtuse; median and inner ones narrowly oblong, length increases inward, 7–8 mm, apex obtuse to acute. Receptacle flat to slightly convex. Florets 25–30 per capitulum, corolla pink or white, 4–5 mm, 5‑lobed; stylar branches 5 mm. Cypselae blackish brown, 3–4 mm, 5‑ribbed, pilosulose along ribs; pappus capillary, subequal to corolla in length.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. W. Lam 2273; HK sheet 38396; C. P. Lau 064 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.

Euphorbia antiquorum L. 火殃簕

Sp. Pl. 450. 1753; FKH 232. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 62, pl. 25: 4 – 7. 1997; FGD 5: 133. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 266. 2005.

Euphorbia trigona Haw., Syn. Pl. Succ. 127. 1812.


Small tree, 1–3 m tall; stems 3–5-angled, much branched; branchlets succulent, green, sharply 3–5-angled. Leaves succulent, subsessile, borne on the ridge of angles and at apex of young branches, caducous; leaf blade obovate or obovate-oblong, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, base attenuate, apex rounded, entire, glabrous; stipules in pairs, spiny, 2–5 mm. Cyathia usually 3 forming a cyme borne on leaf scar; peduncles 2–3 mm; involucres broadly campanulate, ca. 5 mm in diam., 5-lobed; lobes suborbicular, margin denticulate; glands 5, entire. Male flowers numerous; bracts lacerate. Female flower solitary, ovary glabrous; styles 3, free; apex 2-lobed. Capsules triangular-oblate, 3.4–4 × 4–5 mm.


Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 7132; S. Y. Hu 13161 (CUHK).

Distribution: Tropical Asia, cultivated and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.

Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: All year round.

Uses: Ornamental.

Euphorbia atoto G. Forst. 濱海大戟

Fl. Ins. Austr. 36. 1786; FKH 232. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 36, pl. 6: 1 – 3. 1997; FGD 5: 136. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 268. 2005.

Chamaesyce atoto (G. Forst.) Croizat, Fl. Hawaii. 190. 1936; FTW ed. 2, 3: 433, pl. 224. 1993.


Perennial herb or subshrub, glabrous, 20–40 cm tall; stems woody at base, prostrate or ascending, dichotomous branched; nodes inflated. Leaves opposite, thin-leathery; petioles 1–3 mm; stipules membranous, broadly triangular, margin fimbriate; leaf blade oblong-elliptic or ovate-oblong, 1–3 × 0.4–1.3 cm, base oblique, suborbicular or subcordate, apex obtuse, mucronulate, margin entire. Cyathia in compound cymes; peduncles 2–5 mm; involucres cupular, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., margin 4–5-lobed; lobes triangular-ovate, apex acute, margin lacerate; glands 4, thin-discoid, margins with white appendages. Male flowers several, slightly exceeding involucres; bracts lanceolate, margin lacerate. Female flower solitary, pedicels 2–4 mm, prominently exceeding involucres; ovary smooth, glabrous; styles 3, free, apex 2-lobed. Capsules trigonous, ca. 3.5 × 3.5 mm, glabrous.


Locality: Deep Water Bay, Lamma Island, Ping Chau. Gibbson 5132; HK sheet 5264; J. P. Woo & T. K. Woo 715 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Japan, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Indonesia, Pacific Islands to Australia.

Ecology: Sandy seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. –Nov.

Euphorbia bifida Hook. & Arn. 細齒大戟
Bot. Beechey Voy. 5: 213. 1837; FRPS 44(3): 42, pl. 8: 1 – 4. 1997; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 269. 2005.
Euphorbia vachellii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey voy. 5: 213. 1837.
Chamaesyce vachellii (Hook. &Arn.) Hurus., J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 6(6): 283, fig. 34. 1954; FTW ed. 2, 3: 451, pl. 236. 1993.

Annual herb to 50 cm tall; stems woody at base; nodes annular. Leaves opposite; petioles very short, less than 3 mm; stipules membranous, subulate-triangular, caducous; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to broadly linear, 10–25 × 2.5 mm, base inaequilateral, subtruncate or slightly oblique, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin serrulate; midvein raised adaxially, depressed abaxially, lateral veins prominent. Cyathia clustered, rarely solitary; involucres cupular, ca. 1 × 1mm, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, apex lacerate; glands 4, with reddish appendages. Male flowers several, slightly exceeding involucres. Female flower solitary; ovary smooth, glabrous; styles 3, free, apex 2-lobed. Capsules trigonous, ca. 2 × 2 mm, glabrescent.

Locality: Quarry Bay, Causeway Bay, Castle Peak, Long Ke, Lok Ma Chau, Luk Keng, Po Toi Island, Sha LoWan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 440; Y. W. Lam 276, 335; S. Y. Hu 6006, 10125 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; S and SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology:Wastelands, shrublands and margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. – Oct.

Euphorbia helioscopia L. 澤漆

Sp. Pl. 459. 1753; FHK 301. 1861; FKH 232. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 71. 1997; FGD 5: 134. 2003.


Annual herb, 10–50 cm tall; stems simple or with a few branches ascending from the base. Stem-leaves alternate, obovate or broadly oblong, 1–3.5 × 0.5–1.5 cm, apex rounded to subtruncate, serrulate, narrowed from middle into a short stalk; involucral-leaf opposite, sessile, obovate-oblong, 3–4 × 0.8–1.4 cm, minutely toothed. Cyathia in umbel of 5 rays, each ray once or twice forked; the branches very short; glands of the involucre entire and rounded. Male flowers several, exceeding the involucres. Female flower solitary; ovary glabrous; styles short, 2-lobed. Capsules ca. 2.5–3 × 3–4.5 mm, smooth and glabrous; seeds pitted, with raised reticulate veins.


Locality: Cultivated. specimens

Distribution: Native to Europe, now a weed widely spread over temperate and subtropical regions of the Old World.

Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr. – Oct.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Euphorbia hirta L. 飛揚草

Sp. Pl. 454. 1753; FRPS 44(3): 44, pl. 8: 5 – 8. 1997; FGD 5: 137. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 276. 2005.

Euphorbia pilulifera L., Sp. Pl. 454. 1753; FHK 302. 1861.

Chamaesyce hirta (L.) Millsp., Publ. Field Columbian Mus., Bot. Ser. 2(7): 303. 1909; FTW ed. 2, 3: 436, pl. 226. 1993.


Annual herb, to 70 cm tall; stems simple or with a few branches, more or less hirsute with spreading yellowish hairs. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 mm; stipules lanceolate or linear, 1.5–2 mm, free or nearly so, margin lacerate; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate or oblong, 1–5 × 0.5–1.3 cm, base oblique and usually narrowed, apex acuminate or obtuse, margin sparsely serrulate or entire, pubescent on both surfaces. Cyathia crowded in head-like cymes on short axillary peduncles; involucres campanulate, ca. 1 mm in diam., pubescent, 5-lobed; lobes triangular-ovate; glands 4, subcupular, with appendages. Male flowers several; female flower solitary; ovary slightly pubescent; styles 3, free, apex 2-lobed. Capsules 1–1.5 mm in diam., more or less hairy with appressed hairs; seeds ovoid, obtusely 4-angled, slightly winkled.


Locality: Naturalized. H. C. Tang 875; Y. S. Lau 1420, 1656; S. Y. Hu 8641, 10047 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; a very common weed in tropical and subtropical countries, both in the New and Old World.

Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Euphorbia hypericifolia L. 通奶草

Sp. Pl. 454. 1753; FHK 301. 1861; FKH 232. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 41. 1997; FGD 5: 138. 2003.


Annual herb to 30 cm tall; stems erect or ascending, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 mm; stipules triangular, free or connate; leaf blade narrowly oblong or obovate, 1–2.5 × 0.4–0.8 cm, base usually very oblique, apex obtuse, margin serrulate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces or adaxially glabrescent; bracts leaves 2, homomorphous as the stems leaves. Cyathia in small, loosely dichotomous cymes, terminal or in the upper axils; involucres turbinate, ca. 1 mm in diam., 5-lobed; lobes ovate-triangular; glands 4, small and entire, with small orbicular white petal-like appendages. Male flowers several, slightly exceeding involucre. Female flower solitary; ovary glabrous; styles 3, free, apex 2-lobed. Capsules triangular-globose, ca. 1.5 × 2 mm, glabrous.


Locality: Tsim Sha Tsui, Kwai Chung Park, Fanling, Lok Ma Chau, PokWai, Sai Kung, Siu Lek Yuen Tsuen, Tung Chung, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 446; Y. W. Lam 866, 1257.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.

Ecology: Wastelands, open fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Dec.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Euphorbia milii Des Moul. 鐵海棠
Bull. Hist. Nat. Soc. Linn. Bordeaux 1(1): 27, pl. 1. 1826; FRPS 44(3): 58, pl. 14: 1 – 4. 1997.
Euphorbia splendens Bojer ex Hook., Bot. Mag. 56: pl. 2902. 1829.

Diffuse shrub, somewhat climbing; stems much branched, dark brown, obtusely angulate, to 1 m or longer, armed with stout spines. Leaves obovate or oblong-spathulate, 1.5–5 × 0.8–1.8 cm, base attenuate, apex rotund and mucronulate, entire, sessile or nearly so. Cyathia in long-pedunculate dichotomous cymes, each cyathium closely subtended by 2 broadly ovate bright red bracts about 1.3 cm in diam.; peduncles 4–7 cm; pedicels 6–10 mm, with a membranous bract; glands 5, kidney-shaped, ca. 1 × 2mm, yellowish. Male flowers several; bract lacerate, pubescent at apex. Female flower solitary; ovaries smooth, glabrous; styles 3, connate up to middle, apex 2-lobed.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Y. Chan 1323 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Madagascar; widely cultivated
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Euphorbia prostrata Aiton 匍匐大戟（鋪地草）
Hort. Kew 2: 139. 1789; FRPS 44(3): 51, pl. 10: 5 – 8. 1997; FGD 5: 138, fig. 81. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 281. 2005.
Chamaesyce prostrata (Aiton) Small, Fl. S. E. U. S. 713, 1333. 1903; FTW ed. 2, 3: 442, pl. 231. 1993.

Annual herb; stems much branched from the base, usually reddish, glabrous or glabrescent; branches prostrate, up to 20 cm. Leaves opposite; petioles very short or almost none; stipules narrowly triangular, caducous; leaf blade elliptic to obovate, 3 – 8 × 2 – 5 mm, base subrounded, oblique, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or irregularly serrate, green adaxially, sometimes red or reddish abaxially. Cyathia in small cymes, 1 – 3 in axil of leaves; involucres turbinate, ca. 1 mm in diam., usually glabrous, rarely pilosulose, 5-lobed; lobes triangular or suborbicular; glands 4, with small white appendages. Male flowers several, often included in involucres. Female flower solitary; ovary sparsely white-pubescent on ribs; styles 3, connate at base, apex 2-lobed. Capsule triangular-globose, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 mm, pilose on ribs.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 1652, 1963; Y. W. Lam 765.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong,Yunnan, Hubei, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology:Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Dec.

Euphorbia pulcherrima Willd. ex Klotzsch 一品紅（聖誕樹）
Allg. Gartenzeitung 2(4): 27 – 28. 1834; FRPS 44(3): 63, pl. 16: 1–3. 1997; FGD 5: 133. 2003; K. Chayamarit &P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 281. 2005.
Poinsettia pulcherrima (Willd. & Klotzsch) Graham, Edinburgh New Philos. J. 20: 412. 1836.

Shrub, 1–3 m tall; stems and branches glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–8 cm, reddish; stipules broadly triangular, ca. 1.5 mm; leaf blade ovate-elliptical to lanceolate, 6–25 × 4–10 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acuminate or acute, entire or sinuate-toothed or lobed, pubescent abaxially; bracteal leaves 5–7, narrowly elliptic, 3–7 × 1–2 cm, usually entire, bright vermilion-red. Cyathia in terminal cymes; peduncles 3–4 mm; involucres greenish, 6–8 mm in diam., margin 5-lobed, bearing a large yellow gland on one side; lobes triangular, glabrous. Male flowers many; filaments red; bracts membranous, lacerate. Female flower solitary, ovary glabrous; styles 3 connate at the base, apex 2-lobed. Capsules triangular-globose, 1.5–2 × 1.5 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. Hu & K. H. Yung 194 (CUHK).
Distribution: Mexico, Mesoamerica, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct. –Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Euphorbia thymifolia L. 千根草（小飛揚）
Sp. Pl. 454. 1753; FHK 302. 1861; FKH 232. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 52, pl. 11: 6 – 11. 1997; FGD 5: 139. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 286. 2005.
Euphorbia sanguinea auct. non Hochst. & Steud. ex Boiss.: Benth., FHK 302. 1861; FKH 232. 1912.
Chamaesyce thymifolia (L.) Millsp., Publ. Field Columbian Mus., Bot. Ser. 2(11): 412. 1916; FTW ed. 2, 3: 448, pl. 235. 1993.

Annual herb; stems prostrate, much branched, up to 20 cm, sparsely pilose. Leaves opposite; pedicels ca. 1 mm; stipules lanceolate or linear, 1–1.5 mm, caducous; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or obovate, 4–8 × 2–5 mm, base oblique, rounded or subcordate, apex rounded, margin serrulate, rarely entire, sparsely pilose on both surfaces, rarely glabrous. Cyathia in small compact almost sessile axillary cymes; involucres narrowly campanulate to turbinate, ca. 1 mm in diam., sparsely pilose abaxially, 5-lobed; lobes ovate; glands 4, with white appendages. Male flowers several, slightly exceeding involucres. Female flower solitary; ovary hairy; styles short, free, apex 2-lobed. Capsule ca. 1.5 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent with appressed hairs.

Locality: Stubbs Rd., Tai Hang Rd., Victoria Park, Sheung Pak Nai,Yuen Long, TsingYi. Y. S. Lau 1665, 2236; Y. W. Lam 377; S. Y. Hu 6875 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiaugsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology:Wastelands, roadsides, open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Euphorbia tirucalli L. 綠玉樹（光棍樹）
Sp. Pl. 452. 1753; FHK 301. 1861; FKH 232. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 3: 469. 1993; FRPS 44(3): 58, pl. 14: 5 – 6. 1997; FGD 5: 133. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 291. 2005.

An erect unarmed shrub or small tree, 1–3(–6) m tall; branches cylindrical, scattered or clustered, very divergent, ca. 6 mm in diam., ± succulent, smooth, bright shining green. Leaves none or very few and small, linear-oblong, 7–15 × 0.7–1.5 mm, caducous. Cyathia clustered on a very short stalk in the forks of some of the smaller branches; involucres turbinate, ca. 2 mm; glands 5, ovate or subrotund, peltate. Male flowers several, exceeding involucres. Female flower solitary; ovary glabrous; styles 3, connate at the base, apex 2-lobed. Capsules rhomboid-triangular, ca. 8 × 8 mm, smooth, slightly puberulent or glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Gibbson 6783; Y. W. Lam 1035; HK sheet 32230; S. Y. Hu 5023 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to E Africa (Angola); widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul. – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Eurya acuminatissima Merr. & Chun 尖葉毛柃
Sunnyatsenia 1: 72. 1930; FGD 2: 166. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 100. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, 1.5 –7 m tall; young branchlets densely covered with spreading long hairs; terminal buds villose. Leaves thinleathery; petioles 2–3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate, 5 –9 × 1.1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex caudate-acuminate, margin closely serrulate, dark green and shining adaxially, light green abaxially, glabrous or initially sparsely appressed pubescent on abaxial surface, lateral veins ca. 9 on each side of midvein. Flowers white, axillary, solitary or in cluster of 3; pedicels 1–3 mm, glabrous or nearly so. Male flowers: bracteoles orbicular; sepals ovate, 1 mm, apex rounded, mucronate; petals oblong, ca. 2.5 mm; stamens 14–16; anthers not locellate; pistillode densely pubescent. Female flowers: sepals ovate, apex acuminate; petals lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent, 3-locular; styles slender, 3 –3.5 mm, 3-lobed. Fruit ellipsoidal-ovoid or globose, 3 – 4 mm, sparsely pubescent.

Locality: Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. P. S. Choi 99; Y. W. Lam 688, 1358.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi. Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests on mountain slopes or in valleys. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.

Eurya chinensis R. Brown 米碎花
Narr. J. China 379, t. 1818; FKH 44. 1912; FGD 2: 175. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 132. 1998.

Shrub, 1–3 m tall; young branchlets 2-ribbed, pubescent; terminal buds densely yellowish brown, pubescent. Leaves thinly leathery; petiole 2–3 mm; leaf blade obovate, 3 – 4.5 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or slightly emarginate, rarely acuminate, margin closely serrulate, glabrous, lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2– 4 clustered; pedicel ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Male flowers: bracteoles very small, glabrous; sepals ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex subrounded, glabrous; petals obovate, 3–3.5 mm, glabrous; stamens ca. 15; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles lightly smaller; sepals ovate, 1–1.5 mm, glabrous; petals ovate, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, glabrous, 3-locular; styles 1.5 –2 mm, apex 3-lobed. Fruit globose, 3 – 4 mm in diam. Seeds reniform, blackish brown, shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 950; Y. W. Lam 1275; Y. S. Lau 2239.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes or by streams.

Eurya chinensis R. Brown var. glabra Hu & L. K. Ling 光枝米碎花
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 11: 314. 1966; FGD 2: 175. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 133. 1998.

Differs from var. chinensis by its terminal buds and the branchlets of the current year's growth are completely glabrous.

Locality: Stanley, Ho Pui, Ninepin Group. S. P. Lau 130; Y. W. Lam 141, 1144.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes or by streams. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul. of the following year.

Eurya distichophylla Hemsl. 二列葉柃
J. Linn. Soc. 23: 77. 1886; FKH 43. 1912; FGD 2: 167. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 89. 1998.
Eurya swinglei Merr., Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 12: 106. 1917.

Shrub; young branchlets terete, densely covered with spreading long hairs. Leaves thin-leathery; petioles short, ca. 1 mm, villose; leaf blade lanceolate, 3– 6 × 0.8 –1.5 cm, base obliquely rounded or oblique-cordate, apex acuminate or long-acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous adaxially, densely appressed villose abaxially, lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein. Flowers white, axillary, solitary or in clusters of 3; pedicels ca. 1 mm, villose. Male flowers: bracteoles ovate, very small; sepals ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, apex slightly acute or obtuse, densely villose abaxially; petals obovate-oblong to obovate, ca. 2.5 mm, apex rounded; stamens 15–18; anthers locellate; pistillode densely pubescent. Female flowers: sepals ovate, ca. 1 mm, apex acute or obtuse, densely villose abaxially; petals lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent, 3-locular; styles 3–5 mm, 3-lobed almost to base. Fruit globose or ovoid, 4–5 mm in diam., pubescent. Seeds orbicular-reniform.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2497; L. T. Lo 213; Y. S. Lau 3060.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines.

Eurya groffii Merr. 崗柃
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 25: 247. 1919; FHN. 1: 507. 1964; FGD 2: 170. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 119. 1998.
Eurya acuminata DC. var. groffii (Merr.) Kobuski, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 325. 1937.

Shrub or small tree, 2–7 m tall; young branchlets terete, densely yellowish brown-pubescent or glabrescent; terminal buds densely yellowish brown-villose. Leaves leathery; petioles ca. 1 mm, densely villose; leaf blade lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.2–2.2 cm, base obtuse or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or long acuminate, margin closely serrulate, dark green and glabrous adaxially, yellowish green and appressed pilose abaxially, lateral veins 10 –14 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 –9 clustered; pedicels 1–1.5 mm, densely pubescent. Male flowers bracteoles ovate, ca. 1 mm; sepals ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse and mucronate, yellowish brownpubescent abaxially; petals obovate, ca. 3.5 mm; stamens ca. 20; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles and sepals as in male flower, but slightly smaller; petals lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, glabrous, 3-locular; style 2 mm, 3-lobed to the base. Fruit globose, ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Po Kau, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang. C. P. Lau 5; Y. W. Lam 558; K. L. Yip 4251.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets.

Eurya loquaiana Dunn 細枝柃
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 38: 355. 1908; FHN 1: 508. 1964; FGD 2: 171. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 124. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, young branchlets terete, puberulous. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 2– 4 mm, puberulous; leaf blade ovate-elliptic, 4 –9 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex long-acuminate, margin serrulate, adaxially dark green or yellowish green, glabrous, abaxially light green, becoming purplish red when dry, sparsely puberulous or only hairy on midvein, lateral veins 10 –20 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or in clusters of 4; pedicel 2–3 mm, puberulous. Male flowers: bracteoles ovate, ca. 1 mm; sepals ovate or suborbicular, ca. 2 mm, subglabrous; petals obovate, ca. 3.5 mm; stamens 10–15; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles and sepals as in male flowers, but smaller; petals elliptic, 3 mm, ovary glabrous 3-locular; style 2–3 mm, 3-lobed. Fruit globose, 3–4 mm in diam. Seeds reniform, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. F. W. Xing 9030; Y. W. Lam 1442, 1755.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests and thicktets in ravines. Flowering: Oct.– Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep. of the following year.

Eurya macartneyi Champ. 黑柃
Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. 2: 99. 1850; FHK 27. 1861; FKH 43. 1912; FHN 1: 509. 1964; FGD 2: 172. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 144. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout; young branchlets terete. Leaves leathery; petioles 3– 4 mm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic, 6 –14 × 2– 4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin subentire or serrulate on distal portion, adaxially yellowish green, abaxially reddish brown when dry, lateral veins 12–14 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 –4 clustered; pedicels 1–1.5 mm. Male flowers: bracteoles suborbicular, ca. 1 mm; sepals leathery, orbicular, ca. 3 mm, apex rounded, mucronate or retuse; petals obovate, 4 – 6 mm; stamens 17–24; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles as in male flower; sepals ovate, 2–2.5 mm; petals obovate, ca. 4 mm; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3, free. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., purplish black. Seeds reniform, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lion Rock, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2101; N. K. Chun 41907; K. L. Yip 4403.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: Nov.–Jan.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Eurya muricata Dunn 格葯柃
J. Bot. 48: 324. 1910; FKH 43. 1912; FGD 2: 172. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 115. 1998.
Eurya huiana Kobuski f. glaberrima H. T. Chang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3: 36. 1954.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout; young branchlets terete. Leaves leathery; petioles 3 – 5 mm; leaf blade elliptic, 5 – 8.5 × 2–3.2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin subentire, dark green adaxially, light green or yellowish green abaxially, lateral veins 9 –11 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 – 4 clustered; pedicels 1–2 mm. Male flowers: bracteoles suborbicular, 1–1.5 mm; sepals orbicular, 2–2.5 mm; petals oblong, 3–3.5 mm; stamens 15–22; anthers locellate; pistillode very small. Female flowers: bracteoles as in male flower; sepals ovate, 1.5 –2 mm; petals obovate, 2.5 –3 mm; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3-lobed. Fruit globose, ca. 4 mm in diam. Seeds reniform, dark brown, shining.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Gough. S. T. Dunn s.n. (Herb. Hongk. No. 1772).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Nov.–Jan.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Gough around 1909.

Eurya nitida Korth. 細齒葉柃
Verh. Nat. Gesch. Bot. 3: 115, t. 17. 1840; FHN 1: 509. 1964; FGD 2: 176. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 134. 1998.
Eurya japonica var. nitida (Korth.) Th.-Dyer, Fl. Brit. Ind. 1: 284. 1874.
Eurya japonica auct. non Thunb.: Benth., FHK 28. 1861; FKH 43. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout; young branchlets 2-ribbed. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles ca. 3 mm; leaf blade oblong or obovate-oblong, 4–7 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin closely serrulate or crenulate, dark green and shining adaxially, light green or yellowish green abaxially, lateral veins 9 –12 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 – 4 clustered; pedicels ca. 3 mm. Male flowers: bracteoles suborbicular, ca. 1 mm; sepals suborbicular, 1.5–2 mm, apex rounded; petals obovate, 3.5– 4 mm; stamens 14 –17, as long as petals; anthers not locellate; pistillode very small. Female flowers: bracteoles and sepals as in male flower; petals oblong, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 1.5–3 mm, apex 3-lobed. Fruit globose, 3– 4 mm in diam., bluish black. Seeds reniform or globose-reniform, brown and shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 450, 2140; Y. S. Lau 1360; Y. W. Lam 1244.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, S Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Myanmar, Malaya, Indonesia, Philippens.
Ecology: Forests and thickets.

Eustigma oblongifolium Gardn. & Champ. 秀柱花
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 312. 1849; FHK 132. 1861; FKH 101. 1912; FHN 2: 335. 1965. FRPS 35(2): 96, pl. 21. 1979; FGD 1: 162, fig. 179. 1987; FOC 9: 34. 2003.

Shrub or small tree; young branches lepidote. Stipules linear; petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 7–17 × 2.5 – 6 cm, leathery, base obtuse or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes dentate towards apex, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences 2–3 cm; general bracts ovate, ca. 1 cm; bracts and bracteoles ovate, stellate-pubescent. Floral cup ca. 2.5 mm, stellate-pubescent. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm, deciduous. Petals obovate, slightly shorter than sepals, apex 2-lobed. Anthers ovoid, 0.8 –1 mm. Styles 0.8 –1.2 cm. Capsule ca. 2 cm, glabrous. Seeds 0.8–1 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 222; P. S. Choi 471.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun., fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Evolvulus alsinoides (L.) L. 土丁桂
Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 392. 1762; FHK 240. 1861; FKH 181. 1912; FHN 3: 473, fig. 865. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 12, pl. 2: 1 – 4. 1979; FFJ 4: 477, fig. 381. 1989; FOC 16: 276. 1995; FGD 4: 335, fig. 197. 2000.
Convolvulus alsinoides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 157. 1753.
Evolvulus chinensis Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 8: 77. 1837.
Evolvulus pudicus Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 115. 1852.

Perennial herb. Stems slender, prostrate or ascending, slender, with appressed and spreading pale yellow hairs. Petiole short, hairy; leaf blade petiolate or subsessile, 1–2 × 0.4–0.9 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, mucronate, appressed pale yellow pubescent on both surfaces, sometimes subglabrous adaxially; lateral veins 3 pairs, slightly prominent abaxially. Cymes 1 – few‑flowered, pubescent; peduncles filiform, 2.5–3.5 cm; bracts linear‑subulate to linear‑lanceolate, 1.5–4 mm. Pedicels 2.5–4 mm, hairy. Sepals lanceolate, 2.5–4 mm, villous. Corolla rotate, white, pale blue, sometimes pale purple, 6–10 mm in diam. Stamens inclusive; filaments filiform, adnate to base of corolla tube. Ovary glabrous. Styles 2, distinct. Capsule globose, 4‑valved. Seeds 4 or fewer, black, smooth.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tsim Bei Tsui, Castle Peak, Sha Chau, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 129; P. S. Choi 382; Y. S. Lau 1533.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; S & SE Asia, E Africa.
Ecology: Sandy soil, dry slopes, maritime areas, grasslands, thickets, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Exacum tetragonum Roxb. 藻百年
Fl. Ind. 1: 398. 1832; FRPS 62: 5, pl. 1: 1 – 5. 1988; FOC 16: 3. 1995; FGD 4: 323, fig. 190. 2000.

Annual herb, 25–60 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, 4‑angled, branched at upper part. Leaves sessile; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate to ovate, 1–5 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base rounded, nearly clasping, and decurrent into narrow wings on stem, apex acute; veins 3–5, prominent abaxially. Flowers 4‑merous. Pedicel 0.3 – 1 cm. Calyx 5–6 mm; lobes ovate, margin broadly membranous, apex caudate, midvein keeled. Corolla mauve‑blue to lilac, 1.5–2.5 cm; tube cylindric, 4–6 mm; lobes elliptic, 1.1–1.7 cm, margin entire. Filaments linear, 1.5–2 mm; anthers 5.5– 6.5 mm. Ovary 2.5–3 mm; style linear, 1–1.2 cm; stigma lobes orbicular. Capsules subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam. Seeds ellipsoidal, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Lantau Peak, Tap Mun. Ross 11440; HK sheet 4014, 26217.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi; Cambodia, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, New Guinea, Philippines, Sikkim, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Grasslands, roadsides. Flowering: Jul. –Aug.

Exbucklandia tonkinensis (Lec.) H. T. Chang 大果馬蹄荷
Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni; 1959(2): 3. 1959; FRPS 35(2): 43, pl. 8. 1979; FGD 1: 152, fig. 167. 1987; FOC 9: 24. 2003.
Bucklandia tonkinensis Lec., Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 30: 392. 1924.
Bucklandia tonkinensis (Lec.) Steenis, Blumea 7(3): 595. 1954, nom. illeg.
Symingtonia tonkinensis (Lec.) Steenis, Fl. Malesiana, Ser. 1, Spermatoph. 5: 375. 1957; FHN 2: 332. 1965.

Tree to 30 m tall; young branches brown-pubescent. Stipules elliptic, 2– 4 × 0.8 –1.3 cm, puberulent; petioles 3 –5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, 8 –13 × 5 –9 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes 3-lobed, dark green and shining adaxially, glabrous and tuberculate abaxially; palmately 3–5-veined. Inflorescences capitate, solitary; heads 7–9-flowered; peduncles 1–1.5 cm, brown-tomentose. Petals absent. Stamens less than 1 cm. Ovary brown-pubescent; styles 4–5 mm. Capsules ovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.8 –1 cm, tuberculate. Seeds 6, narrowly winged at lower part.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 3242; N. H. Li 21.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Excoecaria agallocha L. 海漆
Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 1288. 1759; FKH 241. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 9, pl. 2: 3 –5. 1997; FGD 5: 129. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P. C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 293. 2005.
Commia cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 606. 1790.

Evergreen tree, 2 – 5 m tall; branchlets stout, glabrous. Leaves alternate, papery to sub-leathery; petioles stout, 1.5– 3 cm, glabrous, with 2 glands at apex; stipules ovate, 1.5–2 mm; leaf blade elliptic or broad-elliptic, rarely ovate-oblong, 4.5–10 × 3–5 cm, base obtuse or broad-cuneate, apex acute, tip blunt, margin entire or ± crenulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins slender, 10 on each side of midvein. Racemes axillary, the male 3–4.5 cm, the female shorter, 2–3 cm; bracts broad-ovate, fleshy, ca. 2 × 2mm, with 2 glands at base. Male flowers: solitary in axils of bracts; sepals 3, lanceolate, ca. 1.2 mm; stamens 3, usually exceeding the sepals. Female flowers: sepals 3, broad-ovate or triangular, slightly connate at base, ca. 1.4 × 1 mm; ovary ovoid, styles 3, free. Capsules globose, 7–8 × ca. 10 mm, trisulcate, cocci ovoid, rostrate at apex.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Tam Reservoirs, Kiu Tsui Chau, Sha Tin, Tai LongWan, Ting Kok. H. C. Tang 1271; Y. S. Lau 231, 313; Hu & But 20904 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Australia and Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Littoral muddy swamps and in mangrove forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Sep.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control, ornamental).

Excoecaria cochinchinensis Lour. 紅背桂
Fl. Cochinch. 612. 1790; FRPS 44(3): 7. 1997; FGD 5: 129, fig. 78. 2003; K. Chayamarit & P.C. van Welzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 295. 2005.
Antidesma bicolor Hassk., Cat. Hort. Bot. Bogor. 81. 1884.
Excoecaria bicolor (Hassk.) Zoll. ex Hassk., Retzia 1: 158. 1855.

Evergreen shrub, 1–2 m tall; branches slender, glabrous. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate or in whorls of 3; petioles 3–10 mm, eglandulose at apex; stipules ovate, ca. 1 mm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or oblong, 6–14 × 2–4 cm, base attenuate, apex long-acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous, dark green adaxially, purple or dark-red abaxially; lateral veins 8–12. Racemes axillary or terminal, the male 1–2 cm, the female 3–5-flowered, slightly shorter than the males. Male flowers: solitary in axils of bracts; pedicels ca. 1.5 mm; bracts broad-ovate, ca. 1.7 × 1.7 mm, with 2 glands at base; sepals 3, lanceolate, ca. 1.2 mm, serrulate at apex; stamens 3; anthers globose. Female flowers: pedicels 1.5–2 mm; bracts as in male flowers; sepals 3, ovate, 1.8 × ca. 1.2 mm, slightly connate at base; ovary globose, glabrous; styles 3, free or more or less connate at base. Capsules globose, ca. 8 mm in diam., truncate at base, concave at apex; seeds nearly globose, ca. 2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 60; HK sheet 25106, 25107; S. Y. Hu 6552 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangxi, cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; and in countries of SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Falcataria moluccana (Miq.) Barneby & J. W. Grimes 南洋楹
Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 74(1): 255. 1966.
Albizia moluccana Miq., Fl. Ned. Ind. 1: 26. 1855.
Albizia falcataria (L.) Fosberg, Reinwardtia 7: 88. 1965; FRPS 39: 68. 1988; FGD 5: 149. 2003.

Large tree, up to 45 m tall. Branchlets minutely pubescent with many tiny, pale lenticels. Stipules small, caducous. Rachis of leaves up to 40 cm, usually with a large, oval, disk-shaped gland near its base; pinnae densely rusty tomentellous, ca. 6– 20 pairs, up to 10 cm; leaflets 6– 26 pairs, sessile, obliquely oblong, slightly falcate, 1 – 1.5 cm × 3 – 6 mm, base obtuse, rounded or nearly cuneate, apex acute, midvein at about 1/4 lamina width along distal margin, with conspicuous other basal veins, glabrous adaxially, sparsely (denser on veins) puberulous abaxially. Spikes axillary, solitary or forming a panicle. Flowers greenish-yellow to cream. Calyx broadly campanulate or hemispherical, sericeous, 2.5 mm, with small teeth. Corolla sericeous, 5– 7 mm, lobes oblong-ovate, 2.4– 4 mm. Stamens 1 cm. Pods straight, strap-shaped, flat, 10 – 13 × 1.3 – 2.3 cm, late dehiscent through both sutures. Seeds 10 – 15, compressed-ellipsoidal, 7 × 3 mm, testa brown, with narrowly U-shaped pleurogram.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Y. Tam 3.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi and Fujian (cultivated); Moluccas, New Guinea, New Britain and Solomon Island, cultivated elsewhere in tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, widely planted in tropical countries as a fast-growing timber tree.
records.uses: Ornamental, widely planted in tropical countries as a fast-growing timber tree.

records.text:
Polygonum multiflorum Thunb. 何首烏
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 379. 1784; FKH 218. 1912; FGD 4: 86. 2000.
Fallopia multiflora (Thunb.) Harald., Symb. Bot. Upsl. 22(2): 77. 1978; FRPS 25: 102. 1998; FYN 11: 357. 2000; FOC 5: 317. 2003.

Perennial herb, with thick, tuberous rhizomes. Stems twining, 2–4 m or longer, much branched, glabrous, woody at base. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to oblong-ovate, 3–7 × 2– 5 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Ocrea tubular, scarious, brown, 3 – 5 mm, apex oblique, glabrous. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, 10–20 cm. Peduncles papillose. Bracts triangular ovate, papillose, each embracing 2– 4 flowers. Pedicels slender, 2–3 mm, articulate at lower part. Perianth white or light green, 3– 4 mm, deeply 5- lobed; lobes elliptic, unequal, the outer 3 larger, dorsally winged; wings suborbicular, enlarged to 6 –7 mm in diam. in fruit. Stamens 8; filaments dilated at base. Ovary ovoid; styles 3, very short; stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 2.5 –3 mm, dark brown and shining, enclosed in the winged persistent perianth.

Locality: Severn Road, Stubbs Road. H. C. Tang 687; P. S. Choi 168; Y. S. Lau 176.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, S Gansu, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests on rocky slopes and in valleys. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal.

Farfugium japonicum (L.) Kitam. 大吳風草
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 8(4): 268. 1939; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 262. 1966; FRPS 77(2): 1, pl. 1. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 964, pl. 457, photo 453. 1998.
Tussilago japonica L., Mant. Pl. 1: 113. 1767.

Perennial herbs, the scapes, leaves, petioles, peduncles and phyllaries slightly to densely covered with greyish brown woolly hair especially when in young stage, later glabrescent; stem scapose, 25–70 cm tall, lanate hair much denser at base. Leaves mainly radical and in rosette, reniform, 3–10 × 4–20 cm, margin mucronulate‑dentate to broadly sinuate‑dentate, base cordate, apex rounded; petiole 6 – 28 cm with base dilated. Cauline leaves absent, or with few appeared as bracts, oblong or linear‑lanceolate, 1–2(–6) cm. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2–7 arranged as corymbs; peduncle 3–12 cm. Involucres broadly campanulate to turbinate; phyllaries 12–14 in 1 series, oblong, 10–15 × 2–2.5 mm, apex acuminate, abaxial side puberulent to lanate, margin scarious. Bracteoles narrowly lanceolate, 4–7 mm. Marginal pistillate florets 8–12, corolla ligulate, yellow, ligule oblong, 1.5–1.8 × 0.3–0.4 cm, 2‑lobed at apex, tube 7–10 mm. Disk bisexual florets many, corolla tubular, 11–12 mm, lower half narrow, upper half broaden as campanulate form, apex with 5 acute and lanceolate‑oblong lobes about 1.5 – 2 mm; anther tubes conspicuously exserted, base sagittate, apical appendages lanceolate‑oblong; stylar branches roughened on abaxial side, truncate and penicillate at distal ends. Cypselae cylindric, 3–6 mm, ribbed and villous, brown. Pappus white, unequal in length, 8–13 mm.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Sunset Peak and Lantau Peak. H. Y. Yeung 160 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 8295 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 326.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests, ravines. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.

Fatoua villosa (Thunb.) Nakai 水蛇麻
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 41: 516. 1927; FOC 5: 22. 2003.
Urtica villosa Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 851. 1784.
Fatoua pilosa auct. non Gaudich.: FKH 244. 1912; FHN 2: 372. 1965; FGD 1: 169. 1987.a

Annual herb, 30–80 cm tall, few-branched. Branches slender, slightly villose. Petioles long, slender; leaves membranaceous, broad-ovate, 5 –10 × 3 –5 cm, base cordate or cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex acute, margin crenate-dentate, triplinerved; lateral veins 3 –11 each side, roughly and appressed-pilose on both surfaces. Cymes axillary, 5 mm in diam.; male and female flowers mixed together. Male flowers: perianth campanulate, 4-lobed; stamens 4, exserted, opposite perianth-lobes. Female flowers: perianth-lobes boat-shaped; ovary slightly compressed-globose; style lateral, filiform, 1–1.5 mm. Achenes compressed-trigonous, 1 mm, with dispersed, raised, minute spots, 1-seeded.

Locality: Causeway Bay. HK sheet 6429; H. C. Tang 1413.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; E & SE Asia to Australia, New Caledonia.
Ecology: Roadsides and by streams. Flowering and fruiting: Late spring to autumn.

Ficus altissima Blume 高山榕（雞榕）
Bijdr. 444. 1825; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 391. 1965; FGD 1: 196. 1987; FOC 5: 43. 2003.

Large tree, 25–30 m tall; bark grey, glabrous. Young branchlets puberulent. Stipules 2–3 cm, grey sericeous. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaves thick leathery, broadly ovate to ovate-elliptic, 10–19 × 8–11 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Figs paired, axillary, elliptic-ovoid, 17–28 mm in diam., enclosed within cauducous bracts when young, red or yellowish when ripen, apex umbilicate-salient, basal bracts short, broadly obtuse, leaving annular scars after falling off. Male flowers scattered in inner walls of figs; perianth 4-parted, membranous; stamen 1. Perianth of gall and female flowers as in male flowers. Achenes verrucose; style elongated.

Locality: Cultivated. Caine Rd. Y. S. Lau 1154; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 36186).
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, margins of forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, host of lac insect.

Ficus benjamina L. 垂葉榕
Mant. 1: 129. 1767; FHN 2: 392. 1965; FGD 1: 196. 1987; FOC 5: 45. 2003.

Large tree, up to 20 m tall; crown broad, aerial roots pendulous from large branches, reaching ground and rooting, forming new trunks with drooping branches; bark grey, glabrous. Branchlets pendulous. Stipules lanceolate, ca. 6 mm. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves thinly leathery, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate, margin entire, not 3-veined at base; lateral veins many, parallel, fine, connected at margins. Figs paired or single, red, yellow or orange, globose or compressed-globose, 0.8–1.5 cm in diam., glabrous, basal bracts 3, triangular-ovate; male, female and gall flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, shortly pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, broadly ovate; stamen 1; filament short. Gall flowers: many, pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4–5, narrowly spathulate; ovary ovoid; style lateral. Female flowers: sessile; perianth-lobes 3, shortly spathulate. Achenes ovate-reniform, shorter than style; styles sublateral; stigma dilated.

Locality: Cultivated. C. I. Lei 92.
Distribution: S to SW China; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Roadside tree.

Ficus concinna (Miq.) Miq. 雅榕
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 3: 286. 1867; FGD 1: 198. 1987; FOC 5: 40. 2003.

Tree, 15–20 m tall; bark dark grey, lenticellate. Branchlets thick, glabrous. Stipules lanceolate, ca. 1 cm. Petioles short; leaves alternate, elliptic, 5 –10 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–8 pairs, conspicuously, net-veined. Figs light blue-purple, sometimes with yellow spots, paired or 3– 4-clustered, axillary, globose, 5–8 mm in diam., basal bracts minute; peduncles 1–5 mm; male, female and gall flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, near mouth, perianth-lobes 2, lanceolate; ovary oblique-ovate; style lateral, stigma round. Gall flowers similar to female flowers; style filiform, short.

Locality: Ma On Shan Village. Y. W. Lam 1675.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.

Ficus elastica Roxb. ex Hornem. 印度榕（印度橡樹）
Fl. Ind. 3: 543. 1832; FHN 2: 391. 1965; FGD 1: 196. 1987; FOC 5: 42. 2003.

Large tree, 20–30 m tall. Branchlets thick. Stipules membranaeous, up to 10 cm, leaving annular scars on branches after falling down. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaves thick leathery, oblong or elliptic, 8–30 × 4 –11 cm, base rounded, apex acute, margin entire, shining abaxially, midvein distinct; lateral veins many, parallel. Figs paired, borne on axils of leaf scars, ovate-oblong, 10 × 5–8 mm, male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, ovate, stamens 1. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes 4, ovary glabrous; style subsessile, curved. Female flowers: sessile. Achenes ovoid, verrucose, persistent style long; stigma subcapitate.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 25431; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35991).
Distribution: Cultivated in S to SW China. Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions; native to Sikkim, NE India, Myanmar, N Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ficus erecta Thunb. 天仙果
Diss. Ficus 5. 1786; FKH 246. 1912; FOC 5: 54. 2003.
Ficus erecta Thunb. var. beecheyana (Hook. & Arn.) King, Ann. Bot. Gard. Calcutta 1(2): 142, pl. 178A. 1888; FRPS 23(1): 134. 1998; FGD 1: 208. 1987.

Small tree or shrub, 2–7 m tall. Branchlets densely hirsute. Stipules caducous. Petioles 1–4 cm, slender, densely white hirsute; leaves thick papery, obovate-elliptic, 7–20 × 3 –9 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or rarely undulate on upper margin, surfaces scabrous, sparsely pubescent adaxially, pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 5–7 pairs.
