Figs yellow-red or purple-black, solitary axillary, globose or pyriform, 1.2–2 cm in diam., terminal bracts umbilicate, basal bracts 3, ovate-triangular, male and gall flowers in one set, female flowers in another set. Male flowers: pedeicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3 or 2– 4, elliptic to ovate-lanceolate; stamens 2–3. Gall flowers: subsessile or shortly pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 –5, lanceolate, hairy; ovary ellipsoid-globose; style lateral; stigma 2- fid. Female flowers; perianth-lobes 4 –6, broadly spathulate; ovary glabrous, shortly stalked; style lateral; stigma 2-fid.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 382, 597.
Distribution: SW to SE China; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Ficus esquiroliana H. Lév. 黃毛榕（馬鞍天仙果）
Bull. Acad. Int. Geogr. Bot. 24: 252. 1914; Hill, Figs. Hongk. 59, pl. 39. 1967; FOC 5: 60. 2003.
Ficus fulva auct. non Reinw. ex Blume: FKH 247. 1912; FHN 2: 390. 1965; FGD 1: 193. 1987.

Small tree or shrub, 4–10 m tall; bark with longitudinal ridges. Young branchlets yellow hirsute, hollowed at center. Stipules lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, caducous. Petioles 5 –11 cm, sparsely brown hirsute; leaves alternate, thick papery, broadly ovate, but lobed when young, 17–27 × 12–20 cm, base shallow-cordate, apex caudate, tip ca. 1 cm, margin serrulate, teeth point pilose, sparsely strigose adaxially, long or short, brown-yellow or grey white hairy; basal veins 5 –7, lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Figs paired, sessile, axillary, conic-ovoid, 20 –25 mm in diam., light brown hairy; basal bracts ovate-lanceolate, 8 mm, terminal bracts umbilicate. Male flowers at inner wall of mouth, stipitate; perianth-lobes 4; stamens 2. Gall flowers same as female flowers; perianth-lobes 5; ovary globose, glabrous; style lateral, short; stigma funnel-shaped. Achenes obliquely ovoid, verrucose.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ta Tit Yan. HK sheet 25476, 32110.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang, Fujian; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests or along streams. Flowering and fruiting: May–Nov.

Ficus fistulosa Reinw. ex Blume 水同木
Bijdr. 442. 1825; FGD 1: 192. 1987; FOC 5: 50. 2003.
Ficus harlandii Benth., FHK 330. 1861; FKH 247. 1912; FHN 2: 388. 1965.

Small tree; bark black-brown. Stipules ovate-lanceolate, ca. 1.7 cm. Petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaves alternate, papery, obovate to oblong, 10–20 × 4–7 cm, base oblique cuneate or rounded, apex mucronate, margin entire or repand, glabrous adaxially, slightly pubescent or minutely punctate-scabrous abaxially; basal veins short, lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Figs clustered on verrucose brachyblast from old wood, orange, subglobose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., glabrous. Peduncles 8–24 mm, male and gall flowers in one set, pedicellate. Male flowers near mouth, few; perianth-lobes 3–4; stamen 1, filaments short. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes very short or absent; ovary glabrous, obovoid; style sublateral, slender; stigma ampliate. Female flowers: in another set; perianth tubular, enclosed lower part of fruit stalk. Achenes rhomboidal, verrucose; style elongated, clavate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2196; Y. S. Lau 1970.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests in valleys or by streams. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Ficus formosana Maxim. 台灣榕
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 27: 546. 1881; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 397. 1965; FGD 1: 206. 1987; FOC 5: 58. 2003.
Ficus formosana var. shimadai (Hayata) W. C. Chen, FGD. 1: 207. 1987, nom. illeg.
Ficus formosana f. shimadai Hayata, Ic. Pl. Form. 8: 118. 1919.

Shrub, 1.5 –3 m tall. Branchlets sparsely pilose. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 0.5 cm. Petioles 0.7–1 cm; leaves membranaceous, oblanceolate to linear, 4–11 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or rarely coarsely dentate; lateral veins 5–15 pairs. Figs green with reddish, solitary, axillary, ovoid-globose, 6 –9 cm in diam., apex mucronate, basal bracts 3; stalk stout, 0.5–1 cm; male and gall or female flowers mixed. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, ovate; stamens 2, rarely 3. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes 4–5; ovary globose, stipitate; style lateral. Female flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 4; styles elongated; stigma infundibular.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau. HK sheet 36154, 36288, 36249.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Ficus hederacea Roxb. 藤榕（爬牆榕）
Fl. Ind. 3: 538. 1832; FHN 2: 398. 1965; FGD 1: 211. 1987; FOC 5: 68. 2003.

Climber. Young branchlets pubescent. Petioles 10 –20 mm; leaves distichous, thickly leathery, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, 6–11 × 3.5 –5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse, rarely round, margin entire, hairy when young, papillary on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Figs simple or paired, axillary, globose, 7–14 mm in diam., apex umbonulate; basal bracts connate below medium, upper 3-lobed. Peduncles 10–12 mm. Male flowers: few, sparsely, sessile; perianth-lobes 3– 4; stamens 2, filaments free. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, lanceolate; ovary black, obovate; style short, subterminal; stigma curved. Female flowers: pedicellate, in another figs; perianth-lobes 4, linear. Achenes ellipsoid, keeled abaxially; style elongated.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau. C. Ford s.n. (HK 25645); Y. S. Lau 482.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, on rocks. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Jul.

Ficus hirta Vahl 粗葉榕（牛奶仔）
Enum. Pl. 2: 203. 1806; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 247. 1912; FGD 1: 194. 1987; FOC 5: 60. 2003.
Ficus simplicissima var. hirta Migo in Bull. Shanghai Sci. Inst. 14: 331. 1944; FHN 2: 390. 1965.

Shrub or small tree. Young branchlets shollowed, branchlets, leaves and figs golden hirsute. Stipules red, ovate-lanceolate, 1–3 cm. Petioles 2–8 cm; leaves alternate, papery, very variable in shape, oblong-lanceolate to broadly ovate, 10 –25 cm, base rounded, shallow-cordate, or broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrulate, entire or deeply 3 –5-lobed, basal veins 3 –5; lateral veins 4 –7 pairs. Figs paired, axillary, or on leafless branches, globose or ellipsoid, 10–15 mm in diam., sessile or subsessile, apex umbonulate, basal bracts ovate-lanceolate. Male flowers near mouth, pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, red, lanceolate; stamens 2–3; anthers longer than filament. Gall flowers: perianthlobes 4; ovary globose; style lateral; stigma infundibular. Female flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 4. Achenes ellipsoid, glabrous; style elongated; stigma clavate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 36; Y. S. Lau 2319.
Distribution: SW to SE China; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, thickets, near villages by streams. Flowering and fruiting: almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ficus hispida L. f. 對葉榕
Suppl. Pl. 442. 1781; FHK 329. 1861; FKH 247. 1912; FHN 2: 387. 1965; FGD 1: 190. 1987; FOC 5: 49. 2003.

Shrub or small tree; young branches hispid. Stipules ovate-lanceolate, often 4, decussate. Petioles 1– 4 cm, hispid; leaves mostly opposite, thickly papery, ovate or obovate to oblong, 10 –25 × 5 –10 cm, base rounded to cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or crenateserrate, very rough on both surfaces with stiff hairs; lateral veins 6 –9 pairs. Figs yellow, axillary or 2–3 together on leafless branches of old stem, turbinate, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam., densely hirsute. Male flowers near mouth, many; perianth-lobes 3, membranous; stamen 1, perianth of gall and female flowers truncate, thin and transparent (easily overlooked). Gall flower: style subterminal, short. Female flower: style lateral, hairy.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 6501; L. T. Lo 488.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Thickets of wasteland, by streams. Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ficus langkokensis Drake 青藤公
J. Bot. (Morot) 10: 215. 1896; FGD 1: 208. 1987; FOC 5: 53. 2003.

Tree, 6–15 m tall; bark red-brown or grey-yellow. Branchlets slender, ferrugineo-scurfy. Stipules lanceolate, 7–10 mm. Petioles 1–4 cm. Leaves alternate, papery, elliptic-lanceolate to elliptic, 7–19 × 2–6 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; basal nerves 3, lateral veins 2–4 pairs. Figs paired or simple, axillary, globose, 5–12 mm in diam., ferrugineo-scurfy, apex umbonulate; basal bracts 3, broadly ovate; peduncles slender, 5–15 mm, ferrugineo-scurfy. Male flowers: pedicellate; perianthlobes 3– 4, ovate; stamens 1–2, filaments short. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 4, obovate, dark red; styles lateral.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lai Chi Wo. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 25749); Y. W. Lam 525.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; India, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Sep.

Ficus microcarpa L. f. 榕樹（細葉榕）
Suppl. Pl. 442. 1781; Corner, Gard. Bull. Singapore 17: 397. 1959; FHN 2: 393. 1965; FGD 1: 198. 1987; FOC 5: 44. 2003.
Ficus retusa auct. non L.: FHK 327. 1861; FKH 246. 1912.

Large tree, 15–25 m tall; bark deep grey, crown ample. Branches often bearing pendulous aerial roots. Stipules lanceolate, 1.5 –3.5 cm. Petioles stout, 5–10 mm, glabrous; leaves leathery, elliptic, ovate-elliptic or obovate, 4–8 × 3–4 cm, base cuneate, apex bluntly apiculate, entire, rarely emarginate, basal veins 3; lateral veins 3–10 pairs. Figs yellowish or reddish, paired or solitary, axillary, obovoid, 6–8 mm in diam., without peduncles, basal bracts 3, oval, persistent; male, gall and female flowers in one set, with few bristles mixed with them. Male flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3–4, elliptic to oblanceolate; stamen 1. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3–5, broadly spathulate; ovary globose; style lateral, rather long; stigma trumpet-shaped. Female flowers: sessile; perianth-lobes 3–5; ovary ovoid; style slender; stigma acute.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2323; L. Gibbs 7567.
Distribution: SW, S to SE China; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Roadside tree.

Ficus nervosa B. Heyne ex Roth 九丁樹（凸葉榕）
Nov. Pl. Sp. 388. 1819; FHK 327. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 393. 1965; FGD 1: 200. 1987; FOC 5: 46. 2003.

Medium sized tree; bark dark brown. Branchlets pubescent. Stipules fugacious. Petioles 1.5–2.5 cm, scurfy; leaves leathery, oblanceolate, oblong to elliptic, 6 –15(–20) × 2.5 – 6 cm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex short-acuminate, margin entire, basal nerves 3; lateral veins 7–11 pairs, midvein and lateral veins prominent abaxially. Figs yellow or reddish-brown, solitary or paired, axillary, globose, 1–1.2 cm in diam., glabrous, basal bracts none; stalks slender; male, gall and female flowers mixed in one fig. Male flowers: few near apex of figs; perianthlobes 3–5; stamen 1, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary ovoid; style sublateral; stigma clavate. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 3– 4, ovoid; style slender, terminal or sublateral; stigma elongate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Yim Tso Ha, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2271; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 34799).
Distribution: SW, S to SE China; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, along roadside by streams. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Timber.

Ficus pandurata Hance 琴葉榕
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 229. 1862; FHN 2: 400. 1965; FGD 1: 205. 1987; FOC 5: 59. 2003.
Ficus holophylla Migo, Bull. Shanghai Instit. 14: 329. 1944.
Ficus pandurata Hance var. holophylla Migo, Bull. Shanghai Sci. Inst. 14: 329. 1944; Check List HK Plants 27. 2004.

Small shrub, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets white, pubescent when young. Stipules lanceolate. Petioles 3 –5 mm; leaves papery, pendurate, obovate, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 3 –15 × 1.2– 6 cm, base rounded or to broadly cuneate, sometimes constricted at middle, apex acute, mucronate, glabrous adaxially, verrucose and sparsely pubescent on nerves abaxially; lateral veins 3 –5 pairs. Figs scarlet, solitary, axillary, elliptic or globose, 4–10 mm in diam., apex umbonate, basal bracts 3, ovate. Peduncles slender, 4 –5 mm. Male flowers: near the mouth; perianth-lobes 4, linear; stamens 3, rarely 2, unequal. Gall flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3 – 4, oblanceolate to linear, ovary subglobose; style lateral, very short. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 3 – 4, elliptic; style lateral, elongate; stigma infundibular.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, the New Territories. P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35391); Levine & Kwok s.n. (HK sheet 25463, 25465).
Distribution: SW, S to SE China.
Ecology: Open field, near villages. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Nov.

Ficus pumila L. 薜荔（文頭郎）
Sp. Pl. 1060. 1753; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 395. 1965; FGD 1: 212. 1987; FOC 5: 69. 2003.
Ficus stipulata Thunb., Dissert. Ficus 8. 1786; FHK 328. 1861.

Shrub prostrate or creeping, adventitious roots arising from unfruiting branches. Stipules 2, lanceolate, yellow-brown silk hairy. Leaves on sterile branches thin leathery, ovate-cordate, ca. 2.5 cm, base slightly unequal, apex acuminate. Petioles 5–10 mm, very short; leaves on fertile branches leathery, ovate-elliptic, 5–10 × 2–3.5 cm, base rounded to shallow cordate, apex acute to obtuse, margin entire, glabrous adaxially, yellow-brown pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 3–4 pairs, reticulate veins distinct, alveolar. Figs solitary or paired, axillary, yellow-green or reddish, pearshaped or turbinate, 3.5 – 6.5 cm in diam., somewhat pubescent, basal bracts 3, stalk short and thick, 0.5 –1.5 cm, pubescent. Male flowers: long-pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; stamens 2, sessile. Gall flowers: long-pedicellate to sessile; perianth-lobes 4, linear; ovary sessile; style lateral; stigma dilated. Female flowers in another fig: long pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 4–5; ovary sessile. Achenes subglobose, mucilaginous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 714, 2271; Y. S. Lau 1347.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Japan, India, Vietnam.
Ecology: On walls and trees. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Dec.
Uses: Edible, medicinal (folklore).

Ficus pyriformis Hook. & Arn. 舶梨榕
Bot. Beechey Voy. 216. 1836; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 396. 1965; FGD 1: 203. 1987; FOC 5: 54. 2003.

Shrub, 1–2 m tall, branchlets hirsute. Stipules red, lanceolate, ca. 1 cm. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaves papery, oblanceolate or oblonglanceolate, 4–11 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, round, apex obtuse-acuminate, margin entire slightly revolute, puberulent and verrucose abaxially; lateral veins 5 –9 pairs, anastomosing very near margin. Figs solitary, axillary, pear-shaped, 2–3 cm in diam., glabrous, white, maculate, much constricted at base. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, lanceolate; stamens 2. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes 4, linear; ovary globose; style lateral. Female flowers in another fig; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary reniform; style lateral, elongated. Achenes verrucose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1347; L. T. Lo 51.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Along ditches, in thickets. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Nov.

Ficus religiosa L. 菩提樹
Sp. Pl. 1059. 1753; FGD 1: 197. 1987; FOC 5: 41. 2003.

Large tree, epiphytic when young, 15 –25 m tall; crown ample. Branchlets grey-brown, pubescent. Stipules small. Petioles slender, articulate, as long as leaf-blade or longer; leaves leathery, triangular-ovate, 9 –17 × 8 –12 cm, base truncate to shallow-cordate, apex caudate, margin entire or undulate, 2–5 cm, basal veins 3; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs. Figs red, globose to oblate, 1–1.5 cm in diam., basal bracts 3, ovoid; peduncles 4–9 mm; male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, near mouth, sessile; perianth-lobes 2–3, involute; stamen 1, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary globose, glabrous; style short; stigma dilated, 2-fid. Female flowers: sessile; perianth-lobes 4, broadly lanceolate; style slender; stigma narrow.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 15; Y. S. Lau 2261.
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; native to India.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ficus rumphii Blume 心葉榕
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 437. 1825; FOC 5: 42. 2003.

Tree, ca. 15 m tall, usually epiphytic when young. Bark grey. Stipules caducous, ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 cm, scar conspicuous. Petiole 6–8 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ± leathery, cordate to ovate-cordate, 6–13 × 6–11 cm, glabrous, base ± cordate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate; basal lateral veins 5, secondary veins 5 or 6 on each side of midvein. Figs axillary on leafy branchlets, paired or in small clusters on leafless older branchlets, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., with dark spots when young, dark purple when mature, sessile; involucral bracts orbicular, small; apical bracts ± navel-like. Male, gall, and female flowers within same fig. Male flowers: few, scattered among other flowers; perianth-lobes 3, lanceolate; stigma clavate. Achenes tuberculate and with adherent liquid; style long; stigma clavate.

Locality: Cultivated in parks and along roadsides.
Distribution: Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ficus sagittata Vahl 羊乳榕（箭葉榕）
Symb. Bot. 2: 185. 1806; FHN 2: 395. 1965; FGD 1: 204. 1987; FOC 5: 68. 2003.

Tree when mature, epiphytic vine when young; rooting from nodes. Stipules caducous. Petioles ca. 15 mm, slightly pubescent; leaves leathery, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 7–13 × 5 –10 cm, base cordate, apex acute to short-acuminate, margin entire to sinuate, nerves pubescent abaxially when young; basal veins 3 –5, lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Figs paired or solitary, axillary, rarely clustered on leafless branches or verrucose brachyblasts, orange, subglobose, 8–15 mm in diam., apex umbonulate, basal bracts 3, base constricted in short stalk. Male flowers: Perianth-lobes 3, ovate; stamens 3; filaments connate. Gall flowers: Perianth-lobes 3; ovary obovate; style lateral, short. Female flowers in another set; perianth-lobes 3. Achenes elliptic; styles long.

Locality: No precise locality. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6562, 6563).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Ficus sarmentosa Buch. -Ham. ex Smith var. impressa (Champ. ex Benth.) Corner 爬藤榕（凹葉榕）
Gard. Bull. Singapore 18(1): 6. 1960. FHN 2: 398. 1965; FGD 1: 212. 1987; FOC 5: 71. 2003.
Ficus impressa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 76. 1854; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 246. 1912.

Shrub prostrate or creeping. Stem much branched. Petioles 5 –10 mm; leaves distichous, leathery, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, 4 –7 × 1–2 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs, reticulate veins prominent abaxially. Figs paired, axillary, globose, 7–10 mm in diam., pubescent when young. Basal bracts 3, triangular. Peduncles 5 –15 mm, bristles dispersed in inner wall of figs. Male and gall flowers in one set, female ones in another set. Male flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3– 4, oblanceolate; stamens 2, filaments very short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, obovate-spathulate; ovary ellipsoid; style short; stigma shallow-infundibular. Female flowers similar to gall flower; ovary obovoid; style subterminal. Achenes ovoid-ellipsoid, mucilaginous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mun Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lautau Island. HK sheet 6506, 25549.
Distribution: Area S of Hebei; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering and fruiting: May–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Ficus subpisocarpa Gagnep. 筆管榕
Notul. Syst. (Paris) 4: 95. 1927; FOC 5: 40. 2003.
Ficus superba var. japonica auct. non Miq.: Hill, Figs Hongk. 18. 1967; FRPS 23(1): 96. 1998.
Ficus wightiana auct. non Wall. ex Miq.: FHK 327. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 392. 1965.

Deciduous tree, sometimes with aerial roots; bark black-brown. Branchlets reddish, glabrous. Stipules lanceolate, ca. 2 cm. Petioles 3 –7 cm; leaves alternate or clustered, subpapery, elliptic to oblong, 10–15 × 4 – 6 cm, base round, apex short-acuminate, margin entire or slightly undurate; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Figs purple-black, solitary or paired, axillary or on leafless branches, oblate, 5 – 8 mm in diam., apex concave, basal bracts 3, bradly ovate; peduncles 3–4 mm; male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, sessile; perianth-lobes 3, broadly ovate; stamen 1, anthers ovate, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3, lanceolate; ovary stipitate, stigma linear; style short, lateral. Female flowers as gall flowers but ovary sessile; stigma capitate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 290; Y. S. Lau 1966.
Distribution: S, SW to SE China; E, S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Open field and forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Sep.

Ficus subulata Blume 假斜葉榕
Bijdr. 461. 1825; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 393. 1965; FGD 1: 201. 1987; FOC 5: 66. 2003.

Shrub scandent, male plants erect. Branchlets slender. Stipules subulate, 1.5 –2 cm. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade papery, obliquely elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 8 –15 × 2.5 –7 cm, usually asymmetrical, apex abruptly acute to acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces when grown up, verruculose abaxially; lateral veins 7–10 pairs. Figs orange, paired or clustered, axillary or on leafless branches, globose or ovoid, 2–5 mm in diam., verruculose. Basal bracts sometimes sheath-shaped. Male flowers: perianth tubiform, 4-toothed; stamens 1. Gall flowers: perianth as in male flowers; ovary globose; stigma capitate. Female flowers in another set: perianth connate, apex toothed, hairy. Achenes ellipsoid; style lateral, elongated.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Mau Ping, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok. Y. S. Lau 1631, 2118.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Bhutan, Sikkim, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Nov.

Ficus tinctoria G. Forst. subsp. gibbosa (Blume) Corner 斜葉榕（水榕）
Gard. Bull. Singapore 17: 476. 1960 & 21: 74. 1965; FOC 5: 65. 2003.
Ficus gibbosa Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 466. 1825; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 394. 1965; FGD 1: 201. 1987.

Tree or epiphyte when young. Branchlets brown. Stipules ca. 7 mm. Petioles 0.6 –2 cm, stout; leaves alternate, leathery, very variable in shape, ovate-elliptic or subrhomboid, unequalsided, less than 13 × 5 cm on large trees, base cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse, acute or short-acuminate, margin entire or angulate, glabrous on both surfaces, basal veins 3; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces. Figs yellow, paired or solitary, axillary, subglobose, 5– 6 mm in diam., base abruptly constricted into a 5 –10 mm stalk, glabrous or puberulent, apex umbonulate, basal bracts 3. Male flowers: white; perianth-lobes 4 – 6, linear; stamen 1, rudimentary ovary present. Gall flowers: perianth as male one; ovary oblique-ovate; style lateral. Female flowers in another set: perianth-lobes 4, linear, hyaline. Achenes elliptic, verrucose and keeled; style lateral, elongate; stigma dilated.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Yuen Long, Fung Kat Heung, Tuen Mun, Sheung Shui, Sha Tau Kok. HK sheet 25493, 36769.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Taiwan; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Forests near villages. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Timber, host of lac insect, ornamental.
records.uses: Timber, host of lac insect, ornamental.

Ficus variegata Blume 青果榕
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 459. 1825; FHN 2: 388. 1965; FGD 1: 191. 1987; FOC 5: 49. 2003.
Ficus chlorocarpa Benth., FHK 330. 1861; FKH 247. 1912.
Ficus variegata var. chlorocarpa (Benth.) Benth. ex King, Ann. Bot. Gard. Calcutta 1: 170. 1888; FRPS 23(1): 174. 1998.

Large tree, up to 15 m tall; bark grey. Young branchlets green, sparse pubescent. Stipules ca. 1 cm. Petioles 5–7 cm; leaves thickly papery, broadly ovate to ovate-elliptic, 7.5–15(–20) × 6–13 cm, base round or shallowly cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire, shallowly sinuate or sparsely serrulate, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; basal veins 5, lateral veins 4–6 pairs, with reticulate veins distinct abaxially. Figs usually green, clustered on brachyblasts of trunk or branch, pear-shaped or globose, 1–2.5 cm in diam., apex umbonulate; basal bracts 3, caducous; peduncles 2–4 cm. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, broadly ovate; stamens 2, filaments base connate into a stalk. Gall flowers: perianth tubular, 4–5 toothed; style lateral; stigma infundibular. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, linear-lanceolate, membranaceous. Achenes obovate, slightly verrucose; style as long as achenes; stigma clavated.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 6470; L. T. Lo 490.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, host of lac insect.
Notes: The type specimen of Ficus chlorocarpa was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Ornamental, host of lac insect.
Notes: The type specimen of Ficus chlorocarpa was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Ficus variolosa Lindl. ex Benth. 變葉榕
London J. Bot. 1: 492. 1842; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 399. 1965; FGD 1: 209. 1987; FOC 5: 55. 2003.

Shrub or small tree, 3 –10 m tall; bark grey-brown. Branchlets with short internodes. Stipules long-triangular , ca. 8 mm. Petioles 5 –10 mm; leaves thinly leathery, narrowly elliptic, elliptic-lanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire; lateral veins 7–11 pairs. Figs paired or solitary, axillary, globose, 10 –12 mm in diam., verrucose, apex umbonulate; basal bracts 3, ovate-triangular , base slightly connate; peduncles 8–12 mm. Male flowers: near apical pore. Gall flowers: ovary globose; style short, lateral. Female flowers in another set; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary reniform; style lateral, slender. Achenes verrucose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 19; Y. S. Lau 1306.
Distribution: S, SW to SE China; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets or forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

Ficus vasculosa Wall. ex Miq. 白肉榕
London J. Bot. 454. 1848; FKH 246. 1912; FOC 5: 46. 2003.
Ficus championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 76. 1954; FHK 328. 1861; FGD 1: 204. 1987.

Tree, 10 –15 m tall. Branchlets grey-brown. Stipules ovate, ca. 6 mm. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves leathery, elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 4 –11 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin entire or irregularly lobed, dark green and shining adaxially, pale or whitish abaxially; lateral veins 10 –12 pairs, prominent on both surfaces, reticulate veins distinct adaxially. Figs yellow or yellow-red, globose, 7–10 mm in diam., base constricted into a short stalk. Peduncles 7–8 mm, basal bracts 3, deciduous; male, gall and female flowers within same fig. Male flowers: few, shortly pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3–4; stamens 2, rarely 1 or 3. Gall and female flowers: many, pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3–4; ovary obovate; stigma 2-fid. Achenes glabrous, apex keeled one side.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 327, Y. S. Lau 1232.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou; Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Dec.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen of Ficus championii was collected from woods of the Happy Valley by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Notes: The type specimen of Ficus championii was collected from woods of the Happy Valley by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Ficus virens Aiton 黃葛樹（大葉榕）
Hort. Kew 3: 451. 1789; FGD 1: 199. 1987; FOC 5: 40. 2003.
Ficus virens var. sublanceolata (Miq.) Corner, Gard. Bull. Singapore 17: 377. 1959, et 21: 9. 1965; FRPS 23(1): 95. 1998.
Ficus wightiana Wall. ex Benth., FHK 327. 1861; FHN 2: 392. 1965.
Ficus infectoria auct. non Willd.: FKH 247. 1912.

Deciduous or semideciduous tree, epiphytic when young, with buttressed or prop roots. Stipules lanceolate-ovate, up to 10 cm. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaves leathery or rigid papery, sublanceolate, 10–15(–20) × 4–7 cm, base obtuse-rounded, cuneate or shallow-cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins 7–10 pairs, prominent abaxially. Figs purple-red, solitary, paired, axillary or clustered on leafless branches, globose, 7–12 mm in diam., basal bracts 3, minute; peduncles absent; male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, sessile; perianth-lobes 4–5, lanceolate; stamen 1, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3–4; style lateral, shorter than ovary. Female flowers: like gall flowers; style longer than ovary. Achenes wrinkled.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1844, 2426.
Distribution: SW, S to SE China; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Roadside tree, timber, medicinal (folklore), host of lac insect.
records.uses: Roadside tree, timber, medicinal (folklore), host of lac insect.

records.text:
Fimbristylis acuminata Vahl 披針穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 285. 1806; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 102. 1961; FHN 4: 295. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 262. 2000; FGD 8: 309. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.
Fimbristylis setacea Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 2: 239. 1843.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 3–35 cm tall, 0.2–0.6 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves reduced to basal sheaths; sheaths cylindrical, 1.5–5 cm, pale green to light brown. Ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1, glume-like. Inflorescence a single terminal spikelet. Spikelet ovoid to ovoid-conical, terete, (4–)613 × 2–3 mm. Glumes 5–15 per spikelet, broadly ovate to elliptic, 2.7–4 × 1.5–2 mm, apex subacute, sides thinly papery to membranous, pale greenish, yellow brown to reddish brown, margins pale-hyaline, keel obtuse. Stamens 2; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Style long and compressed, sparsely ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate to orbicular, biconvex, 1–1.3 × 1–1.3 mm, whitish to cream, coarsely transversely wrinkled, very finely striate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Kellet, Yung Shue O, Chek Keng, Sai Kung, Ham Tin. Y. W. Lam 1717, 1723, 1726.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Papua New Guinea, Japan, tropical Australia.
Ecology: Sandy farmlands, secondary forests and crevices of rocks. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Fimbristylis aestivalis (Retz.) Vahl 夏飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 288. 1806; FHK 392. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 99. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 262. 2000; FYN 15: 614. 2003; FGD 8: 306. 2007; FOC 23: 214. 2010.
Scirpus aestivalis Retz., Observ. Bot. IV.: 12. 1791[1786].

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 3–20 cm tall, 0.3–0.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, 1.5–4 cm × 0.3–0.6 mm, acuminate, flattish or with incurved margins, ± pilose; sheath 0.5–1.5 cm, pale green to yellowish brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3(–6), leaf-like, the longest 1–5 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 2–7 × 2–7 cm; primary branches 3–7, 0.5–3.3 cm. Spikelets many per inflorescence, solitary, ovoid-conical, subterete, 2.5–7 × 1–1.5 mm. Glumes 10–40 per spikelet, spirally imbricate, ovate, 1–1.5 × 0.6–0.8 mm, acute, recurved-mucronate to shortly cuspidate, sides membranous, yellowish brown, keel subacute, finely 3-veined, green. Stamens 1, anthers 0.3 mm. Style long and compressed, basally inflated, apically ciliate; stigmas 2. Style-base glabrous or ciliolate. Achenes obovate, thickly biconvex, 0.5–0.6 × 0.3–0.4 mm, maturing yellowish, sometimes slightly shiny, smooth or faintly cancellate with a few rows of transversely oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Kau Wa Keng, Lam Tsuen, Tung Chung River. Y. S. Lau 2681; J. C. Shaw & Macia 291; HK sheet 40872.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Chongqing, Hunan, Hubei, Heilongjiang, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link 扁鞘飄拂草
Hort. Berol. 1: 292. 1827; FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 81. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 575. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 265. 2000; FYN 15: 603. 2003; FGD 8: 298. 2007; FOC 23: 205. 2010.
Scirpus complanatus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 14. 1791.

Perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms crowded in series along rhizome to ± tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 0.9–5 mm thick, flattened, smooth to scabrid, narrowly winged above. Leaves basal; blade linear, up to 26 cm × 2–5 mm, obtuse to rounded, flat, margins incurved; sheath 1–8 cm, obliquely truncate, pale to rusty brown; ligule a fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest suberect, 1–8 cm. Inflorescence compound, 4–10 cm; primary branches 4–7, 1–5 cm. Spikelets ellipsoidal to ovoid-lanceolate, terete, 4–9 × 1–2 mm. Glumes 5–20 per spikelet spirally arranged, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.8–2.5(–3) mm long, mucronate, sides chartaceous, yellowish brown to brown, margins paler, keel acute, green. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1 mm long. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated to conic; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 0.5–0.7 × 0.3–0.4 mm whitish, finely cancellate with several rows of transversely oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 812, 954, 1623.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics.
Ecology: Muddy seashores, wet places by streams or paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Fimbristylis cymosa (Lam.) R. Br. 黑果飄拂草
Prodr. 228. 1810; FRPS 11: 82. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 266. 2000; FGD 8: 299. 2007; FOC 23: 206. 2010.
Scirpus cymosus Lam. Tabl. 1: 141. 1791.
Fimbristylis spathacea Roth, Nov. Pl. Sp. 24. 1821; FKH 299. 1912.
Fimbristylis cymosa R. Br. var. spathacea (Roth) T. Koyama, J. Jap. Bot. 46(3): 66. 1971; FOC 23: 207. 2010. Fimbristylis wightiana Nees, Contrib. 99. 1834; FHK 392. 1861.

Perennial; rhizomes not or hardly elongate. Culms tufted, 5–60 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, rosetteforming; blade narrowly linear, 5–30 cm × 1–4 mm, subobtuse, subleathery, flattish to weakly inrolled; sheath up to 3 cm, whitish or cinnamon-brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1–3, leaf-like, the longest shorter than inflorescence, 0.5–1.8 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to congested; primary branches 2–6, 1–3 cm. Spikelets few to many per inflorescence, ellipsoidal-cylindrical to ovoid-cylindrical, 2–6 × 1–2 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate to broadly ovate, 1–2.2 × 0.5–1.5 mm, apex obtuse, sides membranous, mid-brown, margins broadly white-hyaline, keel obtuse, obscurely 3–5-veined, paler brown. Stamens 1–3; anthers 0.8–1 mm, connective smooth. Style slender, not ciliate, basally slightly thickened; stigmas 2(–3). Achenes obovate, biconvex to rarely compressed-trigonous, 0.7–0.9 × 0.5–0.7 mm, maturing dark brown to black, smooth to indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Stonecutters Island, Castle Peak, Ping Chau. J. C. Shaw 583; Y. W. Lam 986; Y. S. Lau 2476.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; tropics.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and mangroves. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Fimbristylis dichotoma (L.) Vahl 兩歧飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 287. 1805; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 89. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 580. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 266. 2000; FYN 15: 609. 2003; FGD 8: 303. 2007; FOC 23: 210. 2010.
Scirpus dichotomus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 50. 1753.
Fimbristylis diphylla (Retz.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 289–290. 1805; FHK 392. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 233. 1903; FKH 299. 1912.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms loosely tufted, 10–70 cm tall, 0.5–2.5 mm thick, triquetrous, glabrous to sparsely pubescent smooth. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, (3–)10–30 cm × 1.5–5 mm, obtuse, flattish, margins ± incurved; sheath 2–12 cm, pale green to mid-brown, apex truncate; ligule a fringe of dense hairs. Involucral bracts 2–7, the longest 1–2 leaf-like, 2–8 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to congested, 2–17 × 1–15 cm; primary branches 2–12, 1–8 cm. Spikelets 2 – many per inflorescence, solitary or in clusters of 2–3, ovoid to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 3–10 × 2.5–3.5 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, broadly ovate to suborbicular, 1.5–3(–4) × 1.5–2.2 mm, subacute, mucronate, sides thinly chartaceous, 2–4-veined or veins 0, mid-brown to dark reddish brown, margins pale-hyaline, keel obtuse, greenish to pale brown. Stamens (1–)2–3, anthers 0.5–1.7 mm long. Style compressed, apically ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate to broadly obovate, biconvex, 0.7–1.3 × 0.8–1 mm, maturing cream to pale brown, deeply cancellate with 5–13 rows of transversely oblong epidermal cells, occasionally verrucose on shoulder.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 529; Y. W. Lam 1217; K. L. Yip 4040.
Distribution: Spread over most provinces of China; widely distributed in subtropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Forage.
Notes: The type specimens of Fimbristylis diphylla Vahl var. leptophylla Benth. (FHK 392. 1861) were collected by H. F. Hance, C. Harland and C. Wright from Hong Kong in 1850s, but is not treated because no material is available. Clarke (J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 233 – 235. 1903) discussed the range of variation of this widespread species, including the two varieties from Hong Kong Island described by Bentham (FHK 392. 1861).

Bot. 36: 233 – 235. 1903) discussed the range of variation of this widespread species, including the two varieties from Hong Kong Island described by Bentham (FHK 392. 1861).

records.text:
Fimbristylis diphylloides Makino 擬二葉飄拂草
J. Jap. Bot. 11(4): 252, fig. 3. 1935; FRPS 11: 87. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 578. 1988; FGD 8: 301. 2007; FOC 23: 209. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent or very short. Culms tufted, thin, flatly 4-angled, striate, 15–50 cm tall, bearing 1–2 bladeless sheaths at base, sheaths cylindrical, 2.5 – 6.5 cm, mouth obliquely truncate, acute, covered with fibriform old sheaths; leaves shorter than or nearly equalling culms, flat, acute at apex, finely toothed at margins, 1.2–2.2 mm wide; sheaths membranous and rusty-brown adaxially, mouth obliquely split, without ligule. Bracts 4–6, much shorter than inflorescence, setaceous, dilated at base, finely serrulate on margins; anthelae simple or nearly compound, 1.5–6 × 2–6 cm; anthelae 4–8, scabrid, 0.6–4 cm; spikelets solitary, obovate or oblong-obovate, obtuse or nearly acute, 2.5–7.5 × 1.5–2.5(–3) mm, densely many-flowered; glumes broadly ovate or oblong-ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1 mm, membranous, extremely obtuse at apex, margins hyaline, 3-veined abaxially, veins green and slightly keeled. Stamens 2, anthers oblong, ca. 0.8 mm, about 1/2 length of filaments. Style not ciliate, base slightly inflated, stigmas 2–3, slightly longer than or nearly equalling style. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous or biconvex, ca. 1 mm, brown, with sparse verrucae and transversely oblong reticulation.

Locality: Lung Kwu Tan. HK sheet 37113.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. – Sep.

Fimbristylis eragrostis (Nees) Hance 知風飄拂草
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 132. 1873; FRPS 11: 103. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 269. 2000; FGD 8: 311. 2007; FOC 23: 216. 2010.
Abildgaardia eragrostis Nees, Contr. Bot. India 95. 1834; FKH 299. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1–few, 10–70 cm tall, 0.5–3 mm thick, 4–5-angled, smooth. Leaves basal; rosette-forming; blade linear, 5–20 cm × 1.5–5 mm, apex obtuse to ± truncate, mucronate, flattish, subleathery, margins often incurved; sheath 1–3 cm, brownish to yellowish brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–5, narrowly lanceolate to ± setaceous, 0.3–2 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to rather congested, 2–8 × 2–8 cm; primary branches 2–6, 1–6 cm. Spikelets 12– many per inflorescence, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 6–13 × 2–4 mm, often twisted, somewhat flattened. Glumes 8–25 per spikelet, ± 2-ranked to spirally arranged above, ovate, 3–5 × 2–3 mm, apex subacute, mucronate, sides papery, slightly shiny yellowish brown tinged dark brown, margins pale-hyaline, keel acute, 1-veined. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm long. Style brown, 3-sided, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–1 × 0.5–0.7 mm, light brown, verruculose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak. H. C. Tang 1988; HK sheet 13476.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan; Cambodia, Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, tropical Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Fimbristylis exaltata (T. Koyama) Y. F. Deng, st. nov. 血色飄拂草
Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link f. exaltata T. Koyama, Bull. Arts Sci. Div. Ryukyu Univ. 3: 70. 1959.
Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link var. exaltata (T. Koyama) Y. C. Tang ex S. R. Zhang & T. Koyama, FOC 23: 205. 2010.
Fimbristylis consanguinea auct. non Kunth: FGD 8: 297. 2007; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 110. 2004.
Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link var. kraussiana auct. non (Hook. ex Steud.) C. B. Clarke: FRPS 11: 81. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome short, covered with pale brownish scales. Culms densely tufted, often forming a large clump, slender, 15–50 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, glabrous, glaucous-green leaved at base. Leaf blades herbaceous, glabrous, mostly 1/2–2/3 as long as the culm, linear, 1–2.5 mm wide, margin apically finely serrulate, apex acute; ligule a fringe of short whitish pubescence; sheaths cylindrical with obtuse pale green back, 1–6 cm, the hyaline ventral side tinged with light brown, the orifice obliquely truncate, ciliolate, generally ± auriculate. Corymbs simple or in part subcompound, subdensely bearing 3–20 spikelets, 1–2.5 cm long and as wide; bracts 2–4, elongate, the lowest leaf-like, 5–25 mm, slightly shorter than to surpassing the corymb; anthelas 1–3.5 mm. Spikelets few, solitary, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 4–6 × 1.5–2 mm, brown to dark brown, several–10-flowered. Glumes spirally imbricated, ovate or ovate-oblong, 2.5–3 × ca. 2 mm, shallowly boat-shaped with convex keel, apex mucronate, thinly membranous, brown, finely 1–3-veined. Stamens 3; anther oblong, ca. 1.5 mm. Style 3-sided, ca. 2 mm, glabrous, basally inflated to conical; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.2 × 0.8–0.9 mm, apex rounded to mucronulate, base cuneate, pale yellowish, substantially smooth, with transverse oblong reticulation.

Locality: Happy Valley. HK sheet 8087.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Marshes and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Fimbristylis fusca (Nees) Benth. 褐穗飄拂草
Gen. Pl. 3: 1048. 1883; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 105. 1961; FYN 15: 615. 2003; FGD 8: 313. 2007; FOC 23: 217. 2010.
Abildgaardia fusca Nees, Contr. Bot. India 95. 1834; FHK 390. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with fibrous leaf sheath remnants. Culms few to several, (15–)30–55 cm tall, 0.5–1 mm thick, angular, smooth to hispid-scabrid above. Leaves basal; blade linear, 4–15 cm × (1–)2–4 mm, often weakly falcate, obtuse to rounded shortly acuminate, flat; sheath ca. 0.5 cm, yellowish brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 3–5, setaceous, 0.7–3 cm, glabrous or pubescent. Inflorescence simple to compound, open, 2–15 × 1–12 cm; primary branches up to 10 cm. Spikelets 3– many per inflorescence, lanceolate, subterete to ± flattened, 5–10 × 1.7–2.5 mm. Glumes 3–10 per spikelet, 2-ranked, lanceolate, 4–6.5 × 2–2.5 mm, sides herbaceous to ± papery, shortly hispid, chestnut-brown, margins narrow, hyaline, keel subacute, 1-veined, brown. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm. Style 4–5 mm, 3-sided, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obvoid, trigonous, 0.9–1 × 0.6–0.8 mm, light brownish, densely verrucose, obscurely reticulate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Kellet, Tai Mo Shan, Castle Peak. J. C. Shaw 526; S. C. Ng 1439; HK sheet 7976.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Nepal, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Fimbristylis hookeriana Bócklr. 金色飄拂草（羅浮飄拂草）
Linnaea 37: 22. 1871; FRPS 11: 94. 1961; FGD 8: 302. 2007; FOC 23: 212. 2010.
Fimbristylis fordii C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 236. 1903; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 94. 1961; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 111. 2004.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome absent. Culms tufted, 6–40 cm tall, without rhizome. Leaves nearly equalling culms, ciliate, 1–2.5 mm wide, apex acute, midvein prominent abaxially. Bracts 2–5, leafy, longer than inflorescence, sometimes up to 8 cm, apex acuminate or acute; anthelae simple, rarely compound, with few slender anthelas; spikelets solitary, narrowly lanceolate or linear, 7–17 × ca. 2 mm, lowest 1–2 glumes empty; flowering glumes oblong-ovate, 2.5–3.5 × 1.5–2 mm, greyish green or brown-hued, apex mucronate or awned, sometimes hairy, margins hyaline, with 3 or more veins abaxially. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, ca. 0.8 mm. Style slender, compressed, apically ciliate, basally slightly inflated, stigmas 2. Achenes obovate, biconvex, white, ca. 1 mm, shortly stipitate, verruculose.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar. S. C. Ng 2005, 4047; HK sheet 42172.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; India, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy fields, rocks along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.

Fimbristylis insignis Thwaites 硬穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 349. 1864; FKH 300. 1912; FGD 8: 300. 2007; FOC 23: 207. 2010.

Perennial; rhizomes short. Culms densely tufted, 20–60 cm tall, 0.5–2 mm thick, ± trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, many; blade linear, often somewhat falcate, 5–18 cm × 1–4 mm, rounded, leathery, margins serrulate, incurved; sheath 1–2 cm, pale greenish; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3, subulate, erect, the longest shorter than inflorescence, 0.5–1.5 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, 3–10 × 3–5 cm; primary branches 2–6, 1–8 cm. Spikelets (2–)4–18 per inflorescence, oblong-conical to cylindrical, terete, 12–20 × 2–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, ovate, 4–7 × 2.5–4 mm, apex obtuse, shortly cuspidate, sides chartaceous, orange brown, slightly shiny, margins narrowly pale-hyaline, keel obtuse, 1-veined, yellowish. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm. Styles 0.5–1 mm, 3-sided, glabrous; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid to obovoid-pyriform, trigonous, 1–1.3 × 0.8–1 mm, apex ± truncate, deeply furrowed on each side, indistinctly cancellate, sometimes verruculose.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam. S. Y. Hu 8497, 10876 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Burnt-over grasslands, rock outcrops, rarely wet forest floors.

Fimbristylis leptoclada Benth. 纖細飄拂草
FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FGD 8: 297. 2007; FOC 23: 208. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms tufted, 15–60 cm tall, 0.2–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth to scabird. Leaves basal, few; blade filiform, 10–30 cm × 0.3–0.5 mm, obtuse margins ± incurved; sheath 1.5–4 cm, pale-hyaline to mid-brown, apex oblique; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1–3, glume-like or setaceous, the longest 5–20 mm. Inflorescence simple or capitate, 5–20 × 5–8 mm; primary branches (when present) up to 2 cm. Spikelets 3–12 per inflorescence, in clusters of 2–8, ellipsoidal, 2.2–3.5 × 1.5–2 mm. Glumes 10–15 per spikelet, spirally imbricate, broadly ovate, 1–1.5 × 0.7–1.3 mm, rounded-truncate or shallowly emarginate, mucronulate, sides membranous, brown, densely gland-dotted, margins pale-hyaline, fimbriate-ciliate above, keel obtuse, 3-veined, pale brown. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.5 mm. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–0.9 × 0.5–0.7 mm, cream, verruculose.

Locality: High West. HK sheet 7977.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian; Japan, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Dry sandy grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Wright 579, K, holotype; US, isotype) was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong in 1850s.

Fimbristylis littoralis Gaudich. 水虱草（日照飄拂草）
Voy. Uranie 10: 413. 1829; FTW ed. 2, 5: 271. 2000; FOC 23: 208. 2010.
Fimbristylis miliacea (L.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 287. 1805, nom. rej.; FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 85. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 577. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 271. 2000; FYN 15: 604. 2003; FGD 8: 300. 2007; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 111. 2004.
Scirpus miliaceus L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 868. 1759, nom. rej.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome short. Clumstufted, 10–60(–90) cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, 4-sided, smooth, bearing 1–3 bladeless sheath at base. Leaves basal, or cauline reduced to bladeless sheaths; blade linear, 10–50 cm × 1–4 mm, apex subacute, bilaterally flattened; basal sheaths 1–18 cm, open, cauline sheaths tubular, 2–10 cm; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–4, setaceous, the longest 1 –3 cm. Inflorescence compound to decompound, open, 3–10 × 3–10 cm; primary branches 3–7, 1–7 cm. Spikelets many per inflorescence, ovoid-globose to globose, 1.5–3(–5) × 1–2.1 mm, 6–10-flowered. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, broadly ovate, 1–1.2 × 0.6–0.8 mm, apex obtuse, sides membranous, reddish brown, margins broadly hyaline, keel obtuse, yellowish, obscurely 3-veined. Stamens 1(–2); anthers oblong, ca. 0.6 mm long. Style 3-sided, apically compressed, sparsely pilose, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 0.6–0.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, creamy yellow, sparsely verruculose especially on angles, cancellate with 5–7 longitudinal rows of transversely linear-oblong cells.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1556; Y. W. Lam 1555; HK sheet 42185.
Distribution: Widely spread over S, SW and E China; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Fimbristylis longispica Steud. 長穗飄拂草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 118. 1855; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 91. 1961; FYN 15: 608. 2003; FGD 8: 304. 2007; FOC 23: 211. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms tufted, 25–60 cm. tall, with some leafless sheaths at base. Leaves shorter than culms, nearly glabrous, 1.5–2.5 mm wide, subglabrous, apex obtuse, margins often involute. Sheath brownish, glabrous. Bracts 2–3, leafy, the lowest one usually longer than inflorescence, apex obtuse; anthelae compound, decompound or simple, with 3–6 anthelas; spikelets solitary, narrowly oblong, oblong or oblong-ovate or ovate, 6–20 × 3–4 mm, apex acute or obtuse; glumes spirally arranged, broadly ovate, boat-shaped, ca. 3 × 2.5 mm, with 3–5 brown or pale brown veins, glabrous, apex mucronate. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 3 mm. Style slightly longer than achene, apically ciliate, basally slightly inflated, stigmas 2. Achenes globose-obovate, biconvex, 1.2–1.5 mm, pale brown to brown, sessile, with hexagonal reticulation, without vertical ribs and verrucae.

Locality: No precise locality. Faber 221 (K).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang; Japan, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia.
Ecology: Coastal area and wet places.

Fimbristylis nutans (Retz.) Vahl 垂穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 285. 1806; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 102. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 272. 2000; FGD 8: 309. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.
Scirpus nutans Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 12. 1786.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 20–75 cm tall, 0.5–1.5 mm thick, subterete to trigonous above, smooth. Leaves reduced to basal sheaths; sheaths cylindrical, 1–12 cm, light green to pale brownish, apex obliquely truncate; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1, glumelike. Inflorescence a single terminal spikelet, erect at first, soon becoming patent to ± horizontal. Spikelets ovoid to ovoid-ellipsoidal, terete, 8–16 × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, broadly ovate to ovate, 4–5 × 2.5–3 mm, apex rounded, mucronate, sides membranous to thinly papery, mid-brown, striate with dark brown below keel, margins broadly pale-hyaline, keel flattish to obtuse, indistinctly 4–5-veined, yellowish brown. Stamens 3; anthers 2 mm long. Style long and compressed, 3-sided, basally slightly inflated, apically sparsely ciliate; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovate, unequally biconvex, 1.25–1.5 × 0.8–1 mm, maturing cream to slightly brownish, coarsely transversely wrinkled.

Locality: Aberdeen, Lion Rock, Tung Chung. Y. S. Lau 2798; Y. W. Lam 1262; HK sheet 13448.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Fimbristylis pauciflora R. Br. 海南飄拂草
Prodr. 1: 225. 1810; FHN 4: 295. 1977; FGD 8: 308. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.
Fimbristylis hainanensis Tang & F. T. Wang, FRPS 11: 101, 228. 1961.

Perennial. Rhizomes hardly developed. Culms densely tufted, 5–18 cm tall, slender, short, flatly cylindrical, smooth, glabrous, with few leaf sheaths at base. Leaves bladeless; sheath brown, cylindrical, apically attenuate, margins membranous, mouth obliquely truncate. Involucral bracts absent. Inflorescences reduced to a single terminal spikelet, narrowly oblong to clavate-oblong, 3.5–4.5 × 1–1.5 mm, few-flowered, with basalmost glume empty. Glumes pale with rust-coloured short lines, oblong to oblong-ovate, 3–4.5 × 1–1.5 mm, 7–9-veined, midvein abaxially green, apex obtuse and not mucronate. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style long and compressed, sparsely ciliate, basally slightly broader; stigmas 3, with sparse papillae. Achenes white, obovoid, ca. 0.8 mm, trigonous, with sparse verrucae and nearly hexagonal reticulation.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 42200.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; India, Indonesia, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Wet places by ponds

Fimbristylis polytrichoides (Retz.) Vahl 細葉飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 248. 1806; FRPS 11: 96. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 274. 2000; FGD 8: 305. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.
Scirpus polytrichoides Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 11. 1786.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome very short or absent, with many remnant fibers from old leaves. Culms 5–30 cm tall, 0.3 – 0.5 mm thick, subterete to trigonous, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal; blade filiform, up to 4 cm × 0.2–0.5 mm, obtuse, shallowly canaliculate, often reduced to bladeless sheath; sheath 1–4 cm, yellowish brown, apex obliquely truncate; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1, glume-like or setaceous, 0.3–2.5 cm. Inflorescence a single, terminal spikelet. Spikelets ellipsoidal to oblong-ovoid 5–9 × 2.5–3.5 mm, obtuse. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 2.5–3.2 × 1–1.3 mm, obtuse, sides thinly membranous, pale brown on upper part, margins hyaline, keel obtuse, 1-veined. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.7–1 mm. Style long, slightly compressed, basally inflated, apical half ciliate; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate, biconvex, 0.8–1 × ca. 0.5 mm, maturing brown to greyish purple, minutely cancellate with 15–20 longitudinal rows of transversely linear epidermal cells, often verruculose above.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Rocky Harbour, Yi O. J. C. Shaw 701; Y. W. Lam 925; HK sheet 41737.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Africa, Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Muddy seashores and crevices of rocks. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

Fimbristylis rigidula Nees 結壯飄拂草
Contr. Bot. India 99. 1834; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 91. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 581. 1988; FYN 15: 609. 2003; FGD 8: 303. 2007; FOC 23: 211. 2010.

Perennial; rhizomes short, woody, covered with fibrous leaf sheath remnant. Culms usually solitary, 15–50 cm tall, 0.5–1.2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, often sparsely hairy above. Leaves basal; blade linear, 4–20 cm × 2–3.5 mm, acute, shortly apiculate, flat margins weakly incurved, glaucous; sheath 3–7 cm, pale to mid-brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest leaf-like, 1.5–4 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, rarely decompound, 2–5 × 2–3 cm; primary branches 3 – 6, up to 4 cm. Spikelets 5–20 per inflorescence, solitary or in pairs, broadly ovoid to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 5–8(–12) × 3–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate to broadly ovate, 3–3.2 × 2 mm, apex obtuse, often mucronate, sides chartceous, 3–4-veined, reddish brown, margins broadly white-hyaline, keel obtuse, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 1.7–2 mm. Style slender, compressed, apically ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate-orbicular, biconvex, 1–1.5 × 0.8–1.2 mm, greyish brown, verruculose, with 25 – 30 fine longitudinal rows of epidermal cells.

Locality: Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1256; HK sheet 8057.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, India, Thailand, Philippines.
Ecology: Grasslands of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Fimbristylis schoenoides (Retz.) Vahl 少穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 286. 1805; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 95. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 274. 2000; FYN 15: 610. 2003; FGD 8: 305. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.
Scirpus schoenoides Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 14. 1789.

Perennial; rhizome very short. Culms tufted, 5–50 cm tall, 0.3–0.8 mm thick, smooth. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear to ± filiform, 2–16 cm × 0.5–1 mm, flattish or with inrolled margins; sheath 2–6 cm, cinnamon-brown, apex obliquely truncate, ciliolate; ligule a fringe of dense short hairs. Involucral bracts 1–2, glume-like, rarely with short setaceous blade. Inflorescence usually a solitary spikelet sometimes simple; primary branches (when present) 1–2, 1–3 cm. Spikelets 1–2(–3) per inflorescence, ovoid to ellipsoidal, 5–10 × 3–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, ovate-orbicular, 2.5–3.2 × 2–3 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, shortly mucronate, sides thinly papery, 5–7-veined, pale to orange brown, slightly shiny, keel rounded. Stamens 2; anthers 0.5 mm. Style long, compressed, basally inflated, apical half ciliate; stigmas 3. Achenes obovate-orbicular, biconvex, 1.1–1.3 × 1–1.2 mm, ± rounded, maturing yellowish white, smooth with minute isodiametric epidermal cells.

Locality: Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Chek Keng. Y. W. Lam 1073; HK sheet 13457, 42171.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; S & SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Fimbristylis sericea (Poir.) R. Br. 絹毛飄拂草
Prodr. 228. 1810; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 83. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 276. 2000; FGD 8: 299. 2007; FOC 23: 208. 2010.
Scirpus sericeus Poir., Encycl., Suppl. 5: 99. 1804.

Perennial; rhizomes long-creeping, covered with often blackish brown fibers from old leaf sheaths. Culms erect, (10 – )30 – 60 cm tall, 1.2–2.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, many; blade linear, 4–10 cm × 1.7–4 mm, obtuse, margins inrolled, glaucous, with appressed silky hairs on the lower surface; sheath 2–3 cm, pale green to dark rusty brown, apex obliquely truncate; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3, leaf-like, the longest up to 2 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 3–10 cm × 3–4 cm; primary branches 2–6, 1–8 cm. Spikelets few to many per inflorescence, in cluster of 3–10, ovoid to oblong-ovoid, terete, 6–12 × 2.5–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate to broadly ovate, 2.5–4 × 2–3 mm, subacute to subobtuse, mucronate, sides herbaceous, brownish grey, shortly pubescent, margins whitish-hyaline, keel obtuse, brown. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1.5 mm. Style slightly compressed, basally slightly inflated and hairy, apically slightly pubescent; stigmas 2–3. Achenes obovate, biconvex, 1–1.5 × 0.8–1 mm, purplish or dark brown, ± smooth to minutely dotted.

Locality: Long Ke, Tai Wan (Sai Kung). Y. W. Lam 1736; HK sheet 39433, 41561.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Thailand, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and wet sand dunes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Fimbristylis sieboldii Miq. ex Franch. & Sav. 鏽鱗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 118. 1877 [“sieboldi”]; FOC 23: 212. 2010.
Fimbristylis ferruginea (L.) Vahl var. sieboldii (Miq. ex Franch. & Sav.) Ohwi, J. Jap. Bot. 14: 576. 1938; FRPS 11: 93. 1961.
Fimbristylis ferruginea auct. non (L.) Vahl: FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 93. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 269. 2000; FGD 8: 303. 2007; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 110. 2004.

Perennial; rhizome woody, creeping. Culms tufted, often forming clumps or crowded along creeping rhizome, 15–5 cm tall, 0.5–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves arising from lower part of culm; blade narrowly linear, 1–15 cm × 0.6–2.5 mm, obtuse, canaliculate to inrolled-margined; sheath cylindrical 2–12 cm, pale glaucous to brown or orange brown, apex truncate; ligule a fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 1–3, leaf-like, the longest ± erect, shorter to longer than inflorescence, 1–3 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, rather compact, 1.2 – 5 × 1– 3.5 cm; primary branches 3–7, 0.7–4 cm. Spikelets (1–)3–15 per inflorescence, usually solitary, ovoid-conical or ellipsoidal-conical, terete, 8–20 × 2.5–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, broadly ovateelliptic or broadly ovate, 3.5–4.2 × 1.8–2.8 mm, apex obtuse, mucronate, sides thinly chartaceous, pale to dark brown, sparsely to densely shortly pubescent, margins ciliate, keel obtuse, 1-veined. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–7 mm. Style long and flat, sparsely ciliate, basally broader; stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, biconvex, 1–1.2 × 0.7–0.8 mm, maturing light orange brown or yellowish brown, ± smooth, with indistinct isodiametric epidermal cells.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 2166; K. L. Yip 4193; Y. S. Lau 2490.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Fimbristylis subbispicata Nees & Meyen 雙穗飄拂草
Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 29(Suppl. 1): 75. 1843; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 95. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 277. 2000; FGD 8: 305. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Culms tufted, slim, 7–60 cm tall, flatly trigonous, greyish green, smooth, striate, with few leaves at base. Leaves shorter than culms, ca. 1 mm wide, slightly stiff, flat, upper part ciliate, sometimes involute. Bracts absent or only 1, erect, linear, longer than inflorescence, 0.7–10 cm; spikelet usually single and terminal, rarely 2, ovate, oblong-ovate or oblong-lanceolate, cylindrical, 8–30 × 4–8 mm, many-flowered; glumes spiral, membranous, ovate, broadly ovate or nearly elliptic, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, apex obtuse, mucronate, brown with short rusty-brown lines, not keeled, with many veins abaxially. Stamens 3, anthers linear, 2–2.5 mm. Style slender, compressed, ciliate, base slightly inflated, stigmas 2. Achenes globose to obovoid, flatly biconvex, brown, 1.5–1.7 mm, stipitate, with hexagonal reticulation, slightly shining.

Locality: Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Wu Kai Sha, Tung Chung. J. C. Shaw 667; Y. W. Lam 810, 1621.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hunan, Henan, Hebei, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Hillslopes, ravines along streams, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Fimbristylis tetragona R. Br. 四棱飄拂草
Prodr. 1: 226. 1810; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 100. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 277. 2000; FGD 8: 308. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.

Annual or perennial. Rhizome poorly developed. Culms densely tufted, 10–60 cm tall, 0.8–1.3 mm thick, sharply 4-angled, smooth. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths; sheaths 1 – 15 cm, pale greenish adaxially, yellowish brown abaxially, apex obliquely truncate, broadly hyaline; ligule absent. Inflorescence a single, terminal spikelet. Involucral bracts glume-like, inconspicuous. Spikelets broadly ellipsoidal to ovoid-ellipsoidal, terete, 5–12 × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, oblong-elliptic, 3–4.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, apex rounded, incurved, sides membranous, finely many-veined, yellowish brown and often tinged darker brown below keel, keel broad, 3-veined. Stamen 3; anthers 1–1.5 mm. Style long and compressed, sparsely ciliate, basally gradually broader and nearly as wide as nutlet; stigmas 2–3. Achenes linear-oblong to oblong, biconvex, 1.5–1.7 × 0.3–0.4 mm, cream, cancellate with 5 – 8 longitudinal rows of transversely oblong-hexagonal epidermal cells.

Locality: Aberdeen, Wong Chuk Hang, Wong Nai Chung. HK sheet 8085, 39296, 41584.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Fimbristylis thomsonii Boeck. 西南飄拂草
Linnaea 37: 37–38. 1871; FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 80. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 279. 2000; FYN 15: 602. 2003; FGD 8: 297. 2007; FOC 23: 205. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizomes short, stout. Culms 1–several, 20–80 cm tall, 0.7–2 mm thick, flattened-trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, 2-ranked; blade linear, up to 40 cm × 2–5 mm, abruptly acuminate, flattish; sheath up to 5 cm, truncate, pale green to rusty brown; ligule a dense fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest suberect, 1–8 cm. Inflorescence compound, rather open, 5–12 × 4–8 cm; primary branches 2–5, 0.7–9 cm. Spikelets oblong-ovoid to ovoid-lanceolate, angular, 5–8 × 2–3 mm. Glumes 6 – 17 per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate, 3–4 × 2–2.5 mm, acute to mucronate, sides papery, indistinctly 5–7-veined, chestnut-brown, margins membranous, keel acute, green. Stamens 3; anthers 2 mm. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 1.2–1.5 × 0.7–1 mm, whitish yellow, cancellate with several rows of hexagonal to transversely oblong epidermal cells and scattered papillae towards apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 390; H. C. Tang 1932; Y. S. Lau 1802.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam, Laos, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets and wet grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.

Fimbristylis tomentosa Vahl 絨毛飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 290. 1805; FYN 15: 610. 2003; FGD 8: 304. 2007.
Fimbristylis diphylla (Retz.) Vahl var. tomentosa (Vahl) Benth., FHK 392. 1861.
Fimbristylis podocarpa Nees, Contr. Bot. India 98. 1834; FHK 391. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 233. 1903.FKH 299. 1912.
Fimbristylis dichotoma (L.) Vahl subsp. podocarpa (Nees) T. Koyama, Micronesica 1: 87. 1964; FOC 23: 211. 2010.

Caespitose annual; rhizome absent, with fibrous roots. Stems tufted, angular, compressed just below the inflorescence, smooth, 40–60 cm tall, 0.5–1 mm thick. Leaves nearly distichous, ascending, 1/2–3/4 the length of the culms, 2–3 mm wide, flat, abruptly acuminate, softly hairy, rarely glabrous, scabrid on the margins in the upper part; sheaths margin ciliate-scabrid, abaxial surface pilosehirsute. Inflorescence simple or compound, loose, with 5–25 spikelets, very rarely reduced to a single spikelet, up to 8 cm. Involucral bracts up to 5, the longest overtopping the inflorescence, up to 10 cm. Primary anthelas obliquely erect, compressed, glabrous and smooth, the longest 2–4 cm. Spikelets solitary, ovoid or oblong-ovoid, rarely oblong, terete, 5–10(–15) × (1.5–)3–4 mm, apex acute, densely many-flowered, brown; rachilla narrowly winged. Glumes spiral, papery, appressed, broadly ovate or orbicular, 3 – 3.5 × 3.2 – 3.5 mm, apex mucronulate, scarcely keeled, with strong midvein. Stamens (1–)2; anthers oblong-linear, 0.7–1 mm. Style 1.2–1.5 mm, compressed, short and broad, hyaline-margined, gradually but slightly dilated towards the base, ciliate in the upper 2/3–3/4; stigmas 2, shorter than the style. Achene biconvex, broadly elliptic to orbicular, 1.1–1.5 × 0.9–1.4 mm, prominently stipitate (the gynophores obpyramidal, often somewhat saucer-shaped, 0.3–0.5 mm long and wide), umbonulate, sometimes tuberculate, especially towards the obtuse, thickened edges, at first white, finally stramineous, reticulate by the impressed epidermal cells superposed in 16–24 vertical rows on either face, verrucose.

Locality: Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1256; S. Y. Hu 6266 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropical Africa and Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Open places or light shaded moist grasslands.

Fimbristylis tristachya R. Br. 三穗飄拂草
Prodr. 227. 1810; FGD 8: 306. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms tufted, 30–70(–100) cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, angular, smooth to scabrid above. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, 7–27 cm × 0.5–1.5 mm, apex obtuse to shortly acuminate, flattish to canaliculate; sheath up to 15 cm, yellowish to brown, apex truncate; ligule a fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 1–2, leaf-like, the longest suberect, 0.5–3 cm. Inflorescence a single spikelet or simple to compound open; primary branches (when present) 0.8–4 cm. Spikelets (1–)3–6 per inflorescence, solitary, ovoid to ovoid-cylindrical, terete, (6–)10–25 × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, broadly ovate, 4–6 × 3–4.5 mm, apex obtuse, mucronulate, sides papery, indistinctly 7–10-veined, mid- to chestnut-brown, margins scarious, keel obtuse. Stamens 3; anthers 1.8–2.5 mm. Style ca. 3 mm long, compressed, apically ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate, biconvex, (1–)1.2–1.5 × 0.8–1 mm, rounded, yellowish brown, smooth, somewhat shiny, with minute isodiametric epidermal cells.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Shek O, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2504, 2520; Y. W. Lam 790.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; Asia, tropical Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Fimbristylis velata R. Br. 曲芒飄拂草
Prodr. 1: 227. 1810; FGD 8: 306. 2007.
Fimbristylis squarrosa Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 289. 1805; FHK 392. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 97. 1961; FYN 15: 612. 2003.
Fimbristylis aestivalis (Retz.) Vahl var. esquarrosa (Makino) T. Koyama, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 3. 8: 116. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 265. 2000; FOC 23: 214. 2010.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 10–25 cm, compressed and obtusely trigonous, with fewer leaves at base. Leaves shorter than culms, extremely narrow, less than 1 mm wide, flat or sometimes folded, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, sheaths pale brown, densely pubescent. Bracts 3–7, leafy, the lowest equalling or slightly shorter than inflorescence, base broader, pubescent; anthelae compound or decompound, spreading; anthelas many to fewer, up to 2.5 cm, slim; spikelets solitary, lanceolate or oblong, 3–7 × 1.2–2 mm, apex acute, many-flowered; glumes spiral, membranous, oblong, 1.5–2 mm, yellowish brown, obtuse, with 1 midvein abaxially, vein slightly upheaving extending into short awn ca. 1/5 length of glumes, slightly recurved; stamen 1, anther linear, ca. 0.5 mm; style long, slightly compressed, sparsely ciliate, base inflated with white long filiform pendent hairs covering the top of achene; stigmas 2, with papillae. Achenes obovate, flatly biconvex, yellow, ca. 0.5 mm, shortly stipitate, almost smooth or with very indistinct hexagonal reticulation.

Locality: Aberdeen. J. C. Shaw 345; Y. W. Lam 1505.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Yunnan, Shandong, Hebei, Heilongjiang, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Japan, Korea, Russia, S Europe to S Africa.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Firmiana simplex (L.) W. Wight 梧桐
U.S.D.A. Bur. Pl. Industr. Bull. 142: 67. 1909; FHN 2: 75. 1965; FGD 1: 130 1987.
Hibiscus simplex L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 977. 1763.
Firmiana platanifolia (L. f.) Marsili, Sagg. Sci. Lett. Acc. Padova 1: 106 –116. 1786; FRPS 49(2): 134. 1984.
Sterculia plantanifolia L. f., Suppl. Pl. 423. 1781; FHK 36. 1861; FKH 49. 1912.

Deciduous tree; bark green, smooth. Petioles as long as leaf-blade; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, palmately 3 –5-lobed, 15–30 cm in diam., base cordate, apex acuminate, glabrous or slightly pubescent abaxially, 7-veined. Panicles terminal 20– 50 cm; calyx yellowgreenish, 5-lobed, lobes linear, 7–9 mm, abaxially yellowish pubescent; anthers about 15; cells usually unequal and very irregularly crowded in a terminal head, often with imperfect, sessile anthers round the base of ovary in female flowers. Follicles stipulate, dehiscent before maturity, each carpel with seeds 1–2 on edge near base.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Shek O (Tai Long Wan), Sai Kung, Sai Wan, Po Toi. Cultivated or naturalized.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.
Uses: Ornamental, timber.

Fissistigma glaucescens (Hance) Merr. 白葉瓜馥木
Philip. J. Sci. 15(2): 132. 1919; FHN 1: 251. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 136, pl. 60. 1979; FGD 2: 33. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 415. 1996.
Melodorum glaucescens Hance, J. Bot. 19: 112. 1881; FKH 30. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches glabrous. Leaves sub-leathery; petioles 4–7 × ca. 2 mm; leaf blades 10–12 × ca. 2 cm, (obovate-) oblong or elliptic, glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent with simple hairs abaxially and glaucous when dry, base cuneate or subrounded, apex acute, obtuse or retuse; secondary veins 10–12 pairs; tertiary veins indistinct. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, (1–)6–10- flowered. Flowers light yellow; pedicels 4.5–7 × ca. 0.6 mm; bracts adnate to base or middle of pedicel, ca. 0.6 × 0.4 mm, ovate. Sepals 2–4.5 mm, triangular. Petals triangular; outer petals ca. 3.5–6 × 2–5 mm, pubescent both sides; inner petals ca. 5 × 4 mm, pubescent abaxially. Stamens numerous, ca. 1.5 mm long; connective pyramidal. Carpels ca. 15 per flower; ovary pubescent; stigma 2-cleft, glabrous. Monocarps few per fruit, 5.5–8.5 mm long, globose, glabrous; stipes ca. 2 mm long. Seeds 1–2 per monocarp, globose, pale yellow.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wu Kau Tang. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/07b (HKU); HK sheet 107.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Lowland forest. Flowering and fruiting: Spring to autumn.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Ford s.n. in Herb. Hance No. 21141, BM) was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in August, 1879.

Fissistigma oldhamii (Hemsl.) Merr. 瓜馥木
Philip. J. Sci. 15(2): 134. 1919; FHN 1: 250. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 162, pl. 57: 1–9. 1979; FGD 2: 36, fig. 26. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 416, pl. 193. 1996.
Melodorum oldhamii Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 27. 1886; FKH 30. 1912 (as M. oldhami).

Scandent shrubs. Young branches pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles ca. 5 × 1.1–1.4 mm; leaf blades 7–12(–16.5) × 2.5–3.5 cm, oblong to elliptical, densely pubescent with simple hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acute to obtuse; secondary veins 13–15 pairs; tertiary veins distinct. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–3-flowered. Flowers light yellow; pedicels 8.5–12(–20) × 1 mm; bracts towards middle of pedicel, 3–5 × 2–3.5 mm, oblong. Sepals 4.5–7.5 × 4–4.5 mm, ovate-triangular. Petals broad triangular; outer petals 12.5–16.5 × 5.5–7 mm, glabrous or hairy both sides; inner petals slightly smaller and more slender, glabrous. Stamens numerous, ca. 2 mm long; connective pyramidal. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary pubescent; stigma 2-cleft, glabrous. Monocarps 25–30 per fruit, ca. 18 mm long, globose, pubescent; stipes 2–2.5 cm long. Seeds ca. 10 per monocarp, broadly ellipsoid or lenticular, brown.

Locality: Mount Parker, Shek O, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Shek Pik Reservoir. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/03 (HKU); N. H. Li 32; Y. S. Lau 2125.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Fissistigma uonicum (Dunn) Merr. 香港瓜馥木
Philip. J. Sci. 15(2): 137. 1919; FHN 1: 251. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 136, pl. 61. 1979; FGD 2: 34. 1991.
Melodorum uonicum Dunn, J. Bot. 48: 323. 1910; FKH 30. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 6–10 × 1.3–1.9 mm; leaf blades 7.5–14.5 × 2–3.5 cm, oblong, sparsely pubescent with simple hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base cuneate to subrounded, apex obtuse to acute; secondary veins 14 – 16 pairs; tertiary veins indistinct. Inflorescences axillary, 1–2-flowered. Flowers yellow; pedicel ca. 6 × 2 mm; bracts near base of pedicel, small, oblong or ovate. Sepals ca. 2.5 × 2 mm, ovate-triangular. Petals ovate; outer petals ca. 24 × 13 mm, glabrous both sides; inner petals slightly smaller, glabrous. Stamens numerous, 1– 2 mm long; connective liguliform. Carpels few per flower; ovary pubescent; stigma clavate, glabrous. Monocarps 3 – 7 per fruit, 30 – 40 × 20 – 26 mm, ovoid, glabrous to pubescent; stipes ca. 4 mm long. Seeds 2– 3( – 11) per monocarp, flattened-ovoid, deep brown.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Tai Tam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/05 (HKU); HK sheet 1036, 34483.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fuji an.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Autumn.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by W. J. Tutcher from Hong Kong Island in 1893.

Flacourtia rukam Zoll. & Mor. 大葉刺籬木
Syst. Verz. 2: 33. 1846; FHN 1: 457. 1964; FGD 3: 107. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 42, pl. 9: 9 –11. 1999.

Tree, 5–15 m tall; trunk and old branches zigzag. Young plants armed; spines up to 10 cm; branches spiny or not. Mature plants without spines. Bark brown to grey, smooth; branchlets terete, puberulous, tuberculate and lenticellate when young. Petioles 6–8 mm, brown-pubescent; leaf blade ovate, elliptic to lanceolate, 6 –12 × 4 – 6 cm, more or less leathery, base rounded to obtuse, apex acuminate, margin crenate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent along midvein and lateral veins abaxially; lateral veins 5 –11 pairs. Racemes axillary, 0.5 –1 cm, puberulous. Bracts long-ovate, ca. 1 mm. Pedicels 3– 4 mm. Flowers yellowish green or white. Sepals (3–)4(–6), ovate, puberulous on both surfaces. Male flower: stamens ca. 25; filaments subglabrous, 3 – 4 mm; anthers yellow, small; disc fleshy, 8-lobed. Female flower: staminodes usually absent; ovary bottle-shaped, with 4– 6 parietal placentas; ovules 2 per placenta; styles 4 –6, distinct; stigmas 2-lobed. Drupe globose, deep red, 1.4 cm in diam., 4 – 6-angled, with persistent styles.

Locality: Shing Mun. L. T. Lo 459.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes or near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Flemingia macrophylla (Willd.) Prain 大葉千斤拔
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 66(2): 440. 1897; FRPS 41: 325. 1995; FGD 5: 340. 2003.
