Crotalaria macrophylla Willd., Sp. Pl. 3(2): 982. 1802.
Flemingia congesta Roxb. ex W. T. Aiton, Hort. Kew. (ed. 2) 4: 349. 1812; FKH 85. 1912.
Moghania macrophylla (Willd.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 199. 1891.

Erect shrub, 1 –2 m tall. Young branches angulate, densely sericeous. Stipules lanceolate, 8–9(–20) mm, caducous. Leaves digitately 3-foliolate; petioles 3 – 9 cm, narrowly winged; terminal leaflets broad-lanceolate to elliptic, 8– 15 × 4 – 7 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, pubescent on both surfaces, dotted with glands, especially on abaxial surface; lateral leaflets smaller, oblique. Racemes 3–8 cm, densely flowered, several-clustered in axil of leaves or forming terminal panicles. Bracts ovate, appressed sericeous, caducous. Calyx green, campanulate, sericeous; tube 2 – 3 mm; lobes lanceolate, 5 – 10 mm. Corolla pink; vexillum oblong, 10– 12 × 5– 8 mm, clawed and auriculate; wings narrowly elliptic, subauriculate, clawed; keel oblong, base long-clawed, auriculate on one side. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary sericeous. Pods brown, elliptic, 1– 1.6 × 0.6 – 0.7 cm, slightly pubescent, beaked at tip. Seeds 1– 2, globular.

Locality: Sai Kung, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Yuen Tun Ha, A Ma Wat. H. C. Tang 1427; Y. S. Lau 1167, 1333.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, thin forests. Flowering: Jun. –Sep.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Flemingia prostrata Roxb. f. ex Roxb. 千斤拔
Hort. Bengal. 56. 1814, & Fl. Ind. ed. 2, 3: 338. 1832; FGD 5: 340. 2003.
Flemingia philippinensis Merr. & Rolfe, Philipp. J. Sci. 3(3): 103. 1908.

Scandent or erect shrub. Young branches triangular, densely grey-brown pubescent. Leaves digitately 3-foliolate; terminal leaflets oblong or ovate-lanceolate, 4 – 7(–9) × 1.7 – 3 cm, base rounded, oblique, apex obtuse, sometimes mucronate, sparsely pubescent abaxially, densely villose adaxially. Racemes axillary, 2–2.5 cm, densely greyish brown or greyish white villose. Calyx deeply 5-toothed, teeth lanceolate. Corolla purple, 8 – 9 mm; vexillum oblong, shortly clawed, obscurely auriculate; wings falcate, clawed, slightly auriculate on one side; keel elliptic, slightly incurved, clawed, acute-auriculate on one side. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary hairy. Pods elliptic, 7–8 × 5 mm, turgid. Seeds 2, subglobular, black.

Locality: Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 3193; Y. W. Lam 1135.
Distribution: S, SW & E China; E Asia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Floscopa scandens Lour. 聚花草
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 193. 1790; FKH 284. 1912; FHN 4: 69, fig. 991. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 81. 1997; FOC 24: 25. 2000; FGD 6: 317, fig. 181. 2005.
Floscopa paniculata Hassk., Pl. Jungh. 151. 1852; FHK 377. 1861.

Perennial herb, 20–70 cm tall; stems simple, usually glabrous, creeping at the base. Leaves sessile or with short, winged petiole; leaf sheath hairy or only with hairs on 1 side, margin fringed with long hairs, at least at the top; leaf blade elliptic to ovate-lanceolate, 4–12 × 1–3 cm, scabrous adaxially; covered with multicellular hairs near the base abaxially. Panicle terminal, to 8 × 4 cm, densely glandular with long hairs; peduncle nearly absent; pedicels very short. Sepals shallowly boat-shaped. Petals blue or purple. Fertile stamens 6; filaments glabrous. Capsule ovoid, compressed, ca. 2 × 2 mm. Seeds grey-blue, semi-ellipsoidal, ca. 1.5 mm, shallowly radiate striate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen, Fanling, Sai Kung, Tai Mong Tsai, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2642; Y. W. Lam 454, 1378.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Oceania.
Ecology: Forests, wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Flueggea virosa (Roxb. exWilld.) Voigt 白飯樹（金柑藤）
Hort, Suburb. Calcutt. 152. 1825; FRPS 44(1): 72, pl. 19: 1 – 3. 1994; K. Chayamarit & P. C. vanWelzen, Fl. Thailand 8(1): 301. 2005.
Phyllanthus vorosus Roxb. exWilld., Sp. Pl. 4: 578. 1805.
Securinega virosa (Roxb. exWilld.) Baill., Adansonia 6: 334. 1866; FGD 42, fig. 25. 2003.

Unarmed, glabrous shrub, 1–4 m tall; branchlets sharply angular, glabrous, reddish-brown in new growth. Leaves papery; stipules lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm, entire or minutely lacerate; petioles 2–9 mm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong, obovate or rotund, 2–5 × 1–3 cm, base obtuse to cuneate, apex rounded to acute, mucronulate, entire and slightly revolute when dry, whitish abaxially; lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Flowers small, yellowish, in axillary glomerules; bracts thin, scarious, mostly less than 1 mm. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 3–6 mm; sepals 5, ovate, 0.8–1.5 × 0.6–1.2 mm, entire or obscurely serrulate; stamens 5, filaments 1–3 mm, anther ellipsoidal, 0.4–0.7 mm; rudimentary ovary usually 3-partite. Female flowers: 3–10-clustered, sometimes solitary; pedicels 1.5–12 mm; sepals as in male flowers; disk annular, entire; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3, 0.7–1.1 mm, bifid, connate at base. Capsules baccate, subglobose to oblate, 3–5 mm in diam., pericarps whitish when mature, indehiscent.

Locality: Tai Tam, Ngau ChiWan, Fanling, Po Leng , Tai Po, Butterfly Hill. Y. S. Lau 396, 2226; L. T. Lo 342; S. Y. Hu 7891 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in the area S of Qingling Range; widespread in Africa, Oceania, E and SE Asia.
Ecology: Shrublands on montane slopes. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Foeniculum vulgare Mill. 茴香
Gard. Dict., ed. 8, Foeniculum no. 1. 1768; FKH 117. 1912; FRPS 55(2): 213, pl. 86. 1985; FGD 2: 340, fig. 229. 1991; FOC 14: 134. 2005.
Anethum foeniculum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 263. 1753.

Biennial herb, 0.4–2 m tall, glabrous and glaucous throughout; stems erect, much branched. Basal leaves tufted; petioles 5–15 cm, sheathing; leaf blade broadly triangular in outline, 4–30 × 5–40 cm, 4–5-pinnatisect; ultimate segments linear, 1–6 × 0.1–0.5 cm; upper stem leaves smaller and shortly petiolate. Umbels 5–15 cm across; peduncles 2–25 cm; rays 5–25(–40), unequal, 1.5–10 cm; umbellules 14–39-flowered; pedicels slender, 2–10 mm, unequal. Calyx-teeth obsolete. Petals yellow, obovate, ca. 1 mm, 1-veined. Stylopodium conic; styles very short, 2-cleft. Fruit oblong, 4–6(–10) × 1.5 – 2.2(–2.5) mm; ribs 5, acute or round-obtuse; vittae 1 in each furrow, 2 on commissure.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 80; Y. S. Lau 2722; HK sheet 12514.
Distribution: Native to the Mediterranean region; cultivated and adventive worldwide.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food.

Fordiophyton peperomiifolium (Oliv.) C. Hansen 無距花

Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat., B, Adansonia 14(3 – 4): 425. 1992 [1993].

Sonerila peperomiifolia Oliv., Icon. Pl. 19: t. 1814. 1889.

Fordiophyton brevicaule C. Chen, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 18(1): 62. 1980; FRPS 53(1): 243, pl. 48: 2 –3. 1984, syn. nov.

Gymnagathis peperomiifolia (Oliv.) Stapf, FKH 107. 1912.

Stapfiophyton peperomiifolium (Oliv.) H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arb. 25: 29. 1944; FRPS 53(1): 235, pl. 48: 1. 1984.


Herb, with thick rootstock. Stems very short, densely brown hirsute. Leaves 3–5. forming a basal or sub-basal rosette; petiole 4 – 14(–20) cm, densely hispid, with glandular hairs, or rarely glabrescent; leaf blade ovate, ovate-elliptic, or broadly ovate, 5.5–11 × 3–7.5 cm, base subcordate, cordate, or rarely rounded, apex broadly acute, margin denticulate, the teeth with a setose tip, abaxially usually purple and setose on veins, adaxially with white spots and tuberculate after shedding of dense hairs, lateral primary veins 3 or 4 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences compound cymes, hirsute on nodes otherwise glabrous; peduncle 14–35 cm. Pedicel to 1.2 cm, lengthening to 1.9 cm in fruit, with sparse glandular trichomes and puberulous. Calyx-lobes triangular, ca. 1.7 × 0.8 cm, oblique, apex acute to shortly acuminate with a setose tip. Longer stamens ca. 2.5 cm; anthers oblong-linear, ca. 1.2 cm. Shorter stamens ca. 1.2 cm; anthers oblong, ca. 4.5 mm. Ovary oblong, apex truncate and with a membranous ciliate crown. Capsule funnel-shaped, 4-sided, 8-ribbed, ± hispid, apex truncate.


Locality: Ma On Shan, Nam Chung, Lung Chu Tam. P. S. Choi 221; Y. W. Lam 2138; HK sheet 35343.

Distribution: Guangdong.

Ecology: Lowland damp places, moist soil on stones. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Jun.

Notes: The type specimen of Fordiophyton brevicaule (C. Wang 32407, IBSC) was collected from Hong Kong on 1 Jun 1933.

Fortunella hindsii (Champ. ex Benth.) Swingle 山橘
J. Wash. Acad. Sci. 5: 175. 1915; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 556, fig. 2841. 1972; FHN 3: 48. 1974; FGD 2: 266. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 172, pl. 45: 2 –3. 1997.
Sclerostylis hindsii Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Misc. 3: 328. 1851.
Atlanthia hindsii Oliv. ex Benth., FHK 51. 1861; FKH 56. 1912.

Shrub, to 3 m tall, multibranched, shortly spiny. Leaves unifoliolate, sometimes simple; petiole 0.6–0.9 cm, winged; wings linear or conspicuous; blade elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 4–6 × 1.5–3 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex rounded, rarely acute or obtuse, margin denticulate near apex, rarely entire. Flowers solitary or few-fasciculate in axils; pedicels rather short. Calyx 4–5-lobed. Petals 5, shorter than 5 mm. Stamens ca. 20, filaments connate into 4–5 bundles, shorter than petals. Ovary 3–4-locular; styles as long as ovary. Fruit globose or slightly compressed globose, less than 1 cm in diam.; pericarp orange-yellow or red, smooth, pungent and slightly bitter; pulp acid. Seeds 3– 4, broadly ovoid, apex acute, smooth and not ridged.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Diamond Hill, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9963; H. C. Tang 2135, 1471.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Anhui.
Ecology: Secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by R. B. Hinds from Hong Kong Island in 1841.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by R. B. Hinds from Hong Kong Island in 1841.

records.text:
Fortunella japonica (Thunb.) Swingle 金柑（圓金橘）
J. Wash. Acad. Sci. 5: 175. 1915; FGD 2: 266. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 172, pl. 45: 4 –5. 1997.
Citrus japonica Thunb., Nov. Act. Upsal. 3: 199. 1780.

Small tree, 2–5 m tall. Branches spiny. Leaves unifoliolate; petioles 0.6–1 cm, winged; wings narrow to obvious; leaflets ovate-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, 4–8 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute. Flowers solitary or 2–3 in clusters; pedicels rarely longer than 6 mm. Calyx lobes 4–5. Petals 6–8 mm. Stamens 15–25, slightly shorter than petals, filaments connate into several bundles, few distinct. Ovary globose, 4–6-locular; styles nearly as long as ovary. Fruit globose, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam.; pericarp orange-yellow to orange-red, 1.5–2 mm thick, sweet; pulp sweet or acid. Seeds 2–5, ovoid, base rounded, apex acute or obtuse.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Nov.–Feb.
Uses: Edible (fruit), ornamental.

Fortunella margarita (Lour.) Swingle 金橘
J. Wash. Acad. Sci. 5: 170, fig. 2. 1915; FHN 3: 49. 1974; FGD 2: 267, fig. 177. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 173, pl. 45: 6 – 12. 1997.
Citrus margarita Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 467. 1790.
Citrus aurantium var. japonica Hook. f., Bot. Mag. 3: 30, pl. 6128. 1874.

Shrub to 3 m tall. Branches spiny. Leaves unifoliolate, thick, dark green; petioles to 1.2 cm, with rather narrow wings; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate or long elliptic, 5–11 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex slightly acute or obtuse. Flowers solitary or 2– 3 in clusters. Pedicels 3– 5 mm. Calyx 4– 5-lobed. Petals 5, 6–8 mm. Stamens 20–25. Ovary ellipsoidal; styles slender, usually 1.5 times as long as ovary; stigmas slightly enlarged. Fruit ellipsoidal or ovoid-ellipsoidal, 2–3.5 cm, orange-yellow to orange-red; pericarp sweet, ca. 2 mm thick; segments 4– 5; pulp acid. Seeds 2–5, ovoid, apex acute.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: S China (cultivated).
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Nov.–Jan.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Fraxinus chinensis Roxb. 白蠟樹
Fl. Ind. 1: 150. 1820; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 364, fig. 296. 1989; FRPS 61: 30, pl. 8: 7 – 10. 1992; FOC 15: 277. 1996; FGD 5: 414. 2003.

Deciduous tree to 20 m tall; branchlets terete, glabrous, or initially villous; winter buds broadly ovoid or conical, brown tomentose, pubescent or glandular hairy. Leaves 12–25 cm; petiole 4–6 cm; axis puberulent or pilose at first; leaflets 3–7(–9); petiolule 2–15 mm; leaflet blade broadly ovate to lanceolate, or elliptic to obovate‑lanceolate, 3– 10 × 2–4 cm, terminal one somewhat larger, base blunt or cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, papery to leathery, glabrous or villous, sometimes villous along midvein abaxially, margin regularly serrate; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal or lateral, 5–12 cm. Flowers dioecious, opening with leaves. Staminate flowers congested; calyx cupular, 1 mm; corolla absent; pistillate flowers lax; calyx tubular, 2–3 mm. Samara spatulate, 3–4 cm × 4–6 mm; wing decurrent to middle part of nutlet.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 481; F. W. Xing 9319; HK sheet 18390.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Vietnam, Korea.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Fraxinus griffithii C. B. Clarke 光蠟樹
Fl. Brit. India 3(9): 605. 1882; FHN 3: 217, fig. 669. 1974; FFJ 4: 363, fig. 294. 1989; FRPS 61: 10, pl. 3: 1 – 2. 1992; FOC 15: 274. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 132. 1998; FGD 5: 413, fig. 218. 2003.
Fraxinus formosana Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 30(1): 189 – 190. 1911.
Fraxinus guilingensis S. K. Lee & F. N. Wei, Guihaia 2(3): 130 – 131, fig. 3. 1982.

Tree 10–20 m tall, semi‑evergreen. Branchlets greyish, with raised lenticelles; winter buds naked, scurfy‑pubescent. Leaves 10–25 cm; petiole 3–8 cm; axis glabrous or puberulent; leaflets 5–7(–11); petiolule 3–8 mm, with slightly dilated joint at base; leaflet blade ovate to lanceolate, 4–12 × 1.5–5 cm, leathery or thinly leathery, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glandular dotted, slightly asymmetrical, apex acuminate, mucronulate, margin entire; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, obscure or convex abaxially. Panicles terminal, 10–25 cm, puberulent, spreading, many‑flowered; leafy bracts persistent, spatulate‑linear, 3–10 mm, puberulent at first. Flowers polygamous, opening after leaves. Peduncle 4–5 cm; pedicel slender, 2–4 mm. Calyx cupular, ca. 1 mm, puberulent or glabrous, shortly toothed. Corolla white; lobes navicular, ca. 2 mm. Stamens ca. equal to corolla lobes. Samara broadly lanceolate‑spatulate, 2–3 cm × 4–5 mm, surface nerviform; wing decurrent to about middle of nutlet.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Keung Shan, Tong Fuk, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 1285; F. W. Xing 7350; S. C. Ng 2214.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Fraxinus insularis Hemsl. 苦櫪木
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 86. 1889; FFJ 4: 367, fig. 299. 1989; FRPS 61: 20, pl. 5: 5 – 8. 1992; FOC 15: 276. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 132, pl. 49. 1998; FGD 5: 414. 2003.
Fraxinus taiwaniana Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 24: 210. 1934.
Fraxinus retusa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 330. 1852; FHK 214. 1861; FKH 166. 1912.
Fraxinus retusa var. calcicola C. Y. Wu ex P. Y. Bai, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 5(2): 178. 1983.
Fraxinus insularis var. henryana (Oliv.) Z. Wei, FRPS 61: 20, pl. 5: 4. 1992.

Deciduous tree, 20–30 m tall. Winter buds broadly obovate to conical, brown scaly or tomentose, becoming dark and shiny when dry. Leaves 10–25 cm or longer; petiole 3–8 cm; leaflets 3–5(–7); petiolule slender, (0.5–)1– 1.5 cm; leaflet blade ovate‑lanceolate, or elliptic‑lanceolate, 5–12 × 2–4 cm, thinly leathery, glabrous, base broadly cuneate or blunt, serrate or entire from below the middle, apex acuminate; lateral veins 7–11 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal or terminal and lateral, 20–30 cm, many‑flowered. Flowers polygamous, appearing after leaves. Pedicels slender, ca. 3 cm. Calyx cupular, ca. 1 × 1.5 mm; teeth truncate, upper chaffy. Corolla white; lobes spatulate, ca. 2 × 1 mm. Stamens longer than corolla; anther 1.5 mm, apex blunt; Style almost equal to stigma; stigma 2‑lobed. Samara long spatulate, 2–4 cm × 3–5 mm, red to brown; wing decurrent to upper part of nutlet.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wong Chuk Hang, Deep Water Bay, Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 656, 3061; Y. W. Lam 261.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of Fraxinus retusa was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley Woods between 1847 and 1850.

Fuirena ciliaris (L.) Roxb. 毛芙蘭草
Hort. Beng. 81. 1814, nom. nud.; Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 184. 1820; FRPS 11: 43. 1961; FHN 4: 279. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 281. 2000; FYN 15: 585. 2003; FGD 8: 286. 2007; FOC 23: 179. 2010.
Scirpus ciliaris L., Mant. Pl. 2: 182. 1771.
Fuirena glomerata Lam., Tabl. Encycl. 1: 150. 1791; FHK 396. 1861.

Annual. Rhizomes short. Culms tufted, 5–50 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, ciliate-pubescent above. Cauline leaves 5–7; blade linear, 5–15 cm × 3–8 mm, abruptly acute, margins pubescent or ciliate; sheath 1–3 cm, pubescent. Inflorescence with 1–3 clusters of spikelets; peduncles short, ciliate-pubescent. Spikelets ovoid or oblong-ellipsoidal, 4–7 × 3 mm, subacute, squarrose, greyish green. Glumes obovate to obovate-oblong elliptic, 1.5–1.7 × 1.25 mm, apex acute or obtuse, thinly membranous, shortly pubescent outside with pilose centre, awn ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Perianth segments 6; 3 outer ones needle-like, occasionally much reduced, scaberulose or smooth; 3 inner ones with a subquadrate blades, apex mucronate, base abruptly narrowed to a distinct stipe for ca. 0.3 mm long. Stamens 3; Anthers oblong, ca. 0.25 mm. Styles linear, stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid to ellipsoidal, 0.8–1 × 0.5–0.6 mm, brown, smooth to obscurely wrinkled.

Locality: Castle Peak, Sha Tin, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1467; Y. W. Lam 1218; HK sheet 39282.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei, Fujian, Jiangsu, Shandong, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropical Africa, Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia, Japan, Malesia and Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and other wet places.

Fuirena umbellata Rottb. 芙蘭草
Descr. Icon. Rar. Nov. Pl. 70, tb. 19, fig. 3. 1773; FHK 395. 1861; FKH 301. 1912; FRPS 11: 44. 1961; FHN 4: 278. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 282. 2000; FYN 15: 587. 2003; FGD 8: 285. 2007; FOC 23: 179. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizomes horizontally creeping. Culms solitary, erect, 30–100 cm tall, 6–9 mm thick, 5-angled, pubescent below inflorescence. Cauline leaves 5–7; blade lanceolate to linearlanceolate, 10–20 cm × 5–25 mm, apex acute, ciliate at base; sheath 2–5 cm, usually glabrous. Inflorescence with 3–12 clusters of spikelets; peduncles whitish villous. Spikelets ovoid or ovoidellipsoidal, ± squarrose, 4–10 × 2.5–3 mm, apex acute, brownish green or dark brownish green. Glumes obovate to ovate elliptic, 2–2.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, apex rounded, shortly pubescent, awn 0.8–1 mm, often pilose. Perianth segments 3, in 1 whorl only, obovate, all alike, obovate, membranous, truncate, subsessile, gradually narrowed at base. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, 0.5–0.7 mm. Styles linear, stigmas 3, equalling the style. Achenes obovoid to ellipsoidal, 0.8–1.2 × 0.6–0.7 mm, shiny, smooth to obscurely wrinkled.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 266, 289; Y. W. Lam 2107.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Moist grasslands, near rivers or in paddy fields.

Gahnia tristis Nees ex Hook. & Arn. 黑莎草
Bot. Beech. Voy 228, 1837 [Linnaea 9: 301. 1834, nom. nud.]; FHK 398. 1861; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 121. 1961; FHN 4: 303. 1977; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 588. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 283. 2000; FGD 8: 319. 2007; FOC 23: 258. 2010.

Perennial. Culms densely tufted, 50–100 cm tall, 2–5 cm thick, subterete to trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal and cauline; blade rigid, 40–120 cm × 3–12 mm, caudate-acuminate, leathery, margins strongly inrolled, cauline sheaths 7–15 cm, yellowish brown, basal sheaths up to 30 cm, dark or chestnut brown. Involucral bracts several, leaf-like, the lowest up to 30 cm; sheath up to 3 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, resembling a spike, ± cylindrical to linear-oblong, 15–50 × 3–7 cm with 10–28 ± sessile partial inflorescence each 1–5 × 1.2–1.7 mm. Spikelets many, densely clustered, oblong, becoming turbinate in achene, 7–10 mm, 6–8-glumed, 1-flowered. Glumes ovate-lanceolate, 10–12 mm, long-acuminate, sides papery, dark brown, upper 2–3 glumes broadly ovate, much shorter, ciliolate, obtuse to rounded. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 3; filaments slender, enveloped by glumes; anthers linear, 3–4 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal, trigonous, 4.5 × 2 mm, conical, dark brown to shiny black, smooth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 344; H. C. Tang 1931; HK sheet 8198.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Malaysia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Material (oil).

Gaillardia pulchella Foug. 天人菊
Mém. Acad. Sci. Paris 1786: 5, t. 1. 1788; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 265. 1966; FRPS 75: 390. 1979.

Annual herbs 20–60 cm tall, with ascending branches at upper half, pubescent. Lower leaves spatulate to oblanceolate, 5–10 × 1–2 cm, pinnatifid lobed, lobes obtuse to rounded, leaf base narrowed to stem, sessile, adaxial surfaces loosely pilose, abaxial surfaces densely hispid; upper leaves narrowly oblong, oblanceolate to spatulate, 3–10 cm, entire or loosely serrate or shallowly 3‑lobed, sessile or subamplexicaul. Capitula 2.5–6 cm across, terminal to branches and with long peduncles. Involucres with lanceolate phyllaries, foliaceous, acuminate at apex, ciliate along margin, densely pilose on abaxial side especially near the base, glandular. Marginal ligulate florets with ligule obovate to broad cuneate, and acutely 2–3‑toothed at apex, 1–2 × 1.5 cm, yellow at tip and purple at base, or yellow‑tipped and red‑based, hairy on tube. Central tubular florets yellow, red to dark purple, hairy, apex 5‑lobed, acuminate and caudate. Cypselae 2 mm, with long hair at base. Pappus scales stiff, ovate and long‑aristate, 5 mm, straw‑coloured.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7094, 13663 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to USA, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Another species Gaillardia aristata Pursh. was also recorded previously in cultivation (Check List HK Plants 96. 2004). Native to America, this perennial species differs in leaves being basal and cauline, ray florets yellow, and receptacular setae of 3–6 mm long.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: Another species Gaillardia aristata Pursh. was also recorded previously in cultivation (Check List HK Plants 96. 2004). Native to America, this perennial species differs in leaves being basal and cauline, ray florets yellow, and receptacular setae of 3–6 mm long.

records.text:
Galactia tenuiflora (Klein ex Willd.) Wight & Arn. 乳豆
Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 206. 1834; FRPS 41: 215. 1995; FGD 5: 308, fig. 164. 2003.
Glycine tenuiflora Klein ex Willd., Sp. Pl. 3: 1059. 1802.

Slender twining herb. Stipules lanceolate, small, caducous. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets rounded and emarginate at apex, with appressed hairs. Racemes axillary, slender. Flowers 4–8 mm. Calyx 6 mm, pubescent. Corolla purple to pale blue; petals auriculate; vexillum obovate, 10 × 7 mm; wings oblong, 9 × 2 mm; keel slightly longer than wings, apex obtuse. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary densely tomentose. Pods linear, flat, sparsely pubescent, 7 – 8-seeded. Seeds elliptic; hilum elliptic at center of seed.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Au Mun, Clear Water Bay, Po Toi Islands, Cheung Chau. Y. S. Lau 3333; P. S. Choi 366; Y. W. Lam 1051.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. –Sep.

Galinsoga parviflora Cav. 牛膝菊
Icon. 3(2): 41, pl. 281. 1795; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 267. 1966; FRPS 75: 384, pl. 66: 5–8. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 967. 1998.

Annual herbs 10–70 cm tall; stem branched especially near the bottom, subglabrous below, pilose and stipitate glandular in upper portion. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.3–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 1.8–4.8 × 0.4–3.4 cm, gradually smaller when growing upward, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute, both surfaces pilose, hair multicellular, denser along margin and veins, margin shallowly serrate or undulate‑serrate, sometimes entire. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, arranged as loose corymbs at terminal. Peduncles 1–2.5 cm, densely pilose and stipitate glandular. Involucres hemispherical, 3–4 mm across; phyllaries 1–2‑seriate; outer ones smaller, ovate, 2–2.5 × 1–1.2 mm, puberulent; inner ones ovate‑oblong, 3 × 2 mm, glabrous on abaxial surface; both membranous, ciliate along margin, and with obtuse apices. Receptacle conical, usually with phyllaries shed off upon fruiting stage. Paleae oblanceolate‑oblong, acute, about 3 × 1 mm, ciliate along margin especially at apical half. Marginal ligulate florets 5, female, white, 2.3–2.5 mm, ligule suborbicular with apex deeply 3‑lobed, lobes obtuse, corolla tube elongate and densely pilose. Disk tubular florets many, bisexual, yellow, 1–1.5 mm, densely pubescent on lower part, apex 5 deltoid lobes. Cypselae black or blackish brown, obovate‑oblong to obovate‑deltoid, 1.5–2 mm, 3‑ribbed or those developed from disk florets 4–5‑ribbed, pubescent. Pappus scarious, white, linear‑lanceolate, unequal in length with about 0.5–1.2 mm, apex aristate, margin fimbriate.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 3055; S. Y. Hu 9437; HK sheet 38970.
Distribution: Native to S America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Galium aparine L. var. echinospermum (Wallr.) Farw. 拉拉藤
Rep. Michigan Acad. Sci. 19: 260. 1917.
Galium aparine L. var. echinospermum (Wallr.) Cuf., Oesterr. Bot. Zeitschr. 89: 246. 1940; FRPS 71(2): 235, pl. 54: 5 – 8. 1999; FYN 15: 307, pl. 64: 8 – 11. 2003; FGD 6: 245, fig. 134. 2005; Check List HK Plants 262. 2002; 90. 2004.
Galium aparine auct. non L.: FHK 164. 1861; FKH 135. 1912.
Galium agreste Wallr. var. echinospermum Wallr., Sched. Crit. 59. 1822.

Annual herbs. Stems trailing or climbing, 30–90 cm or longer, with small, recurved prickles on the angles. Leaves sessile, (4–)6–8 in a whorl; leaf blade linear or linear‑lanceolate, 1–3(–5) × 0.2–0.7 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex mucronate, with small prickles on the margins and midveins of abaxial surface. Flowers small, greenish white, 3–8(–10) in loose cymes; peduncles axillary, usually longer than the subtending leaves; pedicels slender, to 10 mm in fruiting time. Calyx‑tube ovoid, covered with small prickles; limb truncate. Corolla rotate, 4‑lobed; lobes oblong, less than 1 mm. Fruit consisting of 1–2 subglobular segments, covered with hooked bristles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Fanling (Loi Tung). H. F. Hance s.n. (fide FHK 164. 1861); F. W. Xing 6790 (HKU).
Distribution: Widely spread almost all over China; Japan, Russia, Europe, Africa, N America, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Wastelands and grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Garcinia multiflora Champ. ex Benth. 多花山竹子
Hook. J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 310. 1851; FHK 25. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 94. 1990; FGD 3: 209. 1995; FHN 2: 54. 1965.

Shrub or tree, 3–12 m tall; bark grey-white. Petioles 0.5–4 cm; leaves leathery, obovate, oblong-obovate to oblanceolate, 5 –20 × 3 –10 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, acute or acuminate, margin slightly revolute; lateral veins 10–20 each side, oblique. Cymes rearranged in corymbs, terminal. Flowers orange, unisexual, rarely polygamous. Male flowers: sepals 4, orbicular, concave, outer ones 6 –7.5 mm, inner ones 8–10 mm; petals obovate-spathulate, 12–14 × 6–7 mm; stamens united into 4 bundles; anthers densely on top of bundles, globose. Female flowers: sepals and petals similar to those of male flowers; ovary 2-locular, without style; stigma peltate, persistent. Berries green-yellow, globose, ovoid or obovoid, 1.8 –3 cm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. L. T. Lo 98; Y. S. Lau 920; P. S. Choi 85.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Secondary forests on higher grounds. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Food (fruit).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from “the Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Food (fruit).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from “the Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Garcinia oblongifolia Champ. ex Benth. 嶺南山竹子（黃牙果）
Hook. J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 331. 1851; FHK 25. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 106. 1990; FHN 2: 55. 1965; FGD 3: 210. 1995.

Shrub or tree, 5–15 m tall. Petioles 0.5 –1.5 cm; leaves thinly leathery or papery, oblong, obovate-oblong, elliptic to oblanceolate, 4–14 × 1.5–4.3 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute rarely shortly acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins 10 –18 pairs, slender. Flowers unisexual, solitary or a few in fascicle, axillary or terminal. Male flowers: sepals 4, orbicular, 3– 4 mm; petals 4, obovateoblong, 7–9 mm; stamens many consolidated into a fleshy mass; pistillode absent. Female flowers: sepals and petals similar to male flowers; staminodes united into 4 bundles; ovary ovoid, without style; stigma peltate. Berries ovoid or subglobose, 2– 4 × 2–3.5 cm, with persistent calyx at base and stigma at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 23; W. J. Tutcher 10542; Y. S. Lau 2178.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Fung Shui Woods and lowland secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Materials (timber).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in the Happy Valley woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Materials (timber).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in the Happy Valley woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Gardenia jasminoides J. Ellis 梔子（水橫枝）
Philos. Trans. 51(2): 935, pl. 23. 1761; FHN 3: 325. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 259, pl. 112, photo 172. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 332, pl. 87: 1 – 5. 1999; FGD 6: 175, fig. 89. 2005.
Gardenia florida L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 305. 1762; FHK 153. 1861; FKH 131. 1912.

Evergreen, unarmed shrubs, 1–3 m tall, glabrous throughout, or young shoots pulverulent. Leaves opposite, or rarely in whorls of 3, subleathery; petioles 2–4 mm; stipules ca. 1 cm, united into a sheath, membranous, apex oblique; leaf blade elliptic, oblong‑elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate, 3–10 × 1–4.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Flowers terminal, solitary, sessile or nearly so. Calyx‑tube obconical, 8–20 mm, with 5 – 6 sharp ribs; limb usually 6‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, usually slightly longer than the tube. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric, 2.5–4 cm, green; limb 5–6 cm in diam., usually 6‑lobed; lobes white, obovate‑elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, 1.5–2.5(–4) × 0.6–2.8 cm. Anthers linear, 1.2–1.6 cm, exserted. Fruit ellipsoidal, 2.5–3 cm, crowned by the long linear‑lanceolate persistent calyx‑lobes, and marked outside by as many raised ribs or angles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1833; S. P. Lau 135; HK sheet 40130.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian,
Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Ravines and thickets on hills. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), material (dye).

Gardenia jasminoides var. fortuniana (Lindl.) H. Hara 白蟾
This variety differs in the double corolla.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China; native to China and Japan.
Ecology: Shrub. Flowering: Spring to summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gardneria multiflora Makino 蓬萊葛
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 15: 103. 1901; FRPS 61: 243, pl. 63(1 – 8). 1992; FGD 3: 311, fig. 201. 1995; FOC 15: 328. 1996.
Gardneria hongkongensis Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formos. 9: 75. 1920.
Gardneria chinensis Nakai, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 38: 45. 1924.

Lianas or scandent shrubs, to 8 m, glabrous. Branchlets terete, with prominent leaf scars. Petioles 1 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic to narrowly elliptic, sometimes ovate to very narrowly elliptic, 5 – 15 × 2 – 6 cm, papery to thinly leathery, base obtuse to rounded, apex acuminate, lateral veins 6 – 10 pairs. Cymes 3‑branched, 2 – 4 cm, many‑flowered; bracteoles 2 per flower. Flowers 5‑merous. Pedicels ca. 5 mm. Sepals nearly orbicular, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., ciliate. Corolla yellow to yellowish white; tube short; lobes narrowly to very narrowly elliptic, ca. 5 mm, thick, fleshy. Stamens inserted near base of corolla tube; filaments short; anthers oblong, ca. 2.5 mm, 4‑celled, free. Ovary with 1 ovule per locule. Berries red, globose, ca. 7 mm in diam. Seeds dark, orbicular.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Tam, Sai Wan, High Island Reservoir. P. S. Choi 432; Y. W. Lam 491; HK sheet 40324.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Dense forests, scrub. Flowering: Apr. – Aug.; fruiting: Dec. – Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Garnotia acutigluma (Steud.) Ohwi 三芒耳稃草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 55: 393. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 5: 429. 2000; FOC 22: 563. 2006; FGD 9: 363. 2009.
Urachne acutigluma Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 121. 1854.
Garnotia triseta Hitchc., Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 200. 1931; FRPS 10(1): 139. 1990; FFJ 6: 182. 1995; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.

Perennial, tufted herb. Culms glabrous, 20–60 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths longer than internodes, usually with a ring of stiff hairs along mouth and the membranous margins, otherwise glabrous; leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, flat or folded, 5–20(–35) × 0.2–0.7 cm, adaxial surface hispid or scabrid, hairs tubercle-based or not, abaxial surface usually glabrous; ligule membranous, 0.2–0.5 mm. Panicle narrow, branches appressed or loosely erect or ascending, slightly scabrous; spikelets in threes at lower nodes, paired or solitary toward apex. Spikelets narrow lanceolate, 3–5 mm, base usually conspicuously pilose, pedicels slightly scabrous; glumes narrow lanceolate, subequal, membranous, scabrid on veins, apex acute to awned; lemma lanceolate, as long as glume, papery, smooth, 1–3-veined, acuminate and awned; awn slender, slightly scabrous, slightly flexuous, 8–15 mm; palea elliptic, slightly shorter than lemma, membranous, margins ciliate, 2-veined; lodicules 2, small, cuneate, emarginate, smooth.

Locality: Hong Kong (fide FGD 9: 363. 2009).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread over India, Myanmar, Vietnam through Indonesia, Malay Peninsula to Indonesia and Philippines.
Ecology: Moist mountain slopes and shady places along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Garnotia patula (Munro) Benth. 耳稃草（葛氏草）
FHK 416. 1861; FKH 317. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 140. 1990; FFJ 6: 182, fig. 149. 1995; FOC 22: 563. 2006; FGD 9: 363, fig. 175. 2009.
Berghausia patula Munro, Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 362. 1860.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 60–130 cm tall, glabrous, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths keeled, longer than internode, glabrous or thinly pilose; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 15–60 × 0.4–1.2 cm, glabrous to sparsely pilose, sometimes with tubercle-based hairs, margins slightly scabrous; ligule membranous, 2–5 mm, ciliate. Panicle open, 15–40(–60) cm; branches stiff and very spreading, up to 12 cm. Spikelets narrow lanceolate, 4–4.5 mm, base shortly pubescent; glumes awned; awn of lower glume 2–8 mm; lemma as long as glume, glabrous, 3-veined, apex acuminate, awned; awn 7–15 mm, very slender.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Fo Tan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3094; Y. W. Lam 1240; HK sheet 42038.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; E Myanmar, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, moist grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 and 1856.

Garnotia patula (Munro) Benth. var. mutica (Munro) Rendle 無芒耳稃草
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 387. 1904; FOC 22: 563. 2006; FGD 9: 364. 2009.
Berghausia mutica Munro, Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 362. 1864.
Garnotia mutica (Munro) Druce, Bot. Exch. Club Soc. Brit. Isles 4: 624. 1917; FRPS 10(1): 136, pl. 42: 1–4. 1990; Check List HK Plants 336. 2002; 118. 2004.
Garnotia stricta auct. non Brongn.: FHK 416. 1861.

Culms 30–100 cm tall. Glumes acuminate or lower glume with a mucro; lemma acuminate, awnless or with a mucro to 1.5 mm.

Locality: No precise locality. C. Wright s.n. (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; E Myanmar, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of moist woodlands, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 and 1856.

Gastrochilus japonicus (Makino) Schltr. 黃松盆距蘭（港盆距蘭）
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. Beih. 12: 315. 1913, et l. c. 4: 288. 1919; FRPS 19: 407, pl. 60: 7. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 887, pl. 378. 2000; FGD 7: 475. 2006; FOC 25: 494. 2009.
Gastrochilus holttumianus S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 32. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 114. 1977.

Epiphytic monopodial herb; roots many, greyish green, 2 mm in diam.; stems very short. Leaves dull green, conduplicate in bud, articulate at base and slightly papillose at the joint; leaf blades elliptic, 4–6 × 1–1.2 cm, base oblique and twisted, apex acute, midrib canaliculate above, elevated beneath, margin strongly wavy. Flowers yellowish green; sepals and petals almost similar in colour, shape and size, equally spaced, forming a semicircle behind the column, the segments fleshy, rounded at apex, cuneate at base, 5 × 2–3 mm, petals slightly narrower; lip saccate, yellowish to white, very smooth inside, red at base and dotted red here and there along the margin, the front lobe rounded, 3 × 7 mm, notched at apex, margin slightly recurved, greenish white, the middle portion yellow with red dots; column very short, red, 1.5 × 5 mm, adnate to the lip by a short foot; anther dorso-ventrally compressed, the back globular, gradually attenuate at apex, yellow; pollinia 2, front view spherical, back view slightly flat with a depression at centre, supported by a slender transparent stipe; ovary and pedicel indistinct, glabrous, shallowly grooved.

Locality: Victoria Peak. S. Y. Hu 12349B (CUHK).
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Trunks in forests.
Notes: The holotype specimen of G. holttumianus (S. Y. Hu 12349B, K) was collected by H. Tai from Victoria Peak in 1962.

Geissaspis cristata Wight & Arn. 睫苞豆（雞冠苞覆花）
Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 218. 1834; FKH 77. 1912; FRPS 41: 357. 1995; FGD 5: 350, fig. 194. 2003.

Annual herb. Stems procumbent, 15–60 cm tall, many-branched from base, branchlets slender, striate. Stipules lanceolate, distinctly spurred. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 2 pairs, obcordate or obovate, oblique, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, base cuneate, apex truncate or slightly emarginate and spinulose, lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal or axillary, in compact heads, 1.5–1.6 cm. Bracts 6 – 12, imbricate, suborbicular or obliquely reniform, 7 – 10 × 15 mm, yellow bristly ciliate. Corolla purple, 2.4–3 mm; vexillum ovoid-rounded, 5 mm wide, shortly clawed; wings and keels smaller, ovate. Pods 1–2-segmented; segments reniform, 4 mm, compressed emarginate, reticulate. Seeds 1–2, brown, 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Mong Tsai, Sai Keng, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 800; L. T. Lo 333; F. W. Xing 8281.
Distribution: Guangdong; Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Gelsemium elegans (Gardner & Champ.) Benth. 鈎吻（胡蔓藤、斷腸草）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 1: 90. 1856; FHK 229. 1861; FKH 173. 1912; FRPS 61: 251, pl. 66: 1 – 4. 1992; FGD 3: 310, fig. 200. 1995; FOC 15: 329. 1996. Medicia elegans Gardner & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 325. 1849.

Climbers, to 12 m or longer. Petioles 6 – 12 mm; leaf blade ovate, narrowly ovate, or very narrowly ovate, 5 – 12 × 2–6 cm, membranous to papery, base broadly cuneate to nearly rounded, apex acuminate, lateral veins 5 – 7 pairs. Thyrses with main nodes each having 2 lateral cymes and a continuing main axis; bracts acutely triangular to awl‑shaped, to 4 mm, ciliate. Pedicels 3 – 8 mm. Corolla yellow to orange, 1.2–1.9 cm; tube 7–10 mm, outside brownish, mouth with reddish spots; lobes ovate, 5 – 9 mm, apex blunt to acute. Stamens inserted at middle of corolla tube; filaments 3.5–4 mm; anthers narrowly ovate, 1.5 – 2 mm, exserted. Ovary narrowly ovoid, 2 –2.5 mm; style 0.8–1.2 cm; stigma pubescent. Capsules ellipsoidal to ovoid, 10–14 × 6–8 mm, smooth, glabrous. Seeds elliptic to reniform, ca. 5.5 mm in diam., central part hairy, winged all around.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Ng Tung Chai, Ho Pui, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1524, 1700; HK sheet 33887.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Scrubby forests, thickets. Flowering: Jun. – Dec.; fruiting: Dec. – Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), very poisonous.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1849.

Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1849.

records.text:
Gentiana loureiroi Griseb. 華南龍膽
Prodr. 9: 108. 1845; FRPS 62: 254, pl. 38: 4 – 6. 1988; FFJ 4: 400, fig. 330. 1989; FOC 16: 97. 1995; FGD 4: 320, fig. 188. 2000.
Ericala loureiroi G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 192. 1837.

Perennial herb, 3–8 cm tall. Roots cylindric, fleshy, robust. Stems purple, erect, loosely caespitose, densely papillate. Basal leaves rosette; leaf blade narrowly elliptic, 1.5–3 × 0.3–0.5 cm; cauline leaves opposite; petiole 1–8 mm; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic‑lanceolate, 5 – 7 × 1 – 2.5 mm, apex acute, abaxially glabrous, adaxially densely minute papillate. Flowers solitary and terminal. Pedicel 0.5–1.2 cm. Calyx campanulate, 5–6 mm; lobes linear‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 2.5–4 mm. Corolla purple, funnelform, 1.2–1.7 cm; lobes ovate, 2–2.5 mm, margin entire, apex obtuse; plicae ovate‑orbicular, 1–1.5 mm, margin entire or denticulate, apex rounded. Stamens inserted at middle of corolla tube, equal; filaments ca. 5 mm; anthers 1.8–2.5 mm. Ovary ellipsoidal, 5 – 6 mm; style 1.5–2.5 mm; stigma lobes narrowly oblong. Capsules obovoid, 4.5–5.5 mm, winged; gynophore to 1.8 cm.

Locality: Shek Pai Wan, Wan Chai Gap, Tai Mo Shan, Fanling, Pat Sin Leng. L. T. Lo 56; P. S. Choi 197; K. L. Yip 4503.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Mar. – Jun.

Geodorum densiflorum (Lam.) Schltr. 地寶蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nor. Beih. 4: 259. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 96, fig. 54. 1977; FRPS 18: 187, pl. 31: 4–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 896, pl. 381. 2000; FGD 7: 390, fig. 197. 2006; FOC 25: 259. 2009.
Limodorum densiflorum Lam., Encycl. 3: 516. 1789.
Geodorum semicristatum Lindl., Fol. Orch. Geodorum 2. 1854; FKH 265. 1912.
Geodorum dilatatum auct. non (Roxb.) Aiton: FKH 265. 1912.

Terrestrial herb; roots cord-like, 3–4 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs subglobose and dorso-ventrally compressed-globose. Leaves 2–4, all basal; petioles sheathing, the sheaths closed; leaf blades plicate-venose, chartaceous, delicate green, elliptic or lanceolate, 20–30 × 4.5–7.5 cm, slightly wavy along the lower margin, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate. Flowers white, or light purplish pink, crowded, non-resupinate; sepals uniform in colour and similar in size and shape; the odd one oblong-elliptic, 10 × 3 mm, apex obtuse and mucronate; lateral sepals widespread, 18 mm between apices, oblong-elliptic, 12 × 3 mm; petals oblong, 10 mm between apices, 11–12 × 5 mm, apex obtuse; lip trowel-shaped, base saccate, adnate to the broad column foot, delicately fleshy, white within, margin slightly wavy or crisped, apex rounded or notched, disk papillose, yellow or orange along the upper middle portion, rugosely keeled; column white, short and very broad, 4 mm broad, 3 mm wide, extending to a broad triangular foot white or maculated maroon; anther semispherical; pollinia 2, waxy, globes in front and strongly sulcate at the back; ovary shiny green, glabrous, striate and sulcate.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Aberdeen, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 1026; Y. W. Lam 35; HK sheet 34724.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Taiwan; Philippines, tropical Asia.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides and grassy slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.

Geophila herbacea (Jacq.) K. Schum. 愛地草
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(4): 119. 1891; FHN 3: 359, fig. 771. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 261, pl. 113, photo 173. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 63, pl. 15: 5 – 9. 1999; FYN 15: 231, pl. 47: 5 – 7. 2003; FGD 6: 210, fig. 113. 2005.
Psychotria herbacea Jacq., Enum. Syst. Pl. 16. 1760.

Perennial creeping herbs, to 30 cm or longer. Stems and branches pubescent, rooting at nodes. Leaves membranous; petioles 1–5 cm, densely pubescent; stipules broadly ovate, 1–2 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, entire; leaf blade reniform or broadly ovate‑cordate, ca. 1–2(–3) cm in diam., base cordate, apex rounded or obtuse, subglabrous, palmately 5–8‑veined. Flowers solitary, or 2–3 in umbels; peduncles 1–4 cm, pubescent or glabrescent. Calyx‑tube 2–3 mm; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, ciliate. Corolla‑tube ca. 8 mm, hairy on both sides; lobes 4, ovate or ovate‑lanceolate. Drupe subglobose, 4–6 mm in diam., smooth, red when mature.

Locality: Tate's Cairn, Tai Om, Tai Po, Chuen Lung, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 453, 2053; K. Y. Tam 139.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical and subtropical areas.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests and other wet places. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Geophila repens (L.) I. M. Johnst. var. asiatica (Cham. & Schld.) Fosberg previously (Check List HK Plants 90. 2004).

Gerbera jamesonii Bolus 非洲菊（扶郎花）
Gard. Chron. 1: 772. fig. 122. 1889; et ex Hook. f., Bot. Mag. t. 7087. 1889; FRPS 79: 96. 1996; FGD 8: 247. 2007.

Perennial herbs. Scape 15–50 cm tall, without scaly leaves on it, tomentose, hair longer and denser upward. Leaves all radical, in rosette arrangement, elliptic to oblong, 8–25 × 5–10 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin coarsely dentate or irregularly pinnatilobed, upper surfaces pubescent, lower surfaces pubescent‑tomentose, or glabrescent when aged, midvein prominent, lateral veins 4–7 pairs; petiole 3–25 cm, striate, hairy. Capitula solitary, terminal to scape, 5–10 cm across at anthesis. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries in 3–4 rows, apex long‑acute; outer ones linear or subulate, 4–7 × 0.5–1 mm, densely pubescent‑tomentose; middle ones lanceolate, 8–12 × 1–2 mm, pubescent‑tomentose, margin scarious; inner ones lanceolate‑oblong, 12–14 × 2 mm, scarious, abaxial side loosely pubescent or glabrous. Receptacle flat, glabrous, alveolate. Marginal florets 2‑seriate, the outermost florets colour various, pale red, purple‑red, orange‑red, orange to yellow, corolla ligulate‑bilabiate, ligule elongate‑oblong with length 2.5–3.5 cm, width 2–4 mm, apex 2–3‑lobed, the opposite lip 6–10 mm, deeply cut into 2 filiform segments, lower tube 2–3 mm, about 1/8 of the ligule, staminodes linear, slightly exserted; style conspicuously exserted, minutely branched. Inner female florets shorter, outer lip 6–7 mm, 2–3‑toothed, inner lip 4–5 mm, deeply cleft into 2 linear segments, lower tube 3–4 mm; staminodes linear, stylar branches tiny. Central florets numerous, corolla bilabiate, total 8–9 mm, inner lip deeply 2‑cleft; anther bases caudate, apical appendages subtruncate‑oblong; style usually hidden in anther tube, branches short, less than 1 mm, apex obtuse. Cypselae cylindric‑fusiform, 4–5 mm, densely pubescent. Pappus 6–7 mm, greyish white, or orange‑brown after dried.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 428; H. Y. Yeung 101 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 6385 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Africa, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Winter to spring of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gerbera piloselloides (L.) Cass. 毛大丁草
Dict. Sci. Nat. 18: 461. 1820; FHK 191. 1861; FKH 149. 1912; FRPS 79: 94. 1996; FGD 8: 246. 2007.
Arnica piloselloides L., Pl. Rar. Afr. 22. 1760.
Piloselloides hirsuta (Forsk.) C. Jeffrey, Kew Bull. 21: 218. 1967.

Perennial herbs; stem scapose, 20–60 cm tall, usually without bract‑like leaves, or occasionally have one, densely tomentose, hair denser upward. Leaves radical and rosulate, obovate, obovate‑oblong or oblong, 5–15 × 1.8–6 cm, base attenuate or obtuse, apex rounded, margin entire and densely hairy, adaxial surfaces pubescent, or glabrescent when aged, abaxial side densely white arachnoid‑tomentose, midvein prominent on lower side, lateral veins 6–9 pairs; petioles 1–8.5 cm, densely tomentose. Capitula solitary to scape terminal, 2.5–4 cm across. Involucres tubular; phyllaries 2‑seriate, linear or linear‑lanceolate, apex acute, abaxial side densely brownish tomentose; outer ones 6–10 × 1–1.3 mm; inner ones 12–16 × 1.5–2 mm, margin scarious. Receptacle naked, alveolate. Marginal florets female, in 2 rows, outermost one with corolla ligulate‑bilabiate, 14–15 mm, outer lip ligule‑form, white adaxially, purple or purple‑pink abaxially, oblanceolate or spatulate‑oblong, 8–10 mm, apex faintly 3‑toothed; opposite lip 4–5 mm, deeply divided into 2 filiform segments; lower tube about 6 mm in length; style minutely branched. Inner female florets about 10 mm, outer lip nearly as long as inner lip, about 3 – 5 mm, outer lip minutely 3‑toothed, inner lip 2‑cleft; lower tube 5 mm; style shortly branched. Central florets bisexual, many, corolla 10–11.5 mm, outer lip and inner lip 2–2.5 mm, the outer one 3‑lobed, the inner one 2‑cleft; lower tube 8– 9 mm; anther bases caudate, apical appendages truncate; stylar branches short, about 1 mm, obtuse at apices. Cypselae fusiform, 6‑striate, 5–6 mm, pubescent, apex bearing glabrous beak 6 – 8 mm. Pappus capillary, 9– 10 mm, orange‑red or pale brown.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 2127; S. P. Lau 43; S. Y. Hu 11946 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Nepal, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gigantochloa atroviolacea Widjaja 黑毛巨竹
Reinwardtia 10(3): 323. 1987.
Gigantochloa nigrociliata auct. non (Buse) Kurz: HKB 62. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 197, pl. 50: 12 – 14. 1996; FOC 22: 47. 2006; FGD 9: 274. 2009; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.

Culms 8–15 m, 4–10 cm in diam.; internodes 36–46 cm, yellow striate, brown hispid; wall thick. Branches several, central ones prominent. Culm sheaths deciduous, brown, 18–22 cm, leathery, densely dark brown hispid; auricles minute; ligule ca. 4 mm, serrulate; blade recurved. Ultimate branches with ca. 11 leaves. Leaf sheath initially sparsely pubescent; ligule ca. 1 mm; blade 19–36 × 3–5 cm. Pseudospikelets in heads ca. 2.5 cm in diam. Spikelets 1–1.2 × 0.2–0.3 cm; florets 2. Glumes 2–3, ovate, dark brown ciliate; lemma margins dark brown ciliate; palea shorter than lemma. Anthers yellow. Ovary ovoid; style 6–7 mm; stigma 1. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: HKU campus, Tsiu Hang (cultivated). P. S. Choi 268; Nan-Zhu 2844.
Distribution: Indonesia.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gigantochloa verticillata (Willd.) Munro 花巨竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 123. 1868; FRPS 9(1): 200. 1996; FOC 22: 47. 2006; FGD 9: 275. 2009.
Bambusa verticillata Willd., Sp. Pl. 2: 245. 1799.
Arundo maxima Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 58. 1790, nom. illeg. hom.
Bambusa maxima (Lour.) Poir., Encycl., Suppl. 8: 704. 1808, nom. Illeg.
Bambusa pseudoarundinacea Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 330. 1854.
Gigantochloa maxima (Lour.) Kurz, Natuurk. Tijdschr. Ned.-Indië 27: 226. 1864, nom. illeg.; HKB 61. 1985.
Gigantochloa pseudoarundinacea (Steud.) Widjaja, Reinwardtia 10(3): 305. 1987; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.

Culms 8–15 m, 7–10 cm in diam.; internodes yellow striate, 28–42 cm, white or brown hispid; wall ca. 1.6 cm thick. Branches several, central dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, green, yellow striate initially, later brown, leathery, initially densely white hispid, margins ciliate; auricles minute, inconspicuous; oral setae absent; ligule ca. 3 mm, irregularly serrate or fimbriate; blade reflexed. Leaf sheath initially pubescent; ligule 5–10 mm, entire; blade 24–47 × 3.5–7 cm. Inflorescence unknown.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 270; Nan-Zhu 2868.
Distribution: S Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer to early autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ginkgo biloba L. 銀杏
Mant. Pl. 2: 313. 1771; FRPS 7: 18. 1978; FOC 4: 8. 1999; FGD 4: 6, fig. 3. 2000.

Tree, deciduous, up to 40 m high and 4 m in d.b.h.; bark greyish brown, fissured and rough; branches nearly verticillate, ascending; long branches pale brownish yellow to grey; brachyblasts densely covered by leaf scar, grey. Leaves spirally arranged on 1st year branches, and 3–8 in clusters on brachyblasts, pale green, turning yellow before fallen off in autumn, fan-shaped, 5–8 cm wide at apex, notched or bilobed, base broadly cuneate, glabrous, with many dichotomous veins; petiole 3–10 cm. Pollen cones pedunculate, catkinlike, pendulous, microsporophylls with short stipe. Seed ellipsoid or ovoid, 2.5–3.5 × 2 cm, yellow or orange when mature, glaucous.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. P. S. Choi 417, 472.
Distribution: Zhejiang (Tianmushan). Widely cultivated in China and E Asia, Europe and America.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: Aug.–Oct. Uses: Ornamental, medicinal, food (seeds).

Gironniera subaequalis Planch. 白顏樹
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 3, 10: 229. 1848; FHN 2: 371. 1965; FGD2: 227. 1991; FOC 5: 11. 2002.
Gironniera chinensis Benth., FHK 321. 1861; FKH 243. 1912.

Tree, 10 –20(–30) m tall; bark grey or dark grey. Branchlets yellow-green, sparsely yellow-brown hirsute. Stipules paired, lanceolate, 1–2.5 cm, enclosing bud. Leaves leathery, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 10 –25 × 5–10 cm, base rounded or broad-cuneate, apex shortly caudate, margin subentire or sparsely and obtusely serrate at upper most, glabrous adaxially, scabrous on nerves abaxially; lateral veins 8 –12 pairs. Cymes paired, axillary; male cymes many branched, female racemose. Male flowers: sepals 5, broad-elliptic, margin membranaceous. Drupes yellow, elliptic, 4 –5 cm in diam., hirsute when young, with persistent sepals and styles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Wai, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Sheung Wo Hang, Bride's Pool. H. C. Tang 1921; Y. W. Lam 606.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore).

Gladiolus × gandavensis Van Houtte 唐菖蒲（劍蘭）
Fl. Serres Jard. Eur. pl. 1. 1846; FGZ 706, fig. 370. 1956; FRPS 16(1): 124, pl. 39: 7–8. 1985; FGD 6: 386, fig. 231. 2005.

Perennial herb; bulbs compressed globose, 2.5–4.5 cm in diam., with brown or yellowish brown membranes. Leaves basal or alternate at the basal part of scapes, sword-shaped, 40–60 × 2–4 cm, base sheathing, apex acuminate, greyish green. Scapes erect, 50–80 cm, unbranched, with several basal leaves. Spikes terminal, 25–35 cm, bracts usually 2 below each flower, membranous, yellowish green, ovate or broadly lanceolate, 4–5 × 1.8–3 cm, midveins conspicuous. Flowers solitary in each bract, red, yellow or pink, etc., 6–8 cm in diam.; tube ca. 2.5 cm, curved at base; perianth segments ovate or elliptic, unequal, upper 3 (2 in outer whorl, 1 in inner whorl) slightly larger, the upper one of inner whorl much broader and larger, helmet-shaped; stamens 3, erect, adnate to the helmet-like inner segment, ca. 5.5 cm, anthers linear, reddish purple or dark purple, filaments white. Ovary ellipsoidal, green, style ca. 6 cm, apex 3-lobed, stigmas slightly enlarged, flat, tomentose.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 12.
Distribution: Widely cultivated all over the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec. Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species is a hybrid. Perhaps G. psittacinus Hook. and G. cardinalis Curtis are its parents. It is widely cultivated as a cutting-flower.

Glechoma longituba (Nakai) Kuprian. 活血丹
Bot. Zhurn. (Moscow & Leningrad) 33(2): 236, fig. 1(4), 2. 1948; FRPS 65(2): 316, pl. 61: 1 – 3. 1977; FOC 17: 118. 1994; FGD 3: 410. 1995.
Glechoma hederacea L. var. longituba Nakai, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 35(418): 173 – 174. 1921.
Glechoma brevituba Kupr., Bot. Zhurn. (Moscow & Leningrad) 33(2): 236. 1948

Perennial herbs, 10–30 cm tall; stems ascending, often purplish red at base, young parts sparsely villous. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 times as long as blade; leaf blade upper leaves cordate, 1.8–2.6 × 2–3 cm, apex acute to obtuse, margin coarsely crenate or serrate‑crenate, adaxially sparsely strigose or puberulent, abaxially purplish, veins pilose or hirsute. Verticillasters usually 2‑flowered, rarely 4–6‑flowered; bracts and bracteoles linear, to 4 mm, ciliate. Calyx tubular, 0.9–1.1 cm, villous especially on veins; teeth ovate‑triangular, 3–5 mm, apex awned, ciliate, adaxial ones longer. Corolla blue to purple with dark spots on lower lip, long‑tubed corolla 1.7–2.2 cm, short‑tubed corolla 1–1.4 cm, ± pilose or puberulent abaxially; upper lip straight, 2‑lobed, lobes subreniform; lower lip elongate, obliquely spreading, middle lobe reniform, 2–3 times as long as upper lip, apex emarginate; lateral lobes oblong, ca. 1/2 as long as middle lobe. Nutlets ca. 1.5 × 1 mm, basally ± triquetrous, apex rounded.

Locality: Lai Chi Chong, Kop Tong. W. J. Tutcher 11721; HK sheet 34038.
Distribution: Spread over all provinces except Gansu, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Xizang; far E of Russia, Korea.
Ecology: Thin forests, streamsides, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gleditsia australis Hemsl. 小果皂莢
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 23: 208, t. 5. 1887; FKH 89. 1912; FRPS 39: 83, pl. 28: 5–8. 1988; FGD 5: 166. 2003; FGX 2: 446, pl. 183: 4–7. 2005.
Gleditsia microcarpa F. P. Metcalf, Lingnan Sci. J. 19(4): 552, fig. 3. 1940; FHN 2: 224. 1965.

Tree, 3 –20 m tall. Branches greyish brown, armed with stout (3 – 5 cm), purplish brown, branched thorns. Leaves bipinnate or sometimes pinnate, 10– 18 cm; pinnae 2 – 6 pairs; petiolules 0.5 – 1 mm; leaflets 5 – 9 pairs, papery or thinly leathery, oblique elliptic or rhomboid-oblong, 2.5–5 × 1–2 cm, base oblique, cuneate, apex obtuse and emarginate, margin obtusely dentate or entire, slightly pubescent along veins adaxially, glabrous abaxially; reticulate veins sparse, inconspicuous. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, to 28 cm. Male inflorescences many-flowered; bisexual inflorescences few-flowered. Flowers polygamous, pale green or greenish white. Pedicels 1–2.5 mm. Male flowers: 4 – 5 mm in diam.; calyx lobes lanceolate, as long as hypanthium, densely puberulous abaxially; petals elliptic, ca. 2 mm, densely pubescent on both surfaces. Bisexual flowers: 7 – 9 mm; hypanthium ca. 2 mm, glabrous, lobes 5–6, lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, puberulous abaxially, densely pale brown villous adaxially; petals 5 – 6, elliptic, pubescent abaxially, densely villous adaxially; stamens 5, included; ovary sessile, densely pale brown silky hairy. Pods linear-ellipsoidal, 8 – 12 × 1– 2.5 cm, straight or curved, brownish black. Seeds 5–12, elliptic or oblong, 7–11 × 4 – 5 mm, blackish brown.

Locality: Tai Hang, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Wai, Tai Po. S. P. Wong 9123; H. C. Tang 1005; Y. S. Lau 320.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests in valleys, sunny slopes. Flowering: Jun. – Oct.; fruiting: Nov. –Apr.
Notes: Two syntypes of this species, Ford s.n. and Hance 18780 (K, BM), were collected from Hong Kong. The species was reported as Gleditsia macracantha Desf. previously (Check List HK Plants 31. 1993, p.p.).

Gleditsia fera (Lour.) Merr. 華皂莢
Philipp. J. Sci. 13(3): 141. 1918; FGZ 319, fig. 173, 1956, excl. syn. G. australis; FHN 2: 223, fig. 417. 1965, excl. syn. G. australis; FRPS 39: 83, pl. 28: 1 – 4. 1988; FGD 5: 166. 2003; FGX 2: 446, pl. 183: 1– 3. 2005.
Gleditsia formosana Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 30(1): 85. 1911.
Gleditsia macracantha auct. non Desf.: FKH 89. 1912.
Gleditsia sinensis auct. non Lam.: FHK 100. 1861.
Mimosa fera Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 652. 1790.

Tree, 3– 42 m tall. Branches greyish brown, armed with stout (to 13 cm), branched thorns. Leaves pinnate, 11 – 18 cm, rachis furrowed, glabrous or pilose; petioles not swollen at base; petiolules ca. 1 mm; leaflets 5–9 pairs, papery to subleathery, oblique elliptic or rhomboid-oblong, 2 – 7(–12) × 1 – 3(–5) cm, base oblique cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse and emarginate, margin crenate or shallowly dentate, glabrous or sometimes pubescent along veins, dark brown and shining adaxially; reticulate veins dense, prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescences racemose, axillary or terminal, 7–16 cm. Flowers polygamous, pedicellate, greenish white. Male flowers: 6–7 mm in diam.; hypanthium ca. 2.5 mm; calyx-lobes triangular-lanceolate, 2.5 – 3 mm, densely pubescent abaxially; petals oblong, pubescent on both surfaces; stamens 10; staminodes linear, 4 – 5 mm, villose. Bisexual flowers: 8–10 mm in diam.; calyx, petals as male flowers except calyx-lobes with a ring of villose at base adaxially; stamens 5 – 6, anthers 5 – 6, ovate-triangular, apex sharp; ovary densely covered with brownish yellow silky hairs, with many ovules. Pods flat, 13.5–26 × 2.5–3 cm, straight or slightly curved, densely brownish yellow pubescent at first, later glabrescent, blackish brown, with a 5 – 10 mm fruit neck. Seeds many, ovate to oblong, flat or slightly raised on both surfaces, 8 – 11 × 5–6 mm, brown to brownish black, glossy.

Locality: Causeway Bay, Tai Po, Shek Kong, Lantau Island. Wild or cultivated. K. Y. Chan 177; F. W. Xing 8595; HK sheet 38806.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun.– Dec.
Uses: Fruit used as substitute of soap.

Glehnia littoralis F. Schmidt ex Miq. 珊瑚菜
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 3: 61. 1867; FGD 2: 345, fig. 234. 1991; FRPS 55(3): 77. 1992; FOC 14: 173. 2005.
Phellopterus littoralis Benth., Gen. Pl. 1: 905. 1867; FKH 117. 1912.

Perennial herb, 5–20 cm tall, densely white-pubescent except leaf blade; roots slender, to 40 cm long, fleshy; stems short, usually simple, 5–30 cm, often buried in sand with apical part emerged above ground. Petioles 5–15 cm, sheathed; leaf blade usually deltoid or ovate deltoid in outline, 10–20 cm, once or twice ternate; leaflets rather thick, elliptic, obovate-elliptic or ovate-orbicular, 2–5 × 1–3 cm, apex obtuse to rounded, often partly tinged with red, often glabrous except on the veins, margin irregularly denticulate. Umbels 3–6 cm across; peduncles 2–6 cm; rays more than 10, 4–6 cm; bracteoles linear, not exceeding the flowers. Calyx-teeth 0.5–1 mm. Styles 1.5–2 mm. Fruit ovoid-oblong, 0.5–1.3 × 0.3–0.9 cm, villose, ribs all equally winged, thick.

Locality: Ham Tin Wan, Tai Wan. Y. W. Lam 1420; HK sheet 39280, 40314.
Distribution: Coastal areas of Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hebei, Liaoning; Japan, Korea, Russia.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Glochidion eriocarpum Champ. & Benth. 毛果算盤子（毛漆、漆大姑）

Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 6. 1854; FHK 314. 1861; FKH 235. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 150, pl. 40: 1 – 5. 1994; FGD 5: 58. 2003.

Phyllanthus eriocarpus (Champ. & Benth.) Müll. Arg., Linnaea 32: 67. 1863.


Shrub or treelet to 5 m tall; branchlets densely hirsute with short spreading often reddish hairs. Leaves papery; stipules subulate, 3– 4 mm; petioles 1– 2 mm, villose; leaf blade broadly ovate to narrowly ovate, 4 – 8 × 1.5 – 3.5 cm, base obtuse, truncate or rounded, aequilateral, apex acuminate or acute, winkled and hirsute on both surface; lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Flowers solitary or in axillary clusters of 2–4. Male flowers: inserted at lower part of branchlets; pedicels 4 – 6 mm; sepals 6, oblong-obovate, 2.5 – 4 mm, apex acute, sparsely pubescent abaxially; stamens 3, connate. Female flowers: inserted at upper part of branchlets, subsessile; sepals 6, oblong, 2.5 – 3 mm, villose on both surfaces; ovary depressed globose, densely pubescent, 4–5-locular, style-column cylindric, erect, ca. 1.5 mm, 4–5-lobed. Capsules depressed globose, 8 – 10 mm in diam., densely yellowish- or grey-villose, 4–5-sulcate, with a cylindrical, persistent style-column.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2220; Y. S. Lau 74; HK sheet 39974; S. Y. Hu 7159 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand.

Ecology: Ravines, shrublands, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley woods, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Glochidion hirsutum (Roxb.) Voigt 厚葉算盤子
Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 153. 1845; FRPS 44(1): 141, pl. 42: 1 – 4. 1994; FGD 5: 57. 2003.
Bradleja hirsuta Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 699. 1832.
Glochidion dasyphyllum K. Koch, Hort. Dendrol. 85: 3. 1853.
Glochidion molle Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 210. 1837, nom. illeg.; FHK 314. 1861.
Glochidion arnottianum Müll. Arg., Linnaea 32: 60. 1863; FKH 235. 1912.

Shrub or treelet, 1 – 8 m tall; branchlets densely villose. Leaves leathery; stipules lanceolate, 3 – 4 mm; petioles 5 – 7 mm; leaf blade ovate, oblong-ovate or oblong, 7 – 15 × 4 – 7 cm, base shallowly cordate, truncate or rounded, obliquely inaequilateral, apex obtuse or acute, adaxially pubescent, glabrous in age, abaxially, densely pubescent; lateral veins 6 – 10 pairs. Cymules usually supra-axillary, pedunculate, but sometimes sessile and axillary; peduncles 5 – 7 mm, pubescent; sepals 6, biseriate, pubescent abaxially. Male flowers: pedicels 6 – 10 mm; sepals oblong or obovate; stamens 5 – 8. Female flowers: pedicels 2 – 3 mm; sepals ovate or broadly ovate, ca. 2.5 mm; ovary globose, ca. 2 mm in diam., pubescent, 5–6-locular, styles forming a short subconical column, truncate at apex. Capsules depressed globose, 8 – 12 mm in diam., pubescent, 5 – 6-sulcate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 9472; L. T. Lo 92; Y. W. Lam 640.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Guangxi,Yunnan, Xizang; India.
Ecology: Thin forests, stream banks, shrublands. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Glochidion lanceolarium (Roxb.) Voigt 艾膠算盤子（大葉算盤子）
Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 153. 1845; FRPS 44(1): 144, pl. 42: 5 – 8. 1994; FGD 5: 58. 2003.
Bradleja lanceolaria Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 697. 1832.
Glochidion macrophyllum Benth., London J. Bot. 1: 491. 1842; FHK 315. 1861; FKH 235. 1912.
Glochidion cantoniense Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 5, 5(5): 241. 1866.

Evergreen shrub or tree, usually 1 – 3 m, rarely 7 – 12 m tall; throughout glabrous except for the hairy ovary and capsules. Leaves leathery; stipules triangular-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm. petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 6–16 × 2.5–6 cm, base acute or broadly cuneate, slightly decurved, subaequilateral, dark-green adaxially, yellowish-green when dry; lateral veins 5 – 7 pairs. Flowers in axillary clusters. Male flowers: pedicels 8 – 10 mm; sepals 6, obovate or obovate-oblong, ca. 3 mm, yellow; stamens 5–6. Female flowers: pedicels 2–4 mm, biseriate, inner ones narrowly ovate, 2.5–3 mm, outer ones slightly larger, ovate; ovary globose, 6– 8-locular, densely pubescent; styles connate, less than 1 mm, subtruncate at apex. Capsules subglobose, 12 – 18 × 7 – 10 mm, apex usually concave, puberulous to glabrous, 6 – 8-sulcate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 251, 489; L. H. Li 34.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Guangxi,Yunnan; Cambodia, India, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, shrublands. Flowering: Apr. – Sep.; fruiting: Jul. of the following year.

Glochidion philippicum (Cav.) C. B. Rob. 菲島算盤子（甜葉算盤子）

Philipp. J. Sci. 4(1): 103. 1909; FRPS 4(1): 154, pl. 4: 6 – 10. 1994; FGD 5: 60. 2003.

Bradleja philippica Cav., Icon. 3: 48, pl. 371. 1797.

Glochidion philippinense (Cav.) Benth., FHK 314. 1861; FKH 235. 1912.


Tree, 5–12 m tall; branchlets pubescent when young, glabrescent. Leaves papery or sub-leathery; stipules ovate-triangular, 1–1.5 mm; petioles 4– 6 mm; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate or oblong, 5 – 15 × 2.5 – 5.5 cm, base acute or broadly cuneate, usually oblique, apex acuminate to obtuse, dark green and shining adaxially, paler abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Flowers in axillary clusters, 4–10-flowered per cluster. Male flowers: pedicels 6–7 mm; sepals 6, oblong or obovate-oblong, 1.5–2.5 mm, glabrous, yellowish-green; stamens 3. Female flowers: pedicels 2 – 4 mm; sepals 6, as in male flowers; ovary globose, pubescent, 5 – 6-locular, styles thick, connivent in a short almost globular mass. Capsules depressed globose, 4.5 – 5.5 × 8 – 12 mm, very much impressed in the centre, deeply 10 – 14-sulcate, pubescent.


Locality: Bowen Rd., Aberdeen, Wong Chuk Hang, Sai Kung, Tai Long, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1714; K. Y. Tam 129; H. C. Tang 105 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines.

Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar. –Aug.; fruiting: Jul. – Dec.

Glochidion puberum (L.) Hutch. 算盤子
Pl.Wilson. 2: 518. 1916; FRPS 44(1): 151, pl. 44: 5 – 9, 45: 1 – 9. 1994; FGD 5: 59. 2003.
Agyneia pubera L., Mant. Pl. 2: 296. 1771.
Bradleja sinica Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 127, pl. 109: 1. 1791.
Glochidion sinicum (Gaertn.) Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 210. 1836; FHK 314. 1861.
Glochidion fortunei Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 228. 1862; FKH 235. 1912; FGD 5: 61. 2003.

Erect shrub, 1–5 m tall, much branched; branchlets densely pubescent. Leaves papery or sub-leathery; stipules triangular, ca. 1 mm; petioles 1 – 3 mm; leaf blade oblong, oblong-ovate or obovate-oblong, rarely lanceolate, 3 – 8 × 1 – 2.5 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex obtuse, acute, short-acuminate or rounded, glaucous and glabrous adaxially except on the midvein, pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 4 – 8 pairs, raised abaxially, reticulation of veins prominent. Flowers small, in axillary clusters of 2–5. Male flowers: pedicels 4–15 mm; sepals 6, narrowly oblong or oblong-obovate, 2.5 – 3.5 mm, spreading green to yellowish, densely pubescent abaxially; stamens 3, connate into a cylindrical column. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 1 mm; sepals 6, as in male flowers but shorter and thicker, green; ovary globose, densely pubescent, 5–10-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles forming a short thick annular. Capsules depressed globose, 8 – 15 mm in diam., 8 – 10-sulcate, densely pubescent, reddish when mature.

Locality: Aberdeen, Barker Rd., Shek O Rd., Cape D'Aguilar, D’Aguilar Peak, Fanling, Sai Kung, Tai Mei Tuk, Chuen Lung. Y. S. Lau 2186, 2394; Y. W. Lam 771; S. Y. Hu 5820 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Montane slopes, stream banks shrublands or margins of forests. Flowering: Apr. –Aug.; fruiting: Jul. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Glochidion triandrum (Blanco) C. B. Rob. 裏白算盤子
Philip. J. Sci. 4(1): 92. 1909; FRPS 44(1): 146, pl. 44: 1 – 4. 1994; FGD 5: 59. 2003.
Kirganelia triandra Blanco, Fl. Filip. 1: 711. 1837.

Shrub or treelet, 3–7 m tall; branchlets angulate, tawny pubescent. Leaves papery; stipules ovate-triangular, 1–1.5 mm, pubescent; petioles 2–4 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade oblong-elliptic or lanceolate, 4–13 × 2–4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, slightly inaequilateral, apex acuminate, acute or obtuse, adaxial surface sparsely pubescent when young, glabrous in age, abaxial surface glaucous, pubescent; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Flowers in axillary clusters of 5–6-flowered. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 6–7 mm; bracteoles ovate-triangular, ca. 1 mm; sepals 6, biseriate, obovate, ca. 2 mm, pubescent; stamens 3, connate. Female flowers: subsessile; sepals as in male flowers, ca. 1.5 mm, concave inside; ovary ovoid, pubescent, 4–5-locular, styles forming a column, dilated at apex. Capsules depressed globose, ca. 4 × 5–10 mm, sparsely pubescent, 8–10-sulcate; fruiting pedicels 5–6 mm; seeds triangular, ca. 3 mm, brownish red.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai. P. S. Choi 484, 485, 535.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Nepal, Sikkim, Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests, valley woods, stream banks. Flowering: Mar. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul. – Dec.

Glochidion wrightii Benth. 白背算盤子
FHK 313. 1861; FKH 235. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 158, pl. 39: 1 – 4. 1994; FGD 5: 60, fig. 34. 2003.

Shrub or treelet 1 – 8 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves papery; petioles 3 – 5 mm; leaf blade oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 2.5– 5.5 × 1.5 –2.5 cm, base acute, very oblique, apex acuminate, often obliquely falcate, green adaxially, glaucous abaxially; lateral veins 3 – 6 pairs. Flowers androgynous, in axillary clusters. Male flowers: pedicels 2 – 4 mm; sepals 6, oblong, ca. 2 mm, yellowish; stamens 3, connate. Female flowers: subsessile; sepals 6, biseriate, ovate, elliptic or oblong, ca. 1 mm, the inner ones smaller; ovary globose, 3 – 4-locular, styles erect, oblong and connivent, less than 1 mm. Capsules subglobose, 6 – 8 mm in diam., very depressed in the centre.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2361; Y. S. Lau 3101; L. T. Lo 110; S. Y. Hu 6420, 13239 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan.
Ecology: Thin forests, shrublands. Flowering: May– Sep.; fruiting: Jul. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island around 1854.

Glochidion zeylanicum (Gaertn.) A. Juss. 香港算盤子
Euphorb. Gen. 107. 1824; FRPS 44(1): 145, pl. 42: 9 – 12. 1994.
Bradleia zeylanica Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 128. 1791.
Glochidion hongkongense Müll. Arg., Linnaea 32: 60. 1863; FKH 235. 1912.
Glochidion littorale auct. non Blume: FHK 314. 1861.

Shrub or treelet 1 – 6 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves leathery; stipules triangular, persistent; petioles 5–8 mm; leaf blade oblong, ovate-oblong or ovate, sometimes oblong-elliptic, 6–18 × 4–8 cm, base cordate, subcordate, truncate or rounded, slightly oblique; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Flowers in axillary clusters or forming supra-axillary, pedunculate, short cymules, usually female flowers inserted at upper part of branchlets, male flowers inserted at lower part of branchlets. Male flowers: pedicels 6–9 mm; sepals 6, biseriate, ovate or broadly ovate, spreading, yellowish-green; stamens 5–6, connate into a column. Female flowers: sepals as in male flowers; ovary globose, 5–6-locular, styles very short, connate into very short column. Capsules depressed globose. 8–10 × 5 mm, 8–12-sulcate; seeds hemispheroid, red.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1964; Y. S. Lau 864; P. S. Choi 335; S. Y. Hu 6400 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Japan, Indonesia.
Ecology: Ravines, stream branks shrublands. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes : The type specimen of Glochidion hongkongense was collected by H. F. Hance from Victoria Peak between 1844 and 1850.

Glossocardia bidens (Retz.) Veldkamp 鹿角草
Blumea 35(2): 468. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 971, pl. 461, photo 455. 1998.
Zinnia bidens Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 28. 1788.
Glossogyne tenuifolia (Labill.) Cass. ex Less., Syn. Gen. Compos. 212. 1832; Benth., FHK 184. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 271. 1966; FRPS 75: 381, pl. 66: 1 – 4. 1979; FGD 8: 137, fig. 72. 2007.

Perennial herbs 15–30 cm tall; stem branched mainly at base, glabrous. Radical leaves many and persistent, pinnatisect with 2–3 pairs of lateral segments, without clear distinction of lamina and petiole, totally 3.5–9 cm long, the apical divided portion 1.5–2.5 cm, the basal undivided petiole‑like portion 2–6.5 cm, lateral segments linear, the lowest ones longer, 5–20 × 1–2 mm, all apex rounded to obtuse, mucronate, both surfaces glabrous; cauline leaves few, usually linear, some pinnatisect. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 5–8 mm across, solitary and terminating branches, base bearing one linear prophyll (ca. 2 mm). Involucres campanulate‑hemispherical; phyllaries in 2 series, lanceolate‑oblong, 2–3.5 mm with the inner layers longer, apex obtuse, margin scarious and ciliate. Receptacle flat. Paleae linear with hyaline and shallowly dentate margin, those subtending inner disk florets with broad bases. Ray florets 8–9 in one row, female, corolla yellow, about 4 mm, ligule elliptic‑oblong, 2.5–3 × 2.5 mm, spreading, apex 3‑dentate. Disk tubular florets bisexual, corolla yellow, 2.8–3 mm, basal 1/3 narrowed, apical 2/3 campanulate, apex 4‑lobed. Cypselae black, linear, 5–6 × 0.8–1 mm, flat, ribbed, glabrous. Pappus 2 stiff awns, 1–1.5 mm, pale brown, retrorsely barbed.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap, Tai Tam, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Po Toi Islands. L. T. Lo 144, 502; Y. W. Lam 1040.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Philippines, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy slopes and rocky places near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Glycine max (L.) Merr. 大豆
Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 274. 1919; FRPS 41: 234. 1995; FGD 5: 313. 2003.
Phaseolus max L., Sp. Pl. 725. 1753.

Annual herb, 30 – 90 cm tall. Stems erect, densely brown hirsute. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets rhomboid-ovate or broadly ovate, 7–13 × 3–7 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, lateral ones smaller, usually sparsely hirsute on both surfaces or only on abaxial surface. Racemes axillary, 1 – 3.5 cm, 5 – 8-flowered. Calyx campanulate, 4 – 6 mm, brown hirsute, 5-toothed.
