Corolla purplish or white, 6 – 8 mm; petals clawed; vexillum obovate, emarginate, reflexed; wings and keel auriculate, shorter than vexillum. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary hairy. Pods oblong, 4 – 7.5 × 0.8– 1.5 cm, slightly curved, densely yellow-brown hirsute. Seeds 2–5, greenish, yellow, elliptic, ovate to subglobular, 6 – 10 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 617, 624; Y. S. Lau 3103.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Food (seeds).

Glycosmis citrifolia (Willd.) Lindl. 小花山小橘（山小橘）
Trans. Hort. Soc. 6: 772. 1826; FTW 3: 517, pl. 709; 1977; FTW ed. 2, 3: 519, pl. 269. 1993.
Glycosmis parviflora (Sims) Kurz, J. Bot. n.s. 5: 40. 1876; FRPS 43(2): 124, pl. 29: 1. 1997.
Limonia citrifolia Willd., Enum. Pl. Hort. Berol. 448. 1809.
Limonia parviflora Sims, Bot. Mag. t. 2416. 1823.
Glycosmis erythrocarpa (Hayata) Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form. 8: 14. 1919.
Citrus erythrocarpa Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form. 6: 13. 1916.
Glycosmis pentaphylla auct. non Corrêa: FKH 56. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3 m tall. Leaves 2–4(–5)-foliolate, rarely unifoliolate; petiolule 1–5 mm; leaflet blade elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, sometimes obovate-elliptic, 5–19 × 2.5–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, sometimes obtuse, glabrous, margin irregularly wavy when dry; midvein flat or slightly raised, or slightly impressed at lower half adaxially. Thyrse terminal, 3–5(–14) cm; rachis, pedicels and calyx lobes often covered with deciduous brown rusty hairs. Calyx lobes ovate, apex obtuse, ca. 1 mm wide. Petals white, long elliptic, ca. 4 mm. Stamens 10, rarely 8, filaments slightly unequal, wider at upper part, anthers with 1 apical gland. Ovary broadly ovoid to globose, glands not prominent. Fruit globose or ellipsoidal, 1–1.5 cm in diam., pale yellowish white, turning to pale red or dark red, translucent, conspicuously glandular-dotted, (1–)2–3-seeded.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 391, 798; HK sheet 38809.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Glycosmis parvifolia (Sims) Little previously (Check List HK Plants 200. 2002; 71. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Glycosmis parvifolia (Sims) Little previously (Check List HK Plants 200. 2002; 71. 2004).

records.text:
Glyptostrobus pensilis (Staunton ex D. Don) K. Koch 水松
Dendrologie. 2(2): 191. 1873; FRPS 7: 299, pl. 69. 1978; FOC 4: 57. 1999; FGD 4: 22, fig. 12. 2000.
Thuja pensilis Staunton ex D. Don in Lamb., Descr. Pinus, ed. 2, 2: 115. 1828.
Glyptostrobus heterophyllus (Brongn.) Endl., Syn. Conif. 70. 1847; FKH 255. 1912.
Glyptostrobus sinensis A. Henry ex Loder, Gard. Chron., ser. 3, 66: 259, fig. 118, 122, 123. 1919.
Taxodium japonicum (Thunb. ex L. f.) Brongn. var. heterophyllum Brongn, Ann. Sci. Nat. (Paris) 30: 184. 1833.
Taxodium sinense J. Forb., Pinet. Woburn. 179. 1839.

Semi-deciduous tree to 15(–25) m tall; trunk to 1.2 m d.b.h., basal part (ca. 0.7 m) buttressed; bark brown or greyish white with brown tinge, cracking into long, irregular strips; main branches spreading horizontally; lateral branchlets in 2 rows, those of older branches often very dense and broomlike. Scale leaves on mature branchlets appressed, ca. 2 mm long, with scattered, white, stomatal spots, adaxial surface convex, persistent; linear leaves compressed, thin, usually in 2-rows, 1–3 cm × 1.5–4 mm, pale green, base narrow, apex acute, with stomatal bands along midveins on each side abaxially; linear-subulate leaves compressed, slightly falcately recurved distally, 4–11 mm long, in 3-rows; linear and linearsubulate leaves deciduous with short branchlets in winters. Seed cones obovoid, 1.4–2.5 × 0.9–1.5 cm. Seeds brown, ellipsoid, slightly flattened, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, with a basal wing 4–7 mm.

Locality: Fanling (recorded at Tai Hang Village in 1912, probably planted but no longer exist; see Iu & Lay, J. Roy. Asiatic Soc. H. K. Br. 22: 302–305. 1982). Also cultivated in gardens. S. C. Lau s.n.; L. T. Lo 280.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Vietnam.
Ecology: River deltas, etc., on flooded or waterlogged soil in full sun; near sea level. Pollinating: Jan.–Mar.; seed maturing: Sep.– Oct.(–Nov.), persisting until following spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gmelina chinensis Benth. 石梓（華石梓）
FHK 272. 1861; FKH 203. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 129, fig. 64. 1982; FFJ 4: 537, fig. 423. 1989; FOC 17: 33. 1994; FGD 3: 370. 1995.

Tree or shrub, 4–12 m tall; bark grey. Branchlets robust, yellowish brown pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole 2–5.5 cm, sulcate, pubescent when young, glabrescent; leaf blade papery to thickly papery, ovate‑elliptic to ovate, 5–15 × 3–7(–9) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially greyish white, puberulent and glandular; basal veins 3, lateral veins 3–5 pairs, prominent abaxially. Inflorescences terminal thyrses. Bracts leaf‑like, deciduous. Peduncle 5–10 cm, hairy. Calyx campanulate, 0.5–1.2 cm, apex truncate or 4‑denticulate, adaxially sparsely glandular and glabrous, abaxially pubescent, grey downy and with several disk‑shaped glands. Corolla funnelform, white or pinkish, 3–3.5 cm, throat ca. 2.5 cm in diam., sparsely glandular adaxially, densely glandular abaxially. Filaments flat, sparsely glandular‑hairy. Ovary obovoid, apically densely pubescent, basally glabrous. Drupes obovoid, ca. 2.2 cm.

Locality: Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1279, 2730; HK sheet 36035.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong between 1853 and 1854. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Gnaphalium affine D. Don 鼠麴草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 173. 1825; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 272. 1966; FRPS 75: 225. 1979: FGD 8: 170. 2007.
Gnaphalium multiceps DC., Prodr. 6: 222. 1837; FHK 188. 1861; FKH 144. 1912.
Gnaphalium luteoalbum subsp. affine (D. Don) Koster, Blumea 4: 484. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 4: 977. 1998.

Annual herbs; stem (4–)15–30 cm tall, striate, densely lanate, usually with creeping or ascending branches at base. Leaves sessile, oblanceolate‑spatulate, 1.5–6 cm × 2–10 mm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex rounded and mucronulate, margin entire, both surfaces tomemtose, woolly hair appearing much denser on lower surface. Capitula subsessile, compacted tightly into terminal corymbs. Involucres globose‑campanulate, 2–3 mm across; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, membranous, shinny golden or lemon‑yellow, outer ones elliptic‑ovate, 2 mm, base densely woolly, apex rounded; middle and inner ones oblanceolate‑spatulate to long‑spatulate, 3 mm, subglabrous or slightly woolly, apex obtuse. Receptacle concave, naked. Florets yellow or pale yellow. Outer female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 2 mm, apex minutely 3‑toothed. Central bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, 2–2.2 mm, apex shortly 5‑lobed. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, 0.5 mm, papillose. Pappus setae rough, 2 mm, yellowish white, deciduous separately or with several setae connate at base.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2676, 2697; S. Y. Hu 6940 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also found in Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Indochina, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages, weed in gardens. Flowering: Jan.–Apr., Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gnaphalium hypoleucum DC. 秋鼠麴草
Contr. Bot. India 21. 1834; FHK 187. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; FRPS 75: 226. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 975. 1998; FGD 8: 172. 2007.

Annual herbs; stem 30–80 cm tall, striate, densely white‑lanate and with short glandular hairs, usually branched on the upper portion. Leaves sessile; basal leaves withering before anthesis; lower stem leaves narrowly lanceolate to linear, 6–13 cm × 3–10 mm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire, adaxial surfaces green, densely covered with short glandular hairs, and with sparsely lanate on the midvein, abaxial surface densely white woolly. Capitula numerous, sessile or shortly pedunculate, in terminal congested corymbs. Involucres globose‑campanulate, 3–5 mm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, membranous, shinny golden‑yellow, subequal, 3–5 mm, outer ones obovate, apex rounded, abaxially white woolly at base; middle ones obovate‑oblong, apex obtuse, slightly white woolly at base abaxially; inner ones narrowly oblong to linear, apex acute, glabrous. Receptacle pitted. Florets yellow or pale yellow. Outer female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 3 mm, apex minutely 3– 4‑toothed. Central bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, ca. 4 mm, apex shortly 5‑lobed, style exserted. Cypselae oblong, 0.5 mm. Pappus white, ca. 3 mm, deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 2592.
Distribution: Widely distributed in E, S, C, SW & NW China; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Indochina, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Open fields and wastelands near villages, roadsides. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gnaphalium pensylvanicum Willd. 匙葉鼠麴草
Enum. Pl. Hort. Berol. 867. 1809; FRPS 75: 238. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 979. 1998; FGD 8: 172. 2007.
Gnaphalium purpureum auct. non L.: FHK 188. 1861; FKH 144. 1912.

Annual herbs, 10–35 cm tall; stem erect, striate, white woolly, with or without ascending branches at base. Leaves sessile, oblanceolate or spatulate, 2–8 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex rounded, and some mucronulate, margin entire, both surfaces tomentose, woolly hair much denser on lower side, leaf smaller gradually upward. Capitula many, tightly compacted into terminal or axillary spike about 1–5 cm, together with some small leaves included inside. Involucres ovate‑urceolate, 2–3 mm across; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; outer ones ovate‑oblong, 2–2.5 mm, densely woolly near base, centre green and herbaceous, apex brownish yellow, margin broadly membranous, acuminate; middle ones lanceolate, membranous, straw to brownish yellow in colour, slightly green‑veined at the middle, loosely woolly, apex acuminate; inner ones linear‑oblong, 3 mm, totally membranous, subglabrous, apex acute to obtuse. Receptacle deeply concave at centre, protruded at the periphery, naked. Marginal female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, about 2 mm, apex minutely 3‑toothed. Disk bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, about 2 mm, apex 5 triangular lobes, obtuse to rounded, glabrous. Cypselae elliptic‑oblong, 0.5 mm, finely glandular. Pappus 2 mm, white, connate at base and deciduous as a ring.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1189; S. Y. Hu 6788, 7184 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical Asia, S America, S Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.

Gnaphalium polycaulon Pers. 多莖鼠麴草
Syn. Pl. 2: 421. 1807; FRPS 75: 239. 1979; FGD 8: 172. 2007.
Gnaphalium indicum auct. non L.: FHK 188. 1861; FKH 144. 1912.

Annual herbs, 8–10 cm tall; stems basally creeping or ascending, densely white woolly, many‑branched. Leaves sessile, oblanceolate, 5–25 × 2–4 mm, base decurrent, apex obtuse and mucronulate, margin entire, both surfaces white woolly and with abaxial surface more hairy. Capitula many, tightly arranged as terminal spike about 5–15 mm, together with some small leaves included inside. Involucres ovate‑urceolate, 2 mm across; phyllaries 2‑seriate, membranous, greyish or straw yellow, tinged purple at base, apex acute; outer series oblong‑lanceolate, 1.2–1.5 mm long, lanate; inner ones 2 mm, loosely hairy or subglabrous. Receptacle shallowly concave, naked. Marginal female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 1–1.2 mm, apex finely 3‑toothed. Central bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, 1.2 mm, apex shortly 5‑lobed, acute, glabrous. Cypselae cylindric‑oblong, 0.5 mm long, minutely glandular. Pappus 1.2 mm, white, deciduous separately.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 831.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Zhejiang; India, Thailand, Australia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands and paddy fields. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.

Gnetum luofuense C. Y. Cheng 羅浮買麻藤
W. C. Cheng et al., Acta Phytotax. Sin. 13(4): 89. 1975; FOC 4: 105. 1999; FGD 4: 44, fig. 31. 2000.
Gnetum scandens auct. non Roxb.: FHK 336. 1861, p.p.; FKH 255. 1912, p.p.
Gnetum montanum auct. non Makgraf: FRPS 7: 492, pl. 114: 1–5. 1978; FFJ rev. ed. 1: 324. 1991.

Bark purplish brown, lenticels shallow, obscure. Petiole 8–12 mm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic or oblong-ovate, 10–20 × 4 – 10 cm, leathery or papery, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, glossy, reticulate veins evident on both surfaces. Male spikes simple or once branched; involucral collars 12–20, each collar with 60–80 male flowers plus 15–30 sterile female flowers, often patent at anthesis; male flower: basal hairs dense, brown, false perianth slightly succulent, in irregular rhomboid tube, apex truncate. Female spikes with 10–20 involucral collars, each collar with 8–13 female flowers. Seeds sessile, ellipsoid, 1.5–2.8 × 1.5–1.8 cm, very fleshy, base often contracted into an apparent stipe when dried, apex acute with a mucro, outer coat orange-red, coarsely reticulate-wrinkled when dried.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1369; Y. W.Lam 635.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan,Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forest; Pollinating: May–Jul.; seed maturing:Aug.– Oct.

Gnetum parvifolium (Warb.) C. Y. Cheng ex Chun 小葉買麻藤
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 9: 386. 1964; FRPS 7: 498, pl. 117. 1978; FFJ rev. ed. 1: 325, fig. 301. 1991; FOC 4: 104. 1999; FGD 4: 44, fig. 30. 2000.
Gnetum scandens Roxb. var. parvifolium Warb., Monsunia 1: 196. 1900.
Gnetum montanum Markgraf. f. parvifolium (Warb.) Markgraf., Bull. Jard. Bot. Buitenzorg, ser. 3, 10: 468. 1930.
Gnetum scandens auct. non Roxb.: FHK 336. 1861, p.p.; FKH 255. 1912, p.p.

Bark pale or greyish brown, lenticels usually relatively conspicuous. Petiole 5 – 8(–10) mm; leaf blade elliptic to narrowly elliptic, or long-obovate, 4 –10 × 2.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acute or attenuate, sometimes obtuse, lateral veins usually inconspicuous adaxially, reticulate veins conspicuous abaxially. Male inflorescences simple or once branched; peduncle slender, 0.5 –1.5 cm; involucral collars 5 –10, each collar with 40 –70 male flowers plus 10 –12 sterile female flowers, enclosed at anthesis; male flower: basal hairs few, brown, short, false perianth rhomboid. Female inflorescences usually borne on old branches, 10 –15 cm in fruit; peduncle 1.5 –2 cm; female spikes with involucral collars 6 –9 mm apart, nodes each with 5 – 8 female flowers, basal hairs brown, short. Seeds sessile or nearly so, red, elongate ellipsoid or fusiform to narrowly oblong-obovoid, (1.3 –)1.6 –2.2 cm × (4 –)5 – 8(–10) mm, 2–3 times as long as wide, apex usually with a small, pointed tip, outer coat thin, longitudinally striate when dried.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 448; Y. W. Lam 844.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests; 100 –1000 m. Pollinating: Apr.–Jun.; seed maturing: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Food (seeds).

Gomphostemma chinense Oliv. 中華錐花
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 15: 54. 1884; FKH 212. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 116, pl. 23: 1 – 6. 1977; FOC 17: 74. 1994; FGD 3: 398. 1995.

Perennial herbs, 20–80 cm tall, rhizomatous. Stems erect, obtusely 4‑angled, densely stellate tomentose. Leaves subleathery; petiole 2–6 cm, densely stellate tomentose; leaf blade elliptic to ovate‑elliptic, 4–13 × 2–7 cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex obtuse, margin irregularly coarse serrate to subentire, adaxially stellate pubescent and sparsely strigose, abaxially dense grey stellate tomentose. Flowers solitary or in 4–many‑flowered whorls at the axils of the lower leaves; peduncle to ca. 2.2 cm; bracts elliptic to lanceolate, 11–16 × 5–7 mm, margin coarsely serrate or entire on apical half; bracteoles linear, shorter than bracts. Calyx narrowly campanulate in flower, 12–13 mm, densely grey stellate tomentose outside; teeth lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 6 – 7 mm, apex acuminate. Corolla yellowish to white, ca. 5.2 cm, sparsely puberulent outside; upper lip erect, ca. 6 × 8 mm, apex rounded and emarginate; lower lip 1–1.4 × 1.3–1.9 cm, middle lobe obovate‑subcircular, 7–8 × 6–7 mm; lateral lobes ovate, ca. 5 × 5 mm. Stamens almost as long as upper lip of corolla; filaments complanate, margin puberulent. Style shorter than stamens, slightly thicker on apical 2/3, apically unequally 2‑cleft. Nutlets 4 per flower at maturity, obovoid, triquetrous, ca. 4 × 2.8 mm, brown, bullate, hairy.

Locality: Tate's Cairn, Pyramid Hill, Fo Tan. HK sheet 32249, 38428, 39407.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gomphrena celosioides C. Martius 銀花莧（野千日紅）
Nova Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 13(1): 301. 1825; FHN 1: 410. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 239. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 407. 1996; FGD 4: 113. 2000; FOC 5: 428. 2003.

Annual herb, 10–35 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, white-pilose. Leaves papery, shortly petiolate or subsessile; leaf blade oblong to somewhat spathulate, 3– 4.5 × 0.5 –1.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire and ciliate, adaxially ± with appressed hairs or glabrous, abaxially pubescent. Inflorescence a terminal head, initially globose, afterwards elongate into a short spike, to 2– 4 cm. Bracteoles triangular lanceolate, ca. 6 mm, silvery white, winged dorsally. Perianth-segments lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, woolly outside; filament-tube slightly shorter than perianth-segments; style 2 branched. Utricles ellipsoid, enclosed by the woolly persistent perianth.

Locality: Harlech Road, Ngau Chi Wan, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Sham Tseng, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 400, 1641; H. C. Tang 2113.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan (naturalized). Native to S America, widely naturalized in tropics.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Sep.

Gomphrena globosa L. 千日紅
Sp. Pl. 224. 1753; FHN 1: 410. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 238. 1979; FGD 4: 113. 2000; FOC 5: 428. 2003.

Annual herb, 20–60 cm tall. Stems erect, covered with hoary long hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, hairy; leaf blade oblong to elliptic or somewhat obovate, 3.5–13 ×1.5–5 cm, apex acute or obtuse, base attenuate, margin entire and ciliate, white-pilose on both surfaces. Inflorescence a dense globular head, 2–3 cm in diam., closely subtended by 2 broad leafy bracts. Bracteoles triangular lanceolate, ca. 1 cm, violate, red, yellowish or white in different garden races, winged dorsally. Perianth-segments lanceolate, 5–6 mm, woolly outside. Filamenttube as long as perianth-segments. Style 2 branched. Utricles subglobose, 2–2.5 mm in diam., enclosed by the woolly persistent perianth.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 640; Y. S. Lau 1011.
Distribution: Widely cultivated throughout tropical and warm temperate regions, sometimes naturalized.
Ecology: Usually cultivated as a pot plant in Hong Kong. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gonocarpus chinensis (Lour.) Orchard 黃花小二仙草
Bull. Auckland Inst. Mus. 10: 207. 1975.
Haloragis chinensis (Lour.) Merr., Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc., n.s., 24(2): 39. 1935; FHN 1: 431, fig. 236. 1964; FRPS 53(2): 141, pl. 29: 6. 2000.
Haloragis scabra (Koenig.) Benth., FHK 139. 1861.
Haloragis tetragyna auct. non (Labill.) Hook. f.: FKH 102. 1912.
Gaura chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 225. 1790.

Perennial terrestrial herbs, 10 – 60 cm tall. Stems slender, 4-angled, erect or diffuse, much branched, rough and more or less with minute, retrorse hairs, rooting at nodes. Leaves opposite, subsessile, lanceolate or narrowly oblong, 10–28 × 1–9 mm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse, margin sparsely serrate, scabrous and ± hirtellous on both surfaces. Flowers small, 0.2 – 0.7 mm, almost sessile, solitary in each bract, forming slender, terminal, one-sided racemes or interrupted spikes, and usually branching into narrow panicles. Calyx tubular, 4-lobed; lobes triangular, margin yellowish, cartilaginous. Petals narrowly oblong, 0.5 – 0.9 × 0.4–0.6 mm, yellow, sparsely puberulent abaxially. Stamens 8, nearly as long as the petals. Ovary ovoid, 4-locular; style very short; divided at the top into a tuft of hair-like lobes. Nuts subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., with 8 ribs and scabrous tubercles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 8127; Y. S. Lau 2052, 3144.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Moist and wet grassy slopes. Flowering: May –Aug.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Haloagis chinensis (Lour.) Merr. previously (Check List HK Plants 158. 2002; 58. 2004).

Gonocarpus micranthus Thunb. 小二仙草
Nov. Gen. Pl. 3: 69. 1783.
Haloragis micrantha (Thunb.) R. Br., Fl. Jap. 1: 25. 1835; FHN 1: 431. 1964; FRPS 53(2): 141, pl. 29: 6. 2000.

Perennial terrestrial herbs, 5–45 cm tall. Stems slender, sulcate, erect or prostrate at the base, much branched, usually reddish brown. Leaves opposite, short-petiolate or subsessile, ovate, 6–17 × 4–8 mm, base rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin sparsely serrate, usually glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers small, ca. 1 mm, almost sessile, solitary under each bract, forming slender, terminal, one-sided racemes or panicles. Calyx-tube 0.8 mm, apex 4-lobed, lobes triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Petals pink, narrowly oblong, ca. 1.5 mm. Stamens 8; filaments ca. 0.2 mm; anthers linear, 0.3–0.7 mm. Ovary ovoid, 2–4-locular. Nuts subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., obtusely 8-ribbed.

Locality: Sunset Peak. L. T. Lo 613; Y. W. Lam 1635.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina, India, Malesia, New Zealand, Australia.
Ecology: Moist grassy slopes. Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Jun. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Haloragis micrantha (Thunb.) R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 158. 2002; 58. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Haloragis micrantha (Thunb.) R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 158. 2002; 58. 2004).

records.text:
Gonostegia hirta (Blume ex Hassk.) Miq. 糯米團
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 4: 303. 1868; FRPS 23(2): 367, pl. 82: 2–7. 1995; FOC 5: 178. 2003; FGD 6: 99, fig .42. 2005.
Memorialis hispida Buch.-Ham. ex Wall. Cat. sub n. 4601; FHK 332. 1861.
Memorialis hirta (Blume ex Hassk.) Wedd., Prodr. 16(1): 235(6). 1869.
Pouzolzia hirta Blume ex Hassk. in Teismann & Binnendijk, Cat. Hort. Bogor. 80. 1844, based on Urtica hirta Blume (1826), not Swartz (1797); FKH 250. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems prostrate or upper part ascending, 50–100 cm or longer, pubescent. Leaves opposite; stipules subulate, ca. 2.5 mm; petioles 1– 4 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to narrowly ovate, (1.5 –)3–10 × 1–2.8 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, adaxial surface ± scabrous, sparsely strigose or subglabrous, abaxial surface sparsely pubescent on the veins or glabrescent, 3 – 5-nerved. Flowers in axillary clusters of 2–9 mm in diam. Male flowers: pedicels 1–4 mm; bud turbinate, top flat, with a ring of hairs on the rim; perianth‑segments 5, free, oblanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, apex abruptly acute; stamens 5; staminodes very small. Female flowers sessile, perianth tube ovoid, ca. 1.6 mm, longitudinally 10-ribbed, apex 2-toothed; stigma ca. 3 mm, hairy. Achene ovoid, ca. 1.4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 937, 2152; Y. S. Lau 606.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Waste and shady places. Flowering; May–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Goodyera foliosa (Lindl.) Benth. ex Clarke 多葉斑葉蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 25: 73. 1889; FKH 268. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3 – 4): 400. 1973; FRPS 17: 142. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 904. 2000; FOC 25: 51. 2009.
Georchis foliosa Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 496. 1840.
Goodyera foliosa (Lindl.) Hook. f. var. alba S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 8. 1967; Check List HK Plants 376. 2002; 131. 2004.

Terrestrial herb, 10–17 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves ovate or oblong, 2.5–7 × 1.5–2.5 cm, acute; petioles 1–2 cm. Flower colour varying greatly, salmon-pink with orange lip white at apex; dorsal sepal pink with white margin, lateral sepals 5–7 × 0.4 cm, margin strongly curved; petals salmon-pink, creamy-white along margin, 5–7 × 4 mm; lip deep orange, white at apex, strongly saccate and round at base; column yellow, 2 mm; anther ovoid, 2.5 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11037, 11059 (CUHK); HK sheet 35642.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, S China; Bhutan, Nepal, N India, Myanmar, Japan.
Ecology: Ravines near mountain streams. Flowering: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The holotype specimen of G. foliosa var. alba (G. Barretto 100, K) was collected by Ruy Barretto from Tai Mo Shan in Jul., 1970.

Goodyera procera (Ker Gawl.) Hook. 高斑葉蘭
Exot. Fl. 1: t. 39. 1823; FHK 360. 1861; FKH 268. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3–4): 402. 1973, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 48, fig. 19. 1977; FRPS 17: 151. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 908. 2000; FGD 7: 351. 2006; FOC 25: 51. 2009.
Neottia procera Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 8: t. 639. 1822.

Terrestrial herb; stem upright, to 35 cm tall, pubescent. Leaves petiolate; petioles 2.5–8 cm; leaf blades elliptic or lanceolate, 6–12 × 1.3–4.5 cm, reticulation obscure, apex acuminate or acute. Scape 32 cm; flowers small, greenish white, up to 120 in a terminal raceme; dorsal sepal 3 × 1.5 mm, lateral sepals 2.5 mm; petals white, forming a roof with the odd sepal; lip fleshy, white, 2.5 mm, attached to a column foot; column 2 mm; anther globose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary and pedicel 3–4.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9946, 11846 (CUHK); HK sheet 40375.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; Japan, Philippines, S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Earth pockets on rocks in stream bed. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Goodyera seikoomontana Yamam. 歌綠斑葉蘭（香港斑葉蘭）
J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 4: 187, 1932; FRPS 17: 152. 1999; FOC 25: 49. 2009.
Goodyera youngsayei S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 10, fig. 5. 1976; FRPS 17: 153. 1999.

Small terrestrial herb, 10–15 cm tall; stems creeping, consisting of 5–10 internodes. Leaves petiolate; petiole 1.5–3 cm; leaf blades oblique-ovate, 3–7.5 × 1.7–3.6 cm, apex triangular-acute. Flowers pearl-colour, slightly pink at apex; 1–3 in a small spike terminal to a scape of 8–12 cm; odd sepal 1.5 × 0.6 cm, arcuate and hood-like; lateral sepals ovate-lanceolate, 1.4 × 0.6 cm, spreading and pointing backward; petals oblique oblanceolate-spathulate, 14 mm; lip ventricose, apex recurved; column ivory white; anther sagittate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary cylindrical, 11–15 mm, villose at apex. Fruit a capsule.

Locality: Fo Tan Valley, Pat Sin Leng. Y. S. Lau 1778; HK sheet 30752.
Distribution: S Taiwan.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests.
Notes: The type specimen of G. youngsayei (G. Barretto 107, K, holotype; A, isotype) was collected from Pat Sin Leng in 1975.

Goodyera viridiflora (Blume) Blume 綠花斑葉蘭
Orch. Archip. Ind. 41, pl. 9c, f. 2(12–16). 1858; FRPS 17: 152. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 912, photo 121. 2000; FOC 25: 50. 2009.
Neottia viridiflora Blume, Bijdr. 408. 1825.
Goodyera cordata (Lindl.) Benth. ex Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 114. 1890, et Hooker's Icon. Pl. t. 2187. 1894; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 46. 1977.

Small terrestrial herb, 10–15 cm tall at flowering time; portion of stem lying on the damp ground as a rhizome, slightly swollen, internodes 5–7 mm long, 2 mm in diam., ascending and bearing a rosette of leaves. Leaves 3–5, petiolate; leaf blades ovate-cordate, 2.5–4.5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers greenish pink, 2–5 in a terminal spike; odd sepal cucullate, 1 cm; lateral sepals same colour, ovate-lanceolate, 9–10 × 3–4 mm, reflexed; petals greenish-pink, whitish along margin, linear-falcate, 8 × 1.5 mm, upper margin coalescent with margin of odd sepal; lip white, tinged green, base slightly saccate, 8 mm; column green, very short (2.5 mm); anther ovate-cordate, beaked; pollinia 4; ovary and pedicel hairy.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Fanling. S. Y. Hu 9905 (CUHK); HK sheet 41730.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Wet grounds along streams in shade.

Goodyera yangmeishanensis T. P. Lin 小小斑葉蘭
Native. Orch. Taiwan 2: 173. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 914. 2000; FOC 25: 54. 2009.
Goodyera shixingensis K. Y. Lang, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 34(6): 636, fig. 2. 1996; FRPS 17: 140, fig. 18: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 349. 2006.

Small terrestrial herb; stem erect from the creeping base, 8–11 cm tall, reddish or reddish brown, bearing 3–5 leaves near the base. Leaves petiolate; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 1.5–4.5 × 0.8–1.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute, dark green, with fine white network on adaxial surface; petiole 1–1.5 cm, dilated and amplexicaul at base. Peduncle 5–8 cm, glabrous proximally, hairy distally; floral bracts ovate-lanceolate, ca. 6 × 3.2 mm, apex caudate-acuminate, serrulate or entire at base. Flowers small, several to more than 10 in a terminal raceme, and usually turning on one side; sepal greenish brown, dorsal one ovate-elliptic, 3–3.3 × 2.5 mm; lateral ones obliquely ovate, 4 × 2.8 mm; petals white, obliquely spatulate, ca. 3 × 1 mm; lip 4–5 mm, undivided, base deeply saccate, hairy inside, limb ovate, irregularly toothed at margin near apex; column 2–2.5 mm; anther cordate; pollinia 4; ovary and pedicel glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. HK sheet 33355.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.

Grangea maderaspatana (L.) Poir. 田基黃（荔枝菊）
Encycl. Suppl. 2(2): 825 – 826. 1812; FHK 185. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 279. 1966; FRPS 74: 83. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 982. 1998; FGD 8: 191, fig. 110. 2007.
Artemisia maderaspatana L., Sp. Pl. 849. 1753.

Annual herbs; stems 5–20 cm, decumbent and ascending, branched at basal portion, strigose. Leaves obovate, oblanceolate to spatulate, 1.5–6 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, sessile or some forming winged petioles, apex obtuse, margin sinuate‑pinnatifid with 2–5 pairs of lateral lobes, irregularly serrate‑crenate, pubescent and glandular punctate on both surfaces, abaxial surface covered with denser hair and glands. Capitula globose, 0.5– 1 cm across, solitary, growing terminal or axillary to the stems. Involucres bowl‑shaped; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, herbaceous, hirsute, margin fimbriate; outer ones lanceolate‑oblong, 4–5 mm, apex acute to obtuse; inner ones oblanceolate or obovate, apex rounded, slightly shorter. Receptacle convex, spherical. Marginal pistillate florets numerous, in 2–6 series, corolla yellow, tubular, 1–1.2 mm, narrow, glandular, with 2–4 lobes at apex; style exserted. Disk hermaphrodite florets many, corolla yellow, tubular, funnelform, glandular, 1.5 mm, with 5 ovate‑deltoid lobes at apex. Cypselae compressed, with thickened ribs on margin, 1.5 mm, glandular. Pappus scarious cupular, about 1 mm, irregularly toothed and ciliate.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Tam Tuk Reservoir, Tai Lung, Ting Kok, Ho Pui Reservoir. Y. S. Lau 2469, 2483; Y. W. Lam 1486.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Lowland thickets, abandoned fields. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.

Graphistemma pictum (Champ. ex Benth.) Benth. & Hook. f. ex Maxim. 天星藤
Melanges Biol. Bull. Phys.‑Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 9: 776. 1876; FKH 170. 1912; FRPS 63: 412, pl. 152. 1977; FGD 1: 490, fig. 552. 1987; FOC 16: 228. 1995.
Holostemma pictum Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 53. 1853; FHK 224. 1861.

Lianas to 8 m, glabrous. Stipules present, leafy, rounded to ovate, 10–35 × 8–15 mm, amplexicaul; petioles 1–4.5 cm, flat, with group of adaxial glands; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, 6–20 × 2.5–7 cm, base rounded, sometimes slightly cordate, apex acuminate or acute, veins pale, lateral veins ca. 10 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences 3–12‑flowered; peduncle 0.5–5 cm. Pedicels 0.5–1.5 cm. Corolla abaxially green, adaxially purplish with yellow margin; lobes oblong, 8–10 × 3–4 mm, minutely ciliate. Follicles 9–11 × 3–4 cm. Seeds brownish, ovate, 1.3 cm; coma to 4 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Chek Keng, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 600; L. T. Lo 353; HK sheet 40095.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets; 100–700 m. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Grevillea robusta A. Cunn. ex R. Br. 銀樺
Suppl. Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holl. 24. 1830; FGZ 173, fig. 76. 1956; FHN 1: 442, fig. 243. 1964; FGD 1: 95, fig. 105. 1987; FRPS 24: 7, pl. 2: 1 –6. 1988.

Evergreen tree, 10 – 25 m tall; bark dark grey to blackish, longitudinally fissured; young shoots and peduncles rusty tomentose. Leaves alternate, bipinnatifid, 15 – 30 cm, ultimate segments lanceolate, margin recurved, adaxial surface glabrous or sparsely covered with silky hairs, abaxial surface densely covered with silvery silky hairs and brown tomentum. Racemes 11–15 cm, axillary or sometimes several crowded together on leafless short branches. Pedicels ca. 1 cm, glabrous. Perianth orange; tube 1–1.3 cm; lobes small, oblanceolate, 4 –6 mm. Ovary stipitate; style 1.8–2 cm, with oblique discoid stigma. Follicles oblique ovoid, ca. 1.5 cm; seeds oblong, winged.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang & N. B. G. 1; Y. S. Lau 2198.
Distribution: Native to Australia, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Grewia biloba G. Don 扁擔桿
Gen. Hist. 1: 549. 1831; FFJ 3: 401, fig. 282. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 94, pl. 24: 5 –9. 1989; FGD 4: 158, fig. 101. 2000.
Grewia glabrescens Benth., FHK 42. 1861; FKH 51. 1912.
Grewia parviflora Bunge var. glabrescens Rehd. & Wils., Pl. Wils. 2: 371. 1916.
Grewia biloba G. Don var. parviflora auct. non (Bunge) Hand.-Mazz.: Check List HK Plants 43.1993.

Shrub or small tree, 1–2.5 m tall, much branched. Branchlets covered with yellow stellate hairs. Stipules subulate, 3–4 mm; petioles 6–15 mm, stellate hairy; leaf blade ovate, rhomboid-orbicular or obovate elliptic, 4–12 × 2.5–7 cm, thin leathery, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate, rough and sparsely stellatehispid abaxially and adaxially; basal veins 3, lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Cymes axillary, many-flowered, peduncle less than 1 cm. Pedicels 3–6 mm, bract subulate, 3–5 mm. Sepals narrow oblong, 4 –7 mm, hairy abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Petals 1–1.5 mm. Stamens 2 mm. Ovary hairy; style as long as sepals; stigma swollen, disk-shaped, lobed. Drupe red, with 2–4 drupelets.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar, Sai Kung, Tai Wan, Beaufort Island, Po Toi. Y. W. Lam 1563, 653; S. P. Lau 166.
Distribution: Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, Hunan, Hubei, Guangdong, Sichuan.
Ecology: Shrubby forests. Flowering: May–Jul; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Grewia eriocarpa Juss. 毛果扁擔桿
Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 4: 93. 1804; FHN 2: 60. 1965; FRPS 49(1): 91, pl. 24: 1– 5. 1989; FGD 4: 156. 2000.
Grewia celtidifolia Juss. var. eriocarpa (Juss.) Hsu & Zhuge, Bot. Journ. South China 2: 19. 1993.
Grewia asiatica auct. non L.: FKH 51. 1912 (quoad Birdwood s.n.).

Shrub or small tree, 1– 8 m tall. Young branchlets grey stellate-pubscent; branchlets subglabrous, dark brown to brown after dried. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 0.5–1 cm; petioles 0.6 –1 cm, densely stellate hairy; leaf blade oblique ovate or ovate-oblong, 6–13 × 3 – 6(–9) cm, papery, base oblique and rounded, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrulate, sparsely stellate hairy and rough adaxially, grey stellate-pubescent abaxially; basal veins usually 5, rarely 4 or 6, lateral veins 2–3 pairs. Cymes 3- to several-flowered, axillary, 1.5 –3 cm, densely yellow or greyish yellow stellate-pubescent; peduncle 3 – 8 mm. Bract lanceolate, densely yellow or greyish yellow stellate-pubescent abaxially. Flowers bisexual. Sepals narrowly oblong, 6–8 mm, hairy on both surfaces. Petals subulate, ca. 3 mm, glands less than 1 mm. Stamens distinct, unequal, shorter than sepals. Ovary densely villose. Style pubescent; stigma peltate, 4-lobed or entire. Drupe subglobose, 6– 8 mm in diam., stellate hairy, slightly grooved or nearly smooth, apex mucronate, not divided into drupelets.

Locality: Cultivated but nowadays not common. L. T. Lo 458; Y. S. Lau 381; Birdwood s.n. (HK sheet 3763).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan, Yunnan; India, Indochina, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Notes: This species was reported as Grewia tiliaefolia Vahl (椴葉扁擔桿) previously (Check List HK Plants 94. 2002).

Grewia oligandra Pierre 寡蕊扁擔桿（粗毛扁擔桿）
Fl. Forest. Cochinch. 2: 163. 1888; FRPS 49(1): 102. 1989; FGD 4: 157. 2000.

Shrub. Branchlets stellate tomentose, old branches dark brown. Stipules subulate, 4 mm, caducous. Petioles 5–8 mm, densely stellate-tomentose; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong lanceolate, 9–10.5 × 2–3.5 cm, papery, base round, apex acute, margin serrulate with alternating large and small teeth, sparsely stellate-hispidulous and dark brown when dry adaxially, densely grey-brown-tomentose abaxially; basal veins 3, lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Cymes 3–5-flowered; peduncle 4–7 mm, tomentose. Pedicels 3–4 mm, tomentose. Bracts 3–4 mm. Sepals 5– 6 mm, tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Petals oblong, 2–3 mm; glands scale-like, surrounded by hairs. Stamens shorter than sepals. Ovary hairy; stigma multi-lobed. Drupe double or tetra-globose, 1 cm in diam., shiny; stalk 0.5–1 cm, densely tomentose.

Locality: Chuen Lung. Y. S. Lau 2542, 2331; L.T. Lo 382.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Indochina.
Ecology: Shrubby forests or thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: This species was reported as Grewia hirsuta Vahl previously (Check List HK Plants 94. 2002).

Gymnanthera oblonga (Burm. f.) P. S. Green 海島藤
Kew Bull. 47: 33. 1992; FOC 16: 193. 1995; P. T. Li & X. M. Chen, High. Pl. China 9: 136, pl. 213. 1999.
Jasminum oblongum Burm. f., Fl. Indica 6, t. 3, fig. 2. 1768.
Gymnanthera nitida R. Br., Prodr. 464. 1810; FGD 1: 537, fig. 617. 1987.

Lianas to 2 m. Branchlets tawny‑brown, lenticellate, slightly pubescent. Petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic, 3 – 5.5 × 1.5 – 2. cm, papery, glabrous, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex rounded, apiculate. Cymes aparently axillary, nearly sessile, congested, ca. 2 cm wide, to 7‑flowered, glabrous. Pedicels 5 – 10 mm. Sepals ovate, 2 × 1 mm, basal glands 5 – 10. Corolla yellowish green; tube 6 – 9 mm; lobes ovate, 7 × 5 mm, obtuse. Corona‑lobes ovate, apex apiculate. Pollen carriers short cylindric, erect. Ovary of 2 separate carpels, glabrous. Follicles dark brown, 8 – 12 × 0.5 – 0.6 cm. Seed tawny‑brown, oblong, 7 × 2 mm; coma ca. 2 cm.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tsing Yi, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1721; HK sheet 39781, 40264.
Distribution: Hainan, S Guangdong; Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, New Guinea, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy beaches or rocks by streams. Flowering: Aug. –Oct.; fruiting: Sep. –Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gymnema inodorum (Lour.) Decne. 廣東匙羹藤
Prodr. 8: 551. 1844; FRPS 63: 425. 1977; FGD 1: 501, fig. 567. 1987; FOC 16: 240. 1995.
Cynanchum inodorum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 166. 1790.

Lianas to 10 m. Stems glabrous; young branchlets pale grey, lenticellate, puberulent. Petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade membranous, ovate‑oblong to ovate or broadly ovate, 4–13 × 2–9 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex acuminate to caudate, glabrous or thinly puberulent along veins, lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences eventually raceme‑like with sessile umbel‑like cymes arranged in spiral, up to 4 cm; peduncle 1–2 cm. Pedicels 1–1.5cm. Sepals oblong, 2–3 × 1.4 mm, shorter than corolla‑tube, puberulent, ciliate. Corolla yellow, 6–7 mm, minutely puberulent outside; tube cylindric, glabrous except for longitudinal bands of stiff hairs alternating with lobes; lobes oblong, 3–4 × 1.6–1.8 cm, apex rounded, glabrous except for ciliate margins. Pollinia oblong. Stigma head dome‑shaped, exserted from corolla‑tube. Follicles lanceolate in outline, up to 16 × 3 cm, wall thick and slightly fibrous, glabrous. Seeds ca. 15 × 10 mm; coma 4 cm.

Locality: Sai Kung, Fung Yuen. Y. S. Lau 2841; L. T. Lo 343.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Nepal, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Jan.–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Gymnema sylvestre (Retz.) R. Br. ex Schult. 匙羹藤
Syst. Veg. 6: 57. 1820; FRPS 63: 418, pl. 154. 1977; FGD 1: 500, fig. 565. 1987; FOC 16: 238. 1995.
Periploca sylvestris Retz., Obs. Bot. 2: 15. 1781.
Gymnema affine Decne., Prodr. 8: 622. 1844; FHK 227. 1861; FKH 170. 1912.

Woody lianas, with white latex. Stems to 8 m, sparsely lenticellate; yong branchlets pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 3–12 mm; leaf blade obovate to ovate, 3–8.5 × 1.5–5.5 cm, thick‑papery, adaxially pubescent to glabrous except for groove of midvein, abaxially tomentose to glabrous except for veins, lateral veins 4 or 5 on each side of midvein, convergent. Cymes much shorter than leaves, pubescent; peduncle 2–5 mm, rachis with close‑spaced spiral of pedicel‑scars. Sepals ovate, ciliate. Corolla greenish white; lobes ovate, glabrous. Corona‑lobes and stigma head exserted. Follicles mostly solitary, broadly lanceolate in outline, 5–9 × 2 cm, glabrous, with an acuminate beak. Seeds ovate, 8 × 4 mm; coma silky white, 3.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 162; N. H. Li 141; HK sheet 39262.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang,
Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), poisonous.

Gymnopetalum chinense (Lour.) Merr. 金瓜（越南裸瓣瓜）
Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 256. 1919; FRPS 73(1): 213. 1986; FGD 3: 130. 1995.
Bryonia cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 595. 1790.
Evonymus chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 156. 1790.
Gymnopetalum cochinchinense (Lour.) Kurz, J. As. Soc. Bengal 40: 57. 1871; FKH 112. 1912; FHN 1: 479. 1964.
Gymnopetalum quinquelobatum Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 70. 1938

Perennial herbaceous vine, monoecious. Stems 5-angled, hispid, glabrescent. Petioles 1–5 cm; leaf blade membranous or thinly papery, ovate-heart-shaped in outline, pentagonal or 3 –5-lobed, 4 – 8 × 4 – 8 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin dentate or undulate, scabrous and tuberculate on both surfaces. Male flowers: solitary or 3 – 8 in racemes; peduncle slender, 10 – 15 cm; bract leaf-like, rhomboid, pubescent; calyx-tube narrow, 2 cm, pubescent, lobes linear, 7 mm; corolla white, lobes oblongovate, 15 mm; filaments 0.5 mm, anthers 7 mm. Female flowers: solitary; pedicels 1– 4 cm; ovary ellipsoid, 1–1.2 cm, 5 mm in diam., yellow-brown-villous, acute at the both ends, style 5 –8 mm, stigmas 3. Fruits ellipsoid, orange, 4 –5 cm, smooth, 10-ridged, acute at the both ends. Seeds oblong, 7 x 3 –3.5 mm, both ends obtuse, rugose and marginate.

Locality: Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 2535; HK sheet 12023.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong; India to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Cleome gynandra L. 白花菜
Sp. Pl. 2: 671. 1753; FHN 1: 344, fig. 174. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 739, pl. 346. 1996; FRPS 32: 533. 1999; FGD 1: 82, fig. 88. 1987.

Annual herb, ca. 1 m tall. Stems erect; young branches, petioles and inflorescence ± with glandular hairs. Leaves digitately compound; petioles 2–6 cm; leaflets 3–7, sessile or nearly so, blade obovate-elliptic to oblanceolate, the middle one larger, 1–5 × 0.8 –1.6 cm, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, base cuneate, margin serrulate, glabrescent on both surfaces. Racemes terminal, 15 –30 cm. Bract leafy, 3- lobed. Pedicels 1–2 cm, hairy. Sepals lanceolate, elliptic or ovate, 3 – 6 × 1–2 mm. Petals white, suborbicular or broadly obovate, 6–12 × 2– 6 mm , claw ca. 5 mm. Stamens 6, exserted. Androgynophore 5 –18(–22) mm. Ovary cylindrical, with viscid glandular hairs; style very short. Capsule cylindrical, 4– 8 cm.

Locality: Cheung Chau. Exotic. Y. W. Lam 1550; HK sheet 204.
Distribution: Widely distributed from Hainan northwards to Hebei, and from Yunnan eastwards to Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gynostemma pentaphyllum (Thunb.) Makino 絞股藍
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 179. 1902; FHN 1: 485. t. 266. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 269. 1986; FFJ 5: 242, fig. 226. 1993; FGD 3: 140. 1995.
Vitis pentaphylla Thunb., Fl. Jap. 105. 1784.

Stems slender, ridged and sulcate, glabrous or pubescent. Tendrils long, 2-branched at apex. Petioles 2–7 cm, hairy. Leaves membranous or papery, palmately (3 –)5(–7)-foliolate, pubescent or glabrous; leaflets ovate-oblong or lanceolate, 2–15 × 0.8 –5 cm, central one larger, lateral ones smaller, base attenuate, apex acute or acuminate, mucronate, margin undulate-dentate, glabrous or pilose on both surfaces, lateral veins 4–8 pairs; petiolules 1–5 mm. Male inflorescences 10 –16 cm, many-branched. Male flowers: pedicels filiform, 1– 4 mm; bracteole subulate; calyx-tube very short, lobes triangular, 0.7 mm; corolla pale green or white, lobes ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, ciliolate. Female inflorescences much shorter. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 5, short; ovary globose, 2–3-locular, styles 3, stigmas bifid. Berries globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., indehiscent, black when mature, glabrous, 2-seeded. Seeds compressed, papillose.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tsz Mun Tin. Y. W. Lam 419, 420, 421.
Distribution: S Shaanxi and regions S of Changjiang River. E Asia to tropical Asia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal.

Gynura divaricata (L.) DC. 白子菜
Prodr. 6: 301. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 280. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 317, pl. 71: 5–8. 1999; FGD 8: 227, fig. 138. 2007.
Gynura ovalis (Ker Gawl.) DC., Prodr. 6: 300. 1837.
Cacalia ovalis Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 2: pl. 101. 1816.
Senecio divaricatus L., Sp. Pl. 866. 1753.
Gynura pseudochina auct. non DC.: FHK 189. 1861.

Perennial herbs, odorous like bad egg smell; stem erect or decumbent, about 0.3–1(–2) m tall, branched in upper inflorescence portion, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves fleshy, mainly growing at lower portion, petiole 0.5–4.5 cm, pubescent, base usually with pseudo‑stipules, leaf blade ovate, elliptic to oblanceolate, 3.5–13(–23) × 1.2–5(– 6.5) cm, base cuneate and narrowed down to petiole, apex obtuse or acute, margin coarsely dentate, adaxial surfaces green, abaxial surfaces pale green, both densely pubescent with hair multicellular, venation appeared as numerous black lines after dried. Median leaves smaller in size, subsessile to sessile, elliptic‑oblong, dentate. Upper leaves few, sessile, linear‑lanceolate to linear, 0.5–2 cm. Capitula 1.5–2 cm across, with 3 – 5 heads arranged as loose corymbs at terminal; peduncle 1–6.5(–9) cm, pubescent. Involucres campanulate, length 8 – 10 mm, base calyculate with several linear bracteoles 3–5.5 mm; phyllaries 11–14 in 1 series, linear‑lanceolate, 8–10 × 1–2 mm, apex acuminate, margin scarious, 3‑veined, subglabrous or puberulous abaxially. Receptacle flat, pitted with areoles elevated at centre. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, total 10–14 mm, lower portion filiform 7–10 mm, upper portion abruptly broaden as cylindric or campanulate form, 3–4 mm, apex with 5 acute ovate‑oblong lobes, floret colour brilliant orange‑yellow, some tinged red near apex; anther bases obtuse or shortly sagittate; stylar branches papillose hairy. Cypselae cylindric, 3–4 × 0.8 mm, 10‑ribbed, truncate at both ends, brown, puberulent. Pappus capillary, silky, white, 8–9 mm, easily shed off individually.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1425; S. Y. Hu 10072 (CUHK); T. W. Lau 0072 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Habenaria ciliolaris Kraenzl. 毛葶玉鳳花
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(2): 169. 1892, et Orch. Gen. Sp. 1: 367. 1898; FKH 270. 1912; FRPS 17: 462, pl. 76: 1–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 914. 2000; FGD 7: 373, fig. 191. 2006; FOC 25: 155. 2009.

Perennial terrestrial herb requiring winter resting underground, to 30 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves basal, ovate or lanceolate, 8–12 × 3 cm. Flowers white or greenish-white, occasionally washed pink; 6 15 terminal to a raceme, 30 cm; rachis pedicels and ovary pilose; dorsal sepal ovate, 6–9 mm, acute or obtuse, lateral sepals ovate, recurved, 10 mm; petals erect, lanceolate, 6–7 mm; lip 3-lobed, the lateral one filiform; ovary pilose and stellate.

Locality: Hong Kong Peak. HK sheet 7137.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Hillslopes or shaded places of forests. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Ford (K, holotype) from Little Hong Kong in 1884.

Habenaria coultousii Barretto 香港玉鳳花
Orchadian 7(1): 10, fig. 1. 1981; FRPS 17: 450. 1999; FOC 25: 152. 2009.

Perennial herb 15–45 cm tall, requiring a resting winter period underground. Leaves 3–4, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–5.2 × 0.8–1.2 cm. Raceme 2–9-flowered; scape glabrous. Flowers white, 1.5–2 cm; petals oblique ovate; lip trilobate, 9–12 × 1.5 mm, spur pale yellow-green, 2–2.4 cm, longer than ovary and pedicel together; column greenish white; pollinia 2, yellow, viscidia exposed; rostellum erect, 1.5 mm, glands conical. Capsules 2.5–2.9 cm.

Locality: Violet Hill, Tai Tam. HK sheet 34048.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests along streams, alt. 300 m. Flowering: Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by B. Coultous from Violet Hill in 1978. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Habenaria dentata (Sw.) Schltr. 鵝毛玉鳳花（齒片鷺蘭）
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. Beih. 4: 125. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 33, fig. 9. 1977; FRPS 17: 472, pl. 78. 2. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 915. 2000; FGD 7: 375. 2006; FOC 25: 157. 2009.
Orchis dentata Sw., Kongl. Vetensk. Acad. Handl. 21: 207. 1800.
Habenaria miersiana Champ. ex Benth., J. Bot. Kew Misc. 7: 37. 1855; FHK 363. 1861; FKH 270. 1912.

Perennial herb 25–50 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all cauline, the lowerest one ovate, 5 × 3 cm, apex acute; the upper ones elliptic-lanceolate, 10–15 × 2–4 cm, acute to acuminate at apex. Flowers white, in terminal spikes consisting of 8–20 flowers; sepals papillose along margin, the dorsal one ovate, 12–13 mm; lateral sepals spreading, oblique-ovate; petals small, falcate-lanceolate, 11 × 2.5 mm; lip 3-lobed, spur 4 cm; column broad; anther with divergent thecae; pollinia 2; ovary clavate, 2 cm, papillose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. K. Mark 24(2821) (CUHK); P. S. Choi 5.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; Nepal, Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Japan.
Ecology: Hillsides. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimens of Habenaria miersiana (Champion 336, K) was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak in Sep. 1847 and 1848.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimens of Habenaria miersiana (Champion 336, K) was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak in Sep. 1847 and 1848.

records.text:
Habenaria leptoloba Benth. 細裂玉鳳花（天使蘭、仙子蘭）
FHK 362. 1861; FKH 270. 1912; FRPS 17: 483. 1999; FOC 25: 159. 2009.

Perennial herb 25 cm tall, requiring winter rest; underground tubers ellipsoidal, ca. 2 cm long and 8 mm thick. Leaves basal and subcauline, oblong-lanceolate, 6–8 cm, the next two linear-lanceolate, 10–14 × 1–1.7 cm, acuminate and acute. Flowers light yellowgreen, 6–14 on a terminal raceme; pedicels 1–2 mm; dorsal sepal ovate, 3.5 mm, obtuse, lateral sepals oblique-ovate; petals obliqueovate, 4 mm; lip plane, spur calcarate; column deeply notched at apex; anther with widely separate thecae; pollinia 2; ovary cylindrical, 7–8 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Aberdeen, Ma On Shan, Fanling. K. K. Mark 19(2765) (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1181 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2521.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Wet places near streams. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by C. Harland and H. F. Hance from Hong Kong Island before 1857. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Habenaria linguella Lindl. 坡參
Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 325. 1835; FHK 362. 1861; FRPS 17: 467, pl. 80: 1–5. 1999; FGD 7: 372. 2006; FOC 25: 156. 2009.
Habenaria acuifera auct. non Lindl.: FKH 270. 1912.

Perennial herb up to 45–60 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all cauline; leaf blade linear-lanceolate; 7.5–9.5 × 0.7–1.4 cm, amplexicaul at base, apex acute. Flowers bright sulphur-yellow, in a spike of 10–35 flowers; dorsal sepal ovate, 4 × 3.5 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals spreading side-wide, oblique-ovate, 4 × 2 mm; spur of lip 2.7 cm, column broad-triangular, 4 mm wide; pollinia 2; ovary clavate, 1.7 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Fanling, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 10706, 10784 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 254.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Moist grassy slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.

Habenaria reniformis (D. Don) Hook. f. 腎葉玉鳳花
Fl. Brit. India 6: 152. 1894; FKH 270. 1912; FHN 4: 192. 1977; FRPS 17: 436. 1999; FGD 7: 374. 2006; FOC 25: 149. 2009.
Listera reniformis D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal 28. 1825.
Aopla reniformis Lindl., Bot. Reg. 20: t. 1701. 1834; FHK 363. 1861.

Perennial herb with a winter resting period, 18–20 cm tall at flowering time; underground tubers, 1 cm long, 7–8 mm thick. Leaves 2, basal, lying flat on the ground; the lower one larger, 2.5 cm. Flowers green-yellow, 3 to 8 in a terminal raceme; pedicels 2–3 mm; dorsal sepal ovate, 6 × 3 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals ovate, 6 × 2.5 mm, acute; petals linear-falcate, connivent with the dorsal sepal; lip yellow-green, lanceolate, 6 mm, 3-lobed; column V-shaped at apex; anther with 2 subparallel thecae; pollinia 2; ovary 1.2 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1445; HK sheet 27749, 34221.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.

Habenaria rhodocheila Hance 橙黃玉鳳花（紅人蘭）
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. ser. 5. 5: 243. 1856; FKH 270. 1912; FRPS 17: 470, pl. 79: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 374. 2006; FOC 25: 157. 2009.

Perennial herb 20–25 cm tall, with a winter resting stage underground. Leaves all cauline; the lowerest one ovate or oblong, 4–8 × 1.5–3 cm; the middle one oblong-elliptic, 8–15 × 1.7–3 cm, acute at apex. Flower coral red; racemes consisting of 5–10 flowers on scape of 12–15; dorsal sepal cucullate, 1 cm; petals linear; spur 3.5–4 cm; anther with 2 parallel thecae; ovary 9 mm. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Mount Parker, Aberdeen, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun Reservoir, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ho Chung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 10738A (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1153 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1739.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Rocks on the banks of streams. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hackelochloa granularis (L.) Kuntze 球穗草
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 776. 1891; FHN 4: 465, fig. 1252. 1977; FFJ 6: 257, fig. 227. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 278, pl. 70: 1–3, 79: 2. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 549, pl. 231. 2000; FOC 22: 647. 2006; FGD 9: 485, fig. 256. 2009.
Cenchrus granularis L., Mant. Pl. 2: 575. 1771.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, erect, branched, 20–60(–100) cm tall, glabrous or sparsely hispid. Leaf sheaths loose, usually shorter than internode, papillose-hispid; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.4–1 cm, coarsely hispid, base ± cordate, apex subacute; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, margins ciliate. Racemes lower part usually included in terminal sheaths, rachis-joint and pedicel grown together. Sessile spikelet hemispherical, usually cream-coloured at maturity; lower glume leathery, hemispherical, coarsely reticulate-rugose, pits shallow and separated by broad rounded ribs; upper glume thicken membranous, hyaline, appressed to the cavity formed by rachis-joint and pedicel, 3-veined; lower lemma hyaline; upper lemma hyaline; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet ovate, glumes with prominent green veins and whitish wings.

Locality: Fanling, Po Toi Islands. Y. W. Lam 1047; HK sheet 15312.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; spread throughout the tropics.
Ecology: Farmlands, open grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Halophila beccarii Asch. 貝克喜鹽草
Nuov. Giorn. Bot. Ital. 3: 302. 1871; Fl. Males., Ser. I, 5(4): 411. 1957; FRPS 8: 188, pl. 74. 1992; FTW ed. 2, 5: 15. 2000; Kuo & den Hartog in Short & Coles, Global Seagrass Research Methods 50. 2001; FGD 6: 300, fig. 169. 2005; Yip & Lai, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 44(4): 460. 2006; FOC 23: 102. 2010.

Marine herb. Thin rhizomes with 2 scales covering the base of the erect stem bearing a group of 4–10 leaves at the top. Blades lanceolate, up to 13 mm long, 1–2 mm wide, with pointed apex but lacking cross-veins. Female flowers with 2 styles, 10–15 mm long. Fruits ellipsoidal to ovoid, 4–5 mm by 1.2 mm. Seeds globose, 1.2 × 1 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam Bay, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai. HK sheet 33274, 33275, 39064.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Indo-Pacific region.
Ecology: Coastal mudflats. Flowering: May.
Notes: The lack of cross-veins clearly distinguishes this species from other Halophila species. The species is usually associated with mangrove communities and often exposed at low tide (Kuo & den Hartog, 2001), and has high fecundity and rapid rhizome extension rates so that it can colonize some areas in very short time and disappear quickly when unfavourable conditions come (Fong, Asian Marine Biology 16: 109 – 121. 1999).

Halophila minor (Zoll.) Hartog 小喜鹽草
Flora Males., Ser. I, 5(4): 410. 1957; FRPS 8: 188, pl. 73: 8. 1992; Kuo & den Hartog in Short & Coles, Global Seagrass Research Methods, 50. 2001; FGD 6: 301. 2005; Yip & Lai, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 44(4): 459. 2006; FOC 23: 102. 2010.
Lemnopsis minor Zoll., Syst. Verz. 1: 75. 1854.
Halophila lemnopsis Miq., Fl. Ind. Bat. 3: 230, fig. 176. 1856.
Halophila ovata auct. non Gaudich.: Hodgkiss & Morton, Mem. HK Nat. Hist. Soc. 13: 28–32. 1978; Check List HK Plants 73. 1978; 77. 1993 [quoad specim. May 1978, Morton s.n. (HK sheet 33276); 23 Jun 1971, Thrower s.n. (HK sheet 30426)].

Marine herb. Leaf blades ovate, 6–12 mm long, 3.5–6 mm wide with (4–)7–12 occasionally branched cross-veins, space between intramarginal veins and blade margin narrow. Dioecious. Male flowers with tepals l.5 mm long, anthers 2.5–3.5 mm long. Female flowers with 3 styles, 8–20 mm long. Fruits 2–3.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Ho Chung, To Kwa Peng, Hoi Ha, Tsam Chuk Wan, Sunny Bay. HK sheet 38542, 39894, 39895.
Distribution: Hainan, Nansha Islands; Indo-Pacific regions.
Ecology: Coastal mudflats. Flowering: Aug.
Notes: This species has recently been recorded on mudflats adjacent to mangroves (Kwok, Lam & Yip, HK Biodiversity No. 10: 16. 2005). This also represents the first locality of the species in continental China (Yip & Lai, 2006). A re-examination of herbarium specimens found that this species was also previously recorded as Halophila ovata (Check List HK Plants 73. 1978; 77. 1993). There is recent molecular evidence indicating potential divergence between H. minor and H. ovalis (Xu et al., Am. J. Bot.: e56 – e57. 2010).

Halophila ovalis (R. Br.) Hook. f. 喜鹽草
Fl. Tasm. 2: 25. 1858; Fl. Males., Ser. I, 5(4): 408. 1957; FRPS 8: 186, pl. 73: 1–7. 1992; K. F. Zhao & F. T. Li, Halophytes of China 320. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 15. 2000; Kuo & den Hartog in Short & Coles, Global Seagrass Research Methods 50. 2001; FGD 6: 301. 2005; Yip & Lai, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 44(4): 459. 2006; FOC 23: 101. 2010.
Caulinia ovalis R. Br., Prod. Fl. Nov. Holl. 1: 339. 1810.
Halophila minor auct. non (Zoll.) den Hartog: Xing et al., Mem. HK Nat. Hist. Soc. 23: 122. 2000.
Halophila ovata auct. non Gaudich.: FKH 257. 1912; Fong, Asian Marine Biology 16: 111. 1999.

Marine herb. Rhizome internodes and petiole up to 10 cm long. Leaf blade varies in shape from oblong-elliptic, spatulate, obovate, to ovate, rarely linear, 10–40 mm long, 5–20 mm wide, with 12–28 often branched cross-veins on either side of the midrib. Dioecious. Male flowers with tepals 3–5(–6) mm, anthers 1.5–2.5 mm long. Female flowers with 3 styles, 10–40 mm long. Fruits 3–6 mm in diam. Seeds subglobose.

Locality: Tai Tam Bay, Ho Chung, Lai Chi Wo, Wu Shek Kok, San Tau. Y. W. Lam 821; HK sheet 39897, 39898.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan, Nansha Islands; N Pacific, S Africa, Indo-Pacific, S Australia.
Ecology: Coastal mudflats on shallow beaches. Flowering: Aug.
Notes: The species is the most common seagrass in the tropical and subtropical regions of the Indo-West Pacific and inhabits various environments, resulting in considerable morphological variation (Kuo & den Hartog, 2001). Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Hamelia patens Jacq. 長隔木（希美利）
Enum. Syst. Pl. 16. 1760; FRPS 71(1): 390, pl. 103: 1 – 5. 1999; FYN 15: 194, pl. 39: 10 – 13. 2003; FGD 6: 191, fig. 101. 2005.

Shrubs, 1.5–4 m tall, many‑branched, all young parts cinereous‑pubescent. Branchlets, petioles and peduncles reddish. Leaves usually in whorls of 3 or 4; petioles 1.5–4.5 cm; stipules subulate, ca. 6 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblanceolate, 7–15(–20) × 4–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Cymes terminal, with 3–5 radiate branches; primary branches 2.5–4 cm, secondary branches 1.5–2 cm. Flowers arranged along one side of the ultimate branches. Pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, ca. 3 mm; lobes 5, triangular, ca. 1 mm. Corolla scarlet‑orange, tubular, ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous; tube 5‑ribbed, slightly enlarged at the base; lobes 5, ovate‑triangular, ca. 2 mm erect. Stamens 5, equal to the corolla‑tube; filaments 5–6 mm; anthers linear, 9–10 mm, with projected connective. Style 11–12; stigma clavate. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 991, 1945; L. T. Lo 152.
Distribution: Native to C America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep. It is a typical ornithophilous plant. The flowers are pollinated by humming birds in the New World. It does not set fruit in S China.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hedera helix L. 洋常春藤
Sp. Pl. 1: 202. 1753; D. A. Webb., Fl. Euro. 2: 314. 1968.

Evergreen scandent shrub, climbing or creeping, to 30 m or longer, glabrous, except for apex of young branches, pedicels and abaxial surface of calyx with greyish white stellate hairs. Leaves dimorphic, those on sterile branches narrowly to broadly triangular-ovate to nearly reniform in outline, 7–15 cm in diam., palmately 3–5-lobed, base usually cordate to truncate, dark green adaxially, veins often light colored; those on flowering branches narrowly ovate to rhombic, 6–10 × 2–12 cm, entire, base truncate to cuneate. Umbels globose, usually several forming a raceme on a slender peduncle. Petals 5, 3–5 mm, yellowish white. Fruit black, globose, ca. 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2377; S. P. Lau 83, 84.
Distribution: N Africa, Europe, W Asia, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Climbing on rocks, walls or trunks.
Uses: Ornamental

Hedychium coronarium J. König 薑花
Observ Bot. 3: 73. 1783; FRPS 16(2): 26. 1981; FGD 2: 402. 1991; FOC 24: 372. 2000.

Pseudostems usually 1–1.5 m. Leaves sessile; ligule 2–3 cm, membranous; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 20–40 × 4.5–8 cm, base acute, apex long acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially finely pubescent or thinly hairy. Spikes ellipsoidal, 10–20 × 4–8 cm; bracts imbricate, ovate, 4.5–5 × 2.5–4 cm, 2–3-flowered. Flowers white, fragrant. Calyx ca. 4 cm, split on 1 side. Corolla tube ca. 8 cm, slender; lobes lanceolate, ca. 5 cm, central one spatulate, apex mucronate. Lateral staminodes oblonglanceolate, ca. 5 cm. Labellum white, pale yellow at base, obcordate, 4–6 × 4–6 cm, apex 2-cleft. Filament ca. 3 cm; anther ca. 1.5 cm. Ovary sericeous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2086, 2421.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Sichuan, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Hedyotis acutangula Champ. ex Benth. 金草（方骨草）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 171. 1852; FHK 148. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FHN 3: 303. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 46, pl. 9: 5 – 9. 1999; FGD 6: 123. 2005.
Oldenlandia acutangula (Champ. ex Benth.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial herbs, somewhat shrubby, 25–60 cm tall, glabrous. Stems woody at base; branches very acutely quadrangular, or even 4‑winged. Stipules ovate or triangular, 3–5 mm, margin entire or with minute glandular teeth. Leaves opposite, leathery, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate; midvein distinct; lateral veins and reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, sessile, numerous, in loose dichotomous or trichotomous cymes, forming a terminal oblong or corymbose panicle. Peduncles 1.5–4(–6.5) cm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth ovate, shorter than the tube. Corolla white, tube 2.2–3 mm, slightly expanded at throat, upper part tomentose inside; the lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ± equal to the tube. Stamens attached to the top of the corolla‑tube, included; filaments very short or almost wanting. Ovary inferior; style equal to the corolla; stigma bifid. Capsules obovate, 2–2.5 × 1–2 mm, top flat or slightly convex, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1809; Y. S. Lau 24; HK sheet 40066.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Hedyotis auricularia L. 耳草
Sp. Pl. 101. 1753; FHK 150. 1861; FKH 128. 1912; FHN 3: 299. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 37. 1999; FYN 14: 35. 2003; FGD 6: 119. 2005.
Oldenlandia auricularia (L.) F. Muell., Syst. Cons. Austral. Pl. 74. 1882.
Exallage auricularia (L.) Bremek., Verh. Kon. Ned. Akad. Wetensch., Afd. Natuurk., Tweede Sect. 48: 142. 1952.

Perennial herbs, 0.3–1 m tall. Stems almost erect or decumbent; young shoots ± quadrangular, densely hispidulous, or rarely glabrous in age. Stipules membranous, pubescent, united at the base into a short sheath, apex fringed with 5–7 bristle‑like lobes. Leaves opposite, subleathery; petioles ca. 2.5 mm; leaf blade lanceolate or elliptic, rarely ovate, 3–8 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate or slightly decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, adaxially smooth or scabrous, abaxially usually puberulent; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, conspicuous, obliquely ascending and in an acute angle with the midvein. Flowers 4‑merous, in axillary, densely flowered, head‑like cymes. Peduncles none. Pedicels ca. 1 mm or almost obsolete. Calyx‑tube pubescent, tube ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, 1–1.2 mm. Corolla white, tube 1–1.5 mm, hairy on throat; lobes lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, spreading. Stamens inserted in throat of corolla‑tube; filaments very short. Ovary inferior; style ca. 1 mm, hairy; stigma bifid. Capsules globose, 1.2–1.5 mm in diam., sparsely hispidulous or almost glabrous, indehiscent.

Locality: Kwai Chung, Shing Mun. Y. W. Lam 1018, 1545.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, India, Nepal, Thailand, Myanmar, Malesia, Australia and tropical Africa.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, thickets. Flowering: Jul. – Oct.; fruting: Sep. –Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis biflora (L.) Lam. 雙花耳草
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 272. 1792; FHN 3: 308. 1974; FTW 2, 4: 265, pl. 115. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 77. 1999; FYN 14: 45, pl. 7: 7 – 10. 2003; FGD 6: 135. 2005.
Oldenlandia paniculata L., Sp. Pl. 119. 1753; FHK 152. 1861; FKH 128. 1912.
Oldenlandia biflora L. Sp. Pl. 1: 119. 1753.

Annual slender herbs, glabrous except flowers. Stems diffuse or nearly erect, 10–50 cm tall, usually many‑branched. Stipules membranous, ca. 2 mm, united at the base, apex cuspidate. Leaves opposite, membranous; petioles 2–5 mm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic‑ovate, 1–4 × 0.3–1 cm, base cuneate or decurrent, apex acute or shortly acuminate; midvein plane adaxially, slightly raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, 3–8 together, in cymes on peduncles in the upper axils, sometimes paniculate. Peduncles slender, 8–18 mm. Pedicels slender, 6–10 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 1–1.2 mm; calyx‑teeth triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 1 mm, pilose in throat; lobes oblong, 1.2–1.5 mm. Stamens sessile, inserted in the tube, included. Ovary inferior; style 0.8–1 mm, hairy on the upper part; stigma bifid. Capsules turbinate, membranous, 2.5 – 3 mm in diam., with 2–4 prominent ribs, opening loculicidally when mature.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Wong Nai Chung Gap, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Au Mun, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2976; Y. W. Lam 689, 1478.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Polynesia.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Hedyotis bodinieri Lévl. 大帽山耳草
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 11(274 – 278): 64. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 49. 1999.
Oldenlandia bodinieri (Lévl.) Chun, Sunyatsenia 1: 310. 1934.
Hedyotis lancea auct. non Thunb. ex Maxim.: FKH 127. 1912.

Small shrubs, to 50 cm tall. Stems erect, oppositely branched; branchlets terete, puberulous. Stipules ovate triangular, ca. 2 mm, entire, with short hairs on the margin. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade elliptic to ovate elliptic, 2–3.5 × 0.8–2 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein slightly raised abaxially; lateral nerves 3–4 on each side of midvein, obscure. Cymes axillary, 3‑flowered or arranged in trichotomous cymes on axillary branchlets. Peduncles slender, 4–6 mm, puberulous. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm, puberulous. Flowers 4‑merous; calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.5 mm, calyx‑teeth ovate‑lanceolate, slightly longer than the tube. Corolla white, ca. 4 mm; tube slightly longer than lobes, glarous. Capsules ellipsoid.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. N. K. Chun 40663 (IBSC); HK sheet 39914, 39925.
Distribution: Known only from Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Jul–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen (E. Bodinier 1158) of this species was collected from Tai Mo Shan on 7 May 1895.

Hedyotis bracteosa Hance 大苞耳草
J. Bot. 23: 323. 1885; FKH 128. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 56, pl. 9: 1 – 4. 1999; FGD 6: 127. 2005.
Oldenlandia bracteosa (Hance) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial herbs, to 50 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, quadrangular. Stipules broadly triangular, 9–10 mm long, 7 mm at base, apex acute, margin revolute, with black glandular dots. Leaves opposite, or subverticillate on the upper part, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade papery, oblong to oblong‑lanceolate, 12–15 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, tip blunt; midvein depressed adaxially; lateral veins slender, 7 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein, prominent on both surfaces. Flowers 4‑merous, in axillary heads of 1.6 cm in diam. Peduncles 4–15 cm. Pedicels none. Bracts 4, broadly ovate, 1.5–2.5 × 1–1.8 cm, subtending the flowering heads. Calyx‑tube oblong, ca. 2 mm; calyx‑teeth ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2.5–3 × 1.8–2 mm, apex acute, sometimes ciliolate. Corolla white, ca. 5 mm; lobes lanceolate, equal to the tube, recurved outward. Stamens attached to the upper part of the corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers included. Ovary inferior; style exserted; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, ca. 3 × 2 mm, separating septicidally into 2 carpels when mature; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang, Bride's Pool, Mirror Pool, Pat Sin Leng. Y. S. Lau 2808, 3195; Y. W. Lam 829.
Distribution: Guangdong. Flowering: May –Dec.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Ecology: Forests.

Hedyotis consanguinea Hance 擬金草（紅花耳草）
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 221. 1862; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 47. 1999; FGD 6: 124. 2005.
Oldenlandia consanguinea (Hance) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Erect herbs, 30 – 40 cm tall. Stems slender, unbranched, slightly angular, glabrous, becoming greyish yellow when dry. Stipules oblong‑ovate, apex acuminate, fringed with minute, glandular teeth. Leaves opposite, subsessile; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong‑ovate, 2 – 3 × 0.8 – 1 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, glabrous, except on the depressed midvein on adaxial surface, margin revolute when dry; lateral veins 2 – 3 on each side of midvein, obscure. Cymes terminal or axillary, or paniculate, 3 – 4 cm. Peduncles 2 – 3 cm. Pedicels 0 – 2 mm. Flowers 4‑merous. Calyx‑tube ca. 1.2 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, ca. 0.8 mm. Corolla white or slightly tinged with purple, tube 2 – 2.5 mm; lobes lanceolate, equal to the tube. Stamens attached to the upper part of the corolla‑tube, exserted in short‑styled flowers, included in long‑styled flowers. Ovary inferior; style dimorphic (long or short); stigma bifid. Capsules ellipsoidal, ca. 3 × 2 mm, apex projecting from the calyx, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 5285; H. C. Tang 1253; K. L. Yip 4419.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, grasslands. Flowering: Feb. – Sep.; fruiting: May – Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis corymbosa (L.) Lam. 傘房花耳草
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 272. 1791; FHN 3: 307. 1974; FTW 2, 4: 267. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 72. 1999; FYN 14: 44. 2003; FGD 6: 133. 2005.
Oldenlandia herbacea DC., Prodr. 4: 425. 1830; FHK 151. 1861.
Oldenlandia corymbosa L., Sp. 1: 119. 1753; FKH 128. 1912.

Annual slender herbs, 10–50 cm tall. Stems diffuse, many‑branched; branches glabrous or sparsely pubescent on the edge of angles. Stipule membranous, sheathing, 1–1.5 mm, apex truncate, fringed with short bristle‑like teeth. Leaves opposite, almost sessile, membranous; leaf blade linear to linear lanceolate, 1–2.5 × 0.1–0.3 cm, narrowed at the base, apex acute, margin revolute when dry, scabrous on both surfaces or slightly puberulent on the midvein adaxially; midvein depressed adaxially, plane or slightly raised abaxially; lateral veins obsolete. Peduncles axillary, usually solitary and shorter than the leaves, bearing either a single flower or a 2–5‑flowered cyme. Pedicels filiform, 5–10 mm. Flowers 4‑merous. Calyx‑tube tubular, slightly pubescent, 1–1.2 mm; calyx‑teeth narrowly triangular, ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Corolla white or pink, tube 1.2–1.5 mm; lobes oblong, ca. 1 mm. Stamens inserted in the corolla‑tube; filaments very short. Ovary inferior; style 1.3 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules globular, 1.5–1.8 mm in diam., with minute calyx‑teeth in a ring around the apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 1; Y. S. Lau 1973; Y. W. Lam 908.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa and America.
Ecology: Wastelands, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis costata (Roxb.) Kurz 脈耳草
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal. 45: 135. 1876; FHN 3: 297. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 32, pl. 4: 1 – 8. 1999; FYN 14: 33, pl. 6: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 6: 117, fig. 51. 2005.
Spermacoce costata Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 10. 1814.

Perennial diffuse herbs, 30–50 cm tall, except for the flowers and fruits all parts sparsely covered with long hairs, which becoming golden yellow when dry. Stipules membranous, united at the base, apex truncate, fringed with several bristles. Leaves opposite, membranous; petioles 5 – 10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 5– 8 × 1.5–2.8 cm, base cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex acuminate; lateral veins slender, 4–5 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein. Flowers 4(–5)‑merous, in axillary, simple or compound cymes. Peduncles 5–12 mm. Pedicels very short or almost obsolete. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 0.5 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, ca. 1 mm, recurved outward. Corolla white or purplish, tube 1.2–1.5 mm, apex hairy; lobes oblong, ca. 1 mm. Stamens attached to the top of corolla‑tube; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style 1.2–1.5 mm, hairy on the upper half; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, 1–1.5 mm in diam., indehiscent.

Locality: Tung Chung, Tai Ho, San Tau, Pui O. Y. W. Lam 662, 799, 1248.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, India, Malesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis diffusa Willd. 白花蛇舌草
Sp. Pl. 1: 566. 1797; FHN 3: 307. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 267. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 75. 1999; FYN 14: 45, pl. 7: 4 – 6. 2003; FGD 6: 134. 2005.
Oldenlandia diffusa (Willd.) Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 11. 1814; FKH 128. 1912.
Oldenlandia herbacea L. var. uniflora Benth., FHK 150. 1861.

Annual diffuse herbs, 20–50 cm tall, glabrous throughout; branches slender, quadrangular. Stipules triangular, 1–2 mm, united at the base, apex aristate. Leaves opposite, membranous, sessile; leaf blade linear, 1–3 × 0.1–0.3 cm, narrowed at the base, apex acute, margin revolute when dry, adaxially smooth, abaxially sometimes scabrous; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, solitary or in pairs in axils of leaves. Pedicels 2–5 mm, rarely longer. Calyx‑tube tubular, ca. 1.5 mm; calyx‑teeth linear oblong‑lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, ciliate. Corolla white, tube 1.5–2 mm, glabrous; lobes ovate‑oblong, ca. 2 mm. Stamens inserted in the throat of the tube; filaments very short. Ovary inferior; style 2 – 3 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules membranous, depressed globular, 2–2.5 mm, in diam., opening loculicidally at apex.

Locality: Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Sai Kung, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 301, 2310; HK sheet 39827.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Anhui; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
