Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis effusa Hance 鼎湖耳草
J. Bot. 17: 11. 1879; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 44. 1999; FGD 6: 123, fig. 55. 2005.
Oldenlandia effusa (Hance) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial glabrous herbs. Stems erect, 0.5–1 m tall, woody at base. Stipules 2–3 mm, triangular or truncate but with a mucro at apex, margin entire. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 2–5 mm; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate, 4–9.5 × 2–4 cm, base subrounded or cuneate, apex acute, tip blunt; lateral veins slender, inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, in dichotomous cymes, forming terminal panicles to 10–15 cm long and 4–10 cm broad, branches divaricate and often zigzag. Peduncles slender, 2–4 cm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Calyx‑tube ovoid, ca. 0.7 mm; calyx‑teeth triangular, ca. 0.4 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 2 mm; the lobes lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, spreading or recurved,. Stamens inserted in the tube. Ovary inferior; style exserted; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, top flat, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Tung Chung, Tai O, Lung Chai, San Tau. Y. W. Lam 838, 1241, 1658.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Hedyotis hedyotidea (DC.) Merr. 牛白藤
Lingnan. Sci. J. 13: 48. 1934; FTW ed. 2, 4: 268, pl. 116. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 67, pl. 12: 1 – 6. 1999; FYN 14: 42. 2003; FGD 6: 131. 2005.
Hedyotis recurva Benth., Lond. J. Bot. 1: 486. 1842; FHK 148. 1861.
Hedyotis macrostemon Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 192. 1833; FKH 128. 1912.

Half‑climbing subshrubs, 1–3 m or longer. Stems and old branches terete or nearly so; young shoots quadrangular, pulverulent. Stipules 4–6 mm, apex truncate, fringed with 4–6 bristles. Leaves opposite, membranous or papery; petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑oblong, 4–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially scabrous, abaxially pubescent; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending, appressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Flowers 4‑merous, heterostylic, 10–20 together, in little umbels on short peduncles in the upper axils, the upper ones forming a terminal oblong panicle. Peduncles 1.5–2.5 cm, puberulent. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.5 mm; calyx‑teeth linear‑lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, recurved outward. Corolla white, tube ca. 2.5 mm; lobes lanceolate, 4–4.5 mm, spreading or recurved, sparsely pubescent on adaxial surface. Stamens included in long‑styled flowers, exserted in short‑styled flowers; filaments barbate at the base. Ovary inferior; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, ca. 3 × 2 mm, apex projecting from the calyx, separating septicidally in the upper part into 2 carpels; carpels opening loculicidally in 2 valves.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1401, 2191; Y. S. Lau 1322.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Hillslopes, forests and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis loganioides Benth. 粵港耳草
FHK 149. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 54. 1999; FGD 6: 126. 2005.
Oldenlandia loganioides (Benth.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial herbs, to 30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems ascending or erect; branches terete, obtusely angular, slightly compressed when young. Stipules ovate triangular, entire. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles ca. 4 mm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 2.5–5 × 1.4–3 cm, acute on both ends; midvein slightly raised abaxially; lateral veins 3 –5 on each side of midvein, obscure. Flowers 4‑merous, 10–20 together in trichotomous cymes. Peduncles 14–20 mm. Pedicels very short. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.5 mm; calyx‑teeth linear slightly shorter than the corolla. Corolla white, tube short and slender, glabrous. Capsules ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm long, crowned by the calyx‑lobes, the 2 carpels separating to the base, and opening wide by a fissure on the inner face.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung, Pat Sin Leng, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 630; Y. S. Lau 3256; Y. W. Lam 1400.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Notes: A syntype specimen was collected from Mount Gough, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford in 1858.

Hedyotis matthewii Dunn 疏花耳草
J. Bot. 47: 376. 1909; FKH 128. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 54, pl. 6: 7 – 10. 1999; FGD 6: 127. 2005.
Oldenlandia matthewii (Dunn) Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 312. 1934.

Perennial herbs 30–75 cm tall, except the flowers glabrous. Stems erect, ± woody at the base, lower part terete, upper part quadrangular. Stipules ovate triangular, ca. 2 mm, margin with minute, glandular teeth or deeply lobed. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles ca. 3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 4–8 × 1.5–4 cm, base acute or cuneate, apex long acuminate; lateral veins 3 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein, appressed adaxially; veinlets obscure. Flowers 4‑merous, in terminal or axillary dichotomous cymes. Peduncles 0.5–3 cm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate or obovate, ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, 2–2.2 mm, apex acute. Corolla white or tinged with purple, tube 2–2.5 mm; the lobes lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, recurved, tomentose on adaxial surface. Stamens attached to the corolla‑tube. Ovary inferior; style ca. 8 mm, exserted; stigma capitate. Capsules ellipsoidal, 3–4 mm long, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2578; HK sheet 30343.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr. –Dec.

Hedyotis pinifolia Wall. ex G. Don 松葉耳草
Gen. Hist. 3: 526. 1834; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 3: 60. 1880; FKH 128. 1912; FHN 3: 301. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 43, pl. 4: 9 – 14. 1999; FYN 14: 36. 2003; FGD 6: 122. 2005.

Annual diffuse herbs, 10–25 cm tall. Stems many‑branched; branchlets slender, sharply 4‑angular, turning dark brown when dry. Stipules united into a short sheath at the base, apex truncate, fringed with 2–4 bristles. Leaves whorled or opposite, sessile; leaf blade linear, 1.2–4 × 0.1–0.2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin revolute when dry, both surfaces scabrous, rarely pubescent; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, 3–10 together, in axillary or terminal glomerules. Peduncles none. Pedicels ca. 1 mm. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1–1.5 mm, sparsely hispidulous; calyx‑teeth subulate, ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Corolla white, tube 4–4.2 mm; lobes oblong, equal to the tube. Stamens inserted in the throat of the tube; filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style ca. 9 mm; stigma 2‑lobed; lobes linear, ca. 1 mm, spreading. Capsules ovoid, 2.5–3 × 1.5–2 mm, sparsely hispidulous, opening at apex when mature.

Locality: Aberdeen, Shek O, Tsim Shan, Lamma Island, Lantau Island, Po Toi Islands. Y. W. Lam 772, 1061; K. Y. Tam 147.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Nepal, Vietnam, Malesia.
Ecology: Open fields, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis shiuyingiae T. Chen 秀英耳草
Harv. Pap. Bot. 13(2): 283, fig. 1 – 2 A – C, E. 2008.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, erect, 15 – 35 cm tall, glabrous. Stems slightly quadrangular, internodes 1–3.5(–4.5) cm. Stipules triangular, 4–8 × 5–10 mm, acute at apex, with dense trichomes at margins. Leaves decussate, thick papery, subleathery when dry; petioles 5–10 mm or leaves subsessile; leaf blade broadly lanceolate or obovate‑lanceolate, (2–)3–12.5(–19) × (1.4–)2 – 4.5(–8) cm, base decurrent and cuneate, apex acuminate or acute; midvein prominent abaxially, flattened adaxially or slightly impressed; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous abaxially, slightly conspicuous adaxially. Flowers 4‑merous, heterostylic, shortly pedicellate, crowded in head‑like clusters, these clusters 2–3 together forming a terminal compound cymes of 12–35 cm, terminal, or sometimes 2 or more in uppermost leaf axils. Peduncles ca. 10 cm; lower bracts leaf‑like, becoming smaller upward and finally subulate. Calyx lobes 2.5–3 mm, subulate. Corolla purple outside; tube narrowly infundibuliform, 4– 5 mm; abaxially glabrous, adaxially white hairy; lobes 4, reflexed, 2–2.5 × 1.5–1.8 mm; stamens 4, included; long‑style ca. 5 mm, short‑style 1–2 mm. Capsules globular, ca. 2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Shing Mun Reservoir, Tai Po, Hoi Ha, Pat Sin Leng, Pin Fung Shan, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 2495, Y. S. Lau 422, L. T. Lo 612.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Thickets and forests on wet rocks. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen (T. Chen et al. 2007004, HK, holotype; A, SZG, isotypes) was collected from Tai Po in 2007. The species was reported previously as Hedyotis yangchunensis W. C. Ko & Zhang (陽春耳草) (Check List HK Plants 265. 2002; 91. 2004).

Hedyotis tenelliflora Blume 纖花耳草
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 971. 1826; FKH 128. 1912; FHN 3: 300. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 271, pl. 118. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 41. 1999; FYN 14: 36. 2003; FGD 6: 121. 2005.
Oldenlandia angustifolia Benth., FHK 151. 1861.
Hedyotis angustifolia Cham. & Schltdl., Linnaea 4: 153. 1829.

Perennial herbs. Stems diffuse or decumbent, 15–40 cm or longer; branchlets quadrangular, glabrous. Stipules 3– 6 mm, united at the base, slightly pubescent, with several bristle‑like teeth. Leaves opposite, almost sessile, thin‑leathery; leaf blade linear to linear lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.2–0.4 cm, base cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, in dry state margin ± revolute, adaxial surface turning black, covered with rounded, pellucid minute scales, abaxial surface paler, smooth; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, sessile, 2–3 clustered in axils of leaves. Calyx‑tube obovate, ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth linear‑lanceolate, ca. 1.8 mm, ciliate. Corolla white, tube ca. 2 mm; lobes oblong, 1–1.5 mm. Stamens inserted in the throat of corolla‑tube; filaments ca. 1.5 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style ca. 4 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules ovoid or nearly globular, 1.5–2 mm in diam., crowned by the linear lanceolate calyx‑teeth.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ping Shan Chai, Ng Tung Chai, Po Toi Islands. H. C. Tang 1407; Y. S. Lau 1661; Y. W. Lam 898.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Abandoned farmlands, margins of fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis uncinella Hook. & Arn. 長節耳草
Bot. Beechey Voy. 192. 1833; FHK 149. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FHN 3: 304. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 271, pl. 119. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 59. 1999; FYN 14: 38. 2003; FGD 6: 128. 2005.
Hedyotis borrerioides Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 171. 1852.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect, quadrangular, glabrous, or rarely puberulent. Stipules triangular, 11–12 mm, united at the base, apex with several teeth or lobes. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles very short or almost obsolete; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3.5–7.5 × 1–3 cm, base obtuse or attenuate and decurrent, apex acuminate, glabrous or sparsely puberulent on the veins of adaxial surface, rarely puberulent on both surfaces; lateral veins slender, 4–5 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein; reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, densely crowded in terminal or axillary heads of 12–15 mm in diam., subsessile. Pedicels obsolete or very short. Calyx‑tube subglobular, ca. 3 mm; calyx‑teeth oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, apex obtuse, glabrous or ciliolate. Corolla white or purple, tube ca. 3 mm, tomentose at throat; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, shorter than the tube. Stamens attached to the top of corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers included. Ovary inferior; style ca. 2 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules broadly ovate, 1.8–2 mm in diam., top flat, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Au Mun, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan. S. P. Lau 30; L. T. Lo 300, 456.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; India.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Hedyotis borrerioides was collected by J. G. Champion from “Chuckchow” (Stanley), Hong Kong Island, between 1847 and 1850.

Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Hedyotis borrerioides was collected by J. G. Champion from “Chuckchow” (Stanley), Hong Kong Island, between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Hedyotis vachellii Benth. 香港耳草（華氏耳草）
FHK 148. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 49. 1999.

Perennial herbs, 30–40 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems woody at base; branches terete or scarcely angular. Stipules triangular, apex acute, ciliolate. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 2 mm, or almost obsolete in the upper leaves; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, 4–7 × 1–2 cm, acute at both ends; midvein slightly raised adaxially, broad and plane abaxially; lateral veins almost invisible. Flowers 4‑merous, in dichotomous or trichotomous cymes, forming a terminal oblong or corymbose panicle to 4–4.5 cm long and ca. 3.5 cm broad. Peduncles ca. 2 cm, primary rays ca. 1.5 cm, secondary rays 0.8–1 cm. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 0.5 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, equal to the tube, spreading, apex obtuse. Corolla white, tube ca. 3 mm, pilose inside; the lobes ovate‑triangular, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens inserted in the tube, exserted. Ovary inferior; style included; stigma thick and bifid. Capsules subglobose, ca. 1.8 mm in diam., separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Fanling, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 11162; P. S. Choi 96; Y. W. Lam 2209.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Valleys. Flowering: Mar. –Dec.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Hedyotis verticillata (L.) Lam. 粗葉耳草（輪葉耳草）
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 271. 1792; Hara & al., Enum. Flow. Pl. Nepal. 2: 202. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 271. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 42. 1999; FYN 14: 37. 2003; FGD 6: 121. 2005.
Hedyotis hispida Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 23. 1786.

Annual diffuse herbs, 25–30 cm tall. Branches often decumbent, sparsely or densely hirtellous. Stipules united with petioles into a sheath, apex almost truncate, fringed with bristles. Leaves opposite, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade papery or thinly leathery, elliptic, ovate‑elliptic or lanceolate, 2.5–6.5 × 0.6–2 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, hispidulous on both surfaces, margin revolute when dry; midvein depressed adaxially, raised; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, in axillary glomerules. Peduncles and pedicels none. Calyx‑tube obconical, ca. 1 mm, hispidulous; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 2 mm; lobes lanceolate, 1.8–2 mm, barbate at apex. Stamens inserted in throat of the tube; filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style 4 – 4.5 mm; stigma capitate. Capsules ovoid, 1.5–2 mm in diam., hispidulous, opening only at apex when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Ta Kwu Ling, Lantau Island, Peng Chau. Y. S. Lau 1961; Y. W. Lam 874, 909.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Helianthus annuus L. 向日葵
Sp. Pl. 2: 904. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 285. 1966; FRPS 75: 358. 1979; FGD 8: 118, fig. 58. 2007.

Stout annual herbs; stems erect, 1–2(–3) m tall, usually not branched, scabrous to hirsute, hair much denser near the head. Leaves mostly alternate except the lowest; petioles 2–17 cm or longer, not winged; leaf blade ovate to cordate‑ovate, 4.5–18 × 2–15 cm, or much larger, apex acute or acuminate, 3‑nerved, margin coarsely serrate, both surfaces scabrous. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 10–25(–30) cm across, solitary at terminal, usually nodding. Involucres dish‑like, densely hairy at base; phyllaries 2 – 3‑seriate, foliaceous, ovate to lanceolate, 1.5– 7 cm, apex attenuate and long‑caudate, pilose. Receptacle nearly flat; paleae enfolding the cypselae, trilobed with the midlobe cuspidate, margin of all lobes pubescent. Ligulate florets 1‑seriate, corolla yellow, limb spreading, elliptic‑oblong, apex acute and entire, tube minute and densely pubescent, infertile. Tubular florets numerous, purplish black, reddish black or brownish black, corolla 5 hairy lobes apically, basally swollen as a ball and densely pubescent. Anther bases sagittate, apical appendages ovate‑acute, exserted; stylar branches short and hairy. Cypselae obovate or ovate‑oblong, white or greyish, black‑lineolate, about 9 × 4–8 mm, slightly compressed, pilose near the summit. Pappus 2 cuspidate scales, deciduous.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7648 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 205 (CUHK); H. Y. Yeung 171 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to N America, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Food (oil/fat), ornamental.

Helicia cochinchinensis Lour. 小果山龍眼（越南山龍眼）
Fl. Cochinch. 83. 1790; FHK 295. 1861; FKH 226. 1912; FHN 1: 444, fig. 244. 1964; FGD 1: 97. 1987; FRPS 24: 21, pl. 4: 5. 1988; FOC 5: 197. 2003.

Evergreen tree, 4 – 15 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves alternate, thin-leathery or papery; petioles 0.5 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong, obovate-elliptic or elliptic, 5 – 11 × 2.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate, ± decurrent to the petiole, apex acuminate, margin entire or coarsely serrate in the upper part. Racemes axillary, 10–14 cm. Flowers white or light yellow. Pedicels 3–4 mm, in pairs and often united to the base. Perianth tubular, 1 – 1.2 cm. Hypogynous scales 4, free or slightly united at middle, less than 1/2 of the ovary. Nuts ellipsoidal, 12–15 × 8–10 mm, blue-black or black.

Locality: Mount Parker, Happy Valley, Lam Tsuen. N. K. Chun 40205; Y. S. Lau 2755; HK sheet 24784.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering: Jun. –Oct.; fruiting: Nov. –Mar. of the following year.

Helicia kwangtungensis W. T. Wang 廣東山龍眼
Act. Phytotax. Sin. 5: 297. 1956; FGD 1: 98, fig. 108. 1987; FRPS 24: 19. 1988; FOC 5: 197. 2003.

Evergreen tree, to 10 m tall, branches and leaves glabrous; buds brown pubescent when young. Leaves alternate, firmly papery; petioles 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade oblong, obovate or elliptic, 10–26 × 6–12 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, shortly acuminate or obtuse, margin entire or sparsely serrate on the upper part, lateral veins inconspicuous. Racemes axillary, 15–20 cm, densely brown pubescent. Flowers yellowish. Pedicels ca. 2 mm, in pairs and often united at the base. Perianth tubular, 1.2–1.4 cm, sparsely puberulous abaxially. Hypogynous scales 4, free or slightly united at the base. Nuts subglobose, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. S. C. Ng 2120; Y. S. Lau 3026; HK sheet 24681.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Jun. – Jul.

Helicia reticulata W. T. Wang 網脈山龍眼

Act. Phytotax. Sin. 5: 300, pl. 56. 1956; FGD 1: 98. 1987; FRPS 24: 19, pl. 5: 1– 3. 1988; FOC 5: 196. 2003.

Helicia erratica auct. non Hook. f.: FKH 226. 1912.


Evergreen shrub or tree, 2 – 10 m tall, glabrous except the bud and inflorescence brown pubescent when young. Leaves alternate, leathery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong, ovate-oblong or obovate, 7 – 27 × 3 – 9 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin sparsely serrate or serrulate, secondary and tertiary veins raised on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 10 – 15 cm. Flowers yellowish white. Pedicels ca. 3 mm, in pairs and often united at base. Perianth tubular, 1.3 – 1.5 cm. Hypogynous scales 4, free or slightly united at base. Nuts ellipsoidal, 1.6–1.8 × 1.2 – 1.5 cm.


Locality: Aberdeen, Lan Nai Wan, Pat Sin Leng, Ng Tung Chai, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1479, 3035; HK sheet 40247.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.

Ecology: Thin forests in ravines or on slopes. Flowering: May–Jul.

Helicteres angustifolia L. 山芝麻
Sp. Pl. 963. 1753; FHK 37. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 80. 1965; FGD 1: 141. 1987; FRPS 49(2): 156. 1984.

Small shrub, to 1 m tall. Branchlets grey-green pubescent. Petioles 5–7 mm; leaves narrow-oblong or linear-lanceolate, 3.5–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base rounded, apex obtuse or acute, glabrous or nearly so adaxially, grey white or yellowish stellate-tomentose abaxially, sometimes mixed setae. Cymes 2–several-flowered; bracteoles 4; calyx 4 mm, stellate-pubescent, 5-lobed; lobes triangular ; petals 5, reddish or purple, with 2 appendages at base; stamens 10; staminal column 10-cleft, with 1-celled anther; staminodes 5; ovary 5-locular, hairy. Capsules straight, ovoid-oblong, 12–20 × 7–8 mm, apex acute, densely stellate hairy and mixed with long tangled hairs. Seeds brown with small elliptic spots.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 595; Y. S. Lau 2202; K. L. Yip 4381.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy slopes or thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

Heliotropium indicum L. 大尾搖
Sp. Pl. 1: 130. 1753; FHK 235. 1861; FKH 177. 1912; FGZ 568, fig. 303; 1956; FHN 3: 457, fig. 855. 1974; FTW 4: 403. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 29. 1990; FFJ 4: 509, fig. 405. 1989; FOC 16: 341. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 396. 1998.

Annual herb, 20–50 cm tall. Stems erect, stout, multibranched, spreading strigose. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petiole 2–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 3–9 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or truncate, decurrent to petiole, apex acute, margin undulate, pubescent or strigose on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, impressed adaxially, spreading hirsute or strigose. Cymes solitary, scorpioid, unbranched, 5–15 cm, ebracteate. Flowers sessile, crowded. Calyx lobes lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, strigose. Corolla light blue or blue‑purple, salverform, 3–4 mm, ca. 1 mm wide at base; throat evidently contracted; limb 2–2.5 mm wide; lobes suborbicular, ca. 1 mm wide, margin crispate. Anthers narrowly ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm, inserted ca. 1 mm above base. Ovary glabrous. Style ca. 0.5 mm; stigma conical, pubescent. Fruit glabrous or nearly so, ribbed, 3–3.5 mm, deeply 2‑cleft into mericarps, each mericarp divided into two 1‑seeded pyrenes.

Locality: Lai Chi Wo, Butterfly Beach, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau. Y. W. Lam 1544, 1549; HK sheet 41517.
Distribution: Yunnan, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Hills, river banks, open wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Heliotropium strigosum Willd. (細葉天芥菜) was previously recorded from Lantau Island (FKH 177. 1912) and differs in its leaf blade being small and linear‑lanceolate.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Heliotropium strigosum Willd. (細葉天芥菜) was previously recorded from Lantau Island (FKH 177. 1912) and differs in its leaf blade being small and linear‑lanceolate.

records.text:
Helixanthera parasitica Lour. 離瓣寄生（五瓣寄生）
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 142. 1790; FYN 3: 355, pl. 103: 1–2. 1983; FGD 1: 218. 1987; FRPS 24: 96. 1988; FOC 5: 225. 2003.
Loranthus pentapetalus Roxb., Fl. Ind. 2: 211. 1824; FKH 229. 1912; FHN 2: 462. 1965.

Shrub to 1.5 m tall. Branches and leaves glabrous. Leaves opposite; petiole 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 5–12 × 3–4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute to acuminate, lateral veins conspicuous on both surfaces. Racemes solitary or paired, axillary, 40–60-flowered, 5–10(–30) cm; bracts subovate or ovate-triangular, 1–1.5 mm. Flowers 5-merous. Pedicel 1–2 mm. Calyx ellipsoidal, 1.5–2 mm, limb annular, ca. 0.5 mm, entire or 5-denticulate. Corolla red, pink, or yellowish; petals (4–)6–8 mm, reflexed from above basal keels, dark brown or greyish white papillose, basal 1/3–1/2 abruptly expanded into 5 prominent semicircular keels at buds. Filaments 1–2.5 mm; anthers 4-celled, 1–1.5 mm. Style cylindrical, 5-angled, constricted in middle, 3–6 mm; stigma capitate. Fruit red, ellipsoidal, ca. 6 × 4 mm, papillose.

Locality: Fanling, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung. P. S. Choi 385; Y. W. Lam 29; HK sheet 39457.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, on trees of Fagaceae, Cinnamomum camphora and Schima superba. Flowering: Jan. – Jul.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hemarthria compressa (L. f.) R. Br. 扁穗牛鞭草
Prodr. 207. 1810; FHN 4: 464, fig. 1251. 1977; FFJ 6: 255, fig. 224. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 262, pl. 65: 4–6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 551, pl. 232. 2000; FOC 22: 642. 2006; FGD 9: 480, fig. 251. 2009.
Rottboellia compressa L. f., Suppl. Pl. 114. 1782 ["1781"]; FKH 321. 1912.
Hemarthria fasciculata auct. non (Lam.) Kunth: FHK 418. 1861.

Perennial herb, with horizontal rhizomes. Culms erect, 60–150 cm. Leaf sheaths glabrous or hairy along mouth, often shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, 2–15 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous, base rounded, margins scabrous; ligule 0.3–1 mm. Racemes solitary or few per node, sometimes several aggregated. Sessile spikelet sunken in a cavity formed by the adnation of the rachis and the pedicel, long ovate, with a distinct callus of 1–2 mm; lower glume ovate-lanceolate, leathery, flat or subconvex on abaxial surface, marginally keeled, apex acute or slightly obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, adnate to rachis, equalling lower glume; lower floret absent to lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline membranous. Pedicellate spikelet lanceolate, as long as or slightly longer than sessile spikelet, lower glume ovate-lanceolate, herbaceous; upper glume boat-shaped, completely adnate to rachis cavity, acuminate-caudate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Wu Kau Tang. Y. S. Lau 2281; Y. W. Lam 892, 2177.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Nei Mongol, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, SW Asia (Iraq).
Ecology: Farmlands and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Hemisteptia lyrata (Bunge) Bunge 泥胡菜
Dorp. Jahrb. Litt. 1: 222. 1833; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 287. 1966; FRPS 78(1): 138. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 989. 1998; FGD 8: 253, fig. 154. 2007.
Cirsium lyratum Bunge, Enum. Pl. Chin. Bor. 36. 1833.
Saussurea carthamoides Benth., FHK 168. 1861.
Saussurea affinis Spreng. ex DC., Prodr. 6: 538. 1838; FKH 149. 1912.

Annual herbs; stem 30–100 cm tall, striate, arachnoid‑tomentose hairy, branched apically. Radical leaves usually withered at anthesis. Lower and middle cauline leaves oblong to oblanceolate, 4–21 × 1.5–9 cm, adaxial surface green and glabrous, abaxial surface greyish white and densely tomentose, lyrately pinnatisect or sometimes the lower leaves not lobed, lateral lobes 2–6 pairs, variable in shape, elliptic, obovate, to oblanceolate, those near base smaller; apical lobe large, rhomboid, deltoid or ovate, apex acute, obtuse to rounded, leaf margin shallowly toothed or not; petioles long in the lowermost leaves, gradually shorter for leaves growing upward. Upper leaves few, linear to linear‑lanceolate, sessile. Capitula arranged as loose corymbs at stem terminal, rarely solitary. Involucres ovoid; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate; outer few layers triangular‑ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 1.5–4 × 1.3–1.5 mm, acute or acuminate, with purple‑red cristate appendages on abaxial side near the apex; middle layers ovate‑oblong to oblong, 4–7 × 1.2–1.3 mm, apex not crested; inner ones linear‑lanceolate to linear, 6 – 12 × 0.8 – 1 mm, acuminate and without appendages, tinged red. Florets purple to red, corolla 8.5–13 mm; upper limb 2.2 – 3 mm, deeply cleft into 5 linear lobes 2–2.5 mm; lower tube filiform, 6.5–10 mm. Cypselae oblong‑cuneate, 2.5 – 4 × 1 mm, brown or reddish‑brown, 13 – 16‑ribbed, apex obliquely truncate. Pappus white, in 2 rows; inner ones plumose, 6–9 mm, base connate and deciduous as a ring; outer 3–9 short scales, growing on one side.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Po, Fanling, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 3294; Y. W. Lam 191; S. Y. Hu 22790 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Xinjiang and Xizang; also in Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.

Heritiera littoralis Aiton 銀葉樹
Hort. Kew, 3: 546. 1789; FHK 36. 1861; FKH 49. 1912; FHN 2: 76. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 140. 1984; FGD 1: 133. 1987.

Evergreen tree. Branchlets white lepidote when young. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves leathery, oblong-lanceolate, elliptic or ovate, 10 –20 × 5 –10 cm, base obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, densely silvery-lepidote abaxially. Panicles axillary, manyflowered densely stellate-hairy and lepidote. Flowers red-brown; calyx campanulate, 4– 6 mm. Male flower: stamens 4– 5. Female flowers with 4–5 carpels; stigmas as many as carpels. Ripe carpels woody, yellow-brown, nut-like, ovoid, 6 × 3.5 cm, with a slightly projecting inner edge, and a strong projecting almost winged keel along the outer edge.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Yung Shue O, Lai Chi Wo. Y. W. Lam 683; Y. S. Lau 1698; H. C. Tang 1436.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, SE Asia, E Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Seashores. Flowering: Autumn.

Hetaeria abbreviata Lindl. 小片翻唇蘭（亮葉翻唇蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 481. 1840.
Rhomboda abbreviata (Lindl.) Ormerod, Orchadian 11: 329. 1995; FOC 25: 68. 2009.
Hetaeria cristata auct. non Blume: FKH 268. 1917; FRPS 17: 183, pl. 25: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 358, fig. 182. 2006; Check List HK Plants 378. 2002; 131. 2004.

Terrestrial herb; stems rhizome-like, lower part lying on ground, consisting of 6–7 internodes; the upright stem purple-green, including flowering portion up to 20 cm tall, usually lower. Leaves petiolate; petioles 1.5–3.5 cm, salmon-pink; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 5–6 × 2–2.3 cm, dark green with inconspicuous lateral veins. Flowers creamy white, 5–13 in a terminal spike; odd sepal ovate, 4 × 2 mm, apex acute, sparsely hairy; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 4 × 2.5 mm; petals forming a hood with the odd sepal over the column; lip uppermost, 4 mm, transparent and pink tinged, ovate, completely covered by lateral sepals, gibbose at base; apex truncate; column white, 1 mm, the front with 2 parallel wings, each with a large gland at apex; anther ovate; pollinia 2 on short caudicles; ovary glabrous, brown-red, 1 cm. Capsule oblong, 1 cm, dull red.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Po, Wang Shan Keuk, Sha Tau Kok. S. Y. Hu 12129, 12387A (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; NE India, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand.
Ecology: Humus in the shade of dense shrubs and along bank of streams. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Anoectochilus abbreviatus (Lindl.) Seidenf. previously (Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 129. 2004).

Hetaeria youngsayei Ormerod 香港翻唇蘭（卵葉翻唇蘭）
Oasis Suppl. 3: 7. 2004; FOC 25: 66. 2009.
Hetaeria shiuyingiana L. Li & F. W. Xing, Novon 19: 187–190. 2009.
Hetaeria nitida auct. non Ridl.: S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 51, fig. 21. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 104. 2002; Check List HK Plants 378. 2002; 131. 2004.

Terrestrial herb, 30–40 cm tall at flowering time; internodes 2–3 cm; annual growth bearing 3 large leaves at the apical end. Leaves petiolate; petioles sheathing, 2.5–3 cm; leaf blades oblique-ovate, 3–6 × 2–3.5 cm, shortly acuminate at apex. Flowers small, 9–10 in terminal spike; sepals 2 above, 1 below, densely glandularly hairy, ovate, 6–7 × 3–4 mm, all free, green with pink margin and apex; petals glabrous, obliquely ovate, 6 × 4 mm, apex obtuse, pink-white; lip honey-yellow, conical, 5 × 2 mm, slightly saccate; column fleshy, extending forward into a wing on each side; anther red; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary densely glandular, villose, 9 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough. S. Y. Hu 13233 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan; Thailand.
Ecology: Along ravines in forests. Flowering: Apr.

Heteropanax fragrans (Roxb. ex Candolle) Seem. 幌傘楓（火通木）
Fl. Vit. 114. 1866; FRPS 54: 137. 1978; FGD 1: 290. 1987.
Panax fragrans Roxb. ex Candolle, Prodr. 4: 254. 1830.

Evergreen tree, usually 5–10 m tall, glabrous except for apex of branches and inflorescence; branches stout, with many V-shaped leaf scars. Leaves 3–5-pinnately compound, 50–100 cm, more or less crowded towards apex of stems and branches; petioles (10–)15–30 cm; leaflets opposite, papery, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, (3–)5.5–13 × (2–)3.5–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, lateral veins 6–10 pairs, distinct on both surfaces. Inflorescence a terminal panicle of umbels, 30–40 cm, densely rusty stellate tomentose, glabrescent; pedicels 4–8 mm, lengthening after anthesis. Flowers pale yellowish white, fragrant. Calyx ca. 2 mm, minutely 5-toothed. Petals 5, ovate, ca, 2 mm. Stamens 5. Ovary 2-locular; styles 2, free. Fruit ovoid-globose, ± compressed laterally, 5–7 × 3–5 mm, black when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 469, 2065; HK sheet 34698.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Indonesia.

Heteropogon contortus (L.) P. Beauv. ex Roem. & Schult. 茅
Syst. Veg. 2: 836. 1817; FKH 322. 1912; FHN 4: 483, fig. 1268. 1977; FFJ 6: 269, fig. 242. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 240, pl. 60: 1–12. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 551, pl. 233. 2000; FOC 22: 638. 2006; FGD 9: 503, fig. 267. 2009.
Andropogon contortus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1045. 1753.
Heteropogon hirtus Pers., Syn. Pl. 2: 533. 1807; FHK 424. 1861.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, tufted, usually geniculate at base, glabrous, 20–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths keeled, longer than the internode, pilose at mouth; leaf blades flat or folded, 10–30 × 0.3–0.6 cm, scabrid or adaxial surface pilose at base; ligule short, membranous, ciliate, truncate. Racemes 3–6(–10) cm, mostly long exserted, solitary or aggregated into a scanty false panicle, the awns forming a twisted spire. Spikelets paired, basal 3–10 spikelets imbricate, sterile, persistent, awnless; upper 7–12 spikelets paired, heterogamous, 1 pedicellate, other sessile. Sessile spikelet ca. 7 mm, bisexual; callus fiercely pungent, acute and pungent, brown bearded; lower glume narrow oblong, hispidulous, abaxially rounded, apex obtuse, margins embraced same texture upper glume; upper glume narrow, 2-veined, hispidulous between veins, apex obtuse, margins membranous; lower lemma oblong; upper lemma membranous, very narrow, apex tipped with a geniculate awn of 6–10 cm long, column twisted and hairy, dark brown, column white-hirtellous, tips of successive awns often twisting together; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet oblong-lanceolate, barren.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 802, 987; K. L. Yip 4382.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics and subtropics of the world, extending to Mediterranean and other warm-temperate areas.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Heterosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Maxim. 合絲肖菝葜
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Pétersbourg. 17: 176. 1872; FHK 370. 1861; FKH 277. 1912; FHN 4: 127, fig. 1031. 1977; FOC 24: 117. 2000; FGD 6: 377. 2005.
Smilax gaudichaudiana Kunth, Enum. Pl. 5: 252. 1850.
Heterosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Maxim. var. hongkongensis (Seem.) A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1: 45. 1878.
Heterosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Maxim. var. latifolia Bodinier ex H. Lév., Liliac. etc. Chine 22. 1905.
Heterosmilax japonica Kunth var. gaudichaudiana (Kunth) F. T. Wang & T. Tang, FRPS 15: 244. 1978; Check List HK Plants 367. 2002; 128. 2004.
Oligosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Seem., J. Bot. 6(68): 258, pl. 83. 1868.
Smilax hongkongensis Seem., Bot. Voy. Herald 420. 1857.

Climbing vine. Stems woody, 3–6 m, glabrous. Petiole 1–2.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower part; tendrils well developed; leaf blade broadly ovate to orbicular, 5–15 × 2–8 cm, base truncate, rounded or cordate, apex long acuminate, 5–7(–9)-veined. Peduncle 1–3.5(–9) cm, slightly flat. Umbels often 20–40-flowered; pedicels slender, 0.5–1.5 cm. Male flowers: perianth tube red-purple, ovoid-ellipsoidal, 4–7 mm, teeth 3, deltoid; stamens 3, 3–4 mm; filaments nearly connate for its full length and forming a column; anthers ovoid, 0.5–0.7 mm. Female flowers slightly shorter than male ones, staminodes 3. Ovary ovoid. Berries purplish red, compressed globose, 6–9 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2197; Y. S. Lau 324, 2592.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and hillsides. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Notes: The syntypes (Hance s.n., Seemann s.n.) of Smilax hongkongensis Seem. were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Heterosmilax japonica Kunth 肖菝葜
Enum. Pl. 5: 270. 1850; FTW 5: 137. 1978; FRPS 15: 242, pl. 80: 1–3. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 100, pl. 32. 2000; FOC 24: 117. 2000; FGD 6: 377, fig. 224. 2005.

Climbing vine, glabrous. Stem woody, branches slightly ridged. Petiole 1–3 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/4–1/3; tendrils well developed; leaf blade papery, ovate, ovate-lanceolate to nearly heart-shaped, 6–20 × 2.5–12 cm, base subcordate, apex acuminate, mucronate, main veins 5–7. Umbels borne in axil of leaf or scalelike bract, 20–50-flowered; peduncle 1–3 cm, ± flat; pedicels slender, 2–7 mm. Male flowers: perianth ellipsoidal or narrowly obovoid, 3.5–4.5 mm; stamens 3, as long as 2/3 of perianth; filaments connate at lower half, forming a column. Female flowers: perianth ovoid, 2.5–3 mm; stigmas erect; staminodes 3. Berries globose, slightly compressed, black, 6–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 10539.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Anhui, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Bhutan, India, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Hewittia malabarica (L.) Suresh 豬菜藤
An Interpretation of Van Rheede's Hortus Malabaricus. 88. 1988; FOC 16: 285. 1995; FGD 4: 338, fig. 200. 2000.
Convolvulus malabaricus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 155. 1753.
Convolvulus bicolor Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 25. 1794.
Convolvulus bracteatus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 25. 1794.
Convolvulus sublobatus L. f., Suppl. Pl. 135. 1781[1782].
Hewittia bicolor (Vahl) Wight & Arn., Madras J. Lit. Sci. 1(5): 22. 1837.
Hewittia sublobata (L. f.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 441. 1891; FHN 3: 479, fig. 870. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 43, pl. 10: 1 – 2. 1979; Check List HK Plants 222. 2002; 77. 2004.
Shutereia sublobata (L. f.) House, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 33: 318. 1906.

Perennial herbaceous herb. Stems twining or prostrate, ± pubescent. Petiole 1–6 cm; leaf blade ovate, 3–10 × 3–8 cm, base cordate, hastate, or truncate, margin entire or 3‑lobed, apex acuminate, acute, or mucronate, appressed pilose or subglabrous on both surfaces; basal veins 5. Cymes often 1‑flowered; peduncle 1.5 – 10 cm, pilose; bracts oblong‑lanceolate, 0.5–1.5 cm, pubescent. Pedicel 2–4 mm. Sepals unequal, pubescent abaxially; outer 3 broadly ovate, ca. 1.5 cm; inner 2 oblong‑lanceolate, smaller, ca. 1.1 cm. Corolla pale yellow or whitish, with a purple center, 2–2.5 cm, midpetaline bands densely pilose. Stamens ca. 9 mm. Ovary villous. Capsule enclosed by persistent calyx, depressed globose, 8–10 mm in diam., pilose, irregularly 4‑valved.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau, Tai A Chau. Y. W. Lam 456, 1169, 1183.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Africa, tropical Asia.
Ecology: Sandy soil and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.

Hibiscus mutabilis L. 木芙蓉（芙蓉花）
Sp. Pl. 694. 1753; FKH 48. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 49. 1955; FRPS 49(2): 73. 1984; FGD 2: 184. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 742. 1993.

Tall shrub, 2– 5 m tall; branchlets, petioles, pedicels and calyx very densely lanate, the hairs straight and stellate mixed. Leaves papery; petioles 5–20 cm; stipules lanceolate, 5 – 8 mm, caducous; leaf blade broadly ovate to ovate-orbicular in outline, 10 –15 cm in diam., base cordate, apex acuminate, 5- or 7-lobed and 7- to 11-nerved, sparsely stellate-hispid and punctate adaxially, densely tomentose abaxially. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves near apex of branches. Pedicels 5 –8 cm, articulate towards apex. Bracteoles 8, linear, 10 –12 × 2 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2.5 –3 cm, conspicuously 5-lobed; lobes ovate, acuminate, 1.6 –2 cm. Corolla white, pink or red, the color changing from morning to afternoon; lobes suborbicular, 4– 5 cm in diam. Capsules subglobose, 2.5 cm in diam., setose and lanate, inside of the sutures densely villose. Seeds reniform, the back long villose, 2 to 6 hairs sharing a common base.

Locality: Extensively cultivated, wild plants observed below Victoria Peak. H. C. Tang 1452; Y. S. Lau 2044; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 21356 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to China; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), fiber.

Hibiscus rosa-sinensis L. 朱槿（扶桑、大紅花）
Sp. Pl. 694. 1753; FKH 48. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 47. 1955; FHN 2: 98. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 69. 1984; FGD 2: 185. 1991.

Shrub, 1–4 m tall; branchlets sparsely stellate pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 5–20 mm, pubescent; stipules linear, 5–12 mm; leaf blade ovate, 4 –9 × 2– 5.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, coarsely dentate above base, glabrous and punctate on both surfaces. Flowers solitary; pedicels 3.5 –7.5 cm, articulate towards the apex; bracteoles linear, 8 –15 × 1.2–2 mm, hardly connate at the base. Calyx campanulate, 1.7–2.5 cm, glandularly stellate puberulous; lobes 5, obovate deltoid, 7–10 mm. Corolla scarlet, funnel-form, 6 –15 cm in diam. Staminal tube 4 – 8 cm long, the upper 1/3 stameniferous. Flowers dropping off after anthesis, fruit not observed.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong gardens. Y. S. Lau 903, 3069; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22141 (CUHK).
Distribution: Long been accredited as a native of China, cultivated in temples and gardens of South China; wild form not yet discovered; many cultivars with double pink, red and even tinge orange flowers in Hong Kong.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: A cultivated form with double red flowers (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis L. var. rubro-plenus Sweet 重瓣朱槿) is also commonly cultivated in gardens and flowers almost all year round.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: A cultivated form with double red flowers (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis L. var. rubro-plenus Sweet 重瓣朱槿) is also commonly cultivated in gardens and flowers almost all year round.

records.text:
Hibiscus schizopetalus (Masters) Hook. f. 吊燈花（裂瓣槿）
Bot. Mag. 106: t. 6524. 1880; FHN 2: 98. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 69, pl. 17: 6. 1984; FGD 2: 185. 1991.
Hibiscus rosa-sinensis var. schizopetalus Masters, Gard. Chron. n. s. 12: 272, fig. 45. 1879.

Shrub 2–3 m tall; branchlets glabrous. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2 cm, stellate-pubescent; stipules subulate, ca. 2 mm, caducous; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, 4–7 × 1.5– 4 cm, base obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, basal half entire, apical half serrate. Flowers solitary, pendulous; pedicels slender, 10 –14 cm, articulate at the middle; bracteoles 8, very minute, 1–2 mm, ciliate. Calyx spathulate, tubular, 1.5 cm, shallowly 5-toothed. Corolla scarlet; lobes 4 –5 cm, reflexed, laciniate. Staminal tube 9–11 cm. Capsules oblong-cylindrical, 4 × 1 cm. Seed smooth.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong gardens. Y. S. Lau 1821; HK sheet 3506; S. Y. Hu 5827 (CUHK).
Distribution: Said to be native to E tropical Africa; cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round, flowers drop after anthesis; fruit not observed.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hibiscus syriacus L. 木槿
Sp. Pl. 695. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae 50. 1955; FHN 2: 99. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 75. 1984; FGD 2: 185. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 742. 1993.
Hibiscus chinensis auct. non DC.: Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 88 (Ind. Fl. Sin. I). 1886.

Shrubs, 2–4 m tall. Young branches and pedicels stellate puberulous. Leaves papery; petioles 3–16(–25) mm, stellate pilose adaxially; stipules linear, ca. 6 mm; leaf blade ovate-rhomboid to narrowly elliptic, 3 –10 × 2–4 cm, apex acuminate, base cuneate, irregularly dentate or shallowly 3-lobed, glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 4 –14 mm. Bracteoles 6 or 7, linear, 7–9 × 1–1.5 mm, very sparsely stellate pilose. Calyx campanulate, 1.4–1.7 cm, densely short stellate tomentellate, 5-toothed; lobes triangular, 6– 8 mm. Corolla lilac, 5– 6 cm in diam.; lobes obovate, 3.5– 5 cm, ciliate and puberulous abaxially. Staminal tube 2.5 –3 cm, antheriferous to the base. Capsules oblong-ellipsoid, densely golden stellate tomentose, 1.5–2 cm, apex 1.5 cm in diam., shortly rostrate. Seed glabrous, with a row of long white hairs along the back, like the mane of a horse.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1864; HK sheet 3526; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22193 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to China; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, food (vegetable), fibre.

Hibiscus tiliaceus L. 黃槿
Sp. Pl. 694. 1753; FKH 48. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 44. 1955; FRPS 49(2): 64, pl. 16: 2–3. 1984; FGD 2: 182, fig. 115. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 743, pl. 373. 1993.

Small tree, 3–7 m tall; branchlets glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 2–4 cm; stipules foliaceous, oblong, 2 × 12 mm, rounded at the apex, caducous; leaf blade roundish or broadly ovate, 6 –15 cm in diam., base cordate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire or crenulate, inconspicuously stellate pilose adaxially, grey, densely and shortly stellate tomentose abaxially, 7- or 9-nerved, with glands at the base of the main nerves. Flowers in simple axillary or terminal cymes; peduncles 4 – 5 cm; pedicels 1–3 cm, subtended by a pair of stipule-like bracts; bracteoles 7–10, linear-lanceolate, connate about the middle. Calyx 3 cm, basal 1/4 connate; lobes 5, lanceolate, 1.5 × 5 – 6 mm. Corolla campanulate; lobes obovate, 4.5 cm, united at the base, yellow, crimson at base. Capsules oblong-ellipsoid, 2.5 × 2 cm; pericarp woody. Seeds smooth, glandularly papillose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shek O, Ma Liu Shui, Mai Po, Leung Shuen Wan Chau (Tall Island). Y. S. Lau 1435, 1910; S. Y. Hu 6007; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 21922 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; coastal regions in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Ecology: Thickets, seashores behind mangroves. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, timber, fibre.

Hippeastrum vittatum (L'Hér.) Herb. 花朱頂蘭
Appendix 31. 1821; FRPS 16(1): 15. 1985; FGD 5: 445, fig. 238. 2003.
Amaryllis vittata L’Hér., Sert. Angl. 8, pl. 15. 1788.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs large, globose, to 7.5 cm in diam. Leaves basal, linear to strap-shaped, 30–40 × 2–6 cm, appearing with or after the flowers. Scape erect, hollow, 40–50(–70) cm. Umbel 2–6-flowered; involucres 2, lanceolate, 6 – 8.5 cm, recurved; bracts linear or lanceolate, 4–6.5 cm; pedicels 3.5–5 cm. Perianth funnel-shaped; tube ca. 3 cm, with minute scales at throat; segments obovate-elliptic, 10–15 × 2.5–4 cm, inner ones narrower, apex acute, red with white stripes. Stamens 6, insert in the throat, shorter than perianth segments. Style erect or slightly declinate, with a 3-lobed stigma. Capsule globose, loculicidally 3-valved.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hiptage benghalensis (L.) Kurz 風箏果（風車藤）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 43: 136. 1874; FGZ 256, fig. 127. 1956; FHN 2: 106, fig. 347. 1965; FFJ 2: 390, fig. 287. 1985; FGD 3: 221. 1995; FRPS 43(3): 119. 1998.
Banisteria benghalensis L., Sp. Pl. 427. 1753.
Hiptage madablota Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 169, pl. 116. 1791; FHK 49. 1861; FKH 53. 1912.

Woody vines, up to 30 m or longer; young branches densely yellowish brown pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 0.7–1 cm, blackish brown; leaf blade leathery, elliptic-oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 7–15 × 3–7 cm, base broadly cuneate or rotund, apex acuminate, often with 2 glands at base abaxially, young leaves light red, pubescent, old leaves green, glabrous; midvein and lateral veins elevated on both surfaces. Racemes 3–10 cm, yellowish brown pubescent. Flowers large, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam., fragrant. Sepals elliptic or ovate, 5–6 mm, densely yellow-brown pubescent abaxially, with a large gland at base abaxially. Petals white or pink, orbicular to broad-elliptic, 6–12 × 5–10 mm, base clawed, apex rounded, margin fimbriate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially. Longer filaments 8–12 mm, shorter ones 2 – 4 mm, glabrous; anthers 1–2 mm. Style terete. Samara subglabrous, middle wing elliptic or obovate, 3–5(–7) cm, apex entire, or retuse, lateral wings lanceolate-oblong, 1.5–3 cm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Chuen Lung, Tai Mo Shan, Kat O, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2941; HK sheet 39123, 40119.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia, Laos, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets or forests. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–May.

Holmskioldia sanguinea Retz. 冬紅花
Observ. Bot. 6: 31. 1791; FRPS 65(1): 192, pl. 21. 1982; FFJ 4: 550, fig. 430. 1989; FGD 3: 383. 1995.

Evergreen shrub, 3–7 m. Branchlets tetragonal, 4‑sulcate, hairy. Petiole 1–2 cm, sulcate, hairy and glandular; leaf blade membranous, ovate or broadly ovate, base rounded or subtruncate, margin serrate, sparsely hairy and glandular on both surfaces, hairs dense along veins. Thyrses composed of 2–6 cymes, each cyme 3‑flowered. Peduncle and pedicels with glandular hairs and long simple hairs. Calyx red to orange‑red, to 2 cm in diam., sparsely ciliate, reticulate veins conspicuous. Corolla red; tube 2–2.5 cm, glandular. Stamens 4, filaments 2.5–3 cm, glandular. Fruit obovoid, ca. 6 mm, enclosed in enlarged persistent calyx.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1458, 3197; HK sheet 22007.
Distribution: Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi (cultivated); native to Himalaya.
Uses: Ornamental.

Homalium cochinchinense (Lour.) Druce 天料木
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club. Brit. Isles 4: 628. 1917; FHN 1: 461. 1964; NFFJ 4: 17, fig.16. 1989; FGD 2: 114. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 30, pl. 6: 6. 1999.
Astranthus cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 222. 1790.
Homalium digynum Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 3: 247. 1914
Homalium fagifolium Benth., J. Linn. Soc.4: 35. 1860; FHK 122. 1861; FKH 110. 1912.
Homalium phanerophlebium How & Ko, Acta Bot. Sin. 8: 44. 1959.

Shrub or small tree; bark grey-brown; branchlets densely rusty tomentellate when young, glabrescent in age. Petioles 2–3 mm, yellow-pubescent; leaf blade broadly elliptic to obovate-oblong, 6 –10(–15) × 3 –7 cm, papery, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin remotely and obtusely dentate, pubescent along midvein and lateral veins on both surfaces, rarely sparsely pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Racemes axillary, sometimes with short branches, (5–)8–15 cm, densely yellow-tomentellate. Pedicels filiform, densely yellow-tomentellate, 2–3 mm. Flowers 7- or 8-merous, 8–9 mm in diam. Calyx tube turbinate, 2–2.5 mm, sparsely pilose and grooved; lobes linear or oblanceolate, ca. 3 × 0.3 mm, subglabrous abaxially, sparsely villous adaxially, margin ciliate, apex slightly obtuse. Petals spatulate, 3– 4 × 1 mm, subglabrous or sparsely hairy abaxially, sparsely puberulous adaxially, margin ciliate, conspicuously veined; filaments longer than petals; disc glandular; glands nearly square, hairy. Ovary hairy, styles usually 3, filiform, ca. 3 mm, hairy near base; parietal placentas 3, ovules 2– 4 per placenta. Capsule obconical, 5– 6 mm, subglabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 512; Y. S. Lau 717, 1033.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Almost all year round; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Timber.

Houttuynia cordata Thunb. 蕺菜（魚腥草）
Kongl. Vetensk. Acad. Nya Handl. 4: 149, 151. 1783; FHK 334. 1861; FKH 220. 1912; FHN 1: 338. 1964; FRPS 20(1): 8, pl. 3: 1–3. 1982; FGD 1: 79, fig. 84. 1987; FOC 4: 109. 1999.

Herb, 30– 60 cm tall; rhizomes creeping. Basal part of stems creeping, rooted at nodes, apical part erect, glabrous or pubescent on nodes, sometimes purplish red. Stipules membranous, 1– 2.5 cm, lower part connate with petiole and forming a 8–20 mm sheath. Petiole 1–3.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thinly papery, broadly ovate or ovate-cordate, 4 –10 × 2.5 – 6 cm, base cordate, apex short acuminate, densely glandular, usually glabrous, sometimes pubescent at vein axils, usually purplish abaxially; veins 5 –7, basal or innermost pair arising ca. 5 mm above base. Inflorescences 1.5 –2.5 cm × 5 – 6 mm; peduncles 1.5 –3 cm, subglabrous; involucral bracts oblong or obovate, 10 –15 × 5 –7 mm, apex rounded. Stamens longer than ovary. Capsules 2–3 mm, with persistent styles.

Localitiy: Lam Tsuen, Sha Lo Tung. HK Sheet 23812, 23813.
Distribution: S, E, C, SW & NW China; SE Asia, Africa (Madagascar), Pacific Islands.
Ecology: In wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal, food (vegetable).

Hoya carnosa (L. f.) R. Br. 球蘭
Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 1: 27. 1810; FHK 228. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 481, pl. 179. 1977; FGD 1: 488, fig. 549. 1987; FOC 16: 232. 1995.
Asclepias carnosa L. f., Suppl. Pl. 170. 1781.

Shrub, epiphytic, climbing on trees or rocks, glabrous except for inflorescences. Stems robust, to 6 m, pale grey, smooth. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate‑cordate, ovate, to ovate‑oblong, fleshy, 3.5–13 × 3–5 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex obtuse or short‑acuminate, lateral veins ca. 4 on each side of midvein, obscure. Umbels extra‑axillary, globose, ca. 30‑flowered, pubescent; peduncle 4 cm; pedicels 2–4 cm. Corolla white, sometimes with a pink center, rotate, 1–2 cm in diam.; lobes triangular, densely papillate inside, margin recurved, apex reflexed. Corona‑lobes stellately spreading, outer angle acute, middle ridge prominent, margin strongly reflexed and enclosing a hollow space at base, inner angle acute, incumbent on anthers. Stigma head obtuse or obscurely apiculate. Follicles linear‑lanceolate, 6–10 × 0.5–1.5 cm. Seeds small; coma 2.5 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, West Buffalo Hill, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1251; P. S. Choi 540; K. Y. Tam 140.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Japan, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: On trees or rocks. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Humulus scandens (Lour.) Merr. 葎草
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc., n.s., 24: 138. 1935; FGD 6: 107. 2005; FOC 5: 75. 2003.
Antidesma scandens Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 157. 1790.
Humulus japonicus Sieb. & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 2: 89. 1849.

Stems, branches and petioles with retrorse spines. Leaves papery, palmately 5 –7-lobed, rarely 3-lobed, 7–10 × 7–10 cm, base cordate, rough on both surfaces, sparsely strigose, pubescent and with yellow glands abaxially, lobes ovate to broadly lanceolate, margin serrulate, apex acute. Male flowers: small, yellowish green in laxly paniculate cyme, axillary; sepals 5; stamens 5; anthers pendulous on filaments. Female flowers in cone-like spikes of 5 mm in diam. Bracts violet, brown-green, triangular, apex acuminate, spinulose. Ovary enclosed by bracts; style 2, exserted from bracts. Infructescences 0.5 –1.5 cm. Achenes enclosed within enlarged calyx, compressedglobose, 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Sai Kung. Exotic. P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 36004, 36005).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Xinjiang and Qinghai; Russia (Asian region), Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wasteland, roadside, near villages. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Huodendron biaristatum (W. W. Smith) Rehd. var. parviflorum (Merr.) Rehd. 嶺南山茉莉
J. Arnold Arbor. 16: 346. 1935; FGD 1: 384. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 128. 1987; FOC 15: 265. 1996.
Styrax parviflorus Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 8: 15. 1927.
Huodendron biaristatum (W. W. Smith) Rehd. subsp. parviflorum (Merr.) Y. C. Tang, Ic. Corm. Sin. 3: 335. 1974, nom. nud.

Shrub or tree, to 7 m tall; bark greyish brown, exfoliating; branchlets reddish brown or greyish brown, tomentose or glabrous. Leaves sub-leathery; petiole 7–9 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, 6–11 × 2.5– 4.5 cm, apex acute or short acuminate, base cuneate, margin remotely serrate, glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, sub-corymbose, ca. 5 cm, densely grey-tomentose; pedicels 1 cm; calyx 2-2.5 mm; petals yellowish, narrowly oblong, ca. 6 mm, densely greyish tomentose; stamens 10, as long as petals; filaments flattened, pubescent; anthers as long as filaments, connectives 3-toothed, the middle one smaller than lateral ones, pubescent; styles slightly longer than stamens, 3-lobed at apex. Fruit ellipsoid, ca. 5mm, densely greyish tomentose. Seeds ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai. P. S. Choi 502; Y. W. Lam 36.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Forests in valleys.

Hydrangea macrophylla (Thunb.) Ser. 繡球
Prodr. 4: 15. 1830; FFJ 2: 226, fig. 192. 1985; FRPS 35(1): 226. 1995.
Hydrangea hortensia Sieb., Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. (pt. 2) 14: 688, fig. 2. 1829.
Hydrangea macrophylla (Thunb.) Ser. f. hortensia (Regel) Rehd., J. Arnold Arbor. 7(4): 240. 1926; FGD. 2: 208. 1991.
Hydrangea scandens auct. non Maxim.: FKH 98. 1912.
Viburnum macrophyllum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 125. 1784.

Deciduous shrub, 1 – 4 m. Branchlets robust, with conspicuous lenticels and leaf scars. Leaves opposite; petioles 1 – 3 cm; leaf blade elliptic, broadly ovate to obovate, 7 – 20 × 4 – 10 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin coarsely serrate except the base, green and glossy adaxially, glabrous or hirsute along veins abaxially. Inflorescence terminal, corymbose, globose, to 20 cm in diam.; pedicels pubescent. Flowers white, pink or bluish, mostly sterile. Sterile flower: sepals 4, broadly ovate or orbicular, 1 – 2 cm. Fertile flower: calyx 5-lobed, lobes ovate or triangular; petals 5, oblong; stamens 10, unequal in length, to 4 mm; ovary semi-inferior, styles usually 3. Capsules narrowly ovoid, ribbed.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1899.
Distribution: S, C & E China; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.-Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hydrilla verticillata (L. f.) Royle 黑藻
Ill. Bot. Himal. Mts. 1: t. 376. 1839; FKH 257. 1912; FGZ 647. 1956; FHN 4: 59. 1977; FRPS 8: 183, pl. 72: 1 – 6. 1992; FFJ 6: 24, fig. 17. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 15. 2000; FGD 6: 295, fig. 164. 2005; FOC 23: 101. 2010.
Serpicula verticillata L. f., Suppl. Pl. 416. 1781[1782].

Submerged herb. Leaves in whorls of 3–8, linear or narrowly strap-shaped, 0.7–1.7 cm × 1–4 mm, midvein distinct, margin conspicuously denticulate, apex acute. Male spathe green; sepals white, ca. 2.3 × 0.7 mm; petals reflexed, white, or reddish, ca. 2×0.5 mm. Female spathe green; flowers similar to male ones. Fruit with 2–9 spine-like projections or smooth and without projection. Seeds (1–)2–6.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 13709.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW; Asia, Australia and Europe, introduced into N America.
Ecology: Running freshwater in ponds and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides Lam. 天胡荽
Encycl. 3(1): 153. 1789; FRPS 55(1): 17. 1979; FGD 2: 328. 1991; FOC 14: 15. 2005.
Hydrocotyle perexigua Hance, Wailp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 691. 1851 – 52.
Hydrocotyle rotundifolia Roxb. ex DC., Prodr. 4: 64. 1830; FHK 134. 1861; FKH 116. 1912.

Perennial prostrate herb; stems slender, glabrous or sparsely hairy, rooting at the nodes. Leaves alternate; petioles slender, 0.5–3 cm, glabrous or sparsely hairy on the distal part; leaf blade, suborbicular or reniform, 0.5–1.5 cm in diam., base cordate, margin shallowly 5–7-lobed; lobes crenately toothed, glabrous or sparsely hispid on veins of abaxial surface. Umbels head-like, simple, 2–5(–10)-flowered; peduncles 0.5–2 cm, usually shorter than petioles. Flower greenish, subsessile. Fruit suborbicular, 0.8–1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2469; Y. S. Lau 1790, 2665.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Nepal, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Korea, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Damp and half-shady places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides Lam. var. batrachium (Hance) Hand.-Mazz. ex R. H. Shan 破銅錢
Sinenesia 7: 480. 1936; FRPS 55(1): 18, pl. 2: 7– 9. 1979; FGD 2: 328. 1991; FOC 14: 15. 2005.
Hydrocotyle batrachium Hance, Ann. Sc. Nat. 4. ser. 18: 220. 1862.
Hydrocotyle rotundifolia Roxb. var. batrachium (Hance) Chermezon, Bull. Soc. Bot. Fr. 68: 508. 1921.

Leaves deeply 3–5-divided, parted nearly to base; lobes obovate, margin crenate.

Locality: So Kwun Po, Tai Po. HK sheet 2058, 36137, 36141.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Damp and half-shady places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hydrocotyle wilfordii Maxim. 腎葉天胡荽（惠氏天胡荽）
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 31: 45. 1887; FKH 116. 1912; FRPS 55(1): 23. 1979; FGD 2: 328. 1991; FOC 14: 17. 2005.

Perennial prostrate herb, 14–45 cm tall, rooting at the nodes, glabrous or sparsely hirsutulous on leaf blades and petioles. Leaves alternate; petioles slender, 2.5–13 cm, more or less pubescent on distal part; leaf blade suborbicular to reniform, 1.5–3 cm in diam., glabrous or sparsely hirsute on veins of abaxial surface, base deeply cordate, margin shallowly 5–9-lobed; lobes crenate, subequel. Umbels simple, head-like, (5–)10–15(–20)-flowered; peduncles usually longer than the leaves, 1–5 cm. Flower greenish-white. Fruit suborbicular, 1–1.5 mm in diam., or broader than long.

Locality: Shing Mun, Lam Tsuen, Tai Mo Shan, Mau Ping. H. C. Tang 2503; L. T. Lo 431; Y. S. Lau 3306.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Streamsides, wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Sep. –Nov.

Hygrophila erecta (Burm. f.) Hochr. 小葉水蓑衣
Candollea 5: 230. 1934; FHN 3: 546. 1974; FRPS 70: 71. 2002.
Ruellia erecta Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 135. 1768.

Perennial herb, up to 1 m tall. Stems erect, quadrangular, bisulcate. Petioles (0–)3–5 mm, sulcate, hispid; leaf blades elliptic, obovate or oblong, 2–9 × 1–3 cm, base decurrent onto the petiole, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, hirsute on both surfaces, with numerous cystoliths, lateral veins 8–15 pairs, prominent abaxially. Flowers several‑fasciculate in leaf axil, sessile. Bracts leaf‑like, ovate, lanceolate or elliptic, ca. 1.1 cm, densely hispid‑ciliate; bracteoles linear‑oblong, ca. 6 mm, densely hispid‑ciliate. Calyx ca. 1.1 cm, 5‑lobed below to middle; lobes linear‑lanceolate, densely white hispid‑ciliate. Corolla purplish blue, 1.8–2.2 cm, pilose, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm, gradually widened to ca. 6 mm at mouth; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip triangular, 2‑lobed, lower lip oblong, 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 6 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anther‑thecae linear, ca. 2 mm, divaricate at base. Ovary glabrous; style pilose. Capsule 1.2–1.5 cm. Seeds oblong, flattened, blackish brown, ca. 1.5 × 1 mm, glabrous, margin circled with translucent membrane.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 6407 (PE).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Spring.

Hygrophila megalantha Merr. 大花水蓑衣
Philipp. J. Sci. 12(2): 110. 1917; FRPS 70: 71. 2002.
Hygrophila salicifolia var. megalantha (Merr.) H. S. Lo & L. D. Chou, Guihaia 16: 374. 1996.

Perennial herbs, 30–60 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, glabrous. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blades narrowly oblong‑obovate to lanceolate, 4–9 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or undulate, glabrous, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Flowers several‑fasciculate in leaf axil, sessile. Bracts oblong‑lanceolate, 0.8–1 × 0.3–0.5 cm, apex acute, ciliate; bracteoles oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 6 × 2 mm, apex acute, ciliate. Calyx 1.4–1.6 cm, 5‑lobed to the middle; lobes linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, sparsely hispid‑ciliate. Corolla purplish blue, 2–2.5 cm, pilose outside; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 7 mm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip ovate‑oblong, ca. 1.2 × 0.8 cm, apex emarginate, lower lip oblong, ca. 1.3 × 0.8 cm, 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 4 × 2 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 1.4 cm, the shorter pair ca. 0.7 cm, anther‑thecae ovate, ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary glabrous, styles filiform, ca. 1.6 cm, slightly hairy, stigma quite unequally bilobed. Capsule oblong, 1.4–1.6 cm, glabrous, 12–16‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 mm, glabrous.

Locality: So Kwun Po, Sha Kok Mei, Shek Pik Reservoir. W. J. Tutcher 1079; Y. S. Lau 799; HK sheet 34480.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The species was reported as Hygrophila quadrivalvis Nees previously (Check List HK Plants 253. 2002; 87. 2004).

Hygrophila salicifolia (Vahl) Nees 水蓑衣
Pl. Asiat. Pl. 3: 81. 1832; FHK 261. 1861; FKH 197. 1912; FHN 3: 545. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 661. 1998; FRPS 70: 69. 2002.
Ruellia salicifolia Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 84. 1794.
Justicia lancea Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. 2: 338. 1794.
Hygrophila lancea (Thunb.) Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.‑Bat. 2: 123. 1865; FTW ed. 2, 4: 660. 1998; Check List HK Plants 252. 2002; 87. 2004.

Perennial herbs to 80 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent at base, quadrangular, striate, slightly pubescent. Petioles 0.5–1 cm, glabrous; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate to oblanceolate, 3–10 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base attenuate and decurrent onto the petiole, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous, with numerous cystoliths on both surfaces, lateral veins 8–11 pairs. Flowers 2–10 fasciculate in leaf axil, sessile. Bracts ovate, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, pubescent on margin, with numerous cystoliths; bracteoles narrowly ovate, ca. 3 mm, apex obtuse, pubescent on margins. Calyx narrowly campanulate, ca. 6 cmm, 5‑lobed to the middle; lobes linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, sparsely hispid‑ciliate. Corolla ca. 1 cm, pale purple, tube ca. 7 × 2 mm, glabrous, 2‑lipped, upper lip elliptic, ca. 3 mm, shallowly 2‑lobed, puberulent outside, lower lip obovate, ca. 3 mm, 3‑lobed to the middle, lobes ovate, apex obtuse. Stamens 4, included, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm. Ovary glabrous; style filiform, slender, included, ca. 8 mm; stigma unequally 2‑lobed. Capsule narrowly oblong, acute, 8–10 × ca. 1.5 mm, 12–18‑seeded. Seeds orbiculate, ca. 1 mm long, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Chuen Lung, Tai Po, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 1083; L. T. Lo 177; HK sheet 35582.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Streamsides and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The species was also reported as Hygrophila phlomoides Nees previously (Check List HK Plants 253. 2002; 87. 2004).

Hylocereus undatus (Haw.) Britt. & Rose 量天尺
Fl. Bermuda 256. 1918; FHN 1: 493. 1964; FGX 1: 739. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 283. 1999; FGD 4: 136, fig. 84. 2000.
Cereus undatus Haw., Phil. Mag. 7: 110. 1830.

Succulent cactus, climbing by aerial roots. Stems 6 –7 m or longer, 3-angled, depth of ribs 1–2.5 cm, margin undulate; areoles borne on the ribs, 3 – 4 cm apart, with 1–3 small spines. Flowers solitary, 25 –30(–35) cm long; limb 10 –12 cm in diam.; segments many, outer ones yellowish green or purplish, inner ones white. Stamens many, cream-white, equaling the perianth-segments. Fruit a fleshy berry, oblong, ca. 10 cm, with large scales outside.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 12287.
Distribution: Originated from neotropics; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Climbing by aerial roots on walls and tree trunks. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental, food (beverage base, vegetable).

Hylodesmum laterale (Schindl.) H. Ohashi & R. R. Mill 側序長柄山螞蝗
Edinburgh. J. Bot. 57(2): 177. 2000; FGD 5: 276. 2003.
Desmodium laterale Schindl., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 22(618 – 626): 258 – 259. 1926.
Podocarpium laterale (Schindl.) Y. C. Yang & P. H. Huang, Bull. Bot. Lab. N.-E. Forest. Inst. Harbin 4: 7. 1979; FRPS 41: 52. 1995.

Small slender herb. Stems angular, 25–30 cm tall, thinly pubescent. Stipules lanceolate, 5–7 mm, acuminate. Leaves 3-foliolate; petioles 3–5 cm; leaflets membranous or subleathery, pubescent or glabrous adaxially, sparsely hairy on veins abaxially, 3-veined at base, veinlets conspicuous, terminal leaflet narrow ovate, 5–10 × 1.5–3 cm, 2–3 times longer than broad, apex acute, lateral ones smaller. Pseudoracemes terminal, sometimes oblique. Peduncles slender, 20–40 cm. Flowers in clusters of 1–3; pedicels slender, 1–2 cm. Calyx-lobes shallow and rounded, 1 mm, slightly pubescent. Corolla pink, 5–7 mm; keel and wings with spur at base. Bracts ovate, acuminate, 1–3 mm, deciduous. Pods 1–2 cm, with stalk of 1 cm, 2–4-jointed, segments 9 × 4 mm, half-rhomboid, width half of length, covered with hooked-hairs, constricted nearly to ventral suture.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 407; Y. W. Lam 1145; HK sheet 40639.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan (Rykyu Islands).
Ecology: Forests near streams. Flowering: Sep. – Oct.

Hylodesmum leptopus (A. Gray ex Benth.) H. Ohashi & R. R. Mill 細長柄山螞蝗
Edinburgh. J. Bot. 57(2): 179. 2000; FGD 5. 275, fig. 146. 2003; FGD 5: 275, fig. 146. 2003.
Desmodium leptopus A. Gray ex Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 226. 1852.
Desmodium laxum subsp. leptopus (A. Gray ex Benth.) H. Ohashi, Ginkgoana 1: 141. 1973.
Podocarpium leptopus (A. Gray ex Benth.) Y. C. Yang & P. H. Huang, Bull. Bot. Lab. N.-E. Forest. Inst. Harbin 4: 6. 1979; FRPS 41: 50. 1995.

Erect herb. Stems ca. 30 cm tall, thinly pubescent. Stipules lanceolate, 5–10 mm. Leaves 3-foliolate; petioles 5– 8 cm; leaflets membranous, terminal one ovate or broadly ovate, 6–10 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, lateral ones smaller, bases slightly oblique, with 3 pairs of veins at base, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface with whitish spots, only pubescent on veins. Pseudoracemes 10–30 cm, terminal. Flowers loosely arranged, 5– 7 mm; pedicels 1– 1.5 cm. Bracts linear, deciduous. Calyx campanulate, glabrous, 1 – 2 mm. Pods 2 – 5 cm × 5 mm, 2 – 3-jointed, long stalked; stalks 1 cm, with constrictions between joints; segments oblique, 13 –16 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Mau Ping. L. T. Lo 336; Y. S. Lau 3029.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Shady places in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Sep.

Hymenachne amplexicaulis (Rudge) Nees 膜稃草
Fl. Bras. Enum. Pl. 2: 276. 1829; FOC 22: 510. 2006; FGD 9: 430. 2009.
Panicum amplexicaule Rudge, Pl. Guian. 1: 21. 1805;
Hymenachne acutigluma (Steud.) Gilliland, Gard. Bull. Sing. 20: 314. 1964; FRPS 10(1): 298, pl. 92: 1–5. 1990; FYN 9: 501. 2003; Check List HK Plants 338. 2002; 118. 2004.
Hymenachne pseudointerrupta C. Muell., Bot. Zeit. 19: 333. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 5: 478, pl. 199. 2000.

Perennial herb. Culms spongy, creeping and rooting at the base, up to 1 m tall, many-noded, glabrous. Leaf sheath slightly shorter than internode, nodes pubescent. Leaf blades broadly linear, thick, 30–40 × ca. 2 cm, glabrous or the adaxial surface and margins loosely tuberculate-hairy, base rounded and slightly clasping, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Panicle 20–40 × 1–2 cm; spike-like, branches 0.5–2 cm, erect, appressed; rachis winged, fasciculate spikelets in one side; pedicels very short, scabrous. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate, 3.5–5 mm; lower glume ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, 1-veined; upper glume and lower lemma lanceolate, 3–4 mm, herbaceous, apex with 0.5–2 mm awn; upper lemma ca. 3 mm, membranous, acuminate; palea 2, mucronate; anthers ca. 1 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.5 mm, apex rounded.

Locality: Hong Kong. HK sheet 33914.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Thailand, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malay Peninsula, Philippines.
Ecology: Ponds and marshes in shallow water. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Hymenocallis littoralis (Jacq.) Salisb. 水鬼蕉（蜘蛛蘭）
Trans. Hort. Soc. London 1: 338. 1812; FRPS 16(1): 14. 1985; FGD 5: 446, fig. 239. 2003.
Pancratium littorale Jacq., Select. Stirp. Amer. Hist. 99, t. 179, fig. 94. 1763.
Pancratium biflorum auct. non Roxb.: FHK 367. 1861; FKH 275. 1912.

Perennial herb, stout, bulbiferous, glabrous throughout. Leaves basal, ensiform, to 100 × 7.5 cm, slightly narrowed at base, tapering to apex, dark green, midvein impressed adaxially, keeled abaxially. Scape erect, to 1.5 m, slightly flattened and 2 ridged. Umbel 3–8-flowered; involucres 2, ovate-lanceolate, 5–8 cm, membranous; bracts lanceolate, ca. 4 cm; Flowers sessile, fragrant. Perianth tube slender, 5–13 cm, greenish white; segments white, linear, 6.5–10 × 0.5–0.7 cm, apex acuminate. Staminal cup white, petaloid, to 3 cm high, free parts of filament green, 4–5 cm; anther linear, versatile, ca. 1.8 cm, apex acuminate. Style exceeding stamens; stigma capitate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1912.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; native to Mesoamerica.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hyparrhenia diplandra (Hack.) Stapf 短梗苞茅
Fl. Trop. Africa. 9: 368. 1919; FRPS 10(2): 235, pl. 58: 4. 1997; FYN 9: 705. 2003; FOC 22: 633. 2006; FGD 9: 501. 2009.
Andropogon diplandrus Hack., Flora 68: 123. 1855.
Hyparrhenia eberhardtii (A. Camus) Hitchc., Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 247 – 248. 1929[1931]; FHN 4: 482, fig. 1226. 1977.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, coarse, 1–2 m tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous or upper margins hispidulous; leaf blades linear to narrowly linear, 30–60 × 0.3–0.6 cm, glabrous or hirsute at base, margins scabrid; ligule reddish brown, ca. 2 mm, dry membranous, apex obtuse and rounded, ciliate. Spathate panicle loose, peduncle scarcely exserted from spatheole, densely golden tuberculatehirtose; racemes 4–8-awned per pair, reflexed at maturity; raceme bases subequal, flattened, short, broadly oblong, glabrous on outer face; usually 2 pairs of homogamous spikelets at base of both lower and upper raceme of pair; pedicel longer than rachis internodes, ca. 1/2 length of sessile spikelet. Sessile spikelet lanceolate, glabrous or pilose, callus acute and pungent, densely bearded; callus 1–1.5 mm, sharply acute, white bearded; lower glume lanceolate, margins inrolled, obtuse; upper glume slightly longer than lower glume, boat-shaped, apex rounded and obtuse, 3-veined; lower lemma lanceolate, hyaline membranous, ciliate; upper lemma linear, 2-lobed; awn geniculate, column with white or brown ca. 0.5 mm hairs; palea absent; stamens 3 or absent. Pedicellate spikelet narrow, staminate or barren.

Locality: Castle Peak. HK sheet 15837.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Hypericum japonicum Thunb. ex Murray 地耳草（田基黃）
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 702. 1784; FHK 23. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 47. 1990; FHN 2: 52. 1965; FGD 3: 207. 1995.

Annual or perennial herb, 2– 45 cm tall. Branches diffuse or ascending, 4-angled. Leaves sessile, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–18 × 1–10 mm, base slightly cordate, amplexicaul, rarely cuneate, apex obtuse, with transparent dots, 3-basinerved. Cymes terminal. Flowers yellow, 4 – 8 mm in diam. Sepals narrow-oblong or elliptic, 2– 5.5 mm, often with glandular dots. Petals elliptic, oblong or obovate, equaling to sepals. Stamen many; filaments base united; ovary ovate to elliptic, 1–1.8 mm; style 3 –2. Capsules ellipsoid, 2.5 – 6 × 1.3 –2.8 mm, dehiscing into 3 valves when ripen. Seeds yellow-brown, 0.5 mm.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Tsim Shan, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 661; H. C. Tang 2472; Y. S. Lau 2134.
Distribution: Liaoning, Shandong to S regions of Changjiang River; Japan, Korea, Nepal, Sikkim, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar to Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand, Hawaii.
Ecology: Along roadside. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hypericum monogynum L. 金絲桃
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 1107. 1763; FRPS 50(2): 12. 1990; FGD 3: 206. 1995.
Hypericum chinense L., Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1184. 1759 non Osbeck (1757).

Small shrub, 0.5 –1 m tall, many branched. Leaves papery, elliptic, oblong, obovate, oblanceolate or ovate-oblong, 2.5 –11 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate or slightly cordate, sometimes amplexicaul; lateral veins 4–5 pairs, slender, obvious abaxially. Cymes terminal. Flowers yellow, ca. 3 – 6.5 cm in diam. Sepals ovate-oblong, 4.5 –13 mm. Petals obovate, 2–3.5 cm; stamens many, base united into 5 bundles, slightly shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid, 3– 4 mm, 5-locular; style 5-lobed. Capsules ovoid, 6 –10 × 4 –7 mm. Seeds dark red, ca. 1.3 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 2695.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Sichuan, Hubei, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Henan, Hebei, Shaanxi, Shandong, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Hypericum sampsonii Hance 元寶草
J. Bot. 3: 378. 1865; FKH 41. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 60. 1990; FGD 3: 205. 1995.

Perennial herbs, 0.2–0.8 m tall, often branched above. Leaves opposite, in perfoliate pairs, oblong-lanceolate, 3 –15 × 1–3.5 cm, base wholly connate, apex obtuse or rounded, sparsely black glandular dotted; lateral veins ca. 4 pairs. Cymes terminal. Flowers yellow, 6 –15 mm in diam. Sepals elliptic or oblong, 3 –7 mm, with black glandular dotted. Petals oblong or obovate, 4– 8 mm, persistent, sparsely glandular dotted. Stamens united into 3 bundles. Ovary 3-locular; styles 3. Capsules ovoid to narrowly pyramidal, 6 –9 × 4 – 5 mm, with yellow-brown vesicular glands. Seeds orange-brown, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan (Ngong Ping).
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; India, Japan.
Ecology: Farmland. Flowering: Mar.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hypoestes purpurea (L.) R. Br. 槍刀藥
Prodr. 1: 474. 1810; FHK 265. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FHN 3: 564. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 665. 1998; FRPS 70: 249. 2002.
Justicia purpurea L., Sp. Pl. 16. 1753.
Peristrophe purpurea (L.) Hochr., Candollea 5: 234. 1934.
Hypoestes sinica Miq., J. Bot. Neerland 1: 117. 1861.

Spreading to erect perennial herbs or shrubs, up to 1.5 m tall. Stems erect or decumbent, young stems subquadrangular, sulcate, slightly puberulent. Petiole 1–3.5 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 5–13 × 1.5–7 cm, base narrowed and cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire or subundulate, adaxially green, sparsely pubescent, or glabrous except for pubescent along the veins and on the margin, abaxially pale green, glabrous, lateral veins 5–8 pairs.
