Ipomoea batatas (L.) Lam. 番薯
Encycl. 2: 465. 1793; FKH 180. 1912; FHN 3: 486. 1974; FTW 4: 363. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 89. 1979; FFJ 4: 493. 1989; FOC 16: 306. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 357. 1998; FGD 4: 353. 2000.
Convolvulus batatas L., Sp. Pl. 1: 154. 1753.
Batatas edulis (Thunb. ex Murray) Choisy, Convolv. Orient. 53. 1833.
Convolvulus candicans Sol. ex Sims, Bot. Mag. 39: pl. 1603. 1813.
Convolvulus edulis Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 203. 1784.
Ipomoea batatas var. edulis (Thunb. ex Murray) Makino, Fl. Japan 476. 1927.
Ipomoea edulis (Thunb. ex Murray) Makino, Somoku‑Dzusetsu 4: pl. 25. 1903.
Ipomoea fastigiata (Roxb.) Sweet, Hort. Brit. 1: 288. 1826.

Annual herb with ellipsoidal, fusiform, or elongate subterranean tubers; sap milky. Stems prostrate or ascending, green or purplish, much branched, rooting at nodes, glabrous or pilose. Petiole 2.5–20 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to orbicular, 4–13 × 3–13 cm, margin entire or palmately 3–5(–7)‑lobed, herbaceous; lobes broadly ovate to linear‑lanceolate, sparsely pilose or glabrous. Cymes (1–)3–7‑flowered. Peduncle 2–10.5 cm, stout, angular. Bracts caducous, lanceolate, 2–4 mm. Pedicel 2–10 mm. Sepals ± unequal, oblong or elliptic, apex acute, mucronulate, margin ciliate, glabrous or pilose abaxially; outer 2 sepals 0.7–1 cm, inner 3 sepals 0.8–1.1 cm. Corolla pink, white, pale purple to purple, with a darker center, campanulate to funnelform, 3–4 cm, glabrous. Stamens inclusive. Pistil inclusive; ovary pubescent or glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2849; HK sheet 9363, 19756.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Food.

Ipomoea biflora (L.) Pers. 心萼薯
Syn. Pl. 1: 183. 1805; FOC 16: 304. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 358, pl. 159, photo 208. 1998.
Convolvulus biflorus L. Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 1668. 1763, non Forssk. 1775.
Aniseia biflora (L.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 483.1833; FRPS 64(1): 41, pl. 10: 3. 1979; FFJ 4: 481, fig. 384. 1989; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.
Convolvulus sinensis Desr., Encycl. 3(2): 557. 1789.
Ipomoea sinensis (Desr.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 459. 1834; FGZ 588. 1956; FTW 4: 373, pl. 1046. 1978; FGD 4: 350. 2000.

Annual, scandent or twining herb. Stems slender, finely striate, greyish white hirsute. Petiole slender, 1.5–9 cm, hairy; leaf blade papery, heart‑shaped or triangular‑heart‑shaped, 3–9 × 2–7 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire, rarely slightly 3‑lobed, hirsute‑villous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4 – 5 pairs. Cymes (1–)2(–3)‑flowered, shorter than petiole. Peduncle 0.3–1.5 cm. Outer 3 bracts linear‑lanceolate, small. Pedicel 0.8 – 1.5 cm. Sepals slightly enlarged in fruit; outer 3 deltate‑lanceolate, 0.8–1 × 0.4–0.5 cm, greyish white hirsute abaxially, ciliate, subglabrous adaxially, base auriculate; inner 2 linear‑lanceolate, ca. as long as outer ones or slightly longer. Corolla white, narrowly campanulate, 1–1.5 cm; limbs 5‑lobed, midpetaline bands pubescent. Stamens ca. 3 mm; anthers ovoid‑deltoid, base sagittate. Ovary conical, glabrous. Style clavate. Stigma capitates, 2‑lobed. Capsule subglobose, 0.8–1 cm in diam., glabrous. Seeds ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 4 mm, black, puberulent to tomentellous, margin sometimes white woolly.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2415, 2779; Y. W. Lam 1141.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Myanmar, Vietnam, E Africa, N Australia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, valleys, thickets and forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea cairica (L.) Sweet 五爪金龍
Hort. Brit., ed. 1, 287. 1827; FGZ 586, fig. 312. 1956; FHN 3: 489, fig. 874. 1974; FTW 4: 364, pl. 1040. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 97. 1979; FFJ 4: 494, fig. 394. 1989; FOC 16: 309. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 358, pl. 160, photos 209 – 210. 1998; FGD 4: 353, fig. 208. 2000.
Convolvulus cairicus L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 2: 922. 1759.
Ipomoea palmata Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.‑Arab. 43. 1775; FKH 181. 1912.

Perennial twining herb with a tuberous root, glabrous throughout. Stems often tuberculate. Petiole 2–8 cm, base with leafy pseudostipules; leaf blade palmately 5–7‑parted to base; lobes ovate, ovate‑lanceolate or elliptic, apex acute or obtuse, mucronulate, entire or minutely undulate, basal pair usually again lobed or parted; middle lobe larger, 3–9 cm. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm. Bracts and bracteoles caducous, small. Pedicel 2.5–3 cm. Sepals equal or the outer ones slightly shorter, 6–7 mm, abaxially ± verruculose. Corolla pink, purple, or reddish purple, with a darker center, funnelform, 5–7 cm. Stamens inclusive, unequal. Capsule ± globose, ca. 1 cm. Seeds black, ca. 5 mm, densely tomentose, margin with longer hairs.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1592, 2388; L. T. Lo 188.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; widely distributed in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets, wastelands, sunny slopes. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), weed.

Ipomoea carnea Jacq. subsp. fistulosa (Mart. ex Choisy) D. F. Austin 樹牽牛
Taxon 26(2 – 3): 237. 1977; FOC 16: 311. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 361. 1998.
Ipomoea fistulosa Mart. ex Choisy, Prodr. 9: 349. 1845; FRPS 64(1): 101. 1979; FFJ 4: 494. 1989; FGD 4: 351. 2000; Check List HK Plants 223. 2002; 77. 2004.
Batatas crassicaulis Benth., Bot. Voy. Sulphur 134. 1845.
Ipomoea crassicaulis (Benth.) B. L. Rob., Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 51(10): 530. 1916; FTW 4: 364. 1978.

Shrub, 1–3 m. Branches terete or angular, stout, solid or hollow, pubescent when young. Petiole 2.5–15 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 6–25 × 4–18 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex acuminate, mucronulate, margin entire, adaxially subglabrous, pubescent abaxially; midvein 2‑glandular abaxially at base. Cymes several‑flowered. Peduncle stout, 5–10 cm. Bracts caducous, small, ovate. Pedicel 1–1.5 cm, pubescent. Sepals ovate, thinly leathery, equal or inner ones longer, 5–6 mm, abaxially puberulent, often with glands alternating to sepals at base. Corolla pink, darker inside, funnelform, 7–9 cm; tube and midpetaline bands pilose abaxially. Stamens inclusive; filaments unequal. Pistil inclusive; ovary puberulent. Style puberulent at base. Capsule pale brown, ovoid, 1.5–2 cm, 4‑valved, apiculate. Seeds black, ca. 1 cm, brown sericeous‑pubescent.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 284; Y. S. Lau 2770, 2844.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; native to tropical America, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: All year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea fimbriosepala Choisy 狹花心萼薯
Prodr. 9: 359. 1845; FOC 16: 304. 1995.
Aniseia stenantha (Dunn) Ling ex R. C. Fang & S. H. Huang, FRPS 64(1): 42. 1979; FFJ 4: 481. 1989; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.
Ipomoea setifera Poiret var. fimbriosepala (Choisy) Fosberg, Smithsonian Contr. Bot. 36: 24. 1977.
Ipomoea stenantha Dunn, FKH 180. 1912; FGD 4: 355. 2000.

Annual twining herb. Stems slender, sparsely hairy to glabrescent or hirsute on nodes. Petiole 2–5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade triangular or ovate‑triangular, or oblong‑cordate‑sagittate to narrowly hastate, 5–9 × (1–)3–6 cm, base auriculate or sagittate, apex acuminate, mucronulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs, inconspicuous. Inflorescences axillary, 1(–2)‑flowered; peduncle 5(–9) cm or shorter; bracts 2, ± ovate, 0.5 – 1.5 cm, glabrous. Pedicel angular, 1.3–4 cm. Sepals unequal; outer 3 larger, ovate to lanceolate, 1.5–2.2 cm, base shallowly cordate, apex mucronate, strongly 3‑keeled abaxially, keels toothed basally, glabrous. Corolla red, with a darker center, funnelform, ca. 3.5 cm, glabrous; limb lobed, lobes slightly triangular. Stamens inclusive; filaments pilose below middle. Ovary conical, glabrous. Style filiform, ca. 5 mm; stigma capitate, 2‑lobed. Capsule ovoid to globose, pale brown outside, whitish inside, ca. 1.2 cm. Seeds blackish brown, densely tomentellous.

Locality: Sai Kung. HK sheet 35671.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang; New Guinea, Africa, Mexico, Pacific islands, S America.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Ipomoea imperati (Vahl) Griseb. 假厚藤
Cat. Pl. Cub. 203. 1866; FOC 16: 308. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 361, pl. 161, photo 212. 1998.
Convolvulus imperati Vahl, Symb. Bot. 1: 17. 1790.
Convolvulus sinuatus Petagna, Inst. Bot. 2: 353. 1787.
Convolvulus stoloniferus Cirillo, Pl. Rar. Neapol. 1: 14, pl. 5. 1788, nom. illeg. superfl.
Ipomoea carnosa R. Br., Prodr. 485. 1810; FKH 181. 1912.
Ipomoea stolonifera (Cirillo) J. F. Gmel., Syst. Veg. 1: 345. 1796, nom. illeg. superfl.; FHN 3: 488. 1974; FTW 4: 375, pl. 1047. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 96, pl. 20: 2 – 3. 1979; FFJ 4: 496, fig. 396. 1989; FGD 4: 352. 2000.

Perennial prostrate herb, glabrous throughout. Stems to 5 m, rooting at nodes. Petiole 0.5–5 cm; leaf blade variable in shape, often linear, lanceolate, oblong, or ovate, 1.5–3 × 0.8–2 cm, base truncate or shallowly cordate, apex obtuse or emarginate to 2‑lobed, margin entire, undulate, or 3–5‑lobed; middle lobe ovate to oblong, lateral lobes smaller. Cymes 1(–3)‑flowered. Peduncle ca. 2 cm. Bracts deltate, ca. 2 mm. Pedicel ca. 6 mm, stout. Sepals unequal, oblong, ± leathery, apex obtuse or acute, mucronulate; outer 2 ca. 0.7–1.1 mm; inner ones to 1.5 cm. Corolla white, with a pale yellow tube and a dark red center, funnelform, 3.5–4 cm. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule subglobose, ca. 1 cm, smooth. Seeds ca. 8 mm, tomentose, margin with longer hairs.

Locality: Tai Long Sai Wan, Tai Wan, Soko Islands, Fan Lau. Y. S. Lau 2583; Y. W. Lam 459; HK sheet 39425.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering: May–Dec.
Notes: It was reported as Ipomoea stolonifera previously (Check List HK Plants 223. 2002; 78. 2004), which is illegitimate, because it is based on the same type as the earlier Convolvulus sinuatus which is a later homonym of I. sinuata Ortega.

Ipomoea indica (Burm.) Merr. 變色牽牛
Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 445. 1917; FOC 16: 305. 1995; FTW 4: 363, pl. 162, photo 213. 1998.
Convolvulus indicus Burm., Index Univ. Herb. Amb. 7: 6. 1755.

Pharbitis insularis Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 439. 1833.
Pharbitis learii (Knight ex Paxton) Lindl., Edwards's Bot. Reg. 27: pl. 56. 1841.

Annual herbaceous herb. Stems twining or sometimes prostrate, 3–6 m, sometimes rooting at nodes, ± densely retrorse pilose. Petiole 2–18 cm; leaf blade ovate or orbicular, 5–15 × 3.5–14 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate or abruptly acuminate, margin entire or 3‑lobed, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely short, soft, pubescent. Cymes dense, umbellate, several‑flowered. Peduncle 4–20 cm. Bracts linear, sometimes lanceolate. Pedicel short. Sepals subequal, broadly lanceolate, 2–2.5 cm, glabrous to appressed pilose. Corolla bright blue or bluish purple, funnelform, 5–8 cm, glabrous. Stamens and styles inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule subglobose, 1–1.3 cm in diam. Seeds 4–6, ca. 5 mm, brown, glabrous.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 608; Y. W. Lam 1029, 1161.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan (Tong Sha Islands), Guangdong; native to S America, widely cultivated and naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Forests near seashore. Flowering: Jan.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea mauritiana Jacq. 七爪龍
Collectanea 4: 216. 1791; FOC 16: 310. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 363, photo 215. 1998.
Ipomoea digitata auct. non L.: FKH 181. 1912; FGZ 587. 1956; FHN 3: 489. 1974; FTW 4: 366. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 99. 1979; FFJ 4: 489. 1989; FGD 4: 354. 2000.

Perennial twining herb with tuberous roots, glabrous throughout. Stems to 10 m, thinly angular. Petiole 3 – 11 cm; leaf blade orbicular in outline, usually palmately (3–)5–7(–9)‑divided to or beyond middle, rarely entire or shallowly lobed, 5–18 cm, base cordate or truncate; segments lanceolate or elliptic, apex acuminate or acute, mucronulate, entire or irregularly undulate. Cymes several–many‑flowered. Peduncle 3–10 cm. Bracts caducous, triangular, 3–6 mm. Pedicel 1–2.5 cm. Sepals broadly ovate, thinly leathery, equal or outer 2 shorter, 7–12 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse. Corolla pink or reddish purple, with a darker center, campanulate, 5 – 6 cm; limb 5 – 7 cm in diam., undulate. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule ovoid, 1.2–1.4 cm, 2‑locular, 4‑valved. Seeds dark brown, ca. 6 mm, densely woolly‑sericeous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1440, 2001; S. P. Lau 165.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets and wastelands. Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), weed.
Notes: The species was reported as Ipomoea digitata L. previously (Check List HK Plants 223. 2002; 77. 2004), which is endemic to West Indies and does not occur in Asia.

Ipomoea nil (L.) Roth 牽牛
Catal. Bot. 1: 36. 1797; FHN 3: 486. 1974; FTW 4: 369. 1978; FOC 16: 305. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 366, photo 216. 1998.
Convolvulus nil L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 219. 1762.
Ipomoea hederacea (L.) Jacq., Collectanea 1: 124, pl. 36. 1787; FKH 181. 1912; FGZ 585. 1956.
Pharbitis nil (L.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 439. 1833; FRPS 64(1): 103. 1979; FFJ 4: 490, pl. 391. 1989; FGD 4: 356. 2000; Check List HK Plants 225. 2002; 78. 2004.

Annual twining herbaceous herb. Stems 2–5 m, retrorsely hirsute. Petiole 2–15 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate or suborbicular, 4–15 × 4.5–14 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire or 3(or 5)‑lobed, hirtellous. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–18.5 cm, hirsute. Bracts linear or narrowly lanceolate, 5–8 mm, spreading hirtellous. Pedicel 5–8 mm. Flowers large. Sepals subequal, lanceolate, 1–2.5 cm, abaxially spreading hirsute, slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla pale to bright blue with whitish tube, funnelform, 5–6(–8) cm, glabrous. Stamens inclusive, unequal. Pistil inclusive; ovary glabrous, 3‑locular. Stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule straw coloured, ovoid to subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam., glabrous. Seeds black, ovoid‑trigonous, 5–6 mm, grey puberulent.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2052; Y. S. Lau 2801; HK sheet 35870.
Distribution: Native to S America, now widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets on slopes, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea obscura (L.) Ker Gawl. 小心葉薯
Bot. Reg. 3: t. 239. 1817; FKH 181. 1912; FHN 3: 487. 1974; FTW 4: 369. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 92, pl. 12: 1. 1979; FOC 16: 307. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 366, photo 217. 1998; FGD 4: 352. 2000.
Convolvulus obscurus L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 220. 1762.

Twining herb. Stems slender, 1–2 m, sparsely villose or glabrous. Petiole 1.5–3.5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to suborbicular, occasionally reniform, 2–8 × 1.5–8 cm, base cordate, apex attenuate, acute, margin entire or minutely undulate, subglabrous, sometimes ciliolate; lateral veins 3 pairs. Cymes 1–3‑flowered. Peduncle almost filiform, 1.5–6 cm. Bracts subulate, ca. 1.5 mm. Pedicel 1 – 2 cm, subglabrous, thickened and recurved in fruit distally. Sepals subequal, reflexed in fruit, elliptic‑ovate, 4 – 5 mm, glabrous or ± pubescent, mucronulate. Corolla white or pale yellow, with darker midpetaline bands and a purple center, funnelform, 2–2.5 cm. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule ovoid, 0.8–1 cm in diam., apiculate. Seeds black‑brown, 4–5 mm, densely greyish brown tomentellous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 70; Y. S. Lau 2477; HK sheet 35850.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; tropical Africa, tropical Asia, N Australia.
Ecology: Sandy beach, thin forests or thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea pes-caprae (L.) R. Br. 厚藤（海灘牽牛）
Narr. Exped. Zaire. 477. 1818; FHK 238. 1861; FHN 3: 488. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 96. 1979; FFJ 4: 495, fig. 395. 1989; FOC 16: 308. 1995; FGD 4: 352. 2000.
Convolvulus pescaprae L., Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753.
Convolvulus bilobatus Roxb., Fl. Ind., (ed. 1820) 2: 73. 1824.
Convolvulus brasiliensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753.
Convolvulus maritimus Desr., Encycl. 3(2): 550 – 551. 1792.
Ipomoea biloba Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.‑Arab. 44. 1775; FKH 180. 1912.
Ipomoea maritima (Desr.) R. Br., Prodr. 486. 1810.
Ipomoea pes‑caprae var. emarginata Hallier f., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 37: 332. 1898.
Ipomoea pes‑caprae subsp. brasiliensis (L.) Ooststr., Blumea 3(3): 533. 1940; FTW 4: 371, pl. 1043. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 367, pl. 164, photo 218. 1998.

Perennial prostrate herb, with a thick tap root, glabrous throughout. Stems 5–30 m, pale red. Petiole 2–10 cm; leaf blade thickly papery, ovate, elliptic, orbicular or reniform, 3.5–9 × 3–10 cm, base broadly cuneate, truncate, or shallowly cordate, apex emarginate or deeply 2‑lobed, mucronulate, margin entire, abaxially with two glands near midvein at base. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle stout, 4–15 cm. Bracts caducous, broadly deltate, 3–3.5 mm. Pedicel 2–2.5 cm. Sepals unequal, ± leathery, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous, 3‑veined; outer 2 ca. 1 cm; inner ones slightly longer. Corolla purple or reddish purple, with a darker center, funnelform, 4–5 cm. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule subglobose, ca. 1.7 cm in diam., glabrous, leathery. Seeds black, trigonous‑globose, 7–8 mm, densely brownish tomentose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. May 11496; L. Gibbs 5382; Y. S. Lau 387.
Distribution: Taiwan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Forage, medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea pileata Roxb. 帽苞薯藤
Fl. Ind. 2: 94. 1824; FHN 3: 485. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 88, pl. 18: 4. 1978; FOC 16: 306. 1995.
Convolvulus pileatus (Roxb.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 4(Cur. Post): 61. 1827.

Annual twining herb. Stems slender, retrorse hispid‑pilose. Petiole 1.5 –6 cm; leaf blade ovate or broadly ovate, 3.5–8 × 2.5–7 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate or attenuate, margin entire, sparsely appressed pubescent. Cymes capitate, several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–7 cm. Involucral bracts navicular, 3–5.5 cm, tapered at both ends, long hirtellous adaxially, densely pubescent abaxially; bracteoles oblong‑spatulate, much smaller, villous. Sepals subequal, 0.8–1 cm; outer 3 elliptic‑spatulate; inner 2 narrower, lanceolate, villous, apex obtuse. Corolla pink or purple, salverform, 2.5–3 cm; tube cylindric; limb with deltate lobes, midpetaline bands pilose. Stamens inserted near middle of corolla tube, inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Capsule subglobose, 5–6 mm in diam., glabrous. Seeds dark brown, 3–4 mm, glabrous or short pubescent.

Locality: Tai Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 4813; H. C. Tang 1890; HK sheet 34505.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Asia, tropical E Africa, Mascarene Islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, sunny grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.

Ipomoea purpurea (L.) Roth 圓葉牽牛
Bot. Abh. 27. 1787; FOC 16: 305. 1995.
Convolvulus purpureus L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1: 219. 1762.
Ipomoea hispida Zucc., Collectanea 127. 1806.
Pharbitis hispida (Zucc.) Choisy, Convolv. Orient. 56. 1833.
Pharbitis purpurea (L.) Voigt., Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 354. 1845; FRPS 64(1): 104. 1979; FFJ 4: 490, fig. 392. 1989; FGD 4: 356, fig. 209. 2000; Check List HK Plants 225. 2002; 78. 2004.

Annual twining herb. Stems and petioles short pubescent and long retrorse hirsute. Petiole 2–12 cm; leaf blade suborbicular or broadly ovate, 4–18 × 3.5–16.5 cm, base cordate, apex acute or ± abruptly acuminate, margin entire or ± 3‑lobed, strigose on both surfaces. Cymes 1 – 5‑flowered. Peduncle 4 – 12 cm. Bracts linear, 6–7 mm, hirsute. Pedicel 1.2–1.5 cm, short pubescent and long retrorse hirsute. Sepals subequal, 1.1–1.6 cm, spreading hirsute abaxially at lower half; outer 3 oblong, apex acuminate; inner 2 linear‑lanceolate. Corolla red, reddish purple, or blue‑purple, funnelform, 4–6 cm, glabrous. Stamens inclusive, unequal; filaments pubescent at base. Pistil inclusive; ovary glabrous, 3‑locular. Stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule subglobose, 9–10 mm in diam., 3‑valved. Seeds black or straw coloured, ovoid‑trigonous, glabrous or hilum sparsely pilose.

Locality: Naturalized. Aubrey 11570.
Distribution: Most provinces of China; native to America, now introduced and naturalized worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea quamoclit L. 蔦蘿松
Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753; FTW 4: 337. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 371. 1998.
Convolvulus pennatus Desr., Encycl. 3: 567. 1791.
Quamoclit pennata (Lam.) Bojer, Hort. Maurit. 224. 1837; FHN 3: 492, fig. 876. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 110, pl. 23: 1. 1979; FFJ 4: 498, fig. 398. 1989; FGD 4: 359, fig. 211. 2000; Check List HK Plants 225. 2002; 78. 2004.

Annual twining slender herb, glabrous throughout. Petiole 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate to oblong in outline, 2–10 cm, pinnately parted; segments 10–18 pairs, linear, basal one pair often 2‑lobed. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–10 cm. Bracts small, triangular, deciduous. Pedicel 1–2 cm, clavate in fruit. Sepals slightly unequal, elliptic, 4–6 cm, apex obtuse, apiculate. Corolla bright red, rarely white, salverform, ca. 3.5 cm; limb 5‑lobed, lobes nearly triangular. Capsule ovoid, 6–7 mm, glabrous. Seeds elliptic, black.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 136.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America, widely cultivated in tropical and temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea triloba L. 三裂葉薯
Sp. Pl. 1: 161. 1753; FTW 4: 378, pl. 1048. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 90, pl. 19: 4. 1979; FOC 16: 307. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 371, pl. 167, photo. 219. 1998; FGD 4: 352. 2000.
Batatas triloba (L.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 8: 49. 1838.
Convolvulus trilobus (L.) Desr., Encycl. 3(2): 564. 1792.

Annual twining or prostrate herb. Stems glabrous or nodes sparsely pubescent. Petiole 2.5–6 cm, glabrous, sometimes tuberculate; leaf blade broadly ovate to orbicular in outline, 3–7 × 2–6 cm, base cordate, margin coarsely dentate to deeply 3‑lobed, or entire, glabrous or sparsely pilose. Cymes dense, umbellate, 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 2.5–9 cm, glabrous, angular, verruculose at upper part. Bracts triangular, minute, ca. 3 mm. Pedicel 5–8 mm, glabrous, verruculose. Sepals subequal, oblong, 5–9 mm, apex obtuse or acute, mucronulate, margin ciliate. Corolla pink or pale purple, funnelform, 1.5–2 cm, glabrous; limb obtusely 5‑lobed. Stamens and styles inclusive. Ovary pubescent. Capsule subglobose, 5–8 mm, pilose. Seeds dark brown, ca. 3.5 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 215, 535; Y. W. Lam 397.
Distribution: Anhui, Guangdong, S Shaanxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang; native to the tropical West Indies, now a circumtropical weed.
Ecology: Thickets and grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Iris speculatrix Hance 小花鳶尾
J. Bot. 13: 196. 1875; FKH 274. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 174, pl. 56: 1–4. 1985; FOC 24: 309. 2000; FGD 6: 383, fig. 227. 2005.
Iris cavaleriei H. Lév., Liliac. & Chine 18. 1905.
Iris grijsii Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 26: 527. 1880.

Rhizomes creeping. Roots thick. Leaves slightly curved, dark green, glossy, linear, 15–30 × 0.6–1.2 cm, veins 3 – 5. Flowering stems 20–25 cm, 1–2-leaved; spathes 2 – 3, green, lanceolate, 5.5–8 cm, 1–2-flowered, apex acuminate. Flowers violet or light blue, 5.6–6 cm in diam.; pedicel 3–7 cm. Perianth tube ca. 5 mm; outer segments spreading, spatulate, with a central, dark circular patch, 3–4 cm, crest yellow; inner segments erect, narrowly oblanceolate, 3–3.7 cm. Stamens ca. 1.2 cm; anthers white. Ovary fusiform, 1.6–2 cm. Style branches ca. 2.5 cm × 7 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 5–5.5 cm, apex long beaked. Seeds dark brown, angled, with aril drying as a pale brown wing.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Tam, Sunset Peak, Po Toi Islands. Y. S. Lau 2564; P. S. Choi 351, 459.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Qinghai, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests, moist grasslands. Flowering: May; fruiting: Jul. – Aug. Uses: Ornamental (flowers).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance (Herb. No. 18465, BM) from Victoria Peak and Mount Davis in April 1874. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental (flowers).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance (Herb. No. 18465, BM) from Victoria Peak and Mount Davis in April 1874. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Isachne albens Trin. 白花柳葉箬
Sp. Gram. 1(8): t. 85. 1828; FRPS 10(1): 185. 1990; FFJ 6: 169, fig. 138. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 448. 2000; FOC 22: 559. 2006; FGD 9: 370. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, erect or decumbent at base, tufted, 30–100 cm tall, branching and rooting at basal nodes. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than the internode, with ciliate margins; leaf blades firm, narrowly lanceolate, 7–15 × 0.8–1.8 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface glabrous to hispidulous, margins thickened; ligule 1–2 mm, a row of hairs. Panicle pyramidal, 10–20 cm; branchlets and pedicels without glandular bands. Spikelets whitish green, elliptic-globose, 1–1.5 mm; florets similar, lower floret usually bisexual, upper floret usually female; glumes herbaceous, subequal to spikelet, usually glabrous, occasionally with a few stiff bristles above middle, obtuse, 5–7(–9)-veined; lower lemma globose to elliptic-ovate, leathery, puberulous or subglabrous, obtuse. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Hong Kong (fide Corlett et al. 2000).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, N India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillsides, margins of forests, other moist open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Isachne globosa (Thunb. ex Murray) Kuntze 柳葉箬
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 778. 1891; FHN 4: 401, fig. 1029. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 188. 1990; FFJ 6: 171, fig. 139. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 448, pl. 185. 2000; FOC 22: 555. 2006; FGD 9: 371, fig. 180. 2009.
Milium globosum Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 109. 1784.
Isachne australis R. Br., Prod. 1: 196. 1810; FHK 414. 1861; FKH 313. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms rather slender, tufted, decumbent, creeping and rooting at the lower nodes, ascending to 80 cm tall or more, nodes glabrous. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, ciliate on margins; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 3–10 × 0.4–0.8 cm, very rough with a minute pubescence, base rounded or slightly cordate; ligule 1–2 mm, a ring of hairs ciliate. Panicle open, ovoid, spreading, 4–11 cm, rather loose; pedicels variable in length, shorter or longer than spikelets, mostly marked with a pellucid discoloration or gland. Spikelets greenish or purplish brown, elliptic-globose, 1.5–2 mm; outer glumes glabrous; lower floret usually male, with a glabrous glume, upper floret female, pubescent; lower lemma oblong, soft texture, glabrous; upper lemma abaxial glabrous or puberulous, upper margins ciliate; lodicules cuneate, truncate and emarginate. Caryopsis subglobose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1687, 2239; HK sheet 41607.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over Nepal, India, Malay Peninsula to Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines, and northward to Japan and Korea.
Ecology: Moist places of grasslands, path between paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Isachne myosotis Nees 荏弱柳葉箬
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 2: 98. 1850; FHK 415. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 5: 449, pl. 187. 2000; FOC 22: 558. 2006.
Isachne debilis Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 322. 1904; FRPS 10(1): 179, pl. 56: 11–14. 1990; FFJ 6: 168. 1995.
Isachne firmula Büse, Pl. Jungh. 3: 39. 1854; FKH 313. 1912; Check List HK Plants 338. 2002; 118. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms slender, decumbent, branching and rooting at nodes, flowering branches up to 10 cm tall. Leaf sheaths less than 1/2 length of the internode, thinly to densely hispid with spreading hairs, or hairs confined to margins; leaf blades ovatelanceolate, 1–3 × 0.2–0.5 cm, rough, ± appressed-hairy on both surfaces, base rounded, apex acute; ligule a ring of hairs. Panicle ovate or contracted, 1.5 – 5 cm; branches spiculate to base, with short stiff branchlets and pedicels, smooth. Spikelets tinged purplish, subglobose, 1–1.5 mm; florets similar; glumes equal to spikelet, separated by a short internode, ovate-oblong, 5–7-veined, hispid, usually with a few stiff hairs toward the apex, obtuse; lemmas strongly convex, leathery, puberulous to densely pubescent.

Locality: Kam Shan, Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 226; HK sheet 14969, 35873.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Indonesia to New Guinea.
Ecology: Moist grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Ischaemum aristatum L. 有芒鴨嘴草
Sp. Pl. 2: 1049. 1753; FKH 322. 1912; FHN 4: 460. 1977; FFJ 6: 252, fig. 221. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 163, pl. 38: 10–13. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 557, pl. 235. 2000; FOC 22: 610. 2006; FGD 9: 474. 2009.
Ischaemum barbatum auct. non Retz.: FHK 425. 1861.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, ascending or branched, 40–90 cm tall, glabrous or bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose, shorter than internode except the base, sometimes long-ciliate near mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–25 × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous or thinly pilose, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule membranous, 2–3 mm. Racemes terminal, paired, appressed back to back, long exserted from uppermost sheath; rachis internodes clavate, triquetrous, scabrid or ciliate along outer angle. Sessile spikelet lanceolate; lower glume obtuse or slightly 2-toothed, broader and 2-keeled above, keels narrowly to broadly winged, wing margin scabrous, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as lower glume, keeled, margins ciliate, apex acute; lower floret staminate, slightly shorter than glume; lemma papery, acute, obscurely 3-veined; palea membranous, 2-keeled; upper floret bisexual, lemma 2-cleft to the middle, with a geniculate awn from sinus, exserted from spikelet; palea as long as or slightly shorter than lemma; stamens 3; style free. Pedicellate spikelet dorsally compressed, similar to sessile.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. L. Thrower s.n.; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20878, 22741 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Liaoning, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open grassy sandy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Ischaemum aristatum L. var. glaucum (Honda) T. Koyama 鴨嘴草
J. Jap. Bot. 37: 239. 1962; FFJ 6: 253. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 163. 1997; FOC 22: 611. 2006; FGD 9: 475. 2009.
Ischaemum crassipes (steud.) Thell. var. glaucum Honda, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 3: 355. 1930.

Rachis internodes and pedicels scabrid or shortly ciliate on outer angle, inner angles glabrous or shortly ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblanceolate, narrowly to broadly winged, mucronate or shortly awned; awn included within spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 32262.
Distribution: S Anhui, Hebei, Jiangsu, Liaoning, Shandong, Zhejiang; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy places, usually near the sea.

Ischaemum barbatum Retz. 粗毛鴨嘴草
Observ. Bot. 6: 35. 1791; FHN 4: 460. 1977; FFJ 6: 253, fig. 222. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 156, pl. 37: 6 – 11. 1997; FOC 22: 613. 2006; FGD 9: 474. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or ascending, 30–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous to villous; leaf blades linear or narrowly lanceolate, 5–30 × 0.3–0.8 cm, apex acute; ligule 1–5 mm. Racemes terminal, paired, usually appressed back to back; rachis internodes oblong, triquetrous, ciliate along outer angle, inner angles glabrous or shortly ciliate. Sessile spikelet lanceolate-oblong, callus bearded; lower glume leathery, herbaceous above with many anastomosing green veins, glabrous to villous, marginal nodules at lower 2/3, these sometimes extended into weak transverse ridges, 2-keeled, keels asymmetrically winged, one wing wider than the other; upper glume as long as lower glume, hard papery; lower floret staminate, lemma boat-shaped, 1-veined; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline membranous, 2-deeply-clefted, with a geniculate awn from sinus; palea slightly shorter than lemma. Pedicellate spikelet dorsally compressed, as large as sessile but marginal nodules less developed, awnless or awned.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 817, 2174; HK sheet 40833.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Australia, W Africa.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Summer and autumn.

Ischaemum ciliare Retz. 細毛鴨嘴草
Observ. Bot. 6: 36. 1791; FKH 322. 1912; FOC 22: 611. 2006; FGD 9: 475, fig. 248. 2009.
Spodiopogon obliquivalvis auct. non Nees: FHK 426. 1861.
Spodiopogon obliquivalvis Nees var. villosus Benth., FHK 426. 1861.
Ischaemum indicum auct. non (Houtt.) Merr.: FHN 4: 461. 1977; FFJ 6: 252. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 159. 1997; Check List HK Plants 339. 2002; 119. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted or creeping and rooting at the base, ascending or erect, 30–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths sparsely to densely pilose with tubercle-based hairs, mouth haired; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 5–25 × 0.5–1cm, ± pubescent, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous. Racemes terminal, paired (seldom 3 or 4); rachis internodes and pedicels subequal, oblong, triquetrous, ciliate along angles. Sessile spikelet obovate-oblong, callus ca. 1 mm, pubescent; lower glume leathery with rounded flanks in lower half, upper half flat, papery, sometimes wrinkled, flanks keeled, winged, forming 2 rounded lobes at apex; upper glume boat-shaped, swollen and keeled above middle, keel narrowly winged; lower floret staminate, lemma papery, obscurely veined, apex acuminate; upper floret bisexual, lemma short, apex 2-clefted to the middle, with an awn arising from sinus; awn 1–1.5 cm. Pedicellate spikelet laterally compressed; lower glume with a solitary median winged keel; upper lemma awned.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 931, 1261, 1321.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields.

Ischaemum muticum L. 無芒鴨嘴草
Sp. Pl. 2: 1049. 1753; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 255. 1971; FRPS 10(2): 161, pl. 38: 6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 560. 2000; FOC 22: 610. 2006.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms erect, geniculate at base, with a shallow groove along one side, glabrous. Leaf sheaths ciliate along outer margin, inner margin glabrous or sparsely appressed hairy; leaf blades long ovate-lanceolate to linear, lanceolate, tinged reddish brown, 2–10(–18) × 0.3–2 cm, base cordate, very shortly pseudo-petiolate, apex acute; ligule membranous, truncate, 0.2–0.6 mm. Racemes usually paired, appressed back to back, base enclosed by subtending sheath; rachis internodes and pedicels oblong, triquetrous, outer angle narrowly winged, inner angles glabrous or ciliolate. Sessile spikelet lanceolate; lower glume broad lanceolate, herbaceous, glabrous, winged from near base, apex entire; upper glume boat-shaped, thinly leathery, winged on upper keel, 3-veined; lower floret staminate, slightly shorter than glume, lemma and palea hyaline membranous; lodicules cuneate; pistil absent; upper floret bisexual, lemma long ovate, apex 2-toothed, midvein extend to a short and straight awn; upper lemma subentire, mucronate or with ca. 1 mm awnlet. Pedicellate spikelet laterally compressed, otherwise resembling sessile or smaller, awnless.

Locality: Hong Kong. HK sheet 32263.
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan (S Ryukyu Islands), India, Indochina, Malesia, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Coastal area.

Ischaemum rugosum Salisb. 田間鴨嘴草
Icon. Stirp. Rar. 1, t. 1. 1791; FKH 322. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 158, pl. 37: 12. 1997; FYN 9: 672. 2003; FOC 22: 613. 2006; FGD 9: 474. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect, loosely tufted or solitary, 20–100 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths longer or upper shorter than internode, glabrous or sparsely pilose, ciliate; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 5–30 × 0.5–2 cm, pilose or covered with scattered tubercle-based hairs, apex acuminate, margins scabrid; ligule membranous, oblong, 2–5 mm. Racemes terminal and axillary, paired, appressed back to back, or usually separated, fragile; rachis internodes inflated, thickly clavate, outer margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet ovate; lower glume 2-keeled, crustaceous, transversely 4–7-ridged below, ridges sharp, mostly continuous, herbaceous above with many anastomosing green veins, keels scabrid, wingless or winged on one side, apex obliquely obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, abaxially keeled; lower floret staminate, lemma as long as or slightly shorter than lower glume, apex acuminate; stamens 3; palea as long as or slightly shorter than lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma membranous, apex 2-lobed to middle; awn exerted from sinus, geniculate and twisted; palea shorter than lemma. Pedicellate spikelet dorsally compressed, variable in size, often much reduced especially toward raceme apex, awnless; pedicel elongate when spikelet rudimentary.

Locality: High Island, Nai Chung. S. Y. Hu 8087, 8466, 8679 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia, Malesia, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Stream and ditch banks, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Isodon amethystoides (Benth.) H. Hara 香茶菜
J. Jap. Bot. 60: 233. 1985; FOC 17: 274. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 470, pl. 204. 1998.
Rabdosia amethystoides (Benth.) H. Hara, FRPS 66: 429. 1977; FGD 3: 463. 1995.
Plectranthus amethystoides Benth., Labiat. Gen. Spec. 45. 1832; FKH 208. 1912.

Perennial herbs, with thick, woody rhizomes. Stems erect, 30–150 cm tall, quadrangular, 4‑sulcate, densely appressed incurved‑pilose or puberulent. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.2 – 2.5 cm; leaf blade ovate‑orbicular to lanceolate, 0.8–11 × 0.7–3.5 cm, base abruptly attenuate or broadly cuneate‑attenuate, apex acuminate, acute or obtuse, margin crenate, adaxially olive green, ± densely hispidulous, sometimes subglabrous, abaxially greenish, pilose or tomentulose, sometimes subglabrous. Cymes many‑flowered, arranged in loose, terminal panicles; floral leaves ovate, similar to stem leaves but smaller, gradually reduce to bracts upward. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely hirtellous or subglabrous abaxially, with scattered white or yellow glands; teeth 5, subequal, triangular; fruiting calyx erect, broadly campanulate, 4–5 mm, slightly shorter than wide. Corolla white bluish, white, or purplish, purple bluish on upper lip, ca. 7 mm, sparsely puberulent abaxially. Stamens included. Style included. Nutlets ovoid, ca. 2 mm, brown to yellow or white glandular.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8394.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests, wet grasslands. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Isodon coetsa (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) Kudô 細錐香茶菜
Mem. Fac. Sci. Taikoku Imp. Univ. 2: 131. 1929; FOC 17: 286. 1994.
Rabdosia coetsa (Buch.‑Ham ex D. Don) H. Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 47(7): 194. 1972; FRPS 66: 494. 1977; FGD 3: 464. 1995.
Plectranthus coetsa Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 117. 1825.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–2 m tall, with woody rhizomes and numerous fibrous roots. Stems erect, obtusely 4‑angled, puberulous or subglabrous. Stem leaves opposite; petiole 1–5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 3–9 × 1.5–6 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin crenate, glandular, adaxial surface sparsely strigose, minutely hispid on veins, abaxial surface densely minutely hispid on veins. Cymes 3–5‑flowered, forming narrow, terminal or axillary panicles, pubescent; peduncle of cymes 2–3 mm; pedicels 1–3 mm, puberulous; lower floral leaves sessile, ovate, upper floral leaves bract‑like, ovate‑lanceolate, shorter than pedicels. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 mm, pubescent abaxially, glandular, slightly 2‑lipped; teeth ovate‑triangular, ca. 1/3 as long as calyx, apex acute; fruiting calyx tubular‑campanulate, dilated to ca. 4 mm, slightly curved, netted at apex. Corolla purple to purple‑blue, ca. 6 mm, pubescent, tube ca. 2.5 mm, upper lip ca. 2.5 mm; lower lip broadly ovate, ca. 3.5 mm. Stamens included. Style included or slightly exserted. Nutlets brown, obovoid, ca. 1 mm wide, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 3241.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.

Isodon lophanthoides (Buch‑Ham. ex D. Don) H. Hara 線紋香茶菜
J. Jap. Bot. 60: 235. 1985; FOC 17: 278. 1994.
Rabdosia lophanthoides (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) H. Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 47(7): 194, 197. 1972; FRPS 66: 479. 1977; FGD 3: 466. 1995.
Plectranthus striatus Benth., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 17. 1830; FKH 208. 1912.
Isodon striatus (Benth.) Kudô, Mem. Fac. Sci. Taihoku Imp. Univ. 2: 134. 1929.
Hyssopus lophanthoides Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 110. 1825.

Perennial herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall, with underground globose root tubers. Stems erect or ascending from repent base, puberulent or pilose. Stem leaves opposite; petiole equal to or longer than blade; leaf blade broadly lanceolate to ovate, 1.5–20 × 0.5–8.5 cm, base cuneate to rounded, rarely shallow cordate, apex obtuse to acuminate, margin crenate, minutely hirsute, adaxially olive green, abaxially greenish, sparsely brown glandular. Cymes helicoid, 11– 13‑flowered, forming terminal and axillary panicles of 7–20 cm; floral leaves bract‑like, ovate; bracteoles linear, 3– 5 mm, slightly longer than pedicels. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, lengthening to 4.5–5 mm in fruit, base sparsely villous abaxially, sparsely red‑brown glandular, 2‑lipped; teeth ovate‑triangular, lower 2 longer. Corolla white or rose, with purple spots on limb, 2–7 mm; tube 3.7–5 mm, straight; upper lip 1.6–2 mm, lower lip slightly longer. Stamens and style much exserted. Nutlets brown, compressed ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.75 mm, glabrous, smooth.

Locality: A Ma Wat, Sheung Miu Tin, Lantau Island. HK sheet 22119.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Forests, thickets in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Isodon ternifolius (D. Don) Kudô 牛尾草
Mem. Fac. Sci. Taihoku Imp. Univ. 2: 137. 1929; FOC 17: 273. 1994.
Rabdosia ternifolia (D. Don) H. Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 47(7): 201. 1972; FRPS 66: 436, pl. 92: 1. 1977; FGD 3: 464. 1995.
Plectranthus ternifolius D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 117. 1825; FKH 208. 1912.

Perennial robust herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–2 m tall. Stems erect; branches hexagonal, densely tomentose‑villous. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 or 4; petiole 2–3(–10) mm; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to oblong, rarely ovate‑oblong, 2–12 × 0.7–5 cm, base broadly cuneate to cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acute to acuminate, rarely obtuse, margin serrate, adaxially ± wrinkled, pilose to villous, abaxially densely whitish or dull yellow tomentose. Cymes many‑flowered, ca. 6 mm in diam., forming terminal and axillary, compact spikes; floral leaves similar to stem leaves, gradually reduced, bract‑like apically. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.3 mm, lengthening to 4 mm in fruit, densely grey or tawny villous; teeth triangular, equal, ca. 0.5 mm, obscurely veined. Corolla white to purplish; upper lip purple‑spotted, 5–6 mm. Stamens and style usually included. Nutlets triquetrous, ovoid, ca. 1.8 × 1 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng. HK sheet 22127, 22128, 22130.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar, Bangladesh, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Open grassy uplands, thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Dec.–May of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Itea chinensis Hook. & Arn. 老鼠刺（鼠刺）
Bot. Beech. Voy. 189, fig. 39. 1833; FHK 129. 1861; FKH 99. 1912; FGZ 285. 1956; FFJ 2: 237, fig. 200. 1984; FRPS 35(1): 271, pl. 62: 1 – 2. 1995; FGD 3: 228. 1995; FOC 8: 426. 2001.

Shrub or small tree, 4 – 15 m. Young branchlets glabrous. Petioles 1 – 2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thinly leathery, obovate or ovate-oblong, 5 – 12( – 15) × 2.5 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin obscurely glandular-crenulate at upper half or subentire, slightly revolute, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, erect, 3 – 6 cm, glabrous or puberulous; bracts linear-subulate, 1 – 2 mm. Flowers many; pedicels slender, ca. 3 mm, puberulous. Calyx shallowly cupular; lobes triangular-lanceolate, ca. 1 mm, puberulous. Petals erect at anthesis, white, lanceolate, 2.5 – 3 mm. Stamens nearly as long as petals or slightly longer; filaments puberulous. Ovary superior, puberulous. Capsule narrowly ellipsoidal, 6 – 9 mm, puberulous, apex acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 793, 2387, 7021.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan; Bhutan, Laos, India.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Aug.
Notes: Some specimens were misidentified as Itea chinensis var. oblonga (Hand.-Mazz.) C. Y. Wu previously (Check List HK Plants 122. 2002).

Ixeridium chinense (Thunb.) Tzvelev 中華小苦蕒（山苦蕒）
Fl. URSS 29: 390. 1964; FRPS 80(1): 251. 1997.
Prenanthes chinensis Thunb., Fl. Jap. 310. 1784.
Lactuca chinensis (Thunb.) Nakai, Bot. Mag. Tokyo 17: 89. 1903.
Ixeris chinensis (Thunb.) Nakai, Bot. Mag. Tokyo 34: 152. 1920; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 1. 1967; FTW ed. 2, 4: 996. 1998; FGD 8: 271. 2007; Check List HK Plants 283. 2002; 97. 2004.
Ixeris versicolor auct. non DC.: FHK 193. 1861.
Lactuca versicolor auct. non Sch.‑Bip.: FKH 150. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 15–60 cm tall, branched apically. Leaves glabrous on both surfaces. Basal leaves narrowly elliptic, linear or oblanceolate, 8–23 × 0.3–2 cm, base narrowed down as winged petiole, apex acute, obtuse or attenuate, margin subentire or toothed, undivided, or sometimes pinnatilobed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect with lateral segments 2–7 pairs; segments triangular, linear‑triangular or linear, the middle segments largest, becoming smaller towards both ends. Cauline leaves few, about 2–4, rarely none, lanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, 5–9 cm, undivided or pinnatifid, margin entire or mucronate‑dentate, base slightly to broadly widen and auriculate, amplexicaul, apex acuminate. Upper leaves bract‑like. Capitula erect at maturity, homogamous with all florets ligulate and bisexual, corymbose at terminal. Involucres cylindric, about 7–9 mm; phyllaries 3 – 4‑seriate, glabrous; outer layers ovate, 1–1.8 × 0.8–1 mm, acute; inner layers oblong‑lanceolate, 7–9 × 1–2 mm, acute or obtuse, margin scarious. Florets 21–25 per head, corolla yellow, 7–10 mm. Cypselae brown or reddish brown, narrowly elliptic, 2.8–4 × 0.3–0.6 mm, obtusely 10‑ribbed, minutely hirtellous along ribs particularly the upper portion, apex acute and beaked, the beak filiform, 1.8–2.8 mm. Pappus 3–4 mm, white, scaberulous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Fanling, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung. P. S. Choi 423; Y. W. Lam 486; S. Y. Hu 10067(CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Japan, Korea, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ixeridium gracile (DC.) J. H. Pak & Kawano 纖細苦蕒菜
Mem. Fac. Sci. Kyoto Univ., Ser. Biol. 15(1–2): 45. 1992.
Ixeridium gracile (DC.) Shih, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 31: 545. 1993; FRPS 80(1): 257. 1997.
Ixeris gracilis (DC.) Stebbins, J. Bot. 75: 50. 1937; FGD 8: 273, fig. 166. 2007; Check List HK Plants 284. 2002; 97. 2004.
Lactuca gracilis DC., Prodr. 7: 140. 1838; FHN 3: 427. 1974.

Perennial herbs, 15–50 cm tall, glabrous. Stem erect, slender, apically many‑branched. Basal leaves rosulate, with winged petiole; leaf blade linear to linear lanceolate, 7–15 cm × 5–9 mm, margin entire, narrowed towards both ends. Cauline leaves few, linear to linear‑lanceolate, base sessile. Capitula numerous, terminal, corymbose to corymbose‑paniculate, with ca. 6 florets. Involucre very small, cylindric, ca. 6 mm. Phyllaries in 2 rows, abaxially glabrous; outer phyllaries 2 or 3, ovate, less than ca. 1 × 0.5 mm; inner phyllaries linear‑elliptic, ca. 6 × 0.8 mm. Florets yellow. Achenes brown, narrowly pyramidal, ca. 3 mm, with 10 slender rib or lines, apically gradually narrowed into a filiform ca. 1 mm curved beak. Pappus brown to pale yellow, ca. 3 mm, scabridulous.

Locality: Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 488.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Myanmar, India, Bhutan, Nepal.
Ecology: Cultivated areas, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ixeris japonica (Burm. f.) Nakai 剪刀股
Bot. Mag. Tokyo 40: 575. 1926; FRPS 80(1): 242. 1997; FGD 8: 270. 2007.
Lapsana japonica Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 174. 1768.
Lactuca debilis (Thunb.) Benth. ex Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19: 533. 1874; FKH 150. 1912.
Ixeris debilis A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. Arts, n.s. 6(2): 397. 1858; Benth., FHK 193. 1861.
Lactuca stolonifera auct. non A. Gray: FKH 150. 1912.

Perennial herbs. Stem base creeping and forming adventitious roots at nodes, upper part erect, 12–35 cm tall. All leaves glabrous above and beneath. Radical leaves persistent at anthesis, spatulate‑oblanceoalte or ligulate, 3 – 17 × 1–3.5 cm, base narrowed into long petiole, margin entire, toothed, pinnatilobed, pinnatifid, or lyrately pinnatilobed to pinnatifid, apical lobes elliptic or obovate, apex obtuse or rounded, mucronulate; lateral segments 1 – 3 pairs, obliquely triangular or elliptic, acute or obtuse. Cauline leaves few, similar to the basal ones, or appearing narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, base narrowed, sessile or shortly petiolate. Upper leaves small, ovate. Capitula corymbose at terminal. Involucres campanulate, 12–14 × 7 mm; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; outer 1–2 layers ovate, 2–5.5 × 1–1.5 mm, acute; inner ones oblong‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 12–14 × 2–3 mm, obtuse, abaxial side glabrous, sometimes with crested appendages near apex. Ligulate florets 24 per head, corolla yellow, 12–15 mm. Cypselae brown, fusiform, 5–6 × 1 mm, glabrous, sharply and acutely 10‑ribbed as wings, apex acute and bearing filiform beak 2 mm. Pappus 6.5–7 mm, white, scaberulous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3249; Y. W. Lam 467; S. Y. Hu 10113 (CUHK).
Distribution: Distributed in S, E, C & NE China; also in Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ixeris polycephala Cass. 多頭苦蕒菜
Dict. Sci. Nat. 24: 50. 1822; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 6. 1967; FRPS 80(1): 243. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 998. 1998; FGD 8: 271. 2007.

Annual or perennial herbs; stem erect, 10–80 cm tall, branched, glabrous. Leaves glabrous above and beneath, margin entire or loosely mucronulate near base. Basal leaves linear or linear‑lanceolate, 6–12 × 0.5–0.8 cm, base attenuate to the short petiole, apex acute. Lower and middle cauline leaves sessile, linear or lanceolate, 5 – 24 × 1.2–3 cm, sagittate and semi‑amplexicaul basally, acute apically. Upper leaves gradually smaller in size when growing upward. Capitula many, corymbose or in false umbelliform at terminal, nodding after anthesis; peduncle 5 – 10 mm, having few bracteoles 0.5–2 mm. Involucres cylindric, 5–7 × 2.5–3.5 mm, becoming ovoid upon fruiting; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; outer 1–2 layers tiny, ovate, 0.5–0.8 × 0.2–0.3 mm, acute, inner ones in one row, lanceolate, 5–6 × 1.1–1.5 mm, acute or obtuse, margin membranous, abaxial side sometimes with cristate appendages near apex. Ligulate florets 10 – 25 per head, corolla yellow, rarely white, 4 – 4.5 mm. Cypselae fusiform, 2.5 × 0.8 mm, brown, glabrous, sharply and acutely 10‑ribbed as wings, apex acute and rostrate, rostrum 1–1.2 mm, filiform. Pappus 3 mm, white, scaberulous, persistent.

Locality: Sai Kung, Fanling. Y. W. Lam 490; S. Y. Hu 6941, 10008 (CUHK).
Distribution: Distributed in S, SW, C & E China; also in Korea, Japan, India.
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ixonanthes reticulata Jack 黏木
Malay Misc. 2(7) : 51. 1822; Hance, J. Bot. 14: 243. 1876.
Ixonanthes chinensis Champ., Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. 2: 100. 1850; FKH 53. 1912; FHN 2: 110, fig. 350. 1965; FFJ 2: 347, fig. 265. 1985; FRPS 43(1): 113. 1998; FGD 4: 166, fig. 107. 2000.

Evergreen tree or shrub, 4–20 m tall. Bark brown. Stipules to 1 mm. Petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade papery to leathery, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 6–14 × 3– 5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex to slightly obtuse, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences lax; peduncle 5–8 cm. Flowers ca. 6 mm in diam. Pedicel 5–8 mm. Sepals ovate-oblong, 4–5 mm. Petals white, broadly ovate, 4–5.5 mm. Stamens 10, exserted; filament up to 2 cm. Disk cupular, ca. 1 cm in diam., with 10 grooves. Ovary globose, ca. 3 × 2 mm, glabrous. Styles to 2 cm. Capsule long ellipsoidal, 2–3 × 1 cm, brownish black, striate, with persistent enlarged sepals and petals at base. Seeds oblong, 0.8–1 cm; wing 1–1.5 cm, membranous.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung, Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 1025; Y. S. Lau 3170; Y. W. Lam 785.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets or thin forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen of Ixonanthes chinensis was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong kong Island between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Ixora chinensis Lam. 龍船花
Encycl. 3: 344. 1789; FKH 132. 1912; FRPS 71(2): 37, pl. 11: 1 – 5. 1999; D. M. Bridson, Kew Bull. 55: 1012. 2000; FYN 15: 212, pl. 43: 8 – 12. 2003; FGD 6: 203. 2005.
Ixora stricta Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 10. 1814, nom nud.; Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 388. 1820; FHK 158. 1861.
Tsiangia hongkongensis (Seem.) But, Hsue & P. T. Li, Blumea 31: 311. 1986; FPRS 71(2): 110. 1999.
Gaertnera hongkongensis Seem., Bot. Voy. Herald 384. 1857.

Evergreen shrubs, 0.5–2 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves subleathery; petioles thick, 2–5 mm; stipules broadly ovate, 3–5 mm including the aristate apex; leaf blade lanceolate, oblong‑lanceolate or oblong‑oblanceolate, 6–13 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate or obtuse; apex acute, tip blunt, lateral veins slender, 7–8 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal, trichotomous, subsessile, the branches and pedicels scarlet‑orange; primary branches 6–15 mm; pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx‑tube 1–1.5 mm; lobes 4, triangular, ca. 0.8 mm. Corolla scarlet‑orange; tube slender, 3 – 4 cm; lobes 4, elliptic, (5–)7–9 × 3.5–7 mm, apex rounded, spreading. Style and anthers exserted. Drupe globular, 6–8 mm in diam., reddish black when mature.

Locality: To Fung Shan, Man Kam To, Sai Kung, Ha Pak Nai, also widely cultivated. L. T. Lo 558; Y. W. Lam 1012; HK sheet 40210.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Gaertnera hongkongensis was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
