Jacaranda mimosifolia D. Don. 藍花楹
Bot. Reg. 8: 631, t. 631. 1822; FRPS 69: 56. 1990; FFJ 5: 91, fig. 100. 1993.
Jacaranda acutifolia auct. non Humb. & Bonpl.: FGZ 609. 1956; FHN 3: 533. 1974.

Deciduous tree to 15 m tall, 45 cm in d.b.h.; bark grey. Leaves 2‑pinnately compound, 15–30 cm, pinnae over 10 pairs; pinnae 5–10 cm, leaflets 16–24 pairs; leaflets small, papery, sessile, narrowly elliptic, 0.6–1.2 × 0.2–0.7 cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate, margin entire, slightly revolute, glabrous or puberulent along veins and margin. Panicles terminal, many‑flowered. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1 mm, apex 5‑dentate. Corolla bilabiate, bluish purple, tube tubular‑campanulate, 3–4 mm, white adaxially, throat 0.7–1.2 cm wide, lobes 0.3–0.8 cm, pubescent abaxially. Stamens didynamous; filaments pubescent at lower half; anthers 1‑celled, ca. 2 mm; staminodes 2 – 2.5 cm, glandular hairy at upper part. Pistil 2.2–2.5 cm; ovary 2 – 3.5 mm, glabrous. Capsule orbicular, ca. 5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1830; HK sheet 21204.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan (cultivated); native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Jacquemontia paniculata (Burm. f.) Hallier f. 小牽牛
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16: 541. 1893; FHN 3: 478, fig. 869. 1974; FTW 4: 380, pl. 1049. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 45, pl. 1: 5 – 6. 1979; FFJ 4: 485, fig. 387. 1989; FOC 16: 285. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 374, pl. 168. 1998; FGD 4: 340, fig. 202. 2000.
Ipomoea paniculata Burm. f., Fl. Indica 50. 1768.
Convolvulus parviflorus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 29. 1794; FKH 181. 1912.
Convolvulus violaceus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 29. 1794.
Jacquemontia parviflora (Vahl) Roberty, Candollea 14: 32. 1952.
Jacquemontia violacea (Vahl) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 8(1): 61. 1838; FHK 239. 1861.

Twining herb. Stems slender, terete, stellate‑pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole 1–5 cm, stellate‑pubescent; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 3.5–7 cm, base cordate to truncate, apex acuminate, mucronulate, rarely acute or obtuse, ± stellate‑pubescent or subgl abrous on both sur fa c e s . Inf lor e s c enc e s umbelliform‑cymose, loose to dense, several – many‑flowered; peduncle 1 – 6 cm; bracts subulate, ca. 2 mm. Pedicel 3–6 mm, pubescent. Sepals unequal, stellate‑pubescent on both surfaces; outer 3 ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 6 mm; inner 2 smaller, ovate. Corolla pale purple or red, funnelform, 1–1.2 cm; limb shallowly 5‑lobed. Ovary glabrous. Style filiform, ca. 8 mm; stigmas 2, oblong. Capsule globose, 3–4 mm in diam., 8‑valved, glabrous. Seeds 1.5–2 mm, minutely tuberculate, glabrous, edges narrowly winged.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 758, 2961; Y. W. Lam 1131.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia, tropical E Africa, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Thickets, roadsides, often dry soils. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Dec.

Jasminanthes mucronata (Blanco) W. D. Stevens & P. T. Li 黑鰻藤
Novon 5: 10. 1995; FOC 16: 242. 1995.
Apocynum mucronatum Blanco, Fl. Filip. 852. 1837.
Stephanotis chinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 53. 1853; FHK 227. 1861; FKH 172. 1912.
Stephanotis mucronata (Blanco) Merr., Sp. Blancoan 316. 1918; FRPS 63: 466, pl. 174. 1977; FGD 1: 520, fig. 594. 1987.

Lianas, to 12 m. stems with 2 lines of hairs, lenticellate. Petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blade ovate‑oblong, 7–12 × 4.5–8 cm, papery, base cordate, apex acuminate, pubescent or glabrescent, lateral veins ca. 8 on each side of midvein. Cymes usually 2–4‑flowered; peduncle 1.5–2 cm; bracteoles ovate, pubescent abaxially. Pedicels 2–3 cm. Sepals oblong, 7 mm. Corolla white, with purple juice; tube 2 cm, glabrous outside; lobes falcate, 3 × 0.5 cm, spreading. Gynostegium shorter than corolla‑tube. Corona‑lobes 5, shorter than anthers. Apical appendage of anther oblong‑ovate, longer than stigma; pollinia ellipsoidal. Stigma head capitate, apex obscurely 2‑lobed. Follicles lanceolate, 12 × 1 cm, glabrous. Seeds oblong, 1 cm; coma 2.5 cm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 222; HK sheet 19025, 30755.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Montane forests, often attached to trees; 100–600 m. Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Jasminum elongatum (Bergius) Willd. 扭肚藤
Sp. Pl. ed. 4, 1(1): 37. 1797; FRPS 61: 211, pl. 56: 2 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 317. 1996; FGD 5: 434. 2003.
Nyctanthes elongata Bergius, Philos. Trans. 61: 289, pl. 11. 1772.
Jasminum undulatum Ker‑Gawl. Bot. Reg. 6: pl. 436. 1820; FKH 165. 1912.
Jasminum amplexicaule Buch.‑Ham. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 60. 1837.

Scandent shrub, 1–7 m. Branchlets terete, densely tomentose. Leaves opposite, simple; petiole 2–5 mm; leaf blade papery, ovate to lanceolate, 4–7 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base rounded, truncate, or subcordate, apex acute or obtuse and mucronulate, pubescent or glabrescent except for hairy veins abaxially, lateral veins pinnate, 3 or 5 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal or axillary, many‑flowered, congested, yellow‑pubescent; bracts 1–3, linear or ovate‑lanceolate, 1–5 mm, or absent. Flowers heterostylic; pedicels 1–4 mm. Calyx densely tomentose, tube 1.5– 3 mm; lobes 6–8, subulate‑filiform, ca. 1 cm. Corolla white, salverform; tube 2–3 cm; lobes 6–9, lanceolate, 10 × 2 – 3 mm. Fruit subglobose or ovoid, 10 × 5–8 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 2551.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar to Himalayas.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Jasminum lanceolaria Roxb. 清香藤
Fl. Ind. 1: 97. 1820; FHN 3: 205. 1974; FFJ 4: 387, fig. 321. 1989; FRPS 61: 197, pl. 52: 1 – 2. 1992; FOC 15: 314. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 134. 1998; FGD 5: 430. 2003.
Jasminum lanceolaria var. puberulum Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 78. 1889.
Jasminum shimadai Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 9: 70 – 71, pl. 5, fig. 26. 1920.
Jasminum pachyllum Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26(173): 79 – 80. 1889; FKH 165. 1912.
Jasminum paniculatum auct. non Roxb.: FHK 216. 1861; FKH 165. 1912.

Large scandent shrubs, 5–15 m. Branchlets terete, sometimes angled, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves opposite, trifoliolate; petioles 1–4.5 cm, adaxially canaliculate; leaflet blade elliptic, ovate, or lanceolate, 5–13 × 1.5–6.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acute or acuminate; lateral veins obscure; petiolules 1–3 cm; terminal leaflet slightly larger than or equal to lateral leaflets. Compound cymes paniculate, terminal or axillary, many‑flowered; bracts linear, 2–5 mm. Flowers fragrant, heterostylic; pedicels 0–5 mm, stout. Calyx tubular, 2–3 mm; lobes 5, deltate. Corolla white, salverform; tube 2–2.5 cm; lobes 4–5, ovate to oblong, 7–10 × 4 mm. Fruit globose or ellipsoidal, 0.5–1 × 0.8–1.5 cm, black when matured.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 42, 1287, 1341.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Jasminum mesnyi Hance 雲南黃素馨
J. Bot. 20(230): 37. 1882; FFJ 4: 387, fig. 322. 1989; FRPS 61: 183. 1992; FOC 15: 311. 1996; FGD 5: 430. 2003.
Jasminum primulinum Hemsl., Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1895(100 – 101): 109. 1895.

Evergreen shrubs, scandent, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets slight, 4‑angled, glabrous. Leaves opposite, trifoliolate; petioles 1 cm, adaxially canaliculate; leaflets sub‑leathery, narrowly ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, glabrous, terminal one larger 3–5 × 1–2 cm, basally decurrent into a short petiolule (ca. 1–2.5 mm); lateral leaflets smaller, sessile, 2.5–4 × 0.7–1 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse and mucronulate; lateral veins and veinlets obscure. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves; pedicels stout, 3–8 mm; bracts 2–5, leafy, narrowly ovate to obovate, 5 × 2 mm. Calyx campanulate, tube 2.5–5; lobes 5–8, leafy, lanceolate, 4–7 mm. Corolla yellow, 2–4.5 cm in diam.; tube 1–1.2 cm; lobes 6–8, sometimes doubled, obovate to oblong, nerviform, 1.2–1.8 cm. Fruit ellipsoidal, 6–8 mm in diam., two carpels connate at base.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2096
Distribution: Guizhou, Yunnan, SW Sichuan, widely cultivated in China.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Mar.
Uses: Ornamental.

Jasminum multiflorum (Burm. f.) Andrews 毛茉莉
Bot. Repos. 8: t. 496. 1807; FRPS 61: 213, pl. 56: 1. 1992; FOC 15: 317. 1996; FGD 5: 435. 2003.
Nyctanthes multiflora Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 5: pl. 3, fig. 1. 1768.

Scandent shrubs, 1–6 m. Branchlets terete, slender, densely yellow‑pilose. Leaves simple, opposite; petiole 4–10 mm, densely pilose, articulate near base; leaf blade elliptic, ovate, 2.5–5.5 × 1.5–3 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex acuminate, acute or blunt, mucronulate, papery or thinly leathery, scattered pilose on both surfaces, or glabrous adaxially, lateral veins pinnate, 4–6 on each side of midvein, flat adaxially, raised adaxially. Cymes terminal or axillary, many‑flowered, congested, peduncle densely yellow‑tomentose; pedicels short or absent; bracts leafy, basal ovate, 1–3 cm, upper linear, 3–5 mm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx densely yellow‑pilose; tube ca. 1 mm; lobes 6–9, subulate, 2–6 mm. Corolla white, tube 1–1.7 × 0.2–0.3 cm; lobes 7–9, oblong, 1–1.5 cm × 0.4–0.6 cm. Fruit ellipsoidal, brown.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 30544, 40752.
Distribution: Native to SE Asia and India, widely cultivated in the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Jasminum nervosum Lour. 青藤仔
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 20 – 21. 1790; FHN 3: 207. 1974; FRPS 61: 209, pl. 54: 4 – 5. 1992; FOC 15: 316. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 135, pl. 50. 1998; FGD 5: 434. 2003.
Jasminum elegans (Hemsl.) Yamam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 13: 151. 1914, non Knobl. 1893.
Jasminum nervosum var. elegans (Hemsl.) L. C. Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 2(1): 56. 1952.
Jasminum nervosum var. villosum (H. Lév.) L. C. Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 2(1): 55. 1952.
Jasminum laurifolium auct. non Roxb.: FKH 165. 1912.

Scandent shrub, 1–5 m. Branchlets terete, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Leaves simple, opposite; petioles 5– 10 mm, articulate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 3–10 × 1.8–4 cm, papery, base broadly cuneate, rounded to subtruncate, apex acuminate to acute, glabrous or puberulous abaxially, especially on veins; veins 3 or 5 from base, outer pair usually obscure when 5‑veined. Cymes terminal or axillary, 1–5‑flowered; peduncle 0–12 mm, glabrous; bracts linear, 5–13 mm; pedicels 2–10 mm. Calyx glabrous, cupular, tube 2 – 2.5 mm; lobes 6 – 8, subulate to linear, 5–8 mm, often enlarged to 15 mm in fruit. Corolla white, salverform; tube 1–2 cm; lobes 8–10, linear to lanceolate, nearly as long as tube, apex acuminate to blunt. Fruit subglobose, red becoming black, 9–15 × 7–13 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 137, 1236, 1540.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, India, Bhutan, Sikkim, Nepal.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.

Jasminum sambac (L.) Aiton 茉莉花
Hort. Kew. 1: 8. 1789; FHN 3: 208. 1974; FFJ 4: 385, fig. 319. 1989; FRPS 61: 218, pl. 55: 4. 1992; FOC 15: 318. 1996; FGD 5: 435. 2003.
Nyctanthes sambac L., Sp. Pl. 1: 6. 1753.

Diffuse or scandent shrubs, to 3 m. Branchlets terete, slightly compressed near nodes, pubescent to glabrous. Leaves opposite, simple; petioles 3–5 mm, pubescent, articulate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, or sometimes obovate, 3–10 × 2.5–7 cm, base rounded, blunt or subcordate, apex acute, blunt or cuspidate, glabrous or sparsely pilose abaxially, usually with tufted hairs at vein axils, lateral veins pinnate, 5–6 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal, usually 3‑flowered; peduncle 1–4 cm, pubescent; bracts subulate, 4–6 mm; flowers very fragrant; pedicel 0.5–1 cm. Calyx cupular, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; lobes 8 – 9, subulate to linear, 5–8 mm. Corolla white, usually doubled; tube 0.6–1.2 cm; lobes oblong to suborbicular, 11–15 × 7–10 mm. Fruit globose, purple‑black, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1114, 1850.
Distribution: Native to India, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, additive (flavoring), material (essential oils), medicinal (folklore).

Jasminum sinense Hemsl. 華素馨
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 80 – 81. 1889; FKH 165. 1912; FFJ 4: 386, fig. 320. 1989; FRPS 61: 199, pl. 52: 3 – 4. 1992; FOC 15: 314. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 135. 1998; FGD 5: 430. 2003.

Scandent shrub, 1–8 m. Branchlets terete, densely rusty villous. Leaves opposite, trifoliolate; petioles 5–15 mm; leaflet blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, papery; base rounded, apex acuminate to acute; rusty pubescent on both surfaces, rarely glabrous and rusty pubescent only along veins; terminal leaflet 3–10 × 2–5 cm, petiolule 0.8–3 cm; lateral leaflets smaller, 1.5–4.5 × 1–2.5 cm, petiolule 2–3 mm. Cymes terminal or axillary, many‑flowered congested panicles, rarely 1‑flowered in leaf axils. Flowers fragrant, heterostylic; pedicels 1–5 mm. Calyx pilose; lobes linear, 1–5 mm, enlarged in fruit. Corolla white or yellowish, salverform; tube 2–3.5 cm × 1–1.5 mm; lobes 5, oblong or lanceolate, apex acute, 7–14 mm; anthers lanceolate, 3 mm; style tenuous, 1.5–2 cm; stigma clavate. Fruit black, globose or subglobose, 8–17 mm × 6–10 mm.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 8952, 9929; Y. W. Lam 1741.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–May of the following year.

Jatropha curcas L. 麻瘋樹
Sp. Pl. 1006. 1753; FHK 309. 186l; FKH 237. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 148. 1996; FGD 5: 110, fig. 64. 2003.

Shrub or treelet 2–5 m tall, with watery juice; branches stout, glabrous. Leaves papery; stipules small; petioles 6–18 cm; leaf blade ovate-orbicular, 7–18 × 6–16 cm, base cordate, apex acute, unlobed or 3–5 angular or obtusely lobed, glabrous adaxially, puberulous on veins or glabrous abaxially; palmately 5–7-veined. Cymes axillary, 6–10 cm; bracts lanceolate, 4–8 mm. Male flowers: calyx-lobes 5, ca. 4 mm, connate at base; petals oblong, greenish yellow, ca. 6 mm, connate up to middle, hairy adaxially; disk-glands 5, nearly terete; stamens 10, the inner 5 united in a column. Female flowers: pedicels elongate; calyx-lobes free, ca. 6 mm; petals and disk-glands as in male flowers; ovary 3-locular, glabrous; styles bifid at apex. Capsules of 2–3 bivalved cocci, ellipsoidal or globose, 2.5–3 cm; seeds ellipsoidal, 1.5–2 cm, black.

Locality: Fanling, Tai Po,Yuen Long,Wu Kuai Sha, Luk Keng, Shek Pik Reservoir, Sheung Shui, Sha Tin, Lantau Island (cultivated). Y. S. Lau 795, 2193; L. T. Lo 439; S. Y. Hu 12912 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to America; cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; cultivated and naturalized elsewhere in tropics.
Ecology: Hedges and near habitats. Flowering: Sep. –Nov.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Material (lipids), poison (mammals).

Jatropha gossypifolia L. 棉葉麻瘋樹
Sp. Pl. 1006. 1753; FGD 5: 110. 2003.

Shrub 1 –2 m tall, with milky juice. Leaves red when young, deep green or glossy coppery green and with red veins when mature; petioles 5 – 10 cm, with branched glandular scaly or bristly hairs; stipules capillary multifid glandular; leaf blade broadly ovate or sub-orbicular in outline, 5 – 10 cm, palmately 3 – 5-lobed or 3 – 5-partite; lobes broadest in the middle, glandular-serrulate. Cymes paniculate, terminal, 5–15 cm; bracts linear lanceolate, glandular-ciliate. Male flowers: calyx-lobes lanceolate, ca. 3 mm; petals elliptic, ivory-white, ca. 4 mm; stamens 10–12; filaments united up to middle. Female flowers: calyx-lobes lanceolate to ovate, ca. 5 mm, ciliate, persistent; petals as in male flowers; ovary hairy; styles 3, slender, free; stigma bilobed. Capsules ellipsoidal-globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., 3-ribbed, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated in Tai Po Kau. H. C. Tang 2511.
Distribution: Native to Brasil; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Jatropha integerrima Jacq. 全緣葉麻瘋樹（全緣葉珊瑚）
Enum. Pl. Carib. 32. 1760; FGD 5: 111. 2003.
Jatropha hastata Jacq., Select. Strip Amer. Hist. 256, pl. 173, f. 43. 1763.

Shrub 1 –3 m tall, with milky sap, glabrous or close-pubescent. Leaves leathery, basifixed; petioles 2 – 3 cm, pilose; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade various in shape, ovate, obovate, oblanceolate or fiddle-shaped, 9 – 11 × 2 – 4.5 cm, base broad-cuneate or rounded, often with 2 small lobes on each side; lobes caudate or sharp-acuminate, with a gland at apex, glabrous or the midvein pilose on both surfaces. Flowers scarlet to vermilion or rose, in supra-axillary cymes; peduncles 13.5 cm, glabrous; bracts lanceolate, 3 – 6 mm. Male flowers numerous; calyx ca. 3 mm, 5-lobed; petals 5, narrowly obovate, ca. 1 cm, red; stamens 10, filaments united to middle. Female flower solitary, calyx and petals as in male flowers, but slightly larger; ovary glabrous, styles 3, united at base; stigma divided into 2 linear lobes. Capsules globose, 1 × 1 cm, with 3-ridges.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34810, 34975; Hu & But 22900 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Brasil; cultivated in Hainan and Guangdong.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Jatropha multifida L. 珊瑚花
Sp. Pl. 1006. 1753; FRPS 44(2): 149. 1996; FGD 5: 111. 2003.

Shrub or treelet, 2 – 6 m tall. Branches stout, glabrous. Leaves basifixed; petioles slender, 10 – 25 cm; stipules bristle-like, 1 – 2 cm; leaf blade nearly orbicular in outline, 10 – 30 cm in diam., palmately and deeply divided into 7 – 11 lobes; lobes lanceolate, 10 – 15 cm, apex long-acuminate, often with 1 – 3 small lobelets on each side, glabrous on both surfaces. Cymes compound, terminal; peduncles 13 – 22 cm; pedicels short. Male flowers: calyx 2 – 3 mm, 5-lobed; lobes rotund, glabrous; petals 5, spathulate, ca. 4 mm, red; stamens 8, filaments connate at base, anthers elongate. Female flowers: calyx as in male flowers; petals 6 – 7 mm, red; ovary glabrous; styles 3, connate in lower half part. Capsules ellipsoidal to obovoid, ca. 3 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 24690; S. Y. Hu 11288 (CUHK); Hu & But 21137 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native of tropical and subtropical America; widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul. – Dec.; fruiting: Sep. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, poison (mammals), medicinal (folklore).

Jatropha podagrica Hook. 佛肚樹
Curt. Hot. Mag. 74, t. 4376. 1848; FHK 301. 1861; FKH 237. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 148. 1996; FGD 5: 111. 2003.

Erect shrub to 2 m tall. Stems swollen at base; branches stout and short, fleshy, with bristled scars. Leaves peltate; petioles 6–16 cm, glabrous; stipules spiniform, 1–2 mm, glandular tipped, persistent; leaf blade orbricular-ovate to elliptic, 8–18 × 6–16 cm, base truncate or obtuse, apex obtuse, entire or shallowly 2 – 6-lobed, with obtuse sinuses, green and shining adaxially, paler abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces. Cymes terminal, long-pedunculate; pedicels red. Flowers small, coral-red; calyx ca. 2 mm, lobed to middle; petals obovate-oblong, ca. 6 mm; stamens 6 – 8, connate at base, anthers nearly as long as the filaments; ovary glabrous; styles 3, connate at base, bifid at apex. Capsules ellipsoidal, 1.3 – 1.8 × 1.5 cm, with 3 longitudinal grooves; seeds ca. 1.1 cm, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1512; L. T. Lo 356; HK sheet 24692; K. Y. Chan 1561 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to America; cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi,Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely cultivated in tropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental, poison (mammals), medicinal (folklore).

Juncellus serotinus (Rottb.) C. B. Clarke 水莎草
Fl. Brit. India 6: 594. 1893; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 159. 1961; FYN 15: 644. 2003; FGD 8: 335. 2007.
Cyperus serotinus Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 31. 1773; FTW ed. 2, 5: 250. 2000; FOC 23: 239. 2010.

Perennial; rhizomes stoloniferous, slender stolons terminated by a small tuber. Culms solitary or a few together, erect, 40–100 cm tall, triquetrous with shallowly concave sides, rather soft. Leaves few, usually shorter than the culms, rarely slightly overtopping culm; blades linear, 3–10 mm wide, folded toward base, flattish above, soft; sheaths brownish. Corymbs compound, sublax, 7–15 cm long and as wide; anthelas 5–7, unequal, 2–16 cm, each bearing 1–3 spikes; spikes ovate-elliptic, 2–4 cm, subloosely bearing 5–17 spikelets; rachis hispidulous to nearly smooth; leafy bracts 3–4, lowest to 8 mm wide, to twice as long as corymb. Spikelets patent, linear to linear-lanceolate, 1–2 cm × 2–2.75 mm, 10–34-flowered. Glumes broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 2 mm, reddish brown to dark brown, apex obtuse, 5–7-veined, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style short; stigmas 2. Achenes orbicular-obovate, plano-convex, 1.5 mm, greyish brown.

Locality: New Territories. W. J. Tutcher 8115; S. Y. Hu 8281 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, NW Himalaya, C Europe, Mediterranean region.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Juncus effusus L. 燈心草
Sp. Pl. 1: 326. 1753; FRPS 13(3): 160. 1997; FOC 24: 48. 2000; FGD 6: 403. 2005.

Perennial herb, densely tufted. Rhizome shortly creeping, thick. Stems terete, 25–90 cm or taller, 1–3(–4) mm in diam., striate; pith continuous. Cataphylls closely embracing stem, reddish brown to chestnut brown, sheath-like, 2–22 cm. Inflorescences pseudolateral, densely to laxly many-flowered; involucral bract erect, seemingly a continuation of stem, terete, 5–28 cm. Perianth segments usually pale brown, linear-lanceolate, 2–2.7 × ca. 0.8 mm, unequal, with outer ones slightly longer than inner ones, apex acute. Stamens 3(or 6), about 2/3 the length of perianth; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm, slightly shorter than filaments. Ovary 3-locular; style very short. Capsules ovoid to oblong, slightly depressed or not, subequaling or slightly longer than perianth, 3-septate, apex obtuse. Seeds ovoid-oblong, 0.5–0.6 mm, reticulate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 29955, 42769.
Distribution: Widely distributed worldwide.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Material (weaving), medicinal (folklore).

Juncus prismatocarpus R. Br. 笄石菖
Prodr. 259. 1810; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 265. 1977; FOC 24: 54. 2000; FGD 6: 405. 2005.
Juncus leschenaultii J. Gay ex Laharpe, Mem. Soc. Hist. Nat. Paris 3: 137. 1827; FHK 330. 1861.
Juncus prismatocarpus R. Br. var. leschenaultii (J. Gay ex Laharpe) Buchenau, Pflanzenr. 25(36): 180. 1906.
Juncus alatus auct non Franch. & Sav.: FKH 285. 1912.

Perennial herb, tufted, (8–)10–65 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, terete or compressed, 0.7–3 mm in diam. Basal leaves few, cauline leaves 2–4; leaf sheath auricles obtuse, short; leaf blade linear, terete to compressed, 10–25 cm × (1–)2–4 mm, distinctly and perfectly to incompletely septate, apex obtuse, acute, or acuminate. Inflorescences terminal, sparingly or much branched; involucral bract leaf-like, shorter than inflorescence; heads 5–10(–30), globose to hemispheric, 7–10 mm in diam., (3–)8–15(–20)-flowered. Bracts 2–2.5 mm, broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, thinly membranous. Perianth segments narrowly lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, subequal, veins longitudinal, apex acute. Stamens 3, inserted opposite to outer perianth segments; filaments 1.2–1.4 mm; anthers 0.9–1 mm. Stigmas very long, often recurved or sinuous. Capsules narrowly prismatic, 3.8–4.5 mm; angles prominent, acute; placentas not or only slightly intruded, hence fruit 1-locular. Seeds wax-yellow, oblong, 0.6–0.8 mm, regularly longitudinally ribbed; transverse veins faint, remote.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 1761; HK sheet 7667, 39861.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Taiwan; widely distributed worldwide temperate and subtropical sea area and salt lakes.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Juncus prismatocarpus R. Br. subsp. teretifolius K. F. Wu 圓柱葉燈心草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 32: 455. 1994; FRPS 13(3): 193. 1997; FOC 24: 55. 2000; FGD 6: 406. 2005.

Differs in these characters: Plants large, robust. Leaf blade terete, sometimes slightly compressed when dry, distinctly and perfectly septate.

Locality: Tsing Fai Tong, Sha Lo Tung. Y. Yip s.n. (HK sheet 42848, 42849)
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Paddy fields, marshes. Fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Notes: According to FOC (24: 54. 2000), this subspecies is morphologically very close to Juncus wallichianus, and their relationship awaits further research to clarify. Juncus wallichianus differs in the apex of its capsules being cuspidate (cf. FOC Ill. 24: fig. 44: 7 – 9. 2002; Fl. Nei Mongol., ed. 2, 5: 453, fig. 187: 1–5. 1994).

Juniperus chinensis L. 圓柏
Syst. Nat., ed. 12, 2: 660. 1767; Mant. Pl. 1: 127. 1767; FOC 4:74. 1999; FGD 4: 30. 2000.
Sabina chinensis (L.) Ant., Cupress. Gatt. 54. 1857; FRPS 7:362, pl. 80: 6 – 8. 1978.

Tree to 25 m, 3.5 m in d.b.h., dioecious, rarely monoecious; bark greyish brown, fissured; branches spreading; branchlets straight or slightly curved, terete or 4-angled, 1–1.2 mm in diam.; crown of trees pyramidal to open, broad and irregular. Leaves dimorphic; needlelike leaves present on both young and adult plants, decussate or in whorls of 3, loosely arranged, ascending, nearly lanceolate, 6 –12 mm, with 2 white stomatal bands adaxially; scalelike leaves present on adult plants, decussate, closely appressed, 2.5–5 mm, abaxially with an elliptic slightly concave gland near center. Pollen cones yellow, ellipsoid, 2.5 –3.5 mm; microsporophylls 10–18, each with 3 or 4 pollen sacs. Seed cones mature in 2nd year, brown when ripe, usually glaucous, subglobose, 6–8 mm in diam., 1– 4-seeded. Seeds ovoid, 3–6 × 2–5 mm, slightly flattened, ridged, with resin pits, apex blunt.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 2704; HK sheet 26824.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, Myanmar, E Russia.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Juniperus chinensis L. ‘Kaizuca’ (龍柏) is also cultivated in gardens in Hong Kong for ornamental purpose. It differs from J.chinensis by its crown being cylindrical or pyramidal, branches initiating from lower part and twisted.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: Juniperus chinensis L. ‘Kaizuca’ (龍柏) is also cultivated in gardens in Hong Kong for ornamental purpose. It differs from J.chinensis by its crown being cylindrical or pyramidal, branches initiating from lower part and twisted.

records.text:
Justicia adhatoda L. 鴨嘴花
Sp. Pl. 15. 1753; FHK 264. 1861; FKH 199. 1912.
Adhatoda vasica Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 103. 1832; FHN 3: 571. 1974; FRPS 70: 277. 2002.

Shrubs, to ca. 4 m tall. Stems thickened, subquadrangular, lenticellate, pubescent when young, soon glabrescent. Petioles 0.8 – 3 cm, puberulent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 7 – 18 × 2 – 7 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, sometimes slightly falcate, margin entire, adaxially densely tomentose when young, becoming glabrescent except for tomentose along the veins, abaxially puberulent, lateral veins 9 – 12 pairs, meet near the margin. Spikes terminal and axillary, 3 – 7 cm, ovate or broadly ovate in outline. Peduncles 3 – 7 cm. Bracts ovate‑oblong, 1 – 2 × 0.5 – 1.5 cm, apex acute, margin ciliate, puberulent, 3 – 7‑veined, imbricate; bracteoles linear‑lanceolate, 1 – 1.4 × 0.4 cm, apex acute, margin ciliate, puberulent, 3 – 5‑veined. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑oblong, ca. 1 × 0.3 cm, narrowly scarious at margins, ciliate. Corolla white or pink, purplish or pinkish striped inside, 2.5 – 3 cm, broadly tubular, outside pilose; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm, faintly inflated and bent above; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, ovate‑oblong, ca. 1.8 cm, shallowly 2‑lobed, lower lip spreading, oblong‑orbicular, 3‑lobed, middle lobe suborbicular, ca. 9 × 5 mm, lateral lobes ovate, ca. 8 × 4.5 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments declinate, ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous except for silky hairy at base; anther‑thecae equal, elliptic, ca. 3.5 mm, superposed, lower one with a spherical appendage at base. Ovary pubescent especially at the tip; style ca. 2.5 cm, recurved, pubescent at lower part; stigma simple. Capsule obovoid, woody, 2.5 – 4 × 0.5 cm, stalked at base. Seeds orbicular, compressed.

Locality: Tai Tam, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan Country Park, Tai Po Kau, Kadoorie Farm. Y. S. Lau 2867; HK sheet 4281; S. Y. Hu 12970 (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated or naturalized); native to India, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Cultivated or naturalized. Flowering: Mar. – May.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), dye.

Justicia austrosinensis H. S. Lo & D. Fang 華南爵床
Guihaia 17(1): 52. 1997.
Mananthes austrosinensis (H. S. Lo & D. Fang) C. Y. Wu & C. C. Hu, FRPS 70: 292. 2002.

Herbs, 40–70 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous. Petioles 0.5–3 cm, bifariously pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blades broadly ovate or ovate‑elliptic, 7–15 × 2.5–7 cm, base cuneate and decurrent onto the petioles, apex short acuminate or acute, margin crenate or entire, glabrous, adaxially green, cystoliths numerous especially on the veins, abaxially pale green, lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Spikes mostly terminal or rarely axillary, 5–7 cm, usually 1–2  flowers subtending by one bract. Peduncles 1–3 cm, glabrous, cystoliths numerous. Bracts flabellate or broadly obovate, 5–8 × 7–9 mm, apex acuminate or obtuse, mucronate, margin ciliate; bracteoles subulate, ca. 3 mm, apex acuminate, margin ciliate. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apex acuminate, margin ciliate. Corolla yellowish green, ca. 1.3 cm, outside pilose, inside glabrous except few hairs on the filaments; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, ovate‑triangular, ca. 6 × 3 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm, apex rounded. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 4 mm; anther‑thecae unequal, ca. 2 mm, superposed, lower one spurred at base, upper one muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; style ca. 1 mm, pilose. Capsule clavate, ca. 1.2 cm, pubescent, base solid stalked, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 mm, rugose.

Locality: Ho Chung, Sai Kung, Ng Tung Chai, Castle Peak. Y. S. Au 3265; HK sheet 21462; C. J. Huang 694 (IBSC); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23472 (PE).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.
Notes: The species was reported as Justicia glauca Rottler previously (Check List HK Plants 253. 2002; 87. 2004).

Justicia brandegeana Wassh. & L. B. Sm. 蝦衣草
Flora Il. Catarin. 102. 1969.
Beloperone gutta Brandegee, Univ. Calif. Publ. Bot. 4: 278. 1912, non Justicia gutta Wall., 1830.
Calliaspidia guttata (Brandegee) Bremek., Verh. Kon. Ned. Akad. Wetensch. Afd. Natuurk., Sect. 2, 45: 54. 1948; FHN 3: 571. 1974;FRPS 70: 274. 2002; Check List HK Plants 252. 2002; 86. 2004.
Drejerella guttata (Brandegee) Bremek., Philipp. J. Sci. 80: 14. 1952.

Herbs, 0.3–1 m tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, brown, densely tomentose. Petioles 1–2 cm, tomentose; leaf blades ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 2–6 × 1–3 cm, base acuminate to rounded, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute, margin entire, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely greyish white tomentose, especially along veins, lateral veins 4–6 pairs. Spikes terminal, 2–7 cm, densely flowered, pendulous. Peduncles 5–7 mm, densely greyish tomentose. Bracts ovate, green when young, becoming wine‑red when old, 1.2–1.8 × 0.9–1.3 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute, adaxially glabrous, margin entire and ciliate, abaxially greyish white tomentose, pinnately‑veined; bracteoles broadly lanceolate to elliptic, 0.8–1.3 × 0.5–0.7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire and ciliate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially greyish white tomentose. Calyx white, densely pilose on both surfaces, 5‑lobed; lobes narrowly triangular, ca. 5 × 1 mm, apex acuminate, margin ciliate. Corolla ca. 3.2 cm, white, red spotted on throat, outside densely tomentose; tube slender, ca. 2 mm wide at base, then gradually widened to ca. 5 mm at the base of the lips; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip ca. 3.5 mm broad, entire or emarginate, lower lip ca. 5 mm broad, 3‑lobed, 3‑striped, lobes ovate, ca. 1 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 2 cm; anther‑thecae divergent, 2 – 3 mm, superposed, spurred at base. Ovary comose; style ca. 1.5 cm, retrorsely pubescent. Capsule obovate, ca. 8 mm, stalked at base, pubescent, 2‑seeded. Seeds suborbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 250, 1218; L. T. Lo 372.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Uses: Ornamental.

Justicia carnea Lindl. 珊瑚花
Edward's Bot. Reg. 17: pl. 1397. 1831.
Cyrtanthera carnea (Lindl.) Bremek., Verh. Ned. Akad. Wetensch. Naturk. Afd. Sect. 2, 45(21): 50. 1948.
Jacobinia carnea (Lindl.) G. Nicholson, Ill. Dict. Gard. 2: 206. 1885.

Herbs or subshrubs, to 2 m tall. Stems subquadrangular, sulcate, glabrous or minutely puberulent. Petioles 1–2.5 cm; leaf blades membranous, oblong‑ovate, to 25 × 7 cm, sparsely puberulent, base cuneate to rounded and decurrent onto the petiole, apex acuminate. Spikes terminal, sessile, ovoid or spherical in outline, to 19 × 8 cm, densely flowered, 1–several flowers on each node; rachis puberulent. Bracts elliptic or oblong, to 2 × 1 cm, diminished in size upward, apex obtuse or rounded, moderately firm, glabrous, or sparsely hirsute, sparsely ciliate; bracteoles lanceolate, ca. 1.5 × 0.1–0.2 cm. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, ca. 1 × 0.2 cm, subhyaline, glabrous, or sparsely hirsute and ciliate towards the apex. Corolla lilac or red, outside sparsely glandular‑puberulent, ca. 6.5 cm; tube‑base ca. 2.5 mm, gradually widened to ca. 5 mm wide at throat, upper lip erect, arched and bilobed at apex, lobes ca. 1 × 0.7 mm, lower lip spreading or recurved, 3‑lobed, cuneate, ca. 8 mm wide at base of the lobes, lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2 mm. Anther‑thecae slightly superposed. Capsule unseen.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32965.
Distribution: Native to Brazil, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Uses: Ornamental.

Justicia championii T. Anderson ex Benth. 杜根藤
FHK 264. 1861, “Championi”; FKH 199. 1912.
Adhatoda chinensis Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 134. 1853, non Justicia chinensis L. ex Walp., 1845‑46.
Justicia chinensis (Champ.) Druce, Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Rep. 1916: 629. 1917, non L. 1753, nec Vahl 1791.
Calophanoides chinensis (Champ.) C. Y. Wu & H. S. Lo ex C. C. Hu, FRPS 70: 281. 2002.

Herbs, ca. 50 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, retrorsely pubescent. Petioles (0–)0.5–1.5 cm, sulcate, pubescent; leaf blades elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, ovate, 1–4(–7) × 0.5–2(–3.5) cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, sparsely pubescent when young, soon glabrescent or pilose along the midvein abaxially, cystoliths numerous adaxially, lateral veins 3–6 pairs. Flowers 1–several clustered in leaf axils. Pedicels 2–4 mm, sparsely pubescent. Bracts leaf‑like, orbicular to obovate‑spathulate, 5–8 × 3–6 mm, petiolate, glabrous or adaxially sparsely pilose, apex rounded or obtuse, pinnately‑veined; bracteoles subulate or triangular, ca. 1 mm, apex acute, glabrous or sparsely yellow puberulent. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 6–7 mm, ciliate, 1–2‑veined, yellowish white except for green along the veins. Corolla 0.8–1 cm, white, with purplish red streaks in 2 lines, outside puberulent, bilabiate, upper lip lanceolate, ca. 3.5 × 1.5 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip ovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm, 3‑lobed, middle lobe semi‑orbicular, ca. 0.8 × 1.3 mm, lateral lobes ovate, ca. 1.2 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 4 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae superposed, lower one spurred, upper one muticous. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; style ca. 6 mm, with a few hairs towards the base; stigma capitate. Capsule ca. 8 mm, glabrous, base with a solid stalk, 4‑seeded. Seeds oblong, ca. 2 × 1.5 mm, verrucose.

Locality: Mount Gough, Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Beacon Hill, Ma On Shan. HK sheet 34775, 40194, 40897.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Autumn.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian.
Notes: The holotype specimen (J. G. Champion s.n., K) was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Justicia gendarussa Burm. f. 小駁骨
Fl. Ind. 10. 1768; FHK 264. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 665. 1998.
Gendarussa vulgaris Nees, Prodr. 11: 410. 1768; FHN 3: 569. 1974; FTW 4: 632. 1978; FRPS 70: 300. 2002.

Subshrubs, 0.7–1.5 cm tall, many‑branched. Stems subterete, tumid above the nodes, glabrous. Petioles 0.3–1 cm; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 6–10 × 1–1.5 cm, base cuneate, attenuate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin subsinuate, glabrous, lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Spikes 3–12 cm, interrupted, terminal or axillary, usually in a leafy panicle. Peduncles 0.5–1.5 cm. Bracts triangular, ca. 2 × 1 mm, apex acute, ciliate; bracteoles elliptic to linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm, apex acute, ciliate. Calyx ca. 5 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 3 – 4 × 0.5 mm, subequal, apex acuminate. Corolla creamy‑white, 1.2–1.5 cm, tube‑base cylindric, 8–9 mm; limb bilabiate, upper lip triangular, ca. 7 × 3.5 mm, violet‑blotched, 2‑fid, lower lip cuneate‑obovate, basally violet dotted, 6–10 mm broad, 3‑lobed, lobes oblanceolate, 3 – 5 × 3.5 mm. Stamens 2, exserted, filaments glabrous, 3–6 mm; anther‑thecae superposed, one slightly above the other, oblong, ca. 1.2 mm, lower one spurred at base, upper one muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, glabrous; style ca. 1 cm, glabrous; stigma capitate, shortly 2‑lobed. Capsule clavate, ca. 1.2 cm.

Locality: Tsuen Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Kiu Tsui. H. C. Tang 1260; Y. S. Lau 1132, 2944.
Distribution: S & SW China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

Justicia hayatai Yamam. 早田氏爵床
Suppl. Icon. Pl. Formosa 2: 35. 1926.
Justicia procumbens L. var. hayatai (Yamam.) Ohwi, Bull. Nat. Sci. Mus. Tokyo 33: 86. 1953; FTW ed. 2, 4: 667. 1998, as “hayatae”.
Rostellularia hayatai (Yamam.) S. S. Ying, Mem. Coll. Agr. Natl. Taiwan. Univ. 29(2): 45. 1989.
Justicia hayatai Yamam. var. ciliata Yamam., Suppl. Icon. Pl. Formosa 2: 35. 1926
Rostellularia procumbens (L.) Nees var. ciliata (Yamam.) S. S. Ying, Mem. Coll. Agr. Natl. Taiwan. Univ. 29(2): 45. 1989; FRPS 70: 307. 2002.
Justicia ciliata (Yamam.) C. F. Hsieh & T. C. Huang, Taiwania 19(1): 21. 1974; FTW 4: 696. 1978.

Herbs, 0.3–0.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, bifariously pubescent along sulci. Petioles 1–9 mm, glabrous; leaf blades ovate, 1.5–3.5 × 0.8–2 cm, base attenuate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute, glabrous, adaxially green, cystoliths numerous, abaxially pale green, without cystoliths, lateral veins 3–4 pairs. Spikes mostly terminal or axillary at upper leaf axils, 1–4 cm, elongate to 7 cm in fruit. Peduncles (0–)0.5–2 cm, glabrous. Bracts obovate‑elliptic, 4–5 × 2 mm, glabrous, apex acute, white‑margined; bracteoles lanceolate‑elliptic, ca. 5 × 1.2 mm. Calyx 4‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 4 × 1 mm, glabrous, white‑margined. Corolla ca. 6 mm, glabrous, 2‑lipped to middle, upper lip ovate, 3 × 2 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip oblong, ca. 3 × 3 mm, minutely 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous except for hairs at base, ca. 2.5 mm; anther‑thecae ovate, ca. 1.3 mm long, superposed, the lower one spurred at base, upper one muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1.3 mm, glabrous; style ca. 6 mm, glabrous. Capsule oblong, ca. 4 mm, brownish yellow short stipitate, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1 mm, glabrous, rugose.

Locality: High Island, North Ninepin Island. F. W. Xing 9253, 9704 (IBSC).
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Justicia procumbens L. 爵床
Sp. Pl. 15. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 4: 665. 1998.
Ecbolium procumbens (L.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 484. 1891.
Rostellularia procumbens (L.) Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 101. 1832; FHK 265. 1861; FRPS 70: 305. 2002.

Procumbent herbs, 20–50 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, pubescent. Petioles 3–8 mm, pubescent; leaf blades elliptic, ovate‑elliptic or elliptic‑oblong, 1.5–4 × 0.8–1.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, or slightly decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, subglabrous or sparsely hispid, cystoliths numerous, lateral veins 3–6 pairs, prominent. Spikes terminal or axillary in upper leaf axils, 1–6 cm. Peduncles 0.5–7 cm, densely pilose. Bracts elliptic lanceolate, 4–5 × 1 mm, abaxially pilose, ciliate; bracteoles lanceolate, 4–5 mm, abaxially pilose, ciliate. Calyx 5–6 mm, 4‑lobed to the base; lobes linear, 1‑veined, with yellowish white margin, abaxially pilose along the veins, ciliate. Corolla pink or white, red spotted on the lower lip, ca. 7 mm, 2‑lipped, upper lip ca. 3 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip ca. 3 × 3.5 mm, 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, the middle lobe slightly larger, ca. 1 × 1–1.5 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 4 mm; anther‑thecae superposed, lower one spurred at base, the upper one muticous. Ovary pubescent; style ca. 5 mm, pubescent. Capsule ca. 5 mm, with a solid stalk at base, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1 × 1 mm, rugose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 430; Y. S. Lau 3152; Y. W. Lam 774.
Distribution: Area S of Qinling Range to Huaihe Valley; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands and open fields. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Justicia ventricosa Wall. ex Sims. 黑葉小駁骨
Curtis's Bot. Mag. Pl. 2760. 1867; FHK 264. 1861; FKH 200. 1912.
Gendarussa ventricosa (Wall. ex Sims.) Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 104. 1832; FHN 3: 569. 1974; FRPS 70: 299. 2002.
Adhatoda ventricosa (Wall. ex Sims.) Nees, Prodr. 11: 107. 1847.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, up to 1 m tall. Winter buds ovate, ca. 2 mm long, pubescent. Stems subterete, glabrous. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades elliptic or obovate, 6–17 × 2–6 cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate or acute, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous, midveins impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially, lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs, meet near the margin, prominent on both surfaces. Spike terminal, 5–10 cm, densely flowered, usually 1–3 flowers on each node. Peduncles ca. 1 cm. Bracts leaf‑like, broadly ovate or suborbicular, 1–1.5 × 0.8–1 cm, apex acute, pinnately‑veined, abaxially pilose or subglabrous, margin ciliate, imbricate; bracteoles linear, 3–5 × 1–2 mm, margin ciliate. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, ciliate. Corolla creamy white, purplish pink striped on the lips, 1.5 – 1.8 cm, outside pilose, inside pubescent; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip oblong‑ovate, 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, apex rounded. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 6 mm; anther‑thecae ovate, subequal, superposed, lower one with white appendage. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, cymose; style ca. 1.6 cm, pilose at base. Capsule ca. 8 mm, pubescent, 4‑seeded.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung, Sai Kung, Sha Tin, Hin Tin, Ma On Shan Country Park, Chuk Kok, Sha Lo Tung. H. C. Tang 101; Y. S. Lau 3211; C. Wright 372 (A).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Kadsura coccinea (Lem.) A. C. Sm. 黑老虎
Sargentia 7: 166. 1947; R. M. K. Saunders, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 54: 41– 46. 1998 & Sp. Pl. 4: 32–34. 2001.
Kadsura chinensis Hance ex Benth., FHK 8. 1861, p.p.

Woody vine, glabrous. Petiole (9–)10–30(–41) mm; leaf blade papery to leathery, elliptic, rarely ovate-elliptic or ovate, 7–16(–19) × 2.5–7.5(–10) cm, base acute (younger leaves) to obtuse (older), rarely truncate, apex acute to short acuminate, rarely obtuse, margin entire, rarely denticulate with 1–17 teeth; secondary veins (3–)5–8(–12) pairs. Flowers borne solitary in axils of leaves, often at base of short shoot. Flowering peduncle (4.5–)7–38 mm. Receptacle elongate-conical. Tepals (8–)10–16(–24), white with red tips, or entirely (purple-) red (occasionally yellowish); outermost tepal ovate, 1–4 × 1.5–4.5 mm; innermost tepal variably ovate to oblong to obovate, (5–)7.5–19.5 × 2–5.5 mm; largest tepal variably ovate to oblong to obovate, (8–)12–23 × 6–12(–15) mm. Staminate flowers with androecium of (10–)20–50 essentially free stamens; distal apex of receptacle with 0–14(–22) sterile (occasionally partly fertile) staminodes. Pistillate flowers with gynoecium of 20–68 carpels; pseudostyle narrow, subulate, without pseudostigma. Fruit of up to 60 apocarps, ripening red or purple-red, apocarps ca. 14–24 × 7–17 mm. Fruiting peduncle 26–49 mm long. Seeds 1–2 per apocarp, pyriform, 10–18 × 7.5–11 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pak Ngan Shek (Kadoorie Farm), Lamma Island (Sok Kwu Wan). L. T. Lo 315; HK sheet 33466; S. Y. Hu 13701 (A, IBSC); R. M. K. Saunders & H. P. Y. Ho 96/1 (HKU).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi; Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Semi-open shrubland and forests. Flowering: May– Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal, food (edible fruit).
Notes: The type specimen of Kadsura chinensis was collected by J. G. Champion in a ravine below Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island around 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal, food (edible fruit).
Notes: The type specimen of Kadsura chinensis was collected by J. G. Champion in a ravine below Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island around 1850.

records.text:
Kadsura heteroclita (Roxb.) Craib 異形南五味子
Fl. Siam. 1: 28. 1925 (“1931”); R. M. K. Saunders, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 54: 46 –54. 1998 & Sp. Pl. 4: 35 –37. 2001.
Uvaria heteroclita Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 43. 1814.

Woody vine, glabrous. Petiole (7–)10 –20(–29); leaf blade ± papery to subleathery, elliptic, rarely ovate-elliptic, (6.5 –)7.5 – 13.5(–16) × (2.5–)3.5–6.5(–9.5) cm, base cuneate to obtuse, often short-attenuate, apex acute to (short) acuminate; margin entire, to denticulate, 0(–11) teeth per margin; secondary veins 5 –9(–16) pairs. Flowers borne solitary in axils of leaves, occasionally with secondary flower borne in axil of bract. Flowering peduncle (1.5–)3–33(–35) mm. Receptacle subglobose. Tepals 10–17(–25), white, cream or yellow; outermost tepal ovate, 1–2.5(– 8) × 1.5 – 4(– 9) mm; innermost tepal elliptic to ovate (rarely obovate), (2–)3.5 –10.5 × (1–)2–7 mm; largest tepal elliptic to ovate (rarely obovate), 4.5 –20.5 × (3.5 –)4.5 –12(–15) mm. Staminate flowers with androecium of 40– 62(–74) stamens, anthers ± sessile, closely appressed in subglobose to ellipsoid head, 2–4.5 mm in diam., connectives broader than thick, with lateral thecae so that thecae of adjacent stamens contiguous. Pistillate flowers with gynoecium of 28–72 carpels; pseudostigma broad, subpeltate. Fruit of ca. 33–41 (or more) apocarps, ripening red, apocarps ca. (7–)10 –22 × (6 –)8 –10(–15) mm. Fruiting peduncle ca. 14– 46 mm long. Seeds 1–2(–11) per apocarp, pyriform, discoid or reniform, 4 –5.5(–7.5) × 4.5 – 7 mm.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 212; Y. W. Lam 1696; R. M. K. Saunders & G. Hao 96/2 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hunan; Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Malesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal.

Kalanchoe integra (Medik.) Kuntze 匙葉伽藍菜
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 229. 1891; FOC 8: 205. 2001.
Cotyledon integra Medik., Hist. & Commentat. Acad. Elect. Sci. Theod.-Palat. 3: 200, pl. 9. 1775.
Kalanchoe spathulata DC., Pl. Grass. pl. 65. 1799 – 1829; FKH 99. 1912; FRPS 34(1): 38. 1984; FGD 3: 44, fig. 30: 5. 1995.

Annual succulent herb, 0.3 – 1.2 m tall, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 2 – 3 cm; leaf blade oblong-spathulate, 7 – 10 × 2 – 4 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse. Cymes terminal and paniculate, to 10 cm; flowers erect. Sepals green, deeply 4-lobed; lobes triangular or narrowly ovate, 5 – 12 mm, apex acuminate. Corolla yellow, salverform, 1.5 – 2 cm; lobes 4, lanceolate, apex acuminate. Stamens 8, in two whorls; filaments very short, inserted near apex of corolla-tube. Carpels 4, free, apically narrowed into styles. Fruit a group of follicles, many-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. Y. Hu 5249, 9377 (CUHK); HK sheet 1686.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread over tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.-Mar.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Kalanchoe spathulata DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Kalanchoe spathulata DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).

records.text:
Kalanchoe laciniata (L.) DC. 伽藍菜
Hist. Pl. Grass. 2: 100. 1802; DC., Prodr. 3: 395. 1828; FKH 99. 1912; FHN 1: 370, fig. 190. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 39, pl. 13: 1 – 6. 1984; FGD 3: 44, fig. 30: 1 – 4. 1995.

Perennial succulent herb. Stems erect, to 1 m tall, few-branched. Leaves opposite; petioles 2.5 – 4 cm; leaf blade 8 – 18 × 5 – 15 cm, pinnatipartite; lobes lanceolate, entire, irregularly toothed or lobed again. Cymes terminal and paniculate, 10 – 30 cm, many-flowered. Sepals green, deeply 4-lobed; lobes linear-lanceolate, 4 – 7 mm, membranous, apex acute. Corolla salverform, yellow or reddish; tube ca. 1.5 cm, inflated at the base; limb ca. 2 cm in diam.; lobes 4, ovate, 5 – 6 mm, apex acute. Stamens 8, in two whorls; filaments very short, inserted near apex of corolla-tube. Carpels 4, free, apically narrowed into styles. Fruit a group of follicles, many-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2669; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 1685).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread and naturalized in tropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all the year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Kalanchoe pinnata (L. f.) Pers. 落地生根
Syn. Pl. 1: 446. 1805; Backer, Fl. Malesia I. 4: 199, fig. 1. 1951; FHN 1: 371, fig. 191. 1964.
Crassula pinnata L. f., Suppl. Sp. Pl. 191. 1781.
Bryophyllum calycinum Salisb., Parad. Lond., pl. 3. 1805; FHK 127. 1861; FKH 99. 1912.
Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken, All. Naturgesch. 3: 1966. 1841; FRPS 34(1): 36, pl. 12: 11 – 17. 1984; FTW ed. 2, 3: 10, pl. 5. 1993; FGD 3: 42, fig. 29. 1995; FOC 8: 204. 2001.
Cotyledon pinnata Lam., Encyclopédie Méthodique, Botanique 2: 141. 1786.

Succulent perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, 0.5 – 1.5 m tall, ± woody at base. Leaves opposite, simple (early ones) or pinnate, petiolate; leaflets 3 – 5, ovate to ovate-oblong, 5 – 10 × 3 – 8 cm, apex rounded or obtuse on both ends, margin crenate. Flowers in paniculate cymes, pendulous. Calyx campanulate, light green or tinged with reddish-yellow, 2.5 – 4 mm; lobes 4, triangular. Corolla tubular, 4 – 5 cm, inflated at base; lobes 4, ovate-lanceolate, pink or purplish red. Stamens 8, attached to the base of corolla-tube. Follicles ca. 5 mm, included in corolla and calyx.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 10721); Y. S. Lau 2124, 2733.
Distribution: Native to Africa, but naturalized elsewhere in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).

Kalanchoe synsepala Baker 趣蝶蓮
J. Bot. 20: 110. 1882.

Perennial succulent herb. Stems very short, 2 – 8( –15) cm; runners slender, 15 – 25 cm, arising from axils of leaves and rooting at the tip. Leaves decussately opposite, forming rosette-like tufts crowded on apex of stem and runners; leaf blade broadly ovate to suborbicular, (3– )5 – 10( –15) cm in diam., base subtruncate, abruptly narrowed into a short and broad petiole, apex rounded, margin purplish, with sharp teeth. Flowers in dichasial cymes terminal on axillary long peduncles; pedicels ca. 4 mm. Calyx ca. 4 mm, lobed to one-third of its length; lobes 4, triangular, acute. Corolla white, salverform; tube ca. 1 cm, glabrous; lobes 4, ovate-elliptic, 6 – 7 mm, apex acuminate. Stamens 8, in two whorls; filaments very short, inserted near apex of corolla-tube; anthers purple, exserted. Carpels 4, free, slightly longer than the corolla-tube, apically narrowed into styles. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Cultivated as a pot plant.
Distribution: Native to Madagascar, but cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Kalanchoe tubiflora (Harv.) Raym.-Hamet 洋吊鐘
Beih. Bot. Centrabl. 29(2): 41. 1912.
Bryophyllum tubiflorum Harv., Fl. Cap. 2: 380. 1862.
Bryophyllum verticillatum (Scott-Elliot) A. Berger, Nat. Pflanzenfam. (ed. 2), 18a: 411. 1930; FGD 3: 43. 1995.
Kalanchoe verticillata Scott-Elliot, J. Linn. Soc. 29: 14. 1981.

Succulent perennial herb, to 1 m tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, simple or branched from the base. Leaves opposite or verticillate, sessile, linear, subcylindric, 2.5 – 15 × 0.4 – 0.5 cm, greyish green, mottled with violet-brown, producing plantlets at the tips. Flowers pendulous, in terminal cymes. Calyx campanulate, 6.5 – 10 mm; lobes 4, triangular to triangular-lanceolate. Corolla tubular, 2.5 – 3 cm, inflated, constricted above ovary; lobes 4, suborbicular or broadly ovate, salmon to scarlet. Stamens 8, in 1 whorl; filaments as long as corolla-tube, attached to the base of corolla-tube. Fruit a group of follicles.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 200, 453, 688 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to S Africa, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Preferred sunny and dry places. Flowering: Oct.-Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Kalanchoe verticillata Scott-Elliot previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Kalanchoe verticillata Scott-Elliot previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).

Kalimeris indica (L.) Sch.‑Bip. 馬蘭（雞兒腸）
Syst. Verz. 125. 1854; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 11. 1967; FTW 4: 892. 1978; FRPS 74: 99, pl. 30: 1 – 3. 1985; FGD 8: 180, fig. 101. 2007.
Aster indicus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 876. 1753; FKH 141. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 855. 1998.
Boltonia indica Benth., FHK 174. 1861.

Perennial rhizomatous herb, 30–75 cm tall; stems erect, with hair on upper portion. Leaves on basal part oblanceolate or obovate‑oblong, coarsely dentate above, 3–6 × 0.7–1.5 cm, base attenuate and narrowed down to form wing with petiole, apex acute or obtuse; those on upper part smaller in size, linear or lanceolate, subentire. Capitula solitary to each branch, or loosely corymbose. Involucres hemispherical, 0.5–1 cm across; phyllaries 2 – 3‑seriate, margin membranous and hair‑bearing; outer ones elliptic, 1.8 mm; middle ones obovate; inner ones oblanceolate‑oblong, 4 mm, apex obtuse. Receptacle convex with each areole elevated at centre. Ligulate marginal florets 15–20, 1‑seriate, 8–10 mm, limb purple; stylar branches papillose along margin. Tubular disk florets 3.5 mm, yellow, pilose; anther bases obtuse and entire, apex appendages ovate‑lanceolate; style with triangular appendage at apex. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, 1.8 mm, brown, hirsute, with a crown of scarious pappus, marginal one 3‑ribbed, inner disk one laterally compressed and 2‑ribbed.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tseng Lan Shu, New Territories, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 438; C. P. Lau 051 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 308 (CUHK).
Distribution: E to SW and S to NE China; S & E Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Kandelia obovata Sheue, H. Y. Liu & J. Yong 秋茄樹（紅蓢、水筆仔）
Taxon 52: 291, fig. 3: a– k. 2003.
Kandelia rheedii auct. non Wight & Arn.: FHK 110. 1861; FKH 102. 1912.
Kandelia candel auct. non (L.) Druce: Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 6(4): 329. 1928; FHN 2: 51, fig. 317. 1965; FRPS 52(2): 133, pl. 37: 1–8. 1983; FGD 1: 111, fig. 119. 1987; FFJ 4: 57, fig. 54. 1989.

Small tree to 3 m; bark smooth, reddish brown. Stipules 2–3 cm. Petioles 1–1.8 cm; leaf blade oblong to obovate-oblong, 5–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex rounded or obtuse, veins inconspicuous. Inflorescences 4–9(–13)-flowered; peduncle 1–3(–4) cm; pedicels (3–)5–6 mm; bracteoles U-shaped in outline, (2.5–)3 mm, 2-lobed, each lobe with ca. 30 colleters at base. Sepals white, lanceolate, 1.2–1.6 cm, reflexed when fruiting; petals white, bifid, with or without a long seta in the sinus, each lobe with (6–)8–12(–14) slightly sinuate threads. Filaments 7–13 mm, anthers 1.2–1.8 mm; ovary 1-locular, with 6 ovules, style filiform, 1.4–1.6 cm, stigmas 3. Fruit ovoid, 1.0–1.5 cm. Hypocotyl 12–20 cm, acuminate at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 312, 2706; K. L. Yip 4201; Hance 603 (BM); Hu 5005, 11546, 13762 (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Margins of mangrove swamps. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Notes: This species was recorded as Kandelia candel (L.) Druce before 2003 (e.g. Check List HK Plants 168. 2002.)

Keteleeria fortunei (A. Murr.) Carr. 油杉
Rev. Hort. 37: 449. 1866; FRPS 7: 50. 1978; FOC 4: 42. 1999; FGD 4: 12. 2000.
Picea fortunei A. Murr., Proc. Hort. Soc. 421. 1862.

Tree to 30 m tall; trunk to 1 m d.b.h.; bark dark grey, rough, irregularly fissured; branches spreading; young branchlets hairy or glabrous, reddish or pale pink when dry, 2 or 3 years old branchlets pale yellowish grey or yellowish brown. Leaves linear, 1.2–3 cm long, 2–4 mm wide, base attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, green and glossy adaxially, pale green abaxially, stomatal lines 12–17 on each side abaxially. Seed cones cylindric, 6–18 cm long, 5–6.5 cm in diam. Seed scales compressed orbicular, rhombic-orbicular, or rarely oblong, thick or thin, 2.5–3.2 × 2.7–3.5 cm, exposed part glabrous abaxially, margin entire, apex convex, rounded, or roundedtruncate. Seeds oblong, 1–1.3 cm × 5–6 mm; wing yellowish brown, more or less cuneate, apex oblique.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Stanley. Y. S. Lau 1584, 1266.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: In secondary forests, on coastal hillside. Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: Oct.
Uses: The species is propagated locally for afforestation and ex-situ conservation.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
