Khaya senegalensis (Desr.) A. Juss. 非洲楝
Mem. Mus. Hist. Nat. 19: 250. 1832; FGD 2: 296, fig. 190. 1991.
Swietenia senegalensis Desr., Encycl. 3: 679. 1791.

Evergreen tree to 25 m tall or more, quite glabrous throughout. Young branches with dark greyish brown lenticels. Leaves alternate, crowded towards apex of branches, 15–60 cm including the petiole; leaflets 6–16, alternate to subopposite; petiolules 5–10 mm; leaflet blades oblong to elliptic, 7–17 × 2.5–6 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex broadly obtuse, with a short cusp, dark green adaxially, paler abaxially, lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein, margin entire. Panicles terminal or axillary, shorter than leaves. Sepals 4, distinct, oblong, ca. 1 mm. Petals 4, distinct, oblong to obovate, ca. 3 mm, glabrous. Staminal tube urceolate; anthers inserted on apical inside of the tube, included. Ovary ovoid, usually 4-locular, with amphitropous ovules. Capsule globose, dehiscing from apex when mature; pericarp woody. Seeds broad, ellipsoidal to suborbicular, margin with a round membranous wing.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to tropical Africa and Madagascar.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun. of the following year.
Uses: Timber, ornamental (roadside tree).

Knoxia corymbosa Willd. 紅芽大戟
Sp. Pl. ed. 4, 1(2): 582. 1789; FHK 164. 1861; FKH 132. 1912; FHN 3: 360, fig. 772. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 274, pl. 120, photo 175. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 5, pl. 2. 1999; FYN 15: 197. 2003.

Perennial erect herbs, to 1 m tall. Stems and branches obtusely 4‑angled, pubescent. Leaves membranous; petioles 1–6 mm, or almost obsolete; stipules 3–6 mm, fringed with 3–5 bristle‑like teeth; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong, 3– 10 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, covered with appressed hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces. Flowers numerous, subsessile, loose, terminal dichotomous cymes of 2 – 6 cm long. Calyx‑tube ca. 1 mm, glabrous, with minute, triangular teeth. Corolla white or purple; tube ca. 2 mm, hairy inside; lobes less than 1 mm. Capsule ovoid, ca. 2–3 mm, with 4–8 weak ribs, usually falling off entirely from the filiform persistent axis.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Lan Nai Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Po Toi Islands, Peng Chau. Y. S. Lau 1481; Y. W. Lam 277, 1053.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Open fields, thin forests and thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Koelreuteria bipinnata Franch. 複羽葉欒樹
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 33: 453. 1886; FRPS 47(1): 56, pl. 19: 6. 1985; FFJ 3: 321, fig. 219. 1987; FGD 1: 254. 1987.
Koelreuteria bipinnata var. puberula Chun, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3: 408. 1955; FYN 1: 286. 1977.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Branches pubescent, densely lenticellate. Leaves bipinnate, 45–70 cm including petioles; axes pubescent; leaflets 9–17, alternate, rarely opposite; petiolules ca. 3 mm or leaflets subsessile; blades papery or subleathery, obliquely ovate, 3.5–7 × 2–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, slightly oblique, apex acute to acuminate, margin incurved serrate, abaxially densely pubescent or sometimes mixed with appressed hairs, adaxially glabrous or pilosulose on midvein. Thyrses large, 35–70 cm, pubescent. Calyx 5-lobed to middle; lobes broadly triangular or elliptic, 2 mm, margin erose. Petals 4, oblong-lanceolate, 6–9 × 1.5–3 mm, apex obtuse or acute, claw 1.5–3 mm, villous, scale deeply 2-lobed. Disk red at base. Stamens slightly shorter than petals; filaments white villous. Ovary trigonous-ellipsoidal, pilose. Capsules pale purplish red, brown when mature, ellipsoidal or subglobose, 3-ridged, 4–7 × 3.5 –5 cm, apex obtuse or rounded, mucronate. Seeds subglobose, 5–6 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3266.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Kopsia arborea Blume 蕊木
Catalogus 13. 1823; FOC 16: 162. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 61, fig. 20. 1999.
Kopsia lancibracteolata Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 23(3): 262. 1923; FGD 1: 434, fig. 481. 1987; FRPS 63: 41, pl. 14. 1977.
Kopsia officinalis Tsiang & P. T. Li, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 11: 356, pl. 40. 1973. FRPS 63: 43, pl. 15. 1977.

Trees to 15 m tall. Branches greenish, terete, slightly compressed, puberulent when young. Petioles 5 – 15 cm; leaf blade elliptic, narrowly elliptic, or narrowly ovate, 8 – 24 × 3.5 – 8.5 cm, glabrous, apex acute or short acuminate, lateral veins 10 – 20 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbose, many‑flowered; peduncle to 14 cm, puberulent or glabrous; bracteoles narrowly oblong, puberulent or glabrous. Pedicel 3 – 4 mm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 4 – 6 mm, puberulent or glabrous. Corolla white; tube ca. 2.5 cm; lobes narrowly oblong, 1.5 – 2 cm. Disk scales narrowly oblong, longer than ovary, fleshy. Ovary ovoid, puberulent. Drupes black or blue‑black, ellipsoidal, 2.5 – 3.5 × 1.5 – 2 cm.

Locality: Kadoorie Farm. HK sheet 32239, 32240.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, N Australia.
Ecology: Wet places under forest. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Korthalsella japonica (Thunb.) Engl. 栗寄生
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1: 138. 1897; FYN 3: 372, pl. 109: 5 – 6. 1983; FGD 1: 225, fig. 253. 1987; FRPS 24: 140. 1988; FOC 5: 240. 2003.
Bifaria japonica (Thunb.) Tiegh., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 43: 173. 1896.
Bifaria opuntia (Thunb.) Merr., Enum. Philipp. Fl. Pl. 2: 113. 1923, nom. illeg. superfl.; FTW 2: 240, pl. 282. 1976.
Korthalsella opuntia (Thunb.) Merr., Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 30: 68. 1916, nom. illeg. superfl.; FHN 2: 464. 1965.
Pseudixus japonicus (Thunb.) Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 188. 1915.
Viscum japonicum Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 2: 329. 1794.
Viscum opuntia Thunb., Fl. Jap. 64. 1784, nom. illeg. superfl.

Subshrub, 5–15 cm tall. Branches flat, usually opposite, green; stem internodes narrowly obovate or obovate-lanceolate, 7–17 × 3–6 mm, longitudinally 1-ribbed when dried. Leaves scale-like, fused into a ring. Inflorescence lateral at nodes. Male flower greenish, subglobose in bud, ca. 0.5 mm; perianth lobes triangular; synandrium compressed spherical; pedicels short. Female flower ellipsoidal in bud, 5–7 mm; perianth lobes broadly triangular, minute; stigma papillate. Berry yellowish, ellipsoidal or pyriform, ca. 2 × 1.5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 225, 226; K. Y. Tam 106.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, S Gansu, Shaanxi, Hubei, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Australia, E Africa and Madagascar.
Ecology: Often growing on trees of Fagaceae and Theaceae. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.

Kummerowia striata (Thunb.) Schindl. 雞眼草
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 10(257–259): 403–404. 1912, pro parte excl. syn.; FGD 5: 293, fig. 157. 2003.
Lespedeza stipulacea Maxim., Prim. Fl. Amur. 85 – 86. 1859; FRPS 41: 159. 1995
Hedysarum striatum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 289. 1784.
Lespedeza striata Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 262. 1841; FHK 85. 1861; FKH 81. 1912.

Annual prostrate or decumbent herb, 10– 45 cm tall. Stems and branches white-pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets obovate or oblong, 6 – 15 × 3– 8 mm, base subrounded or broad-cuneate, apex rounded, sometimes emarginate; lateral veins numerous and parallel. Flowers small, solitary or 2– 3, axillary. Bracteoles 4, one of them smaller at pedicel-joint. Calyx campanulate, deep purple, 2.5–3 mm, 5-toothed, white pubescent. Corolla pink or purple; petals clawed, 5 –6 mm; vexillum elliptic; wings oblong, shorter than keel. Pods orbicular or obovate, 3.5– 5 mm, apex acute, minutely pubescent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Ma Liu Shui. W. J. Tutcher 11218; H. C. Tang 2071; Y. S. Lau 2271.
Distribution: S, SW, NE China; Korea, Russia, Japan.
Ecology: Farmlands and grasslands on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul. –Sep.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), forage, green manure.

Kyllinga brevifolia Rottb. 短葉水蜈蚣
Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 13, pl. 4, fig. 3. 1773; FKH 297. 1912; FRPS 11: 187. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 610. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 284. 2000; FYN 15: 658. 2003; FGD 8: 347. 2007; FOC 23: 248. 2010.
Cyperus brevifolia (Rottb.) Hassk., Cat. Hort. Bot. Bogor. 24. 1844.

Perennial; rhizome slender, long-creeping. Culms arranged in a row along the rhizome, 7–30 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves radical and subradical; blade narrowly linear, 2–17 × 1–3 mm, acute, flattish-plicate; sheath 1–20 cm, brownish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest 3–20 cm × 1.7–2.4 mm, sometimes erect. Inflorescence capitate, globose. Spikes 1(–3), globose, 0.5–1 × 0.5–1 cm. Spikelets oblonglanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 3–3.5 × 1 mm, 1(–2)-flowered. Glumes ovate-elliptic, 1–3.5 mm, shortly cuspidate, sides membranous, 5–7-veined, pale green to pale brown, keel sparsely spinulose, green. Stamens 1–3; anthers 1 mm long. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes 1–2 per spike, obovate or elliptic, 1–1.5 × 0.5–0.7 mm, brownish, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 329; S. P. Lau 5; K. L. Yip 4079.
Distribution: Widely spread over Areas S of Changjiang; tropics.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Kyllinga nemoralis (J. R. Forst. & G. Forst.) Dandy ex Hutch. & Dalz. 單穗水蜈蚣
Fl. W. Trop. Afr. 2: 486. 1936; FTW ed. 2, 5: 286. 2002; FYN 15: 659. 2003; FGD 8: 346. 2007; FOC 23: 249. 2010.
Thryocephalon nemorale J. R. Forst. & G. Forst., Char. Gen. Pl. (ed. 2) 129–130, pl. 65. 1776.
Kyllinga monocephala Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Nov. Pl. 13, t. 4, fig. 4. 1773, nom. illeg.; FHK 388. 1861; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 190. 1961; Check List HK Plants 317. 2002; 111. 2004.
Kyllinga triceps auct. non Rottb.: FKH 297. 1912; Check List HK Plants 88. 1993.

Perennial. Rhizome long creeping. Culms tufted, close together or spaced along rhizome, erect, 10–45 cm tall, triquetrous, not thickened at base. Leaves many, usually shorter than culm; blades narrowly linear, 2–5 mm wide, rather soft, flattish; sheaths brown to purplish brownish. Inflorescence a single head, bearing a globose central spike and 2–3 small lateral spikes; central spike 5–10 × 5–7 mm, densely bearing many spikelets, whitish; leafy bracts 3–4, spreading to reflexed, lowest to 30 cm. Spikelets ovate-elliptic to lanceolate-ovate, 2.7–3.5 × 1.5 mm, 1-flowered. Glumes usually 5, lowest two smaller or narrow, 1–1.5 mm, remaining glumes 2.5–3.5 mm, boat-shaped, thinly membranous, whitish and eventually becoming straw-coloured, variegate with rusty brown, 3–4-veined on each side, broadly winged on acute green keel, wing serrulate, keel ending in a short usually recurved cusp. Stamens 3. Style slender, stigmas 2. Achenes oblong-obovate or suborbicular, biconvex, 1.25–1.5 mm, maturing brownish.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 5; J. C. Shaw 569; K. L. Yip 4018.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Yunnan, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Puapua New Guinea, Japan, Australia, Madagascar, tropical Africa, Indian Ocean islands, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Kyllinga polyphylla Willd. ex Kunth 水蜈蚣（香根水蜈蚣）
Enum. Pl. 2: 134. 1837; FOC 23: 248. 2010.
Kyllinga aromatica Ridl., Trans. Linn. Soc. London, Bot. 2: 146. 1884.

Perennial; rhizome horizontally creeping. Culms crowded in series along rhizome, up to 75 cm tall, triquetrous, smooth. Leave on uppermost 1–2 sheaths only, linear-lanceolate, 2–6.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, apex acute, flat; sheaths up to 15 cm, greenish to purplish. Involucral bracts 4–7, linear, the longest up to 14 cm. Inflorescence capitate. Spikes 4–5; terminal spike ± spherical, 0.7 × 0.7 cm, lateral spikes smaller, in axils of involucral bracts. Spikelets elliptic, 3–3.7 × 0.8–0.9 mm, 1–2-flowered. Glumes ovate-elliptic, 2.5–3 × 2 mm, apex obtuse, shortly mucronate, sides membranous, indistinctly 3–5-veined, whitish to pale greenish, keel greenish, smooth to sparsely toothed. Stamens 1; anther 1–1.2 mm. Stamens 3; anther linear. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes oblong-obovate, 1 × 0.6 mm, greyish brown.

Locality: Victoria Park, Tsiu Hang, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 2254, 3090; Y. W. Lam 327.
Distribution: Taiwan; native to W Africa, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Spice.
Notes: The species was reported as Kyllinga aromatica (Ridl.) Mattf. & Kunth previously (Check List HK Plants 316. 2002; 111. 2004).
records.uses:
Spice.
Notes: The species was reported as Kyllinga aromatica (Ridl.) Mattf. & Kunth previously (Check List HK Plants 316. 2002; 111. 2004).

records.text:
Lablab purpureus (L.) Sweet 扁豆
Hort. Brit. 481. 1826; FRPS 41: 271. 1995; FGD 5: 325, fig. 178. 2003.
Dolichos lablab L., Sp. Pl. 725. 1753.
Dolichos purpureus L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 1021. 1763.

Perennial twining vine. Stems up to 6 m, usually purplish. Stipules basifixed, lanceolate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; terminal leaflet deltoid-ovate, 6–10 × 6–10 cm, lateral ones oblique, base subtruncate, apex acute or acuminate. Racemes axillary, erect, 15–25 cm. Flowers 2–5-fasciculate at each node. Calyx campanulate, 6 mm, upper 2 teeth almost wholly connate, lower 3 teeth subequal. Corolla white or purple; vexillum orbicular, 12 mm, base with 2 appendages and 2 auricles below the appendages; wings broadly obovate, blade 10 mm; keel curved at right angle, base attenuate. Ovary linear, styles longer than ovary, laterally compressed, apex bearded. Pods oblong-falcate, 5 – 7 × 1.4 – 1.8 cm, compressed, straight or slighty curved, beaked. Seeds 3 – 5, oblong, white, purple or purple-black, hilum linear.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 272; Y. S. Lau 3229; Y. W. Lam 1159.
Distribution: Widely cultivated, native to Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated in garden or escaped in open wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Food (pods), medicinal (folklore).

Lactuca sativa L. 萵苣
Sp. Pl. 785. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 27. 1967; FRPS 80(1): 233. 1997; FGD 8: 262. 2007.

Annual or biennial lactiferous herbs 25–100 cm tall, glabrous throughout; stem white erect, apically branched. Basal and lower leaves large, undivided, oblanceolate, elliptic‑oblanceolate to elliptic, 6–15 × 1.5–7.5 cm, sessile, base cordate or sagittate, semi‑amplexicaul, apex obtuse to rounded, margin sinuous or bearing short teeth. Middle and upper leaves with shape similar to the basal and lower ones, or appearing as lanceolate, size gradually smaller when growing upward; the uppermost leaves small, ovate‑cordate, sessile, base cordate or sagittate, amplexicaul, margin entire or slightly sinuous. Capitula many, paniculate at stem and branch terminal. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 10 × 6 mm; phyllaries 5‑seriate, apex acute, abaxial side glabrous; outer ones broadly deltoid to ovate, 3–4 × 1.5–2.5 mm; middle and inner ones ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 6–10 × 1.5–2 mm. All florets yellow, corolla ligulate, 6–7 mm long, ligule 4–5 mm, apex 5‑lobed, lower tube 2 mm, hairy near summit, hermaphrodite and fertile. Cypselae oblanceolate, 4 × 1.3 mm, compressed, pale brown, 6–7‑ribbed on each surface, apex acute and beaked, beak filiform, 4–5 mm, equal to or longer than the cypsela body. Pappus bristles in 2 rows, white, scaberulous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2962; HK sheet 16362.
Distribution: Native to Mediterranean region, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Lafoensia vandelliana Cham. & Schltdl. 麗薇（萊浮樹）
Linnaea 2: 346. 1827; FRPS 52(2): 89. 1983; FGD 3: 77, fig. 53. 1995.

Shrub, 2–8 m tall. Branches terete. Leaves decussate; petioles 2–8 mm; leaf blade thinly leathery, obovate or obovate-oblong, 5–9 × 3 – 4.5 cm, apex subrounded or obtuse, emarginate, often reflexed, light green and shining adaxially, with a gland or small hole near tip of midvein abaxially, lateral veins 15 – 18 on each side of midvein, rather prominent on both surfaces. Flowers showy, 8–12-merous, solitary or in panicles. Calyx oblate, 13 – 16 mm, lobes 10, lanceolate-deltoid, ca. 7 mm, often reflexed. Petals white, oblong or obovate-oblong, 2.5 – 3 cm, apex emarginate or erose. Stamens 22, filaments 6 – 7 cm. Capsules 3.5 × 2.5 cm. Seeds 2.5–3 × 1.2 cm including wings.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 200; Y. S. Lau 803; HK sheet 11770.
Distribution: Native to Brazil, Paraguay.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Lagenaria siceraria (Molina) Standl. 葫蘆
Publ. Field Mus. Nat. Hist. Chicago Bot. Ser. 3: 435. 1930; FHN 1: 480. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 216. 1986; FFJ 5: 247, fig. 231. 1993; FGD 3: 131, fig. 93. 1995.
Cucurbita siceraria Molina, Sag. Stor. Nat. Chili 133. 1782.

Stems and branches sulcate and ridged, sticky pubescent. Petioles 5–20 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, suborbicular-cordate in outline, pentagonal or slightly 3 –5-lobed, 10 –35 × 10 –35 cm, margin irregularly dentate, puberulous on both surfaces, palmately 5 –7-nerved. Male flowers: calyx-tube infundibular, 2 cm, 1 cm in diam., pubescent, lobes lanceolate, 12 × 1.5–2 mm; corolla lobes 3 – 4 × 2–3 cm, slightly rugose, conspicuously veined; filaments 3– 4 mm, anthers 8 –10 mm. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary ellipsoid, 3 × 1.3 cm, densely pubescent; stigma enlarged. Fruits varied in shape and size, flask-shape, clavate etc., 20 – 60 cm long, 9–16 cm in diam. Seeds white, obovate or triangular, apex truncate or bifid.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Li 5388; HK sheet 12025, 12035.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autunm.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal.

Lagenophora stipitata (Labill.) Druce 瓶頭草（瓶頭菊）
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles. 4: 630. 1917; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1–2): 32. 1967; FRPS 74: 85. 1985; FGD 8: 190, fig. 108. 2007.
Bellis stipitata Labill., Pl. Nov. Holl. 2: 55, t. 205. 1806.
Lagenophora billardieri Cass., Bull. Soc. Philom. Paris 34. 1818; FHK 173. 1861; FKH 140. 1912.

Small perennial herbs; rootstock 5–7 mm, densely covered by remnant of petiole bases; bearing 2–5 tuberous storage roots. Leaves all radical, rosulate, obovate to spatulate, 1–3 × 0.5–1.3 cm, base cuneate and gradually running to become wing of the petioles, apex rounded or obtuse, margin inconspicuously 1–3 toothed, softly pubescent on both surfaces, especially on the veins and along the margin. Capitula 5 mm across, solitary and terminal; scape 2.5–13 cm, slender, rarely bearing a branch. Involucre hemispherical, 4 mm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, apex acute, glabrous, margin membranous; outer ones ovate‑lanceolate; middle ones long‑oblong; inner ones linear. Receptacle 1 mm across, space between floret glandular. Ray florets 30, fertile, 3 mm, ligules 1.6 mm, entire; style short, branches stout. Disk florets 14, tubular, 2 mm, limb 4‑toothed; stamens 4, base obtuse, apical appendages small; stylar branches slender, appendages acute; ovary narrowed towards the apex. Cypselae brown, compressed oblanceolate, margin thickened, beaked, 2.5 mm including the glandular beak, end of beak with a waxy ring. Pappus absent.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2989; Y. W. Lam 234, 1434.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.

Lagerstroemia fordii Oliv. & Koehne 廣東紫薇
Pflanzenreich IV. 216(Heft): 262, fig. 56b. 1903; FKH 109. 1912; FRPS 52(2): 105. 1983; FGD 3: 83. 1995.

Tree, up to 8 m tall. Branchlets terete, sometimes slightly 4-angled. Leaves alternate; petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade papery, broadly lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–10 × 2.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex caudate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent along midvein abaxially, later glabrescent, lateral veins 4 – 5 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 6– 12 cm, grey-white tomentose; pedicels 4 – 6 mm. Calyx ca. 6 mm, 10–12-angled, grey-white pubescent; lobes 6, deltoid, apex sometimes caudate, densely pubescent abaxially. Petals cordate-orbicular, 10–12 mm including the 5 mm claw. Stamens 25–30, inserted at base of calyx-tube, 5– 6 of them longer than others. Capsules brown, ovoid-globose, 1–1.2 × 0.7 – 0.9 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Mount Nicholson, Tai Tam, Cape D'Aguilar, Lantau Island (Shek Pik, Yi O). H. G. Ye et al. 1265;K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 38715); HK sheet 40598.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian; widely distributed in tropical regions.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Jun. – Oct.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Lantau Island by C. Ford around 1888. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Notes: The type specimen was collected from Lantau Island by C. Ford around 1888. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Lagerstroemia indica L. 紫薇
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 734. 1762; FHK 112. 1861; FKH 109. 1912; FRPS 52(2): 94. 1983; FGD 3: 82, fig. 57. 1995.

Shrub or small tree, up to 7 m tall. Branchlets slender, 4-angular or narrowly winged. Leaves alternate or sometimes opposite, elliptic, broadly oblong or obovate, 2.5 – 7 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base broadly cuneate or suborbicular, apex acute or obtuse, sometimes emarginate, glabrous, or puberulent along veins abaxially, lateral veins 3–7 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 7 – 20 cm. Flowers red, purple or white; pedicels 3–15 mm. Calyx 7–10 mm, tube not furrowed as in other species; lobes 6, deltoid, without appendages. Petals 6, 12 – 20 mm, crisped, clawed. Stamens 36–42, outer 6 much longer than others. Capsules purple-black, nearly globular, 1 – 1.3 cm in diam., loculicidal. Seeds ca. 8 mm, winged.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 176; HK sheet 1927, 39299.
Distribution: E, S, C & SW China; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.

Lagerstroemia speciosa (L.) Pers. 大花紫薇（洋紫薇）
Syn. Pl. 2: 72. 1807; FRPS 52(2): 97. 1982; FGD 3: 81. 1995.

Large trees, 10 – 20 m tall; bark grey, glabrous. Branchlets terete. Leaves alternate, leathery; petioles 6 – 15 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic or oblong-ovate, 10–25 × 6–12 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex obtuse or acute, lateral veins 9–17 on each side of midvein, curved and connected at margin. Panicles 15 – 25(–40) cm, scurfy hairy. Flowers purple or purple-red, 4 – 5 cm in diam.; pedicels 1 – 1.5 cm. Calyx 12 – 13 mm, 12-angled, 6 lobed, appendages scale-like. Petals 6, suborbicular or oblong-obovate, 2.5–3.5 × 2–2.5 cm, margin crisped. Stamens 100– 200. Capsules grey-brown, globular, 2 cm in diam., dehiscing into 6 valves. Seeds many, 10 –15 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 11784, 11785, 34227.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian (cultivated); Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, timber, medicinal (folklore).

Lagerstroemia subcostata Koehne 南紫薇
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 4(1): 20. 1883; FKH 109. 1912; FRPS 52(2): 104. 1983; FGD 3: 82. 1995.
Lagerstroemia microcarpa auct. non Wight: Hance, J. Bot. 16: 107. 1878.

Tree or shrub, up to 14 m tall; bark thin, grey or brown. Leaves deciduous, opposite; petioles 2 – 4 mm; leaf blade membranous, oblong, oblong-lanceolate, rarely ovate, 2 – 9 × 1 – 4.4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, glabrous or sparsely puberulent on both surfaces, lateral veins 3–10 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 5–15 cm, densely flowered. Flowers white or roseate. Calyx 3.5 – 4.5 mm, 10–12-angled; lobes 5, deltoid. Petals 6, 2 – 6 mm, crisped and clawed. Stamens 15 – 30, 5 – 6 of them longer than others. Capsules elliptic, 6– 8 mm, dehiscing in 3– 6 valves. Seeds winged.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Qinghai, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Laggera alata (D. Don) Sch.‑Bip. ex Oliv. 六棱菊
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 29: 94. 1873; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan. Mus. 20(1–2): 33. 1967; FRPS 75: 47. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1006. 1998; FGD 8: 163, fig. 89. 2007.
Erigeron alatum D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 171. 1825.
Blumea alata DC., Prodr. 5: 448. 1836; FHK 177. 1861.

Perennial erect herbs; stem base woody, 50–100 cm tall, densely covered with glandular pubescent to tomentose hair, with wings 1–2 mm broad and entire. Cauline leaves oblong, 3–8 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base decurrent, apex obtuse to rounded, margin mucronulate or sometimes entire, densely glandular‑hairy and with strong midvein protruded on both surfaces. Upper leaves gradually smaller in size, especially those on branches, 1.5–3.5 × 3–6 mm, narrowly oblong to linear. Capitula many, drooping, growing as raceme on axillary winged branches, and branches grouped together as large racemose‑panicle. Peduncles 0.5–2 cm, glandularly pubescent, without wings. Involucres ovoid to campanulate, 7–10 mm; phyllaries 6‑seriate, shape changing inward from obovate, to ovate, lanceolate and linear‑oblong, length increases from outermost 2.5 mm to innermost 8 mm, apex acute; outer several layers herbaceous, green or apically green, some tinged purple near the tip, glandular and hairy on abaxial surfaces and along margins, usually recurved; inner series scarious, sparsely puberulent to glabrous. Receptacle plain and nude, areoles with elevated centers. Florets purple; marginal ones many‑seriate, pistillate, corolla filiform‑tubular, 5–6 mm, minutely 3 – 4‑lobed; disk ones few, hermaphrodite, 5–6 mm, bearing 5 lobes ovate and papillose, loosely hairy; anther bases sagittate and acute, apical appendages oblong and rounded; style reddish, papillose. Cypselae elliptic‑oblong, 0.8 mm, 10‑ribbed. Pappus bristles white, 5 mm, deciduous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Bride's Pool, High Island, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1291; S. L. Thrower 1408b (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 8590 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to SW and E China; Indochina, Malaysia, India, E Africa.
Ecology: Banks of paddy fields, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.

Lantana camara L. 馬纓丹（如意草）
Sp. Pl. 2: 627. 1753; FHK 268. 1861; FKH 201. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 17, fig. 4. 1982; FFJ 4: 520, fig. 412. 1989; FOC 17: 2. 1994; FGD 3: 343. 1995.

Erect shrub 1–2 m or taller. Stems and branches tetragonal, armed with stout recurved prickles, pubescent. Petiole 1–2 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, wrinkled, very rough, with short stiff hairs, aromatic when crushed, ovate to oblong, 3–8.5 × 1.5–5 cm, base rounded to subcordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin crenate; lateral veins 5 pairs, elevated. Capitula terminal, 1.5–2.5 cm across. Peduncle robust, longer than petiole. Bracts lanceolate, 3 times as long as calyx, hirsute abaxially. Calyx tubular, membranous, ca. 1.5 mm, limb very short dentate. Corolla yellow or orange, often turning deep red soon after opening, tube ca. 1 cm, 4–6 mm in diam., pubescent on both surfaces; limb 4–5‑lobed, spreading. Ovary glabrous. Drupes globose, ca. 4 mm in diam., purplish black.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 579, 2536; L. T. Lo 487.
Distribution: Naturalized in S China; native to America, widely naturalized in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets and open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: A very wide range of flower colours has been developed within cultivars of this species. Lantana camara ‘Snow White’ (雪白馬纓丹) is also cultivated for ornamental uses.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: A very wide range of flower colours has been developed within cultivars of this species. Lantana camara ‘Snow White’ (雪白馬纓丹) is also cultivated for ornamental uses.

records.text:
Lasia spinosa (L.) Thwaites 刺芋
Enum. Pl. Zeyl., 336. 1864; FGZ 687. 1956; FHN 4: 129, fig. 1033. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 14. 1979; FYN 2: 740. 1979; FFJ 6: 413, fig. 374. 1995; FGD 9: 179, fig. 95. 2009; FOC 23: 16. 2010.
Dracontium spinosum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 967. 1753.
Lasia heterophylla (Roxb.) Schott, Melet. Bot. 1: 21. 1832; FKH 289. 1912.
Pothos heterophylla Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 457. 1820.

Perennial herb, 1 – 2 m tall; stem ascending or creeping, prickly. Leaves of juvenile plants sagittate-hastate on 6–10 × 9–10 cm, that of adult plants deeply pedate-lobed, 15–45 × 15–20 cm, abaxial surface sparsely covered with curved prickles on veins, basal lobes oblong-lanceolate, central lobe larger, ovate-lanceolate; petiole 20–60 cm, longer than blade, prickly, sheathed at base. Peduncle, 20–35 cm, prickly; spathe 15–30 cm, dark-red abaxially, upper portion twisted; spadix yellow-green, cylindrical, 3–5 cm; tepals oblong, 1.5–3 mm, apex triangular-hooded, keeled; ovary ovoid. Fruits obovoid, apex truncate, densely warty-aculeate; seed ovoid-cordate, 5–7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 29773, 33099.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, Bangaladesh, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Forests, near water. Flowering: Sep.; fruiting: Feb.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Lasianthus attenuatus Jack 斜基粗葉木（小葉雞屎樹）
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 14(1): 126. 1823; FYN 15: 237, pl. 49: 1–8. 2003; FGD 6: 215. 2005.
Lasianthus wallichii (Wight & Arn.) Wight, Calcutta J. Nat. Hist. 6: 503. 1846; FTW ed. 2, 4: 295, pl. 133, photo 180. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 72, pl. 18: 1 – 7. 1999; Check List HK Plants 267. 2002; 92. 2004.
Mephitidia wallichii Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 390. 1834.

Shrubs, 1–2(–3) m tall. Branchlets, petioles and abaxial surface of leaves densely yellowish hirsute. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 2–5 mm; stipules linear‑lanceolate; leaf blade elliptic‑ovate or oblong‑ovate, rarely lanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, 4–10(–13) × 2–4.5 cm, base cordate and oblique, apex abruptly acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous and ± shining; lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces; tertiary veins slender, loosely reticulate. Flowers 5–6 in axillary sessile clusters. Bracts and bracteoles many, subulate‑lanceolate or linear, 10–15 mm. Calyx‑tube cupular, ca. 1.5 mm; lobes 5, triangular‑lanceolate, about the length of the tube or slightly longer. Corolla white, ± funnel‑shaped; tube 7–8 mm, villose inside; lobes 5, subovate, 3.5–4 mm, densely hairy on the adaxial surface. Drupes subglobose, 4–5(–10) mm in diam., hirsute, blue when mature.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Wong Chuk Yeung, Shing Mun, Yuen Tun Ha, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 1629; P. S. Choi 261; Y. W. Lam 508.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Lasianthus chinensis (Champ. ex Benth.) Benth. 粗葉木
FHK 160. 1861; FKH 134. 1912; FHN 3: 337. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 280, pl. 123, photo 177. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 84, pl. 22: 1 – 5. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 123. 2001; FGD 6: 221. 2005.
Mephitidia chinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 196. 1852.

Shrubs, 2–4 m tall. Branches flattened and shortly tomentose when young, terete and nearly glabrous in age. Leaves thin‑leathery or thickly papery; petioles 6–8 mm, shortly tomentose; stipules triangular‑subulate, the upper ones rather long; leaf blade oblong, elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate, 11–21 × 3.5–7.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous, tawny tomentose on abaxial surface; lateral veins 9–14 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces; veinlets reticulate. Flowers 5 – 6 in axillary sessile clusters. Bracts absent. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped, shortly tomentose outside; lobes triangular‑ovate. Corolla salverform; tube ca. 10 mm, white tomentellous on the upper part; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, about the length of the tube, very hairy on the abaxial surface. Drupes globular, 5–6 mm in diam., pubescent, blue or purplish when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 605; S. C. Ng 3789; K. L. Yip 4380.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by J. G. Champion from Wong Nai Chung and Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Lasianthus curtisii King & Gamble 廣東粗葉木
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal. 73(3): 128. 1904; FTW ed. 2, 4: 280, pl. 124. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 92, pl. 24: 7 – 12. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 126. 2001; FGD 6: 219. 2005.
Lasianthus kwangtungensis Merr., Lingnan. Sci. J. 7: 323. 1929.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and stipules densely hirsute. Leaves papery; petioles rather thick, usually less than 10 mm; stipules small, narrowly triangular, 1.5–2 mm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate or oblong, sometimes subovate, 5–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate or caudate, olive green or glaucescent when dry, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface villose or hirsute; lateral veins 5–6 on each side of midvein; veinlets slender subparallel. Flowers more than 10 in axillary sessile clusters. Bracts none or very small. Calyx‑tube subobconical, ca. 1.5 mm, densely hirsute; lobes usually 5, linear‑lanceolate or narrowly lanceolate, 3 – 4(–5) mm, much longer than the tube. Corolla white, 7–8 mm, hirsute outside, villose inside; lobes 5, oblong‑lanceolate, about the length of the tube, very hairy on the abaxial surface. Drupes subglobose or ovoid, 4–5(–7) mm in diam., hirsute, blue to dark blue when mature.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po. W. J. Tutcher 10919; Y. W. Lam 180, 497.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

Lasianthus fordii Hance 羅浮粗葉木
J. Bot. 23(275): 324. 1885; FKH 134. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 284, pl. 126, photo 178. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 97, pl. 25: 5 – 9. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 127. 2001; FGD 6: 221, fig. 119. 2005.

Shrubs, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets slender, slightly angled, glabrous. Leaves papery; petioles 5–10 mm, hirsute; stipules small, subtriangular, 1–1.5 mm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate or oblong‑ovate, sometimes oblong, 5–12 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate‑acuminate, glabrous or sparsely hirsute on midvein and lateral veins; lateral veins 4–5(–6) on each side of midvein; veinlets slender, subparallel. Flowers subsessile, in axillary clusters. Bracts very small or absent. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1.2–1.5 mm, usually glabrous; lobes 4 or 5, very small, 0.3–0.5 mm, sparsely hirsute. Corolla white, tubular or ± funnel‑shaped; tube 4–5 mm, glabrous outside, white‑villose on the upper part of inside; lobes 4–5, narrowly triangular‑lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm, apex incurved and beak‑shaped, sparsely hirsute near apex abaxially, white pubescent adaxially. Drupes subglobose, ca. 6 mm in diam., glabrous, blue or purplish when mature.

Locality: Shing Mun, Yin Ngam, Wong Chuk Yeung, Wu Kau Tang. P. S. Choi 438; Y. W. Lam 495, 504.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

Lasianthus hirsutus (Roxb.) Merr. 雞屎樹
J. Arnold Arbor. 33(3): 229. 1952; FRPS 71(2): 79, pl. 27: 5 – 10. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 129. 2001; FGD 6: 217. 2005.
Lasianthus cyanocarpus auct. non Jack: FHK 160. 1861; FKH 134. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 280, pl. 125. 1998.
Triosteum hirsutum Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 180. 1824.

Shrubs, 1–2(–3) m tall. Branchlets, bracts and abaxial surface of leaves densely rusty hirsute. Leaves papery; petioles 8–15 mm or slightly longer, densely covered with appressed coarse hairs; stipules ovate‑triangular, 8–12 mm, densely hirsute; leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, oblong‑obovate, oblong, or sometimes oblanceolate, 15–25 × 4– 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, broadly cuneate or obtuse, adaxial surface hirsute or glabrescent, abaxial surface thickly hirsute; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein; veinlets parallel. Bracts many, outer ones larger, ovate or lanceolate, 2.5–3 × 1–1.5 cm, apex caudate, inner ones smaller, linear‑lanceolate. Flowers 5 – 6 in axillary sessile clusters. Calyx‑tube sub‑bell‑shaped, 1.5–2 mm, densely appressed setose on the upper part; lobes 4 or 5, subulate, ca. 1.5 mm. Corolla white, funnel‑shaped; tube 12–13 mm, sparsely glandular pubescent outside, densely villose on the upper part inside; lobes 4 or 5, oblong or lanceolate, ca. 3.5 mm, glandular‑ciliate. Drupes subglobose, 7–8 mm in diam., blue or purplish when mature, sparsely hairy or glabrescent.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Happy Valley, Wong Chuk Yeung. Y. W. Lam 750, 507, 1642.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

Lasianthus verticillatus (Lour.) Merr. 斜脈粗葉木
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. n.s., 24(2): 372. 1935; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2):144. 2001; FYN 15: 245. 2003; FGD 6: 224. 2005.
Lasianthus obliquinervis Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 1 (suppl. 1): 136. 1907; FRPS 71(2): 100, pl. 26: 1 – 6. 1999; Check List HK Plants 267. 2002; 92. 2004.
Lasianthus trichophlebus auct. non Hemsl.: FHN 3: 336. 1974.
Dasus verticillatus Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 142. 1790.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall. Branches subterete, becoming black or dark grey when dry, sparsely puberulent (visible under hand lens). Leaves thickly papery or subleathery; petioles rather thick, usually less than 10 mm, densely appressed‑pubescent; stipules subtriangular, 3.5–5 mm, appressed‑pubescent; leaf blade oblong to narrowly oblong, occasionally elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, rarely obovate, 10–20 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base acute or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, often slightly oblique, grey or greyish brown when dry, adaxial surface glabrous and shining, abaxial surface appressed‑pubescent on veins and veinlets; lateral veins 5–7(–9) on each side of midvein; veinlets subparallel. Flowers sessile, in axillary clusters. Bracts none. Calyx‑tube ± bell‑shaped, 4–5 mm, pubescent; limb almost truncate. Corolla white; tube ca. 6 mm, hirsute abaxially, white‑villose on the upper part adaxially; lobes 5, oblong or ovate, ca. 4 mm, villose on the adaxial surface. Drupes ovoid, 7 – 9 mm in diam., pubescent.

Locality: Tai Tam, Fei Ngo Shan, Shing Mun, Wu Kau Tang, Kai Kung Leng. S. C. Ng 3151; K. L. Yip 4458.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

Launaea sarmentosa (Willd.) Sch.‑Bip. ex Kuntze 匍莖栓果菊
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 350. 1891; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 35. 1967; FRPS 80(1): 164. 1997; FGD 8: 262. 2007.
Prenanthes sarmentosa Willd., Phyt. 10: t. 6, fig. 2. 1794.
Launaea pinnatifida Cass., Ann. Sci. Nat. (Paris) 23: 85. 1831; FKH 151. 1912.

Perennial creeping herbs; stem 20–250 cm or longer, glabrous, subglabrous or arachnoid hairy, with adventitious roots and rosulate leaves growing at nodes. Basal leaves in rosette, oblanceolate, 2–8(–15) × 0.5–2.5(–6) cm, pinnatilobed or with margin crenate‑sinuate, apical lobes irregularly rhomboid, triangular or elliptic, apex rounded or obtuse; lateral lobes 1–5 pairs, triangular to elliptic, gradually smaller downward, opposite or alternate with each other, apex obtuse to rounded. Cauline leaves growing on stem nodes, rosulate, shape similar to basal ones but smaller in size. All leaves with base attenuate into winged petiole 0.5–5 cm long or sessile, both surfaces glabrous. Capitula homogamous, about 12–14 florets per head, solitary to the rosettes of basal leaves and of stem nodes; peduncles 0.5–4.5 cm, bearing few ovate bracteoles about 3 mm long near the capitulum. Involucres cylindric, 12–14 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, margin membranous, glabrous abaxially; outer rows small, triangular or ovate, 2–4 × 1.2–2 mm, obtuse; median ones ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 5–8 × 1.2–2 mm, acute to obtuse; inner ones linear, 10–14 × 1.5–2 mm, acute or obtuse. Ligulate florets yellow, 1.8 cm, lower tube 1 cm, ligule 0.8 cm, 5‑lobed apically; anther bases sagittate and serrulate, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches slender and hairy. Cypselae brown, cylindric, 3.5 mm, largely and obtusely 4‑ribbed, transversely rugose. Pappus white, capillary and slender, 8–10 mm, connate at base, shed off as a whole ring.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 42; Y. W. Lam 463; S. Y. Hu 10252 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong and other S China coastal regions; India, Egypt, W Africa.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Laurentia longiflora (L.) Endl. 同瓣草
Gen. Pl. 512. 1838; E. Wimm., Field Mus. Nat. Hist., Bot. Ser. 13(6/2): 474 – 475. 1937; Das Pflanzenreich. IV. 276b (Heft 107): 405. 1953; FGD 3: 331, fig. 217. 1995.
Hippobroma longiflora (L.) D. Don, Gen. Hist. 3: 717. 1834; FTW ed. 2, 4: 787, pl. 364. 1998.
Isotoma longiflora C. Presl, Prodr. Monogr. Lobel. 42. 1836.; FKH 152. 1912.
Lobelia longiflora L., Sp. Pl. 930. 1753.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect, to 50 cm tall, ± pubescent, marked with raised lines descending from base of petioles. Leaves alternate; petioles very short or almost obsolete; leaf blades oblong‑oblanceolate or lanceolate, 6–16 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin coarsely serrate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces when young. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves; pedicels 5–8 mm, densely hirsute; bracteoles 2, linear, attached to the base of pedicels. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes linear, 8–10 mm, hairy and irregularly serrate. Corolla white, hairy; tube slender, 5 – 9 cm; lobes 5, subequal, lanceolate, 1.5–2 cm. Stamens adnate to the middle of corolla‑tube; anthers coherent, bearded at apex. Ovary usually with 10 ribs, densely hairy, especially on the ribs. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 1.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 351, 2036; L. T. Lo 66.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; native to W Indies and S America; widely cultivated or naturalized elsewhere in tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: May–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, poison (mammals).

Lawsonia inermis L. 散沫花（指甲花）
Sp. Pl. 349. 1753; FKH 109. 1912; FRPS 52(2): 111. 1983; FGD 3: 80, fig. 56. 1995.

Shrub, unarmed, up to 6 m tall. Branchlets slightly 4-angled. Leaves decussate, elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 1.5 – 5 × 1 – 2 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, decurrent to petioles, apex acute, lateral veins 5 on each side of midvein, slender. Panicles up to 40 cm. Flowers very fragrant, white, rosy to vermilion, 6–8 mm in diam. Calyx 2–5 mm, 4-lobed, lobes deltoid. Petals 4, slightly longer than calyx-lobes, crisped, margin involute. Stamens 8. Ovary subglobular. Capsules oblate, 5–7 mm in diam., with 4 concave tracks. Seeds numerous, thick.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 42; Y. S. Lau 2612; HK sheet 11775.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Jiangsu, Zhejiang (cultivated); Asia, N Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. – Oct.; fruiting: Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (spice, dye).

Leersia hexandra Sw. 李氏禾
Prodr. 21. 1788; FKH 317. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 6: 321. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 9, pl. 2: 4. 2002; FOC 22: 184. 2006; FGD 9: 333. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect from decumbent base, up to 50 cm or more tall, nodes swollen, retrorsely puberulent. Leaf blades narrowly linear-lanceolate, 3–12 × 0.2–0.6 cm, flat or sometimes rolled, abaxial surface scabrid on midrib, base contracted, apex sharply acute; ligules membranous, 1–3 mm, truncate; leaf sheaths smooth or scabrid. Panicle loose, lanceolateoblong in outline, 5–10 cm. Spikelets narrowly elliptic to ellipticoblong, 3–5 × 1.2– 1.5 mm, pale green or purple tinged, contracted at base; lemma 5-veined, conspicuously pectinate-hispid on keel, lateral veins and sometimes surface sparsely spinulose, margins shortly hispid, apex contracted into a short obtuse beak; palea same texture and length as lemma, 3-veined. Stamens 6, anthers 2–2.5 mm.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 891; HK sheet 30737, 41941.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Marshlands, stream banks, shallow water. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Lemna minor L. 浮萍
Sp. Pl. 2: 970. 1753; FKH 290. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 210, pl. 42: 3. 1979; FGD 4: 410, fig. 249: 4–6. 2000; FOC 23: 82. 2010.

Small aquatic herb, free floating on water surface. Frond flat, suborbicular, obovate to obovate-elliptic, 2–6 × 2–3 mm, 1–many cohering in small groups, green and shining, sometimes reddish adaxially, scarcely reddish abaxially, margins entire, with a pouch on one side; veins 3(–5), reaching nearly apex. Root usually 2–4 cm, mostly with a rounded tip. Flowers minute, petalless; stamens 2; ovary 1-locular, with 1 ovule. Fruit winged laterally towards top; seed with 10–16 distinct ribs.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 29837.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical to temperate regions.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and ditches.
Uses: Animal food.

Leonurus japonicus Houtt. 益母草
Nat. Hist. 9: 366. 1778; FOC. 17: 163. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 480, pl. 210. 1998.
Leonurus artemisia (Lour.) S. Y. Hu, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 2(2): 381. 1974; FRPS 65(2): 508, pl. 99: 1 – 7. 1977; FGD 3: 420. 1995.
Stachys artemisia Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 365 – 366. 1790.
Leonurus sibiricus auct. non L.: FHK 276. 1861; FKH 211. 1912.

Annual or biennial herbs, 30–120 cm tall. Stems obtusely angled, furrowed, retrorse strigose. Leaves very variable in shape, the lower and basal leaves ovate in outline, base broadly cuneate, 3‑palmatipartite; lobes oblong‑rhombic to ovate, 2.5–6 × 1.5–4 cm, pinnately divided, adaxially strigose, abaxially pilose, glandular; upper leaves deeply divided into 3 or more oblong‑linear to linear segments, or the uppermost sometimes linear and entire. Verticillasters 8–15‑flowered, 2–2.5 cm in diam., the lower ones axillary and distant, the upper ones forming a terminal spike; bracts subulate or spinescent, 4–10 mm. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 5–6 mm, lengthening to 7–8 mm in fruit, appressed puberulent; teeth 5, subulate. Corolla red or white, 10–12 mm; tube often obliquely hairy annulate inside; upper lip erect, obovate, entire, pubescent abaxially; lower lip 3‑lobed, the middle lobe obcordate, pubescent. Filaments sparsely scaly. Nutlets ellipsoidal, apex truncate, smooth.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Plover Cove, Sai Kung, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 76; P. S. Choi 461; Y. W. Lam 1553.
Distribution: Widely distributed in all provinces of China; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Africa, America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lepidagathis incurva Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don 鱗花草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 119. 1825; FHN 3: 552. 1974; FRPS 70: 200. 2002.
Lepidogathis hyalina Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 95. 1832; FHK 263. 1861; FKH 199. 1912.

Herbs, 0.3–1 m tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, pubescent along sulcus and on nodes, soon glabrescent. Petiole 0.5–3.5 cm, glabrescent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 3–11 × 1–4.5 cm, base cuneate and obviously decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire and slightly undulate, pubescent, soon glabrescent with few hairs or sparsely pubescent along veins, sparsely covered with cystoliths, the lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Spike (0.5–)1–3 cm, mostly terminal or axillary, one‑sided, usually 2–3‑clustered. Bracts whitish yellow, oblong‑lanceolate, 6–8 × 1.5–2 mm, apex long acuminate, abaxially scarious, puberulent, margin ciliate; bracteoles whitish yellow, similar to bracts, but smaller, ca. 6 × 1.5 mm. Calyx whitish yellow, 5‑lobed; lobes heteromorphic, linear‑lanceolate, abaxially scarious, puberulent or glabrescent, margin ciliate, anterior two ca. 7 × 1 mm, connate to the middle, posterior one slightly longer than others, ca. 8 × 1.5 mm, lateral ones smallest, ca. 6 × 0.8 mm, Corolla white, streaked with purple, ca. 0.8–1 cm, outside sparsely pilose, inside densely white pubescent below throat tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, ovate, 2 × 3 mm, emarginate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted near middle of corolla tube, exserted from mouth of corolla; filaments ca. 2.5 – 3 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae ovate, ca. 1 mm. Ovary ca. 1 mm, hispid at tip; style ca. 8 mm, subglabrous. Capsule ca. 5 mm, ovate‑oblong, 4‑angled, glabrous except for pilose at tip, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 167; K. L. Yip 4466; HK sheet 39399.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets, grasslands, roadsides. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lepidium virginicum L. 北美獨行菜
Sp. Pl. 2: 645. 1753; FGD 3: 32. 1995; FOC 8: 32. 2001.
Lepidium ruderale auct. non L.: FKH 35. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, 10 –25 cm tall. Stems erect, with clavate glandular hairs. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; basal leaves oblanceolate, 1–5 cm, pinnatifid; lobes apex acute, margin serrate or dentate, adpressedly pubescent on both surfaces; cauline leaves shortly petiolate, oblanceolate or linear, 1.5 –5.5 cm × 5 –10 mm, apex acute, margin serrate or entire. Racemes terminal. Sepals elliptic, ca. 1 mm. Petals white, spathulate, 1–1.2 mm, rarely rudimentary. Stamens 2 or 4. Silicles orbicular, 2–3 mm, narrowly winged apically, apex emarginate. Seeds reddish brown, ovate, ca, 2 mm, narrowly winged, cotyledons accumbent.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 35619, 38871, 40207.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Liaoning, Shandong, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Japan, Pakistan, Russia; native to N America; introduced elsewhere.
Ecology: Fields, roadsides, waste places, grassy areas. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: May–Sep.
Notes: This species was reported as Lepidium apetalum Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 111. 2002).

Lepidosperma chinense Nees 鱗子莎
Linnaea 9: 302. 1834; FHK 398. 1861; FKH 302. 1912; FRPS 11: 120. 1961; FGD 8: 321. 2007; FOC 23: 260. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome stout, short. Culms slender to rather stout, rigid, (25–)40–150(–250) cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, subterete or slightly angular, smooth, few-leaved at the base. Leaves shorter than the stems, almost terete, 2–4 mm thick, with a shallow, very inconspicuous groove, rigid, glaucous, pith chambered by many approximate transverse partitions; sheaths chestnut-coloured, lower ones bladeless. Panicle narrowly oblong, dense, often somewhat interrupted at the base, 3–10 cm, consisting of several oblong-lanceolate, suberect spikes. Involucral bracts spathe-like, shortly sheathing, blackish brown, rounded at the apex, the lowest ending in a short pungent blade. Spikelets crowded, oblonglanceolate, 5–6 mm, 2-flowered. Glumes 5–7, firm, oblong to lanceolate, 3–5 mm, black with rusty margins, apex obtuse to acute, the empty ones mucronulate, the upper ones subacute. Hypogynous scales small, connate at the base, whitish, 0.5–0.7 mm. Stamens 3, anthers ca. 2 mm, yellow. Styles slender, stigmas 3. Achene ellipsoidal, 2.5–4 × 1.5–3 mm, apiculate, shining rusty, purplish dotted.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 493; Y. W. Lam 1330; Y. S. Lau 2479.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Grasslands in valleys. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Lepironia articulata (Retz.) Domin. 石龍芻（蒲草、肇慶草）
Biblioth. Bot. 85: 486. 1915; FHN 4: 269. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 286. 2000; FGD 8: 349. 2007; FOC 23: 171. 2010.
Restio articulatus Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 14. 1786.
Lepironia mucronata Rich., Syn. Pl. 1: 70. 1805; FKH 301. 1912; FRPS 11: 202. 1961.

Perennial. Rhizome with greyish brown scales at least distally. Culms crowded in row along rhizome, stiff, 10–120 cm tall, 2–7 mm thick, terete, smooth. Leaf sheath open, the uppermost 12–26 cm long. Apex obliquely truncate. Involucral bract subulate, terete, 2.2–6 cm long. Inflorescence comprising 1 spike. Spike elliptic or oblong, terete, 10–35 × 3–7 mm, green to chestnut brown or purplish brown. Spicoid bracts oval, ovate-orbicular, 3.2–6.7 × 3–6.2 mm, apex rounded and often weakly recurved, easily detaching when mature. Spicoids ± equalling spicoid bracts. Floral bracts up to 15, lowest 2 linear-lanceolate, 4–6 mm long, keel ciliate. Achenes ovate or obovate to broadly obovate, biconvex, 3–4 × 2–2.8 mm (excluding 0.5 mm long beak), hard, brown, ± smooth to indistinctly longitudinally veined, often spinulose at apex.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. W. Lam 1776; K. L. Yip 4204; HK sheet 20634.
Distribution: Guangdong; Madagascar, India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Malesia, Micronesia, Australia, New Caledonia and Fiji.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Jun.
Uses: Weaving.

Leptochloa chinensis (L.) Nees 千金子
Syll. Pl. Nov. 1: 4. 1824; FHK 430. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 383. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 56, pl. 16: 7–12. 1990; FFJ 6: 158, fig. 130. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 425. 2000; FOC 22: 470. 2006; FGD 9: 353. 2009.
Poa chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 69. 1753.

Annual herb, 30 – 100 cm tall. Culms erect or geniculate at base, glabrous. Leaf blades flat or slightly involute, 5–25 × 0.2 – 0.9 cm, glabrous, scabrid on both surfaces or abaxial surface smooth, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–5 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous. Panicle 10–50 cm, composed of many unilateral racemes; rachis scabrid. Spikelets usually purplish or brownish green, narrowly elliptic-oblong, laterally compressed, 2–4 mm, 3–7-flowered; glumes scabrid along keels and sometimes laterally; lower glume lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm, apex acute; upper glume elliptic-oblong, 1.2–2 mm, apex obtuse; lemmas elliptic-oblong, keeled, lowest ca. 1.5 mm, shortly appressed-hairy along lower margins and on either side of midvein, apex obtuse or minutely emarginate; palea minutely hispid on keels, appressed hairy on back and flaps. Anthers ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis oblong, 0.7–0.9 mm, plano-convex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1352; HK sheet 42037, 42063.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Moist places in farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Leptochloa fusca (L.) Kunth 雙稃草
Revis. Gramin. 1: 91. 1829; FOC 22: 469. 2006; FGD 9: 353. 2009.
Festuca fusca L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 2: 876. 1759.
Diplachne fusca (L.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrost. 80, 163. 1812; FHN 4: 381. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 54, pl. 16: 1–6. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 410. 2000; FYN 9: 433. 2003; Check List HK Plants 333. 2002; 117. 2004 [“Diplachine”].

Perennial herb, 60–150 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, often rooting and branching from the lower nodes. Leaf blades tough, usually inrolled and needle-like, 10–45 cm × 1.5–3 mm, scabrid, grey-green with a broad white central vein; ligule hyaline, ca. 2 mm, tongue-shaped; leaf sheath glabrous. Inflorescence a contracted panicle, 15–35 cm, composed of many slender racemes of 7–15 cm. Spikelets narrowly elliptic to elliptic, 8–15 mm, slightly overlapping, grey-green or olivegreen, shortly pedicellate, 6 – 11-flowered; glumes papery, conspicuously 1-veined, keeled, scabrid on the keels, the lower lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 2–4.5 mm, apex acute or acuminate, the upper narrowly oblong, 3–7.5 mm, apex acute or obtuse and minutely mucronate; lemmas narrowly oblong, 3–6 mm, 3-veined, pilose on the lower part of the veins, 2- or more toothed and mucronate; midrib prolonged into a short awn of ca. 1.5 mm; palea elliptic, papery, 2-keeled, siliceous on keels. Anther ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 2 mm, dorso-ventrally flattened.

Locality: Sha Tin, Mai Po. Y. W. Lam 852; HK sheet 34224, 39692.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Hebei, Henan, Liaoning, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed from India through Malaysia, Indonesia to Australia, and extending to Africa.
Ecology: Swamps, marshes and other places with shallow water. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Leptochloa panicea (Retz.) Ohwi 蟣子草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 55: 311. 1941; FHN 4: 382. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 57, pl. 16: 3. 1990; FFJ 6: 159. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 427. 2000; FOC 22: 470. 2006; FGD 9: 354. 2009.
Poa panicea Retz., Observ. Bot. 3: 11. 1783.
Leptochloa filiformis auct. non Roem. & Schult: FKH 327. 1912.

Annual herb, 30–80 cm tall. Culms slender, tufted, ascending from the geniculate base. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–20 × 0.3–0.7 cm, glabrous or sparsely covered with tubercular hairs along lateral veins; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm, usually lacerate; leaf sheaths papillate-pilose. Panicle elliptic to oblong, 10–30(–50) cm, often purplish, composed of many slender unilateral racemes; rachis scabrid. Spikelets glaucous-green or purplish green, elliptic, ± laterally compressed, 1.4–2.5 mm, 2–5-flowered; glumes subequal, scabrid along keel; lower glume lanceolate, 0.7–1.5 mm, apex acuminate; upper glume narrowly oblong, 0.9–1.6 mm, apex acute or obtuse and mucronate; lemmas longer than the glumes, elliptic-oblong, keeled, lowest 0.8–1.3 mm, veins puberulous, usually also a few appressed hairs between veins, apex obtuse; palea keels scaberulous. Anthers ca. 0.2 mm. Caryopsis broadly elliptic, 0.7–0.8 mm, brown, obtusely trigonous, apex obtuse.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 1954; L. T. Lo 575.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa, America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, rice fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Lespedeza chinensis G. Don 中華胡枝子
Gen. Syst. 2: 307. 1832; FRPS 41: 155. 1995; FGD 5: 292. 2003.
Lespedeza cyrtobotrya auct. non Miq.: FKH 81. 1912, “cyclobotrya”.

Erect or ascending small shrub, ca. 1 m tall, all parts covered with white depressed hairs. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, widely-spaced along stem; leaflets ovate-oblong or obovate, 1.5–4 × 1–1.5 cm, apex emarginate or obtuse (sometimes truncate), bristle-tipped, margin slightly revolute, glabrous or puberulous adaxially, densely adpressed white-pubescent abaxially; terminal petiolules and rachides 3– 4 mm long. Racemes axillary, shorter than leaves. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes lanceolate, 3 mm. Corolla white or yellow; vexillum elliptic, 7 × 3 mm, clawed and with 2 auricles at base; wings narrowly oblong, 6 mm, long-clawed; keel 8 mm. Cleistogamous flowers on lower branches, axillary, without pedicels. Pods ovate, 4 × 2.5– 3 mm, apex beaked, reticulate and adpressed white-pubescent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Ham Tin, Ping Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1625; P. S. Choi 537; Y. W. Lam 1213.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Grasses and thickets. Flowering: Aug. – Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Lespedeza cuneata (Dum.-Cours.) G. Don 截葉鐵掃帚
Gen. Syst. 2: 307. 1832; FKH 85. 1861; FRPS 41: 156. 1995.
Anthyllis cuneata Dum.-Cours. Bot. Cult. 6: 100. 1811.
Lespedeza juncea auct. non Pers.: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 81. 1912.

Erect or ascending small shrub, up to 1 m tall. Leaves palmately 3-foliolate, closely-spaced along stem; leaflets linear-lanceolate, 10 – 30 × 2 – 5 mm, base cuneate, apex truncate, bristle-tipped, glabrous adaxially, appressed hairy abaxially; terminal petiolules and rachides to 1 mm long. Flowers 2 – 4-fasciculate, axillary. Calyx narrowly campanulate, 5-lobed; lobes narrowly lanceolate. Corolla yellowish or white, ca. 6 mm; vexillum whitish-yellow, violet-stripped at base; wings equal to vexillum; keel slightly longer. Cleistogamous flowers few, in axillary fascicles. Pods subglobular, 2.5 –3.5 × 2.5 mm, sparsely silk-hairy.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Ping Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1673; P. S. Choi 285; Y. W. Lam 1132.
Distribution: Shandong, Gansu and widely spread over areas S of Changjiang River; Korea, Japan, India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Australia.
Ecology: Roadsides, grassy fields. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Lespedeza formosa (Vogel) Koehne 美麗胡枝子

Deut. Dendro l. 343. 1893; Akiyama & Ohba, Univ. Mus., Univ. Tokyo, Bull. No. 31: 225. 1988; Akiyama, Univ. Mus., Univ. Tokyo, Bull. No. 33. 1988; FRPS 41: 138. 1995; FGD 5: 289, fig. 156. 2003.

Desmodium formosum Vogel, Nova Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 29. 1843.

Lespedeza bicolor Turcz. subsp. formosa (Vogel) Hsu, X. Y. Li & D. X. Gu, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 31: 314. 1983.

Lespedeza viatorum Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 46. 1852; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 183. 1887; FHK 56. 1861; FKH 81. 1912.

Lespedeza wilfordii Ricker, Lingnan Sci. J. 20 (2 – 4): 203. 1942; FRPS 41: 143. 1995.


Erect shrub, 1–2 m tall. Stems much branched. Branchlets pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets ovate (or oblong), 2.5–6 × 1 – 3 cm, emarginate or mucronate, sparsely pubescent adaxially, adpressed pubescent abaxially; petioles 3 cm; terminal petiolules and rachides 10–15 mm long, petiolules swollen. Racemes axillary or forming terminal panicles, 7–8 cm. Calyx campanulate, 5–7 mm, 5-lobed; lobes oblong-lanceolate. Corolla violet, 1 – 1.5 cm; petals clawed and auriculate at base; vexillum suborbicular; wings obovate-oblong, shorter than vexillum and keel, 7 – 8 mm. Pods obovate or obovate-oblong, 8 × 4 mm, reticulate and pubescent, 1-seeded.


Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Lam Chung, Castle Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Long Sai Wan. Y. S. Lau 1688, 2061; P. S. Choi 109.

Distribution: Area S of Qinling and extending northward to Shaanxi and Gansu; India, Korea, Japan.

Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests. Flowering: Jul. – Sep.; fruiting: Sep. – Dec.

Notes: The type specimen of Lespedeza viatorum was collected from Little Hong Kong by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850 whereas the type specimen of Lespedeza wilfordii was collected from Hong Kong by C. Wilford between 1857 and 1858. These two formerly published species feature leaflets with obtuse-rounded or emarginate apex. Leaflets of L. viatorum are broadly obovate or broadly obcordate, 1.5– 4 × 1– 3 cm and pods are 8– 10 mm long, whereas leaflets of L. wilfordii are oblong-elliptic, 4– 5 × 2.5– 3.5 cm and pods are 10 –12 mm long. Lespedeza formosa is a broadly-ranged species (from E Himalayas to China, Korea and Japan) and shows remarkable geographical variation in the shape and size of calyx and corolla. As shown in the studies by Hsu et al. (1983), Akiyama and Ohba (1988) and Akiyama (1988), the various forms within the geographical range should be recognized as subspecific entities. Akiyama (1988) synonymized Lespedeza viatorum and L. wilfordii under L. formosa subsp. formosa, the range of which includes SE China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.

Leucaena leucocephala (Lam.) de Wit 銀合歡
Taxon 10(2): 53. 1961; FRPS 39: 18. 1988; FGD 5: 156, fig. 90. 2003.

Mimosa leucocepha Lam., Encycl. 1(1): 12. 1783.
Leucaena glauca (Willd.) Benth., J. Bot. (Hooker) 4(32): 416. 1842; FHK 100. 1861; FKH 91. 1912.
Mimosa glauca L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 1504. 1763, non 1753.

Shrub or small tree, 2–6 m tall, unarmed. Branchlets pubescent, glabrous in age, with brown lenticels. Stipules deltoid, very small, caducous. Pinnae 4–8 pairs, 5–9(–16) cm, rachis pubescent, with black glands at the insertion of lowest pinnae; leaflets 5–15 pairs, linear-oblong, 7–13 × 1.5–3 mm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin ciliate, midvein close to upper margin. Heads usually 1–2, axillary, 2–3 cm in diam. Bracts pubescent, deciduous. Peduncle 2–4 cm. Flowers white. Calyx 3 mm, apex 5-toothed, pubescent abaxially. Petals narrowly oblanceolate, 5 mm, pubescent abaxially. Stamens 10, sparsely pubescent, 7 mm. Ovary shortly stipitate, sparsely pubescent, stigma cupulate. Pod leathery, strap-shaped, 10–18 × 1.4–2 cm, straight, flat, base attenuate, pedicels in fruit up to 3 cm, pubescent, beak acute, hard. Seeds 6–25, brown, oval, 7.5 mm, flat, glossy.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. H. C. Tang 623, 870; Y. S. Lau 3290.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan; originally from tropical America, now widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Hillslopes, margins of forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jul; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Environmental (agroforestry), green manure, animal food, fuelwood.
records.uses: Environmental (agroforestry), green manure, animal food, fuelwood.

Leucanthemum vulgare Lam. 濱菊（延命菊）
Fl. Franc. 2: 137. 1778; FRPS 76(1): 25. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1010. 1998; FGD 8: 197, fig. 116. 2007.
Chrysanthemum leucanthemum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 888. 1753.

Perennial erect herbs 15–100 cm tall, with simple or branched stems, glabrous or subglabrous. Basal and lower cauline leaves obovate‑spatulate to oblanceolate‑spatulate, 5–10 × 1.5–2.2 cm, margin crenate to obtuse‑dentate, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex obtuse; upper cauline leaves oblong, margin crenate to pinnatifid, base attenuate, sessile, somewhat auriculate and semi‑amplexicaul, both surfaces glabrous; uppermost leaves smaller in size, sometimes pinnatisect. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2–5 cm across, long‑pedunculate, solitary, terminal to stem and branches. Involucres 0.5 – 1 × 1–2 cm; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, ovate‑oblong to lanceolate, glabrous, green, margin and apex scarious, brownish or dark, the innermost one with apical scales broaden as rounded appendages. Ray florets pistillate, corolla white, ligule oblong, 0.8–2.5 cm. Disk florets hermaphrodite, corolla yellow, tube base swollen and skirt‑like, slightly covering the apical region of hypanthium, middle part constricted and upper part campanulate, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae subcylindric, cuneate at base, 2 – 3 mm, prominently 10‑ribbed, ribs projected into the apical rim, ribs pale brown and grooves black. Pappus absent or with short coronate scales or auricles on ray cypselae.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 586 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22008 (CUHK).
Distribution: Caucasus, W Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Leucas lavandulifolia Sm. 線葉白絨草
Cycl. 20, sect. 2, pt. 40. 1812; FRPS 65(2): 426, pl. 83: 7 – 8. 1977; FOC 17: 143. 1994; FGD 3: 416. 1995.
Leucas linifolia (Roth.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 2: 743. 1825; FKH 212. 1912.
Phlomis linifolia Roth., Nov. Pl. Sp. 260. 1821.

Annual herbs, 20–80 cm tall, often many‑branched. Stems and branches grey pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles very short or almost obsolete; leaf blade linear‑lanceolate, rarely lanceolate, 3–7 × 0.5–1.2 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire or sparsely undulate‑serrate, greyish puberulent on both surfaces. Verticillasters many‑flowered, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam.; bracts linear, 3–4 mm, puberulous. Calyx obliquely turbinate, 5– 6 mm, lengthening to 7–9 mm in fruit, puberulent or glabrescent abaxially, veins inconspicuous, mouth oblique; teeth varying from 8 – 10, the uppermost one the largest. Corolla white, ca. 1.5 cm; tube villous annulate inside near the middle; upper lip oblong, woolly; lower lip patent, the middle lob large, obovate. Nutlets ovoid, brown.

Locality: Chai Wan. HK sheet 4479.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan; India to Cochichina, Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.

Leucas mollissima Wall. ex Benth. var. chinensis Benth. 疏毛白絨草
Prodr. 12: 525. 1848; FRPS 65(2): 421. 1977; FOC 17: 142. 1994; FGD 3: 415. 1995.
Leucas mollissimum auct. non Wall. ex Benth.: FHK 279. 1861; FKH 212. 1912.

Annual or perennial herbs, 40–60 cm, sometimes up to 1 m tall. Stems slender, twisted, and many‑branched, appressed tomentose‑villous. Leaves papery; petioles short, less than 1 cm, or subsessile in upper leaves; leaf blade ovate, 1.5–4 × 1–2.3 cm, usually the leaves on the lower part of branches larger, gradually reduced in size upwards, base broadly cuneate to cordate, apex acute, margin crenate or serrate, densely appressed tomentose on both surfaces, the lower often silvery glaucous. Verticillasters axillary, globose, 1.5–2 cm in diam.; bracts linear, 2–3 mm, densely villous. Calyx cylindric, 6–7 mm, densely pubescent abaxially, 10‑veined, mouth truncate; teeth 10, 5 long and 5 short. Corolla white, yellowish to pink, ca. 1.3 cm, curved, puberulent near throat abaxially; upper lip 3– 4 mm; lower lip 7–9 mm, nearly flat. Nutlets ovoid, triquetrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3072; Y. W. Lam 780, 1067.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: This species was recorded as Leucas flaccida R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 76. 1993).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: This species was recorded as Leucas flaccida R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 76. 1993).
