Licuala fordiana Becc. 穗花軸櫚
Malesia 3: 198. 1889; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 159. 1977; FGD 2: 444. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 30. 1991; FOC 23: 149. 2010.

Moderate shrub, 1.5–2 m tall. Stems clustered, short. Leaves palmate, subrounded or fan-shaped in outline, deeply divided into 15–20 segments; middle segment wider than others, 25–45 × 2–5 cm, apex dentate; petioles 0.8–1 m, the lower half sparsely armed with recurved spines on margins, or sometimes without spines. Inflorescence axillary, 0.5–1.2 m, unbranched or only branched at base, rachillae 1–3, 15–20 cm, hairy; flowers hermaphroditic 6–8 × 2.5 mm. Fruits globose, 7–8 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Parker. HK sheet 7673, 7675, 33472.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests, altitude below 500 m. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Mar.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ligularia japonica (Thunb.) Less. 大頭橐吾
Syn. Gen. Comp. 390. 1832; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1–2): 61. 1967; FRPS 77(2): 14, pl. 2: 4–6. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1012, photo 472. 1998.
Arnica japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 319. 1784.
Senecio japonicus (Thunb.) Sch. Bip., Flora 28: 50. 1845; FKH 148. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 50 – 100 cm tall, puberulous or glabrous, tinged purple. Radical and lower leaves revolute in young stage, leaf blade reniform, 5 – 15 × 7 – 22 cm, palmately lobed and veined, margin serrate, abaxial surface puberulous or glabrescent; petiole 4 – 27 cm. Cauline leaves few; shortly petiolate, sheath amplexicaul. Uppermost leaves much smaller and without sheath. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2 – 8 arranged as corymbs, without subtending bracteoles at base; peduncles 2 – 26 cm, tomentulose‑puberulous. Involucres hemispherical, abaxial side puberulous; phyllaries 9 – 12, oblong, 1.5 – 2 × 4 – 5 mm, acute or acuminate, margin scarious. Marginal female florets 1‑seriate, corolla ligulate, yellow, ligule oblong, 4 – 5 × 0.5 – 1 cm, tube 7 – 10 mm. Disk bisexual florets many, corolla tubular, about 1.5 cm, apex 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 5 mm. Cypselae cylindric, 0.7 – 1 cm, ribbed and glabrous. Pappus reddish brown, 1 – 1.4 cm.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lautau Peak. HK sheet 15868, 15869, 35601.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, India.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ligustrum liukiuense Koidz. 台灣女貞
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 30: 82. 1916; FTW ed. 2, 4: 137. 1998.
Ligustrum japonicum Thunb. var. pubescens Koidz., Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 30: 82. 1916.
Ligustrum amamianum Koidz., Pl. Nov. Amami‑Ohsima 7. 1929; FRPS 61: 144, pl. 40: 1 – 2. 1992; FOC 15: 301. 1996.

Evergreen shrubs, 3–5 m tall. Branchlets terete, puberulent at first, soon glabrous, compressed near nodes. Petiole 4–8 mm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, oblong to ovate, 3.5–7.5 × 1.8–3.8 cm, base obtuse to acute, decurrent, apex short acuminate or obtuse or acute, sometimes retuse, margin strongly revolute, glabrous, densely glandular dotted; lateral veins 5–8 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, slightly raised abaxially. Panicles terminal, 7–12 cm; rachis pubescent. Flowers subsessile; bract linear. Calyx ca. 1.8 mm. Corolla 4–6 mm; tube ca. as long as lobes. Stamens nearly approaching apex of corolla lobes; anthers ca. 2 mm. Fruit elliptic, 5–9 mm in diam.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2474; P. S. Choi 477; K. L. Yip 4493.
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Woods on limestone mountain ridges. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Ligustrum longipedicellatum H. T. Chang 長柄女貞
Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsen. 1982: 2. 1982; FOC 15: 304. 1996, pro syn. sub L. sinense var. luodianense M. C. Chang.
Ligustrum sinense var. luodianense M. C. Chang, Investig. Stud. Nat. 6: 77. 1986, p. p. quoad syn. L. longipedicellatum H. T. Chang.

Shrubs or small trees, 2–10 m tall. Young branchlets terete, glabrous. Petioles 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade subleathery, glabrous, oblong, 7–14 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acute, adaxially lustrous; margin entire; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 6–27 × 5–15 cm, rachis villous to glabrescent, 4‑ribbed; pedicels 3–5mm, glabrous and tenuous; bracteoles leafy, lanceolate, 1–3.5 × 0.3–1.5 cm. Calyx 4‑lobed, 1 mm. Corolla 3–5 mm; tube ca. 1–2 mm; lobes 2.5–3 mm. Stamens reaching apex of corolla lobes; filament ca. 5 mm; anthers ca. 1.8 mm. Ovary spheroidal, glabrous; style shorter than stamens. Fruit ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41615, 41867, 41872.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Notes: The species was considered as a synonym of L. sinense var. luodianense M. C. Chang, but it differs from the later by its oblong, glabrous leaves, and the terminal panicles.

Ligustrum lucidum W. T. Aiton 女貞
Hort. Kew. ed. 2, 1: 19. 1810; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 381, fig. 315. 1989; FRPS 61: 153. 1992; FOC 15: 302. 1996; FGD 5: 426. 2003.
Ligustrum nepalense Wall., Roxb. Fl. Ind. ed. 1, 151. 1820.
Ligustrum japonicum Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 207. 1780; FKH 166. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs or trees, 4–8 m or taller, glabrous. Branchlets terete, lenticellate. Petiole 1–3 cm; leaf blade leathery, glabrous, ovate to long‑ovate or elliptic, or elliptic to lanceolate, 6–17 × 3–8 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 10– 23 cm, spreading; rachis angular in fruit. Flowers sessile or nearly so. Calyx campanulate, 1–2 mm. Corolla white, 3.5–4.5 mm; lobes elliptic, slightly longer than tube. Stamens approaching apex of corolla lobes; anthers oblong, 1 – 1.5 mm; style 1.5–2.5 mm; stigma clavate. Fruit 7–10 × 4–6 mm, reniform or nearly so, white farinose and red‑black when matured.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2714; HK sheet 35579.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, host (lac/wax insect), medicinal (folklore).

Ligustrum punctifolium M. C. Chang 斑葉女貞
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 23(1): 53 – 54, pl. 1, fig. 1. 1985; FFJ 4: 379, fig. 311. 1989; FRPS 61: 142, pl. 39: 1 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 301. 1996; FGD 5: 424. 2003.
Ligustrum quihoui auct. non Carr. 1869: Merr. & Chun in Sunyatsenia 1: 79. 1930, quoad specim.Y. Tsiang 2933.

Evergreen shrubs, to 2 m tall. Branchlets terete, puberulent. Petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, rarely ovate or obovate, 1–2 × 0.8–1.2 cm, base cuneate to suborbicular, apex obtuse or retuse, occasionally acute, glabrous except for midvein adaxially, sometimes puberulent, brown glandular dotted and abaxially much denser; lateral veins 2 or 3 on each side of midvein, obscure. Panicles terminal, ca. 5 × 2 cm; peduncle puberulent; pedicels 0.5–1.3 mm, glabrous. Calyx ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous, apex undulate‑denticulate or truncate. Corolla 7.5–9 mm, white or yellowish; tube ca. as long as lobes. Stamens 2, reaching apex of corolla lobes; anthers oblong. Fruit subglobose, ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Chung Mei, Sam A Chung, Sham Chung. W. J. Tutcher 10927, 10950; HK sheet 36612.
Distribution: Hainan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Tidal flood plains. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen (Y. Tsiang 2933, IBSC) was collected from a tidal flood plain in Hong Kong on 12 Aug. 1929. Lai (2003, Porcupine No. 23: 19. 2001) provided a review of the history of discovery of this species. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Ligustrum sinense Lour. 山指甲
FL. Cochinch. 1: 19. 1790; FHK 215. 1861; FKH 166; 1912; FFJ 4: 382, fig. 316. 1989; FRPS 61: 158, pl. 44: 1 – 8. 1992; FOC 15: 303. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 138, pl. 51. 1998; FGD 5: 427. 2003.

Deciduous shrubs or small trees, 2–4(–7) m tall. Branchlets terete, villous to glabrescent. Petiole 2–8 mm; leaf blade papery to thinly leathery, ovate, elliptic or suborbicular, 2–7 × 1.5–3 cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, sometimes retuse, villous to sparsely pubescent or puberulous on midvein, epunctate, lateral veins 4–8 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Panicles terminal or axillary, 4–11 ×3–8 cm; peduncle yellowish puberulent to glabrescent; pedicels 1–3 mm. Calyx campanulate, 1 mm, glabrous or pubescent. Corolla white, 3.5–5.5 mm; tube ca. 1.5–2.5 mm, lobes oblong to ovate‑oblong, ca. 2–3 mm, slightly longer than tube, apex blunt. Stamens reaching apex of corolla lobes or exserted; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm. Fruit subglobose, 5–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong and widely cultivated. H. C. Tang 40, 104, 197.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam. Becomes invasive in Australasia and SE USA.
Ecology: Naturalized along thickets and roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Lilium brownii F. E. Brown ex Miellez 野百合
Cat. Expos. Soc. Hort. Lille. 1841; FKH 280. 1912; FRPS 14: 121, pl. 31: 7. 1980; FOC 24: 147. 2000; FGD 6: 339. 2005.
Lilium longiflorum auct. non Thunb.: FHK 374. 1861; FKH 280. 1912.

Perennial herb. Bulb globose, 3–5 cm in diam.; scales white, lanceolate, 2–4 cm. Stem 0.7–2 m, green or sometimes with purplish strips. Leaves scattered, lower leaves lanceolate to ellipticlanceolate, or obovate, 5–15 × 0.6–2 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex acuminate, 5–7-veined; distal ones gradually becoming smaller, lanceolate or linear. Flowers funnel-shaped, fragrant, solitary or 2–3 on a short peduncle; pedicels 3–10 cm, bent downward; bracts lanceolate, 3–9 × 1–2 cm. Perianth segments 6, oblong-oblanceolate to spatulate, 13–18 × (1–)2–4.3 cm, spreading distally and recurved apically, milk white adaxially, unspotted, with bronzy purple markings abaxially; nectaries papillose on both surfaces. Stamens curved upward; filaments 10–12 cm, densely pilose to glabrous; anthers oblong, 1–1.5 cm. Style 8.5–11 cm. Capsule subcylindrical, 4.5–6 cm.

Locality: Mount Violet, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Clear Water Bay, Tsing Yi. Y. S. Lau 2497.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Hillsides amongst grass. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Food, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Lilium longiflorum Thunb. is cultivated for ornamental in Hong Kong. It resembles L. brownii in aspect but may be distinguished by its glabrous filaments and the not papillose nectaries.

records.text:
Limnocharis flava (L.) Buchenau 黃花藺（黃花絨葉草）
Abh. Naturwiss. Vereine Bremen 2: 2. 1868; Fl. Males., Ser. I, 5(1): 120. 1954; FYN 4: 747, fig. 207. 1986; FRPS 8: 149, pl. 57. 1992; FOC 23: 89. 2010.
Alisma flavum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 343. 1753.
Limnocharis emarginata Bonpland, Pl. Aequinoct. 1: 116, t. 34. 1808[“1807”].

Aquatic herb. Petiole trigonous, 20–65 cm, stout; leaf blade 6–28 cm × 4.5–20 cm, veins 9–13, transverse veins many, parallel, base obtuse or subcordate, apex obtuse or retuse. Scapes upper trigonous, 20–90 cm; umbels 2–15-flowered; bracts green, orbicular to broadly elliptic, 1.5–2 × 1–1.5 cm. Pedicels thick, triquetrous, 2–7 cm. Petals yellowish but blackish toward base, broadly ovate to orbicular, 2–3 × 1–2 cm, apex rounded. Stamens shorter than petals; filaments green. Carpels yellowish green. Fruit cluster 1.5–2 cm in diam.; follicles suborbicular. Seeds brown.

Locality: Sha Tin, also cultivated in Hong Kong Wetland Park. Y. S. Lau 2603.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Yunnan; naturalized throughout S and SE Asia; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Marshes, shallow-water fields. Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, forage.

Limnophila aromatica (Lam.) Merr. 紫蘇草
Interpr. Rumph. Herb. Amb. 466. 1917; FHN 3: 502. 1974; FOC 18: 27. 1998; FGD 4: 368. 2000.
Ambulia aromatica Lam., Encycl. Meth. 1: 123. 1783.
Limnophila punctata Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14. 750. 1826; FHK 248. 1861.
Limnophila gratissima Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14. 749. 1826; FKH 186. 1912.

Annual herbs or perennial. Stems 30–70 cm tall, simple to many‑branched, glabrous or glandular, base decumbent and rooting from nodes. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3, sessile, ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate‑elliptic, 1–5 × 0.3–1.5 cm, base semiamplexicaul, margin crenate and serrate; veins pinnate. Flowers solitary in leaf axils or in terminal racemes. Pedicel 0.5–2 cm, glabrous or glandular. Bracteoles linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm. Calyx 4–6 mm, glabrous or glandular pubescent, with raised veins in fruit. Corolla white, blue‑purple or pink, 1–1.3 cm, sparsely and finely glandular, white villous adaxially; styles apex dilated. Capsules ovoid, ca. 6 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Au Mun, Sai Kung (Sai Wan), Tsing Fai Tong, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2528, 2957; Y. W. Lam 1215.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: A morphologically similar form was described as Limnophila aromaticoides Yang & Yen (擬紫蘇草; Bot. Bull. Acad. Sinica 38: 285 – 295. 1997), which could be distinguished by its verticillate submerged leaves, white corolla with occasional pinkish colour at top of tube, and orbicularly ellipsoidal capsule; whereas L. aromatica, in strict sense, is characterized by its submerged leaves mostly lacking corolla (occasionally with 2 – 3 submerged leaves), pink or purple corolla and ellipsoidal capsule. This form is observed in Hong Kong growing and flowering together with L. aromatica. Other authorities, however, considered the distinguishing characters of L. aromaticoides fell within the range of variation of L. aromatica and therefore put in the synonymy of the latter (e.g. FOC 18: 28. 1998).

records.text:
Limnophila chinensis (Osbeck) Merr. 中華石龍尾
Amer. J. Bot. 3: 581. 1916; FHN 3: 503. 1974; FOC 18: 28. 1998; FGD 4: 365. 2000.
Columnea chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 230. 1757.
Limnophila hirsuta (Heyne ex Benth.) Benth., Prodr. 10: 388. 1848; FHK 248. 1861; FKH 186. 1912.
Stemodia hirsuta Heyne ex Benth., Scroph. Ind. 24. 1835.

Herbs, 5–50 cm tall. Stems basally prostrate, rooting from nodes, simple or basally branched, villous or subglabrous. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 or 4, sessile, ovate‑lanceolate, linear‑lanceolate, or rarely spatulate, 0.5–5.3 × 0.2–1.5 cm, base subamplexicaul, margin serrate, abaxially villous along veins, adaxially glabrous or sparsely villous; veins pinnate, inconspicuous. Flowers solitary in leaf axils, or in terminal panicles. Pedicel 3–5 mm, villous to subglabrous. Bracteoles ca. 2 mm. Calyx 5–7 mm, villous or subglabrous, with raised veins in fruit. Corolla purple‑red, blue, or rarely white, 1–1.5 cm. Capsules compressed, broadly ellipsoidal, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung (Tai Wan). C. G. Matthew 5230; HK sheet 35392, 37908.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.

Limnophila heterophylla (Roxb.) Benth. 異葉石龍尾
Scroph. Ind. 25. 1835; FKH 186. 1912; FOC 18: 27. 1998; FGD 4: 366. 2000.
Columnea heterophylla Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 97. 1832.

Perennial herbs, aquatic or mesic. Aerial stems with sessile glands, pilose or nearly glabrous. Submerged leaves to 50 cm, multiparted; segments capillary. Aerial leaves opposite or whorled, oblanceolate or oblong, ca. 15 × 3 mm, base subamplexicaul, apex obtuse, margin subcrenate, glabrous, veins 3–5, parallel. Flowers sessile, in terminal spikes, or shortly pedicellate and solitary in leaf axils. Bracteoles absent. Calyx ca. 3 mm, with sessile glands, without raised veins in fruit. Corolla pale purple or pink, ca. 5 mm, glabrous. Capsules pale brown, subglobose, ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8156; HK sheet 4120, 20427.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

Limnophila rugosa (Roth) Merr. 大葉石龍尾
Interpr. Rumph. Herb. Amb. 466. 1917; FHN 3: 502. 1974 ; FOC 18: 27. 1998; FGD 4: 367. 2000.
Herpestis rugosa Roth, Nov. Pl. Sp. 290. 1821.
Limnophila roxburghii auct. non. G. Don: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 186. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 10–15 cm tall, with horizontal rhizomes. Stems 1 – few, ± fasciculate, erect or ascending, usually unbranched, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–2 cm, narrowly winged; leaf‑blade ovate, rhomboid‑elliptic, or elliptic, 3–9 × 1–5 cm, margin crenate, abaxially hispidulous along veins, adaxially glabrous or sparsely hispidulous, veins pinnate, ca. 10 on each side of midvein. Peduncles 0.2–3 cm. Bracts subspatulate‑oblong, with flattened glands, margin entire or apically undulate‑toothed and ciliate. Flowers sessile, 5–10 congested on apex of axillary short branches, usually appearing a head. Bracteoles absent. Calyx 6–8 mm, smooth, in fruiting time with 5 raised veins and flattened glands. Corolla purple‑red to blue, to 1.6 cm; styles slender, pubescent, with a membranous auricle on both sides. Capsules pale brown, ovoid, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Lantau Island. HK sheet 4122, 20440.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Limnophila sessiliflora (Vahl) Blume 石龍尾
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 749. 1826; FKH 186. 1912; FOC 18: 26. 1998; FGD 4: 365. 2000.
Hottonia sessiliflora Vahl, Symb. Bot. 2: 36. 1791.

Herbs aquatic or terrestrial. Submerged stems slender and long, glabrous or subglabrous. Aerial stems 6–40 cm, simple or sparsely branched, hairy or rarely subglabrous. Submerged leaves 0.5–3.5 cm, multiparted; segments flattened or capillary. Aerial leaves whorled, blade elliptic‑lanceolate, 5–18 × 3–4 mm, glabrous, densely glandular punctate, margin crenate to lobed; veins 1–3. Flowers sessile or rarely with a pedicel to 1.5 mm, solitary in axils of submerged and aerial leaves. Bracteoles absent or rarely present and to 1.5 mm. Calyx 4–6 mm, hairy, without raised veins in fruit; lobes ovate, 2–4 mm, apex narrowly acuminate. Corolla purple‑blue to reddish, 6–10 mm. Capsules compressed, subglobose.

Locality: Fanling. HK sheet 20433.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Liaoning, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places, margins of ponds. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

Limonium sinense (Girad) Kuntze 補血草
Rev. Gen. Pl. 2: 396. 1891; FHN 3: 439, fig. 841. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 30, pl. 5: 5. 1987; FGD 3: 314, fig. 204. 1995; FOC 15: 199. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 80, pl. 35, photo 50. 1998.
Statice sinensis Girad, Ann. Sci. Nat. 3, 2: 329. 1844; FHK 281. 1861; FKH 155. 1912.

Perennial herb, 15–50 cm tall, with thick tap root. Leaves in a basal rosette, obovate-oblanceolate or spatulate, 4–10 × 0.8–2 cm including petiole, apex obtuse or rounded, tapering from middle into the petiole, glabrous, margin entire. Spikes with 2–3 secund flowers, arranged in cymose panicle, terminal on scape; Bracteoles scarious, elliptic, 5–6 mm. Calyx funnel-form, 6–7 mm, with white hairs on ribs. Petals pale yellow, connate only at base, slightly longer than calyx. Stamens 5, inserted at the base of petals. Ovary obovate; style 5, filiform. Capsule cylindrical, ca. 3 mm long and 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shatin, Sai Kung, Chek Keng, Tai Po, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 757; C. Ford s.n. (HK sheet 2814); Y. S. Lau 557.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hebei, Liaoning; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy grassy lands near seashore. Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Lindera aggregata (Sims) Kosterm. 烏藥
Reinwardtia 9(1): 98. 1974; FHN 1: 299. 1964; FRPS 31: 434. 1982: FTW ed. 2, 2: 456, pl. 211. 1996.
Laurus aggregata Sims, Bot. Mag. 51: t. 2497. 1824.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, up to 5 m tall. Young shoots green, densely covered with golden silky hairs, glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.5 –1 cm, brown pubescent, glabrescent; leaf blade leathery or subleathery, ovate, elliptic to suborbicular, usually 2.7–5(–7) × 1.5 – 4 cm, base rounded, apex long acuminate to caudate, adaxially green and shining, abaxially glaucous, densely brown pubescent when young, glabrescent, triveined; midvein and the basal pair of lateral veins impressed, rarely raised on adaxial surface, but prominently raised on abaxial surface. Umbels 6 –7-flowered, sessile, usually 6 –8 clustered on axillary spurs, each umbel subtended by a bract. Perianth-lobes 6, subequal, usually yellow or yellowish green, white pubescent abaxially. Pedicels ca. 0.4 mm, pubescent. Fruit ovoid or subglobose, 4 –7 mm in diam.; fruiting pedicels 5 – 8 mm, apex slightly enlarged.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Lai Chi Wo. P. S. Choi 420; N. H. Li 28.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets on sunny slopes, or in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Nov.

Lindera aggregata (Sims) Kosterm. var. playfairii (Hemsl.) H. P. Tsui 小葉烏藥
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 69. 1978; FHN 1: 299. 1964; FRPS 31: 435. 1982: FTW ed. 2, 2: 458. 1996.
Litsea playfairii Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 384. 1891; FKH 225. 1912.

Differs from the type variety by the following characteristics: hairs on young shoots, leaves and flowers thiner, usually greyish white, or subglabrous; leaves smaller, narrowly ovate to lanceolate, 4 – 6 × 1.3 –2 cm, apex usually caudate; flowers smaller.

Locality: Kat O. HK sheet 24475, 24573.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Nov.

Lindera communis Hemsl. 香葉樹
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 387. 1891; FKH 226. 1912; FRPS 31: 408,pl. 101: 6. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 458. 1996.
Lindera glauca auct. non Blume: FKH 226. 1912 (quoad specimens from Hong Kong).

Evergreen shrub or small tree, (1–)3–4 m tall. Branchlets slender, sparsely or densely yellowish puberulous, glabrescent in age. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–8 mm long, yellowish puberuous or glabrescent; leaf blade leathery, usually lanceolate, ovate or elliptic, 4–9 × 1.5–3 cm, base broad cuneate or subrounded, apex acuminate, acute or sometimes caudate; adaxially glabrous, abaxially greyish green or yellowish, initially tawny pubescent, glabrescent in age, margin involute, pinnately veined; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, together with midveins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 5 – 8-flowered, solitary or paired in axils of leaves. Peduncles short and stout, 2–5 mm. Pedicels 2–2.5 mm, slightly golden puberulous. Perianth-lobes 6, ovate, subequal, ca. 3 × 1.5 mm, ± golden puberulous abaxially. Fruit ovoid, 7–8 mm in diam., glabrous, red when mature; fruiting pedicels 4–7 mm, yellowish brown puberulous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2804; N. H. Li 35.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India, the Ryukyus.
Ecology: Mixed forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Lindera megaphylla Hemsl. 黑殼楠
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 389. 1891; FKH 226. 1912; FRPS 31: 384. 1982.

Evergreen tree, 3 –15 m tall. Branches terete, stout, usually purplish black, minutely pubescent to glabrous, sparsely lenticellate. Leaves alternate or often crowded towards apex of branchlets; petioles 1.5–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, oblanceolate to obovateoblong, 10 –23 × 2– 6 cm, base attenuate to cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, green and shining adaxially, pale greenish to glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces, pinnately veined, lateral veins 15 –21 on each side of midvein. Umbels many-flowered, usually borne on axillary spurs. Peduncles of male umbels 1–1.5 cm, those of pistillate umbels 6 mm, all tawny puberulous. Perianth-lobes 6, ± tawny puberulous at base abaxially. Fruit ellipsoid to ovoid, ca. 1.8 × ca. 1.3 cm, glabrous, purplish black at maturity; fruiting pedicels ca. 1.5 cm long, thickened upwards.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai. HK sheet 4953, 24577.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and thickets on slopes or in valleys. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Lindera metcalfiana C. K. Allen 滇粵山胡椒
J. Arnold Arbor. 22: 3. 1941; FRPS 31: 401, pl. 104: 1– 4. 1982.
Lindera meissneri auct. non King: Merr. et Chun, Sunyatsenia 2: 1935.

Shrub or small tree, 3–12 m tall. Branchlets slender, brown to greyish brown, initially ± yellowish puberulous. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–8 mm long, yellowish brown pubescent; leaf blade leathery, elliptic or oblong, 5–13 × 2–4.5 cm, base broadly cunneate, apex acuminate or caudate, usually falcate, dark green to yellowish green adaxially, glaucous abaxially, tawny puberulous on veins of both surfaces, pinnately veined; lateral veins 6–10 on each side of midvein, turning purplish brown when dry, reticulation of veins prominent abaxially. Umbels 1–2(–3) on axillary spurs, tawny pubescent, inserted on axillary spurs. Male umbels 6–8-flowered; peduncles slender, 1–1.6 cm; pedicels 2–3 mm. Female umbels 4 –8-flowered; peduncles 0.6 –0.8 cm; pedicels 2–2.5 mm. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., purplish black at maturity; fruiting pedicels ca. 6 mm, stout, slightly brownish puberulous.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 1744.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest on hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.

Lindera nacusua (D. Don) Merr. 絨毛山胡椒
Lingnan Sci. J. 15: 419. 1936; FHN 1: 300. 1964; FRPS 31: 406. 1982.
Laurus nacusua D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 64. 1825.
Daphnidium bifarium auct. non Nees, in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 63. 1831; FHK 294. 1861.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 2–10 m tall. Branchlets brown, densely tawny villose when young, glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles stout, 5–7(–10) mm, densely tawny pubescent; leaf blade leathery, broadly ovate, elliptic or oblong-ovate, 6 –11 × 3.5–6 cm, base cuneate to attenuate, sometimes rotunded, asymmetrical, apex usually acute, adaxially glabrous, sometimes puberulous on the midvein, abaxially densely tawny villose, pinninerved; lateral veins 5–10 on each side of midvein, together with midvein impressed adaxially, prominently raised abaxially. Male umbels 8–9-flowered, female umbels (2–)3–6-flowered, solitary or 2–4 clustered in axils of leaves; peduncules short, 2–3 mm. Pedicels 3–5.5 mm long, densely yellow villose. Perianth-lobes 6, ovate to broadly ovate, 2–3.5 mm. Fruit subglobose, ca. 6 mm in diam., red at maturity; fruiting pedicels stout, 5–7 mm, thickened upwards, slightly yellowish brown puberulous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. H. C. Tang 727; Y. S. Lau 74.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests in valley or on hillslopes. Flowering: May– Jun.; fruiting: in Jul.– Oct.

Lindernia anagallis (Burm. f.) Pennell 長蒴母草（長果母草）
J. Arnold Arbor. 24(3): 252. 1943; FHN 3: 506. 1974; FOC 18: 35. 1998; FGD 4: 389. 2000.
Ruellia anagallis Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 135. 1768.
Lindernia cordifolia (Colsm.) Merr., Enum. Philipp. Fl. Pl. 3: 437. 1923; FGZ 598. 1956.
Gratiola cordifolia Colsm., Prodr. Desc. Grat. 15. 1793.
Vandellia pedunculata Benth., Scroph. Ind. 37. 1835, & DC., Prodr. 10: 416. 1846; FKH 188. 1912.

Annual herbs, 10–40 cm. Stems creeping, striate, glabrous, rooting from nodes. Leaves shortly petiolate to subsessile; leaf blade triangular‑ovate, ovate, or oblong, 0.4–2 × 0.7–1.2 cm, base truncate to subcordate, apex rounded to acute, margin shallowly crenate. Flowers axillary, solitary. Pedicels 6–10 mm, to 2 cm in fruit. Calyx ca. 5 mm, basally connate; lobes lanceolate. Corolla white or light purple, 0.8–1.2 cm; lower lip slightly longer than upper lip, spreading flat, 3‑lobed, lobes subequal; upper lip ovate, 2‑lobed, filaments of anterior stamens basally with a clavate appendage, stigma 2‑lobed. Capsules linear‑ovoid, ca. 2 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds ovoid, tuberculate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Wai, Chuen Lung, Tai Po, Fanling, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 2473; Y. S. Lau 2260; HK sheet 4130.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; S & SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides, wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lindernia antipoda (L.) Alston 泥花草
Handb. Fl. Ceyl. 6 (Suppl.): 214. 1931; FHN 3: 508. 1974; FOC 18: 36. 1998; FGD 4: 389. 2000.
Ruellia antipoda L., Sp. Pl. 635. 1753.
Bonnaya veronicifolia (Retz.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 41. 1824; FHK 252. 1861; FKH 189. 1912.

Annual herbs, to 30 cm tall. Stems suberect or prostrate basally, many‑branched, channeled. Petiole short and wide; leaf blade oblong, oblong‑lanceolate, or linear‑lanceolate, 0.8–4 × 0.6–2 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acute to rounded, margin obscurely to sharply serrate or subentire. Racemes terminal, to 15 cm, 2– 20‑flowered. Pedicels to 1.5 cm, ascending, spreading, to deflexed in fruit. Calyx lobed to base; lobes lanceolate, hispidulous along midvein and edges. Corolla purple, purplish white, or white, to 1 cm; tube to 7 mm; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal; upper lip 2‑lobed. Fertile stamens 2, posterior; filaments unappendaged. Reduced stamens 2, anterior; filaments slightly curved, glandular, stigma 2‑lamellate. Capsules cylindric, 2 times or more as long as persistent calyx. Seeds brown, irregularly triangular‑ovoid; testa reticulate.

Locality: Happy Valley, Shing Mun, Sha Tin, Fanling, Tai Lam Chung, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2529, 2548; Y. W. Lam 1216.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides, wet places or farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Spring to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lindernia ciliata (Colsm.) Pennell 刺齒泥花草
Brittonia 2: 182. 1936; FHN 3: 508. 1974; FOC 18: 36. 1998; FGD 4: 390. 2000.
Gratiola ciliata Colsm., Prodr. Desc. Grat. 14. 1793.
Bonnaya brachiata Link & Otto, Icon. Pl. Select. 25, pl. 11. 1820; FKH 189. 1912.
Ilysanthes serrata (Roxb.) Urban, Ber. Deutsch. Bot. Ges. 2: 436. 1884; FGZ 602. 1956.
Gratiola serrata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey & Wall. 1: 139. 1820.

Annual herbs, to 20 cm tall. Stems diffuse, many‑branched. Branches decumbent. Leaves sessile or short petiolate; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate‑oblong, 0.7–4.5 × 0.3–1.2 cm, glabrous, base amplexicaul, apex acute to obtuse, margin densely aristate‑serrate. Racemes terminal. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 1/2 as long as pedicels. Calyx ca. 5 mm, lobed to base; lobes narrowly lanceolate, with a spine‑like tip. Corolla light purple or white, ca. 7 mm; tube to 4.5 mm; lower lip almost as long as upper lip, often unequally 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger than other lobes; upper lip ovate. Fertile stamens 2, posterior; sterile stamens 2, anterior, forming prominent plaits on base of lower lip. Capsules cylindric, ca. 3 times as long as persistent calyx, apex mucronate. Seeds irregularly triangular.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9599; Y. W. Lam 1076; HK sheet 4135.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lindernia crustacea (L.) F. Muell. 母草
Syst. Census Austral. Pl. 1: 97. 1882; FHN 3: 507. 1974; FOC 18: 32. 1998; FGD 4: 388. 2000.
Capraria crustacea L., Mant. Pl. 1: 87. 1767.
Vandellia crustacea (L.) Benth., Scroph. Ind. 35. 1835; FHK 251. 1861; FKH 188. 1912.

Annual herbs, 10–20 cm tall, many‑branched. Branches widely spreading, subquadrangular, deeply sulcate, glabrous. Petioles 1–8 mm; leaf blade triangular‑ovate to broadly ovate, 1–2 × 0.5–1.1 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex obtuse to subacute, margin shallowly crenate to serrate, abaxially pilose along veins to subglabrous, adaxially subglabrous. Flowers axillary and solitary. Pedicels slender, 0.5–2.2 cm, subglabrous. Calyx 3–5 mm, 5‑toothed, often splitting into 5 lobes after anthesis, outside sparsely pubescent. Corolla purple, 5–8 mm; tube slightly longer than calyx; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger and slightly longer than upper lip; upper lip ovate, sometimes shallowly 2‑lobed. Stamens didynamous, styles fugacious. Capsules broadly ellipsoidal, almost as long as persistent calyx. Seeds pale yellow‑brown, subglobose, scrobiculate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kwai Chung, Shing Mun, Tsiu Hang, Ta Kwu Ling, Peng Chau, Lantau Island, Ping Chau. Y. W. Lam 840, 1075, 2541.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang, Henan; a common weed widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Moist areas, rice fields, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lindernia hyssopioides (L.) Haines 尖果母草
Bot. Bilhar Orissa 4: 666. 1922; FHN 3: 509. 1974; FOC 18: 37. 1998; FGD 4: 387. 2000.
Gratiola hyssopioides L., Mant. Pl. 174. 1771.
Bonnaya hyssopoides (L.) Benth., Scroph. Ind. 34. 1835.
Ilysanthes hyssopoides (L.) Benth., Prodr. 10: 419. 1846; FHK 252. 1861; FKH 188. 1912.

Herbs, to 30 cm tall. Stems erect or somewhat ascending, simple, striate. Leaves sessile, subamplexicaul, narrowly ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–15 × ca. 4 mm, margin entire or with 2 or 3 pairs of inconspicuous small teeth, veins 3, parallel. Flowers in axils of upper leaves, solitary. Pedicels 0.5–3 cm, slender, ascending in flower, spreading to reflexed after flowering. Calyx ca. 3 mm, lobed to base; lobes lanceolate. Corolla red, purple, or white, with 2 convex lines at throat, 0.9–1.1 cm; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal; upper lip deeply 2‑lobed, lobes narrowly triangular‑ovate. Fertile stamens 2, posterior; staminodes 2, anterior; filaments short, divided, styles apex 2‑lamellate. Capsules linear‑ovoid, ca. 6 mm, 2 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds yellow‑brown, oblong, obscurely ribbed.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 2750; HK sheet 4134.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; Vietnam, India to Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Lindernia micrantha D. Don 狹葉母草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 85. 1825; FOC 18: 35. 1998.
Lindernia angustifolia (Benth.) Wettst., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(3b): 79. 1891; FHN 3: 507. 1974; FRPS 67(2): 141. 1979; FGD 4: 388. 2000; Check List HK Plants 246. 2002; 85. 2004.
Vandellia angustifolia Benth., Scroph. Ind. 37. 1835; FKH 188. 1912.

Annual herbs, to 40 cm tall. Stems usually erect, branches ascending, glabrous. Leaves sessile, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1–4 cm × 2–8 mm, margin entire or somewhat irregularly serrate, glabrous. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels to 3.5 cm in fruit. Calyx to 4 mm in fruit, lobed to base; lobes lanceolate. Corolla purple, blue purple, or white, ca. 6.5 mm, lower lip slightly longer than upper lip, spreading flat, 3‑lobed; upper lip 2‑lobed. Filaments of anterior stamens with a linear appendage; posterior anthers with connective of lower locule produced into a long tail. Capsules linear, to 1.4 cm, more than 3 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds brownish, oblong.

Locality: Shing Mun, Plover Cove, Tung Chung. L. T. Lo 305; Y. W. Lam 1534, 1580.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Korea, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia, Myanmar, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Farmlands, wet places along streams. Flowering: May – Oct.; fruiting: Jul. – Nov.

Lindernia oblonga (Benth.) Merr. & Chun 棱萼母草
Sunyatsenia 5: 180. 1940; FHN 3: 507. 1974; FOC 18: 32. 1998; FGD 4: 388. 2000.
Vandellia oblonga Benth., Scroph. Ind. 35. 1835; FHK 251. 1861; Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. ser. 4, 15: 227. 1861.
Torenia oblonga Hance ex Maxim., Mel. Biol. 9: 411. 1875; FKH 187. 1912.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect or sometimes procumbent and ascending, subquadrangular, median internodes to 6 cm. Leaves short petiolate below, sessile and subamplexicaul above; leaf blade rhomboid‑ovate to rhomboid‑lanceolate, 5 – 20 × 3 – 8 mm, base broadly cuneate, apex subacute to rounded, margin often with few irregular undulate sinuses or small teeth, or entire. Racemes lax, usually less then 10‑flowered; bracts lanceolate. Pedicels slender, 0.7 – 2.5 cm. Calyx narrowly campanulate, lobed to 1/4 length; lobes triangular‑ovate, apex acute and recurved, midvein evident. Corolla purple to purple‑blue, to 1.3 cm or more; tube ca 7 mm; lower lip 3‑lobed; upper lip 2‑lobed, stigma broadly 2‑lamellate. Capsules ellipsoidal, shorter than persistent calyx. Seeds numerous.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Long Sai Wan, Long Ke, Beaufort Island, Lamma Island. S. P. Lau 157; Y. W. Lam 782, 1031.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia.
Ecology: Sandy soil. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Lindernia procumbens (Krock.) Borbás 陌上菜
Békés Vámegye 80. 1881; FOC 18: 32. 2002.
Anagalloides procumbens Krock., Fl. Siles. 2(1): 398, pl. 26. 1790.
Lindernia procumbens (Krock.) Philcok, Taxon 14: 30. 1965; FGD 4: 389. 2000; Check List HK Plants 247. 2002; 85. 2004.

Herbs erect, caespitose, 5–20 cm tall, basally many‑branched. Leaves sessile; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, somewhat rhomboid, 1–2.5 × 0.6–1.2 cm, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or weakly obtusely toothed. Flower axillary, solitary. Pedicels slender, 1.2–2 cm, longer than subtending leaf. Calyx lobed almost to base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, outside sparsely pubescent. Corolla pink to purple, 5–7 mm, tube ca. 3.5 mm; lower lip ca. 3 mm, 3‑lobed, middle lobe rounded and longer than other lobes, upper lip ca. 1 mm, 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, all fertile; filaments of anterior stamens with a small glandular appendage; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsules globose to ovoid‑globose, as long as or slightly longer than persistent calyx. Seeds oblong, testa reticulate.

Locality: Chuen Lung, Pak Nai, Sheung Shui, Ta Kwu Ling, Peng Chau. L. T. Lo 258; Y. W. Lam 390, 998.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Asia, S Europe.
Ecology: Wet places along streams. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Lindernia pusilla (Willd.) Bold. 細莖母草
Zakfl. Java 165. 1916; FHN 3: 505. 1974; FOC 18: 33. 1998; FGD 4: 386. 2000.
Gratiola pusilla Willd., Sp. Pl. 1: 105. 1797.
Vandellia scabra Benth., Scroph. Ind. 36. 1835; FHK 251. 1861; FKH 188. 1912; Philcox, Kew Bull. 22: 41. 1968.

Annual herbs, 6–30 cm tall, sometimes long stoloniferous. Stems suberect, subglabrous or hairy, densely coarsely hairy on nodes. Leaves shortly petiolate below, sessile above; leaf blade ovate, cordate, or occasionally orbicular, to 1.2 cm, sparsely covered with appressed coarse hairs, base cuneate to subcordate, margin subcrenate or entire. Inflorescences terminal, subumbellate‑racemose, 3–5‑flowered. Pedicels slender, 0.8–1.5 cm. Calyx deeply lobed; lobes lanceolate, coarsely hairy outside. Corolla purple, ca. 9 mm; lower lip ca. 5.5 mm, much longer than upper lip; upper lip broadly ovate, emarginate; filaments of anterior stamens slender, base geniculate, stigma 2‑lamellate. Capsules ovoid‑globose, almost as long as persistent calyx. Seeds oblong, tuberculate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sha Tin, Shing Mun, Fung Yuen, Mui Tsz Lam, Ho Chung, Tai O. Y. S. Lau 2749; Y. W. Lam 519, 875.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India to Malaysia, Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Lindernia ruellioides (Colsm.) Pennell 旱田草
Brittonia 2: 182. 1936; FHN 3: 509. 1974; FOC 18: 36. 1998; FGD 4: 390. 2000.
Gratiola ruellioides Colsm., Prodr. Desc. Grat. 12. 1793.

Annual herbs, 10–15 cm tall; stolons to 30 cm. Stems usually branched, subglabrous, rooting from nodes. Petioles 0.3–2 cm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic, ovate‑oblong or orbicular, 1–4 × 0.6–2 cm, scabrous, pubescent to subglabrous, base subamplexicaul or broadly cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin above base densely and regularly acute‑serrate. Racemes terminal, 2–10‑flowered; bracts lanceolate‑linear. Pedicels short, distally gradually thicker, glabrous. Calyx ca. 6 mm, to 10 mm in fruit, base connate; lobes linear‑lanceolate, glabrous. Corolla purple‑red, 1–1.4 cm; tube 7–9 mm; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal or middle lobe slightly larger than other lobes; upper lip 2‑lobed. Fertile stamens 2, posterior, without appendages; sterile stamens 2, anterior; stigma flattened. Capsules conical, ca. 2 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds brown, ellipsoidal.

Locality: Fung Yuen, Ng Tung Chai, Plover Cove. Y. S. Lau 2513; Y. W. Lam 887; HK sheet 40248.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India to Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Liparis bootanensis Griff. 鐮翅羊耳蒜
Not. Pl. Asiat. 3: 278. 1851; FRPS 18: 80, pl. 13: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 938. 2000; FGD 7: 450. 2006; FOC 25: 221. 2009.
Liparis plicata Franch. & Sav., Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 509. 1879; FKH 261. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977.

Epiphytic small herb, glabrous throughout; pseudobulbs crowded, compressed, bearing 4 cataphylls and 1 leaf. Leaf 1 to each pseudobulb, yellowish green to green, petiolate; petioles folded, articulate; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4.5–15 × 1.5–2.5 cm, slightly plicate, apex acute. Flowers 5–9, non-resupinate, in varying shades of green, turning to orange with age; the odd sepal linear-oblong, slightly recurved, 6–7 × 2 mm, obtuse at apex; lateral ones curving backward, lanceolate, 6 × 2 mm, obtuse; petals linear-filiform, 6 × 1 mm, obtuse; lip olive-green, tongue-like, curved downwards, apex truncate, slightly notched, with 2 distinct calli at the base, dark green; column snow-white, cylindrical, slightly compressed, base enlarged, apex arcuate, with a triangular wing on each side; anther cap ovoid, greenish, notched at the apex; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary strongly ridged and sulcate.

Locality: Violet Hill, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Pak Tai To Yan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12747, 12763 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 487.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Rocks in shady ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

Liparis ferruginea Lindl. 鏽色羊耳蒜
Gard. Chron. 1848: 55. 1848; FRPS 18: 75, pl. 11: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 449. 2006; FOC 25: 220. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs narrowly ovoid, very small. Leaves 3–6, linear to lanceolate, (13–)20–33 × 0.8–1.2 cm, membranous or herbaceous, base slightly contracted and decurrent into amplexicaul sheath, not articulate, apex acute or shortly acuminate. Racemes several to 10-flowered; rachis 8 – 20 cm; pedicel 8–10 mm at fruiting time; floral bracts lanceolate, (2–)4–6 mm. Flowers yellow, lip pale yellowish brown slightly tinged with pale purple. Dorsal sepal linear, 6–7 × ca. 1.5 mm, 3-veined, margin revolute, apex obtuse; lateral sepals reflexed, obliquely ovate-oblong, ca. 6 × 2.5 mm, 5-veined. Petals nearly linear or narrowly oblanceolate-linear, ca. 6 × 1 mm, 1-veined, margin revolute; lip ± recurved, obovate-oblong, 4–5 × ca. 3 mm, with a pair of basal auricles backward spreading and 2 calli near base, apex broadly truncate, often emarginate and sinus apiculate. Column 3–4 mm, upper part with narrow wings on both sides. Capsule oblong or obovoid-oblong, ca. 1.5 cm × 6 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung. P. S. Choi 504; Y. W. Lam 700.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, swamps. Flowering: Jul.

Liparis gigantea C. L. Tso 紫花羊耳蒜
Sunyatsenia 1: 136. 1933; FOC 25: 219. 2009.
Liparis macrantha Rolfe, Ann. Bot. 9: 156. 1895, non Hook. f. 1854; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977.
Liparis nigra auct. non Seidenf.: FRPS 18: 73, pl. 10: 4. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 948. 2000; FGD 7: 449. 2006; Check List HK Plants 378. 2002; 132. 2004.

Terrestrial herb, 12–25 cm tall at flowering time; pseudobulbs cylindrical; the third year's plant bearing 2 leaves. Leaves petiolate; petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 5–15 × 2.5–6.5 cm, apex acuminate. Flowers dark-purple, almost black, in a terminal raceme on scapes of 10–20 cm; pedicels 1–1.5 cm; odd sepal linear, 2 × 0.2–0.25 cm, curved backward, apex obtuse; lateral sepals 1.7 × 0.4 cm, falcate, pointing forwards, recurved, parallel to the lip; petals linear, 1.5–2 × 0.1 cm, pointing backward, obtuse; lip 1.2–2.2 cm, bent at middle, basal portion narrowed, apical portion 1–1.1 × 1.2–1.3 cm, truncate, sharply toothed; column 1 cm, light green, arcuate turning reddish purple at fading; anther subglobose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary 4–6 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 13643 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Rocks or shade places in forests. Flowering: Feb.–May.

Liparis nervosa (Thunb. ex A. Murray) Lindl. 見血青（脈羊耳蒜）
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 26. 1830; FHK 352. 1861; FKH 261. 1912; FRPS 18: 71, pl. 10: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 947. 2000; FGD 7: 448, fig. 226. 2006; FOC 25: 218. 2009.
Ophrys nervosa Thunb. ex A. Murray, Linn. Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 814. 1784.

Caespitose terrestrial herb, 15–25 cm tall at flowering time; pseudobulbs elongate-conical, 5–10 cm or longer, 0.8–1.3 cm thick. Leaves petiolate; petioles 1–4 cm, that of the lowest leaf the longest; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 2–19 × 1.5–8.5 cm, base unequal, one side subcordate, the other cuneate, apex acuminate. Flowers dull purplish green, very variable, sepals green or rosepurple or purple tinged green, even greenish yellow; odd sepal oblong or ovate-falcate, pointing upward, 6–12 mm; lateral 2 ovate-falcate, 4.5–9 × 2–4 mm; petals rose-purple or greenish yellow, linear, 5–10 mm; lip purple and light-green at base, tonguelike, curving downward; column fleshy, winged at apical end, green; anther purple; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary striate-sulcate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 12885A, 13659 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 427.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Rocks along streams in shade of forests. Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore)

Liparis odorata (Willd.) Lindl. 香花羊耳蒜
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 26. 1830; FHK 352. 1861; FKH 261. 1912; FFJ 6: 630. 1995; FRPS 18: 69, pl. 11: 6–8. 1999; FGD 7: 449. 2006; FOC 25: 218. 2009.
Malaxis odorata Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 91. 1805.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs subglobose, 1–2 cm long and 1–1.5 cm in diam., articulate, covered with membranous white sheaths. Leaves 2 or 3, ovate-oblong or linear-lanceolate, membranous, 6–15 × 2–5 cm, base attenuating gradually into a sheath-like petiole, apex acuminate; petiole non-articulate, 2–10. Flowers greenish yellow; odd sepal oblanceolate, strongly recurved along the margin, appearing linear, 7–10 × 1–1.5 mm, pointing backward, apex obtuse and thickened; lateral sepals ovate-oblong, reflexed, curved downwards, 5–7 × 3 mm, apex acute; petals filiform, 4–7 × 0.5 mm, wide spread and curved backward; lip green or tinged rose-pink, notched, with 2 triangular calli near the base, apex subtruncate; column arcuate, winged; anther greenish, apex mucronate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary strongly ridged, the ridges winged and spiral.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. T. Dunn 192; Y. S. Lau 2743.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; India, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Among short grasses in full sun at high elevations on exposed mountain tops. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.

Liparis ruybarrettoi S. Y. Hu & Barratto 包瑞羊耳蒜
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 22. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977; FRPS 18: 80. 1999; FOC 25: 211. 2009, pro syn. sub L. bootanensis Griff.

Epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs compressed-ovoid, the oldest the smallest, 5–6 close together forming an irregular curved line, with each succeeding pseudobulb emerging from the base of the previous one. Leaf 1 to each pseudobulb, linear-lanceolate, 11–17 × 1.4–2.5 cm, the basal half slightly plicate at anthesis, becoming plane and slightly folded near the base, apex acuminate and acute; midrib impressed above, elevated beneath, the 1 or 2 lateral parallel veins on each side rather obscure. Flowers non-resupinate, in various shades of green; sepals green, the odd one linear, farthest away from the rachis, 7 × 1 mm, apex slightly curved outwards; lateral sepals ovate-lanceolate, oriented below the lip and strongly curved outwards, 6 × 1.5–2 mm wide at middle; petals filiform, yellowish green, 7 × 0.25 mm, slightly curved forward; lip olive-green, tongue-like, curved downwards, apex truncate with a small obtuse middle projection, base furnished with 1 prominent shiny dark green glandular tubercle; column light yellow tinged green, curved forward; anther cap-like, ovate-lanceolate, acute; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary subtriangular-cylindrical, striate-sulcate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 11444A, 12569 (isotype), 12570 (holotype) (CUHK).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Cliffs in shade and mossy rocks, alt. 500 m. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 12569, K, holotype; A, CUHK, US, isotype) was collected from Tai Mo Shan in 1972.

Liparis stricklandiana Rchb. f. 扇唇羊耳蒜
Gard. Chron. n. s. 13: 232. 1880; FRPS 18: 95, pl. 14: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 453. 2006; FOC 25: 225. 2009.
Liparis chloroxantha Hance, J. Bot. 21: 231. 1883; FKH 261. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 77, fig. 40. 1977.

Epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs oblique-ovoid to oblong-ovoid, slightly compressed, 2–4 cm long and 0.5–1.5 cm in diam., bearing 2 leaves at apex. Leaves petiolate; petioles articulate, 4–15 cm; leaf blades chartaceous, oblanceolate or linearoblanceolate, 15–45 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate. Flowers non-resupinate, greenish yellow; sepals narrowly obovate, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm, lateral ones slightly wider; petals filiform, 5 × 1 mm; lip fan-shaped, 5 × 6 mm, apex truncate, mucronate, margin unevenly denticulate, base attenuate with an oblate callus; column slender, arcuate, slightly swollen at base; anther terminal, suborbicular; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, faveolate.

Locality: Mount Parker, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Ng Tung Chai. S. Y. Hu 9484, 12757 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1760.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Bhutan, Sikkim, India.
Ecology: Rocks along streams in shade. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

Liparis viridiflora (Blume) Lindl. 長莖羊耳蒜
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 31. 1830; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 27(3–4). 428. 1974; FRPS 18: 90, pl. 16: 1–2. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 950. 2000; FGD 7: 452. 2006; FOC 25: 224. 2009.
Malaxis viridiflora Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 392. 1825.
Liparis longipes (Lindl.) Rchb. f., Bonplondia 3: 250. 1855; FHK 352. 1861; FKH 261. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977.

Caespitose herb, 10–25 cm tall; pseudobulbs 8–9 cm or longer, 0.4–1 cm in diam. Leaves 2, linear-lanceolate, 15–21 × 2–3 cm, apex acute. Flowers non-light green, many in a terminal raceme 7–12 cm; scapes 5–10 cm, odd sepals recurved backward, 3 × 0.7 mm; lateral sepals ovate-lanceolate, pointing forward, 3 × 1.5 mm; petals linear, turning backward, 3 mm; lip fleshy, light green, apical portion ovate, obtuse; column erect, 2 mm, cylindrical; anther green; pollinia 4; ovary cylindrical, 1.5 mm. Capsule obovoid, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Violet Hill, Tai Tam, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Peak. S. Y. Hu 10629, 11097 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1756.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Taiwan; S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Wet rocks and damp places in forests or ravines. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.

Lipocarpha chinensis (Osbeck) Kern 華湖瓜草
Blumea, Suppl. 4: 167. 1958; FRPS 11: 192. 1961; FHN 4: 373. 1977; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 613. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 287. 2000; FYN 15: 662. 2003; FGD 8: 348. 2007; FOC 23: 250. 2010.
Scirpus chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 220. 1757.
Scirpus senegalensis Lam., Tabl. Encycl. 1: 140. 1791.
Lipocarpha senegalensis (Lam.) T. Durand & H. Durand, Syll. Fl. Congol. 619. 1909; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 613. 1988.
Lipocarpha argentea R. Br., Narr. Exped. Zaire 459. 1818, nom. illeg.; FHK 388. 1861; FKH 301. 1912.

Annual or perennial. Rhizome absent. Clums tufted, 15–70 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, flat or compressed triquetrous, longitudinally sulcate, sparsely puberulent. Leaves basal; blade up to 40 cm × 2–4 mm, ± flat, apex acuminate; sheath 1–15 cm, reddish brown or reddish purple, glabrous. Involucral bract 2–3(–5), the longest up to 20 cm, basal ones bladeless, apical ones leaved. Inflorescence terminal clustered spikes. Spikes (1–)3–10, oblong or ovoid-ellipsoidal, 5–8 × 4–5 mm. Spikelet bracts spathulate to obovate or oblong, 1.5–2.7 × 0.4–1.3 mm, triangular-acute, apical part 1 2 mm long, membranous, white to pale yellowish or greenish brown, midvein green. Spikelets with two glumes and 1 bisexual flower; glumes elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse or acute. Stamens 2; anthers narrowly oblong, ca. 1 mm long. Style slender; stigmas 3, puberulent. Achenes oblong or oblong-ovoid, trigonous, 1–1.2 × 0.3–0.5 mm, pale yellowish brown.

Locality: Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Yung Shue O, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 2155; J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 258; HK sheet 42192.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Jiangxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Lipocarpha microcephala (R. Br.) Kunth 湖瓜草
Enum. Pl. 2: 268. 1837; FHK 388. 1861; FKH 301. 1912; FHN 4: 273. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 287. 2000; FYN 15: 664. 2003; FGD 8: 348. 2007; FOC 23: 250. 2010.
Hypaelyptum microcephalum R. Br., Prodr. 220. 1810.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Clums densely tufted, 5–40 cm tall, 0.51 mm thick. Leaves basal; blade up to 10 cm × 1–2 mm, flattish or weakly inrolled; sheath up to 3 cm, pale to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 2–3, the longest 5–10 cm. Inflorescence terminal. Spikes (1–)2–4(–5), ellipsoidal to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 3–8 × 2–3 mm. Spikelet bracts obovate-oblong, 1–1.5 × 0.2–0.4 mm, acuminate, the apical part recurved, 0.5–0.8 mm, scaberulous at tip, yellowish to brown, midvein green. Spikelets with 2 glumes and 1 bisexual flower. Glumes linear-oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 1–1.3 × 0.2 mm, white, 5-veined, apex obtuse or acute. Stamens 2; anthers linearoblong, 2–3 mm. Style slender, exserted from subtending glumes; stigmas 3, puberulent. Achenes linear-oblong, often slightly curved, trigonous, 0.9–1 × 0.2–0.3 mm, yellowish brown, densely puncticulate, shiny, apex acuminate.

Locality: Fanling, Yung Shue O. S. P. Lau 23; HK sheet 13660, 42164.
Distribution: Widely spread over NE, E, S & SW China; Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Liquidambar formosana Hance 楓香
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 5, 5: 215. 1886; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 55. 1979; FGD 1: 156. 1987.
Liquidambar formosana var. monticola Rehd. & E. H. Wils., Pl. Wils. 1: 422. 1913; FRPS 35(2): 55. 1979; FGD 1: 153. 1987.

Tree to 30 m tall; bark grey-brown; branchlets pubescent or glabrous, slightly lenticellate. Buds ovoid, glossy. Stipules linear, red, free or adnate to petiole, 1–1.4 cm, caducous; petioles to 12 cm, pubescent; leaf blade broadly ovate, palmately 3-lobed and 3-veined, central lobe longer, base rounded, apex caudateacuminate, margin glandular serrate, usually grey-white, pubescent or glabrous abaxially, veins prominent on both surfaces. Male inflorescence a short spike, several arranged in a raceme. Female inflorescence capitate, 20–40-flowered; peduncle 3–6 cm. Male flowers: stamens many. Female flowers: staminode-teeth 4 –7, needlelike, 4 – 8 mm; ovary hairy, styles 0.6 –1 mm. Infructescence globose, 3 – 4 cm wide. Capsules with persistent staminodes and styles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely planted. H. C. Tang 1473; Y. S. Lau 2487.
Distribution: S, SW, E & C China; S Korea, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Materials (timber, resin), ornamental, medicinal.

Magnolia championii Benth. 香港木蘭

FHK 8. 1861; FRPS 30(1): 117, pl. 26: 7–13. 1996; FGD 1: 7, fig. 6. 1987.

Magnolia pumila Andr. var. championii Finet et Gagnep., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 52(4): 36. 1906.

Magnolia liliflora Baill. var. championii Pampan., Bull. Soc. Tosc. Ort. Ser. 4, 1: 136. 1916.

Magnolia paenetalauma Dandy, J. Bot. 68(7): 206–207. 1930; FRPS 30(1): 117. 1996.

Magnolia pumila auct. non Andr.: FKH 28. 1912.

Magnolia tenuicarpella H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni. 1: 56. 1961.


Evergreen shrub or small tree; twigs green and hairy when young; Stipular scars nearly reached apex of petioles. Petioles 0.5–15 cm. Leaves elliptic, narrowly oblong-elliptic or narrowly obovate-elliptic, 7–14(–20) × 2– 4.5(–6.5) cm, leathery, base slightly decurrent, cuneate or narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate or cuspidate, rarely acute, adaxially deep green and glossy, abaxially pale green, ± hairy on midvein; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein. Flowers globose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., very fragrant; peduncles 1–1.5 cm, densely covered with pale yellow silky hairs, with 3–4 spathose-bract scars ca. 1 cm below tepals; tepals 9, outer 3 pale green, oblong-elliptic, 3.5–4 × 2 cm, the inner 6 in two whorls, white, obovate, fleshy, 2–2.5 × 1.5 cm, apex sometimes emarginate; stamens 7–9 mm, anthers 6–7 mm, dehiscing introrsely, connectives exserted and forming a triangular mucro; gynoecium narrowly obovate, 1–1.4 cm, white villose; carpels 8–9 mm, furrows reached to the base of style abaxially, ovules 2, parallel. Aggregate fruit 3–4 cm; follicles ca. 1 cm, each with a beak of 2 mm; seeds narrowly ellipsoid or irregular ovoid, 8–12 × 4–6 mm.


Localities: Tai Tam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1838; L. T. Lo 638.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.

Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: May – Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Uses: Ornamental.

Notes: The type specimen (Champion 37, holotype, K) was collected between 1847 and 1850 from Hong Kong Island.
records.uses:
Ornamental.

Notes: The type specimen (Champion 37, holotype, K) was collected between 1847 and 1850 from Hong Kong Island.

Magnolia coco (Lour.) DC. 夜香木蘭（夜合花）
Syst. 1: 459. 1818; FHN 1: 224. 1964; FGD 1: 6. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 113, pl. 26: 1– 6. 1996.
Liriodendron coco Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 347. 1790.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 2–4 m, glabrous; bark grey, twigs green, smooth, slightly ridged and glossy. Stipular scars reached apex of petioles; petioles 5–10 mm. Leaves elliptic, narrowly elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 7–14(–28) × 2–4.5(–9) cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex long-acuminate, adaxially deep green and glossy, slightly wavy wrinked, margin slightly revolute; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein, reticulations of veins sparse. Peduncles pendulous, with 3–4 bract-scars. Flowers globose, 3–4 cm in diam.; tepals 9, fleshy, obovate, adaxially concave, the outer 3 greenish, 5-veined, ca. 2 cm, the inner 6 in two whorls, purely white, 3–4 × 4 cm; stamens 4–6 mm, filaments white, ca. 2 mm, anthers ca. 3 mm, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium green, ovoid, 1.5–2 cm; carpels ca. 10, narrowly ovoid, 5–6 mm, abaxially with 1 furrow downward to the base of style, stigma short.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1907; HK sheet 32247.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Liriope spicata (Thunb.) Lour. 山麥冬（麥門冬）
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 201. 1790; FKH 273. 1912; FRPS 15: 128, pl. 41: 1–2. 1978; FOC 24: 251. 2000; FGD 6: 359. 2005.
Ophiopogon spicatus (Thunb.) Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 7: pl. 593. 1821; FHK 371. 1861.
Convallaria spicata Thunb., Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 334. 1784.

Perennial herb, to 50 cm tall, with short rhizomes and creeping stolons; roots usually with fusiform, fleshy tuberous part near tip. Leaves radical, tufted, narrowly linear, grass-like, 20–60 cm × 4–6 mm, distinctly 5-veined, margin serrulate. Scape erect, about the length of leaves or longer. Flowers in clusters of (2–)3–5 in the axil of a scarious bract and surrounded by several smaller bracts, forming a rather dense narrow raceme of 6–18 cm; pedicels ca. 4 mm, articulate above middle or near apex. Perianth purplish or bluish; segments 6, in 2 series, suboblong, 4–5 × 2–2.5 mm. Stamens 6; filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers narrowly oblong, about the length of filaments. Ovary superior; style ca. 2 mm; stigma as wide as style. Seeds subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 82; HK sheet 30224.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, moist places in ravines. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Litchi chinensis Sonn. 荔枝
Voy. Ind. Orient. 3: 255, pl. 129. 1782; FRPS 47(1): 32, pl. 10. 1985; FFJ 3: 318, fig. 216. 1987; FGD 1: 246, fig. 272. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 3: 606. 1993.
Dimocarpus litchi Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 223. 1790.
Nephelium litchi Cambess., Mem. Mus. Hist. Nat. 18: 30. 1829; FHK 47. 1861; FKH 67. 1912.

Tree, often less than 10 m tall. Bark greyish black; branches brownish red, terete, densely white lenticellate. Leaves including petioles 10–25 cm or longer; leaflets 2–3(–4) pairs; petiolules 7–8 mm; blades thinly leathery or leathery, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, sometimes elliptic-lanceolate, 6–15 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex cuspidate or shortly caudate-acuminate, margin entire, adaxially deep green and shining, abaxially glaucous, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins often slender, conspicuous or slightly prominent abaxially. Inflorescences terminal, large, many-branched. Pedicels 2–4 mm, slender, sometimes short and stout. Calyx golden tomentose. Stamens 6–7(–8); filaments ca. 4 mm. Ovary densely tuberculous and hispid. Fruit usually dark red to fresh red when mature, globose to subglobose, 2–3.5 cm. Seeds thoroughly covered by fleshy arillode.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 843; Y. S. Lau 1543; K. L. Yip 4258.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; SE Asia, widely cultivated in subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Summer.
Uses: Fruit, medicinal (folklore).

Lithocarpus attenuatus (Skan) Rehd. 尖葉柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 123. 1919; FRPS 22: 134, pl. 40: 4 –7. 1998; FOC 4: 350. 1999.
Quercus attenuata Skan in F. B. Forbes & Hemsley, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 506. 1899; FKH 254. 1912.

Tree, 10 –15 m tall, glabrous throughout. Bud-scales with oily resin when dry. Branchlets of last year growth white-farinose. Leaves thin-leathery; petioles 1.5 –3 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic or lanceolate, 7–13 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent to the petiole, apex long-acuminate, entire or sometimes undulate, abaxial surface glaucous when dry, with adhersive waxy-scales; lateral veins 9–13 on each side of midvein, slender; veins invisible or obscure. Male spike solitary or branched, axillary. Female flowers solitary and scattered on rachis; rachis sulcate, with white waxy scales. Cupules globose in fruiting time, base slightly narrowed like a stalk, 30–35 mm high, 25–30 mm in diam., enclosing nut completely, wall less than 0.5 mm thick, crustaceous; bracts triangular, small and obscure, the proximal ones united into concentric rings, the distal ones only remaining a subulate tip or wart-like. Nut subglobse, 20–25 mm high, 18 –28 mm in diam., white-farinose, wall ca. 0.5 mm , apex slightly narrowed, obtuse, base flat, scar 7–12 mm in diam., concave to 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Tam. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6708); HK sheet 4515.
Distribution: S Guangdong, SW Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Jun.– Oct.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley woods by C. Ford.

Lithocarpus corneus (Lour.) Rehd. 煙斗柯（石柯）
Stand. Cycl. Hort. 3569. 1917; FFJ 1: 393, fig. 344. 1982; FRPS 22: 128, pl. 36: 1–3. 1998; FOC 4: 349. 1999.
Pasania cornea (Lour.) Liao, Taxon. Revis. Fam. Fagac. 118, fig. 34: 1–2. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 96, pl. 46, photo 40. 1996.
Quercus cornea Lour., Fl. Cochinchin. 572. 1790; FHK 322. 1861; FKH 252. 1912.

Tree, to 15 m tall. Branchlets light tawny, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves papery or leathery, ± crowded towards apex of branches; petioles 0.5–2(–4) cm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to ovate-oblong or lanceolate-elliptic, (4–)6–13(–20) × 1.5–4(–7) cm, base cuneate to subrounded, symmetric or oblique, apex acuminate to acute, margin serrate or dentate, sometimes shallowly undulate, rarely entire, adaxial surface glabrous, or puberulent on the compressed midvein, abaxial surface slightly pubescent on midvein, or only with tuft of hairs on axils of veins; lateral veins 9–12 on each side of midvein, ending in teeth. Spikes mostly androgynous, terminal, erect, 2.5–4 cm, with female flowers on the lower part of the rachis. Cupule broadly turbinate, 22–45 mm high, 25–55 mm in diam., enclosing most part of nut, wall woody and thickened at base; bracts deltoid or rhomboid, central and margin ridged, the upper ones turned inwards. Nut hemispherical and glabrous in the enclosed part, the exserted flat top slightly concave and tomentose, wall ± horny, usually thicker than the wall of cupule; scar covering 2/3 of the nut.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. C. P. Lau 44, 68; H. C. Tang 1893.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Guizhou, SE Yunnan, S Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods, frequent on sunny slopes. Flowering: Almost all the year round, but mainly May–Jun.; fruit matures in the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Lithocarpus elizabethae (Tutch.) Rehd. 厚斗柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 125. 1919; FRPS 22: 157, pl. 46: 1– 5. 1998; FOC 4: 357. 1999.
Quercus elizabethae Tutch., J. Bot. 49: 273. 1911; FKH 254. 1912.

Tree, 9 –15 m tall. Branches and leaves glabrous. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade narrowly oblong or lanceolate, 9 –17 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate, margin entire, concolorous or ± glaucous abaxially; lateral veins slender, 13 –16 on each side of midvein; veins almost invisible. Male spikes 3-many forming panicle, or sometimes solitary in axils of leaves; rachis sparsely pubescent. Female spikes 2–4 congested at apex of branches; rachis 4– 6(–10) mm thick in fruiting time; female flowers usually in cluster of 3. Cupule subglobose, apex abruptly narrowed and slightly elongate into a nipple, 15 –30 mm high, 15 –28 mm in diam., usually covering nut completely, wall 2 mm (upper part) to 4 mm (lower part) thick; bracts broadly triangular or rhomboid, imbricate, the apical ones incurved. Nut compressed globose or subglobose, 14–24 mm in diam.; scar concave, 13–16 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Ta Tit Yan. HK sheet 26371; W. J. Tutcher 9114, 9469.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Guizhou, SE Yunnan.
Ecology: Mixed forests, frequent in moist places. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimens were collected from Victoria Peak and Tai Wai by W. J. Tutcher (nos. 4616, 9114, HK) around 1910.

Material (wood), environmental.

Lithocarpus fenestratus (Roxb.) Rehd. var. brachycarpus A. Camus 泥柯
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 90: 201. 1934; FRPS 22: 172, pl. 51: 8 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 360. 1999, pro syn. sub L. fenestratus auct. non (Roxb.) Rehd.
Quercus fenestrata auct non Roxb.: FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Young shoots tawny scurfy-lepidote. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 10 –18 mm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic or lanceolate, 9–15 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire, abaxially tawny scurfy-lepidote, ± greyish when dry; lateral veins 12–16 on each side of midvein, usually impressed adaxially; veins slender or invisible. Male spikes usually in panicles. Female spikes solitary and axillary, to 18 cm; rachis 5– 8 mm thick in fruiting time, scurfy-lepidote. Cupules in cluster of 3, only 1 or 2 developed, compressed globose, 10–15 mm high, 15 –28 mm in diam., covering most part of nut, wall ca. 0.5 mm thick, scurfy puberulent abaxially; bracts triangular, imbricate and appressed, only the subulate tips separate from the cupule. Nut compressed globose 10–15 mm high, 13 –25 mm in diam., apex rounded or pointed; scar concave, 10 –18 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak. HK sheet 6707; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6747).
Distribution: Hainan, SW Guangxi, SE Yunnan; NE Vietnam.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Aug.– Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Lithocarpus glaber (Thunb.) Nakai 柯
Cat. Sem. Spor. Hort. Bot. Univ. Imp. Tokyo 8. 1916; FFJ 1: 400, fig. 355. 1982; FRPS 22: 186, pl. 58: 6. 1998; FOC 4: 363. 1999.
Pasania glabra (Thunb.) Oerst., Nat. Foren. Vidensk. Meddel. 18: 83. 1866; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 91. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 2: 99, photo 42. 1996.
Quercus glabra Thunb., Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 858. 1784.
Quercus thalassica Hance, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 176. 1849; FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 15 m tall. Branchlets and bud-scales densely tawny tomentose. Leaves leathery or thick papery; petioles 1–2 cm, initially tomentose; leaf blade obovate, obovate-elliptic or oblong, 6 –12 × 2.5 – 4(– 5.5) cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly acute, shortly caudate or long-acuminate, margin entire or with 2– 4 teeth near apex, abaxially scurfy tomentose when young, later glabrate or nearly so; lateral veins 6– 8(–10) on each side of midvein; veinlets usually invisible. Male spikes forming panicle or solitary in axils of leaves, 5 –10(–15) cm; rachis densely tawny tomentose. Female spikes 7–13(–18) cm in fruiting time, often with a few male flowers; female flowers 3(– 5) clustered. Cupule discoid or cup-shape, 5 –7(–10) mm high, 9 –11(–15) mm in diam., thickened towards base, woody; bracts small, triangular, appressed, imbricate or united into concentric rings, densely puberulous abaxially. Nut ellipsoid, 12–25 mm high, 8 –15 mm in diam., apex pointed, ± white-farinose, dark chestnut brown; scar concave, 3 – 5(– 8) mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 6850; C. P. Lau 147; Y. W. Lam 31.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods, frequent on sunny slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen of Quercus thalassica was collected from Hong Kong Island by H. F. Hance before 1850.

Lithocarpus haipinii Chun 耳柯（卷葉石櫟）
J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 233. 1947; FFJ 1: 398, fig. 353. 1982; FRPS 22: 209, pl. 65: 1. 1998; FOC 4: 369. 1999.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Branchlets of the current year, petioles and rachis of inflorescence densely covered with greyish white or tawny long hairs. Leaves firmly leathery; petioles 2–3.5 cm; leaf blade broadly elliptic, ovate, obovate or obovate-elliptic, 8–15 × 4–8 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, often asymmetric, apex rounded or acute, sometimes shortly caudate, falcate, margin recurved, abaxial surface densely pilose; lateral veins 9–13 on each side of midvein, veins as is the lateral veins impressed adaxially. Male spike forming panicle. Female spikes shorter, usually terminal on apex of branches, 6–14 cm; female flowers 3–5-clustered. Young cupule covering entirely nut; bracts linear; mature cupule discoid, 3–6 mm high, 15–25 mm in diam., covering ca. 1/3 nut, wall almost woody; bracts reflexed, tip hooked. Nut subglobose but slightly compressed, bottom flat, 18–26 mm high, 20–30 mm in diam., white-farinose when young; scar concave, 8–14 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1268, 2053; P. S. Choi 512; W. Y. Chun 9159.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Hunan, S Guizhou.
Ecology: Woods, frequent on gentle, dry slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak in 1930 (C. L. Tso 22580, IBSC).

Lithocarpus hancei (Benth.) Rehd. 硬殼柯（漢斯石柯）
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FFJ 1: 400, fig. 356. 1982; FRPS 22: 176, pl. 54. 1998; FOC 4: 362. 1999.
Quercus hancei Benth., FHK 322. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 15 m tall, glabrous except the inflorescence. Branchlets ± tawny or grey, usually with a thin layer of translucent wax. Leaves thinly papery to rigid leathery; petioles 1–2(– 4) cm; leaf blade variable in shape and size, ovate, obovate, broadly elliptic, obovate-elliptic, narrowly elliptic or lanceolate, usually 6–14 × 3 – 5 cm, the ratio of length/width = 1.2– 5:1, base attenuate to broadly cuneate, usually decurrent to the petiole, apex shortly caudate-acuminate, sometimes rounded obtuse or acute, margin entire, ± recurved, concolour or sometimes white farinose adaxially when dry; lateral veins 11–14 on each side of midvein, slender and closely spaced; veins reticulate. Male spikes rarely 4 –10(–13) cm, usually forming panicle, sometimes with female flowers on the basal part; rachis sometimes twisted. Female spikes 2–many crowded at apex of branches, 5 – 8 cm. Cupule usually 3 – 5 clusterd, rarely solitary, shallow-bowl-shaped or discoid, 3–7 mm high, 10 –20 mm broad, covering nearly 1/3 of nut; bracts scale-like, triangular, appressed, imbricate or connate into a few concentric rings. Nut compressed globose, subglobose or broadly conical, 8 –12 mm high, 6 –25 mm in diam., apex rounded to pointed, rarely flat, glabrous; scar concave, 5 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 354, 418, 1329.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island around 1850 by J. G. Champion.

Lithocarpus harlandii (Hance ex Walpers) Rehd. 港柯（夏蘭柯）
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FFJ 1: 402, fig. 358. 1982; FRPS 22: 193, pl. 60: 1– 5. 1998; FOC 4: 365. 1999.
Quercus harlandii Hance ex Walpers, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 382. 1852; FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 18 m tall, glabrous except inflorescences. Young branches sulcate, purplish brown, becoming dark brown when dry. Leaves firmly leathery; petioles 1.5 –3 cm; leaf blade oblong to elliptic 7–18 × 3 – 6 cm, base attenuate-cuneate, often slightly oblique, apex caudate-acuminate, often falcate, margin entire or obtusely undulate-dentate near apex, rarely entire, glabrous; lateral veins 8 –13 on each side of midvein; veinlets obscure. Male spikes 2.5– 5 cm, solitary in the upper axils of leaves or forming panicles to 15 cm, erect, tomentose. Female spikes terminal, rigid, flexuose, ca. 5 cm, lengthening to 5 –10 cm in fruiting time; female flowers in cluster of 3, scattered on rachis; rachis shortly tomentose. Cupule cup-shaped, 6–10 mm high, 14 –20 mm in diam.; bracts triangular or rhomboid, margin and midvein ± ridged, imbricate, puberulous outside. Nut conical or broadly ellipsoid, 22–28 mm high, 16 –2 mm in diam., apex rounded or obtuse, wall 1.5 –2 mm thick; scar concave, 9–12 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen, Wong Nai Chung, Repulse Bay, Bowen Road, Lantau Island. C. P. Lau. 79; H. C. Tang 367; Y. S. Lau 2393.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Jiangxi, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley woods around 1850.
