Lithocarpus irwinii (Hance) Rehd. 廣南柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FRPS 22: 103. 1998; FOC 4: 342. 1999.
Quercus amygdalifolia auct. non Skan: FKH 252. 1912.
Quercus irwinii Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. ser. 2, 18: 229. 1862.

Tree, 8–12 m tall. Young shoots sulcate, with raised lenticels, densely tawny pilose, soon glabrate. Leaves thickly and rigidly leathery; petioles usually less than 1 cm, brownish black when dry; leaf blade elliptic or lanceolate, 7–12 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, margin ± revolute, entire or undulate on the upper half, dark brown and often oily on adaxial surface when dry, abaxial surface reddish brown scurfy and sparsely pilose on midvein when young, greyish when mature; lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein; veins very slender or inconspicuous. Male spike 3 – 5 cm, solitary in axils of leaves or 2–3 in panicles; rachis tawny pubescent. Female spike in pairs terminal on branchlets, 2–5 cm; rachis 5–8 mm thick in fruiting time; flowers in clusters of 3, sometimes solitary. Cupule turbinate, broadest at apex, 20 –26 mm high, 18 –24 mm in diam., apex almost flat, enclosing the nut completely, wall 2– 4 mm thick; bracts deltoid, middle and margins thickened in ridges, imbricate. Nut subglobose, ca. 15 mm in diam., densely covered with minute appressed hairs; scar convex, covering ca. 1/4 of the nut.

Locality: Mount Cameron, Tai Tam, Lantau Island. HK sheet 6694, 26307; W. J. Tutcher 5589.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island in Nov. 1862 by J. J. Irwin (in Herb. Hance No. 9818, BM).
records.uses:
Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island in Nov. 1862 by J. J. Irwin (in Herb. Hance No. 9818, BM).

records.text:
Lithocarpus iteaphyllus (Hance) Rehd. 鼠刺葉柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FRPS 22: 146. 1998; FOC 4: 353. 1999.
Quercus iteaphylla Hance, J. Bot. 22: 229. 1884; FKH 253. 1912.
Lithocarpus iteaphylloides Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 236. 1947.

Tree, 5 –10 m tall. Branchlets of the current year growth conspicuously sulcate, dark reddish brown, glabrous; bud-scale glabrous. Leaves thickly papery; petioles usually 5– 8 mm, sometimes to 3 cm, ± thickened at base; leaf blade narrowly oblong or lanceolate, 8 –13 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, apex acuminate, base broadly cuneate, decurrent to petiole, margin entire; midvein raised on both surfaces; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein, slender, conspicuous on both surfaces. Spikes usually androgynous, 3 –7 cm, solitary or congested on apex of branches of last year growth, with male flowers on apical part and female ones on basal part, both solitary and scattered on tawny puberulous rachis. Cupule bowl-shaped, 5– 8 mm high, 10–14 mm broad, base thickly woody; bracts reduced and united into 6 – 8 concentric rings, tawny waxy-lepidote and sparsely puberulous abaxially. Nut ellipsoid, 10 –18 mm high, 10 –14 mm in diam., sometimes as broad as high, apex pointed or rounded, glabrous, light chestnut brown; scar concave, 5– 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Happy Valley, Causeway Bay. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6791, 6792).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Hunan, S Jiangxi.
Ecology: Woods on sunny slopes and banks of streams. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in 1882.
records.uses:
Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in 1882.

Lithocarpus konishii (Hayata) Hayata 油葉柯
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6 (Suppl.): 72. 1917; FRPS 22: 145, pl. 43: 4 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 353. 1999.
Quercus konishii Hayata, J. Coll. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 25(19): 201. 1908.
Pasania konishii (Hayata) Schott., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 673. 1912; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 93. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 2: 108, pl. 53, photo 46. 1996.

Trees, usually to 5 m tall. Bud-scales with light grey silky short hairs. Spring shoots glabrous; autumn shoots tawny pubescent. Leaves firmly papery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, obovate, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 3–6 × 1.2–2.4 cm, apex acute or shortly caudateacuminate, base cuneate, margin with 3–6 obtuse teeth on each side, with tuft of hairs at axils of veins on abaxial surface when young; midvein puberulous adaxially; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein, slightly impressed adaxially; veins slender but visible. Male spikes 3–5(–10) cm, solitary or forming panicles; rachis tawny tomentose; female flowers solitary or rarely 2 in clusters on the basal part of the male rachis, or in separate spike. Cupule discoid, 4–8 mm high, 15–23 mm in diam., enclosing the bottom of nut, wall 1.5–2 mm thick; bracts broadly triangular, midvein ridged, imbricate, greyish brown tomentose. Nut compressed globose, apex rounded or flat, 10–18 mm high, 15–25 mm in diam., wall 3–6 mm thick, horny, glabrous; scar margin concave, central ± convex, 13–24 in diam.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Long Ke, Sai Wan Shan, Kau Ling Chung. Y. S. Lau 1480; Y. W. Lam 294, 462.
Distribution: E Hainan, S Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Lithocarpus litseifolius (Hance) Chun 木薑葉柯（多穗柯）
J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 152. 1928; FRPS 22: 201. 1998; FOC 4: 367. 1999.
Lithocarpus synbalanos (Hance) Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 152. 1928; FFJ 1: 399, fig. 354. 1982;
Quercus litseifolia Hance, J. Bot. 22: 229. 1884.
Quercus polystacha auct. non Wall. ex DC.: FKH 253. 1912.
Quercus synbalanos Hance, J. Bot. 22: 228. 1884; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall, glabrous except the inflorescence. Branchlets and petioles sometimes ± white-farinose when dry. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, obovate-elliptic or ovate, rarely narrowly elliptic, 8 –18 × 3 – 8 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or abruptly acute, margin entire, concolorous or ± glaucous abaxially; lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein, concealed near the edge; veins slender, reddish brown or brownish yellow when dry. Male spike 7–15(–25) cm, forming panicle, rarely solitary. Female spikes 14 –25 cm; female flowers 3 – 5 clustered, but the spikes sometimes androgynous, 2– 6 congested at apex of branches; rachis sparsely pubescent. Cupule discoid, 8 –14 mm in diam., glabrous, thickened towards base, woody; bracts triangular, appressed and imbricate, the basal ones connate into concentric rings. Nut broadly conical or subglobose, rarely compressed globose, 8–15 mm high, 12–20 mm in diam., glabrous, often ± white-farinose; scar concave, ca. 11 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ta Tit Yan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6813); HK sheet 6814; C. P. Lau 118.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Hubei, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Myanmar, Laos.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Lithocarpus macilentus Chun & C. C. Huang 粉葉柯
Guihaia 8: 30. 1988; FRPS 22: 184, pl. 57. 1998; FOC 4: 363. 1999.
Quercus irwinii auct. non Hance: FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, 7–12 m tall. Young shoots and petioles tawny tomentose. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles less than 1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, rarely oblanceolate, 6 –11 × 2–3 cm, narrowed to both ends, base decurrent, margin entire, covered with fugacious, minute and crisped hairs on both surfaces when young, abaxially scurfy; lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein; veins inconspicuous. Male spikes forming panicle. Female spikes 7–10 cm, lengthening to 20 cm in fruiting time. Rachis tawny tomentose; female flowers in cluster of 3. Cupule bowl-shaped, 6– 8 mm high, 15–20 mm in diam., covering basal part of nut, wall thin, ± thickened at base. Nut broadly conical or compressed globose, glabrous, dark chestnut brown, 13 –15 mm high, 15–17 mm in diam., scar concave, 7– 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Cameron Road, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1721; HK sheet 6782; X. Y. Zhuang 1920; K. Wong 1188.
Distribution: W Guangdong, E Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods on banks of streams. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The species was reported as Lithocarpus irwinii (Hance) Rehd. previously (Check List HK Plants 38. 1993).

Material (wood), environmental.

Lithocarpus quercifolius C. C. Huang & Y. T. Chang 櫟葉柯
Guihaia 8(1): 16. 1988; FRPS 22: 142, pl. 43: 1–3. 1998; FOC 4: 352. 1999.

Tree, 5 – 6 m tall. Branchlets of the current year growth pubescent. Leaves usually crowded towards apex of branches, firmly papery, concolour; petioles 2– 5 mm; leaf blade oblong or obovate-elliptic, 4 –11 × 1– 4 cm, apex acute, base rounded or broadly cuneate, margin with a few acute teeth towards apex, usually with tuft of hairs on axils of veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein, branched near the edge; veinlets conspicuous or slender, ending in teeth. Male spike 3.5 –7 cm, with solitary and scattered female flowers on the proximal part of the rachis; rachis tawny pubescent. Cupule discoid, 2–5 mm high, 20–25 mm in diam., enclosing the basal part of nut; bracts lanceolate when young, rhomboid or broadly triangular when mature, imbricate, midvein ridged. Nut compressed globose, 12–16 mm high, 20 –14 mm in diam., with appressed minute hairs; scar with the margin concave, center convex, 16 –20 mm in diam.

Locality: Shek O, Mount Parker. W. J. Tutcher 6798; HK sheet 6733, 34314.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Jiangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Litsea acutivena Hayata 尖脈木薑子
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 163. 1915; FHN 1: 293. 1964; FRPS 31: 328. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 465, pl. 215. 1996.
Actinodaphne acutivena (Hayata) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 14: 191. 1938.
Litsea dolichocarpa Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 166. 1915.

Evergreen tree, to 7 m tall. Branchlets densely tawny villose when young, glabrescent in age; bud scales rusty pubescent abaxially. Leaves alternate or crowded towards apex of branches; petioles 6–12 mm, densely tawny pubescent; leaf blade leathery, lanceolate, oblanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 4 –11 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially yellowish tawny pubescent; pinnately veined, lateral veins 9 –10 on each side of midvein, midvein and lateral veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 5–6-flowered, clustered near apex of branchlets. Peduncles 3 mm, pubescent. Pedicels densely pubescent. Perianth-lobes 6, long-elliptic, ca. 2 mm, abaxially pubescent on midvein. Fertile stamens 9; filaments pubescent. Ovary ovoid, subglabrous, style ca. 2.5 mm; stigma 2-lobed; staminodes pubescent. Fruits ellipsoid, 12–20 × 10–12 mm, black at maturity, subtended by enlarged, cupshaped perianth-tube; fruiting pedicels 1 cm.

Locality: Victoria Peak. Y. S. Lau 467; C. Ford s.n. (HK sheet 4975).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.–Feb.

Litsea cubeba (Lour.) Pers. 木薑子（山蒼樹）
Syn. Pl. 2: 4. 1807; FHN 1: 289. 1964; FRPS 31: 271. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 470, photo 198. 1996.
Laurus cubeba Lour. Fl. Cochinch. 252. 1790.
Tetranthera polyantha Wall., Cat. No. 2538, nom. nud.; FHK 293. 1861.
Litsea citrata auct. non Bl.: Dunn & Tutch., FKH 225. 1912.

Deciduous, aromatic shrub or small tree, 8–10 m tall. Branchlets slender, green, glabrous; terminal buds conical, pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 6–20 mm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, lanceolate, oblong or elliptic, 4–11 × 1.1 –2.4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, dark green adaxially, glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; pinnately veined, lateral veins slender, 6–16 on each side of midvein, together with midvein raised on both surfaces. Umbels 4–6-flowered, solitary or fascicled; peduncles slender, 6–10 mm; bracts ciliate. Perianth-lobes 6, broad ovate. Fertile stamens 9; filaments pubescent in the lower part; staminodes in female flowers pubescent on the lower part. Ovary ovoid, stigma capitate. Fruit subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam., black at maturity; fruiting pedicels 2–4 mm, slightly enlarged at the apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1304, 1480.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Sunny slopes, thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Materials (essential oil), ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Litsea elongata (Wall. ex Nees) Benth. & Hook. f. 黃丹木薑子
Gen. Pl. 3: 163. 1880; FKH 225. 1912; FHN 1: 294. 1964; FRPS 31: 329, pl. 86: 1. 1982.
Daphnidium elongata Nees in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 63. 1831.

Evergreen tree, to 12 m tall. Branchlets yellowish brown or greyish brown, densely brown-tomentose; bud scales covered with silky short hairs abaxialy. Leaves alternate; petioles 10–25 mm, densely brown tomentose; leaf blade leathery, oblong, oblong-lanceolate, narrowly lanceolate or oblanceolate, 6–22 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate or subrounded, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially puberulous and villose along midvein and lateral veins; pinnately veined, lateral veins 10 –20 on each side of midvein, midvein and lateral veins immersed or slightly impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 4 –5-flowered, solitary, rarely clustered. Peduncles stout, 2–5 mm, densely brown tomentose. Pedicels villose. Perianth-lobes 6, ovate, abaxially villose along midvein. Fertile stamens 9 –12; filaments villose. Female umbels smaller than the males. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Fruit oblong, 11–13 × 7– 8 mm, subtended by enlarged, cup-shaped perianth-tube, blackish purple when mature; fruiting pedicels 2–3 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Wu Kau Tang, Lai Chi Wo. Y. W. Lam 156.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Nepal.
Ecology: Roadsides, streamsides, forests on mountain slopes; thickets, moist places in sparse forests. Flowering: May–Nov.; fruiting: Feb.–Jun.

Litsea glutinosa (Lour.) C. B. Rob. 潺槁樹
Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 6: 321. 1911; FHN 1: 291, fig. 144. 1964; FRPS 31: 285. 1982
Sebifera glutinosa Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 638. 1790.
Tetranthera citrifolia sensu Benth., FHK 293. 1861.
Litsea sebifera Pers., Syn. Pl. 2: 4. 1807; FKH 225. 1912.

Evergreen tree, 3 –15 m tall. Branchlets greyish brown, initially tawny tomentose. buds scales greyish yellow tomentose. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–2.6 cm, grey yellow tomentose; leaf blade leathery, obovate, obovate-oblong or elliptic-lanceolate, 3.5 –10(–26) × 1.5 –11 cm, base cuneate, obtuse or rotund, apex obtuse or rounded, initially tomentose on both surfaces, glabrate in age; pinnately veined, lateral veins 5–12 on each side of midvein, together with midvein slightly raised adaxially, distinctly raised abaxially; Umbels few flowered, solitary or several clustered on short spurs, or more often in axils of distal leaves. Peduncles 1–1.5 cm, together with pedicels tawny tomentose. Perianth inconspicuous or wanting. Fertile stamens 15 or more; filaments greyish pubescent. Ovary of female flowers subrounded, glabrous; staminodes pubescent. Fruit globose, ca. 7 mm in diam.; fruiting pedicels 5 – 6 mm, slightly thickened at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2220; P. S. Choi 290.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Fujian; India, Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest edges, streamsides, or thickets.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), bark is used to make incense.
records.uses: Medicinal (folklore), bark is used to make incense.

records.text:
Litsea greenmaniana C. K. Allen 華南木薑子
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 394. 1938; FRPS 31: 316. 1982.
Litsea greenmaniana var. angustifolia Y. C. Yang & P. H. Huang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 56. 1978.
Litsea variabilis auct. non Hemsl.: Check List HK Plants 28. 1993.

Evergreen small tree, 6 – 8 m tall. Branchlets reddish brown, pubescent when young, glabrescent in age; bud scales covered with silky short hairs. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.7–1.3 cm, initially pubescent; leaf blade thin leathery, elliptic or suboblanceolate, 4 –13.5 × 0.7–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or falcate, green and shining adaxially, glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; pinnately veined, lateral veins slender, ca. 10 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins prominent abaxially. Umbels 3 – 4-flowered, 1– 4 clustered on axillary spurs. Peduncles 3 – 4 mm, puberulous. Male flowers: pedicels puberulous; Perianth-lobes 6, yellow, ovate or elliptic, ca. 2 × 1 mm, pubescent abaxially, glabrous adaxially; fertile stamens 9, filaments villose. Fruit ellipsoid, 13 × 8 mm, subtended by enlarged, cup-shaped perianth tube (receptacles); fruiting pedicels 3 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan. W. J. Tutcher s.n.(HK sheet 4923); F. W. Xing 8467.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests on valleys, dense forests on mountain slopes; below 1200 m. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.–Mar. of the next year.

Litsea monopetala (Roxb.) Pers. 假柿木薑子（假柿樹）
Syn. Pl. 2: 4. 1807; FHN 1: 292. 1964; FRPS 31: 302, pl. 78: 1– 4. 1982.
Tetranthera monopetala Roxb., Pl. Coromandel 2: 26, pl. 148. 1798; FHK 292. 1861.
Litsea polyantha Juss., Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 6: 211. 1805; FKH 225. 1912.

Evergreen tree, to 18 m tall. Branchlets and bud scales densely rusty pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–3 cm, densely rusty pubescent; leaf blade thin leathery, broadly ovate, obovate to ovate-oblong, 8 –20 × 4 –12 cm, base rounded or acute, apex obtuse or rounded, occasionally acute, adaxially rusty pubescent along midvein when young, glabrescent in age, abaxially densely rusty pubescent, pinnately veined, lateral veins of 8–12 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 4(– 6)-flowered, clustered on axillary spurs. Peduncles 4– 6 mm. Pedicels 6–7 mm, rusty pubescent. Perianth-lobes of male flowers 5– 6, lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, yellowish white. Fertile stamens 9; filaments slender, pubescent. Female flowers smaller, Perianth-lobes oblong, ca. 1.5 mm; staminodes pubescent. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Fruit long-ovoid, 7 × 5 mm, subtended by slightly enlarged, shallow discoid perianth tube (receptacles); fruiting pedicels 1 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Lantau. H. C. Tang 122, 984.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SW Guizhou, S Yunnan; India, Pakistan, SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets or sparse forests on sunny slopes; up to 1500 m, but mostly found on hills at low altitudes. Flowering: Nov.–Jun. of the next year; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Litsea rotundifolia (Nees) Hemsl. 圓葉豺皮樟
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 385. 1891; FKH 225. 1912; FRPS 31: 292. 1982.
Iozoste rotundifolia Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 63. 1831.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, up to 3 m tall. Branchlets slender, greyish brown, glabrous or nearly so; bud scales yellow silky puberulous. Leaves thin leathery, alternate; petioles 3 –5 mm, initially pubescent, glabrescent in age; leaf blade thin leathery, broadly ovate-rounded to suborbicular, 2.2–4.5 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base subrounded, apex rotund or shortly acuminate, adaxially dark green and shining, abaxially glaucous, glabrous on both surfaces; pinnately veined, lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein, midvein and lateral veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 3 – 4-flowered, often 3 clustered in axils of leaves. Peduncles and pedicels almost lacking. Perianth-lobes 6, obovate-rounded, unequal. Fertile stamens 9; filaments villose. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam. subsessile, greyish bluish black when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Fanling, Haihung. HK sheet 24421.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Sparse forests, thickets of lower parts on mountain, roadsides on mountains, riversides; below 800 m.

Litsea rotundifolia (Nees) Hemsl. var. oblongifolia (Nees) C. K. Allen 豺皮樟
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 386. 1938; FRPS 31: 292. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 474, pl. 220. 1996.
Iozoste rotundifolia Nees var. oblongifolia Nees in J. D. Hooker & Arnott, Bot. Beechey Voy. 209. 1836 (based on Litsea chinensis Bl.).
Litsea chinensis Bl., Bijdr. 565. 1825, non Lam.
Actinodaphne chinensis Nees, Syst. Laur. 600. 1836; FHK 293. 1861.

Differs from var. rotundifolia by leaves ovate-oblong, 2.5 – 5.5 × 1–2.2 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate; reticulation of veins conspicuous on both surfaces.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 6; Y. W. Lam 960.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, thickets.

Litsea verticillata Hance 輪葉木薑子（槁樹）
J. Bot. 21: 356. 1883; FHN 1: 289. 1964; FRPS 31: 287, pl. 76: 1–2. 1982
Litsea multiumbellata Lec. f. annamensis H. Liu, Laurac. Chine et Indochine 171. 1932 et 1934.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 2–5 m tall. Branchlets brown, densely yellow hirsute, glabrous in age; bud scales densely tawny pubescent. Leaves 4–6 irregularly whorled; petioles 2–6 mm, densely yellow villose; leaf blade thin leathery, lanceolate or oblanceolate-oblong, 7–25 × 2–6 cm, base acute, obtuse or rotund, apex acuminate, adaxially green and glabrous excepting the puberulous midvein, abaxially greyish green or yellowish brown, brown pubescent, margin ciliate, pinnately veined, lateral veins 12–14 on each side of midvein, midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 5–8-flowered, subsessile, 2–10 clustered at apex of spurs; bracts 4–7, greyish brown puberulous; Perianth-lobes 6 (4), lanceolate, abaxially villose along midvein. Fertile stamens 9; filaments exserted, villose. Ovary ovoid or ellipsoid; styles slender; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit ovoid or ellipsoid, 10–15 × 5–6 mm, apiculate, subtended by enlarged, discoid perianth-tube.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2765; P. S. Choi 418.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan; Cambodia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets in valleys, streamsides. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.; fruiting: Nov.–Jun. of the following year.

Livistona chinensis (Jacq.) R. Br. ex Mart. 蒲葵
Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 240. 1838; FKH 286. 1912; FGD 2: 445, fig. 311. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 26. 1991; FOC 23: 148. 2010.
Latania chinensis Jacq., Fragm. Bot. 1: 16. 1800.
Livistona subglobosa Mart., Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 319. 1838.
Livistona chinensis (Jacq.) R. Br. var. subglobosa (Mart.) Becc., Webbia 5: 16. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 660. 2000.

Large tree, to 20 m tall. Stems 20–30 cm in diam., rough ringed with leaf scars; petiole bases persistent when young. Leaves palmate, blades rounded or subrounded, 1–1.8 m in diam., divided to 1/2 depth into single fold, linear-lanceolate segments; segment split to 20–30 cm depth and pendulous; petioles 1–2 m, proximally with green or black-brown, recurved spines on margins; hastula 1–3 cm. Inflorescences 1–1.5 m, branched to 3 orders, partial inflorescences 6–7, about 35 – 45 cm; rachillae 10–20 cm; flowers bisexual, 2–2.5 mm, 4–7 clustered, whitish yellow; calyx deeply 3-lobed, triangular; petals 3-lobed; stamens 6; carpels 3. Fruits ellipsoidal, about 1.8 × 1.2 cm, blue-black or black when matured. Seed 1, ellipsoidal, about 1.5 × 0.9 cm, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. R. Helms 2953; Y. S. Lau 1691; HK sheet 29535.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Vietnam, S Japan.
Ecology: Coastal forests, often on sandy soils at low elevations. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, material (weaving).

Lobelia alsinoides Lam. subsp. hancei (Hara) Lammers 假半邊蓮
Bot. Bull. Acad. Sin. 33: 286. 1992.
Lobelia hancei Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 17: 23. 1941; Check List HK Plants 89. 2004.
Lobelia alsinoides var. cantonensis (E. Wimm. ex Danguy) E. Wimm., Ann. Naturhist. Mus. Wien 56: 360. 1948.
Lobelia chinensis Lour. var. cantonensis E. Wimm. ex Danguy, Fl. Gén. Indo‑Chine 3: 681. 1930.
Lobelia alsinoides auct. non Lam.: FGD 3: 329. 1995.

Annual herbs, 10–30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems succulent, erect or ascending, simple or few‑branched, angular. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged; petioles 1–3 mm; leaf blades ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–20 × 3–7 mm, base attenuate or obtuse, apex rounded or acute, margin crenate. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels slender, 1– 1.5 cm, with 2 lanceolate bracteoles at base. Calyx tube turbinate, 2–3 mm; calyx lobes linear‑lanceolate, entire. Corolla pale blue, 4–8 mm, 2‑lipped, upper lobes oblong‑oblanceolate, erect, lower lobes oblong‑elliptic, patent. Filaments connate above middle; anthers all barbate at apex. Capsule hemispheric or ovoid, 3–5 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung. HK sheet 39668.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Xizang, Yunnan; Japan.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places by water. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.

Lobelia chinensis Lour. 半邊蓮
Fl. Cochinch. 514. 1790; FKH 152. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 154. 1983; FGD 3: 329, fig. 215. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 789, pl. 366, photo 397. 1998.
Lobelia radicans Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 2: 330 – 331. 1794; FKH 152. 1912.

Perennial herbs, glabrous. Stems decumbent or ascendent, 6–15 cm or longer, rooting at the nodes. Leaves alternate, sessile or nearly so, linear to lanceolate 8–25 × 2–6 mm, base rounded or slightly narrowed, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or shallowly serrate above middle. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves; pedicels 2–3 cm. Calyx‑tube 3–5 mm, narrowed at base; lobes 5, lanceolate, about the length of the tube, entire or with a pair of teeth on the lower part. Corolla pink, light purple or white, 10–15 mm, slit open on the upper side nearly to the base; tube white pubescent; limb 5‑lobed, lobes spreading in a plane, the 2 lateral longer, lanceolate, the other 3 oblong‑lanceolate; filaments united above middle, the free parts pubescent laterally; anther‑tube glabrous or sparsely pubescent dorsally, the 2 lower ones bearded at the top. Capsule obconical, 5–6 mm long.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Fanling, Ng Tung Chai, Tsiu Hang, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1607; L. T. Lo 76, 396.
Distribution: S, C & E China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Lower banks of paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering : Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lobelia zeylanica L. 疏毛半邊蓮
Sp. Pl. 932. 1753; FKH 152. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 148. 1983; FGD 3: 329. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 792, pl. 369, photo 400. 1998.
Lobelia affinis Wall. ex G. Don, Gard. Dict. 3: 709. 1834; FKH 152. 1912.
Lobelia trigona auct. non Roxb.: FHK 196. 1861.

Annual herbs. Stems slender, decumbent or prostrate, 10–30(–40) cm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, rooting at the lower nodes. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged; petioles 3–12 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–4 × 1–3 cm, base truncate, shallowly cordate or cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire serrate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially sparsely covered with small coarse hairs on the veins. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves; pedicels 1–2 cm, sparsely pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, sparsely pubescent; lobes 5, lanceolate or narrowly triangular, 3–5 mm, ciliate. Corolla light purple or white, bilabiate, 5–9 mm, the 2 upper lobes shorter, obovate‑oblong, the 3 lower ones ovate to spathulate; filaments with the upper 1/3 united; anthers 5, all shortly bearded at the top. Capsule obovoid, 3–7 mm long.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 317; Y. W. Lam 1312; HK sheet 16499.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E to SE Asia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Feb. of the following year.

Loeseneriella concinna A. C. Sm. 程香仔樹（希藤）
J. Arnold Arbor. 26(2): 170. 1945; FRPS 46: 9. 1981.
Hippocratea obtusifolia auct. non Roxb.: FHK 62. 1861; FKH 62. 1912.

Woody climber, glabrous throughout. Branchlets slender, with rough lenticels. Petioles 2–4 mm; leaf blade papery, ovate-oblong or elliptical, 4–7 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base rounded, apex obtuse or shortly and obtusely acuminate, margin sparsely crenate, lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins conspicuous. Cymes axillary or terminal, 2–3.5 cm; peduncles 1.5–1.8 cm, bracteate and bracteolate. Sepals deltoid, 0.7 mm, ciliate. Petals yellowish green, thinly fleshy, oblong-lanceolate, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm, ciliate, dorsal appendiculate; disk cupular. Stamens 3, filaments 1.3 mm. Ovary deltoid, most part immersed in disk, 3-locular; ovules 4 per locule. Capsules obovate-ellipsoidal, 3–5 mm, 4-seeded. Seeds 3 cm, with membranous wing at base.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lion Rock, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1613, 2979; K. L. Yip 4177.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Jul.; fruiting: Sep.
Notes: The holotype specimen (Y. W. Taam 2105, A) was collected from”Shantau” (San Tau), Tung Chung on 4 Jun. 1941.

Lolium perenne L. 黑麥草
Sp. Pl. 1: 83. 1753; FRPS 9(2): 289, pl. 33: 6. 2002; FOC 22: 244. 2006; FGD 9: 387. 2009.

Perennial herb, 20–90 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or spreading, 1–2.5 mm in diam., 3–4-noded, sometimes prostrate and rooting from the lower nodes. Leaf blades linear, soft, 5–20(–30) cm × 3–6 mm, glabrous, folded when young, with or without 3 mm auricles at the base; ligule membranous, tongue-shaped, 1.5–2.5 mm; leaf sheaths 5–20 cm, glabrous. Raceme stiffly erect, or rarely slightly curved, 10–30 cm; rachis glabrous, smooth. Spikelets 0.5–2 cm, florets 3–10(–14); rachilla internodes ca. 1 mm, smooth, glabrous; lower glume absent, upper glume lanceolate, 1/3 as long to subequalling spikelet, 3–9-veined, margins narrowly membranous, apex acute or obtuse; lemmas oblong, herbaceous, 5–9 mm, 5-veined, smooth, apex obtuse to subacute, not turgid at maturity, usually awnless, rarely with an awn up to 8 mm; palea oblong, as long as the lemma, 2-keeled, minutely ciliate along keels, apex sinus. Anther ca. 3 mm. Caryopsis length more than 3 times width.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tseng Lan Shue (cultivated). HK sheet 35645, 38096.
Distribution: Commonly cultivated in China; widely distributed in Europe, N Africa and the temperate regions of Asia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control), animal food (fodder, forage).

Lonicera confusa (Sweet) DC. 華南忍冬（山銀花）
Prodr. 4: 333. 1830; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 238, pl. 62: 5 – 6, 1988; FGD 4: 309, fig. 179. 2000.
Nintooa confusa Sweet, Hort. Brit. ed. 2, 258. 1830.
Lonicera multiflora Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 167. 1852; FHK 144. 1861.

Semi‑evergreen climbers; young branchlets, petioles and peduncles densely grey‑yellow pubescent, with crisped hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 5–8 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 3–6 × 2–4 cm, base rounded, truncate or cordate, apex acute, margin ciliate, sometimes mucronate, densely pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 3–4 on each sides of midvein. Flower‑pairs axillary on branchlet top, or in short racemes with distinct involucrate bracts. Bracts lanceolate, 1–2 mm. Calyx 2.5–3 mm. Corolla white, becoming yellow when dry, 3.2 – 5 cm; limb slightly shorter than tube. Stamens and styles exserted. Berry black, elliptic or subglobular, 6–10 mm in length.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. U. A. On 140; HK sheet 13346, 13348.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Nepal.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lonicera japonica Thunb. 忍冬（金銀花）
Syst. Veg. 14: 216. 1784; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 236, pl. 62: 1 – 4. 1988; FGD 4: 306, fig. 178. 2000.

Semi‑evergreen climbers; branchlets densely tawny hirsute, with spreading hairs and mixed with glandular hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 4–8 mm; leaf blade ovate to elliptic‑ovate, rarely obovate or ovate‑lanceolate, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, rarely subcordate, apex acute or obtuse, margin ciliate, glabrous or pubescent on both surfaces; lateral veins 3 – 5 on each side of midvein. Flowers paired, axillary on upper part of branchlets, often in racemose‑cymes. Peduncles 2 – 4 cm. Bracts leaf‑like, 2–3 cm. Calyx tube ca. 2 mm, glabrous, teeth ovate‑deltoid or long deltoid. Corolla white, becoming yellow, 2‑labiate, 3–4.5 cm, hirsute and glandular hairy, labium linear, reflexed. Stamens and styles exserted. Berry blue‑black, globular, 6–7 mm in diam., shining.

Locality: Tai Tam. Y. S. Lau 971; HK sheet 2243, 13394.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Heilongjiang, Nei Mongol, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Xizang and Hainan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lonicera longiflora (Lindl.) DC. 長花忍冬
Prodr. 4: 331. 1830; FHK 143. 1861; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 242, pl. 66: 1 – 2. 1988; FGD 4: 308. 2000.

Climbers; branchlets glabrous or sometimes slightly yellow‑brown hirsute. Leaves leathery; petioles 5 – 8 mm; leaf blades oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, rarely ovate, 5–8 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, apex acuminate, margin slightly revolute, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein, very obliquely ascending, net‑veins prominent abaxially. Flower‑pairs axillary or forming loose terminal heads or short racemes. Peduncles 5 – 8 mm. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm. Calyx‑tube subobconic, ca. 2.5 mm, subglabrous, teeth deltoid‑lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm. Corolla white, gradually becoming yellow, 2‑labiate, 5–10 cm; tube 2.5–4 cm, labium, rolled back at top, lower lip linear, upper lip 4‑toothed. Stamens and pistil exserted. Berry white.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Hung Mui Kuk, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1167, 1247, 3205.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Lonicera macrantha (D. Don) Spreng. 大花忍冬
Syst. Veg. 4(2): 82. 1827; FHK 143. 1861; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 240, pl. 63: 1 – 5. 1988; FGD 4: 308. 2000.

Semi‑evergreen climbers; young branchlets thickly pubescent and hirsute with spreading hairs and sometimes mixed with glandular hairs. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic or ovate‑lanceolate, 5 – 12 × 2 – 7 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acuminate, margin ciliate, slightly revolute, hirsute and red glandular hairy on abaxial surface; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flower‑pairs in axillary, corymbiform, clusters on upper parts of branchlets. Bracts lanceolate or linear, 2–5 mm. Calyx 3–4 mm. Corolla white or yellowish, fragrant, pubescent, 4.5–7(–10) cm; tube 3–5 cm; limb 2‑labiate, lower labium reflexed, upper lip long ovate. Stamens and style slightly exserted. Berry black, globular or ellipsoidal, 8–12 mm in length.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 505; K. Y. Tam 138; K. L. Yip 4104.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Nepal, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.

Lonicera rhytidophylla Hand.‑Mazz. 皺葉忍冬（顯脈忍冬）
Symb. Sin. 7(4): 1049, pl. 16, fig. 8. 1936; FRPS 72: 246, pl. 67: 3 – 6. 1988; FGD 4: 309, fig. 180. 2000.
Lonicera reticulata Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 167. 1852. non Rafin. 1838; FHK 144. 1861; FKH 122. 1912.

Evergreen climbers; branchlets and inflorescence densely covered with a short soft velvety tomentum. Leaves leathery; petioles 8–15 mm; leaf blade broad‑elliptic, ovate, ovate‑oblong to oblong, 3 –10 × 1–4 cm, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, rarely truncate, apex obtuse and mucronate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous and shining, and winkled with a network of impressed veins, abaxially covered with a white or yellowish or white dense tomentum; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flower‑pairs 6 or 8 together in heads or short cymes, axillary or terminal. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, 2–3 mm, hairy. Calyx‑tube ca. 2 mm, calyx teeth subulate, 1–2 mm. Corolla white, then becoming yellow, 2‑labiate, 2.5–3.5 cm, densely hirsute and glandular hairy, lower lip reflexed, upper lip erect. Stamens and styles exserted. Fruit ellipsoidal, blue‑black when mature, 7 – 8 × 4–5 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Magazine Gap, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 998; L. T. Lo 469; HK sheet 36043.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Lophatherum gracile Brongn. 淡竹葉
Duperrey, Voy. Monde 2: 50. 1831; FHK 433. 1861; FKH 329. 1912; FHN 4. 366, fig. 1176. 1977; FFJ 6: 133. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 334, pl. 128. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 35, pl. 3: 5. 2002; FOC 22: 445. 2006; FGD 9: 385, fig. 193. 2009.

Perennial herb, 60–150 cm tall, with short, knotty rhizomes and spindle-shaped root tubers. Culms loosely tufted, slender, stiffly erect. Leaf blades lanceolate, 5 –30 × 2–5 cm, tesselate veined, base rounded to a 8–12 mm pseudopetiole, glabrous or with long hairs on both surfaces; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, brown, hispid on backside; leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose. Inflorescence loose, outline elliptic, 10–30 cm. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate, subterete, sessile, 7–12 mm, base glabrous or hairy, with 1 perfect and 3–7 neutral florets; glumes ovate, rounded on back, subleathery with membranous margins; lower glume 3–4.5 mm, 5-veined, glabrous or stiffly hairy near margins and apex, apex acute; upper glume ca. 5 mm, 5–7-veined, glabrous, apex obtuse; sterile lemma subleathery, 5–6 mm, siliceous, 7–9-veined, apex obtuse with 1.5–2 mm awn; fertile lemma oblong with straight back, 6–7 mm, awn 1.5–2 mm; palea lanceolate, hyaline, 2-keeled, ca. 5 mm. Caryopsis 3.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 149, 2028; HK sheet 42059.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, S Korea, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Malesia.
Ecology: Shady slopes, roadsides and moist forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), animal food (fodder).

Lophostemon confertus (R. Br.) Peter G. Wilson & J. T. Waterh. 紅膠木
Austral. J. Bot. 30(4): 424. 1982; FOC 13: 329. 2007.
Tristania conferta R. Br., Hort. Kew. (ed. 2) 4: 417. 1811 [1812]; FGZ 208. 1956; FHN 2: 6, fig. 290. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 31, pl. 6: 1 –2. 1984; FGX 1: 899. 1991.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Bark blackish brown, ± persistent. Branchlets flat and angulate at first, later becoming terete, puberulous. Leaves clustered at apex of branches; petioles 1–2 cm, flat; blade leathery, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 7– 15 × 3 – 7 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, with pellucid oily dots adaxially, sometimes greyish abaxially; lateral veins 12– 18 pairs, slightly prominent abaxially, reticulate veins conspicuous. Cymes 2–3 cm, 3–7-flowered; peduncle 0.6–1.5 cm. Pedicels 3–6 mm. Hypanthium obconic, 4–5 mm, covered with greyish white silky hairs. Sepals triangular, 3–4 mm, apex sharply pointed. Petals obovate, ca. 6 mm, pubescent abaxially. Stamen bundles 1–1.2 cm; filaments partly distinct; anthers ca. 0.5 mm. Capsule semiglobose, 8–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 83, 825; HK sheet 40141.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan, and Yunnan (cultivated); native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Aug. – Sep.
Uses: Environmental, ornamental, timber.

Loropetalum chinense (R. Br.) Oliv. 檵木（紙末花）
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 23: 459. 1862; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 70, pl. 16. 1979; FGD 1: 160, fig. 176. 1987; FOC 9: 33. 2003.
Hamamelis chinensis R. Br. in G. F. Abel, Narr. Journey China 375. 1818.

Deciduous or semi-evergreen shrub or small tree, much branched; branchlets stellate-pubescent. Petioles 2–5 mm, stellatepubescent; leaf blade leathery, ovate, elliptic or, rarely obovate, 2–6.5 × 1–3 cm, base unequal, rounded or cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, sparsely pubescent adaxially, densely stellate-pubescent and slighty greyish abaxially; lateral veins 4–8 pairs. Flowers usually 3–8 arranged in a short spike or head; peduncle 0.8–1 cm, stellatepubescent; bracts linear, ca. 3 mm. Flowers shortly pedicellate. Floral cup cupular, stellate-pubescent, 1.2–1.5 mm. Sepals 4, ovate, 2–3 mm. Petals 4, white to slightly yellowish, 1–2 cm. Stamens 4, filaments very short, connective elongated into a horn, anthers ovoid, 0.5–0.6 mm; staminodes 4, scale-like, alternate with stamens. Ovary inferior, stellate-pubescent, styles very short. Capsules ovoid or obovoid-globose, 7–8 mm, adnate to floral cup, stellate-tomentose. Seeds ovoid-globose or ellipsoid, 4–7 × 3.5–4 mm.

Locality: North Point, Shing Mun, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 935; P. S. Choi 398.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River to Tropic of Cancer; Japan, India.
Ecology: Tickets. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Loropetalum chinense f. rubrum H. T. Chang (紅花檵木)(Photo 176) is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It differs from L. chinense by red petals.
records.uses:
Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Loropetalum chinense f. rubrum H. T. Chang (紅花檵木)(Photo 176) is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It differs from L. chinense by red petals.

Loropetalum subcordatum (Benth.) Oliv. 四藥門花
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 15: t. 1417. 1883; FKH 101. 1912; FOC 9: 33. 2003.
Tetrathyrium subcordatum Benth., FHK 133. 1861; FRPS 35(2): 68, pl. 15. 1979; FGD 1: 159, fig. 175. 1987.

Evergreen shrub or tree, to 12 m tall; branchlets glabrous. Stipules lanceolate, 5 – 6 mm, stellate-pubescent, caducous; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic, 7–12 × 3.5 –5 cm, base rounded or subcordate, apex acute, margin entire or sparsely serrulate on distal part; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Inflorescence axillary, 14 –25-flowered; peduncle 4 –5 cm; bracts linear. Flowers subsessile. Sepals 5, ca. 1.5 mm, stellate-pubescent. Petals 5, ca. 1.5 cm. Stamens 5, anthers ovoid; staminodes divergent. Ovary semiinferior, stellate-pubescent, styles very short, glabrous. Capsules subglobose, 10–12 mm in diam., adnate to floral cup, dehiscing into two valves. Seeds ovoid-ellipsoid, 6 –7 mm.

Locality: Jardine's Lookout, Bowen Rd., Wong Lung Hang. Y. W. Lam 281; P. Chow s.n. (HK sheet 38315).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Note: The type specimen was collected from “Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford between 1857 and 1858. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Ludisia discolor (Ker Gawl.) A. Rich. 血葉蘭（石蠶）
Dict. Class. Hist. Nat. 7: 437. 1825; FHN 4: 199, fig. 1089. 1977; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 47, fig. 18. 1977; FRPS 17: 157. 1999; FGD 7: 353, fig. 178. 2006; FOC 25: 55. 2009.
Goodyera discolor Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 4: 271. 1818.
Haemaria discolor (Ker Gawl.) Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. 490. 1840; FHK 361. 1861; FKH 267. 1912.

Saxicolous herb clinging onto bare damp rock; stem creeping, succulent, 8–15 cm, internodes 7–8 mm in diam.; ascending stems 12–40 cm tall, bearing 4–5 leaves with pink petioles, midrib and margin. Leaves oblong-elliptic, 2.5–6 × 1.2–2.5 cm, apex acute and mucronate, metallic green above, reddish maroon beneath. Flowers white; dorsal sepal and petals forming a white shell of 9–10 mm long and 3 mm wide; lateral sepals white with pink tips, ovate, 8 × 5 mm, twisted at base, turning backward; petals falcate, 8–10 × 2.5 mm, obtuse; lip white, saccate at base, adnate to the column, the apical lobe tongue-like, bilobed, one curving backward, the other stretching forward; column 3 mm, apical end enlarged, the sides and front extending forward, forming a twisted beak-like rostellum; anther elongate-ovate, yellow, fitting into the centre of the beak, apex acuminate; pollinia 2, tessellate; ovary hairy. Fruit an oblong capsule.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Sha Tin, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 13144, 13274 (CUHK); HK sheet 41805.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Ludwigia adscendens (L.) Hara 水龍
J. Jap. Bot. 28: 291. 1953; FYN 4: 187. 1986; FRPS 53(2): 35, pl. 10: 5 – 6. 2000; FGD 8: 6. 2007.
Jussiaea adscendens L., Mantissa 1: 69. 1767.
Jussiaea repens L., Sp. Pl. 1: 388. 1753; FHN 1: 430. 1965; FFJ 4: 141, fig. 120. 1989.

Perennial herb, with creeping or floating stems, rooting at nodes, with white, erect pneumatophores at nodes of floating stems. Terrestrial stems 20–60 cm, floating stems to 400 cm, much branched. Leaves alternate; petiole 5–20 mm; leaf blade oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, 2–5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, apex obtuse to subacute, margin entire, glabrous. Flowers solitary, white or pale yellow. Pedicels nearly as long as calyx-tube. Calyx-lobes 5, lanceolate, ca. 7 mm, glabrous or villous abaxially. Petals obovate, 9–18 × 6–10 mm. Stamens 10; filaments white, 2.5–4 mm; anthers 0.7–1.8 mm. Ovary sparsely villous abaxially; style 4–10 mm, glabrous; stigma capitate, 5-lobed. Capsules cylindrical or terete, light brown with dark brown ribs, 1.2–2.7 cm, 3–4 mm in diam., glabrous or villous, thickly walled, tardily and irregularly dehiscent. Seeds many, oblong or elliptic, pale brown, 1.1–1.3 mm, raphe inconspicuous.

Locality: Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Mui Tsz Lam, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2464; Y. S. Lau 694, 2159.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; S and SE Asia, Australia and Africa.
Ecology: Damp to wet places, marshes, margin of ponds. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ludwigia hyssopifolia (G. Don) Exell 草龍

Garcia de Orta 5: 471. 1957; Raven, Reinwardtia 6: 385. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 3: 955, pl. 478. 1993; FYN 4: 186, pl. 55: 11–13. 1986; FGD 8: 7. 2007.

Jussiaea hyssopifolia G. Don., Gen. Syst. 2: 693. 1832.

Jussiaea linifolia Vahl, Eclog. Am. 2: 32. 1798; FHN 1: 430.1965.


Annual erect herb, 0.6–2 m tall; stems often woody at base, 3–4-ridged at upper part, branched, puberulous when young. Petiole 0.2–1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate to linear, 2–10 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate, subglabrous or puberulous. Sepals 4, ovate-lanceolate, 2–4 mm, finely puberulous. Petals yellow, obovate to subelliptic, 2–3 × 1–2 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 8; anthers 0.4–0.6 mm; pollen in monads. Style 1–1.5 mm; stigma depressed-globose. Capsule 4-angled when young, subterete when mature, 1.5–3 cm, finely puberulous. Seeds in 2 or more rows per locule in upper capsule, in one row per locule in lower capsule.


Locality: Tai Lam Chung. H. C. Tang 1889.

Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; widespread in SE Asia, Africa, Australia, Pacific Islands and S America.

Ecology: Ditches, marshes and other damp to wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Notes: This species was recorded as Ludwigia prostrata Roxb. previously (Corlett et al. 2000; Check List HK Plants 165. 2002; 60. 2004.)

Ludwigia octovalvis (Jacq.) P. H. Raven 毛草龍
Kew Bull. 15: 476. 1962; FTW 3: 893, pl. 857. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 3: 958, pl. 479. 1993; FYN 4: 183, pl. 55: 1 –7. 1986; FRPS 53(2): 29, pl. 9: 1 –3. 2000; FGD 8: 6. 2007.
Oenothera octovalvis Jacq., Enum. Pl. Carib. 19. 1760.
Jussiaea suffruticosa L., Sp. Pl. 1: 388. 1753; FHN 1: 430. 1964; FFJ 4: 142. 1989.
Ludwigia pubescens (L.) H. Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 28(10): 293. 1953.

Perennial herb, up to 2 m tall. Stems erect, well-branched, densely hirsute at least on upper part, slightly ribbed. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–10 mm; leaf blade linear to subovate, 1–14 × 0.3–4 cm, base narrowly or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, entire, yellowish hirsute on both surfaces. Flowers solitary in leaf axils, large, yellow, sessile to subsessile. Calyx-tube slender; lobes 4, ovate or lanceolate, 6–15 mm, triveined. Petals 4, broadly obovate, 6–17 × 5–17 mm, apex emarginate. Stamens 8; filaments 1–4 mm; anthers 1.2–4 mm. Ovary 4-locular; style 1.5–3.5 mm; stigma subglobose, shallowly 4-lobed. Capsule cylindrical, terete, pale brown with 8 ribs, 1.7–4.5 cm, 2–8 mm in diam. Seeds many, in 2 or more rows per locule, free, brown, 0.6–0.75 mm, raphe inflated and equal to seed body in size, evenly transversely ridged.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Mai Po, Sheung Shui, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Po Toi Islands. Y. S. Lau 1278; P. S. Choi 345; Y. W. Lam 1045.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Africa, S and SW Asia, Australasia, Europe, N America, Pacific Islands, S America.
Ecology: Ditches, rice paddies and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Mar. –Nov.

Ludwigia perennis L. 細花丁香蓼
Sp. Pl. 1: 119. 1753; FTW 3: 897. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 3: 960, pl. 480. 1993; FYN 4: 184, pl. 55: 8– 10. 1986; FRPS 53(2): 32, pl. 9: 8. 2000; FGD 8: 7. 2007.
Jussiaea caryophyllea Lam., Encycl. 3: 331. 1789.
Jussiaea perennis (L.) Brenan, Kew Bull. 8: 163. 1953.
Ludwigia caryophyllea (Lam.) Merr. & Metcalf, Lingnan Sci. J. 16: 396. 1937; FHN 1: 428, fig. 234. 1964; FFJ 4: 139, fig. 119. 1989.

Annual erect herb, 15–100 cm tall, with taproot. Stems branched, often purplish, subglabrous. Petiole 2–15 mm, winged; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, 1–11 × 0.3–2.7 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex subacute. Flowers solitary in leaf axils, yellow, shortly pedicellate. Calyx-lobes 4(–5), lanceolate, (1.3–)2–3.5 mm, ± puberulent. Petals elliptic, 1–3 × 0.7–2 mm. Stamens as many as sepals, or rarely more; filaments 0.3 – 0.7 mm; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm. Style 0.7–1.5 mm; stigma globose. Capsule terete, often nodding, pale brown, 3–16(–19) mm, 2.5–5 mm in diam., glabrous or puberulent. Seeds many, in 2 or more rows per locule, free, brown with fine brown lines, 0.3–0.5 mm, raphe very narrow and inconspicuous.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 2379; HK sheet 11890, 11892.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; SE and SW Asia, Australia, Pacific Islands (New Caledonia).
Ecology: Rice paddies and other low moist to wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Nov.

Luffa acutangula (L.) Roxb. 廣東絲瓜（絲瓜）
Hort. Beng. 70. 1814; FKH 112. 1912; FRPS 73(1): 196. 1986; FFJ 5: 251, fig. 235. 1993; FGD 3: 123, fig. 86. 1995.
Cucumis acutangula L., Sp. Pl. 1011. 1753.

Stems stout, sulcate and angled, pubescent. Tendrils often trifid. Petioles 8–12 cm; leaf blade membranous, suborbicular in outline, often 5–7-lobed, 15–20 × 15–20 cm, base cordate, apex acute, margin sparsely dentate, slightly scabrous on both surfaces, sometimes with raised white spots adaxially. Male flowers: 17–20 arranged in racemes; peduncles 10 –15 cm; pedicels 1– 4 cm; calyx-tube campanulate, 5–8 × 10 mm, lobes lanceolate, 4–6 × 2–3 mm, slightly reflexed; corolla rotate, lobes obcordate, 2 × 2–2.5 cm, apex emarginate; stamens 3, filaments 4–5 mm, anthers puberulous. Female flowers: ovary clavate, ridged. Fruits cylindric or clavate, 8 –12-ribbed and sulcate, glabrous, 15 –75 cm long, 6 –10 cm in diam., dark green, scabrous. Seeds ovate, black, 1–1.2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, margin not winged.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 520; HK sheet 12028, 12030.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Luffa aegyptiaca Mill. 水瓜
Gard. Dict. ed. 8. 1768.
Luffa cylindrica (L.) Roem., Syn. Mon. 2: 63. 1846; FRPS 73(1): 194. 1986; FFJ 5: 250, fig. 234. 1993; FGD 3: 124. 1995.
Momordica cylindrica L., Sp. Pl. 1009. 1753.

Stems and branches scabrous, ridged and sulcate. Tendrils usually trifid. Petioles scabrous, 4–12 cm, puberulous; leaf blade triangular or suborbicular in outline, base cordate, 10–25 × 10–25, often palmately 5–7-lobed, lobes triangular, apex acute or acuminate, margin dentate, puberulous on both surfaces, white punctate adaxially. Male flowers: usually 15 –20-flowers in a raceme; peduncles stout, 10 –15 cm, pubescent; pedicels 1–2 cm; calyx broadly campanulate, 5 –9 mm, puberulous, lobes ovate-lanceolate or nearly triangular, 1cm; corolla rotate, 5 –9 cm in diam., lobes oblong-cuneate, 2– 4 × 2–2.8 cm, densely yellow-white-villous adaxially, apex rounded to truncate, base attenuate. Stamens 5, filaments 6 – 8 mm. Female flowers: pedicels 2–10 cm; ovary long cylindrical, puberulous, stigmas 3, expanded, bifid. Fruit cylindrical, straight or slightly curved, 15–55 cm, grooved or striped, not ridged, puberulous, strongly fibrous inside when mature. Seeds ovate, smooth, black, margin slightly winged.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 332; Y. S. Lau 2627, 2618.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Lumnitzera racemosa Willd. 欖李
Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Neue Schriften 4: 187. 1803; FHN 2: 43. 1965; FTW 3: 875, pl. 850. 1977; FRPS 53(1): 15. 1984; FGD 3: 199, fig. 137. 1995.

Shrub or small tree, to 8 m tall, ca. 30 cm in diam.; bark brown or greyish black, rough; branchlets red or greyish black, with conspicuous leaf scars, pubescent when young, glabrescent. Leaves often fasciculate at apex of branches, sessile or shortly petiolate; leaf blade spatulate or narrowly obovate, 4.5–6.5(–7) × 1.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex rotund or slightly emarginate, thick, fleshy, green when fresh, yellowish brown when dry; lateral veins 2–4 on each side of midvein. Racemes axillary, 2–6 cm, 6–12-flowered; peduncle compressed; bracteoles 2, scalelike, triangular, persistent. Calyx-tube prolonged well beyond ovary, ca. 5 mm; lobes 5, triangular, 1–2 mm. Petals white, fragrant, elliptic, 4.5–5 × 1.5 mm. Stamens 5 or 10, nearly as long as petals, filaments 4–5 mm, slightly flattened at base, apex curved, anthers small, ellipsoidal. Ovary fusiform, 6–8 mm; ovules 2–4; style terete, 4 mm. Fruit ovoid or fusiform, laterally compressed, woody, 1.4–2 cm, 5–8 mm in diam., 2–3-ribbed.

Locality: Aberdeen, Nai Chung, Kei Ling Ha, Yung Shue O, Plover Cove, Ting Kok, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 80; HK sheet 1727, 31563.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Mangroves. Flowering & fruiting: Dec. –Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Timber.

Lycianthes biflora (Lour.) Bitter 紅絲線
Abh. Naturwiss. Vereine Bremen 24: 461. 1920; FHN 3: 466, fig. 859. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 122, pl. 30. 1978; FGD 2: 383, fig. 263. 1991; FOC 17: 326. 1994; FTW 2, 4: 552, pl. 252, photo 295. 1998.
Solanum biflorum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 129. 1790.
Solanum decemdentatum Roxb., Hort. Beng. 16. 1814; Fl. Ind. 2: 247. 1824; FKH 243. 1861.

Erect herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Branchlets, petioles, pedicels and calyx densely covered with pale yellow, simple hairs and mixed with 1–2‑rayed hairs. Leaves solitary or the upper unequal paired; petioles 0.5–4 cm, narrowly winged; leaf blade sparsely pubescent adaxially, denser and mixed with 1–2‑rayed hairs abaxially; blade of the larger leaves elliptic‑ovate to oblong, 9–15 × 3.5–7 cm, base cuneate and decurrent to the petioles, apex acuminate; blade of smaller leaves broadly ovate, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex shortly acuminate. Flowers usually 2, rarely 3–6 fascicled in axils of leaves; pedicels 5–13 mm. Calyx broadly campanulate, ca. 5 mm, with 10 subulate teeth. Corolla white or pale purple; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate to narrowly ovate, ca. 6 × 1.5 mm. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers ca. 3 mm, opening by subapical and introrse pores. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style slender, ca. 8 mm. Berry globose, 6–8 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Wang Shan Keuk Ha Tsuen. Y. S. Lau 302, 2306; L. T. Lo 648.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; S and SE Asia to Malaysia.
Ecology: Ravines, streamsides and other wet places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Lycium chinense Mill. 枸杞
Gard. Dict. ed. 8, no. 5. 1768; FHK 245. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FHN 3: 470, fig. 862. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 15, pl. 3: 1–4. 1978; FGD 2: 364, fig. 247. 1991; FFJ 5: 5, fig. 3. 1993; FTW ed. 2, 4: 557, pl. 254, photo 297. 1998.

Shrubs, 50–100 cm tall, glabrous, much branched; branches often with spines. Leaves alternate, or in clusters of 2–4; petioles 4–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate‑oblong or obovate, 1.5–5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire. Flowers solitary or in pairs on long shoots, or clustered with leaves on short shoots. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Calyx 3–4 mm, 3–5‑lobed. Corolla funnelform, 9–12 mm, pale purple, limb broadly campanulate, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate, apex rounded. Stamens 5, exserted. Berries ovoid or shortly oblong, 7–15 mm, orange‑red.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1508; L. T. Lo 50; HK sheet 34820.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Korea and Japan.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Lycopersicon esculentum Mill. 番茄
Gard. Dict. ed. 8, no. 2. 1768; FHN 3: 467. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 137, pl. 35. 1978; FGD 2: 385, fig. 264. 1991; FOC 17: 329. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 557. 1998.

Annual herbs, erect or sprawling, 1–2 m tall, viscid pubescent and strong‑smelling. Leaves odd‑pinnate, ovate‑oblong in outline, unequal, 10–35 cm or longer; leaflets usually 5–9, ovate or oblong, 5–7(–12) × 2–5 cm, base oblique, apex acuminate, margin irregularly toothed or lobed. Cymes lateral, 5–8 cm, 3–7‑flowered; peduncles 2–4 cm; pedicels 1–1.5 cm. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate. Corolla rotate, yellow, ca. 2 cm in diam. Berry red or yellow, usually subglobose, flattened at the ends.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 5341, 9025, 12904 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico and S America; widely cultivated throughout the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (vegetable, fruit).

Lyonia ovalifolia (Wall.) Drude var. hebecarpa (Franch. ex Forb. & Hemsl.) W. Y. Chun 毛果珍珠花
Sunyatsenia 4: 253. 1940; FOC 14: 463. 2005
Pieris ovalifolia (Wall.) D. Don var. hebecarpa Franch. ex Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 17. 1889.
Xolisma ovalifolia (Wall.) Rehd. var. hebecarpa (Franch. ex Forb. & Hemsl.) Metcalf, J. Arnold Arbor. 12(4): 275. 1931.

Shrub, deciduous or semi-deciduous, 1–2(–4) m tall. Branchlets, petioles, abaxial surface of leaves inflorescence puberulent. Buds narrowly ovoid, 4–7 × 3–4 mm, glabrous. Leaves papery; petioles 2–8 mm; leaf blade ovate, ovate-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 3–7.5 × 1.5–4 cm, base usually rounded, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, adaxial surface glabrescent; midvein and secondary veins prominently raised on abaxial surface. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate, terminal or axillary, 5–7(–20) cm. Pedicel 2–5 mm, with 1–3 leafy bracts near base. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes ovate to triangular-lanceolate, ca. 1.4 × 1.2 mm. Corolla white, tubular or tubular-urceolate, 8–10 mm, shortly 5-lobed. Stamens 10; filaments with a pair of appendages near apex. Ovary ovoid, densely puberulent. Capsule subglobose, 3–5 mm in diam.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1398; Y. W. Lam 1290; K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 38879).
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Very rare locally, only several plants were found in shrublands at open exposed rocky cliffs, alt. ca. 450 m. Flowering: May; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Lyonia ovalifolia is a highly variable species with up to six varieties differs slightly in leaf shape and hair covers being distinguished in China. At least three of them (var. ovalifolia, var. hebecarpa, and var. lanceolata) have almost overlapping ranges and were recorded in Guangdong. Among them, var. hebecarpa only differs from the other two varieties in having pubescent, instead of glabrous, ovary and capsule. The typical variety (var. ovalifolia) is very variable and therefore needs further studies to ascertain the taxonomic status.

records.text:
Lysidice rhodostegia Hance 儀花
J. Bot. 5(58): 299. 1867; FRPS 39: 204, pl. 71: 1 – 5. 1988; FGD 5: 197. 2003; FGX 2: 489, pl. 207: 1 – 5. 2005.

Shrubs or trees, 2–5(–10) m tall. Petiolules short and thick, 2–3 mm; leaflets 3–5 pairs, papery, long-elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 5– 16 × 2– 6.5 cm, base obtuse, apex caudate; lateral veins slender, subparallel, conspicuous on both surfaces. Panicles 20 –40 cm, rachis, bracts and bracteoles pubescent; bracts and bracteoles pink, ovate-oblong or elliptic; bracts 1.2 – 2.8 × 0.5 – 1.4 cm; bracteoles 2 –5 mm. Calyx-tube 1.2–1.5 cm, 1/3 longer than lobes; calyx-lobes oblong, dark purplish red. Petals purplish red, broadly ovate, ca. 1.2 cm, apex obtuse and emarginate. Fertile stamens 2, anthers ca. 4 mm; staminodes often 4, subulate. Ovary hairy, ovules 6 – 9; styles slender, hairy. Pods obovate-oblong, 12 – 20 cm, base slightly oblique, sutures unequal, dehiscent; valves often coiled. Seeds 2 – 7, brownish red, oblong, 2.2 – 2.5 × 1.2 – 1.5 cm, margin not thickened; seed-coat thin and rigid, slightly wrinkled.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2577, 2586, 3220.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Lysimachia alpestris Champ. ex Benth. 香港過路黃
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 299. 1852; FHK 202. 1861; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 552. 1987; FRPS 59(1): 98, pl. 26: 5. 1989; FOC 15: 56. 1996.

Perennial herb, stiffy hairy throughout. Stem extremely abbreviated, 1–4 cm tall, often emitting runners. Leaves subsessile, spirally arranged, ± forming a rosette on stems and apex of runners; leaf blade spathulate to narrowly oblanceolate, 3 –6 × 0.6–1.5 cm, apex rounded and mucronate, tapering toward base. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels ca. as long as to slightly longer than leaves. Calyx lobes lanceolate, 5– 6 × 2 mm, apex acute. Corolla yellow, deeply parted; tube 1–1.5 mm; lobes obovate-elliptic, 4–15 mm wide, apex rounded, erose. Filaments ca. 3 mm, connate into a tube at base; anthers dorsifixed, opening by lateral slits.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1449, 230; C. P. Choi 460.
Distribution: Outside Hong Kong only found in Gu Dou Shan (Xin Hui Xian) of Guangdong province.
Ecology: Damp places on banks of streams, secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Lysimachia candida Lindl. 澤珍珠菜
J. Hort. Soc. London 1: 301. 1846; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 552. 1987; FRPS 59 (1): 127. 1989; FOC 15: 77. 1996.

Annual or biennial glabrous herb, 10–30 cm tall. Stems erect, simple or branched from base. Basal leaves spatulate to oblanceolate, 2.6–6 × 0.5–2 cm, with winged petioles, usually withered before anthesis; stem leaves alternate, rarely subopposite, sessile or subsessile; leaf blade obovate to oblanceolate or linear, 1–5 × 0.2–1.2 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate to obtuse, with sparse black or reddish glandular dots on both surfaces. Racemes terminal, initially short and coniform, lengthening to 5 –10 cm in fruiting. Bracts linear, 4 – 6 mm. Pedicels ca. two times as long as bracts, the lowest to 1.5 cm. Calyx lobes lanceolate, 3–5 mm, with black glandular stripes abaxially, margin membranous. Corolla white, 6 –12 mm, divided to middle; lobes oblong to oblong-obovate, apex rounded. Stamens slightly shorter than corolla lobes; anthers dorsifixed, opening by lateral slits. Capsule subglobose, 2–3 mm in diam.

Locality: So Kon Po. HK sheet 2834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Cultivated areas, banks of ditches, rice paddies and other wet places. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Lysimachia decurrens Forst. f. 延葉珍珠菜
Fl. Ins. Austr. 12. 1786; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 552, fig. 633. 1987; FRPS 59(1): 120. 1989; FOC 15: 73. 1996; C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 161. 1999.

Perennial herb, 40–90 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, with raised lines descending from the base of leaf petioles, usually much branched. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–4 cm, narrowly winged; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic lanceolate, 6–13 × 1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, with scattered black glandular dots or short stripes on both surfaces, especially near margins. Racemes terminal, 10 –25 cm. Bracts subulate, 2–3 mm. Pedicels 2–9 mm, lengthening to 10 –18 mm in fruit. Calyx split nearly to base; lobes narrowly lanceolate, 3 – 4 mm, glandular ciliate, with black glandular stripes abaxially. Corolla white or tinged purple; tube ca. 1.5 mm; lobes oblong-spathulate, 1–2.5 mm, apex rounded. Stamens long-exserted; anthers ovoid, purple, ca. 1 mm. Ovary ovoid; style slender, ca. 5 mm. Capsule globose or slightly compressed, 3– 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Tsat Muk Kiu, Luk Keng, Lantau Island. K. Y. Tam 141; Y. W. Lam 664; L. T. Lo 55.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, damp places by streams, wastelands near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May.

Lysimachia fortunei Maxim. 紅根草
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 12: 68. 1868; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 551, fig. 632. 1987; FRPS 59(1): 104, pl. 27: 6 –10. 1989; FOC 15: 71. 1996.

Perennial glabrous herb, with creeping, reddish rhizomes. Stems erect, 30 –70 cm tall, terete, usually unbranched, with black glandular dots. Leaves alternate, subsessile; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, 4 –11 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, with many scattered glandular dots on both surface when dry. Racemes slender, 10–20 cm. Bracts lanceolate, 2–3 mm. Pedicels as long as to slightly shorter than bracts. Calyx lobes ovate-elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, apex obtuse, margin membranous. Corolla white, ca. 3 mm, divided slightly below middle; lobes elliptic to ovate-elliptic, with black glandular dots, apex rounded. Stamens included; filaments adnate to base of corolla lobes; anthers dorsifixed, opening by lateral slits. Capsule globose, 2–2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 2832.

Macaranga lowii King ex Hook. f. 刺果血桐

Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 453. 1887.

Macaranga auriculata (Merr.) Airy Shaw, Kew Bull. 19(2): 325. 1965; FRPS 44(2): 61. 1996; FGD 5: 84. 2003.

Tree, 5–10 m tall; branchlets hairy when young. Female flowers: pedicels 1–6 mm, pubescent; sepals 3–4, lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, hairy, persistent; ovary soft-echinate, 2-locular; styles 2, linear, 7–12 mm, connate at near base, papillose. Locality: Aberdeen,Wu Kau Tang, Tai Po Kau. Y. W. Lam 175, 203, 494.

Macaranga sampsonii Hance 鼎湖血桐

Macaranga tanarius (L.) Müll. Arg. var. tomentosa (Blume) Müll. Arg. 血桐

Machaerina ensigera (Hance) T. Koyama 劍葉莎

Cladium ensigerum Hance, J. Bot. 23: 80. 1885; FKH 302. 1912; FRPS 11: 119. 1961.

Machaerina rubiginosa (Spreng.) T. Koyama 圓葉劍葉莎
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 69: 65. 1956; FOC 23: 259. 2010.
Schoenus rubiginosus Sol. ex G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 89. 1786.
Fuirena rubiginosa Spreng., Mant. Prima Fl. Hal. 29. 1807.
Cladium glomeratum auct. non R. Br. ex C. B. Clarke: FKH 302. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome short, emitting long horizontal stolons covered with 2-ranked, pale, lanceolate scales. Culms tufted, slender, compressed-biconvex to subterete, usually with 1 node above the base, smooth, (30–)100–180 cm tall, (2–)3–6 mm thick. Basal leaves shorter than to about as long as stems, erect, biconvex with obtuse edges to subterete, smooth, pungent, spongiose inside, (2–)4–7 mm wide; cauline leaf long-sheathing, with short blade. Panicle erect, narrow, dense or interrupted, (10–)20–50 cm, consisting of 3–7 fascicles of branches, the lower branches distant, subtended by long-sheathing, shortly laminate bracts; upper branches approximate, their bracts gradually shorter. Lower branches often solitary, up to 25 cm, upper ones 2–4 together, erect, rigid, scabrous, much shorter. Spikelets in oblong to almost globose clusters, lanceolate or finally ovate, 2–3-flowered, maturing 1–2 achenes, 4–7 × 2–2.5 mm. Glumes 5, ovate to lanceolate, acuminate, long-ciliate, the longest 4.5–6.5 mm. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm, with distinctly produced connective. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to oblong-ellipsoidal, trigonous, sessile, smooth, shining, orange to reddish-brown, 3–5 × 1.5–2 mm, densely pubescent, persistent style base included.

Distribution: Yunnan; Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, India, Indoneasia, Philippines, New Guinea, Japan, New Zealand, Australia.
