Maclura cochinchinensis (Lour.) Corner 構棘（葨芝）
Gard. Bull. Singapore 19: 239. 1962; FOC 5: 35. 2003.
Cudrania cochinchinensis (Lour.) Kudo & Masam., Annual Rep. Taihoku Bot. Gard. 2: 27. 1932; FHN 2: 379. 1965; FGD 1: 180. 1987; FRPS 23(1): 58. 1998.
Vanieria cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 564. 1790.
Cudrania rectispina Hance, J. Bot. 365. 1876; FKH 247. 1912.
Cudrania javanensis Tréc, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 3, 8: 123. 1847.

Erect or scandent shrub. Branches glabrous, with axillary spines. Petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaves alternate, leathery, ellipticlanceolate or oblong, 3– 8 × 2–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–10 pairs. Head axillary, yellowish, 6–10 mm in diam., glabrous. Flowers dioecious, bracts subulate, with 2 yellow glands inside. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 4, unequal; stamens 4, pistillodes subulate or peltate. Female flowers: bracts tomentose; perianth-lobes 4, free or connate below; style 2-lobed, stigma filiform. Syncarp orange, globose, 2–5 cm in diam., slightly hairy; achenes ovoid, brown.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Au Mun, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 29810, 31248.
Distribution: SW to SE China; E Africa, E, S & SE Asia to Australia, New Caledonia.
Ecology: Open thickets, forests, near villages. Flowering and fruiting: May–Nov.

Maclura tricuspidata Carr. 柘樹
Rev. Hort. 390. 1864; FOC 5: 36. 2003.
Cudrania tricuspidata (Carr.) Bureau ex Lavallée, Arb. Segrez. 243. 1877; FGD 1: 181. 1987; FRPS 23(1): 63. 1998; Check List HK Plants 61. 2002.

Deciduous shrub or small tree, 1–7 m tall. Branchlets slightly angulate, with spines. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves ovate or rhomboidovate, 5 –14 × 3– 6 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire or occasionally trilobed, green-white and glabrous or pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 4 – 6 pairs. Head globose, solitary or paired, axillary; peduncles short. Male heads 5 mm in diam., bracts 2, adnated on perianth-lobes. Male flowers: perianth-lobes fleshy, apex thick, involute, with yellow glands; stamens 4, pistillode subulate. Female heads: 10–15 mm in diam. Female flowers: perianth-lobes shield-shaped at apex, others as in male one. Syncarp orange, subglobose, ca. 2.5 cm in diam., fleshy.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9536.
Distribution: S Hebei; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Early summer; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Leaves for feeding silkworms, medicinal (folklore).

Macrosolen cochinchinensis (Lour.) Tiegh. 鞘花（苞花寄生）
Bull. Soc. Bot. France. 41: 122. 1894; FYN 3: 350, pl. 101: 1– 2. 1983; FGD 1: 216, fig. 247. 1987; FRPS 24: 89. 1988; FOC 5: 221. 2003.
Elytranthe cochinchinensis (Lour.) G. Don, Gen. Hist. 3: 426. 1834; Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 69. 1927; FHN 2: 463. 1965.
Loranthus ampullaceus Roxb., Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 220. 1824; FKH 229. 1912.
Loranthus fordii Hance, J. Bot. 23: 38. 1885; FKH 229. 1912.
Loranthus cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 195. 1790.

Shrub 0.5–1.3 m tall. Branches greyish white, scattered lenticellate. Petiole 0.5–1 cm; leaf blade leathery, broadly elliptic to lanceolate, 4–12 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate, lateral veins 4–5 pairs, reticulate veinlets obscure on both surfaces. Inflorescences racemose, solitary or 2 –3-fasciculate, axillary, (2–)4–8-flowered; peduncle ca. 2 cm; bracts suborbicular, 1–2 mm; bracteoles triangular, connate at base, 1–1.5 mm, slightly shorter than bracts. Pedicels 4–6 mm. Calyx ellipsoidal, 2–2.5 mm, limb annular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla orange, straight, 1.2–1.5 cm, inflated at lower part, 6-angled, lobes lanceolate, ca. 6–7 mm, reflexed. Filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers ca. 1 mm. Fruit yellowish red, subglobose, ca. 8 mm.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Ting Kok Rd., Sha Tau Kok. W. J. Tutcher 9241; Y. S. Lau 2484; Y. W. Lam 28.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian; Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, New Guinea, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Often growing on trees of Schima superba and Cunninghamia lanceolata. Flowering: Feb. – Jun.; fruiting: May –Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Maesa japonica (Thunb.) Moritzi & Zoll. 杜莖山
Syst. Verz. 3: 61.1855; FRPS 58: 27.1979; FOC 15: 7. 1996.
Doraena japonica Thunb., Nov. Gen. Pl. 3: 59. 1783; Fl. Jap. 84. 1784.
Maesa coriacea Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 300. 1852; FHK 204. 1861.
Maesa doraena Blume ex Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math.-Phys. 4: 138. 1846; FKH 158. 1912.

Shrub 1–3(–5) m tall, glabrous throughout; branchlets wrinkled with longitudinal lines when dry, sparsely lenticellate. Leaves alternate; petioles channelled, 6–12 mm; leaf blade generally elliptic but variable from elliptic-lanceolate to obovate or oblong-ovate, (5–)7–12(–15) × 2–4(–5) cm, base cuneate to obtuse or sometimes rounded, apex acuminate or acute, subentire or remotely serrate with callose teeth, leathery, without veinlike glandular lines; lateral veins 5–8 pairs, curved-ascending, ending in the teeth; reticulation of veins very fine, but visible on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, solitary or sometimes 2–3 together, 1–3(–4) cm, racemose or with a few branches near base. Pedicels 2–3 mm, with a pair of minute bracteoles near apex. Calyx ca. 2 mm, split to middle; lobes ovate to orbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, distinctly glandular striate. Corolla white, tubular-campanulate; tube 3.5–4 mm, glandular striate; lobes ca. 1/3 length of tube, ovate or reniform, apex obtuse or rounded, ± spreading. Stamens adnate to upper part of corolla-tube, included; anthers oblong or ovate, as long as filaments. Ovary conical; style slender, ca. equaling calyx; stigma lobed. Fruit globose, 4–5 mm in diam., fleshy, with longitudinal glandular lines.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 56, 1078, 1174; P. S Choi 364; Y. W. Lam 510.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets on hillsides. Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–May.
Notes: Flowers of this species are functionally unisexual, but with limited sexual dimorphism; the staminate flowers possess carpels with aborted ovules, and the pistillate flowers have degenerate stamens that lack pollens. The type specimen of Maesa coriacea was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Maesa montana A. DC. 金珠柳
Prodr. 8: 79. 1844; FHK 204. 1861; FRPS 58: 18. 1979; FOC 15: 3. 1996.
Maesa indica auct. non (Rox.) A. DC.: FHK 203. 1861.
Maesa tenera auct. non Mez: FKH 158. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees, 2–3(–10) m high; branchlets generally sparsely pilose or puberulent, sometimes glabrous, with scattered lenticels when mature. Leaves alternate; petioles channelled, 5 –10 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, rarely broadly ovate, 7–16 × 3 –7 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, coarsely serrate or undulate-dentate, with callose teeth, firmly papery, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface glabrescent or occasionally sparingly hirsute, especially on veins; glandular nervilliform lines invisible or sometimes evident; lateral veins 8–12 pairs, curved-ascending, ending to the teeth; veinlets not evident. Inflorescence axillary, racemose or paniculate, 2–7(–10) cm, sparingly hirtellous or puberulent. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 1 mm. Pedicels 1–2(–3) mm, with a pair of minute ovate or lanceolate bracteoles at apex. Calyx split a little below middle; lobes ovate, ca. 0.6 mm, obtuse, minutely ciliate. Corolla white, lobed to middle; lobes broadly ovate or suborbicular, ca. 1 m wide, apex obtuse or rounded, entire or slightly crenulate. Stamens adnate to middle of corolla-tube, included; anthers suborbicular, ca. 0.25 mm, equaling filaments. Pistil slightly longer than calyx; stigma minutely bilobed. Fruit globose or ovoid, 2.5 – 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sha Tau Kok. F. W. Xing 8212, 8468 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests, hillsides and stream banks. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Maesa perlarius (Lour.) Merr. 鯽魚膽
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc., n. ser. 24. 298. 1935; FRPS 58: 25. 1979; K. Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 173. 1996; FOC 15: 6. 1996.
Dartus perlarius Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 124. 1790.
Maesa tonkinensis Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236 (Heft 9): 30. 1902.
Maesa sinensis A. DC., Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 2, 16: 80. 1841; FHK 203. 1861; FKH 158. 1912.

Shrub 1–3 m high; branchlets hirtellous or pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles channelled, 5–10 mm; leaf blade elliptic to ellipticlanceolate, 7–11 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or abruptly acuminate, coarsely serrate except for a short distance near base, papery, adaxial surface hirsute or pilose when young, rapidly becoming glabrous except midvein, abaxial surface hirsute, especially on veins; lateral veins 7–9 pairs, raised abaxialy, curved-ascending, ending to the callose teeth. Inflorescence axillary, racemose or paniculate (with 2–3 branches near base), hirtellous or pubescent, 1–5 cm. Pedicels 1.5–2 mm, with a pair of small ovate bracteoles at apex. Calyx ca. 1 mm, split below middle; lobes ovate, acute, ciliate, puberulous abaxially. Corolla white, ca. 2 mm, lobed to middle; lobes broadly ovate to suborbicular, obtuse, with brown glandular lines. Stamens inserted on the upper part of corolla-tube; anthers broadly ovate to reniform, not punctate. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 0.75 mm; stigma obscurely 4-lobed. Fruit globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., striate from the elongated vertical glands.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 32, 520; E. D. Merrill 10961; Lei 356; Xing 7144 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Margins of forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Dec.–May.

Magnolia grandiflora L. 荷花玉蘭（洋玉蘭）
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1802. 1759; FHN 1: 224. 1964; FGD 1: 8, fig. 7. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 125. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 30 m in native place; bark pale brown or grey, thin scaly fissured; twigs, buds, abaxial surfaces of leaves and petioles densely brown or greyish brown tomentellate. Petioles 1.5–4 cm, without stipular scar, deeply furrowed. Leaves elliptic, oblongelliptic or obovate-oblong, 10–20 × 4–7(–10) cm, thickly leathery, base cuneate, apex obtuse or mucronate, adaxially deep green, glossy; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers erect, white, fragrant, 15–20 cm in diam.; tepals 9–12, thickly fleshy, obovate, 6–10 × 5–7 cm; stamens ca. 2 cm, filaments flat, purple, anthers introrse, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium ellipsoid, densely tomentose; carpels ovoid, 1–1.5 cm, styles reclinate. Aggregate fruit terete or ovoid, 7–10 × 4–5 cm, densely brown or pale greyish yellow tomentose; follicles dehiscing along dorsal sutures, abaxially rounded, apex long-beaked; seeds ovoid, ca. 14 × 6 mm; testa red.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 773, 23652.
Distribution: Cultivated in S China; native to SE region of N America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Mahonia oiwakensis Hayata 海島十大功勞
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6: 1. 1916; Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 175. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 2: 583, pl. 279, photo 254 –255. 1996; FRPS 29: 220, pl. 42. 2001.
Berberis nepalensis auct. non Spreng.: FKH 32. 1912.
Mahonia hainanensis C. M. Hu et al., Guihaia 14 (1): 18. 1994.

Evergreen shrub, 1–7 m tall. Leaves crowded at apex of stems, odd-pinnate, narrowly oblong-elliptic in outline, 15 – 42 × 8 –15 cm; leaflets 12–20 pairs, sessile, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 2–10 × 1–2.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute to acuminate, margin with 2–9 spinulose teeth on each side, adaxially dark green, abaxially yellowish green; terminal leaflet petiolulate or sometimes sessile. Racemes fascicled, upright, 9 –25 cm. Pedicels (2–)5 – 6 mm. Flowers golden yellow, outer perianth-segments ovate to elliptic, inner ones oblong, 4.5 – 6.5 × 22.7 mm, with 2 glands at the base, apex bilobed; stamens 3 – 4 mm; ovary 3 – 4 mm, with 2–3 ovules; style very short. Fruit ovoid, 5 – 6 mm in diam., blue to blue-black, white-farinose.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2812; L. T. Lo 328.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang.
Ecology: Forests by streams. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Malaisia scandens (Lour.) Planch. 牛筋藤
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. Ser. 4, 3: 293. 1855; FHN 1: 377. 1964; FGD 1: 177. 1987; FOC 5: 27. 2003.
Caturus scandens Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 612. 1790.
Trophis scandens (Lour.) Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 214. 1836.

Climbing shrub. Branchlets slender, with white lenticels. Petioles 3 mm; leaves alternate, papery, oblong or elliptic-obovate, 5–12 × 2–4.5 cm, base rounded to shallow-cordate, asymmetric, apex acute, margin entire or obscurely serrate, slightly rough abaxially; lateral veins 7–12 pairs. Male spikes cylindric, solitary or 2– 4-clustered; peduncles 2– 4 cm; bracts connate at base. Male flowers: perianth 3–4-lobed, lobes triangular , pubescent; stamens as many as perianth-lobes and opposite to them, anther subglobose; pistillodes minute; female heads 3–5 in clusters, subglobose, ca. 6 mm in diam., densely pubescent; bracts crowded; peduncles ca. 10 mm, hairy. Female flowers: perianth urceolate, 1–1.5 mm, enlarged later; ovary included; style 2-fid, filiform, 10 –13 mm. Achenes red, ovoid, 6–8 mm.

Locality: Man Kam To, Tai O, Fan Lau, Shui Hou, Tong Fuk, Tai A Chau. HK sheet 36190, 36496.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Thickets or forests, often on trees and rocks.
Uses: Fibre.

Malaxis acuminata D. Don 淺裂沼蘭（紫盾沼蘭）
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 29. 1825; FRPS 18: 116, pl. 20: 5–6. 1999.
Crepidium acuminatum (D. Don) Szlach., Fragm. Florist. Geobot. Suppl. 3: 123. 1995; FOC 25: 233. 2009.
Malaxis allanii S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 18, fig. 9. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 79. 1977.

Terrestrial or half-epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs fleshy, cylindrical, 4–9 mm in diam., articulate, covered by ochreous dried leaf sheaths. Leaves 3–5, oblique-ovate or elliptic, 6–10 × 3–5 cm, base attenuating into a petiole, apex acuminate; petiole sheath-like, 2–4 cm, lower portion amplexicaul. Flowers purplish red, 1.5 cm in diam.; odd sepal linear, 8–10 × 2 mm, apex obtuse, margin recurved; lateral sepals oblong, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, apex obtuse, margin recurved; petals linear, 8–10 × 1 mm, margin recurved; lip ovate-oblong or obovate-oblong, 1 cm, the basal lobes pointing from the middle downwards, the apical lobe faintly cleft at the tip; column very short, 1–1.5 mm; anther suborbicular, wax-yellow and red at the base; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy; ovary 6-striate and sulcate, curved downwards.

Locality: Tai Tam, Repulse Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 1355 (holotype of M. allanii S. Y. Hu), 13010 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2993.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Indonesia, Java, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Forests and ravines. Flowering: Jun.
Notes: The type specimen of M. allanii (S. Y. Hu 13551, K, holotype; A, CUHK, isotype) was collected by W. G. L. Allen from Repulse Bay in 1969.

Malaxis latifolia Sm. 闊葉沼蘭

Rees Cyclop. 22. Malaxis n. 3. 1812; FHN 4: 207, fig. 1096. 1977; FRPS 18: 111. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 964, pl. 409. 2000; FGD 7: 455, fig. 228. 2006.

Dienia congesta Lindl., Bot. Reg. 10: sub t. 825. 1824; FHK 352. 1861.

Dienia ophrydis (J. Koenig) Ormerod & Seidenf., Contr. Orchid. Fl. Thailand 13: 18. 1997; FOC 25: 235. 2009.

Microstylis congesta (L.) Rchb. f., Walp. Ann 6: 206. 1861; FKH 260. 1912.

Malaxis parvissima S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 22, fig. 10. 1976.


Terrestrial or half-epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs fleshy, cylindrical, 3–11 cm, articulate, covered by the sheathing base of degenerated leaves. Leaves 4–5, oblique ovate-elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–17 × 3–8 cm, base attenuating into a petiole, apex acuminate; petiole sheath-like, 3–5 cm, amplexicaul. Flowers purplish red or greenish yellow, non-resupinate; odd sepal narrowly oblong, 3–5 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, curved inward and forward, 2–3 × 1–2 mm, apex obtuse; petals linear, 3–4 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse; lip dark purplish red, 2–3 × 2.5 mm, 3-lobed; midlobe narrowly ovate, 0.5–1 mm, apex obtuse; lateral lobes very short or not obvious, apex obtuse; column very short, 1.5 mm; anther 2-celled, sunk in the apical cavity of the column, attached at the back; pollinia 4, in 2 obovoid pairs, waxy; ovary very short, green with 6 purple cristate ridges, not twisted nor sulcate.


Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 3305.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina, Malesia, Australia.

Ecology: Along banks of streams in wooded areas. Flowering: May–Jul.

Notes: The type specimen of M. parvissima (S. Y. Hu 12453, K, holotype; A, CUHK, isotype) was collected by W. G. L. Allen from Tai Mo Shan in 1972.

Mallotus apelta (Lour.) Müll. Arg. 白背葉（白桐、楸桐）
Linnaea 34: 189. 1865; FKH 240. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 39, pl. 10: 1 – 2. 1996; FGD 5: 79. 2003.
Ricinus apelta Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 589. 1790,
Rottlera cantoniensis Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 878. 1826.
Rottlera chinensis A. Juss., Euphorb. Gen. tab. 18: 33. 1824; FHK 306. 1861.

Shrub or treelet, usually 1–4 m tall; branchlets, petioles and inflorescences densely yellowish-stellate-pubescent and sparsely sprinkled with orange glands. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–15 cm; leaf blade ovate or broadly ovate, rarely cordate, 6–16(–25) cm in diam., base truncate or slightly cordate, with 2 brown glands near the insertion of petioles, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely serrate, glabrous or sparsely hairy adaxially, white-stellate-tomentose and sprinkled with orange glands abaxially; basal veins 5, lateral veins 6–7. Inflorescence terminal or lateral, spicate or paniculate, the male 15–30 cm, the female sometimes shorter, 5–30 cm. Male flowers: 2–8 clustered in bract; pedicels 1–2.5 mm; alabastrum ovoid or globose, ca. 2.5 mm; calyx-lobes 4, ovate or ovate-triangular, ca. 3 mm, densely yellowish stellate-pubescent abaxially, sparsely sprinkled with minute glands adaxially; stamens 50–75, ca. 5 mm. Female flowers: solitary in bract; pedicels very short; calyx-lobes 3–5, ovate or nearly triangular, 2.5–3 mm, densely white-stellate-hairy and glandular; styles 3–4, ca. 3 mm, connate at base; stigma plumose. Capsules subglobose, 1–1.3 cm in diam., densely stellate-hairy and softly echinate; prickles linear, yellowish, 5 – 10 mm; seeds subglobose, ca. 3.5 mm in diam., brown, rugose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 331, 1933; S. Y. Hu 5411, 12333 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong. Guangxi,Yunnan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests, shrublands. Flowering: Jun. – Sep.; fruiting: Aug. –Nov.

Mallotus barbatus (Wall.) Müll. Arg. 毛桐
Linnaea 34: 184. 1865; FRPS 44 (2): 36, pl. 9: 6 – 8. 1996; FGD 5: 78. 2003.
Rottlera barbata Wall., Cat. 7822. 1828.

Treelet 3–6 m tall; young branches, petioles, abaxial surface of leaves and inflorescences densely stellate-floccose. Leaves alternate, broadly peltate; petioles 5–22 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate-triangular or ovate-rhombic, 13–35 × 12–28 cm, base rounded or truncate, apex acuminate, margins serrate or undulate, sometimes 2–3-lobed, sparsely dotted with yellow glandular granules abaxially; palmately 5 –7-veined; lateral veins 4–6. Inflorescence terminal, racemose, the male 11–36 cm, the female 10–25 cm, multiramose at lower parts; bracts linear, 5–7 mm; bract-axils with 4–6 male flowers. Male flowers: 4–5 clustered in axil of bracts; pedicels ca. 4 mm; calyx-lobes 4–5, ovate, 2–3.5 mm, densely stellate-pubescent abaxially; stamens 75–85. Female flowers: 1–2 in axil of bracts; pedicels ca. 2.5 mm; calyx-lobes 3–5, ovate, 4–5 mm; styles 3–5, slightly connate at base, stigma ca. 3 mm, plumose. Capsules globose, 1.3–2 cm in diam., covered with soft prickles, densely stellate-tomentose; seeds ovoid, ca. 5 × 4 mm, black, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 6043.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Sep. – Oct.

Mallotus hookerianus (Seem.) Müll. Arg. 粗毛野桐

Linnaea 34: 193. 1865; FKH 239. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 17, pl. 5: 1 – 3. 1996; FGD 5: 74, fig. 42. 2005.

Hancea hookeriana Seem., Bot. Voy. Herald. 409, pl. 96. 1857; FHK 306. 1861.


Shrub or treelet, 1.5–6 m tall; young branches and petioles sparsely hispid with stiff spreading hairs. Leaves opposite, differing in size and shape, sometimes strongly reduced, stipuliform; stipules linear-lanceolate, ca. 1 cm, sparsely villose, persistent; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade normally oblong-lanceolate, 8–12 × 2–5 cm, base obtuse or rounded, apex acuminate, margin subentire or undulate, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface villose near base of midvein and pubescent in axils of lateral veins; lateral veins 8–9. Male racemes 4–10 cm, in axils of reduced leaves; bracts subulate or lanceolate, 1–5 mm, hairy. Male flowers: pedicels 3–4 mm, jointed at middie; calyx-lobes 4, elliptic or rotund, ca. 4 mm; stamens 60 or more. Female flowers solitary, sometimes several forming short racemes; pedicels 3–4 mm; calyx-lobes 5, lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, villose; ovary globose, echinate; styles connate at base; stigma 10–15 mm, plumose. Capsules triangular-globose, 1–1.4 cm, with numerous soft prickles; seeds globose, brown, smooth.


Locality: Happy Valley, Shek O, Wong Nai Chung, Nam Chung, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Lo Tung, Fo Tan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 426, 427; Y. S. Lau 1801; S. Y. Hu 10472 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.

Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar. –May; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.

Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Mallotus paniculatus (Lam.) Müll. Arg. 白楸
Linnaea 34: 189. 1865; FRPS 44(2): 35, pl. 9: 3 –5. 1996; FGD 5: 78. 2003
Croton paniculatus Lam., Encycl. 2: 207. 1786.
Mallotus cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 655. 1790; FKH 240. 1912.
Rottlera paniculata (Lam.) A. Juss., Euphorb. Gen, tab. 18: 33. 1824; FHK 307. 1861.

Tree or shrub, 3–15 m tall; branchlets, petioles and inflorescence brown-stellate-tomentose. Leaves alternate, slightly peltate; petioles 2–15 cm; leaf blade ovate, ovate-triangular or rhombic, 5–15 × 3–10 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex long-acuminate, margin undulate or subentire, 2-lobed or sparsely toothed, grey-yellow- or white-tomentose on both surfaces when young, glabrous in age; veins 5, basal. Inflorescence terminal, racemose or paniculate, the male inflorescences 10–20 cm, the female 5–25 cm. Male flowers: 2–6 clustered in axil of bracts; pedicels ca. 2 mm; calyx-lobes 4–5, ovate, 2–2.5 mm, densely stellate-pubescent abaxially; stamens 50–60. Female flowers: 1–2 in axil of bracts; pedicels ca. 2 mm; calyx-lobes 4–5, oblong-ovate, 2–3 mm, densely stellate-pubescent abaxially; styles slightly connate at base, stigma 2–3 mm, plumose. Capsules oblate, 1–1.5 cm in diam., brown-stellate-tomentose and with sparsely spiny; spines soft, 4–5 mm, puberulous; seeds subglobose, brown, often rugose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1280, 2026; P. S. Choi 396; S. Y. Hu 6325, 12728 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE. Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests, shrublands. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.

Mallotus peltatus (Geiseler) Müll. Arg. 山苦茶（富列野桐）
Linnaea 34: 187. 1865.
Aleurites peltata Geiseler, Cronton. Monogr. 81. 1807.
Hancea muricata Benth., FHK 306. 1861.
Mallotus oblongifolius (Miq.) Müll. Arg., Linnaea 34: 192. 1865; FRPS 44(2): 23, pl. 6: 4 – 5. 1996; FGD 5: 73. 2003.
Rottlera oblongifolia Miq., Fl. Ned. Ind. 1(2): 396. 1859.

Shrub or treelet, 2–10 m tall, curry-scented when dry; branchlets stellate-pubescent or glabrous, glandular. Leaves alternate or sometimes nearly opposite, basifixed to peltate; stipules ovate-lanceolate, stellate-hairy, caducous; petioles 0.5–3.5 cm; leaf blade oblong-obovate, 5–15 × 2–6 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, with 4–6 glands near the insertion of petioles; apex acute or caudate-acuminate, entire or slightly undulate, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface stellate-pubescent on veins and with tufts of hairs in axil of lateral veins, sometimes sprinkled with orange glands; pinnately-veined, lateral veins 8–10. Male racemes terminal, 4–12 cm, the male with small clustered flowers; bracts ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 mm; pedicels ca. 3 mm. Male flowers: alabastrum ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm; calyx-lobes 3, broadly ovate, unequal, ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous; stamens 25–45; connectives broader. Female racemes terminal, 7–10 cm, with few distant flowers; bracts subulate, ca. 2 mm long, hairy; pedicels ca. 2.5 mm. Female flowers: calyx spathaceous ca. 4.5 mm, unilateral-lobed, apex tridentate, abaxially stellate-hairy and sparsely sprinkled with yellow glandular dots; ovary globose, densely echinate and puberulous; styles connate below middle; stigma 4–5 mm, densely plumose. Capsules oblate, ca. 1.4 cm in diam., muricate with soft and usually recurved points, puberulous and sprinkled with orange-yellow glands; seeds globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., maculate-striped.

Locality: Aberdeen, Nam Fung Rd., Deep Water Bay Rd., Lady Clementi's Ride, Kei Ling Ha Lo Wai, Tai Long Wan. Y. W. Lam 749; HK sheet 38801, 40154.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; widely spread over S and SE Asia.
Ecology: Shrublands, margins of forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Mallotus philippensis (Lam.) Müll. Arg. 粗糠柴
Linnaea 34: 196. 1865; FKH 240. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 31, pl. 8: 7. 1996; FGD 5: 77. 2003.
Croton philippensis Lam., Encycl. 2: 206. 1786.
Rottlera tinctoria Roxb., Pl. Coromandel 2: 36, pl. 168. 1798; FHK 307. 1861.

Shrub or tree, 2–18 m tall; branchlets, young leaves and inflorescences densely tawny stellate-pubescent. Leaves alternate or sometimes opposite; petioles 2–5(–9) cm, brownish hairy, slightly thickened on both ends, stellate-hairy; leaf blade subcoriaceous, ovate, oblong or ovate-lanceolate, 5–23 × 3–6 cm, base rounded or truncate, with 2–4 brown glands near the insertion of petiole, apex acuminate, margin subentire, glabrous adaxially, stellate-tomentellous and sparsely sprinkled with red glands abaxially; basal veins 3, lateral veins 4–6. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, racemose, solitary or clustered, the male 5–10 cm, the female 3–8 cm, lengthened to 16 cm in fruit; bracts ovate, ca. 1 mm. Male flowers: 1–5 clustered in axil of bract; pedicels 1–2 mm; calyx-lobes 3–4, oblong, ca. 2 mm, densely stellate-hairy and sprinkled with red glands; stamens 15–30, connectives slightly broad; bracts ovate, ca. 1 mm. Female flowers: pedicels 1.2 mm; calyx-lobes 3–5, ovate-lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, densely stellate-hairy; ovary pubescent, styles 2–3, 3–4 mm, stigma densely plumose. Capsules oblate, 6–8 mm in diam., densely covered with red glands and mealy hairs; seeds ovate or globose, black.

Locality: Barker Rd., Findlay Rd., Mount Gough, Pok Fu Lam Reservoir, Stubbs Rd., Victoria Peak, Butterfly Hill, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 851; N. H. Li 128; HK sheet 39979; S. Y. Hu 10769 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E to SE Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests, margins of forests. Flowering: Apr. –May; fruiting: May–Aug.

Mallotus repandus (Rottler) Müll. Arg. 石岩楓
Linnaea 34: 197. 1865; FKH 240. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 28. 1996; FGD 5: 74, fig. 42. 2003.
Croton repandus Rottler, Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Neue Schriften 4: 206. 1803.
Rottlera cordifolia Benth., FHK 307. 1861.

Climbing shrub; young branches, leaves, petioles and inflorescences densely yellowish stellate-pubescent; older branches glabrous. Leaves alternate, papery or membranous; petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic-ovate, 3.5–8 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate, rounded or cordate, apex shortly and obtusely acuminate, entire or slightly sinuate, adaxially glabrous or nearly so, abaxially in axils of veins, but sprinkled with glandular dots. basal veins 3, lateral veins 4–5,. Inflorescence racemose, terminal, rarely axillary, the male 5–15 cm, sometimes branched at base, the female terminal, 5–8 cm. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 4 mm, calyx-lobes 3–4, ovate-oblong, ca. 3 mm, tomentose abaxially; stamens 40–75, filaments ca. 2 mm, anthers oblong. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 3 mm; calyx-lobes 5, ovate-lanceolate, ca. 3.5 mm, tomentose and glandular abaxially; styles 2–3; stigma ca. 3 mm, stellate-hairy, plumose. Capsules depressed globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., densely covered with powdery-hairs and glands; seeds ovoid, ca. 5 mm in diam., black, lustrous.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar,Victoria Park Rd., Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam Rd., Tai Hang Rd., Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Green Island, Hei Ling Chau, Cheung Chau. H. C. Tang 1295; Y. S. Lau 565; P. S. Choi 356; S. Y. Hu 5227 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; widely distributed in SE to S Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests, margins of forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen of Rottlera cordifolia was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island in 1853.

Malva verticillata L. 冬葵（冬莧葵）
Sp. Pl. 689. 1753; FKH 46. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 5, pl. 1: 5 – 6. 1984; FGD 2: 196, fig. 122. 1991.

Annual or perennial herb, 0.5–1 m tall at anthesis; stem stellate villose. Leaves basal and alternate on stem; petioles 5–8 cm; stipules ovate-lanceolate; leaf blade reniform or orbicular, 5–11 cm in diam., usually 5–7-lobed; lobes of the lower leaves rounded, those of the upper ones triangular, apex obtuse, margin crenulate-dentate. Flowers in compact fascicles. Pedicels very short, stellate villose; involucral bracts linear-lanceolate. Calyx cup-shaped, 5-lobed. Corolla white or pale purple, almost twice as long as the calyx. Staminal tube setose. Fruit 5–7 mm in diam., entirely glabrous; carpels 10 or 11, smooth abaxially, rugose along the rounded angles, palmately striate on the side.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 455, 3320.
Distribution: Widely distributed over China; India, Myanmar, Korea and N Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Food (leaves edible), ornamental.

Malvastrum coromandelianum (L.) Garcke 賽葵
Bonplandia 5: 297. 1857; FRPS 49(2): 14, pl. 3: 4 – 6. 1984; FGD 2: 197, fig. 124. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 745, pl. 374. 1993.
Malva coromandeliana L., Sp. Pl. 2: 687. 1753.
Malvastrum tricuspidatum (R. Br.) A. Gray, Pl. Wright. 1: 16. 1852; FHK 32. 1861; FKH 47. 1912.

Perennial herb, usually shrubby, up to 1 m tall, sparsely covered with simple and 4-armed stellate strigose hairs. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–3 cm, densely pilose; stipules lanceolate, 5 mm; leaf blade ovate, or ovate-elliptic, 3 – 6 × 1–3.5 cm, apex obtuse, base subrounded, margin coarsely serrate, sparsely pilose on both surfaces. Flowers yellow, solitary, axillary, ca. 1.5 cm in diam. Pedicels 5 mm. Bracteoles linear, 5 × 1 mm. Sepals ovate, acuminate, 8 mm, basal 1/3 connate. Petals obovate, 8 × 4 mm. Fruit depressed globose, 6 mm in diam.; carpels reniform, weakly stellate pilose, with 2 spines at the middle, and a stiff, persistent style.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1974; HK sheet 35650; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22236, 22302 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropical, native to N America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.

Malvaviscus arboreus Cav. var. penduliflorus (DC.) Schery 垂花懸鈴花
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 29: 223. 1942; FRPS 49(2): 50. 1984; FGD 2: 193, fig. 120. 1991.
Malvaviscus penduliflorus DC., Prodr. 1: 445. 1824.

Shrub, 1–3 m tall; young branchlets and pedicels sparsely pubescent and with a line of long hairs on one side. Leaves narrowly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 6 –12 × 2.5– 6 cm, undivided, or rarely shallowly 3-lobed, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex long acuminate, margin obtusely dentate, glabrescent or sparsely stellate pubescent on nerves. Flowers bright red, hanging at anthesis. Pedicels 1–4 cm, pubescent. Bracteoles lanceolate to spathulate, 1.2–1.5 cm, pubescent adaxially. Calyx bell-shaped, 1.5 –2 cm, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, 5 –7 mm. Corolla 5 –7 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 683, 1889; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22634 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong & Yunnan. Native to Mexico & Columbia.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round in Hong Kong.
Uses: Ornamental.

Mangifera indica L. 杧果
Sp. Pl. 1: 200. 1753; FKH 69. 1912; FGZ 446, fig. 240. 1956; FHN 3: 102, fig. 597. 1974; FYN 2: 367. 1979; FRPS 45(1): 74. 1980; FFJ 3: 242. 1987; FGD 2: 308. 1991.
Mangifera austro-yunnanensis Hu, Bull. Fan Mem. Inst. Biol., Bot. 10: 160. 1940.

Tree, 10–20 m tall; branchlets brown, glabrous. Leaves often crowded towards apex of branchlets; petiole 2–4 cm.; leaf blade leathery, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, rarely oblong-ovate, 12–20 × 3.5–6.5 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, undulate, deep green adaxially, light green abaxially, glossy and glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins ca. 15 on each side of midvein. Panicle as long as or slightly longer than leaves, pubescent; bracts ca. 1.5 mm, lanceolate, pubescent; pedicels 1.5–3 mm, articulate. Calyx lobes ovate or long elliptic, 1.7–3.5 mm, pubescent. Petals light yellow or white, later turning to purple, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 2 times as long as calyx-lobes, glabrous, recurved at anthesis. Fertile stamen 1, ca. 2.5 mm; staminodes 4, 0.7–1.5 mm. Disk inflated, fleshy, 5-lobed. Ovary oblique, ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm in diam.; style ca. 2.5 mm. Drupe ellipsoidal to nearly kidney-shape, greenish yellow to red, 8–15 cm, fleshy mesocarp bright yellow, endocarp more or less compressed.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 698, 1753; HK sheet 6455.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to India, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, cultivated in tropical regions worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Fruit, ornamental.

Manglietia fordiana Oliv. 木蓮（綠楠）
Hook., Icon. Pl. 20(3): t. 1953. 1891; FKH 28. 1912; FGD 1: 4. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 105. 1996.
Magnolia fordiana (Oliv.) Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 5(4): 228. 1924.
Paramanglietia microcarp Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1: 53. 1961.

Trees, up to 20 m tall. Young twigs and buds reddish brown pubescent, glabrescent. Stipular scars semi-elliptic, 3– 4 mm. Petioles 1–3 cm, base slightly swollen. Leaves narrowly obovate, narrowly elliptic-obovate or oblanceolate, 8 –17 × 2.5 –5.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, decurrent to petioles, apex acute, margin slightly involute, abaxially sparsely reddish brown pubescent; lateral veins 8 –12 on each side of midvein. Pedicels 6 –11 × 6 –10 mm, with 1 annular bract-scar, reddish brown pubescent; tepals white, in whorls of 3, the outer 3 slightly thinner, nearly leathery, oblong-elliptic, 6–7 × 3–4 cm, the inner ones smaller, usually fleshy, obovate, 5– 6 × 2–3 cm; stamens ca. 1 cm, anthers ca. 8 mm, connectives obtuse; gynoecium ca. 1.5 cm, 23–30-carpellate, smooth, basal carpels 5 –6 × 3–4 mm, middle ones ca. 5 mm wide on exposed side; styles ca. 1 mm; ovules 8–10, in 2 series. Aggregate fruit brown, ovoid, 2–5 cm; follicles dotted with protuberance on exposed side, apex with ca. 1 mm beak; seeds red.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1439; HK sheet 33073.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Ford 90, holotype K) was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in 1883. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental, medicinal.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Ford 90, holotype K) was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in 1883. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Manihot esculenta Crantz 木薯
Inst. Rei Herb. 1: 167. 1766; FRPS 44(2): 172, pl. 44: 1 – 4. 1996; FGD 5: 121, fig. 73. 2003.
Jatropha manihot L., Sp. Pl. 1007. 1753.
Manihot utilissima Pohl, Pl. Bras. Icon. Descr. 1: 32, pl. 24. 1827.

Erect shrub, 1.5–3mtall, with fleshy elongated tuberous root. Leaves ± peltate; stipules triangular-lanceolate, 5 – 7 mm, entire or with 1–2 bristly segments; petioles 6–35 cm; leaf blade usually deeply palmately 3–9-parted; lobes spatulate- or linear-lanceolate, 8– 18 × 1.5– 4 cm, apex acuminate, entire. Racemes terminal or axillary, 5 – 8 cm; bracts oblong-lanceolate; pedicels 4 – 6 mm. Male flowers: calyx ca. 7 mm, purplish red, divided beyond middle; lobes narrowly ovate, 3 – 4 mm, hairy adaxially; stamens 10; anthers white-pubescent at apex. Female flowers: calyx as in male flowers, but slightly longer; lobes oblong-lanceolate, ca. 8 × 3 mm; ovary ovoid, with 6 longitudinal ridges; styles 3, connate at base, apex dilated. Capsules ellipsoidal, 1.5 – 1.8 × 1 – 1.5 cm, with 6 winged angles.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 631, 1109, 3001.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep. –Nov.
Uses: Food (starch), material (petroleum substitute, alcohol).

Manilkara zapota (L.) P. Royen 人心果
Blumea 7: 410, fig. l–q. 1953; FHN 3: 160. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 50, pl. 9: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 310. 1989; FGD 2: 351. 1991.
Achras zapota L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2. 1190, 1753; FGZ 469, fig. 257. 1956.
Sapota achras Mill., Gard. Dict. ed. 8. Sapota no. 1. 1768.

Tree, 6 –10 m, with milky juice. Branches brown, with conspicuous leaf scars. Petioles 2 cm; leaf blades oblong or ovate-elliptic, 6 –19 × 2.5 – 4 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate, apex short-acuminate to obtuse, sometimes emarginate, margin sometimes undulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins many, nearly parallel, inconspicuous. Flowers usually solitary and axillary. Pedicels 2 cm or longer, yellowish brown-tomentose. Sepals ovate, 6 – 8 mm, rusty tomentose abaxially. Corolla white, 6 – 8 mm; lobes ovate, 3 –5 mm, irregularly dentate at apex. Staminodes petaloid, as wide as half of corolla lobes. Ovary densely brown-tomentose. Berry ovoid or ovoid-ellipsoid, 4 – 8 cm, brown.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 17906; Y. S. Lau 2721.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan, Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Yunnan (cultivated); native to C America.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Mapania silhetensis C. B. Clarke 華擂鼓藶（擂鼓藶）
Fl. Brit. India 6: 681. 1894; FOC 23: 170. 2010.
Mapania sinensis H. Uittien, Recueil Trav. Bot. Néerl. 33: 288. 1936; FRPS 11: 197. 1961.
Mapania wallichii auct. non C. B. Clarke: FGD 8: 350. 2007, p.p. quod syn. M. sinensis H. Uittien; Check List HK Plants 317. 2002.

Perennial. Rhizomes thick, woody. Culms lateral, 25–55 cm tall, ca. 3 mm thick, with several cataphylls toward base. Leaves basal, distichous; leaf sheath brownish, ca. 12 cm, margin thickly membranous; leaf blade ca. 130 × 2.5–3.5 cm or longer, subleathery, smooth, 3-veined, apical margin and abaxial midvein serrulate, apex caudate to acuminate. Involucral bracts brown, glumelike, ovate to ovate-deltate, 1.5–2.5 cm, shorter than inflorescence, leathery, apex acute. Inflorescences capitate, broadly ovoid, 2–4.5 × 1.5–2 cm, with 4 spikes fascicled at apex of culm, with many glume-like bracts and spicoids. Glume-like bracts straw-coloured, spirally and imbricately arranged, narrowly oblong, ca. 1 cm, papery, apex obtuse. Spicoids with 6 glumes, 3 male flowers, and 1 female flower; basal 2 glumes opposite, cymbiform, membranous, keeled, spinulose on apical part of keel, each subtending 1 male flower; remaining 4 bracts narrowly oblong, outermost one subtending a male flower. Filaments to 1.6 cm; anthers linear, 7–8 mm. Style ca. 6.5 mm; stigmas 3. Achene dark brown, obovoid, 4–4.5 mm, obtusely 3-sided, outer surface succulent, apex conically rostrate.

Locality: Sai Kung, Wong Chuk Yeung, Pat Sin Leng, Wang Shan Keuk. F. W. Xing 6973, 7161.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Bangladesh, India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Mappianthus iodoides Hand.-Mazz. 甜果藤（定心藤）
Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl., Anz. 58: 150. 1912; FRPS 46: 53. 1981.

Woody climber, young shoots, petioles and inflorescence densely tawny strigose. Petioles 6 – 14 mm; leaf blade oblong, 8 – 17 × 3 – 7 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, olive-green adaxially, yellow-green abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces or sparsely strigose abaxially, lateral veins 3 – 5 on each sides of midvein. Cymes axillary, rarely super-axillary or terminal, 1 – 4(–8) cm. Male flowers: pedicels 1 – 2 cm; calyx small, cupular, ca. 2 mm, shallowly 5-dentate, densely strigose; corolla 4 – 6 mm, lobes ovate, apex caudate, incurved, densely strigose; stamens 5, as long as corolla; pistillode conic. Female inflorescence not more than 1 cm. Female flowers: calyx as in male flowers; petals oblong, 3 – 4 mm, apex acute, incurved, densely yellow-brown strigose; staminode 2 mm; ovary subglobose, 2 mm; stigma disciform. Drupe orange, elliptic, 2 – 3.5 × 1 – 1.5 cm, sweet, with persistent slightly enlarged calyx; 1-seeded.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Kadoorie Farm, Pat Sin Leng, Tai Po Kau. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24072; Y. S. Lau 3327; Y. W. Lam 129.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Sunny places of forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Maranta arundinacea L. 竹芋
Sp. Pl. 1: 2. 1753; Curt's Bot. Mag. t. 2307. 1822; FHN 4: 106. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 167, pl. 59. 1981; FGD 2: 440. 1991; FOC 24: 382. 2000.

Herb, 40–130 cm tall. Rhizomes sympodial, spindle-shaped, fleshy, starchy. Stems slender, erect, dichotomous branched. Basal leaves 4–8; cauline leaves 1–8; petiole 3.5–20 cm in basal leaves, often absent in cauline leaves, pulvinus 5–10 mm; leaf blade green, ovate-oblong, 10–20 × 4–10 cm, base round, apex acuminate, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose. Racemes terminal, 15–20 cm, loose. Bracts linear-lanceolate, 3–4 cm, involute. Flowers mostly self-pollinating; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Sepals green, narrowly lanceolate, 1.2–1.4 cm. Corolla white; tube curved, ca. 1.3 cm, base inflated; lobes 8–10 mm. Staminodes white; outer staminodes 2, obovate, ca. 1 cm, inner staminodes 1/2 as long as outer ones. Ovary glabrous or pubescent. Capsules green or tinged reddish brown, oblong, 7–8 × 4–5 mm, dehiscent. Seeds brown, rugose; aril basal, white, 2-lobed.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28063.
Distribution: Widely cultivated elsewhere in tropics; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental, food (starch).

Maranta bicolor Ker Gawl. 花葉竹芋
Bot. Reg. pl. 786. 1824; FRPS 16(2): 169. 1981; FGD 2: 440. 1991.

Herb compact, 25–40 cm tall, bearing tubers at base. Petioles up to 2.5 cm; pulvinus 5 mm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic or ovate, 7–12 × 5–7 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex round, mucronate, margin ± undulate, glaucous-green and with dark brown spots adaxially. Racemes simple; peduncle 6–10 cm; bracts 2–4, lanceolate, 2.5–3 cm; flower-pairs 3 each bract; sepals 5 mm; corolla white, tube 4 mm, lobes lanceolate, ca. 8 mm; outer 2 staminodes larger, obovate, emarginate, white with violet spots and striped, inner staminode very small.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical regions, native to Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Mariscus cyperinus (Retz.) Vahl 莎草磚子苗
Enum. Pl. 2: 377. 1805; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 182. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 290. 2000; FYN 15: 655. 2003; FGD 8: 343. 2007.
Kyllinga cyperina Retz., Observ. Bot. 6: 21. 1791
Cyperus cyperinus (Retz.) J. V. Suringar, Cyperus, 154. 1898; FOC 23: 238. 2010.
Mariscus sieberianus Nees ex C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 622. 1893; FKH 296. 1912.
Cyperus umbellatus auct. non (Vahl) Benth.: FHK 386. 1861.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody, clothed with brown fibers. Culms solitary or few together, erect, 20–70 cm tall, triquetrous, smooth, leaved at ± thickened base. Leaves several, shorter than culm; blades narrowly linear, 5–7 mm wide, herbaceous, flattish plicate; sheaths pale green and stained with purplish pink. Corymbs simple, open, with short anthelas, sometimes nearly head-like; anthelas 6–10, 0–5 cm, each terminated by a cylindrical or oblong, spike narrowed to base, 1.5–3 × 8–12 mm, greenish, densely bearing many spikelets; leafy bracts 4–10, lower few surpassing corymb. Spikelets patent to erect-patent, linear-lanceolate, subterete, 4–6.5 mm × 1 mm, bearing 4–7 glumes and 2–3 achenes; rachilla with lanceolate wings, jointed above prophyll. Glumes tightly erect, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 3–3.5 mm, inrolled, membranous to thinly chartaceous, obtuse or suddenly acute at apex, glaucous green and eventually tinged with straw-brown, 3–4-veined on both sides, green keel convex. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style slightly longer than achene; stigmas 3. Achenes linear-oblong, trigonous, 1.5–1.8 × 0.6–0.9 mm, brown, minutely granulate.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Shing Mun, Hong Kong Wetland Park, Hau Hok Wan. J. C. Shaw 411, 456; HK sheet 42176.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Sichuan; Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Japan, Australia, SW Asia, Pacific islands, Indian Ocean islands.
Ecology: Moist grasslands of valleys and hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Mariscus cyperoides (L.) Urb. 磚子苗
Symb. Antill. 2(1): 164. 1900; FGD 8: 342. 2007.
Scirpus cyperoides L., Mant. Pl. 2: 181. 1771.
Mariscus umbellatus (Rottb.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 376. 1805; FRPS 11: 179. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 608. 1988.
Kyllinga umbellata Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 1773; Check List HK Plants 357. 2004.
Cyperus umbellatus Benth., FHK 386. 1861.
Mariscus sumatrensis (Retz.) J. Anthelanal, Adansonia n. s. 15: 110. 1975; FTW ed. 2, 5: 291. 2000; FYN 15: 654. 2003.
Kyllinga sumatrensis Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 13. 1786.
Mariscus albescens Gaudich., Voy. Bonite, Bot. 415. 1826; FKH 296. 1912.

Perennial with short woody rhizome clothed with brown fibers. Culms solitary or few together, erect, triquetrous, 10–50 cm tall, smooth, ± thickened base leafy. Leaves rather many, shorter than to equalling culm; blades linear, 3–6 mm wide, flattish plicate, herbaceous; sheaths pale, eventually becoming brownish or reddish brownish. Corymbs simple, open, 3–8 cm wide; anthelas 3–12, patent, longer ones to 8 cm, terminated by a spike; spikes cylindrical, 1–2.5 cm × 6–10 mm, densely bearing many spikelets, greenish; leafy bracts 3–8, lower ones surpassing corymb. Spikelets spreading or lower ones ± reflexed, linear-lanceolate, 3–5 × 0.7 mm, bearing 4–5 glumes, 1–2-fruited; rachilla jointed above base, with white-hyaline lanceolate wings. Glumes lanceolate-oblong, ca. 3 mm long, membranous, pale green, apex obtuse or mucronate, margined inrolled, several-veined, keel 3-veined, forming an obtuse back. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes linear-oblong, ca. 2 mm long, straw-coloured, minutely puncticulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 483; K. L. Yip 4080; Y. W. Lam 754.
Distribution: S, E, C & SW China; SE Asia, Himalaya, Africa, Australia, America.
Ecology: Grasslands of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Mariscus javanicus (Houtt.) Merr. & F. T. Metc. 羽穗磚子苗
Lingnan Sci. J. 21: 4. 1945; FRPS 11: 177. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 290. 2000; FGD 8: 340. 2007.
Cyperus javanicus Houtt., Nat. Hist. 2: 13, pl. 88, fig. 1. 1782; FOC 23: 237. 2010.

Coarse perennial. Rhizome short, woody, thick. Culms tufted, robust, 40–110 cm tall, 3–5 mm thick, obtusely trigonous, minutely granulate, glaucous green. Leaves many, mostly surpassing culms; blades linear, 8–12 mm wide, leathery, plicate below middle, flattish to incurvd-marginate above middle, glaucous-green and often whitish powdery, separate-nodulose, prominently scabrous on margins; sheaths dark brown or purplish brown, cylindrical, septate-nodulose. Corymbs compound to decompound, ample, 10–15 cm; primary anthelas 6–10(–12) cm, patent, subrigid; secondary corymbs with 3–6 anthelalets; spikes cylindrical to oblong, 1.5–3 × 8–12 mm, bearing many spikelets; leafy bracts 5–6, lower ones much surpassing corymb. Spikelets divergent to slightly reflexed, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 4.5–6 × 1.8–2 mm, turgid, 4–6-flowered; rhachilla rather broadly winged, jointed above prophyll. Glumes broadly ovate, ca. 3 mm, subleathery, brownish with rusty lineaolate, apex acuminate, margins whitish hyaline, many-veined; keel hardly ridged, forming an obtuse back. Stamens 3; anther linear. Style slender, 1–1.5 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes oval to obovate, trigonous, ca. 1/2 as long as glume, black-brown at maturity, minutely puncticulate; style elongate.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Shek O, Sha Tin. Y. W. Lam 755; Y. S. Lau 2305; HK sheet 7848.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, India, Cambodia, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Japan, Madagascar, tropical Africa, Australia, Hawaii.
Ecology: Sandy beaches, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Mariscus radians (Nees & Meyen) Tang & F. T. Wang 輻射磚子苗
FRPS 11: 177. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 290. 2000; FGD 8: 341. 2007.
Cyperus radians Nees & Meyen ex Kunth, Enum. Pl. 2: 95. 1837 [“radiates”]; FHK 386. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FOC 23: 225. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short, clothed with brownish fibers. Culms ± tufted, very low, 2–6 cm tall; obtusely trigonous smooth, usually hidden in leaf tuft, which much surpass culm. Leaves several, surpassing corymb; blades linear, plicate, 2–4 mm wide, stiffish; sheaths purplish brown. Corymbs simple with 2–7 elongate anthelas; anthelas somewhat unequal, patent, lower ones 9 – 12 cm, each terminated by a head-like cluster of spikelets; leafy bracts 3–7, equalling or shorter than corymb anthelas. Heads globose, 8–25 mm across, bearing 5–20 spikelets. Spikelets ovate to lanceolate-ovate, 6–12 × 2–4 mm, slightly turgid, bearing 4–15 flowers, pale green and tinged with brown. Glumes broadly ovate, 3.5–4 mm, papery, pale-green with purplish brown striate, sometimes tinged with purple brown, 11–13-veined, greenish keel convex, ending in a short recurved cusp at acute apex of glume. Stamens 3; anther broadly linear. Style slender; stigmas 3. Achene oval, trigonous with shallowly concave sides, 1.5–2 mm, dark brown, style elongate.

Locality: Sai Kung. S. C. Ng 2212.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.

Markhamia stipulata (Wall.) Seem. ex K. Schum. var. kerrii Sprague 貓尾木
Kew Bull. 1919: 310. 1919; FOC 18: 224. 1998.
Markhamia cauda‑felina (Hance) Benth. & Hook. ex Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 235. 1890; FGZ 611, fig. 324. 1956.
Dolichandrone cauda‑felina (Hance) Benth. & Hook. f., Gen. Pl. 2: 1046. 1876; FHN 3: 534, fig. 912. 1974; FYN 2: 722, pl. 200: 2 – 3. 1979; FRPS 69: 50, pl. 14: 3 – 4. 1990; FFJ 5: 87, fig. 95. 1993; Check List HK Plants 256. 2002; 88. 2004.
Spathodea cauda‑felina Hance, Journ. Bot. 10: 257. 1872.
Dolichandrone stipulata var. kerrii (Sprague) C. Y. Wu & W. C. Yin, FYN 2: 724. 1979; FRPS 69: 52, pl. 14: 2. 1990.

Tree 5–15 m tall. Young branches, leaves, and peduncles yellowish brown pubescent to tomentose. Leaves 40– 50 cm, exstipulate, often with rudimentary simple leaves at the base of petiole; leaflets 3 – 9 pairs; petiolules 1–3 mm or subsessile; leaf blades papery, oblong, elliptic‑oblong, elliptic‑lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 5–28 × 4–9 cm, base rounded, apex caudate‑acuminate, margin entire to serrulate, rusty yellow pubescent when young, glabrescent adaxially, pubescent to puberulent abaxially; lateral veins 8–9 pairs; petiolules 1–4 mm or leaflets subsessile. Racemes rusty yellow pubescent, 4–10‑flowered. Flowers 10–12 cm in diam. Pedicel 2–6 cm. Calyx 3.3–5.5 cm, yellowish brown tomentose to floccose, apex with 6–8 black tubercles. Corolla dark purple, yellow at upper part, funnelform, ca. 10 cm; tube red‑brown or purple on lower part, 1.5–2 cm in diam. at base; mouth 10–15 cm in diam.; lobes irregularly wrinkled. Stamens and style included; staminodes present or absent. Capsule linear, compressed, 30–70 × 2–3 cm, densely yellowish brown tomentose or floccose. Seeds long elliptic, including wing 3–5 × 1–1.3 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 2102; Y. S. Lau 644, 1708.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan (cultivated or wild); Thailand, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Environmental (landscaping).

Marsdenia lachnostoma Benth. 毛喉牛奶菜
FHK 226. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 450. 1977; FGD 1: 518, fig. 590. 1987; FOC 16: 248. 1995.

Lianas, suffrutescent, to 2 m or longer, stems, petioles and inflorescences thin pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 6–17 mm; leaf blade ovate to oblong, 2.5–9 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or subcordate, apex acute or obtuse, abaxially pale or glaucous. Inflorescences umbel‑like, branched, compact, much shorter than leaves; peduncle 10–15 mm; pedicels 1.5–2 mm, ciliolate. Sepals ovate, 2 mm. Corolla campanulate, 3.5–4 mm; tube longer than lobes, with reflexed hairs inside and a very dense tuft of woolly hairs at throat, conspicuous in dried material; lobes oblong, glabrous except at base. Corona‑lobes ovate‑lanceolate, shorter than anthers; pollinia oblong or reniform. Stigma head conical. Follicles ellipsoidal, thickly walled, 4.5–5.5 × 1.5–2 cm. Seeds ca. 0.9–1.3 cm × 6–8 mm; coma 2–2.5 cm. Follicles oblong‑ovate or elliptic, 3.5–5 × 2–3 cm, glabrous, greenish; fruit stalk 2–2.5 cm; seeds broadly ovate or suborbicular, flat, 2–2.5 mm, margin membranous; coma white, 2–2.5cm.

Locality: North Point, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Tung Lung Chau. Y. S. Lau 1400; S. C. Ng 2170; HK sheet 38590.
Distribution: Hong Kong; Cambodia, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island in 1854. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Marsdenia tinctoria R. Br. 藍葉藤
Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 1: 30. 1810; FHK 226. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 444, pl. 165. 1977; FGD 1: 516, fig. 588. 1987; FOC 16: 248. 1995.

Lianas to 5 m or longer, densely to sparsely pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petioles 1–4 cm; leaf blade oblong to broadly ovate, 5–13 × 2–7 cm, thin‑papery, bluish when dry, base rounded to cordate, apex acuminate, lateral veins 5–7(–10) on each side of midvein. Inflorescences densely flowered, globose to long raceme‑like cluster of cymules, (1.5–)3–15 cm; peduncle (0.5–)2.5–5 cm; pedicels 3–5 mm. Sepals suborbicular, ca. 2 mm. Corolla yellowish white, dark blue when dry, urceolate, 3.5–4(–6) mm, throat with a ring of hairs, otherwise glabrous; tube ca. 2.5 mm; lobes ovate, 1–1.5 mm, apex rounded. Corona‑lobes 5, lanceolate, as long as anther. Pollinia narrowly oblong. Stigma head discoid, slightly convex at apex. Follicles oblong‑lanceolate, 5–10 × 0.8–1 cm, pilose to sub‑tomentose. Seeds ovate, 1 × 0.3 cm; coma 1–2 cm.

Locality: Aberdeen. HK sheet 3917.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore)

Mazus pumilus (Burm. f.) Steenis 通泉草
Nova Guinea n. s. 9(1): 31. 1958; FOC 18: 46. 1998.
Lobelia pumilus Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 186. 1768.
Mazus japonicus (Thunb.) Kuntze, Rev. Gen. 2: 462. 1891; FRPS. 67(2): 187. 1979; FGD 4: 372. 2000.
Lindernia japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 253. 1784.
Mazus rugosus Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 385. 1790; FHK 247. 1861; FKH 185. 1912.

Annual herbs, erect or decumbent, 10–20 cm tall, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Stems few, few‑branched, rooting from prostrate nodes. Basal leaves rosulate, caducous; leaf blade spatulate to oblanceolate, 2–6 × 1–1.3 cm, base decurrent, margin dentate or lobed; stem leaves opposite or few alternate, usually smaller. Racemes terminal, usually 3–10‑flowered, laxly flowered. Pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx campanulate, 3–8 mm, not enlarged in fruit; lobes ovate, as long as tube. Corolla white, purple or blue, 1–1.2 cm; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe smaller than lateral lobes, obovate; upper lip 2‑lobed, lobes ovate. Ovary glabrous. Capsules globose, ca. 3 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 822; L. T. Lo 529; Y. W. Lam 840.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia, Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet grasslands, wastelands, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Medicago falcata L. 野苜蓿
Sp. Pl. 779. 1753; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 321. 1998.
Medicago sativa L. subsp. falcata (L.) Arcang., Comp. Fl. Ital. 160. 1882.

Perennial herb. Stems 40 – 100 cm tall, prostrate or ascendent, copiously branched, subglabrous. Stipules lanceolate, base hastate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets obovate or oblanceolate, 8–15 × 2–5 mm, terminal one larger, base cuneate, 1/4 of margin dentate, apex obtuse, aristate, glabrous adaxially, adpressed pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 12– 15 pairs. Racemes axillary, 6– 60-flowered. Calyx campanulate, ca. 4 mm, teeth setaceous. Corolla bright yellow, 6– 9 mm; vexillum oblanceolate; wings equal to keel, but shorter than vexillum. Ovary linear, pubescent; ovules 2 – 5. Pods falcate, 10 – 15 × 3.5 – 4 mm, adpressed pubescent, fine venose. Seeds 2 – 4, yellow-brown, ovate-elliptic, 2 × 1.5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized.
Distribution: NE, N, NW China; Europe, C Asia to Siberia.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Jul. –Aug.
Uses: Herbage.

Medicago lupulina L. 天藍苜蓿
Sp. Pl. 779. 1753; FHK 75. 1861; FKH 74. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 314. 1998; FGD 5: 360. 2003.

Annual, biennial or perennial herb, 15 – 60 cm tall. Stems diffuse or ascendent, pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets obovate, ovate or suborbicular, 5– 20 × 4– 6 mm, base cuneate, apex truncate or emarginate, mucronate, margin denticulate on distal part, glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 10 pairs. Heads 10 – 20-flowered. Peduncles longer than leaves. Calyx campanulate, 3 mm, densely hairy. Corolla yellow; vexillum suborbicular, apex emarginate; wings and keel shorter than vexillum, obovate. Pods sickle-shaped, reniform, 3 × 2 mm, marked with much curved veins, black when ripe. Seed single, ovate, brown.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized.
Distribution: N & S China; naturalized in elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.

Medicago polymorpha L. 南苜蓿
Sp. Pl. 779. 1753; FRPS 42(2): 327. 1998; FGD 5: 361. 2003.
Medicago hispida Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 349, pl. 155. 1791.

Annual or biennial herb, 20 – 90 cm tall. Stems decumbent or erect, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, branched at base. Stipules conspicuously lacerate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets obovate or broad-obovate, 7 – 20 × 5 – 15 mm, emarginate, base cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate, mucronate, margin shallowly denticulate on distal 1/3, glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent abaxially. Heads 2 –10-flowered. Peduncles usually shorter than leaves. Calyx campanulate, 2 mm, teeth lanceolate, as long as tube. Corolla yellow; vexillum obovate, apex emarginate; wings oblong, base auriculate and clawed; keel shorter than wings, base hooked-auriculate. Pods 1.5– 2.5(–6)-coiled, 4 – 6 mm in diam., spinose. Seeds brown, 1 – 2 in each coil, reniform, 2.5 × 1.2 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 11284; HK sheet 1259.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River, Shaanxi, Gansu, Yunnan, Guizhou; Europe, Asia, Africa, America, Australia (cultivated).
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: May– Jun.

Medicago sativa L. 紫苜蓿
Sp. Pl. 778. 1753; FRPS 42(2): 323. 1998; FGD 5: 360, fig. 201. 2003.

Perennial herb, 30–100 cm tall. Stems caespitose or prostrate, 4-angular, many-branched. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets obovate to oblanceolate, 10 – 25 × 3 – 10 mm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, terminal one often larger, margin denticulate on distal 1/3, lateral veins 8 –10 pairs. Racemes or heads axillary, 1 – 2.5 cm, 5–30-flowered. Peduncles longer than leaves. Calyx campanulate, 3 – 5 mm. Corolla yellowish, deeply blue or dark purple; petals clawed; vexillum oblong, apex emarginate; wings longer than keel. Ovary linear, pubescent. Pods brown, 2 – 4-coiled, 5 – 9 mm in diam., slightly pubescent. Seeds 10– 20, ovate, 1– 2.5 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough. W. J. Tutcher 5264; H. C. Tang 751.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to Asia, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Melaleuca cajuputi Roxb. subsp. cumingiana (Turcz.) Barlow 白千層
Novon. 7: 113. 1997; FOC 13: 329. 2007.
Melaleuca cumingiana Turcz., Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 20: 164. 1847.
Melaleuca leucadendra auct. non (L.) L.: FGZ 209. 1956; FHN 2: 5. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 54 – 55. 1984; FFJ 4: 93, fig. 78. 1989; FGX 1: 900. 1991; FGD 3: 172. 1995; FYN 7: 106. 1997.

Tree to 18 m tall. Bark white, thick and soft, peeling off in thin layers. Branchlets greyish white. Leaves alternate, fragrant; petioles very short; leaf blade leathery, narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, 5 – 10 × 1 – 2 cm, acute at both ends, with many oil glands; basal veins 3 –5( – 7). Spikes pseudoterminal, 15 cm; rachis shortly hairy. Flowers white. Hypanthium ovoid, ca. 3 mm, pubescent or glabrous. Sepals orbicular, ca. 1 mm. Petals ovate, 2 – 3 × ca. 3 mm. Stamens ca. 1 cm. Style slightly longer than stamens. Capsule subglobose, 5 –7 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 30220, 35088, 35846.
Distribution: Native to Australia, widely cultivated in tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov.
Uses: Environmental, essential oil.
Notes: The species was reported as Melaleuca quinquenervia (Cav.) S. T. Blake previously (Check List HK Plants 163. 2002; 59. 2004).
