Environmental, essential oil.
Notes: The species was reported as Melaleuca quinquenervia (Cav.) S. T. Blake previously (Check List HK Plants 163. 2002; 59. 2004).

records.text:
Melastoma dodecandrum Lour. 地菍
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 274. 1790; FRPS 53(1): 154. 1984; K. Meyer, Blumea 46(2): 362. 2001.
Melastoma repens Desr., Encycl. 4(1): 54. 1797; FHK 113. 1861; FKH 106. 1912.

Perennial herb or subshrub, 10– 30 cm tall. Stems creeping or ascending, rooting at nodes, multibranched, sparsely covered with appressed bristles when young, later glabrous. Leaves opposite; petiole 2–6(–15) mm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 1–4 × 0.8–2(–3) cm, base broadly cuneate, apex rounded to acute, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces except some appressed bristles along the margin on adaxial surface, 3 – 5-basiveined. Inflorescences 1(–2)-flowered, in upper leaf axils. Pedicel 2 – 10 mm, strigose, with 2 bracteoles at apex; bracteoles ovate, abaxially strigose, margin ciliate. Calyx-tube ca. 5 mm, strigose; calyx-lobes lanceolate, 2–3 mm, sparsely strigose. Petals purplish red to purple, rhomboid-obovate, 1.2–2 × 1–1.5 cm, ciliate along the margin. Stamens dimorphic, outer ones with longer filaments than inner ones. Ovary adnate to the hypanthium for ca. 2/3 of its length, sparsely strigose. Fruit a berry, globose, ca. 7 × 10 mm, dark purple when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1811, 1841; L. T. Lo 104; N. K. Chun 40156 (IBSC); S. Y. Hu 13809 (IBSC); W. Y. Chun 6622 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Open fields, hillslopes, thickets, roadsides, alt. 900 m. Flowering: May– Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, food (fruit edible).

Melastoma intermedium Dunn 細葉野牡丹
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 38: 360. 1908; FKH 106. 1912; FHN 2: 26. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 154. 1984.

Subshrub, 20–30 cm tall. Stems creeping or ascending, multibranched, appressed strigose. Petioles 2–6 mm, strigose; leaf blade elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 2–4 × 1–1.5 cm, base acute to rounded, apex obtuse to acute, margin entire, papery, adaxially densely appressed strigose, the hairs immersed in epidermis with a projecting tip, abaxially sparsely strigose along veins, (3 – )5-basiveined. Inflorescences terminal or nearly terminal, corymbose, 3–5-flowered, with 2 foliaceous bracts at base. Pedicel 3–5 mm, densely strigose. Calyx-tube ca. 7 mm, ca. 5 mm in diam, densely strigose; calyx lobes lanceolate, ca. 7 mm, strigose abaxially, glabrous adaxially, with 1 lobule between the lobes. Petals purplish red, rhomboid-obovate, 1 – 1.4 cm, upper part ± oblique, minutely ciliate, apex ± emarginate, with a bundle of bristle. Stamens 10 or rarely more; anthers ovate-lanceolate, 2 – 2.2 mm; connective of longer stamens extended and with 2 tubercules at base, connective of shorter stamens not extended, with 2 tubercules at base. Ovary globose, 5-locular, apically hispidulous. Capsule, subglobose, ca. 10 mm in diam.; persistent calyx densely strigose.

Locality: Fei Ngo Shan Rd., Tai Mo Shan, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 10520; S. P. Lau 41; HK sheet 40827.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, banks of hillsides, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.– Sep.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.

Melastoma malabathricum L. 野牡丹

Sp. Pl. 1: 390. 1753; K. Meyer, Blumea 46(2): 364. 2001, p. p. excl. syn. M. intermedium Dunn; S. S. Renner et al., Fl. Thailand 7(3): 441. 2001.

Melastoma affine D. Don, Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 4: 288. 1823; FHN 2: 28. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 156. 1984.

Melastoma candidum D. Don, Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 4: 288. 1823; FKH 106. 1912; FHN 2: 27, fig. 300. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 157. 1984.

Melastoma macrocarpum auct. non D. Don: FHK 113. 1861; FKH 106. 1912, pro syn. sub M. candidum D. Don.

Melastoma septemnervium Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: t. 273. 1790.


Shrubs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems obtusely quadrangular or sub-terete, covered with appressed or slightly spreading scaly bristles. Leaves papery; petioles 5–15 mm, densely covered with scaly bristles; leaf blade ovate to elliptic-ovate, 4–10 × 2–6 cm, base shallowly cordate or sub-rounded, apex acute, margin entire, strigose or subvillous on both surfaces, 5–7-basiveined. Inflorescences terminal, 1–5-flowered cymes; each flower subtended by a pair of foliaceous bracts; bracts lanceolate or narrowly lanceolate, densely villous. Pedicel ca. 5 mm long. Calyx-tube ca. 1 cm long, densely covered with closely pressed chaffy bristles; calyx-lobes lanceolate, 8–12 mm, hairy on both sides. Petals bright purple to violet, obovate, 3–4 cm, apex rounded and ciliate. Stamens dimorphic, outer ones with longer filaments and connectives. Ovary about half of its length adnate to the calyx-tube, the free part densely strigose. Fruit urceolate-globose, 8–12 × 7–10 mm, densely covered with chaffy bristles.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3233; K. M. Lau 1331, 1332.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Indochina, Philippines, Australia.

Ecology: Secondary forests, hillslopes, roadsides, streamsides, thickets. Flowering: Feb. – May; fruiting: Aug. – Dec.

Notes: The species was reported as Melastoma affine D. Don and Melastoma candidum D. Don previously (Check List HK Plants 166. 2002; 60– 61. 2004).

Melastoma sanguineum Sims 毛菍
Bot. Mag. 48: pl. 2241. 1821; FKH 106. 1912; FHN 2: 27. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 161. 1984; K. Meyer, Blumea 46(2): 379. fig. 7. 2001; S. S. Renner et al., Fl. Thailand 7(3): 447. 2001.
Melastoma decemfidum Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 406. 1824; FHK 114. 1861.

Shrub, 1.5 – 3 m tall. Stems, branches, petioles and pedicels densely covered with spreading bristles up to 8 mm. Leaves papery; petiole 1–2.5(–4) cm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, (4.5–)8–15(–22) × (1.7–)2.5–5(–8) cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, strigose on both surfaces, with 2 pairs of lateral primary veins on each side of midvein. Flowers terminal, 5(–7)-merous, solitary or 3–5 in cymes. Pedicels 2– 5 mm. Calyx-tube 1–2 cm, densely covered with spreading red bristles; calyx-lobed, narrowly triangular to linear, 6–10 mm. Petals purple, broadly obovate, (2–)3 – 5 × (1.5–)2 – 2.2 cm, apically slightly oblique, apex emarginate. Stamens 10, rarely 8 or 12, dimorphic, outer anthers 12–15 mm, purple, connective prolongation 16–18 mm, inner anthers ca. 11 mm, purplish or yellow; connective not prolonged. Ovary crowned by golden bristles. Cupsule fleshy, 1.5–2.2 × 1.5–2 cm, dehiscing irregularly at maturity.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1924; S. P. Lau 134, 142; T. C. Chen et al 177 (IBSC); W. Y. Chun 5006, 5025 (IBSC); Y. Tsiang 277 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand and Malesia.
Ecology: Disturbed forests, streamsides, thickets on low hills, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: All year round, usually Aug. – Oct.

Melia azedarach L. 楝（苦楝）
Sp. Pl. 1: 384. 1753; FKH 58. 1912; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 566, fig. 2864. 1972; FHN 3: 61, fig. 566. 1974; FYN 1: 220, pl. 52: 8 – 10. 1977; FGD 2: 285. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 564. 1993.

Tree, to 10 m or taller. Bark brownish grey, longitudinally fissured. Leaves imparipinnate, bipinnate or tripinnate, 20–40 cm; leaflets opposite or alternate; blades ovate, elliptic, or lanceolate, 3–7 × 2–3 cm, base oblique, cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate to caudate, margin serrate, rarely entire, covered with stellate trichomes when young on both surfaces, glabrescent; lateral veins 12–16 on each side of midvein. Panicles shorter than or as long as leaves, glabrous or puberulous. Flowers slightly fragrant. Calyx 5-parted, pubescent; lobes ovate to oblong-ovate. Petals 5, lilac or pale blue, obovate-spathulate, ca. 1 cm, pubescent abaxially, glabrous or slightly pubescent adaxially. Staminal tube purple, 7–8 mm, glabrous or slightly hairy, apical margin with 10–12 dentate lobes; anthers 10–12, inserted at adaxial surface of lobes and alternate to lobes. Ovary subglobose, glabrous, 5–8-locular, ovules 2 per locule. Drupe globose to ellipsoidal, 1–2 × 1 cm, yellow when mature; endocarp bony. Seeds 1(–2), ellipsoidal, black when dry.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 539; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24054; HK sheet 39517.
Distribution: Area S of Yellow River; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, tropical Australia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Forests, open fields near villages, roadsides. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), raw material (industrial oil), timber.

Melicope pteleifolia (Champ. ex Benth.) T. G. Hartley 蜜茱萸（三椏苦）
FTW ed. 2, 3: 521. 1993.
Zanthoxylum pteleifolium Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 330. 1851, as ‘Xanthoxylum pteleaefoilum’.
Ilex lepta Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 496. 1825.
Lepta triphylla Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 82. 1790.
Evodia lepta (Spreng.) Merr., Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. 23: 219. 1915; FHN 3: 34, fig. 546. 1974; FTW 3: 514. 1977; FGD 2: 242, fig. 156. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 59, pl. 13. 1997.
Evodia lamarckiana Benth., FHK 59. 1861.
Evodia chunii Merr., J. Arnold Arb. 6: 132. 1925.
Evodia lepta var. chunii C. C. Huang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 6: 92. 1957.
Evodia triphylla auct. non DC.: FKH 55. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, 2–8 m tall. Bark grey. Juvenile branches flat. Leaves (1–)3-foliolate; petiole 1.5–14 cm; leaflet blade elliptic or oblong, sometimes obovate-elliptic, 6–12 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to subcaudate, margin entire and wavy, scattered with many small glandular dots, puberulous on midvein, especially abaxially. Inflorescences axillary, rarely terminal, 2–10 cm. Flowers unisexual or rarely bisexual, small. Petals white or pale yellow, ca. 1.5 mm, glandular-dotted. Male flower: stamens 4, filaments slightly longer than petals. Female flower: staminodes often with anthers but without pollens; ovary glabrous to pubescent, carpels connate at base. Fruit 1–4 basally connate follicles; follicles subglobose to obovoid, 3–7.5 mm, glabrous to puberulous. Seeds subglobose, 2.5 mm in diam., brownish black, glossy.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2095; Y. S. Lau 25; HK sheet 39951.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, Guizhou; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Secondary forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Gough, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Gough, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Melinis minutiflora P. Beauv. 糖蜜草
Ess. Agrostogr. 54. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 228, pl. 69. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 480. 2000; FYN 9: 548, fig. 94: 7–11. 2003; FOC 22: 539. 2006; FGD 9: 400, fig. 206. 2009.

Perennial herb, densely tomentose with glandular, slightly sticky hairs and a strong smell. Culms tufted, branched, rooting at lower nodes, 50–150 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, sparsely villous or tuberculate-pilose; leaf blades linear, 5–20 × 0.5–1.5 cm; ligule short, membranous, apex hairy. Panicle purplish, spreading, 10–20 cm. Spikelets narrowly ovate-oblong, ca. 2 mm, ± laterally compressed, glabrous; lower glume minute, veinless; upper glume oblong, 7-veined, 2-lobed, awnless or with a mucro to 1 mm from the sinus; lower floret neuter without a palea, lemma narrower oblong, 5-veined, 2-lobed, awnless or with a slender awn to 15 mm from the sinus; upper floret bisexual, lemma ovate-lanceolate, 3-veined, 2-lobed, hyaline; lodicules 2; styles 2. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: So Kon Po, Yau Tong Wan (locally naturalized). L. T. Lo 223; Y. S. Lau 2713; Y. W. Lam 1204.
Distribution: Yunnan, Taiwan; a fodder grass of Africa origin.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food.

Melinis repens (Willd.) Zizka 紅毛草
Biblioth. Bot. 138: 55. 1988; FOC 22: 539. 2006.
Saccharum repens Willd., Sp. Pl., ed. 4, 1: 322. 1797.
Rhynchelytrum repens (Willd.) C. E. Hubb., Kew Bull. 1934: 110. 1934; FRPS 10(1): 232, pl. 70. 1990; FFJ 6: 184, fig. 152. 1995; FTW ed, 2. 5: 507. 2000; FGD 9: 401. 2009; Check List HK Plants 345. 2002; 120. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, branched, up to 1(–1.5) m tall. Leaf sheaths loose, usually with tubercle-based hairs, mostly shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, up to 20 × 0.2–1.4 cm, glabrous; ligule a ring of long (ca. 1 mm ) hairs. Panicle silverypink or purple, ovate to oblong, 8–20 cm; branches capillary; pedicels with a few long hairs. Spikelets ovate, laterally compressed, 2–5 mm, densely villous, hairs up to 6 mm; lower glume narrowly oblong, 0.3–1.5 mm, 1-veined, with stiff short hairs; upper glume 5-veined, pink hairs, gibbous below middle, tapering upward into a glabrous membranous beak, emarginate, mucronate or with short awn up to 1 mm; lower floret staminate, lemma similar to upper glume but narrower and less gibbous, pink hairs, palea keels ciliate; upper floret whitish, ca. 2 mm, thinly cartilaginous, smooth, shining; lodicules 2; stamens 3, anthers 2 mm; styles 2, free, stigma plumose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong (naturalized). H. C. Tang 628; Y. S. Lau 754; HK sheet 14556.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; originated from tropical S Africa, now introduced into most warm countries.
Ecology: Grasslands, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Meliosma fordii Hemsl. 香皮樹
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 14. 1886; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 118. 1985; FGD 1: 268, fig. 297. 1987.
Meliosma hainanensis How, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3: 433. 1955.

Tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and inflorescences brownish pubescent. Leaves simple, subleathery; petioles 1.5 – 3.5 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate or lanceolate, 9 –18(–25) × 2.5 – 5(– 8) cm, base narrowly cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes with a few teeth near apex, adaxially more or less shining, appressed pubescent on midvein and lateral veins, abaxially sparsely pubescent; lateral veins 11–20. Panicles terminal or subterminal, 4–5-branched. Flowers 1–1.5 mm in diam. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm. Sepals 4(–5), broadly ovate, 0.5 mm, sparsely pubescent abaxially, ciliolate. Petals white, outer 3 suborbicular, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., inner 2 smaller, bifid halfway at an obtuse angle; lobes linear. Ovary glabrous, style about the length of ovary. Drupes subglobose or compressed globose, 3–5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 339; HK sheet 32241.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Guizhou, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Meliosma rigida Sieb. & Zucc. 筆羅子
Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss., Math.-Naturwiss. Kl. 4(2): 153. 1845; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 117. 1985; FGD 1: 267, fig. 296. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 3: 612. 1993.
Meliosma patens Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 145. 1886; FKH 68. 1912.
Meliosma glomerulata Rehd. & Wils., Sargent Pl. Wils. 2: 203. 1914.

Tree, to 7 m tall. Young branches, bud scales and inflorescences rusty tomentose. Leaves simple, leathery; petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate or narrow obovate, 8–25 × 2.5–4.5 cm, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate, tapering from middle into a cuneate base, margin entire or with a few teeth above middle, adaxially glabrous except the puberulous midvein and lateral veins, abaxially rusty pubescent; lateral veins 9–18 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, erect, thrice branched. Flowers sessile, 3–4 mm in diam. Sepals 4(–5), ovate or suborbicular, unequal, ciliolate. Petals white, outer 3 suborbicular, 2–2.5 mm in diam., inner 2 bifid halfway at an acute angle, lobes acute, apex ciliolate. Ovary glabrous; style 2 times the length of the ovary. Drupes globose, 5–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Po Kau, Tai To Yan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1262, 2978.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Guizhou, SW Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Meliosma squamulata Hance 樟葉泡花樹
J. Bot. 1: 364. 1876; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 111. 1985; FGD 1: 265, fig. 294. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 3: 612, pl. 314. 1993.

Evergreen small tree, to 15 m tall. Young shoots appressed pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves simple, thin leathery; petioles slender, 2.5– 6.5(–10) cm; leaf blades elliptic or ovate, 5 –12 × 1.5 –5 cm, base cuneate, more or less decurrent, apex caudate-acuminate, tip blunt, margin entire, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially glaucous, densely covered with yellowish brown tiny scales; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal or axillary, 7–20 cm, densely tawny pubescent. Flowers white, 3 mm in diam. Sepals 5, ovate, ciliolate. Petals glabrous, outer 3 suborbicular, 2.5 mm in diam. inner 2 ca. 1 mm, bifid to middle, lobes acute divaricate. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style ca. 1 mm. Drupes globose or obovoid, 4– 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 299; HK sheet 1216.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, S Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Timber.

Meliosma thorelii Lecomte 山檨葉泡花樹
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 54: 677. 1907; FRPS 47(1): 109. 1985; FGD 1: 265, fig. 293. 1987.
Meliosma buchananifolia Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 23: 250. 1923.
Meliosma affinis Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 21: 375. 1940.
Meliosma henryi Diels subsp. thorelii (Lecomte) Beusekom, Blumea 19: 449. 1971.
Meliosma simplicifolia auct. non Walp.: Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 119. 1927.

Tree, 6–14 m tall. Leaves simple, subleathery; petioles 1.5–2 cm; leaf blades oblanceolate-elliptic or oblanceolate, 15–25 × 4–8 cm, base cuneate, decurrent to the petioles, apex acuminate, margin entire or sharply serrulate, glabrous or sparsely pubescent abaxially and barbate in axils of nerves; lateral veins 15 –22 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins raised on both surfaces. Panicles terminal or axillary, erect, 15 –18 cm, branches flatted, brownish pubescent. Flowers fragrant, 2–2.5 mm in diam., shortly pedicellate. Sepals 5, ovate, 0.6–0.8 mm, apex obtuse, ciliolate. Petals white, outer 3 suborbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam., inner 2 narrow lanceolate, entire, shorter than the outer ones. Ovary pubescent; style ca. 1 mm. Drupes globose, slightly oblique, 6–9 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7221, 8588.
Distribution: SE Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Guizhou, SE to SW Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Melochia corchorifolia L. 馬鬆子
Sp. Pl. 675. 1753; FHN 2: 82. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 167. 1984; FGD 1: 143. 1987.

Subshrub, less than 1 m tall. Branchlets slightly stellatepubescent. Stipules linear, 2– 4 mm. Petioles 5 –25 mm; leaves thinly papery, ovate, oblong-ovate or lanceolate, rarely indistinctly 3-lobed, 2.5 –7 × 1–1.3 cm, base rounded or cordate, margin serrate, apex acute or obtuse, nearly glabrous adaxially, slightly stellate-pubescent abaxially, 5-veined. Cymes or glomes terminal or axillary; bracteoles linear; calyx campanulate, slightly 5- lobed, hairy; petals reddish, oblong, ca. 6 mm, base attenuate; ovary densely pubescent. Capsules globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., 5-angulate, pilose. Seeds brown-black, subtriangular, 2–3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong, Ma Liu Shui, Fanling, Ho Pui, Sha Po, Tuen Mun. Y. W. Lam 673; L. T. Lo 221; W. J. Tutcher 11554.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Fibre.

Melodinus fusiformis Champ. ex Benth. 尖山橙
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 332. 1852; FHK 218. 1861; FKH 167. 1912; FRPS 63: 29. 1977; FGD 1: 431, fig. 477. 1987; FOC 16: 150. 1995.

Lianas stout, to 10 m, juvenile parts pubescent, glabrous when older. Bark grey‑brown. Petioles 4–6 mm; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, rarely narrowly elliptic, 4.5–12 × 1–5.3 cm, somewhat leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate; lateral veins ca. 15 on each side of midvein, obliquely spreading and reticulate toward margin. Cymes terminal, 3–5 cm, 6–12‑flowered. Pedicels 5 – 10 mm. Sepals ovate, 4–5 mm, acute. Corolla white; tube 1.2–2 cm; lobes obliquely narrow ovate or obovate, (0.8–)1.1–2 cm × 3.5–9 mm; corona scales 5, indistinct, apices 2‑ or 3‑cleft, exserted, villous. Stamens inserted near base of corolla tube. Berries fusiform, 3.5 – 5.3 × 2.2 – 4 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Victoria Peak, Wong Chuk Yeung, Ng Tung Chai, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 394; HK sheet 38556, 40138.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou.
Ecology : Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Melodinus suaveolens (Hance) Champ. ex Benth. 山橙
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 333. 1852; FHK 218. 1861; FKH 167. 1912; FRPS 63: 22, pl. 7. 1977; FGD 1: 430, fig. 476. 1987; FOC 16: 148. 1995.
Lycimnia suaveolens Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3(1): 31. 1852.
Melodinus monogynus auct. non Roxb.: FHK 218. 1861; FKH 167. 1912.

Lianas to 10 m, glabrous except for inflorescences. Petioles to 1.2 cm; leaf blade elliptic or ovate, 5–10 × 1.8–5 cm, leathery, base attenuate to rounded, apex short acuminate. Cymes terminal and axillary. Flower buds rounded or obtuse at apex, minutely pubescent outside. Flowers fragrant. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm, minutely pubescent abaxially, apex rounded or obtuse. Corolla white; tube 1–1.4 cm; lobes shorter than or as long as tube, suborbicular, falcate, with a distinct notch near apex; corona campanulate or tubular, apex 5‑cleft, exserted from throat. Berries globose, 5–8 cm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 454, 3070; HK sheet 39868.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Open forests, humid thickets; 100 – 800 m. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley Woods between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley Woods between 1847 and 1850.

Memecylon ligustrifolium Champ. ex Benth. 谷木
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 117. 1852; FHK 117. 1861; FHN 2: 40. 1965; FKH 108. 1912; FRPS 53(1): 289. 1984.

Shrub or small tree, 1.5 – 5(–7) m tall, many-branched. Branchlets terete or sometimes quadrangular. Petiole 3 – 5 mm. Leaf blade leathery, elliptic, ovate, or ovate-lanceolate, 5.5–8 × 2.5–3.5 cm, glabrous, base cuneate, apex acuminate with an obtuse tip, margin entire, midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins inconspicuous. Inflorescences axillary, cymose, ca. 1 cm. Peduncle 1–3 mm; bracts ovate, ca. 1 mm. Pedicels 1 – 4 mm, bearded at base and nodes. Calyx-tube hemispherical, 1.5–3 mm; calyx-teeth 4, very broad and short. Petals white or yellowish green or purple, suborbicular, ca. 3 × 4 mm. Stamens blue, ca. 4.5 mm; theca and conical connective 1 – 2 mm. Ovary inferior, ovoid, apex truncate. Fruit a baccate drupe, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., densely tuberculate, apex with an annular persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 132, 441; K. Y. Tam 124; C. Wang 32396 (IBSC); W. Y. Chun 6805, 5105 (IBSC); N. K. Chun 40266, 40202, 40084 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, mountain slopes, valleys, damp places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.– Feb.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in Jan. 1850.

Memecylon nigrescens Hook. & Arn. 黑葉谷木

Bot. Beechey Voy. 186. 1833; FKH 108. 1912; FHN 2: 41. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 293. 1984.


Shrub or small tree, 2–8 m tall, multibranched. Branchlets terete, glabrous. Petiole 2–3 mm. Leaf blade papery, brownish yellow-green when dry, elliptic or rarely ovate-oblong, 3–6.5 × 1.5–3 cm, both surfaces glabrous and glossy, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, sometimes with a retuse tip, margin entire, midvein depressed adaxially, lateral veins slightly raised abaxially. Inflorescences axillary, cymose, nearly capitate, less than 1 cm, 2–3-branched, many-flowered. Peduncle very short; bracts very small, caducous. Pedicel ca. 0.5 mm, glabrous. Calyx-tube shallowly cup-shaped, ca. 1.5 × 2 mm, glabrous, apex truncate and shallowly 4-lobed. Petals blue or white, broadly lanceolate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, base unguiculate, apex acuminate, margin irregularly 1–2-dentate. Stamens ca. 2 mm; filaments 1.2–1.5 mm; theca and conical connective ca. 0.8 mm, Fruit a berry-like drupe, black when dry, globular, 6–7 mm in diam., apex with annular persistent calyx.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. N. K. Chun 40208; Y. S. Lau 406; F. W. Xing 8262;W. Y. Chun 3150 (IBSC).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.

Ecology: Forests, thickets, hillsides. Flowering: May – Jun.; fruiting: Dec. – Feb.

Mentha canadensis L. 薄荷
Sp. Pl. 2: 577. 1753; FOC 17: 237. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 487, pl. 214. 1998.
Mentha haplocalyx Briq., Bull. Soc. Bot. Geneve, ser. 2, 5: 39. 1889; FRPS 66: 262, pl. 60. 1977; FGD 3: 442. 1995.
Mentha arvensis auct. non L.: Benth., FHK 276. 1861; FKH 209. 1912.

Perennial aromatic herbs, 30–60 cm tall, with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, ± hoary with adpressed retrorse hairs. Petioles 2–10 mm, puberulent; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, lanceolate to elliptic or ovate‑lanceolate, 3–5(– 7) × 0.8–3 cm, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acute, margin remotely coarse dentate‑serrate, sparingly puberulous on adaxial surface or only on the veins, often densely puberulous on veins of abaxial surface. Verticillasters axillary, globose, ca. 1.8 cm in diam. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 2.5–3 mm, puberulous and glandular abaxially, glabrous adaxially, obscurely 10‑veined; teeth subequal, lanceolate or subulate. Corolla purplish or white, 4–5 mm, puberulent abaxially. Nutlets ellipsoidal, finely granular.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 8119; Y. S. Lau 2621; HK sheet 39283.
Distribution: Widely distributed in all provinces of China; also in Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Russia (Far East) and N America.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Material (essential oils), spice, medicinal (folklore).

Merremia dissecta (Jacq.) Hallier f. 多裂魚黃草
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16: 552. 1893; FRPS 64(1): 68. 1979; FOC 16: 294. 1995.
Convolvulus dissectus Jacq., Observ. Bot. 2: 4. 1767.
Ipomoea dissecta Willd., Phytogr. 5, t. 2. 1794; FKH 181. 1912.
Ipomoea sinuata Ortega, Nov. Pl. Descr. Dec. 7: 84. 1798
Operculina dissecta (Jacq.) House, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 33: 500. 1906.

Semi‑woody vine. Stems woody basally, tuberculate, ± yellowish spreading hirsute, glabrescent. Petiole 2.5–7 cm; leaf blade palmately 5–7‑divided nearly to base; segments lanceolate, middle 2.5–10 × 0.5–3 cm, lateral ones smaller, apex mucronulate, margin coarsely dentate to irregularly pinnately lobed, glabrous or pubescent along veins abaxially. Cymes 1 – several‑flowered. Peduncle 5–10 cm. Pedicel 1.5–2 cm, thicker distally, minutely tuberculate, glabrous. Sepals subequal, ovate‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 cm, enlarged and leathery in fruit, glabrous. Corolla white, with purple‑red throat, funnelform, midpetaline bands distinct. Ovary glabrous. Capsule globose, glabrous. Seeds black, glabrous.

Locality: Stubbs Rd., Tai Hang. Y. S. Lau 215; H. C. Tang 1895.
Distribution: Coastal Islands of Guangdong; India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Thailand; native in N & S America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Nov.

Merremia hederacea (Burm. f.) Hallier f. 魚黃草
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 18: 118. 1894; FGZ 584. 1956; FHN 3: 480. 1974; FTW 4: 383. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 61. 1979; FFJ 4: 487, fig. 389. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 378. 1998; FGD 4: 347. 2000.
Evolvulus hederaceus Burm. f., Fl. Indica 77, t. 30, fig. 2. 1768.
Convolvulus chryseides (Ker Gawl.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 598. 1825.
Ipomoea chryseides Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 4: pl. 270. 1818; FHK 239. 1861; FKH 180. 1912.
Lepistemon glaber Hand.‑Mazz., Sinensia 5(1 – 2): 7. 1934.
Merremia chryseides (Ker Gawl.) Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552. in obs. 1893.
Merremia convolvulacea Dennst. ex Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552. in obs. 1893.347. 2000.

Twining or prostrate herb. Stems often minutely tuberculate, glabrous or sparsely hirsute. Petiole 1–5 cm, glabrous or pubescent; leaf blade ovate, 1.5–6 × 1.5–4 cm, base cordate or broadly cordate, irregularly crenate, or 3‑lobed, margin entire, subglabrous to spar sely puberulent on both sur faces . Cymes (1–)several – many‑flowered, umbelliform. Peduncle slender, 1–7 cm, thicker than petiole. Bracts caducous, minute, narrowly obovate. Pedicel 2–5 mm, glabrous or sometimes tuberculate. Sepals unequal, broadly obovate to spatulate or oblong, reflexed in fruit; outer 2 sepals 3.5–4 mm, apex emarginate, mucronate, glabrous, sometimes hairy along margin; inner 3 ca. 5 mm. Corolla yellow, campanulate, 6–10 mm, villous at base adaxially, glabrous abaxially, midpetaline bands 5‑veined, glabrous. Filaments dilated and sparsely villous at base. Ovary globose, glabrous; stigma globose. Capsule compressed globose or broadly conical, 5–6 mm, reticulate or wrinkled when dry. Seeds trigonous‑globose, 2.5–3.5 mm, puberulent, woolly along angles and at hilum.

Locality: Wah Fu Tsuen, Sai Kung, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Tai Wai, Ta Kwu Ling, Sham Tseng. L. T. Lo 528; P. S. Choi 425; Y. W. Lam 396.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Yunnan; tropical Asia, tropical Africa, Mascarene Islands, N Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thickets, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Merremia hirta (L.) Merr. 毛山豬菜
Philipp. J. Sci. 7: 224. 1912; FGZ 584. 1956; FHN 3: 481. 1974; FTW 4: 384. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 63, pl. 14: 2 – 4. 1979; FOC 16: 294. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 378. 1998; FGD 4: 348. 2000.
Convolvulus hirtus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753.
Ipomoea linifolia Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 13: 721. 1825; FKH 181. 1912.
Lepistemon decurrens Hand.‑Mazz., Sinensia 5(1 – 2): 6. 1934.
Merremia decurrens (Hand.‑Mazz.) H. S. Kiu, FHN 3: 586. 1974.

Twining or prostrate herb. Stems rooting at nodes or internodes, spreading yellow hirsute to glabrous. Petiole 1 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade variable in shape, linear, oblong‑lanceolate, ovate‑oblong, or ovate, 1.5 – 5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base truncate, rounded, ± auriculate to hastate, apex obtuse, acute or slightly emarginate and mucronulate, margin entire, sparsely appressed hirsute or glabrous. Cymes 1–4(–8)‑flowered. Peduncle slender, 1–2.5 cm, sparsely pubescent at base. Bracts persistent, ovate, 1–2 mm, glabrous. Pedicel 3 – 10 mm, glabrous. Sepals unequal, elliptic or elliptic‑oblong; outer 2 sepals 3–5 mm; inner 3 ca. 6 mm, apex obtuse. Corolla pale yellow or whitish, campanulate, 1–2 cm, midpetaline bands 5‑veined, glabrous abaxially. Stamens inclusive; filaments dilated and pubescent at base. Ovary glabrous. Capsule broadly ovoid to globose, 6–7 mm; pericarp thinly papery, glabrous. Seeds brownish black, trigonous‑ellipsoidal, ca. 3 mm, glabrous or sparsely floccose at margin and hilum.

Locality: Tai Po. Aubrey 11571.
Distribution: Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Sikkim, Thailand, Malaysia, N Australia.
Ecology: Grasslands and margins of forests.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Merremia quinata (R. Br.) Ooststr. 指葉山豬菜
J. Arnold Arbor. 29: 417. 1948; FHN 3: 482. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 66, pl. 1. 1979; FTW 4: 384. 1978; FFJ 4: 489, fig. 390. 1989; FOC 6: 294. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 379. 1998; FGD 4: 346. 2000.
Ipomoea quinata R. Br., Prodr. 486. 1810; FHK 237. 1861; FKH 181. 1912.
Convolvulus quinatus (R. Br.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 590. 1825.
Ipomoea pentadactylis Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 471. 1833.

Perennial twining herb. Stems slender, yellow spreading hirsute. Petiole 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade palmately compound; leaflets 5, linear‑lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 1.5–4 × 0.5–1 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse and mucronulate, entire, margin entire, often glabrous on both surfaces, sometimes hirsute along midvein and margin abaxially. Cymes 1(–2)‑flowered. Peduncle nearly as long as petiole, glabrous or hirsute at base. Pedicel 5 ‑6 mm. Bracts ovate‑triangular, 2–4 mm. Sepals thickly papery, unequal, elliptic to ovate‑oblong, glabrous; outer 2 sepals 8–10 mm; inner ones ca. 1.1–1.5 cm. Corolla white or pale yellow, campanulate or funnelform, ca. 3–4 cm, midpetaline bands 5‑veined, glabrous. Ovary glabrous. Capsule ovoid, 1–1.3 cm. Seeds oblong, 4–6 mm, pale yellow pubescent at apex.

Locality: Deep Water Bay. W. J. Tutcher 11726.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia, N Australia.
Ecology: Sunny places of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Merremia tuberosa (L.) Rendle 木玫瑰
Fl. Trop. Afr. 4(2): 104. 1905; FTW ed. 2, 4: 379. 1998; FGD 4: 346. 2000.
Ipomoea tuberosa L., Sp. Pl. 1: 160. 1753.

Woody vine. Stems glabrous. Petiole glabrous; leaf blade palmately compound; leaflets 5, lanceolate to elliptic, central one larger, 6–12 cm, apex acuminate, entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Cymes axillary, (1–)several‑flowered. Peduncles 3 – 10 cm, glabrous. Pedicels ca. 1 cm, gradually thickened upward, glabrous. Sepals unequal, oblong, glabrous, outer ones 2.5 cm, apex obtuse; inner ones ca. 3 cm. Corolla yellow, campanulate, ca. 5 cm, midpetaline bands glabrous. Stamens inclusive. Capsules subglobose, ca. 3 cm in diam., irregularly dehiscing. Seeds black, tomentellus.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. Y. S. Lau 205, 809.
Distribution: Native to tropical Africa, cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Merremia umbellata (L.) Hallier f. subsp. orientalis (Hallier f.) Ooststr. 山豬菜
Fl. Malesiana, ser. 1, Spermatoph. 4(4): 449. 1953; FHN 3: 483, fig. 872. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 72, pl. 16: 3–5. 1979; FFJ 4: 488. 1989; OC 16: 297. 1995; FGD 4: 347. 2000.
Merremia umbellata (L.) Hallier f. var. orientalis Hallier f., Verslag Staat Lands Plantentuin Buitenzorg 132. 1895 (1896).
Ipomoea cymosa auct. non Roem. & Schult.: FHK 238. 1861; FKH 180. 1912.
Ipomoea fulvicoma Hance, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 176. 1849.

Twining herb. Stems densely pubescent or subglabrous. Petiole 1–10 cm, pubescent; leaf blade variable in shape, ovate, ovate‑oblong, or oblong‑lanceolate, 4–14 × 1.5–10 cm, base cordate, rarely hastate, apex emarginate, acute to acuminate, margin entire, sparsely puberulent or subglabrous adaxially, pale greyish pubescent abaxially. Cymes umbelliform, several–many‑flowered. Peduncle 1–6 cm, densely pubescent. Bracts caducous, lanceolate, minute, 2–3 mm. Pedicel 0.5–2 cm. Sepals slightly unequal, thinly leathery, strongly concave; outer 2 broadly elliptic or nearly circular, 0.8–1.4 cm, rounded or emarginate, abaxially pubescent; inner ones usually slightly longer. Corolla white, sometimes yellow, funnelform, 2.5–5.5 cm, midpetaline bands inconspicuously 5‑veined, with a strip of whitish pubescence at apex; limb slightly lobed. Stamens inclusive; anthers not twisted. Ovary glabrous or sparsely pubescent apically. Capsule conical‑ovoid, ca. 1 cm; pericarp glabrous. Seeds ca. 5 mm, densely spreading villous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1457; L. T. Lo 418; Y. S. Lau 3273.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical E Africa, N Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thin forests, thickets or roadsides. Flowering: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Mesona chinensis Benth. 涼粉草
FHK 274. 1861; FKH 207. 1912; FRPS 66: 547, pl. 116. 1977; FOC 17: 294. 1994; FGD 3: 470, fig. 293. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 487, pl. 215. 1998.

Annual herbs. Stems erect or decumbent, 15–100 cm, slightly pubescent or hairy, glabrescent. Leaves opposite; petiole 2–15 mm; leaf blade oblong‑ovate to broadly ovate, 2–5 × 0.8–2.8 cm, base cuneate to sometimes rounded, apex acute to obtuse, margin serrate, finely hispid, pubescent, or only hairy along veins abaxially. Verticillasters forming interrupted or nearly continuous terminal racemes of 2–10(–13) cm; floral leaves or bracts ovate or lanceolate, scarcely longer than the flowers, mostly coloured at the base. Pedicel 3 – 4( – 5) mm, short hairy. Calyx 2–2.5 mm in flower, densely white pilose, middle lobe of upper lip acute to obtuse, lower lip sometimes emarginate; fruiting calyx 3–5 mm, subglabrous or hairy on veins, deeply reticulate and pitted between the veins. Corolla white or reddish, ca. 3 mm, puberulent, throat inflated; upper lip 4‑lobed, lateral 2 lobes distinct, longer than middle lobes, or upper lip subentire. Nutlets black, oblong.

Locality: Shek O, Tai Tam Tuk, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 679, 779, 3012.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Ravines, grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: The decoction of dried plants mixed with starch and water is used to make a jelly‑like cooling drink in S China.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wilford from “Saywan” (Chai Wan) between 1857 and 1858.

Metasequoia glyptostroboides Hu & W. C. Cheng 水杉
Bull. Fan Mem. Inst. Biol., n.s. 1: 154. 1948; FRPS 7: 310, pl. 71. 1978; FOC 4: 60. 1999; FGD 4: 24, fig. 14. 2000.

Tree to 50 m tall; trunk buttressed at base, to 2.5 m d.b.h.; bark of young trees pale orange-brown, dark reddish brown to grey, fissured; branches ascending; branchlets pendulous; winter buds ovoid or ellipsoid, apex obtuse, scales yellowish brown. Leaves linear, (0.8–)1.3–2 (–3.5) cm × (1–)1.5–2(–2.5) mm, pale green, with 4–8 stomatal bands along midvein each side. Pollen cones ovoid, 2.5 –5.5 × 2–3.8 mm; bracts triangular-ovate or obovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm, lowest minutely ciliate distally, others glabrous. Seed cones purplish black when young, oblong-ellipsoid and to 9 × 5.5 mm at pollination, subglobose and 1.4 –2.5 × 1.6 –2.3 cm when mature; basal cone scales 9-ovulate, middle 7-ovulate, distal 5-ovulate, apical sterile. Seeds ca. 5 × 4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 429; HK sheet 40548.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China. Native to E Sichuan & NW Hubei.
Ecology: Pollinating: Jan.–Mar.; seed maturing: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Michelia champaca L. 黃蘭
Sp. Pl. 536. 1753; FGZ 81. 1956; FHN 1: 227. 1964; FGD 1: 12, fig. 9: 1–7. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 157, fig. 40: 1–7. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 10 m or taller; buds, young twigs, young leaves and petioles covered with pale yellow appressed hairs. Stipular scars exceeding middle of petioles. Petioles 2– 4 cm. Leaves lanceolate-ovate or lanceolate-long elliptic, 10 –20(–25) × 4.5 –9 cm, base broadly cuneate or cuneate, apex long acuminate or subcaudate, abaxially slightly puberulous. Flowers yellow, fragrant, tepals 15–20, oblanceolate, 2–4 × 0.4 – 0.5 cm; connectives exserted and forming a long tip; gynoecium hairy; gynoecium stalk ca. 3 mm. Aggregate fruit 7–15 cm; follicles obovoid-ellipsoid, 1–1.5 cm, tuberculate; seeds 2– 4, rugose.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 2617; HK sheet 820.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, cultivated in Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan and Taiwan; India, Nepal, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Michelia chapensis Dandy 樂昌含笑（景烈含笑）
Journ. Bot. 67: 222. 1929; FGD 1: 17, fig. 16. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 170, pl. 45: 7–9. 1996.
Michelia tsoi Dandy, J. Bot. 68: 213. 1930.

Tree, up to 15–30 m tall; bark grey to dark brown; twigs glabrous or greyish puberulous on nodes when young. Petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm, without stipular scar, adaxially furrowed, puberulous when young, glabrescent. Leaves obovate, narrowly obovate or oblong-obovate, 6.5–15(–16) × 3.5 –6.5(–7) cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex abruptly short-acuminate, tip blunt, adaxially deep green and glossy; lateral veins 9 –12(15) on each side of midvein. Peduncles 0.4 –1 cm, puberulous, with 2–5 bract scar. Flowers fragrant; tepals 6, pale yellow, in 2 whorls, outer 3 obovate-elliptic, ca. 3 × 1.5 cm; inner 3 narrower; stamens 1.7–2 cm, anthers 1.1–1.5 cm, connectives exserted and forming a 1 mm mucro; gynoecium narrowly cylindrical, ca. 1.5 cm; gynophore ca. 7 mm, densely covered with silvery appressed hairs; carpels ovoid, ca. 2 mm, styles ca. 1.5 mm; ovules 6 in each carpel. Aggregate fruit ca. 10 cm, fruiting peduncle ca. 2 mm; follicles ellipsoid or ovoid, 1–1.5 × 1 cm, base broad, apex with short and curved tip; seeds red, ovoid or ellipsoid-ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.6 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. N. H. Li 56; G. Barretto 283.
Distribution: Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Michelia figo (Lour.) Spreng. 含笑
Syst. Veg. 2: 643. 1825; FGZ 82. 1956; FHN 1: 227. 1964; FGD 1: 12, fig. 10: 1– 6. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 165, pl. 43: 1– 6. 1996.
Liriodendron figo Lour. Fl. Cochinch. 1: 347. 1790.
Magnolia fuscata Andr., Bot. Repos. 4: t. 229. 1802.
Magnolia figo (Lour.) DC., Syst. Nat. 1: 460. 1817.
Michelia fuscata Bl. ex Wall., Fl. Javae 19-20: 8. 1829; FKH 28. 1912.
Liriopsis fuscata (Andr.) Spach, Hist. Nat. Veg. 7: 461. 1839.

Evergreen shrub, 2–3 m tall, much branched; buds, young twigs, petioles and peduncles densely yellowish brown-tomentose. Stipular scars reached petiole apex. Petioles 2–4 mm. Leaves narrowly elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 4–10 × 1.8–4.5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex obtusely acute, adaxially glossy and glabrous, abaxially covered with brown appressed hairs on midvein, other parts glabrescent. Flowers erect, sweet fragrant; tepals 6, fleshy, thick, long-elliptic, 1.2–2.0 × 0.6 –1.1 cm, pale yellow, margin sometimes red or purple; stamens 7–8 mm, connectives exserted and forming a sharp tip; gynoecium glabrous, ca. 7 mm, exceeding androecium; gynoecium stalk ca. 6 mm, pale yellow tomentose. Aggregate fruit 2–3.5 cm; follicles ovoid or globose, apex beaked.

Locality: Widely cultivated in gardens. Y. W. Lam 204; F. W. Xing 8626.
Distribution: S China, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul. –Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Michelia maudiae Dunn 深山含笑（莫氏含笑）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 38: 353. 1908; FKH 28. 1912; FGD 1: 14, fig.12. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 179. 1996.
Michelia chingii W. C. Cheng, Contr. Biol. Lab. Chin. Assoc. Advancem. Sci., Sect. Bot. 10: 110. 1936.

Tree, up to 20 m tall, glabrous. Buds, young twigs, abaxial surfaces of leaves, bracts white farinose. Petioles 1–3 cm, without stipular scars. Leaves oblong-elliptic, rarely elliptic-oblong, 7–18 × 3.5–8.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex abruptly short-acuminate, tip blunt, adaxially deep green and glossy, abaxially greyish green and glaucous; lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Peduncles green, with 3 annular bract scars; spathose bracts pale brown, thinly leathery, ca. 3 cm. Flowers fragrant; tepals 9, purely white, slightly pale red at base, outer 3 obovate, 5–7 × 3.5–4 cm, base clawed, apex acute, inner 6 narrower, nearly spoon-shaped, apex acute; stamens 1.5–2.2 cm, filaments flat, pale purple, ca. 4 mm, connectives exserted and forming a 1–2 mm tip; gynoecium 1.5–1.8 cm; gynophore 5–8 mm; carpels green, narrowly ovoid, 5–6 mm including style. Aggregate fruit 7–15 cm; follicles ellipsoid, obovoid, ovoid, apex obtuse or abruptly mucronate. Seeds red, obliquely ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.5 cm, slightly compressed.

Locality: Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2952; L. T. Lo 316.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Fujian, Zhejiang, Hunan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Timber; ornamental.
Notes: The lectotype specimen (S. T. Dunn s.n. in Herb. Hongk. No. 2065, HK sheet 834) was collected from “Fung Wong Shan” (Lantau Peak), Lantau Island in 1905. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Michelia odora (Chun) B. L. Chen & Noot. 觀光木
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 80(4): 1086. 1993.
Tsoongiodendron odorum Chun, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 283. 1963; FHN 1: 230. 1964; FGD 1: 20, fig. 20. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 194, pl. 55. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 25 m tall; twigs, buds, petioles, abaxial surfaces of leaves and peduncles yellowish brown-strigose. Stipular scars nearly reached middle of petioles. Petioles 1.2–2.5 cm, flattened at base. Leaves obovate-elliptic, 8 –17 × 3.5–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, adaxially green and glossy; lateral veins 10–12 on each side of midvein; midvein, lateral veins and reticulations impressed adaxially. Spathose bract dehiscing along one side, pubescent. Peduncles 6 mm, with 1 bract scar. Flowers fragrant; tepals ivory-yellow, dotted with red, narrowly obovate-elliptic, outer ones largest, 1.7–2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, innermost ones 1.5–1.6 × 0.5 cm; stamens 35–45, 7.5–8.5 mm, filaments white or reddish, 2–3 mm; carpels 9–13, narrowly ovoid, densely appressed pubescent, styles subulate, red, ca. 2 mm, ventral sutures conspicuous; gynophore stout, ca. 2 mm, sulcate, densely strigose. Aggregate fruit long-ellipsoid, sometimes globose because of upper carpels aborted, 13 × 9 cm, pericarp olive-green, dark brown when dried, markedly yellow-dotted; valves thick, 1–2 cm; fruiting: peduncle 1–2 × 1–2 cm; seeds 4– 6 in each carpel, ellipsoid or triangular-obovoid, ca. 1.5 × 0.8 cm.

Locality: A rare species in Hong Kong, only found in Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7898, 8928; Y. W. Lam 199.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Michelia × alba DC. 白蘭
Syst. 1: 449. 1818; FGZ 81, fig. 23. 1956; FHN 1: 226. 1964; FGD 1: 12, fig. 9: 8 –9. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 159, fig. 40: 8 –14. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 17 m tall; bark grey; young twigs and buds densely covered with pale yellowish white hairs. Stipular scars nearly reached middle of petioles. Petioles 1.5–2 cm, sparsely puberulous. Leaves long-elliptic or lanceolate-elliptic, 10–27 × 4–9.5 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate, apex long acuminate or caudate-acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely puberulous, reticulations of veins very conspicuous on both surfaces when dry. Flowers white, very fragrant; tepals 10, lanceolate, 3–4 × 0.3–0.5 cm; connectives exserted and forming a long tip; gynoecium puberulous, gynoecium stalk ca. 4 mm; carpels numerous, usually undeveloped.

Locality: Widely cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1840; L. T. Lo 96.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China and tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Microcarpaea minima (K. D. Koenig ex Retz.) Merr. 小果草
Philipp. J. Sci. 7(2): 100. 1912; FOC 18: 49. 2000; FGD 4: 370. 2000.
Paederota minima K. D. Koenig ex Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 10. 1789.
Microcarpaea muscosa R. Br., Prodr. 435. 1810; FHK 253. 1861; FKH 189. 1912.

Annual herbs, cushion‑like. Stems prostrate, slender, filiform, base 4‑angled, many‑branched, striate, glabrous. Leaves opposite, sessile, amplexicaul, linear to narrowly oblong, 3–6 × 1–2 mm, margin entire, somewhat thickened; glabrous on both surfaces, punctuate above, veins inconspicuous. Flowers solitary and axillary, sessile. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1.5 mm, lobes deltoid‑ovate, sparsely ciliate. Corolla pink, 2–3 mm, upper lip erect, lower lip spreading. Stamens 2. Capsules ovoid, shorter than calyx. Seeds brownish yellow, ca. 0.3 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tsiu Hang, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling. L. T. Lo 534; Y. W. Lam 332, 1238.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Jul. –Oct.

Microchloa indica (L. f.) P. Beauv. 小草
Ess. Agrostogr. Expl. Pl. 13. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 87. 1990; FFJ 6: 163. 1995; FOC 22: 492. 2006; FGD 9: 378, fig. 187. 2009.
Microchloa setacea R. Br., Prodr. 208. 1810; FHK 428. 1861; FKH 326. 1912.

Perennial herb, 10–20 cm tall. Culms very slender, densely tufted and clothed at base with fibres of disintegrated leaf sheaths. Leaves mostly basal; leaf blades narrowly linear, 1–6 cm × 0.5–1.2 mm, adaxial surface usually with long scattered hairs, margins scabrous, midrib and submarginal veins thickened, apex obtuse; ligule 0.1–0.3 mm. Spike (3–)5–20(–25) cm, falcate when dry; rachis shortly ciliate on margins or glabrous. Spikelets light green, lanceolate, 1.6–4 mm, acute; lower glume slightly asymmetrical; lemma 1.5–3 mm, mucronate. Caryopsis ca. 1 mm.

Locality: No precise locality. C. Wright s.n. (K)
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Dry and stony places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Microcos nervosa (Lour.) S. Y. Hu 破布葉（布渣葉）
J. Arnold Arbor. 69(1): 79. 1988.
Fallopia nervosa Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 336. 1790.
Grewia microcos L., Syst. Ed 12. 2: 602. 1767; FHK 42. 1861; FKH 51. 1912.
Microcos paniculata auct. non. L.: FHN 2: 58. 1965; FFJ 3: 402, fig. 283. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 87. 1989; FGD 4: 154, fig. 100. 2000.

Shrub or small tree, 3 –12 m tall. Branchlets hairy. Stipule linear-lanceolate, 5 –7 mm. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, hairy; leaf blade ovate or ovate oblong, 8 –18 × 4 – 8 cm, thin leathery, base round, apex acuminate, margin finely serrulate, stellate-pubescent initially, glabrescent on both surfaces in age. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, 4 –10 cm, stellate hairy; bracts lanceolate, yellowish-pubescent and stellate-pubescent; pedicels short and slender. Sepals oblong, 5–7 mm, stellate hairy abaxially. Petals oblong, about 1/3 –1/2 the length of sepals, yellowish-pubescent on both surfaces; glands as large as half of petals. Stamens shorter than sepals. Ovary subglobose, glabrous, dark brown; stigma pointed. Drupe subglobose or obovoid, ca. 1 × 0.7 cm, dark brown, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 150.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Microdesmis caseariifolia Planch. 小盤木
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 8: 758. 1848; FRPS 43(1): 2. 1998; FGD 5: 120, fig. 71. 2003.
Microdesmis caseariifolia f. sinensis Pax & Hoffm., Pflanzenr. 47(IV 147, 3): 106. 1911.

Shrub or treelet 3–8 m tall; branchlets slender, initially pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves alternate, papery to thin-leathery; petioles 3–6 mm, pubescent to glabrous; stipules narrowly triangular, ca. 1 mm; leaf blade lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate to oblong, 6–16 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, sometimes caudate, margin crenulate or subentire, glabrous on both surfaces or sparsely puberulous along midvein abaxially when young; lateral veins slender, 4–6 on each side of midvein. Flowers small, yellow, in axillary fascicles. Male flowers: pedicels 2–3 mm; sepals ovate, ca. 1 mm; petals elliptic, ca. 2 mm; stamens 10, the outer 5 longer; anthers 2-celled, connectives triangular or caudate-acuminate; staminodes fleshy. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in male flowers, but slightly larger; ovary globose, 2-locular, glabrous. Drupes subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Au Ha. Y. W. Lam 2317; F. W. Xing 6905.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Philippines to Indonesia.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar. – Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Microglossa pyrifolia (Lam.) Kuntze 小舌菊
Rev. Gen. 1: 353. 1891; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 286. 1967; FRPS 74: 337. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1014. 1998; FGD 8: 182, fig. 103. 2007.
Conyza pyrifolia Lam., Encycl. 2: 89. 1786.
Erigeron pyrifolius Benth., FHK 176. 1861.
Microglossa volubilis DC., Prodr. 5: 320. 1836; FKH 141. 1912.

Perennial scandent subshrubs, 70–150 cm tall; stem branches with prominent ribs, puberulous, glandular punctate. Leaves ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–10 × 2.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin inconspicuously serrate or nearly entire, pubescent and with yellow glands abaxially; petiole 7–13 mm. Capitula 5–7 mm across, clustered in terminal corymb, with lanceolate bract 2–5 mm. Involucre campanulate, 5‑seriate, with scarious margin and brown midvein; outermost herbaceous, ovate‑lanceolate, apex obtuse, glandular and pilose; inner ones becoming increasingly longer, changing from lanceolate to linear, from herbaceous to scarious with hyaline margin, apex slightly acute or obtuse. Receptacle alveolate, each areole with a large elevation at center, naked or rarely scarious. Female florets numerous at the margin, ligulate, corolla 3 mm, filiform; bisexual florets 2–3 in the middle, 4.5 mm, tubular, 5‑lobed. Cypsela oblong, 1 mm, ribbed, minutely pubescent, apex truncate, base with white ring. Pappus bristles white to pink in colour, numerous.

Locality: Tai Po, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9136, 11286; S. Y. Hu 10022 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Africa and tropical Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests and open grasslands. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.

Microstegium ciliatum (Trin.) A. Camus 剛莠竹
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, N. S. 68: 201. 1921; FFJ 6: 242. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 69, pl. 16: 11–13. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 563, photo 62. 2000; FOC 22: 597. 2006; FGD 9: 463. 2009.
Pollinia ciliata Trin., Mem. Acad. St. Petersb. ser. 6, 2: 305. 1833.

Perennial herb. Culms ascending from creeping base, up to 1 m tall, pubescent below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths longer or the upper shorter than internode, pilose or glabrous; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 6–20 × 0.5–1.8 cm, pubescent, base narrow, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous, ciliate. Racemes terminal, 3–20 digitate; rachis internodes linear, slightly inflated upward, margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet 3–3.5 mm, callus hairy; lower glume oblong, 2-keeled, 2–4-veined between keels, upper keels stiffly pectinate-ciliate, acute, obtuse or 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, sharply keeled, apex acuminate into a 0.3–3 mm hair-like awnlet; lower lemma absent or very small; upper lemma linear or lanceolate, occasionally broader, 0.5–1 mm, apex usually entire; awn 1–2 cm, flexuose with weakly developed column and fine hair-like apex; anthers 3. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet; pedicel 2–3 mm, margins densely ciliate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1684; L. T. Lo 115, 582.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Thin forests, open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Microstegium fasciculatum (L.) Henrard 蔓生莠竹
Blumea 3: 453. 1940; FOC 22: 597. 2006; FGD 9: 463, fig. 240. 2009.
Andropogon fasciculatus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1047. 1753.
Microstegium vagans (Nees ex Steud.) A. Camus, Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 68: 200. 1921[1922]; FRPS 10(2): 72, pl. 16: 1–5. 1997; Check List HK Plants 340. 2002; 119. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms rambling, up to 1 m or more. Leaf sheaths glabrous or tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades linearlanceolate, 10–18 × (0.5–)0.8–2 cm, pubescent, base narrow, stipe-like, apex acuminate into a setaceous point, margins scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm. Racemes 3–12, digitate in glabrous rachis, purplish; rachis internode ciliate at margins. Sessile spikelet oblong; callus hairs ca. 1 mm; lower glume elliptic-oblong, scabrid-hispidulous, 2-veined between keels, upper keels stiffly pectinate-ciliate, abaxial shallowly grooved or almost flat, apex subentire or 2-lobed; upper glume sharply keeled, apex acuminate or with a brief mucro; lower floret usually absent; upper lemma ovate, ca. 0.5 mm, 2-lobed, with an awn arising from the sinus; awn geniculate with distinct column. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet, lower glume keel scabrous, glabrous.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 6204, 11157, 11239 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Africa.
Ecology: Shade and moist banks, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Microstegium vimineum (Trin.) A. Camus 柔枝莠竹（莠竹）
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, N. S. 68: 201. 1921; FFJ 6: 242, fig. 210. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 76, pl. 15: 5–7. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 565, pl. 238. 2000; FOC 22: 596. 2006; FGD 9: 462. 2009.
Microstegium nodosum (Kom.) Tzvelev, Bot. Mater. Gerb. Bot. Inst. Komarova Acad. Nauk SSSR 21: 23. 1961; Check List HK Plants 340. 2002; 119. 2004.
Arthraxon nodosus Kom., Trudy Glavn. Bot. Sada 18: 448. 1901.
Andropogon vimineus Trin., Mem. Acad. St. Petersb. VI. Math, Phys. Nat. 2: 268. 1832.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect from the decumbent base, up to 1 m, with deep groove in one side, glabrous. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous except margins and mouth pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–9 × 0.5–1 cm, often sparsely pubescent, midvein white, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, membranous, truncate. Racemes   6, subdigitately arranged; rachis internode linearclavate, ciliate, shorter than spikelet. Sessile spikelet 4–5.5 mm, callus with a few short hairs; lower glume narrowly lanceolate-oblong, abaxial deeply grooved, puberulous-scaberulous or occasionally hispidulous, 0–4-veined between keels, veins connected by veinlets below apex; upper glume boat-shaped, scabrid on keel, acuminate; lower floret reduced to an inconspicuous linear-lanceolate scale or absent; upper lemma very narrow, 1–1.5 mm, with a mucro or an awn of about 5 mm long, arising from the apex; awn weakly geniculate, often included within spikelet; upper palea ovate, ca. 1 mm; anthers 3.

Locality: Sha Tin. S. P. Lau 586.
Distribution: Widely distributed from N to S China; Indian Subcontinent, SW to E Asia, Indochina, Philippines, introduced in America and elsewhere.
Ecology: Margins of forests, moist grassy places.

Microtropis biflora Merr. & Chun ex Merr. & F. L. Freeman 雙花假衛矛

Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 73: 288. 1940; FRPS 45(3): 170. 1999.


Shrub to 2 m tall. Branchlets terete, greyish white; internodes slender, usually 4–8.5 cm. Leaves papery, greyish when dry; petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blade ovate-oblong to oblong-elliptic, 6–10.5 × 1.8–4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to narrowly acuminate; lateral veins slender, 8–11 pairs, slender, obliquely ascending. Cymes axillary or lateral, usually 2-flowered. Peduncles 0–1.5 mm. Flowers sessile, 5-merous. Sepals rounded at apex. Petals oblong, ca. 3 mm; disk shallowly plateform. Ovary ovoid. Capsules broadly ellipsoidal, 1.3–1.5 × 0.8–0.9 cm.


Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 8725, 8464; Y. W. Lam 2264.

Distribution: Guangdong.

Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.– Feb.

Microtropis obscurinervia Merr. & F. L. Freeman 廣州假衛矛
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts, 73: 283. 1940; FRPS 45(3): 172. 1999.
Microtropis latifolia auct. non Wight ex Laws; FKH 61. 1912.

Evergreen shrub, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets purple-brown, black or black-purple. Petioles 8–15 mm; leaf blade thickly leathery, slightly fleshy, with small tubercular points when dry, narrowly oblong or broadly oblanceolate. 8–18 × 2.5–7 cm, lateral veins 7–11 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences glomerulate, ca. 10-flowered. Peduncles nearly absent. Flowers 5-merous. Sepals thick-leathery, nearly orbicular-reniform, 1.2–1.4 mm. Petals oblong, 2.5–3 mm, shortly clawed; disk annular, entire. Ovary ovoid, stigma obscurely 2-fid. Capsules ellipsoidal, 1.5–2 cm. Seeds ovate-elliptic, ca. 1.5 cm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Gough, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Kellet. W. J. Tutcher 4625, 11204; HK sheet 36088.
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Fruiting: Sep.– Dec.

Microtropis reticulata Dunn 細脈假衛矛

J. Bot. 47: 375. 1909; FKH 61. 1912; FRPS 45(3): 169. 1999.

Microtropis paucinervia Merr. & Chun ex Merr. & F. L. Freeman, Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts, 73: 285. 1940; FRPS 45(3): 167. 1999, syn. nov.


Small shrub. Petioles 3–6 mm; leaf blade thickly papery, oblong, narrowly elliptic or narrowly ovate-elliptic, 5–10 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acute, rarely shortly acuminate, tip blunt, margin revolute, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, slender, obviously raised abaxially. Cymes head-like, axillary or terminal, densely flowered. Peduncles ca. 2 mm. Flowers subsessile, 5-merous. Sepals suborbicular. Petals oblong, ca. 2 mm; disk annular. Stamens short; filaments slightly conic. Ovary ovoid. Capsules ellipsoidal, ca. 2 cm.


Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Tung Lung Chau, Ninepin Group. F. W. Xing 10016; Y. W. Lam 476; S. C. Ng 3211.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines.

Ecology: Exposed rocky slopes. Flowering: Mar.

Notes: The type specimen (Herb. Hongk. no. 6346) was collected from Lantau Island by S. T. Dunn in March 1909. The type specimen of Microtropis paucinervia (N. K. Chun 40294, IBSC) was also collected from Hong Kong.

Mikania micrantha Kunth 薇甘菊
Nov. Gen. Sp. (folio ed.) 4: 105. 1820.

Scandent herbs climbing over shrubs and small trees up to 5 m high; glabrous or subglabrous, slightly hairy at nodes. Leaves ovate‑deltoid, those on vegetative stems 4–9 × 2.5–6 cm, cordate with prominent broad sinus at the base, apex acuminate, the acumens 1–1.4 cm, margin undulate dentate or subentire, glandular on both surfaces; petiole 1–6 cm. Capitula 5 mm, in subumbelliform‑paniculate clusters terminal to lateral shoots with small leaves of 1–2.5 cm; each capitulum with 4 florets and 4 phyllaries, subtended by linear‑lanceolate bract 1.5–3 mm; phyllaries oblong, 3.5–5 mm, apex acuminate or obtuse, finely ciliate along margin of tip. All florets tubular, bisexual and fertile, corolla white, funnelform, 3–5 mm, 5‑lobed, the lower narrow tube glandular. Cypselae linear‑oblong, 4‑angled, 2–3 mm, glandular. Pappus of scabrid bristles 3–4 mm, white to reddish.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 6146, 6280 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 195.
Distribution: Native to S America, widely naturalized in the tropics
Ecology: A very troublesome weed commonly growing on margins of forests, open fields and especially in wastelands. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.

Millettia championii Benth. 綠花崖豆藤

Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 74. 1852; FHK 79. 1861; FKH 76. 1912; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 152. 1912; FRPS 40: 166. 1994; FGD 5: 235. 2003.


Woody climber. Leaves odd-pinnate; leaflets 5 or 7, ovate or ovate-oblong, 3–7 × 1.5–3 cm, base rounded, apex obtusely acuminate, glabrous, lateral veins 5 – 7 pairs, conspicuous. Panicles racemiform, terminal, 5 – 15 cm. Calyx broad-campanulate, 2 mm. Corolla white, 12 mm; vexillum marked with green spots at base, orbicular, 9 mm in diam., glabrous, without callosities; wings erect, with 2 auricles at base; keel oblong. Stamens 10, diadelphous; vexillary stamens free. Ovary linear; disk tubiform. Pods elongated, 6 –12 × 0.5 – 1.2 cm, compressed. Seeds 2– 3, brown, lenticular.


Locality: Mount Gough, Mount Parker, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Nam Chung. Y. S. Lau 883; HK sheet 39264, 39708.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.

Ecology: Thickets in valleys and by streams. Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: This species is nearest to M. reticulata, but readily distinguished from that species when growing by its slender habit and smaller pale green flowers. The type specimen (Champion 263, K) was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: This species is nearest to M. reticulata, but readily distinguished from that species when growing by its slender habit and smaller pale green flowers. The type specimen (Champion 263, K) was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Millettia dielsiana Harms 香花崖豆藤（山雞血藤）

Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29(3 – 4): 412. 1900; FKH 76. 1912; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 160. 1912; FRPS 40: 180. 1994; FGD 5: 237. 2003.


Woody climber, 2 – 5 m. Young branches subglabrous. Leaves odd-pinnate, 15 – 30 cm; leaflets 5, elliptic or ovate-oblong, 4 – 15 × 1.5 – 6 cm, base obtuse or rounded, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous or adpressed pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 6 –9 pairs. Panicles large, 15 – 40 cm. Calyx campanulate, 3 – 5 mm, puberulent. Corolla purple, 1 – 1.5 cm; vexillum broad-ovate to broad-obovate, densely rusty sericeous, base slightly cordate, without callosity; wings 5–8 mm, auriculate; keel falcate. Stamens 10, diadelphous. Ovary linear, densely tomentose; disk discoid. Pods narrowly oblong, 7 – 12 × 1.5 – 2 cm, compressed, grey tomentose. Seeds 3 – 5, oblong, lenticular, 8 × 6 mm.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 488, 489; S. C. Ng 3231.

Distribution: SW to SE China, Shaanxi, Gansu; Vietnam, Laos.

Ecology: Forests or thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Millettia nitida Benth. 亮葉崖豆藤（亮葉雞血藤）
London J. Bot. 1: 484. 1842; FHK 78. 1861; FKH 76. 1912; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 161. 1912; FRPS 40: 177. 1994; FGD 5: 234. 2003.

Woody climber. Branchlets initially rusty-pubescent. Leaves odd-pinnate, 15 – 20 cm; leaflets 5, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 5 – 11 × 2– 4 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex obtusely acuminate, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Panicles terminal, 10– 20 cm, densely rusty tomentose. Calyx campanulate, 6 – 8 mm, tomentose. Corolla violet, 1.6 – 2.4 cm; vexillum oblong, densely sericeous, with 2 callosities at base; wings truncate at base; keel falcate. Stamens diadelphous; vexillary stamens free; disk discoid. Ovary linear, densely tomentose. Pods 10 –14 × 1.5–2 cm, densely tomentose, tip beaked. Seeds 4 –5, brown, shining, obliquely oblong, 10 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3239; N. H. Li 190; Y. W. Lam 1033.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: May – Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected from Hong Kong Island by R. B. Hinds and C. Millett around 1840.

Millettia oosperma Dunn 皺果崖豆藤

J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 157. 1912; FRPS 40: 169. 1994; FGD 5: 234. 2003.


Woody climber, up to 20 m. Branchlets brown, initially tomentose. Leaves odd-pinnate, 25 – 40 cm; leaflets 5, lanceolate-elliptic or ovate-oblong, 8 – 20 × 4 – 8 cm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex obtuse, rounded or rarely emarginate, glabrous or sparsely hairy adaxially, densely brown-villose abaxially, lateral veins 7 – 12 pairs. Panicles terminal, 10 – 20 cm, densely brown-tomentose. Calyx campanulate, 6 mm. Corolla red or pink, 1.5 – 2 cm; vexillum brown, ovate, densely sericeous, with 2 callosities at base; wings lanceolate, with 2 auricles at base; keel falcate. Stamens 10, diadelphous. Ovary densely sericeous; disk cup-shaped. Pods turgid, ovate when 1-seeded, cylindric when several-seeded, 6 –13 × 2 – 2.5 cm, tip beaked. Seeds 1 – 4, ovate, 2 – 3 cm in diam.


Locality: Cape D'Aguilar. HK sheet 32374, 40151, 40204.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.

Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Aug. – Nov.

Notes: A syntype specimen was collected in Cape D'Aguilar in 1904.

Millettia oraria (Hance) Dunn 香港崖豆（香港崖豆藤）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 149. 1912; FRPS 40: 159. 1994; FGD 5: 232. 2003.
Tephrosia oraria Hance, J. Bot. 24: 17. 1886.

Shrub or small tree; bark smooth. Branchlets densely grey-tomentose. Leaves odd-pinnate, 15 – 20 cm; leaflets 9 – 13, elliptic or broadly ovate, 4 – 5.5 × 2 – 3 cm, base rounded or subcordate, apex rounded, pubescent adaxially, densely tomentose abaxially, lateral veins 6– 7 pairs. Panicles racemiform, axillary, 6 –15 cm, densely yellow-pubescent. Flowers 1 – 3 on each node. Calyx campanulate, 3 mm, tomentose. Corolla purple, 8 –11 mm; vexillum suborbicular, pubescent; wings oblong-falcate; keel broadly ovate, base truncate. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary densely sericeous; ovulus 2–4. Pods 5–9 × 1–1.5 cm, compressed, densely brown velutinous, later deciduous. Seeds 2 – 3, orange, orbicular, caruncle white.

Locality: Tai Long Wan, Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Kellett, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 792; K. L. Yip 4497; HK sheet 40322.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Cape D'Aguilar, Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in Dec. 1884.

Millettia pachycarpa Benth. 厚果崖豆藤（厚果雞血藤）
Pl. Jungh. 2: 250. 1855; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 168. 1912; FRPS 40: 148. 1994; FGD 5: 232, fig. 129. 2003.

Large woody climber, up to 15 m. Branchlets initially yellow-tomentose. Leaves odd-pinnate, 30 – 50 cm; leaflets 13 – 17, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 10–18 × 3.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, glabrous adaxially, tomentose abaxially, lateral veins 12–15 pairs. Panicles racemiform, 15–30 cm, densely brown–tomentose, with 2–5 flowers on each node. Calyx cup-shaped, 6 mm, densely-tomentose, obscurely toothed. Corolla purplish, 2–3 cm; vexillum ovate, with 2 auricles at base, without callosities; wings oblong, hooked on lower side; keel truncate and shortly hooked at base. Stamens 10, monadelphous, vexillary one free at base. Ovary linear, tomentose. Pods woody, oblong or globose, 5 – 23 × 4 cm, densely dotted with yellowish tubercules, indehiscent. Seeds 1–5, black-brown, reniform.

Locality: Shing Mun, Lam Tsuen. Y. S. Lau 2850; HK sheet 33109.
Distribution: SW to SE China; India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr.– Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Millettia pulchra (Benth.) Kurz 印度崖豆印度雞血藤）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 42(2): 69. 1873; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 150. 1912; FKH 77. 1912; FRPS 40: 156. 1994; FGD 5: 231. 2003.
Mundulea pulchra Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 248. 1852.
Tephrosia tutcheri Dunn, J. Bot. 47(6): 197. 1909.

Shrub or small tree, 3 – 8 m tall; bark rough. Leaves odd-pinnate, 8 – 20 cm; leaflets 13– 19, lanceolate or lanceolate-elliptic, 2– 6 × 0.7–1.5 cm; base attenuate or obtuse, apex acute, sparsely pubescent adaxially, adpressed pubescent abaxially. Panicles racemiform, axillary, 6–15 cm, densely yellow-pubescent. Flowers 3–4 on nodes of rachis. Calyx campanulate, ca. 4 mm, densely pubescent. Corolla 9 –12 mm, pinkish to purple; vexillum oblong, emarginate, base truncate; wings oblong, auriculate; keel oblong-falcate. Stamens 10, monadelphous, vexillary stamen free at base. Ovary densely pubescent, without disk, 5-ovuled. Pods 5 – 10 × 1 – 1.5 cm, compressed. Seeds 1–4, brown, elliptic, ca. 1 cm wide.

Locality: Shek O, Deep Water Bay, Aberdeen, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2851; H. C. Tang 2100; HK sheet 1290.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Laos.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Apr. –Aug.; fruiting: Jun. – Oct.
Notes: The type specimens of Tephrosia tutcheri Dunn were collected from Hong Kong Island (behind Aberdeen, near Little Hongkong, and near Shek O) and Lantau Island by W. J. Tutcher and U. A. On between 1905 and 1888 respectively.

Millettia reticulata Benth. 雞血藤
Pl. Jungh. 2: 249. 1853; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 154. 1912; FKH 77. 1912; FRPS 40: 164. 1994; FGD 5: 235. 2003.

Woody climber. Branchlets initially yellowish brown-pubescent, glabrescent. Stipules and stipels spiniform. Leaves odd-pinnate, 10–20 cm; leaflets 7–9, ovate-oblong or oblong, 3–6 × 1.5–4 cm, base rounded, apex obtuse, acuminate or emarginate, glabrous, lateral veins 6–7 pairs. Panicles terminal or axillary, 15–30 cm. Calyx campanulate to cup-shaped, 3–4 mm. Corolla purple, 13–17 mm; vexillum ovoid-oblong, without callosities at base; wings and keel slightly longer than vexillum. Stamens 10, diadelphous; disk tubiform; ovules numerous. Pods linear, 15 – 9 × 1 – 1.5 cm, compressed, valves ± woody. Seeds 3–6, oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 483; Y. W. Lam 270, 1176.
Distribution: SW to SE China; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Millettia speciosa Champ. ex Benth. 美麗崖豆藤（美麗雞血藤）

Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 73. 1852; FHK 78. 1861; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 41: 155. 1912; FKH 76. 1912; FRPS 40: 162. 1994; FGD 5: 233, fig. 130. 2003.


Woody climber, bark brown. Branchlets initially tomentose. Leaves odd-pinnate, 15 – 25 cm; leaflets often 13, oblong-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 4 – 8 × 2 – 3 cm, base obtuse or rounded, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate, glabrous adaxially, rusty pubescent or glabrous abaxially, lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Panicles racemiform, axillary, up to 30 cm, densely tawny tomentose. Flowers fragrant. Calyx campanulate, 1.2 cm, silky-tomentose, teeth obtuse. Corolla yellow or pink; vexillum orbicular, ca. 2 cm in diam., base cordate, with 2 callosities; wings oblong, hooked-auriculate; keel falcate. Stamens 10, diadelphous. Ovary linear, densely tomentose; disk tubiform. Pods oblong, 10 – 15 × 1 – 2 cm, compressed, brown-tomentose, valves thick leathery. Seeds 4 – 6, ovate, flattened.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 416, 1283; HK sheet 39049.

Distribution: SW to SE China; Vietnam.

Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Jul. – Oct.; fruiting: Feb. of the following year.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The type specimens (Champion 261, 505, K) were collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.
