Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The type specimens (Champion 261, 505, K) were collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Mimosa bimucronata (A. P. de Candolle) O. Kuntze 光莢含羞草
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 198. 1891.
Acacia bimucronata A. P. de Candolle, Prodr. 2: 469. 1825.
Mimosa sepiaria Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. 4(32): 395. 1842.

Shrubs deciduous, 3 – 6 m tall. Branchlets unarmed in distal parts, in lower parts armed by up to 1 cm, recurved prickles, densely yellow tomentose. Pinnae 4 – 9 pairs, to 1.5 – 8 cm, rachis unarmed, pubescent; leaflets 12 – 16 pairs, linear, 5 – 7 × 1 – 1.5 mm, leathery, glabrous to puberulous with ciliate margin, main vein near upper side, apex mucronate. Heads globose, forming a spreading panicle with compound, spreading lower branches. Flowers white, scented. Calyx cup-shaped, minute. Petals oblong, 2.5–4 mm, connate at base. Stamens 8; filaments 4–5 mm. Ovary initially glabrous. Pods brown, straight, strap-shaped, 3.5 – 4.5 × 0.6 cm, unarmed, finely reticulate-venulose, usually with 4 – 8 segments. Seeds olivaceous, ovoid, compressed, ca. 4.5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2554; L. T. Lo 464; P. S. Choi 241.
Distribution.: Guangdong (cultivated); S America (native to NE Argentina and E Brazil).
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Sept.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Mimosa pudica L. 含羞草
Sp. Pl. 518. 1753; FKH 91. 1912; FRPS 39: 16. 1988; FGD 5: 156, fig. 89. 2003.

Diffuse shrubby herb, 30–90 cm tall. Stems terete, branched, with reflexed bristles and scattered curved prickles. Stipules lanceolate, 5–10 mm, bristly. Pinnae and leaflets sensitive; pinnae usually 2 pairs, digitate, 3–8 cm; leaflets 10–20 pairs, linear-lanceolate, 8–13 × 1.5–2.5 mm, apex acute, margins ciliate. Heads globular, 1 cm in diam.; peduncle long, 1–2, axillary. Flowers small, pink, numerous; bracts linear. Calyx minute. Corolla campanulate, lobes 4, pubescent abaxially. Stamens 4, exserted. Ovary with short stalk, glabrous; ovules 3–4; style filiform, stigma small. Pods oblong, 1–2 × 5 mm, flat, slightly recurved, consisting of 3–5 one-seeded joints which fall away from the persistent, bristly sutures. Seeds ovate, 3.5 mm.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 138; HK sheet 1579, 8719.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan; native to tropical America, naturalized in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides or cultivated. Flowering: Mar.– Oct.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, weeds.

Mirabilis jalapa L. 紫茉莉
Sp. Pl. 177. 1753; FGZ 171, fig. 75. 1956; Fl. Europ. 1: 111. 1964; FHN 1: 440, fig. 242. 1964; FGD 2: 107, fig. 74. 1991; FRPS 26: 7. 1996; FOC 5: 432. 2003.

Perennial herb, 30 –100 cm tall, glabrous or slightly pubescent, with thick, conical roots. Stems erect, much branched, often reddish, with tumid nodes. Leaves opposite; petioles to 6.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-triangular, 5 –11(–15) × 3.5 – 6 cm, base truncate or cordate, apex acuminate. Flowers in terminal dichotomous cymes, opening in the afternoon, each flower subtended by a involucre. Involucre calyx-like, green, 9 –10 mm, united to middle; lobes 5, narrowly triangular, 1-nerved, ± ciliate. Calyx corolla-like, red, yellow, white or striped; tube 4.5 – 5 cm, constricted above the ovary; limb 5-lobed, ca. 2.5 cm in diam. Stamens 5; anthers compressed globose, slightly exserted. Ovary ovoid; style filiform, as long as or longer than filaments; stigma capitate. Fruit ovoid, ca. 5 mm in diam., black, with tubercles.

Locality: Cultivated or sometimes escaped from cultivation. Y. S. Lau 1579, 2157.
Distribution: Native to tropical America; widely cultivated and naturalized elsewhere in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: May.– Oct. Flowers opening late afternoon till next morning.
Uses: Ornamental.

Miscanthus floridulus (Labill.) Warb. ex K. Schum. & Lauterb. 五節芒
Fl. Schutzgeb. Südsee. 166. 1901; FHN 4: 448. 1977; FFJ 6: 240, fig. 208. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 4, pl. 1: 1–6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 567, pl. 239, photo 64. 2000; FOC 22: 582. 2006; FGD 9: 454. 2009.
Miscanthus japonicus (Trin.) Andersson, Öfvers. af Förh. Kongl. Svenska Vetensk.-Akad. 12: 166. 1855.
Eulalia japonicum Trin., Mém. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Pétersbourg, Sér. 6, Sci. Math. 2(3): 333. 1832; FHK 420. 1861.
Saccharum floridulum Labill., Sert. Austro-Caledon. 13: t. 18. 1824.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 1.5–4 m tall, glabrous, unbranched. Leaf sheaths glabrous or margins sparsely ciliate, longer than internode or the upper slightly shorter than internode; ligule 1–3 mm, rounded, ciliate; leaf blades linear, flat, tough, 20–85 × 0.5–4 cm, glabrous or pilose on the base of adaxial surface, midrib prominent, margins scabrid. Panicle oblong or elliptic, dense, 30–50 cm; axis more than 2/3 the length of the panicle; racemes many, 10–30 cm, appressed or ascending, glabrous, scaberulous. Spikelets of a pair similar, unequally pedicellate along a slender continuous rachis; callus hairs as long as or slightly longer than the spikelet, white, spreading; glumes subequal, membranous, margins pilose near apex, veins obscure, acuminate; lower lemma boat-shaped, hyaline, pilose, acuminate; upper lemma similar to the lower, glabrous or margins sparsely short ciliate at the lower, acute, slightly 2-toothed; awn straight or geniculate; upper palea a small hyaline scale; anthers 3, 1–1.5 mm. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1865; K. L. Yip 4181, 4246.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, valleys, open grassy fields.

Miscanthus sinensis Andersson 芒
Öfvers. Kongl. Vetensk.-Akad. Förh. 12: 166. 1855; FKH 319. 1912; FHN 4: 448, fig. 1238. 1977; FFJ 6: 241, fig. 209. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 6, pl. 1: 7–11. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 567, photo 65. 2000; FOC 22: 582. 2006; FGD 9: 454. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 1–2 m tall, solid, unbranched, glabrous or puberulous at nodes. Leaf sheaths glabrous, longer than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, 20–50 × 0.6–1 cm, glabrous, glaucous or pilose, midrib prominent, base tapering or broad and rounded, apex acuminate, margins scabrid or smooth; ligule 0.5–4 mm, ciliolate. Panicle 20–50 cm; axis up to 1/2 the length of the panicle, subglabrous to pilose or puberulous. Raceme 10–30 cm; rachis internodes glabrous, scaberulous or smooth, nodes glabrous; lower pedicel 2 mm, upper pedicel 4–6 mm. Spikelets 4.5–5 mm, callus hairs as long as spikelet; lower glume 3–4-veined, abaxial surface glabrous or pilose, apex acuminate; upper glume 1-veined, upper margins inrolled and ciliate; lower lemma oblong, hyaline, margins ciliate; upper lemma shorter than lower lemma, bifid, with an awn from the sinus; awn geniculate, 9–12 mm; upper palea 1/2 length of upper lemma.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 41504, 41961.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Hillslopes, rivers and stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Mischobulbum cordifolium (Hook. f.) Schltr. 心葉球柄蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. Beih. 1: 98. 1911, et 4: 180. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 66, fig. 32. 1977; FRPS 18: 231. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 971, pl. 413. 2000; FGD 7: 409, fig. 210. 2006.
Tainia cordifolia Hook. f., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 19(3): pl. 1861. 1889; FOC 25: 282. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs petiole-like, 8 cm or longer, 3–4 mm thick, unifoliate. Leaves semi-succulent, ovate-cordate, 7–13 × 4–8 cm, base cordate, apex acute, dull green, with 6 arching primary veins in addition to the midrib and faintly reticulate veinlets. Flowers large, bracts small, lanceolate, 7 mm, apex acuminate; sepals and petals brown with purple-brown veins; sepals subequal, lanceolate; the odd one 2–2.5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, apex acuminate; lateral ones oblique, connate at the base forming the mentum of 12–14 mm; petals slightly larger than sepals, lanceolate, 2–2.2 × 0.5–0.7 cm, acute, oblique at the base, 5-veined and keeled along the midvein; lip fleshy, attached to the mentum, rhomboid, 2.4 × 1.4 cm, the apex triangular and acute, with 3 prominent ridges, purple; column erect, fleshy, slightly curved, winged along both sides; anther terminal, with 2 ear-like projections; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs; ovary subcylindrical, striate, glabrous.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 34413.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Mitracarpus hirtus (L.) DC. 蓋裂果
Prodr. 4: 572. 1830.
Mitracarpus villosus (Sw.) Cham. & Schltdl., Linnaea 3(4): 363. 1828, nom. inval.
Mitracarpus villosus (Sw.) DC., 4: 572. 1830; Verdc., Fl. Trop. East Africa 375, fig. 55. 1976; FRPS 71(2): 210, pl. 50. 1999;Check List HK Plants 267. 2002; 92. 2004.
Spermacoce hirta L. Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1: 148. 1762.
Spermacoce villosa Sw., Prodr. 29. 1788.

Perennial herbs, 40–80 cm tall. Stems erect, slightly angled on the upper part, sparsely hirsute. Leaves sessile; stipules united at base, apex with unequal bristle‑like lobes; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 3–4.5 × 0.7–1.5 cm, apex acute, tapering to the base, adaxially scabrous or with sparse short hairs, abaxially pubescent, margin scabrous; lateral veins slender, inconspicuous. Flowers small, in head‑like axillary clusters. Bracteoles linear, about the length of the calyx. Calyx pubescent; tube subglobular; lobes unequal, 2 larger ones 1.8–2 mm, smaller ones 0.8–1.2 mm, ciliate. Corolla funnel‑shaped, 2–2.2 mm, glabrous inside; lobes triangular, about 1/3 of the tube, apex obtuse. Capsule subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., scabrous or sparsely puberulent.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Kwai Chung, Sha Tin, Sha Kok Mei. P. S. Choi 55, 159; Y. W. Lam 1017.
Distribution: Hainan; India, tropical America & Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Mitrasacme indica Wight 姬苗
Icon. Pl. Ind. Orient. 4: 15. 1850; FRPS 61: 257. 1992; FOC 15: 322. 1996.
Mitrasacme alsinoides R. Br. var. indica (Wight) H. Hara, J. Japan Bot. 30(1): 24. 1955.
Mitrasacme alsinoides auct. non R. Br.: FKH 173. 1912.

Plants annual, erect, to 15 cm tall. Stems usually branched, slender, distinctly 4‑ribbed to narrowly 4‑winged, glabrous or nearly so; internodes 2 – 4 times as long as leaves. Leaves ovate to very narrowly ovate, 3 – 7 × 1.5 – 2.5 mm, herbaceous, apex acute, glabrous or glabrescent, midvein abaxially prominent, lateral veins inconspicuous on both surfaces. Flowers solitary in upper leaf axils. Pedicel filamentous, 3 – 8 mm, glabrous or scabrous. Calyx to 2 mm, glabrous, basally connate to ± half its length, lobes narrowly oblong. Corolla white, campanulate, 3 – 4 mm, shortly and sparsely beared at mouth; lobes nearly rounded, ca. 1.5 mm. Stamens included; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers introrse, ovate to rarely sagittate, ca. 0.7 mm, with an apical appendix. Pistil ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm in diam. Style ca. 1 mm, base strongly parted, connate along apical half; stigma broadly truncate to 2‑cleft. Fruiting pedicel 0.6 – 2.5 cm. Capsules subglobose, to 2 mm in diam. Style connate only at apex. Seeds angular‑ovoid, coarsely reticulate.

Locality: Fanling, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan. W. J. Tutcher 9960; HK sheet 40390.
Distribution: Hainan, Jiangsu, Shandong, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia, SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Grassy open places. Flowering: Sep. – Oct.

Mitrasacme pygmaea R. Br. 水田白（裸莖姬苗）
Prodr. 453. 1810; FRPS 61: 257, pl. 68: 1 – 5. 1992; FGD 3: 312, fig. 202. 1995; FOC 15: 322. 1996.
Mitrasacme capillaris Wall. in Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 420. 1820; FHK 230. 1861.
Mitrasacme chinensis Griseb., Nov. Acta Acad. Caes. Leop. – Car. Nat. Cur. Suppl. 1: 51. 1843.
Mitrasacme nudicaulis auct. non Blume: FHK 230. 1861; FKH 173. 1912.
Mitrasacme polymorpha auct. non R. Br.: FKH 173. 1912.

Annual or perennial, ephemeral plants, to 20(– 30) cm tall. Stems terete, erect, simple or few‑branched from base. Leaves in a basal rosette or separated by internodes longer than leaves except for uppermost 2 pairs which from a whorl of 4 leaves; leaf blade ovate, oblong, or linear‑lanceolate, 2 – 13 × 1–5 mm, herbaceous, base broadly cuneate to attenuate, apex obtuse to acuminate, abaxially hirsute on midvein, adaxially hirsute but glabrescent, rarely both surfaces ± glabrous, margin hirsute, lateral veins 3 inconspicuous pairs. Inflorescences terminal, sometimes subterminal, long‑pedunculate, umbel‑like, often irregularly compound, rarely reduced to a single long pedicellate flower; bracts ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, ciliate. Pedicel 5 –9 mm. Calyx campanulate, 1.5 – 2.8 mm; lobes narrowly triangular, as long as tube. Corolla white, pale yellow, or rarely bluish white, campanulate, 3 – 6 mm, inside often sparsely bearded; lobes suborbicular, to 1.5 mm. Stamens included; filaments 1.5 – 3 mm; anthers narrowly ovate to sagittate, apex acute. Pistil to 4.5 mm. Ovary ca. 1 mm. Styles free for lower 1/4 to 1/3; stigma 2, 2‑cleft. Fruiting pedicel ca. 1.5 cm. Capsules subglobose, ca. 3 mm in diam., base enclosed by calyx, apex opening by loculicidal slits, many‑seeded; style persistent, free or connate toward apex. Seeds ellipsoidal to angular, minutely reticulate to papillate.

Locality: Mount Gough, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Po Kau, Lo Wu, Ma On Shan, Kwai Tau Leng, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 57; L. T. Lo 255; Y. W. Lam 2315.
Distribution: E, S & SW China; E, SE to S Asia.
Ecology: Grassy open places. Flowering: Jun.– Nov.

Mnesithea laevis (Retz.) Kunth 假蛇尾草
Révis. Gramin. 1: 154. 1829; FOC 22: 643. 2006; FGD 9: 483. 2009.
Rottboellia laevis Retz., Observ. Bot. 3: 11. 1783.
Heteropholis cochinchinensis (Lour.) Clayton, Kew Bull. 35(4): 816. 1981; FRPS 10(2): 276. pl. 67: 3–4. 1997; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.
Thaumastochloa cochinchinensis (Lour.) C. E. Hubb., FHN 4: 467, fig. 1255. 1977; FFJ 6: 259, fig. 230. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 583, pl. 246. 2000.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect, slender, glabrous, 15–70 cm tall. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous, often keeled; leaf blades linear, 8–25 × 0.1–0.4 cm, glabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm. Racemes solitary, terminal or axillary, cylindrical; sessile spikelets paired at each joint and separated by a pedicel, or triads present only at raceme base, or whole raceme with solitary sessile spikelets; rachis internodes clavate, 3.5–4 mm. Sessile spikelet 3–5 mm; lower glume oblong, smooth, or slightly sunken between lower part of veins, or ribbed throughout, rarely pitted, margins not winged, apex obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, equal to lower glume, membranous; lower lemma slightly shorter than glumes, palea absent; upper lemma ca. 2.5 mm; stamens 3; style free. Pedicellate spikelet minute or absent; pedicel linear, adnate to rachis internode, when paired sessile spikelets present the pedicel between them often adnate only at apex.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 1039; Y. W. Lam 952; HK sheet 8435.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Indonesia, Philippines, Pacific islands (Polynesia).
Ecology: Open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

Mnesithea mollicoma (Hance) A. Camus 毛儉草
Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 25: 57. 1919; FHN 4: 468, fig. 1256. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 280, pl. 66: 1–3, 78: 4. 1997; FOC 22: 643. 2006; FGD 9: 483, fig. 254. 2009.
Rottboellia mollicoma Hance, J. Bot. 9: 134. 1871; FKH 321. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, up to 1.5 m, softly pilose. Leaf sheathes the upper usually shorter than internode, densely pilose or with caducous tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 10–60 × 0.5–2 cm, softly pubescent, tapering to both ends; ligule 1–2 mm, glabrous or ciliolate. Racemes 5–10 cm; rachis internode as long as or slightly shorter than spikelet, with short hairs at base; sessile spikelets 3–4 mm, paired at each node and separated by a pedicel, or occasionally only one sessile spikelet present; lower glume leathery, rib-like veins separated by deep slits, slits interrupted by tubercle-based hairs along their length, margins narrowly winged toward apex; upper glume boat-shaped, keeled toward apex; lower floret usually reduced, lemma membranous, 3-veined; upper floret bisexual, upper lemma and palea subequal. Pedicellate spikelet ca. 0.5 mm, linear, flattened, pilose, reduced to a glume, pedicel subequal to sessile spikelet, ca. 0.5 mm wide.

Locality: Sha Tin. P. P. H. But 284; S. Y. Hu 11197 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Grassy fields.

Mollugo stricta L. 粟米草
Sp. Pl. 2: 131. 1762; FHK 23. 1861; FKH 114. 1912; FRPS 26: 28, pl. 6: 7. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 326, pl. 151, photo 139. 1996; FOC 5: 439. 2003.
Mollugo pentaphylla auct. non L.: FHN 1: 382. 1964; FGD 2: 85. 1991.

Annual glabrous herb, 10– 40 cm tall. Stems diffuse, much branched. Basal leaves rosulate, oblong-obovate 1.5– 5 × 0.6–1 cm; stem-leaves opposite or in false whorls of 4–6; petioles 1–3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, rarely narrowly elliptic, 1.5–5 × 0.2–0.8 mm, base attenuate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire. Flowers very small, in slender bifid racemes or dichotomous cymes, on slender peduncles. Pedicels filiform, 1–2.5 mm. Sepals 5, light green, with white edges. Petals none. Stamens 3–5; filaments dilated at base. Ovary 3-locular; styles 3, linear, very short. Capsule subglobose, opening by 3 valves; seeds tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Cameron, So Kong Po, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2284; HK sheet 36034.
Distribution: Widely distributed in areas S of Qingling and Yellow River. Dispersed over tropical and subtropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, cultivated fields, sandy places near seashore.

Mollugo verticillata L. 種棱粟米草
Sp. Pl. 89. 1753; FGD 2: 85. 1991; FRPS 26: 29. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 328. 1996; FOC 5: 439. 2003.

Annual glabrous herb, 10–30 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, much branched. Basal leaves rosulate, obovate or obovate-spathulate 1.5–5 × 0.6–1 cm; stem-leaves opposite or in false whorls of 3–8, subsessile; leaf blade oblanceolate to linear-oblanceolate, 1.5 –2.5 × 0.15 –0.5 mm, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire. Flowers in umbellate-clusters of 3 – 5, on one side of nodes. Pedicels slender, 3 – 5 mm. Sepals 5, or rarely 4, oblong to ovate-oblong, 2.5–3 mm, whitish adaxially, with scarious edges. Petals none. Stamens 3, rarely 2, or 4 – 5; filaments slightly dilated at base. Ovary 3-locular; styles 3. Capsule ellipsoid or subglobose, opening by 3 valves; seeds smooth and shining.

Locality: Pak Nai, Castle Peak. Y. W. Lam 1513; HK sheet 32383.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, tropical America, S Europe.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Momordica charantia L. 苦瓜
Sp. Pl. 1009. 1753; FHK 125. 1861; FKH 112. 1912; FHN 1: 473. 1964; FFJ 5: 249, fig. 233. 1993; FRPS 73(1): 189. 1986; FGD 3: 122, fig. 85. 1995.
Momordica indica L., Herb. Amb. 24. 1754.

Annual herbaceous vine, many-branched, monoecious; stems and branches pubescent. Tendrils unbranched. Petioles slender, pilose, glabrescent, 4 –17 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate-reniform or suborbicular, 4–24 × 2.5 –12 cm, base cordate, puberulous or subglabrous on both surfaces, 5–7-partitioned, lobes ovate-oblong, margin crenate or irregularly lobed. Flowers yellow, solitary and axillary. Male flowers: pedicels slender, puberulous, 3 –7 cm; calyx-tube ovoid, 5 mm, pubescent; lobes ovate-lanceolate, 7 × 5 mm, pubescent; corolla 4 cm in diam.; lobes obovate, 2 × 1.3 cm, pubescent; stamens 3, distinct, anther cells conduplicate. Female flowers: pedicels 10 –12 cm, with a bract at base; perianth as in male flowers; ovary fusiform, densely verrucose. Fruits fusiform or cylindrical, verrucose, 10–20 cm, orange when mature, glabrous, dehiscing into 3 valves. Seeds many, compressed, oblong, with red arils.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 870, 871; Y. S. Lau 2616.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Momordica cochinchinensis (Lour.) Spreng. 木鼈子
Syst. Veg. 3: 14. 1826; FHN 1: 473. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 192, pl. 49: 8 –12. 1986; FFJ 5: 249, fig. 232. 1993; FGD 3: 122. 1995.
Muricia cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 596. 1790.

Perennial stout herbaceous vine, dioecious. Root tuberous. Stems and branches glabrous or puberulous. Tendrils unbranched. Petioles stout, 5–10 cm, with 2–4 glands at the base or middle; leaf blade broadly ovate-cordate, 8 –20 × 6–20 cm, 3–5-lobed, median lobe larger, base cordate, with several glands at margin, apex acute or acuminate, margin undulate-dentate, rarely entire, glabrous on both surfaces, or white punctate abaxially. Male flowers: solitary or in a short racemes; pedicels stout, 3–5 cm, bracteate at the apex, bracts orbicular-reniform; calyx-tube infundibular, lobes oblonglanceolate or oblong, 10–16 mm, scabrous or pubescent; corolla white, yellowish, lobes ovate-oblong, 5– 6 cm, densely pubescent along veins, yellow-glandular at the base; stamens 3, anther cells reflexed. Female flowers: solitary; pedicel 5–10 cm, bracteate at the middle; bracts 2 mm; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary ovoid, 1 cm long, densely spiny. Fruit ovoid, 12–15 cm in diam., red, fleshy, densely spiny. Seeds many, ovate or square, both surfaces sculptured, margin undulate-sublobulate.

Locality: Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Fanling, Sha Tau Kok. Y. S. Lau 765, 891; W. J. Tutcher 9613.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bangladesh, India, Indochina, Malaysia, Myanmar.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal.

Monochoria hastata (L.) Solms 箭葉雨久花
A. DC & C. DC, Monogr. Phan. 4: 523. 1883; FHN 4: 121. 1977; FFJ 6: 463. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 136, pl. 32: 11. 1997; FOC 24: 41. 2000; FGD 8: 274, fig. 168. 2007.
Pontederia hastata L., Sp. Pl. 1: 288. 1753.
Monochoria hastifolia C. Presl, Reliq. Haenk. 1(2): 128. 1827, nom. illeg. (included Pontederia hastata); FKH 281. 1912.

Perennial aquatic herb, 50–200 cm tall. Stems often long and robust. Leaves radical or alternate on stems; leaf blade triangular or triangular-ovate, 5–15 × 3–15 cm, base sagittate to hastate, apex acute to acuminate; petiole 7–10 cm, broadened and sheathed at base. Racemes 8–18 cm, 10–40-flowered, erect or suberect; peduncle distinctly shorter than associated leaf petiole. Perianth segments bluish with green median vein and reddish blotch, ovate, 1–1.6 cm. Stamens 6, one larger with blue anther (ca. 6 mm), the others smaller, with yellow anthers (ca. 3 mm); style hairy at apex. Capsule oblong, ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9626.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields. Flowering: Aug.–Mar. of the following year.

Monochoria vaginalis (Burm. f.) C. Presl ex Kunth 鴨舌草
Enum. Pl. 4: 134. 1843; FHK 374. 1861; FKH 281. 1912; FHN 4: 121, fig. 1028. 1977; FFJ 6: 463, fig. 416. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 138, pl. 32: 1–6. 1997; FOC 24: 41. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 135, pl. 52. 2000; FGD 8: 275. 2007.
Pontederia vaginalis Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 80. 1768.

Perennial aquatic herb, 12–45 cm tall, with very short rhizomes. Stems usually inconspicuous. Leaves radical or spirally arranged; leaf blade ovate, oblong-ovate to lanceolate, 2 – 6 × 1–4 cm, base subrounded or shallowly cordate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire; petiole dilated and with a broad sheath at base. Racemes 2.5–5 cm, 2–20-flowered, initially erect, soon reflexed; peduncle 1–3 cm, base bracteate; bract lanceolate. Perianth segments purplish, ovate-lanceolate to oblong, 0.8–1.5 cm. Stamens 6, one larger and longer, the others smaller and shorter; anther 1.8–4 mm in larger stamen, 1.5–3 mm in smaller stamens. Capsule ovoid to ellipsoidal, 0.7–1 cm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Wan, She Shan Tsuen, Tai Ho. P. S. Choi 416; Y. W. Lam 2226; S. C. Ng 1043.
Distribution: Widely spread throughout China; Korea, Japan, Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy field, ponds and ditches. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Myrica rubra (Lour.) Sieb. & Zucc. 楊梅
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: 230. 1846; FHK 322. 1861; FKH 251. 1912; FGD 3: 239, fig. 160. 1995; FOC 4: 276. 1999.
Morella rubra Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 548. 1790.

Evergreen tree, dioecious, to 15 m tall; bark grey. Branchlets robust, glabrous. Petioles 0.2–1 cm. Leaves obovate-oblong to oblanceolate, 5–14 × 1– 4 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin entire or serrate at upper part, glabrous on both surfaces, sparsely to moderately golden-glandular abaxially. Male spikes solitary or sometimes several together in leaf axils, 1–3 cm, usually not branched; bracts imbricate, suborbicular, ca. 1 mm, glabrous, with golden glands abaxially. Male flowers: bracteoles 2– 4, ovate; stamens 4 – 6; anthers dark red, ellipsoid. Female spikes often solitary in leaf axils, 0.5 –1.5 cm, many-flowered; bracts imbricate, glabrous, with golden glands abaxially. Female flowers: bracteoles 4; ovary ovoid, velutinous; stigmas 2, bright red. Drupe dark red or purple-red at maturity, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; pericarp fleshy, juicy, papilliferous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated. H. C. Tang 2408, 2486; Y. S. Lau 501.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Vietnam, Philippines, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Morinda cochinchinensis DC. 大果巴戟
Prodr. 4: 449. 1830; Pit. in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. Indo‑chine 3: 420. 1924; FHN 3: 331. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 188. 1999; FGD 6: 236. 2005.
Morinda villosa auct. non Hook. f.: FKH 133. 1912.

Climbing shrubs. Branchlets, petioles and peduncles densely covered with rusty long hairs. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 5–11 mm; stipules tubular, scarious, 6–10 mm, apex truncate, with 2 mucros on each side; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or obovate‑oblong, 8–14 × 3–6 cm, base obtuse or slightly cordate, apex caudate‑acuminate or shortly acuminate, adaxially sparsely strigose, abaxially densely rusty pubescent; lateral veins slender, 7–10 on each side of midvein. Flower‑heads 5 – 15‑flowered, arranged in terminal umbels; peduncles 1–3 cm. Calyx‑tube hemispherical, sparsely pubescent abaxially; limb 4 – 5‑lobed; lobes unequal, subulate, 1–2 m. Corolla white; tube ca. 2 mm, glabrous; lobes 4–5, oblong‑lanceolate, 4–5.5 mm, apex incurved, abaxially puberulent, densely bearded on the lower part of adaxial surface. Compound berry subglobose, 1–2 cm in diam., pubescent, orange when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Hoi Ha, Lai Chi Wo. HK sheet 14148, 35586, 35712.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Morinda parvifolia Bartl. ex DC. 雞眼藤
Prodr. 4: 499. 1830; FHN 3: 333. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 299. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 194. 1999; FGD 6: 238. 2005.

Climbing shrubs. Branchlets hirsute on the distal nodes. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 3 – 6 mm, glabrescent or ± puberulent; stipules 1.5–3 mm, apex truncate, glabrescent; leaf blade obovate or obovate‑elliptic, rarely elliptic‑oblong, 2–6 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse and mucronate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially with cluster of hairs in axils of veins, or sometimes with short hairs on the veins; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein. Flower‑heads 4–8‑flowered, 2–6 arranged in terminal umbels; peduncles 5–10 mm, covered with short hairs. Calyx‑tube hemispherical, apex truncate. Corolla white or greenish white; tube ca. 1 mm, with curling hairs on the lower part of abaxial surface, bearded adaxially; limb deeply 4‑lobed, oblong. Compound berry depressed globose, 8 – 10 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 41; S. P. Lau 174; P. S. Choi 533.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Morinda umbellata L. 羊角藤
Sp. Pl. 176. 1753; FHK 159. 1861; FKH 133. 1912; FHN 3: 332. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 301. 1998.
Morinda umbellata L. subsp. obovata Y. Z. Ruan, FRPS 71(2): 324. 1999.

Trailing, diffuse or somewhat climbing shrubs. Branchlets, petioles and peduncles glabrous or slightly puberulent. Leaves opposite, thinly leathery or papery; petioles 6–10 mm; stipules scarious, 2–5 mm; leaf blade lanceolate‑ovate, obovate‑oblong, or oblong‑lanceolate to ovate‑oblong, 5–12 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sometimes puberulent or with cluster of hairs in axils of veins; lateral veins slender, 5–7 on each side of midvein. Flower‑heads 6–8 mm in diam., 6–12‑flowered, arranged in terminal umbels; peduncles 5–12 mm. Calyx‑tube hemispherical, 0.8–1 mm, apex truncate or obscurely toothed. Corolla white; tube short, glabrous abaxially, bearded in throat; lobes 4, narrowly oblong, 3–3.2 mm, apex obtuse and recurved. Compound berry depressed globose, 8–12 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Sai Wan Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1264; Y. W. Lam 842, 2150.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, India, Sri Lanka, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: May–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Morus alba L. 桑
Sp. Pl. 2: 986. 1753; FKH 244. 1912; FHN 2: 374. 1965; FGD 1: 172. 1987; FOC 5: 23. 2003.

Tree or shrub, 3–10 m tall or more; winter buds red-brown, scales imbricate. Branchlets fine hairy. Petioles 1.5–5.5 cm; leaves ovate or broad-ovate, 5–15 × 5–12 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute, acuminate or obtuse, margin serrate, sometimes variously lobed, pubescent along veins abaxially. Flowers unisexual. Male spike pendulous, 2–3.5 cm, densely white villose. Male flowers: perianth-lobes broad-elliptic, greenish; anther globose or reniform. Female spike 1–2 cm. Female flowers: perianth-lobes obovate, outside and margin hairy; style absent, stigma 2-parted. Syncarps ovoid-ellipsoid, 1–2.5 cm, red or dark purple when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated. H. C. Tang 1164; Y. S. Lau 279.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; cultivated in Korea, Japan, C Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Aug.
Uses: Host (silkworms), food (fruit), fibre, medicinal (folklore).

Mosla dianthera (Buch.‑Ham.ex Roxb.) Maxim. 小魚仙草
Bull. Acad. Imp. Petersbourg. Ser. 3, 20: 457. 1875; FKH 209. 1912; FRPS 66: 297, pl. 64: 1 – 7. 1977; FOC 17: 245. 1994; FGD 3: 447, fig. 280. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 492, pl. 217. 1998.
Lycopus dianthera Buch.‑Ham. ex Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 144. 1820.

Annual aromatic herbs, up to 1 m tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, subglabrous, often woody at base. Leaves opposite; petioles 3–18 mm. pubescent; leaf blade rhomboid or ovate 1.2–3.5 × 0.5–1.8 cm, base acute or cuneate, apex acute, margin few‑toothed, glabrous or nearly so, sparsely dotted with sunk glands. Racemes terminal, 3–15(–30) cm, often branched; bracts lanceolate, 1–2 mm subtending the flowers. Calyx campanulate, 2– 2.5 mm, lengthening to 4–5 mm in fruit, throat hairy annulate inside; teeth deltoid, the lower 2 teeth larger than the upper ones. Corolla purplish, 3.5–5 mm, puberulent abaxially, glabrous or obscurely hairy annulate adaxially. Nutlets ellipsoidal 1–1.6 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 3257.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Malaysia, India, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.; friuting: Oct.–May of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Mosla scabra (Thunb.) C. Y. Wu & H. W. Li 石薺薴
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 230. 1974; FRPS 66: 294. 1977; FOC 17: 244. 1994; FGD 3: 446. 1995.
Perilla lanceolata Benth., Prodr. 12: 164. 1848; FHK 276. 1861.
Mosla lanceolata Maxim., Melanges Biol. Bull. Phys.‑Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 9: 434. 1879; FKH 209. 1912.
Ocimum scabrum Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 2: 338. 1794.

Annual aromatic herbs, 20–100 cm tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, densely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 3–6 mm, pubescent; leaf ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–3.5 × 0.9–1.7 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin serrate, adaxially grey puberulent, abaxially subglabrous or slightly puberulent, densely dotted with sunk glands. Racemes terminal, 2.5–15 cm; bracts ovate, 2.7–3.5 mm, apex caudate‑acuminate; pedicels ca. 1 mm, lengthening to 3 mm in fruit, densely grey pubescent. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely pubescent abaxially; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑toothed; teeth ovate‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, the middle one slightly smaller, the lower lip 2‑toothed, teeth linear, apex acute. Corolla pink, 4–5 mm, puberulent abaxially, hairy annulate near base adaxially. Nutlets globose, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Cheung Sheung, Plover Cove, Tai Lam. L. T. Lo 642; HK sheet 39291, 40259.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Liaoning, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open fields near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Mucuna birdwoodiana Tutcher 白花油麻藤（勃氏黧豆）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 37: 65. 1904; FKH 83. 1912; FRPS 41: 179. 1995; FGD 5: 299. 2003.

Large woody climber; flowing white juice first then become red soon when hurt, transverse section of stem red-brown, with 3 – 4 obliquely concentric circles. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, subleathery, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; terminal leaflets elliptic, ovate or ± obovate, 3–16 × 2–6 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex caudate-acuminate; acumen 1.3 – 2 cm; lateral leaflets oblique at base. Racemes axillary or borne on old branches, 20–38 cm. Flowers 2–3 on each node. Calyx campanulate, rusty pubescent on both surfaces; calyx-tube 1–1.5 cm, the upper 2 teeth connate, the lowest tooth longest, 5–15 mm. Corolla greyish white, vexillum ovate-orbicular, 3.5 – 4 cm; wings 6 – 7 cm; keel 7.5 – 8.7 cm, narrowly winged, brown pubescent. Stamen-tube 5.5 – 6.5 cm. Ovary densely brown pubescent. Pods leathery, loriform, 30– 45 × 3.5–4 cm, 5–13-seeded, densely rusty-pubescent, with 2 narrow wings along sutures, slightly constricted between seeds. Seeds suborbicular, 2.8 – 3 × 2 – 2.5 cm, purple-black, shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1106, 2852.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal, ornamental, seed poisonous.
Notes: The type specimen (Herb. HK. Bot. Gard. n. 980) was collected from Mount Parker by W. J. Tutcher in 1903.
records.uses:
Medicinal, ornamental, seed poisonous.
Notes: The type specimen (Herb. HK. Bot. Gard. n. 980) was collected from Mount Parker by W. J. Tutcher in 1903.
