Mucuna championii Benth. 港油麻藤（香港黧豆）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 49. 1852; FHK 87. 1861; FKH 83. 1912; FRPS 41: 172. 1995; FGD 5: 298. 2003.
Mucuna nigricans var. hongkongensis Wilmot-Dear, Kew Bull. 39(1): 45. 1984.

Tall woody climber, up to 10 m or longer. Branchlets densely rusty pubescent when young, glabrescent in age. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; terminal leaflets broadly ovate, ovate-elliptic or elliptic, 5–10.5 × 3.5–5.5 cm, base obtuse or rounded, apex acute or obtuse, apiculate, lateral ones obliquely ovate, adaxial surface covered with golden-yellow silky hairs when young, rusty pubescent on abaxial surface, glabrescent on both surfaces in age. Racemes 8 – 20 cm. Flowers often 3 on each node. Calyx broadly campanulate, brownish hairy on both surfaces; tube 7 – 9 mm, the lowest tooth longest, 4 – 8 mm. Corolla purple; vexillum suborbicular or ovate-orbicular, 2.5 cm; wings 4–4.3 cm; keel as long as wings or slightly longer. Stamen-tube 3–3.2 cm. Ovary hairy, 4-ovuled. Pods leathery, obliquely oblong, 3 –4-seeded, 15 – 17.5 × 5 – 5.8 cm (including wings), winged on both surfaces, valves reticulate, with 11 – 15 pieces of folds. Seeds red-brown to brown-black, reniform-elliptic, 2.5–2.8 × 2 – 2.5 cm.

Locality: Causeway Bay, Tai Po, She Shan Tsuen, Lam Tsuen Valley, Fung Yuen, Plover Cove, Kuk Po. Y. S. Lau 3337, 3386; HK sheet 39902.
Distribution: Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Climbing on rocks and trees in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Buddhist Temple, East Point by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Buddhist Temple, East Point by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Mucuna macrobotrys Hance 大球油麻藤（長莢黧豆）
Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 422. 1851; FHK 87. 1861 (sphalm. “macrobotrya”); FKH 83. 1912; FRPS 41: 174. 1995; FGD 5: 297. 2003.

Large woody climber. Stems rusty-pubescent or glabrous. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, glabrous; terminal leaflets elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 9.5 – 11 × 4.2 – 5.5 cm, base obtuse or rounded, apex acuminate; acumen 5 – 7 mm or longer; lateral leaflets very oblique, slightly smaller, lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Racemes axillary, 7– 27 cm, on a very long peduncle. Flowers often 3 on each node. Calyx broadly campanulate, densely sericeous; tube 10 mm; teeth unequal, the lowest tooth longest, up to 10 mm. Corolla dark purple; vexillum rounded, 3.7 – 4.5 cm; wings 6 – 7 cm; keel 7.5 – 9 cm, with a hard beak. Stamens tube 6.5 7 cm. Ovary 3-ovuled. Pods oblong, 16 – 17 × 4.5 – 5 cm (including wings), 2 – 3-seeded, pubescent, winged on both sutures, valves purple-black, reticulate, with 12–16 pieces of oblique folds, folds 6– 15 mm wide. Seeds reniform, 1.2 cm.

Locality: Causeway Bay.
Distribution: Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Climbing on trees in forests.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected near Buddhist Temple, Causeway Bay by Hance before 1851, but the plants perhaps are introduced (Bentham, 1861).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected near Buddhist Temple, Causeway Bay by Hance before 1851, but the plants perhaps are introduced (Bentham, 1861).

records.text:
Murdannia bracteata (C. B. Clarke) Kuntze ex J. K. Morton 大苞水竹葉
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 59(380): 472. 1966.
Murdannia bracteata (C. B. Clarke) J. K. Morton ex D. Y. Hong, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 473. 1974; FRPS 13(3): 109. 1997; FOC 24: 30. 2000; FGD 6: 330. 2005.
Aneilema nudiflorum (L.) R. Br. var. bracteatum C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 3: 211. 1881.

Perennial herb, with horizontal rhizomes; roots fibrous, 0.5–1 mm thick, densely tomentose. Main stem strongly abbreviated, with basal rosulate leaves and usually 2 fertile stems arising from the base of main stem, creeping or ascending apically, 20–60 cm; internodes ca. 10 cm, pubescent throughout or only on one side. Basal leaves linear, 20–30 × 1.2–1.8 cm, glabrous on both surfaces or abaxially puberulent, margin ciliate proximally. Cauline leaves ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–12 × 1–1.5 cm, glabrous or scabrous abaxially; leaf sheath pubescent throughout or only hispid-ciliate at mouth. Cincinni (1–)3–5, densely flowered, capitate; peduncle 2–3 cm; involucral bracts leaf-like but smaller; bracts orbicular, 5–7 mm, caducous; pedicels very short, strongly curved, lengthening to 2 – 3 mm in fruit. Sepals ovate-elliptic, ca. 4 mm. Petals blue, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments pubescent; staminodes 3; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, trigonous, ca. 4 mm, Seeds 2 per valve, yellow-brown, radiate striate, white reticulate, not pitted.

Locality: New Territories.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Ravines, sandy soil by water. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Murdannia loriformis (Hassk.) R. S. Rao & Kammathy 牛軛草
Bull. Bot. Surv. India 3: 393. 1961; FRPS 13(3): 108, pl. 27: 3 – 4. 1997; FOC 24: 30. 2000; FGD 6: 330. 2005.
Aneilema loriforme Hassk., Pl. Jungh. 2: 143. 1852.
Aneilema nudiflorum R. Br. var. rigidior Benth., FHK 377. 1861. A
neilema angustifolium N. E. Br., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36(251): 151. 1903; FKH 283. 1912.

Perennial herb, without rhizomes; roots fibrous, 0.5–1 mm thick, glabrous or tomentose. Main stem undeveloped, with several fertile stems arising from leaf rosette, diffuse or ascending, 15–50(–100) cm, glabrous or puberulent on one side, very rarely densely hirsute. Basal leaves in rosulate tufts, blade linear, 5 – 15( –30) cm × 6–9 mm, apex acute, margin ciliate only proximally; cauline leaves smaller, 2.5–8 cm × 4–7 mm, ciliate only on one side of sheath mouth, glabrous elsewhere, very rarely densely hirsutulous. Cincinni terminal, with several densely arranged flowers, solitary or 2–3 forming a subcapitate panicle; proximal involucral bracts leaf-like but smaller, distal ones very small, less than 10 mm; peduncle ca. 2.5 cm; bracts suborbicular, ca. 4 mm, caducous; pedicels slightly curved, 2.5–4 mm in fruit. Sepals ovate-elliptic, 3–4 mm. Petals blue or purple-red, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments pubescent; staminodes 3; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, 3–4 mm. Seeds 2 per valve, yellow-brown, radiate striate, finely white reticulate, neither pitted nor verrucose.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 39300, 39301.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Sri Lanka, New Guinea.
Ecology: Wet grassy fields, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. – Sep.

Murdannia nudiflora (L.) Brenan 裸花水竹葉
Kew Bull. 7: 189. 1952; FFJ 6: 460, fig. 415. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 106, pl. 27: 1–2. 1997; FOC 24: 30. 2000; FGD 6: 330. 2005.
Commelina nudiflora L., Sp. Pl. 1: 41. 1753.
Aneilema nudiflorum (L.) R. Br., Prodr. 271. 1810; FHK 376. 1861; FKH 283. 1912.

Annual herb, without rhizomes; roots fibrous less than 0.3 mm thick; stems in tufts, diffuse or ascending from the creeping base, 10 – 50 cm, glabrous. Leaves nearly all cauline, sometimes 1–2 basal; leaf sheath mostly less than 10 mm, hirsute throughout, sometimes glabrous except for a hirsute line along mouth slit; leaf blade linear or lanceolate, 2–7(–10) × 0.5–1 cm, glabrous or sparsely hispid on both surfaces, apex obtuse or acuminate. Cincinni several, in terminal panicles, or solitary, with several densely arranged flowers; peduncle slender, to 4 cm; proximal involucral bracts leaf-like but smaller than leaves, distal ones less than 10 mm; bracts caducous; pedicels slender, straight, 3–5 mm. Sepals ovate-elliptic, ca. 3 mm. Petals purple, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments bearded proximally; staminodes 2–4; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, 3–4 mm. Seeds 2 per valve, yellow-brown, deeply pitted, or shallowly pitted and radiate white verrucose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Lai Chi Chong, Luk Keng, Po Toi Islands. Y. S. Lau 2357; Y. W. Lam 1065; HK sheet 41521.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Fujian; Japan, Philippines, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea, Indian Ocean and Pacific islands
Ecology: Shaded and wet places, watersides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Murdannia simplex (Vahl) Brenan 細竹篙草
Kew Bull. 7: 186. 1952; FRPS 13(3): 110, pl. 27: 5 – 6. 1997; FOC 24: 31. 2000; FGD 6: 331. 2005.
Commelina simplex Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 177. 1806.
Aneilema sinicum Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. t. 659. 1822; FKH 283. 1912.

Perennial herb, without rhizomes; roots robust, 2–3 mm thick, densely tomentose. Main stem strongly abbreviated, with 2–4 fertile stems arising from the base of main stems, usually erect, sometimes ascending, to 50 cm. Basal leaves rosulate, with sheath hirsute only on one side; leaf blade linear, 15–35 × 0.6–1.5 cm, glabrous. Cauline leaves often 2–3, rarely more, proximal one longer, to 12 cm, distal ones shorter, sometimes only ca. 1 cm, glabrous. Cincinni several, to 2 cm, forming narrow panicles ca. 5 cm; peduncle ca. 1 cm; involucral bracts ovate or ovate-lanceolate, less than 1 cm, membranous, caducous; bracts subequaling sepals, caducous; flowers pendulous in bud, ascending after anthesis; pedicels straight, ca. 5 mm in fruit. Sepals elliptic, 4–5 mm. Petals purple, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments bearded; staminodes 3; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, 4–5 mm. Seeds 2 per valve, brownblack, white radiate verrucose.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Sai Kung, Fanling, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 52; Y. W. Lam 283, 1778.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan; Africa, India to Indonesia.
Ecology: Marshes, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Murdannia triquetra (Wall. ex C. B. Clarke) G. Brückn. 水竹葉
Nat. Pfl.-Syst. (ed. 2), 15a: 173. 1930; FFJ 6: 460, fig. 414. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 95, pl. 25: 1 – 3. 1997; FOC 24: 27. 2000; FGD 6: 327, fig. 188. 2005.
Aneilema triquetrum Wall. ex C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 3: 208. 1881.

Perennial herb, with elongate, horizontal rhizomes and fibrous roots. Stems ascending from the creeping base, to 40 cm, with a line of harsh, white hairs on one side. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath fringed with white hairs; leaf blade linear-lanceolate or linear-elliptic, 1.5–4(–6) cm × 4–6(–8) mm, apex acuminate or obtuse, ciliate only in proximal part. Cincinni terminal and axillary, usually 1-flowered; peduncle 1–4 cm, with linear bract at middle, sometimes with a flower in axil of bract; pedicels 1–2 cm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 4–6 mm. Petals pink, purple-red, or blue-purple, obovate. Fertile stamens 3; filaments bearded; staminodes 3; antherodes sagittate. Capsule ovoidglobose, trigonous, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, obtuse or acute at both ends. Seeds (1–)3 per valve, uniseriate, reddish grey, not flattened.

Locality: Tai Mong Tsai, Lai Chi Wo. Y. S. Lau 307; HK sheet 39267.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India.
Ecology: Wet places, watersides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food, medicinal (folklore).

Murdannia vaginata (L.) G. Brückn. 細柄水竹葉
Nat. Pfl.-Syst. (ed. 2), 15a: 173. 1930; FRPS 13(3): 99. 1997; FOC 24: 28. 2000; FGD 6: 329. 2005.
Commelina vaginata L., Mant. Pl. 2: 177. 1771.
Aneilema vaginatum (L.) R. Br., Prodr. 271. 1810; FKH 283. 1912.
Dictyospermum vaginatum (L.) D. Y. Hong, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12(4): 477. 1974.

Perennial herb, with elongate rhizomes and fibrous roots; stems slender and creeping or slightly robust and ascending, 15–50 cm, branched at base, glabrous or with a line of hairs on one side. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath open, ciliate; leaf blade linear, 4–10(–20) cm × 4–7 mm, glabrous, margin ciliate. Flowers 1–5, fasciculate in sheath-like involucral bracts; peduncle slender, 5–10(–20) cm; involucral bracts 1–3 on each stem, distant, striate; pedicels 1–1.5 cm, with 2 bracteoles at middle, hirsute distally. Sepals lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, initially hairy, glabrescent, persistent. Petals blue, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments pubescent; staminodes 3 or 4; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule globose, ca. 3 mm in diam. Seeds 1 per valve, grey-black, reticulate.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling, Lo Wu, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2777; Y. W. Lam 893; HK sheet 41814.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangsu; Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Murraya paniculata (L.) Jack 九里香
Malay. Misc. 31. 1820; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 554, fig. 2838. 1972; FHN 3: 44. 1974; FTW 3: 521, pl. 710. 1977; FGD 2: 260, fig. 172: 2– 3. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 141, pl. 36: 2– 3. 1997, excl. syn. M. omphalocarpa Hayata.
Chalcas paniculata L., Mant. Pl. 1: 68. 1767.
Murraya exotica L., Mant. Pl. 2: 563. 1771; FHK 50. 1861; FKH 56. 1912; FGD 2: 259, fig. 172: 1. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 143, pl. 36: 1. 1997.
Murraya paniculata var. exotica (L.) C. C. Huang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 100, pl. 11 –12. 1959; FHN 3: 44. 1974.

Small tree, to 12 m tall. Trunk and branchlets greyish white or pale yellowish grey, slightly glossy. Juvenile branches green, obtusely triangular in cross section. Leaves 3 –5(–7)-foliolate; petiolule less than 1 cm; leaflet blade ovate, ovate-lanceolate, broadly obovate or obovate-elliptic, 1–9 × 0.6–4 cm, base cuneate, symmetrical or slightly asymmetrical, apex long acuminate, rounded or obtuse, margin entire and wavy, glossy adaxially. Inflorescences axillary or terminal. Calyx lobes ovate, ca. 2 mm, margin sparsely hairy, persistent. Petals white, oblanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 1–2 cm, reflexed when full blooming, scattered with pale yellow translucent glands. Stamens 10, unequal, glabrous; filaments white, filiform, slightly shorter than style. Ovary 2-locular, ovule 1 per locule; style green, slender. Fruit orange-yellow to red, narrowly ellipsoidal, rarely ovoid, 1–2 × 0.5–1.4 cm, apex narrowed. Seeds 1–2, hairy.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 220, 1897; HK sheet 9269.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental (hedge, bonsai).

Musa acuminata 'Dwarf Cavendish' 香蕉
Mem. Reale Accad. Sci. Torino 25: 394–395. 1820; FGD 2: 394. 1991; FOC 24: 316. 2000.
Musa nana Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 644. 1790; FRPS 16(2): 9. 1981.
Musa cavendishii Lamb. ex Paxt., Mag. Bot. 3: 51, pl. s.n. f. 1. 1837.
Musa chinensis Sweet, Hort. Britann. ed. 2, 596. 1826.

Pseudostems clumped, ca. 6 m tall, yellow-green, often with large, black markings. Petiole 60–75 cm, margin open, ca. 2 cm wide, often closed when young; leaf blade ovate-oblong, ca. 2.9 m × 90 cm, base auriculate, asymmetric, adaxially green and slightly pruinose or not. Inflorescence pendulous, ca. 2.5; peduncle and rachis glabrous. Bracts of bisexual and male flowers adaxially purple-red, abaxially brownish purple to yellow-green and pruinose, ovate to lanceolate, persistent, apex obtuse, reflexed after flowering; bracts of female flowers deciduous. Male flowers up to 20 per bract, in 2 rows. Compound tepal adaxially pale purple, abaxially pale purple-white, 4–5 cm, striate, teeth yellow to orange; free tepal milky white, translucent, obovate, about half the length of compound tepal, apex emarginate, shortly mucronate-apiculate. Infructescence pendulous, with ca. 8 clusters (“hands”) each of 15 or 16 berries in 2 rows. Berries grey-green, obovoid, ca. 13 × 4 cm, distinctly angled at maturity, base arrowed into a stalk ca. 2.5 cm, apex contracted or not into a short, angled column ca. 2 cm. Seeds many, brown, oblate, 5–10 mm in diam., minutely warty.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 9189.
Distribution: S China; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Edible fruit.
Notes: The species was reported as Musa acuminata ‘Cavendishii’ previously (Check List HK Plants 351. 2002; 122. 2004).
records.uses:
Edible fruit.
Notes: The species was reported as Musa acuminata ‘Cavendishii’ previously (Check List HK Plants 351. 2002; 122. 2004).

records.text:
Musa balbisiana Colla 野蕉
Mem. Reale Accad. Sci. Torino 25: 384. 1820; Cheesm., Kew Bull. 1948(1): 14. 1948; FHN 4: 88. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 8. 1981; FGD 2: 393. 1991; FOC 24: 317. 2000.
Musa × paradisiaca L. subsp. seminifera (Lour.) Baker, Ann. Bot. 7: 213. 1893.
Musa seminifera Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 644. 1790.

Pseudostems clumped, to 6 m tall, yellow-green, often with black blotches. Petioles 60–75 cm, margin open, ca. 2 cm wide, often closed when young; leaf blade oblong, 2.9 m × 90 cm, base auriculate, asymmetric, adaxially green and slightly pruinose or not. Inflorescence pendulous, ca. 2.5 m; peduncle and rachis glabrous. Bracts of bisexual and male flowers adaxially purple-red, abaxially brownish purple to yellow-green and pruinose, ovate to lanceolate, persistent, apex obtuse, reflexed after flowering; bracts of female flowers deciduous. Male flowers up to 20 per bract, in 2 rows. Compound tepal abaxially pale purple, abaxially pale purple-white, 4–5 cm, striate, teeth yellow to orange; free tepal milky white, translucent, obovate, about half the length of compound tepal, apex emarginate, shortly mucronate-apiculate. Infructescence pendulous, with ca. 8 clusters (“hands”) each of 15 or 16 berries in 2 rows. Berries grey-green, obovoid, ca. 13 × 4 cm, distinctly angled at maturity, base narrowed into a stalk ca. 2.5 cm, apex contracted or not, into a short, angled column ca. 2 cm. Seeds many, brown, oblate, 5–10 mm in diam., minutely warty.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 756; Y. W. Lam 1154.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Moist places in ravines.

Musa coccinea Andrews 紅蕉
Bot. Repos. 1: pl. 47. 1799; FRPS 16(2): 14. 1981; FGD 2: 392. 1991; FOC 24: 316. 2000.
Musa uranoscopos Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 645. 1790.

Pseudostems 1–1.5 m tall, green. Petioles 30–40 cm, with narrow erect margins clasping pseudostem, not becoming scarious; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 55–100 × 15–25 cm, base rounded or obtuse, noticeably asymmetric, yellow-green, not pruinose. Inflorescence erect, elliptic, to 30 × 12 cm, very shortly pedunculate above sheath of topmost normal leaf, rachis glabrous. Bracts bright scarlet with green tips, lanceolate or oblong, 5.5–15 × 2.5–5.5 cm, after anthesis persisting during a very long time in an unfaded state. Male flowers 2 per bract, orange. Syntepalum 3.5–4 cm, 5-obtuse-dentated at top, free tepal nearly equaling syntepalum. Female flowers 1–3 per bract; perianth as in male flowers. Ovary orange-yellow, dorsiventrally compressed. Berries orange-yellow at full maturity, oblong, 4–10 cm, crowned persistent perianth; stalk 3–3.5 cm. Seeds many, cylindrical, 6 × 4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28086.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Musa × paradisiaca L. 大蕉（甘蕉）
Sp. Pl. 2: 1043. 1753; FHN 4: 87. 1977; FGD 2: 394. 1991; FOC 24: 317. 2000.
Musa saepientum L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1477. 1763; FKH 273. 1912.
Musa paradisiaca L. subsp. sapientum (L.) Kuntze, Rev. Gen. 2: 692. 1891.

Pseudostems clumped, 3–7 m tall, pruinose. Petiole pruinose, more than 30 cm, margin closed; leaf blade oblong, 1.5–3 m × 40–60 cm, base subcordate to auriculate, subsymmetric, apex acute, adaxially deep green, abaxially light green and distinctly pruinose. Inflorescence pendulous; rachis glabrous. Bracts adaxially deep red, abaxially purple, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 15–30 cm or more, deciduous. Flowers in 2 rows in each bract; male flowers with tepals yellow to pale yellow. Compound tepal 4–6.5 cm; free tepal suborbicular to oblong, about half the length of compound tepal, waxy, apex acuminate or rolling into a sac. Infructescence with 7 or 8 clusters of berries. Berries straight or slightly curved, oblong, 10–20 cm, angled; pulp sweet or sweet and acidic, not very fragrant; stalk elongate. Seeds absent or few.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 9190.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Edible fruit.

Mussaenda erosa Champ. ex Benth. 楠藤（野白紙扇）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 193. 1852; FHK 153. 1861; FKH 130. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 293, pl. 78: 4 – 6. 1999; FYN 14: 146, pl. 28: 1 – 5. 2003; FGD 6: 167. 2005.

Evergreen scandent shrubs, to 3 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Stipules narrowly triangular, 7–8 mm, glabrous or strigose, deeply 2‑lobed. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 6–12 × 3.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to long‑acuminate, initially slightly pubescent on veins of adaxial surface, sparsely appressed‑pubescent on abaxial surface, but glabrous on both surfaces in age. Corymbs terminal, large and loose, long‑pedunculate. Calyx‑tube ellipsoidal, 3–3.5 mm, glabrous; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, sparsely covered with short hairs at the base, one of them in a few of the outer flowers enlarged, broadly elliptic, white, 4–6 × 3–4 cm, apex rounded or acute, base abruptly narrowed into a long (0.9–1 cm) petiole, glabrous. Corolla yellow, tube 1.2–1.8 cm, pubescent abaxially, densely covered with clavate hairs at throat; lobes ovate, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, with minute yellow tubercles inside. Berries subglobular to broadly ellipsoidal, 8–10 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Ng Tung Chai, Ping Shan Chai, Fanling, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 390, 558; Y. S. Lau 616.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Mussaenda kwangtungensis H. L. Li 廣東玉葉金花
J. Arnold Arb. 25: 427. 1944; FRPS 71(1): 302, pl. 80: 4 – 6. 1999; FGD 6: 169, fig. 85. 2005.

Evergreen scandent shrubs 1–2.5 m tall. Branchlets covered with grey short hairs. Stipules 1.5–2 mm, divided to the base; lobes linear, puberulent. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 5 mm, densely puberulent; leaf blade elliptic‑lanceolate, 7–8 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate, apex long acuminate, both surfaces pubescent on veins, other parts sparsely puberulent or glabrescent. Corymbs terminal. Peduncle ca. 5 mm. Calyx‑tube oblong, 2–2.5 mm, puberulent; lobes linear, 3–3.5 mm, densely puberulent, one of them in a few of the outer flowers enlarged, oblong‑ovate, white, 3.5–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex acute, base narrowed into a 1.5 cm long petiole, pubescent. Corolla yellow, tube ca. 4 cm, puberulent abaxially, covered with clavate hairs on the upper part inside the tube; lobes ovate, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, densely pubescent abaxially, with minute golden yellow tubercle adaxially. Style short, included; stigma bifid.

Locality: Bowen Rd. W. Y. Chun 9183 (IBSC).
Distribution: SE Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Spring to summer.

Mussaenda pubescens W. T. Aiton 玉葉金花
Hort. Kew. ed. 2, 1: 372. 1810; FHK 153. 1861; FKH 130. 1912; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 863, fig. 348. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 4: 302. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 296, pl. 79: 5 – 7. 1999; FYN 14: 146. 2003; FGD 6: 168. 2005.

Evergreen scandent shrubs. Branchlets densely appressed‑pubescent. Stipules 5–7 mm, lobed to 2/3 of its length; lobes subulate. Leaves opposite or sometimes subverticillate; petioles 3–8 mm, pubescent; leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, obovate‑elliptic to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–9 × 2–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, pubescent, but the hairs denser on abaxial surface. Cymes corymbiform, terminal. Peduncle 0–7 mm. Pedicels scarcely 1 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 2–2.5 mm, pubescent; lobes subulate, 6–7 mm, one of them in a few of the outer flowers enlarged, broadly ovate or orbicular, white, 2 –4.5 × 1–3.5 cm, apex obtuse or acute, base narrowed into a 1 – 2.8 cm long petiole. Corolla salverform; tube slender, 1.2 – 1.8 cm, green, sparsely appressed‑pubescent abaxially, densely yellowish villose on throat; lobes bright yellow, oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 4 × 2 mm, spreading, with minute golden‑yellow tubercles inside. Style short, included. Berries globular, 8–10 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2143; Y. W. Lam 259; HK sheet 39950.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on roadsides and in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Myoporum bontioides (Siebold & Zucc.) A. Gray 苦檻藍
Proc. Amer. Acad. Art. & Sci. 6: 52. 1862; Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 200. 1912; Z.Y. Li, FRPS 70: 311. 2002.
Pentacoelium bontioides Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Akad. Wiss. Math. Phys. 4(3): 151, t. 3, B. 1846.
Polycoelium chinense A. DC., DC. Prodr. 11: 706. 1847.

Shrubs, evergreen, 50–80 cm tall. Petioles 1–1.5 cm. Leaves alternate; leaf blade narrow‑elliptic, lanceolate or oblong, 6–10 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex acuminate and mucronate, margin entire. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 1.5–2 cm. Calyx 5‑lobed, lobes ovate‑elliptic or deltoid‑ovate, 4–5 mm. Corolla white with purple‑blue spots, campanulate, 2–2.2 cm, 5‑lobed, lobes ovate to oblong, 8–10 mm. Stamens 4, on inside of corolla‑tube, filaments 15–18 mm. Ovary with 5–8 compartments. Drups purple‑red, globular, 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, 5–8‑angulate when dry.

Locality: Tai Po, Chung Pui, Sheung Wo Che. U. A. On 630; H. C. Tang 2509; Y. S. Lau 681.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Myosoton aquaticum (L.) Moench 鵝腸菜（牛繁縷）
Methodus 225. 1794; FRPS 26: 74, pl. 16: 1–9. 1996; FOC 6: 38. 2001. Stellaria aquatica (L.) Scop., Fl. Carn. 2(1): 319. 1774; FHK 20. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FGD 2: 79. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 373, pl. 174, photo 150. 1996.
Cerastium aquaticum L., Sp. Pl. 439. 1753.

Biennial or perennial herbs. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, 50– 80 cm or longer, glabrous or glandular hairy on upper part. Leaves ovate to broadly ovate, 2.5 –5.5 × 1–3 cm, apex acute, base cordate, margin entire, sometimes ciliate, upper ones smaller, on long petioles; lower ones sessile or stem-clasping. Flowers in terminal dichotomous cymes. Bracts foliaceous, ciliate. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm, lengthening after flowering, with glandular hairs. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, 4 – 5 mm, with scarious margin and glandular hairs abaxially. Petals white, deeply 2-lobed to near base; lobes linear to linear-lanceolate, 3 –3.5 × 1 cm. Stamens 10, slightly shorter than petals. Capsule ovoid, opening to middle into five 2-toothed valves.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, So Kon Po, Tai Long Wan, Shing Mun, Mui Tsz Lam. Y. W. Lam 516, 611; HK sheet 294.
Distribution: Dispersed over most parts of China. Widely distributed in temperate Asia; Indian subcontinent; Europe, and naturalized elsewhere in temperate regions.
Ecology: In fields, wet places by streams. Flowering: May– Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (vegetable).

Myriophyllum spicatum L. 穗狀狐尾藻
Sp. Pl. 992. 1753; FHN 1: 432. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 3: 973. 1993; FRPS 53(2): 136, pl. 27: 1 – 3. 2000.

Perennial submerged herbs, with creeping rhizomes rooted on bottom. Stems terete, 1 – 2.5 m, much branched. Leaves in whorls usually of 5, but sometimes in whorls of 3–4–6, feathery, to 3.5 cm or longer, segments liner, 10 – 15 mm; petioles very short or almost wanting. Flowers small, in a whorled spike (6–10 cm) projecting above water, with male flowers above the females. Male flowers: calyx-tube broadly campanulate, apex 4-lobed; petals 4, pinkish, broadly spathulate, concave, ca. 2.5 mm; stamens 8; anthers ca. 2 mm, light yellow. Female flowers: calyx-tube tubular, apex 4-lobed; petals absent or inconspicuous; ovary 4-locular, styles 4, with feathery stigmas. Fruit ovoid or oval-ellipsoidal, 2–3 mm, 4-grooved.

Locality: Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 3212.
Distribution: Widely spread over most regions of the world.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds. Flowering: Apr. –Aug.
Uses: Animal food, medicinal (folklore).

Myriophyllum tetrandrum Roxb. 四蕊狐尾藻
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 470. 1820; FHN 1: 433. 1964; FRPS 53(2): 140. 2000.

Perennial submerged herbs, with creeping rhizomes in mud. Stems terete, to 2 m or longer, less branched, apex projecting above water. Leaves in whorls usually of 4, feathery, to 8 cm or longer, segments liner, 10–13 mm; leaves at apex of stem above water lanceolate or spathulate, margin ± toothed, decreasing gradually upwards into bract of about 0.4 mm, palmately lobed. Flowers solitary in axils of the whorled leaves, male above female, short-pedicellate. Calyx-tube 4-angled; lobes triangular, 0.2 × 0.15 mm. Petals spathulate, flat, membranous, 1 × 0.4 mm. Stamens 4. Styles 4, with papillose stigmas. Fruit globose, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Sha Kok Mei, Wang Tong Tsuen. P. S. Choi 26; Y. S. Lau 3251; Y. W. Lam 193.
Distribution: Hainan; Indochina, India.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds and ditches. Flowering: Sep.

Myrsine seguinii H. Léveillé 密花樹
Fl. Kouy-Tcheou 288. 1915; FOC 15: 37. 1996.
Myrsine neriifolia Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: 137. 1846, non Casarato (1843).
Rapanea neriifolia (Sieb. & Zucc.) Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 361.1902.
Myrsine capitellata auct. non Wall.: FHK 205. 1861; FKH 158. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees, 2–7 m, occasionally to 15 m tall. Branches somewhat thick, greyish brown to dark brown, glabrous, wrinkled when dry. Leaves spirally arranged; petioles subterete, 0.9–1.5 mm; leaf blade leathery, narrowly oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 5–15 × 1.3 –3 cm, apex acute or obtuse, base cuneate, entire, narrowly recurved, glabrous, with many tiny sunken pits on abaxial surface; lateral veins usually more than 15 pairs, inconspicuous, meeting in an intramarginal vein near edge. Inflorescence umbellate, terminal on short verrucose spurs, 3 –10-flowered. Pedicels rather thick, 1– 4 mm. Flowers white to light green, sometimes reddish. Calyx-lobes ovate, ca. 1 mm, obtuse or acute, fused at base, ciliate, sparsely punctate or not. Corolla 2.5–3 mm; lobes split to 3/4 of its length, lobes ovate to elliptic, acute or obtuse, punctate, densely papillose along the margin. Stamens adnate about to the base of corolla-lobes; filaments very short; anthers ovate, ca. 1.2 mm. Ovary glabrous; stigma as long as or longer than corolla-lobes, cylindric at base, upper part ± flattened, sometimes split at apex. Fruit subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam., punctate.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 984, 2884; L. T. Lo 594; H. C. Tang 12244.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Yunnan, SE Xizang; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Thickets and disturbed evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Nageia nagi (Thunb.) Kuntze 竹柏
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 798. 1891; FOC 4: 80. 1999; FGD 4: 33, fig.22. 2000.
Myrica nagi Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 884. 1784.
Podocarpus nagi (Thunb.) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 17:113. 1903; FRPS 7: 404, pl. 90. 1978.

Tree to 20 m tall; bark nearly smooth, reddish brown, dark purplish red, peeling off in small, thin flakes; branchlets spreading; crown broadly conical. Leaves opposite; petiole strongly twisted at base; blade leathery, ovate-lanceolate, elliptic-lanceolate, or narrowly elliptic, 3.5–9 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, dark green and glossy adaxially, pale green abaxially, parallel veins indistinct. Pollen cones axillary, solitary or in clusters of up to 10, cylindric, 1.8–2.5 cm. Seed-bearing structures axillary, solitary rarely paired. Receptacle obsolete, consisting of few bracts. Epimatium green with white bloom when young, dark purple with sparser white bloom when ripe. Seed globose to pyriform, 1–1.5 cm in diam., with dense punctiform depressions, base pointed, apex rounded.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 26939, 34481.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Najas graminea Delile 草茨藻
Descr. Égypte, Hist. Nat. 2: 282. 1813; FKH 291. 1912; Triest , Mém. Acad. Roy. Sci. Outre-Mer, Cl. Sci. Nat. Méd., Collect. 8vo. 22: 135. 1988; FRPS 8: 123. 1992; FGD 6: 312. 2005; FOC 23: 93. 2010.
Najas minor auct. non Allioni: FHK 345. 1861.

Stems unarmed, 10–20(– 60) cm tall, 0.5 – 1(– 1.5) mm in diam. Leaves narrowly linear to linear, 10–25(–33) × 0.4–1 mm; septa absent; fibres mostly present on and near both sides of the midrib and near margins; sheath 1.5–3(–4) × 1–2 mm, deeply auriculate; auricles narrowly triangular or lanceolate, 1–2 × 0.2–0.3 mm, serrulate with several teeth on each side, apex acute; leaf margin minutely and densely serrulate with 30–50 inconspicuous teeth on each side, consisting of brownish spine cells only. Plants monoecious; flowers solitary, or sometimes 2–4 together. Male flowers naked, usually more toward upper axils, ca. 1 mm, elliptic; spathe absent; anther 4-celled. Female flowers naked, 1.5–2(–3.7) mm; style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 2(–4)-lobed. Fruit oblong, 1.5–2 × ca. 0.8 mm. Seeds ellipsoidal-oblong, 1.5–2.4 × 0.5–0.7, with 25 – 35 rows of pits; areoles hexangular and irregularly polygonal toward ends, or rectangular, 0.06–0.08 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung. C. Wright 511 (BM, K); HK sheet 42834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hebei, Henan, Liaoning, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in Asia, Australia and Europe; introduced in N America.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields, usually in still or slow-moving water. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The species was recorded as Najas minor Allioni previously (Check List HK Plants 293. 2002; 103. 2004), based on an un-confirmed sighting record in the 1990s. The earliest record is the specimen collected by Charles Wright during the U. S. North Pacific Exploring Expedition (1853–1856), then identified as “N. minor” (FHK, 1861). However, N. minor as currently recognised is distinguished by its stems armed with spines and leaves with septa. Recently, a population of N. graminea has been found in a sheltered pool in Sai Kung.

Najas pseudogracillima Triest 擬纖細茨藻
Mém. Acad. Roy. Sci. Outre-Mer, Cl. Sci. Nat. Méd., Collect. 8vo. 22: 98. 1988; FOC 23: 93. 2010.

Stems ca. 10 cm tall, ca. 0.5 mm in diam. Leaves often in pseudowhorls of 5, 9–11 × ca. 0.3 mm; midrib lacking spines; septa absent; fibres absent; sheath truncate, 1–2 mm; auricles orbicular to slightly obcordate, short, minutely serrulate with 3–5 teeth, upper margin on each side minutely serrulate with 6 – 10 teeth. Plants monoecious; flowers 1–3 per axil, male flowers in upper axils and female ones below. Male flowers elliptic, 0.6–0.8 mm; spathe absent; anther 1-celled; unisporangiate. Female flowers inconspicuous, ca. 1 mm; style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 2–3-lobed. Fruit 1.8–2 × ca. 0.5 mm. Seeds elliptic-oblong, 1.85–2.0 × 0.5 mm, with more than 25 rows of pits, not enclosed in spathe; areoles oblong, longitudinally elongate, rather irregularly arranged per 12–15 in each longitudinal row, irregularly shaped and longer than broad; cell walls not raised.

Locality: Sha Tin (Chung Chi College Campus). J. P. W. Woo 2 (P); S. Y. Hu 11263 (K).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 11263, K) was collected from the campus of Chung Chi College on 22 Nov. 1971. Triest (1988) noted that, in the specimen Woo 2 (deposited at P), this species was found mixed with N. pseudograminea. Najas pseudogracillima is vegetatively similar to N. gracillima but differs by having male flowers without a spathe, whereas N. gracillima has male flowers with a spathe.

Najas pseudograminea W. Koch 擬草茨藻
Ber. Schweiz. Bot. Ges. 44: 339. 1935; Triest, Mém. Acad. Roy. Sci. Outre-Mer, Cl. Sci. Nat. Méd., Collect. 8vo. 22: 121. 1988; FOC 23: 93. 2010.
Najas tenuifolia R. Br. subsp. pseudograminea (W. Koch) W. J. de Wilde, Fl. Malesiana 1(6): 168. 1962.

Stems ca. 10 cm tall, ca. 1 mm in diam. Leaves often in pseudowhorls of 3, 16–20 × 0.6–1.0 mm; midrib without spines; septa clearly visible up to halfway the margin; fibers present near each margin but absent on and near both sides of the midrib; sheath truncate to auriculate, 1–2 mm; auricles linear, short, minutely serrulate with 3–8 teeth, upper margin on each side minutely serrulate with 30–50 teeth. Plants monoecious; flowers 1–3 per axil, male flowers in upper axils and female ones below. Male flowers elliptic, 1.5–2.3 mm, enclosed in spathe with short neck; anther 4-celled. Female flowers inconspicuous, ca. 0.7–1 mm; style ca. 0.7 mm; stigmas 2- or 3-lobed. Fruit 1–1.3 × ca. 0.4 mm. Seeds not enclosed in spathe, elliptic-oblong, 1–1.3 × 0.24–0.43 mm, with more than 20 rows of pits; areoles regularly arranged per 25–30 in each longitudinal row, squarish to hexagonal or rectangular; cell walls not raised.

Locality: Sha Tin (Chung Chi College Campus). J. P. W. Woo 2 (P).
Distribution: Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia, East Timor, Solomon Islands, N Australia.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.
Notes: Triest (1988) noted that, in the specimen Woo 2 (deposited at P), this species was found mixed with N. pseudogracillima.

Nandina domestica Thunb. 南天竺
Fl. Jap. 9. 1784; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 32. 1886; FGZ 98. 1956; FGD 3: 15. 1995; FRPS 29: 52, pl. 11. 2001.

Evergreen shrub, 1.5 –2 m tall, glabrous throughout. Stems tufted, unbranched. Leaves twice or thrice pinnate, 30 –50 cm; petioles sheathed and semi-amplexicaul at the base, rachis articulate; pinnae opposite; leaflets subsessile, thinly leathery, lanceolate to ellipticlanceolate, 1.5– 4(–7) × 0.8 –1.5 –2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, apiculate, margin entire. Panicles terminal, erect, 13 –25 cm; pedicels 3 –5 mm. Sepals many, greenish, scarious, the lowest small, triangular, ca. 1 mm, upper ones larger, ovate to ovate-elliptic, to 4.5 mm. Petals 6, white, sub-scarious, elliptic, 6–7.5 × 3–3.5 mm. Stamens 6, rarely 7, subsessile, 4.5–5 mm, yellow. Ovary urceolate, about the length of the stamens; style very short. Fruit a globular berry, scarlet, ca. 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 32807; Y. S. Lau 1902.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Henan, Shandong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: The plant shrives in calcareous soil, but also grows well in acid soil. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov. to Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Narcissus tazetta L. var. chinensis M. Roemer 水仙
Fam. Nat. Syn. Monogr. 4: 223. 1847; FRPS 16(1): 28, pl. 8: 1–2. 1985; FOC 24: 269. 2000; FGD 5: 444, fig. 237. 2003.

Perennial herb, whole plant somewhat glaucous. Bulbs ovoid. Leaves broadly linear, flat, 20–40 × 0.8–1.5 cm, apex obtuse, margin entire. Scape erect, about the length of the leaves. Umbels 4–10-flowered; involucres membranous. Flowers fragrant, spreading or nodding; pedicels unequal, perianth salverform; tube slender, ca. 2 cm, pale green, nearly 3-angled; segments 6, white, widely spreading, broadly elliptic to obovate, ca. 1.5 cm, apex shortly acute; corona pale yellow, shallowly cupular, scarcely half the length of the perianth, margin not undulate. Stamens 6, inserted at upper part of perianth tube; filaments very short. Ovary 3-angled, green, with a slender style and a 3-lobed stigma.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28331.
Distribution: Fujian, Zhejiang; possibly of Mediterranean origin.
Ecology: Usually the plant is cultivated in water as a pot plant, especially during the Chinese New Year. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.
Uses: Ornamental.

Nasturtium officinale R. Br. 西洋菜
Hort. Kew. 4: 110. 1812; FGD 3: 40 1995; FOC 8: 136. 2001.
Rorippa nasturtium-aquaticum (L.) Hayek, Sched. Fl. Stir. Exs. 22. 1905.
Sisymbrium nasturtium-aquaticum L., Sp. Pl. 657. 1753.

Perennial herb, 20 – 40 cm tall, glabrous. Stems decumbent or prostrate on water surface, many branched, rooting at nodes. Leaves all cauline, pinnately compound, 3–9-foliolate, leaflets sessile, ovate, oblong or suborbiculate, 2–3 cm, base obtuse or subcordate, margin subentire or repand. Racemes terminal. Sepals oblong, 2–3 mm, lateral pair slightly saccate. Petals white or pink, obovate or spathulate, 3–4 mm, claw slender. Stamens 6. Siliques cylindric, 0.5 –2 cm. Seeds biseriate, reddish brown, ovoid, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hebei, Shanxi, Shandong, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shaanxi, Heilongjiang.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Vegetable, medicinal.

Nauclea officinalis (Pierre ex Pit.) Merr. & Chun 烏檀
Sunyatsenia 5: 188. 1940; FHN 3: 287, fig. 728. 1974; Ridsdale,Blumea 24(2): 328. 1978; FRPS 71(1): 260, pl. 66. 1999.

Evergreen trees, 4–12 m tall. Branchlets slender, smooth; terminal bud obovoid. Stipules obovate, 6–10 mm, apex rounded, caducous. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 10 – 15 mm; leaf blade elliptic, rarely obovate, 7–9 × 3.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, tip ± blunt, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 5–7 on each side of midvein, slightly raised on both surfaces. Flowering head solitary, terminal. Peduncles 1–3 cm. Calyx‑tubes connate, fleshy. Corolla funnel‑shaped, 5‑lobed. Stamens 5, inserted in the upper part of the corolla‑tube. Fruiting head globular, yellowish brown when ripen, 9–15 mm in diam., composed of numerous drupelets.

Locality: Sheung Wo Hang, Wu Kau Tang. S. C. Ng 2644; Y. W. Lam 2012; F. W. Xing 8643.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Indochina, Thailand, Malesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Timber, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Neanotis boerhaavioides (Hance) W. H. Lewis 卷毛新耳草
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 53: 37. 1966; FRPS 71: 82. 1999; FGD 6: 135. 2005.
Hedyotis boerhaavioides Hance, J. Bot. 8(88): 73. 1870.
Anotis boerhaavioides (Hance) Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 29: 165. 1883; FKH 128. 1912.

Annual diffuse herbs, to 6 cm or longer. Stems decumbent at base, rooting at nodes, together with petioles, abaxial surface of leaves and stipules covered with pellucid, curling long hairs. Stipules 3–6 mm, strigose, united with petioles at the base. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate lanceolate, 1.2–4 × 0.6–2 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, ± decurrent, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxial surface sparsely pubescent; lateral veins 4–5(–6) on each side of the midvein. Flowers white, in terminal or axillary cymes. Peduncles 2 – 20 mm sparsely pubescent or glabrescent. Pedicels 1–2 mm or almost obsolete. Calyx‑tube obovate oblate; calyx‑teeth ovate. Corolla‑tube ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous; lobes ovate oblong. Stamens slightly exserted. Ovary inferior; stigma bifid. Capsules in pairs or solitary, oblate, 2–3 mm in diam., pubescent or glabrescent.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 1268; HK sheet 38588.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn to winter.

Neanotis thwaitesiana (Hance) W. H. Lewis 新耳草
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 53: 40. 1966; FRPS 71: 82, pl. 17: 1 – 4. 1999; FGD 6: 136. 2005.
Anotis thwaitesiana Hance, J. Bot. 6: 298. 1868; FKH 129. 1912.

Perennial diffuse herbs, glabrous except flowers. Stems slender, 4‑angled, woody at base. Stipules pectinate, united at the base, apex with a few linear lobes. Leaves opposite, submembranous; petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 × 0.5–1 cm, base obtuse or subrounded, apex acute, scabrous on both surface and margins; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers white or pink, in axillary cymes or paniculate, 2–many times longer than the subtending leaf. Peduncles slender, 1.5–3 cm. Pedicels slender, 3–4 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, 2–2.5 mm; calyx‑teeth triangular ca. 2 mm. Corolla‑tube ca. 1 mm, pubescent outside; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Stamens exserted. Ovary inferior; stigma clavate, bifid. Capsule oblate, 2 – 3 mm in diam., crowned with calyx‑teeth.

Locality: Yi O. HK sheet 35357, 40187.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Wastelands, grasslands. Flowering: Apr.

Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn. 蓮（荷花）
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 73. 1788; FHN 1: 311, fig. 152. 1964; FRPS 27: 3. 1979; FOC 6: 114. 2001.

Aquatic plant. Rhizome 1–5 m, with many constricted nodes and stout internodes, bearing many scale-like leaves and foliage leaves. Foliage leaves peltate, without sinus; petioles 1–2 m, with scattered small prickles; leaf blade almost orbicular, 25–100 cm in diam., glabrous and ± glaucous. Flowers solitary and terminal, 16 –23 cm in diam., pink or white, scented. Pedicels as long as or longer than petioles, also prickly. Nuts ellipsoid or ovoid, 1.7 × 1.3 cm, exocarp leathery.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 1348, 40214.
Distribution: Asia-temperate, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Australia, E Europe; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: In ponds or paddy fields.
Uses: Ornamental, food (nut, rhizomes).

Neolitsea cambodiana Lecomte var. glabra C. K. Allen 香港新木薑子
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 418. 1938; FRPS 31: 346. 1982.
Actinodaphne angustifolia auct. non Nees: Benth., FHK 293. 1861.
Actinodaphne hongkongensis Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 8: 22. 1927.
Neolitsea hongkongensis (Chun) C.K. Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 418. 1938.

Tree, 8 –12 m tall. Branchlets tawny adpressed-pubescent. Leaves 3 –5, subverticillate; petioles 1–1.5 cm, adpressed-pubescent; leaf blade leathery, oblong-lanceolate, oblong-elliptic lanceolate, obovate or elliptic, 10 –17 × 3.5 – 6 cm, base attenuate or cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, glabrous on both surfaces, glaucous abaxially, pinnately veined or subtriplinerved, lateral veins 4 –5 on each side of midvein. Umbels 4 –5-flowered, clustered, sessile or subsessile; bracts 4, pubescent on the ridge of abaxial surface. Male flowers: Perianth-lobes ovate; fertile stamens 6, exserted, filaments villous at the base; pistillodes glabrous. Female flowers: Perianth-lobes linear or ovate-lanceolate, staminodes pubescent at the base; ovary ovoid, stigma bifid. Fruit globose, 8 –10 mm diam., on a discoid perianth tube; fruiting pedicels 7 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak (Lugard Road), Happy Valley. Y. S. Lau 2524, 2649.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian; Cambodia, Laos.
Ecology: Mixed forests, thickets. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of Actinodaphne hongkongensis Chun was collected in Happy Valley Woods by C. Wilford between 1857 and 1858.

Neolitsea chuii Merr. 鴨公樹
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 306. 1929; FRPS 31: 372, pl. 95: 1–2.1982; FGD 6: 50. 2005

Tree, to 8 m tall, glabrous, except for the inflorescence. Leaves alternate or crowded toward apex of the branchlets; petioles 2.5–4 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 8–16 × 3–9 cm, base acute, apex acuminate, glaucous abaxially, triplinerved, lateral veins of 3 –5 pairs. Umbels pubescent, 5 – 6-flowered, axillary or lateral, clustered; peduncles very short or almost obsolete; pedicels 4 –5 mm. Perianth-segments 4, ovate or oblong, abaxially puberulous at base and on midvein. Male flowers: fertile stamens 6; filaments pubescent at base; pistillodes ovoid. Fruit ellipsoid or subglobose, ca. 8 mmin diam.; fruiting pedicels 7 mm, slightly thickened.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau. S. C. Ng 3209, 3240; K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 39679).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Native forests in valleys. Flowering: Sep.– Oct.; fruiting: Dec.

Neolitsea kwangsiensis Liou 廣西新木薑子
Laurac. Chine & Indochine 146. 1932; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 423. 1938; FRPS 31: 370. 1982

Shrub or small tree, to 5 m tall; bark greyish, smooth. Branchlets stout, yellowish brown, glabrous. Bud scales subglabrous abaxially, margin ciliate. Leaves leathery, alternate or clustered towards apex of branchlets; petioles 2.5 –4 mm, slightly compressed, glabrous; leaf blade broadly ovate, ovate or ovate-oblong, 11–19 × 6.8 –12.5 cm, base rotund or attenuate, apex acuminate or obtuse, dark green and slightly lustrous adaxially, glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; triplinerved, primary veins raised on both surfaces. Umbels 5-flowered, 5 –8 in axillary fascicles. Bracts 4, puberulous abaxially. Pedicels short, densely pubescent. Perianth-lobes 4, ovate or ovateorbicular, 3.5 × 2.5 –3 mm, puberulous on both surfaces. Fruit globose, 15 –16 mm in diam.; fruiting pedicels 6 –7 mm, puberulous.

Locality: Ma On Shan (Mau Ping Village), Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 8547; Y. S. Lau 1486.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Flowering: Dec.; fruiting: Aug. of the following year.

Neolitsea levinei Merr. 大葉新木薑子
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 13: 138. 1918; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 423. 1938; FRPS 31: 359. 1982
Neolitsea lanuginosa Gamble var. chinensis Gamble, Sarg. Pl. Wils. 2: 79. 1914.

Tree, up to 22 m tall. Branchlets terete, densely tawny pubescent when young, glabrate in age. Buds scales rusty puberulous abaxially. Leaves 4–5 whorled; leaf blade leathery, oblong-lanceolate to oblong-oblanceolate or elliptic, 15–30 × 4.5–9 cm, base acute, apex shortly acute, adaxially dark green and shining, glabrous, abaxially glaucous, initially densely tawny villose, glabrate in age; triplinerved, lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Umbels 5-flowered, clustered. Pedicels 3 mm, densely tawny pubescent. Perianth-lobes 4, ovate, sparsely pubescent abaxially, margin ciliate. Fruit ellipsoid or globose, 12–18 × 8–15 mm, black when mature; fruiting pedicels 7–10 mm, densely pubescent, slightly enlarged at apex.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7554; Y. W. Lam 1232.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Neolitsea ovatifolia Yang & P. H. Huang 卵葉新木薑子
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 44, fig. 5. 1978; FRPS 31: 369, pl. 94: 9 –10. 1982; FGD 6: 49. 2005.
Neolitsea ovatifolia var. puberula Yang & P. H. Huang, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 44. 1978.

Shrub. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves alternate or crowded toward apex of branchlets; petiole 8 –10(–15) mm, slightly flattened, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, ovate, 4–6(–8.5) × 2–2.5(–4) cm, base obtusely rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, glabrous, glaucous abaxially, triplinerved, distinctly foveolate on both surfaces, due to the raised midvein and lateral veins. Umbels 5-flowered, solitary or 3–4 fascicled; peduncles very short or obsolete; pedicels sericeous-pubescent. Perianth-segments 4, elliptic. Male flowers: fertile stamens 6; filaments glabrous; pistillodes glabrous. Fruit globose or subglobose, ca 1 cm in diam., glabrous; fruiting pedicels 5–8 mm, very stout, glabrous.

Locality: Lantau Peak. S. C. Ng 3226, 3228.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Neolitsea phanerophlebia Merr. 顯脈新木薑子
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 305. 1929; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 430. 1938; FRPS 31: 360. 1982

Small tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets, bud scales and petioles, densely rusty puberulous. Leaves in false whorls or scattered; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade papery or thin-leathery, oblong to oblong-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate to ovate, 6 –13 × 2– 4.5 cm, base acute or obtuse, apex acuminate, adaxially pale greenish, ± shining, glabrous except puberulous on veins when young, abaxially glaucous, densely appressed-pubescent and villous; triplinerved, lateral veins 3 –4 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Umbels sessile, 5 – 6-flowered, 2– 4 clustered in axils of leaves or leaf scars. Bracts 4, appressed-puberulous abaxially. Pedicels 2–3 mm, densely rusty pubescent. Perianth-lobes 4, ovate or orbicular, 3 × 2 mm, margin ciliate, pubescent at the base of adaxial surface. Fruit subglobose, 5 –9 mm in diam., glabrous, purplish black when mature; fruiting pedicels 5–7 mm, appressed-pubescent.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. L. T. Lo 473, 592.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests in valleys. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.

Neolitsea pulchella (Meisn.) Merr. 美麗新木薑子
Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 13: 137. 1918; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 427. 1938; FHN 1: 297. 1964; FRPS 31: 361. 1982
Litsea pulchella Meisn. in DC. Prodr. 15(1): 224. 1864; FKH 225. 1912.
Litsea ceylanca auct. non Nees: Benth., FHK 294. 1861.

Small tree, 6–8 m tall. Branchlets slender, initially brown pubescent; bud scales densely brown puberulous. Leaves alternate or crowded towards apex of branchlets in false whorls; petioles 6–8 mm, initially brown pubescent; leaf blade leathery, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 4–6 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate, adaxially dark green and shining, glabrous except for the pubescent midvein when young, adaxially glaucous, grey villous when young, glabrescent in age, triplinerved, lateral veins 2–3 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Umbels 4–5-flowered, solitary or 2–3 clustered in axils of leaves. Pedicels ca. 2 mm, densely villous. Perianth-lobes 4, elliptic, 2.5 × 1.5 mm, abaxially villous on midvein. Fruits globose, 4–6 mm in diam., on a discoid cupule; fruiting pedicels slender, 5–6 mm, slightly thickened at apex.

Locality: Aberdeen, Pok To Yan. Y. S. Lau 46; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35879).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Mixed forests. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep. of the following year.

Nepenthes mirabilis (Lour.) Druce 豬籠草
Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles Rept. 4: 637. 1916; FHN 1: 329, fig. 164. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 12, pl. 5. 1984; FGD 2: 46, fig. 32. 1991; FOC 8: 198. 2001.
Phyllamphora mirabilis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 606. 1790.
Nepenthes phyllamphora Willd., Sp. Pl. 4(2): 874. 1806, nom. illeg.; FKH 219. 1912.

Erect or climbing herb, 0.5 –2 m tall; young parts densely tomentose, later glabrescent. Basal leaves forming dense rosette, subsessile; leaf blade lanceolate, ca. 10 cm, base semi-amplexicaul, margin usually denticulate; tendril shorter than blade; pitcher variable in size, narrowly ovoid to terete, 2– 6 cm long, 0.6 –2 cm in diam., pilose and stellate hairy, 2-winged, 2–8-spurred between lid and mouth; lid ovate or rounded, densely glandular inside. Cauline leaves petiolate; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate, 10–25 × 4–8 cm, base decurrent, entire or ciliate-denticulate, with purplish red dots on both surfaces; tendril nearly as long as blade, with or without pitcher; pitcher subcylindrical, slightly enlarged at base, 8–16 cm long, 2–5 cm in diam., often with purplish red dots, pilose and stellate hairy, 2-winged, inner wall smooth on distal half and densely glandular on proximal half; mouth narrowed or not, with 1–2 spurs on the place bearing lid; lid ovate to oblong, densely glandular inside. Raceme 20–50 cm, villous, opposite to leaves or terminal; pedicels 0.5–1.5 cm. Flower red or purple. Male flowers: tepals 4, elliptic or oblong, 5 –7 mm, densely glandular adaxially, villous abaxially; stamens in 1 whorl, slightly contorted, filament column slightly shorter than tepals. Female flowers: tepals ca. 0.5 cm; ovary ellipsoid, shortly stipitate or subsessile, densely pale yellow-pubescent or stellate hairy. Capsule with persistent perianth at base, dehiscing into 4 valves when mature; valves lanceolate, 1.5 –3 × 0.3 –0.5 cm, brown, shiny. Seeds filiform, ca. 1.2 cm.

Locality: Tai Lam Chung, So Kwun Wat, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 915; P. S. Choi 35; Y. S. Lau 3045.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Swamps and marshes. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, carnivorous plant.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Nephelaphyllum tenuiflorum Blume 雲葉蘭
Bijdr. 8: 373. 1825; FRPS 18: 232, pl. 39: 7–12. 1999; FGD 7: 408, fig. 209. 2006; FOC 25: 281. 2009.
Nephelaphyllum cristatum Rolfe, Kew Bull. 194. 1896; J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 19. 1903; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 27: 442. 1974, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 64, fig. 31. 1977.

Terrestrial creeping herb; rhizomes fleshy, 2–5 mm in diam., with 1 cm long membranous sheaths; pseudobulbs petiole-like, fleshy, 1–2 cm long, 1–2 mm thick, unifoliate. Leaves ovatecordate, slightly fleshy, 2–5 × 1–4 cm, base cordate, apex acute. Flowers non-resupinate; sepals and petals alike in colour, shiny light green, striped purplish red; sepals obovate-lanceolate, apex acuminate, 1 × 0.3 cm, lateral ones being narrower; petals spathulate, same length with sepals but being wider, apex acute; lip nearly elliptic, slightly notched, 1 × 0.5–0.7 cm, inobviously 3-lobed; lateral lobes growing downwards, midlobe curving upwards, apex slightly notched, margin crispate; column flat, veined along the sides; anther cornute, rectangular; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, oblong, compressed; ovary obconical, green tinged purplish red.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1891; Y. W. Lam 235, 1648.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong. Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of N. cristatum (C. Ford 48, 254, K) was collected by C. Ford from Victoria Peak before 1884. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Nerium oleander L. 夾竹桃
Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753; FGD 1: 460, fig. 515. 1987; FRPS 63: 149. 1977; FOC 16: 173. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 79. 1999.
Nerium indicum Mill., Gard. Dict. ed. 8, n. 2. 1786; FRPS 63: 147, pl. 49. 1977.
Nerium odorum Sol., Hort. Kew 1: 297. 1789.

Evergreen shrubs, to 6 m tall. Leaves very narrowly elliptic, 5–21 × 1–3.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate or decurrent on the petiole, apex acuminate or acute. Flowers showy, fragrant. Sepals narrowly triangular to narrowly ovate, 3–10 mm. Corolla purplish red, pink, white, salmon, or yellow, tube 1.2 – 2.2 cm; lobes 1.3 – 3 cm, single or double. Follicles cylindric, 12 – 23 cm. Seeds oblong, coma 0.9 – 1.2 cm.

Locality : Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1436; L. T. Lo 201; HK sheet 34938.
Distribution: Native to S Europe, N Africa and SW Asia; widely cultivated in tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Nervilia fordii (Hance) Schltr. 毛唇芋蘭（毛葉芋蘭）
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 45(3): 403. 1911; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 38, fig. 12. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 104. 2002; FRPS 18: 25, pl. 4: 4–5.1999; FOC 25: 200. 2009.
Pogonia fordii Hance, J. Bot. 23(272): 247. 1885; FKH 268. 1912.
Pogonia pulchella auct. non Hook. f.: FKH 268. 1912.

Terrestrial herb without aerial stem except the scape; rhizome delicate, terminated by a globose corm 1.5–2 cm in diam. Leaves lying flat on ground, solitary, cordate, 5–9 cm in diam., green above, purple-green beneath. Flowers rose-pink, two terminal to a purplepink scape of 12–15 cm, emerged from the corm before growth of leaf; pedicels 6 mm; sepals greenish pink, oblanceolate, the odd one 2–2.5 × 0.6 cm, apex truncate, cuspidate; lateral sepals narrower; petals linear-lanceolate, 2.4 × 0.3 cm, acute and cuspidate; lip 2.5 cm, embracing the column, slightly gibbous at base, apical one-third rose-pink, apex retuse and notched; column 7 × 2.5 mm, dumb-bellshaped; anther 2-celled, white; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, glandular; ovary 3–4 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Clear Water Bay. S. Y. Hu 13686 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 530; S. C. Tse 427.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Thailand, Vietnam, India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Nervilia plicata (Andr.) Schltr. previously (Check List HK Plants 379. 2002; 132. 2004).

Neuwiedia singapureana (Baker) Rolfe 三蕊蘭
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1907: 412. 1907; FRPS 17: 15. 1999; FOC 25: 21. 2009.
Tupistra singapureana Baker, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 14: 581. 1874.
Neuwiedia veratrifolia auct. non Blume: S. Y. Hu, Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 107. 2004.

Perennial rhizomatous erect herb 40–50 cm tall. Leaves 4–5, elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 13–25 × 3.5–6.5 cm, base acute, apex acuminate; petioles 6–10 cm. Inflorescence racemose, 8–9 cm. Flowers white, fragrant; scapes bracteate; bracts 3–4 × 1.5–2 cm, hispid; perianth erect, 1.5 cm, connate at base forming a slender (about 4 mm) tube; anthers white, 5 mm; ovary inferior, ellipsoidal, 5 × 3 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Peak. H. W. Mak ex N. H. Li 191 (CUHK); HK sheet 36122, 35377.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

Neyraudia reynaudiana (Kunth) Keng ex Hitchc. 類蘆（石珍茅）
Amer. J. Bot. 21(3): 131. 1934; FHN 4: 369, fig. 1176. 1977; FTW 5: 386. 1978; FFJ 6: 131. 1995; FRPS 9(2): 23, pl. 4: 5, 5a. 2002; FOC 22: 460. 2006; FGD 9: 340, fig. 160. 2009.
Arundo reynaudiana Kunth, Révis. Gramin. 1: 275. 1830.
Neyraudia arundinacea auct. non (L.) Henr.: FTW ed. 2, 5: 329. 2000.
Neyraudia madagascariensis auct. non (Kunth) Hook. f.: FKH 328. 1912.

Perennial herb, 1–3 m tall, with short, woody rhizomes. Culms reed-like, erect, 3–10 mm in diam., usually fasciculately branched, many-noded, internodes somewhat glaucous, nodes purple. Leaf blades flat or involute, 20–70 × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose, apex long acuminate; ligule 1–2 mm, truncate, shortly ciliate on dorsal side; leaf sheaths pilose at mouth. Panicle 30 – 70 cm, branches slender, ± nodding; pedicels 1–4 mm. Spikelets 5–9 mm, 4–10-flowered, the lowest floret sterile, resembling glumes but somewhat longer; glumes membranous, lanceolate, golden-brown or purplish, glabrous, subequal, 1.5–3 mm, apex acute; lemmas purplish, ca. 4 mm, lateral veins ciliate with white, soft, ca. 2 mm hairs, awn recurved, 1–2 mm; palea membranous, ca. 3 mm, 2– keeled, apex slightly cleft, minutely ciliate along keels.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3180; HK sheet 32294, 35659.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, hillslopes, rocky places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control).

Nicandra physalodes (L.) Gaertn. 假酸漿
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 237. 1791; FRPS 67(1): 6. 1978; FOC 17: 301. 1994.
Atropa physalodes L., Sp. Pl. 1: 181. 1753.

Annual herbs, up to 1 m tall; stems erect, angular, glabrescent or sparsely pubescent. Leaves alternate; petiole 1.5–6 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 4–12(–20) × 2–8(–13) cm, apex acute or shortly acuminate, base cuneate, margin coarsely sinuate‑dentate or lobed, papery, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, axillary or in branch forks. Pedicel 1.5–4 cm. Calyx 0.8–3 cm, deeply 5‑parted; lobes broadly ovate, apex acute, base cordate‑sagittate, with 2 acute auricles. Corolla pale blue, blue‑purple, or bluish with white center, 2.5–4 cm in diam. Berry brown or yellow, 1–2 cm in diam. Seeds pale brown, 1–1.2 mm in diam.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2995.
Distribution: Naturalized in Gansu, Guizhou, Hebei, Sichuan, Xinjiang, Xizang, Yunnan; a widely distributed weed, native to Peru.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Nicotiana tabacum L. 煙草
Sp. Pl. 180. 1753; FHN 3: 471. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 152, pl. 39. 1978; FGD 2: 389, fig. 267: 1–2. 1991; FOC 17: 332. 1994.

Annual herbs, 0.5–2 m tall, viscid‑pubescent throughout. Leaves alternate, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, lanceolate to oblong‑ovate, 10–30(–70) × 8–15(–30) cm, base attenuate, auriculate or semi‑amplexicaul, apex acuminate, margin entire or slightly sinuate. Panicles terminal, many‑flowered; pedicels 5 – 20 mm. Calyx tubular or tubular‑campanulate, 5‑lobed; lobes triangular‑lanceolate. Corolla funnelform, pink; tube 4 – 6.5 cm; limb 1.5–2 cm in diam., 5‑lobed. Stamens 5; filaments pubescent at base. Ovary 2‑locular; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule ovoid, ca. 1.5 cm, many‑seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 129; Y. S. Lau 2107, 2552.
Distribution: Native to S America; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Tobacco (source of nicotine).

Nymphaea lotus L. var. pubescens (Willd.) Hook. f. & Thom. 柔毛齒葉睡蓮
Fl. Brit. India 1: 114. 1872; FOC 6: 117. 2001.
Nymphaea pubescens Willd., Sp. Pl. 2: 1154. 1799.

Aquatic herb. Rhizomes erect, producing slender stolons. Leaves papery, suborbicular, 20 –40(–65) cm in diam., base deeply cordate, basal lobes subparallel or slightly spreading, margin with acute to subspinose teeth, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent on the strongly raised veins. Flowers emergent, usually 15 –25 cm in diam.; sepals 4, abaxial surface green to purplish, conspicuously veined, adaxial surface white or red, oblong, 10–11 × 3 – 4 cm; petals 20–25, white or red, oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, 7–10 × 1.5 –3.5 cm decaying after anthesis; stamens numerous, shorter than the petals; filaments dilated at base; anther connectives apically unappendaged; ovary crowned by 15 –20 radiating furrowed stigmas. Fruit ovoid to subglobose, 3.5 –5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 1324.
Distribution: S & SE Asia. Cultivated elsewhere in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds. Flowering: Jun.–Dec. Flowers open from late evening till next noon.
Uses: Ornamental.

Nymphaea nouchali N. L. Burm. 延藥睡蓮
Fl. Ind. 120. 1768; FOC 6: 118. 2001.

Aquatic herb. Rhizomes erect, unbranched. Leaves papery, suborbicular, (15 –)20 – 40(–50) cm in diam., base deeply cordate, basal lobes parallel or slightly overlapping, margin subentire or with irregular and broadly triangular teeth, glabrous, secondary nerves raised abaxially, reticulation inconspicuous. Flowers emergent, usually 8–15 cm in diam.; sepals 4, leathery, broadly lanceolate, 6–10 × 3 –3.8 cm, abaxial surface green and shining, adaxial surface blue-violet, persistent; petals 20–25(–30), blue-violet, broadly lanceolate, 6 –9 × 2–3.8 cm; stamens numerous, shorter than the petals; filaments dilated at base; anther connectives apically appendaged; ovary crowned by 15 –25 radiating furrowed stigmas. Fruit globose, 1.5 – 4.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 1318.
Distribution: E & W Asia, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Australia. Cultivated elsewhere in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds. Flowering: Jun.–Dec. Flowers open in the morning till evening.
Uses: Ornamental.

Nymphoides cristatum (Roxb.) Kuntze 水皮蓮
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 429. 1891; FRPS 62: 417. 1988; FFJ 4: 407. 1989; FOC 16: 141. 1995; FGD 4: 327. 2000.
Menyanthes cristata Roxb., Pl. Coromandel 2: 3, pl. 105. 1798.
Limnanthemum cristatum (Roxb.) Griseb., Gen. Sp. Gent. 342. 1839[1838]; FKH 175. 1912.
Villarsia cristata (Roxb.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 582. 1825[1824].

Stems unbranched, with a terminal leaf. Petiole 1–3 cm; leaf blade subleathery, ovate‑orbicular to suborbicular, 3 – 10 cm, base cordate, margin entire, abaxially densely glandular, veins inconspicuous. Flowers many, grouped on nodes, 5‑merous. Pedicel slender, 3–4.5 cm. Calyx 3–5.5 mm, lobes ovate‑elliptic to ovate, apex obtuse. Corolla white with a yellow base, 4–8 mm; lobes ovate with a keeled fold from base to apex, apex obtuse. Filaments linear, 1–2 mm; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Ovary sessile. Style short; stigma lobes triangular. Capsules subglobose, 3–5 mm in diam., few seeded. Seeds light brown, globose, 1.3–1.5 mm in diam.; seed coat smooth or scabrous.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling, Yuen Long. W. J. Tutcher 8154, 8390, 9983.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Taiwan; E India.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Nymphoides peltatum (S. G. Gmel.) Kuntze 荇菜
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 429. 1891; FRPS 62: 415, pl. 67: 4 – 6. 1988; FFJ 4: 407, fig. 335. 1989; FOC 16: 141. 1995.
Limnanthemum peltatum S. G. Gmel., Novi Comment. Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 14(1): 527. 1770.
Menyanthes nymphoides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 145. 1753.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Stem unbranched, terete, sometimes rooting from nodes. Leaves alternate at stem base but opposite at apex; petiole 5–10 cm, base amplexicaul; leaf blade subleathery, ovate‑orbicular to orbicular, 1.5–8 × 1.5–8 cm, base cordate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially purple‑brown and densely glandular, veins indistinct. Flowers usually densely clustered at nodes, 5‑merous. Pedicel 3–7 cm. Calyx 7–9 mm, lobes elliptic‑lanceolate to elliptic, apex obtuse. Corolla golden yellow, 2.5–3 cm, rotate, lobed to near base; lobes obovate, margin broadly membranous and irregularly laciniate, apex rounded to emarginate. Filaments sparsely pilose, 1–2 mm; anthers 2–3.5 mm. Ovary 0.7–1.7 cm; style to 1 cm; stigma large, 2‑lobed, suborbicular. Glands golden yellow. Capsules elliptic, 1.7 – 2.5 × 0.8–1.1 cm. Seeds brown, compressed, elliptic, 4–5 mm, densely ciliate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1000.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Hainan, Qinghai, Xizang; Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia, C & SW Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ocimum basilicum L. 羅勒
Sp. Pl. 2: 597. 1753; FKH 206. 1912; FRPS 66: 561. 1977; FOC 17: 296. 1994; FGD 3: 473. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 495, pl. 219. 1998.

Annual herbs, 20–80 cm tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, often tinged red, glabrous or retrorse puberulent when young. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic ovate, 2.5–5 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex subobtuse to acute, margin irregularly dentate or subentire, glabrescent or hairy, glandular abaxially. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming simple or branched racemes of 10–15 cm or more, puberulent or densely pilose; bracts sessile, oblanceolate, 5–8 mm, ciliate, often coloured. Pedicel ca. 3 mm in flower, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit. Calyx campanulate, ca. 4 mm in flower, 5–6 mm in fruit, pubescent outside, pilose at throat inside; middle tooth of upper lip suborbicular, concave, apex mucronate; lower lip teeth lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, apex spinescent, ciliate. Corolla purplish or with upper lip white, limb puberulent outside; upper lip wide, ca. 3 × 4.5 mm, 4‑lobed, ± flat; lower lip purple, ca. 6 mm. Stamens free, slightly exserted, upper filaments with a tooth above the base. Nutlets dark brown, ovoid, ca. 2.5 × 1 mm, glandular foveolate.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 2018; HK sheet 25715, 40312.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xinjiang, Jilin, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread throughout the Old World tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages. Flowering: Nearly all year round; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Additive (flavouring), material (essential oils).

Ocimum tenuiflorum L. 聖羅勒
Sp. Pl. 597. 1753.
Ocimum sanctum L., Mant. I. 85. 1767; FRPS 66: 566, pl. 121. 1977; FOC 17: 297. 1994; FGD 3: 474, fig. 296. 1995.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, covered with spreading soft hairs. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic‑oblong or elliptic, 2.5–6 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex obtuse, margin shallowly undulate‑serrate, puberulent and glandular on both surfaces, especially on veins abaxially. Verticillasters 6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes or panicles of 6–10 cm; bracts sessile, cordate, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 mm, apex acute. Pedicel ca. 2.5 mm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm in flower, to 6 mm in fruit, villous; middle tooth of upper lip broadly oblate, abruptly acute; lateral teeth broadly triangular, shorter than lower lip teeth, spinescent; lower lip teeth lanceolate, apex spinescent. Corolla white to reddish, ca. 3 mm, slightly exserted, sparsely puberulent; upper lip less than 1 × 2.5 mm, lobes ovate; lower lip oblong, ca. 1 × 0.6 mm, flat. Stamens slightly exserted; upper filaments puberulent at base. Nutlets brown, ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.7 mm, glandular foveolate.

Locality: Luk Keng. Y. S. Lau 2875.
Distribution: Hainan, Sichuan, Taiwan; pantropical.
Ecology: Dry grassy fields. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Additive (flavouring, leaves used as a condiment in salads and other foods).
records.uses: Additive (flavouring, leaves used as a condiment in salads and other foods).

records.text:
Odontonema tubiforme (Bertol.) Kuntze 紅樓花
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 494. 1891, “tubaeforme”.
Justicia tubaeformis Bertol., Novi Comment. Acad. Sci. Inst. Bononiensis 4: 405. 1840.
Thyrsacanthus tubaeformis (Bertol.) Nees, Prodr. 11: 324. 1847.
Odontonema strictum (Nees) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 494. 1891; Check List HK Plants 254. 2002; 87. 2004.
Thyrsacanthus strictus Nees, Prodr. 11: 324. 1847.

Shrubs, to 3 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, sparsely pubescent. Petioles 0.5–3 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades ovate, elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, 7–22 × 3–10 cm, base cuneate, attenuate, slightly decurrent onto the petiole, apex acuminate to falcate, margin entire, subglabrous on both surfaces or sparsely pubescent abaxially, cystoliths conspicuous adaxially, lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Racemes 6–15 cm, sometimes branched basally and forming a panicle, 1–3 flowers on each node; peduncle 6–9 cm; rachis quadrangular, subglabrous to pubescent usually concentrated in 2 or more lines. Pedicels 2–6 mm, pubescent. Bracts lanceolate to linear‑subulate, 2–4 × ca. 1 mm, abaxially puberulent or glabrous; bracteoles subulate, 2–4 × ca. 1 mm, abaxially puberulent or glabrous. Calyx 2–4 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes subulate, 1–3 × 0.5–1 mm, abaxially puberulent or glabrous. Corolla red, 2.4–3.3 cm, outside glabrous; tube slender, 2.0 – 2.7 cm, limb 2‑lipped, upper lip 4 – 5 mm, 2‑lobed, lobes orbicular, 2–3 × ca. 1.5 mm, lower lip 4–5 mm, 3‑lobed, lobes elliptic to suborbicular, 3–4 × 2–3 mm. Stamens 2; stamens of thrum flower 1.2–1.5 cm, those of pin flower 6–8 mm; anthers oblong, 2–3 mm. Ovary glabrous; styles of thrum flower to 1 cm, styles of pin flower 1–1.6 cm, pubescent, stigma 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 0.3 mm. Capsules 1.7–2.3 cm, glabrous, basal stalks 0.7–1.1 cm. Seed suborbicular, subelliptic to broadly obovate, 4–5 mm, ca. 3 mm wide, bumpy to tuberculate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2638, 2660; Y. W. Lam 1121.
Distribution: Native to C America, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Oenanthe benghalensis (Roxb.) Benth. & Hook. f. 短幅水芹（少花水芹）
Gen. Pl. 1: 906. 1867; FKH 117. 1912; FRPS 55(2): 200. 1985; FGD 2: 338. 1991; FOC 14: 131. 2005.
Seseli benghalensis Roxb., [Hort. Bengal. 22. 1814, nom. nud.] Fl. Ind. ed. 2, 2: 94. 1832.
Oenanthe benghalensis (Roxb.) Kurz., J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal. 2: 115. 1877.
Dasyloma benghalensis (Roxb.) DC., Prodr. 4: 140. 1830.

Perennial herb, 15–60 cm tall; root fibrous; stems usually erect, angular, branched from base. Basal petioles 1–4 cm; leaf blades triangular-ovate in outline, 1–2-pinnate; ultimate segments rhombic-ovate, rarely lanceolate, 5–20 × 1–5 mm. Upper stem leaves smaller, sessile, 1-pinnate, pinnae rhombic-ovate or lanceolate. Umbels 0.5–3.5 cm across; peduncles short, 0.5–1(–2) cm, often leaf-opposed, or obsolete; involucral bracts absent; rays 4–10, 0.5–1 cm; bracteoles numerous, linear, as long as pedicels, umbellules 8–15-flowered; pedicels 0.5–2 mm. Calyx-teeth ca. 0.4 mm. Petals white. Styles 1.4–1.8 mm. Fruit ovoid, 2.5–3 × 1.5–2 mm; dorsal and intermediate ribs slightly corky-thickened.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Luk Keng. Y. S. Lau 2876; HK sheet 2045.
Distribution: Sichuan, Yunnan, Guangdong; Japan, India.
Ecology: Forests by streams. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–May. Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Most authors merged the species into O. javanica (Blume) DC., whereas Chinese authors treated it as a distinct species. Wu pointed that it might be a subspecies of O. javanica.
