Notes: Most authors merged the species into O. javanica (Blume) DC., whereas Chinese authors treated it as a distinct species. Wu pointed that it might be a subspecies of O. javanica.

records.text:
Oenanthe javanica (Blume) DC. 水芹
Prodr. 4: 138. 1830; FRPS 55(2): 202, pl. 81: 1 – 4. 1985; FGD 2: 338, fig. 226. 1991; FOC 14: 131. 2005.
Sium javanicum Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Nederl. Ind. 15: 881. 1826.
Dasyloma javanica (Blume) Miq., Fl. Ind. Bat. 1(1): 741. 1856.
Falcaria javanica (Blume) DC., Prodr. 4: 110. 1830.
Oenanthe stolonifera (Roxb.) DC., Prodr. 4: 138. 1830; FKH 117. 1912.

Perennial herb, 10–80 cm tall, with fibrous roots; stems erect or decumbent at base, striate, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves basal and alternate on stems, blade oblong to ovate in outline, pinnate to tripinnate; ultimate segments ovate, or rhombic-ovate, 1–4 × 1–2 cm, margin irregularly serrate or sometimes lobed; petioles 2–10 cm, sheathing. Umbels compound; involucre lacking, or of a few linear bracts; rays 5–15, 0.5–3 cm; bracteoles 2–8, linear. Pedicels 1.5–4 mm. Calyx-teeth ca. 0.5 mm. Petals white, ca. 1 mm. Style 1.5–2 mm, persistent. Fruit glabrous, oblong, ca. 2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, the commissure broad, the ribs more or less corky-thickened.

Locality: Tai Tam, Wong Nai Chung, Ng Tung Chai, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 2705; N. H. Li 55; P. S. Choi 130.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia and Australia.
Ecology: Borders of rice fields, ditches and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Oenothera drummondii Hook. 海濱月見草
Bot. Mag. 61: t. 3361. 1834; FRPS 53(2): 67. 2000; FGD 8: 5. 2007.
Oenothera littoralis Schltdl., Linnaea 12: 268. 1838; FFJ 4: 138. 1989.

Annual to perennial herb, erect to procumbent, 10–50 cm tall. Stems simple or branched, densely strigillose. Leaves variable in shape, linear-lanceolate to long elliptic-oblanceolate, 2–5 × 0.5–1 cm, base cuneate, apex rotund, margin entire or shallowly dentate, rarely lyrate, densely strigillose, sometimes also glandular puberulent, veins inconspicuous. Inflorescence a lax, open spike. Flowers large and showy. Calyx-tube 2.5–6 cm, upcurved in bud; lobes lanceolate, 1.3–3.3 cm, hairy abaxially. Petals yellow, 2–4.5 cm. Anthers 4–12 mm. Ovary densely strigillose to villous, sometimes also glandular puberulent; stigma exserted above anthers. Capsules cylindrical, 2.5–5.5 cm, sessile. Seeds in two rows per locule, ellipsoidal to suborbicular, 1.1–1.7 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 33, 467; HK sheet 39278.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian; N America, native to coastal areas of SE United States and NE Mexico, naturalized in Africa, SW Asia, Australia, Europe, and S America.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering; Jul.–Nov.; fruiting: May– Dec.

Olea tsoongii (Merr.) P. S. Green 異株木犀欖
Kew Bull. 50(2): 338. 1995; FOC 15: 297. 1996; FGD 5: 423. 2003.
Ligustrum tsoongii Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 21: 506. 1922.
Olea brevipes Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3. 343. 1955.
Olea dioica auct. non Roxb.: FRPS 61: 133, pl. 37: 1 – 3. 1992; FFJ 4: 377, fig. 309. 1989; Check List HK Plants 243. 2002; 84. 2004.

Shrubs or trees, 3–20 m tall. Branchlets terete, slightly compressed at nodes, pubescent to glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 3–10 mm, pubescent to finely puberulent; leaf blade oblanceolate or elliptic‑lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or blunt, margin entire or irregularly serrate; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, obscure or slightly raised on both surfaces. Flowers polygamodioecious, usually in subumbellate groups and rearranged in axillary panicles. Corolla white or yellowish; lobes subrotund, apex cucullate. Staminate flowers: pedicels 1–5 mm, slender; calyx 1–1.5 mm; corolla 2–3.5(–4.5) mm, lobes deltate. Bisexual flowers: pedicels 0–2 mm, stout; calyx 1–1.5 mm; corolla 2–4.5 mm, lobes 0.5–1.5 mm; filament short; anthers elliptic, 0.5– 1 mm; ovary elliptic with a sharp tip; stigma capitate. Drupe blue‑black, elliptic or subglobose, 6–13 × 3–9 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Sharp Peak, Sheung Wo Hang. F. W. Xing 6936, 9890; Y. W. Lam 417.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Arundinaria shiuyingiana Chia & But 秀英竹
Kew Bull. 37: 591. 1983; HKB 25. 1985; FGD 9: 299, fig. 142. 2009.
Oligostachyum shiuyingianum (L. C. Chia & But) G. H. Ye & Z. P. Wang, J. Nanjing Univ., Nat. Sci. Ed. 26(3): 486. 1990; FRPS 9(1): 582, pl. 178: 1–3. 1996; FOC 22: 130. 2006.

Culms 4–6 m, 1–2 cm in diam.; internodes grey-green, usually with purple speckles, initially usually white powdery below nodes and sparsely setulose; nodes elevated, supra-nodal ridge more prominent than sheath scar. Culm sheaths yellow-green with purple-green base, brown strigose, margins ciliate; auricles small; oral setae 2–several; ligule truncate, ca. 1 mm, white ciliate; blade erect, brown-green, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, base ca. 1/2 as wide as apex of culm sheath. Leaves 5–9 per flowering branch; sheath with purple speckles, glabrous; auricles not developed; oral setae 2–3; ligule purple, truncate, 0.5 – 1 mm, weakly exserted, hairy; blade 12–20 × 0.8–1.3 cm, both surfaces glabrous, abaxially transverse veins distinct, rectangular. Racemes or small panicles with 2–4 spikelets, partially exserted from leaf sheaths; axis and branches slender, glabrous or branches sparsely hirtellous along angles. Spikelets lanceolate, 3–8 × ca. 0.5 cm; florets 5–15. Glumes 2, 1st smaller, 8–9 mm; lemma purple speckled, 1.7–2 cm, deciduously pubescent, apex with mucro 2–3 mm; palea 1.2–1.4 cm, pubescent, keels sparsely ciliolate, apex obtuse, thickly hairy; lodicules 3. Stamens 3. Style 1; stigmas 3.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 3163; Nan-Zhu 2809; F. W. Xing 9874.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Partially shaded slopes of hills, alt. below 100 m.
Uses: Environmental.
Notes: The type specimen (Nan-Zhu 2862, IBSC) was collected from Eagle's Nest on 21 June 1981. It was named in honour of Prof. Shiu- ying Hu. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Operculina turpethum (L.) Silva Manso 盒果藤
Enum. Subst. Bras. 16. 1836; FHN 3: 484, fig. 873. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 80. 1979; FOC 16: 300. 1995; FGD 4: 344, fig. 205. 2000.
Convolvulus turpethum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 155. 1753.
Ipomoea turpethum (L.) R. Br., Prodr. 485. 1810; FKH 180. 1912.
Merremia turpethum (L.) Rendle, Fl. Trop. Afr. 4: 102. 1905.
Spiranthera turpethum (L.) Bojer, Hortus Maurit. 226. 1837.

Perennial herbaceous vine, to 4 m. Stems reddish, narrowly 3–5‑winged, ± angular, sparsely pilose or glabrous. Petiole 2–10 cm, often winged; leaf blade papery, broadly ovate to ovate‑oblong, 5–17 × 3.5–14 cm, base cordate, truncate or obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, mucronulate, margin entire or undulate, adaxially appressed pilose to glabrous, abaxially pubescent. Cymes often 2‑flowered. Peduncles 3 – 5 cm or longer. Bracts 2, oblong to ovate‑oblong, 1–2.5 cm, concave, pubescent. Pedicel 1.5–2 cm, striate‑angular, clavate, to 4 cm in fruit, pubescent. Sepals ovate to broadly ovate, unequal; outer 2 sepals 1.5–2 cm, abaxially pubescent; inner 3 shorter, subglabrous. Corolla white, broadly funnelform, ca. 4.5 cm, glabrous; limb 5‑lobed. Filaments pubescent at base. Fruit enclosed in cupular calyx, compressed globose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam. Seeds dull black, ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 6 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Fung Yuen, Luk Keng, Ping Chau. L. T. Lo 249; Y. S. Lau 2874; Y. W. Lam 1139.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical E Africa, Mascarene Islands, Seychelles, tropical Asia, tropical Australia, Polynesia, Antilles.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ophiopogon japonicus (L. f.) Ker Gawl. 麥冬（沿階草）
Bot. Mag. 27: pl. 1063. 1807; FKH 274. 1912; FRPS 15: 163, pl. 55: 3–5. 1978; FOC 24: 261. 2000; FGD 6: 361, fig. 214. 2005.
Convallaria japonica L. f., Suppl. Pl. 204. 1782.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Roots cord-like, usually with tuberous part near middle or tip; tubers fusiform, 1–2 × 0.5–1 cm, fleshy. Leaves radical, tufted, sessile, grass-like, generally 15–45 cm × 1.5–3 mm, 3–7-veined, margin serrulate. Scape 6 – 15( – 27) cm, much shorter than leaves. Inflorescence a raceme or reduced panicle, 2–5 cm, several- to more than 10-flowered; bracts lanceolate, basal one 7–8 mm. Flowers solitary or paired, usually nodding; pedicels 3–4 mm, articulate near middle. Perianth segments 6, white or purplish, lanceolate, ca. 5 × 2 mm. Stamens 6; filaments very short; anthers ca. 3 mm. Ovary semi-inferior, style somewhat narrowly conical, ca. 4 mm, narrowed gradually upward from the widened base. Seeds globose, 7–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 7202.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Forests, moist and shady places in ravines. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Ophiopogon reversus C. C. Huang 高節沿階草（廣東沿階草）
FHN 4: 534. 1977; FRPS 15: 160. 1978; FOC 24: 260. 2000; FGD 6: 362. 2005.

Perennial herb, without creeping stolons and tuberous roots. Leaves radical, tufted, sessile, long linear, 18–50 cm × 3–8 mm, (5–)7–9-veined, base attenuate, without membranous sheath, margin subentire or serrulate distally. Scape 18–25 cm, slightly flattened and ridged. Inflorescence a raceme or reduced panicle, 5–7 cm, many-flowered; bracts deltoid to ovate, basal one to 2 cm. Flowers in clusters of 2–3 or solitary; pedicels curved, 5–10 mm, articulate above middle. Perianth purple, or white tinged with purple; segments 6, oblong-ovate, ca. 5 × 2 mm, 1-veined. Stamens 6; filaments short; anthers oblong. Style 5–6 mm, slender. Seeds ellipsoidal or globose, purple-blue at maturity.

Locality: Mount Violet, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po. G. Barretto 275; HK sheet 36143.
Distribution: Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Moist places in forests. Flowering: Sep.–Oct.; fruiting: Dec.–Mar. of the following year.

Ophiorrhiza cantoniensis Hance 廣州蛇根草
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 222. 1862; FKH 129. 1912; Ferguson, Not. Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 32(1): 111. 1972; FRPS 71(1): 165. 1999; FGD 6: 143. 2005.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 30–50 cm tall. Stems prostrate at base, rooting at nodes, upper part erect; young branches and inflorescence puberulent. Leaves papery; petioles 1.5–4 cm; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade usually oblong‑elliptic, or sometimes ovate‑oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 5–13 × 2–5.5 cm, base cuneate, rarely subrounded, apex acuminate or abruptly acuminate, glabrous, or sometimes sparsely strigillose adaxially or on both surfaces. Flowers heterostylic, in loose, many‑flowered, terminal cymes or panicles; peduncles 2–7 cm, covered with rusty or reddish hairs. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 1.3–1.5 mm, with 5 ribs; calyx‑teeth small, triangular. Corolla white or slightly pink, glabrescent or sometimes puberulent abaxially; tube 1–1.2(–1.5) cm, with a ring of white long hairs inside the slightly dilated throat; lobes 5, triangular, 3–5 mm. Capsule 3–4 mm high and 7–9 mm broad subglabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2438; Y. S. Lau 609, 1373.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan.
Ecology: Forests of valleys and by streams. Flowering: Winter to spring; fruiting: Apr.–May.

Ophiorrhiza japonica Blume 日本蛇根草
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 978. 1826; FKH 129. 1912; Ferguson, Not. Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 32(1): 112. 1972; FTW ed. 2, 4: 308, pl. 140. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 163. 1999; FGD 6: 142. 2005.
Ophiorrhiza eryei Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 170. 1852; FHK 147. 1861.

Perennial herbs, 20–50 cm tall. Stems ascending, rooting at the base, with 2 lines of hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2(–3) cm, glabrous or pubescent; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade ovate, elliptic‑ovate or lanceolate, 4–8(– 10) × 1–3 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, glabrous, or sometimes sparsely strigillose adaxially and pubescent on veins abaxially, with a red tint in drying. Flowers heterostylic, 5 – 10, or rarely more, in loose terminal cymes; peduncles usually 1–2 cm, ± puberulous. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.3 mm; calyx‑teeth small, triangular. Corolla white or pink, glabrous abaxially; tube 1–1.3 cm, dilated in the upper half, pubescent inside; lobes 5, triangular, 2.5–3 mm. Capsule 3–4 mm high and 7–9 mm broad subglabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 4; HK sheet 38519, 39999.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Feb.–May.

Ophiorrhiza pumila Champ. ex Benth. 短小蛇根草
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 169. 1852; FHK 147. 1861; FKH 129. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 311. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 171. 1999; FGD 6: 144. 2005.

Small herbs, 10–25 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, rooting at the base, ± pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5 – 1.5 cm, pubescent; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade ovate, lanceolate, elliptic or oblong, 2–5.5(–9) × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, ± decurrent, apex obtuse or subrounded, glabrescent or sparsely strigillose adaxially, puberulent abaxially. Flowers homostylic, crowded in small terminal cymes; peduncles ca. 1 cm, puberulous. Calyx small, shortly and densely pubescent; tube turbinate or subglobular, ca. 1.2 mm, with 5 ribs; calyx‑teeth small, triangular. Corolla white, ca. 5 mm, puberulent abaxially; tube slightly dilated at the base, with a ring of white long hairs inside throat; lobes 5, triangular, 1.2–1.5 mm. Capsule 2–2.5 mm high and 6–7 mm broad, shortly strigose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mum, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 608; P. S. Choi 493; Y. W. Lam 1546.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Wet and shaded places in forests and by streams. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Oplismenus compositus (L.) P. Beauv. 竹葉草
Ess. Agrostogr. 54. 1812; FKH 316. 1912; FHN 4: 416. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 245, pl. 75: 1–3. 1990; FFJ 6: 211, fig. 179. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 482, pl. 201. 2000; FOC 22: 502. 2006.
Panicum compositum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 57. 1753; FHK 411. 1861; FGD 9: 416, fig. 215. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms stoloniferous, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, upper part ascending, 20–80 cm. Leaf sheaths shorter or the upper longer than internode, glabrous, pilose or tuberculatehairy; leaf blades lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 3–20 × 0.5–3 cm, subglabrous to tuberculate-hairy, base ± embraced stem and usually asymmetrical oblique. Inflorescence axis 5–15(–25) cm, glabrous to tuberculate-hairy; racemes 3–6, alternating, ascending to erect. Spikelets lanceolate, glabrous to thinly pilose; glumes herbaceous, subequal, ca. 1/2–2/3 length of spikelet, margins usually ciliate; lower glume awn 5–10 mm; upper glume awn to 1–2 mm or occasionally absent; lower floret neuter, lemma papery, 7–9-veined, acute or with a stout mucro, palea membranous, narrow or absent; upper lemma coriaceous, smooth, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1031; HK sheet 42019, 42066.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Australia, extending westward through India to E Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Opuntia stricta (Haw.) Haw. var. dillenii (Ker-Gaw.) L. D. Benson 仙人掌
Cact. et Succ. J. (Los Angeles) 41: 126. 1968; FRPS 52(1): 277. 1999.
Cactus dillenii Ker-Gaw., in Edwards, Bot. Reg. 3: pl. 255. 1818.
Opuntia dillenii (Ker-Gaw.) Haw., Suppl. Pl. Succ. 79. 1819; FKH 114. 1912; FGX 1: 735. 1991; FGD 4: 138. 2000.

Shrubby or tree-like cactus, 1– 4 m tall. Trunk almost cylindric, woody at base. Stem-joints flat, green, obovate to oblong, 1–30 × 7–10 cm; areoles raised, with woolly hairs; spines solitary, white, tip dark brown. Leaves small, subulate, caducous. Flowers solitary, yellow, 5– 8 cm in diam. Fruit a berry, obovate, 6 – 8 cm, spineless.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. HK sheet 12291, 2049.
Distribution: Hainan, S Guangdong, S Guangxi; Mexico, S-C USA, S America; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Dry grassy places. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Oreocharis benthamii C. B. Clarke 大葉石上蓮
Monogr. Phan. 5: 63. 1883; FKH 193. 1912; FRPS 69: 165. 1990; FOC 18: 260. 1998; FGD 6: 253. 2005.

Herbs, perennial, 15–25 cm tall. Leaves basal; petioles 2–8 cm, densely light brown woolly; leaf blade elliptic or ovate‑orbicular, 4–20 × 2–8 cm, base slightly cordate, apex obtuse to acute, margin shallowly crenate to entire, adaxially densely pubescent, abaxially densely pubescent to densely woolly and densely brown woolly along veins; lateral veins 6–8 pairs. Cymes 6–10‑flowered; peduncle 5–20 cm, densely pale brown woolly; bracts 2, linear, 5– 10 mm, apex acute, margin entire, densely pubescent; pedicels 0.5–1.5 cm. Calyx campanulate, 5‑sect from base; segments lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apex acute, margin entire, villose. Corolla purple, 0.8–1 cm, outside pubescent to puberulent; tube tubular, gradually ampliate from base to mouth, 8–10 mm; limb slightly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed from middle, abaxial lip 3‑lobed from base, lobe equal, 1–2 mm, nearly rounded. Stamens 4, free, adnate to corolla tube near middle; filaments ca. 7 mm; anthers broadly oblong, ca. 1 mm. Disk ring‑like, entire. Pistil glabrous; ovary linear, ca. 5 mm; style ca. 2 mm; stigma 1, disk‑shaped. Capsule 2 – 3.5 cm, oblong.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 922; L. T. Lo 610; P. S. Choi 410.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Cliffs in ravines and in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.

Oreocnide frutescens (Thunb.) Miq. 紫麻
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 3: 131. 1867; FHN 2: 419. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 386, pl. 84: 3 – 6. 1995; FOC 5: 184. 2003; FGD 6: 85, fig. 33. 2005.
Villebrunea frutescens (Thunb.) Blume., Mus. Bot. Luggd. Bat. 2: 168. 1856; FHK 332. 1861; FKH 250. 1912.
Urtica frutescens Thunb., Fl. Jap. 70. 1784.

Shrub or rarely small tree, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets and petioles purplish brown, strigose or pubescent, rarely grey tomentose. Leaves usually borne on the upper part of branches; stipules linear-lanceolate, ca. 10 mm, apex caudate-acuminate; petioles 1–7 cm; leaf blade ovate to narrowly ovate, rarely obovate, 3–15 × 1.5–6 cm, base rounded, rarely broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, serrate or coarsely dentate above the base, adaxial surface sparsely strigillose, sometimes subglabrous, abaxial surface usually ashy-white-tomentose, later glabrate, or only with short hairs on veins, 3-nerved. Flowers in subsessile clusters on older branches. Male flowers: perianth-segments 3, oblong-ovate, incurved, united at base, hairy on the upper part of outside; stamens 3; rudimentary pistil clavate, ca. 0.6 mm, white-wooly. Female flowers sessile, ca. 1 mm. Achene ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 1.2 mm, surrounded by the fleshy cupular receptacle at base.

Locality: Mount Parker. HK sheet 6596.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, SE Gansu, S Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, N India, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Moist places in ravines, margins of forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.

Oreocnide frutescens subsp. insignis C. J. Chen 細梗紫麻
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 21(4): 475. 1983; FOC 5: 185. 2003; FGD 6: 85. 2005.

It differs from subsp. frutescens mainly by the following characters: female inflorescence distinctly pedunculate; peduncles 5 –13 mm; leaves narrowly obovate to oblong-obovate, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface sparsely pubescent, margin with 13 –21 serratures above middle.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun. S. T. Dunn 7055; Y. S. Lau 1522, 3004.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Ormosia emarginata (Hook. & Arn.) Benth. 凹葉紅豆
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 77. 1852; FHK 96. 1861; FKH 88. 1912; FRPS 40: 34. 1994; FGD 5: 212, fig. 119. 2003.
Layia emarginata Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 183, pl. 38. 1833.

Small tree, 5–6(–12) m tall; glabrous throughout. Leaves odd-pinnate, 10–16 cm; leaflets 3–7, thick leathery, obovate-oblong or elliptic, 3.5–8 × 2–3 cm, base obtuse or broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate; lateral veins 7–8 pairs. Panicles terminal, 10–11 cm. Flowers fragrant. Corolla white or pink; vexillum oblate, 7 × 8 mm; claw 2 mm; wings with long claws, base auriculate; keel irregularly oblong, auriculate at one side. Stamens 10, unequal. Pods rhomboid or oblong, 3–5.5 × 1.7–2.4 cm, compressed. Seeds 1–4, scarlet, suborbicular or elliptic, 7–10 × 7 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 368; Y. S. Lau 1883; HK sheet 40131.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed forests. Flowering: May – Jun.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Ormosia indurata L. Chen 韌莢紅豆
Sarginetia 3: 104. 1943; FRPS 40: 45. 1994; FGD 5: 214. 2003.

Tree, 5 – 9 m tall. Old branches purple-brown or yellowish brown, glabrous, with salient lenticels and leaf scars. Leaves odd-pinnate, 8 – 16 cm; leaflets (5–)7 – 9, leathery, oblanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 2.5–6 × 0.7–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, emarginate, margin slightly revolute, glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent or glabrous abaxially, lateral veins 4 – 6 pairs. Panicles terminal. Corolla white. Ovary densely grey-brown pubescent, 4-ovuled. Pods obovate or oblong, 3 – 4.5 × 2 – 2.5 cm, valves thickly woody. Seeds 1 – 4, red-brown, elliptic, 1 × 0.7 cm, nitid.

Locality: Mount Gough, Aberdeen, Mau Ping, Wu Kau Tang, Shing Mun, Wong Lung Hang. Y. S. Lau 191; P. S. Choi 101; F. W. Xing 8638.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Fruiting: Nov.

Ormosia pachycarpa Champ. ex Benth. 茸莢紅豆
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 76. 1852; FHK 96. 1861; FKH 88. 1912; FRPS 40: 13. 1994; FGD 5: 208. 2003.

Tree, 12–15 m tall; bark greyish green. Young branches, petioles, abaxial surface of leaflets, panicles, calyces and pods thickly covered with whitish cottony wool. Leaves odd-pinnate, 20–25 cm; leaflets 5–9, elliptic-oblanceolate to oblanceolate, 5–15 × 3–7 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute, glabrous adaxially, lateral veins 11–17 pairs. Panicles terminal, 17–30 cm, 5-toothed. Corolla white; petals clawed; vexillum oblate, ca. 1.2 cm wide; wings broadly elliptic, 9 mm, base auriculate; keel 7 mm, base auriculate on one side. Stamens 10, unequal, 6– 10 mm. Ovary sessile, densely villose. Pods obovoid, hard, turgid, densely tomentose. Seeds 1– 2, dark brown, suborbicular or broadly ovoid, 1.5 – 2.4 cm, shining.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Wong Chuk Hang, Bowen Rd., Beacon Hill, Tsiu Hang, Tai Po, Shing Mun, Ta Tit Yan. P. S. Choi 22; HK sheet 40144, 40681.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun. – Jul.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley by J. G. Champion around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Ormosia semicastrata Hance 軟莢紅豆
J. Bot. 20(231): 78. 1882; FKH 88. 1912; FRPS 40: 22. 1994; FGD 5: 210. 2003.

Tree, up to 12 m tall; bark brown or grey. Branchlets sparsely tawny pubescent. Leaves odd-pinnate, 18–25 cm, rachis elongating from the apical pair of leaflets to 1.2–2 cm; leaflets 3–9(–11), ovate-elliptic, narrowly elliptic or lanceolate, 4 –12 × 1–6 cm, base obtuse to rounded or cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, glabrous on both surfaces or pubescent along veins on abaxial surface, lateral veins 10–17 pairs. Panicles axillary, densely yellow-brown pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 4–5 mm, rusty pubescent abaxially, 5-toothed. Corolla white; petals clawed; vexillum suborbicular, 4 mm in diam.; wings linear-oblanceolate, 4.5 × 2 mm; keel oblong, equal to wings. Stamens 10, 5 fertile, 5 abortive. Ovary yellow-brown pubescent. Pods suborbicular, 1.5–2 cm in diam., leathery. Seed 1, scarlet, oblate, 9 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan. C. P. Lau 53; Y. S. Lau 2062; HK sheet 40785.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr. –May.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by C. Ford (Hance Herb. No. 21018) in April 1879.

Oroxylum indicum (L.) Benth. ex Kurz 木蝴蝶（千層紙）
Forest Fl. Burma 2: 237. 1877; FOC 18: 215. 1998.
Bignonia indica L., Sp. Pl. 2: 625. 1753.
Bignonia pentandra Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 379. 1790.
Calosanthes indica (L.) Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 760. 1826.
Oroxylum indicum (L.) Vent., Dec. Gen. Nov. 8. 1808, nom. inval; FKH 196. 1912; FGZ 610. 1956; FHN 3: 533, fig. 911. 1974; FYN 2: 696, pl. 194: 1 – 3. 1979; FRPS 69: 11, pl. 4: 1 – 3. 1990; FFJ 5: 92, fig. 101. 1993; Check List HK Plants 257. 2002; 88. 2004.

Trees 6–10(–15) m tall, 15–20 cm in d.b.h. Bark greyish brown. Leaves 2–3(–4)‑pinnately compound, borne nearly at stem apex, 50–150 cm; petiolules 5–20 cm; leaflets ovate to elliptic, 5–14 × 3–10 cm, base subrounded or cordate, oblique, apex short acuminate, glabrous, becoming blue after drying; lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Inflorescences 40–150 cm. Flowers usually open at night, with foul smell. Pedicel 2–7 cm, bracteolate. Calyx purple, campanulate, 2.2–4.5 × 2–3 cm, glabrous, leathery, becoming subwoody in fruit. Corolla purple‑red; tube fleshy, 4 – 4.5 cm; mouth 5.5 – 8 cm in diam.; upper lip 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes slightly reflexed. Stamens inserted at middle of corolla tube; filaments ca. 4 cm, slightly exserted from corolla tube, tomentose basally. Disk large, fleshy, 5‑lobed, 4–5 mm thick, ca. 1.5 cm in diam. Style 5–7 cm; stigma 2‑parted, ca. 7 mm. Capsule woody, 40–120 × 5–9 cm, ca. 1 cm thick; valves with midrib, margin convex. Seeds orbicular, 6–7 × 3.5 –4 cm including white membranous wing.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen. S. T. Dunn 1173; HK sheet 21143.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Forests near villages. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), environmental.

Oryza sativa L. 稻
Sp. Pl. 1: 333. 1753; FKH 317. 1912; FHN 4: 396. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 323. 2000; FOC 22: 183. 2006; FGD 9: 332. 2009.
Oryza formosana Masam. & Suzuki, Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Formosa 25: 320. 1935.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Culms tufted, erect. Leaf sheaths glabrous; auricles falcate, ciliate; leaf blades cauline, linear, 25–80 × 0.5–3 cm, glabrous, smooth or scabrid on both sides, margins scabrid, apex acuminate; ligule ovate to lanceolate, 10–40 mm, margins decurrent to the sheath; leaf sheaths slightly inflated below, upper sheaths tight, glabrous, auricles falcate, ciliate. Panicle loosely contracted, up to 30 cm, nodding at maturity; branches 1–3 at lowest node, longest 2–12 cm, axils bearded or glabrous. Spikelets flattened, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 6–10 mm; sterile lemmas lanceolate, 1.5–4 mm, apex acuminate; fertile lemma 5-veined, hard, siliceous, hispidulous, apex acuminate, as long as spikelet; palea 3-veined, same texture and length as lemma; awn very variable, slender or stout, up to 60 mm or more, scaberulous, sometimes absent. Anthers 1–3 mm. Caryopsis ovate or elliptic to cylindrical, 5–7 mm, whitish yellow to brown or blackish.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2419; HK sheet 14939, 14943.
Distribution: Cultivated throughout tropical, subtropical, and warm temperate regions.
Ecology: Usually two crops a year in Hong Kong.
Uses: Food (cereal).

Osbeckia chinensis L. 金錦香
Sp. Pl. 345. 1753; FHK 114. 1861; FKH 106. 1912; FRPS 53(1): 140. 1984; S. S. Renner, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 451. 2001.

Erect herb or subshrub, 20 – 60 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, with appressed short stiff hairs. Leaves opposite, very shortly petiolate or subsessile; leaf blade papery, linear, linear-lanceolate, oblong-ovate, elliptic-ovate, or rarely ovate-lanceolate, 2–5(–9) × 0.3–1(–3.2) cm, base obtuse to rounded, or subcordate, apex acute, margin entire, strigose on both surfaces, 3 – 5-basiveined. Inflorescences terminal, capitate, 2 – 10-flowered, with 2 – 6 foliaceous involucral bracts at base. Bracts sessile, ovate or ovate-lanceolate. Calyx-tube usually pink, 6 – 6.5 mm, glabrous or with 1–5 setose tubercles; lobes 4(–5), triangular-lanceolate, margin with 4 accessory ciliate scales inserted between and a little below them on the outside. Petals 4 or 5, pink or purplish, obovate, 1 – 1.5 × 1.3 cm, ciliate. Stamens 8 or 10, turning to one side; filaments as long as anthers; anthers narrowly lanceolate, apex beaked; connective slightly inflated at base. Ovary subglobose, 4 – 5-locular, apex densely setose or strigose. Fruit capsular, purplish red, ovoid-globose, ca. 6 × 4 mm, glabrous or with bristle-like tubercles.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1007, 1304; P. S. Choi 278; W. Y. Chun 6521, 23675 (IBSC); S. C. Chen 11149 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, N Australia.
Ecology: Grassy areas on open slopes, thin forests, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Osmanthus fragrans (Thunb.) Lour. 桂花（木犀）
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 29. 1790; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 373, fig. 305. 1989; FRPS 61: 107, pl. 29: 4 – 6. 1992; FOC 15: 292. 1996; FGD 5: 418. 2003.
Olea fragrans Thunb., Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 57. 1784.
Osmanthus longibrateatus H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 2: 5. 1982.

Trees or shrubs, 3–12(–18) m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Petiole 8–12 mm; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic‑lanceolate, 4– 12 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or usually serrulate on distal half, midvein and lateral veins (6–10 on each side of midvein) impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Cymes fasciculate in leaf axils, 10 – 20‑flowered. Flowers androdioecious; bracts broadly ovate, 2–4 mm; pedicel 4–10 mm, slender. Calyx ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, yellowish, or orange, 3–4 mm, 4‑lobed to near base; lobes 2–3 mm; stamens attached to middle of corolla‑tube; anther 1 mm, connective elongate into an obscure mucro; style 0.5 mm; stigma 2‑lobed. Drupe elliptic, slightly oblique, 1–1.5 cm, purple‑black when matured.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 35994, 38727, 38776.
Distribution: Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–May of the following year; fruiting: Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, material (essential oil, perfume).

Osmanthus marginatus (Champ. ex Benth.) Hemsl. 厚邊木犀（月桂）
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 88. 1889; FKH 166. 1912; FHN 3: 211. 1974; FFJ 4: 369, fig. 301. 1989; FRPS 61: 87, pl. 23: 1 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 288. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 142. 1998; FGD 5: 416. 2003.
Olea marginata Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 330 – 331. 1852; FHK 215. 1861.

Shrubs or trees, 5–15 m tall. Branchlets glabrous, compressed. Petiole 1.5–2.5 cm; leaf blade broadly elliptic to narrowly lanceolate, 5–15 × 2–5 cm, thick leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, rarely serrate, revolute; midvein and primary veins somewhat impressed adaxially and raised abaxially. Cymes in short panicles (ca. 2 cm), congested, axillary, 10 – 20‑flowered. Flowers dioecious, yellowish or greenish; pedicel 1–2 mm. Calyx 1.5–2 mm, 4‑lobed to middle; lobes broadly deltate, ciliate. Corolla 3.5–4.5 mm; lobes oblong, ciliate, revolute. Stamens attached near top of corolla tube; anther suborbicular, connective not elongate; abortive pistil hemispheric, 0.3–0.5 mm; abortive stamens short. Ovary subglobose, 1.5 mm; style slender, 3 mm; stigma 2‑lobed. Drupe elliptic or oblong, 1.8–3 × 1–1.5 cm, black when matured.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Pak Tam Chung, Long Ke, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2646, 2653; Y. W. Lam 289.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests, ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion 436, K) was collected by J. G. Champion near the top of the Waterfall in the Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion 436, K) was collected by J. G. Champion near the top of the Waterfall in the Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Osmanthus matsumuranus Hayata 牛矢果
J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo. 30(1): 192. 1911; FHN 3: 211, fig. 665. 1974; FFJ 4: 370, fig. 302. 1989; FRPS 61: 89, pl. 23: 4 – 5. 1992; FOC 15: 288. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 142. 1998; FGD 5: 416. 2003.
Osmanthus obouatifolius H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 1982(2): 12. 1982.
Osmanthus maximus H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 1982(2): 8. 1982.

Shrubs or trees, to 2–15 m tall. Branchlets glabrous, compressed. Petiole 1.5–3 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate, 5–15(–19) × 2.5–4.5(–6) cm, thin leathery to papery, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate, margin usually serrate on distal half, midvein and lateral veins adaxially impressed and abaxially raised. Cymes in short panicles, axillary, 1.5–2 cm, 10–30‑flowered; bracteoles deltate‑ovate, 1–2 mm. Flowers dioecious, white or yellowish. Calyx lobes ciliate. Corolla 3–4 mm, 4‑lobed to middle, ciliate; stamens attached near top of corolla‑tube; connective not elongate; abortive pistil oblate; abortive stamens 1 mm. Ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 mm; style slender, 3 mm; stigma capitate, 2‑lobed. Drupe 1.5–2.5 × 0.8–1.2 cm, elliptic, 6 – 8‑ribbed, purple to black when matured.

Locality: Shing Mun, Ho Chung, Tai Wai, Tai Po Kau, Yuen Tun Ha, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 222; Y. S. Lau 811, 2878.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, India.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering; May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Osmanthus minor P. S. Green 小葉月桂
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 22(5): 465, pl. 13. 1958; FFJ 4: 371, fig. 303. 1989; FRPS 61: 91, pl. 23: 6. 1992; FOC 15: 289. 1996; FGD 5: 416. 2003.

Shrubs or small trees, to 2–5(–10) m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Petiole 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or narrowly obovate, 4.5–10 × 1.5–3.5 cm, thin leathery, glandular dotted, base cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire; lateral veins 5–8 on each side of midvein, adaxially obscure, abaxially slightly raised. Cymes in short panicles, axillary, 1–1.5 cm, slender, 8–12‑flowered; bracts deltate, thick, hairy abaxially; bracteoles thin, broadly ovate to lanceolate, apex tipped, crested abaxially, ciliate. Flowers dioecious, yellowish; pedicels 2 mm. Calyx 1–1.5 mm; lobes 0.5–1 mm, ciliate. Corolla 3–3.5 mm, 4‑lobed to middle. Stamens attached near top of corolla‑tube; connective not elongate; abortive pistil oblate, 0.5 mm. Drupe 1.5–2 × 0.8–1.2 cm, elliptic or obovate, 6 – 8‑ribbed, black when matured.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Chuk Kok. S. P. Lau 104; Y. W. Lam 1407.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.

Osterium citriodorum (Hance) C. Q. Yuan & R. H. Shan 隔山香（檸檬香鹹草）
Bull. Nanjing Bot. Gard. Mem. Sun Yatsen 1984– 1985: 3. 1985 [“1984”]; FRPS 55(3): 67. 1992; FOC 14: 170. 2005.
Angelica citriodora Hance, J. Bot. 131. 1871; FKH 117. 1912; FGD 2: 343, fig. 232. 1991.

Perennial herb, 0.5–1.3 m, glabrous, with thick taproot. Stems 2–5 mm thick, branched above, surrounded at base by fibrous remnant leaf-sheaths. Petioles 5–30 cm, sheaths triangular-ovate, 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong-ovate to broadly triangular-ovate in outline, 15–22 × 13–20 cm, 2–3-ternate-pinnate; leaflets subsessile, oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, 3–6.5 × 0.4–2.5 cm, apex acute and mucronate, margin inconspicuously serrate. Umbels compound; peduncles 6–9 cm; involucral bracts 6–8, lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, multi-striate; rays 5–12; bracteoles 5–8, linear, 2–3 mm, reflexed. Calyx-teeth conspicuous, triangular-ovate. Petals white, obovate, apex inflexed. Fruit ellipsoid to broad-ovoid, 3–4 × 3 –3.5 mm, yellowish brown; dorsal ribs prominent, lateral ribs broad-winged; vittae 1–3 in each furrow, 2 on commissure.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tin Fu Tsai, Lam Tsuen, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 2767; P. S. Choi 287; K. L. Yip 4492.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ottelia alismoides (L.) Pers. 龍舌草（水車前）
Syn. Pl. 1: 400. 1805; FKH 257. 1912; FGZ 649. 1956; FRPS 8: 153, pl. 58. 1992; FFJ 6: 26, fig. 19. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 18, pl. 7. 2000; FGD 6: 291. 2005; FOC 23: 95. 2010.
Statiotes alismoides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 535. 1753.
Damasonium indicum Willd., Sp. Pl. Editio quarta 2(1): 276. 1799, nom. illeg. superfl.
Ottelia alismoides (L) Pers. f. oryzetorum Kom., Izv. Imp. Bot. Sada Petra Velikago 10: 122. 1910.
Ottelia condorensis Gagnep., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 54(7): 543. 1907.
Ottelia dioecia S. Z. Yan, J. Sci. Med. Jinan Univ. 2: 162, fig. 187. 1982.
Ottelia indica Planch., Bombay Fl. 278. 1861.
Ottelia japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 271. 1866.

Submerged herb. Petiole varying greatly in length according to depth of water, 2–40 cm; leaf blade wholly submerged, varying greatly in shape and size, usually broadly ovate, ovate-elliptic, nearly orbicular, cordate, or sometimes lanceolate, ca. 20×18 cm or more, membranous, margins entire or serrate. Flowers bisexual or plants occasionally dioecious-polygamous. Spathe 2.5–4 × 1.5–2.5 cm, 2–3-lobed at apex, with 3–6 longitudinal wings. Flowers solitary, sessile. Petals white, slightly purple, or bluish, obovate, 2–3 cm. Stamens 3–9(–12); filaments glandular hairy; anthers narrowly oblong, yellow, 3–4 mm. Ovary nearly globose, with 3–9(–10) carpels; styles 6 – 12, deeply 2-lobed. Fruit 2–5 × 0.8–1.8 cm. Seeds fusiform, 1–2 mm, densely hairy, whitish.

Locality: Tai Po, San Wai, Fanling, Lantau Island, also cultivated in Hong Kong Wetland Park. W. J. Tutcher 9958; HK sheet 27121, 27129.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China especially in E & SW; Africa, E & S Asia, Australia; introduced into N America.
Ecology: Paddy fields, ponds and ditches. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Forage.

Ottochloa nodosa (Kunth) Dandy 露籽草
J. Bot. 69: 55. 1931; FHN 4: 409, fig. 1213. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 222, pl. 67: 1–9. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 485, pl. 202. 2000; FOC 22: 512. 2006 ; FGD 9: 408, fig. 209. 2009.
Panicum nodosum Kunth, Enum. Pl. 1: 97. 1833, not Lamarck (1798); FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, decumbent and rooting at the lower nodes, ascending up to 60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths conspicuously ciliate along one margin; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 4–11 × 0.5–1 cm, smooth, glabrous, base rounded or cordate, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule ca. 0.3 mm. Panicle 10–15 cm, branches 3–8 cm, stiffly spreading, subverticillate in the lower part, the spikelets grouped in clusters or short racemelets, or sometimes loosely spaced. Spikelets elliptic to elliptic-oblong, 2.8–3.2 mm, acute; glumes lanceolate, lower glume 1/2 spikelet length, 3–5-veined; upper glume 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, 5–7-veined; lower lemma 7-veined; upper lemma smooth, apex laterally compressed to a very small crest.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, San Tau. HK sheet 42018, 42021, 42025.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Pacific islands, Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Ottochloa nodosa (Kunth) Dandy var. micrantha (Balansa ex A. Camus) S. L. Chen & S. M. Phillips 小花露籽草
Novon. 13: 467. 2003; FRPS 10(1): 222, pl. 67: 10–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 202. 1995; FOC 22: 513. 2006; FGD 9: 408. 2009.
Ottochloa nodosa (Kunth) Dandy var. micrantha (Balansa ex A. Camus) Keng f., Iconogr. Cormophytorum Sinicorum 5: 160, fig. 7150. 1976, nom. inval.
Hemigymnia arnottiana Stapf var. micrantha Balansa ex A. Camus, Fl. Indo-Chine 7: 455. 1922.

Spikelets 2–2.5 mm; upper glume ovate, ca. 1/2 spikelet length, 7-veined; lower lemma 5–7-veined.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42003, 42006, 42008.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Ottochloa malabarica (L.) Dandy previously (Check List HK Plants 341. 2002; 119. 2004).

Oxalis corniculata L. 酢漿草

Sp. Pl. 435. 1753; FHK 56. 1861; FKH 53. 1912; FHN 1: 416. 1964; FGD 2: 100. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 401, pl. 209. 1993.


Perennial herb, sparsely pubescent throughout. Stems prostrate or ascending, 10–20 cm or longer. Leaves alternate, digitate-trifoliolate; petioles 2– 8 cm; stipules small, adnate to the petiole; leaflets broadly obcordate, 5–17 × 6–18 mm. Peduncle axillary, longer than the petioles, bearing an umbel of 2–6 flowers. Pedicels 5–10 mm, lengthening to 10 – 15 mm in fruit. Flowers ca. 1.2 cm in diam. Sepals lanceolate, 3–4 mm. Petals yellow, obovate, 6–7 × 3.5–3.8 mm. Capsule column-like, 1.5–2 cm, 5-angled, pubescent.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2353; Y. S. Lau 89, 2136.

Distribution: Worldwide weed, origin obscure.

Ecology: Roadsides and wastelands.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Oxalis debilis subsp. corymbosa (DC.) O. Bolòs & Vigo 紅花酢漿草

Fl. Paisos Catalans, 2: 286. 1990.

Oxalis corymbosa DC., Prodr. 1: 696. 1828; FHN 1: 416. 1964; FGD 2: 101, fig. 69. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 401. 1993.

Oxalis martiana Zucc., Denkschr. Konigl. Akad. Wiss. Munchen 9: 144. 1824; FHK 56. 1861; FKH 53. 1912.


Perennial stem-less herb, with a compound bulbous rhizome, covered with brown 3-ribbed scales. Leaves radical, digitate-trifoliolate; petioles 8–25 cm, sparsely villous; leaflets broadly obcordate, 1–3 × 1.5–3 cm, ciliate, glabrous or nearly so adaxially, pubescent, especially on veins abaxially. Cymes umbel-like, branched twice or thrice, each branch bearing 1 or 2 flowers. Peduncle radical, 10–30 cm, longer than the petioles, sparsely villous. Pedicels 6–18(–25) mm. Flowers 2–2.5 cm in diam. Sepals elliptic-lanceolate, 4.5–5.5 mm, apex obtuse, with 2 dark red minute glands at the tip. Petals spathulate, 12–15 × 5–6 mm, pale purplish red, with darker strips. Stamens 10, outer 5 longer than the pistils, inner 5 half as long, with very small anthers. Ovary puberulent, styles 5, free. Capsule unknown.


Locality: A common weed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1657, 1723.

Distribution: Native to S Brazil, now naturalized elsewhere in tropical and subtropical regions.

Ecology: Cultivated fields and wastelands. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.

Notes: The species was reported as Oxalis corymbosa DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 202. 2002; 71. 2004).

Oxyceros sinensis Lour. 雞爪簕
Fl. Cochinch. 151. 1790; Yamazaki, J. Jap. Bot. 45: 340. 1970; FRPS 71(1): 345, pl. 91; 1 – 7. 1999; FYN 15: 173, pl. 35: 1 – 4. 2003; FGD 6: 179, fig. 93. 2005.
Oxyceros sinensis Lour. ex Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 5: 248. 1819.
Randia sinensis (Lour.) Schult. in Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 5: 248. 1819; FHK 155. 1861; FKH 131. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 319. 1998.
Fagerlindia sinensis (Lour.) Tirveng., Nordic J. Bot. 3(4): 458. 1983.

Shrubs or small trees, sometimes straggling, 1–7 m tall. Branches stout, greyish white; branchlets, petioles and inflorescence covered with tawny hairs. Thorns axillary, in pairs or solitary, 4–15 mm. Leaves papery; petioles 5 – 15 mm; stipules triangular, 3–5 mm, pubescent, apex long‑acuminate, deciduous; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic, oblong or ovate, 2–21 × 1.5–9.5 cm, base cuneate or slightly rounded, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface pubescent or only with hairs on midvein, lateral veins and in axils of veins; lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers in rather dense terminal cymes, on very short common peduncles, 3–4.5 cm in diam. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, 4–6 mm; lobes 5, narrowly triangular or ovate‑triangular, 1–4 mm, apex acute. Corolla white or yellow, salverform; tube slender, 12–24 mm, pubescent on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, 5–9 × 4–4.5 mm, spreading. Anthers linear‑oblong, 4 – 5.5 mm, exserted. Style 12–18 mm; stigma fusiform, 2‑lobed. Berry globose, 8–12 cm in diam., often congested into a globular cluster.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island, Lamma Island, Po Toi Islands, Ping Chau. L. Gibbs 7551; P. S. Choi 474; HK sheet 36023.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Environmental (barrier).

Pachyrhizus erosus (L.) Urb. 豆薯（沙葛）
Symb. Antill. 4(2): 311. 1905; FRPS 41: 214. 1995; FGD 5: 307, fig. 163. 2003.
Dolichos erosus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 726. 1753.
Pachyrhizus angulatus Rich., Prodr. 2: 402. 1825; FKH 84. 1912.

Robust twining vine. Roots fleshy tuberous, 10 – 20 cm in diam. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; terminal leaflet rhombic or ovate, 4 –18 × 4 – 20 cm, distal margin often somewhat dentate or lobed, lateral ones very unequilateral, sparsely pubescent abaxially. Racemes axillary, 15– 30 cm. Flowers 3–5 at thickened nodes. Calyx campanulate, 9 –11 mm, adpressed pilose. Corolla purplish or pink; vexillum suborbicular, 15 – 20 mm, with yellow-green spot and 2 callous appendages near base, 2-auriculate; wings falcate, linear-auriculate; keel subfalcate, 1.5 – 2 cm. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary yellowish hirsute, styles curved. Pods loriform, 7.5 – 13 × 1.2 – 1.5 cm, compressed, hirsute. Seeds 8 – 10, subquadrate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 791; Y. W. Lam 279, 1136.
Distribution: SW to SE China (cultivated); native to tropical America, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Cultivated in garden. Flowering: Aug.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Pachystachys lutea Nees 金苞花（黃鴨咀花）
Prodr. 11: 320. 1847.

Subshrubs, to 2 m tall. Stems slightly quadrangular, brownish yellow, glabrous. Petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blades papery, oblong‑lanceolate, 7–16 × 1.5–5 cm, base attenuate, auriculate, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, densely covered with claviform cystoliths especially along veins, lateral veins 5–7 pairs, netted near the margin. Spikes terminal or axillary, 5–9 cm. Peduncle ca. 1 cm. Bracts yellow or orange, ovate, 1.6–3 × 1–1.8 cm, glandular‑pilose along the entire margin, pinnately‑veined, densely imbricate; bracteoles yellow, ovate‑elliptic, ca. 1 × 0.3 cm, 3‑veined. Calyx yellow, ca. 6 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 1 mm broad, glabrous or ciliate on margin. Corolla white, 4.5–5 cm, outside pilose and glandular‑punctate, 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, lanceolate, ca. 2 cm, slightly 2‑lobed, lower lip spreading, ovate, ca. 1.5 cm, 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, attached near the corolla base; filaments subequal to the corolla, exserted; anther 2‑thecous, thecae subequal, sagittate, ca. 4 mm. Staminodes 2, rudimentary. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 4 cm, sparsely pilose at base. Capsule 4‑seeded. Seeds brown.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34738.
Distribution: Native to Peru, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pachystoma pubescens Blume 粉口蘭
Bijdr. 376. t. 29. 1825; FRPS 18: 249, pl. 42: 7–8. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 993. 2000; FGD 7: 405, fig. 207. 2006; FOC 25: 286. 2009.
Pachystoma chinense (Lindl.) Rchb. f., Bonplandia 3: 251. 1855; FHK 356. 1861; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 70, fig. 35. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; rhizome fibrous or yoke-shaped. Leaves 1–2, produced after anthesis, papery, linear-lanceolate, 7–40 × 0.5–1.2 cm, cuneate at base, acute at apex. Flowers 5–13, purple, hanging; pedicels 4–5 mm, hirsute; dorsal sepal elliptic or oblonglanceolate, 11–15 × 4–6 mm, truncate at base, obtuse at apex, with 5 pink veins, glabrous above, sparsely pubescent towards the base beneath; lateral sepals oblique, slightly narrower, pubescent on both surfaces; petal linear-oblong or oblanceolate, 12–13 × 1.5–3 mm, apex acute or acuminate, ciliate along margin; lip 3-lobed, fleshy, pubescent at base, connate to the column foot; lateral lobes erect, rounded, purplish red on both surfaces; midlobe ovate-oblong, recurved at apex, bright purplish red with 3–5 papillose, rough, bright yellow-green ridges; column uniformly dark purple, arcuate, hirsute; anther sparsely pubescent, dark purple; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4 pairs.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Luk Keng, Sai Kung, Nai Chung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 7322, 11849 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 607.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes. Flowering: Mar.–May.

Paederia pertomentosa Merr. ex Li 白毛雞矢藤
Journ. Arnold Arb. 24: 458. 1943; FRPS 71(2): 115. 1999; FGD 6: 226. 2005.

Shurbby or herbaceous vines, to 3 m or longer; branches, petioles and inflorescence densely tomentellous. Petioles (0.5–)1–3(–5) cm; leaf blade papery, ovate to ovate‑elliptic or oblong‑elliptic, 4–12 × 2.2–5.5 cm, base rounded, sometimes slightly decurrent, apex acuminate, adaxial surface ±olive‑green, inicially puberulous, glabrescent, abaxial surface densely whitish tomentose; lateral veins ca. 4 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, 6 – 20 cm, paniculate, with opposite or subverticillate branches of 1–3 cm apart; flowers 5‑merous, arranged in compact cymes or glomerulate at the branches. Pedicels very short. Calyx densely tomentose; lobes triangular, apex acute, glabrous adaxially. Corolla purpleish; tube 5 mm, densely puberulous abaxially; lobes ovate, 1–1.2 mm, acute. Fruits globose at maturity, 4–5 mm in diam., straw‑yellow, shiny; pyrenes semi‑globose 3–4 mm in diam., without wings.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sai Kung (Wong Chuk Yeung). Y. S. Lau 3167; HK sheet 40893, 41515; R. K. Huang 3201 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets or exposed grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.

Paederia scandens (Lour.) Merr. 雞矢藤
Contr. Arnold Arbor. 8: 163. 1934; FHN 3: 358. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 118. 1999; FYN 15: 257, pl. 55: 8 – 11. 2003; FGD 6: 226, fig. 122. 2005.
Gentiana scandens Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 171. 1790.

Perennial herbs; stems glabrous, 3–5 m or longer, woody at the base, with disagreeable odour when bruised. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5–7 cm; stipules triangular, 3–5 mm, glabrous; leaf blade ovate, ovate‑oblong or lanceolate, 5–15 × 1–6 cm, base cuneate, rounded, truncate, or sometimes shallowly cordate, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous or nearly so; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, sometimes with turf of hairs in the axils of veins. Flowers sessile along the branches of the loose dichotomous or trichotomous cymes, forming long loose panicles. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 1–1.2 mm; lobes 5, triangular, 0.8–1 mm. Corolla pale purple; tube 7–10 mm, pulverulent outside, tomentose inside; lobes 5, suborbicular, 1–2 mm. Anthers dorsifixed; filaments unequal. Fruit globular or ovoid, 5–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2260; Y. S. Lau 1988, 2010.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Thickets, wastelands near villages. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Paederia scandens (Lour.) Merr. var. tomentosa (Blume) Hand.‑Mazz. 毛雞矢藤
Symb. Sin. 7(4): 1023. 1936; FHN 3: 358. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 119. 1999; FYN 15: 258. 2003; FGD 6: 226. 2005.
Paederia tomentosa Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 968. 1826; FKH 134. 1912.

Differs from var. scandens by its hairy branches, petioles, inflorescence and abaxial surface of leaves, and by its white (not pale purple) flowers.

Locality: Mount Davis, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1575; P. S. Choi 100, 372.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, India, Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets, wastelands near villages.
Flowering: Jul. – Oct.; fruiting: Sep. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Paliurus ramosissimus (Lour.) Poir. 馬甲子
Encycl., Suppl. 4(1): 262–263. 1816; FKH 62. 1912; FRPS 48(1): 128. pl. 35: 4 –5. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 3: 684, pl. 354. 1993; FGD 4: 266, fig. 158. 2000.
Aublletia ramosissima Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 283. 1790.
Paliurus aubletia Schult., Syst. Veg. 5: 343. 1819; FHK 66. 1861.

Deciduous small tree, sometimes shrubby, to 5 m tall. Young shoots and leaves ± tomentose, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–8 mm, initially tomentose, with a stipular spine on each side; leaf blade ovate to orbicular, 3–6 × 3–5 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex rounded or obtuse, margin crenately serrate, 3-veined at base. Cymes axillary; peduncle and rachis very short, yellow-tomentose. Flowers yellow, ca. 6 mm in diam. Calyx lobed to middle; lobes ovate-triangular, tomentose abaxially. Petals obovate-spathulate, 1–1.5 mm. Stamens slightly longer than petals. Ovary ellipsoidal, lower half immersed in the disk; style 3-cleft to base. Fruit cup-shaped, densely tomentose, surrounded by a 3-lobed horizontal wing.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Mai Po, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 311; L. T. Lo 102; P. S. Choi 154.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests and coastal habitats.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Pandanus austrosinensis T. L. Wu 露兜草
FHN 4: 535. 1977; FRPS 8: 20, pl. 7. 1992; FGD 6: 402. 2005; FOC 23: 129. 2010.
Pandanus austrosinensis T. L. Wu var. longifolius L. Y. Zhou & X. W. Zhong, J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 10(1): 12. 1992.

Herb. Stems underground branched, with many adventitions roots, stems terrestrial unbranched. Leaves subleathery, strap-shaped, 0.7–1.3 m × 3–5 cm, apex acuminate to triangular, with small serrated flagelliform tips, margin with hamate spine, midrib raised abaxially, sparsely spinose. Male inflorescence consisting of several spikes; spathes towards 25 cm; male flowers many; stamens 5–9, filaments connate into a column; anthers linear, ca. 3 mm, connective prolonged into a small point. Syncarps ellipsoidal-cylindrical, 9–15 × 5–8 cm, consisting of 120–260 drupes; drupes obconical, ca. 3 cm, persistent stigma spinose, furcated or not.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 38938, 39341.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides or roadsides. Fruiting: Sep.

Pandanus kaida Kurz 簕古子（露兜簕）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 38(2): 148. 1869; Warb., Pflanzenr. 3(9): 52. 1900; B. C. Stone, Fl. Cambodge Loas et Vietnam 20: 43. 1983; FOC 23: 129. 2010.
Pandanus forceps Mart., Webbia 1: 363. 1905; FKH 287. 1912; FHN 4: 177. 1977; FRPS 8: 15. 1992; FGD 6: 401. 2005; Check List HK Plants 296. 2002; 105. 2004.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3 m tall. Stems branched, without aerial roots. Leaves loriform, 1(– 4) m × 3–5 cm, margin and midrib spiniferous, apex acuminate, long flagelliform-caudate. Male inflorescences consisting of several spikes, each spikes ca. 10 cm, spathes in lower part 45 × 4.5 cm; male flowers white, fragrant; stamens 10–20, nearly on top of filament bundle, free parts of filaments ca. 1 mm; anther long-elliptic, ca. 3 mm, apex cuspidate; female inflorescences capitate, 4 × 1.7 cm; spathes several, 14–20 × 2–3 cm; carpels 2–3 connate into a drup, stigma short, forked. Syncarps composed of ca. 150 drupes; drupe obconic, 3 × 1.7 cm, top 5-angled, persistent stigmas 2, opposite, forked, dentiform.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan. W. J. Tutcher 7222, 5137.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Near seashore in forests or cultivated. Flowering: May – Jul.
Uses: Cultivated as hedges, food (young shoot edible).
records.uses: Cultivated as hedges, food (young shoot edible).

Pandanus tectorius Parkinson 露兜樹

J. Voy. South Seas 46. 1773; Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 903, fig. 364. 1963; FHN 4: 176. 1977; FRPS 8: 18. 1992; FGD 6: 401. 2005; FOC 23: 129. 2010.

Pandanus fascicularis Lam., Encycl. 1: 372. 1783; FKH 287. 1912.

Pandanus odoratissimus L. f., Suppl. 424. 1781, excl. syn.; FKH 287. 1912; Stone, Rev. Fl. Ceylon 3: 311, fig. 6 – 7. 1981; Fl. Cambodge Laos et Viet-nam 20: 23. 1983.

Pandanus odoratissimus L. f. var. sinensis (Warb.) Kanehira, Form. Trees rev. ed. 63, fig. 24. 1936; Li, FTW 5: 825. 1978.

Pandanus remotus St. John, Pacif. Sci. 16: 70. 1962.

Pandanus sinensis (Warb.) Martel. in Kanehira, Fl. Micrones 69. 1933.

Pandanus tectorius Parkinson var. sinensis Warb., Pflanzenr. 3(9): 48. 1900; FRPS 8: 20. 1992; FGD 6: 402. 2005.


Shrub or small tree, 1–4 m tall; stem branched, with aerial roots. Leaves aggregated on top of stem, leathery, loriform, usually over 1 m × 2–5 cm, margin and midrib abaxially with strong and upward spines, apex long caudate. Male inflorescence consisting of several 4–8 cm spikes; Spathes whitish, long-lanceolate, 20–40 × 1–5 cm, decrescent toward upper; stamens 10–15(–25) on a column of 1 cm, free part of filament ca. 1 mm; anther linear, 3 mm, conective prolonged into a small point. Female inflorescence terminal, globular; spathes several, milk white, 14–35 × 1–3 cm, margin serrate; carpels 2–12, connate, but free at apex. Syncarps pendent, red, yellow to orange, consisting of 40–80 drupes; drupe obconical, ca. 4 cm, truncate, angular, persistent stigma subsessile, slightly protruded, auriculate, nipple-shaped or hippocrepiform.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2880; HK sheet 7724.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia to Australia.

Ecology: Sandy beaches or cultivated in gardens. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jan.–Oct.

Uses: Ornamental, material (fiber), medicinal (folklore).

Notes: A mutant cultivar ‘Sanderii’ is cultivated in Hong Kong for ornamental use. It is characterized by the leaves with several lengthwise golden-yellow bands from midrib to margin, and with minute spines on the margins.

Pandanus urophyllus Hance 分叉露兜
J. Bot. 13: 68. 1875; FKH 287. 1912; B. C. Stone, Fl. Cambodge, Laos et Vietnam 20: 34. 1983; FOC 23: 130. 2010.
Pandanus furcatus auct. non Roxb.: FRPS 8: 15. 1992; FGD 6: 400. 2005; Check List HK Plants 296. 2002; 105. 2004.

Tree, 7–12 m tall; stem with thick aerial roots, dichotomous branched. Leaves aggregated on top of stem, leathery, loriform, 1–4 m × 3–10 cm, margin densely denticulate-spiniferous, spines incurved, abaxially midrib with upward curved acute spines, apex 3-angulate-flagelliform-caudate. Male inflorescence consisting of several spikes; spikes golden yellow, cylindrical, 10–15 cm, spathes towards 1 m × 10 cm; male flowers many, stamens usually 3–5-clustered on top of filament bundle; anther linear, 5 mm, connective with long and curved awn-like point; female inflorescences a head, to 80 cm, with many spathes; female flowers with 1 carpels, rarely 2 connate; stigma forked, spineform, incurved. Syncarps red-brown, oblongoid to ellipsoidal, 23 × 12 cm, drupes bony, top pyramidal, 1–2-locular, exocarp fleshy, sweet and fragrant, persistent stigma dichotomous, spine-form.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 7107, 7222; L. T. Lo 455.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Sikkim to Indochina.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.
Uses: Cultivated as hedges.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18394, BM) was collected by J. Lamont and C. Harland from Hong Kong Island before 1875.

Cultivated as hedges.

Pandanus utilis Bory 扇葉露兜樹（馬達加斯加露兜）
Voy. Îles Afrique 2: 3 – 5. 1804.

Tree to 15 m tall, trunk smooth with aerial roots, much branched. Leaves spirally arranged in 3 series, crowded towards top of stems, erect, stiff, long-linear, 40–180 × 3–11 cm, uniformly green throughout, grey glaucous abaxially, tapering in a long point at apex, margins and ribs abaxially with many sharp, ascending reddish, 1–4 mm spines. Male inflorescence a branched spadix, 30–80 cm , in axil of a pale spathe; female inflorescence a subglobose head. Male flowers odorous, with 8–12 stamens inserted pseudo-umbellately on slender column of 10–15 mm. Syncarps solitary, pendulous, long-pedunculate, yellow when ripen, subglobose, 15–20 cm in diam., comprising of 100–200 fibrous drupes, each drupe 2.5–3.5 cm, with lower part prism-shaped and upper part convex-pyramidal, 2–8-celled, persistent stigma sessile, reniform.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 743.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical regions, no wild populations are known.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, food (fruit), leaves also used for making baskets and domestic articles.

records.text:
Panicum brevifolium L. 短葉黍
Sp. Pl. 1: 59. 1753; FKH 316. 1912; FHN 4: 404. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 216, pl. 64: 1–7. 1990; FFJ 6: 204, fig. 171. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 487, pl. 204. 2000; FOC 22: 509. 2006; FGD 9: 406. 2009.
Panicum ovalifolium Poir., Encycl., Suppl. 4: 279. 1816; FHK 413. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms rambling and rooting at lower nodes, flowering branches 10–50 cm tall, nodes glabrous or pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, puberulous or glabrous, margins ciliate; leaf blades ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–10 × 0.5–3 cm, glabrous or sparsely pilose, base cordate, amplexicaul, apex acute, margins scabrous or the base with tuberculate-ciliate; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, a ciliolate membrane. Panicle oblong or ovate in outline, spreading, much branched, usually glandular patches present. Spikelets elliptic, 1.5–2 mm, sparsely puberulous to pilose; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, slightly shorter than or as long as spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined, dorsally convex, apex beak-like; lower lemma oblong, similar to upper glume, palea well developed; upper floret ovate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2032; L. T. Lo 559; HK sheet 42039.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Humid places in open fields and margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May – Dec.

Panicum dichotomiflorum Michx. 洋野黍（水生黍）
Fl. Bor. Amer. 1: 48. 1803; FRPS 10(1): 207. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 490. 2000; FOC 22: 506. 2006; FGD 9: 403. 2009.
Panicum paludosum Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 310. 1820; FRPS 10(1): 206. 1990; Check List HK Plants 342. 2002; 119. 2004.

Annual or perennial hydrophilous herb. Culms creeping and rooting at lower nodes, branching, 30–110 cm, upper nodes glabrous. Leaves cauline; leaf sheaths striate, glabrous, longer than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, 7–35 × 0.5–1.5 cm, glabrous, scabrid, base straight or subcordate, apex acute; ligule 1–2 mm, a ciliate membrane. Panicle terminal or axillary, open, 10–30 cm, much branched; branches glabrous, scabrid, secondary and tertiary branches often appressed. Spikelets lanceolate to narrowly ovate, 3–4 mm, glabrous, acuminate; lower glume 1/6 – 1/3 length of spikelet, clasping at the base of the spikelet, membranous, 0–1-veined, apex obtuse to acute; upper glume as long as spikelet, 7–9-veined; lower lemma similar to upper glume, palea absent or well developed, narrow and small; upper floret green or pale yellow, 2/3 length of spikelet, smooth, shiny, acute.

Locality: New Territories. Y. W. Lam 1574; HK sheet 41942, 42013.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan , Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, tropical regions of the New World.
Ecology: Swampy places in shallow waters. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Panicum incomtum Trin. 藤竹草
Gram. Panic. 200. 1826; FHN 4: 406. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 211, pl. 63: 14–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 207. 1995; FOC 22: 509. 2006; FGD 9: 405. 2009.
Panicum sarmentosum auct. non Roxb.: FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms woody, branching and scrambling, up to 10 m. Leaf sheaths loose, puberulous; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 10–25 × 1–3 cm, pilose, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 0.5–1 mm, ciliate. Panicle spreading, 10–20 cm; central axis erect, much branched, viscid. Spikelets ovate, 1.5–2.2 mm, obtuse or slightly acute; lower glume ovate, 2/3–3/4 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined, base inrolled embraced spikelet, acute or ciliate; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined; lower lemma similar to upper glume, palea well developed; upper floret as long as spikelet, brown, smooth, shiny.

Locality: Causeway Bay, Fung Yuen, Ng Tung Chai, Cheung Chau. Y. W. Lam 1314, 1735; HK sheet 41721.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Shade in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Mar.

Panicum maximum Jacq. 大黍
Icon. Pl. Rar. 1: 2. 1781; FKH 315. 1912; FHN 4: 405. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 214, pl. 63: 18–22. 1990; FFJ 6: 205. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 490, pl. 205. 2000; FOC 22: 506. 2006; FGD 9: 405. 2009.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms stout, erect, 1–3 m tall, nodes glabrous or densely pilose. Leaf sheaths sparsely tuberculatehispid; leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, flat, 20–60 × 1–3 cm, adaxial surface tuberculate-hispid near base, base broad, taping downward, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 1–1.5 mm, membranous, long-ciliate. Panicle oblong, spreading, 20–35 cm, much branched; branches spreading, lowest arranged in a whorl. Spikelets oblong, ca. 3 mm; lower glume broadly ovate, 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 1–3-veined or veinless; upper glume elliptic, as long as spikelet, 5-veined, acute; lower floret staminate, lemma similar to upper glume, palea well developed, stamens 3; upper floret oblong, thinly coriaceous, shiny, finely transverse rugulose.

Locality: Cultivated for forage. Y. S. Lau 2232, 2537; HK sheet 35001.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan (introduced); Africa, Arabian Peninsula; widely naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder, forage).

Panicum notatum Retz. 心葉稷（山黍）
Observ. Bot. 4: 18. 1786; FHN 4: 404. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 210, pl. 63: 10 – 13. 1990; FFJ 6: 207, fig. 175. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 491. 2000; FYN 9: 496. 2003; FOC 22: 509. 2006; FGD 9: 404. 2009.
Panicum montanum Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 315. 1820; FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, often rooting at lower nodes, branched. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, ciliate; leaf blades lanceolate, 5–12 × 1–3 cm, subglabrous to pubescent, cross veins present, base cordate, apex finely pointed to acuminate, margins scabrid; ligule very short, a ciliate membrane. Panicle broadly ovate, spreading, much branched; branches slender, spreading, glabrous, smooth or scabrid, bearing spikelets toward the extremities. Spikelets elliptic, 2–2.5 mm, glabrous or puberulous; lower glume ovate or oblong, nearly equaling or slightly shorter than the spikelet, 3 –5-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined, acute; lower lemma similar to upper glume, 5-veined, palea absent; upper floret as long as spikelet, leathery, smooth, shiny.

Locality: New Territories. Y. W. Lam 426; HK sheet 41979, 41980.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia. Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Panicum repens L. 鋪地黍
Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 1: 87. 1762; FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912; FHN 4: 404. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 207, pl. 62: 1–8. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 491. 2000; FOC 22: 506. 2006; FGD 9: 404. 2009.

Perennial, rhizomatous herb. Culms erect or decumbent, 20–120 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, puberulous to ciliate on margins; leaf blades linear, 5–25 × 0.2–0.8 cm, flat or convolute, often stiff and pungent, apex acute or acuminate; ligule 0.5–1.5 mm, a ciliate membrane. Panicle terminal, narrowly oblong, open, 5–20 cm; branches ascending. Spikelets oblong, ca. 3 mm, glabrous, acute; lower glume 1/4–1/3 length of spikelet, thin membranous, hyaline, clasping at the base of the spikelet, obtuse or truncate; upper glume as long as spikelet, membranous, 7–9-veined, beak-like; lower floret staminate, lemma similar to upper glume, stamens 3, palea well developed; upper floret bisexual, nearly equal to spikelet, oblong, acute, smooth and shiny.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1637, 2282; Y. W. Lam 760.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Streamsides, paddy fields and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Papaver rhoeas L. 虞美人
Sp. Pl. 1: 507. 1753; FFJ 2: 156, fig. 131. 1985; FGX 1: 406, pl. 168: 1–2. 1991; FRPS 32: 53. 1999; FGD 4: 61, fig. 38. 2000.

Annual herb; stems branched, 30 – 80 cm, sparsely hispid. Leaves alternate, pinnately or bipinnately lobed, 3–15 cm, lobes lanceolate, margin coarsely serrate, leaves on the upper part of stems coarse-serrate-pinnately lobed, sparsely hispid on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, pedicels 10–15 cm; sepals 2, broadly elliptic, 1–2 cm, green, hispid; petals 4, red, purple or white, usually with black patches at base, suborbicular or obovate, 2– 3.5 cm; stamens many, filaments red; ovary obovoid, ca. 1 cm, glabrous, stigmas plateform, with 5 –18-radiate lobes, persistent, 1.2–2 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 32.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China, native to Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Paphiopedilum purpuratum (Lindl.) Stein 紫紋兜蘭（香港兜蘭）
Orchideenbuch 481. 1892; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 27, fig. 5. 1977; FRPS 17: 69, pl. 8: 1. 1999; FGD 7: 330, fig. 160. 2006; Z. J. Liu et al., Genus Paphiopedilum in China 181. 2009; FOC 25: 43. 2009.
Cypripedium purpuratum Lindl., Edward's Bot. Reg. 23: t. 1991. 1837; FHK 364. 1861.
Paphiopedilum purpuratum (Lindl.) Pfitzer, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 19(1): 40. 1894; FKH 270. 1912.
Cypripedium sinicum Hance ex Rchb. f., Walp. Ann. 3: 602. 1853.

Terrestrial or semi-epiphytic herb. Leaves 4–8, distichous, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 8–17 × 2–4 cm, tessellated dark and light green above, pale green beneath; margins ciliate near the base. Flower solitary; scape 15 – 20 cm, purple, pubescent; bract ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 × 1 cm, villose at margin; perianth 8 cm across; dorsal sepal ovate-cordate, 3–4 × 2.5–3 cm, white, veined purple-maroon; synsepalum ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 × 1–1.5 cm, pale green with dark veins; petals horizontal, ellipticoblong, 4–5 × 1–1.5 cm, glossy maroon or pale chestnut with dark veins, flushed green-white and spotted black-maroon; lip 4 × 2 cm, incurved, lateral lobes verrucose, brown-maroon; staminode lunate, 8 ×10 mm, pale ochre-purple veined darker.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Clear Water Bay, Lantau Island. K. K. Mark 38 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 632, 1762.
Distribution: S Fujian, S Guangdong, Hainan, S Guangxi, SE Yunnan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Humus-rich stony places in forests. Flowering: Nov.–May of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The holotype specimen of Cypripedium sinicum Hance ex Rchb. f. (Hance s.n., W) was collected by H. F. Hance from Hong Kong Island around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The holotype specimen of Cypripedium sinicum Hance ex Rchb. f. (Hance s.n., W) was collected by H. F. Hance from Hong Kong Island around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Paraixeris denticulata (Houtt.) Nakai 黃瓜菜
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 34: 156. 1920; FRPS 80(1): 262, pl. 1: 3, pl. 58: 1 – 2. 1997.
Prenanthes denticulata Houtt., Nat. Hist. 10: 385. 1779.
Youngia denticulata (Houtt.) Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11(2): 128. 1942.
Ixeris denticulata (Houtt.) Stebbins, J. Bot. 75: 46. 1937; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 2. 1967.
Lactuca denticulata (Houtt.) Maxim., Mélanges Biol. Bull. Phys.‑Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Pétersbourg 19: 529 – 530. 1874; FKH 150. 1912.
Ixeris ramosissima A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad.Arts n.s. 6: 397; FHK 193. 1861.
Brachyramphus ramosissimus Benth., London J. Bot. 1: 489. 1842.

Annual or biennial herbs; stem erect, 30–120 cm tall, branched in apical half, glabrous. Leaves glabrous on both surfaces. Radical and lower leaves ovate with margin irregularly dentate, or oblanceolate and lyrately pinnatisect, long‑petiolate, withered at flowering stage. Middle cauline leaves mostly sessile or sometimes broadly winged petiolate; leaf blade spatulate, pandurate, pandurate‑ovate, elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, 3.5–11 × 1–7 cm, undivided or sometimes lyrately pinnatilobed with 1–2 pairs of elliptic or triangular lateral lobes, base abruptly broaden as round auricles and amplexicaul, apex obtuse to rounded, and usually mucronate, margin entire, mucronate‑toothed, or irregularly dentate. Upper leaves sessile, smaller in size, elliptic, oblong to ovate‑cordate, base auriculate and amplexicaul. Capitula corymbose‑paniculate; peduncles 4–12 mm. Involucres cylindric, 6–8 mm, 1.5–2 mm wide; phyllaries in 2 series, glabrous; outer ones small ovate, 0.5 – 1 × 0.3 – 0.5 mm, apex acute; inner ones lanceolate to linear, 6–8 × 0.8–1.5 mm, acute or obtuse, abaxial side with spongy thickening along midvein, sometimes bearing horn‑like structure below apex. Ligulate florets 10–15 per head, corolla yellow, 7–8 mm, lower tube about 2.5 mm, upper ligule 4–6 mm, apex 5‑lobed. Cypselae cylindric‑elliptic, black or blackish brown, 3.2–5 mm including the apical beak, obtusely 10–11‑ribbed, hirtellous along ribs, apex attenuate to form a thick and brown beak. Pappus white, minutely scaberulous, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 524; Y. W. Lam 779; S. Y. Hu 8579 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia (Far East region), Mongolia, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, open fields and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.

Paraphlomis javanica (Blume) Prain var. coronata (Vaniot) C. Y. Wu & H. W. Li 小葉假糙蘇
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 13(1): 72. 1975; FRPS 65(2): 552. 1977; FOC 17: 172. 1994; FGD 3: 422. 1995.
Lamium coronatum Vaniot, Bull. Acad. Int. Geogr. Bot. 14: 174. 1904.
Phlomis rugosa Benth., Numer. List n. 2067. 1829; FKH 212. 1912.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems usually solitary, retrorse strigose. Leaves succulent; petioles slender, 2– 8 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, 3–9( –15) × 1.5–6 cm, base rounded to subtruncate, apex acuminate to acute, margin shallowly and remotely serrate to crenate, with minute scattered hairs on both surfaces. Verticillasters many‑flowered, globose, ca. 3 cm in diam., subtended by few bracteoles at base. Calyx turbinate, 8–12 mm, abruptly spreading at mouth, hairy on veins abaxially; tube slightly curved; teeth 5, lanceolate, the base triangular, often broken off in fruit. Corolla yellow or yellowish, 2–2.5 cm, pubescent annulate inside; both lips pubescent abaxially, upper lip narrow, rounded at apex; lower lip 3‑lobed; the middle lob oblong, the lateral lobes lanceolate. Stylar branches subequal. Nutlets obovoid, acute and triquetrous at base.

Locality: Mount Parker, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 1338; L. T. Lo 359; Y. W. Lam 379.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.; fruiting: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Paris polyphylla Sm. var. chinensis (Franch.) H. Hara 華重樓（重樓）
J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, 10: 176. 1969; FRPS 15: 92. 1978; FOC 24: 91. 2000.
Paris chinensis Franch., Nouv. Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat., ser. 2, 10: 97. 1888.
Paris polyphylla auct. non Sm.: FKH 281. 1912.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout, 30–100 cm tall, with thick horizontal jointed and scarred rhizome. Leaves 5–10, but usually 7, in a terminal whorl; petiole 0.5–3 cm; leaf blade variable, oblong-lanceolate or obovate-oblanceolate, 5–20 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute. Flower terminal, solitary; peduncle 1.8–10 cm. Outer perianth segments 5–6, ovate-lanceolate 2–6 × 1–2 cm, leaf-like, green or yellow-green; inner ones linear, usually shorter than outer ones, 1–1.5 mm wide, usually yellow-green. Stamens 8–10, in 2 series; filaments 5–6 mm; anthers 10–12 mm; free portion of connective 0.5–1.5 mm. Ovary subglobose, ribbed, 1-locular, sometimes tuberculate; style short, base enlarged, purple to white; stigma lobes (4–)5. Capsule globose, sometimes tuberculate. Seeds enveloped by red, succulent aril.

Locality: Mount Parker, Shek O Rd., Lantau Island, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2126.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar.
Ecology: Forests, ravines in humus soil. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
