Parthenocissus dalzielii Gagnep. 爬牆虎（異葉爬山虎）

Notul. Syst. (Paris) 2: 11. 1911; FRPS 48(2): 24. 1998.

Parthenocissus heterophylla auct. non (Blume) Merr.: FHN 3: 20. 1974; FFJ 3: 375, fig. 263. 1988.


Branchlets terete, glabrous throughout; tendrils slender, short and branched, apex enlarged and turning into sucker. Leaves dimorphic, thickly papery, deep green adaxially, pale green or glaucous abaxially; simple ones on long branches; petioles 5–20 cm; simple leaves oval, 2.5–7 × 2–5 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely toothed; trifoliolate on short branches; central leaflet long ovate, broadly lanceolate-ovate or obovate-oblong, 6–21 × 2.5–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely toothed; petiolules short, 0.3–1 cm; lateral leaflets sessile, ovate-elliptic, 5.5–19 × 2.5–7.5 cm, base conspicuously oblique, apex acuminate, margin irregularly sparsely toothed or subentire. Polychasium pseudoterminal or leaf-opposed, shorter than petiole; peduncles absent to 3 cm. Flowers small, pale green. Pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx shallowly cupular, undulate or subentire. Petals obovate-elliptic, 1.5–2.7 mm. Anthers yellow, ellipsoidal, 0.7–1.5 mm. Stigma inconspicuously enlarged. Berry purplish black, 0.6–1 cm in diam.


Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1834, 2221; HK sheet 34320.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Henan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.

Ecology: Climbing on walls. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Uses: Ornamental.

Paspalum conjugatum P. J. Bergius 兩耳草
Acta Helv. Phys.-Math. 7: 129. 1772; FKH 313. 1912; FHN 4: 425. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 288, pl. 88: 1–6. 1990; FFJ 6: 220. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 495, pl. 206, photo 56. 2000; FOC 22: 526. 2006; FGD 9: 427. 2009.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms in small tufts along rhizomes, 20–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous or pilose along upper margins and mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, thin, 5–20 × 0.5–1.3 cm, glabrous or papillose-pilose along margins, apex acute; ligule very short, a ring of hairs. Inflorescence of a pair of racemes, racemes 6–12 cm; spikelets solitary, in 2 rows; rachis 0.5–1 mm wide, serrate. Spikelets solitary, ovate to suborbicular, 1.5–1.8 mm, 2-floret; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as lower lemma, hyaline, thin, margins with long silky hairs; lower lemma similar but not ciliate; upper lemma pallid at maturity, ovate, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 6; Y. S. Lau 1692, 3133.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics and subtropics throughout the world.
Ecology: Grassy fields, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Paspalum dilatatum Poir. 毛花雀稗
Encycl. 5: 35. 1804; FRPS 10(1): 294, pl. 88: 7–12. 1990; FFJ 6: 221, fig. 187. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 497, pl. 207. 2000; FOC 22: 527. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tuft, erect from a short rhizome, 50–150 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose in the lower part; leaf blades linear, 10–45 × 0.3–1 cm, glabrous; ligule 2–5 mm, truncate, membranous, glabrous. Racemes 2–10, spaced, diverging, axils pilose. Spikelets broadly ovate, in 4-rows, 3–4 mm; lower glume absent; upper glume membranous, as long as spikelet, 5–9-veined, sparsely pubescent to almost glabrous on back, margins fringed with long white hairs; lower floret barren, lemma ovate-lanceolate, 5–7-veined, glabrous; upper lemma pallid at maturity, orbicular, ca. 2 mm, leathery, papillose-striate, apex rounded.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 39684, 41557, 42050.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; originated from S America, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Grassy fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.

Paspalum distichum L. 雙穗雀稗
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 855. 1759; FKH 313. 1912; FHN 4: 426. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 497, pl. 208. 2000; FOC 22: 528. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.
Paspalum paspaloides (Michx.) Scribn., FRPS 10(1): 290, pl. 89: 6–11. 1990; FFJ 6: 220, fig. 186. 1995; Check List HK Plants 342. 2002; 120. 2004.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms ascending from creeping and rooting base, 20–60 cm tall, nodes usually pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, keeled, glabrous, margins ciliate; leaf blades lanceolate, 5–15 × 0.3–0.7 cm, glabrous, apex acute; ligule membranous, 2–3 mm, glabrous. Racemes 2, arising together or separated by a short axis, raceme 3–5 cm; spikelets solitary, in 2 rows; rachis flat, 1.5–2 mm wide. Spikelets obovate-oblong, 3–3.5 mm, loosely pubescent, acute; lower glume usually absent or small; upper glume papery, 3–5-veined with distinct middle vein, loosely appressed pubescent; lower lemma 3–5-veined, usually glabrous, apex acute; upper lemma pale green, subequal to spikelet, cartilaginous, apex apiculate and minutely pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2255; Y. W. Lam 2223; HK sheet 39654.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangsu, Shandong, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Farmlands, grassy fields, roadsides, ditches and other disturbed places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Paspalum longifolium Roxb. 長葉雀稗
Fl. Ind. 1: 283. 1820; FHN 4: 425. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 288, pl. 87: 1–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 222, fig. 188. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 497. 2000; FOC 22: 530. 2006; FGD 9: 429. 2009.

Perennial stout herb. Culms tufted, erect, 80–150 cm tall, many-noded, glabrous. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, keeled, papillose-pilose along margins; leaf blades linear, 10–60 × 0.5–1.2 cm, glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence axis 4–10 cm; racemes 5–20, 4–8 cm, ascending; spikelets normally paired, occasionally solitary but 2nd vestigial spikelet present; densely overlapping; rachis broadly winged, purplish, margins scabrous with conspicuous close-set teeth. Spikelets purple or pale green, broadly obovate, paired, in 4 rows; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as lower lemma, membranous, 3-veined, minutely crisped-pubescent, apex slightly acute; upper lemma pallid, yellow-green, indurate.

Locality: Tai Tam, Lin Tong Mei. P. S. Choi 521; HK sheet 41949.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Pacific islands, N Australia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, grassy fields, swampy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Paspalum scrobiculatum L. 鴨乸草
Mant. Pl. 1: 29. 1767; FHK 408. 1861; FKH 313. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 282, pl. 85: 1–6. 1990; FFJ 6: 223. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 500. 2000; FOC 22: 528. 2006; FGD 9: 430. 2009.

Perennial or annual herb. Culms tufted, erect or decumbent at base, 90–150 cm tall. Leaf sheaths longer or upper shorter than internode, compressed, keeled, usually glabrous; leaf blades lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 10–20 × 0.4–1.2 cm, usually glabrous, base subrounded, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule membranous, 0.5–1 mm. Inflorescence of 2–5(–8) racemes, subdigitate or on a short axis; racemes 3–10 cm, ascending to widely spreading. Spikelets usually solitary, suborbicular or broadly elliptic, 2–3 mm, glabrous; lower glume absent; upper glume membranous, 7–13-veined; lower lemma 7 –9-veined, veins often concolorous with back; upper lemma dark brown at maturity.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1037, 1870; HK sheet 36082.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, tropical SE Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Paspalum scrobiculatum L. var. orbiculare (G. Forst.) Hack. 圓果雀稗
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 6: 233. 1885; FOC 22: 529. 2006; FGD 9: 430. 2009.
Paspalum orbiculare G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 7. 1786; FHN 4: 427. 1977; FFJ 6: 223, fig. 190. 1995; FRPS 10(1): 284, pl. 87: 12 – 16. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 500. 2000; Check List HK Plants 342. 2002; 120. 2004.

Spikelets elliptic or broadly obovate, 2–2.2 mm, often paired, imbricate, in 2 rows; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as lower lemma, membranous, 3–5-veined, slightly acute; upper lemma yellow-brown or mid-brown at maturity, as long as spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3181; Y. W. Lam 2176; HK sheet 41983.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands (Polynesia).
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Paspalum urvillei Steud. 絲毛雀稗
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 24. 1853; FRPS 10(1): 294. 1990; FFJ 6: 221. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 501. 2000; FOC 22: 527. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.

Perennial stout herb, with a short rhizome. Culms tufted, up to 2 m tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths densely hispid, with long hairs at the mouth; leaf blades linear, 15–30 × 0.5–1.5 cm, glabrous or pilose at the base; ligule 3–5 mm, tipped with long hairs. Inflorescence axis 10–40 cm; racemes 10–25, 8–15 cm, narrowly ascending or suberect; spikelets paired, 2–3-rows on one side of rachis; rachis ca. 0.5 mm wide. Spikelets light green or purplish, ovate, 2–3 mm, margins densely covered with silky long hairs, sharply acute; lower glume reduced; upper glume membranous; lower lemma similar to upper glume; upper lemma elliptic, coriaceous, smooth, margins inrolled.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. W. Lam 853; S. C. Ng 1850; HK sheet 40839.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to S America, but widely introduced and naturalized in war areas.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May – Oct.

Paspalum vaginatum Sw. 海雀稗
Prodr. 21. 1788; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 182. 1971; FRPS 10(1): 290, pl. 89: 1–5. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 501. 2000; FOC 22: 528. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.

Perennial halophilous herb, with short rhizome and long stolons. Culms solitary or tufted, many-noded, flowering culm 6–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, imbricate, often keeled, margins membranous, mouth with long pilose; leaf blades linear, 2.5–15 × 0.3–0.8 cm, inrolled, acute; ligule membranous, truncate, 0.5–1 mm. Inflorescence of (1–)2(–3) racemes arising together at culm apex; racemes 2–5 cm, usually closely approximate when young, later spreading; spikelets solitary, in 2 rows; rachis 1–2 mm wide, glabrous, triangular, often zigzag. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, acute; lower glume absent or rarely a tiny vestige; upper glume thin papery or membranous, midvein often compressed, glabrous; lower lemma similar to upper glume, glabrous; upper lemma 2.5–3 mm, shorter than spikelet, cartilaginous, apex minutely pubescent; upper palea ca. 2/3 length of upper lemma.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1639; K. L. Yip 4208; HK sheet 37212.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropics and subtropics throughout the world.
Ecology: Sandy seashores, margins of streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Passiflora moluccana Reinw. ex Blume var. teysmanniana (Miq.) de Wilde 蛇王藤
Fl. Mal. 1: 7. 1972 & Blumea 20: 239. 1972; FGD 2: 118, pl. 78: 1– 6. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 101. 1999.
Disemma horsfieldii Miq. var. teysmanniana Miq., Fl. Ned. Ind. 1: 700. 1856,
Passiflora cochinchinensis Spreng., Syst. Veg. 4(Cur. Post.): 346. 1827; FHN 1: 466, fig. 257. 1964.
Passiflora ligulifolia Mast., Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond. 27: 632. 1871; FKH 110. 1912.
Passiflora hainanensis Hance, J. Bot. 16: 227. 1878.

Stems glabrous, rarely angled. Stipules absent. Petioles 0.6 –1.5 cm, pilose; leaf blades alternate or sometimes opposite, leathery, variable in shape, linear, linear-oblong or broadly elliptic, 4 –14 × 1– 6 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex rounded and emarginate or very short acute, margin entire, glabrous and shining adaxially, sometimes pubescent and glandular abaxially. Cymes 1–2-flowered. Bracts and bracteoles very small, linear. Flowers white, 3.5–5 cm in diam.; pedicels 2.5–4.5 cm. Sepals 5, narrowly oblong, 2 cm, pilose abaxially, without appendage at apex. Petals oblong, ca. 1.5 cm; corona consisting of many filiform lobes, lobes in 2 whorls, outer ones 1.2–1.5 cm, inner ones 1.5–3 mm, greenish purple or yellow. Stamens 5, filaments distinct, 6 –10 mm; anthers ellipsoid, ca. 4 mm. Ovary globose, sessile, subglabrous; styles 3, distinct, curved, ca. 5 mm. Berries ovoid or subglobose, 1.5 –2.5 cm or longer, 1–2 cm in diam., glabrous, green, glaucous. Seeds greyish yellow, compressed, ca. 4 mm.

Locality: Lung Kwu Tan, Po Toi. Y. W. Lam 2252; HK sheet 40262, 40294.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Passiflora foetida L. 龍珠果
Sp. Pl. 2: 959. 1753; FHK 123. 1861; FKH 110. 1912; FHN 1: 466. 1964; FRPS 52(1): 111, pl. 25: 8 –11. 1999; FGD 2: 120. 1991;
Passiflora hispida DC. ex Triana & Planch., Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 5, 17: 172. 1873; C. Y. Wu & W. T. Wang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 6: 236. 1957.
Dysosmia foetida (L.) M. Roem., Fam. Nat. Syn. Monogr. 2: 150. 1846.

Stems slender, terete, angled, pubescent or glabrous. Stipules filiform, lobed, glandular at apex. Petioles 2– 6 cm, villous; leaf blades broadly ovate to oblong-ovate, membranous, 4.5 –13 × 4–12 cm, 3-lobed, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin irregularly undulate, ciliate or glandular-ciliate, villous on both surfaces, mixed with a few glandular hairs adaxially and with scattered small glands abaxially. Cymes 1-flowered. Flowers white or pale purple, white patched, 2–3 cm in diam.; bracts pinnately 1–3-lobed, forming many filiform lobules, lobules glandular hairy at apex. Sepals oblong, 1.5 –1.8 cm, with a horn-like appendage near apex abaxially. Petals as long as sepals. Corona lobes in 3–5 whorls, outer 2 whorls 4–5 mm, those of the inner 3 whorls 2.5 mm. Androgynophore 5–7 mm; filaments connate at base; anthers ellipsoid, 4 mm. Ovary ellipsoid, ca. 6 × 4 –5 mm, stipitate, glandular hairy or glabrous; style 3(– 4), 5 – 6 mm, stigmas capitate. Berries ovoid or globose, 2–3 cm in diam. Seeds ellipsoid, ca. 5 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. H. C. Tang 1785; Y. S. Lau 1930; G. Gibbs 7546.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (naturalized); native to Mexico, S & C USA, S America, widely naturalized in tropical regions worldwide.
Ecology: Thickets on wastelands. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Food (fruit edible).

Pavetta hongkongensis Bremek. 香港大沙葉（茜木）
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 37 (961 – 973): 104. 1934; FHN 3: 346, fig. 763. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 27, pl. 9: 4–8. 1999; FYN 15: 205, pl. 41: 4 – 7. 2003; FGD 6: 200. 2005.
Pavetta indica auct. non L.: FHK 157. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves thin‑papery; petioles 1–2 cm; stipules broadly ovate‑triangular, ca. 3 mm, glabrous abaxially, white villose adaxially; leaf blade oblong to elliptic‑obovate, 8–15 × 3–6.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glabrescent or pubescent on midvein and in axils of veins; lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midven. Cymes trichotomous, 7–15 cm in diam., sessile above the last leaves. Pedicels 3–6 mm. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped, ca. 1 mm; limb inconspicuously 4‑toothed. Corolla white, tube to 15 mm or longer, glabrous outside, sparsely pubescent near the base inside; lobes oblong, ca. 6 mm, apex acute. Style ca. 35 mm, long exserted. Berry globular, ca. 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 99, 278; K. Y. Tam 146.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Mar.–Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Pecteilis susannae (L.) Raf. 白蝶蘭（鵝毛白蝶花）
Fl. Tellur. 2: 38. 1837 [“susanna”]; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 28, fig. 6. 1977; FRPS 17: 395, pl. 62. 1–2. 1999; FGD 7: 370, fig. 190. 2006; FOC 25: 136. 2009.
Orchis susannae L., Sp. Pl. 939. 1753.
Habenaria susannae (L.) R. Br., Prod. Fl. Nepal 321. 1819; FHK 363. 1861.
Platanthera susannae (L.) Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 295. 1835; FKH 269. 1912.

Perennial large herb requiring a winter rest period underground 30–40 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all cauline, ovate-oblong, 5.5–11 × 2–4 cm, acute. Flowers fragrant, large, showy, 2–5 in a terminal raceme; pedicels 1.5 cm; dorsal sepals, suborbicular, 2.5 cm in diam.; lateral sepals 4–5 cm, pointing upward, apex obtuse; petals cornute, small, inconspicuous, 12 × 2 mm; lip long, 3-lobed at base, butterfly-like, the lateral lobes triangular, 3 × 4 cm, prominently fringed, midlobe linear, 3 × 0.6 cm; spur 12 cm, 2–3 mm in diam.; column fleshy, 1.7 × 1 cm, rounded and notched at apex; anther with widely separate thecae; pollinia 2; ovary ellipsoidal.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Clear Water Bay, Lantau Peak. J. P. W. Woo 110 (CUHK); S. P. Lau 31; Y. S. Lau 1604.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests, ditches or grassy slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pelargonium hortorum Bailey 天竺葵（洋葵）
Stand. Cyl. Hort. 2531. 1916; FHN 1: 414. 1964; FFJ 2: 345, fig. 263. 1985; FYN 5: 97. 1991; FGD 2: 98. 1991; FRPS 43(1): 85, pl. 25: 4– 8. 1998.

Perennial herb, 30–60 cm tall. Stems erect, base woody, upper part fleshy, multibranched or not branched, densely pubescent, pungent. Leaves alternate; stipules broadly triangular or ovate, 7–15 mm, pubescent and glandular-hairy; petiole 3–10 cm, finely pubescent and glandular-hairy; blade orbicular or reniform, 3–7 cm in diam., base cordate, margin shallowly undulate-lobed, crenate, transparently pubescent on both surfaces, with a dark red horseshoe-shaped patch adaxially. Umbels many-flowered, peduncles longer than leaves, pubescent. Bracts several, broadly ovate. Pedicels 3–4 cm, pubescent and glandular-hairy. Sepals narrowly lanceolate, 8–10 mm, densely glandular hairy and villous. Petals red, orange-red, pink or white, broadly obovate, 1.2–1.5 × 0.6–0.8 mm, base clawed, apex obtuse, lower 3 often larger. Ovary densely pubescent. Capsule ca. 3 cm, pubescent.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Cultivated in China; native to S Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Jun.– Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pelexia obliqua (J. J. Sm.) Garay 肥根蘭
Bot. Mus. Leafl. Harvard Univ. 28(4): 345. 1980; FRPS 17: 231. 1999; S. Y. Hu, Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 107. 2003; FOC 25: 86. 2009.
Spiranthes obliqua J. J. Sm., Bull. Dep. Agric. Indes Neerl. 43: 74. 1910.
Manniella hongkongensis S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 6, fig. 13. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 42, fig. 15. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; leaves and flowering plants appearing in different seasons. Leaves caespitose, petiolate; petioles up to 1 cm; leaf blades elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 3.5–6.5 × 1.5–3.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers small, white, 5–18 terminal to a scape of 12–15 cm; sepals longer than petals, glandularly hairy on the basal portion, 4 mm, the lateral two connate at base; petals 4 mm; lip fleshy, the lower portion forming a groove and extending backward into 2 appendages, hooked at the ends in the spur; column short, apex ovoid; anther lanceolate; pollinia 2; rostellum ovate; stigmas 2; ovary glandularly hairy.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 13266 (CUHK).
Distribution: Indonesia.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Sep.
Notes: The holotype specimen of M. hongkongensis (S. Y. Hu 13266, K) was collected from Sha Tin in 1965.

Peliosanthes macrostegia Hance 大蓋球子草
J. Bot. 23: 328. 1885; FKH 273. 1912; FRPS 15: 167, pl. 56: 1–2. 1978; FOC 24: 263. 2000; FGD 6: 357, fig. 212. 2005.

Perennial herb, with short rhizomes and thick roots. Leaves 2–5, basal; petiole 7–30 cm; leaf blade lanceolate-oblong, 14–27 × 3–6 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate or acute, with 5–9 parallel veins, netted veins conspicuous. Scape 15–29 cm. Inflorescence a raceme, 10–22 cm, rachis purplish when dry; bracts ovate-lanceolate, 6–15 mm, membranous. Flowers solitary; pedicels 2–5 mm, articulate near apex; bracteole 1, 3–5 mm. Perianth purple; tube ca. 2 mm, basally adnate to ovary; segments 6, ovate-oblong, 4–5 mm. Stamens 6; filaments connate into a fleshy ring; anthers ca. 1 mm. Ovary 3-locular; style short; stigma 3-lobed. Seeds subglobose, ca. 1 cm, berry-like.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1726; HK sheet 30161.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, SE Yunnan, NE Sichuan, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests, thickets, shady and humid rocky places. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Pellionia brevifolia Benth. 短葉赤車
FHK 330. 1861; FKH 249. 1912; FHN 2: 409. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 174, pl. 38: 4. 1995; FOC 5: 125. 2003; FGD 6: 79. 2005.

Perennial herb. Stems prostrate, 10–30 cm or longer, rooting at nodes, hispid, hairs recurved or slightly spreading. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, 1.2–2 mm; petioles 1.5 –2 mm; leaf blade very obliquely elliptic to obovate, 5 –32 × 4 –20 mm, base very unequal, slightly obtuse or cuneate on the narrow side, auriculate on the broad side, apex obtuse or rounded, sparsely and obtusely serrate above the middle, adaxial surface glabrous or with scattered, appressed short hairs, abaxial surface pubescent on veins, subtriplinerved. Male cymes 8–15 mm in diam.; peduncles 2.5 – 4 cm, puberulent; female cymes compact, 2.5–4 mm in diam., almost sessile or on peduncles of 2–6 mm. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 2 mm, slightly unequal, glabrous; stamens 5. Female flowers: perianth‑segments 5, very unequal, linear-lanceolate, 1–1.8 mm; staminodes lanceolate, bent in at about the middle. Achene narrowly ovoid, ca. 1.2 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Sunset Peak. W. J. Tutcher 7248.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: May–Jul.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Gough and Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford (No. 227, K) between 1857 and 1858.

Pellionia grijsii Hance 華南赤車
J. Bot. 6: 49. 1886 & 12: 262. 1874; FRPS 23(2): 178. 1995; FOC 5: 126. 2003; FGD 6: 81. 2005.

Perennial herb. Stems 40 –70 cm tall, unbranched, or occasionally with a few branches, hirsute, the hairs 0.5 –2 mm, slightly recurved or spreading. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, ca. 4 mm, glabrous; petioles 1– 4 mm, hirsute; leaf blade obliquely oblong to oblong-lanceolate or oblique-elliptic, 6 –14(–18) × 2.4 – 5(– 6) cm, base very unequal, cuneate or obtuse on the narrow side, auriculate on the broad side, apex long-acuminate or acuminate, sometimes caudate, obtusely serrate above the base, adaxial surface glabrous or with scattered short hairs, rarely densely strigose, abaxial surface hirsute on veins, sub–pinnately nerved; lateral veins 4 – 5 on each side of midvein. Male cymes 2–3 times branched, 0.5 – 5.6 cm in diam.; peduncles 0.9 – 8 cm, together with the branches hirsute; female cymes more compact and densely flowered, 3 –10 mm in diam.; peduncles 1.5–7 mm, hirsute. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 2 mm; stamens 5; rudimentary pistil ca. 0.2 mm. Female flower: perianthsegments 5, ca. 0.6 mm, unequal, 3 larger, narrowly navicularoblong, 2 smaller, narrowly lanceolate; staminodes very minute or none. Achene ellipsoid, ca. 0.8 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11443 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Jiangxi, S Fujian.
Ecology: Ravines, by streams or on rocks. Flowering: Winter.

Pellionia radicans (Sieb. & Zucc.) Wedd. 赤車
Prodr. 16(1): 167. 1869; FKH 249. 1912; FHN 2: 408. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 171, pl. 37: 6. 1995; FOC 5: 125. 2003; FGD 6: 79. 2005.
Procris radicans Sieb. & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 218. 1846.

Perennial herb. Stems ascending from the procumbent base, 20 –60 cm or longer, glabrous or puberulent, the hairs ca. 0.1 mm. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, 1–4 mm; petioles 1–4 mm; leaf blade obliquely rhomboid-ovate or lanceolate, (1.2–)2.4 – 5(– 8) × 0.9– 2(–2.7) cm, base very unequal, obtuse on the narrow side, auriculate on the broad side, apex shortly acuminate to long-acuminate, serrate above the middle, glabrous on both surfaces or nearly so, subtriplinerved. Flowers usually dioecious. Male cymes loose, 1– 5(– 8) cm; peduncles 0.4 –3.5(–7) cm, glabrous or papillose-puberulent; female cymes compact, 3– 5 mm in diam.; peduncles 0.5 –3(–18) mm, with a few short hairs. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous or puberulent outside; stamens 5; rudimentary pistil narrowly obconical, ca. 0.6 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments 5, ca. 0.4 mm, 3 larger, navicular-oblong, 2 smaller, narrowly oblong; staminodes very minute or none; ovary about the length of the perianth-segments. Achene ellipsoid, ca. 0.9 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Ma On Shan. F. W. Xing 8463.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; N Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets, forests in ravines. Flowering: May–Dec.

Pellionia scabra Benth. 蔓赤車
FHK 330. 1861; FKH 249. 1912; FGZ 404. 1956; FHN 2: 407. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 168, pl. 37: 5 & 44: 3 – 4. 1995; FOC 5: 124. 2003; FGD 6: 79, fig. 29. 2005.

Subshrub. Stems erect or ascending, 30–100 cm tall, woody at base, upper part hirsute; hairs 0.3–1 mm. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, 1.5–3 mm; petioles 0.5–2 mm; leaf blade obliquely rhomboid-oblanceolate or narrowly oblong, 3.2–6.5(–10) × 1.3–3.2(–4) cm, base very unequal, slightly obtuse on the narrow side, broadly cuneate, rounded or auriculate on the broad side, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, serrate above the middle, adaxial surface scabrous, with short hairs on the midvein, abaxial surface pubescent, sub-triplinerved. Male cymes loose, on slender peduncles of 0.3 –3.6 cm, puberulent; female cymes very compact, subsessile, densely puberulent. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, united at base, unequal, 3 larger, the other 2 smaller; stamens 5; rudimentary pistil subulate, ca. 0.3 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments 4 – 5, narrowly oblong, ca. 0.5 mm, 2 or 3 larger than others; staminodes very minute or none. Achene ellipsoid, ca. 0.8 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 2435; L. T. Lo 591; Y. W. Lam 1388.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines, on shady and wet places. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.
Notes: The type specimens were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s by A. W. Harland, C. Wright and C. Wilford.

Peltophorum pterocarpum (DC.) Baker ex K. Heyne 盾柱木（雙翼豆）
Nutt. Pl. Ned.-Ind. (ed. 2) 2: 755. 1927; FRPS 39: 92, pl. 31: 1 – 7. 1988; FGD 5: 168. 2003.
Inga pterocarpa DC., Prodr. 1: 441. 1825.
Caesalpinia inermis Roxb., [Hort. Bengal. 90. 1814] Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 2: 367. 1832.
Peltophorum ferrugineum (Decne.) Benth., Fl. Austral. 2: 279. 1864.
Caesalpinia ferruginea Decne., Nouv. Ann. Mus. Hist. Nat. 3: 462. 1834.
Peltophorum inerme Náves ex Fern.- Vill., Fl. Filip. (ed. 3) 4: Nov. App. 69. 1880, nom. inval.; FGZ 316. 1956.

Tree, 4–15 m; young branches and inflorescences densely rusty pubescent; old branches yellow lenticellate. Stipules entire. Leaves 30–42 cm; petiole robust, densely rusty pubescent; pinnae 7–15 pairs, 8–12 cm; leaflets 10–20 pairs, sessile, leathery, oblong, 1–1.8 × 0.5–0.7 cm, base oblique, apex obtuse, mucronate, entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Panicles terminal or axillary. Bracts 5–8 mm, caducous. Pedicels ca. 5 mm, as long as flower buds. Flower buds globose, 5–8 mm in diam. Calyx-lobes ovate, 5–8 × 4–7 mm, rusty tomentose. Petals obovate, 1.5–1.7 × 0.8–1 cm, densey rusty villose at middle on both surfaces, long stalked. Filaments ca. 1.2 cm, base hirsute; anthers nearly arrow-shaped, ca. 3 mm. Ovary stipitate, 3–4-ovuled; style filiform, elongated; stigma disciform, 3-lobed. Pods dark red when mature, oblong, 5–8 × 1.8–2.5 cm, flat, fusiform, winged along both sutures, wings 4–5 mm wide, densely fine-striate throughout; seeds 2–4.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 36, 2272; HK sheet 24924.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangzhou; Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia and N Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Oct.

Peltophorum tonkinense (Pierre) Gagnep. 銀珠
Fl. Indo-Chine 2: 192. 1913; FHN 2: 228. 1965; FRPS 39: 93, pl. 31: 8 – 14. 1988; FGD 5: 168, fig. 99. 2003.
Baryxylum tonkinense Pierre, Fl. Forest. Cochinch. sub pl. 391C. 1899.
Peltophorum dasyrrhachis var. tonkinensis (Pierre) K. Larsen & S. S. Larsen, Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam 18: 61. 1980.

Tree, 10–20 m; young branches and inflorescences densely rusty pubescent, later glabrescent; old branches densely rusty lenticellate. Stipules lobed, linear or filiform, caducous. Leaves 15–35 cm; petiole robust, 7–16 cm, densely rusty pubescent; pinnae 6–13 pairs; leaflets 5–14 pairs, sessile, leathery, oblong, 1.5–2 × 0.6–1 cm, base attenuate, asymmetrical, apex obtuse, emarginate or mucronate, entire, rusty hairy along midveins at first, later glabrescent. Racemes subterminal, 8–12 cm. Pedicels 1.5–2.5 cm, 2–3 times as long as flower buds. Flower buds globose, ca. 8 mm in diam. Calyx-lobes ovate, 8–9 mm, lowest one narrower, densely rusty hairy. Petals obovate, 1.5 cm, stalked, margin minutely wavy, densey rusty villose along midveins on both surfaces. Filaments ca. 1 cm, base enlarged, densely rusty hairy; anthers ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm. Ovary shortly stipitate, 3–4-ovuled; style slender, 3–4 times as long as ovary; stigma capitate, unlobed. Pods reddish brown when mature, thinly leathery, fusiform, 8–13 × 2.5–3 cm, unequally narrowed on both ends, glabrous, winged along both sutures, wings 5–7 mm wide, not striate at middle; seeds 3–4, oblique obovate, ca. 1.4 × 0.6 cm, flat, yellow.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 40203.
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.

Pennisetum alopecuroides (L.) Spreng. 狼尾草
Syst. Veg. 1: 303. 1825; FRPS 10(1): 366, pl. 111: 1 – 4. 1990; FFJ 6: 197, fig. 164. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 502, pl. 209. 2000; FOC 22: 550. 2006; FGD 9: 444. 2009.
Panicum alopecuroides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 55. 1753.
Pennisetum compressum R. Br., Prod. 195. 1810; FKH 316. 1912.
Gymnothrix japonica Benth., FHK 413. 1860.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 30 – 120 cm tall, hispid below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths longer than internode at the upper part, keeled, imbricate at base; leaf blades linear, flat or often involute, 10 – 80 × 0.3 – 1 cm, base papillose-hispid, apex long acuminate; ligule a ring of hairs, ca. 0.5 mm. Panicle cylindrical, spike-like, 5 – 25 × 1.5 – 3.5 cm; axis hispid, peduncle stumps short with crateriform tips; involucre usually enclosing one spikelet, rarely 2, basal stipe (1 – )2 – 3 mm; bristles greenish or purple, longest 2 – 3 cm but not conspicuously longer than the others, all slender, hispid. Spikelet solitary, seldom paired, lanceolate, 5 – 8 mm; lower glume minute or absent; upper glume ovatelanceolate, 1/3 – 2/3 length of spikelet, 3 – 5-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7 – 11-veined; upper lemma lanceolate, as long as spikelet, 3 – 7-veined, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea; lodicules 2; stamens 3, style base connate. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1504; HK sheet 39643, 40814.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; and tropical Asia, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Grassy fields, roadsides, paths between paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Pennisetum polystachion (L.) Schult. 牧地狼尾草（多穗狼尾草）
Mant. 2: 146. 1824; FTW ed. 2, 5: 505. 2000; FOC 22: 550. 2006; FGD 9: 444. 2009.
Panicum polystachion L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 2: 870. 1759.
Pennisetum setosum (Sw.) Rich., Syn. Pl. 1: 72. 1805; FRPS 10(1): 365. 1990.

Perennial or annual herb with short rhizomes. Culms tufted, 50–150 cm tall. Leaf sheath loose, hispid, margin ciliate. Leaf blades linear, 10–20 × 0.3–1.5 cm, hispid; ligule a ring of long hairs, ca. 1 mm. Panicle contracted panicle, yellow or purplish, 10–25 cm; bristles unequal, outer ones shorter, inner ones feathery, up to 1 cm. Spikelet ovate-lanceolate, 3–5 mm; lower glume absent or a small triangular scale; upper glume as long as spikelet or slightly longer, 5-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, lemma similar but slightly shorter than spikelet, 5-veined, obtusely 3-lobed; upper floret shorter than spikelet, cartilaginous, smooth, shiny, readily deciduous at maturity.

Locality: New Territories. L. T. Lo 411; Y. W. Lam 1205; HK sheet 42645.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan; native to Africa, naturalized throughout the tropics.
Uses: Animal food (potential as forage).
Notes: The species was reported as Pennisetum polystachyum (L.) Schult. previously (Check List HK Plants 343. 2002; 120. 2004).
records.uses:
Animal food (potential as forage).
Notes: The species was reported as Pennisetum polystachyum (L.) Schult. previously (Check List HK Plants 343. 2002; 120. 2004).

records.text:
Pennisetum purpureum Schumach. 象草
Beskr. Guin. Pl. 44. 1827; FRPS 10(1): 373, pl. 111: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 198, fig. 165. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 505. 2000. FOC 22: 550. 2006; FGD 9: 443. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, erect, 2–4 m tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous or hispid; leaf blades linear, flat, 20–50 × 1–2 cm, adaxial surface hispid or papillos-pilose at base, abaxial surface glabrous, margins scabrous; ligule 1.5–5 mm, ciliate. Panicle golden, brownish or purplish, cylindrical, 10–30 × 1–3 cm; axis densely pilose, closely beset with small peduncle stumps. Spikelets solitary or 2–3-fasciculate, subsessile, lanceolate, 5–8 mm, subrounded by an involucre of bristles, falling off together with spikelet at maturity; lower glume ca. 0.5 mm or absent; upper glume lanceolate, 1/4–1/2 length of spikelet; lower floret staminate or neuters, lemma 1/2–4/5 spikelet length, 5–7-veined; upper lemma as long as spikelet, smooth and shiny, 5-veined; lodicules 2, small; stamens 3, anthers with a tuft of short hairs at tip; style base connate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1674; L. T. Lo 38; Y. W. Lam 1206.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; native to Africa.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control), animal food (forage).

Pentaphylax euryoides Gardn. & Champ. 五列木
Hook. J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 245. 1849; FHK 28. 1861; FKH 44. 1912; FHN 1: 510. 1964; FRPS 45(1): 136, pl. 39. 1980; FGD 4: 141. 2000.

Shrub or tree, 4 –15 m tall, glabrous except bracteoles and sepals. Branchlets terete, greyish brown. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, grooved adaxially; leaf blade ovate, ovate-oblong or oblong–-lanceolate, 4–9 × 2– 5 cm, leathery, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex caudate, margin entire and slightly revolute, dark green adaxially, pale green abaxially, lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Pseudo-racemes axillary or terminal, 4.5–12 cm. Pedicels ca. 0.5 mm; bracteoles triangular, 1–1.5 mm, sparsely white puberulous adaxially, margin ciliolate. Sepals 5, orbicular, 1.5 –2.5 mm in diam., sparsely white puberulous adaxially, apex slightly 2-cleft, margin ciliolate. Petals white, oblong-lanceolate to oblanceolate, 4– 5 × 1.5 –2 mm, apex retuse to 2-cleft; filaments oblong, petaloid, 2.5 –3.5 mm; anthers globose, ca. 0.5 mm in diam. Ovary ca. 1 mm long; style columnar, ca. 2 mm, 5-ridged. Capsule ellipsoid, 6–9 × 4 – 5 mm, purplish brown to dark brown, dehiscing into 5-valves when mature. Seeds reddish brown, 5 – 6 mm long, apex very compressed or winged.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 10912; P. S. Choi 212; K. L. Yip 4452.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.
records.uses:
Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Pentas lanceolata (Forssk.) Deflers 五星花
Voy. Yemen 142. 1889; FGD 6: 145, fig. 65. 2005.
Pentas lanceolata (Forssk.) K. Schum., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(4): 29. 1891; FRPS 71(1): 175. 1999; Check List HK Plants 270. 2002; 92. 2004.

Subshrubs, to 70 cm tall. Stems and branches quadrangular, covered with white multicellular hairs when young. Leaves opposite; petioles 1.5–3 cm, pilose; stipules short and broad, apex bristly; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, 5 – 14 × 2–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially pubescent or scabrous, abaxially densely pubescent on the veins. Corymbs terminal; peduncles 3–12 mm, together with bracts and calyx covered with white multicellular hairs. Calyx‑tube subglobose, apex with 5–6 unequal lobes. Corolla carmine‑rose, rosy or white, salverform; tube to 2 cm, sparsely pubescent abaxially, densely covered with white long hairs in throat; limb usually 5‑lobed, ca. 1.2 cm in diam.; lobes elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate. Anthers slightly exserted or included. Style 2‑lobed, purplish black.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1595; S. P. Lau 89; L. T. Lo 614.
Distribution: Native to tropical Africa and Arabia; widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pentasachme caudatum Wall. ex Wight 石蘿藦
Contr. Bot. India 60. 1834; FOC 16: 262. 1995.
Pentasachme championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 54. 1853; FHK 228. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 415, pl. 153. 1977; FGD 1: 499, fig. 564. 1987.

Herbs to 80 cm tall, branched, glabrous throughout. Petioles 1 – 2 mm; leaf blade linear‑lanceolate, 4–16 × 0.5–2 cm, midvein prominent on both surfaces, lateral veins obsolete. Cymes subsessile, much shorter than leaves, raceme‑like, 4 – 8‑flowered. Pedicels 0.3–2 cm. Sepals lanceolate, 1.5–3 × 1 mm. Corolla white; tube short; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 6–15 × 2 mm. Corona‑lobes white, thick, margin denticulate. Anthers laterally flattened; pollinia attached to caudicle at middle, retinaculum 1/3 of pollinia. Follicles cylindric‑lanceolate, 5–7.5 × 0.3 cm. Seeds minute; coma 1.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2247; Y. S. Lau 420, 1804.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Guangxi, Yunnan; Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Streamsides in forests, open woodlands and thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
