Phalaris canariensis L. 加那利虉草（虉草）
Sp. Pl. 1: 54. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 5: 361. 2000; FOC 22: 335. 2006.

Annual herb. Culms loosely tufted, 30–60(–100) cm tall, glabrous. Leaf blades 10–30 × 0.5–1.2 cm, glabrous; ligule acute, 3–8 mm; leaf sheaths cylindrical, mostly shorter than the internode. Panicle spike-like, 1.5–4 × 1.5–2 cm, ovate to oblong-ovate. Spikelets obovate, 3-flowered, extremely compressed, 6–9 mm; glumes 7–10 mm, oblanceolate, glabrous or puberulent, whitish with green longitudinal stripes, keel broadly winged above middle, apex acute; sterile lemmas 2, equal, narrowly elliptic, chaffy, 2.5–4 mm, appressed-pilose; fertile lemma lanceolate, 5–6 mm, shiny, densely appressed-pubescent; palea oblong, 2-veined. Anthers 3–4 mm.

Locality: Clear Water Bay (cultivated). L. T. Lo 615.
Distribution: Hebei, Shanghai, Taiwan (cultivated or naturalized); native to Madagascar and N Africa, naturalized throughout the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.

Phaseolus vulgaris L. 菜豆
Sp. Pl. 723. 1753; FRPS 41: 296. 1995; FGD 5: 333, fig. 183. 2003.

Annual twining or suberect herb. Stems pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; terminal leaflet broadly ovate or ovate-rhombic, lateral ones oblique, 4–16 × 2.5–11 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, entire, tomentose. Racemes shorter than leaves, several-flowered at apex of rachis. Calyx cupular 3–4 mm. Corolla white, yellow, violet or red; vexillum subquadrate, 9–12 mm wide; wings obovate; keel 1 cm, apex spirally twisted. Ovary pubescent. Pods loriform, 10–15 × 1–1.5 cm, slightly curved and turgid, glabrous, beaked. Seeds 4–6, white, brown, blue or variegated, oblong or ensiform, 0.9–2 × 0.3–1.2 cm.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated everywhere, native to America.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Jul.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Philydrum lanuginosum Banks & Sol. ex Gaertn. 田蔥
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 62, fig. 16. 1788; FHK 380. 1861; FKH 282. 1912; FHN 4: 182. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 144. 1997; FOC 24: 43. 2000; FGD 5: 455. 2003.

Leaves 40–80 cm long (including basal sheath), glabrous, thick, aerenchymatous; sheath 14–30 × 1–1.5 cm. Inflorescence 20–60 cm long; scape slender, terete, glabrate below, villous towards the flowers; bracts ovate to subulate, 2–10 cm × 7.5–10 mm, woolly on abaxial side, short-acuminate to attenuate. Flowers with thin perianth, outer tepals 10–15 × ca. 10 mm, manyveined, long villous outside, the upper with 2 stronger veins and bidentate, acute, margins inflexed, inner tepals spathulate, ca. 8 × 2 mm, membranous, 3-veined, with base hairy outside. Stamen ca. 9 mm long, glabrous, anther ± spherical. Ovary densely longwoolly; style glabrous; stigma broad-triangular, long-papillose. Fruit 9–12 × 4–5 mm. Seeds dark reddish-brown, bulb-shaped, ca. 1 mm long.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Ham Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Lam Chung, Wu Kau Tang, Yung Shue O, Wang Toi Shan, Lantau Island. R. M. K. Saunders s.n. (HKU); Y. S. Lau 2071, 1447.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Andaman Islands, Malaysia, Australia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds and marshes at low altitudes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phoenix loureiroi Kunth 刺葵
Enum. Pl. 3: 257. 1841; FOC 23: 144. 2010.
Phoenix hanceana Naudin, J. Bot. 17: 174. 1879; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 165, fig. 1066. 1977; FGD 2: 455. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 10. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 5: 660. 2000; Check List HK Plants 295. 2002; 104. 2004.
Phoenix hanceana Naudin var. formosana Becc., Philipp. J. Sci., C 3: 339. 1908.
Phoenix acaulis auct. non Roxb.: FHK 340. 1861.

Small to moderate tree, 1–5 m tall. Stems solitary or clustered, 25–40 cm in diam., sometimes short and subterranean, rough, with petiole base remains. Leaves pinnate, to 2 m; pinnae 35–120, acanthophylls (pinnae on lower rachis) about 15 per side of rachis, linear, solitary, or 2–3 grouped, not in the same plane; middle pinnae 20–45 × 1–3 cm; sheaths and petioles to 40 cm. Inflorescences branched 1 order, with 30–40 rachillae; prophyll 15–20 cm, dark brown; peduncles to 50 cm. Flowers yellowish white; male flowers: calyx 1–1.5 mm, 3-lobed; petals 3, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm; stamens 6; female flowers: calyx-lobe ca. 1 mm, petals 2 mm in diam., carpels 3, free, ovoid, 1.5 × 0.8 cm. Fruits oblong, 1.5–2 cm, black or purplish black. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 663; S. P. Lau 154; K. L. Yip 4414.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia.
Ecology: Open forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, material (weaving).

Phoenix roebelenii O'Brien 江邊刺葵（軟葉刺葵、日本葵）
Gard. Chron., ser. 3, 6: 475. 1889; FGD 2: 455, fig. 319. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 10. 1991; FOC 23: 144. 2010.

Small trees, 1–3 m tall. Stems solitary, slender, to 10 cm in diam., with spirally arranged remains of triangular petiole bases. Leaves pinnate, 1–1.5(–2) m; pinnae 25–50 per side of rachis, regularly arranged and in the same plane, linear, soft, 20–30 cm × 5–10 mm, with persistent grey scales on abaxial midribs; acanthophylls (pinnae on lower rachis) about 12 per side. Inflorescences branched 1 order, prophyll 30–50 cm. Male inflorescences 30–55 cm, rachillae ca. 20, 7–20 cm; male flowers: sepals ca. 1 mm; petals 3, ca. 9 mm, stamens 6. Female inflorescences to 35 cm; rachillae 35–45; female flowers subovoid, ca. 6 mm; carpels 3, free. Fruits oblong-obovoid, 14–18 × 6–8 mm, purplish brown. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 636; HK sheet 29497.
Distribution: Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pholidota cantonensis Rolfe 細葉石仙桃
Kew Bull. 1896: 196. 1896, et J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 23. 1903; FHK 354. 1861; FKH 264. 1912; FRPS 18: 392. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1005, pl. 427. 2000; FGD 7: 460, fig. 230. 2006; FOC 25: 338. 2009.

A small terrestrial herb; rhizome zig-zag, covered with brown scales; pseudobulbs globose-ovoid. Leaves petiolate, petioles 2–4 mm; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–8 × 0.4–0.7 cm, acute. Flowers white-yellow, in a terminal raceme; pedicels 2 mm; sepals all white, 5 × 2.5 mm, acute; petals similar; lip undivided, ventricose, 3 mm, gibbose at base, apex subobtuse; column very short, 1.5 mm; anther suborbicular; pollinia 4; ovary 1 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, 7 mm.

Locality: Tai Po, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 9701 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

Pholidota chinensis Lindl. 石仙桃
J. Hort. Soc. London 2: 308. 1847; FHK 354. 1861; FKH 264. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 82, fig. 44. 1977; FRPS 18: 394, pl. 65: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 460. 2006; FOC 25: 338. 2009.
Coelogyne chinensis (Lindl.) Rchb. f., Ann. Bot. Syst. 6: 237. 1861.

Terrestrial herb; rhizomes creeping; pseudobulbs ovate-oblong, 2–8 cm. Leaves 2, terminal to pseudobulb; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 10–20 × 3–4 cm, apex acute to acumninate. Flowers white to pale yellow, 5–20 in a pendant raceme on scapes of 2–4 cm; dorsal sepal ovate-elliptic, 10–12 × 5–8 mm; lateral sepals 11 × 7 mm, broader; petals ovate-oblong, 9–10 × 4 mm; lip firmly attached to base of column, fleshy, enlarged and sac-like at base, the rounded front lobe turning downward; column white 5 mm, winged; anther suborbicular; pollinia 4; ovary cylindrical. Capsules ellipsoidal, 1.2–1.8 cm, 6 ridged.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 11089, 12744 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 199, 222.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Boulders in damp ravines in forests, high shaded valleys. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Photinia benthamiana Hance 閩粵石楠
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 5, 5: 213. 1866; FKH 97. 1912; FRPS 36: 250. 1974; FFJ 2: 324. 1985; FGD 4: 185. 2000; FOC 9: 133. 2003.
Pourthiaea benthamiana (Hance) Nakai, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 30(349): 24. 1916.

Deciduous small tree or shrub, 3 – 10 m tall; branchlets greyish-black, initially greyish-white pilose, glabrescent, lenticellate. Petioles 6– 10 mm, initially pubescent, glabrescent; leaf blade papery, obovate-oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 5–11 × 2–5 cm, base attenuate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin sparsely serrulate, initially both surfaces grey villous, later glabrous or with a few long hairs on veins abaxially, lateral veins 5 – 8 on each side of midvein. Compound corymbs terminal, many-flowered, shorter than leaves; peduncles and pedicels densely grey villous; bracts subulate, 2–4 mm; pedicels 1–5 mm. Flowers 7–8 mm in diam.; hypanthium campanulate, 3–4 mm, densely villous abaxially; sepals triangular, ca. 1 mm; petals white, obovate or orbicular, 3 – 5 mm, glabrous or adaxially puberulous, apex emarginate or obtuse; stamens 20, as long as or slightly shorter than petals; styles 3, glabrous, connate at base. Pomes ovoid or subglobose, 4–6 × 3 – 5 mm, sparsely yellowish villous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2273; Y. S. Lau 2748; K. Y. Tam 117.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jul. – Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Photinia raupingensis K. C. Kuan 饒平石楠
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8(3): 228. 1963; FRPS 36: 237. 1974; FGD 4: 184. 2000; FOC 9: 130. 2003.
Photinia prunifolia auct. non Lindl.: FHK 107. 1861; FKH 97. 1912.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 3–5 m tall; branchlets initially densely villous, later glabrescent. Petioles 8–15 cm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, oblong, obovate or oblong-elliptic, 4 – 8 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin serrulate, adaxial surface glabrous and shining, abaxial black glandular-punctate, villous along midveins when young, later glabrescent, lateral veins 12–17 on each side of midvein. Compound corymbs terminal, 3 – 7 cm in diam., many-flowered; rachis, peduncles and pedicels densely grey villous; bracts subulate or linear, 3–4 mm, grey villous; hypanthium campanulate, 1 mm, abaxially densely grey villous; sepals triangular, 1 mm, abaxially villous, apex acute, persistent; petals white, obovate, 2 mm, basally villous, apex acute; stamens 20, shorter than petals; ovary 2-locular, apically villous; styles 2, connate at base. Pomes ovoid, 5 – 6 × 3 – 4 mm, red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1363; P. S. Choi 437; Y. W. Lam 2236.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar. –Apr.; fruiting: Jun.– Dec.
Notes: Early records under the name P. prunifolia are referrable to the present species (Forbes & Hemsley, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 262. 1887). The species was reported as P. prunifolia Lindl. previously (Check List HK Plants 29. 1993).

Photinia serratifolia (Desf.) Kalkman 石楠

Blumea 21: 424. 1973; FOC 9: 125. 2003.

Crataegus serratifolia Desf., Tabl. Ecole Bot. (ed. 3) 288. 1829.

Photinia serrulata Lindl., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 13(1): 103. 1821, nom. illeg., superfl.; FHK 107. 1861, in obs.; FRPS 36: 220. 1974; FGD 4: 182. 2000.


Evergreen shrub or small tree, 4 – 6(–12) m tall; branchlets brownish grey, glabrous. Petioles 2 – 4 cm, pubescent initially, glabrescent; leaf blade leathery, oblong, oblong-obovate or obovate-elliptic, 9 – 22 × 3 – 6.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin finely crenate to serrate, pubescent on both surfaces when very young, soon glabrescent, lateral veins 15 – 30 on each side of midvein. Compound corymbs terminal, 10 – 16 cm in diam., many-flowered, glabrous; pedicels 3 – 5 mm. Flowers 6 – 8 mm in diam.; hypanthium conical, 1 mm; sepals broadly triangular, ca. 1 × 1.5 mm, apex acute or obtuse; petals white, suborbicular to broadly ovate, 3 – 4.5 × 3 –3.5 mm, apex obtuse or emarginate; stamens 16 – 20; ovary 2(–3)-locular, pillose apically; styles 2(–3), 2.5 mm, free, stigmas capitate. Pome globose to ovoid, 5 – 6 mm in diam., red or brownish-purple, 1-seeded.


Locality: Cultivated. J. Lamont s.n. (K).

Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Gansu, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Hebei, Henan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; India, Indonesia, Japan, Philippines.

Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun.– Dec.

Uses: Ornamental.

Phragmites australis (Cav.) Trin. ex Steud. 蘆葦
Nomecl. Bot. ed. 2, 1: 143. 1840; FFJ 6: 129, fig. 100. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 329. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 27, pl. 4: 3, 3a. 2002; FOC 22: 449. 2006; FGD 9: 338, fig. 158. 2009.
Arundo australis Cav., Hist., Nat. 1: 100. 1799.
Arundo phragmites L., Sp. Pl. 81. 1753.
Phragmites communis Trin., Fund. Agrostis 134. 1820; FKH 328. 1912.

Perennial reed, with creeping rhizomes. Culms erect, 1.5–3(–6) m tall, ca. 6 mm in diam., usually farinose below nodes. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate, 15–45(–60) × 1–3.5 cm, smooth or margins scabrous; ligule a minute membranous rim, ca. 1 mm, ciliate, hairs 0.2–0.6 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous or thinly hairy. Panicle 10–40 cm, usually hirsute at axils of lower branches; pedicels 2–4 mm, glabrous or pilose at base. Spikelets 10–20 mm, florets 4–5; glumes lanceolate, 3-veined, lower glume up to 1/2 length of lowest lemma, 3–7 mm; upper glume 5–10 mm, sharply acute, usually apiculate; lowest lemma linear-lanceolate, 8–15 mm; floret callus elongate with hairs equal to lemma; palea 2.5–4 mm, 2-keeled, margins minutely ciliate, apex truncate.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. HK sheet 8663, 16103, 16109.
Distribution: A worldwide weed.
Ecology: Beaches, river banks, margins of ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Environmental (ornamental, erosion control).

Phragmites vallatorius (L.) Veldkamp 卡開蘆
Blumea 37(1): 233. 1992; FTW ed. 2, 5: 332. 2000.

Arundo vallatoria Pluk. ex L., Herb. Amb. 15. 1754.
Phragmites karka (Retz.) Trin. ex Steud., Nomenl. Bot., ed. 2, 1: 144. 1840; FKH 328. 1912; FHN 4: 368. 1977; FFJ 6: 129. 1995; FRPS 9(2): 25, pl. 4: 4, 4a. 2002; FOC 22: 449. 2006; FGD 9: 337. 2009; Check List HK Plants 344. 2002; 120. 2004.
Arundo karka Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 21. 1786.
Phragmites karka (Retz.) Trin. ex Steud. var. cincta Hook. f., Fl. Brit. India 7: 305. 1897; FHN 4: 368. 1977.

Perennial reed, 4–6 m tall, with creeping rhizomes. Culms very stout, woody, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam. Leaf blades linearlanceolate 20–50 × 2–3 cm, base slightly narrowed, apex long acuminate, glabrous; ligule 0.3–1 mm, upper margin ciliolate; leaf sheaths glabrous. Panicle 30–60 × 10–20 cm, copiously branched; branches mostly in whorls, the lowermost branches bare of spikelets toward base, ± glabrous at insertion. Spikelets 9–12 mm, 4–6-flowered, rachilla-hairs 4 – 7 mm, rather sparse; glumes lanceolate-elliptic, obtuse to acuminate, lower glume up to 1/2 length of the upper lowest lemma, 2.5–4 mm, upper glume 4–6 mm; lowest lemma narrowly elliptic, 7–12 mm; bisexual lemmas linear-lanceolate, 8.5–11 mm, apex long attenuate; floret callus elongate with 4–8 mm hairs; palea 3 mm, 2-keeled, margins minutely ciliate, apex truncate.

Locality: Mai Po, Castle Peak, Lin Au, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Soko Islands. Y. W. Lam 1300; HK sheet 40925, 41502.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, N Australia, Pacific islands, Africa.
Ecology: Beaches, river banks, shady roadsides, swamps. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Environmental (ornamental, erosion control).

Phrynium placentarium (Lour.) Merr. 尖苞柊葉
Philip. J. Sci. 15: 230. 1919; FHN 4: 105. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 164. 1981; FGD 2: 439. 1991; FOC 24: 380. 2000.
Phyllodes placentaria Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 13. 1790.

Plant ca. 1 m tall. Leaves basal 1(–2); petiole to 30 cm, pulvinus 2–3 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, oblong-lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 30–55 × ca. 20 cm, glabrous, base rounded with an acute centre, apex acuminate. Inflorescence sessile, composed of 4–5 or more spikelets, globose, 3 – 8 m in diam. Bracts crowded, oblong, 2–2.5 cm, apex with a spinescent acumen. Flowers 2 per bract, white to yellowish white. Sepals linear, ca. 5 mm. Corolla tube ca. 8 mm; lobes elliptic, ca. 5 × 2 mm. Outer staminodes obovate, ca. 5 mm. Ovary glabrous or apically puberulent. Fruits oblong, ca. 1.2 cm; exocarp thin. Seed 1, ellipsoidal, ca. 1 cm; aril red.

Locality: Tai Po. L. T. Lo 426; Y. S. Lau 2840.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.

Phrynium rheedei Suresh & Nicolson 柊葉
Taxon 35: 355. 1986; FOC 24: 380. 2000.
Phrynium capitatum Willd., Sp. Pl. 1: 17. 1797, nom. illeg. (included Pontederia ovata); FHN 4: 105. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 162. 1981; FGD 2: 437. 1991.

Plant ca. 1 m tall, with tuberous rhizomes. Basal leaves several, thinly leathery; petiole to 60 cm, pulvinus 3–7 cm; leaf blade ovate-oblong to oblong, 25–50 × 10–12 cm, base acute, apex shortly acuminate, glabrous. Inflorescence sessile, composed of 4–5 or more spikelets, capitate, ca. 5 cm in diam. Bracts crowded, oblong-lanceolate, 2–3 cm, apex initially acute, shredding into fibers after anthesis. Flowers 3 per bract, sessile. Sepals linear, ca. 1 cm, sericeous. Corolla tube violet, shorter than calyx; lobes dark red, oblong-obovate. Outer staminodes light red, obovate, slightly corrugated; cucullate and callose staminodes yellowish, shorter than outer staminodes. Ovary sericeous. Fruit dark red, shining, pyriform, ca. 1 cm, slightly 3-angled; exocarp hard. Seeds 2–3, shallowly grooved.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. HK sheet 42839.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Wet and shaded places in forests. Flowering: May–Jul.

Phyla nodiflora (L.) Greene 過江藤
Pittonia 4(20E): 46. 1899; FTW 4: 427. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 19, fig. 5. 1982; FFJ 4: 520, fig. 413. 1989; FOC 17: 3. 1994; FGD 3: 344, fig. 225. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 421, photo. 252. 1998.
Verbena nodiflora L., Sp. Pl. 1: 20. 1753.
Lippia nodiflora (L.) Michx., Fl. Bor.‑Amer. 2: 15. 1803; FKH 201. 1912; FGZ 623. 1956; FHN 4: 4, fig. 945. 1977.
Phyla chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 66. 1790.

Perennial herb, multibranched. Branches many, creeping, rooting at distal nodes, minutely strigose. Leaves subsessile; leaf blade papery, spatulate, obovate to oblanceolate, 1–3 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex obtuse, margin distally sharply serrate, pubescent. Spikes cylindric to ovoid, 0.5–3 × 0.6 cm. Peduncle 1– 7 cm. Bracts broadly ovate, ca. 3 mm wide. Calyx ca. 2 mm. Corolla pinkish purple or white, glabrous. Stamens inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Capsules pale yellow, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Shek O, Mount Kellet, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Long Sai Wan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 658, 2582; Y. W. Lam 777.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guizhou, Hainan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Taiwan, Xizang, Yunnan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Grasslands, along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phyllanthus acidus (L.) Skeels 酸果葉下珠

U.S.D.A. Bur. Pl. Industr. Bull. 148: 17. 1909.

Averrhoa acida L., Sp. Pl. 428. 1755.

Cicca acida (L.) Merr., Interpr. Rumph. Herb. Amboin. 314. 1917.


Small tree, up to 10 m tall; branchlets slender, glabrous. Leaves distichous, borne on deciduous branchlets resembling pinnate leaves; stipules triangular-acuminate, 0.8–1.2 × 0.5–0.8 mm, entire or denticulate-fimbriate; petioles 2–3 mm; leaf blade papery, broadly ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–9 × 2–4.5 cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex acute, mucronate, olive-green adaxially, glaucous abaxially; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Flowers mostly borne on short leafless branchlets of the thick older stems; cymules many-flowered, with 1–9 female flowers accompanied by 25–40 males in each cymule. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 1.3–3 mm; sepals 4, subequal, elliptic to suborbicular, 1.1–1.4 × 0.8–1.4 mm, entire, apex rounded or obtuse; stamens 4, filaments free. Female flowers: pedicels straight, terete and rather stout; sepals 4, subequal, triangular-ovate or elliptic, 1–1.4 × 1–1.3 mm, base thickened, apex obtuse or rounded, entire; staminodes sometimes persistent; ovaries pyriform, smooth, shallowly 3–4-lobed; styles very shortly connate into a column, deeply bilobed. Drupes derpressed-globose, 2–2.5 cm in diam., 6–8-furrowed.


Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 24288.

Distribution: Native to Brazil; cultivated or naturalized in tropical and subtropical areas.

Ecology: Flowering: Jan. – Jul.

Uses: Food (beverage base, fruit), ornamental.

Phyllanthus cochinchinensis (Lour.) Spreng. 越南葉下珠（鐵包金）
Syst. Veg. 3: 21. 1826; FRPS 44(1): 96, pl. 28: 7 – 11. 1994; FGD 5: 50. 2003.
Cathetus cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 608. 1790.
Phyllanthus cinerascens Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 211. 1837; FHK 311. 1861; FKH 235. 1912.

Shrub up to 3 m tall, much branched; branchlets slender, yellowish-brown-pubescent when young, glabrous in age. Leaves leathery, distichous or 3–5-fasciculate on short branches; stipules ovate-triangular, ca. 2 mm, ciliate; petioles 1–2 mm; leaf blade obovate, oblong-obovate or spatulate, 1–2 × 0.6–1.3 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, rarely retuse; lateral veins obscure. Flowers dioecious or monoecious, solitary or 2–3 in axillary fascicles, with many bracts; bracts membranous, yellow-brown, margin fimbriate. Male flowers: usually solitary, pedicels ca. 3 mm; sepals 6, obovate or spatulate, ca. 1.3 × 1–1.2 mm, margin membranous, thicker at base; anthers 3, oblong, diverging from a thick central column; disk-glands 6, obconical. Female flowers: 1–2 together, pedicels 2–3 mm; sepals 6, ovate or ovate-rhombic, 1.5–1.8 × 1.5 mm, margin membranous, thicker at base; disk thick, annular, truncate; ovary globose, ca. 1.2 mm in diam., 3-locular, styles 3, 1.1 mm, united to middle, each with 2 recurved lobes. Capsules globose, ca. 5 mm in diam.; seeds minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1784; L. T. Lo 145; S. P. Lau 163.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, India.
Ecology: Thin forests, shrublands, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Phyllanthus emblica L. 餘甘子（油甘子）
Sp. Pl. 982. 1753; FHK 312. 1861; FKH 235. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 87, pl. 23: 1 – 5. 1994; FGD 5: 49. 2003.
Emblica officinalis Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 122, pl. 108. 1791.

Tree or shrub, up to 10 m tall; branchlets tawny pubescent. Leaves papery or leathery, distichous; stipules triangular, 0.8–1.5 mm, ciliate; petioles 0.3–0.7 mm; leaf blade oblong or linear-oblong. 8–20 × 2–6 mm, base shallowly cordate and slightly oblique, apex truncate, rounded or obtuse, mucronate or retuse at the tip, green adaxially, greenish abaxially, reddish or brownish when dry; lateral veins 4–7 pairs. Flowers in axillary cymes, 3–7-flowered, usually with only one female flower in each cyme. Male flowers: pedicels 1–2.5 mm; sepals 6, membranous, yellow, obovate or spatulate, 1.2–2.5 × 0.5–1 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, margins entire or denticulate; stamens 3, filaments coherent into a central column, anthers erect, oblong, 0.5–0.9 mm, apex mucronate. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 0.5 mm; sepals 6, oblong or spatulate, 1.6–2.5 × 0.7–1.3 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, thicker, margins membranous, apex ± lobed; ovaries ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3, connate at base, apex deeply bilobed. Fruit a drupe, globose, 1–1.3 cm in diam., epicarp fleshy, pale green or yellowish-white, endocarp crustaceous; seeds reddish, 5–6 × 2–3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 933, 1152; Y. W. Lam 1055; S. Y. Hu 5211 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi,Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Philippines, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia.
Ecology: Dry and open forests or shrublands. Flowering: Apr. –Jun.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Food (fruit), material (lipids), medicinal (folklore).

Phyllanthus glaucus Wall. ex Müll. Arg. 青灰葉下珠
Linnaea 32: 14. 1863; FRPS 44(1): 85, pl. 22: 4 – 6. 1994; FGD 5: 49. 2003.

Shrub up to 4 m tall, glabrous throughout; branchlets slender. Leaves membranous or thin-papery; petioles 2–4 mm; stipules ovate-lanceolate, membranous; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, 2.5–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex acute, mucronulate, slightly glaucous abaxially; lateral veins 8–10. Flowers 3–7 in axillary clusters, with 1 female and several male flowers in each cluster. Male flowers: pedicels slender, ca. 8 mm; sepals 6, ovate; disk-glands 6; stamens 5, filaments free. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 9 mm; sepals 6, ovate; disk annular; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3, connate at base. Fruit baccate, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., black, with persistent sepals at base.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tap Mun. S. Y. Hu 10524 (CUHK); Hu & But 233234 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sikkim.
Ecology: Lowland forests and shrublands. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phyllanthus leptoclados Benth. 細枝葉下珠（幼枝葉下珠）
FHK 312. 1861; FKH 235. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 112, pl. 32: 6 – 8. 1994; FGD 5: 52. 2003.
Epistylium leptocladon Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 229. 1862.
Phyllanthus glabrocapsulus Metcalf, Lingnan Sci. J. 10: 483. 1931.

Small shrub, 0.2–1 m tall, glabrous except for the branchlets. Branchlets slender and divaricate, the smallest almost filiform, with a line of glandular short hairs on one side. Leaves membranous; stipules lanceolate or linear lanceolate. inserted bilaterally at the base of petioles; petioles ca. 1 mm; leaf blade obliquely ovate or oblong, 6–13 × 4–7 mm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex initially with a short (1.5–3 mm) tail, later the tails fallen off, and the apex becoming acute or obtuse, glaucous abaxially; lateral veins ca. 5 pairs. Flowers monoecious. Male flowers: solitary, axillary; pedicels to 1 cm; sepals 4, oblong-ovate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, apex acute, margins lacerate serrate; disk-glands 4, rotund, truncate at apex; stamens 2, on the top of a short central column. Female flowers: pedicels to 1.5 cm; sepals 6, lanceolate, margins lacerate serrate; disk annular, truncate, entire or lobed; ovaries globose, smooth, styles 3, free, spreading, divided into 2 slender lobes. Capsules oblate, ca. 5 mm in diam.; seeds minutely tuberculate.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. HK sheet 5397.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian,Yunnan.
Ecology: Montane shrublands. Flowering: May– Sep.; fruiting: Jun. –Nov.
Notes: One of the two syntype specimens (C. Wright 479, GH) was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 to 1856.

Phyllanthus maderaspatensis L. 麻德拉斯葉下珠

Sp. Pl. 982. 1753; FHK 311. 1861; FKH 234. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 89. 1994.


Shrub up to 1.5 m tall, much branched, glabrous throughout; branches slender, ± quadrangular, glaucous when young. Leaves papery; stipules membranous, linear-lanceolate; petioles 1–1.5 mm; leaf blade obovate, or cuneate-oblong, 2 × 0.4–0.5 cm, base cuneate, apex mucronate. Flowers nearly sessile, in axillary fascicles, with one male and 2–3 female flowers in each fascicle. Male flowers: 1.2 mm in diam.; sepals 5, obovate; disk-glands 5, rotund, free; stamens 3, nearly sessile on an almost globular column. Female flowers: 2.5 mm in diam.; sepals 5, obovate; disk-glands 5, oblong, free; ovary globose, 3-locular; styles 3, free bifid at apex. Capsules globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., smooth; seeds very minutely tuberculate or almost smooth.


Locality: Cultivated. J. G. Champion s.n. (K).

Distribution: S Guangdong; India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Australia, Africa.

Ecology: Montane shrublands. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Phyllanthus myrtifolius (Wight) Müll. Arg. 瘤腺葉下珠
Prodr. 15(2): 396. 1866; FRPS 44(1): 95. 1994; FGD 5: 50. 2003.
Macraea myrtifolia Wight, Icon. Pl. Ind. Orient. t. 1902, fig. 2. 1852.

Shrub, ca. 50 cm tall; branchlets puberulous. Leaves leathery, distichous; stipules small, ovate; petioles very short; ca. 1 mm; leaf blade oblanceolate, 12–16 × 3.5–4.5 mm, base shallowly cordate, apex acute or obtuse; lateral veins numerous, nearly parallel. Flowers minute, ca. 3 mm in diam., male and female together in axillary fascicles; pedicels filiform, 3–5 mm. Male flowers: sepals 5, oblong; stamens 3, filaments connate up to middle; anthers 2-celled; disk-glands 5, tubercular. Female flowers: sepals 6, larger than in male flower; disk cup-shaped, entire; ovary globose, 3-locular; styles 3, shortly bilobed, lobes recurved. Capsules oblate, 2 × 3mm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34796.
Distribution: Native to Sri Lanka; cultivated in Taiwan, Hainan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Phyllanthus niruri L. 珠子草
Sp. Pl. 981. 1753; FHK 311. 1861; FKH 234. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 101, pl. 26: 1 – 5. 1994; FGD 5: 47. 2003.

Annual herb, much branched, up to 50 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves thin papery, distichous; stipules lanceolate or triangular; petioles ca. 0.5 mm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic-oblong, 3–10 × 2 – 5 mm, base rounded, apex obtuse or rounded and often apiculate; lateral veins 4–7 pairs, obscure adaxially, slightly conspicuous abaxially. Flowers solitary or in axillary pairs, often the female flowers on the upper part and the males on the lower part of the branchlets. Male flowers: pedicels 0.5–1 mm; sepals 5, obovate, broadly ovate, 1.2–1.5 × 1–1.5 mm, base reddish, apex obtuse or rounded, yellow-green; disk-glands 5, obovate; stamens 3, anthers nearly globose, on a central column. Female flowers: pedicels 1.5–4 mm; sepals 5, inaequilateral, broadly elliptic or obovate, 1.5–2.3 × 1.2–1.8 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, green, margin membranous and yellow-white; disk discoid; ovary globose, smooth, 3-locular; styles 3, free, bilobed, lobes revolute. Capsules oblate, ca. 3 mm in diam., brown-red, smooth; seeds 1–1.5 × 0.8–1.2 mm, marked with longitudinal striae.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. HK sheet 27028.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi,Yunnan, Taiwan; a common weed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa and some parts of tropical America.
Ecology: Sunny places, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phyllanthus reticulatus Poir. 小果葉下珠（爛頭砵）

Lam., Encycl. Meth. 5: 198. 1804; FRPS 44(1): 82, pl. 22: 1 – 2. 1994; FGD 5: 48, fig. 29. 2003.

Cicca microcarpa Benth., FHK 312. 1861.


Shrub to 4 m tall; branchlets slender, initially yellowish pubescent or puberulous glabrescent. Leaves membranous or papery; petioles 2– 5 mm; stipules triangular-lanceolate, 1.7 mm; leaf blade very variable in shape, mostly elliptic to ovate, 1 – 5.5 × 0.7 – 3 cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex acute, obtuse or rounded; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, usually prominent on both surfaces. Flowers usually in axillary clusters, with 2 – 10 male flowers and 1 – 2 female flowers in each cluster. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 5 – 10 mm; sepals 5 – 6, in 2 series, ovate or obovate, unequal, 0.7 – 1.5 × 0.5 – 1.2 mm, entire; stamens 5, erect, in two sets: three with longer filaments coherent in a central column, two with shorter filaments, free; anthers triangular; disk-glands 5, scale-like. Female flowers: pedicels slender, 4–8 mm; sepals 5 –6, in 2 series, unequal, broad-ovate, 1 – 1.6 × 0.9 – 1.2 mm, puberulous inside at base; disk-glands 5 – 6, oblong or obovate; ovary 4–12-locular, smooth, styles free, bifid at apex, lobes linear, revolute and connivent over the top of the ovary. Fruit baccate, globose to oblate, ca. 4 – 6 mm across, black with dark purplish when mature.


Locality: Pok Fu Lam Rd., Stubbs Rd., Deep Water Bay, Lam Tsuen, Ma On Shan, Tai O, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2263, 2287; Y. S. Lau 2688; S. Y. Hu 5233, 5730 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, India, Sri Lanka, Queensland,W Africa.

Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Oct.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phyllanthus urinaria L. 葉下珠（珍珠草）
Sp. Pl. 2: 982. 1753; FHK 310. 1861; FKH 234. 1912; FRPS 44(1): 93, pl. 26: 6 – 8. 1994; FGD 5: 46. 2003.
Phyllanthus cantoniensis Hornem., Enum. Pl. Hort. Hafn. (Revised ed.) 29. 1807.

Annual herb; stems slightly compressed, erect or decumbent at base, up to 80 cm tall; branchlets puberulous. Leaves thin papery, distichous; stipules ovate-lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm, conspicuously auriculate at base; petioles very short; leaf blade oblong to oblong-obovate or nearly linear, sometimes slightly falcate, 4–10 × 2–5 mm, base mostly obtuse and sometimes conspicuously asymmetrical, apex rounded, obtuse or acute, mucronulate, hispidulous near the margin on abaxial surface; lateral veins 4–5 pairs, conspicuous. Flowers minute, almost sessile, 2–4 in axillary fascicles; the females solitary, the males 2 or 3 together; sepals 6, yellowish-white, ovate in the males, narrower in the females; stamens 3, anthers on a central column; styles 3, free, bilobed, lobes revolute. Capsules depressed-globose, 2–2.5 mmin diam., with reddish blotches and scurfy-tuberculate; seeds triangular, 1–1.2 × 0.9–1 mm, light greyish-brown, with 12–15 sharp-transverse ridges on the back and sides.

Locality: Happy Valley, Harlech Rd., Pok Fu Lam Reservior Rd., Stubbs Rd., Ling Nam San Tsuen, Kowloon Reservoir, Fanling, Sha Tin, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 121, 1920; L. T. Lo 320; S. Y. Hu 10694 (CUHK).
Distribution: Area S of Qingling; widely spread over tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Sunny places, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phyllanthus ussuriensis Rupr. & Maxim. 蜜甘草

Bull. Cl. Phys.-Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg Ser. 3, 15: 222. 1857; FRPS 44(1): 107, pl. 25: 10–12. 1994.

Phyllanthus simplex Retz. var. chinensis Müll. Arg., Linnaea 32: 33. 1863.


Annual herb, glabrous throughout; stems erect, up to 60 cm tall, usually branched at base; branchlets slender, angular. Leaves papery; stipules ovate-lanceolate; petioles very short; leaf blade elliptic to oblong, 5–15 × 3–6 mm, base rotund, apex acute to obtuse, white-green abaxially; lateral veins 5–6 pairs. Flowers solitary or several in axillary fascicles. Male flowers: sepals 4, broad-ovate; disk-glands 4, free, alternating with sepals; stamens 2, filaments free. Female flowers: sepals 6, oblong-elliptic, reflexed in fruit; disk-glands 6, oblong; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3, bifid. Capsules oblate, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., smooth; fruiting pedicels short; seeds ca. 1.2 mm in diam., brown-tuberculate.


Locality: Deep Water Bay, Fanling, Sha Tin. Y. W. Lam 672; W. J. Tutcher 9959; HK sheet 5380; S. Y. Hu 7839 (CUHK); Hu & But 20943, 22308, 22732 (CUHK).

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE. Russia, Mongolia, Korea, Japan.

Ecology: Grassy slopes, wastelands or roadsides. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul. – Oct.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phyllanthus virgatus G. Forst. 黃珠子草

Fl. Ins. Austr. 65. 1786; FRPS 44(1): 91, pl. 25: 5 – 9. 1994; FGD 5: 47, fig. 28. 2003.

Phyllanthus simplex Retz., Obs. Bot. 5: 29. 1789; FKH 234. 1912.

Phyllanthus anceps auct. non Willd.: FHK 311. 1861; FKH 234. 1912.


Annual herb, glabrous throughout; stems erect or decumbent, 15–60(–100) cm tall, much branched; branchlets ± flat, with acute angles. Leaves papery to sub-leathery, distichous; stipules membranous; petioles very short, ca. 1 mm; leaf blade linear-lanceolate, oblong or narrow-elliptic, 5–25 × 2–7 mm, base rounded and slightly oblique, apex obtuse or acute; midvein flattened adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins obscure on both surfaces. Flowers in axillary fascicles, usually 2–4 male flowers and one female flower per fascicle. Male flowers: pedicels ca. 2 mm; sepals 6, broad-ovate or rotund, ca. 0.5 mm; stamens 3, filaments free; disk-glands 6, oblong. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 5 mm; sepals 6, ovate-oblong, ca. 1 mm; disk orbicular; ovary globose, 3-locular, with elevated scales, rarely smooth; styles 3, bilobed nearly to base. Capsules oblate, 2–3 mm in diam., purple, with smooth or glandular; fruiting pedicels 5–12 mm; seeds small, 0.5 mm in diam., finely warty.


Locality: Wong Nai Hang, Sha Tin, Tuen Mun, Ping Chau. L. T. Lo 321; P. S. Choi 373; Y. W. Lam 997.

Distribution: Hebei, Shaanxi, Shanxi and E, C, S & SWChina; India, Indochina and throughout Malaysia to Polynesia.

Ecology: Grassy slopes, mixed forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phyllodium elegans (Lour.) Desv. 毛排錢草

Mem. Soc. Linn. Paris 4: 324. 1825; FRPS 41: 12. 1995; FGD 5: 265. 2003.

Hedysarum elegans Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 450. 1790.

Desmodium elegans (Lour.) Benth., FHK 83. 1861, non DC. (1825) nec Schlecht. (1838); FKH 79. 1912.


Shrub, 0.5 –1.5 m tall. Stems, branchlets and petioles densely yellow-villous. Leaves 3-foliolate; terminal leaflets ovate or rhomboid, 7–10 × 3–4 cm, lateral ones obliquely ovate, smaller, densely villous on both surfaces, margin repand, lateral veins 9 –10 pairs, pinnately branched reaching margin. Umbels 4 – 9-flowered, enclosed in leafy bracts, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Calyx campanulate, 3–4 mm, grey-white-pubescent. Corolla white or greenish; vexillum oblong, 6–7 × 3–4 mm, base obscurely clawed; wings linear, 5–6 × 1 mm, base auriculate and clawed; keel 7 – 8 mm, clawed. Stamens monadelphous. Ovary sessile, linear, hairy. Pods 10 – 12 × 3–4 mm, ventral suture straight or repand, dorsal suture undulate, 3 – 4-jointed; joints suborbicular, flat.


Locality: Kowloon Reservoir, Shing Mun, Yuen Tun Ha, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Fanling, Sha Tau Kok. H. C. Tang 1049; Y. S. Lau 1677, 2310.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.

Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Jul. –Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Phyllodium pulchellum (L.) Desv. 排錢草

Mem. Soc. Linn. Paris 4: 324. 1826; FRPS 41: 11. 1995; FGD 5: 264, fig. 143. 2003.

Hedysarum pulchellum L., Sp. Pl. 747. 1753.

Desmodium pulchellum (L.) Benth., FHK 83. 1861; FKH 79. 1912.


Shrub, 0.5 – 1.5 m tall. Branchlets white or grey pubescent. Leaves 3-foliolate; terminal leaflets ovate, elliptic or obovate, 6–12 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex obtuse or acute, lateral ones smaller, base oblique, margin repand, subglabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 6 – 10 pairs, reticulate at the leaf margins. Umbels 5 –6-flowered, enclosed in leafy bracts, forming terminal panicles; leafy bracts orbicular, 1.5 cm in diam., pubescent and ciliate. Calyx white or yellowish. Petals clawed; vexillum 5 –6 mm, base attenuate; wings linear, 5 × 1 mm, base auriculate; keel 6 × 2 mm, auriculate. Stamens monadelphous. Ovary sessile, linear. Pods oblong, 6 × 2.5 mm, margin ciliate, slightly constricted on both suture; joints 2, ciliate at edges only.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1675; L. T. Lo 147; HK sheet 39273.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.

Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Jul. – Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Phyllostachys aurea Carrière ex Rivière & C. Rivière 人面竹
Bull. Soc. Natl. Acclim. France, sér. 3. 5: 716. 1878; FTW 5: 723, pl. 1489. 1978; HKB 67. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 255, pl. 67: 5–7. 1996; FOC 22: 168. 2006; FGD 9: 319, fig. 150. 2009.
Phyllostachys bambusoides Siebold & Zucc. var. aurea (Carrière ex Rivière & C. Rivière) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 11: 158. 1897.
Phyllostachys breviligula W. T. Lin & Z. M. Wu, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(3): 229, pl. 8. 1988.
Phyllostachys formosana Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form. 6: 140. 1916.
Phyllostachys reticulata (Ruprecht) K. Koch var. aurea (Carrière ex Rivière & C. Rivière) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 26: 22. 1912.

Culms 5–12 m, 2–5 cm in diam.; internodes 15–30 cm, usually strongly shortened and commonly ventricose at basal nodes, distally inflated for several minimetres below node at mid-culm and basal nodes, initially white powdery, glabrous; wall 4 – 8 mm thick; nodal ridge as prominent as sheath scar or slightly more prominent; sheath scar initially fringed with white pubescence. Culm sheaths yellowgreen or pale red-brown, becoming straw-coloured, with variably sized brown spots, base edged with white pubescence; auricles and oral setae absent; ligule yellow-green, truncate or weakly convex at apex, very short, 1–2 mm, margin longer pale green ciliate; blade reflexed, green, with yellow margins, linear, flat or crinkled in upper sheaths. Leaves 2–3 per ultimate branch; sheath glabrous; auricles and oral setae absent or deciduous; ligule short; blade 6–12 × 1–1.8 cm, abaxially pilose especially near petiole.

Locality: Kadoorie Farm (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2874.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Uses: Ornamental.

Phyllostachys reticulata (Rupr.) K. Koch 桂竹
Dendrologie. 2(2): 356. 1873; FOC 22: 176. 2006; FGD 9: 322. 2009.
Bambusa reticulata Rupr., Bambuseae, 58. 1839.
Phyllostachys bambusoides Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 3(3): 746, pl. 5, fig. 3. 1843; FTW 5: 725, pl. 1490. 1978; HKB 68. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 292. 1996; Check List HK Plants 344. 2002; 120. 2004.
Phyllostachys lithophila Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6: 141, fig. 51. 1916.
Phyllostachys megastachya Steud., Flora 29: 21. 1846.
Phyllostachys pinyanensis T. H. Wen, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 2(1): 67, fig. 6. 1982.
Phyllostachys quilioi Rivière & C. Rivière, Bull. Soc. Natl. Acclim. France 5: 697, fig. 24 – 27. 1878.

Culms to 20 m, to ca. 15 cm in diam.; internodes to 40 cm, not white powdery or initially faintly so below nodes, glabrous; wall ca. 5 mm thick; nodal ridge slightly more prominent than sheath scar. Culm sheaths yellow-brown, sometimes tinged with green or purple, with dense, variably sized, purple-brown spots, glabrous or sparsely deciduously erectly brown hairy; auricles deciduous, sometimes absent, purple-brown, small to large and falcate; oral setae radiate; ligule brown or green, arcuate, ciliate; blade reflexed, green in centre, purple or brown on both sides, pale yellow along margins, linear, flat or sometimes slightly wavy at apex. Leaves 2–4 per ultimate branch; auricles suborbicular; oral setae well developed, radiate; ligule obviously exserted, arcuate or sometimes truncate; blade 5.5–15 × 1.5–2.5 cm. Flowering branchlets spicate, 5–8(–10) cm, scaly bracts 3–5; spathes 6–8; auricles small or inconspicuous, oral setae usually developed, blade orbicular-ovate to linear-lanceolate, base rounded, apex subulate-acuminate. Pseudospikelets 1–2(–3) per spathe, absent from basal 1–3 deciduous spathes. Spikelets lanceolate, 2.5–3 cm; florets 1–2(–3). Glumes absent or 1; rachilla pubescent, extension glabrous, terminated with a rudimentary floret; lemma 2–2.5 cm, sparsely puberulent, apex aristulate-acuminate; palea slightly shorter than lemma, glabrous except for keels or pubescent at apex; lodicules rhomboid-oblong, 3.5–4 cm. Anthers 1.1–1.4 cm. Stigmas 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2877; S. C. Lau 760; HK sheet 16404.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Shaanxi, Shandong, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: New shoots: Late May.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (construction, flooring and furniture).

Phyllostachys nidularia Munro 篌竹（白筍竹、花竹）
Gard. Chron., n.s., 6: 773. 1876; FKH 330. 1912; FRPS 9(1): 304. 1996; FOC 22: 178. 2006; FGD 9: 324, fig. 152. 2009.
Phyllostachys cantoniensis W. T. Lin, J. S. China Agric. Univ. 14(3): 112, fig. 4. 1993.
Phyllostachys subulata W. T. Lin & Z. M. Wu, J. Bamboo Res. 13(2): 16, fig. 2. 1994.

Culms to 10 m, to 4 cm in diam., straight; internodes to 30 cm, white powdery, glabrous or initially setulose below nodes; wall ca. 3 mm or more thick; nodal ridge conspicuously elevated, equaling or more prominent than sheath scar; sheath scar flared, glabrous or initially with margin brown setose. Culm sheaths green, unmarked, distally milky-white striped, otherwise usually purple striped, white powdery, densely brown strigose toward base or glabrous, margins purple-red or brown ciliate; auricles at culm apex green-purple, very broad, contiguous with and extending from swollen cupped base of blade; auricles absent on mid- and lower culm; oral setae absent or few, radiate, short; ligule purplebrown, slightly arcuate, broad, margin densely white ciliate; blade erect, broadly triangular to triangular, cupped. Leaves usually 1 per ultimate branch, pendulous; auricles and oral setae weakly developed or absent; ligule short, weakly or not exserted; blade 4–13 × 1–2 cm. Flowering branchlets densely capitate, 1.5–2 cm, scaly bracts 2–4; spathes 1–6, basal ones ovate, distal ones narrower and papery, to 1.6 cm, both sides and apex ± hairy, margins ciliate, blade inconspicuous to narrowly ovate. Pseudospikelets 2 – 8 per spathe; bracts narrow, variable in size or sometimes absent, membranous, keeled, 5–7-veined, pubescent on keels and near apex. Spikelets with 2–5 florets, distal 1–2 sterile. Glumes 1(–3), resembling uppermost bract, to 1.5 cm; rachilla internodes elevated, compressed and sparsely pubescent on side facing floret, apex truncate; lemma leafy, densely hirsute, many-veined, apex acuminate with an awn-like tip, 1st lemma 1–1.2(–1.6) cm; palea shorter than lemma, 0.6–1.1 cm, densely hirsute. Anthers 4.5–5.5 mm. Stigmas (1–)3.

Locality: Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Mau Ping, Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Nan-Zhu 2773, 2865; HK sheet 16421.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Shaanxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang; introduced in Europe and N America.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. New shoots: Apr.–May; flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Vegetable (shoots), ornamental.

Phyllostachys nigra (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Munro 紫竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 38. 1868; FTW 5: 730, pl. 1493. 1978; HKB 71. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 288. 1996; FOC 22: 175. 2006; FGD 9: 321. 2009.
Bambusa nigra Lodd. ex Lindl., Penny Cyclop. 3: 357. 1835.
Phyllostachys filifera McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 42. 1940.
Phyllostachys nana Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. 36: 441. 1904.
Phyllostachys nigripes Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form. 6: 142, fig. 53. 1916.

Culms 4–8(–10) m, to 5 cm or more in diam.; initially green, gradually developing purple-brown or brown-black spots and patches, or finally becoming uniformly purple-brown or brown-black, 25–30 cm, initially white powdery, densely puberulent; wall ca. 3 mm thick; nodal ridge slightly more prominent than or equaling sheath scar; sheath scar initially brown hairy on margin. Culm sheaths redbrown, sometimes tinged with green, unmarked or densely extremely minutely and imperceptibly dark brown spotted, spots aggregating into a distal dark brown patch, thinly white powdery, brown strigose; auricles and oral setae well developed, purple-black; ligule purple, arcuate to acutely so, long ciliate; blade erect or gradually deflexed, green or tinged with purple on both sides, triangular to triangularlanceolate, navicular, ± wavy. Leaves 2–3 per ultimate branch; auricles weak or absent; oral setae deciduous; ligule slightly exserted; blade thin, 7–10 × ca. 1.2 cm. Flowering branchlets shortly spicate, 3.5–5 cm, scaly bracts 4–8. Spathes 4–6, glabrous or puberulous; auricles absent; oral setae few or absent; blade usually subulate or ovate-lanceolate, small. Pseudospikelets 1–3 per spathe. Spikelets lanceolate, 1.5–2 cm; florets 2–3. Glumes (absent or)1–3, abaxially ± distally pubescent; rachilla pubescent; lemma 1.2–1.5 cm, densely pubescent; palea shorter than lemma. Anthers ca. 8 mm. Stigmas 3.

Locality: Lung Tsai Ng Yuen (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2794; N. K. Chun 2840; HK sheet 35371.
Distribution: S Hunan, cultivated elsewhere in China.
Ecology: New shoots: late Apr.; flowering: May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Physalis angulata L. 苦蘵
Sp. Pl. 183. 1753; FHK 244. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 56, pl. 15: 3–4. 1978; FGD 2: 366, fig. 249: 1–4. 1991; FOC 17: 312. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 560, pl. 255, photo 298. 1998.

Annual herbs. 30–50 cm tall, much branched, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, oblong or almost lanceolate, 3–6 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire or with a few coarse irregular teeth, almost glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves; pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx campanulate, 4–5 mm, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes lanceolate, as are the pedicels sparsely and shortly pubescent. Corolla 4–8 mm, pale yellow, often marked with 5 purple spots near the throat, shallowly 5‑lobed; limb 6–8 mm in diam. Stamens 5; anthers blue‑purple or yellow. Fruiting calyx globular, 1.5–2.5 in diam., papery, pale green. Berry globose, ca. 1.2 cm in diam., completely enclosed by the persistent calyx.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Mai Po, Tai Po. P. S. Choi 415; Y. W. Lam 2210; HK sheet 35170.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical and subtropical region.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Phytolacca acinosa Roxb. 商陸
Fl. Ind. 2: 458. 1832; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 21. 1886; FGD 2: 94, fig. 65. 1991; FOC 5: 435. 2003.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout, with thick, conical tap root. Stems branched, green or reddish, 1–1.5 m tall. Petioles 1.5 –3 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic or oblong, 12–25 × 4 –10 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire. Racemes terminal and lateral, often opposite to leaves, 3 –15 cm, more or less erect; bracts linear-lanceolate. Pedicels slender, ca. 6 mm. Perianth-segments usually 5, cream or greenish, becoming pink or reddish in fruit, 2–3 mm. Stamens 8 –10; anthers pink; carpels 8–10, distinct; styles separate. Fruit compressed-spherical, purplish to black, with 8 –10 fused fruitlets.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 515; HK sheet 23274, 33267.
Distribution: Dispersed over most parts of China except Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Nei Mongol and Xinjiang; Korea, Japan, India.
Ecology: Cultivated, sometimes escaped from cultivation, in waste places near villages. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phytolacca americana L. 美洲商陸
Sp. Pl. 1: 441. 1753; FGD 2: 95. 1991; FRPS 26: 19, pl. 3: 6–7. 1996.
Phytolacca decandra L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 631. 1763.

Perennial herbs, with thick, conical root. Stems erect, sometimes reddish purple, terete, 1–15 m tall. Petiole 1– 4 cm; leaf blade elliptic-ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 10 –30 × 5 –16 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate and mucronate, margin entire. Racemes terminal or lateral, 10 –15 cm. Pedicel 6 – 8 mm. Flowers ca. 6 mm in diam. Perianth-segments 5, white, slightly red. Stamens, carpels, and styles 10; carpels connate. Infructescence pendulous. Fruit purple-black when mature, oblate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 731; HK sheet 32242.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Taiwan; native to N America; widely naturalized in Asia and Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal, ornamental.

Picrasma quassioides (D. Don) Benn. 苦樹
Pl. Jav. Rar. 198. 1844; FHK 61. 1861; FKH 12. 1912; FYN 1: 190, pl. 44: 8 – 10. 1977; FFJ 2: 380. 1985; FGD 1: 231, fig. 257. 1987; FRPS 43(3): 7. 1997.
Simaba quassioides D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nep. 248. 1825.

Deciduous tree, up to 10 m tall, dioecious; bark purplish brown, smooth. Leaves 15–30 cm; stipules lanceolate, caducous; petiolules 1–4 mm; leaflets 9–15, blade ovate-lanceolate or broadly ovate, (4–)7–12 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, oblique except for the terminal leaflet, apex acuminate, margin irregularly coarse-serrate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent along midvein or lateral veins when young abaxially; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein. Thyrses axillary, to 12 cm; rachis densely puberulous. Sepals (4–)5, small, ovate or oblong. Petals as many as sepals, ovate or broadly ovate. Stamens twice as long as petals in males, shorter than petals in females, opposite to sepals. Disk (4–)5-lobed. Carpels 4–5. Drupe ovoid, greyish black when mature, 6–8 × 5–7 mm, with persistent and enlarged sepals.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1586; N. H. Li 29; HK sheet 39973.
Distribution: Area S of Yellow River; N India, Bhutan, Nepal, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Picria felterrae Lour. 苦玄參
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 393. 1790; FHN 3: 504. 1974; FOC 18: 29. 1998; FGD 4: 384. 2000.

Herbs, to 1 m tall, rooting from lower nodes. Petioles 0.5 – 2 cm; leaf blade ovate to sometimes suborbicular, to 5.5 × 3 cm, base cuneate, rounded, or truncate, margin crenate‑serrate, abaxially hispid on veins, adaxially short hispid; lateral veins 4 or 5 on each side of midvein. Racemes 4 – 8‑flowered. Pedicels to 1 cm. Sepals oblong‑ovate, to 1.4 × 1 cm in fruit, veins conspicuously reticulate; lower and upper sepals enlarged in fruit, 2 lateral ones linear. Corolla red‑brown, ca. 1.2 cm; tube ca. 6.5 mm, constricted at middle; limb strongly 2‑lipped; lower lip ca. 6.5 mm, upper lip erect, ca. 4.5 mm. Anterior stamens 2, reduced, posterior stamens 2, fertile. Capsules ovoid, 5 – 6 mm. Seeds numerous.

Locality: Fung Yuen. Y. W. Lam 872, 873; HK sheet 38610.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Indochina, Thailand, Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy fields. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Pieris swinhoei Hemsl. 長萼馬醉木
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 17. 1889; FKH 154. 1912; FGD 1: 301, fig. 321. 1987; FRPS 57(3): 27, pl. 7: 9 –12. 1991; FOC 14: 461. 2005.

Shrub, evergreen, 1.2(–3) m tall. Branchlets slender, shortly pubescent. Leaves and spirally arranged, crowded towards the nodes of branches. Petiole 3–6 mm, shortly pubescent, ± swollen at the base; leaf blade leathery, narrow elliptic to oblong oblanceolate, 4.5–13 × 0.6–1.5 cm, base attenuate, ± decurrent, apex acute, often with a blunt to sharp point, margin serrulated above middle, glabrous to sparsely puberulent on both surfaces, lateral veins almost in right angle with the midvein. Inflorescences terminal, single to several, racemose or paniculate, erect, 10–15(–20) cm, shortly pubescent, 20–30-flowered. Pedicels 3–4(–7) mm, shortly pubescent. Calyx-lobes lanceolate 5–6 × 2–2.5 mm, thick papery, pubescent adaxially, puberulent abaxially. Corolla tubular-urceolate, 7–9 mm; lobes broadly triangular, 1–2 mm. Stamens 10; filaments ca. 3.5 mm, flat, geniculate at top, 5.5–7.5 mm; filaments puberulent at base. Ovary conical to subglobous, densely pubescent; style ca. 7.5 mm, glabrous, base sunken into apex of ovary. Capsule ovoid, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Localities: Shing Mun. HK sheet 16851; IBSC sheet 53317.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The above cited specimens are probably duplicates of a single collection from Shing Mun in 1931. The author has not yet noticed this species in the wild.

Ornamental.
Notes: The above cited specimens are probably duplicates of a single collection from Shing Mun in 1931. The author has not yet noticed this species in the wild.

records.text:
Pilea aquarum Dunn subsp. acutidentata C. J. Chen 銳齒濕生冷水花
Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 60. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 90. 1995; FOC 5: 102. 2003; FGD 6: 94. 2005.

Perennial herb, 30 –70 cm tall. Stems fleshy, puberulent or subglabrous. Leaves unequal on the same pairs, membranous when dry; stipules subcordate, 3 – 5 mm, apex acute; petioles 1– 4 cm; leaf blade ovate, 5 –14 × 2.5 –7 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, slightly oblique, apex acute, margin sharply dentate, in dry state adaxial surface dark green, shining, abaxial surface paler, puberulent or subglabrous on both surfaces, trinerved. Male inflorescence cymose-paniculate, 2– 6 cm including peduncle. Female inflorescence cymose, compact or cluster-like, ca. 2 cm. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, elliptic; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil very small. Female flowers: perianth‑segments 3, unequal, in fruiting time the middle one sub-navicular, about half length of the fruit, the lateral 2 much small. Achene subglobose, ca. 0.7 mm, apex slightly oblique, tuberculate.

Locality: Robin's Nest (Sha Tau Kok) (fide Xing et al. 2000).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Ravines, by streams or on other shade places. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Pilea chartacea C. J. Chen 紙質冷水花
Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 63. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 92. 1995; FOC 5: 103. 2003; FGD 6: 96. 2005.

Perennial herb, with creeping rhizomes, glabrous. Stems fleshy, above 30 cm tall, pinkish. Leaves papery; stipules membranous, ovate, ca. 3 mm; petioles 0.7–1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic-lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.2–2.3 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate, margin shallowly serrate, in dry state adaxial surface dark green, sometimes bullate, abaxial surface paler, often with purplish scattered red scaly dots along veins; trinerved. Male cymes shortly pedunculed, 1–1.5 cm; female cymes subsessile, ca. 7 mm across. Male flowers: perianth pink, ca. 2.5 mm in the bud, united at base; segments 4, ovate-oblong; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil coniform. Female flowers: perianth-segments 3, unequal, the middle one ovate-oblong, about one-third length of the fruit, the lateral 2 much smaller; sterile. Achene ovoid, ca. 1 mm, apex slightly oblique, inconspicuously tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11621 (CUHK, PE).
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Ravines, wet shady places. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Tai Mo Shan by S. Y. Hu in 1972.

Pilea glaberrima (Blume) Blume 點乳冷水花
Mus. Bot. 2(4): 54. 1856; Gierson & Long, Fl. Bhutan 1(1): 112. 1983; C. J. Chen, Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 71. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 100. 1995; FOC 5: 105. 2003; FGD 6: 96. 2005.
Urtica glaberrima Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 493. 1826.

Straggling herb or subshrub, stoloniferous, 0.5–1.5 m tall, glabrous. Stems much branched, woody at base. Leaves opposite; stipules triangular, 1–2 mm; petioles 1.5–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, elliptic, oblong-lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–15 × 2.5 –7 cm, base rounded, obtuse or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin shallowly serrate or crenate above middle, sometimes subentire; trinerved. Flowers in clusters; the clusters forming axillary panicles, usually shorter than the subtending leaves. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, elliptic-navicular; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil very small. Female flowers: perianth-segments 3, unequal. Achene ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 1 mm, minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 31557.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Indonesia.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Pilea microphylla (L.) Liebm. 小葉冷水花
Kongel. Danske Vidensk. Selsk. Skr., Naturvidensk. Math. Afd., ser. 5, 5(2): 302. 1851; FOC 5: 119. 2003; FGD 6: 90. 2005.
Parietaria microphylla L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 1308. 1759.
Pilea muscosa Linndl., Coll. Bot. t. 4. 1821, nom. illeg.; FKH 248. 1912.

Delicate herb, 3–17 cm tall, glabrous. Stems fleshy, erect or ascending, simple or branched, with dense cystoliths. Leaves membranous when dry; stipules triangular, ca. 0.5 mm; petioles slender, unequal in length, 1– 4 mm; leaf blade obovate or spathulate, unequal in size, 2–7 × 1.5 –3 mm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire, adaxially green, abaxially paler, foveolate when dry, pinnately nerved. Flowers in compact cymose capitulum on a peduncle of 1.5 – 6 mm, sometimes sessile. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, ovate, corniculate near apex; stamens 4; rudimentary ovary minute. Female flowers smaller, perianth-segments 3, subequal, oblong, the ventral one larger, subequal to achene, the lateral 2 ovate, acute. Achene ovoid, ca. 4 mm, compressed, smooth, enclosed by persistent perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong (naturalized). H. C. Tang 1406, 1795; L. T. Lo 156.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (naturalized). Native to tropical America, naturalized elsewhere in tropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Shady old walls, moist rocks and other wet places. Flowering; Jun.–Aug; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Pilea peploides (Gaudich.) Hook. & Arn. 齒葉冷水花
Bot. Beechey Voy. 96. 1832; FKH 248. 1912; FOC 5: 119. 2003.
Pilea peploides (Gaudich.) Hook. & Arn. var. major Wedd., Prodr. 16(1): 109. 1869; C. J. Chen, Bull. Bot. Res. 2(3): 115. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 150, pl. 33: 1–3. 1995.

Annual herb, 5–30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems fleshy, often clumped. Leaves membranous when dry; stipules small, triangular; petioles slender, 3–20 mm; leaf blade rhomboid-orbicular to depressed orbicular, sometimes fan-shaped, (7–)10–21 × (7–)11–23 mm, apex rounded or broadly obtuse, base obtuse or sub-rounded, sometimes broadly cuneate, shallowly dentate or undulate above middle, rarely sub-entire, trinerved. Flowers in subsessile clusters, or in compact cymes on short peduncles. Male flowers: perianth‑segments 4, ovate; stamens 4. Female flowers: perianth-segments 2, unequal, the ventral one larger, navicular or obovate-oblong, thickened in fruit, about the length of the fruit or slightly shorter. Achene ovoid, with scattered minute spiny projections.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. W. J. Tutcher 4619.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests, moist rocks and wet places. Flowering; Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Jul.

Pilea sinofasciata C. J. Chen 粗齒冷水花
Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 85. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 115, pl. 24: 5 – 8. 1995; FOC 5: 110. 2003; FGD 6: 95. 2005.
Pilea wightii auct. non Wedd.: FKH 248. 1912.

Perennial herb, 25–100 cm tall. Stems fleshy, scarcely branched, glabrous or sometimes puberulent on the upper part. Leaves subequal on the same pair; stipules membranous, triangular, ca. 2 mm; petioles 1– 5 cm, ± puberulent; leaf blade elliptic, or oblong-lanceolate, (2–)4–17 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate or rounded, slightly oblique, apex caudate-acuminate, margin coarsely serrate, adaxial surface green, initially with scattered pellucid short hairs, glabrescent, often with 2 white stripes along the midvein, abaxial surface subglabrous, or sometimes puberulent on veins; trinerved. Leaves on the lower part of the stem smaller, obovate or fan-shaped, apex acute or subrounded. Flowers in cymose panicles, usually shorter than petioles of the subtending leaves. Male flowers: perianth united at base, segments 4, elliptic, concave, apex obtuse; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil small, conical. Female flowers: perianth-segments 3, subequal. Achene ovoid, ca. 0.7 mm, apex slightly oblique.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 25864, 25867.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, SW Shaanxi, SE Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Ravines, by streams. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Pilea swinglei Merr. 三角冷水花
Philip. J. Sci. 13: 136. 1918; Hand.-Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 141. 1929; FRPS 23(2): 151. pl. 33: 4 –9. 1995; FOC 5: 120. 2003; FGD 6: 92. 2005.

Annual herb, 7–30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems fleshy. Leaves membranous when dry; stipules small, triangular, ca. 1 mm; petioles 5 –30 mm; leaf blade broadly ovate, triangular or narrowly ovate, 1– 5.5 × 0.8 –3 cm, apex acute, sometimes obtuse or shortly acuminate, base cordate, obtuse or truncate, margin sparsely serrate, adaxial surface green, abaxial surface paler, foveolate when dry, often densely marked with purple minute dots; trinerved. Leaves on the lower part of the stem much smaller, ovate-orbicular or sub-orbicular, apex obtuse or subrounded. Flowers in head-like clusters, 2.5 – 5 mm in diam.; the clusters 2–4 arranged on a slender, simple or little branched rachis, usually shorter than the subtending leaves. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, obovate-oblong; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil inconspicuous. Female flowers: perianth-segments 2, very unequal, the larger one oblong-navicular, 2‑keeled on upper part of abaxil surface, another very small. Achene broadly ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 0.5 mm, apex slightly oblique.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1550, 2739.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Rocks by streams and wet places near villages.

Pileostegia tomentella Hand.-Mazz. 星毛冠蓋藤
Anz. Akad. Wiss. Wien. Math.-Nat. 59: 55. 1922; FFJ 2: 230. 1984; FRPS 35(1): 175, pl. 35: 4 – 7. 1995; FGD 2: 212, fig. 135. 1991; FOC 8: 404. 2001.

Branchlets, petioles, inflorescences and abaxial surface of leaves densely rusty stellate hairy. Petioles 0.5 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade leathery, oblong to obovate-oblong, 5 – 10( – 18) × 2.5 – 5( – 8) cm, base shallowly cordate, apex acute, margin entire and slightly revolute, irregularly undulate or sparsely serrate at upper part. Inflorescences 5 – 25 × 10 – 25 cm; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx tube turbinate, ca. 2 mm; lobes triangular, sparsely stellate hairy. Petals white, broadly triangular, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens 10; filaments 3 – 6 mm; anthers globose, ca. 0.7 mm in diam. Ovary truncate at apex; style ca. 1.5 mm; stigma conical, 4 – 6-lobed. Capsule dark brown, turbinate, ca. 4 mm in diam., 5 – 10-ribbed, apex truncate, sparsely stellate hairy. Seeds ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ho Pui Reservoir. F. W. Xing 10094; HK sheet 10543.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests in valleys. Flowering: Mar. – Aug.; fruiting: Sep. – Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pileostegia viburnoides Hook. f. & Thomson 冠蓋藤

J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 2: 76, fig. 2. 1857; FKH 98. 1912; FHN 2: 190. 1965; FFJ 2: 230, fig. 195. 1984; FGD 2: 212. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 57, pl. 32. 1993; FRPS 35(1): 173, pl. 35: 1 – 3. 1995; FOC 8: 404. 2001.

Pileostegia viburnoides Hook. f. & Thomson var. parviflora Oliv. & Maxim., Mem. Acad. Sci. St. Petersb. ser. 7, 10(16): 18. 1867.


Branchlets decussate, glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent. Petioles 1 – 3 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, elliptic-lanceolate to oblong-obovate, 7 – 18 × 2 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, abaxially glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent. Inflorescences 7 – 25 × 15 – 25 cm, glabrous or pubescent; pedicel 3 – 5 mm. Flowers small. Calyx tube ca. 1.5 mm; lobes 4 – 5, triangular, glabrous. Petals 4 – 5, white, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens 8 – 10; filaments 3 – 6 mm, usually coiled; anthers compressed subglobose. Ovary inferior, truncate at apex; style ca. 1 mm; stigma 4 – 6-lobed. Capsule turbinate, ca. 4 × 2 – 3 mm. Seeds ca. 2 mm.


Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Peak. D. P. M. Guile s.n. (HK sheet 30346); L. T. Lo 360; P. S. Choi 544.

Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; India, Vietnam, Japan.

Ecology: Valleys. Flowering: Jul. – Aug.; fruiting: Sep. – Dec.

Pimpinella diversifolia DC. 異葉茴芹
Prodr. 4: 122. 1830; FKH 117. 1912; FRPS 55(2): 70. 1985; FGD 2: 336, fig. 224. 1991; FOC 14: 96. 2005.

Perennial herb, 50–100 cm tall, with fibrous, fragrant roots; stems erect, branching on the upper part. Basal and lower stem leaves simple, undivided, or shallowly 3-lobed; petioles 2–10 cm, sheathing; leaf blade ovate-cordate, 2.5–8.5 × 2.5–7 cm; leaves on the middle of stem usually ternate, margin coarsely serrate, short-petiolate, the terminal one ovate, 4–6 × 1.5–3 cm; lateral ones oblique at base; upper stem leaves reduced, lanceolate, sessile. Inflorescence of compound umbels. Involucre wanting or of 1–2 linear bracts; bracteoles 1–8, linear. Pedicels 1–3 mm, unequal. Flowers white, with narrow inflexed apex; styles slender, reflexed; stylopodium conical. Fruit slightly laterally compressed, ovoid to globose, 1.5–2 mm, a little broader than long, glabrate to puberulent, the ribs filiform, evident. Vittae 3–4 in each furrow, 2–4 on the commissure. Seed-face plane.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 12480.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Pakistan, India, Afghanistan, Nepal, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), vegetable.

Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Breitenb. 半夏
Bot. Zeitg. (Berlin) 37: 687. 1879; FRPS 13(2): 204, pl. 40: 1–7. 1979; FYN 2: 837. 1979; FFJ 6: 430, fig. 391. 1995; FTW ed 2, 5: 682, pl. 294. 2000; FGD 9: 200, fig. 115. 2009; FOC 23: 42. 2010.
Arum ternatum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 233. 1784.
Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Makino f. angustata (Schott) Makino, Check List HK Plants 300. 2002; 106. 2004.
Pinellia tuberifera Tenore, Atti Accad. Sci. Fis. Mat. Napoli 4: 57. 1839; FKH 288. 1912.

Perennial herb, tuber globose, 1–2 cm in diam. Leaves (1–)2–3(–5); petiole 15–20 cm, base sheathing; leaf blade of seedlings usually simple, ovate-cordate to hastate, that of adult plants trifoliolate; leaflets oblong-elliptic or lanceolate, base cuneate, apex acuminate, terminal one 3–10(–20) × 1–3(–5) cm; lateral ones smaller; lateral veins 8–10 pairs. Peduncle longer than petiole, 25–35 cm; spathe greenish or whitish green, tube narrowly cylindrical, 1.3–2 cm; limb oblong, green or usually purplish at margin, 4–5 cm, apex obtuse or acute; spadix: female portion 1.3–2 cm, sterile portion 3 mm, male portion 5–7 mm, appendage linear, green to purplish, 6–12 cm, erect or sigmoid. Berries ovoid, yellowish green.

Locality: Mount Violet. HK sheet 34816.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Nei Mongol, Xinjiang, Xizang, Qinghai; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grasslands, farmlands and thin forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Makino previously (Check List HK Plants 300. 2002; 106. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Makino previously (Check List HK Plants 300. 2002; 106. 2004).
