Pinellia tripartita (Blume) Schott 三裂葉半夏
Syn. Aroid. 5. 1856; FOC 23: 41. 2010.
Atherurus tripartitus Blume, Rumphia 1: 137. 1835.

Perennial herb, tuber subglobose, ca. 2.5 cm in diam. Leaves 2–5; petiole green, 30–35 cm; leaf blade green, 3-partite; leaflets broadly ovate to ovate-oblong; anterior leaflet ca. 15 × 4–7 cm, apex ca. 1.5 cm; lateral leaflets smaller; primary lateral veins 8–12 per side on each leaflet, forming a distinct marginal collective vein, also with 2 thinner collective veins along margin. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle to 25 cm, shorter than petioles, slender. Spathe whitish to light green, slightly constricted, 7–9(–10) cm; tube oblong to subcylindrical, ca. 3.5 × 1–1.25 cm; limb boat-shaped, oblong, ca. 4 × 2.5 cm. Spadix 20–25 cm; female portion ca. 3 cm, adnate to spathe; female flowers densely arranged; pistil 1–1.2 mm; ovary ovoid, 0.9–1 mm; style distinct, 0.2–0.3 mm, attenuate; stigma subhemispheric; sterile portion between female and male portion 0.6–0.7 cm; male portion 1.8–2 cm; thecae elongate, opening by a slit; appendage long exserted from spathe, sigmoid, 15–20 cm, base ca. 3 mm in diam., smooth. Berries 1-seeded, pale green to whitish, ovoid.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. C. Wright 508 (P).
Distribution: Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.
Notes: The species can be easily distinguished from P. ternata by petioles lacking bulbils.

Pinus elliottii Engelm. 濕地松
Trans. Acad. Sci. St. Louis. 4: 186, pl. 1–3. 1880; FRPS 7: 274, pl. 65: 8 –14. 1978; FOC 4: 20. 1999; FGD 4: 17. 2000.

Tree to 30 m tall; trunk to 0.8 m d.b.h. in native range; bark orange- or purple-brown, furrowed into irregularly oblong, large, papery, scaly plates; branchlets growing twice or more each year, orange-brown, later becoming brown to greyish brown, stout, roughly scaly; winter buds silvery brown, cylindric, scales fringed at margin. Needles 2 or 3 per bundle, 18–25 cm × 2 mm, stout, yellow- or blue-green, stomatal lines present on all surfaces, base with persistent sheath 1–2 cm, margin finely serrulate, resin canals 2–9(–11), mostly internal. Seed cones solitary or paired, pedunculate (peduncle to 3 cm), pale brown, ovoid or ovoidcylindric when open, (7–)9–18(–20) cm, maturing in 2 years. Apophyses lustrous, slightly raised, strongly cross keeled; umbo depressed-pyramidal, with a short, stout prickle. Seeds dark brown, ellipsoid, 6–7 mm, apex oblique; wing to 2 cm.

Locality: Widely planted in countryside. Y. S. Lau 2950.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei (introduced). Native to SE United States.
Uses: Afforestation.

Pinus massoniana Lamb. 馬尾松
Descr. Pinus. 1: 17. 1803; FKH 10: 256. 1912; FRPS 7: 263, pl. 63: 1– 6. 1978; FOC 4: 14. 1999; FGD 4: 16. 2000.
Pinus sinensis auct. non Lamb.: FHK. 337. 1861

Tree to 45 m tall; trunk to 1.5 m d.b.h.; bark red-brown, irregularly scaly and flaking; crown broadly pyramidal or umbrellalike; branchlets usually growing once per year, yellowish brown, occasionally glaucous; winter buds brown, ovoid-cylindric or cylindric. Needles 2(rarely 3) per bundle, slender, slightly twisted, 10–18 cm, stomatal lines present on all surfaces, resin canals 4–8, marginal, base with persistent sheath. Seed cones pendulous, shortly pedunculate, green, turning chestnut brown at maturity, ovoid, conical-ovoid, or ovoid-cylindric, 4–7 × 2.5–5 cm. Seed scales suboblong-obovoid or subsquare; apophyses rhombic, slightly swollen or flat, slightly transversely ridged; umbo flattened, slightly sunken, blunt or shortly mucronate in apical part of cone. Seeds narrowly ovoid, 4–6 mm; wing 1.6–2.1 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong, also widely planted in countryside. Champion s.n. (K); H. C. Tang 1227. Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River.
Ecology: On hills. Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Oct.–Dec. of 2nd year.
Uses: Afforestation.
Notes: The local populations of the species declined because of the attack of pinewood nematodes from 1978 onwards.
records.uses:
Afforestation.
Notes: The local populations of the species declined because of the attack of pinewood nematodes from 1978 onwards.

records.text:
Piper austrosinense Y. C. Tseng 華南胡椒
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 17: 36, fig. 12. 1979; FRPS 20(1): 54. 1982; FGD 1: 68. 1987; FOC 4: 125. 1999.

Climber, woody, glabrous except for rachis and bracts. Petioles 0.4–2 cm; leaf blades ovate or ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 6–11 × 5 – 6 cm, base usually oblique, rounded or slightly cordate, apex acuminate. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes white, 3– 6.5 cm, ca. 2 mm thick; peduncle 1–1.8 cm; rachis and abaxial surface of bracts densely white pubescent; bracts orbicular, ca. 1 mm wide, peltate, sessile. Stamens 2, filaments nearly as long as anthers. Female spikes white, 1–1.5 cm, ca. 3 mm thick; peduncle nearly as long as rachis; bracts as in male flowers. Ovary partly immersed in rachis; stigmas 3 or 4, tomentose. Drupe globose, red, ca. 3 mm in diam., partly immersed in rachis.

Locality: Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen. K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK Sheet 39789).
Distribution: E & SW Guangdong, SE Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Forests, climbing on trees or rocks. Flowering: Apr–Jun.
Notes: This species when without fruits may be confused with Piper hancei, but can be easily distinguished by its white spikes.

Piper betle L. 蔞葉
Sp. Pl. 1: 28. 1753; FRPS 20(1): 42. 1982; FGD 1: 67, fig. 70. 1987; FOC. 4: 120. 1999.

Climber; stems rooted at nodes. Petioles 2–5 cm, very finely powdery pubescent; leaf blade papery to ± leathery, ovate to ovateoblong, 7–15 × 5–11 cm, base cordate, sometimes rounded in upper leaves, symmetrical or nearly so, apex acuminate, abaxially densely glandular, with very finely powdery pubescent veins, adaxially glabrous; veins 7, apical pair arising 0.7–2 cm above base, usually opposite. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes nearly as long as leaf blades at anthesis; peduncle nearly as long as petioles; rachis pubescent; bracts orbicular or suborbicular, rarely obovate, 1–1.3 mm wide, peltate, ± sessile. Stamens 2, filaments thick, ca. as long as anthers or longer, anthers reniform. Female spikes 3 –5 cm, longer in fruit, ca. 1 cm thick; rachis fleshy, densely pubescent. Ovary partly immersed in and connate to rachis, apex tomentose; stigmas usually 4 or 5, lanceolate, tomentose. Drupes fused to form fleshy, reddish cylindrical mass; tips tomentose, prominent.

Locality: Cultivated. N. H. Li 117 (HK).
Distribution: Cultivated in S, SW & E China; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Madagascar.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Social (masticatory), medicinal (folklore).

Piper cathayanum M. G. Gilbert & N. H. Xia 華山蔞（青蒟）
Novon 9: 191. 1999; FOC 4: 118. 1999.
Chavica sinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 116. 1854.
Piper sinense (Champ. ex Benth.) C. de Candolle, Prodr. 16(1): 361. 1868, non Piper chinense Miq., 1845; FHK 335. 1861; FKH 221. 1912; FRPS 20(1): 38, pl. 13: 7–11. 1982; FGD 1: 71, fig. 74. 1987.

Climber, to 5 m or longer. Petioles 10 –15 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate, ovate-oblong, or oblong, 8–15 × 3.5 – 6.5 cm, base deeply cordate, basal lobes often overlapping, ± symmetrical, apex obtuse or acute, abaxially pubescent, especially along veins, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pubescent at base; veins 7, usually opposite, apical pair arising 0.5–1 cm above base. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes 2.5 – 4 cm, 4 –5 mm thick; peduncle shorter than petioles, roughly pubescent, rachis glabrous; bracts orbicular, ca. 1.2 mm wide, peltate, glabrous, ± sessile. Stamens 2. Female spikes to 3 cm in fruit; rachis and bracts as in male flowers. Stigmas usually 3. Drupe globose, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., partly connate to rachis.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 593; Y. W. Lam 17.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan.
Ecology: Forests streamsides, often climbing on trees. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Piper hancei Maxim. 山蒟
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Pétersbourg, sér. 3, 31: 94. 1887; FKH 221. 1912; FRPS 20(1): 60, pl. 19: 1–3. 1982; FGD 1: 69, fig. 72. 1987; FOC 4: 127. 1999.
Chavica leptostachya Hance, J. Bot. 6: 301. 1868, non Piper leptostachyon Nutt. 1822.
Piper matthewii Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 377. 1909; FKH 221. 1912.

Climber, glabrous except for rachis and bases of bracts. Petioles 0.5 –1.2 cm; leaf blade papery to ± leathery, ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, rarely lanceolate, 6 –12 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, base gradually tapered or cuneate, sometimes rounded, symmetrical or nearly so, apex acute or acuminate; veins 5(–7), apical pair arising 1–3 cm above base, alternate, nearly reaching leaf apex. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes yellow, 6–10 cm, ca. 2 mm thick; peduncle ca. as long as petioles or slightly longer, rachis pubescent; bracts suborbicular, ca. 0.8 mm wide, peltate, adaxially pilose, ± sessile to short stalked. Stamens 2. Female spikes ca. 3 cm, longer in fruit; bracts as in male spikes. Ovary subglobose, distinct; stigmas (3 or) 4. Drupe yellow, globose, 2.5–3 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 499; HK sheet 34040.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests, usually climbing on trees or rocks; Flowering: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Piper hongkongense C. DC 毛蒟
Prodr. 16: 347. 1868; FOC 4: 121. 1999.
Chavica puberula Benth., FHK 335. 1861.
Piper puberulum (Benth.) Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-petersbourg 31: 94. 1887, non (Benth.) Seemann, 1868; FKH 221. 1912; FHN 1: 332. 1964, p.p.; FRPS 20(1): 34. 1982; FGD 1: 70. 1987.

Climber. Young branches softly hairy, glabrescent. Petioles 5 –10 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate-lanceolate or ovate, 5 –11 × 2– 6 cm, base ± cordate, apex acute or acuminate, usually asymmetrical, abaxially pubescent, mixed with a few dichotomous hairs, adaxially ± glabrescent; veins 5 –7, apical pair arising 1.5 –3 cm above base, alternate, others ± basal. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious), in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes ca. 7 cm long, ca. 3 mm thick; peduncle slightly longer than petioles, pilose; bracts orbicular, sometimes slightly tapered, peltate, glabrous. Stamens usually 3, filaments very short, anthers reniform. Female spikes 4–6 cm; peduncle, rachis, and bracts as in male flowers. Ovary subglobose; stigmas 4. Drupe globose, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. N. H. Li 22 (HK); HK Sheet 35607.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thickets or forests, often climbing on trees or rocks; Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by Seemann around 1850.

Piper sarmentosum Roxb. 假蒟
Fl. Ind. 1: 162. 1820; FKH 221. 1912; FHN 1: 332. 1964; FRPS 20(1): 42, pl. 14: 7–10. 1982; FGD 1: 68, fig. 71. 1987; FOC 4: 119. 1999.
Chavica hainana C. DC., Annuaire Conserv. Jard. Bot. Geneve 2: 275. 1898.
Chavica sarmentosa (Roxb.) Miq., Syst. Piperac. 242. 1843; FHK 335. 1861.

Perennial stoloniferous herb, most parts very finely powdery pubescent at least when young. Fertile stems ± erect. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaf blade membranous, toward base of stem ovate to suborbicular, those toward apex of stem smaller, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 7–14 × 6–13 cm, base cordate to rounded, sometimes cuneate on uppermost branches, subsymmetrical, apex acute, finely glandular, abaxially finely powdery pubescent along veins, adaxially glabrous; veins 7, glaucous when dry, abaxially very prominent, apical pair arising 1–2 cm above base, reaching leaf apex; reticulation of veins conspicuous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes white, 1.5–2.5 cm, 2–3 mm thick; peduncle nearly as long as spikes, rachis pubescent; bracts transversely elliptic, 0.5–0.6 mm, peltate, ± sessile. Stamens 2, filaments ca. two times as long as anthers, anthers subglobose. Female spikes 6–8 cm, to 8 mm thick in fruit; peduncle as in male spikes, rachis glabrous; bracts suborbicular, peltate, 1–1.3 mm in diam. Stigmas 3–5, hispidulous. Drupe subglobose, 4-angled, 2.5–3 mm, partly connate to rachis.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Fanling, Ma On Shan.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; India, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests and wet places near villages. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Pistia stratiotes L. 大薸
Sp. Pl. 2: 963. 1753; FKH 288. 1912; FGZ 687, fig. 362. 1956; FHN 4: 141, fig. 1047. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 83, pl. 12: 6–9. 1979; FYN 2: 784, fig. 209: 6–9. 1979; FFJ 6: 421, fig. 382. 1995; FTW ed 2, 5: 682, pl. 295, photo 73. 2000; FGD 9: 193, fig. 111. 2009; FOC 23: 79. 2010.

Aquatic herb, with many feathery roots, floating on stagnant water. Leaves in rosulate clusters on a very short stem; petioles almost absent; leaf blade broadly cuneate to obovate-cuneate, 1.3–10 × 1.5–6 cm, truncate or emarginate at apex, entire or undulate, pubescent on both surfaces, especially near the base. Characters of inflorescence and flowers as the description of the genus.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung. HK sheet 7726, 30264.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Ponds and ditches. Flowering: May–Nov.
Uses: Animal food.

Pisum sativum L. 豌豆
Sp. Pl. 727. 1753; FKH 82. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 287. 1998; FGD 5: 357, fig. 199. 2003.

Annual climbing herb, 0.5 – 2 m tall, glabrous and glaucous. Stipules larger than leaflet, leaf-like, cordate, margin serrulate on proximal part. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 2–3 pairs, ovate, 2–5 × 1 – 2.5 cm. Flowers solitary or several in racemes. Calyx campanulate, 5-lobed, lobes lanceolate, 5–7 mm. Corolla usually white or purple or of other colours; vexillum erect, suborbicular, 1.5 – 1.7 cm wide; wings obliquely ovate or oblong, blade 10 × 7 mm; keel lunate, 7 × 5 mm. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary glabrous. Pods oblong, 2.5–10 × 0.7–1.4 cm. Seeds 2–10, green, globose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2643; HK sheet 7698.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Food, green manure, forage.

Pittosporum glabratum Lindl. 光葉海桐（崖花子）
J. Hort. Soc. London 1: 230. 1846; FHK 19. 1861; FKH 37. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 11. 1979; FFJ 2: 241. 1984; FGD 1: 102, fig. 111: 2. 1987; FOC 9: 6. 2003.
Pittosporum fortunei Turcz., Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 236: 562. 1863.

Shrub or small tree, 2 – 3 m tall, glabrous except pedicels. Petioles 6 – 14 mm; leaf blade narrowly oblong or oblanceolate, 5 – 10 × 2 – 3.5 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin slightly rugose. Inflorescences 1 – 4 in leaf axils at branchlet apex, umbellate or corymbose; pedicels 4 – 12 mm, puberulous. Sepals ovate, ca. 2 mm. Petals oblanceolate, 0.8 – 1.2 cm. Stamens 4 – 7 mm. Ovary long ovoid, 3-carpellate; placentae 3; ovules ca. 6 in each placenta; style ca. 3 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, 2 – 2.5 cm, dehiscing by 3 valves; pericarp thinly leathery. Seeds red, subglobose, 5 – 7 × 4 – 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2195; L. T. Lo 3.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Hubei, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests and shrublands on slopes. Flowering: Mar. – Aug.; fruiting: Jun. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Pittosporum glabratum Lindl. var. neriifolium Rehder & E. H. Wilson 狹葉海桐
Pl. Wilson. 3(2): 328. 1916; FRPS 35(2): 12. 1979; FGD 1: 103. 1987; FOC 9: 6. 2003.
Pittosporum cavaleriei Levl., Fedde, Rep. Spec. Nov. 11: 492. 1913.

Leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, 8 – 18 × 1 – 2 cm.
Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1439; HK sheet 271, 40905.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Yunnan; India.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Nov.

Pittosporum tobira (Thunb.) Aiton 海桐
Hort. Kew. (ed. 2) 2: 37. 1811; FKH 37. 1912; FHN 1: 449. 1964; FRPS 35(2): 6. 1979; FFJ 2: 240, fig. 202. 1984; FGD 1: 103, pl. 112, fig. 1. 1987; FOC 9: 4. 2003.
Euonymus tobira Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 208. 1780.

Shrub or small tree, to 3 m tall. Young branchlets lenticellate, brown hairy. Petioles ca. 2 cm; leaf blade obovate or obovate-lanceolate, 4 – 9 × 2 – 4 cm, leathery, base narrowly cuneate, apex rounded or obtuse, usually emarginate, margin revolute. Inflorescences terminal or near so, umbellate or corymbose; pedicels 1 – 2 cm. Sepals lanceolate, 3 – 4 mm. Petals oblanceolate, 1 – 1.2 cm. Stamens 5 – 6 mm, sometimes sterile. Ovary long ovoid, densely pubescent, 3-carpellate; placentas 3; ovules many per locule. Capsule globose, angular, ca. 1 – 1.2 cm in diam., dehiscing by 3 valves, ± pubescent; pericarp ca. 1.5 mm thick. Seeds red, ca. 4 mm.

Locality: Ninepin Group, Sung Kong and Ng Fan Chau; also cultivated in parks and gardens. S. P. Lau 137; F. W. Xing 9708.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Seashore hillslopes. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: May – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Plantago lanceolata L. 長葉車前
Sp. Pl. 13. 1753; FKH 212. 1912; FRPS 70: 338. 2002.

Herbs perennial. Leaves basal, rosulate; petioles 7–10 cm, base sheath‑like; leaf‑blade papery, linear‑lanceolate, elliptic‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 6–20 × 0.5–4.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire or very sparsely serrulate, glabrous or sparsely pubescent on both surfaces; (3–)5(–7)‑veined. Spikes cylindric or head‑like, 1–5(–8) cm. Bracts ovate or elliptic, 2.5 – 5 mm, apex caudate, densely hirsute. Sepals 4, 2– 3.5 mm, carinate, anterior 2 connate near top, posterior free. Corolla white; tube 1.5–3 mm; lobes lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm. Anthers white to yellowish, elliptic, 2.5–3 mm. Capsules ovoid, 3–4 mm, circumscissile. Seeds (1–)2, light brown to dark brown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Wong Nai Chung Gap. HK sheet 9650.
Distribution: S, E & NE China; Europe.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Spring to summer.

Plantago major L. 車前草
Sp. Pl. 112. 1753; FHK 280. 1861; FKH 213. 1912; FGD 3: 317. 1995; FRPS 70: 324. 2002.

Herbs perennial. Leaves basal, rosulate; petioles about equaling to leaf‑blade in length, base expanded; leaf blade broad‑ovate, oblong‑ovate or suborbicular, 5–12 × 3.5–10 cm, base decurrent, apex obtuse, margin entire or irregularly obtuse‑dentate, pubescent or glabrous on both surfaces, 5–7‑veined. Spikes erect, 6–20 cm. Bracts green, scarious. Sepals elliptic, 2.3–3 mm, slightly unequal, carinate. Corolla‑tube constricted at throat; lobes deltoid, ca. 1.3 mm. Anthers purplish. Capsules elliptic, 3.5–4 mm, circumscissile. Seeds 8 – 18, dark‑brown.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Yuen Tun Ha, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Yuen Long, Wu Kau Tang, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1946; L. T. Lo 74; P. S. Choi 357.
Distribution: Widely distributed in Asia and Europe.
Ecology: Roadsides in rural areas, wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Platanthera mandarinorum Rchb. f. 尾瓣舌唇蘭
Linnaea 25: 226. 1852; FKH 269. 1912; FFJ 6: 644, fig. 569. 1995 [“mandarinonum”]; FRPS 17: 298, pl. 43. 6–7. 1999; FGD 7: 366. 2006; FOC 25: 105. 2009.

Terrestrial herb, up to 20 cm tall at flowering time; stems angular. Leaves one normal, 2–4 strongly reduced; normal leaf ellipticlanceolate, 3–5 × 0.8–1.7 cm, apex obtuse; the reduced upper leaves linear-lanceolate 1.5–3.5 × 4–7 mm. Flowers green, 5–12 in a terminal spike; dorsal sepal ovate-cordate, 4 mm long and wide, apex acuminate, acumen 1.5 mm; lateral sepals pointing downward, oblique linear-falcate, 8 × 2 mm, twisted at base; petals oblique ovate-lanceolate, pale green, 6–7 × 4 mm; lip tongue-like, 10 × 2 mm; spur slender, 1.5 cm, green; column creamy-white; anthers 2-thecae; pollinia 2, tessellate; ovary ellipsoidal, twisted and ridged.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11628A (CUHK); HK sheet 27798.
Distribution: S, E & SW China, Henan, Shandong; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Short grasses on exposed mountain tops. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.

Platanthera minor (Miq.) Rchb. f. 小舌唇蘭
Bot. Zeit. Berlin 36: 75. 1878; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 31, fig. 8. 1977; FRPS 17: 303, pl. 43: 4–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1014. 2000; FGD 7: 367, fig. 187. 2006; FOC 25: 109. 2009.
Habenaria japonica (Thunb.) A. Gray var. minor Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 207. 1865.
Platanthera interrupta Maxim., Bull. Acad. Sci. St. Petersb. 31: 106. 1886; FKH 269. 1912.

Terrestrial herb, 15 30 cm tall at flowering time; stems 5-angled. Leaves one basal, the largest, ovate-elliptic to oblonglanceolate, petiolate, petioles 1.5 cm; cauline leaves linearlanceolate, sessile, 8–10 × 1.3–1.5 cm. Flowers yellowish green, 5–12 in a terminal spike; odd sepal ovate, 6 × 5 mm, acute; lateral sepals ovate-falcate, 7 × 2.5 mm; petals oblique-ovate, 6 mm, the upper margin connivent with odd sepal; lip calcarate, ovatelanceolate, 9 × 3–3.5 mm, greenish yellow, with a slender spur 1.4 cm; column 2.5 mm; anthers 2, obovate, at each side of the column.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20548 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2171, 2972.
Distribution: NE, E, C, S & SW China; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grasses on sunny mountain slopes or shade of ravines on humus-covered rock niches. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.

Platanus × acerifolia (Ait.) Willd. 二球懸鈴木
Sp. Pl. 4: 474. 1797; FRPS 35(2): 120, pl. 26. 1979; FGD 4: 248, fig. 148. 2000.
Platanus hybrida Brot., Fl. Lusit. 2: 487. 1804.
Platanus orientalis L. var. acerifolia Ait., Hort. Kew 3: 364. 1789.

Deciduous tree, to 30 m tall. Bark greyish green, exfoliating in large flakes. Young shoots brownish tomentose, glabrous and reddish brown in age. Leaves papery; petioles 3–10 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade broadly ovate, 10 –24 × 12–25 cm, base truncate to cordate, upper part palmately (3 –)5(–7)-lobed; lobes triangular-ovate or broadly triangular, the middle one about as long as broad, entire or sparsely toothed, tawny tomentose when young, glabrous or nearly so at maturity. Infructescence a globular head, usually 2, rarely1 or 3 racemosely arranged, 2.5–3 cm in diam., bristly. Nutlet ovoid or rounded at apex and crowned by the persistent remnant of the style.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1552, 2773.
Distribution: Probably a hybrid of P. occidentalis L. and P. orientalis L. Widely cultivated in temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering: May; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Platycladus orientalis (L.) Franco 側柏
Portug. Acta Biol., ser. B, Sist. Suppl. 33. 1949; FRPS 7: 322, pl. 74: 5 –7. 1978; FOC 4: 64. 1999.
Thuja orientalis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1002. 1753; FGD 4: 25, fig. 15. 2000.
Biota orientalis (L.) Endl., Syn. Conif. 47. 1847; FHN 1: 213. 1964.

Tree 8–20 m tall; trunk to 1 m (or more) d.b.h.; crown pyramidal when young, broadly ovoid when old. Leaves 1–3 mm, green, not glaucous, apex bluntly pointed; facial leaves rhomboid, with a conspicuous, linear, glandular groove at center abaxially; lateral leaves overlapping facial ones, boat-shaped, ridged, apex slightly incurved. Pollen cones yellowish green, ovoid, 2–3 mm. Seed cones when immature bluish green, when ripe reddish brown, subovoid, 1.5 –2.5 × 1–1.5 cm; fertile cone scale 1–2-seeded. Seeds greyish brown or purplish brown, ovoid, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, slightly ridged, usually wingless.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. C. Lau s.n.; Y. S. Lau 2067.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Henan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Shanxi, Hebei, Inner Mongolia, Jilin, Liaoning; Korea, Russia.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: Oct.
Uses: Timber, ornamental.

Platycodon grandiflorus (Jacq.) A. DC. 桔梗
Monogr. Camp. 125. 1830; FKH 153. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 77. 1983; FGD 3: 322, fig. 209. 1995.
Campanula grandiflora Jacq., Hort. Bot. Vindob. 3: 4, t. 2. 1776.
Wahlenbergia grandiflora Schrad., Cat. Hort. Götting. (ann. 1814); FHK 197. 1861.

Perennial herbs, 40–100 cm tall, glabrous and somewhat glaucous, with thick fleshy tap root. Leaves in whorls of 3 or opposite, rarely alternate on the upper part of stem, subsessile; leaf blades ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, 2–7 × 0.5–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute, margin serrulate. Flowers solitary or 2–3 in terminal loose raceme. Calyx‑tube hemispheric; lobes 5, triangular to narrowly triangular, 2–8 mm. Corolla broadly campanulate, deep blue, 3–5 cm in diam.; lobes 5, triangular, apex acute. Stamens 5, flattened at base, hairy on the inner side. Capsule obovoid or globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., opening in 5 valves opposite to the calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Long Ke. H. C. Tang 270; Y. S. Lau 2337; HK sheet 39269.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW regions; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Sunny grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Pluchea indica (L.) Less. 闊苞菊
Linnaea 6: 150. 1831; FHK 179. 1861; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 301. 1967; FRPS 75: 51. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1036. 1998; FGD 8: 162, fig. 88. 2007.
Baccharis indica L., Sp. Pl. 861. 1753.

Upright shrubs, (0.3–)1–2 m tall; stem striate‑sulcate, sparsely puberulent to tomentulose in younger parts, older parts nearly glabrous. Leaves sessile or shortly petiolate, obovate, 3–7 × 0.8–3 cm, with upper leaves gradually smaller, base attenuate‑cuneate, apex rounded or obtuse, margin irregularly dentate, but entire near the base, puberulent on both surfaces, midvein prominent on both sides. Capitula arranged in terminal or axillary corymbs; peduncles 3–10 mm, tomentulose hair relatively denser. Involucres cylindric when fresh, campanulate when dried, 4–6 mm; phyllaries in 5–6 series, ciliate along margin; outermost ones broadly ovate, 2.5 × 2 mm, apex obtuse; middle layers changed from ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, length increased from 3 to 4 mm, width decreased from 2 to 1 mm, apex obtuse to acute; innermost 5 × 0.7 mm, apex attenuate. Receptacle flat, fimbriate. Florets purple. Outer florets numerous, pistillate, corolla filiform‑tubular, 4–5 mm, limb finely 3–4‑lobed; style exserted, shortly branched, papillose; cypselae cylindric, ribbed, 0.5 – 0.8 mm, nearly glabrous; pappus uniseriate, white or greyish white, 4–5 mm. Disk hermaphrodite florets few, functionally staminate, corolla tubular, 5–6 mm, apex with 5 triangular lobes glandular outside; anther tubes greatly exserted; cypsela vestigial; pappus white or greyish white, 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 12248 (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1344 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 746.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Marshes near seaside, tidal flats, and sandy beaches, adapted to saline habitats. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Food (young leaves).

Pluchea pteropoda Hemsl. 光梗闊苞菊（翅煙茜）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 422. 1888; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3–4): 302. 1967; FRPS 75: 51. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1036. 1998; FGD 8: 161. 2007.

Subshrubs or herbs 20–30 cm tall; stems procumbent to ascending, striate‑sulcate, subglabrous to sparsely puberulent, woody at base. Leaves slightly succulent, obovate, oblanceolate or somewhat obovate‑spatulate, 2–5 × 0.4–3 cm, base sessile, attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, margin irregularly dentate, both surfaces glabrous; upper leaves appeared smaller in size. Capitula arranged into tight corymbs, peduncle 0.5–2 cm or subsessile. Involucres ovoid‑hemispherical, or broadly campanulate; phyllaries glabrous, in 5–6 series, outer ones broadly ovate, 2 mm across, apex obtuse to rounded; middle layers about 3–4 mm, lanceolate‑oblong, apex acute or obtuse; inner ones 4.5–5 × 0.5–1 mm, linear‑oblong, apex acute‑attenuate. Receptacle flat. Florets purple, outer female ones numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 4–5 mm, minutely 3–4‑dentate or truncate apically, glandular near apex. Central florets few, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, 5 mm, apex bear 5 short triangular lobes with glands outside. Cypselae 0.8–1 mm, oblong, 4–5‑angulate, slightly hairy. Pappus uniseriate, white, 4–5 mm, persistent, those of marginal female florets free; those on central bisexual florets united at base.

Locality: Cape D’ Aguilar, Mai Po, Po Toi Islands. HK sheet 40465; S. Y. Hu 11523, 11967 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina.
Ecology: Coastal areas and tidal flats. Flowering: May–Jan. of the following year.

Plumbago zeylanica L. 白花丹
Sp. Pl. 151. 1753; FKH 156. 1912; FGZ 561, fig. 297. 1956; FRPS 60(1): 4, pl. 1: 1–2. 1987; FGD 3: 315. 1995; FOC 15: 191. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 80, photo 51. 1998.

Semi-climbing subshrub, 1–2 cm tall. Leaves alternate, or sometimes in cluster of 3 on branches, ovate to ovate-elliptic, unequal, 3–10 × 2–2.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, ± decurrent, apex acute or acuminate; petioles often dilated in auricles and amplexicaul, usually with a few small leaves in axils. Spikes terminal and axillary, 8–17 cm, often branched; rhachis glandular; each flower subtended by 3 bracts. Calyx-tube ca. 11 cm, 5-ribbed, with glandular hairs. Corolla white or bluish; tube 17–20 mm; lobes elliptic or obovate, ca. 5 mm, spreading. Ovary oblong; style slender; stigma with 5 linear lobe. Capsule oblong, 5–7 mm, opening transversely.

Locality: Sai Kung, Sha Kok Mei, San Tin, Castle Peak, Cheung Chau. H. C. Tang 18; Y. S. Lau 2418; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 17239).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy lands and thickets. Flowering: Sep. to Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Plumeria rubra L. 雞蛋花
Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753; FRPS 63: 78. 1977; FGD 1: 446, fig. 499. 1987; FOC 16: 154. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 39, fig. 13. 1999.
Plumeria acuminata Aiton, Hort. Kew 2: 70. 1789.
Plumeria acutifolia Poir., Encycl. Suppl. 2: 667. 1811.
Plumeria rubra var. acutifolia (Poir.) Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 810. 1949; FHN 3: 223, pl. 673. 1974 (as P. rubra ‘Acutifolia’).

Trees to 8 m tall. Bark pale green, smooth. Petioles to 7 cm; leaf blade elliptic to very narrowly so, 14 – 30 × 6 – 8 cm, glaucous adaxially, apex acute or acuminate; lateral veins 30 – 40 on each side of midvein, slightly elevated abaxially. Corolla tinged with pink or purple at least abaxially, 4 – 6 cm in diam.; lobes pink, yellow, or white, with a yellow base, 3 – 4.5 × 1.5 – 2.5 cm, obliquely spreading. Follicles oblong, 11 – 25 × 2 – 3 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 141; Y. S. Lau 875, 1636.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian (cultivated); native to Mexico, C America, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Sep.; fruiting: May – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The cultivar with yellowish white flowers was recorded as P. rubra var. acutifolia (Poir.) Bailey previously (Check List HK Plants 56. 1993).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The cultivar with yellowish white flowers was recorded as P. rubra var. acutifolia (Poir.) Bailey previously (Check List HK Plants 56. 1993).

records.text:
Poa annua L. 早熟禾
Sp. Pl. 1: 68. 1753; FFJ 6: 141. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 386. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 159. 2002; FOC 22: 263. 2006; FGD 9: 386, fig. 194. 2009.

Annual or biennial herb, 6–30 cm tall. Culms loosely tufted, erect or geniculate at base, smooth. Leaf blades flat or folded, thin, 1–12 cm × 1–2(–5) mm, apex acutely prow-tipped, often transversely wrinkled, margins slightly scabrid; ligules membranous, collar-shaped, 1–3 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse, margin irregularly dentate, smooth; leaf sheaths slightly compressed, thin, smooth, uppermost closed for ca. 1/3 of length. Panicle open, broadly ovoid to pyramidal, (1–)3–10 cm. Spikelets ovate to oblong, dark to light green, (3–)4–6 mm, florets 3–5, distal fertile florets often female; rachilla internodes 0.5–1.5 mm, smooth, glabrous; glumes unequal, smooth or rarely keeled with hooks, the lower lanceolate to ovate, 1.5–3mm, 1-veined, the upper elliptic or oblong, 2–4 mm, 3-veined; lemmas ovate, 2.2–4 mm, apex and margins broadly membranous; palea narrowly lanceolate, apex blunt to acute, 2–2.5 mm, 2-veined, villous on veins. Anthers 0.6–1 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, 1–1.5 mm, apex villous.

Locality: Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2958; HK sheet 30339.
Distribution: A worldwide weed, also widely distributed in China.
Ecology: Moist shady places. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Podocarpus macrophyllus (Thunb.) Sweet 羅漢松
Hort. Suburb. Londin. 211. 1818; FRPS 7: 412, pl. 93: 1–2. 1978; FOC 4: 83. 1999; FGD 4: 35. 2000.
Taxus macrophyllus Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 895. 1784.

Tree to 15 m tall; trunk to 30 cm d.b.h.; bark grey or greyish brown, irregularly fissured; branches dense, spreading, pale brown. Leaves spirally arranged on upper half of branchlets, sessile; blade linear-lanceolate, oblanceolate, or oblong-oblanceolate, 7–12 cm × 7–10 mm, base cuneate, apex mucronate or acute to long acuminate, margin slightly recurved, dark green and glossy adaxially, greyish green, pale green abaxially, midvein prominently raised adaxially, slightly raised abaxially. Pollen cones axillary, usually in clusters of 3–5, spikelike, 3–5 cm, subsessile, microsporangia ovoid. Seed-bearing structures axillary, solitary, shortly pedunculate. Receptacle red or purplish red when ripe, columnar. Epimatium purplish black when ripe, with white powder. Seed ellipsoid or ovoid, ca. 1 cm in diam., apex rounded, with a projected mucro.

Locality: Coastal hillslopes on eastern seashores. It is also cultivated in urban parks and gardens. P. S. Choi 340; Y. S. Lau 666.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Japan.
Ecology: Open thickets. Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Podocarpus macrophyllus var. maki Sieb. & Zucc. 短葉羅漢松
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(3): 232.1846.
Podocarpus chinensis Wall. ex J. Forbes, Pinet. Woburn. 212.1839; FKH 256. 1912.

A small tree or shrublike. It differs from var. macrophyllus byshorter and denser leaves, 2–7 cm × 3–7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in urban parks and gardens. HK sheet 26927, 26928, 40769.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Japan. Possibly native in Guangdong, Taiwan and Zhejiang.
Ecology: Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Podocarpus neriifolius D. Don 百日青
Lambert, Descr. Pinus. 2: 21. 1824; FRPS 7: 409, pl. 92: 1– 4.1978; FOC 4: 82. 1999; FGD 4: 35, fig. 24. 2000.

Tree to 25 m tall; trunk usually to 50 cm d.b.h.; bark greyish brown, shallowly fissured; branches spreading or ascending. Leaf blade lanceolate, leathery, usually slightly curved, 7–15 × 0.9 –1.3 cm, base cuneate into short petiole, apex long acuminate, midvein raised adaxially, flat or slightly raised abaxially. Pollen cones solitary or in clusters of 2 or 3, 2.5–5 cm, basal bracts numerous, spirally arranged. Seed-bearing structures axillary, solitary; peduncle 0.9 –2.2 cm. Receptacle orange-red when ripe, obconical-ellipsoid, 8–10 × 5–8 mm, base with 2 subulate bracts 2–6 mm. Epimatium purplish red when ripe. Seed ovoid or ovoid-subglobose, 0.8–1.6 cm, apex rounded or obtuse.

Locality: Victoria Peak. HK sheet 7044.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Nepal, NE India,Sikkim, Bhutan, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Thailand, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: In forests. Pollinating: May; seed maturing: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pogonatherum crinitum (Thunb.) Kunth 金絲草
Enum. Pl. 1: 478. 1833; FHN 4: 457, fig. 1246. 1977; FFJ 6: 237, fig. 204. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 106, pl. 24: 14–21. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 570, pl. 240. 2000; FOC 22: 591. 2006; FGD 9: 470, fig. 245. 2009.
Andropogon crinitus Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 903. 1784.
Pogonatherum saccharoideum auct. non P. Beauv.: FHK 421. 1861; FKH 320. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculate, tufted, 10–30 cm tall, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or puberulous, mouth long ciliate; leaf blades linear, flat, 1.5–5 × 0.1–0.4 cm, inrolled, scaberulous-puberulous, apex acute; ligule short, ciliate. Inflorescence a solitary raceme, yellowish; rachis internodes and pedicels both compressed, 1/3–2/3 spikelet length, hairs silky white. Sessile spikelet 1–2 mm, membranous; callus hairs equal to or slightly longer than spikelet; lower glume flat, scabrid on abaxial surface, apex truncate, ciliate with ca. 0.2 mm hairs; upper glume boat-shaped, 1-veined to keeled, awn 1.5–1.8 cm; lower floret absent or only lemma present; upper lemma slightly shorter than lower glume, 2-lobed, with an slender awn from the sinus; awn 1.5–2.5 cm, strongly geniculate near base, palea shorter than lemma, broad ovate, 2-veined; stamen 1, anther ca. 1 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet but smaller; lower glume awnless. Caryopsis ovate-oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2177; Y. S. Lau 1041, 1791.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, New Guinea, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Forests, ravines, shade and moist places along roadsides and streams. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses. Medicinal (folklore).

Pogonatherum paniceum (Lam.) Hack. 金髮草

Allg. Bot. Z. Syst. 12: 178. 1906; FRPS 10(2): 102, pl. 24: 1–13. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 570. 2000; FYN 9: 631, fig. 106: 1–3. 2003; FOC 22: 592. 2006; FGD 9: 470. 2009.

Saccharum paniceum Lam., Encycl. 1: 595. 1785.

Pogonatherum saccharoideum P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 56: 176–177, pl. 11, fig. 7. 1812, nom. illeg. superfl.; FHK 421. 1861; FKH 320. 1912.


Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 30–60 cm tall, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or puberulous, mouth long ciliate; leaf blades stiff, 1.5–5.5 × 0.15–0.4 cm, scabrid, apex acuminate. Raceme 1.3–3 cm (excluding awns), yellowish; rachis internodes and pedicels ca. 1/2 spikelet length, hairs silky white. Sessile spikelet 2.5–3 mm, thinly cartilaginous; callus hairs shorter than spikelet; lower glume scabrid or puberulous on back, apex ciliate with 0.5–1 mm hairs; upper glume awn 1–2 cm; lower floret male, lemma slightly shorter than lower glume, palea subequaling lemma; awn of upper lemma 1.5–2 cm, weakly geniculate near base, column not strongly demarcated, limb very fine. Stamens 2, anthers ca. 1.8 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet but smaller; lower glume awnless.


Locality: High Island, Sai Kung, Sha Lo Tung. S. Y. Hu 8555, 8901; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20719 (CUHK).

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam, SW Asia (Arabia), Australia (Queensland).

Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, streams; alt. 100–2300 m. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.

Pogostemon auricularius (L.) Hassk. 水珍珠菜
Tijdsch. Nat. Geschied. 10: 127. 1843; FRPS 66: 379, pl. 79: 1 – 7. 1977; FOC 17: 262. 1994; FGD 3: 454. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 508, pl. 226. 1998.
Dysophylla auricularia (L.) Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14: 826 – 827. 1826; FHK 275. 1861; FKH 208. 1912.
Mentha auricularia L., Mant. Pl. ed. 1, 81. 1767.

Annual herbs, 0.4–1.5 m tall. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, rooting at nodes, densely yellow spreading hirsute. Leaves opposite, shortly petiolate, upper stem leaves subsessile; leaf blade oblong to ovate‑oblong, 2.5–7 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, rarely cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin serrate, yellow hirsute on both surfaces and with scattered impressed glands on abaxial surface. Spikes 6–18 cm, apex caudate‑acuminate, continuous or sometimes interrupted at base; bracts ovate‑lanceolate, as long as corolla, margin strigose. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1 × 1 mm, glabrous, yellow glandular; teeth broadly triangular, margin pilose. Corolla purplish to white, ca. 2–2.5 mm, glabrous. Stamens long‑exserted, exserted parts bearded. Nutlets brown, subglobose, ca. 0.5 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Tai Tam, Mau Ping, Pak Sha O, Tai Po, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ha Hang, Luk Keng, Plover Cove, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 541; HK sheet 39645, 39825.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places along streams, in forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Pogostemon championii Prain 短穗刺蕊草
Bull. Misc. Inform. 1908: 254. 1908; FKH 208. 1912; FRPS 66: 369. 1977; FOC 17: 259. 1994; FGD 3: 454. 1995.
Pogostemon parviflorus Benth., sensu FHK 275. 1861.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, to 80 cm tall. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, initially pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles of lower stem leaves 3–6 cm, those of upper leaves 1–1.5 cm, sparsely strigose; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 6–11 × 2.5–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin double serrate or crenate, sparsely appressed pubescent on adaxial surface, strigose along veins abaxially. Spikes short‑cylindric, 1.5–4 × 1 cm, continuous or rarely interrupted, appressed pubescent; bracts ovate‑lanceolate, 3–4 mm, ca. as long as calyx. Calyx narrowly campanulate, ca. 4 mm, pubescent abaxially; teeth 5, triangular, subequal, about 1/3 the length of calyx. Corolla purplish, slightly longer than calyx, glabrous, margin sparsely ciliate, lobes subequal. Filaments bearded. Style lobes subequal. Nutlets broadly ovoid, smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Fung Yuen, Ha Hang. Y. S. Lau 2825; HK sheet 22172, 30337.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Pollia secundiflora (Blume) Bakh. f. 長花枝杜若（杜若）
Bekn. Fl. Java. 10 (Fam. 211): 10. 1949; FRPS 13(3): 89, pl. 24: 2 – 3. 1997; FOC 24: 34. 2000; FGD 6: 316. 2005.
Commelina secundiflora Blume, Enum. Pl. Javae 1: 3. 1827.
Aclisia sorzogonensis E. Mey., Reliq. Haenk. 1: 138, pl. 25. 1827.
Pollia sorzogonensis (E. Mey. ex Presl) Endl., Gen. Pl. 1029. 1836; FHK 377. 1861; FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb, 1–2 m tall, with slender and long horizontal rhizomes. Stems erect, sparsely white pubescent. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath ca. 2.5 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade broadly ovatelanceolate or oblong, 10–15 × 3–8 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, verrucose adaxially, densely puberulent abaxially. Panicle with 3–4 branches, with peduncle to more than 20 cm, densely brown-yellow hooked hirsute; involucral bracts leaf-like, nearly as large as leaves, distal ones much smaller, to 5 mm, densely brown-yellow hirsute; bracts membranous. Sepals nearly orbicular, boat-shaped, ca. 3 mm, glabrous, persistent. Petals white, obovate, shallowly boat-shaped, ca. 5 mm. Stamens 6; fertile stamens 3, anterior; staminodes 3, with shorter filaments. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Causeway Bay. C. Wright 545 (K), H. F. Hance 1035 (BM).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.

Pollia siamensis (Craib) Faden ex D. Y. Hong 長柄杜若
FRPS 13(3): 89, pl. 24: 4. 1997; FOC 24: 34. 2000; FGD 6: 316, fig. 180. 2005.

Perennial herb, 30–100 cm tall, with slender and long horizontal rhizomes; stems erect or ascending, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves alternate; leaf sheath 2–4 cm, glabrous or sparsely puberulent; leaf blade elliptic to narrowly ovate, 10–25 × 2.5–8 cm, base narrowed into a petiole of 2–4 cm, apex acuminate, glabrous or subglabrous adaxially on both surfaces. Panicle 5 – 10 cm including the peduncle, densely glandular pubescent; involucral bracts leaf-like, but much smaller than leaves, densely glandular pubescent; bracts membranous, often persistent. Sepals ovate-orbicular, boat-shaped, ca. 3 mm, glabrous. Petals white, ovate-elliptic, shallowly boat-shaped, ca. 4 mm. Stamens 6; fertile stamens 3, anterior; staminodes 3, with shorter filaments. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 2432; HK sheet 38314.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, S Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.

Polycarpaea corymbosa (L.) Lam. 白鼓釘
Tabl. Encycl. 2: 129. 1793; FHK 22. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FHN 1: 378, fig. 197. 1964; FGD 2: 81. 1991; FRPS 26: 63, pl. 13: 4 –7. 1996; FOC 6: 7. 2001.
Achyranthes corymbosa L., Sp. Pl. 205. 1753.

Perennial herb, 15–35 cm tall. Stems erect, more or less hoary with loose cotton hairs. Leaves sessile, often clustered at nodes in false whorls; leaf blade linear to subulate, 15 –20 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute, glabrescent. Flowers many, in dense cymes and forming broad terminal dichotomous corymbs. Bracts lanceolate, scarious and translucent. Pedicels slender, white-puberulent. Sepals lanceolate, 2–3 mm, scarious and shining, white or reddish brown. Petals broadly ovate, obtuse, not half so long as sepals. Stamens shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; style single, entire. Capsule ovoid, not half so long as the persistent sepals.

Locality: Silverstrand, Deep Water Bay. L. Gibbs 7665; HK sheet 297, 2625.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian; throughout tropical regions.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, waste places and sandy seashores. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polycarpon prostratum (Forssk.) Asch. & Schweinf. ex Asch. 多莢草
Oesterr. Bot. Z. 39: 128. 1889; FOC 6: 6. 2001.

Annual herb. Stems diffuse or prostrate, 10–25 cm, much branched, usually pubescent, rarely glabrescent. Leaves opposite or almost in whorls; petioles very short; leaf blade oblanceolate, linear-oblanceolate, spathulate or narrowly elliptic, 6–20 × 1.5 – 5 mm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous, veins obscure; stipules ovate-lanceolate, about 1/4 the length of leaf blade, scarious. Cymes axillary or terminal, 2–4 cm. Flowers small, ca. 3 mm in diam.; sepal lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, midvein raised, apex obtuse and more or less hooked, margin hyaline; petals often fewer than 5, linear oblong, less than half the length of sepals; stamens 5, opposite with sepals. Capsules ovoid, shorter than sepals.

Locality: Ho Pui Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1490.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; tropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Open fields, farmlands. Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.

Polygala chinensis L. 華南遠志（金不換）

Sp. Pl. 2: 704. 1753; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 577, fig. 2884. 1972; C. A. Pendry, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 503. 2001.

Polygala glomerata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 426. 1790; FHK 44. 1861; FKH 38. 1912; FYN 3: 289, pl. 81: 19– 27. 1983; FGD 2: 58. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 573, pl. 294. 1993; FRPS 43(3): 186. 1997.


Annual herb, erect, 6–30 cm tall. Stems simple or ± branched, curved-pubescent. Petioles 1–3 mm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, varied in shape, often elliptic, or oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, 1–7 × 1–1.5 cm, base cuneate to rounded or cordate, apex obtuse, mucronate, or rarely emarginate, margin entire, slightly revolute, glabrous or slightly fine pubescent on both surfaces, midvein prominent abaxially, impressed adaxially, lateral veins inconspicuous. Racemes super-axillary, 0.5–2 cm, shorter than leaves. Flowers white or pink, spreading or pendulous, 4–5 mm. Pedicels ca. 1.5 mm, pubescent. Bracts 2, caducous, lanceolate, puberulous. Sepals persistent, ciliate; outer 3 ovate-oblong, ca. 1.5 mm; inner 2 falcate, petaloid, ca. 4.5 mm, 5-veined. Petals connate at base; lateral ones shorter than keel, obovate, with fasciculate white hairs at base adaxially; keel cucullate, ca. 4 mm, apex with 2 bundles of filiform appendages. Stamens almost equally connate in a single bundle. Ovary compressed globose, ca. 1 mm in diam., ciliate. Capsule compressed globose, 3–5 mm in diam., narrowly winged, ciliate; wings 4–6 mm. Seeds black, ovoid, silky hairy; arils white, cucullate, 2-lobed.


Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 21, 1153; P. S. Choi 253.

Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Vietnam, Philippines.

Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.; fruiting: May–Nov.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The species was reported as Polygala glomerata Lour. previously (Check List HK Plants 193. 2002; 68. 2004.)

Medicinal (folklore).

Polygala fallax Hemsl. 黃花倒水蓮（屈頭雞）
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 23: 59. 1886; FYN 3: 271, pl. 75: 10– 19. 1983; FFJ 3: 159, fig. 114. 1987; FGD 2: 53. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 151. 1997.
Polygala aureocauda Dunn, Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew, 1911(4): 188. 1911; FKH 38. 1912.
Polygala arillata auct. non Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don: FHK 45. 1861.

Shrub to treelets, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets pubescent when young, later glabrescent. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, pubescent, sulcate adaxially; leaf blade papery, lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 8–17 × 3–6.5 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex acuminate, margin entire, puberulous along veins adaxially, pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 5–10 pairs, reticulate veins distinct. Racemes terminal or axillary, sometimes leaf-opposed, 8–30 cm, apex pendulous; peduncles nearly absent. Flowers yellow, 1.6 cm. Pedicels ca. 3 mm, pubescent. Sepals 5, ciliate, caducous after anthesis; outer 3 small, unequal, upper one helmet-shaped, 6–7 mm, other 2 ovate to elliptic, ca. 3 mm; inner 2 larger, petaloid, oblong, 1.2–1.5 cm, base attenuate, apex rounded. Petals yellow, lower 2/3 connate; lateral 2 narrowly oblong, ca. 1 cm, keel hooded, ca. 1.2 cm, apex with a bundle of fimbriate appendages. Ovary subglobose, 3–4 mm in diam., narrowly winged, ciliate. Capsule compressed subglobose, 1–1.4 cm in diam., with many longitudinal veins. Seeds brown-black, globose, ca. 4 mm in diam., densely white pubescent; aril membranous, 3-lobed, lobes narrowly oblong, 2 lobes forming a cap and covered 1/3 of the seed, 1 lobe hooked upward.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 468; Y. W. Lam 1662; HK sheet 39422.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polygala hongkongensis Hemsl. 香港遠志
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 23: 60. 1886; FKH 38. 1912; FFJ 3: 161, fig. 116. 1987; FGD 2: 57. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 190. 1997.
Polygala elegans auct. non Wall. ex Royle: FHK 44. 1861, p.p.

Perennial herb or subshrub, erect, 15–50 cm tall. Stems much branched; branches slender, puberulous. Petioles 1–3 mm, pubescent; leaf blade papery or membranous, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 1–6.5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, ± revolute, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 pairs, inconspicuous. Racemes terminal, 3–8 cm, rachis and pedicels pubescent. Flowers purplish red, 7–9 mm. Pedicels 1–2 mm. Bracts 3, subulate, ca. 1 mm, caducous. Sepals persistent, ciliate; outer 3 lanceolate, boat-shaped, ca. 3.5 mm, 1-veined; inner 2 obliquely ovate, petaloid, 5–8 × 3–5 mm. Petals connate at base; lateral ones oblong, 3–5 mm, pubescent at base abaxially; keel cucullate, ca. 5 mm, apex with 2 bundles of fimbriate appendages. Ovary compressed globose, ca. 1.5 mm, shortly stipitate, glabrous. Capsule suborbicular, ca. 5 mm in diam., narrowly winged, apex retuse. Seeds 2, black, ovoid, ca. 3.5 mm, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., apex beak-like; arils 3-lobed, half as long as seeds.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 609; HK sheet 39722, 40743.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected by J. G. Champion, C. Wright and J. Lamont respectively from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected by J. G. Champion, C. Wright and J. Lamont respectively from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Polygala japonica Houtt. 瓜子金

Handl. Pl.-Kruidk. 10: 89. 1779; FTW 3: 558, pl. 726. 1977; FYN 3: 281, pl. 80: 1 – 8. 1983; FGD 2: 58, fig. 38. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 573, pl. 295. 1993; FRPS 43(3): 179. 1997.

Polygala elegans auct. non Wall. ex Royle: FHK 44. 1861, p.p.

Polygala sibirica auct. non L.: FKH 39. 1912.


Perennial herb, 15–20 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, much branched, curved-pubescent. Petioles ca. 1 mm, pubescent; leaf blade thickly papery or subleathery, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, rarely lanceolate, 1–3 × 0.3–1 cm, base broadly rounded, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous or pubescent on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 pairs, prominent on both surfaces, pubescent. Racemes leaf-opposed, or extra-axillary, 1–5 cm. Flowers purple or bluish purple, ca. 7 mm. Pedicels ca. 5 mm, slender, puberulous; bracts caducous, lanceolate. Sepals persistent, ciliate; outer 3 lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, pubescent abaxially; inner 2 ovate to oblong, petaloid, ca. 7 mm, 3–5-veined. Petals connate at base; lateral ones oblong, ca. 6 mm, pubescent at base adaxially; keel cucullate, apex with 2 bundles of fimbriate appendages. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm in diam., winged. Capsule orbicular, ca. 6 mm in diam. with wing, apex retuse, margin broadly winged, not ciliate. Seeds 2, black, compressed ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., white pubescent; arils unequal, 2-lobed, half as long as seeds.


Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 2332.

Distribution: NE, N, NW, E, C, S, SW China; Korea, Japan, Russia (E Siberia), NE India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Philippines, New Guinea.

Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Aug.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polygala latouchei Franch. 大葉金牛（岩生遠志）
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 46: 206. 1899; FFJ 3: 160, fig. 115. 1987; FGD 2: 55, fig. 36: 9–12. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 165, pl. 37: 1–9. 1997.
Polygala nimborum Dunn, FKH 39. 1912.

Subshrub, 5–20 cm tall. Stems simple or branched at base, often with raised leaf scars, curved-pubescent. Leaves crowded on upper part of branches; petioles 5–8 mm, pubescent, narrowly winged; leaf blade papery, ovate-lanceolate to obovate or elliptic-lanceolate, 4–10 × 2–4 cm, base obliquely cuneate, apex rounded and mucronate, margin entire, reddish or dark purple abaxially, green adaxially, ± pubescent on both surfaces or glabrous abaxially; midvein slightly raised on both surfaces, lateral veins 4–5 pairs, reticulate veinlets indistinct. Racemes terminal or axillary, solitary or in pairs, 1–6 cm, pubescent, densely flowered. Flowers pink or purplish red, ca. 1 cm. Pedicels 1.5–3 mm; bract 1, caducous, ovate-lanceolate, ca. 3–5 mm. Sepals caducous, glabrous; outer 3 ovate, subequal, ca. 1.5 mm; inner 2 elliptic, petaloid, ca. 5 mm, 3–7-veined. Petals pink to purple-red, membranous, lower 3/4 connate; lateral ones narrowly elliptic, ca. 8 mm; keel shorter than lateral petals, cucullate, apex with 2 trilobed cockscomb-shaped appendages. Ovary obovoid, narrowly winged, ca. 1 mm in diam., glabrous. Capsule suborbicular, ca. 4–5 mm in diam., narrowly winged, not veined. Seeds ovoid, black, ca. 1.2 mm in diam.; arils wing-shaped, yellow-brown, as long as seeds.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung. HK sheet 39763, 41025.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Streamsides. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polygala polifolia C. Presl 小花遠志
Rel. Haenk. 2: 101. 1835; FTW 3: 558. 1977; C. A. Pendry, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 514. 2001.
Polygala arvensis auct. non Willd. (1802): FYN 3: 283, pl. 81: 1– 9. 1983; FRPS 43(3): 180, pl. 42: 1 – 9. 1997.
Polygala telephioides auct. non Willd., FKH 38. 1912; FHN 1: 366. 1964.
Polygala brachystachya DC., Prodr. 326. 1824, non Poiret (1816), nom illeg.
Polygala chinensis L. f. arvensis (Willd.) Chodat, Mem. Soc. Phys. Geneve 31(2): 386. 1893.
Polygala chinensis auct. non L.: FGD 2: 56. 1991.

Annual herb, 5–25 cm tall. Stems simple or much branched, diffuse, densely curved-pubescent. Petioles very short, pubescent; leaf blade thickly papery, obovate, elliptic to oblong, 1–1.8 cm × 2–6 mm, base broadly cuneate to obtuse, apex obtuse to acute, margin entire, slightly revolute, glabrous on both surfaces or sparsely pubescent; midvein conspicuous, lateral veins inconspicuous. Racemes axillary, extra-axillary, or leaf-opposed, ca. 1 cm, shorter than leaves; bracts 3, minute, caducous, ovate, ciliate. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm, pubescent. Sepals persistent, outer 3 ovate, 1.2–3 × 1–1.2 mm, 1-veined, ciliate; inner 2 asymmetrical, falcate, 2–2.5 mm, 5-veined. Petals bluish purple, connate at base; lateral ones obtriangular, asymmetrical; keel cucullate, longer than lateral petals, ca. 2 mm, apex with 20 laciniate appendages. Stamens unequally connate in three bundles. Ovary obovoid, ca. 1 mm in diam., ciliate. Capsule suborbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam., margin minutely winged, slightly ciliate; wings 3–4 mm. Seeds 2, black, oblong, ca. 1.5 × 1 mm, silky hairy; arils white, 3-lobed.

Locality: Aberdeen, Shek O, Ninepin Group. H. C. Tang 1997; S. P. Lau 140; HK sheet 30746.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang; SE Asia, New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Grassland near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polygonum plebeium R. Br. 腋花蓼（習見蓼）
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holl. 420. 1810; FHK 287. 1861; FKH 217. 1912; FHN 1: 388. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 308. 1996; FRPS 25: 11, pl. 1: 1–3. 1998; FGD 4: 89, fig. 59. 2000; FYN 11: 309. 2000; FOC 5: 285. 2003.

Annual herb. Stems prostrate, branched from the base, 10 – 40 cm, internodes usually shorter than leaves. Leaves subsessile or with a very short petiole; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, 5 –15 × 2– 4 mm, base narrowly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins obscure. Ocrea tubular, 2.5–3 mm, white and translucent, apex lacerate. Flowers 3– 6 in axillary clusters. Pedicels slender, 1–2 mm, articulate at middle. Bracts scarious. Perianth green, margin white or pink, 1–1.5 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic. Stamens 5; filaments slightly dilated at base, included. Ovary 3-angled; styles 3 rarely 2, very short; stigmas capitate. Achenes broadly ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm, sharply 3-ribbed or convex on both sides, blackish brown, smooth and shining, enclosed in the fleshy persistent perianth.

Locality: Fanling, Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang, Mui Wo. Y. S. Lau 2450; HK sheet 9932, 32384.
Distribution: Dispersed over all parts of China except Xizang; also in Japan, India, Australia, Europe and Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated and in waste places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Polypogon fugax Nees ex Steud. 棒頭草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 184. 1854; FFJ 6: 123, fig. 92. 1995; FOC 22: 362. 2006; FGD 9: 393. 2009.
Polypogon littoralis auct. non Sm.: FHK 427. 1861; FKH 326. 1912.

Annual herb, 10–75 cm tall. Culms tufted, geniculate at base, mostly glabrous. Leaf blades narrowly to broadly linear, 2.5–15 × 3–4 cm, scabrid or abaxial surface smooth, apex acute; ligule membranous, 3–8 mm, apex 2-fid or irregularly toothed. Panicle spikelike, 4–15 × 1–3.5 cm, pale green or tinged with purple; branches narrowly ascending, up to 4 cm, bearing densely clustered spikelets. Spikelets narrowly oblong, 1-flowered, 2–2.5 mm; glumes narrowly oblong, puberulous, vein scabrid-aculeate, margins ciliate in lower half, slightly notched at the apex, with an awn equal to or shorter than glume body; lemma papery, elliptic, 1–1.2 mm, apex shortly 4-toothed, midvein extended into a fine, straight, ca. 2 mm awn; palea membranous, as long as lemma, oblong. Stamens 3. Anthers ca. 0.7 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: No precise locality. HK sheet 41965.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Xinjiang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and warmtemperate regions of Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Polypogon monspeliensis (L.) Desf. 長芒棒頭草
Fl. Atlant. 1: 67. 1798; FKH 326. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 253, pl. 62: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 6: 123, fig. 93. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 364. 2000; FOC 22: 362. 2006; FGD 9: 394, fig. 201. 2009.
Alopecurus monspeliensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 61. 1753.

Annual herb, up to 60 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 1.5 mm in diam., 2–3-noded. Leaf blades narrowly to broadly linear, 2–13 × 0.2–0.9 cm, adaxial surface and margins scabrid, abaxial surface smooth, apex acute; ligule papery, tongueshaped, 3–8 mm. Panicle spike-like, 1.5–16 × 1–3.5 cm, pale green, thickly clothed in yellow bristles. Spikelets narrowly oblong, 1-flowered, 1.5–3 mm; glumes as long as the spikelet, papery, narrowly obovate-oblong, vein scabrid-aculeate, margins ciliate, slightly notched at the apex, with a 4–7 mm straight awn; lemma papery, obovate, 1–1.2 mm, apex slightly 4-toothed, midvein extended into a fine, readily deciduous awn; palea membranous, as long as lemma, oblong. Stamens 3. Anthers ca. 0.8 mm. Caryopsis obovate-oblong, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. H. G. Goddard s.n. (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; tropical and warm-temperate regions throughout the world.
Ecology: Moist places, shallow waters. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Polyscias fruticosa (L.) Harms 南洋参
Engel. Jahrb. 56: 412. 1921; FGD 1: 288. 1987.
Panax fruticosa L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 2: 1513. 1763.

Shrub or small tree, 2–5 m tall, glabrous. Leaves 3–5-pinnately compound, 30–60 cm; petioles (2–)5–15 cm, clasping at base; petiolules 1–5 cm; leaflets subleathery, narrowly ovate or oblong-lanceolate, 2–10(–18) × 0.2–5 cm, base narrowly cuneate to attenuate, apex acute, margin spinulose-serrate, sometimes irregularly incised, inconspicuously 3-veined at base, lateral veins 5–10 pairs. Inflorescence a large terminal panicle, consisting of numerous umbels. Pedicels 1–5 mm. Ovary 2–3(–4)-locular; styles free nearly to base. Fruit orbicular to ovate-orbicular, 4–5 × 4.5–6 mm

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 12767, 34766, 34808.
Distribution: Native to Malaysia and Polynesia, widely cultivated in tropical regions. Flowering: Aug–Sep.
Uses: Ornamantal.

Polyspora axillaris (Roxb. ex Ker-Gawl.) Sweet 大頭茶
Hort. Brit. 1: 61. 1827; FHN 1: 501. 1964.
Camellia axillaris Roxb. ex Ker-Gawl., Bot. Reg. t. 349. 1818.
Gordonia axillaris (Roxb. ex Ker-Gawl.) D. Dietr., Syn. Pl. 4: 863. 1847; FGD 2: 148. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 207. 1998.
Gordonia anomala Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 126. 1826; FHK 29. 1861; FKH 45. 1912.

Tree or shrub, up to 8 m tall; young branchlets and terminal buds densely pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.0 –1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong-ovate to oblanceolate, 6–15 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or remotely crenate on distal part, dark green and glabrous adaxially, paler and slightly pubescent abaxially when young, midvein impressed adaxially, veins obscure on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or in pairs, nearly sessile, 7–13 cm in diam., bracteoles 4 – 5, deciduous, suborbicular, densely pubescent abaxially; sepals 5, ovate, 1–1.5 cm, densely pubescent abaxially, persistent; petals 5, white, broadly obovate, 3.5–5 cm, emarginate at the apex, pubescent abaxially; stamens many, unequal, 1.5 –2 cm, glabrous, connate at base and adnate to petals at the base; ovary 5-locular, pubescent; style ca. 2 cm, sericeous. Capsule oblong or oblong-ovoid, ca. 5 cm, pilose. Seeds compressed, oblong, 1.5–2 cm including wing.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2258; Y. W. Lam 418; K. L. Yip 4187.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and early secondary forests. Flowering: Sep.– Oct.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (timber).

Polytrias indica (Houtt.) Veldkamp 單序草
Blumea 36: 180. 1991; FOC 22: 593. 2006.
Phleum indicum Houtt., Nat. Hist. 13: 198. 1782.
Polytrias amaura (Buse) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 788. 1891; FRPS 10(2): 99, pl. 23: 1–5. 1997.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, flowering shoots ascending, 10–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths lightly compressed, glabrous or rarely pubescent; leaf blades purplish glaucous, linear-lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.2–0.4 cm, stiffly pilose with tubercle-based hairs, apex acuminate; ligule 0.2–0.5 mm. Raceme 2–7 cm, densely pilose, shortly exserted from uppermost leaf sheath at maturity; rachis internodes and pedicels much shorter than spikelet, golden-ciliate. Spikelets 3 per node, oblong or linear-oblong, brown, densely hairy with soft golden hairs; callus hairs 1/3 spikelet length; lower glume membranous, long villous, hairs extending beyond glume apex; upper glume oblong, submembranous, truncate, densely pubescent except near base, keel villous on the upper; upper lemma shorter than upper glume, cordate, bidenate, ciliate, with an awn (ca. 1 cm) from the sinus, puberulous; anthers 2.5–3 mm, stigmas exserted from apex of spikelet.

Locality: Happy Valley, Repulse Bay. L. T. Lo 216; Y. S. Lau 3079.
Distribution: Vietnam, Myanmar, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines; introduced elsewhere as a lawn grass.
Ecology: Grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Pongamia pinnata (L.) Merr. 水黄皮

Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 271. 1917.

Cytisus pinnatus L., Sp. Pl. 741. 1753.

Pongamia pinnata (L.) Pierre, Fl. Forest Cochinch. t. 385. 1899, nom. illeg.; FRPS 40: 183. 1994; FGD 5: 238. 2003.

Pongamia glabra Vent., Jardin de la Malmaison 28, pl. 28. 1803; FHK 94. 1861; FKH 86. 1912.


Tree, 8–15 m tall. Young branchlets glabrous or puberulent, old branchlets densely grey-lenticellate. Leaves odd-pinnate, 20–25 cm; leaflets 2–3 pairs, ovate, broad-elliptic to oblong, 5 – 10 × 4 – 8 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded or truncate, apex shortly acuminate or rounded. Racemes axillary, 15– 20 cm. Flowers paired on nodes of rachis. Pedicels 5– 8 mm; bracteoles 2. Calyx ca. 3 mm, teeth obtuse. Corolla white or pink, 12–14 mm; petals clawed; vexillum silk-hairy abaxially, margin involute; wings oblong; keel slightly curved. Pods elliptic, 4– 5 × 1.5 – 2.5 cm, slightly verrucose, top with slightly curved beak. Seeds 1, brown, reniform.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2149, 2708, 2869.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia to Australia.

Ecology: Seashore, near streams and ponds. Flowering: May– Jun.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.

Uses: Timber, ornamental.

Popowia pisocarpa (Blume) Endl. 嘉陵花
Walpers, Repert. Bot. Syst. 1: 74. 1842; FHN 1: 249, fig. 122. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 108, pl. 48. 1979; FGD 2: 27, fig. 21. 1991.
Guatteria pisocarpa Blume, Bijdr. 21. 1825.

Shrubs, to ca. 1 m. Young branches rufous-pubescent. Leaves membranous; petioles 3– 4 × ca. 1.5 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades 9 – 11 × ca. 4 cm, elliptic, oblong or obovate, glabrous except sparsely pubescent veins adaxially, base cuneate, apex acute; midvein impressed adaxially; secondary veins 6 – 9 pairs. Inflorescences supra-axillary or leaf-opposed, 1 – 2( – 4)-flowered. Flowers white; pedicels ca. 6.5 –7.5 mm long, slender; bracts ca. 1 mm long, pubescent. Sepals 1.5 –2 × 1.5 –2.5 mm, triangular-ovate, pubescent abaxially, glabrous adaxially, persistent. Outer petals ca. 2 × 1.5–2 mm; inner petals ca. 3 × 2.7–4 mm. Stamens 15 – 18 per flower, ca. 1 mm long; connective truncate or slightly concave. Carpels 3 – 6 per flower; ovary pubescent; ovule 1, basal; style very short; stigma subcapitate. Monocarps 3 – 5 per fruit, ca. 6 × 5.5 mm, flattened-globose, glabrous; stipes 3 – 3.5 mm. Seeds ca. 5.5 mm in diam., globose, brown; raphes ribbed.

Locality: Lam Tsuen Valley. C. L. Law et al. 00/09 (HKU); Y. W. Lam 200, 446.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Porophyllum ruderale (Jacq.) Cass. 葩葩洛（暫名）
Dict. Sci. Nat. ed. 2, 43: 56. 1826; Fl. N. Amer. 21: 233 – 234. 2006.
Kleinia ruderalis Jacq., Enum. Syst. Pl. 8, 28. 1760.

Annual herbs, 30–80 cm tall. Stems erect and branched, glabrous. Leaves odorous, simple and alternate, elliptic, 1.5–3.5 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded and mucronulate, both surfaces glabrous, midvein prominent on lower side, margin entire and somewhat undulate, with linear oil glands 1–2 mm long growing along leaf margin; petiole 0.3–1.2 cm. Capitula homogamous, discoid, in corymbose arrangement; peduncles 3–6 cm, glabrous. Involucres herbaceous green, cylindric, 1.8–2 × 0.3–0.4 cm wide; phyllaries 1‑seriate, united at anthesis, without calycule at base, divided into 5 linear‑lanceolate involucral bracts and gradually spread out at fruiting stage, each segment 1.2–2 mm broad, margin scarious, apex acuminate or acute. Receptacle small and plain, alveolate, areoles sometimes with remnants of vascular tissue after fruit dispersal. All florets bisexual and fertile, about 50–60 per head or more, corolla yellow, slightly hairy outside, 13 mm, lower part slender filiform‑tubular with length 11–11.5 mm, upper part broaden as funnelform with length 1.5–2 mm, apex 5‑lobed, lobes acute‑ovate; anther bases rounded, apical appendages ovate and acute; stylar branches approximately 3 mm, exserted outside the involucres, bearing hairy subulate apical appendages. Cypselae narrow cylindric, 8 × 0.5–0.6 mm, black or blackish brown, hirtellous with brown adpressed hair pointing upward. Pappus persistent, 8–10 mm, capillary, pale brown.

Locality: Tai Po, Fung Yuen. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24093, 24097 (CUHK).
Distribution: SW United States, Mexico, West Indies, C & S America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep.

Portulaca oleracea L. 馬齒莧
Sp. Pl. 445. 1753; FHK 127. 1861; FKH 41. 1912; FHN 1: 384. 1964; FGD 2: 91. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 336, photo 144. 1996; FRPS 26: 38. 1996; FOC 5: 443. 2003.

Annual succulent herb. Stems prostrate or spreading, 10 –50 cm or longer, usually purplish, glabrous, with inconspicuous scales or minute hairs in axils of leaves. Leaves alternate or subopposite, subsessile; leaf blade flat, obovate to cuneate-oblong, 1–2.5(–4) × 0.5 –2 cm, apex obtuse to rounded. Flowers yellow, solitary or in terminal clusters of 3– 5, sessile above the leafy bracts. Sepals ca. 6 mm. Petals yellow, broadly obovate, fugacious and scarcely exceeding the sepals. Stamens 7–10(–15); styles mostly 5. Capsule ovoid, opening transversely.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. T. Dunn 1072, 4204; HK sheet 298.
Distribution: Worldwide weed.
Ecology: Cultivated grounds, waste places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Portulaca pilosa L. 毛馬齒莧
Sp. Pl. 445. 1753; FHN 1: 384. 1964; FGD 2: 91. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 336, photo 145. 1996; FRPS 26: 38. 1996; FOC 5: 442. 2003.

Annual succulent herb. Stems erect or ascending, 10 –30 cm tall, with long hairs in axils of leaves. Leaves alternate, short petiolate; leaf blade ± terete, linear to elliptic, 0.4 –2.8 × 0.1–0.4 cm, apex acute. Flowers yellow, solitary or in terminal clusters of 2–10, sessile, surrounded by 4 –9 verticillate leaves and axillary hairs. Sepals oblong, 2– 6 mm. Petals 4– 6, obovate, 2.5 –12 × 1.8 –11 mm, red, pink or yellow. Stamens usually 20 –30; style 3 –7-lobed. Capsule ovoid or subglobose, opening transversely.

Locality: Shek O, Lan Nai Wan, Tseng Tau, Pui O, Cheung Chau, Waglan Island. H. C. Tang 2097; K. L. Yip 4194; Y. S. Lau 1473.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Malesia and tropical America.
Ecology: Sandy places near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Potamogeton pusillus L. 小眼子菜
Sp. Pl. 127. 1753; FRPS 8: 44, pl. 12. 1992; FGD 6: 306. 2005; FOC 23: 111. 2010.

Submersed herb, without rhizomes. Stems cylindrical or subcylindrical, 0.5 mm in diam., branched, internodes 1.5–6 cm. Stipules membranous, connate into tubiform, 0.5–1.2 cm. Leaves sessile, linear, 2–6 cm × 1 mm, apex acuminate, entire; veins 1–3, midvein clear, lateral veins inconspicuous; dormant buds thin, fusiform, 1–2.5 cm. Spikes pedunculate, terminal, 8–10 mm, with flowers 2–3 whorls, interruptedly arranged. Flowers small. Tepals 4, green. Drupelets oblique-obovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex with a curved beak.

Locality: Mai Po. S. T. Dunn 6815; Y. W. Lam 34.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China and temperate regions of N hemisphere.
Ecology: Ponds and marshes. Flowering & fruiting : May – Oct.

Pothos chinensis (Raf.) Merr. 石柑
J. Arnold Arb. 19: 210. 1948; FHN 4: 130. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 19, pl. 3: 10. 1979; FYN 2: 742, fig. 202: 8. 1979; FTW, ed. 2, 5: 685, photo 74. 2000; FGD 9: 179, fig. 96. 2009; FOC 23: 7. 2010.
Tapanava chinensis Raf., Fl. Tellur. 4: 14. 1838.
Pothos seemannii Schott, Bonplandia 5: 44. 1857; Aroid. 22, t. 43. 1858; Prodr. Aroid. 564. 1860; FKH 289. 1912.
Pothos scandens auct. non L.: FHK 344. 1861.

Epiphytic liana; stems adhering to rocks or trees by means of aerial roots. Leaves alternate, subleathery; petiole dilated, obovateoblong or cuneate, 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to oblonglanceolate, 6–13 × 1.5–5.6 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate or long acuminate. Peduncle 8 – 20 mm, with 3 – 4 concave ovate bracts; spathe green, ovate, 8 × 10–15 mm, apex acute; spadix globular or slightly ovoid, yellow green, yellowish, 7–11 mm in diam. Berries ovoid to ellipsoidal, red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. N. H. Li 12; K. Y. Tam 150; HK sheet 40008.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Trees and rocks in forests. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of P. seemannii was collected by Seemann from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of P. seemannii was collected by Seemann from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Pottsia laxiflora (Blume) Kuntze 簾子藤
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 416. 1891; FRPS 63: 137, pl. 46. 1977; FGD 1: 457, fig. 511. 1987; FOC 16: 173. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 139, fig. 44. 1999.
Vallaris laxiflora Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 16: 1043. 1826.
Pottsia cantonensis Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey. Voy. 199, pl. 43. 1837; FHK 222. 1861; FKH 168. 1912.

Lianas to 10 m; branches and branchlets slender, pubescent or glabrous. Petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaf blade ovate, narrowly ovate, or elliptic, 6–12 × 3–7 cm, base obtuse to rounded or subcordate, pubescent or glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 4 – 6 on each side of midvein. Cymes to 25 cm, long‑pedunculate, many‑flowered. Corolla purple or rose, ca. 7 mm; tube glabrous, longer than lobes; lobes narrowly ovate, ca. 2 mm, spreading. Ovary pilose. Style thickened in middle. Follicles linear, to 26–40 cm × 3–4 mm, pubescent to glabrous. Seeds linear, ca. 2 cm; coma 2.5 – 3 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Hok Tau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2314; P. S. Choi 264, 501.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Jun. – Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The species was recorded as Pottsia grandiflora Markgr. previously (Check List HK Plants 57. 1993; 74. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The species was recorded as Pottsia grandiflora Markgr. previously (Check List HK Plants 57. 1993; 74. 2004).
