Pouzolzia zeylanica (L.) Benn. 霧水葛
Pl. Jav. Rar. 67. 1838; Wight, Ic. Pl. Ind. Or. 6: t. 2101, f. 45. 1853; FGZ 403, fig. 209. 1956; FRPS 23(2): 364, pl. 81: 1–4. 1995; FOC 5: 177. 2003; FGD 6: 83, fig. 32. 2005.
Parietaria zeylanica L., Sp. Pl. 1052. 1753.
Pouzolzia indica auct. non Gaudich.: FHK 331. 1861; FKH 250. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems ascending or erect, 12– 40 cm tall, covered with appressed short hairs and mixed with spreading hairs. Leaves opposite, or alternate near apex; petioles 0.3–1.6 cm; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 1.2–3.8 × 0.8 –2.6 cm (leaves on short branches much smaller), base rounded, apex shortly acuminate or slightly obtuse, margin entire, sparsely covered with appressed hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 1–2 on each side of midvein. Flowers in small sessile, axillary clusters, 1–2.5 mm in diam., the males and females usually mixed. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, narrowly oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, united at the base; stamens 4, ca. 1.8 mm; rudimentary pistil narrowly obovate, ca. 0.4 mm. Female flowers: perianthsegments elliptic or subrhomboid, ca. 0.8 mm, enlarged to 1.5 mm in fruiting time, apex minutely 2-toothed, densely pubescent outside; stigma 1.2–2 mm. Achene ovoid, ca. 1.2 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1374; Y. S. Lau 1583, 2234.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Sichuan, S Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; widely distributed in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thickets or grasses. Flowering: Autumn.

Pratia nummularia (Lam.) A. Braun & Asch. 銅錘玉帶草
Index Sem. (Berlin) 1861, Append. 6. 1861; FHN 3: 446. 1974; FRPS 73(2): 168. 1983; FGD 3: 332, fig. 218. 1995.
Lobelia nummularia Lam., Dict. 3: 589. 1789; FTW ed. 2, 4: 792, pl. 367, photo 398. 1998.
Piddingtonia nummularia A. DC., Prodr. 7: 341. 1839; FHK 196. 1861.
Pratia begonifolia Lindl., Bot. Reg. 16: sub t. 1373. 1830; FKH 152. 1912.

Perennial herbs, juice milky. Stems prostrate, 12–55 cm, usually pubescent, rooting at the nodes. Leaves alternate, distichous; petioles 2–7 mm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate, or nearly orbicular, 8–16 × 6–18 mm, base cordate, apex subrounded or ± acute, margin serrate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels 7–35 mm, glabrous. Calyx‑tube urn‑shaped, 3–4 mm, glabrous; lobes 5, linear‑lanceolate, 3–4 mm. Corolla usually light purple, 6–7 mm, bilabiate, the 2 upper lobes linear‑lanceolate, the 3 lower lobes lanceolate, shorter than the upper ones. Anthers united into a ring, ca. 1 mm, the 2 lower ones with a short bristle on the top. Berry ovoid‑globular, purplish red, 8–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Ta Ti Yan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Sunset Peak. H. C. Tang 2502; Y. S. Lau 1523.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; E & S Asia to New Guinea and Australia.
Ecology: Wet places on margins of forests and in grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Praxelis clematidea (Griesb.) R. M. King & H. Rob. 假臭草
Phytologia 20: 194. 1970.
Eupatorium clematideum Griseb., Jahresber. Pollichia 22–24: 258. 1866.
Eupatorium catarium Veldkamp, Gard. Bull. Singapore 51(1): 121. 1999; FGD 8: 214. 2007; Check List HK Plants 281. 2002; 96. 2004.

Perennial erect herbs 0.3–1 m tall, malodorous, covered with soft multicellular hairs, denser on branches and peduncles. Leaves ovate, trinerved, 2.5–5.5 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin coarsely serrate with 5 – 8 teeth on each side, scarcely puberulent on adaxial surfaces, pilose and denser on abaxial surface, especially along margin and veins; petioles 0.3–1.5 cm. Capitula in terminal simple or compound cyme. Involucres cylindric campanulate, 7–8 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries in 4–5 series, easily shed off, scarious and translucent with several yellowish green veins, apex caudate or long‑acuminate; outer smaller, ovate‑lanceolate, 4 × 1 mm, slightly hairy; middle lanceolate, 5–6 × 1.5 mm, sparsely ciliate; inner linear‑oblong, 6–7 × 1 mm, glabrous. Receptacle highly conical with phyllaries shed off at the fruiting stage. Florets blue or violet, corolla 3 – 4.5 mm, shortly 5‑lobbed; stylar branches 2 mm, exserted. Cypsela oblong, 4‑ribbed, 2–2.5 mm, black and slightly hairy. Pappus capillary, 4 mm, white, persistent.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. Wong 037 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 19958 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 1130.
Distribution: Native to S America; naturalized in S Guangdong; SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Notes: As a weed.

Premna serratifolia L. 傘序臭黃荊（美娘子）
Mant. Pl. 2: 253. 1771; FHK 203. 1861; FOC 17: 26. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 423, photo 254. 1998.
Cornutia corymbosa Burm. f., Fl. Indica 132. pl. 41, fig. 1. 1768.
Premna corymbosa (Burm. f.) Rottler & Willd., Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 4: 187. 1803. ; FHN 4: 17. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 114. 5. 1982; FFJ 4: 537. 1989; FGD 3: 366. 1995.
Premna integrifolia L., Mant. Pl. 2: 154. 1771; FKH 203. 1912.
Premna integrifolia var. obtusifolia (R. Br.) C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 75. 1932.
Premna obtusifolia R. Br., Prodr. 512. 1810; FGD 3: 367, fig. 238. 1995.

Shrub or small tree, 1–4(–8) m tall, erect or rarely scandent. Branchlets pale yellow lenticellate, densely pubescent when young, subglabrescent. Petiole 0.3–5 cm, puberulent; leaf blade papery to subleathery, oblong, broadly ovate, oblong‑ovate, obovate to suborbicular, 3–15 × 2.5–9.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded, or truncate, apex acute to rarely acuminate or obtuse, margin entire, slightly undulate, or crenate, subglabrous or pubescent only along veins on both surfaces. Inflorescences 1.5–15 × 2.5–24 cm. Peduncle 0.8–3 cm. Bracts to 6 mm, puberulent. Calyx cupular, 1.5–3 mm, 2‑lipped, lower lip subentire to shortly 3‑dentate, upper lip longer than lower lip and 2‑dentate, abaxially puberulent and yellow glandular. Corolla pale yellow, abaxially glandular, slightly 2‑lipped; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal or middle lobe slightly longer and broader; upper lip entire or emarginate. Ovary glabrous, apically glandular. Style 3.5–4 mm. Fruit globose or obovoid, 2–4 mm in diam., sparsely yellow glandular.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Sha Tin, Kei Ling Ha, Castle Peak, Ma On Shan, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 308, 389; HK sheet 39784.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; S & SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests, hillslopes. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn.

Procris crenata C. B. Robinson 藤麻
Philipp. J. Sci. 5(6): 507. 1911; FOC 5: 163. 2003.
Procris wightiana Wall. ex Wedd., Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat. 9: 336. 1856; FRPS 23(2): 317, pl. 71: 1–2. 1995; FGD 6: 87. 2005.
Procris laevigata auct. non Blume: FKH 249. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems fleshy, 30–80 cm tall, glabrous. Leaves alternate, borne on the upper part of stems and branches; stipules very small, ovate, deciduous; petioles 1.5–12 mm; leaf blade narrowly oblong to oblong, (4.5–)8–20 × (1.5 –)2.2– 4.5 cm, base attenuate, slightly asymmetrical, apex acuminate, margin with a few teeth or undulate above middle, glabrous; lateral veins 5 – 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers in clusters; male clusters with short and slender peduncle; the females on a short and thick peduncle and usually borne above the males. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 5, oblong or ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, corniculate below apex; stamens 5. Female flowers sessile; perianth-lobes often 4, ca. 3.5 mm, glabrous; ovary ellipsoid, ca. 0.3 mm; stigma very small. Achene narrowly ovoid, 0.6–0.8 mm, compressed, often minutely punctate or almost smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. P. S. Choi 361; Y. S. Lau 1758.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Thailand, Indochina and Malesia.
Ecology: Shady, moist places in forests, on rocks or tree trunks. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Prunus marginata Dunn 全緣櫻桃（鑲邊櫻）
J. Bot. 45(539): 402. 1907; FKH 93. 1912; FGD 4: 240. 2000.
Laurocerasus marginata (Dunn) T. T. Yu & L. L. Lu, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 4(4): 52. 1984; FRPS 38: 122. 1986; FOC 9: 430. 2003.

Evergreen small tree or shrub, 4 – 6 m tall; branchlets densely tawny pubescent, then glabrescent or persistent; winter buds dark brown, ovoid, with ciliate scales. Petioles 1–5 mm, glabrous; stipules caducous; leaf blade leathery, oblong or obovate-oblong, 5–9 × 1.5–  cm, base narrowly cuneate, oblique, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, abaxially greenish with or without 2 basal glands, lateral veins and reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Racemes solitary, axillary, several-flowered, 2–3 cm; rachis densely pubescent; pedicels 1 – 3 mm, densely pubescent; flowers 2 – 3 mm in diam.; sepals 5, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, apex obtuse or acute; petals 5, white, suborbicular or obovate, 2 – 3 mm, glabrous; stamens 25 – 35, longer than petals; ovary glabrous; nearly as long as stamens. Drupe ovoid, 1 – 1.2 × 0.7 – 0.9 cm, dark brown to blackish purple, glabrous; stone reticulately rugose.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 10082; HK sheet 8991, 39932.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Spring to summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.

Prunus mume (Siebold) Siebold & Zucc. 梅
Fl. Jap. 34(2): 234. 1913; FKH 93. 1912; FFJ 2: 274. 1985; FGD 4: 232. 2000.
Armeniaca mume Siebold, Verh. Batav. Genootsch. Kunsten 12(1): 69. 1830; FRPS 38: 31. 1986; FOC 9: 400. 2003.

Deciduous small tree, 4 – 10 m tall, usually with spine-tipped short branches; branchlets green, glabrous; axillary winter bud 1, glabrous, terminal bud absent. Petioles 0.5–2 cm, glabrous, usually with glands; stipules caducous; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 3.5–8 × 2.5–5 cm, base broadly cuneate or nearly rounded, apex caudate or acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces or abaxially pubescent. Flowers solitary or in clusters of 2, open before leaves, 2 – 2.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 1 – 3 mm, usually glabrous; sepals 5, ovate or suborbicular, apex obtuse; petals 5, or double in cultivars, white, pink or red; stamens many, shorter or slightly longer than petals; style densely pubescent, shorter or slightly longer than stamens. Drupes subglobose, yellow, 2 – 3 cm in diam.; stone pitted.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2456, 2829; HK sheet 9000.
Distribution: E Asia, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.– Feb.; fruiting: Mar. – Jun.
Uses: Fruit, ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Prunus persica (L.) Batsch 桃
Beytr. Entw. Gewächsreich 1: 30. 1801; FFJ 2: 273. 1985; FGD 4: 231. 2000.
Amygdalus persica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 472. 1753; FRPS 38: 17. 1986; FOC 9: 394. 2003.

Deciduous small tree, 3–8 m tall; branchlets glabrous; axillary winter buds (2 –)3, terminal buds present. Petioles 0.5 –2 cm, usually with one to several glands; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or broadly lanceolate, 7–15 × 2– 3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin finely to coarsely serrate, with glandular teeth, glabrous or with few hairs in axils of veins of abaxial surface. Flowers solitary, opening before or with leaves, 2–3.5 cm in diam.; pedicels short or almost obsolete; sepals 5, ovate or oblong, apex obtuse, abaxially pubescent; petals 5, pink or white, oblong or broadly obovate, 1–1.7 × 0.9–1.2 cm; stamens 20–30; anthers purplish red; ovary pubescent; styles nearly as long as stamens. Drupe ovoid, broadly ellipsoidal or compressed globose, fleshy, 3–12 cm in diam., greenish white to orangish yellow, usually with a red tinge on exposed side, densely pubescent, rarely glabrous; stone ellipsoidal to suborbicular, longitudinally and transversely furrowed and pitted.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 27; Y. S. Lau 2689, 3280.
Distribution: E Asia, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. –Apr.; fruiting: Apr. – Sep.
Uses: Fruit, medicinal (folklore).

Prunus phaeosticta (Hance) Maxim. 腺葉桂櫻（腺葉野櫻）
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 29(1): 110. 1883; FFJ 2: 275. 1985; FGD 4: 238. 2000.
Pygeum phaeostictum Hance, J. Bot. 8(88): 72. 1870.
Laurocerasus phaeosticta (Hance) C. K. Schneid., Ill. Handb. Laubholzk. 1: 649, fig. 355k. 1906; FRPS 38: 108. 1986; FOC 9: 427. 2003.
Prunus punctata Hook. f. & Thomson, Fl. Brit. India 2(5): 317. 1878; FKH 93. 1912.

Evergreen small tree or shrub, 4 – 12 m tall; branchlets brown, glabrous or ± pubescent, sparsely leticellate; winter buds ovoid, with several ciliate scales. Petioles 0.3 – 1 cm, glabrous, eglandular; stipules lanceolate, glabrous, caducous; leaf blade leathery, narrowly elliptic, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, rarely obovate-oblong, 6 – 12 × 2 – 4 cm, base cuneate, broadly cuneate or nearly rounded, with 2 large flat glands near the base, apex caudate or acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, abaxially densely black glandular punctate, lateral veins 6–10 on each side of midvein. Racemes axillary, solitary, several– 10-flowered, 2.5–7 cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; pedicels 3–5 mm; sepals 5, ovate-triangular, 1– 2 mm, apex obtuse, margin serrate and ciliate; petals 5, white, suborbicular, 2 –3 × 2–3 mm, glabrous; stamens 20–35, 5 – 6 mm; ovary glabrous or subglabrous, styles ca. 5 mm. Drupe purplish black, subglobose or ellipsoidal, ca. 1 cm in diam., glabrous; stone smooth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1776; P. S. Choi 279; HK sheet 40350.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Japan, India, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, open field. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Apr. –Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of Pygeum phaeostictum was collected from “Pakwan” by H. F. Hance in 1870.

Prunus salicina Lindl. 李
Trans. Hort. Soc. London 7: 239. 1828; FRPS 38: 39. 1986; FFJ 2: 274. 1985; FGD 4: 233. 2000; FOC 9: 403. 2003.
Prunus japonica auct. non Thunb.: FKH 93. 1912.

Deciduous tree, 9 –12 m tall; branchlets greyish brown, glabrous or pubescent; axillary winter buds solitary, ovoid, with many ciliate scales, terminal bud absent. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, with or without glands; stipules linear, caducous; leaf blade papery, oblong-obovate, oblong, or oblong-ovate, 6–12 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or sharply acute, margin remotely irregularly dentate, glabrous, sometimes pubescent along the veins or in axils of veins of abaxial surface. Flowers usually in clusters of 3, 1.5–2.2 cm in diam.; pedicels 0.5 – 2 cm, usually glabrous; sepals 5, oblong-ovate, ca. 5 mm, abaxially glabrous, margin serrate, apex acute to obtuse; petals white, oblong-obovate, base cuneate, margin erose towards apex; stamens ca. 30, unequal in length; ovary glabrous; stigma disk-shaped. Drupe globose or ovoid, 3.5 – 7 cm, glabrous, green, yellow or red, glaucous, grooved; stone ovoid to oblong, rugose

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2882; HK sheet 9069, 9076.
Distribution: E Asia, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. –Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Fruit.

Prunus zippeliana Miq. 大葉桂櫻
Fl. Ned. Ind. 1: 367. 1855; FFJ 2: 275. 1985; FGD 4: 239. 2000.
Laurocerasus zippeliana (Miq.) Browicz, Arbor. Kornickie 15: 6. 1970; FRPS 38: 116. 1986; FOC 9: 429. 2003.

Evergreen tree, up to 25 m tall; branchlets greyish green, glabrous, lenticellate; winter buds ovoid, subglabrous. Petioles 1 – 2 cm, stout, glabrous, abaxially with 2 glands toward the leaf base; stipules linear, caducous; leaf blade thick leathery, broadly ovate, elliptic-oblong, obovate-elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 8– 19 × 4 – 8 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex shortly acuminate or acute, margin serrate, with black glandular-tipped teeth, glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 7– 13 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Racemes axillary, solitary or branched at leaf base, 2 – 6 cm; densely pubescent; pedicels 1 – 3 mm; flowers 5 – 9 mm in diam; sepals 5, ovate-triangular, 1– 2 mm, apex obtuse, abaxially sparsely pubescent; petals 5, white, suborbicular, 2– 4 mm; stamens 20 –25, 4 –6 mm; ovary glabrous; styles nearly as long as stamens. Drupes red, ovoid or ellipsoidal, 1.8 – 2.4 × 0.8 – 1.1 cm, blackish purple, glabrous, apically acute, basally rounded; stone slightly reticulately rugose.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan. K. Y. Tam 109.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Gansu; Japan, Vietnam
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.– Oct.; fruiting: Winter.

Pseudelephantopus spicatus (Juss. ex Aublet) C. F. Baker 假地膽草
Trans. Acad. Sci. St. Louis 12(5): 55. 1902; S. Y. Hu, Quart, J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 305. 1967; FRPS 74: 47. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1041. 1998.
Elephantopus spicatus Juss. ex Aublet, Hist. Pl. Guiane 2: 808. 1775; FKH 139. 1912.

Perennial herbs 45–100 cm tall; stem erect, striate, subglabrous on lower portion, pilose and glandular upward, hairs appearing denser on inflorescence branches. Leaves oblanceolate‑spatulate, 7–22 × 1–6 cm, base gradually attenuate to a short sheath, subamplexicaul, apex obtuse to rounded, margin with callous teeth or entire, pinnately‑veined, pilose on adaxial surfaces, along margins and midveins on abaxial surface, densely punctate abaxially. Upper leaves linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1–11 × 0.1–1 cm, smaller in size especially those on branches. Capitula sessile, solitary or 2–6 clustered into axillary aggregates without stalks, arranged as spicate‑panicle. Involucres oblong‑ellipsoidal, 1–1.2 × 0.3–0.4 cm; phyllaries distal half or 1/3 dark green, sparsely pilose and glandular, apex acuminate‑aristate, margin scarious, midvein prominent, in 2 series with 4 involucral bracts in each layer; outer ones ovate, 5–6 × 3 mm; inner ones oblong, twice longer than the outer ones, 1–1.2 mm. Florets 4 per capitulum, corolla white, 6–7 mm, 5 lanceolate apical lobes. Cypselae linear‑oblong, densely hairy and glandular, 10‑ribbed, 6–7 mm. Pappus few, bristle‑like but slender, dilated and scarious at base, unequal in length, usually with 2 longer and folded as sigmoid near apex.

Locality: Naturalized. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 19973, 23090; L. T. Lo 480.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan (naturalized); tropical America and Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jan.–May.

Pseuderanthemum carruthersii (Seem.) Guillaumin 擬美花
Ann. Inst. Bot.‑Geol. Colon. Marseille, ser. 6, 5 – 6: 48. 1948.
Eranthemum carruthersii Seem., Fl. Vit. 185. 1866.
Pseuderanthemum atropurpureum (W. Bull) Radlk., Sitzungsber. Math.‑Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. München 13(2): 286. 1883.
Pseuderanthemum carruthersii var. atropurpureum (W. Bull) Fosberg, Smithsonian Contr. Bot. 45: 26. 1980.

Shrubs, to 2.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous except for retrorsely pubescent at node. Petioles 0–7 mm; leaf blades leathery, ovate‑elliptic to elliptic, 2.5–8 × 1.5–5 cm, base rounded to attenuate, apex rounded to acute, margin entire, revolute. Spikes terminal, up to 12 cm, flowers 1–3 at each node. Rachis glabrous. Peduncles 1–7 mm. Pedicels 3–6 mm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Bracts elliptic to ovate to triangular, 1.5  4 × 1–1.5 mm, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pubescent with antrorse, short hairs (ca. 0.1 mm); bracteoles lanceolate‑ovate to triangular, ca. 1.5 mm, abaxially glabrous or pubescent. Calyx ca. 4 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate to lanceolate‑subulate, 2–3 mm, abaxially pubescent. Corolla white with maroon spots within, 1.7–2 cm, outside glabrous; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 9 mm, upper lip 8–11 mm, 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 8 × 3 mm, lower lip 9–11 mm, lobes ca. 9 × 4–7 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 6 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae oblong, ca. 2 mm. Staminodes 2, 1–2 mm. Ovary glabrous; style included or exserted ca. 1 mm from the mouth of corolla, 9– 10 mm, pubescent; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 0.7 mm. Capsule not seen.

Pseuderanthemum carruthersii 'Variegatum' 斑葉擬美花
Pseuderanthemum atropurpureum ‘Variegatum’

This cultivar is characterized by variegated venation on its bronze-purple leaves, marked with cream-yellow, and pink flowers.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 41913.
Distribution: Native to Polynesia.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pseudopogonatherum contortum (Brongn.) A. Camus 筆草
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 68: 205. 1921[1922]; FFJ 6: 247, fig. 215. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 93. 1997; FOC 22: 590. 2006.
Pogonatherum contortum Brongn., Voy. Monde 2(2): 90. 1831.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect, 25–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades narrow linear, involute, 10–30 × 0.1–0.2 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface thinly pilose; ligule ca. 0.2 mm. Racemes 3–6, subdigitate, white hairy, all spikelets pedicellate, falling from pedicels at maturity; pedicels usually unequal, as long as or shorter than internode, villous. Spikelets brown, glossy; callus hairs up to 1/2 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly oblong or lanceolate-oblong; upper glume with mucro or awn 0.5–4(–12) mm; upper lemma entire or minutely toothed; awn 1.5–3 cm, column pilose.

Locality: Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 12350 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Bhutan, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, open and disturbed grassy hillsides.

Pseudopogonatherum koretrostachys (Trin.) Henrard 刺葉假金髮草
Blumea 4: 521. 1941; FOC 22: 591. 2006.
Andropogon koretrostachys Trin., Mém. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.- Pétersbourg, Sér. 6, Sci. Math. 2: 273. 1833.
Pseudopogonatherum setifolium (Nees) A. Camus in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. de L’IndoChine. 7: 256. 1922; FHN 4: 455. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 96. 1997; FYN 9: 634. 2003; Check List HK Plants 345. 2002; 120. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, 30–60 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades narrowly linear, usually involute, 5–20 × 0.1–0.2 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, ciliate. Racemes (1–)7–25 or more, subdigitate, 2–8 cm, white hairy, tardily fragile, one spikelet of a pair sessile, the other pedicellate; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2 spikelet length, villous. Spikelets lanceolate, 2–3 mm, brown; callus hairs 1/5–1/4 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly lanceolateoblong, villous except near apex, sometimes sparsely so or glabrous, upper flanks villous, apex 2-toothed or truncate and minutely 2-mucronate; upper glume boat-shaped, with 3–6 mm awn; lower lemma oblong, ca. 1 mm; upper lemma, shortly 2-toothed; awn 1.5–2 cm, column shortly ciliate, hairs ca. 0.25 mm. Anthers 3, 0.5–0.7 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile ones, easily deciduous, maturing before sessile spikelet.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling. HK sheet 15587, 31551.
Distribution: S and E China, Yunnan; Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Arundinaria amabilis McClure 茶稈竹（籬竹）
Lingnan Sci. J. 10(1): 6, pl. 1–8. 1931; HKB 21. 1985; FGD 9: 292. 2009.
Pseudosasa amabilis (McClure) Keng f. ex S. L. Chen et al., FRPS 9(1): 641. 1996; FOC 22: 117. 2006.

Culms 7–13 m, 2–6 cm in diam.; internodes terete, olive-green, 30–40(–50) cm, sparsely brown hispidulous at first, glabrescent, initially grey waxy; wall thick; pith lamellate or spongy. Nodal ridge flat or weakly prominent. Branches (1–)3 per node, deflexed, secondary branchlets undeveloped. Culm sheaths gradually deciduous, dark brown, rigid, fragile when dry, densely brown setose abaxially, margins with ciliate, apex truncate; auricles absent; oral setae several, erect, ca. 1.5 cm, undulate; ligule arcuate, irregular, ciliate; blade erect, dark brown, narrowly triangular, scabrid. Leaves 2–3 per ultimate branch; sheath glabrous abaxially, margins ciliolate; auricles minute; oral setae curved, 0.7–1.5 mm; ligule 1–2 mm, densely ciliolate; blade narrowly lanceolate, 16–35 × 1.6–3.5 cm, glabrous, secondary veins 7–9-paired. Inflorescence paniculate with 3–15 spikelets; spikelets 2.5–5.5 cm, rachilla internodes ca. 3 mm; florets 5–16. Glumes 2, unequal, densely puberulous, margins apically densely ciliolate; lemma ovate-lanceolate, densely puberulous; palea broadly lanceolate, keels puberulous. Lodicules unequal. Ovary fusiform, glabrous. Caryopsis 5–6 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Nan-Zhu 2783, 2866; HK sheet 24998.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: New shoots: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental, environmental, cane (clums).

Arundinaria cantorii (Munro) L. C. Chia 托竹
Kew Bull. 37(4): 591. 1983; HKB 22. 1985; FGD 9: 294. 2009.
Bambusa cantorii Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 111. 1868; FKH 331. 1912.
Arundarbor cantorii (Munro) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 761. 1891.
Arundinaria basiaurita W. T. Lin, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(3): 231, pl. 10. 1988.
Arundinaria basigibbosa McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 1. 1940.
Arundinaria funghomii McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 3. 1940.
Arundinaria pubiannula W. T. Lin & Z. J. Feng, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 30(6): 560 – 561, pl. 2, fig. 5 – 8. 1992.
Pseudosasa cantorii (Munro) Keng f. ex S. L. Chen et al., FRPS 9(1): 654. 1996 [“cantori”]; FOC 22: 120. 2006.
Pseudosasa hainanensis G. A. Fu, J. Bamboo Res. 13(3): 1 – 3, fig. 1. 1994.

Culms 2–4 m, 5–10 mm in diam.; internodes terete, 24–33 cm; nodal ridge obscure. Branches 3 per node. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, thickly papery or thinly leathery, brownish yellow, ± purplish, ca. 1/2 as long as internodes, glabrous or sparsely brown setose, apex subtruncate or slightly convex, margins densely golden yellow ciliolate; auricles well-developed, semilunar or falcate; oral setae many, erect, wavy, 6–13 mm; ligule arcuate or truncate, slightly concave, scabrid, ciliolate; blade erect, narrowly ovate-lanceolate, glabrous abaxially, basally 1/2–3/5 as wide as sheath apex, margins serrulate. Leaves 5–10 per ultimate branch; sheath stramineous, purplish, ca. 4 mm, glabrous or puberulous abaxially, margins ciliate; auricles falcate or semilunar; oral setae ca. 5 mm, deciduous; ligule truncate, short, slightly hairy, entire or laciniate; blade narrowly lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 12–20(–32) × 1.2–2.5(–4.5) cm, both surfaces glabrous, base broadly cuneate, margins serrulate, secondary veins 5–9-paired. Inflorescence paniculate or racemose, terminal on lateral leafy branches; spikelets 3–4 cm, pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm; florets 4–9; rachilla internodes 4–6 mm, flat, thickened toward apex. Glumes 2; lemma 11 mm, 11–13-veined, glabrous abaxially, margins densely ciliolate; palea shorter than lemma, ciliolate along keels and margins, 2–3-veined between keels; lodicules oblong, 2–3 mm; anthers 6–7 mm. Ovary cylindrical, 1.5 mm, glabrous; styles very short; stigmas 3. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Green Island, Lantau Island. Nan-Zhu 2823, 2875; S. C. Ng 1308.
Distribution: S Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, S Jiangxi.
Ecology: Hillslopes. New shoots: Mar.
Uses: Environmental.
Notes: The type specimen (Cantor s.n., K) was collected from Lantau Island in 1840. The species epithet was naming after the collector of type materials, Dr. Theodore Cantor.

Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 31. 1868; FKH 330. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 596. 2000; FGD 9: 293. 2009.
Pseudosasa hindsii (Munro) S. L. Chen & G. Y. Sheng ex T. G. Liang, Fujian Bamboos. 142. 1987; FRPS 9(1): 653, pl. 119: 11–12. 1996; FOC 22: 120. 2006.
Acidosasa denigrata W. T. Lin, J. South China Agr. Univ. 14(1): 48, fig. 4. 1998.

Pseudosasa multifloscula (W. T. Lin) W. T. Lin, Guihaia 10(1): 18. 1990.
Pseudosasa nigronodis G. A. Fu, J. Bamboo Res. 15(1): 4, fig. 1. 1996 ["nigro-nodis"].
Thamnocalamus hindsii (Munro) E. G. Camus, Bambusées 52, pl. 25, fig. a. 1913.

Culms 3–5 m, ca. 1 cm in diam.; internodes dark green, 20–36 cm, basal ones glabrous but apical internodes hairy, initially glaucous. Branches 3–5 per node, erect. Culm sheaths persistent, sparsely white or light brown setose; auricles falcate; oral setae curved; ligule arcuate, ca. 3 mm; blade erect, broadly ovate-lanceolate, nearly as wide as sheath apex, base slightly constricted. Leaves 4–9 per ultimate branch; sheath deciduous, glabrous or sparsely setulose, margins ciliolate; auricles absent; oral setae few; ligule truncate, rigid, 1–1.5 mm; pseudopetiole ca. 2 mm; blade linear-lanceolate or narrowly oblong, 7–22 × ca. 1.6 cm, glabrous or abaxially slightly hairy, secondary veins 3–5-paired, base cuneate, one margin spinescently serrulate, other margin entire, apex acuminate. Inflorescence unknown.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, To Fung Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. N. K. Chun 2841; Nan-Zhu 2799; HK sheet 40923.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Coastal hills, mountains. New shoots: May–Jun.
Uses: Environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected R. B. Hinds from Victoria Peak in 1841.
