Psidium guajava L. 番石榴
Sp. Pl. 1: 470. 1753; FKH 104. 1912; FGZ 200. 1956; FHN 2: 11, fig. 294. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 123, pl. 32: 3 – 4. 1984; FFJ 4: 104, fig. 92. 1989; FGX 1: 903. 1991; FYN 7: 131, fig. 36: 1 – 2. 1997; FOC 13: 332. 2007.
Myrtus guajava (L.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 3(2): 91. 1898.

Tree, to 13 m tall. Bark exfoliating in strips. Young branchlets angular, pubescent. Petioles ca. 5 mm; leaf blade leathery, oblong to elliptic, 6–12 × 3.5–6 cm, base rounded, apex acute to obtuse, slightly rough adaxially, pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 12 – 15 on each side of midvein, usually impressed adaxially, reticulate veins obvious. Flowers solitary or 2–3 in cymes. Hypanthium campanulate, ca. 5 mm, hairy. Calyx cap suborbicular, 7–8 mm, irregularly dehiscent. Petals 1–1.4 cm. Stamens 6–9 mm. Style as long as stamens. Berry globose, ovoid, or pyriform, 3–8 cm, with persistent calyx lobes at apex; flesh white or yellow; placenta reddish, well developed, fleshy.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 870, 3106; L. T. Lo 39.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan (cultivated or naturalized); native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug. – Sep.
Uses: Edible (fruit).

Psychotria asiatica L. 九節（山大刀）

Syst. Nat. (ed. 10), 929, 1364. 1759; A. P. Davis et al., Bot. J. Linn. Soc. 135: 35 – 42. 2001; FGD 6: 207, fig. 111. 2005.

Psychotria rubra auct. non (Lour.) Poir.: Urban Serv. Dept., Hong Kong Shrubs: 79. 1976; FRPS 71(2): 58, pl. 14: 1–4. 1999.

Psychotria elliptica auct. non Ker Gawl.: FHK 161. 1861; FKH 133. 1912.


Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 0.5 – 5 m tall. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5 – 3 cm, glabrous or nearly so; stipules membranous, 3 – 6 × 4 – 8 mm, connected into a sheath within the petioles, apex obtuse, deciduous; leaf blade oblong, elliptic‑oblong or oblong‑oblanceolate, 8 – 15( – 20) × 3 – 6( – 9) cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, or sometimes acute with a blunt tip, margin entire, glabrous, but often with tuft of minute hairs in axils of lateral veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins 5 –15 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform or paniculate, terminal; usually trichotomous; primary branches 2.5 – 3 cm, secondary branches 1 – 1.5 cm; pedicels ca. 1 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, ca. 1.5 mm; limb subtruncate or inconspicuously 5‑toothed. Corolla greenish white; tube 2 – 3 mm, with white long hairs on the throat; lobes narrowly triangular, 2.5 – 3 × 1.5 – 2 mm, erect or ± spreading, tip incurved. Drupe globose or broadly ellipsoidal, 4 – 7 mm in diam., with longitudinal ribs, red when mature.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2250; Y. W. Lam 527, 830.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Malesia, India.

Ecology: Thickets and forests on hillsides and by streams. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.–Feb. of the following year.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Psychotria serpens L. 蔓九節（穿根藤）
Novit. Fl. Suec. Mant. 2: 204. 1771; FHK 161. 1861; FKH 133. 1912; FHN 3: 353. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 316, photo 191 – 192. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 60, pl. 14: 10 – 14. 1999; FGD 6: 208. 2005.

Evergreen small shrubs. Stems prostrate, many‑branched, 0.5–5 m or longer, climbing on trunks or rocks by aerial roots. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–10 mm, glabrous or scurfy puberulent; stipules membranous, shortly sheathing, 2–3 × 2–5 mm, apex obtuse, deciduous; leaf blade ovate, elliptic or obovate‑oblong, 0.7–9 × 0.5–3.8 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 4–10 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal, usually trichotomous; peduncles to 3 cm; pedicels 0.5–1.5 mm. Calyx‑tube obconical, ca. 2.5 mm; limb enlarged, obtusely and minutely 5‑toothed. Corolla white; tube 1.5–3 mm, with white long hairs on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, slightly longer than the tube. Fruit a berry‑like drupe, globose or ellipsoidal, 2.5–6 mm in diam., white when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2061; K. L. Yip 4142; HK sheet 39949.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests or thickets, climbing on trunks or rocks. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Psychotria tutcheri Dunn 假九節（小葉九節）
J. Bot. 48: 324. 1910; FKH 133. 1912; FHN 3: 352. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 53. 1999; FGD 6: 207. 2005.

Evergreen shrubs, 0.5–4 m tall. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 0.5–2 cm, glabrous; stipules ovate‑triangular or lanceolate, 3–5 × 2–4 mm, connected into a sheath within the petioles, apex acuminate, with 2 bristle‑like lobes, deciduous; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, ovate‑lanceolate, lanceolate or oblong, 5.5–22 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 4–13 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform, terminal or axillary. Peduncle 0.5–3 cm; pedicels ca. 1 mm. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1.5–2.5 mm; limb enlarged, lobes 4, broadly triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white or greenish white; tube 2–3 mm, with white long hairs on the throat; lobes 5, oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, recurved. Drupe globose, 4–6 mm in diam., with longitudinal ribs, red when mature.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Mount Kellet, Wu Kau Tang, Ma On Shan. P. S. Choi 387; K. L. Yip 4253; HK sheet 40907.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by W. J. Tutcher from Happy Valley in 1906.

Pterocarpus indicus Willd. 紫檀
Sp. Pl. 3(2): 904. 1802; FRPS 40: 122. 1994; FGD 5: 227, fig. 126. 2003.

Tree, 15 – 25 m tall; bark grey. Branches ascending, glabrous. Leaves odd-pinnate; leaflets 7–11, thinly leathery, alternate, ovate, 5 – 11 × 4 cm, base rounded, glabrous, apex shortly acuminate, main veins fine. Panicles axillary or terminal, many-flowered, brown-pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 5 – 7 mm, slightly curved, finely brown-silky pubescent; teeth broadly triangular, ca. 1 mm. Corolla yellow. Petals long-clawed; vexillum 10– 13 mm wide, margin crisped; wings smaller, distally ± connate. Stamens 10, monadelphous initially, later divided into diadelphous (5+5). Ovary shortly stipitate, densely yellow-brown pubescent. Pods obliquely orbicular, compressed, except the wings covered with silky hairs and net-veined; wings up to 2 cm broad.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1944; L. T. Lo 153; Y. W. Lam 280.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan (cultivated); India, Philippines, Indonesia, Myanmar.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb. –Aug.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Timber.

Pterocypsela indica (L.) C. Shih 翅果菊（山萵苣）
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(5): 387. 1988; FRPS 80(1): 229. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1043. 1998; FGD 8: 264. 2007.
Lactuca brevirostris Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 237. 1852; FHK 192. 1861; FKH 150. 1912.
Lactuca indica L., Mant. Pl. 278. 1771.

Large annual or biennial herbs; stem glabrous, erect, 0.5–2 m tall, branched apically. Leaves glabrous above and beneath. Lower leaves deciduous upon fruiting stage. Middle cauline leaves sessile, linear or linear‑lanceolate, 8.5–31 × 0.5–3 cm, not divided, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or mucronate near base. Upper leaves linear, smaller in size. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, paniculate or racemose‑paniculate at terminal; peduncles 5–25 mm, bearing several linear‑subulate bracteoles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 13–15 × 4–5 mm; phyllaries in 4 series, thick in texture, glabrous abaxially, margin and apex tinged purplish red and narrowly membranous; outer ones ovate, 2.5–3.5 × 1–2 mm, apex acute or obtuse; median ones ovate‑oblong, 5–8 × 2–2.5 mm, acute or obtuse; inner ones linear‑lanceolate, 13–14 × 2 mm, rounded. Ligulate florets 21–27 per head, corolla yellow, 12–14 mm, lower tube 4–4.5 mm, densely hairy near summit, ligule 8–9 mm, apex 5‑lobed. Cypselae black, elliptic, 3–4 × 1.8–2 mm, compressed, lateral margins thicken as wings, apex acute or acuminate, forming pale brown rostrum 1–1.5 mm, 1‑striate on each side. Pappus 2‑seriate, parachute‑like at the end of the rostrum, 7–8 mm, white.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2072; Y. S. Lau 2629; S. Y. Hu 7840 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Indochina, India, Malaysia, Japan, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.

Pterocypsela laciniata (Houtt.) C. Shih 多裂翅果菊
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(5): 388. 1988; FRPS 80(1): 230. 1997; FGD 8: 265. 2008.
Prenanthes laciniata Houtt., Nat. Hist. 10: 381. 1779.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 0.6–2 m tall, stout, branched apically, glabrous. Lower and middle cauline leaves glabrous on both sides, oblanceolate, elliptic or oblong, 13–25 × 8–10 cm, or much larger, leaf base cuneate and sessile, regularly or irregularly 1–2‑pinnatisect, apical lobes long‑linear or sometimes lanceolate, primary lateral segments 1–5 pairs, elongate‑triangular, lanceolate or falcate, gradually smaller downward; secondary lateral segments linear or triangular, length various; all lobes apex mostly acuminate or sometimes acute, margin mucronulate. Upper leaves smaller in size, divided similarly as the middle leaves, or undivided and appearing linear. Capitula many, arranged as panicles at terminal, homogamous with all florets ligulate and bisexual; peduncles 0.5–3 cm, bearing few small ovate bracteoles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 13–14 × 4–5 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, acute or obtuse apically, glabrous abaxially, margin and apex thinly membranous and tinged reddish purple; outer ones ovate, 2–3 × 1–2 mm; median ones ovate‑oblong, 4–5 × 1.8–2.2 mm; inner ones linear‑lanceolate or linear‑oblong, 8–13 × 1.2–2 mm. Ligulate florets about 21 per head, corolla yellow, 12–14 mm, lower tube 6–7 mm, densely hairy near summit, ligule 6–7 mm, 5‑lobed at distal end. Cypselae elliptic, compressed, black, 4 × 2–2.1 mm, margin thickly winged, 1‑striate on each side, apex with pale brown beak 1–1.2 mm. Pappus 2‑seriate, growing on the beak, white, 6–8 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12132 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 641; HK sheet 34062.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Japan, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.

Pterocypsela raddeana (Maxim.) C. Shih 毛脈翅果菊
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(5): 386. 1988; FRPS 80(1): 227. 1997.
Lactuca raddeana Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19: 526. 1874.

Biennial or perennial herbs; stem erect, 0.8–2 m tall; branched apically, usually densely hairy in lower portion, glabrous above. Leaves sessile, scabrous on upper surfaces, pilose along veins and margins on lower surfaces. Lower and middle cauline leaves elliptic‑oblong, 7–13.5 × 2–5.5 cm, or much larger in size, lyrately pinnatilobed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, apical lobes larger than the lateral lobes, rarely equal‑sized, deltoid, ovate‑deltoid, subrhomboid or ovate‑lanceolate, apex acute or acuminate, margin shallowly and irregularly dentate‑sinuate; lateral segments 1–3 pairs, triangular or elliptic, acute, margin mucronulate. Upper leaves smaller, ovate, elliptic, oblong or ovate‑elliptic, acute or acuminate. Capitula homogamous, with all florets ligulate and bisexual, numerous at terminal forming narrow panicle. Peduncles 5–15 mm, bearing few small bracteoles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 7–8 mm; phyllaries 4‑seriate, pale purplish red; outer ones ovate‑triangular, 1–1.5 × 0.5–1.5 mm, acute; middle ones ovate‑oblong, 2–3 × 1–1.5 mm, obtuse; inner ones linear‑lanceolate, 6 – 8 × 1.2–1.5 mm, obtuse. Ligulate florets yellow, lower tube densely hairy near summit, ligule 5‑toothed at apex. Cypselae elliptic, brown or reddish brown, compressed, each side 3‑striate, margin thickly winged, apex with beak 0.1–0.5 mm. Pappus in 2 series, growing on the beak, white, 4–6 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. S. Y. Hu 10554, 12045 (CUHK); HK sheet 30425.
Distribution: Widely distributed in S, E, C, N & NE China.
Ecology: Thickets and cultivated areas. Flowering: May–Sep.

Pterospermum heterophyllum Hance 翻白葉樹
J. Bot. 6: 112. 1865; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 84. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 178. 1984; FGD 1: 146. 1987.
Pterospermum acerifolium auct. non (L.) Willd.: FHK 39. 1861.

Tree. Leaves on coppices: petioles 12 cm; leave blade peltate, palmately 3 – 5-lobed, ca. 15 cm in diam., densely brown stellatepubescent abaxially; leaves on normal branches: petioles 1–2 cm; leave blade oblong to ovate-oblong, 7–15 × 3–10 cm, brown pubescent abaxially. Flowers solitary or 3– 4 in cymes, axillary; bracteoles squamiform; sepals linear, up to 28 mm; petals oblanceolate, equaling sepals; androgynophore 2.5 mm; stamens 15; staminodes 5, linear, slightly longer than fertile stamens; ovary ovoid, 5-locular, hairy. Capsules woody, oblong-ovoid, 6 × 2–2.5 cm, yellow-brown tomentose, stalk thick, 1–1.5 cm. Seeds winged.

Locality: Ho Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Pat Sin Leng, Kop Tong, Au Ha, Ha Wo Hang, Ma Wan, Lantau Island. S. T. Dunn 7143; Y. S. Lau 2624; P. S. Choi 267.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), materials (timber, fibre).

Pueraria lobata (Willd.) Ohwi 葛
Bull. Tokyo Sci. Mus. 18: 16. 1947; FRPS 41: 224. 1994; FGD 5: 311, fig. 166. 2003.
Dolichos lobatus Willd., Sp. Pl. ed. 3, 2: 1047. 1802.
Neustanthus chinensis Benth., FHK 86. 1861.
Pueraria thunbergiana (Siebold & Zucc.) Benth., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 9: 122. 1867; FKH 83. 1912.

Robust vine with tuber roots. Stems up to 8 m, woody at base, yellow hirsute throughout. Stipules dorsifixed, ovate-oblong. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets broad-ovate or oblique ovate, 3-lobed, rarely entire, 7 – 19 × 5–13(–18) cm, apex acuminate, lateral ones smaller, oblique, adpressed yellowish pubescent on both surfaces, more dense abaxially. Flowers 2–3, aggregated on nodes. Calyx campanulate, 8–10 mm, yellow-brown villose, teeth lanceolate. Corolla purple; petals auriculate; vexillum obovate, 10–12 mm, with yellow callose appendage at base; wings falcate; keel falcate-oblong. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary linear, hairy. Pod oblong, 5–9 × 0.8 – 1.1 cm, compressed, brown hirsute.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1060; HK sheet 1396.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E Asia, SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Sep. – Oct.; fruiting: Nov. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Pueraria lobata (Willd.) Ohwi var. montana (Lour.) Maesen 葛麻姆
Agr. Univ. Wageningen Papers 85(1): 53. 1985; FRPS 41: 226. 1994; FGD 5: 311. 2003.
Dolichos montana Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 440. 1790.
Pueraria montana (Lour.) Merr., Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc., n.s., 24(2): 210. 1935.

Terminal leaflets usually entire. Calyx 7– 8 mm; vexillum orbicular, 8 mm in diam. Pods 4– 9 × 0.6 – 0.8 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2053; Y. S. Lau 2027, 2389.
Distribution: SW, S & SE China; Thailand, Philippines, Laos, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forests and open fields. Flowering: Sep. – Oct.; fruiting: Nov. – Dec.

Pueraria lobata (Willd.) Ohwi var. thomsonii (Benth.) Maesen 粉葛

Agr. Unv. Wgeningen Papers 85(1): 53. 1985; FRPS 41: 226. 1994; FGD 5: 312. 2003.

Pueraria thomsonii Benth., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 9: 122. 1867.


Terminal leaflet entire or 2 – 3-lobed, 16 – 18 mm. Calyx up to 20 mm; vexillum suborbicular; wings slightly shorter than keel. Pods 10 – 14 × 1 – 1.3 cm.


Locality: Cutltivated. Y. S. Lau 2408, 2794; Y. W. Lam 1128.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan; India, Thailand, Laos.

Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Sep.; fruiting: Nov.

Uses: Food (tuberous roots).

Pueraria phaseoloides (Roxb.) Benth. 三裂葉野葛
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 9: 125. 1865; FRPS 41: 221. 1994; FGD 5: 310. 2003.
Dolichos phaseoloides Roxb. Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 3: 316. 1832.
Neustanthus phaseoloides Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 235. 1825; FHK 86. 1861; FKH 83. 1912.

Herbaceous twiner. Stems slender, 2–4 m, hirsute, with brown-yellow spreading hairs. Stipules basifixed, ovate-lanceolate, 3–5 mm. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets broadly ovate, rhombic or ovate-rhombic, terminal one larger, 6 – 10 × 4.5 – 9 cm, lateral ones smaller, oblique, entire or 3-lobed, hirsute on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 8–15 cm or longer, flowers aggregated on nodes. Calyx campanulate, 6 mm, 5-toothed, hairy. Corolla light blue or purplish; vexillum suborbicular, 8 – 12 mm wide, with 2 appendages and an auricle at base; wings obovate-oblong, with a rounded auricle on one side at base; keel falcate, shorter than wings. Ovary linear. Pods subterete, 5 – 8 × 0.4 cm, adpressed pubescent at first, 2-valved. Seeds oblong, 4 mm, truncate at both ends.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 248, 2396; HK sheet 40773.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang; India, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Aug. – Sep.; fruiting: Oct. –Nov.

Punica granatum L. 安石榴
Sp. Pl. 1: 472. 1753; FRPS 52(2): 120. 1983; FGD 2: 103, fig. 71. 1991.

Shrub or small tree, 3– 5(–10) m tall; branchlets with many axillary leafless or leafy spurs, often spine-tipped, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petiole 2–10 mm; leaf blade papery, oblong-lanceolate, 2–9 × 1–2 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse or mucronate, margins entire, glabrous; lateral veins slender. Flowers large, terminal, 1 – 5-fasciculate at branch apex, bright red, fleshy, sessile or subsessile. Calyx red or pale yellow, tube funnel-shaped, ca. 2–3 cm, leathery; lobes ovate-triangular, 8–13 mm, with a yellowish green gland at apex, papillate at margin, persistent. Petals bright red, rounded or obovate, 1.5–3 × 1–2 cm, crumpled, rounded at apex. Stamens numerous, yellow, filaments to 13 mm. Style bent near apex, 8 mm; stigma capitate. Fruit subglobose, variously coloured, yellowish green, white or reddish, 5–12 cm in diam., crowned by the persistent calyx. Seeds red, pink or yellowish white.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. H. C. Tang 196.
Distribution: Caucasus, C, W & S Asia, widely cultivated in temperate and tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Edible (fruit).

Putranjiva formosana Kaneh. & Sasaki ex Shimada 台灣假黃楊（台灣核果木）
Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 24: 83. 1934.
Drypetes formosana (Kaneh. &. Sasaki ex Shimada) Kaneh., Formosan Trees (rev. ed.), 336, fig. 292. 1916; FRPS 44(1): 42. 1994; FGD 5: 37. 2003.

Small tree; branchlets sulcate or angulate, glabrescent or glabrous. Leaves thin-leathery; petioles 6 – 10 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-ovate, 5 – 8 × 3 – 5 cm, base unequally obtuse, apex acuminate, margin entire to crenulate-serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces; Racemes axillary, 6 – 8 cm, velutinous, bracteate. Male flowers: calyx 4 – 6-partite, lobes imbricate; stamens 2; petals,disk and rudimentary ovary absent. Female flowers: calyx 5-partite, lobes narrowly elliptic; ovary ovoid, 2-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule. Drupes ovoid-ellipsoidal, 10–13 × 7–8 mm, covered with appressed grey short hairs, 1-seeded.

Locality: Lamma Island, Sung Kong, Ninepin Group, Ching Chau. F. W. Xing 8625, 10144.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests at low altitudes. Flowering: May– Jul.; fruiting: Jul. – Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Drypetes formosana (Kaneh. & Sasaki ex Shimada) Kaneh. previously (Check List HK Plants 179. 2002; 65. 2004). Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Putranjiva roxburghii Wall. 假黃楊（藥用核果木）
Tent. Fl. Napal. 61. 1826; Airy Shaw, Kew Bull. 26: 257, fig. 62. 1972.
Drypetes roxburghii (Wall.) Hurus., J. Sci. Uni. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 6: 337. 1954.

Tree up to 15 m tall; branchlets sulcate, pubescent. Petioles 2.5 – 7 mm. Leaves distichous, obliquely ovate or ovate-lanceolate, sometimes elliptic or rhomboid, 4 – 13 × 1.5 – 4.5 cm, base obliquely cuneate or acute, apex acute or acuminate, margin closely and shallowly serrulate, glabrescent; veins fine. Flowers small, yellow. Male flowers in axillary glomerules, 6 – 12-flowered; pedicels short; calyx 4 –5-partite, ca. 1 mm; stamens 2 – 3( – 4), ca. 1.5 mm; anthers subglobose, sparsely hairy. Female flowers solitary or in pairs; pedicels 1.5 – 2.5 cm, pubescent; calyx 5-partite; lobes erect, very unequal, 1 – 2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent, with 2 ovules in each locule; stigmas 2 – 3, divaricate-recurved. Drupes indehiscent, rhombic-ellipsoidal, white-tomentose, 1-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated in Botanical Garden of Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 588, 1384, 1392, 1813; HK sheet 5824.
Distribution: India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Jul.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Drypetes roxburghii (Wall.) Hurus. previously (Check List HK Plants 179. 2002; 65. 2004).

Pycnospora lutescens (Poir.) Schindl. 密子豆

J. Bot. 64(762): 145. 1926; FRPS 41: 61. 1994; FGD 5: 278, fig. 148. 2003.

Hedysarum lutescens Poir., Encycl. 6: 417. 1804.

Pycnospora hedysaroides R. Br., Prodr. 197. 1834, nom. illeg.; FHK 91. 1861; FKH 80. 1912.


Subshrub, 15 –60 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate. Branchlets grey pubescent. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets subleathery, obovate or obovate-oblong, terminal one 1.2– 1.5 × 1 – 2.5 cm, base cuneate or slightly cordate, apex rounded or emarginate, lateral ones smaller, adpressed pubescent on both surfaces, lateral veins 4–7 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal and axillary, 3 – 6 cm. Flowers paired on rachis. Calyx 2 mm, deeply lobed. Corolla purplish; vexillum elliptic, 4 mm, emarginate; wings and keel oblong, obtuse. Ovary tomentose. Pods oblong, 6 – 10 × 5–6 mm, turgid, thin hairy, marked with very fine transverse veins, black when mature. Seeds 6– 8, small, reniform.


Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Shing Mun, Fung Yuen, Tai A Chau, Lamma Island. L. T. Lo 313; Y. W. Lam 1023, 1182.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.

Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Sep.

Pycreus flavidus (Retz.) T. Koyama 球穗扁莎
J. Jap. Bot. 51: 316. 1976; FTW ed. 2, 5: 292. 2000; FYN 15: 648. 2003; FGD 8: 337. 2007; FOC. 23: 343. 2010.
Cyperus flavidus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 13. 1788.
Pycreus globosus Rchb., Fl. Germ. Excurs. 140. 1830; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 166. 1961.
Cyperus vulgaris Siebold ex Kunth, Enum. Pl. 2: 4. 1837; FHK 385. 1861.

Annual or perennial. Rhizome short; roots fibrous. Culms densely tufted, 8–60 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade narrowly linear to setaceous, 2–24 cm × 1–2 mm, acuminate, flattish-plicate or canaliculate; sheath 1–10 cm, reddish brown. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest up to 25 cm. Inflorescence simple, open congested and appearing ± capitate; primary branches   6, 0.5–7 cm. Spikes broadly ovoid to ± globose, 1–3 × 1.2–4 cm; axis 0.1–1 cm. Spikelets 5–20 per spike, spreading, linear or linear-oblong, 6 – 30 × 1.5–3 mm, axis straight. Glumes oblong-obovate, 1.5–2.5 × 1  .5 mm, narrowly obtuse, sides chartaceous, pale brown to dark reddish brown, shiny, margins pale-hyaline, keel acute, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens 2; anthers 0.5 mm. Style short; stigmas 2. Achenes narrowly obovate to oblong-elliptic, 0.8–1.2 × 0.4–0.6 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 259; Y. S. Lau 2540; K. L. Yip 4044.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW regions; Japan, Korea, Mediterranean regions, S Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Pycreus polystachyos (Rottb.) P. Beauv. 多枝扁莎（多穗扁莎）
Fl. Oware 2: 48, t. 86, f. 2. 1807 [“polystachyus”]; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 169. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 292. 2000; FGD 8: 337. 2007; FOC 23: 244. 2010.
Cyperus polystachyus Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 21. 1773 [“polystachyus”]; FHK 385. 1861.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome absent; roots fibrous. Clums tufted, 10–80 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, 4–25 cm × 1.5–3(–4) mm, apex acuminate, flattish-plicate, soft or subrigid; sheaths reddish brown. Involucral bract 3–5, lowest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence simple, open to congested or ± capitate; primary branches (when present) 2–8, up to 7 cm. Spikes 1.8–3 × 1.3–2.2 cm; axis 0.1–0.8 cm. Spikelets 4–25 per spike, erect or erect-patent, crowded, linear to linear-lanceolate, 5–13 × 1.5–2 mm, flattened; axis zigzag. Glumes oblong-ovate to ovate-elliptic, 1.7–2.5 × 0.8–1 mm, apex acute to sometimes narrowly obtuse, mucronate, sides thinly chartaceous, pale brown or greenish to reddish brown, margins narrowly white-hyaline, keel acute, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens (1–)2; anthers 0.5–1 mm. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes oblong to oblongobovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.5 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 91; HK sheet 30228, 39701.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Taiwan, Liaoning; tropical and warm temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Streamsides and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Pycreus pumilus (L.) Domin 矮扁莎
Bibliogr. Bot. Cracow 85: 417. 1915; FRPS 11: 170. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 293. 2000; FGD 8: 336. 2007; FOC 23: 245. 2010.
Cyperus pumilus L., Cent. Pl. II 6. 1756.
Pycreus pulvinatus Nees, Contrib. 74. 1834; FKH 294. 1912.

Annual. Culms tufted, 1–20 cm tall, 0.5–1 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves few, shorter than to surpassing culm; blade narrowly linear, 1–19 cm × 1–2 mm, gradually narrowed, long-acuminate, flat; sheath 0.5–4 cm, pale brown to light reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the lowest   20 cm. Inflorescence capitate or simple, primary branches 0–6, up to 3 cm. Spikes ovoid to subglobose, 0.6–1.5 × 1–1.2 cm; axis up to 0.3 cm, often distinct. Spikelets 3–many, spreading, oblong to oblonglanceolate, 3–10 × 1.5–2.5 mm, flattened; axis ± straight. Glumes ovate to ovate-elliptic, 1–1.8 × 1–1.3 mm, apex rounded-truncate to emarginate, mucronate, sides translucent, pale greenish to brownish, keel acute, 3  -veined, green to reddish brown. Stamens 2; anthers 0.3 mm. Style ca. 0.5 mm; stigmas 2, ca. 0.3 mm. Achenes elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, 0.5–0.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, brownish, minutely punctate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sheung Shui, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Wan (Sai Kung), Po Toi Islands. S. P. Lau 25; J. C. Shaw 640; HK sheet 30229.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Nepal, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Pycreus sanguinolentus (Vahl) Nees 紅鱗扁莎
Linnaea 9: 283. 1835; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 170. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 293. 2000; FYN 15: 649. 2003; FGD 8: 338. 2007; FOC 23: 245. 2010.
Cyperus sanguinolentus Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 351. 1805.
Cyperus eragrostis Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 322. 1805, non Lam. 1791; FHK 385. 1861.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Culms tufted, 10–60 cm tall, 0.7–2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, lower part with several nodes. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, 4–11 cm × 2–4 mm, acuminate, flattish-plicate; sheath 1–3 cm, pale green to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest 10–15 cm. Inflorescence ± capitate or simple; primary branches 2–5, 1–4 cm. Spikes ovoid, 0.9–2 × 1–2 cm; axis 1–4 mm. Spikelets 3–17, narrowly ovate or oblong-lanceolate, 7–20 × 2–3.5 mm, axis straight. Glumes ovate or broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, obtuse, sides membranous, pale brown to reddish or purple brown, keel rather broad, often distinctly furrowed on both sides of keel, 3–5-veined, green. Stamens 3; anthers 0.7 – 1 mm. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, 1–1.3 × 0.8– 1 mm, black, minutely punctate.

Locality: Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Pui O. Y. W. Lam 1624, 2219, 2232.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; C to E Asia, Mediterranean region, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Pygeum topengii Merr. 臀果木

Philipp. J. Sci., 15(3): 237. 1919; FRPS 38: 126. 1986; FGD 4: 241. 2000; FOC 9: 431. 2003.

Pygeum latifolium auct. non Miq.: FHK 104. 1861; FKH 93. 1912.


Tree, 8 – 25 m tall; branchlets lenticellate, initially brown pubescent, gradually glabrescent. Petioles 5 – 8 mm, brown pubescent; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade leathery, ovate-elliptic or elliptic, 6 – 12 × 3 – 5.5 cm, base broadly cuneate and ± asymmetric, apex shortly acute, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially covered with brown appressed hairs, especially on midvein and lateral veins, with 2 black glands near the base; lateral veins 5 – 8 on each side of midvein, prominent on abaxial surface. Racemes solitary or fasciculate, 4 – 7 cm, many-flowered. Peduncles and pedicels densely brown pubescent; pedicels 1 – 3 mm; flowers 2 – 3 mm in diam.; sepals 5 or 6, triangular-ovate, 1 – 2 mm, apex acute; petals 5 or 6, oblong, slightly longer than sepals or indistinguishable from sepals, abaxially pubescent, apex obtuse; ovary glabrous. Drupe reniform, deeply brown, 0.8 – 1 × 1 – 1.6 cm, glabrous, apically depressed.


Locality: Shing Mun, Yuen Tun Ha, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen Valley, Ng Tung Chai, Lai Chi Wo. Y. S. Lau 232; P. S. Choi 228; Y. W. Lam 1872.

Distribution: Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.

Ecology: Forests and fung shui woods, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.– Oct.; fruiting: Winter.

Uses: Oil (seed).

Pyracantha crenulata (D. Don) M. Roem. 火棘

Fam. Nat. Syn. Monogr. 3: 220. 1847; FRPS 36: 182. 1974; FGD 4: 173. 2000; FOC 9: 110. 2003; FGX 2: 327. 2005.

Mespilus crenulatus D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 238. 1825.


Shrub or small tree, to 5 m tall; branchlets thorny, dark brown, rusty pubescent initially, glabrescent. Petioles short, initially brown pubescent, glabrescent; leaf blade oblong or oblanceolate, rarely ovate-lanceolate, 2 – 7 × 0.8 – 1.8 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, sometimes with a short tip, margin crenulate or sparsely so, glabrous on both surfaces, midvein impressed abaxially, prominent adaxially. Compound corymbs terminal, 3 – 5 cm in diam., many-flowered; bracts caducous, lanceolate; peduncles 4 – 10 mm, glabrous. Flowers 6 – 9 mm in diam.; hypanthium campanulate, glabrous; sepals triangular, abaxially glabrous, apex acute, erect and persistent in fruits; petals white, orbicular, 4 – 5 × 3 – 4 mm, apex rounded; stamens 20; filaments 2 – 3 mm; ovary densely white pubescent apically; styles 5, free, as long as stamens. Pome orangish red when mature, subglobose, 3 – 8 mm in diam.


Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 34, 1800; L. T. Lo 20.

Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Jiangsu; India, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Vietnam.

Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Sep.– Dec.

Uses: Ornamental.

Pyrenaria microcarpa (Dunn) H. Keng 小果石筆木
Gard. Bull. Singapore 26: 134. 1972.
Tutcheria microcarpa Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 197. 1909; FKH 45. 1912; FGD 2: 147. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 203. 1998.

Tree or shrub; young branches yellowish brown, pubescent, soon glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 5–8 mm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; leaf blade elliptic to oblong, 5 –12 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, lateral veins 8 –10 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surface. Flowers axillary, solitary, white or light yellow, 1.5 –2.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 1–2 mm, pubescent; bracteoles 2, caducous, broadly ovate to crescent-shaped, 2–3 mm, densely yellow sericeous abaxially, glabrous adaxially; sepals 5–7, caducous, semiorbicular to reniform, unequal, 3 – 8 × 5 –10 mm, leathery, densely yellow sericeous abaxially, glabrous adaxially, apex rounded; petals 5–7, obovate, 1–1.5 × 1–1.3 cm, sericeous abaxially, slightly connate at base; stamens many, 6 – 8 mm, glabrous; adnate to petals; ovary 3-locular, densely sericeous; styles 5– 8 mm, glabrous. Capsule triangular-globose, 1.0 –1.8 × 1–1.5 cm, 3-locular with 3 seeds per locule, dehiscing from base, sparsely sericeous; pericarp 1–1.5 mm thick when dry. Seeds brown, compressed, oblong-ovate, 6 – 8 mm.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Lin Fa Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Wu Kau Teng, Sunset Peak. L. T. Lo 660; Y. S. Lau 2984; Y. W. Lam 1661.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Broadleaved evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Nicholson in September 1909.

Pyrenaria spectabilis (Champ.) C. Y. Wu & S. X. Yang 石筆木
Novon 15(2): 381. 2005.
Camellia spectabilis Champ., Trans. Linn. Soc. Bot. London 21: 111. 1850; et in Hook., Kew Journ. 3: 131. 1851.
Thea spectabilis (Champ.) Kochs, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 27: 595. 1900.
Tutcheria spectabilis (Champ.) Dunn, J. Bot. 46: 324. 1908; FKH 45. 1912; Yip, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 42: 575. 2004.
Pyrenaria championii (Nakai) H. Keng, Gard. Bull. Singapore 26(1): 134. 1972, nom. illeg.
Tutcheria championii Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 26: 708. 1940; FGD 2: 145. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 197. 1998, nom. illeg.
Camellia reticulata auct. non Lindl.: FHK 31. 1861.

Tree or small tree, branches greyish brown, young branches puberulous, soon glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 12–18 × 4–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or undulate-serrate, yellowish when dry, shining and glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent, soon glabrescent abaxially; lateral veins 10 –14 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary, white, 4–7 cm in diam; pedicels 0.6–1.0 cm, pubescent; bracteoles 2, ovate, 1–1.5 × 1.5 –2 cm, densely yellow sericeous abaxially; sepals 9 –11, white, suborbicular, 2–3 cm in diam., yellowish sericeous abaxially, apex rounded to retuse, margin membranous; petals 5 or 6, broadly obovate, 4– 5 × 2– 3 cm, yellowish sericeous abaxially, apex emarginate, margin membranous; stamens many, ca. l. 5 cm, glabrous, slightly connate at the base and adnate to base of petals; ovary 3 – 6-locular with 2– 5 ovules per locule, densely yellowish tomentose; styles 3 – 6- lobed, pubescent at proximal part. Capsule globose to oblate, 4–7 cm in diam., 3– 6-locular with 2– 5 seeds per locule, dehiscing from base, greyish tomentose. Seeds brown, oblong, 1.5 –2.0 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tao Po, Kwai Tau Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. C. P. Lau 25; N. K. Chun 40709; K. L. Yip 4199.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Broad-leaf evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Onamental, materials (timber, lipids).
Notes: The type specimen (Champion s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Onamental, materials (timber, lipids).
Notes: The type specimen (Champion s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Pyrostegia venusta (Ker‑Gawl.) Miers 炮仗花
Proc. Roy. Hort. Soc. London 3: 188. 1863; FRPS 69: 3, pl. 3: 4 – 5. 1990; FFJ 5: 84, fig. 92. 1993.
Bignonia venusta Ker‑Gawl., Bot. Reg. t. 249. 1818.
Pyrostegia ignea (Vell.) C. Presl, Bot. Bemerk. 93. 1845; FGZ 606, fig. 322. 1956; FHN 3: 530, fig. 906. 1974.

Stems robust, ridged; branchlets sulcate. Petiole ca. 2 cm; leaflets 2–3; petiolules 1–2.5 cm; leaf blades papery, ovate, 4.5–10 × 2.5–5 cm, base rounded, apex long acuminate, margin entire; glabrous and finely glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–4 pairs; terminal leaflet often modified into a 3‑branched tendril. Panicles terminal, 10–12 cm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 7 mm, 5‑dentate. Corolla tubular, orange‑red, 7–8 cm, with a ring of white hairs at middle adaxially, base constricted, upper part bilabiate, upper lip 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 8 mm, erect, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes long elliptic, ca. 1.6 cm, reflexed, margin white pubescent. Filaments filiform, anthers divergent. Ovary cylindric; style slender, exserted; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes lingulate, flat. Capsules long cylindric; valves leathery, boat‑shaped. Seeds in many rows, with membranous wing.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2097.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pyrus calleryana Decne. 豆梨（麻子梨）
Jard. Fruit. 1: 329. 1871 – 72; FPRS 36: 367. 1974; FFJ 2: 335. 1985; FGD 4: 192. 2000; FOC 9: 178. 2003.

Deciduous tree, 5–8 m tall, brachlets initially villose. Petioles 2–4 cm, glabrous; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate, rarely oblong-ovate, 4–8 × 3.5–6 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, rarely acute, margin obtusely crenate, initially pubescent, soon glabrescent, lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein. Racemes umbel-like, 6–12-flowered; peduncles glabrous; bracts linear-lanceolate, membranous, 0.8–1.3 cm, caducous; pedicels 1.5–3 cm, lengthening to 4 cm in fruit, glabrous. Flowers 2–2.5 cm in diam.; hypanthium urceolate, glabrous; sepals lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, pubescent adaxially, glabrous abaxially, apex acuminate, margin entire, deciduous; petals white, ovate, 1.3 × 1 mm, shortly clawed at base, apex rounded; stamens 20, slightly shorter than petals; ovary 2(–3)-locular, glabrous; styles 2(–3), nearly as long as stamens, glabrous. Pomes globose, 1 cm in diam., blackish brown, with pale dots.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Tung Chung. C. P. Lau 13; L. T. Lo 599; Y. W. Lam 17.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei, Henan, Shandong; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Hillslopes, forests. Flowering: Feb. –Apr.; fruiting: Jun. –Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pyrus pyrifolia (Burm. f.) Nakai 沙梨（梨）
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 40: 564. 1926; FRPS 36: 365. 1974; FFJ 2: 334. 1985; FGD 4: 191. 2000; FOC 9: 177. 2003.
Ficus pyrifolia Burm. f., Fl. Indica 226. 1768.
Pyrus sinensis auct. non Lindl.: FKH 96. 1912.

Deciduous tree, 7 – 15 m tall; branchlets initially pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 3 – 4.5 cm, initially pubescent; stipules membranous, linear-lanceolate, 1 – 1.5 cm, caducous; leaf blade ovate or ovate-elliptic, 7–15 × 4–8 cm, base rounded or subcordate, rarely broadly cuneate, apex caudate or acuminate, margin spinulose-serrate, glabrous or initially pubescent; lateral veins 7 – 9 on each side of midvein. Racemes umbel-like, 3 – 9-flowered; peduncles initially pubescent; pedicels 3.5–5 cm, initially pubescent; bracts linear, 1 –1.4 cm, membranous, caducous. Flowers 2.5–3.5 cm in diam.; hypanthium urceolate, abaxially glabrous; sepals triangular-ovate, ca. 5 mm, abaxially glabrous, adaxially densely brown pubescent, margin glandular-denticulate, apex acuminate, caducous; petals white, ovate, 15 – 17 mm, shortly clawed at base, apex rounded; stamens 20, about half the length of the petals; ovary (4–)5-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles (4–)5, glabrous, nearly as long as the stamens. Pome subglobose, 5–8 cm in diam., with pale dots.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 670; HK sheet 10005, 40761.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also cultivated in Korea and Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Fruit.

Quercus acutissima Carr. 麻櫟
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 6: 33. 1862; FFJ 1: 413, fig. 370. 1982; FRPS 22: 219, pl. 68: 1. 1998; FTW ed. 2, 2: 114. 1996; FOC 4: 372. 1999.

Deciduous tree, to 15 m tall. Bark dark greyish brown, deeply fissured. Branchlets yellowish brown, glabrescent. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1.5 –3.5 cm, glabrescent; leaf blade variable in shape, usually oblong-lanceolate, 9–13(–18) × 2– 4(– 6) cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate with bristle-like teeth, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially pubescent when young, soon glabrate, only with tuft of hairs on axil of veins; lateral veins 13–17 on each side of midvein. Male catkins, 3 – 4 cm; stamens usually 3 –7, rarely 2–10; filaments 2.5 –3 mm. Female flowers 2–3, clustered or in short catkins. Cupule cup-shaped, ca. 1.5 cm high, 2–4 cm in diam., enclosing 1/3 –1/2 of nut; bracts subulate to linear, reflexed, greyish-whitetomentose. Nut ovoid or ellipsoid, 1.6 –2.2 cm high, 1.5–2 cm in diam., top rounded; scar convex.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 26470, 40661.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Liaoning, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, N India, Nepal.
Ecology: Woods on sunny slopes.
Uses: Material (timber).

Quercus fabri Hance 白櫟
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 10: 202. 1869; FFJ 1: 414, fig. 372. 1982; FRPS 22: 227, pl. 71: 1–2. 1998; FOC 4: 373. 1999; FKH 253. 1912.
Quercus serrata auct. non Thunb.: FKH 253. 1912.

Deciduous tree to 20 m tall, but often shrubby. Bark dark greyish brown, deeply fissured. Branchlets densely grey to greyish brown tomentose. Leaves thickly papery or thinly leathery; petioles 3 – 6 mm, yellowish-brown-tomentose; leaf blade obovate, to obovate-elliptic, 6 –16 × 2.5– 8 cm, base broadly cuneate or narrowly rounded, apex obtuse, margin undulate-serrate or coarsely and obtusely serrate, covered with greyish yellow stellate hairs on both surfaces when young, only on abaxial surface when mature; lateral veins 8 –12 on each side of midvein, tertiary veins conspicuous abaxially. Male catkins 3 – 4 cm, pendulous, rachis tomentose. Female catkins 1–4 cm, with 2– 4 flowers. Cupule cup‑shaped, 7– 8 mm high, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts ovate-lanceolate, imbricate. Nut ellipsoid to ovoid-ellipsoid, 1.5 –1.8 cm high, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., glabrous; scar convex.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 10934, 11656).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Fuelwood.

Quisqualis indica L. 使君子
Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 1: 556. 1762; FYN 1: 85. 1977; FRPS 53(1): 16, pl. 3: 8 – 9. 1984; FGD 3: 200, fig. 138. 1995.
Quisqualis sinensis Lindl., Bot. Reg. 30: t. 15. 1844.

Scandent shrub, 2 – 8 m tall; branchlets pale yellowish brown pubescent. Petioles 5 – 8 mm, rusty pubescent when young, persistent and like a spine after leaf falling off. Leaves thinly papery, ovate, oblong or elliptic, 5–11 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base rounded, apex short acuminate, margin entire or slightly wavy, glabrous adaxially, sometimes sparsely rusty pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 7 – 8 on each side of midvein. Inflorescence spicate, ca. 10-flowered; bracteoles linear. Calyx-tube long tubular, deciduous yellowish pubescent abaxially, lobes triangular. Petals 5, oblong or obovate-oblong, white at first, turning pale red later. Stamens 10, in 2 whorls, short, included. Ovary 1-locular; ovules 3. Fruit fusiform, 2.5–4 cm, 1.2–2.5 cm in diam., conspicuously 5-ribbed, brown when mature, dehiscing into 3–5 valves at apex, 1-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. S. T. Dunn 5268; W. J. Tutcher 9532; Y. S. Lau 1133.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; India, Myanmar, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: Early summer; fruiting: Late autumn.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ranunculus cantoniensis DC. 禺毛茛（小回回蒜、自扣草）
Prodr. 1: 43.1842; FRPS 28: 321, pl. 99: 1–3. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 550, pl. 260. 1996; FOC 6: 428. 2001; FGD 5: 22. 2003.
Ranunculus pensylvanicus auct. non L.: FKH 27. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems erect, 20–50 cm tall, branched at the upper part, densely yellowish white hirsute. Basal leaves ternate; petioles 4.5–12 cm, hirsute; central leaflet stalked, elliptic or rhomboid 3–4.6 × 2–3.5 cm, 3-lobed or 3-parted, serrate, sparsely strigose on both surfaces; lateral leaflets unequally 2-parted, short-stalked or sessile; lower cauline leaves similar to the basal leaves, upper ones gradually reduced. Flowers terminal, solitary or in few-flowered cymes. Pedicels 2–5 cm, hirsute. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm. Petals 5, yellow, elliptic, 5–6 × 2–3 mm, base clawed. Stamens numerous, anthers ca. 1 mm. Receptacles oblong, white puberulous. Aggregate fruits subglobose, ca. 1 cm in diam.; achenes compressed, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin. H. C. Tang 801; Y. S. Lau 1241.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Wet places, ditches, paddy fields. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Ranunculus sceleratus L. 石龍芮
Sp. Pl. 1: 551. 1753; FKH 27. 1912; FRPS 28: 310, pl. 96: 1–4. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 560, pl. 267. 1996; FOC 6: 421. 2001; FGD 5: 21. 2003.
Hecatonia palustris Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 303. 1790.

Annual herb. Stems erect, 10–40 cm tall, branched above middle, glabrous or nearly so. Basal leaves long petioled, simple, pentagonous or reniform in outline, 1–4 × 1.5–5 cm, base broadly cordate, 3-partite; central lobes obovate-cuneate, apex obtuse, indistinctly 3-lobed, margin coarsely margin coarsely dentate, glabrous; lateral lobes obliquely fan-shaped, unequally 2-lobed. Petioles 3 –15 cm subglabrous. Cauline leaves many, lower ones similar to basal leaves, upper ones smaller, 3-divided, sparsely pubescent on abaxial surface. Cymes terminal, many-flowered. Flowers 4–8 mm in diam. Pedicels 1–2(– 3) cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Sepals elliptic, 2–3.5 mm, puberulous abaxially. Petals 5, yellow, narrowly obovate, ca. 3.5 mm, base shortly clawed. Stamens 10 or more, ca. 2 mm. Receptacles cylindric, sparsely puberulous. Aggregate fruits oblong, 8–12 mm; achenes numerous, obovoid, slightly compressed, glabrous.

Locality: New Territories. H. C. Tang 2466; Y. S. Lau 2457.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China and in subtropical and temperate regions of the N hemisphere.
Ecology: Wet places, near ponds, ditches and in paddy fields. Flowering: Jan.–Jun.; fruiting: Mar.–Jun.

Raphanus sativus L. 蘿蔔
Sp. Pl. 669. 1753; FHK 17. 1861; FHN 1: 356. 1964; FGD 3: 31. 1995; FOC 8: 25. 2001.

Annual or biennial herb, up to 1 m tall; roots fleshy, white or purple, globose or oblong. Stems erect. Basal leaves petiolate, oblong to oblanceolate, 8 –30 cm, lyrate or pinnatisect, lateral lobes 4 – 6 on each side of midrib, oblong or ovate, 10 × 5 cm; upper cauline leaves often narrow and entire. Racemes terminal and axillary; pedicels 5 –15 mm. Sepals oblong, 5 –7 mm. Petals white or pink, often with dark veins, obovate, 1–1.5 cm, claw ca. 5 mm. Siliques cylindric, 3 – 6 cm, constricted between seeds, separated by a pithy substance filling the pods. Seeds red-brown, ovoid, ca. 3 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 20; J. L. Sample 7; C. O. Levine 3272.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Jun.
Uses: Vegetable.

Rauvolfia verticillata (Lour.) Baill. 蘿芙木
Hist. Pl. 10: 170. 1889; FRPS 63: 55, pl. 19. 1977; FGD 1: 440, fig. 490. 1987; FOC 16: 159. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 54. 1999.
Dissolena verticillata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 137. 1790.
Rauvolfia chinensis (Spreng.) Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26(173): 95. 1889; FKH 168. 1912.
Rauvolfia perakensis King & Gamble, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 74(2): 424. 1908; FRPS 63: 53. 1977.

Shrubs to 3 m tall, erect, glabrous. Branchlets pale grey, lenticellate. Lower leaves opposite, terminal leaves in whorls of 3 or 4; petioles 0.5 – 1.5cm; leaf blade narrowly to broadly ovate or oblong, 3.5 – 25 × 5 – 13 cm, nearly papery to membranous, lateral veins 6 or 7 on each side of midvein. Cymes rather lax, 3 – 9 together; peduncle 2 – 15 cm. Pedicel 3 – 6 mm. Corolla white, tube cylindric, 1 – 1.8 cm, inflated and villous from middle to throat; lobes broadly elliptic or ovate, 1 – 4.5 mm. Stamens inserted at middle of corolla tube. Ovary of 2 carpels completely free up to the single style. Drupes ellipsoidal or ovoid, free from each other, ca. 10 × 5 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Mount Gough. H. C. Tang 2406; Y. S. Lau 223, 2347.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jan. – Oct.; fruiting: Apr. – Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ravenala madagascariensis Sonn. 旅人蕉
Voy. Ind. Orient. 2: 223, pl. 124–126. 1782; FHN 4: 89. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 16, fig. 4. 1981; FGD 2: 396, fig. 272. 1991.

Trunk palm-like, woody, 5–6(–30) m tall. Leaves large, musa-like in 2 ranks toward top of stem, giving the plant a fan-shaped appearance; leaf blade oblong, 1.5–2 m × 50–75 cm, slightly narrower toward the rounded apex, base subtruncate, concolorous on both surfaces. Inflorescences axillary; bracts 6–12, large and boat-shaped, one above the other and distichously arranged, each enveloping 5–12 flowers; sepals 3, lanceolate, ca. 20 × 1.2 cm, leathery; petals like the sepals, but the middle one shorter and narrower; stamens 6, slender, 15–16 cm, anthers two times as long as the filaments; ovary depressed, 4–5 mm; style equaling the sepals, stigma fusiform. Capsule woody, dehiscing by 3 valves.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens.
Distribution: Native to Madagascar; widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Fertile soils. Flowering: All year around.
Uses: Ornamental.

Reevesia thyrsoidea Lindl. 梭羅樹
Quart. Journ. Sci. Lit. Arts, 2(2): 112. 1827; FHK 37. 1861; FKH 49. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 150. 1984; FHN 2: 79. 1965; FGD 1: 137. 1987.

Tree; bark grey-brown. Petioles 1–3 cm, inflated at both ends; leaves leathery, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 5 –7 × 2.5 –3 cm, base round or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, margin quite entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorencence corymbose, terminal. Flowers dense; calyx campanulate, 6 mm, 5-lobed, stellate hairy abaxially; petals 5, white, spathulate, 1 cm, slightly spreading; androgynophore ca. 2 cm, with 15 anthers at apex forming a terminal head; ovary globose, 5-locular, hairy. Capsules ellipsoid, pear-shaped, ca. 3 cm, 5-angulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 851; K. T. Tso 20207; N. K. Chun 40707.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Cambodia.
Ecology: Secondary forests, thickets and grassland. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Fibre, timber.

Rehderodendron kwangtungense Chun 廣東木瓜紅
Sunyatsenia. 1: 290. 1943; FGD 1: 383. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 136. 1987; FOC 15: 270. 1996.
Rehderodendron hui Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 291. 1934.

Tree to 15 m tall, bark grey; branchlets reddish brown, smooth; winter buds ovoid to obconical, red-brown. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to elliptic, 7–16 × 3–8 cm, apex acute to acuminate, base cuneate, margin remotely serrate, glabrous or slightly stellate pubescent and villose along veins abaxially, lateral veins 7–11 on each side of midvein. Racemes 6–8-flowered, ca. 7 cm; rhachis, pedicels, bracts and calyx densely grey-yellow stellate tomentose; pedicels ca. 1 cm; calyx campanulate, ca. 6 mm, lobes lanceolate; corolla lobes ovate, slightly unequal in length, 2–2.5 × 1–1.4 cm, densely stellate pubescent on both surfaces; stamens 10, longer ones as long as corolla. Fruit cylindrical, obovoid or ellipsoid, 4.5 – 8 × 2.5 – 4 cm, brown to grey-brown, glabrous or slightly pubescent, 5–10-ribbed, smooth between ribs, exocarp ca. 1 mm thick, mesocarp 0.8 –1.2 cm thick, endocarp woody. Seeds 2– 4, spindly, 2–3 cm.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Kwun Yam Shan. P. S. Choi 348, 323; Y. S. Lau 2746.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Remirea maritima Aubl. 海濱莎
Hist. Pl. Guiane 1: 45, pl. 16. 1775; FKH 302. 1912; FRPS 11: 123. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 295. 2000; FGD 8: 344. 2007; FOC 23: 242. 2010.
Miegia maritima (Aubl.) Willd., Sp. Pl. 1(1): 311 – 312. 1797.

Perennial; rhizomes slender, rigid, horizontally long-creeping, branching, internodes 1–10 cm, clothed with brown sheaths and their fibrous remnants. Culms solitary or a few together at nodes of rhizome, 3–15 cm tall, usually with a considerable length of lower part in sand, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves aggregated on lower part of upper ground portion of culms; blades linear, shorter than or occasionally equalling the culm, 3–8 × 0.4–0.5 cm, acute, leathery, glaucous-green, canaliculate; sheaths 1–1.5 cm, light to reddish brown. Inflorescence terminal, capitate, usually 3–8 congested in a head-like cluster at culm-apex, 1–2 × 1–3 cm. Leafy bracts 3–8, patent or reflexed, equalling or longer than inflorescence, longest one to 8 cm. Spikes ellipsoidal to ovoid, 1–3 × 0.7–1 cm, densely bearing many spikelets, glaucous or yellowish brown. Spikelets ovoid, terete to weakly laterally flattened, 4– 5 × 1–2 mm, acute, bearing 4 glumes, 1-fruited; rachilla jointed above base. Glumes ovate to broadly ovate, lowest 3 empty, fourth bearing a bisexual flower, 3–4.5 × 1.5–1.7 mm, acute to mucronate, margin membranous to chartaceous, 3–5-veined, pale to mid-brown, keel obtuse, brown. Stamens 3; anthers 2 mm long. Achenes oblong, trigonous, ca. 2.5 × 0.7 mm, maturing greyish brown, smooth; style shorter than achene; stigmas 3.

Locality: Hong Kong. HK sheet 8088.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Polygonum cuspidatum Siebold & Zucc. 虎杖
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: 208. 1846; FTW ed. 2, 2: 299, photo 126. 1996; FGD 4: 90. 2000.
Reynoutria japonica Houtt., Nat. Hist. 2(8): 640, t. 51, f. 1. 1777; FRPS 25: 105, pl. 22: 1–3. 1998; FYN 11: 359, pl. 98: 1–3. 2000; FOC 5: 319. 2003.

Perennial stout herb, with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, fistulous, 1–2 m tall, glabrous, with scattered red or reddish purple dots, woody at base. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–2 mm, papillose; leaf blade broadly ovate to ovate-elliptic, 5 –12 × 4 –9 cm, base broadly cuneate, truncate or subrounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, papillose on veins. Ocrea tubular, scarious, 0.3 –1 cm, apex oblique, glabrous, usually caducous. Inflorescence paniculate, axillary, 3 – 8 cm. Peduncles papillose. Bracts funnel-form, 1.5 –2 mm, apex acuminate, eciliate, each embracing 2– 4 flowers. Pedicels 2– 4 mm, articulate at the lower part. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious); perianth light green, 2–3 mm, deeply 5-lobed. Male flowers: perianth-segments with green midvein, not winged; stamens 8, exserted; female flowers: the outer 3 perianth-segments winged dorsally; wings enlarged in fruit. Ovary ovoid; styles 3; stigmas fimbriate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 4 – 5 mm, dark brown and shining, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Castle Peak. Y. S. Lau 2167.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Valleys and other wet places. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (vegetable).

Rhamnus brachypoda C. Y. Wu ex Y. L. Chen 山綠柴
Bull. Bot. Lab. N.-E. Forest. Inst., Harbin. 5: 85. 1979; FRPS 48(1): 85, pl. 23: 1 – 2. 1982.
Rhamnus virgatus auct. non Roxb.: FHK 68. 1861; FKH 64. 1912; FGD 4: 251. 2000.

Shrub, 1.5–3 m tall. Branchlets alternate, tawny pubescent when young, ending in a thorn. Stipules linear or lanceolate, deciduous. Leaves papery, alternate or clustered on abbreviated branchlets; petioles 4–9 mm, sparsely puberulent; leaf blade oblong, ovate-oblong or obovate, 3–10 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, acute or mucronate, margin serrulate, adaxial surface densely puberulent when young, glabrescent or only with hairs on the veins in age, abaxial surface initially puberulent on veins, glabrescent; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein, raised abaxially. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious), 4-merous, solitary, in pairs or 3–4 clustered in axils of lower leaves or at apex of abbreviated branchlets. Pedicels 2–6 mm. Male flowers: calyx funnel-shaped or campanulate, ca. 6 mm, 4-lobed to middle; lobes, ovate-lanceolate, sparsely puberulent on abaxial surface; petals cucullate or spathulate, ca. 2 mm, embracing the stamens. Female flowers: calyx campanulate, ca. 5 mm, 4-lobed to middle; lobes lanceolate, sparsely puberulent abaxially; ovary ovoid; style 3-parted to middle. Drupe obovate, 5–7 × 4–5 mm, black when mature.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Beaufort Island. Y. S. Lau 596; Y. W. Lam 210; S. P. Lau 173.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Rhamnus crenata Siebold & Zucc. 長葉凍綠
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(2): 146. 1843; FKH 64. 1912; FRPS 48(1): 23, pl. 6: 1– 2. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 3: 688. 1993; FGD 4: 254, fig. 150. 2000.

Deciduous spineless shrub, usually 1–2 m tall. Young shoots densely rusty pubescent. Stipules subulate, deciduous. Leaves papery, alternate; petioles 4–10 mm, rusty pubescent; leaf blade obovate, obovate-elliptic or oblong, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or abruptly acuminate, margin crenate-serrulate, adaxial surface puberulent on veins, glabrescent, abaxial surface sparsely pubescent, especially on veins; lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein, raised abaxially. Flowers bisexual, 5-merous, in axillary cymes; peduncle 4–8 mm, densely puberulent; pedicels ca. 3 mm, puberulent. Calyx broadly campanulate, 2–3 mm, 5-lobed to middle; lobes ovate-triangular, sparsely puberulent abaxially. Petals suborbicular, ca. 0.5 mm, apex 2-lobed. Stamens equaling the petals. Ovary globose, 3-locular; style clavate, undivided. Drupe globose or obovate-globose, 5–6 × 0.6–0.7 mm, from red turning black when mature.

Locality: Mount Davis, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lai Chi Wo, Luk Keng, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 52; Y. S. Lau 861; K. L. Yip 4406.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina.
Ecology: Thickets by streams and roadsides. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), material (dye).

Rhamnus napalensis (Wall.) Laws. 尼泊爾鼠李（半樹藤）
in Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 1: 640. 1875, “nipalensis”; FKH 63. 1912; FRPS 48(1): 46, pl. 11: 1 – 4. 1982; FGD 4: 253. 2000.
Ceanothus napalensis Wall., Fl. Ind. 2: 375. 1824.

Shrub, erect or half-climbing, 2–3 m tall, spineless. Young shoots puberulent, glabrescent. Leaves thickly leathery, turning black when dry, large ones and small ones alternately arranged; petioles 1–2 cm, sparsely puberulent or glabrescent. Large leaves oblong, 5–20 × 3–9 cm, base cuneate, apex mucronate or rounded, margin revolute, sparsely serrate, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface pubescent at axils of veins; lateral veins 5–9 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Flowers unisexual (plants dioecious), 5-merous, in cymose clusters, racemosely arranged or branched in panicles to 9 cm. Rachis tawny puberulent. Male flowers: calyx ca. 3 mm, 5-lobed to middle; lobes triangular, sparsely puberulent abaxially; petals ovate, adnate to the top of calyx-tube; stamens equaling to petals. Female flowers: calyx ca. 2 mm; petals caducous; staminodes 5; ovary globose, 3-locular; style 3-parted. Drupe obovate-globose, 5.5–6.5 × 4–5 mm, red when mature.

Locality: Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 2181.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.–Feb. of the following year.

Rhaphidophora hongkongensis Schott 獅子尾（崖角藤）
Bonplandia. 5: 45. 1857; FHN 4: 133, fig. 1038. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 36, pl. 6: 3–4. 1979; FYN 2: 754, fig. 204: 3–4. 1979; FFJ 6: 415, fig. 376. 1995; FTW ed 2, 5: 687, pl. 296. 2000; FGD 9: 185, fig. 101. 2009; FOC 23: 12. 2010.
Rhaphidophora peepla auct. non Schott: FHK 344. 1861.
Rhaphidophora angustifolia auct. non Schott: FKH 284. 1912.

Epiphytic liana. Stems rooting and attaching themselves to trees or rocks. Leaves papery to subleathery, distichous; petioles 5–10 cm, sulcate adaxially. Leaf blade falcate-elliptic to oblonglanceolate or oblanceolate, (10–)20–35 × 5–6(–14) cm, lateral veins many, diverging at an angle about 45˚ from the midrib. Peduncle inserted in long sheathing bracts, cylindrical, 4–5 cm; spathe green to pale yellow, ovate, 6–9 cm, apex acuminate, deciducous; spadix cylindrical, 5–8 cm; ovary hexagonalcylindrical, apex truncate. Berries yellowish green.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Bride's Pool, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. HK sheet 27434, 31061.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Thailand, Kalimantan.
Ecology: Climbing on trees and rocks in forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion 525, K) was collected from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion 525, K) was collected from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Rhaphiolepis indica (L.) Lindl. ex Ker 石斑木（車輪梅、春花）
Bot. Reg. 6: pl. 468. 1820; FKH 97. 1912; FHN 2: 200. 1965; FRPS 36: 276. 1974; FFJ 2: 329. 1985; FTW 3: 109. 1994; FOC 9: 142. 2003.
Crataegus indica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 477. 1753.

Shrub, rarely small trees, 1 – 4 m tall; branchlets initially brown tomentose, glabrescent. Leaves often crowded at apex of branchlet; petioles 5 – 18 mm, subglabrous; stipules subulate, caducous; leaf blade leathery, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 2– 8 × 1.5 – 4 mm, base attenuate and decurrent to the petioles, apex obtuse, acute or shortly acuminate, margin dentate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glabrous or sparsely tomentose, soon glabrescent, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, prominent abaxially. Panicles or racemes terminal, many-flowered, 4 – 6 cm; peduncles rusty tomentose; bracts linear-lanceolate, glabrous, caducous; pedicels 5–15 mm, densely rusty tomentose, glabrescent in fruit. Flowers fragrant, 1 – 1.3 cm in diam.; hypanthium obconical, 4–5 mm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent abaxially; sepals lanceolate, 4.5 – 8 mm, apex long acuminate, glabrous or pubescent abaxially; petals white or pink, obovate-lanceolate, 5–7 × 4–5 mm, pubescent at base, apex obtuse or acute; stamens 15, as long as or slightly longer than petals; ovary glabrous, 2–3-locular; styles 2–3, connate at base, subglabrous. Pome globose, purplish black, ca. 5 mm in diam., crowned by an annular remains of the calyx-teeth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 963, 2971; HK sheet 39936.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Forests or open fields. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Rhaphiolepis lanceolata Hu 細葉石斑木
J. Arnold Arbor. 13(3): 335. 1932; FHN 2: 200. 1965; FRPS 36: 282. 1974; FGD 4: 188. 2004; FOC 9: 144. 2003.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 1 – 3( –10) m tall; branchlets dark grey, initially brown pubescent, soon glabrescent. Leaves often crowded at apex of branchlets; petioles 2–4 mm, glabrous, winged; leaf blade leathery, linear-lanceolate, 3 – 9.5 × 0.5 – 1.2 cm, base narrowly cuneate and decurrent to the petioles, apex shortly acuminate or obtuse, margin sparsely crenate, revolute, glabrous, midvein impressed adaxially, lateral veins slender, prominent abaxially. Panicles terminal or axillary, many-flowered; peduncles brown pubescent; pedicels stout, 5–7 mm, brown pubescent; bracts lanceolate or subulate, 2–4 mm, pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers ca. 1 cm in diam.; hypanthium obconical, ca. 4 mm; sepals lanceolate, 4.5 – 7 mm, pubescent on both surfaces, apex acute to acuminate, or sometimes serrate towards the apex; petals white or pinkish, elliptic-lanceolate, 6–7 × 1.5–4 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse; stamens 15, slightly longer than or equaling petals; ovary 3-locular, pubescent; styles 3, glabrous, connate at base. Pome globose, 4–7 mm in diam., blackish purple, pubescent, crowned by an annular remains of the calyx-teeth.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Hoi Ha, Tsing Yi. L. T. Lo 425; P. S. Choi 174; Y. W. Lam 145.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets.
Notes: The species was reported as Rhaphiolepis salicifolia Lindl. previously (Check List HK Plants 126. 2002; 48. 2004).

Rhapis excelsa (Thunb.) Henry ex Rehder 棕竹
Rehder, J. Arnold Arbor. 11: 153. 1930; FHN 4: 161, fig. 1062. 1977; FGD 2: 448, fig. 313. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 20, pl. 4: 1–3. 1991; FOC 23: 146. 2010.
Rhapis flabelliformis L’ Hér. ex Aiton, Hort. Kew. 3: 473. 1789; FHK 340. 1861; FKH 286. 1912.
Chamaerops excelsa Thunb., J. A. Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 984. 1784.

Moderate shrub, dioecious, rhizomatous, 1.2–3 m tall. Stems clustered, slender, 1.5–3 cm in diam., covered with fibrous interwoven leaf sheaths. Leaves palmate, split deeply into 5–12 uneven segments, segments 2–5-ribbed, 20–32 × 1.5–4 cm, apices erose; sheaths with black interwoven fibres; petioles elliptic in cross-section, unarmed; hastula small, semi-circled or triangular. Inflorescences axillary, branched 2–3 orders, ca. 30 cm; prophyll and peduncle bract brown hairy; rachilla glabrous; flowers spirally arranged; male flowers ovoid to oblong, 5–6 mm, calyx cup-shaped, 3-lobed, corolla 3-lobed, stamens 6; female flowers 4 mm, sepals and petals similar to male flower, carpels 3, free, staminodes 6. Fruits usually developed from 1 carpel, subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam., yellow. Seed 1, globose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lamma Island. H. C. Tang 1776; Y. S. Lau 856, 1873.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or dry forests on slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Rhinacanthus nasutus (L.) Kurz 靈枝草（扭序花）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal. 2: 79. 1870.
Justicia nastus L., Sp. Pl. 16. 1753.
Rhinacanthus communis Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 109. 1832. nom. superfl.

Perennial herbs, 0.5–1 m tall, many‑branched. Stems erect, subquadrangular, faintly striate, densely pilose. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, densely pilose; leaf blades elliptic to ovate‑elliptic, rarely lanceolate, 2–11 × 0.8–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, sometimes obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, adaxially sparsely pilose or subglabrous, marked with copious cystoliths, abaxially densely pilose, lateral veins 5–6 pairs, meet near the margin. Panicles lax, terminal and axillary, 4–8 cm; flowers subsessile, discrete at the ends of divaricate branches. Rachis pilose. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 2 × 0.5 mm; bracteoles subulate, ca. 1 mm. Calyx ca. 3 mm, glandular‑bristly, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, unequal. Corolla greenish white; tube slender, ca. 3 cm, curved from the middle upwards, outside hirsute with downward pointing hairs, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 2.5 cm; upper lip erect, linear‑lanceolate, shorter than lower lip, apex reflexed, shallowly 2‑lobed, lower lip to 12 mm broad, abaxially hispid, 3‑lobed to the middle, lobes obovate. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous; anther‑thecae oblong. Ovary and style sparsely pilose; style ca. 1.5 cm. Capsule ca. 2 cm, with long solid stalk, bristly with gland‑tipped hairs, 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular‑helicoid, ca. 2.3 mm in diam., papillose.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 492, 1358; M. T. Kao 6355 (CAS).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Malesia, S Africa, Madagascar.
Ecology: Roadsides, thickets. Flowering: Dec.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rhododendron championiae Hook. f. 毛葉杜鵑
Bot. Mag. 77: t. 4609. 1851; FHK 200. 1861; FKH 155. 1912; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 72, pl. 9. 1983; W. R. Phillipson & M. N. Phillipson, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 44(1): 9. 1986; FRPS 57(2): 365, pl. 121: 5–10. 1994; FOC 14: 430. 2005.
Rhododendron subespitatum Chun ex P. C. Tam, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 2(4): 90, fig. 3. 1982.
Rhododendron championiae var. ovatifolium P. C. Tam., Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 73, 112. 1983.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1.5–3(–5) m tall, much branched. Young branches, petioles and pedicels densely covered with stiff, bristle-like glandular hairs up to 2.5 mm, hairs persistent on 2- or 3-year stem. Leaves crowded towards apex of branches; petiole 0.7–1.7 cm; leaf blade papery, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 6.2–12.5(–17) × (1.6–)2.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, fringed with bristle-like hairs, adaxial surface dark green, more or less bullate, abaxial surface rather rusty-colored, both surfaces initially clothed with glandular hairs; reticulation of veins prominent. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1–3(–5) per stem, up to 5 × 2 cm; scales ovate to elliptical, up to 4.0 × 1.7 cm, apex acute, adaxial side often with sticky secretion, abaxial side weakly pubescent, margin ciliated. Inflorescence umbellate, 2–5(–7)-flowered. Pedicels 1–2.2 cm. Calyx 4 –5-lobed; lobes triangular to triangular-lanceolate, 1–5 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute to obtuse, margin densely fringed with long hairs. Corolla funnel-shaped, 6–12 cm in diam., 4–6 cm deep, white to very pale pink, with yellow dots on posterior lobes; lobes spreading, elliptic to ovate; limb 6–12 cm in diam. Stamens 10, 4–4.5 cm, exserted; filaments pubescent on the lower half. Ovary oblong, 5–6-locular, densely hairy; style ca. 5 cm, protruding out of the corolla, glabrous. Capsule cylindrical, straight to strongly falcate, (1–)3–6 × 0.5–0.8 mm, covered with long hairs. Seeds many, elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 0.8 mm, with winged appendages on both ends.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island (Tai O). H. C. Tang 1715; P. S. Choi 389; S. C. Ng 98 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Locally restricted in distribution, usually on exposed open hillsides. Large populations can be found on hillfire-maintained hillslopes near Tai O, alt. 50–500 m. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental (garden plants), medicinal (roots and stems).
Notes: This species was first described from Victoria Peak based on the type specimen collected by J. G. Champion in 1849 and was named after his wife. A distinctive species characterized by large flowers and long stiff hairs on all parts of the plants except the petals, otherwise it is morphologically similar to R. moulmainense, with the largest and the most fragrant flowers, often having a strong sweet scent, among the six native rhododendrons. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Rhododendron farrerae Tate 華麗杜鵑
Brit. Fl. Garden ser. 2, 1: t. 95. 1831; FKH 155. 1912; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 28. 1983; D. F. Chamberlain & Rae, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 47(2): 145. 1990; FRPS 57(2): 371. 1994; FOC 14: 433. 2005.
Azalea squamata Lindl., J. Hort. Soc. Lond. 1: 152. 1846 & Bot. Reg. t. 3. 1847; FHK 201. 1861.

Shrub, semi-deciduous, 1–1.5(–3) m tall, with false-verticillate branches. Young branches, leaves, petioles, pedicels and calyx densely clothed with tawny hairs up to 2 mm long. Leaves often crowded towards apex of branches to almost pseudo-verticillate; petiole 2.0–5.2 mm; leaf blade thick papery, ovate to rarely elliptic or obovate, 1.2–6.2 × 0.7–2.7 cm, base rounded to truncate, apex acute or obtuse, with a blunt point, margin entire, fringed with golden to dark brown hairs when young; adult leaves glabrous on both surfaces or with dark brown pilose hairs remaining along veins on abaxial side; reticulation of veins prominent. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–2) per stem, up to 9 × 5 mm; scales persistent until flower wilted, broad triangular to oblong-ovate, up to 5 × 8 mm, apex obtuse, abaxially covered in sericeous hairs, especially towards apex. Flowers usually solitary, rarely in pairs. Pedicels 2–5 mm, covered in tawny pilose hairs. Calyx small and inconspicuous; lobes broad triangular, 0.5 × 1.0 mm. Corolla funnel-shaped, 1.5–2.0 cm in diam., 2.5–3.5 cm deep; purplish pink, pink to pale pink, with magenta dots on posterior lobes; lobes round to elliptic-ovate. Stamens 8–10, 2.0–2.5 cm; filaments, glandular pubescent on lower portion. Ovary ovoid, 5-locular, ca. 3.5 × 1.8 mm, 5-locular, densely tawny pilose. Capsule ovoid, 5-celled, 6–10 × 5– 6 mm, densely strigose when young, stalk erect. Seeds many, ellipsoidal to barely crescent-shaped, ca. 1–1.5 × 0.4–0.6 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok, Castle Peak, Pok To Yan, Tai O. W. J. Tutcher 8263, 11676; H. C. Tang 81.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Locally common, especially in hillfire-maintained shrublands and grasslands on ridges and cliffs, alt. 100–900 m. Flowering: Nov.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct. Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was first described from Hong Kong in 1846 as Azalea squamata, which is now considered one of the many synonyms of R. farrerae. It is distinctive among the six native rhododendrons in having deciduous flowering individuals and its leafless period usually coincides with flowering. Non-flowering individuals, however, often retain their older leaves until young leaves fully expand.

Rhododendron hongkongense Hutch. 香港杜鵑

Sp. Rhodod. 562. 1930; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 71. 1983; W. R. Phillipson & M. N. Phillipson, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 44(1): 5–6. 1986; FRPS 57(2): 345. 1994; FOC 14: 424. 2005.

Azalea myrtifolia Champ., Bot. Mag. 77, sub pl. 4609. 1851, non Rhododendron myrtifolium Lodd. (1824), nec Schott & Kotschy (1851).

Azalea ovata auct. non Lindl.: FHK 201. 1861.

Rhododendron ovatum auct. non Maxim.: FKH 155. 1913.


Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1–3(–7) m tall, much branched. Branchlets short glandular hairy when young. Leaves crowded towards apex of branches; petioles 0.5–1.4 cm, puberulent; leaf blade thin leathery to papery, rhombic-elliptic to oblanceolate, 3.2–7.6 × 1.4–3.0 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to retuse, with a blunt point, margin entire and slightly deflexed, glabrous on both surfaces, but pubescent along midvein. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1–2(–6) per stem, ca. 1.6 × 0.5 cm; scales ovate to elliptical, up to 1.5 × 0.9 cm, apex acute to round, with a sharp to blunt point, abaxially pubescent to rarely glabrous, margin ciliated. Inflorescence umbellate, 1(–2)-flowered. Pedicel 0.7–1.4 cm, glandular hairy. Calyx 5-lobed, glandular hairy at base; lobes ovate to broad elliptic, 3–5 × 3–4.5 mm, apex rounded, margin densely to sparsely glandular ciliate. Corolla sub-rotate, spreading with a shallow tube, 4.5–6 cm in diam., 1.5–2.0 cm deep, white to very pale pink or very pale magenta, rarely very pale green, with magenta (rarely green) dots on posterior lobes; tube very short ; limb 4.5–6 cm in diam. Stamens 5, filaments 2.0–2.5 cm, pubescent below middle. Ovary subglobose to broad ovoid, ca. 1.8 × 2.0 mm, densely glandular hairy; style 2.5–3.2 cm, glabrous. Capsule subglobose to broad ovoid, 5-locular, ca. 5 × 5 mm, tuberculate and sparsely glandular hairy. Seeds many, ellipsoidal to ovoid, multi-faceted, ca. 1 × 0.4 mm.


Locality: Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Wong Lung Hang. H. C. Tang 493; Y. S. Lau 2684; Y. W. Lam 612; HK sheet 33103, 33104; S. C. Ng 85 (HKU).

Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi.

Ecology: Locally restricted in distribution. Populations could be found on rocky outcrops and steep hillside forests, or along streamsides, alt. 100–700 m. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Uses: Ornamental (garden plants).

Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. This species had been misidentified as “Azalea ovata” and “Rhododendron ovatum” in FHK and FKH respectively. Rhododendron hongkongense is morphologically very similar to R. ovatum and R. bachii H. Léveillé, both of which are widespread in S China and recorded in Guangdong and Jiangxi where R. hongkongense was also found. Differs from R. hongkongense, R. ovatum lacks glandular hairs on calyx margin whereas R. bachii bears ovate leaves and calyx lobes. Despite both R. ovatum and R. bachii showed variable flower colour ranging from purple to light pink, R. hongkongense is consistently paler and usually white. These characters are, however, variable within respective species. Specimens of R. hongkongense collected in Hong Kong showed that glandular hairs on sepal margin vary continuously from filling the whole length of the margin (e.g. Y. W. Lam 612 and HK sheet 33103) to complete absence or replacement by cilia (e.g. Y. S. Lau 2684 and HK sheet 33104). Further studies are, therefore, needed to ascertain the taxonomic status of R. hongkongense. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Rhododendron moulmainense Hook. f. 羊角杜鵑
Bot. Mag. 82: t. 4909. 1856; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 78. 1983; W. R. Phillipson & M. N. Phillipson, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 44(1): 13–14, pro parte. 1986; FRPS 57(2): 355, pl. 118: 1–5. 1994; FOC 14: 427. 2005.
Rhododendron westlandii Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 31–32. 1889; FKH 155. 1913.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 2–4(–10) m tall, much branched, glabrous throughout except filaments and rarely young leaf margin. Leaves crowded towards nodes of branches; petiole 1.0–1.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thick-papery to leathery, elliptic, elliptic-obovate, (5–)6.6–10.5(–14) × (1.5–)2.5–5.2 cm, margin entire or rarely ciliated when young, flat to slightly deflexed, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly and abruptly acuminate; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; secondary and fine veins inconspicuous on both surfaces. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1–2(–5) per stem, up to 4 × 2 cm; scales ovate to elliptical, up to 3.0 × 2.5 cm, apex acute, abaxial side glabrous, margin ciliated. Inflorescence umbellate, (2–)3–5(–7)-flowered. Pedicels 1–1.7 cm. Calyx small; lobes broad triangular to broad ovate, 0.5–1 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse. Corolla funnel-shaped, 5–8 cm in diam., 3–4 cm deep, pink to pale pink lobes spreading, elliptic to elliptic-obovate. Stamens 10, 3.5–4 cm; filaments pubescent on the lower part. Ovary oblong, 5–6 mm, 5–6-locular; style 4–4.5 cm, protruding out of the corolla, glabrous. Capsule cylindrical, straight to strongly falcate, (2–)4–6 × 0.4–0.7 cm. Seeds many, ellipsoidal, 2.5–3.0 × 0.5–1.0 mm, with winged appendages on both ends.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Peak. A. B. Westland 1697; W. J. Tutcher 10609; H. C. Tang 492; S. C. Ng 88 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Yunnan; Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia (Peninsular), Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Locally restricted to steep hillside forests, alt. 300–900 m. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species is morphologically variable throughout its range from S China to Indochina. It was described under various names [see FRPS and Phillipson & Phillipson (1986)], including R. westlandii, the type specimen of which was collected from Lantau Island by A. B. Westland in 1886. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
