Rhododendron mucronatum (Bl.) G. Don 白杜鵑
Gen. Syst. 3: 846. 1834; Sleumer, Fl. Males. Ser. I, 6(4): 662. 1967; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 39. 1983; D. F. Chamberlain & Rae, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 47(2): 116–117. 1990; FRPS 57(2): 389, pl. 125: 1–5. 1994; FOC 14: 441. 2005.
Azalea mucronata Bl., Cat. Gewass. Buitenz. 44. 1823.

Shrub, evergreen, 1–2(–3) m tall, much branched. Young branches, petioles and pedicels densely covered with ± appressed long narrow triangular flat scale-like hairs and intermixed with glandular hairs and harsh hairs. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, often crowded towards nodes of branches; petiole ca. 2 mm; leaf blade papery, elliptic, oblong lanceolate to oblong-obovate, deflexed, 1.5–4.7 × 0.7–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute and a blunt point, margin entire, fringed with long hairs, adaxial surface sparsely strigose, abaxial surface strigose and intermixed with short glandular hairs. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–several) per stem; scale of flower buds ovate to elliptic, 4–7 × 4–5 mm, apex obtuse, abaxially pilose and often with sticky secretion. Inflorescence umbellate, 1–2(–3)-flowered, with sticky secretion. Pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx 5-lobed, glandular hairy at base; lobes 5, ovate to lanceolate, 6–8 × 2.5–3 mm, apex rounded to acute, margin glandular hairy. Corolla funnel-shaped, 3–5 cm in diam., 3–4 cm deep, white; lobes elliptic to broad obovate. Stamens 10; filaments glabrous to puberulent below middle. Ovary ovoid, 5-locular, densely strigose, style glabrous, 3–5 cm. Capsule not seen.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1455.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China, Japan and introduced to Europe and America, but no wild population has been found.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was probably originated from R. mucronatum var. ripense (Makino) Wilson which is native to Japan (Chamberlain & Rae, 1990).

Rhododendron pulchrum Sweet 錦繡杜鵑
Brit. Fl. Garden ser. 2, 2: t. 117. 1832; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 41, pl. 2. 1983; D. F. Chamberlain & Rae, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 47(2): 141. 1990; FRPS 57(2): 384. 1994.

Shrub, evergreen, 1–2(–3) m tall. Young branches, petioles, leaf blade, pedicels and calyx covered with ± appressed, harsh long hairs and intermixed with short glandular hairs. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, often crowded towards nodes of branches; petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade papery, elliptic to oblong-obovate or elliptic-lanceolate, 2.7– 6.1 × 0.9 –2.1 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, with a blunt point, margin entire and slightly deflexed, fringed with long hairs, glabrescent adaxially when full-grown. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–several) per stem; scales elliptic to ovate, 7–18 × 6–12 mm, apex acute to short acuminate, basal scales occasionally with leafy extension at apex; abaxially shortly pubescent and glandular papillate. Inflorescence umbellate, 2–4(–5)-flowered. Pedicel 7–10 mm. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes ovate to lanceolate, 7–12 × 3–4 mm, covered in long hairs and shorter glandular hairs, apex rounded to acuminate, margin long hairy. Corolla funnel-shaped, 4–4.5 cm diam., 3–3.5 cm deep, pink to purple, with bright pink to dark purple dots on posterior lobes, 4 –7 cm in diam.; lobes elliptic to obovate. Stamens 10; filaments sparsely puberulent on the lower portion. Ovary ovoid, densely tawny strigose, style 3.5–5.0 cm, glabrous. Capsule not seen.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1453, 2467.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China and worldwide, but no wild population has been found.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental (garden plants).
Notes: A putative hybrid of unknown parentage (Chamberlain & Rae, 1990), this species has long been cultivated in China and worldwide. A number of cultivars of different flower colour and slightly different vegetative morphology are available and at least two cultivars are present in Hong Kong.

Rhododendron simiarum Hance 南華杜鵑
J. Bot. 22(1): 22–23. 1884; FKH 155. 1913; D. F. Chamberlain, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 39: 320, 1982; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 20, pl. II, 1983; FRPS 57(2): 157, pl. 48: 6 –10. 1994; FOC 14: 371. 2005.
Rhododendron fordii Hemsl., Kew Bull. Misc. Inform. 1894(85): 5. 1894; FKH 155. 1913.
Rhododendron fokiense Franch., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 46: 210. 1899; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 21, fig. 19. 1983.

Erect shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1–3(–5) m tall. Branchlets glabrescent. Leaves clustered towards stem apex; thick-leathery; petiole 1.2–2.5 cm, ± pubescent; leaf blade obovate, elliptic-obovate to elliptic, (3.2–)5.4 –9.5 × (1.0–)1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex subrounded, sometimes retuse, margin entire and usually strongly deflexed, glabrous and shiny adaxially, abaxial surface initially covered with grey or light tawny tangled hairs, forming a thin but compact and persistent light brown indumentum; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous, reticulation of veins ± foveolate. Flower buds usually borne singly to very rarely in pair at stem apex, ca. 3.5 × 2.7 cm; scale fall off as flower opened, broad ovate to elliptical, up to 3.5 × 2.7 cm, apex obtuse to round, abaxially glabrous to sparsely pubescent, especially towards the apex and along the longitudinal axis, often with sticky secretion. Inflorescence an umbel-like raceme, 3–7- flowered; rachis 1–2.5 cm, glandular hairy. Pedicels 2.2–3.4 cm, glandular hairy. Calyx small, cup-shaped, inconspicuously 5-lobed, lobes round to broad triangular, 0.5–0.7 mm × 1.5–2.0 mm, apex round, glandular hairy. Corolla oblique-campanulate, 3.5–4.5 cm, pink to rosy red initially, soon turning white to pink, with yellow to pink dots on posterior petals, lobes round to broadly elliptic-ovate, 1.7–2.5 cm × 1.5–1.7 cm. Stamens 10–12, 3–4 cm, similar to or shorter than corolla; pubescent on the 1/3 section. Ovary covered with stellate hairs, sticky when fresh; style 3–5 cm, glandular hairy at lower half. Capsule ellipsoid to oblong-ellipsoidal, 1–3 × 0.5–1.2 cm, glabrous and often with sticky secretion. Seeds many, ellipsoidal to ovoid, 2–2.5 × 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak. U. A. On s.n. (HK sheet 16955); C. Ford s.n. (HK Sheet 16954); Y. S. Lau 936; S. C. Ng 93 (HKU).
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Hunan, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang.
Ecology: Locally restricted in distribution, specialized in shrubland habitats on rocky outcrops or cliffs and often in small rock crevices and surface, abundant and form dense populations wherever occur. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species shows considerable variation within its range. The specimens from outside Guangdong and Hong Kong often have glabrous stamens and acute leaf apexes (Chamberlain, 1982; M.Y. Fang 1994). The species is widespread in S China mainly on ridges and cliffs above 1000 m. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Rhododendron simsii Planch. 紅杜鵑
Fl. des Serres 9: 78. 1854; Sleumer, Fl. Males. Ser. I, 6(4): 665. 1967; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 28, pl. 1. 1983; FRPS 57(2): 386, pl. 124: 1–6. 1994; FOC 14: 440. 2005.
Azalea indica auct. non L.: Sims, Bot. Mag. 35: t. 1480. 1812; FHK 201. 1861.
Rhododendron indicum auct. non Sweet: FKH 155. 1912.

Ascending shrub, usually evergreen, 1–2(–3) m tall, much-branched. Branchlets, petioles, pedicels, calyx and ovary densely strigose with stiff appressed light brown triangular flat scale-like hairs. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, often crowded towards nodes of branches; petiole 1.0–3.0 mm; leaf blade thick papery, elliptic to obovate, 1.5–5.5 × 1.0–2.2 cm, margin entire and flat, base cuneate, apex acute, obtuse, to round, with a blunt point, strigose on both surfaces, often becoming glabrous adaxially, but always retaining the hairs on abaxial surface, especially towards leaf base. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–several) per stem; scales ovate, 7–10 × 4–8 mm, apex acute to obtuse, basal scales occasionally with leafy extension at apex; abaxially covered in strigose hairs, especially towards apex and axis. Inflorescence 1–2(–3)-flowered. Pedicels 4–6 mm. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes elliptic ovate to triangular ovate, 2–2.6 × 3–4.7 mm, apex round, rarely acute, margin entire, fringed with narrow triangular scale-like hairs. Corolla funnel-shaped, 3.5–4.5 cm in diam., 3–3.5 cm deep, bright red, with dark red dots on posterior lobes; lobes elliptic to obovate. Stamens 10, 2.7–4.7 cm; filaments inclusive, sparsely pubescent below middle. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3.0 × 1.7 mm, 5-locular, densely strigose; style glabrous. Capsule ovoid to rarely ellipsoid, 7–9 × 3–5 mm, strigose. Seeds many, elliptic, 1.2–1.5 × 0.3–0.4 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Collinson, Kowloon Peak and Lion Rock, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sharp Island, Castle Peak, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung Peninsula, Lantau. H. C. Tang 1267; L. T. Lo 423.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Japan, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Common in secondary shrubland on hillsides and along streams, alt. 50–980 m. Flowering: Dec.–May; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Rhododendron simsii was first described by Sims in 1812 who mistook it as Azalea indica. It was not properly identified until 1854 by Planchon. As a result, this species was often mentioned as “R. indicum” or “A. indica” in 19th century literature as well as FHK and FKH. This wide-ranging species is probably the most common wild rhododendron in S China and also one of the most widely cultivated rhododendrons in E Asia.

Rhodoleia championii Hook. f. 紅花荷（紅苞木、吊鐘王）
Bot. Mag. 76: t. 4509. 1850; FHK 131. 1861; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 46, pl. 9. 1979; FGD 1: 155, fig. 171. 1987; FOC 9: 24. 2003.
Rhodoleia latiovatifolia G. A. Fu, Guihaia 11(3): 208 –209. 1991.

Tree, to 12 m tall; young branches glabrous. Petioles 3 –5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 7–13 × 4.5 – 6.5 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or subacute, green and shining adaxially, whitish grey abaxially; obscurely 3-veined at base, lateral veins 7–9 pairs, conspicuous on both surfaces, reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Inflorescences 3 – 4 cm, pendulous; peduncle 2–3 cm, with 5–6 scale-like bracts; involucral bracts many, ovate, brown-pubescent; bracteoles 5 or 6, scale-like. Petals spathulate, 2.5 –3.5(– 4) × 0.4 – 0.8 cm. Stamens as long as petals. Ovary glabrous; styles shorter than stamens. Infructescence ca. 3 cm wide, with 5 capsules. Capsule ovoid-globose, ca. 1.2–1.5 cm, without persistent styles.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Aberdeen. H. C. Tang 865; HK sheet 1707.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indonesia (Sumatra), W Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Little Hong Kong, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in 1849. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Rhodomyrtus tomentosa (Aiton) Hassk. 桃金娘（崗棯）

Flora 25(Beibl.): 35. 1842; FHK 121. 1861; FKH 104. 1912; FGZ 201. 1956; FHN 2: 7, fig. 291. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 121, pl. 32: 1– 2. 1984; FFJ 4: 95, fig. 80. 1989; FGX 1: 914. 1991; FGD 3: 173, fig. 123. 1995; FYN 7: 129, fig. 36: 3 – 4. 1997; FOC 13: 331. 2007.

Myrtus tomentosa Aiton, Hort. Kew. 2: 159. 1789.

Myrtus canescens Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 311. 1790.


Shrub, 1–2 m tall. Young branchlets greyish pubescent. Petioles 4–7 mm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic to obovate, 3–8 × 1–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex rounded to obtuse, often slightly emarginate, pubescent at first, glabrescent adaxially, grey tomentose abaxially; reticulate veins conspicuous. Flowers long-pedicellate, often solitary, purplish red, 2 – 4 cm in diam. Hypanthium obovoid, ca. 6 mm, grey tomentose. Calyx-lobes 5, suborbicular, 4–5 mm, persistent. Petals 5, obovate, 1.3 – 2 cm. Stamens red, 7 – 8 mm. Ovary inferior, 3-locular. Style ca. 1 cm. Berry purplish black when mature, urceolate, 1.5–2 × 1 – 1.5 cm.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 142; K. L. Yip 4189, 4402.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Malaysia, Indonesia.

Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Late summer to early autumn.

Uses: Edible (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Rhus chinensis Mill. 鹽膚木
Gard. Dict. (ed. 8) 7. 1768; FHN 3: 109. 1947; FYN 2: 388. 1979; FRPS 45(1): 100. 1980; FFJ 3: 243. 1987; FGD 2: 315. 1991.
Rhus chinensis var. roxburghii (DC.) Rehder, J. Arnold Arb. 20: 416. 1929.
Rhus semialata Murray, Comm. Doc. Goetting. 6: 27, t. 23. 1784; FKH 69. 1912.
Rhus semialata var. roxburghii DC., Prodr. 2: 67. 1825.

Shrub or tree, 2–10 m tall. Bark greyish brown; branchlets, petioles and inflorescences densly rusty pubescent. Leaves 25–45 cm, including the petiole, rachis winged or not; leaflets 7–13, shortly petiolulate; blade ovate to oblong, 5–12 × 2–4 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, slightly oblique, apex acuminate to acute, margin coarsely serrate, adaxially rusty pubescent on midvein, abaxially glaucous and greyish tomentose; lateral veins and reticulate venation impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially. Inflorescence 20–30 cm; peduncles short, robust; pedicels ca. 1 mm. Calyx minutely pubescent; lobes ovate, ca. 0.5 mm. Petals white, oblong, ca. 2 mm. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1 mm, densely white-villous. Drupe red, globose, slightly compressed, 4–5 mm in diam., glandular-pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2216; Y. S. Lau 843, 2300.
Distribution: S, E, C & SW China; SE to E Asia.
Ecology: Thickets or thin forests. Flowering: Late summer; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Tannin, dye stuff, medicinal (folklore).

Rhus hypoleuca Champ. ex Benth. 白背鹽膚木（白背漆）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 43. 1852; FHK 69. 1861; FKH 69. 1912; FTW 3: 569. 1977; FRPS 45(1): 103. 1980; FFJ 3: 244, fig. 165. 1987; FGD 2: 315, fig. 207. 1991.

Shrub or small tree, 1.5–5 m tall; branchlets minutely greyish pubescent to glabrous, with brownish red orbicular lenticels. Leaves 20–25 cm including the petiole; rachis not winged; leaflets 9–17, shortly petiolulate or sessile; blade ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 5–9.5 × 2–3.5 cm, base oblique, apex acuminate to caudate, margin entire to sparsely serrate, slightly revolute, grey tomentose along midvein adaxially, densely white tomentose abaxially; lateral veins dense, 15–20 on each side of midvein, midvein and lateral veins slightly impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially. Inflorescence to 20 cm, greyish yellow tomentose; peduncles very short; pedicels 1–2 mm, greyish yellow tomentose. Calyx lobes 0.5 mm, minutely pubescent. Petals white, obovate-oblong, ca. 2 mm. Ovary globose, densely white hairy. Drupe ca. 4 mm in diam., red glandular-pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2051; HK sheet 1221, 6372.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Rhus succedanea L. 木蠟樹（野漆樹）
Mant. Pl. 2: 221. 1771; FHK 69. 1861; FKH 69. 1912; FGZ 447. 1956; FHN 3: 108, fig. 605. 1974; FTW 3: 570, pl. 732. 1977; FGD 2: 315. 1991.
Toxicodendron succedaneum (L.) O. Kuntze, Rev. Gen. Pl. 154. 1891; FYN 2: 403. 1979; FRPS 45(1): 120. 1980; FFJ 3: 247, fig. 168. 1987.

Shrub or small tree, 2–5(–12) m tall, all parts glabrous. Branchlets stout, greyish white or greyish brown. Leaves ± clustered on apex of branch, 15–30 cm including the petiole; petioles 6–9 cm, not winged; leaflets 7–13, opposite, shortly petiolulate or sessile; blade papery, elliptic-oblong or ovate-lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base oblique, rounded, apex caudate, margin entire, shining adaxially, pale green or greyish green abaxially; lateral veins 15–20 on each side of midvein. Panicles axillary, 5–15 cm. Flowers small; pedicels short and slender. Calyx-lobes ovate, apex obtuse. Petals yellowish green, oblong, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Drupe oblique, compressed, ca. 6–8 mm wide, pericarp thin, separating, mesocarp thick, waxy, stone bony.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. Y. Chun 4804 (IBSC); C. L. Tso 20226 (IBSC); HK sheet 40015.
Distribution: Area S of Changjiang River; SE to E Asia.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Raw material for industry (pericarp, seed).

Rhynchosia volubilis Lour. 鹿藿
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 460. 1790; FHK 90. 1861; FKH 85. 1912; FRPS 41: 334. 1994; FGD 5: 342, fig. 187. 2003.

Slender herbaceous twiner, more or less villous or pubescent. Stems slightly angulate. Stipules lanceolate, 3 – 5 mm. Leaves pinnately or digitately 3-foliolate; leaflets papery, terminal one rhomboid or obovate-rhomboid, 3–8 × 3–5.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, often mucronate, grey or yellowish pubescent on both surfaces, especially dense and with yellow-brown glands on abaxial surface; basal veins 3; lateral leaflets smaller, usually oblique. Racemes 1–3, axillary, 1.5–4 cm. Flowers 1 cm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 5 mm, lobes lanceolate, pubescent and glandular abaxially. Corolla yellow; vexillum suborbicular, incurvedly auriculate; wings obovate-oblong, auriculate one side; keel rostrate. Stamens diadelphous. Pods red-purple, oblong, 1 – 1.5 × 0.8 cm, very flat, apex rostellate, slightly constricted between seeds, slightly pubescent or subglabrous. Seeds usually 2, black, elliptic or subreniform, shining.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 1056; L. T. Lo 395; Y. W. Lam 278.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy banks. Flowering: May –Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Dec.

Rhynchospora brownii Roem. & Schult. 皺果刺子莞
Syst. Veg. 2: 86. 1817; FRPS 11: 111. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 584. 1988; FYN 15: 617. 2003.
Rhynchospora rugosa (Vahl) Gale subsp. brownii (Roem. & Schultes) T. Koyama in Williams, Pl. Coll. Nepal 118. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 298. 2000; FOC 23: 254. 2010.
Rhynchospora rugosa auct. non (Vahl) Gale: FGD 8: 314. 2007; Check List HK Plants 319. 2002; 112. 2004.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms loosely tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 1–1.7 mm thick, trigonous, smooth to scabrid above. Leaves basal and 2–3 cauline; blade narrowly linear, up to 55 cm × 1.5–3 mm, gradually acute, flattish to canaliculate; basal sheath up 8 cm, greyish brown, cauline sheaths up to 5 cm, greenish. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence narrow, panicle-like, 10–30 cm, with 2–3(–4) distant nodes each subtending 1–3 pedunculate spikelet clusters, the clusters rarely with primary and secondary anthelas. Spikelets 2–40 per cluster, ovate-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, subterete, 3–4.5 mm. Glumes 5–7, ovate to broadly ovate, 1–3.5 mm long, acute, mucronate, sides thinly papery, dark brown. Perianth segments 6(–7), shorter or slightly longer than achene. Stamens (1–)2–3; anthers linear, 1–1.5 mm. Stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, biconvex, 1.5–1.8 × 1–1.5 mm, maturing light brown, weakly transversely winkled and lineolate with longitudinally oblong epidermal cells; style-base conical, ± as broad as achenes abruptly widening below.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Shing Mun, Castle Peak, Yung Shue O, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 2175; S. C. Ng 1359.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, Sichuan; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Marshes and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Rhynchospora chinensis Nees & Meyen 華刺子莞
Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 108. 1843; Linnaea 37: 586. 1873; FRPS 11: 111. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 297. 2000; FOC 23: 254. 2010.
Rhynchospora glauca Vahl var. chinensis (Nees & Meyen) C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 672. 1893.
Rhychospora glauca auct. non Vahl: FKH 302. 1912.
Rhychospora laxa auct. non R. Br.: FHK 397. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome very short. Culms loosely to densely tufted (30–)50–140 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, smooth or scabrid above. Leaves basal and 2–4 cauline, blade linear, 10–60 cm × 3–5 mm, long-acuminate, flattish to plicate; basal sheaths yellowish brown to mid-brown, cauline sheaths greenish. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest up to 13 cm. Inflorescence narrow, panicle-like, 20–40 cm, with 3–5(–6) nodes each subtending 1–3 pedunculate spikelet clusters. Spikelets up to 15 per cluster, ovate-lanceolate, 6–8 × 1.5–2.5 mm. Glumes 5–8, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1–5 cm, acute to mucronate, sides membranous, midbrown to rusty brown. Perianth segments 6, longer than achene. Stamens 2(–3); anthers 2–2.5 mm. Stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, compressed, 1.9–2.5 × 1.5–1.8 mm, slightly shiny, yellowish to mid-brown, weakly transversely winkled and lineolate; style base conical, gradually widening below.

Locality: Aberdeen, Stanley Rd., Tai Tam Reservoir, Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. S. C. Ng 1337; HK sheet 13768.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hainan, Hubei, Zhejiang, Shandong, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Vietnam, Indonesia, Madagascar.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Rhynchospora corymbosa (L.) Britton 傘房刺子莞
Trans. New York Acad. Sci. 11: 84. 1892; FRPS 11: 110. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 297. 2002; FYN 15: 618. 2003; FGD 8: 314. 2007; FOC 23: 253. 2010.
Scirpus corymbosus L., Cent. Pl. II 7. 1756.
Rhynchospora aurea Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 229. 1805; FHK 396. 1861; FKH 302. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1– few, 80–120(–150) cm tall, 3–10 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth to scabrid above. Leaves basal and 2–3 cauline; blade narrowly linear, 20–70 cm × 0.8–1.6 mm, long-acuminate, flattish, glabrous; basal sheaths up to 20 cm, pale brown, cauline sheaths 5–8 mm, greenish. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest 10–30 cm. Inflorescence panicle-like, open, 20–40 cm, comprising 2–5 rather distant partial inflorescence, the terminal one corymb-like, 10–15 × 10–15 cm, simple to compound, with primary anthelas (8–)12– many, up to 12 cm. Spikelets in clusters of 2–10, lanceolate or elliptic, subterete, 6–9 mm. Glumes 5–7, sub-distichous, ovate to oblong-ovate, 2.5–6 mm, acute to mucronulate, sides membranous, reddish brown. Perianth segments in bisexual flower 6, ± equalling achene. Stamens 3; anthers 2–3 mm long. Styles ca. 2 mm, stigma 2 or sometimes undivided, very short. Achenes obdeltoid-obovate, compressed, 2.5–3.5 × 2 mm, apex without short neck, glabrous, dull yellowish brown to mid-brown, finely transversely winkled to rugose, style base elongate-conical, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Kau Sai Chau, Sha Lo Tung, Wu Kau Tang. K. L. Yip 4041; J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 333; Y. W. Lam 1849.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Farmlands and river banks. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Rhynchospora gracillima Thwaites 柔弱刺子莞
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 435. 1864; FKH 302. 1912; FGD 8: 315. 2007 [“gracilima”]; FOC 23: 255. 2010.

Annual or short-lived perennial; rhizome very short. Culms densely tufted, 20–60 cm tall, 0.2–0.5 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade setaceous, up to 30 × 0.5–1.3 mm, subacute, canaliculated; sheath 1–4 cm, light green to light brown. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest 2–4 cm. Inflorescence 8–20 cm, with 1–3 nodes each with 1 open partial inflorescence; terminal partial inflorescence up to 4 cm, with primary and secondary anthelas; primary anthelas 3–5, up to 4 cm. Spikelets up to 7 per partial inflorescence, solitary, lanceolate, 5–7 × 1.5–2 mm. Glumes 6–7(–8), ovate to broadly ovate, 2–4 cm, subacute to mucronulate, sides membranous, light rusty brown. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 2–3; anthers linear, 1.5–2 mm long. Stigmas 2. Achenes obovoid, compressed, 1.2–1.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, light grey, undulate-rugose with 6–8 ridges; style base depressed-conical, much wider than long.

Locality: Ho Pui Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1488; S. C. Ng 2032.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian; Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, tropical Africa, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Rhynchospora malasica C. B. Clarke 馬來刺子莞（日本刺子莞）
Fl. Brit. India 6: 670. 1893; FTW ed. 2, 5: 298. 2000; FGD 8: 316. 2007; FOC 23: 255. 2010.
Rhynchospora nipponica Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 18: 145. 1904; FRPS 11: 114. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome long creeping. Sterile shoots elongate to 80 cm, bearing a dense leaf fascicle at distal end. Culms 60 – 100 cm tall, simple, erect, several-nodose, obtusely triquetrous below, regularly triquetrous with acute edges above, surrounded at base with dusky brown sub-aphyllous sheaths, sub-densely leaved on midway portion. Leaves broadly linear, overtopping culm, flattish, 40–60 cm × 5–9 mm, fresh green, gradually tapering above to acute apex, scabrid abaxially and margin; sheath elongate, tightly surrounding culm; ligule short, membranous, rusty brown. Inflorescence 5–20 cm, spicately bearing 2–7 heads, sub-contiguous above, interrupted toward base; bracts not sheathing at base, lower ones with elongate blade 7–20 cm. Inflorescence spicate or racemose, with 2–7 spicate heads; heads sessile, globose, 10–15 mm across, densely many-spiculose, greyish stramineous and tinged with red-brown. Spikelets lanceolateovate to lanceolate, 6–7 mm, weakly laterally compressed, contracted at base, gradually tapering above to acuminate apex, 1-flowered, 1-fruited; glumes 5–6, lower 3–4 ovate, much smaller than lanceolate-ovate upper 2, all 1-veined, acute, membranous, greyish brown. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Stigmas 2, style filiform, 2 mm. Perianth segments 6, filiform, flexuose, smooth, 3.5–4.5 mm. Achenes broadly obovate, 2–2.5 mm, thickly biconvexed with obtuse edges, faintly transversely wrinkled, dark brown; style base narrowly conicalsubulate, 4–4.5 mm, somewhat constricted at base, gradually attenuate from above base to slender style.

Locality: Tai Tam Reservoir. S. T. Chan 590.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Thailand, Indonesia, Malesia.
Ecology: Marshes and swamps. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Rhynchospora rubra (Lour.) Makino 刺子莞
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 17: 180. 1903; FRPS 11: 113. 1961; FGZ 8: 584. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 298. 2002; FYN 15: 619. 2003; FGD 8: 315. 2007; FOC 23: 255. 2010.
Schoenus ruber Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 41. 1790.
Rhychospora wallichiana Kunth, Enum. Pl. 289. 1837; FHK 396. 1861; FKH 302. 1912.

Annual or short-lived perennial; rhizome very short or absent. Culms tufted, 20–70(–100) cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, shorter than culms, up to 42 cm × 2–4 mm, subacute, flattish to folded or canaliculate; sheath 1–7 cm, yellowish brown. Involucral bracts 4–8, leaf-like, eventually reflexed, the longest up to 8 cm, base dilated, margins ciliate. Inflorescence with one terminal head; head subglobose to globose, 1.0–1.7 cm in diam. Spikelets many, ovate-lanceolate, somewhat flattened, 6–8 × 1.5–2 mm, 2–3-flowered. Glumes 6–8, ovate to lanceolate, up to 6.5 mm, acute, sides thinly papery, pale to mid-brown, lower ones sterile. Stamens (2–)3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Perianth segments 3–6, unequal, up to half the length of achene. Style filiform, stigmas 2 or sometimes undivided. Achenes obovate to broadly obovate, bilaterally compressed, 1.3– 1.8 × 1–1.5 mm, scabrid-hispid along margins, maturing somewhat shiny mid-brown, smooth to indistinctly minutely papillose; style base depressed-conical, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2505; H. C. Tang 2256; Y. W. Lam 713.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; tropical regions of Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Roadsides, grasslands and open areas. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Rhynchotechum ellipticum (Wall. ex D. Dietr.) A. DC. 線柱苣苔
Prodr. 9: 285. 1845; FKH 192. 1912; FRPS 69: 558. 1990; FOC 18: 394. 1998; FGD 6: 287, pl. 158. 2005.
Corysanthera elliptica Wall. ex D. Dietr., Syn. Pl. 3: 582. 1843
Rhynchotechum formosanum Hatus., J. Jap. Bot. 15: 132. 1939; FRPS 69: 559. 1990; FOC 18: 394. 1998; Check List HK Plants 251. 2002; 86. 2004.

Subshrubs, 0.5–2 m tall, apically densely depressed rust‑brown woolly. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–4 cm, densely appressed rust‑brown woolly; leaf blade elliptic to obovate, 6.5–v32 × 2.5–10 cm, base cuneate to attenuate, apex abruptly acuminate to acute, margin denticulate, adaxially rust‑brown to brown woolly, glabrescent, abaxially densely rust‑brown woolly, glabrescent except along veins, lateral veins 13–26 pairs, almost parallel. Cymes 5– 30‑flowered; peduncle 2.5–3.5 cm, densely appressed rust‑brown villous; bracts narrowly lanceolate, 5–10 mm; pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx 5‑sect from base; segments lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, abaxially rust‑brown villous, adaxially glabrous. Corolla white or pink, 4–5 mm, glabrous; tube ca. 2 mm; adaxial lip ca. 2 mm; abaxial lip ca. 2 mm, ovate, apex rounded. Stamens 4, adnate to corolla base, glabrous; filament 5–8 mm; anthers spherical, ca. 1 mm; staminode 1, 0.2–0.3 mm. Pistil glabrous; ovary conical, ca. 1 mm; style ca. 4 mm; stigma 1. Berry white, 5–6 mm, widely spherical.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Fung Yuen, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 1753; F. W. Xing 7008; HK sheet 31562.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, India, Bhutan, Nepal.
Ecology: Dense forests, shaded streamsides, rocky areas in valleys. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Oct–Feb. of the following year.

Richardia scabra L. 墨苜蓿
Sp. Pl. 1: 330. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 4: 321. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 203, pl. 48: 1 – 7. 1999; FGD 6: 242, fig. 131. 2005.
Richardia brasiliensis auct. non Gomes: Z. X. Li & F. W. Xing, Guihaia 9(1): 35. 1989.

Annual herbs. Stems creeping or ascending, to 80 cm or longer, sparsely hirsute. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 5 – 10 mm; stipules united with petioles into a sheath, apex truncate, fringed with 2–5 bristle‑like lobes; leaf blade ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, 1–5 × 0.5–3.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, tip blunt, margin ciliate, scabrous on both surfaces. Flowers in terminal sessile heads, subtended by 1 or 2 pairs of broadly ovate bracts. Calyx 2.5–3.5 mm; tube constricted at apex; lobes usually 6, lanceolate, about the length of the tube, ciliate. Corolla white, funnel‑shaped; tube 2 – 8 mm, with a ring of white long hairs near the base inside; lobes pubescent abaxially. Ovary usually 3‑locular; style 3‑branched, the branches bilobed again; stigma capitate. Capsule oblong to obovoid, 3‑furrowed, 2–3.5 mm high, densely and minutely strigose.

Locality: Naturalized. L. T. Lo 67; Y. S. Lau 1825; Y. W. Lam 1157.
Distribution: Naturalized in Hainan, S Guangdong, Taiwan, Xisha Islands; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Ricinus communis L. 蓖麻

Sp. Pl. 1007. 1753; FHK 307. 1861; FKH 240. 1912; FRPS 44(2): 88. 1996; FGD 5: 92, fig. 53. 2003.


Shrub up to 5 m tall (annual herb of 1.5–2 m in cold places), glabrous and glaucous throughout. Leaves alternate; petioles 3.5–50 cm, fistulose; stipules narrowly triangular, 2–3 cm, caducous; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, 10–65 × 10–75 cm, palmately 7–11-lobed, lobes broadly lanceolate, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate. Racemes or panicles terminal, 15–30 cm, sometimes becoming leaf-opposed by the development of a terminal shoot. Male flowers: calyx-lobes ovate-triangular, 6–10 mm; staminal fascicles many. Female flowers: calyx-lobes ovate-lanceolate, 5 – 8 mm, deciduous; ovary ovoid, ca. 5 mm in diam., densely and softly echinate or spineless; styles red, ca. 4 mm, apex 2-cleft and densely papillose. Capsules ovoid or subglobose, 1.5–2.5 cm, softly echinate or tuberculate; seeds ellipsoidal, slightly depressed, 8–18 mm, glabrous, variously marked and colored.


Locality: Cultivated & naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2146, 2360; S. Y. Hu 6770, 9510 (CUHK).

Distribution: Cultivated and naturalized throughout tropics and subtropics, probable origin Africa.

Ecology: Wastelands or in gardens. Flowering: Jun. – Sep.; fruiting: Oct. – Dec.

Uses: Material (lipids), host (silkworms), medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Notes: A cultivar (Ricinus communis L. 'Sanguineus' 紅蓖麻) with red stems and leaves is also cultivated in Hong Kong.

records.text:
Robiquetia succisa (Lindl.) Seidenf. & Garay 寄樹蘭（小葉寄樹蘭）
Bot. Tisskr. 67: 119. 1972; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 116, fig. 68. 1977; FRPS 19: 368, pl. 55: 1–2. 1999; FGD 7: 484. 2006; FOC 25: 476. 2009.
Sarcanthus succisus Lindl., Bot. Reg. 12: t. 1014. 1826.

Epiphytic herb; roots cord-like, shiny grey, turning to olive green when old; stems monopodial. Leaves distichous, petiolate; petioles sheathing, green; leaf blades leathery, linear-oblong, 5–10 × 1.5–2.3 cm, midrib shallowly impressed above, evident beneath, base truncate, apex erose, emarginate, truncate and apiculate. Flowers non-resupinate; pale greenish yellow to lemon-yellow, in places washed and streaked red; sepals orbicular, fleshy, odd sepal concave, 4 mm in diam., apex rounded, greenish yellow washed red in the centre; lateral sepals plane, 5 mm in diam.; petals orbicular, the inner margin fitting into the concave depression of the odd sepal, waxy yellow, flushed red throughout; lip calcarate, disk funnel-shaped, the anterior side extended into a tongue-like lobe with 2 longitudinal ridges in the centre, lateral lobes thickened below, wing-like, erect above with a well-marked deep purple vertical line on each side; column white, short, thick, apex truncate, concave, the anterior portion extended upwards into 2 stout arms, the foot thick and united with the posterior wall of the funnelshaped portion of the lip, extending into a screen-like callus partially covering the throat of the spur; anther white, suborbicular, concave; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, attached by a short filament onto the stipe; ovary short, ridged and canaliculate.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 10815A (CUHK); HK sheet 7117.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, N India, Sikkim, Bhutan.
Ecology: Shade cliffs along streams. Flowering: Jun.–Sep

Rorippa cantoniensis (Lour.) Ohwi 廣州蔊菜（微子蔊菜）
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 6: 55. 1937; FGD 3: 39. 1995; FOC 8: 134. 2001.
Ricotia cantoniensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 482. 1793.
Nasturtium microspermum DC., Syst. Nat. 2: 199. 1821; FKH 34. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, 10 –30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems erect or decumbent. Basal leaves petiolate, rosulate, lyrate or pinnatisect, 4 –7 cm, lateral lobes 4 – 6 on both sides of midveins, margin 2–3-dentate; cauline leaves gradually becoming smaller upwards, sessile, base auriculate, obovate-oblong or spathulate, 1.5–5 cm, margin dentate or entire. Racemes terminal, bracteate. Sepals broadly lanceolate, 0.5 –2 mm. Petals yellow, obovate or narrowly spathulate, 2–3 mm. Siliques cylindric, 6 – 8 × 2 mm, dehiscent. Seeds many, reddish brown, ovate or ovate-reniform, 0.4 –0.6 mm, foveolate.

Locality: Sheung Shui. Y. S. Lau 2954; A. Lao 1123.
Distribution: Liaoning, Hebei, Shandong, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Hubei, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Korea, Russia, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

Rorippa dubia (Pers.) Hara 無瓣蔊菜
J. Jap. Bot. 30: 196. 1955; FGD 3: 39. 1995; FOC 8: 133. 2001.
Sisymbrium dubium Pers., Syn. Pl. 2: 199. 1807.

Annual herb, 10 –30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems erect or decumbent. Basal and lower cauline leaves usually lyratepinnatipartite, 3 – 8 cm, lateral lobes 2–4 on each side of midveins, margin sinuate-serrate; uppermost leaves usually sessile, lanceolate or oblong, margin entire or serrulate. Racemes terminal or lateral, ebracteate. Sepals often pinkish, lanceolate or linear, ca. 3 mm, margin membranous. Petals mostly absent, rarely present and linear or narrowly oblanceolate, often shorter than sepals. Siliques linear, 2–3.5 cm × 1 mm, dehiscent. Seeds uniserrate, brown, ovoid, 0.5 –0.8 mm, foveolate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. HK sheet 180, 32234.
Distribution: Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Hebei, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Shaanxi, Gansu, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang; Japan, Philippines, Indonesia, India, United States.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (whole plant).

Rorippa indica (L.) Hiern 蔊菜（塘葛菜）
Cat. Afr. Pl. 1: 26. 1896; FHN 1: 355. 1987; FGD 3: 38. 1995; FOC 8: 133. 2001.
Sisymbrium indicum L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 917. 1763.
Nasturtium montanum Wall. ex Hook. f. & Thoms., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 5: 139. 1861; FHK 16. 1861; FKH 34. 1912.
Cardamine lamontii Hance, Journ. Bot. 14: 363. 1876; FKH 34. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, 20–40 cm tall, glabrous or rarely sparsely pubescent. Stems often branched. Basal and lower cauline leaves long-petiolate, often lyrate-pinnatipartite, 4–10 cm, lateral lobes absent or 1–5 on each side of midvein; upper cauline leaves broadly lanceolate or spathulate, margin serrulate. Racemes terminal and lateral, ebracteate. Flowers small, many. Sepals ovate-oblong, 3–4 mm. Petals yellow, spathulate, 3–4 mm, shortly clawed. Siliques linear-cylindric, 1–2 cm × 1–1.5 mm, dehiscing into 2 valves. Seeds reddish brown, ovate or ovate-orbicular, 0.5–0.9 mm, foveolate.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 77; Y. S. Lau 1789, 281.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Shandong, Henan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Shaanxi, Gansu; Japan, Korea, Philippines, Indonesia, India.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (whole plant).
Notes: The type specimen of Cardamine lamontii was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. Lamont (in Herb. Hance No. 19355, BM) in September 1874.

Medicinal (whole plant).
Notes: The type specimen of Cardamine lamontii was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. Lamont (in Herb. Hance No. 19355, BM) in September 1874.

records.text:
Rosa chinensis Jacq. 月季花
Observ. Bot. 3: 7, pl. 55. 1768; FFJ 2: 287. 1985; FRPS 37: 422. 1985; FGD 4: 216. 2000; FOC 9: 369. 2003.

Shrub, 1–2 m tall; branchlets with hooked prickles or unarmed. Leaves imparipinnate, 5 – 11 cm, 3– 5( –7)-foliolate; petioles long, with sparse prickles and glandular-hairs; stipules mostly adnate to the petioles, upper free part auriculate, margin glandular-hairy; leaflets broadly ovate or ovate-oblong, 2.5 – 6 × 1 – 3 cm, base subrounded or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin acutely serrate, subglabrous, adaxially dark green, usually shiny, abaxially pale, terminal leaflets petiolulate, lateral ones subsessile. Flowers 4 – 5-clustered, rarely solitary, fragrant, 4–5 cm in diam.; pedicels 2.5–6 cm, subglabrous or glandular-hairy; bracts and bracteoles leafy, linear; hypanthium ovoid or pyriform, glabrous abaxially, pubescent adaxially; sepals 5, ovate, apex caudate-acuminate, sometimes leafy, margin usually pinnatifid, rarely entire, abaxially glabrous, adaxially pubescent, caducous; petals red, pink to white, usually double, obovate, base clawed; stamens numerous, glabrous; carpels 25 – 50; styles free, exserted, nearly as long as stamens. Hip ovoid or pyriform, 1 – 2 cm in diam., red, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3175; HK sheet 1645.
Distribution: Native to China; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Sep.; fruiting: Jun. –Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Rosa cymosa Tratt. 小果薔薇
Ros. Monogr. 1: 87. 1823; FFJ 2: 286. 1985; FRPS 37: 447. 1985; FGD 4: 219. 2000; FOC 9: 379. 2003.
Rosa microcarpa Lindl., Ros. Monogr. 130, pl. 18. 1820; FKH 96. 1912. non Retz. 1803, nec Bess. 1815.

Scandent shrub, 2–5 m tall; branchlets terete, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, with scattered, hooked prickles; prickles up to 6 mm. Leaves imparipinnate, 5–10 cm, 3–5(–7)-foliolate; petioles and petiolules glabrous or pubescent, with sparse prickles and glandular-hairy; stipules membranaceous, free, caducous, linear, apex acuminate, margin entire; leaflets ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, rarely oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–6 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate, margin serrate, adaxially green, lustrous, abaxially paler, glabrous except for sparsely pubescent along veins on abaxial surface. Inflorescences compound corymbose, many-flowered; pedicels ca. 1.5 cm, initially pubescent, soon glabrescent; bracts lanceolate, margin sparsely glandular-hairy; flowers fragrant, 2–2.5 cm in diam.; hypanthium globose or ovoid, glabrous; sepals 5, ovate, apex acuminate, usually pinnately laciniolate, abaxially subglabrous, rarely sparsely setose, adaxially sparsely white pubescent; petals 5, white, obovate; styles free, slightly exserted, nearly as long as stamens, densely white pubescent. Hip globose, 4 – 7 mm in diam., red to blackish brown when mature.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Anhui, Hebei; Japan, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Rosa henryi Boulenger 軟條七薔薇（亨氏薔薇）
Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles, Ser. B, 53: 143. 1933; FRPS 37: 443. 1985; FFJ 2: 290. 1985; FGD 4: 219. 2000; FOC 9: 378. 2003.
Rosa moschata auct. non Mill.: FHK 106. 1861.
Rosa luciae auct. non Franch. & Rochebr.: FKH 96. 1912.

Scandent shrub, 3–5 m tall, with long repent branches; branchlets terete, glabrous, with short, hooked prickles. Leaves imparipinnate, 9–14 cm including petiole, usually 5-foliolate; petioles glabrous, with sparsely minute prickles; stipules mostly adnate to the petiole, free part lanceolate, glabrous or sparsely glandular-hairy; leaflets oblong, ovate, elliptic or elliptic-ovate, 3–9 × 1.5–5 cm, base subrounded or cuneate, apex long-acuminate or caudate, margin serrate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences corymbose, terminal, 3–4 cm in diam., 5 – 15-flowered; pedicels 1.5–2 cm, glabrous or glandular-hairy; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, caducous; flowers fragrant, 2.5–4 cm in diam.; hypanthium globose, glabrous or shortly glandular-hairy; sepals 5, lanceolate, apex acute, margin entire or rarely lobed, abaxially subglabrous, sparsely glandular punctuate, adaxially pubescent, caducous; petals 5, white, broadly obovate, apex emarginate, base broadly cuneate; styles connate into a column, exserted, pubescent, slightly longer than stamens. Hip subglobose, 0.8–1 cm, red or purplish brown.

Locality: Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 2977.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Apr.

Rosa kwangtungensis T. T. Yu & Tsai 廣東薔薇
Bull. Fan Mem. Inst. Biol., Bot. 7(3): 114. 1936; FRPS 37: 431. 1985; FGD 4: 217. 2000; FOC 9: 371. 2003.

Scandent shrub; branches long, repent, dark grey or reddish brown, glabrous; branchlets pubescent, with minute, hooked prickles. Leaves imparipinnate, 3.5–7 cm, 5–7-foliolate; petioles 0.6–1.5 cm, pubescent, terminal leaflets petiolulate, lateral ones sessile; stipules mostly adnate to the petioles, half the length of petioles, free part lanceolate, pubescent, margin irregularly serrate to fimbriate; leaflets elliptic, oblong or elliptic-ovate, 1.5–4 × 0.8 – 1.8 cm, base cuneate or subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate, adaxially dark green, pubescent along midveins, abaxially pale green, pubescent, midvein abaxially with sparse prickles and glandular hairs. Inflorescences corymbose, terminal, 5 – 7 cm in diam., 4 – 15-flowered; pedicels 1 – 2 cm, densely pubescent or glandular-hairy or subglabrous; bracts and bracteoles ovate, margin glandular, laciniate or serrate, apex acuminate; flowers fragrant, 1.5 – 3 cm in diam.; hypanthium obovoid, abaxially pubescent and glandular-hairy; sepals 5, ovate-lanceolate, apex long-acuminate, margin entire, pubescent or subglabrous on both surfaces, caducous; petals 5, white, obovate, slightly shorter than sepals; styles connate into a column, exserted, white pubescent, slightly longer than stamens. Hip globose, 0.7– 1 cm in diam., purplish brown.

Locality: Castle Peak. W. J. Tutcher 10915.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Japan, Korea, Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun.– Jul.

Rosa kwangtungensis T. T. Yu & Tsai var. plena T. T. Yu & T. C. Ku 重瓣廣東薔薇
Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 1(4): 13. 1981; FRPS 37: 432. 1985; FGD 4: 218. 2000.

It differs from var. kwangtungensis by its double flowers and serrate stipules.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk. H. C. Tang 1729.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr. –May.

Rosa laevigata Michx. 金櫻子
Fl. Bor.-Amer. 1: 295. 1803; FKH 96. 1912; FRPS 37: 448. 1985; FFJ 2: 284. 1985; FGD 4: 220. 2000; FOC 9: 380. 2003.
Rosa sinica auct. non Aiton: FHK 106. 1861.

Evergreen scandent shrub, up to 5 m tall; branchlets glabrous, initially glandular-hairy, with sparse hooked prickles. Leaves imparipinnate, 5 – 10 cm, 3( – 5)-foliolate; petioles and petiolules prickly and glandular-hairy; stipules free or adnate to the petioles basally, lanceolate, apex acuminate, margin pectinately lobed, caducous; leaflets leathery, elliptic-ovate, obovate or lanceolate-ovate, 2 –7 × 1.2 –4 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, rarely caudate, margin serrate, adaxially green and lustrous, glabrous, abaxially yellowish green, initially glandular-hairy along the midveins, glabrescent. Flowers solitary, axillary, 5– 8 cm in diam.; pedicels 1.8–3 cm, glandular-hairy or prickly; bracts absent; hypanthium ovoid, densely glandular bristly; sepals 5, ovate-lanceolate, leafy, margin pinnatifid or entire, usually glandular bristly, adaxially pubescent, abaxially glabrous, erect in fruits; petals 5, white, broadly ovate, apex emarginate, slightly longer than sepals; stamens numerous; carpels numerous; styles free, pubescent, much shorter than stamens. Hip pyriform or obovoid, rarely globose, 0.8– 1.5 cm in diam., abaxially densely glandular bristly, purple-brown when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Lai Chi Wo, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 958; P. S. Choi 407; HK sheet 40642.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei, Shaanxi; Japan.
Ecology: Thickets on hilly fields. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rosa luciae Franch. & Rochebr. 光葉薔薇
Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 10: 324. 1871; FKH 96. 1912; FOC 9: 373. 2003.
Rosa wichurana Crép., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 25(2): 189. 1886; FFJ 2: 289. 1985; FRPS 37: 432. 1985; FGD 4: 218. 2000 (as “wichuraiana”).

Scandent shrub, 3 – 5 m; branchlets reddish brown, initially pubescent, soon glabrescent, prickles small, incurved, flattened at base. Leaves imparipinnate, 5 – 10 cm including petiole, 5 – 7( –9)-foliolate; stipules mostly adnate to the petiole, free parts lanceolate, margin glandular serrate or dentate and with glandular-hairs, apex shortly acuminate; leaflets elliptic, ovate or obovate, 1– 3.5 × 0.7–1.5 cm, apex obtuse or acute, margin sparsely serrate, glabrous, adaxially dark green, shining, abaxially pale green. Inflorescences corymbose, many-flowered, or sometimes flowers solitary; peduncles and pedicels initially sparsely pubescent, glabrescent; bracts ovate, caducous; flowers fragrant, 2 – 3 cm in diam.; hypanthium subglobose, sparsely glandular-hairy; sepals 5, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, apex acuminate, margin entire, abaxially subglabrous, adaxially densely pubescent, tardily deciduous; petals 5, white, obovate, apex obtuse, base cuneate; styles connate into a column, exserted, pubescent, slightly longer than stamens. Hip globose or subglobose, 0.8–1.8 cm, purplish black, sparsely glandular-hairy.

Locality: Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Yung Shue O, Tai Po, Fanling, Sha Tau Kok. Y. S. Lau 2162, 2699; Y. W. Lam 684.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets and forests. Flowering: Mar. – Jul.; fruiting: Jun. –Nov.

Rosa multiflora Thunb. 野薔薇（七姐妹）
Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 474. 1784; FHK 107. 1861; FRPS 37: 428. 1985; FFJ 2: 289. 1985; FOC 9: 370. 2003.

Scandent shrub, up to 3 m tall; branchlets slender, glabrous or pubescent, with sparse prickles; prickles nearly straight or slight curved. Leaves imparipinnate, (3– )5 – 9-foliolate, 5– 10 cm including petioles; petioles glabrous or pubescent, usually with glandular hairs, shortly prickly; stipules mostly adnate to petioles, free parts pectinate, margin glandular-hairy or not; leaflets obovate-oblong or oblong, 1 – 5 × 0.8 – 2.8 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin serrate, abaxially pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Inflorescence corymbose, many-flowered; pedicels 1.5 – 2.5 cm, pubescent, glabrous or glandular-hairy; flowers fragrant, 1.5 –2 cm in diam.; bracts small, at the base of pedicels; hypanthium subglobose, glabrous; sepals 5, deciduous, lanceolate, abaxially glabrous, adaxially pubescent; petals 5, white, obovate, base cuneate; stamens numerous, filaments ca. 8 mm, glabrous; carpels many; styles connate into a column, exserted, slightly longer than the stamens, glabrous. Hip globose or ovoid, 6 – 8 mm in diam., reddish brown, glabrous and shining.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 130; Y. S. Lau 528, 2113.
Distribution: Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Henan; Korea, Japan.
Uses: Ornamental.

Rosa rugosa Thunb. 玫瑰
Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 473. 1784; FRPS 37: 401. 1985.

Erect shrub, ca. 2 m tall; stems and branches tomentose, densely bristly and prickly. Leaves imparipinnate, 5–9-foliolate, 5 – 13 cm, including petioles; petioles densely pubescent and glandular-hairy, sometimes with minute prickles; stipules mostly adnate to the petioles, free parts ovate, margin glandular pubescent; leaflets elliptic or elliptic-obovate, 1.5–4.5 × 1–2.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin acutely serrate, adaxially dark green, glabrous, rugose due to concave veins, abaxially pale green, densely tomentose and glandular-hairy. Flowers solitary or several in a cluster, axillary, 4 – 5.5 cm in diam.; bracts ovate, margin glandular-hairy, abaxially pubescent; pedicels 0.5 – 2.5 cm, densely pubescent and glandular-hairy; hypanthium subglobose, glabrous; sepals 5, ovate-lanceolate, apex caudate, leafy, usually pinnatifid, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely pubescent or glandular-hairy, erect in fruits; petals fragrant, semi-double or double, white to purplish-red; styles free, slightly exserted, much shorter than stamens, pubescent. Hip depressed globose, 2–2.5 cm in diam., dark green, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 9886.
Distribution: Native in Jilin, Liaoning and NE Shandong, widely cultivated in China; Korea and Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Aug. – Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, spice, medicinal (folklore).

Rotala diversifolia Koehne 異葉節節菜
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 41(2): 77. 1907; FRPS 52(2): 75. 1983; FGD 3: 74. 1995.

Annual herb, 8–30 cm tall. Stems angled and broadly winged. Leaves decussate, sessile; leaf blade narrowly oblong, 8 – 12 × 3– 8 mm, base broadly subcordate, apex obtuse, semiamplexicaul, lateral veins slender, 5 or more on each side of midvein. Spikes axillary, 3– 5(–10) cm. Bracts leaf-like, 4– 6 mm, base rounded, enlarged; bracteoles 2, white. Calyx-tube broadly campanulate, 2 mm, teeth 4 – 5, deltoid, 1 mm. Petals purplish, 4–5, obovate, 2 mm, persistent. Stamens 4–5. Capsule subglobose, 3-valved.

Locality: Tai Lung. S. Y. Hu 12702; P. S. Choi 529.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Nov.

Rotala indica (Willd.) Koehne 節節菜
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 1(2): 172. 1880; FRPS 52(2): 73. 1983; FGD 3: 73, fig. 50. 1995.
Peplis indica Willd., Sp. Pl. 2(1): 244. 1799.
Ammannia peploides Spreng, Syst. Veg. 1: 444. 1825; FKH 109. 1912.

Annual erect or diffuse herb, 6–25 cm tall. Stems slightly 4-angled, often decumbent and with adventitious roots at base. Leaves opposite, sessile or subsessile; leaf blade obovate or oblong-obovate, 4–17 × 3 – 7 mm, base narrow, apex acute or obtuse, mucronate, margin cartilaginous. Flowers small, less than 3 mm, in axillary, short (8 –15 mm) spikes, rarely solitary. Bracts oblong-obovate, 4–5 mm; bracteoles 2, linear-lanceolate. Calyx-tube campanulate, 2 – 2.5 mm, teeth 4, narrowly deltoid. Petals 4, minute, pinkish, scarcely half the length of calyx-teeth. Capsules elliptic, 1.5 mm, slightly angled, dehiscing by 2 valves.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 8132, 7271; P. S. Choi 64.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Philippines, Indochina, Japan, Russia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and wet places. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Nov. –Mar. of the following year.

Rotala pentandra (Roxb.) Blatt. & Hallb. 薄瓣節節菜
J. Bombay Nat. Hist. Soc. 25: 707. 1918, p.p.; FRPS 52(2): 76. 1983; FGD 3: 74. 1995.
Ammannia pentandra Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 448. 1820; FKH 108. 1912.

Annual herb. Stems decumbent or erect, 8– 30 cm tall, 4-angled. Leaves narrowly lanceolate or lanceolate, 7–30 × 3– 5 mm (only 5 mm in lateral branches), base subtruncate, rarely slightly cordate and amplexicaul, apex acute, obtuse or emarginate; bracteoles linear-lanceolate. Flowers sessile. Calyx pot-like to campanulate, 1 – 1.5 mm, 3– 5-toothed, with bristle-like appendages between teeth. Petals 5, thin and hyaline, sometimes absent. Stamens 3 –5. Capsules red, globular, 3–5-valved.

Locality: Hong Kong. (fide Hu, 2001)
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangsu, Fujian; E & S Asia, Afghanistan, Indonesia, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul. Notes: The species was reported as Ammannia leptopetela Koehne previously (Check List HK Plants 65. 1993).

Rotala rotundifolia (Buch.-Ham. ex Roxb.) Koehne 圓葉節節菜
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 1(2): 175. 1800; FRPS 52(2): 75. 1983; FGD 3: 73. 1995.
Ammannia rotundifolia Buch.-Ham. ex Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 446. 1820; FHK 111. 1861; FKH 108. 1912.

Annual herb, 5–30 cm tall, glabrous, diffuse and often rooting at base. Leaves opposite, sessile or very shortly petiolate; leaf blade orbicular, obovate, or broadly oblong, 5 – 10 × 2.5 – 15 mm, base obtuse, apex rounded, lateral veins 4 on each side of midvein. Flowers solitary in axils of bracts, forming 1–3 terminal densely flowered spikes of 1 – 5 cm. Bracts ovate or long-ovate, as long as flowers; bracteoles 2, membranous, lanceolate or cuneate, as long as calyx-tube. Calyx-tube broadly campanulate, ± hyaline, 1–1.5 mm, 4-toothed; teeth deltoid. Petals 4, obovate, purplish, twice as long as calyx-lobes. Stamens 4. Capsules elliptic, 3 –4-valved.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 834, 3049; L. T. Lo 207.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Indochina, Japan.
Ecology: Paddy fields and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Dec.– Jun. of the following year.

Rottboellia cochinchinensis (Lour.) Clayton 筒軸茅
Kew Bull. 35: 817. 1981; FOC 22: 645. 2006; FGD 9: 481, fig. 252. 2009.
Stegosia cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 51. 1790.
Rottboellia exaltata L. f., Suppl. Pl. 114. 1781[1782], not (L.) L. f. (1779); FKH 321. 1912; FHN 4: 466, fig. 1253. 1977; FFJ 6: 258, fig. 228. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 268, pl. 67: 1–2. 1997; Check List HK Plants 345. 2002; 121. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms stout, 1–3 m tall. Leaf sheaths tuberculatehispid with stiff irritant hairs or sometimes glabrescent; leaf blades linear to linear-lanceolate, 20–50 × 0.5–2.5 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface hispidulous, very scabrid along margins, midrib broad, white, apex acuminate; ligule a ciliate membrane, 1–2 mm. Racemes yellow and green; rachis internode 4–7 mm. Sessile spikelet pale yellow, sunken in a cylindrical rachis-joint; lower glume ovate, minutely scaberulous on abaxial surface, 2-keeled only toward entire or very minutely 2–3-toothed apex, narrow wings along keels; upper glume abaxial convex and keeled, keel with narrow wings, acute; lower floret staminate, lemma oblong, acute, 3-veined; upper floret bisexual, upper lemma broad ovate, acute. Pedicellate spikelet green, variable, 3–5 mm, narrowly ovate, herbaceous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1046; P. P. H. But 68; P. S. Choi 367.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over Old World tropics.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Rourea microphylla (Hook. & Arn.) Planch. 小葉紅葉藤（紅葉藤）
Linnaea 23: 421. 1850; FHK 71. 1861; FKH 70. 1912; FHN 3: 112, fig. 608. 1974; FFJ 2: 338, fig. 184. 1984; FRPS 38: 140, pl. 25: 1 – 8. 1986; FGD 4: 280. 2000; FOC 9: 437. 2003.
Connarus microphyllus Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beech. Voy. 179. 1833.
Santaloides microphyllum G. Schellenb., Pflanzenr. 103: 130. 1938.
Rourea minor subsp. microphylla (Hook. & Arn.) Vidal, Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam 2: 28. 1962.

Climbing shrub, 1 – 4 m, many-branched. Branchlets glabrous or sparsely pubescent when young. Petioles, rachis, and petiolules glabrous; leaflets 7 – 17( – 27), papery to thinly leathery, ovate or lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 1.2 – 5.5 × 0.5 – 2 cm, base cuneate to rounded, often oblique, apex obtuse and acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, slightly glaucous abaxially; petiolule 2 mm. Inflorescences in axillary clusters, usually 3 – 6 cm, central one often longer, many-flowered; peduncles and pedicels slender. Flowers 4 – 5 mm in diam., fragrant. Sepals ovate, 2.5 × 2 mm, ciliolate. Petals elliptic, white, pale yellow or pink, 5 × 1.5 mm. Stamens 10, unequal, longer ones to 6 mm, shorter ones ca. 4 mm. Carpels free, 3 – 5 mm. Follicle red when mature, cylindric or obliquely obovoid-cylindric, slightly curved or straight, 1 – 1.5 × 0.5 cm, longitudinally striate. Seed orange, oblong, ca. 1 cm, with membranous aril at base.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 283; Y. S. Lau 1273.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes or forests. Flowering: Mar. – Sep.; fruiting: May – Mar. of following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rourea minor (Gaertn.) Alston 大葉紅葉藤（牛栓藤）

Fl. Ceylon 6(2): 67. 1931; Li., Woody Fl. Taiwan 329, fig. 114. 1963; FRPS 38: 142, pl. 26: 4 – 6. 1986; FGD 4: 281, fig. 166. 2000; FOC 9: 437. 2003.

Aegiceras minus Gaertn., Fruct. 1: 216, fig. 46. 1788.

Rourea santaloides Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 144. 1834; FHK 71. 1861; FHN 3: 112. 1974.

Rourea millettii Planch., Linnaea 23: 420. 1850; FKH 70. 1912.


Vine or climbing shrub, to 25 m long. Branchlets terete, glabrous or sparsely pubescent when young. Petioles, rachis, and petiolules glabrous; leaflets 3 – 7, usually 3, papery, ovate or elliptic to lanceolate, 3 – 15 × 2 – 6 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, equilateral or slightly oblique, apex acute to shortly acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; petiolules 5 mm. Inflorescences in axillary clusters, 3 – 9 cm, many-flowered, central one much longer than others; peduncles 3 – 9 cm, glabrous. Flowers ca. 1 cm in diam., fragrant. Sepals ovate, 2 – 3 × 1.2 – 2 mm, ciliate at apex. Petals white or yellow, oblong, 4 – 6 × 1 – 1.5 mm, striate, glabrous. Stamens 2 – 6 mm. Carpels free, ca. 4 mm, glabrous. Follicle dark green, turning black when dry, obliquely ellipsoidal, slightly curved, 1.5 – 2.5 × 0.6 – 1.5 cm, striate. Seed red, ellipsoidal, 1.5 × 0.6 cm, completely covered by membranous aril.


Locality: Aberdeen, Hoi Ha, Chek Keng, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 27; P. S. Choi 164.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Philippines, Australia (Queensland).

Ecology: Thickets or forests. Flowering: Apr. – Oct.; fruiting: May – Mar. of following year.

Roystonea regia (Kunth) O. F. Cook 大王椰子（王棕）
Science, II, 12: 479. 1900; FGD 2: 463, fig. 326. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 129. 1991.

Large tree, to 30 m tall, dioecious. Stems solitary, to 50 cm in diam., grey-white, smooth, rings of leaf scars conspicuous when young. Leaves pinnate, about 15 in number, to 5 m long, recurved; pinnae to 250 per side, arranged on different planes, elongate lanceolate, 2-lobed at apices, to 90 × 4 cm; sheaths closed and forming a green, leathery crownshaft. Inflorescences to 1.5 m, branched 3–4 orders. Flowers small, white, male flowers 6–7 mm, stamens 6; female flowers 3–3.5 mm. Fruits subglobose, about 1.3 × 1 cm, dark-red. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: SE USA, C Mexico, Caribbean, Mesoamerica, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Rubia wallichiana Decne. 多花茜草
Recherch. Anat. & Physiol. Garance 61: 1837; FRPS 71(2): 315. 1999; FGD 6: 248. 2005.
Rubia cordifolia auct. non L.: FHN 3: 363, fig. 774. 1974.

Trailing herbs, 1–3 m or longer. Stems and branches quadrangular, ± with recurved, short prickles on the angles, glabrous or pubescent on nodes. Leaves in whorls of 4 or 6, thinly papery or membranous; petioles 1–6 cm, with recurved prickles; leaf blade lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 2–7 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base cordate or subrounded, apex acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous or scabrous, abaxial surface glabrous, glaucous when dry; 5‑veined, with minute prickles on the margins and midvein. Flowers in axillary thyrses, 1 – 5 cm; peduncles quadrangular, subglabrous; pedicels slender, 3–4 mm. Calyx‑tube ovoid, shallowly 2‑lobed. Corolla purplish red, greenish yellow or white; tube very short; lobes lanceolate, 1.3–1.5 mm, apex acuminate. Fruit black, globular or didymous, each segment 3.5–4 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. L. T. Lo 319; Y. W. Lam 436, 2182.
Distribution: Hainan, Gungdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi; India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rubus alceifolius Poir. 粗葉懸鈎子
Encycl. 6(1): 247. 1804; FFJ 2: 309. 1985; FRPS 37: 158. 1985; FGD 4: 212. 2000; FOC 9: 253. 2003.
Rubus moluccanus auct. non L.: FKH 95. 1912.

Scandent shrub, up to 5 m tall; branchlets densely tawny to rusty tomentose, sometimes glandular-hairy, with sparse hooked prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 3–4.5 cm, densely rusty tomentose, sparsely prickled; leaf blade papery or thinly leathery, ovate to orbicular, 6–16 × 5–15 cm, base cordate, apex rounded, rarely acute, margin irregularly 3–7-lobed, usually palmately 5-veined; lobes oblong-ovate, apex obtuse or acute, margin irregularly dentate or crenate, adaxially hirsute, abaxially densely grey or rusty tomentose. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, narrowly paniculate or racemose, 6 – 11 cm, sometimes flowers in axillary clusters, rarely solitary; peduncles and pedicels densely yellow or rusty tomentose, with sparsely minute, hooked prickles; pedicels 0.5 – 1 cm. Flowers 1 – 1.6 cm in diam.; hypanthium obconical, 7–10 mm, abaxially yellowish or rusty tomentose; sepals triangular-ovate, 6–9 × 5–8 mm, outer ones palmately or pinnately laciniate, rarely unlobed, inner ones entire, shortly pointed, abaxially tomentose; petals white, broadly obovate or suborbicular, nearly as long as sepals, clawed at base; stamens numerous, filaments ca. 5 mm, broadened, anthers sparsely tomentose; carpels many, glabrous. Aggregate fruits subglobose, up to 1.8 cm in diam., red, glabrous, enclosed in persistent sepals.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Chuen Lung, Shing Mun, Yuen Tun Ha, Sai Kung. L. T. Lo 263, 397; Y. W. Lam 1673.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.– Sep.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rubus leucanthus Hance 白花懸鈎子
Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 468. 1852; FHK 105. 1861; FKH 95. 1912; FFJ 2: 301. 1985; FRPS 37: 103. 1985; FGD 4: 201. 2000; FOC 9: 229. 2003.
Rubus glaberrimus Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 80. 1852.

Scandent shrub, 1– 3 m tall; stems and branchlets glabrous, sparsely prickled. Leaves imparipinnate, 3-foliolate, sometimes reduced to simple apically on branchlets; petioles 2 – 6 cm, petiolules of terminal leaflets 1.5 – 2 cm, lateral leaflets shortly petiolulate, glabrous, with prickles; leaflets leathery, ovate or elliptic, terminal leaflets slightly larger than or nearly equaling the lateral ones, 4 – 8 × 2 – 4 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, margin irregularly serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences corymbose, terminal on the lateral short branchlets, rarely axillary, 3 – 5 cm, 2 – 8-flowered, glabrous; pedicels 0.5 – 1.5 cm; bracts subulate, 3 – 5 mm, trifid, caducous. Flowers 1 – 1.5 cm in diam.; hypanthium campanulate, abaxially glabrous; sepals erect, ovate, 4 – 7 × 3 – 5 mm, greyish pubescent adaxially and on margins, glabrous abaxially, apex abruptly mucronate, persistent; petals white, narrowly ovate or suborbicular, as long as or slightly longer than sepals, base long clawed, apex obtuse; stamens numerous, somewhat shorter than petals, filaments broadened and flattened, anthers ovate; carpels numerous, glabrous or pubescent apically; styles filiform, shorter than petals, glabrous or pubescent basally. Aggregate fruits subglobose, 1– 1.5 cm in diam., red, glabrous; enclosed by persistent calyx-lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 316, 2183; HK sheet 39975.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian; Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia.
Ecology: Hillslopes and thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Jul.
Uses: Edible (fruit), medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by H. F. Hance between 1844 and 1850.
