records.text:
Rubus parvifolius L. 茅莓（草楊莓子）
Sp. Pl. 2: 1197. 1753; FHK 105. 1861; FKH 95. 1912; FRPS 37: 68. 1985; FFJ 2: 300. 1985; FGD 4: 198. 2000; FOC 9: 213. 2003.

Scandent shrub; branchlets pubescent and with sparse, curved prickles. Leaves imparipinnate, 3(–5)-foliolate; petioles 2.5–5 cm, petiolules of terminal leaflets 1–2 cm, tomentose, with sparse prickles; leaflets ovate, ovate-lanceolate or rhombic-orbicular, terminal ones larger, 1.5–2.5 cm, lateral ones smaller, base broadly cuneate or nearly rounded, apex obtuse or acute, margin irregularly incise-dentate or lobed, adaxially subglabrous or sparsely tomentose, abaxially densely grey tomentose. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, or sometimes flowers solitary in upmost leaf axils; peduncles together with pedicels (0.5–1.5 cm) and the campanulate hypanthium tomentose and with sparse prickles; sepals ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, apex acuminate, tomentose, with prickles; petals pink, obovate, shorter than sepals; stamens many, filaments white, shorter than petals; Carpels tomentose. Aggregate fruits globose, red, 1–1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 773, 2359; HK sheet 39952.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Xinjiang, Qinghai, Xizang, Nei Mongol; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Hillslopes, open fields. Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. –Aug.
Uses: Edible (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Rubus pirifolius Sm. 梨葉懸鈎子
Pl. Icon. Ined. 3: t. 61. 1791 (as ‘pyrifolius’); FRPS 37: 132. 1985; FFJ 2: 308. 1985; FGD 4: 207. 2000; FOC 9: 261. 2003.
Dalibarda pyrifolia (Sm.) Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 17: 1112. 1827.
Rubus hexagynus auct. non Roxb: FKH 94. 1912.

Scandent shrub; branches strigose, with few complanate curved prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 0.6 – 1.5 cm, densely strigose, with sparse prickles; leaf blade leathery, ovate, ovate-oblong or elliptic-oblong, 6 – 11 × 3.5 – 5.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin irregularly dentate, both surfaces glabrous, but pubescent along midvein and lateral veins, gradually glabrescent. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, paniculate or subracemose, many-flowered; peduncle, pedicels and hypanthium densely tawny pubescent, unarmed or with minute prickles. Flowers 1–1.5 cm in diam; pedicels 4 –12 cm; sepals triangular-lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 5–7 × 2–3.5 mm, apex acuminate, margin entire or apically 2–3-laciniate, tomentose adaxially and on the margins; petals white, small, oblong or lanceolate, 3– 5 mm, shorter than sepals, glabrous, margin dentate; stamens numerous, slightly longer than petals, filaments filiform; carpels 3 – 10, hairy, rarely glabrous; styles filiform, 6 – 8 mm, glabrous or basally tomentose, stigmas bifid. Aggregate fruits red, 1 –1.5 cm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po, Ta Tit Yan. Birdwood 663; W. J. Tutcher 10024.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia, Philippines, India.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), edible (fruit).

Rubus reflexus Ker Gawl. 鏽毛莓（蛇泡簕）
Bot. Reg. 6: 461. 1820; FHK 105. 1861; FKH 94. 1912; FFJ 2: 310. 1985; FRPS 37: 176. 1985; FGD 4: 211. 2000; FOC 9: 259. 2003.

Scandent shrub, up to 2 m tall; branchlets densely rusty tomentose, with sparse minute prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 2.5 – 5 cm, pubescent, with sparse minute prickles; leaf blade ovate to suborbicular, 7–14 × 5–11 cm, usually 3–5(–7)-lobed, base cordate, margin irregularly and coarsely serrate or double serrate, adaxially wrinkled and nearly glabrous or sparsely soft hairy on veins, abaxially densely rusty tomentose, with long hairs along veins. Inflorescences terminal, shortly subracemose, or sometimes flowers in axillary clusters; peduncles and pedicels densely rusty tomentose; pedicels 3–6 mm. Flowers 1–1.5 cm in diam.; hypanthium obconical, abaxially densely rusty tomentose; sepals ovate-orbicular or ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 6–8 × 4–7 mm, outer ones usually palmately lobed apically, lobes lanceolate, inner ones usually entire; petals white, oblong to suborbicular, glabrous, nearly as long as sepals, shortly clawed at base; stamens numerous, shorter than the petals, filaments broadened and flattened, anthers glabrous or pubescent apically; carpels many, glabrous. Aggregate fruits ovoid or subglobose, ca. 1 cm in diam., dark red, glabrous, enclosed in persistent sepals.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1727; Y. S. Lau 641; HK sheet 39966.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Aug. – Sep.
Uses: Edible (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Rubus rosifolius Sm. 空心泡（薔薇莓）
Pl. Icon. Ined. 3: 60. 1791; FKH 95. 1912; FRPS 37: 96. 1985; FFJ 2: 298. 1985; FGD 4: 199. 2000; FOC 9: 227. 2003.

Erect or scandent shrub, 2– 3 m tall; branchlets, petioles, petiolules and rachis of leaves pilose and with prickles and yellow glands, sometimes subglabrous. Leaves 5 –12 cm, imparipinnate, usually 5–7-foliolate; petioles 2–3 cm, petiolules of terminal leaflets 0.8 –1.5 cm, lateral leaflets subsessile; leaflets ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 2.5–7 × 1.5–2 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, margin spiny incised doubly serrate, pilose or subglabrous on both surfaces, with yellow glands. Inflorescences terminal or in leaf axils, 1–2-flowered, sometimes several in short racemes; bracts linear or lanceolate, 5 – 9 mm, pilose; pedicels 2–3.5 cm, pilose and with sparse, minute prickles, sometimes glandular. Flowers 2–3 cm in diam.; hypanthium urceolate; sepals lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 0.8–1.3 × 0.4–0.6 cm, apex long acuminate, abaxially pilose and glandular, reflexed after anthesis; petals 5, white, oblong, oblong-obovate or suborbicular, 1–1.5 × 0.8–1 cm, pilose abaxially, apex acute, base clawed; stamens many, shorter than petals, filaments broad; carpels many, up to 2 mm; receptacles shortly stalked. Aggregate fruits globose or ovoid, 1 – 1.5 cm, red, lustrous, glabrous, with few glands.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lam Tsuen. Y. S. Lau 544; L. T. Lo 233; HK sheet 1635.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Anhui, Hubei; Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Myanmar, India, Indonesia, Australia, Madagascar, Africa.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rubus tsangii Merr. 光葉懸鈎子
Lingnan Sci. J. 13(1): 28. 1934; FFJ 2: 206. 1985; FRPS 37: 95. 1985; FGD 4: 200. 2000; FOC 9: 227. 2003.

Scandent shrub; branchlets terete, with sparse prickles and 1 – 2 mm stalked glandular hairs. Leaves imparipinnate, (5– )7 – 9( – 1)-foliolate; petioles, petiolules and rachis of leaves glabrous, with sparse shortly stalked glands and minute prickles; petioles 4–7 cm, petiolules of terminal leaflets ca. 1 cm, lateral leaflets subsessile; leaflets lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 4–7 × 0.8–2 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, margin irregularly serrate or double serrate, initially sparsely pubescent, gradually glabrescent, abaxially with sparse prickles along the midveins. Infloresences corymbose, terminal, 4–6 cm, 3 – 5-flowered, rarely flowers solitary; bracts lanceolate, 0.6 – 1 cm, glabrous; pedicels 2 – 4 cm, with unequal long stalked glands. Flowers 3 – 4 cm in diam.; hypanthium urceolate, ca. 1 cm in diam., with sparse glandular hairs; sepals oblong-lanceolate or narrowly ovate-lanceolate, 0.9–1.5 × 0.4–0.6 cm, reflexed in fruits, inner ones with grey tomentose margin, apex long caudate; petals white, narrowly obovate or oblong, 0.9 – 1.4 × 0.6 – 0.8 cm, base clawed; stamens unequal, shorter than petals, filaments somewhat broadened and flattened; pistils many, shorter than stamens. Aggregate fruits subglobose, up to 1.5 cm in diam., red, glabrous or with glandular hairs.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 9493.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun.– Jul.

Rubus tsangiorum Hand.-Mazz. 東南懸鈎子
Symb. Sin. 7(3): 485. 1933; FFJ 2: 307. 1985; FRPS 37: 203. 1985; FGD 4: 210. 2000; FOC 9: 278. 2003.

Small scandent shrub, 0.3 – 1.5 m tall; branchlets villous and mixed with purplish red glandular hairs and bristles. Leaves simple; petioles 4–8 cm, villous, with purplish red glandular hairs; leaf blade papery, oblong or ovate-oblong, 6–14 × 2 – 5 cm, base deeply cordate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin irregularly coarsely serrate and 3 –5-lobed, lateral lobes broadly triangular, apex obtuse or acute, terminal lobes slightly larger than lateral ones, broadly ovate-triangular, apex acute, adaxially pubescent, with intermixed glandular hairs on veins, abaxially thinly tomentose, with intermixed long hairs and glandular hairs on veins. Inflorescences subracemose, terminal or axillary, 5 – 20-flowered, terminal ones 8 – 13 cm, axillary ones smaller; peduncles and pedicels pubescent and with purplish red glandular hairs; pedicels unequal in length, 0.5–2.5 cm, pubescent and with purplish red glandular hairs. Flowers 1–  cm in diam.; sepals narrowly triangular-lanceolate, 0.7 – 1.2 × 0.3 – 0.5 cm, apically deeply and palmately 2 – 3-lobed, lobes lanceolate; petals white, broadly obovate, 6–7 mm, much shorter than sepals, clawed at base; stamens numerous, filaments ca. 5 mm, linear; carpels many, much longer than stamens, glabrous. Aggregate fruits subglobose, ca. 1.4 cm in diam., red, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Po (Yuen Tun Ha). F. W. Xing 8955 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Aug. – Sep.

Ruellia coerulea Morong 蘭花草
Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 7: 193. 1893.
Cryphiacanthus angustifolius Nees, Prodr. 11: 199. 1847 non Ruellia angustifolia Sw.
Ruellia brittoniana Leonard, J. Wash. Acad. Sci. 31: 96. 1941, based on Cryphiacanthus angustifolius Nees; Check List HK Plants 254. 2002; 87. 2004.
Ruellia spectabils Britton, Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 7: 192. 1893, non Nicholson 1886, based on Cryphiacanthus angustifolius Nees.

Erect perennial herbs, 30–70 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous except for pubescent on the nodes. Petioles 0.5–2 cm, sulcate, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blades linear to linear‑lanceolate, 8–20 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, sometimes falculate, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous, cystoliths numerous, lateral veins 6–8 pairs, prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence of expanded dichasia, axillary, 5–10 cm; peduncles 5–6.5 cm, glabrous. Pedicels 0.5–1 cm, glabrous. Bracts lanceolate to linear, 3–15 × 1–15 mm, glabrous, densely covered with cystoliths; bracteoles 2, at the middle of pedicels, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 0.6–1 × 1 cm, glabrous, abaxially densely covered with cystoliths, often caducous. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes ca. 1 cm, abaxially puberulent. Corolla blue to purplish blue, 2.5–3.8 cm, campanulate, outside densely pilose in bud, then gradually glabrescent; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm, gradually widened to ca. 2 cm at mouth; lobes oblong, ca. 6 × 5 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments of the longer pair ca. 9 mm, the shorter pair ca. 6 mm; anther‑thecae oblong, ca. 3 mm. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 2.5 cm, pubescent; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal, the larger ca. 3 mm, the smaller ca. 0.3 mm. Capsule oblong, 2.5–3 cm, glabrous except for the pilose tip, 12–20‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, 2–2.5 × 2–2.3 mm, covered with hygroscopic hairs.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 846; HK sheet 34793, 38429.
Distribution: S China (cultivated and naturalized); native to Mexico.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Rumex dentatus L. 齒果酸模
Mant. Pl. 2: 226. 1771; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 356. 1891; Sam, Symb. Sin. 7: 168. 1929; FRPS 25: 161. 1996; FYN 11: 379, pl. 102: 6 –8. 2000; FOC 5: 339. 2003.

Annual herb. Stems erect, furrowed, 30–70 cm tall, branched from base; branches ascending. Petioles 1.5– 5 cm. Radical leaves oblong or oblong-elliptic, 4–12 × 1.5 –3 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex obtuse or acute, margin undulate; stem-leaves smaller, upwards gradually passing into bracts; ocrea tubular, 8 –15 mm, scarious, glabrous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal or axillary panicles, to 35 cm. Perianth-segments 6, light green, outer ones elliptic, ca. 2 mm, inner ones enlarged in fruit, triangular ovate, 3.5 – 4 × 2–2.5 mm, with tubercles, apex acute, base sub-rounded, margin with 2–4 spine-like teeth on each side. Achenes ovoid, sharply 3-angled, 2– 2.5 mm, yellowish brown and shining.

Locality: Shatin. Y. S. Lau 2151.
Distribution: Spread over most parts of China; Nepal, India, Afghanistan, Kazakstan and SE Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Rumex japonicus Houtt. 羊蹄
Nat. Hist. 2(8): 394. 1777; FRPS 25: 156, pl. 37: 3– 4. 1998; FYN 11: 376. 2000; FOC 5: 338. 2003.
Rumex crispus auct. non L.: FHK 286. 1861; FKH 218. 1912; FGD 4: 83. 2000.

Perennial herb, with thick root-stock. Stems erect, furrowed, 50 –100 cm tall. Radical leaves oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 8 – 20(–25) × 4– 8(–10) cm, base rounded or cordate, apex acute or obtuse, margin undulate, abaxially papillose on veins; petioles 2– 4 cm; stem-leaves smaller, narrowly oblong, shortly petiolate or sessile, upwards gradually passing into bracts; ocrea tubular, scarious, 1.5–2 cm, glabrous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal panicles. Pedicels slender, 5 –10 mm. Perianthsegments 6, light green, outer ones elliptic, 1.5–2 mm, inner ones enlarged in fruit, broadly ovate, 4 – 5 mm, with tubercles, apex acuminate, base cordate, margin irregularly denticulate. Achenes broadly ovoid, sharply 3-angled, ca. 2.5 mm, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Tuen Mun. Y. S. Lau 2164, HK sheet 30751.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rumex microcarpus Campd. 小果酸模
Monogr. Rum. 143. 1819; FRPS 25: 166. 1998; FGD 4: 83. 2000; FYN 11: 380. 2000; FOC 5: 341. 2003.
Rumex wallichii Meisn., DC. Prodr. 14(1): 48. 1856; FHN 1: 387. 1964.

Annual herb, 40– 80 cm tall. Stems erect, ± furrowed, glabrous, branched on the upper part. Radical leaves oblong-elliptic, 10–15 × 2– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or slightly obtuse, margin entire; petioles 2–4 cm; stem-leaves smaller, narrowly elliptic; ocrea tubular, scarious, caducous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal leafy panicles. Perianth-segments 6, yellowish green, outer ones lanceolate, ca. 1 mm, inner ones enlarged in fruit, narrowly triangular, 3 – 4 × 1.5 –2 mm, with tubercles, apex acute, base truncate, margin entire. Achenes ovoid, sharply 3-angled, 1–2 mm, brown and shining.

Locality: Lai Chi Kok. H. C. Tang 1912, 2468; Y. S. Lau 247.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Liaoning, Hebei, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Jul.

Rumex trisetifer Stokes 長刺酸模（假菠菜）
Bot. Mat. Med. 2: 305. 1814; FRPS 25: 161. 1998; FYN 11: 379, pl. 102: 4– 5. 2000; FOC 5: 340. 2003.
Rumex maritimus auct. non L.: FKH 218. 1912; FGD 4: 83. 2000.

Annual herb, 30 – 80 cm tall, with thick root-stock. Stems erect, brown to reddish brown, furrowed, glabrous. Petioles 1.5– 6 cm; Lower stem-leaves oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 8–20 × 2– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin undulate; upper leaves smaller, narrowly lanceolate; ocrea tubular, 15–20 mm, scarious, caducous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Pedicels slender, 2– 6 mm, articulate near base. Perianth-segments 6, in 2 whorls, yellowish green, outer 3 smaller, lanceolate, inner ones enlarged in fruit, narrowly triangular ovate, 3 – 4 × 1.5 –2 mm, with tubercles, base truncate, apex acute, margin with 1 spine on each side. Achenes ellipsoid, sharply 3-angled, 1.5–2 mm, yellowish brown and shining.

Locality: Hong Kong Islands. Y. S. Lau 1807.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, India.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Rungia chinensis Benth. 中華孩兒草
FHK 266. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FTW 4: 658. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 676. 1998; FRPS 70: 258. 2002.

Spreading to erect herbs, up to 70 cm tall. Stems slender, quadrangular, sulcate, slightly puberulent, usually rooting at lower nodes. Petioles 0.5–3 cm, pubescent; leaf blades membranous, ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 2.5–9 × 1.8–3 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous except for sparsely hirsute along the veins, lateral veins 5–6 pairs. Spikes terminal or axillary, 1–7 cm, 2‑sided. Bract 4‑ranked, dimorphic, outer sterile ones elliptic, ca. 6 × 2–4 mm, sparsely ciliate, inner fertile bracts obovate, or obovate‑oblong, 6–8 × 2.5–4 mm, apex acute; bracteoles orbicular or ovate, 6–7 × 4–5 mm, apex mucronate, margin membranous, sparsely ciliate. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 5 mm. Corolla bluish, 6 – 8 mm, outside slightly pilose and glandular‑punctate; limb 2‑lipped, the upper lip shallowly dentate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ca. 7 mm. Stamens 2; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae subequal in size, lower theca has basal spur. Ovary 2‑locular; style ca. 1 cm, glabrous, stigma obtuse. Capsule ovoid ca. 6 mm, 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, ca. 1.5 mm wide, minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Parker, Cape D’ Aguilar, Po Toi Island. Y. W. Lam 1999; HK sheet 40867.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimens was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimens was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Rungia pectinata (L.) Nees 孩兒草
Prodr. 11: 470. 1847; FHN 3: 563. 1974; FRPS 20: 262. 2002.
Justicia pectinata L., Amoen. Acad. 4: 299. 1760.
Rungia parviflora var. pectinata (L.) Hand.‑Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 898. 1936.
Rungia parviflora subsp. pectinata (L.) Cramer, Handbook Fl. Ceylon 12: 105. 1998.

Annual or perennial herbs, sometimes erect but usually prostrate and rooting at nodes. Stems many‑branched, minutely pubescent. Petioles 0–7 mm; leaf blades oblong‑elliptic, 1–4 × 0.4–1.4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous except for few hairs on veins, lateral veins ca. 4 pairs. Spikes axillary or terminal, 0.5–2 cm, 1‑sided, sometimes 2 or 3 compounded. Bracts dimorphic, outer sterile bracts elliptic, apex obtuse or rounded, green, ca. 4 × 0.7 mm, apex acute, glabrous, inner fertile bracts broadly ovate to orbicular, 4–5 × 2 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, mucronulate, pubescent, broadly hyaline‑margined; bracteoles elliptic, 2–3 mm, subacute, margin ciliate, apex 2‑fid. Calyx colourless, pubescent, lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 0.5 mm, narrowly hyaline‑margined, apex mucronulate. Corolla blue or white, ca. 5 mm, outside pubescent, upper lip ovate, 1–2 mm, emarginate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes triangular. Stamens 2; filaments glabrous; anther‑thecae superposed, lower one spurred at base. Ovary 2‑locular. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 2.5 mm, apiculate, glabrous, 2– 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, ca. 1 mm in diam., minutely verrucose.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Sai Kung, Tseng Kwan O, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 9654; Y. W. Lam 1724; S. Y. Hu 12433 (K).
Distribution: S & SW China; India, Bhutan, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ruppia maritima L. 川蔓藻
Sp. Pl. 127. 1753; FKH 291. 1912; FRPS 8: 83. 1992; FGD 6: 307. 2005; FOC 23: 118. 2010.
Ruppia rostellata W.D.J. Koch ex Rchb., Iconogr. Bot., Ic. Pl. Crit. 2: 66, t. 174, fig. 306. 1824; FHN 4: 65. 1977.

Submersed herb. Stems slender, milk-yellow, angulate, muchbranched, 60–100 cm, internodes 1–6 cm. Leaves linear 2–10 cm × 0.3–0.5 mm, basally with membranous winged-sheath; sheath 2–10 × 0.4 mm, auricle rotund-obtuse, apex acuminate or acute, 1-veined. Spikes 2–4 cm, 2-flowered, exserted out sheath after flowering; peduncle 10–18 mm, not spirally twisted in fruiting. Stamens 2. Carpels 4–6; ovary long-neck bottle-like, asymmetric; stigma umbonate. Drupelets 4–6, ovate-rotund, 2 × 1.5 mm, with straight or slightly curved short beak, stalk 5–17 mm.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung, Mai Po. HK sheet 7778, 39602, 42835.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning, Gansu, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Taiwan; temperate and subtropical sea area and salt lakes.
Ecology: Coastal lagoons, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Russelia equisetiformis Schltr. & Cham. 爆仗竹
Linnaea 6: 377. 1831; L. H. Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 899. 1949; FGZ 592. 1956.

Shrubs, 0.3–2 m tall, many‑branched and glabrous; branches verticillate, slender, green, rush‑like, striate, pendulous at top. Leaves small, ovate or linear‑lanceolate, less than 1.5 cm, mostly reduced to scales on branches. Flowers in racemose‑cymes; calyx light green, ovate or cup‑like, 3 mm; corolla scarlet, 2.5 cm, tube slightly expanded at top, lobes ovate or oblong‑ovate, ca. 3 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. H. C. Tang 191; Y. S. Lau 1904, 2200.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China; native to Mexico.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ruta graveolens L. 芸香（臭草）
Sp. Pl. 1: 383. 1753; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 550, fig. 2829. 1972; FHN 3: 36, fig. 547. 1974; FGD 2: 246, fig. 161. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 89, pl. 20. 1997.

Perennial herb, to 1 m tall. Leaves bipinnate to tripinnate, 6–12 cm; leaflets shortly spathulate or narrowly oblong, 5–30 × 2–5 mm, greyish green or bluish green. Flowers golden yellow, ca. 2 cm in diam. Calyx lobes 4. Petals 4. Stamens 8. Ovary usually 4-locular, ovules many per locule. Fruit 6–10 mm, dehiscing from apex to middle; pericarp with many glandular-glands. Seeds many, reniform, ca. 1.5 mm, brownish black.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 197; HK sheet 4266.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River (occasionally cultivated); native to Mediterranean region.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), medicinal (folklore).

Sabia limoniacea Wall. ex Hook. f. & Thoms. 檸檬清風藤
Fl. Ind. 1: 210. 1855; Benth., FHK 70. 1861; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 93. 1985.
Sabia limoniacea Wall. ex Hook. f. & Thoms. var. ardisioides L. Chen, Sargentia 3: 58. 1943.

Evergreen woody climber, up to 10 m, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.5–2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong-elliptic or ovate-elliptic to lanceolate, 7–15 × 4–6 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex short-acuminate or acute; lateral veins 6–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes 2–4-flowered, solitary, subtended by a leafy bract, or arranged in a long and narrow panicle up to 15 cm. Pedicels 1–3 mm. Sepals 5, ovate or oblong-ovate, 0.5–1 mm, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous, ciliolate. Petals 5, pale green, obovate or elliptic ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex rounded. Stamens 5; filaments flattened; anthers introrse. Ovary glabrous. Drupes globose to obovoid, strongly compressed.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 1; Y. W. Lam 1379.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, SW Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, Myanmar, N India, Thailand, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests, climbing on trees or rocks. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.; fruiting: Jan.–May of the following year.

Sabia swinhoei Hemsl. ex Forb. & Hemsl. 尖葉清風藤
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 144. 1886; FRPS 47(1): 89. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 3: 614, pl. 315. 1993.
Sabia gracilis Hemsl., Hook. Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2831. 1907.
Sabia swinhoei Hemsl. var. hainanensis L. Chen, Sargentia 3: 44. 1943.

Evergreen woody climber or scandent shrub, up to 6 m. Branchlets pubescent or tomentose. Leaves papery to thin leathery; petioles 3–5 mm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic, ovate-elliptic, ovate or broadly ovate, 5–12 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate or abruptly and shortly acuminate to acute, adaxially glabrous but pubescent on midvein when young, abaxially all over laxly or densely pubescent, glabrescent in age; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, straight or curved, anastomosing at a distance of 5–8 mm from the margin. Cymes 2–7-flowered, axillary, sparsely pubescent or tomentose, 1.5–2.5 cm. Peduncles 0.7–1.5 cm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Sepals 5, ovate, 1–1.5 mm, ciliate or not, with inconspicuous red dots abaxially. Petals 5, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3.5 –6 × 1–1.5 mm, light green. Stamens 5, 1–1.6 mm; filaments slightly flattened; anthers ellipsoid, often inflexed, introrse. Ovary glabrous; style 0.3–0.75 mm. Dupes more or less obovoid and compressed, 7–9 × 6–8 mm, blue or dark blue in fresh.

Locality: Mount Parker, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 9865; Y. W. Lam 1437; K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 39787).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.– Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Saccharum arundinaceum Retz. 斑茅（大密）
Observ. Bot. 4: 14. 1786; FKH 319. 1912; FHN 4: 450. 1977; FFJ 6: 250, fig. 218. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 43. 1997; FOC 22: 579. 2006; FGD 9: 458. 2009.

Perennial stout herb. Culms erect, 2–4 m tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, pilose at mouth and margins; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, (60–)100–200 × 1–2.5 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface with long soft hairs on the base, base narrowing, apex acuminate, margins serrate scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous, truncate. Panicle large and dense, axis glabrous; rachis internode 3–6 mm, pilose with long silky hairs. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate, callus small, with hairs ca. 1 mm; glumes subequal, lower glume thinly cartilaginous, abaxial surface with silky hairs twice length of spikelet, 2-keeled; upper glume boat-shaped, upper margins ciliate, 3(–5)-veined; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, subequal to glumes; upper lemma lanceolate, apex mucronate or with awn to 3 mm. Lodicules glabrous. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet; pedicel 3–3.5 mm, with long silk hairs, apex slightly swollen.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2481; HK sheet 42034.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, rivers and stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control), animal food.

Saccharum fallax Balansa 金貓尾
J. Bot. (Morot). 4: 80. 1890; FYN 9: 604, fig. 102: 9–11. 2003; FOC 22: 581. 2006.
Narenga fallax (Balansa) Bor, Kew Bull. 3: 162. 1948; FHN 4: 449. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 37, pl. 8. 1997; FGD 9: 459, fig. 238. 2009; Check List HK Plants 341. 2002; 119. 2004.

Perennial stout herb. Culms erect, 1.5–3 m tall, nodes bearded with golden-brown hairs, hirsute below panicle. Leaf sheaths usually longer than internode, margin brown-hirsute, nodes with yellow pilose; leaf blades stiff, 40–80 × 1–1.5 cm, uppermost usually very small, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose, base narrowed, apex acuminate, margins scabrid; ligule ca. 1.5 mm, thicken membranous. Panicle loosely oblong in outline, 30–60 cm, axis golden or ferruginous brown pilose, bearded at nodes, many branches per node, branches ascending, primary branches sparsely branched in lower part; racemes flexuosely ascending, densely spiculate; rachis internode and pedicel apex slightly swollen, ciliate. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm; callus hairs a little shorter than spikelet, brown; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, papery and becoming herbaceous toward apex, abaxially with brown hairs, apex narrowly truncate; upper glume boat-shaped, 3-veined; lower lemma lanceolate, slightly shorter than glumes, margins ciliate; upper lemma oblong, 1/2 length of glume, obtuse and awnless or minutely mucronate, varying to shortly 2-toothed and awned from sinus; upper palea small; anthers 3.

Locality: Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 3015.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, Myanmar, NE India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Saccharum officinarum L. 甘蔗
Sp. Pl. 1: 54. 1753; FHK 419. 1861; FKH 319. 1912; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 327. 1971; FHN 4: 450. 1977; FFJ 6: 250. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 41. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 574. 2000; FOC 22: 579. 2006; FGD 9: 458. 2009.

Perennial stout herb. Culms 2–4(–6) m tall, white ciliate below inflorescence, lower internode shorten and swollen. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, glabrous, imbricate, pilose at mouth; leaf blades 70–150 × 4–6 cm, usually glabrous, midrib large and white, margins sharply serrate; ligule 2 mm, membranous, truncate. Panicle dense, very large, up to 50 cm; rachis internode pubescent. Spikelets paired, one sessile, other pedicellate; callus hairs 2–3 times length of spikelet; lower glume oblong, subpapery, 2-keeled, margins membranous; upper glume boat-shaped, 3–5-veined, acute; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, obscurely 1-veined, acute; upper lemma small, awnless or absent, palea lanceolate; stamens 3; lodicules glabrous. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet; pedicel 3–4 mm, glabrous, apex slightly swollen.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in warm regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Food (sugar, alcohol, beverage base).

Saccharum spontaneum L. 甜根子草
Mant. Pl. 2: 183. 1771; FKH 319. 1912; FHN 4: 451, fig. 1240. 1977; FFJ 6: 251, fig. 219. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 40, pl. 9: 1 – 6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 574, pl. 242. 2000; FOC 22: 578. 2006; FGD 9: 457. 2009.

Perennial herb, with long rhizomes. Culms erect, 1–4 m tall, softly pilose below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths pilose at mouth and margin; leaf blades linear, 30–60 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous, tapering to midrib at base, apex acuminate, margins serrate; ligule brown, ca. 2 mm, membranous, apex obtuse, shortly ciliate. Inflorescence a large panicle of about 20 cm; branches erect, rachis and pedicels slender, rachis internodes slightly swollen at apex, pilose with long silky hairs. Spikelets paired, 3–5 mm; callus hairs 3–4 times length of spikelet; lower glume lanceolate, 2-keeled, the upper slightly membranous, margins ciliate; upper glume boat-shaped, keel and margins ciliate, acuminate; lower lemma lanceolate, subequal to glumes, acute, fringed at the apex; upper lemma linear or linear-oblong, awnless; lodicules obovate, ca. 1 mm, ciliate; anthers 3. Pedicellate spikelet similar to the sessile, pedicel 2.5–3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3095; HK sheet 8394, 15150.
Distribution: Widely distributed in the warmer regions of Old World.
Ecology: Hillslopes, rivers and stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Sacciolepis indica (L.) Chase 囊穎草（滑草）
Proc. Biol. Soc. Washington. 21: 8. 1908; FHN 4: 410. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 224, pl. 68: 1–7. 1990; FFJ 6: 199, fig. 166. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 509, pl. 212. 2000; FOC 22: 511. 2006; FGD 9: 410, fig. 211. 2009.
Aira indica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 63. 1753.
Panicum indicum auct. non Mill.: FHK 413. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms usually tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 20–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, slightly keeled, shorter than internode, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose; leaf blades linear, flat to slightly involute, 5–20 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or hairy, base slightly narrow, apex acute; ligule membranous, 0.2–0.5 mm, pubescent. Panicle spike-like, 10–16 × 0.3–0.5 cm. Spikelets green or purplish green, ovate-lanceolate, laterally compressed, 2–3 mm, glabrous or papillose-hispid; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, usually 3-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, dorsally gibbous, 7–11-veined; lower lemma as long as upper glume, usually 9-veined; palea small and absent, hyaline; upper lemma yellowish, narrowly ovate, 1/2 length of spikelet, smooth and glossy. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1867; K. L. Yip 4039; HK sheet 35849.
Distribution: Widely spread over E, S, SW and C China; Bhutan, India, Japan, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, Africa, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Margins of paddy fields and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Sageretia thea (Osbeck) Johnst. 雀梅藤
J. Arnold Arbor. 49: 377. 1968; FRPS 48(1): 12. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 3: 691. 1993; FGD 4: 257. 2000.
Rhamnus thea Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 232. 1757.
Rhamnus theezans L., Mant. Pl. 207. 1771.
Sageretia theezans (L.) Brongn., Ann. Sci. Nat. (Paris), 10: 360. 1826; FHK 68. 1861; FKH 63. 1912.

Scandent or diffuse shrub, 1–2 m tall. Young shoots tawny tomentose, glabrescent in age; side-branches often converted into or ending in a thorn. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles 2–7 mm, tomentose; leaf blade ovate to elliptic or oblong, 1–4 × 0.7–2.5 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute or rounded, margin serrulate, glabrous and shining adaxially, initially ± tomentose abaxially. Spikes paniculate; rachis up to 15 cm, branches 2–5 cm, both densely tomentose. Flowers sessile. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, deeply 5-lobed; lobes triangular. Petals white, spathulate, laterally involute, embracing the stamens. Ovary 3-locular; style short, entire or 3-cleft. Drupe subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1224, 2337; Y. S. Lau 163.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina to India.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.; fruiting: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental, beverage (substitute of tea).

Sagina japonica (Sw.) Ohwi 漆姑草
J. Jap. Bot. 13: 438. 1937; FGD 2: 77. 1991; FRPS 26: 255, pl. 61: 5 –7. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 362, pl. 168. 1996; FOC 6: 10. 2001.
Spergula japonica Sw., Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Neue Schriften 3: 164. 1801.
Sagina linnaei auct. non Presl: FKH 40. 1912.

Annual smalll herb, 5 –20 cm tall. Stems tufted, ± diffuse, sparsely glandular hairy on the upper part. Leaves sessile, linear, 5–20 × 0.8–1.5 mm, apex acute, connate at base, glabrous. Flowers small, solitary, terminal or in axils of apical leaves. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm, sparsely pubescent. Sepals 5, ovate-elliptic, ca. 2 mm. Petals 5, white, narrowly ovate, slightly shorter than sepals, apex rounded, entire. Stamens 5, shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; styles 5, linear. Capsule ovoid, slightly longer than the persistent sepals, opening to the middle into 5 valves.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Sunset Peak. W. J. Tutcher 4620; Y. W. Lam 1771; HK sheet 31558.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Indian subcontinent; naturalized elsewhere in temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, grassy banks. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: May–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sagittaria guayanensis Kunth subsp. lappula (D. Don) Bogin 冠果草
Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 2: 192. 1955; FHN 4: 61. 1977; FRPS 8: 129. 1992; FGD 9: 156. 2009; FOC 23: 85. 2010.
Sagittaria lappula D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 22. 1825.
Lophotocarpus guayanensis (H. B. & K.) J. G. Sm., Rep. Miss. Bot. Gard. 4: 35. 1895; FKH 290. 1912.
Lophotocarpus formosanus Hayata, Ic. Pl. Form. 5: 249. 1915; FTW 5: 10. 1978.
Sagittaria cordifolia Roxb., Fl. Ind. 2: 647. 1824; FHK 346. 1861.

Perennial floating herb, stolons lacking. Submersed leaves linear or lanceolate, or petiole-like; floating leaves ovate or broadly ovate, 2–6 × 1–4 cm, base deeply cordate, apex obtuse; veins 4–8 forward, 3–6 backward; petioles 10–20 cm or more. Scapes erect, 8–25 cm, extending out from water surface. Inflorescences racemose, 2–15 cm, 2–5-whorled, each whorl 2–3-flowered; flowers bisexual or unisexual, usually bisexual flowers in 1–3 whorls at lower part of inflorescences; male flowers on upper part. Sepals 3, ovate, 5–9 × 3–6 mm, persistent. Petals 3, white, base yellowish, nearly of same size as sepals, fugacious. Stamens 6 – many. Carpels many. Achenes obliquely oblong, 2–3 × 1.5–2.5 mm, tuberculate, with 1–3 lateral wings, margins irregularly and deeply lobed.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 752, 1277; Y. W. Lam 2229.
Distribution: SW to SE China; S & SE Asia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Sagittaria trifolia L. subsp. leucopetala (Miq.) Q. F. Wang 慈姑
FOC 23: 85. 2010.
Sagittaria trifolia L., Sp. Pl. 993. 1753.
Sagittaria sinensis Sims., Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 39: 163. 1814.
Sagittaria sagittifolia L. f. sinensis (Sims.) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 15(174): 105. 1901.
Sagittaria sagittifolia L. subsp. leucopetala (Miq.) Hartog, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 5: 332. 1957; FHN 4: 62. 1977; R. Haynes, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 358. 2001.
Sagittaria trifolia L. var. sinense (Sims.) Makino, Ill. Fl. Nippon 886, pl. 2657. 1940; FRPS 8: 133. 1992; FGD 9: 157. 2009.
Sagittaria sagittifolia auct. non. L.: FKH 290. 1912.

Perennial herb, emersed, stoloniferous; tuber ovoid-globular or globular, 5–7 cm. Leaves long-petiolate; blades sagittate, central lobe ovate to broadly ovate, 9–16 cm, 5–7-veined, apex central lobe, lateral lobes usually longer than central lobe. Scapes 40–70 cm. Racemes sometimes 1–3-branched at base; female flowers, on lower 1–8 whorls, pedicels 1–2 cm; male flowers with longer pedicels, on the upper part. Sepals ovate, 6–8 mm, reflexed. Petals white, twice as large as sepals. Stamens many, anthers yellow. Achenes obliquely obovate, 4 × 3 mm, winged, shortly beaked. Seeds brown.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 11240; Y. S. Lau 750, 2619.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Asia.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Food (tuber).

Salix babylonica L. 垂柳
Sp. Pl. 1017. 1753; Schneid., Pl. Wils. 3: 42. 1916; FGZ 378. 1956; FRPS 20(2): 138. 1984.

Deciduous tree, to 10 m tall, with slender pendulous branches; young shoots slightly silky, soon glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles (3–)5–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 8–16 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex long-acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous, adaxially dark green, abaxially greyish green. Catkins short-stalked: male 1.5–2(–3) cm, female 2–3(–5) cm; bracts scale-like, villous at base; ovary sessile or nearly so, glabrous; style very short; stigmas oblong, 2-lobed; gland about 1/3 as long as ovary.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2942; S. P. Lau 105; HK sheet 26653.
Distribution: Widely distributed in Yellow River and Changjiang River basin.
Ecology: Usually planted in gardens, by streams, on banks of ponds. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.

Salomonia cantoniensis Lour. 齒果草（莎蘿莽）
Fl. Cochinch. 14. 1790; FHK 44. 1861; FKH 38. 1912; FHN 1: 363. 1964; FYN 3: 290, pl. 83: 1 – 4. 1983; FFJ 3: 163, fig. 118. 1987; FGD 2: 50. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 199. 1997; C. A. Pendry, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 521. 2001.
Salomonia cantoniensis Lour. var. edentula (DC.) C. Y. Wu, Fl. Yunnan. 3: 291. 1983.
Salomonia edentula DC., Prodr. 1: 334. 1824.

Annual erect herb, 5–25 cm tall. Stem much branched, narrowly winged, glabrous. Petioles 1–2 mm; leaf blade membranous, ovate-cordate or cordate, 4–20 × 3–14 mm, base ± cordate, apex obtuse or mucronate, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous on both surfaces, 3-veined. Spike 1–6 cm; bracts caducous, very small. Flowers very small, 2–3 mm, sessile. Sepals 5, persistent, linear-subulate, 0.4–0.5 mm, base connate, persistent. Petals pale red; lateral ones ca. 2.5 mm; keel broadly ovate, ca. 3 mm. Filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers connate. Ovary reniform, ca. 1 mm in diam.; style ca. 2.5 mm; stigma slightly lobed. Capsule reniform, ca. 1 × 2 mm, both lateral margins shortly triangular-denticulate. Seeds 2, black, shiny, ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Ta Ti Yan, Wu Kau Teng, Lung Tsai, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1995; Y. S. Lau 385, 1616.
Distribution: E, C, S & SW China; Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Salomonia ciliata (L.) DC. 橢圓葉齒果草（睫毛齒果草）
Prodr. 1: 334. 1824; FHN 1: 365. 1964; C. A. Pendry, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 522. 2001.
Salomonia oblongifolia DC., Prodr. 1: 334. 1824; FHK 44. 1861; FKH 38. 1912; FTW 3: 560, fig. 728. 1977; FYN 3: 291, pl. 83: 5 –7. 1983; FFJ 3: 164. 1987; FGD 2: 49, fig. 34: 1 – 3. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 200, pl. 47: 5 – 7. 1997.
Polygala ciliata L., Sp. Pl. 1: 705. 1753.

Annual erect herb, 8–30 cm tall. Stem slender, branched or not, subglabrous. Leaves sessile; leaf blade membranous, elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 4–12 × 1–3 mm, base subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire, mucronate, glabrous, basally 3-veined. Spike 2–10 cm; bracts linear, ca. 1 mm, persistent. Flowers small, ca. 2.5 mm. Sepals 5, green, lanceolate-ovate, subequal, 1–1.2 mm, connate at base, apex acuminate, sparsely ciliate, persistent. Petals purplish red, lateral ones subelliptic, ca. 2 mm, proximal 1/2 connate; keel 3 mm, apex rounded. Filaments shorter than petals. Ovary subreniform; style linear, ca. 2 mm. Capsule compressed, reniform or obtriangular, ca. 2 mm in diam., apex retuse, margin 2-seriate filiform denticulate. Seeds 2, black, shiny, ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9964.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as Salomonia oblongifolia DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 193. 2002; 69. 2004).

Salomonia elongata (Blume) Kurz ex Koord. 寄生鱗葉草
Exhursionsfl. Java 2: 453. 1912; FYN 3: 291, pl. 83: 5 – 7. 1983; FRPS 43(3): 202. 1997.
Epirixanthes aphylla (Griff.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 13(3): 142. 1918.
Epirixanthes elongata Blume, Catalogus 82. 1823; FHN 1: 364. 1964; FGD 2: 51, fig. 35. 1991.
Salomonia aphylla Griff., Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. 1: 221. 1844; FKH 38. 1912.

Annual parasitic herb, echlorophyllous, 5–16 cm tall. Stem simple or branched, pink, sulcate and ridged, subglabrous. Leaves scale-like, ca. 2 mm, pubescent. Spike unbranched, 5–25 mm. Flowers minute, 1–1.5 mm; bracts persistent, basal, linear-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 mm. Sepals 5, distinct, imbricate, ovate-lanceolate, 0.5–1 mm. Petals 3, pink; central one larger, obovate, 1–1.5 mm, lateral ones smaller. Stamens 4–5; filaments united and forming a sheath, adnate to petals at base; anthers sessile, free. Capsule heart-shaped, ca. 1 mm wide, less than 1 mm long, margin without spines or denticulations. Seeds 2, black, ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm in diam., slightly rugose.

Locality: Mount Violet, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng. P. S. Choi 548; F. W. Xing 8077; HK sheet 33867.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Salvia chinensis Benth. 華鼠尾草
Labiat. Gen. Spec. 725. 1835; FRPS 66: 181, pl. 45: 1 – 5. 1977; FOC 17: 219. 1994; FGD 3: 431, fig. 272. 1995.

Annual herbs, 20–60 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate at base, pubescent. Leaves simple or 3‑foliolate toward stem base; petiole very short or up to 7 cm, villous; leaf blade of simple leaves ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 1.3–7 × 0.8–4.5 cm, base cordate to rounded, apex obtuse or acute, margin crenate or obtusely serrate, pubescent along veins on both surfaces; terminal leaflet 2.5–7.5 cm, petiolule 0.5–1.7 cm. Verticillasters 6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes or panicles of 5–24 cm, pubescent; bracts lanceolate. Pedicel 1.5–2 mm. Calyx campanulate, purple, veins villous; tube 4–4.5 mm, throat densely hirsute annulate; upper lip ± semicircular, ca. 1.5 × 3 mm, apex 3‑mucronate; lower lip longer than upper lip, ca. 2 × 3 mm; teeth narrowly triangular, apex acuminate. Corolla blue‑purple or purple, ca. 1 cm, pubescent; tube ca. 6.5 mm, pilose annulate inside; upper lip oblong, ca. 3.5 × 3.3 mm, spreading; lower lip ca. 5 × 7 mm, middle lobe obcordate, curved downward, ca. 4 × 7 mm, margin crenulate, apex emarginate; lateral lobes semiorbicular, ca. 1.3 mm wide. Stamens nearly exserted. Nutlets brown, ellipsoidal‑ovoid, ca. 1.5 × 0.8 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Kellet, Mount Nicholson, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 380, 2601; Y. W. Lam 1579.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillsides. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Salvia coccinea Buc'hoz ex Etlinger 朱唇
De Salvia 23. 1777; FRPS 66: 174. 1977; FOC. 17: 217. 1994; FGD 3: 436. 1995.

Annual or biennial herbs. Stems erect, to 70 cm, covered with spreading and recurved hairs. Leaves simple; petiole 0.5 – 2 cm; leaf blade ovate to triangular‑ovate, 2–5 × 1.5–4 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex acute, margin serrate or obtusely serrate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially grey minutely tomentose. Verticillasters 4–many‑flowered, forming terminal, interrupted racemes; bracts ovate, apex caudate‑acuminate, margin ciliate. Pedicel 2–3 mm, white pilose. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 7–9 mm, finely pubescent, intermixed with yellowish glands; upper lip ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, ciliolate, apex mucronate; lower lip nearly as long as upper, deeply 2‑toothed. Corolla scarlet or deep red, 2–2.3 cm, pubescent abaxially; tube ca. 1.6 cm; upper lip shorter than lower lip; lower lip ca. 7 mm. Stamens exserted; filaments ca. 4 mm; connectives ca. 1.5 mm, slender. Nutlets yellow‑brown with blackish spots, obovoid, 1.5–2.5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 22372.
Distribution: S & C USA, Mexico, S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Ornamental

Salvia japonica Thunb. 鼠尾草
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 72. 1784; FKH 210. 1912; FRPS 66: 179. 1977; FOC 17: 219. 1994; FGD 3: 432. 1995.
Salvia fortunei Benth., Prodr. 12: 354. 1848; FHK 277. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 4: 523, pl. 235. 1998.

Annual herbs, 40–60 cm tall. Stems obtusely quadrangular, sparsely villous on angles or subglabrous. Leaves 1– 3‑pinnate; petiole 7 –9 cm; leaf blade 6–13 × 5–9 cm, pilose or glabrous; upper stem leaves 1‑pinnate, short petiolate; terminal leaflet lanceolate or rhombic, to 10 × 3.5 cm, base cuneate; lateral leaflets subsessile, ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–5 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base obliquely rounded, margin obtusely serrate. Verticillasters 2 – 6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes or panicles; rachis densely glandular pilose or pilose; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, 2–5 mm, glabrous. Pedicel 1–1.5 mm, pubescent. Calyx tubular, 4–6 mm, sparsely glandular pilose, hairy annulate on throat inside, 2‑lipped to 1/3 of its length; upper lip triangular or nearly semicircular, ca. 2 × 3 mm; teeth narrowly triangular, apex long acuminate. Corolla reddish, purplish, bluish, to white, ca. 1.2 cm, densely villous; tube obliquely pilose annulate inside, ca. 9 mm, exserted, ca. 2 mm wide at base, to 3.5 mm wide at throat; upper lip elliptic to ovate, ca. 2.5 × 2 mm; lower lip ca. 3 × 4 mm, margin crenulate. Stamens exserted; filaments ca. 1 mm; connectives ca. 6 mm, straight or slightly curved. Nutlets brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 1.7 × 0.5 mm.

Locality: D’Aguilar Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2522; D. P. M. Guile 1185; Y. W. Lam 1653.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Hillsides, thickets, margins of forests. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.

Salvia plebeia R. Br. 荔枝草（雪見草）
Prodr. 501. 1810; FHK 277. 1861; FKH 210. 1912; FRPS 66: 168, pl. 39: 5 – 9. 1977; FOC 17: 216. 1994; FGD 3: 437, fig. 273. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 527, pl. 238. 1998.

Annual or biennial herbs, with thick tap root. Stems erect, 20–60(–90) cm tall, many‑branched, grey pilose or glabrescent. Leaves simple; petiole 4–15 mm; leaf blade elliptic‑ovate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 2–6 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base rounded to cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin crenate, dentate, or serrate, sparsely hirsute adaxially, finely pilose and sparsely yellow‑brown glandular abaxially. Verticillasters 4 – 6‑flowered, numerous, often forming terminal and axillary panicles. Bracts small, linear‑lanceolate. Pedicels 1 – 2 mm, hairy. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm (2.7 mm in fruit), sparsely pilose and yellow‑brown glandular, 2‑lipped; upper lip obtuse, often shortly 3‑fid at the tip; lower lip deeply 2‑toothed, teeth triangular. Corolla reddish, purplish, purple, blue‑purple, to blue, rarely white, 3–4 mm; tube glabrous, hairy annulate inside; upper lip oblong, obtuse, densely puberulent; lower lip 3‑lobed, the middle lobe largest, broadly obovate. Stamens slightly exserted; filaments ca. 1.5 mm; connectives ca. 1.5 mm, arcuate, arms subequal. Nutlets obovoid, 0.4–0.6 mm in diam., brown, rugose.

Locality: Mui Tsz Lam, Fanling, Kuk Po. W. J. Tutcher 9177; Y. W. Lam 520; HK sheet 38878.
Distribution: Widely spread over all provinces except Gansu, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Xizang; Afghanistan, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Russia, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Farmlands, margins of forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Salvia splendens Ker‑Gawl. 一串紅
Bot. Reg. 8: t. 687. 1822; FRPS 66: 172. 1977; FOC 17. 217. 1994; FGD 3: 436. 1995.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect, 50–90 cm tall. Leaves simple; petiole 3–4.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ovate to triangular‑ovate, 2.5–7 × 2–4.5 cm, base truncate or ± rounded, apex acuminate, margin serrate, glabrous, abaxially glandular. Verticillasters 2–6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes to 20 cm, all parts scarlet; bracts ovate, enveloping flowers in bud, apex caudate‑acuminate. Pedicel 4–7 mm, glandular villous. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1.6 cm in flower, dilated to 2 cm after anthesis, veins villous, 2‑lipped to ca. 1/3 of its length; upper lip triangular‑ovate, 5–6 mm, apex mucronate; lower lip slightly longer than upper, deeply 2‑toothed, teeth triangular. Corolla 4–4.2 cm, pubescent; tube slightly dilated at throat; upper lip straight, somewhat concave, oblong, 8–9 mm; lower lip shorter than upper. Filaments ca. 5 mm; connectives ca. 1.3 cm. Nutlets dark brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm, apex irregularly pleated, margin (or midvein) narrowly winged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1877; HK sheet 22452.
Distribution: Native to Brasil, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The corolla is purple or even white in different varieties.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The corolla is purple or even white in different varieties.

Sambucus chinensis Lindl. 接骨草
Trans. Hort. Soc. Lond. 6: 297. 1826; FRPS 72: 6, pl. 1: 3 – 5. 1988; FGD 4: 291, fig. 173.
Sambucus javanica auct. non Reinw. ex Blume: FKH 121. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 1–2 m tall. Stems striate; pith white. Stipules becoming glands or leaf‑like. Leaves imparipinnate; petioles 3–5 cm; leaflets opposite, 3–9, elliptic‑lanceolate, 8–15 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate or suborbicular, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, slightly asymmetric, glabrous or lepidoid hairy only on midvein, with glands on teeth near base. Compound umbel large, 10–30 cm in diam. Peduncles with leaf‑like involucrate bract. Flowers many, white, sometimes with cup‑like sterile flowers. Calyx‑tube campanulate, 1.5 mm; lobes deltoid, shorter than the tube. Corolla‑tube short; lobes ovate, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens as long as corolla. Anthers yellow or purple. Ovary 3‑locular, styles very short; stigma 3‑fid. Drupes red, subglobose, 3–4 mm in diam., pyrenes ovate, ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Shouson Hill, Bowen Rd., Sai Kung (Tai Long), Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9611; Y. S. Lau 2003, 2293.
Distribution: Areas of Qinling Range, westward to Gansu, S Qinghai and Xizang.
Ecology: Brick rubbish and ruins, streamsides, margins of forests. Flowering: May.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sanchezia parvibracteata Sprague & Hutch. 小苞黃脈爵床
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1908: 253. 1908; FRPS 70: 275. 2002.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall. Young stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous. Petioles 1–2 cm, pubescent, soon glabrescent; leaf blades oblong, 7–20 × 3–9 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin undulate, entire or serrulate, adaxially glabrous, cystoliths numerous, yellow along the midvein and lateral veins, abaxially pale green, densely pubescent when young, then soon glabrescent or sparsely pilose along veins, lateral veins 8–12 pairs. Inflorescence of terminal dichasia spikes, 4–12 cm long. Peduncles 1–2.5 cm. Rachis quadrangular, sparsely pubescent. Bracts red or orange, ovate, 1–2.5 × 0.6–0.8 cm, apex acute, glabrous, abaxially densely covered with cystoliths; bracteoles ovate‑elliptic, 1.3–1.5 × 0.3–0.4 cm, glabrous, abaxially densely covered with acerose cystoliths, 3‑veined. Calyx ca. 1.5 cm, 5‑lobed almost to the base, lobes oblanceolate, unequal, 1–2 mm wide, apex obtuse, glabrous except for pilose upward, abaxially densely covered with cystoliths. Corolla yellow or orange, 4 – 5 cm, outside densely white pilose, tube 3.5–4.5 cm × 7–8 mm, lobes recoiled, 2–3 mm long. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 5 cm long, pubescent; anther thecae mucronate for ca. 1 mm at base. Staminodes 2, unequal, 2–2.3 cm long. Ovary ovoid, ca. 4 mm long; style 5–6 cm long, pilose towards the base; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal, the larger ca. 3 mm long, smaller ca. 0.5 mm. Capsule 1.1–1.4 cm long, glabrous except for pilose at the tip.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Y. Chan 1337 (CHUK); S. Y. Hu 5495 (CUHK).
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to Ecuador, widely cultivated in tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The plant was identified as Sanchezia nobilis Hook. previously but Sanchzia parvibracteata has much larger bracts than that species.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The plant was identified as Sanchezia nobilis Hook. previously but Sanchzia parvibracteata has much larger bracts than that species.

Sanicula lamelligera Hance 薄片變豆菜
J. Bot. Brit. & For. 16: 11. 1878; FRPS 55(1): 48, pl. 20. 1979; FGD 2: 330, fig. 218. 1991; FOC 14: 21. 2005.

Perennial herb, glabrous; stems erect, 2–7-tufted, scapiform, 5–20 cm tall. Basal leaves several; petioles 5–15 cm, sheathing at base; leaf blade cordate-suborbicular, 2–5 × 3–9 cm, palmately 3-parted, often purplish red abaxially; central segment cuneate-obovate or rhombic-ovate, usually 2–3-lobed, base cuneate, margin irregularly and coarsely spinulate-toothed; cauline leaves small, 3-lobed, or undivided, sometimes wanting. Umbels 2–3-branched; peduncles 2–5 cm; involucres few, linear; umbellules 4–7-flowered. Staminate flowers 3–6; pedicels 1–2 mm; calyx-teeth persistent, about 1 mm; petals white, ovate, with narrow inflexed apices. Style of perfect flower slender, reflexed, twice as long as the calyx. Fruit oblong-ovoid to ovoid, ca. 2.5 × 2 mm, densely spined; carpels terete in cross section. Vittae 5 in carpel. Seed-face plane.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1742; P. S. Choi 212; Y. W. Lam 1440.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Damp and shady places in ravines and forests. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sansevieria trifasciata Prain 虎尾蘭
Beng. Pl. 2: 1054. 1903; FGZ 709. 1956; FRPS 14: 278, pl. 51: 1. 1980; FGD 9: 215, fig. 123. 2009.

Leaves basal, often 1–2, sometimes 3–6, erect, thickly leathery, flat, linear-lanceolate, 30–70(–120) × 3–5(–8) cm, with transverse green stripes, margin green, gradually attenuate toward base and forming sulcate petiole. Inflorescence 30 – 80 cm, with pale brown membranous sheath at base. Flowers pale green or white, 3 – 8 in clusters, arranged in racemes; pedicel 5–8 mm, articulate in middle; perianth 1.6–2.8 cm, tube nearly as long as lobes. Berries 7–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28222, 38594.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to W Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species is widely cultivated in parks and gardens of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: This species is widely cultivated in parks and gardens of Hong Kong.

Sapindus saponaria L. 無患子（木患子）
Sp. Pl. 1: 367. 1753.
Sapindus mukorossi Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 342. 1788; FKH 66. 1912; FTW 3: 592. 1977; FRPS 47(1): 14, pl. 4. 1985; FFJ 3: 316, fig. 214. 1987; FGD 1: 241, fig. 266. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 3: 281. 1993.
Sapindus abruptus Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 238. 1790.

Deciduous tree, to 20 m tall. Bark greyish brown or blackish brown; young branches green, glabrous. Leaves alternate, including petiole 25–45 cm or longer, axes slightly flat, grooved adaxially, glabrous or pilosulose; leaflets 5–8 pairs, usually subopposite; petiolule ca. 5 mm; blades thinly papery, narrowly elliptic-lanceolate or slightly falcate, 7–15 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate, slightly asymmetrical, apex acute or shortly acuminate, shining adaxially, glabrous or pilosulose abaxially; lateral veins ca. 15–17 pairs, nearly parallel, slender. Inflorescences terminal, conical. Flowers actinomorphic, small. Pedicels very short. Sepals ovate or oblong-ovate, larger ones ca. 2 mm, abaxially pilose at base. Petals 5, lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, abaxially villous at base or subglabrous, long clawed; scales 2, ear-like. Disk acetabuliform, glabrous. Stamens 8, exserted; filaments ca. 3.5 mm, densely villous below middle. Ovary glabrous. Fertile schizocarps orange, black when dry, subglobose, 2–2.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen, Lam Tsuen, Tai Om, Ng Tung Chai. W. J. Tutcher 7261; L. T. Lo 339.
Distribution: E, C, S & SW China; Japan, Korea, Indochina, India.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fruit as a substitute of soap.
records.uses: Medicinal (folklore), fruit as a substitute of soap.

records.text:
Sapium atrobadiomaculatum F. P. Metcalf 斑籽烏桕

Lingnan Sci. J. 10: 490. 1931; FRPS 44(3): 23. 1997; FGD 5: 126, fig. 77. 2003.


Shrub, 1–3 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves papery; petioles narrowly winged, with 2 glands at apex; stipules membranous, linear-lanceolate, 5–12 mm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or lanceolate, 3–9 × 5–3 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, entire, abaxially with 2 glands at the base of the limb; lateral veins 6–7 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 2–4 cm long, with 1–2 female flowers at the base and numerous male flowers on the upper part, or sometimes all male. Male flowers: 2–3 in axil of bracts; pedicels 1–2 mm; bracts ovate to lanceolate, 0.5–2 mm, sparsely serrulate, with 2 reniform glands at the base; calyx cup-shaped, 3-lobed, lobes broad-ovate, serrulate; stamens 2–3; anthers globose; filaments very short. Female flowers: pedicels 3–5 mm; bracts lanceolate, ca. 2 mm; calyx deeply 3-lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1 mm; ovary subglobose, ca. 3 mm in diam.; styles 3, connate at base. Capsules globose, 3-angled, ca. 1 cm in diam.; seeds globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., dark-brown maculate, without waxy aril.


Locality: Black's Link, Repulse Bay, Tai Tam Tuk, Beaufort Island, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 135, 263; S. P. Lau 167; S. Y. Hu 13779A (CUHK).

Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian.

Ecology: Thin forests, shrublands. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Notes: This species was reported as Excoecaria japonica Muell.-Arg. previously (FKH 241. 1912; Check List HK Plants 45. 1993).

Sapium discolor (Champ. ex Benth.) Müll. Arg. 山烏桕
Linnaea 32: 121. 1863; FKH 241. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 18. 1997; FGD 5: 128. 2003.
Stillingia discolor Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 1. 1856; FHK 303. 1861.

Small tree, 5–12 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves papery; petioles 2–7.5 cm, with 2 glands at apex; stipules small, subovate, ca. 1 mm.; leaf blade elliptic or oblong-ovate, 4–10 × 2.5 – 5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate, more or less glaucous abaxially; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 4–9 cm, with several female flowers at base, and many male flowers on upper part. Male flowers: 5–7 in axil of bracts; pedicels 1–3 mm; bracts ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1 mm; calyx cup-shaped, irregular-serrulate; stamens 2–3, filaments short, anthers globose. Female flowers: solitary in axil of bracts; pedicels ca. 5 mm; bracts as in male flowers; calyx 3-partite to base, lobes triangular, ca. 2 mm; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3, divided to the middle. Capsules black, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; seeds subglobose, 4–5 × 3 – 4 mm, covered with a very shiny layer of waxy aril.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also planted. H. C. Tang 340, 2174; Y. S. Lau 2203; S. Y. Hu 5347, 12017 (CUHK).
Distribution: Area S of Changjiang; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, India, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests and shrublands. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore).

Sapium sebiferum (L.) Roxb. 烏桕

Hort. Bengal. 69. 1814, & Fl. Ind. ed. 2, 3: 693. 1832; FKH 241. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 14, pl. 3: 1–4. 1997; FGD 5: 128. 2003.

Croton sebiferum L., Sp. Pl. 1004. 1753.

Stillingia sebifera (L.) Michx., Fl. Bor.-Amer. 2: 213. 1803; FHK 302. 1861.

Triadica sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 610. 1790.


Tree to 15 m tall, with milky juice; glabrous throughout. Leaves papery; petioles 2.5 – 6 cm, with 2 glands at apex; stipules ca. 1 mm; leaf blade rhomboid, rhomboid-ovate or rarely rhomboid-obovate, 3–8 × 3–9 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex sharply acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins 6 – 10 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 6 – 15 cm, with 1 – 4 female flowers at the base and male flowers on the upper part; pedicels slender, 1 – 3 mm; bracts broad-ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm, with 2 glands at the base. Male flowers: 6 or more in each cluster, very small and yellowish; calyx cup-shaped, shallowly 3-lobed, lobes obtuse, irregularly serrulate; stamens 2 – 3, exceeding the calyx, filaments free, nearly as long as the globose anthers. Female flowers: calyx 3-partite, lobes ovate or ovate-lanceolate; ovary ovoid-globose, smooth, 3-locular; styles 3, divided to the middle; stigmas recurved. Capsules pyriform-globose, black when mature, 1 – 1.5 cm in diam., 3-seeded; seeds oblate, ca. 8 × 6 – 7 mm, covered with white waxy aril.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also planted. Y. S. Lau 2710, 2752; S. P. Lau 185; S. Y. Hu 5508, 12032 (CUHK).

Distribution: Area S of the Yellow River; Japan, Vietnam, India, cultivated in Europe, America, Africa.

Ecology: Banks of streams and ditches, sparse forests near villages. Flowering: Apr. – Aug.; fruiting: Aug. – Nov.

Uses: Material (wax), food (oil/ fat), fuel (potential as petroleum substitute/ alcohol), ornamental.
records.uses: Material (wax), food (oil/ fat), fuel (potential as petroleum substitute/ alcohol), ornamental.

records.text:
Saraca dives Pierre 中國無憂花
Fl. For. Cochinch. 5: t. 386B. 1899; FRPS 39: 207, pl. 72: 1– 4. 1988; FGD 5: 198, fig. 113. 2003; FGX 2: 489, pl. 208. 2005.
Saraca chinensis Merr. & Chun, Dict. Fam. & Gen. Chin. Seed Pl. 385. 1958; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 331. 1972, nom. nud.
Saraca indica auct. non L.: Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 331. 1972.

Tree, 5–20 m tall. Petioles short and thick, 0.7–1.2 cm; leaflets 5–6 pairs, slightly purplish red when young, pendulous, subleathery, long elliptic, ovate-lanceolate or long obovate, 15 – 35 × 5 – 12 cm, basal one pair often smaller, base cuneate, apex acuminate, acute or obtuse; lateral veins 8– 11 pairs. Inflorescences axillary, main rachis hairy or subglabrous. Involucral bracts large, broadly ovate, hairy, caducous. Bracts ovate, lanceolate or oblong, 1.5 – 5 × 0.6 – 2 cm, lowest one larger, gradually smaller upward, hairy or not, caducous or deciduous. Bracteoles same as bracts in shape, but much smaller. Flowers yellow, turning red, bisexual or unisexual. Pedicels shorter than calyx tube, not articulate. Calyx tube 1.5 – 3 cm, lobes oblong, ciliate. Stamens 8 – 10, 1 – 2 usually reduced and subulate, filaments exserted, anthers ellipsoidal, 3 –4 mm. Ovary slightly curved, glabrous or hairy along both sutures and stipe. Pod brown, flat, 22 – 30 × 5 –7 cm, valves coiling. Seeds 5– 9, various in shape, flat, with a shallow furrow at middle on both surfaces.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2576; HK sheet 8691.
Distribution: Taiwan (cultivated); Laos, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Saraca indica L. previously (Check List HK Plants 137. 2002; 52. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Saraca indica L. previously (Check List HK Plants 137. 2002; 52. 2004).

records.text:
Sarcandra glabra (Thunb.) Nakai 草珊瑚（雞爪蘭、九節楓）
Fl. Sylv. Koreana 18: 17. 1930; FRPS 20(1): 79, pl. 25: 1–5. 1982; FGD 3:18, fig. 14. 1995; FOC 4: 132. 1999.
Bladhia glabra Thunb., Trans. Linn Soc. 2: 331. 1794.
Chloranthus brachystachys auct. non Blume: FHK 334. 1861; FKH 221. 1912.

Subshrub, evergreen, 50–150 cm tall. Stems cylindric, erect, glabrous, nodes swollen. Stipules subulate; petioles 0.5–2 cm, connate, forming a short sheath; leaf blade leathery or papery, elliptic or ovate to ovate-lanceolate, or broadly elliptic to oblong, 6–20 × 2–8 cm, base cuneate or broad-cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin sharply coarse-serrate, with glandular-tipped teeth, glabrous; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, slightly prominent on both surface. Inflorescences terminal, spicate, usually branched, 1.5–4 cm including peduncle; bracts triangular or ovate. Flowers yellowish green. Stamen 1, fleshy, clavate to terete or ovoid; anther 2-celled, cells lateral or sometimes introrse, on both sides of apical part of connective or nearly as long as connective. Ovary globose or ovoid; style absent; stigma subcapitate or minutely spotted. Drupes green when young, shiny-red or yellowish red at maturity, globose or ovoid, ca. 3–4 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 381, 1472.
Distribution: S, SW, C & S China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes and in valleys. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Sarcococca longipetiolata M. Cheng 長柄野扇花

Act. Phytotax. Sin. 17(3): 99, pl. 8: 1 –2. 1979; FRPS 45(1): 44, pl. 13. 1980; FGD 3: 235, fig. 158. 1995.

Sarcococca pruniformis auct. non Lindl.: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 233. 1912.


Evergreen shrub, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets angled, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate or narrowly lanceolate, rarely ovate-lanceolate, 6–12 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate or cuneate, apex acuminate to long-acuminate, glabrous or puberulous on the midvein of adaxial surface, triple-veined; veins conspicuous on adaxial surface. Racemes 1–1.5 cm, solitary or 2–4-clustered in axils of leaves. Bracts ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, ± acuminate. Male flowers: pedicels thick, ca. 1 mm, subtended by 2 small (ca. 3 mm) ovate bracteoles; sepals broadly ovate or elliptic, ca. 3 mm; stamens ca. 6 mm. Female flowers: bracteoles ovate, 1.5–3 mm, imbricate; sepals similar to the upper bracteoles. Fruit subglobose, ca. 8 mm in diam., red or purplish red when mature.


Locality: Mount Parker. W. J. Tutcher 5219; Y. W. Lam 1453.

Distribution: Guangdong, S Hunan.

Ecology: Forests by streams.

Uses: Ornamental.

Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.
records.uses:
Ornamental.

Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Sarcosperma laurinum (Benth.) Hook. f. 肉實樹
Gen. Pl. 2: 655. 1876; FKH 161. 1912; FHN 3: 163. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 83. 1987; FFJ 4: 314. 1989; FGD 2: 358, fig. 224. 1991; FOC 15: 214. 1996.
Reptonia laurina Benth., FHK 208. 1861.

Tree, to 20 m tall, conspicuously buttressed. Branchlets angulate, glabrous. Leaves mostly alternate, sometimes opposite or whorled; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blades almost leathery, obovate to oblanceolate, rarely narrowly elliptic, 7–16 × 2.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate, apex short-acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–9 pairs; stipules small, caducous. Racemes or panicles 2–13 cm, puberulous. Flowers 4 mm in diam. Pedicels 1–5 mm, yellowish brown-tomentose. Sepals 2–3 mm, subrounded, glabrous adaxially, yellowish brown-tomentose abaxially. Corolla white or pale green, 3 –4 mm; lobes broadly obovate to subrounded, 2–2.5 mm. Staminodes subulate, nearly as long as stamens. Ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 mm, 1-locular, glabrous. Drupe ellipsoid, 1.5 –2.5 × 0.8–1 cm, red and shining, base with recurved persistent calyx. Seed 1, ca. 1.7 × 0.8 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 417; K. Y. Tam 114; Y. W. Lam 208.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by W. A. Harland in 1850s.
records.uses:
Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by W. A. Harland in 1850s.

records.text:
Sargentodoxa cuneata (Oliv.) Rehd. & Wils. 大血藤
Sargent, Pl. Wils. 1: 351. 1913; FGD 4: 56, fig. 34. 2000; FRPS 29: 305. 2001; FOC 6: 454. 2001.
Holboellia cuneata Oliv., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 19: t. 1817. 1889.

Twining woody vine. Bark on old stems longitudinally fissured; branches reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves alternate, ternate; petioles 5 –10 cm. termianal leaflets rhomboid-obovate, 4 –14 × 3 –9 cm, base cuneate, apex acute; petiolules 5 –10 mm; lateral leaflets larger, obliquely ovate, bilaterally asymmetrical, subsessile. Racemes pendulous, 8 –15 cm, many-flowered. Flowers yellow or yellowish green, fragrant. Pedicels 1–1.5 cm, with an oblong bract at base and 2 linear alternate bracteoles near middle. Male flowers: sepals 6, narrowly oblong, 6 –10 × 2– 4 mm, margin slightly involute; nectariform petals very small, rhomboid-orbicular, ca. 1.2 mm; stamens ca. 4 mm; vestigial carpesl linear, ca. 1 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in staminate flower; carpels numerous, spirally arranged on the globose receptalcle. Ripe carpel an ovoid berry, 7–10 mm in diam, dark blue and glaucous, usually 20 – 40 on the enlarged receptacle. Seeds black, ovoid, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Wong Nai Chung, Ng Tung Chai. W. J. Tutcher 8335; Y. S. Lau 1634.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets on hillslopes and in ravines. Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sasa subglabra McClure 光笹竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 45. 1940; HKB 75. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 674. 1996; FGD 9: 291. 2009.

Shrubby running bamboo; culms erect, 1.5–2 m tall, 5–6 mm in diam.; internodes terete, 15–20 cm long, smooth and glabrous. Branches usually solitary at each node, (2–)3 at upper nodes. Culm leaves persistent; sheaths tightly culm-clasping, minute hairy abaxially when young, glabrescent, subtruncate at apex, margin densely ciliate; auricles lacking; ligules 1–1.5 mm high; blades erect, lanceolate, hispidulous on both surfaces when young. Foliage leaves: sheaths puberulous when young; auricles lacking; ligules 1–1.5 mm high; blades ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 12–30 cm long, 2.5–5.5 cm wide, shortly pubescent toward base beneath, reticulate veinlets conspicuous.

Locality: Shatin. Nan Zhu 2824, 2835 (CUHK); HK sheet 37522, 37523.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests.
Notes: The type specimen (H. Fung 21251, SYS, holotype; US, isotype) was collected by H. Fung from Sha Tin Tsuen on 2 May 1938. Discovered in 1938 from Sha Tin Tsuen in ravines on moist clay, this species is endemic to Hong Kong. Up till now, no flowering specimen is available. Therefore its systematic position is still unclear and is thus of special botanical interest. The locality of its occurrence is very close to a village, and its distribution is likely due to folk use. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Saurauia tristyla DC. 水東哥（米花樹）
Mem. Ternstroem. 31, t. 4. 1822; FHK 27. 1861; FKH 45. 1912; FHN 1: 512. 1964; FRPS 49(2): 296. 1984; FGD 3: 152. 1995.

Small tree or shrub, 1– 5 m or taller. Branchlets stout, densely tomentose to glabrescent, with unguiculate hairs or subulate scales. Petiole 2.5 – 5.5 cm, with appressed scales or subulate stiff hairs; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or obovate-oblong, 10–30 × 5 –14 cm, papery, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, sparsely pubescent with appressed stiff hairs along midvein and lateral veins on both surfaces, glabrescent; lateral veins 8 –20 pairs. Cymes solitary or 2–3 fascicled, 2–5 cm, hairy and scaly. Pedicels 0.8 –1 cm. Flowers pink to white. Sepals broadly ovate, 3– 4 mm. Petals ovate, ca. 8 mm, recurved at apex. Stamens 25 –34. Ovary ovoid to globose; styles 3 or 4(or 5), connate at proximal half. Berry globose, 0.6–1 cm in diam., green to white or pale yellow.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. C. P. Lau 87; W. J. Tutcher 5262; Y. S. Lau 633.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, Nepal and Thailand.
Ecology: Broadleaved forests and thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sauropus androgynus (L.) Merr. 守宮木（樹仔菜）

Philipp. Bur. For. Bull. 1: 30. 1903; FRPS 44(1): 175, pl. 49: 8 – 11. 1994; FGD 5: 64. 2003.

Clutia androgyna L., Mant. Pl. 1: 128. 1767.

Sauropus albicans Blume, Bijdr. 596. 1825.


Shrub, 1–3 m tall, glabrous throughout; branchlets slender, green, ± angular when young. Leaves sub-membranous or thin-papery; stipules lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm; petioles 2–4 mm; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–10 × 1.5– 3.5 cm, base cuneate, rounded or truncate, apex acuminate; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Flowers 1 to 2, or several in axillary clusters. Male flower: pedicels slender, 4–7.5 mm; calyx shallowly disk-shaped, 5–12 mm in diam., shallowly 6-lobed, lobes obovate, imbricate; pistillode none; stamens 3, filaments connate; disk-segments 6, opposite to the sepals, incurved. Female flowers: pedicels 6–8 mm; calyx 6-lobed, lobes red, obovate or obovate-triangular, 5–6 × 3–5.5 mm, base attenuate into a short claw, imbricate; disk absent; ovary 3-locular, with 2 ovules in each locule; styles 3, bilobed. Capsules depressed-globose or globose, 1.2 × 1.7 cm, thinly crustaceous, persistent calyx red; fruiting pedicels 5 – 10 mm long; seeds triquetrous, ca. 7 × 5 mm, black.


Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3261; S. Liu 239 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 8751 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan (cultivated); widely spread in Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Sri Lanka, India and New Guinea.

Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (vegetable).

Sauropus bacciformis (L.) Airy Shaw 艾堇

Kew Bull. 35: 685. 1980; FRPS 44(1): 177, pl. 53: 3 – 6. 1994; FGD 5: 65, fig. 35. 2003.

Phyllanthus bacciformis L., Mant. Pl. 2: 294. 1771; FHK 310. 1861.


Herb, annual or a perennial of short duration, 14–60 cm tall, glabrous throughout; branches diffuse, angular. Leaves somewhat fleshy; stipules narrowly triangular, ca. 2 mm, awn-tipped; petioles ca. 1 mm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic-obovate or lanceolate, 1–2.5 × 0.2–1.2 cm, base rounded or obtuse, rarely cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, mucronulate; lateral veins obscure. Male flowers: several in axillary clusters, 1–2 mm in diam.; pedicels 1–1.5 mm; sepals 6, broadly ovate or obovate, inside with gland-pools, apex irregularly crenate; disk almost petaloid, 6-lobed, fleshy, segments opposite with sepals, yellow-green; stamens 3, 3–4 mm, filaments connate. Female flowers: solitary, axillary, 3–4 mm in diam., green; pedicels 1–1.5 mm; sepals 6, oblong-lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, apex acuminate, inside with gland-pools; disk absent; ovary 3-locular, styles 3, free, 2-lobed. Capsules ovoid, ca. 5–6 × 4–4.5 mm, purple when matured, separating into 3 bivalved cocci; seeds trigonous.


Locality: Aberdeen, Ngau Tau Kok, Ma On Shan, Pak Shek Kok, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau, Ping Chau, Lung Kwu Chau. Y. S. Lau 1216, 1985; P. S. Choi 445; S. Y. Hu 5885, 11765 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Vietnam, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Maritius.

Ecology: Coastal areas. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Sauropus garrettii Craib 蒼葉守宮木

Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1914(8): 284. 1914; FRPS 44(1): 175, pl. 49: 1–4. 1994.

Sauropus chorisepalus Merr. & Chun, Sunyatsenia 2(1): 10, pl. 5. 1934.

Sauropus garrettii var. chorisepalus (Merr. & Chun) H. S. Kiu, FGD 5: 64. 2003.


Shrub, 1–4 m tall; branches sometimes compressed, usually sharply bicarinate; branchlets slender, obscurely angulate and puberulent when young. Leaves membranous or thin-papery; stipules oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–4 mm; petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade rhombic-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, rarely oblong or ovate, 2–15 × 1–5.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded or truncate, apex usually acuminate, rarely acute, dark-green adaxially when dry, glaucous or glaucescent abaxially; lateral veins 5–6 pairs. Flowers 1 to several in axillary cluster. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 3–10 mm, densely bracteolate at base; calyx disk-shaped, 1–5 mmin diam., shallowly 6-lobed, segments ovate or subelliptic, apex acute or acuminate, membranous; stamens 3, filaments connate. Female flowers: pedicels 6–15 mm, slender; calyx 6-lobed, lobes ovate or subrhomboid, ca. 5 mm, apex acute; ovary obovate or turbinate, apex truncate, 3-locular; styles 3, bilobed, arms recurved. Capsules obovate or subovoid, 1–2.5 cm in diam., 3-locular; seeds black, triquetrous, ca. 7 × 5 mm.


Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 36045, 36046.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei; Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Malay Peninsula.

Ecology: Ravines, moist shrublands. Flowering: Apr. –Aug.; fruiting: Aug. –Nov.

Sauropus spatulifolius Beille 龍脷葉

Fl. Indo-Chine 5: 652. 1927; FRPS 44(1): 165, pl. 50: 1 – 3. 1994; FGD 5: 63. 2003.

Sauropus changianus S.Y. Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 32(4): 393, pl. 1: 12 – 15. 1951, "changiana".


Evergreen shrublet, 10–40 cm tall; branches terete, initially glandular-pubescent, glabrous in age, internodes short, 2–20 mm. Leaves ± fleshy in fresh, papery when dry, usually crowded towards upper part of branchlets; stipules 2, triangular-auriculate, 4–8 × 3–4 mm, persistent; petioles 2–5 mm, glandular-pubescent when young; leaf blade spatulate, obovate oblong or ovate, sometimes oblong, 4.5–16.5 × 2.5–6.5 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, rarely rounded, apex rounded or obtuse, rarely retuse, adaxial surface dark-green but with grey-white blotches, usually glabrous; lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Flowers red or purple, 2–5 clustered or sometimes in short cymes borne on leafless branches or stems; peduncles short and thick, with many lanceolate small (2 mm) bracts.
