Male flowers: pedicels slender, 3–5 mm; sepals 6, biseriate, subequal, obovate, 2–3 × 1.5 mm; disk segments 6, opposite with sepals; stamens 3, filaments connate into a short column. Female flowers: pedicels ca. 2–3 mm; sepals as in male flowers; disk absent; ovary subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., 3-locular; styles 3, bilobed, lobes recurved.


Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3228; S. Y. Hu 5258 (CUHK); Hu & But 22084, 22336 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian (cultivated); native to Vietnam.

Ecology: In Hong Kong usually cultivated as a pot plant. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Saururus chinensis (Lour.) Baill. 三白草
Adansonia 10(2): 71. 1871; FHN 1: 339. 1964; FRPS 20(1): 6, pl. 2. 1982; FGD 1: 78. 1987; FOC 4: 108. 1999.
Spathium chinense Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 217. 1790.
Saururus loureiri Decne., Ann. Sci. Nat. ser. 3, 3: 102. 1845; FKH 220. 1912.

Herb, to more than 1 m tall; rhizomes creeping, white, thick. Stems strong, basal part creeping and usually whitish, apical part erect and green. Stipular sheath 2–10 mm, ca. as long as petiole, slightly clasping; petioles 1–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 10–20 × 5 –10 cm, base cordate or oblique-cordate, apex acute or acuminate, densely glandular, glabrous; veins 5–7, basal. Apical leaves smaller, 2 or 3 at stem apex, usually petal-like, white at anthesis. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemose, 12–20 cm; peduncles 3– 4.5 cm, glabrous; rachis densely pubescent. Bract beneath each flower spatulate, basal part linear and pilose, apical part orbicular and glabrous or sparsely ciliate, small, apex rounded to acute. Filaments slightly longer than anthers. Fruit subglobose, ca. 3 mm in diam., tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Tam, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Sha Lo Tung, Tai Mei Tuk. P. S. Choi 133; HK Sheet 35615.
Distribution: Hebei, Henan, Shandong and regions S of Changjiang River; Japan, Philippines to Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, ditches and other wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Jun., fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Saussurea japonica (Thunb.) DC. 風毛菊
Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 16: 203. 1810; FHK 167. 1861; FKH 149. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 330. 1967; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1049. 1998; FRPS 78(2): 47. 1999.
Serratula japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 305. 1784.
Saussurea linearis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's Journ. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 235. 1852.

Biennial or perennial herbs; stem erect, 0.5–2 m tall, striate, not winged, densely pubescent and glandular. Lower leaves petiolate, petioles 2–12 cm, narrowly winged, leaf blade lanceolate, elliptic to oblong, 6–22 × 3–9.5 cm, pinnately toothed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, or sometimes not lobed and appeared as lanceolate form, apical lobes lanceolate, lateral lobes 3–7 pairs with shape varied from triangular, lanceolate to linear, the middle ones largest, others gradually smaller towards both ends; all lobes apices obtuse to rounded, margin entire or shallowly toothed. Median cauline leaves shortly petiolate, linear‑lanceolate, pinnatilobed or not, margin entire or toothed. Upper leaves sessile, much smaller, linear‑lanceolate, linear to bract‑like, entire or slightly toothed. All leaves densely glandular and pubescent on both surfaces. Capitula many, arranged as corymbs or corymbose panicles; peduncles 0.5–2 cm, densely glandular and hairy. Involucres cylindric, 10–12 × 5–8 mm; phyllaries 6‑seriate, abaxial side covered with glands and cobwebby‑tomentose hair, 1‑veined at the centre, all bearing purple‑red membranous apical appendages which are orbicular and with margin toothed; excluding the appendages, outer few layers of phyllaries ovate, 1.8–4 × 1–2 mm, mostly herbaceous; median ones lanceolate to lanceolate‑oblong, 3.5–8 × 1–2 mm, basal portion coriaceous and distal portion herbaceous; inner ones lanceolate to linear, 8–10 × 1 – 1.5 mm, leathery almost to the distal end. Receptacle densely fringed with hair about 5–7 mm. Florets bisexual and fertile, corolla purple, tubular, 1–1.2 cm, lower tube filiform, 6–7 mm, upper limb 5–6 mm, deeply cleft into 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 4 mm. Cypselae brown, cylindric and obtusely 4‑angled, 2.5 – 3 × 1 mm, with minute rostrum at apex. Pappus 2‑seriate; outer layers capillary, 2–3 mm, deciduous individually; inner layers plumose, 7–8 mm, united at base, shed off as a ring.

Locality: Stanley, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1348, 3008; Y. W. Lam 461.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.

Saxifraga stolonifera Curtis 虎耳草
Philos. Trans. 64(1): 308, no. 2541. 1774; FOC 8: 287. 2001.
Saxifraga chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 281. 1790.
Saxifraga sarmentosa L. f., Suppl. Pl. 240. 1781; FKH 98. 1912.
Saxifraga stolonifera Meerb., Afbeeld. pl. 23. 1775; FFJ 2: 218, fig. 184. 1984; FRPS 34(2): 75, pl. 15: 7 – 9. 1992; FGD 3: 59. 1995; Check List HK Plants 124. 2002.

Perennial herb; rhizomes short; prostrate stems slender, branched. Stems 10 – 30 cm tall, glandular villous. Leaves usually basal, fleshy; petioles 3 – 15 cm; leaf blade orbicular or reniform, 4 – 9 cm in diam., base cordate or truncate, apex obtuse or acute, margin irregularly dentate, glandular piliferous on both surfaces, green and white spotted adaxially, purplish red abaxially. Inflorescence a many-flowered panicle, glandular hairy and tomentose. Sepals narrowly ovate, 3 – 4 mm, apex acute, abaxially and marginally glandular hairy. Petals 5, white or pink, upper 3 ovate, 3 mm, apex acuminate, lower 2 lanceolate-elliptic, 1 – 1.5 × 2 – 3 mm, apex acute, pinnatelyveined. Filaments 6 – 8 mm. Ovary ovoid; styles slender, divergent. Capsules ovoid, 4 – 5 mm, apex deeply lobed. Seeds ovoid, tuberculate.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 10366.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Apr.; fruiting: Apr. – May.

Scaevola hainanensis Hance 海南草海桐
J. Bot. 16(188): 229. 1878; FKH 151. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 179. 1983; FGD 2: 360, fig. 245. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 803, pl. 373. 1998.

Small diffuse shrubs; stems thick, greyish, sparsely hirsute and with greyish woolly hairs in leaf‑axils. Leaves sessile, fasciculate at apex of short branches; leaf blade linear‑spathulate, 1.2–2.5 × 0.2–0.5 cm, ± succulent, base attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire; midvein obscure. Flowers sessile to short‑petiolate, solitary in axils of upper leaves; bracts 2, similar to leaves, but slightly smaller. Calyx adnate to ovary; tube ca. 4 mm; limb cup‑shaped, obscurely 5‑lobed. Corolla initially pink, gradually turning white, ca. 10 mm when full blooming; tube 5–6 mm glandular and hairy adaxially, ± pubescent abaxially; lobes 5, slightly shorter than or equal to the tube, margin membranous, folded inwards. Drupe ellipsoidal, 6–7 × 4–6 mm, apex crowned with enlarged calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Cheung Shue Tan, Kiu Tsui, Kau Sai Chau. L. T. Lo 639; Y. W. Lam 42, 361.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy shores. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Scaevola taccada (Gaertn.) Roxb. 草海桐
Fl. Ind. 1: 527. 1820; R. K. Shannon, W. L. Wagner & D. H. Nicolson, Taxon 46(4): 801. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 805, pl. 374. 1998.
Lobelia taccada Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 119, pl. 25, fig. 5. 1788.
Scaevola sericea Vahl, Symb. Bot. 2: 37. 1791; FRPS 73(2): 178. 1983; FGD 2: 361. 1991.
Scaevola lobelia L., Syst. Veg. ed. 13, 178. 1774; FHK 198. 1861.
Scaevola koenigii Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 36. 1794; FKH 151. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees, with a thick, ± succulent stem; branches, leaves and inflorescence silky‑pubescent or nearly glabrous, but always with a tuft of woolly or long silky hairs in leaf‑axils. Leaves alternate, crowded towards apex of branches; leaf blade obovate‑oblong to spathulate, 10–22 × 4–8 cm, , base narrowed into a very short and broad petiole, apex round to broadly obtuse, margin entire, rarely obscurely toothed; midvein raised on both surfaces, lateral veins indistinct. Cymes axillary, lax‑flowered, shorter than the leaves; peduncle 1–2 cm; bracts linear‑lanceolate, 6–8 mm, hairy at the base. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 3–5 mm; lobes 5, oblong‑linear, about the length of the tube. Corolla usually white, 20–22 mm, ± pubescent abaxially and always hairy adaxially; tube 10– 12 mm; lobes 5, lanceolate, about half the length of the tube, spreading, bordered on each side with a narrow wing folded inward in the bud. Drupe ovoid or globose, 8–12 mm in diam., apex crowned with enlarged calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 227, 360; L. T. Lo 445.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy and rocky seashores. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Schefflera heptaphylla (L.) Frodin 鵝掌柴（鴨腳木）
Bot. J. Linn. Soc. 104(3): 312. 1990.
Vitis heptaphylla L., Mant. Alt. 212. 1771.
Schefflera octophylla (Lour.) Harms, Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(8): 38. 1894; FRPS 54: 50. 1978.
Heptapleurum octophyllum (Lour.) Benth. ex Hance, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 13: 105. 1873; FKH 119. 1912.
Aralia octophylla Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 187. 1790.
Paratropia cantoniensis Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 189. 1841; FHK 136. 1861.

Evergreen shrub or tree, up to 10 m tall; branchlets, petioles, petiolules, leaves and inflorescence tawny tomentose, with stellate scurfy hairs when young, glabrescent. Leaves digitately compound, generally 6–8-foliolate; petioles 15–30 cm; petiolules unequal in length, 3–6.5 cm; leaflet leathery, elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 7–17 × 3–7.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to nearly rounded, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins ca. 8 on each side of midvein. Umbels many-flowered, 1–2 cm in diam., racemosely arranged on the primary branches, forming a large terminal panicle up to 25 cm. Flowers small, fragrant; bracts triangular, small, 2–3 mm; pedicels 3–5 mm, with a small bracteole at base. Calyx pubescent, 5–6-dentate. Petals 5, fleshy, 2–3 mm. Stamens 5, filaments slightly longer than the petals. Ovary 5–8-locular; styles united into a very short but distinct column. Fruits globose, 3–4 mm in diam.; persistent style-column very short, less than 1 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 224, 2105; L. T. Lo 595.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Dec.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Material (timber), medicinal (folklore).

Schima superba Gardn. & Champ. 木荷
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. l: 246. 1849; FHN 1: 501. 1964; FGD 2: 150. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 224. 1998.
Schima noronhae auct. non Reinw. ex Blume: FHK 29. 1861; FKH 45. 1912.

Tree or small tree, branches greyish brown or reddish brown, glabrescent. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 7–13 × 3 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin crenulate to crenulate-serrate, glabrous, midvein slightly impressed adaxially, veins distinct on both surfaces. Flowers white, 2–3 cm in diam., in short terminal racemes; pedicel stout, 1–2.5 cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; bracteoles 2, deciduous; calyx 5-lobed, lobes semiorbicular, 2–3 mm, glabrous abaxially, pubescent adaxially, margins ciliolate; petals 5, obovate, 1–1.5 cm, proximally connate into a short tube, pubescent at base; stamens many, 5 –7 mm, connate at base; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent on proximal part, glabrescent on distal part; style ca. 5 mm. Capsule subglobose, 1–1.5 cm in diam, pubescent; seeds flat, reniform, narrowly winged, 7–9 × 4.5 – 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 554, 2146; K. Y. Tam 105.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdung, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Materials (timber, fuelwood).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.
records.uses:
Materials (timber, fuelwood).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

records.text:
Schizachyrium brevifolium (Sw.) Nees ex Büse 裂稃草
Pl. Jungh. 3: 359. 1854; FHN 4: 482, fig. 1267. 1977; FFJ 6: 273, fig. 246. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 210, pl. 52: 1–10. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 576, pl. 243. 2000; FOC 22: 622. 2006; FGD 9: 502, fig. 266. 2009.
Andropogon brevifolius Sw., Prodr. 26. 1788; FHK 423. 1861; FKH 323. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms erect or trailing, slender, 10–70 cm long. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear to oblong, flat or folded, 1.5–4 × (0.1–)0.2–0.7 cm, glabrous, base subrounded, apex obtuse, margins scabrous; ligule short, membranous. Raceme slender, enclosed at base by spatheole; rachis internodes and pedicels inflated upward, apex cupular and oblique, glabrous to villous. Sessile spikelet linear-lanceolate, ca. 3 mm; lower glume linear-lanceolate, subleathery, abaxially flat, glabrous to thinly pilose, indistinctly 4–5-veined, flanks keeled toward apex, keels wingless, apex minutely 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, thicken membranous, midvein keeled, 3-veined; lemma hyaline membranous; lower lemma linear-lanceolate, slightly shorter than glume, margins ciliate, apex acute; upper lemma 2/3 glume length, 2-lobed to near base; with a flexuous awn arising from sinus, geniculate; style free. Caryopsis linear, flat. Pedicellate spikelet reduced to 1 or 2 glumes, up to 0.7 mm, lower glume with 3–5 mm awn.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1040; P. P. H. But 140; Y. W. Lam 425.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, S and SE Asia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Open grassy banks, margins of fields, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Schizachyrium sanguineum (Retz.) Alston 紅裂稃草
Handb. Fl. Ceylon. 6: 334. 1931; FHN 4: 483. 1977; FFJ 6: 273, fig. 247. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 212, pl. 52: 11–12. 1997; FOC 22: 622. 2006; FGD 9: 502. 2009.
Rottboellia sanguinea Retz., Observ. Bot. 3: 25. 1783.
Andropogon zeylanicus Arn. ex Benth., FHK 423. 1861, non Nees ex Steud (1854).
Andropogon hirtiflorus (Nees) Kunth, Rév. Gram. 2: 571. 1833; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb, whole plant usually reddish brown. Culms erect, hard, 50–120 cm tall, simple or branched, glabrous. Leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat, 5–25 × 0.1–0.5 cm, glabrous, apex acute, margins scabrid; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, apex subtruncate. Raceme solitary, dark purplish red, very slender, erect, 3–9 cm, finally long exserted from spatheole; rachis internodes and pedicels linear-clavate, equalling or slightly shorter than sessile spikelet, margin glabrous or white-ciliate. Sessile spikelet linear-lanceolate, slightly appressed into the cavity of rachis; lower glume linear, leathery, convex with inflexed margins, keeled from below middle to apex, abaxially scabrid; keels very narrowly winged toward apex, apex 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, thicken membranous, narrow wings on the upper keel; lower lemma linear-lanceolate, slightly shorter than glume, margins ciliate; upper lemma 2-lobed to near base; awn 1–2 cm; styles 2. Caryopsis linear, flat. Pedicellate spikelet lanceolate, reduced to 1 or 2 glumes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 818, 949, 1332.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia, Africa, America.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Schizocapsa plantaginea Hance 裂果薯
J. Bot. 19: 292. 1881; FKH 275. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 50, pl. 12: 1 – 7. 1985; FOC 24: 275. 2000; FGD 9: 223, fig. 129. 2009.
Tacca plantaginea (Hance) Drenth, Blumea 20(2): 391. 1972.

Plant 20 – 30 cm tall. Rhizomes thick and short, often curved. Petiole (5–)–11(–16) cm, winged; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to narrowly elliptic-lanceolate, 10–15(–25) × 4 6(–8) cm, base decurrent, apex acuminate. Scape 6 – 13 cm; involucral bracts ovate to deltoid-ovate, 1–2 cm; umbel 8 – 15(–20)-flowered. Perianth light or dark green or light purple; lobes pointed at apex, outer lobes lanceolate, inner ones ovate, slightly shorter and wider than outer ones. Filaments extremely short, apical hood projected downward into 2 auricles. Stigma 3-lobed, lobes bifid. Capsule obovoid, 6–8 mm, 3-valved; valves splitting to base. Seeds semilunar, oblong or irregularly so, striate.

Locality: Repulse Bay, Lady Clementi's Ride. H. C. Tang 1974; Y. S. Lau 642.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, Yunnan; Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, along rivers, valleys. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Schizostachyum dumetorum (Hance ex Walp.) Munro 苗仔竹
Bot. Voy. Herald. 424. 1857; FHK 435. 1861; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 76. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 20, pl. 3: 1 – 12. 1996; FOC 22: 52. 2006; FGD 9: 277. 2009.
Bambusa dumetorum Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 781. 1853.

Culms flexuose, 3 – 10 m long, 0.5 – 1.1 cm in diam., apically clambering; internodes to 60 cm, smooth and glabrous near base, otherwise white powdery and white strigose; wall ca. 1 mm thick. Branches ca. 40 cm. Culm sheaths deciduous, abaxially slightly glabrous, base of outer margin usually with a conspicuous subcircular expansion below point of attachment, apex truncate with equal sides; auricles usually inconspicuous; oral setae many, straight, 5 – 7 mm; ligule less than 1 mm, glabrous, margin undulate; blade reflexed, those on lower nodes of culm less than 1/2 length of sheath, those on upper nodes of culm longer. Leaves 5 – 7 per ultimate branch; sheaths 2 – 3.5 cm, glabrous; auricles usually inconspicuous; oral setae several, 3 – 5 mm; ligule less than 1 mm; blade lanceolate, 5 – 18 × 1.2 – 7 cm. Pseudospikelets fusiform, 1 – 2.2 cm; prophylls small; bracts 4 – 6, navicular, 1 – 5.5 mm, papery, rigid, keeled, apex obtuse; rachilla disarticulating. Glumes absent; lemma oblong-lanceolate, 1.2 – 1.4 cm, involute, many-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea oblong-lanceolate, to 1.5 cm, markedly involute, thinly papery, apex truncate or emarginate; lodicules absent. Filaments white, ca. 2 cm, base ± connate; anthers yellow, 5 – 6 mm. Ovary ovoid,glabrous, stalked; style purple; stigmas 3, purple-red, 3 – 5 mm, plumose. Caryopsis fusiform, 10 – 13 × ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous, apex beaked.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3053, 3154; Y. W. Lam 1895.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thickets, forests. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance from Hong Kong before 1853.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance from Hong Kong before 1853.

records.text:
Schlumbergera truncata (Haw.) Moran 蟹爪
Gentes Herbarium 8: 329. 1953; FGX 1: 738. 1991; FGD 4: 139, fig. 87. 2000.
Zygocactus truncates (Haw.) K. Schum. in Martius, Fl. Bras. 4: 224. 1890.
Epiphyllum truncatum Haw., Suppl. Pl. Succ. 85. 1819.

Small shrubby cactus. Stems dichotomously branched and short-jointed; joints flat, ovate to oblong, 3–6 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex truncate, margin with 2–4 incurved teeth on each side, green on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, in various shades of red, borne on the apex of the joints; perianth-tube ca. 2.5 cm; limb 4–5 cm in diam.; segments 21–23, in 4–5 irregular tiers on the tube, basal ones ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 0.7–1.5 × 0.5–0.8 cm, distal ones oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 × 1–1.2 cm. Stamens many. Ovary turbinate, 4-angled, glabrous; stigma 6–7-lobed.

Locality: Cultivated. C. Chan 73 (CUHK); M. Y. Wong 36 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: In Hong Kong the species is usually cultivated as a pot plant, or grafted on a stock of Hylocereus undatus. Flowering: Dec.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Schoenoplectus juncoides (Roxb.) Palla 螢藺
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 10: 229. 1889; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 561. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 300. 2000; FYN 15: 577. 2003; FOC 23: 186. 2010.
Scirpus juncoides Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 228. 1820; FHK 395. 1861; FRPS 11: 23. 1961; FHN 4: 277. 1977; FGD 8: 284. 2007; Check List HK Plants 319. 2002; 112. 2004.
Schoenoplectiella juncoides (Roxb.) Lye, Lidia 6(1): 25. 2003.
Scirpus erectus auct. non Poir.: FKH 301. 1912; Check List HK Plants 89. 1993.

Perennial. Rhizome short, roots many, fibrous. Culms tufted, 15–70 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, subterete or obtusely severalangled, smooth. Leaf sheaths 3–4, lower scale-like, brownish, upper 5–15 cm, obliquely truncate, mucronate. Involucral bracts 1, 1.5–15 cm, abruptly subacute, base dilated, 1-furrowed on ventral side. Inflorescence pseudolateral, capitate, with (1–)2–12 spikelets. Spikelets oblong to ovoid-oblong, 6–18 × 3–6 mm, pale yellowish brown. Glumes ovate to broadly ovate, 3–4 × 1.8–2.7 mm, apex rounded to shallowly emarginate, mucronate, thickly membranous, pale brown, keel green, 1–3-veined. Perianth segments 4–6, ± retrorsely scabrous, of which 4 equalling or slightly longer than achene, remainder ± as long as achenes or less. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, ca. 2 mm. Style ca. 2 mm, stigmas 2, one of them rudimentary. Achenes broadly obovate, unequally biconvex, 1.8–2 × 1.5 mm, shiny dark brown, transversely wrinkled.

Locality: Wu Kai Sha, Sai Kung, Pui O. Y. S. Lau 244; Y. W. Lam 2224; J. C. Shaw 200.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Nei Mongol, Xizang and Gansu; Madagascar, tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia, Fiji, Hawaii.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Schoenoplectus lateriflorus (J. F. Gmel.) Lye 側花水蔥
Bot. Not. 124: 290. 1971.
Scirpus lateriflorus J. F. Gmel., Syst. Nat. 1: 127. 1791; FRPS 11: 27. 1961; FGD 8: 282. 2007.
Schoenoplectus supinus (L.) Palla subsp. lateriflorus (J. F. Gmel.) Soják, Cas. Nar. Muz. (Prague) 141: 62. 1972; FTW ed. 2, 5: 303. 2000; FYN 15: 576. 2003; FOC 23: 188. 2010.
Scirpus supinus L. var. lateriflorus (J. F. Gmel.) T. Koyama, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 7(6): 302. 1958; FHN 4: 277. 1977.
Scirpus supinus auct. non L.: FKH 300. 1912.
Isolepis supinus auct. non (L.) R. Br.: FHK 394. 1861.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Culms tufted, 5–30 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, trigonous, striate. Leaf sheath 5–15 cm, brown, apex obliquely truncate, mucronate, the uppermost sheath sometimes with a compressed-triangular blade to 10 cm. Involucral bracts 1, the lower bract erect, 3–12 cm, ventrally sulcate. Inflorescence pseudolateral, capitate or short, paniculate, simple, branches 4, unequal, with 3–10 spikelets; small secondary inflorescence often present at culm base. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate to oblong, 4–8 × 2–3 mm. Glumes elliptic or elliptic-ovate, boat-shaped, 1.8–2.5 × ca. 2 mm, apex acute, mucronate, green to pale yellowish brown. Perianth segments absent, rarely rudimentary. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, connective pilose. Style slender, ca. 0.5 mm, stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.3 mm, black, sides transversely wrinkled.

Locality: Hong Kong. C. Wilford 271; C. Wright 590 (K).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangsu, Yunnan, Taiwan; Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia, Philippines, Madagascar, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Scirpus supinus L. var. lateriflorus Gmel. previously (Check List HK Plants 320. 2002; 112. 2004).

Schoenoplectus subulatus (Vahl) Lye 鑽苞水蔥
Skr. Utg. Svensk Linné-Sällsk. 124: 290. 1971; FOC 23: 183. 2010.
Scirpus subulatus Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 268. 1806; FRPS 11: 17. 1961; FHN 4: 276. 1977.
Schoenoplectus litoralis (Schrad.) Palla subsp. subulatus (Vahl) T. Koyama, Fl. Ceylon 5: 157. 1985.
Scirpus littoralis auct. non Schard.: FGD 8: 282. 2007; Check List HK Plants 320. 2002; 112. 2004.

Perennial. Rhizome short; stolons terminated by a tuber. Culms erect, 60–150 cm tall, 0.5–0.8 mm thick, terete to trigonous below inflorescence, smooth, closed with leafless sheath at base. Leaf sheath cylindrical, 4–20 cm, membranous, septate-nodulose, becoming fibrous with age, apex with a recurved setaceous blade for 5–10 mm. Involucral bracts 1, subcompressed, ± equalling inflorescence, obtuse. Inflorescence paniculate, simple; branches 3–7, unequal, up to 5 cm, scabrous, terminated by 1–3 spikelets. Spikelets oblongovate or elliptic-ovate, 7–15 × 3–4 mm, many-flowered. Glumes oblong-ovate or elliptic, 3.5–4 × 1.8–2 mm, ± obtuse, shortly mucronate, rust brown, the margins tinged red. Perianth segments 3–4, broadly linear to ± spathulate, slightly exceeding achene, fimbriate. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, biconvex, 2 × 1.5–1.7 mm, somewhat shiny, chestnut-brown, very minutely papillose.

Locality: Plover Cove, Mai Po. K. L. Yip 4203; Y. W. Lam 1777; J. C. Shaw 268.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Sichuan, Shanxi, Gansu; India, Sri Lanka, Malesia, Australia, Japan and Micronesia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The species was merged with Scirpus littoralis Schard. or treated as a subspecies of the latter by some authors, but it is easily distinguished from the latter by its terete to trigonous culm and narrower, more laxly fimbriate perianth segments.

Schoenoplectus triangulatus (Roxb.) Soják 水毛花
Čas. Nár. Mus., Odd. Přír. 141(1 – 2): 62. 1972.
Scirpus triangulatus Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 219. 1820; FRPS 11: 21. 1961.
Schoenoplectus mucronatus (L.) Palla subsp. robustus (Miq.) T. Koyama, FTW 5: 214. 1978; FOC 23: 184. 2010.
Scirpus mucronatus auct. non L.: FGD 8: 282. 2007; Check List HK Plants 112. 2004.

Perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms deep green, slightly densely tufted, 45–130 cm tall, 5–11 mm thick, sharply 3-angled with shallowly concave sides, clothed at base with 2–4 leaf sheaths. Leaf sheaths brown, 7–25 cm, membranous to herbaceous, obliquely truncate at orifice. Involucral bract 1, culm-like, upright or obliquely bent, 2–10 cm. Inflorescences a pseudo-lateral hemispherical head, with (3–)5–20 spikelets. Spikelets ovoid, oblong-ovoid, to narrowly ovoid, 10–20 × 4–6 mm, terete, densely many-flowered, apex subacute. Glumes broadly obovate, ovate, broadly ovate, 3.8–5 × 2.5–3 mm, pale green and brownish tinged usually with reddish brown, very concave, papery, margin apically minutely ciliolate, apex with a green 1–3-veined costa excurrent in a mucro. Perianth segments 6, 1.5–2 mm, retrorsely scabrous. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2.5 mm; connective apex slightly prominent beyond anthers. Style ca. 4 mm; stigmas 3. Achene blackish brown at maturity, obovoid to broadly obovoid, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, compressed 3-sided, conspicuously or inconspicuously transversely wrinkled, ± shiny, base contracted to cuneate, apex rounded to mucronate.

Locality: San Tin, Kam Tin. Y. W. Lam 1774; HK sheet 40625.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Sri Lanka; Africa, Europe, Madagascar.
Ecology: Pond and lake margins, swamps, grasslands in streamsides, paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Schoenus falcatus R. Br. 赤箭莎
Prodr. 232. 1810; FRPS 11: 116. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 308. 2000; FOC 23: 256. 2010.
Schoenus sinensis Hand.-Mazz., Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl., Anz. 62: 150. 1925.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody. Culms 60–100(–150) cm tall, 2–5 mm thick, obtusely angular, smooth, glabrous. Leaves mostly basal, 3–4-cauline; blade narrowly linear, rigid, 90 cm × 2–7 mm, long-acuminate channeled, glabrous; basal sheath 3–5 cm, dark purplish, cauline sheath 1.5–3 cm. Involucral bract several, lowest bract 3–16 cm. Inflorescence narrow, panicle-like, 20–40 cm, with 4–10 distant nodes each subtending 2–4 partial inflorescence. Spikelets many, shortly pedunculate, oblong-lanceolate, weakly flattened, 7–14 × 2.5 mm, 8–10-glumed, 3–8-flowered. Glumes ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 5–7 × 1 mm, acute, mucronate, sides papery, brown, margins paler, keel acute, yellow green, the lower 2–5 glumes empty, shorter. Perianth segments 1–3, ± equalling achene. Stamens 3; filaments slender; anthers linear, ca. 3 mm. Style 3–4 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly ellipsoidal or obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.3 × 0.8–1 mm, apex pubescent, rust brown, pittedreticulate with large epidermal cells.

Locality: Penny's Bay. S. C. Ng 1719, 1825.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, New Guinea, Japan, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Rocks near seashore, thin forests by rivers. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.

Schoepfia chinensis Gardner & Champ. 華南青皮木（青皮樹）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 308. 1849; FHK 52. 1861; FKH 58. 1912; FHN 2: 456, fig. 520. 1965; FRPS 24: 43, pl. 10: 3– 7. 1988; FOC 5: 203. 2003.
Schoepfiopsis chinensis (Gardner & Champ.) Miers, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 17(98): 77. 1878.

Shrub or tree, 1–6 m tall, glabrous. Older stems greyish brown, slightly striate; branchlets often deciduous, bark purplish brown, white lenticellate, with rounded deciduous bud scales at base. Petioles 3–6 mm; leaf blade papery to ± leathery, oblong-lanceolate to elliptic, 5–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate and unequal, apex acuminate; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences 0.5–1.5 cm, 2–4-flowered. Pedicel absent; bracteole 1, at base of flowers. Calyx obcampanulate. Corolla pink, urceolate; tube 0.6–1 cm, throat narrower; lobes ovate, 2–4 mm. Stamens (4–)5; filaments coherent to corolla tube; anthers free, slightly exserted from corolla throat. Disk pulvinate. Style 5–9 mm. Drupe ellipsoidal, 1–1.5 × 0.5–0.6 cm, red to purple, blackish when mature.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Pok To Yan. Y. W. Lam 24, 1384; HK sheet 40031.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Ravines, along streams. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Apr. – Jul.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849. The species was also reported as Schoepfia jasminodora Gardner & Champ. previously (Check List HK Plants 50. 1993).

Sciaphila ramosa Fukuy. & T. Suzuki 多枝霉草
J. Jap. Bot. 12: 414. 1936; FRPS 8: 193. 1992; T. L. Wu et al., J. Trop & Subtrop. Bot. 8(2): 158. 2000; Hsieh et al, Taiwania 48(4): 244. 2003; FOC 23: 126. 2010.

Erect herb, 8–12 cm tall, purplish, glabrous. Stems usually branched, 0.5–0.7 mm in diam. Leaves scale-like, lanceolate, ca. 0.8–1.3 mm, apex acuminate to acute. Inflorescence terminal, racemose, erect, ca. 1 cm, 3–9-flowered; bracts lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, apex acute; pedicels 3–4 mm, straight. Male flower on upper part, 2 mm in diam.; perianth segments 6, lobes subequal, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, ca. 0.75 mm, apex mucronate or acute; stamens 2 or 3, subssesile, anther 4-celled. Female flowers perianth segments 4–6, ± equal, oblong to triangular, ca. 0.7 mm, apex acute, without appendage. Carpels ca. 20–30, style subapical, awl-shaped, 0.5–0.6 mm, apex papillate, exceeding ovary. Mature carpels obovate, slightly curved, 0.7 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1600.
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Litter layer in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Sciaphila secundiflora Thwaites ex Benth. 大柱霉草
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc 7: 10. 1855; Meerendonk, Fl. Males. ser. I. 10: 116. 1984; Hsieh et al., Taiwania 48(4): 245. 2003; FOC 23: 125. 2010.
Sciaphila megastyla Fukuy. & T. Suzuki, J. Jap. Bot. 12: 412. 1936; FRPS 8: 191. 1992; T. L. Wu et al., J. Trop & Subtrop. Bot. 8(2): 157. 2000; Check List HK Plants 293. 2002; 104. 2004.

Saprophytic herb, 4–12 cm tall, glabrous, pink or reddish. Stems slender, usually unbranched, 0.7–1 mm in diam. Leaves scale-like, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–4 mm, apex acuminate to acute. Inflorescence terminal, racemose, erect, ca. 1–5 cm, 3–9-flowered; bracts lanceolate, 1–3 mm, acute; pedicels 1–2 mm, straight. Male flowers towards apex, 6–7 mm in diam., perianth segments usually 6, subulate, ca. 2.5–3.5 mm, patent, equal; stamens 2– 3, subsessile; anthers 4-celled. Female flowers towards base, globose, perianth segments 6, ± equal, oblong to lanceolate, ca. 2–2.5 mm, acuminate. Carpels 10–80, free, obovate, 0.5–1 mm, upper papillate; style club-shaped, 0.6–0.7 mm, inserted laterally at base or about halfway. Mature carpels obovoid, 1 mm, with persistent style.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1599; HK sheet 33860.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, Malesia, Japan, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Litter layer in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Scirpus hainanensis S. M. Huang 海南藨草
FHN 4: 538, fig. 1143. 1977; FGD 8: 279. 2007; FOC 23: 174. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short or absent. Culms terete, several-noded, glabrous, 60 – 90 cm tall, 3–5 mm thick. Leaves basal or 3–5 cauline, blades linear, flat, shorter than culms, 3–5 mm wide, apex gradually acuminate, margin scaberulous; sheath brown, 1.5–3 cm. Involucral bracts leafy, usually shorter than inflorescence, gradually shorter upward, with sheath. Inflorescence decompound, primary branches 4–6, unequal. Spikelets in finger-like clusters of 3–12, 5–7 × 2–3 mm, 10–15-flowered. Glumes ovate or oblong-ovate, 2–2.5 × ca. 1.5 mm, apex acute or shortly mucronate, membranous, 1-veined, abaxially yellowish-green in the middle, yellowish or brownish laterally, with brown stripes. Perianth segments 6, ca. 1.5 mm, scaberulous above. Stamen 1, anther oblong, less than 1 mm. Style ca. 1.5 mm, slightly inflated at base, stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid or broadly obovoid, trigonous, ca. 1.5 mm, pale brown, smooth.

Locality: Sunset Peak (fide Corlett et al., 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Forests along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Scirpus ternatanus Reinw. ex Miq. 百穗藨草
Fl. Ned. Ind. 3: 307. 1856; FRPS 11: 13. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 309. 2000; FOC 23: 173. 2010.
Scirpus ternatensis C. B. Clarke, J. L. Soc., Bot. 36: 254. 1903; FKH 301. 1912.
Scirpus chinensis Munro, Bot. Voy. Herald 428. 1857, non Osbeck, 1757; FHK 395. 1861.

Perennial. Culms erect, rather stout to stout, 50–200 cm tall, 4–8 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, several-noded. Leaves basal and up to 7 cauline; blades up to 70 × 0.7–2.5 cm, acuminate, flattish; basal sheaths pale to chestnut brown, cauline sheaths greenish brown. Involucral bracts 3 – 5, leafy, up to 50 cm. Inflorescence decompound, 10–25 × 10–25 cm; primary branches up to 8, unequal, up to 10 cm; secondary and tertiary branches up to 5 cm. Spikelets in finger-like to ± globose clusters of 3–10, ovoid to oblong-ovoid, 2.5–6 × 2–3 mm, obtuse, rarely subacute, dark brown. Gulmes ovate to ± orbicular, 1.2–2.5 × 1–1.5 mm, obtuse, ± mucronulate, membranous. Perianth segments 0–3(–6), delicate, sparsely antrorsely scaberulous in the upper half. Stamens 2–3, anthers ablong-linear, 0.7–1 mm. Style glabrous, stigmas 2(–3). Achenes obovate, 0.7–1 × 0.5–0.8 mm, plano-convex or biconvex, strongly dorsiventrally compressed, minutely apiculate, pale brown, smooth.

Locality: Tai Tam Reservior. J. C. Shaw 929; H. G. Ye et al 1162; HK sheet 8104.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Xizang, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Shandong, Taiwan; Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Japan.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of Scirpus chinensis Munro was collected by Hance from Hong Kong.

Scleria ciliaris Nees 緣毛珍珠茅
Wight, Contr. 117. 1834; FGD 8: 356. 2007; FOC 23: 265. 2010.
Scleria chinensis Kunth, Enum. Pl. 2: 357. 1837, based on S. ciliaris Nees, nom. superfl.; FHK 400. 1861; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 211. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with purplish scales. Culms tufted, 0.4–1.5 m tall, 2.5–6 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth to scabrid. Leaves cauline; blades linear, 15–50 × 0.7–1.5 cm, apex subobtuse, flattish, glabrous or scabrid; sheaths 4–8 cm, narrowly to broadly winged; contraligule oblong-lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm long. Lowest involucral bract leaf-like, up to 20 cm. Inflorescence paniculate but often appearing spike-like, 7–60 × 3–13 cm; nodes 2–3, close or rarely distant, each subtending a single partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence shortly pedunculate, ovoid-lanceolate, compound, 5–15 cm; bracteoles prominent, stiff. Spikelets unisexual, in clusters of 2–3; female spikelets ovoid, 4–5 mm; male spikelets lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm. Glumes ovate to lanceolate, 3–5 mm, acuminate, sides membranous, pale brown to mid-reddish brown. Stamens 3; anther linear, ca. 2 mm. Achenes ovoid-globose to ± depressed-ovoid, obscurely trigonous, 2–2.3 × 2.3–2.5 mm, rounded, shiny white or slightly purplish grey, reticulate or undulate-rugose, usually glabrous; disk 3-lobed, lobes semicircular, brown, acute, obtuse, reflexed.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 695, H. C. Tang 1257; HK sheet 41683.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Malaysia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, tropical Africa, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forest floors and grasslands.

Scleria corymbosa Roxb. 傘房珍珠茅
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 3: 574. 1832; FGD 8: 354. 2007; FOC 23: 263. 2010.
Scleria ridleyi C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 686. 1894; FHK 400. 1861; FKH 303. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome woody, horizontal. Culms solitary, 60–200 cm tall, 0.5–3 cm thick, triquetrous, glabrous, scabrid along angles. Leaves cauline; blade broadly linear, 30–70 cm × 6–25 mm, abruptly acute to subobtuse, flat; sheath 6 – 15 cm, green to brown; contraligule depressed-deltoid, brown. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest up to 47 cm, the lowest one longer than inflorescence, glabrous. Inflorescence paniculate, 35–80 cm; nodes 3–5, each subtending 2 – 3 long-pedunculate, corymbiform partial inflorescence. Spikelets bisexual and male, intermingled, solitary or in groups of 2–5; bisexual spikelets ovoid, 4–5 mm, with a male spikelet in axils of the uppermost glume; male spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 4–4.5 cm long, 7–8-flowered. Glumes broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, acute, mucronate, sides dark chestnut brown, glabrous. Stamens 3, anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Achenes ovoid, trigonous, 3–3.5 × 2–2.5 mm, apex ± acute, base with 3 shallow depressions, shiny white, smooth, glabrous; disk triangular, adnate to base of achene.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 1534.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Wet and swampy forest floors, less frequently in open wet grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Scleria harlandii Hance 圓稈珍珠茅（夏蘭珍珠茅）

Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 5, 5: 248. 1866; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 216. 1961; FYN 15: 672. 2003; FGD 8: 357. 2007; FOC 23: 268. 2010.
Scleria purpurascens auct. non Steud.: FHK 400. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with reddish brown scales. Culms to more than 1 m tall, ca. 6 mm thick, terete to sometimes slightly triquetrous, shiny, glabrous. Leaf sheath 4–6 cm, yellow with purple lines, tightly embracing culm, thinly leathery, wingless, sometimes pilose, apical ones often overlapped; contraligule semicircular or subtriangular, 2–3 mm, purple, margin ciliate, cilia ca. 1 mm; leaf blade linear, ca. 30 × 0.6–0.8 cm, thinly leathery, slightly scabrous, glabrous, apex attenuate. Involucral bracts leaf-like, basalmost to 35 cm, sheathing; bractlets setaceous, nearly equalling spikelets, hairy, base auricled. Inflorescences compound paniculate, to 40 cm, with 8–9 branches; branches ca. 5 cm, triangular, axes often pubescent. Spikelets 1–2, light rust-coloured to purple, 3–4 mm, mostly unisexual. Male spikelets oblong-ovoid to narrowly ovoid, apex truncate to acute; glumes 1.4–3 mm, membranous, with rusty lines. Female spikelets usually at base of branch, narrowly ovoid, apex acuminate; glumes broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, ± keeled, margin apically ciliate, apex cuspidate. Male flowers: stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 1 mm; connective apex ca. 0.3 mm. Female flowers: stigmas 3. Achene white, subspherical or ovoid, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., bluntly 3-sided, smooth, shiny, only apical part sparsely hairy, apex tipped; disk yellow with light rust-coloured lines, ca. 2 mm in diam., 3-lobed; lobes triangular, margins reflexed, apex acute to acuminate or 2–3-lobed.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Shek O, Tai Po Kau. J. C. Shaw 478; L. T. Lo 164; H. C. Tang 1942.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Cambodia.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by C. Harland and J. Lamont from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Scleria laxa R. Br. 疏鬆珍珠茅
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 240. 1810; FGD 8: 360. 2007; FOC 23: 264. 2010.

Annual; rhizome absent. Stem very slender, smooth, 1–2-noded below the inflorescence, 20–45 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick. Leaves narrowly linear, 5–15 cm × 1–3 mm, apex rather abruptly narrowed to the ± obtuse tip, glabrous, smooth or scabrid on the margins and the main veins near the apex, 3–5-veined; sheaths narrow, wingless, upper ones glabrous, lower ones often leafless, pubescent, purplish; contraligule short, broadly rounded, ciliate. Inflorescence occupying by far the greater part of the stem, narrow, very loose, consisting of about 3 very remote fascicles of partial panicles, the terminal panicle not larger than the lateral ones, 1–2 cm; peduncles 3–4 together at the nodes, exserted from the sheaths, ± noding, filiform, slightly incrassate at the apex, 2–4 cm; primary bracts erect, as long as or overtopping the inflorescence. Spikelets unisexual; male spikelets about as long as their peduncles, linear-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 mm; stamen 1; anther oblong-linear, 0.7–1 mm; female spikelets 3.5–4 mm, without a trace of a male part; glumes ovate, acute or mucronate. Cupula very small, 0.7 mm wide, hardly lobed. Achenes globose, ca. 1.7 mm across, deeply longitudinally ribbed, with 3 of the ribs more prominent, ± trabeculate between the ribs, slightly tuberculate at the top, umbonulate, glabrous, shining, white, the ribs not all reaching the base of the achene, but leaving a smooth triangular area above each disk-lobe; disk small, shortly 3-lobed; lobes obtuse, semi-orbicular.

Locality: Shek O, Kwun Tong, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 1258; HK sheet 13874, 39380.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian; Philippines, Queensland, New Guinea.
Ecology: Grasslands of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.

Scleria levis Retz. 毛果珍珠茅
Obs. 4: 13. 1786; FHK 400. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 5: 311. 2002; FYN 15: 673. 2003; FGD 8: 358. 2007; FOC 23: 266. 2010.
Scleria hebecarpa Nees in Wight, Contrib. Bot. Ind. 117. 1834; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 213. 1961.
Scleria pubescens Steud., Syn. Cyp. 168. 1855; FHK 400. 1861.
Scleria hebecarpa Nees var. pubescens (Steud.) C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 689. 1894; FRPS 11: 214. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome woody, creeping, covered with brown scales. Culms 30–90 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, triquetrous, glabrous to puberulent. Leaves cauline; blade linear, 18–35 cm × 2–8(–12) mm, glabrous, scabrid on the margin and along the midvein abaxially, gradually narrowed towards apex, flat; sheath 5–8 cm, winged, green to reddish or purplish brown; contraligule shallowly rounded, pubescent. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 13 cm, upper bracts and bracteoles prominent, setaceous. Inflorescence paniculate, open to compact, sometimes appearing head-like, 5–13 × 1.5–2.5 cm; nodes 3–4, each subtending a single partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence sessile or shortly pedunculate, ovate-lanceolate, 2–8 cm. Spikelets female and male in groups of 2–4; female spikelets sessile, obovoid, 4–6 mm; male spikelets pedunculate, oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm. Glumes ovate, 2–4 mm, acuminate, sides membranous, mid-brown to chestnut brown. Stamens 3; anther linear, ca. 3 mm. Achenes globose, ± terete, 1.7–2.5 × 1.7–2.5 mm, rounded, white, smoothish, pubescent to glabrous; disk 3-lobed, the lobes lanceolate-triangular, acute, minutely toothed at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 753; Y. S. Lau 2544, 3138.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed from India to Myanmar, Vietnam, Japan, throughout Malesia to Queensland and New Caledonia.
Ecology: Grasslands, floors of open forests, margins of rice fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Scleria lithosperma (L.) Sw. 石果珍珠茅
Prodr. 18. 1788; FHK 399. 1861; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 206. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 312. 2000; FGD 8: 354. 2007; FOC 23: 263. 2010.
Scirpus lithosperma L., Sp. Pl. 51. 1753.

Perennial; rhizomatous woody. Culms loosely tufted, base bulbous, 40–80 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, glabrous. Leaves cauline; blade narrowly linear, 8–40 cm × 1.5–4 mm, gradually narrowed, subobtuse; sheath 6–9 cm, reddish brown, puberulent; contraligule depressed-rounded or depressed-deltoid, ciliate. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 10 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, with 3–4 nodes each subtending a single, open, pedunculate narrow partial inflorescence, sometimes the whole inflorescence becoming ± spike-like; peduncles filiform. Spikelets bisexual, 1–3, ovate-turbinate, 3–5 mm long. Glumes ovate, 3–4 mm long, acuminate or acute, mucronate, sides membranous, glabrous, rusty brown, stamens 1(–2). Achenes obovoid-ellipsoidal, trigonous, 2–2.8 × 1.7–2 mm, apex rounded, base cuneate with 3 depressions, shiny white, smooth; disk small, annular.

Locality: Aberdeen, To Tei Wan, Middle Island. Y. W. Lam 1514; J. C. Shaw 559; HK sheet 8209.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropics.
Ecology: Semi-dry open grassy places, floors and margins of forests, particularly near the coast. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Scleria parvula Steud. 小型珍珠茅
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 174. 1855; FYN 15: 670. 2003; FGD 8: 360. 2007; FOC 23: 264. 2010.
Scleria biflora auct. non Roxb.: FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 208. 1961; Check List HK Plants 103. 1993.
Scleria tessellata auct. non Willd.: FHK 399. 1861.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms tufted, (10–)30–90 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, triquetrous, scabrid on angles. Leaves cauline; blade linear, 20–35 cm × 2–6 mm, acute, flattish, glabrous, scabrid on upper margin; sheath 3–10 cm, narrowly winged or wingless, greenish to reddish purple, pubescent along the wing; contraligule rounded-truncate, margin ciliate. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 20 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, 10–20 cm; nodes 2–4, distant, each subtending 1–3 partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence sessile to long-pedunculate, ± simple, narrowly elliptic, 1–4 cm, bracteoles rather prominent. Spikelets unisexual; female spikelets somewhat turbinate, 4–5 mm; male spikelets lanceolate, 4–5 mm, peduncle 1–3 mm. Glumes ovate, 3.5 mm long, acute, mucronate, sides membranous, pale brown to reddish brown, keel green. Stamens 3; anther linear, 1–1.5 mm. Achenes globose to ± ellipsoidal, 2–2.3 × 1.7–2 mm, shiny white, cancellate with regular, longitudinally oblong lacunae, glabrous to ± rufous pubescent; disk deeply 3-lobed, lobes ovate to elliptic-ovate, without deep pit at sinus between lobes.

Locality: Quarry Bay. Y. S. Lau 2546.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang; Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Philippines, New Guinea, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Wet, open grasslands, swamps and occasionally floors of open forests. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.

Scleria rugosa R. Br. 皺果珍珠茅
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 240. 1810; FTW ed. 2, 5: 312. 2000; FYN 15: 669. 2003; FGD 8: 360. 2007; FOC 23: 263. 2010.
Scleria onoei Franch. & Savat., Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 122, 549. 1879; FRPS 11: 209. 1961.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 10–35 cm tall, 0.7–1.5 mm thick, triquetrous, pubescent. Leaves cauline; blade narrowly linear, 5–15 cm × 2–4 mm, ± obtuse, folded, pubescent; sheath 1.5–3.5 cm long, narrowly winged or wingless, pale to midbrown; contraligule rounded-deltoid to suborbicular, ciliate. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 14 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, 9–20 cm; nodes 2–3, distant, each subtending 1(–2) partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence sessile to shortly pedunculate, simple, 1–2 cm, with few spikelets. Spikelets unisexual, solitary or in pairs; female spikelets broadly obovate, 3–4 mm; male spikelets shortly pedunculate, lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm. Glumes ovate, 2.5–4 mm long, acute, sides membranous, pale green sometimes tingled with reddish brown, keel green. Stamens 1. Achenes globose or broadly obovoid-globose, terete, 1.2–1.8 × 1.2–1.8 mm, white, usually smooth or transversely wrinkled above, rarely trabeculate, glabrous; disk shallowly 3-lobed, lobes suborbicular, densely glandular.

Locality: Fung Mun Au. HK sheet 34219.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Japan, Malaysia, Micronesia, Australia and New Caledonia.
Ecology: Open, wet grasslands and rice fields. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.

Scleria terrestris (L.) Fassett 高稈珍珠茅
Rhodora 26: 159. 1924; FTW ed. 2, 5: 313 2000; FYN 15: 676. 2003; FGD 8: 358. 2007; FOC 23: 265. 2010.
Zizania terrestris L., Sp. Pl. 2: 991. 1753.
Scleria elata Thw., Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 353. 1864; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 211. 1961.
Scleria radula Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 4, 18: 232. 1862; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 206. 1961.
Scleria vestita Boeck., Linnaea 38: 482. 1875. nom. illeg. (type same as Scleria radula Hance.)
Scleria laevis Retz. var. scaberrima Benth., FHK 400. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with purple scales. Culms sometimes climbing, (0.6–)1–4 m tall, 3–6 mm thick, triquetrous, scabird, Leaves cauline; often closely spaced; blade linear, 15–40(–60) cm × (5–)7–20 mm, glabrous or scabrid, apex long caudate, flattish; sheath 6–15 cm, triquetrous, winged or not, reddish or purplish brown; contraligule crescent-shaped or depressed rounded, 2–4 mm, ciliate or glabrescent. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 40 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, 25–50 × 5–10 cm; nodes 2–4, rather distant, each subtending a single partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence long-pedunculate, ovate-pyramidal to broadly ovoid, compound, 4–14 cm; bracteoles indistinct. Spikelets solitary or in groups of 2–3; female spikelets sessile, broadly ovoid, 3.7–5 mm; male spikelets lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm. Glumes broadly ovate, 3.5–4 mm, abruptly acute. Achene 2.5–3 × 2.5–2.8 mm, spherical, shiny white to dark purplish, smooth or indistinctly scrobiculate, puberulent to glabrous; disk shallowly 3-lobed, lobes broadly triangular, obtuse to rounded or ± emarginate.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Sha Lo Tung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool. J. C. Shaw 624; Y. S. Lau 1942; K. L. Yip 4087.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Chongqing, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Japan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Floors of forests, thickets and wet grasslands.
Notes: The type specimens of Scleria radula (Hance 1157) and Scleria laevis var. scaberrima (Harland s.n.) were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Scolopia chinensis (Lour.) Clos 刺柊
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. Ser. 4, 8: 249. 1857; FHK 19. 1861; FGZ 179. 1956; FHN 1: 452, fig. 249. 1964; FFJ 4: 12, fig. 13. 1989; FGD 3: 98. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 16, pl. 4, fig. 1–3. 1999.
Phoberos chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 318. 1790.
Phoberos cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 318. 1790.
Scolopia crenata auct. non Clos: FKH 37. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, sometimes with stout spines on trunk and branchlets. Petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 4 –7 × 2–4 cm, leathery, base rounded to broadly cuneate, with 1 gland on each side, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or rarely serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 2– 6 cm. Flowers pale yellow. Sepals ovate-triangular, 1–2 mm, glabrous on both surfaces, margin ciliate. Petals long-obovate, longer than sepals, glabrous, margin ciliate. Anthers globose, connective-appendages triangular, as long as connectives, apex hairy; disc fleshy, 10-lobed. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, with 2–3 parietal placentas; ovules 2 per placenta, pendulous; styles as long as stamens; stigmas slightly 3-lobed. Berry globose, ca. 4 mm in diam. Seeds 2–6.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2261; Y. S. Lau 209, 1999.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: Late autumn to early winter; fruiting: Late winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Scolopia saeva (Hance) Hance 廣東刺柊
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. Ser. 4, 8: 217. 1862; FHN 1: 452. 1964; FFJ 4: 13. 1989; FGD 3: 98, fig. 67. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 18, pl. 4: 7. 1999.
Phoberos saeva Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 825. 1852.
Scolopia cinnamomifolia Gagnep., Fl. Indo-Chine 1: 207. 1939.

Shrub or small tree; trunk usually armed with hard spines; young branches glabrous, lenticellate. Petioles 0.8–1 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 6– 8 × 3– 5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, not glandular, apex abruptly acuminate, margin remotely and shallowly repandserrate, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary or terminal, shorter than leaves. Sepals ovate, ca. 1.2 mm, margin ciliate. Petals obovate, two times as long as sepals, margin ciliate. Stamens ca. 6 mm; anthers ovoid, connectives-appendages triangular, glabrous; disc 8-lobed. Ovary with 2 or 3 parietal placentas, ovules 2 per placenta; styles thick, shorter than stamens. Berry reddish, ovoid, ca. 8 × 3 – 5 mm. Seeds long-ellipsoid, angled.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 689; K. L. Yip 4228; C. P. Lau 112.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Timber.

Scoparia dulcis L. 野甘草
Sp. Pl. 116. 1753; FHK 252. 1861; FKH 189. 1912; FOC 18: 21. 1998; FGD 4: 382, fig. 230. 2000.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.3–1 m tall, many‑branched; branches ribbed to narrowly winged. Leaves usually in whorls of 3; leaf blade rhomboid‑ovate to rhomboid‑lanceolate, 3.6 × 1.5 cm, upper ones small and narrow, glandular punctate, margin toothed above middle, sometimes slightly double serrate, or subentire, apex obtuse. Flowers usually axillary, 1 or 2 per node. Pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx lobed to base; lobes 4, ovate‑oblong, ca. 2 mm, margin ciliate. Corolla white, ca. 4 mm in diam.; tube densely hairy at throat; upper lobe slightly larger than others. Stamens exserted, stigma truncate to 2‑parted. Capsules 2–3 cm in diam.; columella persistent.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1215, 1914; Y. S. Lau 185.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; native to tropical America, now through tropics and subtropics as a weed.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Scurrula parasitica L. 紅花寄生
Sp. Pl. 1: 110. 1753; FYN 3: 362. 1983; FGD 1: 220. 1987, p.p.; FRPS 24: 114. 1988; FOC 5: 229. 2003.
Loranthus chinensis auct. non DC: Benth., FHK 141. 1861; FKH 229. 1912.
Loranthus gracilifolius auct. non Schult.: FHN 2: 459, fig. 523. 1965.
Loranthus parasiticus (L.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 15(3): 232. 1919.
Taxillus parasiticus (L.) S. T. Chiu, Taiwania 41(2): 159. 1996.

Shrub 0.5–1 m tall; branchlets and leaves densely covered with stellate hairs when young, later glabrescent, greyish brown, lenticellate. Petiole 5 – 6 mm; leaf blade papery, ovate, 5–8 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse, lateral veins 5 – 6 on each side of midvein, conspicuous. Racemes solitary or 2–3-fasciculate, axillary, sometimes borne on leafless nodes, 3–6-flowered, brownish hairy; peduncle 2–3 mm; bracts ovate to triangular, ca. 1 mm. Calyx turbinate, 2–2.5 mm, limb annular. Mature bud tubular, tip ellipsoidal, apex acute. Corolla red, slightly curved, 2–2.5 cm, apical portion inflated, lobes lanceolate, 3–8 mm, reflexed. Filaments 2–3 mm; anthers 1.5–2 mm. Stigma subcapitate. Fruit reddish yellow, pyriform, 10 × 3 mm, base tapering into a stipe, smooth.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, King's Park, Tai Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai, Wu Kau Tang, A Ma Wat. Y. S. Lau 2025, 3245; P. S. Choi 324.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Often growing on trees of Citrus maxima, Clausena lansium and Camellia oleifera. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Scutellaria barbata D. Don 半枝蓮
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 109. 1825; FRPS 65(2): 229, pl. 49: 5. 1977; FOC 17: 99. 1994; FGD 3: 406. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 532. 1998.
Scutellaria rivularis Wall. ex Benth., Numer. List n. 214. 1829; FKH 211. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 10–30 cm tall. Stems erect from short, thick rhizomes, glabrous or young parts sparsely puberulous. Leaves papery; petiole 1–3 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade narrowly ovate to ovate, 10–25 × 7– 15 mm, base broadly cuneate to subtruncate, apex shortly acuminate or acute, sometimes obtuse, margin remotely and obtusely shallow dentate, subglabrous to sparsely appressed pubescent along veins. Flowers axillary; lower bracts similar to stem leaves, to 8 mm, reduced upward, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially sparsely pubescent only on veins; bracteoles needle‑like, ca. 0.5 mm, inserted at middle of pedicels. Pedicel 1–2 mm, puberulent. Calyx ca. 2 mm, puberulent along veins abaxially, margin ciliolate, to 4.5 mm in fruit; scutellum ca. 1 mm, to 2 mm in fruit. Corolla purple blue, 9–13 mm, pubescent abaxially; tube saccate in front at base, gradually dilated from middle; limb 2‑lipped; upper lip semiorbicular, galeate, ca. 1.5 mm, emarginate at apex; lower lip broadly ovate, 3‑lobed, middle lobe emarginate, lateral lobes triangular‑ovate, ca. 1.5 mm wide, apex acute. Nutlets brown, oblate, ca. 1 mm in diam., warty.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po, Fung Hang, Sai Kung. P. S. Choi 176, 450; HK sheet 39094.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Farmlands, streamsides, grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Scutellaria formosana N. E. Br. 藍花黃芩
Gard. Chron. Ser. 3. 16: 212. 1894; FKH 211. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 142. 1977; FOC 17: 81. 1994; FGD 3: 402. 1995.

Perennial herbs to 30 cm tall, with ± woody rhizomes. Stems ascending, simple or few‑branched, rooting at basal nodes, subglabrous, often purplish. Leaves subleathery; petioles 8–12 mm, subglabrous, glandular; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3–8 × 1.5–3.3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin with 3‑ or 4‑undulate‑serration on each side, adaxially shiny, abaxially sometimes tinged purple, glabrous and glandular dotted on both surfaces, sometimes sparsely puberulous on veins abaxially. Flowers in terminal racemes of 7–17 cm; bracts narrowly rhombic, ca. 2 mm, pubescent. Pedicel ca. 4 mm, densely pubescent. Calyx ca. 3 mm, ca. 4 mm. in fruit, pubescent abaxially, glandular; scutellum spreading, semiorbicular, to 2 mm. Corolla blue, ca. 2.5 cm, glandular puberulent abaxially; tube ca. 2 cm, base bent, throat to 6 mm wide, villous near base inside; upper lip triangular‑ovate, ca. 8 mm wide; middle lobe of lower lip suborbicular, ca. 4.5 mm in diam., emarginate; lateral lobes ovate, ca. 3 mm wide. Nutlets tuberculate.

Locality: Sham Tseng, Tuen Mun, Wong Lung Hang, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2996; Y. W. Lam 620; K. L. Yip 4436.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering & fruiting: Jul. –Feb. of the following year.

Scutellaria indica L. 韓信草
Sp. Pl. 2: 600. 1753; FHK 278. 1861; FKH 211. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 172. 1977; FOC 17: 87. 1994; FGD 3: 404. fig. 254. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 532, pl. 241. 1998.

Perennial herbs, 8–28 cm tall. Stems usually dark purple, 1–few, ascending‑erect from a short rhizome, puberulous, especially on angles and apex. Petioles 4–15(–28) mm, densely puberulous; leaf blade cordate‑orbicular to orbicular‑ovate, or elliptic, 1–2.6(–3) × 1–2.3 cm, base rounded to cordate, apex rounded to acute, margin crenate, puberulous or strigose, densely so on abaxial surface. Flowers opposite, in a terminal 1‑sided raceme of 4–8(– 12) cm; lower bracts leaf‑like, ovate, to 1.7 cm, crenate; upper ones sessile, ovate to elliptic, 3–6 × 1–2.5 mm, margin entire, puberulent. Pedicels 2.5–3 mm, puberulent. Calyx ca. 2.5 mm, hirsute and puberulent; scutellum ca. 1.5 mm, erect, dilated to 3 mm in fruit. Corolla blue‑purple, 1.3–1.8 cm, sparsely puberulent outside, pubescent on lips inside, to ca. 4.5 mm wide at throat; middle lobe of lower lip dark purple spotted, orbicular‑ovate, slightly constricted at middle, apex emarginate; lateral lobes ovate. Nutlets chestnut to dark brown, ovoid, less than 1 mm in diam., tuberculate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 112; Y. S. Lau 2246; Y. S. Lau 2987.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Scutellaria tayloriana Dunn 偏花黃芩
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 8: 166. 1913; FRPS 65(2): 170. 1977; FOC 17: 87. 1994; FGD 3: 404. 1995.

Perennial herbs, 10–35 cm tall, sometimes with trailing rhizomes. Stems erect to ascending, covered with white multicellular hairs. Leaves in 3 or 4 pairs; petioles 2–5(–9) cm, those of mid stem leaves longest, densely white villose; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑oblong, lower ones 2–4 × 1.8–2.7 cm, middle ones 5–9 × 4.5–7 cm, base cordate or rounded, apex rounded or obtuse, margin shallowly undulate‑crenate, both surfaces white strigose especially on veins, orange glandular dotted abaxially. Racemes terminal, secund, 7–15 cm; peduncle 1–4.5 cm; bracts sessile, gradually narrowed toward apex, ovate, ca. 4 × 2 mm, margin entire. Pedicel ca. 2 mm, villous. Calyx ca. 2.5 mm, densely pubescent. Corolla purplish to purple‑blue, (1.5–)1.8–2.5(–3) cm, bent at base, to 6 mm wide at throat, sparsely puberulent abaxially; middle lobe of lower lip semiorbicular; lateral lobes ovate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. P. S. Choi 486; HK sheet 32233, 39913.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (Ford 107, E) was collected by C. Ford from Tai Mo Shan in March 1885.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (Ford 107, E) was collected by C. Ford from Tai Mo Shan in March 1885.

records.text:
Sebastiania chamaelea (L.) Müll. Arg. 地楊桃（色柏木）

Prodr. 15(2): 1175. 1866; FKH 241. 1912; FRPS 44(3): 4. 1997; FGD 5: 125, fig. 76. 2003.

Tragia chamaelea L., Sp. Pl. 981. 1753.


Perennial herb, 20–60 cm tall, with stout tap root; stems more or less woody at base, much branched, glabrous or pubescent when young. Leaves alternate, thick-papery; petioles short, ca. 2 mm, usually pubescent; stipules persistent, ovate, ca. 1 mm, ciliate; leaf blade linear or linear-lanceolate, 20–55 × 2–10 mm, base slightly attenuate, apex obtuse, margin serrulate, pubescent abaxially; midvein prominent on both surfaces, lateral veins obscure. Spikes 5–12 mm, terminal or leaf-opposed, usually with 1 or several female flowers at the base and numerous male flowers on the upper part. Male flowers: sepals 3, ovate, ca. 1 mm, margin serrulate; stamens 3, anthers globose, filaments shorter than anthers. Female flowers: sepals 3, slightly larger than in male flowers, broad-ovate, margin fimbriate, with 2 glands at base adaxially; ovary triangular-globose, 3-locular, glabrous, aculeate; styles 3, free. Capsules triangular-globose, 3–4 mm in diam., with 2 rows of prickles along the ridges.


Locality: Lung Kwu Chau, Lantau Island. HK sheet 25102, 40212.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; S and SE Asia, Australia.

Ecology: Sandy fields near seashore, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Mar. –Nov.

Sechium edule (Jacq.) Swartz 佛手瓜（合掌瓜）
Fl. Ind. Occ. 2: 1150. 1800; FRPS 73(1): 277, pl. 65: 5 – 8. 1986; FFJ 5: 252, fig. 236. 1993; FGD 3: 141, fig. 103. 1995.
Sicyos edulis Jacq., Enum. Syst. Pl. 32. 1760.

Stem angled and sulcate. Petioles slender, glabrous, 3 –15 cm; leaf blade membranous, ovate-cordate in outline, 8 –20 × 8 –20 cm, base cordate, apex short-acuminate, margin entire or denticulate, polygonal or 3–5-lobed, slightly scabrous adaxially, puberulous abaxially. Male inflorescences: racemose 10–30-flowered; peduncle 8 –30 cm long; pedicels 1–6 mm. Male flowers: calyx-tube short, lobes explanate, 5 –7 mm; corolla pale yellow, rotate. Female flowers: pedicels 1–1.5 cm; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary obovoid, 5-angled, style 2–3 mm, stigma 2 mm broad. Fruit pale green, obovoid, slightly hispid, 8–15 cm long, 6– 8 cm in diam., 5- sulcate in upper part. Seed large, 10 x 7 cm, ovate, compressed.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 72; H. C. Tang 1455; HK sheet 12124.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Sichuan (cultivated or naturalized); native to America.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Securidaca inappendiculata Hassk. 蟬翼藤（蟬翼木）
Pl. Jav. Rar. 295. 1848; FHN 1: 368, fig. 188. 1964; FYN 3: 262, pl. 73: 1–6. 1983; FGD 2: 60. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 141. 1997; C. A. Pendry, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 524. 2001.
Securidaca tavoyana Wall. ex A. W. Benn., Fl. Brit. India 1: 208. 1872; FKH 39. 1912.
Securidaca scandens Buch.-Ham. in Wall. ex Benth., FHK 45. 1861, not Jacquin (1760) nor Poiret (1806).

Scandent shrub. Branchlets densely appressed pubescent. Petioles 0.5–1 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery or subleathery, elliptic or obovate-oblong, 5–12 × 2.5–6 cm, base obtuse to subrounded, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous adaxially, densely white appressed pubescent abaxially; midvein prominent abaxially, impressed adaxially, lateral veins 10–12 pairs. Panicles 10–15 cm, pubescent; bracts caducous, minute, subulate, pubescent. Pedicels 0.8–1.2 cm, glabrous. Sepals 5, unequal, outer 3 oblong-ovate, subequal, small, ca. 2.5 mm, apex obtuse, ciliate; inner 2 petaloid, large, ca. 7 × 5 mm, base clawed, apex obtuse, ciliate. Petals 3, purplish red, connate at base; lateral petals obtriangular, ca. 5 × 2.5 mm, apex truncate, keel suborbicular, ca. 8 mm, apex with cockscomb-shaped appendage. Stamens 8 mm. Ovary subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam.; style inclined to one side, curved. Samara compressed globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; wing woody, oblong, 7–8 × 1.5–2 cm, with strongly curved veins, base narrower, apex obtuse. Seed ovoid, ca. 7 mm in diam., brownish.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Parker, Tai Po Kau, Nam Chung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1442; HK sheet 288, 289.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Fibre, medicinal (folklore).

Sedum lineare Thunb. 佛甲草
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 430. 1784; FRPS 34(1): 144, pl. 32: 17 – 24. 1984; FGD 3: 49. 1995; FOC 8: 250. 2001.

Perennial succulent herb, glabrous throughout. Stems 10 – 20 cm tall, erect or ± diffuse, rooting at the nodes. Leaves sessile, in whorls of 3 or 4, sometimes alternate on the upper part of flowering stems; leaf blade linear or linear oblanceolate, 1 – 2.5 × 0.1 – 0.2 cm, base spurred; spurs truncate or obtuse, apex obtuse. Cymes terminal, with 2 – 3 secund branches, 4 – 5 cm in diam. Flowers sessile, but with one flower between the branches, shortly pedicellate. Sepals 5, narrowly lanceolate, usually unequal, 1.5 – 6 mm. Petals 5, yellow, elliptic-lanceolate, 4 – 6 × 1 – 1.5 mm. Stamens 10, in 2 whorls, shorter than the petals. Carpels 5, 4 – 5 mm, connate at the base, apically narrowed into a short style. Follicles stellately spreading, many-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 859, 2788.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Senecio scandens Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don 千里光
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 178. 1825; FKH 148. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(1–2): 143. 1968; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1056. 1998; FRPS 77(1): 294. 1999; FGD 8: 218, fig. 130. 2007.
Senecio chinensis (Spreng.) DC., Prodr. 6: 363. 1838; FHK 190. 1861.
Cineraria chinensis Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 549. 1826.

Perennial herbs with rhizomes; stem elongate and reclining, from 0.5–5 m, striate, branches many, pubescent or glabrescent, turning woody when old. Leaf petioles 0.5–2 cm, pubescent or subglabrous; leaf blade ovate lanceolate to elongate‑deltoid in shape, 4.5–8 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or truncate, apex acuminate, margin irregularly dentate, pinnately‑veined, adaxial surfaces subglabrous or puberulous, abaxial surfaces puberulous especially along veins. Leaves in upper stem portion appeared smaller in size, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, apex attenuate. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2–2.2 cm across, arranged as compound thyrse form; peduncles 0.7–2.5 cm, puberulous. Involucres cylindric campanulate, 6–7 × 3 mm, base with about 8 linear‑subulate bracteoles as calyculus of 2–3 mm; phyllaries 12–13, herbaceous, linear‑lanceolate, acuminate, margin scarious and ciliate near the apex, abaxially puberulous or glabrous, 3‑veined. Marginal ligulate florets 7– 10, tube 4 mm, ligule oblong with length 9–10 mm, width 2 mm, apex obtuse and minutely 3‑lobed, colour yellow, with 4 veins. Disk tubular florets 5–6 mm, funnelform with apical half broaden and lower half narrowed, 5‑lobed at apex, yellow. Cypselae cylindric, 3 × 0.7–0.8 mm, ribbed, brown, puberulous. Pappus white, 5–6 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 12410 (CUHK); Y. Wong 084 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1370.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Bhutan, Nepal, Japan, Indochina, Philippines.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Senecio stauntonii DC. 閩粵千里光
Prodr. 6: 363. 1838; FHK 190. 1861; FKH 148. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(1–2): 146. 1968; FRPS 77(1): 293. 1999; FGD 8: 219. 2007.

Perennial rhizomatous herbs; stem ascending and subscandent, 30–100 cm tall, angular, branched, glabrous. Basal leaves withered at flowering stage. Cauline leaves sessile, narrowly oblong‑lanceolate, 4–14.5 × 0.6– 2.5 cm, base auriculate and semi‑amplexicaul, apex acuminate to attenuate, margin toothed, pinnately‑veined, pubescent or pilose on adaxial surfaces, and along veins and margins on abaxial sides, sometimes glabrous beneath. Upper leaves smaller and narrower. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, in loose corymbose arrangement; peduncle 1.5–3 cm, glabrous or loosely puberulous. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 13 in 1 series, herbaceous, linear‑lanceolate, 6–8 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute or acuminate, margin scarious and ciliate near apex, abaxial surface glabrous, base with 6–8 linear‑subulate bracteoles 2–3 mm. Marginal ray florets female, ligule oblong, 7–8 × 2.5–3 mm, tube 3.5 mm, apex obtuse and minutely 3‑lobed, 4‑veined, colour yellow. Disk tubular florets bisexual, funnelform, 6–6.5 mm, apical half broaden, lower half narrowed, apex 5‑lobed and papillose hairy, yellow. Cypselae brown, cylindric, 3 mm, ribbed and puberulent. Pappus white, 5–5.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Fo Tan, Shing Mun, High Island, Po Toi Islands, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 778; S. Y. Hu 6318, 8878 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of forests. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.

Senna alata (L.) Roxb. 翅莢決明
Fl. Indica 2: 349. 1824; H. S. Irwin & Barneby, Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 35(2): 460. 1982.
Cassia alata L., Sp. Pl. 378. 1753; FRPS 39: 131. 1988; FGD 5: 182. 2003.

Shrub, 1.5–3 m tall. Branches stout, green. Leaves 30– 70 cm; petioles and leaf rachis winged, with 2 ridges along the adaxial surface; stipules triangular; leaflets 6 –12 pairs; petiolules very short; blade obovate-oblong or oblong, 8 –15 × 3.5–7.5 cm, base obliquely truncate, apex obtuse and mucronate, margin entire, thinly leathery; veins conspicuously raised abaxially. Racemes terminal and axillary, long pedunculate, 10 – 50 cm. Sepals oblong, 1 – 2 cm. Petals yellow, with purple veins, ovate, 2 × 1.5 cm. Stamens 7 fertile, 3 reduced. Ovary densely tawny puberulent; style filiform or gently tapering distally. Pods broadly linear in outline, 10 – 20 × 1.2 – 1.5 cm, winged lengthwise down the middle of each valve. Seeds 50– 60.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3171, 3240; P. S. Choi 271.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan (cultivated); native to tropical America, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov. – Jan.; fruiting: Jan.– Feb.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia alata L. previously (Check List HK Plants 134. 2002; 51. 2004).

Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia alata L. previously (Check List HK Plants 134. 2002; 51. 2004).

Senna occidentalis (L.) Link 望江南（野扁豆）
Handbuch 2: 140. 1831.
Cassia occidentalis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 377. 1753; FHK 98. 1861; FKH 89. 1912; FHN 2: 233. 1965; FRPS 39: 125. 1988; FGD 5: 180. 2003; FGX 2: 464. 2005.

Erect subshrub, 0.8 – 1.5 m tall, glabrous. Branches few, herbaceous, angled. Stipules membranous, ovate-lanceolate, caducous. Leaves ca. 20 cm; with a large, brownish, conical gland near the base of petiole; petiolules 1 – 1.5 mm; leaflets 4 – 5 pairs, membranous, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 4 – 9 × 2 – 3.5 cm, apex acuminate, ciliolate. Inflorescence a corymbose raceme, axillary or terminal, 5 cm. Bracts linear-lanceolate or long-ovate, apex long acuminate, caducous. Flowers ca. 2 cm. Sepals unequal, outer ones suborbicular, 6 mm, inner ones ovate, 8 – 9 mm. Petals yellow, outer ones 15 × 9 – 10 mm, the rest ones to 20 × 15 mm, apex rounded, all shortly stipitate. Stamens 10, 7 fertile, 3 sterile. Pods linear-falcate, brown, compressed, 10– 13 × 0.8 – 0.9 cm, slightly curved, margin thickened, apex mucronate; fruiting pedicels 1 –1.5 cm. Seeds 30– 40, with thin septum between seeds.

Locality: Naturalized. H. C. Tang 2076; Y. S. Lau 233; P. S. Choi 272.
Distribution: SW to SE China; native to tropical America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia occidentalis L. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia occidentalis L. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).

Senna siamea (Lam.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby 鐵刀木
Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 35: 98. 1982.
Cassia siamea Lam., Encycl. 1: 648. 1785; FHN 2: 233. 1965; FGD 5: 185, fig. 108. 2003; FGX 2: 468, pl. 196: 1 – 2. 2005.

Tree, ca. 10 m tall. Bark grey, nearly smooth, slightly fissured. Young branches angled, sparsely pubescent. Stipules linear, caducous. Leaves 20–30 cm; petioles and rachis eglandular, puberulous; petiolules 2–3 mm; leaflets 6–10 pairs, leathery, oblong or oblong-elliptic, 3–6.5 × 1.5 – 2.5 cm, base rounded, apex obtuse and emarginate, mucronate, margin entire, glabrous adaxially, glaucous abaxially. Racemes axillary, arranged in corymbs. Bracts linear, 5 – 6 mm. Sepals suborbicular, unequal, upper ones smaller, lower ones larger, finely hairy. Petals yellow, broadly ovate, 12–14 mm, shortly stipitate. Stamens 10, 7 fertile, 3 sterile, anthers dehiscing by apical pores. Ovary sessile, white pubescent. Pods flat, 15– 30 × 1 – 1.5 cm, margin thickened, pubescent, purplish brown when mature. Seeds 10–20.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 267, 385; Y. S. Lau 905.
Distribution: Yunnan (wild), S China (cultivated); India, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Dec.– Jan.
Uses: Timber, environmental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia siamea Lam. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).
records.uses:
Timber, environmental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia siamea Lam. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).

Senna sophera (L.) Roxb. 槐葉決明（江南槐）
Fl. Ind. (ed. 2) 2: 347. 1832.
Cassia sophera L., Sp. Pl. 1: 379. 1753; FKH 89. 1912; FHN 2: 233. 1965; FRPS 39: 125. 1988; FGD 5: 181. 2003; FGX 2: 464. 2005.

Erect subshrub, 0.8 – 1.5 m tall, glabrous. Branches few, herbaceous, angled. Stipules membranous, ovate-lanceolate, caducous. Leaves ca. 20 cm; with a large, brownish, conical gland near base of petiole; petiolules 1– 1.5 mm; leaflets 5– 10 pairs, membranous, elliptic-lanceolate, 1.7–4.29 × 0.7 – 2 cm, apex acute or shortly acuminate, ciliolate. Inflorescence a corymbose raceme, axillary or terminal, 5 cm. Bracts linear-lanceolate or long ovate, apex long acuminate, caducous. Flowers ca. 2 cm. Sepals unequal, outer ones suborbicular, 6 mm, inner ones ovate, 8 – 9 mm. Petals yellow, outer ones 15 × 9 – 10 mm, the rest ones to 20 × 15 mm, apex rounded, all shortly stipitate. Stamens 10, 7 fertile, 3 sterile. Pods flat and thickened at first, subterete when mature, brown, compressed, 5 – 10 cm, slightly curved, margin thickened, apex mucronate; fruiting pedicels 1–1.5 cm. Seeds 30 – 40, with thin septum between seeds.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 462; L. T. Lo 40; P. S. Choi 277.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Roadsides. Flowering: Jul.– Sep.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), edible (young leaves and pods).
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia sophera L. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).

Medicinal (folklore), edible (young leaves and pods).
