Senna sulfurea (DC. ex Collad.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby 粉葉決明
Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 35: 78. 1982.
Cassia glauca Lam., Encycl. 1: 647. 1785; FKH 89. 1912; FRPS 39: 136, pl. 46: 7 – 8. 1988; FGD 5: 184. 2003.
Cassia sulfurea DC. ex Collad., Hist. Nat. Med. Casses 84– 85. 1816.

Shrub or small tree. Branchlets angulate, sparsely pubescent, glabrescent. Stipules linear, caducous. Leaves 5 –30 cm including the petiole, between the lowest 2 pairs of leaflets each with a clavate gland on the leaf rachis adaxially; petioles 3.5–6.5 cm; petiolules ca. 3 mm; leaflets (4–)5(–6) pairs, ovate or elliptic, 3.5–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex obtuse or inconspicuously emarginate, green adaxially, glaucous abaxially. Racemes axillary. Sepals ovate or orbicular, unequal, upper three 3–4 mm, lower two 8 mm. Petals yellow or deeply yellow, ovate or obovate, 2–2.5 cm, 5-veined. Stamens 10, lower 2 with longer filaments. Ovary filiform, hairy. Pod flat, straight, linear, 15–20 × 1.2–1.8 cm, dehiscent, apex long beaked, fruit neck ca. 1.5 cm, fruiting pedicels 2.5–3 cm. Seeds 20–30.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan (cultivated); India, Sri Lanka, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Australia and Polynesia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Senna surattensis (Burm. f.) H. S. Irwin & Barneby 黃槐決明（黃槐）
Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 35: 81. 1982.
Cassia surattensis Burm. f., Fl. Indica 97. 1768; FHN 2: 232. 1965; FRPS 39: 136, pl. 46: 1 – 6. 1988; FGD 5: 184, fig. 107. 2003; FGX 2: 468, pl. 196: 3 – 6. 2005.

Shrub or small tree, 4 – 7 m tall, many-branched. Bark smooth, greyish brown. Branchlets ridged. Young branchlets, leaf rachis and petioles pubescent. Stipules linear, curved, 6– 8 mm. Leaves 10– 15 cm including the petiole; rachis slightly bilaterally compressed, with 2–3 clavate glands between the lowest 2 –3 pairs and the apical pair; petiolules ca. 2 mm; leaflets 7 –9 pairs, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 2– 4(–5) × 1.4 –2 cm, base obtuse to subrounded, apex broadly obtuse to rounded and emarginate, margin entire, adaxially dark green, glabrous, abaxially paler, sparsely puberulous, especially on the veins. Racemes axillary. Sepals yellowish green, unequal, lower two smaller, ovate, 3–5 mm, upper three broadly elliptic, 6 – 8 mm. Petals fresh yellow to deeply yellow, broadly elliptic, 1.5 – 2 × 1 – 1.4 cm, apex broadly obtuse to subrounded. Stamens 10, all fertile, lower 2 with longer anthers. Ovary filiform, hairy. Pods flat, linear, dehiscent, 7–10 × 0.8 – 1.2 cm, apex long beaked, fruit neck ca. 5 mm; fruiting pedicels conspicuous. Seeds 10–12, glossy.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1469, 2007; L. T. Lo 155.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to tropical Asia, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all the year round.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia surattensis Burm. f. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia surattensis Burm. f. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).

Senna tora (L.) Roxb. 決明
Fl. Ind. (ed. 2) 2: 340. 1832.
Cassia tora L., Sp. Pl. 1: 211. 1753; FHK 98. 1861; FKH 89. 1912; FHN 2: 234. 1965; FRPS 39: 126. 1988; FGD 5: 181. 2003; FGX 2: 464. 2005.

Annual erect shrubby herb, 1– 2 m tall. Stipules linear, pubescent, caducous. Leaves 4–8 cm; petioles eglandular; rachis with 1 clavate gland between each pair of leaflets; petiolules 1.5 – 2 mm; leaflets 3 pairs, membranous, obovate or obovate-elliptic, 2 – 6 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, oblique, apex obtuse and mucronate, sparsely pubescent adaxially, pubescent abaxially. Flowers axillary, usually 2-clustered. Peduncles 6– 10 mm. Pedicels 1– 1.5 cm, filiform. Sepals unequal, membranous, ovate or ovate-oblong, ca. 8 mm, pubescent abaxially. Petals yellow, lower 2 slightly longer, 12 – 15 × 5 – 7 mm. Fertile stamens 7, anthers square, ca. 4 mm, dehiscing by apical pores, filaments shorter than anthers. Ovary sessile, white pubescent. Pods slender, nearly 4-angled, acuminate at both ends, 15 × 0.3–0.4 cm, membranous. Seeds ca. 25, rhomboid, glossy.

Locality: Naturalized. S. P. Lau 149; HK sheet 39274, 39751.
Distribution: Native to tropical America, widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Slopes, open fields and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (seed), dye.
Notes: The species was reported as Cassia tora L. previously (Check List HK Plants 136. 2002; 51. 2004).

Medicinal (seed), dye.

Serissa japonica (Thunb.) Thunb. 六月雪
Nov. Gen. Pl. 9: 132. 1798; FRPS 71(2): 160, pl. 43. 1999; FGD 6: 228, fig. 124. 2005.
Lycium japonicum Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 207. 1780.
Lycium foetidum L. f., Sp. Pl. Suppl. 150. 1781.
Serissa foedida (L. f.) Poir. ex Lam., Tab. Encycl. 2: 211. 1819; FKH 134. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs, 60–90 cm tall. Branches grey, glabrous. Leaves leathery, opposite and crowded on short branchlets, subsessile; stipules very short, apex with 3 bristles; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, 6–22 × 3 – 8 mm, base narrowed into a very short petiole, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers usually solitary in axils of leaves near apex or branchlets. Calyx‑tube ca. 1.5 mm, apex 6‑lobed; lobes triangular, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white or with pink tint; tube 4–5 mm, hairy inside; limb 1–1.2 cm in diam., 5–6‑lobed, lobes oblong, apex 3‑toothed, hairy adaxially. Ovary inferior; style ca. 5 mm; stigma 2‑lobed.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 161; S. P. Lau 93, 94.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Nepal.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Serissa serissoides (DC.) Druce 白馬骨
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club 1916: 646. 1917.
Democritea serissoides DC., Prodr. 4: 540. 1830.

It differs from Serissa japonica by its thinly papery and larger leaves (1–4 × 0.3–1.5 cm), and by its calyx‑lobes, which is equal to the corolla‑tube.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 2502, 38031.
Distribution: SW, S, C & SE China. Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental, hedges.

Sesamum indicum L. 芝麻（脂麻、巨勝）
Sp. Pl. 2: 634. 1753; FKH 196. 1912; FRPS 69: 63, pl. 18: 6 – 7. 1990; FFJ 5: 94, fig. 103. 1993; FOC 18: 226. 1998; FGD 4: 407, fig. 248. 2000.
Sesamum orientale L., Sp. Pl. 2: 634. 1753; FGZ 611, fig. 325. 1956.

Annual herb, erect, 0.75–1(–1.5) m tall. Stems 4‑angled, branched or unbranched, pith hollow or white. Leaves opposite or alternate; those on lower branches ovate to oblong‑ovate, 4–16 × 2–15 cm, base obtuse or rotund, apex mucronate or subrotund, margin lobed or tripartite; those on middle branches serrate at margin; those on upper branches ovate, oblong‑ovate or lanceolate to linear, 3–9 × 0.5–2.5 cm. Flowers white or mauve‑pink, bilabiate. Calyx persistent, 5‑parted to near base, lobes 4.5 – 8 mm, pubescent. Stamens inclusive. Ovary superior, 4(–8)‑locular, pubescent. Capsule erect, ellipsoidal, 1.8–2.8 × 0.6–0.7 cm, beak broad. Seeds many, 2.5–3 mm long, white or black.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 409, 3255; Y. W. Lam 1554.
Distribution: Cultivated in China; possibly native to India or Africa, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Oil, medicinal (folklore), edible.
Notes: According to Z. Y. Wu et al. (Acta Phytotax. Sin. 45: 458 – 472. 2007), the Chinese name “hu ma” (胡麻) should refer to Linum usitatissimum L. (亞麻) of the Linaceae.

records.text:
Sesbania bispinosa (Jacq.) W. F. Wight 刺田菁
U.S.D.A. Bur. Pl. Industr. Bull. 137: 15. 1909; FRPS 40: 235. 1994; FGD 5: 252. 2003.
Aeschynomene bispinosa Jacq., Ic. Pl. Rar. 3: 13. 1793.

Subshrub, 1–3 m tall. Branches usually sparsely prickly. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 20–40 pairs, linear-oblong, 10–16 × 2–3 mm, base rounded, apex obtuse, mucronate, densely purple-brown gland-spotted on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 5–10 cm, 2–6-flowered. Peduncles up to 4 cm, prickly. Calyx campanulate; 4 mm, 5-toothed, teeth triangular, 1 mm. Corolla yellow; vexillum subovate, 10 mm, densely red-brown flecked abaxially, base clawed, apex emarginate, with triangular callosities; wing oblong, 9 mm, auriculate on one side; keel obovate-oblong, 7 mm, with teeth-like auricles at base. Stamens diadelphous, filament-tube 9–12 mm. Pods terete, 15–22 × 0.3 cm, straight or slightly curved, beak 10–12 mm, slightly constricted between seeds. Seeds 35–40, brown, subcylindric, 3 × 2 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Yuen Long, Castle Peak Beach, Tuen Mun, Sha Po, Peng Chau. Y. S. Lau 1022; Y. W. Lam 1002, 1655.
Distribution: Hainan (Xisha Islands), Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; C & S Asia, Indochina, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Moist hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Dec.

Sesbania cannabina (Retz.) Poir. 田菁
Encycl. 7: 130. 1806; FRPS 40: 232. 1994; FGD 5: 251, fig. 139. 2003.
Aeschynomene cannabina Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 26. 1789.

Annual herb. Branches glabrous at maturity. Leaves even-pinnate, 12 – 15 cm; leaflets opposite, 20 – 40 pairs, base rounded, apex obtuse to truncate, mucronate, asymmetric, adaxially glabrous, sparsely sericeous abaxially when young, dotted with minute purple glands on both surfaces, but more densely abaxially. Racemes axillary, 3–10 cm, 2–6-flowered. Calyx campanulate, 3–4 mm, glabrous, linear-appendiculate between teeth. Corolla yellow, all clawed; vexillum transverse-elliptic to suborbicular, 9–10 mm, sparsely purple-black spotted and striate, callosities pear-shaped; wings obovate-oblong, 9–10 mm, base auriculate; keel shorter than wings, triangular-broad-ovate. Stamens diadelphous. Pods terete, 12–22 × 0.2–0.4 cm, slightly curved, beak 5–7 mm, black-brown striate. Seeds 20–35, green-brown, shortly cylindric, 4 × 2–3 mm.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. W. Lam 1014.
Distribution: S & E China (cultivated or naturalized); tropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Dec.
Uses: Green manure.

Sesbania javanica Miq. 沼生田菁

Fl. Ned. Ind. 1(1): 288. 1855; FRPS 40: 234. 1994.

Sesbania cochinchinensis DC., Prod. 2: 266. 1825.


Annual herb, 2 – 4 m tall. Stems terete, pith white; young branchlets sparsely pubescent. Stipules lanceolate, 5 – 6 mm. Leaves even-pinnate, 10–30 cm; leaflets 10–30 pairs, opposite or subalternate, linear-oblong, 10–30 × 2–4 mm, the middle ones larger than others, base slightly unequal, apex obtuse. Racemes axillary, pendulous, 5–12-flowered. Bracts ovate to lanceolate, deciduous. Flowers 18 – 20 mm. Calyx campanulate, 6 – 7 mm, teeth deltoid, 1.5 – 2 mm. Corolla yellow or reddish, with dark striate and spots. Petals subequal; vexillum yellow adaxially, with fine dots abaxially, broadly ovate, 2 – 3 cm, base slightly cordate, erectly clawed; wings auriculate at base; keel deltoid-ovate, with slender auricles at base. Pods light brown, straight or submoniliform, 15–25 × 0.5 mm. Seeds 20 – 30, subglobular.


Locality: Lai Chi Kok, Shing Mun, Tuen Mun. H. C. Tang 1028; Y. S. Lau 1973, 2279.

Distribution: Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.

Ecology: Low-lying lands. Flowering: Jun. – Oct.

Sesuvium portulacastrum (L.) L. 海馬齒
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 1058. 1759; FKH 114. 1912; FHN 1: 383, fig. 201. 1964; FGD 2: 87, fig. 60. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 329, pl. 152, photo 140 –141. 1996; FRPS 26: 30, pl. 5: 4– 6. 1996; FOC 5: 441. 2003.
Portulaca portulacastrum L., Sp. Pl. 446. 1753.

Perennial succulent herb. Stems prostrate, 20–80 cm or longer, glabrous, green or red, often with white tubercles, rooting at nodes. Leaves fleshy; petioles 7–15 mm, base dilated, with membranous, amplexicaul margins; leaf blade linear oblanceolate or linear spathulate, 1.5–5 × 0.2–1 cm, apex obtuse, tapering from middle to the base. Flowers solitary in axil of leaves. Pedicels 5–15 mm. Calyx 6–8 mm; tube ca. 2 mm; lobes 5, ovate-lanceolate, green abaxially, red adaxially. Petals absent. Stamens 15–40, inserted at apex of calyx-tube, shorter than the calyx-lobes; filaments free or united below middle. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, 3- or sometimes 4-locular; style 3, rarely 4–5. Capsule ovoid, opening transversely below middle.

Locality: Tai Tam, Castle Peak, Lung Kwu Tan, Sai Kung, Pui O, Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 1293; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24044; Y. S. Lau 3253.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Xisha Islands; tropical and subtropical coastal areas.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.

Setaria faberi R. A. W. Herrm. 大狗尾草
Beitr. Biol. Pflanzen. 10: 51. 1910; FRPS 10(1): 356, pl. 109: 12–19. 1990; FFJ 6: 195, fig. 162. 1995 [“faberii”]; FTW ed. 2, 5: 510. 2000; FOC 22: 535. 2006; FGD 9: 441. 2009 [“faberii”].

Annual herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at the lower nodes, 50–120 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths loose, ciliate on upper margins; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 10–40 × 0.5–2 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface with scattered hairs, obtuse or narrowed to base, apex acuminate, margins serrate; ligule 1–2 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle densely cylindrical, 5–24 × 0.6–1.3 cm, nodding, branchlets bearing several spikelets each subtended by 1–3 bristles; axis white-pilose; bristles green or brownish purple. Spikelets elliptic, ca. 3 mm; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, broad ovate, acute, 3-veined; upper glume 3/4 length of spikelet or slightly shorter, acute, 5–9-veined; lower floret neuter, lemma 5–8-veined; palea membranous, small; upper lemma strongly convex, distinctly transversely rugose-tuberculate, coriaceous, 5-veined. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Sha Tin. L. T. Lo 375.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Heilongjiang, Jilin, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Setaria italica (L.) P. Beauv. 粱
Ess. Agrostogr. 51. 1812; FKH 316. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 353. 1990; FFJ 6: 194. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 510, pl. 214. 2000; FOC 22: 535. 2006; FGD 9: 441. 2009.
Panicum italicum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 56. 1753.

Annual herb. Culms stout, erect, up to 150 cm. Leaf sheaths loosely embraced culm, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose, margins ciliate; leaf blades long lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 15–45 × 0.6–3 cm, adaxial surface scabrous, abaxial surface slightly smooth, base rounded and obtuse, apex acute; ligule 1–3 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle cylindrical or subfusiform, nodding when mature, 6–40 × 0.5–5 cm; central axis densely hairy; spikelets subtended by several bristles 1–5 times as long as spikelet. Spikelets yellow, brown, orange or purple, elliptic or subglobose, 2–3 mm; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume subequal spikelet, 5–7(–9)-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined; lower palea hyaline, lanceolate; upper lemma as long as lower lemma, oblong or ovate-oblong, cartilaginous, deciduous at maturity, finely rugose to smooth and shiny.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3221.
Distribution: Widely cultivated, origin unknown.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (beverage base, cereal).

Setaria palmifolia (J. König) Stapf 棕葉狗尾草
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 42: 186. 1914; FHN 4: 436. 1977 [“palmaefolia”]; FRPS 10(1): 337, pl. 105: 1–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 193, fig. 159. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 512, pl. 215, photo 57. 2000; FOC 22: 532. 2006; FGD 9: 439. 2009.
Panicum palmifolium J. König, Naturforscher 23: 208. 1788.

Perennial herb, with a short knotty rhizome. Culms erect or slightly geniculate, 75–200 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, usually sparsely hispid, margins tuberculate-ciliate near ligule, otherwise glabrous; leaf blades fusiform-lanceolate, 20–60 × 2–7 cm, glabrous or hispid, plicate, narrowed toward base and petiolate, margins tuberculate-ciliate, acuminate; ligule 1.5–2 m, a ring of hairs. Panicle open or slightly pyramid, 20–60 × 2–10 cm, branches up to 20 cm, laxly spreading, flexuous, some spikelets subtended by a solitary 5–15 mm bristle. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm, densely or sparsely arranged in one side; lower glume triangular-ovate, 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined; upper glume ovate, 1/2–3/4 length of spikelet, 5–7-veined, acute; lower lemma staminate or neuter, as long as spikelet or slightly longer, 5-veined, tipped with a short incurved beak; lower palea narrow, 2/3 length of lemma, hyaline; upper lemma indistinctly rugulose to almost smooth, slightly shiny, apex apiculate. Caryopsis ovate-lanceolate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2011; L. T. Lo 103; HK sheet 40815.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Open forests and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Setaria parviflora (Poir.) Kerguélen 幽狗尾草（褐毛狗尾草）
Lejeunia. 120: 161. 1987; FOC 22: 535. 2006; FGD 9: 442. 2009.
Cenchrus parviflorus Poir., Encycl. 6: 52. 1804.
Setaria glauca (L.) P. Beauv. var. pallidefusca (Schumach.) T. Koyama, J. Jap. Bot. 37(8): 237. 1962; FHN 4: 438, fig. 1228. 1977.
Setaria pallidefusca (Schumach.) Stapf & C. E. Hubb., Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1930: 259. 1930; FRPS 10(1): 358. 1990 [“pallidifusca”]; FFJ 6: 196. 1995 [“pallidifusca”]; FTW ed. 2, 5: 512. 2000; Check List HK Plants 347. 2002; 121. 2004 [“pallidifusca”].
Panicum glaucum auct. non L.: Benth., FHK 411. 1861.
Setaria glauca auct. non (L.) P. Beauv.: FKH 316. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb. Culms erect or geniculate at lower nodes, 20–90 cm tall. Leaf sheaths compressed, slightly keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, stiff, flat or slight infolded, 5–30 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose at base, apex acuminate; ligule very short, margin a ring of ciliate. Panicle densely cylindrical, 2–15 × 0.5–1.2 cm; axis pubescent; bristles golden or purplish brown at maturity, 2–3 times spikelet length. Spikelets elliptic, 2–3 mm; lower glume triangular-ovate or broad ovate, 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, acute, 3-veined; upper glume broadly ovate, ca. 1/2 length of spikelet, thin papery, 5-veined; lower floret neuter, lemma 5-veined, palea similar to upper lemma, membranous; upper floret bisexual, lemma cartilaginous, finely rugose, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea, mucronate; lodicules cuneate, apex finely fringed, stamens 3; styles 2, penicillate.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 2188, 3185.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread throughout the tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Setaria plicata (Lam.) T. Cooke 皺葉狗尾草
Fl. Bombay. 2: 919. 1908; FHN 4: 436. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 340, pl. 105: 9–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 193, fig. 160. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 512, pl. 216. 2000; FOC 22: 532. 2006; FGD 9: 439. 2009.
Panicum plicatum Lam., Tab. Encycl. Meth. Bot. 4: 736. 1791; FHK 411. 1861.
Panicum excurrens Trin., Sp. Gram. 1(8): pl. 89. 1827; FHK 412. 1861.
Setaria mauritiana auct. non Spreng.: FKH 316. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect or decumbent from a knotty rootstock, 45–130 cm tall, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Leaf sheaths submembranous, ± papillose-pilose, margins usually ciliate except at base; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, thin, 10–45 × 1–3 cm, plicate, papillose-pilose, hispidulous or glabrous, narrowed toward base, apex attenuate; ligule ca. 2 mm, consisting of a ring of hairs. Panicle narrow oblong or linear, 15–35 cm, branches up to 8 cm, loose, ascending, some spikelets subtended by a solitary 10–20 mm bristle; central axis ribbed, finely pubescent and scabrous. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm; lower glume broad ovate, 1/4–1/3 length of spikelet, obtuse to truncate, 3–5-veined; upper glume 1/2–3/4 length of spikelet, obtuse or acute, 5–7-veined; lower lemma staminate or neuter, 5-veined; lower palea often well developed, margins slightly inrolled, 2-veined; upper lemma bisexual, as long as or slightly shorter than lower lemma, usually distinctly and finely rugose, rarely smooth, mucronate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. F. W. Xing 8032; Y. W. Lam 1556; HK sheet 40046.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Thailand, India, Nepal, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Margins of forests, ravines and shady pathsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Setaria verticillata (L.) P. Beauv. 倒刺狗尾草
Ess. Agrostogr. 51. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 351, pl. 108: 11–18. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 515. 2000; FYN 9: 543. 2003; FOC 22: 537. 2006; FGD 9: 441. 2009.
Panicum verticillatum L., Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 1: 82. 1762.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, ascending from geniculate base, much branched, 20–100 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths thin and soft, glabrous or papillose-puberulous, margins ciliolate; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, flaccid, 5–20 × 0.4–1.8 cm, usually glabrous or adaxially slightly scabrous, base subrounded, apex long acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle contracted, cylindrical, 4–15 cm, spikelets subtended by 1–4 bristles; bristles green or brownish, 3–8 mm, retrorsely barbed and often becoming entangled. Spikelets elliptic, 1.8–2.4 mm, obtuse; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as spikelet or slightly short, 5–7-veined; lower floret neuter, lower lemma as long as spikelet or slightly longer, 5-veined; lower palea much reduced; upper lemma as long as lower lemma or slightly short, dorsally compressed, finely and transversely rugose; lodicules cuneate, emarginate. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Fung Kat Heung. HK sheet 35660.
Distribution: Nei Mongol, Taiwan, Yunnan; widespread tropical weed, originated from paleotropics.
Ecology: Roadsides, open weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Sida acuta Burm. f. 黃花稔
Fl. Ind. 147. 1768; FHK 32. 1861; FKH 47. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 19. 1984; FGD 2: 201. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 748. 1993.

Herb, usually shrubby, 0.3 –1 m tall, much branched; branchlets pubescent or glabrescent. Petioles 4– 5 mm, villose; stipules linear, longer than the petioles; leaf blade lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 1.5–7 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base obtuse or rounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate, both surfaces glabrous or sparsely stellate-pubescent. Flowers solitary or paired, axillary; pedicels 4–12 mm, the longer ones articulate at the middle. Calyx glabrous, cup-shaped, 6 mm, the lower half connate; lobes 5, deltoid, caudate. Corolla yellow, 8–10 mm across; lobes obovate, ciliate. Fruit subglobose, 4 mm in diam., 6-carpellate; carpels birostrate, reticulately striate and sulcate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Lau Fau Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 375, 2077; S. Y. Hu 8802 (CUHK); K. L. Yip 4242.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, India.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sida alnifolia L. 榿葉黃花稔
Sp. Pl. 684. 1753; FHN 2: 93. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 21. 1984; FGD 2: 203. 1991.
Sida rhombifolia auct. non L.: FHK 33. 1861; FKH 47. 1912.

Subshrub, 0.5 –1(–2) m tall; branchlets slender, densely stellate villose. Petioles 3 – 5 mm, stellate pubescent; stipules subulate, 4 – 4.5 mm; leaf blade ovate, suborbicular or obovate, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or truncate, margin evenly serrate, stellate pilose adaxially, stellate villose abaxially, Flowers solitary. Pedicels 5 mm (2 cm in fruit), articulate near middle, densely stellatevelutinous. Calyx cup-shaped, 5–8 mm, stellate-velutinous, long-villose along angles and margins. Corolla yellow, 6 mm across. Staminal tube hirsute. Fruit subglobose, 6 mm in diam., enclosed, the apical end pubescent; carpels 8, birostrate, awns 2 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Chung Chi College. W. J. Tutcher 5570; F. W. Xing 9914; S. Y. Hu 8768, 7899 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, India.
Ecology: Open fields and thin forests. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.

Sida cordata (Burm. f.) Borss. 長梗黃花稔
Blumea 14: 182. 1966; FRPS 49(2): 26, pl. 5: 6 –7. 1984.
Sida humilis Cav., Diss. 5: 277, t. 134, fig. 2, 1788; FHK 32. 1861; FKH 47. 1912.

Diffuse herb, 0.3–1 m tall; branchlet slender, spreading, covered with long spreading hairs, mixed with short stellate hairs. Petioles 1–3 cm, stellate pilose; stipules linear, 2–3 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade cordiform, 1– 5 cm, apex shortly acuminate, margin obtusely dentate or serrate, stellate pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary or in leafy racemes. Pedicels slender, 2– 4 cm, sparsely stellate pubescent, articulate above middle. Calyx cup-shaped, ca. 4 mm; lobes triangular, acute. Corolla yellow. Fruit depressed globose; carpels 5, not curved.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Po Kau, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Fung Kat Heung. L. T. Lo 539; Y. S. Lau 2022, 2168.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Waste places, roadsides. Flowering: May–Jun.

Sida cordifolia L. 心葉黃花稔
Sp. Pl. 684. 1753; FHK 33. 1861; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 39: 494. 1911; FKH 47. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 25, pl. 5: 2–3. 1984; FGD 2: 203. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 748, pl. 375. 1993.
Sida hongkongensis Gandoger, Bull. Soc. Bot. France 71: 629.1924, nom. subnud.
Sida humilis Willd., Check List HK Plants 40. 2004.

Subshrub, 0.3 –1 m tall, densely stellate hispid and mixed with simple long hairs throughout. Petioles 1–2.5 cm, stipules filiform, 5 mm; leaf blade ovate or subcordate, 1.5 –3 × 1–4 cm, base cordate or rounded, apex rounded or obtuse. Flowers solitary or fasciculate; pedicels 4–15 mm, the longer ones articulate near apex. Calyx cup-shaped; lobes 5, triangular, 5 – 6 mm. Corolla yellow, 15 mm in diam.; lobes oblong, 6 – 8 mm. Staminal tube hirsute. Fruit subdiscoid, 6 – 8 mm across; carpels 10, birostrate, the apical end shortly strigose, awns to 3 mm, exposed, covered with stiff reflexed hairs.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lai Chi Kok, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Tai Long Sai Wan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 801, 1185; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 23289 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Asia and Africa tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Nearly all the year round.
Notes: The type specimen of Sida hongkongensis was collected by Bodinier (No. 922) from Hong Kong.

Sida rhombifolia L. 白背黃花稔
Sp. Pl. 684. 1753; FRPS 49(2): 20. 1984; FGD 2: 203. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 748. 1993.

Subshrub, 0.5–1 m tall, much branched. Branchlets, petioles and pedicels stellate lanate. Petioles 3–5 mm; stipules linear, 3–5 mm; leaf blade rhombic or oblong-lanceolate, 2.5 – 4.5 × 0.6 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse or acute, margin serrate, shortly stellate or subglabrous adaxially, stellate-velutinous abaxially. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 10 mm, (15–25 mm in fruit), geniculate, articulate above middle. Calyx 4– 5 mm, the basal 2/3 connate, stellate velutinous. Petals yellow, ca. 8 mm. Staminal tube glabrous, or sparsely glandularly papillose. Fruits subdiscoid, 6–7 mm in diam.; carpels 8 –10, birostrate, subglabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 43; Y. S. Lau 189; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 20048, 23292 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Sida subcordata Span. 榛葉黃花稔
Linnaea 15: 172. 1814; FRPS 49(2): 24, pl. 5: 1. 1984; FGD 2: 202, fig. 128. 1991.
Sida corylifolia Wall., Num. List. no. 1865. 1829; FKH 47. 1912.

Subshrub, 1(–2) m tall. Branchlets and abaxial surface of leaves sparsely stellate-pubescent when young, soon glabrescent. Petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm; stipules linear, 3 – 4 mm; leaf blade ovate to oblong, 5 –10 × 2.5 –7.5 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin crenulate-serrate. Inflorescence corymbose, subpaniculate; peduncles 2–7 cm; pedicels 6–20 mm, articulate at middle, geniculate. Calyx 8–10 mm. Corolla campanulate, 3 cm in diam.; petals obovate. Staminal tube glabrous. Fruit subglobose, 1 cm in diam.; carpels 8 –10, birostrate, awns 6 mm, exposed, covered with reflexed bristles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Long Ke, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Chung Uk Tsuen, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2410; Y. W. Lam 484; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22720 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, India, Malesia area.
Ecology: Wastelands, thickets, partially shaded woods near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.

Siegesbeckia orientalis L. 豨薟
Sp. Pl. 2: 900. 1753; FHK 182. 1861; FKH 145. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 158. 1968; FRPS 75: 339, pl. 57: 4. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1062, pl. 506, photo 488. 1998.

Annual erect herbs; stem 30–100 cm tall, branched somewhat dichotomously, pubescent, hair multicellular and appeared denser on upper branches. Basal leaves withered at flowering stage; cauline ones papery, ovate‑triangular to ovate‑lanceolate, 3–12 × 1–7 cm, base broadly cuneate and narrowed down to form winged petiole, apex acute, margin irregularly toothed, pubescent on both surfaces, glandular abaxially, triplinerved; upper leaves smaller in size, elliptic, shortly petiolate or subsessile, shallowly serrate or subentire. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, 1–2 cm across, loosely arranged as panicles; peduncles 1–4 cm, densely pubescent. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, hairy and stipitate purplish brown glandular, apex rounded, 2‑seriate; outer phyllaries 5–6, linear‑spatulate, spreading, 7–11 × 0.5–1 mm; inner ones obovate‑oblong, 3–4 × 1.2–2 mm, enclosing the hypanthium of marginal florets. Receptacle small; paleae obovate, 3–3.5 mm, puberulent and sparsely glandular on abaxial side, curved and enveloping the cypselae of disk florets. Florets yellow. Marginal female florets ligulate, corolla tube 1 mm, glandular and hairy, ligule 1.2 mm and 3‑lobed. Disk bisexual florets tubular, corolla 1.5 mm, 5‑lobed; anthers slightly exserted, basal lobes obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑lanceolate elongate; stylar branches very short and slightly flattened, rugose on the abaxial surface. Cypselae blackish brown, 3–3.5 mm, oblique‑tetragonous, narrowed basally, a short crown protruded at apex, glabrous. Pappus absent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 34; H. Y. Yeung 82 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11524 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia, Europe, tropical America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sinobambusa tootsik (Makino) Makino 唐竹
J. Jap. Bot. 2: 8. 1918; FTW 5: 739, pl. 1499. 1978; HKB 77. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 226, pl. 60. 1996; FOC 22: 148. 2006; FGD 9: 309. 2009.
Arundinaria tootsik Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 19: 63. 1905.
Arundinaria dolichantha Keng, Sinensia 7: 418, fig. 6. 1936.
Neobambos dolichanthus (Keng) P. C. Keng, Techn. Bull. Nat’l. For. Res. Bur. China No. 8: 15. 1948.
Pleioblastus dolichanthus (Keng) P. C. Keng, Clav. Gen. Sp. Gram. Prim. Sin. 154. 1957.
Semiarundinaria okuboi Makino, J. Jap. Bot. 8: 43. 1933.
Semiarundinaria tootsik (Makino) Muroi, Amat. Herb. 10: 210. 1942.

Culms 5–12 m, 2–6 cm in diam.; internodes initially deep green, flattened above branches, 30–40(–80) cm, glaucous, glabrous, apically minutely papillate. Culm sheaths initially redbrown, basally suboblong, leathery, slightly glaucous, setose, densely so at base, apex broadly rounded, margins ciliate; auricles very variable, scabrid, tomentose; oral setae curved, ca. 2 cm; ligule arcuate, ca. 3–4 mm, uniform; blade reflexed, green, lanceolate. Leaves 3–6(–9) per ultimate branch; sheath glabrous; auricles obscure; oral setae deciduous, radiate, ca. 1.5 cm, undulate; ligule truncate or subrounded; blade 6 – 22 × 1–3.5 cm, secondary veins 4–8-paired, margins serrulate, abaxially pubescent. Spikelets 1–3(–5), lateral spikelets sessile, terminal spikelet on 2–11 mm pedicel, linear, 8–20 × 0.2–0.3 cm; florets 7–12 mm, glabrous. Lemma ovate, ca. 7 mm wide, margins ciliate, apex acute; palea elliptic; lodicules nearly rhombic, elliptic or ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, ciliolate, with 7–9 veins. Anthers light yellow. Ovary glabrous; style 1, extremely short; stigmas 3, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, HKU campus, Sha Tin (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2778, 2845.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi; N Vietnam, introduced in Japan.
Ecology: New shoots: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Syndiclis hongkongensis N. H. Xia, Y. F. Deng & K. L. Yip 香港油果樟
J. Trop. & Subtrop. Bot. 14(1): 75, fig. 1. 2006.

Tree, up to 16 m tall and up to 90 cm in diam. at base; bark reddish brown, peeling off in small pieces. Branchlets reddish brown, lenticellate, at apex somewhat angular, glabrescent; leaf buds small, hardly hairy. Leaves alternate; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, 6–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate but always asymmetrical, apex acuminate, with sharp tip, margin entire, glabrescent, dark green above, pale green and glaucous below, midvein and lateral veins brownish, flat above, prominent below, lateral veins 3–4 pairs, veinlets densely reticulate. Petioles slender, 1–2 mm long, flat above. Inflorescence a panicle, axillary, 1–3.5 cm long, slender, tomentose, short pedunculate. Bracteoles linear-triangular, rusty-tomentose, ca. 3 × 1 mm. Flowers globose, green-yellow, 1.5 mm long; pedicels 2–4 mm long; perianth-lobes 6, ovate, densely tomentose. Fertile stamens 6 in 2 whorls, slightly exserted, subsessile, villose, eglandular; the anthers 2-celled, cells introrse; staminodes 6, opposite to the fertile stamens, villose. Ovary ellipsoid, sparsely tomentose, styles tomentose at base. Fruit globose, rough, yellowish brown, ca. 4 cm diam., glabrous; pericarp woody, ca. 2 mm thick; fruiting pedicel 8 mm long, cylindrical, thickened under the fruit.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 337; Y. W. Lam 1276.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Oct. of the following year.
Notes: The species was reported as Syndiclis furfuracea H. W. Li previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2002). The type specimen (N. H. Xia et al. s.n., holotype: IBSC; isotype: HK sheet 39986) was collected from Tai Mo Shan in 2005. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Sinosideroxylon wightianum (Hook. & Arn.) Aubr. 革葉鐵欖（鐵欖）
Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam. 3: 68. 1963; FRPS 60(1): 75, pl. 14: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 312, fig. 247.1989; FGD 2: 357, fig. 243. 1991; FOC 15: 212. 1996.
Sideroxylon wightianum Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 196. 1837; FHK 209. 1861; FKH 161. 1912.
Sideroxylon wightianum var. balansae Lecomte, Observ. Bot. 3: 887. 1930.
Mastichodendron wightianum (Hook. & Arn.) P. Royen, Blumea 10(1): 123, 125, fig. 1. 1960.

Evergreen small trees, 4 –10 m tall. Branchlets and leaves rusty tomentose when young, glabrescent, conspicuously lenticellate. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic, lanceolate or oblanceolate, 9 –15(–17) × 2.5 – 4 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate and caudate, glabrous; lateral veins 12–17 pairs. Flowers solitary or 2–5 clustered in leaf axils, greenish white, fragrant. Pedicels 4 –10 mm, pubescent. Sepals ovate to lanceolate, rusty tomentose, ca. 2.5 mm. Corolla white, 6– 8 mm, lobes suborbicular to ovate, glabrous. Stamens slightly longer than corolla lobes. Staminodes lanceolate to subtriangular, petaloid, 2.5 –3 mm. Ovary ovoid, tomentose. Berry ellipsoid or ovoid, 1–1.5(–1.8) × 0.5–0.8 cm, glabrous, deep purple. Seed 1, ellipsoid, compressed; shiny, scar basal to lateral-basal, suborbicular.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Shatin, Lion Rock, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2025; Y. W. Lam 2303; C. H. Tsou 1871.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Siphonostegia chinensis Benth. 陰行草
In Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 203. 1837; FKH 191. 1912; FOC 18: 211. 1998.

Annual herbs, 30–60(–80) cm tall, black when dry, densely tawny hairy. Branches ± angled, densely pubescent. Leaves sessile or short petiolate; leaf blade broadly ovate, 0.8–5.5 × 0.4–6 cm, densely pubescent, 2‑pinnatisect; pinnae 3 pairs, lowermost pair 2‑pinnately parted; pinnules 1–3, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1–2 mm wide, margin entire. Racemes few‑flowered; bracts pinnately parted or pinnatisect. Calyx tube 1–1.5 cm, densely pubescent; lobes green, subequal, linear‑lanceolate to oblong, 2.2–2.5 mm, outside densely pilose, inside pubescent, margin entire or 1–2‑toothed. Corolla tube 1.2–1.4 cm; lower lip yellow, lobes ovate; upper lip red‑purple, apex truncate. Filaments basally ciliolate. Ovary narrowly ovoid, ca. 4 mm. Capsules ovoid‑oblong, ca. 1.5 cm × 2.5 mm, apex suboblique and apiculate. Seeds black, ca. 0.8 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lamma Island. Y. S. Lau 1536; Y. W. Lam 1022; HK sheet 20719.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Siphonostegia laeta S. Moore 腺毛陰行草
J. Bot. 18: 5. 1880; FOC 18: 211. 1998.

Herbs, 30–70 cm tall, erect, blackish when dry, densely glandular hairy. Branches 3–5 pairs. Leaves short petiolate; leaf blade narrowly triangular‑ovate, 1.5–2.5 × 0.8–1.5 cm, densely glandular hairy, nearly palmately 3‑parted; median pinna larger than others, rhomboid‑ovate, pinnately parted, with 3–6 ovate pinnules; lateral pinnae oblique triangular‑ovate. Bracts foliaceous, as long as or shorter than calyx, rhomboid‑ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, densely glandular hairy, margin ± pinnately parted to subentire, apex acuminate. Pedicel 2–3 mm. Bracteoles 3–5 mm. Calyx tubular‑campanulate; tube 1–1.5 cm; lobes 6–10 mm, margin entire. Corolla yellow, sometimes galea purplish; lower lip as long as galea, lobes triangular‑ovate, ciliate with long multicellular hairs. Filaments densely pubescent. Ovary narrowly ovoid, 2–3 mm. Capsules 1.2–1.3 cm × 3.5 mm. Seeds yellow‑brown, 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Lady Clementi's Ride. Y. S. Lau 2519; P. S. Choi 534.
Distribution: Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Skimmia arborescens T. Anderson ex Gamble 喬木茵芋
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 43: 491. 1916; FGD 2: 251, fig. 165. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 112. 1997.
Skimmia euphlebia Merr, Lingnan Sci. J. 13: 32. 1934.
Skimmia kwangsiensis C. C. Huang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 7: 346, pl. 66: 2, 70: 2. 1958.

Small tree, 2–8 m tall. Branchlets with conspicuous pith. Petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade thinly papery, elliptic, oblong or obovate-elliptic, 5–18 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to long acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein slightly prominent adaxially; lateral veins 7–10 pairs. Inflorescences 2–5 cm, rachis puberulous or glabrous. Bracts broadly ovate, 1–1.5 mm, margin hairy. Calyx-lobes slightly larger than bracts, margin hairy. Petals obovate or ovate-elliptic, 4–5 mm, spreading horizontally or ascending. Male flower: stamens longer than petals, filaments fililform; pistillode 3–4 mm, clavate, apex 3–4-parted. Female flower: sterile stamens shorter than petals; ovary subglobose; style ca. 1 mm; stigma capitate. Fruit globose, 6–8 mm in diam., bluish black, 1–3-seeded.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; Myanmar, India, Sikkim, Bhutan, Nepal.
Ecology: Secondary forests of valleys. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.

Sloanea sinensis (Hance) Hemsl. 猴歡喜
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 27(2): t. 2628. 1900; FGD 1: 123, fig. 129. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 43, pl. 9. 1989.
Echinocarpus sinensis Hance, J. Bot. 22: 103. 1884; FKH 52. 1912.
Sloanea hongkongensis Hemsl., Hook. Icon. Pl. t. 2628. 1900; Hayata, Fl. Form. 49. 1911; FKH 52. 1912.
Sloanea sinensis Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 5: 230. 1924.
Sloanea chinensis Hu, Contr. Biol. Lab. Sci. Soc. China 1: 4. 1925, nom. illeg.
Sloanea oligophlebia Chun & Ting, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 269. 1963.
Sloanea parvifolia Chun & How, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 7: 14, pl. 5. 1958; FHN 2: 65. 1965.

Tree to 20 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Petioles 1– 4 cm; leaf blade variable in shape and size, usually oblong or narrowly obovate, 6 –12 × 3 – 5 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acute, margin usually entire or rarely sparsely dentate on distal half, glabrous; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs. Flowers clustered, axillary. Pedicels 3 – 6 cm. Sepals 4, broadly ovate, 6 – 8 × 5 – 6 mm, puberulous. Petals 4, white, 7–9 mm, puberulous, laciniate at apices. Stamens many, as long as petals; anthers awned at apex. Ovary ovoid, 3–7- locular, 4 – 5 mm, pubescent; style 1, 4– 6 mm, puberulous on proximal half. Capsule variable in size, 2–4 cm in diam., dehiscing into 3 –7 valves; prickles 1–1.5 cm; endocarp purple-red. Seeds black, shiny, 1–1.3 cm; aril yellow.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Sham Tseng, Tate's Cairn, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng. H. C. Tang 1861; Y. S. Lau 2386; Y. W. Lam 1377.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Jun.– Oct.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Sloanea hongkongensis was collected from Happy Valley and Aberdeen New Road by W. J. Tutcher (Herb. Hongk. No. 611) in 1895.

Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Sloanea hongkongensis was collected from Happy Valley and Aberdeen New Road by W. J. Tutcher (Herb. Hongk. No. 611) in 1895.

records.text:
Smilax china L. 菝葜
Sp. Pl. 2: 1029. 1753; FKH 278. 1912; FGZ 685. 1956; FHN 4: 125. 1977; FTW 5: 117. 1978; FRPS 15: 193, pl. 63: 1–3. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 106. 2000; FOC 24: 101. 2000; FGD 6: 374, fig. 222. 2005.
Coprosmanthus japonicus Kunth, Enum. Pl. 5: 268. 1850.
Smilax japonica A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. Arts, n.s. 6(2): 412. 1858, nom. illeg. superfl.
Smilax china L. var. taiheiensis (Hayata) T. Koyama, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 10: 9. 1957.
Smilax pteropus Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 89. 1861.
Smilax taiheiensis Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 9: 134. 1920.
Smilax ferox auct. non Wall. ex Kunth: FHK 370. 1861.

Deciduous climbing vine. Rhizomes rigid, thick, irregular, 2–3 cm in thickness. Stem branched, terete, 1–5 m, woody, sparsely prickly. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/2–2/3 of its length, abscission zone just above winged portion, tendrils often present; leaf blade leathery to thickly papery, ovate to orbicular, 3–10 × 2–9 cm, base acute to cordate, apex acute, rounded to emarginate, pale green to glaucous abaxially, main veins 5–7. Umbels axillary, solitary, 10–25-flowered, not prophyllate at base; peduncle 1–2 cm; bracteoles many, small, ovate-lanceolate. Male flowers: tepals yellowish green, 4–5 mm; stamens 3–4 mm; filaments filiform. Female flowers: staminodes 6, linear. Berries globose, red, 0.6–1.5 cm in diam., minutely white powdery.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 11649; H. C. Tang 389; HK sheet 41500.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Feb.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Smilax cocculoides Warb. 銀葉菝葜
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29: 257. 1900; FRPS 15: 228, pl. 74: 1–4. 1978; FOC 24: 112. 2000; FGD 6: 373. 2005.

Subscandent shrub, unarmed. Stem suberect, branched, 0.5–2 m, woody, inconspicuously ridged. Petiole usually curved, 0.5–1 cm, narrowly winged at base, wings sometimes auriculate apically, abscission zone at middle, tendrils absent; leaf blade thickly papery to subleathery, elliptic-ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 5–12 × 2.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex long acuminate, abaxially pale green, slightly shiny, midvein slightly impressed adaxially. Umbels solitary, rarely paired, 3–15-flowered; peduncle 1–2 cm, prophyllate at base. Male flowers: tepals yellowish green, outer ones 2.5–3.5 × 1–1.5 mm, inner ones narrower; stamens very short. Berries globose, ca. 8 mm in diam., bluish black when matured.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 167, 1292.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Smilax astrosperma F. T. Wang & Tang previously (Check List HK Plants 367. 2002; 128. 2004).

Smilax glabra Roxb. 土茯苓（光葉菝葜）
Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 792. 1832; FHK 369. 1861; FKH 278. 1912; FGZ 685. 1956; FHN 4: 125, fig. 1030. 1977; FTW 5: 130. 1978; FRPS 15: 212, pl. 69. 1978; FOC 24: 108. 2000; FGD 6: 373. 2005.
Smilax blinii H. Lév., Fl. Kouy-Tchou 256. 1914.
Smilax dunniana H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222–226): 446. 1911.
Smilax glabra Roxb. var. maculata Bodinier ex H. Lév., Liliac. etc. Chine 23. 1905.
Smilax mengmaensis R. H. Miao, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1982(3): 75. 1982
Smilax trigona Warb., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29(2): 258. 1900.

Climbing vine. Stem branched, terete, 1–4 m, woody, smooth, unarmed. Petiole 0.5–2.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/4–3/5 of its length, abscission zone apical, tendrils well developed; leaf blade leathery to thinly leathery, elliptic-lanceolate to narrowly ovatelanceolate, 3–15 × 1–7 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, ± glaucous abaxially, main veins 5. Umbels 10–30(–60)-flowered, basally not prophyllate; peduncle 1–5 mm; bracteoles many, persistent. Male flowers: perianth greenish white, slightly 6-angled; outer tepals broadly obovate-orbicular, cucullate, ca. 2 mm, inner ones ca. 1 mm wide, margin irregularly denticulate; stamens nearly as long as inner tepals. Female flowers: staminodes 3. Berries globose, blue-black, 0.7–1 cm in diam., white powdery.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 69, 2402; C. H. Tsou 1879.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.; fruiting: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (rhizome).

Smilax hypoglauca Benth. 粉背菝葜
FHK 369. 1861; FKH 278. 1912; FRPS 15: 208, pl. 66: 1. 1978; FOC 24: 106. 2000.
Smilax corbularia Kunth var. hypoglauca (Benth.) T. Koyama, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 13: 15. 1960.
Smilax corbularia auct. non Kunth: FGD 6: 372. 2005, quoad syn. Smilax hypoglauca Benth.

Climbing vine. Stem branched, 2–(–4) m, woody, unarmed. Petiole 0.7–1.3 cm, narrowly winged at lower half, wings each with a lanceolate auricle apically, abscission zone apical, tendrils usually present; leaf blade leathery, narrowly elliptic to ovate-oblong, 5–12 × 2–5 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate, margin slightly recurved, glaucous abaxially, main veins 3–5, reticulate veins conspicuous adaxially. Umbels axillary, 10–20-flowered, basally not prophyllate; peduncle 0.2–1.5 cm; bracteoles many, small, persistent. Male flowers: tepals greenish yellow, outer ones ca. 2.5 mm, inner ones smaller, filaments connate, forming a short column. Female flowers: tepals 2.2–2.5 mm; staminodes 3. Berries dark red, globose, 0.8–1.0 cm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2234; Y. S. Lau 242, 1371.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Fujian, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.
Notes: The syntypes were collected from Happy Valley. The species was reported as Smilax corbularia Kunth previously (Check List HK Plants 80. 1993; 128. 2004).

Smilax lanceifolia Roxb. var. opaca A. DC. 暗色菝葜
Monogr. Phan. 1: 57. 1878; FGZ 686. 1956; FRPS 15: 218, pl. 71: 3. 1978; FOC 24: 110. 2000.
Smilax kainantensis Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 33: 27. 1943.
Smilax laevis Wall. ex A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1. 6. 1878.
Smilax laevis Wall. ex A. DC. var. ophirensis A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1: 57. 1878.
Smilax laevis Wall. ex A. DC. var. parkii A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1: 57. 1878.
Smilax opaca (A. DC.) J. B. Norton, Pl. Wilson. 3(1): 11. 1916.
Smilax lanceifolia Roxb. subsp. opaca (A. DC.) T. Koyama, Fl. E. Himalaya 2: 172. 1971.
Smilax lanceifolia auct. non Roxb.: FHK 370. 1861; FKH 278. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 117, pl. 43. 2000; FGD 6: 372. 2005; Check List HK Plants 81. 1993.

Climbing vine. Stem branched, terete, 1–2.5 m, woody, usually unarmed, rarely sparsely armed. Petiole 0.8–2.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/5–1/4 of its length, abscission zone at middle, tendrils usually present; leaf blade leathery, oblong-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 6–5 × 2–6 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex acute, obviously shiny adaxially, pale green abaxially; main veins 5, raised adaxially. Umbels axillary, many-flowered, basally prophyllate; peduncle 1–2 cm, proximally articulate. Male flowers: tepals yellowish green, 3–4.5 × ca. 1 mm, reflexed; stamens exserted, filaments 2.5–3.5 mm, anthers ca. 1 mm. Female flowers smaller, staminodes 6. Berries purplish black, globose, 6–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen Reservoir, The Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. H. G. Ye et al. 1017; S. C. Ng 4114; F. W. Xing 7562.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and sparse forests. Flowering: Sep.–Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Smilax ocreata A. DC. 抱莖菝葜
Monogr. Phan. 1: 191. 1878; FRPS 15: 234, pl. 75: 2. 1978; FOC 24: 114. 2000.
Smilax perulata H. Lév. & Vaniot, Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(199–201): 78. 1910.

Climbing vine. Stem up to 7 m, woody, sparsely prickly. Petiole 2–3.5 cm, broadly winged at lower 1/3–1/2 of its length, wings 0.5–2 cm wide, basally deeply clasping node, abscission zone at middle or distal; tendrils usually developed; leaf blade leathery, ovate to elliptic, to 23 × 12.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to shallowly cordate, pale green abaxially. Flowers and fruits unknown.

Locality: Tsuen Wan. S. C. Ng 3441.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: It was treated as a synonym of S. perfoliata in FGD.

Smilax retroflexa (F. T. Wang & T. Tang) S. C. Chen 蒼白菝葜
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 34: 436. 1996; FOC 24: 107. 2000.
Smilax aberrans Gagnep. var. retroflexa F. T. Wang & Tang, FRPS 15: 254. 1978.
Smilax aberrans Gagnep. subsp. retroflexa (F. T. Wang & Tang) T. Koyama, Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam 20: 82. 1983.
Smilax ovalifolia auct. non Roxb. ex D. Don: FHK 370. 1861; FKH 278. 1912.

Climbing vine. Stem stout, branched, to 10 m, woody, prickly. Petiole 1.6–3 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/2–2/3 of its length, abscission zone subapical, tendrils well developed; leaf blade ovate to suborbicular, 12–26 × 8–20 cm, main veins 5–7. Umbels several together in axillary racemes or panicles, 1.5–4 cm, 12–40-flowered, basally prophyllate; peduncle 1.3–3 cm. Male flowers: outer tepals 5–6 × ca. 1.5 mm, inner ones much narrower. Female flowers: tepals slightly smaller than male ones; staminodes 3. Berries dark red, ellipsoidal-globose, 0.9–1.2 cm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sunset Peak. W. J. Tutcher 10595; Y. W. Lam 2266.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Nov.

Smithia conferta Sm. 密花坡油甘

Cycl. 33: Smithia n. 2. 1816; FKH 77. 1912; FRPS 41: 353. 1995;FGD 5: 349, fig. 193. 2003.


Annual herb, 15–90 cm tall. Stems slender, many-branched, glabrous, upper nodes congested into dense heads. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 3–6 pairs, oblong, 6–12 × 2–3 mm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, glabrous adaxially, sparsely yellow hirsute abaxially, lateral veins 5 on each side of midvein. Racemes axillary, densely congested. Calyx 2-lipped, 6–8 mm, lips bristly, entire. Corolla yellow, 12–16 mm; vexillum oblong-obovate; wings and keel subequal, clawed, smaller than vexillum. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary shortly stipitate, hairy. Pods 4–6-segmented, turgid and papillose.


Locality: May Rd., Chuen Lung, Sai Kung, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2063, 2345; Y. W. Lam 2153.

Distribution: Guangdong; tropical Asia, Australia.

Ecology: Sandy places of hillsides, ravines and roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Oct.

Smithia salsuginea Hance 鹽鹼土坡油甘
J. Bot. 7(79): 164. 1869; FKH 77. 1912; FRPS 41: 355. 1995; FGD 5: 350. 2003.

Annual herb, 30 – 45 cm. Stems slender, few-branched, sparsely bristly. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 1 – 2 pairs, oblong-obovate, 15–20 × 6 – 7 mm, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes helicoids, 5 – 6-flowered. Calyx scarious, 10 – 12 mm, reticulate, subglabrous, upper lip longer, apex truncate or emarginate, lower one acute. Corolla yellow, 2.5–3 cm, adaxial surface with reticulate veins, abaxial surface with raised stripes. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary shortly stipitate; ovules several. Pods 10 – 12-segmented, segments orbicular, glabrous or papillose.

Locality: Kowloon (fide FHK 77. 1912).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Wet places near seasides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Notes: The type specimen (Sampson 15113) was collected from Kowloon by Sampson in 1868.

Solanum americanum Mill. 少花龍葵
Gard. Dict. ed. 8, no. 5. 1768; FFJ 5: 9. 1993; FOC 17: 317. 1994; TW ed. 2, 4: 564, pl. 256. 1998.
Solanum photeinocarpum Nakam. & Odash., J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 8: 54, fig. 2. 1936; FRPS 76(1): 77. 1978.

Annual herbs, 25–100 cm tall. Stems glabrous or nearly so. Leaves simple; petioles slender, 1–2 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent to the petiole, apex acuminate, margin subentire, sinuate or irregularly and coarsely toothed, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Cymes extra‑axillary, 3–6(–10)‑flowered, almost contracted into umbels; peduncles 1–2.5 cm; pedicels 5–8 mm. Calyx small, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes ovate. Corolla white, sometimes with a yellow eye, 5‑lobed to middle or beyond middle; lobes ovate‑oblong, 3–4 mm, pubescent abaxially. Stamens 5; filaments short, pubescent. Ovary ovoid, white‑tomentose on the lower part. Berry globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 530.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; perhaps native to S America, widely spread to all tropical and warm regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum capsicoides All. 牛茄子（癲茄）
Philos. Math. Soc. Roy. Turin 5: 64. 1773; FOC 17: 323. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 564. 1998.
Solanum surattense acut. non Burm. f.: FRPS 67(1): 105, pl. 27: 3–5. 1978.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems and branches glabrous or pilose, with pale yellow straight prickles. Leaves simple; petioles stout, 2–7 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, 5–13 × 4–12 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin 5–7‑lobed to middle, pubescent on adaxial surface, glabrous, or hairy only along veins on abaxial surface, with prickles along veins on both surfaces. Cymes 1–4‑flowered, extra‑axillary; peduncle short or obsolete; pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx 5–8 mm, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobes ovate, pubescent. Corolla white, greenish at base, tube ca. 2.5 mm; limb deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, ca. 10 × 4 mm. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 2.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry subglobose, 3.5 – 6 cm in diam., initially stellate‑tomentose, orange‑red when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1345; HK sheet 19995.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; perhaps native to Brazil, but widely spread over warm regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages and thickets. Flowering: Summer to autumn; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum erianthum D. Don 假煙葉樹
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 96. 1825; FFJ 5: 12, fig. 11. 1993; FOC 17: 316. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 566. 1998.
Solanum verbascifolium auct. non L.: FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 72. 1978.

Shrubs or small trees, 1.5–10 m tall, densely tomentose. Leaves simple; petioles thick, 1.5–5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate‑oblong, 10–29 × 4–12 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or obscurely sinuate, adaxially green, abaxially greyish green; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbose, subterminal; peduncle 3–10 cm; pedicels 3 – 5 mm. Calyx campanulate, 5‑lobed to middle. Corolla white, tube as long as calyx; limb ca. 1.5 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes oblong. Stamens 5; filaments 1–1.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, densely stellate‑tomentose. Berry globose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., initially stellate‑tomentose, glabrescent, yellowish brown when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 240, 477, 2948.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; native to S America, widespread in tropical Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum lasiocarpum Dunal 毛茄
Hist. Nat. Solanum 222. 1813; FOC 17: 323. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 567, photo: 300. 1998.
Solanum ferox auct. non L.: FHK 243. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 110, pl. 27: 6–9. 1978.

Herbs or subshrubs, 1–1.5 m tall, densely covered with pale yellow stellate hairs throughout. Stems and branches with flat, erect or slightly recurved prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 3–8 cm, often prickly; leaf blade ovate, 10–20 × 8–18 cm, base truncate or subhastate, apex acute, margin with 5–11 sinuate lobes, pubescent and prickly along veins on both surfaces. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, several‑flowered; peduncle ca. 3 mm; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Calyx cup‑shaped, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobe ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 8 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 1 mm; limb ca. 2 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 1 cm. Stamens 5; filaments very short. Ovary ovoid, pubescent. Berry globose, ca. 2 cm in diam., covered with tawny hairs.

Locality: Sai Kung, Mau Ping, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Sha Tau Kok. Y. S. Lau 479, 1344; L. T. Lo 220.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; widely distributed in SE Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum mammosum L. 乳茄（五代同堂茄）
Sp. Pl. 187. 1753; FRPS 67(1): 106, pl. 21: 15 – 19. 1978; FOC 17: 323. 1994
Stout herbs, to 1 m tall. Stems and branches covered with articulate hairs, glandular hairs and compressed prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 2.5–8 cm; leaf blade ovate, 5–10 × 4.5–9.5 cm, base ± cordate, apex acute or obtuse, margin irregularly and coarsely (3–)5(–7)‑lobed; lobes triangular, both surfaces densely covered with hairs, and with prickles on the midvein and veins. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, 2–4‑flowered, sometimes reduced to 1 flower; peduncle 3–10 mm; pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx shallowly cup‑shaped, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate. Corolla violet; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb ca. 1.8 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous or nearly so. Berry inverse pear‑shaped, 4.5–5.5 cm, often with 4–5 protuberances at base, yellow when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. K. L. Yip 4413, 4475.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Solanum melongena L. 茄（矮瓜）
Sp. Pl. 186. 1753; FRPS 67(1): 118. 1978; FFJ 5: 18, fig. 19. 1993; FOC 17: 325. 1994.

Annual herbs or shrubby, to 1 m tall. Branches often purplish and stellate‑tomentose when young, glabrescent. Leaves simple; petioles thick, 2–4.5 cm, stellate‑tomentose; leaf blade ovate to oblong‑ovate, 8–18 × 5–11 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, oblique, apex obtuse, margin shallowly or deeply sinuate‑lobed, stellate‑tomentose and sometimes with a few prickles on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flowers usually solitary; peduncle obsolete; pedicels 1–1.8 cm, stellate‑tomentose. Calyx stellate‑tomentose, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes lanceolate. Corolla purplish or violet; tube ca. 2 mm; limb 3(–5) cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes triangular. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 2.5 mm; anthers ca. 7.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, apex densely stellate‑tomentose. Berry greatly variable in shape and size, usually subglobose or cylindric, more than 6 cm in diam., purple, white or yellow when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 20078.
Distribution: Probably originated from SE Asia; widely cultivated from tropical to temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Solanum nigrum L. 龍葵
Sp. Pl. 186. 1753; FHK 242. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 76, pl. 19: 1–6, 1978; FFJ 5: 9, fig. 6. 1993; FOC 17: 318. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 571, pl. 259, photo 302. 1998.

Annual or biennial herbs, 30–100 cm tall, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves simple; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate, 2.5–10 × 1.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acute, margin entire or irregularly and coarsely toothed; lateral veins 5–6 on each side of midvein. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, 3–6(–10)‑flowered, almost contracted into umbels on short (2–4 cm) lateral peduncles; pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx small, shallowly cup‑shaped, 5‑toothed. Corolla white; limb ca. 9 mm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate. Stamens 5; filaments very short. Ovary ovoid, white‑tomentose on the lower part. Berry globose, ca. 8 mm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 9; Y. S. Lau 2361; Y. W. Lam 441.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in warm regions of Asia, Europe and America.
Ecology: Wastelands and roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum torvum Sw. 水茄
Prodr. 47. 1788; FRPS 67(1): 95. pl. 26: 7–8. 1978; FFJ 5: 15, fig. 16. 1993; FOC 17: 321. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 576, pl. 262, photo 304. 1998.

Shrubs 1–3 m tall, sparsely armed with pale yellow or reddish prickles. Branchlets, petioles, abaxial surface of leaves and peduncles densely covered with tawny stellate hairs. Leaves solitary or in pairs; petioles thick, 2–4 cm; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, 6–19 × 4–13 cm, base cordate or cuneate, ± oblique, apex acute, margin 5 – 7‑lobed or sinuate, densely covered with stellate hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein, unarmed or sometimes prickly. Cymes extra‑axillary, 2–3‑branched; peduncle 1–1.5 cm, sometimes prickly; pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx cup‑shaped, covered with stellate and glandular hairs abaxially, apex 5‑lobed. Corolla white; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb ca. 1.5 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 8 mm. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers ca. 7 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., glabrous, yellowish when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1949; L. T. Lo 78; HK sheet 39452.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, S Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; native to Caribbean; widely naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum tuberosum L. 馬鈴薯
Sp. Pl. 185. 1753; FHN 3: 463. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 94, pl. 23: 7–10. 1978; FOC 17: 320. 1994.

Perennial herbs, 30–80 cm tall, with subterranean tubers; tubers globose, oblate, or ellipsoidal, 3–10 cm in diam. Leaves odd‑pinnate, ovate in outline, 10–20 cm or longer; leaflets 3 or 4 pairs, mixed with small irregular lobes on the rachis, ovate or oblong, unequal, (1–)2 – 6(–8) × 1–4.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute, margin entire, sparsely pilose on both surfaces. Flowers in subterminal, leaf opposed, or axillary sparingly branched panicles. Calyx campanulate, sparsely pilose; lobes 5, lanceolate. Corolla rotate, white, pink or blue‑purple, 2.5–3 cm in diam.; limb 5‑lobed, lobes triangular. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry globose, smooth, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3328.
Distribution: Native to S America; cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Food.

Solanum undatum Lam. 野茄
Tab Encycl. 2: 22. 1793; FOC 17: 325. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 578. 1998.
Solanum cumingii Dunal, Prodr. 13(1): 363. 1852; FRPS 67(1): 119. 1978.
Solanum coagulans auct. non Forssk.: FRPS 67(1): 116. 1978; Check List HK Plants 220. 2002; 76. 2004.
Solanum sanctum auct. non L.: FHK 243. 1861.
Soanum incanum auct. non L.: FKH 182. 1912.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems and branches shaggy‑tomentose with stellate hairs, glabrescent, sparingly armed with prickles. Leaves unequal paired; petioles 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 15–14 × 4–7 cm, base obtuse or truncate, apex acute or obtuse, margin 5(–7)‑sinuate lobed, both surfaces densely shaggy‑tomentose with stellate hairs, and with short stout prickles along veins. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary; peduncles very short; pedicels 0.5–2 cm. Calyx campanulate, 6–9 mm, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobes triangular lanceolate. Corolla purple blue or white; limb 1.5–3 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes broadly triangular or ovate. Stamens 5; filaments 1.5–1.8 mm; anthers 5–8 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry globose, 2–3 cm in diam., glabrous, yellow when mature.

Locality: Tai Po, Sheung Shui. Y. S. Lau 475, 2945; L. T. Lo 260.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in SW and SE Asia, also in Africa.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.

Solanum violaceum Ortega 刺天茄
Nov. Pl. Descr. Dec. 56. 1798; FOC 17: 322. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 578, pl. 263, photo 305. 1998.
Solanum chinense Dunal, Hist. Nat. Solanum 240. 1813.
Solanum indicum auct. non L.: FHK 242. 1861; FKH 182. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 100, pl. 26: 1–6. 1978; Check List HK Plants 220. 2002; 77. 2004.

Shrubs 0.5–2 m tall, much branched. Branchlets sparingly prickled and densely tawny grey stellate‑tomentose. Leaves simple, unequal‑paired; petioles thick, 1.5–4 cm, densely stellate‑tomentose and sparingly prickled; leaf blade ovate, 5–11 × 2–8.5 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex obtuse or acute, margin 5–7 sinuate‑lobed, adaxial surface tomentose with short‑stalked, stellate hairs, abaxial surface with long‑stalked hairs and straight needle‑like prickles; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, 2–6 cm; peduncle ca. 1.5 cm; pedicels 4–15 mm, pubescent and prickly. Calyx cup‑shaped, 4–7 mm, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobes lanceolate, 3–5 mm. Corolla blue‑purple or white; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb 1–2 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–8 × 2–5 mm, obtuse. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers oblong, 5–6 mm. Berry globose, 0.8–1.3 cm in diam., shiny orange when mature.

Locality: Tai Po, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9175; Y. S. Lau 476; HK sheet 36079.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum wrightii Benth. 大花茄
FHK 243. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 115. 1978; FOC 17: 322. 1994.

Trees to 10 m tall. Branches and petioles hispid with stiff stellate hairs or bristles, and armed with a few straight stout prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 5–10 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, 25–30 × 15–20 cm, base oblique, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or sinuate lobed, with irregular ovate or lanceolate lobes, scabrid with dispersed bristle‑like hairs on adaxial surface, coarsely stellate‑hairy on abaxial surface. Cymes many‑flowered, axillary or extra‑axillary; peduncles unbranched or bifid; pedicels 0.6–1.5 cm, very hispid. Calyx 1–1.5 cm, densely hispid, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, apex long‑subulate. Corolla initially deep purple, gradually fading through blue to white; limb 6–9 cm in diam., 5‑lobed to 1/3 of its length, the lanceolate center of each lobe stellate‑hairy outside. Stamens 5; filaments 2–3 mm; anthers 1.2–1.5 cm. Berry globose, 3–4 cm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 4101, 4102, 4103.
Distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions; native to Bolivia and Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of this species was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 and 1854. Bentham (1861) described this species based on a plant cultivated in Hong Kong. Dunn & Tutcher (1912) last recorded the species on the Bonham Road, Hong Kong.

records.text:
Solena amplexicaulis (Lam.) Gandhi 茅瓜
Fl. Hassan District 179. 1976; FRPS 73(1): 178, pl. 47: 1–9. 1986; FFJ 5: 243, fig. 227. 1993; FGD 3: 121, fig. 84. 1995.
Bryonia amplexicaulis Lam., Encycl. 1: 496. 1785.
Bryonia umbellata Klein ex Willd., Sp. Pl. 4(1): 618. 1805.
Karivia umbellata (Klein ex Willd.) Arn., J. Bot. (Hooker) 3: 275. 1841; FHK. 124. 1861.
Melothria heterophylla (Lour.) Cogn., Mon. Phan. 3: 618. 1881; FGZ 184. 1956; FHN 1: 472. 1964.
Solena heterophylla Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 514 –515. 1790.
Zehneria umbellata Thw., Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 125. 1859; FKH 112. 1912.

Plant dioecious. Roots fusiform, 1.5 –2 cm in diam. Stems and branches glabrous. Petioles 0.5 –1.8 cm; leaf blades papery or leathery, very variable, triangular-hastate, narrowly triangular-lanceolate, ovate-cordate, subtriangular, undivided or 3 –5-lobed, 3.5–15 × 3 –12 cm, base cordate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin entire or undulate or sparsely denticulate, often scabrous and glabrous on both surfaces. Male inflorescences umbellate,10 –20-flowered; peduncle very short; pedicels 2–8 mm. Male flowers: calyx-tube 5 mm, lobes subulate, 0.2–0.3 mm; corolla yellow, lobes triangular, 1.5 mm; filaments filiform, ca. 3 mm, anthers curved. Female flowers: solitary; pedicels 0.5 –1 cm; ovary ovoid, 2.5 –3.5 × 2–3 mm; stigmas 3. Fruit red-brown, ellipsoid or subglobose, 2– 6 cm long, 2–5 cm in diam., pubescent. Seeds grey-white, ovoid, 5–7 mm long, 5 mm in diam., emarginate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 321, 709, 3132.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Sikkim, Vietnam, Indonesia (Java), Nepal.
Ecology: Forests or thickets in valleys. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solidago decurrens Lour. 一枝黃花
Fl. Cochinch. 501. 1790; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3–4): 160. 1968; FRPS 74: 75. 1985; FGD 8: 190, fig. 109. 2007.
Solidago virgaurea var. leiocarpa (Benth.) A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. Arts, n. s. 4: 395. 1857; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1064. 1998.
Solidago virgaurea auct. non L.: FHK 179; FKH 140. 1912.

Perennial erect herb, 25–80 cm tall, simple or branching on upper portion. Radical leaves ovate, oblong or lanceolate, 3–7 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate to form long winged petiole of 2–13 cm or more. Cauline leaves similar in shape, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, short‑petiolate, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate or subserrate, much smaller in size upward, sparsely puberulous along margin, subglabrous on both surfaces. Capitula in tight or loose racemes or panicles. Involucres campanulate, 5–7 mm in diam.; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate; the outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 2 mm; the inner ones lanceolate‑oblong, ca. 6 mm. Ligulate florets pistillate, corolla yellow, ca. 8 mm; tubular florets bisexual, corolla yellow, ca. 4 mm. Cypsela glabrous or puberulous above, cylindric.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. Y. Yeung 163 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 7168 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 663.
Distribution: Widely distributed in S, SW, C & E China.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Soliva anthemifolia (Juss.) Sweet 裸柱菊
Hort. Brit. 243. 1826; FKH 146. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 162. 1968; FRPS 76(1): 135. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1068. 1998.
Gymnostyles anthemifolia Juss., Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 4: 262. 1804.

Small prostrate annual herbs; stem short and seems to be stemless, stoloniferous. Leaves alternate, forming rosette at base, petioles 2–3 cm, leaf blade spatulate or oblanceolate, 3–13 × 1–2.5 cm, 2–3‑pinnatisect with segments linear‑elliptic, apex acute, margin entire or irregularly 1–3‑dentate, subglabrous or villose on both surfaces. Capitula subglobose, 7–11 mm in diam., sessile and axillary to leaves, solitary or sometimes with few heads aggregated at basal nodes. Involucres dish‑like; phyllaries 2‑seriate, ovate‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, herbaceous with margin scarious, hairy on abaxial side; outer phyllaries 3–3.5 mm long, 1–1.2 mm wide; inner ones 3–4 × 0.3–0.6 mm. Receptacle convex, naked. Outer florets in many series, female, corolla absent with pistil only, fertile; style minutely divided. Central florets few, about 8–12, bisexual but usually functionally staminate, corolla tubular, yellow, 1.2–2 mm, apex 3‑lobed, base narrowed; stamens 3, anthers enclosed, base obtuse, apical appendages acute; style without branches, apex capitate and flat. Cypselae oblanceolate, 2–2.5 × 0.8– 1.1 mm, dorsiventrally compressed, margin with thicken rugose wings which extended to the apex, colour brown with the wings orange‑brown, villous near the apical region, style persistent. Pappus none.

Locality: Kong Sin Wan, Wu Kai Sha, Tai Po, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Yuen Long, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1774, 1792; S. Y. Hu 6772 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; native to S America.
Ecology: Wastelands, cultivated lands. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.

Sonchus arvensis L. 苣蕒菜
Sp. Pl. 793. 1753; FKH 151. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 162. 1968; FRPS 80(1): 64. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1071. 1998; FGD 8: 260, fig. 161. 2007.

Perennial lactiferous herbs; stem erect, 0.3–1.5(–2) m tall, striate, apically branched, the upper stem portion, branches and peduncles covered with yellow to dark purple stipitate glandular hair. Basal and lower leaves oblanceolate to oblanceolate‑oblong, 6–30 × 1.5–7.5 cm, mostly simple, occasionally lyrately pinnatilobed or pinnatifid with several lateral lobes hemispherical, semi‑elliptic, ovate to deltoid, sometimes oblique; while apical lobes larger, ovate, ovate‑oblong to elliptic; leaf upper and lower surfaces glabrous, margin minutely denticulate or mucronulate; radical leaves with base narrowed and apex obtuse‑rounded; lower leaves with base auriculate and semi‑amplexicaul; apex obtuse to acute. Middle and upper leaves gradually smaller, lanceolate or linear, base sessile and semi‑amplexicaul, apex acute, auriculate or not. Capitula 2 cm across, in corymbose arrangement or sub‑umbelliform. Involucres campanulate‑urceolate with base slightly swollen, 14–15 × 6–8 mm; phyllaries herbaceous green, abaxial side stipitate glandular, margin hyaline, apex acute or acuminate, in 3–4 rows; outer series elongate‑triangular to lanceolate, 4–5 × 1–1.8 mm; middle ones lanceolate, 6–8.5 × 1.8–2.5 mm; inner layers linear, 10–13 × 1.5–2.5 mm. All florets yellow, hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla ligulate, 13 – 15 mm, lower tube 8–9 mm, hairy near the summit, ligule 5–5.5 mm, apex minutely 5‑lobed. Cypselae brown, ellipsoidal, somewhat compressed, 3–3.2 × 0.8–1 mm, narrowed at both ends, glabrous, ribbed, transversely rugose. Pappus white, 7–8 mm, capillary and slender, entangled with each other, deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 231; Y. S. Lau 87; S. Y. Hu 13053 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Europe.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, cultivated lands. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sonchus oleraceus L. 苦苣菜
Sp. Pl. 794. 1753; FHK 194. 1861; FKH 151. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 164. 1968; FRPS 80(1): 63. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1073. 1998; FGD 8: 260. 2007.

Annual or biennial herbs; stem erect, 30–150 cm tall, simple or branched in upper portion, striate, glabrous except the apical branches and peduncles covered with stipitate glandular hair. Basal leaves oblanceolate, lyrately pinnatifid or pinnatisect, base attenuate and narrowed down to form winged petiole, apex rounded or obtuse, margin toothed. Cauline leaves oblanceolate or elliptic, pinnatisect or lyrately pinnatisect, 4–20 × 1.8–9 cm, base abruptly narrowed down to form winged petiole, wing gradually broaden towards the base, forming circular auricles, semi‑amplexicaul, margin and auricle unequally mucronate and spiny, apical lobes broadly triangular, broadly hastate or ovate‑cordate; lateral lobes 1–5 pairs, elliptic to lanceolate, pointing backward, apices of all lobes acuminate, acute or obtuse. Upper leaves similar in shape, or appearing lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, base widen and semi‑amplexicaul, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, toothed throughout or on the apical half only. All leaves glabrous above and beneath. Capitula few, arranged as tight corymbs or racemes at branch terminals, or solitary. Involucres broad‑campanulate, 1 cm × 0.6–0.7 cm; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, imbricate, stipitate glandular hairy on midvein or not, membranous along margin and apex, minutely hairy near apex; outer two layers lanceolate or elongat‑triangular, 3–7 × 1–1.5 mm; middle and inner ones lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, 8–10 × 1.5–2 mm. All florets yellow, ligulate, about 10 mm, ligule 5 – 5.5 mm, 5‑toothed at apex, lower tube 4– 5 mm, hairy near summit. Cypselae brown, ellipsoidal or oblanceolate‑ellipsoidal, 3 × 1 mm, flattened, ribbed, transversely rugose, without hair, apex narrowed, beakless. Pappus white, 6–7 mm, capillary and entangled with each other.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3115; Y. W. Lam 724, 764.
Distribution: Native to Europe and C Asia; widely distributed in China.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Jul.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Sonerila cantonensis Stapf 蜂斗草
Ann. Bot. (Oxford) 6(23): 302. 1892; FKH 107. 1912; FRPS 53(1): 261. 1984.

Herb or subshrub, (15–)20–50 cm tall, sometimes stoloniferous. Stems obtusely quadrangular, covered with spreading coarse and fine, short hairs when young, glabrescent. Petioles 0.5–3(–6) cm, densely hirsute or villous. Leaf blade papery to submembranous, ovate, elliptic-ovate, narrowly lanceolate-oblong, or subelliptic, 3–5.5(–13) × 1.8–6 cm, base cuneate or obtuse and sometimes slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate to acute, margin serrulate and with terminal bristle, with 2 pairs of lateral primary veins, adaxially glabrous or sparsely appressed-strigulose, abaxially purplish red, hirsute only on veins. Inflorescences terminal, scorpioid cymes or dichasial cymes, 3–7-flowered; peduncle 1.5–3 cm, puberulous and with sparse glandular hairs; bracts minute, caducous. Pedicel 1–3 mm, slightly 3-ribbed. Calyx-tube tubular-campanulate, 5–7 mm, 3-ribbed, 6-veined, puberulous or with sparse glandular hairs; calyx-lobes broadly triangular, ca. 1 mm, apex acute. Petals pink to pale rosy, oblong, 5–10 mm, with sparse glandular hairs or pilose on midvein abaxially, apex acute. Stamens 3, equal; filament ca. 7 mm; anthers ca. 8 mm, base slightly forked. Ovary flask-shaped, apex with a membranous crown. Fruit capsular, obconical, 5–7 × 4–5 mm, ± 3-ribbed.

Locality: Ping Fung Shan, Kwai Tau Leng. Y. W. Lam 242; HK sheet 33091.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Vietnam.
