Ecology: Forests, hillsides, valleys, shaded damp places. Flowering: Sep. – Oct.; fruiting: Dec.– Feb.

Sonerila erecta Jack 三蕊草
Malayan Misc. 1(5): 7. 1820; S. S. Renner, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 484, fig. 43. 2001.
Sonerila tenera Royle, Ill. Bot. Himal. Mts. 215, pl. 45, fig. 2. 1834; FKH 107. 1912; FRPS 53(1): 265. 1984.

Herb, 5 –15 cm tall. Stems slender, slightly quadrangular, winged, glandular hairy and puberulent, branched from the apex or the base. Petiole 1 – 3 mm, slightly winged, with glandular hairs. Leaf blade membranous, narrowly elliptic to ovate, (5–)10 – 25 × (3–)4 –7 mm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, strigose, adaxially sparsely setose, abaxially glabrous or scurfy except for sparsely hairy on veins; lateral primary veins 1 – 2 pairs. Inflorescences terminal, scorpioid cymes, 2 – 5-flowered, 1– 2.5 cm, with spreading glandular hairs; peduncle 8–15 mm. Pedicels 1–5 mm, covered with sparsely glandular hairs. Calyx-tube campanulate-tubular, ca. 4 mm, ± 3-angular, 6-veined, usually covered with sparsely glandular hairs only on veins; calyx-lobes very short, broadly ovate-triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Petals pink, purplish red or bluish, oblong-elliptic, ca. 3 mm, apex acute, oblique, sparsely glandular hairy on midvein abaxially; stamens 3, equal; anthers broadly ovate, ca. 1.8 mm, base forked, connective not extended. Ovary flask-shaped, membranous crown slightly 3-lobed. Capsule cylindrical, 6 – 11 × 2 – 2.5 mm, obtusely ribbed, smooth or sometimes sparsely pilose.

Locality: Mount Gough. HK sheet 1800.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests, grovelands, roadsides, grassland. Flowering: Aug. – Oct.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as Sonerila tenera Royle previously (Check List HK Plants 167. 2002; 61. 2004).

Sonneratia apetala Buch. - Ham. 無瓣海桑
Symes, Embassy Ava 3: 477. 1800, cum tab.; Baker & Steenis in Fl. Malesiana ser. 1, 4: 286. 1951.

Tree, to 12 m tall (15(–20) m elsewhere); twigs slender and pendulous; bark light brown and thin; pneumatophores conspicuous, grey, arising from horizontal roots, up to 1m tall. Leaves sparse, opposite; petioles 0.5–1.1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, 4–8.5 × 1–3 cm, glabrous, margin entire. Inflorescence mostly 3, in terminal cyme. Flowers small, apetalous, 1.5 – 2 cm. Calyx 4(–5)-lobed, calyx tube cup-shaped during anthesis. Stigma broad, mushroom-shaped at the anthesis. Stamens numerous; filament white, 1 cm long. Ovary 6–8 locular. Fruit an oval berry, green when young, becoming greyish when mature, 1.5 – 2.5 cm, distinctively smaller than other members in Sonneratiaceae; hypanthium flat-expanded. Seeds compactly arranged in the fleshy pulp of the placenta, rusty, mostly “U” or “V”-shaped, or irregular, 90 – 242 per fruit.

Locality: Deep Bay, Lantau Island. (Naturalized) W. S. Tang s.n. (HK sheet 40305).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong (Shenzhen, introduced); S Asia ranging from India, Bangladesh and Malaysia to Solomon Islands and the New Hebrides.
Ecology: Introduced accidentally. Near the banks of tidal river and mudflat, especially where salinity is low. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Sonneratia caseolaris (L.) Engler 海桑
Engl. & Prantl., Nachtr. 261. 1897; Baker & Steenis in Fl. Malesiana ser. 1, 4: 283, fig. 3c. 1951; FHN 1: 426. 1964, p.p.; FGD 1: 92. 1987.
Sonneratia acida L. f., Suppl. Sp. Pl. 252. 1781
Sonneratia lanceolata Blume, Herb. Lugd. Batav. 567. 1851.

Tree, to 12 m tall (15(–20) m elsewhere), crown sparse; branches horizontal, twigs slender; bark deep to pale brown or grey, smooth or lightly fissured; pneumatophores grey, conical, taper towards the ends, up to 1(–2) m tall. Leaves opposite; petiole short (0.4–0.9 cm) to almost sessile; leaf blade variable in shape, young leaves lanceolate, apex acute; adult leaves elliptic, oblong or obovate, 4 – 7 × 2.5–5 cm, glabrous, adaxial surface deep green, midvein often red at the base toward the petiole. Flower solitary or in few-flowered cyme on the outer pendulous twigs. Calyx 6(–8) lobed; tube cup-shaped during anthesis. Petals inconspicuous, slender, lanceolate, dark red. Stigma capitate but not expanded. Stamens numerous, filaments slender, pink or red below and white distally, 2 – 4.5 cm long; anthers pale yellow. Ovary globose, flattened or depressed above, 15–18(–20)-locular. Fruits edible, compressed globose, 3–8.5 cm in length, pericarp leathery, green when young and turns yellowish green and aromatic when mature; hypanthium flat-expanded. Seeds many, rusty, embedded in the fleshy pulp, mostly “U” or “V”-shaped, or irregular, 800–1300 per fruit.

Locality: Deep Bay, Ma Wan, Tolo Pond, Lantau Island. (Naturalized) HK sheet 39179, 39181, 39182.
Distribution: Native to China (Hainan Island) and cultivated in SE China; SE Asia to N Australia.
Ecology: Introduced accidentally. Near the banks of tidal river and mudflat where salinity is low. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore), timber, corks or floats (pnematophores), paper (pulp).
records.uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore), timber, corks or floats (pnematophores), paper (pulp).

records.text:
Sophora japonica L. 槐
Mant. Pl. 1: 68. 1767; FHK 95. 1861; FKH 87. 1912; FRPS 40: 92. 1994; FGD 5: 220. 2003.

Tree, 15– 26 m tall. Branches glabrous. Leaves odd-pinnate; petioles inflated at base and enveloping the bud; leaflets 9– 15, opposite or subopposite, ovate-lanceolate, 2.5 – 5 × 1.2 – 1.8 cm, base obtusely rounded to broadly cuneate, asymmetric, apex acuminate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially at first, soon glabrescent. Panicles terminal. Calyx campanulate, ca. 4 mm, 5-toothed; teeth obtuse. Corolla white or yellowish, 10 mm. Petals subequal; vexillum broadly cordate, apex emarginate, purple-striate, shortly clawed; wings and keel oblong, clawed; keel narrower, ca. 4 mm wide. Stamens nearly free. Ovary subglabrous. Pods fleshy, moniliform, 2–5 cm, indehiscent. Seeds 1–6, reniform, 9 mm, slightly compressed.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2503, 2620, 2818.
Distribution: Widely spread from N to S China; cultivated in E Asia, Europe and America.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug. – Oct.
Uses: Environmental (ornamental), bee plants (honey), medicinal (folklore).

Sophora tomentosa L. 絨毛槐
Sp. Pl. 1: 373. 1753; FKH 87. 1912; FRPS 40: 84. 1994; FGD 5: 219. 2003.

Shrub or small tree, 2 – 4 m tall. Branches and branchlets greenish, tomentose. Leaves odd-pinnate, alternate, 12 –18 cm; leaflets 11–15(–19), subleathery, broadly elliptic or suborbicular, rarely obovate, 2.5–5 × 2–3.5 cm, base rounded, apex rounded or emarginate, slightly oblique, glabrous adaxially, greyish tomentose abaxially. Racemes terminal, sometimes paniculate, 10–20 cm; pedicels articulate. Calyx campanulate, 6–7 mm, truncate, densely greyish tomentose abaxially. Corolla yellow; vexillum broadly ovate, 17 × 10 mm, claw 3 mm; wings oblong, as long as vexillum, claws 5 mm, slender; keel slightly shorter than vexillum and wings. Stamens 10, filaments free. Ovary hairy. Pods leathery, moniliform, 7–15 cm, densely tomentose, dehiscent when mature. Seeds 6–8, brown, globular, 6 mm in diam., shining.

Locality: Tai Long Sai Wan. Y. S. Lau 1531; Y. W. Lam 493.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical regions.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: Aug. – Oct.; fruiting: Sep. –Dec.

Sopubia matsumurae (T. Yamaz.) C. Y. Wu 毛果短冠草（短冠草）
Novon 9 (2): 288. 1999.
Petitmenginia matsumurae T. Yamaz., J. Jap. Bot. 25: 214. 1950.
Sopubia lasiocarpa P. C. Tsoong, FRPS 67(2): 405. 1979; FOC 18: 87. 1998.
Sopubia stricta auct. non (Benth.) G. Don: Rep. Bot. & Forest. Dep. Hongk. (1913): M21. 1914; (1914): M34. 1915.

Annual herbs, to 38 cm tall. Stems erect, basally terete, apically branched and ribbed, with short crisp hairs. Leaves opposite or subalternate on upper part of stem; leaf blade linear, to 5 cm × 1.5 mm, adaxially hispidulous, margin revolute. Racemes sparsely flowered, forming a large panicle. Pedicels 1.5–2 mm, pubescent. Bracteoles 2, attached near base of calyx. Calyx ca. 1.5 mm, inflated to 3.5 mm in fruit, 10‑veined; lobes narrowly triangular, subequal, outside hispidulous, inside glabrous, apex acute. Corolla purplish, ca. 1 cm; tube ca. 7 mm; lobes obovate, subequal. Capsules 5 –6 mm, much longer than persistent calyx, hispidulous, apex deeply concave, to 2/5 of capsule length. Seeds dark brown, irregularly oblong.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 10554.
Distribution: Hunan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: Autumn.
Notes: This species was recorded as Sopubia stricta G. Don and S. lasiocarpa P. C. Tsoong previously (Check List HK Plants 73. 1993; 248. 2002; 85. 2004).

Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench 高粱
Methodus 207. 1794; FRPS 10(2): 128, pl. 30: 5–7, 75: 4. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 578. 2000; FYN 9: 648, pl. 108: 5–7. 2003; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 490. 2009.
Holcus bicolor L., Mant. Alt. 301. 1771.
Sorghum vulgare (L.) Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 101. 1805; FKH 324. 1912; FHN 4: 470. 1977; FFJ 6: 263, fig. 233. 1995.

Annual stout herb; culms solid, erect, 2–4 m tall. Leaf sheath usually shorter than internodes, glabrous; ligule ca. 12 mm, hard membranous, apex rounded; leaf blades linear-lanceolate or narrow lanceolate, 30–60 × 2–7 cm, glabrous, apex acuminate, margins scabrous. Panicle dense, 15–30 cm; branches subverticillate, base densely white pilose; rachis internode short, not fragile. Spikelets paired, dimorphic, sessile spikelets ca. 5 mm, ovate; glumes dark brown when mature, coriaceous, midsection glabrous, shiny, upper portion and callus hispid; lower glume ca. 5–6 mm, margins inrolled; upper glume ± boat-shaped, rounded; lower lemma long elliptic, membranous, margins inrolled, ciliate; upper lemma subtriangular, membranous, ciliate; awn geniculate ca. 10 mm; palea linear. Pedicellate spikelets short, staminate.

Locality: Cultivated. P. P. H. But 124; L. T. Lo 179, 378.
Distribution: Cultivated throughout tropical, subtropical and warm temperate regions.
Uses: Food (beverage base, cereal, sugar), animal food (fodder, forage).
records.uses: Food (beverage base, cereal, sugar), animal food (fodder, forage).

records.text:
Sorghum halepense (L.) Pers. 石茅（亞刺伯高粱）
Syn. Pl. 1: 101. 1805; FKH 324. 1912; FHN 4: 469, fig. 1257. 1977; FFJ 6: 262. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 119, pl. 28. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 579. 2000; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 489. 2009.
Holcus halepensis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1047. 1753.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 0.5–3 m tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, or puberulous at base nodes; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 20–90 × 0.5–4 cm, glabrous, margins scabrous, midvein white, conspicuous; ligule membranous. Panicle lanceolate to pyramidal in outline, with soft white hairs in basal axil; primary branches solitary or whorled, spreading, lower part bare, upper part branched, the secondary branches tipped by racemes; racemes fragile, composed of 2–5 spikelet pairs. Sessile spikelet elliptic or ovate-elliptic; callus obtuse, bearded; lower glume subleathery, veins distinct in upper part, keel winged, apex 3-denticulate; upper glume slightly boat-shaped, keeled in upper part; lower lemma lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, hyaline membranous; upper lemma oblong, acute and mucronate or 2-lobed and awned; awn 1–1.6 cm; lodicules 2, broad obovate, emarginate; stamens 3; styles 2, base connate. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, narrowly lanceolate.

Locality: Ma Liu Shui, Tai Po. P. P. H. But 73; Y. S. Lau 1978, 3111.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; N Africa, Caucasus, C and W Asia, Indian Subcontinent, naturalized in warm temperate regions, exact native range obscure.
Ecology: Streams, valleys, wastelands, a weed in fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Sorghum nitidum (Vahl) Pers. 光高粱
Syn. Pl. 1: 101. 1805; FHN 4: 469. 1977; FFJ 6: 262, fig. 232. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 118, pl. 30: 8. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 579, pl. 244. 2000; FOC 22: 600. 2006; FGD 9: 488, fig. 258. 2009.
Holcus nitidus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 2: 102. 1791.
Andropogon tropicus Spreng, Syst. Veg. 1: 287. 1825; FHK 423. 1861.
Sorghum fulvum (R. Br.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 164. 1812; FKH 324. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 0.6–2 m tall; nodes bearded with pale spreading hairs. Leaf sheaths clasping, glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear, 10–40(–50) × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous to hispid, dorsally convex; ligule obtuse, 1–1.5 mm. Panicle loose, glabrous but with soft hairs at the nodes; primary branches whorled, simple, flexuous, lower part bare; racemes borne at branch ends, fragile, composed of 2–4 spikelet pairs; internodes and pedicels brown-ciliate. Sessile spikelet ovate-lanceolate, brown bearded, callus obtuse; lower glume leathery, glossy, upper part and margins hispid with brown hairs; upper glume lightly boat-shaped; lower lemma slightly shorter than glume, thicken membranous, subchartaceous, margins inrolled, ciliate; upper lemma hyaline membranous; awn 1–1.7 cm, or awnless; lodicules 2, glabrous; style free, penicillate, brown. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet usually staminate, elliptic.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 3006; HK sheet 15749, 38095.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia, Indonesia, Philippines, Pacific islands, NE Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillsides.

Sorghum propinquum (Kunth) Hitchc. 擬高粱
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 249. 1931 [“1929”] ; FFJ 6: 262. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 121, pl. 29. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 579. 2000; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 490. 2009 [“propinqum”].
Andropogon propinquus Kunth, Enum. Pl. 1: 502. 1833.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms erect, 1–3 m tall, many-noded; nodes puberulous. Leaf sheaths glabrous, ciliate at mouth and margins; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 40–90 × 3–5 cm, glabrous, midvein robust, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm, puberulous. Panicle open, ovate or broadly ovate; primary branches in whorls of 3–6; lower part bare, upper part branched, branches tipped by racemes; racemes fragile, composed of 3–7 spikelet pairs. Sessile spikelet elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate; callus obtuse, pubescent with pale hairs; lower glume subleathery, upper keeled, apex sharply acute, entire or tridenticulate; upper glume lanceolate, upper keeled, pilose; lower lemma lanceolate, hyaline membranous, ciliate; upper lemma broad oblong, acute or emarginate, awnless, rarely with short awn; palea very short; styles 2, free or base connate; stigma penicillate. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, linear-lanceolate, narrower than sessile spikelet, glabrous.

Locality: So Kon Po (cultivated). HK sheet 8613.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; S India, Sri Lanka, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Sorghum sudanense (Piper) Stapf 蘇丹草
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 113. 1917; FFJ 6: 263, fig. 234. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 124. 1997; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 490. 2009.
Andropogon sorghum (L.) Brot. subsp. sudanensis Piper, Proc. Biol. Soc. Washington 28(4): 33. 1915.

Annual herb. Culms erect, 1–3 m tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths longer than internodes at the base, the upper shorter than internodes, glabrous or pilose at mouth and base; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate; 15–40 × 1–5 cm, glabrous, abaxially convex, margins scabrous, midvein white; ligule hard membranous, apex ciliate. Panicle narrow ovate to pyramid, branches slender, subverticillate, obliquely spreading; racemes usually tardily fragile at maturity, composed of 2–5 spikelet pairs. Sessile spikelet elliptic or oblonglanceolate; callus obtuse, pubescent; lower glume ovate, margins inrolled above the middle, keeled near apex, margins ciliate; upper glume boat-shaped, inrolled, margins membranous; lower lemma elliptic-lanceolate, hyaline membranous, glabrous or margins ciliate; upper lemma ovate or ovate-elliptic, apex 2-lobed, awned; awn 10–16 mm, geniculate; stamen 3; style 2. Caryopsis elliptic or obovateelliptic. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, linear-lanceolate, persistent.

Locality: So Kon Po (cultivated). HK sheet 15804.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Heilongjiang, Henan, Nei Mongol, Ningxia, Xinjiang, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian (cultivated or naturalized); native to Africa, now widely cultivated for forage.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Spathodea campanulata P. Beauv. 火焰樹
Fl. Oware 1: 47 – 48, t. 27, 28. 1805; FRPS 69: 23, pl. 7. 1990; FFJ 5: 88, fig. 96. 1993.

Tree to 12 m; bark greyish brown. Branches appressed puberulent when young, subglabrous and greyish white lenticellate when old. Leaves with petiole to 45 cm; leaflets (3–)9–13(–17), subsessile, elliptic to obovate, 5–10 × 2.5–5 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate, entire, subglabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 – 7 pairs. Inflorescences terminal, dense; rachis ca. 12 cm, brown puberulent. Pedicels 2–4 cm. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 2 cm. Bracteoles 2, 0.2–1 cm. Calyx spathaceous, tomentose abaxially. Corolla orange‑red to bright red, campanulate; tube swollen at one side; lobes erect, broadly ovate, unequal, corrugated, 3 × 3–4 cm. Stamens exserted; filaments 5–7 cm; anthers ca. 8 mm. Ovary glabrous; style 6 cm; stigma 2‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate. Capsule blackish brown, 15 – 25 × 3.5 cm. Seeds suborbicular, with peripheral wing.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 125; L. T. Lo 29.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to Africa, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Environmental.

Spathoglottis pubescens Lindl. 苞舌蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 120. 1831, et Bot. Reg. 8(n. s.): sub. t. 19. 1845; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 75, fig. 38. 1977; FRPS 18: 252, pl. 44: 3–4. 1999; FGD 7: 411, fig. 211. 2006; FOC 25: 288. 2009.
Spathoglottis fortunei Lindl., Bot. Reg. 31: pl. 19. 1845; FHK 355. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 71. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, requiring a dormant period over dry season; roots profuse, fibrous, originating from a basal point of the pseudobulb; pseudobulbs irregularly tuberous, compressed, often angular or irregularly humped. Leaves 2–4, all basal, emerging from the base of the pseudobulb; petioles sheathing, purplish; cataphylls membraneous, purplish and soon disintegrating; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, plicate, 12–35(–43) × 1–3(–4.5) cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate. Flowers bright yellow, resupinate; sepals similar in length and width, 1.2–1.6 × 0.5–0.7 cm; the odd one ovate-elliptic, concave, apex acute; lateral ones oblique ovate-oblong, apex acute; petals ovate, similar length with sepals but slightly wider, conspicuously veined; lip strongly 3-lobed, the base bluntly saccate, the interior of the sac with 2 barbate ridges along the disk; lateral lobes oblong, extending forward, the inner surface flecked, speckled or wholly bright brownish red; the midlobe panduriform, with 2 waxy, fleshy, orange calli at the base, with a ridge between the calli extending forward to apex, column long, arching, yellow, winged along the side with a basal annulus; anther pointing downward, ovate, yellow; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4, waxy; ovary inconspicuously sulcate, very hairy.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 10780, 10862 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3173.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina.
Ecology: Open grassy slopes, fire-resistant. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Spatholobus suberectus Dunn 密花豆
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 35(247): 489. 1900; FRPS 41: 192. 1995; FGD 5: 303, fig. 160. 2003.

Climbing shrub, to 10 m or longer. Stems stout, with red juice flood out when injured. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets papery or subleathery, the terminal one broadly elliptic, 9–19 × 5–14 cm, bilateral symmetric, base acuminate, apex rounded or shortly acuminate, lateral ones ovate or broadly ovate, asymmetric, base oblique, glabrous on both surfaces or slightly puberulent, lateral veins 6 –8 pairs, slightly incurved. Panicles axillary or terminal, up to 50 cm; peduncle and pedicels yellow-brown pubescent. Calyx tubular, 3.5 – 4 mm, hairy, calyx-teeth less than 1 mm. Corolla white, 7 – 8 mm, petals all clawed; vexillum suborbicular, 4 – 4.5 mm, emarginate; wings 3.5–4 mm; keel slightly shorter. Stamens included. Ovary densely white hirsute. Pods knife-form, 9–11 cm, densely brown tomentose, 1-seeded. Seeds oblong, 2 × 1 cm, purple-brown, shining.

Locality: New Territories. A. Henry 12780; F. W. Xing 9164; HK sheet 7904.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Spergularia marina (L.) Griseb. 擬漆姑
Spic. Fl. Rumel. 1: 213. 1843; FOC 6: 5. 2001.
Spergularia salina J. & C. Persl., Fl. Cech. 95. 1819.
Arenaria rubra L. var. marina L. Sp. Pl. 423. 1753.

Annual or biennial herb. Stems 8 –20(–30) cm tall, densely pubescent. Leaves linear, 5 –30 × 1–1.5 mm, ± fleshy, apex mucronate; stipules broadly triangular, forming a sheath. Flowers terminal or axillary. Sepals ovate, abaxially glandular pubescent, margin membranous. Petals pink above, white near base, rarely entirely white, shorter than sepals, apex obtuse. Capsules ovoid, 5– 6 mm, slightly longer than calyx.

Locality: Nien Wan (Mei Hui Hu). Y. W. Lam 2018.
Distribution: Most provinces in China; widely distributed Asia, Europe, N Africa and N America.
Ecology: Stream-sides, lake-sides, farmlands near seaside.

Spermacoce articularis L. f. 糙葉豐花草
Suppl. Pl. 119. 1781; FTW ed. 2, 4: 327, pl. 147. 1998.
Borreria articularis (L. f.) F. N. Williams, Bull. Herb. Boissier 2, 5: 956. 1905; FHN 3: 362. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 206. 1999; FYN 15: 296. 2003; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.
Spermacoce hispida L., Sp. Pl. 1: 102. 1753; FHK 163. 1861; FKH 135. 1912.
Borreria hispida K. Schum., Nat. Pflanzenfam. IV(4): 144. 1891, nom. illeg., non B. hispida Spruce ex K. Schum. (1888).

Annual diffuse herbs, 30–60 cm or longer. Stems quadrangular, roughly pubescent or hispid on ribs. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–4 mm, hairy; stipules membranous, pilose; bristles pinkish, longer than the sheath; leaf blade oblong, obovate or spathulate, 1–3.5 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, initially hairy on both surfaces, later glabrescent, margin scabrous or shortly ciliate; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Flowers sessile or nearly so, 3–6 clustered in axils of stipules. Calyx‑tube cylindric, 2–3 mm, hispid; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm. Corolla pink or white, funnel‑shaped; tube 4–4.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, with a few hairs near apex of abaxial surface. Capsule ovoid, 3–5 mm long, 2–2.5 mm in diam., hispid, crowned by the 4 calyx‑teeth, separating into 2 valves.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2525; Y. W. Lam 1264, 1504.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia.
Ecology: Open fields and grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Spermacoce latifolia Aubl. 闊葉豐花草
Hist. Pl. Guiane 1: 55, t. 19, fig. 1. 1775; FTW ed. 2, 4: 329. 1998.
Borreria latifolia (Aubl.) K. Schum., Fl. Bras. 6(6): 61. 1888; FRPS 71(2): 207, pl. 49: 6 – 9. 1999; FGD 6: 244. 2005; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.

Annual diffuse herbs, to 70 cm or longer. Stems quadrangular, with winged ribs, roughly pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 3–10 mm, roughly hairy; stipules membranous, roughly hairy; bristles yellowish brown, longer than the sheath; leaf blade elliptic or ovate‑oblong, 2–7.5 × 1–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or obtuse, sparsely hispid on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 – 6 on each side of midvein, conspicuous. Flowers sessile, several clustered in axils of stipules. Calyx‑tube cylindric, ca. 1 mm, hispid; lobes 4, ovate‑lanceolate ca. 2 mm. Corolla pale purple, or rarely white, funnel‑shaped; tube 2–2.5 mm, sparsely pubescent and with a ring of hairs at base inside; lobes 4, triangular ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, often with a few long hairs near apex. Capsule subglobose, 3–3.5 mm in diam., hairy, separating into 2 valves.

Locality: Naturalized. L. T. Lo 468; Y. W. Lam 1156.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; native to tropical America, widely spread else where in tropical and subtropical areas.
Ecology: Open fields and grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Spermacoce mauritiana O. Gideon 二萼豐花草
Kew Bull. 37(4): 547. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 329. 1998.
Borreria repens DC., Prodr. 4: 542. 1803; FHN 3: 362. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 208. 1999; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.

Annual herbs, 30–60 cm tall. Stems diffuse or decumbent, quadrangular, roughly pubescent or hispid on ribs. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–4 mm, hairy; stipules membranous, pilose; bristles pinkish, longer than the sheath; leaf blade oblong, obovate or spathulate, 1–3.5 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, initially hairy on both surfaces, later glabrescent, margin scabrous or shortly ciliate; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Flowers 3–6 clustered in axils of stipules, sessile. Calyx‑tube cylindric, 2–3 mm, hispid; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm. Corolla pink or white, funnel‑shaped; tube 4–4.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, with a few hairs near apex of abaxial surface. Capsule ovoid, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, Sha Lo Tung. Y. S. Lau 3003; Y. W. Lam 896.
Distribution: Hainan; Java, Mauritius.
Ecology: Open fields and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Spermacoce stricta L. f. 豐花草
Suppl. Pl. 120. 1781; FHK 162. 1861; FKH 135. 1912.
Borreria stricta (L. f.) G. Mey, Prim. Fl. Esseq. 83. 1818; FHN 3: 361, fig. 773. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 208, pl. 49: 1 – 5. 1999; FGD 6: 243, fig. 132. 2005; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.

Annual herbs, 15–60 cm tall. Stems slender, erect or spreading, quadrangular, hispid on the ribs. Leaves leathery, subsessile; stipules united, short and broad, subglabrous or hispid, with a few pink, long bristles at apex; leaf blade linear or linear‑oblong, 2.5–5 × 0.25–0.6 cm, gradually narrowed to the base, apex acuminate, roughly pubescent on both surfaces, margin revolute; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers sessile, in dense, axillary whorl‑like clusters. Calyx‑tube 1.5–2.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, equal to the tube. Corolla white, funnel‑shaped; tube 1.5–2.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, linear‑oblong, ca. 1 mm, sparsely hispid adaxially. Capsule obovate‑globular, slightly compressed, 1–1.5 mm in diam., ± pubescent, separating into 2 valves.

Locality: Stanley, Tai Mo Shan, Tsuen Wan, Sai Kung, Yuen Long, Po Toi Islands, Ping Chau. Y. W. Lam 1155, 1143; HK sheet 38739.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indochina, Indian subcontinent, Malesia.
Ecology: Open fields and grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Sphaerocaryum malaccense (Trin.) Pilg. 稗藎
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 45: 2. 1938; FHN 4: 393, fig. 1201. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 172, pl. 54. 1990; FFJ 6: 183, fig. 151. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 446, pl. 184. 2000; FOC 22: 560. 2006; FGD 9: 372, fig. 181. 2009.
Panicum malaccense Trin., Gram. Panic. 204. 1826.
Isachne pulchella auct. non Roth.: FHK 414. 1861.
Sphaerocaryum elegans Nees ex Steud., Nomencl. Bot. (ed. 2) 2: 620. 1841; FKH 317. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms very slender, prostrate, 10–30 cm, rooting at lower nodes, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, ciliate along margins; leaf blades ovate-cordate, amplexicaul, 1–1.5 × 0.6–1 cm, ± hispidulous, margins ciliate-serrulate; ligule ca. 1 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle shortly exserted from uppermost sheath, ovate, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, with many spikelets on 1–3 mm capillary glandular pedicels. Spikelets 1-flowered, ca. 1 mm; glumes hyaline, glabrous, the lower 2/3 spikelet length, veinless; the upper equal to spikelet or slightly shorter, 11-veined; lemma as long as spikelet, pubescent; palea similar to lemma; anthers 3, yellow. Caryopsis brownish at maturity.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3016; D. P. M. Guile 729; HK sheet 30747.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread over India, SE Asia and southward to Malay Peninsula and Indonesia
Ecology: Watersides and other damp places. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

Sphenoclea zeylanica Gaertn. 尖瓣花
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 113, pl. 24, fig. 5. 1788; FKH 153. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 176. 1983; FGD 3: 326, fig. 213. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 801, pl. 372, photo 403. 1998.

Annual herbs, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, 20–70 cm tall, usually many‑branched. Leaves alternate; petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blades oblong to oblong‑lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 2–9 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, entire, adaxially green, abaxially greyish green; lateral veins slender, inconspicuous. Spikes densely flowered, 1–4 cm, 5–8 mm in diam., terminal or leaf‑opposite. Flowers small, sessile; calyx green, lobes 5, ovate; corolla white, campanulate, with 5 spreading lobes; stamens 5, attached to the lower part of the corolla‑tube, alternate with the corolla‑lobes; ovary inferior, bilocular, with numerous ovules in each locule. Capsule depressed globose, 2– 4 mm in diam., circumscissile, with numerous seeds.

Locality: Tuen Mun, Kuk Po, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3272; F. W. Xing 7843; HK sheet 39068.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical regions.
Ecology: Margins of paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

Spilanthes grandiflora Turcz. 大花金鈕扣
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 24: 185. 1851.
Acmella grandflora (Turcz.) R. K. Jansen, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 8: 75. 1985.

Perennial herbs, 20–70 cm tall; stems erect to ascending or rarely decumbent, glabrous to moderately pilose. Petioles 2–12.5 mm, glabrous to moderately pilose; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate or lanceolate, rarely ovate, 2.5– 8 × 0.3–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acute to acuminate or rounded, usually glabrous to sparsely pilose adaxially, glabrous to usually sparsely or moderately pilose abaxially, margin entire to very coarsely and irregularly dentate, sparsely to moderately ciliate. Capitula radiate, solitary, or several arranged as loose panicles, ovoid in shape, 7.5–15.5 × 5.5–11.5 mm. Peduncles 4–37 cm, glabrous to moderately pilose. Receptacle cylindric‑conical, 4.5–11.5 mm high, 0.9–2.7 mm in diam., apex acuminate. Phyllaries triseriate, lanceolate to narrowly ovate, apex acute. Pales 4.1–6.8 × 0.5–1.2 mm, apex acute to acuminate, stramineous. Ray florets 11–12, greatly exceeding the phyllaries; corollas yellow, tube 1.3 – 2.0 mm, limb 4.1–10.3 × 1.1–3.3 mm; cypselae 1.5 – 2.5 mm. Disk corollas 2.5–3 mm; anthers usually black; cypselae 2 – 2.7 mm. Pappus usually of 3 subequal bristles, 0.7 – 1.1 mm, or pappus absent.

Locality: Kowloon Reservoirs, Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 2438, 3014.
Distribution: Widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.

Spilanthes paniculata Wall. ex DC. 金鈕扣
Prodr. 5: 625. 1836; FRPS 75: 359, pl. 61: 1 – 2. 1979; FGD 8: 126, fig. 63. 2007.
Acmella paniculata (Wall. ex DC.) R. K. Jansen, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 8: 67. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 814, pl. 376, photo 406. 1998.

Annual herbs; stems erect or ascending, rooting at nodes when lower portion of stem touched the ground, 20–60(–100) cm tall, branched, striate, subglabrous or sparsely puberulent, tinged purple. Petioles 0.3–2 cm, glabrous or loosely hairy; Leaves ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–7 × 0.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate and decurrent to the petiole, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate or undulate‑serrate, sometimes entire, both surfaces glabrous. Capitula solitary, or several arranged as loose panicles, ovoid in shape, 6–11 × 5–10 mm, with or without ligulate florets. Peduncles 1.5–6 cm, sparsely puberulent near the head. Involucre like a shallow dish, bearing one series of herbaceous phyllaries, subtending the ligulate florets if present, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 2.8–4 × 1.2–2 mm, apex acute to obtuse, glabrous but ciliate along margin. Receptacle cylindric‑conical, 5 – 7 mm high, longer than the phyllaries. Paleae scarious, cymbiform, enfolding the hypanthia of disk florets, 2.2–4.5 × 1–2 mm. Florets yellow or white, fertile. Ray florets 4–6, with ligule broadly obovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex 3 rounded lobes, tube 1 mm, pubescent. Tubular florets 1.3–2 mm, usually 4‑toothed at apex; anthers included, base obtuse, apical appendages broad‑ovate; stylar branches short, apex truncate, penicillate. Cypselae black, obovate‑oblong, 1.5–2.5 mm, the marginal ones 3‑angled, the disk ones bilaterally flattened, both with concave apices, several hair growing near the summit, densely ciliate along margin. Pappus absent or of 2 unequal awns.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 546, 1348; S. Y. Hu 8981 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Malaysia, S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides and wastelands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Spinacia oleracea L. 菠菜
Sp. Pl. 1027. 1753; FHN 1: 399. 1964; FGD 3: 68. 1995; FOC 5: 366. 2003.

Annual herb, up to 1 m tall; roots conical, often reddish. Stems erect, simple or branched. Leaves light green, tender and juicy, hastate or triangular-ovate, generally 5 –15 × 5 –10 cm, entire or dentately lobed. Male flowers arranged in interrupted spicate panicles; perianth-lobes 4. Female flowers in axillary clusters; bracteoles spinose abaxially; ovary globose; stigmas 4 or 5. Utricles brown, ovoid or subglobose 2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 6741, 6988 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in China; native to Iran.
Ecology: Farmland. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Vegetable.

Spinifex littoreus (Burm. f.) Merr. 鬣刺
Philipp. J. Sci. 7: 229. 1912; FHN 4: 444. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 391, pl. 119, 129: 18. 1990; FFJ 6: 188, fig. 157. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 518, pl. 218. 2000; FOC 22: 553. 2006; FGD 9: 450, fig. 233. 2009.
Stipa littorea Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 29. 1767.
Spinifex squarrosus L., Mant. Pl. 300. 1771; FHK 415. 1861; FKH 317. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms stoloniferous, hard, stout, many-noded, rooting and copiously branching at nodes, flowering shoots ascending to 30–100 cm or more. Leaf sheaths broad, glabrous or pubescent, imbricate, margins ciliate; leaf blades linear, 5–20 × 0.2–0.3 cm, very tough, involute-subulate, curved, glabrous, margins scabrous, apex spiny; ligule small, densely ciliate. Male inflorescence of 2–5 clustered; racemes 3–6 cm, bearing 5–10 loosely imbricate spikelets. Male spikelets lanceolate, 8–12 mm; glumes oblong-lanceolate, unequal, 7–9-veined; lower glume 1/2 spikelet length; upper glume 2/3 spikelet length; lower lemma 8–10 mm, 5-veined, palea as long as lemma, 2-veined. Female inflorescence globose; racemes with needle-like 10–18 cm rachis, with 1 spikelet at base. Female spikelets lanceolate-oblong, ca. 12 mm; glumes herbaceous; lower glume slightly shorter than spikelet, many-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5-veined, palea absent; upper lemma as long as palea, thickened papery, 5-veined.

Locality: Long Ke, Tai Long Sai Wan, Ham Tin, Tai Wan, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 76; Y. S. Lau 2585; HK sheet 34662.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Sandy beaches, seashore dunes. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Spiraea cantoniensis Lour. 麻葉繡線菊（麻葉繡球）
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 322. 1790; FHK 105. 1861; FKH 93. 1912; FRPS 36: 33. 1974; FFJ 2: 267. 1985; FGD 4: 169. 2000; FOC 9: 62. 2003.

Shrub, up to 1.5 m tall, branchlets terete, slender, arched, dark red-brown, glabrous. Petioles 4 – 7 mm, glabrous; leaf blade rhombic-elliptic or rhombic-oblong, 2 – 5 × 1.5 – 2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin irregularly incised-serrate above middle, glabrous on both surfaces, dark green abaxially, pale bluish-green and glaucous adaxially, lateral veins 3 – 5 on each side of midvein. Umbels terminal, pedunculate, many-flowered; rachis and peduncles glabrous or pubescent; pedicels slender, 8– 16 mm, glabrous; bracts linear to lanceolate, 2 – 3 mm, glabrous or pubescent; flowers 5 – 8 mm in diam.; hypanthium campanulate, shorter than 2 mm, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially; sepals triangular to ovate-triangular, 1 – 1.5 × 1.5 – 2 mm, erect in fruits; petals white, suborbicular or obovate, 2.5 – 4 × 3 – 4.5 mm, glabrous, apex emarginate or obtuse; stamens 20 – 30, shorter than to equaling to petals; disk annular, lobed, lobes unequal, suborbicular, apex emarginate; carpels 5, subglabrous; ovary glabrous, styles shorter than stamens. Follicles erect, glabrous; styles terminal, usually divergent.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2690; HK sheet 9135.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; Japan, also widely cultivated in the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Spiraea chinensis Maxim. 中華繡線菊
Trudy Imp. S.-Peterburgsk. Bot. Sada 6(1): 193. 1879; FRPS 36: 41. 1974; FFJ 2: 268. 1985; FGD 4: 169. 2000; FOC 9: 61. 2003.

Shrub, 1.5 – 3 m tall; branchlets arched, yellow tomentose initially, glabrescent. Petioles 4 – 10 mm, shortly tomentose; leaf blade rhombic-ovate or obovate, 2.5 – 6 × 1.5 – 3 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin deeply sharply incised serrate or inconspicuously 3-lobed, adaxially pubescent, abaxially yellow tomentose, lateral veins 4 – 6 on each side of midvein, deeply impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially. Umbels pedunculate, 16– 25-flowered; peduncles 5 – 10 mm, tomentose; flowers 3 – 4 mm in diam.; bracts linear, 2 – 5 mm, pubescent; hypanthium campanulate, puberulous abaxially, pubescent adaxially; sepals ovate-lanceolate, 2 –3 × 1 – 2 mm, erect or rarely reflexed in fruit, apex acuminate; petals white, suborbicular, 2 – 3 × 2 – 3 mm, apex emarginate or obtuse; stamens 20 – 25, shorter than to nearly equaling to petals; disk undulate annular or irregularly lobed; ovary villose; styles shorter than stamens. Follicles erect spreading, wholly pubescent; style terminal, erect or divergent.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak. P. S. Choi 434; S. C. Ng 2923; K. Y. Tam 103.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shaanxi, Nei Mongol.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Mar – Jun.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Spiraea prunifolia Siebold & Zucc. 李葉繡線菊
Fl. Jap. 1: 131, pl. 70. 1835; FRPS 36: 59. 1974; FOC 9: 70. 2003.

Shrub to 3 m tall; branchlets slender, slightly angled, pubescent initially, glabrescent. Petioles 2 – 4 mm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate to oblong-elliptic, 1.5 – 3 × 0.7 – 1.4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin minutely sharply serrate, pubescent on both surfaces initially, then glabrescent adaxially, pinnately-veined. Umbels sessile, 3 – 6-flowered, with few clustered small leaves at base; pedicels 6 –10 mm, pubescent; bracts leaflike, 4 – 7 × 3 – 5 mm, puberulous on both surfaces initially, glabrescent, apex indistinctly and minutely serrate; flowers double, 1–1.2 cm in diam.; hypanthium campanulate, shorter than sepals, pubescent; sepals triangular to ovate-triangular, 1.5–2 mm, shorter than petals, apex acute; petals white, broadly obovate to suborbicular, glabrous. Follicles spreading, glabrous, or pubescent along the adaxial suture.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 9189; G. Barretto s.n. (HK sheet 33346).
Distribution: Sichuan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, Hubei, Shaanxi; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. –May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Spiraea thunbergii Siebold ex Blume 珍珠繡線菊
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 17: 1115. 1826; FRPS 36: 60. 1974; FFJ 2: 269. 1985; FOC 9: 70. 2003.

Shrub, up to 1.5 m tall; branchlets terete, densely pubescent initially, glabrescent. Petioles 1 – 2 mm, pubescent; leaf blade linear-lanceolate, (1–)1.5–4 × (2–)3–7 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex long acuminate, margin sharply serrate above middle, glabrous on both surfaces except for puberulous veins abaxially when young, pinnately-veined. Umbels sessile, with clustered small leaves at base, 3–7-flowered; pedicels slender, 6–10 mm, glabrous; flowers 6–8 mm in diam.; hypanthium campanulate, pubescent adaxially, glabrous abaxially; sepals triangular to ovate-triangular, 1.5–2 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute, erect or reflexed in fruits; petals white, suborbicular to obovate, 2–4 × 2–3.5 mm, glabrous, base shortly clawed, apex emarginate or obtuse; stamens 18–20, to 1/3 as long as petals or shorter; disk annular, 10-lobed; ovary subglabrous; styles nearly equaling to stamens. Follicles spreading, glabrous; styles subterminal, divergent.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1750, 2667; HK sheet 9205.
Distribution: E China; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb. – May; fruiting: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Spiranthes hongkongensis S. Y. Hu & Barretto 香港綬草
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 2, fig. 2b–f. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 41, fig. 14(B–F). 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 105. 2002; FOC 25: 85. 2009.

Acaulescent terrestrial orchid 12–37 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all basal, oblanceolate, 4–12 × 0.5–0.9 cm, apex acute. Flowers white, many, spirally arranged in a hairy spike of 3–12 cm; sepals glandular hairy; odd sepal oblong, 4 mm, white, apex obtuse; lateral sepals white, tinged pink slightly; petals in close contact to odd sepal; lip straight, thickened at base, each side with a transparent gland; column 1 mm, triangular at apex; anther ovate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, powdery; rostellum narrow, membranous, truncate; stigma shield-like, trilobate along the upper margin. Ovary densely glandularly hairy.

Locality: Tsz Wan Shan, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. S. Y. Hu 10035, 13552 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 435.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Australia.
Ecology: Along little streams, paths between paddy, sunny grassy hillsides, newly available open habitats. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13658, K, holotype; A, CUHK, isotype) was collected from Tai Po in 1975. Further to Hu and Barretto's (1976) observations, Sun (1996a, Amer. J. Bot. 83: 252–260) discussed the allopolyploid origin of this self-fertile species, which is a tetraploid (chromosome number ≈60) with putative parents being S. sinensis and S. spiralis (L.) Chevall. Spiranthes sinensis is a pollinator-dependent outcrosser, whereas S. hongkongensis is a pollinator-independent selfer, flowering 2–3 weeks earlier than S. sinensis (Sun 1996b, Conservation Biol. 10: 785–795). Spiranthes sinensis is glabrous on floral parts and its flower colour is normally pink and occasionally white, in a prominent spiral spike, whereas S. hongkongensis has grandular hairs on its bracts, sepals and ovaries in the creamy white flowers, inconspicuously arranged on a spiral spike. Rare occurrence of natural hybrids have also been observed, featuring both pinkish flowers and glandular hairs on floral parts.

Spiranthes sinensis (Pers.) Ames 綬草
Orchidaceae 2: 53. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 41, fig. 14(G–K). 1977; FRPS 17: 228. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1034, pl. 442. 2000; FGD 7: 348, fig. 176. 2006; FOC 25: 85. 2009.
Neottia sinensis Pers., Syst. Pl. 2: 53. 1807.
Spiranthes australis Lindl., Bot. Reg. 10: sub. t. 823. 1824; FHK 360. 1861; FKH 267. 1912.

Terrestrial caespitose herb, glabrous throughout, requiring a resting period in winter. Leaves all basal, linear, 10–12 × 0.3–0.4 cm. Flowers pink, spirally arranged on a terminal spike; scape 15–20 cm; odd sepal dorsal, ovate-lanceolate, 3 mm; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 3 × 1 mm, 4 mm between apices; petals adhering to dorsal sepal; lip white, recurved; column short, arcuate; anther buried in the clinandrium; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; rostellum membranous, bifid; stigma discoid, green; ovary ovoid, 5 mm, glabrous. Capsule ellipsoidal.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 10070, 13655 (CUHK); HK sheet 36119.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E Asia, S to SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Sunny grassy hillsides. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.

Spirodela polyrhiza (L.) Schleid. 紫萍
Linnaea 13: 392. 1839; FRPS 13(2): 207, pl. 42: 1. 1979; FGD 4: 409, fig. 249: 1 – 3. 2000; FOC 23: 80. 2010.
Lemna polyrhiza L., Sp. Pl. 970. 1753; FKH 290. 1912.

Small free floating herb, often forming a complete green carpet on water. Fronds flat or rarely gibbous, obovate to circular, 3 – 8( – 10) × 4 – 6 mm, each with 5 – 21 roots, adaxial surface green, sometimes with indistinct papillae along veins, abaxial surface usually purplish, or sometimes green, palmately 5 – 11-veined. Daughter fronds connected to mother frond by thin white stipe. Flowers minute, male and female separate but within same spathe. Fruit laterally winged towards top.

Locality: New Territories. Y. W. Lam 1339, 1751.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and ditches.
Uses: Animal food, medicinal (folklore).

Sporobolus fertilis (Steud.) Clayton 鼠尾粟
Kew Bull. 19(2): 291. 1965; FRPS 10(1): 99, pl. 31: 6–10. 1990; FFJ 6: 178, fig. 146. 1995; FOC 22: 484. 2006; FGD 9: 360, fig. 173. 2009.
Agrostis fertilis Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 170. 1854.
Sporobolus indicus (L.) var. major (Buse) Baaijens, Blumea 35: 437. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 5: 435. 2000.
Sporobolus indicus auct. non R. Br.: FHK 426. 1861; FKH 325. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect, 25–100(–120) cm tall. Leaf blades linear, flat or involute, 15–50(–65) × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or thinly pilose on adaxial surface, tapering to a long filiform apex; ligule ca. 0.5 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous but margin ciliolate, basal sheaths papery, lightly keeled. Panicle linear, contracted to spike-like, 19–45 × 0.5–1.5 cm; branches 1–2.5(–5) cm, erect and appressed to main axis, or looser and narrowly ascending, densely spiculate throughout. Spikelets greyish or yellowish green, 1.7–2 mm; lower glume oblong, ca. 0.5 mm, veinless, apex truncate-erose; upper glume oblong-elliptic, 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, 1-veined, apex ± acute; lemma ovate, as long as spikelet, indistinctly 1(–3)-veined, acute. Anthers 3, 0.8–1 mm. Grain red-brown, obovate-elliptic, 0.9–1.2 mm, distinctly shorter than its lemma and palea, these gaping widely beyond its top, apex truncate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1047; K. L. Yip 4042, 4483.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands, grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Sporobolus virginicus (L.) Kunth 鹽地鼠尾粟
Rev. Gramin. 1: 67. 1829; FRPS 10(1): 99, pl. 31: 11–14. 1990; FFJ 6: 179. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 438. 2000; FOC 22: 483. 2006; FGD 9: 360. 2009.
Agrostis virginica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 63. 1753.

Perennial herb, with woody rhizomes. Culms erect or decumbent at base, 15–30(–60) cm tall, often fastigiately branched in upper part. Leaf blades leathery, glaucous, stiff, distichous, flat at first, soon inrolled and needle-like, 2–10 × 0.1–0.4 cm, abaxial surface smooth, adaxial surface scabrid, apex pungent; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, upper margin and abaxial surface ciliate; leaf sheaths tightly overlapping, loosely pubescent at mouth. Panicle linear, spike-like, 2–10 × 0.4–1 cm, branches 0.5–1.5 cm, erect, closely appressed to rachis. Spikelets grey-green or greenish yellow, fusiform, 2.3–2.7 mm, with 1 floret; glumes acute, papery; lower glume lanceolate, 2/3–4/5 spikelet length, 1-veined; upper glume narrowly ovate, as long as spikelet, 1-veined; lemma and palea the same texture with the glume; lemma ovate-lanceolate, 1-veined, boat-shaped, about 2 mm long; palea ovate, 2-keeled, truncate at the apex. Anthers 3, 1–1.5 mm. Grain subglobose 0.7–1 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 155; Y. W. Lam 1584; K. Y. Tam 144.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Coastal sands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control).

Stachys geobombycis C. Y. Wu 地蠶（野芝麻）
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 10: 222. 1965; FRPS 66: 21. 1977; FOC 17: 182. 1994; FGD 3: 427, fig. 268. 1995.
Stachys asper auct. non Michx.: FKH 211. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 40–50 cm tall. Rhizomes enlarged into succulent tubers at the end. Stems and branches retrorse hispid on angles and at nodes. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–4.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to oblong‑ovate, 4.5–8 × 2.5– 3 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, apex obtuse, margin coarsely crenate‑serrate, sparsely pilose‑hispid, densely so on veins of abaxial surface. Verticillasters 4–6‑flowered, forming terminal spikes to 5 cm or more. Calyx obconical, ca. 5.5 mm, densely puberulent, 10‑veined; teeth 5, ca. 1.5 mm, callous‑tipped. Corolla pale purple to bluish purple, or sometimes pink, ca. 1.1 cm; upper lip erect, oblong‑ovate, ca. 4 mm; lower lip spreading, ca. 5 mm, 3‑lobed. Stamens included. Style slightly exserted.

Locality: Hung Mui Kuk. L. T. Lo 463; HK sheet 32792.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Wet grasslands and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Food (rhizomes), medicinal (folklore).

Stachytarpheta jamaicensis (L.) Vahl 假馬鞭
Enum. Pl. 1: 206. 1804; FHN 4: 4, fig. 946. 1977; FYN 1: 397, pl. 95: 1 – 2. 1977; FTW 4: 431. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 20, fig. 6. 1982; FFJ 4: 522. 1989; FOC 17: 3. 1994; FGD 3: 345, fig. 226. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 424. 1998.
Verbena jamaicensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 19. 1753.

Perennial robust herb or subshrub, 0.6–2 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal when young, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous. Petiole winged, 1–3 cm; leaf blade thickly papery, elliptic to oblong‑ovate, 2.4–8 × 2–4.5 cm, base elongate, apex acuminate, margin coarsely serrate, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous; lateral veins 3–6 pairs, prominent abaxially. Spikes 10–30 cm. Bracts ca. 5 mm, margin membranous, ciliate. Calyx tubular, membranous, transparent, ca. 6 mm, glabrous. Corolla dark blue; tube 0.7–1.2 cm, slightly curved. Ovary glabrous.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1980, 2205; L. T. Lo 568.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan (naturalized); native to tropical America, widely naturalized in tropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Shaded grassy places in valleys. Flowering: Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Stauntonia elliptica Hemsl. 牛藤果
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2844. 1907; FGD 4: 50. 2000; FRPS 29: 28. 2001; FOC 6: 448. 2001.
Parvatia brunoniana (Wall.) Decaisne subsp. elliptica (Hemsl.) H. N. Qin, Cathaya 8–9: 61, fig. 36. 1997.

Woody twining shrub, glabrous throughout. Leaves trifoliate; petioles 10 –17 cm; leaflets elliptic, oblong to ovate-oblong or obovate, 3 –11 × 2–5 cm, base rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire and slightly revolute, dark green adaxially, pale green abaxially; lateral nerves and veins raised on abaxial surface; petiolules 1–3 cm. Racemes several and fascicled in axils of leaves, with many pendent pale green to whitish flowers. Male flowers: pedicels 10 –12 mm; outer sepals ovate-elliptic, inner sepals lanceolate, 6–9 × 2–3 mm; nectariform petals ovate, 1–1.5 mm; stamens ca. 5 mm, connective apical appendages as long as anther. Female flowers: pedicels 18 –20 mm; sepals narrowly to linear lanceolate, 14 –15 × 2– 4 mm; staminodes ca. 1 mm; carpels 3, free, oblong, with elongated and pointed stigmas. Fruit ovoid or oblong, 4 –5 × 2– 4 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7226.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The species was erroneously reported as Akebia trifoliate var. australis (Diels) Rehd. (Check List HK Plants 53. 2002).

Stauntonia chinensis DC. 野木瓜
Syst. Nat. 1: 514. 1818; FHK 13. 1861; FKH 32. 1912; H. N. Qin, Cathaya 8–9: 151, fig. 67. 1997; FGD 4: 51, fig. 32. 2000; FRPS 29: 29, pl. 5: 1–7. 2001; FOC 6: 449. 2001.
Stauntonia hexaphylla auct. non Decaisne: FKH 32. 1912.

Woody twining shrub, glabrous throughout. Leaves digitate; petioles 5–10 cm; leaflets 5–7, leathery, oblong, elliptic or oblonglanceolate, 6–9(–11.5) × 2–4 cm, base obtuse, rounded or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire and ± thickened, adaxially dark green, abaxially paler and often maculate when young; reticulation of veins conspicuously raised on both surfaces; petiolules 6- 25 mm. Flowers usually 3–4 in corymbose-racemes; pedicels 2–3 cm. Male flowers: sepals 6, yellowish or cream white abaxially, purplish red adaxially, outer 3 lanceolate, ca. 18 × 6 mm, inner 3 linear lanceolate, ca. 16 × 3 mm; nectariform petals liguliform, ca. 1.5 mm; connective apical appendage as long as anther. Female flowers: sepals slightly larger than that of staminate flower; staminodes aciculiform, less than 1 mm; carpels 3, free, narrowly ellipsoid or oblong, with oblique capitate stigmas. Fruit oblong, 7–10 × 3 –5 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1745; HK sheet 1179, 39261.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests of hill slopes. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

Stauntonia decora (Dunn) C. Y. Wu ex S. H. Huang 翅野木瓜
FYN 2: 8. 1979; FGD 4: 50. 2000; FRPS 29: 26. 2001; FOC 6: 448. 2001.
Parvatia decora Dunn, Hooker's Icon. Pl. ser. 4, 8(1): t. 2712. 1901.

Stems, petioles and petiolules narrowly winged. Leaves trifoliate; petioles 3– 8 cm; leaflets leathery, elliptic, ovate, or oblong, 5–12 × 3 –7 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, sometimes subrounded and mucronate, margin entire and slightly revolute, glabrous and shining adaxially, scurfy puberulous abaxially; lateral nerves and veins raised on abaxial surface; petiolules of terminal leaflets 2.5 –4 cm, lateral ones 1–1.5 cm. Racemes several to many, 1–2-flowered, fascicled in axils of leaves; peduncles 4–10 mm. Male flowers: pedicels 2.5–4 mm; outer sepals lanceolate, 20–25 × 5–6 mm, inner ones narrower, ca. 21 mm; petals lanceolate, ca. 2 mm; stamens 7–14 mm, connective apical appendage hornlike, equaling or longer than anther; pistillodes subulate. Female flowers similar to staminate flower; carpels 3, clavate, 6 –7 mm; stigmas lanceolate, reflexed. Fruit ellipsoid, 7– 8 × 2.5 –3.5 cm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 1175, 1928.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Open forests in ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.

Stauntonia obovata Hemsl. 倒卵葉野木瓜
Hooker's Icon. Pl. ser. 4, 9: t. 2847, 1907; FKH 32. 1912; H. N. Qin, Cathaya 8–9: 130, fig. 56. 1997; FGD 4: 53. 2000; FRPS 29: 42, pl. 9: 10 –14. 2001; FOC 6: 452. 2001.
Holboellia obovata (Hemsl.) Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 233. 1934.

Woody twining shrub, glabrous throughout. Leaves digitate; petioles slender, 2–6(–8) cm; leaflets 35(–6), leathery, very variable in size and shape, usually obovate, sometimes oblong or lanceolate, 3.5–6(–11) × 1.5–3(–6) cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex rounded, occasionally acute or acuminate, margin entire and ± revolute, adaxially dark green, abaxially glaucous; lateral veins 5 – 6 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins obscure; petiolules 8–20 mm. Racemes 4–6 cm, 3–5 fascicled in axils of leaves. Pedicels 2– 4 cm. Male flowers: sepals 6, white, rarely yellowish white, outer 3 lanceolate, 10–11 × 3.5–4 mm, inner 3 linear, 6–10 × 1–1.5 mm; petals lacking; stamens ca. 3.5 mm, connectives slightly produced; vestigial carpels 3, very small. Female flowers: sepals as in staminate flower; carpels 3, free, stigmas capitate; staminodes squamiform, less than 0.5 mm. Fruit ellipsoid or ovoid, (3–)4–5(–6) × 2–2.5 cm.

Locality: Mount Victoria, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan. K. L. Yip 4139; Y. S. Lau 518, 2831.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangxu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan
Ecology: Margins of forests in ravines, by streams. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Staurogyne concinnula (Hance) Kuntze 糙葉叉柱花
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 497. 1897; FTW ed. 2, 4: 686. 1998; FRPS 70: 38. 2002.
Ebermaiera coninnula Hance, J. Bot. 1868: 200. 1868; FKH 197. 1912.

Perennial dwarf herbs, ca. 15 cm tall; stem generally short, partially underground, 0.5–6 cm long, usually simple, rarely few‑branched, terete, densely short pubescent. Leaves rosulate at the base of stem; petioles 0.3–3 cm, pubescent; leaf blades oblanceolate, 1.5–7 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base gradually attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, margin obscurely undulate, adaxially green, scarious, sometimes pubescent along the veins, abaxially glaucous, pubescent along the veins, lateral veins 5–8 pairs, prominent abaxially. Spikes 1–4, axillary, sometimes loosely branched, forming a panicle of 5–15 cm; branches slender, with 3–10 interrupted flowers. Pedicels 1–4 mm, pubescent. Bracts linear to linear‑oblanceolate, 2–4 mm, apex obtuse or subacute; bracteoles 2, at the middle of pedicel, linear, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Calyx campanulate, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear or linear‑lanceolate, unequal, 5–6 mm, apex acute, accrescent to 7 mm in fruit, glabrous except for minutely pilose on the margin. Corolla ca. 1 cm, white, tubular‑funnelform; tube ampliate, ca. 6 × 4 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes subequal, orbicular, ca. 3 mm. Stamens 4, included, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, shorter pair ca. 2.5 mm; anthers ellipsoidal, ca. 1.5 mm, thecae equal. Ovary ellipsoidal, glabrous; style filiform, ca. 5 mm; stigma subulate. Capsule oblong, 4–5 × 1.5 mm, glabrous, shorter than persistent calyx, many‑seeded. Seeds suborbicular, ca. 0.2 mm.

Locality: Hok Tau. HK sheet 35393, F. W. Xing 10190 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Streamsides, forests. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Apr.

Stellaria alsine Grimm 雀舌草
Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 3. (app.): 313. 1767; FOC 6: 21. 2001.
Stellaria uliginosa Murr., Prodr. Stirp. Gott. 55. 1770; FHK B22. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FGD 2: 78, fig. 54. 1991; FRPS 26: 129, pl. 30: 1– 5. 1996.

Annual or biennial herb, 15 –25(–35) cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems tufted, ascending, much branched. Leaves sessile, lanceolate to oblong lanceolate, 5 –20 × 2– 4 mm, base cuneate and semi-amplexicaul, apex acuminate, margin cartilaginous, ± glaucous on both surfaces. Flowers in terminal 2–3- flowered cymes, rarely solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels slender, 5–20 mm, turned down in fruiting time. Sepals 5, lanceolate 2–4 × 1 mm, margin scarious. Petals 5, white, shorter than or equaling to sepals, deeply 2-lobed to near base; lobes linear. Stamens 5(–10), slightly shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; styles 3, or sometime 2. Capsule ovoid, opening at top into 6 teeth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Sha Tin. L. T. Lo 287; S. P. Lam 107; Y. W. Lam 1345.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Nei Mongol, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; N Africa, Europe, temperate Asia.
Ecology: Rice fields, moist places by streams. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Stellaria media (L.) Vill. 繁縷（魚腸草）
Hist. Pl. Dauphine 3: 615. 1789; FHK 21. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FHN 1: 376. 1964; FGD 2: 79. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 376, pl. 176. 1996; FRPS 26: 104. 1996; FOC 6: 15. 2001.
Alsine media L., Sp. Pl. 272. 1753.

Annual or biennial herb, 10 –30 cm tall. Stems decumbent or ascending, much branched, with a line of hairs down one side. Leaves opposite, lower ones long petioled; upper ones usually sessile; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate, 1.5 –2.5 × 1–1.5 cm, base abruptly narrowed or sub-cordate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire. Flowers in terminal 2–3-flowered cymes. Pedicels slender, with a line of hairs, lengthening and turning down in fruiting time, 7–14 mm. Sepals 5, lanceolate ca. 4 mm, apex obtuse or sub-rounded, margin scarious, with short glandular hairs abaxially. Petals 5, white, oblong, shorter than sepals, deeply 2-lobed to near base; lobes linear. Stamens 3 – 5, slightly shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; styles 3. Capsule ovoid, slightly longer than persistent sepals, opening at top into 6 teeth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 40607.
Distribution: Dispersed over all China except Xinjiang and Heilongjiang. Widely spread in temperate regions.
Ecology: Waste places, roadsides, cultivated fields. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (vegetable).

Stemona tuberosa Lour. 大百部（百部）
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 404. 1790; FKH 276. 1912; FHN 4: 147, fig. 1053. 1977; FTW 5: 85, pl. 1287. 1978; FRPS 13(3): 256, pl. 62: 4–6. 1997; FOC 24: 71. 2000; FGD 9: 208. 2009.
Stemona acuta C. H. Wright, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 32: 493. 1889; FKH 276. 1912.

Perennial twining herb, thoroughly glabrous. Tubers terete or fusiform, 15–30 cm. Stems often branched, base woody. Leaves opposite, rarely whorled or alternate; petiole slender, 3.5–7.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 10–15 × 5–10 cm, membranous, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin slightly undulate, basal veins 7–13. Inflorescence racemose, 1–3-flowered; peduncle or pedicel axillary or rarely borne on petiole, 0.5–1.5 cm; bracts lanceolate, 0.5–1 cm. Perianth segments greenish with purplish veins, lanceolate, 4–6 × 1.5 cm. Stamens purple, slightly shorter than perianth; filaments stout, 2–5 mm; anthers linear, ca. 1 cm; appendages partially adherent. Capsule ovoid-ellipsoidal, 4–5 cm. Seeds several, ellipsoidal, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Plover Cove. Y. W. Lam 1759; HK sheet 7548.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Bangladesh, Cambodia, NE India, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets, mountain slopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Stenotaphrum helferi Munro ex Hook. f. 鈍葉草
Fl. Brit. India. 7(21): 91. 1896 [“1897”]; FRPS 10(1): 385, pl. 117. 1990; FFJ 6: 190. 1995; FOC 22: 538. 2006; FGD 9: 449, fig. 231. 2009.
Stenotaphrum americanum Schrank, Pl. Rar. Hort. Monac. 2(10): t. 98. 1819[1822]; FKH 317. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms creeping and rooting at base, flowering shoots 10–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, usually longer than internode, compressed, keeled, glabrous; leaf blades broadly linear, 5–17 × 0.5–1.1 cm, glabrous, base truncate or subrounded, apex slightly obtuse or mucronate, margins scabrous; ligule ca. 0.3 mm, apex with white short ciliate. Inflorescence 10–15 cm; axis flattened and winged, 3–5 mm wide, margins scabrous; racemes 7–18 mm, appressed within the curves of the midrib; raceme rachis triquetrous, margins scabrous, tipped with a mucro arising from the terminal spikelet. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 4–4.5 mm; lower glume broadly ovate, 1/2–2/3 the length of spikelet, (3–)5–7-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 9–11-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined, palea well developed, slightly shorter than lemma; upper lemma coriaceous, smooth, cuspidate-mucronate, margins inrolled embraced palea.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay. P. P. H. But 248; HK sheet 8357, 42035.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Open forests, moist grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

Stenotaphrum secundatum (Walter) Kuntze 側鈍葉草
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 794. 1891; FOC 22: 538. 2006.
Ischaemum secundatum Walter, Fl. Carol. 249. 1788.

Perennial stoloniferous herb. Culms much branched, forming a dense turf; flowering shoots 10–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths strongly keeled, often grouped in flabellate clusters; leaf blades broadly linear, folded when young, up to 15 × 0.4–1 cm, apex obtuse; ligule ca. 0.5 mm. Inflorescence 5–12 cm, slender, cylindrical; axis corky, disarticulating into segments at maturity; racemes 4–10 mm, reduced to 1–3 spikelets embedded in one face of the rachis, alternating on either side of the sinuous midrib; raceme rachis a stout pointed appendage within the axis cavity. Spikelets lanceolate, 4–5 mm, acute; lower glume up to 1/4 as long as spikelet; upper glume as long as spikelet; lower floret staminate, lemma cartilaginous, 3-veined, palea well developed; upper lemma papery, subequal to spikelet, smooth, acute.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Lung, Tai Mo Shan, Nim Shue Wan. S. L. Thrower 1190; S. Y. Hu 9929 (CUHK).
Distribution: Maxico, USA, S America; widely naturalized, exact native range obscure.
Ecology: Cultivated as lawn grass in Hong Kong. Flowering & fruiting: Summer.
Notes: The species was reported as Stenotaphrum dimidiatum (L.) Brongn. previously (Check List HK Plants 349. 2002; 122. 2004).

Stephania longa Lour. 糞箕篤
Fl. Cochinch. 608. 1790; FHN 1: 322, fig. 160. 1964; FGD 1: 42. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 51, pl. 10: 7–9. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 602. 1996.
Stephania japonica (Thunb.) Miers var. hispidula Yamam., Icon. Pl. Formosan., Suppl. 3: 33, fig. 11. 1927.
Stephania hernandifolia auct. non Walp: FHK 13. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.

Herbaceous vine, 1–4 m or longer, without tuberous roots, glabrous except inflorescence. Leaves usually more or less peltate, papery; petioles 1–4.5 cm, often twisted at the base; leaf blade broadly ovare, orbicular or nearly triangular, 3–9 × 2–6 cm, base subtruncate or subrounded, rarely slightly concave, apex obtuse, mucronate, sometimes glaucous on abaxial surface, palmately 10–11-nerved. Inflorescences an axillary umbel with 5 or 6 rays, each ray terminated by a head, or partial umbel of 8 to 12 small sessile or shortly pedicellate flowers; peduncles 1–4 cm. Male flowers: sepals 6–8, cuneate or obovate, ca. 1 mm; petals 4 or sometimes 3, greenish yellow, suborbicular, ca. 0.4 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals 4, rarely 3, ca. 0.6 mm; ovary glabrous, stigma lobes divaricate. Drupes red, 5–6 mm; kernel obovate, dorsally with 2 rows transverse tuberculous ridges.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan, Sheung Shui, Tai Mong Tsai. L. T. Lo 79; Y. S. Lau 296, 2837; HK sheet 35909.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests and in thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Stephania tetrandra S. Moore 粉防己
J. Bot. 13: 225. 1875; FGD 1: 42, fig. 43. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 52, pl. 11: 7–9. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 605, pl. 292. 1996.

Herbaceous vine, 1–3 m or longer, with fleshy, cylindrical taproot. Leaves peltate; petioles 3–7 cm; leaf blade papery, broadly triangular to triangular orbicular, usually 4–7 × 5–8.5 cm, base slightly cordate or truncate, apex acute and apiculate, appressed pubescent at least on abaxial surface, palmately 9- or 10-nerved, reticulation of veins conspicuous. Flowers in racemose discoid heads. Male flowers: sepals 4 or sometimes 5, usually obovate-elliptic, 0.8 mm including the claw; petals 5, fleshy, 0.6 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males. Drupes subglobose, red when mature; the kernel ca. 5.5 mm in diam. Dorsally cristate, with ca. 15 transverse ribs on each side.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Ko Lau Wan. HK sheet 34042, 35806.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct. Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sterculia lanceolata Cav. 假蘋婆
Diss. 5: 287, pl. 143, fig. 1. 1788; FHK 36. 1861; FKH 49. 1912; FHN 2: 73. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 132. 1984; FGD 1: 129. 1987.

Tree. Petioles 2.5–3.5 cm; leaves leathery, elliptic, lanceolate or elliptic-oblong, 9–20 × 3.5–8 cm, base obtuse or subrounded, apex acute, margin entire; lateral veins 7–9 pairs, curved, connected near margin. Panicles much branched, axillary, more or less tomentose; calyx 5-parted nearly to base, segments stellately spreading, green and slightly reddish at base, oblong-lanceolate, 4–6 mm, margin ciliate, abaxially pubescent; staminal column shorter than sepals; anthers 10, nearly sessile on outside of the very short lobes, forming a terminal globose head. Follicles bright scarlet, long-ovate or oblong, 5 –7 × 2–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex rostrate, densely pubescent. Seeds black-brown, ellipsoid-ovoid, 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1363; H. C. Tang 460, 845.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan; Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Laos.
Ecology: Lowland secondary forests and valleys. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Fibre, medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Sterculia nobilis Smith 蘋婆
Cycl. no. 4. 1816; FKH 49. 1912; FHN 2: 73. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 121. 1984; FGD 1: 127. 1987.

Tree, bark brown-black. Petioles 2–3.5 cm; leaves thinly leathery, oblong or elliptic, 8–25 × 4 –15 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces. Panicles terminal or axillary. Male flowers: calyx initially milk-white, becoming reddish, campanulate, ca. 10 mm, pubescent abaxially, 5-fid, lobes linear-lanceolate, as long as calyx tube, incurved and sticking together at apex; staminal column curved; anther yellow. Female flowers: slightly larger than male; ovary globose, 5-grooved. Follicles scarlet, thickly leathery, ellipsoid-ovoid, 5 × 2–3 cm, apex rostrate. Seeds 1–4 per follicle, black-brown, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Tsuen Wan, Shatin. Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2723; HK sheet 3603.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Food, ornamental.

Stewartia villosa Merr. 柔毛紫莖
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 315. 1931.
Hartia villosa (Merr.) Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 55. 1938; FGD 2: 153. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 235. 1998.

Evergreen tree, to 8 m tall; branchlets and petioles villose or appressed pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2 cm, narrowly winged; leaf blade oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 8 –13 × 3 – 5 cm, base rounded to obtuse, apex acuminate to acute, margin sparsely serrate, villose or pubescent on both surfaces, glabrescent in age, lateral veins 10 –16 on each side of midvein. Flowers solitary, white; pedicels 6 – 8 mm, villose; bracteoles lanceolate, 0.8 –1.5 cm, villose; sepals ovate-lanceolate, unequal, 1.5 –1.8 × 0.5 –0.8 cm, villose abaxially, apex acute; petals yellowish white, obovate, ca. 1.8 × 1.2 cm; stamens ca. 1 cm, filaments connate at the base; ovary tomentose, style short. Capsule conical, ca. 1.8 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ngong Ping. H. C. Tang 2440; Y. S. Lau 421; S. T. Dunn s.n. (HK sheet 3263).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Materials (timber).

Strelitzia nicolai Regel & Koern. 大鶴望蘭
Gartenflora 7: 265, pl. 235. 1858; FRPS 16(2): 18, pl. 5. 1981; FGD 2: 397. 1991.

Trunk up to 8 m, woody. Leaves in 2 ranks crowded toward apex of the trunk; leaf blade oblong, 90–120 × 45–60 cm, base subrounded, asymmetric, apex broadly obtuse; petiole to 1.8 m, sheathed at base. Inflorescences axillary; peduncle shorter than petiole, distally bearing 2 large spathe-bracts; spathe-bracts rigid, 25 – 32 cm, boat-shaped, ca. 6 cm across at the conduplicate base, green and tinged with purple. Flowers 4–9 in a helicoids cyme (cincinnus), with the lower part (ovary) enveloped in the spathe-bracts; sepals white, lanceolate, 13–17 × 1.5–3 cm, the anterior one narrower and keeled dorsally; petals 3, the middle one small, elliptic, 1.6 × 1.1 cm, apex mucronate, translucent, the lateral 2 connivent and forming an arrow-shaped organ, 10–12 cm, auricled on either side, dull blue; stamens concealed in the groove of the 2 connivent petals and slightly shorter than it, anthers linear, longer than the filaments; style rigid; stigma clavate, 3-branched.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 28106, 28107.
Distribution: Native to S Africa, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Strelitzia reginae Aiton 鶴望蘭
Hort. Kew 1: 285. 1789; FRPS 16(2): 16. 1981; FGD 2: 397, fig. 273. 1991.

Perennial herb, 1–1.5 m tall, trunkless. Leaves distichous, blade oblong-lanceolate, 25–45 × 10 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute, margin entire or ± undulate; petiole equaling or longer than the blade. Peduncle rising from axils of leaves, nearly or quite as long as petiole, usually bearing 1 spathe-bract; spathe-bracts boat-shaped, to 20 cm, green with purple margins. Flowers several in a helicoids cyme, subtended and partly enveloped by the spathe-bracts; sepals lanceolate, orange, 7.5–10 cm; petals 3, the middle one small, the lateral 2 connivent and forming an arrow-shaped organ, auricled on either side, dark blue; stamens as long as petals, anthers linear; style exserted; stigma 3-branched.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 28108.
Distribution: Native to S Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Winter.
Uses: Ornamental.

Striga asiatica (L.) Kuntze 獨腳金
Rev. Gen. Pl. 466. 1891; FOC 18: 88. 1998; FGD 4: 393, fig. 238. 2000.
Buchnera asiatica L., Sp. Pl. 2: 630. 1753.
Striga asiatica var. humilis (Benth.) D. Y. Hong, FRPS 67(2): 359, 405. 1979.
Striga hirsuta Benth., Prodr. 10: 502 – 503. 1846; FHK 254. 1861.
Striga hirsuta var. humilis Benth., Prodr. 10: 503. 1846.
Striga lutea Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 22. 1790; FKH 190. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 627.

Annual herbs, 10–20(–30) cm tall, hirsute throughout. Stems erect, simple, rarely branched. Leaf blade linear to narrowly lanceolate, 5–20 × 1–4 mm, sometimes reduced to scales. Flowers axillary, solitary or in a spike upward. Calyx 4–8 mm, 10‑ribbed; lobes 5, ± as long as the tube, subulate. Corolla usually yellow, rarely red or white; tube 0.8–1.5 cm, apically strongly curved; upper lip 2‑lobed. Capsules ovoid, enveloped in persistent calyx.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap, Ma On Shan, Tai Mei Tuk, Sai Kung (Sai Wan), Lamma Island, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 329, 1640; P. S. Choi 454.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Striga masuria (Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth.) Benth. 大獨腳金
Compan. Bot. Mag. 1: 364. 1836; FHK 254. 1861; FKH 190. 1912; FOC 18: 88. 1998; FGD 4: 394. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 4: 627.
Buchnera masuria Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth., Scroph. Ind. 41. 1835.

Perennial herbs, 30–60 cm tall, entirely hispid. Stems erect, ± quadrangular, simple or weakly branched. Leaf blade linear, 2–3 cm, longest at middle of stem. Flowers solitary, rarely in a spike. Calyx ca. 1 cm at anthesis, to 1.5 cm in fruit, 15‑ribbed; lobes ca. 2 times as long as tube, linear‑elliptic. Corolla pink, white, or yellow; tube to 1.2 cm, apically curved forward; upper lip ca. 1/2 as long as lower lip, apex notched. Capsules ovoid, ca. 6 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay. H. F. Hance s.n.; W. A. Harland s.n. (fide FHK 254. 1861).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar to Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy slopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn.

Strobilanthes apricus (Hance) T. Anderson ex Benth. 山一籠雞
FHK 262. 1861; FKH 198. 1912.
Gutzlaffia aprica Hance, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 142. 1849; FRPS 70: 101. 2002; Fl. Guizhou. 10: 231. 2004; FYN 16: 675. 2006.
Phlebophyllum apricum (Hance) Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 131. 1853.

Isophyllous perennial herbs or shrubs, to 70 cm tall. Stem quadrangular, sulcate, retrorsely white hirsute. Petiole 0.5–1 cm, slightly white pubescent or subglabrous; leaf blades leathery, elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, 2–7 × 1–3 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, ciliate, adaxially scabrous, hispid, especially on veins, abaxially yellowish silky tomentose, or glabrous except for the pubescent midvein, lateral veins 5 – 7 pairs. Spikes capitate, terminal or axillary; upper ones sessile or the lower ones with peduncle to 7 cm. Bracts subleathery, ovate‑lanceolate, 1.3–1.5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, apex acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially and margin covered with white multicellular hairs; bracteoles linear, 1–1.1 × 0.1 cm, abaxially and margin sparsely covered with large‑celled hairs, adaxially glabrous, both surfaces covered white cystoliths. Calyx 1–1.3 cm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear, with large‑celled multicellular hairs on margin, abaxially pubescent or subglabrous, adaxially glabrous. Corolla purple or white, ca 3.5 cm, outside glabrous, inside glabrous except for pilose retaining styles, basal cylindric tube ca. 1.3–1.5 cm, abruptly inflated to ca. 1 cm in diam. and cystiform; limb 5‑lobed, lobes subequal, suborbicular, ca. 5 × 5 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 1 cm; anthers elliptic, ca. 2.5 mm. Ovary narrowly oblong, white, pilose at the tip, 2 ovules per locule; style ca. 3.5 cm, curved, pilose. Capsule oblong, ca. 1 cm, glabrous except for few hairs at tip, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 mm, convex on both surfaces, pubescent, soon glabrescent, areola large.

Locality: Tai Tam, Lan Nai Wan, Wong Nai Chung, Pok Fu Lam. H. C. Tang 1400; Y. S. Lau 255, 1464; F. W. Xing 8615, 9748 (IBSC).
Ecology: Dry forests, thickets on slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Mar.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi; Vietnam, Thailand.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance from Tai Tam, Hong Kong Island in 1840s.

Strobilanthes cusia (Nees) Kuntze 馬藍
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 499. 1891; FTW ed. 2, 4: 678. 1998.
Goldfussia cusia Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 38. 1832.
Dipteracanthus calycinus Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 133. 1853, non Strobilanthes calycina Nees, 1836.
Strobilanthes championi T. Anderson ex Benth., FHK 261. 1861. Based on Dipteracanthus calycinus Champ.
Strobilanthes flaccidifolius Nees, Prodr. 11: 194, 1847; FKH 198. 1912;
Baphicacanthus cusia (Nees) Bremekamp., Verh. Ned. Akad. Wetensch. Afd. Naturk. Sect. 2, 41(1): 59, 190. 1944; FHN 3: 549. 1974; FRPS 70: 113. 2002.

Isophyllous herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stem erect, branched, glabrous or minutely brown puberulent. Petioles 0.5–3 cm; leaf blades papery, elliptic to ovate, 4–20 × 2–9 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin serrate, glabrous or abaxially minutely puberulent along veins, adaxially dark green, abaxially paler, black when dry; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Spike 10–30 cm, usually branched and forming a leafy terminal panicle. Bracts leaf‑like, oblanceolate or spathulate, 1.2–2.5 cm, petiolate, deciduous with flower; bracteole linear‑oblanceolate, 2–3 mm, deciduous before bracts. Calyx 0.8–1.5 mm in flower, accrescent to 2.5 cm in fruit, minutely puberulent, 5‑lobed almost to the base, 4 lobes linear, acute, one spathulate and much longer. Corolla blue, glabrous, 3.5–4. cm, straight, base cylindric, 1–1.5 cm, gradually widened to ca. 1.5 cm at mouth, lobes subequal, oblong, ca. 6 × 6 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous, included, filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 7 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anther oblong, ca. 3 mm; staminode absent.
