Ovary oblong, with 2 ovules per locule, apex puberulent with few glandular‑tipped hairs; styles ca. 3.2 cm, glabrous. Capsule 1.5–2.2 cm, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, 3.5 mm, covered with hairs; areola small, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Sai Kung, Shing Mun, Fo Tan, Ma On Shan, Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen, Ng Tung Chai, Kop Tong. Y. S. Lau 1337; HK sheet 35337, 39052.
Distribution: S, SW & E China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests and wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), dye.
Notes: The holotype specimen (Champion s.n., K) of Dipteracanthus calycinus was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker, Hong Kong between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), dye.
Notes: The holotype specimen (Champion s.n., K) of Dipteracanthus calycinus was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker, Hong Kong between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Strobilanthes dalzielii (W. W. Sm.) Benoist 曲枝馬藍
Notul. Syst. (Paris) 5: 109. 1935; Fl. Indo-Chine 4: 679. 1935.
Acanthopale dalzielii W. W. Sm., Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 11: 193. 1919.
Championella dalziellii (W. W. Sm.) Bremek., Verh. Ned. Aked. Werensch. Afd. Natuurk. II 41(1): 150. 1944.
Pteroptychia dalziellii (W. W. Sm.) H. S. Lo, FHN 3: 547, 592. 1974; FRPS 70: 194. 2002; FYN 16: 733. 2006.

Anisophyllous perennial herbs or shrubs, 0.4–1 m tall. Stems erect, slender, zigzag, branched, slightly pubescent or subglabrous. Leaves unequal in each pair, the smaller 1/3 to 1/2 of the larger in size; petiole very short, ca. 3 mm, or sessile; leaf blades ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, the larger 9–14 × 3–5 cm, the smaller 2–5 × 1–2 cm, membranous, base rounded, or cordate for upper leaves, apex acuminate or acute, sometimes falculate, margin serrate, adaxially green, glabrous, cystoliths prominent, abaxially glaucous, glabrous or sparsely pubescent along the veins, lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Spike terminal and axillary, 2–5 cm, 2–5‑flowered. Rachis usually zigzag, sparsely white puberulent, flowers distant, usually only one flower in each pair. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm, 1‑veined, glabrous; bracteoles linear, ca. 5 × 1 mm, glabrous or puberulent with glandular‑tipped hairs. Calyx ca. 1 cm, densely white pilose at base and along the midvein, 5‑lobed almost to the base, lobes linear. Corolla purplish blue or white, 3.5–4.5 cm, curved, outside densely white pilose in bud, inside glabrous except for hairs retaining the style, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm, ventricose and gradually widened to 1–1.5 cm at mouth; lobes suborbicular, ca. 8 mm in diam. Stamens 4, didynamous, slightly exerted; filaments hirsute, the longer pair ca. 8 mm, the shorter pair ca. 5 mm; anther oblong, ca. 2 mm. Ovary glabrous, with 2 ovules in each locule; style ca. 3.2 cm, pilose. Capsule linear‑oblong, compressed, ca 1.8 cm, apiculate, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm, densely appressed tomentose; areola very small.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. L. T. Lo 186, 283;; P. S. Choi 257; F. W. Xing 7456, 7757 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Streamsides and other wet places. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as Strobilanthes divaricatus (Nees) T. Anderson previously (Check List HK Plants 255. 2002; 88. 2004).

Strobilanthes dimorphotricha Hance 球花馬藍
J. Bot. 21: 355. 1883.
Goldfussia dimorphotricha (Hance) Bremek., Verh. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Amst., Afd. Natuurk., Sect. 2, 41(1): 231, 274. 1944.

Anisophyllous perennial herbs, 0.4–1.5 m tall, many‑branched. Stems somewhat zigzag upward, glabrous or yellowish pubescent. Leaves unequal in each pair, the smaller about 1/3 to 2/3 of the larger in size; petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; leaf blades elliptic, elliptic‑lanceolate, ovate, papery, the larger ones 4–15 × 1.5–4.5 cm, the smaller ones 1.5–2.5 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acuminate or caudate, margin serrulate, adaxially dark green, white appressed pubescent, cystoliths slightly prominent, lineolate, abaxially glabrous, or whitish pubescent along the veins, with or without multicellular hairs, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Spikes terminal or axillary, very compact, head‑like, subspherical in outline, 2–3‑flowered, usually 1–3 forming a forked panicle. Peduncles ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous or pubescent. Bracts ovate‑elliptic, 1–1.3 cm, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous, caducous; bracteoles lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, caducous. Calyx 7–9 mm, accrescent to 15–17 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, glandular pubescent. Corolla purple‑red, 3 – 4 cm, slightly curved, outside subglabrous or sparsely pilose, inside glabrous except for hairs retaining the style, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm, ventricose and gradually widened to ca. 1.5 cm at mouth; lobes subequal, orbicular, 5–6 mm in diam., apex emarginate. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments glabrous, the longer pair unequal, erect, 5–7 mm, the shorter pair equal, incurved, ca. 2 mm; anther spherical, ca. 1 mm in diam. Ovary pilose, 2 ovules in each locule; style ca. 3.5 cm, pilose. Capsule oblong‑clavate, 1.4–1.8 cm, glandular‑pubescent, 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, ca. 2.5 × 2.5 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Tai No, Ho Chung. P. S. Choi 370; HK sheet 31572.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and other wet places in ravines. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The species was reported as Strobilanthes penstmonoides (Nees) T. Anderson (2002) and Strobilanthes pentastemonoides (Nees) T. Anderson (2004) previously (Check List HK Plants 255. 2002; 88. 2004).

Strobilanthes tetraspermus (Champ. ex Benth.) Druce 四子馬藍
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 1916: 649. 1917; FFJ 5: 133. 1993; Fl. Guizhou. 10: 249. 2004.
Ruellia tetrasperma Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 132. 1853.
Championella tetrasperma (Champ. ex Benth.) Bremek., Verh. Ned. Aked. Werensch. Afd. Natuurk. Sect. 2, 41(1): 163. 1944; FHN 3: 546. 1974; FRPS 70: 94. 2002.
Acanthopale tetrasperma (Champ. ex. Benth.) Hand.‑Mazz., Beih. Bot. Centralbl. LVI, B: 454. 1937.
Strobilanthes radicans T. Anderson, FHK 262. 1861; FKH 198. 1912, nom. illeg., based on Ruellia tetrasperma Champ.
Acanthopale radicans (T. Anderson) C. B. Clarke ex Benoist, Fl. Indo‑Chine 4: 673. 1953, nom. illeg.

Isophyllous herbs, 30–50 cm tall. Stems suffrutescent, often procumbent, and rooting at base, quadrangular, sulcate, retrorsely pubescent along sulci, glabrescent. Petioles 0.5–2.5 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades ovate, elliptic or oblong, papery, 1.5–11 × 1–4.5 cm, base attenuate or decurrent onto the petiole, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrate or dentate, glabrous, densely covered with cystoliths, lateral veins ca. 5 pairs. Spike short and abbreviated, head‑like or slightly elongate, few‑flowered. Bracts leaf‑like, obovate or spathulate, 1–1.5 × 0.4 – 0.5 cm, pinnately‑veined, sparsely pilose; bracteoles linear, 5–6 × 1 mm, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose, densely covered with cystoliths; Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear, 5–7 × 1 mm, accrescent to ca. 8 mm in fruit, glabrous except for large‑celled hairs on the margin, densely covered with cystoliths. Corolla purple or purplish blue, 1.5–2 cm, straight, funnel‑shaped, outside pubescent, inside villose, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm long and ca. 2 mm, gradually widened to 1.5 cm at mouth; lobes oblong, ca. 4 × 5 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments of longer pair ca. 5 mm, sparsely pubescent, the shorter pair ca. 2 mm, glabrous; anthers oblong, ca. 2 mm; staminodes short or absent. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, hispid at tip, 4 ovules per locule; style ca. 1.5 cm, hirsute; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal. Capsule oblong, 0.7–1 cm, pubescent at tip, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 157; Y. W. Lam 1868; F. W. Xing 9772, 10033 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The holotype specimen (Champion 17, holotype, K) was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong between 1847 and 1850.

Stromanthe sanguinea Sond. 紫背竹芋
Hamburger Garten-Blumenzeitung 5: 225. 1849; FGD 2: 441. 1991.

Perennial herb, ca. 1 m tall, rhizomes creeping, nearly fleshy. Leaves basal and cauline; basal leaves long-petiolate, cauline leaves shortly petiolate or sessile; leaf blade elliptic-oblong, 30–45 × 6–12 cm, base rounded or acute, apex acuminate, dark green and shining adaxially, wine-purple or striped with green abaxially. Panicles with long peduncle, rachis slightly zigzag; bracts cherry-red, ovate, 1.5–3 cm; sepals cherry-red, oblong, 8–9 mm; corolla white, tube 1 mm; lobes lanceolate, 9 mm; 2 outer staminodes linear, subequal, inner staminode broader. Ovary sericeous.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32243, 32962.
Distribution: Guangdong (cultivated); native to Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Strophanthus divaricatus (Lour.) Hook. & Arn. 羊角拗
Bot. Beechey Voy. 199. 1837; FRPS 63: 152, pl. 51. 1977; FGD 1: 462, fig. 517. 1987; FOC 16: 178. 1995.
Pergularia divaricatus Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 169. 1790.
Strophanthus divergens Graham, Edinburgh New Philos. J. 179. 1827; FHK 220. 1861.
Strophanthus chinensis (Hunter ex Roxb.) G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 85. 1837; FKH 172. 1912.

Lianas or sarmentose shrubs, to 4.5 m tall, stolon‑bearing when pruned, glabrous except for corolla; latex clear or yellowish. Branches dark grey, densely lenticellate, branchlets reddish brown. Petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade elliptic or slightly obovate, 3–10 × 1.5–5 cm; lateral veins 4–9 on each side of midvein. Cymes 3–15‑flowered; peduncle to 1.5 cm; bracts linear or narrowly ovate, deciduous. Pedicels to 1 cm. Sepals narrowly triangular, 4 – 11 mm. Corolla yellow, tube 0.9 – 1.6 cm, puberulent on both sides or glabrous inside; lobes with a red basal spot adaxially, ovate, to 10 cm, abruptly narrowed into pendulous tails to 1 mm wide; corona‑lobes 10, greenish yellow, triangular or awl‑shaped, 0.9–3 mm. Anthers included, connective tail to 0.6 mm. Ovary glabrous. Follicles ellipsoidal‑oblong, 9 – 15 × 2–3.5 cm, hard, woody, divergent at an angle 180 – 250°. Seeds fusiform, 1.3–2 cm, beak 1.2–3.4 cm, coma 3.5–5.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 16; Y. S. Lau 2369; HK sheet 40116.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets or thin forests. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Oct.

Strychnos angustiflora Benth. 牛眼馬錢
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 1: 102. 1857; FHK 232. 1861; FKH 174. 1912; FRPS 61: 234, pl. 61: 1 – 7. 1992; FGD 3: 306, fig. 197. 1995; FOC 15: 326. 1996.

Lianas to 10 m, glabrous except for inflorescences and flowers. Branchlets with axillary tendrils; older branches with axillary thorns. Petioles 4 – 6 mm; leaf blade ovate, elliptic, or suborbicular, 3 – 8 × 2 – 4 cm, leathery, base obtuse to rounded or sometimes slightly cordate, apex acute to obtuse, basal veins 3 – 5, lateral veins more delicate than midvein. Thyrses terminal, 2 – 4 cm, pubescent. Flowers 5‑merous, 8 – 11 mm. Sepals ovate to triangular, 1 – 1.5 mm, outside puberulous. Corolla white, salverform; tube 4 – 5 mm, throat and base of lobes with long woolly hairs; lobes narrowly oblong, ± as long as tube. Stamens inserted at mouth or corolla tube, ca. 2 mm; filaments filiform, longer than anthers; anthers oblong, exserted, base glabrous. Pistil ca. 1 cm, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 0.7 mm; style slender. Berries orange when ripe, globose, 2 – 4 cm in diam., smooth, 1 – 6‑seeded. Seeds pale yellowish grey, orbicular, flat, 1 – 1.8 cm in diam., covered with extremely fine sericeous hairs.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Sam A Tsuen, Tai Wan, Lantau Island, Lamma Island, Beaufort Island, Ching Chau. S. P. Lau 168; Y. S. Lau 3105; HK sheet 40825.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Vietnam, Thailand, Philippines.
Ecology: Open woodlands, scrubs. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), poisonous.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by R. B. Hinds and J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore), poisonous.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by R. B. Hinds and J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Strychnos cathayensis Merr. 華馬錢
Lingnan Sci. J. 13: 14. 1934; FRPS 61: 237. 1992; FGD 3: 307. 1995; FOC 15: 326. 1996.

Lianas to 8 m. Young branchlets pubescent, glabrescent, with axillary double tendrils. Petioles 2 – 4 mm; leaf blade elliptic to narrowly oblong, 6–10 × 2–4 cm, abaxially puberulous, adaxially green, glabrous, and shiny, basal veins impressed adaxially. Cymes terminal or axillary, 3–4 cm, many‑flowered; peduncle puberulous; bracteoles ovate to triangular, ca. 1 mm. Flowers 5‑merous, 0.8–1.2 cm. Pedicels ca. 2 mm, puberulous. Sepals ovate, ca. 1 × 0.5 mm, outside puberulous. Corolla white, salverform, ca. 1.2 cm, glabrous, outside sometimes papillose; tube ca. 9 mm; lobes oblong, to 3.5 mm, slightly thickened. Stamens inserted at mouth of corolla tube, ca. 2 mm; filaments ca. 0.5 mm; anthers oblong, 1.5 – 2 mm, glabrous. Pistil to 1.1 cm, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1 mm; style slender, to 1 cm; stigma capitate. Berries globose, 1.5–3 cm in diam., 2–7‑seeded. Seeds saucer‑shaped, 2–2.5 cm wide, densely puberulous.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Luk Keng. Y. S. Lau 1826; Y. W. Lam 224.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Open woodlands, scrubs. Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), poisonous.

Strychnos umbellata (Lour.) Merr. 傘花馬錢
Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 252. 1919; FRPS 61: 233, pl. 60: 7 – 13. 1992; FGD 3: 306. 1995; FOC 15: 326. 1996.
Cissus umbellata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 84. 1790.
Strychnos paniculata Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 56. 1853; FHK 232. 1861; FKH 174. 1912.

Lianas to 10 m or longer. Branchlets glabrous. Petioles 4 – 6 mm; leaf blade 4 – 9 × 2 – 3.5 cm, ovate to narrowly elliptic, leathery, glabrous, base obtuse, apex obtuse to acute, basal veins 3 – 7. Thyrses terminal or axillary, 6 – 12 cm; peduncle pubescent. Flowers 4‑ or 5‑merous. Pedicels 1 – 4 mm, pubescent. Sepals broadly ovate, ca. 1 × 1 mm, outside pubescent. Corolla campanulate, ca. 4 mm, outside glabrous; tube 0.5 – 1 mm, mouth pubescent; lobes narrowly oblong, 1.5 – 3 mm. Stamens inserted at mouth of corolla tube, exserted; filaments ca. 1.5 mm; anthers narrowly ovate, ca. 1 mm, cordate, base bearded. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, glabrous or apically with shaggy hairs. Style 2.5 – 3 mm; stigma capitate. Berries globose, ca. 1.2 cm in diam., 1 – 3‑seeded. Seeds pale yellowish‑grey, orbicular, ca. 7 mm, covered with very fine sericeous hairs.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, So Kwun Wat, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 388; N. H. Li 153; K. Y. Tam 131.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul. – Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), poisonous.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 and 1856. The type specimen of Strychnos paniculata was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Stylidium tenellum Sw. 狹葉花柱草
Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 1: 51. 1807; FKH 151. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 181. 1983; FGD 3: 334. 1995.
Stylidium roseum Kurz, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 46(2): 212. 1877.
Stylidium tenellum var. minimum C. B. Clarke, in Hook. f., Fl. Brit. India 3: 420. 1881, ‘minima’.
Epilobium tonkinense H. Lév., Bull. Herb. Boissier ser. 2, 7: 588. 1907.

Herbs, annual, erect, 6–16 cm tall. Stems slender, simple or laxly dichotomously branched, glabrous. Leaves alternate, few, sessile or nearly sessile; leaf blades oblong‑obovate to oblanceolate, 4–10 × 0.8–2 mm, apical ones smaller and graduating into bracts, glabrous, veins 3 inconspicuous and arcuate, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin entire. Inflorescences terminal. Flowers solitary, in a spike of 2 or 3, or in a dichotomous inflorescence, sessile. Calyx glabrous or with glandular trichomes; tube (hypanthium) elongate, ca. 1 cm; 2 lobes connate into a slightly 2‑lobed segment. Corolla white or pink or rose purple, less than 2 mm, with sparse glandular trichomes; tube slightly longer than calyx‑lobes; lobes distinct, posterior one 2‑lobed, anterior ones much smaller; labellum minute, subulate; appendage at throat minute but visible. Capsule thinly columnar, to 1.5 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Pat Sin Leng. HK sheet 2743.
Distribution: S Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Yunnan (Xishuangbanna); India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, swamps. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.

Stylidium uliginosum Sw. 花柱草
Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 1: 52. 1807; FHK 195. 1861; FKH 151. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 181. 1983; FGD 3: 333. 1995.
Stylidium sinicum Hance, Walp. Ann. Syst. 2: 1030. 1851.

Herbs, annual, 5–13(–19) cm tall. Leaves all basal, generally in a rosette, each with a short petiole; leaf blade ovate‑orbicular, ovate, or obovate, 4–10 × 2–6 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire, glabrous, veins obscure. Stems 1–3, leafless, simple or dichotomously branched, covered with sparse short glandular trichomes. Inflorescences a long and lax spike; bracts ovate, less than 1 mm. Flowers small, sessile. Calyx tube (hypanthium) narrow, with sparse glandular trichomes; lobes minute, anterior 2 connate into a shallowly 2‑lobed segment, ca. 1.8 mm, but others 3 linear and ca. 1.2 mm. Corolla white, ca. 2 mm; tube short; anterior lobe extremely small, ovate, reflexed, becoming a labellum; 4 remaining lobes patent toward posterior side with 2 most posterior longer, base with an appendage, apex shallowly 2‑lobed. Gynostemium ca. 3.5 mm, exserted. Ovary 2‑locular. Capsule columnar, 6 – 8 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 435; HK sheet 19097.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; India, Sri Lanka, NE Australia.
Ecology: Wet places by streams. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.

Styrax confusus Hemsl. 賽山梅（狗肝柴）
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1906: 162. 1906; FGD 1: 391. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 113. 1987; FOC 15: 262. 1996.
Styrax mollis Dunn, Kew Bull. Misc. Inform. 1911: 273. 1911; FKH 164. 1912.

Tree 2– 8 m tall; bark greyish brown; branchlets densely brownish stellate pubescent. Leaves alternate, leathery to subleathery; petioles 1–3 mm; leaf blade elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 4 –14 × 2.5–7 cm, apex acute to shortly acuminate, base rounded to broadly cuneate, margin irregularly serrulate, sparsely stellate pubescent, gradually glabrescent, lateral veins 5 –7 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 3 – 8-flowered, 4 –10 cm; rachis densely brownish stellate pubescent; pedicels 1–1.5 cm, densely brownish stellate pubescent; flowers 1.3 –2.2 cm; calyx 4 –10 × 4–6 mm, densely yellowish to grey stellate tomentose and villose; teeth 5, deltoid; corolla tube 3– 4 mm, lobes lanceolate, 12–20 × 3 – 4 mm, imbricate or sparsely valvate in buds; stamens 10, filaments slightly expanded, 8–10 mm, free parts basally densely white villose. Fruit sub-globose to obovoid, 0.8 –1.5 cm in diam., densely yellowish stellate tomentose; exocarp 1–2 mm thick, rugose. Seeds brown, obovoid, smooth or deeply rugose.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 18182.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thin forests, margins of forests. Flowering: Apr.– Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as styrax faberi Perkins previously (Check List HK Plants 35. 1993). The type specimen was collected from Lantau Island by Mr. Ford's native collector in May 1888.

Styrax odoratissimus Champ. ex Benth. 芳香安息香
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew. Gard. Misc. 4: 304. 1852; FHK 213. 1861; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 76. 1889, p.p.; FKH 164. 1912, “odoratissimum”; FGD 1: 388. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 99. 1987; FOC 15: 258. 1996.

Tree 4 –10 m tall; bark grey-brown; young branchlets densely stellate pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade leathery to papery, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 4–15 × 2–8 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire or remotely serrulate, densely brown stellate pubescent on both surfaces when young, glabrescent in age, lateral veins 6 –9 on each side of midvein. Inflorescence terminal, racemose or paniculate, 8 –12 cm, 6 –12-flowered, densely yellow stellate tomentose; flowers 1.2–1.5 cm; pedicels 1.5 –1.8 cm; calyx ca. 5 × 5 mm, membranous, apex truncate to undulate; corolla lobes elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 9 –11 × 4 –5 mm, membranous, imbricate in buds; stamens shorter than corolla; filaments slightly flexuous at middle, densely white stellate pubescent. Fruit subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam., densely grey-yellow stellate tomentose, apex with a slightly curved rostrum. Seeds ovoid, brown, tuberculate, densely brown scaly.

Locality: Repulse Bay, Wan Chai Gap, Wong Chuk Hang, Pok Fu Lam, Aberdeen, Tai Tam Tuk, Mount Victoria, Mount Gough, Causeway Bay, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1544; H. C. Tang 809; H. G. Ye et al. 1223.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests, margins of forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Styrax suberifolius Hook. & Arn. 栓葉安息香（紅皮）
Bot. Beechey Voy. 196. 1841; FHK 213. 1861; FKH 164. 1912, “suberifolium”; FHN 3: 182. 1974; FTW 4: 111. 1978; FGD 1: 389. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 109. 1987; FOC 15: 260. 1996.
Cyrta suberifolia (Hook. & Arn.) Miers, Contr. Bot. 1: 182. 1851.

Tree 4 –20 m tall; bark dark brown. Young branchlets, petioles and inflorescence densesly rusty stellate tomentose. Leaves alternate, leathery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 5 –15 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin subentire, glabrous adaxially, densely greyish or brownish stellate tomentose abaxially, lateral veins 5 –12 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate, many-flowered, 6 –12 cm; pedicels 1–3 mm; flowers white, 1–1.5 cm; calyx cup-shaped, 3–5(–7) × 2– 4(–7) mm, densely grey-yellow tomentose mixed with few stellate hairs; teeth ± rudimentary, deltoid to undulate; corolla tube ca. 3 mm, lobes 4 –5, lanceolate to oblong, 8 –12 × 2–3 mm, valvate in buds; stamens 8 –10, shorter than corolla; filaments expanded, stellate pubescent on free part; anthers oblong, 3 mm; styles subequal to corolla, glabrous. Fruit ovoid-globose, 1.2–3 × 0.8–1.6 cm, densely grey to brown stellate tomentose, 3-valvate dehiscent with persistent calyx enclosing to middle. Seeds 1–2, ellipsoid, brown, smooth or rugose, glabrous or scale-like pubescent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Tai Tam, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Happy Valley, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Kellet. P. S. Choi 339; H. C. Tang 980, 1742.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Suaeda australis (R. Br.) Moq. 南方鹼蓬
Ann. Sci. Nat. 23: 318. 1831; FHN 1: 394. 1964; FHK 283. 1861; FKH 215. 1912; FOC 5: 394. 2003.
Suaeda maritima (L.) Dumort, Fl. Belg. 22. 1827; FGD 3: 62. 1995; FTW 2: 387. 1996.
Chenopodium maritimum L., Sp. Pl. 221. 1753.
Chenopodium australe R. Br., Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holl. 407. 1810.
Suaeda monoica auct. non Forssk.: FKH 215. 1912.

Perennial herb or subshrub, 7–10 cm tall. Stems much branched. Leaves fleshy, white or purple, semi-terete, linear, 10 –35 × 1–3 mm, base attenuate, apex slightly acute or obtuse, margin entire. Flowers small, polygamous, solitary or 2– 5-clustered in glomerules. Bracteoles 2–3, oblong, 0.8 –1 mm, persistent; perianth purple-green, 5-lobed; lobes ovate-oblong, enclosing fruit when fruiting. Utricle compressed globose, 1.2–1.5 mm in diam. Seeds black, lustrous.

Locality: Sha Tin, Lau Fau Shan, Plover Cove, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 437; HK sheet 36813.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Jiangsu; cosmopolitan.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and margins of mangroves. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Syagrus romanzoffiana (Cham.) Glassm. 皇后葵（金山葵）
Fieldiana, Bot. 31: 382. 1968; FRPS 13(1): 146, pl. 35. 1991.
Cocos romanzoffiana Cham., Choris Voy. Pittor. (Chili): 5, t. 6. 1822.

Tree, 10–16 m tall. Stems solitary, 25–40 in diam., dark grey, leaf scars roughly ringed. Leaves pinnate, 2–5 m, recurved; pinnae many, linear-lanceolate, 40–70(–90) × 3–4(–5) cm, apex bifid, spreading in different planes, 2–6 in groups, with a small gap between groups; sheaths open. Inflorescences interfoliar, 1–2 × 0.6 m, branched 1 order, rachillae up to 80, 30–50 cm, usually zigzagged; male flowers borne on upper rachis, 7–16 mm, sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 6; female flowers borne on lower rachis, 4.5–6 × 4–6 mm, sepals 3, petals 3, staminodes 6-teethed, ovary 3-locular. Fruits globose or obovoid; 3 × 2.8 cm, orange; mesocarp fleshy, fibrous, endocarp thick, woody, with 3 germinating pores near base. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3252; HK sheet 29595, 29600.
Distribution: Brazil, S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.; fruiting: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Symplocos adenophylla Wall. ex G. Don 腺葉山礬
Gen. Hist. 4: 3. 1837; FRPS 60(2): 37. 1987; FGD 1: 408, fig. 445. 1987; FOC 15: 245. 1996.

Tree 4 –10 m tall; branchlets reddish brown. Young shoots, buds, inflorescences, bracts, and calyx reddish brown powdery puberulent. Leaves thick papery; petioles 5 –10 mm, with marginal glands; leaf blade narrowly elliptic, elliptic, or narrowly ovate, 6 –11 × 1.8 –3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudateacuminate, margin subentire to crenate-serrulate, with ellipsoidal glands at sinus of the teeth; lateral veins 4 –12 pairs. Racemes 2–4 cm, with 1–3 branches, rachis puberulent when young; bracts triangular-ovate, 1–1.5 mm; bracteoles less than 1 mm. Calyx 2–2.5 mm; lobes 5, triangular-ovate, 0.3 –0.5 mm. Corolla white, ca. 3 mm; lobes 5, 2.5 –2.8 mm. Stamens 30 –35; filaments ± united at base. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous; style ca. 2 mm; stigma capitate; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes ellipsoid-cylindric, 6–12 × 3 –5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. F. W. Xing 8459.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thin forests, valleys. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Aug.

Symplocos adenopus Hance 腺柄山礬
J. Bot. 21: 322. 1883; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 61. 1987; FGD 1: 409, fig. 447. 1987; FOC 15: 250. 1996.

Shrub or small tree. Branchlets ± angulate; buds, young branchlets and petioles brown pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5 –1.8 cm, marginal ridges densely glandular dentate; leaf blade elliptic-ovate to ovate, 5 –16 × 2– 6 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin glandular dentate, abaxially appressed pilose to tomentose, especially on the veins; lateral veins 6–14 pairs, impressed adaxially. Glomerules axillary; bracts suborbicular, 2–3 mm in diam., tomentose at least toward apex, margin with large glands; bracteoles elliptic, 1–2 mm, tomentose at least toward apex, margin with small glands. Calyx 2–3 mm; lobes 5, semi-orbicular, 1.5–2 mm, glabrous, sometimes ciliate. Corolla white, ca. 5 mm, divided nearly to base, 5-lobed; lobes elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 3.5 – 4 mm. Stamens 20–30. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous; disc cylindric, 0.5 –1 mm long, glabrous. Drupes cylindric, 7–10 mm, apex with persistent erect calyxlobes.

Locality: No precise locality, only one specimen collected in Hong Kong. HK sheet 17993.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Valleys or thin forests. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.

Symplocos anomala Brand. 薄葉山礬
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29: 529. 1900; FRPS 60(2): 15. 1987; FGD 1: 404, fig. 439. 1987; FOC 15: 242. 1996.
Symplocos anomala Brand var. nitida Li in J. Arnold Arbor. 24: 452. 1943.

Shrub or small tree; terminal buds and young branchlets brown tomentose. Leaves thin leathery; petioles 4 – 8 mm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic, elliptic or oblanceolate, 2–7(–11) × 1.2–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sparsely and shallowly serrulate; glabrous or rarely young leaves finely appressed hairy on abaxial surface; midvein and lateral veins adaxially prominent; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Racemes 0.8 –1.5 cm, axillary, sometimes 1–3-branched from base, pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, margin ciliate, 0.8 –1.5 mm. Calyx 2–2.5 mm, puberulent; lobes 5, semi-orbicular, ciliate. Corolla white, 4 – 6 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, 3– 4 mm. Stamens ca. 30; filaments ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, pubescent. Drupes brown, obovoid, 7–10 mm, puberulent, apex with persistent erect or inflexed calyx-lobes.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 1647, 1745.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River.
Ecology: Broadleaved forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Symplocos cochinchinensis (Lour.) S. Moore var. laurina (Retz.) Nooteb. 黃牛奶樹
Rev. Symploc. 156. 1975; FOC 15: 249. 1996.
Myrtus laurina Retz. Obs. 4: 26. 1786.
Symplocos laurina (Retz.) Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Syst. 4: 3. 1837; FRPS 60(2): 55. 1987; FGD 1: 417, fig. 460. 1987.
Symplocos spicata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 541. 1832; FHK 212, 1861; FKH 163. 1912.

Evergreen tree. Branchlets glabrous; buds brown pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 5.5–11 × 2–8.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin denticulate, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein impressed abaxially, lateral veins 4–5 on pairs. Spikes terminal or axillary, 3–6 cm, usually branched at base, pubescent at flowering time; bracts broadly ovate, ca. 2 mm, margin glandular punctate. Calyx glabrous, ca. 2 mm; lobes 5, semi-orbicular, shorter than the tube. Corolla white, ca. 4 mm, 5-lobed nearly to the base. Stamens ca. 30; filaments 3–5 mm, ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes globose, 4–6 mm in diam., apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2098; HK sheet 36098.
Distribution: S, C, SW & E China; India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.; fruiting: Mar.–Jun. of the following year.

Symplocos confusa Brand 南嶺山礬
Pflanzenr. 6 (IV. 242): 88. 1901; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 74. 1987; FGD 1: 423, fig. 470. 1987.
Symplocos pendula var. hirtistylis (C. B. Clarke) Noot., Rev. Symplocac. 42. 1975; FOC 15: 252. 1996.

Evergreen small tree; buds, inflorescences, bracts, and calyx grey pubescent. Leaves subleathery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ellipticobovate to ovate, 5 –12 × 2–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, tip blunt, margin entire or dentate; midvein abaxially impressed, lateral veins 5–9 per side. Racemes 1–2.5(–4.5) cm, axillary; bracts oblong-ovate, 1.5 –2 mm, apex obtuse; bracteoles narrowly ovate, 1–1.2 mm, apex acute. Pedicels 3 –5 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2.2–3.2 mm, 5-lobed; lobes shorter and rounded. Corolla white, 4.5 –7 mm, 5-lobed; tube 1–2 mm. Stamens 40 –50, filaments flat, connate into a tube and adnate to the throat of corolla tube. Ovary 2-locular; disc annular, pubescent; style ca. 5 mm; stigmas semi-orbicular. Drupes ovoid, 4–5 mm, pubescent, apex with persistent erect or inflexed calyx-lobes.

Locality: Lantau Peak. HK sheet 18014.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Symplocos congesta Benth. 密花山礬
FHK 211. 1861; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 69. 1987; FGD 1: 410, fig. 448. 1987; FOC 15: 251. 1996.

Evergreen tree or shrub; young branchlets and buds brown pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 8 –10(–17) × 2–6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin usually entire, rarely and sparsely glandular serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 –10 on each side of midvein. Glomerules, axillary; bracts and bractlets brown pubescent, margin with 4 or 5 oblong glands. Calyx often reddish brown, 3 – 4 mm, glabrous. Corolla white, 4 – 6 mm, divided nearly to the base; lobes 5, elliptic ovate. Stamens ca. 50, filaments ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc flat to annular, glabrous. Drupes purplish blue, cylindric, 8 –13 × 3 – 4 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 156; HK sheet 37536.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Mixed forests. Flowering: Aug. –Nov.; fruiting: Jan. –Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Symplocos decora Hance 美山礬
J. Bot. 12: 369. 1874; FKH 164.1912; FRPS 60(2): 25. 1987; FGD 1: 402, fig. 435. 1987; FOC 15: 244. 1996, pro syn. sub S. sumuntia Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don
Dicalix decorus (Hance) Migo, J. Shanghai Sci. Inst. 13: 200. 1943.

Evergreen small tree, 4 – 6 m tall; branchlets glabrous, greyish when young, turning purplish black in age. Leaves leathery; petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade elliptic-obovate or elliptic, 4 –11 × 2.5 – 4 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex shortly acuminate, tip blunt, margin shallowly serrate, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein abaxially impressed, lateral veins indistinct. Racemes 3–6 cm, glabrous or slightly pubescent. Bracts suborbicular, ca. 5 mm in diam., caducous; bracteoles oblong-lanceolate, 3–5 × 1.2 mm, caducous. Pedicels 0.8 –5 mm, jointed. Calyx 3– 4 mm, glabrous; lobes 5, triangular-ovate. Corolla white, 5 –7 mm, divided nearly to the base; lobes 5, ovate-orbicular. Stamens ca. 25; filaments united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes urceolate, 6–9 mm, apex with persistent erect or slightly inflexed calyx lobes.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 211; HK sheet 8887.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance in March 1874 from the Hong Kong Botanic Gardens. This species was recorded as a synonym of Symplocos sumuntia Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don previously (Check List of HK Plants 45. 2004).

Symplocos fordii Hance 三裂山礬
J. Bot. 20: 78. 1882; FKH 163.1912; FRPS 60(2): 27. 1987; FGD 1: 414, fig. 455. 1987; FOC 15: 244. 1996.
Symplocos cordatifolia H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25: 424. 1944.

Shrub to 2 m tall. Branchlets slender, dark brown; young shoots, petioles and abaxial surface of leaves covered with spreading greyish yellow long hairs. Leaves thin leathery, subsessile, narrowly ovate or ovate, 3.5 –9 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cordate, slightly oblique, apex long caudate-acuminate, margin sharply serrate; lateral veins 5 –11 pairs, together with tertiary veins prominent on both surfaces. Spikes short, 5–10 flowered, rachis ca. 1 cm, pubescent; bracts broadly ovate, ca. 1 mm, bracteoles ovate, acute. Calyx ca. 2 mm, glabrous; lobes 3, broadly ovate, slightly longer than the tube. Corolla white, ca. 3.5 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, oblong. Stamens 15 –30, filaments ± connate at base. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous. Drupes narrowly ovoid, ca. 1 cm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Victoria Peak, High West. HK sheet 3273, 37728.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thin forests on summits. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by C. Ford in 1881.

Symplocos glauca (Thunb.) Koidz. 羊舌樹
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 39: 313. 1925; FRPS 60(2): 30. 1987; FGD 1: 413, fig. 454. 1987; FOC 15: 244. 1996.
Laurus glauca Thunb. Fl. Jap. 173. 1784.
Symplocos neriifolia Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math.-Phys. 4(3): 134. 1846; FKH 163. 1912.

Evergreen shrub or tree. Buds, young branchlets, and inflorescences densely tawny tomentose. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.5–3 mm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, 6–15 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or short acuminate, margin entire, glabrous or rarely abaxially with cobwebby hairs, adaxially dark green, abaxially glaucous, turning brown when dry; midvein adaxially impressed, lateral veins 5 –8 on each side of midvein. Spikes 1–1.5 cm, mostly basally branched; bracts broadly ovate, ca. 2 mm, downy tomentose. Calyx ca. 3 mm; lobes 5, ovate, tawny tomentose. Corolla 4–5 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, apex rounded. Stamens 30 – 40; filaments slender, ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous; disc cylindric, glabrous. Drupes narrowly ovoid, 1.2–2 cm, apex with persistent erect calyx lobes.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Au Mun, Ho Chung, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lai Chi Wo. L. T. Lo 349; Y. S. Lau 948.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Lowland secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Symplocos lancifolia Sieb. & Zucc. 光葉山礬
Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math.-Phys. 4(3): 133. 1846; FRPS 60(2): 52. 1987; FGD. 1: 420, fig. 464. 1987; FOC 15: 248. 1996.
Symplocos microcarpa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 303. 1852; FHK 212. 1861; FKH 164. 1912.

Evergreen shrub or small tree; branchlets slender, dark brown, yellowish brown when young, glabrous in age. Leaves papery; petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade ovate to broadly lanceolate, 3 –9 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin finely dentate to crenate, abaxially yellowish brown pubescent on veins when young; lateral veins 6–11 on each side of midvein. Spikes 1– 4 cm; bracts elliptic-ovate, ca. 2 mm; bracteoles broadly triangular-ovate, 1.5 × 2 mm, ciliate. Calyx 1.6 –2 mm; lobes 5, ovate, apex rounded, abaxially puberulent; tube glabrous. Corolla cream yellow, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, 2.5– 4 mm. Stamens ca. 25; filaments in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular, apex glabrous. Drupes ellipsoid to subglobose, ca. 4 mm in diam., apex with persistent erect calyx lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1320, 1443.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Japan.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen of Symplocos microcarpa was collected from Happy Valley woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Symplocos crassifolia Benth. 厚葉山礬（光亮山礬、厚皮灰木）
FHK 212. 1861; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 72. 1889; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 13. 1987; FGD 1: 399, fig. 430. 1987; FOC 15: 242. 1996, pro syn. sub S. lucida (Thunb.) Sieb. & Zucc.
Symplocos howii Merr. & Chun ex Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25: 211. 1944.

Evergreen small tree or tree; young branchlets, buds and leaves glabrous. Leaves leathery or thick leathery; petioles 0.8 –1.4 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic, elliptic or narrowly elliptic, 6.5–10 × 2.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sparsely serrate; midvein raised adaxially; lateral veins slender, 6–10 on each side of midvein, Racemes 1–2 cm, pubescent, branched basally, 4 –7-flowered; bracts oblong-ovate, pubescent abaxially; bracteoles broadly triangular-ovate. Calyx 3 –3.5 mm; lobes 5, broadly ovate or orbicular, margin and abaxial surface puberulent. Corolla white, 4 –5 mm, 5-lobed nearly to base. Stamens 60– 80; filaments united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc with 5 glands, villose. Drupes oblong-ovoid or obovoid, 1–1.5 cm, apex with persistent erect or slightly inflexed calyx-lobes.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 196; HK sheet 3269.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Jun.–Nov.; fruiting: Dec.–May of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. This species was recorded as Symplocos lucida (Thunb.) Siebold & Zucc. previously (Check List of HK Plants 45. 2004)

Symplocos paniculata (Thunb.) Miq. 白檀
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 3: 102. 1867; FRPS 60(2): 72. 1987; FGD 1: 422, fig. 469. 1987; FOC 15: 252. 1996.
Prunus paniculata Thunb., Fl. Jap. 200. 1784.
Symlocos sinica Ker-Gawl., Bot. Reg. 9: t. 710. 1823; FKH 163. 1912.
Symplocos crataegoides Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 145. 1825; FKH 163. 1912.
Symplocos hunanensis Hand.-Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 807. 1936.

Deciduous shrub or small tree; branchlets greyish white pilose when young, glabrous in age. Leaves membranous to thin papery; petioles 3 –7 mm; leaf blade broadly obovate, elliptic-obovate or ovate, 3–11 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin sharply serrulate, adaxially glabrous or puberulent, abaxially usually glabrous or sometimes pubescent on veins; midvein adaxially impressed on proximal half, with 4–8 lateral veins on each side. Panicles 5–10 cm, usually pilose; bracts linear, 1(–3) mm, brown glandular, caducous. Calyx 2–3 mm long; tube brown, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; lobes 5, ovate or semi-orbicular, slightly longer than tube. Corolla white, 4– 6 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, shortly ciliate. Stamens 40 – 60, unequal. Ovary 2-locular; disc 5-glandular, glabrous or hairy. Drupes bluish, ovoid-globose, 3– 8 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Tai Long Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Ho Pui, Tai Lam Chung, Castle Peak. H. C. Tang 1245; Y. S. Lau 2471.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, India.
Ecology: Thickets or grasslands. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Symplocos sumuntia Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don 山礬
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 145. 1825; FRPS 60(2): 22. 1987; FGD 1: 401, fig. 433. 1987; FOC 15: 243. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. S. decora Hance.
Symplocos caudata Wall. in DC. Prodr. 8: 256. 1844.
Symplocos punctata Brand in Fedde, Repert. Nov. Sp. 3: 217. 1906.

Evergreen tree; young branchlets brown, mostly glabrous. Leaves thin leathery; petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade ovate, narrowly ovate, or elliptic-oblanceolate, 3.5– 8 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin slightly serrate or sinuolatedentate, glabrous; midvein adaxially impressed; lateral veins 4 – 6 on each side of midvein. Racemes 2.5 – 4 cm, pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles broadly ovate or obovate, 0.5 –1.5 mm, densely pubescent. Calyx 2–2.5 mm; tube glabrous; lobes 5, triangular-ovate, equal or slightly shorter than tube. Corolla white or yellow, 4 – 8 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, obovate-elliptic, 3 –3.5 mm, slightly puberulent adaxially. Stamens 25–35; filaments united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes ovoidurceolate, 7–10 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx lobes.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 931, 1528.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Nepal, Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Thin forests on summits. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Symplocos wikstroemiifolia Hayata 微毛山礬
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 119. 1915; Noot., Fl. Taiwan 4: 131. 1978; FRPS 60(2): 16. 1987; FGD. 1: 400, fig. 432. 1987; FOC 15: 243. 1996.

Tree or shrub; young branchlets, petioles and abaxial surface of leaves covered with appressed hairs. Leaves papery to thin leathery; petioles 3 –10 mm; leaf blade elliptic, broadly oblanceolate, or obovate, 4 –12 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base narrowly cuneate, decurrent to the petioles, apex shortly acuminate, acute, or obtuse, margin entire or obscurely sinuolate-dentate; lateral veins 6–10 on each side of midvein; Racemes 1–2 cm, branched; rachis, bracts and bracteoles pubescent; bracts caducous, oblong or orbicular, 1.2–2 mm, margin ciliate. Calyx ca. 2 mm; lobes 5, broadly ovate or suborbicular, as long as or slightly longer than the tube. Corolla ca. 3 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, obovate-oblong. Stamens 15–20. Ovary sparsely pubescent or glabrous; disc annular, nearly glabrous or sparsely pilose. Drupes ovoid, black or black-purple, 5 –10 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Ma On Shan. HK sheet 37724, 37725.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Oct.

Synedrella nodiflora (L.) Gaertn. 金腰箭
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2(3): 456. 1791; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 173. 1968; FRPS 75: 363, pl. 61: 3 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 132, fig. 68. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1075, pl. 513. 1998.
Verbesina nodiflora L., Cent. Pl. 1: 28. 1755.

Annual herbs; stem erect, 30–120 cm tall, dichotomously branched, appressed pilose, or glabrous in lower part. Leaves ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, middle cauline ones 3–12.5 × 1.2–6 cm, base decurrent to form winged petiole of 0.5–4 cm, apex acute, adaxial surface dark green, abaxial surface paler, both surfaces appressed pubescent, hair denser abaxially, triplinerved, margin crenulate‑serrulate. Upper leaves smaller. Capitula 8–10 × 4–5 mm, mostly sessile or sometimes shortly pedunculate, always with 2–6 heads aggregated in axil or at branch terminal. Involucres ovoid‑oblong; phyllaries few; outermost 2 phyllaries foliaceous green, lanceolate, 8–10 × 2.5 mm, apex acute, pubescent; inner phyllaries scarious, oblong, 6–7 × 2–3 mm, obtuse, glabrous or sparsely puberulent, shortly ciliate along margin, subtending the ray florets. Receptacle small; paleae linear, 6–7 × 0.5–1 mm, margin minutely ciliate, subtending the disk florets. Ray pistillate florets yellow, 3.2–3.5 mm, ligule elliptic, 2 rounded lobes at apex, tube nearly as long as the ligule. Disk florets bisexual, tubular, 3.2 – 3.5 mm, 4‑lobed at apex, yellow. All florets fertile. Cypselae developed from ligulate florets obovate‑oblong, 4 × 1 mm, compressed and slightly curved inward, black in colour, margin with brownish white broad and hard wings, bearing 4–6 pairs of upward‑directed spines; pappus 2 straight hard spines about 2 mm. Cypselae developed from tubular florets oblong‑cuneate, flat or subtrigonous, 4–4.5 × 0.8–1 mm, black or blackish brown, tuberculate, pubescent; pappus 2–4, spiny, 3–4 mm, pale brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2039; H. Y. Yeung 46 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 5810 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.

Syzygium buxifolium Hook. & Arn. 赤楠
Bot. Beechey Voy. 187. 1833; FHK 118. 1861; FGZ 205. 1956; FHN 2: 19. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 90. 1984; FFJ 4: 99, fig. 85. 1989; FGX 1: 911. 1991; FGD 3: 189. 1995; FOC 13: 351. 2007.
Eugenia sinensis Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 23: 298. 1887; FKH 105. 1912.

Shrub or small tree. Young branchlets 4 – 6-angled, blackish brown when dry. Leaves opposite or whorled; petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade leathery, broadly elliptic to elliptic, sometimes broadly obovate, 1.5 – 3 × 1 – 2 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex rounded or obtuse, or sometimes acute and with an obtuse cusp, dark brown and not glossy when dry adaxially, glandular and slightly pale when dry abaxially; lateral veins many, inconspicuous or depressed adaxially, slightly raised abaxially. Cymes terminal, ca. 1 cm, several-flowered. Flower-buds ca. 3 mm. Pedicels ca. 1 –2 mm. Hypanthium obconic, ca. 2 mm. Calyx-lobes shallowly wavy. Petals 4, white, distinct, ca. 2 mm. Stamens ca. 2.5 mm. Style as long as stamens. Fruit purplish black when mature, globose, 5 – 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 100; Y. W. Lam 468; F. W. Xing 9337.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets and secondary forests. Flowering: Jun. –Aug.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Timber, fruit (edible).

Syzygium championii (Benth.) Merr. & L. M. Perry 灶地烏骨木（子凌蒲桃）
J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 219. 1938; FHN 2: 15. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 75, pl. 13: 3. 1984; FGX 1: 908, pl. 354: 1. 1991; FOC 13: 347. 2007.
Acmena championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 118. 1852; FHK 119. 1861.
Eugenia championii (Benth.) Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 23: 296. 1887.

Shrub to tree. Young branchlets 4-angled, greyish white when dry. Leaves opposite; petioles 2–3 mm; leaf blade leathery, narrowly oblong to elliptic, 3 – 6(–9) × 1 – 2 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acute and with a ca. 1 cm cusp, both surfaces greyish green when dry; lateral veins many. Cymes terminal or sometimes axillary, ca. 2 cm, 6 – 10-flowered. Flower-buds clavate, ca. 1 cm, basal part narrow. Pedicels very short. Hypanthium clavate, 8–10 mm. Calyx-lobes 4, shallowly wavy. Petals white or pink, connate into a calyptra. Stamens 3–4 mm. Style as long as stamens. Fruit red, long-ellipsoidal, ca. 1.2 cm, shallowly grooved when dry, 1 – 2-seeded.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Parker, Tai Tam, Deep Water Bay, Cape D'Aguilar, Pat Sin Leng, Ng Tung Chai, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 477, 580; F. W. Xing 8055.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Aug. –Nov.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Syzygium cumini (L.) Skeels 烏墨（海南蒲桃）
U.S.D.A. Bur. Pl. Industr. Bull. 248: 25. 1912. FGZ 204. 1956; FNH 2: 18. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 101. 1984; FFJ 4: 102, fig. 90. 1989; FGX 1: 909, pl. 353: 3. 1991; FGD 3: 187, fig. 133: 1. 1995; FOC 13: 355. 2007.
Myrtus cumini L., Sp. Pl. 1: 471. 1753.
Eugenia cumini (L.) Druce, Bot. Exch. Club Soc. Brit. Isles 3(5): 418. 1914.
Eugenia jambolana Lam., Encycl. 3(1): 198. 1789; FKH 105. 1912.

Tree, to 15 m tall. Young branchlets terete, greyish white when dry. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, 6–12 × 3.5 – 7 cm, base broadly cuneate, rarely rounded, apex rounded to obtuse and with a short cusp, brownish green to blackish brown and slightly glossy when dry adaxially, slightly pale when dry abaxially, both surfaces with small glands; lateral veins many and dense. Thyrses axillary, rarely terminal, to 11 cm. Flowers white, 3 – 5 in clusters, shortly pedicellate or sessile. Hypanthium obconic, ca. 4 mm. Calyx-lobes inconspicuous. Petals 4, white or light purple, united into a calyptra, ovate and slightly rounded, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens 3 – 4 mm. Style as long as stamens. Fruit red to black, ellipsoidal to urceolate, 1– 2 cm, 1-seeded; persistent calyx tube 1 –1.5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 857; Y. S. Lau 1955; HK sheet 36078.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Nepal, Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Feb. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Sep.

Syzygium euonymifolium (F. P. Metcalf) Merr. & L. M. Perry 衛矛葉蒲桃
J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 242. 1938; FGZ 205. 1956; FRPS 53(1): 105, pl. 25. 1984; FFJ 4: 103, fig. 91. 1989; FGX 1: 912, pl. 353: 3. 1991; FGD 3: 193. 1995; FOC 13: 356. 2007.
Eugenia euonymifolia F. P. Metcalf, Lingnan Sci. J. 11: 22. 1932.

Tree, to 12 m tall. Young branchlets terete or compressed, grey when dry, puberulous; old branches greyish white. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.8 – 1 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, elliptic, 5–9 × 3–4 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acuminate and with a 1–1.5 cm cusp, both surfaces greyish green when dry and with many small glands; lateral veins slightly raised abaxially. Cymes axillary, ca. 1 cm, 6 –11-flowered. Flower-buds ca. 2.5 mm. Hypanthium obconic, 1.5 – 2 mm, glandular punctate. Calyx-lobes 4, short, obtuse. Petals white, distinct, orbicular, ca. 2 mm. Stamens 2.5– 3 mm. Style as long as stamens. Fruit globose, 6– 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po. Y. W. Lam 2118; S. C. Ng 4027; HK sheet 38883.

Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Dec. – Jan.

J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 242. 1938; FGZ 205. 1956; FHN 2: 21. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 106. 1984; FFJ 4: 101, fig. 87. 1989; FGX 1: 912. 1991; FGD 3: 193. 1995; FOC 13: 366. 2007.
Eugenia minutiflora Hance, J. Bot. 9: 5. 1871, non Syzygium minutiflorum Miq. (1860) nec S. minutiflorum Gamble (1919); FKH 105. 1912.

Shrub or tree, to 10 m tall. Young branchlets terete, blackish brown when dry. Thyrses axillary, 1 – 1.5 cm, many-flowered. Flowers sessile, buds obovoid, ca. 2 mm. Hypanthium obconic, ca. 1.5 mm. Calyx-lobes inconspicuous. Petals 4, distinct, orbicular, ca. 1 mm. Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 76; Y. W. Lam 104; HK sheet 40805.

Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Jul. – Sep.; fruiting: Nov. – Jan.

Syzygium impressum N. H. Xia, Y. F. Deng & K. L. Yip 凹脈赤楠
J. Trop. Subtrop. Bot. 16: 19 – 22. 2008.

Shrubs, ca. 2 m tall, glabrous throughout; branchlets blackish brown when dry, tetrangular. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 2 mm, glabrous; leaf blades thin leathery, broadly obovate, 1 – 1.8 × 0.7 – 1 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse to retuse, margin entire, slightly revolute, glabrous, abaxially brown when dry and densely covered with glandular dots, adaxially dark brownish when dry, midvein impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially, lateral veins 6– 8 pairs, ca. 1.5 mm apart, at an angle of ca. 50˚ with midvein, adaxially inconspicuous, abaxially slightly conspicuous, intramarginal veins very closed to margin. Fruit globose, ca. 4 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2598; Y. W. Lam 468; HK sheet 11425.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Streamsides in montane forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.

Syzygium jambos (L.) Alston 蒲桃
Handb. Fl. Ceylon. 6: 115. 1931; FGZ 203. 1956; FHN 2: 14, fig. 291. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 68. 1984; FFJ 4: 97, fig. 82. 1989; FGX 1: 905. 1991; FGD 3: 185, fig. 132. 1995; FYN 7: 110. 1997; FOC 13: 344. 2007.

Jambosa vulgaris DC., Prodr. 3: 286. 1828, nom. illeg. superfl.; FHK 120. 1861.
Syzygium jambos var. sylvaticum (Gagnep.) Merr. & L. M. Perry, J. Arnold Arbor. 19(1): 114. 1938.

Ecology: Flowering: Mar. –Apr.; fruiting: May– Jun.

Syzygium levinei (Merr.) Merr. & L. M. Perry 山蒲桃

J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 110. 1938; FGZ 204. 1956; FHN 2: 18. 1965; FRPS 53(1): 115, pl. 29: 1– 2. 1984; FGX 1: 908, pl. 353: 2. 1991; FGD 3: 195. 1995; FOC 13: 358. 2007.

Eugenia levinei Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 13: 39. 1934.

Syzygium rehderianum Merr. & L. M. Perry 紅枝蒲桃
J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 243. 1938; FRPS 53(1): 99, pl. 21: 2. 1984; FFJ 4: 101, fig. 88. 1989; FGX 1: 912, pl. 355: 3. 1991; FGD 3: 193. 1995; FOC 13: 355. 2007.
