Shrub or tree. Young branchlets red, brown when dry, terete, slightly compressed; old branchlets greyish brown. Leaves opposite; petioles 7–9 mm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 4–7 × 2.5–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate and with an obtuse acumen, greyish brown to blackish brown and not glossy when dry adaxially, slightly pale when dry abaxially, both surfaces with many small glands; lateral veins slightly prominent abaxially. Thyrse axillary, 1 – 2 cm, usually 5 – 6-branched. Flowers sessile, buds ca. 3.5 mm. Hypanthium obconic, ca. 3 mm, apex truncate. Calyx-lobes inconspicuous. Petals white, united into a calyptra. Stamens 3–4 mm. Style slender, as long as stamens. Fruit black, ellipsoidal-ovoid, 1.5–2 × ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1293; F. W. Xing 8492, 8684.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian.
Ecology: Secondary forests or fung shui woods. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Nov. – Jan.
Uses: Timber.

Tabebuia chrysantha (Jacq.) G. Nicholson 黃鐘木（風鈴木）
Ill. Dict. Gard. 4: 1. 1887.
Tabebuia chrysotricha (Mart ex DC.) Standl., Field Mus. Nat. Hist., Bot. Ser. 11(5): 176. 1936.

Small tree, semi‑deciduous, 5 – 10 m tall, erect, many‑branched, crown umbellate. Leaves opposite, palmately compound, with 4 – 5 leaflets, ovate, papery, margin serrate, covered with fine pubescence. Cyme terminal; flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, 5‑merous; calyx tube irregularly lobed; corolla golden yellow, funnelform; stamens 4, didynamous, attached to corolla, anther 2‑celled, splitting by longitudinal slits. Pistils 2, connate; ovary 2‑locular. Capsule linear, dehiscing loculicidally. Seeds winged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3283; HK sheet 34328, 39962.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tabernaemontana divaricata (L.) R. Br. ex Roem. & Schult. 狗牙花
Syst. 4: 427. 1819; FOC 16: 153. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 31. 1999.
Nerium divaricatum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753.
Ervatamia divaricata (L.) Burkill, Rec. Bot. Surv. India 10(2): 320. 1925; FRPS 63: 100. 1977; FGD 1: 450, fig. 504. 1987.

Shrubs or small trees, 0.5–5 m tall, glabrous. Petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade elliptic or narrowly so, 3–18 × 1 – 6 cm, apex acuminate; lateral veins 5–17 on each side of midvein. Cymes dichotomous, 1 – 8‑flowered; bracts scalelike. Flower buds with an ovoid head, apex acute or obtuse. Calyx lobes often ciliate. Corolla white; tube 1.5 – 2.7 cm; lobes simple or double, obovate or broadly so, 1.5–2.7 × 0.8 – 2 cm. Stamens inserted at basal third of corolla‑tube. Folliciles obliquely and narrowly ellipsoidal, 2–7 × 0.6 – 1.5 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated. C. P. Lau 102; Y. S. Lau 2006; HK sheet 31543.
Distribution: S Yunnan; cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tadehagi triquetrum (L.) H. Ohashi 葫蘆茶
Ginkgoana 1: 290. 1973; FRPS 41: 63. 1995; FGD 5: 279, fig. 149. 2003.
Hedysarum triquetrum L., Sp. Pl. 746. 1753.
Pteroloma triquetrum (L.) Desv. ex Benth., Pl. Jungh. 2: 220. 1852.
Desmodium triquetrum (L.) DC., Prodr. 2: 326. 1825; FHK 83. 1861; FKH 79. 1912.

Erect subshrub or shrub, 1 – 2 m tall. Young branchlets 3-angulate. Stipules lanceolate, 1.3–2 cm, striate. Leaves 1-foliolate; petioles 1–3 cm, winged, with 4–8 mm wide wings on each side; leaflets papery, narrow-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 5.8–13 × 1.1–3.5 cm, base rounded or shallow cordate, apex acute, glabrous adaxially, pubescent on veins abaxially, lateral veins 8–14 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal and axillary, 15–30 cm, covered with adpressed silky and hook-form hairs. Flowers 3–5 at each node. Calyx campanulate, 3 mm, lobes deltoid, lanceolate or linear. Corolla purplish or violet, 5 – 6 mm; vexillum suborbicular, emarginate; wings obovate, base auriculate; keel falcate. Stamens diadelphous. Pods oblong, 2–5 × 0.5 cm, densely yellow or white strigose, dorsal suture slightly constricted with 5 – 8 segments. Seeds broadly elliptic or elliptic, 2–3 × 1.5–2.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2090; Y. S. Lau 20, 2051.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian; tropical Asia, N Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, margins of forests. Flowering: Jun. –Oct.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tagetes erecta L. 萬壽菊
Sp. Pl. 887. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3–4): 176. 1968; FRPS 75: 389. 1979; FGD 8: 144, fig. 78. 2007.

Stout annual erect and branched herbs, 50–100 cm tall or more; stem striate, glabrous. Leaves opposite to alternate, odd‑pinnatifid, 5–15 × 4–8 cm, leaflets lanceolate‑oblong, lateral segments 4–7 pairs, margin serrate, apex acute, some teeth with long awns at tips when young, glandular‑dotted along the margin below the teeth. Capitula solitary and terminal to branches, 5–8 cm across; peduncle 5–10(–15) cm, the upper part cylindrically inflated. Involucres 1.5–2 × 0.7–1.5 cm, single series of phyllaries united as a cylindric‑campanulate tube with triangular lobes at top, glandular‑dotted. Florets yellow to dull orange in colour. Ray ones with fan‑shaped obovate ligule, 1.4–1.8 × 1.2–1.4 cm, apex broadly 2‑lobed, subtruncate and undulate, tube about 1 cm. Disk tubular florets 0.9 – 1.4 cm, apex deeply divided into 5 oblong‑ovate lobes, some cultivars with the limbs modified into ligules; anthers included, base truncate, apical appendages ovate‑acute; stylar branches elongate with appendages hairy on the abaxial surface. Cypselae linear‑oblong, 8–11 mm, compressed‑tetragonous, brownish black in colour, minutely hairy. Pappus of 1–2 lanceolate long‑awned scales and 2–3 short obtuse scales, sometimes together with some small hyaline linear scales.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7094, 13663 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to USA, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tagetes patula L. 孔雀草
Sp. Pl. 887. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3–4): 176. 1968; FRPS 75: 387. 1979; FGD 8: 144. 2007.

Annual herbs 30–100 cm tall; stem erect and branched. Leaves odd‑pinnatifid, 2–10 × 1.5–3 cm, leaflets linear‑lanceolate, margin serrate, teeth often with long awns at tips when young, glandular dotted along the margin below the teeth. Capitula solitary and terminal to branches, 3.5–5 cm across. Peduncle 5–6.5 cm, apical portion somewhat inflated. Involucres with single row of phyllaries united into a campanulate tube 1.2–1.5 × 0.6–0.7 cm, acute‑triangular toothed on top, glandular‑dotted. Ray florets bright yellow or orange, with maroon‑red patches, ligule suborbicular, 8–10 × 6–7 mm, retuse at apex. Disk tubular florets yellow, 1–1.4 cm, 5‑lobed. Cypselae linear, 8–12 mm, black, pubescent. Pappus of several scales, 1–2 of them long‑awned, 2–3 short and obtuse.

Locality: Cultivated. H. Y. Yeung 134, 177 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tainia dunnii Rolfe 帶唇蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 38: 368. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 67, fig. 33. 1977; FRPS 18: 237, pl. 40: 1–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1043, pl. 447. 2000; FGD 7: 407, fig. 208. 2006; FOC 25: 284. 2009.

Terrestrial perennial herb; rhizome short and thick, consisting of 4 joints; pseudobulbs dull dark green or dull purple, ovatelanceolate, 1.5–3(–7) cm long, 5–12 mm in diam. Leaf solitary, terminal to the pseudobulb; petiole short, 3–5 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 20–30 × 2–4 cm, attenuate at both ends, with 3 prominent veins running from base to apex. Flowers resupinate, up to 21 in a well-spaced raceme; sepals and petals dull purple, tinged yellow, similar in length and width, 10–15 × 2–3 mm; odd sepal linear, apex obtuse; lateral ones falcate-linear, base joined to the column foot forming a short mentum, apex obtuse; petals falcate-linear, apex obtuse or acute; lip attached to a short mentum, 1 cm, narrowed at the base, widening to a 3-lobed blade; lateral lobes erect, light yellow densely speckled with purple inside, flushed dull purple outside, triangular-ovate, 2 mm, obtuse; midlobe panduriform, bright yellow, 6 mm across, truncate, lightly produced and obtuse at middle, with 3 longitudinal creamy yellow ridges, 2 lateral ones higher and more fleshy; column arcuate, winged at both sides; anther resembling the head of a cat, bright reddish purple; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, ovary oblanceolate, glabrous.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 2988, 3097; HK sheet 34321.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests and ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

Talinum paniculatum (Jacq.) Gaertn. 土人參
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 219, t. 128. 1791; FGD 2: 92, fig. 64. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 337, 1. 155. 1996; FRPS 26: 42, pl. 8: 6 –11. 1996; FOC 5: 444. 2003.

Perennial herb, 30 –70 cm tall, with thick roots, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, little branched. Leaves alternate or sub‑opposite, short stalked or subsessile; leaf blade obovate, obovate-oblanceolate or elliptic, 4–12 × 2– 4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire. Inflorescence a terminal thyrse, to 18 cm, usually dichotomous. Pedicels 5 – 10 mm. Sepals 2, ovate, purplish red, 1–3 mm, caducous. Petals 5, pink to light purplish red, oblong obovate or elliptic, 6 –12 mm. Stamens 10–20. Ovary globose, 1-locular; style 3-lobed. Capsule globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., opening by 3 valves.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong, cultivated or naturalized. H. C. Tang 1953; HK sheet 36018.
Distribution: Cultivated and sometimes naturalized in C & S China. Native to tropical America; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Usually cultivated as a pot plant, sometimes escaped, growing on waste places. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Tamarindus indica L. 酸豆
Sp. Pl. 1: 34. 1753; FHN 2: 235. 1965; FTW 3: 389. 1977; FRPS 39: 217, pl. 76. 1988; FGD 5: 202, fig. 117. 2003; FGX 2: 495, pl. 211. 2005.

Tree, 10–15(–25) m tall. Bark dark grey, irregularly fissured. Leaflets 10–20 pairs, oblong, 1.3–2.8 × 0.5–0.9 cm, base rounded, oblique, apex rounded or emarginate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences few-flowered. Peduncles and pedicels yellowish green pubescent. Bracteoles 2, ca. 1 cm, firmly enclosing the buds before flowering. Calyx-tube ca. 7 mm, lobes lanceolate-oblong, ca. 1.2 cm, reflexed after flowering. Petals yellow or mixed with purplish red stripes, obovate, as long as calyx-lobes, margin wavy wrinkled. Fertile stamens 1.2–1.5 cm, hairy near base, free parts of filaments ca. 7 mm; anthers ellipsoidal, ca. 2.5 mm. Ovary terete, ca. 8 mm, slightly curved, hairy. Pods terete-cylindrical, brown, 5–14 cm, straight or curved, often irregularly constricted. Seeds 3–14, brown, glossy.

Locality: Aberdeen, Deep Water Bay, Tai Wai, Peng Chau (cultivated). P. S. Choi 490; Y. W. Lam 981; HK sheet 8685.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; native to Africa, cultivated in tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Dec. –May.
Uses: Edible (pods).

Tamarix chinensis Lour. 檉柳
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 182, pl. 24. 1790; FRPS 50(2): 157, pl. 43: 1–7. 1990. FGD 4: 133, fig. 82. 2000.
Tamarix gallica L. var. chinensis (Lour.) Ehrenb., Linnaea 2: 267. 1827.

Small tree or shrub, 3–6 m; old branches erect, bark reddish brown, fine striate; young branches slender, pendulous, dark purplish red or dark brown. Leaves scalelike, subulate or ovate-lanceolate, 1–3 mm, base attenuate, apex acuminate and incurved, keeled abaxially. Racemes lateral on the apex of current year branches, often clustered in large panicles. Flower pink; bract linear-subulate, as long as or slightly longer than pedicel; pedicel slender, shorter than calyx. Calyx lobes 5, narrowly ovate, 0.7–1.3 mm. Petals 5, obovate, ca. 2 mm, persistent. Stamens 5, longer than petals, filaments inserted between disc lobes, exserted. Disc fleshy, 5–10-lobed. Ovary conical, styles 3, clavate. Capsule conical, 3 mm long, dehiscing into 3 valves; seeds minute, apex with a bundle of hair.

Locality: cultivated. P. S. Choi 341; HK sheet 2654, 33473
Distribution: Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Henan, Hebei, Liaoning; widely cultivated in E, S & SW China.
Ecology: Seasides, sandy places and wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Taraxacum officinale F. H. Wigg. 藥用蒲公英
Prim. Fl. Holsat. 56. 1780; FKH 150. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. Jn. Taiwan Mus. 22: 657. 1969; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1079. 1998; FRPS 80(2): 50. 1999.
Taraxacum dens‑leonis Desf., Fl. Atlant. 2: 228. 1799; FHK 192. 1861.

Perennial herbs; scapes erect and hollow, 5–40 cm tall, glabrous or cobwebby on upper portion, base usually tinged purple‑red. Leaves oblanceolate, 4–20 × 1–7 cm, or much larger, runcinate‑pinnatilobed to pinnatifid, apical lobes usually larger, triangular or triangular‑hastate, acute or obtuse; lateral lobes 4–7 pairs, triangular to triangular‑lanceolate, downward‑pointing, margin irregularly toothed; leaf base sometimes tinged purple‑red, both surfaces glabrous or sparsely arachnoid hairy along veins. Capitula 2.5–5 cm across, homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, solitary at scape terminal. Involucres broadly campanulate; phyllaries green, apex acuminate, without prominent horn‑like structure near apex or slightly thickened along midvein; outer involucral bracts 1–2 rows, lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–3.5 mm, reflexed at flowering stage; inner ones in 1 row, linear‑lanceolate, 16–25 × 1.2–1.5 mm, erect at first and later reflexed at fruiting stage. Ligulate florets yellow in colour, ligule 5‑toothed apically. Cypselae pale brown, obovate‑oblong, 3–4 × 0.8–1.2 mm, ribbed and sharply tuberculate along ribs on upper half, lower half slightly and obtusely roughened, apex forming a narrow pyramidal tubercle 0.4–0.6 mm, subtending the apical filiform beak with length 6–12 mm. Pappus white, 5–6 mm, growing on the beak, like a parachute.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2508; L. T. Lo 653; P. S. Choi 127.
Distribution: Xinjiang; Kirghizstan, Kazakstan, Europe and N America.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Taraxacum mongolicum Hand.‑Mazz. previously (Check List HK Plants 288. 2002; 98. 2004).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Taraxacum mongolicum Hand.‑Mazz. previously (Check List HK Plants 288. 2002; 98. 2004).

records.text:
Cleome hassleriana Chodat 醉蝶花
Bull. Herb. Boissier 6 (App. I): 12. 1898.
Cleome spinosa auct. non Jacq.: FGZ 109, fig. 41. 1956; FGD 1: 82, fig. 87. 1987; FRPS 32: 534. 1999.

Annual herb, 1–1.5 m tall, disagreeably scented. Stems erect, with glandular hairs and spiny stipules. Leaves digitately compound; petioles 2– 8 cm, often with yellowish prickles; leaflets 5 –7, elliptic-lanceolate or oblanceolate, the middle one larger, 6 –10 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, hairy on both surfaces. Racemes terminal, to 40 cm, densely covered with viscid glandular hairs. Bract leafy, ovate-oblong, 5 –20 mm, sessile or nearly so, base ± cordate. Pedicels 2–3 cm, with short glandular hairs. Sepals 4, oblongelliptic, ca. 6 mm. Petals pink or white, oblanceolate-spathulate,10 –15 × 4– 6 mm; claw 5–12 mm. Stamens 6; filaments 3.5– 4 cm. Gynophore 4 –5 cm. Ovary cylindrical, 3 – 4 mm, glabrous; style very short. Capsule cylindrical, 5– 6.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 1752.
Distribution: Native to tropical America; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tarenna attenuata (Voigt) Hutch. 假桂烏口樹（達侖木）
Pl. Wilson. 3(2): 411. 1916; FHN 3: 317. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 382, pl. 100: 12 – 15. 1999; FYN 15: 188, pl. 38: 5 – 7. 2003; FGD 6: 190, fig. 100. 2005.
Stylocoryna attenuata Voigt, Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 377. 1845.
Stylocoryna webera auct. non A. Rich.: FHK 156. 1861.
Webera attenuata Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 3(7): 104. 1880; FKH 130. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs or trees, 1–8 m tall, quite glabrous. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; stipules 5–8 mm, united at the base, apex acuminate; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, oblong‑oblanceolate, oblanceolate or obovate, 4.5–1.5 × 1.5–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or abruptly and shortly acuminate, margin entire, ± shining adaxially, turning black when dry, glabrous, or sometimes with short hairs in axils of veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins slender, 5 – 10 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform, trichotomous, 4–6 cm in diam., shorter than the leaves. Pedicels 2–5 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 2 mm; lobes triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white or yellowish; tube 2–2.5 mm, hairy on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, ca. 5 mm. Style ca. 8 mm; stigma exserted. Berry globular, 5–7 mm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Wai, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. Y. S. Lau 2727; P. S. Choi 513, 532.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, India.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jun. of the following year; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tarenna mollissima (Hook. & Arn.) B. L. Rob. 白花苦燈籠（烏口樹）
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts, 45(17): 405. 1910; FHN 3: 318, fig. 745. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 376, pl. 99: 6 – 10. 1999; FYN 15: 190, pl. 38: 8 – 10. 2003; FGD 6: 189. 2005.
Stylocoryna mollissima Walp., Repert. Bot. Syst. 2: 517. 1843; FHK 156. 1861.
Webera mollissima Benth. ex Hance, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 13: 105. 1873; FKH 130. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 1 – 6 m tall, softly and densely pubescent in every part. Leaves papery; petioles 0.4 – 2.5 cm; stipules 5 – 8 mm, ovate‑triangular, united at the base, apex pointed; leaf blade lanceolate, oblong‑lanceolate, or ovate‑elliptic, 5 – 16( – 25) × 2 – 6( – 10) cm, base cuneate, acute or obtuse, apex acuminate or long‑acuminate, margin entire, turning black in drying; lateral veins 8 – 12 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform, trichotomous. Pedicels 3 – 6 mm. Calyx‑tube ± bell‑shaped, ca. 2 mm; lobes triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white; tube 4 – 5 mm, densely pubescent on the throat; lobes 4 or 5, oblong, about the length of the tube or slightly longer, recurved in anthesis. Style ca. 8 mm; stigma exserted. Berry globular, 5 – 7 mm in diam., pubescent, black when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Pik Uk, Luk Wu. L. T. Lo 111; P. S. Choi 213; Y. W. Lam 1754.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Jul. – Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Taxillus chinensis (DC.) Danser 廣寄生
Bull. Jard. Bot. Buitenzorg, sér. 3. 16: 40. 1938; FGD 1: 223, fig. 251. 1987; FRPS 24: 131, pl. 29: 1 – 6. 1988; FOC 5: 237. 2003.
Loranthus chinensis DC., Coll. Mem. 6: 28, pl. 7. 1830.
Loranthus parasiticus auct. non Merr.: FGZ 411, fig. 215. 1956; FHN 2: 461. 1965.

Shrub 0.5–1 m tall; young branchlets and leaves rusty stellate-tomentose, later glabrescent, greyish brown, lenticellate. Leaves opposite or subopposite; petiole 8 – 10 mm; leaf blade papery, ovate, 3–6 × 2.5 –4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein, slightly conspicuous. Umbels 1–2 together, 1–4-flowered; peduncle 2–4 mm, stellate hairy; bracts triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Pedicel 6–7 mm. Calyx ellipsoidal or ovoid, ca. 2 mm, limb annular. Corolla tubular, 2.5–2.7 cm, tip enlarged, ovoid, brownish, slightly curved, covered with stellate hairs, basal part inflated, lobes spatulate, ca. 6 mm, reflexed. Filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers ca. 3 mm, multilocellate. Style red; stigma capitate. Fruit yellowish, ellipsoidal or subglobose, 8–10 × 5–6 mm, densely verrucose when young, becoming smooth when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1365; HK sheet 35360, 35361.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; SE Asia.
Ecology: Often growing on trees of Camellia oleifera, Vernicia spp., Dimocarpus longan. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Taxodium distichum (L.) Rich. 落羽杉
Ann. Nat. Hist. 16: 298. 1810; FRPS 7: 304, pl. 70: 1–3. 1978; FOC 4: 58. 1999; FGD 4: 22, fig. 13. 2000.

Deciduous tree, to 50 m tall, 2 m in d.b.h. in native habitat; pneumatophores present or absent around trunk; trunk swollen and buttressed at base, strongly tapered upward; bark brown, peeling off in long strips; main branches spreading horizontally or ascending; lateral branchlets 2-ranked. Leaves linear, flat, base twisted, 2-ranked on annual branchlets, 1–1.5 cm × 1 mm, apex acute, pale green, midvein depressed adaxially, yellowish green or greyish green, midvein raised abaxially, stomatal lines 4–8 on each side. Pollen cones borne in terminal, crowded, short, dense racemes or panicles 5–12 cm, shortly pedunculate, ovoid. Seed cones brownish yellow or white powdery, globose, oblong-globose, or ovoid, ca. 2.5 cm in diam.; cone scales shield-shaped, woody, ± conspicuously longitudinally grooved at apex. Seeds brown or reddish brown, irregularly triangular-pyramidal, 1.2–1.8 cm long, sharply ridged.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1705; HK sheet 34504.
Distribution: Introduced to Guangdong, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Hubei, Henan. Native to SE region of N America.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: (Jul.–)Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tecoma stans (L.) Juss. ex Kunth 黃鐘花
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 3: 144. 1818 [1819]; FGZ 610. 1956; FFJ 5: 89, fig. 98. 1993.
Bignonia stans L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 871. 1763.
Stenolobium stans (L.) Seem., Ann. Mag. Nat. Hist. 10: 30. 1862; FYN 2: 706. 1979; FRPS 69: 55, pl. 15: 4 – 6. 1990.

Erect shrub to 6 m. Leaves odd‑pinnately compound, 10–20 cm; leaflets 3–13, sessile or subsessile, oblong‑ovate to lanceolate, 4–10 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrate, subglabrous adaxially, densely grey tomentose abaxially. Inflorescences racemose‑paniculate to 15 cm. Peduncles, pedicels, bracteoles and calyx hairy. Bracts subulate, ca. 1 mm. Calyx campanulate, 5‑dentate. Corolla yellow to orange‑yellow, tube narrowed at base, lobes 5, spreading, wavy at margin; anthers hairy. Ovary terete; style slender, stigma 2‑lobed, lobes lingulate. Capsules 8–10 × 0.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1623.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to America, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tectona grandis L. f. 柚木
Suppl. Pl. 151. 1781 [1782]; FGZ 632. 1956; FHN 4: 25, fig. 956. 1977; FYN 1: 415, pl. 99: 3 – 4. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 80, fig. 41. 1982; FFJ 4: 534. 1989; FOC 17: 16. 1994; FGD 3: 361, fig. 235. 1995.

Tree to 40 m tall. Branchlets grey to greyish brown, tetragonal and sulcate, yellowish to greyish brown stellate tomentose. Petiole robust, 2–4 cm or longer; leaf blade papery, ovate‑elliptic to ovate, 15–50 × 8–25 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acuminate to obtuse, adaxially scabrous and puberulent along veins, abaxially densely greyish brown to yellowish brown minutely stellate tomentose; lateral veins 7–12 pairs, veinlets subparallel, evidently prominent abaxially. Panicles 25–40 × 30 cm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx‑tube 2–3 mm, white stellate tomentose, limb slightly shorter than calyx‑tube. Corolla white; tube 2.5–3 mm, abaxially puberulent and glandular; lobes ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary strigose. Style 3–4 mm. Drupes globose, 1.2–1.8 cm in diam., minutely tomentose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2934; K. C. Chau 3330; HK sheet 34486.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated or naturalized); native to India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore).

Telosma cordata (Burm. f.) Merr. 夜來香
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 19: 372. 1921; FRPS 63: 438, pl. 163. 1977; FGD 1: 514, fig. 586. 1987; FOC 16: 241. 1995.
Asclepias cordata Burm. f., Fl. Indica 72, fig. 2. 1768.

Lianas frutescent, latex white. Stems 1–10 m, yellowish green, pubescent when young, pale grey, glabrescent and usually sparsely lenticellate in age. Petioles 1.5–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 4–12 × 3–10 cm, base deeply cordate with narrow sinus, apex acuminate, basal veins 3, lateral veins 6 on each side of midvein. Cymes umbel‑like, 15–30‑flowered. Peduncle 0.5–1.5 cm, puberulent. Sepals oblong‑lanceolate, puberulent. Corolla yellowish green; tube 6–10 × 4–6 mm, puberulent outside, pilose or glabrous with pilose throat inside; lobes oblong 6–12 × 3–6 mm, ciliate. Corona‑lobes slightly fleshy, basal part ovate, apex acuminate, often notched to deeply lobed, internal appendage often longer than lobe proper. Pollinia oblong or reniform. Stigma head capitate. Follicles lanceolate in outline, 7–13 × 2–3.5 cm, glabrous, somewhat obtusely 4‑angled. Seeds broadly ovate, 1 × 1 cm, flat, apex truncate, margin membranous; coma 3–4 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1276, 2999; Y. W. Lam 1127.
Distribution: Native to S China; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia, Europe and America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Food (flowers edible), ornamental.

Tephrosia purpurea (L.) Pers. 灰毛豆（紅花灰葉）
Syn. Pl. 2(2): 329. 1807; FHK 78. 1861; FKH 76. 1912; FRPS 40: 219. 1994; FGD 5: 248, fig. 137. 2003.

Subshrub, 30 – 60 cm tall, many-branched, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves odd-pinnate, 7 – 15 cm; leaflets 4 – 8 pairs, elliptic-oblong or oblong-oblanceolate, 1.5 – 3.5 × 0.5 – 1.4 cm, apex obtuse or emarginate and mucronate, glabrous adaxially, adpressed pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 7 – 12 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal or axillary, 10 – 15 cm. Flowers 2–4-clustered. Calyx broadly campanulate, 3 – 4 mm, pubescent, teeth subequal. Corolla purplish, ca. 8 mm; vexillum suborbicular, pubescent abaxially; wings and keels oblong. Ovary densely pubescent. Pods 4 – 5 × 0.4 cm, sparsely adpressed pubescent. Seeds 6 – 10, grey-brown with red-brown spots; elliptic, 3–5 mm.

Locality: Cape D’ Aguilar. (fide FKH 76. 1912).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in the tropics.
Ecology: Seashores. Flowering: Mar. – Oct.
Uses: Green manure.

Tephrosia vestita Vogel 黄灰毛豆（黃毛灰葉）
Nova Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 15. 1843; FKH 76. 1912; FRPS 40: 217. 1994; FGD 5: 247, fig. 136. 2003.

Subshhrub, 1 –2 m tall. Young branches angulate, densely yellow-white tomentose. Leaves odd-pinnate, ca. 10 cm; leaflets 3 –5(–6) pairs, obovate-elliptic to oblong, 2 – 4 × 1 – 1.8 cm, base cuneate, apex rounded or emarginate, glabrous adaxially, densely silky hairy abaxially, lateral veins 15–20 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal or leaf-opposed at branch end, ca. 6 cm. Flowers 23-clustered at nodes of rachis. Calyx ca. 3 mm, densely yellow pubescent abaxially, teeth triangular, lower one longer. Corolla white; vexillum suborbicular, ca. 1.5 cm, densely yellow pubescent abaxially; wings obovate-oblong; keel ovate. Ovary densely sericeous. Pods straight, 5.5– 6 × 0.5 cm, densely sericeous, suture thickened. Seeds 10 – 12, black, reniform.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 6859.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi; SE Asia to New Guinea.
Ecology: Thin forests or grassy slopes. Flowering: Jun.– Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Terminalia arjuna Wight & Arn. 阿江欖仁
Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 34. 1834.

Large tree, 15–20 m tall; bark greyish white, exfoliating in flakes; branches alternate, spreading. Leaves subopposite; petioles shorter than 1.2 cm, with 1 pair of glands near apex; leaf blade thickly papery, oblong or elliptic, 10 – 15(–25) × 5 – 10 cm, base cordate, asymmetrical, apex obtuse or very shortly acute, margin slightly undulate to subentire, densely papillate adaxially, subglabrous abaxially, lateral veins 15 – 22 pairs, conspicuous on both surfaces. Bracteoles very small. Calyx-teeth nearly glabrous on both surfaces. Ovary short, densely covered with crisped brown or rusty hairs. Fruit obovoid, 2– 2.6 cm in diam., ridged, wings usually truncate or suddenly narrowed at top.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. P. S. Choi 143; HK sheet 40698.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong, Taiwan; native to India and Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Ornamental (roadside tree).

Terminalia catappa L. 欖仁樹
Mant. Pl. 1: 128. 1767; FHN 2: 42, fig. 311. 1965; FTW 3: 387, pl. 851. 1977; FRPS 53(1): 10. 1984; FGD 3: 198, fig. 136: 4–6. 1995.

Tree, to 20 m or taller; bark brown; branches spreading, densely yellowish brown tomentose. Leaves alternate, often fasciculate at branch apex. Petiole robust, 1–1.5 cm, rusty pubescent when young; leaf blade obovate or elliptic-obovate, 12 – 25 × 8 – 15 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, with one pair of glands near margin, apex rotund or mucronate, margin entire or slightly wavy, pilose abaxially when young, glabrescent; midvein impressed adaxially and elevated abaxially, lateral veins 10–12 on each side of midvein. Flowers polygamous, in axillary spikes, small, 5-merous. Calyx-tube white villous adaxially, lobes as long as tube. Stamens exserted. Disk 5-glanded, hairy. Ovary small, 2-ovuled. Fruit fusiform or ellipsoidal, 3 – 5 cm, 2– 3.5 cm in diam., greenish black when mature, slightly compressed, 2-ribbed, narrowly winged on ribs.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 662, 989; L. T. Lo 384.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Taiwan; Indochina, Malaysia, India, Polynesia, S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Terminalia chebula Retz. 訶子
Observ. Bot. 5: 31. 1789; FGZ 225. 1956; FYN 1: 82, pl. 22: 1 – 2. 1977; FRPS 53(1): 13, pl. 3: 1 – 2. 1984; FGD 3: 199, fig. 136: 7 –9. 1995.

Large tree, to 30 m tall; bark brownish black, greyish black or greyish brown, often fissured, glabrous, with elliptic lenticels. Leaves subopposite or alternate; petioles robust, 1.8 – 2.3(–3) cm, with 1–2 pairs of glands at apex; leaf blade subleathery or thickly papery, ovate or ovate-elliptic to long elliptic, 7–14 × 4.5–8.5 cm, base rounded or cuneate, slightly oblique, apex acute, margin entire or minutely wavy, densely tuberculate on both surfaces, glabrous or slightly puberulous abaxially when young; lateral veins 6–10 pairs. Panicles composed of spikes, 5–10 cm. Flowers bisexual. Calyx-tube cupular, yellowish brown pubescent adaxially. Stamens exserted. Ovary small, 2-ovuled. Fruit fusiform or ovoid, 2.5 – 4 × 1.9 – 2.3 cm; pericarp rigid, green when mature, often ridged.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1702, 2847.
Distribution: Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and Malaysia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul.– Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Terminalia mantaly H. Perrier 小葉欖仁
Ann. Inst. Bot.-Geol. Colon. Marseille, ser. 7, 1: 24, t. 5. 1953.

Tree, to 10 m tall; bark blackish brown; branches pseudoverticillate, horizontally spreading. Leaves often 3–7-fasciculate on apex of short branches; petioles ca. 0.5 cm; leaf blade papery, obovate, 3–5 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate, margin sparsely crenate, glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 5–7 pairs, inconspicuous. Inflorescences 8– 10 cm. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 40662, 40745.
Distribution: Cultivated in S China; native to Madagascar.
Uses: Ornamental (roadside tree).

Ternstroemia gymnanthera (Wight & Arn.) Beddome 厚皮香
Fl. Sylv. 19. 1871; FHN 1: 504. 1964; FGD 2: 161. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 11. 1998.
Cleyera gymnanthera Wight & Arnott, Prodr. Pl. Ind. Occ. 87. 1834.
Ternstroemia japonica auct. non Thunb.: Benth., FHK 27. 1861; FKH 43. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout. Leaves leathery; petiole 5 –10 mm; leaf blade obovate to broadly elliptic, 5 –10 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin entire, dark green and shining adaxially, light green becoming reddish brown when dry abaxially, midvein impressed adaxially, lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein. Flowers andro-dioecious, axillary; pedicels 1.5 –3 cm; bracteoles 2, ovate, ca. 2 mm, margin glandular dentate, apex acute; sepals ovate or oblong-ovate, 4– 5 × 3 – 4 mm, glabrous, apex rounded, margin glandular dentate; petals obovate, 6 – 8 × 4 – 6 mm, apex rounded or retuse; stamens 4 – 5 mm; anthers oblong, longer than filaments; ovary ovoid, 2-locular with 2 ovules per locule; style short, 2-lobed. Fruit purplish red when mature, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., 2-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule. Seeds reniform, ca. 6 × 4 mm, with red aril.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2363; Y. S. Lau 2556; K. L. Yip 4451.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and shrublands. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ternstroemia kwangtungensis Merr. 廣東厚皮香（厚葉厚皮香）
Philip. J. Sci. 13: 148. 1918; FGD 2: 161. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 5. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, 4 – 5 m tall; branchlets stout, greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves thickly leathery; petioles stout, 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade broadly elliptic to obovate, 7–12 × 3 – 6 cm, apex abruptly acute, tip blunt, base broadly cuneate to obtuse, margin entire, glabrous, dark green and shining adaxially, light green and densely reddish brown or brown punctuate abaxially; midvein raised adaxially, plane or slightly impressed abaxially, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or in pairs, white; pedicels 1.5–2 cm, slightly recurved, glabrous. Male flowers: bracteoles 2, ovate to triangular-ovate, 4– 5 × 3 mm, margin sparsely glandular dentate; sepals ovate to suborbicular, 6 – 8 mm in diam., glabrous, margin glandular dentate, apex rounded; petals obovate to oblong-obovate, ca. 10 × 8 mm, apex rounded; stamens many, ca. 6 mm; anther ovate, ca. 3 mm; pistillode very small. Female flowers: bracteoles 2, obovate or triangular obovate, ca. 3 × 4 mm; sepals suborbicular, 6 –7 mm in diam.; ovary 3 –4(– 5) locular, glabrous, styles 3 – 4(– 5)-lobed, 6 –7 mm long. Fruit baccate, depressed-globose, 1.5 –1.8 × 1.5 –2 cm, 3 – 4(– 5)-locular, 1 seed per locule; bracteoles and sepals persistent. Seeds subreniform, 7– 8 × 6 mm, aril red.

Locality: Ping Fung Shan. Y. W. Lam 401, 499; F. W. Xing 9984.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and thickets on hillslopes and by streams.

Ternstroemia luteoflora L. K. Ling 尖萼厚皮香
FRPS 50(1): 183. 1998.

Tree; branchlets glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 5–11 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire and slightly revolute, glabrous, dark green and shining adaxially, light green and becoming reddish brown when dry abaxially, lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midvein. Flowers andro-dioecious, ca. 1.5 cm in diam; pedicels 2–3 cm, more or less incurved. Male flowers: bracteoles 2, ovate-lanceolate, ca. 3 × 2 mm, margin glandular dentate, apex acuminate; sepals ovatelanceolate, 5–7 × 3 – 4 mm, apex acuminate to long-acuminate, margin glandular ciliolate; petals 5, white or yellowish white, obovate or suborbicular, 8 –10 × 8 –10 mm, apex retuse; stamens 35 – 45, ca. 5 mm; anthers oblong, 2– 4 mm; pistillode small, flattened. Female flowers: bracteoles, sepals and petals as in male flower, ovary globose, 2-locular with 2 ovules per locule; style 2-lobed. Fruits globose, 1.5 –2 cm in diam., 2-locular with 2 seeds per locule, bracteoles and sepals persistent. Seeds reddish brown, ellipsoid, ca. 8 × 6 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Ping Fung Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Long Sai Wan. H. C. Tang 584; P. S. Choi 388; Y. W. Lam 244.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Ternstroemia microphylla Merr. 小葉厚皮香
Sunyatsenia 3: 254. 1937; FGD 2: 163. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 20. 1998.
Ternstroemia pseudoverticillata Merr. & Chun, Sunyatsenia 5: 131. 1940

Shrub or small tree; branchs greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery to thickly leathery; petioles ca. 3 mm, glabrous; leaf blade obovate, oblong-obovate, or oblanceolate, 2– 6 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acute, obtuse, or rounded, margin subentire or sparsely serrulate towards apex, green and shining adaxially, light green abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Flowers white, polygamous, axillary, solitary or several borne on leafless branchlets, 5–8 mm in diam; pedicels slender, 5–10 mm, glabrous. Bisexual flower: bracteoles ovate-triangular, ca. 1 mm, apex acute, marigns glandular dentate; sepals ovate-orbicular, 2–3 mm in diam., apex rounded, margin sparsely glandular dentate; petals broadly obovate, ca. 4 × 3.5 mm; stamens 35–45, ca. 3 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1.5 mm; ovary ovoid, 2-locular with 1 ovule per locule; style 2 mm, 2-lobed. Male flower: bracteoles, sepals, and petals as in bisexual flower; stamens 35–45; pistillode very small. Fruit ellipsoidal, 8–10 × 5–6 mm, 2-locular, with 1 seed per locule. Seeds long reniform, 5–7 mm long, aril red.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Wong Leng, Nam Chung, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 33; P. S. Choi 444; Y. W. Lam 400.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and shrublands. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Tetracera asiatica (Lour.) Hoogland 錫葉藤
Fl. Malesiana 1(4): 143. 1951; FHN 1: 446. 1964; FRPS 49(2): 191. 1984.
Segnieria asiatica Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 341. 1790.
Tetracera sarmentosa (L.) Vahl. subsp. asiatica (Lour.) Hoogland, Blumea 9: 588. 1959; FGD 3: 93. 1995.
Leontoglossum scabrum Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 18. 1851.
Dilima sarmentosa auct. non L.: FHK 7. 1861; FKH 27. 1912.

Woody vine, 3 – 5 m or more; branches scabrous, strigose. Petioles 0.5–1.0 cm; pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blade leathery, obovate to broadly lanceolate, 3 –15 × 2–7 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or serrate-crenuate, scabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–16 on each side of midvein, elevated abaxially. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, many-flowered; flower white, ca. 8 –10 mm. in diam.; pedicels 1–5 mm; bracts and bracteoles linear, sparsely pubescent abaxially, margin ciliate; sepals 5, suborbicular, margin ciliate, sparsely pubescent abaxially, the outer two 2 × 1.5 mm, the inner three 4 × 3 mm; petals 3; ovate, ca. 3.5 × 2.5 mm, membranaceous, glabrous; stamens numerous, 3– 4 mm, filaments filiform, dilated at the distal end; anther-cells slightly separated at the apex; carpels 1(–2), with ca. 10–12 ovules, glabrous. Follicles ovoid, 6–10 × 4 – 6 mm with a 2– 5 mm long beak, 1(–2)-seeded. Seeds ovoid, black, ca. 4 × 3 mm with an up to 5 mm fringe-margined aril.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 108.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Thailand, Vietnam, Malesia.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes and in ravines.

Tetradium glabrifolium (Champ. ex Benth.) T. G. Hartley 楝葉吳茱萸

Gard. Bull. Singapore 34: 109. 1981; FTW ed. 2, 3: 533, pl. 275. 1993.

Boymia glabrifolia Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 330. 1851.

Evodia glabrifolia (Champ. ex Benth.) C. C. Huang, Guihaia 11(1): 9. 1991.

Euodia glabrifolia (Champ. ex Benth.) D. D. Tao, FYN 6: 730. 1995, nom. illeg.

Megabotrya meliaefolia Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 259. 1852.

Ampacus meliaefolia (Hance ex Walp.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 98. 1891.

Evodia meliifolia (Hance ex Walp.) Benth., FHK 58. 1861, ‘meliaefolia’; FKH 55. 1912, ‘meliaefolia’.


Tree, to 20 m tall. Bark greyish white, densely covered with orbicular, slightly prominent lenticels. Leaves (5–)7–11-foliolate; petiolule (0.6–)1–1.5(–2) cm; leaflet blade ovate-lanceolate, strongly asymmetrical, 6–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin subentire and wavy, glandular dots inconspicuous, glabrous on both surfaces, greyish green abaxially. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered. Calyx (4–)5-lobed, small. Petals (4–)5, white, ca. 3 mm. Male flower: filaments villous at lower half; pistillode clavate, 4–5-lobed at apex. Female flower: staminodes scale-like. Fruit purplish red, glandular-dotted. Follicles ca. 5 mm in diam., 1-seeded. Seed 4 × 3.5 mm, brownish black.


Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Po, Bride's Pool, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2308; N. H. Li 145; HK sheet 40665.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan.

Ecology: Secondary forests or thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Medicinal (folklore).

Tetragonia tetragonioides (Pall.) Kuntze 番杏
Rev. Gen. 264. 1891; FGD 2: 89, fig. 62. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 331, pl. 153, photo 142–143. 1996; FRPS 26: 35, pl. 7: 5 –7. 1996; FOC 5: 440. 2003.
Demidovia tetragonioides Pall., Enum. Pl. 150, t. 1. 1781.
Tetragonia expansa Murr., Comm. Goett. 6: 13. 1783; FKH 114. 1912.

Annual succulent herb, glabrous, often with small tubercles. Stems thick, terete or slightly angled, initially erect, later elongate and ascending, 30– 60 cm or longer. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.5 –2.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-rhombic or ovate-triangular, 4 –11 × 1– 5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subtruncate, decurrent, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire or undulate. Flowers solitary or in cluster or 2–3, axillary. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx-tube 1.5 –2 mm; lobes 3 – 5, yellowish green adaxially, 2–3 mm. Stamens 4 –10; filaments yellow, 1–1.5 mm. Nutlet turbinate, 0.5 –1 cm, 4 – 5-angled.

Locality: Stanley, Lan Nai Wan, Lung Kwu Tan, Tai O. Y. W. Lam 814, 1523; HK sheet 2054.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; E Asia, Malesia, Australia, New Zealand, S America; cultivated and naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Sandy seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Tetrapanax papyriferus (Hook.) K. Koch. 通脫木
Wochenschr. Gartnerei Pflanzenk. 2: 371. 1859; FRPS 54: 13, pl. 2: 1–6. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 3: 1006, pl. 503. 1993.
Aralia papyrifera Hook., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 50, 53, pl. 1 – 2. 1852.
Fatsia papyrifera (Hook.) Benth. & Hook. f. ex Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23(156): 341. 1888.

Evergreen shrub or treelet, 1–3 m tall; branchlets and inflorescence densely tawny stellate-tomentose. Leaves large, crowded towards to apex of stems; petioles stout, 30–50 cm, glabrous; stipules subulate, ca. 7.5 cm, adnate to the base of petiole, densely tomentose; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, 50–75 cm in diam., papery to subleathery, glabrous adaxially, densely rusty stellate-tomentose abaxially, palmately 7–12-lobed; lobes ovate to elliptic-ovate, apex acuminate, margin entire to coarsely toothed. Umbels many-flowered, 12 cm in diam., forming large terminal, compound panicle, up to 50 cm. Pedicels 3–5 mm. Calyx densely tomentose, ca. 1 mm, margin entire or nearly so. Petals 4(–5), yellowish white, triangular-ovate, ca. 2 mm, tomentose abaxially. Stamens 4–5, filaments 3 mm. Ovary 2-locular, styles 2, distinct. Fruit ca. 4 mm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 64; F. W. Xing 2348; Y. S. Lau 3044.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Jan.–Feb.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tetrastigma hemsleyanum Diels & Gilg 三葉崖爬藤（三葉青）
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29: 463. 1900; FHN 3: 23. 1974; FFJ 3: 384, fig. 271. 1987; FRPS 48(2): 122. 1998.
Tetrastigma alatum H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 528. 1963; FTW 3: 674. 1977.

Herbaceous vine. Branchlets slender, glabrous or sparsely pilose; tendrils unbranched. Leaves trifoliolate, rarely 5-foliolate; petioles 1.5–7.5 cm, petiolules winged adaxially, glabrous or sparsely pilose; leaflets papery, lanceolate, elliptic-lanceolate, or ovate-lanceolate, 3–11 × 1–4 cm, glabrous, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate rarely acute, margin sparsely denticulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral leaflets smaller, base oblique. Inflorescence a dichasium, composed of several to many umbels, 1–5 cm; peduncle 1.2–2.5 cm, pubescent. Pedicels 1–2.5 mm, pilose. Calyx dentate at apex, with fine, ovate-triangular teeth. Petals ovate, 1.3–1.8 mm, apex corniculate, glabrous. Anthers yellow. Disk conspicuous, 4-lobed. Ovary conical, base adnate to disk; style short; stigma 4-lobed. Berry globose, ca. 7 mm in diam., 1-seeded, black when mature.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Davis, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 761, 842; HK sheet 40041.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India.
Ecology: Thickets or forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tetrastigma planicaule (Hook. f.) Gagnep. 扁擔藤（崖爬藤）
Notul. Syst. (Paris) 1: 319. 1910; FHN 3: 25, t. 542. 1974; FFJ 3: 384. 1987; FRPS 48(2): 109. 1998.
Vitis planicaulis Hook. f., Bot. Mag. 94: t. 5685. 1868; FKH 65. 1912.

Woody vine, glabrous except petals. Stems flattened. Branchlets terete or slightly flat; tendrils unbranched. Leaves palmately 5-foliolate; petioles 3–11 cm; leaflets elliptic-lanceolate, or ovate-lanceolate, 6–20 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin dentate; lateral leaflets smaller, base oblique. Inflorescence umbelliform, 15–17 cm; peduncle 3–6 cm. Pedicels 0.3–1 cm, glabrous or sparsely pilose. Calyx shallow and saucer-shaped, papillose, teeth inconspicuous. Petals ovate-triangular, 2–2.5 mm, apex galeate, sparsely papillose. Anthers yellow. Disk well-developed, 4-lobed, or inconspicuous in female flowers. Ovary broadly conical; style inconspicuous; stigma 4-lobed. Berry globose, 2–3 cm in diam., usually 2-seeded.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. C. Ford 1196; Y. S. Lau 555; HK sheet 40379.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; Laos, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, India.
Ecology: Forests of valleys and crevices of rocks. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Teucrium quadrifarium Buch.‑Ham. 鐵軸草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 108–109. 1825; FHK 280. 1861; FKH 212. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 40, pl. 6. 1977; FOC 17: 59. 1994.

Subshrubs, 30–100 cm tall; stems and branches rusty villous or hirsute. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–1.5 cm, the uppermost leaves subsessile; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to very narrowly ovate, 3–8 × 1.5–4 cm, base truncate or cordate, often oblique, apex bluntly acute, margin serrulate, pubescent and slightly rugose adaxially, villous along veins abaxially. Verticillasters forming terminal and axillary raceme‑like inflorescence and rearranged in panicles of 7–10 cm; axis villous. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 3–5 mm, 10‑veined, villous, 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑toothed, the middle lobe large, oblate‑orbicular, the lateral 2 lobes much smaller, triangular. Corolla pink, 1.2–1.3 cm, pubescent abaxially, with a ring of hairs at the throat, limb seemly 1‑lipped, the middle lobe obovate‑orbicular, lateral lobes ovate‑oblong. Stamens exserted. Style equaling stamens. Nutlets obovoid‑globose, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Deep Water Bay, Ng Kwai Shan. Y. S. Lau 2351; HK sheet 39830, 40883.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Nepal, India, Myanmar to Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.; fruitig: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Teucrium viscidum Blume 血見愁
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14: 827. 1825; FRPS 65(2): 31. 1977; FGD 3: 389, fig. 247. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 545, pl. 250. 1998.
Teucrium stoloniferum Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 3. 1832, nom. illeg., non Teucrium stoloniferum Ruiz & Pav. (1814).
Teucrium stoloniferum Hamilt. ex Benth. in Wall., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 1: 58. 1830; FHK 279. 1861; FKH 212. 1912.
Teucrium japonicum Willd in DC. Prodr. 12: 581.

Perennial herbs, 30–70 cm tall, stoloniferous; stems and branches glandular pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–3 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑oblong, 3–7(–10) × 2.5–4 cm, base rounded, broadly cuneate or cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin crenate, subglabrous or very sparsely puberulent on both surfaces. Verticillasters forming terminal and axillary raceme‑like inflorescence of 3–7 cm, viscous; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, 10‑veined, glandular pubescent, limb subequally 5‑toothed. Corolla white, pink tinged with blue, 6–8 mm, limb seemly 1‑lipped, the middle lobe suborbicular, lateral lobes ovate‑triangular. Stamens exserted. Style equaling stamens. Nutlets depressed ovoid or globose, ca. 1.3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 123; Y. S. Lau 2759, 3137.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Myanmar, India to Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places in ravines, thin forests, roadside. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Thalictrum acutifolium (Hand.-Mazz.) Boivin 尖葉唐松草（白蓬草）
Rhodora 46: 364. 1944; Ico. Cor. Sin. 1: 677. 1972; FRPS 27: 553. 1979; FOC 6: 285. 2001; FGD 5: 19. 2003.
Thalictum clavatum auct. non DC.: FKH 26. 1912.
Thalictrum clavatum DC. var. acutifolium Hand.-Mazz., Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl., Anz. 43: 1. 1926.

Perennial herb, 20–40 cm tall, glabrous. Roots fleshy, carrotshaped, to 4 mm in diam. Basal leaves 2–3, long petiolate, biternate; terminal leaflets long stalked, ovate, 1–1.4 × 0.8–3.5 cm, base rounded, broadly cuneate or cordate, apex acute or obtuse, entire or obscurely lobed, margin sparsely dentate, glaucous abaxially; lateral leaflets smaller; petiolule ca. 1.2 cm. Cauline leaves smaller, shortly petiolate. Cymes lax-flowered. Flowers small, ca. 8 mm in diam. Sepals 4, ovate, ca. 2 mm, white or pinkish, caducous. Stamens numerous, ca. 5 mm; anthers oblong, 0.8–1.3 mm; filaments distally oblanceolate, ca. 3 times as broad as anthers, base filiform. Carpels 6–12, stalked; styles short. Achenes compressed, narrowly oblong, sometimes slightly falcate, 3–4 × 0.6–1.2 mm, longitudinally 8-ribbed.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 1401; P. S. Choi 36.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.–Jul.

Thelasis pygmaea (Griff.) Blume 矮柱蘭
Fl. Jav. Orch. 23. 1858; FRPS 19: 62. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1046, pl. 448. 2000; FOC 25: 366. 2009.
Euproboscis pygmaea Griff., Calc. J. Nat. Hist. 5: 731, t. 26. 1845.
Thelasis hongkongensis Rolfe, Kew Bull. 199. 1896, et J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 39. 1903; FKH 267. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 76, fig. 39. 1977.

Saxicolous herb; pseudobulbs compressed, globose, growing close together, 7–11 mm in diam. Leaves terminal, solitary, leathery, oblong or oblanceolate, 1–4.5 × 0.7–1 cm, base cuneate, apex rotundate or obtuse, midrib impressed above, slightly elevated beneath. Flowers non-resupinate, creamy white with a greenish tinge; odd sepal ovate-lanceolate, 2 × 1 mm; lateral sepals folded, 2.5 × 1 mm, apex rotundate, back with a keel running down to the base of the ovary; petals shorter than the sepals, oblong-linear, transparent with 1 medium-longitudinal vein, apex obtuse; lip simple, undivided, ovate-lanceolate and triangular, 2 mm, the base shortly stiped, apex obtuse, margins slightly curved upwards near the base; column very short, horizontal, dorso-ventrally compressed, ovoid, beak-like at the apex, the dorsal side concave, containing an ovoid beak-like 2-chambered anther; pollinia 8 in 2 groups; ovary obconical, winged.

Locality: Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar. HK sheet 7120.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks by streams. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimens of T. hongkongensis (H. F. Hance 1287, BM; C. Ford 13, K) were collected from Hong Kong Island around 1880.

Themeda triandra Forssk. 黃背草
Fl. Aegypt.-Arab. 178. 1775; FKH 324. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 252. 1997; FYN 9: 721. 2003; FOC 22: 634. 2006; FGD 9: 507. 2009.
Themeda japonica (Willd.) Tanaka, Bult. Sci. Fak. Terk. Kjusu Imp. Univ. 1: 194. 1925; FHN 4: 484. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 253, pl. 63: 1 – 11, 79: 3. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 585, pl. 247. 2000; Check List HK Plants 349. 2002; 122. 2004.
Anthistiria japonica Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 901. 1805.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, erect or geniculate at the base, 0.5–1.5 m tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths usually hispid with tuberclebased hairs; leaf blades linear, 10–50 × 0.4–0.8 cm, glabrous or pilose, base subrounded, apex finely acuminate; ligule 1–2 mm, truncate, ciliate. Compound panicle lax, open, with spaced, often nodding spathate fascicles; spathes and spatheoles narrowly lanceolate, glabrous or thinly to densely tuberculate-hispid. Raceme composed of a triad of 1 sessile and 2 pedicellate spikelets above the involucre of 2 homogamous pairs. Homogamous spikelets all sessile, arising at same level, staminate, both glumes present, oblong-lanceolate with lateral scarious wings, glabrous or hispid with tubercle-based hairs. Sessile spikelet bisexual, fusiform-cylindrical; callus 1.5–3 mm, pungent, brown bearded, apex exposed; lower glume dark brown, abaxially rounded, glossy, hispidulous in upper 1/3, smooth below; upper glume and lower glume the same texture, equal, linear-oblong; lower lemma shorter than glume, lanceolate, glabrous; upper lemma 1-veined, awned from the apex. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet similar to involucral spikelet, male or barren.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 184; Y. W. Lam 403, 1150.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over E to S and SW Asia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Dry hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Themeda villosa (Poir.) A. Camus 菅
Fl. Indo-Chine. 7: 364. 1922; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 301, fig. 65. 1971; FRPS 10(2): 248, pl. 62: 5. 1997; FYN 9: 721, pl. 117: 1–2. 2003; FOC 22: 635. 2006; FGD 9: 506, fig. 269. 2009.
Anthistiria villosa Poir, Encycl. 1: 396. 1812.
Themeda gigantea (Cav.) Hack. var. villosa (Poir.) Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 675. 1889.
Themeda gigantea auct. non (Cav.) Hack.: FKH 324. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, stout, 2–4 m tall, smooth. Leaf sheaths glabrous, basal sheaths strongly compressed; leaf blades linear, ca. 100 × 0.7–1.5 cm, scabrid, gradually narrowed to the thicken white midrib toward base, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, ciliate. Inflorescence a leafy compound panicle composed of short racemes; raceme usually 2–3 cm, spathe boat-shaped, glabrous, composed of (1–)2 spikelet pairs and a terminal triad above the involucre of 2 homogamous pairs; homogamous spikelets arising at slightly different levels, staminate or barren, narrowly lanceolate, wingless, shortly pubescent. Sessile spikelet 7–8 mm; callus 1–2 mm, acute; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, abaxially compressed with shallow central groove, densely brown strigose, apex truncate, margins inrolled, abaxial surface and margins with dense brown hairs; upper glume margins embraced by lower glume, abaxial surface with brown hairs; upper lemma lanceolate, midvein produced into mucro or poorly developed short awn. Pedicellate spikelet similar to involucral spikelets.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 1092, 1681; Y. W. Lam 1285.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes, disturbed moist grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Thespesia populnea (L.) Solander ex Corr. 恆春黄槿（繖楊）
Ann. Mus. Hist. Nat. Paris 9: 290, t. 8, fig. 2. 1807; FRPS 49(2): 93. 1984; FGD 2: 190. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 750, pl. 376. 1993.
Hibiscus populneus L., Sp. Pl. 694. 1753.

Evergreen small tree, 6– 8 m tall; branchlets scabrous, densely covered with brown scurfy scales. Petioles 4–10 cm; stipules linear lanceolate, ca. 7 mm; leaf blade ovate-cordate, 7–18 × 4.5 –11 cm, base cordate, apex long caudate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely scurfy. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels 2–6 cm, densely scurfy. Calyx cup-shaped, ca. 15 mm in diam., apex truncate, 5-toothed. Corolla campanulate, ca. 5 cm, yellow, with purple blotches at base adaxially. Fruit pyriform, ca. 5 cm in diam. Seed triangularly ovoid, striate, lanuginose.

Locality: Tai Tam Reservoir, Tai Po, Butterfly Beach, Lung Kwu Tan, Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Lantau Island, Ma Wan, Po Toi. Y. S. Lau 1530; HK sheet 32395; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 23447 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Philippines and tropical Africa.
Ecology: Sunny places near seashores. Flowering: Almost all year round.

Thevetia peruviana (Pers.) K. Schum. 黃花夾竹桃
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(2): 159. 1895; FRPS 63: 36, pl. 12. 1977; FGD 1: 433, fig. 479. 1987; FOC 16: 164. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 69. 1999.
Cerbera thevetia L., Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753.
Cerbera peruviana Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 267. 1805.

Trees to 6 m tall. Bark chocolate‑brown, lenticellate; lower branches pendulous, young branches greenish grey. Petioles ca. 3 mm; leaf blades lustrous green adaxially, light green abaxially, very narrowly oblong, 10 – 15 × 0.5 – 1.2 cm, somewhat leathery, glabrous, apex acuminate, lateral veins obscure. Pedicels 2.5 – 5 cm. Flowers fragrant. Sepals green, narrowly triangular, apex acuminate. Corolla 6–7 × 4.5–5.5 cm; tube 4–5 cm, shorter than the lobes; corona scales present, connected by a transverse row of long white hairs; lobes obliquely obovate. Drupes compressed triangular‑globose, 2.5–4 cm in diam. Seeds light grey, lenticular, ca. 2 × 3.5 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 35, 2385.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to S & C America; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Dec.; fruiting: Aug. – Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Thevetia peruviana ‘Aurantiana’ (紅酒杯花; Photo 21) is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It differs from T. peruviana by red petals.
records.uses:
Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Thevetia peruviana ‘Aurantiana’ (紅酒杯花; Photo 21) is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It differs from T. peruviana by red petals.

records.text:
Thismia tentaculata K. Larsen & Averyanov 三絲水玉杯
Rheedea 17: 16. 2007; Ho et al., J. Syst. Evol. 47: 605-607. 2009; FOC 23: 124. 2010.

Plant holomycotrophic. Stems white, unbranched, erect, 2.5–3 cm. Leaves scale-like, 1.5–5.7 × 0.8–1.1 mm. Flowers 1–4, subsessile, with subtending bracts. Perianth tube white, translucent, actinomorphic, urceolate, ca. 7.3 × 4.8 mm, circumscissile. Outer tepals broadly triangular, ca. 1.4 mm, lacking appendage. Inner tepals narrowly triangular, ca. 2.3 mm excluding appendage; appendage orangish red, spreading, filiform, ca. 1.7 cm. Stamens apically connate. Capsule white, translucent, cup-shaped. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41925.
Distribution: Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen montane forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.

Thrixspermum centipeda Lour. 白點蘭
Fl. Cochinch. 520. 1790; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 28(1–2): 171. 1975, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 105, fig. 59. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 109. 2002; FRPS 19: 345, pl. 50: 3. 1999; FGD 7: 486, fig. 249. 2006; FOC 25: 470. 2009.

Epiphytic herb; roots cord-like, shiny grey; stems monopodial, slightly compressed. Leaves distichous, thick, smooth, appearing sessile, leaf blades oblong-linear, 3.5–7 × 0.8–1.6 cm, base obtuse, apex rotundate, obliquely retuse and apiculate, midrib slightly impressed above. Flowers resupinate, pale yellow, two-ranked, ephemeral; sepals and petals linear-lanceolate, evenly spaced, forming a semicircle; odd sepal dorsal, 2.6 × 0.3 cm; lateral sepals widespread, oblique, 3 mm wide at base; petals slanting upwards, 2.2 × 0.2 cm; lip 3-lobed, white, fleshy, saccate; lateral lobes very short, 2 mm, arching over the column with downy hair along the margin; midlobe triangular, 6 mm, curved, base with a white callus 2.5 mm; disk speckled red both inside and outside; spur stout and rounded at base, papillose inside and at tip, lemon-yellow and fainly dotted pink; column white, very short, fleshy, triangular at the sides; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, unequal; ovary shiny, smooth, light green.

Locality: Castle Peak, Sai Kung. HK sheet 27536, 33094.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Indochina, Indonesia.
Ecology: Trunks in forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.

Thuarea involuta (G. Forst.) R. Br. ex Sm. 蒭雷草
Cycl. 35. 1817; FHN 4: 443. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 387, pl. 118. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 518, pl. 219. 2000; FOC 22: 525. 2006; FGD 9: 449, fig. 232. 2009.
Ischaemum involutum G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 73. 1786.
Thuarea sarmentosa Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 110. 1805; FHK 415. 1861; FKH 317. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms long and creeping, much branched, rooting at nodes, flowering culms up to 20 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, ca. 1/2 length of internode, pilose or only ciliate along margins; leaf blades lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.3–0.8 cm, usually puberulous on both surfaces, margins usually rugulose; ligule very short, a row of white short ciliate. Inflorescence a terminal onesided raceme, enclosed by a spathe; rachis broad and wing-like in lower fertile part, narrowed above in staminate part. Bisexual spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–4.5 mm, 2-floret, only upper floret fertile; lower glume absent or narrow and small, membranous; upper glume subequal to spikelet, leathery, abaxially hairy, 7-veined; lower lemma herbaceous, 5–7-veined, palea membranous, stamen 3; upper lemma thick-papery, palea 2-veined, stamen 3. Male spikelet oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm; lower glume absent; upper glume herbaceous, abaxially hairy, 3–5-veined; lower lemma papery, broad lanceolate, 5-veined; palea membranous, 2-veined, 2-lobed; stamen 3; upper lemma papery, 5-veined; palea 2-veined; male spikelet deciduous at maturity, leaf-like rachis inrolled embraced fertile spikelet.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ping Chau. H. F. Hance 10230 (BM).
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan; widely spread over SE Asia, Malesia, Pacific islands, New Guinea, Australia, Indian Ocean islands and Madagascar.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Thunbergia alata Bojer ex Sims 翼葉老鴉嘴
Bot. Mag. 52: pl. 2591. 1825; FKH 197. 1912; FRPS 70: 24. 2002.

Herbaceous vine; stems subquadrate to flattened, bisulcate, pubescent. Petioles winged, 1.5–3 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades sagittate to deltoid ovate, 2–7.5 × 2–6 cm, base hastate to cordate, apex acute, margin entire or undulate, adaxially sparsely strigose, abaxially hirsute; palmately 5‑veined. Flowers solitary, axillary. Peduncles 2.5–3 cm, sparsely strigose. Bracts subulate; bracteoles ovate, 1.5–1.8 × 1–1.4 cm, apex acute or acuminate, obtuse, 5–7‑veined, abaxially hirsute. Calyx annular, unequally 10–13‑lobed. Corolla 2.5–4.5 cm, orange with dark purple glandular “eye” in throat; tube‑base cylindric, 2–4 mm wide, gradually widened to ca. 4 cm at mouth; lobes obovate, apex truncate. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments glabrous, ca. 4 mm; anther thecae unequal, 3.5–4 mm, pubescent at margin and base. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 8 mm, glabrous; stigma 2‑lobed; lobes unequal, the upper one erect, the lower one spreading. Capsules pubescent, ca. 7 × 10 mm, beak ca. 1.4 cm, base ca. 3 mm wide. Seeds 2, reticulate on the dorsal surface.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2021, 2201; Y. W. Lam 512.
Distribution: Cultivated and naturalized in S & SW China; native to tropical Africa, now widely cultivated and naturalized in the tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thunbergia erecta (Benth.) T. Anderson 硬枝老鴉嘴
J. Proc. Linn. Soc., Bot. 7: 18. 1864; FHN 3: 542. 1972; FRPS 70: 24. 2002.
Meyenia erecta Benth., Niger Fl. 476. 1848.

Erect shrubs, 1–2 m tall, many‑branched; younger stems quadrangular, greyish brown, winged, glabrous or pubescent on the node. Petioles 2–5 mm, subglabrous; leaf blades leathery or thick papery, ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, sometimes rhomboid, 2.5–9 × 1–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or sparsely serrate towards the apex, sometimes undulate, sparsely pilose or subglabrous, pinnately‑veined, lateral veins 4–6 pairs, netted near the margin. Flowers solitary or in pairs, axillary. Peduncles 1.5–2.5 cm, glabrous. Bract subulate; bracteoles oblong‑ovate, 1–2 × 0.5–0.8 cm, base obtuse, apex acute, glabrous or minutely puberulous at the apex. Calyx 12–15‑lobed; lobes unequal, ca. 1 mm, glandular‑pubescent. Corolla 5.5–6 cm, white, purplish or deeply violet with a white or yellowish throat, outside glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm long and 3 mm wide, gradually widened to 2.5–3 cm at mouth; lobes oblong ovate, subequal, ca. 1.5 × 1 cm. Stamens 4, didynamous, filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 1.2 cm, the shorter pair ca. 0.7 cm; anther thecae oblong, ca. 4 mm, with a short awn‑like appendage at base, puberulous at margin and base. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 3.5 cm, sparsely puberulous towards the apex; stigma unequally lobed, the upper lobe erect and angular. Capsules glabrous, ca. 0.9 cm long, 1.2 cm broad, beak ca. 2 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1149, 3227; L. T. Lo 93; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20583, 21048 (KUN).
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; native to W tropical Africa, cultivated elsewhere in tropical regions.
Ecology: Cultivated. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thunbergia fragrans Roxb. 碗花草
Pl. Coromandel 1: 47, pl. 67. 1795; FKH 197. 1912; FRPS 70: 30. 2002.
Thunbergia bodinier Lev., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 12: 21. 1913.

Herbaceous vines. Stems subquadrate to flattened, sulcate, hirsute. Petioles 0.5–4.5 cm, hirsute; leaf blades papery, oblong‑ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 4–14 × 3–7 cm, base rounded, sometimes cuneate or cordate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire to irregularly sinuate to shallowly and coarsely dendate, puberulous on both surfaces, gradually subglabrescent, palmately 5‑veined. Flowers solitary, axillary. Peduncles 3–5.5 cm. Bracts subulate; bracteoles ovate, 1.5–2.5 × 0.8–1.5 cm, apex acute, puberulous, persistent. Calyx unequally 10 – 13‑dentate, glabrous. Corolla white, sparsely puberulous, tube‑base cylindric, 4–7 mm wide, gradually widened to ca. 2 cm at mouth; lobes obovate, ca. 2.5 × 2.3 cm, 7–9‑veined. Stamens 4, included; filaments glabrous; anther‑thecae lanceolate, divergent. Ovary glabrous; style exerted; stigma funnel‑shaped. Capsules glabrous, brown, ca. 0.7 × 1 cm, beak ca. 1.5 cm. Seed smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 677, 1260, 3117; E. Bodinier 1318 (E); M. S. Clemens 4267 (E).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Taiwan; native to India and Sri Lanka, widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Thunbergia bodinieri was collected by E. Bodinier from Hong Kong on 4 Sep. 1895.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Thunbergia bodinieri was collected by E. Bodinier from Hong Kong on 4 Sep. 1895.

Thunbergia grandiflora Roxb. 大花老鴉嘴
Bot. Reg., 6: pl. 495. 1820; FHK 260. 1861; FKH 197. 1912; FHN 3: 543. 1972; FRPS 70: 26. 2002.

Woody vines, up to 8 m or longer. Stem sulcate, glabrous or pilose. Petioles 1–7 cm, sulcate, pubescent; leaf blades papery, ovate or triangular‑ovate, 5–10 × 4–8 cm, base subcordate or truncate, apex acuminate to acute, margin undulate or irregularly lobed below the middle, rarely entire, pubescent, palmately 5–7‑veined. Flower solitary or paired in leaf axil, or in terminal panicle. Pedicles 4 –7 cm, sulcate, pubescent. Bracts subulate; Bracteoles oblong or ovate, 2.5–3 cm, apex acute with a short mucro, glabrous, margin ciliate, 5–7‑veined. Calyx annular, unlobed. Corolla bluish, 4–6 cm, abaxilly glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 7 × 3 mm, gradually widened to ca. 5 cm at mouth, limb 5‑lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2.5 cm. Stamens 4, filaments 7–9 mm, anthers appendaged basally, pubescent dorsally. Ovary glabrous, stigma 2‑lobed; lobes subequal. Capsule pubescent, ca. 1.3 cm in diam., beak ca. 2.5 cm. Seeds ovoid, compressed, verrucose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 729, 1884; HK sheet 32226.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets, sometimes cultivated. Flowering: Mar. – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thunbergia laurifolia Lindl. 桂葉老鴉嘴
Gard. Chron. 1856: 260. 1856; FRPS 70: 28. 2002.
Thunbergia grandiflora (Roxb. ex Rottl.) Roxb. var. laurifolia (Lindl.) Benoist, Fl. Indo‑Chine 4: 618. 1935.
Thunbergia harrisii Hook., Bot. Mag. t. 4998. 1857.

Herbaceous or woody vines. Stems subquadrangular, glabrous. Petioles 0–3 cm, sulcate; leaf blades oblong, oblong‑lanceolate or lanceolate, subleathery, 7–16 × 1.5–6 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire or irregularly undulate, glabrous, palmately 3‑veined. Racemes terminal or axillary. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Bracts subulate, ca. 4 × 1 mm, glabrous; bracteoles oblong‑elliptic, 2 – 2.5 × 0.9 – 1.2 cm, apex acuminate, abaxially densely pubescent upward. Calyx annular, unlobed. Corolla 4.5–6 cm; tube‑base white, cylindric, 1–1.3 cm × ca. 3 mm, gradually widened to ca. 3 cm at mouth; lobes bluish, orbicular, ca. 2 cm in diam. Stamens 4, included; filaments thickened basally; anthers‑thecae acute apically, pubescent dorsally. Ovary and style glabrous, style ca. 2.5 cm. Capsule ca. 1.5 × 1.5 cm, beak ca. 3 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2109; P. S. Choi 116; E. Bodinier 1417 (E); S. Y. Hu 9337 (K).
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian (cultivated); native to India, cultivated in other tropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thysanolaena latifolia (Roxb. ex Hornem.) Honda 粽葉蘆
J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 3: 312. 1930; FTW ed. 2, 5: 336. 2000; FOC 22: 446. 2006; FGD 9: 340, fig. 161. 2009.
Melica latifolia Roxb. ex Hornem., Suppl. Hort. Bot. Hafn. 117. 1819.
Thysanolaena maxima (Roxb.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 794. 1891; FHN 4: 370, fig. 1180. 1977; FFJ 6: 128, fig. 99. 1995; FRPS 9(2): 30, pl. 4: 1. 2002.
Thysanolaena acarifera Arn. & Nees, Gramineae 49. 1841; FHK 417. 1861.
Thysanolaena agrostis Nees, Edinburgh New Philos. J. 18: 180. 1835; FKH 318. 1912; Check List HK Plants 349. 2002; 122. 2004.

Tall reed-like perennial herb, 1–4 m tall. Culms woody, with white pith. Leaf blades lanceolate, leathery, 30–50 × 3 – 7(–10) cm, base sub-amplexicaul, apex acuminate, glabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, subleathery, truncate. Panicle up to 60 cm, open or contracted, elliptic in outline; main branches 1–3 per node, pilose in axils; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Spikelets 1.5–2 mm, cylindrical, the margins ciliate-hispid, florets 2–3; lower floret reduced to only a ca. 1.5 mm lemma; upper floret ca. 1 mm; glumes 1/5–1/4 spikelet length, ovate-lanceolate, margins siliceous; lower glume apex with sinus; upper glume apex rounded; sterile lemma glabrous, as long as spikelet; fertile lemma slightly shorter than lower lemma, ciliate on the margin with 1 mm hairs, spreading at maturity, apex slightly recurved. Caryopsis oblong, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2301, 3301; K. L. Yip 4081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Indian Ocean islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, moist grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Animal food (forage), material (fiber).

Thysanotus chinensis Benth. 異蕊草
FHK 372. 1861; FKH 280. 1912; FRPS 14: 48. 1980; FOC 24: 203. 2000; FGD 6: 356, fig. 211. 2005.

Perennial herb, with short rhizome and fibrous roots. Leaves radical, tufted, linear-subulate, erect and stiff, 13–20 cm × 1–1.5 mm, glabrous. Scape erect, slender, as long as or slightly longer than leaves, bearing a terminal umbel. Umbel 4–10-flowered; bracts ovate or lanceolate, 3–5 mm, membranous and scale-like; pedicels 1–1.5 cm, articulate near base, recurved after flowering. Perianth blue; segments 6, suboblong, 7–8 × 1–2 mm, membranous, 3–5-veined; inner ones sometimes fimbriate-denticulate at margin proximally. Stamens 6, 4–5 mm; outer anthers ca. 1.2 mm, inner ones ca. 2.2 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 4 × 3 mm, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fanling, So Kwun Wat. Y. W. Lam 1725; HK sheet 38434.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Tinospora sagittata (Oliv.) Gagnep. 青牛膽
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 55: 45. 1908; Forman, Kew Bull. 36(2): 383, fig. 1 (d-e). 1981; FGD 1: 34, fig. 32. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 23. 1996.
Limacia sagittata Oliv., Hook. Icon. Pl. 1749. 1888.
Tinospora capillipes Gagnep., Bull. Bot. France 55: 44. 1908.
Tinospora imbricata S. Y. Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 35: 195, t. 1 (2). 1954.

Herbaceous vine, with moniliform roots. Stems slender, striate, usually puberulous. Leaves papery to thinly leathery; petioles 2.5–5 cm or longer, pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blade lanceolate, rarely ovate or elliptic, 7–15(–20) × 2.4 –5 cm, base sagittate or hastate, apex acuminate, sometimes caudate, lobes rounded, obtuse or mucronate, usually puberulous on nerves, sometimes glabrescent adaxially or on both surfaces, palmately 5-nerved; reticulation of nerved raised abaxially. Cymes axillary, usually fascicled, or forming panicles, 2–10(–15) cm or sometimes longer; peduncles and pedicels filamentous; bracteoles 2, closely subtending sepals. Male flowers: sepals 6, or sometimes more, often unequal, the outermost minute, ovate or lanceolate, only 1–2 mm, inner ones conspicuous larger, broadly ovate to obovate, or broadly elliptic to elliptic, to 3.5 mm; petals 6, subrounded or broadly obovate, rarely subrhomboid, often clawed, 1.4 –2 mm. Female flowers: sepals similar to that in males; petals cuneate, ca. 0.4 mm; staminodes 6, usually clavellate, ca. 0.4 mm; carpels 3, subglabrous. Drupes ± subglobose; kernel half-globular, 6 – 8 mm wide.

Locality: Sai Kung, Mount Parker. Y. W. Lam 1451; HK sheet 126, 127, 33668.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, SE Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, bamboo groves and grassy slopes. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tinospora sinensis (Lour.) Merr. 中華青牛膽
Sunyatsenia 1: 193. 1934; FHN 1: 318, 1964; Forman, Kew Bull. 36: 386, fig. 1 (F, G). 1981; FGD 1: 33, fig. 33. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 20. 1996.
Campylus sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 113. 1790.
Cocculus tomentosus Colebrr., Trans. Linn. Soc. 13: 59. 1822.
Menispermum tomentosum (Colebr.) Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 813. 1832.
Tinospora tomentosa (Colebr.) Hook. f. & Thoms., Fl. Ind. 1: 183. 1855.

Vine up to 20 m or longer. Branches slightly fleshy; young shoots green, striate, pubescent; old branches thick, usually glabrous, with brownish, membranous epidermis and convex lenticels. Leaves papery; petioles (4 –)6 –13 cm, puberulous; leaf blade ovate-orbicular, rarely broadly ovate, 7–14 × 5 –13 cm, base deeply to slightly cordate, apex acute, margin entire, puberulent on both surfaces, palmately 5(–7)-nerved. Inflorescences appearing when plant is leafless. Male inflorescences 1– 4 cm or longer, solitary or fascicled. Male flowers: sepals 6 in 2 series, outer 3 minute, oblong-elliptic, 1–1.5 mm, inner ones broadly ovate, 5 × 3 mm; petals 6, sub-rhomboid, ca. 3 mm including the claw; stamens 6, filaments ca. 4 mm. Female inflorescences solitary. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; carpels 3. Drupes red, subglobose, to 10 mm; kernel semi-ovoid, with dorsal ridges and tubercles.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mong Tsai, Mau Ping, Yung Shue O, Ping Chau, Ching Chau. L. T. Lo 308; Y. S. Lau 3010, 3104.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: May–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tithonia diversifolia (Hemsl.) A. Gray 腫柄菊
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 19: 5. 1883; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 13. 1969; FRPS 75: 356, pl. 59: 1–2. 1979; FGD 8: 120, fig. 59. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1083. 1998.
Mirasolia diversifolia Hemsl., Biol. Cent.‑Amer., Bot. 2(8): 168, pl. 47. 1881.

Large shrub‑like perennial herbs, 2–3 m tall; stems striate, puberulent in upper younger part. Leaves alternate in upper stem portion, opposite near base; petiole 1–5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑triangular, 6–18.5 × 2.5– 8.5 cm, 3–5‑lobed or sometimes with upper ones not lobed, lobes ovate‑lanceolate and acuminate, base attenuate and decurrent forming wings with petiole, margin crenate‑serrate, 3‑nerved, upper surfaces scaberulous to puberulent, lower surfaces densely pubescent‑tomentulose and glandular. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, 5– 15 cm across, solitary; peduncle 6–12 cm, swollen near the capitula. Involucres hemispherical, 2–4 cm across; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate; outer rows smaller, ovate‑elliptic, apex acute, 0.7–1 × 0.4–0.5 cm; inward series longer and becoming reflexed, oblanceolate‑oblong, apex obtuse to rounded, 1.8–2.2 × 0.5–0.9 cm, margin membranous on the apical half. Receptacle convex; paleae 11 mm, sharply toothed near the apex. Marginal ligulate florets sterile, 9–14 in one series, corolla yellow, ligule 4 cm, tube 1.5–2 mm and pubescent, apex 2–3‑lobed. Disk tubular florets bisexual, many, corolla yellow, 8 mm, narrowed at the middle, broadened in lower part and slightly contracted at base, pubescent on lower region, apex 5‑lobed. Cypselae blackish brown, oblong, 5 – 6 mm, flat and 4‑ribbed, shortly sericeous. Pappus of ligulate florets minutely scaly, those of tubular florets with scarious crown 1.5–2 mm, irregularly erose, together with 2 rigid awns 3.5–5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 1025; S. Y. Hu 6352 (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1346 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan and Fujian (cultivated); native to Mexico.
Ecology: Often cultivated on margins of farmlands near villages. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Green manure, ornamental.

Toddalia asiatica (L.) Lam. 飛龍掌血（簕鈎）
Tabl. Encycl. 2: 116. 1797; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 552, fig. 2834. 1972; FHN 3: 36, fig. 548. 1974; FTW 3: 529, fig. 714. 1977; FGD 2: 248, fig. 163. 1991; FTW ed 2, 3: 535, pl. 276. 1993; FRPS 43(2): 96, pl. 23. 1997.
Paullinia asiatica L., Sp. Pl. 365. 1753.
Toddalia aculeata Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 249. 1805; FHK 59. 1861; FKH 56. 1912.
Toddalia tonkinensis Guill., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 91: 215. 1945.

Shrub, with weak or flexuose branches. Stems with thick corky layer and yellowish grey lenticels. Stems, branches and leaf rachis armed with many downward curved sharp spines. Young branchlets glabrous or pubescent.
