Leaflets sessile, densely covered with pellucid glandular dots, ovate, obovate, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 5–9 × 2–4 cm, base attenuate, apex caudate, acute or mucronate, sometimes emarginate, margin serrulate; lateral veins dense and slender. Pedicels rather short, subtended by very small scaly bracts. Flowers pale yellowish white. Calyx lobes less than 1 mm, margin ciliolate. Petals 2–3.5 mm. Fruit orange-red to red, 0.8–1 cm in diam., 4–8-furrowed. Seed 5–6 × 4 mm; seed coat brownish black.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Beacon Hill, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Luk Keng, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2830; P. S. Choi 518; Y. W. Lam 19.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range.
Ecology: Secondary forests or thickets. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Toona rubriflora C. J. Tseng 紅花香椿
Univ. Amoiensis Acta Sci. Nat. 9(4): 303. 1962; FRPS 43(3): 42. 1997.

Evergreen tree to 18 m tall; bark grey, longitudinally fissured. Branchlets terete, sparsely pubescent, lenticellate. Leaves 35–40 cm including the petiole; petioles 6–9 cm, together with leaf rachis densely pubescent; leaflets 8–9 pairs, opposite or subopposite; petiolules 2–3 mm; leaflet blades papery, ovate-oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 4.5–13 × 2–4 cm, base oblique, apex caudate-acuminate, margin entire, adaxial surfaces glabrous, abaxial surface pubescent densely on midvein, sparsely on veins, and with tuft of hairs in axils of lateral veins; lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, ca. 17 cm; peduncle densely pubescent. Pedicels ca. 1 mm. Sepals 5, small, broadly triangular, covered with minute coarse hairs, ciliate. Petals 5, red (according to collector), ovate, 3–4 × ca. 2 mm, imbricate, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface densely hirsutulous and keeled at base. Stamens 5, glabrous; filaments ca. 2.5 mm; anthers ellipsoidal. Ovary 5-locular, together with disk densely covered with tawny coarse hairs; ovules 13–15 per locule. Style glabrous; stigma disciform. Capsule black when dry, oblong-obovoid, 3.5–4.5 cm, woody, with large pale lenticels. Seeds with membranous wings on both ends, 2–2.8 cm including wings.

Locality: Kei Ling Ha. S. C. Ng 3518.
Distribution: Fujian.
Ecology: Dense moist forests along valleys and streams. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Nov.

Toona sinensis (A. Juss.) M. Roem. 香椿
Fam. Nat. Syn. Monogr. 1: 139. 1846; FHN 3: 75. 1974; FYN 1: 210, pl. 48: 8– 10. 1977; FFJ 2: 383. 1985; FGD 2: 303. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 37, pl. 9: 1 –5. 1997.
Cedrela sinensis A. Juss., Mem. Mus. Hist. Nat. 23: 241. 1830; FKH 58. 1912.

Deciduous tree, up to 25 m tall. Leaves paripinnate, 25–50(–90) cm; leaflets 14–28, opposite or alternate; petiolules 0.5–1 cm; blades papery, ovate-lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, 6–17 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base oblique, apex caudate to acute, margin sparsely serrate or rarely entire, glabrous and without spots on both surfaces, sometimes slightly hairy when young; lateral veins 18–24 on each side of midvein. Panicles as long as or longer than leaves, glabrous or puberulous. Flowers small. Pedicels short. Calyx cupular, 5-lobed or undulate, ca. 1 mm, pubescent abaxially, margin ciliate. Petals 5, white, oblong, 4–5 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse. Stamens 5; staminodes 5. Disk glabrous. Ovary conical, with 5 stripes, glabrous; ovules 8 per locule. Style longer than ovary; stigma disciform. Capsule purplish brown, narrowly ellipsoidal, 1–3.5 cm, glaucous lenticellate, dehiscing into 5 valves when mature. Seed brown, apex with a long membranous wing.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 873, 1484; HK sheet 35390.
Distribution: N, E, C, S & SW China; India, Indonesia, N Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Timber, vegetable (young shoots).

Torenia asiatica L. 光葉蝴蝶草（光葉翼萼）
Sp. Pl. 2: 619. 1753; FOC 18: 39. 1998.
Torenia glabra Osbeck, Dagbok Ostind. Resa. 210. 1757; FHN 3: 510. 1974; FRPS 67(2): 161. 1979; Check List HK Plants 249. 2002; 86. 2004.
Torenia benthamiana auct. non Hance: FKH 188. 1912.

Herbs creeping to suberect, rooting from nodes. Branches numerous, long, slender. Petioles 2–8 mm; leaf blade triangular‑ovate, narrowly ovate, or obovate‑orbicular, 1.5–3.2 × 1–2 cm, glabrous or sparsely villose, base abruptly constricted, subtruncate to broadly cuneate, margin crenate‑serrate. Flowers axillary and solitary or in fascicles. Pedicels 0.5–2 cm. Calyx 2‑lipped, 0.8–1.5 cm, further lobed into 5 small lobes in fruit, 5‑winged; wings more than 1 mm wide, ± decurrent. Corolla purple‑red to blue‑red, 1.5–2.5 cm, exceeding calyx by 0.4–1 cm. Filaments of anterior stamens with linear appendages of 1–2 mm. Capsules 1–1.3 cm. Seeds yellow, ca. 0.4 mm.

Locality: Mui Tsz Lam. Y. W. Lam 518.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Shady places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Torenia benthamiana Hance 毛葉蝴蝶草
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 226. 1862; FKH 188. 1912; FHN 3: 510. 1974; FOC 18: 38. 1998; FGD 4: 376. 2000.
Torenia hirsuta auct. non. Lam.: FKH 188. 1912.

Herbs creeping, densely white hirsute, rooting from lower nodes. Branches numerous. Petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑cordate, 1.5–2.2 × 1–1.8 cm, margin crenate. Inflorescences axillary, usually 3–5 in fascicles, or racemose, rarely 1‑flowered. Pedicels 3 cm in fruit. Calyx slender, 6–9 mm at anthesis, to 1.5 cm in fruit, 5‑ribbed, somewhat 2‑lipped. Corolla purple‑red, pale blue‑purple, or whitish, 1.2–1.4 cm; lower lip ca. 4 mm, 3‑lobed, middle lobe slightly larger than lateral lobes; upper lip oblong, ca. 5 × 4 mm. Filaments of anterior stamens with appendages of 1.5–2 mm. Capsules narrowly ellipsoidal, ca. 10 × 3 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Tai O. Y. S. Lau 1650; Y. W. Lam 839, 876.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Wastelands, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–May of the following year.

Torenia biniflora T. L. Chin & D. Y. Hong 二花蝴蝶草
FRPS 67(2): 399. 1979; FOC 18: 38. 1998, FGD 4: 376. 2000.

Annual herbs, sparsely hirtellous. Stems to 50 cm, creeping or ascending, rooting from lower nodes. Petioles 6–10 mm; leaf blade ovate to narrowly ovate, 2–4 × 1–2.5 cm, margin coarsely toothed. Inflorescences axillary, usually dichotomous, sometimes racemose, 2–8‑flowered. Pedicels 6–12 mm in fruit. Calyx tubular, ca. 1 cm, 5‑winged; wings unequal, 0.5–1 mm wide; lobes 5, 3–4 mm. Corolla yellow, rarely white and faintly blue, ca. 1.1 cm. Filaments of anterior stamens with appendages of 3 mm. Capsules ellipsoidal, ca. 7 × 3 mm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1373, 1453; F. W. Xing 9861.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.

Torenia concolor Lindl. 單色蝴蝶草（單色翼萼）
Edwards's Bot. Reg. 32: pl. 62. 1846; FKH 187. 1912; FOC 18: 39. 1998; FGD 4: 375. 2000.
Torenia rubens Benth. ex Maxim., Prodr. 10: 410. 1846; FHK 250. 1861 (including var. grandiflora).

Annual herbs. Stems 4‑angled. Branches ascending or erect, rooting at lower nodes. Petioles 2–10 mm; leaf blade triangular‑ovate, narrowly ovate, or rarely ovate‑orbicular, 1–4 × 0.8–2.5 cm, glabrous or villous, base broadly cuneate to subtruncate, margin serrate or crenate‑serrate, apex obtuse to acute. Flowers axillary or terminal, solitary or in fascicles. Pedicels 2–3.5 cm, lengthening to 5 cm in fruit. Calyx 1.2–1.7 cm, enlarged to 2.3 cm in fruit, base decurrent; wings 5, slightly more than 1 mm in wide; lips narrowly triangular with 5 small lobes evident in fruit. Corolla blue to blue‑purple, 2.5–3.9 cm, exceeding calyx lobes. Filaments of anterior stamens with filiform of appendages, 2–4 mm. Capsules 1.5–1.8 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau. W. J. Tutcher 11443; Y. S. Lau 2357; Y. W. Lam 1122.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Ryukyu Islands, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grasslands, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Torenia flava Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth. 黃花蝴蝶草
Scroph. Ind. 38. 1835; FHK 250. 1861; FKH 187. 1912; FHN 3: 510. 1974; FOC 18: 38. 1998; FGD 4: 377. 2000.

Annual herbs, erect, to 50 cm tall. Stems many‑branched, 4‑angled, villose. Petiole 5–13 mm; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, 3–5 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, margin crenate, sparsely pilose on both surfaces or abaxially glabrous except for veins. Racemes terminal, 10–20 cm. Bracts oblong‑ovate, 5–8 mm. Calyx narrowly cylindric, ca. 8 × 2 mm, enlarged to 10–15 × 3–5 mm in fruit, villous, 5‑ribbed; lobes 5, narrowly lanceolate. Corolla yellow; tube 1–1.2 cm; lower lip shallowly 3‑lobed, lobes suborbicular, subequal; upper lip slightly larger than lower lobes, margin entire or apex emarginate. Filaments of anterior stamens with appendages of ca. 1 mm. Capsules narrowly ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 2363; HK sheet 40640.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Torenia fordii Hook. f. 紫斑蝴蝶草（紫斑翼萼）
Bot. Mag. 111, pl. 6797B. 1885; FOC 18: 38. 1998; FGD 4: 377. 2000.

Herbs, 25–40 cm tall, villous. Stems erect, stout. Petioles 1 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to ovate‑triangular, 3– 5 × 2.5–4 cm, sparsely white hairy, base abruptly constricted and broadly cuneate, margin coarsely triangular acute‑serrate. Racemes terminal. Bracts oblong‑ovate, 5–10 mm, margin ciliate. Pedicels ca. 1 cm, lengthening to 2 cm in fruit. Calyx obovate‑fusiform, ca. 12 × 5–7 mm, ca. enlarged to 1.8 × 0.8 cm in fruit, 5‑winged; wings unequal in width; lobes 5, subequal. Corolla yellow, 1.5–1.8 cm; lower lip lobes rotund, ca. 3–3.5 mm, middle lobe apically orange‑coloured, lateral lobes distally blue; upper lip ca. 4 × 5 mm, emarginate. Filaments of anterior stamens with tooth‑like appendages. Capsules cylindric, 9–11 × 2–3 mm, compressed, 4‑furrowed.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Shing Mun, Sai Kung. L. T. Lo 183; Y. S. Lau 2512; Y. W. Lam 877.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Torenia fournieri Linden ex E. Fourn. 藍豬耳
Ill. Hort. 23: 129. 1876; FOC 18: 39. 1998; FGD 4: 376, fig. 226. 2000.

Herbs 15–50 cm tall. Stems erect, 4‑angled, simple or branched above middle, subglabrous. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade obong‑ovate to ovate, 3–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, subglabrous, margin coarsely serrate. Racemes often terminal. Bracts linear, 2–5 mm. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Calyx ellipsoidal, 1.3–1.9 cm, green or purple‑red at apex and margin, 5‑winged; wings 2–3 mm wide; lobes subtriangular, 1.5–1.7 cm. Corolla 2.5–4 cm; tube pale violet, upper side yellow; lower lip purple‑blue, middle lobe with a yellow patch near base, lobes oblong to suborbicular, ca. 10 × 8 mm, subequal; upper lip pale blue, erect, broadly obovate, 1–1.2 × 1.2–1.5 cm, emarginate. Filaments of anterior stamens without appendages. Capsules narrowly ellipsoidal, ca. 12 × 0.5 mm. Seeds yellow.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 1633, 1654, 1953.
Distribution: Cultivated or naturalized in S China; native to Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tournefortia montana Lour. 紫丹
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 122. 1790; FKH 177. 1912; FGZ 568, fig. 302. 1956; FHN 3: 458, fig. 856. 1974; FRPS 64(2): 31. 1990; FOC 16: 341. 1995.
Tournefortia brachyantha Merr. & Chun, Sunyatsenia 2(3 –4): 314, fig. 43. 1935.
Tournefortia sampsonii Hance, J. Bot. 6(71): 330. 1868.

Scandent shrub, 1–2 m tall; branchlets pubescent. Petiole 5–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate‑lanceolate, 8–14 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate to caudate‑acute, sparsely strigose on both surfaces, black when dry. Cymes scorpioid, terminating leafy branches, sparsely branched, 2–15 cm, strigose. Flowers unilateral, sessile. Calyx parted to middle or slightly below, ca. 2 mm, strigose; lobes lanceolate to triangular‑lanceolate. Corolla white, urceolate; limb 5‑lobed. Stamens sessile. Stigma sessile at apex of globose ovary. Fruit subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam.; endocarp divided at maturity into two 2‑seeded mericarps.

Locality: Castle Peak. K. L. Yip 4154; HK sheet 39588, 39667.
Distribution: Yunnan, Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Spring to summer.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Toxocarpus fuscus Tsiang 鏽毛弓果藤
Sunyatsenia. 4: 81. 1939; FRPS 63: 288. 1977; FGD 1: 491, fig. 553. 1987; FOC 16: 197. 1995.

Lianas to 5 m. Young branchlets rusty pubescent, glabrescent and lenticellate with age. Petiole ca. 2.5 cm, rusty tomentose; leaf blade broadly ovate‑oblong, 9–15 × 5–5.8 cm, papery, adaxially glabrous except for rusty hairs along midvein, abaxially rusty pubescent, base rounded, apex acute or short acuminate; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Cymes to 8.5 cm, shorter than leaves, few branched, 12–20‑flowered, rusty pubescent; peduncle less than 1 cm. Flower buds long acuminate. Pedicel ca. 5 mm. Sepals lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Corolla yellow, ca. 9 mm, glabrous; lobes oblong‑lanceolate. Corona lobes ovate, longer than anthers, apex acute. Stigma head long beaked.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Tai Mo Shan, Wong Chuk Yeung, Kai Kung Shan. F. W. Xing 8951.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Open woods. Flowering: May.

Toxocarpus wightianus Hook. & Arn. 弓果藤
Bot. Beechey. Voy. 200. 1836; FHK 224. 1861; FKH 170. 1912; FRPS 63: 284, pl. 97. 1977; FGD 1: 493, fig. 556. 1987; FOC 16: 197. 1995.
Toxocarpus ovalifolius Tsiang, Sunyatsenia 2: 193, pl. 35. 1934; FRPS 63: 282. 1977.

Lianas, slender, to 8 m.; branchlets tawny brown puberulent, lenticellate. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, rusty tomentose; leaf blade elliptic or elliptic‑oblong to ovate‑orbicular, 2.5–6 × 1.5–4.5 cm, somewhat leathery, base rounded to slightly cordate, apex acute to rounded or slightly emarginate, apiculate to cuspidate, glabrous, lateral veins 5–8 on each side of midvein. Cymes ± umbel‑like, to 10‑flowered, much shorter than leaves; peduncle to 6 mm, rusty pubescent. Pedicels 3 mm, minutely villous. Sepals ovate‑oblong, membranous, rusty tomentose. Corolla yellowish, ± rotate, glabrous; tube 2 × 3 mm; lobes narrowly lanceolate, 8 × 1–2 mm. Corona‑lobes triangular, 2 mm, obtuse. Pollinia minute. Stigma head fusiform. Follicles narrowly lanceolate in outline, 8–9 × 1 cm, divaricate at an angle 180–200°, densely rusty tomentose, pericarp thick. Seeds ovate‑oblong, 1 × 0.3–0.5 cm, not beaked; coma 3 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 184; Y. W. Lam 781, 808.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Trachelospermum jasminoides (Lindl.) Lem. 絡石
Jard. Fleur. 1: t. 61. 1851; FKH 169. 1912; FRPS 63: 216, pl. 75. 1977; FGD 1: 472, fig. 531. 1987; FOC 16: 167. 1995.
Rhynchospermum jasminoides Lindl., J. Hort. Soc. London 1: 74. 1846.
Trachelospermum jasminoides (Lindl.) Lem. cv. Variegatum, FRPS 63: 219. 1977.
Trachelospermum jasminoides (Lindl.) Lem. var. heterophyllum Tsiang, Sunyatsenia 2: 146, fig. 15. 1934; FRPS 63: 218. 1977.

Lianas woody, to 10 m or longer. Stems brownish, lenticellate; young branchlets pubescent, glabrous when older. Petioles 3–12 mm; leaf blade ovate to obovate or narrowly elliptic, 2–10 × 1–4.5 cm, papery, glabrous or sometimes sparsely pubescent abaxially. Cymes paniculate, terminal and axillary; peduncle 2–6 cm, puberulent to glabrous. Sepals narrowly oblong, 2–5 mm, spreading or reflexed, pubescent abaxially, ciliate, apex obtuse or acute. Corolla white, tube dilated at middle, 5 – 10 mm, throat glabrous or pilose facing stamens; lobes obovate, as long as tube. Stamens included, inserted at middle of corolla tube. Ovary glabrous. Follicles linear, 10–25 cm × 3 – 10 mm. Seeds oblong, 1.5–2 cm, coma 1.5–4 cm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wan Chai Gap, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 970; HK sheet 18790, 33872.
Distribution: E, C, S & SW China, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Xizang; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Sunny edges of forests, thickets. Flowering: Feb. – Jun.

Tradescantia pallida (Rose) D. R. Hunt 紫鴨跖草
Kew Bull. 30: 452. 1975; FFJ 6: 457. 1995.
Setcreasea pallida Rose, Contrib. U. S. Natl. Herb. 13(9): 294. 1911.

Perennial herb, whole plant purple in colour; stems ascending or decumbent, much branched. Leaves alternate, sessile; leaf sheath 1–1.2 cm, not closely clasping the stem; leaf blade lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.5–3 cm, base narrowed to the sheath, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous, long-ciliate on the narrowed portion of the base. Flower clusters subsessile, terminal on apex of branches, subtended by bracts; bracts 2, leaf-like, conduplicate, one larger up to 6 × 2 cm, glabrous. Sepals 3, free, oblong. Petals 3, purple. Stamens 6, all fertile; filaments covered with moniliform hairs.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to tropical Mexico to Mesoamerica; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Setcreasea purpurea B. K. Boom previously (Check List HK Plants 304. 2002; 107. 2004).
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Setcreasea purpurea B. K. Boom previously (Check List HK Plants 304. 2002; 107. 2004).

records.text:
Tradescantia spathacea Sw. 紫背萬年青
Prodr. 57. 1788; FFJ 6: 458, fig. 412. 1995; FOC 24: 38. 2000.
Rhoeo discolor (L’Hér.) Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 660. 1853; FGZ 653, fig. 346. 1956.

Herb perennial, glabrous, 20–45 cm tall. Stems simple, erect, to 2 cm in diam. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, sessile, crowded toward apex of stem; leaf blade lanceolate, 15–35 × 2.5–5(–6) cm, somewhat fleshy, base narrowed and into the sheath, apex acuminate, dark green adaxially, purple abaxially. Flowers clusters many-flowered, shortly pedunculate, in axils of leaves and subtended by 2 bracts; bracts ovate, conduplicate, 3–4 cm. Sepals white, 3–6 mm. Petals white, ovate, 5–8 mm, apex abruptly acute. Stamens 6, all fertile; filaments white hairy. Capsule 3-valved.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 29373.
Distribution: Native to Caribbean region and C America, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tradescantia zebrina Heynh. 吊竹梅（水竹草）
Alph. Aufz. Gew. 735. 1847.
Tradescantia zebrina Bosse, Vollst. Handb. Bl.-gärtn. 4: 655. 1849, nom. illeg.; FFJ 6: 457, fig. 411. 1995; FOC 24: 38. 2000.
Zebrina pendula Schnizl., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 7: 870. 1849; FGZ 654. 1956.

Perennial herb, ± succulent; stems prostrate or decumbent, branched, rooting at nodes. Leaves alternate, sessile; leaf sheath 8–12 mm, green, with purple longitudinal lines, sparsely villous or glabrescent, mouth fringed with long hairs; leaf blade elliptic-ovate, 3–7 × 1.5–3 cm, base rounded, ± oblique, apex acute or acuminate, adaxially green or purplish, with 2 longitudinal, silver stripes, abaxially purple, glabrous or sparsely pilose at base near the sheath. Flowers in clusters subtended by bracts; bracts 2, leaf-like, 1 larger, ciliate. Sepals lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, ca. 5 × 1.5 mm. Corolla tube white, ca. 1.2 cm; lobes rose pink, ovate, ca. 6 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 6, all fertile; filaments covered with purplish blue multicellular hairs. Capsule 3-valved. Seeds rugulose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1724, 1769.
Distribution: Native to tropical America, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Trema cannabina Lour. 光葉山黃麻
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 563. 1790; FGD 2: 224. 1991; FOC 5: 15. 2003.

Shrub or small tree to 6 m tall, monoecious. Branchlets slender, with appressed pubescence when young, later glabrescent. Petiole 0.6–1 cm, with appressed hairs; leaves nearly membranous, ovate, long ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base rounded, truncate or shallowly cordate, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, margin crenate-serrate; smooth to slightly scabrous adaxially, glabrous abaxially except for scattered tightly appressed hairs on main veins, basally 3-veined; lateral veins usually 3 pairs. Cymes as long as petiole or slightly longer, subglabrous. Male flowers ca. 1 mm in diam. Female flowers ca. 2 mm in diam. Drupes ovoid-globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., shortly stalked, rugate when dry.

Locality: Shing Mun. HK sheet 40449.
Distribution: S, E & SE China; E & SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thickets and open places. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Fibre.

Trema orientalis (L.) Blume 異色山黃麻
Mus. Bot. 2: 62. 1852; FHN 2: 369. 1965; FGD 2: 223. 1991; FOC 5: 13. 2003.
Celtis orientalis L., Sp. Pl. 1044. 1753.

Tree or shrub, up to 20 m. Branchlets grey-brown, hairy. Leaves leathery, ovate-oblong or ovate, 10 –18 × 5 –9 cm, base cordate, slightly oblique, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrulate, discolour on both surfaces, pale green or grey-green adaxially, grey-white or greenish-grey and densely pubescent abaxially, 3-veined; lateral veins 4 – 6 pairs. Male cymes 1.8 –2.5 cm. Male flowers: 1.5 –2 mm in diam., sessile; sepals 5, ovate-oblong, puberulent outside, ciliate. Female inflorescence 1–2.5 cm. Female flowers: stalked; sepals 5–4, triangular-ovate, 1–1.5 mm. Drupes black, subglobose, slightly compressed, 2.5 –3.5 mm in diam., slightly wrinkled. Seeds ovoid, 2–3 mm in diam.

Locality: Shek Kong. P. S. Choi 432; HK sheet 34720.
Distribution: S & SW China, Fujian, Taiwan; S flank of Himalayas, India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Japan, Polynesia, Australia to Tropical Africa.
Ecology: Forests or open places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Fibre.

Trema tomentosa (Roxb.) Hara 山黃麻
Fl. E. Himalaya 2nd. Rep. 19. 1971; FOC 5: 13. 2003.
Celtis tomentosa Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. Carey 2: 66. 1832.
Trema amboinensis (Willd.) Blume, Mus. Bot. 2: 61. 1852, p.p.; FKH 243. 1912.
Celtis amboinensis Willd., Sp. Pl., ed. 4., 4(2): 997. 1805, p.p.
Sponia velutina Planch., Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. 10: 327. 1848, p.p.; FHK 324. 1861.

Small tree or shrub, up to 10 m tall. Branchlets densely tomentose. Leaves broadly ovate or ovate-oblong, rarely broadly lanceolate, 7–5 × 3 –7 cm, base cordate, distinctly oblique, apex acuminate or cuspidate, rarely acute, margin serrulate, concolour on both surfaces, very rough and hirsute adaxially, brown or grey brown pubescent abaxially, 3-veined; lateral veins 4 –5 pairs. Male cymes 2–4.5 cm. Male flowers: 1.5 –2 mm in diam., subsessile; sepals 5, ovate-oblong, puberulous outside, ciliate; stamens 5; rudimentary ovary obovateoblong. Female inflorescences 1–2 cm. Female flowers: shortly stalked; sepals 5–4, triangular-ovate, 1–1.5 mm; ovary glabrous. Drupes brown-black or purple-black, ovoid, 2–3 mm in diam., irregularly rugate, with persistent calyx. Seeds ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 935, 2128.
Distribution: Xizang, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Japan, islands of South Pacific.
Ecology: Flowering: Dec.; fruiting: Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Materials (fibre, timber), medicinal (folklore).

Trichosanthes anguina L. 蛇瓜
Sp. Pl. 2: 1008. 1753; FHN 1: 480. 1965; FRPS 73(1): 248, pl. 61: 1–3. 1986; FFJ 5: 260, fig. 243. 1993.
Trichosanthes cucumerina L. var. anguina (L.) Haines, Bot. Bihar Orissa 388. 1922; FGD 3: 134. 1995.

Annual herbs, monoecious, without tuberous root. Stems slender, branched, ridged and sulcate, pubescent and hispid. Tendrils 2–3-branched. Petioles 3 –8 cm; leaf blade membranous, suborbicular or reniform-orbicular, 8–16 × 12–16 cm, base cordate, margin sparsely serrate, deeply (3–)5(–7)-lobed, pubescent on both surfaces, sparsely hispid adaxially. Male racemes 8 –15-flowered, usually paired with a female flower; peduncle 10 –18 cm; pedicels 5–2 cm, erect; bracteoles minute, subulate-lanceolate, 3 mm; Male flowers: calyx-tube subcylindrical, 2.5 –3 cm, densely pubescent and sparsely hispid; lobes reflexed, ca. 2 mm; corolla white, lobes ovate-oblong, 7– 8 mm, 3-veined, apex long fimbriate. Female flowers: solitary; pedicles to 1 cm, villous; perianth as in male flowers; ovary clavate, densely pubescent and hispid. Fruit cylindric, smooth, often contorted, 1–2 m long, 3– 4 cm in diam., orange when mature. Seed oblong, embedded in fresh red pulp, finely rugulose, margin undulate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 885; L. T. Lo 517; HK sheet 12016.
Distribution: Cultivated in China. Native to India; also cultivated in E Africa, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (root and seed).

Trichosanthes cucumeroides (Seringe) Maxim. 王瓜
Enum. Pl. Jap. 1: 172. 1873
Bryonia cucumeroides Ser., Prodr. 3: 308. 1828.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious, with tuberous roots. Stems slender, branched, grooved, pubescent. Petioles 3–10 cm, densely minutely tomentose and hispidulous; leaf blade broadly ovate or orbicular, papery, 5 –13(–19) × 5 –12(–18) cm, often 3 –5-lobed, sometimes unlobed, base deeply cordate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin serrulate or undulate-dentate; minutely tomentose and hispidulous adaxially; densely and minutely tomentose abaxially. Male flowers in racemes; peduncle 5–10 cm, striate, pubescent; bracteoles linear-lanceolate, 2–3 mm, entire, pubescent, rarely bracteoles absent; calyx-tube 6–7 cm, minutely tomentose, lobes linearlanceolate, 3– 6 × 1.5 mm, entire; corolla white, lobes oblong-ovate, 14–15 × 6 –7 mm, very long fimbriate at apex. Female flowers solitary; pedicels 0.5–1 cm; ovary ellipsoid, densely pubescent; perianth as in male flowers. Fruit ovoid, ovoid-ellipsoid or globose, 6 –7 × 4 –5.5 cm, orange-red, smooth, beaked. Seeds transversely ellipsoid, 7–12 × 7–14 mm, deep brown, 3-locular; the two lateral ones large ca. 4.5 mm in diam., tuberculate.

Locality: Hong Kong without locality. [fide Dunn & Tutcher, 1912]
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Trichosanthes pedata Merr. & Chun 叉指葉栝樓
Sunyatsenia 2: 20. 1934; FHN 1: 482. 1956; FRPS 73(1): 234. 1986; FGD 3: 137, fig. 98. 1995.
Trichosanthes pedata Merr. & Chun var. yunnanensis C. Y. Cheng & Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12(4): 445, pl. 87: 4b & pl. 88: 28. 1974.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems slender, striate, grooved. Tendrils 2-branched. Leaves (3 –)5-foliolate. Petioles 2.5 – 5.5 cm; leaflets lanceolate or oblong-oblancelate, papery, 3 –14 × 1.2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely denticulate, hispidulous or white-punctate adaxially, glabrous abaxially; petiolules 2– 4 mm. Male racemes 8 –19 cm; peduncle and pedicels brownpubescent; bracteoles obovate or rhombic-ovate, 1–2 cm, pubescent, apex laciniate or dentate. Male flowers: calyx-tubes 2– 4 cm, lobes triangular-lanceolate, 0.7–1 cm, entire; corolla white. Female flowers: solitary. Fruit globose, 5 – 6 cm in diam., orange-yellow, smooth. Seeds many, ovate or obovate, slightly tumid, 1–1.2 × 0.8 cm.

Locality: Kop Tong.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Hunan, Yunnan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Trichosanthes ovigera Blume 全緣栝樓（野王瓜）
Bijdr. 934. 1826; FRPS 73(1): 255, pl. 63: 6–13. 1986; FGD 3: 133, fig. 94. 1995, p.p. excl. syn. T. cucumeroides (Ser.) Maxim., T. dicoelosperma Clarke, T. baviensis Gagnep., T. hainanensis Hayata, T. trichocarpa C. Y. Wu ex C. Y. Cheng & Yueh.
Trichosanthes himalensis C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 2(6): 608. 1879; FKH 111. 1912.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems slender, grooved, pubescent. Petioles 4–12 cm, striate, pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate-cordate to suborbicular, 7–19 × 7– 8 cm, unlobed or shortly trilobed or 3 –5-lobed, base deeply cordate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely serrulate or undulate-dentate, pubescent and hispidulous adaxially, minutely tomentose abaxially. Male flowers in racemes, peduncle 10 –26 cm, striate, densely pubescent; pedicels ca. 5 mm; bracteoles lanceolate or oblanceolate, ca. 1.6 × 0.5 –0.6 cm, margin triangular-dentate; calyx-tube tubular, ca. 5 mm; lobes triangular-ovate, 7–10 × 2–3 mm, entire. Female flowers solitary; pedicels 1–3.5 cm, striate, pubescent; calyx-tube terete, 2–5 cm, glabrous or pubescent; ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.3 –0.5 cm. Fruit ovoid or fusiform ellipsoid, 5 –7 × 2.5 – 4 cm, smooth, beaked. Seeds triangular in outline, 7–9 × 7– 8 mm, turgid with a central thickened zone; 3-locular; two lateral locules empty.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Chuen Lung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ping Shan, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. Y. W. Lam 368, 959, 1019.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, E Himalaya, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Trichosanthes rosthornii Harms 中華栝樓
Engl., Bot. Jahrb. 29: 603. 1901; FRPS 73(1): 243. 1986; FGD 3: 134, pl. 95. 1995.
Trichosanthes crenulata C.Y. Cheng & C.H. Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 18(3): 343 –344, pl. 6: 9, 20, 23. 1980.
Trichosanthes kirilowii auct. non Maxim.: FKH 111. 1912.
Trichosanthes guizhouensis C.Y. Cheng & C.H. Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 18(3): 344 –345, pl. 3 & pl. 6: 10. 1980.
Trichosanthes stylopodifera C.Y. Cheng & C.H. Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 18(3): 341, pl. 6: 7, 22. 1980.
Trichosanthes uniflora Hao, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 68(5): 640 – 641. 1938.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems grooved, glabrous or sparsely puberulous. Tendrils 2–7-branched. Petioles 2.5 –7 cm, sparsely puberulous; leaf blade variable in shape, broadly ovate to suborbicular, papery, 7–18 × 6 –16 cm, deeply 3–7-lobed, base cordate or hastate, apex acuminate, rarely acute or obtuse, margin remotely dentate or sometimes undulate, glabrous or sparsely puberulous on both surfaces. Male racemes 8–20 cm, several to many-flowered; peduncle 8–10 cm; pedicels up to ca. 7 cm; bracteoles leaf-like, 6 –25 mm, margin irregularly erose. Male flowers: calyx-tube narrowly cylindric, 1.5–3 cm, lobes subulate-linear, 7–14 mm. Female flowers: solitary; pedicels 5 –8 cm, puberulous; ovary ellipsoid, 1–2 × 0.5 –1 cm, puberulous. Fruit globose or ellipsoid, 8 –16 × 7–10 cm, smooth, glabrous, orange-yellow. Seeds ovate-oblong, compressed, 1.2–2.2 cm, brown, marginate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1509; W. J. Tutcher 9544.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hubei, Shaanxi, Gansu.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (root & fruit).
Notes: The species was reported as Trichosanthes kirilowii Maxim. previously (Check List HK Plants 42. 1993).
records.uses:
Medicinal (root & fruit).
Notes: The species was reported as Trichosanthes kirilowii Maxim. previously (Check List HK Plants 42. 1993).

records.text:
Tridax procumbens L. 羽芒菊
Sp. Pl. 900. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 15. 1969; FRPS 75: 385, pl. 65: 5 – 7. 1979; FGD 8: 138, fig. 74. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1084, pl. 517, photo 493. 1998.

Perennial herbs; stem slender and decumbent, 15–50 cm, branched near the base, pilose. Petiole short, 0.3–1 cm. Leaves ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–4.5 × 0.8–3 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate with tooth size uneven, usually with 1–2 pairs of shallow lobes near base, pilose on both surfaces. Capitula 1–1.5 cm across, solitary. Peduncle 8–23 cm. Involucres campanulate, 7–8 × 6 mm; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, acute or abruptly acute, outer 1–2 layers herbaceous green, tinged purple, strongly pilose; the outermost ones ovate, 5–6 × 2 mm; the median ones ovate‑oblong, longer and broader, 7 mm × 3 mm, with scarious purplish margin; the innermost scarious, oblong, 7–8 mm × 2.5 mm, purplish, less hairy. Receptacle convex, paleae persistent, linear, 7–8 × 1.2 mm, acuminate, slightly serrulate near apex, hyaline, shinny, yellowish to brownish purple apically and along midvein, hairy at apical portion. Marginal ligulate florets 5 or 6 in one row, pistillate, corolla pale yellow or cream white, ligule elliptic, 4 × 3 mm, apex deeply 2–3‑lobed, acute, with 3 longitudinal lines of hair on the abaxial side, tube elongate, 3–3.5 mm, pubescent. Disk tubular florets many, hermaphrodite, corolla yellow, narrowly trumpet‑shaped, 6–7 mm, distal end 5‑lobed, hairy outside. Cypselae brown, oblong‑cuneate, 2–2.5 mm, densely silky hairy. Pappus unequal in length, about 5–7 mm, spreading, plumose, yellowish or brownish.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1432; H. Y. Yeung 528; S. Y. Hu 6790 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to tropical America, distributed in S & SE China as well as Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Nov. –Apr. of the following year.

Trifolium repens L. 白車軸草
Sp. Pl. 767. 1753; FRPS 42(2): 334. 1998.

Perennial glabrous herb, 10 – 30 cm tall. Stems creeping. Stipules ovate-lanceolate, base sheath-like. Leaves digitately 3-foliolate; leaflets obovate to suborbicular, 8 – 20 × 8 – 16 mm, base attenuate, apex emarginate or obtuse, minutely denticulate, lateral veins ca. 13 pairs, elevated on both surfaces. Petioles 1.5 mm. Inflorescence globular, terminal, 15 – 40 mm in diam., densely 20 – 50(–80)-flowered. Peduncles double as long as petioles. Flowers 7–12 mm. Calyx campanulate, teeth 5, lanceolate, slightly unequal. Corolla white, milk-yellow or reddish; vexillum elliptic, double as long as wings or keel; keel slightly shorter than wings. Pods oblong. Seeds 3 – 4, broadly ovoid.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 3246; Y. W. Lam 1315; K. Y. Tam 108.
Distribution: Native to Europe, N Africa, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Cultivated or naturalized. Flowering & fruiting: May– Oct.
Uses: Forage, green manure.

Trigonostemon chinensis Merr. 三寶木

Philipp. J. Sci. 21(5): 498 – 499. 1922; FRPS 44(2): 167, pl. 43: 1 – 5. 1996.


Shrub, 2–4 m tall; young branches densely tawny pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 1–2 cm, hispidulous to glabrescent, with 2 conical glands at apex; leaf blade thin-papery, obovate-elliptic to oblong, 8–18 × 3–5.5 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acute, usually attenuate into caudate, hirtose or villose on both surfaces when young, glabrous or glabrescent in age, usually densely tuberculate adaxially, margin entire or obscurely serrulate on upper part; lateral veins 6–8. Racemes terminal, 9–18 cm, pilose or hispidulous to glabrescent. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 2–5 mm; sepals 5, oblong, ca. 1.2 mm, pilose; petals obovate, 5–6.5 mm, yellow; disk annular; stamens 3, filaments connate up to middle, upper half free. Female flowers: pedicels clavate, 1–15 cm; sepals 5, lanceolate, unequal, 5–6 mm, pilose abaxially; petals obovate, 12 mm, yellow; ovary glabrous; styles 3, short, stigmas subcapitate. Capsules subglobose, ca. 1.2 cm in diam., glabrous, with 3 longitudinal grooves.


Locality: Lantau Peak. F. W. Xing 9655 (HKU, HK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi.

Ecology: Forests, very rare. Flowering: Jan.–Sep.; fruiting: May–Nov.

Tripterospermum nienkui (C. Marquand) C. J. Wu 香港雙蝴蝶（蔓龍膽）
Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 4(3): 132 – 133. 1984; FRPS 62: 270. 1988; FFJ 4: 405. 1989; FOC 16: 11. 1995; FGD 4: 316, fig. 184. 2000.
Gentiana nienkui C. Marquand, Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1931: 76. 1931.
Crawfurdia fasciculata Wall., Tent. Fl. Napal. 63. 1826.

Rhizomes short. Stems subterete, spirally twisted, twining, striate; internodes 5 – 16 cm. Petiole 1 – 1.5 cm, slender; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate to ovate, 3 – 9 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded to subcordate, apex acuminate and sometimes caudate, margin crenulate, veins 3 – 5. Inflorescences 1‑flowered or cymose; bracts 1 – 4 pairs, lanceolate to ovate, 0.3 – 1 cm. Pedicel 0.5 – 1 cm. Calyx campanulate; tube 0.8 – 1.2 cm, winged; lobes lanceolate, 0.7 – 1 cm. Corolla dark violet‑blue, sometimes with green spots, narrowly campanulate, 4 – 5 cm; lobes ovate‑triangular, 4 – 7 mm; plicae triangular‑ovate, 2 – 3 mm. Filaments linear, 1.5 – 2 cm; anthers ellipsoidal, 1.2 – 2 mm. Ovary ellipsoidal, 0.5 – 2 mm, style 1.6 – 2 cm, stigma 2‑lobed. Berries included in corolla, ellipsoidal, dark purple, 2.5 – 4 × 0.6 – 0.8 cm; gynophore 1 – 3 mm. Seeds ellipsoidal to ovoid, dark purple, triquetrous, 1.5 – 2 mm, wingless.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Silver Mine Bay, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1679; Y. W. Lam 1630; HK sheet 36007.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Oct. – Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen (N. K. Chun 4011, IBSC, K) was collected from Hong Kong in 1930.

Triumfetta cana Bl. 毛刺蒴麻
Bojer. 1: 126. 1825; FRPS 49(1): 106. 1989; FGD 4: 161. 2000.
Triumfetta pilosa auct. non Roth: FHK 41. 1861.
Triumfetta pseudocana Sprag. & Craib, Kew Bull. Misc. Inform. 1: 23. 1911.
Triumfetta tomentosa Bojer, Bouton Rapp. Ann. Maur. 19. 1842; FHN 2: 62. 1965.

Erect subshrub, 0.6 –2 m tall. Branchlets densely yellowish brown-stellate-tomentose. Petioles 0.5–3 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate lanceolate, 4– 8 × 2.4 cm, papery, base rounded, apex acuminate, margin irregularly serrate, adaxial surface sparsely, abaxial surface densely stellate-tomentose; basal veins 3– 5. Cymes often 2–6 clustered in leaf axils; peduncle ca. 3 mm; pedicels 1.5 mm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 5–7 mm, stellate-tomentose abaxially. Petals oblong, slightly shorter than sepals, yellow, shortly stalked at base, sparsely stellate-tomentose. Stamens 8 –10(–12). Ovary covered with spiny hairs, 4-locular; stigma 3 – 5-lobed. Capsule globose, ca. 1–1.5 cm in diam. with spines, dehiscing into 4 valves, spines slender, 5– 8 mm, curved, tip straight, not hooked, pubescent. Seeds 2 per locule.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Yuen Tun Ha, Shek Kong, Tai To Yan, Wu Kau Tang. Y. S. Lau 2633; P. S. Choi 371; H. C. Tang 1422.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang; SE Asia.
Ecology: Secondary forests and dry thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Triumfetta rhomboidea Jacq. 刺蒴麻
Enum. Syst. Pl. 22. 1760; FRPS 49(1): 109. 1989; FGD 4: 160, fig. 103. 2000.
Triumfetta bartramia L., Syst. ed. 10: 1044. 1757, nom. superfl. for Bartramia indica L.; FHN 2: 62. 1965.
Bartramia indica L., Sp. Pl. 389. 1753, non Triumfetta indica Lam. 1791.
Triumfetta angulata Lam., Encycl. 3: 421. 1791; FHK 41. 1861.

Erect subshrub, 0.5 –1.5 m. Branchlets greyish browntomentose. Petioles 1– 5 cm; leaf blade variable, those on the lower part of stem broadly ovate-orbicular, or rhomboid-ovate, 3 – 8 × 2– 6 cm, papery, upper part 3-lobed, base rounded; those on the upper part of stem smaller, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, not lobed, sparsely hairy adaxially, stellate-pubescent abaxially; margin irregularly serrate; basal veins 3 – 5. Cymes several in leaf axils. Peduncle and pedicels very short. Sepals narrowly oblong, 5– 6 mm, with a mucro at apex, stellate-hispid abaxially. Petals slightly shorter than sepals, yellow, hairy along margin. Stamens 10. Ovary spiny. Capsule subglobose, ca. 4 – 6 mm in diam. with spines, indehiscent, grey yellow-pubescent; spines 2–3 mm, glabrous, hooked. Seeds 2– 6 per locule.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2079; L. T. Lo 191; Y. S. Lau 2184.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Tropaeolum majus L. 旱金蓮
Sp. Pl. 1: 345. 1753; FGZ 154. 1956; FFJ 2: 346, fig. 264. 1985; FRPS 43(1): 90, pl. 27. 1998.

Annual trailing herb, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Petiole 9–16 cm; leaf blade suborbicular, 2–8 cm in diam., margin variously angled or sinuate but otherwise entire, usually papillose abaxially, 5–9 main veins radiating from petiole. Flowers axillary, solitary, yellow, red, creamy-white or varicolored, 2.5–5 cm in diam. Pedicel 6–13 cm. Receptacle cupular. Sepals connate at base, oblong-lanceolate, 1.7 cm, margin membranous; spur 2.5–4 cm, straight or curved. Petals mostly orbicular, apex sometimes acute or emarginate; upper 2 often entire, 2.5–5 × 1–1.8 cm; lower 3 smaller, clawed, claw finely fringed at margin. Fruit oblate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1796.
Distribution: Native to S America (Peru and Brazil), cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tropidia curculigoides Lindl. 短穗竹莖蘭（仙茅竹莖蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 497. 1840; FHK 359. 1861; FRPS 17: 122. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1057. 2000; FGD 7: 342, fig. 171. 2006; FOC 25: 195. 2009.
Tropidia hongkongensis Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(249): 40. 1903; FKH 267. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 53, fig. 23. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, 30–70 cm tall at flowering time, with short and thick rhizome and fibrous roots. Stems erect, unbranched or occasionally branched, internodes usually 2–4 cm. Leaves elliptic-lanceolate, 15–25 × 2–4 cm, apex acuminate. Flowers green-white, in terminal or axillary racemes; sepals lanceolate, 7–10 mm, base of the lateral two connate; petals 6–8 mm; lip ovate-lanceolate, acute; column 3 mm; anthers 1.5 mm. Capsules oblong, 2 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 7119.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Taiwan; India, Sikkim, Myanmar, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Shady area along streams. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

Tulipa gesneriana L. 鬱金香
Sp. Pl. 1: 306. 1753; FRPS 14: 90. 1980; FGD 6: 338, fig. 194. 2005.

Perennial herb. Bulbs ovoid, slightly tapering upward, ca. 2 cm in diam.; tunic thin, papery, with a few appressed hairs near base and summit. Stem erect, 20–40 cm. Leaves 3–5, alternate, linear-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 10–21 × 1–6 cm, sessile and clasping at base, fringed with a few short hairs near apex. Flowers large, solitary and terminal, variously coloured, ranging from white to yellow, pink to purple. Perianth segments 6, free, outer 3 elliptic to lanceolate, 5–7 × 2–4 cm, inner ones shorter and broader, obovate. Stamens 6, equal; filaments glabrous, dilated below middle; anthers basifixed. Style obsolete; stigma 3-lobed, lobes thickened. Capsule loculicidally 3-valved.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 11.
Distribution: Cultivated in China and elsewhere; possibly originated from SW or S Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

Turpinia arguta (Lindl.) Seem. 銳尖山香圓
Bot. Voy. Herald 371. 1857; FHK 48. 1861; FKH 67. 1912; FRPS 46: 27. 1981; FFJ 3: 298, fig. 203. 1987; FGD 3: 284, fig. 188. 1995.
Ochranthe arguta Lindl., Edwards's Bot. Reg. 21: pl. 1819. 1836.
Eyrea vernalis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 331. 1851.
Staphylea simplicifolia Gardner & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 309 – 310. 1849.

Deciduous shrub, 1–3 m. Leaves unifoliolate; petioles 1.5–2 cm; leaflets thickly papery, long elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 7–22 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate, margin sparsely glandular-serrate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 10–13 pairs, prominent abaxially. Panicles terminal, 5–15 cm. Flowers white, 0.5–1.2 cm; pedicels 1–2 mm; bracteoles 2. Sepals long-ovate, 3–6 mm, ciliate. Petals spathulate or obovate-elliptic. Filaments ca. 8 mm, sparsely pubescent. Styles hairy. Fruit subglobose, 0.7–1 cm in diam., red when mature, rough, base with persistent disk. Seeds 2–3, yellow.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 506, 547; K. L. Yip 4525.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests of valleys. Flowering: Spring to summer; fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Turpinia montana (Blume) Kurz 山香圓
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 44(2): 182. 1857; FHN 3: 99. 1974; FYN 2: 360. 1979; FRPS 46: 33. 1981; FGD 3: 286. 1995.
Zanthoxylum montana Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 248. 1825.
Turpinia cochinchinensis auct. non (Lour.) Merr.: Check List HK Plants 54. 1993.
Turpinia nepalensis auct. non Wall. ex Wight & Arn.: FHK 48. 1861.
Turpinia pomifera auct. non DC.: FKH 67. 1912.

Small tree or shrub, 3–8 m tall. Leaves imparipinnately compound, 3–5(–7)-foliolate; lateral petiolules 2–3 mm, apical one to 1.5 cm; leaflets leathery, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 5–7 × 2–5.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate, margin glandular-serrate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 8 –10 pairs, prominent on both surfaces. Panicles terminal or axillary, 8–12 cm. Flowers 3–4 mm in diam.; pedicels ca. 1.5 mm. Sepals broadly elliptic, ca. 1.3 mm, ciliate. Petals pale yellow, membranous, elliptic or long-elliptic, ca. 2 mm. Stamens slightly shorter than petals, filaments glabrous. Fruit subglobose, green to purplish brown, 4–7 mm in diam. Seeds 3–4, ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 610, 649; HK sheet 39972.
Distribution: S & SW China; Indochina, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug. – Oct.; fruiting: Aug. – Dec.

Tylophora ovata (Lindl.) Hook. ex Steud. 娃兒藤
Nomencl. Bot. (ed. 2) 2: 726. 1841; FRPS 63: 533, pl. 200. 1977; FGD 1: 535, fig. 616. 1987; FOC 16: 258. 1995.
Diplolepis ovata Lindl., Trans. Hort. Soc. London 6: 286. 1826.
Tylophora hispida Decne., Prodr. 8: 610. 1844; FHK 225. 1861; FKH 172. 1912.

Lianas, to 5 m, rusty hispid, villous, or pubescent except for adaxial surface of leaves and sometimes follicles. Petioles 0.5–3 cm; leaf blade ovate, 2.5–12.5(–16) × 1.2–9 cm, base cordate to subcordate, apex acute or short‑acuminate and mucronate, lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences 4–13 cm; peduncle 0.5–2 cm; rachis simple, zigzag, occasionally forked. Cymules sessile, raceme‑like, densely flowered; pedicels threadlike, 5 – 10 mm. Sepals subulate‑acuminate to ovate, ciliate; basal glands 5 or absent. Corolla yellowish or yellow‑green, rotate, ca. 5 mm in diam., glabrous or puberulent; tube ca. 1 mm; lobes oblong‑ovate or ovate, ca. 1.5–2.5 × 1–1.2 mm, obtuse. Corona‑lobes ovoid, pouched, apex obtuse, covering the base of anthers. Anther with rounded appendages; pollinia globose to ovoid, horizontal. Ovaries glabrous; stigma head depressed. Follicles lanceolate to oblong‑lanceolate in outline, 40–70 × 3–12 mm, puberulent or glabrous, apex sometimes recurved. Seeds oval, 5–7 × 2–4 mm; coma 2–3.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2339, 3226; P. S. Choi 543.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Typha angustifolia L. 水燭
Sp. Pl. 2: 971. 1753; FRPS 8: 7, pl. 2: 6–7. 1992; FFJ 6: 3, fig. 1. 1995; FGD 6: 379. 2005; FOC 23: 162. 2010.

Perennial marsh herb; stems erect, 0.5–1.5(–3) m tall, stout. Leaves linear, spongy, 50–80(–120) cm × 4–10 mm, transverse section semicircular. Inflorescences a club-shaped spike, 30–60 cm, with a naked gap about 0.5–10 cm between the upper staminate part and the lower pistillate part. Male flowers with 2–3 stamens; female flowers with many filiform bracteoles on the stalk of ovary. Fruit narrowly elliptical.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 732, 1166; HK sheet 41712.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; temperate and subtropical regions of Asia, N Africa, Europe and N America.
Ecology: Marshes, swamps, shallow water of lakes and ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Typhonium blumei Nicolson & Sivad. 犁頭尖（山半夏）
Blumea 27: 494, fig. 4. 1981; A. Hay, Blumea 37: 373, fig. 17. 1993; FGD 9: 198, fig. 113. 2009; FOC 23: 34. 2010.
Typhonium divaricatum auct. non (L.) Decne: Nouv. Ann. Mus. Paris 31: 367. 1834; FKH 288. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 111. 1979. Arum divaricatum auct. non L.: FHK 342. 1861.

Perennial herb; tuber subglobose, 1–2 cm in diam. Leaves 4–8; petiole green, 20–40 cm, basal; leaf blade cordate-hastate, ovate or deltoid in outline, 5–10 × 3–9 cm, apex acuminate, the 2 basal lobes ovate-lanceolate or oblong, divaricate; lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Peduncle emerging from petiole sheath, pale green. Spathe tubular and green at the base for 14–20 mm, upper part expanded into a deep purple ovate limb, ca. 5 cm broad, and tapering into a long and slender apex. Spadix subequaling spathe, deep purple; female portion at the base, 0.4–0.6 cm, with several rows of female flowers, then followed with several rows of subulate neutral flowers; male portion 0.6–0.8 cm, orange; appendage purple, 10–13 cm, emerging very bad excrement smell, long cylindrical. Berries obovoid, few-seeded.

Locality: Magazine Gap, Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 30636, 31436.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, roadsides. Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Uncaria hirsuta Havil. 毛鈎藤
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 33; 88. 1897; FKH 125. 1912; Ridsdale, Blumea 24(1): 94. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 334. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 255. 1999; FGD 6: 157, fig. 75. 2005.

Woody climbers. Young shoots terete or slightly angular, hirsute. Stipules broadly ovate, deeply bifid; lobes ovate, sometimes with long acuminate apex, adaxially glabrous, but with glandular hairs at the base, abaxially puberulent, and with scattered long hairs. Leaves opposite, leathery; petioles 3–10 mm, hairy; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, 8–12 × 5–7 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate, adaxially somewhat scabrous with scattered hairs, abaxially sparsely to densely strigose, with hairy domatia in axils of lateral veins; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers subsessile, densely crowded in globular heads of 3–5 cm in diam. across corollas. Receptacle densely hairy. Peduncles 2.5–5 cm, unbranched, pubescent, axillary or rarely 3 together at the ends of the branches, each bearing a flower‑head. Calyx‑tube ca. 2 mm, pubescent abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑oblong, 2–3 mm, densely hairy. Corolla‑tube white, 7–10 mm, abaxially pubescent, 5‑lobed; lobes oblong, 2–3 mm, densely hairy on abaxial surface. Style 4–6 mm, exserted. Fruiting head 4.5–5 cm in diam.; fruitlets 10–15 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Shek O, Ma On Shan, Kei Ling Ha, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1709; N. H. Li 37; K. Y. Tam 119.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets by streams or in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The holotype specimen (C. Ford, s.n., K) was collected by C. Ford from Lantau Island. How (1946) cited the specimen W. J. Tutcher 613 as an “isotype”, which was collected from Lantau Island in April 1896.

Uncaria homomalla Miq. 北越鈎藤
Fl. Ned. Ind. 2: 343. 1857; Ridsdale, Blumea 24(1): 95. 1978; FRPS 71(1): 258. 1999; FYN 15: 124. 2003.
Uncaria tonkinensis Havil., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 33: 89, pl. 2, fig. 19 – 20. 1897; Pitard in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. Indo‑Chine 3: 52. 1922.

Woody climbers, 10–25 m or longer. Young shoots tetragonal, slightly rusty puberulent. Stipules triangular to narrowly triangular, 5–8 mm, 2‑lobed to middle; lobes lanceolate. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 3–6 mm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic‑lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 8.5–10 × 3.5–5.5 cm, base obtuse to subrounded, apex acuminate or caudate, covered with short hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 8 – 9 on each side of midvein. Flowers greenish yellow, subsessile, densely crowded in globular heads of 2.5–2.8 cm in diam. across corollas. Peduncles 2.5–3 cm, axillary, compressed, bearing a terminal flower‑head. Calyx‑tube ca. 1.5 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes linear, ca. 1 mm, puberulent. Corolla‑tube 7.5–9 mm, puberulent outside, 5‑lobed; lobes narrowly oblong, ca. 2 mm. Stamens attached to the apex of corolla‑tube; anthers exserted. Style filiform, 10–11 mm, long exserted; stigma clavate. Fruiting head globose; fruitlets obovate, 4 × 2 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island (Glenealy). W. J. Tutcher 8334.
Distribution: Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, India subcontinent and Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Oct.

Uncaria macrophylla Wall. 大葉鈎藤
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 132. 1824; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 3: 32. 1880; Pitard in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. Indo‑Chine 3: 46. 1922; C. E. Ridsdale, Blumea 24(1): 78. 1978; FRPS 71(1): 249. 1999; FYN 15: 121. 2003; FGD 6: 155, fig. 74. 2005.

Woody climbers. Young shoots square to slightly angular, slightly hairy. Stipules ovate, deeply 2‑lobed; lobes narrowly ovate, abaxially pubescent, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pubecent, with colleters at the base. Leaves opposite, subleathery; petioles 3–10 mm, glabrous or sparsely puberulous; leaf blade ovate or broadly elliptic, 10– 16 × 6–12 cm, base obtuse or cordate, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous or ± pubescent on veins of adaxial surface, sparsely to densely hairy on abaxial surface, with hairy domatia in axils of lateral veins; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 6 – 9 on each side of midvein. Flowers densely crowded in globular heads of 4.5 – 5 cm in diam. across corollas. Receptacle densely hairy. Peduncles 3–7 cm, axillary, unbranched, or rarely 3 together at the ends of the branches, each bearing a flowering head; pedicels 2–5 mm. Calyx‑tube funnelform, 2 – 3 mm, covered with sericeous short hairs abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes linear oblong, 3–4 mm, finely pubescent. Corolla‑tube 9–10 mm, pubescent abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes oblong, ca. 2 mm, pubescent abaxially. Style ca. 6 mm, long exserted. Fruiting head 8–10 cm in diam.; fruitlets ca. 2 cm, pubescent.

Locality: Lantau Island. N. H. Li 33; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24077; HK sheet 35603.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Uraria crinita (L.) Desv. ex DC. 猫尾草
Prodr. 2: 324. 1825; FHK 81. 1861; FKH 80. 1912; FRPS 41: 68. 1995; FGD 5: 283. 2003.
Hedysarum crinitum L., Mant. Pl. 1: 102. 1767.

Subshrub, 1 – 1.5 m tall, few-branched, grey pubescent with minute hooked hairs. Stipules broadly lanceolate, with long points. Leaves odd-pinnate, often 3-foliolate at lower part of stem; leaflets subleathery, oblong, ovate-lanceolate or ovate, terminal one 6 – 15 × 3–8 cm, lateral ones smaller, base rounded or subcordate, apex acute, tomentose on veins of both surfaces, lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 15 – 30 cm, densely grey-white hirsute. Bracts ovate or lanceolate, up to 3 cm, white ciliate. Calyx shallow cup-like, short hirsute, 2 upper lobes 3 mm, 3 lower lobes 3.5 mm. Corolla purple, ca. 6 mm. Pods slightly tomentose; segments 2– 4, elliptic, reticulate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, Ta Kwu Ling, Lantau Island, Tsing Yi, Po Toi Islands. Y. S. Lau 326, 885; Y. W. Lam 1068.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Dry open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. – Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Uraria lagopodioides (L.) Desv. ex DC. 狸尾豆
Mém. Soc. Linn. Paris 4: 309. 1826; FKH 80. 1912; FRPS 41: 69. 1995; FGD 5: 281, fig. 151. 2003.
Hedysarum lagopodioides L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1198. 1753.

Decumbent or spreading herb, up to 60 cm tall. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate, rarely simple; leaflets papery, terminal one suborbicular, elliptic or ovate, mucronate, base rounded or cordate, lateral ones smaller, grey-yellow pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 3 –6 cm, densely flowered. Calyx 5-lobed, 2 upper lobes triangular, ca. 2 mm, 3 lower ones subulate, bristle like, three times as long as upper ones. Corolla purplish, 6 mm; vexillum obovate; wings adherent to longer upcurved keel. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary glabrous. Pods enclosed in calyx, segments 1 – 2(–3), brown, elliptic, 2.5 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Tsim Sha Tsui, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 913; Y. W. Lam 1138; HK sheet 36071.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. –Nov.

Uraria picta (Jacq.) Desv. ex DC. 美花狸尾豆
Prodr. 2: 324. 1825; FKH 80. 1912; FRPS 41: 68. 1995; FGD 5: 283. 2003.
Hedysarum pictum Jacq., Collectanea 2: 262– 263. 1788.

Subshrub or shrub, 1–2 m tall, few-branched, shortly grey-hirsute. Stipules 1 cm, caudate, striate, grey ciliate. Leaves odd-pinnate; leaflets 5–7(–9), linear-oblong or linear-lanceolate, 6–12 × 1–2 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, pubescent on veins of both surfaces. Racemes terminal, 10–30 cm. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 2.5 cm, pilose; pedicels becoming hooked in fruit. Calyx 5-lobed, 2 upper lobes subulate, shorter, 3 lower lobes lanceolate, bristle-like, slightly longer than upper ones. Corolla violet, slightly exserted from calyx; vexillum orbicular, 6–8 mm, base clawed; wings earlike, 4–7 mm; keel spathulate, equal to wings, upcurved. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary glabrous. Pods silver grey, glabrous, segments 3–5, ovate, 3 × 2 mm, black with whitish reticulations, folded back on each other.

Locality: New Territories. (fide FKH 80. 1912)
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, wastelands. Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Urceola micrantha (Wall. ex G. Don) D. J. Middleton 杜仲藤
Novon 4: 151. 1994; FOC 16: 184. 1995; Fl. Thailand 7(1): 145, fig. 46. 1999.
Echites micrantha Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 75. 1837.
Ecdysanthera micrantha (Wall. ex G. Don) A. DC., Prodr. 8: 442. 1844; FHK 222. 1861; FKH 169. 1912.
Parabarium micranthum (Wall. ex G. Don) Pierre ex Spire, Caoutchouc Indo‑Chine 38. 1906; FRPS 63: 239, pl. 85. 1977; FGD 1: 479, fig. 541. 1987.

Lianas to 50 m or longer. stem 10–30 cm in diam.; branches often lenticellate. Petioles puberulent, 1.5–3 cm; leaf blade elliptic or narrowly ovate, 5–15 × 1.5–6 cm, base obtuse, apex narrowly acuminate, glabrous, lateral veins 3–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes paniculate, compact, to 9 cm; peduncle pubescent. Sepals ovate, ca. 0.8 – 1 mm, apex subacute. Corolla pink, lobes oblong, as long as to longer than the tube, to 2 mm, 1‑toothed near base. Filaments ca. 0.5 m; disk ring‑like. Ovary pilose; pistil head conical. Follicles narrowly ovoid, 9 – 23 × (0.4 – )1 – 1.2 cm, base dilated. Seeds oblong, 2 – 4 cm, coma ca. 4 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 10169; HK sheet 3789, 40675.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Ryukyu Islands, Laos, Malaysia, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed forests, thickets. Flowering: Mar. – Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Urceola rosea (Hook. & Arn.) D. J. Middleton 酸葉膠藤
Novon 4: 151. 1994; FOC 16: 184. 1995; Fl. Thailand 7(1): 149. 1999.
Ecdysanthera rosea Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 198, pl. 42. 1837; FHK 222. 1861; FKH 169. 1912; FRPS 63: 234. 1977; FGD 1: 477, fig. 538. 1987.

Lianas to 20 m. Stems dark brown, lenticels absent; branches tawny grey, young ones brownish. Petioles 0.8 – 1.2 cm; leaf blade broadly elliptic, rarely subovate, 3–7 × 1–4 cm, apex acute, glabrous, ± lustrous adaxially, glaucous abaxially, lateral veins 4 – 6 on each side of midvein. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm, obtuse. Corolla pink; tube ca. 4 mm; lobes ca. 2 mm, acute.; disk ring‑like, entire. Ovary pubescent. Follicles to 15 cm, terete, densely spotted. Seeds oblong, ca. 1 cm, coma ca. 3 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 438; N. H. Li 105; Y. W. Lam 921.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Urena lobata L. 肖梵天花（地桃花、黐頭婆）
Sp. Pl. 692. 1753; FHK 34. 1861; FKH 48. 1912; FHN 2: 96, fig. 341. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 43. 1984; FGD 2: 194, fig. 121. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 752, pl. 377. 1993.

Small shrub, to 1 m tall, much branched. Branchlets, petioles and pedicels stellate-tomentose. Petioles 1–4 cm; stipules linear, ca. 2 mm, caducous, leaf blade variable in shape, the lower ones subrotundate, rotundate or subcordate at base, shallowly 3-lobed at apex, 4 – 5 × 5 – 6 cm, often broader than long, the middle ones ovate, 5–7 × 3 – 6.5 cm, the upper ones ovate or ovate-elliptic, margin evenly serrate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially grey or yellowish tomentose, the hairs all short, erect, stellate. Flowers solitary; pedicels 3 mm. Epicalyx lobes 6 mm, basal 1/3 connate, stellate pilose. Calyx lobes 5–7 mm, densely lanate at base of keel. Corolla pink; petals 15 mm. Fruit 1 cm in diam., carpels stellate pubescent and glochidiate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 324, 325; Y. S. Lau 1990; S. Y. Hu 8766 (CUHK).
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Japan.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: A very variable species, some individuals or populations may differing from the typical form in the shape of the leaves and in the nature and density of the hairs.

Urena procumbens L. 梵天花（狗腳跡）
Sp. Pl. 692. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae 77. 1955; FHN 2: 96. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 47. 1984; FGD 2: 195. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 752. 1993.
Urena sinuata auct. non L.: FHK 34. 1861; FKH 48. 1912.

Small shrub, ca. 0.5 m tall, with horizontal spreading branches; branchlets stellate tomentose. Petioles 4–15 mm; stipules subulate, 1.5 mm, caducous; leaf blade various in shape, the lower ones ovate in outline, sinuate below the middle, 3-lobed, 1.5–6 × 1–4 cm, apex obtuse, base rounded or subcordate, evenly serrate; the upper ones ovate to elliptic, not sinuate, serrate; all leaves scabrid-hirsute on both surfaces, the hairs homogenous, all short and rigid. Flowers subfasciculate or solitary. Pedicels 2–3 mm. Epicalyx lobes 7 mm, basal onethird connate, sparsely stellate hairy. Calyx lobes 4–7 mm, ovate, acute, stellate along the median longitudinal line, the rest glabrous. Corolla pink to red; petals 10–15 mm. Staminal tube glabrous. Fruits globose, 6 mm in diam., hirsute and echinate, glochidiate. Seeds glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 329; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 21108, 22727 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

Utricularia aurea Lour. 黃花狸藻
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 26. 1790; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 296, fig. 21 – 23. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 623, fig. 190. 1989; FRPS 69: 604. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 719, pl. 329, photo 368. 1998.
Utricularia flexuosa Vahl, Enum. Pl. 1: 198. 1804; FHK 255. 1861; FKH 191. 1912.

Floating small herbs, with filiform, branched stolons, extending to 30 cm or longer. Leaves all submerged and root‑like, alternate on stolons, 2–8 cm long, pinnately divided, each pinna dichotomously divided into numerous capillary segments, interspersed with little globular traps or bladders. Traps obliquely ovoid, 1–4 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 7–15 cm, bearing a raceme of 3–6(–10) flowers; scales absent; bracts basifixed. Pedicels erect and slender at flowering time, turned downward at fruiting time. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes ovate, unequal, enlarged and spreading in fruit. Corolla yellow, 10–15 mm, upper lip broadly ovate, apex rounded, about twice the length of upper calyx‑lobe, lower lip larger, transversely elliptic; the spur obtuse, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary ovoid; style distinct. Capsule globose, 4–5 mm in diam., circumscissile; persistent style about twice as long as the capsule.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Yuen Long. W. J. Tutcher 8130; HK sheet 20925.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E to S Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Ponds and paddy fields. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

Utricularia bifida L. 挖耳草
Sp. Pl. 18. 1753; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 281, fig. 4. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 307, fig. 82. 1989; FRPS 69: 588, pl. 162: 4 – 10. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 721, pl. 331. 1998.

Small marsh herbs, with branched capillary stolons. Leaves alternate on stolons, linear to linear‑oblanceolate, 7–20(–30) × 1–4 mm, base tapering into a short petiole, apex or obtuse, margin entire, membranous, 1‑veined. Traps borne on stolons and leaf margins, globose, 0.5–1 mm, short‑stalked. Scapes usually 10–20 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10(–16) flowers; scales present, similar to the bracts; bracts basifixed, ovate, 1–2 mm. Pedicels 2–5 mm, initially spreading, turned downward at fruiting time, usually flat and dilated under the calyx. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes slightly unequal, 3–4 mm at flowering time, 5–6 mm in fruit. Corolla yellow, 6–10 mm long, upper lip oblong to oblong‑obovate, apex rounded, lower lip suborbicular; the spur subulate, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary ovoid; style short. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, ca. 2.5 mm long, opening by longitudinal slits.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sheung Shui, Sai Kung, Lo Wu, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 40, 2318; Y. S. Lau 738.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shangdong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; S to SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Utricularia caerulea L. 短梗挖耳草
Sp. Pl. 18. 1753; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 287, fig. 12. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 187, fig. 43. 1989; FRPS 69: 593, pl. 163: 8 – 11. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 724, pl. 332. 1998.
Utricularia racemosa Wall. ex Walp., Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.‑Carol. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 401. 1843; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.

Annual marsh herbs, with branched capillary stolons, usually without any leaves at flowering time. Leaves borne on stolons nodes and at the base of scape, linear to linear‑obovate, 3–20 × 0.5–2 mm, base tapering into a short petiole, apex rounded, margin entire, membranous, 1‑veined. Traps borne on stolons and leaf margins, ovoid, 0.25–1 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 5–20 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10(–16) flowers; scales few, similar to the bracts; bracts attached just above the middle, free and pointed at both ends. Pedicels very short, 0.2–1 mm. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes unequal, upper lobe oblong, 2–3 mm, lower lobe shorter, transversely elliptic. Corolla violet, pink or white, 4–10 mm, upper lip oblong to ovate‑oblong, apex retuse, lower lip broadly ovate, apex rounded or emarginate; the spur narrowly conical, usually slightly longer than the lower corolla‑lip. Ovary globose; style short. Capsule globose or ellipsoidal, 1.5–2 mm, opening by longitudinal short slits.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Ho Pui, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2453; Y. W. Lam 956, 1254.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Utricularia gibba L. 少花狸藻
Sp. Pl. 18. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 4: 724, pl. 333. 1998.
Utricularia exoleta R. Br., Prodr. 430. 1810; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 294, fig. 20. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 572, fig. 179. 1989; FRPS 69: 598. 1990; Check List HK Plants 258. 2002; 89. 2004.
Utricularia diantha Roxb. ex Roem. & Schult., Mant. 1: 169. 1822; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 191. 1912.

Floating small herbs, with filiform, branched stolons seldom above 5 cm long. Leaves all submerged and root‑like, alternate on stolons, 0.5–1.5 cm long, unbranched or dichotomously divided into a few capillary segments. Traps lateral on leaf segments, ovoid, 1–2.5 mm, stalked. Scapes slender, 5–10 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–2(– 3) flowers; scales 1, similar to the bracts; bracts basifixed. Pedicels erect or spreading, 2–12 mm. Calyx bilobed nearly to the base; lobes broadly ovate to suborbicular, subequal, 1.5–2 mm. Corolla yellow, 4–8 mm long, upper lip orbicular or broadly ovate, about twice the length of upper calyx‑lobe, apex obscurely 3‑lobed, lower lip slightly smaller; the spur conical, as long as the lower corolla‑lip, or slightly longer. Ovary ovoid; style distinct. Capsule globose, 2–3 mm in diam., opening by valves.

Locality: Happy Valley, Sha Tin, Tung Chung. HK sheet 4216, 38212.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Ponds and paddy fields. Flowering: Jun. – Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Utricularia striatula Sm. 圓葉挖耳草
Cycl. 37: Utricularia no. 17. 1819; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 289, fig. 13 – 14. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 479, fig. 147. 1989; FRPS 69: 595, pl. 163: 1 – 5. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 727, pl. 369. 1998.
Utricularia orbiculata Wall. ex A. DC., Prodr. 8: 18. 1844; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.
Utricularia harlandii Oliv. ex Benth., FHK 257. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.

Perennial lithophytic or marsh herbs, with simple, capillary stolons. Leaves borne on stolon nodes and clustered near the base of scape, persistent to the time of flowering; petioles slender, usually longer than the blade; leaf blades orbicular to transversely elliptic, 3–10 × 2–6 mm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex rounded, margin entire, membranous, with dichotomous veins. Traps borne on stolons, ovate, 0.6 – 0.8 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 5 – 15 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10 flowers; scales few, similar to the bracts; bracts attached just below the middle, narrowly ovate or oblong, 1–1.5 mm. Pedicels 2–6 mm, initially spreading, turned downward after anthesis. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes unequal, upper lip suborbicular or broadly obcordate, 1.5– 2.5 mm, apex rounded or emarginate, lower lip much smaller, oblong‑elliptic. Corolla lilac or white, 5–10 mm long, upper lip smaller, subobovate, apex 2‑toothed, lower lip orbicular to transversely elliptic, apex 3–5‑lobed; the spur subulate, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary globose; style short. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, ca. 2.5 mm long, opening by longitudinal slits.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1463; HK sheet 34406, 40768.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Marshes and rocks by streams. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The syntype specimens of Utricularia harlandii (Harland 307, K; Wilford 92, K) were collected from Hong Kong Island around 1857.

Utricularia uliginosa Vahl 濕地挖耳草
Enum. Pl. 1: 203. 1804; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 282, fig. 5. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 333, fig. 92. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 729, pl. 335. 1998.
Utricularia affinis Wight, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 373, t. 1580. 1849.
Utricularia caerulea auct. non L.: FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.

Small marsh herbs, with slender, simple, or rarely branched stolons, usually without any leaves at flowering time. Leaves alternate on stolons, linear to narrowly obovate, 25–45 × 1.5–6 mm, base attenuate, apex rounded to acute, margin entire, membranous, 3‑veined. Traps borne on stolons and leaf margins, globose, 1–1.5 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 3–12(–15) cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10 flowers; scales few, similar to the bracts; bracts basifixed, narrowly ovate, 0.8–1 mm. Pedicels filiform, 1–1.5 mm, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit, usually flat or narrowly winged. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes subequal, broadly ovate or suborbicular, 2–2.5 mm, thin and membranous. Corolla lilac, violet or white, 3–7 mm long, upper lip oblong, apex rounded or emarginate, about the length of the upper calyx‑lobe, lower lip suborbicular; the spur subulate, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary ovoid; style short. Capsule ovoid, 2–4 mm long, opening by longitudinal slits.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 408, 1253; HK sheet 39845.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; tropical Asia, extending to S Japan and Korea, also in Australia.
Ecology: Marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Uvaria boniana Finet & Gagnep. 光葉紫玉盤
Bull. Soc. Bot. France Mem. 4: 71, pl. 11A. 1906; FHN 1: 237. 1964; FGD 2: 9, fig. 5. 1991.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches stellate-pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 5–7 × 1.3–1.7 mm, pubescent or glabrous; leaf blades 13.5–15 × 3.5–5 cm, elliptic to oblong, glabrous ab- and adaxially, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acuminate; secondary veins 10–13 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or extra-axillary, 1–2-flowered. Flowers purplish-red to pink, ca. 2.5 cm in diam.; pedicels ca. 22 × 0.9 mm, glabrous; bracts near base, ca. 1 mm long, oblong to ovate, pubescent. Sepals ca. 2.5–3 mm long, subrounded, basally connate, pubescent abaxially. Petals broad ovate, apically pubescent both sides; outer petals ca. 10 × 5.5–7.5 mm; inner petals slightly smaller. Stamens numerous, ca. 1 mm long; connective truncate, papillate. Carpels ca. 20 per flower; ovary oblong, densely hairy; stigma 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 10–20 per fruit, 1.5–4 × ca. 1.5 cm, ovoid or cylindrical, rarely globose, glabrous; stipes 4–5.5 cm long, glabrous. Seeds 1–8 per monocarp, ca. 10 × 7–10 mm, ellipsoid to lenticular, blackish brown.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 182; F. W. Xing 6887.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar–Apr.; fruiting: Autumn.

Uvaria calamistrata Hance 刺果紫玉盤
J. Bot. 20: 77. 1882; FKH 29. 1912; FHN 1: 235. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 20, pl. 7. 1979; FGD 2: 10, fig. 6. 1991.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches stellate-pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 5.5–7.5 × 1.5–1.9 mm, pubescent; leaf blades 8.5–13.5 × 3.5–5.5 cm, ovate, obovate or elliptic, densely pubescent with short stellate hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate or acute; secondary veins 8– 12 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or axillary, 1– 4-flowered. Flowers pale yellow, ca. 1.8 cm diam.; pedicels ca. 6 × 4 mm, pubescent; bracts near base, ca. 5.5 × 4 mm, broad ovate, pubescent. Sepals ca. 5 × 4.5 mm, ovate, free, pubescent both sides. Petals oblong, pubescent both sides; outer petals 6–8 × 2.5–3.5 mm; inner petals subequal or slightly smaller. Stamens numerous, ca. 3 mm long; connective liguliform, slightly pubescent. Carpels 7–15 per flower; ovary cylindrical, hairy; stigma 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 1–3 per fruit, 2.7– 3 × 2–2.2 cm, ovate, rounded at apex, spiny; stipes 5.5–6.5 mm long, pubescent. Seeds ca. 6 per monocarp, ca. 12.5 × 9.5 mm, lenticular or discoid, brown.

Locality: Aberdeen, Lady Clementi's Ride, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1477; P. S. Choi 103; Y. S. Lau 1203.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Uvaria grandiflora Roxb. ex Hornem. 大花紫玉盤
Suppl. Hort. Bot. Hafn. 140. 1819; FRPS 30(2): 26, pl. 10. 1979; FGD 2: 11, fig. 8. 1991.
Uvaria purpurea Blume, Bijdr. 11. 1825; FHK 9. 1861; FKH 29. 1912; FHN 1: 235. 1964.
Uvaria platypetala Champ. ex Bentham, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 257. 1851.
Uvaria rhodantha Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 19. 1851.
Uvaria hamiltonii auct. non Hook. f. & Thomson: FKH 29. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches densely stellate-tomentose. Leaves papery or sub-leathery; petioles 6.5 –10 × ca. 1.7 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blades 15–23 × 7.5–9.5 cm, obovate or obovate-oblong, densely villous with long stellate hairs abaxially, sparsely pubescent adaxially, base truncate or shallowly cordate, apex acuminate; secondary veins 10– 14 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or terminal, 1(–3)-flowered. Flowers red, ca. 10 cm in diam.; pedicels 9.5 – 11.5 × 2.3–3.2 mm, tomentose; bracts ca. 3 × 2.5 cm, obovate, tomentose. Sepals 15 –25 × 15– 5 mm, broadly triangular, basally connate, tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Petals obovate or oblong, densely tomentose abaxially, sparsely tomentose adaxially; outer petals 24 –34 × 13–21 mm; inner petals 22–29 × 11–13 mm. Stamens ca. 250 per flower, ca. 7 mm long; connective liguliform, glabrous. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary cylindrical, hairy; stigma cylindrical, 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 15–20 per fruit, 2.9 –6.2 × 0.8 –1.5 cm, cylindrical, densely tomentose, slightly tuberculate; stipes ca. 1.5 cm long, tomentose. Seeds few to many, flat, pale brown.

Locality: Pokfulam, Victoria Peak, Lady Clementi's Ride, Aberdeen, Shatin, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun. P. S. Choi 374; Y. S. Lau 3108.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi. Widely distributed in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Uvaria macrophylla Roxb. 紫玉盤
Fl. Ind. 2: 663. 1824.
Uvaria microcarpa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 256. 1851; FHK 10. 1861; FKH 29. 1912; FRPS 30(2): 22, pl. 8: 1–8. 1979; FGD 2: 11, fig. 7: 1–8. 1991; FYN 5: 8, fig. 2: 1–8. 1991.
Uvaria macrophylla Roxb. var. microcarpa (Champ. ex Benth.) Finet & Gagnep., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 53, Mém. 4: 67. 1906; Finet & Gagnep., in Fl. Indo-Chine 1: 51. 1907.
Uvaria obovatifolia Hayata, Icon. Pl. Forms. 3: 11. 1913; FKH 29. 1912.
Uvaria synsepala Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 128. 1861; FKH 29. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches stellate-pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 3.5–7.5 × 2–2.5 mm, pubescent; leaf blades 14–16.5 × 5–8 cm, elliptic or obovate, sparsely pubescent with short stellate hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base subcordate or rounded, apex obtuse or acute; secondary veins 11–13 pairs. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–2-flowered. Flowers red, 2.5 – 3.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 7–14.5 × 1.3–2 mm, pubescent; bracts basal, 1.5– 3 × 2 mm, oblong, pubescent. Sepals ca. 5 × 10 mm, broad ovate, basally connate, hairy abaxially. Petals ovate, pubescent; outer petals 8.5 – 14 × 7 –8.5 mm; inner petals 9– 11 × 7–9 mm. Stamens ca. 120 per flower, 5.5– 8 mm long; connective liguliform, glabrous. Carpels ca. 40 per flower; ovary cylindrical, hairy; stigma subcapitate, 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 22 – 30 per fruit, 1.1 –1.8 × ca. 1 cm, globose or ovate, sparsely pubescent; stipes 0.9–1.5 cm, densely pubescent. Seeds 1–3 per monocarp, ca. 7.5 × 3.3 –4.5 mm, lenticular or discoid, brown.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/01 (HKU); S. T. Chan s.n. (HKU); P. S. Choi 360; HK sheet 931, 940.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests. Flowering. May–Jun.; fruiting: Autumn–Dec.

Vaccinium bracteatum Thunb. var. chinense (Lodd.) W. Y. Chun ex Sleumer 小葉烏飯樹
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 71: 474. 1941; FGD 1: 335. 1987; FRPS 57(3): 109. 1991; FOC 14: 488. 2005.
Andromeda chinensis Lodd., Bot. Cab. 17, t. 1648. 1830.
Vaccinium chinense (Lodd.) Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 297. 1852; FHK 199. 1861.
Vaccinium bracteatum auct. non Thunb.: FKH 153. 1913, p.p.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1.5–4(–9) m tall, much branched. Branchlets initially ± puberulent, becoming glabrous in age.
