Leaves alternate, firmly papery to thin leathery; petiole 2–5.5 mm, puberulous; leaf blade rhombic-elliptic to elliptic or lanceolate-elliptic, 1.1–4.5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to acute-acuminate, rarely long acuminate, margin thickened, serrulate at least on the distal half, glabrous; midvein and secondary veins slightly raised on both surfaces. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, 2–4 cm, glabrous to puberulent. Bracts caducous or rarely persistent, leaf-like, elliptic to lanceolate, ca. 5 × 2 mm; bracteoles subulate, persistent. Pedicels 2.4–4.5 mm, pubescent to glabrous. Calyx pubescent, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, 0.9–1.1 × 0.9–1.1 mm, apex acute to acuminate. Corolla white, rarely reddish, tubular-urceolate, 4.0–6.3 × 2.1–3.2 mm, puberulent abaxially, shallowly 5-lobed; lobes reflexed, triangular. Stamens 10, included; filaments hairy; anther (theca and tubule) 2.5–3 mm; appendage very short and inconspicuous to absent; tubule 2–2.5 times as long as thecae. Style glabrous; ovary inferior, 5-locular, densely pubescent at least surrounding base of style. Berry globose, 6–7 mm in diam., puberulent to pubescent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Causeway Bay, Repulse Bay, Tai Tam, Mount Parker, Aberdeen, Stanley, Kadoorie Farm & Botanic Garden, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Pat Sin Leng, Lautau Peak. Y. S. Lau 114, 198; S. L. Thrower 764 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Locally common in shrublands and young secondary forests on open hillsides, alt. 200–980 m. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Notes: Vaccinium bracteatum is known to have edible fruits and its leaves and stems can also be used as herbal medicinal. However, there is no documented uses of var. chinense. This variety only differs from V. bracteatum var. bracteatum in leaf size and shape, although the latter also shown considerable variation. Specimens collected from Guangdong seemed to show a continuous range in leaf size and shape. More detailed studies are therefore needed to ascertain its taxonomic status. The type specimen of V. chinense was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Vaccinium iteophyllum Hance 黃背越橘
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 223. 1862; FGD 1: 333, fig. 367. 1987; FRPS 57(3): 122. 1991; FOC 14: 492. 2005.
Vaccinium iteophyllum Hance var. fragrans Rehd. & Wils., Pl. Wilson. 1(3): 558. 1913.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1(–7) m tall. Young branches, petioles, inflorescence and calyx-tube pubescent with light brown to rusty hairs. Leaves spirally arranged, papery to thin leathery; petioles 1.5–3.0 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 3.4–6 × 1.8–2.5 cm, apex acuminate, base cuneate to rounded, margin shallowly serrulate, turned yellow-brown when dry, glabrous, only with short hairs remained on midvein of abaxial surface. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, racemose, 1.5–4(–7) cm. Bracts and bracteoles caducous. Pedicel 2–2.5 mm. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes triangular, ca. 1 × 1 mm, apex acute to slightly acuminate. Corolla white or tinged with red blotches, tubular-urceolate, 7–8.5 × 2.5–3.5 mm, glabrous, shallowly 5-lobed; lobes reflexed, triangular. Stamens 10, filaments 2–2.5 mm, hairy; anthers (theca and tubule) 5.0 mm; appendage ca. 1.0 mm, present at the top of each theca cell; tubule ca. 4 times as long as theca. Ovary inferior, densely pubescent; style glabrous. Berry globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., purplish red when mature.

Localities: Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 491.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Notes: Previously unrecorded for Hong Kong. Only a single specimen collected from Ma On Shan in 1950 is known, which was previously misidentified as V. bracteatum. The author has not yet noticed this species in the wild.

Vallisneria natans (Lour.) H. Hara 苦草
J. Jap. Bot. 49: 136. 1974; FYN 4: 750, fig. 208. 1986; FRPS 8: 177, pl. 69. 1992; FFJ 6: 26, fig. 20. 1995; FGD 6: 294, fig. 163. 2005; FOC 23: 99. 2010.
Physkium natans Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 663. 1790.
Vallisneria gigantea Graebn., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 49: 68. 1912; Fl. Males. 5(4): 388, fig. 4. 1957; FTW ed. 2, 5: 18. 2000.
Vallisneria asiatica Miki, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 48: 329. 1934.
Vallisneria spiralis auct. non L.: FKH 257. 1912; FGZ 648. 1956; Check List HK Plants 77. 1993.

Submerged herb. Rhizome tuberous; stolons white, ca. 2 mm in diam., usually smooth. Leaves 0.2–2 m × 0.5–2 cm, veins 5–9, margin entire or inconspicuously serrulate, apex obtuse. Male spathe ovate-conical, 1.5–2 cm × 5–10 mm, with more than 200 male flowers; sepals strongly convex; stamens 1, filaments sometimes 2-lobed at apex, with hairs at base. Female spathe 1.5–2 cm; peduncle 30–50 cm or longer, slender. Sepals greenish purple, 2–4 × ca. 3 mm, apex obtuse; petals white, minute; staminodes 3. Fruit cylindrical, 5–30 cm × ca. 5 mm. Seeds narrowly obovoid, glandular hairy.

Locality: Ho Chung, also cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3215.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW; tropical and subtropical Asia, Japan, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, ditches and ponds. Flowering: Nov.

Ventilago leiocarpa Benth. 翼核果
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 5: 77. 1860 & FHK 67. 1861; FKH 62. 1912; FRPS 48(1): 147. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 3: 694. 1993; FGD 4: 259, fig. 153. 2000.

Woody climber. Young shoots yellowish puberulent, glabrescent. Leaves alternate, ± 2-ranked; petioles 3–7 mm; leaf blade leathery, ovate to ovate-oblong, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate, margin entire or slightly waved, glabrous or puberulent on midvein of abaxial surface; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, with distinct transverse veinlets between the veins. Flowers small, ca. 4 mm in diam., usually 4–8 in axillary clusters or cymes, the upper ones occasionally forming a short leafless simple panicle; pedicels 2–4 mm. Calyx-lobes triangular, ca. 1 mm. Petals obcordate, ca. 1 mm, apex bilobed. Stamens as long as or slightly shorter than petals. Ovary immersed in a thick, 5-angled disk. Nuts subglobose 4–6 mm in diam., the terminal wing oblong-lanceolate, 3–5 × 0.7–0.8 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 263; Y. S. Lau 1250; Y. W. Lam 622.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Mar.– May; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Veratrum schindleri Loes. 牯嶺藜蘆
Verh. Bot. Vereins Prov. Brandenburg. 68: 139. 1926; FRPS 14: 28. 1980; FOC 24: 84. 2000; FGD 6: 347, fig. 203. 2005.
Veratrum nigrum auct. non L.: FKH 281. 1912.
Veratrum japonicum auct. non Loes.: FRPS 14: 28. 1980; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.

Perennial herb. Stem simple, erect, to 1 m tall, clothed with brown, reticulate fibers of disintegrated leaf sheaths. Leaves basal and alternate on stem; petioles of basal leaves rather long and tightly enclosing the stem; stem leaves with a short, clasping petiole; leaf blade broadly elliptic to lorate, 15–30 × 2–6(–10) cm, gradually reduce in size upward glabrous, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, strongly plicately veined. Panicle variable in length, laxly many-flowered; branches spreading; rachis and pedicels greywhite woolly; bracts ovate-lanceolate, 5–7 mm, abaxially woolly; pedicels 6–8(–14) mm. Perianth segments 6, yellowish green, greenish white or brownish, subelliptic, oblong, oblong-lanceolate, or obovate-elliptic, 5–8 × 2–3 mm, base not clawed, apex obtuse or subacute; outer segments pubescent at least at abaxial base. Stamens 6, 2–5 mm, inserted at the base of perianth segments. Ovary glabrous. Capsule erect, 1–2 × ca. 1 cm. Seeds black, flattened, narrowly winged.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 2418; Y. S. Lau 2605.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Shaded and moist places in forests and ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Verbena officinalis L. 馬鞭草
Sp. Pl. 1: 20–21. 1753; FGZ 624, fig. 330. 1956; FHN 4: 2, fig. 943. 1977; FYN 1: 392, pl. 93: 1–2. 1977; FTW 4: 432. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 15, fig. 3. 1982; FFJ 4: 518, fig. 411. 1989; FOC 17: 3. 1994; FGD 3: 342. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 425. 1998.

Perennial erect herb, 0.3–1.4 cm tall. Stems tetragonal, often hirsute at nodes and along ridges. Petiole 0.3–4 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate, obovate, or oblong‑lanceolate, 2–8 × 1–5 cm, margin coarsely dentate or cut to sometimes deeply pinnatifid or lobed, hirsute especially on abaxial veins. Spikes long, slender, to 25 cm in fruit. Bracteoles slightly shorter than calyx, hirsute. Calyx 1–4 mm, hirsute, glandular, 5‑veined. Corolla blue to pink, 4–8 mm, puberulent abaxially. Ovary glabrous. Fruit ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm, splitting into 4 nutlets.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. Gibbs 7681; Y. S. Lau 1836; HK sheet 38725.
Distribution: S, SW, E & NW China; tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Grassy slopes or hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vernicia fordii (Hemsl.) Airy Shaw 油桐（三年桐）

Kew Bull. 20: 394. 1966; FRPS 44(2): 143, pl. 34: 5 – 6. 1996; FGD 5: 109, fig. 63. 2003.

Aleurites fordii Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: pl. 2801 – 2802. 1906; FKH 237. 1912.


Tree up to 10 m tall; young branches and leaves tawny pubescent, glabrous in age. Leaves crowded towards apex of branchlets; petiole with 2 compressed and sessile glands at apex; stipules oblong to lanceolate (3–)6–8 mm; leaf blade ovate, 5–20 × 3–20 cm, base truncate to shallowly cordate, apex acute, usually entire, rarely 1–3-lobed; palmately 5–7-veined. Panicles 6–12 cm. Male flowers: calyx spathe-like, ca. 1 cm, usually 2-lobed, densely brown-puberulous abaxially; petals obovate, 2–3 × 1–1.5 cm, base unguiculate, apex rounded, white, with reddish nerviform stripes; stamens 8–12, in 2 series; staminodes 5, linear ca. 5 mm. Female flowers: calyx 8–10 mm, hairy, 2–3-lobed; petals as in male flowers; disk-glands 5, linear; ovary pubescent, 3–8-locular; styles 3–8, bilobed. Drupes subglobose, 4–8 cm in diam., pericarp leathery, smooth.


Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1590, 2693; HK sheet 24715; K. Y. Chan 1164 (CUHK).

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, widely cultivated.

Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Uses: Material (lipids).

Vernicia montana Lour. 木油樹（千年桐）
Fl. Cochinch. 586. 1790; FRPS 44(2): 143, pl. 34: 1 – 4. 1996; FGD 5: 108. 2003.
Aleurites montana (Lour.) E. H. Wilson, Bull. Imp. Inst. Gr. Brit. 11: 460. 1913.
Aleurites cordata auct. non (Thunb.) R. Br. ex Steud.: FKH 237. 1912.

Tree up to 20 m tall; young branches and leaves yellowish pubescent, glabrous in age; petioles 7–17 cm, with 2 stipitate cupular glands at apex; stipules lanceolate, 2–4 mm; leaf blade broad-ovate, 8–20 × 5–18 cm, base cordate to truncate, apex acute to acuminate, 2–5-lobed or entire, usually with cupular glands at the sinus. Panicles corymbiform, usually terminal. Male flowers: calyx spathe-like, ca. 1 cm, apex shallowly 2–3-lobed, glabrous; petals obovate, 2–3 cm, ungulate at base, white or purple-red at base and with purple-red nerviform stripes; stamens 8–10, in 2 series, filaments hairy. Female flowers: calyx spathe-like, 1.4–1.7 cm, caducous; petals as in male flowers; ovary densely brown-pubescent, 3-locular; styles 3, biparted. Drupes ovoid, 3–5 cm in diam., 3-ribbed; pericarp leathery, wrinkled; seeds compressed-globose, verrucose.

Locality: Cultivated. K. L. Tso 20238; Y. S. Lau 357, 2378; S. Y. Hu 10435 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, cultivated in Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Material (lipids).

Vernonia cinerea (L.) Less. 夜香牛
Linnaea 4(3): 291. 1829; FHK 169. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22: 18. 1969; FRPS 74: 38. 1985; FGD 8: 236, fig. 144. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1086, pl. 518, photo 494. 1998.
Conyza cinerea L., Sp. Pl. 2: 862. 1753.

Erect annual or biennial herbs, 12–100 cm tall, greyish pubescent throughout, trichomes simple, mixed with T‑shaped and rarely stellate hairs. Stem cylindric, 2–4 mm in diam., glandular, striate‑sulcate, branching only after the formation of terminal capitulum. Middle and lower leaves ovate‑rhombic or ovate, 2–8 × 1.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin undulate‑serrulate, subglabrous‑puberulent and greenish adaxially, densely covered with greyish matted hairs abaxially, gradually attenuate to form winged petiole 0.5–3 cm, sometimes mucronate; upper cauline leaves subsessile, gradually decreasing in size, becoming lanceolate‑linear. Capitula in corymbose panicle; pedunculate at anthesis, peduncles densely pubescent, 0.2–1.5 cm, bearing 1–3 small linear prophylls. Involucres campanulate, 4–5 × 2–3 mm; phyllaries green changing upward to purple, glandular and densely pubescent, apex acuminate to acicular, 4‑seriate; outer ones linear, 1–1.5 mm; middle and inner ones linear‑lanceolate; the innermost ones 4 mm. Receptacles flat, alveolate at anthesis and areolate after fruit dispersal. Florets 20–21 per capitulum, 4 mm, the tube slender, white, the distal enlarged portion and the lobes purple and hairy; stylar branches exserted, purple; anther bases sagittate, apical appendages ovate‑acute. Cypselae terete, apex truncate, slightly cuneate towards the corky ring at the base, 1.5–2 mm, pubescent and glandular. Pappus white, biseriate, outer ones numerous and minute, persistent; inner ones 4 mm, delicate and deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23987 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 6974 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 397.
Distribution: S, SW to C & E China; Japan, India, Indochina, Malaysia, Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vernonia cumingiana Benth. 毒根斑鳩菊
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 232. 1852; FHK 170. 1861; FRPS 74: 21, pl. 9: 7–13. 1985; FGD 8: 234. 2007.
Vernonia andersonii auct. non C. B. Clarke, FKH 139. 1912.

Scandent shrubs or liana, current years’ flower‑bearing growth 60–80 cm, 4–5 cm in diam. near the base, branched off leafy shoots 6–7 mm across. Stem terete, striate, pubescent to densely tomentose, some hair stellate. Leaves ovate‑oblong, elliptic‑oblong or lanceolate‑oblong, 5–14 × 2–6 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire, major lateral veins 5 – 6 on each side of midvein, arcuate, reticulations on both surfaces, glabrous adaxially except the midvein and veins appearing puberulent, abaxial surfaces glandular and densely pilose or tomentose with rusty‑coloured hairs; leaf petiole densely pubescent, 0.5– 1 cm. Capitula numerous, in terminal or axillary panicles; peduncles 0.5–2 cm, rusty hirsute, the distal half with 1– 3 linear prophylls, gradually merging with the involucral bracts. Involucres campanulate to hemispherical, 6–7 × 6–12 mm when dry, apex acute or obtuse, 5‑seriate; outermost ones ovate, 3 mm, densely covered with yellowish hair on whole abaxial surfaces and along margin; middle and inner layers ranging from ovate‑oblong to oblong, 4–7 mm, hairy near the apex. Receptacle plain, fimbriate and with each areole elevated at centre. Florets 18 – 21 per capitulum, corolla 9–12 mm, twice the length of the innermost phyllaries, trumpet‑shaped with distal half enlarged, lobes 3–4 mm, colour pink to reddish purple; anther tubes 4 mm, slightly exserted, with long‑deltoid apical appendages and sagittate bases; stylar branches 2–3 mm, spinulose. Cypselae subcylindric, 3 mm, 10– 12‑ribbed, sparsely puberulent, basal end truncate with a corky ring. Pappus 2‑seriate, outer ones shorter and few; inner ones 1 cm, reddish brown.

Locality: Shek O, Wong Nai Chung, The Peak, Nam Fung Rd., Tai Mo Shan, Luk Keng, Castle Peak. P. S. Choi 497; W. Y. Chun 5054 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11831 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Thailand, Indochina.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets along streams. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vernonia elliptica DC. in Wight 光耀藤
Contrib. Bot. India 5. 1834; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1088, pl. 519. 1998.

Large sprawling woody lianas climbing over fences and trees up to 4 – 5 m high; branchlets, lower leaf‑surfaces and inflorescences silvery hairy. Leaves on flowering shoots petiolate, petioles curved, 2 – 5 mm, densely silky, leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, 2.5 – 9.5 × 1 – 6 cm, base and apex rounded or obtuse, glabrous or bearing little sericeous hair adaxially, densely covered with appressed silky hair abaxially, reticulate veins and midvein elevated on both surfaces. Capitulum subsessile, with 4 – 5 florets each, 3 – 6 capitula forming a stalked cluster, subtended by a diminutive leaf (prophyll). Involucres subcylindric, 3 – 4 × 1.5 – 2 mm; phyllaries herbaceous, imbricate, 4‑seriate, ciliate along margin; the outermost ones ovate, 1.5 × 1 mm, glandular and puberulent on abaxial surfaces, apex obtuse; length and width increases gradually inward; innermost ones obovate‑oblong, apex obtuse to rounded, 3 × 1.5 mm, glandular and hairy near apex. Florets white, tinged pink in bud or when first open, corolla 5 – 6, narrowly funnelform with upper half broaden, 1/3 divided into 5 lanceolate lobes and glandular outside; anther tube honey‑coloured, base sagittate, apical appendage ovate‑lanceolate; style white, base globose, attached to a brown glandular disk, distal end branched and recurved, the abaxial side of the branches bristly, apex acute‑acuminate. Cypsela glossy brown, 2.5 mm, 4 – 5‑ribbed, densely glandular. Pappus greyish to brownish white, persistent, unequal, the outer ones shorter, the inner ones equal to the corolla tube in length, radiating with diam. 0.8 – 1 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. L. Thrower 1577 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22143, 22182, 23942 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to India and SE Asia, naturalized in Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb. – May.
Uses: Ornamental

Vernonia gratiosa Hance 台灣斑鳩菊
J. Bot. 20(238): 290. 1882; FRPS 74: 24, pl. 9: 1 – 6. 1985; FGD 8: 234. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1088, pl. 520, photo 495. 1998.

Scandent subshrubs up to 3 m tall; branches many, pubescent to tomentose. Leaves elliptic‑oblong, 6.5–11 × 1.8–4 cm, petiole densely pubescent, 0.4–1 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or loosely mucronulate, subglabrous or loosely pubescent adaxially, more hairy on the midvein, densely brownish tomentose abaxially. Capitula many, arranged as terminal or axillary panicles; peduncles much densely brownish tomentose. Involucres campanulate, 6 mm; phyllaries in 4 series, apex acute, brownish long hairs growing throughout or mainly distributed near apex and along margin; outer layers ovate, 2 mm; median and inner layers lanceolate to oblong, gradually increases in length inward, 2.5–7 mm. Receptacle slightly convex, areoles fimbriate. Florets about 10 per capitulum, tubular corolla purple, 1 cm, lower portion puberulent, apex divided into 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 2 mm, glabrous. Cypselae terete, 10‑ribbed, 3–3.5 mm, brown in colour, puberulent, truncate at apex, narrowed at base with corky ring. Pappus in 2 series, outer ones short, usually deciduous; inner ones 1 cm, brown to reddish brown, persistent.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Shing Stream. C. P. Lau 188; P. S. Choi 528.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thin forests. Flowering: Aug.–Apr. of the following year.

Vernonia maritima Merr. 濱海斑鳩菊
Philipp. J. Bot. 3(6): 404. 1908; FRPS 74: 39, pl. 15: 1 – 8. 1985; FGD 8: 236. 2007.
Vernonia maritima Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 22: 202. 1906, nom. nud.
Vernonia kawakami Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 30(1): 149. 1911.

Dwarf subshrubs, usually 7–10 cm tall. Stems often procumbent at base, obliquely ascending in upper part, many‑branched, striate, grey‑white hispidulous. Leaves numerous, ± confert upwards, spathulate, 1.5–2.5 × 0.4–0.7 cm, base gradually attenuate into slender petioles, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or repand, densely grey‑white hispidulous. Capitula few, usually 3–5 corymbose, 5–7 mm in diam.; peduncles 5–12 mm, with 1–2 subulate bracteoles, densely hispidulous. Involucres ca. 4 × 5–7 mm; phyllaries 5‑seriate, imbricate, outer ones subsubulate 1.5–2 mm, spinescent, puberulous, median ones ovate, ca. 3 mm, acute and mucronulate, inner ones oblong, sparsely puberulous, with scarious margins. Receptacle flat, foveolate. Florets more than 40 per capitulum; corolla tubular, 2.5 mm, with campanulate limb; lobes lanceolate, apically glandular. Cypselae subcylindric, 1–1.2 mm, 5‑angled, truncate at apex, glandular between the ribs or sometimes sparsely puberulous. Pappus simple, white, ca. 1 mm, deciduous.

Locality: Lantau Island, Cheung Chau. W. J. Tutcher 11923; H. C. Tang 1252.
Distribution: Taiwan; Philippines.
Ecology: Wastelands near seashores. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.

Vernonia patula (Dryand.) Merr. 鹹蝦花
Philipp. J. Sci. 3(6): 439. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 21. 1969; FRPS 74: 41, pl. 12: 8–15. 1985; FGD 8: 233, fig. 143. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1091, pl. 521, photo 497. 1998.
Vernonia chinensis (L.) Less., Linnaea 6: 105, 674. 1831; FHK 169. 1861; FKH 138. 1912.
Conyza patula Dryand., Hort. Kew 3: 184. 1789.

Erect annual herbs 40–60 cm tall; stem terete, striate‑sulcate, glandular and greyish pubescent, the lower portion 3–6 mm in diam. Leaves ovate or ovate‑oblong, the lower cauline ones usually withered at anthesis; the middle ones 3–4.5 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate and attenuate as wings of the upper portion of the petiole, apex obtuse, margin subentire with 2–6 small callous teeth, sparsely pilose above, glandular and greyish woolly beneath; petioles 2–10 mm; upper cauline leaves smaller, subsessile. Capitula 2–3 terminal to leafy branchlets; peduncles 0.4–2.8 cm, tomentose, with or without prophylls. Involucres hemispherical or depressed globose, 5–6 × 6–10 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, apex acuminate‑acicular, hairy and glandular; outermost ones lanceolate, 3 – 4 mm, greenish or sometimes tinged purple; middle and inner layers lanceolate‑oblong, 5–6 mm. Receptacle slightly convex, shortly scarious along margin of areoles. Florets 75–100 in each capitulum; corolla purple, 4–4.5 mm, apical lobes lanceolate; anther tube 1.5 mm; stylar branches exserted, 0.8 mm. Cypselae subcylindric, obtuse at the basal end, truncate at the apex, 2 mm, unequally pentagonous, glabrous, glandular. Pappus white, in 1 series, 2.5 – 3 mm, delicate and deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 233; Y. S. Lau 2214; Y. W. Lam 483.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vernonia saligna DC. 柳葉斑鳩菊
Prodr. 5: 33. 1836; FRPS 74: 25, pl. 10: 1–7. 1985; FGD 8: 235. 2007.

Perennial erect herbs, 60–100 cm tall; stem woody at base, branches terete, striate, puberulent to subglabrous. Leaves subsessile or shortly petiolate, leaf blade elliptic‑oblong to oblanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrate to double serrate, both surfaces scabrous, abaxial side with denser hair and have glands. Capitula many, forming terminal or axillary corymb; peduncles 5 – 10 mm, densely pubescent and glandular. Involucres campanulate, 7–9 × 5–8 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, scarious, purple throughout or apically, margin ciliate; outermost ovate, ca. 2 mm, apex acuminate‑spinulose; middle and inner layers ovate‑oblong to oblong, length increases inward, innermost 8 mm, apex rounded‑ or obtuse‑spinulose. Florets 6–12 per capitulum, pale purple, tubular corolla 7–8 mm, glandular, trumpet‑shaped with apex divided into 5 lanceolate lobes. Cypselae oblong, 2.5–3 mm, 10‑ribbed, hairy and glandular. Pappus white, in 1 series, 7 mm, delicate and deciduous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 4822; L. T. Lo 421; HK sheet 14629.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian; India, Nepal, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vernonia solanifolia Benth. 茄葉斑鳩菊（斑鳩菊）
London J. Bot. 1: 486. 1842; FHK 169. 1861; FKH 138. 1912; FGD 8: 234. 2007; FRPS 74: 12, pl. 1: 8–14. 1985

Densely woolly shrubby lianas, 1–4 m tall, with arching branches. Leaves ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–14 × 3–7 cm, rounded or subcordate at the base, acuminate or obtuse at the apex, margin entire, undulate or loosely obtuse‑toothed, the adaxial surfaces pilose and glandular, and densely hirsute with simple and stellate hair along the midvein, the abaxial surfaces glandular and densely covered with yellowish or brownish matted hairs; petioles strong, 0.7–2 cm, tomentose. Capitula numerous, in axillary and terminal corymbose‑panicles; peduncles 0.7 – 1.2 cm, densely woolly. Involucres hemispherical, 4–5 × 4–6 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, ranging from ovate, ovate‑oblong to oblong, 2.5–5 mm, apex obtuse, outer ones woolly throughout the abaxial surface, inner ones woolly at apical region and slightly scarious along margin. Receptacle plain and alveolate. Florets 10–12, fragrant, corolla pink or pale purple, sparsely glandular, funnelform about 6 mm, 1/3 divided into 5 lanceolate lobes; stylar branches 2 mm, exserted. Cypselae brown,

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 5044 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 1313; P. S. Choi 498.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; India, Myanmar, Indochina.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Veronica javanica Blume 多枝婆婆納
Bijdr. 742. 1826; FOC 18: 74. 1998; FGD 4: 380. 2000.

Annual or perennial herbs, 10–40 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, many‑branched, densely white villose. Leaves alternate; petiole 1–7 mm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑triangular, 1–4 × 1–3 cm, base ± cordate to truncate, apex obtuse, margin deeply incised dentate. Racemes axillary, initially short and subcorymbose, lengthening to 10 cm in fruit; bracts linear to oblanceolate, 4–6 mm; much longer than pedicels. Calyx 4‑lobed; lobes linear‑elliptic, 2–5 mm, subequal. Corolla white, pink or red‑purple, rotate, ca. 2 mm; tube ca. 1.4 mm, hairy in throat. Stamens about half the length of corolla. Capsules obcordate, strongly compressed, 2–3 × 3–4 mm, notched at apex.

Locality: Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 1767.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places near villages. Flowering: Apr.

Veronica persica Poir. 阿拉伯婆婆納
Encycl. 8: 542. 1808; FOC 18: 70. 1998.
Veronica tournefortii C. C. Gmel., Fl. Ead. 1: 39. 1805.
Veronica didyma auct. non Tenore: Check List HK Plants 73. 1993.

Annual herbs, sometimes biennial. Stems diffuse, ca. 20–50 cm, densely pubescent with multicellular hairs, often more densely so along 2 lines. Leaves opposite, usually 3 or 4 pairs; petioles 1–8 mm; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate to suborbicular, 10–20 × 8–15 mm, evenly and sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, margin obtusely crenate‑serrate. Racemes terminal, laxly flowered. Bracts alternate, leaf‑like, upper ones smaller than others. Calyx 4‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, 5–8 mm in fruit, sparsely pubescent, 3‑veined. Corolla usually blue, rotate, 8–14 mm in diam., throat sparsely hairy; lobes ovate to orbicular. Stamens shorter than corolla. Capsules obcordate, strongly compressed, 4–6 × 6–9 mm, venation conspicuously reticulate. Seeds slightly navicular, usually 1.4–2.3 mm; testa deeply rugose dorsally.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2856; P. S. Choi 322; K. L. Yip 4384.
Distribution: S, C, SW & E China; native to SW Asia and since the 19th century spread over most of the world.
Ecology: Grasslands on higher ground. Flowering: Feb.–May.

Veronica undulata Wall. ex Jack 水苦蕒
Fl. Ind. 1: 147. 1820; FOC 18: 79. 1998; FGD 4: 379. 2000.
Veronica anagallis‑aquatica auct. non L.: FKH 190. 1912, as ‘V. Anagallis’.

Perennial herbs, rarely annual. Stems erect or procumbent at base, 10–100 cm tall, ± succulent, sparsely covered with capitate glandular hairs. Leaves sessile, amplexicaul upward; leaf blade elliptic to ovate, sometime ovate‑oblong or linear‑lanceolate, rarely lanceolate, 2–10 × 1–3.5 cm, margin serrate. Racemes axillary, longer than leaves. Calyx 4‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Corolla pale blue, pale purple, or white, rotate, 4–5 mm in diam.; tube short; lobes broadly ovate, slightly unequal in width. Stamens shorter than corolla. Capsules subglobose, as long as calyx, slightly compressed, apex rounded and slightly notched. Seeds slightly flattened, convex on both sides.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2965; HK sheet 4160, 4161.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E Afghanistan, N India, Korea, Japan, Laos, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wet places near villages. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Viburnum hanceanum Maxim. 蝶花莢蒾
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg, Sér. 3, 26 (Mel. Biol. 10: 662): 487. 1880.; FKH 121. 1912; FRPS 72: 63. 1988; FGD 4: 295. 2000.

Deciduous shrubs, up to 2 m tall. Branchlets hairy or not. Leaves opposite; petioles 5–15 mm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 4–8 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, apex rounded and mucronate, margin dentate, stellate hairy on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, running direct into teeth, veinlets parallel. Inflorescence an umbel‑like cymes, 5–7 cm in diam. Marginal sterile flowers 5–6; corolla white, 2–3 cm in diam. Corolla of fertile flowers 3 mm in diam.; lobes ovate, ca. 1.5 mm. Stamens as long as corolla. Drupes red, ovoid, ca. 5 mm, slightly compressed.

Locality: Fanling, Sha Lo Tung, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. K. Barretto 305; Y. W. Lam 202; F. W. Xing 8829.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was reported as Viburnum fordiae Hance previous (FKH 121. 1912; Check List HK Plants 36. 1993). Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Ornamental.
Notes: This species was reported as Viburnum fordiae Hance previous (FKH 121. 1912; Check List HK Plants 36. 1993). Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

records.text:
Viburnum luzonicum Rolfe 呂宋莢蒾
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 21: 310. 1884; FRPS 72: 94, pl. 20: 1 – 4. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 4: 756, photo 383. 1998; FGD 4: 301. 2000.

Deciduous shrubs, 2–3 m tall. Young branchlets, winter buds, petioles and inflorescence yellow‑brown stellate‑pubescent; branchlets of previous year dark purple‑brown, sparsely stellate‑pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 4–10 mm; leaf blade ovate, elliptic‑ovate, or ovate‑lanceolate to oblong, sometimes subrhombic, 5–9 × 1.5–5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute to acuminate, margin serrate, abaxially sparsely stellate‑pubescent, adaxially with transparent glandular dots and fork‑like pubescent on midvein; lateral veins (5–)7–9 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, together with midvein prominent abaxially, ending in marginal teeth. Inflorescences a compound umbel‑like cyme, 3–5 cm in diam., usually terminal on branchlets or short lateral branchlets subtended by a pair of leaves; peduncle usually very short or nearly absent, very rarely to 1.5 cm, with 5 rays. Flowers small, on rays of 3rd and 4th orders. Calyx‑tube ovate‑orbicular, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, rotate, 4– 5 mm in diam., outside stellate‑pubescent; lobes ovate, longer than the tube. Stamens shorter or slightly longer than corolla. Stigmas indistinctly 3‑lobed. Fruit red when mature, ovoid, 5–6 mm.

Locality: Lantau Peak. HK sheet 35751, 40326.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, SE Jiangxi, S Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Philippines to Malaysia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Notes: This species is distinguished from Viburnum fordiae Hance by its leaves with hyaline, sessile small glands adaxially and the very short or absent peduncles, whereas leaves of V. fordiae are eglandular adaxially and the peduncles are up to 4 cm long.

Viburnum odoratissimum Ker Gawl. 珊瑚樹
Bot. Reg. 6: t. 456. 1820; FHK 143. 1861; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 56, pl. 12: 1 – 5.1988; FTW ed. 2, 4: 756, photo 384 – 385. 1998; FGD 4: 296. 2000.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 2–10(–15) m tall. Branchlets glabrous or slightly pubescent, with small, verrucose lenticels. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic‑oblong or obovate, rarely suborbicular, 7–20 × 3.5–8 cm, base cuneate or broad‑cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely and shallowly sinuate or subentire, glabrous on both surfaces, or abaxially pubescent in axils of veins, sometimes sparsely dotted with dark‑red small glands; lateral veins 5–6 on each side of midvein; veins anastomosing near margin. Panicles terminal, ovoid or pyramidal, 6–14 cm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx‑tube campanulate, 2–2.5 mm, teeth deltoid. Corolla white or yellowish, rotate; tube ca. 2 mm; lobes ovate‑orbicular, 2–3 mm, reflexed. Stamens exserted; styles short, stigma capitate. Drupes red to black, ovoid, 8–5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1237; L. T. Lo 8; HK sheet 39426.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Viburnum sempervirens K. Koch 常綠莢蒾（堅莢樹）
Hort. Dendr. 300. 1853; FKH 121. 1912; FRPS 72: 74. 1988; FGD 4: 298. 2000.
Viburnum venulosum Benth., FHK 142. 1861.

Evergreen shrubs, 2–4 m tall. Branchlets purple or grey‑brown. Leaves opposite, leathery; petioles tinged with red‑purple colour, 5–15 mm; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic‑ovate, rarely oblong or oblanceolate, 4–12 × 2.5–5 cm, base narrowly cuneate to obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire or slightly toothed towards end, shining adaxially, with small, brown glands on abaxial surface; lateral veins 3–4(–5) on each side of midvein, anastomosing at margin or running directly into teeth. Cymes arranged into compound umbel, terminal. Calyx‑tube ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, rotate, ca. 4 mm in diam.; lobes suborbicular. Stamens slightly exserted. Drupes red, subglobular or ovoid, 8 × 3–5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2404; P. S. Choi 451; Y. W. Lam 1747.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Vicia faba L. 蠶豆
Sp. Pl. 737. 1753; FRPS 42(2): 269. 1998; FGD 5: 355, fig. 197. 2003.

Annual herb, 0.3 – 1 m tall. Stems erect, 4-angular, glabrous. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 1 – 5 pairs, alternate, elliptic, oblong or obovate, rarely orbicular, 4–6(–10) × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, apiculate, entire, glabrous. Racemes axillary, 2–4(–6)-flowered. Peduncle very short. Calyx campanulate, teeth lanceolate. Corolla white, with large purplish blotches, 2 – 3.5 cm; wings shorter than vexillum, but longer than keel. Stamens diadelphous (9+1). Ovary linear; ovules 2 – 4(–6). Pods turgid, 5 – 10 × 2 – 3 cm, tomentose, becoming black when mature. Seeds 2– 5(–6), oblong, compressed, green, brownish, purplish, or black, hilum linear, black.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 623.
Distribution: Widely cultivated; probably native to N Africa and SW Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: May– Jun.
Uses: Food (seeds).

Vicia hirsuta (L.) Gray 小巢菜（翹搖）
Nat. Arr. Brit. Pl. 2: 614. 1821; FKH 81. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 265. 1998; FGD 5: 355. 2003.

Annual climbing herb. Stems 15 – 90(–120) cm, sparsely pubescent, slender, subglabrous. Stipules lanceolate, 2–3-lobed in lower half. Leaves even-pinnate; leaflets 4–8 pairs, linear, 5–15 × 1–3 mm, base attenuate, apex truncate and mucronate, glabrous. Racemes shorter than leaves. Peduncles 2.5–3 cm, 2–4(–7)-flowered. Calyx campanulate, 2 mm. Corolla white, pale violet or purplish; vexillum elliptic, ca. 3 mm, apex truncate, emarginate; wings equal to vexillum; keel shorter. Pods oblong, 0.5–1 × 0.2–0.5 cm, densely brown hirsute. Seeds 2, oblate, 1.5–2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 1378, 34647.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; E Asia, Europe, N America.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Feb. – Jul.
Uses: Green manure, forage, medicinal (folklore).

Vicia sativa L. 野豌豆
Sp. Pl. 736. 1753; FKH 81. 1912; FRPS 42(2): 268. 1998; FGD 5: 356. 2003.

Annual or biennial herb, 15–100 cm tall. Stems climbing or ascending, glabrous or sparsely pubescent at first. Stipules hastate, 2–4-toothed, with a distinct dark glandular blotch at middle. Leaves even-pinnate; rachis ending in a branched tendril; leaflets 3–9 pairs, linear, elliptic or oblanceolate, 1–4 × 0.2–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex rounded or truncate, emarginate, mucronate, yellow pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers 1–2, axillary, subsessile. Calyx campanulate, 8 mm, pubescent, teeth lanceolate. Corolla purple or red, ca. 1.6 cm; vexillum broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 8–9 mm, apex rounded, emarginate, constricted at middle; wings oblong-obovate, with slender basal auricle, shorter than vexillum, longer than keel; keel curved, 4 mm. Ovary linear, sparsely pubescent. Pods narrowly oblong, 4–6 × 0.5–0.8 cm, constricted between seeds, dehiscent, valves contorted. Seeds 4–8, subglobose, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., globular, brown or dark brown.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 10940, 11430; P. S. Choi 72.
Distribution: Widely cultivated and naturalized. The origin of this variety is unknown, but it is now widespread as an escape from cultivation throughout most temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.
Uses: Food, green manure, forage.

Vigna angularis (Willd.) Ohwi & H. Ohashi 赤豆（紅豆）
J. Jap. Bot. 44(1): 29. 1969; FRPS 41: 287. 1995; FGD 5: 330. 2003.
Dolichos angularis Willd., Sp. Pl. 3(2): 1051. 1802.
Phaseolus angularis W. Wight, U.S.D.A. Bur. Pl. Industr. Bull. 137: 17. 1909.

Annual erect or twining herb, 30– 90 cm tall, sparsely pilose. Stipules dorsifixed, sagittate. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets ovate, rhomboid-ovate, 5–10 × 5–8 cm, apex acute or subrounded, lateral ones oblique, entire or shallowly 3-lobed, sparsely pilose on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 5–6-flowered. Calyx campanulate, 3–4 mm. Corolla yellow, ca. 9 mm; vexillum transversely orbicular or subreniform, apex emarginate; wings broader than keel, shortly clawed and auriculate; keel apex incurved nearly in a half circle. Ovary linear. Pods terete, 5 – 8 × 0.5 – 0.6 cm, glabrous. Seeds obscurely red or with other colours, oblong, 5 – 6 × 4 – 5 mm, hilum not impressed.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 618; HK sheet 34332, 34333.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. – Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Food (seeds), medicinal (folklore).

Vigna marina (Burm.) Merr. 濱豇豆
Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 285. 1917; FRPS 41: 279. 1995; FGD 5: 328, fig. 181. 2003.
Phaseolus marinus Burm., Ind. Alt. Herb. Amboin. 18. 1769.

Perennial prostrate or climbing herb. Stems up to several metres, glabrescent when old. Stipules basifixed, ovate, 3 – 5 mm. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets ovate-orbicular or obovate, 3.5–9.5 × 2.5–9.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex rounded, obtuse or emarginate, very shortly setose to subglabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 2–4 cm. Peduncles 3–13 cm. Calyx 2.5 – 3 mm, teeth deltoid, 1 – 1.5 mm, upper 2 connate. Corolla yellow; vexillum obovate, 1.2–1.3 × 1.4 cm; wings and keel ca. 1 cm. Pods linear-oblong, 3.5–6 × 0.8–0.9 cm, pubescent when young, glabrous when old, constricted between seeds. Seeds 2–6, yellow-brown or red-brown, oblong, 5–7 × 4.5–5 mm, hilum oblong.

Locality: Shek O. L. T. Lo 665; Y. W. Lam 677.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical regions.
Ecology: Sandy beaches.
Uses: Food (seeds edible), medicinal (folklore).

Vigna minima (Roxb.) Ohwi & H. Ohashi 賊小豆（山綠豆）
J. Jap. Bot. 44(1): 30. 1969; FRPS 41: 285. 1995; FGD 5: 329. 2003.
Phaseolus minimus Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 3: 290. 1832; FHK 88. 1861; FKH 84. 1912.

Annual twining herb. Stems slender. Stipules dorsifixed. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets variable in size and shape, from ovate, ovate-lanceolate, lanceolate to linear, 2 – 7 × 0.8 – 3 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, subglabrous or sparsely scabrid hairy on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, slender, 3 – 4-flowered. Calyx campanulate, ca. 3 mm. Corolla yellow; vexillum suborbicular, 1 × 8 mm; keel with long beaked auricle. Pods terete, 3.5 – 6.5 × 0.4 cm, glabrous, spirally contorted after open. Seeds 4–8, deeply grey, oblong, 0.4 × 3 mm, hilum linear.

Locality: Mount Gough, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1420; L. T. Lo 251; HK sheet 36140.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy fields, thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Aug. – Oct.

Vigna radiata (L.) Wilczek 綠豆
Fl. Congo Belge 6: 386. 1954; FRPS 41: 284. 1995; FGD 5: 329. 2003.
Phaseolus radiatus L., Sp. Pl. 725. 1753.
Phaseolus aureus Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 3: 297. 1832.

Annual erect herb, 20 – 60 cm tall. Stems brown hirsute. Stipules dorsifixed, ovate, 0.8 – 1.2 cm. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets ovate, 5 – 16 × 3 – 12 cm, lateral ones ± oblique, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, more or less sparsely pilose on both surfaces, trinerved. Racemes axillary, 4– several-flowered, up to 25-flowered. Calyx 3 – 4 mm, teeth deltoid, 1.5 – 4 mm, upper 2 connate into one but 2-fid at apex; vexillum subquadrate, 1.2 × 1.6 cm, yellow-green outside, pink inside, apex emarginate; wings ovate, yellow; keel falcate, green tinged with pink, pouched at right lateral side. Pods linear-terete, 4 – 9 × 0.6 cm, sparsely pale brown hirsute. Seeds 8 – 14, greenish or yellow brown, shortly terete, 2.5 – 4 × 2.5 – 3 mm, hilum white.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 622; Y. W. Lam 1010, 1565.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Jun.; fruiting: Jun. – Sep.
Uses: Food (seeds), medicinal (folklore).

Vigna umbellata (Thunb.) Ohwi & H. Ohashi 赤小豆
J. Jap. Bot. 44: 31. 1969; FRPS 41: 288. 1995; FGD 5: 330. 2003.
Dolichos umbellatus Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 2: 339. 1794.
Phaseolus chrysanthus Savi, Nuov. Giorn. Sc. 3: 318. 1822; FKH 84. 1912.

Annual twining herb. Stems slender, to 1 m or over, yellow pilose when young, glabrous when old. Stipules dorsifixed, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 10–15 mm. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets ovate or lanceolate, 10–13 × 5–7.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute, entire or slightly 3-lobed, trinerved, sparsely pubescent on veins. Racemes axillary, 2–3-flowered. Calyx campanulate, 3–4 mm, teeth deltoid. Corolla yellow; vexillum oblong, 1 cm, apex emarginate; wings obovate; keel with horn-like appendage at one side. Pods linear, terete, 6–10 × 0.5 cm, glabrous. Seeds 6–10, obscurely red, brown, black or stramineous, oblong, 3–3.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 619; HK sheet 7944, 7946.
Distribution: S China; SE Asia, Philippines, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: May –Aug.
Uses: Food (seeds), medicinal (folklore).

Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp. 豇豆
Repert. Bot. Syst. 1(5): 779. 1843; FRPS 41: 289. 1995; FGD 5: 330. 2003.
Dolichos unguiculatus L., Sp. Pl. 725. 1753.

Annual or perennial, erect, trailing or climbing herb. Stems 1 – 3 m, subglabrous. Stipules dorsifixed, lanceolate, 1 cm. Leaves pinnately 3-foliolate; leaflets ovate– rhomboid, 5 – 15 × 4 – 6 cm, lateral ones oblique, base acute to rounded, apex acute, entire or subentire, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 2–6-flowered, fasciculate on top of rhachis. Calyx campanulate 6–10 mm, teeth lanceolate. Corolla yellow-white with slightly violet, 2 cm; petals clawed; vexillum suborbicular, 1.2–3.3 × 1–3.2 cm, apex emarginate; wings blue to purple, subdeltoid; keel usually white or pale yellow, not twisted. Pods terete, 20–30 × 0.6–1 cm. Seeds several, dark red or black, often mottled with black or brown, oblong or reniform, 6 – 9 mm.

The species usually divided into three subspecies.

Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp. subsp. cylindrica (L.) Verdc. 短豇豆（眉豆）
Kew Bull. 24: 544. 1970; FGD 5: 331. 2003.
Phaseolus cylindricus L., Herb. Amb. 23. 1754.
Vigna sinensis (L.) Hassk. subsp. cylindrica (L.) Van Eselt., Veg. New York 1(2): 11. 1931.

Pods 7.5 – 13 cm, erect or spread.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 240, 620; HK sheet 34334.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Japan, Korea, America (cultivated).
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Sep.

Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp. subsp. sesquipedalis (L.) Verdc. 長豇豆（豆角）
Fl. Turkey 3: 266. 1970 & Kew Bull. 24: 544. 1970; FGD 5: 331. 2003.
Dolichos sesquipedalis L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1019. 1763.
Vigna sinensis (L.) Hassk. subsp. sesquipedalis (L.) Van Eselt., Veg. New York 1(2): 11. 1931.

Annual twining plants, 2–4 m. Pods 30–80(–90) cm, pendulous, slightly fleshly and inflated when young. Seeds 8–12 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 19; K. Y. Chan 168; HK sheet 7981.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; widely cultivated in tropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp. subsp. unguiculata 豇豆
Dolichos sinensis L., Cent. Pl. II. 28. 1756.
Vigna sinensis (L.) Hassk., Cat. Hort. Bot. Bogor 279. 1844; FKH 84. 1912.
Vigna sinensis subsp. sinensis Mansf., Prodr. Enum. Sp. Pl. Agri- et Hort. 209. 1959.

Pods 20 –30 cm, pendulous.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun. – Jul.; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Food (pods).

Viola verecunda A. Gray 堇菜
Mém. Amer. Acad. Nat. Sci. n. ser. 6: 382. 1858; Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 56. 1886; FKH 36. 1912; FRPS 51: 106. 1991; FGD 4: 71, fig. 45. 2000.

Perennial herb, with a short rootstock. Stems 5 –20 cm, glabrous. Leaves basal and alternate on stems; leaf blade broadly cordate, ovate-cordate or reniform, 1.5 –3 × 1.5 –3.5 cm, base cordate, apex broadly obtuse, margin crenate-serrate, subglabrous on both surfaces. Petioles 1.5 –7 cm, usually longer on basal leaves. Stipules of basal leaves adnate to the petioles, free parts lanceolate, 5–10 mm, those of stem leaves free, ovate-lanceolate to spatulate, 6–12 mm. Flowers small, white or pale purple, solitary in axils of stem leaves. Peduncles exceeding the leaves, with a pair of linear bracteoles above middle. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, 4 –5 mm, apex acuminate, basal appendages short. Petals obovate to oblong-obovate, the laterals ca. 10 × 2.5 mm, bearded at base inside, the abaxial one ca. 10 mm including the spur, emarginate at apex; spurs 1.5–2 mm, gibbous. Capsules oblong or ellipsoid, ca. 8 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Sha Tau Kok, Ma On Shan, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1718, 3057; Y. W. Lam 583.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, Mongolia, Russia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Viola betonicifolia J. E. Smith 戟葉堇菜
Cycl. 37(I): 7. 1819; FRPS 51: 71, 1991; FGD 4: 78, fig. 52. 2000.
Viola patrinii auct. non DC.: FHK 20. 1861; FKH 36. 1912.

Perennial herb, stemless, with tufted stock. Leaves all basal; petioles 1.5–13 cm, narrowly winged on the distal half, usually glabrous; Stipules 3/4 adnate to the petioles, free parts linear lanceolate or subulate; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, narrowly triangular-hastate or triangular-ovate, 2–5 × 0.5 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate or truncate, or sometimes slightly cordate, apex acute, margin sparsely and shallowly undulate-serrate, glabrous or nearly so on both surfaces. Peduncles 6–28 cm, equaling or exceeding leaves, with a pair of linear bracteoles at middle, glabrous or sometimes pubescent on the proximal part. Flowers 10 –20 mm across, white or purple, with darker strips. Sepals 5 –9 × 1–3 mm, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, basal appendages 0.5 –1 mm, tip rounded. Petals obovate to oblongobovate, 1–1.2 cm, the laterals bearded at base inside, the abaxial one 1.3 –1.5 cm including the spur; spurs 2– 6 mm, tip rounded. Capsules ellipsoid, 6–9 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsim Shan. H. C. Tang 721; HK sheet 230.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; Himalayas, India, Sri Lanka, Australia, Indonesia, Japan.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, summits of hills, margins of forest. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Viola diffusa Ging. 蔓堇菜
Prodr. 1: 298. 1824; FHK 20. 1861; FKH 36. 1912; FRPS 51: 100. 1991; FGD 4: 75, fig. 48. 2000.

Annual herb, pubescent throughout. Rootstock short, emitting leafy stolons. Leaves tufted on the stock and crowded towards apex of the stolons; petioles 2–4.5 cm, winged; stipules 1/3 adnate to the petioles, free parts linear lanceolate, 4–12 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate-oblong, 1.5–3.5 × 1–2 cm, base broadly cuneate to truncate, rarely shallowly cordate, decurrent to the petioles, apex obtuse or acutish, margin crenate-serrate. Peduncles 1.5– 8.5 cm, exceeding leaves, with a pair of linear bracteoles at middle. Flowers pale purple to yellowish, not fragrant. Sepals lanceolate, 4–5.5 mm, acute, basal appendages up to 0.5 mm, tip rounded, fimbriate-ciliate. Petals obovate to oblong-obovate, the laterals 6 – 8 mm, not bearded, the abaxial one shorter, ca. 6 mm including the spur; spurs very short, only 1.5 mm. Capsules ellipsoid, 8–10 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 478, 773; L. T. Lo 510.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; India, Nepal, Philippines, Malaysia, Japan.
Ecology: Summits of hills, grassy fields, margins of forests.
Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: May–Aug.

Viola inconspicua Blume 長萼堇菜
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 1: 58. 1825; FRPS 51: 52. 1991; FGD 4: 77, fig. 51. 2000.
Viola confusa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 260. 1851, p.p.; FHK 20. 1861, p.p.
Viola serpens auct. non Wall. ex Ging.: FKH 36. 1912.

Perennial herb, stemless, with a short rootstock and long tap root. Leaves all basal; petioles 2–7 cm, glabrous; Stipules 3/4 adnate to the petioles, free parts lanceolate, 3–5 mm; leaf blade triangular or triangular-ovate, 1.5 –7 × 1–3.5 cm, broadest at base, base broadly cordate, with rounded basal lobes, apex acuminate or acute, margin crenate-serrate, usually glabrous on both surfaces. Peduncles slender, equaling or exceeding leaves, glabrous or pubescent. Flowers pale purple, with dark strips. Sepals ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 3–6 mm; basal appendages 2–3 mm, apex acute or sometimes incised. Petals oblong-obovate, the laterals 7–9 mm, bearded inside, the abaxial one 10 –12 mm including the spur. Capsules 6–9 mm, ellipsoid, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Po, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 1628; HK sheet 37538, Y. W. Lam 864.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; Myanmar, Philippines, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of forest, grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of Viola confusa was collected from Mount Parker, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Viola tricolor L. 三色堇
Sp. Pl. 935. 1753; FRPS 51: 127, pl. 25: 7–9. 1991; FGD 4: 69. 2000.
Viola tricolor L. var. hortensis DC., Prodr. 1: 303. 1824.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Stems to 30 cm tall, erect or becoming diffuse and much-branched. Basal leaves long-petioled, orbicular-cordate to oblong-ovate; stem-leaves ovate-oblong or lanceolate, base rounded, apex obtuse, margin crenate-dentate; stipules large, pinnately parted toward base. Flowers solitary and axillary, 3.5 – 6 cm in diam., usually having three colors, mostly blue, whitish and yellow. Sepals 5, oblong-lanceolate, 12–22 × 3 –5 mm. Petals 5, nearly or quite orbicular, imbricate, the lower petal with a short and obtuse spur. Capsules ellipsoid, 7–12 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens or as pot-plants. Y. S. Lau 1582, 1787.
Distribution: Native in Europe; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Viscum articulatum Burm. f. 扁枝槲寄生
Fl. Indica. 311. 1768; FHK 141. 1861; FHN 2: 465. 1965; FYN 3: 377, pl. 109: 3–4. 1983; FGD 1: 227. 1987; FRPS 24: 155. 1988; FOC 5: 245. 2003.
Viscum japonicum auct. non Thunb.: FKH 229. 1912.

Subshrub, monoecious, spreading or pendulous, green, to 0.5 m tall. Branches opposite and decussate or dichotomous; internodes flattened, 1.5 – 2.5× 0.2 – 0.35 cm, longitudinally 3-ridged. Leaves scale-like. Inflorescences axillary, cymes 1 – 3 together; peduncle nearly absent; 3-flowered, central flower female, lateral ones male; involucre ca. 1.5 mm. Male flowers globose in bud, 0.5–1 mm; perianth-lobes 4. Female flower ellipsoidal in bud, 1–1.5 mm; perianth-lobes 4, triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Stigma cushion-shaped. Berry globose, whitish or greenish white, 3–4 mm in diam., smooth.

Locality: King's Park, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang. Y. S. Lau 2838, 3245; Y. W. Lam 22.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Often growing on plants of Loranthaceae and Lauraceae. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.

Viscum ovalifolium DC. 瘤果槲寄生
Prodr. 4: 278. 1830; FYN 3: 379, pl. 110: 1 – 2. 1983; FGD 1: 225. 1987, “ovalium”; FRPS 24: 154, pl. 33: 4 – 9. 1988; FOC 5: 244. 2003.
Viscum orientale auct. non Willd.: FHK 141. 1861; Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 408. 1894; FKH 229. 1912; FHN 2: 466. 1965.

Shrub, monoecious, green, 0.3 – 0.5 m tall. Branches opposite and decussate or dichotomous, terete; internodes 2 – 3 cm, nodes ± swollen, finely striate. Leaves opposite; petioles short; leaf blade ovate, obovate to long-elliptic, slightly fleshy, 3 – 8.5 × 1 –3 cm, base attenuate or narrowly cuneate, apex obtuse, 3 – 5-veined. Cymes axillary, solitary or sometimes fasciculate, 3-flowered, central flower female, lateral ones male; peduncle 1– 1.5 mm; involucre navicular, ca. 2 mm; pedicel absent. Male flowers ovoid in bud, ca. 1.5 mm; perianth-lobes 4. Female flower ellipsoidal in bud, 2.5 – 3 mm; perianth-lobes 4, triangular, ca. 1 mm. Stigma nipple-shaped. Berry subglobose, yellowish, 4 – 6 mm in diam., tuberculate when young, smooth when mature, base constricted into a ca. 1 mm stalk.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tsiu Hang, Tai Po Kau, Yuen Tun Ha, Fanling, Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng. Y. S. Lau 2078; HK sheet 5153, 31585.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Often growing on trees of Diospyros kaki, Citrus maxima. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: This species was reported as Viscum orientale Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 50. 1993).
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: This species was reported as Viscum orientale Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 50. 1993).

Vitex negundo L. 黃荊
Sp. Pl. 2: 638. 1753; FHK 273. 1861; FKH 204. 1912; FGZ 628. 1956; FTW 4: 432. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 141. 1982; FFJ 4: 540, fig. 425. 1989; FOC 17: 30. 1994; FGD 3: 374, fig. 242. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 426, pl. 180. 1998.

Shrub or small tree. Branchlets tetragonal, densely greyish white tomentose. Leaves usually (3–)5‑foliolate; leaflets papery, oblong‑lanceolate or lanceolate, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or rarely with several teeth along apical part, adaxially green, glabrous or puberulent, abaxially greyish white, tomentose; central leaflet 4–13 × 0.5–4 cm, distinctly petiolulate. Inflorescences terminal, 10–27 cm. Peduncle densely greyish white tomentose. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, abaxially greyish white tomentose, 5‑dentate. Corolla bluish purple or pale purple, ca. 7 mm, 2‑lipped, 5‑lobed, puberulent abaxially. Stamens exserted. Ovary subglabrous. Drupes subglobose, ca. 2 mm in diam., mostly enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 8; Y. W. Lam 1027, 2181.
Distribution: S, SW, E & NW China; Japan, E Africa, SE Asia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vitex negundo L. var. cannabifolia (Siebold & Zucc.) Hand.‑Mazz. 牡荊
Acta Horti Gothob. 9(4): 67. 1934; FRPS 65(1): 143. 1982; FFJ 4: 541. 1989; FOC 17: 31. 1994; FGD 3: 375. 1995.
Vitex cannabifolia Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Math.‑Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(3): 152. 1846.
Vitex negundo f. intermedia C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 105. 1932; FYN 1: 452. 1977.

It differs from var. negundo by leaflets often regularly coarse serrate, abaxially greenish, minutely pilose.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap, Quarry Bay, Fung Yuen, Lo Wu, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 8113; Y. S. Lau 342, 1918.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hebei, Henan, Hunan, Sichuan; India, Nepal, SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Vitex quinata (Lour.) F. N. Williams 山牡荊
Bull. Herb. Boissier, ser. 2, 5(5): 431. 1905; FHN 4: 19. 1977; FTW 4: 434. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 135. 1982; FFJ 4: 539, fig. 424. 1989; FOC 17: 29. 1994; FGD 3: 373. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 426, photo 255. 1998.
Cornutia quinata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 387. 1790.
Vitex loureiri Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 206. 1837; FHK 273. 1861.
Vitex heterophylla Roxb., [Hort. Beng. 46. 1814, nom. nud.] Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 75. 1832; FKH 204. 1912.

Tree, 4–12 m tall; bark brown. Branchlets tetragonal, pubescent and glandular. Leaves 3(–5)‑foliolate; petiole 2.5– 6 cm; petiolules 0.5–2 cm; leaflets thickly papery, obovate‑lanceolate to elliptic‑lanceolate, base cuneate, apex acuminate, acute, or cuspidate, margin entire, puberulent along midvein on both surfaces, abaxially yellow glandular; central leaflet 5–9 × 2–4 cm; lateral ones smaller. Panicles terminal, 9–18 cm, densely yellowish brown pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, densely yellowish brown pubescent and glandular abaxially, 5‑denticulate. Corolla pale yellow, 7–8 mm, 2‑lipped, 5‑lobed, abaxially pubescent and glandular. Stamens exserted. Ovary glandular. Fruiting calyx truncate. Fruit obovoid to globose, black, 4–8 mm in diam., subtended by plateform truncate persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 394, 889, 2375.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Open places, forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Vitex rotundifolia L. f. 單葉蔓荊（白背蔓荊）
Suppl. Pl. 294. 1781; FTW 4: 434. 1978; FOC 17: 30. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 428. 1998.
Vitex ovata Thunb., Fl. Jap. 257. 1784.
Vitex trifolia L. var. simplicifolia Cham., Linnaea : 107. 1832; FRPS 65(1): 140, fig. 70. 1982; FFJ 4: 539. 1989; FGD 3: 374. 1995.
Vitex trifolia L. var. unifoliolata Schauer, Prodr. 11: 683. 1847.

Shrub. Stems prostrate to creeping, rooting at nodes; branchlets silky tomentose when young. Leaves mostly 1(–3)‑foliolate, sessile or short petiolate; blade obovate, 2.5–5 × 1.5–3 cm, base attenuate to rounded, apex abruptly subacuminate to rounded, margin entire, adaxially usually pale green and pubescent, abaxially densely tomentose. Thyrses terminal, 3–10 × 1–2.5 cm. Calyx cupular, 4–5 mm, slightly 2‑lipped, 5‑denticulate, glabrous adaxially, slightly silky tomentose and glandular abaxially. Corolla bluish purple, salverform, slightly silky tomentose and glandular abaxially, villous in tube and adaxially. Stamens and style exserted. Ovary globose, glabrous, densely glandular. Fruit dark brown when dry, globose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2325; S. P. Lau 152; HK sheet 40601.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hebei; Japan, SE Asia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vitex trifolia L. 蔓荊
Sp. Pl. 2: 638(as 938). 1753; FHK 273. 1861; FKH 204. 1912; FHN 4: 18. 1977; FYN 1: 442, pl. 105: 1 – 3. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 138. 1982; FFJ 4: 539. 1989; FOC 17: 29. 1994; FGD 3: 374. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 428. 1998.

Shrub, rarely small tree, 1.5–5 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal, densely pubescent. Leaves (1–)3(–5)‑foliolate; petiole 1–3 cm; leaflets sessile, ovate, obovate or ovate‑oblong, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin entire, ± hairy adaxially, densely grey tomentose abaxially; lateral veins 5–8 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces; central leaflet 5–9 × 1.7–3 cm, lateral ones smaller and subsessile. Thyrses terminal, 3–10(–15) cm. Peduncle densely grey tomentose. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, slightly 5‑dentate, glabrous adaxially, grey pubescent abaxially. Corolla purplish blue, 8–10 mm, villous adaxially, white mealy pubescent abaxially, 2‑lipped, upper lip 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed with central one larger. Stamens exserted. Ovary glabrous, glandular. Style glabrous. Fruit subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam., black.

Locality: Fanling, Castle Peak, Lin Tong Mei, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 342; Y. W. Lam 1531; HK sheet 34489.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Open fields, streamsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vitis balanseana Planch. 小果葡萄
Monogr. Phan. 5: 612. 1887; FGZ 422, fig. 223. 1956; FHN 3: 15. 1974, excl. fig. 538; FFJ 3: 367, fig. 256. 1987; FRPS 48(2): 144. 1998.
Vitis flexuosa Thunb. var. gaudichaudii Planch., Monogr. Phan. 5: 348. 1887.

Branchlets and petioles sparsely cobwebby-tomentose when young, later glabrescent; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves simple, unlobed; petioles 2–7 cm; leaf blade membranous, cordate-oval or broadly ovate, 3.5–14 × 3–10 cm, base cordate, notch obtuse, apex acute or mucronulate, margin glandular-denticulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Panicle leaf-opposed, 4–13 cm; axes slelnder, sparsely cobwebby-tomentose. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm, glabrous. Calyx cupular, entire, glabrous. Petals galeate. Berry purple-black at maturity, globose, 4–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Kam Tin, Tai O, Yi O, Peng Chau. Y. W. Lam 1003, 1125, 1245.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Shrublands in valleys. Flowering: Feb.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Vitis bryoniifolia Bunge 蘡薁（野葡萄）

Enum. Pl. China Bor. 11. 1831; FRPS 48(2): 175. 1998, “bryoniaefolia”.

Vitis thunbergii auct. non Siebold & Zucc.: FTW 3: 679. 1977.


Branchlets terete, striate, sparsely cobwebby-tomentose or pubescent when young, glabrescent; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves simple, 3–5-lobed, rarely not lobed; petioles 0.5–4.5 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade thinly papery, oblong-ovate, 2.5–8 × 2–5 cm, base cordate to deeply cordate, apex acute to acuminate, margin incised-dentate, with 9–16 coarse teeth on each side, densely pubescent or glabrescent adaxially, densely cobwebby-tomentose and pubescent abaxially. Panicles 4–9 cm, initially rusty cobwebby-tomentose; peduncle 0.5–2.5 cm. Flowers small, pale green, glabrous. Pedicels 1.5–3 mm, glabrous. Calyx cupular, subentire. Filaments filiform, 1.5–1.8 mm; anthers yellow, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.5 mm. Berry purple at maturity, 5–8 mm in diam.


Locality: Shek O, Tap Mun. F. W. Xing 9075; HK sheet 40173.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.

Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Vitis flexuosa Thunb. 葛藟葡萄

Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond. 2: 103. 1794; FKH 65. 1912; FHN 3: 16. 1974; FTW 3: 677. 1977; FRPS 48(2): 163. 1998.

Vitis flexuosa Thunb. f. parvifolia (Roxb.) Planch., Monogr. Phan. 5: 347. 1887; FTW 3: 678. 1977.

Vitis flexuosa Thunb. var. parvifolia (Roxb.) Gagnep., Sarg. Pl. Wils. 1: 103. 1911; FFJ 3: 371. 1987.

Vitis parvifolia Roxb., Fl. Ind. (ed. 2.) 1: 662. 1832; FHK 53. 1861.


Branchlets and abaxial surface of leaves sparsely cobwebby-tomentose when young, later glabrescent; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves simple, unlobed; petioles 1.5–7 cm, sparsely cobwebby-tomentose or subglabrous; leaf blade ovate, triangular-ovate, oval, or ovate-elliptic, 2.5–12 × 2.3–10 cm, base shallowly cordate or subtruncate, often asymmetrical, apex acute or acuminate, margin with 5–12 slightly irregular teeth on each side, glabrous adaxially. Panicle loose, 4–12 cm; peduncle 2–5 cm, sparsely cobwebby-tomentose or nearly glabrous. Pedicels 1.1–2.5 mm, glabrous. Calyx glabrous, undulately lobed. Filaments filiform, 0.7–1.3 mm; anthers yellow, ovoid, 0.4–0.6 mm. Ovary ovoid. Berry globose, 8–10 mm in diam.


Locality: Wan Chai, Stubbs Rd., Kowloon Peak, Chek Keng. Y. S. Lau 563, 586; Y. W. Lam 1418.

Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Japan, Laos, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.

Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Vitis retordii Rom. du Caill. ex Planch. 綿毛葡萄
Monogr. Phan. 5: 613. 1887; FHN 3: 15. 1974; FRPS 48(2): 171. 1998.
Vitis lanata auct. non Roxb.: FHK 53. 1861; FKH 66. 1912.

Branchlets densely brown villous when young, later glabrescent; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves simple, unlobed; petioles 1.5–9 cm, densely brown cobwebby-tomentose; leaf blade ovate or ovate-elliptic, 6–15 × 4–11 cm, base cordate, notch with an acute angle, the two sides rarely overlapping, margin 19–43-toothed on each side, teeth sharp, green and densely pubescent adaxially, tomentose abaxially. Panicle loose, 6–10 cm; peduncle 1.2–2.5 cm, usually brown tomentose. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm, glabrous. Calyx cupular, ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous, subentire. Filaments filiform, 1–1.2 mm; anthers yellow, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.5 mm. Ovary ovoid. Berry globose, ca. 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ho Pui, Chek Keng, Tap Mun, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 467; Y. W. Lam 97, 253.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: May, fruiting: Jun.– Jul.

Vitis sinocinerea W. T. Wang 小葉葡萄
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 17(3): 75. 1979; FFJ 3: 368, fig. 257. 1987; FRPS 48(2): 175. 1998.
Vitis thunbergii Siebold & Zucc. var. cinerea Gagnep., Pl. Wils. 1: 105. 1911.
Vitis thunbergii Siebold & Zucc. var. taiwaniana Lu, FTW 3: 679, pl. 773. 1977.

Branchlets sparsely pale brown or greyish white pubescent and cobwebby-tomentose, glabrescent; tendrils unbranched or bifurcate. Leaves simple, 3-lobed or inconspicuously divided; petioles 1– 4 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade thinly papery, ovate, 2.5– 8 × 2.2 –6 cm, base subcordate or subtruncate, apex acute, margin 5 – 9-toothed on each side, densely pubescent or glabrescent adaxially, densely cobwebby-tomentose abaxially. Panicles small, 2.5 –7.5 cm, axes and branches rusty cobwebby-tomentose; peduncle 1.5 –2 cm, pubescent. Flowers small, pale green, glabrous. Pedicels 1.5 –2 mm, subglabrous. Calyx cupular, subentire. Filaments filiform, ca. 1 mm; anthers yellow, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.5 mm. Berry purple-black at maturity, 6 – 10 mm in diam.

Locality: Ping Chau. Y. W. Lam 276.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Jul. – Oct.

Vitis tsoii Merr. 狹葉葡萄
Lingnan Sci. J. 11: 101. 1932; FFJ 3: 370. 1987; FRPS 48(2): 163, pl. 27: 10 – 12. 1998.

Branchlets densely pubescent; tendrils unbranched. Leaves simple, unlobed; petioles 1–2 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate or triangular-ovate, 3.5–9 × 1.5–4 cm, base subtruncate or rounded, apex acute, margin 10–15-toothed on each side, teeth sharp and fine, sparsely pubescent on veins adaxially, pubescent on veins abaxially, basal veins 5, lateral veins 5 or 6 pairs. Panicle 2–6 cm, narrow. Pedicels 1.5–2.5 mm, subglabrous. Calyx subentire. Filaments filiform, ca. 0.8 mm; anthers yellow, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.5 mm. Ovary conical; style short. Berry purple-black at maturity, globose, 5–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Chek Keng. Y. W. Lam 1212.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Sep.

Vitis vinifera L. 葡萄
Sp. Pl. 1: 202. 1753; FGZ 421. 1956; FRPS 48(2): 166. 1998.

Branchlets glabrous or sparsely pilose; tendrils bifurcate. Leaves simple, conspicuously 3–5-lobed or cleft; leaf blade ovate, 7–18 × 6–16 cm, base deeply cordate, notch rounded, the two sides usually overlapping to nearly so, apex of central lobes acute, margin 22–27-toothed on each side, teeth large, irregular, and sharp, glabrous or sparsely pilose, basal veins 5, lateral veins 4 or 5 pairs, veinlets inconspicuously raised. Panicle sparse or dense, 10–20 cm; peduncle 2–4 cm, glabrous or sparsely cobwebby-tomentose. Pedicels 1.5–2.5 mm, glabrous. Calyx glabrous, undulate. Filaments filiform, 0.6–1 mm; anthers yellow, ovoid, 0.4–0.8 mm. Ovary ovoid. Berry globose or ellipsoidal, 1.5–2 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1542.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in temperate and subtropical regions; native to W Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Aug. – Sep.
Uses: Edible (fruit).

Vriesea fosteriana L. B. Sm. 紅票
Arq. Bot. Estado São Paulo (2)1: 116, pl. 121. 1943; L. H. Bailey, Hortus Third 1164. 1976.

Plant to 1.8 m tall. Leaves forming a dense compact rosette, blue-green with maroon pencilling, to 65 × 7 cm. Spikes prominent with 2 opposed rows of multiple bracts at top end, unbranched. Petals green with purplish tips, to 3 cm or more, longer than stamens.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to Brazil.
Uses: Ornamental.

Vriesea splendens (Brongn.) Lem. 火劍
Fl. des Serres 162, f. 1850; L. H. Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 193. 1949, et Hortus Third. 1165. 1976.
Tillandsia splendens Brongn., Ann. Fl. Pomone 14: 311. 1845.

Plant to 90 cm tall. Leaves green with many irregularly dark-brown cross bands on both surfaces, ligulate or ligulate-lanceolate, 30–60 × 5–7 cm, concave above, with a rounded, shortly cuspidate tip. Scape equalling or exceeding foliage. Spike flalttened, densely imbricate bright red bracts. Sepals coriaceous, light yellow with a pale base, at the top whether or not tinged with red, 2–2.5 cm. Petals curved, slightly exceeding the bracts, yellow, obliquely opened at the top. Stamens exserted.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to tropical America.
Uses: Ornamental.

Vrydagzynea nuda Blume 二尾蘭
Fl. Jav. Orch. 61, t. 20, fig. 3(3–8). 1858; FKH 267. 1912; FHN 4: 204. 1977; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 52, fig. 22. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 106. 2002; FRPS 17: 203. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1070, pl. 460. 2000; FGD 7: 362, fig. 184. 2006; FOC 25: 76. 2009.

Small glabrous herb, 5–15 cm tall; rhizome elongate, creeping, wire-like, up to 30 cm, internodes 2.5–3 cm, 3 mm in diam.; upright stem continuing the rhizome, bearing 3–4 leaves before flowering. Leaves petiolate; petioles 1.3–1.6 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 2.5–4 × 1.5–2 cm, apex acute. Flowers creamy-white; odd sepal ovate-oblong, 5 mm; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 5 mm, the lower portion covering the spur; petals white, shorter than sepals, partially concealed by sepal; lip undivided, calcarate, concealed by the sepals; spur bladder-like; column green, 1.5 mm; anther discoid, orange-brown; pollinia 2; ovary cylindrical, 5–6 mm, hairy.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 11810 (CUHK); C. P. Lau 108 (CUHK); HK sheet 38876.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Indonesia.
Ecology: Well-drained soil in forests. Flowering: Apr.

Wahlenbergia marginata (Thunb.) A. DC. 藍花參
Monogr. Campan. 143. 1830; FRPS 73(2): 29. 1983; FGD 3: 323, fig. 210. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 798, pl. 371, photo 402. 1998.
Campanula marginata Thunb., Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 211. 1784.
Wahlenbergia agrestis A. DC., Monogr. Campan. 145. 1830; FHK 197. 1861.
Wahlenbergia gracilis auct. non (Forst. f.) Schrad.: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 152. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 10–40 cm tall. Stems erect or ascendent, branched from the base, glabrous or sparsely hirsute on the lower part. Leaves alternate, subsessile; leaf blade linear to narrowly elliptic, 1–5 × 0.2–0.6 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, margin undulate, slightly toothed or entire, glabrous or sparsely hirsute on the abaxial surface. Flowers solitary and terminal, or 2 – 3 forming a loose terminal dichotomous cyme. Pedicels slender, 1–10 cm. Calyx‑tube obovoid, ca. 2 mm, glabrous, with 10 indistinct vertical veins; lobes 3 – 5, lanceolate. Corolla campanulate, 5 – 8 mm, blue or rarely white; lobes 3–5, ovate. Stamens 5; style short; stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule obconical, 5–7 × 2.5–3.5 mm, shortly 3‑valved at the top.

Locality: Fanling, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9168; K. L. Yip 4256; HK sheet 39467.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Ecology: Rice fields, wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Waltheria indica L. 蛇婆子
Sp. Pl. 673. 1753; FKH 50. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 169. 1984;
Waltheria americana L., Sp. Pl. 673. 1753; FHK 38. 1861; FHN 2: 83. 1965; FGD 1: 144. 1987.

Suberect or decumbent subshrubs, up to 1 m or taller, many branched. Branchlets densely pubescent. Petioles 0.5–1 cm; leaves ovate or oblong-ovate, 2.5–4.5 × 1.5–3 cm, base rounded or shallow-cordate, margin serrulate, apex obtuse, densely pubescent on both surfaces. Cymes axillary, head-form; bracteoles narrowlanceolate, ca. 4 mm; calyx tubiform, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, longer than tube; petals 5, yellowish, spathulate, slightly longer than calyx; stamens 5; filaments connate, enclosing ovary; ovary sessile, pubescent; styles excentric; stigma fimbriate. Capsules obovate, ca. 3 mm, opening into 2 valves, hairy, enclosed by persistent calyx. Seeds obovate, minute.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 250; Y. S. Lau 3000; Gibbson 7710.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; widely distributed in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Sunny hillslopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn.

Wedelia biflora (L.) DC. 雙頭菊（孿花蟛蜞菊）
Contr. Bot. India 18. 1837; FHK 183. 1861; FKH 145. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 26. 1969; FRPS 75: 351, pl. 60: 1 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 124. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1093, photo 498. 1998.

Verbesina biflora L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 1272. 1763.
Wollastonia biflora (L.) DC., Prodr. 5: 546. 1836; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 28. 1969; Check List HK Plants 290. 2002; 99. 2004.
Melanthera biflora (L.) Wild, Kirkia 5: 4. 1965.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 1–2 m tall; stem branched, scandent, extending to 2–4 m or longer, glabrous or sparsely strigose. Leaves ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 4–14 × 1–7.5 cm, those on upper stem appearing smaller in size, base varied from rounded, truncate to cuneate, showing slightly decurrent, apex acuminate, margin regularly serrate, both surfaces covered with short appressed hairs, denser on abaxial side; petiole slender, 0.7–5 cm. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, about 2 cm across, usually 2–6 or more heads arranged as loose corymbs at terminal, sometimes axillary; peduncles slender, 1.5–6 cm, densely strigose. Involucres hemispherical or ovoid; phyllaries 2‑seriate, foliaceous, ovate‑lanceolate, two layers subequal in length, 4.5–5 × 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse or slightly acute, densely scabrous, subtending the ray florets. Paleae obovate‑oblanceolate, 5–6 mm × 1.5–2 mm, obtuse or shortly acute, upper portion foliaceous and scaberulous, lower half scarious and glabrous, enfolding the achenes of disk florets. Marginal ligulate florets pistillate, in 1 series, corolla yellow, ligule 6–7 × 3–4 mm, tube 1.5–2 mm, apex 2‑lobed, pubescent near the apical region of the abaxial side. Central tubular florets hermaphrodite, many, 4–5 mm, apex 5 lobes and pubescent on abaxial side. Cypselae 3–3.5 × 2–2.5 mm, those developed from ligulate florets thickly trigonous, those from tubular florets 4‑angled, both cuneate at base, broadly truncate at top, strongly pubescent near the summit, glabrous in lower part. Pappus none or of 1 bristle 1.5–2 mm, easily shed off.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 736; S. Y. Hu 6549 (CUHK); Joseph P. W. Woo & T. K. Woo 864 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; E & S Asia, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Common on sandy beaches or in thickets near seashore. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.

Wedelia chinensis (Osbeck) Merr. 蟛蜞菊
Philipp. J. Sci. 12(2): 111. 1917; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 26. 1969; FRPS 75: 354, pl. 60: 7 – 11. 1979; FGD 8: 125, fig. 62. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1094, pl. 522, photo 499. 1998.
Wedelia calendulacea (L.) Less., Syn. Gen. Compos. 222. 1832; FHK 182. 1861; FKH 145. 1912.
Solidago chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 241. 1757.

Perennial creeping herbs; stems decumbent with the lower part rooting at nodes, upper part ascending and becoming erect, strigose‑pilose. Leaves elliptic‑oblong to linear‑oblong, 2.5–7 × 0.5–1.7 cm, subsessile or shortly petiolate, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire or bearing 1–3 pairs of serrate teeth, scabrous on both surfaces, midvein prominent on abaxial side. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, 1.3–2.4 cm across, solitary. Peduncle 2.8–9.5 cm, densely strigose. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; the outer one or two layers foliaceous, green, oblong, subequal, 8–10 × 3–4 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, abaxially scabrous; the innermost layer scarious in lower portion and herbaceous in upper region, linear‑oblong, 6–7 × 1.8–2 mm, apex acute or acuminate, ciliate along margin of apical half. Receptacle flat, paleaceous; the paleae linear, 6 mm × 1 mm, acuminate, subtending the florets. Ray florets 1‑seriate, pistillate, fertile, corolla ligulate, spreading, yellow in colour, ligule oblong, 8 × 3–3.5 mm, apex 2–3‑dentate, tube 1–1.2 mm. Disk florets many, hermaphrodite, fertile, corolla tubular, yellow, 4–5 mm, apex 5 ovate obtuse lobes, glabrous or puberulent inside. Cypselae obovate‑oblanceolate, 3–4 mm, loosely hairy near apex, those developed from ligulate florets 3‑ridged, those from tubular florets laterally flattened. Pappus a short scarious crown with toothed rim.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 69; Y. S. Lau 2334; P. S. Choi 102.
Distribution: S, E & NE China; E & S Asia, Malaysia.
Ecology: Banks of paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

Wedelia prostrata Hemsl. 滷地菊
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 23(157): 434. 1888; FKH 145. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 27. 1969; FRPS 75: 353. 1979; FGD 8: 125. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1094, pl. 523, photo 500. 1998.
Wollastonia prostrata Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 265. 1838.
Verbesina prostrata Hook. & Arn., Beechey Voy. 195. 1837.

Annual creeping herbs; stem rooting at nodes in lower part, flowering branches ascending, hirsute with the hair basally swollen. Leaves ovate to ovate‑oblong, 1–2.5 × 0.3–0.9 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin 1–3 pairs of serrulate teeth, both surfaces scabrous, 3‑veined; petiole 2–6 mm. Capitula 1–2 cm across; peduncle 0.8–1.8 cm, densely hirsute.
