Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 2‑seriate; the outer ones foliaceous, ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–5 × 2–3 mm, acute or obtuse, densely scabrous; the inner ones basally scarious, apically herbaceous, oblanceolate‑oblong, 5–5.5 × 1–1.2 mm, acute‑acuminate, ciliate near apex. Paleae linear‑oblong, enfolding the floret hypanthia, length 6 mm, apically herbaceous and hairy, acute. Marginal florets pistillate, corolla ligulate, yellow, ligule oblong, 5.5–7 × 3–4 mm, apex lobe 3, tube 1 mm. Central florets many, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, yellow, 4–5 mm, 5‑cleft at apex, lobes sparsely hairy on abaxial side. Cypselae oblong‑cuneate, 3–3.5 mm, apex truncate and hairy. Pappus 1–2 bristles or obsolete.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung (Ham Tin, Tai Long Wan and Long Ke Wan). Y. S. Lau 364, 2568; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22723 (CUHK); N. H. Li & K. M. Lau 157 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Sandy places near seaside. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

Wedelia trilobata (L.) Hitchc. 三裂葉蟛蜞菊
Rep. (Annual) Missouri Bot. Gard. 4: 99. 1893; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1097. 1998.
Silphium trilobatum L. Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1233. 1759.

Perennial creeping herbs; stems prostrate or decumbent, green or dull red, glabrous or loosely hirsute. Leaves opposite, rhomboid to lanceolate in outline, trilobed at about middle, 4–10 × 2–5 cm, base attenuate to form wing with petiole, apex acute, margin coarsely serrate, triplinerved, scabrous on both surfaces with abaxial side glandular‑dotted, veins prominent beneath; the free part of petiole 3–7(–10) mm. Capitula solitary, heterogamous, radiate, 2.5–3 cm across. Peduncle elongate, 6–18 cm, densely pilose. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries in 3 series; the outer 2 layers green, foliaceous, elliptic‑oblong, subequal in length and width, 8–10 × 2.5–3 mm, apex acute, abaxially scabrous; the innermost ones scarious basally and slightly herbaceous adaxially, linear‑oblong, 6 × 1.5 mm, erose‑ciliate near apex, acute, subtending the ovaries of marginal ligulate florets. Receptacle plain or slightly convex, paleaceous; the paleae linear, 6–8 × 1–1.2 mm, serrulate near apex, enfolding the ovaries of tubular florets. Ray florets 12–16, corolla ligulate and spreading, yellow to orange‑yellow, ligule oblong, 6–7(–12) × 5 mm, apex 2–3‑toothed, tube short, 1–1.5(–1.8) mm. Tubular florets many, more than 40, corolla yellow, 4–5 mm, limb 5‑lobed, strongly barbate inside. Cypselae 4.5–5 mm, puberulent and glandular near apex, those of ligulate florets oblong‑cuneate, triangular in cross‑section, those of tubular florets clavate, terete. Pappus cup‑shaped with sharply toothed rim.

Locality: Naturalized and widely cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2587; Y. Wong 014 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11043 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to tropical America, widely distributed in the tropics; introduced into Hong Kong in 1971 from S Africa by Mr. Horace Kadoorie.
Ecology: Commonly planted as ground cover for earth slopes and bare hillsides, recently becoming naturalized in Hong Kong. Flowering: Nearly all year round.

Wedelia wallichii Less. 山蟛蜞菊
Linnaea 6: 162. 1831; FRPS 75: 352. 1979; FGD 8: 124. 2007.
Wedelia urticifolia DC., Contr. Bot. India 18. 1834; FRPS 75: 352. 1979; FFJ 5: 353. 1993.

Perennial herbs, 20–60 cm tall. Stems suberect, hispid to glabrous. Lower leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 5–9 × 3–7 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin crenulate, hispid on both surfaces; upper leaves smaller, lanceolate, petiolate or sessile. Capitula ca. 15 mm in diam., solitary on elongate peduncle. Involucre broadly campanulate or hemispherical, 10–15 mm in diam. Phyllaries in two series; outer ones herbaceous, green, oblong, ca. 10 mm, apex obtuse or shortly acute, dorsally scabrous hairy; inner ones oblong to lanceolate, ca. 7 mm, scarious, dorsally pubescent in upper part, apex acuminate. Paleae oblong, sparsely pubescent. Ray florets one seriate, ligules oblong, 4–6 × 2 mm , yellow, apex 2–3‑toothed. Disk florets tubular, yellow, limbs 5‑toothed. Cypselae obovoid, compressed or obtusely 3‑angled, tip contracted. Pappus cup‑shaped, with 2 – 3 bristles.

Locality: Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 2498.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes, streamsides. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.

Wikstroemia indica (L.) C. A. Mey. 了哥王
Bull. Cl. Phys.-Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 2(1): 347 – 358. 1843; FKH 227. 1912; FHN 1: 437, fig. 240. 1964; FGX 1: 622, pl. 256: 1 – 2. 1991; FGD 3: 89, fig. 61. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 300, pl. 46: 3. 1999.
Daphne indica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 357. 1753.
Daphne cannabina Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 236. 1790.

Shrub, 0.5– 2 m or taller. Branches reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 1 mm; leaf blade obovate, elliptic-oblong, or lanceolate, 1.5– 5 × 0.5 – 1.5 cm, papery to thinly leathery, base broadly or narrowly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, glabrous, reddish brown on both surfaces when dried; lateral veins dense, 5–7 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal, capitate, several-flowered; peduncle 0.5 – 1 cm, glabrous. Pedicel 1 – 2 mm. Calyx tubular, yellowish green, 7 – 12 mm, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent abaxially; lobes 4, broadly ovate to oblong, ca. 3 mm. Stamens 8, in 2 whorls, filaments short. Disk scales often 2 or 4, 1 or 2 bifid at apex. Ovary obovoid, glabrous or apex sparsely pubescent; style very short; stigma capitate. Drupe ellipsoidal, 7– 8 mm, red to dark purple when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 38, 144; K. L. Yip 4106.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Vietnam to India.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.– Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Wikstroemia monnula Hance 北江蕘花
J. Bot. 16(181): 13. 1878; FKH 227. 1912; FGX 1: 620, pl. 256: 5 – 6. 1991; FGD 3: 91, fig. 63. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 312. 1999.
Wikstroemia stenantha Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(177): 400. 1894; FKH 227. 1912.

Deciduous shrub, 0.5–0.8 m tall. Branches yellowish green, turning dark purple, angular, greyish pubescent when young, glabrescent. Leaves usually opposite, rarely alternate; petioles short, 1 – 1.5 mm; leaf blade membranous, ovate-elliptic to elliptic, 3–6 × 1–2.8 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex acute; adaxially glabrous, dark brown when dried, abaxially puberulous at least on veins, light brown, lateral veins slender, 4 or 5 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal, often on short lateral branches, shortly racemose, 3–8-flowered; peduncle 3–15 mm, greyish pubescent. Pedicel short. Calyx tube white, 9 – 12 mm, silky pubescent abaxially; lobes 4, ovate, 1– 2 mm, purplish red. Stamens 8; filaments short; anthers ellipsoidal, ca. 1 mm. Disk scales 1, linear or broadly obovate, apex 3-lobed. Ovary narrowly obovoid, ca. 4 mm, stipitate, apex yellowish tomentose; style very short; stigma capitate. Drupe dry, obovoid, enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 479; Y. S. Lau 1397; HK sheet 40001.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Notes: The species was reported as Wikstroemia chinensis Meisn. previously (Check List HK Plants 40. 1993).

Wikstroemia nutans Champ. ex Benth. 細軸蕘花
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 195. 1853; FHK 297. 1861; FKH 227. 1912; FGD 3: 88. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 298. 1999.

Shrub, 1 – 2 m or taller. Branches terete, reddish or greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petiole 1 – 2 mm, glabrous; leaf blade ovate or ovate-elliptic to ovate-lanceolate, 3– 6(–8.5) × 1.2– 2.5(–4) cm, membranous to papery, base cuneate or subrounded, apex acuminate, green to brownish green adaxially, greenish white abaxially, both surfaces glabrous; lateral veins 6–13 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal, shortly racemose, often pendulous, 3– 8-flowered; peduncle 1.5– 3 cm, slender, glabrous. Pedicel 0.5 –2 mm. Calyx yellowish green; tube (10– )13 – 16 mm, base slightly inflated, exterior glabrous; lobes 4, elliptic, ca. 3 mm. Stamens 8; filaments ca. 0.5 mm; anthers linear, 1.5 – 2 mm. Disk scales 2, each divided by a septum and appearing as 4 scales, ca. 1 mm. Ovary obovoid, ca. 1.5 mm, stipitate, apex pubescent; style very short; stigma capitate. Drupe ellipsoidal, 6–7 × 4.5 mm, dark red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 46; N. H. Li 43; K. L. Yip 4489.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: May– Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Wisteria sinensis (Sims) Sweet 紫藤
Hort. Brit. 121. 1827; FRPS 40: 184. 1994; FGD 5: 239, fig 132. 2003.
Glycine sinensis Sims, Curtis's Bot. Mag. 44: t. 2083. 1819.
Wisteria chinensis DC., Prodr. 2: 390. 1825; FKH 77. 1912.

Large woody twiner. Leaves papery, odd-pinnate; leaflets 7–13, opposite or nearly so, ovate-elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, the terminal one large, the basal pair smaller, 5 – 8 × 2 – 4 cm, base obtuse to rounded or cuneate, sometimes oblique, apex acuminate to caudate, covered with appressed silky hairs on both surfaces when young, glabrescent at maturity. Racemes pendulous, 15 – 30 cm, rachis white-pubescent. Flowers fragrant. Calyx cup-shaped, 5 – 6 mm, densely sericeous. Corolla blue-violet, 2–2.5 cm; vexillum orbicular, emarginate, reflexed after anthesis, with 2 callosities at base; wings oblong; keel broadly falcate, shorter than wings. Stamens diadelphous. Ovary linear, tomentose, 6 – 8-ovuled. Pods oblanceolate, 10 – 15 × 1.5 – 2 cm, velvety-pubescent, 1– 3-seeded. Seeds brown, orbicular, 5 cm in diam., flat, shining.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 2349; L. T. Lo 377; K. Y. Chan 161.
Distribution: Areas S of Yellow River.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Wolffia globosa (Roxb.) Hartog & Plas 無根萍
Blumea 18(2): 367. 1970; FOC 23: 86. 2010.
Lemna globosa Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 565. 1832.
Wolffia arrhiza auct. non (L.) Horkel ex Wimm., Fl. Schles. 140. 1857; Hodgkiss, H. K. Freshwater Plants 82. 1978; FRPS 13(2): 211, pl. 42: 4. 1979; FGD 4: 411, fig. 249: 7–8. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 696. 2000; Check List HK Plants 302. 2002; 106. 2004.

Minute thalloid herb, rootless, free floating on or just below water surface. Fronds ovoid to hemispherical, 0.5–1.5 mm, in diam., rounded or slightly pointed at apex, adaxial surface green, with stomata in parallel rows, abaxial surface transparent green, conspicuously convex, epidermal cells pentagonal or hexagonal. Plants rarely flowering.

Locality: New Territories (fide Hodgkiss 1978).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical to temperate regions.
Ecology: Ponds and ditches.
Uses: Forage.

Wrightia laevis Hook. f. 藍樹
Fl. Brit. India 3(9): 654. 1882; FRPS 63: 125, pl. 42. 1977; FGD 1: 455, fig. 509. 1987; FOC 16: 175. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 85. 1999.
Wrightia hainanensis Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 21: 352. 1922.
Wrightia hainanensis Merr. var. variabilis Tsiang, Sunyatsenia 4: 37, pl. 14. 1939.

Trees to 40 m tall, glabrous except for flowers. Bark dark grey; branchlets brownish, lenticellate. Petioles 5 – 7 mm; leaf blade oblong or narrowly elliptic, rarely ovate, 7 – 18 × 2.5 – 8 cm, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, lateral veins 5 – 11 on each side of midvein. Cymes ca. 6 cm; peduncle ca. 1 cm, puberulent to glabrous; pedicels 1 – 1.5 cm. Sepals broadly ovate, ca. 1 mm, pubescent abaxially, apex rounded or obtuse. Corolla white or yellowish, funnelform, tube 1.5 – 3 mm; lobes narrowly elliptic, 5.5 – 13.5 mm, papillate; corona fringed; scales 25 – 35, linear, puberulent. Anthers as long as corona, puberulent. Ovary of 2 separate carpels. Fruit of paired follicles cylindric, distinct, 20 – 35 cm × 5 – 7 mm, lenticellate. Seeds sublinear, 1.5 – 2 cm, coma to 4 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Yuen Tun Ha. H. C. Tang 100; Y. S. Lau 986; HK sheet 38592.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, N Australia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Xanthium sibiricum Patrin ex Widder 蒼耳
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. Beih. 20: 32. 1923; FRPS 75: 325, pl. 55: 1 – 10. 1979; FGD 8: 142, fig. 76. 2007.
Xanthium strumarium L., Sp. Pl. 987. 1753; FHK 181. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1098, pl. 524, photo 501. 1998.

Annual herbs 0.5–1.5 m tall; stem pubescent. Leaves broadly ovate‑deltoid, median ones 3.5–15 × 3–16.5 cm, 3‑ or 5‑lobed, base cordate to broadly cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin irregularly dentate, both surfaces scabrous. Petioles 1.5–16 cm, scabrous. Capitula monoecious. Male head globose, 4–7 mm across, sessile or shortly pedunculate, shorter than 6 mm, densely pubescent and glandular. Phyllaries 1‑seriate, oblanceolate‑oblong, 1.5–2.5 mm, densely hairy and glandular, apex obtuse‑rounded. Receptacle cylindric. Paleae oblanceolate with length 2.2–2.5 mm, acute, hairy and glandular near apex. Male florets numerous, corolla tubular, bell‑shaped, 2–3 mm, apex 5‑lobed, white or greenish white, hairy and glandular in apical 1/3; anthers free and curved inward, conspicuously exserted. Female heads axillary; phyllaries in 1 row, linear, 2.5–3 mm, hairy; inner phyllaries hard, appeared as a bur with 2 female florets enclosed inside. The bur elliptic, green or yellow‑green, narrowed at base forming a short stipe, 2‑beaked apically, 1–2.3 cm including the stipe and beaks, 4–7 mm wide, the beak 2–7 mm in length, pubescent throughout and bearing hooked prickles of 1.2–4 mm. Receptacles microscopic. Female florets without corolla, with only the pistils; stylar branches long and exposed outside the bur. Cypselae 2 per each capitulum, obovate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1426, 2785; S. Y. Hu 12134 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, Russia, Iran, India.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Material (seed oil used in industry), medicinal (folklore).
records.uses: Material (seed oil used in industry), medicinal (folklore).

records.text:
Xanthophyllum hainanense Hu 黃葉樹
J. Arnold Arbor. 6(3): 142. 1925; FHN 1: 368. 1964; FGD 2: 62, fig. 41. 1991; FRPS 43(3): 138. 1997.

Tree, 5–20 m tall. Branchlets terete, slender, glabrous. Petioles 0.6–1 cm; leaf blade leathery, ovate-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 4–15 × 1.5 –6 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex long acuminate, margin entire, sometimes undulate, yellow, thickened, glabrous, yellow-green when dry, midvein and lateral veins prominent on both surfaces, lateral veins 6–11 pairs, reticulate veins prominent abaxially. Racemes or small panicles 3–9 cm, with a few flowers; peduncles and pedicels densely pubescent; bracteole 1, caducous, lanceolate. Flowers small, pale yellow or white, fragrant, 0.8–1.2 cm. Sepals pubescent on both surfaces, ciliate, outer 3 ovate, small, ca. 2 mm; inner 2 oblong, ca. 4 mm. Petals unequal, abaxial and lateral ones lanceolate and slightly curved, ca. 7 mm, clawed and ciliate. Stamens 4–8 mm, filaments villous at base and apex; anthers basifixed, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.5 mm. Ovary pitcher-shaped, ca. 1 mm in diam., densely pubescent, ovules 4; style 3–6 mm, slightly pubescent at base. Drupe globose, yellowish when mature, 1.5–2 cm in diam., pubescent or subglabrous; fruit stalk terete, ca. 5 mm, stout, pubescent. Seed yellowish, compressed globose, ca. 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Wang Shan Keuk Ha Tsuen, Ha Pak Nai, Plover Cove. F. W. Xing 7898, 8036, 10011.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Timber.

Xenostegia tridentata (L.) D. F. Austin & Staples 地旋花
Brittonia. 32: 533. 1980; FOC 16: 300. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 383, pl. 170, photo 224. 1998.
Convolvulus tridentatus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 157. 1753.
Evolvulus tridentatus (L.) L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 392. 1762.
Ipomoea tridentata (L.) Roth, Arch. Bot. (Leipzig) 1(2): 38. 1798.
Merremia hastata Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552. in obs. 1893.
Merremia tridentata (L.) Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552, in obs. 1893.
Merremia tridentata subsp. hastata (Hallier f.) Ooststr., Blumea 3(2): 317, fig. 2: o. 1939; FHN 3: 482. 1974; FTW 4: 349. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 66, pl. 14: 1. 1979; FFJ 4: 486, fig. 388. 1989; FGD 4: 349. 2000; Check List HK Plants 224. 2002; 78. 2004.
Ipomoea angustifolia auct. non Jacq.: FKH 180. 1912.
Ipomoea filicaulis auct. non Blume: FHK 238. 1861.

Prostrate or twining herb, with a stout root. Stems ± angular to narrowly winged, glabrous. Petiole 1–3 mm or absent; leaf blade narrowly oblong, linear‑oblong, to linear, dilated toward base, 2–8 cm × 0.3–1.5 mm, base hastate, ± amplexicaul, basal lobes dentate, apex acute or obtuse, mucronulate, subglabrous. Cymes 1–3‑flowered; peduncle (1–)5–6 cm, slender, pubescent at base, glabrescent distally; bracts minute, subulate. Pedicel 6–8 mm. Sepals ovate‑lanceolate, subequal or outer 2 shorter, 6–8 mm, glabrous, apex attenuate‑acuminate forming a sharp point. Corolla pale yellowish or white, with or without a maroon to brown center, funnelform, ca. 1.6 cm, glabrous abaxially. Stamens inclusive, subequal; filaments sparsely pubescent at base. Ovary glabrous. Capsule globose or ovoid, papery. Seeds blackish, 3–4 mm, glabrous, apex acute.

Locality: Stanley, Tai Po, Lam Tei, Pui O, Po Toi Islands, Soko Islands. P. S. Choi 25; Y. W. Lam 1048, 1177.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical E Africa, S & SE Asia, tropical Australia.
Ecology: Sandy grounds, thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.

Xylosma congestum (Lour.) Merr. 柞木
Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 249. 1919; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 611, fig. 241. 1963, & FTW 3: 766, pl. 808. 1977; FFJ 4: 14, fig. 14. 1989; FGD 3: 105, fig. 73. 1995.
Croton congesta Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 582. 1790.
Hisingera japonica Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(2): 168. 1845.
Hisingera racemosa Sieb. & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 1: 169, 189, t. 88, 100, pl. 3, fig. 1–14. 1835.
Xylosma japonica A. Gray, Mem. Am. Acad. Sci. Art. n. ser. 2, 6: 381. 1859.
Xylosma racemorum (Sieb. & Zucc.) Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 155. 1866; FRPS 52(1): 37, pl. 8: 1–3. 1999.
Xylosma senticosum Hance, J. Bot. 1868. 328; FKH 37. 1912.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, to 15 m tall. Branches spinescent when young, spineless in age, glabrous or puberulous. Petioles ca. 2 mm, glabrous or puberulous; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate to ovate-elliptic, 3 – 8 × 2–3(– 4.5) cm, leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin serrate, glabrous or puberulous along veins on both surfaces; lateral veins 3 – 4 pairs. Racemes 1–2 cm, puberulous. Sepals 4 –6, ovate, 2.5–3.5 mm. Male flower: filaments ca. 4.5 mm, slender; anthers ellipsoid. Female flower: ovary ellipsoid, ca. 4.5 mm, glabrous; styles short; stigmas 2-lobed; disc rounded, margin slightly repand. Berry globose, 4 – 5 mm in diam., black, with persistent sepals at base.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap, Fanling. S. C. Ng 4508; W. J. Tutcher 9204; HK sheet 262.
Distribution: S, E, SW & NW China; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Xylosma longifolium Clos 長葉柞木
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 8: 231. 1857; FHN 2: 457. 1964; FFJ 4: 15.1989; FGD 3: 105. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 40, pl. 7: 7. 1999.
Xylosma congesta (Lour) Merr. var. kwangtungensis Metc., J. Arnold Arbor. 2: 272. 1931.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, up to 7 m. Branchlets spiny, slender, glabrous. Petioles 5 – 8 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 5 –12 × 1.5 – 4 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin obtusely serrate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4 – 8 pairs. Racemes 0.5 –2 cm, glabrous or puberulous, many-flowered; bracts ovate, small. Sepals 4(– 5), small, ovate, 2– 4 mm. Male flower: yellowish green; pedicels 2–3 mm, puberulous; filaments ca. 4.5 mm; anthers ellipsoid, disc 8-lobed. Female flower: ovary bottleshaped, 3.5– 4 mm; styles short; stigmas 2-lobed. Berry globose, 4– 6 mm in diam., purple, usually with reflexed persistent sepals.

Locality: Fanling, Lam Tsuen, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Sha Tau Kok. P. S. Choi 282, 326; Y. S. Lau 2939.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Indochina.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.

Xyris bancana Miq. 中國黃眼草
Fl. Ned. Ind., Eerste Bijv. 608. 1861; FKH 282. 1912, excl. syn. X. schoenoides; van Royen, Fl. Males., ser. 1, 4: 369. 1953; Hansen, Fl. Camb., Laos, Vietnam 20: 156. 1983; FOC 24: 5. 2000; FGD 6: 333. 2005.
Xyris chinensis Malme, Svensk Bot. Tidskr. 21: 386. 1927; FRPS 13(3): 17. 1997.
Xyris schoenoides auct. non Mart.: FHK 379. 1861.

Tufted herb, 30–50 cm tall. Leaf blade narrowly ensiform-linear, 8–12(–20) cm × 1.5–2 mm, apex acute, smooth or minutely and transversely rugulose; sheath 2–4 cm. Peduncle 15–40(–50) cm, slender, subterete, smooth, basally subtended by a sheath. Head ellipsoidal, 5–12 × 5–8 mm. Basal bracts oblong-ovate, ca. 4 mm, indistinctly keeled, apex rounded and usually emarginate; median bracts obovate, ca. 5 × 3.5 mm, conchiform, not keeled, apex rounded and ± erose, with a papillate triangle in the upper half. Lateral sepals free, subequilateral, linear to narrowly obovate, curved, 4.5–5 mm, less than 1 mm wide, margin ± erose, keel narrow and entire at base and apex but central portion slightly wider and denticulate.

Locality: Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Lam Chung. L. Gibbs 7768; Y. S. Lau 3088; HK sheet 7651.
Distribution: Guangdong; Indochina, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Swamps and other wet places. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Xyris capensis Thunb. var. schoenoides (Mart.) Nilsson previously (Check List HK Plants 302. 2002; 106. 2004).

Xyris indica L. 黃眼草
Sp. Pl. 1: 42. 1753; FKH 282. 1912; van Royen, Fl. Males., ser. 1, 4: 373. 1953; Hansen, Fl. Camb., Laos, Vietnam 20: 157. 1983; FRPS 13(3): 13, pl. 4: 1 – 5. 1997; FOC 24: 4. 2000; FGD 6: 332, fig. 189. 2005.

Perennial, robust herb, 25–70 cm tall. Leaves linear-ensiform, 20–50(–70) cm × (2.5–)3–6(–8) mm, apex acute to obtuse, glabrous, veins indistinct when dry, with many short, prominent, transverse ribs connecting longitudinal veins; sheath 7–20(–30) cm. Peduncle (15–)30–80 cm, with prominent furrows. Head ovoid to subglobose, 1–1.5 × 0.8 – 1.5 cm. Median bracts suborbicular, obovate, or conchiform, 5–8 × 5–7 mm, minutely papillate in the upper third, margin gold-coloured, membranous, apex entire or emarginate. Lateral sepals linear-spatulate, 5–7 × 0.8–1.4 mm, crest denticulate, apex obtuse; median sepal cap-shaped, 4–6 × 2–2.5 mm. Petals yellowish to yellow; limb obovate to suborbicular, 3–4.5 × 3–4 mm, margin serrulate; claw 3.5–5 × ca. 0.5 mm. Stamens ca. 4 mm. Staminodia 2–3 mm. Ovary obovoid, 1-locular. Capsule globose to obovoid, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8392.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; Indochina, Malaysia, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Inundated paddy fields, wet places. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Xyris pauciflora Willd. 蔥草
Phytographia. 1: 2. 1794; FHK 379. 1861; FKH 282. 1912; van Royen, Fl. Males., ser. 1, 4: 371. 1953; Hansen, Fl. Camb., Laos, Vietnam 20: 160. 1983; FRPS 13(3): 18, pl. 4: 6 – 9. 1997; FOC 24: 5. 2000; FGD 6: 334, fig. 190. 2005.

Tufted herb, 14–50 cm tall. Leaves linear-lanceolate, striate when dry, 8–22 cm × 1–3 mm, apex acute to acuminate, sparsely papillose on the margin and between the longitudinal veins on both surfaces; sheath 1–5 cm. Peduncle 5–35 cm, subterete. Head globose to ovoid, usually less than 1 cm in diam. Basal bracts elliptic, papillose along apical 1/2 of midvein, apex emarginate to obtuse; median bracts suborbicular to broadly obovate, 3–5 × 3–4 mm, with a papillate triangular patch in the upper third, margin membranous, mucronate at the top. Lateral sepals boat-shaped, 3.5–4.5 × ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, keel narrow, coarsely serrulate, apex subacute; median sepal cap-shaped, ca. 3.5 mm. Petals yellow; limb obovate, 2.5–3.5 mm; claw 3–4 mm. Stamens 0.9–1.3 mm. Staminodes 2-brachiate, shorter than stamens. Ovary obovoid. Style 1.2–2 mm; stigma capitate. Capsule ovoid to ellipsoidal, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Tai Po, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1438; Y. W. Lam 1263, 1782.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Philippines, New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Ravines damp sandy soils, swamps. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Youngia heterophylla (Hemsl.) Babc. & Stebbins 異葉黃鵪菜
Publ. Carnegie Inst. Wash. 484: 87. 1937; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 32. 1969; FRPS 80(1): 152. 1997.
Crepis heterophylla Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 475. 1888.

Annual or biennial herbs; 30–100 cm tall; stem erect, solitary or fasciculate, branched, loosely hairy in lower portion. Leaves subglabrous or sparsely crisped scabrous above and beneath, upper surfaces green, lower surfaces tinged reddish purple especially for the radical leaves. Basal leaves elliptic or oblanceolate‑oblong, 7– 25 × 3–13 cm, lyrately deeply pinnatisect, apical lobes hastate, irregularly hastate, ovate or lanceolate, 4.5–14 × 2–11 cm, apex acuminate to long acuminate; lateral lobes 1–8 pairs, opposite to each other or obliquely opposite, elliptic or auriculate, apex acute or obtuse, growing smaller downward, all lobes margin mucronulate, faintly or conspicuously dentate‑sinuate; leaf petiole 3–7 cm, winged. Cauline leaves hastate or lyrately trifoliate. The upper leaves lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, often non‑divided, those growing near or on peduncles much reduced in size, linear‑subulate. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, with 11–25 florets per head, corymbose at terminal. Involucres cylindric, 6 mm long; phyllaries glabrous, apex acute; outer layers small ovate, 0.5–1 × 0.5–0.7 mm; inner layers linear‑lanceolate, 6 × 1–1.2 mm. Ligulate florets yellow, length 7–9 mm, lower tube 3 mm, pubescent outside, ligule 4–6 mm, apex 5‑lobed; anther tube exserted, base sagittate, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches slender, 1–1.2 mm. Cypselae brown, fusiform, 3 × 0.8 mm, 14–15‑ribbed, minutely hairy, apex without beaks. Pappus white, 3 – 4 mm, scaberulous.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Kadoorie Farm. P. S. Choi 330; N. H. Li 54; S. Y. Hu 11840 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Mar.–May.

Youngia japonica (L.) DC. 黃鵪菜
Prodr. 7: 194. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 33. 1969; FRPS 80(1): 155. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1098. 1998; FGD 8: 268, fig. 165. 2007.
Crepis japonica (L.) Benth., FHK 194. 1861; FKH 150. 1912.
Prenanthes japonica L., Mant. Pl. 1: 107. 1767.

Annual herbs 10–100 cm tall; stem erect, lower portion covered with crisped multicellular hair. Radical leaves rosulate at base, obovate, oblanceolate, elliptic or oblong, 4–13 × 2.5–5.5 cm, lyrately pinnatilobed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, apical lobes large, ovate, deltoid‑ovate or obovate, apex rounded or obtuse; lateral lobes 3–7 pairs, elliptic or triangular, gradually smaller downward, the lowermost one auriculate; leaf margin mucronulate and somewhat dentate‑sinuate, both surfaces crisped scabrous; petiole 1–11 cm, winged or not. Cauline leaves absent or rarely with 1–2, appearance similar to radical leaves. Capitula 7–8 mm across, corymbose paniculate at stem and branch terminal; peduncle 0.3–2 cm. Involucres cylindric, about 5 × 2–2.5 mm; phyllaries glabrous on abaxial surfaces, apex acute or obtuse, herbaceous with margin membranous; outer layers short ovate, 0.8–1.2 × 0.6 – 1 mm; inner layers linear, 5 × 0.8–1.2 mm. Ligulate florets 10–20 per head, yellow, corolla 5–6 mm, lower tube 2–2.2 mm, pubescent outside, ligule 3–4 mm, apex 5‑toothed; anther exserted, base sagittate, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches slender and recurved, about 1 mm long. Cypselae fusiform, brown, 2 – 2.2 × 0.5–0.8 mm, 10–13‑ribbed, minutely hairy, apex beakless. Pappus bristles 3 mm, white, scaberulous, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 32; Y. S. Lau 1960; S. Y. Hu 12989 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E & S Asia, Indochina.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–May.

Yulania denudata (Desr.) D. L. Fu 玉蘭（玉堂春）
J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 19(3): 198. 2001.
Magnolia denudata Desr., Lam. Encycl. Bot. 3: 675. 1791, excl. syn.; FGZ 88, fig. 22. 1956; FGD 1: 9. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 131. 1996.
Lassonia heptapeta Buc’hoz, Pl. Nouv. Decour. 21, t. 19, fig. 1. 1779, nom. rej. prop.
Magnolia heptapeta (Buc’hoz) Dandy, J. Bot. 72: 103. 1934.
Magnolia conspicua Salisb., Parad. Lond. 1: t. 38. 1806.
Magnolia yulan Desf., Hist. Arb. 2: 6. 1809.

Deciduous tree, up to 25 m tall; bark deep grey, rough and fissured; winter buds and peduncles densely covered with pale greyish yellow silky hairs. Stipular scars 1/4 –1/3 the length of petioles. Petioles 1–2.5 cm, villose, adaxially narrowly furrowed. Leaves obovate to obovate-elliptic, 10–15(–18) × 6–10(–12) cm, papery, gradually narrowed below middle, apex broadly rounded, truncate or slightly emarginate, adaxially deep green, villose when young, pilose on veins in age, abaxially pale green, villose along veins; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein, reticulations of veins conspicuous. Flower appearing before leaves, erect, fragrant, 10–16 cm in diam.; peduncles conspicuously enlarged, densely pale yellow sericeous; tepals 9, white, usually pinkish at base, subequal, oblong-obovate, 6–8 (–10) × 2.5–4.5(–6.5) cm; stamens 7–12 mm, anthers 6–7 mm, dehiscing laterally, connectives ca. 5 mm wide, exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium pale green, glabrous, cylindrical, 2–2.5 cm; pistils narrowly ovoid, 3–4 mm; style conical 4 mm. Aggregate fruit cylindrical, often curved due to some undeveloped carpels, 12–15 × 3.5–5 cm; follicles thickly woody, brown, white lenticeled; seeds heart-shaped, laterally compressed, ca. 9 × 10 mm; testa red, endotesta black.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 799.
Distribution: Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Hunan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Yulania liliiflora (Desr.) D. L. Fu 紫玉蘭（辛夷）
J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 19(3): 198. 2001
Lassonia quinquepeta Buc’hoz, Pl. Nouv. Decouv. 21, t. 19, fig. 2. 1779, nom. rej. prop.
Magnolia liliiflora Desr. in Lam. Encycl. Bot. 3: 675. 1791, excl. syn. “Mokkwuren fl. albo” Kaempfer; FRPS 30(1): 140. 1996.
Magnolia quinquipeta (Buc’hoz) Dandy, J. Bot. 72: 103. 1934.

Deciduous shrub, up to 3 m tall; twigs greenish purple or pale purplish brown. Stipular scars about 1/2 the length of petioles. Petioles 0.8 –2 cm. Leaves elliptic-obovate or obovate, 8–18 × 3–10 cm, base gradually narrowed, decurrent along petioles to stipular scars,apex acute or acuminate, adaxially deep green, sparsely pubescent when young, abaxially greyish green, pubescent along veins; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers appearing at the same time with leaves, vase-shaped, erect, slightly fragrant; peduncles thick, hairy; tepals 9–12, outer 3 calyx-like, purplish green, lanceolate, 2–3.5 cm, caducous, the inner two whorls fleshy, adaxially whitish, abaxially purple or purplish red, petaloid, elliptic-obovate, 8–10 × 3–4.5 cm; stamens purplish red, 8–10 mm, anthers ca. 7 mm, dehiscing laterally, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium ca. 1.5 cm, pale purple, glabrous. Aggregate fruit dark purplish brown, cylindrical, 7–10 cm; follicles subglobose when mature, apex short-beaked.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 35819.
Distribution: Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; Fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal.

Yulania × soulangeana (Soul.-Bod.) D. L. Fu 二喬木蘭（紫玉蘭）
J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 19(3): 198. 2001.
Magnolia soulangeana Soul.-Bod., Mem. Soc. L. Paris 269. 1826; FRPS 30(1): 132. 1996.

Deciduous small tree, 6–10 m tall; twigs glabrous. Stipular scars about 1/3 the length of petioles. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, pubescent. Leaves obovate, 6 –15 × 4 –7.5 cm, papery, base cuneate, gradually narrowed, apex short acute, adaxially remaining with hairs along midvein at base, abaxially ± pubescent; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein. Flowers appearing before leaves, pale red to dark red; tepals 6 –9, the outer 3 usually one third shorter than the inner ones; stamens 1–1.2 cm, anthers ca. 6 mm, dehiscing laterally, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium glabrous, cylindrical, ca. 1.5 cm. Aggregate fruit ca. 8 × 3 cm; follicles ovoid or obovoid, 1–1.5 cm, black when mature, white-lenticeled; seeds dark brown, broadly obovate or obovate, compressed laterally.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 3045, 31231.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in subtropical and temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Note: A hybrid of Y. denudata × Y. liliiflora, it varies in the shape, size and colour of tepals. There are about 20 cultivars in cultivation.
records.uses:
Ornamental.
Note: A hybrid of Y. denudata × Y. liliiflora, it varies in the shape, size and colour of tepals. There are about 20 cultivars in cultivation.

records.text:
Zamia furfuracea L. f. 澤米蘇鐵（牙買加蘇鐵）
Aiton Hortus Kew. 3: 477. 1789.
Palmifolium furfuraceum (L. f.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 803. 1891.

Stem tuberous, cylindrical, to 75 cm tall or more, ca. 20 cm in diam., old plants branched at apex. Leaves 5 –7 per crown, 0.5–2 × 0.1–0.25 m; petioles 15–25 cm, spiny, rare unarmed; leaflets 10–15 pairs, thick and stiff, obovate-oblong 16–18 × 4–6 cm, apex obtuse or irregular. Pollen cones solitary, erect, cylindrical, 7–12 cm long, 1.8 –2.5 cm in diam., densely light brown tomentose; peduncles 8 –10 cm long, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., densely light tomentose; microsporophylls in 10–12 vertical rows of 18 –20 each; sporangia in two patches on the lower edges of the sporophyll with a sterile center band 2–5 mm wide. Seed cones solitary, erect, cylindrical, 16–24 cm long, 6.5 –7 cm in diam., densely reddish tomentose, the sterile apex mucronate, ca. 2 cm long; megasporophylls arranged in 10–12 vertical rows of 14–15 each; peduncle 10–20 cm long, 1.5–2 cm in diam., densely tan tomentose. Seeds red when ripe, 1.1–1.5 × 0.8 –1 cm, light tan, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. W. Lam s.n. (HK sheet 34677)
Distribution: S China (cultivated). Native to Mexico.
Uses: Ornamental.

Zanthoxylum ailanthoides Siebold & Zucc. 椿葉花椒（樗葉花椒）
Fl. Jap. 1: 30. 1846; Abh. Akad. Muchen 4(2): 138. 1846; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 542, fig. 2814. 1972; FTW 3: 531. 1977; FGD 2: 237. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 537. 1993; FRPS 43(2): 35, pl. 10: 11. 1997.
Fagara ailanthoides (Siebold & Zucc.) Engl., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(4): 118. 1896.

Deciduous tree, up to 15 m tall, 30 cm d.b.h. Bark greyish brown to blackish brown, not fissured. Stems spiny, spines 2–5 mm, sharp, base to 3 cm wide. Inflorescence rachis and branchlets scattered with short and straight spines. Leaflets 11–27, opposite, narrowly lanceolate or subovate, 7–18 × 2–6 cm, base rounded, symmetrical or slightly asymmetrical, apex long acuminate, margin obviously dentate, glabrous on both surfaces, densely glandular-dotted, greyish green and glaucous abaxially; midveins impressed adaxially, lateral veins 11–16 pairs. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered, subsessile. Sepals and petals 5. Petals pale yellowish white, ca. 2.5 mm. Male flower: stamens 5, pistillode very short, 2–3-lobed. Female flower: carpels 3(–4). Fruiting pedicels 1–3 mm. Follicles pale reddish brown, pale grey or brownish grey when dry, ca. 4.5 mm, apex not awned, with many glands. Seeds ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Tsiu Hang, Chek Keng, Tai Long, Sai Wan, Lo Tsz Tin, Tai Po Kau, Ting Kok, Tai Mei Tuk. Y. S. Lau 1687, 2786; Y. W. Lam 906.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Zanthoxylum avicennae (Lam.) DC. 簕欓花椒（簕欓）
Prodr. 1: 726. 1824; FHK 58. 1861; FKH 55. 1912; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 543, fig. 2815. 1972; FHN 3: 31. 1974; FGD 2: 238, fig. 153. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 34. 1997.
Fagara avicennae Lam., Encycl. 2: 455. 1788.
Zanthoxylum avicennae var. tonkinense Pierre, Fl. For. Cochinch. 4, pl. 289B. 1893.
Zanthoxylum lentiscifolium Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 329. 1851; FHK 58. 1861.

Deciduous tree, to 15 m. Stems with sharp, thick, pedate-spines. Bark dark grey to brownish grey, not fissured. Branches solid, shortly spiny. Leaf rachis narrowly winged adaxially; leaflets 13–18(–25), usually oblique rectangular, strongly asymmetrical, 4–7 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex acute or obtuse, entire or sparsely dentate at upper half. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered; rachis and pedicels sometimes purplish red. Male flower: pedicels 1–3 mm; sepals and petals 5; sepals broadly ovate, green; petals yellowish white; stamens 5; pistillode 2-fid. Female flower: petals longer than male ones, ca. 2.5 mm; staminodes very small; carpels 2(–3). Fruiting pedicels 3–6 mm. Follicles pale purplish red, 4–5 mm in diam., apex not awned, with many glandular dots. Seeds shorter than 4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1612; S. P. Lau 153; C. H. Tsou 1881.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Secondary forests or thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Zanthoxylum lentiscifolium was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Gough, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.
records.uses:
Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Zanthoxylum lentiscifolium was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Gough, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

records.text:
Zanthoxylum myriacanthum Wall. ex Hook. f. 大葉臭花椒
Fl. Brit. India 1(3): 496. 1875; FKH 55. 1912; FRPS 43(2): 36, pl. 8: 1 – 3, 10: 9. 1997.
Fagara myriacantha (Wall. ex Hook. f.) Engl., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(4): 118. 1896.
Zanthoxylum rhetsoides Drake, J. Bot. (Morot) 6(15 – 16): 275. 1892; FGD 2: 238. 1991.
Fagara rhetsoides (Drake) Reeder & S. Y. Cheo, J. Arnold Arbor. 32(1): 69. 1951.

Deciduous tree, 2–4 m, rarely up to 15 m. Bark dark grey, not fissured. Stems spiny, spines sharp, base to 3 cm wide. Leaf rachis and leaflets without spines. Leaflets 7–17, opposite, broadly ovate, ovate-elliptic or oblong, 10–20 × 4–10 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, symmetrical or slightly asymmetrical, margin conspicuously shallowly crenate, glabrous on both surfaces, glands large and many; midvein impressed adaxially, lateral veins conspicuous. Inflorescences terminal, to 35 × 20 cm, many-flowered, branches pubescent. Sepals and petals 5. Petals white, ca. 2.5 mm. Male flower: sepals broadly ovate, ca. 1/3 mm; stamens 5, filaments longer than petals; pistillode 3-lobed at apex. Female flower: petals ca. 3 mm; staminodes very short; carpels (2–)3(–4). Follicles reddish brown, ca. 4.5 mm in diam., with many glands, apex not awned. Seeds ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 2611, 2810; HK sheet 4445.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Secondary forests, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Zanthoxylum nitidum (Roxb.) DC. 兩面針
Prodr. 1: 727. 1824; FHK 58. 1861; FKH 56. 1912; FHN 3: 32. 1974; FTW 3: 533, fig. 715. 1977; FGD 2: 240, fig. 155. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 14, pl. 1: 1 –3, 2: 5 – 6. 1997.
Fagara nitida Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 439. 1820.
Zanthoxylum asperum var. glabrum C. C. Huang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 6(1): 76. 1957.
Zanthoxylum nitidum f. fastuosum How ex Huang, FHN 3: 32, 573, fig. 544. 1974; FFJ 2: 359. 1985.

Scandent shrub, 1–5 m tall. Spines on branches straight, broad and flat at base. Leaves imparipinnate; petiolule 2–5 mm, rarely sessile; leaflets (3–)5–11, opposite, broadly ovate or suborbicular, narrowly elliptic, 3–12 × 1.5–6 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute to caudate, emarginate, margin sparsely shallow-dentate, teeth glandular-dotted, sometimes entire, glabrous except midveins pubescent at base abaxially. Inflorescences axillary at shoot apex, rachis pubescent. Flowers yellowish green, 4-merous. Sepals purplish green at upper part, ca. 1 mm wide. Petals ovate-elliptic or oblong, ca. 3 mm. Male flower: stamens 5–6 mm, anthers broadly ellipsoidal to subglobose. Pistillode semiglobose, pulvinate, apex 4-lobed. Female flower: petals wider than those of male flower; staminodes absent or scalelike; ovary globose, style thick and short, stigma capitate. Fruiting pedicels 2–5 mm. Pericarp reddish brown. Follicle 5.5–7 mm in diam., shortly awned at apex. Seeds globose, 5–6 mm in diam., slightly flat adaxially.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 954; S. P. Lau 103; HK sheet 40088.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Lowland secondary forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Zanthoxylum ovalifolium Wight 異葉花椒
Ill. Ind. Bot. 1: 169. 1839; FGD 2: 235, fig. 151. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 40. 1997.
Fagara dimorphophylla (Hemsl.) Engl., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(4): 118. 1896.
Fagara robiginosa Reeder & S. Y. Cheo, J. Arnold Arbor. 32(1): 68, pl. 1. 1951.
Zanthoxylum dimorphophyllum Hemsl., Ann. Bot. (Oxford) 9(33): 150. 1895.
Zanthoxylum ovalifolium Tutcher, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 37: 64. 1905.
Zanthoxylum robiginosum (Reeder & S. Y. Cheo) C. C. Huang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 6(1): 35. 1957.

Deciduous tree, to 10 m. Branches greyish black, rarely spiny. Young branches and buds often rusty pubescent. Leaves unifoliolate or digitately 3-foliolate; petiolule slightly enlarged at apex, wings absent or rudimentary; leaflets broadly elliptic or lanceolate, 4–8 × 1.8–4 cm, base acute, apex rounded or obtuse, often emarginate, margin obviously obtuse-dentate; reticulate veins conspicuous. Inflorescences terminal. Tepals 6–8, unequal, slightly various in shape, 2–3 mm, apex rounded. Male flower: stamens 6; pistillode pulvinate. Female flower: staminodes 4–5, half as long as ovary; carpels 2–3, style backward curved. Follicles purplish red, sparsely pubescent when young, 6–8 mm in diam., base with a very short stipe, glands few, apex shortly awned. Seeds 5–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Mount Parker. HK sheet 639.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Sep. –Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Zanthoxylum scandens Blume 花椒簕

Bijdr. Natuurk. Wetensch. 249. 1825; FTW 3: 535. 1977; FFJ 2: 358. 1985; FGD 2: 241. 1991; FRPS 43(2): 20. 1997.

Fagara chinensis Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 13(3): 141. 1918.

Zanthoxylum chinensis (Merr.) Chung, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1: 123. 1924.

Fagara cuspidata (Champ.) Engl., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(4): 118. 1896.

Zanthoxylum cuspidatum Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 329. 1851; FHK 58. 1861; FKH 55. 1912; Icon. Corm. Sin. 2: 545, fig. 2819. 1972; FHN 3: 32. 1974.

Fagara scandens (Blume) Engl., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 3(4): 118. 1896.


Scandent shrub. Stems, branches and leaf rachis armed with many prickles. Leaves imparipinnate; petiolule 2–5 mm; leaflets 5–25, alternate or irregularly opposite, ovate, ovate-elliptic or oblique oblong, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acute to caudate, often emarginate, entire or serrulate at upper half, black when dry, glossy adaxially, glabrous on both surfaces. Panicles 2–5 cm, axillary and terminal. Calyx lobes 4, pale purplish green, broadly ovate, 0.5 mm. Petals 4, pale yellowish green, 2–3 mm. Male flower: stamens 4, 3–4 mm, anthers with an apical gland; pistillode semiorbicular, pulvinate, style 2–4-lobed. Female flower: carpels 3–4; staminodes scalelike. Follicle purplish red, greyish brown or black when dry, 4.5–5.5 mm in diam., apex shortly awned, glandular-dots inconspicuous, flat or slightly prominent. Seeds subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam., slightly acute at both ends.


Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2332; Y. S. Lau 494, 1668.

Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; SE Asia.

Ecology: Secondary forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Notes: The type specimen of Zanthoxylum cuspidatum was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Zea mays L. 玉蜀黍
Sp. Pl. 2: 971. 1753; FKH 317. 1912; FHN 4: 488, fig. 1272. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 287, pl. 72: 1–3. 1997; FOC 22: 650. 2006; FGD 9: 511, fig. 273. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect, solid, 1–4 m tall. Leaf sheaths with transverse veinlets; leaf blades flat and broad, linear-lanceolate, 30–90 × 3–12 cm, glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs, base rounded, margins scabrid, midvein stout; ligule ca. 2 mm, membranous. Female inflorescence axillary, the spikelets in many rows on a thicken, almost woody axis, enclosed by many large foliaceous bracts or spathes; glumes equal, veinless, margins ciliate; florets hyaline, style extremely long and slender, like silky threads. Caryopsis globose or depressed globose. Male inflorescence a "tassel" of many digitate racemes, terminal; spikelets paired, pedicel unequal, one 1–2 mm, the other 2–4 mm, slender pilose; glumes subequal, membranous, ciliate; lemma and palea hyaline membranous, slightly shorter than glume; anthers orange, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2753.
Distribution: Originated from America, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (beverage base, oil/fat, starch, vegetable).

Zehneria japonica (Thunb.) H. Y. Liu 老鼠拉冬瓜
Bull. Nation. Mus. Nat. (Taiwan) 1: 40. 1989.
Aechmandra odorata Hook. f. & Thoms. ex Benth. FHK 124. 1861.
Bryonia japonica Thunb., F1. Jap. 325. 1784.
Melothria indica Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 35. 1790; FKH 113. 1912; FGZ 184. 1956.
Melothria odorata Hook. f. & Thoms. ex C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 2(6): 626. 1879; FKH 113. 1912.
Zehneria indica (Lour.) Keraudren, Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam 15: 52, fig. 5 – 8. 1975; FRPS 73(1): 170, pl. 45: 1–7. 1986; FFJ 5: 244, fig. 228. 1993; FGD 3: 118, fig. 82. 1995.

Plant monoecious. Stems and branches filiform, glabrous. Tendrils unbranched. Petioles slender, 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade membranous, triangular-ovate, undivided or 3 –5-lobed, 2–10 × 2–10 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or sparsely denticulate, scabrous and white-punctate adaxially, glabrous or puberulous along veins on both surfaces. Male flower solitary or in 2–3-flowered racemes; pedicels filiform, 1–2.5 cm, glabrous; calyx broadly campanulate, 1.5 × 2–2.5 mm; corolla white or yellow, puberulous, lobes ovate-oblong, 2–2.5 × 1– 1.5 mm; filaments short, 0.5 mm; anthers ellipsoid, pubescent, 1 mm, anther cells curved, puberulous, connective protrudent at apex. Female flower solitary or rarely paired in the same axil together with male flowers; corolla broadly campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., lobes lanceolate, 2.5 –5 × 1–1.5 mm; staminodes glandular; ovary narrowly ovoid, 3.5 – 4 × 1–2 mm, tuberculate; style 1.5 mm. Berries ellipsoid or ovoid, 1–1.5 cm long, 5 – 8 mm in diam., obtuse at both ends, orange or red. Seeds greyish white, ovate, 3 –5 × 3 –4 mm, margin inconspicuous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Tai Po Kau, Kap Lung. Y. W. Lam 1151; Y. S. Lau 772, 3259.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei; Korea, Japan, India, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Zephyranthes candida (Lindl.) Herb. 蔥蓮（玉簾）
Bot. Mag. 53: pl. 2607. 1826; FGZ 701. 1956; FRPS 16(1): 5, pl. 1: 3. 1985; FOC 24: 265. 2000; FGD 5: 440. 2003
Amaryllis candida Lindl., Bot. Reg. 9: pl. 724. 1823.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs ovoid, 2–3 cm in diam. Leaves all basal, linear, 15–38 × 3–4 mm, adaxial surface ± concave, abaxial surface convex. Scape slender, erect, 18 – 25 cm, fistulose. Flowers solitary and terminal; involucre 1, spathiform, ca. 2.3 cm, membranous, basically united into a tube, upper part splitting on one side; pedicels ca. 1.5 cm. Perianth tube very short, 2–3 mm; segments 6, white, but green at base, outer 3 larger, obovate-elliptic, 3–3.5 × 1.3–1.6 cm, inner 3 narrower. Stamens 6, 7–9 mm, green; anthers linear, 7–8 mm. Style slender, slightly longer than stamens; stigma 3-notched. Capsule subglobose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1956; HK sheet 28341.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Zephyranthes carinata Herb. 韭蓮（風雨花）
Bot. Mag. 52: t. 2594. 1825; FOC 24: 265. 2000; FGD 5: 441, fig. 233. 2003.
Zephyranthes grandiflora Lindl., Bot. Reg. 11: pl. 902. 1825; FGZ 701. 1956; FRPS 16(1): 7, pl. 1: 4–5. 1985; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs ovoid, 2–3 cm in diam. Leaves all basal, linear, 15–35(–40) × 6–8 mm, nearly flat, midvein raised abaxially. Scape slender, erect, 18–25 cm, fistulose. Flowers solitary and terminal; involucre 1, spathiform, 3–4 cm, membranous, basically united into a tube, upper part splitting on one side; pedicels ca. 2.5–3.5 cm. Perianth tube 2–2.5 cm, green; segments elliptic, 5–6 × 1.8–2.5 cm, rose to pink. Stamens 6, subequal, ca. 2.3 cm; anthers linear, ca. 1.8 cm, versatile. Style slender, longer than stamens, with a 3–4-lobed stigma. Capsule subglobse.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28336, 32971.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Zeuxine affinis (Lindl.) Benth. 纖細線柱蘭
Fl. Brit. India 6: 108. 1890; FOC 25: 75. 2009.
Monochilus affinis Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 487. 1840.
Zeuxine gracilis auct. non (Breda) Blume, S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 50, fig. 20. 1977; Check List HK Plants 384. 2002; 133. 2004.

Small terrestrial herb; stems trailing, 3 mm in diam. Leaves 4–7, cauline, leaf blades ovate, 1–4 × 0.6–2 cm, apex acute. Flowers small, white, 5–10 in a terminal spike; odd sepal ovate, 6 × 5 mm at base, green with pink apex; lateral sepals elongatetriangular, 5 × 2 mm, apex obtuse; petals oblique-ovate, 4 mm, white, the upper margin adhere to odd sepal forming a galea; lip white, fleshy, wavy, saccate, apex 2-lobed; column 1 mm long; anther elongate-ovoid, 2.5 mm; pollinia 2, sectile; ovary woolly, 8 mm long. Capsule ellipsoidal, 7 mm, hairy.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lugard Rd., Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. S. Y. Hu 12276, 12277 (CUHK); HK sheet 34778.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Sunny slopes, roadsides. Flowering: Sep.–Oct.

Zeuxine parvifolia (Ridl.) Seudebf. 白花線柱蘭
Dansk Bot. Ark. 32(2): 82. 1978; FRPS 17: 199, pl. 27: 5–7. 1999 [“parviflora”]; FGD 7: 361. 2006 [“parviflora”]; FOC 25: 74. 2009.
Hetaeria parvifolia Ridl., J. Straits Branch Roy. Asiat. Soc. 39: 87. 1903.
Zeuxine leucochila Schltr., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 3: 46. 1907; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 49. 1977.

Small terrestrial herb, 15–20 cm tall. Leaves 3–5, ovate-oblong, 2–4 × 1–1.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers small, white, 3–9 in a terminal raceme on stipe 10 cm; odd sepal ovate-lanceolate, 4 mm, lateral sepals oblong-ovate, 4.5 × 2 mm, acute; petals white, oblonglanceolate, 4.5 mm, obtuse, forming a galea with the odd sepal; lip T-shaped, white and yellow at base, 4.5–5 mm, base saccate, apex 4 mm, 2-lobed, lobes oblong, entire or shallowly toothed.

Locality: New Territories (Hu 1977), Sai Kung (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan, Taiwan; Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Forests and hillslopes. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The species was reported as Zeuxine parviflora (Blume) J. J. Sm. previously (Check List HK Plants 133. 2004).

Zeuxine strateumatica (L.) Schltr. 線柱蘭
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 45(3): 394. 1911; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 49. 1977; FRPS 17: 194. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1080. 2000; FGD 7: 360, fig. 183. 2006; FOC 25: 72. 2009.
Orchis strateumatica L., Sp. Pl. 2: 943. 1753.
Zeuxine membranacea Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. 486. 1840; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 49. 1977.
Zeuxine sulcata Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 485. 1840; FHK 360. 1861; FKH 267. 1912.

Delicate terrestrial herb with a rhizome consisting of 4 internodes; stem upright. Leaves 8 or 9, olive-green with pink veins and margin, leaf blade linear-lanceolate, the middle larger ones 2.5–3.5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous. Flowers white, with pink veins 5–15 in a terminal spike 2 cm long, with pink lower bracts; dorsal sepal ovate-oblong, 6 mm, base saccate; lateral sepal 4 mm, ovate-oblong; petals oblique-linear, forming a hood with the odd sepal; column short; anther ovate-oblong; pollinia 2, sectile; ovary obovoidellipsoidal. Capsule 5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Tai Lung, Tsang Tsui, Sham Chung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12807 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23110 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3202.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, tropical Asia.
Ecology: Damp open grasslands, open ground between large trees in forests. Flowering: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.

Zingiber corallinum Hance 珊瑚薑
J. Bot. 18: 301. 1880; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 142. 1981; FGD 2: 430. 1991; FOC 24: 326. 2000.

Pseudostems ca. 1 m tall. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath sparsely hairy or glabrous; ligule 2–4 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 20–30 × 4–6 cm, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely hairy or glabrous. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, oblong, 15–30 cm; peduncle 15–20 cm; scale-like sheaths 4–5 cm; bracts red, ovate, 3–4 cm, apex acute. Calyx 1.5–1.8 cm, split to middle. Corolla tube 2.5 cm, lobes with purple stripes, oblong, ca. 1.5 cm, apex acute, central one larger than lateral ones; central lobe of labellum obovate, ca. 1.5 cm; lateral lobes ca. 8 mm, apex acute. Anther sessile, ca. 1 cm; connective appendage beak-like, curved, ca. 5 mm. Ovary 2–2.5 mm, sericeous. Seeds black, glossy.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Long Sai Wan. Y. S. Lau 1027; HK sheet 27972, 27973.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests or cultivated. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Zingiber integrilabrum Hance 全唇薑
J. Bot. 20: 80. 1882; FKH 272. 1912; FRPS 16(2): 148. 1981; FGD 2: 431. 1991; FOC 24: 327. 2000.

Rhizomes branched, odourless. Pseudostems 40–100 cm high. Ligule orbicular, 2-lobed, to 1 mm; petiole absent to 5 mm; leaf blade lanceolate, 15–18 × ca. 3 cm, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent or pilose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, ca. 1/2 embedded in ground, 4–5-flowered; peduncle 1–2 times as long as inflorescence; scale-like sheaths 2–3 cm; bracts becoming brownish when old, lanceolate, 2–3 cm, glabrous; bracteoles ca. 2 cm, membranous. Calyx ca. 2 cm, split on one side, glabrous. Corolla ivory white; tube ca. 2.7 cm; lobes lanceolate ca. 1.8 cm. Labellum elliptic, lateral lobes reduced into rounded teeth or absent. Anther sessile, ca. 8 mm; connective appendage ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough. HK sheet 7228.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb No. 21812, BM) was collected by C. Ford from Mount Gough in April 1881. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Zingiber mioga (Thunb.) Roscoe 蘘荷
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8: 348. 1807; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 146. 1981; FGD 2: 430. 1991. FOC 24: 332. 2000.
Amomum mioga Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 51. 1784.

Rhizomes yellowish. Ligule 2-lobed, 3–12 mm, membranous; petiole absent to 1.7 cm; leaf blade lanceolate-elliptic or linearlanceolate, 20–37 × 4–6 cm, apex caudate, glabrous or abaxially pilose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, ellipsoidal, 5–7 cm; peduncle absent to 17 cm; scale-like sheaths oblong; bracts reddish green with purple veins, elliptic. Calyx 2–3 cm. Corolla tube longer than calyx; lobes yellowish, lanceolate 2.7–3 cm × ca. 7 mm. Labellum ovate, ca. 3 cm; central lobe yellow with white margin, ca. 2.5 × 1.8 cm; lateral lobes 1.3 cm × 4 mm. Anther ca. 1 cm; connective appendage ca. 1 cm. Capsule obovoid, loculicidally dehiscent; pericarp red inside. Seeds black; aril white.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 7543; HK sheet 34827.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Moist places in mountain valleys. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore), vegetable (young inflorescence).

Zingiber officinale Roscoe 薑
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8: 348. 1807; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 141. 1981; FGD 2: 429. 1991; FOC 24: 325. 2000.

Rhizomes branched, yellowish inside, thickened, fleshy, strongly aromatic. Pseudostems 50 – 100 cm. Leaves sessile; ligule slightly 2-lobed, 2 – 4 mm, membranous; leaf blade lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 15 – 30 × 2 – 2.5 cm, glabrescent. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, ovoid, 4 – 5 × ca. 1.5 cm; peduncle to 25 cm; bracts pale green, sometimes yellowish at margin, ovate, ca. 22.5 cm, apex mucronate; bracteoles equaling bracts. Calyx ca. 1 cm. Corolla yellowish green; tube 2 – 2.5 cm; lobes lanceolate, ca. 1.8 cm. Central lobe of labellum with purple stripes and cream blotches, oblong-obovate, shorter than corolla lobes; lateral lobes ovate, ca. 6 mm, free nearly to base. Stamen dark purple; anther ca. 9 mm; connective appendage curved, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 27976, 32657.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely cultivated in tropics in Asia.
Ecology: Cultivated in vegetable gardens. Flowering: Oct.
Uses: Flavour, medicinal (forklore).

Zingiber striolatum Diels 陽荷
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29: 262. 1901; FRPS 16(2): 146. 1981; FGD 2: 431. 1991; FOC 24: 332. 2000.

Rhizomes white, slightly fragrant. Pseudostems 1–1.5 m. Ligule brown striped, 2-lobed, 4–7 mm, membranous; petiole 0.8–1.2 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 25–35 × 3–6 cm, base attenuate, apex caudate, abaxially glabrous or sparsely villose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, subovoid; peduncle 1.5–2 cm or longer; scale-like sheaths 2–3; bracts red, broadly ovate or elliptic, 3–5 cm, pubescent. Calyx ca. 2.5 cm, membranous. Corolla tube white, 4–6 cm; lobes white or yellowish with purplish brown stripes, oblong-lanceolate, 3–3.5 cm. Labellum pale purple, obovate, ca. 3 × 2.6 cm; lateral lobes ca. 5 mm. Filaments very short; anther lanceolate, ca. 1.5 cm; connective appendage ca. 1.5 cm. Capsule loculicidally dehiscent; pericarp red inside. Seeds black; aril white.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. G. Barretto 254; HK sheet 34253.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Zingiber zerumbet (L.) Roscoe ex Sm. 紅球薑
Exot. Bot. 2: 105. 1806; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 142. 1981; FGD 2: 429. 1991; FOC 24: 326. 2000.
Amomum zerumbet L., Sp. Pl. 1: 1. 1753.

Rhizomes yellowish inside. Pseudostems 0.6–2 m. Leaves sessile or shortly petiolate; ligule entire, 1.5–2 cm, leaf blade lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 15–40 × 3–8 cm, base narrowed, apex acuminate, glabrescent or abaxially somewhat pilose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, conical or ovoid-oblong, 6–15 × 3.5–5 cm, apex obtuse; peduncle 10–30 cm; scale-like sheaths 5–7; bracts closely imbricate, green when young, red when old, slightly hairy, slimy adaxially, margin membranous; bracteoles ca. 1.5 cm. Calyx 1.2–2 cm, membranous, split on 1 side, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube 2–3 cm, slender; lobes pale yellow, lanceolate, central one 1.5–2.5 cm. Labellum pale yellow, ca. 1.5 × 2.5 cm; central lobe suborbicular or subobovate, 1.5–2 × ca. 1.5 cm, apex emarginate; lateral lobes obovate, ca. 1 cm, free nearly to base. Stamen ca. 1 cm; connective appendage beak-like, ca. 8 mm. Ovary ca. 4 mm, glabrous. Capsule ellipsoidal, 0.8–1.2 cm. Seeds black.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk, Pok Fu Lam, Peel Rise, Bowen Rd., Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 2050; Y. S. Lau 1567; S. C. Ng 2633.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Moist places in forest. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (forklore).

Zinnia violacea Cav. 百日菊（魚尾菊）
Icon. 1(3): 57, pl. 81. 1791; C. M. Hu, Check List HK Plants 290. 2002.
Zinnia elegans Jacq., Coll. Bot. 3: 152. 1789; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 39. 1969; FRPS 75: 336. 1979; FGD 8: 118, fig. 57. 2007.

Annual herb 30–100 cm tall; stem erect, sparingly branched, striate, scabrous. Leaves ovate‑lanceolate to ovate‑triangular, 3–7 × 1–3 cm, base subcordate, somewhat amplexicaul, sessile, apex acute or acuminate, scaberulous on both surfaces and along margin, entire, trinerved. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, 4–6 cm across, solitary and terminal. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, tricolour, margin black, rounded and hairy along apex; outermost broadly ovate or suborbicular, 4–5 × 2–4 mm; innermost obovate‑oblong, 9–10 ×4–5 mm. Receptacle conical; palea with purplish red, triangular and fimbriate appendages at apical end. Ligulate florets variously coloured, white, orange, red to purple, ligules oblanceolate to spatulate, 1.4 – 3 cm, entire or 2‑lobed at apex, scaberulous on both surfaces and along margin, glandular on lower side; style exposed, about 1 cm, branches 5 mm. Disk tubular florets yellow to orange, 7–8 mm, 5 apical lobes ovate‑lanceolate, yellowish hairy; anthers included, base obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑deltoid; stylar branches elongate, apical appendage penicillate. Cypselae compressed, that developed from ray florets obovate, 6–7 × 4–5 mm, ribbed in the middle and along both margins; those from disk florets obovate‑trigonous, 7–8 × 3–4 mm; both hairy and with remnant of corolla attached. Pappus reduced to 2 teeth or absent.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. Y. Hu 12297 (CUHK); H. Y. Yeung 181 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Zornia gibbosa Span. 丁癸草
Linnaea 15: 192. 1841; FRPS 41: 358. 1995; FGD 5: 352, fig. 195. 2003.
Zornia cantoniensis Mohlenbr. 16(1): 124, fig. 45 & 84. 1961.
Zornia diphylla auct. non (L.) Pers.: FHK 80. 1861; FKH 78. 1912.

Perennial, slender, branched herb, 20 – 50 cm, glabrous, sometimes with robust rhizomes. Stipules lanceolate, 1 cm, produced below insertion. Leaves 2-foliolate; leaflets ovate-oblong, obovate-lanceolate, 0.8–1.5(–2.5) cm, base oblique, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces, black or brown gland-dotted. Racemes axillary, 2 – 6 cm, 2 – 6(–10)-flowered. Bracts 2, ovate, 6–7(–10) mm, peltate, ciliate, 5–6-striate. Calyx 3 mm. Corolla yellow, ca. 1.2 cm; vexillum reniform, clawed; wings and keel smaller. Stamens monadelphous. Ovary sessile. Pods 2 –6 segments suborbicular, 2(–4) mm in length and width, reticulate and spiny.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Ma Liu Shui, Ting Kok Rd., Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2342; L. T. Lo 516.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy lands. Flowering: Apr. – Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Sep.

Zostera japonica Asch. & Graebn. 矮大葉藻
Pflanzenr. 31(IV 11): 32. 1907; FRPS 8: 90. 1992; FOC 23: 107. 2010.
Zostera nana auct. non Roth: Check List HK Plants 78. 1993.

Submersed marine herb; rhizomes creeping. Stems slender. Leaves 5–35 cm × 1–2 mm, apex obtuse or emarginate, entire, with a conspicuous midvein and lateral veins, and with 3 or 4 secondary veins between the midvein and lateral veins; sheaths 2–10 cm, margin membranous, with rounded auricles; spathe sheath 5–8 cm, apex blade 8–15 cm; spadix enclosed in spathe sheath. Anther 4.5–6 mm. Ovary 2 mm, stigma 2. Fruits oblong, ca. 4 mm, beaked. Seeds brownish, smooth and nitid.

Locality: Sheung Sze Wan, Lai Chi Wo, Tung Chung Pier. Y. W. Lam 101, 111, 699.
Distribution: Shandong, Hebei, Liaoning; Eurasia and Africa.
Ecology: Sea water.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Zoysia matrella (L.) Merr. 溝葉結縷草
Philipp. Sci. 7(4): 230. 1912; Fl. Ill. Pl. Prim. Sin. Gram. 737, pl. 685. 1959; FTW 5: 508. 1978; FRPS 10(1): 129. 1990; FFJ 6: 176, fig. 144. 1995; FOC 22: 497. 2006; FGD 9: 366, fig. 178. 2009.
Agrostis matrella L., Mant. Pl. 2: 185. 1771.
Zoysia pungens Willd., Ges. Naturf. Feunde Berlin Neue Schriften 3: 441. 1801; FKH 318. 1912.
Zoysia tenuifolia Thiele, Linnaea 9(3): 309. 1835.
Zoysia tenuifolia Willd. ex Trin., Mem. Acad. Sci. Petersb. ser. 6, 4: 96. 1836.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous or stoloniferous. Culms up to 20 cm tall. Leaf blades flat or involute, tough, suberect to spreading, 3 – 8 × 0.1–0.3 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface thinly pilose, apex acute; ligule a ring of hairs ca. 0.1 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous, bearded at mouth with 4–5 mm hairs. Inflorescence linear, 2–4 × 0.2–0.3 cm, exserted above leaves, composed of 10 – 30, loosely overlapping spikelets; rachis somewhat wavy; pedicels shorter than spikelet, 1–3 mm, widened at apex. Spikelets 1-flowered, 2–3 × ca. 1 mm, laterally compressed, lanceolate, yellowish brown or purplish brown, shortly pedicellate; lower glume usually absent; upper glume as long as the spikelet, lanceolate, 5-veined, midrib prominent, sometimes scabrous toward apex, lateral veins obscure, margins thinner and inrolled, apex obtuse; lemma oblong-ovate, 2–2.5 mm, obscurely 3-veined, midvein sometimes shortly excurrent; palea lanceolate, hyaline, 1/2 length as lemma. Anthers 1–1.5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.5 mm.

Locality: New Territories. S. P. Lau 190; Y. S. Lau 2288; S. C. Ng 1220.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in the tropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Sandy places near seaside. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Zoysia pacifica (Goudswaard) M. Hotta & Kuroki 細葉結縷草

Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 45: 71. 1994; FOC 22: 498. 2006; FGD 9: 367. 2009.

Zoysia matrella (L.) Merr. var. pacifica Goudswaard, Blumea 26: 172. 1980.

Zoysia tenuifolia auct. non Willd. ex Trin.: FRPS 10(1): 131, pl. 40: 4–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 177, fig. 145. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 440. 2000; Check List HK Plants 350. 2002; 122. 2004.


Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms densely tufted, 5–10 cm tall, much branched. Leaf blades setaceous, soft, 4–6 × ca. 0.1 cm; ligule 0.3 mm, upper part a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous, bearded at mouth with 2–5 mm hairs. Inflorescence linear, up to 1.5 cm, with 6–12 loosely overlapping spikelets; rachis somewhat wavy; pedicels shorter than spikelet, up to 1.6 mm, scabrous, slightly widened at apex. Spikelets lanceolate, 1-flowered, 2–3 × ca. 0.6 mm, straw-coloured tinged purplish; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as the spikelet, lanceolate, shiny, obscurely 5-veined, apex subacute, sometimes with subapical awn-point; lemma slightly shorter than upper glume, 1-veined; palea and lodicule reduced. Anthers 0.6–0.8 mm.


Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2199; Y. W. Lam 31; HK sheet 42001.

Distribution: Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Pacific islands; widely introduced in tropical and subtropical regions as lawn plant.

Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Uses: Environmental (excellent for lawns).

Zoysia sinica Hance 中華結縷草
J. Bot. 7: 168. 1869; FKH 318. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 126. 1990; FFJ 6: 176. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 440. 2000; FOC 22: 497. 2006; FGD 9: 366. 2009.
Zoysia pengens auct. non Willd.: FHK 418. 1861.

Perennial herb with creeping rhizomes. Culms tufted, erect, arising from nodes of rhizome, stiff, 10–30 cm tall, branched at base. Leaf blades broadly linear, flat or margins involute, stiff, suberect to patent, 2–10 × 0.2–0.3 cm, green or grey-green, glabrous, apex pungent; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, upper part a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous, usually persistent at base, pilose at mouth. Inflorescence linear-elliptic, 2–4(–8) × 0.4–0.5 cm, usually shortly exserted from uppermost leaf sheath, with many closely overlapping spikelets; pedicels shorter than spikelet, ca. 3 mm, widened at apex. Spikelets 1-flowered, 4–8 × 1–1.5 mm, yellowish brown or purplish brown; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as the spikelet, leathery, lanceolate-oblong to narrowly oblong, with slightly falcate apex, obscurely 7–11-veined, midvein usually shortly excurrent; lemma membranous, lanceolate- oblong, 3–4 mm, truncate or with a sinus, 1-veined; palea and lodicule reduced. Anthers 1.5–2.5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 2167; K. L. Yip 4209; HK sheet 39436.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hebei, Liaoning, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Coastal sands, river banks, roadsides and weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.
